name: CYGNI: All Guns Blazing
detailed_description: An unrelenting onslaught of eye-popping visuals, ear bursting soundscapes and mind-melting action makes CYGNI the vanguard for the next generation of Shoot-em Ups. Outgunned and outmanned, plunge into a sky teeming with danger in a last-ditch battle for survival. Choose to route power between weapons or shield systems and go up against unrelenting waves of ground and aerial enemies. Upgrade your ship by picking up new tech and take down colossal alien bosses in visceral combat; do whatever it takes to survive. CYGNI is an exhilarating space shooter elevating the genre to a truly next-generation experience. Encamped within the remains of a long-lost civilization on the planet CYGNI, Earth forces are decimated by a surprise attack from a powerful, biomechanical, alien race. As one of the last pilots on the last carrier in the fleet, you are the only line of defence against the unyielding alien bombardment. CYGNI Features: • With next generation visuals, animation and special effects, CYGNI is a cinematic shoot'em up. • Be the lone fighter battling through intensely hostile levels filled with waves of air and ground assaults. • Choose where to route power on the fly switching between shields (defensive) or weapons systems (offensive). • Collect energy to power up your ship and energise weaponry from hard-hitting nukes to inescapable vortex bombs. • Launch air-to-air and air-to-ground attacks as you traverse neon-lit metropolises, moon-like landscapes and even outer space. • Go one-on-one against gargantuan enemies in cinematically epic boss battles. • Full orchestral score and immersive sound design.

_childDocuments_.review: Stages go on for way too long with the same enemy wave repeating once you already figured it out. As a standout, stage 6 in the lategame consists of a whopping 2 basic enemy types you shoot for over 10 minutes. I remember stage 3 having the same enemy spawning for over 2 minutes. It's as if the stages were stretched out so that the game is longer than the 2 hour steam refund window which is just ass. Doesn't feel like the game is respecting your time with how much the same pattern is cycled over and over.Cool visual designs on enemies and bosses are the main positive standout. But why is the player ship so small its basically invisible and has a messy silhouette? If visuals are the strong point let me look at the cool player ship design and not a tiny blob with fireworks coming out. The circular player ship design and 60° aiming on the right stick feel like they would fit better in 360° twin-stick shooter. Instead you have twin-stick controls in a scrolling shooter which makes you run out of buttons to use. The fact that you have to take your hand off the right stick to shoot missiles by default is ridiculous (it's hard to even find a better mapping). Double tapping the shot button could shoot missiles or something, assuming there's no reason to not be firing at all times.Managing your shield and weapon energy seems like the main gameplay gimmick of the game. But collecting items at max shield does nothing so the player has to mash conversion into missiles before collecting items. This seems like pointless busywork when you could be given missiles automatically when shield is maxed out. The risk/reward is miniscule since you can intentionally stay at low shield high missile and instantly convert them back to shield when you get the low HP warning. It feels like the system might become entirely redudant both in terms of needing player control and involving risk after the player gets used to it.Missiles are a strong weapon and main gameplay mechanic, but if you have fast enemies able to fly off the bottom of the screen missiles tend to target these, straight up just flying downwards not accomplishing anything. Effective strategy by the enemy, considering they can also sometimes shoot bullets upwards from offscreen.There are some pretty cool enemy types (large black flyers introduced early on have multiple attacks including an entrapment laser) but the way the level design is handled makes poor use of them. stages tends to spam the same 2 enemies at you for 5 minutes at a time instead of mixing things up and keeping the player on their toes.Movement has crazy acceleration / inertia. You're best off using the analog stick for movement and maybe d-pad for small taps. This works more naturally on analog but on d-pad the sudden acceleration on holding a direction is hard to manage in dense bullet patterns. Maybe this gets adjusted later.The game has upgrades but you gain no money if you fail a stage which seems counter productive if the idea is to make the player grow stronger over time and stages to become easier if they're stuck. Are you really assuming players want to grind early stages or lower difficulties in a shmup of all things, with the stages lasting almost 20 minutes? Some larger ground and air enemies are unkillable without matching firepower upgrades, so you sit around for minutes waiting for them to time out. Granted the game does have an arcade mode which gets around the upgrade unlocks issue with a static amount of them & a leaderboard.Shield/Weapon energy item system results in the gameplay loop in many stage sections becoming I see 2+ health drops onscreen -> I convert 1 health into missiles & take damage on purpose without caring about it, shoot missiles and collect 2 items returning to max health. Repeat over and over with the screen clearing and me taking damage 40 times and that might be an entire stage. With the repetitive enemy waves this gameplay loop can become mind numbing.It is funny that when there are frequent item spawns the main focus becomes basic calculus of items flying on the screen and pressing the convert button rather than paying attention to dodging bullets or shooting the enemy. There is no reason to care if there are 2 health pickups on screen every second.In terms of UI the game has some fonts so small that they're unreadable at 1080p resolution being sub-pixel size. At launch there are performance issues with big framerate drops (shader compilation stutter?) even on a RTX4080 + 7800x3D system at 1080p 60fps which is I guess pushing the envelope for shmups.TLDR. this reminds me of some janky 200X xbox live shooter you could get for very cheap (Aegis Wing, 0 Day Attack On Earth). but instead of being a humble small indie game it's marketed as pushing the genre forward and has stages bloated in duration to extend the 'time to beat' but wasting the players time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! I'm looking at all the complaint reviews and I'm just not seeing it. It's a shmup, and a hard one at that, but if you pick a sensible upgrade path, and manage your resources right, it's not unbearable. It's been a long time since someone put this much graphical might into the venerable shmup genre. It's good to see a release like this in the year 2024. If you like shumps, don't miss this one.

_childDocuments_.review: 🟩 Pros: + Auto-fire toggle+ Unique energy mechanic+ Challenging levels with enjoyable bosses+ Distinct targeting between air and ground enemies+ A showcase in brilliant audio and visual presentation, truly a cinematic experience+ Weapon slots, modifiers, and custom firing patterns (unlocked after beating the game)🟥 Cons: -	UI isn’t intuitive-	While it presents brilliantly visually, clarity is poor-	Poor movement controls make precise dodging difficult-	Enemy variety is low, leading to sections feeling artificially stretched out-	Ground enemies feel like an afterthought, adding no real value to gameplay-	Stage 1 delivers a horrible onboarding experience, being both overly difficult and too long, especially when compared to the following 6 stages🏷️ Suggestions: ~ Redesign maps for solo play, 16:9 is too wide for a vertical shmup (it makes sense for co-op however)A traditional shoot 'em up (shmup) involves avoiding a screen full of bullets through accurate and precise movement, CYGNI however, attempts to reinvent the wheel. It’s a balancing act between offense and defence having you destroy enemies, collect energy, transfer said energy into your weapons, and unleash a flurry of missiles at the cost of your shield. The mechanic is unique but feels like busywork, ultimately turning the game into a loop of transferring energy from your shield into your weapons so you can spam missiles.A lot of the time it’s hard to distinguish between what you can and can’t destroy amidst the fray of combat. Unclear visuals, coupled with the less than precise movement make avoiding enemy projectiles harder than it needs to be, which is probably why our health pool is so large. Finally, while the 16:9 aspect ratio is perfect for co-op, which is a feature of CYGNI, for solo play it detracts from the experience.Despite the gripes I have with CYGNI, it's a refreshing and unique take on the shmup genre. It’s as chaotic as it is gorgeous, offering a fast, frantic, and fun experience. It takes some getting used to, and the price is far too steep for what’s on offer, so know ‘Recommended’ rating only applies if it’s on a steep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: There's potential here, but overall I recommend skipping this; I feel like I paid $20 for graphics, $5 for the actual gameplay, and $5 for the new ideas towards a good shmup. The game opted for quantity over quality in actual combat and quality in the wrong places.---The game rolls through 7 stages with 3 difficulty options, but it has a really rough introduction with the first stage being arguably the hardest due to being one of the longest, requiring the most multi-tasking between air and ground management, and giving you multiple boss fights; you also have to play it on initial boot with none of the upgrades that the game is very clearly balanced around you already having.The next-to-last stage is exactly at the level of difficulty I expected for the opening stage of a shmup, with super simple enemies, almost no ground interaction, and a boss that I probably could have literally beaten blindfolded based only on sound cues; by that point in most shmups, you're expecting a constant storm.---The devs dropped a "character trailer" a bit before launch with a gratuitous jiggle shot, pretending like the game has anything more than an excuse plot. I probably should have taken that as a warning to skip.Past the opening cutscene of the first mission and the closing scene of the final mission, every other scene is a lower quality, mostly still image aside from simple looped animations and maybe the occasional model click-and-drag movement. Nobody is ever named, no personalities are developed, the aliens just want everyone dead, and the high-point of drama is .It looks great in actual gameplay; that can't be argued. Funny thing about shmups, though? They can look like garbage and still be really fun; 'Frantic' is a free Flash shmup series with barebones graphics and I'll end my life with more time and enjoyment in just one of those games than I will with the entirety of 'CYGNI'.All those fancy explosions are really great at hiding enemy projectiles and concealing small enemies so they can escape from you and cost potential points.---Mechanically, this game does have potential. It's one of the few shmups to have distinct targeting between air and ground targets, you collect energy cells that can go towards shields or weapons, and you can fully customize your basic shot pattern!Oh, excuse me, that's not wholly accurate. You can fully customize your shot pattern after clearing the entire game with the default "all turrets focused forward" pattern that you'd already wanted for maximum DPS. Durrrr...And ground targets? Most of the time, they're just point padding with no bearing on actual combat; a few dedicated elites do pose an anti-air threat in a couple of levels, but you can usually safely ignore the ground in most missions. And only a single boss requires managing both ground (the boss itself) and air targets (the helper tendrils it summons). Early on and in another level you can see allied ground forces fighting enemies and help them out a bit, but this ultimately has no bearing on anything other than a pointless "allies lost" numeric counter.A lot of segments boil down to spamming missiles and then immediately transferring a shield point back into weapons as defeated enemies spray out energy cells to replace the point lost from firing missiles; a few people said back during the demo days that collected energy should automatically filter into both shields and then weapons, but the devs ignored that crucial advice in favor of making us wear out our mouse-wheels' ability to scroll up.The devs also straight up lied about alternative weapons being available; you have your starting basic machinegun array, ground barrage beams, and homing missiles, with the only extra weapon being a cooldown burst damage weapon that does not completely alter your basic weapon set-up.---"Well, maybe the game is super straight-forward because it's designed for perfecting it and getting the highest score!"A lot of shmups are but still have more charm and are easier on the eyes with stylized, unique art styles. I didn't really feel hyped when playing 'CYGNI' like I do with things like the 'Gundogs' trilogy, 'Tyrian 2000' (the thing I judge all other shmups against!), or even ye olde 'Galaga'; I don't feel motivated to get back in and do a perfect 1CC with the maximum possible score.---There's potential here. The devs are so close to it. Maybe for the DLC or a sequel, spend a little less time on the graphics and a bit more on the soul and interesting implementation of your stand-out mechanics, yeah?Or, ya know, swap gears entirely and make a visual novel about the MC post-war; gods know the Youtube crowd would be interested in that based on the "most replayed" tracker for the trailer.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★☆☆☆I really wanted to love Cygni. It’s a new Shmup from Konami with eye-catching graphics that reminded me of Sky Force and those beloved 80s & 90s shooters. I pre-ordered it, played it on both PC and Steam Deck, and even tackled it on hard mode. Here’s the reality check: unless you got it for free or with 75% discount, save your money and your sanity. The typical Shmup formula is start easy, collect points, upgrade your ship, unlock new stuff, rinse, and repeat. But Cygni's execution is seriously flawed. The tutorial introduces weapons that aren’t actually available, then throws you into Stage 1 with a normal difficulty setting. After about 15 minutes of fighting three bosses with just one life, you'll be asking yourself two things: “Am I terrible?” and “Why is normal mode so not normal?” Spoiler: It’s the latter. And seriously, who decided three bosses in the first stage was a good idea? That’s a late-game challenge, not an introductory level!  With seven stages that stretch on like a bad date, each one dragging for 13-15 minutes and the final one reaching an epic 20 minutes, the game’s idea of fun seems to be punishing your patience. Dying during a boss fight means you’ll endure 19 minutes of soul-crushing bullet hell all over again. Enjoy?  You can shuffle energy between your shields and weapons as needed—an idea that sounds great in theory but is a total nightmare in practice. Weapons let you fire homing missiles when you’ve got a charge, and your ray gun (or whatever it’s supposed to be) has a cooldown that depends on your weapon charges. You can even use different weapon configurations based on your charge levels. The first config (which is inconveniently placed on the right side of the upgrade menu—because alphabetical order is clearly overrated) is always active, but the damage doesn’t seem to change with charge levels. If it does, you’ll be hard-pressed to notice.You can collect shield points from enemies to recharge your shields, but if your shield is already full, you don’t get any weapon charge. So you’re stuck constantly shuffling energy back and forth between shields and weapons just to keep up with the demands of the game. On the Steam Deck or a gamepad, this becomes a ridiculous juggling act where you’re pressing five buttons at once—move, aim, fire missiles, transfer energy to weapons, or swap it back to shields. Then there’s the upgrade token system, which is an exercise in futility. Collect energy while your shields are full, and those points turn into upgrade tokens. But die, and you lose them all. It’s not just that you can’t die repeatedly to farm upgrades; it’s that even if you’re playing on easy mode with three lives, your tokens and score reset to zero upon death. You might finish a stage and find yourself with few amount of currency to spend on upgrades. Who thought this convoluted mess was a good idea? The enemy design is hit-or-miss. While some designs are decent, most are poorly executed. You’ll often find yourself overwhelmed by the sheer number of enemies, making it hard to distinguish which ones are actual threats. The enemies tend to target your location or predict where you’ll be, but with the clunky movement controls, dodging attacks feels like an exercise in frustration. You’ll mostly end up just trying to survive while managing the complicated energy system.The game has nice graphics and good visual effects, but the clarity leaves much to be desired. Your ship, the Orca, looks fantastic in the cinematics but is so small and glowy in-game that it’s almost like trying to dodge fireworks. The color patterns and the sheer number of enemies create visual chaos, making it tough to see what's going on and what’s about to hit you.The sound effects are fine, but the music doesn’t quite hit the mark. Aside from the track from the first cinematic, nothing really stood out or stuck with me.Cygni built some hype with its cinematics and a hint of an interesting story. You’re a colonist dealing with rogue robots left by a previous civilization. You harvest them for resources, they wake up, and chaos ensues. The story, however, is a bit of a mess. There’s scant information about the robots, and the main character’s face looks weirdly out of place in the cinematics compared to everything else. We get minimal backstory, and most of it is about the solar system rather than the characters. Cinematics are okay, but they don’t exactly build excitement or engage you before missions.Originally priced at $30, Cygni had been free on the Epic Store. Seems Konami realized the game was less “all guns blazing” and more “all hype deflating” and decided to cut their losses.Unless you snagged it for free from the Epic Store, Cygni – All Guns Blazing isn’t worth the listed price. If you're curious, wait for a bundle or a steep discount (think around $7.50) before giving it a shot.If they update the game mechanics, I might give it another shot with arcade & co-op mode,

_childDocuments_.review: I went into the game unprejudiced, never having heard of Cygni AGB before. Neither did I know about its development history, nor did I read any marketing promises before buying it on a whim... and I had fun.Cygni is not an Arcade Shmup (or Japanese style STG), it is closer to a Computer Shmup or "Euroshmup". Think .Typical for a Computer Shmup among other things Cygni:With these attributes listed, it becomes clear why “core Shmup Fans” may dislike Cygni. It is a different type of shooting game than what would live in an Arcade and that got meticuously balanced around a distilled core mechanic.What the game does not have that would be typical for a Computer Shmup is inertia and a pixel perfect hit detection. There is no stopping inertia and the ship immediately moves as fast or slow as you tilt the analog stick. I find the controls to be a lot of fun. They are more precise and versatile than with an arcade stick. Likewise the hitbox of the player ship strikes me as larger, but not pixel perfect.Still I get it, because I love my , , , , , , , , , , , etc. I am no stranger to Danmaku and will get out my home built Brook based Arcade Stick with Sanwa parts for them.But knowing that Cygni is more of a Computer Shmup than an Arcade Shmup, I don’t care as much about carefully crafted bullet patterns, memorizing the best path, not getting hit or even high scores. The game has gorgeous 3D graphics with a fitting soundtrack and sound design, as well as lots of options to upgrade your ship. Cygni is fast and frantic, sometimes makes you though it through the time it takes to take out extremely bullet spongy ground units, just to go back into a frantic onslaught of airborne enemies. I enjoyed the level designs and found it all diverse enough to not get boring. The graphics and amount on screen was never too much for me and just right to be thrilling.Here is how to play Cygni: Play the Tutorial first, then start on Easy and, while experiencing the game for the first time, collect some currency in passing to upgrade your ship. Then beat the higher difficulties with or without upgrades, that’s up to you.Is it perfect? No. Besides some imperfections in design there can for example be rare stutters (Ultra Settings on a 3080TI with a Ryzen 9) and apparently there are performance issues in high difficulty, which I have not encountered yet myself. But so far nothing has hindered my enjoyment. It is a good Computer Shmup.Is Cygni a casual game or even akin to a mobile game? That’s a loaded and irrelevant question. Here is a better one: Are you having fun with the game? I am. Just like I am having fun with Arcade Shmups, but for different reasons.I am glad Cygni exists, because a decent Computer Shmup makes for something refreshingly different. Just like I might want an orange once in a while after having had apples for a week.Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the price. Don't get hooked by the visuals.The game feels rushed and repetitive. There is a lot of faulty game design overall.Every level is almost 20 minutes long with NO CHECKPOINTS and it consists of almost the same enemy patterns over and over for no reason, and after dying you don't keep any of the currency you gained. Making it really hard to progress for players that are stuck since you can't purchase/upgrade weapons.-Game premise/main feature is getting pick-up drops from enemy kills that regenerate your shields, you can convert shields into missiles by pressing RB and viceversa by pressing LB. You can shot a barrage of missiles with the A button.-Gameplay loop is spamming missiles and quickly converting new pick up shields into missiles after spamming them which literally clears the screen so quickly the game gets boring and you don't even have to dodge any bullets because you are always getting new shields due to the insane amount of drops there are, you just get hit and don't care spamming RB + A.-There is only a total of 7 levels, afterwards you unlock arcade mode that is just a loop of the same 7 levels continuously.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is greatIt's not just a brainless shooter, you have to switch between weapon or shield energy, having more weapon energy allows more special attack, and a full shield offers more points for upgrade laterYou also have to switch between air and ground attacks, and choose a strategy to defeat enemies on bothArt is amazing, background is really alive and blend nicely with foreground, most of the bosses are well integrated too, all of that makes you feel like you are in a real worldSome levels adds a bit of strategy by restricting areas (expect for 6 and 7 which i found a bit more boring), and enemy diversity adds some thinking tooA bit of a downside : the upgrade panel is not very clear, i don't understand what the '50%' means on top of a weapon slot, the weapon sprites you have to unlock on the left are all the same you have to look really closely to see a differenceI would love an 'on hover' information bubble to explain all of itIt could be nice to also have a sandbox to try out the new weapon you just boughtBecause first i didn't understand what weapon pattern i bought, and then i had to figure it ou on a level with everything blasting aroundThere might be too much cinematics, given some of them don't add much to the story, they are visually great thoAll in all it's great, and you have some trophies and scoring system if you like to try hardGo get it

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only giving this a thumbs up because as a shmup gamedev myself I find it incredibly difficult to actually hit that negative review button. Cygni in its current state is simply not worth your time. I did not beat the game at the time of this review, but some of the issues are so apparent from the getgo that I do not feel it's necessary and I honestly just do not have the motivation to play much more of it. If I play more of it and find I was mistaken on some points, or the game gets updated I'll try my best to remember to edit this review.This game had so many eyes on it so it was my hope that it would bring new fans into the genre. If the developers are reading this, please understand I'm sharing these critiques because I want this game to be at least decent. It's hard to make a game and I'm not trying to take a piss all over your hard efforts. I've never had this many friends messaging me about a new shmup asking if it's good or not. There's more people paying attention to this game than any other shmup in the past decade.I looked up the credits to the game and the root of all problems with Cygni became immediately apparent to me. Of the ten people on staff and the nine contractors, only two of them are listed as game designers. Both of which had other roles on the team which I can only imagine were significantly stressful and time consuming endeavors based on the fantastic end results of those elements. As far as I understand, Cygni had no one putting all of their time and effort into the gameplay department. And it shows. It really REALLY shows.There is little to critique in the art and sound department. It's all incredible work. The art style and music aren't to my liking but that's just a personal taste thing. No such thing as right or wrong there. Menus are a bit confusing but I figured them out. That's about it.Already going into it knowing the game takes several hours to complete, I know this will not be a game with the core vision of being a competent arcade-style game. That's fine, there's longer progression based shmups out there and some of them ARE fun despite what genre purists will argue. But even looking at the game through these lens, it is hard to say it's done well.First off, let's talk about the difficulties. There's Easy, Medium and Hard. Pretty standard fare. The game defaults to Medium. I spent about an hour playing stage 1 on Medium, dying and restarting thinking maybe I just wasn't understanding something. It turns out without any upgrades you literally cannot kill some of the enemies and bosses before they time out. Why does the game not only let me play an unwinnable scenario at the beginning, but also DEFAULT to it? Once I switched to Easy I felt like I was playing a real game, and this really feels like the difficulties should be changed to something like "Normal, Hard, and Very Hard" with Hard and Very Hard being unlockables after the player has gotten some ship upgrades.Next, let's talk about how the upgrades work. In the age of roguelites, gachas and Vampire Survivor clones, there is no shortage of games available to study incredibly engaging and addicting progression systems. It should be hard to get this stuff wrong. Cygni requires you to complete a stage in order to receive upgrade currency. This isn't exactly a horrible decision, however the first level took me 17 minutes to finally complete once switching to Easy. So for the first hour or so of playing the game, I made no progress on ship upgrades. And here's when the game gave me the biggest middle finger ever: I didn't even have enough currency to unlock anything. There was a way I was playing that caused this, but it brings to light perhaps the most frustrating design flaw of Cygni:Cygni features a pretty unique mechanic where you can trade shields for firepower, and you can trade firepower for missiles. It's a bit clunky but it is kind of fun to keep filtering the shield pickups into more damage. The way I had the most fun interacting with the game was staying very low on shields and constantly spamming missiles. So here's the thing, the shield pickups are also your upgrade currency. But ONLY if you have your shields maxed out. This is how I cleared stage 1 with no upgrade currency. So understanding this, I now have to make a decision: do I play the game in "action mode" and use all of my tools at my disposal to win? Or do I play the game in "farming mode" and make sure I harvest as many resources as possible so I'm stronger for the next stage? It's not a fun decision to be presented with, and actively encourages the player away from interacting with the most interesting element of Cygni. There's just a complete lack of synergy here.So how are the upgrades once you can finally get them? Honestly pretty underwhelming. It doesn't feel like I'm getting stronger, it feels like I just started with a handicap and slowly get back to a moderate power level. So much so that some of the upgrades are explained in the tutorial before I can even use them. This created a feeling of confusion and disappointment when I tried to use these tools for the first time only to not have access to them. It then also ruined the sense of excitement I would've had from unlocking them.All of that stuff is easily fixable, except for maybe making the upgrades more punchy. Now there's some issues that I'm not sure can be fixed. My biggest personal gripe with this game is the inability to play with an arcade stick. Even Capcom and Namco understand when making a fighting game that part of the fun of a genre born from the arcades is playing on an arcade stick. To many, playing a shmup on a controller feels like playing Guitar Hero on a controller. Sure you can do it but it doesn't feel right. And it's not even the pseudo-twin stick controls that get in the way (although that is a problem and being able to aim with such limits feels pointless). It's the fact that I have to use more than 8 buttons to be able to do everything in the game which means no standard arcade stick will feel good with this game. It just kind of feels disrespectful to the history of the genre, especially when the requirements of a controller or keyboard+mouse doesn't really add much to the game. And coming from a game published by Konami, it feels like a game ashamed of its own legacy when it should be incredibly proud.(word limit reached, continued in comments)

_childDocuments_.review: I went from "I wonder if I should return this" after the first half hour to being glued to my chair and finishing the whole campaign in one sitting. Now that's a dramatic turnaround!At first, Cygni is crazy confusing. There are a bunch of different shot type mechanisms at play, and 100% of the time your screen is absolutely screaming with enemies, bullets, and explosions. It's one of the most chaotic games you'll ever see, so it's really difficult at first to figure out what in the hell is going on and how to best use your different weapons and aiming modes.So, here's the thing: Swallow your pride and knock it down to Easy for now. I know, I know, the horrors. I never play on Easy, it's a thing of pride having played arcade and arcade style games since the 1970s. But once I did, I had a little more leeway to understand and for trial and error. So once I did learn when to use the air gun, when to use the ground gun, when to use lock-on vs. manual aim and so on, the game took off like a rocket and now I'm itching for the harder difficulties. And hey, you get an achievement for beating the campaign on Easy anyway, so why not? Also, once you finish the campaign you unlock the arcade mode, which is a significant portion of the game including leaderboards and persistent ship upgrades.On the downside, the campaign is on the short side and even with an i9 and 4070ti, I had to tinker a bunch to not get frequent framedrops below 60fps (the game's max) at 4K Ultra. For me it was turning off v-sync, MSAA, and turning screen percentage down to 80%. YMMV.Some people might get turned off from Cygni because it doesn't follow the tried and true shmup formula, but the genre could use some new ideas for a change even if not all of them work. It's a wired, white-knuckle experience, the screen constantly on fire with explosions and bullets and hundreds of enemies. If nothing else it's a hell of a spectacle. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: this is a truly terrible shmup game. I still don't think you should get this game.endlessly repeated patterns with little to no variation in long levels that you essentially just strafe your way through without truly trying to avoid bullets (because it's less effective than zooming at top speed and picking up health as you go).The power system to distribute between shield and weapons is useless. You should never have less than full weapon power. If you do, everything becomes exponentially harder and it all falls apart anyway. There is no ebb and flow here like the polarity system in Ikaruga. You are either doing well and NOT USING it. or doing poorly and trying to use it (but it just keeps getting worse if you do)The bosses think the game is a twin stick shooter... but it's not. so half the time you can't even engage with them.The game doesn't explain it's leveling system and how powerups interact with the leveling system. The leveling system using in game power ups to advance fights with the in level economy of shield,weapon, and missile resources.Everytime I try to continue talking about this game, I get more annoyed at how poorly it's executed.

_childDocuments_.review: Any shmup fan can tell you there's a huge difference between classic shmups and bullet hells. Personally, I'm a huge fan of classic shmups, but cannot stand, and I mean CANNOT STAND, bullet hells. Give me Toaplan, Compile, Psikyo, Hudson Soft, Namco, Capcom, Nichibutsu, etc, shmups any day over bullet hells. This game isn't even a bullet hell, it's unbearable. At least bullet hells have patterns that are clear and predictable. The enemies in these game spawn too quick and fire too quickly to possibly manage without being a bullet hell nutjob. I believe it's called insider syndrome, at least that's what I call it. Game developers play their game thousands of hours, thinking they've made a good game, not realizing that anyone else without thousands of hours of experience will not have a good time. Like, at all.I can't stand this game. You're just pummeled with bullets nonstop, it makes no sense. And it has the same flaw that makes dariusburst so boring, namely giving you thousands of repetitive tiny popcorn enemies that serve no purpose but to make the game superficially appear more exciting. It's not exciting to shoot thousands of popcorn that just scroll by, it's boring and repetitive. I really wanted to enjoy this game (and maybe I will, years down the line, and have a change of heart and enjoy it, it wouldn't be the first time a game has done a 180 for me) because of the modern graphics, but it's just not fun at all. It's overly complicated and hectic. I'd play any classic 80s or 90s shmup over this any day of the week.

_childDocuments_.review: Cygni is a latest iteration in modern day shump genre that really did a lot in the visual department. At a glance it looks amazing. The graphics is fantastic to say the least but does the gameplay live up to it?Well gameplay is very fast and fluid but sometimes feels a bit too rushed. Every second you spend in the game even on easy difficulty feels like you are here to dodge shower of bullets from every angle feasible. It's chaotic and for the most part very good for those who wants to train their not-so-great reflex once more in this genre. Having played a lot of old school and amazing classic shumps and modern ones, I found it to be lacking in something. It could be that somehow the fluid fast movement and combat might be too much for me but I've experienced similar games prior and they felt fine. Something about the overall interaction with the enemy and synergy in combat feels a bit off. Either way, if you love this genre, it's a must have. I can break it down more but let's just sum up the overall experience.+ Fantastic graphics. Devs outdid themselves by making it really pleasing to the eyes. + Game got that switch power to shield or weapon system that gives you the choice of defense vs offense. + You collect powerup (only one type) to boost your energy. At full energy the power goes toward your upgrade points for later use for upgrades.+ Decent amount of upgrades.+ Coop+ Lots of graphical and control options. K&M works just as good as controller for this one. + Physical copy is available for console version too.+ A$$ of your protagonist. + A new standard of quality that should be a benchmark for other upcoming shump games of this style of graphics. Now the bad:- A$$. Let me elaborate. Why would the devs put a fancy intro CG cinematic with a nice music and even show her back but it has nothing to do with the story or gameplay mechanics? The game has practically no story whatsoever. So why they spent so much time showing her, the beautiful cockpit, and yet nothing else is shown later on during the gameplay? - Music is meh overall. Intro music is kinda nice. Game sound is good but as generic as you would expect. Nothing fancy but nothing bad either.- You have only ONE upgrade to pick up during mission. Why not have multiple upgrades that give your ship new power-ups for mission only; while having the aforementioned extra ones added for permanent upgrades? This would give this game a bit of a roguelike/lite vibe and also add depths to the already chaotic combat.- Weapons lack varieties. Don't get me wrong, the ones that are available are more than enough. You have lock on, ground attack, and capability to aim your shots in different directions, but the overall visual kind of wear off after long play time. Again, many shump have simple gun system. Nothing wrong with that. For a fancy looking game like this however, it's a missed opportunity to not have many different types of weaponry. Remember Raptor: Call of Shadows? Imagine that game in this graphics. That one had multiple different types of ground based weapons let alone air based ones. Heck, the game itself is called Cygni: ALL GUNS BLAZING. All guns...Now the weird part:// This game will be going free to own on Epic store in a few days. As of writing this review (Aug 5th, 2024) it should be 2-3 days from now on Epic store's weekly game rotation. Why would you give this game free on Epic but not on Steam? I bought it from third party sites just to own it on Steam but is this fair that it's free on one platform while not so in other?// This game had a lot of opportunity to reinvent the wheel of shump by adding more style and unique gameplay mechanics. Powarumi or similar shump where power is used to gain health or shield vs dmg is done here but in a different way. Not bad but nothing unique. For an eye pleasing game like this, they could've gone with a bit more character developments. Maybe you take her out of the craft, then go on foot for some shoot em up (top down style)? Or have some chatter where you get an exposition of background story? Either way, if you want to pick it up for free, then you may wait a few days. I for one would rather pay for it and have it on steam than on Epic store. So the choice is yours. If you like this game, support the devs. Leave some comments and give them ideas. Maybe their next game will be more elaborate on overall presentation than just on visual department. Weighing it all down though, I have given it a thumbs up. It's not bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Very odd schmup as far as they go. Beautiful presentation. Feel wise however, it's sloppy. The ship has a very high max speed. This can trivialize some mechanics, yet make some things which should be easy difficult (i.e. navigating tight spaces). It just doesn't seem geared towards making the player feel like they are in control. Generous health pool makes the game less about perfect bullet navigation and more about refilling shield meter as quickly as possible to keep up with all the chaos. Then it's about how much shield meter you want to risk for damage. Again it looks incredible, and I would probably gladly enjoy the visual feast if the levels weren't so dang long. Trash + Boss should be a level, but they have multiple bosses per level. Just makes the game drag on. Since the bullet patterns dont matter as much, I think the levels need to be shorter and more concise. I could really enjoy this in small bites, but it won't let me do that.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to address some points I see prompting users to thumbs down, which is cool (that's like their opinion, man), but I see "short game" "long stages" a lot and it's true but context is key. I've never met a shmup fan that played these games just to beat it and walk away? These are score attack games. Leaderboards, challenging yourself to do better. Score higher, get hit less. You beat it on easy, so upgrade your ship, you get back out there until you can beat it on hard and then you start beating your high scores. As I state in my original short review, I'd have designed some checkpoints personally, but the long stages I found gave it a sense of scale, and they're just so beautiful. I picked this up on xbox too for some couch co-op and I'm having no trouble repeating missions for currency for upgrades and higher scores. If you liked Ikaruga, this gives me the sense I'm playing something spiritually connected to Ikaruga. It's not a shmup masterpiece like Ikaruga, but it's really solid and it's really fun. So if you like shmups, check this out. If you're looking for a sweeping 40 hour epic story, hit the bricks - not that kind of game. But as a high production value shmup, I'd argue it's pretty, pretty, good. Also, well worth $30. To me it's well crafted enough I consider it a value at that price.This isn't flawless, but I'm just a bit beside myself to see it at mixed rating since I've personally found it so enjoyable. To each his own I suppose. <3 Original:Wow, tough but rewarding. Cool patterns, cool bosses, beautiful graphics. I wouldn't mind check points in the levels but I can't complain, it's a ton of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This ain't it chief. It simply isn't well designed. Below is some text with my thoughts and after that is a numbered list of things I believe this game can change to actually become good. Also as you have seen the graphics are quite good and doesn't really need any changes except in the visibility department. Here are some issues;Bullet sponge enemies, no variety in weapons or mechanics like a shot limit (for example) allowing for skill expression in combat. Controls really badly, has both acceleration and what seems to be a difference in speed between dpad/left stick, I assume this is due to diagonal movement being faster which is also.........a weird design decision.Like I'm not even saying the game is too easy but because the movement is not precise enough to ALLOW you to be good at it, it's simply not engaging on easy nor hard. Being able to take multiple hits instead of the traditional "one hit KO" is also not necessarily bad but it's used as an excuse for doing things that would not fly in another shmup.Because shmups generally are very punishing that means faults in balancing are usually very apparent and damning, especially with a one hit KO. Cygni has bad bullet visibility quite frequently, they are often too small and hide against the background or inside other attacks. Some attacks also seem balanced around the fact that you're supposed to be hit? Even if you have a health system the problem with this is it's not very fun.Here is what can be done to make this game good:1. Fix the movement, acceleration needs to go (you can add visual "fake" acceleration with animation, many shmups do this) and you need to make sure the ship moves at a constant speed (again, probably something to do with diagonals). Left stick and D-pad need to control the same.2: Gameplay need to be more interesting, either add a shot-limit or some other bonus for being aggressive, another alternate weapon which changes up your style of play (think DDP laser, Zeroranger sword or Gunvein charged bomb)3. Bullet visibility needs tweaking.4. Levels need to be more interesting, remove uninsteresting patterns and replace them with more interesting, harder patterns that are more fun to dodge (no just spamming ant sized bullets on the screen to make your shield get hit). Preferably add more enemy types as well.5. I honestly think the player ship needs to be a bit bigger, I get it's a scale thing but there's just so much empty space. I really feel this game would benifit from LESS screen real-estate.6. Pickups need to go straight to missles if you have full shields, it not doing this already is just tedious and janky.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Michael Bay style explosions and games with all style, but no substance nor balance? CYGNI: All Guns Blazing is for you. If you enjoy games like Ikaruga, ESP Ra.De, Swordship, Astebreed, then you need to stay as far away from this game as possible, unless you enjoy laughing at how bad the gameplay designs are.Seriously, KONAMI, the dev/pub who gave us pivotal shmups such as Scramble, TwinBee, Gradius and Axelay, actually approved a shmup with absolutely zero gameplay balance in the year 2024. Having beaten the game on Epic after about 2 hours (can't leave a review there), the game has nearly zero redeemable qualities. What it does do well are:- Explosions- Graphics in general- Audio- Realistic-looking cinematography- Giving the player options on how to attack the enemy.What it does wrong (in no particular order):- Mission time (average playtime for most missions is around 8 minutes, should be 2-5, no more).- Amount of enemies thrown at you at any given time is in the dozens, if not hundreds. Makes you pointlessly choose between killing things here or there just to get the same shield drops, regardless.- Enemy bullet patterns are on the level of a bullet hell, but bullet hells are expected to have *thought* put into the pattern designs. This is just pure randomness thrown at you.- I mentioned shield drops and weapon options. You have a five point shield and a five point missile system which are intertwined. Every item drop adds a point to your shield and you can redirect them to missiles for extra DPS, but since there are so many bullets firing at you even on Easy, you probably won't want to redirect anything away from shields. I say that knowing full well I mentioned ESP Ra.De because ESP at least makes it feel like you have options for clearing out bullets. Also, don't give the player hit points in a shmup; that's inherently bad design on multiple levels, even after I mentioned Astebreed, because that game's overall design allows their shield system to be forgivable. Anyway, sometimes, I'm just sitting there not moving with my finger resting on the fire button waiting for the game to give me a reason to move (I get enough shield drops to be able to afford tanking, let that sink in for a minute).- As for the weapon options, you need to buy them between missions, but the currency is obtained only by having full shields, then picking up more shield drops. These extra drops automatically get added to your currency, but you must finish the mission first AND if you want to retain all of these drops from the beginning of the mission, then you cannot die. Good job on the casual accessibility front there; even soulslikes are more forgiving. - Speaking of dying, I said most missions average 8 minutes. If you play on Normal or Hard, you get a single life and must restart if you die. Easy gives you three lives. Considering the frustration in needing to tank through wave after wave of enemies for that long and as they overwhelm you even when you're just sitting there hammering the fire button, three lives should be the default.- The upgrades themselves don't feel like much of a difference and I didn't even unlock the third weapon until the penultimate mission (primary and missiles are available at start). I earned enough to unlock a fourth weapon as well, but that was after I beat the final boss.- Btw, the final boss didn't even feel like a final boss; just felt like any other boss in the game.- Arcade mode seems almost identical to Story mode, except with everything unlocked, BUT you can't even equip everything (you get enough to equip most, though). You also unlock Arcade after beating Story, would've been nice if it was on a per mission basis.- Last damning point: Missions 1 (first) and 7 (last) last a whopping 17 minutes each! 2-6 are the ones that average 8 minutes. Also, Mission 1 is the only one with three bosses, which is a really weird way to start; everything else has just one.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I've only played about 5 hours at this point, and mostly on Easy, and some on Medium, and no co-op yet.I only got this game a day or two ago, but already put 5 hours into it. That's a lot, for me, these days. Especially for a game this intense, visually, as my eyes are getting old and don't like the craziness too much. But for some reason, this game isn't a problem for me, in that regard. I find myself longing to play another round when I'm not playing, which is a really good sign.My love of shmups goes back to TurboGrafx-16, especially Blazing Lazers. I'd love for a modern reboot of that, but Cygni reminds me of it in some ways. Maybe because I'm just picky about my shmups, and these are two of the few that I have fallen in love with over the years. So many exist, yet so many just don't get things right - the ship is too fast, the ship is too slow, the levels are too long, the enemies are too hard, there is no progression, etc. The few that do it right for me, do it really right, and Cygni is nearly perfect in that regard. Even the lauded Ikaruga, which I still own the GameCube disc of, didn't really do much for me, though I would name it as one of the better vertical shmups I've played.The mechanics used in the game are interesting, as they keep you on your toes and give you interesting choices. Do you move your energy into your weapons to make them stronger and risk your shields? Do you keep your shields maxed at all times and collect upgrade points? Do you fire missiles which uses up a weapon energy point? What fire patterns do you want to use? How will you spend your upgrade points? And so on. It's just exactly the kind of stuff that I love. I do think the game's tutorial didn't communicate certain things to me very effectively, and in the heat of the moment, it can be hard to tell what's going on - specifically I'm thinking of how long it took me to realize that picking up energy points would never fill into the weapon side automatically, and that they would convert to currency to spend on upgrades only if my shield was full. But once I figured that out, it added that extra level of choices to my runs.At the end of the day, this is a refreshing game. It's been a long time since I have found a vertical-scrolling shmup that has had this level of polish and care put into it, AND embraces the widescreen format. So many shmups resort to blocking off two-thirds of the screen or are designed as a horizontal-scrolling shmup, and both of those things annoy me. This game is beautiful, and goes right to the edge of my screen. And, it's fun. It's challenging at the higher difficulties. It's go co-op, which I haven't tried yet. It's got upgrades and customization. It's great. Well-deserving of my money!

A lot of the erratic and more complex enemy attacks feel insanely fast, but would be easier to dodge if I could move much slower on demand. _childDocuments_.review: CYGNI: All Guns Blazing is an absolute blast. This twin-stick shooter is a breath of fresh air in a genre often dominated by nostalgia. It masterfully blends classic arcade gameplay with stunning modern visuals and audio.I recommend watching my full in-depth review to learn more about the game and my thoughts:From the moment you take control of your Orca spaceship, you're immersed in an adrenaline-fueled battle against alien hordes. The core gameplay loop of flying, shooting, and surviving is simple yet incredibly satisfying. The strategic element of power allocation between weapons and shields adds depth, forcing split-second decisions in the heat of combat.The game's visual and auditory presentation is nothing short of breathtaking. The detailed art style, coupled with the full orchestral score and immersive sound design, create a truly cinematic experience. It's like being inside a high-octane action movie.While the campaign offers a solid challenge with diverse stages and boss fights, the game truly shines in arcade mode. The focus on high scores and global leaderboards encourages mastery and replayability. The absence of power-ups forces players to rely on skill and strategic thinking, adding a rewarding layer of depth.Unfortunately, the game's relatively short campaign and limited weapon variety can leave players wanting more. Additionally, some boss encounters feel slightly underwhelming compared to the intense regular gameplay. Other than that some poor onboarding, lack of information for the upgrade screen, relatively long sessions per run, lack of combat dynamics that some would like, and no online co-op at launch might disappoint some players.Despite these drawbacks, CYGNI: All Guns Blazing is a remarkable achievement. It captures the essence of classic arcade shooters while elevating them to new heights. If you're a fan of the genre or simply looking for an exhilarating action game, I wholeheartedly recommend giving CYGNI a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: There are some weird design choices and the basic mechanics are rather unintuitive, but overall it's a decent game. Beginners Advice:Don't expect a Cave-Style shmup. You can't dodge every bullet, you will get hit ALOT and that's ok. Once you accept that, easy mode is indeed easy, cause enemies drop shield power ups like candy. Focus on destroying with some dodging on the side.Weapon loadout: Unlock the widest shot asap (upgrade screen, top left menu), set your loadout (upgrade screen, middle menu) to alternate between straight shot and widest shot. This way you can switch between the modes by pressing X (360 gamepad). Alternatively, use a medium wide shot on all slots.Shield Management: Your weapon energy (red slots around ship) does nothing for your weapon power (yep, it's weird), these are just the weapon slots you've set up in the upgrade menu. So, use them as additional energy shield. If your energy shield slots are full, transfer energy to your weapon slots before you pick up shield energy, or transfer it back, if you're low on shield.Start with easy mode! Every upgrade you get for your ship transfers over between modes, so it's just masochistic to play medium unupgraded. You can also play missions multiple times to save up energy for upgrades.Don't get discouraged by the first level, it's one of the longest in the game and the only one with three bosses (again, weird..).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty solid modernisation of the shooter, not without its rough spots. For example, the music feels completely disconnected to the gameplay. Sometimes, I want to shut off the music completely as it is tone-deaf to the game's presentation.Secondly, the game relying you to upgrade your ship as you play through the campaign is a bit meh, it means the missions feel a bit samey as you go through, because you aren't powering up as you play. You collect energy to use your systems, but those systems stay the same. Furthermore the upgrades are expensive, which prevents experimentation as you upgrade. You're forced to spend you currency without being able to make an informed choice.Third, the encounter design can be bland when it decides to throw hundreds of enemies at you at once. Especially ones that spawn in on screen. Other shooters gave you mechanics to blow up enemy spawners to make the situation more manageable. Cygni doesn't seem to.However, the level design can be quite good, requiring you to switch between attacking the ground and attacking the sky. It's a fun addition that requires you to actually pay attention to what is going on in the world of the game. When the screen isn't 100% full of enemies, it's actually quite cool.The boss design feels quite good as well. Some harken back to more obscure entries in the classic shooter space. If you're a fan of classic Konami shooters, then I'd recommend you pick up Cygni.

_childDocuments_.review: I refunded this crap about 10 minutes ago, this game is a trainwreck.  For starters this game sounds like an opera.  I think they were going for an epic sounding soundtrack but somewhere along the line they turned the soundtrack into something that sounds like an opera.  The explosions and the weapons sound great, I'll give them that, firing your weapons and something blowing up is very satisfying in this game.  But when I'm playing a SHMUP I don't want to think I'm in an opera hall.  I can tell this is a EuroSHMUP because two of the usual problems with EuroSHMUPS are present in this game: the bosses take way too many hits, and you can't tell what is in the air and what is on the ground.  When you make a game where you have air targets and ground targets you better make sure the player can tell what is in the air and what is on the ground, look at the Rayforce games for examples of where this is done right.  This game is too hard for all the wrong reasons, there is no way to micro-manage everything going on with your ship with the number of bullets and enemies coming at you.  You have to be able to operate 8 buttons while operating two analog sticks.  There is NO WAY you can do that without 4 hands.  You don't want to have to remember what is on each of the 8 buttons in the middle of a SHMUP.  That is NOT the genre to have a game where every button is used and it does something different.  You have to micro-manage a shield/weapon powerup system, 8 buttons, and two analog sticks.  Good luck to you.  The lock-on system is broken.  Every time you try to lock on to an enemy you end up locked on to an enemy you don't want to shoot.  If you turn off homing, reposition the right analog stick to aim at the enemy you want to shoot and fire, it just goes back to the last enemy instead (the one you didn't want to shoot but somehow ended up locked on to that enemy anyway.)  I really wanted to like this game.  I was so excited for it when I saw the first trailer.  Now that the game is out, all I've found is disappointment and frustration over a game that looks fantastic, but sadly is unplayable with the micro-managing of your ship and way too many buttons to keep track of and operate at the same time along with two analog sticks.  These people should have looked to Nex Machina, and Never Awake for inspiration (THAT is how you do a SHMUP or a twin-stick-shooter.)  Those are great games, Cygni is a pile of hot garbage and is definitely NOT worth $30.00.  Avoid at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: Controller/mechanics are Over designedI played about an hour and a half the game and during that time I spent almost 30 minutes trying to figure out the controller actions. It feels unpolished as there are duplicated actions in different buttons that could perfectly be used for other useful actions, for example:- For arcade mode: instead of using a specific loadout from the beginning, make the sub-bosses to drop the upgrades to have a motivation in killing them. If a player missed a sub-boss they miss an upgrade. This will make the arcade mode more competitive and not monotonous without upgrades during the entire run.- Movement insanely fast, you can't dodge anything with precision with all the bullets in the screen. There is no micro-dodge.- Some upgrades can be replaced to solve the above issue: The fire rate upgrade can just be removed and just add a focus shot for both air and ground weapons that increments the fire rate but reduce the ship movement speed. This will allow the players to micro-dodge and shoot bosses between the lasers.- Primary and secondary fire? Why are those actions needed if you can assign each weapon independently. Air weapon, ground weapon, missiles and raylight.- Shield blast: A button for this action is wasted as you already have a button to route energy to your shield which can be held to activate it? If the energy assignment mechanic is changed (based on the point below), this button can be kept- The shield/weapon mechanic is over designed given all the things that are happening in the screen the player need to be worried to assign energy to fire missiles and that's annoying more than interesting. Just use a single energy bar for both life/missiles (similar way as in F-Zero) that depletes when the player fires missiles and the player need to manage it. The same bar can be used for the fire patterns, for each level that is filled the fire pattern will change forcing the player to prioritize the fire pattern over using missiles in the same way it is intended but without the annoyance of routing the energy.- Finally, with all the above simplifications. Add a button to change targets when using the ground weapon. This will be really appreciated by arcade controller users.The game looks great but the controller and mechanics are over designed.Devs are taking feedback so kudos to them. Hopefully the gameplay will be improved soon.

_childDocuments_.review: was a ****post review but ill actually review it now.Hard to tell if the game is actually good or not. I feel like it was a mistake on the developers part, by making a game with such high production value as their debut title. Cygni is beautiful, sounds amazing. I'm used to hectic music from Japanese shmups, but Cygni's orchestral soundtrack won me over.But, and this is a really big but, the game lacks many common sense design choices from other games of the genre. - No slowdown button, you have to rely on stick sensitivity. This is new, and doesn't work that well. I end up gripping my controller like I'm trying to strangle it, not fun. Moving the stick a millimeter is the difference between snail and nascar speed.- Depressingly bad bullet visibility. Explosions are orange, most bullets are orange. Bullets don't render over explosions. Combined with a fast bullet speed, you will get shotgunned by patterns you can't see. Bullets can hide in other bullets. The first miniboss has bullets that blend into its laser, and will slide out and jumpscare you.- No miniboss timer. You cannot tell when a miniboss will end until they unceremoniously float to the side of the screen like a pool toy. there really should be a timer. please. (this is probably a skill issue but whatever)I honestly enjoyed this game regardless but its honestly puzzling why so many of these features were not implemented. It feels like the game had a small amount of playtesters, or the developers did not listen to them.Do you like Sine Mora? are you new to the genre? play this game.Are you used to japanese arcade stg's made by cave or treasure? play those instead.but as euroshmups go, this is without a doubt the best one ever made. But that means its fairly average to most sweaty redditor japanese stg fans such as myself.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about it looks amazing and feels very responsive. It is a visual treat. If you're into nostalgic top down arcade shooters like ikaruga, then you'll love this. However, with that being said I cannot recommend this game simple for this one reason. It maxes out at 60fps. That is a incredibly and dastardly sin against very fast action games such as these. Unforgivable. 60fps should be for ultra maxed out 4k settings on RPG's. 120fps, 240fps, and 480fps are for games like these with 120 being the minimum acceptable standard.
_childDocuments_.name: CYGNI: All Guns Blazing

_childDocuments_.review: I would consider myself a top down shooter guru.  I literally love them.  That being said yes this isn't an easy game if you don't come in humble you'll lose.  If you don't understand the controls, you'll lose. If you don't understand the mechanics you'll definitely lose. The music is good in my opinion and the graphics are a lot but you have to know what you are looking for and how the enemies are attacking you.  Long story short I think this is an underrated game and people judged harshly because the suck (skill issue).  I recommend this game to seasoned bullet hell players for a fun yet difficult game. I believe in Konami and support their games.

_childDocuments_.review: 20GB is an insane install size for a shmup. I really don't need shmups to look that fancy, when the cost is the disk space for  similar games.Now, that said, I have enjoyed shmups for as long as there have been shmups, and I like to see devs bring ideas to the table and experiment with potentials in the shmup space, rather than the often oppressive design conservatism that one commonly hears from shmup fans. I've seen the Cygni dev write and respond about the game, and it's clear a pleasing amount of thought and design consideration was put into this even though it comes across very differently from the expected norm for the space, and there's credit to what it does, even if we'll see many people write it off for going against the grain.There's definitely fun to be had here if one spends time with it (and it does take some time in easy difficulty to get used to how it plays as well as check off some small upgrade boxes, like ground damage actually being useful, so keep that in mind, or the "Konami code" will skip the unlock grinding). Pricey for a shmup and the install size is ridiculous, but if you picked it up for free, don't miss out on playing it :)

_childDocuments_.review: So far, Lots of fun. Spirit of an old school bullet hell game like Raiden but updated visuals, effects, and strategy. The bosses are interesting and early on at least it's a great time replaying missions to learn the level layouts and be more effective. Lots of replay-ability here. The weapons are effective and kills are satisfying as hell. Bosses are fun and strategic without being painful. Very good balance right now, upgrade system looks like it might leave a lot to be desired after a lot of play but I expect that may change as time goes on. This game is still young! Worth the price and some time if you're a fan of these kinds of games. Shoutout to Falcon @Gameranx for putting me onto this one

_childDocuments_.review:
An unrelenting onslaught of eye-popping visuals, ear bursting soundscapes and mind-melting action makes CYGNI the vanguard for the next generation of Shoot-em Ups.

Outgunned and outmanned, plunge into a sky teeming with danger in a last-ditch battle for survival. Choose to route power between weapons or shield systems and go up against unrelenting waves of ground and aerial enemies. Upgrade your ship by picking up new tech and take down colossal alien bosses in visceral combat; do whatever it takes to survive.

CYGNI is an exhilarating space shooter elevating the genre to a truly next-generation experience.

name: Farming Simulator 22
detailed_description: Take on the role of a modern farmer! Agriculture, animal husbandry and forestry offer a huge variety of farming activities while you face the challenges of the four seasons, especially when winter sets in. Creatively build your own farm and extend your farming operations with production chains - forming an agricultural empire! Even run your farm together with friends and enjoy crossplatform multiplayer together. Whether you create a lush vineyard or an olive orchard in the Mediterranean south of France, a vast farmland full of wheat, corn, potatoes and cotton in the US-Midwest or a lively animal farm in the hilly landscape of the European Alpine region: More than 400 machines and tools from over 100 real agricultural brands like Case IH, CLAAS, Fendt, John Deere, Massey Ferguson, New Holland, Valtra and many more are available for your farm. Farming Simulator 22 brings a multitude of new gameplay features and offers more content and player freedom than ever before, including new ground working features like mulching or stone picking, an improved build-mode adding greenhouses and beehives, as well as a new character creator to bring your own, individual farmer to life. A large variety of free community-created modifications, officially tested by the developer GIANTS Software, will extend your farming experience many times over. Rise to the challenges of becoming a successful farmer, start farming and let the good times grow!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Absolutely fantastic game. Takes all of the best elements of FS19 and massively upgrades them. The helper system has received a much needed rework which helps with transport, reducing the unnecessary grind, and makes solo play actually enjoyable. The new basic map is very immersive and well laid out. The auction house is also a great feature which improves the immersion and helps you get started early game.Cons: I've noticed a couple of bugs here and there, mainly with trying to return leased items, but nothing game breaking. The helper system still needs some minor tweaks to help them deal with non-rectangular fields.Conclusion: Very much recommend, I can see myself investing many more hours in this therapeutic game.

_childDocuments_.review: "Yeah... I was a gamer...." When I first heard of Farming Simulator and watched the trailer, I thought "Really? How could THAT be fun?" I already work on a dairy and crop farm, so I didn't understand why it would be fun to play a game based on that. Man, was I wrong!FS22 quickly became one of my favourite games in my library, and continues to be to this day.So, if you think this would be to easy or chill, you're wrong. Chill, yes, but easy? No way! It takes so much effort, decision making, and perseverance (I speak from experience!) to be a farmer. In the words of the trailer again, "Farming is easy, mastering it is a challenge."It totally exceeded my expectations and is a (almost) completely accurate look into the lives of us farm hands, equipment operators, problem-solvers and just farmers in general!Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Dec 2023 Update - I'm over the summer sale fiasco, changed recommendation back to "yes" - this is my therapy :)edit - It now appears that there is a "complete your collection" bundle, which offers a degree of savings to those who purchased the base game prior to the announcement of the premium edition / 2023 summer sale. Still think this was more likely a reflexive response to community reaction vice deliberate planning though...and if it was the latter, that's probably worse (imo)...TL;DR - Since I paid (near) full price for the base game around launch, I'm not able to benefit from the current sale...  Nor the previous one when the Platinum Edition was released...  See the pattern emerging?I really want to write good things about this game, having been with the franchise since FS15.  While I have not subscribed to the new season pass model (I despise it, personally, and several of the DLC are either highly niche or functionally repaints of existing elements in game), I have enjoyed the updated gameplay, new production chains, maps and especially the FS22 Platinum Expansion (I like logging, I find it fun!). However, the increasingly aggressive monetization and what feels like increasingly frequent hollow/empty promises is slowly killing the game for me (sadly).The 2023 Summer Sale is just a giant slap in the face to long-term supporters. This is the opportune time to pick up the game if you are new - you can get the base game AND both season passes (functionally, almost everything released and planned at this time, look for the "Farming Simulator 22: Premium Edition" bundle) for roughly the same price as we who already bought the game (and supported the developer!) have to pay for ONE of the season passes... Not even a discounted "Complete your Collection"-style bundle made available, nor are any of the season passes or DLC on sale individually (except the recently announced Premium Expansion, which has a fairly typical 10% PRE-release discount).  I fully support monetization of DLCs in this franchise (they have a steady pacing of releases, some of which are free), but the overall value seems to be decreasing - and so to has the frequency and scale of sales. There is also the highly controversial Kubota Pack, which is required for multiplayer passenger capability - something modders have provided in previous iterations for free, could have (and seriously, should have) been included in the base game has now been functionally paywalled. Come on, Giants - you used to be one of the developers that others were compared against. Maybe your publisher has gotten too greedy? It's not too late...

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Okay have quite a few more hours in and..I just can't recommend this game without two critical mods from FS19 are available for FS22 (which I know one of them is being worked on).  AI is horrible.  I have to manually do most things for the AI.  Same issues in FS19 are in FS22. GO-TO is the only reliable new feature.  Load and Deliver you're lucky if you get it to work. Most of the time you have to load the trailer yourself then it will go deliver but then it gets lost on going to load again and just stays there not knowing how to go fill again.  Even more bugs are showing their heads as I have played more. Like palettes getting stuck in the ground and have to ram them over and over to try to free them or edit a file. This has caused me much headache.  Also, there has been no patches at all trying to fix the issues that are showing up more and more.  -----------------------------------------------------------So, i've played this game for about 3 hours to make sure I understood the entire workings the best I could.  Summary is, wait till the mod community fixes what this should have been.  I wish there was a middle ground between yes and no as I don't think its a hard no but definitely not a yes yet.I have almost 1000 hours on FS19 and loved it.  It had its issues that FS22 I was hoping to solve, and for some of the issues FS22 succeeded at.Graphics:  Yep much much better and have had zero issues. I run it with FidelityFX on it's setting for quality not performance and it looks amazing.  I have had no stutters etc.  I'm not really worried about FPS with the base maps. I'm sure down the road that will be something I'll look into.AI Helpers - Oh I sooo was hoping this would eliminate the need for the two mods that made FS19 sooo much better.  But alas no, AI is still the basic it was in FS19, plus some shiney added to it to hide the fact they will still ram a fence and waste all your product as they spin tires thinking they can still go forward or just ram into each other and scratch their heads (two different fields).   It is better then the default FS19 though.  You can at least loop them to sell your stuff, once you understand how the helper menu works that is. You still can't have the AI unload a combine :(. Don't get me started on trying to have them drive to a field and HOPE you set your waypoint far enough into the field where you don't get "field not found" message when your tractor is on the field. Oh, and plowing...yeah have fun with that if the plow rotates sides.  Their driving on the main roads I've never had an issue with, big plus there! AI Traffic will even stop for them.  I'm hoping the modding community will bring to FS22 the two epic helper programs. Once those are added will be a big improvement. Production - YAY!  I don't have to use a mod anymore.  BOO - you have to buy the buildings and when you start no way you can afford from scratch to buy all the production buildings. Great feature that I look forward to utilizing more. Though I did do some rough math and am wondering if some of them are really more profitable. I would like to have had them add the production chain picture they posted into the game though, would help greatly someone new to the game know what productions can do and need without having to buy each place. Base maps - Well they are base maps, play which one you like until more are added by the community. They are beautiful maps, very well done. Even if you feel like you're in the middle of town on the US map with super tiny fields. :).For those that say there isn't as much stuff as FS19, well of course there isn't.  It's a brand new game!  Be patient.  As for the pay us for black beauty or the mac skin - yeah don't like that one bit. Those should be free if you have a seasons pass at the very least.  Way to try to money grab with micro transactions hidden as something else.Summary - Beautiful game and will be amazing once bugs are worked out and the modding community gets a hold of it.  Once that happens buy it. For now, up to you but I would say wait.
