_childDocuments_.review: Having never farmed a day in my life I can't say how realistic it is. It seems pretty convincing to me, but when is a game too realistic? Is this even a game? To me this is like Desert Bus, it takes realism to the extreme and it's not trying to be fun. Of course that was a joke game and this is serious.I get that a lot of people like it, I love sims too but this just takes it too far. If farming in real-time and endlessly driving over the same fields is what you want in a game or if you want the best farming sandbox ever made you'll love this, but it's not for everyone. For me it got better after I adjusted settings and installed some mods to take away some of the realism and combine some of steps to relive the tedium.It seems like all the You tubers do the same thing, it's almost like the entire community silently agrees that this game is unplayable without some mods for all but the most hard core. I played 85 hours and barely scratched the surface, started trying mods about half way through and eventually got bored/frustrated enough with it that I rage uninstalled.I'm still giving it a thumbs up because most of what is there is done well. Maybe too well. A story mode that both teaches you how to farm and gives some sort of progression would have really helped I think. It's a great simulator, they just forgot to include the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Farming Simulator 22

_childDocuments_.review: to the people complaining about it being the same as fs19.. yes, it is the same. you are still a farmer and you farm. the gameplay has not changed. it has just been prettyfied.there are some quality of life changes and some are said to be but aren't.also some things feel like the devs just plugged in the most popular mods.and that's fine. it works.the ui takes some getting used to, and with that i mean the menu's. the one with all the prices on it no longer is all that easy to compare prices with because you now only display the prices for a single crop. so much switching back and forth.but then there's a tab in the shop where you have everything under crop type and you have a sort of shopping list for farm equipment. so it's not all bad.though sometimes my controller stops working and i have to click stuff with my mouse.the crop draw distance is still meh, but other than that it looks fine.just waiting on my favorite mods to port over and we are set.all in all not bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics and Visuals: The game's graphics have seen a noticeable improvement, offering more detailed and realistic environments, crops, and machinery. The enhanced visuals contribute significantly to the immersion of the farming experience.New Crops and Activities: The inclusion of new crops and activities, such as grapes, olives, and greenhouse farming, adds depth and variety to the gameplay. It diversifies the farming experience and offers more options for players to explore.Improved AI and NPCs: The AI behavior for workers and NPCs seems to have been refined, making it more efficient and responsive. This enhances the overall gameplay by providing better assistance and making the game world feel more alive.Machinery and Equipment: The addition of new machinery and equipment is fantastic, providing a broader range of options for players to manage their farms efficiently. The customization options and detailed machinery models are a significant plus.Modding Support: Farming Simulator has always had a vibrant modding community, and FS22 continues to support mods, allowing players to expand and customize their gameplay experience. However, ensuring seamless integration and compatibility for mods could further enhance the game.Tutorials and Learning Curve: While the game caters well to experienced players, a more comprehensive tutorial or guidance system might benefit newcomers. Farming Simulator can be quite complex, and a more intuitive learning curve could make it more accessible to beginners.Multiplayer Experience: The multiplayer aspect of the game has been improved, but there might be room for further enhancements in terms of connectivity, stability, and additional features to encourage cooperative gameplay.Overall, Farming Simulator 22 has made significant strides in improving various aspects of the game. However, there's always room for refinement and innovation in future updates to continue enhancing the farming simulation experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Although there is potential, I do not like this game as well as FS19 or earlier versions of FS.  I find the pace too slow.  The Seasons mechanism slows things down too much in my opinion.  Although you can fix a certain time of year (turning seasons off in effect), there are still so many growth stages for crops, that it takes many sessions of game play to reach the point of harvest.  This is not adjustable.  In addition, the price fluctuations still follow the pattern of seasonal patterns.  These factors, in effect, force the slow pace of game play.  Although there are still many options of contract work, the small payment for these contracts, especially if you need to lease equipment, makes it hardly worthwhile.  The maintenance cost on your owned equipment is also too high.  One fields use of a new harvester can result in one to two thousand dollars.  Considering depreciation, it is legitimate that there are maintenance costs, but generally smaller than what the game allows.  Before buying FS22, consider what you enjoy.  If seasonal variations in farming and a very slow pace is what you enjoy, go for it.  Otherwise you may do better with one of the earlier versions and get seasons from a mod.

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle with leaving a negative review for this game because I absolutely love the series and will continue to play FS22, but I honestly can't recommend it to anyone still playing 19. The graphics are slightly better than 19, but not mind blowingly so. There are so many bugs that certain parts of the game are absolutely unplayable. I am playing on a dedicated server (that I own). I had to stop with producing silage because the silage bunkers are broken. The AI is absolutely as terrible as it has been since they introduced it years ago. The maps are underwhelming and leave almost no room for your vehicles to turn around effectively. Certain sell points are capped, so if you deliver a load, you might not be able to sell everything at once (or they are broken, still don't know). If you want to do lumber, half the time you cut down a tree and part of the tree glitches out and if you try to touch it the game locks up. This game feels more like a money grab than anything else. It feels like they just redeveloped a few popular mods and released FS19 again. I would stick with 19 if I didn't already purchase this. Maybe in the future it will be better, but I can't recommend it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool enjoyable game, It is literally the same game as FS 17 and FS 19, only with different maps, different vehicles & tools, a few mods taken from the community included in the base game, whole bunch of new DLCs. The game is full of bugs, glitches and weird physics ever since the FS 15. Instead of improving the overall gameplay, Giants Software is still churning out a new game each year to make more money, quantity before quality. This game desperately needs a new reworked game engine. Don't search for any realism in terms of vehicle physics. You can do a full turn with a tractor at a full speed. All user vehicles are glued to the ground like Formula 1 cars, and even a small break in the contact of one wheel with the ground will send your car flying and spinning illogically, even at a low speed of 50 km/h. AI of the traffic cars is pure garbage. AI vehicles are stopping hundreds of meters around a hired employee driving a harvester on a field, but then stop half a meter from you driving it, preventing you from making a tight turn onroad. For why?All the cheap and lazily done animations everywhere, the exact same animation of the cabin movement when you're accelerating, no matter how much and how long, same for stopping. Lightning system is horrible.If you need any visualization of how greatly finished the game is, just watch any video showing what you can do with the horses, that will do.

_childDocuments_.review: My friends always ask me what I find so fun about this game, and the top reason is that there's always so much to do. You never really run out of things to do in the game if you venture into different varieties of work. Varieties of work include animals, crops, and production lines. And if you are waiting for a helper to finish a large field you can always accept contracts.I am personally looking forward to the platinum expansion. The platinum expansion is set to bring so many new features to the game such as construction, new ways of logging and a variety of new production chains to expand in.To sum up: the game brings satisfaction, at an end of an in-game month you can sit back knowing you've done everything there is to be done on the farm and then sleep until the next month/day to enjoy it all again.

_childDocuments_.review: All righty then here we are with another installment of Farming Simulator . Game is nice , runs good. New features are a nice touch and running on a new game engine FINALLY. Good : - Transmission shifting is great. - Graphics look better that they did in 19. - They still have Collectibles scattered around the map. (Open Giant's editor to find them all) - I love the sounds of the tractors. they now feel like they're actually pulling something.  - Avatar customizing is a nice touch.  - New crops.- Rocks in the fields.- Elmcreek is a nice looking map. (Just wish it was about 8 times larger)Bad :- Game map is still a measly 2x2 . Map feels way to small as usual.  - Multiplayer servers seem really hard to connect to at times.  Sometimes it works without issue and then there is times where i cannot find the server anywhere for an hour. - Multiplayer lag-Spikes are horrible at times. (Figured Giant's would have tested this) - Multiplayer , loading in can take a few minutes at times.  (Mostly it loads in 10-30 seconds) - They still have not made Controller steering smooth yet.  you're still ping ponging from one side to the next. Ugly : - Seems to me Giant's rushed this game at the end to meet a dead line rather than pushing it back and fixing the game. The game at times CAN be a hot mess....Then there are times where it loads , runs great.  Online server stuttering drives me Bleeping nuts ! Final Thoughts : I am a fan of Farm Sim series , i've been playing these games since the start with FS09 all the way up to current. But i am not a FaNbOi , i'll tell you what's what with this game.        Now all in all i am proud of Giant's and the work they put in here.  i just with they did a little more testing before launching.  Seems the "We'll fix it after launch" is becoming the normal in the gaming industry . The game is not bad , works fine and it has not crashed once. but it's the little things that add up. The game is a blast to play when your friends are around.   The new crops , rocks , and other things bring this game out above other games.  Sounds , visuals .. it's all a welcoming change.  Learning Curve : Beginners - 30-60 minutes  Returning players - 10-15 minutes Fans of the series will be able to jump right in and play without issue. New players should be fine , the in-game tutorials have enough to teach you what you need. Is it worth a buy ??  YES I'd say yes it is , while the game is not perfect it is a blast to play.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a short and a long answer. If you already have FS19 with DLCs then you should stay away from this game or get it only when its on sale. At this time it has less to offer then what you have in FS19 for 40$. If you are new to the FS then it will be cheapor for you on the long run to buy FS22, but try getting it outside Steam because you can get it cheaper most of the Time. But be warned! The game is more or less the same as FS19 with a little bit of inproved Graphics, sounds and game mechanic.- AI - its dumb and annoying. AI traffic will ignore you and any traffic regulations (Stop signs, right of way, speed signs) that a normal human being would expect the AI traffic to obey. They drive like every human player in GTA. So be wary of them.  The AI Helpers are not better. While the AI Traffic drives with the speed of light, the AI Helper will slow down to a crawl in corners and will come to a stop some times at intersections for no apparent reason. On the fields  if they have a implement that is wider then 4m then they will not go until the Field edge because they are afraid that they will get stuck on a fence or Tree. So instead they will ignore that 6-12m of Field completely.- Graphics- i will give this to GIANTS, FS22 is the most beautiful Farming Simulator that i saw until now. But man they need to do something with the Optimization because it cant be that with a RX 6800xt i need to spend 3 hours homing the settings in on a 60FPS capped game that has a GTX1060 as recommended graphics card. I play on High settings with some settings turned down to get rid of the annoying Stuttering. Optimalise your game GIANTS!!!!!- Gameplay - well its 90% FS19 in this regard with some new FS19 MODS that are integrated in to the game like :- Seasons, Production lines and a semi successful attempt of Coursplay. What they did not manage to do is make it so that we the Players could select how we want our Field to be Plow`d, Cultivated if we want to use a Helper. I mean there is a MOD in FS19 for that, could of been copied like the other tree, but was not so important it seams.  In fact it feels like every aspect of the game is only half made and i would play an Early Access Title with a 40$ Price tag.  Let me elaborate: So lets take the not so new we took it from a FS19 MOD Production lines idea. I can now buy Factories that make from something something (from Wheat  Flour for instance). Its a good idea...FS19 had a mod that did the same but now its integrated in game. Is it better? Well it would be, but its not finished. Not finished you ask, why is that? Well let me explain. So you can buy Factories...all good...but...i would expect to know before i invest my money how much grain will the Grain Mill use up to make how much Flour. I would like to see how much grain and what type will be used up in a period of time and how much Flour will be made in that amount of time. But this info is only available to you if you buy the building. And if you buy the building then you cant sell it, you cant upgrade it. And this half way done attitude is all over the game.  You can let your Factories Store, Distribute (send the End product to the next Factory that you own) or Sell the Product that it makes. But there is a catch...you cant set a minimum Price to Sell, no Time period to sell, the Factory will sell in every Hour whatever is in storage for the best Price that is currently on the market minus 35% for that product. How do i know this? I tested it over one hour long, because this crucial info is nowhere to be found in game. Every step of the way you need to Test, Time and Calculate for your self because there is not even the most basic Information available to you. You would like to Lease a Tractor...go a head... how much will it cost me???...you would like to know right? Well ♥♥♥♥ you. In short that's  how it works. You Lease a Tractor, the Lease price is nowhere to be seen, how much it will cost you per Day or Hour is also missing, but hey if you Press the Lease button it will tell you at least how much is the initial Lease price, good luck Testing the other two out. Price fluctuations make no sense. The chart that should tell you wen is the time to Sell will tell you August for a Crop but the Price will say ♥♥♥♥ that and the Highest price will be in January just because.  And don`t even start with Maintenance. You can now buy used equipment. Another feature that i missed from FS19 is finally in FS22 by the way so i'm very happy. So you can buy Equipment (Implements, tractors, etc) that are in different States of decay, that you can repair. But the fact that these Used equipment will deteriorate 50% faster then the NEW counterparts in the same usage scenario, and Time span is nowhere to be seen. The maintenance is so expensive that most of the time if you plow a Field in Hard mode you need to spend over 50% of your earnings on repairs for a 30 minutes Plowing. Most of the Time the Crops that i planted wont bring so much money in. Helper Cost....that`s another area where GIANTS ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. I mean i used the Helper to plow a field. It took 30$ for going 50m on the the field!!!!... are you kidding me??? I would like to earn so much in my job. I know its a game but if i`m playing on Hard mode and the crops that i just sold made me 20k$ how in hell can i afford to pay a Helper to Plow the field for 2$ every second? The Factories should make you more money and ad to the Gameplay, but because you cant upgrade the buildings you end up waiting a bunch of time on the End Product. And if you want to make a really big profit you end up loading a trailer with pallets with hand (Using another MOD) because Forklifts are annoying as hell. I mean they could of made it so that you park in a area and it will auto fill, like in Euro Truck Simulator, but noooo...you know what players would love? Loading pallets one by one with a Forklift that takes forever to pick up a pallet. Picking up one or two pallets its a satisfying experience but not 30 a Day just so that i don't lose that 35% to autosell. This game has the potential to be way better then FS19, but not now. Maybe latter. Maybe when GIANTS optimalise the game and fill out basic Info regarding gameplay elements that the player should know. Because i spent hours and hours making 80k$ to buy the Oil Mill so that i can make from Canola Canola Oil and sell it to a good profit, just to learn after i bought  the Mill that it will take 200 Canola to make 100Liter of Oil and it will make 2x100Liter/Hour in game. So that means if i want to make Canola Oil from 18k Liter Canola it will take 45 in Game Hours to do so.  This Game looks so promising, everything that you would want from a Farming Simulator in 2021, but its shallow. It bring new and good ideas to the Table but fails to implement it to its full potential. In fact in this game the only gameplay feature that wont disappoint is the Seasons aspect of it. That is beautiful and everything that you would expect. The sounds are amassing, the most realistic sounding Farm sim out there, it gives me the chills and will immerse you to depths that you could not think are possible. Just to be pulled out by Crows and Dears spawning in front of you ever 5-30 Seconds, AI that drive like lunatics, and lack of Information that should be in game from the Start. Its sad that i need to download Mods that fix Gameplay aspects of the game, i should be downloading buildings, maps or Equipment, not Mods that aim to correct a broken gameplay. It`s sad that i spent hours up on hours on YouTube looking at videos on how much Leasing costs or what is the production rate of a Factory instead of seeing this info in game as it should be. If you need to pay people to explain how your game works to players then something is wrong. I want to play and not Run Tests. I want to enjoy the game and not search for ways and workarounds for things that don`t work or are broken.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply put one of the best games I have ever played.  I base this conclusion on the fact that it offers a quality of gameplay that many other games simply cannot match.  Farming Simulator 22 has a lot of depth--there is simply so much to do, and you don't necessarily have to perform certain tasks instead of others when you're in gaming mode.  "Go at your own pace and do things you feel like doing" is the message this game essentially sends its players.  It's an immersive experience in which the player is ultimately in control.  Learning how to do things most efficiently is the reward one gets as they become more familiar with the  tactics of the game and some of the fundamental procedures of farming.    Now unless you're familiar with Farming Simulator, I think there is definitely a learning curve.  For me, there was a lot of trial and error.  Sometimes, I really didn't even feel like playing anymore, as there were also some basic tasks that seemed confusing.  That being said, the tutorial in this game is definitely not sufficient.  But if you go on YouTube, everything you'd ever need to know is available to you.  Considering how much depth this game has, there is going to be some difficulty or frustration in perhaps getting your plants to harvest at a decent yield rate or knowing which vehicle is appropriate for which task but it's not impossible and I never found any glitches that made the game unplayable.The game has beautiful graphics and crisp sound as well.  It's a satisfying experience to view the crops grow, because so much detail comprises the textures of the fields and the plants and objects have a sharpness encompassing them, rather than a blur.  As for the sound, there is a clarity to the rain going against your tractor or the sound of an engine for a particular brand of equipment.  That being said, the game offers a certain element of tranquility.  It can be a very peaceful experience where the player is only focused on growing a certain crop or simply tending to their animals.  And that's what's amazing also about this game--the fact it's challenging, yet relaxing as well.  The presence of mods alone makes this game quite intriguing.  I love playing this game with mods as I'm sure most people do.  Some mods may certainly seem ridiculous in the sense that they detract from a realistic farming experience while others simply give the player the extra push they need to simply play at their own pace or level of comfort.  The bottom line is there are thousands of mods, and that alone makes Farming Simulator 22's replay value very high.  In sum, I think the current price of this game is acceptable considering what if offers and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a challenging, but highly immersive and at times, relaxing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Adam stared intently into the mirror, trying to focus his vision, he felt as if he were drunk. He rubbed his eyes, blinked repetedly, but nothing seemed to help.Barely able to make out the shape of his own head, he slapped himself in a futile attempt to clear his head. Doing this, Adam noticed that all of his senses seemedto be numbed. He hadn't hardly felt those slaps, and the silence! This was more than just being in a quiet room, something was different, wrong. There was no sound, yet he felt as though there was a crash, a roar, an explosion, all at once! Silence, head shaking silence. So quiet it nearly drove him mad. Was this what they meant by deafening silence? His mind raced. Was he really deaf? No, he couldn't be, could he? He had been able to hear just a few moments earlier, right? He coudln't remember, all thoughts of what led to this had seemingly drained from his memory. How had he gotten here, wasn't he supposed to go to Evan's wedding today? How did that turn to... this? Whatever this was. These thoughts were interrupted by a booming thud that filled his head. Though quiet, this sudden noise was a shock to his system. It came again, and then again. Soon the sharp bass faded to a higher, almost click-like noise. *DRIP* There it was again, though now he realized the sound. *DRIP* He looked down into the sink, he seeiong a bit clearer now, red stains led towards the drain. *DRIP* He was bleeding, he examined his hands. Though covered in blood, there didnt seem to be any real wounds. *DRIP* He looked ahead, his face slowly came into focus.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated 10/13/23(Summary at bottom)NOT a reskinned FS19. I have about 650 hours on FS19 and I can most certainly say this is much better in many ways, and many things have been completely overhauled. - Sounds have had a major overhaul, makes the game feel more realistic and immersive.- A few minor realism additions, like visual gear-shifting, cab suspension, etc.- More placeables than ever, including sheds with working doors, refuel stations, seed & fert tanks, etc. Fences, lights, and other decor too, to brighten up your farm a bit.- Many new brands, and more tire brand options. Also license plates for equipment and vehicles.- Character customization. Imo, not the best, graphics and general proportions look weird, but hey, better than before.- Better organized XML files. Much more easier on the eyes compared to FS17, and easier to find things such as the money value. I don't need to use ctrl+f anymore, I can just scroll. (Speaking of XML editing, instead of editing the careerSavegame.xml file like FS17 & FS19 to edit your cash, here you need to edit farms.xml file instead in the same folder, careerSavegame.xml is only for appearance in the main menu.)- Better organized shop UI, not to mention the UI overall. Imo, the weird blue fade on the speedometer/tachometer reminds me of those old games, and I wish they had just instead updated the FS19 one.- An actual American-based map. Major improvement from Ravenport and Goldcrest Valley, feels more of the true american countryside thanks to that new office here in the U.S. that Giants got a while ago.- Buying used equipment. Great for starting a farm on a tight budget, and in multiplayer you can buy other farm's sold vehicles. Wish there was more than 5 at a time though.- Vehicle gearbox. Not required if you don't want to use it, but I like it. A wee bit confusing at times however, I'm used to the way you shift in American Truck Simulator, but this is different. Not bad, maybe needs to be tweaked a bit. Will note that it's sometimes buggy, especially with mods.- Obviously graphics, you won't really notice a huge jump between FS19 and FS22 as the major jump of the franchise was between FS17 and FS19, but there are some noticeable changes. Also, 3D tracks on tractors. No more jpeg tracks.- Seasons. I don't like playing so realistic to the point I have to wait time for the proper planting and harvesting time, but there's an option to make it so the seasons are just visual only. - Multiplayer Voice Chat, very useful.Now, there are of course many bugs with the game, and some features missing since it got released not too long ago. Some rather aggravating bugs/missing features are:- Landscaping, a tad bit annoying with the camera and movement. There's no snapping things to a certain rotation, and the camera angle is from a bird's eye view that swoops down instead of zooming in, which is rather annoying when trying to line things up together. There's also no sprinting like in FS17 (idk about the others)- AI workers. We all know from previous FS games that the AI is notorious, especially in FS17. Here, there have been some improvements, and with the addition of AI being able to drive vehicles to and fro, that's really useful, but again, very buggy. The classic 'Helper F is blocked by an object!' pops up every now and then, you tab over and there's nothing in it's way. Lately, on modded maps, the AI sometimes will just sit there doing nothing. Possibly just a mod-side issue. - Buildings, most notably the farmhouse. If you look into the windows, it's just a copied .jpeg of a weird looking kitchen with yellow cabinets and a granite looking wall. I'm sure Giants will add in an interior at some point, I don't want jpeg interiors like FS13 & FS17. Also, you cannot interact with/enter any existing buildings/sheds/barns on the farms on the land you purchase. I sure hope that gets changed.(note: kinda sorta fixed? some sheds you can enter)Bugs TL;DR:- Landscaping (Controls & viewing angles are awkward)- AI Driving/Transport (Blocked by nothing, drives the wrong path or drives in circles')- didn't note this but general physics, collisions, and the gearbox still need to be tuned.TL;DR:There are many bugs, I hope they'll be fixed before the next year. But there are also many improvements from previous FS games, as someone who's played FS13 (Xbox 360), 17 (Steam), and 19 (Epic Games).At this time, with the amount of bugs/missing features in the game, you can go ahead and buy it if you want. I managed to snag a deal with the season passes where I got both for like $30, damn good deal, would NOT recommend paying full price for each individual DLC.I have not tested everything, and I have not played every map. I do not have all of the bugs and missing features listed, I will update this review as I come across more notable bugs, missing features, and changes from previous FS games.Again, this is a newly released game, so unless Giants decides to not fix these issues/keep them removed like EA did with Battlefield 2042, then I will change this review as needed.11/24/21 UpdateSo you can use Q & E to switch between the license plate types, yet when you're typing in your custom license plate and you need to press Q or E, it switches the license plate type. They do have an on-screen keyboard I assume for consoles, but I really don't want to *click, move mouse (repeat 8 more times)* every single time I have to put in a license plate. My way to bypass this is make sure the color selection is highlighted when you start typing.The field care addon is nice, more stuff to do with Grain farming. I haven't really played around with that yet.Graphics for working the fields look much better, but when the field state changes (harvested to cultivated, to plowed, etc) is still very noticeable and jittery, a bit annoying as it is ruining the immersion a little.Pallet physics have improved a ton, however, but they do still slide around imo a wee bit too easily.Bigbags! Can easily pick them up with anything with forks, and you can feel that you're picking up a heavy item. They have realistic physics, so that's nice.12/31/21 Update- Pre-Placed Buildings can now be deleted off of farms.- The issue with the semi truck axles acting weird is now fixed. They drive much smoother now.4/12/22 Update:- Character customization is saved to the last customized option.- License Plates are also saved the same way.- Updated/revised entire review9/9/22 Update:Revised entire review again, clarified some things, and removed some stuff that didn't need to be here to make room because of the damn review character limit.10/11/23 Update:Fine tuned the review a little bit, moved a few notable things from previous updates to the main category, blablabla. I don't think I can do much more for this review, especially with the character limit.

acquired, take a ford tractor license for example. you cant get a license to recreate a brands tractors in a game if the brand no longer exists, but they have a john Deere license, we got 2 older style machines, they've got a new Holland licence, no old new Holland/ford tractors from the 90's, there's mods that are these types of tractors but again, if the busy modders who have their own lives and jobs can add these features as a hobby, WHY CANT THE DEVS.disappointed.without mods, this game is really difficult to enjoy. with mods, this game is a fantastic look into the industry of agriculture. don't get me wrong, there's plenty of basic farming aspects missing, but we make do.for anyone looking to get into the franchise, i highly suggest going back to fs19 or even 17 and learning on those editions because i can guarantee you'll have fun whilst you learn. once you've got the hang of things, come over to 22 and have a play around, see how you feel, and start experimenting with mods. i know I've got a lot of hours on this game, but it makes me sad that after all that time, I'm still not happy with what the devs have accomplished. looking back on previous versions really shows the drop in care or commitment that the devs seem to have. im sure (some of them) are working hard and do care, but like everything else in this worlds, it seems to be all about the money nowadays. there will be a point where the community gets bored of this lack of effort from the developers, you see comments on Facebook forums, and steam reviews, and YouTube videos that show how upset the community has become. i cant even remember the last time i saw an update to this game where the devs actually did something. this game is getting older and older and yet the Ai is still broken, textures still flicker during different seasons, basic script add-ons such as pro-seed still aren't base game, and im not sure the game changing mods that make this game what they are, will ever be implemented.a quick example before i go, seasons. seasons was and absolutely wicked mod in 17 and 19, and we were all so excited when we heard it was base game in 22, but its still so broken. planting calendars are just not realistic at all, i cant change month length from 5 days to 3 without having to leave the game, because the setting doesn't work. its just disappointing.and what about passengers... need to buy a dlc for that mate... i know a lot of people will say its just a game and not everyone likes to play realistic, but what about those who do. what about those who want to play a "Farming Simulator"? i appreciate those of you who don't always play realistic, or prefer to do some logging or mining, i enjoy a spot of both of those too, but the game just feels unfinished in a way. im sure it'll be blamed on covid, but for how long will covid be blamed. its 2024 as im writing this and yet im sat here saying a game thats now 2 years old, still feels unfinished.so with that said, get it. or dont. its your money.. i dont even know how i feel about this game anymore, and that makes me sad, so im going to go and cheer myself up by doing a spot of ploughing i think! tell me what you guys think, i need a second opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I get it, and yea, that was me too for the longest time. I thought why would anyone play THAT?Now that i have it, i have to admit its a surprisingly good game. You can even play it when being braindead, and that is partly why it is so successfull. There is nothing complex or difficult about it, yet you have a lot of things to do and can build on your plots of land what you want and how you want it. That means you have quite some creative freedom to do things how you like.On top, the game is very open to modding so you can adjust the game to what you want it to be rather easylie, for most things there is at least one mod.And in hard mode(start from scratch), the economy is, to my surprise, quite tight. You operate on smal margins for a long time and i enjoy that. You have to dig yourself out of the financial hole for some time and what you spend your virtual money on does make a difference for many gameplay hours. For a long time you can not afford all you "want" but only one thing at a time, so what´s it gona be?Yes, hard mode is grindy in that sense, but grindy in a good way for my taste.The easy and normaly difficulties, i never tried those, i guess you roll in money more quickly there.In short, the game was a big surprise for me, and with a ton of mod maps i can seem myself playing it some more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: FS22 is a decent game. The graphics are good, the gameplay is fun and interesting especially if you like building something. Out of the box the game is pretty solid, and mods just tweak it or straight off make it better (similar to how mods made FS19 a better game to play). I played a bit of multiplayer in FS19, including running a server for awhile, but haven't ventured forth in FS22 yet.Why play a farming sim? The game itself is relaxing, especially after a sh*t day at work. The game can challenge too-- decide how you feel like playing and FS22 seems to accommodate pretty well. You still need to think, as in planning, overall strategy (ex. what crops to plant, when to harvest etc), tactics (for ex. how you approach tasks, which tractor/tool, when to hire an AI helper, etc.) vs weather, seasons etc.Overall, if you like the idea of building something and using a variety of machines, check out FS22.  YMMV. It's certainly a game I enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that's played hundreds of hours of FS19 and loved every minute of it, at this time, I can't recommend the game right now.  It's actually a bit tough to make a review like this but there are a LOT of things that just don't impress me.  The devs talked about higher fps ingame..yet we're still locked at 60fps even with v-sync off.  They boasted about having 400+ vehicles and tools in the game but it feels like they gutted a lot of the brands down to 3-4 items that had a much bigger presence in FS19.  Seed usage when it comes to planting grass is WAY too high..a field that's just a bit over .5ac took over 4000L of seed to put grass in it.  The Silos that require the conveyors..biggest pain in the butt I've had to deal with so far.  They don't even stay put when you park it.  There's a handful of other issues I have and I just don't feel like this game should of taken 3 years to develop when they didn't really add anything huge other then rocks and new sounds and textures for things.  Maybe if they work out some of these issues down the road, I can recommend it, but I'd give it time to cook a bit more before spending the money on a copy/paste of FS19 with a few new textures and sounds.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a big fan of Farming Simulator since FS2011, my second game I ever purchased. This is their most impressive release yet. If you enjoyed other games from the series, I am sure you will enjoy this too. Equally, if you never found enjoyment in a farming simulator, this will not change that.For starters, I have not experienced any major bugs. I am not sure what other reviewers are doing, but my experience has been vastly different. There have been some small graphical glitches/flickering and some minor gameplay bugs that I have reported to Giants, and I am sure they will get to in due course. This is to be expected with any game release in this day and age, love it or hate it. Giants have been well known to patch their games. I trust they will fix anything that is extremely broken.I will admit being overly un-optimistic about this game based on the pre-release press releases and trailers. It did seem like they were just adding what modders could already do in FS19, however now that I have been hands on with the game that those features have been implemented in ways/with a certain level of polish that modders could simply not achieve with their tool-set. Now lets hope the modders can set their sights further now that these features are baked in.I have appreciated the focus on diversification in workflows too (for example, mulchers, rollers, stone pickers). There are now many different ways to do the same thing, which I will accept must be hard for beginners to wrap their heads around but for simulation enthusiasts such as myself is extremely exciting. There are also additional ways to boost yield, giving you more to do over the winter months.I have also enjoyed the smaller machines, making the startout easier. Their recent games have often leaned heavily on the larger equipment, making the starting few in-game years lacking but this game feels well polished in that area. For example, the smaller balers.Some new features have been heavily glossed over too;A lot of the negative reviews that I have seen have only played the game for a few hours. That is not enough time to go through a full year in the game, nor to try the new features. I have played for 12 hours, and barely scraped the surface of what this name game offers.With all that said, my usual complaints must still be included. It is still an outdated engine, that I believe is holding the game back. It is still an extremely eurocentric game with very little in the way of realistically modelled American or otherwise international equipment. I would love to see this get addressed in future releases, but it won't hold me back from appreciating what this game is...

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to this series. I thought the idea sounded kind of outside the things I want to know about or play in a game. And here I am, 344 hours in. This is the most peaceful and relaxing thing I've played in a long while. And at the same time, stressful and hard as I have had to learn what everything is, does, and how to use it. I've learned more about farming than I've known my entire life and I'm kind of proud of that. This game has great graphics that put you in the feeling of running a harvester, plowing a field, cutting grass, trucking goods, you name it. It strives for realistic machines though the towns themselves are pretty lifeless. The season views as time passes are also quite beautiful, as is the sunset across a field while you're winding down for the day. 7/10Audio is decent and workable for what this game is, but again, you're listening to birds and machinery. Thankfully there is a built in radio that plays not just canned music but also streams from several public music stations, allowing for some good jams as you wind around in your tractor. 6/10Gameplay is strangely addictive. This isn't a baron style game where you're forced to compete, really. This is a wide open map (of several) where you slowly expand your farm empire. The only thing stopping you is your ability to take on more work and learn new things. It's TRUE open gameplay in that you don't have to do anything at all and the sim will gladly let you pass time just to watch the seasons if you want. But it also allows you to enjoy learning things you might know very little about, one step at a time, be that farming, logging, raising farm animals, or doing work for others. The maps are your canvas to play and expand on. There isn't much, if any, pressure. But it has that, "one more thing," feeling in spades. It has that hook that keeps pulling you back to check on things and go another month or three. That's the mark of an excellent game. 10/10Multiplayer is available for those that run or rent dedicated servers. I have not tried that yet but it's quite popular with those who do and one of the highlights of the series, joint farming with friends. ?/10Don't pass by this if you're even remotely interested in the idea. This is a fantastic and relaxing game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think there are some solid improvements in FS22, but there's also still room for improvement.Implementing seasons is a nice a change, it takes a moment to get used to only being able to plant crops during certain months (which I guess you can disable). My first hour in the game I lost an entire field of corn because I didn't finish harvesting it before the season changed. I have been wanting to use the snow plows, but haven't had enough snow yet to do so.Grapes and olives are a fun addition. And so are the new production possibilities. Being able to buy a factory and supply it yourself adds good gameplay. I was excited for bee hives but they literally require you to do nothing after they're placed. A little bit of beekeeping would make it better. Greenhouses are also cool and a good way to make a little extra money, but again, besides adding water, you don't have to do anything for it to produce. Improvements to the store/garage have been made by way of showing you compatible equipment, but no improvement was made to explaining what things are for. Thank goodness for youtube. I spent a few hours clearing a few trees from my property, and it is as time consuming and frustrating as always. God bless the players who actually choose to do forestry in this game.All 3 maps are pretty great, although I don't understand putting in roundabouts and a million light poles in areas where semis need to access. One fantastic improvement is the removal of the need to 'clean' animal feeding areas. Animals seems somewhat more balanced and easier to care for, except you're still expected to spend the majority of your day riding your horses. Being able to hire someone for this task would be awesome. All in all, I like the new game and will be looking forward to new content and more mods.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing: This is the best version of Farming Simulator so far. There are huge improvements, and its basically a fantastic game if you enjoy work simulators. The sound engine updates really add to immersion, loader work is incrementally, but significantly improved (still lots of room for improvement, but important steps forward have been taken)That said, Giants Engine is still a bit of a joke. The improvements are always incremental, and some basic functionality is still broken for features that have been in-game for several versions. It's not Star Citizen clunky, just needs more love. It shows that they put an extra year of development in, just don't expect miracles.For context: I pre-ordered the collector's edition, I bought a key straight from Giants because I was that excited and had to play half a day early, and eventually also bought a 3rd, Steam copy because I realized later Giants/CD keys don't work on steam for this game specifically.  Keep in mind with this review, I'm a little salty that I have paid for 3 copies already. I was planning to have 2 copies, 1 to eventually host a server.Skid steer loaders still have hidden 4 wheel steering instead of differential drive, so they drive like a WWI tank instead of a skid steer.Manual Transmission was promised for 2019, but not delivered, now in 22 it's here, but is badly broken. - Brake+throttle cancel each other out, so there's no way to trim throttle to prevent no load stall in every gear without disabling the brakes.- There's also no reverse gear position for any vehicle, so cars and trucks have the unrealistic need to use a shuttle control instead of selecting reverse.I doubt these issues will ever be fixed, because Giants shows again and again that while they care about the game and the community, they are stubbornly incompetent and won't fix something if it doesn't ruin the game for most players. They mean well, and they do better than anyone else in the genre, but I'm harshly critical because they come so close and just leave stuff a little too broken, and without the passionate modding community, I believe the game would have much more limited success.

_childDocuments_.review: Still no sounds from log collisions. Makes the game seem like it's early access when doing forestry. It's a chill game, but there's very little improvement between the titles. Edit: Farming and logging is the same as it was in FS17 and FS19. When it comes to farming, it's as disappointing as it was in FS17, which was my introduction to the series. Harvesting feels like having an eraser at the front of your vehicle that deletes rows that the vehicle isn't even touching.It's been the same since FS17 and probably even before that. I've been hoping for some vehicle damage- and ground physics, but the game still relies heavily on mods to even be enjoyable, and mods can only do so much.. I bought the Platinum Edition DLC cause I could, and it left a bitter taste in my mouth; It feels like a mandatory DLC if you want any sense of development to logging between the titles in the series. Having game changing equipment like winches and yarders hidden behind a paid DLC is in my book a bad thing. Especially when there's two winches and yarders of different quality in the DLC, half of this pack should've been included in the base game, and the DLC would still have a great value with vehicles like the Volvo 380C and the Hannibal wood harvester and a few tons more of other vehicles and equipment. Disappointing. Most of the controls can be remapped, but not the most basic L1(+)R1 menus. There's no alternative control methods offered by the developers, so instead of utulizing the analouge controllers (PS/Xbox) for vehicles with dual joysticks so that you can operate both joysticks at the same time, the default is to hide the control surfaces behind three different button configurations; R1+joystick, L1+joystick and R1+L1+ joystick. I've spent a lot of time testing and figuring out how to remap the controller to have it operate these vehicles in a more enjoyable manner, but I've run into bugs that makes wheel loaders and front loaders impossible to use when the camera gets stuck. -Needs to offer alternative controls, to have more freedom when remapping, and to be able to remap controls to certain vehicles only. I'm really disappointed that players have to spend so much time and effort on making the game and controllers enjoyable.I've wasted so much time on this game before remapping the controllers and downloading mods like VCA and the Wood harvester Control mod, mostly because I reach a point where it's just mind boggling that the game is as it is, and there has to be a different way to do things. A single one of these changes felt like a game changer in it self, and it's mind boggling and disappointing that the developers don't offer this experience to their players as an alternative, and instead let it be up to modders and players to spend time and effort on improving their game. If you're new to the seires; A lot of fun to be had, greatly detailed vehicles and equipment, and multiplayer can be a lot of fun. Easy to sink hundreds of hours into, so the hour price is usually low. If you've played the previous titles; It's the same. If you think crushing stones on the fields sounds interesting, just think how Giants could implement this with the least amount of effort possible. That's what you get. Prepare yourself to not be impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: These are my thoughts after almost 100 hours of playing. This experience is purely multiplayer because I never play alone these types of games.I'm not not telling you what to do nor imposing you my opinion.To start, I've never played more broken game in my entire life (apart from fallout 76 but that's a different story) and I have hundreds of them in my library. It's kinda sad when you buy €78 game (the more expensive edition) and you get this mess. Although I really like FS22 there are issues that are stealing the joy out of it and discouraging me to play this game. The netcode:- A minor thing but why does the game pause when somebody is joining and freezes for a bit when someone is leaving. A lot older games can do it without a lag, why this one can't?-I don't know if it's a netcode thing but a pallet limit? Really?Especially when the game urges you to manage such enormous amount pallets (if you do it all manually as you should when you want to make the best profit). - Again I dunno if it's a netcode thing or engine issue... What the hell is happening with ingame physics?Pallets are so broken that there is a huge possibility that at least one will send you to space when you move them everyday. No matter the vehicle, no matter the type of goods, no matter anything, it just happens and I have a full folder of clips to proof that.The settings:-Why do I always need to go into menu to change the smallest thing of my graphic settings? - Correct me if I'm an idiot and didn't find the fps limiter but in order to unlock FPS I had to turn on the console window.The bugs:A buggy mess this game is. I'm a fortunate person to find most of the bugs in most games. As a result these are the most annoying:- Pallets, pallets, pallets. The pallet god will always mess with you because he can. As a result you or the pallet will end up in space.- Some cultivators not folding correctly.- Cotton bale front loader not working.- You can enter every building when you park your vehicle near them and get out of it.- Neighbor AI not working when sleeping instead of accelerating the time. So every field that's not yours will be left withered.- Terrain adjustment isn't working as you would need especially when you're placing a building on uneven terrain.- And some more that you can find on this sub that I haven't described.- Graphical glithesSomething about ingame mechanics:- There should be an option for production buildings to stop dropping pallets, especially when it's capped.Animal buildings have no direct storage so they are dropping pallets directly and are not working when the assigned place for it is full.- Steering wheel is bad because there is no force feedback only a central spring. Ughh...- Horse riding...look I'm not expecting Red dead redemption experience but as it is now, it's terrible. Very user unfriendly.While all of those separate things might seem minor things to you as a whole they are not.No matter all the cool vehicles, tools and functions that are present, the technical state of this game is a disaster.You can say I'm whining, too harsh, it's okay but all those things are true and if the devs won't fix it it will end badly.And the last thing I wanted to say is that moders shouldn't be the one fixing games. I agree if it's temporarily but not as a permanent solution, fix it or pay moders for it I don't care. And if you think it's okay you're allowing devs to be lazy and do ♥♥♥♥ about that.All these things considered, this doesn't really look like a finished product, especially not in this price category, more like beta.If devs can't do anything about it, they should probably fire some people and change the game engine as it is not up to todays standard at this state.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a long time supporter of Giants and the farming simulator franchise, having all previous released titles on pc since 08 edition and most of the DLC throughout the years, not to mention getting others to buy and play the games.  And while I was annoyed by how fs19 dlc was handled, when those of us that supported the developer and purchased the game and some DLC along the way as they were released got no bundle rebate on steam (for parts of bundle we already own), nothing come close to how Giants are treating your customers with the Platinum Edition crap they are pulling this time around. A new player getting into the game now can get the FS22 Premium edition, getting the base game and both season passes including platinum expansion for 40 Euro.  This is a good deal, I'm not complaining about this, it's a fair price for this late in the game lifecycle. But if I, with the base game, try to purchase Premium Edition on steam I get the following message: So, according to Steam and how spesifically asked them to set the pricing.. Me wanting to get the full experience of FS22, having already paid 40 euro for the base when it came out, now have to pay 40 euro for year 1 season pass and 40 euro for year 2 pass. An additional 80 euro, a total of 120, instead of 40, just because I dared to buy the base game when it came out.I get and agree on giving a bundle price for new players late to the game, giving a good value bundle price to entice them to the franchise. But you can do so without ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ over your existing players and tell them to go buy everything at full price just because they had the gall to purchase the game when it came out and wait for dlc to release. You price it as if you only have 2 types of customers, those that buy base game + season passes right as they come out (this is fine, they get content as it rolls out, ignoring the dlc outside of season pass issue), and those that buy into the game at the end of the game development, and only wants to because a heavy discount. Sure I could try and buy Premium Edition as a gift and claim it for myself, again getting no value for my existing purchase of the base game.But having to circumvent steam store just to get the bundle price is ridiculous, not to mention most people don't know how steam handles gifted bundles when you own an item in that bundle already, just having to gamble that it works. At a minimum give me the option to buy the same editions as new players have, direct in Steam, there is no reason at all to lock that option from existing players.  But preferably let existing owned items be deducted from the bundle base cost, with the same bundle discount applied for remaining items. Like other developer is doing! Get your act together Giants!I get that I'm most likely screaming into the void, but I for one is never going to buy a new FS game until the "final" premium bundle is out unless this changes, if at all.  And I will be directly recommending noone anyone else do either, both in friends circles and elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: The best iteration of Farming Simulator yet! Many new additions along with a few minor disappointments. While I've listed a fair number of negative points, in no way is this version worse than 19 overall. I have no wish to go back to 19 personally. There's nothing missing here that 19 has that I miss other than some tractors which I imagine may show up with free DLC later. Some have already. + Many more machines and implements. We're not talking a dozen here, there's a LOT more including electric vehicle options which is new to the franchise.+ New realism things like collecting rocks from fields and mulching. + New shifting ability for equipment with manual transmissions.+ No more odd graphical glitches in the medium distance which has been persistent with the FS engine. + Snow! This is new to this version. Personally I don't care for it much, but I'm adding it as a plus as it's a realism thing and many will probably like it. In some ways it is poorly implemented however and needs work. See below.+ New calendar based year. Certain crops must be planted/harvested at certain times. Much more realism. + Seasons. Something the game has needed for a while and required modders to implement. Now it's embedded. + As other FS games before it, FS2022 supports mods. Mods can greatly enhance some aspects of the game. - While there's far more equipment, some is missing. My favorite small/medium tractors, were Valtra and almost all models are missing. Why? Some Case models are missing as well. Only one track option for the New Holland T9 tho that's still better than FS19 which had none. - Snow has a graphics glitch on some systems that has yet to be fixed. It causes some flicker around the edges. Usually reloading the game fixes it, but it can be a nuisance on some systems.- While snow is a positive overall, it's poorly implemented. You don't leave tracks. The snow/ice is slippery but the physics are odd. Often it's not slippery when it should be and is when it shouldn't. Snow in fields doesn't affect equipment at all. - There is still no reason to use tracks or duel wheels outside of what you want to look at. The largest/heaviest equipment can still be pulled with single tires no probs. +/- Some of the negatives above can be fixed with mods, but often they do a mediocre job.I am probably missing a few things to compare against older iterations of the game, but these are the things that stand out to me the most. If you loved other versions of FS, I don't think there's any reason not to get this. If things like snow bug you for any reason such at the above mentioned glitches, you can turn it off.

The game's realistic physics and weather systems also add to the overall immersion, making it feel like you're really working on a farm.Overall, Farming Simulator 22 is a must-play for anyone who loves simulation games and is looking for a truly immersive and engaging experience. _childDocuments_.review: Hello. I fallen to the meme culture back in FS15, On the Xbox 360, thinking, "yeah its a farming simulator who would acctually play that?" but in recent years, i have clocked over 1400 hrs plus on both FS19 on the old Xbox One, and the current game, FS22 both Xbox and PCAs a well seasoned virtual farmer, I can say that any installation of this game is HIGHLY ADDICTIVE, if you build your farm from the ground up, and play the game properly and not rely on the money cheat mods. The modding community for this game is out of this world. on most weekdays there are mods that have been tested by GIANTS SOFTWARE themselves ready for the players to play. Recent years have seen significant changes in NEW brands coming to the game, such as CLAAS, MACK Trucks and many more. New animals within this installation include Horses, which are high maintenance but worth the risk of bringing your own animals up. Also new to this instalment is Productions, but I cant have my say on that because if i'm honest i haven't really touched them just yet.The graphics in the game are much better in FS22, but the most change in the graphics system was FS17-FS19 TBH. That being said, it truly is a great game and brings thousands of players back to it every day. Speaking of players, if you are lucky to have friends who own the game on different consoles (PS and Xbox) then Hey, you can play with them too, in real time! Thanks to the new cross play system in the game, However do be warned, the servers are hit and miss sometimes as me and my friends had to wait around half a hour for my game to show up on there consoles. You know how i mentioned mods before, you must download mods that are cross-play compatible or your game wont show to those on PS and Xbox.Customisation in this game is a mention as if you want to customise a piece of machinery, the most you can do is change the number plate. but with a Valtra Tractor you can have it pink for some reason. Yes it still has its flaws but doesn't every game? Plus, if your on Xbox, Its On Game-pass! (not sure on ps)Overall 9/10. Thanks for listening to my loooong (+probally boring) review on the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played every Farming Simulator and expansion since Farming Simulator 2011. I would promptly rank them in order from most enjoyable to least enjoyable as such:1.) Farming Simulator 20222.) Farming Simulator 20133.) Farming Simulator 20174.) Farming Simulator 20195.) Farming Simulator 20156.) Farming Simulator 2011My reasoning is that with each game, there has been some limiting factor that has held back its success. I have played until I have reached a point that I felt limited by what the game was capable of letting me do and enjoy. I won't elaborate on the issues with the other games but for Farming Simulator 22, the issues have been minimized to the point where they  are not actually impacting my play but rather just small annoyances that could be fixed rather than needing to be. My biggest gripes are the fact that the terrain editing system seems to be poorer than previous games (FS19 in particular). It is usable but seems less intuitive and much harder to perfect what you are attempting. My other complaint being the overall performance of the game. I do like to play with mods and understand that poor mod development can result in poor performance but, even with no mods installed, I can barely average 60 FPS with all settings on max. I have a high end PC and would expect the game to run much better than that in an private single-player game. With that said, this still is the most polished version of Farming Simulator that has been released and it has continued to be an enjoyable experience overall.

_childDocuments_.review: It's great, there is stuff to do for every type of player.You like big machinery? Go out and be a full blown grain farmer.You like animals? Build yourself a farm with cows, sheep, pigs, chicken, horses and even bees.You like to some relaxing wine *cough* i mean grape juice? Get a vineyard in all of it's beauty.Seasons give me a somewhat mixed experience, especially earlygame there is not much to do in the winter. _childDocuments_.review: Great game. I was hesitant buying this when i enjoyed 19 so much and some reviews said it was not much of an update but they are wrong. The construction interface is so much better now and there is way more stock customization in the vehicles. The added gameplay mechanics of stone picking and production lines add much more realism and if you want even more, download the free DLC for precision farming as well. The AI helpers on the field are pretty good and you now have limited built in autodrive features though those definitely need some help so I'd still recommend downloading Courseplay and Autodrive for the full automation experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Its the best installment in the franchise to date. An absolute truck load of love and attention has been poured into all the little details and features within. A little rough around the edges, the odd glitch/issue/problem, etc etc, but nothing that wont be patched out within a few days and nothing game breaking. I can, unreservedly, recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the simulators as a whole, especially ETS/ATS, its got that nice relaxing gameplay element.Of note, the game is much harder now, especially starting out, no more owning the entire map and all the tractors after just a few harvests, now everything feels like an investment, something you earn. And thats on Normal.TLDR; Yes, Its good, it scratches the sim itch, and i highly recommend it.

Nicer sound and graphic, year after year. What's the point. Here's what would have been nice. Playtest your economy. Go back to basic things, like your physics engine, and gain a working knowledge of it. Then start fixing basic things - just to name an example, pallets. Your products suck at launch, and they continue to suck throughout your product lifecycle, and you think you can easily get away with it, and you're absolutely right. Idiots like me pretty much guarantee this can go on and on and on. Without a doubt the modding community will yet again do your job for you, and people will shrug at and silently ignore things that are frustrating, and un-fun, and try to squeeze some enjoyment out of the things that work, which happen to be the same things since FS 11. Or get some mods that bypass the things you guys couldn't figure out. I suppose that's what I will do, in a few months or so. Shame.

_childDocuments_.review: I really dont want to give this a thumbs down but the negatives out weight the positives. don't get me wrong, if you are a simulation player and love agriculture and machines this game is awesome. But i see a call of duty issue of copy paste gaming with maybe a few new features. It feels like you need mods to make the game fresh and have good variety (variety as in old equipment and realistically obtainable equipment). I've played FS15 and 17 and they were fun. i didn't ever play 19 but when FS22 came out i had extreme hopes of awesome things they would have done to the game. but it feels like a copy paste. FS's physics engine is the same from 15 and you feel like you are driving a static block with a hitbox and vehicles dont seem to have weight like real equipment. logging trucks feel like a cylinder when loaded instead of having actual weight. tractors that take turns flip like an upright book but after tipping they just kinda magnetize themselves back on all 4 wheels. bumps in the terrain dont make you feel like you are on real ground but rather on a grid with random bumps. gathering, placing, plowing, and editing all is still done on a gridlike platform instead of a more sophisticated and realistic pattern. tires and plows dont leave ruts and driving over crops doesn't do much other than create a "delete your product" line from where your tracks were. not asking for any BeamNG destruction, but there is absolutely no damage modeling in the game other from how long you use the equipment making wreckless driving very forgiving. vehicle sounds are extremely basic, shifting gears on manual vehicles seems very automatic and braking/stopping feels like a over exaggerated ABS system.This sounds like a gaming Karen complaint but holy hell, the series is over 10 years old going into 2025 and games from 2007 were excelling in physics (GTA4 A revolutionary game). take ideas from mudrunner/snowrunner. Spintires has been out since 2012 and leaves ground deformations and tire/mud trails even after shutting off the game and loading back in. I'm sad to say that even though farming sim is satisfying to grow crops, earn money, make your own fields, and understand some interesting stuff about farming, its just not cutting it anymore. for a game that sells at a triple A price and a large fan base, it doesnt seem the developers care enough to make an overhual or remaster change to the game and if 2025 is going to be the same way, I'm sorry, i wont be getting it..

_childDocuments_.review: I wake up around 9 AM. Today is April. I yawn and see the sun rise from the south. It's going to be another great day here at Elm Creek.Anyway, I immediately teleport out of my bed and into my MF tractor. Gotta get the cultivating in as soon as I can before the tractor breaks. I get about a good work hour or two out of it before the transmission turns to dust. Must be a new model that was outsourced to China or some non-sense.Once the field is cultivated with a stubble texture from the previous crop (hey man, I don't ask questions anymore), I immediately teleport on over to my greenhouse. Ah, the greenhouse. I check to see if it's watered up and it is, this thing pulls in lots of money for me on auto-sell. The magicians down the local grocery mart pay a good price, can't finangle what that really is though, but they enjoy their liters of lettuce!Anyhoo, once the greenhouses are all fixed up I decide to check out my tree farm. The willows just don't want to sprout dag nabbit, but all the other trees around them have become giants! Unfortunately for me, the local sawmill got filled up on wood and they won't accept any more trees! They're quite fussed about the situation after I gave them about 8 trees, told me they can only process about 6 trees a year. Labor shortage I guess. Anyway...I decide to stockpile up on the wood by chainsawing a pine. Suddenly after I cut through it, I'm voided into a realm of nothingness and quickly returned back. This is strange, but I shrug. The local devil worshippers have been spotted in this part of town, putting hexes on my trees. I'm going to have to talk to the local priest about that this week.Once I decide to leave the devil tree alone I head on over to my chicken farm. These guys are amazing. I don't even know why I do anything else to be honest, probably just to pass the time. I load up several pallets of eggs onto my lowloader trailer and immediately get into a head on collision with a local. They shrug it off after wiping the eggs off their windshield and give me the finger and go on their way. Damn city slickers always in a hurry.The local grocer takes my eggs for about $100,000. Hipsters pay a lot for eggs these days, all the rage. I don't get it though but like I said, I don't ask questions.It's only about 11AM now so I decide to help out my neighbor with some work he's paying up for. I rent some of his equipment and decide to help him harvest his wheat. Damndest thing, harvesting wheat in April but that's how it goes here down in Elm Creek. Once I finish up the job he claims it's not done and won't pay me. We argue a bit but then he cancels the contract. Folks just aren't nice anymore like they used to be in the old days I guess.Anyhoo I return home to my dog Ivory. He's been out running around for a while and hasn't eaten in months. Doesn't phase him though. He is still slowly playful as ever. Scamp loves going out into traffic! Haha!After a long day of farming and running chores, I decide to just go to bed. Tomorrow is May after all! It's about 1PM and that's enough for me. Farming is the simple life, and I wouldn't have it any other way.Game could be made to be a great horror game for my channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this series on FS19, and FS22 is a big improvement.  The most significant thing is being able to assign workers to drive vehicles to other spots on the map, or to make a delivery and return to the original location.  Some of the larger equipment might get caught on a bridge or bug out, but all-in-all it makes those parts of the game less tedious.  There is also animals, bees, and other content included right in the base game.  My family got this for me as a gift and didn't get any content packs or anything.  The other significant change is production lines, which seem very cool, although I don't have much experience yet because I'm playing on hard mode and doing lots of contracts.  It's nice to sit and have a beer and listen to the online radio while harvesting cotton or potatoes.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite more than 200 critical reported bugs in FS22 over 2.5 years, the game remains incredibly buggy, unfinished, and performance is still terrible. As Giants continue on their effort to prove to the whole world how utterly incompetent and unprofessional they are by refusing to acknowledge the buggy mess they've created, the game still requires a good dozen mods to work properly and be at all enjoyable to play for more than a few hours. If it wasn't for the modders, every version of Farming Simulator would be a ginormous waste of time and money, FS22 included. For a company that's done nothing but release the same game over and over for 15 years with only negligible and barely noticeable changes, it's mindblowingly mystifying that they flat out refuse to work on that very same game. Instead of working on their only product, Giants instead focuses on procuring licenses for as many brands as possible, with zero consideration for how relevant those products are to the game. Thus we have a dozen (buggy) DLC where the majority are effectively repaints of existing stuff and thus not remotely worth the price tag. Despite of these issues, the game is now officially abandoned and will never be completed, as Giants is now about to release the next enumeration of this game.For FS22, Giants spent a year in lockdown ripping off mods, while failing to adequately credit the more than two dozen mod creators for their work. Thus what makes FS22 different from FS19 was 99% the work of modders. There are no graphical improvements over previous games, no performance improvements, it still fails to utilize the hardware properly, and it is by far the most buggy version of FS yet as Giants stopped supporting the base game within a month after release and instead shifted all their limited resources to developing DLC, for a game that remains broken and only barely functions as intended.The overall performance problems remain the biggest problem, thanks to the game running everything off a single CPU core - despite Giants promising multithreaded performance improvements for FS22. This design (or lack thereof) means the framerate still tanks massively at random for no explicable reason. The game is also still unstable and it is very easy to get it to lock up just by having more than 3-4 helpers going at the same time. And because the game only runs on a single core, throwing higher performance hardware at it makes zero difference, the game simply can't utilize it.Speaking of helpers, they're if anything worse than ever. Just as useless as they've been in the past 12 years since the system was introduced to FS09, but now they're even more glitchy and will happily stop in the middle of a field for "unknown error". They still won't stay on the field, they still turn around in crops and need a whole field to turn around because they don't know how to make 3-point turns, they ♥♥♥♥♥ about stuff "in the way" way outside the field where they shouldn't be going anyway, they won't follow the edge of the fields, and the list goes on and on. The pile of problems with these games keeps getting bigger with each release because Giants refuse to fix anything before releasing the next buggy DLC, which means each release and each "update" results in an even buggier and broken game than the last.

_childDocuments_.review: A really interesting, slow pace game that you can put hours into. A highly dedicated Modding Community that produces new maps, vehicles, fully automated new productions and machinery, sometimes with stunnig details. While the collision model for crashes with (the now faster but still sometimes too slow) AI traffic is not on par with other modern games but can be put aside, since you can also deactivate the AI traffic in your game settings. Cheating through commands is also an option, but usually Mods will offer you a great deal for your buck! All in all it's a great game that you can sink hours into, since it doesn't really have an end. Your opportunities are endless, from RPs to Multiplayer or just some single player farming, all that is possible and makes it a really versatile game for people that want to have fun while doing virtual Farming. A tip: if your PC can handle big maps, look up some times 4 or times 16 scaled Maps online since they are huge and you have even more options, depending on the individual Map. Features:**detailed, life size Models of brand name machinery****Single Player** **Multiplayer** through dedicated servers, paid servers or hosting your own game locally on your system**Mod support** **Season Pass** (optional and really not needed)**Cheating optional** with, so far, no repercussions for cheating people (MP servers may have different guidelines concerning the use of cheats, please beware)**comes with three Maps "out of the box"**** great online Community**
