_childDocuments_.review: Farming Simulator 22 is the game you never knew you needed until you find yourself genuinely excited about planting virtual corn at 2 AM. Yes, it’s a farming game, and yes, you will actually enjoy it. Surprised? So was I.The graphics are good. You get to drive tractors. Sometimes, you even get to drive big tractors. If that doesn’t get your heart racing, I don’t know what will. The fields are vast, and you’ll spend hours plowing, sowing, and harvesting. If you thought real farming was dull, well, you’re not wrong. But somehow, in this game, it’s oddly satisfying.There’s also a lot of farming equipment to buy. Like, a lot. You’ll probably end up spending more time picking out your next combine harvester than you did picking out your last car. But hey, it’s all part of the charm. After all, nothing says "fun" like comparing virtual seed drills.Now, let’s talk about the multiplayer. If you ever wanted to see just how incompetent your friends can be, this is the perfect test. Watching them fumble around, crashing tractors into each other, or spending half an hour trying to figure out how to attach a plow is pure comedy gold. It’s like herding cats, except the cats are somehow less intelligent and more annoying. Instead of working together, you’ll be too busy facepalming as one idiot drives your best tractor straight into a lake while another genius decides it’s a good idea to plant wheat in the middle of your perfectly organized cornfield.But the real joy comes when the game itself decides to join the fun. The multiplayer is so bugged and laggy that you’ll start to wonder if the developers coded it while blindfolded. You’ll watch as your friends teleport around the map like they’re in a low-budget sci-fi movie, and good luck trying to get anything done when the game lags so badly that even driving in a straight line becomes an exercise in frustration. Teamwork? Forget it. You’ll spend more time cursing the lag and bugs than actually farming.In the end, Farming Simulator 22 is a weirdly enjoyable experience. It’s slow-paced, repetitive, and oddly calming. So, if you’re looking for a game where you can unwind by doing virtual chores, this is it. And who knows? You might even learn a thing or two about farming. Or at least learn how to spend a ridiculous amount of time driving in straight lines.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite fun and challenging. It is a huge improvement from previous games in the series. The build mode is excellent, and the general game play (fieldwork, animal husbandry, etc.) is quite fun as well. Generally, I have no complaints about the game play itself. Why then, can I not recommend the game? The progression in the beginning is absurd. This is a problem with simulator games generally, but this game is too difficult to progress through for the average person. Take for example trying to start a vineyard in Haut-Beyleron. Total costs to set everything up eat up nearly half a million dollars. This leaves one starting on the hard start with nearly twenty thousand left over. After harvesting the grapes, buying the fertilizer, etc. the harvest yields...$5600. That is a tad over 5% of the cost to set everything up. That is less than half of the cost to lease the grape harvester. Realising that this was done on the hard start, starting a farm on any of the other starts yields similar results. The developers have decided to have a game that is hyper-realistic instead of one that provides meaningful or rewarding game play. I cannot progress at any pace or in any direction except backward. The costs and the rewards are completely out of sync, unless one settles up and starts a solar farm. Solar panels yield nearly $9000/month and cost only $75 000/panel to set up. This is more than one could make FARMING in a FARMING SIMULATOR. If you enjoy purely the game play from the previous games, then you will probably enjoy the game play here. That is the only reason to play, since the progression is so stunted that you will have no fun playing for longer than ten or so hours.

_childDocuments_.review: For me reviewing this game is not as binary as Yes or No, and I'll explain why.I appreciate that Giants have been developing this game since 2008 - I've only played it since 2019 but what I'm not seeing is anything other than a reskin here and adaption of the best community mods into the main game.  And not even all of them. Positives: - production pocesses are pretty cool, and add another dimension to the game along with seasons.  Although I seriously ran out of steam trying to play single player.  It rebalances the value of various crops so it's worth growing pretty much anything. - there's always a lot to do if you're playing multiplayer so you're not going to get bored (I mean, I play once a week) - the graphics are slightly shinier, I guess...... but honestly I'm not seeing a huge difference here.I could go on here but most of it is just mods from the previous game incorporated into the main title, notably seasons, global company, and courseplay.  The thing is though, they haven't really added anything NEW to the game - I mean stuff that wasn't there before if you were all modded up. It's not a bad game, it's actually fun, it's just......Numerous glaring deficiencies in the UI and game engine remain from the 2019 version - which begs the question what were they doing for 3 years?  Just brainstorming new DLC ideas? Here are just a few.Game Engine: - extremely outdated  and frankly hopeless physics. (eg tree remain standing when you chop them down) - idiotic AI.  I mean don't expect a helper to do any job without you having to go back and do it again afterwards. - Limited graphical rendering after about 100 metres (it means you can see fields being harvested but by invisible tractors, and because objects are rendered but crops aren't an object in the field is visible from far away but hidden when you get close.  This is only for starters, really. - glitches, just everywhere - when it gets dark it's like a 50s movie when they shoot in the daytime but turn the brightness down.  It's rubbish.Clearly a new game engine is needed, and I was expecting it for '22 given the time they spent on it - instead it's just a re-skin, all the exact same problems remain.UI: - in 2019 settings were remembered from session to session for each vehicle (for example for courseplay and for GPS).  It's particularly annoying with courseplay when you have to disable the right click pop up every single login, or GPS when you have to turn the lines on every time you use it).  When it comes to courseplay none of the peopole I play with can work out how to use it in-game - the mods from 2019 were actually way easier to use.  I miss them.- there is still no mouseover or such like telling you what each of the crop symbols represent, or some such.  As a casual player this is a pain in the... well you know what it's a pain in.  WHICH ONE IS WHEAT????- the finance screen still only gives you the last 7 days (months, whatever), and no breakdown beyond the most simplistic.- the shop screens are improved by being able to see related vehicles, but it's still hard to find anything.Generally speaking it feels like the UI is designed as a mish mash for both console and PC.  The resolution gives that away as it's not configured at all for higher res screens with even smaller icons than before.  If you want to be multi platform one size fits all doesn't work.  You think they'd learn that by now.It's also been simplified - animals do not require water (I mean really?), and produce fewer products (eg cows no longer produce manure).  This is clearly driven by cross platform requirements.  But why?  If I wanted a Playstation game I'd buy a Playstation.  But I don't.  I want a grown up PC game please.What I wish it had!! - A proper sim element.  That this is missing is just lazy.  You could have full historical breakdowns of what you've sold, when you've sold it, how much, your income, graphs, charts, all sorts of cool stuff.  All the data is there in their database.  You could have all sorts of info you could actually use to make your farm more efficient.  Instead there is the same useless rolling week by week update from the last game.  To move from just a driving around in tractors sim to actually being a farming sim surely this has to be addressed?  It's a massive disappointment and missed opportunity in the game, which would not be difficult at all to implement.  Railroad tycoon in 1992 had better.  Actually, Sim city in 1989 had better. There is no excuse! - An new graphics engine.  The current one is glitchy, the physics are terrible, and it slows down at the slightest provocation.  Trees are still ridiculous. The default in multiplayer is you can't have more than 100 pallets in the game.  In a production based game.  Then try it with 3 people.  it takes about a day before you hit the limit.  but once you go beyond it you see why.  Try moving a load of pallets at once.  you'll see. - better servers.  Nobody would disagree. - Has anyone tried removing olive trees?  How do you even do that??What the game didn't need: - more processes.  Does anyone really have lime, periodic ploughing, stones, weeding switched on all the time?  Does anyone roll their fields?  Just get the basics right please Giants, THEN add more stuff for us to turn off. - conveyor belts you have to sit in to operate - is this even a thing?  Factorio would be in trouble with this mechanic. - more DLCs.  Platinum is out soon.  Surely that's just a bunch of features the base game should have had when it was rushed out in the first place??  Now the modding community is catching up.... no thanks guys.I enjoy this game, I play this game regularly, but it is no better than its predecessor.  In some ways it is actually worse.  I would say it's a disappointment, but it's not because it was entirely expected.  So I'll just call it another missed opportunity to create something great.

_childDocuments_.review: **Title: "10/10 Would Farm Again (And Probably Lose More Animals)"**⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Look, I didn’t *ask* to become a digital farmer, but this game roped me in with its promises of "peaceful rural life" and "simple farming." Let me tell you, it’s anything but simple. I came for the virtual cows, stayed for the unrelenting panic that I might accidentally let my crops die while I’m trying to figure out how to get my dog to stop running in circles. You start off by building a farm, and for the first few minutes, you’re like, “Yeah, I got this. I’ll plant some tomatoes, pet a few cows, maybe get a chicken or two.” But then, BOOM. Suddenly you’re knee-deep in *farming bureaucracy*, setting up irrigation systems, building a barn, and trying to figure out why your one goat is somehow stuck in a tree. No one warned me about this level of stress. I just wanted to grow some corn, not become a rural real estate mogul. **The crops**: Don’t let the simplicity fool you. You’ll spend hours planting, watering, and *fearing* the weather. I got so attached to my turnips that I had a meltdown when a storm rolled in and ruined my entire harvest. I don’t even know what I was doing with my life before I started giving speeches to my carrots, but here we are.**The animals**: Adorable? Absolutely. Easy to manage? Hahahaha, no. You spend your days trying to keep your chickens from escaping (they’re literally Houdinis) while simultaneously managing your cows, sheep, and a pig who seems to think it’s okay to just *wander* into the neighbor’s yard. I lost a pig once. No, really—I have no idea where it went. I just looked away for a second and now there’s an empty pen. If you can’t handle the emotional toll of losing a virtual animal, maybe rethink your life choices.**The machinery**: This is where it gets *real*—and by real, I mean you’ll spend 80% of your time trying to figure out how to drive a tractor without crashing into your own barn. Honestly, the farming is the easy part. The logistics are a nightmare. I’ve spent more time in this game learning how to attach a plow to a tractor than I did in high school math. **The relationships**: Ah yes, the social aspect. You can talk to townspeople, give them gifts, and eventually marry one of them (which, let’s be real, is just a distraction from the never-ending grind of harvesting wheat). My one regret? I spent more time working on my farm than I did wooing my *virtual* spouse. So now I’m married, but the only thing we do together is stare at our farm and wonder where we went wrong.In conclusion: This game is a toxic, all-consuming love affair that I didn’t ask for but will continue to play until my crops wither and my virtual barn burns down (which I’m pretty sure is the *next* step). If you’re looking for a calming experience, I’ve got news for you: you won’t find it here. But if you want to experience the sweet, sweet chaos of owning a farm and maybe lose a chicken or two along the way, then this is the game for you.P.S. If anyone sees my missing pig, please DM me. It’s the one with the *really* smug look on its face.

_childDocuments_.review: Having several hours in playtime currently there are quite a few improvements overall. I've been playing the FS series all the way back since 2011. I do really like the game and was hyped for it, but I feel like there could really be some improvements. This review is more along the lines of being netural but I feel in the best interests to leave it as being positive for now as theres room for improvements.Some pros:- Better graphics -Somewhat better vehicle sounds.-Quite a few choices for maps, (They all look nice and giants seem like they did a good job in detailing them and etc).- Some vehicle handling and physics seem to be improved.-Ground textures and things related to that seem a bit better than fs19.-New grape and olive plants and equipment related to all that.-MACK trucks added to game that are licensed.-Production chains.Cons:- For some weird and odd reason everytime I go to exit my game it never takes me back to the main menu screen like it did in fs19. This may very well be a bug but its getting pretty annoying that it just exits and closes the game completely and I have to click on the icon or go through steam to launch it again just to get back to the main menu.-The in game builder is a bit horrible right now. When I try to place down a building or fences for instance, it never seems to be fully placed on the ground or gets placed in a weird way and so far I cannot find a way to adjust the objects height placement like in fs19.- There's just not in my opinion that many more vehicle options compared to fs19 and what giants advertised. While this is not a big deal and there are some new vehicles it just feels the same as fs19's vehicle options.- It seems like the MACK trucks have a hard time trying to drive and or switch through gears. I use an xbox controller and have all vehicles set to auto transmission and everytime I use a MACK truck with a trailer or whatever it always won't go or get stuck when it really shouldn't at all and its quite frustrating at times.But giving some of my pros and cons and experiences here, I am going to leave my review as recommended as its a very good game, it just needs some improvements and things to make it better. If your on fs19 still and are thinking of picking up fs22, I would say if your really into farming and simulation like I am most of the time, I would say its worth it overall for picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game for a good 6 hours together with a friend. I will state that this is my first entry of the Farming Simulator franchise, and the first time playing, though with an co-op partner experienced with the previous entries.- Waypoint markers sometimes do not even remotely point to where you need to unload the harvested goods. The map marker for canola on the map Erlengrat pointed to the far east limit of the map, next to the biogas station, when the ACTUAL objective marker was a point more toward the middle of the map along the train tracks.- Infuriating vehicle control. I'm not expecting arcade controls, but backing up with a trailer is a *chore*.- You get stuck on EVERYTHING. Lamp posts that would realistically snap like a twig completely stop you in your tracks. So does traffic. Or a bush. And don't get me started on the times I was got stuck on a low wall with no way of resetting myself.- You can play co-op. Cool. You can't ride together in a pickup that clearly has a passenger seat. What?- "Very high" graphics settings still deliver a horrible draw distance. You need to manually adjust this in the advanced settings.- For long-time fans of the series, this might feel more at home, but I was a bit stumped on some of the mechanics.- Graphical glitches here or there which are negligable, but at some point, our HUD just went blank with no way of refreshing it.Honestly, the game kept reminding me SO much of the ArmA 3 mod Altis Life, where you do jobs around the island and trade. Just without an ounce of fun. Or any kind of excitement. OrThe funniest moment in gameplay was when I just rammed my friend's truck off the road with the harvester to see what happens. It tips sideways, he had no way to right himself, and I had to ram him from the other side.All in all, with the current state it's in, it is NOT worth the price tag. It feels like a beta at full price, with a season pass potentially doubling that initial cost. I will probably give it another chance after it has had some time for bugfixes and patches, but this will likely be the last FS game I buy from here on out.

_childDocuments_.review: My honest review of the game... Back story, I have been playing Farming Simulator since before it joined steam. FS 2011, 13, 15, 17, 19, and now 22.  It has progressed tremendously over its life especially from its very beginnings. Its awesome world wide modding community made the game fun and then they were incorporated into the next gen of the game.  I have enjoyed watching the game expand and add wood, animals, and whole new lines of crops. I especially like the use of real machinery that I see rolling down the roads of my home area.  My kids even comment on it. "Isn't that the harvester you use in your game dad?" Its fun to see how these things can really impact our world.The Good:   -Amazing Modding community   -Incorporation of mods into next generation game   -New Crop lines to harvest   -Real World Machinery   -Great maps to explore    -Go to feature for workers to move equipment   -New construction page is niceSince FS22 came out I have noticed a lot more nickle and diming of the community then is past generations.  Even if you go to the Giant Software site for the Farming Simulator Franchise you will notice how most of the additions to games were mods that added value to the base game.  Then they started coming out with Platinum additions.  This I was ok with.  You can buy the base game if you just wanted to play but if you wanted the extended content you would purchase the next level Platinum Expansion.  I did this every time until FS22.  Now the Platinum is just another DLC jumbled into their season passes.  I really enjoy the game but when i have to pay and additional $80 for Season Passes DLC that should be incorporated into the game it makes me hesitate and ask myself.... is it worth it.. Unfortunately at this time I can't say yes.The Bad:   -Asking to much for DLC that doesn't add much to the game   -The grind of working is FS22 to make money is worse then previous Gens   -The Landscape tool is still not the best but an improvement from FS19   -Forestry still needs some work   -Can's remove some objects to clear path for larger fields. Overall: I still say that FS22 is a good game to play. I do recommend it and I think its a good addition to the Franchise.  Please spend your money responsibly and I see you out in the fields.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may be very good at the end of the day but I'm pretty sure I'll never know. As a first time player trying to pick up the series with FS22 I can honestly say that this is the single most newbie un-friendly video game I have experienced in my entire life. It's like the devs just assumed that anyone playing this game has been playing for years. Players are provided with absolutely 0 guidance in the game. When I say it tells you nothing I mean - literally - absolutely nothing is explained. The main screen will link you to a glorified wiki page that they call a tutorial and I suppose if you want to spend 3 hours reading before you're able to play that could maybe get the job done but even that was pretty lacking in terms of actually providing any kind of structured guidance on how to actually play the game. There are also in-game "guides" in the menu but those are like an even less helpful version of the afore-mentioned wiki. And just to be clear I'm not the type of gamer that needs or even wants every single thing explained to me. I actually kind of hate games that are too hand-holdy and railroad you into playing a certain way because of it. Two of my favorite games ever are Rimworld and Kenshi. So, yeah, I'm OK with a game that gives you the basics and expects you to figure it out from there. This game doesn't give you that though. It drops you in the middle of a map and leaves you to it. After two hours of play all I had gotten out of the game was an overwhelming sense of frustration and boredom. Even after figuring something out I didn't feel any sense of satisfaction. More like "thank god that is over" before the crushing realization that I was about to have to start the process over again to figure out the next step. Back to the drawing board, oh whoops, look I just bought an attachment that apparently doesn't work on my tractor again. Sure would be great if the game gave any kind of indication of whether x piece of equipment will work with y tractor. Or maybe it does but I sure as heck couldn't find anything. There's that whole "0 guidance" thing cropping up again. I can not recommend this game to anyone who hasn't played the series before. If you've played in the past or are OK with spending hours reading through a wiki before playing the game then maybe it's for you. There could be a great game under there but at this point I feel like it's unlikely I'll ever find out because as of right now at least I have little interest in ever picking it up again unless they do something to make it less of a chore for new players.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great example of why more realism isn't always better.  If you've always dreamed of doing the hard work, tedium, and sacrifice of real-life work, but with none of the pay, this might be the game for you.Farming Simulator is kind of fun as a learning experience about modern agriculture, and it's relaxing in a way, but bizarre and frustrating decisions by the developers wreck the experience.For example, there's an insistence on hyper-realistic vehicle movement in some situations (such as loading pallets onto forklifts or bales onto loaders) but "stop-the-vehicle-and-hit-a-button" game logic in other situations (such as loading pallets of fertilizer onto spreaders, or refueling your tractors).  It'd be fine if everything worked by hitting a button, or if the  system hadn't been conceived by zero-G aliens who had never experienced gravity.  The combination certainly gets you the worst of both worlds.Steering your vehicle at all is a skill in itself; which would be fine, if the handling didn't work using a 90s-style all-or-nothing keypress system.  This makes it difficult and tedious (Penn & Teller's -style) to keep your vehicle going in straight lines.  It's better with a gamepad, but still not as good as it needs to be.There are lots of quality-of-life issues too.  The tutorial explains a fraction of the most basic concepts, the in-game documentation doesn't go into nearly enough detail, and the missing information is primarily available through  videos.  Hope you enjoy spending 10 minutes to find information you could read in 30 seconds; you'll be doing it a half-dozen times to answer basic questions about how the game is supposed to work.On top of that, the UI feels like it saw Microsoft's bungling of Windows 11 as a challenge to do worse.  On top of all the modern-style low-contrast one-color idiocy, you have two separate main menus.  The in-menu map doesn't automatically update when your fields are worked; you have to manually switch menus to update.  The icons for keyboard shortcuts are extremely unclear, and confirmation dialogs are inconsistent, leading to poor discoverability.  Dialogs have a minimum wait time before accepting input, making the use of shortcuts frustrating.But wait, there's more!  Scroll wheels don't always work in the menus for some reason.  There's no way to sleep for multiple days at a time, and the best solution apparently is a mod that just speeds up time.  AI workers sometimes randomly decide that they've finished a job with half a field left unworked.  There doesn't seem to be a way to set up permanent jobs, so that a worker can be easily re-hired to do a task you don't like doing.  You can export some things by train, but not others -- how is the single grocery in town supposed to sell your fifth consecutive shipment of a hundred thousand liters of Canola oil?In spite of its unexpected compellingness, surface polish, and sheer potential, Farming Simulator just doesn't make the grain.  Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game currently and there are 2 major reasons why.1. It needs big QC pass. There's too many issues, like contracts that cost more to complete than they pay. I had one where it cost me 22k in seeds to plant a potato field, but the contract only paid 16k. I had another contract to harvest crop and deliver to Grain South, which I did 100%, however the game thought I only did 85%, so it wouldn't complete. I ended up having to cancel, and it charged me for the missing crop. I had 1 other contract to bail and deliver. It used round bails and while I figured out how to make the bails and load them, I could not figure out how to deliver them. There was zero information on how to drop the bails at the target. Maybe that's a bit on me, but also a bit on the game for not explaining how to accomplish something like this. That contract also cancelled and cost me money.2. The major changes are hit or miss, and most, like Seasonal crops, can be turned off thankfully. However, 1 change that can't be justified is that you cannot speed up crop growth as in years past. Most crops take months to grow, and so your're stuck hitting the "sleep" button several times in a row to get your harvest. Speeding up time doesn't do anything towards this. There should at least be a toggle to adjust how long you sleep for in months so you don't have to deal with this tedium, however it still isn't a good change overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh geeze, where to start...Been playing FS since 2017.  Nice incremental improvements in 2019 and then in 2022, but I'm underwhelmed, especially considering that FS2022 has been full price (and more than previous releases) for almost a year before the first sale.  When I say "full price", I mean close to AAA games.  FS is NOT a AAA title, and worse, there's still plenty of add-on content to purchase to get everything, such as "Platinum Edition" which doesn't include Year 1 Season, Year 2 Season, etc... ok, anyways, let's get behind pricing and value (bang for your buck).CaseIH has been mostly nerfed in FS2022.  It's probably not the only brand but the most noticeable for me coming from FS'19.  I get that John Deere is the new hot commodity -- and I suspect that the licensing deal is part of the explanation for increased pricing -- but come on, did we really have to make it THIS obvious?  Several CaseIH models are missing and some that are in the game are almost a joke.  It's almost like each release of Farm Sim is now going to be themed around a specific brand.  Is that really the way to go?  Lol, no, because it's just not right.Ok, so some are thinking I'm a brand loyalist at this point.  Let me REALLY get into the nitty-gritty now. !!! PROS !!!*Runs well on Ryzen 7000-series (almost no CPU utilization) and Radeon RX 7900 XT (about 50% utilization at 1440p @ 60 Hz, max settings).  DX12 introduction new for FS22 is NICE -- almost introduces a problem where it's TOO GPU bound and not enough CPU bound, lol.  Not complaining here though -- TY devs.  Not sure where Vulkan stands though...*Crop seasons, raw variety of different equipment to purchase, and great native mod support are definitely wins.* Multiplayer is nice... even if it has a lot of room for improvement (I elaborate on this later)* Physics seems to have improved, though it's still not like that found in SnowRunner and some other sims/excellent off-road physics games**ADDED 25JUN2023:  I'm generally enjoying the game enough to continue logging hours on it, so it's not all doom and gloom, lol.  I did have to recover an auto-saved game after my son sold a bunch of my equipment for some other "fun stuff" that wasn't really practical... anyways, my point is that I appreciate that relatively robust save-game system.  The wife has been playing Sims 4 for like 10 years and still no auto-save, LMAO.!!! CONS !!!* CaseIH and other brands being nerfed or less models available in favor of John Deere* Only four maps?  Really!?* Rolling can't be turned off.  Not a common thing in the U.S. Midwest so kind of odd...* Limited number of online radio stations; why can't this be more easily customized??* Bushes are hard to get rid of -- painting ground textures (grass, gravel, etc.) is the only guaranteed bet but costs money* Landscaping is EXPENSIVE, **EDIT 25JUN2023** IDEA: Should be able to simulate changes and then choose to commit or discard* The economy on medium difficulty is a bit expensive for equipment repairs (degrades condition too fast) and crops pay a bit low even with near 100% yield bonus which takes a lot of time to achieve such yields  **EDIT 25JUN2023** I also realize that passive income like animals, solar, etc. is a smart way to boost earnings, but either grain sales pays a little too low or maintenance costs/deteriation speed is too aggressive* Contracted jobs pay low, especially when using one's own equipment (after factoring fuel and repairs) and for certain jobs types* Contracted jobs seem to get stuck... e.g. baling and others that *EDIT* take a long time to  move on unless you complete them or at least start them and purposely fail them* Having AI operate one's equipment is too expensive unless the very largest tractors, harvesters, implements, etc. is used, and even then profit margin is still questionable* Variety of side-by-sides and farm trucks is laughable... modded trucks provide a way better value and more worthwhile, even for users trying to be "ultra-realistic".  * Multiplayer should have an option for "realistic" vs. "arcade" whereas realistic means players don't ignore equipment boxes (falling inside and thru tractors, etc.) while arcade is the current style "players of equipment they aren't driving around bound to there dimensions and therefore "fall right through"* Multiplayer should have a manual or automatic refresh option; my friend will create a game, but if I join too early, it doesn't show and won't ever show until I back all the way back out and go into 'Multiplayer' -> 'Join Game' again* Similar to equipment condition, paint condition degrades WAAAYYYY too quickly, even for equipment that is stored under a shed or whatever with a roof and is properly maintained*  There should be some kind of system for discounts, specials, etc. on seed, fertilizer, and other typically-palletized/bagged products.* Still no tractor cab doors and windows that can't be opened unless its modded?  SAD times.* Almost all manual and powershift transmissions are gone in tractors... B.S.!  This relates back to the fact that some brands don't have models from 10, 20, 30 years ago.  How about we have a "used market" for older equipment models; not every farmer wishes to purchase a brand-new, 0 hours tractor.* Maps need to get bigger; semi trucks and other fast vehicles can get from one side to another in no time.  Maybe variable map sizes need to at least become an option the future, with higher-end systems able to play on those larger map sizes (talking stock, not just modded)* No ability to control left/right brake pedals, diff locks, and 2WD vs. 4WD on capable tractors* Tractors with CVT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ still seem to rev high even when engine load is very low *EDIT 25JUN2023:  Not enough PowerShift or other manual/semi-manual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  I think this also reflects that there should be more older-model tractors in the game as many farmers turn to the used market; buying 15-30 year old tractors in the U.S. is a very common practice* Houses, sheds, etc. don't overcome chopped down trees, resulting in some weird foundations and auto-landscaping effects.  Their placement should either require complete elimation of trees and stumps or just raise the price of installation and automatically include the removal (my preference but maybe this could be a setting?)* Loans should have more detail to them, e.g. lines of credit (similar to how it's down now on a monthly basis in small $5K increments) with more formal loans in larger allotments offering more specific pay-off and interest terms* Ability to buy other farm houses, sheds, etc. on property that is purchased* The high pressure washer isn't mobile and costs $5K?  Really?EDIT (ADD):  * NPC traffic likes to turn right in front of you, causing a crash, even when one's own speed is constant, i.e. they should be able to calculate and predict if they should wait to turn or go ahead and make the turn.  They are aggressive drivers as it currently stands.EDIT (ADD):  * When you purchase a dog, he/she runs in slow motion.  It literally had me and my son laughing out loud.  Otherwise, it's a nice touch and fun to play ball with him/her.** EDIT (ADD) on 25JUN2023:  would really like to frame rate limiting natively built-in.This may start to sound like a rant but when you charge near-AAA pricing for a game, one expects near-AAA features and such.  Furthermore, detailed feedback is how I believe the most important, juicy changes will come about, not high-level crabbing and moaning.  All these cons take away my enjoyment from this game, adding up in such a way that either has me not wanting to play anymore or at times thinking "man, FS'25 is going to be a real money-grab, huh?  Guess I won't touch FS anymore."  Nothing against the gaming business model of having DLC to add content and increase margin but a game like the FS franchise can't charge BOTH a high entry cost for the base game and tons in add-ons/DLC's and such.

_childDocuments_.review: A calm game for when I want to play something but don't feel like sucker punching zombies, running from murderous ghosts, or shooting everything that moves. So far I've played this in singleplayer and co-op modes, and this is what I've observed:Pros:- Nice graphics.- Good variety of machinery, equipment, and crops to choose from.- Plenty of jobs to take to earn money while you're waiting for your own crops to grow.- Lots of settings you can adjust to make the gameplay more to your liking.- Lots of nice mods accessible right from the start screen to make it more interesting.- In Co-op mode, you can either work the same farm together, or run separate farms on the same map, each making their own money. You can share equipment either way, and transfer money to each other if you choose the latter.Cons:- It took 20 minutes of Google searches and a lot of trial and error to get Co-op mode to work.- Pallet loading is glitchy: be prepared to chase the ones that fly off across the field at random.- Walking too close to buildings and most other things is glitchy: getting stuck is a thing.- The AI workers are wonky: they get your equipment stuck in bad places, and quit whenever they please.- The terrain leveler only works when it feels like it.- If you aren't a farmer IRL and you collect a lot of equipment, moving your cursor over an implement only to get a mini popup that says something like "GUMDORK BINKOFLYEMER 729" is NOT useful in identifying said item. Would it have killed them to add "cultivator" (or whatever) to the popup?- Deer are everywhere, but you can't kill them with a chainsaw nor squash them with trucks (tested and verified). You can't even run with a chainsaw wtf.None of the Cons are game-breaking for me, but rather just annoying. That said, while I would recommend the game to others looking for something laid-back to play, I'd also suggest waiting until it's on sale to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: In the quietude of my study, I find myself drawn to the contemplation of a game that mirrors the very essence of human endeavor: Farming Simulator 22. This digital creation, much like the creature of my own literary imagination, is a testament to the relentless pursuit of mastery over nature.Upon my initial engagement with this simulation, I was struck by the meticulous attention to detail, a reflection of the tireless labor that defines the agrarian life. The game, in its essence, is a symphony of soil and toil, where each seed sown and harvest reaped is a testament to human ingenuity and perseverance.Features: The game offers a vast array of machinery and tools, each rendered with exquisite precision. One may cultivate fields, tend to livestock, and manage the intricate logistics of a thriving farm. The seasonal cycles, a new addition, bring a dynamic rhythm to the gameplay, echoing the eternal dance of life and death.Drawbacks: As with all creations of great complexity, there are imperfections. The tutorials, though well-intentioned, may leave newcomers adrift in a sea of information. Yet, these are but minor flaws in an otherwise grand design.In conclusion, if you are one who finds solace in the rhythm of the land and the satisfaction of a well-tended field, I implore you to immerse yourself in Farming Simulator 22. It is a journey of discovery and fulfillment, a digital ode to the timeless art of farming.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really isn't well made or thought out.Let's get the first, and most obvious problem out of the way. Despite the ideal scenario of a studio optimizing their product, I'm running this game significantly over recommended spec, and still getting choppy and laggy gameplay - that's with and without mods active in the game. I'm not sure which element is the problem, the graphics are only minimally better than its predecessor which runs significantly better on my system with 100+ mods active, so I'm not really sure who to point fingers at here. Overall, the game's playability is almost impossible at this point, so that's the first and most glaring issue.Let's address other issues, small as they may seem, they make a difference. - Firstly, I understand the studio is not US-based, but they seem to have really put no effort into replicating US-based maps accurately. The fields in the US are very much larger than what their maps would indicate. I know farms that have front yards bigger than half the fields on the US map, not including the fact that our fields are many, many acres larger. Not a great replication and really makes me think that the map-making effort was negligible when account for the US based players. Elements of the game that could be optimized?- Running into cars is like hitting the edge of the map. I'm certain when a Deere X9 1100 hits a compact sedan, the sedan doesn't stop the combine. It's not that hard to make even just slightly more realistic collisions with vehicles. - Surface textures of roads, driveways, grass areas, etc are just simply not well made. They look cheap and of a single dimension. They put a lot of effort into making field states look good, throw in some extra work on everywhere else. It's what makes it stand out from everything else.- Seasons is really half baked in comparison to what Realismus did in FS19. Snow is laughable in terms of what it covers and doesn't.- Roads are weird - and I mean in terms of what the turns look like, and how the roads are cut through the countryside. This isn't at all what most look like, at least in the US. We're very much square road oriented in most of the crop belts of the US. We have a lot of squared off fields, few are sliced by curvy European styled roads. This goes back to the map thing, a simple Google Maps search would show you what our agriculture belt farmland really looks like. Overall I've uninstalled the game and returned to FS19. The maps available from modders are better, which I understand is simply due to the modders still working on their contributions. Giants had quite a while between FS19's release and this to make a great product, including skipping a year due to COVID and really dropped this bomb. Just do yourself a favor and wait.....don't buy it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Since release, I have spent some hours in the game - putting a tl;dr at the start, I have actually found it to be pleasant. However, in some places the experience can be a little disappointing as it feels a lot like its predecessor - FS19. Going into some detail:There is a lot of positive aspects to the game. A revamped sound system definitely makes the experience more enjoyable. However, there is much more to what I have to say besides this very simple change:What I enjoy:- Overall multiplayer experience is great fun. Being able to run multiple farms and help each other out is something that I've enjoyed throughout the game series. FS22 has not failed me and I still find it very enjoyable. - Everything is easy to master, once you give it a quick read. - Overall experience is not bad, however it is also not perfect, unfortunately. I am hoping that as the game continues to be on the market, there will be a number of updates that will improve the experience!What needs worked on:- Something that could make the gaming experience better, would be an improvement in physics. Its nice to see moving parts in the machinery etc. however vehicles still do not feel like they are being driven across a muddy field when it is raining, for example. It all feels 'stiff' - if that is the right way to word it. There is no aspect of a challenge in that aspect - something that I was hoping for, considering how long the franchise has been on the market. - Seasons adds something without really adding something. Yes, through the addition of Seasons, we experience the race against time to make sure that everything is done in a timely manner. However, yet again - I was expecting a challenging environment during the winter. Struggling to get around, snow physics on the ground etc. this is something that would definitely make this new aspect worthwhile. For now it just feels as if you are driving across a flat surface.- Map editing is a whole issue in itself to be fair. It takes a lot of patience, we are given four basic tools that are pretty much useless. I have come against situations where I am unable to utilise the tools e.g. lowering/raising the ground won't work. Personally I think that it's something that needs looked at. - Based on pre-released footage I was expecting more from the AI, both workers and just AI on the roads. There isn't much to be said about this. However the AI doesn't feel like AI... it's just there.

_childDocuments_.review: (Summary at bottom)100%  reskinned FS19. I have about 650 hours on FS19 and I can most certainly say this is much better in many ways, and many things have been completely overhauled.- Sounds have had a major overhaul, makes the game feel more realistic and immersive.- More placeables than ever, including sheds with working doors, refuel stations (diesel, methane, and electric), seed & fert tanks, etc. Fences too, great addon, easy to use.- Many many new brands, and more tire brand options. Also license plates for equipment and vehicles.- Character customization. Graphics wise, it looks a rather bit weird, but I'm sure it'll be improved. Unfortunately you have to change the character per-savegame, not any sort of preset in the main menu.- Better organized XML files. Much more easier on the eyes compared to FS17, and easier to find things such as the money value. I don't need to use ctrl+f anymore, I can just scroll. (Speaking of XML editing, instead of editing the careerSavegame.xml file like FS17 & FS19 to add cash, here you need to edit farms.xml file instead in the same folder, careerSavegame.xml is only for appearance in the main menu.)- Better organized shop UI, not to mention the UI overall. Imo, the weird blue fade on the speedometer/tachometer reminds me of the ol' FS13 UI, kinda wish it was more clean and simplistic as the FS19 UI, but hey, it is what it is.- American-based map. Major improvement from Ravenport and Goldcrest Valley, feels more of the true american countryside thanks to that new office here in the U.S. that Giants got a while ago.- Buying used equipment. As of now it seems limited to 4 pieces of equipment at a time, but very neat feature regardless.- Vehicle gearbox. Not required if you don't want to use it, but I like it. A wee bit confusing at times however, I'm used to the way you shift in American Truck Simulator, but this is different. Not bad, maybe needs to be tweaked a bit.- Obviously graphics, you won't really notice a huge jump between FS19 and FS22 as the major jump of the franchise was between FS17 and FS19, but there is some noticeable changes.- Seasons. I don't like playing so realistic to the point I have to wait time for the proper planting and harvesting time, but there's an option to make it so the seasons are just visual only. You can also make it so it's one season at all times.Now, there are of course many bugs with the game, and some features missing since it just got released today, but I'm pretty sure Giants will get most of them sorted out before the next year.Some rather aggravating bugs/missing features are:- Inability to remove buildings and fences on farms that already exist on the map. I have only tested this on Elmcreek so far, however, but it is most likely this applies to all other maps.- Landscaping, a wee bit glitchy, controls are difficult to get used to from FS19. Can't sprint in landscaping mode.- AI workers. We all know from previous FS games that the AI is notorious, especially in FS17. Here, there have been some improvements, and with the addition of AI being able to drive vehicles to and fro, that's really useful, but again, very buggy. The classic 'Helper F is blocked by an object!' pops up every now and then, you tab over and there's like nothing in it's way.- With some vehicles, most notably (and only tested on so far,) is the Mack Anthem. It's not a true 6x4, more of a 6x2. I was hauling the largest CLAAS wheel loader & the 4755 with rear duals on the non-Lodeking flatbed up a hill, it almost seemed as if the rear axle of the Anthem was going backwards, whereas the front rear axle was slipping. Fine, maybe it doesn't have a lockable transfer case of diffs, but it should go up that hill with the most powerful engine in it, plus the weight on the rear axles from the fifth wheel.- Buildings, most notably the farmhouse. If you look into the windows, it's just a copied .jpeg of a weird looking kitchen with yellow cabinets and a granite looking wall. I'm sure Giants will add in an interior at some point, I don't want buildings to start to function like the ones back in FS13. Also , you cannot interact/enter any existing buildings/sheds/barns on the farms on the land you purchase. I sure hope that gets fixed.Bugs TL;DR:- Existing Building Removal (Cannot remove them, this includes existing fences.)- Existing Building Functionality (Cannot enter buildings and cannot open shed/barn doors)- Landscaping (Buggy, a minor visual glitch, & controls are awkward)- AI Driving/Transport (Blocked by basically nothing or drives the wrong path)TL;DR:There are many bugs, I hope they'll be fixed before the next year. But there are also many improvements from previous FS games, as someone who's played FS13 (Xbox 360), 17 (Steam), and 19 (Epic Games).At this time, with the amount of bugs/missing features in the game, I would just wait and get it on sale in the future.If you're someone who already purchased it, don't bother refunding it, just wait for the bugs to be worked out.I have not tested everything, and I have not played every map. I do not have all of the bugs and missing features listed, I will update this review as I come across more notable bugs, missing features, and good changes from previous FS games.Again, this is a newly released game, so unless Giants decides to not fix these issues/keep them removed like EA did with Battlefield 2042, then I will change this review as needed.(literally a few hours after I made this review) Update:Graphics did a ♥♥♥♥♥ wucky and it's a bit laggy when going first-person pov, in fact while the graphics did said ♥♥♥♥♥ wucky I went into first person and the game crashed. Also note this happened while hosting a multiplayer game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is great, or I wouldn't have played it for 500 hours (except for the forestry, where the textures doesn't match the model/hitbox unless the tree is super-straight), but the multiplayer is terrible. It starts with the fact that you still can't connect with friends via Steam and have to hope that a friend's server will be suggested to you. Sometimes you have to restart the game 5-6 times for that to happen, but sometimes you see the server as soon as it starts. Once you've found the server, you have to spend 20-30 seconds syncing the game data, pausing the game for everyone, then repeating the previous process, because sometimes terraformed objects or textures are set to default locally, which is then fixed by reconnecting. Then when you are finally in the game, desync or rubberbanding occurs. I don't know of any other game where this is so extreme. The multiplayer is the only thing besides mods that keeps the game alive, so it's even sadder that it's so poorly implemented. I really hope these issues are fixed in the next installment and am disappointed that even Farming Simulator 2011 runs more stable.

_childDocuments_.review: Farming Simulator 22 is a game that lets you experience the joys and challenges of being a farmer. You can grow crops, raise animals, manage production chains, and sell your products in a realistic and immersive environment. You can also customize your character, your farm, and your vehicles with a variety of options.The game offers a lot of content and features that make it fun and engaging. You can choose from over 400 machines and tools from over 100 real agricultural brands, such as Case IH, CLAAS, Fendt, John Deere, Massey Ferguson, New Holland, Valtra and many more. You can also explore three different maps with different climates and landscapes: the Mediterranean south of France, the US-Midwest, and the European Alpine region. Each map has its own crops, animals, and production chains to discover.One of the most impressive aspects of the game is the seasonal cycle that affects the gameplay and the visuals. You have to adapt to the changing weather conditions and plan your activities accordingly. You can also enjoy the beauty of the four seasons as they change the appearance of your farm and the environment. The game also has a dynamic day-night cycle and realistic lighting and shadows that create stunning scenes.The game is not only enjoyable by yourself, but also with friends. You can play online with up to 16 players on PC and Mac, or up to 8 players on consoles. You can also crossplay with players on different platforms. You can cooperate with other farmers, share your resources, and work together on your farms. You can also compete with other players in various events and challenges.Farming Simulator 22 is a game that I would recommend to anyone who loves farming or simulation games. It is a game that offers a lot of variety, realism, and fun. It is a game that lets you create your own farm and let the good times grow!

_childDocuments_.review: Farming Simulator 2022 is the successor of Farming Simulator 2019 and for the most part, I think it has done a great job at doing so. Although, with all other things considered there are most definitely bugs I feel can ruin the experience over time. I'm going to provide a list of pros and cons below to express my opinion so far.Pro's- A LOT more vehicles were included in the base game compared to any other Farming Simulator game.- Sounds for the most part have been re-vamped and are "somewhat" realistic now.- Seasons are now built into the game.- Graphics are much better than any previous Farming Simulator game, however, the frame rate does reflect your graphical choices if you have a lower-end system.- Skin customization has been greatly improved. *There are many other positive points to be made about this game, however, these are just the one's I feel most people are going to notice/care about.*Con's- When joining multiplayer games, you are sometimes not given an option to customize your skin. This is a major problem because it automatically fills in your in-game name (IGN) from a location that isn't disclosed. I've already had this game leak my full first and last name because of this, GIANTS THIS NEEDS FIXED ASAP!- Despite the inclusion of Mack trucks, they are awful. This is because they can't even drive on flat ground most of the time. This has been pin-pointed down by many people to be a gearbox issue.- Stemming off of gearbox issues, the introduction of manual gearboxes is very cool, but I've yet to get them to work properly. Most of the time trying to shift something such as a truck will cause the game to panic and constantly flip between drive and reverse. I'm not sure if this is just an isolated issue with me or not...- The mini-map is clunky and confusing in my opinion compared to any other game in the franchise.- The physics in this game can very strange sometimes, for example, my pallet fork will randomly clip through objects and get stuck in the ground. This isn't exactly an issue with just this game, in particular, every Farming Simulator game I've played has had strange bugs/glitches such as this. However, for a game that has suddenly spiked in price compared to any other in the franchise, I'd expect stupid physics issues such as this to be minimal if not eliminated.- Similar to pros, there are many cons, but these are just the ones I've noticed the most and find game-breaking.Overall Review: Farming Simulator 2022 is a strange game in terms of its review status right now. If there was a neutral option offered by Steam, then by far I would rate this game neural. I'm expecting and hoping Giants will fix most of the problems I've brought up in this review. Although, if the glitches in this game aren't fixed within a few months I may consider updating my review. As it stands I would recommend this game under two conditions, if the price was dropped or it was on sale. If you are new to the Farming Simulator scene, I'd recommend trying out Farming Simulator 2019 first as it won't hurt your wallet as much, and it has had many of its bugs fixed.

The addition of new crops and the ability to produce and sell various products adds depth to the gameplay, keeping you engaged for hours on end.One of the standout features of Farming Simulator 22 is the extensive selection of machinery and equipment. This is not a "bash the game dev" rant at all. Just a outcry to see things fixed so we all have a good and healthy game to play and have fun in. I will be more then happy to give this title a pass, but I really do need to see these problems fixed first which should be more then fair.Another thing that seems to be still the same as in previous versions of the game is the poor physics and handling of the vehicles. This seriously needs to be improved to start with as it makes no sense when a vehicle makes very tight corners while seeing the steering wheel do break neck speeds to get the vehicle to turn so fast. But this isn't the only problem, Your vehicle slips and slides on the weirdest moments or gets stuck on hitboxes much bigger then the actual object. Or the fact that your farming tools refuse to function unless you use mods to fix the problem. It would be beneficial to any gamer to see this fixed/resolved.The walking around is rather broken on it self. You move faster then the AI cars, which is rather.... interesting... But the worst part is that if you happen to hit something you can be stopped instantly and bounce back. Now, for all reasonable thinking in this you could state this is a function and not a problem as IRL the same would happen. That wall doesn't suddenly give way just because you hit it full speed. However in-game you have this on slow speeds as well if you run into your intiors. Which may I add are too small to be even realistic and you can't move anything around aside from the fact that it looks extremely dated (looks like this was dragged out of the late 90's to early 2000's to be honest).For all good reasoning I'd like to suggest making buildings bigger to make sense compared to the vehicles and overhaul the entire interiors as it's often limiting and very narrow for no good reason. Also there isn't much there, so I would like to suggest to make specific country or region specific DLC's that would add a huge amount of new buildings and perhaps specific vehicles or machinery that would represent that region the best. This would be a major step forward in the right direction. Also the regular cars is rather limiting, adding some new vehicles might help a lot.There are a lot of mods that became "must install" things, it would make sense that these were integrated with the vanilla game so you don't need to look them up as the mod system is also broken. If you have to re-install it, you are foced to re-install ALL mods on top of that. Which is just insanity! It would make sense that either on the Giants Software website or trough Steam Workshop you could keep these ready to go so it will install automatically and not take you ages to find everything again. If you have a long mod list this can take days if not weeks to do as the lag that the modding pages create is just insane. This to the level that you can wait easily up to 15 minutes to load a page! This isn't cool or needed!Is the game worth it?Well yes and no at this moment in time.YES, if you have it working it will be perfectly do it's job even if you have plenty of things that will get under your skin and rage as things don't function well with the mentioned issues above.NO, you need to re-install the game often for some bizar reason and there are too many things broken or not functioning as they should.Is it fun to play?Well if things go well then it seems to be fun, only to encounter sooner or later bugs that will cause the fun to lessen or completely disappear. This is why I write this very long review in the hope things will get fixed to give this game a better chance.Do you expect a new version of the game soon?Well unfortunately this seems to be a trend with Giants Software and the Farming Simulator title. Minor changes and updates, but let's slap a new year to the title in order to force people to buy everything again instead of fixing the problems and add content to it. It's really a shame and I seriously hope this won't be the case, but I fear for the worse...

_childDocuments_.review: "Farming Simulator 22" delivers an immersive and authentic farming experience that's unparalleled in the gaming world. One of the standout features is the logging mechanic, which allows players to engage in realistic forestry operations. From felling trees to processing logs, every step feels incredibly detailed and true to life. The physics engine adds to the realism, making each tree feel like a genuine challenge to harvest.The farming aspect of the game is equally impressive. With a vast array of crops to plant, cultivate, and harvest, players can truly experience the full spectrum of agricultural life. _childDocuments_.review: When I was younger I'd play Farming Simulator 2013 almost everyday, it was mindblowing when Titanium came out and we got Case IH equipment with a new map. But I stopped after Farming Simulator 15 and subsequent releases because they felt like graphics were improving while everything else remained the same. Now I have returned to this release and it is an upgrade in every way.If you showed me a video of this game in 2014 when all we had was FS2013 I'd say it was prerendered CGI. Not only has the general graphics engine improved, but so has every aspect of the graphics. I know I just said they only updated graphics with previous releases but these changes are so big I have to cover them. There are detailed and unique animations now for every possible action with each tool/vehicle, not janky and stiff like they used to be in older games. The crops are more well animated and rendered now, and textures are so high fidelity you can read the warning labels on all of the equipment if you get close enough.As for gameplay they have improved realism by making the equipment handle more closely to real life. And there is more tasks to do for every goal, it takes more work to get a field ready for planting, and also to achieve maximum harvest yield. You can disable these additional requirements, like periodically having to plow your field to maintain good yields, or having to use a stonepicker to remove stones dug up by cultivators and plows. Personally I leave those requirements enabled otherwise it feels like too little time is passing between harvest cycles. There is also the free Precision Farming DLC which makes it even more realistic and adds field pH levels, soil types, and different seeding/fertilizer application rates. You can get it from the ingame Modhub. They also improved the classic AI helper, now you can give them custom tasks using the map, like having them take a trailer of crop to a sell point and selling it. That's a pretty big upgrade, the AI doesn't always manage to do this without problems though, some tractor/trailer combos are just impossible for the AI to drive on the roads. You're more likely to run into issues trying to get the AI to drive on the roads using mods though.So to sum it up, this is definitely the best Farming Simulator to date. Naturally it needs a decent computer to run maxed out but the graphics really are very impressive considering what these games used to look like. The new shaders are very realistic and materials look real. The helper is better, the equipment is more detailed in every way, the sounds are better. I highly recommend this if you are a fan of the previous games, or if you want a relaxing simulator. You don't need an interest in farming to relax in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Farming Simulator 22 offers an immersive and highly realistic farming experience, allowing players to delve into the captivating world of agriculture. Developed by Giants Software, this latest installment in the Farming Simulator series presents numerous improvements and new features that enhance the gameplay and deliver an enjoyable farming simulation.One of the notable aspects of Farming Simulator 22 is its enhanced graphics and visuals. The game boasts stunningly detailed environments, realistic weather effects, and improved textures, making every field, farm, and vehicle come to life. Whether you're working under the scorching sun or witnessing the gentle drizzle, the game's visual fidelity adds a layer of authenticity to the overall experience.The range of activities and options available to players in Farming Simulator 22 is extensive. From tending to crops, raising livestock, and managing machinery to selling produce and expanding your farm, there's always something to do. The game offers a wide array of vehicles and equipment from leading manufacturers, allowing you to customize and optimize your farming operations according to your preferences. Whether you enjoy planting crops, harvesting grain, or transporting livestock, the game caters to various aspects of farming life.One of the notable additions to Farming Simulator 22 is the inclusion of seasonal cycles. Each season brings its own set of challenges and opportunities. You'll need to adapt your farming strategies accordingly, considering factors such as crop growth rates, weather conditions, and harvesting schedules. This dynamic element adds depth to the gameplay, keeping it engaging and preventing it from becoming monotonous.Moreover, the game offers both single-player and multiplayer modes, allowing you to enjoy the experience at your own pace or collaborate with friends in cooperative farming. The multiplayer mode provides a social dimension, where you can work together to manage larger farms, share resources, and tackle more significant challenges. The inclusion of mods and custom content also extends the game's replayability, as the community continues to contribute fresh and creative additions to the farming simulation.However, despite the improvements, Farming Simulator 22 does retain some of the limitations of its predecessors. The game can still feel slow-paced and repetitive at times, as some tasks require patience and persistence. Additionally, while the visuals have been enhanced, the overall physics and animations could benefit from further refinement to provide a more seamless experience.In conclusion, Farming Simulator 22 delivers a rich and immersive farming experience that is sure to captivate agricultural enthusiasts and simulation game fans alike. With its stunning visuals, diverse activities, and the introduction of seasonal cycles, the game offers an authentic and engaging portrayal of the farming world. While it may have a few areas for improvement, overall, Farming Simulator 22 successfully cultivates an enjoyable and rewarding virtual farming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: **Beginners Beware**After noticing the cult following grow with FS19, I was excited to get involved this time around with what should be a AAA game by now; Sadly, it is not.At best, this is the most in depth version of GMOD with its ridiculous physics in tow. Whack a stop sign in a 40 ton fully loaded truck and you’ll stop dead. Clip a box of eggs at speed and you’ll roll an entire bloody tractor. The game is also locked to 60fps to hide the shortcomings of the ancient engine it runs on. Next thing to know is this is a sandbox game from the absolute beginning. Despite you starting “Career Mode”, everything is available from the start and there is nothing to strive towards other than the satisfaction of growing a crop from start to finish.The “tutorial” can be completed in less than a minute and you are left wondering what the hell to do from there. This game requires incredible amounts of googling and YouTube tutorials before you can do anything.Despite this years version featuring hireable AI workers to plow some fields for you, they are incredibly stupid and if the field isn’t perfectly square with huge amounts of space to turn around outside the field, they will get stuck. If two AI workers meet, they will also just sit facing each other making no attempt to go around. You’re still paying them while this is going on though. If you are expecting automation and ‘running’ a farming empire, this is not the game for you. The emphasis is on doing every task yourself.I have now slogged through 20+ hours and by giving myself £999Mil, I’ve have finally learnt the ins and outs of all the mechanics this game has to offer. I do actually enjoy this game now I understand it but I wouldn’t wish the ridiculous learning curve on anyone and therefore cannot recommend it without a huge improvement to an actual career mode that would take you through each type of farming enterprise with best yield results, step by step.This game continues to have an enormous modding community that the developers actively rely on to improve their game for them. But their emphasis seems to be on endless tractor skins rather than optimisation and quality of life improvements. Would be cool if the dog could jump in my pickup come to work with me too though 👍🏻

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Yes, I would recommend this game. There is enough new content and feature improvements that I don't see myself really looking back at FS19. The build system comes with many improvements but also lacks key features and is the most disappointing aspect of FS22 that I've found so far. More info on this below.The new AI features are a massive improvement over FS19 while still being rather frustrating. Lots of little glitches with the AI particularly when driving from place to place. The new character creation system is quite a step up from FS19 but still leaves a lot to be desired. Would really like to see more face geometries and clothing options. Currently my understanding is that modders can only feasibly modify actual game play. In the future, it might be work allowing modders to work with the character creation system and even create custom character geometries and clothing.The building system... I would argue this is the most important aspect of the game.It's incredibly frustrating. So many improvements and at the same time, so many downgrades.I love the new painting tools and the ability to paint grass, brush, trees onto maps. Huge, huge improvement over FS19. The actual geometry manipulation of the terrain is slightly less frustrating than FS19 however still lacks some of the key functionality of FS19. One key difference is the total inability to override terrain near placed buildings. If the terrain rises as a result of a placed building, it can cause a steep slope that cannot be smoothed.The lack of a grid snapping feature is to me, the most frustrating loss from FS19. Something that as a game developer myself, I can say is so trivial in it's implementation that it makes absolutely no sense not to include it.Snow: Could be amazing but lacks in several ways. They seem to be relying heavily on modders to implement snow equipment with only one serious option for a snow plow in the game, and let's be honest, it sucks.As someone who has lived in areas with snow and has been able to monetize snow ( clearing parking lots )I was a little bit disappointed with how the game handles snow when using any kind of bucket implement to clear snow. Obviously the mechanics of pushing snow are there, we saw it with the plows. When using a front loader or skid steer to move snow, you can't push snow when the bucket is full.Seasons overall: It's okay, It's an improvement over the base FS gameplay. Overall, when it comes to seasons, the way the Seasons mod from FS19 laid all the information out was more digestible than what FS22 has implemented.UI:Overall, the UI hasn't changed drastically in terms of how much and what kind of information is displayed. The way it's displayed has changed significantly. It may be that I'm still getting used to it but I find it much harder to digest the information being displayed with the new layout.

_childDocuments_.review: I know what you're thinking.  300 hours and the game is not recommended?  That doesn't sound right.Well let me tell you I enjoyed the heck out of the previous titles and I was really looking forward to this one.  I bought the game in its "finished" state with all the DLCs and I have spent all those hours trying to find the fun in the game, convinced that if I just do something different I can finally enjoy myself and build my dream farm.I'm sure there's a good game in there somewhere, but the game and its systems are constantly getting in your way of, well... farming.  Unless your preferred play style is running a small hobby farm on one of the pre-built farms that the game offers you're going to run into frustration and disappointment.Any dreams you may have of building your own farm on more than a couple of hectares of land, well I hope you have more patience for jankiness and "what the heck do I do with all this straw" than I do.  The maps are gorgeous, but trying to place anything like a cow barn requires a dance of saving, terraforming, attempting to place the thing you want, finding out you didn't do it right, quitting and reloading your save.  It gets tedious very quickly and because the game is a single save per farm, there's no way to make manual saves to either go back to a previous state for your farm or save individual steps so that you can, say, adjust your terraforming before trying again without starting completely over.  (Yes, there's a way to make manual backups of your saves on PC, no that doesn't really help.)I have plenty of other examples of things and systems in the game that ended up frustrating me and ultimately I couldn't even solve with mods.  I can only hope that Farm Sim 25 spends time polishing all these pain points and not just adding new crops with minimal support (grapes and olives anyone?) and prettier graphics.
