_childDocuments_.review: Farming Simulator 22 is the most recent entry into the series, and it definitely takes the first steps in while to move Farming Simulator out of the casual mode/arcade experience and a closer step towards simulation which the game title suggests it should be. This change however seems to have been received by the community a lot like marmite, some love the direction the series is taken, others seem really upset and offended by the changes.We have for the first time a version of the popular seasons mod included in the base game, with crop planting and growth calendar to follow which dictates at what times of the year you can seed and plant your crops. This has been a much requested feature for Farm Sim since back in FS17 when Seasons Mod first released. So it's also somewhat strange reading reviews and reading forum posts how this much requested feature, now included in the game is not seen by some people as a bad feature and backward step in the game because it makes the game more realistic and makes you have to think about what you are doing. Some players seem upset that they can no longer seed a crop at 7am in the morning and harvest it at 7pm that same evening. Players wanted realism and then complain when the game takes a step in that direction, I don't understand that.The seasons mode can be disabled however by players if they don't want to deal with that or don't have the attentions span required to play a simulation game in that way. The season growth calendar can be disabled to allow players to plant and harvest at whatever time of year. They can also shorten the in game months to last just one in game day, so can fly through a whole year in the game in just 12 in game days, which they could also speed through at x360 normal speed if they really want. So again the negative reviews and comments from players who say it takes too long for crops to grow and too long to get stuff done really baffle me again. Clearly these people just need to play around with their ingame settings to strike the balance that works for them.In Farm Sim 22 this year because of the Seasons Mode and even with it disabled the increase to crop growth time, Giants have implemented and included several new fieldwork tasks like Mulching, Rolling, Stone Collecting as well as changing and revamping the weed system to include more growth stages and longer periods where mechanical weeders and hoes can be used to remove the pesky weeds, whilst also implementing a new penalty system for using herbicide to remove weeds at more advanced stages of growth which can impact your yields. This provides you with more tasks to do fill your time whilst waiting for crops to grow. Again so many negative reviews I see, players are turning these game modes off and then complaining they have nothing to do in game and it's boring. Well yeah that's going to happen, when you turn off half the games features and options, you're not then playing the game then are you? If you're going to turn off ploughing, lime spreading, stone collect, mulching and weeds, you might as well turn your game off and then your computer as well, because clearly this type of game is not for you. I saw one reviewer who said nobody does mulching as there is no point to it, and nobody does weeds. A statement that is very clearly factually incorrect. Mulching removes the stubble leftover from previous harvested crops and introduces the material back into the soil, giving you a bonus to your next crop harvest for fields that you mulch before seeding. So clearly not a pointless task. Same goes for weeds, removing the weeds is much easier in FS22 because you now get to use the Mechanical Weeders and Single In-Game Hoe for longer to remove the weeds and prevent you getting a penalty on your next harvest. It's also a very relaxing thing to do in game after having seeded or planted a field for a few hours and passes the time very nicely. So again would not describe it as a pointless function. Especially when reviewer then goes on to say they find they spend all their time sleeping or fast wording time to find stuff to be able to do. Well duh! You keep skipping over all the tasks you could be doing.For people who say Farm Sim 19 is better then Farm Sim 22, I typically check how many hours they have played the game and see many of these reviewers have played for less then 100 hours, which is nothing in a Farm Sim game. I saw one review say they've played every game from 2009 to now and FS19 is the best in the series. I checked their Steam Profile and sure they have played every game but when adding up their combined play time for every game it still was below 1000 hours for the entire series. I played FS19 alone for 3500 hours and have 400 hours in FS22 at the time of this writing. I don't know how anyone can say this game is better or worse then the previous game when their profile shows they haven't played it. I also find it hard to take anything seriously from someone with so many games in their steam library but they haven't reached triple figure playtime in any of them. Indicates someone with a very short attention span or focus, or someone with too much money who can afford to jump from one game to the next latest and greatest release and never plays or completes anything.FS22 beats FS19 purely from the standpoint of the improved engine and performance, resulting in better looking game that runs at higher framerates on the same hardware as FS19. The sounds in FS22 are so much better than in FS19, with all the various tractors and equipment sounding so much meatier and more like their real life counterparts, you now get the different engine sounds as vehicles are put under load and strain, you have the gearboxes now on many vehicles so hear the transmission changing, and then there is all the environmental sound changes with trailers and tools that clank and clunk and make noise as they are moving. Trailers that have that knocking sound each time they lower as the piston reaches each stage of it's lowering. A lot of small details and tweaks which when given a surface glance by a casual player or viewer they probably don't see or notice, but you definitely do when playing it if you have played past games.Multiplayer is so much better in Farm Sim 22. The data sync between players when players log in or leave a server is so much faster in this years game. No longer do players on a server have to sit and wait for "Syncronising Data Between Players" for ten minutes whenever someone logs onto the server. The delay might just literally be a 1 or 2 second pause now when a player connects, which does not interrupt and distract players as much now.Also this years game is the first that allows CrossPlay between Console Players and PC Players, no other Farm Sim game in the series allowed this. Also for the first time ever in the series, when joining a server in Farm Sim 22 running mods, it's possible to download and synchronise those mods directly from the server page and be in game (Providing the mods are on the in game/Giants ModHub) no more having to back out of the game go to the modhub and manually trying to remember what mods you needs for a server and download them.I still think one area of improvement here though that Giants could make for PC Players hosting and running dedicated servers is that on the Mods Page of their Web Interface, allow that screen to be sorted either alphabetically by players or by most recently uploaded/updated so that when an admin adds or updates mods to a server which might not be on the the in game ModHub and not available for auto download and sync in game, that players can find them and download them much more easily and quickly from the server's webinterface and public mod downloads page.

_childDocuments_.review: So… after three years for a company who’s business-plan seem to be to release a new game every two years I had high hopes for this one. Low expectations, but still… high hopes. Sadly, Giants delivered as expected. In recognizable form they made sure to leave any real visions and improvements on the drawing-board and release what feels more like a free update or a cheap DLC than a new game. New features:    • Seasons. More or less just copy/pasting a good mod from FS19. Instead of showing us what a professional developer can do with a good idea, they just payed (I assume) the modders and called it done.     • Production chains. As with seasons they took a mod(s), streamlined it a little and that’s it, done.    • Sound and gear-system. This is in my opinion the only real improvement to the game, but it still need some polish and I would like a bigger variety in the engine-sounds.     • 3 new crops. One is just another combinable crop and two orchard type crops. A bit of a gimmick, but I guess they tie into production chains so that’s fine.     • New build mode. Improved, but the terrain editor it’s very basic and it’s impossible to smooth it out to look close to real. Even the developer can’t do it right, check out the ground close to the cow-pasture in Erlengrat.    • New worker features. Workers can now be sent from A to B, sent to a field to do a job and carting. I only tested this a few times and it work ok, but the path-finding is far from perfect.     • AI traffic. AI cars drive faster, I’m sure that had to take a month or two to change, right? They are still on rails and it’s still like hitting a brick wall if you drive into them. There is no pathfinding, no avoidance. To call it AI is an insult to AI’s everywhere.    • Used equipment and separate maintenance and paint condition. A good idea, but again, very basic. Also if you repair but don’t repaint you vehicles the condition-bar next to the speed-o stays at about a quarter full(might have been changed/fixed).    • Character creation. It’s fine, but there is no sliders for body-shape or skin-colour and just 16 predefined faces.     • Fieldstone. Stones show up in fields after plowing and cultivating. Sure,  but I suspect most player’s will turn it off after a short time so why bother. In my experience the workers have no idea what parts of a field is done and not if you stop them half-way through.     • Changes to the UI. Sure, but was that the most important thing to improve?Physics:The physics seems to have gotten little to no love. 	    • Machines and equipment still have no real feeling of weight. No change in centre of mass when accelerating or braking, no rocking and rolling on big rubber tires when you drive on uneven terrain or come a sudden stop. Remember, even the smallest tractor in the game weighs 2,9 tons, more than twice the weight of a compact car.     • The physics of bales, pallets and logs are still horrible. If you bump into them they slide around like on ice. They still glitch into pallet-forks, bale-spike and log-claws and many other objects. Hitting the “sweet-spot” for pallets feels like a lottery. Round-bales are perfectly round and will roll away on the slightest gradient instead of compressing slightly under their own weight. And the logs… the logs can make even the most level-headed of us turn to violence.     • There might be a traction-system hiding somewhere deep inside the game, but it mostly seams to have little to no impact on gameplay, it’s just cosmetic. Where is the reason to choose wide or dual tires? Why change away from narrow’s after fertilizing? Why add wheel-weights? Adding rolling resistance might give us a reason to use communal tires to a vehicle mostly used for carting, especially if that is the only way to reach top speed.  Terrain:    • The terrain poly-count can’t have changed much since the first game.    • How can a game released in 2021 have roads with sharp angles like you find around some bridges and (un)loading-stations?    • Otherwise the roads are smooth as glass, with no bumps, cracks, pot-holes or imperfections at all. Most times you cant even tell if you drive from asphalt to grass.     • It would be nice to have a reason to want to stay on the roads and dirt-tracks when moving from A to B but since the grasslands and fields are almost as smooth as the rest of the map most people just cut across. Workers:The workers are as useless as ever. On a perfectly square field they do ok as long as there are no trees or building near by.On a slightly unevenly shaped field they leave little missed bits most times they turn. They will come to a field edge, turn around and line up perfectly to continue before deciding to go home. I created a field with a plow, seeded two full laps of headlands and set this dumbbell off on his own. He managed a few rounds and the proceeded to seed 30 meters into the grassland next it before he quit.It can’t possibly be that difficult to make the worker-AI aware of what they are doing, where they’re supposed to do it and if they are finished doing it. It’s been like this since at least FS15, there is no excuse!!Maps and Gameplay:Other then the addition of production lines, which are minor gameplay-wise, there are no changes. It’s still farm, sell, repeat. The economy is as basic as ever. In the new price-overview it looks like it would be possible to predict when to sell, but from my experience this is either bugged or useless.There are three maps with one starting location on each, nothing new, nothing to be excited about, but they might be slightly bigger than in FS19. It would be nice to have more options when you start a new game instead of starting with the same machines, on the same farm, with the same budget every time you start a map. How about:    • Different starting budgets.    • A variety in starting vehicle-packs to choose from.     • A choice of several different farms on each map, varying in size and feel.    • Rule-sets? I’m the type of person who should love this game, but I don’t. Instead I get frustrated over bad mechanics, I’m disappointed in the lack of creative thinking and development and angry that obvious bugs and flaws stays in the game release, after release. I hope to some day play a good or even great farming simulator, but at this rate though, with statistically only 30-40 year left to live, I don’t like my odds. The Farming Simulator community is big(for a work-sim) and full of supportive players and modders who have been conditioned to lower their expectations for years. It’s about time they are rewarded with a developer that at least aspires to get up to date with modern technology.

_childDocuments_.review: Today is one week after the initial release of the FS22 game, and I’ve been going back and forth trying to sort my thoughts about this release. I didn’t want to write a review just after release, but now, without an update on the game after a week of official release – I see that there is no reason for a polite wait.I’ve been a true fan of the FS game since 17 and 19, and have seen the game evolve. On 19 I have around a thousand hours, and have been really invested in the game. It has helped me a lot having a game where you can immerse yourself and have a break from real life stuff and be farmer for an hour or two. I came to understand that Giants had made some kind of schedule by years when making the games, and people really thought FS21 was going to be a thing – but during the FS19 era they stated that they wanted an extra year to work on the upcoming game, and was not planning a release of a FS21 game. The community accepted this as a good reason for delaying a release. I think we expected more from this statement, and didn’t understand that this was a delay to release several DLCs for the FS19 game (small equipment packs). And under some circumstances it would have been a good thing to release DLCs for the FS19 game, if it had brought some significant to the game – but it really didn’t. 7 of the DLCs was small additions of equipment in one selected brand (Holmer, Anderson, Bourgault, Grimme, Rottne, John Deere cotton and Kverneland) and the two others were ‘expansions’ of Alpine and Platinum. The first added a handful of equipment, and a poorly made alpine map (where none of the fields were in the actual alpine..) and the last one of Platinum just added some Claas equipment. All these DLCs came to a total of almost 100 USD/EUR extra to the already purchased game of around 30-40 USD/EUR. Giants were on a roll.But looking past the half-a**ed work that Giants put into the DLCs that were released, the community recognized the potential of the game. The modders and map makers of FS19 rose to stardom. It has to be the only community I know of that actually take a game to such new levels with their modding skills. And it was not a closed off modding community, Giants have their own mod page both on their site and ingame where the approved mods are released. So Giants has been very well aware of what was made and which mods were the most downloaded and used.Fast forward to late 2021 and the upcoming release of FS21. The community was so excited! Of course we were. We were still living off the high that FS19 gave us, and we were all playing our modded versions with both Courseplay, GPS, Seasons and probably a map from Oxygendavid. FS22 just had to be the next level.Now, after seeing some gameplay from the influencers that received the press release, and after playing for a week on the two new maps, in total of three (Erlengrat is with us still, the ‘alpine’ map). I have to say I’m really confused. I see a lot of new features, ALL of which Giants have taken from their modding community. The graphics are mostly the same, but that’s not a terrible thing because the FS19 graphics were still good. But all the new features bring with them a whole heap of bugs. Reddit has made a gigathread of all the reported bugs on the game, and you can really scroll through that thread to see the mess this is. Many of the bugs are game breaking, and Giants haven’t bothered releasing hot fixes to them a WEEK after the release. I don’t like being a caps lock Andy, but since they took an extra year to work on it, put it up for pre-purchase with an extra of 1 year season pass in total of 80 USD/EUR for the game and pass – some points have to be in caps lock.So yeah. What can I say? I expected more Giants. I really did. And I think you owe more to this community that stick with you through all the releases. And if this was something you finished, sat back and said ‘yes, this is good, release it!’ and expected to receive praise – then this thumbs down is really fitting as a response. Do better, we know you can.- Good graphics- Improved bale and pallet interactions- Fresh and modern overhaul of the UI- Implementation of manual gearboxes- New features (although the modders should have been credited)- Bugs throughout the game- Game breaking bugs that could have been fixed through hot-fixes- Problems with equipment, seasons, game functions, maps and more.- Just read the megathread over at /r/farmingsimulator to get the whole list..Never, under no circumstances pre-purchase a game. Never. And as the game stands today, just continue your favorite save on FS19 and we’ll give you a beep when they clean up their mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I only played previous FS games a little but when I heard that they are adding industry into FS I was very excited for the game.However the more I play the more disappointed I am.So this game supports multiplayer but if you want to host dedicated server you have to buy copy of game. So the person who is hosting has to buy game and all the DLCs twice, once for the server and once for his game machine. That is very unfriendly move from Giants.If you don't want to pay twice you can rent server ... which Giants no doubt take cut from ...Multiplayer itself is lacking many features that I would expect from such game. For example trading between players is not supported at all.  Production buildings needs many different resources but players can't help each other out with them ... not very good multiplayer game isn't it? You can build production and sell point buildings, but other players can't interact with them. They even show in the price comparison list but it is meaningless because no one can sell there. For example you build a spinnery and that will show up as new sellpoint for wool and cotton but you can't sell there because you are just adding stuff to storage for processing and other players can't sell there because they can't  interact with your building .... so why does it list as sell point ?!?!? very disappointingAnother disappointment is the implementation of production chains. They add only a little value to your goods but they add massive workload for you. Production chains produce hundreds of pallets that has to be stored, loaded on trailers and sold at highest price point and you have to do that manually, so you will spend tons of time on forklift just moving the pallets and loading them on trailers and the more production buildings you have the worse it gets.And then there are bugs. There are so many bugs in this game, physics bugs where bales and vehicles can be sent flying for hundreds of meters, physics bugs where your truck going thru curve can suddenly snap into sharp angle going in opposite direction, desync bugs where game will load original shape of map instead of the one you were actually playing on so then you can see vineyards going thru air, you can have your under the surface and so on. Tree cutting is one big exercise in frustration, I had tree disapparing on me after i cut few branches, the tree was still there on ground tho, blocking way and stuff but i coudn't see it ... after server restart the tree was standing on it's original spot like nothing happened. However, after giving it a chance, I found myself pleasantly surprised by the game's depth and complexity.The game offers a vast open-world environment to explore, with a wide variety of crops to cultivate and livestock to raise. The game's mechanics are complex and require careful planning and execution, which can be both challenging and rewarding.One of the highlights of  is the game's new orchard system, which allows players to plant and grow fruit trees such as apples, cherries, and pears. The new crops, such as grapes and olives, also add to the game's complexity, requiring specialized equipment and care.The game's dynamic weather system is another significant addition, with realistic weather affecting the gameplay in many ways. Heavy rainfall can cause flooding, damaging crops, while droughts can reduce yields, requiring the player to use irrigation systems to manage their water resources.The game's graphics and sound are impressive, creating a highly immersive atmosphere. The textures and lighting are excellent, with realistic weather effects such as rain, snow, and fog adding to the immersion. The game's music is relaxing and appropriate for the game's atmosphere.The game's multiplayer mode is an excellent way to engage with the community and share farming experiences with friends. The game's modding support also offers great replay value and community engagement.Overall,  surprised me with its depth and complexity, and I would recommend it to gamers who enjoy simulation and management games. The game's new features, including the orchard system and dynamic weather, add to the gameplay's challenge and reward, making it a must-play for farming enthusiasts.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more then great, buy it!Giants Software has really stepped up and improved Farming Simulator, not least that there is more to do more than cultivate and harvest. _childDocuments_.review: The plot: You are a shapeshifting chronomancer who has decided to take up farming in a mundane world. You have the ability to speed up and slow down the progression of time at will, you can use spells like Save and Load to create a fixed point in time that you can travel back to later if you change your mind about something. The seasons pass like days for you. You can also inexplicably teleport around between various buildings and vehicles you can ride in as well as teleport vehicles and tools back to the shop you bought them from. Thanks to your ability to bend time, stores are always open for you, though there are some strange aspects of this world that you don't quite understand yourself. Cars have an infinite amount of mass and no matter how heavy your vehicle is, they can brush you aside effortlessly, though they are courteous enough to stop and communicate by blowing their horn at whatever is in their way. People and animals are seem to phase through your vehicles, but the people on foot never seem to notice you.With your time warping powers and your ability to control various diesel powered machines, as well as a few electric ones, you set about to build yourself a life as a simple farmer while doing battle with the forces of The Bank who is more than willing to lend you money, but take their interest relentlessly, thin profit margins, and a somewhat unstable economy.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost didn't buy FS 22.  I had 19 modded just the way I wanted and already had access to seasons and factories...why not just keep driving my virtual Kirovets around my virtual frigid Russian potato farm and wait for a heavy discount?Because I have poor impulse control. Especially after a half a case of beer. Anyway...The two big new features for 22 as mentioned are a seasonal cycle and factoriesSeasons function much the same as they did in the popular mod for the two previous games, but quite a bit simplified. Crop rotation is not a thing, nor is having to wait for the ground to thaw in order to sow crops.Instead each crop type has a specific, fixed time of year to plant and a time to harvest. Try to plant too early or too late and a message pops up telling you that you can't. Wait too long to harvest and crops wither, but that's not much of a threat since weather can't ruin your harvest the way it could in 19.In 19 with seasons rain would force you to wait for a couple days of dry sunny weather before you could thresh. In FS 22, 5 minutes after a massive thunderstorm works just fine.And honestly, that's OK.On the previously mentioned Russian potato farm I occasionally lost an entire crop and an IRL hour worth of work because the spring thaw didn't come soon enough, or there was early snow.Sounds like fun to me, but that's because I'm a f***ing strange, strange person. Most people do not want to spend hours on a game treading the same ground (literally) and making little to no progress.So the simplification of seasons mechanics strikes me as more of a calculated design decision and not just laziness. It's not my cup of tea but hopefully someone can still mod in the "crunchier" features I crave.The factories though...I used a TON of factory/production mods in 19 and after a few hundred hours of playing the "wait, this bakery will only accept flour produced by THIS mod, but first I need to download the pallet factory that only works with this OTHER MOD" game, I'm very happy to say that in 22 the productions are simple, user friendly, and fun to interact with.Green houses, bakeries, dairies,ect once purchased all accept raw goods and turn them into refined products which can be sold for far higher profit. Something about turning cereal crops into flour into bread and loading it all up onto a truck to go to the store scratches just the right itch in my weirdo brain. Trains have been changed too, no longer circling the border of the map, useful only as a distraction while you wait for Worker C to finish plowing field 42; they now cut across in a linear path from A-B. You can rent them for a fee to move products from one silo to another or travel off the map to an entirely different region (represented only as a pop-up text box) where you can sell goods for a significantly higher price.All 3 of the base game maps are really good this time around, especially Elm Creek which is a nice fairly detailed mid-western US map. Vehicle handling is still arcade-y but is helped by the new manual transmission option and the fact that vehicles, implements and cargo have actual weight now. Climbing a hill you'll have to drop a couple gears and trailers have a max weight limit, so you might be able to completely fill a trailer with grain, but only half full with potatoes. You cant actually break an axle, but its a nice touch all the same.Paint wear was introduced in 19 and it's here too, but not as thoroughly implemented. None of the base game tractors that I've used, and only some of the tools show cosmetic damage.A 'paint condition' meter ticks down, but you can't actually see it.I suspect this is the trade off we get for having licensed machinery in game. PS1 & early PS2 era racing games did the same thing; you can have real world brands, or you can have vehicle damage. Companies really don't like their products being portrayed as 'worn out' or sub-standard in any way.  Its annoying, but nothing you can do.Sound got a big upgrade. There are a ton of little details you probably won't notice unless you're coming form 19 or older. Thuds driving over railroad tracks, windshield wiper noise, air brakes, improved weather sounds, noises being amplified in a tunnel or garage, its all good stuff. The engines still sound kind of generic and under-powered but we're getting there.Vehicle selection is pretty good, I know licensing is a ♥♥♥♥♥ so I wasn't expecting any 50 year old obscure eastern machinery to be in from the start, but we do get some older equipment like a 90's Valtra Valment and a Massey Ferguson 3670. There's also some electric and methane driven compact tractors and front loaders,and a used vehicle store which changes its stock every in game day, making it easier to buy some of the bigger equipmentAll in all, I'm pretty happy. Its not a whole new game rebuilt from the ground up but i wasn't expecting one.There's enough here to justify the $60, just don't fall for the season pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Farming Simulator 2022 is an incredibly immersive and enjoyable farming simulation game. The game offers a huge variety of farming activities, from agriculture and animal husbandry to forestry, that will keep you engaged and challenged as you face the different seasons, especially the harsh winter. The game's creative building features allow you to build your own farm and expand your farming operations with production chains, allowing you to form an agricultural empire. The multiplayer feature also allows you to run your farm with friends, making the experience even more enjoyable.One of the best things about the game is the wide range of realistic machines and tools available from over 100 real-life agricultural brands like Case IH, CLAAS, Fendt, John Deere, Massey Ferguson, New Holland, Valtra, and many more. The new gameplay features, such as the mulching and stone picking, the improved build-mode with the addition of greenhouses and beehives, and the new character creator all add to the game's richness and player freedom.The large variety of free community-created modifications, officially tested by the developer GIANTS Software, will extend your farming experience many times over. Rise to the challenges of becoming a successful farmer, start farming, and let the good times grow!Overall, I highly recommend Farming Simulator 2022 to anyone who loves farming simulation games. It's an incredibly fun and engaging game that offers hours of entertainment and a great sense of accomplishment as you build and expand your farm. If you're looking for a game that will keep you entertained for hours on end, then Farming Simulator 2022 is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: If your game crashes while loading, do the following...1-Go into File Explorer by clicking its pinned taskbar shortcut.2-Open the This PC > Documents > My Games > FarmingSimulator2022 folder.3-Right-click game.xml (or just game) and select the Open with and Notepad options.4-Change the <renderer>D3D_12</renderer> setting to <renderer>D3D_10</renderer>.5-Click the File menu option and select Save to set the setting.I did it and it worked in principle the game won't crashes anymore.Hope I helped

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this game for about 27.2 hours now and find it quite enjoyable.There is a learning curve, for sure, with what all the equipment does and what is suitable for sustaining a particular type of farm. I wanted to have a ranch, personally, and be self-sustaining for the farm animals that are available. Currently, I have a horse, full chickens, full sheep and full pigs. I'm growing everything for them from scratch and learning as I go how to take proper care of them.I highly recommend watching YouTube How-To's if you want to play this game. It's unfortunate, really, that I have to seek other means to figure out how to play. The guide in-game only gives so much information but doesn't answer fundamental questions on, for instance, how to get loose hay or straw and load it into trailers. I had to figure that one completely out on my own as I couldn't even find a YouTube How-To for that. Hundreds of thousands of dollars later; it's a friggen front-loader and a straw scooper (that goes by an ambiguous name in-game). It doesn't say any of this rather intricate informational questions within the in-game guide. I didn't play any other Farming Simulator (except 19 and I didn't put next to any hours into it) so I didn't have a good basis for how to do pretty much anything. I picked this game up after watching a streamer play about an hour of it... looked really fun. I'm a city-girl IRL and didn't know that half of these machines in-game even existed IRL until I friggen Googled them, lmao. /smhIncredibly fun though. I've lost days now IRL of playing this game... scooping hay, cultivating huge fields, taking care of my animals, riding my horses -- omg. It's fun! There's a few glitches that I've ran into but they were one's I just had to save and restart my game from desktop to fix. The only real gripe I have as a negative to the game-play is the editor for your farm/ranch. It's god-awful. There's no snap to the grid of the map (I've only found 1 shed that does) and the different types of ground sprayers is in small to giant square shape. You're actually pretty limited to how crazy you want your farm to look... atleast for me it is, right now. A lot of practice, I guess, has to go into dealing with rather rudimentary editor tools. Wish that was way different. =/If you play this, YouTube How-To's and the Steam Discussion page for the game is where you'll find answers for everything.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: I like the game, I kinda enjoy it and it is good and would purchase it again. The thumbs down is there to be heard, to show dissatisfaction. Pesky tooltips tell you what to do, even if it increased yield by measly 2.5%... 7.) This game has no tooltips, short explanation or the like. You get thrown in cold water8.) Design aspects don't make sense or are plain wrongTo tell more about the points that nag me:1.)The AI is horribly dumb, that even mere cars in traffic are unmovable. Why? Probably because the pathfinding would literally screw everything up. What pathfinding? Oh...Y'know.. if you tell the dumb bots "drive here" they behave like a laser riding missile. They have a center line and go left until the are over-bounds of their pathline and then they go hard right until it all continues. They drive like drunkenmasters. It's unbelievably bad. Also the workers stil struggle with fields that are not rectangular. Since when is that? LS213?2.) The stock biogasplant is useless. The small one is not worth the hefty price that gets asked. The medium one is "okay-ish" and the large one is impossible to run unless you probably own half the fields on most maps and enjoy spending for freetime running out of silage constantly. Iam using the modular biogasplant mod what does an insanely good joob on making it worthwhile, but not overpowered3.)I own a sawmill that produces planks. I own a carpentry that produces furniture. I can sell furniture for 2000€ more than a pallete of planks. My sawmill does 2400 cycles a month while my carpentry produces ~240 if you supply wood and planks. Thank you for useless tooltips and no tooltips where I'd need em!Yes there is a help menu, but it tells you only how things are done. Not what implements can do.... Woooow8.) So you can buy a huge tank of liquid fertilizer in a square drum. We use that drum to store rainwater for plants here and no, you can fit more than a mere 2000 liters in those. They easily fit 5000 - 6000 liters depending on the size.So you bought a pallete of silage additive. When you got 70 liters remaining, the weight is still 270KG. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this... if you watch someone else play this first before you try it yourself. There is no way you can do the 2 hour refund trick to demo this game, after 2 hours you will have maybe figured out how to plow a field while keeping straight lines. And also because this is not a game. I classify this in the category it's not fun, it's addictive. So make sure you can get addicted to this.I don't have much with farming but watching other people play I saw that it had some depth to it so I decided to make this my time filler while I take a break from my usuals. After a rough start trying to find my way through the slightly ambiguous UI (it took me way longer to figure out how to sell chickens than is necessary...) and having trouble figuring out what all the machines are for, I started to get the hang of it. The tutorial is dreadful by the way, I learned to play by doing two false starts where I just threw away money buying random machines and learning how to use them before I started the third serious playthrough.And after 50 hours of play, I... kind of go back on my claim that it has depth. It has some depth, but not as much as I thought it had. To me it feels like an incomplete sim, a beta version for the full release which might just be Farm Sim 24/25. Part of the game feels rather complete. You can plant grains and other goods, harvest them and they form feed for animals, materials for other products in a product chain or you can just sell them on their own. That's fine. Except its extreme busy work because to properly prepare a field you need to plow/cultivate it, fertilize it twice, roll it, optionally remove large stones, lime it and remove weeds. Good god. I would really recommend turning off stones, that is just one grind too many. Thankfully the game is very configurable.You can let tasks be done by the computer so you can multitask, or you can do multiplayer. A common thing to do is that one does harvesting and the other drives a truck next to it to collect the product so the harvester never has to stop to be emptied. It's just... the AI is dumber than a doorstop. One tree and they will ram themselves right into it and get stuck. They get stuck on corners so you can't trust them to even drive your equipment from A to B successfully. Under-developed to say the least.But I wanted to do a chicken farm. And... chickens are in my eyes really under-developed too. You buy them (pretty cheap, to be honest), they magically transport themselves to your coop and if you just keep the food storage from going empty, they will on their own grow, multiply and produce eggs which you can sell or put into a production chain. And that's it. That's chickens. If the coop didn't radiate some clucking sounds I would confuse them for being plants. It is almost passive especially if you compare it to growing crops. Oh yeah you have the option of putting roosters in your coop so the chickens multiply faster, but truth be told... you don't need them. Chickens multiple like Gremlins in a swimming pool already. There is more you can do. You can do forestry which is kind of a cheat way to get money quick, but the game needs that because otherwise you'd be left with only the option of cheating your way into money with mods, or taking out huge loans and have them be a pain in the neck. In the official maps the devs hid collectables all around which are worth a thousand bucks a pop so if you manage to find them (and they are not well-hidden) that's a few free cheap machines right there. You have greenhouses which are largely passive if you provide them with water. If you install mods you can do things like solar panels to make passive money. On the planting side of things you can plant cotton and setup fields of olives and grapes which have their own unique way of prep and harvesting. You can plant root vegetables like potatoes and beets, but they are a massive pain in the neck to harvest. It takes for-e-ver and you need specialized harvesters to do so which are very slow. You can also do grass which is food for animals, or turn it into hay or silage. A lengthy multi-step process requiring several machines and transports.Long story short. Lots to do... it is kind of fascinating because of the many different machines you get to drive around and use but a pretty shallow experience nonetheless. I am a little disappointed. I have more fun watching other people play it while they edit their videos to skip over the waiting parts than I have playing it myself where there is no skipping.

_childDocuments_.review: This new installment is a great addition to the Farming Simulator Franchise. Although there's few graphical improvements from its predecessor it has tons of new base game material that will give you a lot more to think about than graphics. This time around you have to plan more when you're going to sow your crops, when you should harvest it and then you have to see which month the price of the crop is peaking. Instead of selling only crops, silage, bales etc you can now purchase a production line and make your own butter, for example.Seasons has been a mod the last few editions of FS, but now it's finally in the base game and it's a huge step forward for the Farming Simulator franchise. What's great is that the lenght of the seasons are up to you. You decide how long one season is, and even how your surroundings look like according to the current month. Another noticeable feature is the option to have automatic, manual or even manuel with clutch as default when driving. For me it does take some time to get used to the manuel gearing but it makes it feel much more realistic driving. The other ting i want to point is audio. The audio has improved a ton since fs19 and you can hear it when you're driving your tractor, gear shifting, driving into a shed and even when you are unfolding your farm equipment. The very last thing i'd like to point is that even if you didn't get the small tractors, the mack truck or the Fendt Vario 900 Black Beauty edition with the season pass doesn't mean it's not worth it. There will be 4 dlcs next year that are much more worth than a couple of tractors with 14-25 horsepower, a truck and a tractor skin. You can find free codes for these somewhere on Steam.

Production lines are a another thing that's great to have in the base game. More ways to bring in revenue to your farm and more things to do. There are additional steps you can do to improve yield on fields such as removing field stones and mulching. _childDocuments_.review: I genuinely don't understand the negative reviews people give to this game. Sure, it's very similar to 19, but so was 19 when compared to 17. Objectively this game is pretty much the same as even FS15. What people don't apparently realize is that these game franchises aren't meant to make massive leaps in graphical or physical improvements, but to bring more standalone features and smaller improvements compared to their predecessors. When it comes to modding, I'm sure FS22 will become a lot better when some of the more popular mods from the previous games start to come out for this game.The handling "issues" some people seem to be having are easily fixed by tweaking the two steering settings. Steering and handling are very personal settings, and that it has been updated from FS19 seems to trigger some people. Come on. Also, anyone who doesn't see any graphical improvements to FS19 are either really blind or run on low settings. Foliage looks a million times better and lighting is a lot more pleasing in this game. Some of the textures also seem much sharper and the draw distance has been vastly improved.Most of the people not liking this game seem to have the common "Older is better"- problem, when in reality the improvements are exactly what you'd expect from a new addition to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not that I did not like the game, problem is, i cannot consider it a game. Games in general present challenge&reward system, creating obstacles for you to overcome and reward you for doing so. In FS22, there are no obstacles per say. You know from start, how much crops you get from the harvest, how much money you get for the crops in what month, there are no random events presenting challenge like crops being damaged by storm or some infection, cattle dying from illness, very hard winter, the machines do not even randomly break down and the tear&wear in the game is not having any actual impact, everything is linear and stable. You know, that from this field, that takes ca 1h to prepare, after one year you get X of crops and Y dollars of revenue, the same for 100 years onward. All that while the economics of the game does not present much challenge and i would dare to say, if you do not do complete nonsense, it is impossible-to-fail game.You could say, that in other games it is the same, if you act normally, you cannot lose either.  But in other games you could lose a match, die (until next reload), you to some extent do not know, what to expect. And when you know, it is usually boring grind game, that nobody plays. So why 155hrs of playtime? I was trying to fiddle with the game via mods, trying to make it "a game", but the mods I found eventually do not change the core mechanics of the game enough so to make it lasting fun. Thus most of the 155h was simply plotting a course via CoursePlay, me leaving the PC running and doing something else, while the AI spent hours and hours by plowing, rolling, picking stones etc.. I saw a video on YT, that this game can be perceived as simulation of driving the different machines, supporting the sales of these in the real life. Therefore also DLCs are basically new machines from same or different manufactures. And I do agree, if I would have a gaming steering wheel and nice music track, I can imagine it is actually kind of relaxing and satisfactory (YT image), but than I would put it into the same category as yoga, meditation etc. Positive things, but not .. games. I do not regret the time invested, this "game"does somehow scratch an itch I did not know I have, will still look for mods, that may bring the variability and challenge to the game, but until that happens..

_childDocuments_.review: Truth be told I put a LOT of hours into FS19 and had a good time doing it but FS22 has left me feeling underwhelmed and rather frustrated with Giants. FS22 really feels like a DLC rather than a full game. There is not much difference at all from FS19 besides the inclusion of three new crops - one of which is a standard harvester crop and what were once expansive Mods in FS19 feature in the game as massively watered down versions; RM Seasons and Global Company. Both in themselves exceptional mods for adding some well needed depth and breadth to Farming Sim's 19s shallow gameplay have themselves been clawed back to their bare bones by Giants and stuck in the game; more gimmicks than actual decently improved gameplay mechanics.The economic system is still a shallow and uninteresting loop of sow, harvest, sell, repeat. Vehicle condition bars still mean absolutely nothing - let it run out, you'll pull implements slower and thats it. That's all it does. Vehicles still have no sense of mass or traction. Pallets are STILL buggy and also have no mass or friction and slide around on trailers and the floor like they're on casters. AI vehicles are still immovable mass holes and the AI is still as bad as it was. AI helpers are still as fricken stupid as they ever were and unless working on an infinite and blank plane will get stuck on everything and seem to have no sense of what they're doing or have done.The new maps are actually more dull than FS19's base game offerings; maps are bland and lifeless and STILL look like something from 10 years ago in terms of graphics and animations. This game might have come out in 2021 and be called Farming Sim 22 but make no mistake. . .  this is Farming Sim 17.2.Character creation is nice but its the same as the rest of the game; lazily put together with very little effort or imagination, there are some presets to pick from and that's it. Still no third person mod though unless you're in vehicles.FS22 tbh for the money is just not worth it. I would be more than happy to wait longer between games for Giants to actually make some tangible changes instead of ripping off mods and basically making the same game they've been making since FS15 but selling it to us like its something new. It ain't.

_childDocuments_.review: This being the 5th version of Farming Simulator I have played; it's pretty safe to say that I am a fan of it.  There is no doubt.  I will start by saying that this is literally the same game as FS19.  As it is, FS17-15-13.  A common complaint from some people for reasons that I do not understand.  What makes our favorite games, our favorite game?  If they turned it into a tractor demolision derby; would it be the same game we love now?  While that does sound fun; it is not what we all originally bought the game for.  We buy (and then rebuy) these games because there is something about them that we like.  Why has the GTA Franchise been so wildly popular all of these years?  For the reason I pointed out above.  Standard Psychology aside...After almost 40 hours in game, I will say that FS/LS22 is essentially as it always has been.  And I personally like that.  It's familiar, the game play is easy to fall into and the mechanics are essentially on the same page.  This is something I personally look for when buying a continuation of a title.  If I have to relearn the entire control and play sequence every time a new version comes out; I am eventually going to leave it for something else.  This actually played a hand in what turned out to be my dislike for "Professional Farmer: Cattle and Crops."  The process between the two was so drastic that I determined that I did not have the time to become immersed in CnC, with all the other things going on in my life. (The game had tremendous potential though. I was praying for it's success).  Other games, guitars, synthesizers and autistic sisters do not afford me that luxury.  So being able to skip the Tutorial Mode and actually get right to playing on a basic level with just my Xbox style controller is a huge A+ for me.  My G29 and Saitek panel will follow, but for now, I'm just chugging along old skool.This release does offer some significant changes that are worth investing in if you are an FS17 or 19 player interested in continuing your farming streak.  It does incorporate a new Seasons algorithm comparable to the Seasons mod that has been popular for many years.  I don't use it because time does not allow me crop rotation or choosing localized profiles.  So I will let others speak more on that.  You can turn Seasons off, but keep the seasonal rotation going.  So the months (and the leaves on the trees etc.) change and it snows during the winter (you may want to plow that, and you can), but you can still farming arcade style and not miss some of the prettier details in these updates without extra time required to play more realistically.You can even lock the game to a particular season/month and just play static weather if you want.  Of course, all of the standard settings are there; weeds, plowing requirements, crop destruction,workers buy supplies and so on.So graphics... yeah.  I believe they are improved in the way that one would be able to improve on something that has been working for you for years.  I have heard complaints, but I haven't experienced any real issues while saying that the graphics have advanced well.  Displaying all the mirrors, having lights on and my beacons works way better on FS22 on my now old i5-9400F/GTX 1660i that I used on FS17, where it stuttered under heavy loads and could only display 3 mirrors at a time.  That has to be, by any logic, better.  Your experience may vary, or maybe your rig is crap.  Clinical observation.FS22 introduces "Production."  Having learned from the modding community, that we like to do more than just grow wheat and deliver it to sale, means a lot to us.  So they have introduced bakeries and woodworking shops, and a few other productions that you may simply grow and ship to, or purchase and make part of your operation.  With this has come some added crops, sorghum, grapes and olives specifically.  This is cool and fun thus far in the base game.  And I can't wait to see what modders do with these new opportunities.Serious complaint note here:  The maps that come with the game do not allow very much space for building in these new tools and severely limit how much you can expand your empire.  We need some big a** maps with a lot of buyable land from the modding community!  And I say that with much love, as we have some serious map artists out there. (Looking your way Stevie, dajnet and Papa Smurf)!  My 3 favorite map makers out there.  I'm sure that there are other fans who will be in touch with their people.  There are already a couple of interesting edits of Elmcreek that give a little more space.  Thanks XUL!I could go on, but I suggest you check it out for yourself.  Please keep in mind that there are some bugs that need to be worked out, as always with a new release of FS/LS and some patience is required for the most rewarding experience.  If you are wondering about upgrading?  It is an upgrade, so I would recommend it.Happy Farming!{These are solely my views. I have not be asked or rewarded by Giants Software in any way for this review. Not even sure they would like it}.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I only have 10+ hours of playtime currently, I've noticed almost everything that they've tweaked and improved.Pros:- Built-in seasons mod with the ability to disable it for those, who want the classic FS experience.- Overhauled sounds - everything sounds nicer and more realistic than ever before.- A lot of placeables, decorations, the new fence building system is amazing.- Two new maps (and one from FS19, which looks amazing), they feel very detailed and welcoming.- Better graphics (they aren't very noticeable, but the game looks and feels very good).- Better vehicle physics.- Manual gearbox option.- New plants and equipment for them.- Character customization.- Used equipment (even though this was available as a mod for FS19, it just works better now).- The production chains are just amazing. That means even more ways to earn money.- New ground textures.- Rocks appearing in the fields.- Nicer looking UI.- AI workers can do a lot more.Cons:- There are some bugs that need to be fixed, but I haven't experienced something major.- Improved AI workers sometimes feel just as dumb as they were in FS19.- Some features are missing, like removing existing buildings from your farm.- Some brands from older FS titles are missing (modding community will fix that, probably).- Landscaping feels... well, it felt somewhat better in FS19.I haven't tested every single piece of machinery and I haven't played on all maps, so there might be something I've missed.Overall, I think that FS22 is worth the money and I really recommend it. It doesn't feel improved for the first hour or so, but then you'll notice the small changes they've made. If they will release a patch for the existing bugs, this game will be perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, I've hit 500 hours on this game in the last nearly 2 years, and I figure it's time for a review. So let's get into it.There are alot of people dogging on this game for just being another repeat - which it is. I have to agree with this. But also remember the fact there's a ton of new features and polishing with this. This game feels like a whole different franchise just from the polishing. There isn't random clipping textures, holes in equipment, 144p looking wear textures on equipment.. This game looks good. Like really good. Though if I'm honest this game is what 19 needed to be.Big features with this version are the addition of built in seasons which you can customize to your liking, and while it may not be Realismus seasons, it's pretty damn good. I really enjoy playing with it. Also the maps have tons of live features now, so for example when a new DLC is approaching the billboards and signs start showing info for that DLC, and during seasons, you'll see barbecues in the summer, halloween deco in October, and snowmen/Christmas deco in December. It's a really nice addition, and finally the maps feel like they have some life. As for the maps themselves, you have Elmcreek which is based in the Midwest region of the USA, hard to place exactly where but I would say Iowa/Indiana/Illinois area, just based on the overall area. There is also a french map, that I think is pretty bland and disappointing, and I couldn't say where it's based but I would say it's the western part. There is also Erlengrat which is a Swiss map from FS19's Alpine DLC. It's the exact same map and while I love playing on it, it does have some FPS issues and can be very confusing if you don't understand the concept of the map.Next we move onto equipment. Here's where it gets wild. The brands they brought into this release, among small things everybody has wanted, is insane. There has to be a minimum of 25 new brands in this game and at least 100 new machines not counting any DLC. It's truly insane the equipment selection in this game. There's some weak points, like mid size seeders and cultivators, but there's ways around it. You of course have plenty of mods, or you can stick with smaller stuff and just deal with the extra time taken. I do a mix of both. There's some tractors that have US and EU spec options, all crawler tractors and harvesters have 3D tracks, interiors are fully animated.. There's an insane jump in this version that 19 doesn't have. Yes 19 had some stupid nice tractors but not all. You could see the recycled stuff compared to the new stuff, in this version even the recycled equipment has all the up to date features. It's truly another level of attention to detail. Not to mention loaders and such now make a bang when lowered fully, new hydraulic sounds, new attach sounds.. And don't forget manual transmissions. While the implementation of manuals is pretty garbage, it's still one more thing this game was severely lacking in older versions. It's only weird on some vehicles, on some it works fine. All in all having this feature in the base game is a huge jump even if it's implemented terribly.In terms of the farming aspect, it's pretty much the same, however there are some small differences. With Seasons enabled, you can only plant and harvest in certain months of the year, which adds just a little more realism. Crop growth is no longer randomized. It takes a set amount of months to grow whether you have Seasons on or off. For example wheat takes 10 months, and potatoes take 5. The plant/harvest chart reflects this. Turning off the seasons just makes it where you plant whenever and harvest whenever. There is also parallox occlusion mapping, which makes anything rows look 3D even though they aren't. While it may not be as good as true 3D ground, it looks extremely nice. There are also grape vines and olive groves now, and the respective equipment to harvest these. They are annoying, but fun. There are no new animals in this version. Aside from these it's pretty much the same old farming system from 19.Now on to landscaping and build mode. The landscaping mode remains mostly unchanged from FS19 aside from being way more polished and working a whole lot better, among new ground materials. Foliage and ground are separated, and you can do some truly wild stuff through the landscaping tool. As for build mode, this is a new addition that effectively took the Placeables menu and turned it into it's own mode. There's a ton of new lists and menus, you can place almost anything. Fences, animal pens, decorations, productions.. Almost anything you can place, and if you don't find it there, guaranteed there's a mod for it. You can literally build a map from bare nothing if you want using just the build and terrain tools. It's pretty cool.Coming to the end you have stuff such as the modhub, crossplay support, multiplayer, and other finishing touches. The multiplayer is an absolute disaster. I'm not talking in people, I'm talking the server side. It's been pretty broken since the game's release, and only minimal improvements over time. They consolidated the 6 individual servers down to 1 massive server, and on busy days, forget MP entirely. It overloads in no time flat, and if you do get in, have fun staying in. It's a DISASTER. As for the in game modhub, not much is changed, though you no longer have to restart after getting mods, they just automatically install and you're all set. There's a good selection of mods, both PC only and crossplay, and that brings us to crossplay. You can play with someone on a console, from PC, as long as you have matching CROSSPLAY mods. Not just any mod is crossplay, only certain ones are. Because consoles are so limited on space and licensing, only non licensed (and brands already in-game) are allowed. This will never be changed. If you want a bunch of cool modded stuff, buy a PC and do the game the right way. Consoles are NOT meant for this type of game.All in all, this game is a 7/10. There are a ton of good features about it, it's extremely stable and seems to just work all times unlike the last 2 versions, and there are a few bad features. The biggest thing to me is I feel like a lot of the features of this should have been for FS19 and in this version they should've focused on 3D ground, more realistic harvesting, more crops and other things people have been asking about for years. But maybe the next iteration will have a few of these. Though this is a healthy addition, and while 19 was a ton of fun and I enjoyed it, this is a MUCH more polished game. 19 was constantly crashing, full of broken equipment, missing textures, bugged maps and more. This one has hardly any bugs. Even when it released almost everything worked, and within 2 weeks the game had no bugs. The only real issue is the multiplayer, but it works if you understand when to use it for a good experience. All in all this game is a very polished and fun to play game. The price tag is a little high, but it is worth it. The attention to detail in this version is worth the extra money. You won't notice it until you play but they went over the top with details on everything. It's pretty awesome.Hope this was a helpful review that talks someone into this game. I know I've gotten my moneys worth and will continue to do so. This is a really good game in the series. Let's hope the next one is even better.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do enjoy this game, but in it's current state it's got too many flaws for me to recommend it, I will update this review if the bugs and problems are addressed by Giants in the future.The good:Once again, a fair bit is added to the franchise, we see many new things, some in which we wanted and others that came by surprise. I'll list most of the new ♥♥♥♥:- Giants added weather!!! You can now have it set where you do certain stuff in certain conditions if you want that extra realism.- Grapes and wineries were added, they were coming into effect with multiple maps adding them, although vineyards are a pain in the ass most of the time.- Nice looking maps with high detail.- New game thingies that you can collect as well as little toys that resemble machinery, to continue the 'find all the objects' that fs always had.- Sleeping so you don't have to sit in a tractor waiting for the sun to come up, remove that stash of energy drinks (that don't actually exist).- Additional realism to make your farm feel real.- Horses!!! (could have missed them in FS19, didn't play that one)- The ability to reshape the ground for a fee as well as add additional foliage to satisfy your preferences on terrain and look, many other objects you can spawn in such as lights and other little things.- DOGS!!!!!!!- Electric vehicles so your environment fanatics aren't offended by the use of fuel.- Small details in the interior of vehicles. (fun fact, Lizard Pickup 2017 has Apple CarPlay but it's not usable)The bad:So far, most of the time that I have played is multiplayer with two other friends, we have a good time some nights but there are clear bugs and the engine, despite having quite a graphics update, still lacks the basics of a game engine. Here are a list of the things I mean://////the following have ONLY been noted in multiplayer//////- The physics absolutely flawed, if you're doing logging or such things with a chainsaw, be prepared for, well... you'll know it when you see it, when you cut logs into smaller pieces, sometimes you get some kind of invisible objects that block you from your wood, sometimes smaller pieces of wood are lighter than others, small 5mm thin cuts of wood can be too heavy for your fella to lift, I mean go to the gym mate. Another example is when you walk with an object, it obstructs you and causes strange movement and you randomly drop it, when you throw them, they never land properly and freeze as soon as they hit the ground with a look that makes the map feel like a new planet altogether.- Tessellation (3d textures): This one was featured in other games for a while, they hide it pretty well, but FS22 doesn't have 3d terrain, it looks strange when gravel hits a curb and looks like a mapping issue where the curb is off the ground just a little, this here makes the game look like S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky (2008) with slightly more hd textures.- The overall movement is ugly, this has never been updated since FS13 or one of those older ones, stairs and small spaces are so damn hard to get through, and you randomly climb some objects by jumping up them, it's funny to watch but gets tedious at times. You can also get stuck easy.- Animals were added to give the map more feel, but they're janky as hell, like deer for example, they run through buildings or other things and look like assets from a 90's game.I don't know why, but they downgraded the AI something fierce, AI workers are lifeless idiots and if a navigation mesh is blocked by even the smallest object, they stop and stare, it reminded my of A Bug's Life where all the ants had a hard time going around the the leaf when it fell in their path. But here they don't think of going around it or over it, they just don't know what to do. The drivers are idiots (Must've learnt to drive in the city) and are a part of Elmcreek's biggest family of identical members, every driver is the same person in the same clothes!!!I'm sure there might be more but I really haven't noticed.The bugs I have experienced are also pretty random and although not gamebreaking, still are a hassle to get past, I'll list them below (ALL ARE MULTIPLAYER)- Terrain completely breaks itself. Sometimes, the terrain will randomly elevate, creating massive slopes, when you walk in them you move up and down in a weird way, they inconveniently appear right on machinery storage so we get problems, the other thing is, only I can see them, no other players can. Other times it goes in a weird wavy pattern.- Horse collision is hilarious. When two players on horses collide, they fly up into the air until you move and go back down.- Machinery such as seeders and cultivators fold out and randomly go upside down, rendering them inoperable, causing you to have to sell that one and buy a new one, and if you're on low budget, sometimes you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥.- Machinery can also get stuck frequently and also spin out of control, I fortunately had my friends to get me unstuck on certain objects like trees, this has never been fixed. in any of the builds of Giants Engine.- Invisible objects can sometimes be found around harvesting trees and such, making them difficult, physics engine is an absolute joke.Conclusion: Giants Engine was never intended to be a high quality physics engine but at the moment it's not great, it doesn't hold it's standards to some older engines at times, however 2021 birthed other ♥♥♥♥ games from other franchises, Farming Sim 22 is much more forgivable than Battlefield: 2042, GTA: The Trilogy and Call of Duty: Vanguard. Because unlike those ones, I'm sure Giants will work on tweaking the game, when that happens, I will recommend this game but AT THE MOMENT it's not worth it.

Really, I'm fine with both of those if it wasn't for the lack of improvement and new features.Currently, there are a bunch of bugs and issues that keep me from enjoying this game as much as I could, I'll just name whichever of those go through my head right now:-Multiplayer is super unstable, for two reasons. Some console players have issues with connecting to the point where they are unable to partake in MP. This is confirmed by lots of players throughout discord and the Giants forum. Same goes for the fact that the servers are massively overloaded during peak hours. You can notice this by the fact that you are hardly able to enter the server browser anywhere between 5 and 11pm gmt.-There's a bug that freezes your tractor and renders it useless if you are using the big bag equipment until you reset it to the dealership. If anyone needs help with this: Use the map to reset the tractor to the dealership, then restart the game. That's the fix for now.-The absolute lack of documentation for how game features behave. There are a few ingame hints but really, they've left so many question marks throughout the community, it's just saddening. And the "farming academy" they've released on the game page is at like 10% completeness.-There's a bug that renders direct seeders useless. -The fact that, despite how they've botched the release, they still are already selling a season pass for big money and started a dlc shop with single vehicles for 1-4€ each. People are just left on their own with the broken mp and community assistants deliberately avoid answering questions about this on their discord. However, inbetween the times I've asked, they've been very quick with responding to questions about the delayed release for the Mac OS. However, they've now added a "sEmI aUtOnOmOuS hElPeR" which does nothing more than drive to a preset point. _childDocuments_.review: solid 8/10its boring, i will 100% stand by that, but there's a bit more to it than that, that makes the game into the ultimate "turn your brain off" type game. pop on a twitch stream while you play, hell, i've read books while playing the game. lemmie walk through how i got the hours i have.First i bought all my equipment, then i sewed a field, then i did some contracts, then i made some money, then i wanted to see how it played out, so i sold the crop and made money, and then i wanted to try out the big machines, so i sewed another field, ...and then i harvested, ...and then, ...and then, ...and then, ...and then, ...and then, ...and then, ...and then, ...and then, ...and then, ...and then suddenly you wasted your whole weekend tending to fake sheep to pay off your fake debt to feed your fake video game dog and pay off your fake $500,000 combine harvester.the game has a weird innovation that allows the game to play itself, need to use the bathroom?, don't pause! just tell the AI worker to do your work for you! don't wanna harvest potatoes because its dull? tell the AI to do it! the game paves over the boring parts by just letting you skip them through programmable AI workers making a 2 hour cultivation job into you just waiting to hit the "collect contract" button while you watch TV or do your real world laundry.the QOL features of this game are absolutely second to none, theres an in game mod explorer, in game radio, AI workers for boring stuff, custom time scales, customization in the levels of realism, and good multiplayer configs.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've been plowing through Farming Simulator 22, and here's my take on it.Let's start off with the visuals, as they definitely need work. For example, the water reflections are absolutely terrible, as there's invisible trees showing on the water.  Also, the water ripples aren't even there.  In addition, the lackluster tree designs left me scratching my head.Character customization? More like character limitation! Wardrobe options are on the slim side, and forget about defining facial or body features. Hair choices? Limited. Color options? Unfortunately, its all limited. It's like the farm fashion police are on patrol.Missions, oh nice! Harvesting, bailing, fertilizing, and seeding are all well and included in the game.  However, where's the liming, chaff/silage, transport missions, and weed control action as contract work?  Unfortunately, all are MIA.  Moreover, don't get me started on the realism front. Tracks and multiple wheel sets on farm tractors and implements are a great addition to the game, although field conditions don't affect the use of these features. In addition, vehicles sipping on DEF? Not in this game.  You'll have to look on a mod website for these items.Palm tree enthusiasts, brace yourselves! Giants didn't bring palm trees to the party despite requests from the consumer, for the forestry side of the game. DLCs? appears to be somewhat limited content. Maps and vehicles are slim pickings, although there are some nice ones.Now, the silver lining – the game nails the down-to-earth farmer experience. Planting crops, raising animals, it's all there. Yet, the real MVPs? The modders. They've transformed this game into a global agricultural extravaganza, bringing in maps, machinery, and all the gameplay tweaks that Giants missed.In a nutshell, if you're dreaming of a serene life in the digital countryside, Farming Simulator 22 might just appeal to you. It's a chill, entertaining game with a farm-life vibe. Just be ready to rely on mods for the full farming buffet.Happy farming! 🚜🌾

_childDocuments_.review: *** I Never Wanted to be A Farmer, Until Now ***I've never bought a Farming Simulator. I never thought it would be interesting or fun. I purchased it on a whim, as of the 1.2 patch. Let me tell you, this game is a gem. There are many reasons why.First of all, it's the best sandbox style game I have played in a long time. Perhaps, it is the best. There is just a primal urge for most of us to dig in the dirt, grow things, and play with trucks and tractors. You can also raise animals, and grow your own food for them. You can buy factories and start production chains. You can mow up grass, and make hay bails. There is so much to do.It's a little tricky to start with, especially for a new player. But after about 6 to 8 hours, I got most of it figured out, so it's not too bad. Just try not to learn too much at once.My favorite part of the game is tuning into the many streamed radio stations, and relax while I do my thing that needs doing. There is nothing quite like using a cool mower while jamming out to 80's Hairband music with a nice icy glass of Jack and Coke within reach. I've never been so chill playing a game before.You want to landscape and get really creative? This game has you covered in that, too. You can create your own simple or crazy fields. You can use tree planters to place real growing trees in your yard. With clever use of field creation, you can make your own gravel roads with growing grass down the middle. You want to make weird crop circle type fields to communicate with aliens? Go for it.Do you want to have laughs with your friends chainsawing trees while struggling with goofy physics? You can do that too. Multiplayer works great. Sure, you could potentially behave yourself, but that's for boring people you shouldn't probably play with in the first place. Tell people who are too serious to just play with themselves, and have fun with cool people. Boring stuck-up people suck.Some of the complaining about the game are just crying about things that changed from previous versions. Take that with a huge grain of salt. The same people would have complained if it was the same with a fresh coat of paint. I'm tired of those kinds of people. Let them play their old versions, while you enjoy all the cool new things and features.There are seasons in the game. This is super neat-o, and reminds me of the days I grew up in an area with major farmland. I sure miss rural living where snow used to be measured in feet. This city life I am living now stinks in comparison. Seasons don't matter too much in the city besides when it's way to hot in the summer, and you cook yourself walking on concrete.The only real complaint I have is the snowfall. It's there, but so far, it's sort of lame. I want to see huge banks that are so big you can't see the neighbor's house. Oh well. There's barely enough to write your name in it by <deleted for censorship reasons>.Finally, do you like game options? If your answer is yes, then you will be so happy that it will take plastic surgery to remove your smile. There's a lot of game play customization. Change time and month length all you want. Adjust other things when you feel like it. But don't be a total wimp, and turn off too much stuff. Otherwise, you might as well money cheat your way to infinite wealth, and then end up complaining about lack of content. Don't be a turd.It's not perfect, but seriously, don't miss out. There's a lot of game here.If you enjoyed my review, please rate it. I'm not a Youtuber or even bother with social media, but if i can brighten someone's day with a few chuckles, that's pretty darn cool.Lastly, don't point your chainsaw at anyone. That's naughty.
