_childDocuments_.review: With Farming Simulator 22, Giants Software shows the world that they are the first and foremost in developing farming simulator games, bar none.   No other developer has been able to release such a long running series, that is more than just a 'niche' market at this point.I'll admit, I've spent 1000s of hours playing their games ever since FS2011 (also tried FS2009 later to see how it compared).  I can attest that each release added enough new features and technical advancements to make it worthwhile to purchase and enjoy, but not all were grand slams out of the ballpark hits.   For me personally, after 160hrs of playing FS22, I can say they really, really have done an amazing job.From the get go at launch, I was impressed with the equipment, the maps, and the huge amount of details that has been added to really amplify the realism of the game.   From the textures and design of the crops and vegetation, to the smallest animations of latches opening/closing and having custom sounds for each movement.  It simply really blew me away how much these animations and sounds made this game amazing.Sure, there are some bugs and issues, but relatively few for a newly launched game and compared to some past releases.   It took a bit of time, but were also slowly seeing released mods from the very talented pool of players who are back again in FS22.    The incorporation of some previous mods and ideas made by players have found themselves incorporated into FS22, mind you it's not totally the same but it's a good balance.  Speaking specifically about the Seasons mod vs. FS22 Seasons being actually a thing in the game now.  It's not complex as the mod, but it's enough to simulate the cycles of growing and harvesting crops.Also introduced into the game, thanks to previous player mods, we have factories to either supply or own to operate as part of a small supply chain for your goods.The husbandry is also well made, but I find this is one part that could use some work.   Some of the requirements are a bit lacking when it comes to caring and rearing your animals.  Such as watering being obsolete in the indoor barns being they are on automatic watering.    The feeding requirements could also of been a bit more flexible with more options based rearing, breeding, milk production, etc.  The automatic Lely cow feeding system is real nice, but we have no control on feeding ratios or feeding times like the previous player mod.There is so many options for a player in this game with vineyards for grapes, olive groves, a huge number of crops including the addition of sorghum, or taking care of various animals like chicken, cows, sheep, pigs, and horses.  I would of liked a few other species like previous mods which included rabbits, goats, geese, etc..The forestry portion hasn't had much of a change, except that you can produce planks and furniture now like a previous player mod, but no palettes for all the production points.Another feature which hasn't had much of an upgrade, is greenhouses apart from adding actual palettes of produce that you can store and load for sale.   There's no need for any manure or compost, only water... that's it.  Speaking of manure, your cows and pigs are the only animals that produce manure, but their barns doesn't include a manure storage place.  You need to place one yourself if you choose to collect it for spreading or selling.There's so much more that I could cover about FS22, but part of the fun is to discover some of this on your own.   As well, opinions vary of course, so I understand what  I've said may or may not ring true for some, and that's all fine.   I want to hear what you've found great or not so great about the game, so please leave a comment below.Much appreciated, and Happy Farming.

_childDocuments_.review: Over the past couple years, I've racked up a lot of hours in this game, and while I don't regret a single one of them I unfortunately cannot recommend this product still. FS22 is, sadly, simply FS19 with a fresh coat of paint and a bunch of features shoved in that highlight just how backwards the development of this franchise it. But, that is the end result of becoming the number one farming simulation game and having investors to appease, I suppose. Regardless, the cracks are starting to show, whether through the AI, the physics, or the DLCs.For the first point, there are additional AI features in FS22, but they are unreliable to the point I don't use them. The traditional AI that fails to plow a square field is still there, but now you can unleash them on the world at large (deliberately) with the new routing mechanics. That said, even though they have a new feature, they still work the same under the hood meaning a complete lack of actual pathfinding or collision detection. So, more often than not, they end up stuck, give up, or both, just like in the previous installment.The physics too continue to be a gripe of mine. Productions, even in the base game, are all but required to profit as they generally increase profit by double or more, but also introduce an ungodly number of pallets if done improperly. You can work around this by setting productions to either teleport your goods between themselves, or immediately sell, either way making the productions practically no different to a normal sell point. But pallet handling is a core part of the gameplay loop, yet I continue to both experience myself and observe pallets either having no friction whatsoever, or flying after the pallet fork as you drive away. The physics engine continues to be a problem as DLCs like Silverrun Forest are released, which shows off just how broken the log handling physics are as well.This segues nicely into my final gripe, which is more about the approach to DLCs in general. There is, of course, the obligatory mention of the Pumps and Hoses DLC not being included in either season pass, but that is not actually an outlier as there are also a few $2-3 DLCs that add one or two tools that are also not included. But in general, the DLCs tend to have a lack of meaningful content, Pumps n' Hoses included, either hamfisting things into the old system in the case of Zielonka's ridgers (or the base-game grass mulchers) simply applying a layer of fertiliser instead of having unique mechanical benefits, or paywalling random unrelated features in the case of the Kubota DLCs passenger system. The models in the DLCs also tend to be less feature rich than some mods, and I don't think that is an unfair comparison as mods fundamentally are the same type of content most of the DLCs provide. On their own, the DLCs are fine but they show a lack of integration, instead each DLC exists in its own silo as if meant to be used on its own rather than part of a greater Farming Simulator whole.Overall, then, while Farming Simulator 22 is a game I enjoy, it is not one I can recommend as a product of the capitalist challenges every successful franchise must face. Many new features and content packs have been provided to us over the past two years, providing a very different base game experience to FS19. But the core gameplay loop hasn't changed, the engine and it took two years to get meaningfully different crops. If I didn't play multiplayer, I wouldn't have seen a reason to change. If you are looking to get into the FS franchise, 19 is just as competitive of a farming simulator as 22 unless you really like watching the broken physics struggle or want to try something FS22 specific, like the Pumps n' Hoses DLC. But by the same margin, you may want to wait, as in lieu of a Year 3 Season pass we may hear more about the next PC entry in the coming future. And seeing the direction this franchise has taken, it will only be more expensive and monetized than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from the 1). Step forward 2). Steps back approach. I played the previous Farming Simulator 2019 title and enjoyed it when it was released. I have also worked in agriculture and am familiar with the real life equivalent. Please bear in mind this review is just my 2 cents opinion. At the end of the day it's your time, your money and I hold no judgement against anyone that likes this game. The game is presentable enough, but for the price it feels a lot like a BETA release. The standard draw distance is quite frankly terrible. When I was playing with a friend on flat ground; he and the bales in the paddock would appear and disappear on every run up and down the paddock. Another time I was harvesting corn and the machine kept harvesting outside of the dimensions of the cutting bar; which I personally find irksome. Petty I know.The microtransactions are not a nice addition, from different editions of the game, expensive DLC when compared to free mods and features you expect to be in the base game. I can only speculate the GIANTS Software pays for licensing from many of these companies that essentially advertise to the player. Just saying. In addition I have had a lot of stability issues on my end; which are not hardware issues in the sense that I have a contemporary rig with a 3080. Wasted a lot of time getting the game to run without crashes is common for me; with Direct X 11, not running the game in Administrator mode & graphics card updates breaking the game. Although I cannot lay all these issues at GIANTS Software, the game seems to suffer from optimization bugs which when searched for on the web date back to this games release and have to be solved by you to work around . IMHO the game is not worth the full price tag and lacks the care and attention that would make this game really amazing. I will probably continue to play it from time to time with my friend; even with giving this game a down vote. Please continue to support the mods, they fill in all the gaps that players like myself want to see; grateful to them.If you finished reading this review, thank you for your time. Have a great day.

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional game. Features many improvements over previous titles, in the form of physics, fully functional transmissions, true character customization, and native seasons. However, I have two serious takeaways. One is that they still haven't fixed the hitbox bugs with wood, which makes logging a pain. Shame, as this was one of my favorite moneymaking methods in previous games, and they clearly have no interest in fixing it. Another is that they added passenger support as a feature, then made it so that in order to access the feature, you need to purchase one of their DLC packs. That's a really scummy move for a feature that should have been in the game from the get go. I love this series, it's probably the only game franchise that I will gladly purchase without waiting for reviews or gameplay, and I appreciate that the devs didn't fall into the Devil's trap of making their game a timed epic gaymes store exclusive. However, until the developers fix these two issues, I will have to leave this review at "not recommended." I will change this review in a heartbeat if these things are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Farming Simulator 22: A Veteran Farmer’s Dream Come TrueAs someone who has tilled the virtual fields of Farming Simulator since its early days, I can confidently say that Farming Simulator 22 is the pinnacle of the series. With each iteration, Giants Software has honed their craft, and FS22 is a testament to their dedication to the farming simulation genre.Graphics & Gameplay: The leap in graphical fidelity is immediately noticeable. The landscapes are lush, and the equipment gleams with a realism that only years of refinement can achieve. The addition of seasonal cycles not only adds visual variety but also introduces strategic depth to the farming experience.New Features: The introduction of new crops like grapes and olives, alongside the winemaking and oil production processes, offers a delightful new challenge. It’s a joy to expand my agribusiness beyond the traditional, exploring avenues previously untapped in my farming career.Community & Modding: The cross-platform multiplayer brings together a community of like-minded agriculturists, while the modding support continues to be the lifeblood of longevity, with endless possibilities that keep the game fresh long after release.Final Thoughts: Farming Simulator 22 doesn’t just simulate farming; it celebrates it. It’s a game that has grown with its players, and for veterans like myself, it feels like coming home to a bountiful harvest after years of investment. A well-deserved five stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst I’ve not got a huge number of hours in this version yet (19 at time of writing!), I have played 2 of the previous instalments and let me tell you that FS22 does not disappoint. Playing the game single player is fun but playing the game multiplayer with friends or other players who are serious about getting the job done, is even more fun especially when having a laugh on voice chat too.The attention to detail in the tractors and machinery is amazing and the sheer amount of equipment available is overwhelming, I have no idea what most of these machines do but I’m sure I’ll find out!Sure, there are a few little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, for example when switching from outside to inside cab there can be a kind of lag delay but once you’ve got past it once it doesn’t seem to be an issue again. Occasionally, vehicles/trailers vanish depending on the angle you’re looking around. They are there but they momentarily hide from you. Also, with the sound mysteriously muting then coming straight back on when walking near a particular part of the farm is just another little gripe. I would also suggest to the devs that descriptions of the items should be clearer, the text is small, dark, and hidden pretty much at the top right of the screen. I feel it should be more prominent. The number of times I’ve bought something only to find it doesn’t do what I wanted it to do because I hadn’t seen the description clearly.Having mentioned those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ above, they aren’t game breaking at all so with that said, I highly recommend this game if you’ve got many, many hours to spare as the time goes so quick…so much to do!Look Mammy, I’m a farmer now!

_childDocuments_.review: Another Edit: Was trying to stay away from the game but had a nagging curiosity on how the forestry side went.  Looks like Giants yet again didn't fix any of the forestry bugs from FS19.  Logs still pop right out through the logging tools.  Logs sometimes start to shift all on their own inside the trailer.  Logging tools get stuck on the trees they are cutting down.I seriously think the only thing Giants did with FS22 was update the graphics and added seasons which is worse than the modded seasons from FS19.  Modders seriously know how to code 1000x better than a Giants dev.Edit:  1.5 months later and game is still mostly bugged and I have learned that GIANT doesn't know how to do multicore coding which is why the game only utilizes 30% gpu loads and 50% of my gpu memory and only 15% of my cpu usage.  Surprisingly the game only uses about 2-3 GB of ram and yet it at times runs like a pig.  You can even set the graphics low and it doesn't help because there is probably some really bad coding.The patch before Christmas did next to nothing for the game.  Yes many of them are just quality of life issues but some are annoying. But at least they fixed the contracts that required 100,000 liters from a 0.5ha field haha.  But they haven't fixed it so the AI farms do there own work and all there crops just sit there withered and full of weeds unless you go and do the work for them so it looks really stupid driving down the roads.  And those two examples are just the start of it.After the patch I found 3 of my crops withered, key binds were all gone, and two of my structures disappeared and they were not even mod structures.Then there is damage rates of vehicles.  You don't want to repair vehicles because it costs about 10x more than you make from selling crops at peak selling times.  So you have to keep your vehicles and equipment broken to operate.The amount of stones they show on fields looks really stupid.  A field after plowing looks more like a quarry than a field with mix of some large rocks  here and there.  These guys really need to go do some volunteer work on farms to see what really happens.  Or at least watch some youtube videos of farmers who have plowed a grass field under.  There are rocks pulled up but no where near what it looks like in game.If this is the quality of work people from GIANT do, I wouldn't want to hire them should they go looking for jobs when there done at GIANT.Really disappointed with Giant software and the way they develop.  FS22 has very few original ideas added to it.  Most of the update is graphics (which I don't like) or adding stuff modders already added to the game.  So basically profiting off other peoples ideas (seasons, production chains).  Not that I don't want to see that being added, but it seems so little and not done as well other than graphics maybe.For example:  FS19 modded Seasons gives more weather info, such as chance of precipitation and crop rotations.As for graphics, things seem more blurry.  It is like the farmer always has bad eye sight.  Tried turning on MSAA but it has bad stutters, not sure they coded it correctly.  I've used MSAA in huge amounts of other games with barely any FPS loss.They did not improve the AI, they made it worse.  Luckily the AI doesn't damage fields.  But I've watched the AI drive a harvester back into the field it needs to cut.  The AI vehicles still don't stop at stop signs so expect to get rammed if you don't yield to traffic at all intersections.I was also hoping since they seem to be supporting north american map better that they'd add more american equipment.  But still 99% of the equipment has the EU hazard stripes rather than triangles.  Not sure why they even bothered to put in a US based map.  Thus they really lack in game immersion.Only thing I really liked over a modded FS19 is that they added gear shifting and a bit of force feedback which in itself was a shoddy type of FFB.  Basically just added some centering spring force.  As for gear shifting, it would have been better if they had control settings grouped into vehicle types.  So CVT drive vehicles use certain gamepad/wheel bindings.  And things like the Manual + Powershift would have there own, so that no bindings overlap.  Same goes for trucks which they could have setup similar to how ATS/ETS2 have setup.Overall, I personally feel a person is better off playing FS19 modded until people have remade there mods for FS22.  And from reading forums, it could take a couple of months to get enough mods that will make FS22 worth it.  So basically if you use a lot of mods, stick to FS19 for a bit longer.  My main point is, if your going to add what modders made to the vanilla version of the game, do it 100% or preferably 120-150% better because the modders are sometimes limited by the main game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: A welcome step forwards from 2019. I actually have more than the 4.3 hours, it isn't counting them for some reason.  Yes, there are bugs, yes performance is stuttery, and yes the content isn't super substantial.  It's about on par with FS 19 and its expansions.  The graphics have improved a good bit and the gameplay is enjoyable, the new additions make it a genuinely relaxing experience.  The stuttering and performance issues can be fixed pretty easily (unlike a massive AAA shooter I refunded to buy this)  Look up the Farming Sim 22 fps unlock tutorial. The game is soft locked to 60 fps for the physics engine and this leads to a stuttery experience because the game temporarily throttles framerate when it jumps above 60. This leads to a stutterfest that lasts a few seconds, ESPECIALLY when switching to first person in the vehicles.  This is easily solved by a simple XML edit that allows the game to go higher.  I was sitting at 56% gpu usage before the fix with some rough stutters, now I'm at 99.9% usage at 100fps and the stutters are very few and far between. The best part is the physics seem to still function normally.  Once the modding community transitions over to 22, this will be a highly recommended jump up. Who ever thought a farming sim would get a higher rating and have a smoother launch experience than the massive AAA failures this year?
_childDocuments_.name: Farming Simulator 22

_childDocuments_.review: Cultivated to be bigger and better the ultimate and multimillion selling farming simulation returns this November! Farming Simulator 22 offers more depth and the highest extent of player freedom in the history of the series. With more than 400 machines and tools from over 100 authentic agricultural brands, players can look forward to an improved and realistic as ever simulation. Suited for all ages, players dive into even more diverse agriculture, animal husbandry and forestry. Two new maps inspired by US and EU regions plus an updated alpine Erlengrat map emphasize different kinds of farming operations, including three new crops. The addition of seasonal cycles adds new challenges throughout the year, and enhances the atmosphere many times over. Players can now start various production chains to further extend their income whether they produce bread, oil, juice or more. To allow more individualization of farms and characters, the vastly improved customization tools add plentiful new possibilities. Based on the GIANTS Engine 9, Farming Simulator 22 also features many technical improvements such as more realistic AI behavior, richer worlds and a significant performance boost on all systems.

name: American Arcadia
detailed_description: Tune in to American Arcadia, the most popular reality tv show on the planet! In this retro-futuristic 70s metropolis all citizens enjoy a life of luxury and comfort... and are completely unaware that they're being broadcast 24/7! So escape from the real world and sit back to enjoy the most dangerous contest on air, where a drop in your popularity comes at the highest cost: death. Trevor Hills is your ordinary, everyday, average man. He’s more than happy with his mundane life as an office clerk. Unfortunately, this doesn’t make him very popular with the ever-important viewers of American Arcadia and sets him up for a one way trip to execution – unless he escapes. Luckily for Trevor, he’s got help. Angela Solano is a stage technician for American Arcadia, and she’s determined to make sure that Trevor gets out of Arcadia alive. Assisting from the outside, she uses her technical prowess and wits to manipulate the world around him, clearing the path to his freedom. But neither Angela nor Trevor are prepared for this escape to become a journey filled with twists, turns, and lies. Control two different characters in two different worlds as you play through Trevor’s escape in 2.5D puzzle platforming sections and assist him as Angela in first-person hacking gameplay. It’s only by working together that they have any chance to overcome the corporation they’re up against! After telling the story of love and loss in the 1930’s South Pacific, developers Out of the Blue have created a completely new experience set in a rich world of twists and mystery. Play through a layered narrative with the trademark polish and artistry from an award-winning studio with seasoned acting veterans Yuri Lowenthal ( Spider-Man 1 & 2, Call of the Sea ), Krizia Bajos ( Cyberpunk 2077, League of Legends ), and Cissy Jones ( Firewatch, Call of the Sea ) others bringing the characters and world to life.

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is by far one of my favorite games in general! I loved the platforming elements and the tricky puzzles that I admit, had to phone a friend to help, but besides that its just so well done. The characters were super interesting and the dialogue between both leads was hilarious, speaking of dialogue....the VA's did amazing in their performances, really brought life to the characters, and the music was great, I now have "Don't be a Fool" stuck in my head! Overall, an interesting premise that's super story rich and deserves more praise than what it has already. I look forwards to seeing more games from Out of the Blue

_childDocuments_.review: What a great take on the niche genre that is narrative 2D puzzle platformers (limbo, inside, etc). _childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is one of the best narrative driven games I've ever played. Engaging story with references to today's social media culture is definitely the highlight here. But this is not a walking simulator or anything like that. There is meaningful gameplay combining 2D platforming with first person view puzzle solving. My only gripe is Angela's sections are not as fun as Trevor's. Fortunately majority of the game is on Trevor's side of the story.  Voice acting is also top notch thanks to well know actors behind the mics. I would rate this game 9/10. Definitely one of the best indies of 2023.I also reviewed this on my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED this game!! Great story, super interesting and unique gameplay. Everything felt fresh and exciting. I could not stop playing, and I will definitely be replaying. There were a handful of bugs, but they were fixed once I reloaded the checkpoint. ABSOLUTELY worth the money I spent 10/10 play this game if you like story-based games.

_childDocuments_.review: 100%. SPOILER FREE American Arcadia OVERALL RATING: 8/10LENGTH: 5-7 hours100% ACHIEVEMENT EASE: There is a few missable achievements, but you can chapter select and get them very easily. WORTH THE PRICE?: Worth full price.   OVERALL:  American Arcadia is a Truman show like game, with different aspects but the game general concept. The game is primarily a sidescroller, with new great looking graphics, but it has a retro 90s game feel to it. The game has phenomenal storytelling, with twists and turns that I never expected, and even when the ones I did expect to happen, they still surprised me. You play back and forth between a few characters, and I must say it was very interesting as each is their own unique gameplay style. Very well done, and an absolute must play that wont break the bank, or kill you with a huge gameplay grind. The puzzles are awesome and truly feel natural. Progression also feels very natural, nothing is forced and there isn't any really boring parts of the game. I cannot stress enough how highly I recommend this game. PROS: The story telling is phenomenal, and the voice acting is very good. They set the stage well and really introduce and talk their way through the story well. It feels like true reality TV as you are playing the game. I put it in the cons too, but the amount of puzzles in this game that had a completely simple solution, but took me forever to figure it out was fantastic. The game really presents itself nicely, and while it seemed Truman Show inspired, it definitely takes on its own identity, and It really is like comparing apples to oranges by the end. CONS: Not very many cons I can think of, other than the controls, specifically the jumping mechanic can be odd at times, but otherwise nothing crazy. Sometimes puzzles had some very weird and tough solutions, but I would prefer that over only easy ones.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Limbo and Inside, it's like this but with bigger story and excellent art style.   The puzzles are a good challenge but tough enough to be annoying.   I enjoyed the game from beginning to end and was invested in the story the whole time.  Would recommend if you like games like Limbo and Inside.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool ideas executed in a way that I think is very sophomoric.Truman-show story with its own spin is pretty fun. Dual-mode mechanics also kind of cool. Some of the game is played as a Limbo-style sidescroller. Some of the game is a first person quasi-puzzler. Pretty neat.The puzzles never amount to anything. The gimmick is that you're side scrolling as main character A while also messing around with hacking and security as main character B. It's usually just hold right and click the button mindlessly when prompts appear, though.The storytelling also I think reveals the age of its writer (I think they're probably in their mid 20s). Kind of a by-the-numbers social thriller, but the details betray a lack of wisdom. We don't quit our jobs when severance is an option, for example. Also, yelling at our boss (telling them off) who is in the midst of firing us and then refusing severance to quit on principle will never put our boss in their place. That's something that would feel really good when we're 24 but would feel really stupid and self-sabotaging once we've got the experience that we gained through our 30s.That's an example. The story generally contains details like that. Beats and elements that feel good to someone who doesn't have much experience but are definitely off the mark to someone who has been there before.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool little game with great art direction. The 70s retro-futuristic aesthetic is always interesting and the defining part of the game. You get a nice mix of 2.5D puzzle-platforming with some third person hacking gameplay. There's some awesome voice talent (Yuri Lowenthal of the Spider-Man games) and the story is mostly engaging but falls a little flat at the very end. If you like the Truman Show and games like INSIDE you will enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The Truman Show if Truman knew what was up from the beginning and the whole movie was about him escaping. You switch between a 2d Puzzle Platformer like Limbo or Inside (just much more colourful) and first person puzzles with another character. Personally I much preferred the 2d sections and found myself wanting to go back to them very quickly whenever 3d came up. Much like the whole game, those sections are fairly short though, so they don't hold it back too much.7/10, play it if you're curious about the story and dig the style, don't expect revolutionary gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most enjoyable experiences I've ever had playing a game. It's basically a playable, video game version of 'The Truman Show'. Finished the majority of the game in a single sitting, as I was eager to keep seeing what was coming next. Puzzles aren't too difficult (although definitely a few challenging ones in there), but the story and characters kept me hooked.If you liked Inside, and are interested in something bigger and brighter, this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: First, I strongly recommend American Arcadia, with the caveat that  this is more "interactive storytelling with light puzzles" than it is a game.With that in mind, the setting, storytelling, characters, voice acting, graphical style, and sound design are all excellent.As an aside, I suggest watching this excellent Defunctland video (before playing, if you can), as the setting of Arcadia is HEAVILY inspired by Walt Disney's foolish, and doomed, vision for "EPCOT:  The City of the Future", and this background really adds a lot to the already-excellent satire in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I hardly ever write reviews on Steam, but this game deserves one! I haven't had this much fun with a title in a long time. The story is well written, the gameplay is great and the art style and game world just looks outstanding. I can recommend it to anyone who likes games like Inside or just wants to try something different.

So that the cool surprises feel more fun.I think the best part of the game is the fun factor and how the gameplay mechanics and story have a nice blending, and even though the story is linear and the gameplay is simple, you still have lots of fun experiencing it because of how fun everything is, the visuals, the music, the voice acting, the animation etc.Don't expect a game with deep or complicated game mechanics, this is a game with a simple purpose and that is for the player to have fun.Don't be a fool and get this fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is the perfect blend of story rich sci-fi and pop culture. It's easy to see the media that American Arcadia references and is inspired by. You can easily see the work of Disney, Office Space, The Matrix, The Island, and many others throughout your game play. As a fan of American cinema, this game hits on so many notes for me. Gameplay and controls are fluid, story is familiar yet original, and the switch between third and first person being both real and metaphorical is great.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a lot. I really enjoyed it's clever mix of 1st, 2nd, and 3rd person perspectives as well as a fun Truman Show influenced story, 70s utopia aesthetic, and excellent voice acting.Overall the game is pretty easy and the puzzles are nowhere as involved as Out of the Blue's previous game, Call of the Sea (which you should totally play, it's great!) but are still fun to solve. Definitely a story-first game. I do hope to see another game from OotB that uses the 3 perspective gimmick in a more challenging way in the future.Anyhoo, great game, give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a stylish and engaging mix of first-person adventure game and 2D puzzle platformer. The characters and dialogue are well-written and the story is interesting, though the plot twists are a bit predictable. The game uses a retrofuturistic '70s aesthetic which is quite appealing and there's always something interesting to look at. The first-person segments are mostly comprised of logic puzzles and exploration while the 2D segments are mostly platforming, with some simple navigation puzzles and light stealth elements. As with other games in the genre, there are quite a few instant fail states if you screw up. There were a couple of sections that got a bit annoying because it wasn't entirely clear what the designers wanted you to do, leading to repeated deaths through trial and error. In addition, the game often requires you to make split second decisions and you simply don't have enough time to make the right decision on your first try. That said, the checkpoints are pretty generous so you never lose any significant progress when you fail.Overall, I really enjoyed the 6 hours it took me to finish the game. The many instant fail states were sometimes annoying but the narrative and presentation were more than enough to keep pushing me through.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun story! Very well made, you can tell a lot of care was put into this. You might not like it if you're into walking simulators, since that's most of the game play. The puzzles aren't the most difficult, and they're few and far between, but the game play varies frequently enough that it stays interesting all the way through. Definitely worth a try!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, I enjoy the story and most of the puzzles are great.The gameplay itself in the 2 1/2D sections is a bit simplistic after a few moments near the start of the game and the game really doesn't feel like a Jump and Run.The story is really fun, being a great homage to the Truman Show and paroding a lot of Disney's History.The ending leaves me a bit mixed tho, it feels like kinda an Anticlimax, which actually makes the game more realistic to how the situation would play out in rl.A clear negative: weird technical issues.(For reference am playing on th 64 GB Steam Deck)During my playthrough I expirienced multiple crashes, mainly between switches from gameplay to cutscene, voicelines just not playing and in one weird instant an "enemy" not spawning or their voicelines not playing, leaving me very confused.Overall I'd recommend the game, really fun, wish they fixed the technical issues tho
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game, played together with my wife (she helped me in the puzzles that I got stuck on).  All the puzzles were intuitive and yet still interesting that they were fun to solve.Only criticism is that the game had a really good moment about the 3rd of the way through where you had to split focus bet ween the 2.5d platforming and the first-person interaction with pressure, I wish there was more of that in the later half.  Overall very engaging story though and a good recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I've never posted a review before, but this game was so good it prompted me to leave this glowing response as soon as I finished! I have not played such a good game in many, many years that's such a complete package. Cohesive, strong art style, great characters, the most engaging AND varied gameplay I've encountered in forever, and some of the best game story-writing. American Acardia was so good I played in through in two sittings, probably could've played it all in one if I'd started earlier the day before. This was such a random buy from Steam but the most rewarding experience I've had from a game in a long, long time. It's a crying shame this game isn't more popular because it is such a gem for being a compact but tight story-driven experience with engaging, inventive gameplay.

Saw the review for American Arcadia (of which I never heard of before). Was impressed.3. Checked the forums on the game news site about the game. Was even more impressed.4. _childDocuments_.review: A fun game with a cool premise you don't see often. The Truman show in a comedy puzzle platformer game. I think there's some quirks that need to get ironed out (i.e., boxes need to be in certain areas to allow the puzzle to perform correctly, or reloading a chapter because a certain piece of dialogue wasn't triggered) but it doesn't hamper the enjoyment that much. The voice cast was great and overall I had a great time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this game is very good, similar to Disney World Epcot's Tomorrowland, enjoying your daily life in a city of paradise, Arcadia broadcasts live 24/7 by Walten Media, but this kind of paradise hides dark secrets to what happen to it's residents suddenly vanished without a trace one by one, maybe they left the city for a vacation or should we say, killed.A office worker who's been targeted by unknown agents and police units are pursuing him, an activist tries to warn him that someone is killed here without any traces, not realizing that he's about to be executed, unless he escape the city while the undercover activist guides him to his safety and uncover the truth.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Never written a review before. This time, I have to. Loved the game. Loved the story. Whoever came up with the story-line really knows "The House that the Mouse" built. I loved the vibe and the feel of the whole thing. The Puzzles were not difficult, but it didn't matter. Came for the 70's vibe. Stayed for the plot. Can't wait to see what these cats come up with next. Get this game!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The only issue I had was that every chapter ended in such a way that I just had to play a bit longer, and so I played the whole game in one sitting. Honestly, if that's the only negative thing I can say about it, it's a pretty good sign that it's a great game. Fun music, a twisty plot, wonderful characters, and a solid ending.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the 70s aesthetic, stayed for the plot twists.I loved the visuals and environment of the game, the corporate 70s look is one I feel doesn't get a lot of attention. I wish the 70s vibe showed up more in the OST but that's a minor complaint. Another minor complaint is the captions often had typos or didn't exactly match or sync up to what a character was saying. I enjoyed the use of 2.5D with first-person, but I would have liked to see these modes interact simultaneously more often. The puzzles weren't insanely hard and had reasonable solutions, but it wasn't always clear to me how you were expected to find a solution outside from guessing or clicking on everything.The story is fun and an interesting take on a Truman Show format but applied to a wider scale. There's a lot of hidden secrets/twists that add to the f-ed up nature of the game's world, so be sure to explore as much of the environment as you can. Overall, I enjoyed the game. Check out the demo first and see if the game clicks with you.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The game will clock in around 6 hours and it hits just the right spot. The game plays like a good movie and it doesn't feel too short or too long-winded. New mechanics and riddles are rolled in constantly and the story and characters will engage your for the entire playthrough like a good action thriller.I suggest following the developers to see what they put out next, because this game is crafted so well in so many aspects (story, characters, gameplay, ambience, pacing of the game, directing of scenes) that this indie dev studio can be expected to put out even more great games in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a movie where you play two main characters attempting to jailbreak from a reality TV show - The plot is amazingly camp and there are a ton of references to other games, expertly put in. I cannot impress enough how well the writers did here, even foreshadowing was expertly applied - and I normally get very prissy about my foreshadowing. Game-play is minimal in design and that is a /good/ thing. The puzzles range from 'jump the gap' to 'wander around hoping you find the clue that was actually in front of your face the entire time' --- but even these moments were well placed to help immerse you in what else was going on. There are some mismatched subtitles, which is annoying (Abbreviations where the words are fully said, fully adding or removing words, and a few misspellings.) but the point was gotten across each time, but I hope in the future more detail is paid to the accessibility component - having the option is good, but having several noticeable errors in the subtitles mean our disabled friends get a different, less cohesive experience to a game that has a masterfully crafted story. ALL OF THAT SAID -- the studio is based in Spain so localization sometimes can be tricky, so really this gets more of a pass than what I normally would give. The soundtrack is subtle, intentional, and beautiful. Get into it. Get this game. Do it before someone can spoil you. But most importantly --
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia combines the premise of the Truman Show and the puzzle/platformer gameplay of Limbo. Unfortunately there are a couple trial-and-error sections similar to Limbo which can lead to unfair and immersion-breaking deaths. Yuri Lowenthal voices Trevor – his performance is great but too similiar to his role in Insomniac's Spider-man. The game has an incredible presentation and strong world-building that extends beyond the Truman Show comparison. I strongly recommend to those looking for a short(ish) narrative experience with minimal gameplay mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: When was the last time you played something and felt decently satisfied by the end? Few zany, high-concept plots can truly stick their landing, and this one does it exceptionally well. If you're a fan of The Truman Show and Playdead's INSIDE, there's literally no more that needs saying. Why? Because the less you know the better. Get it!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Go in blind, it's worth it.Amazing visual style, phenomenal story, A+ presentation with an unbreakable visual cohesion.  The attention to detail and polish is something that you notice.  Tons of really fun references I wish I could say without spoiling stuff.  I want to say more about why I love this game so much (easily one of the best story-driven games I've played in the past 5 years or so) but that'd require me to spoil all the super fun surprises it had.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Would never have even known about this gem if it hadn't been for 'Yahtzee' Croshaw.  Short but enjoyable game that switches between two protagonists, one that provides classic platforming-type gameplay and the other which is more 1st person puzzle solving.  Where is lacks in originality, it more than makes up for with the writing, voice acting, and a very satisfying ending.  Well worth a few bucks, particularly if you catch it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game's story, it's like The Truman Show meets The Matrix. I can't really describe the plot without getting into spoilers. This game is like an interactive movie, I was hooked the second I saw someone playing it on yt and I knew I had to play through it myself. I was able to predict what some of the plot twists would be, but man the ending was so good (if a little bittersweet). _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and it was in my top 10 or 15 most wanted before it came out. The presentation and feel of it are great. It's a really nice-looking game. And I love the way that the gameplay mechanics are all over the place. Great variety. The story and writing just didn't grab me enough to warrant all the times the game takes control out of your hands. The cutscenes are mostly reality TV-style "confessionals" where the characters talk straight to the camera, and they kill the momentum. Way too much exposition, not enough stuff happening. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The game does not have replayability but I could not stop thinking about the game while playing and after the game. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. I liked the worldbuilding, most of the dialogues and the ending. The game was mostly well paced with each chapter taking the right amount of time. _childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is one of the most compelling games I've ever played. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game so much. Fresh, smart and visually amazing. I really liked exploring, step by step, every new landmark in Arcadia as the story takes you through it in a seamless flow. The duality of the PoVs works great and generates very cool dynamics, especially when both interact (with really really awesome moments both narratively and gameplay-wise). Really happy there are still studios making games like this one. 10/10 recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing  game! It manages to merge a 2.5D platformer and a 3D adventure game into one, seamless and thrilling experience! I could not put the gamepad down, I was totally invested all the way through.I think keeping Trevor in the 2D-space, to kinda represent his life on a screen, and telling a story about accepting and even loving your mundane life, is ingenious. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game! I decided to check it out after seeing Jake Baldino review and recommend it. It  kept me glued to my seat and to my screen throughout! Game play was fantastic! A mix between side-scrolling platformer and first person action. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of the last few years. As Trevor, we have to escape from Arcadia, a TV show à la true man show. Switching between the two characters is smoothly integrated into the story and the puzzles they solve together are refreshing. The sound design and soundtrack are flawless and the colorful art style is extremely beautiful, detailed and modern with all the lighting effects.All in all, an almost perfect game in terms of story with exciting twists and turns, whereby only the performance is sometimes a little shaky.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: a short but sweet game, it is one of those games where you cant go to far into detail about the story without spoinling it but i had a blast. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I was told this was a good game with a great ending, and having now finished it I can say I was told the truth.Gameplay:You play as two characters, with very different play styles; Trevor, the side scrolling platformer, and Angela, the first person puzzler. Both are well executed. While playing as Trevor you run, jump, climb and sneak though a variety of locations, often while the other character, Angela, who you also control, helps you out. While playing as Angela, you need to preform espionage behind the scenes, collecting info, finding passwords, upgrading your security clearance, and avoiding detection. The best parts of the game were when you had to control both people at the same time, making one character jumping between buildings, while the other hacks into the different objects in the environment to help them out. Graphics:The developers decided to go for simplistic style over high pixel realism, and I think this was definitely the correct decision. It looks great, with very nicely designed levels, where you're either running through a retro-futuristic city, which often had me looking at the awesome backgrounds, or walking through modern office buildings (Which don't have as much appeal, but this is by design). I think going this way will allow the game to keep looking great for many years. Also NO ONE HAS A NOSE!Voice acting:The voice acting was stella! Yuri Lowenthal giving his talent as the main protagonist Trevor was a very pleasant surprise, going from a nerdy nobody who's completely out of his depth, to someone willing to do what is necessary escape.Krizia Bajos as your other protagonist Angela, gave another great performance as the sneaky double agent trying to help Trevor escape.In fact all the voice acting was on point, which was a necessity due to how involved the characters are in the narrative. If they didn't hit such a high mark with the acting this game couldn't have worked. Performance: My system is well above the requirements needed to run this game, but unfortunately I sill ran into some problems. There were some jitteriness when transitioning into a new scene, sometimes during cut-scenes the framerate would drop, and the game would lag. I had some audio issues, where the lines would get cut off just as the final word in a sentence was being said, along with the subtitles sometimes either not being in sync with the dialog, or showing something slightly different to what is being said. At one point I got a gameover at the same time I was moving to a different location, this caused the screen to turn black, while the game continued in the background, making me have to restart from the previous checkpoint. None of these are deal breakers, and hopefully get patched out in the near future. This is not the longest game, my first playthrough was less then seven hours, but I have seen others complete it in 4-5. But this is a case of quality over quantity and I would recommend this to anyone who likes a well old story, with appealing characters, simple but fun game-play (And maybe a bit of self reflection on our society).
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Was looking forward to this game since they announced it and it did not disappoint! The aesthetics are great, the narrative is good with a lot of twists and turns to keep you guessing, also no spoilers but i loved the ending, it fells actually realistic. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Elijah Walton's distinctive blue suit was tailored to perfection and made from the finest wool, giving it a luxurious and refined look. The blue color was not a standard navy or royal blue, but rather a unique shade that was custom-dyed to Walton's specifications. Its cut was considered both modern and classic of the time, giving it the timeless appeal that matched Walton's own creative vision. When asked about his suit during interviews, he once joked that "blue was the color of american heroes" and it helped him feel confident and powerful on and off the set.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Basically the concept is a homage to The Truman Show. The game involves switching perspectives (quite literally) between two characters, one of whom is trying to escape the reality TV show that he is trapped in and an operator offering assistance from the "real" world. However there are some great twists and the humour and character growth kept me engaged from start to finish. Gameplay is basic with fairly light puzzles and "Inside" style escape challenges. It won't set the world on fire but it's more than functional enough to carry the game and it's themes. A minor gripe is that I felt on occasion that the game didn't make the correct very clear and there were moments where it felt like there was no way to react in time unless you knew what was coming. However reloads are pretty much instant so it was a minor annoyance. Visually it's basic but it has it's charm and some really striking art design at times. It's an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Boasting captivating visuals, a compelling blend of gameplay mechanics, and a gratifying narrative, American Arcadia exceeds my expectations. With a duration of approximately 6 hours, the game strikes a great balance in avoiding being too short or dragging on. In combination with many different sceneries, the game is fun from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game will be the surprise of the year. the game has created its own style. story is deep and very strength. the atmosphere of the game also keeps you in the game. the game does not get repeat. my expectations were not high while I bought game. this game is one of the best games I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played. The movement is so incredibly fluid and the concept is incredibly interesting. I also thought the dialogue was really fun, and the voice acting was amazing. Though I've always had a thing for Yuri Lowenthall. 10/10 would recommend this game to any type of gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: HUGE improvement over the developer's last game, Call of the Sea. Fun characters, great voice acting, interesting puzzles (even if they err on too simple sometimes), cool theming, and full of style. I had a couple minors bugs here and there, and some segments dragged a bit, but ultimately, a wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Great plot and characters, overall a fantastic written game.It combines a 2D sidescroller game (more Limbo/Inside than platformer) with some First Person sections with puzzle focus. I liked a lot the setting and the conclusion. Although for what the gameplay can offers, it felt a bit too long for me. Still would recommend very much!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: #TeamTrevor! I loved the game! It's awesome to see such good games coming from my own country. The story, setting and characters are what shine the most. The game has a lot of charm and personality, and it keeps you hooked from the get-go, with some nice and unexpected twists. The voice acting is amazing too!While the gameplay might not be completely polished in some parts, it's good and it doesn't punish you for dying, making it so that the game never gets frustrating. It tries to do its own spin on puzzle platforming, which I appreciate. The mix between 2D and 3D is very well done and adds depth and fun, and helps convey the story better. 100% recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I went in with zero expectations and was surprised how good it turned out to be.I liked Limbo a lot, but since then I haven't really enjoyed the "hold  right and run" games.  This is essentially a mix of Limbo and The Truman show, but it a put together perfectly. Just when I thought it would be more of the same the game changed up the pacing. The ending is a bit plain, but I assume that is what the developer's wanted.  The voice acting is all around fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia jams out to and sweeps you along for the ride. Is the gameplay difficult? No, not really. But you didn't come here for a Dark Souls experience. Is the story the most original thing ever? No, but you didn't come here for Disco Elysium.You came here because the whole package is greater than the sum of its parts. American Arcadia drips panache like a 70s disco that knows it still has soul. As you follow along the story, the clean controls let you solve the gameplay segments and ride along the whole way. No walking simulator, the game gives you enough to do that you invest into the story it is trying to tell, while not getting so dense you take your eyes off the plot.Speaking of the plot, the game hits clean story beats and wraps up nicely. The creators clearly loved their work and it shines through in the various pieces of parody. While others justifiably compare this to the Truman Show, it rhymes rather than repeats. The skewering of Disney and modern social media fit extremely well, along with the mourning of lost potential.Buy this if you want a rollicking good time!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: "DON'T BE A FOOL!!" For real. If you want a short adventure with a great story and excellent voice performances, I highly recommend you play this game. The story will keep you guessing. Gameplay is simple, mostly puzzle solving, but they are all different and not recycled. On Steam Deck, it runs well if you drop it to 30FPS. I had about 2-3 crashes, but the auto save check points are plentiful and I didn't lose more than 5 minutes of progress each time.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: great game, it could be made into a movie / tv show (lol)artistically awesome, it kinda reminded me of Psychonauts 2 in a way that it has the same artistic freedom kind of feel. grippling story from start to finish.but my god has it been a pain technically on Steam Deck OLEDfirst of all, the in-game videos didn't work (they just showed a "no signal" kind of image), so I had to update Proton first and run it on GE-Protonsecondly, it constantly froze when loading between levels/cutscenes, so I had to restart it and replay the segment again and then it'll load properly. it was the most immersive-breaking bug and soooo annoying.1 "FATAL ERROR" crashgame-wise, the QTE / chase-scenes are sooo annoying, I lost count how many times I died just because I missed a nano-second of smth, it's too punishing on the player for no reason, and some puzzles were very unobvious.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! What an incredible game. At first I was worried this would be an unimaginative re-hash of the Truman Show (a movie/premise that I love) but that is simply not the case. While the visual style is a bit simplistic, it is unique and interesting. The writing was excellent. I found myself laughing out loud multiple times during my playthrough. I was constantly immersed in the story, wondering what was going to happen next. I won't spoil anything, but what I will say is that the game keeps you on your toes until the very end. All of the characters in this story were likeable and engaging. Action sequences were well-paced against exploration and puzzle sequences. And best of all the game doesn't overstay its welcome, as many other games in this genre tend to do nowadays.In short, American Arcadia is a diamond in the rough. The fact that so few people have played this game (only ~2000 reviews at the time of posting this) is downright criminal. Definitely give it a try, especially if you can find it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The wide range of artistic themes and concepts in this game is beyond what I expected.The game has a peculiarly great way of hooking you into the story and it is paced extremely well. Rarely was I bored or too tired from playing it. This game could very well have been a Netflix show but I'm glad it came out in the way it did. I can't spoil too much of the story but it is similar to the Truman Show if you liked it. The development team did a really good job at making sure the story takes precedence while also complimenting the already great story with really great game mechanics.Playing the game, you can sense the amount of work and love that was put into it. The dedication from the development team and the faith that was put into the team by the publisher. It is truly a work of art.If you liked Baldurs Gate 3, Alan Wake 2, It Takes 2 and A Way Out, I can assure you that you will really love this game.Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game! It gives out a vibe similar to the Trueman show and that is something I've always been curious about and wanted to experience.  The music, graphics and plot twists are so on-point and mesmerizing. Some parts of the  gameplay was a bit repeating and dull though. But overall, I still think it's a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Just gonna be straight with y'all here. I loved every moment of this game! Love the style, the mixing up of gameplay modes, the story is killer, funny and thought provoking. All around, a very fun time. Granted there are a few points were you die and have to redo a lot, because your not sure what to do or you have to interact and react quickly are rather annoying. And it's always when you are being chased so that adds to the stress, so beware of that. But that still doesn't take away from a great experience. Oh and lastly, this has one of the most satisfying endings to any game or story I've experienced in a very long time. But no spoilers from me. Buy it now! Like, right now Cowards!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game!It's very unique with its gorgeous visuals and great ambience and music, the story is intriguing and has many plot twists, and it's a fun experience overall.It never felt too hard and the puzzles weren't too complicated, I didn't have to look up any guides, only one for getting all the achievements, but this was made easier thanks to the games chapter system. You can replay any part of the game at any time thanks to a chapter select option available from the main menu, so it only took like 3 hours to get half of the achievements that I missed.Also loved the unique idea of having not only two different main characters but also having two entirely different points of view, both 1st person and 3rd person.Totally recommend this if you want a fun game with good characters and story and with many references.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Really a great atmosphere and a cool story. The gameplay works well, some action puzzles are against time which is a mechanism I don't like, but in the end everything is doable.Artistic direction is really well made, I had much fun going to the end.Please note that people craving for permanent action and disliking watching a story may not enjoy totally the game. Everybody is different, for my part I recommend. Disco powa, folks :)
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this review short and say that this game was a mixed bag for me.I adamantly enjoyed the story as it has excellent worldbuilding, pacing  between the two protagonists, intricate plot twists, and a good allegorical message about the entertainment industry as a whole. The narrative is what carries it because a combination between Disney's Tomorrowland and The Truman show makes for some interesting material I never thought I'd enjoy. However the ending was really weird as it felt like bittersweet with extra emphasis on the sweet part. It's like a happily ever after ending for everyone but overall not really in the grand scheme of it all.Now what really drags the game down for me is the gameplay itself. For the most part, it's a mix of platforming and puzzles. It feels like trial and error for some of the platforming because often they put you in hectic chase scenes and expect you to think fast on your feet or else you'll fail right there. Some of the puzzles are unintuitive and annoying, especially the last ones near the end of the game. I should also mention how the game can sometimes have choppy frames and even crash with a fatal error.Overall, I'd recommend this game for the immersive story if you can handle a few crashes.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a good cinematic platformer! None of them had managed to captivate me from start to finish, and finally this one does. I loved the story and the gameplay, although it was simplistic, worked quite well.I absolutely loved how the whole thing concludes, absolutely brilliant!I'd say the only downside would be that many of the locations traversed are unfortunately "platformer levels" instead of being actual places where people might have lived/worked, but that's okay!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a review for a game before but I was compelled to write one anyways. I've never really sat down and played a game through the entirety of its state. Yet there I was 6 HOURS in and completing the game. The Truman Show dynamic kind of show was what intrigued me to the most and I loved the alternating and adjusting game play. If you're someone who would sit down and become immersed in an indie game such as this one, so be it.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Very gripping, super enjoyable, this was truly a blast. Srsly, amazing game - I haven't had so much fun playing a game in a long time. The story, gameplay, voice acting, puzzles - everything was just sooo nice and fresh. There was a little bug here and there, but it didn't mess too much with my game.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This was a blast to play. Fun story and cool concept. Main criticisms would be that I expected the two characters mechanics to intermingle more like that sequence where you control Trevor on one side while having Angela answer questions at the same time.I found the demo pretty representative of the game so give that a go if you're on the fence.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5 / 10The story is great, the gameplay is smooth, the ending was fun.But the game is not without its flaws.First, cardinal gaming sin number 1 was commited:WHYARETHECUTSCENESUNSKIPPABLE?!?You obviously want to watch all of the cutscenes on your first run, but when you're on your second run going for the achievements you missed, you don't want to get stuck in a long blah blah conversation. I can understand locking a skip function on the first run, but once the save data on the profile is complete, for the love of loot, let me SKIP THE CUTSCENES!Second, the various devices "Kovacs" can hack into have very, VERY tiny text boxes. I often found myself toggling things just to see what they did, because I could not read the labels on them. This caused me to die. A lot. Bigger text labels would help here.Finally, the previously mentioned achievements are... vague. I see this a lot on modern games. No clues as to where an achievement is found, or what chapter it is even in. I should not have to Google external guides to unlock all of the achievements. Just give me a tiny clue - the Chapter and Scene at least.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game! The platforming is fun and the puzzles are decently challenging without making me wanna explode. The voice acting is superb and the narrative was really interesting and pretty grim, fitting for a modern era retelling of a Truman show inspired plot. The sections switching between sidescroller and first person were really fun too.HOWEVER I do have one really big issue, and it's the subtitles. They're often filled with typos and sometimes just straight up incorrect - maybe because its imported from the script and didn't account for the actors' adlibbing and alternate takes? But I genuinely found it distracting when it came up and I can imagine it'd be even more frustrating for someone who relies on subtitles to understand speech. I'm surprised it's not been patched in the months the game's been out honestlyOverall it's definitely an 8/10, really fun and stylish experience, but I'd really have liked the subtitles to have had the same attention put into them as the rest of the game :(

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, American Arcadia is vibrant and beautiful.  While the game makes it clear that the inspiration is based in the American 1970’s, from which a lot comes, the colors are not muted like in old film. The world is hyper-saturated, contrasting, and looks fantastic at all times. As people familiar with me know, I’m a big fan of this character art style, too. The 70’s is alive and well in Arcadia, most noticeably in the fashion and the interiors, but there’s a number of older iconic designs as well. Art Deco is prominent in this game as one example, although mostly out of popularity by as late as the 40’s in the real world. In some ways, these things from other generations, like Deco from the  may serve to communicate additional themes beyond just “vintage”, such as prosperity or carefree living. When creatives use symbolism to communicate these messages it adds layers to the game’s onion, and makes it a stimulating playthrough.American Arcadia is not a particularly long game; I finished in 6.3 hours, and spent another hour achievement hunting. So, it’s important that the world is strongly established in short time when you’re telling such a condensed story. This is where that aforementioned symbolism can do some incredible heavy lifting. A subtle, yet brilliant example I caught which I haven’t heard or seen yet in other reviews is that Trevor (the protagonist)’s supervisor, Romano, is wearing a Bill Lumbergh outfit from the movie Office Space. This is the only time we see Trevor interact with hardly anybody else at his work, but it immediately establishes the kind of place he works in, beyond what you could do if you dressed him up any other way and the two characters had the same conversation. This was a shrewd move by the developers!I start to roll my eyes a little though when references to other media start to come in waves that don’t  contribute anything to the player’s understanding of the world. And while at the beginning of the game I felt these were fewer, as the game carried on I felt these got a little excessive. One early example is referencing “Fiji” as the  destination. Not only are Truman Show references  abundant elsewhere in the game, but it misses the point of Fiji in the referenced material. Fiji is Truman’s destination because it’s the furthest place you can go from Seahaven.  Fiji doesn’t mean anything here though. This type of reference feels lazy and without purpose.And unfortunately, lazy is a feeling that permeated other parts of my playthrough as well. There are a number of issues related to stuttering or frame rate drops in early-game cutscenes, a frustrating doubling or overlapping of voicelines, and a  and yes I mean  number of issues with the subtitles. In fact, it almost looks like the game’s subtitles were based on an earlier version of the script. The fact the game has been out for the greater part of a year now and this hasn’t been updated yet is kind of shocking to me.And speaking of the script, I think it hasn’t gotten the criticism it warranted because the voice acting is just outstanding. Trevor, Angela, Vivian… they’re all magnificently performed and they represent some of the best voice acting I’ve experienced in a game. These performances for me are in the upper echelons along with standout titles like Firewatch, Disco Elysium, and Return of the Obra Dinn. They were that immersive and engaging, even when I felt the script was letting them down at times.American Arcadia’s gameplay is no slouch either. Out of the Blue Games clearly crafted the story to be at the forefront, and knew that this title was best served with a gameplay experience which complimented the storytelling, rather than the other way around. While there are times when the gameplay takes centerstage, and they’re not that bad (and one is even very clever and fun), most of the time the gameplay serves as just something for your fingers to do as you listen.While I think the world is visually very nice, only being able to move left and right meant that while environments stayed visually distinct, they eventually got interactively repetitive. This game is touted as “2.5D”, but I wish it were 2.5D in the sense that there were ‘lanes’ for Trevor to run along, so besides just moving left and right, there were more things to run in front of or behind. To a certain degree these already exist, but often only with interactable carts or boxes. I think some of the chase sequences could’ve felt immensely more dynamic with this approach.And this brings me to the plot, which I find fun enough and exciting… . I don’t usually struggle hard suspending my disbelief in games, but this was tested a number of times for me in American Arcadia. Dystopias are hard, what can I say? To reference another game already mentioned in this review, and one that features a standout voice actor from both games, Firewatch, I feel about the opposite as I did at the end of Firewatch. Firewatch doesn’t tie up the loose ends neatly. Firewatch’s end is messy, and to put it frank, grim. I think this was the best decision Campo Santo could’ve made because what happens in Firewatch really never  with the true problem that Henry faces.In Out of the Blue Games, I found the ending upsetting and dissatisfying. While I think my preferred ending is perhaps unrealistic, and the game’s ending is a bit more grounded in reality, I think the game as a whole is far enough away that It’s acceptable, even though the game’s themes are  real, the world isn’t. But I understand this may be a matter of preference, so I can’t say this is a clear-cut fault. I think there are themes which cut through right to the core of who we are as people, and it can be thought provoking for sections. They don’t shy away from this. If anything, they sort of throw these ideas around with a heavy hammer, but without the wit of a game like Disco Elysium, so at times it can feel unrefined. The humor as it pertains to other subjects is great though, in particular the Twitch chat parody. It’s so perfect it almost felt real, except for the lack of emote spam. Truly astounding how they made that.Anyway, as cool as some parts of American Arcadia are, and how I can comfortably say I enjoyed this game, I cannot comfortably call this a “must play” or really super standout in any way besides a vocal performance. I think anybody who enjoys a fun story would like this, too, and there may be some who really think it’s brilliant, but for me this is just a good game.
