_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The new release from Out of the Blue is a gem that explores themes such as freedom, media manipulation and invasion of privacy in a wrapper of comedy, drama and science fiction.With friendly and precise controls, balanced puzzles and action scenes in the style of 'The Fugitive', you will be gripped from start to finish.The duality of gameplay styles of the protagonists is great. And despite the weight of the legacy of 'The Truman Show', they have managed to turn around and bring freshness to a story that already belongs to popular culture.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting knowing what was happening while I was playing, but to my surprise I was wrong the game play is much like the game Inside excluding the other perspective from first person and it's really a trial and error type game but the story was really kept me engaged rooting for Trevor to finally escape but not expecting what comes next. In all it was a wonderful experience and I'd highly recommend it to others to play.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to come out for AGES. I'm so glad I didn't forget about this game, because the wait was so worth it. I have a liking for story based games and the plot has me hooked from the get-go. It's almost like watching a movie unfold. Personally, I find the puzzles could be a bit more challenging for me, but perhaps it'll improve as I play through more.It does have a few issues running on my Steam Deck though, a few of the cutscenes don't play in its entirety... I had to continue playing on my laptop because it was bugging me.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: There were several times when I let out a giggle of glee because of some new gameplay mechanic. That doesn't happen often. This game is very clever!This game is very clear in its influences: The Truman Show, The Matrix, Inside, and many others. Yet despite the clear influences the game never feels derivative or unoriginal. There are many mechanics in this game that I have never seen before. Some standouts without spoilers are an interrogation scene and a trip across a highway. The plot is also interesting and while fairly predictable, I always wanted to see what happened next. The world building is very strong.This is not a difficult game. At times, particularly toward the end, it is essentially a walking sim. But there are also parts where you will die often as you figure out the correct path. But it never feels difficult. If you are hankering for some complex, difficult puzzles, this game does not have them. But I still loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game! For anyone who loves puzzles, this is the game for you.Puzzles - challenging, there is a mix of timed and super chill puzzles, something for everyone.Voice actors and storytelling - amazing. Personally I related to the ''useless life'' of an Account Manager so it made me want to play even more. :D Love that you play with 2 characters so you will for sure find someone to relate to!Environment - very well put together, I noticed they put a lot of attention to details.Not a spoiler: Explore the environment, look into the background, you will find some pretty cool things!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia has its qualities, but no enough for me.First, the gameplay is very basic 2D platforming when playing as Trevor, mixed up with some first person exploration when playing as Angela (I think that was her name). It's nothing too exciting, but still decent.The story itself only gets interesting towards the end, while the start is pretty uninteresting. There is too much conveyed as lengthy speeches, where some character just tells you the history of Arcadia and such. Like a teacher at school. And since they talk pretty slow, it gets annoying and boring.So... Decent gameplay, where a bit too much is about pressing the thumbstick to the right (boring), combined with a decent story, told through long and boring speeches. It's all right and has its moments, but nothing I'd recommend unless you can't find anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: It's a (mostly) 2D puzzle platformer, told from two perspectives. One a side scroller (Trevor) and the other from the 1st person (Angela), with the twist here being that you control both of them during some platforming sections. In some, Angela alters the environment to help Trevor escape pursuers or assist with puzzles, in others, it's Trevor giving advice while Angela carries out some tasks. While a refreshing take, I did find some of these to be rather forced due to how slow and tedious the back and forth mechanics were in order to pad out the pace. In those circumstances, I'd much rather progress the story than be held back in such a way.Voice acting for the most part was great, though some scenes didn't quite sound fitting or lacked the emotional depth of someone in that given situation. I found Trevor's voice (Yuri Lowenthal) in particular to not quite match up to his external demeanour, though this did improve in the latter half of the game. Angela's (Krizia Bajos) was great on all accounts, and I also found Cissy Jones performed better as Delilah in Firewatch than she did here as Vivian. But I did appreciate the inclusion of the entire "Don't be a fool" song during the credits - not as bad as Trevor made it out to be ;)Visually, it's pleasant enough with its own aesthetic (even without the noses). The simplistic approach plays well into the 70s colour pallet and angled designs, but I'm not sure why some levels had to use 100% of my 3070Ti.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous graphic style and an interesting story idea, make for a compelling game. However, too many issues with the gameplay (which is often just "press forward") and the story (which has some notable inconsistencies) sour the experience a bit.This is once again a case where I wish I could have a "thumb in the middle" option for those Steam reviews, as the game definitely has a lot of good in it. But if I'm forced to choose between thumbs up or down, then it's a regrettable thumbs down.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hidden gem, in my opinion! Have never heard about this game in gaming media but it's a very solid story, with two narrators that change the game between a 2d platformer and a 3d walking sim with puzzles, solid writing and great voice work. The only negative I have is that there hasn't been enough gameplay: there are a lot of cinematic scenes, the gameplay if often rudimentary, and the game doesn't have a single interesting puzzle or platforming section. Still, it's not the point of this game, and it's best to just relax and treat it as a casual walking sim that it is. In this capacity, it's great! Thumbs up, recommended! I also liked Call of the Sea, but this one's better, and I can't wait for the studio's next move.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this. The Truman Show influences, the beautiful 70s aesthetic (from the set dressing to the title cards to the transition wipes), the clever meta-textual jokes (like the moment when someone watching the American Arcadia livestream types into the fast-flowing comment stream, "A video game based on this show would be really cool."), the sweaty breakneck pace of the chase sequences where I wanted at least one extra arm in order to control both of the main characters simultaneously... it's all just a sublimely satisfying package, and a blast to play. Cheers to all involved.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest games I have ever had the pleasure of playing!The art style is something of its own, it is so simple but so vibrant at the same time. The story is spectacular, made me feel like I knew what was going to happen when in fact, I never would have guessed... Please continue to make games as amazing as this - what a hidden gem!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Got this recommended few times so i thought i give it a try. A refreshing experience. Compact and hooking story. Nice small gameplay changes. I was all in and had to finish it in 2-3 sessions. Perfect for a gaming weekend. Thanks to the people behind it, i had so much fun playing it and nowadays it really means a lot ^^
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Another neutral rating as the game wasn't meant for me. It's a really cool and interesting "Truman Show" type story with frankly boring gameplay. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: pros: - great story- good voice acting- nice graphical/world aesthetics- some genuinely funny moments- lots of extra dialogue that can go unnoticedcons: - lips don't match up with words most of the time- gameplay gets a bit repetitive (it's hard for it not to in these types of games)- i got stuck due to a glitch at one point, but restarting fixed itoverall: highly recommend if you're looking for a fun story with a realistic ending and smart antagonists. there isn't much 'game' but it's still a lot of fun
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely phenomenal game! From the art direction to the story everything is amazing. The dual perspective game play was so clever and every scene was jam packed with so much personality and world building that gives you something new to discover on every play through. The varied game mechanics made every area so fun to play, even when I was getting stuck on the parkour (Though there are some parts where you have to be very careful in the way you jump, or you may end up falling). I loved the use of the video cameras for puzzles, it really made you feel like Trevor and Angela were working together and it was incredibly clever. I loved how realistic the characters felt, both in their writing but also in their amazing voice acting. The story is so incredibly nuanced, it's Trueman Show influences are very clear and it does an excellent job at adding onto the commentary of the movie. The characters are just bursting with personality from the way they talk and act, like Trevor's little panicked noises, whenever Angela slips into speaking Spanish or Vivian's whole corporate demeanour, to the little details in their environments like Angela's bookshelf of Table Top RPGs and the photos of her friends or Trevor's pet turtle that he loves to talk about. These characters feel like they could be real people. Angela and Trevor's friendship was so compelling and heartwarming and their banter was very funny, you can tell that they come to really care about each other.The game is absolutely gorgeous to look at, especially when playing is Trevor's perspective, the 70's aesthetic, colours and backgrounds are beautiful and I'm only sorry that my computer made some parts lower quality (This is no fault of the game). It did a wonderful job of immersing me in the world. Just the style of the game is so refreshing and unique, I loved the smooth angular edges and the simplistic faces of the characters. The documentary format of the game was also so unique! It was so clever to use in universe archival footage to explain parts of the world and how they seamlessly transitioned into the next chapter's title card, it was very nice.There is the odd glitch here and there that caused my loading to mess up or my game to crash (only once) but it didn't take away or effect my overall experience and wasn't consistent enough to really worry about.Overall I absolutely recommend this game to others! It has amazing characters and a very insightful meta narrative that is just done so exponentially well. If you liked the Trueman show or Black Mirror you will absolutely love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Not great, but better than alright. Got it on sale, and am happy with what I got. It's kind of refreshing to not have to comb everything for collectibles. Just sticks to the experience, and being able to control both characters at once was quite nice. Even though it did get me killed once when I didn't realize I was pushing the wrong stick at a very... unfortunate time. Great checkpointing though, didn't take much time to recover.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: had to quit the game almost halfway through because of the f.cking chase scenes. they are not doable after a point with k/m and no way i'll ever use a controller. the devs could have included a difficulty level for those hectic scenes, like slow it down a bit on easier level, yet they didn't bother. too bad, since the game had a lot going for it otherwise, instead the whole thing proved to be a big waste of time.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The game play was satisfying and fast, which is what is great about the game as the gameplay feels great! You will feel synced to characters as you play the game figuring out puzzles or moving along in the level.Its concept was executed perfectly; the story was intriguing, fun, and amusing encouraging me to explore the game to learn about world building and enjoy the setting. The characters and world were likable, including minor characters, and I was happy to hate the characters I disliked.The only thing that was bad was the crashes I experienced near the end, despite this Arcadia was a fun game to play through the eight hours I played, the time and money I have spent feeling worth it!I have got to recommend it to folks looking for a treat to slowly enjoy and if you are unsure that you will like it play the demo! American Arcadia is one of my favorite games of 2023!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely genius. A child of love of The Truman Show, 1984 and Brave new world in a form of a video game. It smashes the 4th wall and goes META. And goes META hard. It is beautiful looking. It has a great and an interesting story. A talented voice acting. Puzzles are kinda meh, tho. But man oh man, what a journey that was.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, but also more of an experience similar to a movie.It's a linear story-driven game with an amazing presentation. Story is exactly what it says, a mix of Truman Show and Westworld; but the pacing is great and so is the running time that it never strays from being enjoyable.One of my recent favorites. Definitely recommend if the screenshots seems interesting to you.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful mix of walking sim, Inside (more than Limbo) and very very slight puzzles and Stealth gameplay, American Arcadia does not make much sense in the plot if you stop to think about it but it is always fun to play and there is great work with the characters and general artistic design. It was a surprise when I saw it was a Spanish game.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game gets a 10/10 from me. From start to finish I couldn't put this game down and finished it in (for the most part) one sitting. Play this right nowIf you're looking for a longer review here it is:This game is truly one of a kind. It's not often that a game can truly make you think about life in a different way. The writers did an absolutely phenomenal job with this story. From the start to the very end the story is compelling and the different twists keep the story from becoming dull. Before buying any game I always make sure to read a good amount of reviews, and for this game the main criticisms that I saw were the story being boring and the puzzles being confusing or boring. When it comes to the story being boring, I have no Idea what those people are talking about. With the puzzles, I do see how some of them could be confusing as I myself had to look up how to get past 2 of the puzzles. If you're worried about that aspect of the game I'd say just make sure to look around and pay attention to the dialogue, but there's absolutely no shame in looking up how to solve any puzzles you're having trouble with. Overall, though, i don't think the puzzles are a problem. Moving on, the art style and visuals of this game are unique and have a special charm. The music and sound design is always perfect for the situation, and the game play helps move the story along well. My only criticisms of the game are that the walk speed is a little slow. I also kind of wish the whole game was in first person, like when you played as Angela, because I'd love to just explore more of the environments. I know I've written more than anyone's going to read at this point, but if anyone's still here, this game really is that good and I can't wait to see what out blue games is going to next. Anyways PLAY THIS GAME and bye.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this - but it just isn't fun. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and interesting, decent puzzles and good voice acting. Although the writing is a little weak at times and the performance could do with a lot more polish. The premise is interesting and a fresh take on the Truman Show idea. That said, the writing goes back and forth between being witty and relatable to almost patronizing as they overly explain things that could be shown instead. Some really clever puzzles here and there, though often I was left confused until I realized there was some movable object that wasn't obvious. A little highlight or button prompt would have gone a long way in making that issue less apparent.Performance is also lacking, hoping they patch out the issues with frame-drops, stuttering, and subtitles not matching spoken dialogue. Transitions between scenes were also very abrupt and often the culprit of stuttering. (3070 Ti, i7 12th gen, 32GB RAM) Overall, worth a play despite the flaws. Interested to see what else this studio goes on to produce.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10. This game is incredibly unique, it meshes genres in a way that shouldn't work, but does. It is a platformer puzzle game with a storyline very similar to the Truman Show. It also seamlessly switches between first person and platformer. The characters are very well developed and the story is engaging and smart. The puzzles are decently challenging. Even when I was frustrated with a puzzle I couldn't figure out, I still enjoyed it. The chase scenes were so fun and dynamic. The art style is simple and not realistic, but it fits the tone of the game. There are also moments when the art style/graphics change and it is absolutely stunning. A brilliant game. Honestly, I would go as far as to say my favorite of 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I do really like what the team has tried to build here, there's a lot of upside to what's on offer here but I think there are some serious drawbacks to consider. For me, ultimately I would have a hard time recommending the game as it is, but your mileage may very. If you can look past some of the serious technical hurdles, there is a gem here.Positives:- An interesting story that is well presented and voiced- Varied gameplay- An art style that is quite appealingNegatives:- The constant stuttering is an absolute deal breaker for me. Not sure if it's shader compilation issues or something else, but the game will hitch and stutter from beginning to end. It's immersion breaking and really shouldn't be happening. If you're the sort of person that doesn't notice these sort of things, or isn't bothered by them, then maybe you'll be okay.- The controls in the game aren't always as fluid as they should be. There will be many times where you know exactly what you're supposed to do, but the controls won't quite agree with you.Anyhow, it's a fun game and clearly lots of people like it, so if you don't think you'd be bothered by my negatives it could be a great game for you! Try the demo, and see how it goes.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining story with some very solid acting. Although the plot is a bit unoriginal considering the very obvious inspirations, it does still manage to fill out its own identity. Speaking of those influences, the game wears them loud and proud on its sleeve but it does work. As a story rich game with solid acting, i would recommend the experience. The part that falls short is the gameplay, specifically the puzzles. As a whole, they are pretty easy. Thats totally fine, that works perfectly with a game thats narrative and character focused. A game that mostly succeeds in this is Stray. Though it focuses more on world building, its still narrative focused with the protagonist trying to escape. The game reaches a flow state that paces the story well and when you do reach a point of failure, you often know the solution immediately or within a couple failures. In AA, the puzzles can hurt the experience. Repeating a short puzzle several tries in 10 minutes just took me out of the game. You should probably read this as a compliment to the game because the games narrative is very competent and has excellence pacing. But thats what my frustration is about; the way they impacted my enjoyment of the story and the way it unfoldedMaybe im being too critical since this isnt a bad game in the slightest but i just cant recommend it. im clearly in the minority here so you'll likely love it

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T BE A FOOL - I wasn't planning on getting American Arcadia until Christmas, but I got really ill and had a few days off work starting the day after release so I picked it up, and boy am I glad I did! This is another phenomenal game by the fine folks at Out of the Blue, I can't say much to the story without spoiling anything but just know it is 100% worth playing! The gameplay is a lot of fun, switching between the 2.5d platforming and the First Person stuff is very fluid and works incredibly well. The cherry on this already very tasty cake... The Voice Acting, every single character grabs you and makes you want to know more about them and the world they inhabit - Do yourself a favour and get this game!!!(Edit) - After Completing the game I can still wholeheartedly recommend it! An absolutely fantastic ending (that I will not spoil) and now all that's left for me is to replay it and 100% those Achievements!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine, but don't bring any expectations you have from Call of the Sea, it's a VERY different game (well duh). The quality and quantity of puzzles in this game is severely less. It's mostly a walking sim, with lots of cutscenes/dialogue that you just sit and watch. I don't mind these kinds of games if the story makes up for it, but I didn't find the story super compelling, this kind of narrative has been done before, and in much better ways imo. The interview/documentary-style framing was something new so I'll give them that.I see the vision of what they wanted to make and can appreciate how they try to immerse the player into these grand, sprawling environments. That part I did enjoy, and the art style is lovely. But the boring puzzles and gameplay where I'm just holding down D to walk (and sometime's even the space bar to jump!) in an infinite straight line just wasn't fun for me.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia weaves a witty, charming, and earnest narrative, tinged with a delightful mix of melancholy and nostalgia. The story is peppered with fun references, including a nod to the iconic Lumbergh from “Office Space”... which rather made me grin when I watched it unfold quietly, something that shows confidence in writing and vision. I won't mention any others, but they're all fun to spot.This game has something to say, about what we may have lost with social media whilst blinded in the lights of what it offers. If we allow an ever shrinking list of corporations to dictate everything we experience in our culture, what place is there for people who don't fit that mold? If we continue to allow companies to make us the product, what happens on a long enough time-line when you are not "valuable"?The characterisation is top-notch, with each character feeling fully fleshed out and engaging. The voice acting is superb, bringing the characters to life with excellent delivery of jokes and emotional moments alike.The game’s aesthetic is outstanding, 10/10 with no notes. It constantly presents new and beautiful scenes throughout the entire playtime. Utilising the power of the Unreal Engine, the game excels in its (predominantly) 2.5D style, offering stunning reflections, light beams, shafts, and various effects that make each scene a visual delight. The attention to detail in the vistas ensures you're always treated to something new and captivating.On the Steam Deck, the game performs good to great, maintaining a steady 45fps on high settings for both 2.5D and FPS sections. However, scenes that combine both perspectives can be quite laggy. Fortunately, these instances are rare and the “on rails” camera perspectives help mitigate the impact, making the lag noticeable but not game-breaking.It is not without its technical hiccups. I encountered a couple of progression crashes, particularly when transitioning to a new scene with an FMV. The end of the chapter where you board a bus is a known issue, frequently discussed among steam deck players. The out-of-the-box configuration isn’t optimal, but switching to Proton Experimental or a recent GE-Proton build resolves these problems. I had two other crashes besides, that may or may not me SD/linux related."Verified" is a good choice of recommendation here however.My total playtime was around 9 hours, though this included some repeated sections due to bugs. Without these issues, the game would likely take about 7.5 hours to complete. The scripting in the first-person sections is somewhat flawed, leading to lost progress and the need to redo significant portions. One particularly frustrating section near the end involves incrementally gaining access to different shapes. If you lose your way and backtrack, triggering a reload in an earlier level can erase all progress. Additionally, revisiting the same vent or area can cause all dialogue and progression to re-trigger, highlighting poor FPS design that forces a linear path.I'm reminded of early FPS community mods here, where FAQs were full of people suggesting which trigger someone might have missed or what they need to do if they accidentally trigger them out of sequence. It's not the core of the game so this is understandable(?) .. but feel some more thorough game testing would have picked this up. I both found it and can reproduce it, as well as not having any in-game save points or quick saving meaning there's really nothing to do but repeat - in this case - an hour of gameplay. On top of a 7=8hr game.. this is pretty annoying.This may seem like a tepid review, but I think there's something really good in this game studio and I know they're capable of more.

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is about half 2D puzzle platformer and half first-person puzzle game, and would probably take most players around 6-7 hours to complete. The first person segments play very similarly to Call of the Sea, Out of the Blue's previous game. It's definitely the case of a game that is better than the sum of it's parts. The way the story is told and the way the 2D and 3D segments play together is really cool and unique. There are a couple of really neat segments where you're doing something in both segments simultaneously. The game's ending is so strong that it helps smooth out the couple of quibbles I had with the game play and really elevated it to something special.That's the short review, below I give a bit more details and discuss the couple of nitpicks I had with the game. I quite enjoyed Call of the Sea, but thought the story was a little lackluster. American Arcadia definitely flips that on it's head. It's got a strong story hook and the writing is good throughout, and it has a fantastically executed ending. The first person puzzles are fun, without being overly challenging. The triangle and pentagon puzzles were the one exception. I'm not good at that particular puzzle type and struggled with them for a bit.The puzzle platformer sections were pretty fun, although a little janky in spots. When there isn't time pressure, the puzzles are usually fine, but during some chase segments it's almost impossible to know what you're supposed to do until it already kills you once, which occasionally makes it feel like trial and error. There were one or two chases close to the end of the game that might have been bugging out because sometimes I'd spawn and it would be literally impossible to outrun the enemy, but on another spawn I'd have a fighting chance. Overall it wasn't a huge problem, but it did occasionally become annoying.I definitely enjoyed American Arcadia and I'm pretty excited to see what else Out of the Blue comes up with.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Sort of like a light-hearted Limbo/Inside/Somerville with goofy dialogue and less player-interpreted mystery. 5-6 hours in length. I was surprised by the story's twists and enjoyed the unique way it was told through the past, present, and future of Arcadia. Not a whole lot of bad to say, except that the puzzles weren't difficult in any capacity, making the game feel more or less like a walking-simulator at times. Not an issue for me, but if puzzles are your thing with these games you'll be sorely disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: It's The Truman Show meets Logan's Run (it even has the '70s sci-fi thing going for it). It's Walt Disney's reality TV show dystopia. It's a lot of fun (and sometimes frustrating). The voice cast are amazing. There are some funny jokes. And the endless runner-style precision platforming has some really good moments, too.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely lovely, this was exactly what I hoped it would be. A comparatively short (6 to 8 hours) but very focused experience. It could be considered light in terms of actual "gameplay", but it's certainly more engaging than a plain visual novel. While I wouldn't say it did anything particularly ground-breaking I very much enjoyed how it used the medium to tell its story. The attention to detail and variety packed into this were impressive, and as opposed to so, so many games today it didn't overstay its welcome – not even when repeating a few sections to go for 100% completion. Marvellous art design and a great soundtrack round out the package. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game for people who like movies or TV shows. _childDocuments_.review: I have about two hours in this game so far, but it's so much FUN. Although the idea isn't completely original, a lot isn't these days. _childDocuments_.review: Story-heavy, thought-provoking heist side-scroller executed with clean, highly-aesthetic visuals.(+++) Great narrative with amazing pacing that cuts deeper in the problematics of the big-brother topic than its mainstream movie and TV counterparts.(+++) Nails all the correct vibes: utopian retrofuturism, thriller, heist, 70s spy era(+++) Beautifully executed low-poly art style(+++) Aesthetically pleasing; the nature of the skewed 2D gameplay was fully utilized for playful and fresh compositions of the 3D far-planes(+) Most puzzles are decent and fun(+) Well placed checkpoints (keeping occasionally frustrating gameplay at check)(--) Some running parts are done sloppily – unituitive and sometimes outright counterintuitive relying on trial-and-error approach rather than communicating the solutions properly.(--) The gameplay is a bit too simple, especially the driving sequences where the game could break out of the forward-backward 2D mechanic for at least some basic left-to-right weaving-through-traffic.(-) Story has some plot holes or was bent to allow for some additional scenes(-) Minor polish issues: animations could use more care here and there (e.g. feet-placement walking up and down the stairs); texturing is very imprecise (sharp UV artifacts in the seams of 3D models); memory leaks causing some crashes and performance issues; minor bugs requiring reloads; minor lighting bugs; only the main lights are casting shadows (even on max settings); the lipsync is way off.

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia was a surprise in many ways: Limbo-like gameplay intermixed with first-person walking simulator sections and a story that is a mix of the Truman Show with Disney empirialism and a modern social media cynicism that flows smoothly with few hiccups -- it's really good. While there were some stealth and trial-and-error sections that I didn't particularly enjoy, overall the story kept me going and had a few surprises in order. The style and overall design is spectacular and fitting, and I mean the complete package of the different gameplay elements and movies; the presentation is very polished.I don't think there is enough here for a replay (as without the elements of surprise in the story, the gameplay on its own probably cannot maintain a high interest level), but for my six hours with the playthrough, I am satisfied. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a highly enjoyable 2D platformer that skilfully incorporates puzzle elements without overwhelming players. The game uniquely splits into two playstyles: a 2D platformer where you must run or hide from enemies, solving puzzles by manipulating switches or controlling mechanical droids and platforms, and a first-person view that also includes puzzles. These puzzles are not overly complicated but can be tricky without careful consideration.The story is compelling, filled with twists and turns leading to a surprising and engaging finale. The humorous and enjoyable conversations between the two main characters and the antagonists add depth and entertainment to the narrative, showcasing the developers' dedication to storytelling.The 2D platforming can be challenging but is never overly difficult. If you fail, you restart close to where you left off, minimizing frustration. The developers have put considerable effort into the platforming mechanics, introducing original ideas that enhance the gameplay experience.Achievements in the game are varied; while some are easy to miss, the option to replay specific chapters makes it easy to go back and collect them. This replayability adds to the game's overall appeal.The game's aesthetic, a mix of 1970s and Fallout influences with a touch of "The Truman Show," works exceptionally well, creating an engaging and immersive atmosphere. This unique style, combined with solid gameplay and an intriguing story, keeps players entertained from beginning to end.In summary, American Arcadia is an outstanding game that balances challenging platforming with accessible puzzles and an engaging narrative. Its unique visual style and thoughtful design make it a must-play for fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The sidescrolling isn't as brutal as Inside and the first person puzzling isn't as complex as the studio's previous Call of the Sea but both together make for a light, breezy, and well paced 8 hour romp through the very pretty retro-future 70's.The biggest criticism I can level is that since 90% of the puzzling is for the first person parts that leaves chase sequences to carry most of the sidescrolling, book-ended by walk-and-talks, and that started to feel a bit samey by the end.  There is some variety but outside of there there's only so much you can do running/jumping to the right and most of the time one failure is all you really need to know what to do the next time.As someone that loses patience with puzzles relatively quickly when I feel I didn't get enough info I think its a compliment to say the puzzle sections never gave me much trouble at all.  You still have to find the clues or observe what's in front of you and then apply everything yourself but nothing was so difficult as to shatter the pacing or frustrate me out of the story.The story itself is relatively simple so it makes it hard to talk specifics but I will say that it is much more cynical, and delightfully so, than it might appear.  More than a lot of other games I think the ending in particular hit the exact note it needed to rather than abandoning a lot of its premise and setting.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Many thoughts come to mind regarding the balance of gameplay and linear storytelling....the game certainly gets an "A" for ambition, even if the execution is uneven at times.  It is tiresome hearing the same dialogue over and over in the more challenging parts.I rather enjoyed the novelty of switching between platforming and 1st person Myst-like puzzle solving. However, the hybrid sections where you have to activate cameras and manipulate devices can feel clunky and less than crystal clear.  Also, it would be helpful to the player to highlight movable objects in the platforming sections in addition to interactable ones.Even if you anticipate the story twist, the ending still throws some curves and makes you think.Overall, great production values despite some mismatches with voices and subtitles, and some minor quibbles with  English translations.

_childDocuments_.review: The TLDR version of this review first: This is more akin to a walking simulator and well worth it going in with that expectation AND grabbing it on a sale. With that accounted for you can consider this a thumbs up, even though the game still has a lot of problems.The game is split into 2.5D side-scrolling platforming with one character, Trevor, and first-person exploration with another, Angela. Each mode requires the player to solve regular puzzles of different sorts to progress. Trevor’s puzzles require him to manipulate the environment, sometimes with Angela hacking in to move things around.The first-person sections have Angela walking around her environment, balancing trying to help Trevor and not get caught by the organisation she works for, who are also the game’s antagonist. The puzzles here require you to find clues around the environment, such as a code to unlock a door, or sliding puzzles and the like to rearrange buttons.From the promotional material, screenshots and demo you might get the impression it’s focused mainly on the platforming, however it’s closer to an even split when all things are considered. But other than the balance between the two, the length of the side-scrolling sections is artificially inflated with the equivalent of holding ‘W’ in a walking sim. So many times you’re just holding the thumb stick right while exposition is spilled over the top. This is particularly apparent in driving sections where literally nothing happens.The flow of the game is all over the place. You’ll spend a significant time just walking while listening to dialogue, then you’re suddenly thrust into a platforming puzzle that requires precise timing of Trevor's movement and manipulation of Angela’s tool set to help him. You go from five minutes of mostly walking to suddenly having to repeat one section over and over again until you work out ‘the trick’. Additionally, control is taken away from you far too often and during odd times in the middle of walking. You’ll be frozen in place looking at where you want to be going, desperately pressing right or forward, until an exposition dump is over.It does, however, have some extremely clever and engaging presentation scattered throughout. In one section you play as Angela at her computer being interrogated by security and you have to juggle answering questions while controlling Trevor through a stealth section on your monitor. Later in the game is a quasi-dream sequence with a series of platforming puzzles in and around televisions where you’re shifting between a normal and pixelated (and sometimes inverted) view.The story is the main focus of the game and it does most of it well. The characters are likeable and engaging, although they constantly throw around the fact that Angela is Hispanic as if it's some sort of important character trait (but it is 2023 in entertainment after all). Any plot holes are easily forgiven when taking the slightly fantastical world into account and it’s easy to get swept up in Trevor's plight and development over the course of his journey.Performance is mostly fine. It has to be said that it has some minor stutters during transitions and twice the game crashed for me during the seven hour run time with a ‘Fatal Error’ message. Some other minor bugs, but nothing game breaking.Overall I cannot recommend this game for what it appears to be and for the price it’s at. In that respect I was severely disappointed. If you’re willing to accept it for what it actually is and you can grab it for a discount, then you definitely should.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a real tough one. I had to debate with myself whether or not I was going to give it a negative review. But I think your opinion of the game will change with what expectations you have. So at the end of the day, this is kind of a neutral review.The artstyle is mostly gorgeous, with some nice visuals in one level at the end, the voiceover is stellar, and there are several gameplay combinations that are clever. But the gameplay in itself is pretty lacking. It's more or less a walking simulator, and definitely not a puzzle game. The large majority of the "puzzles" are just push a thing and jump on it, and the rest is very easy. One was interesting, one was confusing. For the most part, you'll be walking right, on a rail, with no real choices.The story is not bad per say, but it's not really original either. The first "plot twist" happens not even one hour in, and is expected since 1998, but you could say this is where its inspiration comes from. The final plot twist is also expectable. There are some nice lore here and there through the adventure, but what is in focus here is the display of characters.Optimization-wise, I had some frequent lags/stutters that I never could fix. There were some weird graphical glitches. And it even crashed once.All in all, not a great game. But I can see some people liking it for what it is. It's a casual dystopian adventure game that tries some stuff. Some fails, some wins. I'm more interested to see what the studio will have to offer in their next game, because there is a lot of potential here.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's get the obvious out of the way first before starting this review in earnest. This is literally a Truman Show video game, everyone knew that going in and so the game doesn't treat it like a twist... so I won't. An everyday man's life is a lie and he's unaware that he's living in a television show with zero privacy as his life is broadcast to the world. The overall premise is exactly the same. There is no difference. With the difference in the amount of time spent telling the story, you would think it would lead to a more thorough exploration of that premise and its themes, but, if anything, this game's telling of that premise is much more hollow and one-dimensional compared to Truman Show's nuance and deep character journey. I won't spend my words trying to convince you otherwise, I'll instead be telling you of the voice acting, character moments and pacing that carried this game to its conclusion and made me play through this game in its entirety without a single stop. The gameplay is your average puzzle-platformer, the only difference is the addition of first person segments through the eyes of the secondary protagonist. NOW, I won't sugar coat this, this is the Yuri Lowenthal show and he doesn't even try to hide it. If you've played the Spider-Man games, you've heard this voice. The main character is essentially just if Tobey Maguire was trapped in the Truman Show, and Yuri using his recognisable Peter Parker voice for him as the character grows more and more unhinged over the course of this game makes his performance in this game even more ironically entertaining. Essentially imagine Spider-Man having a 4-7 hour mental breakdown and you're on the right path. The rest of the voice cast is great in there own way, though I'm not gonna lie that there isn't much depth to work with a lot of the time... however everyone's natural humor and charisma creates an extremely distinct identity for this game that isn't very easily replicated. I'm never gonna recommend this as the next masterpiece in storytelling and its not even close to being the funniest game that I've played recently, but that doesn't mean it's not entertaining enough to get a good kick out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I remember seeing this game on some 'indie game sizzle reel' in some video game conference/show. RIGHT when I saw It I knew I had to wishlist it based on aesthetic alone. Now after finally playing it I can say that my excitement was VERY well placed! Simply put; this game is a brilliant and stylish puzzle platformer, with sections of first person puzzle solving too. That is what you can expect gameplay-wise. Not only was I in love with that, but I really loved the characters as well! The voice cast was amazing and their performance lent a wealth of emotion and life to this games story. I had many parts that I laughed at, shed tears at, and just plain shouted in hype for! When in comes to indie games that try and bring a new perspective to a genre with a unique brand of storytelling, it is hard for me to recommend anything greater than American Arcadia. In a year that was awash with incredible games, I am sure to say this is one with an impact that will stick with me forever.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Truman show meets conspiracy thriller!an awesome trip with some unexpected twists and turns. The last bit of the story is a roller-coaster, but unfortunately it quite suddenly stops and the conclusion  of the story is a bit of a letdown, given what you have been working to in the past 8-10 hours. It had a really good commentary on control and the current state of social media but it doesn't follow through till the end and just ends with some jokes and you got the felling your actions didn't achieve anything in the end and the "bad guys" won or at least haven't been stopped. The full story and some of the biggest revelations are unfortunately hidden. So on your first play through you might not get the whole picture (like me) when the credits roll. Later on, while getting missing achievements some open questions got answered.Presentation: The voice acting is top notch and excellent and I love the graphic style. Gameplay: I usually don't have the patience or brain power for puzzles, but I think this is one of the first games I didn't need to look up a solution for a puzzle. Some Action sequences are kinda hard and unfair, but also manageable if you don't have the reaction time of a teenager anymore. The save-points are distributed quite fair.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: What Sherlock (the TV series) was to Sherlock Holmes' novels, American Arcadia is to the premise of The Truman Show — a man's life is part of reality TV, and he spends decades without knowing anything about it  — made interactive.Having said that, the common thread between American Arcadia and The Truman Show, is only that, the premise. Everything else — the characters, the world building, and the narrative — is entirely original.American Arcadia is a fine example of Naval's words when he said, "Movies will be Games". Play the game! Nah! Watch the game? Play it while watching, probably? Or, watch it while playing... Anyway, you'll love it, it is an amazing interactive experience! 🎶 Believe me - Don't be a fool! 🎶 And of course, please remember not to break the fourth wall!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A decent retelling of a now well-known, cult film - The Truman Show. This game brings it own interesting spin and ideas to the story. Ideas that are just enough to keep you trudging through the mind-numbingly simple gameplay. Fantastic voice performances from some big names help propel the story some more, while you push right some more.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a single-player multi-perspective puzzle platforming game that takes you through the story of Trevor Hills, an ordinary guy living his mundane life in the city of Arcadia. An extremely compelling story, the gameplay consists of 2D sidescrolling puzzle platforming and 3D puzzle sequences that for the most part works very well. A fleshed out world, interesting aesthetic, compelling narrative, and incredible voice work make this an extremely satisfying game that I think everyone should experience! There's a few moments of frustration where one might need to trial and error but for the most part, American Arcadia is a pretty easy and seamless experience.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Lemme just say: If you're a fan of Disney park history and puzzles, buy this!The story is engaging from start to finish, and just keeps getting more interesting the more you go forward. The gameplay mixes 2D and 1st person perspectives in a creative way, and integrates them well within the puzzles. And I'm not gonna spoil any of it, but the worldbuilding of this game is full of details that would make any Disney World enthusiast squeal. it's really obvious that the dev team loved the subject matter, and it shines throughout the game.I'll miss playing it for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I swear people will call any game a walking sim these days. Nothing against walking simulators themselves, it's just that there is definitely enough gameplay to call this a 2d puzzle platformer & 3d adventure game hybrid.None of the puzzling is particularly challenging, but it's there to facilitate the story, which is very very good. This game really understands what makes The Truman Show and Epcot compelling, and does a good job modernizing it.Don't be a fool. Give the Demo a try.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia took me by surprise in the best way possible. The story is gripping and exceptionally well-paced, keeping you hooked with every twist and turn. The way it switches between first-person exploration and a stunning 2.5D platformer is incredibly well-executed, adding depth and variety to the gameplay that few games achieve.The characters are unforgettable, each with a unique personality that makes them feel real and memorable. The voice acting is top-notch, breathing life into every interaction. The developers really went above and beyond to craft an engaging narrative with meaningful, impactful moments.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a "meh" button on these reviews.The story is good and the art is pretty. It's a good game. I really LOVE the message.BUT I finished it in about 8 hours (5 hours of my play time was basically idle time) and there is actually VERY little in terms of gameplay. The platforming is super simple and the puzzles can barely be called puzzles.It's a good game but I just can't say it's good value for money though. I'd expect a game that is about a tenth of a AAA in terms of length and about a hundredth of a AAA in terms of gameplay mechanics to be about a tenth or a twentieth of a AAA's price, so about $3 to $6. It's not that, even on sale...
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I really recommend this game!!! If you're looking for that meta, mind-screw, truman show esque experience... YOU'VE COME TO THE RIGHT PLACE. I adore the story and the well thought out concept and lore behind this whole game, the way it was presented and setup really makes you care, and want to continue playing to see how everyone ends up. Although the ending was a tad unsatisfying for me (i wont spoil) I still wholeheartedly loved my experience playing this game. I really think the perspective change between Trevor and Angela was so well thought out, I loved playing the 2.5D platformer style and switching the first-person 3D view instead. I also love how there are constant moving parts during the chase scenes and such where you have to control things while still controlling trevor. I think the pacing of all of that was really well done. Overall, this game took me just about 6 hours to complete and I think those 6 hours were very well spent. This game itched a scratch I didn't know I had, which is why I think I enjoyed it very much. COME ONNNNN GIVE IT A CHANCE - EVEN MY GRANDMA CAN MAKE THIS JUMP COME ON
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Long time casual gamer here who rarely finishes games, let alone wishes for games to be longer, and yet here we are. The art style is what drew me in, but this game's visuals, voice acting, and story-telling are all stunning. The game-play is slick and I don't want to spoil anything, but there were spots where the merging of story and play were so creative and seamless (not to mention endlessly gorgeous) it left me with my jaw wide open. A game like this doesn't drop very often. The story was fun and engaging (I totally chuckled and cheered out loud at parts) and they really stuck the landing--the folks who weren't happy with the end...I wonder if they watched through the credits to the end cut scene? It honestly made me a bit giddy.  I would totally play through more adventures in Arcadia (maybe from the pov of an actor?) or even watch a show based on this story. Give me more! The whole experience was just 😘
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: What's the best compliment I could give to the game? It's a worthy successor to INSIDE. It has the same cinematic style of narration, but it actually offers a more diverse range of gameplay and puzzles. It also switches up the game formula by intersecting the platforming with first person view sections.The subject matter is clearly a love letter to the Truman Show, but it puts it's own modern spin on it, that is 'more updated' with the current level of social media permeance and I thought it actually had a clever and poignant twist on it in the end. To me the ending was not disappointing at all, as much as I 'braced' for it from other reviewers' comments.Buy it, it's worth the full price. You get a solid 6-7 hours of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Funny story, I almost died trying to get this game. Anyway, American Arcadia is amazing! The humor, story, twists, characters, visuals, action, puzzles, mystery, it's perfect!My only issue is there are some small spelling and grammar mistakes, but nothing that makes it confusing!In conclusion, this game is a must for fans of story-driven titles! It also has a good price!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a great surprise, the plot takes inspiration from some very great movies and has a quite few very good thought easter eggs, it took me 6 hours to finish, but to be honest, it is not short or long, it is a good time for this type of gameThe puzzles were not too complicated, except one that to me it made not much sense (near the end) the way the game wants you to thinkThe duoprotagonist dynimic is quite good and I love their interactionsOverall it was a great experience, if you can, play this indie game, they did an amazing job
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia absolutely surprised me in a positive way! It's one of the most amazing, creative and exciting games I've played in the last two years. The gameplay has an interesting twist, the story is well thought out and excitingly told, the soundtrack is really good and the art style is absolutely appropriate. A great game - I hope the developers surprise us with the next one AND land a real hit. They absolutely deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The story, setting, gameplay mechanics, everything look sooo good, but even with a decent computer and only Medium graphics settings across the board it still ran very poorly. The game's built-in benchmark test said that I should be able to run all of the graphics settings at "Epic" quality, but if it's potatoing at Medium with literally nothing else running in the background then there's something wrong. VSync also caused bad stuttering and I had to play around with the settings before figuring out that VSync itself was the issue (I had to turn it off). Then the audio wasn't well balanced, so the dialogue would be too quiet during the gameplay and then come out BLASTING during the interview scenes. It looks like it'll be a great game, but right now it really needs some patches. Asking for a refund. Will rebuy if these issues get fixed down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this on the ending alone. Semi-spoilers here.I feel similar to how I felt about Firewatch's ending. However, Firewatch had one thing going for it: *It picked a lane*. It decided to go realistic and grounded and normal. It teased that something more interesting might be going on, but it fully committed to that truth in the end.American Arcadia does not. It has over-the-top evil, crazy schemes and lies, espionage and conspiracy, and then gives you a very corporate, realistic, boring, unsatisfying bad ending. YOU CANNOT HAVE IT BOTH WAYS! If you're going to have over-the-top evil, you need to have an ending that handles it on those terms. You cannot wimp out at the last second and decide to make the ending unsatisfying as hell.I'm sure someone will defend it as brave or innovative writing. Sacrificing any satisfaction in your ending to get it is not an even trade. It sucks because everything up to the ending was genuinely pretty great. The art style and voice acting are great. But it blew away all good will with that ending.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. The story premise was unique and interesting all the way through. The characters and voice cast were all great with Yuri giving 100% like always! The gameplay wasn't anything new but it was fun and relaxing to play through. The visuals were amazing and I enjoyed them immensely. The environments were so good looking and I wanted to spend as much time in them as I could. Kudos to the team on the vibes of the game. Nailed it!I wasn't a huge fan of the ending personally but it's definitely not enough to ruin any of the games strengths.Really looking forward to the devs next project!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game part of a humble bundle, but I would honestly recommend getting it even if it wasn't essentially on sale. The plot kept me invested and the humor was fun. It has two elements, third person plat former with a first person experience as you try to get Trevor out of a seemingly 1970's utopia. It felt like if the Disney company decided to do the Truman Show, but make it into a city with thousands of unknowing victims. The twists in the story are surprising, but never feel out of place.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I was blown away by how amazing this game was from start to finish. The game design was top notch and consistent throughout. The voice acting was top notch and the story, while comparisons to Truman Show are obvious, was unique in its own fun way. I really loved the puzzles - some were maybe too simplistic but overall I thought they were well thought out and made sense in the context of the game. Especially the one where you had to answer questions on one monitor while trying to keep an eye on the other monitor in order to control things there. This game is unlike any I have played before and I cannot wait to see what the developers do next.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game with a really pretty art style - the atmosphere is great! I really enjoyed the crossover gameplay between Trevor and Kovacs switching from a 3rd person side scroller/platformer to a 1st person walk-around/puzzle game and sometimes both at the same time. The story is really good too, reminding me both about The Trueman Show and EPCOT at Disney World, but that's about it. The gameplay is not much since it plays a lot more like an interactive movie than a video game. You end up walking a lot, both as Trevor and as Kovacs while you get told the story by dialogue between said characters. As the gameplay loop is mostly the same in the levels it can end up feeling a little repetitve, it especially gets repetitive when playing as Trevor, but it's worth it to stick it out for the story in my opinion. So if you enjoy heavy story-based games like I do you'll really like this game!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: How much money would you spend on a narrative game. A game which doesn't have all too much replayability, but is great for a playthrough. Where the gameplay is more a vehicle to move the story along and isn't a selling point for the title. American Arcadia made me ponder these questions through my playthrough and after for the review.To begin, the visual style has an interesting style. It's more stylized than other games which try and take a more realistic angle, And it helps to elicit a sort of aesthetic with Angela helping to show a more modern take with her own visuals. I don't want to overrate the visuals as I, personally, wasn't blown away fully, but I do commend the studio to do something more stylistic rather than a different direction.And as for the music, I think it's inoffensive. There are a couple of tracks which really aid in the scene playing out while others are background and forgetable. There is a song which plays during the credits along with snip-its through the game, but I didn't think it was all too memorable. Overall, fairly average. As for gameplay, as mentioned in the beginning, it's really nothing to write home about. There are light puzzles and light action sequences which involve some platforming, but neither is done to a degree which would beckon someone back in. However, it does the job well enough as a vehicle, allowing the player to feel like they're doing something to move the story along.Finally, the story. This section will be short, but I do think this is the sole reason to check the game out. It felt like the movie, The Truman Show, but there are enough changes here and there which luckily let it become it's own thing. There are missteps, though small, throughout the work, but I believe it tells a good enough story which strong characters which certainly make the journey worth going through.This is a narrative game. A game which doesn't really beckon a player to play through it multiple times. And the game is asking for $20. For the asking price, I would say hold off. However, I did have a good enough time while going through. I found Trevor, Angela, and Arcadia fascinating during my time. And, while short as my playthrough was about 5ish hours, I found myself engaged the whole time. So I would recommend picking the game up if you happen to see it on sale. And while it might not be one you'll keep coming back to, that journey you take seeing the sights is well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This written review is part of my longer video review, which you can find here: *American Arcadia* was the last game I played in 2023 and the first game I finished in 2024. I couldn't have wished for a better ending, or a better beginning: this narrative-driven story is told in such a delicious way. Dual narratives, Office-style cuts to the main characters' (and villains!) comments as they tell their story, plenty of humour, and a graphics style that prioritises clarity and colour...while also being damn stylish. I'm enamoured with the character models, whether in motion or across cutscenes; they are adorable and the lack of noses gives them such a unique identity. I love the framing even more, this idea that everything going on the screen is the visualisation of Angela and Trevor's interweaving story of escape in the face of surveillance from hell. That's right, Arcadia is the worst thing in the universe, the next step and evolution of reality television: the domed city that keeps everyone in a perpetual version of America's seventies, every single moment of every single person's life always caught on camera! And there's our lad Trevor, the most normal, ordinary person in all of Arcadia. He isn't one for drama. He's not endlessly popular, doesn't have an innate charisma (outside of being voiced by Yuri Lowenthal), and isn't a magnet for drama. Trevor's nice, he's relatable (maybe because both him and I are twenty-eight years old), and his jokes have the energy of dad-jokes-to-be, all he's missing is the kid. It's not his fault he's grown up in an atmosphere that encourages the most toxic traits imaginable. We all know what version of reality reality shows sell. As different as Arcadia is marketed as being from other corporate products meant to entertain by packaging and selling off reality, that's one of the game's messages: entertainment is driven by the same standards in this fictional version of America as it is in our own world. And those standards, I'm sorry to say, are about as glamorous as a gilded ♥♥♥♥♥. Trevor's life isn't interesting; he's no one anyone would care to watch. His life is defined by a rich interiority which doesn't have the sex appeal of a melodramatic human trash panda's existence. So when a series of incidents start to break the ordered nature of his life, that spooks him; when management calls him up and asks him to come up to the executive suit of his boss, that spooks him more; and when an unfamiliar voice tells him he's about to be made to disappear, that sets him off on a running spree that won't soon see an end. The voice in his ear? That's Angela, an activist working at Walton Media, the very corporation that's in charge of American Arcadia, the in-world show that follows the lives of all these unsuspecting people. Angela is the best, using her position as an executive assistant to try and save the life of our lad Trevor as she aids the anti-Arcadia organization Breakout. Angela's fun, chaotic, and her game sections aren't the 2.5D of Trevor's runny nonsense but puzzle solvers in the first-person, reminiscent in control (though certainly not in atmosphere) of something like Call of the Sea. Don't be a fool, play this game. It's one of the most enjoyable works of fiction in the medium I've come across, and its short length invites you to jump in without a moment's hesitation. You can be done with American Arcadia in anywhere between four and six hours; it's the length of two to three good movies, or a single Martin Scorsese Irishman! Treat yourselves -  a good time's waiting.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay.  The gameplay isn't obnoxious, the puzzles and platforming are mild and pleasant; it's practically a walking simulator.The graphics/style is okay and probably what sold it for a lot of folk though there's a fine line between charmingly lofi stylized and... basic.The writing/story is perhaps the main draw and it's pretty okay except:* The mocumentary bits are cringe* The twists are no surprise at all* The ending is unsatisfactory and just handwaves over the repercussions for one of the two main characters and almost everyone elseI think the damp squib of the ending's story and pacing probably puts this review into negative territory for me. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: What if the Truman Show didn't have... a happy ending? a soul wrenching? I dunno how to explain. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I'm going insane. The world and concept are charming and all, but I find it SO HARD to not get taken out of it by how awkward and stilted the writing and voice acting are. Just as an example, here's two killer sentences one after another: "Sadly, a heart failure deprived Elijah Walton of seeing his magnum opus finished. On June 3rd, 1963, the world of entertainment mourned the loss of the most talented mind of the 20th century." Like what's going on here. Human beings don't talk like this. Normally this wouldn't be the world's biggest issue, but when 60% of the game is listening to dialogue while you hold D/A and occasionally press Tab or Space, it can get a bit grating. Otherwise it's a fun enough game
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I was already spoiled on the plot of this game before buying it. I wasn't a huge fan, but it should have been easy to look past that, plus gameplay looked kind of cool. Well, "knowing" something and actually experiencing it are two completely different things.I don't want to give any spoilers because "story" (and I use the term loosely) is all this game has. Let's just say that there is no conclusion, nor resolution. The story takes an incredibly cynical view of the world and plays that out to completion. Maybe some people can enjoy that, but it left me feeling dirty, and not in a good way. This is the last time I'm taking Yahtzee's recommendation on a video game.But more practically, the game looks like ass. Crude way of saying it, but it does. And I don't mean the art style. That sort of "Cunist Oban: Star Racers" is perfectly fine. No it's the game's technical quality which is absolutely awful. Low-resolution textures abound, low-poly models are everywhere, the animations are abominable. This feels like a mobile phone game which got direct-ported to PC. I don't need games to melt my video card into slag, but I'd at least like for them to not look like a student project.The game also plays awful. It's split into sidescroller and first person sections. The side-scroller sections are tolerable, borrowing a little from Inside here and there. But the controls are stiff, the animations are clumsy and so, so, SO much time is spent just holding forward while the game talks at me. There are a few puzzles to do with manipulating background objects and those are... acceptable.But then there are the third-person sections. Those are absolutely intolerable. They're all puzzles with a character who moves glacially slow, and somehow with a good half-second's worth of input delay. There are puzzles in those, but to call them "primitive" would be an understatement. I genuinely don't know why those sections exist, considering they're just... not fun.The game started feeling like a slog for me about half-way through, when the bottom fell from under the core narrative. I managed to reach the end purely on the strength of the gameplay, but that too was made less interesting since there were no more puzzles past that point. Just running, and the running isn't very good. I can't in good conscience recommend this title, because the ending feels contrived, rushed and incredibly unsatisfying.Buying this game was a mistake. Hopefully, it's a mistake I'll learn from.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A very well done and worthwhile story. It's a somewhat old-hat premise, but told in a unique and mostly well put together way which really makes it an enjoyable experience.  I can't ignore the fact that it did run *far* worse than I would expect a game like this to run on my system. Sometimes dipping my frame rate to noticeably choppy levels with a 7600X + 3070TI.  Overall American Arcadia is a good story with great game design and deserves a bit more love than it's getting,
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The voice acting is fantastic and the story is good. The puzzles are not difficult and the game-play is very simple.My worst criticism of the game is how buggy it is - I faced five bugs during my play-through:The first bug made it impossible to proceed without restarting the level as I was not able to interact with an objective. The most frustrating aspect of this bug was that there was not way for me to tell whether I was just missing something or if it really was a bug. Specifically, the bug was related to when .The second bug resulted in the game crashing. I believe this occurred because I completed one section too fast. Specifically, the bug was related to when .The third bug was more pervasive. Often times I would hear multiple pieces of dialogue simultaneously. For example, if I was near a TV generating audio at the same time the level transitioned into a cut-scene, then I would hear the audio of the TV overlapping the audio of the cut-scene.The fourth bug started to occur towards the end of the game where certain controls would trigger interactions from a previous level which wasn't currently in focus. This is difficult to explain without spoiling so I'll just leave this vague for now.The fifth bug would occur sometimes when you fail a level.
