_childDocuments_.review: It's the Truman Show but different. *Played on Steam Deck LCD. Performance is alright, with some slowdown in areas where you're controlling 2 characters at once. The game recommended max settings but I found just lowering graphical settings to 'High' made the experience smoother with slightly longer battery life. I had about 8 or 9 crashes throughout the whole game, notably at the start of multiple cutscenes. Optimally, it's still best played plugged in.*   It's a simple narrative driven story with a mixture of gameplay elements. Puzzles aren't terribly difficult, but the story is enough to keep the pace going throughout the game. The time period creates a more interesting environment that draws different expectations than what you actually experience, which I'd say is a positive. I especially dig the neo-futuristic and technicolor design of the scenery.   All around I recommend the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The game's alright but honestly not worth more than $15, get it on sale if you're really interested. I like the map design, the story is nice, the puzzles are mid at best. I think this game would have benefited tremendously from being a multiple choice narrative game like Detroit: Become human, they had a solid setting and a decent story to go with it. The game-play is so minor that you could trim it and not lose anything, its a glorified walking simulator with some puzzles thrown in there. The best parts of it for me were the 3d sections as I love to look around the scenery and interact with the environment. The parts of the game where you control both protagonists at the same time are also fun although they're rare. Fortunately the ending kind of leaves the game open for a sequel so they could definitely take it in a more interesting direction and judging by the other game the studio is working on being a choice matters story heavy type game, this might definitely be a thing they look into. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I had some good laughs while playing this game and loved the humor and the scenery of the futuristic seventies. The challenges in the game are not too hard and if you fail at some point you just restart at the last checkpoint. When hunting the missed achievements after finishing the game I wished to have the option to skip the non-interactive parts. All in all a really funny and entertaining game I can recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Really great Truman Show inspired game. It mixes 2.5D Limbo/Inside style gameplay when playing as Trevor and first person view when playing as Angela, activist hacker helping him escape. Engaging storyline and characters (wonderful voice acting). There are many parts where the activist has to keep their cover while helping Trevor get out of tricky situations all the while the player controlling both, which are very fun and tense.One negative though is that I don't thing the ending is very satisfying. It should maybe have been cut shorter and to the point to leave things to the imagination like the ending of the Truman Show.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I whole-heartedly recommend this game! While the gameplay is very simple, the writing, characters and performances are stellar! The story took a twist at the end that actually caught me off guard. The vocal performances are amazing! THE Yuri Lowenthal is the main character and he is stunning! All other voice actors like Krizia Bajos and Cissy Jones give the game life as well! The game doesn't run as well as I hoped, but it wasn't enough to detract me from the experience.It is a MUST play for lovers of side scrolling platformers and a deeply interesting story!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I streamed this game for a few friends and we were laughing the whole time! Puzzles were challenging at times, but so rewarding once you got it. The art and story/world were some of the best for an indie game! I LOVED each segment, and never felt like I was bored or that things were dragging on. I loved learning of the past and now, knowing all that I know, I really want to replay the earlier chapters and see if there were any signs I missed! Good all around!! Great job to the dev team :)
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: What a disappointment. It's so frustrating to watch such a good story/universe be completely ruined by such poor gameplay mechanics. The ergonomics are so bad that it pushes the game to become a die and retry that would interrupt the suspension of disbelief so much. What a waste... I wouldn't recommend the game, or else on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).American Arcadia is a puzzle platformer with some stealth action sequences, where you play as a character that suddenly sees his life collapse around him. The story is heavily inspired by the movie  It’s very well written and full of surprises, even if you watched the movie I mentioned, and the main characters are interesting, funny and likable. The graphics are stylized and cartoonish, but colorful and vibrant or somber and dark depending on the scene. The characters have a unique look that is a bit weird at first and afterwards you get used to it. The engine used is most of the time 2,5D, but always with a lot of depth and very detailed backgrounds. There are also a few levels where you play with a second character in first person. The OST is also very well made and helps set the mood of the level, for both the more relaxed scenes and also the action scenes.The gameplay mixes a lot of elements from platforming, object manipulation, logic puzzles, stealth and exploration, but also a lot of world building where the story and past events are narrated or explained through animated videos. All these challenges are rather simple to solve so even if you’re not great at puzzle solving you just need to pay some attention and explore the available objects around you to solve the puzzles. The chase levels give you less time to think but after a few tries you’ll figure out what you have to do.     29 Achievements. Around 8 hours, spent in one run and replaying some levels for the rest of the achievements. Easy, the puzzles and the platforming aren’t very challenging. Easy, with a guide. Most of the achievements are story related or can be obtained by doing some things in a certain way or interacting with other elements, but a few of them are too random to guess how and where you can get them.You can reduce the time needed to finish the game by completing the levels while following the guide to complete everything in just one run, but the story might be spoiled. American Arcadia is a great indie platformer/puzzle game with amazing world building and a very well written story and characters. The graphics are colorful and vibrant and the gameplay is easy so you won’t get stuck too often.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Every time I thought this beautiful, inventive, disco reality tv madhouse had shown its last trick, it found a new way to surprise me, plot wise and gameplay wise. The writing and characters are so wonderfully well done, you WILL care about Trevor and Angela, you will hate Vivian, and you will be thoroughly invested and satisfied by the end. Truly one of the most pleasant surprises of the year gaming-wise, and it should be played by EVERYONE.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so this game is complicated. Voice acting, gameplay, and artstyle aesthetic is top-notch, and I loved it a lot. The puzzles and mechanics are fun to play around with and there's a lot of neat extra stuff too! The story and characters are really lovable too and there are a lot of laughs to be had.But the ending is a little...unsatisfying? I understand that may be the point but when I finished it I was left with a feeling of "...that's it? Really?" and it kinda drags the game as a whole down a lot for me. But overall it's a good experience! I'd give it an 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is brilliant, fun, at times hilarious, and full of delightful surprises from the first moment to after the credits roll. I was expecting your typical story driven side scrolling puzzler, but I got so much more. Go in with no spoilers and enjoy the incredible story, characters and music of this gorgeous little masterpiece which, while is may be light on mechanics, is just brimming with entertainment at every turn. 10/10, I wish I could forget it so I could re-experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game. The story is nice and the setting is .. well, funky (in a disco kind of way). It's not hard to play and towards the end it feels more like a movie. Some of the 2D-platforming can feel a bit tedious and/or quick-time-event-y, but all in all that was a solid two evenings of entertainment!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best stories in a game I've played in a while and definitely one of the best endings to a game I've ever played. The game aspects (platforming/puzzles) are okay, nothing very challenging (and I would say the platforming controls felt kind of sticky, at least to me), but that's the side dish, not the main course. Play it for the story, which is well worth your twenty bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so. The best way to experience this game is having an idea about The Truman show and its concept and then going in blind. I had a wander-ful time (pun intended) experiencing what was essentially a new format for an interactive movie/show/story. The humor was great, the intensity of certain moments were fantastic, Trevor was hilarious and Angela was just awesome to play as. I honestly think the studio did an amazing job on this! If you see this game and are somewhat interested in it, I urge you to play it. You get 1st person moments, 3rd person, 2nd person, you get puzzles, you get minigames, everything feels like an intense and humorous spy/escape movie and it is FANTASTIC. The Twists n turns and characters are phenomenal. For a fun story based adventure? easy 8.7/10Oh and if someone tells you this game looks "cheap"..? ♬Don't be a fool~♬
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in a Humble Bundle bundle So I did not pay the full price. I haven't finished it yet But so far it has been quite a fun game. I have been streaming it if anyone wants to watch.  The game mixes First person and side scrolling in a unique way. It seems to have pulled plot elements from a lot of popular movies like The MAtrix, The Running Man, The Truman Show and more. Check out my stream.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game was a very fun puzzle-platformer experience. If a puzzle-platformer with a good story and great style sounds like something you'd enjoy, definitely pick it up.Okay, to get the most important aspect out of the way first let me answer the question: Can you pet the cat?You can both pet AND boop the cat.Story: The story and characters are fun. Trevor is the right combination of long-suffering and sarcastic to get you invested in his story and subsequent escape. Angela was a little frustrating to me at times, but her growing friendship with Trevor and her dedication to doing what's right make you root for her. I think part of what rounds out all the characters are their flaws. The people involved feel real, which is funny given the circumstances.The message about media consumption isn't by any means unique, but it's wrapped in a really engaging narrative. If you have the love/hate relationship with the House of Mouse that is fairly common these days, the combination of nostalgia and scathing criticism the game levels at Walton Media should be engaging for you. I know it's low-hanging fruit, but I liked that "Walton" can tie both to Disney and to the Walton family - that is, the people who own and run Walmart. I'm not sure if the latter was intentional.Though it's half visuals and half story, I'm going to say that whoever came up with the sidebar towards the end of the game deserves an award; that is hilarious the whole way through. #TeamTrevor #TeamPunchVisuals: The visuals are really good. The seventies style inside the dome and the modern setting outside the dome are both really nice; realistic without being cluttered. If you like the seventies aesthetic, the game is 100% here for you. Gameplay: Transitioning between controlling Trevor and interacting with the environment directly are really smooth and I appreciate that a lot. The puzzles are reasonable, checkpoints are very good, and the platforming works well. Minor issues: If you have anti-nausea controls on, there is an instance in scene 3 where it is virtually impossible to see the answer to a puzzle.Ladders: If you're using a controller, getting onto a latter to descend doesn't always work. Best advice for this is to just use your keyboard if it's giving you issues. This hasn't changed after the hotfix.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: So, American Arcadia is a nice experience, more than a game.You control 2 characters, where the one is locked to a platform environment where you basically you are running from left to right, but also you control a second character, which is in a full 3D environment and you are solving puzzles. The puzzles are OK, there aren't hard for sure, but the point of the game isn't to make you solve hard puzzles (like Talos for example), but it want you to be part of the story that unfolds in front of these two characters.I played like 8 hours of this game, I wanted to complete all the achievements, and I enjoyed that.I will say that this game isn't for everyone, but it has some nice and uniques aspects that you will not find easily in a game.If I had to rate this game, I will go with a 7.5 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I bought a bundle this game was a part of on a whim and boy am I glad I did. I regret not paying full price for it, actually. For what it is, it's about as close to perfect as it can get. It combines what I guess you would call "cinematic platforming" a la LIMBO or Inside with a first person walking sim. You switch back and forth between the two playstyles, and they interact with each other in a cool way that serves both the mechanics and the story. The writing and worldbuilding is phenomenal, and is done in an efficient and interesting way that never brings down the moment-to-moment gameplay. The sections where you get to learn about the game's universe will have you actively looking around to make sure you didn't miss any tidbit of info. The voice acting is great, and the characters are well done and will have you rooting for them within minutes of meeting them. This dev made another game I really love called Call of the Sea. I can't wait to see what's next for them because so far they've been nothing but quality.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly one of the best written games I've played in a very long time. Despite the plot device of it all being televised, not a moment of plot or development feels trite or contrived. Plus I deeply enjoyed some of the yelling matches, they felt true to life. Especially the Spanish. Sometimes you've just got to let it out.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit on the fence about this one. A pretty little game (~7h to get through). The story is way too close to The Truman Show plus a big dose of Disney background story parallels and some sprinkles of The Matrix and The Fugitive.Nice consistent comic style. Mostly 2.5D side scroller scenes and some first person 3D scenes. Narration from a point in the future with the action taking place in flashbacks. Voice acting is good. Animations look mostly nice considering the comic style (walking on stairs not so much, but many games struggle there).Technically a really good looking comic action game with almost no player freedom rounded off with a nice start and end. I like the way characters are introduced and the switching between them is story driven and feels good. The replay value is pretty low and it's pretty short, so that's a bit sad.My suggestion to the devs would be: 1. Hire good writers and have them come up with a new unique story for the next game. 2. Put more content in.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This is great, someone finally made a game out of an idea you may have seen in the Truman Show. Unlike Truman, Trevor Hills is just one unwitting participant in this voyeuristic TV show called American Arcadia. Unfortunately for him, he's the most unpopular one and is about to get cancelled from the show. Much like the Truman Show there's someone on the outside wanting to free him from his fabricated life --in this case, Angela.In practical terms this is a puzzle platformer, 2.5D when viewed from Trevor's perspective, but in 3D when acting as Angela. As Angela you'll be hacking scissor lifts, stage lighting and other obstacles to aid Trevor's escape, but as Trevor you'll be running, climbing and jumping your way to the exit, whilst both characters solve puzzles that present themselves along the way.I really enjoyed the story, I found the characters relatable and it didn't outstay its welcome. The whole thing runs great on the Steam Deck, too. Very highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare for me to finish a single player game. One of the requirements for this is have a good and interesting story. I enjoyed this story, very much. Both protaganist characters were enjoyable to watch and get behind. I was cheering for them the whole time.There are a couple spots were I had some hicups. A video cut along with a character disappering was one of them and the model of Trevor clipped through the floor when I died. Nothing really super big or game crushing.I'd like to talk more about it, but don't want to spoil anything for anyone. What I will say is if you want a chill game to sit back and listen to a good story, this is one of those games.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Fun side scrolling, platforming, puzzle adventure game with homages to and inspired by The Truman Show. Had a couple minor issues like crashes on new chapters (unsure if this was patched) and an early issue where a screen would not display a video that was important to the plot. Finished it and had fun with it either way, played on Steam Deck
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, going back and forth between characters, 3rd person side scrolling to playing 1st person was a nice touch. Great Truman Show esque story. Just had one bug towards the end getting stuck on an object, had to seek answers on here to get past it but I did. Highly recommending this one!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: "American Arcadia" is a video game developed by Out of the Blue Games and published by Raw Fury. Set in a retro-futuristic city inspired by the 1970s, the game presents a unique blend of genres, combining elements of platforming, exploration, and puzzle-solving.The story revolves around the inhabitants of Arcadia, a seemingly perfect utopian city where life is televised 24/7. The protagonist, Trevor Hills, discovers that his life is part of a reality TV show and that not everything is as idyllic as it seems. When Trevor becomes the target of the show's producers and enforcers, he must escape the city with the help of a mysterious ally who communicates with him through an earpiece.Gameplay in "American Arcadia" alternates between two perspectives: Trevor's third-person adventure sequences where he navigates the city and solves puzzles, and the first-person sequences of his ally, who manipulates the city's systems and hacks security measures to aid Trevor's escape.The game features a strong narrative focus, immersive environments, and a mix of stealth, strategy, and action. "American Arcadia" aims to challenge players with its innovative mechanics and engaging storyline while offering a visually distinctive and nostalgic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: great game, the setting and characters are really good and keeps you wanting to find what happens next. Theres a lot of tricky puzzles, but not so bad that youll need a guide. The guy that voices Trevor is the same guy who voices Yosuke from Persona 4, so sometimes he sounds a bit like a whiny schoolboy, but maybe im just used to Yosuke. All in all, you should play this, its a real gem
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game. The format was refreshing, the story was good and the pacing was just right. It always had me guessing what was gonna happen next and most of the time it tricked me. It also contains a great message about modern society. The puzzles were simple but that was a good thing because the main hook is the story and you won't want to waste a lot of time on puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a fantastic indie game that combines two different yet cohesive gameplay styles. On top of this is a well-paced narrative that is intriguing from start to finish; there are lots of really neat nods to material that acted as inspirations for this title, and it is very clear throughout that the developers are very passionate about their work. There are minor glitches in some parts of the game but these do not impact the overall experience. One thing to note, however, is that the game is limited to a 16:9 box on a 21:9 ultrawide display (Black bars are placed on either side). despite this I would still highly recommend playing this game, I look forward to seeing what out of the blue games develops in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Good one ! If you expected an adventure, then you get one, but not a pure adventure game.  AA is a real genre mix. With Trevor you play in third person mode and have a lot of action scenes - when you play as Trevor, be prepared to run, even though, your char even tells you, he doesn't want to and stops at the most inconvenient moments... but you will have your chances, you get help from Angela. That is a great feature, when you are able to chose the CCTV option and let her put some objects out of the way or assist a bit.  Parts with Angela as your char are in first person mode and full of stealth and well designed puzzles.  I was really enjoying this game, only small minus point:  the game is unforgiving, the slightest mistake, when e.g. hiding, is punished and you are dead. Often you just die when trying to find out, where to escape to or how to avoid an obstacle. It may be made as part of the fun, as you respawn directly and won't have to replay too long passages.So, all in all, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A quick and terrible explanation of it would be if Andrew Ryan from Bioshock founded Warner.Bros. and created a 70s Trueman show, You play a low rating Ned Flanders who gets force fed a blue pill from Morpheus and yanked out of his boring little corner of Wonderland away from his turtle and forced on an adventure to the outside world. I got this game in a recent bundle, it was the only reason I got the bundle.I hadn't heard of it I just thought the art style was neat. It did not disappointI had 2 minor glitches, which I caused just messing around with the game on purpose, I lost nothing from itIts a 2.5d linear story, if that's your thing and your thinking about it, just buy it. My only gripe is I wanted more
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time.It's not overly long and is paced very well, I completed it in a single unplanned sitting of 7 hours (I'm writing this immediately after finishing it, it is 3am.)The characters are all delightfully written, with quirks and depth and some amazing voice acting to bring them to life.The sound and visual design is top notch. and the worldbuilding is very nicely and organically doled out.If you enjoy a good narrative, interesting characters, and some platforming interspersed with puzzles, I can absolutely recommend you get this.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Great story. Thoroughly enjoyed it all the way through.- The music great as it always sets the vibe for the situation/scene.- I really like the simplistic design of the characters yet they're still distinct. The 70's fashion is also a nice.- Sidescrolling adventuring is always a blast.- "Behind the scenes" and meta portions are really charming and well done.Cons:- Repeative dialogue on puzzle fails- A couple of puzzles seem vague, but it could've just been a me problem.- First person mode gives me a headache with its movements as times.- Overlapping audio if one is playing and you select something that triggers additional audio. Happened on a few occasions.Overall entertaining game that doesn't take too much of your time. Completed it in about 7 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to a deeply unsettling setting.  A world where the villains honestly don't think they're doing anything wrong and where realism beats narrative convenience or traditional story structure (but not platforming logic-poor Trevor is forced to do things that would have exhausted parkour masters and left their arms very sore in the morning) and where, when all is said and done, you still won't be entirely sure how you feel about any of it.If you're looking for a game for the gameplay, this probably isn't the best idea; my six and a half hours is after at least an hour wasted on paused while doing other things, from replaying unskippable cutscenes that I'd hoped the checkpoint would be after instead of before and a little extra exploring, and my platforming skills are poor enough that Steam always pushes RPGs or idlers at me.  If you want a story that hits harder than the AAA companies seem to know how to, consider this....unless you have a hard time with typos and subtitles that don't match the voices.  The achievement 'Intrincate Lies' is far from the only one.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cool twist on the "story heavy platformer" genre in that it's comedy focused, dialogue heavy and switches between two characters. It tells a story that's clearly inspired by The Truman Show, but does its own thing with it. The voice acting is top notch and the writing is snappy and pretty funny in spots. Some of the puzzles might take a bit to solve, but I suck at puzzle games and didn't have any real trouble with any of them. It's also a fair bit longer than typical story platformers, clocking in over 6 hours for me, but there's plenty of content to keep things interesting until the end.This is a really polished, fun, and funny experience that does something new with this genre that's often known for being grim. It's got some things to say that aren't always pleasant, but this will leave you laughing, which is a nice change.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Well written, VERY well voice acted tribute to classic puzzle-light platformers like Another World, Flashback, Aladdin (?) or whatever else you remember from your childhood.Very enjoyable through and through, excellent music, very reasonable plot development, game mechanics don't get overused, just... everything is done well. This game truly sets the standard high for platformer-puzzle-adventure-story games.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome "2nd person" game, interesting story, nice graphics, A blend between puzzler, platformer, adventure, and more. Unfortunately, I encountered at least two progression breaking bugs which forced me to restart chapters. Should be easy to fix, but a patch is still outstanding. Go devs!Update: Hotfix just came out, great work!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok game with great music. The narrative is a bit naive and the jokes are older than my grandma. Most annoying thing is that you don't know when it saves and there is no possibility to skip the cutscenes so if you quit, you might have to play some parts again and watch minutes of cutscenes all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I can count 2D, 2.5D, 3D… whatever platformer which i realy like with one hand, American Arcadia is now among them.The game is a mix of the above mentioned platformer and „puzzle“ solving 1st person walking simulator. By playing the game it makes perfect sense why it is like that. Not just because it is a game it just fits the narative flow and viewpoint.It is a story focused game where the gameplay elements mostly merge into it. Not once was i bored or distracted from other things around me during the 7h it took me to complete the game, which is allways a good sign on its own.Another easy game to recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A very well done plot that takes obvious inspiration from The Truman Show without treading on things that the film touched on. Lots of really cool foreshadowing as well as some hidden secrets that kept me interested the whole way through.Only thing that really irked me was that some of the platforming/running sections felt a little bit trial and error, and some of the puzzles were a bit obtuse.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game - well worth anyone's money. The story writing and voice acting is 👌 It's beautifully put together and has enough challenge to keep it interesting throughout. Ideally, play it through in two to three sittings and it's effectively like binge watching a box set thriller. More from this developer, please! Money very well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A few rough pacing issues plus some trial & error puzzle design aside, American Arcadia is an earnest, bitingly relatable game for anyone even slightly involved in the entertainment industry at large. If you've ever wondered how utterly stifling and hopeless it is to work in this business? This might be one of the best poeticised analogies available.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game for almost 1.5 years now. I can safely say that the game did not disappoint and that it also exceeded my expectations as well! From start to finish, I had a lot of fun. The story is really good with some twists sprinkled on top. The characters and the voice acting are really well made as well. The gameplay having both first person and 2.5D platforming sections are well implemented additions where they really made the atmoshpere of the game better. Switching perspectives was fun and engaging. The puzzle sections are neither too hard or too easy.I strongly recommend this game, it is well worth playing and you will have a fun time playing it from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my play-through.I was getting kind of bored by the end but then the game ended without overstaying its' welcome.What I liked:  - Graphical style - Predictable, but still enjoyable story.  - Some puzzles were creative - Music was niceWhat I didn't enjoy as much: - Some puzzles were tedious - Quite a few platforming sections require multiple tries by design - All themes are touched very briefly, the story is not deep - Game is sometimes stuttery even on RTX3080 (how???)Anyway, try this game game...DON'T BE A FOOL!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to spoil the story because it's really interesting and worth playing through. The game play is basically split between two characters. One character has a 2D stealth/action-adventure platforming gameplay similar to what you'd expect from the game Inside. That's actually what drew me into the game to begin with.The other character switches to a first person perspective and still revolves around puzzles. The game is heavily story based. There aren't as many chase sequences or puzzles as I was expecting but the story was really engrossing and it made me keep playing. I took me about 7 hours to 100% after going back to complete an achievement I missed and I did it all in one day which even surprised me. This is a great little indie game. American Arcadia is definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. It's a visual novel that plays while you run through platforms and solve interesting puzzles. The following point are really great:*  Design: 70's retro futuristic, reduced palette and simplified graphics. Great 3rd person body animation.*  Interface: 2.5 D side scrolling with some switches to POV full 3D.*  Plot: Interesting subject, the gullibility and relativism of today's media audiences; lot's of plot twists and interesting characters.*  Text and voice acting: This is probably the best part, along with the characterization.*  Puzzles: Difficult enough not to break the flow of the narrative. Some solutions are a bit ambiguous, but not unsurpassable.*  Platforms: Reminiscent  of Chucky Egg, Saboteur and Manic Miner for the ZX Spectrum  (this is how old I am)*  Duration and pace: the writers managed to mix enough text with the action so that you always stay engaged. With a few restarts I managed to finish the game in about 12 h.The only thing I would liked to have seen in the game was some more choice. The game plays like a railroading event: there are no possible choices except running in a specific direction and overcoming a specific puzzle. Perhaps the script could have had some branching possibilities like in Life in Strange.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T BE A ... - and try this game (it even has a demo if you are not from risky ones). The good combination of two characters' points of view - side one and first person one who help each other throughout the game. Overall, the game story is quite exciting with a few plot twists which sometimes seem illogical but the general atmosphere and gameplay is quite satisfying. You will mainly be experiencing a platformer, logic pazzles, and cast-scenes that will travel you into a deep history of the location you play in. For the fans of "Inside" and "Limbo" it will be a bright colourful journey. The graphics are stylized and good-looking, the game has its unique style and vibe. For the completionists: I recommend to track just one achievement during your walkthrough, everything else is achievable after game.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: What a great little game! I love the premise of the story and the aesthetic of Arcadia; and the idea of changing between different camera perspectives and characters is really neat. The characters (especially Trevor) are endearing and the voice acting is great. (I spent the first hour trying to figure out where I recognised Trevor's voice from, before realising he's Spider-Man in the PS4 games!)One thing I wish the game had would be some hints if you get stuck on a puzzle for a long time. There were a couple where I was banging my head aginst the wall, looked up a walkthrough on YouTube, just to find there was some action I didn't know was even an option. So the character saying "I wonder if I could do X" after a while would have been really helpful.I ran into a few bugs too, which I hope will be patched soon:- The game crashed after I did the sliding lights puzzle (but it was right after a checkpoint so I didn't lose progress)- The cutscene audio is much louder than game audio- Subtitles show in cutscenes even if you turn them off in settings- A few times after dying and respawning, I would immediately be attacked by a drone and die again (I think it would happen if I died from falling right before an Interceptor called a drone strike).I also got a little motion sick from the first person view, even with the motion sickness reduction on; I think a reticle in the middle of the screen would help with this. But I'm very sensitive to motion sickness so I doubt this will be a problem for most people.Overall I really enjoyed this game. I played it while I was sick with covid and it made my sad week at home a bit happier. Thank you to the devs and cast for all the love and care you put into this game. <3
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game. Easily my favourite of 2024 so far. It has the gameplay of "Inside", (with some very clever mechanics thrown in), a really fun and vibrant universe, and the writing of a doublefine game. It's also the kind of story that video games as an art form are uniquely capable of telling. Couldn't reccomend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing little game.  Some of the puzzles are obtuse at first, and one of the action / getaway sequences was more tedious than anything else, but that's really the only nitpicks I've got over a great experience.The story is fun, the characters are endearing, and the art direction is great.  I enjoyed it so much I actually went back to 100% the achievements for the game, which I almost never do.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a genuine 10/10 for me. I started watching someone play this game at it's release and stopped not even five minutes into the game because I was hooked. It has a similar story to The Truman Show movie but looking closely, they're very different.You are a simple man, with a simple life, working at a simple job. The disappearance of your coworker raises a red flag, but is brushed off by your coworkers. You continue your simple life, a simple life that's about to get much more complex. Like the Truman Show, your life is being broadcasted to the entire world, but you aren't alone in this scenario, as most of the people around you are also unaware of the true nature of their lives. The producers of the show have deemed you too boring to watch and have decided to KILL you. You work with Angela, someone in the outside world, to escape the prison that is your simple life.To say this game is awesome is an understatement. The game is absolutely incredible and I couldn't stop playing. The game is 2D while playing as Trevor, and first-person 3D while playing as Angela. It's one of the coolest concepts I've seen in a video game. The puzzles were so much fun and never was I frustrated. When I reached a point where I was stuck, I realized it was because I was being stupid and the game had laid it out very clearly for me. The story, the characters, the puzzles, everything about this game is peak and I enjoyed every minute of it.I got this game about a week after release and only experienced a single bug, which has since been patched. I was really impressed on how the game ran and held up and other than that one bug, I have no complaints. I'm actually redownloading the game now to play again!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Super interesting story with lots of twists and turns. Rather simplistic gameplay, made up for by the mix of platforming and first-person that does a great job of giving the perspective of the two main characters. The interspersion of videos taken from within the world is a great touch too. Overall a very unique short narrative game that's definitely worth a go if the store page has got you interested!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Yes it lacks optimization, I suspect memory leak even BUT what a ride!!!This needs to be played just for the story, decors and the way devs played with the camera :DPros:- Immersive- Storyline- Characters- Music- Decors (Fabulous!)Cons:- Lacks optimization- Too short- Would have like to get some choice system
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: 4.8/10 not awful, but not really worth the time. I highly recommend playing Inside by Playdead instead of this. The games share a lot of similar mechanics but Inside is much better in every way.The good: What little platforming elements and puzzles there are in the game are passably entertaining, and usually somewhat clever. The game is at its best when you have to multitask between the 1st person POV gameplay at the same time as the 3rd person POV gameplay. In other words, when the two main characters are working together or dealing with their own problems in parallel. The graphics and art design/aesthetics are enjoyable, but have been done better elsewhere. Music is fine but gets a little repetitive. The key voice actors themselves are solid performers (but they are given way way too much to say). The side characters are not great. If you really really just need to play a new 8 hour platformer to scratch an itch, this may do it for you... at a deep discount.The bad: The dialogue/writing is bad. So many cheesy lines, on-the-nose exposition, and unnecessary or repetitive conversations. There are so many unskippable cutscenes, and they're long! Super annoying. At least 1/3 of the total playtime is cutscenes, or a "play" segment where you're just walking with nothing to do, while listening to more dialogue. I understand the desire to do wordlbuilding & characterization, but it was not well done here. Despite tons of talking I still don't really feel like the characters or the world of Arcadia is more than 1 dimensional. The plot line itself is somewhat interesting, but it's desperately trying to be deeper than it is, all while the dialogue bashes you over the head just to make sure you got the point. Also the plot definitely drags on and gets messy & confusing at certain points. It feels like this game was made for kids in terms of game difficulty level (easy) and writing complexity (low), however the more mature corporate themes and the moderately profane dialogue makes this one tough to recommend for kids. I guess 14 year olds who haven't played many platformers yet might get a kick out of this? The core gameplay loop is very boring, a whole lot of walking slowly with only brief instances of platforming and puzzles. And you can only jump when they let you. Also the walking is super slow, did I mention that? I wish the developers the best on their next project, hopefully it can be a little more innovative than just being a "Inside but if it's The Truman Show".
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Loved playing the game, this is the first of the genre that I've played, and I had a blast! I think the story is quite captivating, I didn't quite expect the ending twist to be honest. I just loved the simple relaxed mechanics. Some of the puzzles were a bit difficult for me. Especially the animatronic one, because it required me to look at places where I wouldn't normally look to think, also the puzzle for elevating permissions after the first one, were kinda hard except the last one.Anyway, I loved this game. It has a good story, and the gameplay mechanics are fun as well - the CCTV controlling of the environment while also having control over the protagonist. The story keeps on the edge but not too much to the point where you're constantly fearful. Would recommend purchasing if you're looking for some relaxed yet excitable fun.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Picture Walt Disney's Epcot turned into a creepy mix of The Truman Show and Logan's Run by Walt's descendants and you get this fun cinematic adventure game that blends Sidecrolling and Observation/The Xperiment style assiting from the cameras gameplay, with full 3d FPS puzzle solving and a cool story. Problem is, the gameplay lacks polish and frankly, tests your patience as its too trial and errory and too "oops, you moved 1 inch out of the inteded zone because you are tired of this and want to get over it, guess what, try again from a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ checkpoint, patience is a virtue!" And that irked me someMy complaints: -There's constant scene transitions and there is shader stutter in them-Escape segments can be trial and error, and it adscribes to the "be seen and it's over" philosophy of "stealth". Even if you can jump and run, bullets will magically hit you when detected even if there was room to maneuver, there is no running after you have been spotted. This can sometimes try your patience, it could have used more polish.Overall it's about a 7.8/10. Its fun

_childDocuments_.review: - I was actually a little split on American Arcadia's visuals, with the downside being, in my view, the lack of consistency between the lush environments and the simplified character designs. They just look a bit too cartoonish and abstract while the environments are richly detailed and, if not realistic, at least a nicely stylistic interpretation of realism. I'm just glad they deigned to give most of the characters mouths unlike some other games with similarly designed characters- Those environments really steal the show at some points. Whenever the game flips to a wide angle for you to run through any large open area (busy shop-lined streets, gorgeous art deco hotel lobbies, sterile cubicle-filled open offices, etc.), the effort that went into set dressing becomes evident. These spaces feel alive with flashing lights, moving signboards, and speeding cars. Although there are occasionally NPCs milling about or chatting in groups, I would say that some of the larger places can feel a little underpopulated, unfortunately. Everything is colorful and appropriately lit, at least. The artists who worked on these set pieces should be very proud of what they pulled off on an indie budget- The game takes place in a town that's supposed to be stuck in the 1970s, so that sort of brown-on-orange-on-red 70's palette forms a thick veneer over the visual design when the action is taking place in Arcadia. If you love gaudy neo-futurism, you're in for a treat- The voice acting is, overall, pretty decent, though I did find it to be a step down overall from Out of the Blue's previous title, Call of the Sea. Norah is a tough act to follow, though, so it may only seem inferior in comparison to that game. Cissy Jones (The Absolute from BGIII, Delilah from Firewatch) gives a great performance in a villain role, but I was a little let down by uneven efforts from Yuri Lowenthal (Peter Parker from the Spider-Man games and more voice credits than I can reasonably recount here) and the rest of the cast- The OST is excellent and a great accompaniment to the game's action. For the most part, the tracks sound like theme songs and backing music to 70s TV shows and cinema. The gem is the original funk-heavy R&B number "Don't Be a Fool", with its excellent vocal work, lively brass, and groovy bassline- Although I wouldn't have known some of the backstory if I hadn't read up on the lore a little after finishing the game, the commitment to world-building (another strength these devs showed in their previous game) is impressive. American Arcadia takes place in an alternate timeline where the Berlin Wall never fell, the Eastern Bloc never got broken up, and the Soviet Union is still alive and kicking- Anyway, one of story-relevant ways that the America of American Arcadia differs from our version is a key piece of legislation that permits the construction of an utopian city known as Arcadia, courtesy of corporate lobbyists working for Elijah Walton (a thinly-veiled Walt Disney stand-in). When the plan largely fails, Walton's cronies pivot to an entertainment focus- While this bullet may seem like a spoiler, I'm not about to reveal anything that you couldn't pick up on if you read marketing blurb or watch a trailer or two. The "entertainment focus" I alluded to above is in fact a version of The Truman show, but carried out at a city-wide scale. You see, although it's 1979 within Arcadia's bubble, the game actually takes place in the modern day. Arcadia is designed to lag some 40-50 years behind the actual year, and its citizens are available to watch streaming all day, every day. Of course, leadership within the dome are all entertainment suits cosplaying as disco-era politicians, and many other Arcadians are corporate lackeys there to help keep up the illusion. Additionally, regular American citizens are able to visit undercover so they can go on a little vacation back in time. Gotta love multiple revenue streams- Unfortunately for our protagonist, a milquetoast office zombie named Trevor, things are about to undergo a little bit of a shape up. Skimming over some details to avoid spoilers (particularly the really tasty build-up to the dramatic irony getting shattered), Trevor is eventually contacted by, Angela, a freedom-fighter working for an underground organization that it doing its best to smuggle Arcadians out of Arcadia and into the real world- This conspiracy to free Trevor forms the framework for the narrative. You'll get to see a lot of the beautiful Arcadian sights and sounds while frantically trying to keep Trevor from getting captured. Occasionally, the story will follow Angela instead as she handles the nuts and bolts of the escape plan from the outside. Unlike the Truman Show, which focuses almost solely on the world inside the illusion, I appreciated how the back-and-forth in setting paired with lore-dropping plot interstitials helped to build a solid foundation for the more focal parts of the narrative- Although it's prominently an adventure game and puzzle platformer mashup, there's elements of cinematic platformers (think Flashback or Another World/Out of This World) mixed in occasionally as well. When you're sneaking around, the puzzle elements take center stage. Although I mostly didn't find these to be terribly difficult, some of them did require some planning and attention. The suitcase puzzle in particular stands out- When you're fleeing from Arcadia's security forces, however, the cinematic platformer parts come to the fore. If you're unfamiliar with games like those, be prepared to die over and over again on the same screen until you figure out the correct sequence of events you have to complete to survive. It sounds frustrating, and in truth, it can be at times. But thankfully, AA spawns you right back onto the same screen for another attempt rather than putting you back to a previous save or checkpoint- Regardless of the type of platforming you're doing, most of the time, you'll be tasked with controlling Trevor with the left stick and Angela's hacking tools with the other. This may sound like a clunky or unintuitive idea, but I can't think of a single time that it was anything other than seamless in practice- At its heart, though, the focus truly is on the story. It may be easier for some to think of American Arcadia as an adventure game with way more engaging gameplay than you're probably used to from the genre, rather than a blend of platformers- I managed to 100% the game and am therefore unlikely to replay AA anytime soon, but it's good enough to justify a revisit someday- Sure they've only released two full games with a third on the way, but I've been roundly impressed with what Out of the Blue has been putting out. This Spanish studio have proven that they're good puzzle makers, capable artists, and better writers. Call of the Sea was an excellent experience, and American Arcadia manages to showcase the progress the devs have made since they released that title. There are some parts of that game that I maybe liked a little more (the puzzles were more challenging, Norah is a better character than anyone in AA, and the slow-burn pacing was right in line with my preferences), but I think American Arcadia is the superior game at the end of the day. The writing, world-building, and cool blend of genres all represented promising steps forward. I'm excited about their upcoming title The Vigilante Diaries, but it's got two very tough acts to follow- The game was a great experience on the Steam Deck. While the aesthetic and gameplay may not suit all tastes, if you have any interest in adventure games or platformers, this is one to throw on your wishlist. If you even have a passing interest in the game, I'd heartily recommend giving it a try

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is fine and an experience that is worth the time, however I think there is a strong argument for just watching a playthrough of this game.The good: The visuals and concept are great, the story is good albeit somewhat disappointing near the conclusion. The Bad: The gameplay is very weak to the point that I would call this a walking sim, the controls are pretty shoddy allowing for unintended mistakes to happen all the time, and the intention of some scenes or sequences is pretty vague and can only be discovered by continuous trial and error. Mistakes are also punished by replaying the last sequence again, which in some cases means replaying the last minute again by holding left or right and jumping once or twice before getting to the spot where you didn't move a box quickly enough or whatever and hoping that you can do it faster this time.My recommendation: Avoid some frustration by watching a playthrough or wait for a sale to get it.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun. The story was a joy to experience from beginning to end. It's extremely well-written, and the voice acting is amazing. It has a nice style and aesthetics and a decent sound design.The gameplay is interesting. It does not have a defined loop or mechanics. Every stage has its twist that makes the 2.5D platforming sections interesting, and the 3D puzzles unique.There were some minor issues with the polish of the game. I experienced minor bugs and even a crash while playing. Some of the levels have a few design flaws, like some timed platforming sections being almost impossible to get through, or not properly highlighting interactable objects in the 3D puzzles.However, the positives of the game far outweigh the negatives. By the end of the game, I was on the edge of my computer chair, fully invested in the characters and the story.The best thing about this game is that it's worth playing. I will remember Trevor, Angela and Kovacs the turtle (best character) for a long time.P.S. If I hear "Don't be a Fool" again I'm throwing my chair out the window.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, I took a chance on it, and it was worth it. I love the story, love the twists, and I really love the ending (some endings are better left unhappy). The soundtrack alone is reason enough to buy at least the OST, wonderful tracks across the board. The mechanics are quite simple, but really versatile, so the puzzles keep up the challenge even in the end.I agree with the negative reviewers saying that the game is poorly optimized and stutters. I myself was trying to fiddle with the settings to try fix it, but after the halfway point it either fixed itself, or I was just having so much fun, I forgot about it.Overall it's a great experience, you should buy it if you like comedy and a rich story, 20 bucks is not at all a high price for this kind of production value.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: *** ABSOLUTE MASTERPIECE!! ***- Incredible amount of top quality voice acting- Very interesting storyline - think Truman show- Way cool graphics- Amazingly huge living breathing world- Some neat puzzles- Lots of running action- Play as 2 characters with 2 perspectives- The most inventive scenarios- Tons of "video" content within the gameJust buy it and try it and PLAY IT ALREADY!!!!Bottom Line: You need to play this game!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I had had a great fun discovering the world of Arcadia ! I enjoyed following the story to the point I couldn't stop the gameCharacters are cool and are well written, the story is thrilling, and the lore inspired by the city Walt Disney wanted to make is really interesting.The only thing I found the game misses is when you're playing with Trevor, beacuse I think it lacks challenge and there is a lot of moment when you just walk and do nothing else, but it isn't so bad honestly, I followed this adventure with pleasure.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I DID NOT expect the roller coaster this game put me through! It drew me in with its Truman Show meets Epcot story, continued to build out a deep and full world, and ended with an absolute killer ending. This game is so well done, and while, yes, it may have simpler game play mechanics, if you're a sucker for a good story, you should play this game YESTERDAY!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The Truman Show meets Under the Dome, and its all orchestrated by Walt Disney...s legally distinct and unrelated doppelganger.Surprisingly good game, definitely wasn't expecting to enjoy it as much as I did.I'm not usually one for side scrollers, or games with simplified artwork. But givenm that it was in a bundle through Humble, I decided to give it a go. I would've shut it down really quick if I hadn't gotten so hooked by the premise. The gameplay has a refreshing amount of variety: side scroll, first person stealth, and even some puzzles.The humour is plentiful, but not enough to take away from the story or take away from the awfulness of Trevor's situation.The character personalities are done beautifully, and I felt connected to both of them.I did have a couple points in the game where I found myself a little frustrated. Mainly with some of the chase sequences. There is almost no time to think or figure out the path, i ended up being reset about 10 times in some sections. When I did get reset, I found that a lot of the catch/game over animations dragged on, getting quite repetitive after a while.  But I was willing to stick with it because the world is so fun to discover.The subtitles have quite a few errors, which for me with pretty good hearing isn't an issue, but could be distracting for those harder of hearing.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely funny and thought provoking game. Can we ever really escape from the systems we are born into? What does it mean to be autonomous and make choices for oneself? What is the complicity of an audience in atrocities? It doesn't provide many black and white answers to any of these questions. It sort of reminds me of that Black Mirror Episode "White Bear". Not quite as grim.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: 2.5D platformer / 3D Walking simulator mix. What if there was The Truman Show, but with a scale of hundred thousand times bigger? a city full of people living in made up town where everything about everyone is recorded and broadcasted to entire globe, without their consent of course! American Arcadia! Game is one of the best of its genre. Nearly everything is competently and meticulously executed, voice acting(with Yuri Lowenthal as the protagonist, Trevor Hills), graphic design, animations all in the setting of satisfying retrofuturistic seventies aesthetic. But if I have to point out the game's weakest point, it's the gameplay. There's no challenging level or moment in the entire duration of a story, it is so strictly narrative to the point it might as well be a movie. When they said 'cinematic', they weren't exaggerating for sure. To make up for it, whether it is a cleverly written dialogue, cinematic inserted in between or a change of scenery, game tries a lot to make its otherwise boring and repetitive sections enjoyable to players. But were they effective? At least to me, yes.A must play for fans of story driven games. Don't be a fool and buy this game on the next sale if you don't have it yet. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Love the art style, voice acting and the 2D/3D mix, but once the interceptors got on my tail having to both maneuver the character and move things around with split second precision is much too difficult for a casual gamer like myself. I don't even have time to look around for the solution so I end up having to look up the solution online, and even then I can't do it. Was expecting puzzles where you have to use your head rather than fast paced keyboard gymnastics.I still recommend the game because it's well made (what I got to see of it, anyway) BUT casual it is not.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful experience!I really didn't know what to expect going into this one.  I picked it up from a humble bundle and I decided to give it a go.  First off, I adore the vibrant art style and color palette.  It is emulating the 70's and it is so crisp and clean looking.  The gameplay is largely move to the right and interact with some light puzzling elements.  The story is similar to the film "The Truman Show" but with a few twists along the way.  The story is what you are here for and the voice acting is stellar as well.  The game doesn't overstay its welcome, with around 6 hours on my play through.  I was never bored and the narrative was engaging.  My only gripe is that towards the end there are 3 puzzles that are absurdly stupid and even after looking up the solution I struggled to complete.  Without spoiling anything, I absolutely LOVED the ending.  Made the whole thing worth it.  Definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved the day and its message. Very funny dialouge, amazing characters, some really fun and tense sections just one or two puzzles I didn't enjoy but other than that an absolutely outstanding experience. Haven't had this much fun with a singleplayer game in a while altho the gameplay might not be for everyone, the story and humor alone is more than worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Was really good! Saw someone playing it on a stream, looked interesting enough and story heavy enough that I decided I wanted to try it on my own without spoilers. Puzzles were a good difficulty level, hard enough to be a challenge but easy enough to not bang your head against a wall for more than 30 minutes. Inside meets Truman Show would be a decent descriptor for this, but there's a good couple sections that screw with the formula a bit
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A game that's just like The Truman Show.I was surprised the game had very good voice acting from all the characters in the game but just a minor thing to take away is that their were a few occasions where the subtitles don't exactly match what the character says & about 1-2 swear words that was censored even though theirs quite a bit of that in the game that's not.The game was able to hold my attention from start to finish completing it in one sitting and the ending scene where they replicated a twitch chat was surprisingly accurate and funny to see some of the chat comments.There were some stuttering loading from scene to scene not sure if that would have happening if i played on my high end pc but i played this game on the steam deck and the fps was stable for the most part playing on high preset & aside from the one hard crash i got towards the end of the game, overall it was a good game to experience and would recommend for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT VERSION:Buy it NOW. It's a super fun game similar to "Inside" with a background story about media, freedom and the society of spectacle with a philosophical approach. Made by a small spanish team <3LONGER VERSION:A game made with so much LOVE and attention to detail like you don't see in this videogame industry anymore.That's the first thing that comes to my mind when I think about American Arcadia. A game that feels longer that it is (in a good way) cause it's constantly giving you game mechanics that are super fun with a bit of: platforming, puzzles, thriller, plot twists and tension. With really really good written dialogues and characters, you'll love Trevor. Incredible voice acting too.I love that the story is not "just a story" and it leaves you thinking about so many philosohpical questions, but all without being savvy or too dense.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game with great voice acting, visual style, and fun but not too challenging puzzles.  Really though it's about the story and watching the plot unfold.  Only negatives to consider are the ladders and not knowing the exact spots of the checkpoints.  But really it's worth it especially if you get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: As many people mentioned before - interesting concept and story BUT the gameplay gets a bit stale and the puzzles in Trevor sections could be more challenging, frequent and in general  be better designed. For example  robot in the hotel room - give us more of that quality!Overall decent 7/10 - play it for the story, not the challenge. Especially recommended to people new to games.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is by far one of the games I have enjoyed the most this year. It's witty, funny, and presents a plot that really lures you in with the mystery surrounding it. The characters are amazing, with incredible voiceacting and very fun personalities. The puzzles are fun, enjoyable, and at some points get hard enough to take your mind for a spin.I cannot recommend enough this game, it will give you a ride for your time. Buy it now, dont be a fool!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a neat dual-protagonist puzzle-platformer that presents like if you combined The Truman Show with Little Nightmares. The puzzles can be a bit hit or miss, but the narrative offers all sorts of twists and turns and one of the most cathartic final acts I've played in a game in quite a while.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun cinematic experience.  I won't say anything in this game surprised me, but it was really well executed.  Excellent writing, believable characters, an interesting plot, and gameplay mechanics that reinforced the story.  I love that Trevor is played as a side scroller because he's on TV.  You can tell a lot of care went into this game.  Definitely worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Very good narrative, amazing voice acting, and great visuals that will get you hooked for 7-8 hours. This game is all about delivering the story since the gameplay is linear and very simple. There are few basic puzzles to be solved, combined with several rather long platformer sections that are entertaining but become a bit repetitive after a while. Some of the these sections are interesting and refreshing as they require combining actions from the main two characters simultaneously, All in all, the game is definitely worth it for the story. Hopefully we will see more quality content from this small developer in the future. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Grabbed this after I saw it was made by the same people who did Call of the Sea and was pleasantly surprised.It was pretty much what I expected: A narrative written around a "Truman Show" like concept mixed with some 2.5D platforming and some first-person puzzles here and there. Though I do wish there were more puzzles, but I'd give it the benefit of the doubt since I actually sunk a decent amount of time into it. The story was pretty well thought out too and I found myself actually caring for what would happen next so I sort of couldn't stop playing for a couple hours, though that's probably because I enjoy story-driven games too much.Overall a pretty decent experience and while the puzzles were (in my opinion) lacking in number, the story and writing makes up for it.All I can say now is LEAVE ME THE **** ALONE!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be a fool!American Arcadia is a wonderful storytelling experience with a really creative way to explore the story with twists and turns. It would make for a great movie but also works better as a game specially towards the end.However it's not without flaws, the game sections are mostly moving to the right of the screen and all the animations are pretty slow, thankfully it's not too long of a game and the pace of the story is good because it could become boring quickly.Play this game if you like creative storytelling & adventures which could be your next favorite TV show!

_childDocuments_.review: Quality entertainment! Seriously, though, it was a fun game and I'm glad to have played it. American Arcadia is a video game version of The Truman Show but with higher set stakes, a larger scale, and significantly more platforming than Jim Carrey ever had to endure. Some of the different puzzles (especially in the middle of chases) felt tedious or poorly communicated, but everything was possible through patience or, at worst, brute force.I played this game in one sitting with breaks, and my total actual playtime (not counting leaving the game paused while taking out the trash) was around six hours. It didn't feel like the game had too much bloat, and the various set pieces and ideas were engaging. There are definitely some issues here and there, but overall I would regard this game as a solid and fun experience, reminiscent of any one of the classic indie titles one might have watched a play-through of on YouTube ten years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the best, just all around enjoyable blind plays I've had. American Arcadia is worth your time. At its core it's a mishmash of so many ideas that all work really well but are all strengthened by a fantastic story. There's quite a bit of Playdead's Inside here. A collage of first person puzzley walking sims. And interesting dynamic between two great characters that makes both of those game play elements work together in constantly creative ways. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know how this game flew under the radar so deftly, but this was one of the most unique games I've played. The shift from 2.5D to first person had a wonderful narrative function that worked so beautifully. The voice acting, writing, twists, and absolutely stellar ending made this such a joy. It's hardly a challenging game, but that really doesn't detract from the enjoyment. There are few games that would make a better movie than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely a cinematic experience with a story similar to the Truman Show. The artstyle is very beautiful and both protagonists have distinct personalities and are very much so likeable. The gameplay is a mix of a puzzle platformer and a first-person hacking game. I definitely preferred the latter sections, but the puzzle platformer had it's little tweaks to make it more interesting. And the landscapes and surroundings you went through were beautiful!Story-wise it was a mixed bag to me tbh. Some of the plottwists were a little meh, but all in all i did like the ending that the protagonists got. The soundtrack was great, too!I did get a little frustrated with some sections, especially in the chasing category, as it doesn't give you a lot of time to figure out what exactly your supposed to do and even when I knew I did have some trouble on getting the timing right. Also at one point some of the voice-over bugged, so i was still hearing a recording from another section while a different cutscene was playing. I also found some of the cutscenes a little bit disruptive. There was a lot of infodumping going on and i must say i did kind of mentally tabbed out with some of these. All in all I had a good 6-7hrs with this game. I am however honestly tempted to call this a cartoon with some gameplay elements, instead of an actual game, but I feel like that would be a little too mean. It does what it wants to do and does it well.I recommend to get this game on sale, however!

_childDocuments_.review: Watching Defunctland's video on Walt Disney's EPCOT made me buy this a day later.American Arcadia is basically a cross of Inside and Call of the Sea, mechanically, but they tell a very interesting and surprisingly grounded story. I enjoyed my time with this game quite a bit, although it took me about 7 hours to beat, including going back to get all the achievements I missed, so I'd wager there's only about 5 hours of content for the average player. Having said that, the story is ultimately the main draw of AA, and the gameplay could be considered mostly a framing device. Although I'm actually impressed how thought went even into making the two characters' gameplay parallel their origins and situations - it's really neat.About the story and setting then; I thought it was thought-provoking and entertaining. It had twists I wasn't expecting, and often made me laugh or had unexpected but welcome easter eggs that, though often seemingly small and inconsequential, really showed the depth of the developers' care and attention for their world. It was fun to play around in it.The art, design and set pieces were phenomenal. As can be expected from a game clearly inspired by Inside, the attention put towards the environments and world of American Arcadia is truly breathtaking. The music was also quite good, but not enough for me, personally, to buy the soundtrack.Having said that, there are a few small things one may wish to bear in mind if they wish to purchase American Arcadia:1: While I did really enjoy the story and ending. I can see why some people might be dissatisfied with it. (Hopefully minor spoilers ahead)  I think the crux of it can be summed up in the fact that (again, slight spoiler), 2: The game is strangely very graphically intensive - my fans kept screaming at me throughout my playtime. I never experienced any real issues (except in one room in... I think it was Scene 4? Where the screen wouldn't move - the character just got stuck as the voice line played), but with Ultra settings there was a decent amount of screen tearing and stuttering. Turning them down to High fixed these issues, except for the screen one - I couldn't get that one to go away. Expect to need lower graphics settings without a high end PC, and I wouldn't try playing on a potato.3: The puzzles are incredibly easy. Because I viewed the gameplay as essentially a medium for the story, much like in a walking simulator, I didn't find this an issue, but don't go into AA expecting complicated, brain titillating puzzles, or high-skill, high-adrenaline platforming action.-----------------------------------------------------Tl;dr: A fun game with excellent art. Plays like Inside if Inside had a clear, interesting and chillingly plausible story about a modern take on Walt Disney's EPCOT, with some simple first person Escape Room puzzles thrown in for flavour. May need a decent graphics card to run well.

_childDocuments_.review: Your whole life is a lie, and that lie is just another lie?This game is crazy. It never stops subverting your expectations of how the story should go. Its dystopian approach is also not a Cyberpunk 2077-ish approach that has been overused in the media. It's more like the 2007 Disney's movie, Meet the Robinsons. A future with a 50s or 60s setting. I can imagine a lot of 1957 Motoramas cruising around this city of Arcadia.From a gameplay perspective, it's maybe like INSIDE or Limbo but with more context and narrative, ...and maybe also more relevant. The puzzles are not that difficult. Well, there may be some tricky bits that require precise timing and speed in executing a puzzle, but other than that, it's really a game that is very enjoyable. Also, the story bring lots of conspiracy that I believe is enough to pique the curiosity of many people.A truly fun game. Love the game. Also love my guy, Yuri Lowenthal, here. Although I still find it a bit unsettling that his voice doesn't seem to fit a character with a mustache covering his mouth. Really recommend to buy this game especially while on sale.
