_childDocuments_.review: Trevor Hills is a simple man of routine. He wakes at seven AM sharp, settles into his mundane desk job, and finds his way home without attracting much attention. He's generally well-liked yet remains inconspicuous, and he wouldn't have it any other way. He calls Arcadia home: a retro-futuristic metropolis filled with gaudy, extravagant architecture, greens, blues and oranges so verdant they're almost sickly, and perfect sunshiny weather 24 hours a day, seven days a week. It's an uncannily gorgeous '70s interpretation of what the future might look like, and, incidentally, the colossal set of a city-wide reality TV show, in which each and every resident is the star; unfortunately for Trevor, however, his honest, peaceful life isn't good for business, and the showrunners are keen to have him... retired at their earliest convenience.It's a tantalising introduction that wastes no time satirically poking fun at modern reality TV culture and even the recent degradation of Disney through the cartoonishly evil and not-so-subtly-named Walton Media pulling the show's strings. The lighthearted yet astute commentary comes from a writing team that clearly knows what they're doing, and the quality is everywhere you look throughout Trevor's story; the pacing is breakneck but controlled, providing a steady cadence of new information and plot developments yet giving more critical reveals room to breathe. The storytelling is meticulous, loaded with surgical foreshadowing, taking great care not to reveal the narrative's hand too early; however, leaving just enough breadcrumbs that the eventual jaw-dropping rug pulls feel anything but cheap. The comedic timing is brilliant, through genius call-back jokes, abrupt, almost documentary-style cuts to interviews providing humourous context, and other fourth wall-breaking gags that, given the overall subject matter, are as inspired as they are hilarious.Yet among the seemingly endless narrative strengths, the character writing trumps all, particularly in the relationship between Trevor and Angela, the hacker and activist working from within Walton Media, instigating and facilitating Trevor's whirlwind extraction from his dystopian gilded cage. Their witty back and forths are the heart and soul of the seven-or-so-hour experience: Angela's playful confidence juxtaposes nicely with Trevor's understandably overwhelmed disposition, and their budding friendship feels as natural, authentic and believable as it is satisfying.Stellar voice performances round out the package, with charming and compelling renditions across the board. Special mention goes to Yuri Lowenthal's portrayal of Trevor: Lowenthal's delivery of the creeping frustration seeping through the cracks of Trevor's optimistic facade as he grapples with what his life has been and the severity of his predicament is so genuine, and the relatability and depth he breathes into the leading role while preserving the fundamental and intentional vapidity inherent to the character feels only possible through the marriage of a sharp script and an exceptional performance. Trevor is every bit a protagonist, yet I can completely buy that the man I'm watching is categorically the least interesting individual in Arcadia.While the narrative is a triumph in every sense of the word, gameplay isn't quite as honed. Taking plenty of inspiration from INSIDE and similar experiences, Trevor is controlled in a 2.5D space, but don't expect constant puzzles or precise platforming; most of your time in Arcadia will be spent holding right until the next story beat. That general lack of traditional gameplay won't be everybody's cup of tea, but it's by no means boring; the story is engaging enough on its own, and partnered with bustling backdrops and clever dialogue pacing that never leaves an empty moment, I hardly wound up missing the more action-focused set pieces at all.And for good reason, too: the occasional chase and stealth sequences as Trevor's pursuers close in on him are, unfortunately, more frustrating than anything else. With controls made up of little more than a basic run and jump, these scenes prioritise quick thinking over motor skills; however, all that approach really ends up delivering are hard-to-see jumps and dubious objectives. Angela does what she can to keep Trevor safe through the cameras, allowing you to influence some of the electronics in the environment, but with the added complexity and any hesitation resulting in failure, these sections culminate in far too much trial and error for my liking; the last thing I want holding up the adrenaline-filled climactic moments are half a dozen setbacks before I even realise what I'm supposed to be doing.However, they're not all Out of the Blue Games have up their sleeve: in the lulls of Trevor's escape, the perspective shifts to Angela, though not by simply taking control of a new character, but also the complete transformation from a 2.5D side scroller to a first-person puzzler. The brain-teasers in these scenes are delightful; they're wonderfully creative and novel, a satisfying challenge, yet more than intuitive enough to prevent any stagnation in the gripping narrative.The striking contrast between the two characters isn't just for show or the sake of it, either. I can't go into much detail without spoiling the myriad surprises; however, expect not only phenomenally inventive, one-of-a-kind gameplay sequences facilitated by the ingenious blending of genres but also remarkable storytelling techniques that make the very best of the dual perspectives.Had someone told me back in January that some bizarre amalgamation of INSIDE, Firewatch, The Truman Show and somehow Disney's Tomorrowland would end up becoming one of my favourite games of the year, I doubt I would've believed them; however, I really can't remember the last time I was this captivated by a narrative and this blown away as it reached its conclusion. Through its modern twists and inversions of its inspirations and its extraordinary blend of 2.5D platforming and first-person puzzling, American Arcadia is a tour de force, a new standard for video game storytelling, and a title I  strongly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a incredibly compelling puzzle platformer, because of it's style, story, and characters. The side-scrolling perspective and the first person perspective serve to mix up the gameplay in fun ways. I prefer the side-scrolling gameplay, and found using the CCTV to hack devices and solve puzzles really fun. The first person gameplay was okay, but the story during those bits was really good. I went back and forth on whether the puzzles were too simple, but then I'd come across one that would stump me for a while until a helpful in game nudge came along. So I think they were just about right difficulty wise. Tricky enough to make you think, but not tough enough to block progress.Hands down my favorite part of the game is the story and atmosphere. It oozes style and the tale of escaping corporate overlords and the things we do to be free to live our lives is top notch. It's relatively short, I finished it in just under 8 hours, and I don't think it will take much longer even for a very slow playthrough. I'm very satisfied with the experience, but I definitely want more. I finished it about a week ago, and I haven't stopped thinking about it since.

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a unique game, where its both a platformer and a walking sim. You play as 2 characters, Trevor, a man living in an idyllic city which turns out to be a TV show, and Angela, an activist who tries to help him escape. When you play as Trevor, the game plays like a side-scroller, usually with platforming elements. As Angela, the game plays as a first-person walking sim. Sometimes, you can control Angela during Trevor's sections, in which she can remotely interact with objects to help him progress. I love the game's low-poly artstyle, it actually fits the tone better, and makes the levels look beautiful and unique. I'd say this game has a unique method of storytelling. Other than the gameplay switch, it's told like a documentary, where sometimes when the character explains an idea or lore, instead of them monologuing we are given clips like from an old documentary or advertisement. There's also tons of pop culture references, and of course meta humour. And if you're worried about the puzzle or platforming elements, none are too hard, definitely much easier than their previous game Call of the Sea (also a good game and got referenced here), having no brain twisters or time-sensitive, precision platforming. There are chase scenes, but its quite forgiving and not difficult.My only problem with this game is that sometimes there are minor mistakes in the subtitles, but no big deal since it's usually just a few words swapped around. If you like the movie Truman Show or stories with themes like that, American Arcadia is a unique experience that you should give a try. I wish it was a bit longer and had more walking sim levels though, there seems to be an imbalance with the side-scrolling ones. But it's understandable since Trevor is basically the main character, and we can see more of the world that way.

_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really one to leave reviews often, but after finishing this game I feel compelled. American Arcadia is a master class in gaming narrative design and character development.Granted it has a couple of issues. There was some stuttering and lag during some cut scenes, the platforming is a little rough, and there were a couple of bugs during the first person sections. But those are minor quibbles in the face of one of the most unique video games to come out in years. The voice acting was top notch, the humor was genuine, and each character is memorable in all the right ways. Trevor and Angela make excellent co-protagonists, with both having their strengths, flaws and history. Not to mention a surprising attention to detail and an excellent use of environmental story telling. Plus the main narrative itself remained compelling and full of enough twists to keep most players from guessing what's going to happen until the very satisfying end.In short, Trevor and Angela's story is one worth playing through and I don't regret a single cent on the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say upfront this is not a game to play if you want dense, involved gameplay. The interactive aspects of American Arcadia are largely just there to push the story forward. Puzzles, platforming segments etc are mostly quite simple, although the scene where you  was particularly cool.It's the narrative you're here for, and it's a really good one. The story is tightly paced with some interesting twists, sprinkling in a good dose of comedy while also touching on a lot of really interesting themes. The art style is minimalistic but nails the setting, the music is fitting and the voice work is great. (Yuri Lowenthal as the guy from a bygone age made me laugh more than it should have).I played the whole thing in one sitting and I was ravenous the whole time. If you're at all interested in narrative games, this gets a big thumbs up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't watched The Truman Show play this game first then go watch it as it is heavily influenced by that Jim Carrey movie. The plot revolves around Trevor Hill, his routine, mundane life working as a data entry wage slave at the INAC Corporation in the city of Arcadia and the actions of a mysterious third party intent on interrupting and distorting his daily life. The INAC Corporation along with everything else in Arcadia is not what it seems though. Nearly each and every persons' lives are being televised to the outside world unknowingly to Acadia's residents. Ratings are down though; costs need to be cut and unfortunately for Trevor, his viewership is rock bottom making him next in line to be taken offline. Enter Angela, our outside agent responsible for tracking Trevor in the real world and a member of an anti-Arcadia liberation faction who is intent on saving Trevor from being retired permanently.What ensues is a mix of two perspectives where Trevor moves about his environments in a traditional side scrolling platformer manner while Angela controls in a first person visual novel adventure manner. Trevor's sections have him running, jumping, moving boxes, driving cars and performing stealth actions. Angela's outside help will be required for Trevor to advance and takes the form of her manipulating objects like lights and doors. Her gameplay sections though are mainly puzzle focused where she must interact with mostly computers and the environment to aid in Trevor's escape and to maintain a low profile preserving her undercover status.The 70's nostalgia and color palette are front and center in this game and hit the mark well. The music is great and the voice acting is superb. The plot, while cribbing heavily from The Truman Show, stands on its own and is  entertaining and engaging. The are a few technical hiccups like stuttering when new scenes load in and audio tracks playing over one another unintentionally. I haven't really noticed any other problems with the game. The stuttering seems to be a shader compiling issue because as I've progressed they've become considerably less frequent.As a person that has visited both the Warner Bros studios in Burbank, California and Disney's Epcot Center in Florida I find Acadia being a tongue in cheek amalgamation of the two hilarious.Needless to say, I'm enjoying this game and am about to start the 2nd to last chapter as I write this review. I'm playing this game after completing Yakuza 0 and being so tonally different from that game it makes for a great palette cleanser before I move onto the next 20+ hour long game. I believe this game is under the radar for most as it came out so late last year and didn't make it to The Game Awards (I think) but other outlets are giving it the recognition it deserves. Hopefully, word of mouth carries it to financial success.Completed the game -- The ending was great. I think they're giving Amazon / Twitch ideas on where to go next.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game and let me say, this was an incredible story. I was hooked the whole way through, because the characters are believable, the story writing was amazing, and the voice acting was sooo convincing.Add to that the playful art style to the animations... just,  If you're contemplating getting this game- do it. You won't regret it
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Inside meets "The Truman Show".A refreshing take on the 2.5D story-driven platformer formula with a parallel 1st person puzzle gameplay as we follow two characters living in two different worlds. The art direction is pretty and colorful, the voice actors are top notch, the story and dialogues are well written... It quickly made me wonder "Why on Earth isn't American Arcadia an animated movie already?!", because it's definitely enjoyable as one. The story is clever and Trevor's misadventures are so action-packed you get hooked pretty quick. It's full of humor, not too childish, not too edgy, not too dark ... and also not to hard! Which makes it perfect if you wanna enjoy a good story without having to pull your hair for it. Oh, and plays well with or without a gamepad.It was a very pleasant surprise. One of the best games i've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: IN SHORT: I would bang Trevor,.IN DEPTH: I'm having real fun with this one. A tongue-in-cheek version of INSIDE, where The Sims need to escape their horrible fate. Quite an easy puzzle-platformer game with astonishing design. Less obtuse than their previous - but equally mesmerizing- game, Out of the Blue have outdone themselves with this one. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Its...fine, but I would only really recommend it to fans of cinematic platformers. The story is fairly derivative of other works and dialogue is occasionally pretty cringe (think marvel humor, puny), but it occasionally has some excellent chase sequences where the dual protagonists really come into play.It definitely could have shaved off and hour or two, but overall it has a nice presentation, emotive voice acting, some interesting game play moments, and its a somewhat enjoyable thriller.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Best game I've played in recent memory. My steam year-end review had 200+ games and this is on the shortlist of my favorites for sure.Narrative and art direction in this game is pitch perfect.  Acting is S tier. Gameplay is solid and polished.  If you like puzzle platformers this is a must play. Game took me 7 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a short, well execute narrative in the vein of The Truman Show, seeing its protagonist, Trevor attempt to escape from the faux world of Arcadia.The 1970s aesthetic - and the beautiful colors draped over it - give much the world an interesting tone. And this is taken further by the solid display of voice acting behind a fascinating set of characters that will deliver a fun set of twists.When interacting with Trevor, the game is largely a 2.5D platformer. When interacting with Angela, it is in first person. This perspective variety would be interesting enough, there are a couple points where they manage to mix the perspective in interesting ways I can't recall seeing elsewhere off the top of my head.I can't say the gameplay itself is terribly exciting. There is the slight thrill of some chase scenes I suppose, but, it is not as though there is combat or anything, So if that's what you're looking for, this may not appeal. May even feel a bit slow or drag for you in places. But the lack of action didn't bother me much. The narrative kept me invested for what, again, was a relatively short game anyway.If you've got a few hours to kill, I think American Arcadia is well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a unique and engaging game that combines elements of adventure, puzzle-solving, and platforming. Set in a retro-futuristic world, the game stands out with its innovative mechanics and intriguing gameplay loop.The game's core mechanic revolves around controlling two characters with distinct abilities and perspectives. One character navigates the 2D side-scrolling environment, solving puzzles and overcoming obstacles, while the other operates in a 3D first-person view, providing assistance and manipulating the environment from afar. This dual-perspective gameplay requires players to think strategically and coordinate actions between the two characters to progress.American Arcadia's systems are designed to keep players engaged and challenged. Each level presents new puzzles and obstacles that require creative problem-solving and precise timing. The game gradually introduces new mechanics and tools, ensuring that players constantly face fresh challenges and must adapt their strategies. The dynamic interaction between the two characters adds depth to the gameplay, making each puzzle a rewarding experience.The gameplay loop of American Arcadia is well-crafted, offering a mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and platforming. Players are encouraged to explore the environment, uncover hidden secrets, and piece together the story behind the world of Arcadia. The game balances its challenging puzzles with moments of discovery and narrative development, keeping players invested in the unfolding story.American Arcadia delivers an engaging and satisfying experience with its inventive mechanics, well-designed systems, and captivating gameplay loop. Players looking for a game that challenges their intellect and offers a unique blend of genres will find American Arcadia a delightful journey.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I'm absolutely blown away by the story, lore, and world-building of this game. I feel like i was just part of an action movie. I loved every minute of it, well maybe not some of the stealth missions, lol as they could be tricky,, but the gameplay stayed fresh through out and the story still managed a few surprises at the end. The VA is really great, and sells the characters not just the main ones.  The art style is different, but effective at conveying that 70s feel. This is like if walt disney, Orwell, and truman show had a baby...and well no spoilers. Great game happy to support this dev!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, almost sublime game. American Arcadia lays down a wonderful narrative about how over-saturated the concept of "Watch someone else's life" has really become. To an absurd degree, yes, but it still stands while also taking potshots at one of the most gigantic corporations currently in reality (without ever really saying, but play the game and you'll know immediately who they based Walton Media after). It's funny, witty, the characters are likable and relatable without being overbearing, and the controls are tight in both styles of gameplay.What stops this game from being "totally sublime" instead of "almost sublime" is that there are some rather glaring mistakes in the subtitles; they either have blatant misspellings or don't match what is actually being said. It kept slightly fracturing my immersion into the game and, let's be honest, should have been caught on Q&A. It's not hard, guys. Also, the game does suffer from lack of direction at times, being very vague about what it wants you to do for either chase or puzzle sequences. Yes, they can be figured out, but at those times, I felt more annoyed than accomplished. Less "Hell yeah!" and more "Ugh, FINALLY."Also, this game is in a big damn hurry. It's only 6-7 hours long and moves very quickly, very very rapidly telling its story. While it's well made, I don't know that it's worth a full $20 pricetag for such a short game. I know that someone might compare this to Portal and how Yahztee Croshaw once said he'd take short-but-perfect over long-and-pretty, but in this instance I do believe that if you're asking that price, you need more than a game that can be beaten in an afternoon. I wouldn't buy full price because of that. $15, probably would be a more accurate price-to-enjoyment feel than $20. Still, even with hairline fractures, this game's damned good and a lovely Take That at how companies are monetizing what should be left well enough alone: our privacy. Might be worth a think, yeah?
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This is just... boring for me personally, maybe it's for you, but definitely not for me, I find myself simply want to finish the game just to be done with it. - There is no gameplay, you just walk / run in a direction and occasionally there is a little puzzle for you to solve, but all of the puzzle is just the basic run-of-the-mill puzzle you see in every other games. 2.5D and 3D part of the game is the same, just with different perspective. You can basically make this into a short film and there would be no difference at all. There are alternative paths you can go in this game, but they do absolutely nothing in the grand scheme of the story. So basically you are not playing the game, you are just watching the game while pressing buttons. - It's essentially "The truman show" in game format, but I find the overall story to be average and a bit predictable, and the ending is extremely unsatisfying. - The artstyle of the game look generally beautiful, but the optimization on pc is horrible, my pc run super hot while playing the game, while nowadays AAA games didn't even run that hot, it just didn't make sense for it to run this hot, with it being neither CPU-intensive nor GPU-intensive with the gameplay / graphics, probably problems with CPU / GPU utilization?Overall I am very disappointed with this purchase, I would refund if I have the chance unfortunately
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Your going to get exactly what you expect getting American Arcadia. It's what  I want from a movie video game. it's a amazing linear story line, but all through out "I" am the a character in it and controlling it. _childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Great game altogether! Yes, there were some bugs but all in all the story, the voice acting and the gameplay were very good! i really enjoyed my playthrough and will go back to get all achievements! if you can buy it now, do it, it's worth it! if not, on sale you will definitely get a great deal - really hidden gem of a game to finish the year!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I haven't played a game in a while where I wanted to keep playing until it was finished but this is one of those games that I sat down for an entire day to finish because I was invested. This is definitely more of a story game than a game with gameplay but the story at every turn had a twist for either gameplay or story elements. I really love every part that I went through even if I struggled with some of the simple puzzles or quick time events with running and the camera. For the ending I wish it was a little more fleshed out to have some gameplay wrap ups instead of just the decision and what happened after. I think it's fine for what it is but I expected a little more for that part specificallyAll the level design has so much detail into either the secrets it hides or the illusion  it keeps to hide the fact that something is wrong. I imagined the inspiration was things like A Clockwork Orange, Truman Show, Disney Company (Theme Parks and History)The main reason when I saw this game a long time ago at a games showcase was the switching between 2D side-scroller and 3D first person which is extremely awesome for the reasons of switching up gameplay and keeping the two characters extremely separate by camera view from the players point of view, really smart idea honestly I even love how low poly the charterer designs were, really added to the style of the game and probably made it easier to work with to focus on bigger elements with that includedI would play this for so many reasons, a good mystery, a good story, or even casual gameplay with some thinking involved sometimes. Even the dialogue from all the characters felt really polished Thank you for an enjoyable game experience!!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard trying to review this without spoiling too much, but I think at the very least you can pretty easily immerse yourself into the art-style and amazing world building that American Arcadia provides. Either way, its better for you to go into it as blind as you can. Don't be a fool, just play it.vvvv  vvvv
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is set in the future-retro Walt Disney-inspired city of Arcadia, whose citizens are almost all unwitting participants in a capitalistic dystopian Truman Show-style reality show, and follows two protagonists: Trevor, an Arcadian citizen with abysmally low ratings and is about to be terminated and must platform his way out, and Angela, an outsider enabling his escape from Arcadia, solving puzzles to help him. These two characters, along with American Arcadia's villains, are well voiced and rather charming. The gameplay is alright, nothing mind-blowing, while the story is just a little above average but builds up to a very strong climax. I found American Arcadia to be a decent enough story driven puzzle platformer.

_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game not too long ago so it's still fresh in my mind. Great story telling, good platforming with some twist here and there. Got a lot of freshness to the genre ala Limbo/Inside and else.Enjoyed the whole premise and didn't feel like I was playing a game but living an adventure, which is what everybody should look for when playing a story-driven video game.Definitely recommend it for any fan of the genre.I played the first game of the studio and I wasn't very convinced, it was enjoyable but frustrating at times. This one is so much more fledged out and careful in its puzzles, I never felt that it was too tedious or irritating.Note: Played entirely on the SD OLED and the game looks gorgeous, a bit laggy on high but manageable. However, it crashed almost every time after about 1 hour of play, complete crash with reboot of the device. Resuming my game made it okay and nothing was lost but definitely annoying. Especially when it happens at the credit scene and you keep wondering if that's a normal behavior or something's broken.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is essentially "The Truman Show: The Game" but taken to even further extremes as there's a whole city full of unwitting reality show celebrities.Your character, Trevor Hills, is the most unpopular 'star' on the show however, and when he comes to understand that he's about to be "retired" he goes on the run. To tell any more would be to spoil the story, so I won't.The game itself is a sideways platform-puzzler in a similar vain to games like Inside and Limbo, though a lot more cheerful and (for the most part) less weird. There are also several 3D FPS sections in addition to the 2.5D sideways scrolling.In all honesty the platforming and puzzling are not great; neither is particularly challenging. The game's main aim is to tell a good story though, which is served best through this simplicity.My primary concern when playing a game is "Did I have fun?" And in American Arcadia's case, I had an absolute blast so I definitely recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a LOT more than just the sum of its parts.The gameplay is just "good enough" and the puzzles are "ok" at best, but what really matters here is the story and let me tell you, it's amazing, the characters, the dialogue, the setting and especially the twist... this game is a must-play.SCORE: 8/10. don't be scared by the low playtime, it's worth your money.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a blast for anyone who loves a good story and a cool world to explore.  The game keeps you guessing the whole way through, with surprises popping up left and right as you help Trevor escape. You'll really feel for him as he tries to crack the code of Arcadia.The best part? The world itself! It's like stepping into a technicolor dream of 1970s America.  Everything from the happy townspeople to the wacky buildings looks amazing, and it all helps suck you right into this fake town. It's like a super stylish movie you can play through!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, light and relatively relaxing experience that doesn't overstay its welcome with a good story!It's taken me 5-6 hours to complete the game and I had an overall enjoyable time. The story is straight-forward with a few fun turns along the way. I won't go into the story in detail, but it's basically The Truman Show, but more light-hearted. It had a couple of turns I didn't expect and it's fun to just enjoy the ride. The gameplay loop is very simple and revolves around 2 types of play depending on which character you are controlling. One is Trevor which is a left to right platformer 2.5D/ 3D style with some environmental puzzles. The other character is a first person logic puzzle solving game.I did encounter some issues along the way such as the game not telling me what the buttons were. I just got dumped into the game and got no prompts telling me what button did what - hopefully this is a bug as I found myself in several scenarios having no idea what to do and pressing every button on my controller to see what happened. Some of the puzzles and chases it is not possible to complete first time on a blind playthrough. The game relies on trial and error to navigate some areas. This is frustrating as it broke up the immersion in the otherwise fun story and simple gameplay. I experienced what I think were some noticeable stutters throughout. I don't typically spot them, but I had a few sections where this was obvious. Frame rates varied widely from 144fps before jumping to 40-60fps within short sequencesIt's not always clear what you are meant to do when playing as either of the playable characters. The game does a poor job at explaining some situations and what you need to do to move forward in the game. Overall - this is a game I highly recommend and had a really fun experience with. This game reminded me there is a world of gaming outside of the AAA scene and that the smaller games are generally the ones that are more fun to play. The story is light and easy to follow, the graphics are lovely and the game play is simple but fun. I had more fun with this than some of the AAA games that have come out recently.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun, short game.What I mostly enjoyed about it is voice acting and level design. The platformer elements were easy but appealing. Some parts, however, required good timing and failing them was irritating because the sequence had to be repeated. Overall the game looks good, plays well and pacing is just right. I found 1 bug - sometimes 2 voice lines would play at the same time if I interacted with the world while the character was talking.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: I had to change this to a negative review, since I ran into a game-ending bug in the 5th or 6th chapter.  I tried restarting the path, looking at walkthroughs.  The detective guy always caught me before I could jump to the ladder, after a long sequence of running and jumping.  stupid stupid stupid.If there were a sideways thumb, I would probably give it to this game.  The setting and aesthetics are great, and the voice acting is good.  The puzzles can be annoying, and the action puzzles, where you have to do the same actions over fifty or more times, hearing the same voice lines, can be aggravating.  I ended up using a walkthrough, because I wanted to see the story, but not get bogged down by the puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, wow. This is a really good story! ☺The plot is interesting, the aesthetics are brutal, it keeps you on edge but at the same time has funny moments, the voice actors are awesome, it's exciting,... and I love that so much about Arcadia's history is explained.I really like the feeling of being a hacker with Angela and having control over the set elements. I've played it with a keyboard and I never thought that a mouse and keyboard could generate such a feeling of gameplay. It feels like I'm actually infiltrating and shutting down cameras. Before playing the game I thought I would identify more with one of the characters than the other, but I didn't. Playing with the two separately, I felt like I could identify more with one of the characters than the other. Playing the two separately, who are both so alive through voice acting and have distinct personalities, it's easy to get into the shoes of both and feel comfortable. Trevor is a guy with an ordinary life and subjected to routine, it's easy to empathise with him. Plus, he has a turtle - I love it! But I also love Angela. It's perfect. It's challenging at times, you'll have to replay it a few times until you figure out what to do, but it's well indicated in the scenarios and it's completely accessible.Play it! Don´t Be A Fool! ♥
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The game is pretty good! A solid 7/10 in my opinion. I don't think it's going to win any game of the year awards or anything and people will probably complain about the length of the game at this price point, but in the end I think it's worth it.Pros:+ Story:The story is definitely a strong point for the game. It's not the most unique concept ever, but it's very well written an enjoyable the whole time.+ Voice Acting:The voice acting is top notch. Very believable performances that help to draw you in to the plight of the main characters.+ Puzzles:There are several puzzle sections where you need to figure out something or other to progress. These are never super difficult and range from gaining admin privileges to navigating a messy storage room. Nothing groundbreaking, but also not baby's first block puzzle. It's just enough to keep you engaged.+ Visuals:The game has a distinct art style and amazing color range. No bland tan or grey areas to slog through for 10 hours.+ Length:Some might complain $20 is a lot for a sub 10 hour game time, but I felt it didn't overstay it's welcome. There's enough added throughout the environment to stop and look at, but not enough to interact with to bog you down.+ Perspective:Keeping one character 2D and one 3D really drives home the point they are trying to make with the story (which I will not spoil).Cons:- "Action Sequences":Not really a huge complaint here but some of the more "action heavy sequences" are more exciting than others. Some involve solving little puzzles and platform sections on the fly, while others are kinda just holding A or D and pressing the Spacebar frequently. I like the mix, but the more involved ones were definitely more fun/memorable.- Subtitles:Sometimes the subtitles didn't match the actual lines being delivered. Also, when the MC speaks Spanish those lines are still in Spanish in the subtitles. So I mean, cool to know what she's saying in Spanish, but I unfortunately don't speak it so I just don't know what she said.- Gameplay/Cut-scenes:At times the game feels like a visual novel. The story is good and worth watching/listening to, but a lot more sections could have been a cut-scene, rather than me needing to hold the D key while you exposition at me.Review:American Arcadia is good! Definitely one of those indie games that probably won't get as much attention as it should. It tells a good story, with good characters, and with some excellent voice acting. It could just be me, but I feel the ending is pretty telegraphed a couple hours out and there's no meaningful choices to impact getting there, but it's still solid regardless. It suffers from some subtitling issues and the occasional moments of uninteresting "gameplay", but it's also fairly short so you don't have to deal with it for long at any given time. It's one of those things I gave a shot on a whim and I'm personally not disappointed. I like taking risks on neat, more original IPs like this. Not everything needs to be a million dollar AAAA game that turns out to be kinda stinky.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very enjoyable. I beat it in about 7 hours which is a little short, but I am very used to platformer-puzzle games in the same vein as Abe's Exodus etc. Probably another 5 hours to get achievements you may have missed depending on your playstyle. The various real-world references and the story are very engaging, and the ever-evolving plot leading to the finale kept me interested all the way through to the end.  Gameplay-wise, the game is very forgiving. Checkpoints are close together and the delay between attempts is very short so it never gets particularly frustrating even with repeated failures. Additionally, I don't think I encountered a single technical issue.Graphics are a little simple but I think that works in its favor. The game has a retro vibe as it is and the style being what it is, this is necessary to maintain graphic consistency between the two gameplay modes (platformer and first-person). Overall a fun, entertaining game and definitely an enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

What soured me the most was the last quarter (third?) of the game. The story breaks down and doesn't make sense. Thigns arent explained and I ran into a few (non-major) bugs. The mechanics from the beginning just repeat.Buy it on a sale for 5€ or something, definitly don't buy it for 20€.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: One of the hidden gems of 2023, a game which humour, characters, gameplay and graphics really make me get into it and fell in love with it. In a year where BG3 came out, American Arcadia is a game that you can play to move on from "big games" like BG3 is and just continue enjoying shorter games in term of hours and have a more than great experience. Again, the characters, the gameplay (that is pretty similar to Inside) and the story that the game tells through the time you play are flawless. And a lot of little details and touches that show that the developers love their game so much. I would recommend this to anyone, really really love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: After Call of the Sea, I couldn't wait until Out of the Blue Games released their next installment. It was many years between both games, but it was worth the wait. This one isn't much of a puzzler like Call of the Sea, but it's a great narrative platformer. Highly recommend to anyone who likes games like Inside. Rating: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunaly there isnt much "game" here. While the story has an interesting narrative the game mostly consists of sidescrolling to the left. The things that make other sidescrollers fun just isnt there. I do not want to give this game a bad review since I did enjoy my time with it but I do sincerely think that there are just many better games to put your time into. This game is just better as a walkthrough video rather than being played by yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: If you've heard there are  references, don't watch the movie but play this game. The concept is developed a lot more and carries the game much further than the movie.Gameplay-wise, it's a short platformer with undemanding puzzles (with a few retries for reflexes) and a neat dual perspective mechanic. What really saves it is the writing, characters, and delivery format.To top it all off, the ending is top notch. I was laughing for about 5 min straight as the credits rolled...Also, watch the movie after you play the game. It's great
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: So I started playing this game today and couldn't stop until I got to the end. Because of the nature, I feel like I may have missed a few things, but I can unreservedly recommend this game to anyone who played the demo and liked it. This was a puzzle game that I felt SMART for getting it and it didn't feel tedious and frustrating. Highly recommend it for anyone who likes puzzles or narrative stories.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite gaming experience of the year. An exciting, fun and charming cinematic puzzle platformer that hits every beat it wants almost perfectly. There's some polishing that needs doing but don't let a little bit of roughness around the edges keep you from experiencing my favourite cinematic platformer in years
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a rich story, amazing gameplay mechanics, beautiful models, sound design, just everything. So many twists, challenging puzzles that are never too hard to figure out. Absolutely one of my new favorite games. This game is what I aspire to make as a game artist. I am in love with Trevor Hills.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Funny and charming, American Arcadia is another gem from the creators of Call of the Sea. I had a great time playing it; I only intended to try it out, but ended up finishing it in a few days! The game is full of cool references to movies and boasts a fantastic idea and execution. Strong recommendation for anyone who enjoys quality indie games!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very short game, but it is very different to any other game I have ever played. I never do good on puzzles games, but I liked the puzzles here, easy for people who likes those types of games for sure. I just found out too that the developers are from Spain, which is pretty neat :) Congrats on the team, I just hope in the future they drop some hotfixes for steam deck because it is a joy to play this game on handheld but it stutters way too much. Please Out of the Blue, please we would looveee a patch to optimize the game for handheld! All hail Arcadia
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn’t sure at first what to make of American Arcadia, I had played the demo so I knew a bit about what I was getting into but for a bit, I wasn’t sure it was going to go anywhere interesting, this turned out to be an incorrect feeling.Combining 2.5D platforming elements with first-person for the two different protagonists each taking on a vastly different role provided for a unique experience that kept the gameplay fresh, each section of either would only go on for a short time and each served the story well. The platforming was relatively simple with some minor puzzle platforming, each puzzle in the platforming sections was easy to figure out despite having some unforgiving checkpoints that didn’t serve a mainly story-based game well. The first-person sections were the quieter sections and involved stealth as well as puzzles, some of these puzzles were quite convoluted to figure out and I still haven’t grasped exactly how some of them worked, it doesn’t help that the character here gets audibly frustrated when you aren’t doing the puzzle correctly.It also helps that the visuals, especially in the 2.5D sections are striking and colorful. The areas match the 70s theme well and create impressive backgrounds. The story is the most interesting aspect and the reason to give the game a try. It follows Trevor Hills and his companion codenamed Kovacs, Trevor is in a sort of Truman Show-like TV show while Kovacs is the man on the outside helping him to escape. It seems at first that it isn’t going to have much to add to this style of story but this feeling is quickly removed as it has much to say about the ethics of certain media. Another important aspect is the relationship between media mega conglomerates and the government and how it often allows things to happen. Themes of control and freedom are frequent and it’s not clear that the result of the events of the game are positive, by being guided towards and potentially to freedom is that truly being free? Is Trevor ever in control?Despite that lingering question, there is one genuinely beautiful scene, it is perhaps the freest that Trevor ever is, not following orders or instructions it is that scene which is somehow the most innocuous and important scene in the entire game. The scene before this one was also touching as it confirmed that the whole thing was more than just some ideologically driven moving of pieces on a board but actual genuine human concern that isn’t parasocial.Another piece that struck me about the whole thing is both the metaphorical and literal comparison to prison, it is a system in which people are genuinely unable to adjust to normal life after spending much of their lives in there and this touches on that idea and doesn’t necessarily have an answer for that.Lastly of course is the condemnation of capitalistic systems of exploitation, the man in the chair protagonist at one point asks how one could do some of the horrific things we see throughout the game and it is explicitly pointed out to them that they work at American Arcadia, the reality show that keeps people imprisioined. The forces of capitalistic exploitation are so powerful they can seem inescapable which is another theme that is touched on, though later on in the game and it is from that highpoint scene I mentioned earlier and beyond that that the game truly shines and shows that it has something interesting to say.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe the most beautiful game I have ever played.I bought this on a whim and never has a whim been so satisfied. Every screen is gorgeous, the writing is fantastic, and the soundtrack made me cry while playing. I'm being serious.It's the Truman Show meets EPCOT meets the tragedy of Steve Wozniack. It's wild and creative.I love Trevor and Angela, they're such lame dorks. They both think they're hilarious and they aren't, it's really endearing and funny.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Don't waste your money on this game. Watch a no-commentary playthrough, instead. My trust in Yahtzee Croshaw is shaken for the first time, and I started watching ZP in 2010.I have no idea how reskins of Limbo keep getting critical acclaim. Especially this one. The characters are endearing, the setting is colorful, and, like in Limbo and Inside, the ending is cerebral and interesting. But I have no idea how these things are games. If you can replace what you're doing with cutscenes of the exact same thing happening, then what is the point of you playing it? All you will get from doing it yourself is frustrated with the fact that it's impossible to figure out how to not die the first time, so you have to listen to the incessant chatter for that part over and over and over and over.The obstacles that keep you from moving to the right (and the occasional token left) don't feel like puzzles, they feel like nuisances. The few that felt like puzzles were ruined by the fact that I needed to go through them over and over listening to the same peanut gallery commentary over and over. Every obstacle is mandatory and there's pretty much only one way to deal with it. This game is more linear than the original Mario, where you at least have collectibles to choose whether to get or ignore.The only parts that made me feel like maybe this game wasn't complete trash were some of the hacking parts in the few cases where I didn't discover that they were only being difficult because I was awake at 3 in the morning. I didn't personally find them challenging, but I can see them being interesting for someone who hasn't played a lot of video games.All of this is not to mention the bugs and qa/qc problems: the typos in the subtitles, the voice clips cutting out before the end, the subtitles being cut off by the widescreen black bars, respawning in a place to immediately get caught, Trevor occasionally not using a hiding place as a hiding place. Let's not even hold the crashes against it because I was playing on Steam Deck, and this game still feels rushed. Somehow this is fine when it's an indie game. It's Bear and Breakfast all over again.I'm going to close the game review proper by writing about the incident that made me start thinking this game sucks. At around the halfway point, Trevor is pressured into doing something that he was not set up to have done and clearly does not want to do. Then the game puts Trevor in your hands. I wasn't going to do it. I went to a guide letting him sit there to find out that you must do it. What is the point of putting him in my hands at that moment if you weren't going to let me decide myself? Just show me the cutscene of him doing it! Why am I even here???There's some fun stuff that I genuinely enjoy in the story, but this is a game review, and full stop: this is barely a game. You know why this is sold as a video game? Because the creators knew that this as a 4 hour movie wouldn't sell. Because they're a slave to what the audience wants, just like the evil corporation in this game. And no, doing this whole thing as a performance stunt to show what fools we were doesn't make me think it was actually good when you really think about it. My time is still wasted.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that offers an amazing trip from start to end, the characters are highly likable and lovable.The game does not feel like something you would watch behind a screen but rather something you would experience along with the characters.You are part of the audience, you are the audience and will be in for one of the greatest journeys that this game has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This being my inaugural Steam review, I want to clarify that my intention isn't to deem American Arcadia a subpar game. However, I find it perplexing that it has garnered numerous 10/10 reviews, labeling it as the best game ever experienced. While it is indeed a decent game, I fail to perceive the intricacy and challenge in the puzzles, and the promising concept is not fully explored.Allow me to express that American Arcadia, although enjoyable, lacks puzzles of substantial complexity and difficulty. The game's potential remains untapped, and its concept is not fully realized. Without giving away specific details, the anticipated story twist is discernible from a considerable distance.Despite the entertainment value, the game is marred by lackluster and tedious puzzles, extended run scenes that fail to leave a significant impact, and a narrative that lacks player engagement. If seeking a recommendation, I'd suggest exploring titles like "The Fall" or "Black the Fall" (despite the title similarities, the games are unrelated).If I could give this game a big meh. _childDocuments_.review: This game came up on the suggestion list for me, but I was ignoring it. I thought: "Pfft ! It is a story about American life I do not care about (I do not live in the USA). It was set in the 1970s ! How boring could that be ?"But then I got it at the discount on the Christmas sale. The game drew me in. It is a work of art, and a work of love. The 1970-style environment was engaging. The story was engaging too, and had twists. Aaand... this is the first time for me when the game combines the 2.5D side-scroller and the 3D first-person action. I am keen to play more game from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the story and pacing of this game. I am not usually a fan of games were I need to run away/hide but the stress levels were well done. In areas that required more time you werent under pressure of being caught. The puzzles were clever but not frustrating so that was enjoyable as well. Dislike: I played this 100% on steam deck and there were glitches in transitional phases that just stopped the game from loading/progressing further. It would just hang. I had to completely close the game and return and this caused having to redo some puzzles and story line as I did not trigger a checkpoint. That said it would have been a lot more helpful if the game told you when the last save/checkpoint was. Played another game that had a counter of "checkpoint 35 second ago" etc.. I was always afraid to close the game not knowing if Id have to do a puzzle again.. Overall I still recommend the game and may pop back in to try and get the bunch of acheivments I originally missed :)
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Big "eeeeehhhhhhhhh, I guess" for this game.It's split between side-scrolling puzzle solving and chase sequences, and first-person exploration and puzzle solving. The side-scrolling puzzle solving and first person exploration are genuinely good and engaging but the side-scrolling chase sequences and first-person puzzles are bad. Really, really bad.The chase sequences are built around failing the first time so you know how to evade what is coming. There's no way to get through a whole scene the first time except by luck. On top of this the timings in the chase sequences aren't always the same. Warning about an enemy to avoid will play at the same time they're grabbing me the first time through a chase and after a reload they're playing a few seconds ahead of time so that I can react. Items that look like they should act as cover or concealment sometimes aren't despite being the same general size and shape as cover objects in their same depth. Red herring paths abound with no other purpose than causing the player to need to restart from a checkpoint. I've also had movable items not spawn in on some attempts, or a chasing NPC vanish halfway through a chase leading to me hearing only half of the dialogue and ending in a crash at the end of the sequence.The puzzles in the first-person section just kind of suck. They're either brain-dead simple or brain-murdering difficult without anything between them. There's a couple whose rules I can't figure out even after watching a walkthrough with their solution. Red herring false solutions can also be found here but not as much with the chases. Nowhere near as bad as the chases but it gets in the way of making at least half the game fun.Grab it on sale if you want to play it. $20 at full price isn't much but antagonistic game design ought to stay buried back in the Sierra days. If all is you want is the story save yourself some money and a headache and watch a Youtube playthrough. I'm just past the halfway point but don't see my review changing at all.Edit: After finishing the game I can say that towards the end it got really cool and they pulled out all the stops. Except for when the game stopped because it crashed. It also looked like they were doing something neat by forcing the first-person segments into some sort of first-person-forward-scroller but that was just the game glitching and ignoring the mouse until I opened and closed the menu.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks like concept art; It did not lose its beauty after being run through corporate whatevers. The story was better than any other game I've ever played. Funny, poignant, creative, other adjectives. It's a puzzle platformer of The Truman Show set in Walt's original Epcot plan. This game tries so many things and all of them work marvelously. They Trevor-fied Steve Just!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on sale bundled with Call of the Sea (which I haven't played yet) at a time when I was between AAA game releases that I wanted to play.  I was looking for something to kill a few hours waiting for a title that I was eagerly anticipating, and it didn't disappoint.  This is a great - if somewhat short - diversion.  Not gonna name the couple of movies & books that I thought this "took advantage of" because it's not a big issue (and I think everyone knows what they are anyway).  So, recommended 9/10 on sale - whether you wait until it's on sale is up to you.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: The story, game design, mechanics, and puzzles make this game one of a kind. It switches between the main character and their confidant who is helping them escape certain death. The gameplay is so smooth, and even when it does switch between the two characters it never feels off or disturbs the story in any way. Also if you love Defunctland documentaries then you will love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: American Arcadia is a mixed bag, there are some good elements such as the voice acting and the overall world building. However to me it borrows/steals too much from other media. There is clear inspiration from other games, movies and tv but it is so blatant and appears so often I was wondering if the devs ever had an original idea of their own. The ending as well was quite disappointing and really didn't match up with what had happened so far, at least to me. However saying all that I really don't want to give this game a thumbs down, if it was possible I would give it a mid rating. It isn't that bad really but the concept has been explored better in other games, films and tv already.  It isn't a long game and is very simple to play so if you like the genre and can pick it up for about £5.00 I would say go for it other than that you can safely give this one a miss.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Don't Be A Fool! get this game if you're into Conspiracy theories, subliminal messaging etc, from the get go this portrays a mix of themes/elements that will remind you of "The Matrix" and "The Truman show" mixed in with a Disney facade (think of the dark what goes on "behind the scenes' at Disney) the story and game play so far are top notch enough to keep you engaged and want to progress to see what happens. Loving this
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome little adventure of a guy who lives in a "safe Eden" of a city every citizen of which is involuntary 24/7 live streamer. During adventure he will wreak havoc as he discovers "Arcadia's intricate lies".Game easily plays in one go with interesting revelations about order of Arcadia.You play as a Trevor in 3rd person platformer mode, and as his helper in 1st person mode. Game art style despite simplistic looks good in both modes and has a unique charm.Game mainly consists of "story mode" and puzzles some of which are time-based.Overall awesome game for a few evenings.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with an interesting spin on a Truman Show story, likable characters and fun (for me) humor. The gameplay is not the most exiting, with sidescrolling jump and run sections and first person sections with some light puzzling mixed, but the pacing of the story makes it so the game never gets boring. After this and Call of the Sea I'm exited to see what Out of the Blue does next.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

_childDocuments_.review:
Welcome to Arcadia! A 70's retro-futuristic metropolis where all its citizens enjoy a life of luxury and comfort... unaware that they're being broadcast live 24/7! Arcadia is not an ordinary city, but the most watched reality show on the planet - where a drop in popularity ratings comes at the highest cost: death.

Uncover the truth and escape with your life in 'American Arcadia'!

American Arcadia gives you control over two characters in completely different environments and unique playstyles: A 2.5D action side-scroller including challenging platform action, breath-taking chases, stealth and puzzles. As well as a full 3D first-person game, with hacking, exploration, stealth elements, and puzzles to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: American Arcadia

name: Skully
detailed_description: On a mysterious remote island, a skull washes up on shore and is reawakened by an enigmatic deity. Dubbed Skully, the newly reanimated being has been summoned to intervene in a war between the deity’s three siblings, whose quarrel jeopardizes the island they call home. Fate has bestowed Skully with a second chance at “life” and his adventure will take him across a strange paradise as he seeks an end to the conflict that plagues the isle. Hop, skip and roll your way to victory. Dodge obstacles across the island as Skully, a skull reanimated by the power of magical clay. Adapt to your environment. Transform into three distinct forms to overcome challenges and defeat enemies. Traverse a mysterious island. Roll through 18 different levels in 7 distinct ecosystems each packed with unique dangers. Explore a compelling story. Fully voiced dialogue and cutscenes breathe life into the island’s inhabitants and the charming world of Skully!

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming game with a nice artstyle and a beautifully designed world, but ultimately held back by "puzzles" that required a lot of going back and forth to get different forms which just turned out to be way more aggravating. Overall playing with the Golems way more just an annoying tidbit which got in the way of rolling around at high speeds with the skull form.For example: When there was a flower just out of reach and a block I could use to jump up and grab it just a bit further. This means I had to go to the Checkpoint and summon a "Swift-Form"-Golem to move it sideways. Then I had to leave it there, go back to the Checkpoint, summon a "Vault-Form"-Golem to move it vertically so that I can get enough height to reach the flower. Then I had to leave the Golem holding the block in midair and roll back to the Checkpoint to summon a third "Vault-Form"-Golem just so that I could hop on the block and grab the single flower. There are 5,000+ flowers in the game. Cases like these are not uncommon.Really nice to look at, but it was just really painful to play through. Would probably skip.
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice puzzle-platformer. The game's controls are tight and it feels better on a controller. If you liked Crash-Bandicoot style quirky platformers, this may be for you.The game starts with just being able to roll as a skull, but quickly introduces other forms that you can take to solve puzzles or navigate tricky terrain.Ultimately, it's a nice game with a lot of heart and charm where you can bring some of your own creativity in resolving puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: It was a surprisingly fun game to play.It has an upbeat feeling to it that will lift your emotion at least for 80% of the game.Later more on those last 20%When you play the game it feels like it is the start of summer and you have no care in the world.The music, the game play, the graphics all look really well.But now those last 20%.It almost feels like that part was made by a different dev team.Suddenly the nice pacing that the game had stops.Brutally boring puzzles come in its place.The puzzles arent hard however it requires many steps for some and the accuracy of control that is needed is severely lacking at those precise moments.A few times I wanted to quit but I persevered after walking away for a bit.TLDRGreat fun little game, overstays its welcome a bit and seems that in the homestretch it was a different dev team that came and ruined the smooth pacing of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good 3D-platformer (with a few puzzle elements in it) all in all, I was actually really surprised how much I enjoyed it. Levels offer quite some variations, and the constantly added new forms/characters (with unique abilities) you can change into even make it possible to master certain sections in different ways. Yeah, sometimes controlling the ball-like skull reminds you of early 80s games, and admittedly it’s not really precise, but this actually feels intended and gives this game a kind of distinct charm. Honestly, can’t really put my finger on it, but somehow the longer I played, the more I liked the game. Environments are beautiful. Cutscenes (presented in stills, but in a weird style, like they were molded in clay for real), story-telling and voice-overs are great. Music is fittingly professional as well with some nice atmospheric tunes (though I maybe would have wished for more and longer tracks over time), and gameplay never is really unfair (e.g. no overdoing of sinking or disappearing platforms, also many checkpoints). So, what’s left, maybe one good advice. If you’re going for some of the achievements (game length is pretty ideal then, around 10+ hours), there’s a good trick to get all the collectathon-like flowers without too much hassle (they also unlock all of the artwork). After you gather some, just quit to the main menu and resume from there, and you keep them (without having to restart from the checkpoint and having to collect them again). This also works if you do this just before you die for the No-Dying-Achievements. Believe me, keeping this in mind, this way your life will be much easier, and it’s quite doable to 100% the game this way ;)Anyway, definite recommendation from me. Though the price is pretty steep in my opinion, but all Modus games obviously feature that high pricing policy. Just wait for a good sale, or get it in a bundle (actually I got it in Humble Choice, so I absolutely don’t regret it).
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: Skully appears to be a straightforward marble-rolling game with beautiful art and a charming aesthetic. When it actually IS that, the game is fine. The issue is that you spend the vast majority of your time as a variety of clunky and ill-controlling golems doing boring platforming and absolutely tedious block-moving puzzles. On top of that, the beautiful and richly detailed environments all have collision, so it's extremely common to bounce off a random bit of geometry on an otherwise smooth path and go flying to your death. This is especially egregious in the bewildering chase segments where you have no camera control and have to blindly control your momentum to make jumps you can't see. Additionally, because checkpoints for the marble rolling are also golem spawn points, their placement is often far more a matter of what makes sense for the puzzles rather than level flow. Writing and voice acting is oddly high quality given the cutscenes being voiceovers of static images, but all of the characters are deliberately insufferable so it's not exactly stellar. If they'd stuck to their guns about being a little skull rolling around on a beach, this game would be lovely. Unfortunately every new mechanic makes the core gameplay worse and it devolves into a mess that feels unfinished by the devs and going off steam achivement rates is also not finished by the players.
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: Precision platformers aren't my thing but Skully was actually not bad. The rolling was fun and it looked great, but there were a few things that rubbed me the wrong way, and one big issue….Firstly the small stuff; the hundreds of flowers scattered throughout are for perfectionists only, and if you aren't going to go for 100% of them it's not even worth paying attention to which is a shame, and if you are going for all of them it's pretty annoying to find that last one...There is a metric for beating a level with no deaths, but no way in the chapter select to see which levels you've done no death on.Now for the biggest thing: no protection on misclicking the New Game option which effectively means "DELETE ALL SAVE DATA"........ Even when you are going in the chapter select that will overwrite your autosave it asks "Your save progress will be overwritted, load chapter?" but in the main menu the second option, right BETWEEN RESUME AND CHAPTER SELECT is 'New Game' which immediately wipes all progress. I did misclick this and instantly bye bye all my work to collect the flowers and no death runs. I Alt+F4'd within seconds of pressing it but no luck, the deletion is immediate. Before this I was leaning towards thumbs up but after having this happen I can't recommend Skully.
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: It's like playing a bland platmormer with stiff controllers at time, while listening to an infuriating episode of Dr.Phil. The Siblings in this game are yelling at eachother all the time and it's annoying to listen to while you try to focus on the platforming.The asking price is pretty crazy too since it's a rather short game (I 100% it in 11h). So I'm glad I got it as part of a humble bundle. If you are still eager to try it out, wait for a big sale.I'm happy to uninstall this game now and just let it sit in my library, never to be played again.
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: Skully has everything it needs to impose himself as a mix between a frantic platformer like Marble Blast Ultra and an original take on Metroidvania genre, but it wastes too much time before showing its true potential. The lack of enemies and situations to deal with does not help to keep you engaged until the game unleashes all its features, and it is a shame because it’s a pretty game, and also very responsive to player input. Anyone willing to bear with the first few hours will be rewarded with fascinating gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for April 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before March 4th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.After an playing an hour to review for the Humble Choice April 2021 Bundle:This is a strange platformer where the player is a skull with a head full of mud, and he’s assisting what appears to be a deity fight with his siblings.  It’s a very colorful and bright game, has some wonderful music, and solid controls. The level design is good with a lot of collectible items.  The character design looks expressive and I liked the look of the first form that Skully could transform into.  There’s a decent challenge but also a lot to see and explore and the world is interesting enough to see what comes next.There are a few potential issues.  It’s probably not the longest game, and the music seems to repeat in different zones.  That’s unfortunate because I want more of that music.  But the experience here is solid Pick this up if you like platformers and like what you’re seeing.  I had a great time with this one though it isn’t the most exciting game I’ve seen. _childDocuments_.review: There's no nice way to say this, but Skully doesn't even come close to being worth the $30 pricetag. I got it off Humble Bundle and even though it was essentially free b/c of it, it still feels like it was too much.I've gotten to chapter 12 and decided to quit for several reasons. I will say that the voice actors are doing an excellent job and do the best they can with the material written (more on that later), and the environments are absolutely gorgeous, but they're the only things I don't have gripes with.I lied, actually. I really enjoy Wanda, because she's the only character that seems to have boundaries, and she's absolutely fed up with the "messy family fistfight behind the back of the Denny's you witness walking home after a night shift energy" that can loosely be called the game's plot. Also she just wants you to leave her be which seems pretty simple but I guess not for Terry... we'll get to you Terry #justiceforwandaSome complaints are, in no particular order:CONTROLS: Skully himself controls like a pinball who regularly snorts Pixie Sticks in dire need of an ADHD diagnosis. His controls feel slippery and hard to use, which I understand is part of the point, but when the entire game is platforming, it makes for a miserable experience. This makes it especially difficult during the many scripted chase sequences the game likes to throw at you, with either the threat in front of you and blocking half your vision so you jump blindly, or with the threat behind you, leaving you to sometimes jump off the screen and awkwardly spam your movement keys to keep Skully from sliding to his doom while you wait for the camera to catch up. I died 27 times alone in the scripted event in Chapter 11 and that alone made me want to quit.CHECKPOINTS: Checkpoints are less common then useful, mainly only triggering when moving onto a mud pile or before a scripted chase scene. Checkpoints also don't save the collectible flowers you get if you die, so if you do (which again, very easy with the shoddy controls) you lose all progress. Eventually I completely gave up on getting the collectible flowers, especially when...COLLECTIBLES: ...the collectibles (the flowers found across the chapters) only unlock concept art. That's it. It just makes it a collect-a-thon with no actual merit other than to waste your time. The game also likes to sometimes not put flowers in more confusing parts of levels, leaving you wandering for minutes on end trying to figure out how to progress. Normally wouldn't complain about that, but when levels have anywhere from 200-400 collectible flowers, there's no reason to leave players confused.LEVEL DESIGN: Maybe the game becomes a joy to play after chapter 11 but I found it often confusing to navigate where I was supposed to be going. In chapter 2/3, you unlock a "strong form" that can M1 for punching through walls and M2 for a ground attack, but the game never tells you about how to M2. I tried to M1 enemies that were only venerable to M2 attacks, leaving me desperately flailing at enemies wondering why I couldn't kill them. I had to look into the controls menu to figure it out.On a similar note, chapter 8 was especially awful from a design perspective. You gain a "nimble/double jump" form that can move some platforms vertically, which compliments your "quick form" that can move platforms horizontally. The game never bothers to tell you this, but you can eject from a form while it's holdiing a platform, leaving it stationary while you jump onto it. From now on the game expects you to eject from/enter both of these forms to move platforms, leaving the gameplay stale and repetitive while you jump in and out of forms to move a single platform.STORY: I really wanted to like the story- you're a cute lil reanimated skull that rolls around, what's not to love? Unfortunately, our rolly boi takes a backseat while Terry becomes the main character trying to make peace with his siblings (ie yell at them and have nothing get done). WHY they're fighting is never made clear, and the mystical macguffin they all want so desperately, the heart, is only mentioned a couple times. I love Skully but he has no depth or real purpose to be there, other than to play the level and have Terry and Wanda magically teleport to him for the next cutscene. Wanda was the only character with some depth that I actually enjoyed (because she's the only one with a braincell and just wants to vibe alone in her realm), but she immediately gets sucked into a magic jar only to become an EXTREMELY unlucky and unwilling sidekick that tags along while Terry continues to ruin everything. Speaking of which...TERRY: I could forgive everything else in the game but I can't forgive Terry. He's annoying. He's obnoxious. He's giving me "bootleg Dreamworks side character" energy, except he's unfortunately our main character. He's got that particularly annoying combo of character traits where he'll ignore other characters' advice/opinions/anything because he's the quirky funny man haha lmao epic amirite winks to camera. I hate him. Death to Terry. I'm a proud supporter of himbo rights, but Terry is simply too stupid to live. (His voice actor does a great job though no shade to him)CONCLUSION: This game is not worth it. It's too pricey for an unpolished, uninteresting, rage-inducing collect-a-thon. It was the spiritual equivalent of being invited over for a sleepover only for you friend to have a messy fight with their parents for the entire night while you look on in second hand embarrasement. Terry is an annoying rat with no boundaries that the game keeps insisting I should like because he acts like a Dreamworks comic relief character. I came in excited, and left as Wanda: feeling frustrated, bitter and irritated with the insufferable family drama and shoddy gameplay.Wanda deserved a better game, and Terry should've been scrapped before the first draft.
