_childDocuments_.review: If you don't like 3D pinball exploration games, this isn't for youIf you DO like 3D pinball exploration games...this still isn't for youSkully is a hybrid pinball and 3D platformer collect-a-thon with light puzzle elements. You roll around as a skull pinball, and can utilize mudpools to transform yourself into various clay bodies, each with their own unique skills: One is strong, one can double jump, and the third...just moves blocks basically. you can exit these clay bodies at any time, and can create up to 3 simultaneously.Ok, now that the description is out of the way...Pros:++The game's atmosphere and sound design is well done, evoking a lighthearted, but grand adventure across the island+The voice acting is well done, and gives the characters a light likeability++The pinball platforming is mostly well done, and there's even the ability to skip areas if you're clever enough (See cons for full explanation)Cons:-Skipping areas only works when there's no invisible walls impeding your progress. Early on, there's a few here and there, but later, it turns the game into feeling like there's only one way.--Dialogue and story are basic, kind of bland, and brings down the voice work. Brad, in particular, can get on your nerves, as he's supposed to be the "WaCKy" one---The puzzle elements devolve into tedium really quickly. It involves a lot of unnecessary steps that could be resolved by allocating all the "platform moving" mechanics to one body. There are a couple that end up stumping you for a bit, but most end up boring you to tears instead.---The swift's running skill is required for maybe 1 level, and feels wasted. Why does it even have this ability?-In escape sequences, starting over from a checkpoint actually increases the difficulty by moving what is chasing you to right behind you, making it nearly impossible to collect the collectibles in the level-collectibles have no real purpose outside of getting concept artI like a lot of elements of Skully, and feel like the game has quite a lot of potential. However, the fun platforming gets bogged down into tedium by lackluster and repetitive puzzles. The story is nothing to get excited about, but is helped a little by some good voice work.TL;DR: I can't recommend cause it just gets tedious. Score: One eye socket/Skull

_childDocuments_.review: “He’s not a pebble!” exclaims exasperated and awfully named earth deity, Terry. “He’s a reanimated skull moulded in magical clay. Why is that so hard to understand?!”He’s speaking of the titular Skully, who is effectively a large marble sent to trundle about a tropical island and make gamers initially really angry at anything set at a slope. Being an undead ball means that your mobility options never extend any further than rolling, which is an issue if you want to go anywhere. For example, because you’re made mostly out of clay, submerging yourself in water is fatal, seeing as it washes away the majority of your substance. But there are numerous crooks and rivers to cross. Fortunately, there’s almost always a convenient series of cropping rock formations you can 3D platform yourself across. Unfortunately, they’re rarely flat which means learning how to land and instantly adjust yourself so you don’t just roll casually off the platform to your death.You’ll drown a few times before you figure out how to stick uneven landings, but you’ll soon be making minute adjustments a split second after touchdown and laughing in the face of 45° angles in no time. Sections of the game where you control Skully as is – a macabre sentient beach ball of sorts – are perhaps the purest part of the game, trying to deal with and manipulate the momentum of being in control of a sphere traversing oft irregular terrain. Cocky players soon become dead ones. It’s easy to rocket forward and lose control once an unexpected hill shows up, or you’re forced to try and navigate a steep curving corner. But, also, play it safe and slowly poke forward in overly cautious dribbles, and you’re not going to have enough momentum behind you to hop across stepping stones or navigate your way up a slope.Not long into the game, though, and regular Skully will stop being your only option. For the first few stages, bubbling clay pits act as checkpoints as well as stations to top up flagging heath, but the further you delve into the game, the more useful they become. They start giving you the ability to produce clay bodies, which shift considerable sections of Skully away from pure platformer, introducing puzzle stages into the fold. The first brutish form isn’t able to help you a lot with this; his skillset doesn’t extend a great deal further than lumbering around and hitting things, but this allows you access to areas hidden behind cracked stone walls. He’s also the only chance you have to fight back against the island’s hostile wildlife; your only option up until his discovery was to cautiously avoid them. The most common of these are these annoying sentient water bubble creatures who systematically explode, drenching the surrounding area with clay-stripping water. It’s a death bath for little marble Skully; it’s a damp nuisance for his stompy hulk form.The puzzle element really ramps up once his other two forms are introduced; on the surface, one’s a smaller, faster model, while the other has access to a double jump. To begin with, both primarily exist to further flesh out the platforming, but possess the ability to manipulate platforms, one being able to move them at will, while the other can raise and lower them. Sometimes this means just arranging your own path, or building and dismantling platforms on the fly as you try to trek across large bodies of water. Bridge building becomes more and more complex, however, forcing you to make use of the ability to have up to three clay bodies constructed at the same time. Pop Skully out of one of these bodies, and they’ll stay put, holding a platform in place for you to strategically build around. This leaves you with an open canvas and, often, several different ways to beat the puzzle. I have zero doubt a few of my resolutions weren’t what the developer had in mind as I mashed random skills together to make a bastardised Frankenstein’s solution, but if they don’t like that, they shouldn't have given the hulk clay form the ability to lob Skully like a quarterback. It’s in my nature to maliciously abuse that.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. There seems to be some mixed reviews on this game so I'm going to do my best to lay everything out for everyone before they make a decision. Let me start by saying, I love this game. That being said, nothing is without faults and Skully is no exception to that. This game has a lot of charm and is unique enough to set it apart from other games in this category. The characters were well written, and they had a lot of really good chemistry. Everything they said to one another felt natural. The story was nothing too new, siblings fighting + gods fighting gives you Skully. The puzzles weren't overly difficult, but every now and then I would stumble across one that had me looking around for a few minutes until something stood out to me, but that was rare. I have seen people say that there is an issue with poor programming but honestly, I didn't see that. Sometimes when climbing i would hit a bump that would knock me off that platform and i would have to start it over, but to me things like that only add to the challenge. I did come across one or two puzzles that if i was standing a certain way on a moving platform it would get stuck and i would have to move slightly to remedy the situation, but if that's the worst thing i have to deal with in a game, then I wouldn't give it enough thought to complain about it. My only real complaint would be on start up sometimes there would be quite a bit of lag that caused the camera to go crazy for a while until the game caught up to itself, but this isn't the only game I've seen with an issue like that so ill give it a pass. TL;DR Don't listen to the negative reviews. This game is a great, relaxing, casual game (although everything has its faults). I'd guess that the people leaving negative reviews aren't that good at this style of game in the first place and don't want to just admit that they are bad.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect example of where steam ratings need to be more complex than a simple "yes" or "no." This game is a maybe.The art style is great, and it's a cute story. My 3 year old son begs me to play it so he can watch, and it's nice to hang out with him, even though this isn't really the style of game I would normally play. The gameplay style is pretty simplistic. Collect flowers, solve puzzles, boss fight, repeat. Then there are some puzzles that are mind numbingly frustrating. One particular puzzle, which requires throwing Skully 4 times back and forth underground is particularly frustrating. If you don't throw him at the exact right arch, and the exact right vector, he will bounce off a stalagmite  into the water and you will have to start over from scratch. I repeated this infuriating puzzle for almost an hour and a half to try to figure out the exact right place to throw Skully each of the 4 times, starting over countless times with each mistake I made. If the level had been designed properly, this should have taken no longer than 5 minutes once you figure out the combination (which on it's own, was pretty clever). If my son didn't like the game so much, there's no way I would have spent so long to try to get past it so he could see the end of the game. So I really can't recommend this game. I know some people might find this mind numbing repetition rewarding once you finally pass the level, but in my mind, it's just endless frustration. Outside of that, the game really is rather charming, especially for younger kids, but I foresee many broken controllers in the hands of those not old enough to control their emotions with this one. I wish I could recommend it, and for around $5, it's definitely worth giving it a try. But at full price, I just can't in good conscience flick the yes button to this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game for the first 5-6 levels, and I even wanted to 100% it, because I like simplistic platformers without any complex mechanics - I just wanted to relax, ride around as a skull, and enjoy myself.However, three big problems made me drop the game halfway through and give it a negative review:1. The main problem is that the game does everything possible to make you bored and tired. Pretty soon you gain the ability to possess larger stone creatures, which have the most simplistic purposes of all time: one can punch walls, the other can sprint and move platforms horizontally, the third one can double jump and move platforms vertically. I think there might be more of them, but I did not reach that point.The abilities are simple, but they are used to just drag, drag and drag the game along, especially if you want to collect collectibles. You possess one creature, move the platform, jump, move the platform, jump, move the platform, jump. ALL THE TIME.The worst of all offends is that when you are just a simple scull - it's actually fun to ride around. However, generally all you do is run around for 15 seconds, and then spend a few minutes as a larger creature.These sections also cannot be described as a puzzle, because there is nothing to solve. You just create a bridge or a platform to jump onto - and move on. Just a drag...2. The second problem was that the game manages to make it even worse. Platforming itself is sensitive, and it would be fine and fun, if not for the checkpoints being put BEFORE you solve some "puzzle". You have a section which involves big creatures, you spend five minutes doing it - then you quickly die because of one mistake and have to do it all over again.WHY? Even if you wanted to put those "puzzles" into the game, could it maybe be a different way around? AFTER you finish the dangerous section?3. The third point, which, combined with the first two, creates a big infuriating experience, is the lack of depth perception. I have no idea how developers managed to do it, but most of the time (especially when related to picking up collectibles or to the chasing sequences) it's very hard to understand how your character is positioned in relation to the objects around.It is very hard to put in words, but I honestly don't remember the last time I had this problem. You really have to try the game to feel this.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - a little uninspired but an overall entertaining mechanical basis. price point is too high, wait for a large sale.Unfortunately, whether this is a positive or negative review depends on whether I would recommend this game. At roughly £25/$30, no, I would not recommend this game.It has charm, though personally I found it wearing off rather soon. The mechanics are... Alright, but the enemy design is repetitive, the puzzles are either too easy or just awkward, and the central marble platforming mechanic is alright (though a little awkward at times) but it's constantly interrupted by the other forms you must take for puzzle solving.It's just... Odd. The game is nice to look at, the music - if somewhat forgettable - is alright, the plot is simply there to drive the gameplay, and all enemies fall into one of two categories: A blob that just blobs around and occasionally does a large AoE attack, or some form of projectile, either on its own or fired by a boss or a stationary variant of one of the blob enemies.The tutorials felt a little lacking at times too, as all of your instructions are simply inscribed on walls, so the game never even tells you that you can have more than one mud golem out at a time (which is completely necessary for puzzles pretty much at least a couple of times per chapter since like chapter 6, roughly speaking.It feels... A little uninspired at times. But it certainly doesn't seem completely uninspired, as the mechanics are quite an interesting idea on a basic level. Nonetheless, I have 2.5 hours now, and I was roughly halfway through, maybe a third of the way through Chapter 9. Based on steam achievements, there are only 15 chapters, so I'm more than halfway through and will likely not be hitting even 5 hours of playtime as such.More than £5 an hour isn't bad but it's far from good too. This game simply doesn't deserve its high price point - If it was on a large sale - anywhere between £5 and £10, i would more or less recommend it, but for its current asking price of £25, you must be interested in full completion (lots of collectables and achievements), marble physics platforming and... Transformation based puzzles? I guess?

_childDocuments_.review: It really hurts not recommending this game. I love platformers and all kind of indies so I picked this up expecting a pretty fun experience. Sadly, I was disappointed. The game is very repetitive and the gameplay mechanics get old really fast. There are some power ups and puzzle elements that try to keep the game fresh, but overall as the game progresses it feels more and more like a chore instead of an entertainment medium.The graphics are amazing and the soundtrack above average. The story is very childish but the voice acting (although some times too frustrating) is pretty well made and fits the goofy characters of the game.It's an overall mediocre game. The love put into the game is apparent but still, the design of the levels (especially later ones) is very boring and same-y.I would say that you miss nothing by skipping this one, especially at this price tag (currently 30€). I finished it at 7 hours and took my time to get some achievements. For achievement hunters this could potentially last for about 10 hours in total. The game length is definitely not the problem since I constantly felt that this one overstayed its welcome, but the gameplay/level design simply are not on par with the price.5/10Generally not recommended. Recommended only to people that are REALLY interested in this specific game. Otherwise, there are many, much better puzzle platformers out there.Again, I feel bad for not recommending an indie game and I will happily support the developers in their next game (as I have already done with their previous one called "Maize", which I still haven't played though)

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game.  I left it open for a few hours by mistake.  It probably took closer to 4 maybe 6?  I have about 75% of the collectibles, only 3 extras I didn't find and apparently there are super secret ones...Graphically the game is awesome and the voice acting is fantastic. The collectibles are fun until the worlds open up a lot more and again, it just feels like it slows the game down a lot with placement.   This reminds me of the 2D Sonic games.Aside from the questionable design choices, that I personally feel take away from the pure fun, the game is quite good. _childDocuments_.review: I recently played this game for my April 2021 Humble Bundle review, starting at 19.07 in the video below:I would give this game a mixed/neutral review if possible, simply for the price. I don't think this game provides $32 (USD) of value. Imo this is the type of game I would expect to see priced around $10-15. Get it on sale or in a bundle.As for the game itself, Skully is a puzzle platformer where you take control of the titular Skully, a skull reanimated with some magic clay in order to aid in the dispute between a god and his siblings. This is definitely a game you want to play on controller so you can best take control of the crisp controls when controlling Skully.Skully has a nice art style and voice acting. The story, from what I was able to see, was interesting enough. The tutorial section went on about 5 minutes too long in my opinion, I was getting dreadfully bored. But when I got into the second area the challenge picked up a bit and I became more interested. However, I will say that the tentacles in that are seem to have wonky hitboxes and often I would get killed by them when it didn't look like they had hit me at all.Aside from the tutorial not capturing me as much I would also say that the introduction of new forms - while unique - didn't really do it for me. I did not get to see the second form, but the slow troll form did not really improve the gameplay in my opinion. I was enjoying running around fast and manoeuvrable as Skully's marble form, and being forced to use the slow form as extra health made things slower and more boring than they needed to be. His bland abilities - being able to knock down specific pillars and objects to create paths, and the mediocre combat, didn't serve to make playing as that form more interesting. If you like puzzle platformers you might want to grab this on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried so hard to like this game. I mean, it's from the guys who created Maize. But no matter how much I tried, I only wound up with frustration and disappointment. This is quite possibly the most  game I have ever played.The game has charm, I'll give it that, but it is full of physics puzzles and "where the ♥♥♥♥ do I go?" moments. And I'm not talking the good kind like Portal and Half-Life. The physics engine is so bad and scuffed, and the level design so confused and messy that it makes me rage every time I play it. I raged at devil daggers. A lot. But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the level of rage I felt playing DD doesn't even compare to what I feel when I play this. Every minute I played of this game was pure and unadulterated torture. Time after time, I would fight with the physics engine rather than play the game, and basically all of my deaths were from sliding off the edge of a platform that I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blatantly landed on top of but the floor collision is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that I just get forced off and into whatever hazard is below. Or, from trying to jump off of one platform and onto another but some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the dev team decided it would be a good idea to put a bump there and match the hitbox to it as well, causing me to bounce off of it, lose my jump, and die in the majority of attempts to make a SIMPLE JUMP. I absolutely, genuinely despise this game. If you like games that are consistent and challenge you properly with no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that forces you to fight with the game's underlying systems to get anything done, stay as far away from this game as humanly possible. If you like torturing yourself with ♥♥♥♥ like QWOP, Jump King and Getting Over It, then maybe you'll like this game. Or maybe you'll hate it even more than I do because of the scuffed physics engine screwing up 90% of your jumps and setting you back 2-6 minutes for no good reason.Either way, ♥♥♥♥ this game. It had so much potential, but these problems ruin it completely, and words cannot describe the disappointment I feel.Edit: I know it might seem hard to believe that I've raged harder at a game I've played for 5 hours than a game I've played for 1000 hours (I have 1,022 hours in Devil Daggers at the time of writing), but here's the difference between games like Skully and games like DD, Jump King, Getting Over It, Dark Souls, I Wanna Be The Guy, etc. The latter are  to be difficult. They are  to be a mountain of a challenge to get past, so you go in with the mindset that you're in for some hell. The fastest anyone in the world has "beaten" Devil Daggers (getting a certain score) is in the realm of 50 hours. Games like Skully are  meant to be difficult. They're meant to be a fun little story-driven adventure that you play and finish in a couple sittings, maybe more if you bother to get the achievements. When these games suddenly become hard and it's due to faulty programming/design, THAT is the most frustrating ♥♥♥♥ in the world. "Where the ♥♥♥♥ do I go?" moments and physics puzzles are annoying and awful, yes, but those alone couldn't make me yell in rage after only 5 hours of playtime. Dying 50 times in a row to stupid ♥♥♥♥ in a casual game sure as hell can.

_childDocuments_.review: One day, a skull gets washed up on the shore. A funny dude named Terry picks it up and puts it in one of his clay pools. Suddenly, the skull gets infused with some magical power and comes alive. It turns out Terry really loves rocks and needs your help to take care of his family.  You roll. You're a skull, what else did you expect! Movement feels nice and the skull leaves a nice trail in the dirt. There are a couple extra things you can do as well, like jump and climb on green surfaces. It's all very simple and doesn't take long to get accustomed to the controls. But while moving on flat surfaces is a joy, going up a narrow log or a slope turns into quite a challenge. If you ever played anything similar, you know the feeling. Push too soft and the skull rolls down the slope, push too hard and it'll fall off the edge.Stages are basically a maze of dirt and rocks where you need to use your platforming and puzzle-solving skills to reach the end. There are narrow paths, rocks sticking out of the water that require precise jumping and water enemies. The problem is, the rolling skull is not a big fan of water. It hurts as soon as it touches you. There's a health bar and death isn't instantaneous, so one wrong move won't ruin your entire progress, but you better move away fast. The aforementioned clay pools serve as checkpoints and can be used to recover health.Soon you gain the power to create rock golems from those clay pools. Up to three can be created, but you can only control one at a time. They come in three forms. The first one is the brute who can eliminate enemies by hitting the ground, destroy walls that block your progress or push a rock to create paths across the water. Those rocks and walls have a little crack on them, so you know exactly which ones to hit. The second one can double-jump and the third one has the speed. Both can also move platforms, but you'll need to use them together because each can only move in certain directions. While one form holds the platform in the air, the other can jump on it. This turns into a problem if you accidentally drop a platform into the void. They don't respawn, so the only way to fix this is to restart from the nearest checkpoint or get yourself killed. As you progress through the level, you'll reach points where those forms can't pass and will have to be left behind. That's why the pools have a feature to dissolve all forms regardless of where they are.Since rolling on the ground is too boring, you'll keep yourself busy by collecting flowers. Except for unlocking art in the extra menu, these don't mean anything. You can also skip them entirely and still beat the level. A number in the upper right corner shows how many flowers are hidden in the level and how many you've already collected. Getting all of them can be frustrating because you need to collect them and then reach a checkpoint to save your progress. If you die, you'll have to go get them again. Naturally, they're hidden in the most dangerous spots. While there's plenty of checkpoints, you'll constantly decide between risking it all by going for that one flower in the middle of the water or just skip everything. You'll soon learn that they just aren't worth the effort.Unfortunately, the save system leaves a bad taste in my mouth in later levels where puzzles require all three forms. Since you don't know which form is needed to solve the puzzle that lies ahead, you'll be going back to the last pool at least a couple of times. Sometimes you need to use all three and sync their movements. And again, if you happen to die after spending ten minutes setting everything up, all progress will be lost.Camera is usually the main reason behind many unnecessary deaths in platformers. This game had some of those moments, especially in the few levels with a fixed camera where you run from water or lava, but those also have a very generous auto-save. Last thing I want to mention is that the game has great voice actors. Each of Terry's siblings is a little weird and they have funny conversations. Their quarrel is never explained directly and the animated skull never questions Terry's words. He just does what he tells him to do, but you know that something bigger is going on. Cutscenes, however, are not great. Characters don't move and you're watching at pictures. You probably won't get all the flowers on your first playthrough. That's why every level can be replayed from the main menu as soon as you finish it. But what I don't like is the color of the missing and already collected flowers. The only difference between them is the level of brightness; collected flowers have a darker shade that doesn't help in a very bright stage.   Rating: 6/10Reviewed by:

_childDocuments_.review: Skully is a (badly) console ported 3D marble/platformer where you roll a mud filled skull around various 3D environments.The console port is particularly bad to the point of being borderline insulting to PC gamers.  There's no camera follow, you need to manually shove the camera around, which isn't acceptable.  Console peasants like that kind of thing, but PC gamers have standards.  To add insult to injury, if you have any game controllers plugged in, keyboard and mouse is disabled.  This is completely unacceptable.  There's no mouselook, basically the game is borderline unplayable for many gamers.   The developers hamfisted console port here doesn't include any controller customisation, either, so there's no way to work around their epic failure here. While the graphics look pretty good and this might have had some hope as a game, the botched console port renders this unplayable for many and unrecommendable from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game. The art style is beautiful and the design looks great. I love how the game feels and looks. However, that is the only good thing I can say about this game. Only a bit over an hour in and I'm bored out of my mind and very irritated with the game play. I understand this is supposed to be a platformer so it isn't the easiest game ever. But the sheer number of deaths is ridiculous. I can't even enjoy the game because I'm constantly making a minor mistake that ends up killing me because you only have 1 second of health and then you have to restart a mile away. Not to mention it's literally the same thing over and over again. The only thing they do is add an additional mechanism to pay attention to, a different thing to avoid, or a different thing to learn or time. It makes it so tedious and irritating. And this is just my issues with the mechanics. The gameplay itself is outright atrocious. There is nothing to do other than roll a skull around an island and occasionally punch things. It made me feel like I was at work it was so boring and irritating. And don't think the story helps either. The story is garbage. Honestly, the story provides so little to the game that removing the story altogether would actually almost help make the game better. Finally, the actual environment itself, while beautiful, is such a disaster for a play through. As several other people have commented about, there are so many points in the environment where you roll around on a flat surface or nearly flat and then somehow get flung into another direction. There are so many cracks and holes that you get stuck in with no way to escape other than either rolling and dying or restarting from the checkpoint. Which, again, is a mile away. Now that the gameplay itself is out of the way, what about the price? At $30, I cannot recommend anyone buy this. Taking a look at howlongtobeat, this game, assuming you 100% it, only take 16 aggravating hours. Even just 1 hour in, I was already halfway through chapter 3 out of, what I assume is, 15 total chapters. It likely won't take more than 5-6 hours to complete the story and then another 10 to grind through collecting the collectables. To me, $30 is way too much to ask for a game with only 5 hours of actual story and the rest is just grinding. If you like aggravating, slow platformers that you just mindlessly roll a ball around for a few hours and you are have $30 you are burning to waste, go ahead and get this. However, for the vast majority of gamers out there, save your hard earned time and money. You might like it for the first hour but then you'll realize how mindlessly boring, tedious, and aggravating this game is. I feel bad for the developers because it's such a beautiful game with such a great potential but they overlooked some of the basic elements that make a game fun like not putting miles in between checkpoints and not making the gameplay super tedious. Overall, if they lowered the price or you got it on sale, I would say it might be worth it. But just be prepared to be bored and irritated the entire time.

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been a really fun game with just some minor adjustments. It starts out great, but the level designs and game mechanics quickly become increasingly frustrating.The gameplay gradually loses that initial feeling of flow and instead turns into a tedious back-and-forth grind between checkpoints and puzzles, where you have to shape-shift the character multiple times in order to solve the puzzles. You can only shape-shift on checkpoints that are often placed frustratingly far away, and on top of that the shape-shifting animations are too long; just a few seconds, but it quickly adds up to wasted minutes. If you could shape-shift instantly and on the spot it would be so much more fun to play this game.You'll also come across jumps between platforms that must be carried out with pixel-precision or you'll fall to your death over-and-over until you happen to get it right by pure luck, and each time you die you'll have to start all over with the frustrating back-and-forth shape-shifting puzzle you had started before dying.I gave up after 16 hour of play. Life is too short.

_childDocuments_.review: Your main character is a ball, which is really fast and has some fun movements. _childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: The environments look pretty nice, and rolling through them as a skull marble is fun... unfortunately, EVERYTHING else distracts from that and makes the game not so fun to play... Imo, platformers of this style generally need remain laidback, avoid (forced) annoying challenges that bottleneck progression, and ideally present a cast of cute characters that are *not* insufferably annoying. Skully starts off fun enough, and unlike some reviewers I didn't think the action was entirely derivative. BUT as the clunky-handling golems are introduced, and both gameplay and the "story" start to grate on one's nerves, it makes one question why they are playing this when they could be playing Mario, A Hat in Time, Banjo-Kazooie, or many other classic 3D platformers that respect the player and genuinely bring a smile to one's face. Instead of a sort of scowl, which is what I found myself with around halfway through the chapters...
_childDocuments_.name: Skully

_childDocuments_.review: Overall fun little parkour platformer, but the difficulty is NOT consistent.One stage, you'll be rolling along with no challenge, then the very next room, PIXEL-PERFECT-JUMPS-WITH-NO-CHECKPOINTS!The game could do with about twice as many checkpoints or the ability to quick save after performing a complex object setup. It's no fun switching between three golems sixteen times to get your platforms just right, then slide off the edge and lose everything.Skully himself needs an ability to halt all inertia, by pressing or holding a button. There are many times when the game expects you to hit a ramp a fully speed, then land on a much-too-small ledge. Your inertia will send you flying to your death.The escape sequence in Fiona's Chamber is also extremely badly designed - the lava raises to EXTREMELY quickly, the Player has no choice but to skip half the collectables per run. The lava timer should be removed entirely, there is nothing fun about dying 50,000 times in a row.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Maize, and because of that game, i wanted to play more Finish Line Games. i also enjoy platformers and Skully really jumped out to me. Overall, i really enjoyed Skully. The world designs, the graphics and platforming were pretty fun. They can be challenging, but after taking a minute or so to look around it is pretty simple to figure out what to do to traverse the simply beautiful levels. While Skully is not Ghost of Tsushima in terms of graphics, I really enjoyed them and thought it was well done and adds charm to the game. The music is decent as well. Not amazing, but well done. Then I also really liked the story and characters. The game does not go into extreme detail about the characters, and the story is pretty simple, i could not help but enjoy everyone and what they were going through. Then the rolling mechanic of Skully himself. This is not a hard game, but it is not easy either. Some of the rolling traversals were fairly challenging, but fun too. I also enjoyed the 3 forms that Skully can take to help traverse. While not groundbreaking in any sense, the 3 forms were fun to figure out how to use them and help move on in certain levels. You can beat the game in like 6 hours, but if you decide to get every flower then this can take over 10 hours.The hardest parts for me were the half circle ramps at weird angles. I kept getting stuck on the sides and falling off. No biggie, but some of the other mechanics i found were a bit inconsistent. Jumping, making self moving platforms and grabbing onto the vines were the worst. While not terrible, it is something to mention. i would try to jump to a platform and i barely moved. Then I would sometimes disconnect from the vines randomly. And I would try to set a platform to move over a gap and nothing would happen and have to restart at a checkpoint. The other problem I had was it is hard to judge depth in this game. Trying to figure out how to set a platform to make a jump was a challenge. I think I would have it and get to the jump and be WAY off. Some of these problems could be my problem, but want to mention them. Nothing in this game is broken or annoyingly challenging, but I would find myself a bit cross when some of that stuff happened. However, none of this will ruin the game, as this game is a bit challenging and fairly rewarding when you get some of these right. Also the price might be a bit high, but if you want to wait, I am sure another sale will knock it down.With all that said, Skully is a fun and decently challenging platformer with a good story, good graphics, fun mechanics and all around great charm and i would suggest it to any platformer gamer out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey Dev, this is more for you than other purchasers.I took the time out to play this game as I saw it only had 17 reviewers at the time of writing this and I personally would be heartbroken if I spent the time on making a game and only 17 people reviewed it.I thought this game was pretty good, and it has a lot of good ideas.I also played your Maize game but full disclosure I did not finish it. I got to the underground lab and stopped playing because the puzzling got too hard for me.There a few key problems with skully and I think a lot of them probably could have been picked up by playtesters-There are parts where the platforming as the skull is way too hard, I recall a bit in level 3 where I just could not jump over rocks. The game has a MASSIVE difficulty spike in the 4th level with the lilly pads and slashing tentacles. It went from kids platformer to "precision platformer for hardened platforming veterans"-The lilly pads in level 4 are really hard to counter balance, I would have rathered that the skull stayed still on themMy key complaints are as follows: -The game tries to do too much, rather than having rolling platforming and a big knack-like creature, why not just have the one main mechanic-The game suffers from quantity over quality. The levels are very long, but thats not to say theyre lacking of ideas. I think that you could have gotten playtesters to list their favourite sections from each level and halved the length of each level to really condense the game down.-The physics of the skull head is quite slippery and can be unforgiving, making it a bit easier would go a long way.-I would not have put any writing into the game, the NPC that talks to the player throughout the game seems like a major macguffin and his "dudebro" way of speaking really takes me out of the game. I would have rather have some murals placed around the levels that explain the gameworld to me instead. The reality is that you dont need this guy explaining anything to play and get the game, so what purpose does he actually serve?I would still have him in the game, but instead of him speaking, have him gesture to the murals and provide non verbal language.-Projectiles in this game are a bit "thin" is how I would describe it, there are blue blob enemies that fire projectiles at you and it is REALLY hard to see them.-I personally would not have all the flower collectibles. I'm not a fan of lots of in game collectables in general. If a collectible does not tie into the core mechanics of the game, then I dont see the point. I realized halfway through level 1 that they don't have a core gameplay purpose other than unlocking the concept art and stopped going out of my way for them. This is another aspect where you could heavily condense the experience and favor quality over quantity. Rather than having 350 flowers in a level, why not have 10 well placed ones that heavily reward the player for taking the time to explore the levels you've put so much love an care into?-Some aspects of the game are really well polished, some seem very rushed. My key example of this is the lilly pads in level 4 that pop in and out of hte water, their animation is quite janky.-Skully is VERY fast when he rolls, I think that his base speed should have been half or even a third the speed, and the player should have been given a button to boost up.-I found the soundtrack to be well constructed but a bit middling and forgettable. This is another aspect where its better to have risks, have a kooky producer make something a bit different so that your game stands out. There are a few games where a producer by the name of Calum "Bo En" Bowen creates the soundtrack and he really makes them memorable. The games he puts his name to are PikuNiku, Lovely Planet, Voyage, Omori, Snipper Clips. His risk taking approach to soundtracks pays off almost every time. Those sound tracks stick with you-The textures used are quite heavy handed in their specular value, which leads to objects seeming "shiny" "plastic" or "wet" this can lead to giving a stock unreal or unity engine look.The game has some great positives though- The character design is cool and cute, I like skully and his other versions, I like the enemies.-The animations for this game are quite good, the attention to detail where the big mud hulk lifts his head and spits out skully is cool. I also like how the clay in skullys hed disappears as he gets lower health.-I found the game very fun when I wasn't getting frustrated with a bit of jank. My favourite bits are when you get to speed around as the skull, bounce off of walls and get chaotic. What I would have found really cool is if you stuck to the vine grabbing sections like glue (and didnt have to hold left mouse) and could speed along them, a bit like a wall run from action platforming games.You might balk at this, but I genuinely think this game could have gone on another tangent and been a golf game instead.If players were able to putt or kick skully from the start and then have a limited amount of influence over how skully moves after being putt, I would have enjoyed the platforming a lot more. Obviously the difficulty of the platforming would have really needed toning down, but it would have been something different that makes the game memorable. You could have then also changed skully to be on fire or something for putting at the blue monsters to pop them.All in all, you have done a great job with this game, good on you for finishing two games now. Take a grain of salt with what I'm saying because obviously you've made two games and I've finished none. I think because you are an indie dev it would be better to just condense your content down, take some more risks and "follow the fun". Because worst comes to worst you've made something that doesn't work, but you'll learn from it.Having more condensed levels probably would have helped a lot with people finishing the game. I would argue that its better to have 70% of players finish the game and say its short than to have 10% of players finish the game, as that means a bigger chunk of players have given up before getting to experience all the ideas you spent time and care on.By the way, I am a big believer in making improvements to your game post-release in response to feedback. No mans sky has taught us that changing your game post release does actually work. Also if you're looking for a volunteer playtester I'll put my hand up lol

_childDocuments_.review: While obviously a lot of effort went into making this game, across my playthrough I didn't come across any major blanders of bugs. Unfortunately, the result is still somewhat bland. I'd give it a "it's fine" score if that was an option. Unfortunately it isn't, and since the price tag is high I'll go with a no.The story is very childish, and not in a good "whimsical" way, but in a boring, pedagogical one. It reminds me of  the worse side of today's kids' cartoons. The music definitely doesn't do it any good. It's painfuly bland and repetitive. After 30 minutes it got so bad I just played without it. The camera also felt very crippling at times, when quick angle changes had to be made, or the game locked you into a certein uncomfortable angle for a scene. If the gameplay was a 10 I'd forgive all of this, but it's more like a 6 or a 7. I liked the controls. While they could definitely be improved, they generally felt solid and smooth. The gave has very few, basic mechanics and it tries to make the most out of them, resulting in levels that are at times reptitive and include backtracking. While not awful, I can't find anything particularly great about it. It's just... meh. Definitely not worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Acquired in Humble monthlySkully is an interesting mixed speed platformer.Gameplay: you start as a high speed scull brought to life with clay and will quickly learn that water is VERY harmful to you, as you progress you will gain access to three golem forms to use. each of the golems have unique abilities, one has the power to fight, break walls and even throw the skull a go distance. One can sprint for a long jump and move platforms, and the last can double jump and levitate platforms.There are three boss fights and the fist and last fights what you need to do is fairly intuitive however the second one i needed a hint for (hit him with the skull). The skull when outside a golem can roll and cling to some walls (that have been marked in-game as climbable), when rolling Skully will accelerate (and thankfully stop) at speeds that rival Sonic, the top speed is not too shabby either. this can make the precision platforming tricky but once you get used to it you will find that skully is actually easy to control on narrow sloped surfaces above pools of lava!The levels have a linear design and flow with few branches for collectables. however some backtracking to and forth between the last checkpoint and the current (optional) collectable may be required.There is one type of collectable and there is a lot of it, used mainly to guide players on were to go it is also used to unlock the art in the extras part of the menu.The game is best played with a controller (mouse and keyboard are supported but may struggle in some sections)My biggest complaint about the game is the Camera, it is fully manual and defaults too low to the ground. the latter s fixed by a quick nudge of the right stick, but the former can cause some serious problems and almost made the volcano escape section unplayable (devs please add a automatic recommended viewpoint mode)play time: I was able to finish the main story with 75% of the collectables in about 10-16 hours (steam failed to record my hours played correctly so i am unable to give a more accurate number)Story:I was not expecting to actually get into the story of the game, but I did and it worked into the gameplay very well, even repeating the last lines said if you die as they are being said. Each of the five spoken characters are unique, although you only truly have any significant interaction with Terry.Graphics: Beautiful but not to the point of distraction or obscuring anything important. Important things usually are easy to spot and can even stand out. no visual glitches spotted. cut scenes are a little jarring at first as it is a mixture of smooth movement backgrounds and minimal movement foreground. this appears to be intentional (at first i thought it was a playback problem) and even helped ramp up the excitement at some points! Sound: Music is good and fitting. The spoken dialogue is clear such that i did not really need to use the subtitles! Final Verdict:A hidden gem of a platformer with only a camera that has to be positioned manually at all times to complain about.I recommended Skully to those who like platform games

_childDocuments_.review: A very unpolished game with some nice environmental art. I spent most of my first hour jumping from platform to platform with no additional mechanics or challenges. _childDocuments_.review: What can I say, it's a fun game with lots of different racing styles and tons of roads to explore.  Just be sure to get some offroad tires before taking to the dirt, I missed that little bit and nearly pulled my hair out trying to get a podium finish LOL. Cons?  Well, I don't think it has an offline mode for days when the internet is down.  Also seems to rain a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Game itself runs terrible. I am on a i9-14900k with 4090 ti, 2 tb of NVME, 64 gb of DDR5 Ram, best of the specs. Crashes constantly, no cross play, they limit you cross regionally, no online players for online races waiting up to times of 15-30min for races. AI difficulty cannot be changed so you are forced to use meta cars and even then good luck. Played this for roughly 30 hours and have not ONCE seen either a real player or AI car free roaming but they claim its a MMO. During races if you drive on a road you haven't explored it won't count unless you are in free roam. 99 Cars but its more like 4 variations of the same car. This rant is to show that I have played TDU and TDU2 as a kid and loved them so much. This game is a terrible execution as a SEQUEL to this established franchise. They copied other game structure like Forza Horizon with having you do just races and open world speed traps. The only pros of this game is so far better graphics, driving physics, engine sounds, and the headlight/turn signal feature is still there from TDU2. I feel that this game was rushed and also lost its essence of what it was. If you want to make a MMO competitive racing game that is fine, but using the name Test Drive is just not the right choice. I was looking forward to this game since it was announced to drive with my buddies, fantasize a luxurious life with my collection of cars and houses, and have a good story presented in front of me. Instead I feel alone, lost with the progression, and not making any impact when all races give the same amount of money yet the cars get more and more expensive.
_childDocuments_.name: Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown

_childDocuments_.review: - Very poor PC performance. Out of luck if you can't support DLSS or FSR and enjoy more than 10fps (developer insinuates this is a problem affecting only a minority).- Inconsistent AI difficulty. It seems to scale with player skill(?) but results in either opponents leaving the road on the first corner, or able to drive as if on rails in a car with seemingly higher stats. Losing a race reduces your already small reward.- Characters emote (and look - in some areas) as if they're from GTA IV.- Music selection sounds as if from a royalty-free site - including a hip-hop remix of a classical song you'll hear way too many times.- Progression results in grinding previously done races many times for a small reward if all other side challenges have been completed.- Very obvious meta of AWD vehicles being objectively better than 2WD vehicles, reducing the amount of viable cars from an already small overall selection.- Far smaller map size than TDU/TDU2, and fewer features than predecessors and competitors (Horizon, Motorfest).Post-launch support is promised, including the return of previous TDU features (housing/casino/motorcycles/Ibiza). However the game in its current state cannot be recommended - with or without those features.
_childDocuments_.name: Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown

If you are selling a 'service' instead of a 'product', the service has to work. I don't care how early it is or how hard it is to make a game. If things don't work out, at least let us know whats going on.So far this looks like a refund speed run for meEDIT: I retried the connection thing for to long to be able to refund. After ~5h i managed to do ~6 races. Of those races at least one is not counted as completed. If you like PAIN this might be the program for youAlso it says "Single Player" on the store page. I did not find any way to not allow random players to join my race. So either thats just a false label or a issue with some hidden setting?

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to start by saying, no the game is not perfect but it is also not NEARLY as bad as the negative reviews make it out to be. I have almost 6 hours of play time as I write this and have had only 2 instances of being disconnected from the server. Sure its annoying but what do you expect from a new online game in 2024? Its nothing compared to say the Payday 3 launch which was completely unplayable for several DAYS! I see people complaining that the game is "Always online" well ya duh, its advertised as an MMO. Thats liking being mad you need to be online to play WoW. People are forgetting to realize this is a relatively small studio that is making a game that is more ambitious then most AAA studios. With the sometimes buggy servers and ill be honest less then great optimization this game is more fun then Forza Horizons 4 & 5 or any of the newer Need For Speed games. Like I have said its not a perfect game, I have some pretty bad fps in certain areas, even with a pc that handles FH5 on ultra and a constant 60fps. But since yesterday they have already improved the performance. So far on day 2 of playing for around 3 hours I havent had a single disconnection from the server. There isnt nearly as many cars as Forza and the cosmetic upgrades are laughable when compared to NFS. THIS IS NOT A PERFECT GAME. But it does not deserve this level of hate. The "story" is boring but name a modern racing game that had a good story. The Character customization is bland but who cares you see your character once for 10 seconds after a race.Some things about this game I like is the progression, you dont just get given a free lambo for winning a race like in Forza, you really have to grind and work towards the cool stuff! The Ai is competitive, I play FH5 on unbeatable with no assists and I can beat the AI while blindfolded. This game I actually lose sometimes! Its refreshing! I play a mix of controller and wheel, both play great! For my wheel I am using a G923 and its so much better then the wheel in FH5! Traffic density is better then FH5, you get on the highway and you get to actually swerve in and out of traffic. I swear I will play FH5 and go 15-20 minutes without seeing a traffic car. The map is so much more interesting then then the flat boring map that is Mexico in FH5! I dont mean to keep dogging on FH5, I like FH5, I have hundreds of hours in it, a collection of over 1,000 cars and in game balance of over $100,000,000 . But im comparing how bland something made by the massive AAA studio that is Turn10 is when compared to what a much smaller studio is doing, there will be growing pains. You are going to have bugs, its 2024 you wont find a single new multiplayer release that has a smooth launch its never going to happen. Do not give up on this game or the devs. There is so much potential for this game, its not bad! By all means wait till the 12th and buy the standard addition and by that point im sure they will have ironed out some bugs and odds are there will be a bunch of new ones! I give this game a 7.5/10 I hope that with some updates and little bit of new content in the future I can give this game an 8 or maybe a 9/10 I think it has that much potential. As of right now though it is just a fun and slightly buggy car based MMO with good controls, an interesting map, and a very addictive grind

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the state of the game as of 11/25/2024. I have a deep understanding of the game and its mechanics so I can tell you exactly why this an objectively- not subjectively, objectively- badly designed game- and in theory it wouldn't take much to fix it- given time. Perhaps to your surprise I'm also not going to call it a bad game. Many of my subjective takes on why the game is bad have little to do with the countless specific gripes (often understandable, TDU2 was a very specific thing for people) various TDU2 devotees have placed it on a sadly understandably lofty pedestal to achieve. Most of them aren't even adjacent, in fact, so if you're interested read on.The OBJECTIVE reasons this game is bad:-AI: THE biggest objective reason why this game is badly designed is the way the AI fundamentally works. Even if they added all the Forza Horizon-esque features people seem to want out of this game, you will always be facing AI at some point, no matter how many are playing the game. So your AI needs to be beatable. Sane. You can argue particulars on that but the AI is neither of those things. They have taken measures to make it better since launch, but the AI is currently very, very good in MOST measures at being a good opponent- except the one that matters most- pacing. If an AI car gets in front of you, it will apply what appears to be a multiplier to what it is allowed to do compared to the upper limits of a human driver, up to a factor of 2. It's a crude way to describe it but it's as far as I'm concerned the most apt way. The AI, especially over longer races, will get better and better at its job, and that multiplier is only infunced in your immediate vicinity where you see it otherwise. This is absurd, objectively bad design, and needs to be fixed as soon as humanly possible. This is not speculation so much as it is observation paired with literal interviews, by the way, they have literally admitted the AI is capable of twice those limits in interviews. This applies to all races, without exception all the way up to and including Crown Jewel Ruby, a 69.7 mile race takes over 39 minutes to complete under the most ideal human circumstances- the AI will frequently run it as low as 32.-Race rewards: Giving the exact same amount for every single race, regardless of length/difficulty, is an bad design choice, objectively, for any purpose you would use it for in a racing game. Every race starts with a base of 15000 payout, which, sans first time bonus, will net you between 10000 and 27000 extra. Once you have done everything, this is what you're left with. It's absurd and given they bill this as something they're effectively building into a racing MORPG (there's no massive, it's instanced), you need varied rewards to incentivize players to play and compete. The only exceptions to this are the Crown Jewels, which you get at the very end of the game and pay out from 50000 to 22000 (meaning the most you will realistically ever make from a single race is 380000). As if to add insult to injury, doing the race more than once in a day PENALIZES you. You will get diminishing returns for each successive same race you do in a 24 hour period.The above have been mentioned ad nauseum and I doubt many people will find disagreement that those two factors alone are beyond damning for the game. They need to be fixed before I could in good faith give the game a passing grade.That being said: Let me opine on the good for a bit, for there is much! Note I never said this was a bad game. In every other respect, it had an audaciously rocky launch (which I observed major fixes to within a few days of the 'early access' week) that has slowly been on the uptick. -Physics: If you do any amount of research on this game you'll no doubt find blooper clips of cars flying into the sky like a player in Skyrim hit by a troll. Practically gone are those days. They've been running a fine-toothed comb through their map and I seldom find a place where this now occurs. it happens, but it's not going to ruin your race unless you're already driving poorly. Add to that the handling model- which is generally a fine line between arcadey and realistic, but with real-time weather that syncs to the server time and actively influences your car's handling, as well as nuance on road conditions the extends so far as 'it's night, your car will have less traction' and 'that puddle will make you regret turning in to slowly to that corner.' It's no Project Cars, but on the whole it's damned convincing. These are pretty much live 'track' conditions, for all intents and purposes. This is also one of the only open world racing games that actually DOES this, It makes joyriding immensely fun, and fast speeds appropriately dangerous.-World design- This is, without question, the most complicated map ever recreated on a 1:1 scale. I looked it up for good measure, it is a safe bet to say HKI has far more roads to drive than Forza Horizon 4 and 5 combined. The foliage is constant, lush, incredibly detailed and destructible, no part of the city outside of the hotel feels low-poly, and racing down the road I daresay this looks like one of the most photorealistic racing games on the market, easily. Is it photrealistic in place? Not so much. But you will always feel exactly the sense of speed you should as the ATD rush by.-Wheel support- With the glaring ommission of proper support for 900-degree steering (I would recommend 360 or 540 at most), this game has excellent and fairly customizable wheel support. It instantly recognized my G920 and H-Shifter and the game works wonderfully with the presets out of the box.-Sound design: Barring some glitches that have cropped up on occasion, the sound endpoint is among the best I have seen in a racing game. Cars sound closer to Forza than Gran Turismo- they have very natural sounds to them, and while many of them are unified, it all sounds right. Little details like blowoff valves, the game sounding fundamentally different when you put the top down, the various sounds of the city... it's all there to thoroughly immerse you into your time with it.Now we have to get into the SUBJECTIVELY bad:-This is a TDU game, but it doesn't feel like one: probably the most common complaint. I would point out TDU1 was drastically different than TDU2, and much of what I've seen people gripe about is planned as future updates. They're very valid gripes. This isn't Drive Club. This isn't Forza Horizon. This game is in the TDU franchise and with that comes an expectation that currently just isn't met- the social features are incredibly lacking to nonexistent outside of races, about the only place you will see other people is in the customization area and rarely the hotel, and there is zero reason to engage with the world around you outside of racing or joyriding. You can indeed test drive a car you don't own, for all of two minutes. But there's no glue keeping the community coming back in that sense, and the events give you meager cosmetic/sticker rewards, never anything meaningful.-Matchmaking: my gripes here are unlikely to be similar to others'. I have zero problem with facing bots in races so long as they're good. I don't even have a problem with the total lack of playlists, fundamentally. The problem I cannot abide here is that there is no indication outside of a tiny icon that anyone is... *anywhere*. You don't see "insertnamehere" is starting a race, you have x time to join them, which would probably be the easiest fix to the lack of lobbies. Given the excessive need for POI travel, trying to roam in packs often fails, too. Online almost ends up feeling like an afterthought, rather than the core thing. Just the Sharps and the Streets that you can join at level 12 (which allows you to basically gain a guaranteed 50K every day you play if you're a Sharp).I'd like to opine more... but Steam review character limit. I'd say I got 95% of my point across anyway so.......

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game has potential to be good in the future, unfortunately I cannot recommend it in its current state.I didn't even know this new test drive game was coming out until I saw it advertised on steam, so thought I would buy the gold edition to get early access. Having fond memories of playing TDU2 when I was a kid, I had high hopes for this one without (naively) doing any background research. I tried to load the game on the first day of pre-release, and couldn't play as the servers were overloaded. This could have easily been alleviated by the game not being always online.When I finally managed to access the game on release day, I couldn't do any races as it would time out, so spent the time exploring the map, which was fun as Hong-Kong is a nice place to drive around. I think the best way to portray my experience is with a pros and cons list.Pros:- Driving mechanics are enjoyable for an arcade racer- Initial progression is fun, gaining large amounts of XP for completing certain races, speed traps, and using different cars Unfortunately, i cant think of any other pros after being sat here a couple of minutes racking my brain... Onto the cons...Cons:- Always online, and the forced interaction to be social with other players. Loading the game always starts you in the 'Solar Hotel' where you are forced to leave your room (cant fast travel from here) to a lobby full of other players. Personally, I prefer solo experience but each to their own.- Cant (currently) purchase houses in different parts of the map. The only progression is you get better suites at the hotel as you progress in levels. These suites cannot be customised. This also annoyingly means you always spawn in at the same spot on the map- Limited car selection in game other than supercars and hypercars. There are other categories of cars, but they all have a limited selection of cars, so you end up just choosing a meta car rather than one you like.- The racing AI... unbelievably bad. When you start a race, the majority of the time, the AI cars aggressively launch to the left and drive into walls. The rubber banding of the cars is either the AI aggressively launches and drives off into oblivion, beating world records on the track. The flip side is the AI drive so aggressively that they continuously spin out, crash into walls, crash into each other, crash into you... Also, you cant change the AI difficulty which seems to be always set to expert.- Wet track... soooooo many wet tracks with no access to wet tires. This means most of the meta cars are 4 wheel drive to prevent spinning out all the time. Its not as bad on the slower cars, but when you get to super car, the constant wet tracks become annoying. This then discourages you from using 3/4 of the high end RWD cars.- Car physics are terrible. Clip a kerb and you flip out like a toddler throwing a hot wheels in the air. Hit a tree, and you get severely slowed down whilst AI blissfully breeze through with no penalty.- Variety of races is poor. No championships with multiple races. All just single car type single track races. Would have been so easy to allow different classes on the same track, or have multi track events.- The coins you earn from races are painfully low. You initially get around 15,000 coins a race, which jumps to around 30,000 at end game level. To put into perspective, the top end hypercars cost 10,000,000+ coins. This is roughly 333 races to afford that. That's roughly 16.5 hours of racing just to afford 1 Bugatti...- Graphics optimisation is a joke. With my RTX 2080 super & I5-12600k, I can play MEDIUM settings @ 1080p to get 60fps... In comparison, I can play Forza Horizon 5 on Ultra everything @1440p and still get 60fps... Due to this, it has made the game less enjoyable as the car textures load in sporadically, the LOD is so short, cars and bushed pop up out of thin air right in front of you. I know its not all about graphics, but this really takes away from the immersiveness. Obviously this wont be an issue with a top spec rig, but important if you have a mid/low end rig.- There are clans you can join and race for. this whole mechanic seems like an afterthought by the developers to try add an element of story. It fails. You earn clan XP in specific races to then race clan 'bosses'. You defeat the boss and earn... a sticker and an item of clothing... they could've given cool boss cars or monetary reward but nope... a sticker and a hat...- Bugs galore... I am on 99% road discovery progression but cant get to 100% because driving on certain roads doesn't register. Likewise, I have driven to the same dealership and meeting points 5+ times, and they reset to undiscovered once you reload server. Annoyingly, this is in one area of the maps, so if you want to do a race there, you're in for a treck.- All the car dealerships are nearly identical, same layout, same style, same size, lots of empty space and some weird futuristic looking design. Its the same experience going to buy an alpha mito as it is a lambo.- Nothing really to do past level 60. I reached level 60 and was excited that I finally reached the level cap. Once you get there, you are given lots of new challenges to do. These consist of... complete 100 races in x car, complete 100 races in xx car and repeat over and over again. I get its a racing game, but there is not much else to do other than race after a certain point.- Crown Jewel races that you unlock after level 55. The longest one is complete a 44 minute race. I got 10 mins into the race and disconnect from the server... Additionally, when I finally completed it without disconnecting, I came first and only got 110,000 coins, when the description says 220,000.Despite the looooong list of cons, I have enjoyed the game to some extent, but this felt like a Beta that needs an extra year of work compared to a fully released £69.99 game. I hope the game does improve with future updates, but for now I will be putting it down until something majorly changes. Back to Forza Horizon 5 and Gran Turismo 7! :)

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid TDU enthusiast, playing these games since I was about 6 years old, I couldn't wait until I heard the news that TDUSC would be reviving the series as a now-23 year old. After having played this game, I am just so thankful, and overall amazed at how the new developers at KT Racing stayed mostly true to what made the old games great. I do believe that there is a TON that can be improved, and that's to be expected with almost every new game that has come out since 2015 - especially when the greedy investors are breathing down the publishers/developers throat. But overall, my play-through on TDUSC has been overwhelmingly positive.Here are my Pros and Cons as of playing the game since early launch:Pros:- I believe that this game truly lives up to what makes TDU, TDU. Everything from the car selection, the vibe, the music, the map - this game ticks almost every box of what made the TDU series great imho. Granted, we do have some missing features like houses, online/offline capability, lack of diverse dealerships, storefronts, etc., but thankfully some of these have been announced to come in the upcoming roadmap for TDUSC.- Car physics, if you have played the previous TDU games, are easily the best in the series. The cars no longer feel like the 'bricks' they did and TDU2 and have some weight to them unlike the first TDU. It is fun to be able to drift, and correct the car from the slide - which was virtually impossible in TDU2- The depth of the map and the selection of things to do are endless, and we actually get rewarded for just simply 'driving,' unlike previous TDU games. I think it is a nice mechanic to be able to receive XP for discovering more parts of the map. I also really enjoy the tasks that the developers gave us to receive money and XP for driving a certain amount of miles in a particular group of car - very neat!- This one might be controversial, but the PC graphics overall (with the exception of reflections on certain cars) look spectacular despite the backlash we see online, and I have 0 issues running the highest settings.- The depth of the map and the amount of things to do are endless. That is one thing that TDU will always be known for, and TDUSC delivers on that promise spectacularlyCons:- Don't mean to kick a dead horse, but launch day was a disaster. Thankfully, I did not suffer for a long time with the server issues. But I resonate with those who were affected, and it is always upsetting when we cannot get online after having paid extra to do so early on. But I am glad it got mostly sorted out!- The AI is near impossible to beat, and it is easily my biggest gripe with TDUSC. Especially once you start to hit higher levels. The level of rubber banding, and cheating from the AI, and how they beat online leaderboards is something that needs to be worked on. TDUSC takes the 'crown' for having the most unbalanced AI I have ever seen in any racing game. Nothing comes close. I am always up for a challenge, but it makes progression very hard until you begin to unlock certain tire selections, which isn't until level 25-30 or so. - The game is obviously unfinished, but I can't blame the developers. It was upsetting to see the lack of features the game released with. Houses especially. _childDocuments_.review: Test Drive is back! Had some doubts before release, and the initial performance was a tad underwhelming, but that was quickly forgotten once I found some settings I was happy with. The game ticks the boxes. The driving strikes a comfortable balance between realism and arcadey, the sounds are fantastic, the IRL spec options for the cars are brilliant, and the map is very much a Test Drive map: expansive, detailed, and an absolute joy to cruise around. A lot of my time so far has been spent exploring every corner of it, and burying the pedal in the carpet on a long stretch of coastal road brings memories of the first TDU flooding back. I feel like I'm sat in front of my XBOX 360 again, pushing that rental Audi B6 S4 Cabrio to its limits as I take in the map for the first time. That's whassup.DualSense support is a welcome addition. Feeling the brake trigger fight my finger as I load up the front end and ease off in a trail brake is great fun.The car list, although relatively small, feels much more "curated" than that of any other open-world racing game. Almost like a selection of the greatest hits, as opposed to Forza filling the game with utter bloat for the sake of having more cars. Always Online isn't a problem until it is, and I struggle with the occasional crazy fast race AI driver, but I feel that Solar Crown absolutely nails the fundamentals of a Test Drive game. Worth the wait!

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game.  The graphics are great.  The cars seem nice.  The driving physics are absolute rubbish.  AI cars corner like they are on rails, and you're lucky if you can get the car to turn at anything resembling regular driving speeds, let alone going fast (as if you're in a race with other people).  You can't do a clutch kick, because there's a 1-second delay on you pressing the button and the clutch in the game actually responding.  You can do an e-brake slide, but then you're sliding on a sheet of ice with zero traction.Unlike previous Test Drive games, where you could actually drive without being wide-open-throttle, and shift up/down at your leisure, this game makes you be in the optimal RPM for peak torque/power at all times.  I would not recommend this game, unless you are a glutton for punishment.Update 10/07:I really miss a lot of what made the Test Drive Unlimited series enjoyable.  It wasn't just a racing game, you had "fares" to pick up and deliver places, vehicle delivery missions, and various other things to do, besides just racing, unlocking all roads, and finding "barn" cars (Hello, and welcome to a poorly done fascimile of the Forza: Horizon series).  The "police" in this game do absolutely nothing, there's no such thing as traffic lights and traffic that follows any type of driving laws, just a bunch of cars cruising around.I miss driving to the dealership, choosing what trim of vehicle I want to purchase, then driving to the upgrade shop and seeing what my upgrades did to my car (eg, visual aesthetics: Saleen conversion on the 2005 Mustang GT).

There's no connection to road. You cannot feel when wheels will start losing grip. Small bumps can send you into space. No weight transfer.* ALL FWD and RWD cars understeer like pigs and then snap in high speed corners. None of these cars would pass basic EU safety tests - they are death traps. AWD cars are the only ones that are even remotely controllable. If you want to be competitive and win races, get only AWD cars.* Brakes are made out of cheese. Often the only way to stop is to smash into something. Grass patches stop cars better than brakes.* Car selection is weak. With this few cars in the base game, they still locked some of them behind premium paywall on launch. And when races require specific classes and power levels, there's usually only 1-3 cars to choose from for each race.* AI is terrible. Bots have super boost out of the corners, while ignoring race trajectories to keep up with their pre-programmed lap times. One mistake means you will lose the race, because bots are always cheating. building gap means nothing.* Difficulty changes based on your results. Time trials and some intro races will be very easy, then most others will be against cheating expert level opponents if you keep finishing in top 3. You cannot adjust anything manually. If you want to win specific race, finish the race in last position on purpose few times, then race against easy opponents again.* Progression is not thought out or tested. It includes a lot of grinding the same few races. Just driving around island in free drive, unlocking roads and looking for few collectables is more interesting XP grind than repeating same race against cheating bots. I don't like, when game throws lots of rewards at you, but the grind for XP and money here is a bit to much. * Optimization is really bad, while the game looks mediocre.* Traffic cars randomly pop in, sometimes right into your car. Both the ones that drive on road, and the ones that are parked around the map. AI racers sometimes will drive right through them. * Some things break when you smash into them, some don't.
