_childDocuments_.review: **Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown – A Frustrating, Incomplete Mess**After sinking 32 hours into *Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown*, I can confidently say that this game is a colossal disappointment. What was marketed as a grand open-world racing experience turned out to be a lag-riddled, unoptimized mess that leaves you more frustrated than entertained.First off, the performance is abysmal. No matter how powerful your setup, the game consistently struggles to maintain a stable frame rate. Lag spikes are so frequent that they become part of the racing experience, forcing you to anticipate stutters just as much as you anticipate turns. The map itself is a joke—it never fully renders, leaving you driving through an ugly, low-res environment that feels more like a game in early access than a finished product.Worse yet, Solar Crown’s insistence on being an online-only game is a massive mistake. Why a racing game—especially one that should be focused on high-speed, precise driving—needs to rely on constant server connections is beyond me. Server issues frequently result in lost progress, rubber-banding cars, and races that become unplayable. For a genre that’s supposed to deliver fast-paced thrills, being tethered to unreliable servers completely kills the immersion.The biggest offense is that this is a racing game. The essence of racing is precision and timing, both of which are compromised when you're constantly fighting against network lag and server disconnects. Not everyone wants to race online, and forcing players to do so just alienates those who prefer a single-player experience. Why make a core mechanic—driving—depend on the state of your internet connection?At 32 hours in, I can safely say that unless the developers address these massive performance issues and re-evaluate the need for online-only functionality, *Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown* isn’t worth your time. If you're looking for a smooth, enjoyable racing experience, there are much better options out there that actually let you play the game without constant interruptions. Save your money and wait for this one to (hopefully) get fixed—or better yet, avoid it altogether.

_childDocuments_.review: Horribly disappointing game that suffers issues that most neglected or fast franchise racing games have suffered from since 3D racing games became a thing. The launch server issues are negligible to me as those can be fixed. My review is on glaring issues the game itself has at its core mechanic. There is a lot of good here; a lot, but for everything good there are 3 or 4 things that are bad. The open world design has returned from previous Unlimited Series titles including shops, map discovery, and fast travel points. The downside of this is the map feels lifeless and small. Realistically this may be a bigger map than Oahu, but it just doesn't feel like it. It lacks the feeling of scale and liveliness the previous games had. Even the more recent Need for Speed titles managed to make an interesting and believable map. Traffic randomly disappears (and reappears in front of you in some instances,) the buildings and streets just feel washed out, there is just something missing from it all and to boot it really does not look that much better than TDU from the Xbox360 era. It is Doom 2 with Ray Tracing aesthetically. The cars feel and look great. Like previous titles, the care in the detail of dashboards, door panels, interior controls, and other finer details its phenomenal. The cars feel "weighty," accelerating and decelerating can be jarring, traction can be lost, all of the things that make driving interesting. Plus!, there are a lot of ways in which to upgrade, update, and change the performance of your ride by either using a preset or even making your own for specific events. All of these things they have done and done well. The problem is none of it matters. Not one bit of that matters because like the opening statement, developers more often than not simply make the AI or races uninteresting. Unlike  Need for Speed Undercover where the early game is real easy and the later game is near impossible, TDU Solar Crown let's the player know right away that the learning curve will be high and anything less than perfection will result in a loss. A perfect example is the early D 550 races. This class system (which isn't ever really explained) should give the player a sense of the type of difficulty of this race. A player going in with a stock early game car might be able to win this race, but it would be challenging to do so. As a player continues to get used to their car, the game mechanics, and learns about upgraded parts as well car loadouts (cross-country, dynamic, rain, sport, etc.) they should be able to return to this race while meeting the requirements and feel more in line as an experienced racer with a better car. You will not. You will be met with AI that has been ramped up to match your level despite this being a beginners race, with cars that out perform your own even though you are at the Max 550, and unless it is 5th place and below, will never make a racing mistake. It isn't a complaint about making the game easier, but an observation on how nonsensical the AI actually is. There is certainly a learning curve for racers picking up this game. Learning the follow the racing line, not pressing the accelerator or brake to the "floor," learning to feather the throttle, things that might be more familiar to Sim racers than Arcade style racers. If you do not teach yourself how to properly drive you will certainly find yourself sitting at 3rd or less, but this isn't about that. Yes, with enough time and talent you will consistently place first, but the needle's eye is far too narrow in my opinion and the AI seems as nothing more than marker going around the track at a set perfect pace rather than another racer or machine. These rubber-banding AI mechanics of racing game isn't challenging or fun, it doesn't test the players cognitive or skills, promote learning the physics and mechanics of the cars; its just poor (maybe even lazy) design we've seen in so many forgotten racing games before and that is heartbreaking. Test Drive has never been on the cutting edge or miles above its Arcady counter parts like Need For Speed or Horizon, but Unlimited did bring a good feel to the genre that wasn't so arcade-like as NFS and not as overbearing as GT. For many of us, TDU was near perfect. This game makes the attempt, but ultimately turns into a dusty cough of its former self.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: It's now been 8 days since the launch and I still cannot progress the game past the initial tutorial race. 3 days ago the support team told me that the reset will be processed within 24 hours. It's now 72 hours later (3 days) and I'm still at square one. It's also 1 day after the official release so I've essentially paid for early access but got a big fat middle finger from the whole TDU team. This is hands down the worst experience I've ever had with a video game.It's a bit sad that this is my first time writing a review but the whole state of affair has left me saddened. I understand developing a game is a difficult task and that getting everything working from the get go seems rather impossible nowadays. And I'm pretty sure people are aware of that.But the lack of communication to the people who PURCHASED early access and the fact that for the 2nd day now, people are not able to log into the game, let alone play it, is not acceptable. Yesterday, I was unable to log into the game. I kept getting connection errors. After the team supposedly released the fixes for servers, I was at least able to get into the queue. However, after sitting in the queue for minutes on end, the connection would just drop resulting in the same error. More than 2h out of my supposed gaming time were spent trying to log into the game.Today, in 5 out of 10 tries, my game is stuck on "waiting on proxy". Thanks for the fixes I suppose? When I do actually get into the game, I cannot do anything other than free roam because after completing the 1st tutorial game, the game just won't progress. At this point, I dunno which is worse, waiting for something to happen, or watch at the constant "waiting on proxy" message. Maybe the game is indeed waiting on a proxy, who knows.Whatever, I'm a patient person and I will wait for the team to fix the issues so that we can all enjoy the game we've been waiting on for so long. BUT if you're here for the "driving" more than the "racing" hear me out.With the last update things are starting to look good. With recent changes to steering wheel support I felt obligated to say something. Force Feedback and driving in general feels pretty good now (Moza R5). If you're the type of person that wants a solid blend of arcade/realism this is it. In general, a little better than Forza Horizon IMO. I really enjoy just driving around. Each car feels unique, the sound and visuals are really solid and the roads offer pretty engaging driving all around. Almost everything else kind of sucks though lol. There's a lot of little things but here are some heavy hitters. Its a grind to get a solid fleet of cars, which I think would be fine if there were more ways to earn revenue besides races. The time trials are okay but the races suck. Mostly because I like closed course racing and this game does not offer that. In the city you're forced to choose between a clean racing line or avoiding medians with metal fences, bushes, trees, etc. The problem is the medians and bushes slow you down significantly. This alone is not an issue. The fact that cars on the same line aren't effected as much, paired with the AI breaking physics, introduces unnatural variables that I don't particularly like in racing.Also just wish me and my friends didn't have to jump through hoops to drive together. Definitely better now than at launch but still weird sometimes.Overall I think if the devs stick with it, we'll have a really solid game that hopefully leads to future solid games

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game, I played the betas and had loads of fun. Sadly the game turned out to be a complete disaster. I was holding off from reviewing this until the patch came out, in case it would fix some of the major issues of the game, but it really hasn't... This review will be updated if later updates end up fixing any of these issues.Let's start with the positives. Freeroaming is where this game is at its best. It's really fun to just drive around, the handling feels nice, the map is nice to drive on. I couldn't get my controller working with this game, so I used my keyboard, but the cars are still perfectly controllable, so I don't mind that.But it can't be all perfection, you have to go through the races too and that's where the hell begins.At the start of the game, it's quite easygoing and the AI doesn't give too big of a challenge. Eventually the game decides the fun time is over and throws the maximum difficulty AI at you and you will be restarting races A LOT, either due to the AI ramming you off the road or the Huracans or Taycans flying away out of reach from you. It's even worse when there is no actual restart option outside of time trials so you have to quit the race, enter it again and wait for the matchmaking to end (99% of the time you will be racing on your own anyway) and hope you won't get rammed off the track again. There are also many very questionable decisions made when creating these races, for example when you unlock slick tires, many of the races you get have forced rain, so you can't even use them. Another strange occurrence is supercar races that go on dirt roads. That would be a funny one off event, but there are so many of them it becomes frustrating.The economy is one of the worst I have seen.Whenever you finish the race, you get from 20k to 30k credits, which is alright for the first half of the game where the cars you buy cost under a million. Freeroaming gives you a very good amount of credits from collectables. Sadly the rewards don't increase when you unlock higher level races, so when the game forces you to buy high end cars, some cars can be completely out of reach for you. There are also some anti-grinding methods set up, so if you complete a race 5 times, the rewards will be cut down significantly. FRIM returns from TDU2, but you are limited to 10 uses per season (I think, at the start of the game there were 10 uses and now that the season has started, it has reset), so the maximum you can get from it is 1 million, which isn't even that much considering the car prices. Some cars are so expensive that it's impossible for anyone to buy them at the moment.The car classes are so unbalanced that you may end up buying something that is completely useless, and you can't even sell cars if this happens, so you will be forever stuck with your mistake. Of course this is not a problem for those who bought the silver or gold edition, as the DLC cars are some of the fastest in their class. And even the silver edition was not without its issues, for a long time the DLCs didn't even work for those who bought it, so they couldn't even use those cars (I preordered the base version and it took until the first patch for me to get the GT, at that point I had already beaten the supercar races, so thanks for that)I got to a point where I unlocked the hypercars, but was several millions away from the cheapest one (I bought some cars for fun but turns out I wasn't meant to do that) so I'm basically stuck until a decent money making method comes up. At every unlock cutscene a money reward is mentioned, but I have never received any.Then there's the server issues... Well you have heard of them so I'm not going too in depth to it. This game is a perfect argument against online-only games. Everything that can go wrong has gone wrong, and making the game playable offline would fix so many problems I don't understand why it hasn't been done yet.If you still want to play this, get one of the special editions to get some of the useful cars, and only buy the cars you need, maybe that way you can actually beat the game :))))

_childDocuments_.review: Second Edit: 20 hours in, I think it's time to make a fair review of the game. First of I'm going to say that I will still play the game despite there being more cons than pros, simply to see what the game has to offer until you complete the "Story".Pros:Audio. The sound is the best thing about this game. It's outstanding and revving your engine is different in every single car, which brings me to the next point. Physics. Every car feels different to drive and there's a remarkable difference in the physics when you tune your cars. The cars are also much more likely to slide when it's wet and raining. Graphic. The game is pretty and the cars look quite good. The biom is not that different when you compare it to other racing games in the same genre (Forza Horizon, The Crew etc) Time consumption. I actually like the fact that you can't get the best cars from day one (maybe some people can) but you have to grind it out to purchase the cars you want. They don't hang on the trees. Cons: Multiplayer. The world feels dead. I have twice, in 20 hours raced against another person and a few times seen people drive around in the world. This is a shame since the game is online-only and the devs have cut several great features from their older games (being able to purchase houses to increase your garage size because "it felt like a single-player experience"). Clans. There's two. You can't create your own. Again, a huge missed opportunity. Imagine being able to drive for your clan, earning your clan points so you can upgrade your clan to maybe unlock cheaper car parts, cars, higher earnings in races etc. But you get nothing of the before mentioned. You can drive against 4 or 5 clan members (NPC's) and that's it. Car styling. It's very limited. The biggest deal breaker to many will probably be to many, that you can't change the hood, roof, spoiler, skirts, lights or anything else to make your car stand out. I don't know if it's a license issue or what not, but other big games can do it, so it's a huge let down and a big missed opportunity to not have it in the game. The only thing you can do is to change the livery of your car. This works quite all right though.AI. You can't change the difficulty of the AI. It adjusts after your driving skill which would be a great feature if it worked properbly. My AI opponents is at expert and they are either very fast (depending on the car) or quite slow which brings me to the next point. Car balancing. It would be nice if you could actually drive your favourite car within the game and still be competetive but guess what? You can't. There's a must buy car in every race category if you want to be competitive. You can't fine tune your car either, there's some presets you can pick from but who knows, it might just be a skill issue you could say - until you look at the global leaderboards - which are all dominated but a single car in every category. Misc. Game still "crashes" when you shut it down. You get an error message and is asked to submit the report. Traffic. Randomly spawns and despawns. Again, seems to be coded quite bad. I haven't counted but my guess is theres 15, maybe 20 different cars in the traffic. It gets VERY repetitive very fast. Will edit again some time in the near future.  Edit: It's nice to see that the devs are involved with the community and are giving the players a compensation (my guess will be in-game credits) but it's now day 5 and I'm not able to finish a single race without getting a connection error. 3 days in and the connection to their service is still garbage. So glad I bought the gold edition so I could play earlier... The game should be called Test Drive Unlimited Server Clown instead. Will change my review if they fix the server issues before the official lauch and theres some kind of compensation to those of us who bought it early.

Looking past the graphical mishap - it seems fairly un-optimised, character models seem weird and voices seem AI, or very robotic-y, i don't know if that is what they were going for but its jarring and weird. Map and area is really nice and actually really detailed - however, they have this always online mode - i cant just race in single player, it has to be online, multiple times, races and events crashed because it lost connection, its so moronic i cant even comprehend why they would do this, at least give us the option. My god.Anyway, i managed to get 1-2 hours game time in before i was kicked from the server, then put in a queue out of 700 to get back into the game, nice one, thanks. After waiting ten minutes in this queue the game went down for server maintenance, i get its advanced access, but for the love of god, this is a limited amount of the player base who was foolish enough - like myself - to get the gold edition. When the full release comes out and you have 5 times the amount of players getting on, their servers might just implode.I'm willing to give it some time and see if things improve, but its just a shame, a game that was so promising through development and then has a start like this is just tragic, i cant believe this wasn't seen coming.True shame.Edit - After further playing the game, yes things have improved however, the game feels so flat, the map feels empty, almost all the time. _childDocuments_.review: This game delivers a very grindy experience and is nothing for the casual player who just wants to play a few hours per week.For the ultimate TDU SC experience I highly recommend to play the game with a wheel and pedals because every car feels very unique and the driving physics are very fun when you turn off all the driving assists. Try the game with a Fanatec, Moza, Thrustmaster or Logitech wheel.Driving with a wheel makes the TDU experience complete, just how it should be played and not with a controller which offers you no force feedback at all.You gotta embrace the grind and work for each car by putting hours and driven kilometers and miles into the game so beware that you are not getting anything here for free.The game overall runs fine on my rig in 1440p with max settings but I have a RTX 4080 in my system, so I can not complain and always have over 85fps stable because I locked it to that number.The server in the europe version is also causing no issues anymore for me at all, nothing to complain here as I am writing this here in november 2024.Of course the game experience is far from complete in 2024 and many things are missing from the old TDU series but if you get the game via a cheaper method via key or in a sale this game can offer a lot of hours and content.The map is well made and offers a great feeling for freedom without it getting boring after a couple hours.There is still room for improvement on the endgame experience that is for sure but give the game a try and do not be guided by too negative comments or videos. Make your own experience and see if you enjoy it.Especially cruising around the island and mastering the cars when driving with a steering wheel and pedals offers a very rewarding feeling.You can simply feel how you improve over time and get better and better.If you enjoy to improve yourself, grind and love collecting cars, then TDU SC will keep you busy for many hours!Go give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm really enjoying this game when I didn't think I would. There are major issues, most notably the AI being badly difficulty balanced (please fix this as a priority devs), but there's so much love and care under the surface with this game I think people are missing.The map is amazing, the sounds and car modelling are great, lighting is actually better than people make out, and most importantly the physics are really, really good. The cars all feel distinctly different and have better or worse handling in specific areas which is something I can't say the same for with games like Forza - it really adds value to the vehicles when they are each so interesting to drive. _childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of racing games since I was a kid one racing game I fondly remember was the Test Drive Unlimited series of games, and when they announced Solar Crown in 2020 I was thrilled to play a Test Drive Unlimited game again. Playing Solar Crown has left me disappointed and wondering, “why did they release the game in this state?” and “why did they have to make the game like this?” I have a few complaints that I'm sure many if not everyone is experiencing in Solar Crown. The elephant in the room everyone is talking about is the always online aspect of the game. One way this function effects game-play is when you are doing a race with only AI and you have a… ‘skill issue’ there is no restart option for the race. Because the game was built around online only and you racing with other players there simply is no option to restart. The only way to do so is finish the race and retry it or completely abandon the race and restart from the beginning. My next issue with the online only aspect of the game might not be irritating for some but it is for me, every transaction in the game that you do such as buying upgrades or cars has to go back to the server and then confirmed. This could take up to 5-10 seconds which may not seem bad but when you are doing 10 or more upgrades on a car its quite annoying having to wait for the server to verify the transaction, this again is an issue with the game being built around always online. There is more I could write about this but that's just my main gripes. In terms of missing content for the game my main thing is the fact that there is no player houses, casinos, and variety of clothes stores that were prevalent in previous instalments, instead we have to resort to the Solar Hotel being the player home and the one single clothing store in the hotel. I know there is a plan to release this content in the future but this should have been content that was there from launch. Time to address the game-play aspect, for one the handling mechanics of the game are for the most part fine except specifically slow speed turning, the cars turning circle is very large making it difficult to make tight corners. The off-road part of the game might actually have worse handling mechanics, After watching AR12 Gaming video on his opinions it seems we both feel the same way about the off-road handling in Solar Crown. While trying to turn it seems as the cars do not react properly specifically the suspension as the off-road cars feel stiff and not using the suspension properly. When cornering the under-steer makes it near undriveable and its even worse at slow speeds, I would most of the time e-brake drift to take most corners on the off-road races. I will keep this last part short as this is a long review but graphics and optimisation… optimisation, there is none. On PC this game is just not optimised and even with my PC having better specs then whats recommended I can run the game 1080p 60fps on medium settings. The fact that I would have to sometimes go all the way down to low settings to run the game when there was server issues. My theory which was also said by AR12 because the game is running with cloud computing server issues may affect individual performance of the game which would explain me forcing to reduce quality when server issues arrived. Overall I really want the developers to bounce back from this disaster of a launch and have a game that is great to play not ‘has potential to be great to play’. Because of the current state of the game I could not justify paying the 57 dollars CAD for it I would wait until they can fix the issues with the game and missing content.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the idea, after three hours, but they clearly ran out of whatever it was they would have needed to polish off these visuals and clean up the performance. It runs horribly for looking worse than the last two Forza Horizons and NFS Unbound. I'll probably give it a bit more time and some patches before swearing it off for good though.The driving is inoffensive but not great. Speed loss from basically everything, including tiny bushes, which are everywhere, is heavier than in any game I've played previously. That wouldn't be a problem in a better performing game with better opponent AI. That's not this game. I have no idea how they're programmed, but I feel like every race is either a close finish because I skidded once, or no contest because 2nd is a full minute behind. No in between. And both the fancy car you play in the intro and the starter car felt janky too, in very different ways.If you've played any racing game with a player character creator in the last several years, you've played one with better models than Solar Crown, though the facial customization and hair textures are decent enough. Most disappointing are the on-foot sections, which feel like a guided VR tour tech demo. They went first-person in a game with costume creation, which you quickly realize is just, yet again, cheapness since every surface in this game is reflective and not a single mirror shows your model as you *glide* around clumsily. They designed this fancy, luxurious hotel, but it's too soulless and empty to create the atmosphere they were clearly targeting, and you don't feel like your character is even there.It's yet another game that could've been cool with another year, more money, and no competition. Too bad, because I find the high-class race context and city setting more convincing/compelling than Horizon's relentlessly perky, fairly ridiculous festivals.I hope they turn it around, but I don't know that that's the trend in this genre. It wouldn't be cheap to fix.

_childDocuments_.review: After an additional 21 hours and the resolution of some previous issues mentioned below, I still have a hard time recommending this game for the following reasons::The graphics aren't spectacular, even on ultra, which is a shame because the appeal for the car enthusiast segment of the market is to see the cars represented in all their glory. : The handling is decent, but at times feels too floaty and at others feels too stiff. You wont notice this most of the time but I've personally found it difficult to judge corners and how various obstacles (which the game often encourages you to plough right through) will affect your cars momentum and grip. It feels like a departure from other racing games I've played, including Test Drive Unlimited 2, and other titles like Juiced 1 & 2.  The game features several unskippable custcenes and obstacles to getting to the gameplay. Every time you log in, you start in a hotel on foot, from which you have to walk down to the lobby before you can access the map to fast travel, or traverse the lobby to exit the hotel to get into driving mode. This does not take long, but does still delay the time it takes to get into the action. Furthermore, there is a waiting lobby before going into a race which requires you wait at minimum 10 seconds. There is no option to restart a race, you either have to abandon it and go through three loading screens and at least a 10 second delay, or finish the race and restart from the finish menu.All in all, as it stands right now the negative reviews fairly accurately represent my experience with the game, and I only continue to play because I'm a big fan of one of the cars in the game and being able to "drive" that car makes up for the issues, but most will not have that kind of consideration, and thus I still find it difficult to recommend this game to the average consumer.The issue with the pre-order DLC has since been resolved with the late release of the DLC a week or so after the release of the main game, so I've struck that section from the original review. If you still find yourself interested in this game, installing it on an SSD is a requirement, not a suggestion. If it's installed on a Hard Disk Drive, regardless of your PC spec, it will most likely massively lag and stutter to a degree that significantly impacts the outcomes of most races.As a final point, I share the frustration of many players that this is an always online game that will likely become unavailable to play once the developers decide to shut the servers down. For me there are reasons I purchased this that likely do not apply to a majority of players, and which more than make up for that fact, however it's something serious to consider and is in no way consumer friendly.

_childDocuments_.review: - AI Always CheatingFirst of all, you cannot change the difficulty of each game, and the AI cars feel cheap—like they're cheating. You'll get stuck in your progression because the AI drives erratically, coming out of nowhere, and since you can't adjust the difficulty, it becomes frustrating and not recommended.- Poor Steering Wheel SupportI'm using the MOZA R9 v2 + SRP pedals with an automatic gearbox: when pressing the brake pedal, it automatically shifts to Reverse gear (R). _childDocuments_.review: Review in progress, 11hr in on launch day 9/12.TLDR: , yes, it feels rushed/shorted in a few areas, but with player support and time, it has potential to be exceptionally solid. If you like simcade urban racing, with some great rallying as well, and need something new and high quality, this is it. To me it's like NFS 2015 but with actual physics, not spreadsheet-lookup fakery.  If you can't live without MTV lifestyle influencer dollhouses in your , you will be disappointed. 80+fps Ultra settings on my 5800x3d and 7900xtx, when locked at 60 it has never dropped a frame or hung/snagged. My call to action is to keep the reviews constructive and support the dev team however possible to give the game a chance to build from this moderate state - DO NOT 'Concord' this potential diamond in the rough.Full comments below.About me:I've been playing racing games since Al Unser Jr Turbo Racing on NES. I own almost every Gran Turismo, Forza MS 6/7, Horizon 3, 4, 5, many NFS titles, all three PCARS, and have played hundreds more through the years. I played dozens of hours of TDU on PS2 and PSP, then dropped the series completely after an hour of TDU2. When I learned of the development on TDUSC I was more excited than I think I've ever been for a new racing entry. A few favorites: PCARS 2, GT4&7, FH4, NFS 2014 Positives:The most important part of a RACING game is GOOD driving physics and feel. TDUSC has it in spades. I spent multiple hours on an XB X/S pad, Dualsense, and T300rs wheel and all three feel FANTASTIC out of the box, the only thing I changed was mapping the shift buttons on the pads. Cars feel planted, lose traction progressively and predictably, and react to physical stimuli remarkably realistically. There is no BS 'behind the scenes' table running things like every Need For Speed game ever, and everything feels incredibly realistic compared to Forza Horizon's coin-op nature. The cars of TDU bump, jiggle, bounce, rise and fall exactly as they should. It's like Gran Turismo level physics on the street, just more forgiving, and drifting is a thousand miles better than GT on both controller and wheel.The highlights of the presentation include smooth, consistent performance, incredible foliage density in the jungles, limited draw/pop-in, a realistic sense of speed, and great lighting (forests especially) and exciting sound design. Again, BDE hardware here.The map is enormous, as per usual for a TDU. Traffic is appropriate for a street racing game (gridlock is NOT fun or conducive to racing), and the world overall feels like it could house the next Watch Dogs for how dense and detailed it is in general. The GPS works well enough, and there are tons of little pieces of candy to pick up along the way everywhere you go, if that's your thing.The 'plot' is very limited and so far only serves as locked gates for progression. You have to interact with some NPCs now and then as directed, then get back on the road.Tuning is very streamlined though uninteresting, and the game provides many quick-build sheets to unlock and an auto-tune tool if a car is above-spec for a race.I have found the competition/difficulty to be challenging and fun. Some are complaining that the AI cheats or rams a lot, etc., which I have not experienced. Compared to the mindless slot car, 50,000lb ramming tanks of Forza and GT AI, these guys are respectable gentlemen who will sometimes take revenge on you for your own bad sportsmanship XDNegatives:The visuals overall are not very impressive and feel a generation behind. The game engine is an in-house development, and just expresses the underdog/AA status of the developers, so they deserve a little bit of slack in my opinion. As a total package, the experience of driving in the game is still shockingly immersive, moments like slipping and sliding on dirt roads through light and shadows, and the realistic density of little touches and details help to make up for this slightly dated look. I know performance is comparatively rough for a lot of people, but it's seems overblown. Almost every game that hits PS5 runs at 30fps upscaled from 1800p or less, and yet somehow this single game gets lambasted for running 40fps on a GTX1060... Come on man... It is not exceptionally well-optimized, and hopefully they can grow into this through updates, but the expectations seem to be quite unreasonable or imbalanced from a lot of disreputable reviewers/commenters. Interior locations and NPCs are very disappointing to behold, especially when the interface forces you to walk into and throughout dealerships, nightclubs, and tuning facilities. It's kind of nice to experience these tasks through more than just a text menu, but it's not well executed. The voice overs are also poorly written and read/directed.The tuning process is lifeless and nothing more than grinding to unlock generic upgrade tiers that you then just blanket buy/install on every car. There is nothing I find appealing about the plot or characters - This is nothing remotely close to the same galaxy as a good NFS Underground adventure... or even FH. The Solar Crown is a broad competition(?), that feels like it was supposed to be a festival, but there's zero evidence in the world in or outside of races. There is no interactivity or characters in the races, just an opponent 'clan' that shows up in some races where you compete directly. It's completely superfluous, but contrasted with the garbage that was in TDU2, this is a MASSIVE improvement. It's also odd how diverse the NPCs are for an island that's 85% Chinese in reality... lolAside from assist settings, there are no difficulty options - I don't know if the game adapts on the fly to your performance, or if it just gets harder as you level up... There is a low emphasis on finishing first anyway, so not sure how much my per-race performance matters anyway.The network status is shaky. I got d/c'd a couple of times and the one 'live' event I saw failed to even let me try to enter it, just glitching out in the HUD. I saw other players in game on the map and out on the streets, but didn't interact with any, nor attempt to race anyone directly - so I cannot vouch for that process at the moment. I saw this game as a solo experience anyway.I have experienced a lighting bug caused by fast travelling to indoor locations - it causes the lighting outside to completely break and makes the game unplayable without closing and restarting the game. The solution is to simply ONLY fast travel to the OUTSIDE of any facility with an indoor component, then manually enter. The bug is already on the list of urgent fixes with the devs. Closing thoughts: Paid $60, I played this game for almost 11hrs straight on launch and regret NOTHING. I think the base experience here is exceptionally satisfying to drive and explore. It gave me urges to travel, explore, and drive in the real world, because it felt so dang real in the game. The racing, even in entry level cars, is fast and exciting in ways I haven't felt in a long time. So many people are complaining that the 'soul' of TDU is lost in this game because the lifestyle-sim elements are basically completely absent. The problem for me is that, that experience was thoroughly, disgustingly cringe-worthy and irritating. It was the worst of Reality TV filth portrayed by inept VAs, and it completely ruined TDU2 for me. I DO NOT need any of that trash in my RACING GAME experience. This is a series about succeeding as a fledgling sports car driver and collector - Look at Goodwood if you want to see how such people present themselves. If it were a true street racing underground situation, look to F&F, GTA and NFS for how it should be handled. This aspect of the series has never resonated with me, and the vitriol the core that apparently does is deeply concerning to me as a gamer... I look forward to everything on offer here.

_childDocuments_.review: *Post 1st Patch Review.God i hope i can change this in the future to recommended but even following the 300+ bug fix and performance patch TDU: Solar Crown is in a sorry state of affairs.Seeing the Test Drive Unlimited name in such a mess honestly breaks my heart. I spent hours upon hours in TDU1 and 2 loving the social life aspects of the game, the offline mode. The delivery missions, salons, tailors, houses and personal garages so on and so on and i was hooked on it, even after Atari decided to hide the bikes behind paywalls before removing them completely (yeah don't think i'm going to forgive you for that one Atari as i bought the bikes). This took up alot of my early 20's and got me back into that "Arcade" like racer having been hooked on the likes of Race 07 and RFactor, i met some epic folk whom i still hang out with to this day all through TDU.I wanted to wait until post patch to review the title as i still had a burning hope that the current ship could change direction and sail into a prospective future and a rebirth of the franchise but sadly this is not the case. Before the patch we had major performance issues, for example if i want to run higher than 1080p then expect to drop my settings to low/medium at best and still... the fps is not ideal, no i have not got the best system in the world but against the likes of GTA V and other large open world games TDU:SC lacks any sort of optimisation for the PC platform (even though i hear console is not exactly much better). Frankly for a game in development for as long as it was and being a new 2024 release you would have expected something that looks like it has come straight from the Xbox one/PS4 era it would at least run without an issue on a modern system, this unfortunately is not the case.... and this is just the icing on the cake.The Always Online system has reared it's ugly head post patch, I would love to comment on the AI to see if that has changed in any shape or form being before hand they either never turned up and racing was just an easy run or you had a field of Michael Schumachers, there really was no in between but I cannot comment if there has been improvements simply because the servers are failing and you cannot connect to any races... so yes we have a "racing game" where it's actually impossible to race... go figure.We move on to the "Clans" system next. Basically as soon as you hit level 12 you are forced to join a "Crew" (either the Sharps or Streets) and earn "Respect Points" through racing and beating opposing clan members. So far it's the most one sided thing ever with the majority of players already have chosen one side meaning the folk who picked the other side will never win any of the weekly events already making the game unbalanced. The only numbers that should dictate the outcome of a racing competition should be number of wins not how many players are in a clan. The casino in TDU2 was a fun side thing, the Clans are not.Car handling has never been TDU's selling point but as janky as it was at least it was fun, stupid but fun however SC is just horrid. 4WD cars will just suddenly break traction at high speed with only the slightest input of turning throwing the car into a powerslide and oh boy if you start to lose the rear good luck getting it back without coming to a dead halt.RWD cars just slide, "Oh is that a slight corner and your going over 50? let me just step the backend out for you buddy". There seems to be no feeling or torque at all, its just power... no power with little to play with inbetween. I can imagine this is a lot easier on a wheel and at somepoint ill try myself but for us mere controller players... my soul... it hurts.Don't know about FWD cars yet, mainly because i've not bothered to get one.BUT WAIT!! I HAVE A POSITIVE THING TO SAY!!The off-roading is pretty fun and handles pretty well, so hats off and Kudos where it's due. Now can we have that but for like... all the racing? Please?Annnnnd back to the bad bits. So there were (according to the devs) 300+ bugs ironed out in this patch, seems a bit excessive that it was released with 300+ bugs in the first place and personally i have no idea what the bug fixes are, being only 7 are listed on the dev blog.The "Performance enhancements" have granted me a wonderful +2fps however i have noted their is much more AI traffic on the road it seems to perhaps there have been some improvements, certainly not in terms of the AI behaviour though.. they are still driving like they just had a good few hours at the Jack Daniels distillery and in some cases some AI just forgetting what a road is completely.The game overall for me personally anyway seems empty. Test Drive Unlimited by name but that is about all that ties it to the original. The social aspect of the game is almost gone. For now no houses, nowhere to store your cars, no extra side missions to generate cash such as my personal favourite delivery missions, boy i enjoyed them. Fair enough its hard to get a social thing going when your always online platform spends most of it's time offline but yeah unfortunately so far it really is a disappointing title. I held out for this patch to hopefully bring back even a smidge of that fun from my early 20's but alas there really isn't much more than there already was on release.... well technically less since the servers are derp'in and i literally can't do racing but TDU: Solar Crown is a shell compared to it's predecessors. I am still holding a glimmer of hope that Nacon can turn this around but I certainly am no longer holding my breath.Looks: 6/10Sound: 8/10Physics: 4/10Game play: 4/10Replay Factor: 2/10Always Online: -50000/10Overall: (so far) 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: **I am purely recommending the game due to my love of the franchise, read the friggin review to decide if its right for you**TLDR- Im having fun and thats all that matters. so this is obviously a first impressions review as its still in pre-launch, I will not go over any of the multiplayer or seasonal events as the game hasn't officially released yet so the only people playing are die hard fans and idiots like me who don't learn their lesson from pre-ordering.  First and foremost, this game IS NOT forza horizion, you dont get **** for free, you have to work for every little thing (though so far the payouts are much better than in previous games), its not a casual game, the AI goes from laughably easy to completely impossible and you cant adjust it so far, so if you are looking for an easy arcade racer keep looking.  The good.-graphics look great (see the ugly for more on this though)-very interesting map, plenty to do-decent car list (but many duplicates, typical of TDU)-car sounds may not be accurate but they sound good-solid customization options-good driving physics The bad-laughable character animations and voice acting-everything locked behind a rep level, no more grinding to get a veyron at level 1, you must drive crappy cars no one really wants to drive for hours just to drive a corvette-baffling amount of overlooks (I.E. not being able to adjust difficulty, day one bugs, etc.)-always online, i know this has been beaten to death but it just shows the devs dont really love this game enough to turn it over to the modding community to give it a real life, it will die when the devs say it dies.-8 player lobby max,  seriously why?  its 2024 and we are stuck at 8?  this is just lazy.The ugly-this game is not optimized whatsoever, if you don't have at least 16gb VRAM you CANNOT play in 4k no matter how fast your card is, not that it matters since the game is so poorly optimized you wont get much over 60fps anyway.  don't get me wrong the game looks good, but not what I would expect from a game that takes 15.6GB of VRAM at 4k.  I don't want to drag this on forever so I will use my own computer as an example.  I have a 7900X3D with a RTX 4090, with DLSS ON max frames at 4k is 60-70 with constant dips into the 40s, do with that what you will. -devs have big plans but they specifically noted only the first few updates will be free so its pretty easy to see where they at least want to go. overall I am having fun with the game but im worried due to it being a small developer that it wont get the attention required to make it an actual contender again in the genre.  Time will tell, if you are risk averse and poor dont spend your money on this yet.  If you have money and still havent learned to wait and see how a game actually is before you buy it then jump on in!

_childDocuments_.review: Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown had the potential to be a standout in the open-world racing genre, but it's unfortunately bogged down by severe technical issues that ruin the experience. One of the biggest drawbacks is its unreliable connectivity. Players constantly face disconnects, and servers often aren’t synced properly, meaning you can’t even play with your friends, which is a huge letdown for a game designed around multiplayer interaction.Even worse, in the middle of races, players frequently get disconnected, causing all progress to be lost. Imagine being in a thrilling race, only to be booted from the server right before you finish—it's frustrating beyond belief. These issues seriously damage the game’s playability, and the developers have yet to provide a fix for this major problem.Given these persistent connectivity issues, I would strongly recommend not purchasing Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown at this time. Until the developers can stabilize the servers and resolve the synchronization problems, the game simply isn’t worth the investment, especially for those looking for a reliable multiplayer experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could have recommended this game, as I have very fond memories of TDU2 on the PS2. However, unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game currently. When you take into account the many server issues, the unbalanced AI with no manual difficulty adjustment, the general horrible driving feel of the game and horrible optimisation overall, I simply cannot recommend TDU Solar Crown to anyone in its current state. There was a LOT of potential for this game, with a significant amount of hype surrounding it. For a game that was in development for six years, there are far too many unpolished aspects to be ignored. This game should have been held back for AT LEAST another 2 months to have internal play tests to sort out server hiccups, optimisation issues, balance the AI, etc... Why would you release a product that is unfinished when you've seen how poorly that has gone down with other games over the past 4 years?A very big negative point to look at is also the horrible vehicle handling. There is no way of personalising your vehicle tunes to make the car react how you want it to react. Personally, I prefer a darty car that turns in quickly with a bit of over steer. But most of the cars that I have driven in this game understeer like crazy unless you take the corners far slower than the AI are taking them on the same line, or you have to slam on the handbrake to get the car to rotate, which also costs you a load of speed. There is no predictability in the handling, and you can take the same racing line twice around a circuit with a vastly different result both times you take the corner. Then there is the objects on the race circuits to consider, such as the metal fencing, bushes, trees, etc. which in best case slow you down 10 to 20 mph if you brush them, or in worst case can reduce your speed to 40mph or below in 2 or 3 seconds whilst the AI goes ploughing on through without being effected. When you play Solar Crown, it feels like the devs have taken all of the GOOD parts of TDU2 and just... thrown them away. Its so beyond disappointing. I was waiting for this game to release for quite a long time, expecting good things. And all I got was yet another taste of bitter sadness as yet another beloved game franchise has been ruined by a company that is more focused on money than providing a good game for its loyal players.I probably don't need to talk about the "always online" aspect that literally *no one* asked for or wanted. A needless feature that causes more trouble than good. We should have the choice as to whether we play online or offline, and we shouldn't be kicked out of a SINGLE PLAYER RACE AGAINST AI because the servers can't cope with the fact that we want to drive at more than 2mph. It is also unbelievably stupid that we cannot restart a race due to the always online aspect. Who in their right mind thought that was a good idea? There are many, MANY other things I can talk about after just 6 hours of play time. Mostly negative with very few positives, if any positives at all. I was really excited to play this game, but now I regret pre-ordering. I wish I'd just stuck with my gut feeling and left it until a few days after release to see the reviews of streamers and youtubers. My overall feelings about Solar Crown is that I've been left thoroughly disappointed and I feel that the game is lacking the charm of TDU2.TLDR: Too many negatives to count, the game isn't worth playing in its current state. I was massively disappointed when I started playing. I won't be playing again until major updates have been released.

_childDocuments_.review: TDU Solar Crown is an enjoyable game that shows a lot of promise! Pros (+)Fantastic Progression: Unlocking super or hypercars requires considerable time and effort, which adds depth to the game and makes you care more about the cars you drive since you've invested time in acquiring them.Intriguing Map: The game features a map filled with hidden paths and collectible tokens for XP and money. Boasting beautiful coastlines and extensive highways, I would rate the map an 8/10. It's perfect for casual driving as well as for racing (and it's significantly better than FH5). The upcoming addition of Ibiza is an exciting bonus!Great Car Handling: The cars strike an excellent balance between arcade fun and semi-realism, with noticeable differences in handling, depending on whether the vehicle has RWD or AWD, as well as the settings for ABS and TCS.Unique Car Experiences: While the car selection is way to limited, each vehicle has its own unique characteristics, including detailed interiors and realistic sound effects. You can quickly turn on headlights, use your blinker, or open and close the windows, which greatly enhances the immersive experience.Decent Tuning Options: Customizing your car through sport and dynamic modes is enjoyable. Although some presets may be less effective and most of the time you just pick Sport mode or create your own tuning setups, which offer a wide range of options.Open World Exploration: TDU Solar Crown excels as an open-world game, rewarding players with lots XP for discovering the map. This encourages exploration of its stunning coastlines and hidden spots. Driving to a dealer is also cool although this was done better in TDU 2 having an actual BMW or Porcshe dealer would have been way cooler and the dealerships look a bit to extreme and all have nearly the same design.Car Interiors: Having the option to change interior color is awesome, some cars have lots of choices when it comes to interior colors while lots of cars are missing some real interior colors but it is still a nice personal touch to your car. Races: Racing can be an enjoyable experience, although many are annoyed about the AI on Expert level. whilst they are sometimes annoying be beaten with the right car and strategy, you can outsmart the AI. At least the challenging AI adds a layer of difficulty, ensuring you don't always 100% of the time finish in first place. Also not having a Rewind button like in FH5 is good because if you screw up you will most likely lose the race but this makes you wanna get better at the game and not just kind of cheat your way to first place.Cons (-):Limited Car Selection: The game’s roster could be way more extensive. For a car-centric game, having only two BMWs and five Porsches is very very disappointing. Fortunately, the developers have announced plans to expand the car selection with upcoming updates. Ferrari and Lamborghini have more options, but it would have been nice to see them focus more on other car makersCar options: Interiors aside you can't do much to your car besides a couple of different Rims, Tints etc. There should be spoiler options, side skirts, exhausts, bumpers... there should also be BBS rims etc but at least they have a couple of different factory rims unlike FH5 where you only have 1 factory RimServer Issues: Frequent crashes during races can lead to a frustrating loss of time and progress and sometimes the AI mainly when having other online players in the race Rubberband which is very annoying!Poor Optimization: While sometimes the game can look beautiful most of the time the game looks like a 10 year old game which is not that bad because not everything is about graphics but the game has terrible perfomance when considering the graphics. If the game were properly optimized which hopefully will happen I would expect 2x as much fps considering the graphics (only get 80-90 fps (2k resolution) on a RTX 3080 whilst games like FH5 which are amazingly optimized and look way better and run with way higher FPS)Online: max lobby size in free roam is about 8 players I think which is quite bad considering the big map and for a new game, there is also no Cross play which is also quite bad for a new game Always online: I don't think I have to explain this oneConclusion:TDU Solar Crown is worth it and has lots of promise, but it requires significant improvements, especially in car variety and Server/FPS performance. That said, I still recommend the game as is, as it offers countless hours of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: As with many soft and hard reboots, sequels, requels, remasters, spinoffs, prequels, and remakes symptomatic of the creative bankruptcy and sickening risk aversion of vast swathes of the entertainment industry as a whole, Solar Crown is yet another entry on the now very long list of titles that really should have been a new and entirely original IP.The  reason this game carries the TDU moniker is to entice the inbuilt fanbase.Having said all that, I was actually more than happy to overlook many of the game's flaws on account of not having anywhere near enough open world racers. In the end unfortunately it just became overly frustrating trying to enjoy it, here's my top reasons why which are by no means a complete list of my grievances.- This is a live service game, but it feels woefully empty. In my 20+ hours with it so far, I have raced a human being twice, and it was just little mini challenges. The so called  proper 'ranked' races have been impossible to populate. Multiplayer functionality hilariously seems to have been a bottom priority. Why was this made live service???- AI is all over the place. They blatantly play by different physics sometimes. Or they just crash for no apparent reason at other times. This game could well have the worst driving AI I've ever encountered. I do not exaggerate. There isn't even an attempt to hide the dodgy way they behave.- Somewhat grindy from the beginning, however once you hit rep level 30 its like a brick wall with regards to progression. Money and reputation payouts become comparatively miniscule. It is apparent that the game's economy and progression systems were tuned specifically for live service style play. Get on the hamster wheel. - You cannot sell cars. Take it for a test drive before purchase, but once you pile on some upgrades it'll handle radically differently than where it started. Don't like the changes? Too bad. You're stuck with it. It takes literally hours of grinding to make enough money to buy a different ride. Live service hamster wheel!- The game is optimized very poorly, and doesn't look anywhere near good enough to warrant such poor performance. - My lowest class car is the most fun to drive by a significant margin. Every other class of vehicle I've unlocked so far, despite my best efforts at tuning and messing with settings, all handle much worse. I'm sure there's cars in these categories with better handling, but I can barely afford to buy one of each let alone try multiple. Hamster wheel.At a guess, it'd take maybe 10 more hours for me to unlock the final tier of vehicles,  and I can already tell I won't be able to buy the one I really want unless I do even more grinding. Most of these 10 hours would need to be spent racing cars that I do not enjoy driving due to category restrictions. With no way to make sure I'll actually enjoy the way the final tier handles I feel like I might just drop this title for now idk we'll see. One things for certain, this game frustrates me more than anything else, and it breaks my heart to say this.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to really love this game and in some aspects I do - even as a shell of the franchise's former self. That being said the revolutionary gameplay of TDU1 and the expansive but undercooked TDU2 DNA isn't felt nearly as strongly in this title.  The map is unique and interesting.. but small. The Online requirements aren't ideal but I could make an excuse for it if it was implemented well but... it just isn't. Singleplayer race wait-times anyone? You can't restart a single player race without abandoning it first and having to sit in the lobby again? great. Worst of all the AI driver scaling is frustrating at best and horrific at worst - not to mention they crash all the time.I've been a huge fan of the TDU franchise as a kid and the idea of the Open World racing game market still feels untapped to me. I'll revisit this game as updates and as the developer fine-tunes but as it stands now I can't really play this game without feeling annoyed and upset - let alone recommend it to anyone. This feels underbaked at best and unfortunately negligent to the wants of community that loves this franchise at worst.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; this game is pretty good, but desperately needs a performance patch and more content.Firstly, I cannot recommend this game at full price. This should have been released in early access, because there is not enough content to justify the price and the performance leaves much to be desired for the level of fidelity. The selection of cars is fairly small, but the individual models are pretty well done. The sounds are decent, though some cars sound like complete ass (Maserati MC20 to name one). The map is fairly large, but is not incredibly varied.The story is laughable, but you kinda expect that with a TDU game!The performance needs work. I have a fairly beefy machine (4080 Super, 7700x, 64gb 6000mhz mem), and I only get ~70-80 fps on medium-low. This game does not look nearly good enough to justify this level of performance.  If this was fixed, I would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, played as soon as it launched without any disconnects or server issues but unfortunately the optimization is a joke in this game, pretty much non existent. After getting such a poor performance not only on the closed playtest but in the demo as well (pretty much the same) I was hopeful that in the meantime between those and the official launch it would at least be optimized to an extent that is moderately playable but that is far from being true, and it leaves me incredibly disappointed especially after waiting for this game for so many years and having a very optimistic view on it. My hardware runs Forza Horizon 5 on high settings at 90+ fps while TDUSC runs on medium settings with DLSS on performance mode at a whopping 30 fps with an outrageous and unnecessary use of vram, and this is just frustrating, waiting so long only to have performance this poor only proves that releasing unfinished games really became the new standard in the current days. Despite being incredibly bummed I still stand optimistic that they will get things right and make the game run better given time, this is just the beginning. As per writing this review I do not recommend buying it unless you have hardware that runs it good enough for it to not bother you, otherwise stay away from this game until you see somewhere that they got optimization going for it. I want to love this game and so far it has done stuff right at least for me, especially since they solved most of the server issues before launch (again, haven't had any issues getting into the game and launching races, can't say anything about multiplayer races as I haven't found anyone playing in my region yet) and the handling is great.My hardware for context:Ryzen 5 5600H16gb ram ddr4 3200mhzNvidia RTX 3050 Laptop 4gbOnce this game gets properly optimized I'll think about changing this to a recommendation, until then it will remain as is, this just sucks especially since this was the very first time I placed a pre-order on a game, yikes. Maybe game studios should begin to take into consideration that not everyone has an over the top pc with the latest and greatest hardware, a simple look at the Steam hardware survey would do wonders.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I, like many others who bought this game, have played the previous TWO Test Drive Unlimited's. What I can say, about this game;Positives:  ~Cruising around is great. It brings me back to when I would hook up a steering wheel and roam Ibiza and Oahu with my brother. ~Insane detail within the cars and the world when you stop and take a gander at them. Even with the constant rain that seems to never end, the game still runs well with amazing detail.~Roadmap seems to have many features and implementation that will continue to keep the game alive as long as the company chooses to follow through with them.~OK variety of cars at launch with new cars being added. Also, pre-order/gold edition bonus cars being implemented after a set exclusivity period is a thumbs up from me.Good and Bad:~There is not a really defined path for the "career" which is good for some, eh for others. It would be nice to have more structure within the campaign, but to each their own.~Ranked Races are dumb. Clans are mid at best. ~Live events are alright, same with Solar Pass.~AWD cars are by far supreme and it is so evident that this is because of the WRC handling. Just having AWD off the line will give you the upper hand for the entire race.Negatives: ~The AI changing difficulty without having any option to adjust it on your own. Many races are borderline impossible if you do not have the exact perfect car and get lucky with the AI.~Rubber banding AI are insane. Every race there is always ONE AI that is driving at an impossible pace for the conditions. Pouring Rain and these AI are flying around corners no brakes in RWD cars. Just impossible to compete with that.~Traffic AI have zero brain and the roads feel empty even with them~No offline play, and Ranked Races taking over regular eventsOverall: I would say this game is like a 7/10 right now. If everything they say they will add gets added, potential for a 9-10. But as of now, its an investment and therefore a 7/10. If the devs add the changes that we are all asking for and fix the darn AI, then it will go to an 8/10. But for a racing game, the value isn't in races, but the overall driving free roam aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so first of all the launch (Gold Edition) was absolutely catastrophic. The game was basically unplayable for a couple of days and still has it`s server problems but it`s getting better.But the more I get to play the game, the more disappointed I become. It`s been about 13 years since TDU 2 launched and I absolutely loved TDU & TDU 2. Sure they both had their flaws but I loved them.I loved the housing, the configuration, the dealerships and side missions like car delivery.. "Drive this car from point A 50 km to point B. You can take as long as you want but everytime you get damage you lose money".. those missions got you a ton of money and they were special because you could only do them once.Now all I have seen are sprint races, round courses, time trial and domination (which is basically a sprint race) that`s it and it get`s grindy af pretty quick.In TDU & TDU 2 you had some kind of cups with a couple of races.. when you won that the next one is available.. in this one you progress with levels. Like every 5 levels new races appear. Of course the higher your level the slower your progress. I`m now on level 22, did all races I unlocked with level 20 so now I have to repeat and repeat and repeat to progress in leveling. But I need the money anyway because for some races you need a specific car.. per race you earn about 15-20k Solar Coins.. sounds good right?Not so much when a frickin Mini Cooper John Works costs almost 700k.. dont ask what the high powered cars cost.. you can spend easily 10+ mio for a car.. while getting about 20k a race.. which doesn`t matter of course because you have to get to level 40 to buy such cars.. so I wonder which you will hit first.. level 40 or the 10 million after doing the shortest race you could find for the 500th time.I get it that most racing games are grindy to a point but this just feels insane to me.. of course as a so called Live-Service-Game they need to keep people occupied which is quite the hard task if you almost have no content.So that was my little rant about grinding..What else?AI is absolute dogsh*t, no housing system besides you being in the Solar Hotel, driving feels okayish, cars all sound the same, graphically it is ok at best, Hongkong Island is for me an absolutely boring location, no casino which was always a fun time in TDU & TDU 2.. but hey at least that is announced for season 4 of the Solar Pass wohooo.. aka Live-Service-Game.. aka let`s put out an unfinished game and milk the people more money for content.I really hate to say it, but that game is propably not for me. I was really hoping to get that TDU feeling back, but there`s none of that.. at least for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've simply enjoyed driving around an open world in a racing game. TDUSC is a beautiful and fun arcade  styled racing game with a modest selection of cars and enjoyable areas to drive in. The game can be grindy at times, but the moment to moment driving and the locale that this game is based in is fun and somewhat relaxing. I, personally, have not experienced any server issues since playing as of September 13th, and a quick tweak of the options allows the game to run at near maximum settings at a comfortable and consistent 60 FPS. Content is a little scarce and repetitive and the AI opponents are very hot and cold. Sometimes they drive perfectly, sometimes they get really friendly with a wall. There's also occasions where the Ai opponents are not affected by in world objects.Assuming that the game continues to grow, the developers have already planned patch fixes for a large majority of the issues, as well as several content updates planned in the upcoming year.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, where do I even begin? This game has negatives, so, let me talk about those first.From wonky physics upon hitting a curb, railing, or even a wall, optimization, and to the server issues themselves is what truly is holding the game back from it's TRUE potential. The hate the game is getting is more than justified especially with seeing ANOTHER ONLINE ONLY GAME. This game and the test drive NAME deserve more and deserve better than being online only. Which is why I say, keep pushing the narrative of "We do not want more online only ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" As that's how we lose the games we love and care about so dearly.I also DO say please each and everyone of you whom do own the game. PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD if this game shuts down or gets announced in the future to save ALL FILES of the game to preserve what we do have to revive it later. TEST DRIVE DOES NOT DESERVE TO DIE AGAIN NOR SHALL IT.This game past all of the nonsense of servers, optimization, dumbass region lock servers (Yes US players cannot play with EU players) is awesome as ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hell. The AI does need some work to make the races a bit more realistic and not "AI GO BRRR, HIT WALL, BRRR, HIT PLAYER LIKE THEY NO EXIST, BRRRR" This game is like if you're discovering a pure diamond the needs to be excavated just right otherwise you'll damage it. So much potential that you can easily the hope and pride of devs who put the time into it. The handling itself it great especially when you drive with only 75 percent traction control to truly at least feel your car slip when you're on the throttle. Off roading races are awesome too and normally I HATE RACING OFF ROAD. But I genuinely love it on this game I can't explain why. Car sounds are amazing (except for a couple of vehicles. I'm looking at YOU Porsche 918) There is also detailed tuning of vehicles but I believe you have to be level 30 or 35 to unlock it? Which is fine because some vehicles come with "Vehicle Modes" IE Sport, Circuit(Same thing really), Trail, Cross country etc... Just depends on the vehicle being driven.  Which these modes are game changing. Do not sleep on them.  I can go on and on but I have to end this review at least lol.Test Drive is a if not THEE home of open world (real life almost) racing. Especially in the current over saturated "Happy time festival every where, everyone super duper happy" environment we have with The Crew Motor(Trash)Fest and Forza (Give you bugatti first race you do) Horizon. There's an actual grind to this game that can be a little boring if you're alone but HELLA fun if the servers work and your friends aren't across the pond. This game needs the devs to just listen to what the players require, what we wanna see, and figure out how to go about it. While also keeping the hope alive of wanting to just work on the game. Please do not attack the devs as that's what demoralizes them and makes them not want to work on the game. Instead, give them hope, constructive feedback, Give them something worth working towards. This is truly a diamond that NEEDS so much love and attention and I really want it to be something we ALL can enjoy and race with each other in! At the end of the day, There's truly something here that is amazing. Our racing community (The true ones who LOVE racing games) is small yet niche. Not everything will be perfect but nor should not hold our own expectations of course.EDIT- AS OF THE 30th OF SEPT THE GAME IS NO LONGER PLAYABLE AS INTENDED AND OR NEEDS TO BE. POSITIVE PARTS WILL STAY ON THIS REVIEW BUT DO NOT BUY UNTIL THIS ♥♥♥♥ IS FIXED.

_childDocuments_.review: Positive review to counteract countless negative ones only because of server issues.This game is the first online project for the devs, and this is not even the real launch period so I dont know why people review bomb the game...The game is sort of a mix between games like The Crew and Forza and Test Drive Unlimited. It still retains some things from original, but it is made to be a lot more like The Crew etcThere are no photo tasks, tasks where you need to escort a person to a place while being careful / fast etcHowever there's some new things, and the world overall is pretty nice. _childDocuments_.review: As a Test Drive Unlimited 2 sequel - this is not it.In the previous two games, driving around on an island (Oʻahu, Hawaii and Ibiza, Spain) was just right for a game like this. You didn't expect a lot of traffic or people in general; you felt free in a way. Choosing Hong Kong as the destination for TDUSC was clearly a mistake. While it looks somewhat detailed, the city itself feels completely dead.As a brand new open world driving/racing game - it's decent fun at best.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a Forza killer. Forza has better driving mechanics for an arcade game. This game feels like it wants to be an arcade racing game but also realistic. You get an offroad car and pretty much are limited to the road or the tracks they made. Driving "offraod" is very bumpy. Also customization is meh at best. upgrading spark plugs for better performance doesn't make sense why not the head or internals, bigger exhaust. Was there not a car guy in the development team? also with upgrades. Why at lvl 15 do I unlock all the upgradable parts for every vehicle. Why not have it like black ops 6 where i have to use the vehicle to get upgraded parts. So normal level to get them then have to drive or do missions to get those unlocked for that vehicle. Idk feels like a let down where they could have jumped ahead of all other similar racing games. It looks good and cars sound fine except for the same back fire the same way with multiple cars. I wouldnt say it has room to approve it just falls in line behind forza and maybe maybe in front of the crew 2.The Crew MotorFest is the way to go!!

_childDocuments_.review: In 48.6 hours I reached max level 60 and max Sharp clan level 50. I was using meta cars always because I'm a fast grinder. The grind was why I considered buying this game because I love grinding online games.Think if this game wasn't always online it would be worse, because in NFS Unbound / Heat / Payback you can simply just download a 100% savegame from the internet and be done with the game. There is no real reason to waste your time playing the game if it's not an online game and you can just use a savegame. I only enjoyed NFS 2015 for the same reason.So TDU Solar Crown got a lot of hate but I think it's a little bit overhated because every hater is probably level 50 or 60 because the gameplay is actually fun. Yes, sometimes the race crashes or you can't join a race, then just restart the game. It happens rarely. In my opinion Solar Crown was a fun grind, not too long and not too short.In order to enjoy the game with minimal pain I highly recommend only buying the meta cars for each class. I will tell you what the meta cars are. Buy the cars in this order:- Starter car: I suggest picking the Ford Mustang.- Buy the Audi TT for Daily Driver.- Buy the Sientero for Cross Country.- Buy the Porsche Taycan for Grand Tourer.- Buy the Lamborghini SVJ for Supercar and then you can also buy the 812 Superfast (there is a challenge race which can only be done with the Ferrari. Queen's Gambit.)- Buy the Porsche 918 for Hypercar and later when you reach level 55 you can buy the Bugatti Veyron SS.Make sure to not waste your money on too many upgrades until you reach level 45 when you can buy the best upgrades for your car. That's how I played this game. The gameplay is fun and the car sounds are awesome. However, I feel the game needs more content in clothes for your character, more cars, and more maps but that is coming with the Ibiza update.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the biggest waste of money I've ever done this year.
