_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped for this game, as someone who played the original TDU and TDU2. I was so glad to see the franchise coming back. I even signed up for testing last year which when I played it I was really impressed... Oh, how so much can change.Day One:As a Youtuber I started a stream to unveil a game I was incredibly excited about to find I was sat in a queue... For an hour. An hour my viewers had to sit and watch me wait to get into a game that kept kicking me out of the queue... I don't want to say it but I'm unimpressed that you weren't prepared for this after nearly two years of testing the game.I am incredibly disappointed. After having to change my stream over to iRacing for an hour (A fully functioning game), I finally was able to get straight into the server to find that the graphics were incredibly poor. My computer in 2 months old... I have a intel i7, 32 GB ram and a NVIDIA 4080 Super... After the intro I go into the settings to find the game is running in low...? That's ridiculous.After then spending 30 minutes getting my steering wheel settings right for my Logitech G920 (Still not right... Feel like I am driving a boat... Which is saying something as someone who has driven a boat) I go to do a race and it keeps coming up with a different error message saying it can't connect to server. After several minutes sitting in a near by underground car park, it finally lets me into a race... But wait! It's AI? Why did it struggle to get me into a race with AI?... Oh well, finish the race... Oh and you guessed it, I am jump scared by a message "unable to connect to server". Bit of a joke now, do the race again after waiting another 10 minutes to race AI.... And you guessed it right again, greeted with another "no connection" message.I know the game has just come out and being a massive fan of the TDU franchise I know its tradition to have bugs but never was it this bad. I want to hope the game will improve because after over a decade of waiting for this franchise I expected so much more.Day Two:Improvements have been made, was actually able to get into the game after they advised the servers would be out for "30 minutes" was more like 2 hours. Got to do the final race in tutorial and purchase my first car. did my first race in the car I purchase, went to do the second and race server was down again.... And was down for most of the day.I came back later in the evening and everything was up and working again. Leaved up more from exploration so far than actually racing, but was an improvement from the day before.Day Three:Everything is complete operational, the steering is still a problem which I am hoping they will patch for the Logitech steering wheels. Hopefully it won't be too long till that.Now I have actually had a chance to play the game, it doesn't remind me massively of the original TDU games and for anyone who is a fan it's a must have. They still have improvements to make but I am hoping these will be sorted by official public launch day on 12th September and I hope the servers can cope with the traffic from more people trying to get onto the game.On this basis, I am changing my recommendation of the game to yes.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, it's quite difficult to give an objective opinion about a game you've been waiting over a decade for and a franchise that holds a lot of sentiment to you, but I'll try my best!Firstly, lets talk about the most basic thing, the packages offered when purchasing. Right off the bat, if you bought the gold edition to play the game early (as I did), it was definitely not worth the money paid. However, I'd say that was mostly due to the server issues that occurred during the very early release which persist (albeit less severe) after the "First Major Patch". At this point the game is publicly available regardless of the edition you buy, my only advice here really is unless you want the DLC for both sharps and streets, buy the package of the group you want to align yourself with, and that's IF you want to buy this game.Secondly, I'll move on to the game itself and I'll start with how the game feels to play. Honestly, with the current state of the game (2nd Oct 2024 nearly 1 month after release) it's a mixed bag. On one hand, the physics feel quite good and the cars are generally enjoyable to drive around, the sense of speed in this game is nearly unmatched par a few games I can think of like Night-Runners Prologue, when you drive fast, you feel it. On the other hand, the server issues during races make actually playing the game nearly unbearable as you could be at the finish line, only to get disconnected and forced to run the entire race again, which may seem like a minor point but when it occurs frequently and especially if you're doing the crown jewel races which take over 30 min each to complete, it becomes a reason to stop playing entirely. Another point which I attribute to the "feeling" of the game has to include the AI as they are an integral part to how the game feels to play since right now, the main content is racing and you'd be hard pressed to race against other actual players due to the low player count and region + console lock. To sum it up in one word, the AI is abysmal. AI in this game is highly over-tuned and either make ridiculously stupid plays or are downright cheating, setting world record times that active players even with the best tuned cars cannot hope to surpass. Now, you may say "skill-issue" but consider that the physics in this game try to blend "realism" in with a semi-arcadey feel, you'd be hard pressed to believe a RWD super/hyper car could seriously out corner an equally or greater tuned AWD super/hyper car which were made, specifically, to out-corner those very same RWD cars.Thirdly, the content itself. Right now the content is baron and it seems like the devs have the wrong idea about what the integral TDU experience should be. It's not racing, that isn't the central content. The central content for TDU was and has always been the lifestyle, it's what made the game so beloved by fans and drew and kept so many players in. Purchasing and showing off your houses, collection of cars on display (the display limit right now is a mere 6). This brings me cleanly to the next point, cars. Where are they? Most show rooms, especially on the higher end, you'll find replicated cars just slightly different, basically special edition variants of same model cars. The variety of cars has dwindled massively compared to previous iterations of TDU and other open-world MMO racing games these days. Though, take that last point with a pinch of salt as other open-world MMO games, such has Forza Horizon 5, have been out for far longer and utilise seasons to add cars to the game making the overall list utterly expansive and I attribute that more to longevity of the game itself so I'm hopeful that, with time, TDUSC will introduce more cars as the seasons progress.The map is fantastic, there's a lot of drive-able terrain and exploring the map is a lot of fun. It's a bold move to make a TDU game centring around a city metropolis unlike Ibiza or Hawaii which had a lot more scenic views and terrain. But I think it has been executed very well, cities are densely packed with road to drive in and explore, the mountainous region is a blast to drive through and thanks to the car and grip physics, you'd best think twice about driving a supercar off-road to explore, giving the player incentive to seek out alternative vehicles that can and will do the job better in certain terrain. Onto graphics and optimisation. The graphics are great IF you've got a powerful enough PC to run the game smoothly. I unfortunately don't have a PC powerful enough and have to run the game at very low on everything to squeeze out enough FPS to make the game playable so it doesn't look great (since everything is on very low), which brings me to the next point, optimisation. I think a lot of people would be in agreement that this game should have been delayed further by 3-6 months because the optimisation is horrific, I can load up for more graphically demanding games and get better performance on my system with elevated graphics settings than playing this game with everything on the lowest settings which is not a good look at all for KT Racing. Not everyone has, or can afford a 4090 to appreciate this games graphics. Additionally, the lighting in this game is a little funky and can either make the graphics look excellent, or make it look like you're playing a PS2 ported game so that's definitely something that needs work.To conclude (there's a lot more I could talk about but I'd suggest doing some independent research for more), at this point I cannot recommend this game in its current state, it's hard to play with the always online model and consistent server issues, it's hard to play with the level of optimisation the game has for most systems since the performance is abysmal, especially in cockpit cam which sucks because the interiors of vehicles have a lot of detail to them and because there just isn't much content right now, you race and explore and that's about it. Ironically, you can't fully enjoy either because of a) the AI and b) the optimisation and server issues. Wait and see how the game pans out, right now it's not worth your money, wait until the game has been patched and improved to a level that's more enjoyable than it is frustrating, kind of like what happened to No Man's Sky.

Game has great potential, I absolutely love this type of arcade driving style (huge fan of the first unlimited), even tho I prefer sim racing. Starting with still quite bad optimization, badly implemented dlss- even set on quality look no further than 10/20m and everything is blurry, turn it off equals 30/40fps on RTX 3080, res 1440p. Constant fps drops, disconnecting from server, a lot of bugs like traffic cars transcends through obstacles or you just go through them without a crashing. I'm playing on controller at the moment, didn't have time to plug it to my racing rig and from what I've heard its utterly pointless from countess reviews that I've read. So if you're massive fan of the franchise... you probably already bought it. If not i would recommend to stay away from this game until they fixed those problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Do Not buy this game as it currently is.Servers are extremely unstable and it's an always online game. If a hamster farts in the server room mid race. You lose your progress.Understeer is a joke and you have no feedback whatsoever (I have vibration at Max) so you cant even feel that its broken loose at the front. Brakes are either 100% or 0%. No inbetween. Even with ABS at 75% you cannot even turn slightly. Straight line braking only I'm afraid.The turning is so poor that even the AI cannot make it round some corners.Even when you aquire a high HP RWD car you have alot of understeer. Also if you apply throttle its like the back end is on ice. No wheelspin sound or anything.The AI is infuriating. Apparently if you win regular it ups the AI level and never reduces it. You cannot set the AI level. I am at the point where the AI is unbeatable without cheating. The AI cheats and does it obnoxiously. Goes through bushes and trees and continues to accelerate. If you do the same you almost come to a complete stop. The AI has an obscene amount of grip, power and stopping capability despite you at the max level PI for that race using the specific car for that race.It took me 6 hours to finish 2 races due to server and AI issues.The car sounds leave something to be desired. Too much emphasis on racing and not the enjoyment of the car.Traffic randomly disappears from infront of you. Also spawns randomly aswell.On the plus side. On PC it does look pretty. Going around Hong Kong is quite pleasant when you drive around at your own pace out of races. Going around in a MB 300sl is good.I really wanted to enjoy this game as a driving game. Not a racing game as what Test Drive is supposed to be. I would give it a 3/10 in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying the core gameplay is quite good, driving around the map is very fun, the map itself is small but nice, and the races are enjoyable up to a certain point. If you liked other racing games but want something a little different, this might be good for you.However, that's a might, and whilst I enjoy the game compared to the newer Forza Horizon's, I simply can't recommend the game to others. Its buggy and there's been network issues. As expected of most game releases nowadays unfortunately. Some get fixed in a patch, and then new ones are added.The early to mid game grind is fun, but towards the end game, the payouts barely increase, so you're left with hours and hours of mindless grinding just to even buy a hypercar. Not collecting a rare Ferrari, I mean buying a standard hypercar.This is worsened by the fact the gameplay doesn't evolve. There's no new events, barely any variation to races, the Free Roam 'do skills and earn money' is LIMITED for some reason, and its a hard grind to get to the higher levels just to earn reasonable amounts of money. Outside of this, there's no other ways to earn money. No fun missions, no special quests.But worst of all, the developers. Last year they announced the game more and started doing monthly newsletters. By the 3rd newsletter, it was already late, and then they stopped doing them all together. They don't listen to the community and they are very lazy when it comes to communication - the new season started today and absolutely nothing as an announcement for it on any social media. The solar pass has nothing exciting at all.The game has no crossplay, and is region locked. If you want to play with your friend on a different console or in a different region. You can't. In their dev diary they revealed these things were possible, but they just didn't want to do it. Why? Why can other games do it so easily, but these devs can't?Furthermore, they advertise this game as an MMO?! What kind of MMO limits multiplayer like this. In addition, free roam lobby sizes are limited to 8, and so are races. Apparently the limit is higher at 12 in workshops and the hotel. Because surely you'd want to see people more when you're in a hotel lobby than out on the road in a car in a racing game wouldn't you? You can't interact with anyone in these indoor locations either except for wave.As an ALWAYS ONLINE MMO, you will barely interact with anyone. This game is just an O, there's no massive or really any multiplayer, but it is online.And throughout all this, the devs are clueless as to what the community wants. Game breaking bugs are listed as 'Misc and minor', server issues causing players to be able for days are dismissed as small and 'not everyone is affected'.Oh yeah and maintenance is at minimum 6 hours, and for the last update is lasted up to 30 hours.Finally, this isn't a TDU game. I've touched on some elements in the post, but its missing so much from the previous 2 TDUs.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello!CAUTION ! This review was written on 08/09/24. Therefore, the game is in its early days and this review may not fit at all in the future.I've recorded about 26 hours and I'm level 34 in the game, so I think I already know what to expect from this game.I'll start with the positives:+ The beautiful atmosphere of Hong Kong and the overall world is beautiful and it's a joy to drive through it and find hidden alleys, and even better, the game rewards it quite well...+ The game keeps car shopping confidential (You come to a car showroom. You take a good look at it, take a test drive and see if it will be your car or not)+ Interesting, not simple, but for me really great behavior of cars in the field when you really want to have offroad tires and preferably 4WD, otherwise you will have a lot to do to stay on the road...+ Clan system. Very simple and nothing special at first glance, but since 2 clans make up the whole game, there is a lot of room for improvement, and they already have their own image, which in most cases is also taken over by the players themselves, example: Sharp players are often dressed luxuriously, while streets simply somehow+ The progress system is cleverly set up, so you still have something to compete for and something to look forward to. Later, a smaller grind will start, but you still know that as a reward you will be able to buy the Ferrari that you wanted so much and looked at in the showroom, and that keeps you behind the wheel...+ There are cars that don't appear in the game much and that I was very surprised (Example: Audi R8 in the Decennium version...)+ Every day it seems to me that the game is more beautiful. I don't really care about the graphics, but the graphics are nice for me.+ A very effective combination of the assistant with your driving style and the car you currently have. I mean in the Audi TT RS I had almost everything at 0 while in the Mercedes SLS,Maserati MC20 I had to have the traction at 100 Because the rear wheels are pretty relentless in this game+ A very open speed and turn adjustment system. There are preset styles, but you can set each one exactly to your liking.+ The radio has acceptable songsThere could be more, but I can't think of anything else right now, so let's go to the negatives. And I would like to say that there will probably be a few of them, but in terms of weight they will be stronger than the positives...- Optimization = Its just bad. But to tell the truth, you can see that it is being worked on and it is getting better day by day- SERVER ISSUES = I play for hours without crashing and then I can't even complete a single race because it keeps kicking me out in the middle or at the end of the race... Let's roll the dice and see. But then again, that's reality. It's improved a lot but it still causes a lot of problems and it wouldn't be the first rage I've gotten with the game because of this- AI racers!!! = I so hate AI in this game... Rubber band is crazy, they are aggressive. The first place always gets such a speed that it mostly disappears in seconds. When you're the first one, you can see how they overtake you like a rocket in a slow car, and the only way to stop them is to simply knock them down or block them. They are dull on wet tracks, but this is the first modern game where I would probably rather play against real players than AI because it turns out to be easier. And speaking of playing with players...- ALWAYS ONLINE = I think that there are already so many things being resolved around it that I don't need to write anything down... I'll just point it out. Add the option to race offline when the system is already fully in the game, and apart from the Ai I want to kill, it works...- It is not possible to sell purchased cars- In the later parts, a bit of a grind for respect and clan reputation begins by completing the same races several times in a row...That's about all I can think of.Summary: I recommend this game. Today, the game is pretty much in a playable state, and those were the biggest problems. Well, there is still a lot to be done and you will have to reckon with lags, sometimes getting kicked out of the race, sometimes not connecting to the server, etc... But if you get over this, you will play a really great racing game that I personally enjoy a lot and enjoy the moments (as long as I don't bang on the table when it says connection lost in 99% of the races)... As for TDU, TDU2... I think that the game, if it will be cared for and will receive updates and, above all, will be played, will be able to achieve the glory of its predecessor. Not yet at this point... Not yet...Bye.

Cliche, lame, cheesy, tacky clan rival  a nutshell, drive and win to gain rep to impress some pointless overlord big wigs for some reason?...,although let me guess...the Solar Crown?....big whoop! Judging by the bad futuristic Clan fashion sense and architecture of the hotel and garages, your Bugatti Veyron should look like an old barn find in this. Is it supposed to be the present day or 2124?....a complete missmatch!  I think they must have coded it in Word 95. Maxed out on my 4090 looks nothing like the photos above. Water looks lame, map is lifeless bar the traffic and all looks dated. The Sims has better animation than this Must have hired the Script Writer from Temu. For a game set in Hong Kong, where 85% of the residents are Chinese, there sure is a lot of western looking folk in this. Pointlessly oversized and fancy. Full of NPC's sat round doing nothing and when they are animatedly talking, nothing can be heard. Can only imagine this is to accommodate future paid cars. About 20 vehicle models on repeat, Taxis galore!. All randomly de-spawn around you as you drive. Pretty good but nothing special. Interiors are OK too, although the mirror graphics are woefully jerky and bad.Nothing special. Cars behind you sound like chainsaws and close to you even when they are a good distance away. Well, there's racing, speed traps, racing, time trials, racing, explore the map, racing, find the car wrecks (only 2 cars to find all the wrecks to unlock from what I see so far), racing, racing the rival gangs (excitement overload!) and racing....edit: I missed off racing sorry. I've done 6 races so far, not one gave me real people opponents. Zero players in the lobby! All parking lanes have a floating neon sign saying "Parking Lane"...wtf for?, if you stay parked for long enough, you start getting Doggers turn up!?!Petrol stations....ya don't get petrol there no....you magically fix your car at the pump!?! 90% of Test Drive Unlimited goodness. No real estate to buy, no police, no ferry jobs, no hitchhiker jobs, no sense of being different to any other similar game like Forza. Get rid off the giant futuristic player hub "hotel built especially for the competition", cause there's absolutely nothing to do in there and no one wants a hub. Glad I didn't pay full price (I searched for cheaper game keys), I suggest if you can't wait for a sale then do the same. Not worth the asking price.....yet.RIP TDU

_childDocuments_.review: This might be a bit of a rant not really knowing where it goes but here we are. I had high hopes for this game. Truly. I wished so hard for it to be a success and live up to its predecessors' legacies. But no. Yes I poured in maybe close to 200 hours on that game, having lost money, patience, sleep, a controller (it flew through the wall), space on my hard drive and fuel driving to and from the hospital after I had to get checked in and treated for dizziness and hypertension caused by the physics in general and getting booted from long races because of connection timeouts or whatever. It is, in itself, not a bad game but the negatives massively outweigh the positives. Yes it is pretty and sounds good but the physics are all over the place (how is it that drifting and hitting a kerb sends you off flying and sliding on the side of your car that far, that fast??). The supposed competitive aspect is completely thrown out of the window as nobody apparently plays or is willing to play or race against or with you. The instant challenges are always ignored by the other party as soon as they see your level and car (in my experience) and some of the players sometimes appear stuck somewhere under the map causing the traffic to spawn out of thin air and ruin your FRIM run. The heavily criticised Super AI is now performing at an acceptable level, presenting a challenge but not dominating you without lube as it used to although it sometimes appear it wants to push you into traffic or off the side of a cliff and god forbid they pushed you when drifing and caused you to hit a kerb or you'll end up flying and landing on the side of a building if you're in a city. (Crown Jewel Amethyst). Test Drive Unlimited 1 and 2 were pace setters, the first being the first of its kind and setting an example of what can be done in a open world LUXURY AUTOMOTIVE LIFESTYLE game and the second added in options, allowing playing around with the functions of the cars and dynamic weather with day and night cycles. Here, we get these TDU2 options and more (windows, roofs (Why is it that convertibles are always closed btw?) manual headlights and wipers and indicators and wings (another one, some cars are automated but completely manual in others (bugattis vs ford GT 2016 for example, what's up with that?? If i wanna put the wing up like Porsche drivers in real life, lemme do it, otherwise, have it use its real life behaviour with actual impact on the aerodynamics). Yes I digress, sorry not sorry, I've had a long day.  KT and Nacon, whoever made the game, not gonna lie, this is a good start but NOT WHAT THE PLAYERS WANT. A Test Drive Unlimited game cannot be a forced online experience and have a map you can fully discover (I'm at 99% discovered yet have driven all roads, shown and hidden) in less than six hours like I did after I finally managed getting in following the first crap show (sorry but can't argue with that) of a launch in gold edition early access. An open world racing game cannot be just that: Big map (yeah right) with races sprinkled around and nothing else. Where are the shops, where are the side missions (not speaking of tasks or quests or whatever you want to call them), where's the true in-game competition and the importance of the clans and how they came to be? I'm not saying there should be a story to complete and then you're set free to do whatever you wanna do but that would at least bring in some intrigue, questions, discoveries and plot like in a specific Required for Velocity game from 2019 and push players to keep playing, build up their garages and their reputation amongst other players. Yes this is a rant, at this point I would be surprised if anybody did read up to this point and if you did, both thank you and congrats. Maybe somebody somewhere at the developers' and publishers' would see this and know exactly what needs to be done to push this game I wanted to love and drag on about to friends into the right diection. NO ONE SHOULD BE FIRED but everybody should take a breather, listen to what is being asked and take proper actions to regain followers. I'd suggest doubling the rewards from races, or setting gradually increasing rewards according to vehicle category AND add in a multiplier by increments of 20% up to 200% for each race you WIN without quitting the races (actual races of course, I saw what you did setting the Times trials' reward at only 1500 solar coins). When it comes to clan races, how about you get a random challenge from time to time that you can refuse from one of the clan members you might have beaten already in a different car? A one on one high stake race on one of the existing sprints (you win or lose 50k for example) if Jo Munoz (the first that came to mind when typing this out and I felt bad beating her somehow), she challenges you and the weather is completely randomized for that challenge specifically? I'm not dumping a load on your game, your efforts, your certainly countless sleepless nights of work. I respect what you did and the vast majority of players, I hope, will be with me on that one. Thank you but this is not what the people were asking. The 80 USD and time I spent on that game can't be refunded at this point but I'll let it go. Do not expect me spending any more money on it when the 3rd season and its solar pass come unless I hear overly positive reviews from short tempered impartial but fair youtubers. I'll keep and eye out and my controllers safe, meanwhile. Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: The game as a template is fine. There is a lot of grinding potential the sounds are marvellous  and the overall experience would have been quite nice and entertaining aside from the cringe story. Only, there is a giant issue. The game is practically broken, servers are useless, if there is an actual ten seconds when the game starts to be enjoyable because some random guy with a stronger car calls you out on a challenge you can be sure that at the next second the game will crush and you will be thrown out of the servers. I have spent 3 hours to try and put a custom paint on my car, and I have been forced to remake it 3 to 4 times only to be unable to save it either way. Because I am apparently considered timed out. Kicked because of being AFK, I am trying to customise my damn car, and the game registers me as being AFK. What the hell!? It makes my blood boil the very second I think about it. The optimisation is out of this world, since it's apparently not made for human PC-s, some Marsh tech might be able to run it with high preset. Aside from that, the graphics while not bad, compared to the ridiculous resource amounts it just looks like crap, because of the none existent optimisation.My wheel doesn't work with it, by the way. I can't even manually set it up since the game doesn't notice if I press a button on it. It true that the damn thing is old as hell, but I should still be able to manually set it up? What's with that?As of now, I am considering this game as a single player, since over 3-5 days I could barely connect to any other player, because of the ridiculous and seemingly constant server melt downs. The only time I was somewhat able to get an actual glimpse of the game is mid week early afternoon, when most people work and the servers are relatively working because of that. At the weekends its practically unplayable.Even so, I can barely consider the game as a multiplayer to be in a state of Alpha testing. You guys were so not ready for the launch, it's kind of impressive in it's own right... I had low expectation from the beginning to the early server states, but this is far beyond my worst expectations. And I am saying this, while I have been among the few people out there, who didn't actually mind the always online state of the game. Since it will be a lot harder to cheat this way. Alas, I have to agree with the others ultimately, because you couldn't deliver an always online game. It just doesn't work. There is not enough server capacity, which is a marvel in itself since I have never seen more then 8 people at the same time on my server. This is highly a game with a thousand player, if you can't see them what is it good for?Which means that most of the players are pushed into sub lobbies of the main server making it less of a massive multiplayer like WOW, and more like a Baldur's Gate like experience where you invite over 3 friends and play it. This is hardly a massive multiplayer in any sense. You can barely see other players on the street, and they tend to disappear before you meet with them. Probably pushed into a different lobby or kicked out.As of now, the game is too frustrating to play, while I do not intend to refund it, I am still surprisingly disappointed even with the low low starting expectation. I do not intend to annoy myself with this anymore for the foreseeable future, as I do not enjoy finding car wrecks or starting races for the game to not save it or kick me out at the middle, not even mentioning the car customisation, which in itself is quite good, only that it doesn't actually allow you to save any changes that you make.It's quite ironic, that  when I try to save the new paint, it doesn't allow me to, yet it still shoves the warning message into my face when I try to leave it without saving, that: If I don't save the changes it will be lost... _childDocuments_.review: It's a mixed bag, but I'm still having a good time with it. There's a good game in here and I hope the devs take the feedback constructively. It's not a triumphant return to Test Drive, but it isn't a bad attempt. I'm sure there are others like myself who want to go back to the grind of older car RPGs where the grind to get better cars was fun in of itself. Nowadays it feels like these games thrown things (money and cars) at you left and right and don't give you enough time to enjoy what you have. Pros:1. The driving feels good. Cars have weight and require finesse. 2. It's hard to describe but it feels like effort was put into finding the best roads for tracks rather than just tracks that feel thrown together.3. Not everything is thrown at you in terms of money/cars. You have to rise up the ranks and grind. I actually highly appreciate this.4. The tight technical tracks of the urban areas are a nice contrast to the off road areas. 5. You can roll down windows, turn on/off lights, use turn signals, etc.6. Avatar customization is in with some nice looking cosmetics.7. The tone is dialed down from the constant barrage of notifications/commentary/etc that both Forza Horizon and The Crew are known for. 8. The plot/tone isn't super serious and I found myself enjoying the dynamic of Streets vs Sharp clan. Cons:1. The AI doesn't scale well. You'll start on novice difficulty opponents and eventually be placed in expert difficulty where the AI has insane speed. Hopefully this is patched.2. Performance issues everywhere. I'm playing on a 7800X3D and a 4090 at 5120x1440 averaging 65 fps on ultra with DLAA. The visuals don't support the hardware requirements.3. The voice acting isn't great. 4. The car selection is small - hoping this gets increased through patches.5. There's only one "home", your hotel. I believe real estate purchases are mentioned in their road map.6. The sounds are bad - not sure what the deal here is but everything sounds very subdued. 7. Lack of event types. So far I've only counted 3 (Time trial, Domination and circuit/sprint races).8. Uneven pedestrian areas/lifeless city blocks. Some areas of the island have NPCs, others don't. You don't see them walking around. Also traffic should be increased.9. Server issues & lack of offline mode. Online only so you're at the mercy of their infrastructure. They've mentioned an offline mode so maybe this will change in the future.Long story short the foundation is good. It's worth it at around $25-35. I hope the devs get to execute their road map as that would add to the package. The most urgent issues are the performance/optimization and bugged AI but these can hopefully be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Full of potential, riddled with bugs, lacking optimisation, graphics levels mostly good, but inconsistent I've never been so split minded about my opinions over a racing game before. To name a few of the bugs, traffic cars just spawn or sometimes get "Thanos snapped" out of existence right in front of you. Guess it has something to do with the game's lacking rendering ability to keep up with the speed, as this happens not only with traffic at times.My Sientero Reinita has some quirky jumps when the wheels get hit in certain angles. As if I'm on the moon.Server disconnections are an annoyance, especially in the middle of a race.I also do not appreciate the fact that the "meta" cars are just ridiculously way faster than the rest in their respective class. It really makes the AI  unbearable if you do not want to drive them, rather experience driving YOUR favourite cars, and win some. This also means that you can't really trust the stats at all because they do not reflect actual performance.The reflections in the rear view mirrors are like 10FPS. Its embarrassing, better have it like "The crew" with no reflections if you ask me.No option to restart, i gotta abandon the race, get all the race set up all over again. What a waste of time.I have RTX 4080, at ultra settings with plenty of G RAM left, the game runs on 40-55 FPS most of the time on ultra 4k settings. WHY. It's also the ONLY game I currently have that actually raises my ROOM temperature so much that my desk fan actually started blowing HOT AIR on my face.Car reflections are absurd. I really don't know how they did that. Not only is everything that's reflected on the car pixelated and low quality textured, but sometimes it's just blatantly unrelated to your surroundings. Why is the ROAD from BENEATH my car reflected on my rear window?! Doing burnouts gets smoke in your car as if you have an open bottom. There's a weird, cropped and blurry shadow beneath your car as you drive, seems like a bugged layer of shadows. I had a terrible bug where my customised keyboard key binds got deleted so bad that when I launched the game after quitting, all the keys went and got deleted. Not reset to default, DELETED. luckily, the Esc button worked. Because even my mouse clicks had no feedback to try and fix that. And the TDU tech support simply told me to make a post in the forums about it to see if others are experiencing it, but gave no solution. I actually used an AI as tech support to solve that problem. Imagine having to set all the key binds from NULL each time you start the game. I do admit that some bugs made me laugh as if i was in Skyrim. The graphics has potential but require plenty of tweaking to not look terrible. The bloom effects, the motion blur, the depth of field options, ruin it so badly, they honsetly make the game look bugged and from 2012. Wayyy too much noise. Also, you will probably want to raise the contrast levels to around 75 and brightness to 65-75 for the colour balance to make sense, or else the lights in the game don't illuminate enough (street lights, traffic cars lights), which makes bloom feel almost necessary, but it's not. After all my tweaking and working around it, I did reach a result I'm happy with which makes the game look vibrant, dynamic, and balanced, aside to looking more like a 2020 game than a 2012 one.*Also, since when does the bloom effect take away the rain droplets if you disable it? I liked that, but the game is way better off with no bloom so I gave up on that..It's a shame that the default graphics look so poorly, it makes people think this game looks terrible for it's release year, but frankly, not necessarily so. I do admit, some textures, especially in the buildings, need improving.On the bright side, I do appreciate some of the smaller details that they did pay attention to, like some smoke details, and tire trail tracks when going off-road.Driving the cars is fun. Very fun. The map is probably my favourite of all time. Very dynamic, big, plenty of city streets to roam, highways, and off road trails. Most racing games get that balance very wrong and give you mostly country roads and some highways , which feel like they just didn't want to invest in actual city-scaping of your environment. While being very beautiful and colourful, still, the city feels DEAD, as there are no civilians walking the streets, but the seldom occasion of people grouping in places out of reach. That's just weird. I don't know why i have to go to the hotel lobby before being able to open the map. I also hate the fact that looking back while not moving above certain speeds simply rotates the camera. I'm not in photo mode, let me just look back on prompt and snap the camera instead of rotating it. The audio is also imbalanced. I had to lower my car's volume to hear things like the dings of an abandoned classic car nearby. And opponent cars are somehow way louder than my car.Speaking of audio, I don't understand the choice to separate the the free cruising radio, from racing. Maybe on some special occasions, have a special track, yeah..But they got separate options for them in the audio options, and if in free roam, you turned your radio off, to listen to some "Skeler Night Drive" mix while you're at it, your radio will still run in a race (and you don't have the time luxury to just set the radio off in the middle of the race) BECAUSE YOU CAN'T PAUSE THE RACE. So I just had to mute that. Well, guess I do understand why they split it then.YOU CAN'T PAUSE A RACE. EVEN IF YOU PLAY ALONE. Listen. I'm a father of two young kids. I get plenty of interruptions when I try to play. Not being able to pause is a real pain for me.Customisation is important, they say...But all you can do is put some stickers with very lacking customisation options. Like the inability to have a vinyl layer of a different colour type.  I also don't understand why they gave us a "front" "top" and "back" options, if they all overlap when you try to scale something to cover an entire area but not the left or right sides.I kind of miss having nitro, though i know that the TDU franchise never had it. Wish they had. Finding other players to race with is not even on my list, it's not done well, I almost always play alone, and when players do join me, they usually cause lags, and I have 1GB symmetrical connection with very low pings. On its own, I don't really consider this a Test Drive game.. More like the Need for Speed/ The crew that "Motorfest" should have been. I do realise that for most of the long time followers of the franchise, a big part of the game's QoL, and lifestyle, housing systems, clubs, etc are not in the game. I guess I wish they put some effort in that too. But as a racing game, the racing it good. Car list is underwhelming, very. Next time, give me more cars instead of 3 versions of the same base model, please. The progression is sometimes lacking, especially when you need to save over 1M cash for expensive cars. You really need to start finding what to do next so it won't be so repetitive. You get a boost at the start of your daily run because of all sorts of "first of the day" bonuses, but then it goes down and it feels terribly slow to gain cash afterwards. The always online mode has GOT. TO. GO. I know i said mostly negative things, yet none are deal breakers, yet. I love the game overall, i love driving the city, and with the right tweaks, it is a great game to drive.I truly hope the devs take these notes to improve on the gameEven though I do not enjoy the idea of "games as services", and most games nowadays have a terrible launch as if it's the new standard, I hope they work on it to make it better. It actually has the potential to be a GOAT. Bottom line, it's fun, I'll keep playing, but for the sake of it, I can't make a positive review and feel good about it. I'd be the first to update it once they deal with all the above.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was ever a game I'd like to give a "mixed" review rating on steam, this would be it.TLDR - Positives: Handling/Map/Audio. - Negatives - Always online/server issues, AI, general lack of polishThe map is pretty great, the handling feels generally very good and driving is generally fun. What isn't fun, is being disconnected from a race which is populated with just myself and AI. The server situation has so far improved since the disaster it was at the start of advanced access but it shouldn't have been a problem in the first place. Always online doesn't seem to add anything of value. I have had just one race with another real player - who behaved exactly as you'd expect in an online racing game, so I'm glad this "feature" of having all races be public lobbies isn't quite working out how I assume it was intended to. The AI while definitely beatable, especially with the right cars, are some of the worst I've seen. They have no awareness of each other, the player or traffic/obstacles in the world. They are guided through corners by the hand of god at incredible speeds and some appear to have a rocket booster to deploy on the straights. AWD cars are broken enough to offset these issues but that isn't a positive either. Performance - with a Ryzen 9 7900X & Radeon RX 7900 XTX I'm getting 70-90fps on ultra/1440p. _childDocuments_.review: Edit V2: The handling on this game is truly awful. It's unlike any other racing game and feels unpredictable at best or like your a steering a boat. The cars have no grip and understeer constantly. The driving is wonky and the game rewards driving the car unnaturally. Such a shame, I was so thrilled about this game but it has truly been a let down and at this point I think I deserve a refund. You'd think being at the Ferrari Lambo part would be cool but no its impossible to play against the AI and its just a meaningless grind. I couldn't be more upsetEdit: With the new season I literally have no determination to grind it out. It feels really boring. They should switch their focus to the lifestyle aspect of TDU instead of this competitive, online racing, fomo thing It's a fun game. The map is awesome and plenty fun to cruise around. Weather and lighting is beautiful if you got a nasa computer. The AI is cheeks they got some mega rubber bands on them and they dummy fast cars for no reason, either that or they fly off the road and then you might win but its one or the other. For an "online" game it feels pretty lonely. I am a huge fan of TDU2 and they massively missed the mark on the things that make test drive special, like unique dealerships, houses, and an expansive car list to name a few. These are the things that upset me most. I do think there is a lot of potential and this game doesn't deserve all the hate it gets. At least right now it still deserves a lot of the hate. There's plenty I think needs to be added and fixed. I looked forward to this game for a while and don't really have a desire to play it which is weird for me. It feels truly next gen and the map is amazing. The scale and graphics are great, it does a lot of things right. Cars sound and feel awesome. It just feels like a generic racing game tho and I guess that's where it goes wrong. While the game impresses me with some things and is a fun time, it bums me out with other. We need more cars, we need houses, the AI needs to be fixed, and it feels too much like a grind. I am only recommending because it doesn't deserve all the hate, People should still give it a chance because it's a cool game and I think it's fun. If they make improvements it can be truly great and a proper follow up to TDU2

_childDocuments_.review: Favorite Open-world Racing Game so far,server issues are mostly fixed now, so no worries here anymore. Racing is really competitive and I like that. You have to be carefull with objects, or footpaths you hit which adds a great variable for racing. The AI is very strong but thats a rather good thing. Physic are actually great too. Its satisfiying  to complete drifts, to avoid traffic etc.. Then there are the sounds. These are much better than in comparable games like Forza, NFS or The crew and add the immersion of driving specific cars. In general, each car feels and sounds completely different! The map adds to the immersion too. There are many small roads, offroad paths, big city skylines, a huge dock, many many small details like small parks and individual models like statues. But is the game perfect? - No and not even close. Things that can be hugely improved are for example the story immersion. In TDU SC you just drive races, have the solar hotel and thats it. I remember TDU2 having the party at the beginning, the used car dealer because you were broke, much slower starter cars, driving schools, appartments that show your progression, opponents with characters you have to defeat and so on. The car list is also a thing to improve. When racing I sometimes get the feeling that there are only three distinct cars in one class. Something that probably improves with time.Its hard to describe this feeling objectivly but in my opinion TDU2 and TDU SC are opposites in some scenarios. TDU2 was a game to vibe but driving was more on the bad side. TDU SC on the other side is an amazing game for driving but the soul is a different one to the older games.Still, really recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state I can definitely not recommend it.The island is beautiful and really nice to drive around. The exploring is great, the sounds are great and it's fun to drive around in general.Fortunately, the bad server launch didn't affect me, and I have been able to play for quite a while now.I'm playing on a wheel and that's mid at best. The max wheel angle is not configurable and stuck at 360 degrees, while my moza wheel is capable of way more. Then, the paddles. They do not do anything unless you press them halfway already and it's quite difficult to brake properly without locking the wheels.Last but not least, the cherry on top: AI gets increasingly difficult. While that is completely fine, the implementation of said AI is absolute garbage. You notice it's programmed to slingshot, follow the line precisely (they massively steer to the racing line at the start of a race) and they also drive like a cannonball, not aware of what's happening, I've seen plenty of cars launched in the air because another AI squashed them against guard rails.The vibe of the game is also way different than the previous TDU games. It's quite futuristic and revolves all around the SC competition instead of it just being a part of the game. They doubled down on it with the clan wars. So if you're buying this hoping for a successor of TDU 2, simply don't. Devs said they wouldn't disappoint the fans of the previous games, but so far they did with me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm barely holding myself back from screaming AJ's classic punchline, "You f..ked it up!"I have such mixed feelings, especially after the last public beta, which was in horrible condition. However, I saw some potential and hoped that most of the issues would be fixed or that some gameplay elements would change. But... the game is a total mess right now.After that disastrous release, I really want to believe that the developers will fix at least something in this game. WRC Generations was definitely a solid game with decent arcade physics and a good amount of content. Yeah, you don't have the right to make a bad game with the WRC license, but where's EA's new WRC from Codemasters right now? Just check the reviews or try it if you don't believe me.Anyway, here is a list of things the devs need to fix or change ASAP. If you buy this game right now, you'll encounter the following:- Requirement for an internet connection for single-player events- Problems with saving your progress and numerous errors due to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ servers- Unstable servers that frequently kick you back to the main menu, more often than you actually see the cars- The most broken AI I've ever seen in a racing game (last time I saw something this bad was in Project CARS 2 at launch).Here’s why:-- AI drivers don’t respect your lane and constantly try to crash into you. Sometimes they don’t know how to drive and get stuck in trees or bus stops-- AI can be faster than you even if their car rating is significantly lower than yours-- The same old problem with that one AI driver who is always faster than the others and catches up with you instantly-- Races are not balanced in terms of difficulty (imagine, in 2024 you can’t adjust bots driving level), and instead, it adjusts automatically (after 3 races, I was suddenly facing "Expert" level AI for no reason)- Rubberbanding and teleporting, with traffic disappearing right in front of you- The damage model is mediocre — hitting something feels like punching an air balloon- Multiplayer feels dead, it's hard to find someone in the race lobbies (with those servers, lol)- On certain tracks, you’ll see checkpoints that are placed poorly, causing you to miss them constantly (watch some videos on YT and you’ll understand)- Tons of graphical issues, including broken SSR reflections, poor GTAO implementation, flickering shadows, and poor quality of lighting during daytime- DLSS and FSR do not provide a significant performance boost unless set to maximum performance mode, which makes it look like low-resolution YouTube videos- Anti-aliasing with DLAA looks worse than native, and even worse than TAA (!)- Poor optimization overall (60 fps on a 4070TiS at high-medium settings in 1440p resolution is embarrassing)- In terms of content, there are just over 100 cars on the roster, and there aren't many interesting ones (I'm not asking for FH or GT numbers, but it could at least match the last NFS game)- Race rewards get cut in half after 4 repeats, and you need to grind for money to get anything good (after 12 hours, I only managed to get 3 decent and upgraded cars and a little more than 1.200.000 cash — next level cars from Gran Turismo category cost above 1.000.000)- Not much external customization for cars (at least they could add a library of pre-made liveries or the ability to share them with other players, which would be a decent feature)Amazingly, other aspects of the game feel extremely good. I liked Hong Kong island andI enjoyed from amount of details and exploring process. Even off-road racing is fun, and at least you get real race tracks rather than the MotorStorm-style, open-field nonsense of Forza Horizon. The driving model has improved since the last beta, and driving in this game is genuinely fun and satisfying. You can definitely "read" your car, and you can adjust it manually or with presets, which makes things easier. After a long while, we finally have a game with a progression system that makes you want to earn cars and race through events, instead of casino or gacha style bulls..t.Actually, there is a lot of potential for TDU SC to become a good MMO racing game, so please, devs at KT, just fix the bugs and give people at least an average sim-cade racing experience — we really need it.Overall 6 / 10, not recommend until sales and bug fixes come out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best/most fun open world racing game I've played!I'm 14 hours in and almost level 30 and my fastest car is a Porsche Taycan Turbo S Cross Turismo.Other games throw super- and hypercars at you but this game makes you work for those cars, the progression is a lot more fun (imo) then other open world racing games.The graphics look good on ultra settings and the sound of the cars is amazing.After upgrading your car the sound of the engine/exhaust changes as well.The map is and city is designed well and fun to drive/cruise in.Radio stations pump out some good music.One major bonus is that bumping into things and cutting corners actually slows you down.You cannot drive in a straight line through the forest with you Ferrari and be quicker then driving on the road like some other games.The AI can be hard (which is a good thing tbh) but make sure to get the cars below for easier progression:- Daily Driver: Audi TT RS- Cross Country: Sientero Reinita- Grand Tourer: Porsche Taycan Turbo S Cross TurismoI haven't come to the supercars yet but the Ferrari 812 Superfast seems OP.You also don't have to win ALL the races for progression, there is a reduced payout but not that much that you cannot progress.Don't let the haters tell you it sucks because of always on.Yes the first day of launch there where some connection issues (which was expected tbh) but the devs communicated about this quickly on official channels and resolved the issue within a day!There are a lot of plans for this game and the roadmap looks very promising.If you're looking for a fun open world racing game with good progression, car sounds and overall fun this is it!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Wait a while if you're interested in this game.The game currently is riddled with issues ranging from the map not working properly, crashing randomly, locking up during load screens, resetting progress, bugged story missions and presenting the user with random errors. On top of that I've waited for 6 days for support to respond to a ticket I made (claimed 2 day response time), so if you have an issue, you'll need to solve it yourself.Regarding the actual content : It's similar to the old Test Drive Unlimited games, except you drive on the other side of the road and traffic has a habit of despawning randomly. The TDU parts obviously missing are : Houses, Casino, Escort and car delivery missions as well as the feeling of being on a big island. Somehow Hong Kong island feels a lot smaller (It might be irl, dunno).For a game set in Asia, there's not a lot of Asian looking npcs, no Chinese brands and the 'Pearls of Asia' car dealer has the fewest cars available of all the dealers. The amount of cards available is somewhat limited, and only the 4wd cars have any realistic chance of beating the story missions without retries.Speaking of retries - you can only restart time attack races, and even if you do you're sent back to the car selection screen before you can drive again (means 2 load screens for a restart). With every other type you need to abandon the race and go from free roam to the car select screen (3 loading screens).This is made worse by the fact that the AI has a habit of trying to ram you off the line and the fastest way around a corner is running into another car.Not sure if that's related to the story line, but there are very few older vehicles in the game and some brands have suspiciously few cars if any.There aren't any 'ordinary' cards you can upgrade, so no K20 swapped monsters or the like. I can see a 'season' thing in the game, so there'll possibly be micro transactions or a season pass at some point.Also the collectible car wrecks are disappointing. It's a beetle again, as well as an old mercer. During the last week of pre-launch driving, I've yet to see a single mod or company representative do something on their official Discord server, except for posting the known issues on the 5th and a short update on the 9th. In short, they've skimped on PR, support and backend staff and probably hope the title of Test Drive is enough to ship the units to hire the needed staff (or abandon the entry).I had hoped for more.

_childDocuments_.review: After a horrible start to advanced access, they managed to make the game somewhat playable. Though if the servers will be able to uphold the wave of new players who didn't get the Gold edition is still up for debate. We will see in a couple of hours, if they can withstand it.For now tho, I have to say that Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown is indeed a fun game, but for me personally the car pool at launch is just a little bit too small. I know they will add more cars over the seasons, but it definitely would have been nice to have a few more.Another thing that really needs to be added is the ability to adjust the AI difficulty. You have no say in when the game will raise it and on the higher difficulties, the AI is sometimes just unbeatable, which is kind of unfair. So that would be a very welcome addition.Last but not least, to not expand on this review for too long, there is one more thing they should add. It's been mentioned multiple times and everything inside of the game is practically build upon it, yet it doesn't exist. An offline mode.If an offline mode will be added to the game and there's is no always online forced upon you, then it is worth calling Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown a worthy successor (including all the things they will add in the future like houses, the casino, bikes, etc.).The driving itself feels a lot like a mixture of both the Forza Horizon games and the old Test Drive Unlimited games, so if you've played either of them (or even both), you will feel right at home.The open world is one of the two aspects where Test Drive Unlimited really shines the best. It really is a vast open world with a lot of hidden paths and little secrets.The second one, and by far the best thing in the game in my opinion so far, is the sense of speed. It is absolutely incredible. I haven't had such a thrill because of the sense of speed in racing games in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Test Drive Solar Crown has really surprised me in the best way possible. I've played plenty of racing games recently—Forza Horizon, The Crew, Need for Speed Unbound—but none of them capture the driving experience quite like this. It feels like a game for real car enthusiasts. First off, the driving feels just right. The cars have weight, and there's a real sense of connection with the road. It's not just about going fast; you actually feel like you're driving, not just floating through a virtual world. For me, the standout feature is the sound. I drive an F-Type, and I've never heard a game come close to replicating the growl and roar of its engine like Solar Crown does. Forza Horizon can't even compare when it comes to capturing that authentic sound and feel.The progression system is another win. Unlike other games where you're handed a garage full of cars from the start, here, you have to earn every single one. You’re forced to stick with your car, learn its quirks, and really establish a bond with it. It feels rewarding when you finally unlock a new car because you've genuinely worked for it and mastered what you already have.The graphics are solid—great at times—but it's the overall experience that has won me over. This is the first racing game in a while that feels like it was made by people who genuinely love cars.

_childDocuments_.review: Moving past all of the server/log-in issues this game had at it's early access launch I have had heaps of fun in this game. If you have a lower end PC it may be worth holding on to your wallet until some more optimizations are made. To sum it up, if you've got a monster PC this game will be an awesome purchase. It's not a hardcore, always gunning to the next race style of game, it takes more of a relaxed driving position with big a bigger focus than usual on the exploration. There are a lot of incentives and rewards for going around the map and finding prizes, new locations, and rewards such as cash, XP, or even a car if you find all the pieces. As a long time fan of the TDU series this has been really good blast of modern nostalgia. Finally, I understand that houses and the casino are on their way. I do hope houses are coming sooner than later as it would be nice to have something other than cars and clothes to spend my cash on. The roadmap that has been laid out for us is promising, and I hope that the team can deliver. Thank you to Nacon and KT Racing for pumping life back into the TDU series, it's been a long time since 2011 but this game makes me feel like I never left.

_childDocuments_.review: Always been an TDU fan - played a massive amount of TDU2 on console, and a little more here on Steam.  I don't feel like this is what people are going to be wanting from a successor, though it's in the same vein, perhaps even frustratingly close to a good entry for some. Good:- Environment is pretty, and fun to drive in - Staggered vehicle progression / cars actually matter, not a collect-a-thon / Forza-esque stickerbook garage- Some odd "lifestyle sim" elements are still here (clothing, walking around dealerships, weird NPCs)- Decent customisation options (decent livery editor, trim / wheels / tint / paint options, etc)- Sense of speed and freeroam driving feels great- Still has that camp, cheesy, quirky vibe to it from older titles (UI, NPCs, VO, etc). Bad:- Performance is atrocious. 7950X / 3090, unless everything's on low with DLSS on I cannot hit 60FPS- Traffic will randomly spawn / despawn- Several game crashes- AI has insane rubberbanding- Handling feels off. (note: I suspect this is from overtuned TCS, turn it off and it's a little better)- Radio stations are really bad, annoying presenters, bad music (Classical is unironically the best)- Always online / account-bound licence agreement (hello The Crew 1, what could possibly go wrong)- No AI in freeroam, but will always make up your lobbies as no-one seems to be in your races(?)- No chase mode / police mode, or traffic infractions (?)- No alternative missions (hitchhikers, delivery, photo ops, etc)- No used car dealer or selling cars altogether (?!)- No real estate / houses- FRIM is limited to 10 a day (?) - Limited car roster, and/or cars are similar hypercars or trims for the most partThere's the bones of a decent game here - I'm sure it could be polished on, but there is no guarantees, particularly with the rumoured financial troubles of Nacon and supposed strike by the developers.  Probably worth revisiting later if it's actually improved upon, but for now, it's not got much over other freeroam racers, and it'll likely leave some TDU fans disappointed or frustrated. I personally feel like it's one step forward and about three steps back. It's prettier, sure, but it's missing a good chunk of the series' soul.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: So they released the first major """"patch"""" for the game. What did it do? It fixed points of interest not saving. That's... it. I mean they said they fixed more and they probably did, but this was literally the only change I noticed. Races still disconnect you, traffic is still buggy, AI is still unpredictable and if there were performance improvements, I certainly didn't notice them.Essentially, buy the game at your own risk. Like my first review (see below), the gameplay can still be fun, but it basically ends there. It's a shame this game had such an awful launch and I can only hope KT Racing can resolve the issues and add back TDU features before it's too late. Hopefully the first season that starts tomorrow actually adds to the game, else I can't imagine this game keeping a playerbase for very long.--------------------------------------------------------------------------So this game is an interesting one. Going purely off of gameplay, I would definitely recommend it - the driving is fun and there is plenty to do. If that was the entire story I would have recommended it, so what's wrong? Here's a quick list:- AI is entirely unpredictable. Some races they can feel incredibly difficult to beat, others you won't have a problem staying tens of seconds ahead.- Server issues. This includes from being booted from races randomly, racers randomly teleporting in races and points of interest (dealerships, gas stations e.t.c.) being "undiscovered", so you keep having to rediscover them.-  Performance issues. Obviously you will need to have a decent PC to run the game, but people with particularly beefy PCs might even have problems running at medium/high settings.- The physics can be pretty janky, although I would argue this isn't a massive problem.- Always online. This partly links to the server issues but there is no offline mode, meaning any server issues render you unable to play the game. I find this concept strange since it feels like most of the game is supposed to be played offline anyway.This is likely not an exhaustive list of the issues in the game, but it should give you a pretty good idea of what you're getting into if you purchase the game. I should also mention that it is much unlike the previous two games in the TDU series as it is missing key features such as real estate and clothing stores, although this might be added in the future.

So, welcome to TEST DRIVE UNLIMITED - SOLAR CROWN!At first, like others i bought the Gold Edition and yes i was a Connection Problem Victim, too.Yes, i was totally Angry, too. And yes, i was thinking About refunding.I mean, the developers had a number of Gold Editions sold and should have known how many servers should have been available at the beginning. Especially when you have a Game where you ALWAYS have to stay online to Play. It should haven been clear that every buyer wanted to get started immediately.Well, you can call me dumb but i didn´t refund.Gamers Passion for a Franchise and the will to give the Team a second Chance.I waited 2 Days and then i returned.And look. _childDocuments_.review: I've been really trying to like this game because I loved TDU2, but this is just not a good game.The world is empty and boring, there are way too few cars to choose from. This car list is just not acceptable in 2024. Every race you start has the same boring line-up.The graphics are just bad, very bad. Anyone who says the graphics are good hasn't seen a reputable racing game in the last 10 years. Performance is horrendous, especially because it looks so bad. Difficulty is all over the place and the AI drivers are really inconsistent and dumb. Some races are laughably easy and others are just impossible to win.Traffic pops in and out right in front of you.There are definitely things I'm forgetting to mention, but these are bad enough already.There are definitely some fun elements in the game as well, but not nearly enough to make up for all the bad stuff. This game is an immense waste of potential and a huge letdown for anyone who was a fan of the previous games.There are changes and additions planned for the future, but a lot is going to have to change before I can recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to love it, this game isn't ready.It has a lot of promise and has some good ideas, but it's not  Test Drive game. Gone are the big open expanses and feeling that you're working your way up earning licenses and cool properties to aim for, instead we're given dreary repetitive enclosed grey hellscape streets and AI which don't play by the same rules the player car does. Running over a small plant will somehow inexplicably slow you down to half your speed whilst the AI will go speeding off into the distance, or are so aggressive that they actively try and spin you into corners at which point the race is pretty much over. Half baked, low attention to detail and a far cry from the magic of TDU of old. Very sad indeed.I hope to come back in a few months and find it in a better, more enjoyable state with more features from the old games which made them so enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be the end of TDU forever.1) Handling - Cars handle terribly. The worst handling I have ever seen in a racing game. Maybe the worst I have seen in non-racing games too! (Note brakes feel extremely weak. No matter how early I brake I glide right past turns.)2) AI's - The game selects the difficulty for you. Plus the AI's seem to not have the same performance restrictions as you and at high difficulty will always be 30 seconds ahead.3) Number of People in Server - 8.....seriously that's it? 8 was how many we were allowed back in TDU1. Which may I remind you was 2006. 18 years and this number can't be increased?4) Weather - Its always  80% of me playing was in rain. Its extremely annoying. 5) Optimization - This doesn't make any sense. The game doesn't really look all that good and yet despite me having a 4070Ti, I have to run low settings? How can I possibly be maxing out my VRAM on Medium and higher. I just don't get it. All other games I play, I am always on Ultra settings. 6) Casino - This was a feature that was shown in all the teasers for the game years ago. Yet it will take a whole year after launch to be added to the game? The casino was out day one in TDU2. So now you guys are just using it as bait to get people to still play this game and buy season passes. 7) Map size - Probably the most disappointing thing that I hate about this game. If its one thing that the TDU games had, it was very large maps. This map is so small in comparison. It makes Forza Horizon look big. There will be no fun cruising around the map if it only takes 20 mins. Old TDU games would take almost an hour at full speed to make it around. Yes I realize that Ibiza is coming, but its only the city part. Its just going to be too small. 8) Currency - So far while playing the game (Rep Level 16) the amount of funds you get is so little. The amount seems to be the same no matter what race I do. I just don't understand how we will ever afford any of these high level cars.9) Cars - There are so few vehicles its sad. Plus some of the cars in the game are the same ones from TDU2. I am assuming that licencing for these cars were still covered from TDU2. Cause I can't understand why we have the 2009 version of cars instead of the new versions. (its also frustrating to see cars being triplicated in dealerships. I would rather they be blank spots for an expansion than show the same car three times). Also why is the Ford Dealership just listed as 'American' when Lamborghini and Ferrari both get specific labels?10) Offline Mode - There should be a difference between racing online and not. Plus, if your servers are not working (no surprise) we should not be punished, by not being able to play.Verdict - Don't buy this game for another year. This is basically a beta, there is to much that needs corrected. -I was apart of the Alpha and Beta, not much has changed, which is disappointing, developers are not listening to fans, and they forgot why this game had such a huge following in the first place. We don't just want another Forza Horizon, NFS, or The Crew-

_childDocuments_.review: Why would I recommend it?1. It has the best map of any open-world racer I have ever played, bar none.  Unlike other open-world racers (Forza Horizon series, The Crew series) the roads feel authentic, like driving in the real world and not in some place someone made up.2. The driving physics are definitely better than its competition.  I've played a lot of Forza Horizon 3, 4, and 5, and a fair bit of The Crew 2, and the driving in this game feels significantly more realistic than those. It's not iRacing or Asetto Corsa, but by open-world racing terms it's quite good.  That said, the collision physics can get a bit weird, so it's not perfect.Caveats:  The game is not perfect by any means.  It does have some flaws.  But they are flaws I can live with because the overall driving experience is great.1. The game is a little light on content right now.  The developers say there is more coming.2. Car customization is more limited than I would like.3. I'm not a fan of the way the reputation system works.  It's a pain, and being locked out of a lot of cars while I rep grind is a little bit annoying (though it does make you appreciate those cars once you get them).4. Apparently the game has some optimization issues and needs a pretty high-end rig to run well.  I can't testify to this, because I'm playing on an i9 with an RTX 4090.  I've had no problems with it.So, the long and short of it is, it's flawed but it has the best driving experience of any open-world racing game I've ever played, and I'm willing to live with those flaws for that.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend the game in it's current state. 1. Always datamining ---Not only always online that is a terrible choice, but also the game forces you to have a Nacon account with compulsory Steam link before being able to play at all. Not for extra ingame stuff or something, just to play the game. That isn't mentioned on the store page before buying... 2. Graphics. -/+Stock settings after starting the game make it look worse than it should be, because everything is set to low. Because of the full screen window mode as standard, it is also stuck on 1080p and a refresh rate of 50 with vsync, normal full screen mode allows higher res and FPS. After changing to ultra, 1440p and cranking the refresh rate up it looks a lot better. 3. Rewards & progress +The races earn you enough rewards to not worry about money too much and it is kind of refreshing to have to reach certain levels before even owned DLC cars are unlocked. Also, there are goodies to collect in free roam. But it would've been nice if there were other options to upgrade the car at level 5 than just plopping a turbo on it. 4. Handling model & car sounds +This is actually quite good. Not eSim difficult, but also a noticable difference between the cars. Suitable for a wide range of ages and skill level. Car sounds have been great so far also. 5. The AI. -The AI does seem to follow a bit of a traintrack, could be better, but who cares, because...6. Forced multiplayer racing --The game has a tag Singleplayers, but there's no way to select singleplayer in races. Even when you click start race immediately, the game takes time to try and add other players. WHY IS THERE NO SOLO OPTION? Seeing the difference in laggy AI when only 1 other player enters a race vs a full AI race, the AI doesn't seem serverside, so why not add a single player mode? That way, my kids can also race at a lower difficulty to keep it fun for them. Forza Horizon 4 and 5 aren't perfect, but they do it wayyyy better, with freeroam populated online to keep the world feeling alive, but in races the choice to play SP or MP. 6. Laggg ---If you're lucky enough to not have anyone join, the racing is fine, but as soon as another player joins, the lag with the AI opponents is quite bad, while other games like Forza Motorsport or FM5 have no issues in online mode. And that is with only the Gold Edition owners playing now, not very promising for after sept 12th... I hope it does improve a lot over time, so TDU 2 can have a worthy and equally fun successor, but for now, it's not worth the money.

detailed_description: Grab Your Longboard and Race to the Top Meet Tanuki , a rad longboarding raccoon from Sunset Island. They may just be a raccoon, but they’re a raccoon with a dream — to land on the cover of FISH , the #1 longboarding magazine in the world! Master the longboard as you drift through stunning mountain ranges, swerve through bustling city streets, and board along the sandy beaches of Sunset Island. Train Tanuki to perform epic tricks, from jumping off ramps to longboarding backwards. Sounds easy, right? Well, it is… if you can do it all while avoiding cars, trucks, and unexpectedly sharp corners. And don’t forget to feed him! Raccoons are hungry trash pandas after all. Collect Tanuki Bits along the way to keep Tanuki fed and to upgrade your gear at Bob's Skate Shop. If Tanuki’s going to be on the cover of FISH, they need some cool threads for the occasion. Ready to longboard to the top of the charts?
