_childDocuments_.review: *Note that 2 achievements are broken as of this time of writing (February 4, 2023). 42.8h (13/15 achievement, finished the game) Yes (~2 achievements that can take ~30h). Yes (12 achievements). No (some achievements can be hard for some people). is a racing game where you play as a tanuki on a longboard. The game introduces a unique control that causes turning to take a lot of effort and controlling drifts to be challenging. Its gameplay focuses on two aspects: finishing the level in the fastest time possible and getting a high score.- Relaxing music- Optional challenges for the more experienced players- Steep learning curve- Checkpoints are sparsely placedIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 uses 3D, simplified visuals. Each character looks cute with its cartoonish style and the background doesn't look busy while still providing a nice view with its lighting. It's easy to get lost in thoughts while playing the game, especially when combined with relaxing music.To be honest, I didn't know that the game has a story. Most dialogues at the beginning just serve as a tutorial to let you know everything that the game has to offer, and then it starts to drop some plot points after you are halfway through the game.The story is pretty light, although the ending was well thought out with its moral message. I liked the message that it tries to convey and how the ending was displayed. Sadly, you can't advance the dialogues manually in the ending and are forced to rewatch it whenever you finish the last level.As I said before,  is a racing game. However, unlike other games where you drive a vehicle, you are using a longboard instead. Controls become different as a result, and you need to get used to it. I didn't like the controls one bit, as turning left and right takes too much effort before it moves in the proper direction. This also causes issues with drifting, making it easy to get thrown off the tracks since doing so will move you further back from your initial spot.The thing is, it's easy to fall off the tracks. There are no fences or anything on the side of the road, causing you to fall into an endless pit if you go off track. As I said before, controlling your tanuki is hard due to the controls, and this will give a lot of issues to those who just learned the ropes. The tracks in the early levels might be easy for beginners, but you will fall several times to figure out the controls. Combine this with the sparse checkpoints, and you won't get a good experience out of it.You'll die a lot. Heck, I still died a lot even after learning the controls. If it's not falling, then it's crashing into obstacles.  likes to introduce more obstacles as you progress the level, forcing you to learn new tricks and get used to them. If I had to choose, I would still prefer the controls of other racing games compared to this, especially since it's the controls that largely make the obstacles to be challenging.There are 9 main levels in , with 9 optional challenge levels that you can aim for. Every 3 main levels will introduce a new set of challenges, with a different set of available tracks to loop. Yes, levels in  are randomly generated - no levels will be the same, even if you died and respawn in a checkpoint. There is only a small pool of tracks in the loop though so muscle memory still helps to finish them. You just need to get familiarized with the whole set and you'll be at ease.The game also offers different playstyles in the form of stickers. Those who just want to get fast can aim for the fastest time, while those who want to be cool can aim for the highest score. The score can be obtained by performing tricks, which consist of a lot of things: drifting, moving close to any objects, going to the edge of the track, and many more. Aiming for the best time or score will require some skill, although the main levels give a lot of leeway for them.Those who are more into challenge can finish the optional levels instead. There are 7 levels that are focused on specific challenges, and 2 that combines everything into a final challenge. The levels are not randomly generated, and beating the scores will be more challenging than the main levels. You have to find ways to optimize your run, and you'll spend your time dying trying to check which works rather than falling off the tracks from a mistake.I finished the game in 13.5h. You can finish it in less time since I was aiming for high scores in each main level. The rest of the achievements can be either grindy or challenging, which took me 42.8h to finish. Note that 2 achievements are currently broken.There is a steep learning curve. You need to get used to the controls, and you'll die a lot in the process. The sparse checkpoint also means that you'll spend a long time before you finish each level, giving you a source of frustration. The only thing that keeps me going at that time was the relaxing music, and it still is until after I finished the game. Even if you have learned the ropes, the optional challenges can give you a hard time if you are not skilled enough. is hit-and-miss for me. I didn't like it at first, and then I sorta get used to it. But at the end of the day, it's a game that helps me to relax and get lost in thought, especially with the relaxing music and empty backgrounds. And by that, I didn't mean that the background is completely empty - most objects are concealed with a certain color or provide a nice view, making it easy for the brain to process. That being said, playing the game that way can be boring to some people.The steep learning curve can be problematic to some people, though. Although I said that it helped me to relax, it frustrates me in the early game. I'm not sure if the experience is worth it, especially for casual players. Hardcore players might get more challenged with what the game has to offer, although there isn't much content for them to begin with. I'm not sure whether to recommend it or not, but if you end up wanting to get it, make sure you are okay with the cons.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game so, so so badly. I was incredibly excited when it came out. I love raccoons. I love skateboarding games, I loved SSX games on the gamecube and PS2.I followed the devs on twitter, and as soon as realized it was available for sale, I bought it. Unfortunately, this game just isn't what I was looking for, and it comes down to three things; controls, game feel, and difficulty. First, the controls aren't *bad*, but I would really prefer being able to remap break / accelerate to the triggers. Within a short amount of time, my finger hurt a bit from holding "forward", and it made turning while going fast, or slowing down while needing, a two step process to get right. Next, game feel; the game really, truly wants to be a low fi chill relaxation game, but the long boarding mechanics don't support that. It's finicky, and very slippery. I don't feel like I have precise control over the board, or understand at what angles it's going to move. When I drift, I frequently lose nearly all control over it and go careening off the edge. I can't collect all the bits that I want, despite feeling like my inputs should be close enough, but I end up a little too far, either overshooting or not edging close enough.That wouldn't be a problem if checkpoints weren't so spread out and far between, and that any mistake immediately drops you back to the last, far away checkpoint rather than dropping you where you died or offering some other penalty. The only outcome for a lack of technical mastery is just repeating the same thing you were doing again, but because it's a randomized track, you can't even advance with any sort of reliability from muscle memory. Sometimes you'll get a  break with nice, smooth transitions, and other times you're thrust quickly into a bunch of careening turns which send you flying off the edge, forcing you to go back and redo what feels like 5 minutes of skating. In my short play time, I found myself yelling "NO!" at the screen a few times, and that's enough for me to realize that at least for me, there's a dissonance between what this game wants to tell me it is, a chill, relaxing, zone out game, and what it is, which is a game that stresses me out with every turn. That's not to say that there's not a lot of good to this game. The soundtrack is short, but incredible. The visuals are lovely. It oozes cuteness and a cohesive visual design. The writing is adorable. But those are ultimately dressing for a game that doesn't do what I hoped it would. There's people out there with more patience than me, or who might be just better at the game than I am, for whom what I've listed isn't going to be a problem. But sadly, I don't think this is a game I'm good at, and it frustrates me enough that it's not something I'm willing to invest the time into to get better at.

_childDocuments_.review: Tanuki Sunset is a game in which you play as a rebel raccoon not only disobeying their mother by not wearing a helm but also all of the Tony Hawk knowledge I possess that you don't do tricks on a longboard  the titular Tanuki even does it without looking ahead!The visuals of Tanuki Sunset are a gorgeous depiction of the 80's synthwavey style with dancing to the music suns and buildings and overall vibrant and un-photorealistic style of the entire game and it's menus. As for the mechanics boy is this game an example of easy to learn and hard to master. Much further than steering, drifting and a few tricks the game doesn't push you but if you want to do it well you need to be on the ball!The absolute first thing I noticed when playing the game is that a bit counter intuitively drifting is  good and only slows you down. You should learn when and where you  need to drift. All of the stages aren't always the same and it's more comparable to a Super Mario World 'tileset' where a stage has road shapes and obstacles to progressively pick from which can be really kind to you or create triple s-curve snakey hell on earth! A few small quirks I'd like to mention though are things like the difference between doing a ramp well and not is basically non-existent so at first you have no clue if you do it well or not and that sometimes the tutorial monkey flat out forgets to explain the controls for keyboard and just says "press Y". That said I absolutely appreciate the attention to detail of giving you a smooth and continuous experience from the soundtrack I'll go into detail about later and the game not catapulting you off of your board if you don't perfectly do 180 degree increments of a spin or if you hit most obstacles. A lot of the obstacles just slow you down instead of ending your attempt.The soundtrack is varied between quite a few genres and artists but it overall creates a really cool homogeneous blend of a 'mini-soundtrack' per location. Every location change also changes what songs the shuffle picks from so that every location  stage feels and sounds largely different. To be a bit nitpicky however some songs really don't fade well into each other creating a long trailing fade-out or silence halting the continuous mood. On the side of the sound design it's largely a non-intrusive and charming selection of sounds emphasizing your actions but every now and then the jump squeak does get overly present.Then, in conclusion, would I recommend you to get this game? Absolutely! Tanuki Sunset is a very enjoyable experience that will keep you hooked for many hours and the experience  outweighs the small 'new game hiccups' like the highlight in menus not following your selection but just remembering the last option picked and that for example the second checkpoint indicated on the progression bar between 3-1 and 3-2 doesn't exist. Tanuki Sunset is ideal for people just wanting a fun and enjoyable game and a great challenge for the completionists among us!

_childDocuments_.review: The glory of an indie game is the freedom to do with it what you please.  Gone are the shackles of publishers chucking deadlines and investors expecting what will profit the most over what will be enjoyed the longest.  Take the craziest idea in your head and so long as you have a decent crew and the wherewithal to plug the hours in, you can make that crazy idea happen.  Like, say, piloting a longboarding tanuki through 80s inspired chillwave landscapes worthy of a computer wallpaper while Tokyo Drifting to a slappin’ soundtrack.  Yeah.  Indie games, man.Tanuki Sunset leaves its premise nice and easy for you: a tanuki with a board and a dream to be on the cover of FISH! Magazine carves the roads of Sunset Island honing the craft necessary to be able to speed through the entire island.  Your journey, after a short tutorial, starts at Bob’s Shop.  Here you’re introduced to a cast of characters able to help customize your gear.  Swap out different wheels, trunks, and boards for your ride, and slap on hats, shirts, glasses, and your own Walkdude for your trash panda.  The vaporwave, 1980s skater, synth style aesthetic is full on display, with button-down shirts that would fit at home on Saved By the Bell and boards that would’ve graced an old Skateboarder magazine.Once you hit the road, Tanuki Sunset will initially give the familiar feel of an endless runner.  There will be various obstacles to give you trouble, various twists and turns to drift through, and a smattering of checkpoints to help you progress.  The experience is escalated tenfold with a beautifully constructed soundtrack.  Your usual suspects of lite-synthwave and 80s city pop instrumentals carry the frontload, but Sunset peppers in little pinches of Future Funk, Lo-Fi, Beach Rock, and even Bossa Nova to tickle taste buds you didn’t know you had.Little collectibles dubbed Bits, which your Tanuki Mom would personally like you to stop eating so many of, are strewn about each level like a pseudo draft line.  Collecting these in bunches can be used to purchase items at Bob’s Shop, so it’s worth taking the time to ride the line.  Later levels start to add additional obstacles like ramps to jump off of, clusters of blue bits to pull reverts and catch on the fly, and bubbled bits over speed traps to jump off your board to grab and avoid.  And don’t get started on those Crabs.Moves like the aforementioned revert and ramp jumps can net Tanukis a higher score for riskier plays.  Points are earned by doing tricks in the air; Kickflipping and grabbing your board in mid-air are done with a push of the button, though I wish there were more variations in the tricks as you only get one of each from what I’ve played.  You can also come into close contact with any cars or roadblocks on the road, or by getting dangerously close to the edge of the road and not falling off, almost like a simpler, easier, less advantageous Shift Boost ala F-Zero GX.These points outside of bragging rights can net you stickers in the campaign’s nine levels.  Stickers are doled out for beating a track record, not failing during any part of the run, or beating one of the few side characters: Steven, He the Man of the Sky, in a mini-race during your downhill bomb.    The nine levels are enjoyable enough to replay, especially if you’re looking to gather enough bits to go crazy in the Shop, but the amount of content will run you roughly a hour to consume.  Thankfully, Sunset’s Arcade mode fills in a few time gaps with a dozen or so challenges to conquer and an Endless mode because honestly this game would feel fraudulent without one.There were only a few rocks in the road during my 7 hours with Tanuki Sunset.  Reverts can feel really weird when first used, since they don’t allow any fine tune turning during and will have a tendency to careen you off course during your first few goes.  The blue revert rings can sometimes be put in precarious places that would almost mean certain death if you went for them unless you purposefully went slow to collect, which in a game looking to build enough speed to drift fast and burn ass...is a little ass-backwards in practice.The ability to hide the HUD is a welcome option for longer playthroughs, but the full-on omission of a timer is a little perplexing given campaign levels as said before have a time to beat.  This can be a little pinching when trying to hit a perfect run and essentially guessing by the end if you made it or not, especially in the game’s last level, where a particularly long but great outro scene is unskippable.  And fine, let’s talk about the Crabs.The Crabs are a late campaign inclusion that will latch onto your board and be just annoyingly intrusive to your downhill jam.  The only good ways to remove said crabs from the sides of your board are to clip them on cars and debris on the road or kickflip them off a ramp jump, which removing two at once will net you a nice point bonus.  Personally they aren’t really a bad addition, but the wonkiness of them combined with other problems make them a logistical nightmare.When casually playing, it’s hysterical to see a Tanuki riding for dear life alongside two crabs with a death wish looking to take a third with them, only to kickflip them off-screen and continue your run.  Trying to mitigate crab grabs while aiming to beat a track record where getting knocked off your board is almost a certain fail and you honestly can’t tell how much they hurt your time because you don’t know your own time...and it can get a little too hectic for a game that’s so aesthetically low-vibe.But that’s really only gripes for people who like to unlock everything, which I have a gut feeling this really isn’t the place for them.  For the folks who want to sit back, listen to some fantastic tunes, and drift through a hour or two of simple, comedic, and engrossing gameplay involving a trash panda and some 1980s vibes, Tanuki Sunset is worth every bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent the first 3-4 minutes disliking this game. The speed didn't make sense, the controls weren't responsive, it was way too hard, and resets were way too punishing. Then... it clicked! Suddenly I was drifting around corners, going at maximum speed, and dodging cars easily.Tanuki Sunset has a synthwave / beach vibe mashup, and once you work past adapting to the controls, it's a solid skateboarding game. Each stage is a few minutes long, and a single failure (very easy to do!) will send you back to the start.The complexity comes through a risk/reward mechanic, where you can push the analog stick to go faster, perform near misses on cars, and all kinds of other terrifying behaviour, in exchange for more points. These don't seem too useful, whereas "bits" can be used on all kinds of cosmetics and accessories. It's worth keeping in mind that all of the jumps / drifts etc are optional, and staying on the road is waaaay more important.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game because I messed up my ankle and heel and can't go cruise on my new board. This game did not disappoint. If you liked old console (like sn64, cube, etc) racing games then you are probably going to like this. I love it. It's chill, groovy, and fun. When you fall you can quickly get back on. The few environments are really great. The music is good cruise music for this style of game and helps give that air of nostalgia. I almost played the whole map on my first play through and had to stop myself. I enjoyed going back and playing where I already completed. I had no issues using the keyboard except for a cramped hand from playing hard for too long. I just really love this little game and definitely see myself coming back to it, relaxing, and playing it over and over. I've already gifted it, too.If I had to list any negatives (and I just don't really see any for what it is) it would be that there should be different environments for the arcade modes.The only improvements to this game that I would recommend is an old school split-screen option so you can play with friends like kids used too after coming back from a cruise. And the ability to add your own music. New environments wouldn't hurt, but it doesn't really need them imo, old racing games didn't have that many either.Overall 10/10. I enjoyed this a lot more than I thought I would.

_childDocuments_.review: Tanuki Sunset immediately caught me eye before release due to the nature of the game - a skateboarding raccoon. Who'd ever think of making a game about that? Well, Rewind Games did. Luckily they didn't fail to deliver on their unique concept. The gameplay is smooth, and I enjoyed it a lot even though I don't usually play racing games. The music is great and ranges from lo-fi to bossa nova and electro swing. The sound effects are on point, as well. My only complaint in the audio department would be that there aren't really that many songs in the game and a larger tracklist would have been nice.I don't have any real complaints about the game. it's cute, funny, plays well and is just a joy to open up and race around in for a little while. You can tell a lot of love went into this game. I just wish there were more levels or a DLC or something. Unfortunately, from what I've read on the Steam discussion board for this game, Tanuki Sunset did not make back its production costs. As a result there has been virtually no support for the game after release, and one of the achievements appears to be bugged.I can recommend the game and I do not regret my purchase, but you probably won't get too many hours out of it. Even including the general replayability of doing levels again and finishing all the trial/challenge levels, there's only so much time you can realistically spend on it. As a result, I would suggest you wait until a sale before picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a game to relax to, and enjoy the pathing of racing games, then you'll have a good time with Tanuki Sunset. The issues with the game stem from a 100% completion standpoint: the flag for marking a level as 'completed' is only checked upon finishing the level, and isn't applied retroactively, so stickers obtained from a later area from the bird will not 'complete' the level, forcing you to beat it again. This, unto itself, isn't a big deal, but the 'complete all trials' achievement is bugged, and triggers for almost no one, and the bit requirements to purchase all of the items is downright insane. Getting all basic items requires a bit of a grind, but nothing too severe, with items ranging up to 1,000 bits. The crown you must purchase at the end of the game? 100,000. That's insane, and requires tens of hours of grinding, in a game that is 2-8 hours long, when completing everything there is to do.I had a blast with this game, but the ending ultimately left me feeling bitter and disheartened as someone who loved the game, and wanted to fully complete it.----------(The devs stated they were going to fix it, but then later noted that they could not further fund development with the sales costs, so I'm presuming the game being unprofitable was the cause for further content not being published, and the bugs not being fixed)"What is going on is that sales from the game's launch were unable to fully cover the cost of development. This meant taking the decision to prioritize porting the game to the consoles as soon as possible in order to remain sustainable." - Dev

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun for a little bit at a time, but the lack of polish ends up ruining the experience as a whole.The core of the gameplay works pretty well and the visuals along with the music really nail the vibe the game is aiming for. On its own, rolling down a hill, dodging, weaving and doing the occasional trick is pretty satisfying. Unfortunately the level design is where the game primarily fails. Checkpoints are far too distant, meaning the player has to have a perfect run in order to advance, but the levels are randomly regenerated upon failure, meaning the player cannot learn from their mistakes and work on improving performance on particular combinations of obstacles. The random generation also worsens this by linking together track elements that shouldn't go together, like a reversal just before a hairpin turn. This can lead to frustration as progression slows. The Arcade mode alleviates this somewhat with its bespoke fixed courses, however, you need to advance on the main map in order to unlock arcade mode courses, so you end up right back on the grind.Overall still fun in small doses, but could have been much more. Wait for a summer sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The fundamental problem I had with this game are the controls.  Acceleration and deceleration are mapped to the analogue stick, and can't be rebound.  I found this a really awkward control scheme, compared to putting these controls on a separate button.  The simple act of speeding up while going in a straight line becomes hard because of this; the sensitivity of the analogue stick means you'll tend to veer from side to side.  Given that one mistake can easily cause you to crash and restart, this can get quite frustrating.I actually have quite a few other complaints.  But, this isn't my usual genre; I only picked it up as part of a bundle.  So I don't want to go too hard with my criticisms.  Still, I can't honestly say that I enjoyed myself here, and so I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It's upsetting that I can't recommend this game. I mean the description of the  aesthetics and the premise are winners but that's just the paint on the surface, not the actual game. The negatives.- The game is not chill and punishingly difficult. Checkpoints are incredibly sparse. Add into the incredibly not chill instant failure system if you touch a stationary object or fly off and you can lose minutes of progress from a small mistake. This goes against the whole "chill" vibe it's going for. - The Tanuki is lame. You can barely customize your tanuki at all. Half of the customizations are solely on the bottom of your longboard (the other half being clothing) that you can't see. There is no additional way to express yourself really with the Tanuki while riding so it just becomes a fleeting novelty. - The three maps has nice variation but there is no gameplay variety. Nor are there any upgrades that the store page claims exists, there are only cosmetic options (that I already said are weak).- RNG map creation for the main campaign is just not something I'm a fan of at all even though the arcade minigame mode I believe are bespoke levels.It was fun and novel for a little bit but the constant small mistakes resetting minutes of my progress have made me just quit and uninstall the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: there are no tanukis in this game. The protagonist is a raccoon  Tanuki. He looks exactly like a raccoon and is always called a raccoon. Tanukis are an unrelated species that happen to look similar.Anyway... I love this game, so it may seem bizarre that I'm disrecommending it. The reason is I had to go through hell to get to heaven. There aren't enough checkpoints on the later racetracks, and you can easily get trapped in a sort of hell where you're on the track's last checkpoint and you can't stop playing because you're so close to finishing -- you can't quit and resume at checkpoints, only between stages -- yet the last leg of the track is so difficult, it takes forever to get through. If they fix this, this game gets a thumbs-up from me. I've gotten good enough at the game that it's no longer an issue, but damn was it frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: i wanted to like this game, but i just can't recommend it.it heavily punishes failure while not rewarding risk taking. there is no reason to do any of the cool tricks shown in the screenshots and trailers. there's no reason to go fast. you don't get anything for it. the points are meaningless. the actual game will be played as slow as possible because if you fall off the edge you lose five minutes' progress. likewise there's no real reason to collect the shiny coin trinkets, except for cosmetics. there's no board upgrades or anything.the main difficulty mechanic in this game is how far apart checkpoints are. toward the end of the game, if you slip up once you are going back several minutes. it's not a fun mechanic and it makes the game feel artificially harder than it should be. there's a character you race once in each level, but if you fall off the edge while racing, you have to redo the entire level if you want to get the little cosmetic he gives you.the levels are procedurally generated so it's not a question of learning each one and getting good at it. it's navigating the same repetitive sections over and over, in random order, except more of them and faster.the drift mechanic doesn't feel smooth. when letting off a drift, it feels like a gamble whether or not you will launch in a seemingly random direction off the edge.because there is no reason to go fast, the obstacles that slow you down- bags of trash, barrels of toxic waste, random electrical zapper things- are a relief to hit rather than something to avoid.overall this game felt like a chore to complete. it has a great aesthetic but the gameplay is... i guess tedious would be the best word to describe it. i don't hate it but i can't recommend it. certainly not for $15 USD.

_childDocuments_.review: (full review with screenshots:  )Taunki Sunset is a game about longboarding down an extremely long road while being a tanuki. The road was built with wanton disregard for the safety of both longboarding tanukis and drivers, so there are no barriers preventing you from plummeting thousands of feet to the ground below. The road is also strewn with hazards like giant piles of rocks, random trash, and highly aggressive crabs. You need to weave between and drift around all of these safety issues to reach the checkpoints as quickly as possible. You can also collect bits off the road to buy cosmetic items and do tricks to increase your score, but if you're just interested in reaching the credits, not falling off is all that matters. Like most of these sorts of time trial racing games, Tanuki Sunset makes a very good podcast game. There's hardly any story to distract you from whatever you're listening to, the lofi soundtrack will blend easily into just about anything, and, for me at least, having something to split my focus on makes playing the game easier. If you're like me and are only interested in playing to the credits, you'll have to be okay with not getting very much playtime for your money. It's pretty easy to get there in under two hours, and while the postgame does unlock one secret track in the arcade mode, it's not much of a challenge to survive and is much less interesting than the main campaign levels. The game is clearly intended for people who want to chase high scores, best times, and beating levels without dying, and you'll get far more playtime out of it if that's what you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is joy. I find myself trying to hold back my completionist nature and just enjoy the ride; spills and all. It isn't an easy game so to speak, but it's not punishing, it doesn't penalise you too hard, it just encourages you to jump back into the vibes and chill ride down a hill as a racoon (Hopefully in a cute lil' hat). This game has a charm and a "Made me smile" factor that is just way too pleasant. Great to jump into for 10 minutes, catch the chill vibes and drop til you're ready for more 'Nuki.

_childDocuments_.review: As a vapor-wave raccoon myself I can say I HIGHLY enjoyed this game!!With its custom and chill soundtrack you just vibe while playing.The game has a good mix of difficulty and reward that makes you want to keep doing, it punishes you for dying but rewards you for taking risks in stunts and tricks~!!The small addition of the story is super cute and I actually hope the developers add more to the game, once finished there isn't much to do but re-play the few levels and get 100% on the achievements like 0 deaths.Overall this game is super chill, I streamed on my twitch and people seemed to enjoy it there also. I recommend using a controller to play this game as well.Been on my wish list for awhile so glad I got to experience what felt like a game made for me~!!8/10 Trash <3

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite literally the greatest game to ever grace this earth. As a child, I often dreamed of a man chasing my car, jumping from tree to tree. This game almost fully encompasses that very idea, giving a seemingly simple idea like a racoon longboarding and adding an immense amount of depth. When I first purchased this game, I thought it nothing more than a joke. As minutes turned to hours and I grasped what it meant to master tanuki sunset, I realized that this was more than just a game. Tanuki Susnet brought out the best in me, and no matter what happens, I will always hold this game deeply in my heart, a core memory that will allow to me to grow in life. The character development of tanuki is well thought out, and executed perfectly. From a small town racoon wanting to skate into an emperor gundam buddha ascended level diety, this game subtly shows what it means to be alive. Starting in Sunset Peaks, which represents our childhood and the vast world to explore. We then move to midnight city, which embodies the typical work life. Narrow streets, trash and traffic, and a darker map make you almost cower in the sight of it. We finally move onto Sunrise peak, which is turning a new leaf in life, finding ones passion, ones purpose, ones meaning. The final ramp shows truly what it means to be human, which is ironic considering Tanuki is a racoon. All the characters are lovable, the map designs are phenomenal, and the gameplay is truly awe-inspiring. A lovely hidden background is the music, which truly expresses all feelings, what it feels like to have a somber boring life, or a free life, free from burden and free from all shackles. My first and only 10/10 game, Tanuki Sunset will always be the peak of gaming history.
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely fun and chill downhill skateboarding game with a raccoon that is way cooler than I will ever be as the player character. What's not to love? Would have loved to get an OST for this game, and adding shoes to 'Nuki would be a fantastic update, but this is a wonderful standalone experience which I'm extremely happy with. Bought this on sale but I'd even suggest buying at full price. It's like $20, some people spend that much money on loot boxes. Get it, you'll be happier with a little Tanuki kickflipping in your life.
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: The Gameplay is smooth and very satisfying, It can also be chill or exciting with just enough challenge that naturally makes you want to keep playing to complete all the sticker challenges for each level. On top of the that the soundtrack is vibin' off the charts! You can't go wrong with this charming waccoo smooth rolla, it's a good time. There really aren't many games out there anymore that can put you in good spirits anymore like this one can. FEEL GOOD AND HAVE FUN! ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent music, atmosphere and aesthetic.  Really easy to just sort of get into and chill.Ran into some issues with checkpoints.  It seems that, because the courses are randomly generated, sometimes the checkpoints just straight-up won't load on a track.  A bit of a bummer.Otherwise pretty good. _childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the perfect game to wind down or if you are a mega adult, smoke weed and vibe to. I just generally appreciate this game, it's aesthetics, and it's big chill vibe. Granted it doesn't take much to get my attention, but it does take quite a bit to keep my attention and this is one of those games for me.We gotta appreciate the games that are just "yeah you're just doing it". _childDocuments_.review: Fun runner game with an excellent soundtrack. The dialogue is funny, the new mechanics and gimmicks keep coming, and there's a decent amount of fun ♥♥♥♥ happening at any given time. If you're good at it, you can beat it really quickly. I have two problems with it, though. First of all, the settings menu is kind of not great. You can't review tutorials, view the controls, or change mapping within the game. This isn't really a huge deal, but I did end up skipping the dialogue that told me how to do a flip in the air, which in the final area becomes an important mechanic, and it was annoying trying to figure out how to do one. Not a huge deal, just a slight annoyance.My second problem is that I want more of it. There's an endless mode, and various score attacks and time trials included, which admittedly I have not done yet (I'll probably mess around with them a bit), but in terms of core content I don't think it was getting stale yet by the time it ended, and really would have liked to see some more areas and levels and songs (the soundtrack ends up looping a fair few times by the time you beat the game, which is inevitable due to how the game is designed, but a few more songs would have been nice), because they're all so good. It's not the worst problem to have, it just means I want more of this game than exists. I know I haven't messed around with the time trials or endless modes yet, but I don't think they're going to radically alter the game for me. If I play them and it ends up changing things for me, I'll make sure to update this. As it stands, it's a pretty easy recommend despite the caveats. I really loved my time with the game, and it's great to look at.
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: Tanuki Sunset is an extremely fun game.This is the kind of difficult game that I can just sit back and relax with while I keep my brain engaged just enough to know what I'm doing right and wrong. This isn't an easy game, of course, but as long as you don't get frustrated at it, it'll show you a great time. It's not a complicated game, just, check it out, you'll probably like it if you go into it with the right mindset.(but also the beach levels aren't great)
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this game. I actually got to hear the interview with the developers with Lenovo which was really cool. The guys really put a lot of work into this game. Small developers always make better games and this game is no exception. You could run this game on any lower end graphics card no problem. If you don't know where the settings are for the game, it is the radio and just press A on a controller or whatever key substitute for keyboard. I personally used a controller most of the time and was a lot easier. The levels were a lot of fun! I hope the developers continue to add levels or maybe another story to this game. I beat all the levels at the time of this review. To the developers: Keep up the great work! Looking forward to whatever you put out next! Oh btw for some reason the achievements weren't registering at all because I did some of the things they require and they haven't registered as completed.

_childDocuments_.review: few problems that definitely need to be fixed in coming updates. its obvious the devs want a game that people can just relax and vibe to but its hard to do that when certain parts of the game are too difficult or straight up broken. First, if I am falling off the edge of the road while drifting and even one wheel slides off the road Tanuki stands straight up, which completely ends the drift and guarantees my restart even if I had a chance to recover (fix that) and in the 3rd world the crabs should walk side to side on the road instead of just following the player because it makes it borderline impossible to get past a wave of crabs without picking up one or two (fix that). my reviews are usually one to two sentences but i feel like this game deserves to know exactly what some issues are so that the devs can see and work on it. 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Tanuki Sunset is the perfect example of a 15 dollar game. A singular polished concepts with a nice touch of depth, that doesn't try to be bigger than it is. It's fun, with trials and customization options to keep you coming back. After you beat it, it's the perfect game to leave installed to just chill and listen to the great soundtrack while riding through some levels. Highly Recommend as a fun side game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: It's good casual fun! Worth $15 if you like raccoons or hate crabs. You can fling them off your board on jumps, which probably doesn't ever get old.My only gripes:1. I wish that you could continue a drift when changing directions, because it would be fun to try to keep one going as long as possible.2. I wish there was more terrain to skate on, such as quarter pipes, tunnels, rails, etc.3. I wish there was a mode w/ a lower road that you can't fall off of, and then other roads branch above it with lots of ramps and features.4. The seagull and little raccoon don't show up often enough.5. Can you imagine spending years developing a game about a raccoon, and not knowing what a raccoon looks like? They're Plantigrade, not Digitigrade. They also don't have canine paw pads. I guess "Tanuki" is a fitting name, since this raccoon is part dog.I know it looks like a lot of complaints, but it's still a fun game, and good for listening to your own tunes with. The included soundtrack is a 4.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun little game to just vibe to. The core gameplay, while simple and arcade-y, feels extremely polished and you'll find yourself in a state of flow within seconds. The visuals and soundtrack of course play a huge role in accomplishing this as well. Even though the music is great, it can get a bit repetitive if you're playing for an extended period of time. Two or three additional songs might have helped alleviate that. I noticed a few typos in the dialogue as well, but that hardly matters when the core experience is so solid.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm awful at this genre, not gonna lie - but this is the most fun I've had with a game of this nature in ages. No rage, only vaporwave. Cosmetics. Fun play. Tricks. Badass raccoon. I can see myself playing this on plane rides for work regularlyt. Overall, easy 9.5/10. Fix some of the grammar mistakes and some of the weirdness with default mouse controls and I'll give it a 10, for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: What's something about this game I don't like! The main story mode is majestic with it's long flowing courses, Cool cast of characters you meet along the journey. Lets not forget the absolute banger soundtrack bringing that 80's funk to fit the Retrowave art style. After getting done with the story you can head over to the Arcade machine and get a good challenge trying to beat times and scores on tracks that do not appear in the story. I can't wait to sink more time into Tanuki Sunset

_childDocuments_.review: the game is surprisingly hard to get to grips with but is charming enough both terms of audio and visuals to hold your interest long enough to learn the deceptively difficult gameplay, though my only gripe with the game is the "story" is too short for my liking, even though I had at least around 60 restarts on various levels, the games story only took me a little over 3 hours to beat. Yes there are trials to complete but they are in my opinion too hard for a causal player such as myself. I highly recommended waiting for a discount or if you're really desperate to either play the game or to support the dev, to pick it up now. I do still recommended the game but it's just a little too short for my liking

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this release with great anticipation and it was well worth the wait! If you've played endless runner games before this has some unique mechanics and level variation to set it apart. Unlike normal endless runners it has levels and goals and a trace of a story with an endearing ending. Something I noticed that I really appreciated was the levels have a hint of random generation, which is very nice when you have to repeat a sequence many times due to falling off the level or crashing. If I could change anything I'd suggest online leaderboards and the option to change the graphical fidelity prior to the main hub. I use steam on my mediocre school laptop and the intro level was very laggy and incredibly difficult. Once I beat it and got to the hub area I was able to change the graphics settings and it was smooth sailing. Overall I had a blast with this one and the aesthetic and soundtrack are certainly going to keep me coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing as how my main two primal needs have been satisfied, that being skateboarding and raccoons, I must say that this game is for cool kids only. Is the game perfect? Well, I don't want to delve too much into quantum physics, but let's just say that I can dress up the main character like a ghetto Elton John so that must count for something. Speaking of which, I don't know where the false narrative that this game is "relaxing" came from. Midnight City 2-2 gives me such bad road rage that it makes my pizza delivery gig look like a peaceful protest in comparison. Homicidal anger aside, I don't think any of us can deny that if Tanuki was anthropomorphic and had a set of abs, we'd all be on that ♥♥♥♥ like Monica on Lou Bega or Bill Clinton in Mambo No. 5. Would certainly recommend.  Hail Satan

_childDocuments_.review: I've never had a game both chill me out and hype me up at the same time. The vaporwave aesthetic somehow fits so perfectly, the music on this soundtrack is SUPERB, the controls harken back to the PS2 era (which was exactly their goal, going off of their description of the game), and it all comes together for a fantastic experience. I can see me picking this up when I'm waiting for friends for multiplayer games or for when I need a pick-me-up. Absolutely recommend this game for anyone and everyone. Picked up day one at full price and have absolutely no regrets.

_childDocuments_.review: I discovered the store page for this game one day on a whim, I loved the concept of it and shortly after downloaded the demo. I loved the demo and likely put 30-40 hours into it just doing the first stage over and over, finding new tricks and how to get the most points. And now after months of waiting Its everything I hoped it be and more.   This game is an arcade "racing?" game, your only really in a race during time trials and when the seagull shows up, otherwise your primary objective is to get to the end. You collect bits and rack up points to get a higher and higher score again this is an arcade type game so it might not be for everyone. There isnt very much depth to it, its just extremely replayable because of the fun gameplay.   The gameplay is very fun and exactly what you might expect it to be. You long board down a sky path doing sick drifts and going fast. There is a bit more to it but this is a review not analysis. The different trails very distinct unique styles and each introduce new obsticals. there is a bit of a learning curve, but its extremely fun trust me.Just looking at the style of this game you know what kind of music your getting yourself into, and its all good.Again this is an arcadey game so there is not much story, the characters are fun, and what story there is I appriciate. The campaign is short and sweet and after words you have the challenge arcade to grind at.A few nitpicks I do have is 1. I may be a bit of a hypocrate for saying this, but there are only 3 maps as of right techically 4 I guess. I love the maps and If i had 30 hours of fun with only 1 map on a demo I can certinely have plently of fun with 3. I just hope more updates come out for this game with more maps, story pebbles, and features. I dont know what rewind games plans to do in the future, move on? or make updates? Regardless its not that big a deal I love these maps. 2. You cant pet Dio and thats not ok. 3. There is a bug where crabs wont get knocked off by garbage/dump trucks, idk why, but they just phase through them.Overall I like this game, its good, biased? maybe, But i dont care because its good. The lads at rewind games keep cranking out bangers.EDIT: I REVISE MY ♥♥♥♥ ASS STUPID ASS STATEMENT! YOU CAN PET THE DOG 10/10 PERFECT GAME!

_childDocuments_.review:
Tanuki Sunset is a third-person longboarding game where players follow Tanuki, a rad raccoon with a longboard and a dream to land on the cover of the #1 magazine in Sunset Island: FISH!

Players must master longboard drifting to make their way from mountains ranges, through the city and down to the beach of Sunset Island. Throughout the journey players will guide Tanuki to perform rad tricks, jump-off ramps, all while avoiding cars and multiple obstacles. Collecting Tanuki Bits along the way is important to redeem for items and gear at Bob's Skate Shop, where players can customize Tanuki's outfit and longboard to better suit their personal style.

name: DEATHLOOP
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition DELUXE EDITION CONTENT Base Game Unique Weapon: Eat The Rich Tribunal Unique Weapon: .44 Karat Fourpounder Unique Weapon: Chrome Demon MG-1 Pepper Mill Character Skin: 'Party Crasher' Colt Character Skin: 'Sharp Shooter' Julianna Original Game Soundtrack Selections Two Trinkets (equippable buffs) About the Game DEATHLOOP is a next-gen first person shooter from Arkane Lyon, the award-winning studio behind Dishonored. In DEATHLOOP, two rival assassins are trapped in a mysterious timeloop on the island of Blackreef, doomed to repeat the same day for eternity. As Colt, the only chance for escape is to end the cycle by assassinating eight key targets before the day resets. Learn from each cycle - try new paths, gather intel, and find new weapons and abilities. Do whatever it takes to break the loop. If At First You Don’t Succeed... Die, Die Again Every new loop is an opportunity to change things up. Use the knowledge you gain from each attempt to change up your playstyle, stealthily sneaking through levels or barreling into the fight, guns-blazing. In each loop you’ll discover new secrets, gather intel on your targets as well as the island of Blackreef, and expand your arsenal. Armed with a host of otherworldly abilities and savage weaponry, you’ll utilize every tool at your command to execute takedowns that are as striking as they are devastating. Customize your loadout wisely to survive this deadly game of hunter vs hunted. SINGLE PLAYER GAMEPLAY INJECTED WITH DEADLY MULTIPLAYER Are you the hero or the villain? You’ll experience DEATHLOOP’s main story as Colt, hunting down targets across the island of Blackreef to break the loop and earn your freedom. All the while, you’ll be hunted by your rival Julianna, who can be controlled by another player. So if you’re feeling devious, you, too, can step into Julianna’s stylish sneakers and invade another player’s campaign to kill Colt. The multiplayer experience is completely optional, and players can choose to have Julianna controlled by AI within their campaign. The island Of Blackreef – Paradise Or Prison Arkane is renowned for magnificently artistic worlds with multiple pathways and emergent gameplay. DEATHLOOP will present a stunning, retro-future, 60s-inspired environment, that feels like a character within itself. While Blackreef may be a stylish wonderland, for Colt it is his prison, a world ruled by decadence where death has no meaning, and delinquents party forever while keeping him captive.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm changing my review from positive to negative because "Protect the Loop" is now impossible, one of the main modes of gameplay has completely broken. It can take over an hour to get a match then it rubber band lags so bad you can't even equip a weapon without it disappearing back into the holster. There's no way to fight Colt if you can't turn in a direction without rubber banding back to the direction you were facing before.And the devs have just completely abandoned the game, and went on to disgrace themselves with Redfall. This game was awesome, I guess single player is still awesome, but multiplayer is dead and there's no Single Player for Julianna.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of a game where you have to kill 8 people in one life, or else you start over wasn't enticing at first to me, but as I learned more and more about it over time, I decided to give this a go, and I liked it a lot!  Going back to the four maps during different times and learning about the world/routines of these characters was fun to do.  The combat is fun, though I did tire of the Juliana invasion gimmick near the end of the game despite really liking it at first.  If this game interests you,  I say give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: Performance aside, there has been enough mention of that. The game is mediocre at best which is why I would like to give this a middle thumb if I could, it has no idea what it wants to be and this is where the game falls over, it is an assassination game which plays more like a shooter. The game clearly wants you to play sneaky sneaky but nearly every weapon is designed to go in blazing. It wants to be an fps but it does not feel like one when you play it as such, it wants to be dishonored but the sneaking aspect has been simplified to the point of feeling like it was ripped out of an fps from 15 years ago. I feel that Arkane took parts of Dishonored, parts of Prey and somehow made it worse. This game would have been perfectly placed a few years ago, now however it all feels very outdated and pretty mediocre across the board.Edit: I have changed my review to positive, even though all of my criticisms still apply, the game has developed into something that just does not feel like it should be thumbed down. I do want to add however that the combat gets stale really fast, the weapon variation is just terrible and the powers are ripped right out of the last gen.  I think the game is a 6/10 with everything taken into consideration, so a very low pass.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game by Arkane although not on the level of Prey and Dishonoured 1&2. The gunplay, visual style and voice performances are excellent. Story and general structure of the game are good but not great. Would have liked more interactions in some way between Cole and the visionaries. During the middle part of the game the Deathloop's time and location structure is a lot of fun as you put together some of the optional puzzles and go through the main quest. Towards the end however, it can be a bit of chore to go through the first few steps which are never particularly difficult but take some time. I HIGHLY recommend that you turn off the objective markers on the HUD as it makes the game much more engaging rather than just following the markers everywhere. Some of the optional puzzles do a good job making you feel smart and make good use of the loop to build some intrigue. The Residuum system works really well although I found I peaked in power a little too early for my liking.On a technical level, I was lucky that the game ran fine (1070 GTX card) with 1 crash during my roughly 23-24 hour Colt play-through. Multiplayer also worked reasonably well for me and was lots of fun as both Colt and Julianna. Invasions reward smart power usage, map knowledge and some amount of trickery. You do get some games where the lag is horrible and the experience is just miserable, I'd say this happened about 1-2 in every 10 games for me.Overall probably an 8-8.5/10 for me. _childDocuments_.review: One of Arkane Studios' most inventive and intelligently designed games to date and EASILY the most stylish. Dishonored 2 sits atop my list of favorite Arkane games and I'm happy to say that Deathloop is now seated alongside it, tied for first place. Deathloop's game, level and art design are so intentional and deliberate in the best of ways. The 1960s aesthetic visually pops with a wide spectrum of colors and there is always something that catches the wandering eye. The gameplay is smooth and polished to a shine, maybe even better than the Dishonored series. Gunplay is as tight and responsive as you would expect from a AAA FPS but the addition of the slabs and trinkets give the moment to moment gameplay so much depth and variety. The four districts that you explore are fairly compact and self-contained but they are filled to the brim with secrets to find and routes to explore. In fact, I'd go so far as to say that these four levels might be the most well designed in an Arkane Studios game. Even though you'll be returning to each area again and again, the amount of unique routes to take and unique ways to play each level are almost limitless. Even though I wish there were maybe one or two more districts to explore, Arkane made good use of their development time by condensing the content down to four tightly constructed levels. The story is a rollercoaster of mystery that incorporates some really cool investigative elements even if some of it might be construed as "too handholdy" I quite enjoyed the way allowed me to uncover the secrets of Blackreef on my own terms. Deathloop also has some of the best voicework in a AAA title I've ever experienced. Jason Kelley as the protagonist Colt is a revelation and had me rolling on the floor laughing at several points! Ozioma Akagha also provides a unique voice as Julianna, who constantly goades and belittles you via the ingame radio. The invasion PVP is a great addition to the game to spice up the experience and for Arkane's first proper attempt at incorporating a multiplayer component, I have to say I was pleasantly surprised by it's quality. Deathloop also features one of the best original soundtracks in recent years with incredibly immersive ambient tracks and catchy radio tunes.Overall, Deathloop is easily the best and most fun game I played in 2021 and it has cemented itself as one of my new all-time favorites. I implore you: if you find the game for a good sale price, it is ABSOLUTELY worth your money and the investment of your time! Arkane Outsiders For Life! :D

_childDocuments_.review: This will probably be an unpopular opinion but I think Deathloop is the best work Arkane has put out yet.  It takes the fun and addictive gameplay of Dishonored but now you can actually kill people without constantly being berated for what a bad person you are.  The powers are also mostly taken from Dishonored too.  Though they aren’t as powerful in this game it's still a lot of fun to play around with, that being said you’ll almost certainly only use flash and the invisible power as they are just inherently the best ones.  Dishonored had the same problem though they remedied this in a way by making your power regenerate fully instead of needing elixirs or whatever.  This really allows you to play around with your powers rather than just neglecting the high demanding ones.Then they have the excellent gunplay of Prey and pump it up to 11.  Every gun in this game has a real punch to it and it’s just so much fun to shoot people.  The game is both very generous with its ammo, having dispensers on every corner but also limiting your ammo capacity to only 2-3 mags.  It makes refilling fully after a fight fully viable but running low mid-fight is also a problem you have to worry about.What I’m trying to say is they took all of the annoying and debilitating gameplay of their old games and fixed them to maximize fun.I’ve heard a few different people say how disappointing the story is or how boring it is.  By that I mean I read like 3 other bad reviews but I wanted to address it anyway.   It’s no Bioshock or anything.  But the story is still solid, fun, and interesting.  It might think it’s a little smarter than it really is at times but it does it in such a way that makes it almost endearing.What really carries the story from an interesting but okay story into something great is the characters.  They are all interesting, quirky, and most importantly, well written.  Especially Colt, he balances a thin line between being a psychotic killing machine and a struggling man stuck in the wrong place.  The writing that pops up along the walls and in the air depicting visualizing your train of thought is also a cool touch.  Showing the inner workings of Colt’s mind, growing the character subconsciously, literally.It can be hard to take a game like Deathloop seriously so the game as a whole has a much lighter tone.  Sure it goes into a lot of sci-fi mambo jumbo about space-time but the world also has this sort of wacky “taking-the-piss” sort of attitude which works really well in its favor.  Think something along the lines of Borderlands or GTA V.The mystery is definitely a key aspect of the game and I think it's done wonderfully.  It really incentivizes exploring every nook and cranny, and because the maps are so small and packed full of secrets it doesn’t seem daunting to actually search a map top to bottom.  It’s all very digestible in a nice format that’s easy to understand and play but also still feels rewarding.  It’s going to be a long time before I get the same excitement from exploring as I did in this game.As you explore the maps of Deathloop you’ll discover passcodes, areas of interest, and important locations of key characters and events.  This is all saved in your inventory where you can track leads that will act as a mission with a marker and will auto show passcodes on safes and doors you’ve found the passcode to.  It seems a little daunting at first but once you get into it it’s actually very streamlined and enjoyable.Some people seem to have a real problem with how you discover clues.  They want to have to physically write everything down and learn important information based on subtle dialogue ques you can easily miss in the chaos.  They even call it hand holding to have your character remember codes they read.  I can’t stand this mentality.  Because for maybe null .01% of people will find that fun, for the rest of us it would just be frustrating.  Most of the time when I play a video game I just want to sit back and relax.  Just enjoy myself I don’t have the kind of time or patience to write out everything I hear.  One of the big reasons it took me so long to boot this game up was because I thought it might be a game that requires a lot of physical writing.  But I love the system it has in place.  Acting as a mission structure rather than having you run around like a headless chicken.The difficulty is kind of weird.  On the one hand, you can sit in a sightline and kill all the NPCs on a map as they file in one by one in front of your gun.  But on that same note, they will flank you and coordinate attacks around you.  It’s both a rather smart AI and a vastly stupid one.One thing that it does very different from other games is how it treats stealth.  In that if you are in their line of sight of someone THEY WILL SEE YOU.  The bar fills up almost immediately and then it will spread.  If you manage to hide after being seen that one solitary person won't just give up they will tell their friends around them and have that whole area looking for you.  This can be fun as it makes the stealth a lot more satisfying but also a lot more annoying as if you are even a microsecond too early entering a building or jumping to cover you’ll alert the entire island.There is a silver lining to this though.  The area of effect for your spot is dependent on the area.  So if you mess up and are spotted you can kill the people in that small arena and the people in the other parts of the map won't notice.  To some, this is “unrealistic” or maybe a flaw in the AI but it’s a deliberate design choice.If you’ve ever played a game like Hitman or even Dishonored you probably know how being spotted can spiral things out of control for you.  It completely puts an end to any semblance of stealth and the game becomes a pure action game.  With the tight area of effect stealth is still a viable option even after messing up.  It lets you continuously think on the spot.  Once well thought out missions can spiral out of control in a way that doesn’t push you into a corner with only one way left to complete the level.  There are still a hundred different ways to take on a situation even after a hard fight.  It’s just textbook good game design all around.There is also no difficulty slider and for once I actually appreciate it.  it's a system that makes running and gunning your way through possible but not always the baseline easiest solution.  All it takes is one enemy with a half-broken SMG to take half your health if you’re not careful.  This may seem like a turn-off at first but the enemies are usually pretty stupid and will only get a solid kill off you if you play stupid or get overconfident.  I died more than I’d like to admit and it was almost always my fault.  I never felt like I was cheated or that the game was unfair.  It was always some stupid half-sighted plan I concocted that ended in disaster.It’s a hard sell but it will probably help to tamper your expectations.  I know that’s ironic to say after I just praised it but I feel like if you go into this expecting a masterpiece you might be a bit disappointed.  I think the reason I think it is so great is because I didn’t really expect anything from it.  It sort of came and went and thought I wanted to play it I just couldn’t shell out the $60 for it.  Also, I had heard mixed things about it which also dampened my outlook on it.  If my friend hadn’t gifted it to me for my birthday I probably wouldn’t have touched it for a good while.  It’s the fact I thought it’d be just okay and it ended up being fantastic that probably boosts the score up a bit more than it deserves.But, to be fair I started out already biased towards Deathloop.  I am an Arkane simp, a Bethesda shill, a gimmick FPS defender, a story over gameplay cuck, and a dirty casual.  But the game still shines through and stands as one of the best games I’ve ever played.  Fight me.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this game gets my highest recommendation. It is one of the best playgrounds filled with the most fun toys I have ever seen in video games. You should only pass on this if you just don't enjoy first person shooters.Even if you're not into stealth games I would recommend this. I am also not a huge fan of sneaking around and slowly picking enemies off. However, unlike most games that focus on stealth, this one not only allows you to go in guns blazing, it encourages it. About half way through the game I got a gun that shot exploding bullets. The explosion would go off at roughly the same time as my gunshot, so enemies would always look towards the explosion rather than my position. This enabled me to be "stealthy" while still playing fast and loud. Stealth through explosives, I've never seen anything like it in any other game.There are a couple of times where you're going to have to be quiet, at least for a little while. But that just brings up another thing I love about the game, the sheer amount of options allow you to plan and equip yourself for any situation that arises. In that way it reminds me of From Software's titles like Dark Souls and Elden ring. Your game plan is just as important as your execution, and when you pull off a plan perfectly it feels great.Another way Deathloop reminds me of From Software games is the environmental story telling and deep lore hidden everywhere. There are bits of the backstory that I completely missed until I was reading about it after beating the game. That might sound lame to some people, but I personally love unraveling a game's mysteries both through playing it and interacting with the community. That being said the main story of the game is told clearly with a very satisfying twist in the late game.This game is a 10, the gameplay, the graphic design, the soundtrack, it's all perfect. And for those wondering the game ran great on my Ryzen 7 3600x/RTX 2060 Super. I had the settings cranked all the way up with DLSS set to quality. The game looked amazing and the frame rate was rock solid. I did run into one crash as a level was starting, but other than that my experience was free of glitches.In closing I will say it again, I cannot recommend this game highly enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This plays like a combat sandbox in Arkane’s Dishonored engine. Judged on that basis alone, it’s a success. And, there are worse concepts for a game! The Dishonored series’ well-kept secret is that that they’re pretty fun action games. Many players—myself included—never figure that out, instead choosing to flagellate themselves through nonviolent, stealth-forward experiences. But the most fun and emergent moments in Dishonored always come when you screw up and things get loud. DEATHLOOP does away with non-violence altogether and encourages you to get loud from the start. It’s liberating.In almost every other way, however, it’s very mediocre. Immersive sim fans will be very disappointed.There is almost no plot—or, at least, no sign of one by the 20-hour mark. You learn only the most superficial details about the world you’re in.The characters are boring and generic. This seems like an obvious missed opportunity. The setup is that you have to hunt a rogues’ gallery of villains, but they all turn out to be variations on the same brand of vulgar, arrogant, vaguely icky internet troll. Gameplay-wise they’re indistinguishable from their henchmen; I often didn’t realize I had killed one until I got a HUD notification that the last guy I mowed down was important.Everyone is written as angry, petty, and dumb. This includes, perplexingly, Cole and Julianna, the two protagonists on the cover. The cool, suave, mod style promised by the box art is nowhere to be found in DEATHLOOP’s actual dialogue (where it CAN be found, thankfully, is in the game’s soundtrack. All the combat tracks are bangers).The time loop thing has no real impact on gameplay. Functionally, it just results in the game’s four maps having different features at four different times of day, for a total of 16 levels. “Solving the time loop” is a simple matter of following hud waypoints and rummaging through logs; there are no notable puzzles in the game.Perhaps most damningly for a combat sandbox, there are no interesting weapons or powers. Everything is pulled from the standard post-2010 FPS toolkit.One cool aspect, I’ll say, is the drop-in competitive multiplayer. Players who enjoy an occasional FPS skirmish might welcome the variety, and the concept of dueling 1v1 in an immersive sim level is interesting. But, these “invasions” happen at random and materially increase the stress of the game, so it’s good that you can turn them off. They won’t be for everyone.I’m only 20 hours in, and I intuit this to be maybe 2/3 of the way through the game, so it’s possible that big things could be waiting for me in the final third. But I’m not sure I’ll make it. It’s become a slog. I can’t help but think that it would’ve been a better use of my time to instead do another playthrough of Prey or Dishonored, and just go loud and have fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: In many ways, Deathloop feels familiar to previous Arkane Studios titles, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing. What makes it shine is not just how it offsets this familiarity by introducing a time loop element but, more importantly, how it skilfully avoids frustration by constantly making you feel like you’re learning something new.Venturing across Blackreef did lose freshness by the 30-hour mark, but the vast majority of that time was filled with loud gunfights, intense games of cat and mouse against invading Juliannas, lots of sneaking, manipulating the environment to score satisfying kills, and plenty of discovery that made us feel like a master detective that’s pretty badass with a gun.Deathloop turns both succeeding and failing into learning experiences and never makes you miss the lack of a quicksave option. It’s a mean feat that sets it apart from other games, and one of several reasons why it should be on the list of any immersive sim fans out there. It might not be Arkane’s best game and Blackreef may struggle clearly defining a personality for itself, but it’s certainly no stranger to great moments..

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I recommend the gameplay, I don't recommend the story.The gameplay is engaging and the trinkets / slabs can change the style of play and strategies you can use to a high degree. Overall a thumbs up for the gameplay.The story is a car crash. The mainline quest leaves a great deal untold, and I'm not convinced that 100%ing the game would improve it much. The endings are unsatisfying. They gave me the same unfulfilled feeling I had at the end of Bioshock Infinite. It felt like someone failed to make the metaphysical crap come together in a meaningful way and spent far too much time on that rather than on a narrative story that held together. _childDocuments_.review: A marginal technical improvement over Dishonored 2. Still extremely shoddy, wait for patches. You won't get a good technical experience regardless of your hardware if you wish to play at a high refresh rate like 120 or 144 hz. Might get abandoned without ever being completely fixed like Dishonored 2 was. No DLSS. FidelityFX is broken in this game with far right and bottom pixels not being correctly post-processed leaving an extremely distracting discolored line at the edges of the screen. This game has noticeable micro-stuttering which could be caused by Denuvo (the anti-piracy software used by this game) or simply the engine itself. I'm not sure if the fact that Arkane returned to the borderline broken Void engine without fixing it and ignored the performance concerns from fans shows their incompetence or a lack of consideration for the people that play their games, but it definitely shows that they are not a studio that learns from their mistakes. I see this as the main problem. This isn't a case of the developers simply not having enough time to iron out the kinks in their engine. The Void engine was bad when Dishonored 2 launched and the Void engine is still bad right now. Arkane seem fine with continuously releasing their games in a terrible state and not learning whatsoever from previous launches. It's now clear that Prey was an exception and not a new direction for the studio. These things would be disappointing coming from an indie studio, but should be completely unacceptable coming from a larger studio like Arkane. I do not recommend that you buy this game.NOTE: I played this name on an NVIDIA RTX 2070 Super. The FidelityFX issue might not exist on AMD cards.

_childDocuments_.review: The basic premise of this game is to try and break a time loop that you are caught in. This requires you to assassinate certain targets scattered across 4 different areas and 4 different times of day. The end goal is to get it all done in a single day before the day ends and resets the loop.I'll start with the good since it'll be a lot shorter list than the bad. Colt and Juliana, the 2 main characters, are pretty decently written and the voice acting for both of them is well done. There are also some pretty cool stylistic choices in the game.  The combat is functional although a bit uninspired.None of the issues are necessarily deal breakers but when you add them all up they certainly outweigh the average game play.- The Denuvo anti cheat definitely hampers game performance.- The lack of enemy types is staggering. I get it was going to mostly be humans given the setting but they could at least have some more varied weapons, abilities, or combat style.- The weapons are extremely basic and the upgrades are pretty uninspired and not very impactful.- The very few powers/abilities are all knock offs from previous Dishonored games and due to the loop mechanic you can only run 2 per level. - The actual "loop" mechanic wears on you very quickly and the 4 locations that you constantly have to replay to solve the puzzle and break the loop get old fast.- The 4 maps on the surface seem like they offer multiple ways to accomplish your goal but honestly most of the time your first basic option is just as easy as maybe a path that takes a bit more experimenting to figure out.- The enemy AI is really bad and doesn't adapt to anything you do. You can typically go loud immediately and pretty easily stand in a doorway and mow them all down one by one as they all run at you mindlessly.- The progression system that allows you to spend in game currency to keep slabs (powers), guns, and mods across your loops is really shallow. The currency is so abundant that I got good enough upgrades to complete the game easily very early in and the powers weren't specific enough for me to care to switch between levels.The biggest issue and primary reason I can't recommend the game is the story and the way the mystery unfolds. The mystery of the loop fades pretty quickly as the game forces you to take out targets to understand their patterns and what times of day they do certain actions. The problem is that every time the game presents you with an opportunity to solve a puzzle or get a target in the right place and time you just get a way point that essentially points you to a note or sign that tells you what to do. This really becomes an issue when you finally take out all targets independently and unlock all clues and get a cut scene of the exact order and manner that you need to take them out and break the loop. The ending of the story was also pretty anticlimactic without going into detail.

_childDocuments_.review: +Excellent core gameplay, similar to that of Dishonored. In Deathloop, your goal is to kill all 8 of the game's bosses in a single day to escape a time loop. The problem is, their schedules have to be manipulated in such a way to make this possible. This involves fighting through 4 different maps that each go through dramatic changes depending on the time of day. Each map is essentially like 4 maps in one, with there being a version for morning, noon, afternoon, and night. Killing all 8 bosses on the same day is like one giant jigsaw puzzle, and you'll have to gather information on each map at different times of day in order to put the pieces together.+Satisfying progression system. When a day ends, you lose all of your items and abilities unless you've infused them to your character. The feeling of growth as you add more weapons, abilities, and perks to your permanent arsenal comes at a nice and steady pace.+Great overall presentation. I don't care much for the 60's aesthetic, but it's well executed by the art direction and soundtrack.+Multiplayer that lets you invade another player's game.+Maps are varied and highly detailed.+Entertaining characters.-DEEPLY flawed premise. While it is interesting, it ultimately involves visiting the same locations A LOT of times until you figure out how to beat the game. That may be the nature of a game centered around a time loop, but it can get tiring.-There's only one path to beating the game. If you were hoping to solve the puzzle in your own way, that's not happening. That being said, HOW each boss dies is still up to you.-Enemy AI is very easy to exploit.-Weak ending.
