_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It’s Dishonored. It’s a little Prey. It’s pretty funky good and bad. It’s a solid 6/10.Let me speak frankly, if you have played Dishonored you’ve already played this game. I’m not talking about the visuals or the story, but the core gameplay is Dishonored. Speaking directly to the artistic side of the game, Arkane nails it. The game has its own style much in the same way Dishonored and Prey feel like their own unique worlds. The voice acting is on point. These actors are directed exceptionally well and give life to the cast.If you’re a fan of Arkane’s super powered abilities well the ‘Slab’ abilities are similar to the Prey/Dishonored powers with a few new exceptions. Teleport still being my favorite! The gunplay is without a doubt Prey and some RPG weapon quality/perk system built. Each weapon has personality and feels unique enough. More importantly the player can feel the impact of the weapons.Deathloop introduces a few new things such as the changing of environments through the day’s cycles. Each area is its own unique playground of the island and changes layout, AI, and VIP placement depending on which of the 4 day cycles the player visits. This is important because events and information that drives investigations may be tied to one of these 4 cycles. Player’s will be challenged to think about what tasks to prioritize and track.Arkane emphasizes the “Play your way” which is refreshing because it does feel like Prey where the player can choose their rout of subterfuge, stealth, or direct combat without feeling restricted on how to approach a situation. AI may be stupid (and they are very stupid) but they are keen sighted make no mistake they will punish overconfidence and carelessness. Overall, the marketing has you believe players will die a lot… mmm-but not really. If you’re a cool customer it’s easy to avoid death. Players of all skill levels will find something to enjoy here.There is a chance of being invaded too. However, it’s not as intense as the feeling one would get from being invaded in Dark Souls. It does get a little harry if you’re on your last “life”. In my experience I’ve only had AI (which is awfully dumb as previously mentioned). Lots of trouble with connecting to the Bethesda servers. When I do it’s… well more waiting than I’m happy with to just invade someone’s game. My personal experience feels like I’m missing out on 1/3rd of this game. Great idea on paper but functions horribly, so it feels like dead weight. One may as well play in offline mode and forget the “PVP” aspect exists.As for the technical issues mentioned in other posts... this is one player’s opinion. I believe everyone is going to have their own issues with the game. Personally, I have been lucky not to experience any raw technical problems, or show stopping bugs. However, with having connection issues with the Bethesda servers (yes my anti-virus has white listed the game) it feels like I’m missing out on a very intentional part of what the developers had in mind for the user experience. I still have to give the game credit where it’s due. Deathloop has good gunplay, a tried-and-true gameplay foundation. It is a story driven game with enough lore and a cast of crazy (literally) characters to build the unique and weird worlds which Arkane is known for.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those occasions where I wish Steam had a neutral review option.Deathloop managed to grab me with it's initial concept. The premise of a version of Dishonoured that had no pressure to use non-lethal means or remain a ghost at all times seemed like the change to that gameplay formula I had wanted, and the concept of needing to solve an island wide murder puzzle using a time loop sounded engaging as well. And while the game did offer both of these things, their execution felt wanting.The gameplay has a good feel to it, the guns feel punchy and using the powers alongside them feels fun and intuitive. The problem in this area is that the game severely lacks difficulty. After a few loops almost none of the standard enemies you face will pose any threat to you whatsoever and the Visionaries, the targets whom you must assasinate over the course of the day, are only marginally more difficult to kill. The sheer ease with which you can wipe out entire levels means that the multiple playstyles the game offers feel completely token, as you will never really feel the need to change your approach once you settle on one.This problem I would accept completely if the games murder puzzle was complex, as it would make sense that the challenge wouldn't be killing the visionaries but simply finding out how to kill them all in a single day. However the puzzle itself is barely a puzzle at all, the game offers you objectives that if followed will eventually give you the solution with no real effort or thought. This extends so far that even the final list of tasks you must do to kill every Visionary is outright handed to you as a quest chain. Since there are no alternate solutions to this murder puzzle the idea that you're using the loop to figure things out yourself falls completely flat.The invasions by other players (or an NPC if you so wish) do up the difficulty when they occur, and for the first half of the game I saw these invasions as a fun diversion from my plans. However after a while even this aspect of the game became repetitive, with the invasions moving from a fun diversion to something annoying I had to get out of the way before finishing off the loop.While these complaints mean that the game on the whole feels like a much weaker product than it had the potential to be, I must confess that I did still enjoy my time with Deathloop. The writing (on everything that isn't the terminal conversations) feels great, with a great deal of energy and lightness of tone to it. The interactions between Colt, the player character, and Julianna, who works as both the invader and a constant antagonistic voice on the radio, are a particular highlight, full of funny moments and great character building. Sadly the story does not manage to stick the landing, ending on a rather sudden note that left me feeling rather unfulfilled.In summary Deathloop is a game with many problems that prevent it from coming close to reaching the potential of its concept, but if you simply want some fun Dishonoured style gameplay with some decent writing then it can at least deliver on that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is yet another game that is unfairly treated by the binary "yes" or "no" review system. Did I have a great time and beat the game? Absolutely! I really enjoyed the game from beginning to end. I love a timeloop story, and getting to experience that in a FPS game was a lot of fun. Arkane's game design from the Dishonored games meshes extremely well with a game designed around trying a scenario over and over again until you get it just right. One of the biggest issues with the Dishonored games was how much they encouraged savescumming through the whole experience, and having the game be built all around that is great. However, this game has 1 major flaw that makes this game very difficult to recommend to other people. And that issue is the lack of manual save. This game has levels that can take easily an hour or more to complete based on how you go about them, and being forced to redo all of it because you alt-tab'ed out of the game to look at Discord and it crashed. I really wish they incorporated the Fire Emblem system where you can save whenever, but then the save is wiped as soon as it's loaded. The fact this game has been out for a year now and that system still doesn't exist means it never will, so my review will stay as a "no" with a caveat. As time has gone on, the game has become a lot more stable and crashes are very rare these days. So if you're the type that never has to turn off a game early to go do something else, and you can quit playing whenever you want without any outside forces upon you, then yeah go for it. Also, small spoiler for the end: it was really disappointing. I didn't want all the questions answered, but I'd love to have had ...at least a few more questions answered than we got.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has many of the hallmarks of another Arkane title, "Prey Mooncrash": the same type of limited  map, the same repetitive gameplay and the same general outcome (having to work out a lot of actions that you then have to perform in a strict sequence one last time at the end).If you enjoyed Mooncrash, then there are good odds you'll enjoy Deathloop. If you didn't enjoy Mooncrash, or got frustrated by its limitations, then the same is likely to happen here too.Far and away the biggest problem with Deathloop is the same problem Mooncrash had, but worse - saving your game. The game is only saved at very particular points, and the consequences of quitting the game anywhere other than at a save point can be quite serious - you can lose important equipment and discoveries that may have taken you quite some time to gather. Why Arkane Lyon didn't implement an "exit save" feature of the kind Fallout 4 has is incomprehensible to me - forcing me to play until *they* are ready to save my game can be a real fun-killer. For me, this is the worst game-save scheme I've ever encountered in a majortitle.Aside from that, Deathloop is generally good, if very repetitive. The graphics are beautiful and atmospheric, the gameplay is quite smooth, and the difficulty is balanced enough to make it challenging without being unduly frustrating. The voice acting and script are excellent. As in Prey, there aren't many weapons, and  annoyingly, you can only carry three (plus the mandatory knife). The absence of a working inventory is frustrating, as it means you will have to leave quite nice and potentially useful weapons behind in the field, to  be lost forever.I have advanced a fair way into the story after 19-odd hours, but in all honesty, I'm starting to find the game rather tedious and it's unlikely I'll finish it - that's a matter of personal preference, though: the game is definitely good enough for a thumbs-up, especially if you can get it on special.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great immersive sim from Arkane, as always. Previously, the main "problem" with Arkane games was the following: It's fun to run and gun, but that leads to a bad ending. Why are you making me play the game in a way that I don't want to (stealth and non-lethal)? - such comments can still be seen under dishonored, and even under Prey. Well this issue is fully addressed in DEATHLOOP - to beat the game you HAVE to kill your targets, and it makes no sense to not kill people since they come back to life once the loop, well, loops. As such, there are literally no non-lethal options in the game. So you're free to go around all sneaky like, taking out enemies with traps and stealth, or barge in with guns blazing and kill everyone around. More than that - you can beat one loop the first way only to go beat the next one the other way. So yeah, do what you want, play as you want - it's all here.Now, the game has four locations and four times of day, so that makes 4 versions of each of the 4 locations. This is a massive asset reuse, which leads me to believe that Arkane was working with quite a limited budget, trying to polish what they have instead of adding what they don't. They managed that magnificently - it's very interesting to see how locations change throughout the day. Now, and important clarification - I'm a huge fan of non-lethal sneak playthroughs. (So the aforementioned "problem" wasn't a problem at all for me, ever.) And I'm not a huge fan of PvP. As such, DEATHLOOP made me very wary when it was announced- Arkane removed what I like and added what I don't. Thankfully the wariness was in vain - the game is still plenty fun, and there's a single player mode that makes it so that live players don't invade you. You still get invaded by bots though, but they're hardly any trouble. Single player mode also allows you to pause the game which is the main reason I used it, actually - I need that at the moment. Overall I bought it on a small discount instead of waiting for a huge one because I really want to support Arkane - after Square Enix went full Marvel, Arkane are the only company that makes AAA immersive sims, which are arguably my favorite genre. Please, Arkane, live on and keep on giving.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool art style and polished gameplay, but that's about it. Worth like five bucks maybe if you can get it on sale.Nothing this game does is unique, and everything remotely good about it is done better elsewhere.The "Slab" system, the powers you get, are done better in Arkane's other games. Dishonored, Arx Fatalis, Dark Messiah, etc. Several of them straight up are reskinned from Dishonored. The time loop is conceptually cool for a bit, but because you can "Infuse" gear within like hour 2 of the game to make it last between loops, it doesn't really matter. As a puzzle concept, it's really just going through some small locations at different times of day with slight changes. If you like this concept, The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask did it better. There's an actual feeling of urgency there where you have to start back from day 1 with new items and knowledge. In Deathloop, it's just annoying. And it is intentionally annoying, because the protagonist will straight up say it's annoying. If you can keep your gear, and keep your knowledge, 99% of the loop is rendered irrelevant. Majora's Mask also had some items moving between your resets, but that game was also on a constant timer and you couldn't keep EVERYTHING. Also, only YOU and your direct ally knew about resetting, to everyone else, it was just the end of the world. In this, everyone loops and some even keep memories, so why bother? It doesn't make for a unique story and it doesn't serve much gameplay purpose, so why?Gaining new knowledge and planning ahead based on where you know people will be is really cool, but again, not original, and seen in better games. If you like that gameplay, I urge you to play the Hitman series. In that, the planning matters, unique kills earn more rewards, being efficient is super rewarding in and of itself, and the levels are designed around it instead of being designed like every big bad is designed to be a boss fight. Especially considering said "boss fights" are usually ended in like 4 seconds.Lastly, the weapon system. Whoever said "Hey we should have item rarities in this game" needs to be kicked in the balls. If they have no balls, give them some, and then kick them. You have:Heavy pistol, a small semi-auto strong weapon that can be dual wieldedSMG, a small automatic weapon that can be dual wieldedA shotgun, which is a shotgunA sniper rifle, big heavy gun with long rangeA nail gun, a small weapon that produces no sound when firingAnd an automatic rifle, big full autoThere's no real reason not just to have these as the ONLY guns a-la Half Life series and choose whichever best fits a scenario. instead, Deathloop has a weird item rarity system where the enemies have crappy versions of these you can loot, and then you can find slightly rarer ones with slightly better stats that don't really impact gameplay. Maybe it's more important in PVP, but if the 1-shot rifle 1-shots everyone even at its weakest, there's little reason to hunt down a better one. Not that finding a better one is hard, as these rarer variants with slightly better abilities have set spawn locations. Some weapons also have neat little abilities like explosive impacts or headshots improving damage, but again, why? This isn't a looter shooter, the marginal effectiveness of killing 3 enemies in 2.6 seconds instead of 2.8 is irrelevant when there are only like 30 enemies on any given map, spread all around it. If a shotgun is better in a situation, ANY shotgun does pretty much the same job, no need to have like 10 variants.Overall, it's a mish mash of like 5 types of game, and none of the pieces fit together. Go play Dishonored, Hitman, or Majora's Mask, and this game just pales in comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: DEATHLOOP is good ... but man, it needs to slow down! Arkane Studios have delivered another amazing story world, interesting game-play mechanics and an art style that could only be theirs. The fact that this game is not a complete mess (what with the sheer amount of ideas they shoot for) is commendable. The game itself is actually quite linear and sleek--going against most of my fears when I first heard about it and its high-concept, um, concept. It holds your hand and guides you through the various 'leads' and 'discoveries' your character makes, so that you never feel overwhelmed by the complexities of the time loop thingamajig.Only problem is: you find yourself rocketing through a story world you'd much rather take your time in. The four distinct areas in the game are so rich and full of interesting things and ideas; most of this was lost on me for the majority of time I spent in DEATHLOOP as I was either running and hiding, or killing (samey) enemies en masse. As I continued, I started to long for a slower pace--perhaps some kind of mechanic where not all characters are immediately hostile--just so I could take in all this great work A.S. have done. It's especially true for the "visionaries" you need to assassinate to destabilise the loop. These eight figures are intriguing, and yet so little of your time is spent doing anything truly meaningful with them other than filling them full of holes. One of the greatest achievements of DEATHLOOP is the truly non-linear play-style. I found myself irritated by Dishonoured's morality system, which effectively punished a player by approaching the game with a certain path. In this game, your choice to run-and-gun or go it slow are neither encouraged or discouraged. As a result, I actually opted for a stealthier character build than I'd normally try in such a game: it was there to try, and not simply default to. You're never forced into a choice.Overall, DEATHLOOP is worth your money and your time. There's nothing quite like it I've played before. Funnily enough, the game it had me thinking about the most was "We Happy Few". It does a lot of what that game tried so hard to implement, and yet with the polish of a studio who has constantly proven themselves to be quiet, effective innovators. Give it a whirl (especially the excellent PVP content when you comandeer Juliana in another player's game). You'll likely find yourself looping back to play it again.Rating: 7 Wolf Masks out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played dishonored series, I cannot help but to compare Deathloop with dishonored all the time, the gameplay is quite similar to dishonored in a sense that it's a first person view game with stealth elements and superpowers. What distinguishes Deeathloop from dishonored is probably the level design choice. Deathloop is essentially an open world stealth game using 4 different time window to make a variety on their level designs. Different enemies will appear in different period of time. Gameplay wise, the start of the game is really weak. It presented you as an FPS stealth game instead of supernatural murder simulator like dishonored, because you need to kill certain enemies from the game before you can access the superpowers. This is a different approach compared to dishonored as you can access the powers from the start of the game and only need certain currencies to unlock more powers. There is also an interesting design choice where they only give you 2 lives before your final death will reset your progress. It creates a tension which makes you allow trial and error, but not so much that you need to save scum.The AIs are very stupid, since they are programmed to not leave their post, and you basically can use doors to hide after you shot the enemies. They also put a lot of health potions, bullets, infinity bullets, and infinity health potion stations to reduce the difficulty even more. Overall, Deathloop is a very engaging game that is not incredibly difficult and quite accessible for anyone who wants into stealth games, although it may take a while before getting used to the mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: "What if Groundhog's Day and Hitman had a baby?"A stripped-down immersive sim focused on shooting, with a rogue-lite twist. If you wanted to like Deus Ex but felt it was a bit more trouble than it was worth, this is the game for you.Audio design that is so good it will slap you in the face (plus a good soundtrack), excellent level design, and a cast of genuinely interesting and unique villains. Swappable super powers, equipped in pairs, lead to novel combats. It also has a neat feature where you can allow other human players to enter your game at-will and play as the primary antagonist, hunting you as you pursue your mission, which is a really neat idea. The writing and voice acting are some of the best out there.It's worth noting there are currently three bugs that can be a pain: an occasional display bug in character inventory, an intermittent performance problem that can occur if you leave the game sitting for a long time, and a rare issue where it becomes impossible to dismiss the pause menu.All said, I will be sad when I finish this game. It's a fun, sophisticated, stylish, and polished, and whatever I play next will suffer by comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: Game exceeded my initial expectations ten fold .Gameplay is king with Deathloop and Arkane Lyon have provided you with a wealth of gameplay options. Empowering the player to play however the feel is correct . With many different options in regards to rules of engagement.The story is wonderfully told its not overt but its very much existent. With twist and turns along the way told to you in a rather fitting manner.Graphics - game looks spectacularly it does not run to well however this took nothing away from experience (playing at 1080p 60 FPS mostly on High settings RTX 2060 6GB)The best part of this game is the overall gameplay loop and balancing stealth , all out murder and detective work to really create an almost perfect immersive sim .Multiplayer on launch has been spotty at times and the lack of a harder difficulty initially turned me off at first but the solution was staring at me the entire time ,Allowing the invasion (turning off single player) really helped to realise my difficulty issues and amped up the tension and really gave my last few runs weight . I felt the tension of failure and really enjoyed meeting the demands (whether psychological or not). The tension of knowing your so close to completion but that there is a real life person invading you really was the icing on the cake .On the flip side similar tension was felt playing as Juliana (the invader) knowing that I had to Kill colt three times cultivated my entire approach. I acted methodically and attempted to put myself into the person I was attempting to stalks shoes .I would recommend only playing as Juliana once you've been around the block a few times as it helps with the psychological element.Not many games have compelled me to continue playing them even after the end credits have rolled and even fewer have I sat through the credits hoping for a further glimpse into a potential sequel (hopefully a tie in with the prey series )All in all Deathloop is one of the best games I've played full stop . Up there with the likes of Silent Hill 2 (I cannot express to you how much I love silent hill 2) , Which I played in 2020) , Bioshock infinite and Half life 2 . I also feel compelled to go back to prey and try some of the alternative play styles. Arkane have managed to make a game akin to Dishonoured and prey but without the repercussions of your gameplay choices .10/10

_childDocuments_.review: It didn't click for me at first, I love Arkane studios but this one i felt way less immersed than I did in Prey or Dishonored for my first several loops. Not a big fan of any of the characters except Julianna and 2-Bit, which is actually fine (makes it super satisfying to drop Aleksis into his own meat grinder), but since I didn't like the protagonist at first either and a lot of gameplay is more simplified than previous games, it made it feel a little bit of a slog.The thing is I realized fairly early on that I'd been trying to enjoy it the wrong way. Dishonored is more of a stealth series, Prey is more of an immersive sim, Deathloop is a detective game. You're supposed to spot something, go "Huh, that's odd," and come back on subsequent days to figure out why. Collect leads, gather clues, and piece them together into schemes, which then reward you with new loot and powers. And doing that, while Julianna and Colt snark at each other and you dodge assassins played by real people, is actually really satisfying. DEFINITELY you should play online if you can, it's frustrating at first but it adds so much tension and drama, plus a deep sense of satisfaction and a great crash course on mechanics and easier access to gear you might want early.I have two primary complaints: First, that there appears to be only one way to do the perfect loop: You are increasingly funneled towards the perfect day and reach the credits. And second, but related, I wish there had been an option to turn off the hints and lead tracking. It holds your hand the whole way through and when you get your last lead, it gives you an (admittedly cool) cinematic where Colt monologues his master plan to himself, which... I had already figured out and it made me feel robbed of my own cleverness, in a weird way. Their commitment to accessibility is great and I'm thankful for it, and I'm absolutely not saying the mission clues tabs should be removed entirely or even disabled by default, but it would be nice to implement something like hitman's options where you can have the full walkthrough, reduced clues, or disable the display of opportunities altogether.I hope future updates might add more options, the goldenloop update a little while ago was great and added some real fun new quests and gear, so it might be a big ask but I'd LOVE a new area or two of the island which brings new paths to reach the endgame in a future update, would absolutely buy it as DLC. Plus the ability maybe to get a version of Masquerade on Colt? Billie Lurk's powerset was my favorite out of the dishonored series, after all. And in the meantime, I invite anyone who is on the fence to give it a shot. I hope to help Julianna dome you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game in my opinion can be summarized as wasted potential. The looping concept of the game is better than any of the elements actually present in the game. Everything is too basic and not fleshed out nearly enough to reach their potential to be good or fun. There are essentially only 4 levels in the game and you spend the majority of your time in 1.5 of them over and over again. The problem is none of these levels are large or interesting enough to make each visit unique or engaging. Some visits are so short, you spend more time in loading screens (especially when you're about to get invaded) and menus than actually in the level. At no point does the AI of the enemies get any better, only the amount of enemies you fight. I was literally just one tap headshotting everything with the silenced pistol I got about 2 hours into the game still at the end of the game. During the final mission I could just walk up to visionaries and kill them with no threat of actually dying. The visionaries are not fleshed out at all. There's a bit of lore about their relationships, but they are all essentially the same fights. There is a lack of choice in how you do anything in this game. You are pushed to the same conclusion no matter what. This is the biggest shortcoming of the game. There aren't enough "ah hah" moments that change things drastically or assist you in making your own path to killing everyone. There is a minimal selection of powers, weapons, and tools to use. In combination with the easy combat, it makes every encounter and strategy feel identical. This is also a reason why invasions are incredibly basic. It's a race to who one shots the other by pressing F for an instant execute. That is if your opponent has a good connection. Choosing to deal with the level or the invasion makes choosing the abilities and upgrades strange. Either pick general upgrades to deal with everything but then most upgrades are just not worth taking since they have would have no effect (ex. poison immunity). The ending feels abrupt and not fleshed out at all. Overall, I feel like the game ended before it ever hit an interesting stride. There are one or two moments that show potential, but the feeling of your actions and time actually having an affect on the world really isn't there. It just feels like a single linear path, but stuffed into 4 small levels. This game is absolutely not worth it at full price for the content you get in my opinion and is a definite wait for sale game. As an aside, the marketing for this game was absolutely ridiculous and in your face so I find it amusing how basic and unfinished the delivered product feels. This feels like a step backwards from Prey and there's no real reason to replay this since there are no other options to explore or different kind of playthrough (ex. stealth vs loud, full pacifist) to get different outcomes to look for. Additionally I didn't have any technical issues or stuttering on max settings and ray tracing enabled (80-144 fps) like many are complaining about, however this game crashed at least 5-6 times during my play though.

_childDocuments_.review: One more try and decided to ignore the performance issues with the menus and VRAM texture bloat.  I played through the story and the gameplay was fun, so I find it fair to give it a thumbs up.  However, almost every other aspect of the game is pretty bad.The story is a disaster, and only about 10% of your questions are answered in the end (God awful ending, Halo 2 times 100).  Every piece of lore you collect is cryptic and never really explains what's going on in good detail.The game is a mish mash of many games.  Dark Souls with invasions from other players. Music, Dialogue, and Guns straight out of Borderlands.  Powers and stealth straight out of Bioshock and Dishonored.  The main game mechanic, hacking, and resource gathering straight out of Prey.  All features that are great within their own games, but just a jumbled mess when forced into this game.  Not enough maps, and the ones available are too small.  Not enough secrets to find or explore.  Combat is waaaaay too easy even at the highest loop stress, which leads to boring combat.

_childDocuments_.review: While Deathloop's vibe and general level design are interesting, this doesn't stop the game from feeling like an incomplete version of Arkane's previous titles. The overall decisions to attempt to balance Cole's character feel extremely limiting and frustrating; Less slots for guns and powers mean less power in general. This is in addition to the general gamefeel in Deathloop feeling very confused - do you bother dealing with the neutered stealth or try to combat dumb, yet powerful AI? Not even to talk about the Invasion mechanic, or initial performance issues on release, or the fact that the only characters that feel fairly fleshed out are the protagonist and lead Visionary. Playing Deathloop was annoying, and beating it was annoying, and it makes me worry about their next Big Project, RedFall. You're better off playing any other Arkane title, 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10TL;DR: I really enjoyed this game, but your level of enjoyment will depend on what style of storytelling and gameplay you like.This game was really hyped up over the last couple of years, and then IGN gave it a 10/10, and then everyone disagreed. I was actually not interested in this game at all, but then it kept being talked about and started going on sale really early after its release, so I picked it up, and I really enjoyed this one. Your level of enjoyment is going to depend on a few things. Do you like finding clues, listening to audio tapes and reading notes? Think about Bioshock audio logs and Fallout computer terminals. The game does give a summary of what you read that pops up and is gone way too quick, but I was able to come to conclusions before the protagonist, Colt, announced them to me because I would read or listen to everything I found. Planning out how to kill the targets was really fun too, it was kind of like a big puzzle you have to figure out. But once again, I can see it not being for everyone.This game feels like Bioshock gameplay mixed with Dark Souls ideas. You can get invaded, you can lose your "souls," and you will play the same things over and over and over until you get it down. I actually had a few moments where I experienced Soulslike frustration after having obtained a weapon I was trying to get for a while, being invaded, killed and then my day was reset and I lost everything. You can turn invasions of multiplayer off, which I only did on the last day when I beat the game because I got invaded four times in a row while trying to complete the game and got annoyed. Other than that, I would not consider this game hard.Speaking of multiplayer, I had severe lag a couple of times when I was invaded where my single player game was suddenly acting like I had really bad ping, but I found that to be a nuisance. So when you get invaded, your quality of play may go down.I didn't experience too many bugs, occasionally audio would cut out and be off, but it usually fixed itself.Overall, I had a blast playing this one, and if everything I said about it sounds like its up your alley, then by all means go for it. I got this on sale for $30 and it was totally worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: "Meh" review. It's decent, not amazing. Worth €15/$15 at most. Their earlier game, Prey Mooncrash, has similar gameplay but MUCH better execution:DEATHLOOP's story segments and core gameplay are fun, but its mid-to-late-game pacing ruins it. Roughly half of your playtime will be speedrunning between objective markers unlocking clues and/or new equipment. You run out of places to explore and meaningful character upgrades at the half-way point, but still have to do a ton of objectives to get the rest of the story. It's a chore.It tries to use Immersive Sim-style gameplay by offering a variety of weapons, powers and tactics, but they're so unbalanced that there's little point in experimenting. My first non-"common" gun was a silenced SMG that could headshot someone from 50m away - no other weapons could even compare, and I just stopped trying new guns after a while. The same happened with the powers.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Arkane at both its best and its worst in a lot of ways. The AI being fantastically stupid definitely limits the challenge, but they are supplemented by the PvP. The ending is lackluster, but isn't held back by some morality system discouraging you to go ballistic. The models are a little goofy but the visual design is pretty as hell. The characters aren't as deep as the game's contemporaries, but they're funny and dynamic enough to hold your interest for the short missions they're in. The maps aren't enormous, but they're stuffed to the gills with secrets. It's not quite as Immersive Sim as other games but it's not bad, either.I need to give credit to the power system as I always do with Arkane games. A small toolkit where every single combination is viable is always going to be preferable to something bloated and directionless. The PvP adds some genuine suspense and an extra level of thinking to my gameplay as I had to balance a toolkit to handle the NPCs versus one that would keep me alive against an adept invader. Unlike Dishonored and (I dare not speak the name) Redfall, you're never going to be completely untouchable -- just strong enough to feel badass with the right amount of skill and practice at your back.Overall it's a fun game. Imperfect but good. If you like Dishonored you'll love this.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. Art direction, soundtrack, sound design, writing and voice acting are all top-notch. Level design is good but the limited number of locations means things get a bit samey after a while (the different times of day do not make up for this.)The guns are cool and it's fun finding rare gear and infusing it for later loops. The powers are toned down a bit from Dishonored with only a few available, but I suppose with PvP in mind they had to be careful not to make them too unbalanced.I also enjoy how you manipulate the targets to be in certain locations at certain times of day to try and kill them all in one loop, but I would have liked to see more examples of Hitman style kills where you can use the environment to your advantage.One thing I really appreciate about this game is the doing away with non-lethal takedowns and the reduced pressure from being spotted. Too often do stealth games make it too easy to save-scum and undo any mistakes, but in Deathloop you have to live with what happens. And it's fun! Shooting your way out of a bungled stealth attempt shouldn't be a punishment, it's a part of the game and there to be enjoyed when it happens.The real appeal of this game for me is the invasions. You can forgive revisiting the same locations when there's always the threat that someone is going to show up and make it a fight for survival. If that's not your thing you might find it a bit harder to enjoy the overall experience if you turn it off. Or if it's *very* your thing, you can play as Julianna and invade other people's games. I feel like the PvP is pretty unbalanced. Colt very much has the advantage with having 3 lives to Julianna's 1. I have yet to die to an invasion so far after experiencing roughly 10, though there have been a couple of close calls. I nitpick about this but I don't know how I would fix it, as buffing Julianna too much would frustrate Colt players just trying to do their thing.I definitely recommend it this game if you like Dishonored, Hitman or stealth games in general.Oh one more thing- Julianna is holding a sniper rifle in her character select screen. Why the ♥♥♥♥ can't we use it? What a tease.*Edit*Apparently you can get the sniper rifle after ranking up a bit. I also found it as Colt! So ignore that part.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly amazing, Not sure what negative reviewers were expecting.There are few glitches that needs to be addressed (can crash in menus when raytracing is enabled) and you need to have decent hardware to have good experience, but still it is enjoyable and runs a way better on maximum details than CP2077, with raytracing enabled.I have tested it with RTX 3090 at 4K (~85-110 fps) and Quadro P5000 at full HD (GTX 1080 equivalent, with 16 GB VRAM, got 45-65 fps). On both it was very playable. I would personally suggest to keep VSync and NVIDIA reflex enabled if possible, to have stable frame rates. NVIDIA FreeStyle (details filter) makes game to look better than some pixar movies.I have spent more than 40 hours already and got eye bags for playing late, but I enjoyed the story, the exploration part, the graphics, artistic details, interesting game play, great soundtrack and amazing tiny little object details everywhere in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: INTRO = 09-25-2022.Been playing this Deathloop on PC Game Pass. About some 8 hours in or so. It's a game that seems built to totally kick my butt & make sure that I'll die a billion times, before I get this one right. Some thoughts incoming.PREPARE TO DIE.You play as Colt, if you're trying to "Break The Loop" (i.e. finish the game's campaign mode). You're stuck in a time-loop here & not sure why you're here. Not only that, you have a foe named Julianna, who seems hellbent on also killing you, for some reason. About Julianna: depending on how you play (Online Mode, Friends Mode Only, or Single Player Mode), could be another player (if played online) or an A.I./bot. You can play as Julianna, but you need to finish the Tutorial section of the game; then you can invade other players' games & stop them from trying to Break The Loop (i.e. finish the campaign mode).COLT 45.As Colt, you are constantly running through time & going through the same areas over & over at Different Times of Day...which can have different schedules & things going on, at different times of days. You have 3 times of day here: Morning, Afternoon, and Evening. Once you finish the Tutorial, which took me about 2 hours or so, then you can decide how to tackle which areas & at what times. You're trying to go trough the game-world to gain important information & Lore, trying figure out how to kill these 8 Visionaries, which must all be killed by the end of the Day. A "Day" here advances by finishing a game's actual level & surviving it, whether you kill a Visionary in there...or not.LOOPY.You have a certain number of times you can die called "Reprieves" per each level & time that you take on - it's set to 2 Reprieves by default, which can be changed if you switch the game to Single Player Mode for amounts of also either 3, 4, or Infinite times. Some certain areas in levels, you cannot use any Reprieves there...so you die there, you reset the loop & start that whole time-loop all over again. If you don't kill these 8 Visionaries by the Day's End - well, you're going to start the Day all over again from Scratch in every way...except only keeping the Knowledge you've learned, which feels like something out of Groundhog Day. You're going to have to try again and wipe out all 8 Visionaries again, as the time-loop resets.GAMEPLAY & COMBAT.The Tutorial teaches you, as Colt, basically how to play the game. In the game-world, you can find weapons, trinkets, superpowers for skills, and whatnot that you can equip. Gameplay-wise, combat feels like this is right out of both the Dishonored camp here and Prey 2017. You can play this as a stealth game, like Dishonored. You can play this as a shooter, like Prey (2017). You can use these superpowers, both like those two other Arkane games (Dishonored and Prey 2017). Heck, if you want - mix all these styles all you want, in typical immersive sim type of gameplay - which is often what I do in those type of games...and yes, even in this game here. Combat is, to say the least, certainly takes a stab here at being a blast - and certainly, it succeeds at that. Combat and gameplay here is always fun, to say the least.Though, when you feel like you're doing well as Colt & having a good run going...well, all can come crashing down. This feels especially true if you're playing online and allowing other players to come in, where players can hop in to play as Julianna. Let's put it this way: I feel like I've learned a lot in my 8 hours of gameplay & got a lot of knowledge of the game, Lore, and its inhabitants for future strategies on how to take these Visionaries down - but I also feel like that I've also gotten almost nowhere b/c you're likely restarting the loop all over again b/c things will reset when you die too much in a level & time...or you do not kill 8 Visionaries by the end of the Day. It can be often very satisfying to die numerous times...and then kill your first Visionary & exit a level, feel like you're jumping for joy that you survived. In many ways, this gives this kind of difficulty reminds me of old-school Nintendo games & stuff like many of those Souls-like games. And yet - well, at least so far anyways - I can't stop wanting to take on another run & keep playing this game, no matter how much it seems to kick my butt. Hopefully, this trend continues...and I can actually finish this game, at some point.PERFORMANCE.With mostly High & Ultra settings here at 1080p with RT On & DLSS On, this game's normally running in the 50-60fps ballpark. From both an artistic standpoint & technical standpoint, the game looks great with its graphics and usage of RT (Ray-Tracing). I'm running the game here on my desktop loaded with i7 10700KF; 16 GB RAM; RTX 3070 with 8gb VRAM; 1 TB SSD; 2 TB HDD; and W10 x64. OUTRO.And so far, those are my thoughts. Despite it kicking my butt quite often: I can't stop playing this & trying to do "one more run" to try to Break The Loop and stop these 8 Visionaries - and hopefully also find out how I, as Colt, got into this loop & can break this loop. Hopefully, more to come, at some point in time.ADDENDUM = 10-05-2022.So...recently, my time with Game Pass ended, after around 10 hours or so with it - and so far, I think the game's awesome. Though, thanks to yesterday's Humble Choice: you guessed it, I bought that bundle with Deathloop it in. In there is the Steam-version. Tried copying my Game Pass saves to the right folder for Steam and - well, they do NOT work. Nothing new w/ Microsoft's Xbox for PC versions (or Windows Store versions), as I've had similar issues w/ Wolfenstein: Youngblood and even Metro Exodus (though, people have figured out how to get Metro Exodus saves working from Game Pass to Steam). So, looks like I'll be restarting Deathloop from scratch on the Steam-version. Meh. More to come on Steam-version & this new playthrough, at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: In DEATHLOOP, Colt's greatest enemy isn't Julianna or the Visionaries. Heck, it's not even the performance issues (FSR 2.0 set to performance mode carried my underpowered system throughout my experience). In DEATHLOOP, Colt's greatest enemy is Arkane's nauseating, overwhelming reliance on clunky menus.It's not much of an exaggeration to say that about 50% of this game is played on menu screens, and horrendous ones at that. Soft crash and menu lock issues aside, you have to undergo a terrible loadout selection screen before every level, and there are so many ways it could have been handled, and yet Arkane decided to go for an 80s theme here as well, much to their detriment. The menu stuff is practically all that is holding this game back for the average player. DEATHLOOP represents Arkane at their most basic, and yet at their most stylish yet. The writing is pretty good compared to previous Arkane offerings, and the voice acting and dialogues across the board are excellent and full of heart.If you are looking for a fresh take on the usual FPS/AAA formula, DEATHLOOP is a very fun experience. However, if you are looking for some Prey-goodness, hoping for some immersive sim stuff, you will be very disappointed. DEATHLOOP is not as replayable as Prey or Dishonored, but is a fun, fulfilling experience nevertheless, best enjoyed as a standalone, one-and-done game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Mixed opinion. Poor optimization (might get better later). Way too much handholding in the story. Fun gameplay. Multiplayer feels awful, but the game doesn't need it. Definitely wait for sale. For a smaller price tag it's a great game.I played on a 2060, i7 8700, 16gb 2666mhz pc and it works okay. Had a couple crashes playing at 1440p resolution, dropped it to 1080p and had no more crashes.If optimization is something that bothers you maybe wait a few months.Gameplay is really fun. I started Dishonored multiple times and always ended up dropping it. This one I couldn't put down. The progress in this game is very steady and you pretty much never get stuck. It has very clear objectives. A little too clear. You don't really uncover that much because of that. The game tells you where to go and what to do at every step, so you're not really exploring the loop, you're just following one of the multiple storylines that the game presents you.I would LOVE a harder difficulty where you don't get these objectives, and you have to find everything on your own. Have an interactive map for each area where you can put as many custom markers as you can (group of enemies here, weird puzzle there, lock with THIS combination here, etc). Maybe this is just me, but I felt like I never felt like I was missing anything when I was playing. That is great for most games, but this IS a timeloop and you SHOULD get stuck at least a little I think. It doesn't encite exploration. Just follow the quest marker and you're good. If they made that kind of harder difficulty even if it was a DLC I would buy it and play it in a year or two when I don't remember the game anymore. That sounds like the perfect thing this game lacks.The map is actually four smaller areas. The day/loop is basically four levels (morning, noon, afternoon, evening) where you choose the area that you're going to. Each area changes with the different times of day, and so do enemy placements. If you're expecting an open world with lots of freedom this is not it.Despite the handholding it's still fun. There are some puzzles that you have to figure out on your own, but those are secondary. The game doesn't have as many secrets as I thought it would have, but there's enough.Story spoiler:  Tried multiplayer. Hated everything about it. Maybe with a friend it could be fun. Glad it's not mandatory.Overall, if there was a mixed option I would pick it. For the price tag, it's not worth it. If it drops below $40, it's a great buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this game is really disappointing. I'm a big fan of Dishonored, especially Dishonored 2, I consider that very close to a perfect game. Arkane has the chops to make a great game, don't doubt it for a minute, but this ain't it.Deathloop is a great example of why publishers don't typically want to spend AAA resources into more experimental games.There's very little story, lots of lore and background but not much actual plot other than kill all 7 bosses in 1 loop.Gameplay is inherently repetitive, it *is* a timeloop after all. You can see almost everything the game has to offer in just a few hours.The game's setting is a weird 60s future aesthetic that doesn't really add anything.Game is very demanding on your hardware despite not looking that great.Outside of these minor failings, there's a much bigger one that plagues the whole experience. Often in immersive sim type games, there's a design philosophy that all problems should have multiple valid solutions, and the player's creativity can earn them victory in ways the developers perhaps didn't expect. I generally am a big fan of systemic games that take this approach, but Deathloop proves that there is an extreme to this design philosophy that actually sabotages the whole concept. Simply put, there's a lot of ways to solve every problem, in fact, there are SO many ways that almost EVERY solution works for EVERY problem. So instead of requiring some amount of problem solving skills, you instead quickly land on a single loadout/strategy, and that works for everything in the whole game. Instead of having the game be open enough to allow players to be creative in how they approach the various challenges, the game is SO open that it doesn't even matter what you do because it's going to work. The game has no stakes, and it's too afraid to meaningfully challenge you or force you to think about what you're doing. You can play the whole game the same way and that's just not interesting or fun to me. That is why Deathloop isn't good, everything else can be forgiven, but the core gameplay is just intensely boring and unchallenging.

_childDocuments_.review: There's so many cool ideas here but sadly it doesn't come together well due to some serious compromises.The first problem is that the game has no faith in it's player.Solving this clever mystery amounts to following markers on the screen, turn those markers off and you're following some fairly clear hints that tell you exactly what to do until you complete the game.This is no great mystery or time loop mastery here. Anything smart is reserved to secrets found in the map.Invasions are another pain. The game seems to be scared of them.You can only be invaded for 3 minutes when you start a map, and only if the level has a target you're hunting.This means, you won't be invaded by your friends unless you literally tell them "I'm starting a map right now."There's no option to turn off these limitations which is a real shame.Especially since this feature severally limited the scope of content in the game. The powers are straight up boring because they have to work in multiplayer. You've seen all of these abilities before, and none of them are the best versions you've seen.Lastly the enemy variety.There is none. You're fighting the same guys with slightly different guns none stop.They don't even use powers against you and they all die in one shot.Even the targets you're assassinating are just guys with slightly more health and 1 power their poor AI struggles to use.This makes all the fun gun collecting completely redundant when the first weapon you get is pin point accurate and kills in one head shot.This in the end, completely killed the game for me. Everything became so trivial I didn't really see the point in continuing to play.It's such a shame that a game with so many cool ideas and the potential to be one of the most innovative triple A games ever fell so far short.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Arkane's previous immersive sims like Dishonored and/or Prey then you'll absolutely have a great time with this entry. I only have a couple tiny issues with it, the multiplayer experience greatly depends on internet connections between clients as it's peer to peer hosted. (A side effect of this also is users can and have used trainers to ruin the experience for the invader or  Colt.) The second is as the items are balanced for SP the MP component is filled with various easily exploited ability advantages. As long as you don't take the MP as a competitive E-Sport title and more of a casual challenge added to the already great SP experience you will no doubt have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Escape the Samsaric loop of life, death, and eternal suffering, and you get to do so while enjoying the rockin' 60s inspired music and art style. This game also has the opposite of 2 player co-op, instead you have two player murder-fights with the outsider powers from DISHONOURED. I was worried at first I would hate this mechanic, have some rando join my game to kill me while I'm getting my bearings, but the chance of getting into a machete fight with a shapeshifter adds a certain "je ne sais quoi", where I might get rewarded for placing an explosive mine behind me as my would-be assassin is exploded while trying to back-stab me. I did enjoy the creative use of textures and assets from the earlier Dishonoured games, which is actually diagetic to the story in a nice touch (no spoilers here).  In short, a lot of fun, great story, and I hope to get this for my friends so I can pursue them through the levels, like the Predator hunts Arnold aka Dutch.

_childDocuments_.review: I had an amazing experience with Deathloop. I want to keep this review spoiler free as always. The gameplay was extremely fun with the different combinations of powers (slabs + slab upgrades) and weapons combined with certain character power-ups (trinkets). The gunplay was very responsive and smooth. The day of release was rough as there are some stuttering issues that make it feel like there is some input lag regarding using a mouse to play the game. If you tinker with the video settings then you might be able to achieve a playable playthrough but i know alot of these issues is because of the anti-cheat software built into the game. The Dev's have already talked about patching things up for PC players so im sure everything will be fixed soon. Regarding the story it was a really fun journey that strongly encourages you to explore every district's area. The reason why is because you learn how certain events only happen in certain times of the day during the loop which in turn will give you insight on how to kill these special individuals called "visionaries" in the most efficient way possible before the end of the day loops again. I think that there may be some kind of dishonored/deathloop comparison as I strongly believe the two games are connected by the same universe and you will see that more as you play through it. The ending was definitely a let down but leaves room for a possible second game in the new IP.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is okay at best. It is nowhere even close to the 10/10s it's been receiving. There are only 4 maps in the whole game, which are relatively small, and you repeatedly move between them for the objectives. The number of guns in the game is laughable, the AI are completely braindead, the multiplayer has more lag than my 2005 dial-up, the gameplay/stealth gets played out and repetitive, and the gunplay feels clunky and decades old. At it's absolute best, which is honestly in the first hour or two when you're learning the game, it feels like an honest 8/10, but after a few more hours when you start to get deeper into the gameplay loop, you can barely settle on a 6/10. _childDocuments_.review: I am SO disappointed in this game. I'm a longtime fan of Arkanes work, I've played and beaten every single one of their games, but this one is just NOT good. Where to even begin? Weapons, there are so few tools with which to do your thing, there aren’t many weapons to choose from, only one grenade, you're limited to two powers for any given level, which is honestly only ONE choice since of course you're going to run with shift as one of your powers, you'd be a fool not to. There's no non-lethal options, and none of the guns you get are all that interesting, some make a toxic cloud when you shoot, but even that isn’t all that useful.Difficulty, there is NONE! Enemies don’t even notice when a dead body literally falls on top of them. _childDocuments_.review: Let's first start with the bad. The biggest glaring issue in this game is that it is painfully short. And not just in a story sense, I also mean in a replayability sense. As someone who plays plenty of roguelikes, I think DEATHLOOP kind of missed the mark on replayability - I am not sure if Arkane we're even going for mass replayability but if I were to pin the lack of replayability on anything it would be because of how quick you can power yourself up in the game as well as the lack of "endgame" content. Secondly, what also bothered me a ton about this game is that it is REALLY linear for a game that is essentially Bill Murray's Groundhog Day but with guns. Not to get into any spoilers, but I just felt I had little control over the story for a game about looping and time travel. DLC isn't entirely out of the question and perhaps we can see a revamp of some of the game design in a future update.Don't get me wrong, this game is very much an Immersive Sim from Arkane; there are plenty of ways to approach situations and a good variety of viable playstyles that can work, which brings us to the good parts about this game. As you'd expect from a studio like Arkane, the game plays like butter (if you have the system to support it) and really feels like a sandbox for you to mold and conquer. Even so, if you are a person like me and sticks to a single viable playstyle that you enjoy, it's still fun as hell to optimize around that. And while the idea of looping isn't really that much of a unique idea, there were definitely times where I felt like I mastered the loop like Bill Murray's character in Groundhog Day, optimizing every decision because you've lived through the day multiple times already. With the combination of smooth and varied gameplay as well as the unique take on time looping, DEATHLOOP is very much deserving of its Innovative Gameplay and Best Game Direction awards. Speaking of awards, the game also earned the Best Art Direction award and rightfully so - this game just oozes with charm. From the retro feel that feels like a mix between Bioshock, Fallout, and Dishonored, to the caricature like depictions of its minor villains throughout the game, DEATHLOOP is a game where you can wholly appreciate the world they've built. But the part of the game that oozes with the most chemistry is absolutely the interactions between the antagonist and protagonist. The chemistry between Colt and Juliana is through the roof and not to mention also very well voice acted.Overall, while the game is surprisingly linear and has a lack of replayability, the game makes up for it with its varied gameplay and great art direction - such praise can be seen in its deservedly won awards.Recommended if you are a previous fan of Arkane's work and if you felt like the games could have used a bit more guns, although you may be better off buying the game on sale. And if you aren't familiar with Arkane's work, what are you doing? You should be playing Dishonored, it has aged very well for a decade old game.P.S. I can't really speak for the Online part of the game as I did the bare minimum PvP required for 100% achievement completion, but it behaves a lot like the Dark Souls PvP if you are into that. And if you aren't, you can always opt out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a frustrating game, it is full of wonderful ideas, but every single one of them is just underdeveloped and not polished enough to grant this game a  title. You will constantly think how you'd just tweak something here and there and it'd make a huge difference.The potential of the game was unparalleled, but unfortunately Arkane came short and failed to deliver what could be a completely unique experience.The game utilizes the Groundhog day concept and while that sounds fun in a shooter game, it becomes apparent how little of influence it actually has. You learn some stuff, but lose items at the end of the day and that sounds challenging. However, about 2-3 hours in, you'll find a solution to this problem and that will be no longer an issue. The game also encourages you to play the way you want, getting rid of the "save spam" mechanic, forcing you to improvise after a failed plan. That's a great idea and surely a step forward from the "Morale" mechanic that influenced the world around the player in other Arkane games. To add to the fun, you have neat superpowers and trinkets at your disposal. But as it is the theme with this whole game, Arkane came short in this aspect too. You see, you can only have 2 superpowers at the same time, and the "Shift" one, which allows you to teleport, will probably stay locked for you once you get it, essentially leaving you with only one slot for a superpower. The story is spread out across the world and you learn it by picking up notes, audio logs, messages, the design of the world, and occasionally, from dialogue. Still, it's hard to say what kind of story it is, because I wasn't too interested in reading a lot of those notes or paying close attention to the audio logs. To me, it's not the best storytelling, but it may be just the matter of taste. The detective part of the plot and gameplay is interesting, but it involves so much hand-holding, it deflates any good will almost completely.The game's only challenge is Julianna and only if she's controlled by a real player, because they sometimes can be pretty crafty when trying to eliminate you. On the other hand, the AI of the enemies, including AI-controlled Julianna is just laughable, they have no way of stopping you, unless you are cornered by a whole horde of enemies. Not taking into account cases of real player Julianna invasions, I never felt once I could fail any given mission. The ending is lackluster and kinda confusing, buy maybe that's salvaged by reading all the notes and whatnot.Despite the above-mentioned cons, the game still manages to be fun. The gun-play is great (though playing with mouse and keyboard is unfair to the potato AI enemies), the guns are different enough to where you can change them from time to time just to try something new. I didn't like the looter-shooter mechanic at first, but it turned out to be alright.Colt and Julianna have a great chemistry together despite the odd circumstances in which they usually interact. Other visionaries are interesting too, but not to the point where I'd like to find everything there is about them. The world-building is top notch, at this point it's almost a given with Arkane games, but still gotta pay respects. Nothing quite like it!The soundtrack is fantastic too, my balls were blown away.Long story short, it's a game worth checking out, but due to low difficulty, somewhat disconnected story, mild repetition, some performance issues (this game should not require the horsepower that could run Red Dead Redemption 2 at high settings) and most importantly, the lost potential and opportunity to be something really special, I'd recommend getting it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the Dishonored series, I was eager to get my hands on Deathloop, as it looked similar enough. My favourite way to play Dishonored games is stealthy, so I was anticipating that playstyle here too. But this is not really that type of game. In fact, it took me like 7 hours even to begin to approach Deathloop stealthily. However, as soon as I gave in to this game being more akin to Rogue Legacy than Dishonored, I have had a blast playing it. In fact, I'm still having a great time, since the game is chock-full of hidden areas and easter eggs, just like Prey was btw, a game that started off really well, but that in my mind got tedious and frustrating after a while. Deathloop allows for much more variety in gameplay than Prey though IMHO. Still, this is not a masterpiece like Dishonored 1, but a very solid game that you can pick up and play whenever you feel like blowing up some really whacky rockin' sixties. There are fragments of a decent story, but I can't say that I care too much. Trying out stuff in the various maps, aiming for hard-to-reach areas or wiping out enemies in a new cool fashion, this is the core of the game, which makes it grindy at times, but also a fun experiment I keep coming back to, like waking up with increased control in a familiarly weird and rather harmless nightmare over and over. Give it a whirl, I think you'll enjoy being hip in the 60s too, or at least shooting from the hip in this twisted version of that decade.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, so Deathloop gets a positive review from me, but only just... overall I have to confess that once I got the hang of the premise of the game, I kinda enjoyed it. I put this down to my age, not reading everything properly, playing whilst in the grip of Covid (I bought this to see me through my isolation period) and as I mentioned earlier, just not getting it. I have to echo some of the points raised in other reviews though. I could of completed the entire game with just one silenced weapon, no need to use any of the fancy powers, no need to use any other weapons, no need to go in all guns blazing... Why? The NPC'S are dumb as stumps, which is a shame. The store page video shows sliding whilst firing, teleporting, kinesis and all sorts of other things.... you just don't need to use them. The interactions you have with Juliana become grating over time, the limited number of maps and weirdly and I know this will cause some consternation, the repetitiveness all become very tired very quickly.  With a few more or significantly larger maps, some challenging AI this could have been really good. I've played all the other Arkane titles because I always prefer the exploration, finding alternate routes and generally operating in stealth mode and as other people have stated the Dishonoured titles and Prey do these really well. _childDocuments_.review: Another absolute banger from Arkane, my favorite part definitely is how it truly makes you feel like the protagonist.The premise is that you're completely alone in wanting to take down the routine that everyone else follows, you don't have anyone helping you, no one on the radio to boss you around. the only person you talk to is someone who taunts you for your efforts.And the gameplay completely supports this idea. Whenever I went back to my HQ to plan my next move, I actually planned and took notes by myself without the game telling me (or before the game points me towards it).Unlike most singleplayer games nowadays, this game doesn't have constantly updating and super intrusive objective markers, it also doesn't have a minimap. these aren't anti-QoL because the game simply does not need these things.The maps are incredibly compact to a point where a minimap would only get you more confused if you depended on it through progress, you instead learn all of the maps by the time you reach the end-game.The objective markers are vague and only show you in what segment of the map a certain thing is, you could play without these markers too as you are allowed to choose them however you want, but the way they're placed is perfect as it only shows what you've already seen/would know if you remembered/put full concentration into tracking your environment. It's the ultimate way to tackle objective markers. Just the right amount of QoL to make it accessible but not OP or distracting.The gameplay itself is really good and intricate, as an Arkane game, you're allowed complete freedom with whatever you want to do, no invisible walls what so ever. But this freedom also brings some variety problems, more so; lack of.Don't get me wrong, there's incredible variety in the loadouts you can create, given you have the items, but there is little reason to change when you've already made up a perfect strategy. Since the game never stops you, it also never punishes you if you think of every thing in advance. Sure, you should be rewarded for good planning, But the engagement could be improved tenfold if you were nerfed through several runs of the same strategy.Hear me out, I absolutely loved it when I [MINOR SPOILERS] lost the upgrades on my active gear when I first finished the game. I got one of the endings but wanted to see the other but when I retried i saw that it took away all those upgrades i depended on, I had to resort to other weapons I had and took different slabs (superpowers) and used different parts of the map to win again.The game early on does not have any sort of item preservation between days, but it later (still early-game) gives you the ability to save items in trade for points taken either from killed bosses or some spots scattered on a map (they work like Dark Souls' souls) and the idea that beating the game reset that slightly, at least for the strat I already used made me explore my freedom under different situations, if the game explored this idea across the whole game instead of just the end, it could've been really great,Hell, I even unequipped certain items throughout my playthrough cause I thought they were too OP but it was still not enough.Another complaint is probably the enemy AI, They're not completely bad, they are really good in loud fights and really hurt aswell, when you're getting hunted by AI Julianna (invader that specifically hunts you, can either be AI or another player, also like Dark Souls) sometimes she pauses to mock you for trying to get her with a mine, etc. but usually in stealth; especially if you're running Aether (invisibility) they get SUPER dumb, took me out of it at points where I'd be sniping with Flicker (stay invisible whilst shooting) where enemies would hear the sound, rush towards me, and look straight at me the entire time but not shoot, almost felt like cheating.The final complaint is not something Arkane can control, I started playing late, the game's singleplayer-focused, not many people (Even I) will not want to have their first go be ruined by some veteran who knows every exploit in the game, What I'm getting at is, Playing AS Julianna is near impossible, you won't find a game, you just won't, by that extent, stuff like unlocking outfits or getting some achievements is also near impossible.Some other points, speed round:-Never had reason to run low tier guns, never experienced the Jamming feature even once.-Akimbo makes slab/hackamajig/nade usage very finnicky, ignored all akimbo related stuff for most of the game apart from the Verso (really strong gun that usually operates in akimbo)-Some minor plot-points that weren't very clear for way too long-What the hell were the delivery booths for!?-There should be better item sorting-Should've had more direct and numeral stats instead of vague wordings like "significantly more"-Added immersion how there's no censoring on swears whatsoever, when people are on edge or angry they just hurl swears like hell. NPC chatter is also extremely natural and makes them feel like real people vaguely hired to be there. But it's also a double edged sword how horned up these mofos are. like damn dude, chill tf out..-Wish I could combine Attributes so they lower their effect but take up one space...Conclusion? Extremely immersive Arkane game that allows a lot of freedom, in fact, TOO MUCH freedom. Some parts of the game could be extended to put more focus on certain characters or certain tiers of items.Has some minor shortcomings but for the most part I'm very glad I played it. Well worth the time, I picked it up during a sale, but I'd willingly pay full price too.9.25/10

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its many flaws, I give DL a thumb's up. My recommendation is based on the following: CONS: - The difficulty: Too easy. There are no difficulty settings. The first few minutes or missions are the most challenging, and then very VERY quickly you obtain significantly better gear (better weapons, special powers in the form of mana-using "slabs") which your opponents lack, and your opponents do not scale up similarly. The basic enemies are poorly controlled AI idiots who pose no challenge whatsoever, while the seven "bosses" pose only minor ones once you have even halfway decent gear. The world is filled with an overabundance of ammunition and healing kits, so its economy of choice is massively overinflated. Similarly its currency of upgrading, "Residuum", which lets you keep gear throughout loops: After the first loop in which you are able to use it, you will always have a massive overabundance and nothing new with which to use it. - Denuvo anti-tamper: I noticed too late that this game comes complete with the hideous mess which is Denuvo, which you are forced to install upon your system. - Replayability: Lacking, since you will have seen enough of the 4 areas by the time you finish the story. It took me about 40 hours to complete, which I did very slowly and exploring as much as I could. I don't think it has the same compelling itch to try again, unlike for example Dishonored 2 with the promise of trying different tactics using a different character. PROS: - The voice acting: Superb and compelling. - The sound in general: Very good. Decent original music, well-worked orchestration of audio effects. - The world presentation: Beautiful and detailed. While sometimes absurd, the world felt "real", full of interesting but also mundane and useless tidbits which are there simply to look realistic. The designers succeeded. -  The story: While this would make a sub-par story in any other medium, implemented in an action game such as DL, the story is surprisingly original and interesting, at least most of the time. The characterization is well-done, if frequently clichéd and trite. The main protagonists (Colt and Juliana) are well-fleshed out. Despite some flaws in logic here and there, the narrative succeeds more than it fails. - The level design: Good. Not nearly as impressive, bordering on genius, as was parts of Dishonored 2, but solid. The four key areas offered enough variety for 40 hours of gameplay. All in all: an entertaining, if not terribly challenging, experience. I purchased it on deep sale and do not regret it. Would wholeheartedly recommend it on sale once Denuvo gets removed.
