_childDocuments_.review: In Deathloop you play as Colt Vahn, an assassin determined to break a time loop by killing 8 targets known as Visionaries. Sounds easy? Well, here is the catch: you must kill them all in the same time loop. They appear on different places at different times of the day and usually are well protected, so you must gather every piece of info and plan your loop accordingly. Failing or dying restarts the day, until you are finally able to kill them all. Due to Colt’s terrible amnesia, you don’t know who he really is, what he’s doing, and most importantly, why a woman named Julianna is constantly trying to kill him.The story is set on Blackreef Island, an exotic location where immortality is reality and everyone is forced to live the same day over and over (mostly drinking, having parties, doing experiments or just getting bored). Only Colt and Julianna are able to retain their memories through the different loops, which makes their relationship much stronger, also thanks to the constant funny dialogues between the two of them. As per Arkane tradition, knowledge is key. Every intel you gather will make your next loop easier to understand, until you will be able to put the pieces together on your own. The island is divided into four different locations that you can only visit during a certain time: morning, noon, afternoon and evening. Fortunately, there is no pressure. Once you have chosen a location for that particular time of the day, you can stay as long as you like. Much of the story content is hidden in written notes, audio recordings, computer logs etc. and everything is noted on your personal journal. From there you can track new leads and see how your actions unlocked new possibilities after each loop.The game holds your hand during the opening hours with a wordy tutorial that explains every single aspect of the game. I recommend following the tutorial closely during the first loops, as any equipment you may find by randomly exploring on your own will be immediately removed when the day is over. Once you complete the tutorial and acquire the ability to keep your gear forever, you are finally free to explore every part of the island as much as you like.While playing as Colt, Julianna will invade your game at different times of the day and depending on your settings she will be either controlled by AI or by a smarter online player. The area will be locked, so you won’t be able to escape, unless you hack the antenna that opens the tunnels. If you feel confident you can decide to stay and fight, since killing her rewards you with her equipment. From the main menu, you can also play as Julianna, protecting the loop from other Colts while also leveling up and unlocking new gadgets and abilities after each win.Overall the non-linear narrative structure is great, with well written dialogues, interesting characters and a great variety of situations. And if you are scared about it being a short game, then don’t. Longevity depends entirely on your actions through the loops; completing the story and finding all Blackreef side content may take quite some time, while the PVP online mode gives some extra replay value as Julianna.Gameplay wise, Deathloop tries something that was only briefly experimented with Prey’s Mooncrash DLC, mixing its immersive sim formula with a roguelite structure and Hitman’s targets assassination. While Dishonored and Prey offered predefined objectives and multiple ways to reach them, Deathloop unlocks its objectives only when you have explored and gathered enough info. You still get a powerful arsenal of weapons: guns, grenades, a machete, a hacking machine and slabs, which are basically the special abilities from Dishonored. During each loop you collect Residuum, which is a currency you can use to keep your gadgets forever. You will most likely spend the first loops trying to find and keep new slabs and better weapons, making the next day easier. Combining all your gadgets together and making a good use of the environment is not only encouraged, but also fun.The game lacks traditional difficulty settings and while I like this decision, I must say that combat is generally too easy. Colt feels overpowered, with a great variety of weapons and a hacking device that can easily turn turrets machines against enemies. Plus, he has not 1, not 2, but 3 lives at his disposal for each time of the day, meaning he can get killed two times before dying for real and restarting the loop. This can be a serious problem in the PVP online mode, where even a skilled Julianna can do nothing against Colt’s cat lives.Like a generic looter shooter, Deathloop also includes different variants of weapons with colors highlighting their rarity; basic weapons are more prone to malfunctions, while legendary ones have unique bonuses. Unfortunately, shooting feels clunky and inaccurate, and while I wasn’t expecting Doom’s or Wolfenstein’s gunplay here, this has been Arkane’s weakness for too many years. It went mostly unnoticed in games like Dishonored and Prey where stealth was the best and most enjoyable approach, but in Deathloop stealth has been simplified in favor of a much more action oriented experience. This makes the gameplay unable to excel in any of these fields. It’s still enjoyable thanks to a sublime level design and immersive freedom, but gunplay actions will definitely include some messy spray and pray moments.Another big flaw is the AI, which is one of the worst I have ever seen in a videogame. It’s really easy to sneak around enemies, taking them out silently or just shooting at them. Enemies movements are locked into limited zones, even if they hear a shooting behind the corner they won’t come to investigate unless the alert is given; when this happens, you suddenly appear on their radar and they start chasing you aggressively, making things a little bit more interesting.Graphics is decent enough. It’s not breathtaking for today standards and very much resembles Dishonored graphics, with some low quality visuals in the background and occasional texture pop-in. There is a lack of details on enemies that can be seen particularly when performing a stealth kill. The fact that after dying their body simply disappears is a good narrative way to solve a probably more technical limit.Considering the game features multiple loading screens and it’s built around small sandbox areas, PC requirements should have been lower and performance should have been much better. The Void Engine desperately needs a major overhaul or to be completely replaced with another engine for future games. These performance issues may also be related to a poor implementation of Denuvo DRM, which causes the game to microstutter even at lower settings. Limiting the framerate to 60 and disabling Nvidia Reflex gets rid of some stutter, but it’s clear there are many problems under the hood. Even alt-tabbing the game a couple of times can make it easily crash and wipe out all your progress in a location.Compared to Dishonored and Prey, Deathloop offers an inferior gameplay experience, sacrificing stealth elements in favor of a clunky run and gun approach. The non-linear storytelling combined with Arkane unique level design is obviously the major point of attraction, though it’s impossible to hide a bit of disappointment for what was promised to be a truly innovating experience. That said, Deathloop is still a wonderful immersive sim with a great roguelite structure and an interesting asynchronous online mode. Despite its flaws, I still had a good time exploring Blackreef Island and putting the pieces together day after day, but due to multiple bugs and performance issues on PC I would say it’s probably best to wait for more patches and hopefully the removal of Denuvo DRM.

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing Deathloop, I was afraid that this game was the beginning of the end for Arkane. There were quite a few things that I was afraid of or didn't like the sound of it. However, not only was I wrong, but it was actually the complete opposite. As a long-time fan of the studio who loves both the Dishonored series and Prey, I can confidently say that Deathloop is probably the best-designed Arkane game to date. Pros:- The core gameplay loop (the actual time loop) is boldly novel but very engaging and fun to play. Before playing it, I was afraid, for some reason, that the game revolves around procedurally generated content, but I couldn’t have been more wrong. Everything is hand-crafted and carefully designed to create a compelling experience. The loop mechanic is just a medium for the story to unravel (and the main part of the story in itself), and it is done in such a good way that it’s really hard to describe with words. - The level design is hands down one of the best I've seen in immersive sims and games in general (And I’ve been playing games since the early ‘90s). Despite the game having “only” four areas which you can freely visit, each time you will find something new, reach a previously unavailable location, discover a new secret, enter some new building, meet new characters, or learn a new piece of information. There’s always something new to uncover.- The game essentially plays as a detective story where your main goal is to collect information and learn about the places you explore and the main characters in order to eventually break the loop. All information is neatly collected on your dashboard screen, where you can check all notes, messages, audio logs, info about characters, and everything else you’ve found. It helps both to connect the dots of the story and to understand the characters, setting and the overarching story better.- The 1960s aesthetics and Arkane's signature attention to detail make the world of this game extremely immersive and tangible. The more you explore and look around, the more interesting details you find. It’s such a densely packed world that was crafted with love and clear vision.- Gameplay is simply fun. Both preparation for the missions and actual action. You have a lot of options on how you want to approach missions (stealthy, guns blazing, or a mix of both) thanks to a myriad of weapons, powers and various “trinkets” that can change both you and your powers and weapons. Of course, the locations themself also allow for a lot of different approaches, depending on how well you know them.- I love the fact that there are no maps of the locations, which are quite huge and intricate. You actually need to learn and memorise each of the four massive maps and to know every nook and cranny in order to complete your goals on a particular deployment safely. It makes the gameplay more exciting and challenging and, therefore, more rewarding.- The sound in this game is just perfect - be it excellent voice acting of the main cast, nostalgic 60s-inspired tunes, or various sound effects. It hits you just right.- The world-building is phenomenal. The main set of characters is unique and well-fleshed-out, and the main story is intriguing and will keep you pushing for answers until the end.Cons:- You might feel overwhelmed at the beginning due to Deathloop's unique design and the number of systems you need to understand how they work and what's important. It can be daunting. However, once you get a grasp on it, you will absolutely enjoy it.- The biggest issues with this game are all kinds of bugs, which is a very unfortunate thing. I’m talking about game-breaking bugs where progress doesn’t register. You will get stuck because of that. Then, there are the game crashings, certain important things not being where they should be, or you are unable to interact with important stuff… It’s very unfortunate. Especially so for a game which is a rogue-lite title.- Despite giving you a lot of freedom on how you want to play the game, in terms of the story branching, the only decision you will make is at the end. However, the exploration is key here, as the more you find optional stuff, the more you learn about the story and its overarching setting. It's not about agency. It's about discovering.- Some loops might feel tedious, especially when you get stuck on a certain thing that is important for progress, and you need to repeat the loop over and over again.- The AI of "normal" enemies is not the smartest one. However, this can be explained in-universe as intentional, so I'm kinda okay with it. Nevertheless, don't be fooled. You can quickly get swarmed in this game and die.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend Deathloop because the gameplay can be really fun, but the game is incredibly unstable and generally frustrating. It crashes incredibly frequently which makes it nearly unplayable at times. This is especially a problem because the game does not save unless you advance time. There have been games where I completed multiple objectives and survived a player invasion only to crash and completely lose all progress. This combined with the fact that invasions often one hit kill Colt makes objectives repetitive and annoying.What makes this more frustrating is the game often fails to live up to its promise of open ended levels with an objective system that tends to heavily railroad you. I tended find myself repeatedly running towards an objective and losing progress over and over, only to find that the objective is just a note that leads to another location where I have to repeat the process again. when the game manages to pull off it's intent it is an incredible game, but not enough that I would recommend to anyone other than a big fan of immersive sims

_childDocuments_.review: I've read a lot of reviews attacking this game for poor optimisation and stuttering, but I am below the recommended specs, and at least in my case, as long as I was willing to go into the graphics settings and dial things down to a realistic level for my hardware, it ran just fine.Early days, but it has been really fun, like dishonored only snappier and with a sense of humour.  Stealth and combat flows well, there are plenty of mystery and objectives but tons of freedom in how to solve them.  Haven't gotten into the invasion style PVP yet, but I'm not sure how vital that gimmick is to the experience- it could be an extra challenge and a chance to troll the newbs if you want it, but easy enough to just  turn off and forget if you don't.  The AI isn't so sharp, but if we're honest most games like this with a stealth component and big, open, well populated levels would be pretty frustrating if all the minions were smart enough to converge on you at the 1st sound of a gunshot then hunt you down methodically in teams.  The bad AI just lets you feel cool and get away with pulling off hilarious stunts, as it should be.End of the day, the base game play loop is rad, the jokes are mostly bangers, and the well-voiced banter between the primary antagonist and protagonist pretty much always hits perfect.  Definitely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I am mixed about the game, but since that is not a review option here, I have to go thumbs down.TLDR: Get it on sale and go in not expecting anything. I feel like there is a lot of missed potential here, I don't know the schedule this game had, but it screams a bit  to me, (and if that is the case then I can't really fault the devs too much), but still there is a lot more I ended up wanting from the game.Deathloop screams Arkane style and passion and as much as this game is a Dishonored-esc assassination game it's trying to be it's own thing (which is good). It's more of a puzzle. A puzzle which in my opinion could have had more solutions than one. The loop system is an interesting system or it could be, but I feel like it isn't utilized enough to make replays that much more interesting. Its a way to easily separate encounters and times of day to add cheap "level variaty".There is a cast of colorful characters with wonderful performances, but that alone isn't enough to make tackling the loop and visionary assassinations any more interesting, since at the end of the day; there is a definitive way to actually beat the game. I would have loved to see scenarios where for example after going high alert/or messing up, a visionary would flee the scene and possibly team up with another, with tougher security to take Colt on, but that's too much to ask for since in general the "challenge" of the game is minimal.AI absolutely sucks. Not once did I feel challenged by any enemy encounters and loosing enemy interest was laughably easy, also enemy variety is pretty much nonexistent.Even the puzzle aspect of the game felt.. just dumb, the game blurts answers and "hints" constantly, so I never felt that I achieved anything by myself especially since, again, there only is one default solution for the puzzle. Give some agency to players ffs! But then again how else will a game journalist give that high appraisal review..I did have some fun in the beginning and the great performances of especially Colt and Juliana were fantastic, but in the end I really was left with a "that's it?" feeling. Idk there is a lot more I'd want to say, (or I guess at this point: complain about), but eh. Get it from a good sale and don't expect anything, I'm sure you will have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Prey and Dishonored are two of my favorite games.  Deathloop was the only upcoming game that I've been looking forward to since I'm a big fan of Arkane Studios.  Unfortunately, this game  feels like a huge step back from their previous games.  There are lots of invisible walls.  Want to go through that window?  You can't, its locked.  Want to smash that window?  You can't, the glass can't be broken.   Want to climb over that cliff?  You can't.  There are too many instances where there's only one way of doing something.  For most games, that wouldn't be so bad.  It's just disappointing coming from Arkane.  Next is the terrible enemy AI.  There have been plenty of times where I walk up behind an enemy and stab them while someone nearby just watches, with the meter over their head going up slightly before returning to normal.  There is some good level design but none of the levels are anywhere near as impressive as the kind of stuff that was in Dishonored 2.Finally, the game has no right to be as demanding as it is.  There's absolutely nothing "next gen" about this game.  I just replayed the first Dishonored, and despite being 9 years old and not hardware intensive at all, that game looks far more impressive to me than Deathloop.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to be clear – you can have fun in Deathloop. It’s just that while you could make gameplay repetitive and boring in Dishonored and Prey, in Deathloop the game actively encourages you to play in a boring and repetitive way. Deathloop in my mind is built on three pillars and those unfortunately detract from each other, preventing neither from being great.I put “immersive” in bracket as I don’t think it applies here, but if you played Arcane’s previous titles I think you get the idea – first person, intricate levels to explore, systemic design allowing for creative use of weapons, skills and environment. It’s ok, but not brilliant – the game is painfully easy, and it has to be. It has to be because of the repetition (making things more difficult would make later loops incredibly tedious) and because of multiplayer. While there is plenty of skills and weapons to use they are honestly skipable against NPCs – a silent SMG you are likely to find early in the game will be enough to handle anything. 5 enemies? Just pop them with easy headshots with you SMG with what seems like almost unlimited range and accuracy. You CAN have more fun than that, but it’s shallow fun as enemies provide no resistance. There are neat things to find in levels, with some side activities to do, but again – rewards aren’t very worthwhile – you will be drowning in epic gear before long (more on that later), and extra weapon with unique properties does little for your singleplayer playthrough. Levels are very small by Arcane standard and easy difficult level, and lack of reward for keeping enemies alive means that the most efficient way is just to run through the level and pop every enemy with a quick SMG headshot. Level design is decent, but not terribly well utilised. It’s the least timeloopy timeloop game I played. Essentially each day consists of 4 times of day, and you can visit most of the four levels within each of those four times – each level changes a bit depending on when you visit it – enemy positioning is a bit different, different parts of the level can be opened or closed. I never felt engaged by this system – because of the time passes when you exit levels, it doesn’t really feel like the time passes – it’s more like the game cut each level into the pieces and forbid you from accessing everything at once. Progressions worked for me like that: part1 – lengthy and dull introduction to story and core systems. Part2 – the part I enjoyed the most. Exploration of levels, fighting each of the “bosses”, acquiring new skills and weapons. Part3 – lengthy end game where you complete errands waiting for Colt to figure out how to finish the game (and I mean Colt – player isn’t required to do much thinking). At this point I was bored with the game, and only multiplayer kept me entertained from time to time.I think good game loop succeeds in players wanting to explore the timeframe – the same way a good open world makes players ask “what’s over there”. Deathloop is like a bad openworld game – with lots of marker, inability to figure things yourself unless storyline tells you to do something, and lack of faith in its world, its loop and the player. You are also able to keep skills and weapons between loops, so it feels more like you are replaying the same levels over and over again, if more and more OP character, rather than getting better as player in each run.Deathloop has dark souls like “invasion” mechanic – where an enemy player can invade your level and try to kill you. Don’t be afraid – odds are stacked heavily in favour of Colt. This was to my surprise my favourite part of the game. Enemy players offer a resistance that NPCs simply don’t, and those weapons, skills and upgrade finally come in handy. The system suffers from two things: 1) as far as I can tell it’s peer-to-peer connection which means quality of the experience varies quite a lot. Sometimes I had a decent opponent, and sometimes lag was so bad, that taking out a machete and hoping that the game will register an instant-kill was my best bet.2) balance – one can have a lot of fun with various toys in our disposal, but the most effective ways of playing are also the most boring ones – especially if you need to be ready to compensate for extreme lag that you might encounter. And it is difficult to justify being adventurous with Colt if game progression is at stake. Some encounters I had where by far the best time I had in Deathloop (both as invader and as the one being invaded) but the quality of the experience is highly uneven. If you opt out of multiplayer (which you can do) Juliana will be AI controlled, making her about as useless and unthreatening as the other opponents.So those are three imperfect pillars of Deathloop – and I am afraid they all make each other worse – you can't have a tighter, more demanding “immersive sim” without making time loop and multiplayer frustratingly tedious. You can't have better loop, and roguelite mechanics, in a game where other levelled up players can invade you (I personally think that less progressions and "scavenge what you can and fight" would be far more interesting), and multiplayer can’t be truly great without better rules, better balance, and better netcode/connection system. You can have fun with immersive sim sandbox, but danger of invasion encourages sticking to things that work, and things that work are usually boring. You can come up with interesting loadouts for multiplayer but you have to hope that connection is decent, your opponent isn't a try hard, and you have to accept that experimentation might mean lack of progress in the story.Time loop is just not very interesting.The game is unique, but mediocre. If you wanna play it, I would recommend doing it sooner than later though, while the online community still exists. I think it will become a dull ghost town once there are no players to mess around with.If you haven't, play: Dishonored1&2 and Prey. All are better Arcane's singleplayer games. Hopefully upcoming Arcane's vampire thingy, will be a better mulitplayer game.

_childDocuments_.review: Deathloop's often an artistic masterpiece that's a lot of fun to play and features a wicked hook. That being said, it's a severely flawed game, and the vast majority of praise I have for the game comes from its higher level philosophy and design and not necessarily in its execution.The game is an artistic powerhouse. It looks phenomenal due to the incredibly talented artists at work on developing this game. Its sense of style is really unmatched by most other contemporary games. Its color palettes, its character designs, its setting, and its music are all phenomenally good and work to craft a really unique feel for the game. The fact that it looks so good is really impactful, because Void Engine is—there's really no other way to put this—a god-awful garbage heap of an engine on PC. The game frequently chugs in certain environments, and huge frame drops of double digits are overwhelmingly common. It also has a tendency to crash. This is even more unforgivable considering all of these problems were present in Dishonored 2 when it released back five years ago. Most damningly, Deathloop isn't even that technically pretty, so there's even less excuse for such huge, arbitrary drops in performance. Luckily for Arkane, though, the art at Deathloop's core is more than good enough to carry the experience along.The game is also quite fun to play. I was surprised to find out how close it plays to Dishonored 2. Many of the powers are simply carry-overs from Dishonored 2, and that's not a bad thing. The player is pushed to use them in a more wide-open fashion in Deathloop than they ever were in the Dishonored games, and it works exceptionally. The shooting is also much tighter than it was in the Dishonored games. Further, the core gameplay loop of replaying levels to gain more infusion points to improve abilities and equipment in order to better replay levels is really compelling and addictive, and Arkane's level design supports repeated playthroughs of the same area—at least, for a time.The problem is that so much of this game seems to lack cohesion, and playing it for an extended period of time begins to feel disjointed. The world, to me, feels remarkably flimsy, which is a criticism I'm really surprised to be making considering how utterly realistic and lived-in Arkane's previous worlds have felt—particularly Dunwall. Blackreef in Deathloop feels like a set of multiplayer levels. They're designed fantastically for gameplay and they're a joy to play through and explore, but nothing in the game actually felt like a real, lived-in place. I never had the experience of poking through an apartment or a building and wondering how these people lived like I did so frequently in Dishonored, and that really damaged the experience in Deathloop for me. I didn't care about the setting or the lore because none of it felt real or genuine, and thus I never lost myself in this game like I did in some of Arkane's previous efforts. I was never really immersed and was always consciously aware that I was playing a video game. I lacked the transcendental experience I often have with some of my favorite video games, and a lot of Deathloop—despite being fun—felt dry and meaningless to play.Feeding into this great flaw is the fact that almost all of the story content the player will experience is drip-fed through text items which are picked up in the world. The game does not pause as you read, so often the player finds themselves skimming very quickly through such text, barely paying attention in case they are detected by enemy NPCs patrolling the area. This quickly turned into a huge problem, because I was very rarely grasping where I was meant to be headed, or why, even, I was heading there. Several times I would be tasked with assassinating one of the game's primary enemies without having any idea who they are, what they were doing, or why they were doing it. The game does an exceptionally poor job relaying important plot- and character-critical information to the player, which leads you to simply following the marker on your screen and killing everything in your way. The only effort it shows in developing its characters is between Colt and Julianna, and the effort pays off as they're both the only people in the entire game who feel human. The rest are dry, boring, lifeless NPCs, despite some great voice performances. Cherami Leigh as Fia is a particular stand-out, but they're all really great.Pacing is also an issue. Deathloop is the most blatantly offensive "Sorry, Mario! Your princess is in another castle!" game I have played in literal generations. The way this game artificially stretches out its quest lines is absolutely shameless and infuriating. There were several instances in which the player proceeds to the next step in a given questline, only for the game to throw a locked door or a literal wall in your way with a note attached to it, saying something like "whoops! You've got to come here in at another time of day to proceed in this quest!" Great, so I just spent this time period in a completely wasted manner, only for you to tell me in the most gamey way possible that I can't do this right now, and have to wait until the next day to proceed. This kind of thing grew frustrating very quickly, and my joy in replaying areas to explore further or increase my own power quickly turned to frustration with the tedium of the way the game structures its quest design. The quests are given far too many fetch-quest-caliber objectives and end up being stretched out far too long. This, again, feeds into the feeling gaminess that the best games do a great job of hiding from the player. I eventually went from having trouble keeping a grasp of the game's quests due to the poor way in which it relays its storytelling, to simply not caring, because so much of it felt flimsy and meaningless when I did grasp it, which is a real shame considering some of the character designs are so good, and the voice cast bringing them to life are all exceptional, particularly the game's two leads. There's a real missed opportunity to create some memorable characters here, because the player will end up simply not caring since it's too much of a chore to really become invested in them in the first place. My issues with the way the game imparts its story and designs its quests won't be a problem for everyone. If you're looking for a rip-roaring time in a combat arena where you can play in a fast-paced manner and kill everything in sight using a variety of weapons and powers, all while being surrounded by exceptional art and level design, while great music plays, then you're likely going to love Deathloop. But if you're looking for a more cerebral experience where you can explore, learn about the world you're in, and piece together things for yourself as you proceed—like you did in a game like Dishonored or Prey—you're probably going to have a mediocre, up-and-down time with Deathloop, as I did. When it's firing on all cylinders it's a joy to play, but I never felt I was truly immersed in its world and its characters, and those are by far the most important reasons why I typically play single player games. So for someone like me, I would not recommend Deathloop. It's an ambitious game made by people who clearly care a whole lot about their medium, but it ended up being a bit too tedious and gamey for my tastes, in addition to running very poorly on PC.I don't really regret the purchase because I'm happy to fund Arkane as they keep trying creative, ambitious stuff like this, but I sure hope they do it on a different engine next time, and I hope they put more emphasis into executing on delivering a more cohesive, genuine world and narrative to suit such great style and characters in the future.Feel free to follow  if you like my reviews.Chat with me on !

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review. I have been a participant in heavy frame stutter and memory issues. However, I believe that since the 17th. There has been a patch that fixed the issue. As my 3080 seemingly can run this at 100 fps in the bigger outdoor areas without stutters or drop offs (as seen on streams). So good props for Arkane to listen to the reviews, and fixing them. There are many devs that should look up to what they did. Which is 'listening to the customers'So what is the game about? Well, after 6 hours. I feel I have gotten the basic gist of the game. You play as Colt. A man with Amnesia, who after a run in with the individuals of blackreef, takes it to himself to break the loop. What is the loop? Well, due to science, time doesn't progress to the next day. Instead it reverts back to the morning before. And you waking up on the beach with sand on your face.The game asks you to complete objectives and explore blackreef. Using guns, tools, powers, and the loop itself. Alot of discoveries and domino bricks you find, can only be toppled over in certain periods in the day. And alot of breakthroughs are the kind you find while exploring. There is stealth for the people who prefers subtle approaches. but there is also enough explosive guns you can use to go guns blazing.A complaint I notice is the difficulty of the game. It's true, if you go area to area and guns blaze sections. Then the game can be a bit easy, since if you take time exploring the place, you can easely find ammunition and health. However I have died a couple of times, some from mines while others was because I walked into a compound filled with guards, and one triggered the alarm for the compound. I personally don't believe the game was designed to be 'difficult'. I think it is a game that want to promote a power fantasy of a stubborn action hero with abnormal powers.It's a simple premise, and it does the job well. Would I recommend it at 60€? which is where I bought it from? Only if you are itching for the game. And genuinly like what you see in the trailers or what streamers have pumped out.If not? then give it some time in the oven, let some patches go through and snag it at 40€ or even 30€. The game is Unique. And I encourage new IPs that want to try a premise, wether it sinks or swims. And here? I feel it floats well.Edit: Finished the game. I'm a B-liner type of person. So I didn't go out to fully explore the options and opportunities. The game took me 8 hours to finish. But I will still say that those 8 hours have been enjoyable. And I liked setting up the domino bricks and seeing everything play out

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've been this disappointed by a game's ending in quite some time, but Deathloop managed it.Looking back at Arkane's previous endings, they either revealed something previously unknown (Prey), or provided an epilogue that took into account your choices (Dishonored 1 +  2). Deathloop's, however, is simply an unsatisfying and seemingly rushed conclusion that retroactively soured my opinion on the rest of the game.Honestly, every aspect of this game feels like a straight downgrade from Dishonored 2; animations aren't as fluid, gunplay feels worse, and I'm not sure if this is due to the change in art style, but it doesn't look quite as good as 2 did 5 years ago. The latter point I'm not overly hung up on, as it can look quite good during snowstorms and nighttime, and graphics are irrelevant if the gameplay is good enough, which Deathloop's definitely is.However, as I alluded to above, it all just feels worse than Dishonored 2, which is quite sad.Unlike previous Arkane games, Deathloop is clearly designed around action, not stealth, although both playstyles are viable. I'm not sure why we needed an ADS button instead of following Dishonored's zoom-in on a separate key, keeping the left mouse button free for Void powers. I think I aimed down sights about twice the entire game after acquiring a few accuracy trinkets.All I've mentioned above are aspects I'd be willing to look past if the core of the game was amazing. Unfortunately, Deathloop's main hook, that of solving a timeloop by killing 8 people in one day, is its most disappointing aspect. Why?There's only ONE SOLUTION TO THE TIMELOOP!Like, what? Are we sure this is an Arkane game? I realise the difficulty of creating a timeloop with multiple solutions, but it's sort of become what I expect from Arkane following the reactivity of A Crack in the Slab or the secret death for Delilah. The game essentially leads you by the nose to its intended ending, making it virtually impossible to organically fail. It's incredibly frustrating, particularly following on from the Dishonored games, which had only your final objective marked on the HUD and left it up to you to figure out how to reach it. I'd like to stress here the sheer disappointment I felt when I realised there was only one solution. It kills replayability, a long-time staple of Arkane games, and honestly feels like a conceit that shouldn't exist considering this game launched on PS5 and PC, both platforms without the technical restrictions of last-gen hardware.With this in mind, (and with the knowledge that it makes me sad to not recommend an Arkane game), I don't recommend playing Deathloop unless it's 75% off and you head into it knowing there's going to be little of the Dishonored depth and (for lack of a better term) magic.

_childDocuments_.review: DEATHLOOP is a fun package, an extension of Arkane's experience with the Dishonored games, with more of a focus on gunplay and level replayability. The core DNA of stealth/powers is still present here, as is getting a lot of world flavor by overhearing NPC conversations and finding logs. The latter part here, information gathering plays a much larger role now though, as for the most part information is one of the few things you can bring with you across loops, so building your knowledge of Blackreef and its inhabitants is critical for a successful playthrough. That being said, there are some drawbacks -- the AI feels significantly less intelligent than a modern game's should, and the promise of figuring out the ideal way to assassinate everyone in one perfect day is more of a guarantee than a puzzle -- the game does a good deal of handholding in that regard. That being said, this was a perfectly enjoyable experience, and the solid bones are here for Arkane to build off of in the future should they opt to build out this core concept further.For completionists -- getting all of the achievements in this game is very doable, and took me just over 30 hours. The only word of warning here is regarding the 2 multiplayer only achievements -- even now less than a year after release, the queue times are rather long, and once you're in, the connections aren't the most stable. Best way to guarantee getting those two is to have a friend who can also queue up in friends only mode rather than waiting for 30 minutes to get matched with a rando who disconnects as soon as you load in.

_childDocuments_.review: A Dishonored reskin with more guns, more humor and lightweight pvp.Loop through the same day over and over looking for a way to break the cycle OR invade players and ruin their day to gather random cosmetics and upgrades.The single player is pretty much the same as dishonored, you get active powers like shift (short range teleport), nexus (link enemies to kill more at once) and equippable passive powers that, combined with unique weapons, allow for a fair variety of "builds". You have to assassinate a few targets like in dishonored but since the day loops, this time you get to try different approaches in the same run without having to restart . It's really fun to see how some targets that used to be difficult become easy and almost routine to take out once you have some knowledge and upgrades.Also, to progress in the story, you have to figure out the optimal way through your objectives so you can do everything in a single day; so overall, it plays a bit like a puzzle game as you gather knowledge and info on how to get as many things done as possible in the shortest time. Kinda like outer wilds but with crazy people shooting at you.Pvp is not a big deal in my opinion, don't buy this for the online feature. You invade others like in dark souls and that's it. Host has the advantage BUT as an invader you get points and upgrades even if you lose, and fairly quickly at that. I have something like 22 losses and 3 wins but still got my hands on half a dozen different skins. The game seems to reward having fun more than victories, with more points being awarded for weird kills or simply just surviving long enough.The story is well written, I liked all the characters and dialogue. There's plenty of lore and secrets to be discovered and theories to craft. Beware that the story is open ended so you might find the ending disappointing.Many people complained of performance issues but personally I've had none on my old gtx 1080 with everything on high and antialiasing, motion blur and depth of field off (my boomer eyes cant see ♥♥♥♥ if I leave those on).Definitely not a 10/10 but I enjoyed it well enough and recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to preface my review with a quick buyer's guide for those unsure if this game is for them or not.-- B U Y E R ' S     G U I D E --It took me about 24-25 hours to finish the story once, and another 22-23 hours to finish all of the content including all achievements.For Arkane fans: It's a game that boasts the quality we've come to expect from Arkane titles. It's well worth your time, although with a few shortcomings.For Action/Roguelite fans: It's a fast-paced shooter with some great weighty guns that look and feel really powerful. Sound also hits really hard which further emphasizes that heavy feel for all firearms and supernatural powers across the board. It also has elements of a Roguelite in terms of progression which is made in small to medium doses, leading to a satisfying feeling after each successful loop.For Immersive Sim fans: Sadly for those looking for a deeper player-driven experience you won't find the same quality as in Prey. It has great moments of exploration and world-building but it won't scratch the itch left by Arkane's 2017 instant classic. With that said, there are plenty of secrets you can easily miss, so exploring levels fully is advised, and also greatly rewarded both narratively and mechanicly.-- R E V I E W --I had three major gripes during my time with the game, my biggest being its lackluster multiplayer mode, contrasting its otherwise great singleplayer counterpart. In case you don't know already, you have to kill 8 targets in this game to break the perpetual time loop the protagonist Colt Vahn has inexplicably found himself in.One of those targets, Juliana Blake, can be a player controlled character but the combat in this game isn't complex enough to warrant this Demon's Souls' style invasion system. Rewards for killing Juliana aren't amazing either, and there are no significant differences between an AI or player controlled Juliana, just that it might be considerably harder if a talented and creative player invades your game.I played the mode as Juliana to invade other players, mainly to take a break from the singleplayer mode as curiosity for its multiplayer side overcame me, but also to get the two achievements associated with it. After a few matches I got bored of the long matchmaking periods (on release week of all times) and decided to retire not only from it, but to turn off the feature entirely so I could finish the experience on singleplayer mode in peace. I did not miss it until the end of my playthrough, which further cemented the feeling of its unwanted and unneeded existence.My second gripe with the game was the fact that there's only one real sequence of events you can take to reach the end of the game. You need to kill all 8 targets in a very specific order, which is fine the first time you do it, but since the game's nature is in looping continuously, there aren't many reasons to keep playing after you see the credits, unless you're like me and enjoy reaching that 100% in Arkane titles. Something I highly recommend because the achievements are very fun and allow you to see almost everything the game has to offer leading to a more complete, varied and prolonged experience.My third and final gripe with the game were the unfulfilling endings. There are two different endings both of which felt rushed and without a decent payoff or sense of real conclusion to speak of. It really felt as if the developers just rolled with the excuse of the infinite time loop, and decided not to make a meaningful ending to allow the game and player some closure. This was the only instance during my time with the game where the narrative felt weak and uninspired.Every other aspect of this game is otherwise well realized, from its shooting, to its exploration and world design the game shines with the typical polish we've come to expect from this artist-filled studio. Arkane are industry leaders when it comes to creating unique worlds filled with interesting corners begging to be scrounged through. This game is no different, although it takes a unique approach to their usual formula.The world is open in nature, an island divided into 4 zones functioning as sandboxes, which are comparable to smaller Dishonored levels. They provide several different routes from which to approach your targets, and player freedom is fully realized through its vertical and interconnected level structure. Deepening this segmented world structure, is a time-of-day feature which further divides the game into 4 different time periods, Morning, Noon, Afternoon and Evening after which the day ends, the loop finishes and the player returns to the beginning of the original day.Almost all 4 island regions have variants for each time of day (14 variants in total), where the environment, enemy locations, target availability and unique side activities change and become locked or available, giving the player answers to events happening earlier in the day only later at the end of it, and vice-versa. This ensures you'll have plenty of reasons to search every corner of every map during the day's entirety to maximize all possible gameplay opportunities, and finish all of the side content available. Some of which can and will be skipped by less attentive players.To provide a sense of progression the game includes a mechanic which allows for all 12 weapons, all 14 weapon trinkets (which function as perks for your guns) all 7 powers, all 20 power upgrades and all 33 character trinkets to be permanently attached to Colt, ensuring that when the next loop unsurprisingly comes, either by finishing it, skipping it or dying during it, players will be able to keep their favorite finds during each go around. This mechanic is directly tied to exploration, so the game gives you several reasons to explore levels to their fullest. There are also a couple of unique weapon variants with special properties which can be obtained by killing targets, stronger NPCs around the world and some optional side content.There are 7 powers in total, 2 of which are character specific, one for Colt which functions more as a passive ability and another for Juliana. The catch here is that unlike in the Dishonored franchise, you can't have all of your powers equipped during missions as you unlock them, having to choose only 2 before every level along with a maximum of 2 corresponding upgrades for each of them. This felt to me like a balancing decision from the developers accounting for the multiplayer portion of the game, which ultimately removed mechanical depth, freedom of choice and roleplaying value away from the singleplayer portion of the game. Something Dishonored 2 and Prey gave us in droves and we have yet to see Arkane do better since.Visuals are gorgeous, sound is great across the board, the soundtrack is very interesting because it brings 60's rock and jazz to an Arkane title, where they fit right in, and overall the presentation even down to its UI is very saturated and stylish.You can really feel this game could have used more development time to increase its various narrative outcomes, and perhaps refine some of its gameplay systems, but even so, I still thoroughly enjoyed my time with Deathloop, even after several distasteful realizations the game still found ways to keep me hooked, because at its core it's still an Arkane title and so it's right up my alley with its unique blend of narrative and gameplay.I would score the game a 7/10. I subtracted a point for the lackluster multiplayer integration, another point for the lack of freedom in combining powers and abilities like we've come to expect from their previous titles and another point for the unfulfilling endings. It has been a fun and positive experience, so I still do recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: DEATHLOOP is not without its flaws but to say it is anything less than the most standout AAA game of this year is a disservice. Impeccable style, fantastic level design, the willingness to remove quicksaving, the fantastic invasion mechanic, and consistently funny character writing and acting, and you've got a game that's a winner on all fronts. I just wish it was more brave and less handholdy - the element of discovery in terms of figuring out the loop is the strongest hook of the game, and it tends to downright give you the answer in a effort to prevent you from wanting to ever stop playing the game. This keeps the game engaging and fun, but never elevates it to the genuine masterpiece it could had been.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated after 33 hours of play time. The game concept, setting, theme and gameplay are excellent. However, the game setup makes it very unforgiving for bugs as there is NO SAVE between large level completions. That means if your have a crash to desktop or get stuck in a bug you lose whatever you had been doing so far that level. For me this meant losing an hour having had a tough fight with Julianna and killed a visionary only to crash and lose an hour of play. Overall I had 2 crashes to desktop and 1 falling through the floor (and then unable to get to my body to retrieve stuff) with about 1.5 hours of replay time from these crashes/bugs. In terms of performance it ran ok, but I have a high end system with a 3090 and the latest drivers.  The multiplayer aspect didn't seem particularly well thought out and the ending was disappointingly brief. Overall I would recommend it but ideally in a month or two when some issues have been fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: They is 2 types of people, the type that takes their time with a stealth game,watching the enemies for ages, learning their patterns,finding every hiding hole, trying to kill every enemy on a map without being spotted using nothing but their bare hands.The type of people tend to love RTS games,and are in it for the long haul.Then you have the other type of person, the person who runs and guns through a level of splinter cell wondering why they fail at the end, the type of person who spends 90 percent of their time on Metal Gear trying to lose the enemies because they keep setting off a radar, the type of person, who turns the game from ''Thief'' to ''Mugging simulator at bow point'', the type of person who plays Call of Duty not Battlefield.If you are the first type of person, this game is for you , the levels are well designed, with hundreds of ways to tackle each of the 4 levels, and yes they is only 4, but the day cycles 4 times, and when the day cycles the level changes, and makes it feel fresh but familiar. They is loads of dialogue to stumble on lots of lore to get the back story if you pay attention. They is multiple weapons and skills to use to kill your enemies you can even use the environment to your advantage. This game will take you well past the point of 20 hours before you complete it,the more you kill the bad guys and the more skills you get the harder the game becomes as the enemies get better equipped as you do. You will look forward to each new loop, for new dialogue, and finding even more ways to kill your targets, and when you are done you will be wanting more games from Arkane Studios. You will see why this game won awards. You will feel like you got a great game for the price. I recommend this game to you. It is an amazing experience.If you are the second type of person you will run and gun your way through this, complain that they is only 4 levels, how nothing changes, how easy it is to beat. You will complain the game did not take you more then 10 hours, how they is a lack of story, and how you couldn't stand the looping aspect of the game. You will complain that the game won awards and you don't think the game is worth it on offer let alone the asking price. If you are this person, i DO NOT recommend it to you.The game ran flawless on my RTX 2070S,i7 9700k, 32gb ram. I played between 80-144fps on high.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Deathloop, although it doesn't quite fulfill it's promise of breaking the timeloop in whatever way and order you want. I still had a lot of fun with the game overall and enjoyed Clay, who is a massive departure from the usual stoic Arkane protagonists. Clay is frustrated with his situation and is very vocally annoyed, but this doesn't make him humorless. He wisecracks and has a penchant for grim jokes.He's a very unstable character the deeper you dig into his character. Gameplay wise it's a very high chaos dishonored playthrough vibe, you can go non lethal but why would you? It's loads of fun just gunning through all the inhabitants of the island in order to break through the loop, the pvp is also really fun if not a bit inconsistent. Disconnects are frequent but when it works and you kill another Clay, it's very satisfying.My only real gripe with Deathloop is that it feels a bit unoptimized for pc. But it may just be my hardware, i would really recommend getting Deathloop on sale.Have fun breakin the loop <3

_childDocuments_.review: Totally recommend for Arkane fans. However, this is a smaller game than the previous titles from the studio. There is a lot of interference in the reviews from people who have technical problems with the game. I had one or two crashes and occasionally the menu backgrounds would behave a bit quirky during my current record of 42 hours of playing the game.Second divisive factor are the invasions. Another player can occasionally invade the game. This can be turned off, and in that case, at given points an AI actor will invade instead. However, after initial frustration with the mechanic I came to enjoy it. Sometimes you win, other times you lose.The story is OK and I liked the banter between the lead roles. There is also a ton of tidbits for the player to find and to figure out int the game. I missed a whole lot though I usually sweep all the corners. Sometimes the "side-quests" are interwoven through multiple areas and times of day which can make them quite challenging to solve.The main story can be criticized to be a bit hand-holdey especially during the intro/tutorial phase of the game, whereas the more obscure side-quests have none of that.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played. Biased, because I love this style of game, but it just FEELS GOOD TO PLAY. Doesn't matter what you decide to do. It is FUN! I understand that at launch there were loads of technical issues, and to be honest, I have run into a few (especially around graphics settings) that detracted from the overall experience even now. If it weren't for those technical issues, I would pretty much have nothing negative to say about this game. I consider the art direction and implementation the best I have probably ever seen. I would consider this "every frame a painting" in video game form. Be warned though, if you find yourself frustrated instead of challenged when needing to execute fast-paced combat, this may not be for you. Lots of things require perfect or near-perfect execution to get, but when you do execute, it feels so good after preparing and working so hard for it. I think where this game differs from others on this feature is a lot of games feel like they "punish" you for not getting the "platinum trophy" or the optimal time on a level, etc., whereas with DEATHLOOP, it is always a learning experience where you can improve without feeling like you lose player agency. I highly recommend this title as I do think it is quite a novel gaming experience and I have thoroughly enjoyed it!

_childDocuments_.review: Deathloop is another excellent entry form Arkane. With some caveats.So, to begin, this game is notoriously rough on PC. Severe framerate issues and constant crashing exist for users both below and above the recommended specs. I personally didn't experience a huge amount of these problems. I constantly received warnings of VRAM issues despite rarely having performance dip below 60 playing at 1080p on high. Towards the end of the game when things became more frantic, high settings started to hitch down to the 30 fps range and I lowered the settings to medium. Mind you, I'm just barely under the recommended specs with having an i5 from the same generation as the recommended specs and same everything else. I also experienced periodic crashing which made me lose some progress but never anything big. You may lose a lot more progress as the way the game is structured, the world is split into 4 zones with 4 time periods: morning, noon, afternoon and evening. If you crash or leave during any one of these time periods, your progress is set back to the beginning of that time period so you actually need to leave a zone to have your progress save. No quicksave on this game so buyer beware.All that aside, I loved this game. The combat, character interactions, music, presentation, everything's top notch. This game is significantly funnier than actual comedy games out there end up being most of the time just from the back-and-forth of Colt and Julianna. In a lot of ways this almost felt like playing a spy thriller movie from the 60s. The guns feel great to use and the powers feel like cheating sometimes which is an approach I highly prefer. However, after getting into the rhythm of the game, it becomes very very easy. Enemies and major targets are pretty easy to take down, sometimes the AI just breaks and other times it's a savant but still very fragile. The big difficulty spikes of Prey are completely absent for this game.Overall, I think this game is very fun and original despite being like the 4th timeloop game to come out in its launch window. It doesn't quite hit the high points of Dishonored 2 or Prey 2017, but it's still a delightful experience from beginning to end which is what I've come to expect from Arkane. I highly recommend Deathloop, but only after a good amount of fixing and patching is done. I got lucky but plenty others didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: So, let’s break this loop. The first 2-3 hours are hard and frustrating because you lose everything after each death and you must do the very same things again, but after some time, there is a big game changer – Residuum. I will talk about it later, but in short, you can save your loadout so you don’t lose everything after death.Your task is to kill all visionaries in a single day to break the loop. It won’t be easy because they are divided into different parts of the day: morning, noon, afternoon and evening, and locations of Blackreef island. You must gather intel about them and try to bring two or more to one place by changing their routines, but there are enemies called Eternalists, along with your rival from your dream at the beginning, that want stop you. If they kill you, you will wake up on the beach. Later, you will gain a Reprise that gives you two spare lives, so if you die you will respawn close to the place where you ended.After each loop, you will learn more about the island, find out who Colt and his rival are and the whole lore of the game. With this information, you will be able to end the loop nightmare. Lore is well made and you will want to learn more about it. Especially that mysterious rivalry between the two main characters is nice and it forces you to play the game more. The good thing is you can play in two styles: stealth or loud. I preferred stealth, but when things went wrong I changed to Rambo.The gameplay was fun, but three things bothered me. The first is the artificial intelligence of enemies which sometimes looks more like stupidity. You can encounter weird behaviour during shootouts, where enemies jump on obstacles without reason or they come in front of your gun. The second was bugged ragdolls that sometimes wanted to fly out of Blackreef and the third was a bugged menu. It happened only a few times but I had to restart the game to fix it. I’m not sure what caused it, but a few times menu controls started stacking and I was able to see controls that should hide after I pressed the back button.Deathloop has some weapons that help you jump out of the loop. You can find handguns, submachine guns, rifles and shotguns. In the beginning, you have weak weapons that can jam during a shootout, but later you can find some that have a special ability like silencer, explosive ammo and so on. Also, you can upgrade them with trinkets that add various buffs: higher rate of fire or magazine capacity, faster reload, better accuracy etc. They are hidden around the island and drop from enemies.Colt can have trinkets as well and he can get slabs that give him paranormal skills. He can be invisible for a short period, teleport a few metres and more. Slabs are obtainable only from visionaries or Colt's rival. After some time you will find the best combination of slabs and trinkets that suits your play style most. I preferred higher health, bigger magazine capacity along with faster reload and Aether slab for invisibility and Shift for reaching higher places.It’s an in-game currency that gives you the ability to save your loadout for the next loop. Without it, it would be very hard for me to play the game because I’m not a big fan of souls-like. After each part of the day, you can infuse (save) your stuff in the inventory for the next loops. Also, you can sacrifice items to gain Residuum if you didn’t get enough during a mission, but be aware at the end of each loop because you will lose it if you don’t spend it.The island is divided into four parts: Fristad Rock, Karl's Bay, The Complex and Updaam. In the beginning, you can feel lost because there is no minimap, so you must learn how each part looks and what is where, but they aren’t too complicated because size is ideal for the game's needs. You get used to them fast and they offer decent freedom to move around and plan your assassination. While moving around you can see how Eternalists talk and interact with each other and see changes in layout during each part of the day, so Blackreef feels like everyone is living their own life here. Along with a nice soundtrack that I was listening to while I was writing this review, the game offers a good atmosphere and it reminds me of the Groundhog Day movie.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, it has some of the worst pacing I've seen in a game, ever, coupled with an extremely unsatisfying ending. The story is ok at first, but nowhere near good enough to justify the massive slog you have to deal with. Did you like The Outer Wilds, and are looking for a new timeloop game? Save your money. I beat the game in only 19 hours, and I only enjoyed half of that time. The most disappointing thing is that this game starts out great. First 4 hours are full of interesting dialogue, intriguing mysteries, and cool new guns and abilities for you to experiment with. You get into a rhythm, and might guess "I bet the rest of the game will keep up this pacing."Then, the pacing gets really bad, really quick. The game is designed in such a way that you can only discover 1 new thing per area, maybe 2. You know what you need to do, you know where you need to go, but you have to beat wave after wave of AI who grind your gameplay to a screeching halt every time anyone knows you're there.Killing people without stealth is incredibly unsatisfying, despite the fact that all of the "best guns" (which have entire hour-long sidequests tied to them) alert everyone around you. In other words, you're actively punished for using the guns you spent so long getting. It honestly feels like you have to play a stealth game with the worst stealth mechanics you've ever seen. There's exactly 1 gun that lets you do stealth kills, and it's inaccurate at midrange. You also cannot kill the main bosses with that stealth gun, as they're all bullet sponges. Finally, the story. Oh, god, the story. It starts off setting up some extremely interesting mysteries which could be cool to figure out. Instead, you're spoon-fed the exact location you need to go to, given a bunch of extremely dense information all in one go, then spoon-fed the summary of that information. Literally every mission follows this exact same format except two, and one of those missions has an insta-kill unless you know exactly how to stop it (which the game gives you no hints for; I found the solution by accident). After 8 hours of "I really hope things get better" and then things not getting better, I was met with one of the most unsatisfying endings in any game I've seen. Questions were left unanswered, loose ends were left loose, and plot holes were left as holes. I honestly feel like Deathloop could have been a great game. It had a great foundation, witty dialogue, a fun gameplay loop at first, and a good sense of giving just enough info to leave you wanting more. If you told me that the developers ran out of time and were like "shoot, we need to spread out the story to justify the $60 price tag," I'd believe you.

_childDocuments_.review: Deathloop is a game that's a bit hard to recommend. On one hand, you have a visually stunning world with a real 60's vibe going for it, an engaging story and gameplay loop, and interesting weapons and abilities to play around with while you go through killing Visionaries to break the Loop. The campaign is a little short, as I made it through in about 8 hours or so, but there are also a number of side quests that can add a few hours to that. That being said, most if not all of the positives are outweighed by absolutely atrocious performance. This came can and usually does run like utter **** due to a well known and unfixed memory leak. Thankfully, there is a bit of a workaround to this. If you follow the settings that Digital Foundry suggest in their video for best Deathloop PC settings, the game should run fairly decently. You will still get frame rate drops, but going from being unable to play the game because I was getting sub-20 fps to being able to play at around 70-100fps is a big difference. If you have any major frame rate drops AFTER changing the settings, give your computer a restart. It's a pain in the ***, but it works. Summary: Deathloop is a good looking, fun game with a lot to offer, but is bogged down by massive technical issues that can render the game unplayable at times. If you use the settings that Digital Foundry suggests, I think this would be worth a $20-25 purchase when it's on sale. It has built in replayability, as there are many different ability and weapon combinations that could easily make subsequent runthroughs feel completely different.

_childDocuments_.review: Like dishonoured? Or did you find dishonoured required too much thinking by you and lost all interest? If you are the latter than this is for you, this is the most commercialised watered down form of Dishonoured possible. _childDocuments_.review: Arkane Studios is one of the last standing Western studios that are willing to take risks and create actual video games, not products that drive the sales of microtransactions or gaming-themed casinos. They deserve the support for their continued passion in this hobby.I must be in the minority because I had no issues running this game, no stuttering, no crashes. I had one soft lock that was resolved by restarting the level. Not ideal, but hey, nothing is perfect.Except this game. I cannot think of a single piece of content in this game that is worthless, tacked on or there to pad out the game. Everything ties into the mystery of Blackreef and the characters that inhabit it. The biggest draw is that mystery and how to end the timeloop.This game is not a "roguelite". It isn't a multiplayer shooter. It is something entirely its own. It borrows inspiration from many titles (Dark Souls invasions, Hitman's puzzle-like assassinations, Dishonored's powers) but this is a love letter to the genre that birthed Arkane and a hint of what games can be. You can express yourself in this game in a systemic, smart way that rewards forward thinking and careful planning.  I truly believe this to be a masterpiece, as hyperbolic as that sounds. It isn't for everyone, surely. But if you understand smart game design, clever storytelling and rewarding gameplay challenges, you owe it yourself to check this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is pretty good and fun. My main criticism is that it's a bit too easy, gameplay wise. Ammunition and Health is abundant throughout all of the maps at every time of day to the point where you never really feel a need to plan your engagements around resources. Health stations have infinite uses, munitions stations supply three ammunition types. Almost everyone dies in a single headshot which can make open combat very easy as you leisurely headshot enemies as they funnel into a doorway with the machine pistol, so there's rarely ever a need to actually take cover unless you're getting shot at from multiple sides or by a turret which makes the open combat a bit less engaging and getting caught during stealth sections very "whatever", lowering the overall stakes of gameplay interactions. Nexus should get 100% nerfed to have a cap on how many people you can link so you cant link like 9 people and then just nail-gun headshot one of them to clear a whole building. I know the powers in Arkane games are supposed to be strong but this one makes stealth ridiculously easy, and because your mana (?) passively regenerates there's no real reason not to use it in any 1vsX situation. I think capping it at four people (as Domino is capped in Dishonoured 2) would be a very healthy change. I think the Nail-Gun having 30 rounds by default also makes stealth quite easy. I know this is exacerbated by the aforementioned ammunition abundance criticism I have, but there's a reason you only got a set amount of Sleep Darts in Dishonoured - a silent, ranged 1 hit takedown is very powerful and can seriously cut down on the need to take any risks, especially as the Nail-Gun is fairly accurate even at medium ranges and it's not hard to headshot a static enemy. Being able to infuse guns to keep them between loops feels a bit too strong to me and also discourages the need to explore the map for higher level weapons because once you've got a loadout you're comfortable with and got three-trinket-slot iterations of the weapons you like you're basically set for the rest of the game. I think infusing Slabs and Trinkets is a good idea because getting those is partially random (for example, getting Slabs from Julianna invasions) and I imagine it wouldn't be too hard to justify in the lore as part of their mystical nature, but losing your guns on consecutive loops would give you reason to explore and search for rare gear, as well as plan out routes around finding guns that you remember the locations of (such as the Nail-Gun in Colt's Apartment). It'd also make your experiences between different loops vary more as, for example, if you don't go to Updaam in the morning, you'd have to go through whatever area you picked for the morning without an early Nail-Gun and therefore would have to approach stealth differently until you found a Nail-Gun in the map. In summary, infusing to keep guns between loops discourages exploration and makes consecutive loops considerably easier simply due to gear balancing rather than player ability. I feel like the reason the game has all of these design features that make the game so easy and the reason for the lack difficulty settings (as the first Arkane game in years to not have any) is probably down to the existence of multiplayer. This is because if players can be invaded, there's a need to keep everyone on a level playing field as the invaded player has to contend with Julianna *and* the level enemies, so scarce resources combined with the double-threat could be too punishing. I also imagine this is why we can infuse guns - getting invaded would probably suck if you've only managed to scrounge a basic machine pistol and nail-gun. I think that for a game with a primarily single-player audience from a publisher with a reputation for quality single-player titles, it should always come secondary to the single-player gameplay experience. In this respect, I think accommodating for the optiional multiplayer has placed burdens on single-player design choices to the overall detriment of the experience. I didn't play much of the multiplayer. On paper, I'm interested in it because I used to play a lot of Dark Souls 3 so the concept of being invaded is fine with me. However, unlike Dark Souls invasions, you have significantly more to lose from dying to an invader because if you can't beat the invader you can lose your entire loop progress - weapons, slabs and trinkets too - which is pretty annoying compared to Dark Souls invasions where you only 'lose' your souls, that you can just pick up again (under no threat of consecutive invasion unless you use an Ember/Humanity) when you respawn. I don't know enough about the multiplayer to comment on how matchmaking works but I think it's a reasonable assumption that the online gameplay is peer-to-peer (to enable Julianna to seamlessly enter your world), but the one dude I met was laggy as hell evident in his ability to teleport vast distances in front of me which is a very cool and interactive thing to lose your progress to. As far as other criticisms go: I didn't really care much about the other Visionaries. I know supposed to kill them to break the loop and I know from the audiologs and documents that they're all quite unique people, some more messed up than others but generally there's no narrative attachment to any of them other than Julianna - it lacks that narrative aspect of wanting to defeat the 'villain' and therefore murdering each of them is not very cathartic or rewarding compared to when you finally defeat the antagonist in other Arkane titles. The only character beyond Colt and Julianna that I actually felt anything for was 2-BIT (who I genuinely liked and think is well done) which really says something about the characterisation and what little the game tries to make you 'feel' for the other characters.As far as praises go: Colt and Julianna's dialogue dynamic is great, especially as you uncover more about them. This is a joint accomplishment of the voice acting performances and the writing. All of the voice acting in this game is great. The levels are pretty cool and distinct from one another. As you complete more loops you get more familiar with the layout and the most efficient routes which is a good form of self-progression where you begin to move faster and more confidently throughout the environment as you (and Colt) have both become smarter and more knowledgeable compared to your first times through, slowly traipsing around. The whole idea of coming back to areas you've been to already armed with new knowledge or abilities to unlock new paths is very appealing to me as a Metroid fan. Visually the game is pretty good although I did have it on lower settings most of the time. The premise is very unique and is definitely a story I'll remember for a long time, which is appreciated in the current market of sequels, spin-offs and remasters. While I have criticised the gameplay a lot for being too easy, one thing is does have over other Arkane titles is that the quicksave trial-and-error gameplay of their previous titles is straight up gone and replaced with an intended, in-universe mechanic now with the loop system. I think this is great for making the gameplay flow more and be interrupted less. This is because getting caught in stealth sections isn't a big deal and there being no chaos system or equivalent, so you can really get engaged with the gameplay without having to hit F9 and redo the past 5 minutes because some guy 400 meters away happened to look up. If you do end up dying and have to reset the loop, you're able to go through it faster and more efficiently than before because both you and Colt literally just did it. I like this kind of meta-progression. It feels natural and lets you play out full interactions rather than reloading every few minutes because you got caught Overall, the game is good and fun. Get it on sale if you can.

Save rushing through the levels once you've mastered them and have left no stone unturned. After all, you've got infinite loops to get familiar with Blackreef.Some additional things worth addressing:- Disabled player invasions and fought AI controlling the invader. Didn't want to be bothered with a laggy / cheating invader as well as losing potentially hours of progress toward the end of a loop. AI opponent is still not a pushover, though.- Suffered zero crashes in my full 23.3hr playthrough. Only suffered one bug from UI between levels that prompted a restart but no progress was lost.- Performance was very comfortable playing on mostly High settings at 4k (RTX 2060S / Ryzen 7 3700x).
