_childDocuments_.review: In terms of gameplay, in terms of mechanics, there's nothing to complain about inherently. It plays just like Dishonored, even inheriting the iconic Blink ability, and Dishonored played pretty great. The first point I want to make is that, mechanically speaking, there is no gameplay reason for Deathloop to be set in a timeloop. If you're not convinced, bear with me for a bit. Solving any of the puzzles has basically nothing to do with your mechanical skill, and while there's a mechanic for carrying equipment between loops, you never actually know what puzzles or encounters give you items that are actually helpful: in that way, it's more comparable to expansive games like Fable or Skyrim where you find or earn equipment through exploration and sidequests, rather than a new sort of timeloop game where you're building up an armory to overcome the final challenge. As far as pure game mechanics are concerned, this game could have just as well been a Soulslike set across an actual passage of time.To be clear, nothing I said there is a criticism: you could say the same for The Sexy Brutale, and that's an incredible game. However, it does mean that the game very much needs its story and writing to carry it, and this is where Deathloop falls so far short of the mark. As a player, you might consider asking questions like: How long has the loop been going? What determines who can remember things? What's the deal with the alternate timelines of myself that show up for plot convenience? What's with the military bases, and what was my character's connection to them? In fact, you'll definitely consider asking these questions, because the game asks them for you: Your protagonist vocally asks them, the floating text across the game references them, and the antagonist constantly suggests she has the answers and refuses to tell you. These are extremely basic questions about fundamental aspects of the game's conceit, and the game contains absolutely no answers for them. If you look online, you'll find lots of people speculating or guessing about them, but even fans struggle to come up with complete and satisfying answers. To the point where one quoted date for the ending is the year 2254, because apparently an early pitch for the game gave that date - not because of anything in the game itself. And I've only picked a tiny selection of questions, but the game is written to encourage a constant stream of them: there's one character who detonates a nuclear reactor when they spot you, as they will "do anything to protect their secrets." That character also "shouldn't be here." What secrets? What does that mean? Who knows. A lot of games get defended as being "open to interpretation," and if that's your first response to a situation like this, it's worth considering the difference between 'players interpreting ambiguous information' and 'fans needing to make up information because the game provides none.'As a timeloop game, especially a timeloop game that doesn't drive the player forward mechanically, the game relies on its story to push the player forward and reward them for their progress - and timeloop games tend to frame their narratives as mysteries for this reason, so that answers to burning questions make the player feel rewarded. I've mentioned The Sexy Brutale as one example, but of course Outer Wilds absolutely satisfies that analysis. Deathloop does frame itself as a mystery, and very much relies on its story to push the player forward, but it severely lets those players down. Not only does it fail to satisfy the players' curiosity, it even runs out of story to encourage you with: the player character and the main antagonist have a dialogue interaction every time you enter an area, at least until the game runs out of dialogue interactions. Much of my final hours were spent watching my character pass through the doorway, even tapping their fingers to their head as if they were talking on the radio, in complete silence - an animation that grows more and more frustrating the more often it happens pointlessly, especially since it seems to be deliberately long to allow for dialogue that isn't happening.I'm in two minds about my conclusion here. One takeaway might be that the game is incomplete: it absolutely would have benefited from more writing to answer those questions, more voice acting to pad out the silent animations. The second takeaway might be that the game shouldn't have been a timeloop to begin with: unlike The Sexy Brutale, Deathloop gives the player free reign of its loop... at least after a lengthy linear tutorial, and even then it tells you what the first things you should do are, because you need to unlock more of the mechanics (though again, you have no idea what mechanics you're unlocking until you do). Unlike Outer Wilds, you can't use prior knowledge from past playthroughs to skip anything, in part because you need to solve puzzles that remain solved between loops. At the very least, even if it was a timeloop, Deathloop probably would have benefited from being linear like The Sexy Brutale - or even, of course, Dishonored, a game which also had you exploring the same areas multiple times across its linear missions.One highlight of the game is its characters - the targets you're tasked with assassinating are delightfully hateable, especially Aleksis, who I would absolutely love to see more of. Of course, the nature of the game being a nonlinear timeloop means that there's only so much of them you can ever get to experience. And even then, it feels like the game is simply void of characterization where there could be more - like that character who has secrets to hide, apparently. You get to see her have a heated argument with another character, an argument that simply... ends. They don't agree or agree to disagree, they just stop talking and start wandering around a huge room in silence. It's utterly surreal. Another surreal element of the game is the multiplayer - you can invade other players as the antagonist, a mechanic which is as basic and barebones as it gets. Almost every time I was invaded, I was still at the start of the area, and could have simply turned around and left. When I attempted invading, it took ages for me to find my target, and the only reason I found them was because they seemingly forgot I was there. But also remember: there's no gameplay reason for the game to be a timeloop, and there's no gameplay reason for it to be multiplayer, either. The multiplayer doesn't unlock any more story, so it's not unfair to say that it's all but pointless: there's no reason to engage with it, after all.I can't think of a good note to end on, so I'll end on the game's ending: when you finally break the loop. It's the thing the game has been pushing you towards from the moment you start, with the text all across the game's world urging you to break the loop. The ending is as disappointing as you might expect if you've been following my review. There's some indication that I'm not the only one who felt that way, as there was a relatively recent update that extended the final cutscene. It's basically just a montage of all the named characters as they realize the loop is over. But in terms of information - narrative rewards for beating the game - what does it add? As far as I can deduce, the only thing you learn is that . That is such an extremely minor detail that it makes the whole cutscene feel superfluous.

_childDocuments_.review: Deathloop is one of the rare games I did not finish. I usually find enough interest to play even bad games to completion, but Deathloop's design takes too much pleasure in wasting the player's time, absolutely draining hours at no benefit to any party. The tragic part is there's something very promising in here, but it's buried in awful mechanics and unreliable controls. Played single player, can't imagine multiplayer being any better, considering it would just exacerbate some of the worst parts of the game.I was sort of interested in the story, but at this point, I'm so done I don't even want to read up or watch a video to find out what happens.The combat and some of the stealth and mobility was fun, but the way running and jumping is handled makes it impossible to have any faith in your jumps. Like some sort of anti-coyote time, it feels like you start falling  you even walk off an edge. Approximately 70% of my deaths were falling to my doom as the jump key did its very best to ignore being pressed.The leads and objectives are plain miserable. , et cetera.  Doesn't help that most of the rewards aren't worth the effort, and in the cases they are, hope you don't mind losing it all to one mistake that easily chains into several other ones and throws you back to square one.What I don't understand is, in single player, they offer the ability to enable infinite lives, aimlock, instakill shots as well as difficulty and loot tuning, yet it's too much to ask for a save feature. Not so much as a suspend save of any kind.I think I'm going to have to concede and say that time loop games are not for me. I only moderately enjoyed Majora's Mask, I dropped Ephemeral Fantasia like a box of spiders, and I've now done the same to Deathloop. I recognize that a lot of effort went into making this game, and it shows in many places, but it isn't enough to make me consider this an enjoyable game. It's spiteful, padded and self-important, and I hate when games remind me of myself.At least it had some nice music.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm cautiously switching my review to a thumbs up and rewriting it to highlight some positives, but it's with massive caveats that I'll get into later and highly encourage you to at least read the second paragraph and on.  The game is really great.  So far, I would not call it a 10/10, but it's damn close.  The biggest issue gameplay-wise is that it's far too easy to run and gun, which invalidates the immense effort the developers put in to providing so many tools and options in these sandbox style levels.  Outside of the enemy AI having a bit too much in common with Dishonored 2 for a gun heavy title, the game is impeccably designed and there isn't much else like it.  The way puzzles are presented is super refreshing and non-obtrusive to the pacing of the game.  It's really cool that they pulled that off.  Some people would call this game a rogue-lite, but I don't think that's a totally fair comparison.  It has a similar idea with the way "loops" work, but fundamentally it doesn't really feel like a rogue-lite.  Structurally, it has similarities to mega man games of all things (go into stages, kill the boss, get their power).  The loop factors into how you should kill the "bosses", and that's where the non-obtrusive puzzle solving comes in.  You always remain in control of the action, the puzzle of the loop is there but it doesn't stop you from playing the game, but you still need to solve it.  To reitierate, it's a very refreshing experience that any long-time gamer should be able to appreciate.As for the big caveat: technical issues.  The biggest issue is for VRR users: the game doesn't work right.  I've tested this very extensively at this point.  Mouse input and controller input provides inconsistent animation speed at arbitrary framerates when VRR is enabled, which is perceived similarly to bad frame pacing.  If you look at a frame pacing graph though, it's extremely smooth.  The game actually runs pretty great.  It's a heavy game, but it does run smoothly especially with dynamic resolution and a framerate cap.  The fix for VRR users is to disable in-game vsync, set the in-game framerate cap to 60 fps, and set dynamic resolution to target 60 fps, because any deviation up or down from 60 will feel pretty bad.  This will smooth it out, but you will still get the occasional frame or 2 of out of sync motion.  It's still a massive improvement, and this is a low latency, unobtrusive way to resolve the problem.For non-VRR users, you will also have a problem.  Mouse input is only smooth at 60 fps or 120 fps, and it will only be smooth if you are targeting those framerates via vsync (meaning full vsync, 1/2 vsync, 1/3 vsync, etc).  If you play on a controller, then you can get smooth motion by targeting arbitrary framerates via vsync.  So, sorry 144hz users without VRR that want to play with kbm, you'll have to change your desktop refresh rate to 120hz/60hz and use 1/2 vsync for an optimal experience.There are also a lot of users reporting regular crashing issues, though I can't comment on those as I haven't had a single crash yet.And I might as well comment on this, there is absolutely 0 evidence that Denuvo is causing any serious performance issues in this game.  If Denuvo is responsible for anything, it might be the fairly long loading times even on an SSD.  There is consistent precedent for that much.  I don't like Denuvo either, it will only harm actual customers in the long run, but I gotta keep it real and assign blame where it's due.

_childDocuments_.review: This review can (and will) be edited as time progresses and things get better.Day one (September 13th) - the first hour:Pros:- Great introduction to the story.- Game helps you to understand the rules of the game, but doesn't hold your hand for too long.- Voice acting is solid, the jokes and conversations that I've heard so far had me immersed and impressed.- Amazing variety of weapons, ways to handle situations and freedom right from the start.Cons:- Game audio wasn't synced right from the very first mission (after restart it got better, but after about 30 minutes the audio became worse again).- Stutters every now and then.- Multiple freezes up to the point where I had to stop the game to prevent it from becoming worse.Day two (September 14th) - game keeps crashing:- After multiple attempts, whenever I start the mission where I left off, the game crashes.- The error doesn't give me much information as to what actually caused the crash, only a lot of numbers and codes.Day 4 (September 16th) - first acknowledgement and small fix:- Arkane has released a small post that acknowledges the ongoing stutters. No audio issues are mentioned in the post. To my knowledge, no actual fixes either, just an update on the situation.- Apparently crash messages are supposed to give the user more information now, but nothing changed for me. The wait continues.Day 8 (September 20th) - game runs, audio issues are still a thing:- After some more tweaking, verifying game files, messing with resolutions and Nvidia settings, I managed to get the game to run again. I'll say that the game itself runs perfectly fine for me (based on 2 minutes of running around in a small area).- The audio is where the issue lies though. Gunshots seemed to be fine, voicelines seemed to be fine, the background sounds and music seems to be cutting out still though. One could turn the volume off and play without any issues, sure, but that's not what I'm about.FINAL DAY (FOR NOW):- It has been two weeks. My visual issues seem to be fixed, the game doesn't crash anymore, and that is great. BUT; my audio issues are still a thing. Some of the audio is perfectly fine, like the Colt/Julianna conversations, but other sounds are completely off-sync, like gun shots, doors opening, movement-audio. I will say that I'm unsure if this is something others are experiencing as well, but for me it's a big nope.So I've refunded the game, for now. Based on the fact that the visual issues have been solved and that the audio issues might be a local issue instead of one because of the game, I will change my review to positive so you won't get discouraged to try it out yourself and see how the game runs for you. You have the 2-week/2hour refund period as well anyways!Thank you for taking time to read through my updates these past few weeks, I seriously hope the game runs well for you!Edit #1: Just fixing grammatical errors. It's late. I need coffee.Edit #2: Added Day 4 update.Edit #3: Added Day 8 update and refund message. Edit #4: Added FINAL DAY segment.Edit #5: Actually changed the recommendation to positive - I forgot :P- Mango

_childDocuments_.review: Deathloop is a flawed game, to say the least. While visually very appealing the strongest thing about the game overall is the aesthetic. The guns are limited, the powers lackluster, and the story drops. It pretends to be a mystery, but there isn't anything to solve.On PC, it's laggy at times, experiences random freezing, and it's crashed more than once. Online play is miserable as the game becomes even less playable while you are "invaded" as the game drops frames faster than the AI drops the ball.I don't think I switched from a silenced pistol and Shift (Blink but bad) the whole game. Unlike Dishonored and Prey, which slowly unraveled their world and it's lore through exploration and interesting characters there aren't any of those. The most you'll get are text logs and recordings, and whatever snappy comebacks Colt and Juliana say at the start of the level.For those who loved the moral choices of Prey and Dishonored, there aren't any. All the enemies are cartoonishly evil or sociopathic to the point where killing them over and over starts to become tedium, not planning. There is exactly one true choice in the whole game with any consequences and it is, unsurprising, at the end.Unfortunately, as is the nature of Time Loop plots, the game quickly gets old. The sad thing is, there just aren't many things to do besides the main plot. Whole levels are unavailable at certain times because "There Nothing For Colt There", there are no side plots, no characters to talk to (besides a robot, kind of) and no mystery to be solved. For a game that spent so long teasing the player about "Why would you want to break the Loop" it does very little to show any reason NOT to, and doesn't even bother to explain anything else. leaving most of the curiosities to the player to tease out of short one page notes and diaries, rehash from old recordings (which had to be recorded that day, or before the loop, one would imagine) or just make up.While Arkane certainly tried something new, this game is hardly a 10/10, and until recently didn't even function correctly on many systems. If you want a fun, stealthy game that gives you arcane abilities and let's you make fun choices that impact the world, play Dishonored.If you want to play Deathloop, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am able to reproduce crashes in this game successfully every time simply by using a pepper mill gun and getting multiple headshots. I don't know why, but this will produce hitching and ultimately an "access violation" in one of the many threadworkers of 5950X causing the game to hard crash and have to be force-quit. This is similar to RE8 stuttering with headshots early on, when the Denuvo access hooks from Capcom's anti-cheat were misconfigured. I wonder if this is another case of that. If you are having lots of microstutters and crashes while playing this game, navigate to your Steam library, right click DEATHLOOP, select properties, betas, and then input the beta code "juliannashotme" to opt-in to a public fix for those issues. This used to help me, but now I am  crashing whenever using the pepper mill guns and getting headshots consistently. This game has a variety problem. People complained of Prey and Dishonored having too few enemies, yet curiously this game has only one enemy type: Eternalists. These are the indistinct mannequin looking party-going denizens that litter the island of Blackreef. They can have different loadouts, or even powers if they're members of the group known as the Visionaries (more on that later), but they all fail to stand out to me in the heat of the game as every last one of them are incredibly easy to dispatch. To compound this issue, the game has only 4 stages. Each stage is quite small and many of the levels in Dishonored 2 for instance feel larger than all 4 of DEATHLOOP's stages combined. The looping mechanic only serves to exacerbate the small scale of this game's world, each loop making you pull in closer with magnifying glass to reveal something truly ugly: this game flips many of the assets from Arkane's previous work. The buildings are ripped straight out of Dunwall it seems. The turrets are the briefcase turrets from Prey. All of the praise for this game's artstyle has me completely baffled. Yes, I too enjoy the concept art of this title. But in practice, during gameplay, the assets clash. The dreary buildings of Dunwall have random plastic faces glued to them with large fluorescent light arrays and glowing bright colors. There are chairs and tables within a bar built into random open air cliff sides. There are platforms in standing water (that for some reason kills you instantly?). All of this serves to create a visual clutter I've never experienced before in a game. DEATHLOOP's 4 stages feel like some kid with a level editor produced them with access to assets across Arkane's other games. This is in stark contrast to the carefully crafted worlds of Arkane's previous work.This game is Arkane's attempt at freeing the player from their decisions and allowing them to experiment with the sandbox. That's great, but the issue is that this game is incredibly easy. There is ammo everywhere, so why hack into turrets or use distractions to group enemies up? Eternalists die in one hit from most weapons if you are even slightly decent at aiming, so why use powers to position yourself or domino enemies for multi-kills? Even the Visionaries, the bosses of DEATHLOOP, are so incredibly easy to kill it took me multiple loops to even see half of their abilities (slabs) and stage gimmicks in action, and it was only due to me not wanting to kill them right away to see more. This game's story has an interesting premise, I'll give it that. The Visionaries are all unique sociopaths that keep the loop going day after day, and I think that the true shame here is that the player is given nothing to grab on to with respect to their backstories and motivations from the start of the game. Most of this is revealed through documents and terminal chat histories. Again, this contrasts from Dishonored where each target had an immense effect on the world around you that you could often just observe. In DEATHLOOP the Visionaries motivations and current dealings are given exposition through over-radio dialogue that often makes next to no sense and fails to engage the player due to a lack of foundational understanding/introduction. I didn't once care to know more about the Visionaries, I just killed them because I had to and that's the objective.The player is constantly interrupted by Julianna annoyingly yelling some curse words at them over the radio and condescending them for, as far as the player is concerned, no reason. The multiplayer facet of this game is busted beyond belief at the moment. Julianna players with high level loot can invade just starting out Colt's worlds and blow him away in an few moments. Additionally the matchmaking appears to group people together from all over the globe causing a laggy frustrating and awkward gunfight to ensue. Even the AI Julianna doesn't add much and often times turns into a game of cat and mouse. I like the idea of invasions in a game like this, but I think it needs more polish and more ways of interacting for it to become a positive for this game. There are too few powers and weapons to keep DEATHLOOP interesting. I feel like I've already seen every gun in the game and all the slabs I'm going to get. I can tell you right now the arsenal is far smaller than Dishonored/Prey. There are no new powers either, they are all some sort of remix of one of the Outsider's gifts, or in most cases just direct rips. Blackreef is littered with literal walls of text scrawled on objects, buildings, and landscapes. The text makes little sense and often displays platitudes like "Kill all of these m*therf*s". I find them distracting, with no way to turn them off. They break immersion and add to the visual clutter outlined above.This one is less objective, but I can't stand 90% of the voice acting in this game. The Eternalists overact so much, as well as the Visionaries. Think Forrest Whitaker levels of overacting. It makes dialogue nearly unbearable to listen to and has made me want to mute the voices in game multiple times. The worst offender is Julianna who will blurt into mission starts and ruin immersion time and time again during your playthroughs of Blackreef's 4 areas. If you are an extremely creative type and want to experiment, maybe this game is just what you've been looking for. The sandbox, while limited, is fun. There are no consequences for your actions on the overarching world. The story is very static and you won't miss out on anything for creating an orchestra of death with your toolkit. Additionally the movement in this game is very polished. It feels more like Dishonored's lightweight movement than Dishonored 2's heavy weighted action.The soundtrack to this game is KILLER. It's probably the best part of the game when the music gets bumping and the kill combos get high.Colt is a likable main character and has a great voice actor with solid banter. Shame about Julianna though. All-in-all this game makes me wonder what Arkane has been doing all these years. Why the delays when this title seems to just be derivative in nature with such a small stage count and few original assets / powers? The limited number of gun models, the small stage size, the lack of new powers all point to maybe bloat at the voice acting / performance end. This title has a lot of dialogue, most of which makes little sense and is obnoxious 90% of the time. If you are looking for an immersive sim, look elsewhere. If you are looking for a crazy sandbox to experiment in, look at Prey: Mooncrash. DEATHLOOP in its current state is just too small, too derivative, and too all over the place in what it's trying to achieve for $60 USD.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:Deathloop's core premise makes for an interesting setting, unique among triple A titles. It feels like Arkane were allowed to take a few risks, and created a stand-out experience. Combat is tight and controlled, and the integration of colt's various powers gives a really slick, fast power trip of a game. The 'murder puzzle' aspect is intriguing and drives progress in the early levels.The multiplayer provides an interesting dynamic, giving an interesting challenge to an otherwise straightforward game. Playing as Julianna, hunting down colt, is a lot of fun and very different to the campaign experience. The bad:Due to the constantly repeating environments and enemy placements, the game only gets easier as it goes along. Being able to repeat sections over and over means you quickly learn AI placements and routes, and by the end of the game It feels trite, like you're going through the motions to get to your objectives. This isn't helped at all by the very hand-holdy mission guides that waypoint you through the entire process. I would liked to have used my brain a little.Enemy AI is atrocious. They don't use cover. They'll stack up at door ways waiting to be murderd. Run into turrets. Stumble into mines and traps. Stand stock still unloading at you. They will swarm and overwhelm you sometimes, but once you have a spoilery ability, crowds become trivial to deal with.Getting invaded by sweaty juliannas 3x in a row while you're trying to plot a stealthy route through a minefiled is no fun at all - especially when playing with a controller on PC. I turned off invasions most of the time because I had no chance against the twitch shotting julies with endgame gear. SSBM (controversial, I know) and dedicated controller queues might go some way to alleviating this issue.Note: Since writing this review, Arkane added dedicated controller queues, and the game is much more enjoyable for it.The ugly:60% of the time, I booted this game, and it would have frame drops every 5-15 seconds. There was no consistency, no rhyme nor reason, and nothing I changed would make any difference. Often it would take just changing the resolution and back again to kick it into gear, but this didn't always work.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of technical problems and balance issues ruin what could be a fun game.The game runs horribly, before even playing the game consider spending an hour or so tweaking the settings and watching guides to get it to an acceptable place. High end gaming PCs are struggling to run this on medium settings and there is an awful stuttering issue that makes it difficult to aim.The  game is essentially a simplified version of Prey but with a much smaller map. The thing that sets it apart is the invasion mechanic which is horribly imbalanced. It basically allows a fully kitted out player to invade another players game easily kill them without anyway for the new player to counteract that unless they also happened to play the game on release day. The game will forever be in this broken state after release because there's no mechanisms in the game prevent this style of griefing.Add in that there are many ability and weapon combinations that are either impossible to counter or just not fun to play against and you have a mechanic that only serves to frustrate new players that must disable the mechanic, the sole mechanic that separates this game in a crowded genre, to farm out the required items to counter the maxed out invaders.Poorly thought through and obviously not tested. Would not recommend and I wish I could get a refund. It's just Dishonored with a gimmick.

_childDocuments_.review: After tinkering with the settings for half an hour to get the game to run smooth, I was rewarded with one of the most unique games I have played to date. But with the PvP the game becomes a new beast all together. Colt Vs Juliana PvP matches feel like intense spy vs spy battles of cat and mouse.Juliana invading your game as Colt is always rewarding as well, if you can manage to kill her you can take whatever power and gun she was using for yourself, and players will often bring in orange rarity or strong purple gear.Juliana has her own leveling system that is engaging enough, but they probably could have done a bit more. I find myself wishing Juliana had something to do while waiting for matches.(Colt for instance gets to run around the game world, hunt secrets and other things while waiting for Juliana so it never feels like your waiting) If you know what the game is, and it sounds interesting to you I would suggest picking this game up, just make sure you know what your buying.

_childDocuments_.review: DEATHLOOP has a great premise and great voice acting. Unfortunately, the game ultimately failed to deliver. None of the plot reveals were very satisfying, and the game ends on a whimper. Missions are mostly a series of fetch quests (half of which amount to finding a document to get a password for a door).The core gameplay was mediocre. Stealth is extremely straightforward - you can crouch your way past most enemies without them noticing. There are mechanics where you can throw bottles or hack objects to distract enemies (seen in every stealth game ever), but there's never any real reason to engage with these mechanics when the game is already so easy. The shooting mechanics are also equally uninspired. The AI is pretty bad, and mostly rely on bumrushing you. Once you find a silenced weapon you can headshot 80% of enemies before they even notice you (in fact IMO it breaks the whole game). There are mechanics where you can upgrade your character with special abilities and upgrade your weapons, but most of it felt fairly superficial, and the game never really becomes challenging enough to push you into investing into it systems. If you're really interested in the time loop concept, this may be worth playing if its on sale. Otherwise, if you're more interested in a stealth/assassination game, HITMAN is better in every metric.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game with high expectations and so far I have not been let down at all. While I love slowly analyzing movements and learning patterns coming up with strategies for executing 5 enemies without alerting anyone. Sometimes it's just fun to throw a grenade, teleport kick a dude into it and shoot the remaining with a shotgun. _childDocuments_.review: Deathloop is a pretty great game. You won't be committed to one style of play, you can kill with impunity, mix and match different loadouts, and no worrying about morality. In these respects, Deathloop shines brightest. It really leans into the gamey-ness of the whole affair and thus frees it from the shackles of its predecessors. As is customary with Arkane games, there is a ton of freedom with how you approach each level, and all of them are a masterclass in world design. There is quite a bit to discover, but the game will also hold your hand through the important things if you want it. There is something thrilling about going through a level for the first time, cautious and unfamiliar your are likely to turn to stealth and take things slow. As your arsenal grows and you get more comfortable, I found myself switching my playstyle to be much more aggressive, almost speedrunning things toward the end of the game and it was a blast.Deathloop is also not without it's shortcomings. Unraveling the mystery behind it all is great, but this is definitely a case where the journey is better than the destination. While the lore is great, it is also told through audio logs or notes exclusively. While a lot of this is par for the course for Arkane games, I couldn't help but feel that there was a bit too much fluff and they leaned a bit hard into the memer-yer elements of the characters. So many of the emails you read are dry or nonsensical that it makes it easy to miss something important. Deathloop could have really benefited from trimming the fat and making each of the things you find less prevalent but more impactful. Additionally, the nature of the game means that each encounter is the same every time, and there is nothing "missable" within a given time of day. I feel like the game would have really benefited from some opportunity-esque schedule for the main Visionaries, a la Hitman. Each time there is no reason to really stick around or watch the Visionaries go about their day to learn info about them or different ways to kill them. A missed opportunity in my book.At the end of the day Deathloop is a blast to play its flaws are more missed opportunities rather than things that weigh down what makes it great. It also doesn't overstay it's welcome, by the time you grow weary of running the same levels again and again and unlocked everything you want, it wraps it up.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Setting aside the poor optimization, the controls are easily the biggest problem with Deathloop. The game was clearly designed with controller in mind, leaking to an awkward experience on that wasn't well translated to Keyboard and Mouse. This may be a deal breaker for many, but I decided to give controller a go. Problem is that even at max sensitivity, you still turn VERY slowly. I can only assume this is a bug, but either way it makes controller almost unusable on this version of the game.Until they patch this controller bug and/or improve on the keyboard controls (IE: smartly switch which mouse button fires which weapon depending on if you are duel wielding or not) I'd consider this game a hard pass

_childDocuments_.review: This feels more like a very elaborate DLC for Dishonored than its own game, at least gameplay-wise, and that feels odd considering it's more expensive than both Dishonored games combined.There's also no real gameplay incentive not to just run around murdering everything you see, which also feels weird considering this is supposed to be a stealth game(?). There is no score system anymore, the 'special enemies' aren't very special, alerts don't do anything outside of boss rooms, and even if they did, you get your hands on a fully silenced, fully automatic 30-round SMG that one-shots 99% of the enemies in the game (even the special ones and some of the bosses) during the first part of the 'tutorial', heavily trivializing combat no matter how many enemies you have running at you.Limiting the player to just 2 'powers' is also a strange design choice for a stealth sandbox, which I think is meant to be a balance thing for the multiplayer invasions part. The very same part I suggest you try a couple times and then turn off completely, that poorly designed it feels to me. Neutering your creativity over such an insignificant part of the experience is clearly not worth it.Not having some kind of a 'rewind' feature in a game about timeline manipulations is another bizarre choice, in addition to there being no quicksaves/quickloads anymore. Having to ALT+F4 and restart the map just because you've screwed up a puzzle or killed somebody in a way you didn't like does not feel good, and the game isn't even challenging nor mechanically deep enough to warrant this in the first place.The level design is top-notch, but there are only 4 levels. Sure they change a little between the times of day, but they are fundamentally the same levels, hence why it feels more like a DLC.The character designs are awesome, even though you have to look past the painfully bland 'inclusiveness' to really enjoy them. A shame you don't get to interact with any one of them other than the main antagonist very much.The narrative is refreshing, and surprisingly not as confusing as you'd expect a timeline manipulation story to be. Only one of the endings feels like a complete one though, and it's not even the one the game is pushing you towards the whole time. I'd be perfectly happy without having multiple in this case.It could feel like I am bashing the game too much for this to be a positive review, and I do think this game is worse than Dishonored in almost every way, but it is still a fun and unique experience, and it only costs $30 ($5 with a good discount). Definitely worth your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, I absolutely love it but I'm currently in the process trying to get a refund to my Steam Wallet, JUST so that I can get the DELUXE version of this game, because the skins that come with it are really good looking.This game has solid gunplay and its all about Perseverance. After the first 2 or 3 deaths, you unlock the upgrade system that allows you to keep weapons after each death. This is when the REAL FUN with the game starts. Its just a giant mountain of going through the same day, getting better gear, upgrading it so you keep it after you die, and repeat. Its extremely fun.4 different zones, 4 different time zones for each day loop, so technically 16 different areas, cause each zone is different at each time zone.2 types of Shotguns, 1 type of Rifle, 1 type of SMG, 2 types of Pistols, 1 Nail gun for stealth, cool powers with power upgrades. Gray quality items are the worst. Then Blue. Then Purple. There are 4 legendary weapons in the game, but Purple weapons are still EXTREMELY powerful for specific playstyles.Gray weapon trinkets, then Blue, then Purple. Gray character trinkets, then Blue, then Purple. Specific effects on Purple weapons too. Like Stealing Health from enemies with your SMG, or a Rifle that tracks enemies after you shoot them. Its a really simple, powerful system.I wish their were more SMGs in the game, a Legendary SMG as well. I wish there were 2 assault rifle types as well, and maybe a Second Type of Rifle. And maybe even a Grenade Launcher and/or Rocket Launcher, but they've updated this game in the past, so they might add more weapons in later on.Make sure you play Single Player mode early on, or a Julianna with the best items in the game will INVADE your game and kill you in 2 seconds. Wait until you have a TON of Purple items, then turn Multiplayer Mode on, and wait for fools to enter your game. I can definitely see Multiplayer being a LOT of fun, once you get your Purple Items. Because then people will INVADE only for you to kill her almost immediately.All in all, absolutely an awesome game definitely worth $60. Hope you play it yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good arkane game, it's got the same gameplay feel as Dishonored only with less focus on stealth and more focus on guns. As a roguelike guy, the whole time mechanic is fun, and I think the whole gameplay loop of getting guns and abilites and then "infusing" it to keep it forever is a simple grind that feels rewarding. The story is superb, in my opinion, the characters are fleshed out even without the gaming sin of having to read notes and journals. _childDocuments_.review: looking at the game as a whole, it seems marred in a difficult development process. Visually and geographically it looks like it was supposed to be part of the Dishonored universe, somewhere to the north. The movement generally feels like the signature Dishonored style too.The AI, the guns (perhaps except for the four pounder) do not. And it's between these two that offer the biggest nails in the coffin for the game itself. Whereas Dishonored allowed for plenty of stealth, Deathloop forces you (often through no fault of your own) to deal with everything loud. It takes but one tiny mistake to alert half or more of an entire level, and it's not a given that you would know it's a mistake beforehand.AI can sometimes see through walls, can sometimes see out the back of their heads, sometimes get alerted over things that have nothing to do with you as a player, as well as tiny insignificant things like a door left open on the premises. It is tedious to go through the minute to minute gameplay with this in mind, and so any kind of playstyle other than gunning people down seems not catered for. It's disheartening to see this especially given that it wouldn't have taken much to bring the AI from essentially mirror what you can find in Halo or other pure combat shooters to something more sophisticated.Beyond this, even the way to complete the loop only really has one option, which to me is another nail in the coffin. For so much focus on "do whatever you want in a loop", only one solution will bring the game to the end, and it requires many loops to go through before you can achieve it. It would have been more interesting to see that a loop would be easy to complete with all visionaries dead, but the way their deaths was handled would have more of an impact on the ending. As it stands, it's just an incredibly linear experience that allows or no creativity on the part of the player.The level design mirrors classic Arkane Lyon style level design, so very much in the style of Dishonored. Generally, it feels fine if a bit one note. The environments, however, seem incredibly dull as between the four locations there isn't really a change in scenery. It's the same cold rock you're on, with no trees, grey buildings, and the occasional snow. Narratively, the visionaries themselves aren't interesting and the way of killing them (or forcing their hand through numerous side missions) is tedious and not fun. It also often requires you to restart loops over and over to find the exact time of day where a person is in a state that you can utilize as a player, which further funnels player action to be repetitive. If one of those tiny mistakes happen to influence this as well, it means you have to not just restart the level, but sit through another entire loop up until the same point, which invalidates any progress made in previous time periods. Endless repetition.The one cheery note that felt fleshed out was the banter and narrative between the two protagonists. Colt and Julianna's dialogue is good if not great. But it's a tiny sliver of goodness in an otherwise dull grey and rusty world. Finishing the loop made me think that getting off the rock was the best thing that could have happened in the narrative.I did not enjoy Dis- Deathloop. I understand Arkane Lyon wanted to try something new, and I recognize that an attempt was made. It would perhaps even have made a fine movie. But as a game, it falls apart at the seams.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to recommend. Consider this a 6/10. This game is creative in a certain way. The world is crazy and unique. The premise is interesting and the overall setup in general works nicely.However, in roughly 22 hours, there was only like an hour I REALLY had fun. And that was when I finally had a plan to go into the "perfect loop" and make it to the ending(s). The anxiety of knowing that I had to kill Julianna again, not knowing exactly when she will show up and with the idea in mind, that she could be an actual player who ruins that perfect run for me gave me something that I haven't experienced in quite a while. And this is probably why I recommend to play this game at least once.The big problem however: Every single character is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Everyone. Some have a tragic backstory. The only character who actually has character development has this development played out as a joke. And for the rest, since we never get to experience how they were before (radiologs and messages are not the same as actually interacting with them) and we HAVE NO CHOICE other than killing them anyway, it's utterly POINTLESS to invest any time into these characters. And that is where the game falls flat with it's own premise. If there WAS a way to get to the end without having to kill them. if there was a way to fix them, talk to them, properly play them out against each other... In other words. If I as a player had an actual impact on the characters or the world - OH BOY, this would have been 11/10. But no matter what you do... It's just: Find a way to kill everyone in one loop, get to the end and then make a final decision for one of 3 endings. And only that perfect loop with the anxiety of online invasions is actually worth experiencing, at least once.Hence: 6 / 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game on two conditions: 1. If you are an absolute fan of Arkane’s previous “immersive Sim” shooters/stabbers, then this game will literally feel right at home for you. It’s basically Dishonored (UI and powers) but without the “story-karma” annoyances in the narrative. You're encouraged to kill in this. Have fun. Like before, the game wants you to experiment and strategize to begin which will award you adequately once you get the basics down. Like Infusion weapons to take with you for each day loop.   2. If you want a different yet interesting take on the whole “Time-Loop” or Rogue-Whatever genre, this game already feels like a more generous for your time entry (especially if you are new to these types of games). Also, the dialogue is actually entertaining which helps push the "Ground Hog, but with guns" nature of the story. Don't expect it to be as deep as Hades. Just roll with the banter between the two main assassins. Also note that some veterans of these types of games might think this title is too easy and possibly not enough content to justify the price. I personally think it’s just fine at the moment with what it’s trying to be.However, like every freaking AAA title that gets heavily marketed to death lately, there’s seems to be some release-performance annoyances even with this title. The "stuttering" has been addressed or patched, but who knows what else is still there. It could be just Arkane’s typical luck on PC, or it’s the annoying DRM that’s impacting performance. If you want high resolution with Raytracing on, there’s a high chance you won’t be able to get the desired frame rate yet. Here’s hoping somebody gets a patch out ASAP. It plays pretty well on my machine (RTX2060Super AMD 5600X), but I know if can run a hell of a lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like playing a movie about a time loop, which is exactly what I wanted. It's not great as a vehicle for "emergent gameplay," like Prey and Dishonored were, unfortunately. It is great as a vehicle for a simple story that delivers cool "FPS gameplay" with original-looking guns and cool abilities to move around with. The writing is humorous and light hearted for the most part.The thing that carries the experience for me is the game feel; it's fun to weave around the levels quickly and execute your goals. If you mess up or die it doesn't matter much, you can try again. If "getting good at a game" and then pulling off a perfect run is your type of thing, I recommend it. If you want emergent gameplay with RPG elements... Look at Prey or Deus Ex. Or System Shock 2.Additionally, I think Cruelty Squad actually pulls off a lot of the game stuff that this game does better. The level design is just as good, the writing is fun and more thematically relevant to the gameplay, and death itself losing meaning is explored much more seriously. It even has the same core premise of repetitious target assassinations. It might not have the slick art style and 60s / 70s musical influences, but it has a great art style in its own way.

_childDocuments_.review: You will not like this game if:1. You hate Arkane games.2. You're expecting the same exact thing as other Arkane games (people that are saying stuff like tHiS IZ jUsT DISH0noored probably also think Among Us and Star Wars are the same because they involve space). 3. You're expecting a hardcore challenge. Two things to note for my playthrough: First, I did not have the major stuttering and tech issues other people seemed to have so I was able to enjoy this masterpiece without annoying stuff. Second, I am only interested in single player games so I did not even attempt the multiplayer. This game blends elements of Arkane's previous games, a unique roguelike loopy storytelling concept similar to Hades, splashes of colorful designs, wacky characters, and weird sci-fi plot stuff and it exceeded all of my expectations. The story and banter between Colt and Julianna are great. The game overall is just fun from the fast combat to the variety of weapons, weapon upgrades, skills, and abilities you can mix and match. Highly recommended to anyone that can run it without issues and just wants to have a fun game front to end. My favorite weapon was easily the silent submachine gun and I attached upgrades to it that let me shoot from the hip with accuracy, and shoot from long distances with great accuracy/damage. While the combat and AI intelligence is on the easier side which works better for casul gamers like me, I love that the game makes you piece the puzzle together when it comes to figuring out the past history of the environment, characters, and how to get to Colt's main end goal. A landmark in immersive sims.

_childDocuments_.review: Only after trying a few other games did I appreciate how well designed Deathloop is. It manages to strike a perfect balance between exploration and guided gameplay, without ever getting overwhelming or stale. Skills and guns are a real treat to mess around with, and open the door for new strategies. The characters express themselves in small doses, without assaulting you with bricks of dialogue or long cutscenes. The progression system, however, is not that well paced in the single player or the multiplayer. You tackle the beginning of the game trying to hold on to any upgrades you find, but eventually you find that perfect set of broken weapons and even the golden unlockable guns are not interesting anymore. Still, the loot system gives you a real desire to stay alive, without being too punishing, similar to a fight in a battle royale after spending 5 minutes collecting loot. Multiplayer randomly awards upgrades through every "match" played,  but ultimately it relies on a player base that is no longer there.I've also had some problems with graphical settings. If you are too, I highly recommend you follow the digital foundry recommended settings except replace FSR with DLSS (I believe that video was made before DLSS was added to the game).

_childDocuments_.review: NOT A PERFORMANCE REVIEW. cant speak about performance cause it ran really well on my rig. from what im hearing they're introducing fixes to the stuttering issues. _childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game and I've got to say, I am very impressed. This game was gripping the entire way through with the right mix of adult humour to make it funny. I am a massive dishonoured fan and only now decided to check out deathloop and this game does not disappoint. The Soundtrack is slow but can ramp up and become epic during high action scenes and the whole premise of a day constantly repeating and you having to memorise what people do, the best routes to take at what time etc is truly immersive. One main focus of the game is learning what to do with your character, the way I think of it is that Colt (your player character) is learning the methods and ways to traverse levels at the same time you are which really allows you to immerse yourself into the game, as Colt wakes up knowing absolutely nothing about the situation he is in so you learn about things at the same time he does. One thing I can't stress enough though for new players is AT ALL COSTS AVOID SPOILERS, a key element of the game is gradually learning about the story of blackreef and whats going on, if you look up spoilers it would completely ruin that aspect of the game. This game also has a fair deal of fan service sprinkled in through references to other games that Bethesda/Arkane developed. Another thing that is spectacular about the setting being a time loop is that stealth doesn't matter, if you are caught and get into a firefight throughout your adventure you A. Have 3 "revives" of sorts and B. Its a flipping time loop so if you fail you can just retry the exact same scenario again. At the start the game is frustrating because you loose all your guns and trinket (Practically upgrades)but after about an hour of gameplay a major game mechanic is introduced that allows you to keep your items through loops. Despite only having 4 different zones to visit throughout the game they are all vast and depending on the time of day all offer significantly changed layouts in terms of item placement, guard patrols, stuff that's happened etc that it offers enough variety to always feel fresh. A complaint I sometimes hear about the game is some of the magical ability's are almost identical to those from the dishonoured franchise but in my personal opinion they are varied enough to feel different. For example, the Nexus ability allows you to link enemy's together so that if one, for example dies, all of them die which, at surface level, sounds exactly like the Domino ability from dishonoured 2, but once the many upgrades for the ability are utilised it becomes vastly different, more versatile, and most of all overpowered as ♥♥♥♥ (who thought giving you the ability to kill 20 enemy's by just headshotting one of them was a good idea) Overall this game and the characters in it are amazing, the setting is amazing, and most of all the game play is amazing. In my opinion this game is easily a 9.5 out of ten, my only major complaint would be that sometimes enemy's are able to seemingly see me through what should be solid objects but that rarely happens. The last think I would like to say is that because this is a Bethesda game you should NOT buy it full price because it will undoubtedly go on sale. One last quick thing to mention though is that this game SHOULD NOT, be played by anyone under the age of 11~ as this game is, constantly making sex jokes and swearing. Thank you for taking the time to read this and please, do yourself a favour and buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: is Arkane's most recent immersive-sim. Its release was overshadowed by technical difficulties that have been fixed for the most part.You play as the amnesiac Colt who awakens on Blackreef island trapped in a time-loop. Intent on breaking the loop you start exploring the four areas of Blackreef. The locations change depending on the time of day and buildings that were inaccessible before may open up. The gameplay is similar to Arkane's other games Dishonored and Prey. You sneak, stab and shoot your way through. There are supernatural abilities that you can find and retain through the loop that make subsequent exploration easier. The levels are well designed and there is something to find in every nook and cranny. The other, new gameplay element is that of a detective game. In order to break the loop you have to find out the day-to-day routines of the time-loop's architects. You look for clues, solve puzzles and neatly arrange your leads in your journal. DEATHLOOP maintains the strong gameplay that Arkane established over the years although with a weak AI. NPCs barely react to silenced weapons for example.The game also has a multiplayer that is rather unnecessary. In the multiplayer you invade other player's games as the assassin Julianna to stop Colt from breaking the loop. Fortunately it is optional since it is not fleshed out whatsoever and feels like a nuisance. On one occasion I invaded another player but before I had even loaded into the game they escaped netting me a loss. A different time the player I invaded just hid, not going for any objectives and just waited for me to disconnect. Since it is peer-to-peer with Colt being the host you'll more than likely experience issues with lag. Aside from two achievements you can complete the entirety of DEATHLOOP in single-player.The area in which the game really shines is the aesthetic, world-building and characters. Blackreef is perpetually stuck in a 60's disco retro-futurism. So between jukeboxes and Eames lounge furniture you'll find heavy CRT monitors and oversized phones, all in a colorful palette. The voice-acting is remarkable and the writing excels as well. Especially the quips between Colt and Julianna. Great soundtrack too.It took me around 20 hours to finish DEATHLOOP. You may want to wait until Denuvo has been removed from the game but other than that I wholly recommend it to fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of reviews for this game that are either not about the gameplay (technical issues, etc) or that are coming from a very different perspective than mine, so here's a different take. Deathloop is a pretty unique game that makes the mistake of looking like other, established games - it's a good game, but only if you understand that it's different from what you'd expect out of Arkane or an immersive sim.I was not enjoying it for the first couple hours, and to be blunt I'm still not sure that I think it's "great" - but it _is_ a good game and if you're after the right thing, you'll enjoy it. The thing is, if you try to play it like any of the games it looks like, it's kind of... bad? But hear me out.1) The enemies are incredibly non-challenging. This is not a FPS, or a challenging stealth action game. Sure they have killed me a few times, but they do not create tension, I'm not afraid of them, and it's easy to mow down mooks like a cartoon gangster with a tommygun, cackling madly. While this game could definitely benefit from better, more challenging combat - the Eternalists you fight in Deathloop are best compared to Goombas from Mario. They are not a challenging enemy, they will rarely kill you, but does that make them bad enemies? No - they are a part of the environmental puzzle. The enemies in Deathloop facilitate the gameplay - they give you a _reason_ to do gameplay things, but they are _not_ the gameplay themselves. They are a hurdle you need to consider while solving other problems. Sometimes you need to keep one or more of them alive, which breaks up the violent monotony.2) The "challenge" is, again, not in the shooting, stabbing, or sneaking. The challenge is mostly cerebral - solving complex temporal problems by performing different actions in successive loops to gather different information, then combining it into a whole to take out your targets. It's, again, VERY EASY to run into a Visionary's compound with a shotgun and blast everyone in the face. That doesn't mean the game is "easy" because guess what? You will later on learn that one of the mook guards you killed is important for an event at a later time of day, so now you need to do it all over again and find a way to single them out and _not kill them_ while still achieving everything you achieved before. Deathloop is entirely about experimenting with this specific process, and the easy enemy difficulty feels meant to prevent this from turning into a chore or a grind. You are a killing machine who has been through this loop thousands of times before, the enemies aren't good enough to bar your progress - but you start having fun with them, approaching them in new ways, doing silly things. If you're the kind of player who enjoys things like that, you won't mind the weak combat here.3) And finally, if you slowly crawl through every map combing it for loot, exploring every corner - you need to stop doing that to enjoy Deathloop. The weak combat means that there aren't interesting encounters to break up the monotony of that slow-crawl exploration, and there's no sense of tension because you're not afraid of your enemies. You're also going to revisit all of these locations dozens of times before you beat the game, if you explore every inch right now, you're going to be bored out of your mind the next 10+ times you come through here. Leave some for later! Don't stress about it! In a time loop nothing is ever permanently missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I will defend this game until I die. If you're a fan of Arkane because of their game design, I'll admit that Deathloop is not going to satisfy that immsim itch, the best I can compare it to is a character action sandbox that allows you to use the beautifully thought out level design of an Arkane level to become the most stylish murderer you can be. It's a game that really shines in atmosphere and world building though. Blackreef, the island that you'll be exploring and the time loop that surrounds it, scratches an itch that I can never get anywhere else. The music, style and just *feel* of this game is borderline perfect to me.Obviously this game has its issues, its a lackluster puzzle game and the multiplayer has a lot of performance issues, but if you come to Deathloop for the action I can assure you that you won't be dissapointed.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a long time to understand this game.Not story wise, thats pretty straight forward, but the game as a whole.I saw the trailer, I loved dishonored and was disappointed for all the reasons and things that it didn't do and was.It has no Karma system, no deeper meaning to killingThe Time loop isn't really a loop, more like levels,There are a lot of different upgrades to not so many weapons.AND there is no quicksave. Once the level is started there is not turning back.This also means no saving within a level.OK and now here is what I learned and I figured this out after I played through the entire game and all achievements (at the time - they added more now, gonna get them soon though)Everything fits.The game is EXACTLY what it says it is. And that is the way it's meant to be played.It has no Karma system because it's an island where exactly that is the point, you don't have to be pacifist, go and have fun, something i could never do in dishonored games, let loose like everybody else.Experiment and be creative.The timeloop is no realtime loop but rather levels and this is beatiful, because even though you have different setiings and goals you are never under time pressure, something I always struggled with in other time games, because when time is critical I get stressed and make mistakes, have to start aaall over again and get frustrated, in Deathloop this is the second genious design, yo don't have to go through the entire level all over again you start somewhere within the day and once you know where you have togo it's often quite straight forward to get there. There are a few segments that take time, but thats unavoidable I think. There arent a lot of weapons to choose from, yes, but thats not necessary bc every gun feels different and the different perks make it rewarding and satisfying to find the best version of your favourite playstyle gun and also let you experiment.I do miss the quicksave option, but at the same time it forces a playstyle that I wouldn't have if there was a save option like that. The game really gives you that imersion that you have the respawn power but only limited amount of times (3) so you better be careful and use it wisely, or run straight in die and have all the guard distracted. So you see it's not about perfection it's about rolling with what you got while still giving plenty of room for sick combos and perfection.And yes you can't save within a level, but you don't have to discover the whole level at once!in dishonered you would spend sometimes 2-3h looking for every secret int the map before finishing a quest, but theres no such pressure in deathloop, come back as many times as you like, you'll always find some new detail here, understand a bit more of a puzzle there..It's not a story game, It's not a loot shooter, it's not a war simulation.It's a game for reckless fun. A game and world where there are no consequences, a game where you are free to ♥♥♥♥ around and find out. And thats great I think.I at first didn't see it for what it was, but now I give it the rating that it deserved. 7/10Edit: originally i foolishly gave it a 10/10 review, for the reasons mentioned before, but even with great execution of what it says it does there is one thing it simply lacks: charcter, soul, meaning, depth, name it however you want. It's a well made game, but nothing more, therefore the real rating it deserves is a good 7/10 but It's not a classic, and I barely think about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was massively disappointed with this game. I was fine with it not just being "Dishonored with guns" like I was hoping for after the announcement, but this game wasn't even fun as its own thing, and became downright frustrating soon into the experience. -There is no way to revert to a quicksave if you make a mistake, meaning that you have to redo the entire day if you realize you missed something or if you miss a jump to a ledge.-The game litters your screen with floating messages from the character's brain. It was funny at first, but soon became obnoxious. -You will basically explore every location within your first play session, but to progress in the story you have to a) do everything in a precise order and  b) find the passwords for a bunch of random safes and little tucked away closets and shacks. The precise order takes hours of repetitive gameplay to discover, and it is often hard to tell if the safes and closets are actually worth the effort of finding their passwords (Which are randomized for each player, so no looking up guides).+There is one redeeming quality about the game: you can kick enemies to make them ragdoll off of ledges. If that were the whole game, and they sold it at a quarter of the price, I might even recommend it. But they put too much else in the way.Overall, I am sad to say that this game is too frustrating to be worth its price.

_childDocuments_.review: After 5 hours of running around I learned that this is the worst Arkane game so far. Here is why:The stealth is like if you took dishonored and gave the player 24 crossbow bolts + have them littered around everywhere. You can mark groups of enemies with the link power and one shot them all with one nail for no challenge.The action is ruined by terrible AI and corridor level design - you can just cheese most gunfights. The enemies come in a corridor in large groups and it's very easy to kill them with one grenade or a few headshots. It's way to easy to pop headshots on PC, even on the worst quality weapons you can easily one-shot large groups almost risk free.The "leads system" is a mess. The worst implementation of objectives in linear levels I have ever seen. You will basically go to a location, wait for a loading screen, watch 2 animations of door opening, to then open a safe 20 meters from the door and go back.The lack of a scoring (non lethal / stealth etc.) makes this game worse than Dishonored. The lack of a solid linear level progression with a kill by the end of each level and an RPG progression makes this game worse than Prey.The powers are not very interesting. If you played Dishonored before you basically are already tired of them. The weapon variety is also extremely slim.It's a good experiment, but I honestly would have liked if they just stuck with a linear path, have us kill 8 people in a row instead of this weird puzzle game that plays you instead of you playing it.I don't recommend this game, don't let the paid reviews on IGN 10/10 fool you.

_childDocuments_.review: , when the writing (particularly on the dialogue front) comes into its own, it positively roars. I struggle to recall a game released this year brimming with as much personality as Deathloop. The guns pack a punch; and when combined with Slab abilities that punch hits that much harder. The pep in its step and its commitment to carrying out it's highly stylized vision of a timeloop is endearing, and eventually charms. The light-hearted tone it adopts is also a great decision - in the hands of other devs, this game could be a poignant statement on the futility of time and the inherent comfort - or discomfort - of eternity. To some degree it does attempt to say that as well, but does so with a distinctly fun tone....that almost militant drive to stay faithful to its vision comes at a cost. The dialogue - condensing primarily along the banter of Colt & Julianna - leaves little room for exposition, which is then delivered via random flavour text scattered across the world. Blink, and you miss it (no pun intended). Crucial backstories lay buried somewhere inan email on a computer that you might never even see. As a result, when you do complete the "story", you might just be going "wait, what? When did this happen?" The AI in the game is also just...incoherent, completely oblivious to their fellow NPCs keeling dead literally over their heads (even after the patch).But that can still be overlooked to a degree. . I personally got so many crashes - and they combined with the save system in horrible ways (basically, nothing you do is saved until you successfully exit a level that you're currently playing in; play for 3 hours in Updaam and if you get a crash at 2 hours 55 min....all the progress of those 3 hours is lost).I will spare you the details of Bethesda support's competency; I guess the inspiration for the AI of the NPCs must have come from observing them in the wild. [After days of troubleshooting basics, they told me my system is just below specs when every benchmark assessment software has said otherwise, lol. Plus the CTD I kept getting is one so many others have gotten as well - ones with literal 3000 series cards]. This game has no reason to be this technically demanding in the first place, but that's a different discussion altogether.All in all, I walked away from Deathloop very pleasantly surprised, but frustrated with it stifling its own potential. I do not think this is a masterpiece in any way (and side-eye all publications calling it such), but I do think there lays the making of one in its skeleton. Though some may find the looping mechanics rudimentary, I think they worked very well for what it set out to do, and an actual time limit imposed would just discourage player exploration.My "rating" for this game, - if I had to  give one that is - would be a strong . I can only hope Bethesda continues to fix the mess of the PC version - I have broken the loop, but a few secrets and mysteries remain. I however, have no incentive to look for them since a crash is guaranteed. :/Thanks for reading!
