_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I really really do. I think it's a great concept and I can truly get lost in it. The gameplay is fluid, the story is intriguing and the voice acting is spot on, I especially like the banter between Juliana and Colt as annoying as it gets - it just fits the stories and the characters!So why the thumb down? You know what they say about first impressions. If you can wait for this game to get stable before you buy, please do so. It. Crashes. At. Random. Times. In the middle of a level, when loading out your gear, at the end of a level. It doesn't matter. It crashes with such randomness it's annoying. And the worst part is when you've just finished an objective or two and are headed back to the tunnels, why you ask? Because the game doesn't save until you make it into the tunnel and exit the stage.If I could actually put the game down, I'd wait till they started releasing patches and updates but for now, I'm suffering through Deathloop. It's still easily one of the best gaming experiences for me this year and I hope when you eventually get this game, you have as much fun sans the crashes.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fun, but it's expensive for what is included.I had a good ~10 hours to get through the game. The time loop mechanic can get old, and repetitive.The game implies that it is a lot more dynamic than it is, The invasions are fun enough, I had issues with latency a lot, and its not fair in any sense of the word. I've also heard that there are meta guns that are just completely overpowered in invasions.  It will just frustrate you when you lose the last 30-40 minutes of progress AGAIN. My advise is to turn off invasions and just enjoy the base game with the AI invader.At the asking price, there is NO WAY I could recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: Deathloop is by all-means a mixed bag. As a big fan of arkane's previous titles, Dishonoured and Prey as well as the insane acclaim that followed this title by journalists and game reviewers alike, I expected an almost perfect game. What I found was a highly repetitive shooter with poor gunplay and bad level design (inclusion of mines was the worst), with a cool premise, characters and story. Although gorgeous, the few different explorable areas weren't that interesting and the neccessity to go back and forth from each on a regular basis purely to fulfill boring tasks, meant that the overall experience wasn't incredibly enjoyable. All in all, not a bad game, but certainly not a great game. I'd give Deathloop a 6/10 and suggest only playing it if everything surrounding its tepid gameplay intrigues you.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: Reading a lot of the reviews and some assorted tech analysis, doesn't surprise me that this game has some bad optimization + possibly some bad anti-piracy stuff slowing down your system. The game's heavy into being level-based, in that you collect loot but if you don't finish the level you lose it. I've had the game stutter like crazy and freeze on me twice now losing me my run each time. Freezing that often in a game like this? Driving me insane. I'm refunding it now and I'd suggest staying away unless your graphics card is the very best on the market or if they patch some of the issues.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: A culmination of all the game systems Arkane developed for Dishonored, Mooncrash, and stuff they learned while helping with that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Wolfenstein we don't talk about. Great voice acting, cool visual setting, for a Zenimax game surprisingly few bugs. UI could use some work, though, same as the netcode for multiplayer invasions, and AI. Guns don't really feel that interesting.A 'Groundhog Day: The game' with guns.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: It's got style, it's got class...     it also has annoying bugs and a rushed ending.I was ready to give this game a recommendation during my first 15 hours. I liked the art direction, the gameplay was fun, the loop and information gathering felt rewarding. Then, the longer I played the more it would become a stuttering mess until I quit and restarted the game. On start, it would run like butter, but 30-40 mins in and the frametiming would go ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! By the end I couldn't take the repetition of restarting the game every few missions.Speaking of the end... wow! All the endings are a real kick in the junk. I'm unclear why they rushed this wet fart of an ending, because the story felt like it was building up to be so much more. I was left feeling like, "wtf did I waste all this time for"? Total clown pubes.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very confusing. At the start of the campaign, there is no proper tutorial that defines the basic mechanics. Initially going over and over through the same small maps and gaining very little to no info about the happenings was very frustrating.But after completing 3-4 loops I started to like the game as I gained new powers and guns. Finally after completing the campaign, I guess I did enjoy parts of it.Coming from the creators of Dishonored series, I did expected more from this game. But nevertheless its a good game, but obviously not a great one.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: In it's current state, I can't recommend this game. The devs need to work on optimization before this game could be considered playable. The writing and characters are all really charming and engaging but the random stuttering and uninspired gunplay made me refund. Looking to pick it back up on a sale when the issues have been fixed hopefully.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: No good for busy gamers, because you cannot save and quit.There are no saves within each level, only when you exit/enter the level. This is part of the game design that I like, because you are forced to deal with whatever happens inside the level and sometimes must abort your plans and make an escape.But if something comes up IRL and you have to walk away, you have no choice but forfeit any progress made within the level. This might also ruin the entire loop, since you have 3 other times of day to wait through before you are able to retry the level you were in.Give us "save and quit" and I might recommend this game, although it is not as good as Prey or the Dishonored series.Deathloop reuses many Dishonored level assets, and seemingly all of the Dishonored art design, which is unsettling as a fan of the original and comes off as lazy. Even the magic powers are 90% copied and shuffled around from the Dishonored series.Probably the worst part of this game is that there are no likable characters or places. Everyone in Dishonored and Prey and even Prey Mooncrash seemed to have their own lives and motivations and, whereas the characters in Deathloop seem to just hang around in battle arenas waiting for the player to come. In the old games, the levels were part of a living city where suddenly an action scene breaks out... In Deathloop everything is a samey deathmatch arena.Most disappointing, there seems to be no reason to play stealth or non-lethal, which was my preferred style. I guess this is because you're trapped with the most awful people, and the story never lends you sympathy for any of them.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: i tryed to give a shot to the game because i loved the dishonored games but this game is just stuck in a loop (i know thats the point of the game) i've put 3 hours into the game and i feel like im done with this.its not fun at all, the ai is dumb, and the levels are dull the abilities are just copy paste from dishonored... i regret buying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: Its an Arkane-lite game not as intense on the immersive sim side of Arkane games like prey and dishonored... It also extremely on rails with how you approach targets sure tehres different ways to kill but the approach of setting up the targets and the kill order is presented to the player in a nice little flow chart of what to do.Recommend on sale
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: A buggy, strictly worse version of Prey: Mooncrash that costs way more than it should.The amount of content is very low with a heavy emphasis on repetition.You can only save after each mission. Even just opening the menu can cause the game to soft lock. So you get to run that boring mission, again and again.Deathloop simply isn't worth the money, frustration or time
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: Colt and Juliana's performances are excellent and the world looks cool visually.Those are the only positives this game has. What should be hitman with magic set in a quirky 40s/50s alternate reality world is instead a game where 90% of any planning and action happens through boring menus. There's no loop here to speak of where you have to get everything right from the first try, you just load different missions which ensure you eliminate your targets in order. Combat's never been Arkane's strong suite...and that trend definitely continues here. I couldn't bring myself to keep playing because I was just so incredibly bored and disinterested, the exact opposite of how I felt with their previous work (Dishonored and Prey).Dishonored 1 is one of my favorite games of all time and I am a massive fan of Arkane's work, but this game isn't it. Quite frankly, it's awful
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: The game had a very intriguing storyline and setup, and while I understand you are in a 'loop' the game got pretty tedious at the halfway point.If you forgot a mission or forgot which cycle to do yours in, you had to do everything over again or at one point I had to run through the same 3 missions at 3 different times in the story to get one piece to the quest.It's fun to try out, but after the first cycle through, the game feels hollow and redundant.
_childDocuments_.name: DEATHLOOP

_childDocuments_.review: If at first you don't succeed Die, Die Again. From the team at Arkane Lyon comes an innovative take on first-person action. "DEATHLOOP" transports players to the lawless island of Blackreef in an eternal struggle between two extraordinary assassins. Explore stunning environments and meticulously designed levels in an immersive gameplay experience that lets you approach every situation any way you like. Hunt down targets all over the island in an effort to put an end to the cycle once and for all, and remember, if at first you don't succeed die, die again.

name: A Juggler's Tale
detailed_description: FEATURES Make use of the puppet’s strings in unique puzzles, find your way around obstacles, cross raging rivers, sneak through bandit camps and make it past dangerous traps to find freedom. Explore a beautiful and grim world, inspired by the tone and mood of traditional fairy tales. Live through an intense story of hope and empowerment. Find out what it takes to truly break free from all strings attached. STORY 'Ladies and Gentlemen! Come in, come in! In the mood for a story, are we?' Abby is an artiste held captive at a circus: She spends her days entertaining the audience and her nights in a cage, longing for freedom. One day, she escapes the circus and gets to explore a mystical world. Alas, freedom comes at a cost and Abby soon finds herself dragged into the dangers this world has to offer: In a war-torn, medieval fairytale, surrounded by ravaged, starving citizens and hunted by the relentless cut-throat Tonda, Abby has to cross raging rivers, make it through bandit camps and around traps. Her adventure is always accompanied by the lyrical rhymes of puppet master Jack, who is telling her story while holding the strings of his puppets firmly in his ever-helpful hands. Who can Abby trust? Can she find a way to truly break free? Despite dangling from her threads, will Abby learn that she can still influence her destiny? 'Abby, Abby... Don't you see, the threads holding you up – also hold you back.'

_childDocuments_.review: A small pearl that shines among a few reviews. My impression so far is that it is a beautiful game, very pleasant graphics and with good background music. Really easy puzzle games, but if they had been more difficult the sweetness of the game would have been lost. My overall rating is 8/10, unfortunately there are some graphic bugs but the translation and narration are well done.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a very short, but innovative little gem that oozes charm right from the menu screen. From its variety of picturesque settings, impressive rhyming narration and sinister twist on childhood fairy-tales, this is a must play for Indie lovers of puzzle and adventure titles.The narrator in A Juggler's Tale only speaks in rhymes, utilising a familiar and friendly premise to capture players' attention. This purposeful resemblance to fairy-tales is obvious right from the beginning but combined with its Tim Burton styled graphics and faceless characters, it exudes the perfect concoction of uneasiness. The protagonist is a young girl named Abby. She is a string puppet and kept locked away by the circus ringmaster, until she is needed to complete her sole task of entertaining audiences. One day, Abby manages to escape and is suddenly thwart into a grim world where everything and everyone is seemingly set on causing her failure. She is relentlessly chased by the ringmaster’s thug named Tonda and has to face numerous obstacles with the odds stacked against her. The narrative explores metaphors surrounding the strings that hold her back, can she ever be freed of them? Can she change her path? It is a whimsical but compelling story about empowerment, hope and the desire for freedom whilst showcasing  how beautiful and dark reality can be.A Juggler's Tale is a puzzle adventure game with light platforming elements. Players can interact with objects by pushing them, picking up and throwing items. Movement is redolent of 2D platformers, whilst the game environments have 3D elements. I did not find the puzzles themselves to be difficult nor overly simple, but logical. If I did become stuck, it did not take long to figure out what to do, as the mechanics are very straightforward. However, what I did find quite unique was the concept of puppet strings. They quite literally hold you back from moving forward, if something overhead is blocking them, you cannot pass. I found this to be quite clever as it was both physical and metaphoric.There is a mixture of chase, puzzle and stealth scenes. All are quite forgiving as I noticed the narrator frequently giving a small hint if I took too long in a certain area. Each segment feels fresh and seamlessly flows between chapters.The game is quite short, I played at a leisurely pace, and it took me approximately 3 hours to finish it. Those who are puzzle connoisseurs may even finish it before the 2-hour mark. Considering the games story, excellent pacing and combination of differing elements, I thought it ended on a high note, without adding tedious unnecessary scenes just to prolong game time. It only focuses on the main plot; thus, I think the short game length is adequate. I especially enjoyed the ending, it felt an excellent conclusion for each character, also utilising the string mechanics once more. I did not perceive the lack of playtime to be a con and would not wish for it to be extended. Furthermore, I failed to find any aspect of the game to be negative, hence my lack of a cons list. Perhaps the price is a bit too high for my liking, but the quality is palpable.Upon launching this game, I was impressed at its beautiful art style, the contrast between the gorgeous vibrant settings and the condescending, hyperbolic tone of the narrator was done brilliantly. For such a short game, there was a vast array of unique environments, from a ravaging open sea, a calm picturesque countryside to a dimly lit forest overrun with spider webs.  The graphics exude a gothic aesthetic, seeming to have been inspired by the likes of Tim Burton but maintain their vibrant beauty, truly manifesting in their obscurity.Similar to the graphics, the audio is just as impactful. The menu screen plays an overtly cheery tune, reminiscent of exaggerated circus themes and was actually quite catchy. The voiced narration was also notable with every single line in the game being rhymed which came together extremely well. I thought the narrator’s changes in tone were portrayed brilliantly and were purposefully uncomfortable in some more poignant scenes. The sound effects and music in other areas were just as memorable. These elements of the game were by far the most standout feature, giving it a unique edge over other titles. A Juggler's Tale is an impressive adventure puzzler, excelling in its beautiful visuals and gothic undertones. Featuring a rhyming narrator redolent of children's storybooks, but with an eerie, mysterious twist. Highly recommended for fans of the genre but consider its short playtime before purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler’s Tale is a charming fairy tale adventure with puzzle and platform elements.Abby, is being held hostage. Confined in a cage, she is only released to perform circus tricks for scraps of food. The ring master is mean and domineering, and her life is tedious and unfulfilled.All she wants to do is break free from her prison and see the world.One day the opportunity arises and Abby escapes, but the ringmaster won’t let his cash cow escape so easily, and enlists the help of Tonda and his gang to track her down. Abby must run for her life, navigating rough terrain and solving puzzles to progress. It’s easy to fall for the charms of A Juggler’s Tale. It felt very polished and considered. Behind the cute fairy tale façade lied quite a dark tale of confinement and control, and the need to break free. As with all fairy tales, there are heroes and villains, and the characters in this play are very compelling.I loved the style of narration, even if the rhymes felt a little forced sometimes, I was still impressed with how the story was told in an effective manner. I thought the narrator struggled sometimes to keep in character but he grows on you and becomes a comforting voice in the end. The only issue I had with the game was its repeating text when dying in tricky situations. It can become slightly frustrating hearing the same verse over and over again. I wish the game would learn to omit this. The puzzles are quite imaginative and woven into the story very well. They are quite varied with stealth sections, platforming, boss fights and various situations to escape from. The only downside is that although they feel original, they are reasonably easy to solve. The puzzle designs are so realistic and practical that it becomes a case of trying different things until you get that Eureka moment. Sometimes, it is plainly obvious what direction to take whilst other times it took me longer. I never felt that I struggled on any of the puzzles though. The game has a habit of helping you out too much. If you are short on a jump, the game will correct your shortfall, if you ponder too long, the narrator will throw a clue your way. The experience is absolutely frustration free and I loved that.The pacing of the game is masterful with slow, poignant moments, interspersed with frantic chases and dramatic scenes. I absolutely loved the ending. A Juggler’s Tale is cleverly presented as a stage play.The stage curtains open and we are introduced to Abby, the leading lady of the show.All members of the cast are puppets and are controlled by the strings that hold them up. We watch as events unfold on stage. There are five acts of the play, with chapters in each act that can be accessed after the game to easily pick up any achievements you might have missed. The game should take between three and four hours to complete. Controlling Abby, your movement is restricted by her strings. She is unable to pass objects that are in the way of her thread like shackles. To pass, she must find a way to circumvent these obstacles. Engaging like a 2D platform experience, the characters and the environments have 3D elements.  Abby is able to jump, climb, push and pull objects, as well as swinging on ropes and throwing projectiles. All these attributes will be used in solving puzzles and navigating the landscapes.There is quite a lot of stealth involved whilst trying to escape the clutches of the Ringmaster and Tolda’s gang. Avoiding searchlights is a common occurrence, and thinking up ways to distract and disable enemies is a popular puzzle choice.A Juggler’s Tale is one long run for freedom and there are sequences where you have to use your platforming skills to evade the chasing pack. Jumping up rocks, climbing ladders and solving puzzles under pressure of capture can occur.There are a few, what you would call, boss fights in the game. They usually involve Tolda as he hunts you down, but instead of combat, you must defeat him by solving puzzles and tricking him into submission. There are quiet moments of reflection and contemplation, along with some words of wisdom from the narrator.The story teller acts like a friend, or even a father figure, offering Abby clues, and sometimes even lifesaving assistance by reaching for her strings and saving her from death.As you travel through the different environments, the narrator talks in rhymes, describing the scene, her predicament, and the likely outcome. It is very reminiscent of a fairy tale storybook being read out as you play.The visuals are a treat. They feel quite gothic in style with some stereotypical fairy tale evil. The landscapes are colorful and detailed and look absolutely gorgeous.The strings on the characters are very well done and look very effective and I love the stage aesthetics that drive the story.There are some absolutely beautiful soundtracks throughout the game, which give an amazing whimsical feel to proceedings.Sound effects are impressive also with some noticeable environmental sounds like insects in the grass and weather effects.The narrator’s voice can lose a bit of traction now and again but the way they have managed to tell the story through rhymes was admirable.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of the game starts straight ahead and away from any complications. A cafe in the corner of which a puppet show is about to take place and the audience is watching. The narration of the events that you will witness during the one and a half hour gameplay is done by the puppeteer and the director of the show, and all the sentences are recited in the form of poetry. The catchy tone of the narrator makes you curious to follow the continuation of the story, and in the meantime, the exchanges with the main character double the charms of the story. The protagonist of the story is a puppet named Abby, who continues to work as a slave in a big circus. Like many people, he is not satisfied with his work and sees himself as a prisoner. So he decides to start new adventures by escaping from the circus.The story part should be considered one of the strengths of the game, which stimulates the player's sense of adventure. The voice actor of the narrator also coped well with his role and gave a memorable performance. Abby's actions with the environment and the narrator's funny jokes are among the strengths of A Juggler's Tale, which will not diminish its charm until the last moment.If you are looking for realistic graphics, this game cannot be recommended; But if you intend to stay away from the usual atmosphere of skirmish games and wander a little in fantasy worlds, this title will be a good option. The world of A Juggler's Tale has a simple design, but it manages to capture your attention. One of the features of this game is the variety of colors and the design of its attractive environment; A large farm with the sunset behind it or a village where people are celebrating and dancing are among the beauties of A Juggler's Tale.Music has always been considered one of the important elements in inducing dramatic load and this importance has been used well in the game. Understanding the space and atmosphere, the composer decided to choose the folk genre to implement his thoughts; A right decision that ended up in favor of the game. The variety of pieces seems appropriate, but the rhythms of the pieces are very similar to each other, and the audience who struggles with solving the puzzles may not notice the changes in the background music. However, the music helps the picture well in the critical moments and keeps the beat up well in the chase sequences.The gameplay of A Juggler's Tale has undeniable similarities with titles such as Limbo and Inside. Moving along the screen and not interacting with the background and solving different puzzles are the features of Playdead studio games, and the game also follows this rule. On the other hand, Button Mapping, or the arrangement of the handle keys that you interact with, is completely similar to Inside and its fellow games. The use of objects is done with the R2 key and X is used to jump. As a puppet, Abby has no special powers and must use her intelligence to survive. The puzzles of the game are not particularly challenging and this is not acceptable considering the time required to complete the game. The creators have tried to create puzzles through the ropes that restrained Abby in the form of a puppet, but this does not help A Juggler's Tale much in terms of gameplay, and in this sense, the player will be disappointed. For diversity, the production team has included chase sequences in the gameplay, which are not very attractive and cannot be memorable. If you fail during these game chases, don't worry; Because thanks to the proper checkpoint system - which was also one of the sources of inspiration for the creators from Inside and Limbo - you will not be nervous.Finally, the construction of the small and compact Kaleidoscube studio should be considered a short and acceptable work that, although it has shortcomings, can entertain its audience.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun side-scroller reminiscent of games like Little Nightmares and Inside.  It features beautiful scenery and feelsy music alongside a fun children's story.The only downside was the incredibly short game length which only took me 90 minutes to complete.  I'm all for supporting indie game devs but $18 for 90 minutes is pushing it.  I'd recommend catching this one on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Abby is a puppet who lives in a beautiful, scenic storybook-like world and works at a lovely circus with the ringmaster and a friendly bear; but sometimes things aren’t so nice, like how the ringmaster locks them up in a cage at night. Abby escapes, and goes on a grand adventure! But the story isn’t done just yet, and the ringmaster isn’t exactly willing to let her go.2-3 hours to complete, A Juggler’s Tale is a dark fairytale sidescroller with easy puzzle and platforming sections. With a charming storyline and an interesting plot twist, the game is genuinely very nice to play and look at as the graphics and explorable areas are picturesque. Easy to beat, easy to complete, stress-free gaming at its finest.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler’s Tale is a dark fairytale-esque sidescrolling puzzle game presented with beautifully vivid graphics showing sprawling landscapes, and polished narration. After escaping a circus, Abby finds herself fleeing for freedom and navigating the dangers of the world. She is guided by her unseen puppet master, speaking in rhymes and riddles. The primary innovation is how the character as a puppet is integrated into the puzzles - her strings dictate how she moves, sometimes allowing her to glide unnatural distances but mostly preventing her from making progress. Other puzzle sections include throwing objects, moving blocks, playing with basic physics. Quite a few sections require timing alongside some stealth, jumping and chase sequences. It’s very reminiscent of / &  in that respect but much more colourful. As far as I could tell, there are no mouse controls. Aiming throwables felt awkward both with keyboard and controller. Aside from some points in the story, jumping feels stunted, especially for someone on strings. There were sequences that were shockingly unforgiving with how precise the game sometimes requires, it’s not a difficult when this is realised but prior it was quite annoying. Whilst going for the achievement ‘On Dry Feet’, it further cemented in my mind how frustrating the controls in this game can be.The game is short - one playthrough will take approximately two hours, full completion in three to four hours.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, buggy experience.Quick list of pros/cons:+ Beautiful landscapes and atmosphere+ Lovely cartoony aesthetic (no wood texture on most objects, even though it's applied to cutouts at the start/end of each act)~ Roughly 2 hour playtime. Consider the price...~ Puzzle solutions are either straightforwards or extremely obtuse (red is used to indicate interactibles. They put a red handle on a cart filled with apples at one point, you're expected to pull/push the cart and use the apples once it's in position. I didn't notice the red handle due to dark lighting, so I figured the puzzle only used the apples)~ Narrator didn't appeal to me. He did great when trying to sound grandfatherly, but as the game progresses and he's supposed to sound more villainous/foreboding, it seems really fake and half-hearted- Strings clips through objects and are 2d textures (it stands out because very few objects clipped during my playtime)- Story is meandering and doesn't seem to know where it wants to go, opening context makes the ending more confusing- EXTREMELY buggy, to the point where I bypassed most of the 3rd act by flying through the air to the end (I interacted with a ladder in midair, it caused the game to freak out?)So, I'm okay with short games, and how valuable the game's length vs price will be a personal decision on your part. I cannot help but notice (based on other reviews) that I'm the only person who seemed to have bugs during their playthrough.- Near the beginning, you need to lure a bear away from a post with an apple. I got stuck between the post and bear, unable to reach the apples, and the bear knocked me away from the apples every time I tried to pass it. Abby wouldn't interact with the post to progress the game, since the bear needs to be on the opposite side of the post for the event to trigger. I feel like this is an oversight?- During stealth segments, enemies would occasionally see me through walls and clip through them to get me. Nobody else seems to have had this issue...?- During a segment involving lighting fires with a torch, the torch wouldn't light campfires/lanterns if I brought a lit torch to one. Rebooted the game and it worked; not sure why it happened to begin with...? (You can hold 'interact' near a fire to increase the intensity of a torch past it's initial status, fyi)- After getting locked in a cage at one point, you're supposed to break out. Upon doing so the narrator cried 'ABBY!' and my screen went grey, Abby clipping through the ground to oblivion. Had to reload. - Aforementioned glitch by the dog segment where I pressed the interact button near the hanging ladder and Abby began to fly through the air. This is probably an edge case but it let me bypass roughly a quarter of the game. Some puzzles are obtuse for the wrong reasons.- At the beginning, you're supposed to figure out to knock over an object to get a guard's attention. The problem is the thing you need to hit isn't presented well to the camera, with emphasis being put on an irrelevant area to make the camera angle more pleasing. The scene looks good this way, but it makes progressing confusing.- Aforementioned apple/cart puzzle in the 3rd act.- Final boss(?) had weird detection issues for me and I looked up a guide to verify I was doing the right thing to beat it. I figured out the first half but the second part seems obtuse, even in retrospect.- Water based hazard (you'll know it when you see it) isn't well explained, I wasn't sure I solved some puzzles properly until I looked up a guide and went 'oh that's actually supposed to happen'Game looks gorgeous, and clearly has some great art design. Theater segments/framing looks good, opening segment is nice (but is never followed up on), and moment to moment gameplay is very similar to  and . Music is good, if somewhat generic. Game design is... mixed. Good setpieces, camerawork tends to mislead players towards unimportant items that look nice. I hope that if the devs make another game, to focus more on the camerawork and story. Otherwise good cornerstone for a team to begin to learn and grow from, hope to see more from these devs.

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a beautiful and artsy side scroller, with immersive narration and a fairly solid and light-hearted story-line. You play as a girl named Abby, tied by strings and moved along by a puppeteer (also the narrator). The game is split into 5 acts, with each one being set in different scenery with amazing and captivating views. Extremely aesthetic and calming. Narration is quite immersive and well-done and the music sets the scene.The game is constantly making you figure out the next move as most of it is puzzle-like scenarios to be able to move along to the next stage. None of it felt repetitive and explored different methods time and time again. The achievements also tie in really well, as it gives the game a bit of replayability with hidden challenges set inside each Stage.The game itself is quite short, only lasting about an hour and a half.Overall, I really did enjoy it and would happily go back to it. The story kept me submerged in the game, and the ending made me feel emotions. The game itself is quite short, which is not a negative unless analysing it to it's fairly high price to gameplay ratio. I really do recommend this game, as I thoroughly enjoyed it - just not at the full price mark.

_childDocuments_.review: tells the story of Abby, a circus performer kept in captivity who wishes to see the world outside of just the circus. The story is beautiful, the artwork is creative, and the writing is in verse, with a bemused and still soothing narrative voice, all within this short puppet story.The game is set in the form of a 2D puzzle platformer to help tell the story, which is broken up into 5 acts, each with its individual small checkpoints that you can revisit at any time. The game uses autosaving but you can always go back to the main menu to go to an earlier checkpoint. No manual saving is needed.The individual puzzles are all well contained on-screen. You don't need to carry tools or clues from one part of the game to the next and so it's just a matter of figuring out the mechanics of the puzzle and the available pieces before figuring it out. Because Abby is a puppet and is on strings, well, those strings play a critical role when it comes to the puzzles at times.There are not many games that are written in rhythmic verses and so this game really stands out. The other one that comes to mind immediately is a straight up platformer called  But back to this game, putting the artwork and the verses onto flowing pages and you would find a very appealing children's story, filled with hope, wonder, bewilderment, and conflict. There is time to bond with Abby and to face her fears together as you solve your way through the game. There are some puzzles and platforming that are somewhat time-dependent, so you do need to act with a certain degree of precision, but nothing is super difficult. If you fail, you just reload right at the last checkpoint and the game is filled with plenty of those that you never lose any progress. The only thing you might have to endure is some repeated animations/narrations that repeat at those checkpoints as well.The controls are easy to get used to, you can use either a controller or mouse + keyboard. There's no complexity in the controls.The artwork is beautiful in this game, every scene and every set has some neat things to look at, in the foreground and the background. You can feel the love poured into creating this game in the artwork alone.I took a screenshot to share here to give you an idea of what you could expect:The sound effects are pretty well put together, and the music is very fitting for the intended atmosphere.For people who want a good short story, with excellent writing and narration, but especially for those who enjoy puzzle platformers as well. As I mentioned above, there are some time-dependent elements but are not difficult, so most people should be able to play this game with ease.This game is short, my first go around took around 2.5 hours, and I was taking it easy fiddling with the game's mechanics. Another run through probably would take about an hour. There is a little bit of replay value for there are a few achievements that I missed, but they shouldn't be hard to get. I see that there are 100% guides out there already, so there.That length in mind, a base price of $17.99 USD is a bit heavy for such a short game. I definitely think the game is worthwhile, but perhaps on a reasonable sale due to its very short length.My very first half hour with this game can be found here, with some small spoilers, of course, and so watch only if you don't mind that: is a family friendly puppet-based puzzle-platformer where the idea of puppetry is not a simple artistic decision but factors into your puzzle-solving with clever use of the strings at times. It contains a heartwarming tale and fun gameplay, but is just a bit too short for the price.Definitely play this when you get a chance, but definitely get it on a reasonable sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A typical puzzle-platformer in the meanwhile well-known Limbo/Inside-tradition that probably was initially developed as a university project. Alright, I admit that’s just my guess, because I read in the intro that obviously Filmakademie BW is involved in the making, but hey, it makes sense, because to quote it with Jurgen from Sam&Max, what’s else there to do in Baden-Württemberg? :P Alright, bad jokes with unknown citations aside, all in all I can’t really bring myself to say something bad about A Juggler’s Tale. Sure, gameplay isn’t really innovative or new, lots you probably already have seen or played. Yet, no, I seriously don’t want to use the term mediocre here, because at least the string/puppet optics and the few related mechanics definitely add something new to the mix. I somehow just wish that they would have been used more frequently, and in a much more complex way. Just keeps popping to my mind that in this case it’s a kind of missed opportunity if you know what I mean, the game somehow just scratches the surface of possibilities. It’s also very short, by the way. Nevertheless, after finishing it, I’d still say it’s definitely enjoyable if you don’t expect too much, so it still ranges in a solid thumbs up region in my opinion. But as a good advice, if you understand German a bit, you might want to switch to German audio, because in this case it’s much better than the English version. The German speaker (though not perfect) at least tries to really narrate the tale, even changing his voice accordingly, but the English one sounds kind of bored, and even the English texts (obviously the original was written in German) don’t rhyme like they should. Yeah, to be honest, the English poetry sometimes even hurts one’s ears a bit, that’s how wrong some lyrics actually sound. Long story short, check it out if you dig that stuff, just be sure (like always) about what you’re getting into, and maybe wait for a sale because of the short game length.

_childDocuments_.review: As an actual marionette player, this game feels like a gift appreciating our wonderful hobby and the dying art of puppetry itself. I might want to mention first that I've not been completely free of bias since some of the game's developers have visited my theater a few years ago, in order to get an idea of how marionettes actually work. I was excited to see how they would implement this mechanic in their game and I was glad to see it not being done in an exaggerated way and the movements are all very convincing. Though, the strings are more of a stylistic device at times, and it would have been nice to see the game play with the mechanic more."A Juggler's Tale" resembles games like INSIDE and Limbo a lot. In terms of gameplay and character design, it actually felt like a shortened version of INSIDE. But that's nothing bad for me since I like that kind of gameplay and the art style and atmosphere of "A Juggler's Tale" are still very unique in itself. I'd even go as far as to say that this alone makes the game worth playing, at least if you're into artistic games.The riddles are nice, not too easy but nothing that'll make you get stuck. If you're looking for a riddle-intensive and challenging game tho, this one isn't for you. If you're looking for a game with a long runtime, it's not for you. If you want to get the most for your money concerning playtime, don't buy it (maybe, if it's on sale). This game is more about the aesthetics, the music and the narration. If this alone is enough for you, which it certainly is for me, go get it :)The aesthetics are stunning, the color schemes used are dreamy and look beautiful all throughout the game. The medieval-folk-sounding music is really nice and fits the rest, I loved the score. The narration also seperates "A Juggler's Tale" from other games as those mentioned above. A narrator (or marionette player to be more specific) guides you through the game, telling the story. While in other games I've played, narrators tend to be annoying, this one wasn't. He is part of the story. After all, I can recommend this game to those who like short and artful games. "A Juggler's Tale" is like a fairytale. It evokes some kind of nostalgia and throws you back into your childhood when you were in awe listening to fairytales or watching actual puppet shows that made you lose sense of reality for an hour or two. A feeling captured perfectly in "A Juggler's Tale".

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a story-centric platformer and puzzle game centered around a puppet girl who seeks freedom.Decent music and graphics are ok, but characters could use some polishing up, even as wooden puppet characters. Backgrounds and scenarios are definitely more pleasant to look at than the main characters.While the game plays as a sidescrolling platformer, and there are obstacles to avoid or bypass, the game is more akin a puzzle game in that it requires solving of multiple puzzles along the way. Infinite lives and frequent chapter checkpoints that can be loaded at any time once unlocked, make it for a rather relaxing gameplay.Puzzles are not too hard to figure out though there are little to nothing in the way of hints, so it does require some thinking and/or trial and error - not bad for those seeking a challenge, or might frustrate those who expect a more streamlined experience.The story is by far the best aspect of the game. It is enthralling and charming, and accompanied with well voiced and scripted narration, even if he can get a little on the nerves at later stages of the game, as his demeanor changes as the story progresses.There are some issues with clipping and stuckage that require restarting.For achievement hunters, 100% is very easy to get.Alas, the price is very steep for what it offers, given how short the game - a couple of hours - is and the lack of replayability once completed. I do recommend waiting for a sale. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: ‘A Juggler’s Tale’ is a 2.5D puzzle platformer reminiscent of Play Dead’s Limbo and Inside. You play as Abby, a marionette juggler held captive at a circus. After escaping the ringmaster, you set out on a fourth wall breaking quest for freedom that plays out like a cross between Pinocchio and The Truman Show.Presented in the form of a children's pop-up book, the story is told through poetic rhyming couplets voiced by the puppet master Jack, who appears to cheer on Abby’s new found freedom at the start of the game – although, all may not be as it seems. Abby’s adventures take her through woods, battlefields and stormy waters, with plenty of surprises along the way. Everything looks beautiful, character animations are super smooth, and your puppet strings make for some inventive physics-based puzzles. It’s an audio-visual extravaganza where you are watching, and playing, Abby’s story atthe same time.'A Juggler’s Tale' has a lot in common with the two aforementioned Play Dead games. And like those, it’s a one and done game, with a pretty short run-time – probably 2-4 hours depending on whether you want to replay chapters to get any missing achievements. Yet, A Juggler’s Talee is a cathartic experience, packing an emotional punch; it’s a tale of hope and empowerment that will stay with you long after the credits have rolled.

_childDocuments_.review: This right here is indie game gold, up there with the best such as inside, unravel, inmost or gris. The game is irresistibly charming from the getgo, with jawdropping visuals (among the best i've seen for a puzzle platformer), great narration and a gripping story. The puzzles are straightforward & fun, the achievements are easy & clever and the pacing is superb. This leads to playing through the whole thing in one sitting, reaching the end before you know it... And you know what? That's perfectly fine, because a puzzle platformer has that sweetspot in lenght, where it needs to entertain you sufficiently without overstaying it's welcome. This game does that as good as inside did, and while it isn't as thought provoking, it certainly leaves you in better spirits by the end. All in all this game is a must play for fans of the genre, and while it's lenght may not warrant a purchase at full price, it's an easy steal on sale. I enjoyed every second i spent with it, and the high ratings are 100% deserved!

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler’s Tale is a side scrolling narrative platformer in the vein of LIMBO and Little Nightmares. Although the attitude is much more fairytale than existential horror, the gameplay is very similar. You’ll be pushing boxes, flipping switches, and throwing rocks as you make your way across a picturesque countryside. If it weren’t for some tedious puzzles and vague signposting, A Juggler’s Tale would have completely won me over with it’s charm and beauty.You play as Abby who is a circus performer, juggler, and prisoner of the cruel circus master. In a harrowing escape attempt aided by your bear pal Urs, you break out of your cage and flee your life of captivity. The odd catch here, though, is that you and everyone else are actually marionette puppets, limbs dangling from the sky on strings and all. A rhyming voice narrating your every move almost as if he’s retelling a story.In truth, the narrator is the one in charge. Setting the scenes, creating the conflicts, and telling the story. You’re just another one of his puppets. The marionette angle plays into many of the puzzles you must over come. Your strings will get caught on objects that you must move in order to pass. It’s a clever diegetic mechanic that lasts for the first third of the game. The rest sees you being pursued by bounty hunters in a stealthy game of cat and mouse. All the while the narrator turns from a benevolent overseer into an angry antagonist, manipulating the world around you in order to put obstacles in your path.In all honestly many of the more complex puzzles required a bit too much trial and error for my taste. Enemy cones of vision during some stealth sequences were questionable, resulting in some slow moving puzzles needing to repeated over and over. To add insult to injury, many of these fail states were followed up by the same lines being repeated over and over by the narrator. For a game so short and simple, it sure pushed a lot my buttons. And as good as the narrator was, I only needed to hear his lines once. The final sequence of encounters was an exceptional headscratcher, one that really sucked the excitement out of the story.On the other hand, A Juggler’s Tale is a lovely game to look at and listen to; the art, narration, and story telling are all top notch. It’s unfortunate then that you are often distracted from that beauty by some questionable puzzle design and mechanics. Ultimately, I think the charm does outweigh the blemishes, but just by an inch. I was satisfied with how A Juggler’s Tale wrapped up, and believe it tells a compelling and family friendly story. But just like little Abby, don’t expect to be cut loose into this world without stumbling a little along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a delightful and enchanting experience that seamlessly blends puppetry with a compelling narrative, creating a gaming masterpiece that stands out on the Steam platform. Developed by kaleidoscube, this indie gem offers a unique and refreshing take on the puzzle-platformer genre.From the moment you enter the whimsical world of A Juggler's Tale, you're greeted with stunning visuals that resemble a beautifully crafted storybook come to life. The game's puppetry aesthetic adds a touch of magic, making every scene feel like a living, breathing piece of art. The attention to detail in the design of characters and environments is truly commendable, creating an immersive atmosphere that captivates players from start to finish.The narrative is where A Juggler's Tale truly shines. The story follows Abby, a string puppet yearning for freedom, as she embarks on a journey through a captivating world full of challenges and surprises. The tale is narrated by a puppet master, adding a unique layer to the storytelling that keeps players engaged and invested in Abby's adventure. The narrative cleverly explores themes of freedom, choice, and the desire to break free from preordained paths, creating a thought-provoking experience that lingers in your mind long after you've completed the game.Gameplay-wise, A Juggler's Tale offers a perfect balance of puzzles, platforming, and storytelling. The mechanics are intuitive, making it accessible to players of all skill levels while still providing a satisfying challenge. Abby's ability to interact with the environment using the strings attached to her limbs adds a layer of depth to the gameplay, requiring players to think creatively to overcome obstacles.The soundtrack deserves special mention for complementing the game's atmosphere beautifully. The enchanting melodies enhance the emotional impact of key moments, pulling players even deeper into the narrative.A Juggler's Tale is not just a game; it's a work of art that showcases the creativity and passion of its developers. With its endearing characters, imaginative world, and thought-provoking narrative, this indie title deserves a place in every gamer's library. If you're looking for a unique and memorable experience that goes beyond traditional gaming, A Juggler's Tale is a must-play that will leave you spellbound.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I thought that this would be one of those generic games, you know the type; game with no storyline and horrible graphics that you play for fun for an hour or so, get absolutely nothing out of but the fact that it helped you through your lunch break... And at first glance, A Juggler's Tale really does look like exactly that but, it isn't. It actually took me by surprise.You are in a tavern and the bartender, a narrator who does greatly voicing his part, starts telling the guests about a girl called Abby, using his strings to control a puppet, he'd tell a story in a little puppetshow of his. You control this Juggler girl, who's been encaged and enslaved her entire life to work in a circus, with a very evil ringmaster... Until one day she decides to escape. Sounds silly enough at first, but the metaphoric and the physical will really start making your brain work after Chapter 3... where Abby breaks her strings (the ones the bartender, real life person controls) and even so, the puppet still keeps on moving and forcing the surprised, SHOCKED bartender to continue narrating this story, as if this puppet was so driven by the will to live free that it became sentient, seeing its story through to the end.The poetic way the narrator keeps telling this story is really nice, and the platforming puzzles, although weak and really do not test your intelligence at all, is always a welcome addition! Past Chapter 2, I wasn't really playing a Platformer as much as a Story-driven atmospheric game that should've been longer in my opinion, but still had enough of a charm to really be enjoyed.  and it's NOT a generic game with no storyline... You better be prepared for the twists and turns ahead!

_childDocuments_.review: A very short and predictable but nevertheless charming story, with a unique gameplay element.Pros:* Animation is excellent at conveying unspoken subtexts.* Great music and voice acting.* Unique gameplay element, your/others' marionette strings, that affect the world and limit movement.* Forgiving, if you screw up - and you will.* Creative achievements.Cons:* Very short - 1.6 hrs on my 1st playthrough.Meh:* Plotline isn't exactly subtle - think "average children's story" level of sophistication.* Game had TONS of unfulfilled promise - hoping the dev makes a DLC to let them further explore the potential.TL;DR: If you like a fun (albeit short) experience and can get it on sale, definitely get it. _childDocuments_.review: A Juggler’s Tale is an interactive puppet performance - or at least that’s what it would originally like you to believe! It’s the tale of Abby. She juggles for a circus sometimes, but she’s multi-talented; as you join her tale, her first big act is outsmarting a giant bear for the entertainment of the crowds. There’s no prevalent danger at this stage; the bear will playfully swat her away if she comes too close, but her early trials are there to set the tone. Juggler’s Tale is a puzzle platformer with a twist. Rather than rely on twitch reflexes and precision, pixel-perfect jumping, she has to try and figure out how to use her surroundings to her advantage. Except, sometimes, her surroundings actively work against her. Abby’s unique burden is that she’s a marionette puppet, and her strings will get tangled up with anything overhead.That won’t be an issue in the early goings as she explores the circus and outsmarts her bear friend. Only, the wholesome scene soon starts to dissipate. You quickly discover that Abby’s not a willing performer, but a captive, and the conclusion of her act sees her locked inside a tiny cage by the ringmaster. Things start to change from here on out; the game is no longer about a carefree young performer, but a desperate girl longing for freedom. It’s a sudden tonal change in every aspect apart from the narration. Through the game, there’s a voice from above, narrating the game with rhyming verse. As the game goes on, it becomes clear that this isn’t just a charming feature, but the voice is instead dictating the story. He’s in control and Abby is just an actor in his plans. Except, sometimes, Abby wants no part in the tale he’s trying to tell. She’s capable of rebelling, and he’s not especially fond of that.For every direction ignored, the world around Abby becomes a little darker, and the obstacles placed in her path slightly harder to overcome. Initially, her escape sees her surge through sunlit fields and picturesque plains. There’s no immediate threat and the quaint surroundings suggest no immediate threat. Then, as the sun retreats, the fields give way into a forest. There’s not a lot of light, and the guiding fires lit along Abby’s path are endangered by the sudden bout of driving rain. For a while, this is only going to slow down her puzzle solving progress; there’s a drawbridge mechanism to bypass, or there’s foliage that needs to be burnt to clear her path. But there’s bigger dangers lurking in the first, just out of sight. Hungry things.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful. If you like Little Misfortune, also try A Juggler's Tale. It tells a good story, clever puzzles, cute characters, well-made atmosphere with a stunning narrative. I wasn't expecting the graphics but the fields/rocky mountain look amazing, the sea with color gradient is a highlight. A lot of interesting things to see like Abby juggling balls while crossing a river on the string. The puzzles are clever - easy to know what to do, but how it is executed is creative - like how Abby steals the key when she was locked in the cage, and got past the bear. Unexpected but rational. This game is not specifically made for children, keeping the torch lit in the forest is challenging, and a puzzle requires moving a body bag.Wolf riding and bear riding is fun. The Merry Bandits song is amazing, I've been listening to it the entire day, I only wish there is an OST.A brave story, great for children and entertaining for adults, I'd love to see a sequel.

I bought it because it was rated "Overwhelming Positive" and had tags matching my typical favorites.For being an "interactive story" that is so short (youtube walkthroughs of ~1 hour), it's rather expensive. Personally, the most irritating aspect is the *abominable* poetry. The narration is mostly done in "poetry" composed of couplets and "couplets" with near-rhymes. The "couplets" are infuriating because of their rhythm; some lines are extremely long, seemingly just to make the second line rhyme with the first. All of it feels extremely forced, like an elementary school student writing poetry, using certain words because they *vaguely* fit the meaning, and (also vaguely) sound similar to the "rhyming" word. _childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a side-scroller adventure game that has you playing as Abby, a string puppet who, at the introduction, is forced to serve as a circus performer. Wanting to be free, Abby escapes from her captors to the big wide world, but is ultimately pursued and hunted.Despite having a narrative focus, A Juggler's Tale doesn't have any dialogue. Abby doesn't speak. Instead, there is a narrator who details the events of each chapter, while also serving as an extra layer of charm and humour. He also only talks in rhyme, which just adds another level of style to the game.My favourite aspect, however, was the environments. As you can see from the screenshots, the visuals are magnificent. Vibrant colours mixed in with some beautiful-looking landscapes make each and every frame a treat to look at. The detailing in each level is meticulous, and it's hard to not get distracted by your surroundings.It's a short game, coming up at about two hours, but the gameplay is surprisingly varied in that time frame. On the one hand, you have puzzles which aren't overly difficult, but engaging enough to keep you occupied. Then, on the other hand, you have the intense sequences, ranging from chase scenes, to stealth situations, to life-and-death scenarios. There was never a moment that felt like it was lacking something.So overall, I was massively impressed with A Juggler's Tale, and I have no issue recommending it to just about anyone. The price tag is a bit steep, but what you're getting is a clear labour of love product that is full of charming details. If you would like to see a more detailed version of this review, be sure to check out my video for it here:

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a charming and whimsical puzzle platformer that will make you smile and cry at the same time. The game is beautifully crafted, with stunning visuals, atmospheric music, and clever level design.-----------------------------------------------------------You play as Abby, a marionette who escapes from her cruel puppeteer and embarks on a journey of freedom and discovery. The story is touching and emotional, with a narrator who guides you through Abby's adventures and challenges. The gameplay is simple but engaging, as you have to use your strings to swing, jump, pull, and interact with the environment. The game is short but sweet, lasting about 2-3 hours, but it will leave a lasting impression on you.

The puzzles are rather easy, one playthrough takes around 2 hours. What makes this game really special is the outstanding narrative voice acting. Every step Abby makes throughout the whole game is accompanied by a narrator... in rhymes. The narrator is literally talking non-stop. You can even use him as cheat sheet. If you don't know what to do next, just listen to him... he will tell it. Usually I always choose English voices because German voice acting is generally bad. Mostly everybody sounds bored, just like only waiting for the end of work day. Not with this game. The German narrator is as good as the Englisch one... if not even better. It's really enjoyable to listen to the German version too. That's also the reason why I've ended up playing two times through the whole game... once with the Englisch narrator and once with the German one. But anyway! What more to say... rather than: Buy, buy, buy! (© and ® and ™ by )★★★★★5/5

_childDocuments_.review: A simply gorgeous and delightfully fulfilling side-scrolling narrative adventure set in a medieval-style world in which you play as a young girl named Abby. Nothing so far sounds too out there or different however what makes this game stand out is the fact that the game in its entirety takes place within a travelling puppet theatre cart and of course, every character as well as the animals within the world are marionettes - Having to control Abby where the game essentially places you in the role of puppet master is both such a unique mechanic and perspective. Everything in the world acts as if they are being controlled by forces outside of their control; the movement animation of the characters feel so genuine and true to life, much like an actual puppet show which just adds to what is already an incredible art style.One of the biggest standouts of the game outside of the story and visuals has to be the inclusion of playwright and actor Shaun Lawton as the voice of the Narrator, a role that initially just appears to do exactly that, narrate and guide our adventure as we traverse through the lands however later on, takes on a more sinister and fiendish antagonistic role which was both an unexpected and fun twist to an already exceptional game.Throughout the game, there are a number of puzzles which for the most part are pretty simplistic and easy to figure out in nature. The game does a fairly good job of teaching you the the mechanics you'll need to overcome a challenge before a situation arises where you will need to use what you have learned in order to progress. The only one bit I had any kind of issue with was when I was sailing across the sea and had to lead a pursuing boat into a maelstrom in order to escape but this very much is a minor nit-pick. Stealth also plays a very big part of the game as you attempt to sneak past numerous enemies without detection and although occasionally a little tough or harsh, the mechanic is implemented very well and it's always fairly obvious as to what you need to avoid detection and how slink on through.The soundtrack of the game is short, sweet and fits the game perfectly. The main instruments used throughout are what sounds like a lute and a flute which are accompanied by drums, the occasional brass instrument, what I think might be a harp as well as a smattering of other instruments.Every single element of the game blends perfectly to make what feels like a living a breathing world - It's like being a young kid marvelling at the wonder of a very well put on puppet show and letting your imagination run wild.Overall the game is pretty short at approximately only 2 hours in length, which to some will be just fine and to others it may be disappointing; for me personally, I was perfectly happy with the length of the game - While a longer game would have been awesome, I was perfectly contempt and satisfied with the length of game I was presented with. I did receive my copy of the game for free however having played it, I would have been perfectly happy paying full price for it (£12.99 GBP) although as always I would still recommend trying to pick it up on sale if you can.In conclusion... A Juggler's tale is a short yet incredibly rewarding and satisfying narrative puzzle adventure game that I cannot recommend highly enough. Well worth playing and well worth the price.

When that happens, return to the menu or exit completely, then resume the game. At one point, a puzzle might be unsolvable .Having said that, the game is delightful. Take the time to read Abby's story as you play. For the most part it is a pleasant rhyming tale, telling us all about Abby's adventure. _childDocuments_.review: Some comparisons have been made to games like "Little Nightmares", and at first, that seemed far fetched, but it actually turned out to be kinda true: even though this game isn't nearly as horror-themed, there are several scenes which are moody and scary and also involve chase sequences.The story itself is presented as an actual story, with the narrator doing a great job setting the tone and also, sometimes, explaining what to do if the player ever gets stuck. The mechanics and riddles might not be that innovative to players who are familiar with these kinds of games, but for newcomers, there are several tricky parts. I especially struggled with some of the scenarios, but managed to solve them without needing to look anything up online. So, if I can do it, pretty much everyone can do it. There are even some nice conceptual twists thrown in, with drastic turns you might not expect. It has an undeniable meta-quality to it, and the game takes good advantage of that.The biggest pleasures of "A Juggler's Tale" come on the audio-visual level: this game looks downright gorgeous! Even though you only run from left to right and sometimes back, there is great depth in the backgrounds. All of the places are stunning, be it a field, a forest, swamps, ruins or mountains. The sound design is immersive, the character designs are simple, but cute and the score by Jordan Toms is absolutely fantastic, with a lot of different themes."A Juggler's Tale" is a game which makes the main character easily likable. We don't want anything bad happen to her and therefore do our best to get her through all the obstacles. Despite the playful colors and cute designs, this is not exactly a children's game, though: some of the places and creatures are really scary, even morbid, and some of the puzzles could be too cryptic for younger players.That said, I really enjoyed my time with this game. I recommend it to anyone who wants a fun, but also suspenseful adventure for a couple of hours and who easily gets lost within amazing enviroments and enjoys wonderful music. Congrats to all of the developers for creating this journey - I will gladly return.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful and beautiful game. From the very first minute I was charmed by the storytelling and picturesque environment. I found myself taking screenshot after screenshot while making my way through Abby's enchanting story. If you like rhyming, you will not be disappointed at the subtle clues and clever use of narration. The puzzles weren't extremely hard, but challenging enough to make you think. Though the later chapters took a darker turn, the overall story is one of hope and freedom. I absolutely adored playing through this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed playing through this and although the game was short at around 2 hours of play time, it was wonderful. _childDocuments_.review: Puppet girl Abby escapes circus captivity and sets off to free herself from what shackles her. That is the story of A Juggler's Tale, and one of its many weak points. A Juggler's Tale is very visually appealing with its landscapes and its puppet characters, but that is the only credit I really can give to it. I found myself quickly annoyed by this game due to its crashes, having to restart from checkpoints due to bugs like clipping, and some of the most irritating narration I've ever heard. _childDocuments_.review: First, let me start by stating that I can't not recommend this game, but I do think it's more worth it to get on sale or within a bundle of some kind. The game itself is very gorgeous. I love seeing the way things move and scroll by as you walk around as this little puppet character... But I personally found the narrator annoying. I would be trying to figure out a puzzle or in the middle of completing one and the narrator would almost always come in with some quip or unnecessary hint about what I had to do, which took away some of the fun of actually solving the limited puzzles in this game. Also I think I personally just hate rhyming. But overall, the game was an enjoyable short experience and the visuals are very pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a clear recommendation from me!The game really grabbed me, the story is very good and I loved the change in the storyline. I personally think that the money of 15€ is worth it, but if you do not necessarily want to spend so much money for 2 hours I can definitely recommend waiting for a sale.Absolute recommendation: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Well this was not at all what I expected. I thought it was gonna be a pleasant jaunt through a Inside-y/Limbo-y kinda game but more lighthearted and pretty. Part of that was true but hooo boy was it disproportionately frustrating. I've never had to look up solutions to puzzles more in such a short time (either because I was confused or, later on - more frequently too frustrated to screw around failing and getting set back to a checkpoint). I got it discounted for like $4 and that's probably just about the perfect price for this game. I can't imagine paying $18, I'd be mad if I did. As it stands, it's about a 6.8. There's an interesting twist as things progress and the visuals were gorgeous. The bugs and unintuitive puzzles were rough though.

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a interesting game with a peculiar story. You play as a string puppet named Abby. The strings are not just for decoration, they will hinder your ability to move past some objects or into certain areas. This will play into the puzzle solving portion of the game. The art style and atmosphere are visually appealing and relaxing. The puzzles are simple but engaging. The game will only take you around 2 to 3 hours to complete. It's a great game to sit back, relax and play after a long day. It runs great on the Steam Deck too, which is the device I played it on. Considering the game is frequently discounted down to $4 CAD, it is definitely worth picking it up at that price. I'm not sure I would recommend it at it's full price due to the short length of the game and lack of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: After 2.6 hours, I finished A Juggler's Tale, including getting all achievements. A Juggler's Tale is a 2D side scrolling platformer with a unique art style and an immersive story. The game's visual design can be likened to a puppet theater, as the narrator drones on in the background. The game mechanics can be quite glitchy at times but overall it was a smooth experience.Storytelling is a huge aspect in A Juggler's Tale. We follow Abby, a puppet determined to break free from the strings that bind her. From breaking the fourth wall (kinda) to freeing Abby from her 'strings', the game's short but impactful story lingers long after the credits roll. One aspect which I really liked was how the narrator rhymes every alternate line. It made for an enjoyable audio experience while Abby runs across gorgeous yellow fields, navigates through dark forests, or sails across the dark and stormy seas. A Juggler's Tale is a cosy indie game that reminds me of cute children books with a wonderful world.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this a thumbs up, because this is a game I feel some people would love dearly.. but as much as I hate to say it, for as great as it is, it's almost a no for me. That might make it sound like I didn't enjoy it, but I did. So let me explain.In this game, you play a little girl who is locked up at night, forced to work in the circus. Actually, you play a little PUPPET - she is a puppet on strings, as are all other living creatures. She longs to experience the freedom and joy of the world, so she escapes... and the game is her story of trying to get away and find her freedom.There is so much that is GOOD about this game. Rather than the usual greyish or greenish tint so commonly used in this type of game (to denote how dark and cruel the world is, etc) this one is filled with vibrant, warm colors, like a kind of a fall aesthetic. The graphics are pretty solid, the sounds fit right in, and the music blends well.You go through a variety of little chapters, solving some puzzles (some of them somewhat frustrating) and stuff like that. It's pretty fun.However... however. There's some drawbacks here that it would not be fair not to mention in my review.First, the game is VERY short. I logged 2.2 hours. I beat half the game on my lunch break at work. You barely get to know Abby, and then the credits are rolling. Next, there are game-breaking bugs - the kind where you have to restart a checkpoint not because you've got YOURSELF stuck, but because the game didn't do what it was obviously supposed to. One example (& I'll try to refrain from spoilers) is a scene in which I'm performing a task and trying to keep away from another character. The completion of that task requires that that character be in the scene. When I got on the scene, I saw the task I was obviously supposed to do, so I began to do it.. and just kept doing it and doing it. Nothing happened. I looked all over, trying to see if I had missed some clue, but couldn't find anything. I looked up a walkthrough online & found that that other character was a part of this scene. The character had never made his appearance - and not because of anything I did (to my knowledge). So, I had to go back to the main menu and "continue," and what do you know, now the character is in the scene, and I can complete the task. This very much breaks the immersion.Next, the price. I got it on sale. I cannot in good faith say that this game is worth $18. That means I would have paid $9 an hour, so... no. If you'd like to play this game, get it as a part of a bundle or wait for it to go on sale. If you can catch it on sale, it's a nice little experience. Just not an $18 experience.Next, there are just some plot things that don't make sense. For example, why is it called A Juggler's Tale when I only see Abby juggle like one or two times? Yes, I get it, she works in a circus, but even in her intro, it's not JUGGLING she's doing! She's doing something else! Or - and here there are spoilers, so read only at your own risk - Finally - and this is just a personal note... perhaps others might feel differently - I just couldn't make that emotional connection with this one. You know what I'm talking about - when you play one of  those epic storyline games, and when the ending comes around you're so invested in the story that you're just blown away. As this game was so short, and as the plot just sometimes kinda broke the immersion for me, I wasn't getting that 'blown away' feeling at the end. I was happy to have beaten the game, and happy to have shared a brief time with Abby, but that's it.I did enjoy the game. I did. It just objectively was not one of the better ones I've played. Wait for a sale, bro. You'll be glad you did.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overpriced for the content it delivers. And, to be honest, the content isn't that fantastic to begin with. This is another short game - 2 hours with minimal replay value - in which you walk right constantly while solving simple puzzles and performing light platforming. You’ve seen better examples and you’ll probably see many more.While the novel string mechanic appears to be intriguing, it is actually a wasted opportunity. The whole concept is that the strings prevent you from moving under objects. In such situations, you must either find a way above the obstacle or remove it entirely. The strings can also be used to push objects around, however this is only employed in a few unoriginal puzzles.Another novelty is the puppet master's rhymed narration of the story. It pretends to be more interesting than it is. It turns out that the words are forced, and the story is meaningless as a result. The narrator doesn't tell you anything about the setting or the character; he just describes the scene. And he uses the girl's name a lot. It's always Abby this or Abby that.Oh, and he has a habit of saving you when the narrative requires it. He'll merely tell you to try again if you drown in a puddle. However, miss a jump over a specific gap and he'll securely drop you on the opposite side. I hate it when a game treats you like a fool and forces this solution down your throat. It devalues the entire experience and deprives the gamer of the joy of solving a challenge.The game is buggy. In the first chapter you need to throw apples to a bear; I threw it on top of it and the bear got stuck. Other time I pushed a box close to a wall; when I jumped over the box, I got stuck in mid-air between the wall and the box. Juggler's Tale will try to entice you with its stunning artwork and string mechanic, but don't be fooled. It's just a mask to hide a generic game.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to hit "not recommended," Because it's charming and I truly did enjoy what I played. I'm well into Act 2, and it seems fun and charming, but if this wasn't part of a bundle I'd return it since it runs so bad for me.
