_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine. A little too short, and the story a bit too clichéd, although told in a nice way. The art is beautiful, best part of the game for sure. The story is ok enough, a little fairy-tale with a run-of-the-mill morale about searching for freedom in spite of the dangers, and the comfort and support of our puppet strings. Pretty average on that front. The narrator is great (especially the transformation he undergoes as the story moves forward). One thing I didn't like at all was the amount of dead bodies scattered around, which weren't really needed; bit of mixed content on that front, going darker than the average fairy-tale (from this day and age, of course; the fairy-tales of old were even darker), without any sort of justification for it (they could have been absent, they had plenty of ways to raise the stakes without going that dark). Gameplay is also fine, I've found a couple of bugs (I even fell off the map at one point), but nothing major. Performance dropped here and there, but overall, it wasn't too noticeable. All in all, I'd say, wait for a sale if you really want it, but don't expect something incredible; except for the art, it's pretty average.

_childDocuments_.review: Historic Review:  Games I played months if not years ago – I decided to start reviewing right at the end of 2023!  Memory of a trepanned, ADHD toddler with impulse control issues notwithstanding.  Teaboy's Basic(ish) Reviews....I read a lot of reviews when looking at games on Steam, and it quickly gets tiring – those who write involved, down to the micron scale reviews, although helpful, end up like looking at War & Peace when you’ve only got time for a quick 5 minute dump!  This is middle of the road and to the point – not easy for me as I tend towards sesquipedalian loquaciousness!  Vociferously Verbose?  Alright, verbal diarrhoea.  (Although I hate panning a developer’s work and all the time, effort and love they put into designing these – it is their life after all – this is my honest, personal opinion of my level of enjoyment.  Sorry devs!).  A note on time played:  My Steam clock does not seem to work properly, indeed, it even minuses time on occasion! _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for October 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before November 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Seriously stop rhyming. A Juggler’s Tale tells the story of a girl who escapes from the circus, though it’s not clear why she was locked in a cage, or what is going on other than an attempt to get a Limbo or Inside style game.  In the story, the girl is a puppet in a stage play, but also that’s part of the gameplay, as the wires get caught on things.  It’s a strange idea, but a unique one that does make for a couple of interesting puzzles. There’s one big issue, the writing in this game is bad, like horribly bad.  The narrator rhymes everything, and they’re not even good, interesting, or clever rhymes, but it’s just incessant to the point where I muted the narrator even with the subtitles.  Also, there’s not much else to stand out and the puzzles are what you expect from an “inside” or “Limbo” Game, not much more than that, sadly. Pick this up if you want an average game.  This is a title I don’t hate but I don’t like, it’s okay.  But I want so much more or something interesting.  It takes about two hours to beat, but the narrator makes it hard for me to recommend, even then, nothing makes me say not to buy it, if that makes sense.  It’s just that average.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler’s Tale is a side scrolling puzzle platformer released by German developer kaleidoscube in 2021. The game plays out as a puppet show about a juggler named Abby who is trying to escape from the circus ringmaster that she is a prisoner to and who forces her to perform. The game shares a lot in common with Limbo and Inside, though not as brutal or dark (though it has some moments.)For most of the game you are running left to right, jumping from platform to platform, solving puzzles by dragging objects around and pulling switches, throwing rocks and other items, swinging on the ends of ropes, and sometimes sneaking through areas and avoiding detection by hiding behind walls. The mechanics of the game are straightforward, and the puzzles are not too difficult. One interesting quirk of the puzzles is that as the different characters are puppets, working around or taking advantage of their strings is a regular component. I had to look up one solution and I felt like a dummy afterwards because I probably could have figured it out if I were more patient.The game is narrated over constantly by the puppetmaster who has a pleasant Gandalf-esque kind of voice, and provides the narrative context for what Abby is doing and trying to accomplish. The art style starts off as a clearly constructed, cardboard cutout puppet stage but as the game progresses becomes more vivid and real and is beautifully rendered. Abby will run through fields and forests and swamps and ruins, and I always enjoyed the moments where she’s just running and you could take it in.The plot itself is well written and moving and has an interesting twist at the climax. The narration is mostly in rhyme and some of the rhyming is a little rough or doesn’t sound right on the ear, possibly because the game was originally written in German and translated? But it’s good enough for giving you the feel of a fairy tale story.The game sells for 17.99 USD at full price, and I was able to complete it in a little over two hours. I thought the gameplay was fun and the story was compelling. I enjoyed Limbo and Inside a lot, so it was fun to play a game with similar gameplay and structure but that was a little more uplifting and less crammed with horrifying violence. If that sounds good to you, or if a light platformer with some gentle puzzles is up your alley I recommend checking it out.I’d love to hear your thoughts on the game, and if you’re interested please follow my Steam Curator page  for reviews of lesser known titles like this of all genres.

_childDocuments_.review: If it was any longer or more expensive, I wouldn't be able to recommend, but at its length and cost I enjoyed it well enough. There are plenty of games in this cosy games genre that I would recommend first but if you have a spare couple of hours to kill and it's on sale definitely pick it up.The puzzle mechanics with the strings certainly add a fun and interesting twist to this platformer and is used to great effect in a few parts. Some areas of glorious artistry mixed with sometimes bland foreground and characters was also an interesting style choice, but overall it works well.The narrator, despite being integral to the story later on, gets incredibly frustrating, particularly when you die, and some of the puzzles seemed glitchy. There were definitely some bad bugs around too , some that you could work around but others that I had to restart the game.The last chapter really won me over and helped elevate the game by making the narrator a real character in their own right, and helping to explain the seemingly baffling frustrations with the narrator mechanics early on.Overall a bit of polish with a bit more length could have seen this game really shine in this category, but as it is, it's a fun way to kill a couple of hours, but definitely only buy it on sale! 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem, an awesome cinematic marionette platformer!It's a well-made artsy piece with a beautiful color palette, cheerful background music and a pleasant old man's voice telling rhyming bedtime stories. The story of fighting for freedom also makes us think whether we are living a life with free will, or just a puppet with strings of views of others, family and social responsibilities, and if any of us brave enough live a life without any strings. _childDocuments_.review: "A Juggler's Tale" is like a quirky circus act that you stumble upon while searching for your lost popcorn. From the moment Abby, the puppet protagonist, starts her escapade, you know you're in for a wild ride—emphasis on the 'wild' and the 'ride.'Picture this: you're guiding Abby through a world that's as unpredictable as a clown with a banana peel. One moment, you're tiptoeing past sneaky guards, and the next, you're swinging from ropes like a puppet Tarzan. It's like the game's saying, "Hey, forget the rules—let's have some fun!"And speaking of fun, let's talk visuals. "A Juggler's Tale" is so visually stunning that any artist would be like, "Whoa, that's some art!" The world feels like it popped straight out of a storybook, complete with vibrant colors and characters that look like they're about to burst into a puppet rendition of "Bohemian Rhapsody."But what really steals the show is the storytelling. It's like someone mixed Shakespeare with slapstick comedy and sprinkled it with a pinch of fairy dust. Abby's quest for freedom is so relatable that even Pinocchio would nod in approval. And the way the game breaks the fourth wall? In the end, "A Juggler's Tale" isn't just a game—it's a sideshow extravaganza that'll leave you laughing, gasping, and maybe even questioning the meaning of life.Gameplay:

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a sidescroller in 3D environments à la Limbo and Inside and is made by the German company Kaleidoscube. This is a small game studio founded by a few students from the Filmakademie Württemberg in the south of Germany. The studio previously worked on animated films and contributed to other game projects. This is the team's first full game.A Juggler's Tale is a string puppet performance and the show is about a girl named Abby. She works, on a string, in the circus and puts on shows together with one of her few friends, a brown bear. The two artists are not very happy. Circus life is not a bed of roses, because they have no freedom at all. Every night when the shows are over, they are locked up in a cage. One day, Abby decide to take matters into their own hands and escape. From that moment on, it is important to stay out of the hands of the circus staff and bandits.The unique thing about A Juggler's Tale, then, is that the entire game is a puppet show, with all the characters tied to strings. The strings offer a few unique moments in the gameplay. Sometimes they save you from a painful fall or drowning and other times they get in the way, preventing you from walking any further. That makes for some nice puzzles, but it's never difficult. That is not a bad thing, unless you're a puzzle fanatic who wants tough challenges, because it keesps the flow in the game with.The strings offer mostly nice symbolism, as Abby tries to break free from the restriction of freedom. It may seem like a bit of a gimmick, but the strings actually work well mechanically.Overall 'A Jugglera's Tale' is a wonderful, (relatively) short, experience with gorgeous visuals. It's comparable with games like 'Limbo', 'Inside' or 'Far Lone Sails'. I personally love games that tell a beautiful narrative in a short time frame, I appreciate games that don't outstay their welcome so for me the fact that the game is not that long is actually a plus.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: ✅The narrator adds some whimsy to the adventure ➖Simple in every aspect, but endearing. No real glaring cons. The gameplay in A Juggler’s Tale is simple, yet endearing. It’s just a heartwarming adventure consisting of navigating a young girl named Abby throughout the world. You complete some puzzles that I thought were well made for the world. I did not find the game difficult other than a few puzzles that took longer than a few minutes to see what to do. The game world is charming. You move Abby through various scenes accompanied by the (usually) rhyming narrator as he tells a story. While the content itself is slim – I finished the game in around 2 hours, I felt that the adventure was worth it and the narration/writing was good enough to make an enjoyable experience. The game also doesn’t have any established lore. You have no idea of your characters backstory or whom the narrator is exactly. A big step up from pixel graphics, the Unreal Engine looks great here with rainfall, fire, and lighting. The animations are on-point and the art style fits perfectly within the adventurous charming world. I encountered no performance issues of any kind. The graphical options are limited, but it ran perfectly. There is only really the narrator voice acting and some occasional music. I did really enjoy the ambiance of the final act, as this is really where the music game into the spotlight. Overall, well done, but like most other parts of the game, simplistic. There are no choices to make, no side quests, and no NG+. The only reason to ever play this again is achievement hunting. A cute and short game that I can easily recommend for a quick platforming adventure. While it doesn’t do anything exceptional, what it does, it does well enough. I am glad to have experienced this game. I as of this review it is $4, which is an absolute deal. You can find my curator page here:

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a short, but rewarding experience.You play as the puppet, Abby, a young girl forced to perform as part of a circus. The game is a story about her quest for freedom - in more ways than one. Her journey is narrated by the puppeteer and his relationship with Abby is an interesting thing to experience and explore.The game is a relatively straightforward platformer, made a bit more interesting by the fact that Abby has strings attached to her. The strings themselves do interact with the physical space and because of this, factor into numerous puzzles. You may need to use them to manipulate the environment in your favor or find ways to navigate the environment despite being so bound. The puzzles aren't insanely difficult and there is a nice visual cue to help you along: things you can interact with generally being marked with red in some way (though I do think the colors and shadows in a few scenes might make it a bit difficult to see at times).The controls are fine. There was a wee bit of jank and a few interactions that I wished were a little faster/smoother, but it was fine. I won't be screaming into my pillow at night over it.Visually the game is beautiful, a great use of color and lighting. The music is nice too, though sometimes I wish there was a bit more of it, as there are sections that fall back to just using ambient sounds.Overall the game is a great way to kill a couple of hours. Though given that length, I could understand waiting for a bit of a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I only approached this game with mild expectations but ended up especially charmed by the graceful visuals and brilliant soundtrack.The introductory story animatic cartoon surprisingly gets no conclusion by the game's end, yet the narrative still feels like a satisfactorily woven tale. Each act begins and ends in a theater cutout, then makes way for impressive vistas without ever losing sight of the puppet show premise.Abby's strings are more than just a prop; they hold her back as she comes across obstacles. They work great as an original game mechanic to interact with the environment, both for herself and her eventual assailants, and without spoiling plot twists they leave plenty of room to evolve as the story progresses, along with an important change of tone in the narration.Gameplay remains simple: push or pull items, jog and jump, escape or avoid danger, keep the fire alive, throw rocks and apples, steer a boat through a storm, pet the dog and free trapped animals, activate a few mechanisms, appreciate the moment, and more.It seems a lot, but in truth remains very short with four main acts and a smaller fifth one, all achievable in a single session or two. There's hardly any repetition so the entire journey feels fresh from start to finish.Though Abby linearly travels through light 2D platforming sections and a few action segments, most are more contemplative and all are relatively straightforward, with several pauses in areas in need of fair puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOILER-FREE)THE GOOD- The conceit of playing as a puppet in a puppet show is very cool, and the game contains some really interesting ideas- The game looks gorgeous, and nails the aesthetics overall- There is an interesting plot twist around halfway throughTHE BAD- Despite the intriguing premise, the story is weak. A big reason for that is that the villains seem to lack any motive for their villainry, and overall little about why things happen in the plot seems to make any logical sense.- I'm not a fan of the rhyming narration gimmick, but if you're going to have it, at least make sure that *everything* the narrator says does in fact rhyme. In this game, some of the rhymes are simply bad, but around half of the narrator's lines don't rhyme at all.- I encountered several major bugs. One forced me to restart the scene, as it made progress impossible (thankfully, checkpoints are frequent). About three more times the game would randomly teleport me to a different place in the level.CONCLUSIONAll in all, I found this to be a short little game with plenty of charm. It could have been so much better if it explored its premise more deeply and had a better crafted story, but it was still a fun way to pass a couple of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I first saw this game demoed at AdventureX 2019 and was immediately intrigued. I'm glad I now finally got to play it myself. A Juggler's Tale is an absolutely gorgeous game. Story and narration are quite simply perfect. The gameplay style with the puppeteer's strings being both help and hindrance at times is quite novel and this makes for a totally unique experience.I don't want to spoil anything about the story (and if you're interested enough to be reading the reviews, you really ought to try it out for yourself) but despite how sweet it starts out, there's some genuinely unsettling moments in there and it got my adrenaline rushing at times. Although some of the puzzle sections do require some reflexes, there's nothing too twitchy and even people whose platforming skills aren't great shouldn't have major trouble making it through to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but overall pretty good puzzle platformer, mostly resembling games like Limbo and Inside. I like the premise of it taking place in a puppet theatre where you are a string puppet and the puppeteer is narrating your success and failures. Graphics and music is pretty great (remember, the characters are not supposed to look realistic, they are puppets.)It's not especially hard, the puzzles are pretty easy to figure out if you played any similar game before (pull this, move that, climb on things and so on) and the platforming is very basic, although with a twist. Since you are a string puppet your strings can get caught up in things, both as an extra obstacle to keep in mind as well as a way to solve puzzles. It's a novel idea that works well. You will most likely finish it in about two hours, with an hour more to get the rest of the achievements, most of them will only take a minute or so if you know what you need to do since you can jump around to checkpoints, but one of them is a bit more difficult and will take up the majority of the time. As long as you don't mind finishing the game in a sitting, you will probably enjoy this quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is a simple sidescrolling puzzlegame, telling the story of Abby, a puppet on a string on her way to freedom.The game is rather light on puzzles though and concerns itself more with telling a great fairytale, with a storyteller telling rhymes and commentating on your actions, similar to something you'd find in Portal or the Stanley Parable.Especially visually a Juggler's Tale manages to impress, displaying vast, beautiful vistas in the background, with stunning colours and lighting. The soundtrack also bears mentioning, which is surprisingly strong for such a short game.This may be the biggest drawback for some people considering the asking price - the game is only about 90 to 120 minutes long, maybe another half hour if you're interested in finding the hidden achievements.However, i found the the time i spent with the game and the story told very enjoyable, so i'd highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a small little masterpiece. The graphics and the color schemes are just beautiful. The sound and music is also really good. But one of the biggest point's which makes this game good is the narrator. His voice is absolutly made for a narrator voice and this game.I had no bugs exept one pretty far at the end but loading from the checkpoint fixed it quickly.The only thing i would change if i could would be more of the music for some parts. Because in some parts there is only the sound of the backround and i think some music would be another big plus in these parts.And for the developers all i can say is: Give me more of this or give me other awesome games and thank you for this amazing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous graphic design, fun puzzles and chase sequences, I only wish it was a fully fleshed-out game! How having strings affected the world and the puzzles was marvelous, definitely could be expanded upon and I'm hoping to see more from this indie developer team (4 people!).Great narrative as well, 100% got a reaction out of me which is all I could ask for (I played the English version)
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This story about abby seek about her freedomGood : + Nice story altough it get little dark at chapter 4+ Fun gameplay ( because your character is marionette doll ) and puzzle+ Wonderful atmosphere and music+ Superb voice actor for narrator+ You play with dog, ride wolf and bearBad : - Bug animationScore : 89

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is so beautiful, I'm writing this review having played through once but I'll go back and play again because it's so pretty. I played using a keyboard which felt a little tricky. Some of the puzzles are intuitive but some kept me guessing for a while before I figured them out. Worth buying, even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the epitome of why I love playing games from indie companies. They may not be terribly complex or lengthy, but they are passion projects and tend to be beautiful and impactful in a way mass-produced games often miss. I love games that make me think in a different way and the limitations of the strings made for surprises and a feeling of limitation I had never considered before. Yes the game is pricey for its length, but becoming a part of this wonderful community and the story you discover is worth far more than what you pay.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 - Fun story. Beautiful scenery. Great Narration and a wonderful atmosphere/audio.This game was an absolute delight. Although it was short I'd recommend it at full price. The story was enjoyable, the audio was phenomenal and the narration had me smiling cheek to cheek. It was comical & adorable. Short and sweet. A 2 hour journey for £13 seems worth it to me. I would happily pay for this again if they released a different story in the same style.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing through this game. I'm even trying to get the last achievement that I need. And I don't do that often. What I liked the best was the twist in the story and the music. The music was my favorite part of the story.The puzzles were fun and you had some choices that can change gameplay a bit. I would recommend. Just note that it is a smaller game. You can finish the game within two hours.*Spoiler*What I liked less was that I still didn't understand was why the narrator disliked Abbey so much. But maybe that is just me. Maybe I missed some big clues.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetics of this game are great. I love how the (beautiful) scenes transition from woodland to puppet show stage and back again.I suppose the game costs around the same price as peak adult cinema tickets, but it offers more entertainment, for that matter. It's just a gorgeous story you can take part in.The puzzles are fun, and the puppet strings are taken advantage of in puzzle construction. Very clever indeed.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool premise where everything in the game is attached/controlled by strings. Leads to plenty of moments where you have to think outside of the box or where the game can have a little bit of fun with the concept. There are a few frustrating moments but overall the good outweighs the bad very easily. A great spin on a somewhat classic genre <3
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, cool art style. Bright vivid colors, and a story well told.Can be finshed in one sitting.Interesting level design and great littles ideas implemented throughout the game.I really disliked the narrator, ended up muting his voice. For the most part, the story worked that way better for me. I needed him for the final act
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A Juggler's Tale is one of those hidden gems in today's game industry! The visuals are stunning, the story is cute and captivating. Don't even get me started on how well-written the Narrator is! But what truly grabs your attention is the unique gameplay mechanic of the strings. Initially I thought they were just for aesthetic purposes, but as it turned out - they're an important aspect of both the game and the story!Yesterday I livesteamed the entire game on my YouTube channel and both me and my viewers loved it. Here's a link to the VOD if anybody wants to see the game more in-depth.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only 1 hour into it so far, and it's been a very beautiful game! While some of the puzzles are obvious, it is a great gem that can serve as an introduction for younger audiences and for players who are new to linear adventure games.My only complaint is it's a rather short game for seasoned players, but it's a great game to admire for the love that's been put into it, from the graphics and music to the smooth UX and storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I really enjoyed this bite sized game. It's like a gourmet cupcake. It' may be a bit overpriced but the experience helps alleviate the sticker shock. It has so many life metaphors that allow you to interpret them however you want. The game delivers the goods.Now there were a few occasions where I had to restart from a checkpoint because I either couldn't move my character, stuck in a wall, or a glitch that kept me from progressing. Not a huge deal but lowers the score a tad. The game can be completed in about 2 easy yet calming hours or 3 if you Achievement Hunt. So yes it is a very short game but I loved everything about it. It's almost like playing a popup book, an interactive visual storybook. If you have read or seen The Gruffalo, The Grufalo's Child, or Room on the Broom, then you will get those vibes for sure. The artwork, the narration, graphics and the ease in which you can acquire achievements make the small price tag worth it. If you have played Inside, Limbo, or Little Nightmares and enjoyed those then this will be right up your alley.Despite the game being short and occasional glitches I give A Juggler's Tale a 7.75 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a little rough around the edges in parts. Expect loose platforming, and a few odd bugs here and there. But also expect a fun game that isn't super hard and isn't as cliched in its story telling as it appears in the first half of the game.I enjoyed this as a fun weekend game and particularly enjoyed the music, visuals and narration.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game with nice art and beautiful lighting.Fun and engaging story with simple but thought provoking puzzles.music is understated and accompanies the game well.However,With a very short play time and a fair amount of bugs/glitches, if you haven't got spare cash maybe wait a bit for more patches to be released.All in all if you liked the little nightmares games you'll like this.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous visuals, fantastic narrative, and a sublime soundtrack each combine to create a wonderful side-scrolling adventure which is well worth the asking price. None of the puzzles are overly difficult but the atmosphere is incredible and and it took me roughly 3 hours to complete the game plus all available achievements. If you're a fan of INSIDE, LIMBO, or Little Nightmares then you really can't go wrong. Grab it now and see for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I would actually say that this game is pretty overprized.It has only about 2-3 hours of gameplay tho i still recommend it!!All in all it just looks so damn beautiful and the music is also pretty nice. I enjoyed the whole game and I played it bc i thought this could be very interesting (and it was) and also bc i saw these guys on tt so i also know that it took them 4 years to make. And that's also why i spent the money.I think the story is also great and I would say that the game in general is pretty detailed and i really liked just walking around for a bit to enjoy the atmosphere.Tho I sometimes felt pretty lost bc i didnt know what to do next but that is also what kept me playing. To find out what you could do and just think for yourself what possibilities are given. I also like that it's not based on only one language. Thanks that you put so much effort in this game!!So in general I think it's for people who wanna play a cute and "simple" game :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Overall enjoyed the game, but it is very short and the game play is somewhat simple and each section only has a few puzzles.Graphical its beautiful to look at.Personally I  was happy with the length Vs cost and thought that it was good value despite how short it was, appreciate some others may disagree.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. The art, the graphics, the story, the narration: all amazing. I really became emotionally invested, and  to play all the way to the end to see what happened to my character.Two minor complaints:1. The game's a bit short for the price. I completed it in 2.5 hours, and I took my time.2. The cut scenes when you fail get a tiny bit aggravating.But still a lovely, enjoyable, engrossing game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, it has such a beautifull atmospear.The narrator and the story telling is something I haven't played like this before, it's made with so much love and little details that just make you smile.The art is so great, sometimes I had to stop to simply enjoy  it for a while, all these beautiful colors that fill the scenery are just beautifull.I'm happy that I've bought it and can recommend it if you like games that focus on storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really cute game with some shock moments (if you think about some stuff you see in contrast to the way the game looks like at first). I really like the concept of "It's not really what you expected" and was super surpised abot the way the story went.The price could be discussed but I think you can support the work and effort.^^
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A beautfiul art style, wonderful score/soundtrack, excellent narrator voice acting (both in the english AND the german version which are currently available), overall a very charming and endearing 2,5D sidescrolling game in the likes of Inside, Limbo, Little Nightmares etc. (though with less horror in this case ^^)To think that this game has been developed by only such a small team of relative "newcomers", I am absolutely impressed and am eagerly awating what else they will bring out in the future. You can absolutely feel the love, passion and care that has been put into "A Juggler's Tale".The game itself is might be not that long (1,5 to 3, max. 4 hours depending on your play style, trying to get achievements done, replaying sections etc.), but given the fact that this is an independent first time game and also rather fairly priced, and that "A Juggler's Tale" is a truly beautiful game, this is absolutely okay in my eyes. "A Juggler's Tale" is filled with lots of charming little details both in the foreground and background, and lots of those details and fun ideas made me smile and chuckle quite a bit. Every now and then more of the environment can be interacted with than you might think at the moment, which leads to some of these nice little surprise moments. Sometimes the solution to a puzzle might not be that obvious at first, as for instance it is not always easy to make out the coloured markings that show you what you can now grab/throw or how they should be combined, how to properly avoid an enemy in certain situations etc., but with time everybody should be able to figure it out. ;-)I wholeheartedly recommend this game to everyone!PS: Currently the Mouse/Keyboard Controls are not that great when it comes to aiming/throwing, which you'll have to do a couple of times. Also the jump controls sometimes feel a bit janky regarding the timing and length/height estimation (only really troublesome when you try to not fall into the water when jumping over it and such). The game did not recognise my PS4 controller (even though Steam did), but the developers already mentioned in the forums that they are aware and working on it, so I am sure they will fix this and a few other minor bugs that can always happen when a game just came out recently on so many different platforms.Overall the developers reply really fast on the forum and I have an overall impression that they really care about the feedback of players and users. I will definetely support them in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A Jugglers Tale is an incredibly cute little game. This is a story heavy game with light puzzling about a puppet going on an adventure. The puzzles are simple but clever with the use of the puppet strings. Visually the game is stunning, character models are quite basic with them being "puppets" but the backgrounds in each area are fantastic with everything intended to be part of a live puppet show. The whole package is very well presented and I enjoyed the hell out of streaming the game. The only negative really is that it wasnt long enough. I understand the reasoning around it just wish there was more.A very enjoyable byte size story focused fairytale, I completed it in just under 2 hours having gained about half of the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Full Video Review Can Be Seen By clicking The YouTube link Below.PROSA charming yet simple, beautiful looking & sounding puzzle platformer.A nice story which is narrated very well.Fun but simple puzzles.ConsThe game is short, I completed it in 2 hrs 2 mins & no doubt it could be done quicker.The Puzzles are very simple and having more complex & challenging ones would have benefited the game and it's longevity.Overall this is an enjoyable experience and I did have fun with my time in the game.I will recommend this game as I do believe it should be played, however due to the shortness of the game I do believe it's up to the individual to decide if they wish to pay the current asking price or wait until the game comes up in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Totally short but sweet. Works out as an expression of the idea of people's freedom. Who or what controls it? What do you do with your freedom? Is the puppeteer, hidden from you behind the play screen, a good being or bad? Or does it truly matter and you ought to cut your strings of safety and be thrown out to the wilds?
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to love about the game and there are a few shortcomings too but nothing too serious. Graphics, music, sound design, art are an easy 9/10 Every scene could be turned into a wallpaper. Gameplay makes good use of the string mechanic and it beautifully blends with the story (which by the way is laid on the player by excellent narration and a script). However, animations are rough. This also effects the puzzles. More than a few times I had difficulty placing the character where I wanted and couldn't tell what the enemy is trying to do. Sometimes things clip into each other or float/glide above each other.  One thing that particularly bugged me was the strings themselves clipping through the character pretty much at all times. Makes it look like a technical hurdle that was given up on. If you like Inside, Limbo, etc.. you will like this one too. It may not be quite as polished and quite as long but it's close.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Its like a small gourme dinner. Its small, but its very delicious. So. I am still hungry, but happy. I dont miss anything. The dinner was awesome, so I am okay with being hungry. And you can play it again to collect achievements. So you can have a second helping of the very good gourmet dish if you want.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

_childDocuments_.review:
Lead Abby the string puppet through a grim fairy tale world, while you solve riddles, evade traps, and shake off pursuers. A Juggler’s Tale is a cinematic puzzle-platformer. Play as Abby, the marionette, and make your way through a medieval fairy tale world to find freedom. Use the puppet’s strings in unique puzzles, find your way around obstacles, and evade the relentless cut-throats that are hot on your heels – while the puppet master holds the strings firmly in his hands.

FEATURES
• Make use of the puppet’s strings in unique puzzles, find your way around obstacles, cross raging rivers, sneak through bandit camps and make it past dangerous traps to find freedom.
• Explore a beautiful and grim world, inspired by the tone and mood of traditional fairy tales.
• Live through an intense story of hope and empowerment, while listening to folk-inspired music and the narrator’s ever-present charismatic voice.
• Find out what it takes to truly break free from all strings attached.
_childDocuments_.name: A Juggler's Tale

name: Rogue Legacy 2
detailed_description: Rogue Legacy is back! But now it's got a 2 on the end of it! Rogue Legacy 2 is a genealogical rogue-LITE. That means it has all the trappings of a typical rogue-like (randomized runs, changing characters, and more), but with persistent upgrades, and persistent dead heirs. In this game, your legacy defines you. Spend your parents’ inheritance and grow the family manor to give your children a better fighting chance. Each child is unique, with their own traits and abilities. Your daughter could be a Ranger. She could also be vegan. It’s a new experience every time. Rogue Legacy 2 also lets you play how you want to. Go hard and fast, and dive deeper into the depths of a randomly-generated world. Or take it slow and steady and build your character up until you’re ready for greater challenges. Every Adventure is Unique New monsters, new traps, and new layouts await you every time you enter the Kingdom. This is a world where improvisation, and not memorization is the key to success. Wildly New Classes No two classes play the same. Hide atop Ivy Canopies as the Ranger, and rain poisoned arrows down onto your foes. Take to the skies as a Dragon Lancer and fly across the skies striking foes at massive speeds. Or sing and dance through your enemies, as the joyous bard, leaving only a trail of bodies behind you. Rogue Legacy 2 supports 15 new classes, with 15 distinct styles of play. Brand New Style We’re taking a whole new artistic approach to Rogue Legacy 2. The sequel features 2.5D stylings, with 3D characters against hand-drawn backdrops. The art uses heavy shading and all animations are done using stepping techniques to keep the familiar RL look and feel. Revamped Biome Generation We went all-out with biome generation to make each area in RL2 feel completely new. Each biome adopts different “build strategies” to create completely unique yet-still-randomly-generated regions. True Metroidvania To really push the metroidvania flair, RL2 introduces heirlooms: special items that permanently give your heroes new abilities that fully reveal the world’s secrets. These are not basic lock-in-key abilities, but powers that fundamentally change how you play. And heirlooms are not simply handed to you. You must prove your worth, provided you can find them. Traits 2.0 Though fun the first time, the traits in RL1 often wore their welcome later in the game. We’ve now added gold modifiers to entice players to take on new challenges. The more debilitating the trait is (in-game), the bigger the reward. This makes choosing your heirs a meaningful decision every time. Relics and Resolve One of the most exciting new features to Rogue Legacy 2 is the ability to pick up Relics, which are unique items that change how your run is played. Gain stat modifiers, complete special challenges, and even gain brand new abilities as you traverse the kingdom. But be careful, the more Relics you obtain the more your resolve is shaken, and all Relics are lost if your hero perishes. Improved Accessibility We’ve taken accessibility to the next level with the introduction of House Rules. Toggle contact damage, tweak global damage and health, and even give yourself flight for difficult platform sections. You have complete control over how you want to play the game. We’ve also introduced new mechanics such as Off-shore Banking to give struggling players more ways to succeed. A Rich Narrative Not only is the lore to the world of Rogue Legacy greatly expanded in the sequel, but it runs deep. New lore awaits you all the multiple NG’s in. Beating the game once is only the beginning. Learn about the inevitable collapse of a once thriving kingdom, and discover the dark secrets of the ones responsible. And connect and build relationships with the characters you meet along the way. New Game+ for Days Your journey has only begun after beating the final boss in RL2. There is a ton more to explore and discover on multiple playthroughs. You must choose how the game gets harder, from unique biome hazards, to special boss fights. The experience keeps changing for near infinite replayability. More of Everything Of course we’re also adding more of everything people loved from the original Rogue Legacy. More traits, more spells, more classes, more biomes, more enemies, more equipment, more rooms, more story. More secrets ... Just more everything. Clownanthropy. Holy smokes! Punching clowns! AND THERE'S A WHOLE LOT MORE. This only scratches the surface of what Rogue Legacy 2 has to offer. Scar Challenges, Fairy Rooms, the Curio Shoppe, the list goes on, but reading is for nerds. Go out and discover the world of Rogue Legacy 2 for yourself!

short_description: Rogue Legacy 2 is what you'd get if you mashed Rogue Legacy and a sequel together. Every time you die, your children will succeed you, and each child is unique. Your daughter might be a Colourblind Archer, and your son could be a Pacifistic Chef. Either way, one of them is getting conscripted.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that is very heavily about grinding, it's unfortunately a very "guided" grind, in that it won't allow you to grind certain things more than they want you to.(such as items and runes).  That's a huge drawback because it forces you to play more at their pace than your own.Speaking of the grind....it's honestly insane.    You spend hours for the most tiny incremental upgrades.   A lot of the classes are significantly less combat-worthy as well and need major adjustments to make them even decently viable, such as the pirate and the archer upgrade.  As the game is pretty recently released this review is subject to change pending any updates they make.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very promising sequel, very close from the original, with some great additionsOnly the first biome is available for now, and most of the skills/classes are locked until further updated, so after some hours there's not much left to do, but there's no doubt it's going to be a amazing game upon release(in the meantime, i'm going back to Hades)
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: I maxed out the game and was waiting around for the next patch to come out and wow I'm so impressed. Quality of life changes, massive changes to the castle, better classes, new classes, class changes. The entire game feels more fluid and is getting to the point of where it doesn't seem like an early access game. I love Rogue-like games and this has filled an empty space in my relaxing gaming. Obviously you can get rough runs with nasty traits and your abilities just suck, but very rarely does the game feel unfair when you die. There's progression when you die so it doesn't feel like a completely wasted run. The animations are fun and cartoony in a way that they can get away with so much more. I enjoyed the game pre-patch and I'm excited about sinking even more hours into it.P.S. It's still good
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be shorter and more nit-picky than my other reviews, but I was a very big fan of Rogue Legacy (1) and jumped on this game day one, despite it being an early access title. This game has changed so much about the first game, especially the controls and movement, that there is no way for me to play comfortably, since I can't break my muscle memory from the first game, and control options are limited. I've tried KB+M as well as controllers, and it's just too different for me. I even stopped playing it for months, just to try to go into it fresh without having played the first game in awhile, while also allowing the devs more time to update the game... and it's still just not what I am looking for.The introduction of a dramatic slowdown for EVERY. SINGLE. TIME you are damaged completely breaks the flow and pacing of this game for me, and not having an option to turn it off is very disappointing and kind of annoying, really. If you've never played Rogue Legacy before, but were curious, you might want to wait awhile for the devs to finish this one up and give it a shot instead of RL1, but otherwise just go with RL1. The graphics are very nice and I like a lot of the new additions, but others not so much. Simplicity in design was RL1s best friend. RL2 feels much more... cluttered and chaotic by comparison? More is nice but isn't always better. I will be requesting a refund, but maybe down the road when the game is finished there will be more/better options and customization and I will just buy it again. Only time will tell.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first Rogue Legacy, so I can't help but compare the two.The music in this one feels ok, but less memorable.The game features a new class system where classes are meant to feel completely different between one another - and they do. Each class has an unique weapon, combat style and ability. I have a mixed opinion about this choice.On one hand the game feels less tedious as you play new runs of the castle; on the other, however, that feeling of "getting better" is slightly lacking as you're constantly switching between playstyles.That being said, everything else is a straight improvement over the first game, which was already very good on its own. The combat has been expanded with new moves and random relics with unique bonuses have been added to spice up each run (like TBoI).I felt the game generally more difficult than the first one, but fairer, especially as the new game + handicaps stack up.Overall I think anybody who liked Rogue Legacy will enjoy playing this one as well. I am happy they just expanded over the first one without trying something fancy that might have strayed too far from it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: For better and worse, it's the exact same as the original Rogue Legacy in most aspects instead of an evolution of it. Grinding gold to fill out a passive tree so I can progress a bit further and get the essentially mandatory skills, such as Dash (which you don't start with). The Heir system is still just dice roll for choosing the least bad, with many traits being more for laughs than anything else playable. There's no actual passing down of play preferences, like playing a barbarian a certain amount doesn't weight your heirs to have more attack and less mana at all, for instance; it's solely down to the class.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is even better than the first and the House Rules help guide the pace of the runs to better fit to how you want to play a run. _childDocuments_.review: Edit at hour 30, because I wrote this at hour 4: It's still awesome.I did not like Rogue Legacy 1. I love a good roguelite, but that one didn't do it for me. The 'traits,' like being tiny, farting, etc, were primarily annoying. I just couldn't get into to it even though I love a good meta-progression system.Rogue Legacy 2 is truly excellent. It's a challenging skill-based platformer, but it also leans heavily into a well thought-out and meaningful meta-progression system. Even your worst runs will move the dial by a little bit. RL1 had that too, but this one just works a whole lot better, in my opinon.The noisome 'traits' have been worked into something that I actually like- you get three choices of character at the beginning of every run, so if you HATE traits, you can generally get away with avoiding them- however, they're a bit more interesting this time, and you get a gold bonus for using a disadvantageous trait, which scales with how difficult the trait will make your life. I dig it.The level design is wonderful- I have yet to feel that "Oh, this room again" that plagues so many procedural-generated games. I've seen a few more than once, but it's more of a 'hey there, I know this guy' type of thing. Furthermore, while progression through the biomes is fairly slow-going at first, the later levels look TOTALLY different- I don't mean new paint job- like they look as though they're from a different game. Completely different design.The meta-progression system is fantastic- I'll try to keep it short here- there are many, many different types of gear, runes, metroidvania-upgrades, classes, secrets, etc that you can keep persistently once acquired, and will serve to make your life easier, as well as to fundamentally change your play style in some cases. What I think is so impressive though, is that as beefy as the meta-prog system is, this remains a skill based game. It's easy to basically artificially extend the life of a game by walling you off until you have enough health and stats to make it through a certain area, as many RPGs do by design, but this remains a game where a high-platform skill will carry you, even with a low level character. I think it's damned impressive what they have done. I genuinely believe that this is a game where a casual player and a hardcore Celeste/ Super Meat Boy maniac could both have a great experience.There is fairly low RNG to a given run. There are relics, which are buffs that can be significant and change your play style, but it's not Hades-esque in the vein of compounding off-the-wall builds. That's neither good nor bad, it's just the style. Because the fundamental gameplay is so good, I think it is the right choice. You're not going to get a build so powerful that you can clear half the game on a lucky run- you would have to be that good. But you will get some advantages.It plays more like an RPG in its progression- you get stronger over time (and better at playing, hopefully). There is only one class that I hate, so that's not too much of a worry (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chef- I'm sure someone's good with it).All this to say- I wasn't planning on buying this, because RL1 had sounded so much like a game that I would really like, but ultimately was not. I'm glad I changed my mind- this is a great game right now, and I'm excited to see what comes with the final content updates. It's a little steep at first (hard), but a few hours in, you'll be happy you stuck it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though i recommend this game in a binary yes/no system of steam reviews,my real opinion is more like maybe.In this game you play as a hero (a rebel?), slowly conquering the everchanging castle,which consists of many different rooms and wings. Each wing have its own main theme,enemies,challenges and a unique boss. Defeating enemies yields gold and other resources. After you kill the last wing boss you are allowed to fight the ultimate boss, and then its new game+N all over again,but with higher difficulty.The main feature of this game is that after you die, you can choose one of 3-4 randomly generated "heirs" of yours to continue your playthrough (your legacy) with a different castle composition. All the gold and resources you've accumulated from the previous hero is spent on meta-progression: you have a big tree of permanent upgrades,equipment and other things to unlock.So far so good,but whats the catch? Its the difficulty, which is quite punishing, unless you are a veteran in roguelike genre and pretty damn fast with your fingers. Because if you are not,you are going to die, in a pretty humiliating manner, A LOT. And when i say A LOT - it means hundreds,possibly thousands of silly deaths (that ofc technically COULD be avoided if you were a better player,duuuuh). If that doesnt discourage you - then this game can be quite enjoyable.PROS+strong gameplay loop, each run is unique+a lot of available custimization options to make your playstyle even more personal+huge amount of content+high replayability,still a lot of stuff to do in NG++CONS-difficulty-difficulty-difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this game a thumbs up, and a SUPER thumbs up if you liked the first one and want more of it. Its fun, funny, and just a great time overall. I just finished the game (what is released) on my first playthrough at about 40 hours, so even if you do not intend to do any new game + runs, the game is also pretty long, assuming you aren't bumrushing the bosses and trying to finish it as quickly as possible. If you do intend to do new game + runs, its really easy to do, considering that the finale isn't released yet and, to my understanding, you can also revert your decision to up the difficulty on new game + if you decide its too hard, you don't like it, or you just want to do the vanilla difficulty of the rest of the content when it releases. This game gives you plenty of options, which is awesome!For people who have played the previous one, this is a direct upgrade in every sense. It still looks great, all the classes feel way more unique and fun, most of the changes overall feel like quality of life improvements (my favorite of which being that gold gain increases are tied mostly to the traits of your successor, so you are rewarded for picking the more tricky traits to play with, as opposed to just loading up on bounty runes and running miners endlessly).For people who have never played the first one, this is a roguelike game where you take a character into a randomized castle and accomplish all you can before running out of HP. Your character selections are randomized based on your unlocks, and every time your character dies, you are given 3 successors to choose from, and it is up to you to make the most out of the character you pick. However, when your character dies, all the gold you earned through your run with them is essentially banked for you to use on permanent  upgrades for all future successors, which means that nearly every run, even if not a complete success, will normally help make your next runs a little easier so you can get further. Its done in such a way that, while you may die frequently depending on skill level with this type of game, it rarely feels irritating, because you are always making progress. I personally think the system is perfect.Now above, i mentioned your characters are randomized. What that means is, there are classes (these you unlock with gold), spells, and personality traits that each character can randomly have, and the game mashes them together in the form of 3 heir choices every time you die. The classes all feel very mechanically different but equally as efficient, which means every player will certainly have a favorite. There are a number of spells (I'm still seeing new ones from time to time so i'm not going to give a solid number, but there are more than 10, which seems like a low number, but in this game it is more than enough) and each of these also feels unique. Some of them are purely offense, and some serve much better as utility. Once you know what they all do, it helps greatly when choosing which heir will work best for your next run.There are also a TON of personality traits, that can range from really affecting your heir in some way (an example being your heirs having gigantism, which means that heir will be very large, and their weapon is much bigger, often making combat easier, but navigating tight spaces is much harder.) to completely trivial and funny, such as having IBS and farting every time you jump. The trait system as yet another great addition to help every run feel unique, and challenge the player to adapt a class they may know very well to a slightly different style that mixes better with the trait that character has. These things together make nearly every run feel different and fresh.There are also equipment sets and runes that can be found within the castle that you can buy once you have died and returned to town as your next heir (these are 1 time purchases that all characters in the future can use) that you can also use to help customize your character stats for what you think will help you most, which adds yet another reason to enjoy exploring the ever-changing castle time and time again. The only, ONLY gripe I have with this game, is that there is a challenge mode type of thing in this game ( similar to the first game optional boss fights with pre-built heros, that's difficulty was far above normal gameplay) that you unlock fairly early. These challenges can be very difficult, and they use pre-determined stats, so there is no leveling up to make them easier. Like the first game, it is completely optional. However, in this game, doing them each multiple times with multiple different classes will give currency to unlock other, separate upgrades that feel significantly more important to your progress through the castle. (Like one of the upgrades from the challenge mode allows you to find higher level equipment and runes. I do not believe you can find them without getting these upgrades.) Some of these challenge fights are quite difficult, and while i personally will power through them nomatter what it takes, I can see this being an aspect of the game that might annoy other players, as these fights need to be done over and over with different classes and, with how hard some of them can be, depending on the players skill, I can see it not being enjoyable to some players to have to do each of these challenges 5 or more times. However, as it is optional, I am not listing this as a point against the game, just mentioning it because I feel some people would like to know about this for, whatever reason they may have. Edit on above: You can farm this currency in new game plus runs (infinitely, to my understanding) so these challenges may be completely skippable without missing out on anything after all. You may run into a situation of not having been gaining higher level items as quickly as you could have been during your first playthrough had you been focusing these challenges as early as possible, but compared to having to play content you may not care for just to unlock everything, this solution is greatly welcomed and appreciated.Overall, this game is nothing short of great if you are into roguelikes that are difficult, but always give you that sense of progression. It has clearly been made with a lot of love from the developers, who understood what made the first one so special, and they did a great job on giving a sequel that has a ton of improvements, while still maintaining the aspects that made the first one such an enjoyable experience.TL:DR- THE GAME IS GOOD, GET IT!Edit 2: Changed first paragraph to state how long it took me to actually complete the first run, as well as adding a few new bits of information I learned upon completing the game about the currency mentioned in my biggest critique of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually like roguelikes - and i still don't - but i wanted to give a try to the father of all roguelikes' heir. As a major fan of metroidvania titles i still think RL are a cheap way to add depth and longevity to a game, however i can see their appeal. RL2 is quite funny so far: cool stylized graphics with both grim and humor fantasy; the classes are all very cool to play and diverse; a sense of progression can be felt with all the castle's improvement and equipment reinforcement. As being said i'm not very fond of dying to restart over with random generated levels, but in some way this title doesn't push too hard in that sense: there's ways to speed up the running back thanks to specific unlocks and NPCs.Boss combats are fun; the heritage system is also very cool and forces you to try different playstyles.I recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Grind, grind, grind. L1 boss can tank 50 crits in a row and only lose half their health after 20k+ worth of upgrades. 20-30 minute runs where you can purchase 2 meaningful upgrades and find 1 piece of equipment. Git good, it's meant to be slow, you just need to figure out the timing for the bosses 10 moves every 15 minute run with completely different classes and gear. Cool if it's your jam, but damn is it boring and unexciting for me.Edit: Using house rules to maximize "cheating" and decrease enemy health/damage by 50% each, it was pretty easy to get to a run beating the first 3 bosses in 1 round and reaching over 20k in gold, more than 5-7 decent runs before and spanning 30-40 minutes. It let me get 2-3 of the more expensive upgrades and unlocked blueprints for close to twice the equipment/runes I previously had. It was underwhelming as anything. I could have gotten 3-5x the amount and it maybe would have felt worthwhile. Classes, skills/spells, relics are still highly unbalanced. Hades is a completely different Rogue-lite, but most runs felt meaningful from beginning to end. Combat was fresh and had dozens of different, equally viable builds, and allowing for an almost completely blank slate to start each run. Options to turn difficulty up or down were so much more organic. Dying 40-50 times to get to the first "real" ending was mildly frustrating at times, but the story, fun nature of each run, fast combat, and meaningful upgrades made runs feel meaningful. None of that is true for me in RL2. Once you realize that it's just grind after grind, you had best love the core loop, because apparently you'll be doing it for dozens of runs, and then a dozen or so NG+, before you've come close to unlocking most of the "end game" content.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Legacy 2 improves on pretty much everything the first game did. It still retains the same core gameplay but with more depth. The new mechanics that are introduced are done so at a pace that it never felt overwhelming, and after a little while they become second nature. Controls were good on both controller and keyboard, so don't worry if you only are a keyboard user.There's also more of a story this time around given through diaries and memories (more or less unrelated to the first game though). It's nothing super deep, but it's enough to make you want to find out more of what exactly happened. They're spread out across the six regions of the game, and each region has different enemies, hazards, and general layout for you to learn and contend with. The lore is how the game encourages you to do repeat playthroughs and they recently added an option to allow you to skip doing over 7 repeat playthroughs in favor of one in order to get the true ending, props to the devs. Most of the enemies follow the same general pattern as Rogue Legacy 1, which each variant being tougher versions of their lower selves, sometimes firing more projectiles or adding new attacks. Bosses however are unique and are not just big versions of normal mobs, a welcome change from RL1.Most classes return and some have been tweaked for better usability; each class is now far more distinct with each one having their own dedicated weapon and class talent, whereas in the first game classes all used the same sword you had equipped. Do you like slow, powerful attacks that reward you for good positioning, but you can also clear a room by doing "nothing personal, kid" slashes to each enemy? The Ronin is for you. Perhaps ranged combat is more up your alley, with a bit of explosives for fun. The Gunslinger is your go-to. Most of all though, the traits that were so core to Rogue Legacy 1 have been changed significantly; rarely are there traits that just are purely awful to take (no more vertigo aka flip your screen upside down which was basically a throwaway run), now most negative traits give you a healthy gold gain bonus for you deciding to pick the heir that has them as compensation for you taking up the challenge.I think the nicest thing of all though is just how many PLAYER COMFORTS there are in this game. There's upgrades you can purchase at your castle that let you reroll your heirs multiple times in case you get none you like, and an upgrade you can get from these two cute spirits that let you lock one of your heirs as always being a certain class with a certain spell, in case you're really good at them or enjoy that combination. Furthermore, there's an option called "House Rules" which lets you change things like having enemy contact damage, reducing how much health or damage enemies have, or even increasing it. AND THEY DON'T DISABLE ACHIEVEMENTS. This is an unbelievably good thing to have and I wish more games would do it, so the devs deserve praise for doing so. It lets you tweak the experience to be how YOU enjoy it, without penalizing you for doing so. Even New Game+ is in the player's hands; you can choose what modifiers you want to have on your next run (there is a minimum you must select but still). If you don't want the enemies to be super tanks on your next run, just crank up the world size. Or maybe you'd rather deal with environmental hazards having more damage than just the enemies. This makes the game SO much more enjoyable when you can have things the way you want them.I wholeheartedly recommend this game if you enjoy side scrolling platformer games with some RNG thrown in (and a healthy amount of options to customize things how you like) or if you enjoyed the first game, since this game is all that and so much more refined. I definitely found myself having nights where I went "just one more run..." and then ended up doing like five more because I got so close to beating the bosses. There's a lot to do in this game, between the main game, challenges, lore, trying out all the classes, armor, relics (items you can start with or find in the game world that offer unique buffs, but reduce your max HP if you pick up too many) and finding combinations you like...You'll get your money's worth out of this game. It might be a bit frustrating to have short runs early on and feel weak, but once you get into the flow of things, it's a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good game! It feels like mix of Hollow Knight (the gameplay, fighting style, tough enemies, unforgiving mistakes, some elements of metroidvania) and a rogulite platformer (after you die, you keep the gold you can use for upgrades, there are permanent upgrades you can obtain).It is quite hard, especially at the beginning, but fair. Sometimes you need to choose if you're up to the challenge in a specific room, either it's testing your platforming or fighting skills. High risk - high reward.There are several classes to choose from, each of them having different fighting styles and abilities. You get to choose 3 characters at the start with randomly generated spells and traits. Traits can make the game easier or harder. Some traits grant more gold gain, but make game REALLY hard. Runs can be quite quick if you die early, but it's one of the "one more run" games.Worth trying!
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Legacy 2 is a decent sequel for an already good game. What story? You are a greedy adventurer, who keep stealing things and killing stuff in unknown castle.For centuries. Your son, your grandson, your grandgrandson all have that one common goal. ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)The game progressed a lot, if you compare it to the first title. Much more complex mechanics added and the game is a bit more fast paced now.In the current Early Access version there's only 4 classes available:- His main trait is high HP and Block ability, which for 50 Mana can reduce incoming damage by (around) 85%. After hit you'l gain invulnerability for 2~ seconds.- High DPS ground attacks and multi-hit aerial cleave. Barbarian hit like a truck, but his ranged & defense option are rather limited, which balance it out. His unique skill is "Shout", which stuns all enemy onscreen and -the most important part- cancel their attacks, even if it's spells.I did complete the game with Barb, though my favorite class is Ranger. - Your go-home-club Robin Hood, which has quite high damage and mobility, but absolutely lacks HP. Ranger skill creates a platform right under you, which allows you to complete some challenges or reach secret zones.  - this class got quite a unique basic attack, which separates into two parts: direct hit with a staff with low damage and AoE blast (0 mana cost) at a fixed range. Both attacks perform simultaneously and also provides 15 MP per hit. (you only get 5 MP per hit from other classes)TL;DR All the classes in the game are quite fun, you can't tell if that one is OP or not, seems like a fair balance to me. Personally, i can't recommend any class, but again - my most successful run was with Barbarian. Equipment and spells.Spells and abilities are generated on a new character and you can't change them. There's also currently no alternative for unique class abilities (each class got only one so far).As soon as possible get some weapon upgrades and maybe unlock a Vampire rune, it will help greatly. All upgrades that you purchase in the Castle screen or from Merchants are permanent, so, don't be afraid to use some of those hard earned gold coins.In order to unlock Runes, you need to complete a challenge and get a Fairy Chest. A fantastic sequel with a lot of improvements, which currently kinda lacks content and can be completed in under 4-7 hours average.I suggest that you purchase the game if you want to support the developers and the game, otherwise wait for more updates/content releases.- This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.

_childDocuments_.review: **My previous review was made a year or two ago while the game was still in early access. After all this time, I finally took the time to beat the game through once. No product could ever be perfect, though Cellar Door Games did their absolute best perfecting nearly everything in RL2. The bosses are unique, fun, and can be a good challenge depending on your class. The platforming feels quite nice, and the abilities you obtain feel quite nice in the environment. The game can become quite a grind in NG+, however there is no need to significantly grind before NG+. Clearing as much of the map as you can in each run will allow you to beat the game with a good bit of playtime while not feeling too repetitive. The style throughout the whole game appears consistent and looks incredible, and the soundtrack is even better than the first game's by miles.I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys roguelikes and rogelites.Everything below this point was written while the game was in early access, and may not be relevant to the latest update.Where do I even start? Compared to the first game, there is so much more content packed in, despite the first game having plenty of content already. While some enemies do end up returning from the previous entry, most of the cast is never before see enemies that pose a much greater difficulty than those found within the first game. Being honest here, the bosses are so difficult in this game that I have been unable to defeat one yet, however I have gotten close on a number of occasions. Despite the difficulty level, the game is still extremely fun to play through, and is frequently being updated by Cellar Door Games (as it is still in early access). There are many different classes that can be unlocked through the skill tree system, which is fueled by the gold you obtain in each run done. Each class is so unique from one another that every play style is represented. There are many other systems that I'd love to go through, however I feel that it would spoil part of the experience if I said too much.Despite mentioning in the positives, the only negative I currently see with the game is the boss difficulty, along with an imbalance in the class system. Don't get me wrong, the bosses are amazing and interesting, but it can be quite difficult if you want to try and face one semi-early game (when you have developed your skill tree a bit and are able to glide through the zones with ease). I find it confusing that I am able to explore nearly every part of the map easily, yet when I approach the first boss, I end up being steamrolled. However, it does provide for motivation to continue playing, so I do understand why this is implemented, and respect it.The class system is where my major issue with the game comes in. Some classes are spectacular, easy to grasp for all types of players, and are very balanced. However, I have noticed that some of the newer classes (while their concepts are honestly amazing) turn out to either be a hot bag of garbage or an overpowered mutant beast. I do understand that the game is still in development, though, and I am sure that this gameplay will not remain in the game permanently. Even if it did, though, it just leaves the challenge of learning how to utilize one of the bad classes in such a way that you are able to glide through the game, thus adding more replayability.Rogue Legacy 2 is amazing in its current state, and I am expecting for it to only get better as it approaches its official release. The slight flaws within the game are understandable, as it is an early access game, and the graphics and gameplay are absolutely stunning for a game that isn't officially released. It even have me questioning whether or not this game was unfinished. You can feel the love poured in by the devs with each different map you go through. I can't say much more, but I can say that this game is worth buying, and you should do that right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I wasn't too sure about this, I liked the first Rogue Legacy, but was very doubtful a sequel would change anything significant.Many positive points to note about this game:+ Very nice QoL stuff you usually don't expect from roguelites: relics tell you exactly what they do after you discover them (pick them up once), glossary tells you exactly what all the game terms mean clearly (game keywords are highlighted like you expect from deckbuilding games, making it easier to know what to look for in the glossary), easy access to the descriptions of your gear/relics/stats/etc.+ Jumping / platforming sections were upped nicely, they were already pretty challenging, and still are, but now they feel more varied.+ Relic system is very nice (relic power varies, but it is reflected in their usage cost, AKA resolve). This makes taking a weaker relic a potential valid choice (especially if you're close to your resolve limit) where in any other game you wouldn't even consider it.+ Traits come with gold modifiers (worse traits give more gold).+ Some traits seem to be locked to certain classes (usually traits that synergize with or challenges said class, e.g. the glass cannon trait only seems to show up on the Knight, which can block damage).+ This is a massive point for me, instead of making the game easier, they added "House Rules", which let you make the game easier for yourself if you're having trouble. E.g. you can disable damage on enemy contact, reduce enemy health, etc. This is a great idea that isn't really done anywhere else.- Many of the same enemies (especially in zone 1) as Rogue Legacy 1, could've been nice to get some more new enemies right off the bat for returning players.- Castle (permanent) progression feels a little bit more linear, many upgrades are locked to a certain level, so it almost feels like there is an order you need to unlock everything in.

_childDocuments_.review: We are now pretty well into the development cycle, so, steam friends, hear me out:The game is worth playing if you are into Roguelites. It far surpasses what the first game ever did, but understands its own limits and is a labor of love rather than any kind of technical masterpiece. This game will never be Hades. But, it is really good, and the game is reaching its fullest potential. The gameplay loop is well tuned and feels good, difficultly is the most balanced I've ever really seen from a roguelite (and they're still adjusting), the area variation and the actual level design is top notch, and the art style is fun and has creative uses that shine within the game. In short, this game is sick. Get it, it's worth it if you love this genre.
