_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with Rogue Legacy 2 - at least for the first 10-15 hours.You get to unlock a bunch of upgrades and new classes to play around with every time you die, but with each boss you beat and each new biome you unlock it feels more and more like the game is statchecking you instead of the player relying on skill.Enemies will quickly become tankier and tankier while chunking you for more and more health.At that point you're supposed to increase your own stats through the upgrade system to go along with the stronger enemies.But while you were able to buy a dozen upgrades per run early on, most of the time you will only be able to save enough money for a single upgrade later on, slowing your progress down to a halt.However, the gameplay overall is really good though.The player gets to unlock more and more mobility options throughout the game, like double and triple jumps, dashes and spin jumps, which help traverse the levels and avoid enemy attacks and hazards.The different classes also offer some decent run variety early on, from simple sword & board knights to gunslingers and mages.The issue however is, that for a roguelike, runs tend to feel *very* samey.There's a lot of reasons for that - one of the worst being the resolve mechanic.Rogue Legacy 2 has a mechanic called "resolve" - a pool of points you start every run with.Now, whenever you pick up a relic on your run, it will cost a certain amount of resolve, ranging form 20-ish to 50ish points, depending on the item.If your resolve ever drops below 100, you will lose a bunch of your MAX Health cap, depending on how many point you went below 100.Even though i spent a lot of my ressources increasing the amount of resolve i start with, i only reached around 200ish points.However, there also another type of upgrades, which is equipment.Equipment however also increases you "weight", which inversely also lowers your maximum resolve.This means that on any given run, i will probably only get to pick up 3-4 items, because otherwise i'll go below the resolve limit and get an HP penalty for it.The natural consequence of that is, that you'll keep going for the same few "strong" relic, because why waste your precious resolve on mediocre items, especially since you can't drop them once you pick them up.Usually in a roguelike finding a new item is exciting! But in Rogue Legacy 2, more often than not you'll just ignore it, becuase it's not worth taking up your precious resolve.Instead of building up more and more items over the course of the run, you only pick and choose the best.Even worse is that the pool of relics is already rather small, so you more often than not will rotate between the same few relics again and again, making for a rather monotone roguelike.Add the repetetiveness of runs feeling samey to the speed at which you can grind upgrades to progress the game and the game will quickly start feeling like a chore to play.The grind wouldn't be such an issue if the gameplay loop was still fun, but with the lack of any real variation between runs, it became such a slog to play the game, that i used the ingame "house rules" options, to change enemy damage and HP to 50%, so i could progress, without spending hours upon hours increasing my damage and armor by one point per run.It's such a shame, because i can see a very, very good game underneath all that.It's just completely held back by the totally backwards resolve system and the amount of grind the game expects you to do.As a huge fan of roguelikes, i was hoping to spend a lot more time on this game, like i did on Enter the Gungeon or Hades, but there's just too much of a lack of variety here.Maybe it'll get better with upgrades, but for now i sadly wouldn't recommend it, even though it's a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Legacy 2 is an amazing example of a well done 2nd entry of a series that follows the "never change a running system formula". The general game and mechanics is not that much different from the 1st game, still your castle to upgrade, your armor to buy, runes to equip.The gameplay itself improved the most. RL1 had one weapon for each character, they just had different traits. RL2 has way more character types and each one plays very different, they feel balanced and it is easy to get into each of them.Boss fights are still the highlight of the game, great design + nice difficulty. Overall a rogue-lite that deserves a spot in my personal top 5. If you enjoyed the first one, you will enjoy this one - if you are a rogue lite fan, you should definitely give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: What a game this is.  I will admit, I hesitated on picking this up as I strongly disliked the first game as it felt clunky and didn't do it for me.  However, soon after purchasing this, I realized that this game was incredible.  The controls and movement are super smooth and tight allowing for great platforming skills amidst the combat.  Multiple different areas that vary in difficulty and randomly generated keep each run unique and exciting.  The metroidvania aspect works extremely well as the upgrades allow more and more fun- especially when you first get an extra jump and the ability to dash in air.  I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game and uncovering all the secrets and achievements.  The only complaint I can see this getting is that it can be "grindy" for the average player.   While it may feel like that initially, you will begin to appreciate it as finding a new set of gear and then buying it to make the next run more powerful is where I had the most excitement.  There's no fun in just having everything unlocked at once and nothing to play for.  Regardless, once you get to a new game run or 2 you will amass millions of gold to buy tons of upgrades at once.  This is just straight up an addicting and fun game that deserves a 10/10 in my book.  I don't see any real flaws other than preference or needing to get good.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Legacy Two is already a Game of the Year candidate, and it isn't even finished. It's hard to top the astonishingly good game play and generally goofiness of the first Rogue Legacy game, but this sequel just may be better. The gameplay is the star here with influences possibly culled from other platform games including Hollow Knight and The Messenger. Rogue Legacy Two is a combination of the spirit of Dead Cells, The Messenger, and Hollow Knight, added to the fun and feel of the original Rogue Legacy One. Even with all these influences from recent platform games, Rogue Legacy Two adds gameplay elements never before seen. This is an evolution of not only the genre, but possibly videogames in general. The game has downright funny features such as vegetarianism and color blindness. This game is literally laugh out loud funny. The stories, along with character traits, blend together to provide instances of irony and despair. No spoiler here, but this is a world where people embrace death with a sense of humor. Sadly, since this game is in alpha, or pre-release, many features are not present yet. The upgrade tree from Rogue Legacy One is somewhat similar to the new system. The blacksmith, sorceress, and Charon are back. Some of these sections feel unfinished at the moment. This game is well worth paying for. Rogue Legacy 2 is one of those games that could retail for twice the price it retails for.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun rogue-lite metroidvania.  It improves upon the original in every way, particularly the introduction of multiple classes that all play quite a bit different.  The excellent core game remains: you run a castle until you die, then an heir takes over with bonuses from your prior runs, with a new randomized version of the castle.  Not unlike a side-scrolling version of Hades.  My main gripe is that it is more grindy when compared to, say Hollow Knight.  However, it's a really fun grind and the controls are excellent, with great platforming and combat.  All of the classes are fun and you're encouraged to try them all out.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: With a mixture of Hollow Knight's atmosphere and rich story, Celeste-like platforming, and the classic Rogue Legacy combat and upgrade system, this game gets a absolute 9 / 10. The different weapons + character traits add to the replay value of each run, while upgrading your manor offers permanent buffs that allow you to explore further into the game.Each class is distinctly defined within their own play-styles, and the game rewards experimenting with its many systems. (Ex. Dash + Air attack into combo on ground into special into another dash combo, is one of the many options the game offers) Overall fantastic game, a legend within rogue-likes.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic sequel to Rogue Legacy 1 (RL1) that's better in every way in my opinion. I loved my first playthrough, and appreciate that the NG+ system lets you pick specific ways to make the game more challenging, however, I think the enemies scaling their health/damage each NG should have been a burden to choose as well (at least to a degree, the default scaling felt steep enough that the average player will need to substantially grind for more stats). Luckily, the games assist mode (house rules) allows you scale enemy damage/health to remove the grind, but still make it challenging.Each class is fun to play, and feels more differentiated than they did in RL1. The art, music, and story is enjoyable. The boss fights, combat, and platforming are great. My only other critique is that the true ending requiring you to play through NG+7 (or 8, can't remember). Felt like too steep of a requirement for one extra cutscene.Overall, a great game that's absolutely worth full price!

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 35.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the first game and the sequel is an improvement in every conceivable dimension.It took me a while to get a handle on the controls because I have muscle/button memory issues from using a Playstation controller, and switching to the steam deck had me tripping up a bit. However, once I put some hours in and got used to it, I have to say - this is an impressively tight, fair platformer. Some of the bosses are super challenging but the game encourages you to try new things - I was surprised to see that switching to Duelist (a class I had barely played) made the fifth boss a lot more manageable, for example. Lots of "broken" combinations across classes and relics make things pretty fun as well. Later on, you unlock secondary weapons for several classes which breathes new life into some of them - the ballista on rangers is amazing. All in all - well worth the price of entry. Heavily recommend this game to anyone who likes tough platformers.Played on steam deck - mostly flawless portable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't just  Rogue Legacy with more mechanics. RL2 has seriously evolved the formula in all the right ways. Remember all the "hard" rooms in RL1 where the only thing hard about them was the fact  that there were a million enemies in them with stuff flying  all over the  place? There are (Generally) fewer enemies per room in the  sequel, the trade off being  that each individual enemy is more intelligently designed; enemy damage can pose a serious threat but compared to  the  first game enemies' attacks are less random, but not to the point of predictability. In addition enemy placement is so much more nuanced and creates a more deliberate challenge for the player.     Remember all the platforming you did in RL1? No, you don't because there was hardly any. RL2 has it, and it's WAY more than just a flourish. Seeing all these different techniques  you can use and how they combine in interesting ways as the game progresses shows a much more nuanced and confident design from Cellar Door.     Remember trinkets from RL1? Probably not if you haven't played it pretty recently. It's stuff like the hedgehog's curse or charon's obol. Pretty forgettable. Greatly expanded in RL2 to the point  where they are  a major feature of the game. It adds a lot.     Probably one of the best early access titles out there. Absolutely worth a purchase even in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: So I got 18 hours out of this game, and that is impressive but I am finding this to be more of a chore than fun.  It is in some ways an improved Rogue Legacy.  However after about 10-15 hours you should have many upgrades, but nothing besides the trait and class system makes each run feel unique.  In other games (such as Hades) the runs feel special and exciting.  After you get to the point where you can change your starting 3 heirs, you typically pick one of the few  classes you are best with, and with traits that you don't find annoying.  Unfortuantely this makes each run feel similar to the last run.  You simply grind gold to get your damage and health a little higher with each run, until you can ultimately defeat the boss of the area.I found the game fine, but my power level is increasing so slowly I've lost interest before I beat Rogue Legacy 2.  If you haven't played Hades, I'd recommend trying that first.  Only buy this if you love roguelikes and are having trouble finding something to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Review for Early Access V0.1.0 and V0.1.1 ( Beware of Spoilers! )Graphics:Major Update from RL1. I like it! Looks more define and mature as RL1 but still acknowledge the first game as an origin,Biomes:So far the first biome is complete and it does make a lot of fun. You already have a lot of custom rooms with a lot of challenges. Some rooms are optimized for specific classes but that is okay, because you will always play a different classbecause you kind of have to.The second biome is teased with 2 screens and functions as connection between biome 1 and 3.The third biome is very small and act more as an additional challenge if you are done with the first biome. Enemy kills you really fast and the second boss for this biome is quite a hard challenge but the reward for it, is really special :)Classes:So far they are 4 classes:Knight, Ranger, Wizard and BarbarianSo far the Knight and the Barbarian are the most powerful classes. They both have a lot of HP and deal a lot of damage in a short amount of time.The Ranger is fun to play but is quite difficult to master. He lacks a bit of damage but because of range attacks you avoid most of the damage from the enemies.The Wizard, for me, feels useless right now. Spells are more like tools instead of a weapon and this is exactly what goes wrong for the Wizard. If the damage to spells is increased for the Wizard, he might be hilarious!Class - Skills:Knight - Shield to block:Right now it does not feel useful. Rarely or never have I used this.Barbarian - Shout:Freeze enemies and removes fire shots and such! Nice for rooms with a lot of enemies.Ranger - Platform:Nice for difficult platform levels and nice for the bosses as well. Need!Wizard - Additional Spell:Does not feel special. Like I said more of a tool as for a weapon.Armor and Weapons:They do their job and since the game is in Early Access there is not really much about them. You can upgrade most of them to +1 and that's it. The bonus you get for wearing the same type of armor ( e.g. Leather ) is minimal and will probably change to something more meaningful in the future.Runes:Some are need and some are meh :)A lot of them depends on how the user wants to play. Some of them are not working as intended but the devs are working on it right now. Later you will be able to upgrade them and decide which one should be more usable than other.Traits:A lot of traits are fun to play with e.g. hurting enemies with a big fart =)The visual ones that give a bonus of finding gold are most likely really disappointing and too much to handle. I can not see the gameplay for more money at this point. Either increase the gold bonus or reduce the effect on the user.The castle aka the Skill Tree:Looking great so far and it is just a way to improve your character or to unlock other classes. Its kind of limited right now but will grow with future updates.Heirlooms:Heirlooms are items that improve your skill sets for all classes. Works like a tutorial and you need to work for it. Feels like a kind tutorial and is all right. Future heirlooms could be more difficult!Right now the heirlooms are for insight ( Talking with "Ghosts" ) and a dash!Overall:Great game so far, and I am just waiting for future content updates!Also, the devs are really active at Discord and already released a patch after 24h of the release!

_childDocuments_.review: This is my review after a single playthrough of RL2. It's clearly a game that's meant to have a very complete and long post game content, but I won't be talking about that. The base content lasts for about 30 hours and gives you a fulfilling experience by itself. Rogue Legacy 2 Is a top tier Rogue lite that excels in almost all of what it's trying to do. Your general appreciation of the title will partly depend on your appreciation of its sub-genre. Rogue lites come with a set of design choice that often causes issues such as: some grinding required for progression, a weird difficulty curve where the game becomes easier as you play because of your character's leveling, some repetitiveness and a sense of being on autopilot during your later runs. RL2 does carry some of that, but unlike most of its counterparts (even the best ones like Dead Cells for example), it always finds ingenious ways to circumvent those flaws by balancing them and adding more fun to the mix.It's a game obsessed with balancing and giving the player interesting choices that always come with consequences. In a lot of games, even outside of rogue lites, your character only becomes more and more powerful with everything you find. You have no reason not to pick up an up a weapon or an upgrade, because everything pushes you towards that ultimate power fantasy. It can be fun for a few minutes but can quickly transform your experience into boring a cakewalk. In RL2, every item comes with a lot of power but also restrictions. The best example is the resolve system where each time you grab a power up, you get closer to a point where any additional power up will decrease your total health. Will you risk your health bar to get a slight edge in combat that could help you defeat a boss? Will you grab this special weapon knowing it will force you into extremely close quarter combat? You then find yourself strategizing around your character's progression, not just thinking about how to better increase your damage output, but also your health, your range, your speed, your mobility.  Speaking of which, RL2 rises above other Rogue Lites with its stellar platforming. You may be rewarded and get more powerful by simply “playing”, but challenging platforming sections will always demand your full attention. You cannot win in this game by remaining static, you need to master your jumps your dashes, your spinkicks to be proficient in exploration, puzzles and most of all in the stellar boss fights. For the latter, another key aspect is the spacing which I found particularly engaging. Each archetype has a very specific set of moves and hitboxes that come with advantages and disadvantage. In each run you must adapt to those in the randomly generated situations, keeping you always thinking and on your toes.Aside from the gameplay, I must talk about the graphics. This is some of the most polished, unique and beautiful art direction in the genre. It uses a baffling 2D/3D aesthetic that tastefully takes inspiration of DnD, with a touch of dark fantasy and a lot of humor. In a world where every other Metroid-Vania is legally required to look like Hollow Knight, it's breath of fresh air to see such an original art direction. On a more negative note, like any game, RL2 isn't perfect. I did feel forced to grind for gold at some points because the bosses were nearly impossible to beat with the stats I had. These situations didn't happen a lot which made them stick out even more. Needless to say, grinding isn't the best part of any game... ever... But then again, RL2 makes it more palatable with funny character traits that can drastically change the way you approach your run while also rewarding you with more gold. Which ultimately means less grinding. Which is good. But washing the dishes, even if it’s with a very nice sponge, is still washing the dishes.I want to conclude with what is probably the least relevant and most subjective part of my review. I like all styes of games but my favorites are usually narrative led. RL is definitely not that and nor does it try to be. However, RL2 has a story and some lore and it looks like the devs put a lot of efforts into them. They both left completely indifferent. It never grabbed me so I skipped most of it. This means I am unqualified to write a deep review on it but I will say this very useless and subjective speculation: If the game had a stronger narrative, maybe we would have had the best Rogue Lite ever made. That being said it seems like it wasn't the developers’ ambition and they put their all in the rock solid gameplay and progression. Which is a choice I respect deeply … But will be the reason why I wouldn't put this title above Hades, my favorite Rogue lite.  But I would easily put it above all the others I have played.Thank you Cellar Door Games!
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first one on PS3 and grabbed this as soon as I saw it existed.  If you have never played a video game before (i.e. you can't handle losing) then this might not be the game for you.  Let me be clear: you will die. You will die over and over, just like Dark Souls.  If you are a delicate flower or a child raised in the 2000s then just pass on this game. Dying and learning from your death is how the game is designed, literally.That out of the way, It's a very fun game that is as hard as you want it to be.  I am in the phase of exploring and unlocking, so I have all the House Rules to easy-mode style and you won't find me embarrassed over it.NOTE: there are some non-fan reviews out there who you'll spot saying "ooooooooowee this game is too haaaaard" and to them I say that the game literally embraces the idea of you tuning their difficulty settings with no Steam achievement penalty or anything, so stop complaining and play the game.  As a fairly busy busy person, I personally find this game more fun on its easiest settings because when I do have the chance to play once the kids are asleep I don't want to waste time dying and re-dying just because I'm too principled to click on some assists.  I bet those same people are playing Forza Horizon 5 with all assists on and not having any moral issue with it either. Also note: Valkyrie class has that D-up (or even D-down) swipe that you want the starting warrior to have.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't realize it was so long ago since I played the first one, almost 10 years. The game had been on my mind frequently since. I'm not a huge metroid/castle/rogue-vania person either, I don't mind them but I don't really look for them. RL1 had a lot of charm and challenge and I enjoyed it a lot, to my surprise. And while I have no complaints, I do consider this sequel better in every way.It has, for me, just the right amount of everything. Story, randomness, challenge, RPG elements, platforming, silliness, replay-ability, pick-up-and-put-down-ability, and accessibility. Not to mention it boasts a great art style and soundtrack as well. I sing along to the soundtrack that has no words, and joined the discord with the sole intention of tracking down some of the artwork, I loved it that much.There were times I was convinced I wouldn't be able to beat the game, the difficulty scales pretty quickly, but it made it that much more satisfying when I overcame those obstacles. They give you so many different ways to avoid damage and bounce around a room, it became apparent quickly how much you can use enemies attacks against them or others, and that really makes the game so enjoyable. I hardly used spells or talents at first, and was still able to complete a lot of the story, but mastering those abilities will take you so much further in the later game.After beating the story once, I gave the controller to my kid and he turned on some house rules to have some fun. He used the time to try and learn how to handle the game, and then it wasn't long before he killed the first two bosses in one run. I thought he'd just play for a minute and give up, instead he has his own copy of the game to play now. He was cheering me on during my playthru, I'm looking forward to doing the same for him.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't realize how much I'd enjoy this game. The procedural generation is fantastic where every dungeon run will be VERY UNIQUE. Will the next room be a trap room or treasure room or a treasure room disguised as a trap room? Who knows, ya gotta stay on your toes and be very 'present' while you play.The OSTs are solid and fit well with each biome.The combat is fluid and each class is unique with their own 'playstyles' but the trait system and relic system allows for many different combinations. Wanna be a flying, spinning vampire barbarian that heals and spins through the air like a buzz-saw, you absolutely can!The designers have done a great job of keeping the game quirky and challenging. The NPCs have funny and witty dialogue and the overall game seems like it's had a lot of attention, care, and love poured into each pixel.10/10 would recommend. Lots of replayability with the NG+
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment, I feel that this game has tried to stretch its content too much. The sheer number of runs necessary to get a decent number of upgrades for the castle, the smith, or the enchantress is kind of absurd. My other problem is that I think this game tries to balance things too much. It really will not let you become super powerful, no matter how lucky you are or how far you've progressed, the gains are low and they try to actively prevent it with certain features. My final problem is that right now there is absolutely no way to re-fight bosses. Once you've beat them for that save it's over. This makes runs significantly less interesting and less challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty epic. This game is a very enjoyable medium-complexity roguelite. There's a lot of action, an interesting (but poorly paced) story, and some fun choices in abilities. Notably, there are a ton of different classes with various strengths, weaknesses, and quirks. They play very differently - playing as a Ranger and picking enemies off from afar is a very different feeling from playing a Barbarian and smiting the enemy up close.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked rogue legacy 1 this game is everything you want and more.  So many more classes, so many more ways to interact with things.   It's shocking how much better this game is already shaping up to be than 1.  I can't recommend this more.  Get it before it gets out of EA and bumps up in price because it'll be worth whatever the final cost is.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a good amount of RL2 throughout early access. This game has become ENORMOUS and has an insane amount of content. If you've read other reviews, you'll see a lot of people complain about the grind and how many upgrades there are to get. It's true, it's probably near impossible to earn all of the upgrades since the price goes up the more you buy.The thing is, you just don't need many upgrades to get through the content. If you're a completionist, this might upset you but the bottom line is that you can see and complete all of the content that the game has without even half of the upgrades probably. They're just there as a little treat after a productive run.In terms of actual gameplay, the variety is VERY high with the different classes, attributes, weapons, spells, procedural levels, NG+, thread system-the list goes on and on. I find the actual combat challenging and interesting, although I often wind up sticking to my comfort zone and not enjoying several of the classes (looking at you Mage).My main concern is more about the gameplay "loop." Since it's a roguelite, you expect to hop into a run and have that run end at some point, either by death or by winning. But with Rogue Legacy, your boss progress and Metroidvania-esque upgrades are saved even when you die. So you're really just crossing off all of the bosses, often 1 at a time, until you've beaten them all and need to increase the difficulty. I think my issue is that it doesn't FEEL like a roguelite because so much carries over. If you wanted to treat it as a roguelite and make yourself do all of the bosses each "run," the only issue there is that the game is VERY long for that. This concern might be unique to me though, since I really desire roguelite games with 30-60 minute runs with high replayability.Overall though, I got 80 happy hours in so far and am looking forward to more with 1.0. If that isn't worth $25, I don't know what is.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was really concerned that it was going to be too much like the original.  Which isn't a BAD thing, it's just that since the first game, some much better games have come out.  Things like Binding of Isaac, Dead Cells, Children of Morta, Hand of Fate, Hades, etc.  So there was a lot of worry that it wouldn't really stack up to the greats.  And while I don't think 2 is better than any of these games, it does get close.  A lot of the new things they introduced are good and were the right direction to take the game.  There is an appropriate amount of replayability, but I finished the first run and didn't really think I wanted to do much else.  But it was worth it just for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just play the first one instead.After waiting so long for this sequel to finally release, I find it difficult to imagine myself more disappointed in how it ended up. And that's the key word here: Disappointed. I don't think this game is particularly bad or anything, but the main feeling I had while experiencing it was "I want to play Rogue Legacy 1 again." Because the changes in this sequel range anywhere from "kinda cool" to "just take it away..."For example: the spin kick. I don't know what was wrong with the down attack from the first game that they needed to introduce this thing, but I can't stand it. I would guess that this exists because each class has its own weapon now (instead of just "sword") but the problems with this mechanic don't stop with being simply different. For some reason that I cannot fathom, certain enemies are only vulnerable to this attack. Why. Just why? Repeatedly goomba-hopping off of the same enemy doesn't exactly fill me with joy. And it wasn't any better when implemented into the boss fights.Speaking of bosses, I found the three that I fought to be considerably worse than those of the original, which especially hurts, because it's clear that they tried a lot harder in this one. Instead of being a super-sized enemy with around 1-2 attacks, bosses in this game have actual attack patterns, and even multiple phases! And... that was kind of my issue with them, honestly. The original's bosses were simple but effective, and I enjoyed learning them. But in adding complexity to the bosses in the sequel, rather than finding them more challenging, they become more tedious instead, and I just found myself annoyed.Some other thoughts: graphically the game looks great, although the music is rather forgettable this time around. Level design is a mixed bag; the first area, along with the 3rd and 4th were all good fun, but the 2nd area was such a horrible slog that I never want to go back there ever again. Adding progression locks feels counter to the first game's design, and I didn't much enjoy those. The "lore" or whatever was insipid, and I couldn't find myself caring about these J Z people in the slightest.I wanted so much to love this game, but overall I found this to be a very disappointing sequel, although not a terrible game on its own. I'll reiterate: just play the first game instead. Sometimes, simpler is better.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sick as hell, also fairly addictive. If you want replay value, this is it.I played RL1, loved it, and waited until RL2 left early access to finally pick it up. It beat all of my expectations. There are very few negative things to say about this game and honestly I think they just come down to personal preference. If you want a well-made rogue-like, this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a treat that I received as a gift from a friend but I would absolutely buy this game.Different classes to unlock and gameplay that encourages you to try different weapons and powers. The music is great, the art style is fantastic and the enemy types are varied enough to provide a challenge throughout. Bonus points to the difficulty settings that allow you to adjust the hp of enemies and their damage output so you can play at your unique skill level. Reducing difficulty doesn't exclude you from achievements so play your way. Happy playing everyone
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun enough until you get to a stat wall (5th boss for me) where it becomes more about grinding effectively the exact same run so you can increase your base damage. Art direction is solid, soundtrack is unmemorable but not particularly bad. I particularly liked the 4th boss, but the last 1/3rd of the game is such a slog I can't really recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this a 'neutral' score between yes and no I would. There's a lot to like here. There's loads of charm, platforming feels good, multiple spells and abilities to use, and artifacts that change up each run. The biggest issue is that elements of the game feel like they're from a bygone era that other modern roguelites have improved upon and done better.The biggest issue is with how classes and combat work. There's lots of classes but only a few classes that can attack either diagonally or vertically. This leads to those classes massively outclassing the rest of the classes in the game by being able to have a more consistent damage output and being able to attack small enemies instead of playing a class that can only attack horizontally and dying to a trash mob because the monster is hovering slightly over your head and your attacks wont connect.Your dash roll also doesn't give you a brief frame of invincibility to dodge an attack or create an opening like in other roguelites. You can eventually find an upgrade that lets you dodge *some* projectiles but it's so wildly inconsistent that you'll find yourself trying to dodge via dash and still take damage.There's also no option to re-roll your RNG generated classes with randomized traits before a run without an expensive and grindy castle upgrade. Due to how debilitating some traits are this can mean your choices for a character can be limited to two characters unless you want to play a joke character. Do you enjoy not being able to deal damage? How about only having 1 HP? Well you're out of luck. Better pick one of the other classes unless you want your run to be over in ten seconds.It's not bad, but wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: Currently you can beat the game in less than and hour or so if your pretty good at this genre and likely less than 2 hours even if your not. What's here is alright, but the genre of roguelites have come a long ways since the first Rogue Legacy was released and frankly this just isn't up to par for 2020.I'm honestly surprised at the amount of reviews giving it a thumbs up, considering there are about 7 enemy types, one boss and two areas. Compared to any recent roguelite, even the early access ones, this one just doesn't have any content. I would say wait for future updates and then consider it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: One thing I can say is the basic structure has been set nicely. This giving me the same feeling of sequel design Doom 2016 to Doom Eternal. The game is  much more diverse and demand more attention from you now. It's faster and more creative. The art direction is vibrant but still clean enough to see what is happening.It's only lack one thing "Content". Compared to  the first Rogue Legacy, this release has just about 20% content the first one has. Which is understandable for Early Access title but I kind expected more because RL2 in one aspect supposed to expand the game out. It will surely be updated to the satisfied package soon but this release is pretty much just appetizer   that will just leaving you ended up hunger even more.Still, Potential that I can feel out weighted the lack of content in my case.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone that enjoys single-player games that you have to spend time on and grind to get good at. This game involves skill but also requires you to put effort and time into it to get better. I got this game one week ago and when I first started playing it I immediately knew that it would be one of my favourites and at first I thought "Oh no, I can't play too much or I'll burn out the game and complete it", however now I realise that it would take a tremendous amount of time for this game to be burnt out. This game also have a system after you complete it, and with this (and save slots) it makes sure that you can continuously play the game the most you want while having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. I love it. I've played for 61 hours as of writing this and I am not close to done. I still haven't even beaten the fifth boss. This might give the impression that the game is super hard, or maybe grindy as other reviews have said, but I'm happy to say that while the game is challenging, it doesn't feel at any point unfair (which is honestly really remarkable in itself). Other reviews have also indicated that it's like the first Rogue Legacy, just bigger and better in every way. I agree! I didn't even come expecting a story, but I'm finding the writing really enjoyable. I only have one problem.. the soundtrack doesn't compare to the original.Don't get me wrong, this game has a good soundtrack, but it is simply not in the same ballpark to the original. It sounds like it was composed for a different purpose: to give the environment life, and to make the scenes feel both thematic and threatening. It does a fantastic job of this! The vibe in each area is just perfect. But the original soundtrack was made of tracks that could seriously all stand on their own. I want Tettix and A Shell In The Pit back.If you are a normal, reasonable person who wants their game to be fun to play and who doesn't buy games for the soundtracks, you'll probably have a lot of fun with this one. I buy things partly for the soundtracks and I am nonetheless having a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After 130 hours, I'm at NG+7. This game is just the absolute best. Buy it.I'm on NG+3 at the moment, and man do I love this game. All of the classes feel unique and fun, there's a ton of passive skills to unlock, so I almost always feel like I'm making some progress with each run. The bosses are all interesting, the art style is fantastic, there's not much I don't like about this game.There's for sure a grind, like I said the passive tree is really big and there's a ton of stuff to unlock, but that's part of the fun for me. I think my only nitpick is I wish there were more relics and spells to find, just to add some extra flavor to each run, but I think that can be fixed with a content patch or two.I think this is one of the best roguelites out there and encourage everyone to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Family can be a central theme in many games, whether it be a revenge mission for harm done or a rescue mission from a kidnapping. Sometimes you even get to play as a family a la Kratos and Atreus in God of War or the entire Bergson family in Children of Morta. Rarely though do you get to play as 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 10th, 50th, or even the 100/200/300th generation of a family. This is not some new idea but a sequel. Can the sophomore entry reach the same level of success?Developed by Cellar Door Games, Rogue Legacy 2 is the sequel to 2013’s Rogue Legacy. “Rogue Legacy 2 is what you’d get if you mashed Rogue Legacy and a sequel together” (direct quote from the Steam page). That is some hard logic to argue. Dying is not the end. Your children and their children and their children and their children and their children (my editor stopped me or I would have continued) will carry on your legacy (see what I did there?) They will inherit everything from you. EVERYTHING. Look, being colorblind is no joke…How do you follow up a great game? For starters, improve everything. There were 9 classes in the last game. How does 15 sound this time around? That is 15 different classes with 15 unique playstyles and those 15 playstyles could have countless variations. All classes now have a basic attack, a talent, a random castable spell, and of course, let us not forget the traits. Classes can end up with zero traits or as many as 2. Like its predecessor, you begin the game with a number of classes but as you advance through the game, more classes become available. A neat feature is that when you do unlock a new class, you can choose to swap over and play it without waiting for it to randomly appear in the generational lottery. Classes range from knights, mages, and assassins to bards, rangers, and even chefs. No two runs will be the same. Did someone order a pizza?Classes now level up individually as you play the game. If you played the first game, you most likely had a preferred class (I was partial to the mages). At the end of each run, all experience you earned from kills is tallied and you can rank (level) up which provides an added bonus.Knights increase their equip weight, Barbarians have increased vitality, and Mages have increased intelligence to name a few. You still are bound to play favorites but at least there is a reason to try different classes.Similar to Rogue Legacy, the game has several biomes that all end with a boss fight. Unlike the first game, there are now 6 zones to clear before reaching the final level. The biomes are more than just different looks and just finding the boss door. Each zone has various objectives to unlock the boss door and in your travels, you may find random challenges and new abilities to unlock for all of your characters. Additionally, you can unlock the teleporter, for a price, so that you can easily return to each zone on subsequent runs.This is a huge change from the first game where each run was a completely fresh layout. The layouts are still randomized but it is much easier to return to the start and feel like you are making progress each time.One of the best aspects of the first game that had to be in the second game was the various traits that classes could spawn with each run. It had another entire level of randomization on top of the already random dungeon layouts. Characters can have alexithymia (the inability to recognize emotions aka you cannot see the damage dealt), have dyspraxia (being clumsy aka items that drop from enemies or looted from chests go flying all over the place), be a Puritan (everything is considered lewd and enemies are censored), or even have ol’ reliable IBS. Super IBS in Rogue Legacy 2 is not just a cosmetic feature as it replaces your class talent to allow for an extra little boost to your jumps. The talent is actually called Super Fart and I still laugh about it each time.Traits can be seen on the character select screen but until you have actually played a run with the trait, they only show the name and unless you are well versed in nameology (someone better get this reference), you will have no idea what can happen.Of course, no one wants Osteogenesis Imperfecta (you die in one hit). To make less desirable traits more appealing, the developers added an incentive: GOLD. Sometimes you just need to have a few runs with a not-so-perfect setup if it means you can level up the castle just a little bit more.Combat works relatively the same as the first game with some exciting new additions. Double jump and dash are no longer equippable runes and become standard play on all characters once unlocked. New abilities added to your arsenal are a spin kick which can be used to bounce off objects and climb higher and the damage recovery window. What that does is allow for you to quickly dash or jump after taking damage. How many times have you been platforming a section only to take a hit and fall to the bottom? It is almost a quality of life thing but it does take skill to utilize it to the fullest and a much-welcomed ability when you get it to work.Also new to the series are relics and resolve. Resolve equates to how many relics can be held and affects your health. Everyone starts out at 225% resolve. The more armor you wear, the lower your resolve goes. Relics cost resolve as well so that will bring the number even lower. If you dip below 100% resolve, you lose max health directly proportional to the resolve loss. 99% resolve means 99% total health. You may play as one class and feel confident enough to take that health hit while other times you may be a class you are not proficient with or just do not like and can drop some armor to get back above the 100 mark. Relics are found throughout the dungeons and cost resolve to purchase (they usually appear as a choice of two). Like traits, if you have not found the relic yet, the effects will be hidden until equipped. Some relics are great, some are just alright and some can be awful (in a sense). One so-called awful relic makes you killable in 1 hit unless you can kill X enemies or pickup Y items. If you manage to complete the objective, you are granted a buff like 30% increased health or a flat damage buff. It becomes a risk or reward type thing when choosing this relic. Other relics grant more damage from range at the cost of less damage in melee. Sucks to be melee when you get this one, trust me. The downside to many relics is not knowing what they are but the longer you play, the less likely you will find relics without a description.Making their return from the first game are the architect, blacksmith, enchantress and, of course, Charon (he’ll still rob you of all your money). The architect can serve to lockdown the castle and prevent a new run from randomizing the rooms. While the blacksmith operates in a similar fashion requiring you to find blueprints so that he can craft, the enchantress works slightly differently. You still need to find her runes so that they can be equipped but runes have a weight that determines how many can be used versus equipping by armor slot. Managing the weight is relatively easy (there are indicators in the menu) and being able to see how runes stack in one place is a nice improvement.The house always wins. Well, this time, the house is on your side, so to speak.House rules completely change game settings and go beyond just easy, normal, and hard difficulty levels. Enemy health and damage can be lowered or raised, a flight option can be toggled if you feel you struggle with the platforming, and you can even turn off traits. The game even provides recommended levels for each option based on the type of experience you are looking for when playing.Rogue Legacy 2 is a sequel done right. All that humor, charm, and excellent gameplay from the first are still there but with more than enough improvements to give the game a fresh spin.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic roguelike with way more depth than expected and even more customization that the first. Absolutely wicked difficulty, but a great feeling of progression as you begin to level up your lineage, equip new armors, unlock multiple new types of character and more. Just fantastic and a great successor to the original!
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes everything about the original Rouge Legacy and enhances it and makes it feel like it always should have. The original was a classic amazing game and this one makes it look like a beta demo for Rouge Legacy 2. Loving it so far and can't wait to dump even more time into this than the OG.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun to play. The mechanics are all really solid and the new classes all feel different from the bog-standard classes from the first game. I really appreciate the addition of the archer as well. The downside to early access is that you can hit the wall I have (about 10-12 hours in) where my castle is built out as far as it can go in this patch and I've beaten the first boss. The upside is that I know that the game will continue to expand in early access and I'm going to be eagerly looking forward to every content update. Highly, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Legacy 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty easy thumbs up... with a handful of caveats and personal gripes.First off, I have not finished the game. I was playing with a friend where we would hand the controller off every character, and we managed to get up to the fifth boss located at Sun Tower. After several failed attempts we realized that our options were to either grind out enough upgrades to have a better chance with the boss, or keep making a beeline straight to the boss and keep attempting. After kind of switching between both, alternating between "gold" runs and "boss" runs, eventually we lost interest and decided we were finished with the game. Our lost interest stems from multiple things which I will get to in this review.But first, the positives. For starters, I think most aspects of the game are a straight up improvement over the original. The presentation, the gameplay, the huge increase of content are all appreciated. Not only are there more classes, some of which dawn an alternate version you can unlock as well, but some are even reworked to be more viable than they're RL1 counterpart. The Scar challenges were a neat addition as well to test your skills and gave something to do if you felt like taking a break from runs. Individual classes have their own levels now, giving a slight bonus if you prefer some classes over others. The manor has more upgrades and more features. Overall the game gives more bang for your buck and I respect it for that. However, the game isn't perfect.For starters, the increased amount of content sometimes makes the game feel bloated. The first region of the game, for example, feels twice as big as the RL1 counterpart. This on its own is fine, but combining that with harder bosses, the "labor cost" mechanic, and 2 more regions than RL1, all adds up to a lot more runs that take way longer. It felt like it took twice as many runs to successfully beat a region's boss, with the average run taking 20-30 minutes. If you got a character with decent gold bonus and wanted to take full advantage of it, runs could even take up to 40-50 minutes. Sure the gameplay is decent, but I don't think its decent enough to play 40-50 times (we were approaching our 40th run by the time we quit). Part of RL1's strength was its somewhat simple and short nature. You could easily beat the game within 15 hours or so and walk away satisfied. I have a sneaking suspicion that if my friend and I forced ourselves to play another 10-20 hours, we would walk away frustrated and bored more than anything. "Labor cost" is the biggest reason for this, since it is an increased cost that is added to every upgrade in your manor that goes higher with each and every upgrade purchased. Meaning that not only would upgrades go higher in cost for each rank you put into them, but also increase from the labor cost mechanic. We have runs where we'd clear out multiple regions, defeat a boss, and STILL only have enough to buy 2 or 3 upgrades. Considering that these upgrades are usually very minuscule and only add 1 damage, 5 HP, etc... makes the game one of the grindiest I have played in awhile.Bosses are another strange issue. Their designs and themes were interesting and set them apart from each other. By the fourth boss, however, the way they decided to make bosses more difficult is to add a whole lot of projectiles to the screen. Projectiles ranging in shape and size, coming from all directions. Irad (the boss we were stuck on) in particular was ridiculous in this regard, to point where the game felt less like a platformer and more like a "bullet hell" game. Again, the game needlessly making things more complex for the sake of complexity.All this being said, I think my friend and I already spent more time playing this than RL1, and for the most part had more fun doing so, which already justifies the purchase in my book. I highly encourage giving the game a try whether you're a RL1 fan or a newcomer.

Having said that, I loved this game.  It's better than the 1st Rogue Legacy.  Additional classes, additional passives, etc.  It feels almost too overwhelming with the extra content.  But, the difficulty is balanced extremely well and the boss fights were fun.  Definitely worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been playing a lot of roguelite games these days like Curse of the Dead Gods, Hades, Skul: Slayer Hero and one of the things I've notice is that despite the map is randomly generated, its not true randomly generated (like Dead Cells). You start to notice similar patterns layout throughout the level of these games. Why I'm bringing this up? Its not really a flaw in the game design but playing 54+ hours in this game, I've started to notice these patterns layout in RL2. Not saying its bad but thats how much commitment you can put yourself into lol.Anyway, I can tell you off the bat, its a definitely better game than its predecessor. RL1 was hard and it really put me off playing it because of how clunky & difficult it is.This sequel however, is everything better than RL1. The art, soundtrack, game mechanics is just 10x better. The tower OST is especially a banger.Game mechanic wise, there are different classes. Some people prefer certain classes than others but there are some classes that are OP af and some....well not so much. However like every game, there are some flaws in the game (IMO). The water village is  that doesnt have a teleport at all, the lore chamber is mixed icon with the arcane chamber, there is a weird game mechanic that need souls to activate but to activate it, you need to score a certain number which requires different class.... which you need to do it every run ( kinda annoying. Just let the player choose the class from the area ). Also have an area where we can read up the lore or something. I forgot what was RL1 lore. Its a good game. I like the lore, the art, the ost, the game mechanic of the game. Price wise, its a bit heavy on $25USD but I guess 10 years in the making justified it.

_childDocuments_.review: For being early access, this game is basically complete. I have yet to encounter any bugs of any sort, or (too m)any imbalances. I die as much as I do cause I suck, but Is till thoroughly enjoy the game. just under 28 hours and I just beat  on my first try (#5 of 6) in my first play through after having cleared out all 4 of the areas leading to the . I have all the Gems, but nowhere near the full armory of weapons/helms/capes/trinkets. Castle is something like Lvl 157 or something and I have a LONG way to go. Never thought I'd enjoy this game as much as I do, but I cannot recommend it enough. 10/10, keep up the good work Cellar Door Games! I would also be interested in seeing how well a co-op mode would work. I feel like the chaos would make the game just that much more hysterical and fun to play.Some of the classes just don't feel viable. The Bard for example seems VERY niche, and I feel like it would be difficult to make it viable. Meanwhile the Barbarian basically roflstomps everything in his path. Yes, his attacks leave him open to being hit for all of 1s, but a 100% crit chance as long as you're on the ground? Combined with the relic that boosts damage by 12% while on the ground makes it pretty broken good. Knight: your starter class, is viable all the way through so no complaints there. It's the perfect middle ground. Cook: very fun because you can rebound projectiles and heal on demand up to 3 times before running out of charges and you inherently have Amaterasu's Sun. Dragon Rider: hit or miss, it's pretty solid but the way it attacks just throws a wrench in the game flow, maybe a little adjustment is needed. Mage: solid, perfectly balanced and perfectly broken when you figure out how to abuse the Leach trait.Boxer: solid, albeit a little more difficult to play than other classes, but becomes infinitely more easy when you get the Boxing Bell relic (build up 2 combo per hit instead of 1). Ranger: tad bit lacking, but I could also just be playing it wrong. For what it's worth, the ranger is fun to play now and then if a bit difficult in a good way. Valkyrie: like the Dragon Rider, but does have a bit more utility to it with the upward attacks. TheAssassin: the 1-2-3 combo and crit on the 3rd hit is a fun change of pace and does decent damage for a class that dual wields daggers. However Obscura doesn't get much use by me, and I find minimal reason to use it at all. Clearly there IS a meta to this at the moment, which is almost unavoidable, but there's a very clear winner as to which class is the most viable and which is the least (I give the crown to the Barbarian and the dunce cap to the Bard).I feel like there also could be a bit of a slight buff to the drop rate of food items, as I can't count the number of runs that I have cleared out the first 3 areas  and gotten less than 5 health drops, but a dozen and a half potions. But my next run I'll get 9 foods in Castle Agartha but as soon as I leave to any other area, I get 1-2 through the rest of that Heir's life.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the hell out of the first Rogue Legacy, and absoluetly loved it. However, I never managed to defeat more than the first two bosses. However, I did put a lot of time into the game, and unlocked all the classes.So when I first heard of the sequel, I was excited, and bought it right away. However, it being early access and all, i decided to hold off on playing it for a bit. So about two weeks ago I began to play it in ernast, and I can say that I freaking love it. It feels more than just a sequel, but improves everything the prior game set out to do. The combat is fun and enjoyable, map exploration is great, and the improved rune system is so much better than the original.The only major thing I could complain about is the classes, or more specifically the gunslinger. Every other class, including the freaking chef, all had their own unique uses, and played very well once you got used to them. But the gunslinger, just freaking sucked. The reload time leaves you very open to attacks, and attempting to reflect will cancel the reload. To put it bluntly, it is akin to the archer class(which i freaking love) but so much worse. I think either the class' ammo count should be massively increased, or the reload time reduced. Because as it stands now, I will not use the class when any other is avaliable. To add onto the crappy gunslinger class, i found the extra weapons to also feel lackluster. Their move sets either felt clunky/gimmicky or were just more damage, but a cripiling weakness. Such as the archer sub class, which does much more damage and fires further, but you have to be stationary. I found that in this game, where enemies like to move a lot, sacraficing mobility just put you in a bad spot. Again, it was just never worth taking these weapons when given the chance,Besides those two complaints, I found myself really enjoying the game, and just beat the boss in the sun tower.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a skill based Rogue Like.The more classes you unlock, the harder the game gets because nearly all of the unlockable classes are gimicky and have severe animation locks as well as pushback or knockups that force you into damage.The game has off-screen damage and traps, things the developers attempted to fix by adding warning signs for incoming off-screen projectiles. The issue is the devs already proved they could zoom the screen out on big maps, yet they keep it zoomed far in on randomly generated rooms with random BS flying around.The enemies, the traps, the projectiles all blend in with the backgrounds, making it extremely hard to see anything and sometimes youll wonder what even hit you when an arrow from the bottom corner thats the same color as the background finds its way in your back.There's also CONTACT DAMAGE for enemies that have attack animations, imagine playing dark souls, except brushing up against the boss's toe hurt you. Why?BUT THATS OKAY, you're meant to get hit~! you just need to GRIND GOLD to unlock better stats, better gear, and equip very specific load outs that have high amounts of armor (damage negate) so you can just face roll the hits instead of avoiding them!every-single-thing in this game is meant to be won by attrition. 99% of the rewards for clearing a room, or killing a mini-boss are going to be currency you CANT USE UNTIL YOU DIE. You're meant to die, thats the games goal, not to progress but to intentionally die. There's even perks you can pick up that kill you but let you carry over your gold bonuses, literally pick up an item and lose. thats winning!Every win in this game feels cheap, the boss that used to 2-shot you that you just beat? Oh right, you got hit 9 times this round because you grinded up health/armor. You face rolled it.You don't improve at this game, you just play longer.If you suck at games, and want the game to let you win just because you slam your head against its wall for 20 hours please buy this game.If you're looking to play a tight, clean platformer rogue-lite that rewards you for taking risks with perks/weapons for your current run, then run.

_childDocuments_.review: Early thoughts for Early Access.Just gonna start this off if you like metroidvanias and roguelike/lite games you'll probably like this game. People say there is not a ton to the game so far, but the entire point of roguelike/lite games is the ability to replay the game over and over with different layouts/play styles. More content will get added as time goes on, but what is there already is still good for a game at $20. To the game itself. It improves on most of the issues I had with the original game. Classes actually behave differently. As a hammer player in Monster Hunter, I'm immediately drawn to the Barbarian class which has a tumbling air attack. The archer has a bow and requires quick aiming. The mage is the only class I'm not a massive fan of yet, but I think I need a bit more time with the class to be sure. The castle and upgrades system is very similar to the first game just expanded in various ways. The castle upgrades, heirlooms, and runes help to give certain flavors to each run. If you have a vampire rune that will help you with some traits that might leave you a bit helpless otherwise on health regen, or you can sacrifice a large amount of rune capacity and gain more gold with a different rune. I personally like the art style. It helps break up the rooms a bit more to me than the first game. It feels easier knowing where I am without having to constantly peep the map. I hope the same care is put into the rest of the game's areas, and from the sneak peak already present, it looks like they're getting there.Overall, if you liked the first game or similar games there's something here to enjoy. It's only 20 dollars not on sale, and I think that's a good price for what is present and coming down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler alertIt has promise, and was entertaining to play until the end of the content, but after all was said and done, it was about <5 hours in total to grind it out. No crashes, smooth animation. In the end, I feel like they just could have extended the first one, and the second one wasn't necessary so far. Most of the gags are kinda funny. I appreciate them. The best parts feel like hollow knight, the worst parts are unseen obstacles and moving objects while falling down, and treasure rooms where it's impossible to get the treasure. (You're big, and the space to fit is too small)The negatives: The game is really not finished at all, but I believe in Cellar Door for now...Last game had 4 "Zones" with different themes. This one so far only has 1 zone + 1 transition + some of a second zone is finished. The stats top out sooner than you'd want. Some classes are absolutely terrible. The archer, or the pacifist debuff are totally worthless. Mage isn't great either. I just kill myself to skip to another generation.One boss is finished. The last optional boss is two of them at the same time. I don't know what to think of it, but I didn't want to continue playing after seeing that lol. I'll grind out the next content when it comes out. Sidethought: Why did this happen to dungeon defenders as well? They released a barebones-beginning as well. Updated to not recommended. Game is in version 0.6.2 as of this new writing. The game is still not completed. This update is 13 months later. I'm incredibly disappointed in the piecemeal delivery of the content. I'm not bothered to pick it up until it's done. It's over a year later now. I don't want to incrementally enjoy a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is an improvement on the original in every single way. And I'm a pretty big fan of Rogue Legacy 1, so that's saying something.One of the most lackluster things about RL1 in my opinion are the classes - Although the class you choose in the beginning does change your strategy to an extent, every single class ultimately has the exact same core gameplay. Not only did RL2 add a ton of new classes, but every single one of them (including the ones brought back from RL1) have completely unique playstyles that make the game feel significantly different. And in a roguelike game, variety like this is one of the most important things to make sure the game doesn't get stale. Fighting the exact same boss as a knight vs a bard vs a gunslinger(!?) feels fresh every time, and that's before you even get into the traits.There's quite a lot of content, too. It took me 30 hours to beat Rogue Legacy 1 on New Game +4. I'm at just about the same hour count in this one and I still have a decent length to go before beating the game even a single time. I could say more but it's all pretty much just "Remember this thing from RL1? It's better now." The progression feels good, the bosses are fun, the items lead you to make interesting decisions, they made Charon's gold fee feel less punishing, there's a whole 6 areas now, etc. They did a really good job with the visuals and music as well, they feel very faithful to the original game while still being unique and pleasant. The humor is somewhat hit or miss but I think it's been more hits than misses.Oh yeah, did I mention they added a GUNSLINGER? It totally kicks ass, too. Well done guys, you made another banger.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful sequel that improves on the original in every way, and the original was a good game to begin with. This review is in it's early access phase on the stygian library update so things could change but even now this game is 100% worth buying and is a solid 8.5/10. If it keeps this exact level of quality up to full release content it's gonna probably be a 9/10. Edit: Each major update takes this gem and polishes it even further. I've had a blast.Edit 2: 1.1-steam release. This game has delivered in pretty much every way possible.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been addicted to this game for the last two weeks and I have a lot to say.First of all,  negative reviews say that this game doesn't do much more than the original and I wonder if these players even played the first one recently. Pretty much every single element from the original game has been improved. It looks better. The gameplay feels smoother. There is actual variety between each class, most of which are fun to play in my opinion. ( is probably the least fun one in my opinion because it's hard to hit and run with it.)The bosses are also great. Their moves are all fairly telegraphed and must all be avoided in different ways. Some are more gimmicky than that but the 1rst and 6th one are very good. The lore was also much better than expected. To be fair, the first game put the bar on the ground but this one's pretty good. The writing is good, the characters you read about are cool the world is very unique. I also like how  at the end of the story. It's, obviously, fully optional but you should still pick up new lore with to get the side quests even if you don't want to read it.Speaking of which, the side quests were pretty entertaining. They give you better insight into the lore, make the world feel more immersive and give you tangible rewards. This also include finding , those points all apply too. I like figuring them out myself but some of them did drive me nuts for a little while and I have not found everything available to me.One aspect I feel more lukewarm about is the metroidvania aspects. They are fine but awfully linear. Most of the time ability A will unlock the next area which gives ability B to unlock next area where you find ability C, etc... And when it is not the case, if you try to explore an other area, you'll get slapped because the enemy level scale linearly from an area to an other, forcing you to do them in order. On top of that, these abilities won't reset on NG+, (expect ) making them feel even more forgettable once you start looping them. It's definitely the right decision because gathering them all over again would feel tedious but I think that illustrate even more how these features are not a core part of the game at all compared to an actual metroidvania where the journey of collection these abilities is the fun part of replaying. Long story short, they are passable, but very un-impressive.The NG+ were a great surprise to me. They are very well integrated into the gameplay loop and you still have plenty of levelling up and unlocking ahead of you after beating the game. The last thing I want to touch on is the grind. I started played on V1.0 which allegedly help with it so my experience may be different from the reviews written before that. For most of the game, up to the 5th area, I never felt like I needed more stats to survive. Most of the time, I feel like I'm strong enough to beat the current challenge with some practice. And if I do become underpowered (which usually happens because I used the architect too many times in a row to beat a boss) a good farming run is often enough to get me back up. It's a little tedious at times but going back to the previous area is often a nice break from trying the harder ones over and over again.So all of that to say.. I don't really mind the grind. It feels well balanced to me and integrated into the game. When it does occasionally become an issue, I like the challenge of playing around it. It is an issue for other players, and that's a fair reason to dislike the game so uhh, decide for yourself I guess.So, all of that so say, I'm addicted, send help, 9.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the original Rogue Legacy, but this game plays like the creators forgot what made their game fun, and replaced all of that with dumb gimmicks.Yes, it's in early access, but they delayed it, making it seem like they would be adding more than the bare minimum in it. The manor system is one of the main reasons why I ever played this game, it's absurd that they only added the most simple upgrades and classes to the second one.The indie game humour from RL1 is back, and it's way more obnoxious than ever. I genuinely think someone at Cellar Door Games has a scat or fart fetish with all of the really weird references to them. It's not a dealbreaker, but it's pretty sad that the writers didn't grasp the idea of less is more.Speaking of totally subjective things that I get way too mad about: what is wrong with this game's art? Everything is 3D but not, and also weirdly bright. The original game's pixel art lent itself well to the game as a whole. This feels like they were inspired by Cuphead and other indie games of that make but didn't study them well enough. A pattern I'm noticing.Now for the completely pointless stuff:This game was made for consoles. Which is funny, because unlike RL1, RL2 isn't available on consoles, probably because console players aren't complacent with "early access" games.The previous game had quite an attack that required two button presses simultaneously, but had the decency to bind it to "down" if it felt uncomfortable. This game throws too many controls at you and hardly lets you fix them. Maybe that's an overstatement, but completely changing the control layout is a stupid decision for a sequel, especially since nobody complained about the first game's controls.This game had a really solid base to improve on, and decided to completely ♥♥♥♥ it up. Why does taking damage cause slo-mo? It isn't a fun mechanic to watch my character fly across the screen, it just wastes a few seconds, and makes me less prepared to continue playing the game. Who thought of this? It must have taken time to implement, which makes me think they were making a different title before realizing they had a good existing title.Mage's close combat makes trying to hit an enemy at a different height (eyeballs, those turrets that spit fire) nearly impossible, which isn't helped by the more involved magic system that feels like a worse reskin of the original. Quirky is fine. I know this is an indie game. But there's a limit to how cute you can make everything before I start to feel annoyed. Oh, and you can't even test out the spells outside your manor to learn their trajectories. You lose mana there. Why?! It's a testing ground! That's what the training dummy is meant for! tl;dr: No. It's not worth your money. It wasn't worth my money, that's for sure.
