I'm serious, if you are one of those people that think playing in Easy is a shame, ignore this review, really.So how is the game is Casual Mode? It's fantastic. I took about 13 hours to get All Achievements, and it was a blast. It's so much better than the 1. Every single detail that was bothering me in the 1(like jumping on stairs that are outside the displayed field) has been changed in the 2 for the best.The new characters are fantastic. Dominique is able to do so much, Robert is thrilling to play, and Hachi is just so good that I need to dedicate a paragraph to it. It is broken, sure, but its hitbox is so big that you also need to be very careful with it. Its invincibility gauge needs to be used with wisdom, and its hover rewards you so much when you spend time learning in details how it works. Really Hachi is just so good."Spoiler Paragraph": Seriously it is so good that when you unlock the Solo Mode, I immediately did a Solo run with Hachi and it was a massive blast.Now, I know that the game is way harder than the 1 in Veteran. Even unfair at some point. But sorry, I don't care. Casual was just so much fun, that I'm gonna replay the game for a long time I think!
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like developers didn't understand what made the first CotM so great and beloved. We enjoyed the challenge, yes, but it always felt fair and well designed. This game just says f*ck it and fills rooms with enemies/pitfalls. It's just frustrating and not enjoyable, which really sucks because I loved CotM so much but I guess I'll just replay that and RotN.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Demons are running a muck once again and the demon slayer Zangetsu is up to the task. This time around, he’s going to need all the help he can get to defeat this new army of demons and bring peace back to the world. This is Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2.So, something that I liked from the first that I didn’t note in my review at the time, was the diverse abilities each characters had at their disposal. In the sequel, that trend continues.With as many as 7 characters to play as (the 4 from the first game, plus 3 newcomers), it makes for an interesting experiment when you can go through the stages and try to complete them with either this character or that character, and so on, so forth. Without spoiling too much of their abilities, the variety of choices from the roster certainly makes the game interesting to experience.Curse of the Moon 2’s progression is broken down in 3 - 4 chapters. The stages that you go through are all the same, but the purpose of your journey is different in each chapter. So, just to make sure that it’s noted, you need to beat the game at least 3 times to truly say that you finished the game.In the first game, while you only need to beat the game once, you can easily replay it again and again, but you can choose to do something different in each playthrough. Here, the game takes those options away, to have you follow the story as it should be told.On a personal note, I played the game with the intention of getting all the achievements and I wasn’t sure if I was going to get them all, because I got tired of playing the game after 6 playthroughs…While the first game had replay value by giving you multiple pathways to choose from and explore for each stages, the second game’s level design took that away. What we have presented can be summed up like this. You go through the stages in one of two pathways, with shortcuts available for certain characters and overall, the stages feels longer in comparison to the first game. The game’s biggest problem is the length of it, or rather, the way it’s handled. Besides that, the fun factor is still there and I can recommend this for those looking for a retro style experience. For those who go for the achievements, take note that this might bore you.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: COTM 1 was arguably better than ROTN in my humble opinion, with an admitted personal bias for 8bit and retro themed games.  Now with COTM2 this Classicvania style game is yet another entry into the glorious retro resurgence and is definitely one of the closest to a spiritual successor of the original Castlevanias (1-3) on NES.  This sequel implements Dominique as a spear user similar to Eric Lecarde of CV Bloodlines for Sega Genesis, further evoking more retro Castlevania games.  Thank you IGA and Inti Creates for this installment.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely excellent game for the first 5 hours, completely worth the entry fee. Tight platforming, solid controls, interesting and fun to use characters, great art & music.After your first playthrough, you get a bad ending and are asked to play Episode 2 (repeating all levels but harder) which is still pretty fun but really stretching the content. Unless you fulfill obscure requirements, you then get ANOTHER bad ending and are sent to Episode EX. This asks you to repeat the levels AGAIN, but with 4 much weaker characters and more sadistic layouts in certain rooms. Expect many cheap deaths from being knocked back into pits if you aren't pixel-perfect. This episode is an exercise in frustration and loses much of the fun.This game would be stronger if it didn't try to overstay its welcome by stretching its content and withholding a real ending. As-is, still worth doing the first playthrough for fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game. Played through every route, got every ending. Bloodstained 1 is a great game, go buy it right now if you haven't already.But I found myself exhausted trying to play through the sequel. BloodStained 2 tends to resort to a lot of cheapshots / ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game design. Large clusters of enemies that feel unavoidable to get past without taking dmg or just having Hachi ready, and many maps with bottomless pit for enemies to shove you into, makes playing this game feel like a slog.Call it old school challenge, but I call it frustrating. I really want to like this game, but I can only try to convince myself "it'll get fun, keep practicing!" so many times. Off to the uninstall folder with you.Strongly urge caution before purchasing. Look up game-play footage before you decide to commit to this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this because you enjoyed the original.I did assuming that it would be at least as good, but it's increasingly frustrating. Unlike the first, I've no desire to sit and play through it multiple times.It just does feel as well designed as the original. The game should feel difficult, but fair, but it's full of very frustrating screens and it feels disproportionately punishing for dying as character. The mech character seems like a fun addition until you realise the hover controls are frustrating and it's so much larger than other characters that it becomes useless without mana for invincibility.It's a real shame after how good the original was.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not enjoying this one, sadly. The first few levels were great, but then it felt like every enemy I encountered was a puzzle. This is due to the characters and their abilities. They're too extreme. The minute you unlock the dog who can become invincible, all semblance of balance is thrown out the window. They can throw a complete mess of enemies at you and justify it, because you were supposed to switch to the dog and brute-force it. Or accept that you'll inevitably take damage, then use the girl's heal ability. It becomes annoying. You also have the flimsy sniper guy who can attack enemies that aren't even on-screen yet. So there are instances where you have to predict what's coming or die to it. This character dies in two hits so he's useless in boss battles. It all feels too gimmicky.In the first game, you could play through the entire game with only Zengetsu if you wanted, or only Zengetsu and Miriam, and there were even achievements for doing that. It was super fun, because the game was properly balanced to be played with those characters. But in this game, you have to recruit everyone, so they balanced the game with the idea that you'll use every ability at your disposal. That might sound like good game design, but when the characters are unbalanced and boring to use, it makes for a very poor game.Often, if one character dies, you might as well kill the rest of your party to return to the checkpoint with everyone at full health. Otherwise you'll have a hard time getting to the boss without taking severe damage, and then you'll die instantly at the boss without having learned anything about its attack pattern.I completed five stages on normal difficulty, then I decided to try the sixth stage on Casual to see if it was more fun to play. It's not. It only highlights this game's flaws even more.Also the music was way better in the original and the dog is a meme character, there I said it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: In true Castlevania fashion, the second one is much worse. The level design is less encouraging towards taking alternate paths and finding secrets than the first one, the boss fights are just lesser versions of the first game's bosses (i.e. the Gladiator Dozer (Stage 3 of CotM2) takes several tactics from the Glutton Train (Stage 1 of CotM) while offering less opportunities to attack, not to mention Gremory (Stage 7)'s first form is outright taken from the first game (Stage 8). The option to forgo an ally by ignoring them or simply killing them for their power is also removed. Zangetsu continues to be the all-around character until the Soul Eraser is acquired, which is equivalent to Ultimate mode in CotM, in addition to upgrading your subweapons. Dominique is the Bloodlines expy of the group, wielding a polearm. Just as Miriam of the past, her jump is higher, and her weapon is longer. Her subweapons are magic spells, with the important ones being heal-focused. Golden lanterns drop the Resurrection Anthem, meaning in order to have everyone alive, you have to ensure that everyone dies before Dominique. If you happen to lose her, then you've essentially lost a life.Robert is a bizarre character. His rifle weapon travels instantly across the screen, allowing you to kill some enemies before they've even truly appeared. His subweapons are nothing to brag about aside from the D. Cannon, which is practically necessary with its kickback giving the player a vertical boost. Rapid switching between him with his wall jump and the next character's hover ability are necessary to exploit the game into getting one where they need to go.Hachi is a meme dog with an enormous hitbox unlike any other. The ability to completely ignore spikes as well as an invincibility button subweapon says a lot about modern game design. The game feels justified in throwing dozens of enemies in one area simply because of invincibility. A character like this completely ruins the flow of what's already painfully slow gameplay.Just buy the first game. It's better and cheaper.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Another slash with the whip another win. Continuing our saga with  beloved heroes. This time we also joined by three new members to the cast. Like previous title this time you get much more gameplay and more awesome secrets to discover. The story wont unfold you its true nature until you kill the last monster. The game is more skilled based this time. Once again the awesomenes of levels details synchronized with great boss fights. Each new cast member adds to complexity and metrovania style exploration. On the top of this beautiful thing the music will accompany you with love. Draculvania reborn with passion thanks to these developers. It makes Halloween month more special. Will wait for Curse of the moon 3 for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game, but not as good as the first. Where the first one let you have one save that you could go back and choose a different path to experience the different endings, this one forces you to go in a specific path. You will do mostly the same path in 3 or 4 different "episodes" and only one of the episodes has any choice to make. If you make the "good" choice, you only have to beat the game 3 times to actually finish the game. If you make the "bad" choice, you have to beat the game 4 times.The problem is, there is very little difference in the episodes. In all 4 episodes, the first 7 levels are all exactly the same, although the bosses get slightly updated attacks, and you have different characters so you can take different shortcuts. The different paths do not feel that much different though. The 8th level is the only one that changes, which feels very weird. You get so used to the first 7 bosses that you can do most of them without thinking, and then you have to do a brand new boss that you'll only ever see this one time (the "bad" choice extra episode even has the 8th level and boss be the same though).Luckily, the core gameplay loop is extremely fun, so you'll likely beat it the 3/4 times to actually beat the game, but having to do them again with so little variance really cheapens the experience. And Zangetsu is so balanced that you'll mostly be depending on him and his skill set. You have access to him every episode and episode 2 only gives you 3 characters, with the other 2 characters both having pretty severe drawbacks, so you get used to sticking to Zangetsu.I recommend the first Curse of the Moon over this one, but once you finish that game and want more, this one is more of the same with a bad aftertaste.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: The other negative reviews were right. The first game was better. This sequel can feel far more like some kind of rage game at times, by comparison.These new stages can be far more obnoxious than in the first game. Yes, we have a dog in a mech that can activate a temporary invincibility, and also momentarily hover for better platforming, but good luck if you lose that character for any reason. Worse yet, they didn't properly label the legendary difficulty, so my sad self played through episode 1 not realizing that it also fills stages with more enemies. I opted to choose veteran difficulty in subsequent episodes. However, the true problem with this game is its bosses. The first three aren't so bad, but after that, well... This is your warning. For some reason, they become unbearably trial-and-error. Hence why I say it feels like a rage game. Even worse, Gremory, the final boss of the last game, makes a return, but with more unforgiving movement patterns.As far as positives are concerned, the game has a total of 7 playable characters, 4 episodes + a mode for using only 1 character, a boss rush, and the aforementioned legendary difficulty which arguably acts like a reflection of how old games handled new game+. Achieving an ending in the final episode also allows you to choose power levels for Zangetsu from the start of a save file. The game offers a more challenging experience for anyone interested; I'm just not sure it was worth it.I haven't tried the co-op mode (yet). It may or may not be an extremely redeeming feature.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is rather fun at times but the bosses and around half the levels are absolutely terrible, they rely on incredibly strict memorization instead of reaction time and are unpredictable at times, robert as a character is too slow and ruins the pacing, hachi is comically overpowered and shatters the difficulty if he is playable. the enemies and bosses are way too fast and tanky for the controls. im someone who adores the first game and almost every single classicvania and metroidvania and i cannot earnestly recommend this game with how frustrating it is.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I loved Bloodstained: Curse of The Moon 2, this game is a lot harder than the previous entry due to its more complex platforming levels, making it harder even in Casual difficulty if the player is terrible in platforming.The new characters are great especially Dominique, but sometimes the controls feel clunky whenever I use the pogo spear on lanterns or enemies, making me unable to progress to the place I wish to go and instead use the alternate routes.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is another title that emulates the classic Castlevania games, & is very similar to the original Bloodstained: Circle of the Moon.  The main character has all of the same moves that he had in the last, & will be easy to slide into after the first.  However, improvements were made on the level design, with what seems like very few sudden hit & instant death traps, feeling a bit stronger as a result.  The bosses are still a blast to go up against, & the soundtrack hits just as good. Sadly, this game feels a little too similar to the last.  The constraints on movement while airborne, the knockback, it's all here.  There is a lower difficulty setting for those who want to escape knockback, but the larger abundance of bottomless pits shows that knockback was in the game's design.  A lot of the extra passages may also be confusing, until the final episode has been unlocked. Just like the previous title, this will be a challenge to some.  Amusingly enough, it will take 6 playthroughs of the game to clear the list, just like the last one.  Thankfully, however, it isn't as difficult, just a little time consuming.  Just bring your "A game,' & hope for some luck. This is, once again, another stellar throwback, & in many ways, a better game than the first.  Though some of the same problems still exist, they did fix many of them, making it a worthwhile sequel to grab.

_childDocuments_.review: Super good game, specially if you're looking for a retro Castlevania game. You cannot go wrong with this one.I'll give it a 9/10-Good Story and Gameplay-Good Music-Have many Replayability with 4 episode in total-Have Co-op to play with a friendIt would have been a perfect score if it weren't for this few issue that are as follow:-Game become pretty hard and unforgivable as you progress threw the game, keep in mind I was playing on veteran difficulty, which is kind of the normal difficulty and boss start to get hard to read from stage 5, 6, 7. _childDocuments_.review: While CotM1 was a fair, yet challenging instant classic with stellar and well-thought out level design, CotM2 quite simply misses the mark. Where CotM1 felt like Castlevania 3 without all the aggravating aspects of it, CotM2 nears, and oftentimes exceeds, the level of frustrating design displayed in Castlevania 3. The best way to describe the difference would be Dark Souls 1 versus Dark Souls 2. Now I love Dark Souls 2, it's arguably my favorite in the trilogy, but you cannot say with pure objectivity that the game has better level design than Dark Souls 1. Dark Souls 1 and Curse of the Moon 1 are games with tightly woven levels designed to challenge you, but not make you feel like the game is just out to get you. Dark Souls 2 and Curse of the Moon 2 are the polar opposites; everything about these games are hand-made to just piss you off and kill you in the most unfair ways imaginable, with enemy placement or traps that you cannot possibly anticipate or counter-act without throwing yourself into the meat grinder by dying and continuing over and over to "learn" what's on the road ahead.Curse of the Moon 1 learned all the right lessons from Castlevania 3, took out what didn't work, and improved on the overall concepts in the design document. Curse of the Moon 2 un-learned those aspects, and instead equated "challenge" to "let's just kill the player over and over", bringing us back to some of the worst antiquated aspects of Castlevania 3. There are redeeming aspects and improvements in CotM2, compared to CotM1, but many of them are not worth the pain and agony that is playing through CotM2's levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon was developed as a stretch goal on Kickstarter campaign for Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night. Even though I really like the main game, I've enjoyed CotM even more. The different combinations of characters you can take on your journey added a great replay value. So it was a nice surprise for me, when I've heard they are going to release this sequel.And Inti Creates did it again. The game is everything I hoped a sequel would be. The main protagonist Zangetsu is back. And this time is joined by three new characters. Dominique, a woman sent by the churh. Armed with a spear, she has a longer reach and can attack in different directons. She also jumps higher. Next one is Robert, Zangetsu's old war buddy. Armed with a gun for long range attack, but low healt bar. And last Hachi, little corgi in a giant steampunk mecha suit, that packs a hefty punch, can hover and turn invincible for a few moments. Together they go on a demon hunt through 8 stages, with a powerfull boss at the end of each one. Of course this is just a beginning. After finishing the game once, you unlock new episodes and different modes, that send you through this stages with new abilities and character combinations. At one point you also meet your 3 friends from a privious game, so you end up playing with 7 different characters. The game is full of twists and surprises, which I won't spoil. It also has a 2 player local co-op option and a great soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Moon 2 is one of those games where I really wish you could leave a "Mixed" review on Steam. There's a lot of charm to this game, but it falls short of its predecessor in some areas that really hurts the experience.Pros:- Overall tight controls- A wide variety of playable characters- A fantastic "Episode 1"- Challenging boss fightsCons:- Other episodes fall short of the first one, partially due to pure tediousness and repetition. The game expects you to play through the game 4-5 times for the full experience, and the only difference is SOME paths through the levels- The design is less carefully handled than the original Castlevania games. The existence of a character with channeled invincibility makes the developers feel justified to insert insane clusters of enemies in certain areas- Checkpoints are incredibly far apart, and losing a character on the Veteran mode (i.e. Normal) can be so devastating in certain areas (especially if you want to grab a permanent upgrade item no other characters can reach) that you need to retry from a checkpoint just to get back to grab the item- The downside of some bosses being so difficult is that while you're learning the boss, you should be prepared to hike fifty miles back to the boss when you die. This is a problem when you enjoy the difficulty but don't have the time to spare going back over and over through slow, tedious levels- The Final Episode has sloppy execution with all the backtracking you may be required to do for all upgradesThe first game has a simpler design, but it's both cheaper and more enjoyable than its sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're interested in playing Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2 (which is overall a solid game featuring great additions, especially on Final Episode + Ultimate Zangetsu), just make sure to play the console version instead. For a change, this one runs pixel perfect and you don't need to jump through hoops. But on other hand, it has game breaking bugs such as a black screen after alt tabbing and a rather frustrating multiplayer softlock that makes it impossible to carry on with the level, forcing you to restart the game. Moreover, if you want to play this game solely for its multiplayer mode, I'll let you know overall damage and HP boss scaling on the true ending episode is very broken, making some parts of the game unfun and unfair.From Blaster Master Zero 2 and 3's resolution scaling issues to these dire oversights I mentioned, Inti really needs a hand with some of their PC releases.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: "Oh no way! You get to play as a dog who rides around in a mech suit? This game's going to be awesome."I wish, I really wish I could've carried that enthusiasm with me when I finally played this. God, do I wish.I do want to stress that as much as I am about to unload a volume of issues the game suffers from, there is one part of the game I really, really love, and that's the inclusion of some cool character writing/portrayal.In between stages, there are brief cutscenes featuring the main cast sitting around a campfire where you see how they react to each other and how they grow as characters. This is especially heartwarming from Episode 2 onward, where one character realizes their biases against two others were completely unfair, to the point where they break down from the event and are soon comforted by the other member whom they viewed so dispassionately previously. With a newfound sense of determination, they begin to feel remorse for their past behavior as they set out to save their lost comrade while making up for their previous behavior with the rest of the crew.This all culminates in a genuinely great amount of build-up to the final level where the remainder of the party comes together to save their comrade, and all of this is done with barely a line of dialogue. On top of that, depending on whether or not you gain the new weapon on your run of Episode 2, you may still fail to save your comrade, and you can see how badly this impacts the party afterward, to the point where Zangetsu is the only one left initially who can still stand and make a second attempt, all because he faltered at the end, costing him even more. These scenes provide some of the best story presentation I've seen in an Inti Creates game and sincerely hope this sort of approach is the standard for their future games, as nothing else they've done compares.To top it all off, the final episode changes things up by letting you have short chats with any teammates you recruit and get more of their perspectives as a neat bonus, which update when everyone is recruited. When you reach that point, some of the dialogue gets genuinely hilarious, most notably the exchange between Zangetsu and Robert, who go full himbo and try to figure out how to light a campfire in their final destination, which features a total lack of oxygen. The campfire is a far greater concern to them than whether or not they'll be able to breathe. I love these two with all of my heart, doubly so since the madmen actually somehow succeed in making the campfire during the ending credits. Bless this cast of characters.Inti Creates finally managed to craft the best method for story-telling I've seen in a platforming game. They made the scenes brief enough to not get in the way of the gameplay, yet charming and enjoyable enough for you to want to engage with the plot. I would love to see this approach more in the future. I never felt a desire to skip any story beats I saw.Tragically, that is the end of my compliments for this game, which means the best part of the game is the part where you aren't playing it.Here we go.The thing that blows my mind the most is that Curse of The Moon 1 took the approach of "What if we remade Castlevania 3 to be reasonable in its difficulty and pacing while also giving the player more freedom in how they play the game?" and it was pulled off with aplomb. I still feel it's one of the best games Inti Creates has ever made, and I don't just mean that comparatively, it's genuinely a fantastic game.Then Curse of The Moon 2 just unlearns everything the first game did right and goes back to being Castlevania 3 again, but with more repetition, a comparable amount of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, most notably enemies that are placed just in the right spot to screw you, and made every playthrough more obnoxious than the last.That's not even including the boss design of this game. If stage 5 somehow doesn't make you want to stop playing, the Mummy boss from stage 6 probably will. If you do play this game and find yourself hating the Mummy boss, just stop playing, because it is only going to get EXPONENTIALLY WORSE during your playthroughs of Episode 2 onward, where things just become completely unreasonable, especially for the Mummy boss and the boss that comes after it, which wouldn't you know it, is also the one and only boss from the first game nobody liked, now with more health. Fun."But Ultimate Mode fixes the game!"No, it doesn't. Even if you go the most optimal route to unlock Ultimate Mode asap, you still have to beat the game 3 times in increasingly harder formats with a worse weapon for Zangetsu for the majority of those 3 playthroughs. You did all of that just to make an incredibly frustrating game somewhat more tolerable, which goes back to being frustrating if Zangetsu dies at any point since he's the only character Ultimate Mode improves.Ultimate Mode is definitely a better way to experience the game, but it doesn't erase how frustrating and obnoxious my time with the game was prior to unlocking. As much as I'd like to say it makes up for it, I don't feel it does. Asking someone to play through a game 3 times just to start having a better time with it is a tall order and one I don't see many people having the patience for. Even I got burned out by the final episode. It's just too much repetition.I could spend another few paragraphs easily on how this game also features the most shockingly awful shmup sequence I've ever played in a video game, which was chock-full of "Wait, what just killed me?" moments due to how many of the most basic and important rules of shmup gameplay were disregarded. I even recorded footage of the segment to review later so I could see what did, and it still took me multiple viewings to notice the culprits for my deaths. It was always something that blended in with my own attacks (THIS SHOULD NEVER HAPPEN IN A SHMUP) All this segment did was provide me with more reason to believe that people who don't work on shmups should not add shmup gameplay/attacks into their games. Inti falls into this category, for the record. It shows. It really, really shows.It's examples like these that make the game so frustrating to me. There is good content buried beneath the bad, but my God, there's so much bad stuff you have to dig through, and it makes it so much harder to enjoy as a result. Play the first game, then look up the campfire scenes, dialogue, and soundtrack for this game. If you do decide to play this, I implore you to play on Casual difficulty if for no other reason than to at least have more reasonable checkpoint placement.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Being I'm in self imposed debtor's prison when it comes to my entertainment budget, I started to revisit older games. Curse of the moon 2 was on that list!If you know me you know anything inspired by the classic Castlevanias or the Igavanias that came afterwards ends up in my library eventually! So how does Curse Of The Moon 2 fare next to it's predecessor?I put 9 hours into this strangely beautiful and engrossing hell-pit abomination and completed most of the story routes. Impressive considering I thought I'd never get there. Even if you play this on casual difficulty it is still a merciless murder machine!Regardless Zangetsu is joined by a new cast of characters. There's Dominique which is the typical sexy "librarian battle nun" whom wields a dragoon spear and various magics. There's Robert whom is a retired soldier big on using a sniper rifle along with his traps and bombs. Then there's Hachi,a cute corgi that pilots a furnace powered steam-punk battle mech! Yeah,it's obvious Inti creates and Iga had "fun" here,combining the grim-dark-goth-fantasy tone the game has overall with some tongue and cheek humor. (Which is "good" because you are going to need a few therapeutic laughs to trudge through the game's toughest most ridiculous bosses and treacherous terrains!)The time line as is follows.....-Zangetsu and his friends fight thru demon hordes until Dominique is kidnapped. This means you have to do the consecutive play thru without her. (Which sucks because she had a nice nature based healing spell that created fruits of vitality from a growing vine.)-To continue on the higher road you have to do a side quest to collect various mystic swords hidden away in miscellaneous areas for Zangetsu. If you fail to do this it leads down another darker path.-Finally after you do all the above,Miriam,Gebel,and Alfred from the first game can finally be acquired to stop the demon invasion fleet from the moon. To do that you have to collect  components to make a space-ship that looks like a bigger version of Hachi's mech. If you meticulously complete every zone in this run you will get to unlock ALL the protagonists. (Both old and new alike!) Later you will pilot the assembled space-ship in a bullet-hell section before facing off against the penultimate eldritch evil!Being this is an old skool action platformer using very minimalist retro ways to convey its'' story nothing above trespasses into spoiler territory. There have already been numerous speed runs,lore dumps,and let's plays of COTM2 so I'm just revealing a few hints on what you have to do to unlock the "true" ending. But is Circle Of The Moon 2 "better" than its predecessor? It depends. For one thing, it can be more frustrating. The original had a straight to the point forwardness that was refreshing. Yes, it still had multiple routes and multiple endings "but" you were not stuck replaying through nearly as much content. I also thought it's difficulty curve was much more fair. Challenging to be sure but at no point did I feel completely overwhelmed. (Unlike COTM 2 that I had to put down for awhile and then come back to later to fully appreciate it.)However, if you want bang for your buck,"more" of what the original offered,a larger cast of playable characters,and a steeper challenge with twice as many ghastly ghouls and intimidating screen-filling demon over-lords then yes,it is totally worth the price tag!Pros+Newly introduced characters are enjoyable to play as.+Much more content than the original+Equally memorable soundtrack+Varied routes and even a few unlockables+Miriam,Alfred,and Gebel eventually return to partner up with the newer protagonists.Cons-More unforgiving difficulty spikes (Even on casual)-More retreading -If you prefer a shorter compact "retro" experience COTM2 comes off as being long in the tooth.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, I have got all achievements in the game and I think it's about time to write a review.Short version: Less is more.Long version: Gameplay:Just like the first game, the controls feel really tight and all characters have their own unique abilities. You have your main weapons and your sub-weapons. The levels all have multiple pathways for your to take, each with their own unique enemies. There have been a few additions like "pink candles" which drop hearts for health refill. We also have more episodes this time around. The first one is your classic Curse of the Moon action, the second one is your nightmare mode but this time we have 2 endings, episode extra which is basically the same game with the cast of the first game and finally the final episode which is a megaman X set up where you choose your stage.The difficulty is a bit harder this time around, more akin to Castlevania 3 and to be honest, at times it was just frustrating.Presentation:Sprite work is as good as it was in the first game, and might even be better at certain instances. That being said, I am not really the biggest fan of the music. I am not sure if someone else worked on this game but I can't remember a single track as they all sound the same. We also have these really cool mini cutscenes between each stage which is a nice addition.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Like classic games but wish they had a little bit of modern in them? Try the Curse of the moon games. This time around you get 3 new comrades and end up with a total 7 characters to swap between on the fly in the end game. If you liked Curse 1 you'll definitely like Curse 2 with its fresh ideas and harder difficulty. Oh and did i mention you can play locally with a friend?
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I praised the first game for being better than the nes games it was paying homage to but sadly this game falls into the same old nes tropes like cheap enemy placement. And I don't know why they went with press and hold for Hachi's hover ability instead of just being able to tap the button in the air because the majority of the time it activates when you don't want it to. This game also cranks the difficulty through the roof while the first game was tough but not so overbearing. Losing a party member is a lot more detrimental, for example there are these charging spearmen that zangetsu can duck under the spear to land a hit but hachi is just too big to kill them without taking damage so depending on who you have left you might just be screwed. Another example is the several fast moving enemies that Robert takes multiple shots to kill as he's almost 100% gonna take a hit with his stationary reload animation. All it takes is one cheaply placed enemy to drop you in a pit and you're stuck with a character that can't handle the enemies in the room and you might as well just game over to get everyone back. And lastly the boss design.....bosses on the first play through are fair and fun to fight and it feels really good once you learn the pattern and take them down. Bosses on the 2nd play through and beyond are just "hey what if the entire arena was on fire except this tiiiiiiiiny little spot here" and the timing to dodge some of the attacks is just too short.Long story short it's another sequel that couldn't live up to the first game. Mind you I'm no gaming god by far but I did 100% the first game and enjoyed doing it. With this game however, I had fun the 1st play through, had to force myself to finish the last half of the 2nd, and just lost interest not long after the start of the 3rd.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is alright  and are looking for more classic Castlevania.  It feels a lot like Castlevania 3 and the first cotm.  I played on casual mode.  I wanted to do Veteran difficulty but wished there was an option between these 2 difficulties that still caused monsters to knock me backwards, but with unlimited continues.  I did like playing more hardcore with the level memorization when it came to  though, but these levels are quite a bit bigger and more sprawling.  The character swapping seemed to work well, though I think I actually prefer a sole protagonist to swapping between the different characters that each have their own tricks and HP bars.  In any case, it was a fine time.  I didn't unlock the secret stuff and there is plenty of replayability with the ability to replay the levels taking different routes, and on the higher, more intended difficulty settings.  Another incentive for replaying these stages is to find and collect all of the upgrades to make your heroes stronger.  For me personally, unless I was stuck here with just this game and nothing else, I just don't have the love/drive/motivation to want to grind and live that all out properly.CoTM 2 is great at what it sets out to do, albeit it nothing groundbreaking obviously, being a solid NES game (albeit with better graphics etc) in 2020.

_childDocuments_.review: It is unfortunate that I cannot recommend this game, seeing as I loved the first bloodstained COTM, and the Metroidvania-style ROTN. I want to like this game, it's very colorful, and the cast of characters is larger with unique play-styles. That all being said, the level design in this game is purely frustrating, along with some of the bosses just being utterly un-fun to fight against, even when you know what to do. Entire levels feel hampered if you lack certain characters, certain bosses are a complete slog to fight against, and it has some of the most frustrating end-game areas ever. Even switching to the casual mode doesn't make some of these boss fights any better, and that's with the game cheating in your favor... I gave up beating act 2 on the final boss, simply because the "fight 8 eyeballs firing grim reaper pattern orbs" annoyed me to no end. In the end, I can only see this game as annoying and frustrating, rather than a welcome challenge. If the first game could be said to perhaps be too easy, this one is too frustrating. I realize not everyone feels that way, and good on you if rose to the challenge, but this wasn't what I was looking for.-----------------------------------------------It's been a while since I posted this review. I've gone on to 100% the achievements. I stand by my general statements that it can be a slog at times, and seems geared towards co-op in a way I can't really DO (none of my friends wanna play ;-; ) But all in all, I did get my money's worth and had a good time with this game. Took a pandemic and bashing my head against it for a while to click, but it did eventually... This game is great for co-op, just the right level of hard for it, though if you are solo'n it expect to suffer

_childDocuments_.review: Just like for its predecessor, you expect a modern castlevania III, you get a modern castlevania III.A really good game with just the right balance between retro and 2020 game design philosophies.Multiple characters to alternate between on the fly, each with their own ability, similarly to CotM1.Zangetsu makes his return and gets new allies as you progress, and you can play as RotN's best girl, Dominique!This time, their playstyles are more varied and further reward character mastery. A good player will swap constantly to get the most out of each. For instance, .Due to this, CotM2 is much more unforgiving, and focused on high risk & reward, which might put off some and please others. Losing a character gimps you heavily and can prevent you from using level shortcuts, but lowers maximum boss health by 25%.The game has a lot of quality content for what it's worth. The game and level design are (most of the time) really tight and mindful, the spritework looks great and the soundtrack blows its predecessor's out of the water with even more memorable tracks.It's polished, has a lot of nice gotcha moments and has a decent lifespan of 5-8hrs for the first Episode.Very safe buy if you've already played the first retro Bloodstained (better to, but not mandatory), like nostalgia games or castlevania-likes.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10A great sequel to an already great game.COTM2, for the most part, doesn't try to reinvent the wheel compared to the first game - the main differences are the addition of new characters and one new ability for Zangetsu, along with some very small adjustments, like the Casual difficulty no longer causing the character to flinch when taking damage. This is a good thing, as the gameplay from the first game already felt satisfying.However, I say "for the most part" because COTM2 includes a 2 player mode. I haven't tried it out myself, but from what I've seen, it seems to be quite fun and well done.While the game is still pretty repetitive, it's a bit less so than the previous game and there are also more upgrades to be found along the way, with one chapter in special having each stage be replayable before the conclusion, allowing for all upgrades to be obtained.The OST for this game is even better than the first one, which is an accomplishment by itself. Some of the tracks from this game are incredible.COTM2 also has one of the most epic boss fights and moments I've played recently, when trying to achieve a specific ending during the last chapter of the game - one moment so great (and accompanied by one of the best tracks in the game) that I replayed it a few times just so I could re-experience it.My main issue with the game is the boss design. While the first game felt more fair in terms of bosses, COTM2 feels like they got carried away designing some of these bosses. At times there are so many things going on at once in the screen that it feels near impossible to get through some of these bosses without taking a few hits.That said, still an easy recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: For Fans of the first game, this entry offers more of every aspect compared to the original and you probably already own it, if you don't own it yet, it's a no brainer.For newcomers, judging this type of game by its graphics as lazy and low effort, is the absolute worst thing you can do.TL;DR: IGA-SAAAAAAAAAAN!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: COTM2 is a decent game but it's game design doesn't feel like a Vania. COTM2 is trying more it's own thing as the stage layouts and enemy designs don't reflect what an old Vania would be like. COTM1 nailed the game design aspect and difficulty, being hard but easy to master. COTM2 has overly sporadic enemy & boss designs along with some questionable enemy placement. It's not that I don't like hard games, I've beaten CV3 and the NES Ninja Gaidens, but the difficulty needs to be fair and balanced when it comes to enemy placement and designs. COTM2's stages range from too little enemies to too many enemies at once and the stage layouts feel way less inspired and polished than COTM1. There's still fun to be had, and I haven't tried to co-op, but not nearly as good as COTM1 or even ROTN (even though thats an Igavania). Presentations still great though!
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: 1) Overpowered characters, 2) but still extremely challenging, 3) but also so fair that everything can be beaten with any character without special abilities. You would think this balance would be impossible to achieve, but these are the traits that define Curse of the Moon 2 to me. It shows that Inti creates know what they're doing when it comes to 2D action games. A bit more detail on this:Almost everything is a small step up from the first Curse of the Moon. Backgrounds and boss spites/animations are more beautiful than ever. In fact, despite stiff competition, I think this game has the best 8-bit inspired graphics out there. Then you have the intricately designed levels, with more devilish enemy placement and alternate routes sometimes requiring more interesting use of specific abilities. The only thing I'm mixed on is the music, which just didn't stand out as much as the tracks in the first game did. The Bloodstained series is extremely blessed to have such a high-quality, linear action series to be their "Classicvania".  In fact, in some ways I appreciate the Curse subseries more than the metroidvania main series, because while there are many great metroidvanias released every year there are very few linear action games with the Castlevania-style committed jumps and restrained walk-speed. Inti brought their own design principles to this subgenre, which means I am reluctant to compare them directly to Dracula's Curse and Rondo of Blood (they feel different in small but significant ways and will never say that Curse replaces those classics) I do believe that Curse of the Moon 2 is in the very top tier of this style of action game, probably the best we've had for 25+ years.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: So here we are again, back in to the 8-bit fray. If you enjoyed the original game, there's more fun and alternate paths to be had here. The game starts you off being hand glided on to some mysterious floating demon castle and Zangetsu must slash and dash his way through hordes of monsters, golems and other assorted creatures of the night... all with a new support cast, and I must say, some of them are down right broken.This game does more of the same from the original except it breaks it down in to steps to really extend the life of the game. Honestly the game doesn't even really begin until you hit the very final episode, the first 3 chapters are more like a training mode. I will break it down for you here: You start as Zangetsu all gimped in his normal form, no double jumps, no dashing and no allies. The first episode is pretty tame and after every stage you'll acquire a new ally who save you from the bosses "final attack". Unfortunately this time, you don't have an option of whether or not you want to leave them, take them with you or down right murder them and absorb their energy to strengthen Zangetsu. Instead you kind of just romp around and get used to the new characters mechanics and see what they can do for you. (Hachi is bae) Okay so now that you've conquered training mode, the real game begins except you're down a member just like in the original (well sort of) and you must complete the game with 3 characters right from the start. The bosses all have new / extended patterns and their final attacks can no longer be skipped and must be manually evaded. There is an optional mission during Episode 2, where if all alternate paths are taken, it can net Zangetsu a new sword so he can combo attack and his sub weapons all acquire upgrades as well. (Still no dash or double jump though) The old cast reunites and you'll be traversing all the stages once again on a 3rd path only the original cast can access. It's mostly Gebal that has access to these new paths but Miriam and Alfred shine in 1 or 2 stages. It's a bit harder not having Hachi around but Gebal is a decent alternative and Alfred's Lightning attack makes quick work of bosses. So basically once you're done all of the tutorial modes and have practiced the ins and outs of every single stage / boss with every possible character configuration, you're now ready for this. This, as far as I'm concerned is the true version of the game and the way it was meant to be played from the start. You will start with Zangetsu in a hub like area and you can choose any of the 7 stages to play, in any order and can also revisit them all. 6 of the 7 stages will be associated with a companion and they will accompany you through the stage. Once the stage is complete you will obtain a key item and that companion will join you for the rest of the adventure. You will have to play through each stage multiple times as this mode keeps track of all of the stages power ups, and yes, you can acquire every single one of them (14 in total, 2 per stage) but you'll need Gebal, Hachi and Miriam at the very least, so recruit them first. After this mode is complete you unlock the option to use Ultimate Zangetsu in any episode you want, which means you can dash, combo and double jump. (A bit too late but there it is)There's also a bonus mode you can unlock where you can choose to play the entire game as any ONE character and only that character for a true challenge. Basically there's not much to be said here except that it cheapens the entire experience. Take that for what you will, I enjoyed it, it's a very enjoyable mode and makes the game a lot less frustrating and will help you bond more with whoever you're playing it with. This mode allows both players to play as Zangetsu, a Red and Blue version, as well as switch between any characters you've acquired along the way. You can use an assist mode at any time to save yourself from damage or a fatal pit fall by just hitting a series of buttons and your avatar will warp and hover around the other character. If there's a hard section coming up and one of you isn't so good at the game, you can just take a break and let the other player do all the work. You can exploit this on bosses as well if you're about to take damage.Another great feature is being able to reach otherwise hard to reach shortcuts by just standing on the other persons head and jumping. Places that only Dominique can reach, can be reachable by any character using this method. It's worth it for the co-op alone.  It's definitely a longer game than the original.  There's a lot of replay value here if you're looking to play it solo, with a friend or even challenge yourself to veteran mode or single character mode.  The possibilities are near endless for what custom challenges you want to present yourself with. The achievements are all really easy to obtain and it's a very fun experience. The music doesn't stand out quite as well as the original game did but it's decent enough.  More 8-bit goodness, just a bit more watered down in terms of challenge. The game does become tiresome playing the same batch of stages over and over again and the first 3 episodes are essentially tutorial stages.  It's marred a bit by Zangetsu being a total gimp until the game is fully complete but other than that, it's a solid experience.There are some things I would improve upon, if they ever make another sequel, but until then, great game! It's a definite must buy for any self respecting old school Castlevania fan!
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'll come out and say it: I am not particularly fond of Curse of the Moon 1. Half of that game's levels just , the game doesn't feel like it's actually designed around how broken your party's moves are. It's towards the end that that game becomes more fun, but by then it's already over. The whole thing goes by very quickly anyway.But I thought that was fine, it was a small bonus for people interested in Ritual of the Night. And I loved that game, so no complaints from me. It was no Castlevania 3, Rondo, Bloodlines, or even Castlevania 1 or Adventure ReBirth but it wasn't .Suddenly, this thing gets announced out of nowhere, and with barely any time before it actually comes out. And come out it did. I decided to pick it up, because why not. I didn't have the highest expectations but CotM1 was still fun.I can safely say this game is on another level compared to 1.Mainly, the new characters have more interesting abilities, and levels are much more fleshed out (and also harder). The bosses are still very good. The visuals are just as good, and in general this is just a blast to play. My one gripe is the music - it's competent, but not much of it particularly stands out. Were this any other series, I'd just leave it at "yeah, it's fine", but compare this to any Castlevania soundtrack, or even CotM1. I'm not that big on CotM1's OST too but it still had a couple of pretty iconic songs. It does still serve its purpose though, and I never feel like I have to mute the game or anything.Curse of the Moon 2's design philosophy elevates it beyond "Castlevania 3 clone" and really into its own thing imo. Instead of seeing it as 4 different characters, pretend that you're just one character with 4 health bars and 4 different movesets. With how much you'll be switching back and forth every step of the way, you may as well just be one clustered character. CotM2 really forces you to strategise starting fairly early on, and thus you're always on your toes, thinking of the most effective way to get rid of a new problem with your vast array of attacks, range, subweapons, etc. Castlevania 3 did not lend itself that well to this because it took 10000 years to change between characters, and you can do this in CotM1 too, but that game never really requires it.I have seen people claiming that this game is "as hard as Castlevania 3". While I'm still on my 4th playthrough of this, and have not finished every mode/episode yet, I would disagree. It is challenging for sure, but you're given all the tools you could possibly need to handle whatever you want. The game is very manageable once you come up with adequate ways to tackle particularly troublesome parts. Definitely not a cakewalk, and it's fairly thought out. Harder than CotM1 for sure.Oh yeah, the plot exists lol. Yeah I've barely been paying attention to that, especially with how CotM1 and RotN have nothing to do with each other plot-wise anyway.This is an easy 9/10 game for me, and gameplay-wise, this is up there with Castlevania's best imo. The missing point is just the music being merely "good" and not "extraordinary". Great game! Consider it even if you weren't that big on CotM1 too like me, as this one actually has meat on its bones.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon and Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night it is more than safe to say Koji Igarashi cannot make a bad "Castlvania" game. From what I have played so far in this new title it is better than the first which was already great in my opinion, but that speaks volumes. The music once again has that really cool Famicon Disk sounding audio to it which I do adore as it reminds me of true retro classics. This developer isn't playing never have I seen an update to fix an issue within hours of the initial release... that's dedication. Also a Corgi in a Mech suit is the wildest thing ever in this series!

As good (or even better) as the first game, with more paths to take in levels, more ways to play, and both crews tackle levels and take different secret routes, there is a lot more reason to play this game repeatedly than the first game, especially with more modes, more teams, and a last episode that feels really tacked on but has a badass ending if you finish only with zangetsu, honestly after you beat the final episode once you can ignore it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Ritual of the Night and the first Curse of the Moon so I got this game to complete my collection. What I got was a game that was mostly better than its predecessor with a few shortcomings. The best improvement was the boss fights. The fights are quick, the bosses come with health bars to track your progress, and if an ally dies you don't have to start ALL over again (the boss's health is still depleted) until all your allies die. The cast of characters are unique and balanced, and very fun to play as. My favourite addition is Hachi, a corgi who rides a tank that allows you to fly and be invincible for a short period. The game is tough as hell (stage 7 requires precision platforming and the final boss fights get increasingly harder), but the more you play, the better you get at it. I wasn't sure if I was going to LOVE the game after episode 2, but the final episode had some really awesome surprises that made me glad I kept playing. If you're a huge fan of old school hard as hell NES style games then this is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: When compared to the original it just feels clunky. There are some improvements to the systems but the levels feel worse. The decisions are not as impactful. Episode 2 just feels painful. There are plenty of slow bosses that force too much reliance on their patterns unless you want to just Corgi power through it. And then it doesn't give a sense of satisfaction. Difficult games are good when there is satisfaction when you overcome the challenge, but this doesn't really have that. The levels feel insanely slow if you aren't following 'their intended route' and creativity in playthrough falls to the side. Too many cycle platforms in later levels just grinds progress to slow n steady.I mean, this game isn't horrendously bad, but there is just more interesting things out there to play right now.

_childDocuments_.review: My only two beefs with this game are the lack of volume adjustment in the main menu and the way the revival item works.The game is lacking it's own internal volume controls so if it happens to be obnoxiously loud for you (which it is for me), you have to turn down your system volume. For me, this means I also have to turn it back up when I'm done playing because it makes my system too quiet.As for the "revival" beef... there is only one item that will let you revive dead party members, and it's relatively rare. This is fine in and of itself, but it also happens to be an item only ONE character, Dominique, can use... and if she's dead, you're legitimately ♥♥♥♥♥♥.This almost discourages you from playing her at all, since you want to keep her alive in case you need to revive anyone else in your party and mistakes with her become way too costly. I don't know what they were going for with this decision, but I don't think it was worth it.That said, it's a great game and still worth a try. If you have a friend who already has it, ask them to let you co-op with them a bit so you can essentially try it for free!

_childDocuments_.review: If you dig the first one, then this is a must.  If you are a Castlevania fan who dreams of a new Castlevania game that dosen't suck ass, then this is a must.  If you are jonesing for a new retro style platformer, then you have to get this.  It's great.  Even if you weren't so impressed with Ritual of the Night, i would get this.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little NES style castlevania clone. You get multiple party members each with different attacks and abilities and switch between them for certain situations. The stages are varied, and theres some secrets and upgrades. Many of the items you pick up arent explained at all which can be annoying. Also the mech's hover ability is super finnicky and never found out how to consistently get him to do it. The bosses are well done too. But the game is short and after you beat it then you think there's more episodes but its just replaying the same game again, but this time with 1 less party member, and for some reason with all your upgrades gone which is about the dumbest thing ever. So its the same bosses, same levels, etc. The jumping is also a bit finnicky and theres too many instant death traps but overall the game is decent. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Moon returns with a more ambitious riff on the Dracula's Curse mechanics and adds in a steampunk Big O mech piloted by a Corgi because why the hell not.The sequel expands your different character options, and there's parts where you're more directly encouraged to use specific characters to traverse the stages and manage resources, and that's pretty rad, all told. The individual characters are more unique and not the Dracula's Curse stand-ins from the previous game (not that they were bad, just derivative of the CV3 alternates) and have a lot of interesting attack and movement options that are pretty easy to pick up and encourage mastery and creative usage, and I enjoy that. There is no crime in giving a player a character a robust selection of attack and movement options and letting them determine their best path through a stage, rather than creating room after room that demands you use the method the programmer intended and nothing else.Do I like it as much as the first? The graphics are more colorful, the characters more unique, and the concepts from the first have been expanded on. That's pretty cool. At the moment, I like them both equally, mainly because they're just compulsively fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: While in some ways better than the first one, other problems mar this game. Good - Lots of character variety- Fairly good controls- The whole gang is here plus new characters- Very difficult challenge- 2 Player mode is very funBad- Game feels cheap in terms of difficulty. A lot of stuff is very planned out to kill you. You're going to die a lot. Also, stage 6 and 7 are just insanely difficult compared to the others. Definitely that "old school" BS.- Controls while they work have archiac symptoms. Most of your moves need utmost precision to come out. The game requires way too much perfection on your part to accomplish the tasks. I especially hate how down and up inputs for moves have to be EXACTLY in that direction for them to come out. You can't do diagonals on them. Also, the flight mechanic with the dog character just feels kinda off with having to hold the button to fly. Just a personal gripe.- Stages are WAY TOO LONG. Check points are far between which affects pacing. At times, losing a character felt like it was pointless to continue outside gaining money for lives as I wouldn't be able to beat bosses with just 1 or 2 characters. The games feels designed for 2 players, not really 1.- Game speed is SLOW. Not my particular cup of tea. Love the "Metroidvania" versions of castlevania much more than the classic ones. Give me Symphony of the Night over this.- The music feels like a big step back compared to the first game. None of the tracks really felt like they stood out in any amazing way. - The "replayability" of this game feels a bit lacking. You literally play the same levels over and over (5 times I believe) to get all the endings. While you may play different characters, I would like to play different stages. After 2 times of doing the same thing, I really had no desire to do it again. The game just feels dated in a lot of bad ways as it is trying way too hard to replicate Castlevania 3 in every single way while adding a lot of nuance.As much as i love the Castlevania franchise, I just wasn't feeling it with this one very much. It felt like a big step back in a lot of ways which kind of ruined the experience. I'll stick to Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like classicvania games or action platformers, this game is for you.Curse of the Moon 2 includes much more content than the first game, requiring multiple playthroughs to see everything. The game is divided into episodes, and although they share most of their stages, the challenges stay fresh through changed enemy placement, different sets of playable characters, and access to different branching paths within the levels.The difficulty is also increased from the first, an improvement as the first felt too easy for large portions of it. Legend difficulty in particular feels very close to the difficulty of the NES castlevanias. The difficulty increase was done very fairly, there were very few instances where I felt something was truly out of my control and I was not at fault for my death, although checkpoint placement can feel a bit brutal if you're playing on legend.The music and sprite art are also excellent, and the little details and hidden interactions, such as the "stylish" way to finish the 1st and 3rd bosses, make it clear that a lot of love was put into making this game.I highly recommend this to anyone who likes classicvania or action platformers in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this is a fantastic follow-up to the first game.  If you like 8-bit platformers, you owe it to yourself to play Curse of the Moon, and if you liked it, you need to play CotM2.CotM adds three new side characters, all of whom are more varied than the original cast.  It's longer than the first, too, and has a wider variety of stages, and quite a bit of replay value thanks to multiple routes through stages and different arrangements of party members.  The only real caveat is that it does get quite a bit harder than the original; Stage 6's boss is arguably harder than the first game's last boss, and the game only proceeds to get more difficult on Episode 2 and further.  Even "Casual" mode can be quite difficult.  Don't be discouraged, though, because there's always a way to dodge everything, and with practice and study, everything is doable.The only thing that really disappointed me is the music.  It's not bad, but it's definitely not as good as the original, and really only one of the stage themes has gotten stuck in my head.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of review, I've unlocked all available in-game options and achievements. I only played on the Veteran difficulty for perspective. I did not play any co-op, so I can't speak about that experience. Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2 is the sequel to the kickstarter companion game, Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon (as you might expect). Apparently, the first game was liked so much, Inti opted in for a sequel. I'm not complaining though since I genuinely liked the first game.Curse of the Moon takes on a retro aesthetic with modern twists added in and the sequel is no different. If you're familiar with NES Castlevania games, Dracula's Curse in particular, then you'll probably enjoy this one. From the start, you can choose from two difficulties: Casual and Veteran. The key differences between the two difficulties to my knowledge are lives and knockback. You have unlimited lives on Casual, but you're limited on Veteran. For what it's worth, the game is rather generous about lives if you play carefully. The main difficulty of Veteran comes from the classic knockback. In old school Castlevania, taking damage meant that your character was knocked backwards in the air. That might not sound like a big deal, but in a platformer, a single hit could mean death by pit. I'm used to it from playing the older games, so I have nostalgic patience. I would certainly understand why folks would hate it though.For characters, you begin the game with Zangetsu, a relatively tanky swordsman with a standard jump. As you progress through the game, you meet new characters that have specific abilities such as higher jumps, long range attacks, and ground pounding. You're able to switch characters at will to get the most out of each character's individual skills. It might sound odd, but when you get the hang of it, you can do some pretty cool movement tricks. Fortunately, the transition is instant and doesn't take long to pull off like the NES-era. To top it off, each level has multiple paths that can be explored if you have the right character to bypass an obstacle. Each character can also pick up specific sub-weapons. These weapons require magic and all of the characters share the same magic pool, so careful use between the characters is important. And really, that's about it for the gameplay. It focuses on platforming simplicity and it does it pretty well.The soundtrack was decent, but nothing memorable I'd say. Really, I don't have much to say on it. It exists. Eh.The story is interesting enough for a game like this. It goes completely "video game" on the player in two particular sections, which I won't spoil here, but they both got a laugh out of me (a good laugh that is). I'd say the biggest downside to this game is the "replayability factor." To get the most out of the game (including achievements), I believe you need to play it at least 6 times through. Unfortunately, it felt like padding at that point. Games like these are often short enough to replay, but 6 times was a bit much to see everything. That's just a personal gripe though. It's not a deal breaker. There were also a couple of bosses that felt more annoying than they needed to be, but again, personal gripe. Nothing awful.All in all, I'd recommend the game. My first playthrough took about 2.5 hours and all subsequent playthroughs were faster due to my increasing knowledge in the game. I'd probably say to pick the game up on sale. It's worth a runthrough.

In last episode multiple times the same level to get all the upgrade and collect all characters. I didn't bother to finish it. I fill really mix on this one.
