_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Liked the first one? Buy this one then, it's goodDid you enjoy the first game? If yes, then most likely you'll like this one too. It's basically what made the first game good, but improved upon, with new level design, new characters, bosses but still familiar enough that you won't feel weird to jump right to it in this one... You get the picture by now. Even if it is a bit pricier when compared to the first game, it's still very much worth getting it.If I had to say, the one thing that caught me by surprise is the difficulty. Generally speaking both the enemies/Bosses and the level design pose a significant challenge over the first game, and I'm not even done with this one, can't wait till I get to the later bosses and compare them to the ones in CotM.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this game on PS4 and got all the achievements. I wanted to replay it, so I bought it again. This is like Curse of the Moon but longer & harder - while the original game was way too easy even on the hardest mode, this game has many difficult rooms. Sometimes, it even feels a little too much, but in general it skirts the BS line pretty well. I also appreciate how the final chapter works and how you accomplish extra endings.This is one of my favourite Inti games overall, but you definitely need to enjoy frustration to tolerate the later stages.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great like the first game if not more enjoyable! The game is harder than the original but to compensate the new party members are much more powerful (with Robert and Hachi being especially broken). The ability to kill your party members is gone and with it an episode system that streamlines the 2nd and 3rd playthroughs. This is a downgrade from the original but because the new characters are so busted it softens the tedium of playing the entire game again (that and the bosses get to be actual threats the 2nd time through. 6th stage boss will test your limits). Overall roughly equal in game quality to that of the first one, but the added widescreen makes this my preferred COTM. Highly recommend to someone who loves the first game, to everyone else play the first it's cheaper and not as hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: A sequel that pretty much surpasses the original in every way. Fun new characters to play as on top of the classic ones. More game modes, and some insanely satisfying final bosses. Yeah, Final Bosses, plural. You thought things got crazy with the alternate final boss in CotM 1's Nightmare Mode? You haven't seen anything yet.Lots of people are whining about Stage 6's boss being too hard. Honestly he's not that bad. Hard? Yes. Hard enough to warrant a refund of the game? Heck no. If you liked the original and you like Classic (pre Metroidvania) Castlevania? Get this already.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked CotM1, you're going to love CotM2.- A lot of content to unlock.- Many characters to play as and they all have unique abilities.- Co-op play through local or Remote Play.- An amazing soundtrack.- Very tight and responsive controls.- The same stages are used over and over.- As mentioned below, there is a critical bug when opening screen saver settings while the game is running.- No native online support. In a game about precise timing, Remote Play doesn't cut it.I did manage to get the second controller working during Remote Play with my friend. I do have all the "configuration support" settings enabled in Steam's controller settings.1. I started the game and invited him to join.2. Both our controller icons in Remote Play were highlighted. Mine was mapped to slot 1. His was mapped to slot 2.3. Select "Detect Controllers" in the in-game options menu.4. Then configure controls for controller 2 and the remote player should be able to configure their controls.Game plays okay but I noticed the following issues:- Opening up screen saver settings breaks the game. You have to open Task Manager to close the game.- I couldn't get player 2 controller to work for my friend during Remote Play. He had to be player 1 on keyboard and I had to be player 2. Playing on keyboard is not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: For those who are new to the genre, Curse of the Moon is one of those brutally hard old school platformers where you'll die often due to a lack of mastery over your spacing and timing. It starts out fairly tame but the difficulty will ramp up forcing you to use everything at your disposal to get through on your first-playthough. Fortunately, you get multiple characters meaning more options and health bars which makes things a little easier. Basically, it's one of those games where it's hard as hell but satisfying when you finally beat it. While not a requirement, having played Curse of the Moon 1 and Ritual of the Night makes Curse of the Moon will make the game just a little bit better. For those who played Curse of the Moon 1, If you liked the first game and want more, Curse of the moon 2 is quite good. This game managed to one up the first game and went to places I did not expect.It takes at least 3 playthroughs to get to the very end and at least 6 to get all the achievements. While you will replay levels often, Curse of the Moon 2 places a bigger emphasis on alternate routes so you will get a slightly different experience each time. After the second playthough however, boss patterns mostly stay the same and any new experiences will come from fighting them with different party compositions.In short, it's what you'd expect from a sequel, more of the same with some new mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite challenging and requires using the right skill and strategy at the right time, with the right characters. The stage aesthetics are as atmospheric and as good as the first game, and I liked how the stage transition scenes are animated in this game. The three new characters' subweapon choice is also quite great and unique, and I also like Zangetsu's powered-up subweapon forms.The Episodes provide a variety of routes in the same stage, and the final bosses of all episodes are definitely not pushovers - when used properly, tactics can make short work of them. I have played this game for over two years and will definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the harder difficulty, I generally enjoyed this more than the first CotM game. The new characters bring some new gameplay elements to the series and the stages are designed more to cater to their unique abilities. Difficulty can vary wildly in the game from area to area and upon which game mode you use. Casual is on the easier side while veteran is on the more difficult side (like Castlevania 3 kind of hard).There's plenty to do in the game once you start unlocking the various game episodes. My only real criticism is the 8 standard stages which you will be replaying a LOT and by the Final Episode you'll be kind of sick of replaying them for the umpteenth time.Overall, it's a good game for those looking for a retro style platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the first game, so I was really surprised and excited when I found out they were making a sequel. I am pretty critical when it comes to reviews. So far Curse of the Moon 2 has done nothing but deliver. They took alot of elements from the first game and build on them for the second game. Some of the visuals are just so great for a 2D old school side scroller. I am almost finished beating it and have been very entertained so far.  Some people gave this game some bad reviews and I don't understand why. This game is great for the price they are asking.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Moon 2 is an excellent follow-up to the first Curse of the Moon.  The challenge level feels a little higher than the first game, but it doesn't feel like an unfair game.  All the bosses follow patterns that are learnable after awhile.  It's nice to play a new retro Castlevania game again.  The game needs more levels.  There are multiple play throughs to get the whole story, but only a limited amount of levels
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I had just read about this game coming out only a few weeks ago and here we are! Seriously this brand (entirely) deserves our money, it's going to continue to propel the Castlevania brand in a new direction and keeps getting better every time I fire up a new entry. These NES-inspired COTM(s) are so great, punishing, art design is tight! I am very impressed at how fast they cranked this out at this quality, feels just like a NES-cart to me and for 19 bucks CAD... My dad used to pay 45-60 bucks per cart and you'd get a game shorter than this in the 80s, they easily earned the price point here.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: More of not-castlevania platformer!Pretty much everything that you may enjoy (faithful graphics, challenge) and hate (knockback and pits) from the 1st game applies here as well. The only changes that come to mind are:- CotM2 seems more difficult than CotM1 (corgi does simplify platforming, yet still around half-point game gets significantly harder)- more enemies with some returning ones- checkpoints made more obvious- more character building and story bits (in 8bit style so it's rather minimalistic)- (purely subjective) the soundtrack in 1st game was slightly more memorableAll in all a fun and challenging game for folks to relive their childhood gaming experiences (and grievances..).PS: oh, is it better than CotM1? I'd say yes, but only marginally, if you're on the fence about getting into it, pick the cheaper one.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first one, you'll like this one, if you didn't like the first one, this one won't change your mind.  That's not to say it's the same game again, it does enough to differentiate itself to make it feel worthwhile and different from its predecessor, but it is still channeling Castlevania 3.  I should also probably note, this one is significantly harder than the first one was, though it still feels fair most of the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: CotM2 is not as 'slim' as the first CotM. It expands the game by requiring multiple playthroughs to unlock the ending. You will end up playing the entire game through several times,  The game itself is very good but I personally wasn't a fan of the multiple playthroughs. I've got a bit burned out with it. However, for the price, the graphics and a decent chiptune soundtrack I'd definitely recommend it. It's also nice how the casual difficulty from the first game is still present. i.e. no knockback! Co-op play is only local but this work well over Steam Remote Play. It's quite funny to hop on to each other and get to unreachable areas that way. The co-op is a well made addition and something not even the Castlevanias back in the day allowed us to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game all ways possible, getting all the achievementsThis game is more fun and beatiful than the first one, this also aplies for the difficult. The bosses here are more complexity with shorts windows of time to hit them. And when comes to the 'hard' version of these bosses you should have more patience.The most fun thing was playing in the Ultimate Form of Zangetsu, it's like a modern Ninja Gaiden. The soundtrack is good, but the first one was better, i think this is because Michiru Yamane participating in the first game.The only cons i can see is about the multiplayer, not the multiplayer itself, is well made and pretty fun, but the problem is the steam remoteplay that sucks with lags and problem with controller - not only this game, i have issues in another games playing with friends.  I will seek alternatives like Parsec.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very frustrating. I love the genuine challenge from learning enemy attack patterns and the bosses are great! But all this game does to increase difficulty is decrease the size of platforms.. seriously, right away you're sliding on ice, falling into lava and finally just falling off a cliff for a cheap insta-death.Bloodstained 2 isn't trying to be a retro game, it is a retro game! The problem is they kept all the bad stuff that was in all those oldschool games I played growing up and frankly I don't have the patience to do it again.Great game, just not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Follows the same formula as Curse of the Moon 1, but attempts to evolve with a new cast harnessing different movesets. While it feels familiar, the bosses seem more gimmicky and will require a little bit to learn, especially in Zangetsu-only mode (if achievement hunting). Also contains an interesting story mechanic in which subsequent playthroughs can both change the story, the stages, and even the overall cast of characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Moon 2 is fun, but a hell of a step up in difficulty from its predecessor. And sometimes, it's not always in the right ways. Enemy placement can feel cheaper, though for the most part it's a non-factor once you've figured out how to deal with them. It's more when it feels like there are far too many enemies on screen at once. Some of the bosses, while definitely flashy, can feel overwhelming with how much is going on. Many attacks can feel unpredictable the first time as well.If this doesn't bother you, then this will be one of the greatest retro-style action-platformers you've ever played. Even with some flaws, I still overall highly enjoy the game. Just be prepared to invest a lot of time into the extra modes if you want to unlock everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: So i'm gonna be a little harsh on the game. I feel like the level design has a little too many rude moments where you get launched into pits unless you play on casual mode. The characters has some extreme strengths and losing a character in a specific situation can cost more than losing the other 3... Happened more in this game than in the first one i experienced due to cleaner and more friendly level design. Having the sniper can just destroy some enemies in the distance and being invincible on the dog is just insane. Makes the bossfights a mash fight. The bosses doesnt regain all HP after you die... Which made the last boss in episode 1 very wierd for me... The bosses lost a lot of challange due to this. I think the bosses them self are pretty good tho. Maybe a little extra mimicy than the first game. Over all the game is badly balanced i think and not as clever as the first game. Still if you really like CotM 1 you should try this out! Still nice art and cool characters. Kinda pricy for what it is tho...
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just a few levels in so far and I can already say I like it. I think I can already say it's even better than the first, which says a lot, since I really liked the first one. I like the improvements like boss health meters and the little interactions between the characters and stuff like the campfire screen when the map shows between levels. It adds character to the game. And the bosses themselves, from what I've played so far, are fun to fight and well-designed. Keep these games coming!
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: 🌗 【Please tell «INTI CREATES» about the possibility of adjusting regional prices.】 Well, this is definitely a surprise sequel and honestly feels less like a gift to fans and more like a commercial product. It's still a good adventure, but it's not as good as the first in virtually every way. The game can only be praised for the refinement of individual mechanics, but these are minor things. The level design is lackluster and the rooms can be very similar, the locations themselves are less impressive, and the music isn't as memorable, the same applies to the bosses. Yes, there are more characters, adding variety, and even replayability has turned into episodic play with successive different endings. However, constant management about who to choose, what to collect for whom — reduces the dynamics. It could've been worse, thank God it wasn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Revised...If you're a fan of the first installment you'll prolly like this... to a point.  Most of the levels are enjoyable, but some of the bosses post scenario one really bring the game down.  They're either braindead easy or you're just trying to tank them and hope for a good pattern.  It's one of the two.  This is especially weird considering how easy and gimmicky the levels are.  You expect the bosses to be a thematic exclamation point on a similarly paced level, but that's definitely not the case here.  Instead you get repeated slogs through stages to face one of  the two scenarios pointed out before.  It's not very rewarding.The episodes and/or modes don't feel quite right either... don't love it, don't hate it, I just think that the late game is the most appealing aspect of the game as a whole and you really have to work for it.  This doesn't bode well for people who aren't willing to sink the time to unlock everything.  Really wanted to like this, loved the original.  All other aspects of the game outside of my previous complaints are fantastic.  Can't win em all I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Huge numbers of possible endings, multiple final bosses, harder versions for each boss, 8 levels and a bonus level, 7 playable characters and more game modes. High replayability with shortcuts, powerups and alternate routes hidden in levels. Very difficult but rewarding, and you can cheese the game if it's too hard. Large selection of subweapons.Cons: linear at first, you can't unlock new content until you beat the current level. Starts out slow and painfully difficult, takes a long time to get used to the outdated clunky controls. I wish the control were more responsive, somehow. I don't want to be punished by death by falling from a platform because I pressed the jump key too early when the character was in attack posture and wasn't responding to controls. I so don't want that.Overall this is totally worth it and was great fun in the end. I recommend this for people who like tough platformers with fixed jumping arcs and, basically, good old castlevania.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me tell you this: this game might seem really difficult at the start and scare you off, so what I really, really recommend is to turn on Casual mode for just fun (it's ok, don't be afraid), since the default Veteran mode is more suited for, like, really experienced players who are really good at specific type of platformers (Castlevania games). You won't lose anything, and the plot/levels will progress the same way as in Veteran, you just will receive a much more reasonable amounts of damage, and most importantly, YOU WON'T HAVE THAT ANNOYING KNOCKBACK. Yeah, that knockback that always pushes you off the platforms straight into the pits. Casual mode ON and knockback dissappears, and it's great!Amazing game. I really like how polished the game is - the music, the graphics, it looks and feels just right. The old NES game kind of aesthetic is captured perfectly here while having a modern approach to the game itself, that's actually a rare sight to see. I am a huge fan of the "switch characters ingame for different abilities and separate health pools", I don't think I've seen this idea being implemented anywhere else in such a way. I love it! This game is much bigger than it seems. Replays with the different characters in Episodes will reward you with new levels. Try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game overall, but not as enjoyable as the first game. The main reason for this is that the developers went overboard with the difficulty (I mean, my playtime of this game vs that of its prequel is pretty indicative).There are quite a few unbalanced segments and bosses that require specific characters (some of them are almost useless against some bosses), so that if said characters have died, it would be better to retry that part with a full team.Ok to be honest, the first Curse of the Moon had also this issue, but it was nowhere near as frequent. For example the majority of the bosses in that game had clear patterns that you could memorize after a couple of tries, and even with an incomplete team, you could get through most tough situations.I am starting to think that the developers believed that giving us some characters with really cool abilities would justify throwing a ton of ♥♥♥♥ at us. I am perfectly fine with a good challenge, as long as it is fair and satisfying to tackle.Last but not least, the soundtrack in Curse of the Moon was killer. In the sequel, it seems like it's mostly comprised of Castlevania B-side tracks.Despite that, I recommend Curse of the Moon 2 to those looking for a classic Castlevania type of game, since it is still more accessible than the 8-bit Konami titles.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed CotM 1, or if you like any sort of retro-style game, then I recommend to give this game a shot.What I will say boldly, is that I did not enjoy this game as much as CotM 1. With that being said, it does not mean that I dislike the game. With the game being a sequel, I appreciate the amount of features and options that are given to the player; more modes, co-op mode, more characters, more techniques.The sprites and graphics are as classic and glorious as they are, the boss fights are (mostly) entertaining, the OST is neat, just not as memorable as CotM 1 in my opinion.Going back as to why I didn't enjoy the game as much as the first - As you progress through each episode and stage, you are given more characters and options to play around with. Naturally the game becomes more difficult, but especially with the later stages, the game feels like a frustrating mess. I am the type that likes challenge, and know for a fact that it is an absolute must for the player to adapt to each situation, but I felt that (if the developers truly intended this or not) the game constantly attempts to induce frustration with questionable level design, enemy placement, and moments where there will be 50 objects on the screen coming at you at once.As I mentioned before - I still recommend playing this game. Just prepare for a grind if you plan on unlocking everything that the game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Not much has changed, which is both a good thing and a bad thing. Good because that Classicvania action is as good as ever, and bad because this game commits the same sin of its predecessor in requiring you to replay the whole thing to see the ending which is something that I just... do not have a lot of interest in doing right now. I'm told said ending sequences are really cool, and maybe I'll revisit this game someday. But for now, I'm content. I think I preferred the first game a little bit, but this game did make a few improvements. Unlike the first game where I pretty much exclusively used Miriam, this game actually makes four useful characters that you are motivated to use. They made Zangetsu not pathetic in his own game! Good job! I'm so happy Bloodstained exists, and I hope we see more of it in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first game, expect more of the same and then some. The devs really tried to expand on the experience of the first game. Repeat playthroughs present players with more branching paths, more challenge, more characters and more bosses. Each playthrough is different enough to keep this game interesting. To optimally play you'll want to use all the characters at your disposal. They all have their own distinct strengths and the game feels designed around you using their kits to overcome a decently challenging game. This made losing a character feel like a major loss compared to the first CotM game. Some frustrations I had with this game came from its bosses. I wont say the bosses are bad, but a lot of the bosses are very samey. Most of them are giant static background objects that spam projectiles. Some attacks or patterns are so subtly telegraphed that it feels impossible to avoid damage unless you have repeatedly attempted the boss. Also, some of the rooms just before bosses are packed to the brim with enemies to try and handicap you before the fight.Originally I left a negative review and shared some of the sentiments a others that had done the same. This game really grew on me after my first playthrough. If you played the first CotM, just be advised that the sequel is balanced around having several characters where the first was balanced around the possibility of completing the game with a single character. Things can feel a little chaotic as a result. I feel like my review is not very flattering, but I still recommend this game. I went from 11 hours played with a negative review to over 40 hours played and positive review. If you like retro style games, this is one of the better ones out there.

_childDocuments_.review: It might be one of the best 2D side scrolling platformers out there.  But I will never know because it's unplayable.  For some reason there is a keyboard / controller configuration that pops up on first play.  Great!  I figured out that despite the screen's erroneous instructions, you press ENTER to configure the buttons with the keyboard.  But then you find that on the main menu, those keys don't work.  It says to press A but A doesn't do anything.  On the contrary, several of the action buttons I defined now act as arrow keys.  ???  Fine.  I finally figure out that if you use ENTER, you can go back to the configuration and discover that there are TWO places to configure keyboard buttons.  The one it prompted you for is just not even used for the keyboard!  So I configure the right one for the keyboard and find that it won't let me use the ARROW KEYS on the keyboard to map to ARROW keys in the game.  Yes, really.  I can instead turn on the number lock and use the numeric keypad arrow keys.  Fine.  Dumb, but fine.  Now I find that the characters who can attack high and attack low will not attack low.  There is actually a button on the keyboard, "B" which will attack low.  But if you duck and use the normal attack, the player moves from prone to a standing position to attack instead.  WHAT?  SO I wonder if I have a keyboard binding conflict.  Nope.  None there.  Instead I reconfigure it to use another key and now the player always ducks to attack when I attack standing up.  OMFG.  FINE!  I'll do it their way.  I configure WASD for the arrow keys, then I pick some arbitrary keys for attack and jump.  It won't accept  the quote, semicolon, square brackets, period, comma or question mark keys.  It only lets me use letters.  So I choose U and I.  Nope.  They don't do what they're supposed to.  For some reason, they are mapped to match Q and E and they cycle through the characters.  I loved BloodStained.  I REALLY loved BlooStaned:ROTN.  I was all set to love this game too.  But I've been fighting this bullcrap for an hour.  I've never written a review on Steam before.  But this was so stupid that I decided it was worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: - Brilliant 8-bit graphics and animations- Music is good and actually makes sense compared to earlier installment- Great character roster and character abilities- Pretty decent controlls (save for crouching attack, and switching direction you face while crouching. Not very possible and it can cost you entire lives, this function alone).- Very nice new way of getting lives where score is omitted; you have one bar, which you fill up. When it's full, you earn 1-UP. Very nice addition, because no one cares about score points. They're just messy and don't give you overview when you can expect to get a 1-UP. This has been fixed in a very creative manner.- Level backgrounds and general locations feel more Castlevania this time around, and are so very very welcome. Truly everything, in this aspect, is top notch.- The enemies make more sense. They look less like aliens, and more like demons this time.- Overall presentation is very charming. I like the characters action when you are shown at map screen. They all do different stuff, depending what kind of level they've been through. Makes game feel more alive.- Beautiful user interface. Truly. When you pause, you can get character tips of your current character, and how to use your current sub-weapon. But often, the text scroll speed is far to quick to read. And you really can't switch manually for next tip, which would have been a big bonus, instead of having to pause/unpause all the time.- EXTREMLY Difficult. Oh boy... let's talk about this game's ludicrous difficult. I'm gonna break it into sections, because honestly, I think and feel that the developers and IGA himself need to take a real good look at it. Don't let chapter 1 fool you, because soon after you've completed it, the game is getting exponentially harder. And no, it doesn't really matter what game mode you play "CASUAL", "VETERAN" or "LEGENDARY"... there is no middle ground. The game is extremly difficult. Veteran and Legendary just make it exponentially worse.The boss fights are an absolute mess, requiring you to have pixel perfection of your jumps. Sometimes, you won't even be able to dodge at ALL (lava boss anyone?), and other times you are attacked from so many places/directions at once, in such speed, and in such angles that any hope of evasion is impossible. This is even worsened if you do not have a certain character and/or powerup, that makes a battle completely impossible to beat. (Lava boss, anyone?) Think you know tacticts of a boss? Think again, because they may change tactic to completely mess up all your planning. Not that it will ever matter to begin with.Level layout is filled with annoying death traps, where one little hit will insta-kill you. This especially true in later levels, close to end game. There will be moments in the game which will require you to be on tiny moving platforms, where miscalculating your jumps is so extremly easy to do, which will ofcourse result in you getting killed. This is even worsened with the fact that just as you think you have made a jump, there was a quick shooting projectile enemy just outside your field of view, waiting for you to make that jump, so he can shoot you down and kill you in 1 shot. Final levels are filled with that. In fact, they are ENTIRELY made up with heart-stopping, pixel perfection death traps that gives player no breathing room whatsoever. There is no rest, nor change of pace. It's EXTREME. Even your checkpoints when you've come far and get killed, you will be respawned at the most annoying locations where you will have to re-do ALL the pixel perfect jumps/death traps again.Some enemies and some enemy tactic is to attack you from angles that you can't protect yourself from. You MAY, MAYBE, have a sub-weapon to deal with it... but when playing through the game for 1st time, and don't know what to expect and don't have such a sub-weapon... what happens?... Exactly. Even if you have played through it, and you don't have proper weapon, you are pretty much as good as dead. Veteran or newbie alike.Now that difficulty has been somewhat covered, let's continue the list.- Amount of levels are few. Seriously, why tho? You did well enough with the art and ideas,why not more levels? And you expect players to have 7-8 levels to re-play through as 4 different chapters?- There is no CRT effect video filter mode. Even though people really like it, and game claims to be a throwback to the old-school games. You can't feel more old-school than CRT effect. It's not in the difficulty, it's in the presentation and overall feel of the game.- The game supports 2 players, but the 2nd player MUST have a controller. Even on online coop/remote play, the one joining me MUST have a controller. Now why is that?- I can't rebind my keys. ESC should be pause, but it's not. It MUST be "P" on my keyboard. Why can't I change that?- The homepage is more informative about the product than the actually manual you PAID for. And it STILL doesn't tell you about game modes or how to start coop modes online.The game looks beautiful, with many and compelling characters, along with a decent storyline. But the gameplay and level layout is so unforgiving that it renders the game unplayable. I like to take it easy when playing games, i.e, use it as entertainment and relax my mind. However, "Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2"'s difficulty, completely kills the atmoshphere it builds up. At least to me. It feels like a painstaking work that rewards nothing, and doesn't give you anything to look forward to. I just feel... "Oh no.. not this again. More?" throughout the entire game. I have been a fan of Castlevania series for 31 years (so yeah I'm an old-school gamer), and I have Loved most of IGA's work. We all know he changed face of Castlevania forever, with titles such as Symphony of the Night.. and quite frankly, knowing his background in this, and following it intimatelly, I have expected that someone like him would have had a clear understanding of what makes a good game and what's not. This game, to me, goes hands down as the greatest gaming disappointment of 2020. Maybe because I liked previous installment and Castlevania series so much, and also the fact that I have a deep faith in IGA and was so happy that he got to do what he wanted to do, the way he envisioned it, after that turbulence with Konami, do I feel this game to be such a huge slap in the face for me, as a fan and long-time player/gamer. I can only hope that the developers can take in, and fix some of the issues that are present in the game. They truly did an outstanding work with everything else, that I personally think they should fix these issues as they overshadow all their efforts and hard work. Failing that... If the next game doesn't change any of this, I will not support or follow IGA's future work and projects. I see no reason to.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this. You have no idea how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ badly I wanted to like this. I loved the first game. It was an absolute joy to play. The difficulty was harsh but fair. This game, it's just needlessly unforgiving. Yeah I get that the original castlevania games were unforgiving, but see the thing is I've PLAYED the original castlevania games, and the unforgiving nature wasn't as bad as it is in this game, in my opinion. and I'm gonna share what I mean, spoilers ahead:At the end of part one you fight a black bug thing. His main attack is shooting beams of some dark energy in either a high or low direction. He telegraphs it pretty well but even still the game's movement is seriously flawed, making dodging these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things difficult. And when he finishes one attack pattern, he can turn himself into that dark energy and either fly across the stage, or swirl around you and damage you. The latter attack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I've tried every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing I can think to try, and I can't dodge it. I swear to ♥♥♥♥ you just have to get lucky. and when you beat him? oh buddy, the fun times are just beginning. The bug, who I have given the nickname mr. Chuckles, begins the second stage. Now, there's nothing wrong with bosses that have more than one stage, I like that. What I DON'T like is when the game gives you NO CHANCE TO RECOVER BETWEEN STAGES. --MOST-- games I've played, no matter what kind or how difficult, give you a --CHANCE-- to heal up and prepare yourself. Not here. and yeah, I get that a few other games have done that before. And I sincerely want those games to go ♥♥♥♥ themselves. I didn't like this ♥♥♥♥ in the first game, I don't like it here. I wouldn't care that much if Mr. Chuckles' first phase wasn't that difficult, but he has a WAY too generous health pool, and his attacks take huge chunks out of any of your character's life bars. Oh and I forgot to mention: If you die on the second phase, you have to go back to the first and fight Mr. Chuckles jr. all over again. I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ what anybody says, this is a bad gimmick that ruined this game for me, and it's a gimmick that should have died off in the 1980's. And I get that there's gonna be people who are gonna say "hee hoo git gud". Listen bud. It's hard to "git gud" when the game's mechanics themselves are seriously flawed, but that's for another discussion. Bottom line: If you want to play a competent Castlevania-style game on the pc, you really can't go wrong with this. I really do technically love this game, but the final boss of chapter one is where I'm throwing in the towel, which is disappointing. Maybe you'll have better luck with it than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the first Curse of the Moon, this was a real disappointment. The game is great for the first four levels, but from level 5 onwards it becomes a tedious slog, even on Casual mode. I can't really say whether it's because of the characters or the bosses, but it just doesn't feel fun to play. That said, both have issues.Zangetsu is fine, as he was in the first game. No real complaints.Dominique replaces Miriam, but is worse than her in every way save for the ability to revive fallen characters and fully heal them. Her basic attack has less range, her pogo jump is finicky, and her healing abilities apparently gave the designers the bright idea to make forced damage instances necessary to justify the ability to heal instead of using it as a safety net.Robert is just... bad. His range is nice, yes, but his low HP makes him useless in any combat-heavy situation. Unlike Alfred, who also has low HP, Robert has no useful abilities to make up for it. For comparison, Alfred's subweapons provide utility that reward smart play. Robert's... just attack at different angles, just like Zangetsu's. This redundancy makes him feel very poorly designed.Hachi is just dumb. Yes, the cute corgi driving a mech suit is funny, but his special ability suffers from the same problem that Dominique's heals do: the designers felt the need to justify the existence of on-demand invincibility with instances that essentially boil down to "use Hachi or die". Even most of the bosses suffer from this problem with attacks that can only be dodged with his ability. Powerful defensive abilities should be a tactical choice, not a requirement.Probably my biggest complaint about the game, though, is that it suffers the same problem that The Wild Eight does: it advertises itself as a multiplayer title, but the multiplayer doesn't work without wasting a lot of time trying workarounds, especially when using Remote Play.3/10. Playable, but the broken multiplayer and poor character and late-game level design push this out of "hard, but fair" and into "needlessly frustrating", even on the easiest difficulty. If you want a classic Castlevania experience, go play the first Curse of the Moon instead.

Words cannot express how much contempt I have for inti creates. I don't honestly know why they have fans sometimes because they always pull ♥♥♥♥ like this ever since the zero games, where you infamously had to Rank A-S to even get the special attacks that would make the game playable without save states to all but the most autistic and dedicated players. _childDocuments_.review: I finished the game once on classic difficulty before reviewing. That is I finished all 3 episodes of this game, not just a single playthough.This game is the ultimate challenge for everyone who deemed the first game too easy.But the problem is that this difficulty comes at a cost, that will be too much for "normal" players, even those that enjoy challange. While I praised first game for being hard but fair, this sequel is anything but fair. It's really telling that devs decided to add a character who's power is being INVINCIBLE. That's because some of the sections of this game are unreasonable to get through without getting hit. And we all know that getting hit in a game like this will result in you gravitating to the nearest bottomless pit to your death.If you want tough but reasonable difficulty – this isn't it. If you want hair-pulling difficulty, this may be the game for you.I decided on a „not recommended” verdict, because it forgets what made first game good and took a turn into lazy difficulty instead of proper, challenging design.Please, do not play this game unless you are ready to cry out of frustration.A 2D platform game most similar to the first Curse of The Moon, which was inspired by Castlevania 3.You have multiple characters that you will unlock by progressing, same as the first game. New arrivals are:- lady priest with a lance, who gets longer reach than the main hero, can attack in up and down directions and bounce on top of objects and enemies and has high jump- guy with a rifle, who has unlimited range, but slow attack with less damage, he can also crawl on the ground lower than other characters- mech-suit, which can hover in the air, traverse spiked floors has more HP bigger attack hurtbox and more damage, but is a larger, slow-moving targetYour main hero is Zangetsu, same as in the original.2 new heroes come with their own special weapons, most of which are useful. Standout is the priest's healing spell and resurrection spell that only appears in hidden secret areas similar to the lightning spell for the alchemist in the first game. Mech-suit does not have special weapons, instead always having the ability to become invincible. It drains your special power as long as it's active, but will prevent any hit from dealing damage to you or knocking you back. Several areas in the game seem to be designed with this ability in mind, because going through them legit would require near perfect execution of very complex jumps while also using correct special weapons to fend off dangerous enemies where every hit would result you in getting thrown to your death.Game is designed to be replayed with different playthroughs having different characters taking part in the story and some new ways of progressing through the levels are unlocked thanks to their abilities. Bosses also get different attacks.Overall very similar to the first game and I recommend playing that before giving this a try.Pixel-art looks fantastic when done well, and here it's done well.Game has to have a story, but it doesn't have to be complex or try to be funny or quirky. The Messenger's story made me not want to play. Here the story is enough to drive you forward. There are some neat little animations of characters interacting with each other in between missions that add a lot to humanize them while taking just a few seconds to play out. This game does not waste your time with needless, long dialogue.Technically that's untrue. There are videos showing virtuossos playing the game legit without getting hit and without using mech's invincibility.The level of skill you need to achieve to be able to do that is quite unreasonable. Some sections require you to keep track of like 5 different attack nagles and 2 different timings to avoid damage and protect yourself from projectiles. Some large-aoe attacks, especially in last episode barely give you any time to react while requiring to move into specific spots on the arena to avoid damage.Point is that some sections are VERY difficult and without invincibility skill of the mech you wouldn't be able to reasonably beat them.Speaking of invincibility skill, it's inclusion seems to be sort-of a band-aid solution to the problem posed by the difficulty level devs set for this game. I would rather have a more reasonable challange instead of having a limited cheat button.There are many gauntlets filled with projectiles, enemies and difficult jumps that kill you easily while also requiring you to move forward constantly. You will spend multiple lives and continues to remember when to switch to which character, use certain weapons and how to jump and attack to go through these and after you learn that - every subsequent time will just be a boring slog.I just really want to hammer the point home. But let me mention something I haven't touched upon yet. Medusa heads. Ok, they are the same as in 1st game, what's different to make them worse? They can spawn on top of you if you are close to the side of the screen and the game is designed to make you ride slow-ass platforms near the screen edge. Invincibility is the only help here.I still like the story, but the end twist is too similar.It's too effing difficult for me. I mean, I finished it, but I can't say I had fun doing it and I wouldn't be able to repeat some sections in a consistent fashion. I kinda finished it out of spite and felt more like relief rather than pride when I was done. Who gives a fk if I finished this very difficult game? You'd have to be some kind of ♥♥♥♥♥ nerd to think that...... well fk this game anyway.If you beat this game, "Conglaturation". You can assume I care to make yourself feel better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just fine. It's more Curse of the Moon, and it still carries a lot of the design flaws the original had, and they are GLARING due to the increased difficulty. The problem of losing a vital character and having to simply continue or lose a life carries on, and the boss of stage 7, which comes back from the first game, is more random and unfair than they were originally, as well as more random than any other boss up to that point, which were usually more predictable and, well, skill based. Also, they took out good, unique systems, such as being able to deny or even kill companions (dynamic difficulty through gameplay!)Also, why can't I play with unlimited lives and knockback? Does the game have to take half the challenge out because you don't want to lose all your progress to a pit? I don't understand this choice, Celeste had a robust accessibility system in 2016 and this game has 2 difficulty options and 1 bad choice. I will likely continue to play this game, as I enjoy Castlevania and Igarashi, but I don't think this game is worth it. You'd be better off playing older Castlevanias with save states on or something. I've had much more fun with Castlevania 3 and Rondo than I did with this.It's more Curse of the Moon, but worse. If you liked the first game and also are a masochist, you might like this.All that said, the original Curse of the Moon is a master work, and you should play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Inti Creates breaks every rule of classic platformer design by making the subweapons and consumables damn near mandatory to get through certain rooms and setups.This is good in that it is a refreshing take on Classicvania that even Classicvania seldom reached. This game is certainly tough, but in a classic Inti Creates manner more than Classicvania (You might have to excuse my hazy memory on this if I am off base.). Inti Creates throws their characteristic utter bulls**t patterns at you, but they have given you a few incredibly powerful subweapons to cope, including one character who literally has an invincibility toggle.But it's bad in that losing the invincibility character or not having the subweapon juice you need means your progress slows to a crawl of fidgeting around the enemy to try to make progress or just damage tanking and hoping a continue point is in the next room (There are a couple of bosses who give you such tiny windows to strike them that if you aren't using invincibility as an offensive move to create your own attack opportunities, you're going to be fighting them all day). The patterns are still bulls**t, and every single enemy is annoying to match. Even the basic zombies take two hits of the basic weapon to kill so you have to hit them, back up, and hit them again. Classicvania would at least give you a couple enemies that were popcorn. Not here, every single enemy is as annoying as a Medusa head in a platforming segment and just as intrusive. The game never lets up. This relentless annoyance combined with the Classicvania limitations makes this game incredibly aggravating and draining to play rather than especially fun.Worse still they expect you to run the same game four times to see all the content, and only the second run onward introduces serious changes in enemy patterns.All that aside it is exactly what it looks like, a retro inspired spinoff of Bloodstained, itself a spinoff of Castlevania. It calls back to Classic Castlevania in every way, especially in the old school no air control platforming and ruthless enemy knockback, but the monster designs and aesthetic remains terrible because the OG Castlevania stole every single cool movie monster aesthetic. And, surprisingly for Inti Creates, the level design is actually pretty decent, complete with good variety even if the pacing is just destroyed by the monster encounter design.So I have to give the game a reluctant thumbs up. The only part of this product that is objectively bad is how, in never giving you a second to catch your breath while being stuck with the incredibly slow and unpleasant platforming and combat pace of Classicvania, all that combines into something just draining and not much fun to play. I could barely manage to do the 2nd of the rather bloated 4-5 required clears to see the game's content.  It's a good product and all the individual parts work well but it is so constantly demanding that it ends up feeling more of a slog than a fun ride.Somewhat related, I believe Konami's Castlevania collection is on Steam if you're hungry for the real deal.Also did this game seriously need four different enemies who all are just "fat, sits there, every few seconds sends out a shockwave you must jump over"?

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Curse of the Moon, it was a great prequel to Ritual of the Night, which I also love.Curse of the Moon 2 sucks.Now I will be the first to admit, I suck at video games, especially ones that are designed to be difficult. But if you actually take the time to git gud, it shouldn't be a problem, right? RIGHT?!This game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ball buster and not in the fun way, so absolutely frustrating that it makes CBT appealing. It starts simple enough, like the last game, it starts off with Zangetsu, introduces you to the game's mechanics, subweapons, until you reach the first boss. Once there, this game becomes a sick wake-up call that it's done ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around.Next character you get is Dominique... why? Whatever, she's cool, got healing, different spells and abilities, even a single use one that can resurrect fallen party members. Very useful.Next is Robert... Robert sucks... his health pool is low to the point that a single hit from a strong attack is enough to down him. His weapon is only good in a straight line, you'll want him mostly for his subweapons, which can be useful... rarely. I've never found a use for that cannon. I'm not even gonna talk about his wall jump because there are only a couple places in the game that it's even remotely useful, otherwise it ♥♥♥♥♥ you over.Next is Hachi, he's a godsend. A good boi that rides a steam mech, yeah his attack range sucks and he can't hit enemies low to the ground... unless you hover and use his stomp attack. You're gonna be abusing his Invincible Iron ability a lot, especially with the more frustrating sections...After stage 4, the kid gloves come off and you're introduced to Heart of FIre. You better have mastered each of your character's abilities and be switching constantly otherwise you're gonna have a BAD, BAD time... I swear, every stage after 4 is more frustrating than the last with sections that seem designed to be barely doable. Then you get to the Titan's Sarcophagus... ♥♥♥♥ this level...You've got enemies above and below you, spitting projectiles, sometimes from off the screen, you've got mean spirited enemy placements which Hachi can't one shot and traps. And if you're playing on Veteran (or God forbid... LEGEND...) good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ luck! There's a difference between HARD and IMPOSSIBLE and this level is definitely close to the latter. The home stretch is designed in such away that the platforms rise quickly and you can't use Dominique because she jumps too damn high! So you think, Hachi! Yeah, okay fine, except you've got maybe just enough weapon points to break some spikes, kill some smaller enemies that you run out just before the end. Only to reach the last platform and get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ by an enemy spitting fire at you. If the knockback damage doesn't kill you the spikes certainly will. Who thought THAT was a good idea? Oh, IT WAS THE SICK ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WHO DESIGNED THIS!I got so frustrated, I turned the difficulty to casual! Something I never do unless I am secret hunting!Muted Cries isn't bad I guess, you meet Gremory... again... and she pulls the second form ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ only to kamikaze herself with a giant blood moon, but I guess you get to see demon titties? _childDocuments_.review: I played with an XBONE controller in fullscreen. I am using an i9-9900k & 2080 Ti, current drivers and patches manually installed on Windows 10 x64.I would not recommend playing this with a keyboard and mouse.PLEASE NOTE, even though I have left comments on, I am not interested in you telling me that I should put 4000 hours into a game I don't enjoy so I can "git gud", and then I would like it. That is a stupid and dismissive argument. Don't be stupid.Skill is not indicative of enjoyment, and I have better things to do than bash my head on what I personally feel are bad / mediocre games on the off chance I could maybe like one of them one day. I have a life and don't play games to develop Stockholm Syndrome.I will update this review if I continue to play and have more to add.PROS:- Looks like a more modern version of Castlevania 3.- Runs well, as you'd expect for such a light game.- No crashes during my time with it.- Cards & achievements.NEUTRALS:- Music is okay. Not even close to comparable to the NES games, but not bad.CONS:- While remaking a new version of Castlevania, they also disregarded all of the control improvements of anything beyond the early NES days. Did you live through one-hit death precision platforming on the NES? I did. I hated it then, and I still hate it now. The original Bloodstained demake wasn't this picky, but this one certainly is.- Some character abilities do not trigger when you want them to, instead choosing to activate not at all, or incorrectly. Most notably the hover ability which, again, deeply and badly affects platforming.- Still short, but the game is now stretched out because you'll have to play maps over and over again due to the unreliable controls killing you.- There's a story, but I watched all of it to the point I quit and I could not tell you ANYTHING that happened. It may as well not exist.CONCLUSION: Kinda cool to watch, but deeply frustrating to play. I would try the game again if they did a pass on the controls to make them less punishing.

_childDocuments_.review: One word describes this game: Terrible.It has a lot of the ingredients for a good game, but they aren't mixed very well and combined with bad programming and straight up -douchebag level- design choices, makes me wonder who actually made this game. The first game in the series wasn't trying to be more then it was; a simple action platformer with some varing gameplay through character swapping. Cool idea. In this game, it's mandatory you have every character, or you're pretty much boned depending on where you actually are. The worst thing though isn't just the awful level design, but the poor programming. I think the game is just straight-up on responsive at times. For example, if you're going to hover in the air as Hachii, it just straight-up doesn't work. I have no idea why it doesn't, but it basically requires you to stand still, hover, and then move, and on certain bosses, you don't have time to wait or you'll take damage or die.Another BIG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ COMPLAINT I have is the music. What the hell happened??? The first game had catchy tunes, but this one, NOTHING--I mean, absolutely nothing, is something I want to listen to or enjoy. It's just extremely bad or very repetitive musical tracks. The boss music is the very definition of trying WAY too hard.Were you guys trying to get people to like this, or is it just a cash-grab? It's so sad and miserable that I don't want to even play this. Some of the levels are extremely cruel in their overall designs, as if it only wants the player to fail due to cheap ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tactics. And you might say the original castlevanias are hard, but they're at least fair-- you can see what's coming up and you aren't overwhelmed most of the time. In this game, you are constantly overwhelmed and having slow characters with one jump is a recipe for frustration. What else was Castlevania known for? Oh yes, great music, which as mentioned previously, is not present here.Overall, this is very disappointing, I wanted to put more time and effort into playing this, but it's so border line frustrating (and even boring), that I can't be bothered.Please,  you guys can do SOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO much better.Thanks.~ God.

_childDocuments_.review: (x-posted to my Wordpress blog, Gunlord500)Inti's done it again! The original Curse of the Moon was a delightful throwback to the retro NES castlevania games, and this one is an EXCELLENT followup--more of the same, sure, but with the addition of more characters, a non-linear story path in the last episode, and some nice two-player mode action, you definitely get a good deal with this. It's much harder than the first game, but man, so many new characters, stages, and enemies, it's so much fun. While the plot doesn't make a whole lot of sense--SPOILERS:The final episode has you building a 18th century space shuttle and blasting off to the moon, where you just fight demons without any oxygen, or any clear way to get home for that matter--though this also leads into a REALLY nifty little shooter bonus minigame!/SPOILERSThere's a good bit more dialogue, and you can learn about the character's backstories a little more, which is cool. People initially complained that the game is just an hour long, but that's BEFORE you unlock everything--once you do, it's easily 4 to 8 hours long, and there's also an element of randomness to the final episode that MASSIVELY adds replay value. So yeah, definitely awesome! Inti did a great job on this!

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost: there's no penalty for going Casual or Veteran. Difficulty-wise they are about the same, what really weighs is that you have more Weapon Points to work with, no worrying about lives (not that it matters, it's easy to consistently stay above 3 lives on Veteran anyways) and no knockback (as knockback is more often than not a nuisance and punishment for not minding your position). So, no shaming people going Casual, OK?That out of the way, let's go on to analyze: The first game didn't have much story in it, it was more similar to how Castlevania 3 told its story, but was a well-rounded game with mostly fair bosses with a couple exceptions... And the "couple exceptions" comes to bite back, but all in its due time.Now, the sequel... Or rather: Curse of the Moon 2. While it takes more loops than the first to achieve a full clear, the story is more evident and the characters have more interaction with one another. This may annoy people who do not like doing multiple loops of a game to truly beat it, but those eager for story might be amused by what is told, and the intermission animations.Like the first... The second also suffers with "a couple exceptions". I won't sugarcoat it for you, their names are Titankhamun and Gremory. While the former is somewhat random and hard to get a read on, it is possible to find a safe strategy to use, but the later is very hard to get a read on and has no safe strategy if you can't read her in time. RNG luck only really factors in 3 out of all bosses in the game (and there are plenty bosses), but these two are the worst in terms of RNG, while the third one in question is less likely to trouble you with the RNG luck (unless you are down to your last hero and low on health).There are some nice surprises to see in the game, which I will refrain from spoiling, and ideas I would absolutely love to see Inti Creates exploring more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it short and sweet, CotM2 took everything that made the first game bad and decided to double-down on it's shortcomings. Horrible game design in the form of more cheap stagger/knockback into pit insta-deaths, more hordes of fodder enemies where its practically impossible to avoid damage, more attack spam screen clutter (ESPECIALLY for S6, Titankhamun, and somewhat for Lavamandra) and numerous other cheap tactics. Enemies (including some bosses) are not only reused from the first game (so practically more of the same), but also reused BETWEEN LEVELS THEMSELVES.Game encourages alternate paths a lot less now by locking like 95% of different paths (spoilers) to using characters you quite literally don't have until other playthroughs (or they're dead and require a restart).Cheesy character switching for mobility will be required - at least make your platforming less gimmicky, as it stands it's very annoying.Like the first game, being forced to pickup sub-weapons upon walking over them still exists instead of providing players with a choice via a pickup hotkey. Balance between subweps also remains horrid.Clunky movement remains from the first game, as well as the issue that casual is a tad too easy, and veteran is way too punishing (especially with the ♥♥♥♥ game design that is somehow worse than the first game).The game also feels justified at throwing insane obstacles in your way just because of Hachi's invincibility or other cheese like Gebel Bat form or the woman's high jump and leave other characters without any chance of retaliation (especially if their attacks are just plain underwhelming).Oh, and for some reason, the game thinks replaying the same levels not once, not twice, but THREE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TIMES is an enjoyable experience. Be prepared to play them even MORE to see all the content as well. I didn't have it in me to keep playing on Veteran after my first run - the game is just straight up horribly designed and really only fun in certain scenarios. Bosses on the second run also have an absurd amount of extra HP tacked on despite the player not really receiving much in compensation. And -sorta spoilers- for later endings the player will actually have to give up what little smooth combat there is provided in the form of Zangetsu's air+ground combos.And the alt-tab bug that requires a force close + loss of progress carries over from the first game.3.5/10 - Faux sense of difficulty disguised behind horrible level + enemy design with many cheap moments and reused assets that's a slog to get through and restrictive player exploration. Where CotM1 was at least SOMEWHAT recommendable only for those REALLY looking for a (subpar) metroidvania to play, all should avoid CotM2 unless your not only a mashochist but actively somehow have a hard on for games designed poorly. Really, really should've dropped this. Here's to hoping that Ritual of the Night is actually as good as I've heard.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really impressed by this game. It's simple like the original Curse of the Moon, but trickier with way more content. Like, three times more than before. With better characterization and story too, which includes two new original characters and three varieties of final bosses. The developers also decided to test you with the way they designed things. Like how Zangetsu actually gets WEAKER in Episode 2 after the power up he gets in Episode 1. You might end up not liking their decisions. But this is genuinely a good game that get's really fun once you manage to figure things out. Honestly, Curse of the Moon 2 is what sold me on Inti Creates and the Bloodstained franchise. I need more Dominique. I think I'm finally gonna play Ritual of the Night after this.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2 continues to build off the momentum of what it's predecessor had started. It brings you an experience seemingly lost because Konami still didn't care enough to bring back one of their sacred IPs during this time. So Inti Creates had to pick up the slack and do the work instead. They didn't disappoint in this sequel.Unfortunately, I'm under the impression that this game got a tiny bit harder for my liking. I've beaten the first game in Veteran difficulty, so I thought I was going to get a similar experience like before. I suppose not, because I've failed to get very far and only managed to reach a boss before dying shortly.Regardless, if that's your thing, then you'll find something to enjoy with this title. Everything is retained as faithful as the first is. I do wish though that Dominique had the spear skills like Eric Lecarde in Bloodlines did, would've made things interestingly fun for gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game very much, and I am very bias in that I am a huge Symphony of the Night fan.  All that being said, some of the level designs in this sequel are very frustrating.  I only usually play at least on Veteran difficulty or higher but yeah towards the end of the game it's a little ridiculous.  Only "critique" I'd care to mention.  The local co-op is dope, if only it had an online co-op support.  Maybe if they decide to make a 3rd installment?
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Finished "Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2". I like to play these kinds of retro games on my Steam Deck, because playing it on my desktop with a gigantic screen seems like a waste. Great opportunity to use the portable system, and with a low-end game like this the battery lasts as long as I could want it to.This game was alright. Definitely captures that NES-era Castlevania vibe with some interesting mechanics brought about via real-time character switching, where each character has different abilities. The story is pretty corny, but the level designs and character abilities are fun.I will say that the amount of trial-and-error isn't one of the things I would've brought in from the retro NES era, but the amount of retries you get (even on the Veteran difficulty) is effectively infinite. So winning is more about persistence than anything else.After you beat it the first time, the story makes an attempt to string you along to repeat mostly similar content that's been made a bit harder. I didn't love the game enough to keep on with it after that. But for the first go-round, I enjoyed it. If you like challenging retro action platformers, you'll probably enjoy CotM2.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion the overall package is not as good as the first game. I think the former one had a better collection of levels and branching paths. I feel the main reason for this discrepancy is due to the new abilities available to the player thanks to the new cast. Having multiple characters with enhanced mobility options (as opposed to only Gebel with flight) in a game demands some harsher design decisions to keep a solid level of challenge intact. And whilst many of the same qualities of the first game are still present (multiple, balanced paths and even the chance to clear some without the proper loadout) I feel this concept is way harder to follow in some stages (with the volcano area being the worst one and the only one I actively dislike, sadly).On the plus side you get the entire cast from the first game on top of the new ones so you get many ways to play around with all kinds of combinations. You'll also have to face more challenging bosses compared to B:CotM. I only wish we could've gotten access to the old stages with the new cast. If that were the case I would probably rate this game higher than it's predecessor.Don't let the harsh critic fool you, though. This game still sits at the top of all classicvanias without question and it is worth every cent. I would still recommend the first installment as one's first purchase since I feel it overall has the more tight design. Once done you can happily buy B:CotM2 and enjoy even more hours with quality gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Curse Of The Moon 2 is definitely a good game, but I think it is a tad bit too hard. There's a strong focus on timing (stage 5 and 6 boss) and platforming (Stage 5 in general and Stage 2's boss).And then there's Gremory. Unless you backtrack to gather the extra upgrades, each hit takes out a massive chunk of HP, squishier characters even getting instakilled, or twoshotted. Somehow, she feels much more difficult despite only having 1 phase. If she corners you, you're almost guaranteed to lose a chunk of HP if Hachi is downed or not in your party.The stage 5 boss Lavamandra is also rather annoying to fight, as it is constantly in the lava so I am constantly unable to hit them. Not only that, the burning rocks that are produced when the boss re-enters the lava are also quite hard to dodge as its patterns are a bit unpredictable, so I end up getting hit by at least one of them. It's doable, but quite difficult because you also need to have enough stamina to keep dodging the attacks.You'll definitely need quick reflexes and a keen eye to beat them.I also noticed that those robots in stage 7 are almost impossible to dodge without Dominique and Miriam, and you must destroy them before they hit you.I did manage to beat stage 5, 6, and 7 in veteran in episode 1 and 2, but I was already on my knees when trying to beat them in the final episode, even with the returning party members. Everything hit so hard that my party was already on their way out by the time I reached the boss, only to get doubly trashed by them, yikes!As a side note, If there is going to be a Curse Of The Moon 3, Please make it easier than this, but still more challenging than Curse 1.Regardless, Curse Of The Moon 2 is still a good game, but is a tad bit too hard without backtracking. Regardless, every time I stop playing, I'm already raring to go for another round! I highly recommend buying it if you enjoy the classicvania games!Additional note: My experience became a lot better after unlocking Ultimate Zangetsu. If you are willing to push through, you'll have a wonderful reward waiting for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Even more entertaining and difficult than the first game.Curse of the Moon 2 offers a new plethora of levels, characters and bosses that make the game feel fresh and highly replayable. The levels are even bigger than the first game, with much more alternative routes to explore thanks to the expanded cast of 7 playable characters, and each level feels more unique with less repetition of monsters and castles that the first game had.Along with the return of the original cast of characters, the new 3 playable characters offer interesting options to both traverse the levels and face the dangerous monsters that Curse of the Moon 2 posses. Dominique serving as an hybrid of mage and mid-range fighter with a high jump and her pogo moveset, Robert with sniper capabilities along with interesting movement options for both crouching and wallcling, and Hachi as the heavy character that can take quite the beating while also offering a temporal jetpack to traverse air space.And the big plate are the bosses, these have been designed to be even more challenging than the ones in CotM 1 to keep up with the higher powerlevel of the characters. And boy, some of the bosses are truly nerve wracking, they will be relentless, punishing and may even feel unfair, but that's part of the fun (The game also gives an advantage to the player by leaving the boss at half health if you managed to damage it enough).The game still keeps the difficulty slider if you want a more forgiving experience, and this sequel added a new difficulty level for hardcore players. I haven't had the chance to play with a second player at my side, but the option is there if you have a friend and want to wreck the levels together.Truly a fun experience that combines the best of old and modern.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2

_childDocuments_.review: Finally getting around to this one and got all achievements. More of the first game, but better. Most of this game's difficulty is all the trial and error on the bosses so you WILL die a lot. You can't really react to bosses, you just have to learn what their cues are or just anticipate their next move. And every attempt requires a walk of shame back to the boss door, but the first episode is forgiving and places that checkpoint one screen over. Later episodes assume you're familiar and place it maybe 3 rooms back. One tip I can give is to just watch a video of the boss fight so you can get a feel of what the boss does before doing it yourself if you wish save time.The COTM series is a refinement and tribute to the Castlevania 3 formula, which is my favorite classic Castlevania, and I do appreciate that the roster this time isn't a near copy and paste of the Castlelvania 3 characters. I think retro-tribute games copy TOO much from their source instead of taking the opportunity to build on what came before.The UI here is polished up a bit more too, getting rid of the score and showing a progress bar to your next 1up. Boss healthbars show here too so you know how much further you have to go, how much damage you're doing and to show bosses don't restore all their health between attempts so you can whittle them down. I like the episode structure in this one where in the previous game was about the recruitment/kill choice you made in the first mode to unlock other modes.  so there is a bit more content here than the first.

While fair, the game is significantly harder than the first title, play that first especially if you're not a big fan of the linear Castlevania games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is chalk-full of variety. While not as good as its predecessor, it was still enjoyable. The formula is back, and it now contains more substance than it did before. However, assuming that you were exposed to this series because you are a classic-style 'Castlevania' fan, it might disappoint you because it feel like it was trying to take a step away from that formula (according to my opinion).

_childDocuments_.review: If you like classic Castlevania, controls INCLUDED, you'll likely enjoy this.If the only thing you didn't like about classic Castlevania was the stiff, hypercommital controls, you're going to have a bad time here.In Curse Of The Moon, you push a button and you wait. Sword swing? Wait. Jump? Wait. And you'd better hope you didn't fat-finger the input, because a neutral jump is just up and down, you're locked in, there's no air control, you're perpetually eating the consequences of a decision you made a second ago.There's also a lot of weirdly precise inputs, like the down pogo, and unintuitive ones like the air hover (which you can't engage midway through a jump arc, only at the beginning by holding jump.)These controls don't vibe with me. I play like a mess, perpetually jamming on buttons to try and rectify my last input, and this is a control scheme designed to punish that. I liked the previous Curse Of The Moon, and stuff like Shovel Knight, and La Mulana, and every GBA Castlevania, but couldn't find any enjoyment here.Again, this isn't a bad game, and if you like classic Castlevania controls you'll have a good time. But if you're like me, and you don't, then you should probably wait for the next mainline Bloodstained instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is MUCH more difficult than the first Curse of the Moon.  If you played the first one and thought it was super easy, like I did, then this game will definitely surprise you with the level of challenge.  To get the true ending of the game, you have to beat it three times which is a bit excessive.  Having said that, the way they split things up in the third playthrough was actually fairly interesting by letting you choose which stage to go to for your allies.  It's also completely randomized which is interesting.  Graphics and sound are pretty much on par with the first game, though it doesn't really make much sense how this game could follow the first.  Either way, this game is definitely worth a playthrough if you want a challenge.  It's worth persevering.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my favorite 2D platformer of all time. The way that it requires every character to work in sync to progress, the exploration elements, and the challenging difficulty make it an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a good classicvania-type title. To fully complete it, you'll have to replay the game 2-3 times, but the game manages to keep itself interesting by removing or adding in new playable characters every play-through so that different routes are forced upon you, thus causing your experience to vary drastically each time. One complaint I do have though is that the final level shouldn't have been omitted from the final play-through, and there should be a way to play through the final final one without having to go through that weird mini-game.

_childDocuments_.review: CoTM 2 is a great sequel to the first game, with new characters and game mechanics. Though, I have to warn you that this game is VERY difficult if you decide to do it on "Veteran". CoTM 1's Veteran is equal to CoTM 2's Casual style, to be honest. It borrows many elements from Castlevania 3 to begin with, like more deathtraps, spikes and moving platforms (many clocktower elements). Fans put the difficulty between CV3 and Dracula X on "Veteran", so if you want a fair challenge that's more like Castlevania 1 and CoTM 1 then "Casual" it is (it won't be easy either, last stage of episode 1 has around 34% completion rate). The new characters are interesting and you'll have to learn each one's abilities to proceed to the next stage and find all the secrets. Conclusion: A huge Improvement in every aspect compared to the first game, but IGA and Inti decided to make it somehow much more difficult, so at first you might not enjoy it but you can get better at it definitely with practice. Just get ready to repeat a stage or a sequence a lot if you decide to challenge it on "Veteran".
