_childDocuments_.review: SOLAS 128 is a good game that is also very annoying at times.the puzzles in themselves are interesting, intricate, with clear set rules and solutions that are fun to engineer and iterate on BUT there are more than a few times where I was completely stumped not because I couldn't come up with the solution but because I was completely unable to identify a key element of a puzzle, it could be me missing that the current screen share a few tiles with an adjacent screen that can be used to share props, or me missing that a certain tile under a beam isn't stripped and that I can place props on it...I felt more challenged by the game not being able to convey these crucial pieces of information than by my capacity to actually solve the puzzles, I'd estimate that I spent around 3 to 4 hours banging my head trying to solve puzzles while I missed key component to actually succeed. You may fare better than me in this regard but it was an issue common enough for me that I can't overlook it.If you're into puzzle games and are interested in the visuals / music of SOLAS 128, definitely check it out but keep in mind that it can be misleading at times and that you should reevaluate what the setpieces you can play with actually are when you're unusually stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Decently challenging game with simple mechanics and plenty of RGB. The soundtrack has some nice bangers in there, too. One cool gameplay mechanic is the use of time -- many levels aren't as simple as "memorize solution, rearrange pieces" because they often require dynamic actions such as hitting toggle switches, blocking other beams temporarily (and in the right order), creating self-sustaining mini-loops, moving a piece around repeatedly to bounce a laser to a separate area, repurposing a setup to accommodate a new objective, etc. You'll also need to be able to adapt to timing errors when beats don't sync up, and be able to recover from mistakes. Overall, this game is a lot more "active" than your typical laser-style puzzler. Check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to begin with this game in terms of a review....there is so much to say and so little space to say it.SOLAS 128 is a very slick timing color-change-match machine puzzle box that requires players to use mirrors to bounce the colors around, combine them into other colors, and make sure that you are able to open the next door.  Your task is to fix the broken music box, a la ghost in the machine.  Along the way, you will have to fight a glitch in the system in order to restore order to the machine.Above was a very general overview of this game.  There is so much more to this game that that overview does not even give justice to how amazing this game is.  As usual, here are the pros and cons (neutrals, too) of this game:Pros:* Absolutely ingenious level design.  Everything works perfectly, all puzzles scale in difficulty at just the right pacing, and every new puzzle you are able to beat is an absolute thrill when you finally do it.  Almost every puzzle is able to be solved in only one way, but the developer of this game has made it so that you can actually solve some of the puzzles in more than one way, which is a neat idea.* New mechanics are introduced at a steady and appreciable rate that makes this game just right in terms of difficulty, while continuing to add new mechanics to make sure that the game is never boring for long.  All of the added mechanics not only add to the genius that is the level design, but also makes you think in more ways than one, which is always a good thing.* Even after you've beaten the game, there are more challenges for you to go beat, including .  This keeps the game fresh well after you've beaten it, but you will never have the same joy as you had when you first beat the game.  Just watch out for some difficulty spikes in the !* The pacing of the game is excellent.  In order to pretty much complete this game 100%, a casual player should expect to play no less than 20 hours to complete this game to the fullest extent.  A lot of this time will be spent fiddling with the different pieces to get the right combination in order to make the puzzle work.* The music for this game fits this game so well that there are literally no words to describe how absolutely incredible it is.  This whole game was designed around the music, and you will definitely need to have the music on in order to get everything out of this game that you want to.* The price point is absolutely fair for the amount of content you get.  You will easily get at least twice as many hours per dollar.  This game is worth it even without it being on sale.Neutral*  Not going to ding you for that.**The music can end up becoming too grating after listening to it for a few hours.  Not sure how to fix this without breaking the game, so no ding for this.*I think that there was so much more than this game could have done to make it a true master puzzle game.  It already is a master puzzle game, but there's just so many things you could do with this game that I think it would make sense to possibly make a DLC for this game at some point in time.Cons:*   This game would be  if there was a level designer and Steam Workshop support.  I know that it would take a lot of work to make something like this happen, but trust me when I say that it will definitely be worth it!Overall, this game has given me one of the best puzzle game experiences since playing The Witness, and I do not regret buying this game at full price.  Everything just clicks and works in unison to create an absolutely mesmerizing experience. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: An original and great puzzle game that gently ramps up in difficulty introducing new mechanics just as you feel like you're mastering it. The mechanics are all related to light so feel intuitive and satisfying to learn. Each screen is a puzzle on its own but always connects to the next in a vast chain of reflecting, merging, filtering and splitting lights.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this, after a few hours (my playtime count is wrong, I think due to being offline). Not many reviews, so figured it deserves an early thumbs-up.It's a reflecting laser puzzle game with a bunch of unique twists. You have to get different coloured lines to their exits by placing and rotating pieces that change their direction, split them apart, and so on. The laser lines have discrete pulses moving along them which can collide with other pulses to change their directions, blend colours, and so on. Those pulse mechanics add a lot on top of the old laser formula, and are used really well in the puzzle design.Puzzle design is what makes or breaks a game like this, and it's on point here. Things often look deceptively easy, and then you run into the hidden snag and have to use creative thinking to find a way around it. So far it has been complex enough in places that I had to take a break, but nothing has been so hard that I couldn't solve it when I came back, and it hasn't started throwing so many elements together that it feels overwhelming to work through all the possibilities. It's more about giving you a handful of pieces to use in a clever way than about making you work through a million options until you find the one which works.A really nice aspect of the game is that it isn't just single-screen puzzles. That's what you'll be solving most of the time, but the puzzles also feed into each other, and the whole game is one giant meta-puzzle. Sometimes you have to solve one screen before you can solve another, or you may have to make some temporary solutions to get somewhere, then come back and change the routes and outputs to complete a bigger puzzle involving multiple rooms. It isn't overdone, and you're usually just trying to solve one thing at a time; it makes things more interesting without getting in the way.If you like this kind of game you should definitely pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This game expands the "redirect laser beams" mechanic you often see in minigames and turns it into a proper full puzzle game with minimalist but engaging graphics and sound. I really liked how the solved puzzles link together into a coherent system that feels a bit like a construction/exploration game. Really satisfying sense of progression for hours

_childDocuments_.review: . The puzzles, the secrets, the soundtrack, and how all of it connects with each other. There's a demo available, if you're having doubts. The worst I can say is that even after 24 hours of playtime, I still struggle with the timing of the laser beams, and that the secret minigame is too RNG-dependent, but neither issue will impact your playthrough of the main game.

_childDocuments_.review: While I think the comparison with The Witness is not quite correct, this is still one of the best logic puzzles in recent memory. Every time I felt I had figured it all out, there was something new to discover, as well as inventive new ways to use the things I already knew. Definitely a worthwhile purchase for anyone that likes this genre, with surprising depth of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Really easy to click with the game. Challenging enough to stay engaging but never too hard. Some puzzles seems to have unintended solutions. Visuals can get annoying, but there's options to turn down the different effects.Only negative is that on the low spec system I have, it can desync, and you need to wait for the light to travel through 30-ish screens. Probably not a common problem.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, one of the best puzzle games I've ever played. The mechanics are basic yet the game gets a lot of mileage out of them, the difficulty curve increases both by complexity of individual rooms as well as ratcheting up how large-scale any puzzle is - from single-screen at the start to entire areas become one gigantic interconnected puzzle by the end. And that's not even getting started on the bonus puzzles, which both have some of the most inventive uses of mechanics and which turn the entire game map into a tool - the last bonus section in particular is just some of the most clever, galaxy-brain puzzling I think I've ever done. This game makes me feel like a mad genius every time I clear a particularly difficult puzzle. It's also the perfect length, I feel - explores its mechanics thoroughly but never burns itself out or gets tedious and ends when it feels like it should end. I could complain about minor things - a few really touchy screens, the very occasional jank, the soundtrack ending up getting kinda repetitive due to how much time you spend in each area, but that's like... nitpicking at best, and the core of what's here is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool it barely matters. You're missing out if you don't pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This is a contender for my favourite puzzle game of all time.I have played literally hundreds of puzzle games, to the point where I am basically burned out on puzzles... so when I saw Solas 128 I thought "uh-huh... lasers, mirrors, yada yada" but boy oh boy was that initial assessment wrong!This game takes what seem like familiar puzzle elements, adds some brilliant twists and builds a huge sequence of constantly surprising puzzles from them. Time and again it hits you with those "wait but that's impossible" problems, before delighting you with your own genius a few minutes later. On top of that, the puzzles are all integrated into a single overworld, so that they connect and interact with each other, adding another mind-blowing layer to the experience. It's a vast intricate clockwork construction of utter perfection.Side note: this is the first game *ever* to scratch the itch that SpaceChem (my very favourite puzzle game... until now??) left permanently burned into my mind. There's something similar about the spatial reasoning here... searching for just the right shape to create the pattern that you need. It's a beautiful thing.(FYI the mouse cursor behaves very weirdly, I recommend just using the arrow/spacebar keys even though it's a little slow)
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting and challenging puzzle. Zero words, except for those in options(fun fact - even those have translations). Starting levels may seem easy and plain, but give game a chance and progress a bit further :)Music is synced with particles which adds some additional layer to the game. However in some parts of the game music impacts some psychological pressure and heavily distracts from the puzzle itslef. In most levels this is unrelated.Also there are secrets to unlock, which I'm currently in pursue of.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle gameIt is very easy to get into this game. Every mechanic is carefully presented to you in a very clean way so that you can use them in your solutions. You can see what the game is about by simply looking at the screenshots. The only flaw in it are the visuals. I'd recommend turning off all visual effects as soon as you start the game. The "intended" look of the game simply hurts the eyes
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know... The game was fun at the beginning but got annoying real fast, as a software dev logic is not my problem, unexplained and obfuscated logic is! This game is like reading code with var names like v1, v2, v3 and f1, f2, f3 for functions, yeah I know, you can handle code this way but it's not fun, it's annoying! Some mirrors can reflect on both sides, some can't? The splitters look almost identical which was confusing. The final straw was the stupid switches, that made me Alt+F4 real fast. Yeah, some could argument you can do trial and error to figure things out, but not me, not in logic games (it's more puzzle than logic)! Don't get me wrong I like figuring stuff out on my own but not in this case. The other thing that bugged me was the glow of the level walls.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Darn, I can't remember having such a negative reaction to a puzzle game so soon after starting it.Right away the complete lack of information on how to play the game put me off. There is no text on the menu screen, only those obscure icons that you can only understand the purpose of after you have clicked on them, and even then not always.I'll admit that I should have read the Steam description page more closely but since I have played and enjoyed numerous mirror puzzle games I thought this would be a sure bet. I'm not too keen on puzzles that involve colours, but perhaps I could learn to like them if the game explained what I am supposed to be doing.Perhaps there are interesting puzzle but I'm not willing to put the time into this game because the developers weren't willing to put ANY time into explaining the rules of the game to me (except for more obscure icons).
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Game is really good. Extremely good. I love everything about it, from the music to the aesthetic to the puzzles themselves. I'm just not smart enough for it.The hint system did a good job of helping me through some of the puzzles I was looking at wrong and got stuck on in the early/mid game.The hint system is fully disabled in the late game and that's why I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: I have played about the amount I would consider a " chapter " to be, and played a bit beyond that to see some advanced mechanics at play.pretty chill experience so far. The puzzles involve you refracting light by moving little angled pieces ( and other pieces that interact differently ) The lights have lil bumps on em, and your goal is to get those bumps to the goal zones on each part of the level area, so you can open up the next path. All of this happens even if you don't see it, so some puzzles involve you working around a room for a bit, going back and forth to complete the circuit.you also get multicolored lights that; when connecting to another color, start to branch off in different angles, and coping with that to get past areas has been pretty fun so far. the aesthetics are rather nice, it's quaint and  not overly busy ( aside of some cutscene-y type things, but those aren't too often ) you can also undo, and fast forward time ( if you're impatient ) - something the intro shows you, haha. It was a neat touch.I'll update this if any real issues occur, or I feel liek expanding on what I've written so far. As of right now? I'm into it. it's a different type of puzzle game, no time limits, no panic - just time to site, vibe, and work them out at your own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This might seem like a lot to pay for a puzzle game, but it offers over 150 levels that are going to progressively get harder and harder and challenge you for many hours!It's just a laser light game where you use mirrors and other items to reflect, combine, and separate colored lasers to get them to their destinations.  This is not the first puzzle game to do this, but I love this one!  I also love the music while you play at your own pace and leisure.  You can adjust the sounds and music and even turn the game music off if you don't like it.Love it, Highly Recommended.. especially if you like well designed puzzle games!My Score:  9 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most tedious puzzle game I will ever give a thumbs up.* Can't see deactivated switches or placement blockers under filter beams. Not clear why beams couldn't have been translucent in some fashion? Just weird choice.* Any puzzle that spanned multiple tiles (which is where a lot of the interesting stuff happens, obv) was made so much worse by the way you move between tiles. It was fun for about 5 minutes to navigate by way of "continuing the beam" or whatever, but after setups get more complex and the sensation of shepherding a single beam is gone, the tile movement became a major impediment. ESPECIALLY BAD were the puzzles that required you to move mirrors or blockers between tiles, because that inevitably meant tons of clicking back and forth to examine or move things around.Despite all that it's creative and fun. There's just some infuriating oversights.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing puzzle game! Was frustrating at times, but in a good way. Excellent difficulty ramping/introduction of concepts. An excellent  of the concepts, which can be difficult to pull off, and to top it all off, some post game content/secrets, which is always nice to see in a puzzle game. All around, I'd give it a 9/10. Only not giving it a 10/10 cause 1 or 2 puzzles were really frustrating. But yeah, excellent game, highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: because i am smartand i like to dancewith my brainand not with my fat assThere's a fast-forward feature, but I almost never used it because it also fast-forwards the music. Not skipping bangers like that.My only real complaint about this game is how long animations/screen transitions are. I know this game looks gorgeous, but I still would like to jump between rooms without looking at a crosshair gently flowing where I want it to go.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This game Ratatouilled me back to when all the neighborhood kids had the N64s and I was playing ancient DOS games on a Gateway 2000. One of the ones I liked was a puzzle game called Laser Light, It was clunky and punished mistakes, so it was more like playing laser golf with a sledgehammer, but when I'd get my laser to all the targets on the first try, it was a rush. For some reason there were fruit lying around and you'd get points for burning your laser through them. Bit weird, but at least it promoted a healthy lifestyleSOLAS 128 is not Laser Light, thankfully. I haven't seen any fruit, but I'm keeping my eyes peeled. I still get that same rush from burning through a few levels in a row though, as my beam zooms from room to room. It's not really an entry level puzzle game, but not too inaccessible by any means. The rooms are woven together in a nontrivial way, There's some nice storytelling without words. The soundtrack is wonderful. Pick this up when you can.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Although its an excellent puzzle game, I found that the line will randomly reset, thus cutting off everything and to reactivate it, I have to navigate to the room that misfired (even if I already solved it) and follow the line back to where it needs to be. All in all though, fantastic game involving the use of lights. Just be ready for frustration
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing puzzle game. Everything about it is good. Music, puzzles, atmosphere, secrets. Although the game may be lacking a more obvious story, and some of the puzzles may have some difficulty ramping issues, its very easy to look past these faults and just enjoy the puzzles.It's a shame this game doesn't have enough reviews to get an overwhelmingly positive score on steam. It totally deserves it.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the great music while solving the puzzles. The visuals are pleasing as well.Took me just under a day of play time total to complete the game (including all the optional content).There were only a few leaps in understanding which I got stuck on.Upon returning to the game after taking a break each time helped a lot with getting past them.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I found recently. It never really feel like you're just solving a series of isolated rooms, but actively progressing through the map, bit by bit. Working with the more open areas was especially fun.Oh yeah, the music is also great. Never expected a puzzle game to sound that good.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Certainly there can't be a Metroidvania-Deflektor right? Oops, wrong again. Enter SOLAS 128.While still at early stages upon writing the review, already I'm filled with positive vibes and expectations. The atmosphere is truely unique, calming and inviting to crack the light reflection/spectrum/angle puzzles. I don't really have anything clear to complain so far, everything has been so painstakingly designed so far, be it the puzzles or the user UI. If I have to knack about something, maybe the area based soundtrack starts to be a bit too repetitive due to long time spent on the respective areas.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: What a surprise in the puzzle genre. Have played other games involving  mirrors, lasers, and color combination. It is worth your time. Puzzles run the gambit from easy to head scratching. Didn't spend the time played as indicated. As I would leave it running and come back to it periodically. Wish I would have known the last achievement is time dependent. Still a lot of game and have nothing but praise for the developer and the puzzle design.  I definitely enjoyed my time playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect combination of tricky puzzles, gorgeous graphics and ridiculously good music. It begins by introducing you to new concepts and teaching you new mechanics before letting you discover how and when to use them. The puzzles go from fairly straightforward to delightfully difficult, but by that point there are often several different puzzles you need to solve, meaning if you get stuck on one there is still something else to try! I absolutely recommend this to anyone who loves puzzles games.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: The background is trippy, but there are settings to make it better - the same with the shaking and trippy affects - that seem to have no function except to make it harder to concentrate on the puzzles.  The lazer puzzles themselves are very clever and make me think a lot.  The 3 hints I've had to use so far (seem to be about 1/3 of the way through) were helpful but not too detailed.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the main content and liked it overall, but were things that drove me nuts as well.Starting with the good; a lot of the puzzles are good and many require an interesting flavour of out of the box thinking with many tasteful curve-balls. It's hard to say more about it without spoiling anything. If you're into puzzle games you owe it to yourself to look into this one as there's a big chance it offers something you have not seen before (once you make it far enough).And the bad; the entire game feels like it woke up still drunk from the night before. Everything feels sluggish and imprecise. I usually have a relatively high tolerance for this kind of stuff, but this game is does it pretty bad. Everything takes way too much time for no good reason. Strongly, strongly disliked it.To elaborate: at some point you will start working on puzzles that are larger than one screen and moving between screens is incredibly slow, making looking around to get an overview a pain in the ass. You can't move to adjacent screens unless there's a button for it, even if you have unlocked the screen, which in turn force you either to slowly jump from screen to screen or use the map which has to pan (slowly) to the screen you want to go to. Adding to that, the cursor movement is smoothed out, making it feel mushy and heavy, hover feedback is slow, it sort of snaps to things when when you get close in an unpleasant way.The puzzles are good though which is what counts in the end, even if I liked them as much as I disliked interacting with the game itself.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: It's hindered at times by some odd design choices, strange balancing, and lack of any explicit communication; and it could *really* use a little more music. However, there's a solid core here that is very compelling when it works, with several stretches of rooms that deliver on the premise of interconnected puzzles that feed back into themselves. There are lots of fun "aha!" moments along the way, but be prepared to be stuck on a few rooms without anywhere else to go.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Try the demo. Solas 128 has some novel ideas to play with and manages to merge the theming with the core mechanics. You'll listen to bumpy electronic music, while trying to synchronize or desynchronize lines of moving bits.Solas is quite clever for the most part, but sort of falls apart midgame when you start to hit rooms that stress your ability to merge bits back together. However, I never really felt that I had really learned how to math out how to manipulate bit timing and I feel that Solas didn't really tutorialize the skill at any point by the time I really needed it.Overall I recommend the game, but be aware that you may end up on tilt at some point in some rooms and start brute forcing the puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit bizarre understanding if I am making progress or undoing some of it, until I see that the maze is completing its separate rooms to towards the main completion. I cant really describe this game other than using mirrors to deflect the light sources to each desired goal. Light sources can merge to create diagonal paths if the "beat" is the same and change colour to meet the target. So far, I have played 4 hours and enjoying this, so I will continue. The menu interface is well confusing and dont understand what the symbols really mean, so I press a button with fear of either wiping out my progress or something else. Im too scared to hit some. Any it does seem to auto save a specific points. Good game.Update: I have reached my intellectual and frustration limit now as I cant seem to find a way to progress further. The switch gates have hampered my progress and cant find the unlock. Also, I think I have undone some of my work and its become too tedious for me to continue despite the completed map looking quite full. So, I still recommend this game as its totally not like any other game I played but like many logic games, I never finish them totally,
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Bouncing light puzzles but one giant interconnected machine. Everything moves to the background music which while it has no gameplay purpose it just makes everything feel great.Built in hint system if you get stuck. Starts out easy but eventually I got to the point of solving one room a day. The solutions are always fair and make you want to think outside the box instead of just brute forcing stuff which is great puzzle design. Putting this as one of my steam gems!
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: The game caught my interest as a step up from "light beam" puzzles with the added rhythm aspect, and I have to say it's very well-executed. A few points get a bit confusing as it's unclear which of the branching paths you need to take next, but overall reuse of previous rooms is very well done. Great music, great puzzles, just overall well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: I am fairly new to puzzle games, the only one I have played before this was The Witness, but like that game Solas128 does a good job of slowly teaching you the principles you need to solve the puzzles while adding more and more layers of complexity, all conveyed without words. The puzzles are sometimes quite challenging for a novice like me but all the more satisfying when I've solved them. I really like the visual style and the music and sound design are excellent and work well with the visuals. I have found that the strong colours and music can become a bit trying after extended periods of play, but that is mainly the result of my becoming stuck in certain sections for some time, and can be solved by adjusting the games volume and contrast settings. Over all I would recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Having played and loved the Prologue, it's been a pleasure getting into the full SOLAS. This is a thoroughly absorbing puzzle game and one that's highly immersive - the music and rhythmic feel to the whole thing, combined with the eye-catching computer world it all takes place in, make it easy to get stuck. The light manipulating mechanics are clever and puzzles require satisfyingly cunning solutions. Highly recommended puzzle game to chill with.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Love this puzzle game working with mirrors and light beams. It starts off easy but progressively gets more challenging – each screen is connected to the previous which can add to the challenge as the game processes!  I certainly recommend this game which is created by one developer based in Edinburgh. Well done and thanks…
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: The game has an amazing aesthetic, and the gameplay is pretty fun. The puzzles are fairly well balanced, being hard without being too difficult (most of the time at least). I love the way that some of the puzzles also interact with one another, leading to some pretty intertwined challenges. Would definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Whatever you do, do not be fooled by the low rating on the ArmorGames demo. This is very well-executed and it's healthy for the brain to be forced to think about how to apply the mechanics without a wordy tutorial. The use of symbols to communicate everything is absolutely exquisite . The music pulsating with the patterned paths is catchy and the dark tone is just epic.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: SOLAS 128 is a cyberpunk style puzzle game with a retro arcade feel.The puzzles are very satisfying, and starts off easy, then progressively gets more difficult and complex. The puzzle itself is one giant puzzle that is solved in many smaller parts, which are unlocked as you progress through the game.The synthwave style music is fitting, but gets repetitive. The music does change as you move to different sections of the game, and if you do find it getting repetitive, you can always turn off the music and keep the sound affects on; The other sound effects are quite nice too.The game makes good use of symbols that are easy to understand, and help to guide the player through the game. There's also a fast forward button at the bottom of the screen that can speed you through some of the slower bits of levels, if you are feeling a bit impatient. If you are struggling with any of the levels, there is a hint button at the top of the screen (the question mark).There's a purposeful glitch effect through the game, as well as shaking, which can make the experience more immersive for some, though if you do not enjoy this, you can turn these effects off in the settings, as well as alter the quality of the graphics, and contrast of the colors.I also appreciated that there are 3 save slots, which is handy if more than one family member wants to give it a try.This game provides for an impressive list of 29 languages at the time of this review.Themes:No violence or adult themes, making it family friendly.***~ House Blythe, curator for Non-violent Entertainment:
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed SOLAS 128, it is a very nice and tricky game!  Like all high quality puzzle games, you have to think out of the box to be able to finish all the puzzles. Moreover, the interconnected puzzles and the mistery behind the this broken machine give a metroidvania flavour to the gameplay.  And with this well-made gameplay and puzzles, you have synthwave musics and neon-style graphics which recalls the 80s.If you like challenging puzzle games, go for it!
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute belter of a game. If you're into puzzle games, you should definitely pick this up.The "bounce lasers off mirrors" idea may sound derivative, but Solas manages to make it interesting again. The light beams have symbols travelling along them to the beat, and these can interact - if they collide the colours combine and the combined beam changes direction. So sometimes you need to get the symbols to line up, sometimes they need to be out of step so the beams can pass through each other. Combined beams can be separated with splitters - there's lots going on here, and the game introduces them at just the right rate to keep things interesting.The symbols on the beams also allow you to differentiate between them without relying on colour, so the game is accessible to colourblind players.At the start, each room is self-contained, but soon you find you need to solve a room one way to make progress in one direction, and later rewire it to go somewhere else. By the end you're directing beams across the void between rooms and you've got several puzzles working together towards a solution. There's real artistry in the puzzle crafting here.It's also one of those games that manages to teach you about new mechanics almost without you realizing it.  Apart from the first two rooms, which cover the absolute basics, you're never told to click on anything, rather you're taught by example from the initial setup of a room.Once the main game is complete and the credits have rolled there are various secret areas to find. The only thing about Solas I didn't like was a minigame that can be unlocked by finding all the secrets, but that's a very minor criticism that doesn't detract from the triumph of the game itself.Buy this thing.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Rythm and laser-bouncing puzzle with just a few tweaks and changes to make sure it brings enough to the table to be original, while the game itself constantly introduces cool new mechanics. One of the best puzzle games I've played in a while. If you are curious, try the free demo : It marvellously shows off some great puzzles and teases the game very well.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gem of a puzzle game where you control a beam of light as it moves around the levels. Easy to get into, intuitive and very pleasing to play. The simplicity begins to fall away as, piece by piece, the puzzle gets more challenging. The way the game introduces new elements in a very simple and staggered way stop it from becoming overwhelming. Not that it's easy - at times it's joyfully frustrating, but it's incredibly satisfying when you finally solve it.Throughout it all is a fantastic synthwave soundtrack that beats in time with the movement of the pulses of light, making it an oddly relaxing and tricky experience at the same time. The rhythm of those pulses even become a part of the puzzle at times.I can sometimes find puzzle games off-puting when they can get to a point where I just can't solve them any more, but Solas always feels possible to solve, even when stuck. Masterfully put together, it's well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Very smart puzzle game that leaves you scratching your head. Love the fact that all of the puzzles interconnect, and it's a little scary to have dismantle the answer to one puzzle in order to solve the next. Found it quite difficult (in a good way), but the hint system was a tad frustrating, especially being turned off in the late game. Had to check a guide a few times as I just found myself completely stumped without a clue where to get started.Thoroughly enjoyable though, and good fun.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: SOLAS 128 is a great game and has a beautiful atmosphere. The level design is very well done, and the soundtrack is excellent too, reminiscent of the Miami hotline style. This game is not easy, but the player has the option to ask for clues to solve the puzzles. In addition, the game is huge. I played 7 hours and completed 50% or less of the game. Score: 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting and good take on the pipework style of puzzle games, combining it into one overarching meta puzzle at the same time. Has a lot of lightbulb moments when you figure out the solution, but (so far!) hasn't been so obtuse in getting there. Especially like the little after action reports when you collect a glyph and can track the various light beams through out the map.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game!Really enjoyed my time with it and I couldn't stop bopping my head up and down while solving the intricate connections.Be warned, it gets hard and you can sometimes feel at a loss for where to work your solutions.Take your time. Take breaks. Don't overthink it.Overall, really good game with great visuals and sound.9/10 (sometimes I found some solutions a bit far fetched)
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: SOLAS 128 is a puzzle game where you bounce light around puzzle rooms, combining or splitting colours and aim to get them to the corresponding gates to move to the next room.All accompanied by a chill synthwave soundtrack that helps keep you zoned into the experience.  There's a mysterious and intriguing vibe to the game which keeps you wanting to explore and figure out what's ultimately happened to the machine.The game is colourblind friendly, since all the different colours are accompanied by symbols and a wealth of other visual options.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Congratulations on the BAFTA award!This is no ordinary beam deflection game. Don't let the slightly overused core mechanic put you off. In SOLAS 128, beam deflection is only a tiny scratch on the surface. You will find yourself intrigued by the wordless story-telling, the way that every level in the game is connected and running at the same time, allowing for puzzles that utilise several screens of puzzles at once later on. It feels almost metroidvania-like in its design, introducing new mechanics slowly over the introductory levels, opening up new areas and abilities. And the entire thing is set to a banger soundtrack that fantastically complements the gameplay. Another major aspect is accessibility, with tweaking options for colour-blind players among others.I seriously cannot recommend it enough to anyone who enjoys puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle to express what a good puzzle game gives; what this game gives in spades. Mechanically, it's a laser puzzle, built holistically by a top-notch puzzle setter, and if that's enough for you, and no reason why it shouldn't be, you'll have a fun and rewarding time.But that does rather feel like a placeholder for the algorithm gods. The game *is* special and mustn't get lost, but I do hope one day to be able to explain my experience with it, at least to meaningfully thank the devs. Hope you find it.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

_childDocuments_.review: Explore SOLAS 128, a game of interconnected puzzles where you redirect and reconfigure rhythmic pulses of light to breathe life back into an ancient machine.
_childDocuments_.name: SOLAS 128

name: Clea 2
detailed_description: Four years have passed since the Whitlock Mansion tragedy. Florine, a former maid, is determined to resurrect the person who means everything to her. To succeed, she must travel past the third dimension and into the realms beyond. Otherworldly horrors lie in wait, but Florine is determined to soldier on. This, after all, is her final chance at redemption. * * * Skill-focused horror: Clea 2 is primarily a test of skills. Enemies roam the halls dynamically in real-time, reacting to the players' every noise. Clea is a challenging title, rewarding those who have mastered its mechanics. No jump scares: Clea 1 was a jump scare free experience, and the tradition continues here in this sequel. Replayability: Unlockable costumes/galleries/difficulty modes, multiple endings and even an arcade feature. Plenty of reasons for Florine to revisit her journey. Fully voiced: Every cutscene is fully voiced. Please enjoy the cast’s performance as we sink deeper into Clea’s lore than ever before. * * * Thank you for all your support with Clea throughout 2019. I hope this sequel is everything you have dreamed of and more. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Tension Driven Players Clea 2 is more of what made Clea 1 such an interesting experience: a game that puts tension at the forefront more then anything else. The focus on sound in order to sneak around enemy monsters still feels unique enough compared to others in the genre, but the layers of detail that it has within is what makes it stick out in the end. Granted, it's much of what made the first game interesting, and when it comes to evolution Clea 2 doesn't exactly do much more to expand the concept. Despite that, the tight loop of enemy paths and sneaking gameplay still works on a fundamental level, and even with having known the mechanics of the first game, I still got surprised and scared in this game as well. With that said, the story feels a little bit piece meal in its implementation, I wanted more from it as the world it creates is interesting and the characters are ones you want to see more of, but it fell a little short in that department. The visuals are nice for a weird match up of anime and paper mario in a sense,  and the atmosphere it creates can be cut with a knife. I do wish the game would have played up the possible puzzle elements more this time around, I feel the evolution of the game could have really be taken up a notch by focusing on that. And despite all of my praise for the game, it sorta feels like a Clea 1.5, an alternate route and universe compared to the first game.If you want tension, this game is for you. If you hate tension, avoid it.
_childDocuments_.name: Clea 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pros and cons are down below) If the review will be useful - drop a like so it could be useful to other people as well)Feel free to check out the gameplay here:Advantages:1. The game promised to be tense and it IS tense! I love the mechanics of the game so much! It's pretty simple (at least at the start, I haven't finished the game yet, but I'll update the comment as soon as I will so the review will be accurate)) but very entertaining nonetheless!2. The game has secondary objectives and mini challenges which is pretty cool. That really makes me wanna replay the levels and try to avoid getting noticed or avoid running. Also, you have to collect additional objects that will (I'm like 99% sure) affect the ending. I really like that as it adds a lot to replayability.3. There are a bunch of endings which is pretty cool, obviously.4. I love the style of the game. When I first saw the images on steam, I thought (honestly) "meh" but the more I play the more I like the style. There's something unique and charming about it.Disadvantages:1. If you haven't played the first game (like me), you'll be SO confused about the story! What the heck is going on? I'm 2 chapters in and I'm getting more and more confused. I keep on going through the levels and intend to finish the game because it's fun but I have no clue of what's happening. I'll update the review if something changes.2. The levels feel very empty. This game reminded me a lot of Coma and comparing the 2, I have to say that Coma's levels were filled with details. These levels (at least so far, haven't finished the game yet) are pretty bland-looking. I hope later on this will change.Overall:I haven't expected that I'll like the game so much! I'll update review and rate the game as soon as I finish it but at the moment, I strongly recommend playing it. I'm having a blast playing this title even though I don't understand the story at all. I guess, I'll have to look the first part of the game up to make some sense of the story. Thanks for reading till the end) If the review was useful - pls drop a like so it could be useful to other people as well))
_childDocuments_.name: Clea 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an unique gameplay which consists of labyrinths and where you have to hide from different monsters. I didn’t like the plot in this game, it’s too raw and there are very few storytelling scenes, because of this it’s simply impossible to describe the characters and the motives for their actions well. The game is moderately frightening, but the creepy atmosphere is always present. The game has very nice graphics (not pixelated, as in most similar games) :D I really liked this game, despite the fact that I completed it in just one evening. I recommend this game to everyone at least to get acquainted with this genre
_childDocuments_.name: Clea 2

_childDocuments_.review: OH MAN WHAT A SEQUEL! Another great game by InvertMouse we have here, Clea 2 takes the foundation of the first game and spices it up to make it interesting. New gameplay mechanics are present as well and they feel natural, If you played Clea 1 you'll feel right at home. Also Fluorine is GREAT lead, and I enjoyed her journey. The Story also more deep than Clea 1, but some of the characters kind come and go (Nacy looking at you) but either than it it's fine. Overall GREAT GAME and I recommend it to anyone who is into the genre/who has played the first game as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Clea 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to remember when and how I subscribe InvertMouse because it was a long time ago. But I always get letters from her from time to time. After I subscribed, in the first email, she asked me some questions, and I answered them. Unexpectedly, she replied that day (very fast in memory and it was not the auto-reply). After that, I was busy with my work and English was not my native language. A series of emails about questions asked by InvertMouse, because the questions are very deep and wide, and I am sorry to ignore to reply after reading.Another email series is the game recommendation and the research and development status of clea2. Seriously, seeing the sale of Clea2, I'm filled with emotion. There are all kinds of information about clea2 in the email: from demo, soundtrack, costume, upgrade, wallpaper and expression pack, to the final delivery and publication. Like InverMouse and we have made Clea2 together.I hope I can find the physical version of Clea2 to collect in my lifetime.=)
_childDocuments_.name: Clea 2

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of horror games this masterpiece kept me entertained, through great storyline and challenging levels that made me have to think about different ways to approach a situation, I highly recommend playing this game as the Clea series has never disappointed, Clea 2 being an excellent sequel to the first. There are many things to do even after beating the game such as, trying harder difficulties, finding every secret, and getting every unlockable item. I don't want to spoil anything of Clea or Clea 2, but please consider playing this game, I can almost guarantee you'll like it, if not, feel free to slap me.
_childDocuments_.name: Clea 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun 2D horror game that is definitely worth the price point, since it is tense to play and has a interesting story. It also has a lot of replay value through difficulty modes, outfits you can unlock by meeting certain criteria (like Resident Evil 2 Remake with only save once or get an S rank) and leaderboards for arcade mode score.I also learned how easy it is to split my own soul orb. Worked just like splitting a bagel.
_childDocuments_.name: Clea 2

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game! Stealth-based game mainly playing hide and seek with enemies, solving simple puzzles and a slight mixture of combat. Very well done audio cues keeps the tension going. I like that this is a skill-based game where it is possible to 100% dodge the enemies. The game is not difficult once figured out how to react to different sounds. The characters are so cute and fully voiced. Recommended. Give it a try if you like games that give you some tension.
_childDocuments_.name: Clea 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Clea 1, you can pretty much expect the same thing with this game, only with another game mode added to it! However... I must admit...there's alot of cons I need to list for this game. This is not at all a bad game. I still recommend it, but I feel I need to still say what I had a problem with for this game, so that the developers can take it and hopefully learn from it, so that they may improve for their next game. I wish I could leave this as a neutral review but I can't, so a positive will have to do, as I still enjoyed my experience.Spoiler warnings below!The puzzles in this game are pretty... lackluster. They're all ultimately the same. Take item from one place to another, activate thingy in this area and go activate it in another. It was disappointing, because in Clea 1, the puzzles were different. In one of them you had to memorize the order of buttons you have to press, there were more key pieces you'd have to find and combine, there was a maze segment, etc. But all the puzzles in this game are ultimately the same, just with a different coat of paint splashed on them.The character, Nancy.... is completely unnesscary. Aesthetically she does not fit at all and her story is boring to boot with honestly no pay off. It feels like the devs kind of just shoved her in there and didn't know what to do with her afterwards. She contributes ultimately nothing to the plot and ends up dying in the end to two chaos servants. I was hoping that she was going to become an enemy. She stole Mei's gloves, and the lore behind them was that they would drive their user to madness. Yet Nancy was perfectly fine the entire time. Honestly, if she had just became an enemy at a certain point due to being driven to madness, and you would have to avoid her like the others, that would of made her far better. As is... it's just wasted potential.The extra chapters also suffer from being repetitive. All you do is find a magic circle, lure the maids there and exorcise them. The extra chapters in Clea had you playing as different characters and had different goals, and even brought forth more lore. The extra chapters in this one brought a little more lore, but that's it. It was repetitive and kind of boring...Ultimately this game suffers from being repetitive and that's unfortunate, because I loved the first game. As such, I recommend the first game more than this one. Again, this is STILL a good game, and I still plan on going through to beat all modes and difficulties, but I just cannot ignore the flaws this game has. As for positives:All characters have WONDERFUL designs! (Except Nancy, she sticks out like a sore thumb.)I still found myself getting spooked a good number of times, and I still have to learn the enemy patterns and how best to avoid them!The atmosphere is great, I was immediately on edge my first playthrough.While the fighting wasn't done perfectly, I actually enjoyed that bit. It was interesting and I wish it lasted longer.War Maiden is freaky as ♥♥♥♥ and the ending segment with running away from her is chef's kiss.Clea's Quest is a pretty fun mini game that was added into this game, that the previous one didn't have.The dimension lore is good and level design is nice.The sister character is the scariest enemy in my personal opinion and I wish there was more lore to her. I always look forward to playing her segment.This game, like the first, has lots of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: A FANTASTIC sequel to the original Clea game! The plot is simple, I had had high hopes that there would be a little more to give or expand on what happened in the first game, but sometimes simple works well too -if the player isn't being bombarded with a ton of information or backstories to remember they can focus more or be engaged more in the actual game. As ever the hand drawn characters and backgrounds are a delight to see, enemies very much replicas of the first but then they would be to an extent, the addition of new characters and finally seeing the ever spoken of War Maiden made me happy - BONUS - the new addition of a pet, simply having Mei's cat in the game made a change but then for it to be an alert enemy changed things up too. The puzzles are fairly easy to solve BUT what makes it harder is the utter labyrinth of rooms and corridors all looking the same, if you're not careful you can end up running around for an age like I did. One thing I'd love to commend has been the new features of combat and the final chapter chase scene; this never happened in the first game this is completely new and WOW, the fact that it was only a small part meant a fresh new take for recurring players like myself and stopped the game from turning into just another survival/combat horror game. The developer is great at listening to players feedback on bug fixes, additional bonus items, and what people would like to see either in the game or in the future - there are collectable dress mods, arcade (and now invisible) mode,  different difficulty settings and achievements for different endings including a secret one. I think my negative would be the same as I had for the first game; for it to be a longer game, and if that's not possible then the addition of a side quest or 2 because I want to see so much more! 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a solid sequel ill start with that.-Still keeps all aspects of the original game, as in you are gonna be tense more than once, testing your patience to avoid a game over...  (looking at you  .-Sound design: as with the first game, it is top notch, you WILL be using sound as a tool to get around and the game does this aspect beautifully.-Played with no issues on a xbox one controller, and controls in general are responsive, no issue on that end as well.-Story-wise?, play the first game before the sequel is mandatory otherwise you are going to be lost as to what is happening, liked the story as well with memorable characters.-What I like also, is that when you start the game, it gives you the option of enabling infinite saves or not, it tells you its the intended experience to play without it and encourages you to do so, but if you are not in a Resident Evil old-school typewritter ink anxiety mood, you can play however you like, it respects your time, and this is also available on the first game.-The game features several difficulty settings, an arcade mode, leaderboards to unlock extra content such as concept art and skins, heck you can find skin mods too.-In short, is a damn good sequel to an already solid first Clea title, doesn't overstay its welcome, the game is short and sweet, keeps you wanting more once you finish it... and in my book that's a good game right there.-

name: Song of Iron
detailed_description: Behind you lies a trail of broken helms, shattered shields. You hold the axe of a fallen foe. Worn and dented, it will suit it's purpose. What lies ahead is still a mystery, your goal is not. To save your people you must find the Great Temple of the Gods, but do not expect a warm welcome. Prepare to be met by a world set against you. In Song of Iron, man, monster and nature itself will try to stop you. Fight through it all in this gritty adventure where combat is intense, visceral and dangerous. Use bow, axe and shield to fight back but take care, weapons can be lost, arrows will run out and shields will be broken. With the blood of your ancestors and valor regained along the way you can fight on! Explore your ancient, and mysterious homeland as you journey through forests, into caves and climb mountains as you seek vengeance. Keep your eyes peeled, danger is all around you and when a fight is too big you may need to find a subtler way to pass foes. SONG of IRON 2 Has been announced! ABOUT RESTING RELIC Resting Relic is a solo-dev game development studio started by Joe Winter, a long time game artist and developer. Song of Iron is the first title by the new studio which seeks to bring unique, beautiful and rewarding games to people everywhere looking for a high quality escape. Join the Discord Community!

_childDocuments_.review: If Limbo, Inside and Black the Fall had a Viking lovechild with combat, that fully bearded fetus would be Song of Iron.  This is some solo dev on game action that absolutely looks and sounds the part but does it play the part?  Whew, that's a tough one.  Just when you thought it was safe to go back into your review scroll, here comes this jagoff with the obligatory, "I wish there was a neutral rating," rant to spoil your day.  I am your cliche.  I wish Song of Iron was a landscape photography book.  Seriously, I could look at that sh*t all day long in awe of the places I should explore one day.  The scenic environments, the sense of scale when you climb, those Viking vs mountain moments, scenic rivers and streams...  As a hunter, fisherman and general outdoorsy wanderer when I can be, I could wax poetic about the graphics all day.  The natural flora and fauna of this game is truly something to behold. They're fantastic for a sidescroller of this ilk.  Character design (your hero, monsters, enemies) are all solid as well, everything coming together to put the 3-D into the 2-D.  The sound is well-done too but it's nowhere near the majesty of the graphical design on display here.  Storywise you get what seems to be a basic Viking revenge opera and when playing a game involving a Viking on a rampage I'm quite fine without a Shakespearean level of auteur-ism when it comes to the unfolding of the tale at hand.  I knew I was going to have to do some fighting in this game but was unaware that my toughest foes were going to be the mouse and keyboard.  They put up quite a fight and they're not something I could roll past like most enemies in this game.  This thing listens about as well as some 20-something with earbuds in all of Thanksgiving dinner that occasionally corrects anyone that tells them anything other than what they've learned on social media (they keep the music volume slightly low just to tell you you're wrong).  If that describes you, hey, I'm sorry, I say what I say.  I don't use social media, so there's no glass house in my backyard.  Now, before you tell someone who's been playing video games since '84 or so to git gud, let me just tell you some of the difficulties I had here.  If I had to climb downwards, it was game over.  Climbing upwards wasn't always on my character's list of priorities either.  When my input managed to work, combat was fun.  Projectile weapons are great fun to use throughout.  When my inputs didn't, it was the kind of misery they're still deciphering a word for from the ancient Viking tomes.  I found the roll button to work most consistently, so whenever my Viking champion refused to skirmish, I just rolled my way forward.  If I rolled to my death, I just chalked it up to the laws of physics and forward-motion.  Boss fights were mostly fun but the dragon chase was a real mongrel because of the above-mentioned issues.  Rolling got me through most of it.  I need to make it clear that I'm not knocking the deliberate, timing oriented feel to the actions you are trying to perform.  I actually really like heavy handed combat.  Underrated Metroidvania Redo! was permeated with tough, grueling combat that was all based on your lengthy animations finding holes in your enemies attack timing gauges.  These are things you just learn when you're figuring out a game.  My entire beef is based on controls not working at all and completely getting me killed.  I know it seems like I'm being a total jerk and I am, because this game has a lot of good qualities and I want the dev to know I'm not trashing on him.  This game does have something.  If the developer can weld gameplay to the visual/audio style he's got going for himself, he is going to be an unstoppable force in the future.  Mark my words.  In all of the games I've played over the years, this might be the most painful case of "I wanted to like this so bad but I just didn't quite dig it," of all time that I've ever mentioned.  I'm still not going to entirely say to skip Song of Iron.  I really enjoyed the locations, some of the boss battles and generally seeing where the game was going to take me next.  Ranged combat was engaging when it worked, hand to hand combat made a 60 hour week of overtime sound like something I'd like to do until the day I die.  So, there was enough to like here that made me bitterly soldier onto the end.  With generous control upgrades, I'd replay this one.  As it stands now, it's one of the most beautifully and ungodly irritating 3 hours I've ever spent gaming.  Take that as you will.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this game is SHORT from a player's perspective. I beat it in 3 hours with some extremely minor navigational issues. It probably took forever to make seeing as it came from a single dev. The game has it's issues, most have been pointed out by people already (control issues and whatnot) but I don't think this is a bad game. I actually really liked it for the music and atmosphere. The linear gameplay was refreshing after all these open world games nowadays too.I first saw this pop up and Reddit and I was excited to give it a try. It was no different from my expectations going into it due to it being a solo project. In my mind, the $20 was worth it, if only to invest in the future of this game or future projects from the creator.Feedback for the dev:- Combat needs a lot of work. The big enemies can be rolled through and attacked endlessly.- Stamina should feel punishing. I run out and can still roll and have no issues running around and healing to stay alive.- The puzzles, although clever in some places, can be changed from drag heavy box to X spot as a few of them were.- A longer game would be cool so definitely keep working through it and adding more content. I'll keep playing.I think some people may get the wrong ideas about the scope of this project so maybe a disclaimer about it being short for the $20 price tag might help avoid bitter reviewers.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, huge kudos to the solo dev for putting together this game alone. It's impressive, and the fact that it's only a solo dev behind the game should be taken into consideration when reading my review of the game. And ontop of that, the 2 BIGGEST issues that I have with this game, are completely fixable, so if the dev wants to, then they can certainly get a positive review from me once those are fixed.Pros: #1. It looks very pretty#2. The combat sounds and also music are on-point#3. Enemies approach from both the foreground and background, which means you have to defend yourself from different angles, which is very interesting in a side-scrolling game.Cons: #1. Unresponsive controls ie. I've died about 4 times because my character wouldn't roll when I double-tapped the directional buttons or wouldn't 'power attack' when I wanted to (and sometimes it freaking 'power attacked' when I was just doing a string of 'light attacks'). I HIGHLY suspect that this is a side-effect of the game being a port from console, because I've seen similar 'unresponsive controls' issues from games that are ports from consoles. So it very likely has something to do with the console's 'controller emulation' in the game which isn't implemented properly.#2. PUZZLES! I actually stopped playing the game after I couldn't solve one of the puzzles, as a result I simply couldn't progress any further, so I wish the puzzles were optional and didn't gate your progression, because I would have played more, if I weren't blocked by the puzzles.#3. No indication or clarification on whether different weapons have different stats ie. attack speed/damage/reach. Is the double-axe more powerful than the single-axe? Is the sword more powerful than the single-axe? NO idea...#4. When you throw your weapon, it disappears.#5. Health regens incredibly slowly (even outside of combat), so often times I just stand there for 60seconds+ waiting for my health to get back to 100%I will revisit the game in a couple of months to see if the controls have been fixed at the very least, and see if any other improvements have been made, but right now, I simply can't recommend paying $20 for a souls-lite puzzle side-scroller with broken controls. There's simply better games out there right now for $20.Here's 60minutes+ of raw gameplay: For more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:

_childDocuments_.review: Er...yesss, well....that was certainly...uh....something.What is 'Song Of Iron?' If I told you it would be a massive spoiler, but then we could all laugh at how stupid the ending of this game is. Not to mention it being humongously derivative. Have you looked at the steam page and thought "oooh! A side-scrolling hack and slash that's about Vikings and Norse mythology", well....you'd be wrong. Watched 1899 recently? Ever seen The Matrix? Did you like that bit in Thor 2 where it turns out ancient Asgardians and other otherworldly creatures of ancient supposed myth actually fly around in f*ckin' spaceships?I'll say no more.Anyhoo, I suppose I should mention what the game is like to play.Gorgeous mediocrity. Yup, that sums it up in a nutshell. Looks beautiful, but plays like a clunky, basic version of God Of War viewed from the side. You block, you stab, you shoot arrows, you roll around, you jump and climb on things. All in a stodgy manner that's not awful, but not great either. It's a short game at under 4 hours, which by itself isn't a good thing, but at least half of that is pretty bland fighting. The rest is fairly reasonable, albeit uninspired, platforming and one half-decent set-piece cribbed from elsewhere.Up until about half an hour before the games end I was debating giving this a positive, a 6 out of 10 if you will. It looked reet pretty and had nice enough music. The dialogue was, uh, a tad iffy, but it's not overly heavy on the narrative. Enemies were thick as pig-sh*t but they could hit each other with attacks, which I thought was a nice touch. It had the potential to be better, even if it is what it is, and what it is, is not quite good enough. The fighting doesn't feel right, the action doesn't flow enough to be exciting,  and some of the animation is pretty dubious ragdoll physics, yet it's passable. Albeit debatable whether it's worth it for the cost, and other than the setting (which is a problem too) you wouldn't have to think too hard to come up with much, much better games in the genre. But that ending? They can f*ck right off with that dumb crap. And the "to be continued?" I can't wait for the next instalment after they just sh*t all over the basic premise.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game. A bit clunky mechanics but still sound. Nice animations and use of lighting.The main reason for not recommending is the short duration for the game. I do not think 16 Euro is a good price for 2-3 hours. Although I got it at discount(12 Euro), I still doubt the price. I think the game is worth about 8 Euro in it's current state.I got to the door right before the ending cutscene, but the door wouldnt open due to a bug(I guess). I never activated one of the right shrines. The shrine I didnt activate did not react to my input, so I moved on(I tried pressing E among other buttons). After getting to the closed door, I could not backtrack to fix it. Thus I would have to replay the game due to a mechanic not reacting to my input.(Add a teleport back to replay sections? Skipping the need to replay entirely from scratch)My tip to the dev would be to fix the shrine or make the shrine more reactive to input and add some length to the game. The ending feels a bit cheap and does not give the satisfaction it could. It's more of an "is this it?" feeling, needs more "Oomph". Also I would recommend polishing movement when changing direction(Maybe put a nice animation on it). I would also consider tweaking the combat to not have "roll,slash,roll,slash..." be the best option for bosses and trolls. I know you can use your bow but you have to create distance to have time to turn with the clunky turning, but once you stun the troll you have to close that distance, which would use most of the time of the stun.Fighting ranged units felt good because it forced you to vary your fight-style and use bows and throws. More of that would be nice to see. GL HF

_childDocuments_.review: Song of Iron is a great game, one that I think everyone should play. However, it is far from being a perfect game and there's definitely room for improvement.The combat. It is alright for the most part but I think the weapon "feeling" could be improved a lot more. E.g, make the person feel like they are actually hitting something, cause right now the hit sounds etc doesn't feel that great. Another problem with the combat is there seems to be some sort of inconsistency. For example, knocked down enemies sometimes get up immediately without their animation even finishing and continue to fight, which should be made better in my opinion. And then there's the fact that for some reason, enemies ramming into you make you vulnerable even if you have your shield up.. I think that should be changed so that if you have a shield up, it shouldn't make you entirely vulnerable as it feels like you'll freely get hit. There was also some inconsistency with the roll mechanic sometimes not letting me roll through enemies.The controls. I think they are alright for a controller (I played on my Dualshock 4 using DS4Windows since the game does not support a DS4 natively) but the main issue is that there is an inconsistency here too. Sometimes my character stops climbing for no reason and other times I just either can't move at all or can't start my hit animation since the game doesn't seem to register the input. E.g, I roll on the ground but I can't throw my weapon until 2 seconds pass, which seems weird and not so intentional as it really breaks the pacing of the game. Other problem is how it seemed like I activated the lightning weapon but I actually got the fire one instead. At one occasion, even the audio for the lightning one played, but I still clearly had the fire one. Since down d-pad isn't used, I'd suggest changing the "element" you can use this way since I am stuck with fire/lightning and can't swap them out as I want to during combat.The music etc is awesome though, and I really liked the story (especially the ending bits). It was interesting to play through, even if it started out a bit slow. The visuals of the game were fantastic and can be really immersive. I am rather looking forward to how it goes from here on out.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my oh my... I found this game via reddit and thought it looked cool! I love nordic themes and it looked like a solid story game from the preview I saw way back when. Got it from a friend and was excited to play... But man does this game have its issues.pros:-Music: great vibes, feels great, makes me feel like a nordic warmother traversing the landscape.-Art: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the art is beautiful in this game. The foreground can kind of get in the way at times, but overall, 10/10 for art/visuals.-Sound design: abilities, movement, and everything sound wonderful and they did a great job at this aspect.cons:-combat: holy unresponsive controls batman! It takes a solid 1.5 seconds for a command input to register (my pc's great as are my peripherals, it's the game here)... Sometimes the game makes you run away from an enemy and sometimes you must fight them. How do you know? beats-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-me. I tried fighting each enemy I came across just to find most big ones aren't actually killable, and if they are they have health pools the size of texas. Visual cues on whether you fight or flight a mini-boss should be more existent... The controls, at default, are also pretty clunky and jank, I'm always asking myself "what button is block/bow again???" and even after rebinding it, it doesn't feel right. Dodging and "dodging" are also an issue, as some mini bosses that you're supposed to run from won't let you dodge through them, and half the time a dodge results in damage taken anyways or you not going through the enemy like it's intended...-movement: if you're not climbing... or crouching... or jumping... or swimming... the movement's fine. But the input to "climb down" practically never works. Swimming, while rare in the game, makes me scratch my head. Like I can run 5km without losing a bit of stamina, I touch knee-deep water and suddenly I have to catch my breath? Bit odd, but it's whatever. Jumping needs a LOT of work. If you go *next to* a small ledge that you must jump over and attempt to jump, it'll bug out and get you no where quickly. Crouching (especially if you're trying to slide after a sprint) is inconsistent and after a slide will often pop your head up just enough to trigger traps and other damaging things. Really only annoying when you're racing against time.-story: when I saw this game I thought, "this would be a really cool story-based game!" but the story's super... vague? and random?? You start off 'avenging your people', run into thor, he taunts you then leaves (????), you then end up in a troll/orc-infested cave network and their king(?) demands you fight for... reasons??? you fight, but before you kill the enemy, the floor drops and you swim to shore unharmed (relatively). Then you end up back on the surface running away from the orc-things... Like, where is the story going? What was that all about?? There's little to no ambient/visual story telling, too. It's all told through dialogue that's 1-sided (your character doesn't/rarely) speaks so conversations feel like enemy monologue more than exposition or basic narrative. I'm a HUGE lore nerd and a writer, myself, so when I play a game it's usually for the story... So this game being what it is, was painful to play...Overall: 4-5/10. Get it on sale, or from a friend... But don't have high expectation, and be prepared for extra-clunky controls :/

_childDocuments_.review: Song of Iron is one of those games where you can't let your assumptions about how a game will play in your mind overshadow what the game is giving you. It's a decisive game: it's got definite traits that will drive people insane. Controls are purposefully slower and less responsive based on the combat that's designed here. Sure, the game has the tendency to throw you into “setpiece syndrome”, where it wants you to get through a segment in a certain way, and if you don't do it that way, well sucks to be you. Yes, this game is much better when using a controller. But if you're willing to adapt to what the game is  giving you, you'll find a game that's beautiful to look at, and one that does a good job with game progression, and will get a few laughs out of you in the process.The presentation is the game's major strength. The environmental detail is amazing (seriously, look at those rivers) and there's a layer of realism built into the different ecosystems you go to. Just looking at the grass or the snow on the mountain gives a sense of what the world is like, and the background and how they are drawn helps to create a sense of scale, both large and small. It's complimented by great sound design that emphasizes the metal clashing in battle or the struggle to keep going with limited stamina. Music ends up enhancing the experience as well. It's definitely the game's biggest strength, and noticing small details like how the lighting lights up things. Where people are probably going to have more issues is with the combat, which is deliberate and purposeful, but also not too difficult. Learning what enemies can do is easy and you can die a couple of times in a scenario, but it's nothing where you're wondering what you're going to throw against the wall. The traps are small section of the game but can lead to a lot of laughs, and honestly, that's sorta of what the game does best. The ragdoll physics of an enemy being thrown. Repeatedly drop kicking people. Accidently dodging off a ledge into a hammer. It's a game that does good in progression, is purposeful in combat, and tells a laid back but competent story, but in the end what gets the recommendation is the fact that I was smiling and laughing through some of its absurdities. The game isn't buggy, it's solid where it counts, but otherwise the game can have scenarios that can make you want to just keel over with the funnies. For those on the fence, I would wait for a sale, but in the end I have to recommend it. Not the strongest in the genre, but also ends up feeling like it's own thing within it.
