_childDocuments_.review: So bottom line this is a good game that's an experience worth checking out. It is a pinch on the shorter side that you'll play through once, maybe twice and then put it away but it does some things that are really good and some other things that are just okay. But if you like the art, story, music & experience tale that has an interesting plot, then this is the game for you.Pros:- It's beutiful. Animations are good. There's moments of scenery, etc.- The music is great.- I like how the story is told through experience & not a ton of dialog. - This is hard to quantify but the experience of getting lost in the world, investing in your character. It's good.Cons:- It's a little clunky. Controlling the character is fine but you cannot remap buttons on the controller and there's things we've learned to do from other games that are quality of life things not in this one. Ex: Why is run left trigger? Why couldn't walk & run be on the left thumstick. Pushed a little for walk. Pushed all the way for run. Draw bow is Right trigger, aim up & down with the left thumstick and X fires. There have been so many games that have in a way taught us that arrow is drawn, aimed & fired all with the right thumb stick. Have a button to cancel firing if you don't want to & you're set. I'd also like it if that right thumbstick if pointed left or right turned your character where aiming. As it is now, you have to be sure your character is facing the right direction with left thumbstick before drawing your arrow. You'll be facing the wrong direction if you don't.- A pinch buggy. I seem have have problems getting past this boss fight of Groorg where the game tends to freeze a lot during that point. Playing with my windowed vs fullscreen and/or frames seemed to get me past this spot. Looking forward to Son of Iron 2 to come out and I will be picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, lovingly crafted, and a joy to play. I believe I heard the developer say he got a lot of inspiration from games like Limbo and Inside, and it's clear what parts are heavily influenced by those games in both level/game design, and art direction. In my opinion it works very well. Like in Limbo, you'll die quite frequently. Several of the platforming areas and puzzles require a little bit of trial and error, but with a frequent checkpoint system it never gets frustrating since you aren't playing long portions of the game over and over.This is not a Metroidvania style game so exploration is quite limited, however, I very much enjoy the linear progression and pace of the game. There is a great balance of combat and platforming, with occasional upgrades to your character, keeping things fresh and giving you a motive to keep pushing on.I played with a controller and the controls can be a little tough to master, but overall feel good once you get the hang of them. There did seem to be a few bugs from time to time, but nothing to ruin my experience.All in all, I had a great time playing this game. I did make it to the end, and although it is a bit short, I do believe I got my money's worth at $20. Some may think that is a bit much for the length of the game, but personally I would much rather play a short, but tight, experience with a good pace, rather than a game bloated with boring filler content that ends up making me stop playing. If you like 3D graphics set in a 2D playing field then this game is a must play. If $20 is too much for a 3-4 hour experience, it is certainly worth picking it up on a sale and having a fun afternoon.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game which can be very enjoyable especially if you like to play something that doesn't last long or you simply don't have much time for gaming. So should be appreciated also because of that and forgiven some issues that can be encountered.There are many positive sides that should be relevant in choosing and playing this game:- Very nice graphics with clean style, not so much details but in general very solid environments and each is nicely structured, be that a cave where everything is darker and more creepy or snowy mountains.- There are even several number of weapons and each has different impact on combat.- Bow aiming is hard and that is actually a plus in my book, considering that you should have a instinct about aiming and not just to have a pointer where an arrow will hit. _childDocuments_.review: Huh... a lot to say. Ever since the announcement, I couldn't wait for this to come out. This game does a lot of things great but some of them really need to be worked on.The style and the theme really hit my sweet spot and I love them. The environments are plentiful and done in a really nice way so the background compliments the game quite well. Add very nice music to it and all together it's a winning combination.A couple of things to note: 1. If you are doing keyboard and mouse, you are not gonna have a fun time. Combat still feels clunky and controls responsiveness needs work. 2. For a game that adopts the whole Viking/Nordic style, something I would personally like to see is a different font for the instructions that you get in the very beginning of the game (It's not groundbreaking in any way but I just think it would be a nice touch)3. Maybe it eludes me but is there a point of picking up different single handed weapons? The 2hander and the spear i understand, but what is the difference between using a one handed sword, bearded axe or the goblin cleaver? Picking up different shields makes sense but just wondering if there is a point in switching 1handers.4. If I remember it correctly your character has lines, talks to the dying wife. Later you meet Thor, Goblin king etc and your lines are "....."? He became a mute in the meantime?5. For a viking there sure is a lot of running away constantly and potential amazing challenge will be rewarded with... nothing. First fight, cave troll, point is to run away from it once he releases the box? I reloaded the game again to beat him and got... nothing? Then you fight the Wolf viking dude (forgot the name) to.... jump off a cliff because he is oh so scary, to meet him litteraly 15 minutes later and kill him first try no problem. The only boss so far that I actually NEEDED to fight was the goblin king while the rest... I ran away from lol6. I get that the games focus is to tell this story, which I think is amazing, but from a gameplay perspective (also related to the last point) there is no point in fighting anyone. No currency, no better weapons, nothing. When coming out of the goblin cave you are met by at least 15 goblins. Instead of wasting time fighting this horde... just run away. You don't get anything by fighting them, you also don't lose anything if you run away.All in all, as final thoughts I recommend the game. It's a really nice experience and I am looking forward to finishing it and seeing the end of the story. Still a lot of work to do on it, but to the devs, keep up the great work you are doing!

_childDocuments_.review: I was eager to play this since I saw the first gameplay videos. As it released I saw it struggling with the reviews. Part of the reason I bought it was to see for myself how could it be so bad - well... it's not.So the game is visually stunning,  the music fits well into the mood and the animations/movements are realistic. This means your heavy and loaded viking can't jump one meter into the air, or perform some circus level acrobatics. You can't also swing an axe as if it was a stick or auto-shoot an arrow. Movements take time, weapons are heavy, and so are you. That said, for a huge viking, you still have some moves - you can walk, run, dash (or step back, to be accurate), roll  - which doesn't make you immune to damage / death - kick, and chain things like running and sliding, or running, jumping and attacking. All of those seem actually realistic.Enemies are also not completely stupid, and some will come at you with a raised shield, or actually hit your shield away- and your shield breaks after a few hits. It takes a while to get the hang of the mechanics, and maybe they could be easier and less realistic, but I actually think it suits the game as it is. You don't always manage to one hit kill an enemy, except if you shoot an arrow or throw an axe into his head... but not all arrows hit, because enemies run and slouch, and suddenly you have an angry viking jumping at you with his axe. If you do throw an axe then it's now stuck on your enemy's skull, so you lost your weapon and you better get an alternative fast. You can pick up most of all the weapons dead enemies drop, and shields, and also pick up already shot arrows - you can even pick up arrows stuck on your own body/shield and use them.It's not all good things, the game has quite a few bugs - some places you can get stuck, some were you can stay floating/falling, some waist high obstacles you can't get over when you can climb huge cliffs, and often you want to go back and despite having a low obstacle in your way, the game just won't let you. This can be frustrating because there's some exploration in this game, and objects / upgrades / events you may miss if you went the wrong way but then can't go back. The game also saves frequently, making it impossible to visit an area you left behind. On the other hand, those auto-save locations are so frequent, that often you find consecutive ones without actually having done anything relevant in between both. Those many saves also means that, if you mess up and die, you don't usually start from too far behind.Also, some areas seem unfinished, like there was supposed to be something there, but you go off your way and find nothing that special, or just an empty room.Regarding attributes, you have health and stamina, and later on you also get some sort of magic / mana bar.Health raises quite fast by itself - your viking heals like wolverine really, and with some caution it's easy not to die.Stamina is used for running, rolling, climbing, jumping, so even if it also replenishes quite fast, if may end up lacking once or twice.The mana bar is still somewhat of a mystery. It's easy to run out of it and I still didn't understand how it replenishes.The story has some issues too, because your char stopped speaking. Other chars talk to him, but the responses are all [...]. This doesn't seem like a problem for them, as they continue talking as if your silence actually was an answer, and that feels off. Eventually the story has a major twist at the end, things get revealed, and we are left with a "to be continued".I enjoyed the game, it was fun, and the first thing I did when I ended, was to click on "resume" because I wanted to continue. I'm still struggling with the mechanics but there are so many possible movements that I didn't master the "when to kick and when to roll" right every time, so I get axed, sliced and shot, but that's on me.Bottom line, there's still some issues to be improved, and maybe it was a bit rushed to release, but I believe a developer who already did all of this amazing work on his own will continue to work on it. Can't wait to see more.

_childDocuments_.review: Song of Iron is an immersive and atmospheric, side-scrolling 2.5D adventure game. It focuses its attention on delivering a rich and meaningful experience, over padding out its length, for the sake of it. Its on the shorter side (around 3-4 hours), but every moment in the game feels fresh and unique. It never falls into the trap of repeating tricks, and always keeps your attention fully locked into its engrossing atmosphere.Gameplay is mainly combat focused, with some puzzle solving, and some platforming focused sections too. All aspects are very well balanced and fun, to keep things interesting on your journey.The game absolutely nails the visuals - beautiful lighting, stunning vistas, awesome animations, and a diverse world. Environments feel so immersive, built as actual 3D worlds in Unreal, that you traverse on the 2D plain.Song of Iron is an awesome game - created by just one solo developer (+ 1 composer) making his indie dev debut, after working in AAA for many years. Song of Iron really is an awesome game! Highly recommended! If you fancy checking out my full review on YouTube, feel free to check it out right here:

_childDocuments_.review: I've played about an hour and so far it's great! Exactly what I was expecting. The tutorial style is perfect, the overall ambiance of the environment is so immersive. I love the art and visuals they are very unique. I'm also really digging the viking music, it sounds like Wardruna composed the soundtrack for this game lol. (which is dope)The only thing I'll say is that I'm going to try and play it with my controller next because mouse and keyboard (somehow this one time) feels a little clunky, it just seems like it might be more enjoyable to play with a controller. But so far I definitely recommend!Edit: So after revisiting the game and playing it for a bit longer this time (disregard the 20+hrs I left steam running on my PC with the game open while I watched 2 seasons of a show and then went to sleep so in reality its probably closer to 2 hrs)My review is this - its a good game, I love the art style and the overall feel of the game. The one glaring issue is The Controls. I'm sure many people have said this in their reviews but the controls for this game have a very clumsy/clunky feel to them and no matter how I remap the keys I still feel like the main boss of the game is the Control Scheme. I'm assuming to the developer the controls may seem very straight forward and simple to use - and for most of the default keys its fine but there are certain things that seem minor but make the overall experience feel quite clumsy.  One thing I can think of immediately is having to HOLD down the Space Bar while climbing instead of just having to hit it once and then holding onto whatever surface I'm on. Specifically during the parts where you have to climb and then jump to another wall to climb having to hold down (space bar by default) and then press space bar and then hold it down again while also aiming my character, it seems minor, but in practice it feels so wildly clumsy. It actually feels like the developer wanted to implement a tinge of "Getting Over It" into the gameplay ( but even that game didn't feel clunky in comparison) Another example are the controls while dragging the puzzle boxes. To move the boxes left is a non-issue and feels natural, but to move the boxes right I have stop and think about how I'm positioning my fingers on the keyboard because it's an awkward transition and it feels awkward doing it.Something else is, since Sprint doesn't require any resource to use - most people are going to sprint the majority of the time, so wouldn't it make more sense to just have it be the default- or at least an option to toggle between sprinting and walking (for the 10% of time you want to purposely walk) rather than needing to hold the Shift key down for 90% of the gameplay. There are certainly other examples like using the bow and things I'm just not thinking of right now but again, none of these are game breaking issues and overall I do recommend the game, however just know that the controls are not very fluid or natural feeling and for me thats really my only critique and issue with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game at this point.  It needs more work in multiple areas, and I hope that the developer continues to improve what they've got here.  I want to like it.1) Keyboard/mouse controls are unwieldy.  Dodging won't always work properly; charged attacks sometimes happen without my wanting it; jumping across gaps is inconsistent; running doesn't always activate when you'd expect; having to jump and grab onto something was frustrating.2) Collisions with objects aren't great.  Ran into edges where it didn't feel like there should be.  Things I should be able to jump over I couldn't (right after first boss, got stuck behind a piece of wood and couldn't get out so had to reset the area).3) Glitches still present.  There's a scripted fight at the top of a cliff, and it never worked right.  Instead of getting knocked off the cliff, I would just die.  On one try, the enemy glitched out and wouldn't move/respond.  So I finally jumped off the cliff myself (wasn't clear falling off the cliff was intentional while playing).4) Combat is iffy.  On one hand, taking on a group is complicated and somewhat interesting.  You have to dodge around guys and arrows to gain good positioning.  Shields have rapid deterioration, so you can't just block things.  It's not easy to just bow+arrow all your enemies to death.  However, 1v1 combat is trivial and unfortunately you can run from virtually all combat.  The first boss was easily thwarted.  I'm not sure what can be done here in a quick/easy way.Keep working on this, keep refining the game.  I'm going to try to finish it despite this, and if things improve I'll happily re-review the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent! The environments are gorgeous and the transitions between biomes feel like you really are climbing into the mountains.Combat is tight, dynamic, and a little tricky to get the hang of at first because of all the different moves and options. Every move has its pros/cons and is useful in some situations. Once you've played an hour or two, you learn when to do what and the combat gets really fun.I would definitely play a sequel.Since the game was made by one person, it does lack polish/optimization in some areas. I had to turn the graphics down quite a bit in order to get a good framerate on the deck.My biggest gripe is the "complete the whole game without dying" achievement in a game where all the other achievements are pretty easy to get. As a completionist this really bugs me, because as much as I'd like to 100% this game it just isn't worth playing it over and over and hoping you never make a mistake or get unlucky.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: The game is beautiful. Buttons working is optional. Good guys don't get names. No real story. Very short. The ending is spectacular. Worth a buy on sale.The gameplay was pretty rough lots of getting stuck on objects, the combat was decent but didn't feel very impactful the fights felt hard to lose so long as your button inputs worked. The worst part of the game was just the lack of responsiveness from input; the game looks absolutely beautiful, however the story line didn't compel me to care at all, especially with character names that felt like place holders. With a little bit of polishing on the input the game would be more fun, and if the characters had names it would help make the player care. The story really didnt feel like it was finished, like it was just a rough script that got thrown into a game with a hell of a lot of potential, i never really understood what the goal was, why i was making progress. That being said the twist ending was great really had me on the edge of my seat. Having an actual goal chasing Thor and feeling like i had a reason to progress made the twist even more incredible. In the end if $20 is worth 2-4 hours of fun and frustration go for it. I personally felt pretty let down after getting hyped up by the trailer i saw 3 months before release, and have a hard time fully recommending this game. This dev has massive potential that with the right team i think could lead to incredible things.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, yeah. Review time.Played this as a demo during Steam Fest and finally bought and played it. is some kind of hybrid game between God of War (PS2), Bloodforge and Vikings: Battle for Asgard. But in 2d with 3d models with a focus on atmosphere and combat.While I cannot critic the game like one would for a AAA title, this being developed by a single human being and not an eldritch entity hellbent on adding multiplayer and screaming  horrors to anything it touches, I would still like to point some things out.1. While the story is serviceable as a whole and it being minimalistic is really the only way to go with a limited budget and one man coder. The "save my people" is a weird premise for a journey as everyone is already dead in the first 5 minutes, making the whole trip both emotionally void and pointless at the same time. Instead of seeking out the gods to resurrect your "people" should instead have been replaced by seeking out the gods to make sure your kin would go to Valhalla or find peace in death. The journey would prove the characters worth to the gods and invest you the player to continue going forward both in and out of character. 2. The combat is... okay. My biggest gripe with it is mainly the lack of feedback. Every attack feels weak, and the swings just go through the enemy with only some minor blood splatter showing if you did any damage or not, and you keep swinging until the ragdoll physics kick in. The funny thing is that the solution is kind of there already as throwing a weapon, killing enemies feels excellent as does using the bow and arrows with headshots.3. It didn't happen often and more towards the end but in some areas the way forward was either something climbable or movable but of in a dark area making it hard to spot. Also had to reload one time as the door to proceed didn't open after activating the trigger.1. My covid test.2. The pacing is excellent. Never did I feel bored by too little or too much combat, and exploring was such a joy I always wanted to continue playing. A nice detail here was that after certain intense areas, the MC stopped to catch his breath. A small detail but it adds to the character and reminds me of the MC from Hyper Light Drifter who did the same but coughed up blood instead.3. The atmosphere is stellar. It's not every day a game comes out with such focus on environments in a 2d game and making it all cohesive and thematic without being superfluous with grand vistas and dramatic voice-overs.The set pieces were interesting enough for me to never wanting to use the sprint button and instead just walked forward as it felt more appropriate and immersive. Every new area felt fresh and had enough variety to make the walking not feel stale and boring and instead wanting you to see more.4. The power ups are fun. While getting fire and lighting are just flavors of weapons damage, in combination with finding boots of stomping, armor of speed and helmet of  makes for fun power play as it breaks up the clunky combat with a bit of flavor and makes the game more varied in the long run. I also want to point out that the game isn't that long, and don't see that as a problem. I rather play an excellent game that is 1 hour long then a mediocre game that is 10, and I shove this one into the good category.That's it really, I recommend this to anyone who wants an atmospheric game but also has work and simply wants to chill one Friday evening with something mysterious and new.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Good but short.The heat of the fire burns your face but you don't care. The pain makes you feel alive; it's the only thing that's real. You mourn your village reduced to ruin. Of lives lost. Of a life lost. Only one thing matters now.... Revenge. Songs will be sung of your glory; Your axe will sing its own song with the cries of any who stand before you it's melody. Crush your enemies, earn the favor of the gods, and *feel* the Song of Iron.Plunged into a world of chaos, this game begins with a familiar tale. Your village destroyed, your family killed, now you seek revenge. Though it's familiarity isn't necessarily a bad thing. It lends purpose to your struggle and is a reminder of what lengths one will go in the pursuit of revenge. The world is full of color, but only in the light. Everything outside of it is dark and washed with gray, as if you can't truly see what is there. The camera moves along with you, close to the ground showing gorgeous textures in the environment. The world is truly breath-taking and I found myself wanting to *walk* through it, looking at both the foreground and background. It offers stunning vista's that make you want to take a moment and just... breathe.The combat is effective, allowing the use of a multitude of different weapons with varying attack speeds and patterns. Enemies approach from both sides and even the foreground and background leading to intense struggles requiring some thought on how best to bathe your weapon in their blood. The abilities are unique. Instead of leveling up your weapons and adding passive skills you unlock new forms of elemental damage; A gift from the gods themselves. However the game was definitely made for the story and to display the worlds beauty. Being more cinematic, the combat felt like it was just enough to keep you interested and engaged while exploring a truly beautiful world. I do wish that there was a little bit more platforming. There was a long period of ascending a mountain that was just climbing. I feel like a great sequence of platforming would have filled that void like a horn full of mead.The sound is masterfully done. From the eerie ambient sounds in a cave to the peal of Thunder as you fire a lightning arrow from your bow, I just wanted to *listen*. The music... Incredible. I'm a big fan of Nordic folk music and this scratches that itch. The sounds are both beautiful and haunting. Low chanting accompanied by intense war drums, filling you with suspense for the battle that awaits. Framing your mind and tempering expectations is the best way to fully enjoy this game. If you look at it like playing a movie, more of a cinematic experience as opposed to playing a full fledged game you will enjoy yourself more. I say that only because my only real complaint is that the game was too short.

_childDocuments_.review: So in advance- this review has spoilers in it.This is literally one of the most disappointing times I've had playing an indie game. I respect the man for putting effort into making the game, but I really didn't think that it would be this buggy. If it wasn't the final boss clipping into the floor where he can't be hit mid fight, it was the forced animation loops from interacting with something twice that made me restart the game just to pick up where I left off. Not to mention the plot at the end was literally one of the worst twists I've seen (comparable to The Last Airbender movie bad). Suddenly we're in Star Wars getting shot by lasers and throwing guns at people? Not to mention the plot armor of the dude standing at the end of the bridge so even if you make the jump you have to go through that little path just to get back to what you needed to do. I did like the realism that as the fight continued he actually weakened and slowed down, very nice touch, but still it didn't really feel rewarding to beat the game. Not to mention the length being short, which is give or take. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone sadly. Not until they patch it up and think about how lack luster the ending was. Maybe even add more to the story by giving people actual names. It's nice to have that sense of detachment I guess, but there is no life in any character aside from maybe three.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, on first playthrough ran into many instances with obvious and easily found bugs. The story hard carries the game as it's the most interesting part but even that seems a bit cliche (other than ending), but the experience almost fights you from completing the game or even seeing what the creator has to say. Several times I found myself looking at the same "pull box to spot to jump on" scenario, which just seemed like a way for the dev to buy time between either fights/enemies that I could just run past. Or there were a few spots where I the games lack of direction left me backtracking across an area just to find out that I was supposed to just see that a door hidden by the camera angle had opened for me. I felt like I was a games journalist at times, with how silly this made me feel for not understanding some dumb puzzle for 10 minutes when it was just hidden behind some of the janky foreground elements. Only truly not recommending for the HEFTY price tag on what is a 2 hour or less experience and a very lackluster overall experience. _childDocuments_.review: (Spoilers ahead for this review. I very much did not enjoy my experience with the game, but I do believe the twist is still worth experiencing for yourself and it was definitely the highlight of the game for me.)I'll first say that I understand this was the passion project of a single artist and (with the exception of musical composition and vocal performances) was pretty much a solo endeavour. The game visually at many moments is quite beautiful and the artistry on display is very clearly a product of skill cultivated for years.Unfortunately the game is lacking in pretty much every other aspect. The gameplay isn't what I would describe as "clunky". I don't even necessarily regard clunky gameplay as a bad thing. There just is no real gameplay loop to speak of. There isn't really a difference of playstyles between different weapons. There aren't weapons that deliver long crushing blows at the expense of speed contrasted with fast weapons allowing for fast hits in between dodge-rolls. Whereas in Dark Souls you can dance in and out of enemy range in order to box with enemies, utilizing hitstun clever positioning in order to avoid taking damage, this game makes it so you and your enemies have virtually the same range in all instances. The walking speed is also painfully slow, so if you're not running--mind that there's also no running attack. You will simply stop dead in your tracks and do a regular attack instead.--then you are basically forced into a slap fight with enemies until either they go down or you do.The game allows you to regenerate health extremely fast after not taking damage for about ten seconds or so. This *feels* like an attempt to compensate for the lack of ability to avoid damage without running around enemies for 5 minutes poking at them, but ends up making the game far too easy when (I assume) it was meant to be a fairly challenging pseudo-soulslike.I keep referencing Dark Souls because it's clear that this games combat takes much inspiration from it. The three energy bars and stamina management along with the signature dodgeroll makes it quite clear. Much like a soulslike, you can very easily just run right past 90% of enemies in the game whenever you feel like it, completely avoiding combat if you choose. This ability works in a game like Dark Souls, where avoiding enemies will net you less Souls to level up with, making you much weaker for later areas and bosses. This works much less so in Song of Iron because there is no system of increasing power. You could fight the final boss with the gear you have when you begin the game, and you pretty much do exactly that.There is only 1 genuine boss fight in the entire game. This isn't inherently a problem. The games length justifies having only one real boss fight, even. Unfortunately, the fight against Thor, having genuinely cool moments (the sci-fi reveal) is really *really* ruined by the awful combat of the game. Thor's attacks are mostly *decently* telegraphed, though he does have a slam attack that didn't seem to do any damage to me at all. I'm not sure if that was an intentional choice or it was just one of the many bugs I encountered. Once Thor is weakened he's a pretty pathetic fight; no longer flying he can only swing wildly in front of him so you can just pound on his back with whatever weapon you're using and kill him. Thor dies and his character model just goes limp. There's no grandiosity or even any significance at all given to the moment of you killing the god of thunder single handedly. It's literally just a thing that happens and a nameless character says "What now?" and then credits roll. A very disappointing end after such a cool reveal.The technical state of the game seems to be quite a mess as well. Often times enemies would swing straight through my body and they wouldn't hit me, and vice versa when I'd swing at enemies. There were several moments where I'd have to quit and reload my save because a door was bugged or moving platform would just get stuck. One time I activated the speed boost ability I was slow, but once the speed boost ability wore off I was fast until I reloaded my save (it was kinda cool but doesn't speak well to the technical state). Also something that was odd to me was that I chose the female protagonist but Thor kept referring to me as "he" and "him"? Not sure if that was a bug with the game or if the dialogue just was not altered to fit the player choosing the female protagonist.I'm actually kind of sad because I heard this game with a really good 2D soulslike adventure, and I've been clamouring for a short game that I could crank out in a day of playing. I'm confident the developer would do great as the art director on a video game, but I just couldn't enjoy this game, as much as I really tried to.EDIT: Performance-wise, I didn't notice any significant framedrops while playing. I stayed pretty solidly capped at 90fps with max settings at 1080p on my gaming laptop.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, Steam's all-or-nothing rating system proves to be an absolute dinosaur of a way to rate and review a game.  C'mon, Gabe, get with the times!  Song of Iron is a solid 3 out of 5.  The look and sound of it is absolutely gorgeous.  The Nordic folk chant style of the music sets the tone well.  The ambient touches like the wind blowing the trees really gives the whole thing nice atmosphere.  But the controls are absolute garbage.  The slowness of the combat seems partly by design, it seems, and to that end it works well.  This isn't a button masher where you can spam slashes and just wail your way through things.  But, on the other hand, it's not a souls-like where you just spam dodges.  In fact, you can't since you have a stamina bar that drains with each move including your sword strikes.  You have to put some thought into your combat.  Fortunately, you can toss a weapon for an insta-kill in many cases and quickly pick up a weapon off of a downed enemy.  Shields are ridiculously fragile, on the other hand.  While wear and tear on a shield is a nice mechanic that forces you to drop what you have (if it didn't get wiped out by enemies), the shields can only take 3 or 4 hits before they're gone.  Those famous Norse shields made of balsa wood, am I right?  It also doesn't help that it seems like your block is often ignored.  I don't know if the enemies were doing unblockable slashes or if it's just a bug because there's no difference in the animation to tell you what they're doing and whether you should roll or are safe to block.But the slowness also comes in the form of responsiveness.  It just doesn't feel like your character really responds to your button presses with crispness.  So you have to compete with both the intentionally slow and heavy combat style and button responses that feel mushy.  There were quite a few jumps I had to redo because the character tripped on her own shoelaces or something.  The jump feature is just mucky.There are also some moments in the game where it is not intuitive what you must do.  Without giving any spoilers away, there was one part I was stuck on for a long, long time before I looked it up online and realized that I was not addressing the situation in the way that you're supposed to.  I thought the game was bugged rather than that I was not doing the right thing.  There's a difference between handholding the player and having a solution that's so obtuse that you really should have worked some hints into the game.Overall, it's a nice experience for the atmosphere if you can grab it on sale and have a high frustration tolerance for sluggish controls for the sake of playing the game yourself.  It's definitely not worth the full asking price, though.  Stuff it in your wish list then sit on it until it goes on sale if you really want to give it a whirl or, better yet, save yourself the money and frustration and just watch someone do a playthrough of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Now let me start by saying, I constantly have been scouring countless launchers, youtube videos and websites for listings of games that are set in the Viking Age. For years I have been reading about the history and wanting to be in a setting of such a mystical time. This game starts with the death of someone you love and seems to be a game about avenging your lost loved one and saving your people from further destruction. fighting other warriors, trolls, goblins and other beasts and beings. The game had a great atmosphere and the combat, though could use some work, was still satisfying. There was a major problem I encountered while playing and this was no glitch or game breaking bug.  Also before anyone says anything, i did complete the game.READ ON IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR AN AUTHENTIC VIKING/NORSE SAGASPOILERS AHEAD!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!As many developing companies do with the games they create in the Viking Age, they tend to throw some outlandish wild concept in the mix ruining a perfectly good medieval story. This game had me feeling great right up until the si-fi imperium, science experiment, everything is fake theme came into play. I started to notice something was off when i spotted strange technology while in the caves exploring. While on the hunt for my wife's murderer I came across an unlikely character. He invited me to drink with the warriors in Valhalla but as I had revenge on my mind, i declined. Then when i meet him again, he said he replaced me with my adversary and decided to try and kill me, and I chased him to his underground facility where it resembled something out of a star wars film. this is where I gave a big sigh, finished the game and that was that. Now while this is a perfectly fine and fun game for those who enjoy fantasy games with a little twist like that, as a person who is constantly trying to find authentic medieval viking games and being let down again and again...this has been added to my list. I recommend purchasing the game if you do not care about this as much as I do. Unfortunately I cannot leave a recommend in my review as to warn those like me. If you are a history buff trying to scratch that itch, just go back to Valheim, this will not suffice.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this with the fact that I've bought this game on a 60% discount and even with a price tag that's so much cheaper I don't think it was worth it. Don't get me wrong: atmosphere, graphics and music are all amazing - to me they are perfect.But the controls, oh ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the controls. So clunky, so frustrating, so buggy. You can kick an enemy to have it fall down, but 9/10 times expect that it will insta (almost teleport) get back up. Enemies sometimes start fighting each other, I have no idea what's up with that, but it makes combat silly. Sometimes when you hit them, they stagger a little (like in most games), but sometimes they don't and just brute force hit you despite anything. Sometimes you may roll past an enemy, sometimes the same enemy will act like a wall. Sometimes the lighting spell on your weapon will stun them, sometimes it will do nothing. I could go on and on about how absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the combat in this game is.Oh and if you expect a full game - there's another disappointment. It's only about 3h long in terms of playthrough. This price for so little game time? It's not worth the price, it's barely worth it on a discount. Looks amazing, atmosphere is amazing. Too bad the dev didn't put more thought and work into controls and combat.Overall, game feels as if it's in early access.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to playing Song of Iron, but I was disappointed within the first few minutes of the game. It starts with you standing by the fire and nothing happens. You try to press all the buttons and wonder if the game has a bug. But it doesn't, you just have to stand around for a minute or two and do nothing. Then the story starts. A short time later you are standing by the fire again. But even after three minutes nothing happens, because now you really have to play and run to the right of the screen. Again, there was no indication whatsoever. And that goes on throughout the whole game. Especially for newcomers to the gaming scene, this can quickly lead to frustration.And the next shock doesn't take long to arrive. The controls... Man, it's set like ♥♥♥♥. I don't know if the developers have ever played a game on the keyboard in their lives, but the key assignment is not exactly optimal and the implementation in the game is not much better. Everything feels clunky.Visually, the game looks nice, but doesn't offer anything special either. And the story... there's not much to say. _childDocuments_.review: It's hard to believe that so many obvious problems can exist within the first few minutes of playing a game. If this is what the game has to show for itself, I don't want it. To make my point I'll quickly go over everything that was obvious before progressing past the main menu;The game defaults to 30 fps and only goes up to 90 fps after changing it in the settings menu.Clicking on the buttons doesn't work, you need to actually click on the text, this is basic UI design.Hitting ESC doesn't take you back, you need to click on the back button.Playing on a ultrawide screen zooms the game in so far that the camera clips through the floor.After getting past the disaster of a title screen, you are greeted with PS2 models with PS1 level design and GBA level combat and animations. The previous issue of being limited to 90 fps didn't end up mattering because the game seems to chug at about 72 fps consistently, which it has no right to be doing. I stopped playing because in the second level I came up against a rock wall with no way to progress, I assume a glitch with progression or something cut off by my aspect ratio. Either way, I have no desire to work past it.I think that I could forgive all of the above and any additional problems that popped up over a playthrough if this game was a $5 indie game, but it was listed as $28.95 AUD, which stinks of a dev that doesn't know what their product is actually worth. At that price I was expecting a really high quality and polished experience. I've read a few other reviews that seem to imply that the game was made by a single person, and it really shows. So many of these problems wouldn't exist with a second set of eyes going over it. I'm requesting my refund now.

_childDocuments_.review: Kratos makes an epic comeback as The Nine Realms' greatest dad.ADVERTISEMENTSome of the best films of all time are those whose different strengths all work in concert to create a unified, engrossing whole. The Shining, The Social Network, and Jaws are all excellent examples of films made up of strong individual parts complementing each other to form a fantastic work of art. That is absolutely true of God of War – its musical score elevates story moments, which flow seamlessly into fantastic action gameplay, which facilitates exploration and puzzles that reward you with a deeper understanding of its characters and its expansive and beautiful world. God of War is a masterful composition of exceptional interlocking parts, deliberate in its design and its foreshadowing, which pays off in unexpected ways in both the gameplay and story.ADVERTISEMENTSet in a new, Norse mythology-inspired world and starring a familiar but thoughtfully reimagined character, God of War’s fish-out-of-Greek-water tale is a nonstop whirlwind of emotions. It’s all framed by one continuous camera shot that never cuts away or takes the focus off of the heart of it all: Kratos’ relationship with his young son, Atreus. But the story also encompasses an indelible supporting cast, a gorgeous world consistently rewarding to explore, and immensely satisfying combat.God of War works from minute one thanks to the simplicity of its plot.ADVERTISEMENTADVERTISEMENT“God of War works from minute one thanks to the simplicity of its plot. Kratos and Atreus – who start as, at best, acquaintances – begin their journey having just gone through the loss of Kratos’ wife, whom Atreus bonded with much more than his father. The two set out to the tallest point in all the realms to carry out her final wishes.ADVERTISEMENTThe setup is Journey-like in its visual nature – I saw the peak in the distance and knew I’d get there eventually – but as similar stories have taught me, the path is never a straight or easy one. A number of obstacles, both natural and god-made, extend the adventure to around 25 hours’ worth of terrifying threats, beginning with the first major encounter in the opening hours.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's visually and stylistically pretty interesting.  I love the use of light and sound in this game, a lot.  But the controls and, related, the combat are extremely clunky.  I kind of get what they were going for, make it feel a bit less "hack & slash", but the enemies respond way too quickly half the time and there doesn't seem to be any real stagger element to make up for how slowly your hit enemies, and it really feels like there should be.Also, which picking up things on the ground, it's too easy to get stuck in a loop grabbing something useless like a shield.  One of the mechanics is throwing your weapon, so sometimes you want to throw your weapon, grab another from a fallen enemy, and maybe throw it, or go back to combat, but instead you grab a shield, then grab your own shield again, then grab the new shield, and now the enemy is on you and you're dead.  The mechanics feel interesting, but the execution is a bit flaky and leaves something to be desired.  In the end, a lot of the combat boils down to getting on one side of a pack of enemies, and baiting them one at a time while letting your health regen between rounds.  If they get on both sides, you're slow enough that you're just going to die easily.I'm "recommending it" because it's not bad enough to give it a negative, but there isn't a neutral option.

_childDocuments_.review: The art design for the game is amazing.  In terms of lighting and textures it's beautiful.  The light from fire, lightning and magic all have a great effect on the surroundings.  It is 2D essentially but they use the foreground very effectively, zooming in and out at times and using parallax and shadows to create a very dynamic feel.  There are a variety of environments like forests, caves and snowy mountains each with their own gorgeous atmosphere.  The music fits each environment and scene perfectly, setting the tone for various scenes and moments.  The sound in general is really good with some nice sound effects.  The voice acting is minimal but effective.The combat is mostly solid.  You have a handful of weapons, magic items and moves so you do have a lot of options to develop your own play style.  The magic items have really satisfying effects that deepen the combat as you go along which is nice, keeps it interesting.The story is solid, nothing more than it needed to be while offering an unexpected twist that was fun and intriguing.  No draw out expository dialogue but with good hints in the background.  There's also a New Game Plus which I always appreciate.The block and evade move seemed very under powered.  The block would appear to stagger an enemy but then they'd recover immediately so you couldn't really follow up effectively.  Similarly the evade wouldn't get you out of the way of even basic attacks to then allow you to counter attack so it hardly seemed worth using.  I ended up mostly just roll dodging which worked but with the defensive options were more viable to provide more options.The magic effects, fire and lightning, very clearly effected certain enemies(burning and stun) but not others even though similar visual effects were applied to them.  This, combined with no damage stats or health bars(which I don't mind), made it unclear if they had any effect on certain enemies so I wasn't sure if they were even worth using at times.  Similarly it was unclear if different weapons did more or less damage, mainly two handed vs one handed axes.Controls weren't as responsive as I'd like, particularly with things like jumping, climbing, blocking and rolling.  I also had issues with the heavy attack being triggered after a slightly too long of a click which was annoying since you're then locked into the animation.The game is very short, around 3 hours, but costs $20.  I got it on sale for $15 and that feels a bit steep too, I think $10 would've been fairer even with NG+.There were two bugs that made me have to reload from the main menu and a crash the made me have to fully restart the game. Not too bad but still annoying.The font choice in the menu and dialogue(Arial I think) is kinda boring.  Also there were a few capitalization issues in the dialogue.Overall I'd recommend it, especially if it's on sale for 5-10 bucks.   The game looks beautiful, has some great music, the story is interesting and the combat is mostly really fun.  I'm definitely looking forward to the sequel and hope they  out a few of the mechanical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a stock standard side-scrolling action game.I'm going to ignore the fact that there are platforming sections, and although they are not all that painful, I question why they are there.There is not a lot of content in this game.For most of the game, you press the directional to the right and occasionally mash some buttons and you have beaten the game.You fight the same enemies almost all game, there is no indication for health bars in boss fights or just enemies in general so you have no idea which of your attacks are the best in the given situation. But I can see why this is dumbed down, because all you have to do is mash buttons or run away and shoot arrows enough times that the enemy dies. The game gives you magic, so you can buff your attacks with different colors and you have no idea if they deal more damage or how much more damage your attacks do. The buffs last only a short period of time that I felt using these abilities didn't let me kill the enemies faster, but only made combat more tedious. The powers are not convenient to use and the buff we get is not worth the hassle. Why aren't we being given actual spells we can cast instead of just temporarily swing a flaming sword that supposedly did more damage?The plot is nonsensical, but that's ok, plot in these types of games isn't important.The game has an interesting, stripped down look that is very appealing, but hat's about all that this game has going for it.The game feels like a tech demo how bareboned it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. As other reviews have noted it's short, but I think it's a great game to play through a few times because of its shortness, its forward combat energy, some subtler moments in the story you don't catch the first time, and its handcrafted, beautiful environmental design. The artistic composition of the side scrolling environments coupled with the music gives a cinematic feeling to just walking through a forest or dark cave. Good stuff!The bad guys destroyed your village and killed your loved ones, and the character's heart and sword arm are on a mission to stop them and save what's left of your people. The story's simple and to the point, but it develops in an interesting way that gives it more depth, and new questions arise at the end. I'm curious what happens next if a sequel does indeed get made.I finished my first playthrough and immediately jumped into a NG+ with all the fun gear at the start (just hit resume after you've completed the game). First time walking through the environments, encountering enemies, and seeing the story unfold was great, but a lot of the first time gameplay was a rough experience for me. There were several frustrating moments due to things other reviews talk about (controls feel awkward, sometimes you're confused about where the heck to go next, bugs like doors not opening so you have to reload to reset them but you don't KNOW that). But my second playthrough, when I was used to the combat controls and knew where to go? Had a blast.I played through the whole game four times in pretty quick succession. I noticed background details, story elements, and hidden nooks that I didn't see in my first playthrough. It's a blast to go on a blazing, ax swinging rampage where you never stop running and fighting, or a slower playthrough where you stop and smell the roses, listen to the music, and soak in the lovely or eerie atmosphere before getting back to throwing magic fire axes at your foes.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my playthrough of the game, and I would absolutely recommend this game. Maybe not at its current price if you want more value out of your money (It's basically 3 euro from a game like Fallout 4 when it's on discount), but I did buy it at full price nonetheless.Let's start with the bad stuff.#1 Controls - I'm predicting that this is going to be a very hit-or-miss for people. It felt a bit sluggish and unresponsive when I absolutely didn't need it to be, which caused a lot of unnecessary deaths. It feels very much like a controller-type of game, which isn't bad.#2 Player Character - I realize as much as anyone that not all games have choices that are meaningful, but I think that would have justified the price for sure. And if not that, at least give the character some dialogue and a personality. At the end I didn't feel connected to the character whatsoever.#3 Story - There is none. You might scratch your head at that after playing it, but there's a big difference between plot and story. What started out as a quest for vengeance turns into something quite adventurous in epic proportions, but it never returns to the theme that started the journey nor does it deliver a moral lesson at its end.The Good stuff!#1 Plot - What it lacked in story and thematic elements, it kinda made up for in plot; your village is raided by men led by a man named Wolfrick. You find your beloved and as they die in your arms, they give you a stone that can let you ask the Gods for help. And so you set out on a quest for vengeance. On your way you face off against raiders, trolls, goblins, and even greater and more terrifying creatures from the depths of Nordic mythology.#2 Puzzles - Some people dislike it, but those who complain never had to do the Water Temple without a guide to help them growing up. I really liked these puzzles. They were simple, yet still very much added to my enjoyment.#3 Exploration - I always love it when games reward me for exploring, and here you are truly rewarded. I think some of the upgrades you'll find on your journey are mandatory, but a few of them seemed to be tucked away out of reach unless you let your inner explorer take over. I appreciate that, especially since one of those upgrades helped me a whole lot in the massive fights down the road.#4 and #5 Atmosphere & Music - the game truly deep dives into not only Nordic mythology but also the northern Scandinavian landscape and their viking songs of old. One moment there's a woodland tune that sinks you comfortably into the earth and in the next moment there's drums of war and men singing about the end times as I'm standing before a troll down under the mountains. The end result is an immersive game that grips you and refuses to let go.And by the end of the game, my thoughts echoed that of the player character: "What now?"

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing and gorgeous product from a single-man production. Just take it for what it is and you’ll get a couple of enjoyable hours out of it.-	You can pick up different weapons (sword, axe, spear…) which apparently cause the same amount of damage. I just choose the one I liked the most and stayed with it until the end. Shields lose their usefulness in the second half of the game, or once you realize that offense is the best defense. They also break easily.Bow, which is part of your initial equipment, is a welcome addition to the arsenal. It can be a powerful tool when aiming for those headshots! It’s always fun to pull on the string and drop the ones foolish enough to charge at you without a shield.-	Health slowly regenerates so the battles never felt hard or unfair. I saw them as an obstacle on my path and have died mostly because I choose to fight instead of running away – it’s OK to run away from battle, at certain points you even have a choice to sneak past the enemies. The only problem I have with this system is the slow health regeneration. Especially at the beginning, I found myself standing still and waiting a minute or two for my wounds to heal before moving forward. Also, friendly fire is present. Enemies might miss you and hit their friend.-	Even though I don’t like stamina bars in action games, the one in Song of Iron is more than generous and never causes problems during a battle. Naturally, you can’t just button-mash and punch in the air; when you attack, you better hit something. And you need to be careful not to abuse the dodge move, which takes the biggest chunk out of your stamina bar. -	Checkpoints are spread out quite fairly and I never felt that I lost progress upon death. It was only in the final part of the game that I missed some kind of auto-save or at least a skip button; watching and listening to the entire conversation after every death is not fun. -	You gain elemental powers (fire and lighting) to imbue your weapons. Again, I never felt that these abilities cause any additional damage to the enemy. However, the animation of lighting a sword on fire in darkness is a joy to watch.-	There are no “real” puzzles in this game; pushing a couple of blocks here and there or searching for shiny rocks throughout a level won’t make your brain hurt. With only one exception, elemental powers are not used to solve puzzles, which is a shame.-	I’m not sure if there are any secrets in the game, but there are definitely some optional stuff and easter eggs. -	After you see the ending, you can start a new game with all the abilities available from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: For what is mostly a solo effort, this game turned out surprisingly well.The game's graphics and visuals are excellent. Performance is good - my 6800 XT easily holds 4K 90FPS (which is hard for it to accomplish on most other games of this visual quality).The music is great. It does a good job at complementing the gameplay and holds up well on its own too. Definitely up there with the better video game soundtracks I've heard.Gameplay is comprised of a mix of combat, puzzle and platforming elements.The nicest thing I can say about the combat is that it's functional. It's neither great nor bad, although it can feel a bit clunky at times. The puzzle/platforming sections are reasonably fun and challenging - a nice break between the sections where you're chopping up goblins/Norsemen.The story is a case of unrealised potential. Song of Iron's world seems to have quite a lot of story behind it, but you don't actually get to explore much of it in the game. Even after beating the game, there's a lot of loose ends and unexplained plot points lying around. That's honestly a shame, because I really wanted to know more after finishing the ending.One minor annoyance I have with the game is that it's a bit unpolished. Character dialogue is poorly written and has lots of grammatical errors, which throws off the story immersion for me. Cutscenes start and end abruptly with no indication of when the player loses control or gains it back.It has its issues but Song of Iron is definitely worth playing, although its short playtime (2.5 hours for me) makes it hard to justify paying its full asking price. Maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished playing the game through, and wanted to share my thoughts on it...The artistic side of the game is truly awesome, epic, breathtaking, and awe-inspiring. Every aspect, from visuals to lighting, and sound design to the animations. You can really see the skills of Joe Winter and his sound designer, Will Goss, shine here. The different areas that you journey through have a nice variety to them and keep things visually interesting.For the most part, the gameplay and combat are pretty solid, and once you get used to the minimal intricacies involved, it is very satisfying. There are a couple of glitches here and there, but once you are aware of them, they only hinder very little and can be easily overlooked. You can choose several different styles of combat depending on the type of player you are.Whether it be close combat or ranged or a little of both, with a few magic elements thrown in for good measure.The story-line is a little thin, but does it's job. Maybe some voice acting would have helped.I think my only real disappointment was the way it unfolded near the end. I wasn't a fan of the direction it took, but that's just my personal opinion. Others may have a different viewpoint.Overall I would definitely recommend this game for the price point it's being sold at, and I'm looking forward to the next part. From what I understand, it will be a 3 part series. Hats off to you Joe for making such a great game.Sterling solo effort!

_childDocuments_.review: Reading the mixed reviews on Steam gave me pause before trying this game, but boy am I glad I took a chance.As a fan of games like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, I appreciate how the game gives you a large moveset, a lot of tools available at your disposal to experiment with different playstyles and have some creative expression as the player.Song of Iron has a lot of tools at the player's disposal as well.  And in a way, a lot is left to the player's discretion not only to express themselves, but also to figure things out on their own.Both of these games, in different ways, challenge the player to experiment, and to learn.  And I really like that - not just enemy patterns, but also learn what your own character is capable of.  While Song of Iron doesn't feel quite as mechanically precise as Sekiro, it is still somewhat demanding of the player and so may not be a game for everybody.And I would like to say, while avoiding spoilers as much as I am able, that anyone who is a big fan of fantasy series such as J.R.R. Tolkien's Lord of the Rings and Joe Abercrombie's First Law among others will find some great referential homages done amazingly well in this game.  Bravo to this one-man development team on this game, would absolutely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Song of Iron was a title that struck me immediately by the trailer loaded onto the Steam page. A side-scrolling viking action game appealed to both the gamer in me, as well as my addiction to heavy metal. So, it was a no brainer to lay the $20 US and hit start immediately. Unfortunately, there is room to gripe.You play as a viking returning home to find his village destroyed. His loved one dies in his arms, but is tasked with taking a pendant to ask the gods for assistance in retribution to the fallen. So begins your quest through the lavish landscapes, dark caves, and eventually snowcapped levels that chill to the permafrostic Nordic black metal style I love so much. Even the audio score manages to capture what one would expect the music to be at that time, but with more of a symphonic or cinematic touch to match the feel of the game.And that's one thing to truly admire about Song of Iron. It is developed in a way that it starts at point a and rarely breaks in its quest to point b. With only a couple obvious fades to black as a transition point, much of this title moves forward as a single shot. What few occasions it throws those subtle cuts in are usually a shift through darkness, or your character was knocked out prior.While this was a spetacular decision to make things move on fluidly from start to finish, not all the choices were grand ones. I lost count of how many false battles I wound up in, such as a recurring foes that kicked me off a ledge that I thought would kill me, but instead was intention causing me to waste so much time fighting him. Another instance involved a giant orc that pounded the ground at the start of the battle, caving in the floor as a segway to the next section.And that's part of the other issue with this game. The boss battles are extremely unfulfilling. Your character moves and attacks like molasses. It's a bit annoying at first, but once you get the hang of it and know when to dodge certain attacks, evenemies are easy to dispatch. Your health also slowly regenerates over time (no health pick-ups) so you can also just dodge or run around until you feel comfortable enough to continue the fight. A lot of this works for the standard enemies, as well as the boss fights save for a god you have to fight later on who was a right pain in the ass until the pattern was figured out.Finally, there's the controls. I played this with a controller, and by Odin's beard it nearly went soaring across the room a few times. From randomly being unresponsive to doing things I never said to do, One of the more annoying ones was when a  cut scene would play and if you held a direction prior you'd be frozen until you pushed in that direction again. The unrespnsive moments also hurt in some battles causing me to not dodge, flat out not attack, or press x for a quick attack only to find my momentary pressure on it was treated like it was held down for a strong attack instead. Out of everything, this drastically needs work the most.(this next paragraph has spoilers)Song of Iron is a visual and auditory feast. The steady shot progression with very few fade-to-black transitions (or at least jarring ones) is a highy commendable approach that helped hook me deeper into the title. There isn't much storywise until we get to the end, which in the end is probably the wiser decision. However, the problems with the controls, unsatiating boss battles, and many false fights make justifying the $20 USD price point a bit much to swallow. It also doesn't help this takes two-and-a-half to three hours and doesn't even leave you with the most memorable ending. This isn't to say Song of Iron is bad, but the potential on display proves it could have been a little more than what's present. I DO suggest this game, though maybe hold off for a sale or the devs to tighten up the controls more.

_childDocuments_.review:
Behind you lies a trail of broken helms, shattered shields. You hold the axe of a fallen foe. Worn and dented, it will suit it's purpose. What lies ahead is still a mystery, your goal is not. To save your people you must find the Great Temple of the Gods, but do not expect a warm welcome.

Prepare to be met by a world set against you. In Song of Iron, man, monster and nature itself will try to stop you. Fight through it all in this gritty adventure where combat is intense, visceral and dangerous. Use bow, axe and shield to fight back but take care, weapons can be lost, arrows will run out and shields will be broken. With the blood of your ancestors and valor regained along the way you can fight on!

Explore your ancient, and mysterious homeland as you journey through forests, into caves and climb mountains as you seek vengeance. Keep your eyes peeled, danger is all around you and when a fight is too big you may need to find a subtler way to pass foes.

name: Submarine Titans
detailed_description: In the year 2047, a massive comet ravages Earth's surface and the remnants of mankind descend to the bottom of the ocean in order to survive. A century passes, and humans, resilient and enduring, slowly create new life in their cool blue underwater universe. But even in the still of the deep, one truth remains... where man goes, war soon follows. The craddle of civilization has spawned the seeds of man's destruction and now all the oceans of the world are not big enough for the embattled civilizations of the power-hungry White Sharks, the technologically savvy Black Octopi and the alien Silicons. Deploy armies, research technologies, mine for resources and set in motion a plan to gain control of this spellbinding abyss or find the fate of civilization and mankind dead in the water. Features: Three distinct civilizations to play, each with its own objectives, histories, untis, technologies and strategies to master. Innovative all-new units classes and structures along with the ability to hide units and buildings in caves, unders cliffs or above opponents creates new twistes in offensive and defensive strategies. A fully realized 3D underwater universe including 5 depth/elevationlevels of iridescent swirling waters, winding mountain ranges, dimly lit caverns, cliffs, and dark tunnels. An evolutionary dual control interface allows you to control individual units or entire groups as well as simultaneously planning production and launching attacks on the enemy. Three zoom levels allow you to zoom into or out of the game anytime you need. A powerful scenario editor and an intelligent random mission generator combine to provide an almost unlimited amount of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice to see this obscure RTS find its way to steam, mostly because it's one of those games that nobody ever talks about, but these refuges can always find a home in my library (join Battle Realms, Cossacks and Impossible Creatures). This is the original game from early 2000, not a remake, and as such, it will most likely cause all kinds of technical problems on new systems. The game works fine for me as long as I do not exit it using alt-tab which can be a big problem, whenever you have some kind of notification you have to be careful not to click on it. Also, you have to exit the game through the game's settings, otherwise, it will keep on running in the background. It depends on what kind of system you are running, but I doubt that many people have a 32x system. The compatibility mode generally does nothing for these old RTS games, I had the same problem with Dune 2000.  I will be honest, I am not an expert on this particular game, I only know about it because one of my friends brought it over and we played a few missions (literally like 20 years ago). I thought it was very cool game for the time, this was during the 'Golden RTS Age' when C&C, Warcraft2 and Starcraft reigned supreme (even though I played Dune and KKND2 because that is what I had). What made this game unique is just the fact that it was underwater, giving it a special kind of aesthetic and 3 interesting factions to play as. The game also features some strange mechanics that are not common in other RTS games, such as changing elevation during combat, sometimes allowing you to win with the lesser army if you can control well. You also have to manage oxygen which I think speeds up production if you want to focus on a specific building, a little bit like the energy in Dune but with more control over it. Looking at some of the reviews that it received at the time, I guess people did not like the game because it was kinda slow, and despite having some unique features, it does have some noticeable issues. The gameplay is extremely slow-paced which can be a good or a bad thing, it really depends on your preference, but it reminds of those long nights I spend playing RTS games before they were turned into E-Sports. The first campaign mission for the 'white sharks' took me nearly 2 hours when in most games it would be around 5 minutes - it's definitely a time investment to play it. The interface is somewhat outdated even by the old standards, I noticed that game does not have the usual group controls that you would expect after playing Broodwar.+ was a very unique game for the time (and even today)+ 3 interesting factions to play+ 3 campaigns & skirmish mode+ very methodically slow-paced construction game, if you into that - It really depends on what operating system you have, the older the better. I have win10 with RTX 2060 so the game is having some problems. It works fine for me as long as I don't exit the fullscreen, but you could have completely different problems. If I don't exit through the game settings, it will keep running in the background as well.  - even for an old RTS game, it is missing some basic commands that many of us take for granted in newer games. I knew there would be some technical problems, but I enjoy collecting old RTS games simply for nostalgic reasons (and it's only $5). It's actually a really good time to be an RTS fan, many of the classics and obscure RTS games came to Steam in the last several years so I can't complain. I think this game has a big learning curve, but if you are willing to overcome it, there is hidden-gem of a game that many people never got to play.

_childDocuments_.review: For how obscure this game is, I'm honestly surprised to see one of favorite childhood games on steam. While I may have a bias from the overwhelming nostalgia I will try to review this game as fairly as possible.From what you may see, this game is somewhat similar to starcraft but not quite. The one thing that separates this from the other RTS games at the time is that everything is underwater, this allows units to change altitude to avoid projectiles fired from other units. As for factions there are three in the game, the Black Octopi, the White Sharks, and the Silicons. The Black Octopi and White sharks both work similarly enough, you use the assembler submarines you start with and build things with metal and corium. The key difference between the two are some different submarines and the appearance of subs/buildings. Silicons however, work quite differently, you are given three capsule subs that transform into the things you want to build using silicon and corium while metal is used for energy.I have yet to actually play the campaign myself, as I've always seemed to drift towards the battle scenarios which could for last for a good while as they are pretty fun, they typically last around an 1 hour or so. Graphically speaking, they are decent for a game from 2000 I don't know what else you could expect. As for the gameplay, it's pretty much your standard RTS except with the aforementioned elevation mechanics to give it that "twist" but the gameplay itself is enjoyable overall. Now the thing that has made this game truly amazing (to me at least) is the incredible soundtrack that seemingly matches perfectly with the environment and what's happening in the game. It truly does makes for an immersive play through, playing it now brings back all the fond memories I've had playing this game in the mid 2000s.
