_childDocuments_.review: This old cult classic has remained unknown to me until July of 2021 and until then, I had never heard of this game, which is a shame because this game is a lot of fun, and a game that you should try if you are itching for an older RTS game. But be aware, this is NOT your typical RTS game, which was what the ambitious developers were going for, and what I will be sharing with you now. Submarine Titans is a 3 dimensional RTS game, probably the only one where units have multiple dimensions that they could move in, and build objects, as this game's setting is all in the oceans. A direct result of this means you have some very unique fights, where the submarines can dodge your attacks, prolonging their survivability. You UI is unique, as you can see the information for both your units you have selected AND a structure that you have selected. It can seem a little overwhelming at first, but utilizing hotkeys can make it easier for you. Speaking of, this game has a very extensive hotkey system AI system, one of which you can automate commands to have your base (almost) run on its own. Depending on your faction, your construction unit will act differently. The 2 human factions behave the same, you can que as many structures as you want, and they will build so long as you have the resources. If you are the alien faction, your building unit will transform into the building and will build so long as you have the resources, similar to Zerg in StarCraft. As you build and object or sub, your resources will ticker down, similar to the Command and Conquer series. Resources: You have your typical resources that you expect from an RTS; metal which is your basic, Corium, which is your advanced resource, Sea Gold, which you use for researching new technology and for trading at the markets, Oxygen which serves as your power source, and the weapons that your subs and st. This game allows you to manipulate these resources, which is mostly done in the market, which is critical for the late game as you begin to run out of resources. Really interesting is the use of your Oxygen, which you can direct towards various types of production, such as building structures and submarines, technology research, arms creation, and others. Speaking for arms creation, you have to make sure you have enough ammo for your subs and base defenses to shoot. A little confusing at first and tricky to get the hang of, I found that managing the power and ammunition that your subs use a very nice mechanic to this game. The factions:There are 3 playable factions in Submarine titans. The 2 human factions are the militaristic White Sharks and the scientific, nature balancing Black Octpi. Both factions play relatively similar with some exceptions for their advanced subs and structures; the biggest difference between the two is that the Black Octpi utilize lasers while the White Sharks utilize missiles more. The third faction is the Silicons, who play differently than the other two factions, with many different unique base defenses, subs that combine elements of the first two factions, as well as having different uses for the resources in the game. Game play:With everything that I have said, this game does have a lot of complexity to it that will take some time getting used to, and with how the AI plays, this game can reach Dark Souls level of difficulty pretty quickly. You are constantly on your toes, planning out your next move while trying to figure out what the AI is doing. In the campaign, there are some instances you can figure out the AI's strategy, but being able to stop it is a different story. BE SURE TO SAVE OFTEN and don't be afraid of starting a mission over.  I recommend playing the tutorial and then the campaign of either the two human factions. Winning the campaign missions is very satisfying. Unfortunately, there are some bugs that still remain in the game, some of which makes the campaign missions harder to beat, or even unbeatable. Fortunately, there are patches that you can download that fix these and other issues. A quick google search should lead you to the patch, but as always be cautious about what you are downloading before you download it. Story:This is where I get mixed with this game. There is a lot of lore built into the game through the user manual. The developers really did a good job crafting a unique setting and telling the story about how all three factions came to be fighting each other in the oceans of Earth. On the other hand, the campaigns themselves felt, lacking. I didn't feel invested in the struggles of the White Sharks or the Black Octpi. The Silicons, in my opinion, were the only faction with a decent story besides world domination. Overall, hell of a game that actually was challenging, even on the easiest difficulty. I beat the campaigns on moderate difficulty, and beat an AI on hard in skirmish. There is a multiplayer community, but it is smaller than most, but if you want you play with someone just contact them or go in the lobby. Overall, 9/10. I would by this game at the $4.99 price with the amount of game play that you will have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really strong old-school RTS that includes the best of the genre at its peak, that unfortunately did not hit it big at the time (be it marketing, timing, whatever).I only played in single player (a lot of skirmish matches with AI) and the way I've experienced it I would describe it as being closer to classic Command & Conquer games than Starcraft. The base building is a bit slower and there is a really enjoyable base defence aspect of it (very cool turrets and other systems), there is plenty of upgrades, tech-ing is important in general - one of the final tiers is a weapon of mass destruction, different for each race.Similar to Starcraft though we have three factions - one alien and two human, but distinctive enough to be enjoyable on their own (think: torpedoes vs lasers). Further to that, a number of units have unique skills (stealth, mines, repair platforms, etc.).Music is rather enjoyable, but the sound design and ambience are exceptional - there was a number of times I chose to play one of the factions simply because I LOVED hearing the sound of torpedoes exploding on impact underwater.Mind you though, this game came out in 2000. I would say the graphics, just like in original Starcraft, still kind of hold up and I would have no issues with that, however, don't expect 1080p resolution, widescreen support, or any other luxuries of 2010'.Conversely, some aspects of the interface and game do not run smoothly or are simply awkward for today standards - it might not be for everyone. This includes things like: sometimes clicks don't register, you can just double click to select all units of a given type, there is no function to follow a unit with a camera, etc. This is why Submarine Titans would benefit greatly from a remaster.On the other side, there is a great number of things I have not seen in other RTS games since, or ever - hacking into enemies networks to see what numbers of units and resources they have, capturing technology, you can trade your resources for others if you're short on one of them (this was not a thing in SC & C&C), there's teleportation, nukes, screens to prevent from teleportation, fog of war and radars... the list goes on.If you decide to play it, download a graphics driver wrapper (e.g. .All you do is copy a few .dll files into the directory with the .exe of the game and the game performs much better with it on Windows 10.

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic game from back in the day.  still hangs well, doesnt feel dated. still solid solid graphics and sound..once you get the hang of it, winning through the solo battles is a fairly easy mostly mellow resource aquisition and military conquest romp. if you gain proper control early, you can fool around for an hour or two and completely overwhelm the entire board, capturing enemy stuff instead of blowing it up, mining all the resources and overbuilding bases just for fun. .or you can try to build up fast, plow through the enemy quickly, and set a speed record for yourself..on the other hand, the campaigns, played on hard, are quite challenging.  and since there are three fairly different factions, you can replay the campaign 3 times which makes for a lot of hours of gameplay. .and its a pretty little game too, so youll like bubbling around in it for extended periods.   soft greens and blues, sparks and lasers, and tons of air bubbles. the score is pretty good, and the voice overs are excellent. good thing, because youll hear from the narrator repeatedly. repeatedly. . (do not play on speakers in room with partner - or More Bandages Needed...).the two human factions have a decent amount of variation in their ships and structures, and the alien silicone society is a radically different playstyle altogether.  each of the groups has a Huge tech tree, with lots of goodies to unlock..useful fairly intuitive controls too, and it has a three speed game clock so you can slow down to a crawl while learning, or whistle along briskly when you want too..i only ever played 1 pvp match on a lan back when i played years ago, but it was great fun and worked glitch free..i hated that it would only run on windows 2000, and ive missed it ever since, because even after playing it through the first time, a quick solo battle now and then never got old - so i couldnt believe my luck when i searched steam and it popped up.  playing fine on windows 10 for me now..10/10  A+ Fun

_childDocuments_.review: Submarine Titans is an ancient game from 2000.  It's a whopping 23 years old at the time of this review.  The game lacks proper widescreen aspect ratio support (it's locked at 4:3) or support for any modern gaming display resolutions, hasn't been modernised or updated to run smoothly on modern gaming PCs.  Despite this lack of modernisation, it carries a pretty high price tag for such an ancient game.  This seems to have been put on Steam as a nostalgia gouge.It's a run-of-the-mill base builder/resource harvester/army builder RTS (a great format for games and it's a shame they've mostly stopped being made).  The only big differentiator here is the underwater theme, you build an underwater base and your units are attack submarines.  The gimmick never really caught on.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no options to change the resolution for the game or customise the graphics settings.  There's no way for gamers to ensure this is running at the native resolution of their displays... there's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.  There's no way for gamers to try improve the very badly dated graphics. Another problem here is that you can't alt+tab out of the game properly, another shortcoming that should have been picked up with even a basic amount of software testing.  The graphics will be distorted if you try go back into the game after switching out.  This is extremely frustrating in the modern era of gaming and it's a shortcoming that gamers are unlikely to accept.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Submarine Titans is relatively expensive for an abandonware nostalgia gouge, at $5 USD, and it's not worth it.  The game is just too old, hasn't been modernised.  And as the old saying goes, you can't go home again.

_childDocuments_.review: Submarine Titans, released in 2000, is a real-time strategy game that dives into the depths of underwater warfare, offering a unique and immersive experience. Developed by Ellipse Studios, the game blends tactical depth, innovative gameplay mechanics, and an engaging storyline set in a submerged post-apocalyptic world.One of the standout features of Submarine Titans is its setting—a world ravaged by nuclear war, where the last remnants of humanity have taken refuge beneath the ocean's surface. The underwater environment adds a refreshing twist to the RTS genre, as players navigate through three distinct factions vying for dominance in this aquatic world.The game's single-player campaign is both compelling and challenging, weaving a narrative that explores the struggles of the underwater colonies. The diverse missions, ranging from resource management to intense naval battles, keep players on their toes and offer a well-rounded gaming experience.Submarine Titans introduces a unique resource management system, where players must balance the extraction of resources from underwater vents while fending off hostile sea creatures. This dynamic adds an extra layer of complexity to the gameplay, requiring strategic planning to ensure the survival and growth of your underwater civilization.The three playable factions each have their own strengths, weaknesses, and unique units, adding variety and replayability to the game. Whether commanding the high-tech White Sharks, the nomadic Black Octopi, or the mysterious Silicons, players are presented with different playstyles and strategies to master.The graphics, while perhaps showing signs of aging, capture the essence of the underwater world effectively. The eerie and immersive atmosphere is complemented by a fitting soundtrack that enhances the sense of isolation and tension.Multiplayer, a crucial aspect of any RTS game, allows players to engage in intense submarine battles with friends or other enthusiasts. The strategic depth of the game truly shines in multiplayer matches, where every decision can sway the tide of war beneath the waves.While Submarine Titans may not have achieved the same level of recognition as some other RTS classics, its innovative approach to the genre and captivating underwater setting make it a hidden gem for fans of real-time strategy games. Despite the passage of time, Submarine Titans remains a unique and enjoyable experience, offering a glimpse into a submerged world of strategic depth and aquatic warfare.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice to see this obscure RTS find its way to steam, mostly because it's one of those games that nobody ever talks about, but these refuges can always find a home in my library. This is the original game from early 2000, not a remake, and as such, it will most likely cause all kinds of technical problems on new systems. The game works fine for me as long as I do not exit it using alt-tab which can be a big problem, whenever you have some kind of notification you have to be careful not to click on it.Pros:+ was a very unique game for the time (and even today)+ 3 interesting factions to play+ 3 campaigns & skirmish mode+ very methodically slow-paced construction game, if you into thatCons:Technical issues - It really depends on what operating system you have, the older the better. I have win10 with RTX 2060 so the game is having some problems. It works fine for me as long as I don't exit the fullscreen, but you could have completely different problems. If I don't exit through the game settings, it will keep running in the background as well.Bad UI shortcuts - even for an old RTS game, it is missing some basic commands that many of us take for granted in newer games.Overall Thoughts:I knew there would be some technical problems, but I enjoy collecting old RTS games simply for nostalgic reasons. It's actually a really good time to be an RTS fan, many of the classics and obscure RTS games came to Steam in the last several years so I can't complain. I think this game has a big learning curve, but if you are willing to overcome it, there is hidden-gem of a game that many people never got to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the blast from the past was worth what I paid for it, but ultimately the end was unsatisfying and I perhaps answered the question, at least to myself, as to why this game didn't succeed more than it did.First of all, the game is beautiful to look at even to this day, and I remembered how amazing it looked when I first played it back in 2006.  There's some serious artistry there that isn't necessary for gameplay at all.  I found Submarine Titans to be a graphically er...immersive experience.But this game I believe is just too smart for it's own good.   I made it through nine of the ten White Shark episodes on "hard" AI difficulty before I gave up.   (I always play RTS games on "hard" otherwise they're not challenging for me)   In this game, the objectives for each episode became ever longer laundry lists of things to move and protect, capture, build, and ever longer in terms of plot points, revealed in stages, so that I'd plan a particular approach to an objective only to find it likely won't work for the entire episode.  Surprises in RTS games are fun, but they can go too far.   I ended up saving games a lot so as to not have to do the same things over and over.And, it is possible to go "off script" in an episode and have the next phase of the episode give you instructions that you simply cannot achieve.   How can you nuke both Black Octopi command centers when you just destroyed one of them?   Luckily I got credit for nuking both when I nuked the one left, but plot holes like this should not exist.Furthermore, all these things I had to do had no context within any discernible storyline, other than I was a White Shark and I needed to prevail over those Octopi and Silicons.   At least in the Command and Conquer games there is an overall narrative I'm unfolding in each episode. Also, many common functions do not have shortcut keys.   The control panel says "no key" as if they knew they could have assigned it a key, but they just didn't in order to force a lot of extra pointing and clicking when your're under attack and every second counts.   Finally, I simply couldn't beat the last episode of White Sharks on the "hard" setting.  I remember reaching that point in 2006 and I looked forward to the rematch with a wiser and smarter me.   I learned some game functionality that I was not aware of back then, and I had captured all the available Black Octopi tech that was possible to capture, so I had both tech trees going for me.  But the sheer paucity of non-replaceable resources combined with the huge numbers of enemy defenses and large opposing fleets finally made me think I had better things to do and didn't care anymore.So, I was defeated at the last level fifteen years after the first time.   I think this game should have been intensely play tested and tweaked for about another month before release.   It seemed like a work just not quite finished, which is a shame.   But at least I got to play it again, and get a deep sea blast from the past.

name: Days Gone
detailed_description: Days Gone is an open-world action-adventure game set in a harsh wilderness two years after a devastating global pandemic. Step into the dirt flecked shoes of former outlaw biker Deacon St. John, a bounty hunter trying to find a reason to live in a land surrounded by death. Scavenge through abandoned settlements for equipment to craft valuable items and weapons, or take your chances with other survivors trying to eke out a living through fair trade… or more violent means. KEY FEATURES • A striking setting: From forests and meadows, to snowy plains and desert lava fields, the Pacific Northwest is both beautiful and lethal. Explore a variety of mountains, caves, mines and small rural towns, scarred by millions of years of volcanic activity. • Brutal encounters: With vicious gangs and hordes of Freakers roaming the land, you’ll need to make full use of a variety of customizable traps, weapons, and upgradable skills to stay alive. Don’t forget your Drifter bike, an invaluable tool in a vast land. • An ever-changing environment: Jump on the saddle of Deacon’s trusty motorbike and explore a dynamic world dramatically affected by the weather, a dramatic day/night cycle and the evolving Freakers, who adjust to their surroundings – and the people in it. • A compelling story: Lose yourself in a powerful tale of desperation, betrayal and regret, as Deacon St. John searches for hope after suffering a deep, personal loss. What makes us human when faced with the daily struggle for survival? INCLUDES • New Game Plus • Survival Mode • Challenge Mode • Bike Skins PC features include ultra-wide monitor support, unlocked framerates and improved graphics (increased level of details, field of view, foliage draw distances).

_childDocuments_.review: Introduction:"Days Gone" by Bend Studio is like the lovechild of "State of Decay" and "Far Cry 5," mixing survival, open-world exploration, and storytelling in a way that's been missing from recent game releases. It's got that old-school passion and attention to detail that's hard to find nowadays, plus killer guitar music that sucks you right into the world.Plot and Characters:You play as Deacon St. John, a badass drifter trying to survive in the zombie-filled wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. The story dives deep into themes of survival and redemption, with a cast of characters that'll stick with you long after you put down the controller.Gameplay:Scavenging for supplies, taking down hordes of Freakers, and exploring the open world—it's all here, just like in "State of Decay." But there's also that Far Cry vibe, with dynamic encounters and multiple ways to tackle missions. It's a blast, no matter how you play it.Graphics and Sound:The graphics are stunning, and the sound design is top-notch. But what really sets it apart is the guitar music. Seriously, it's like having your own personal soundtrack as you ride through the apocalypsebut it haunts you when you least expect it which is incredible.Atmosphere:"Days Gone" nails the post-apocalyptic vibe, with a world that feels dangerous and alive. Whether you're sneaking through abandoned towns or fighting off waves of enemies, the atmosphere sucks you right in. And everything make sense here. Replay Value:There's plenty to do in "Days Gone," from main story missions to side quests and just exploring the world. You'll want to come back for more, just to experience everything it has to offer.Overall Impression:"Days Gone" is a wild ride from start to finish. It's got everything you could want in a post-apocalyptic game—action, drama, and killer guitar riffs. If you're a fan of survival games or just looking for something new to play, give it a shot.Conclusion:In a sea of cookie-cutter games, "Days Gone" stands out as a breath of fresh air. It's got that old-school charm mixed with modern gameplay mechanics, and it's an absolute blast to play. So grab your controller and dive into the apocalypse—you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: *Hidden gem*Once in a while a game enters your scope that checks a lot of boxes for you, but somehow doesn't for the rest of the world. Days Gone is such a game. For me it really is a hidden gem. It reminds me a lot of Red Dead Redemption 2, in a good way. I also have a weakness for the Northwestern US setting, so there's a little bias going on here. Be warned. *Slow gaming*I like 'slow' games like RDR2 and Days Gone, which have a certain touch of realism to them, like things having a weighty feel to 'em, nothing looking overtly stylized, but just plain grounded and 'realistic' (taken with a huge grain of gaming salt, ofcourse). And while you can't really compare a horse to a bike for obvious reasons, Days Gone, like RDR2, really succeeds in emphasizing how dependant we as a species are on other things when we want to get somewhere and not waste days walking. Yes, those are the true 'days gone': you'll never get them back. So you better give that bike some TLC :-)*A lot of screaming, frowning and also non-verbalism*I am also really liking most of the voice acting and facial animations, except for maybe when Deek is screaming oneliner after oneliner while sneaking through enemy camps. Dialogues sound like conversations real people might have, very telling and convincing facial expressions (also like real people may have), it's a breath of fresh air not wanting to skip stale dialogue. The game is very lenghty, gunplay is adequate, melee could use some variation, and yes, after a while it gets repetitive, unless you like to change up your playstyle once in a while. But hey, repetition has sort of become the norm in gaming today, so whaddayougonnadoaboutit, right?*Hordes are like dating apps*A special shoutout to the hordes is very well deserved. Man, I haven't felt this vulnerable and underequipped whilst playing a game in a long time. The times when you get overrun by a horde, or a fence-tangled rager bear and some of his furry howling friends... Scary stuff, and really, really great fun. This, like Dying Light, is what zombie games should be like: totally overwhelming you at times when you're not expecting it. Braindead people relentlessly following you around because they want your flesh, until they discover more, or better flesh next to you, kind of reminds you of Tinder, right? Ah yes, Lovely stuff.*Runs like a freaker on a stamina cocktail*For me, the game runs great. Frame time is all over the place though, but it doesn't show dropped frames at locked 60fps. This may have to do with the latest win10 updates, which are screwing with my intel CPU steppings. Still, at 3440p max settings, it never goes over 75% gpu usage (RTX 2080ti) and 25% cpu usage (9900ks).*Yay or nay*Yay. If you like story-rich games with lots of freedom, semi-realism, bikers who thankfully don't dwell on being a biker, and decent acting, Days Gone is the game for you. Maybe not for the rest of the world, but hey, they can all go play Fortnite and CoD, for all I care.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I am enjoying this game so much more than I anticipated.  It is great.  I thought it was going to be a been there done that combination of games we have played without originality.  Voice acting is good enough where I care about characters and listen.  There is versatility to keep me from getting bored.  It's a slow burn as far as introducing new areas and enemies, so you don't see every variation in the first 1/4 of the game.  MOST IMPORTANTLY though, the atmosphere of the game is amazing.  The fear of walking through the woods as an underpowered protagonist caused me to legit avoid confrontations whenever possible and was way to terrified to even try a horde...still a nope for hordes in caves and mine shafts.Quick disclaimer: Several of my in game hours have been sitting in the background of my computer as I get some work done or get called away from computer.  Not nearly as far as you would think with that much time invested.  I am still in the middle of the 3rd region (trying to avoid spoilers here).Now to the point of this post.  It is absolutely mind blowing to me that the game is missing some QOL stuff.  Most glaring of issues is the lack of a statistics page.  Hell, GTA 3 had one, as do almost all open world games now a days.  Multiple storylines are updated at once and I really like the writing, but you have to keep perfect track of what is already in journal to know what is new for you to read.  And why no bestiary?  It's not like it would have been a ton of work because there is only a moderate amount of enemy types.  Would like to have something where a little more is revealed about each enemy as you hit certain kill counts. _childDocuments_.review: It is Fallout 4 meets Last of Us. You get Fallout's huge open world rendered in grittier detail (and without the comic book monsters). And you get a Last of Us-style post-apocalyptic survival story - but with bigger and more memorable npc characters. And you do all of this on a motorbike and with some really cool tattoes.The controls and combat mechanics are good. Great stealth and sniping opportunities. Wide variety of weapons to suit different play styles and approaches. The human enemy AI is basic. Fighting hordes (up to 500 strong) requires strategy.Bend Studios really nailed the motorbiking mechanics. Controls are simple but probably some of the best travel action I've had, EVER. There is a fast travel system, but I never used it. Even when mopping up end game content for the platinum trophy I rode my bike everywhere. With roads, tracks and x-country, lakes, mountains, towns, sun, rain and snow and all in a beautifully rendered landscape - you could have made a whole game out of just riding your bike. In fact DG could be a biking game with zombies, not a zombie game with bikes. I tell you, it's no accident one of the PS trophies is to accumulate 10 minutes of rear wheel drifting!The whole post apocalypse formula is a familiar trope. But DG manages to do something different. It doesn't overdo the mutant monster angle, which keeps it grittier and more realistic. And it throws in the horror aspect with the zombie horde - hundreds of infected humans acting with a hive mind. Plenty of challenge. Lots to do. Good story. The game never felt repetitive and from beginning to end I never got bored. The npc characterisation and voice acting, their stories, their camps - it made it feel like a real place.Sony have reportedly pulled the plug on Days Gone 2 (summer 2021). But this game is going to be a cult classic - in a couple of years Sony will regret it hasn't started work on DG2, I'm sure of it.

_childDocuments_.review: So, despite what the Fortnite, Overwatch, and PUBG crowd will tell you, this is an absolutely phenomenal game.Pros:* The story can be a tad predictable at times, but it is never boring even in the slightest. The story also has an amazing balance on drama, action, horror, and even with the occasional bit of comedy thrown in, but with never quite enough to ruin the atmosphere.* The combat is fulfilling and satisfying* The stealth works really well, and with the exception of some over-sensitivity with hordes, works pretty realistically.* The bike movement feels natural and its pretty obvious that the developers put a lot of effort into making it feel as close to real as they possibly could without sending a drifter bike with the game. Cons:*Even after two years and ported from PS4 to PC, the game will occasionally face game-breaking glitches; however, these can usually be corrected with a simple reset of the game and loading of a previous save. I highly recommend that you save VERY often, especially on higher difficulties.*While it is not an issue for me, I'm well aware that it's a deal-breaker for a lot of people these days; there is no multiplayer and more than likely never will be in this game or any potential follow-ups.Days Gone, in my opinion is, by far, one of the best games that has ever been made up to this point. I give this game a solid 9.5/10 and the only reason it doesn't get a 10/10 is simply because the game does still occasionally run into some massive bugs, even though we are years after the initial release.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea why this game is so glorified.I love games that have a good storyline and character development. Even if the graphics are not amazing at times.But this game... oh boy.. I really had high hopes for it, and was I in for a surprise. The main story is so weak and bland and just allover the place. Most of the time it makes ZERO sense what so ever. The idea was there, but the execution was atrocious. I feel that the writers were so damn lazy, they put the "Post- Apocalyptic Game Scenario" prompt, into Chat GPT, and just went with whatever came out.Here is the story in a nutshell...A homeless bum rides his bike around with his pal killing zombies, discovers his "assumed dead" wife might be still alive, finds her, and then continues to stay a homeless bum killing more zombies. Also I've never played a game where I hated the protagonist as much as Deacon St. John. He is rude the entire game, his snarky responses and zero personality made me want the freaks to tear him apart and eat him. Then we could takeover as BOOZER with his blade arm and go on a killing spree. I'm also annoyed at some of the "Flashback" cut-scenes" which are so pointless, and have absolutely nothing to do with the game play, and you can't skip them. The Game-play on its own as a "standalone" is pretty descent. A lot of the missions are repetitive, driving around from camp to camp essentially doing the exact same thing you just did for the other camp. But what breaks the monotonous story line is that you get to go around and kill weird creatures, and sometimes you have to be really creative, and I like that a lot. Only get it when the Game is on SALE.otherwise don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: In the vast landscape of video games, where innovation, storytelling, and gameplay converge, Days Gone emerges not just as a game, but as a defining experience that sets the bar for what a truly exceptional gaming title can achieve. Developed by Bend Studio and released in 2019 exclusively for PlayStation consoles, Days Gone has garnered acclaim and admiration for its unparalleled depth, narrative complexity, and immersive gameplay. Here's why Days Gone stands as not just a great game, but perhaps the greatest game ever created.At the heart of Days Gone lies its meticulously crafted open world, a hauntingly beautiful rendition of the Pacific Northwest ravaged by a global pandemic. From lush forests to desolate highways, every corner of the game's vast environment teems with life and danger. The dynamic weather system and day-night cycle not only enhance the visual and atmospheric realism but also significantly impact gameplay, requiring players to adapt their strategies and approaches as they navigate through the ever-changing landscape.The protagonist, Deacon St. John, serves as the emotional anchor of Days Gone. A former outlaw turned drifter, Deacon is a deeply flawed yet compelling character whose journey of survival and redemption resonates throughout the game. Voice actor Sam Witwer's nuanced performance brings Deacon to life, portraying his inner conflicts, vulnerabilities, and moments of bravery with authenticity and depth. Players are not merely spectators to Deacon's story; they become invested participants in his quest for meaning and purpose in a world teetering on the brink of collapse.Beyond its captivating narrative, Days Gone excels in delivering a gameplay experience that is both challenging and rewarding. Combat encounters are intense and strategic, requiring players to utilize a diverse arsenal of weapons, traps, and tactics to overcome threats ranging from marauding human factions to hordes of ravenous Freakers. The game's motorcycle, Deacon's primary mode of transportation, serves as more than just a means to traverse the vast open world; it symbolizes freedom, independence, and survival in a hostile environment.The depth of Days Gone extends beyond its main storyline, with a wealth of side missions, activities, and collectibles that encourage exploration and discovery. Each side quest contributes to the overarching narrative, enriching the player's understanding of the world and its inhabitants. The game's attention to detail is evident in its environmental storytelling, where abandoned buildings, makeshift camps, and hidden caches tell silent tales of struggle and resilience in the face of catastrophe.Moreover, Days Gone showcases Bend Studio's commitment to continuous improvement and player engagement. Post-launch updates have introduced new features, challenges, and quality-of-life improvements based on community feedback, ensuring that the game evolves alongside its dedicated player base. This ongoing support not only enhances the longevity of Days Gone but also reinforces its status as a living, breathing world that continues to captivate and challenge players long after its initial release.In conclusion, Days Gone stands as a testament to the transformative power of video games as a storytelling medium. Its immersive world, complex characters, and compelling gameplay combine to create an experience that transcends the boundaries of traditional gaming. For those who seek not just entertainment but an emotional and unforgettable journey, Days Gone represents the pinnacle of gaming excellence. As players embark on Deacon St. John's harrowing odyssey through a shattered world, they are reminded that greatness in gaming isn't just about winning; it's about the moments that resonate long after the game has ended.

_childDocuments_.review: So... full disclaimer.  I was raised in Oregon.  I grew up as a boyscout camping in some of the very locations this game refers to on the regular.  I'm very, very much biased in my opinion....Days gone is what I've wanted from a zombie apocalypse (sorry, freaker apocalypse) game for ages.  It's an open world adventure that from what I've seen is if Last of Us and Red Dead Redemption had a baby.  It has it's flaws.  It has it's imperfections but it left a surprising mark on my mind and that's sort of a big deal.  Days Gone is an open world zombie killing romp that takes place in Oregon.  You're a bad ass biker with a heart of gold.  It's a cliche but one that feels both fairly unique in a game like this and fresh.  This is very much Daryl from "Walking Dead" in video game form.  Some reviews have criticized the pacing  of the game and while I can see that... it's what I personally would like to see more of in video games.  It's just a fleshed out world that I felt very much inspired to keep dipping back into.For those that grew up in Oregon, btw, it's a surreal experience.  It's not a picture perfect, to scale, re-creation of the state of Oregon but it's very much a love note to some of the best natural wildlife landmarks of the state.  As a kid I went camping and hiking on Three Finger jack.  Here I fought a nasty group of outlaws.  In real life I've had several restful and relaxing stays at Belknapp hotsprings and it filled me with a giddy excitement to see it brought to digital life in this game.  (with a lot more rabid zombie attackers.)  Performance wise the game is in the upper echelon of console to PC games.  The graphic settings are nothing to write home about but this game performs spectacularly well.  I bought this on PS4 when it release and was intrigued but turned off by the subpar performance and feel of it.  On a decent PC (my setup is far from cutting edge due to how difficult it is to get a new graphics card these days) this game performs to a stellar level.  High frame rates with most settings maxed out make me feel like it was worth waiting for this moment.  I'm extremely happy with how well this seems to play on my setup and most people with decent computers are going to spend way less time obsessing over settings and a lot more time just enjoying the atmosphere of the game because it just performs really really well.  This game was, by far, my standout sleeper hit of the year.  The location bias is real for me, but even aside from that I think this game would still be continuing to hold my attention and our current age off "what is the latest shiniest thing.." that's sort of a big deal.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried my best to like this game. It's not horrible but I can't give it a positive review. Spoilers below.The graphics are great, performance was super smooth for me. Hordes are exciting to fight, and the Freaks are much more interesting than just normal zombies. Boozer is also a great character, missions with him were enjoyable. These are all good things.Now to the bad. Most of the story was nauseating, and like many modern "open-world" games, it drags on way too long. Sarah is a boring cardboard cutout, I never once bought her and Deacons relationship.The story starts out good enough, focusing on the themes of letting go and forgiving the past. I thought they were going to stick with it, but nope, the cliches all come out around half way through.  That's pathetic and lazy writing. Boozer and Deacon's bromance was more fleshed out than this.Ambushes are annoying - as you're riding around you will get sniped/tripwire'd and your bike durability will be sent to 0 without warning. Wolves, bears, runners are all tedious bullet sponges to fight. The weapon selection is pointless, you will just be using an Assault Rifle 99% of the time. Other weapons are hidden behind Trust levels anyway, which requires grinding.Crafting is boring, and you will find yourself spending 30% of your time just collecting scrap to repair your bike and melee weapons. The "Witcher Sense" ability makes an appearance in the game, but a very dumbed down version. Just walk around and press X on things to solve the mystery.I understand with Zombie games there's not a whole lot of creative options for story telling. But this just got more frustrating the more you played. And in a story-driven game, if you're not interesting in the objectives and characters, then you will find it hard to come back to it. I got this on sale so I wouldn't say my money was wasted, but this game is just very mediocre. Try it at your own discretion.

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable so far and I'm playing it on hard.I'd have started playing it on Survivalist 2 but I wanted the HUD.I'm having a lot of fun with the Residue Bolts. A lot of... fun... heheI wish I could carry more items but I'm early into the game and might get larger carry capacity later?Then again, I am playing on Hard and it seems to be very well balanced.The AI on Hard seems to give up a little too early. I can get into a fight, go around a corner, hide behind a truck in the full open, and the humanoid enemies just give up. Most of the time they'll stand there, swear or call for you to come out until they get bored and then leave. Would be great if they would call over the other enemies and begin a search of your last seen location.I feel the writers could have better left the mystery of Sarah as more of a mystery for far longer. I just got past the part where Deacon fought off the rednecks and the dialogue right before this revealed too much. I can already see her involvement in the 'present tense' of the story. Didn't need to have her bring up her work as a botanist working on rare plants in the area for a bio-engineering research company, ffs.Everything else has been great. From the visuals, the audio, the mechanics, story (despite the glaring give away mentioned above) are all good. I look forward to finishing the game and probably playing it through a second time on Survival 2.

_childDocuments_.review: A good open-world zombie game : 7.5/10 (Its not a 7 but not an 8 game in my opinion)This is definitely not a perfect game, far from it, But it has its own charm for a story-driven zombie game and the fact it has no other rival in its specific genre at the moment. For someone who loves Zombie in medias, I always crave for something like The Walking Dead in games. It has what it takes to be a great zombie games, a well made open world, scavenging as much as you want for your utilities, a typical zombie apocalypse story, and relationship between human, but fail to do so because of some issues.The flaw is what makes this game not perfect, but not bad in any ways. The story is not so deep like The Walking Dead, heck even shallow at some point. The human relationship have many thing that can be explored deeper even after finishing the story. Other issues like the way it takes time to set up the story to get interesting is also the main problem here. Other issues like there are repetitive and unecessary lines when you save random people and how it takes so much time for them to just go away so you can continue exploring. Those are the promiment issues that I immediately recognize that really intervene with my playthrough. There are other than those but definitely not a game changing or interrupting.

_childDocuments_.review: After small issues at the very first intro mission, the game got really good.Story is actually quite nice (in my opinion). You don't have to grind and can just follow the story, which progresses very good. But sometimes the grind is fun. Unfortunately it gets repetetive after a while.It is not a tripple A title, some cutscenes fail to create the emotions intended but the characters are still good (though some are edgy)The best thing: I never felt really safe when travelling the world. This sense of danger is usually lost in other zombie games after you progressed and end up as a one man army. This happens here to an extent, too of course, but Days Gone never gives you the feeling of somebody, who can just do everything unprepared. Never mind how strong you feel, if you meet a horde unprepared you don't "no problem, I just outrun them in circles, or dodge them"One thing you will hate: The main character has sometimes the weirdest voice acting totally not fitting into the situation. And he only basically has two catch-phrases when you have to refuel your bike. You have to refuel it very often at the beginning :DAll in all: 3.5 out of 5. I would recommend trying it. You might actually like it :)

_childDocuments_.review: I normally dont write reviews, but this game is soooooo good i just had to write one:This is one of the few games that i really fell in love with. Like back in the good old days when i was playing Half Life.Days Gone feels like a hybrid of The Last of Us and Read Dead Redemption 2. The open world is really beautiful and it conveys the dreaded feeling of a post-apocalyptic world perfectly. The story is really good and most side missions are really fun. The main characters feel very realistic and believable. The player character Deacon is a bad ass and has very good voice acting. You can really feel his rage, as he descends more and more into insanity.The Gameplay is amazing and the gunplay feels very good. The Survival Aspect is made really interesting without being annoying or farm heavy.The only downside are the 1-2 hours of the tutorial-style missions at the beginning of the game, that teach you the mechanics of the game. But they really do payoff and the game gets extremely good after that.I really recommend this game to anyone who likes a great post apocalyptic open world game with a really good story, awesome gameplay and amazing characters.Rating in numbers: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I owned this on the PS4 and did not play much due to the poor frame rate making the bike riding feel sluggish and mainly not enjoying having to use a controller to aim and shoot.Fast forward a couple years and damn this game is underrated! Nearly 50 hours it has taken me to finish the games main story and there is still loads left to do including New Game+. I enjoyed the game from beginning to the end and did not at any point feel bored playing this game, it was really enjoyable. I compared it to Mad Max many times its literally that with Zombies and a better story line and the reason for the comparison is because instead of upgrading your car like you do in mad max you upgrade your bike you take over militia camps same as you do in mad max the only difference here is there are Freakers/Zombies instead of raving lunatics both post apocalyptic settings and very similar game mechanics, and considering I have completed both games I would put this way above mad max in terms of enjoyment. Comparing it to the PS4 version its so much more fun to play and a far better experience over all, bike handling is a lot better with the unrestricted frame rates making it feel smoother and more responsive, weapon handling on keyboard and mouse is so much nicer and far more accurate although I would say some of the cross hairs in the game felt a little off center? Performance wise this game runs great on my 5600XT everything cranked up by default even when there are massive hoards of freakers the game never slowed down it ran great.Story line wasn't and isn't anything new its the typical I have to find my lost lover and will do anything to find them with the never giving up attitude, and along the way you meet some likeable characters some not so which was great because those I didn't like were the villains anyway so they nailed that, there are few twists and turns on the way but overall the story was enjoyable but again nothing new. The environment was really nice and looks visually great one minute you are in a nice dense forest the next in snowy mountains with random weather changes etc, it is a really nice looking game with a day and night cycle and depending on the time of day you can expect changes in the amount of and the aggressiveness of the freakers night time they literally are everywhere but during the day they hide away in caves and buildings a bit like dying light has a night and day system for the zombies.50 hours in and I have just completed it and I still want to go back and play more get the nests cleared and finish the side stories up and maybe a new game+ play through which for me is unusual as I don't normally feel a need to continue playing a game once the main campaign is done with that does to show how fun it was for me.I highly recommend this game and its a shame they are not going to be making a sequel :( developers have other plans, but don't skip this game it has plenty of content and its a load of fun, nothing like being chased by 300+ freakers as you run for you life tossing molotovs and pipe bombs in panic.

_childDocuments_.review: An emotionally charged narrative centered around survival, loss, and brotherhood set in a post-apocalyptic world overrun by zombie-like creatures known as Freakers. You play as Deacon St. John, a drifter and bounty hunter, navigating the harsh landscape of the Pacific Northwest as he searches for his missing wife and tries to survive in a lawless world.The game excels in its storytelling, delving deep into themes of camaraderie and the bonds between characters. Deacon's relationship with his best friend, Boozer, is particularly compelling, showcasing the struggles of brotherhood amidst chaos. Their loyalty and shared history add emotional depth, making players truly invested in their journey and the decisions they face.Gameplay-wise, Days Gone features a vast open world filled with dynamic weather and day-night cycles, which significantly impact gameplay. Players can approach challenges in various ways, whether through stealth, combat, or utilizing their trusty motorcycle for mobility. The motorcycle becomes a character in itself, enhancing the sense of freedom and exploration.While some gameplay mechanics can feel repetitive, the vast array of side quests and challenges keeps the experience engaging. The combat system is robust, with a mix of melee and ranged options, allowing players to develop their preferred playstyle.Visually, the game captures the beauty of its environment, with lush forests, desolate towns, and the eerie atmosphere of the Freaker-infested world. The sound design also enhances the immersion, from the chilling cries of the Freakers to the rev of your motorcycle.Overall, Days Gone is a heartfelt journey that balances thrilling gameplay with emotional storytelling. It beautifully portrays the bonds of brotherhood in a world filled with despair, making it a memorable experience that resonates long after the credits roll.

_childDocuments_.review: Days Gone has a very similar gameplay style to Last of Us from Sony Studios. In this game, you are a biker dude mourning for the lost of his wife during the zombie apocalypse. I highly enjoyed my time playing through the campaign and is a easy recommend if you can get it on sale.+ THE HORDE (simply the highlight of the game - you can feel the tension everytime you face one and I've never seen any other zombie game have as much zombies chasing you as Days Gone)+ Later part of the main story is engaging + The side characters are really memorable (especially The Colonel, Rikki and Weaver)+ The graphics on this game is really good.+ There are several locations and they each have their own charm (Thick Forest, Desert, Urban suburbia, Wasteland, etc.)- The voice acting of the main character is really annoying - Story is a bit slow paced at the start (takes a while to get invested in what's happening)- Lack of customization on the main character and weapons (you cannot customize how Deek looks and you can only extend the magazine of the guns)- Wish there were more option on the bike (you spend 80-90% of the game on it so I wish there were more options)- Camps are good but I wish there was more shops and options.- JUST HEARD THAT DAYS GONE 2 WILL NOT BE HAPPENING ANYTIME SOONAll in all, I would highly recommend this game. It takes a while to get going but it is a fun journey blasting through zombie to get there.

_childDocuments_.review: Horrible cliché story with characters who I couldn't stand in a over and done open world gameplay loop. Get mission, kill people or a horde somewhere and come back for your reward. Rinse and repeat for 30 hours and you're done. I feel for the voice actor that voiced Deacon. I'm sure he did a good job with the directions he got, but I cringed at his awkward boy biker persona in cutscenes. Especially when he should be portraying this bad ass taking out hordes by himself and it completely juxtaposes with how he is the other 90% of the game. You are not a biker gang survivor on hist last legs in this game. Bad writing and a archaic gameplay loop makes this just a sheer bore to play. Get it if you want something to play whilst doing something else. Which is what I did after playing it for one hour.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most underrated PS4 exclusive to ever come out. This game got hit with constant negative criticism at launch and that kept me from giving the game a chance for a couple years after launch. I ended up trying it out and 100%'ing this game on PS4 during the pandemic and loved the atmosphere and world so much, I came back and 100%'ed it again on PC after it got ported over. Still one of the most graphically impressive games to ever come out, especially on PC with maxed out graphics settings, and the game runs incredibly well, even on mid-tier GPUs at 4K. The combat is one of the most unique aspects about this game. There is literally no other game that can send a swarm of hundreds of zombies at you, all on screen at once, the way this game can. It is truly some of the most exhilarating gameplay you can find. It's really a shame that Neil Druckmann was so threatened by Days Gone that Naughty Dog nearly absorbed all of Bend Studio, and because of this the studio lost some key team members and Days Gone 2 ended up getting shot down by Sony. That's incredibly sad, but I can't wait to see what game Bend Studio makes next, and at least we have this gem on PC. Forget what you've heard about Days Gone, you should really play this if you haven't given it a chance yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I think about this game a lot. I don't quite know what it is that made it so good, but I loved it. I think maybe the story felt small enough to be meaningful, or the interactions between the main character and the camps made sense. Maybe the story and the characters in it wasn't ridiculous and over-the-top like most games. I dunno, really. _childDocuments_.review: Idiot developers who don't play their own game.  I'm about 15 hours in the game and I can count a dozen instances of going to an area and doing a side bounty or tackling a nest-clearing objective and suddenly I'm thrown into an emersion-breaking cutscene that ruins the firefight, pulls me to a different location, and sometimes even changes the time of day.In the same location up north this happened TWICE... once forcing me to stop clearing nests so I could follow a helicopter for a story mission, then when I returned there was an event where a mob of zombies were chasing someone needing help.  I get out a distractor and prepare to engage when... nope, cutscene, day changes, I'm moved to the other side of the bridge and that event is now gone.  What moron thought this would be a good idea?I have other gripes like binding the same control to dropping gas cans the same as jumping off of ledges (I've jumped off a bridge after filling my motorcycle's gas tank a few times already because the game prioritizes movement over dropping the item, even when the control is held) and stuff like the game forcing itself to pause if you Alt+Tab out during a lengthy, unskippable cutscene, but the forced cutscenes that break immersion are ridiculous and completely turns me off of the game.They took the same Far Cry, Red Dead, State of Decay, etc. format and made a decent approximation but didn't think deep enough about player immersion whatsoever. _childDocuments_.review: Update 2: Okay, I can finally recommend this game again, as you can now permanently disable the data collection in the game's settings. It's such a damn shame that we needed to give so much backlash over such a needless invasion of privacy. I don't know why Sony has it out to constantly force stumbling blocks like this on Days Gone, but it's exhausting to see.Update: I'm now marking this review as negative after learning about the frankly outrageous data collection being implemented here. I'm uninstalling the game until this absurd aspect is removed from the game. There is no justification for key logging any sort of game, especially an offline-only experience, and I for am deeply disappointed in Sony for doing this.I already played this game to 100% completion on PS4 back when it first released, and let me tell you - this PC port is worth it, even if you experienced it before. Your reflexes hold true on a keyboard and mouse, but the aiming and performance is far and away the definitive way to enjoy Days Gone.If you miss open world games that don't copy Far Cry and hard-hitting stories that still manage to have a hopeful message, Days Gone is an excellent time. Deacon starts off like a traditional gruffy grump, but he grows into one of the few nuanced male leads in mainstream gaming. The story is a slow burn that pays of beautifully.Easily one of my favorite games in the longest time. Ignore the haters calling this "generic" - I feared that'd be the case my first time going in, but I was delightfully surprised. Bend Studios does great work, and this is their finest game yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to other people when they tell you this game gets better. It's very true to life in that it never gets better.  If you're <2 hours into this game and you have even the slightest feeling of being bored, stop playing and request a refund.  What you get in the first couple hours of this game is the exact same stuff you're going to get for the next 57 hours of the game.  Nothing will change.The story is unoriginal and predictable.  The love story is overly sentimental as if they were written by someone who has never been in love themselves, but learned about it from fan fiction.  What's worse is that you're forced to watch them.  Watch them walk.  For what must have been the length of a marathon at a half mile an hour.  I'm fairly sure that 58 hours of my 59 hours of playing time is just watching scenes where people have to walk.The game is repetitive and bland.  I entertained myself by saying "ooh piece of candy" every time I picked up a resource.There comes a point where you keep playing because you think that the game has to be over soon...right.  But it's not.  It just keeps going, the same things over and over.  It's not possible to be held hostage by a video game, but this made me wonder "...or is it..."I'm convinced that the developer ask their ten year old nephew for their best idea of a tough guy and Deacon is who that child came up with.  I actually really like the actor who plays Deacon, he's a talented guy who I feel was wasted on such a one-dimensional character.  There were moments, though, when the face acting wowed me.Two nice things I will say about this game.  The environment is beautiful; it's what caught my attention in the first place.  The motorcycle has the best motorcycle mechanics I've experience in a game.  I usually dread having to use a motorcycle in a game, but this one was actually fun.  If the point of this game was to ride your motorcycle around and look at trees then A+++ they nailed it.  But after a few hours even the motorcycle riding gets tedious, especially when you're on your way to do that same thing you did 20 times before.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I wish it had been more polished when it was released as I believe from what I've read, a lot of issues were just with performance and glitches. I love how the story unravels as you progress, and the open world aspect is fun to go around and explore. And once you unlock the hoard and have the right skills in place, oh man! The very first hoard battle is nerve-wracking and so much fun. When you finally defeat one for the first time, it's such a sensation of accomplishment. Controls to me are pretty fluid and make sense. With so many side-missions along with the main story, there is so much content here to keep you busy for hours. I would assume to really clear it all out, you're probably looking at 60+ hours or more. Graphically, even being from 2019, this game looks great! The character models for the most part still look great today. And the voice acting to me is also very good. Again, it helps to become invested in the characters. There are so many good aspects to the story that have you worried and sad, and there are others that make you cheer for joy and happiness. Overall, a great game that I feel deserved better. _childDocuments_.review: Underrated gem, takes a few hours to get into a stride but once it gets there the quality of gameplay gets exponentially better. Once you can take on hordes, have an upgraded bike, and iron out your survival strategies the game becomes absolutely fantastic.Pros-Weapons, the Player, and his bike start out weak, but by the end of the game become strong. (Player progression is noticeable.)-Beautiful setting, wonderful voice acting, and great immersion.-Gameplay can go from cat and mouse, and back again depending on your preparedness.-The main two characters in the game have fantastic chemistry and I do buy their brotherhood.-Bike gameplay is both fun and unique, upgrading and maintaining it builds a certain attachment to it I appreciated.-Weapon variety is great, but having more unique differentiating factors play a part would have been nice.Neutral-Gas management can get a bit tedious, but it is understandable.-Certain resources are crazy abundant, while others are so rare that you may not want to part with certain consumables.-Crafting system/ commerce is somehow both overdeveloped and bare bones. Trust system makes sense, but kinda falls on it's face when it comes to the narrative.Cons-Certain characters just kinda suck.-Slow start, and could definitely trim the length.-Early game weapons are really boring/terrible to use.-Drip feed of content(weapons, equipment, bike parts, etc) is too slow.Despite my gripes. I do really love this game, Deacon is a fantastic protagonist. The story is a story of loyalty, brotherhood, and staying true to what you hold dear. Not perfect, but these things rarely are. It feels bloated in some areas, and too skinny in others.8.5/10EDIT: I cannot believe I forgot to mention that there's a Challenge mode, and New Game+ as well as a few more extreme difficulties if you're into that. The Challenge mode gives the player a set of various scenarios to run through, from time trials, a crazy taxi style challenge, to horde and human camp clearing, there's a wide range of replayable missions here.You can even gain rewards in the challenge mode like more efficient stamina, better healing, and faster gas fill ups by clearing them with at least a bronze medal.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, not as good as some other AAA games but still, I enjoyed it a lot. There are a few aspects of Days Gone, that really make the game shine mainly the motorcycle and the zombie hordes. The gun-play is also top notch as are the graphics, environmental design and some of the science fiction horror stuff is very nice. On the down side though, the story is a bit too cringe for me and the characters are too. Although Deacon Saint John (main character) did grow on me and I did start to like some of them after a while. The game-play is kind of repetitive but again, this is mediated by solid and fun game-play mechanics. This game emulates Read Dead Redemption 2 a lot but it’s not as good as that game. Which in fairness is setting the bar about as high as it can go. Days Gone is certainly up there, as a very good, open world, game but I feel like it could have been better. I got the sense that the developers would have taken the survival elements and world building even further but perhaps they were limited, by needing to appeal, to a mainstream player base. This game definitely deserves a sequel and it certainly suggests one at the end (secret ending). Especially with all of the garbage that gets made these days, there should, for sure be a Days Gone 2. It runs great here on Steam and it really is well made, with a lot of attention to detail. Days Gone is a game that manages to overcome it’s more mediocre aspects by truly shining overall. It has it’s own identity and the game really does shine at times, especially when you are up against a massive horde of zombies. I really enjoyed it and I for sure recommend that you play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Days Gone was a game I completely missed when it released in 2019 on PS4. It had mixed critical reception and I always thought "Maybe one day I'll try it." Well that day finally arrived and I have to say this game is great. Deacon St. John is a biker living as a drifter in a post apocalyptic world. It took a bit for me to get into the story but after a few hours I was hooked. The story is well written and the characters are well crafted. This is not a light hearted affair but I think the story is worth playing for anyone looking for a gritty tale. There are some bugs that never got ironed out like delayed dialog while walking and talking or jankie interactions with the world. Some of Deacon's dialog was a bit odd - like he would be yelling and the other person would be talking calmly. But for the most part it is fairly polished. The gameplay feels good. Gunplay feels responsive. Stealth is usually a viable option. The open world is enjoyable as you have to search for supplies, ammo and gas for your bike and clear out freaker nests. I think the only aspect I didn't like was that fast travel was not great since gas was such a limiting factor. The story had me hooked after an hour or so and it did not disappoint. I would definitely recommend this to anyone with an interest in this style of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently, Days Gone has to be in my top 10 games.Yep, there are annoying bugs/flaws (as many people have mentioned), but even so… this game is excellent. If you are looking for a dystopian zombie open world, this is it. For all its flaws, the main reasons to get this game are… the graphics, story and world design. The feeling of “end of the world, with dangerous zombies” is captured perfectly here. It is fascinating to explore all the various locations and wonder “what if this ACTUALLY happened?”.The flaws people mention are real: The policy of the developers to invade your privacy with their data capture? Shocking, and they should be called out for it, as others have done in their negative reviews. And the other major issue is, the Quality Assurance/Playtesting – yep, it’s bad. There are so many minor gameplay gripes/flaws/issues that you are left wondering if anyone actually did any playtesting. Watch the credits - literally dozens of people playtested this? Crazy. However, the annoying bugs are not enough to stop this from being an awesome experience.The story and acting are really well done. The main plot between the male and female leads does take a strange turn about two-thirds of the way into the game, but overall, you do get completely invested in the characters and storyline. The supporting cast is excellent, and you will want to see what happens next.A real standout part of the gameplay is the hordes of zombies. They really are truly terrifying. It’s rare to play a game these days and feel “on edge”, but trust me, as you approach a horde of 150 of these monsters, the adrenaline will be pumping.Respect must be paid to the music and sound effects. The creepy build of the music as a zombie gets near you, or you approach a nest of them… man, it still gives me chills.If you can get past the flaws, you can easily spend 60+ hours on this game. If the bugs had been sorted out, Days Gone would be a universal classic.UPDATE: I completed it for a second time, this time on “Hard II” mode. Pretty tricky, but great fun! :) I still stand by this being a great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Or Days Gone is an open world adventure in a  dystopian near future.  A virus (sound familiar) killed part of the population, mutated another part into mindless flesh eating zombies, and left others to fend for themselves in a world falling apart.  Guess which camp you're in.You play as Deacon St. John an Enforcer for a motorcycle gang known as the Mongrels.  The game opens the night the world fell apart with you putting your injured wife on a helicopter to get her out of harm's way to the medical attention she needs.  There isn't enough room on the evacuation helicopter for you and your fellow gang member "Boozer".The story resumes two years later.  You and Boozer survived this long.  When you attempted to go to the camp where your wife had been taken you find that it has been overrun by Freaks (Zombies).  You have survived and cannot get over losing your wife.The game is divided into two acts.  There is no "official" notification that you're changing acts, but you'll know as the weapons you were using are drastically inferior to the weapons you can now acquire.  Good thing as the enemies are radically superior to what you have been facing.There are multiple factions:Rippers - A cult that worships the Freaks and mutilates their bodies carving RIP into the foreheads and other cutting.Freaks - Individuals that have transformed into Zombies with a taste for flesh.  If that wasn't bad enough, they are evolving at an accelerated rate.NERO - The government research group that was helping evacuate people when the trouble started.  Two years later you see their choppers in the sky.Camps - Groups of people who have gathered together with a common goal, to survive.Marauders - Small rogue bands who look to take what others have.Your mode of transportation is a motorcycle, it gets you where you need to go.  You can upgrade your motorcycle at various camps.  Each camp has their own script (currency) so you will have to do missions for them to earn money to upgrade your bike.You can also purchase weapon upgrades at the camps. Weapons that you pick up from fallen foes are only temporary and not stored in your locker.  The weapons in your locker are purchased from camps.  Weapons range from a basic cross bow to a 50 caliber sniper rifle.Camps tend to specialize in the gear they carry. If they have weapons they probably don't have much for your bike and vice versa.Most of the quests are go wipe out X or go rescue Y.The game is not bug free.  There are the normal graphical glitches with enemies that fall dead through walls, doors, and fences.  The worst one I faced was a horde of zombies that I had to kill.  I killed 10% of them and then the other 90% just went away and were nowhere to be found.  The solution was to save the game and then load the saved game.  This happened multiple times at the Lumber Camp.  My strategy was to get their attention and then string them out as I picked them off with a pistol and it seems that this causes them to pull out of the camp and then just disappear.I recommend this game. The story is good and you can never kill too many zombies.  The bugs are not show stoppers, if you can find a way to work around them.  The save and then reload worked for me. _childDocuments_.review: I'm baffled at why this game is so positively reviewed, especially since people are complaining about the abundance of open world games these days.To start with, the weapons and ammunition system was designed by a complete moron. Guns don't share calibers, you could have a .22 and you can't use the same ammunition from a different model of .22. You also can't pick up any ammunition for anything that you don't have currently equipped. So you can't save shotgun shells up if you have a rifle, or rifle ammo for other rifles. You also cannot store any weapon that you find in your gun locker, only ones you buy (and you're locked out of the weapon shop until you complete a bunch of missions).Who on earth came up with such a nonsensical system, and in a game that's supposed to have survival horror elements? What idiot would ever leave around perfectly good weapons and ammunition in this world when they already have a place to stockpile it, and what possible reason would there be for me to be unable to store different weapons that I've found? Why can I not accumulate my own arsenal of weapons that I ALREADY HAVE?!And speaking of weapons, the ones you have access to while waiting for the stupid weapons shop to open are utter crap. Either they hold very little ammo, and have a tiny max ammo carrying capacity, or they do such low damage that even my pistol is more powerful than an AK-47.Oh and your motorcycle can hold about 1 cup of fuel, even with an upgraded gas tank. You're constantly refilling it from random jugs you find that have infinite fuel but you can't strap a spare can onto your bike for no reason. You drive around and kill zombies and have wolf packs that rip you off your bike all the time, that are somehow a common thing despite the world being filled with bloodthirsty zombies that will eat just about anything living.Then there's traversing the environments. I find myself unable to reach areas because the game decided I can't scale one little rock, because they're forcing you to access that area their way. What are essentially invisible walls that prevent progress are never fun to deal with.People keep saying that you have to play 6 hours in for this game to be good, what kind of crap game wastes your time like that before actually becoming fun? This is a generic zombie game with a generic open world, and extremely poorly designed "survival" elements.

The dynamic weather and day-night cycle add a layer of realism that immerses you completely. The motorcycle, my trusty steed, became an extension of my survival. With its heart-pounding action, emotional depth, and a captivating storyline, Days Gone is a ride you won't want to miss. A true gem for fans of survival and open-world exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: The rating system in Steam should be changed to 5 stars or something, because it distorts reality. May recommend or not recommend. For me this game is 2/5. Days Gone is another game where players evaluate what is happening around the game, not the game itself. But because of this broken rating system, I am forced to not recommend this game. This game wasn't created by indie studio but for corporate money, so I expect a little more. Story is boring and known already for everyone who saw at least half of one zombie movie. There is a lot of typical exposition, irrational characters who acts strange. For example, one lady is very angry at Deek (main character), because he is selfish pri*k. 1 second later (in poorly cuted cutscene) she is like ''help us Deek'' and he is like ''ok, but be gentle to that little girl''. The quickest catharsis I ever saw for a long time. Complete 180 degree change, and this happens many times in cutscene. And of course a sea of boring NPC's. It's like, everyone in this world are complete mor*ns or had serious psychologic problems. I think, the writers were bad :). But what about gameplay, huh? Let's be serious, nobody cares about quality stories in zombie games. It's average at most. Days Gone is Far Cry 6 with zombies (but game in general is smaller than FC). You are riding from point to point and do same tasks over and over, till you marked them as ''done''. Standard enemies sets. Boring not tactical at any point fight (hide shoot hide - with bandits / run shoot run - with zombie (even hordes)). The main character seems artificially castrated so that there is something to develop in this game. I can't believe, after several years spent surviving and fighting hordes of corpses, he can't aim a gun. To measure how long it will take for the aiming, I have to use a calendar, not a watch. Well, it would be too easy, right? (WOW WOW IMMERSION IMMERSION WOW WOW). BSMain Missions are mostly walking with someone, and listening boring dialogues (''I was in Army hu hu! And I know how take care of myself HU HU Bad boy! - surely he forgot to aim since the Army). Some of them you can skip, but mostly not. Even developer knew that form writing side of things, this game sucks. There is a radio Free Oregon or something like that, which you can turn of everytime NPC start's talking about - What happened today in this god-forgotten lands. My bad, there is a lot of other great main mission than walking-talking (remember there is no conversation system in this game). Like sneak mission, where you MUST walk specific road. Example: you have to sneak into camp and steal some crap. The target is at end of the camp. You look on map thinks ''Hey, I can walk around base and sneak from other side, this will be quicker and safer''. Well you can't, you have to go through entire camp and move from bush to bush with occasional stone-decoy throw. Why? Beeeecause. Why do you have to eavesdrop on mad scientists so often in this game?MOTORCYLE - what the he*l is even that? This ''vehicle'' is just too slow. You will be begging for extra fast travel points. And that fights on motorcycles? This are the best vehicle combat you ever saw. There is crafting, but it is focused solely on the gadgets you use. Something like in The Last of us. That's it.What with main dinner? The meat (or soy meat, whatever). The hordes are fun. That's all. Watch gameplays, and you will know why.The ratings for this game do not result from the game itself, but from what happened around it. Read the reviews. ''F*ck console players because they prefer weak Horizon instead of this masterpiece'', ''Gameplay is not repeatable'' and so on. Imagine playing Far cry 6 with less content, and someone says ''This game is not repetitive, story and characters are gold''. And someone scream at you because you not agree, and you are propably a console sleeper agent with mission to destroy PC kingdom. The ratings of PS4 players, those bad console players, were closer to the truth than those here on Steam. I am a simple guy trying to play a good games and rate them occasionally, like a good citizen. That's it.If you like this game, splendid! Have fun and ki*l as many hordes as you can. Drink soda/water eat some snack and have fun! You deserve it and I am completely honest.
