_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game is a pretty wild ride game-play wise. They throw a lot of mechanics at you, and they do most of them very well, though a few come off a bit half-baked. I'd say the things they get well are the mixture of realism/suspended disbelief. I'm cool with the resource drain on gas and what not, and it was a fair way to utilize a fast travel system. You essentially either pick faster travel for the sake of upgrading more slowly. That is of course until the inevitable point where you're making too much money to matter. I do also like that each camp has it's own credit system so you have to earn for each camp individually with bounties and stuff, while also completing the multiple side quests available. I would say near end game though the multitude of side quests did get a bit overbearing. The story is fairly well done. Good amount of tropes and stuff, but the setting and location gives it a fresh coat of paint. Pretty much the only way to describe it without spoiling anything. The gunplay is pretty good. The melee combat is probably the weakest point when it comes to fighting in my opinion, and that even with 90% of all the melee perks unlocked in the game. Where this game shines though I'd say a lot of the other aspect of the game, like mission bounties, and  take a ton of influence from the Far Cry series, as well as The Last Of Us. Not necessarily bad things, but the map fatigue, while not at Ubisoft Assassin's Creed level bad, it's up there. I would say though that the ambient dialogue of the main character does liven up these duller moments that get repetitive. Some of it is lore building, some of it is comedy, other parts are pure unadulterated rage with a bit of self righteousness thrown in. Not much in the way of horror, or even a sense of dread other than maybe one or two areas. I'd say a good way to look at this game when you get started is if you've played Dying Light. It's that same feeling of being afraid of being out at night, to actively hunting why the night time scared you. For me, it's very gratifying. If you can get past the corny tropes and somewhat edgyness of the main character, I think it's something worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: The main protagonist is Deacon St. John a.k.a Deek, who is a member of the motorcycle club, along with his brother from another mother, William "Boozer" Gray. When the apocalypse started, many people turned into zombies called freaks. Deek, his wife Sarah, and Boozer wanted to go somewhere safe. They caught a National Emergency Response Organization – NERO helicopter, but there was only room for two. So, Deek decided to put his wife on board and stayed with Boozer. After two years, the main story starts. You will travel with Boozer around Oregon, try to survive and find out if Sarah is still alive.The map consists of six regions that you unlock by completing story missions. They are not big and could be more diverse, but they are fine. Every part of the map contains one camp where you can spend credits for your loadout, collectables that will teach you about some character's background story, or you can read about the history and landmarks of Oregon. Also, there are infestation zones with Freaks nests and caves where hordes hide. You can find NERO research places and checkpoints that will give you injectors. They will improve your health, stamina, and focus. Each region has ambush camps of enemy clans. When you clear them, you can use these places as a fast travel point or change your loadout in a small underground bunker. By doing all this stuff, you will gain XPs that you can use in the skill tree to improve your combat, survival or weapons skills.No worries, it is not a walking simulator. Your main and only transportation to anywhere is a motorcycle. It requires fuel and repairs if you are a bad rider. Especially in the beginning, without any upgrades, you must drive carefully. You do not want to end up with a broken motorbike in the middle of freaks. You will unlock upgrades for your ride in camps by completing main and side missions. I recommend you buy a better fuel tank first. You will be able to travel further without refuelling often. If your plan screws up and you run out of gas, you can still move your bike with legs. It is slow, and freaks will catch you. So try to find a fuel can or pump as fast as possible. Downhills can help you gain some speed. When you crash or bandits set up an ambush on you, your bike can be totalled. You can repair damage with scraps found under car hoods or lying on the ground. Keep your stash full of it. You never know when you will need it. Crafting explosives, distractions, and repairing melee weapons requires scraps as well.They are places where you can refill ammo, buy upgrades and weapons, and repair or refuel your motorcycle for credits gained by story and side missions. Leaders of camps will give you jobs, and most of them are the same: go somewhere and eliminate someone. After completing a few, you will be bored, but you know the drill: "Nose down, work hard, they feed ya." You will get credits, and raise your trust level with camps, which will unlock more items in shops. If you need more bucks and want higher respect in camps, sell bounties from freaks or meat from animals.The most annoying thing in the game is the respawning of freaks. Let me explain it. After clearing a small zone, you start looting items. Suddenly, you hear screaming freaks, look around, and they are everywhere. How!? They respawned here! It doesn’t happen every time, but Murphy’s law works well here. Freaks, wolves or bears will respawn in situations when you really don't want to fight more attackers. Yeah, you read it right, respawn works on animals too.Another thing that bothers me during gameplay, especially in fights, is flying ragdolls. Sometimes a dead body takes off to the Moon and then returns to Oregon. When you see this bug for the first time, it can be funny, but after 20 or more times it is not. Devs should have fixed it.Visuals impressed me with high-quality textures and scenic views from the hills. The game still looks good nowadays and offers many situations where you will open photo mode, which is well-made. It has many settings that will help you make a perfect screenshot. When it starts raining or snowing, you will open it for sure. Also, facial animations in the cutscenes are detailed and look believable. Only broken ragdolls and flashlight light coming from nowhere spoil the immersion of the atmosphere. Deek looks like a magician when the light comes from the middle of his body without any emitting point.As I mentioned earlier, the map contains collectables and other things to do. You can try clearing all hordes and ambush camps or challenge yourself in New Game Plus and Challenge Mode. Clearing hordes is great fun. You need to prepare a lot of ammunition, traps and everything that will help you stop those massive counts of freaks.New Game Plus offers one new weapon that is useless, in my opinion. You can craft special ammo for it, like for a crossbow, but a .50 calibre sniper rifle in the main game is better. It can kill anyone with one shot. Challenge mode offers 12 short missions, like clear a horde, race on a motorbike, surviving a freaks attack, and so on. You must do everything perfectly if you want a gold score.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Days Gone: A Riveting Journey Through the ApocalypseRating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)Days Gone, developed by Bend Studio, is an absolute triumph in the post-apocalyptic gaming genre. From the moment you step into the worn shoes of Deacon St. John, you are thrust into a visceral and emotionally charged world that demands your attention.The game's strength lies in its meticulous attention to detail, creating a believable and expansive open-world environment. The Pacific Northwest setting is not just a backdrop; it's a character in itself. The dynamic weather, day-night cycle, and realistic ecosystem contribute to an immersive experience that is nothing short of breathtaking.The narrative is a rollercoaster of emotions, expertly weaving personal struggles with the chaos of a world overrun by Freakers — the game's version of zombies. Deacon's journey is poignant and filled with unexpected twists, and the character development is top-notch. Sam Witwer's stellar performance as Deacon adds a layer of authenticity to the character that enhances the overall narrative.The gameplay is where Days Gone truly shines. The motorcycle, your trusty steed in this apocalyptic landscape, is not just a means of transportation but a lifeline. The sense of vulnerability while exploring the vast wilderness is palpable, and the constant threat of Freaker hordes keeps you on the edge of your seat.Combat is a delicate dance of strategy and survival. Whether you're facing off against human enemies or hordes of Freakers, the variety of weapons and the strategic use of the environment add a layer of complexity that keeps the gameplay engaging throughout.The game's attention to detail extends to its robust crafting system. Every item you scavenge feels crucial, and the decisions you make about resource allocation can mean the difference between life and death.Days Gone is not without its flaws. Some technical hiccups were present at launch, but the developers have shown commendable dedication to polishing the game through updates. The vastness of the open world, while impressive, may feel a bit overwhelming for some players.In conclusion, Days Gone is a masterpiece that deserves a place among the pantheon of great open-world games. Its compelling narrative, breathtaking visuals, and intense gameplay combine to create an experience that will stay with you long after you put down the controller. If you're a fan of the post-apocalyptic genre or simply enjoy a gripping narrative with heart-stopping action, Days Gone is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Days Gone

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐*Days Gone Review: The Game That Made Me a Professional Freaker Dodger**So, *Days Gone*. Let me just start by saying this game taught me two very important life lessons: 1) Always keep your gas tank full, and 2) Never, ever, EVER stop to admire the scenery in a post-apocalyptic world. You’ll think, “Wow, this sunset is gorgeous,” and then BAM—50 Freakers later, you’re running for your life like you just insulted someone’s mother at a family BBQ.You play as Deacon St. John, a gruff, leather-clad biker who’s basically Mad Max with a better beard. You ride through the apocalypse on your trusty motorcycle, which, by the way, has the fuel efficiency of a lawnmower from the 1980s. It’s always fun to realize you’re out of gas in the middle of nowhere, surrounded by hordes of zombies, and your only plan is to run faster than Deacon’s emotional baggage.Speaking of the bike, it’s not just a vehicle—it’s a *relationship*. You’ll take care of that thing like it’s your child. You’ll upgrade it, fix it, and then scream at it when it hits a rock and flips over, sending you flying into a pack of Freakers. But when you and that bike are cruising down the highway at sunset (with a full tank, of course), it’s pure magic. Well, until a wolf decides it wants a piece of you. Did I mention the wildlife in this game has a serious attitude problem? It’s like the apocalypse gave them all a caffeine boost.Now, the Freakers. These aren't your average, slow, dumb zombies. No, these guys are the Usain Bolts of the undead world. I’d be creeping around a dark, abandoned town thinking, “Hey, this isn’t so bad,” and then a horde would come out of nowhere like a surprise birthday party from hell. Running away became my main strategy. Forget stealth and combat—it's all about “How fast can I get back to my bike before I become zombie chow?”The story is a mix of heartwarming, tragic, and "Wait, I’m supposed to care about these people while running for my life?" Deacon’s journey is emotional, though he’s so gruff, I’m surprised he didn’t growl at his bike. But the emotional moments hit hard, especially when you’re not dodging the undead or looking for gas cans like your life depends on it. (Spoiler: It does.)Visually, this game is stunning. The Pacific Northwest has never looked so beautiful while simultaneously trying to kill you at every turn. It’s a weird feeling, admiring the serene landscape while knowing that at any moment, a bear might leap out and ruin your day. Yes, the bears are bigger than your bike, and no, you do not stand a chance.And the sound design? Let me tell you, the noise of a Freaker horde is something you’ll never forget. The first time I heard that screeching, I thought my headphones were broken—nope, just 200 zombies saying hello in their own horrifying way. It’s like an orchestra of nightmares, and you’re the conductor who desperately wants to leave.All in all, *Days Gone* is a wild, gas-guzzling, freaker-dodging ride that will make you appreciate every second of peace you get… because it probably won’t last long. 10/10 would run out of gas, panic, and flee from wolves again.
_childDocuments_.name: Days Gone

_childDocuments_.review: As the Earl of Trash, I have faced many challenges in life. However, nothing could prepare me for the tragedy that struck my family. My mother and father, avid skydivers, perished in a freak accident, leaving me to fend for myself. In the days that followed, I found solace in the world of video games, particularly Days GoneDays Gone is a game that tells the story of a man who lost everything, just like I did. The main character, Deacon St. John, is a former outlaw who lost his wife in the early days of a pandemic that swept the world, turning most people into zombie-like creatures known as Freakers. As I played through the game, I couldn't help but feel a connection to Deacon, who, like me, was trying to survive in a world that no longer made sense.The game is set in the Pacific Northwest, a rugged and beautiful landscape that has been devastated by the pandemic. Deacon travels the land on his motorcycle, searching for supplies and survivors, and battling hordes of Freakers along the way. The gameplay is challenging and rewarding, with a variety of weapons and upgrades to choose from.But what I appreciated most about Days Gone was its emotional depth. The game doesn't shy away from the pain and grief that comes with losing someone you love. Deacon is haunted by the memory of his wife, and throughout the game, he has to make tough decisions that test his loyalty and his sense of right and wrong.As I played through the game, I found myself identifying with Deacon in ways I never expected. The loss of my parents left a hole in my heart that will never be filled, but playing as Deacon gave me a sense of purpose and a way to channel my grief. The game reminded me that even in the darkest of times, there is always a glimmer of hope, and that sometimes the greatest strength comes from the love we carry for those we've lost.In conclusion, Days Gone is a powerful and poignant game that speaks to the heart of what it means to be human. The tragic loss of my parents will always be a part of me, but playing this game gave me a sense of closure and a way to honor their memory. If you're looking for a game that will challenge you both emotionally and physically, then Days Gone is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Days Gone - Biker Survival Meets Zombie Hordes and... Freaker Freak-Outs!Alright, folks, hold onto your handlebars because we're diving headfirst into the post-apocalyptic mayhem of Days Gone, where the undead don't politely stay dead! It's like Sons of Anarchy meets World War Z, and it's a wild ride!So, you're Deacon St. John, a gruff biker dude with the coolest name ever. He's not exactly the guy you'd pick to save the world, but hey, life's full of surprises. And when it's swarming with zombie-like "Freakers," you take what you can get.The Good Stuff:Biker's Paradise: Riding your hog through the beautiful, decaying Pacific Northwest is a blast. It's like a cross-country road trip but with more zombies and less scenic overlooks.Zombie Horde Spectacle: Those Freaker hordes are like a mobile mosh pit from hell. Seriously, it's like Coachella, but with fewer flower crowns and more gnashing teeth.Crafting & Survival: You'll be scavenging everything from nails to sterilized bandages to create some wicked zombie-slaying weaponry. It's like MacGyver with more motor oil.The Not-So-Good Stuff:Open World Fatigue: Sometimes you'll feel like a post-apocalyptic FedEx delivery guy, running around from one errand to another. "Hey Deacon, can you pick up my lost cat while you're at it?"Deacon's Mood Swings: Deacon can be a real drama queen sometimes. He's all serious one minute, cracking jokes the next. Make up your mind, man!Freaker Traffic Jams: When you stumble upon a horde, it's a beautiful mess. But sometimes they get stuck on an abandoned car, and you're like, "Come on, guys, move it! We've got a schedule here!"In the end, Days Gone is a fun and unpredictable zombie-slaying extravaganza, perfect for anyone who's ever wondered how they'd survive a zombie apocalypse on two wheels. Just be prepared for the occasional traffic jam of undead enthusiasts and Deacon's roller-coaster emotions. Stay alive, my friends, and keep those Freakers freaked out!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a AA game that tried real hard to be AAA. I recommend this game, but only when it's on sale at 75% or more.Graphics: 8/10Sound & Music: 8/10Combat: 8/10Story: 6.5/10 (Still way better than Cyberpunk2077)In epic single player games the story writing is really important. Unfortunately the plot and themes are pretty hackneyed and underwhelming. It feels as if the writers just regurgitated the same movie tropes they grew up watching and compiled a B-film in the form of a video game. There's nothing here that will make you go "whoa I can't wait to see what happens next" because you can see these cliches coming a mile away. Days Gone can't hold a candle to the proper AAA titles, but then again, the industry just doesn't make AAA games anymore.Days Gone didn't have the best writers, they did have some good engineers and (non-writing) artists. The world looks and sounds great, the controls are smooth, and glitches/bugs happen very rarely. Quite impressive really for an open world game. But that's where the praise ends. Combat is done well enough to distract you from the mediocre story, though it too does get a bit stale after a while. AI is nonexistent. As you can imagine in a zombie game, combat mostly consists of kiting a mob of enemies that beeline towards you. There are a few balance issues because you can get one of the best weapons in the game almost immediately, and a lot of expensive items are just not worth the price. The biggest issue I had on the technical side is the short draw distance and projectile distance (which is quite typical in games like this). There are huge open areas in this game and it really ruins the immersion when your high powered rifle can't launch a bullet out to 150m. Sure that might have been a resource constraint 10 years ago but it's really inexcusable now.

( I would be okay with how they look if the style of everything else followed but nope, just looks out of place and weird)- Character rolls but with no invincibility frames so you get hit anyway.- Only two types of infected (Runners and zombie kids that hide from you)- Seen much more impressive horde AI in other, much older, games.- Seen much more impressive gore in other games. - Stamina replenishes way too slowly.- Not worth $50 POSITIVES- Motorcycle driving feels fun and heavy. (most of the time)- Runs exceptionally well.- Hordes can be fun.- Funny photo mode.OVERALL EXPERIENCE - While fun for the first hour or two you slowly find out that the "open world" is nothing more then empty wilderness and empty buildings that only come stock full of crafting material and ammo. No fun houses with their own stories going on in them, no cool secrets, nadda. Just driving around looking for ammo, crafting material, and fuel. I'd be okay with this if at the least the combat and horde game play is fun, but alas it isn't. The biggest hordes I found were about 5 to 8 in size and were only triggered during the burning of their nests. Guns feel and look lazy. They hardly do any VISIBLE damage to zombies, so the result is very unsatisfying. Deacon controls very assy and half of the time doesn't do what I want him to do, especially when I'm being chased and want to run. He kind of just forgets that i'm holding down the shift key and I have to tap it again. He also doesn't shut the hell up. Either saying the same line about how the zombie Nest smells or some other bull crap, it just gets old and annoying after a while. This does not feel like a PS4 exclusive and feels more like a steam early access game. I want my time and money back.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is written after spending one evening (!) with the game. The reivew will be updated after the game has been finished.When I saw the announcenement of Days Gone, I thought to myself: "Shame on you, Sony, you wanna combine  TLOU 1 and Walking Dead's Deryl - a one immenstly popular game and one immensly popular finctional character. They do it for the money, obviously". Surely, I didn't expect much from the universe they created for this game, or the story, or the characters.Now, that I am able to play this PS4 "exlcusive", for which I am grateful, I can say with certainty, that I never knew I needed a game like Days Gone, until I played it.That said, this game isn't worth playing on any difficulty level lower than Survival 2. It just makes the game and your time with it so much better. And this difficulty level could be the only reason I am recommending the game.If not played on the hardest difficulty, you'll only like your first-time experiences - your first 10 zombie kills, your first 10 human kills, your first 3 motorcycle chases, your first 20 searched car trunks and so on.But to beat this game you'd need to do all of this thousands of times over and it wouldn't be fun. It'd be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chore. And once you've reached the end, you're gonna say "Thank God, I made it all the way", then you delete this game and forget about it.All of this won't happen, if you add just one little element into your playthrough - the danger. It'll make you think, it'll make your trips between any two camps into a thrilling adventure.So, thumbs up, recommend, Days Gone on Survival 2!UPD: Just finished the main story on Survival, nearly 70 hours in. I gotta say - I needed to finish the game, so at some point I started to kind of rush my experience. Not game's fault. But now I feel sad that the story has ended. This is what I always feel after finishing a good game. The kind of games that stay in my memory for long time.Anyhow, when I decided to quickly finish the remaining story misssions, turns out I was at approximately 65% mark. That, ladies and gentlemen - is a lot of content. I ended up doing all the side quests, clearing some of the hardest hordes and having lots of fun just living in the game, surviving. It felt awesome. I really can't say anything bad. It's easy to see that the devs, put their hearts into this one. It would've been a waste if the game wasn't this long (looking at you Mad Max). Days Gone offered me to keep playing after the main story, there's even another kind story/side mission available. But Im gonna have to come back to it later. I want to leave some stuff not unlocked, unfinished, so the next time I play it, there's still going to be things to explore.Overall, Days Gone is an awesome game. The kind of game that reminds you why you bought your console in the first place (even though I played it on my PC). But yeah, great, long game that I will revisit many, many times over the following years!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, would definitely recommend! I'm usually not a fan of the survival/collect&craft type of games, but here it's not as tedious or boring and it's fun. It's more action/story-driven, than survival/collect. Also the combat is quite dynamic and fluent. You can go stealthy, but you can also go rambo-style, especially after you grow up in power a bit.The story is kind of... Not great, not terrible, but honestly nothing to write home about. I also don't like the amount of unskippable scenes where you just have to walk around with Sarah and talk about irrelevant stuff... Felt kind of a drag, to be honest. Wish there would be much more focus on the mutants (story-wise) than on the absolute horrendous soap-opera relationship between Deacon and Sarah. The visuals are great - I've spent quite some time just sitting on a hill, looking at the starry sky, or watching a lake during the day and listening to the sounds of nature! It's quite realistic and immersible.All in all - solid game, lots of content, worth the money, especially if you find it on sale. Killing your first horde after a few attempts is such a satisfactory feeling!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely no complaints, fantastic game. Graphics are gorgeous, game runs flawlessly even on mid ranged hardware. The only real "issue" i've noticed is cut scenes can sometimes have a tendency to have some microstutter but it's rare and never a prolonged issue. Bike handling physics are weighty and satisfying, as is the melee combat. The guns imo could use a *touch* more punch but they're fine as they are. So far i've encountered 2 large dynamic hordes while exploring the map, and neither of them caused any noticeable frame drop, which was a welcome surprise. Overall i'd entirely recommend it, i've encountered no bugs so far and the game is very well optimized and polished for a day 1 (I played when it unlocked at midnight on May 18th) console port release.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, not a great game, not an awesome game, just a good game and it's worth playing and exploring.I write this review after completing the story in 65 hours (took my time) but i still have some hordes and probably a last mission. Why i'm writing this before completely finishing everything? Just a little patience and you'll find out.In my books this game is a 7/10, maybe 7.5. So you get an idea of my ranking God of War, Witcher 3 are a 10, Horizon zero dawn is a 8.5. I really loved this game. The idea is awesome, the story is captivating even though sometimes slow still loved it. I took my time and explored everything and enjoyed it very much. So why 7/10? Don't get me wrong this game could have been easily a masterpiece but i think someone at sony or whoever was in charge just pulled the plug at some points. They decided enough is enough. This reminds me of Cyberpunk at launch ... great but full of bugs and clearly unfinished. Sadly Days Gone is the same. What bugs you may ask ... Well deers flying, bike flying, bike stuck, crows stuck in the air, everyone flying, zombies running suddenly jump in the sky, getting stuck in nothing (literally i was walking and got stuck), getting stuck in a tree, falling off the map, crashes over crashes and so many more.Then there are the little things that are not bugs but clearly give a vibe of bad planning like you could put a truck between two rock but you can't pass between them, you can press "E" to talk with someone and you spin around over and over and over and over again like 20 times before finally talking. Pressing E to get on bike fast but game doesn't let me. Climbing is allowed only on certain things even though in the situation you can climb on and in 65 hours there were so many moments i was like "wtf dude seriously" ... Clearly the game is very rough around the edges. Many tweaks should have been integrated but sadly that wasn’t what happened.Then there's the difficulty which is too easy. I played directly at HARD2 and it's just a normal in comparasion with other games. I think it needed a tweak or new diff like nightmare or something.Then there's the side quests or camp mission which are the same mission over and over again. This makes the difference between a masterpiece and just a good game. There are some quests when Deacon saves someone and they have a little chat and tease like they know eachother but you never met that person and you will never meet him/her again. I mean what a waste when you could implement the camp quests to be like bonding with the people in the camp but no. I think one of the only ones that mattered was when Manny from copeland was kidnapped but it was not enough. What a wasted opportunity. Just go and kill some people with no context and nothing to add to the story.Then there's the walking during a quest when you have to walk at snail pace. We all hate that but happily that doesn't happen too often.Then there's the fact that you can lose content without warning. The devs decided that doing a useless camp quest is more important than some side quests (marked with white) that actually give you an useful insight into Deacon. WTAF! What i mean by that is camp quests stay on the map and you can do them but white ones that usually are really important to the character dissapear. Pay attention at the quests! if you see a white one go do it because if you do something else that white quest can dissapear.If you take your time exploring and you played a couple of games you’ll get a feeling that the game is not finished and i don’t believe for a second that a team that wrote the main story so well, that implemented a zombie survival game so well would, by choice, leave the game as it is. Many substories are left untold and those that are told feel like there was many more to be said. I don’t know how to explain it but this is the feeling that i got.Even with all of this i loved the game!!Oh, i almost forgot, why i’m writing this before finishing everything? BECAUSE IT CRASHED WHEN I WAS FIGHTING A HORDE ... AGAIN!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Zombie survival games are very hard to obtain on PC. If you want a game with good mechanics and game play, the game play is either very *unique* to say the least, or its mechanics are so complicated it seems like a hassle to even play for 10 minutes. And even if the game meets the perfect requirements, it either has dated graphics (due to low budget or creative liberties) or is sometimes very restrictive. You've probably already seen the negative reviews but big surprise, I don't want my data spied on or invaded by anyone but my girlfriend, who I am still looking forward to meeting. Dying Light is a good game but not very grounded, no pun intended. This game is probably one of the best grounded zombie survival games in terms of graphics, mechanics, and game play, but the data BS is a deal breaker.The cut scenes and story are barely, perhaps not even the reason why I bought this game, this is one of the goofiest pieces of media I've ever seen, and that's ignoring the unique approach at "zombies" in this game. I had to go through a tunnel not even 15 minutes into the game and I couldn't walk 3 meters without some useless short cut scene playing. Many games like The Last of Us trick the player into thinking they're experiencing "immersion" by having this same mechanic of quick cut scene to game play - sometimes even a mix of both where you need to mash a single button - but doing so is seemless. Switching from cut scene to game play felt like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ powerpoint presentation most of the time. I know the story is about my wife or some ♥♥♥♥ I honestly couldn't care less because of how corny it was. This game deserves a high rating, but for the game, not what it does in the background.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wish list for a long time and after having a break in between games, I decided to give this a shot and I'm glad I did!  1.  Is the game worth the money?  answer: Absolutely.  I just finished 5 play-throughs and all challenges and have over 900 hours.  Some of those hours are probably afk, but it's clearly worth your money.2.  Replayability: as mentioned above, yes.  You can easily play the game 4 times based on difficulty.3.  Bugs and glitches?  Very few.  I'm trying to think of any gamebreaking bugs I encountered and cannot think of any.  Sometimes there might be a stutter here and there, and a couple times I lost the bike sound but had all other sounds.  So to answer, very few to none.4.  Storyline?  Good to very good.  Note: replaying the game will still have you walking (literally) through cut-scenes and you may not want to go through them again.  You can hold down the spacebar or sometimes "H" (I think) to ignore the cut-scene.  There are a small number of cut-scenes that you cannot get out of, you have to go through it.5.  Combat: This depends greatly on your difficulty setting.  Later in the storyline, some Freakers can only die via headshots and some creatures are frustrating on the harder difficulties.  You have a wide range of weapons including melee, sidearm, primary and special.  (includes a crossbow special weapon as well)6.  Gameplay:  Most of your time will be spent on missions, either for a specific camp or to clear the way for travel.  You will be killing Freakers, infected creatures, wolves, Humans (Marauders, Rippers, Ambush Camps and more).  Improving your stats will be done via injectors found at NERO locations.  Completing missions and gaining camp credits will allow you to purchase fuel, ammo and upgrade/change your weapon(s) and yes, you need to upgrade your bike.  There is a Gun Locker feature that allows you to store guns that you have purchased or earned via unlock and can be accessed via camps at the Merchant or at most NERO locations once you have completed the Mission for that NERO location.  You cannot store weapons in your Gun Locker that you have picked up in the world.PRO's: Everything I mentioned above.  The graphics are good to very good.  Environment effects are good, I love the snow effects.  Storyline flows well.CON's: For some reason Deacon (Deek) seems to yell most of the time.  I think it's because the Dev's figured he'd be on his bike most of the time, so they have him yelling when he really has no reason to.  Some people don't like the save game rules.  If you are on your bike (or next to it) you can quicksave, so do that often.  Normal saves don't seem to happen as much as you would like.So there you have it!  The game was a very pleasant surprise!  Hope you like it as well!

_childDocuments_.review: First, I am not one to leave a review. In fact as far as games go, this will be my first.  I preordered the collectors edition on Playstation when I first was able. I picked it up on release date and started playing immediately.  Mind you, I am a PC player and truly do not enjoy playing on playstation anymore. My son enjoys saying that I am a gluton for punish because I start all my games on whatever the hardest difficulty the game has to offer. This was no exception to that rule.I have beaten the game a total of 3 times now while completing it in its entirety. A lot of the lower reviews seem to find the start to be a slow one. For me, I did not think so (clearly). Now I will say one of the biggest draws for this game for me was the fact that you had a motorcycle and that was basically like your horse in a western styled game. I am someone who has been riding motorcycles for many years and there really aren't many games with them. Truly, I would have played this game for that fact alone. Also, I am a fan of Sam Witwer. So, I probably would have played the game for that as well. I enjoyed him in Forced Unleashed series as well of the many TV Series he has been in. The way he "yelled" at differently things that happened seemed fitting to his character. It truly felt as though I was there. The immersion was simply one of the best that I have been apart of bar none. The scenery  was simply gorgeous. So much in fact I have plans to go up through Oregon just to see it with my own eyes. The interactions with the other character seemed very genuine. There was never a point where I thought to myself "why would he do that" or "why did he do that that way". For me each instance really did fall into place.I won't leave this with nothing negative because simply put nothing will ever be perfect no matter how close it may become. My biggest gripe would have to be I thought there should be more custimizable things for the bike. Sure you were able to change things but there were different types of motorcycles in the game. You should have been able to at the very least emulate any motorcycle the game had. Also, the challenges were not fun nor interesting for me at all. I will leave it at that. Overall in my eyes the game is a solid 9.5 easily for me and is in my top 5. I would recommend to both enemy and friend alike.

_childDocuments_.review: * Edited:I've actually changed the recommendation from no to yes since overall I enjoyed the game, but that's due to a decent story (not as good as TLoU 1/2 and not as good as Telltales' The Walking Dead, but still enjoyable). Everything else ranges from outright bad (like non-skippable horde missions) to mediocre at best.Reading other people reviews I have a feeling that we were playing different games. The story here is good, the graphics are ok too, and that's about all I can say. The gameplay is mediocre at best. The enemy AI is downright bad. The sneaking mechanics are bad. The shooting mechanics are even worse. The melee mechanics are all about spamming one button. Enemy attack patterns are clearly scripted and absolutely predictable and also it's very annoying how enemies spawn out of a thin air and how they're able to easily find you during scripted events like when you destroy a nest. Bike upgrade system is not fun either.Many other gameplay elements are there for the sake of adding timesinks. Like fueling your bike, fixing your bike or collecting plants and animal meat - it's just a chore. Finally, the rpg element is really weak - there are only a few mechanics which are getting unlocked with the skill points throughout the game and they are simply not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Days Gone is a very good game.  Unlike the vast majority of open world map games (Farcry, RDR, AC) this one locked my interest in until the very end.  The Pacific Northwest is extremely well modeled in game and riding around on your bike feels magnificent.    The game has excellent challenge to player power gain ratio and is constantly challenging you to unlock one more weapon or motorcycle upgrade.  Deacon is a good character to get behind and you may find yourself very invested in his quest to find his wife.  The story is good.  The writing is good.  The characters are good.  I'm not certain why more gamers haven't given this title a shot.  In it's current state it was easily the best game I played in 2021.  At one point late in the game I was trying to take down a group of militia wackos who were hunkered down around a house.  I managed to get them to shoot at me at range and that drew the attention of passing zombies that proceeded to attack the house.  That noise drew the attention of a huge infected bear that also wandered in and started eating zombies and militia defenders.  All the while I just kept my head down and hid in a bush as the mayhem proceeded.  After a few minutes all the militia guys were dead without me firing a shot.  Any game that allows you to do that is worth playing.  I have a lot of appreciation for what Bend has accomplished here.  It's a real shame Sony has turned them down for a sequel.  Do yourself a favor and check this one out.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Wow wow wow. Took me 39 hours for my first playthrough, where I took the time to clear hordes I happened upon while on my travels from place to place and tried to unlock every single gun. This is definitely one of my favorite games of all time, and almost certainly on my top 5 favorite singleplayer games of all time. It's one of the best single player experiences out there, but not without its flaws... And here's some.!!! [[SPOILER WARNING]] !!!- DATA COLLECTION POLICY. If you have read some of the other reviews, this game's data collection policy is incredibly intrusive. It's to the point where it's practically a keylogger. It's that bad. Turn off your wifi, and block this game on your firewall or something so your data doesn't end up getting sold on the dark web or some ♥♥♥♥. This is my biggest gripe with this game.- Slow pacing. You'll only deal with the same type of zombie for the first half of the game or so, then the game just suddenly picks up pace and rapidly starts introducing new zombies. The overrall pacing of the game is just pretty slow in general, but isn't really a big deal when the game is thoroughly enjoyable throughout. I never found myself BORED while playing this game, even with my gen Z attention span - Taking control out of the player's hands. There are many, many instances where you'll be forced to sit and watch a cutscene in order to understand more about what you're doing, the world, and the plot. While it is for the most part interesting and worth a watch, I think the game should've made more attempts to deliver information during gameplay sections, while you're still controlling Deacon. There's also a lot times you'll be forced to walk really slowly which I just found a bit annoying. But these issues are by no means a dealbreaker, just nitpicks.- Arbitrary limitations. Upon crossing the mountains over to the region in the south, you're locked there. This makes no sense, especially in an open world game. I shouldn't be limited to one half of the map when there's nothing that stops me from going over Thielsen pass back to the north aside from an invisible wall that teleports me back whenever I try going past it. It could've been handled more creatively, maybe by establishing some checkpoint you're not allowed to go through. I just felt like this was annoying.- Fakeout death. Boozer crashes into the front doors of the wizard mountain fortress and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ explodes, but then he returns unharmed in a later cutscene. This genuinely had me really sad, until I completed the level and he was revealed to be alive. These developers cannot be playing with my heart like this. - The beautiful graphics, lovable characters and well written antagonists, great story, incredible world, fun gameplay, well-designed UI, insanely good tension building, crazy good voice acting and animations, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BOOZER. What are you waiting for?!? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ buy this game and play it!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has much the same content as most zombie games but puts them together very nicely. Good storyline and graphics, a few weapons, craftables and modifications with a weapon degradation system that can be tweaked to your taste with user-generated mods. There's the standard fare of individual zombie types but with the addition of zombie 'nests' and hordes. Not many jump-scare moments, but quite a lot of frantic run, dodge and shoot/smash/burn activity. Travel (and some zombie squishing) is done with a customisable motorbike that handles differently across different terrain types, screeching round corners on the roads, power-sliding on mud and dust or trying to stay upright on snow. Various factions and encampments add to the storyline and gameplay. Recommended, especially if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Days Gone is proof you can't trust reviews at all. The game is amazing. To think what they could have done with a sequel, after fine tuning the recipe on the first one - what a shame.I'm not normally someone who finishes a game but this one I've finished twice. First play through on PS4 and now on PC. It looks amazing and generally run pretty well - on PC though, I had to restart it twice, due to a glitch in about 66 hours of play. I know, it's a bit corny at times, but not over the top. What it does really well in my opinion is feel realistic (yes I know zombies aren't real) but when you are in the world, it's far less "video gamey" than most other games. There's so much to do, but the map isn't littered with npc's asking you for help, like so many open world games are now. And then you have the hordes, which could have been a game in it's own.So, if you like me like open world story driven games like RDR2 and TLOU (I know, it's not open world) then this will very likely tickle your fancy. I say go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The gun play mechanics in this game is absolutely terrible. One of the worst i have played in recent times.Aiming is terrible. The ammo Deacon carries is so low its laughable. Like 9 shotgun bullets at most in the start...is he storing ammo in one of his pockets and that's it? The ammo isnt enough when you come across a horde. For most part, there is no advantage in using guns. Rather use crossbow and melee weapons instead.Shotgun blast in close range doesn't seem to be devastating. You still need head shots for it to be lethal against humans, even in extremely close range. Its pathetic. Enemies can occasionally shoot through walls or objects.Deacon's stamina is laughable. Like try running away from a horde and its painful because you ll be out of stamina in 5-10 seconds.It's as if Deacon has arthritis in his legs or something or no sense of adrenaline. Its like he is doing a morning jog when being chased by zombies.The only saving grace for this game is the story which is somewhat interesting.And the zombie behavior is pretty good.Other than that, its a painfully average game with really really bad mechanics.I know there is a campaign for the sequel for this game but unless they address the gun play and combat mechanics, it will be a hard pass for me. would I recommend this game to others? Not really. Its a niche game. If you like the story, you might like the game. but if you arent into the story, then you can pass on this game as it doesnt offer anything else that is unique or better [other than the zombie hordes, which is often annoying to encounter thanks to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gun play / combat mechanics] Update: After sticking through with the game, i am happy to say the game does get a whole lot better. I really enjoyed it once i got better gear and leveled up my skills. I still maintain that going against a horde early on in the game is essentially a death sentence. You wont have enough bullets and if you try to run, you will soon run out of stamina and get overwhelmed. But once you have enough throwables, bullets, and stamina/focus skill points, it becomes manageable. Dont get me wrong, the hordes arent easy to deal with. I still end up sweating after every horde encounter but it does become fun later on. Like an adrenaline rush. Plus, when you clear a certain % of bandit camps or hordes, you unlock cool gear which you cant buy from the shop. So the reward system is quite satisfying. I still find it dumb that you cant aim down the sights or there is no red dot/holo or military grade suppressors in this world (although you do get a rifle with a built in suppressor by clearing 50% of the hordes). The gun mechanics still need improvement. and if you arent into the story, then you may not enjoy the game. I am interested in a sequel but they definitely need to tweak some aspects of the game for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a very mixed feelings about this game. On one hand - in the entire 1.2hrs that I had to play it, the story looked fairly captivating and the visuals are very nice. However, the movement is a tad clunky and bugs out around some of the objects (which I don't mind as much), the camera can sometimes go into a berserker mode (also not much of an issue). But the save system... my god... I think it's the worst one I've seen in any game up to date.I'm fairly surprised that it isn't mentioned as much, but the save system is why I'm refunding this game. It turns out that you cannot save during a mission. The game will let you, it'll create the manual save, it won't tell you anything, that something might go wrong, but once you try to load it - you'll lose all the progress in the mission that you've made so far. I'm not sure if it's just an issue with the first mission, but if developers didn't give a damn to fix it in over 5 years since the first time it got reported... well, I sadly can't be bothered to waste my time to play their game either, I just don't have the time for that (and even if I did, I wouldn't want to waste it repeating the same, dull tasks).I also wasn't that much fond of the combat system of the game (I'm talking mainly about the melee one). It felt unnecessarily long at times with no fun aspect to it other than just mashing the button and doing a roll every once in a lifetime. I get it, I was playing on survival mode and had some silly wooden bat, but come on, it's a game, the combat should be exciting, not make you want to go to sleep :PArt-wise and story-wise so far it seems like a pretty decent game, so I'm a bit disappointed that the broken save system really put me off that much (it just feels like such a disrespect of player's time), but sadly, for the reasons mentioned above, I'm gonna have to give it a dislike.

_childDocuments_.review: Days Gone takes players on an unforgettable journey through a beautifully crafted, post-apocalyptic Oregon. As Deacon St. John, a former biker turned drifter, you’ll navigate a world overrun by freakers, uncovering a gripping story filled with personal loss, survival, and redemption.Pros:Immersive World: The open-world environment is vast and meticulously detailed. From dense forests and abandoned towns to scenic mountain views, the game’s world feels alive and authentic.Engaging Story: The narrative, while not groundbreaking, is compelling and emotional. Deacon’s personal journey and the relationships he forms provide a strong emotional core that drives the game forward.Dynamic Gameplay: The combination of stealth, combat, and exploration keeps the gameplay fresh. The freaker hordes are a highlight, providing tense and exhilarating encounters that demand strategy and quick thinking.Vehicle Mechanics: Riding your bike through the post-apocalyptic landscape is a joy. The bike isn’t just a mode of transportation; it’s an integral part of survival, requiring fuel and maintenance.Atmospheric Soundtrack: The music and sound design enhance the game’s atmosphere, adding depth to both the tranquil and intense moments.Cons:Repetitive Missions: Some missions can feel repetitive, especially towards the latter part of the game. The formula of clearing out infestations and gathering resources might start to wear thin.Technical Issues: The game had some performance issues at launch, though many of these have been addressed in patches. Nonetheless, occasional bugs and frame rate dips can still detract from the experience.Pacing Problems: At times, the pacing feels uneven. There are moments where the story drags or where the gameplay becomes a grind, affecting the overall flow.Overall, Days Gone is a gripping and immersive experience that fans of open-world games and survival narratives will likely appreciate. Its beautiful world, engaging story, and dynamic gameplay make it a standout title, even if it’s not without its flaws. If you’re looking for a game that combines emotional depth with thrilling action, Days Gone is definitely worth a ride.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I am really impressed with how this port turned out. I was expecting a whole load of issues like terrible optimization, buggy textures, etc but I got the complete opposite and I couldnt be happier. This game for how big and beautiful the world is, runs smooth as butter even on my graphics card which has been visibly dying for a little while now.Now let me get onto the game itself. I bought and completed this game on Ps4 when it first came out and to this day its one of my personal favorite games I've ever played at least being in my top 20. Finding out it was coming to PC was like Christmas had come early and now I have finally played it and as I said before I am incredibly impressed and cant wait to play this game again without having to deal with controller aiming and other console issues. The story for this game is one of the things that really caught me off guard when I first played it, its a rather impressive story for a zombie game especially. Pair that with the beautiful and expansive game world, characters that you'll no doubt become attached to and the top tier voice actors that make them happen and youre in for a beautiful ride.The gameplay is nothing to shrug off either as this game will throw a variety of different enemies at you from and have you fighting everything from unimaginably giant hordes of 'freaks' to bandit encampments as well as the local wildlife. The game also has a wide variety of weapons to choose from which is very limited at the very beginning of the game consisting of weaker weapons such as the starting pistol or a .22 rifle. You can find some rather powerful weapons like AK's or sawed off shotguns as well but, at least on hard difficulty, a shortage of ammunition will mean you'll be switching weapons often. As you progress and do missions for the various encampments however you will eventually gain access to some of the heavier artillery like heavy machine guns, automatic shotguns, .50 Cal Rifles, etc. Thats not even touching the tip of how many different weapons are available throughout the game. All of the weapons I've used so far sound beefy and are satisfying to use making combat insanely enjoyable.I'd say my biggest criticism of this game are the little side quests you can do to gain reputation as this game sadly suffers from the ubisoft virus, meaning a lot of these side missions consist of going to various locations, killing enemies, job finished. The most enjoyable missions by far are the hordes that you unlock in bulk towards the end of the game. Other than that I would say from what I remember the game has about 4 main side missions you'll be doing: *SPOILERS KINDA* motorcycle chases, bandit camps, freak nests, hordes and worst of all the dreaded NERO stealth missions where you just crouch around and follow soldiers to eavesdrop on their conversations. No combat just stealth. Its good for learning some story but they just start becoming a pain in the ass the more you do them. The one thing that makes doing most of these over and over fun however is the wide selection of weapons you get to test out while doing them. Its admittedly not as bad as other games that just have the same 1 mission repeated but its still no Red Dead Redemption or Grand Theft Auto where a lot of non main story missions have unique plots and have you doing different things for the most part.I have more I could talk about but this is getting long so I'll end it by saying if you enjoy a good zombie game and are looking for an immersive game and story to plunge into this game is up there with the best in my opinion. I hope after this other games that were previously console exclusives will start trickling out. I would love to see The Last of Us and Bloodborne come to PC, I dont listen to the people that say it will never happen or will definitely happen, I just hold out hope that eventually it'll happen and honestly I dont think its too far fetched at this point. But Days Gone is a great start and I am verryyy happy that this came to PC and will certainly be putting a disgusting amount of hours into it in the coming weeks.EDIT: Well it took a while for me to really feel like getting into this game for the long haul again but I did and it was just as fun as the first time playing through it. So much better on PC than on PS4 and I forgot a lot of what happened in the story since I havent played the game since it first came out so it was almost like playing it for the very first time again in that sense too. I knew I loved this game but now that I've went through and played it again I REALLY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game and everything about it. The characters are portrayed beautifully and all develop and grow throughout the story and become people you dont want to die or anything when it all comes to a head and it also does a great job at creating villains that you will learn to hate with a passion and will be more than satisfied by seeing them fall one by one. Some say the story is too long and drags on after a while but for me I couldnt get enough of it. If it meant seeing these characters grow more I could play another 100 hours worth of story for all I care which is why it sucks that we likely wont be getting a Days Gone 2. But I just thought I would come back to this review after beating again to share my thoughts. Game is beautiful and everyone should try it out. 12/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Days gone is well optimized and has an immersive world, but it could have been a lot better. Motorcycle driving is perfectly done. As for zombies, 99% of the time you will fight regular zombies, there are two types that are a bit harder to kill but you will almost never run into them in the open world, had a lot more potential. _childDocuments_.review: I'll start with saying that the game might be worth buying on sale but definitely not 50€.The story is okay but it's nothing that we haven't seen before. From time to time gets boring because you have to do similar missions in order to continue with the story but except that I'd say it has an okay story.About - []The fact that it's a zombie / survival game and there's no backpacks that you can use to carry more loot is actually insane. If you rescue an NPC you'll see that every single one of them does not wear any gear such as belts, firearms, tools, weapons in regular or backpacks. In my personal opinion NPCs are extremely boring. If you go by an NPC he'll start a conversation even if you're just passing by or if you're behind them. There's no interaction button to start or continue the conversation and it's not the "Hi! How are you?" type but more like a full normal conversation or a story from their personal life.About - []Ohhhh. Don't get me started. There's a couple different plants that you can gather and I've never actually used them for anything ( you can craft arrows ) other than that you can sell them in the "kitchen" for some "quick" cash or "trust" but you sell them for pretty much nothing. The only thing that the zombies/freakers are dropping is ears that you can sell for some credits that you can use in the camp. Also there's around 5 things that you can loot in the whole world/map and that comes to empty bottles, scrap, bandages and a couple more that you use to create molotovs, repair your bike etc. The loot in the game is extremely low on variety and boring.About - []Quite a few weapons that are hard to obtain. You have to level up your trust in each camp in order to unlock the SAME stuff as in the other camps. For example if I'm trust level 2 in one of the camps I'll be able to buy a suppressor but if I'm not level 2 in the other camp I can't buy that suppressor which is dumb. You can't upgrade your weapons with custom scopes, lasers etc. you can only attach suppressor to them. Half of the weapons require level 3 trust and it's hard to level up. If you want you can scavenge around the world and look for the blue question marks to rescue people and send them to the camp you want for some credits and trust in return and it will still take you a lot of time before unlocking the better weapons ( which are very close to the ones you have in the beginning ). You have to refill your ammo after every fight and your suppressor breaks super fast which is annoying.About - []You can't change your shoes, pants, jacket, hat.. ANYTHING.... The only cosmetics that are in the game is for your bike and your bike only.About - []Winter comes - you still ride that bike and you get covered with snow, so you become a snowman. Super unrealistic. You can't change your outfit and it's weird how you're not cold. There's some nice touches here and there but it's nothing special that will make you say "Wow, what a nice detail".About - []The map is nice in size but the fact that you travel from the same road every single time is getting boring with every minute. Some locations are weird. And the fast travel requires you to clear an infection zone which is fine but 15 minutes later you can't use the location to fast travel because you have to clear the zone again and after another 15 minutes it will let you teleport. Infected zones are super easy to clear ( on normal only 2 or up to 3 zombies are coming out ). I haven't found any hidden or special locations ( maybe there is but I just haven't found any ). Bandit camps are not worth clearing, infection zones are not worth clearing...And most importantly! There's A LOT of places where it seems like you can go trough or climb but you just CAN'T which is annoying. You can't jump, you can't claim a simple rock, you can't go trough places that are wider than you AND there's open areas on the map where if you try to go trough it will say "Leaving Playing Area" or smth like this because you have to unlock it first by doing a quest. Annoying.....About - []Jobs are dumb. You have to catch a guy alive and that's it. Side quests are boring and some of the main quests as well. Some of them repeat and most of them are just riding from A to B get into a fight for 2 minutes and then you go from B to A to finish the quest. There's absolutely nothing that makes you attach to any of the characters and nothing that will make you remember the story after a month.About - []You have to refill it super often and there's plenty of cosmetics for the bike.About - []Overall the game is not worth 50€. I'd pay 15€ or 20€ on a good day. It's not polished and it looks like the devs just rushed the game. RDR2 costs the same and it has MUCH, MUCH greater story, MUCH more details, MUCH bigger map, MUCH better NPCs... Just buy RDR2 if you haven't played it yet and you won't regret it. It took me 15 hours of gameplay to get extremely bored and I don't think that I'll finish the game anytime soon. But at the end of the day.. it's your own decision and opinion that matters. If you feel like the game is good just buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was the best game I've played in a while. I love a storyline that I can sink my teeth into. And I even almost shed a tear once or twice. To be honest, I wasn't excited at all about this game. I thought it was just another cookie cutter zombie game. If it hadn't been on sale, I may never have experienced it.   I found the main character's personality a little annoying and immature at times, (actually a lot of the time) but I guess that means that I was vested in the story. This would be a great limited series or 3 1/2 hr movie. There are a lot of missions to tackle, but they are done in a way that didn't get too monotonous or tedious. Most of the tasks were to go clear out a camp, or go rescue someone from bandits, or go find guy that did something bad. And you could very well get ambushed or sniped off of your bike at about any time while cruising down the road. One thing you might notice tho, it's the same dummy every time during those random encounter rescues. The controls were a touch wonky at times, like trying to jump on my bike wasn't always a seamless operation and can really frustrate you while trying to make a very quick get away.   Good graphics, very smooth performance, engaging story, well acted characters with actual personalities blended with enjoyable missions and goals made this a really good time for me. And there seems to be a lot more to do, even after I've finished the main story.   Overall I give this game an 9.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: They killed it with this port.So far the game runs buttery smooth and had little to no trouble running it on my PC. To be honest, I thought this port was gonna run poorly like Horizon Zero Dawn's PC launch or the absolute dumpster fire state of this game when it first launched on PS4. And I'm glad to admit that I was wrong.Now the game itself:To be blunt, this game doesn't do much to to set itself apart from other open-world zombie games like Dying Light has(Speaking of Dying Light, when the hell are they gonna announce the release date of the sequel?). But that's not to say there wasn't at least an attempt made. The game looks great, using the bike feels good to control, and the games' main selling point: dealing with hordes. When dealing with hordes, having a stamina bar is both a blessing and a curse in this situation. When you run out of stamina, you're as good as dead and have to start all the way over. On the other hand, it forces you to plan your route and the placement of traps which makes each horde mission feel different.The Story:The story can be best described as somewhere between not good and not bad. It's okay. I think the problem lies with the cutscenes having some jarring transitions or just being straight up unnecessary. Hell, in the beginning it felt like there was gonna be playable section but was cut out with little to no changes made to the cutscenes and felt like some context was missing. Everything else I thought did it's job very well.Conclusion:I think this game was pretty underrated. It has its issues but nothing that would completely hinder your experience. I do hope Sony keeps up the trend of making more PC ports for their exclusives and I can't wait to see what else they have planned.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Days Gone: A Thrilling Ride Through the ApocalypseDays Gone delivers an adrenaline-pumping journey through a post-apocalyptic world that will leave players on the edge of their seats. Set in the stunning and perilous Pacific Northwest, this open-world adventure is a triumph in survival gaming.One of the most remarkable aspects of Days Gone is its vast and meticulously crafted world. From dense forests to abandoned highways, every corner of the map is teeming with life, both human and infected. The dynamic weather system adds another layer of immersion, with rainstorms and fog dramatically altering the landscape and gameplay.The heart and soul of Days Gone lie in its gripping gameplay mechanics. As protagonist Deacon St. John, players must navigate through hordes of ferocious Freakers while scavenging for resources and completing missions. The combat system is both intuitive and satisfying, offering a variety of weapons and tactics to dispatch enemies with precision.Beyond its intense action sequences, Days Gone also shines in its narrative depth. The story of Deacon's quest for redemption is compelling, filled with poignant moments of loss and resilience. The emotional journey is further enhanced by stellar voice acting and captivating character development.However, despite its many strengths, Days Gone does stumble slightly in its storytelling execution. While the overarching narrative is engaging, there are moments where pacing issues and predictable plot twists detract from the overall experience. Additionally, some side quests feel disconnected from the main storyline, leading to a sense of disjointedness in the narrative flow.Despite this minor setback, Days Gone remains a must-play title for fans of survival and action-adventure games. With its breathtaking world, thrilling gameplay, and emotional storytelling, it stands as a testament to the power of immersive gaming experiences. Strap in, gear up, and prepare to embark on an unforgettable journey through the apocalypse.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to review. I think the game is quite serviceable, reasonably entertaining, seems well-optimized and clearly has a bit of cult-following. But I tried getting into the game twice (once on PS4, secondly here on PC) and each time I just lost interest or became frustrated with the mechanics.I think a lot of my disappointment has to do with the story, acting, and pacing. Right from the very, very beginning the main character makes the most idiotic decision in history and then we're expected to stick with him for the 30+ hour journey ahead. It's not spoiling much to say that the opening sequence sees our main character voluntarily stick his critically injured wife (who he's infatuated with) on a helicopter headed out of a zombie apocalypse because he feels more obligated to take care of his motorcycle-club drinking buddy. That opening sequence feels lazy, moronic, and uninspired.The story takes off from there and does a reasonable job of introducing you to new characters, acquainting you with the the shape of the new world, and feeding you crumbs about how to find your missing wife. The main character comes across gruff and unlikeable, but I eventually found that he became a more interesting person about 2/3 of the way through the story; there is some character development there but it's a bit shallow. Secondary characters aren't given much development beyond typecasting, in my opinion. Redneck conspiracy theorist, traumatized teenage girl, and insane religious cult leader are all present (among others). There's some small twists and turns, but largely the story fits into some predictable beats. It's nothing ground breaking.What the game nails pretty well is atmosphere. The game takes place in a fictionalized version of central and southern Oregon (around Bend, where the studio that makes this game is based). I live here, in southern Oregon and have visited some of the real places that are featured in this game. This game takes place in my back yard and they did a pretty fantastic job of shrinking some of Oregon's greatest features into a relatively  small open-world map. There are real places, real landmarks, and references to real cities (big and small) that genuinely made me smile. The world isn't incredibly detailed or anything, but it's fits the style and it feels a lot like home, minus the zombies.The gameplay here is pretty standard 3rd-person craft-em-up open-world survival 'horror' stuff. It doesn't do a single thing uniquely here, it's almost  quite literally cookie-cutter design. I will say however that M+K controls are a heaps better than playing with a controller on the PS4. I played on medium difficulty and only felt challenged when dealing with enormous groups of enemies (called Hordes). Ammo is more than plentiful but I found myself struggling to find the right crafting components for some items. I guess one of the selling points of the game is that you get to ride a motorcycle around and you have to care for it by keeping it tuned up and making sure it has enough fuel. It's really just a little resource management that is required to get you from A-to-B. You can run out of fuel and your bike can be damaged too badly to continue to ride, making you look for fuel or 'scrap' to repair your bike.  I never once ran out of fuel, though. The bike handles well and is upgradeable over time and customizable with paint schemes and other visual upgrades.It's a good game, honestly. It's not awful and it's far from a masterpiece, but I just can't get into it. I kept feeling obligated to finish the game rather than wanting to play it. I wanted to see the end of the story only for the satisfaction of having finished it, not because I was actually gripped by the story or characters. It's easily forgettable but it'll definitely provide entertainment. Perhaps I've been spoiled by some truly  monumental games from the last decade. Perhaps my tastes have become overly sophisticated and I'm now a video game snob, but at the very end of this long-winded rant I can't honestly say "Yeah, go ahead and buy Day's Gone, I thought it was great." I can't honestly say that.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a FarCry game with zombies in many ways: it's open world, the world is largely uninteractive, you have a few guns you can carry, a load out you can swap at camps, weapon mods, a very limited amount of stuff you can loot, quests guiding a story through the game, etc. etc.Is it better than FarCry? Yes it is. As a game on its own it's nothing that amazing except you have the excellent bike to travel around with but the game has SOUL which Ubisoft games always lack. The characters in the game feel real & the story really drags you in after a while which makes a huge difference because after 20 hours you've kind of experienced everything the game has to offer in terms of gameplay: lots of camp clearing, bounty hunts, etc. and the story is what keeps you going. Besides this there's some ... less amazing things like:- while open world, exploring is not rewarding - you won't magically find amazing gear or loot. Most stuff you'll want to get is heavily tied to quest lines, no exploration.- you have very strict limits of what you can pick up. 5 of that, 3 of this. You quickly reach those limits which sucks the fun out of further looting since it's quite a tedious process to open every car trunk. Since you only use certain grenades in specific situations I ended up almost always being fully stocked.- there's very very limited crafting which is a shame because the setting lent itself for much more than this.- the story is extremely linear and it's very much on-the-rails. On the plus side, it's well fleshed out and the over-arching story is long and rewarding.The story is definitely what saves it. It gives me "The Last of Us" vibes in the sense that you want to keep playing just to find out what happens next. TLOU had very overrated gameplay however and was extremely linear in both story AND game design whereas Days Gone is a lot more open and gives you more freedom to explore. The combat also allows for more variety & tactics. In the end this game deserved a sequel - but then again, after what they did with TLOU, do you expect modern devs to make good sequels?
_childDocuments_.name: Days Gone

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I did not finish. I waited for a ~50% off deal before picking this up, and even that feels like too much in hindsight. I hear a lot of "the story gets so much better, you just have to wait 20-30+ hours in" commentary, and I just don't see it. The game is freaking gorgeous, and I dig the soundtrack, but everything else just feels so overwhelming bland and generic in its execution. This could have been a *vastly* more engaging and fulfilling experience if they shrunk down the open world to a fraction of its size and focused more on a steady stream of engaging, story-focused content. Even just having the option to ignore all the filler content and proceed uninterrupted through the game's main story would have been a huge improvement.As I slogged through awful stealth missions and endless "runs" for the various camps to curry favor and credits, I kept thinking the main story and some of the more interesting side content was going to really take off, but it drips that content out so slowly that boredom won out in the end. An open-world zombie game shouldn't feel this tedious to play, and I'm starting to low-key hate the industry's obsession with turning everything into an endless sandbox experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into heart-pounding action, Days Gone is your game. Meet Deacon, a tough guy with a knack for taking down zombies and a sweet ride that steals the show.Gameplay-wise, it's like The Last of Us meets Grand Theft Auto. Craft to survive, sneak past enemies, and dive into intense zombie battles. And let's not forget the motorcycle - it adds a whole new level of thrill as you zip through the apocalypse.But the real kicker? The hordes. These massive zombie groups will test your nerves like nothing else. It's a challenge you won't forget.In short, Days Gone keeps you on the edge with its adrenaline-pumping gameplay and epic zombie battles. Plus, that motorcycle? It's practically a character of its own. Here's hoping for a Days Gone 2!

Great game, especially when you can get it on sale for $12.Yeah, the story and dialogue are nothing to write home about, but everything else? I'm having a blast. Combat is dynamic and challenging, even if the AI is a bit janky at times. Scavenging and crafting isn't boring. There's a ton to do as you traverse the world that gives it plenty of replayability, and the way the game scripts things makes every encounter manage to feel organic. The zombies might be "I Am Legend" ripoffs, but man, it's absolutely terrifying to be chased by a horde even when you're speeding away on your bike. The world remembers what you've done, so when you come back to a location, things are still there the way you left them. The game just does a great job of keeping you engaged and coming back for more. Really, the story/dialogue is the only weak point here. The graphics are stunning, and will hold up well for years despite being a 2019 title on last-gen hardware.If you're looking at the gameplay videos and feeling like this is some bland Last of Us copy-paste, trust me, it's not. An hour or two in, time starts to fly and you have to make yourself put it down.Oh, and Steam Deck performance is just wonderful. High settings and 40-60 FPS? Yes please.
