_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. I have played a lot of moto games since Atari days up through modern consoles. I play with the AI on Realistic difficulty using a 125 2 stroke. If I do not play for a while I struggle to get midpack until I get several races in again. So there is a learning curve and constant practice needed to stay competitive to AI which to me adds depth.ADDED CHALLENGE: Anyone clear the uphill QUAD on a 125 at Matterley Basin. With some almost perfect entries and still only cases to show for it. The QUAD I do not think it is possible on a 125 but I have hope. Link video if you get it done.Pros:Fun and challenging single playerBike upgrades actually matter(non cosmetic)Bike setup changes make a big differenceFun tracks that are based on real tracksWeather condition do have impact and good feelingCommunity made maps are fun and now searchable(not searchable at release)Cons:Graphical glitchesScrub/whip easy to accidentally trigger when not wanted on rollers/braking/acceleration bumpsdead multiplayerI do not think all that was promised pre release was ever deliveredGame says dedicated servers but there are none and no dedicated server files for community run serversWindows time sync errors can make game unplayable or time attack leaderboards not update your timesTrack Editor was a let down but does have several improvements from 2019 but missing some featuresNo bug support from devs, I believe that AMD GPU users like myself have more bugs than NVIDIA but it is hard to know for sureThe first track Matterley Basin has aggressively fast AI even on very easy setting that puts off some players. Basically if you win Matterley Basin you are going to completely smoke the AI at almost every round on that difficulty setting. I find the second round to be a challenging one as well. Some tracks are tough others I get into lappers on Realistic difficulty.To compound the difficulty you probably are starting on a stock 125cc 2 stroke. The 250 4 strokes are baseline faster, switch to a 250F if you can. Also the upgraded parts on the 125 make a big difference. You have to ride like Bubba Stewart on a stock 125 to clear a lot of the jumps. Upgraded parts make it more manageable. The bike setup also makes a substantial difference that can affect your lap times.So the game puts off some, if you keep going there is depth to setup and learning the tracks.I have recently(2024) started doing time attack with a friend that normally played MXbikes. Doing time attack will show you the depth of the games mechanics in the bike setup and learning track lines.  Some reviews say that setup changes do not do much...Well while some are hard to feel during casual play, if you go up against the stop watch, watch replays, and attach sections to try new lines in time attack you will see, feel, and be amazed at the difference that adjustments make. Also once you move setup away from neutral you will notice track to track your results are different. The surface condition/material matters. Setup for sand does not work well for harder surfaces. Note that is the bike is left with neutral setup it works ok on all tracks. Manual shifting and ratio adjustment is still the largest accel/speed effect in the game. Multiplayer works but is almost all but dead with no one usually playing My biggest gripe occurs when trying to squeeze all the corner speed i can out of a 125. Using left and right analog sticks to turn and move body position to corner while hitting small bumps/rollers can trigger the scrub/whip which makes your avatar instantly whip/scrub/pancake and crash.I have only race the 125/250f MX2 Championship a few times and never done the 250/450f MX1. I like railing on the 125 because that is what I race IRL. 2024 update here, a friend pointed out that a mx2 125/250f can be used to race the MX1 250/450f class. So I am going to take a shot at racing the MX1 class on the 125 when I get through all maps time attacking and get my lap times fast enough to compete with MX1 AI set to realistic.I do have a bug that started when I fired up the game again after months of not playing...the 125 2 stroke have no seat/subframe/any bodywork. I'll see if I can get it fixed. Update Q1 2024: I was able to get my bikes to have parts again with only the more common checkerboard texture glitch. I changed the cosmetic parts I had on the bike and the subframe/seat came back. HOWEVER when I played multiplayer other people using the cosmetics my install does not like, their bikes are missing half the bike. As for the checkerboard look on bike and rider I have yet to find a fix.Update Q4 2024: It is possible to cheese your way into MX1 class riding your MX2 bike. So for the ultimate hard mode you can enter mx1 and select your custom mx2 bike. The 125 vs 450s on Matterley Basin is quite the challenge

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I've owned and played every iteration of the MXGP and Monster Energy Supercross series that milestone puts out and I generally like it as a simcade dirt bike game. But this game is a slap in the face to anyone who enjoys MXGP. Milestone has always had slightly wonky riding physics, but they are getting better so I can't fault them there. I personally like the way the game feels in first person. Especially since third person is such a joke. But the UI is an absolute abomination. The UI feels like a 2010 indie game, and even they those games had better UI. I'm hoping Milestone was hampered by covid like no other because the menu systems and everything that goes along with it is an absolute joke. From previous reviews I see they already have been fixing their horrible UI and adding in BASIC features that any racing game has but I hope they get it figured out quickly. I'm still holding out hope for this game but as a yearly released game it's unacceptable to regress so far.

_childDocuments_.review: This addition has a lot of stuff going for it. There are kinda-sorta ruts, the air physics are MUCH improved, cornering feel decent. The variety of bike and riders is great, AND 2 STROKES!There are a couple of things that keep this game from being really great. 1)The way the rider handles berms feels awkward and often stands them up mid corner. 2) The way the front end squares up a corner if you aren't going fast feels stupid and ruins the flow, idk what they were trying to accomplish with that mechanic it makes no sense, it happens at too high a speed. 3) MILESTONE QA YOUR GAMES! There are so many tracks where you have to pick the best way to cut the track in order to win. Way too many corners that you can cut to make up time. Also a lot of corners that seems to put you out of bounds mid corner.This game is a big improvement over 2019, I think it's a lot of fun. Some minor tweaks could make it amazing. But I'm enjoying it so far!*UPDATE*Okay after playing this game a lot more and being able to push the rider faster......the cornering physics are fundamentally broke. The faster you go in this game the more awkward it gets. In no way is it ever faster to take the outside line and the rider cannot interact with the berms correctly, they end up shooting up the side of it. While the game feels better in some ways to 2019, the more you play the more you'll realize this game needs a major overhaul. Milestone seems to try to make changes in one are of the game (air physics) and hurts another area (cornering).

_childDocuments_.review: When the game was originally released, I didn't care for it. But after a few hours of play and patches, I'm really enjoying this game and felt I had to update my review.The bike feels great. I really like the little berms that are used to simulate a rut. It's nice having to slow down to hit inside lines or choosing to rail the outside to try to pass someone.The first person view is really good. The overall feel is a lot better, especially on jumps. I feel like I can easily kick the bike out a little or a lot to get the right line over some obstacles.The AI still bothers me on Realistic difficulty. I've noticed a few times my best lap time is listed for the fastest rider. I don't mind losing, but I want it to be fair. And the freight train can be annoying, but this has been all of the releases. Overall, it is nice that they're more difficult than in previous releases.I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing every milestone mx/sx installment thus far, I am still enjoying this series. There are a lot of things with this one that carried over from the previous games, but at the same time the bike still feels a bit different in this one. The physics aren't perfect, but you can at least get some air underneath the bike, and there is a lot more movement with the bike and rider in the air (feels realistic if you're gentle with the analog sticks). The terrain deformation still isn't quite there, but at least there are a variety of pre-made ruts in each of the corners to give different line choices. Graphically the game looks great, i had to set the resolution to 200% to get the full effect, but it looks very nice in 4k and has been running between 50-60 fps for me. By no means is this game a simulator, but the series has never meant it to be. Its fun, it has a good career mode, and its got all the updated teams, tracks, and riders. There's definitely still room for improvement, but this one should keep me occupied at least until SX4 comes out. Still holding out hope that one day we will have official liveried helmets, but thankfully we have mods for that in the meantime.

name: RIDE 4
detailed_description: Are you ready to live the best gaming experience that a motorcycle fan can get? RIDE 4 will spark your competitive soul with hundreds of bikes, dozens of tracks and a whole new level of realism. NEW AND ENHANCED CONTENTS Choose among hundreds of officially licensed bikes and ride on dozens of tracks all around the world, carefully designed with an extraordinary level of detail! Every asset has been created starting from CAD data, laser and 3D scanning to achieve precision down to the smallest detail and let you enjoy the best two-wheel racing experience ever. CHOOSE YOUR PATH Jump into an amazing and dynamic adventure that interacts with your decisions and choose your own path from the regional events up to the professional leagues. Show your riding skills through challenging races, ability tests, track days and a huge set of events. You could even become an official tester for the most celebrated manufacturers! DAY/NIGHT CYCLE, DYNAMIC WEATHER AND ENDURANCE RACES RIDE 4 features a fully dynamic weather conditions system and a complete day/night cycle. Experience the race in a new light and prove you are the best rider in any condition. And for the first time, the 'Endurance' mode will put your tenacity to the test, with animated pit-stops and long lasting races: prepare to face a world where strategy is the ultimate ingredient of your success! NEURAL AI Let us introduce you to A.N.N.A. (Artificial Neural Network Agent), our revolutionary neural AI system based on machine learning. Race against faster, smarter, more accurate riders and compete with an AI more human than ever! EXPANDED CUSTOMIZATION Race with your own style! Choose among plenty of official brands for your rider’s outfit and customize your bikes aesthetically and mechanically. Unleash your creativity and design your helmet, suit and bike livery in total freedom thanks to our new graphics editor. Once you’re done, share your creations online or just discover the best designs of the community! ONLINE COMPETITIONS Enjoy the most complete and lag-free online multiplayer experience ever thanks to our dedicated servers.

_childDocuments_.review: First off i've owned every Ride game and as a bike fan love the series however was expecting so much more from this. The visuals are great and early stages seem promising but why release a game that is not 100% finished?? so many bugs, lights staying on, tyre models not working properly, sound issues and then you release a DLC which we have to pay for straight away. I think you need to look after the fans and sort the game out and give the DLC away for free as a gesture to those who have previously owned all or some of the series (check out the Forza motorsport way of operating) Not sure what was done with all that development time and lockdown and who tests these game prior to launch?? I hope you pay attention to these comments as like me people have invested a lot of good money purchasing the games then the DLC. If your thinking of buying this game i suggest you wait for a few patches to be released first and pay attention to the comments. As a real motorbike rider of many years you still cant beat Isle of Man TT 2 for the real speed and sense of being on a bike, I was really hoping for this with Ride 4 but sadly it does not come close.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very hesitant to pick up this title based on the reviews. Newcomers were recommending it, and veterans of the series weren't. I have 50+ hours in RIDE 2, which is arguably the most recommended in the series. Here are my thoughts on RIDE 4 so far:Let's start by addressing the elephant in the room: The AI. Yes, it's true, the AI are completely unaware of your presence as the player and do not react to you being near them. Yes, it's true, the AI operate on different physics rules allowing them to brake way later than you can. Because of those two points, yes, it's true, the AI will run you over ... a lot. Yes, it's true, even the default "Easy" AI difficulty setting is remarkably challenging to secure a 1st place finish. Heavily utilizing the "Rewind" function, you can attempt corners over and over again until you finally make it through without being crashed into by an AI. Overall, is the AI lackluster for such a polished series? Yes. Is it bad enough to not buy the game? No.The Physics. A lot of reviews complain that the physics feel sluggish, unresponsive, too arcadey, or too simulator-y. I personally haven't had any major complaints with it. Turning feels fine. Riding with assists on feels fine. Bikes have to lean to turn. Because of that, there is a slight delay between telling the bike to turn and it actually turning. Once you adjust to that delay and stop treating this like a car racing game, you'll have a better time. My only minor complaint is that there are no sensitivity adjustment options for inputs. To me, steering feels too sensitive to be smooth, but it's perfectly playable. (It could just be my controller)The content and economy.I bought the game bundled with all of the DLC for $30. That felt like a reasonable entry price to not only have access to all of the available content, but also have a permanent 2x multiplier to credits earned in-game. Am I happy that Milestone monetized this game like a Free-To-Play title? No. Is the "complete" game a good value at $30? To me it is. (Remember, I have 50+ hours in RIDE 2, I knew what I was getting into)I went into this game expecting unplayable levels of jank, based on the reviews I read. That's simply not the case. If you are interested in motorcycles, this is a perfectly fine racing title to help scratch that itch. It looks good, runs well, and plays fine. Yes, there are some frustrating quirks to tolerate, but nothing that has kept me from having a good time overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing Ride since Ride 1 and absolutely love Ride 2 and 3. They all had their problems but Ride 4 seems to have made everything worse. Physics that make no sense, AI that somehow seems even worse than before and a career mode that is anything but enjoyable. In previous games you would start with small bikes and rise through the ranks until you were able to compete with proper pedigree race bikes. Now you jump straight into 600cc races and time trials....oh so many boring time trials. Tracks somehow also got worse. Cadwell Park has never been my favourite, but how is it even narrower now, so you cant even fit 2 bikes next to each other? Cars race here IRL!And then there's supermoto. Why even bother? Physics already got worse in Ride 3 compared to 2. Now Physics for them are not even arcade, they're just weird.Bike roster got even smaller. Where are all the starter bikes from previous editions? Where are all the classics? Oh right, behind the DLC paywall.Costumization in 2 and 3 was great fun. Somewhat basic and predictable (there is exactly 1 part in each category that is the best and its the same for each bike), yet still fun. Now it is even more basic.The one and only thing that got better is graphics and I don't care that much about graphics.In conclusion, save your money and get Ride 3 or MotoGP 20.

_childDocuments_.review: I will begin this by saying that this is is one of the first racing games that I have owned in several years, if not a decade. So, really, this review is tailored to those who are not expert already in racing games. I have never before hit such a learning curve on any game... and I have played the Dark Souls trilogy. Also, I do take my motorcycle to track days in real life. I do not race, but I do ride on a track. I bought this game because there are many motorcycles that I am curious about and this game has them lovingly rendered. I really, really love motorcycles and thought that it might be fun to get to know other motorcycles, if even virtually,  and test some limits without, you know, actually dying. It seems like a great game, I only wish that I could play it. This game does not so much have a learning curve as a complete learning wall. 4 hours into the game and I still cannot qualify the second track, I mean, I am not even competing with other racers, simply a time trial that is impossible and that leaves not even the tiniest fraction of a margin of error. The controller has no finesse at all, the slightest twitch and the motorcycle is careening 90 degrees in the opposite direction, likewise, the accelerator and brakes are totally binary, with either full throttle or no throttle as your only option. Ditto for the brakes. It would be great if there were an option for calibrating the controller sensitivity. Playing with the physics settings doesn't really do anything, no matter what setting you have, the game offers absolutely no room for error whatsoever. Even if going off track won't send your racer flying, the time infraction that it gives you means that there is no possible way of qualifying the track. It's still essentially game over, only you waste more time getting there. It is kind of weird that, generally speaking, in a video game one accomplishes what one cannot do in real life, but in this game I cannot accomplish what I can do in real life, at least so far in these beginner tracks where I am riding alone. Four hours of time investment to not get past the second track; I mean, I like learning curves and entering into a zone, but this is just brutal punishment that has become tedious and boring. If you are a complete newbie with a good four hour intro course and you'll be riding a real motorcycle in real life. Seriously, not worth the effort for a game. The worst thing is that there really are no tutorials or anything to help you learn or get the hang of things. Likewise, the auto-pilot beginning is really annoying and sort of just slingshots you into the middle of a maneuver that is already begun in a very specific way and that you must complete, again, with no margin of error exactly as it wants you to complete it. Like that uncle that teaches you to swim by throwing you into the middle of the lake and calling you names while you drown. I imagine that this must be a wonderful game for those who are already expert at racing games and whose thumbs can control the stick at a hundredth of a fraction of a millimetre. But for the rest of us, we will never actually know what the game is like.

_childDocuments_.review: Five hours in, and I can't recommend this game.The learning curve is extreme, and that isn't always a bad thing, but there are some design choices from the game developers that were really annoying. Let me get this out of the way. The graphics are really good. Replay's are fun to watch. The sense of speed is there, and it really comes to life in some of the camera angles available. Customization is really awesome, except for the fact that customizing helmets does not allow you to overwrite the helmet logos. Also, the rewind feature probably saved my controller/wall/monitor. It's much better then the one in Forza, where you rewind up to a certain point, which could end up ruining your perfect line from a turn before.  In this game, you control how far you rewind, and there is also a nice little slow motion assist to get you back up to speed, giving you time to get your controls where you want them.Easy mode isn't. The AI set to easy is so much better at taking lines then you. I set the assists settings to max, and it really was more of a hindrance then a help. According to the assists, my biker will automatically break, lean forward, lean back, and help me in my race. This would be great, normally, but really it seems that Ideal racing lines do not change based on the bike you have. In some cases, when it tells you to brake it's outright lying. At one point, there was this massive wide turn, and my biker was constantly breaking. All through the turn, the AI were just jamming past me, putting me from third to eighth. Then at the end of the turn, it told me I really needed to break hard at the start of a half-mile strait away, causing me to go from eighth to last place. I turned off assists, and was able to make that same turn without breaking at all during the turn Afterwards, I sped out of the turn putting me in first place, and yes it was telling me to break at the start of the strait-away. I ignored it.Now lets talk about the AI. The first race I did, I had all the assists on, I had the AI set to easy, and I had the starting bike. The race begins, and I start moving forward. Some of the bikes ahead of me just take off way faster then me. While I'm thinking that I probably have to work on my RPM's at the start of a race, one of the AI's behind me slams into the back of my bike, causing a massive pile up of bikes and bodies all over the pavement. There was no one by me, tons of room to go around. Honestly, I laughed, but when it happened again on my third race, I was already tired of it. However, when they are racing, they are following racing lines way better then you on easy. There were times where I felt I was doing well, and getting a feel for the game, when the next three riders ahead of me where the same 3 dots for several laps, and I just couldn't catch up to them.  This was after me rewinding over and over again to get better cornering lines. About the only time I was ever able to catch up to AI was on long strait-away's, and for the life of me, I couldn't get the controls to behave in any realistic way.TL:DREasy mode isn't.Learning curve is high, and very unforgiving.The 'assists' are way more a hindrance then a help.AI is poor, and will slam into from behind like the bike wants to mate.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Over a hundred beautifully crafted motorbikes from past and present, each of them meticulously simulated.- The physics are second to none in the bike genre, it's a true simulation.- Many different tracks, ranging from street circuits like Macau to purpose built racing tracks like Silverstone. - An AI that will challenge all but the most capable riders.- Graphics that are good and at times astonishingly beautiful. - Easily the best sim game for bikes there is. Not that there's a huge market, but if you love riding bikes this is the game for you.- The career mode is pretty meaty, especially once you get past the first regional league. Cons:- Brutally difficult even with driving aids with no tutorial whatsoever. Be prepared to restart races A LOT because small mistakes will throw you off your bike, and there's nothing in game to learn you proper riding techniques if you don't know them already.- The AI is challenging, but has zero sense of self-preservation and at times kamikaze. They'll divebomb you relentlessly if you leave a gap, and sometimes drive right into the back of you. They only rarely avoid incident, and as a result, you are restarting races A LOT thanks to kamikaze AI.- The difficulty curve in the missions/career is very harsh. The first license test in the American tree is a time attack on a 300CC bike, that's gentle enough. But within a few license tests you're strapped onto a nervous 1000CC street bike and expected to blast across VIRginia Raceway. It takes a lot of trial and error, and again, you're not given any guidance.- Only a handful of sub-300CC bikes, whilst they're not exciting to ride compared to 600/1000CC bikes, it would've been nice to have more 'beginner' bikes. Conclusion: It's pretty much THE game if you love to ride bikes and want a game that lovingly recreates speed machines both young and old.BUT the game is harshly brutal to the point of frustration, it expects you to learn everything yourself and doesn't have a tutorial or a good license system that teaches you the basics of riding. So it's hard to suggest this game to people either prepared to do a lot of trial and error to learn riding, or people who know riding techniques.TL:Dr - Dark Souls on motorcycles

_childDocuments_.review: While at first I was unsure, this is definitely an improvement over Ride 3.Pros:-Fantastic handling model with great tire feel, probably the best motorcycle sim out there at the moment-Better motorcycle models (both aesthetically and in terms of physics) with properly functioning dashes (Ride 3 had tons of bugs with dashboards like needles that would sweep wrong or in the case of the Paton S1R street bike was just the wrong texture altogether)-First person view is more immersive than everCons:-Home screen doesn't have as much personality as Ride 3 (used to be a loft apartment/barn with character, now it's just a sterile generic garage, feels like a step back).  Various challenges also lack the personality of Ride 3.  Then again, if budget had to be cut in one area, may as well be there.-License tests are BRUTAL for a new player and is generally harder than the actual races.  Very similar to the old Playstation 1 Gran Turismo titles in that regard.-Far fewer bikes with a stronger focus on sport and race bikes.  I'm not opposed to the race bikes, but I liked how Ride 3 had a lot of variety in bike types that seems to be mostly missing from Ride 4.  DLCs might help fill the gap later.-You have to pay $5 for the credit multiplier to not be stuck in a credit grinding hell.  Better than having to pay for credits outright, though, I guess.-The Paton S1R is 600,000   Just because I want to ride the bike based on my street bike (Ninja 650) shouldn't mean I need to pay multiple times the price of top-tier liter bikes.  If you want the best 600cc class bike, though, yeah, it's the Paton.-AI is kind of inconsistent, it's brutally hard in some races and a joke in others.Overall, if you want the best motorcycle sim possible with really well done physics and immersive first person perspective, this is the best you can get.  Let's hope future updates expand the bike list to include more variety and they tone down the license difficulty to avoid turning off casual players.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally I can actually race!This is the first milestone game I have played where I have enough confidence with the bikes to be in full control of where I position it and how I set myself up to either attack or defend when at the limit.  In previous titles I have generally felt that I was requiring too much concentration to simply nail my lines and changes of direction which often led to either late braking lunges on opponents or simply barging them out of the way, however with Ride 4, the physics inspire just enough confidence and the controls allow for just the right amount of finesse to give me the ability to make passes which resemble a rider who isn't constantly on the verge of a wheelchair.That's not to say it's without fault and there are a handful of larger changes I would like to see but it's at the right point where it's at least great fun to race, and that's what needs to be the major goal.Pros: • The graphics and level of detail in both bikes and circuits is impressive• Performance is very good on my system and I have had zero issues with stuttering or general performance issues• The physics on the most realistic settings feel good and inspire the right amount of confidence at the limit to allow the player to race properly (but there are some changes I'd prefer as listed in the cons)• The career mode content is immense and gives plenty of variety to keep it interesting• The selection of bikes and circuits in the base game is solid and the circuits appear accurate Cons:• The sounds could use some beefing up and I feel they lack "bite"• Some physics could use improving, such as strong front brakes, a quicker change of direction at slow and medium speeds, the grip in wet conditions is too high and inside curbs often feel too slippery in dry conditions.• The trigger rumble on my Elite V2 is very weak and should be increased to improve braking feedback in particular• The AI although not terrible do silly things and often react too late to the player when it comes to avoiding collisions and as a result, I would like to see an option to turn off player collisions with AI at the cost of credits in career events.• The ragdoll and general crash physics are poor• DLC content on day 1 which really should have been in the base gameOverall I am having a lot of fun with it and I would recommend it to those who enjoy the actual racing aspect of these games.

_childDocuments_.review: I would compare RIDE 4 to Assetto Corsa. You can play alone, time trial, and unlock all cars, it is possible to never play with anyone else, and still have a lot of fun. However, at a simulation level, this game is still rough in the edge like a notch below assetto. Riding at the limit in real life, means there is some clutch friction limit, some dribble limit on heavy front weight shift and some feedback from the front end in deep braking. In this game, it is not there, like you are on some sort of rail, when the front end goes divergent due to lack of front grip, it is overly punishing because the front end does not communicate anything at all. Also, a bunch of motorcycle aren't there, Buell? R1100S? K1300S? K1200R? Lambretta? DKW? Niken? Royal Einfeld? BSA? Cagiva? Am I neat picking? I am not sure, there has never been a motorcycle game like this. It is way above TT isle of man 2, which seems a little bit more arcadey if that make any sense. If you get the game, I really strongly recommend you to try the RC390 racing edition. It really is an eye opener. I wish KTM made a 2 stroke out of that chassis. In Laguna Seca, I haven't been able to go sub 1:40 seconds with this bike. It is possible,  I just cannot see the line, you almost never brake and you almost go full throttle the entire track. BUT I AM DEAD SURE IT IS POSSIBLE, even 1:39 should be possible. What a bike. Also, the FZ1R yamaha brakes on that track feels so inadequate, since I never rode this bike in real life, I can't know if it is really that iffy. Whoever owns this bike, you are the devil! How are you still alive? So I spent 10 hours on 1 track, and I got to say that the tarmac is dead on accurate, just like real life, I know it like the back of my hand for my skill level, been there tracking a couple of times.In 9 hours of game, I was able to unlock:-Ducati 916, 999R (divine), at some point I will get the 1098-Honda NSR250R, NS400R, NSR250-RM, I cannot for the life of me prioritize the VTR 1000 SP1-Kawasaki ZX-7RR (almost feels like the real one)-KTM 390R, 390R-RM, Duke 790-Suzuki GSXR1000 (the brakes are good, allows you to go really deep)-Triumph Street Triple R (what a let down, the bike in itself, really feels like a piston is missing)-Vyrus 986 M2 STRADALE (amazingly boring to drive)-Yamaha YZF-R6, FZ-1N (WTF brakes!!!)I could stop collecting bike right here and there, it is already too much fun on just one single time trial track. In the end, you can tell I am having a lot of fun. I haven't raced yet, just time trial, I can't wait to Suzuka and Donington... It is missing so many amazing French and Italian tracks though, Magny-cours Mugello and Imola are there! but I am not so sure about le mans. I am motorcycle curious, and this game cured me of anything above 1000cc.

_childDocuments_.review: Games as enjoyable as previous title and a great step up in many of areas over the priors. The bike selection is as great as ever, with all the little details re created to the T. and with the good ole editor, anything is possible with customization, and now with helmets and gear as well! The physics in this game are excellent in my opinion, I know this is where some reviews say they got it wrong, but I cant imagine any way they could have gotten it more realistic to what actual riding feels like. The main thing I thing throws people off, is the perception of speed. Its hard to get the feeling across that you are flying at 170 MPH, and still see what it is you are doing, just watch your speedometer in game, your ride is booking it, but visually it does not seem like you are going as fast as stated, so when you try to make that turn at 80 - 90 MPH of course you are going to over shoot your turn or crash, the only way to make to corners in the game is to slow way down, down to where it feels like you are going very slow visually. but if you look at the Heads up display, you are still going 50 or 60 around tight turns, which in real life is crazy fast and thrilling, you just dont get that visual feeling of going fast, so at the start, you will want to bullet around the entire track, when you need to slow down, take corners at a relastic but still agressive speed, and work on your throttle control and cornering angles. I will say if you are looking for the most realistic all be it way harder physics in a riding game, try Moto GP 2020 or 2021. they defiently feel the most realstic due to insane control on the players part on throttle control, and a bunch of other factors like rider aids. but for a more casual experience ride 4 all the way. I can dumo hours into this game, learning tracks, editing bike and gear, or just riding the endless amount of bikes to pick from. the only grip I would give this game are, the rider licence challenges at the start, and some of the endurance racing problems like not being able to choose rain tires in the middle of the race, if it started out dry. they may have fixed this issue now since I have the game on PC months later, but if not that was always a issue. but all and all 9 out of 10 in my opinion. cant wait to see what they come out with for future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Best bike game, but AI sucks. Ride 4 is like Forza 5 to Forza series. It's better in gfx in physx than previous game, but has a lot less polish and content. Still Time attack at night at you fav track and fav bike is very cool expierence.Some fixes for this broken game:FIX: Ride 4 g-sync Stuttering (Microshtuttering, tearing, freezing)To fix stuttering in Ride 4 when using g-sync you need to turn off v-sync in game and innvidia controller set vsync on and frame limiter to your monitor refresh rate minut 5. For example i play with 3440x1440 75hz so i set te limit to 70 fps and now the games super smooth even when turning.---FIX: Broken helmet cam on 21:9 resolutions.On 3440x1440 helmet cam is cut out and on loading and career screen you see some ugly things? You can fix helmet cam with this mod. Other 21:9 bugs have to be fixed by the devs.The is unoficial fix for broken helmet cam ---FIX: Easy boring handing after patch. How to disable TCS and AW?Even with pro simulation handling you need to turn off assists like TCS and AW in game. When riding press side d-pad button to change settings from "3" to "0" on all assists. Default values where change in latest pacht that's the reason for broken handling.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth getting? Yep for sure, it's a truly great game with so so much content (you'll be there for like 1000 hours to complete every race)Is this beginner friendly? Still not really, as in there is no hand holding and you do still have to pass a time test to get started, with further career races are license restricted; but the tests aren't really too hard and getting bronze times suffices to "pass"Overall though it's a great game to play and one that is rewarding to get the hang of. _childDocuments_.review: I think a lot of people's expectations were just comparisons to Ride 3, and MotoGP 20. I don't blame them, but after a few hours of Ride 4 I think is a great step forward in terms of realism, and dynamics. Yes there are some features that I wish were in the game like customizing the riders body positioning, and more lower CC bikes, but it makes up for the dynamic weather, bike physics, and tons of modes.  If I compare Ride 4 to MotoGP 20, GP20 does have favorable gameplay because although it was difficult to understand how the bike functions the bikes were inertia machines. You almost had to be precise, and smooth when coming into and out of a corner, as with Ride 4 it's just turns in, and comes out. What Ride 4 does well is having tons of race tracks from all over the world. I have been complaining about the lack of tracks and I finally get to race on some international circuits that weren't previously in this series. The bike characteristics, and dynamics are very realistic. The bikes wobble, and slides around and it makes my heart jump. I would recommend this game to anyone into motorcycles. It's a great game! Give it a try and put some hours into the game!

_childDocuments_.review: So my opinion as of 5 hours of playtime.Nothing but good thing all the way upto reaching the Stock 1000 cup, the game plays pretty well on any bike sub 1000 with the usual 'Ride' arcade like TCS but I am now used to this having owned all the Rides, this one definitely feels the best to play.So now the bad parts, I have genuinely considered refunding this game in sheer rage, the usual borderline impossible time attack challenges still exist and hit you within 30minutes of loading the game up.... This can be extremely frustrating, especially as you require golds in all challenges to receive the reward.600 and smaller gameplay - Flawless, 1000cc Gameplay - Impossible (Or I just suck??)Sounds - Massively improvedClutch? - What's the point you can rev a 1000cc bike to the redline with AW off and no TCS on and it does literally nothingSlow speed turning - Non existent brick like physicsAI - The AI seem to put in the same lap times whether its dry or wet.................... FRUSTRATINGBugs? - I haven't encountered a single bug throughout my 5 hours nor a single crash, lag or anything of the sort.So now the main event, you've just saved up 350k Credits to buy the bike you've been eyeing up (Panigale V4R), you finally load in expecting the bike not to handle like a brick like literally all the other bikes you've ridden before have.... You're massively dissapointed, you can't even make corners on the 1000cc bikes braking 25metres before the brake markers, and when you do finally make a corner you either get rear ended from being forced to brake too early or you lose a stupendous amount of time. I am playing the game on minimum assists - I tried joint brakes to see if this solved the issue, no it just made it worse. The game is currently set at 80% difficulty of which almost all my races pre 1000 were either decently competitive or I was 3/4seconds ahead. In 1000s I am 3 seconds behind on the first lap getting blitzed by everything.... even ducati 1098s and so on.I am writing this having just alt-f4'd the game.Do I recommend the game - Yes definitely it is a better Ride 3 with lots of cool new content, but this recommendation is purely in the hope that either I am doing something completely wrong or they fix this stupid inability to race 1000s on a higher difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: How about a positive review from someone who's played for more than 30 minutes and isn't complaining about how hard this is.This is the Dark Souls of the biking world and one to be mastered. Do not expect to ace every race - Practice and learn the track. You are on 2 wheels, bikes handle slightly different to Mario Kart so for all you whinging numpties who cannot keep a bike upright or even understand the physics of a game like this you should possibly look elsewhere.I am playing with an Xbox One controller using the realistic setting and have no issues at all, TCS off allows complete control and have managed to drift around many bends during races, this does however kill your tyres so be warned.Its tough, but the most enjoyable game i have played for ages in this genre - Coming from Moto GP, TT Isle of Man 2, Ride 2 and 3 this is stunning and one i will be sticking with for the foreseeable future.Handling is on point, tyre wear is a real factor and one not to be ignored. Push it too hard and your final couple of laps during a race will be an absolute nightmare to complete. Visuals are beautiful in 4K HDR and each bike has its unique sound which when pushed to the limit will give you the ultimate feeling of speed.If you like a bikes, like a challenge and enjoy taking the time to master each track then this is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really have a love-hate relationship with Milestone and their Ride games. I've dumped over 770 hours into the Ride franchise, and have played from the original up to the current release. Every iteration of the game seems to build a bit on the last, but also takes away a bit as well.I feel like with Ride 4, more was taken away than given from Ride 3.Graphics:The visual definition is outstanding. Especially on the bikes. You can tell these bikes were completely re-made and not just port overs. The textures and materials are absolutely top notch. A suede seat looks...just like suede. The tires really look like rubber. They definitely hit it out of the park in this department. Milestone giveth.The track environment is also a step up from Ride 3, especially in terms of the track lighting, and the full time\weather variations. Also good to see some additional favorite tracks of mine like Suzuka, Tsukuba, Road Atlanta, and VIR.That said...there are a few details lacking. No 3D grass anywhere really...just grass texture. Trees don't look all THAT great. Also, no dirt or scratches show up on your bike when you crash. Kind of a bummer. Camera views are also kind of odd. Onboard helmet view is very stiff, and just seems wrong. The visor is also always covered in filth. Milestone taketh away.Physics:This one is tough. On the one hand, it's good to see Milestone is pushing the boundaries of what you can emulate motorcycle riding is like in a game. It's also nice that they give you a lot of options to tailor the difficulty of the new physics engine. However, I feel they've gone a little over the top. Mainly, the grip of the bikes. According to Milestone, at ANY lean angle, with ANY 600 cc and above bike, it will break a full slick loose on a dry track under acceleration. I know this to be false, as I've done track days on a 996 Ducati with street tires. Plenty of times I came out of slow corners, piled on the power, and never worried about the rear coming around. I've followed a friend lap after lap on his Ninja 636, and not once did the rear tire break loose. I get what Milestone is trying to do, but there's a difference between actually trying to create a realistic riding experience, and just making making getting around a track more difficult.Ride 3 had a pretty good balance, and when the rear broke lose, you knew it was because you were actually pushing the bike too hard. Another thing I preferred with Ride 3, was the braking. Mainly the vibration. In Ride 3, if you were at the edge of grip on the front tire while braking in a turn, you could feel it. In Ride 4, you just get vibration whenever you touch the brake. That's all. It's like the brake discs are warped. No feeling of what the front tire is doing until you're already on the ground. Milestone taketh away again.Sounds:So far, I'm fairly impressed. The R6, for example, wails beautifully from 600cc's. The increased wind noise is nice, however there are some bugs with the audio. If you have to restart a time trial, you'll get a looping gravel noise for most of your lap until it goes away. Pretty annoying. As well as the time trials themselves...Gameplay:Oof. The time trials. Something that could have been implemented SO much better. You've got to beat a certain time in order to get bronze, silver, or gold. Pretty simple. Rather than let you hotlap until you can get your time, it's a one lap sudden death that ends as soon as you venture off track. And by off track, I mean 1mm off the tarmac. And rather than invalidate that lap, the event is simply failed, and you get a nice cinematic for 30 seconds before you can restart the lap. You'll spend more time looking at this cinematic than the track depending on how difficult you find the new physics.The AI, though touted by Milestone as a huge leap forward, seem...unchanged. The AI still plows into you with little regard for their surroundings. They will take NO action to avoid you under braking, in the middle of turns, or pretty much anywhere else on track. They also take strange racing lines, like hugging the inside of the front straight at Utah, instead of the outside, lining up for turn 1. However, they did seem to adjust the straightline speed difference of the bikes, at least giving you a fighting chance at tracks like Road America and Mosport...as long as you're not in a pack of riders. This all said, I am seeing a little more variation of the riding styles, and more mistakes being made by the AI, which makes for some interesting races.Details and content:The bike list is MUCH smaller than Ride 3. It sucks, but I get it. All the bikes have been completely gone over, and it shows. However, the decisions on which bikes didn't get included is odd. Hardly any Aprilias. Nothing older than the latest models. Only 1 BMW. Only 1 600cc Honda CBR. And worst of all, NO Bimota. My lovely DB8 is no more. Milestone taketh even more.Here's some more bad news. Bike modifications have been SEVERLEY toned down. You can no longer tailor your bike with various parts as you see fit. You still get exhaust and wheels options, but that's pretty much it. The rest are "kits" for your suspension, brakes, and engine. No more painted forks or brake calipers. No customizable mirrors, handlebars, triple clamps, levers, grips. They're all gone. Tires are now streets or slicks. No in between. I'm guessing this is all due to the fact that Milestone didn't port these bikes over, and they couldn't add all these features back in the time and budget they had for this game. You still get the livery editor, and it now extends to your race suit, and helmet! Milestone giveth!Then there's the bugs that will always be ever present in a Milestone game. They're not TOO glaringly obvious, and I've only been in the game for 7 hours. 2 things I've noticed so far, are some clipping issues with the exhaust on the R6, and the brake upgrades on the KTM 390 give you a second brake disc up front in the middle of the spokes. Basically, little things that Milestone didn't consider for different types of bikes by using the same model resources for everything.Conclusion:I want to like this game so very much. I know I'll drop hundreds of hours into it like the others, but I feel like I'm only doing so because Ride 4 is the only game of it's type. You're spoiled for choice in the auto simulation arena, but Milestone holds the entire market for bikes, so I must adhere to their library for my 2 wheeled kicks (Until Poyphony ever decides to make another Tourist Trophy...doubtful). However, although I know I'll play this game regardless of it faults, I can't recommend it for other people. Milestone needs to LISTEN to their fan base. The discussion boards for Ride 3 where inundated with bug reports, requested features, and suggested fixes. All fell on deaf ears, and Milestone simply gave us the same thing with a new number. A game with such promise, but let down by the little details. I'll give credit to Milestone for trying new things, but please STOP tossing out the old stuff that worked so well in the process.In the end, I can't recommend this game until Milestone decide to listen to their fanbase. I said the same thing for Ride 3, and it seems nothing has changed.Take this review as you will. It's 100% my opinion, and my observances of the game are based upon my experience with all 4 titles in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome motorcycle racing game. Much better than MotoGP series. I love the variety of the bikes and how many different options you have. The attention to detail in these bikes is truly breathtaking. I have owned and been around probably 30 of the models of bike in this game and can tell you they have it down and accurate more than any other bike game I've seen. The one thing I wish there was, is more customization. They allow you to upgrade the engine, transmission, chain, tires and a few other minor things. However, the limit of what parts there are, is where it lacks a little. For instance, you can tell they signed contracts with only 3 or 4 exhaust manufacturers because they only offer exhausts from the companies Termignoni, SC Exhaust, Arrow and 1 other. Where in fact like right now, I have a 2015 Triumph Daytona 675. The manufacturers that make truly nice looking exhausts for that bike are CS Racing, Yoshimura, Hindle and a few others, but none of those are presented. The 2004 Honda CBR 600RR and 1000RR, the Yoshimura was the most sought after pipe for that bike and it's not available. Two Brothers Racing is not in the game either. Also I wish there was some more customization like changing the windscreen, handlebar grips, footrests and rearsets. brake levers, headlights, taillights and etc. Other than that, I love playing this game and it keeps me going for hours if I'm not paying attention.One of the biggest reasons I am changing my review to not recommended is the AI. It is absolutely ridiculous and insane. I went through and beat the European series with all gold. No problem. Then I get to the Asian Series. The AI likes to slam into you and knock you off your bike or off track. But their speed is ridiculous. With almost all assists on and the AI difficulty set to the lowest, I can drop into a turn at say 50mph and think hey that's good. But then here will come the AI, taking the exact same line as you, not getting any lower than you, and they're coming through there at 70-90 mph. So I figure, hey next lap I'll do that. I go in at 60 mph and either go way out wide and off the track or the AI will come through even faster. Attention to detail on the bikes is amazing. Gameplay is Fu**ing ridiculous and unacceptable. _childDocuments_.review: - Graphically i think it's good, the rain in particular looks really good. Definitely better than Ride 3. - I do like the different HUD with the ability to alter the electronic riding aids on the go and the little tyre and throttle/brake position sensors. - The bikes sound really good and the modelling looks great, better than Ride 3 i think. - I like that the information on the bikes dash/dials actually reflect the real game environment i.e temperature and time. On some bikes the gauge screen even shows current lap time and assist levels, very impressive. It adds to the immersion when i switch the HUD off, especially on the longer races where the time and weather do change.- The bikes dials and gauges illumination looks really good, same as headlights and the reflections in water,  again better than Ride 3.- The menu UI layout is nicer in general, it feels more like a 'serious' racing game with it's lighter colour palette and softer electronic music. - The Europe/America/Asia career structure with world events adds a bit more of a journey to the game and there seems to be a few more tracks. I like the variety in race types and they finally got rid of drag racing.- The weather is much better, with the chance of it actually changing during longer races. Also, time passes (at an accelerated rate) which is also cool during long races.- The more simulation aspects to the racing add more depth to the game, such as qualifiers and setups, tuning and different tyre selections for the conditions and tyre wear. Of course this can be a negative, as it's not as arcadey/'pick-up and just play' as Ride 3.- Why oh  did they remove the ability to rewind during time trials, time attack and endurance races? It really helped beginners perfect the tracks ideal racing line and brake points in Ride 3, especially when a trial was particularly difficult. Why not make it an assist i can turn on or off?- Why does it finish the time trial after you've posted just one lap? Personally, the best bit about a time trial is racing round and round, slowly shaving time off every lap until you know the track better than the back of your hand and you hopefully post that gold medal time. Having the race end after one lap, telling me what i got and then making me restart adds so much time to the experience and breaks immersion and flow of learning the track.- The autopilot computer control of the bike before a trial actually starts is way too long on some tracks, it doesn't need to be like that if you have a couple of corners before the start line/trial timer begins anyway.- Some visual bike mods like handle bar grips and different mirrors are missing. Not a massive deal, but i did enjoy customising bikes and making them unique and my own. - The factory livery paint jobs now need unlocking with 'affinity', so if you don't like the colour when you originally bought the bike, but know it can be had in a red or blue factory livery, best get investing your time into unlocking those liveries! - They've simplified the performance upgrades massively, instead of all the different individual engine, brake and transmission parts it's all bundled into 'engine uprade 1' etc which takes away some of the depth of modification. Also a lot of bikes can't have the exhaust changed which was a visual aswell as performance change i enjoyed.- The learning curve seems markedly steeper than Ride 3, even with assists on. In fact, it's crushing. Even coming from the previous Ride game with plenty of experience, some of the beginner license challenges seem ridiculously difficult given you cant rewind time trials or tune the provided challenge bike.- Braking has been fettled with and seems to work differently from Ride 3, in terms of stopping distance and physics. The physics have changed aswel and whilst i appreciate the wobble and surface undulation changes under the bike, it can be quite frustrating when the game throws you into 1000cc sports bike challenges quite early on in the career. - The AI is STILL relentlessly on rails, knocking over everything in sight in pursuit of the perfect racing line. How they didn't program in some sort of awareness of the player or even other AI is beyond me, it was one of the biggest complaints about Ride 3. Constantly rewinding the race because i've been knocked off every time the AI decides i don't deserve to live anymore get's really frustrating.- I don't know how the racing assist line is calculated, but on some of the faster bikes it seems ... suicidal. It will tell you to brake way too late, you can wave at the apex as you careen straight into that wall. Sometimes the line it shows you isn't even a very good one, i suppose that does help finding your own. If that was intentional learning aid, well done but i suspect it wasn't.- Probably the most egregious crime in this game seems to be the DLC; there are bikes and a track in the standard edition Ride 3 that are now in DLCs in Ride 4 and to me, this is unacceptable. A game should build on what was before it and add more, not take away and then charge more for it. It also doesn't help that there seems to be quite a few bikes missing from Ride 4 that were in Ride 3, very disappointing. At least they still give away the free bike packs i suppose. I picked up the DLC in a bundle for £12, hoping that would encourage me to invest some more time into it but even with some extra bikes and tracks i find it hard to enjoy.Ride 4 has potential, but i find it way too frustrating as a racing sim to just chill out and enjoy. Ride 3 doesn't look as good visually, but it has more bikes and feels better to play for a filthy casual like myself. If you have enough spare hours and the patience to plough into this game then you could maybe get good, but it's a daunting prospect for a casual gamer, even for someone coming from Ride 3 with over 26 hours behind them. I've lost count the amount of times i've had to walk away from this game, even with assists on. I'd like to return to it at some point because there is some good racing to be had, it's just a bit hardcore for me at the minute and Ride 3 feels easier to hop in and out of after a long day at work.  Hopefully Ride 5 is better than this because there aren't many motorbike games about.

_childDocuments_.review: I applaud the physics engine, every single one of my crashes happened exactly the way I'd expect them to IRL. From low-siding into a sharp bend to high-siding on the way out or even the odd wheelie (not difficult on an R1M), they've modeled the ways to kill yourself on a bike to near perfection!I've seen a lot of people complaining about how difficult it is to ride with any semblance of competence in this game, and though that's true, it's not the game's fault. There's only so much you can do to make a bike rideable with two analogue triggers for throttle and brake, and an analogue stick for lean angle. Some things you just can't simulate, like the feel of the back wheel beginning to slide out from under you (and the rush from living to tell the tale!) or that hard knock in the bars from a bump bottoming out your front suspension. These are all things that we as riders learn to look for, recognise and react to, which are simply absent when you're playing from the comfort of your desk or sofa with a console controller. There's unfortunately not a lot the devs can do about that one, other than shipping you a bike, a racing track, a container-load of tyres and a fuel tanker.What's also absent though is any semblance of finesse, especially in the steering input. Simply put, your thumb just isn't that precise. You can learn fine motor control, and on a real bike that pays massive dividends (see comment about living to tell the tale...), but there's only so much you can do with the limited range of motion of an analogue stick, or for that matter - the triggers. I really appreciate the haptic feedback on the front brake, it's definitely better than nothing, but it doesn't make up for how badly the steering model works.That steering model is actually my main issue with this game. But first a short physics lesson for those who have never thought about it... Bikes steer by leaning. Simple, obvious, kind of scary when you're new, but you get used to it and learn to trust it. Most people assume that shifting your weight around is what gets the bike down, and doing 5mph in a car park - it does. But the faster you go, the more that bike just wants to stay upright, to the point where past about 30mph you could stand on one of the pegs and it would quite happily carry on in a straight line. Maybe start bending your trajectory slooooooowly... Past about 60 - forget it. So how do you get the bike to lean? You steer with the bars. Countersteer, to be precise. Put simply, you turn the front wheel the opposite way to where you want to go. Sounds counterintuitive, and it is, but think for a second about body roll in cars - you turn left, car tilts right. You continue going left, because the car follows the two front wheels, but the tilt is there for all to see. Well, on a bike it's the tilt we want, so we do the same thing - push the right bar, front wheel goes left, bike leans right. Same going the other way - push left, bike leans left. When you're going fast enough you don't even feel the bars move, you just feel the force, which is proportional to the lean rate. And it takes more when you're going faster. Once the bike is on its side, assuming your tyres haven't got flat spots (happens when you mostly go in a straight line), the bike will just stay there until you countersteer the other way to straighten up.Those last few parts are very important. They're what allow a rider to be extremely smooth when going around a bend. That part is also completely missing from this game's riding model. Actually no, that's not exactly true, they've modeled countersteering (you can see it happening when you turn at slow speeds), but they've then added a layer of abstraction on top of it which basically links lean angle with the analogue stick and there's no option to turn that off and have direct control instead.That's the only thing I really wish the game had, it would be such an improvement to the handling model without sacrificing any of the physics!In summary, if you're looking to learn to be a track rider, save your cash and get a real bike. This will never come close. It can't.BUT, if you're looking to mess about on tracks, crash surprisingly accurate models of real bikes, mod, do the whole racing league thing, and can live with the limitations outlined above - this one is as good as any. Just don't expect to be very good at it. Maybe I'll try it with a flight stick later, it's bound to be more precise than a controller's analogue stick...

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I gave this game a negative review. I was disappointed because the promo material promised dedicated servers and gave the impression that multiplayer was a big part of the game but when I went on to multiplayer there only 2 or 3 other players to race with. I'd suggest this might be because the game nudges the player towards the single player elements of the game and lacks any incentive to join online lobbies.I should not have written this game off so quickly. Let me explain why.The handling on this game is absolutely extraordinary. I've played a lot of bike racing games over the years but the ones that were trying to be realistic never had any warning before the bike suddenly fell down. That's not the case with Ride 4. With this game you can feel the tyres gradually slide and you feel like you can play with the limits of the rubber. It's a zen-like experience as you try to improve your lap times.Another strong point is the graphics. Not only does it look just as beautiful as the screenshots, it actually runs smoothly, never dropping below 90 FPS on my 5 year old i5 PC. I'm also impressed with the fast loading times.I enjoy the progression and upgrading the bike, saving some credits for new bikes along the way. It's something a lot of racing games miss out but I get Gran Turismo vibes when playing, especially as I try to get the gold medals on the time trails!The game isn't perfect and there are some occasional weird bugs but nothing game-breaking. The AI will sometimes ram you as other reviewers have pointed out, but if you keep awareness of the bikes around you, it is possible to avoid them.The online net-code is actually really good. There isn't the warping you often see in other games and the bikes around you feel very solid. I did take issue with the fact my bike had road tyres and everyone else had racing slicks. I wasn't able to choose the slick tyres from the menus and it's a shame there is no explanation about this. I'm guessing I need to buy the racing tyres in single player but there is nothing in game to tell you if this is the case.Overall I do recommend this game, especially if it's on offer, and it deserves a higher score than it has currently. I wish it wasn't a binary Yes or No, because it's kind of a 7/10 until they can improve the weak parts of the game. There are too many time trial challenges and it's almost as if they know the AI isn't great so they try to hide it away.

_childDocuments_.review: Ride 4 is probably the best motorbike racing game there is. The graphics are lifelike, to the point that people have mistaken it for real life footage in the past. The game has a huge selection of bikes, all of which are highly detailed and accurate, and they are also customizable, which is pretty cool. There's also a good variety of clothing options for the character, which are also customizable. As far as tracks go, there are quite a few options, with different styles of scenery and a wide variety of lengths, although it would be nice to be able to actually see the length in the track selection screen. One thing I will say is that because of the realism in this game, it is not easy. The physics are quite realistic, which is awesome, but it also makes the game a fair bit more difficult. Fortunately, the game has a variety of options to make things easier, such as the physics accuracy and a variety of driving aids and control simplifications, though even with these it is still difficult. This is the sort of game that takes a long time to get good at, and even longer to master. Expect lots of crashes (not game crashes) in the beginning. Normally I would play with keyboard controls wherever possible, but this game is much more suited to a controller, due to the added precision of the joysticks and triggers.Overall I find it hard to fault this game, because while it doesn't aim to achieve a lot, it does what it does really well. It is a difficult game to learn, but it is well worth it

_childDocuments_.review: RIDE 4:~~~~~~Back in the day, when I was young and invincible at 14 years of age, I started riding motorbikes. Most of my mates had motorbikes, and we used to ride them to go to school and to sporting activities, and then on the weekend we’d ride for hours just for the thrill of it; the feeling of speed and the sense of freedom you experience by riding a motorbike is truly special. But there is one thing you also need to be aware of that all riders have experienced. . . falling off; you never know when or how fast you’ll be going when it occurs! So, I was really excited to give RIDE 4 a go and enjoy the reminiscing.RIDE 4 is a motorbike sports simulation game developed and self-published by Milestone S.r.l. on the 9th of October 2020 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS4 and Xbox One.The game consists of Career and Multiplayer modes, as well as the option of choosing to race on all available tracks (Americas, Europe and Asia) and their variants (some tracks have up to 4 variants) without starting a Career mode.  My first impression of RIDE 4 was not really great. I found the game very difficult to play in the beginning, due to the fact that I had decided to jump into the Career mode straight away. And that was not the right approach, because, as I discovered,  you have to acquire a licence to unlock competitions and exhibitions. To give you an idea, whatever Regional League you decide to start with (Americas, Europe or Asian), you have to accumulate a certain number of points to unlock the first competition of that region. In my case, I went with the European league. I had to reach 72 points within 6 challenges, with three different motorbikes on three alternate tracks. It wasn’t easy at all, not only because each bike handles differently, but because you can’t have your wheels off the track at any time during the Time Attack challenge, otherwise you have to restart the session. And on the Track Test challenge, you accumulate penalties if you haven’t managed to go through all the flags at a specific speed and beat the clock to receive a gold medal and the maximum number of points. Each time you complete a race or a challenge you receive credits, which you can use to upgrade the motorbikes you own. As frustration was creeping into my experience, I decided to play individual races with the bikes that were available in my garage. It took me a while to feel comfortable with each of the bikes, but then I started winning races and accumulating credits, which I used to upgrade these bikes. Then I went back to the Career mode and funnily enough, I started to beat the challenges and unlock competitions and exhibition races. Then new bikes became available, and if I had enough credit to purchase that bike, I would go back to the individual races and start learning about how the new bike handles itself before I went back with it to the Career mode. My experience with RIDE 4 started to grow on me, and I am now enjoying the game. There are several camera views available in RIDE 4; I personally prefer the Onboard view (the one where you can see both of the rider’s hands), rather than the Third Person view, even though the rider animations in the Third Person view are fantastic while leaning to either side. The Onboard views replicate the feel of speed and the handling of the motorbikes far better than the other views, in my opinion. In terms of customisation, there are plenty to play with. The Rider customisation is really good, as you can choose his/her style of riding and you pretty much have the ability to change his/her entire outfit if you have enough credits to spare.In terms of bikes, there are 180 bikes from 18 different manufacturers that you can purchase at the dealership. You can modify 12 components in each bike as you see fit.   Regarding the level of difficulty with the AI, I strongly recommend starting with the conventional Easy difficulty, which is automatically set at 40% when you start the game for the first time. Then gradually move up the AI levels of difficulty. Same thing with the Driving Aids; keep the Simplified option on, then move on to Advanced or Realistic. Expect to be involved in plenty of crashes, but don’t despair, as you can rewind a fair bit to learn from your mistakes, or simply take a photo souvenir of your crashes and then rewind.I haven’t tested the Multiplayer/Online aspect of the game at this stage, and therefore I can’t comment on that specifically. I like the fact that you can set up the race in terms of weather and day/night cycles, and it is really easy to implement. I really enjoy the graphics and scenery in RIDE 4, especially with the unconventional tracks, such as the French Riviera; it’s pretty stunning, I must say.The gamepad is definitely my first choice in regards to the controls. I did have a few goes with the keyboard, and I was pleasantly surprised with the outcome.    Despite having been frustrated at the start, the game grew on me. I guess it’s one of those games that take a while to get used to, where only perseverance will get you through the first three to five hours of gameplay. Then you’ll see the light at the end of the tunnel and ride it through at full speed, screaming, “FREEDOM!”.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Fabulous Graphics all around (tracks, scenery, bikes)+	180 bikes to purchase and upgrade+	A significant number of tracks with some including up to 4 variants+	Easy to set up weather and day/night cycle per race+	Career and online modes+	Several camera views+	Good customisation (Bikes and Riders)+	Challenging gameplay+	Achievements and trading cardsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	The first few hours are extremely challenging, and frustration might get the better of you.RIDE 4: You truly need to earn the right to ride! When you do, it is extremely satisfying!7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

This game has a mix of RIDE 3's bike turn style in with the MotoGP20 kind of grip which makes it an interesting challenge for some who have never rode an actual motorcycle or understand the physics behind it. Bike won't really slide on most sub 400cc motorcycles like the R3 and RC390 but with supersports and higher it will.  It's not rocket science you just have to have throttle control and good riding lines and it will work perfectly.If you're aware of how motorcycle racers get even started in racing then you can wrap your head around this. There is a big limit on the amount of motorcycles available compared to the other games which really doesn't bother me because they normally do DLC packs for this. Now to many that might steer them away but there were free packs in RIDE 3 which it seems no one remembered in reviews of this game. I think it's to let the game live longer by dropping DLCs every so often that way people come back to use those new bikes. Just really a guess based on the 15+ packs they dropped for RIDE 3. If you don't like the sound of it come back after they drop 5+ DLCs but overall this game is an improvement in a Sim racing direction because most of the motorcycles act very much like their real life counterparts. _childDocuments_.review: I have been counting down the days for this game to come out, refreshing the steam page since midnight, and unfortunately now have to say this game did not deserve my excitement. I gave it a solid chance with the 2 hour refund window I had. Most of the time if I buy a game I don't end up liking, oh well, it will just sit in my library. Maybe it will get better with time. However the egregiousness of this game/developer... I couldn't stomach giving them my money in this case. The previous ride games and the hundreds of dollars of bikes cut out as dlc, and now this one with day 1 bike packs... all while the game is utter crap. They will milk you with this one too, make no mistake of that.So with that out of the way, the game itself. I'm not sure how this game made it through play testing. If it even had play testing... because I cannot imagine any play tester playing this game and going " Yep, go ahead, feels good. Ready for release." As I am now older, I can't tell you the last time a game made me frustrated to the point of feeling the rage well up in my chest, on a hairpin trigger ready to explode in a shower of controller pieces. But that's what playing Ride 4 felt like for me. I'm not sure what the intended control method was, but it feels like a dumpster fire with either keyboard or gamepad. The bikes feel like a brick on wheels. You are either up and down, or full lean. Trying to make fine adjustments mid corner is an exercise in futility. If you come into your line anything outside of perfect, you're either going wide, or over compensating and going narrow. As you lean into the corner, you have to hold the bike into the turn. Naturally the bike wants to stand itself up as you accelerate through. Sounds good, that's how bikes work. However, since the controls feel so brick like, this is where the crux of the game feeling so bad comes in. You just don't have a smooth range of control for lean in the corner. Since you have to hold the control stick over, and the bike is trying to stand up, you get into a situation where unless you are absolutely perfect with your stick control the bike goes into this back and forth wobble of leaning in and starting to stand back up. This completely unsettles the bike mid corner and throws your handling out the window. With that being said, one of the early things you'll be doing in ride 4 career is a time attack lap that you have to hit a number of speed trap gates around a circuit. Missing or being under speed through these gates adds .500 to your time. They are about 3 bike widths wide, sometimes positioned strangely off the racing line, and have absolutely no forgiveness on the edges. You need to be damn near dead center, with a bike you can barely control, and missing more than 1 pretty much means pause, reset, load, try again. This same lack of forgiveness was present in other modes as well. You touch the white line on the edge of the track, fail. You come a little wide and run onto the curb run off on the outside of a corner, fail. I am a motorcycle fanatic. I seriously eat sleep and breath 2 wheels. And 4 honestly. I just love racing and motorsport. I ride street, I ride track. I am also a long time gamer. I have a VR headset and wheel setup for sim racing. I know it takes some time to get better with games like these sometimes, and I didn't come into this expecting to be good right away. This was my first motorcycle "sim". I was just ecstatic to have an outlet for my motorcycle addiction while my bikes are all tucked in over the coming winter months. I really wanted this game to be good! Because I know there will be people that think I'm just being salty about being bad at the game, there is a difference between challenging and frustrating. When the controls feel this bad, in a game which the entire premise revolves around controlling your bike, you are far into frustrating territory. There are other things wrong with the game, but the control feel is just by far the refund factor for me. From Soft games are some of my favorite games of all time. I have completed multiple play throughs of Dark Souls Remastered on switch fully in handheld mode. I can deal with wonky controls when there are redeeming factors. But quite honestly everything in Ride, outside of the controls, feels aggressively average. If they just had thumbstick control adjustments, I probably could have tuned the feel to good enough to put up with the rest of the mediocrity for the sake of the bikes. Sadly, the game is just far too frustrating as it is and the business model far too greedy considering what you're getting. I have a back log a mile long, cyberpunk is on the horizon... I guess I will have to continue waiting for a true motorcycle sim, and youtube will have to do for feeding my motorcycle addiction this winter.

This mixture should make about 30 cookies.STEP 7Bake for 8–10 mins until they are light brown on the edges and still slightly soft in the centre if you press them.STEP 8Leave on the tray for a couple of mins to set and then lift onto a cooling rack.RECIPE TIPSFREEZING THE BISCUITSIf you’ve frozen the biscuits, take them out and arrange them on a lined baking sheet. Once defrosted, pop them in a medium oven 190C/170 fan/gas mark 5 and heat for 2-3 mins to crisp up. Don’t leave them too long or they’ll dry out.STORING DOUGHYou can keep the uncooked dough in a sealed container in the fridge for up to two weeks.
