_childDocuments_.review: Starting off, I am myself a motorcycle rider that do a lot of track riding, and my hope going into this game was more looking for a Forza Horizon styled experience (without the open world) more than a NFS one.Is the game good? Yes, if it is your particular kink. The game is unforgiving, it's got glitches/bugs and AI that can ruin your race. But when it doesn't do something stupid, it's my favourite motorcycle game experience out there. MotoGP fills the F1 2020 experience, and this is the Forza one. I do wish they would have carried over more features from MotoGP20 like 3 zone tire wear, engineers to set up the bike if you don't know how to tune and more options for riding styles. I get why they didn't do it, but it's what I really enjoyed in GP20. Tuning also really helps once you figure it out to make the bikes steer better/suit your style. Endurance races are VERY fun, if it's what you are into.The Pros:-It looks much better than Ride 3-I prefer the physics over the Ride 3 one (although, I like the braking in GP20 more, it's still a little "wooden")-Available bikes are fun and do feel like they have a little character to them when compared to each other-Tire choices (S/M/H)-Multiplayer is much more stable compared to previous titles, close racing is now possible-Editor is fun (finally shared stickers are back)-Added gamemodes + weather and day cycles-Track list is decent, with more tracks coming (hopefully free DLC)The Cons:-Earning money is slow, 5 euro DLC to what should be the normal earning rate-Bugs/glitches and an AI that can be a pain at times, the difficulty balancing with the AI slowing down on straights isn't great.-Bike list feels lacking in many areas-Steep learning curve will keep new players itching for the refund button-Some bikes ride horrible for no reason (see: every MV Agusta F4, Yamaha R1/M and more)-Sound on some bikes is underwhelming-Rear brake is almost useless, and very difficult to get working right-Difficulty system with AI isn't great, see leader bugger off whilst rest of pack is in slow motion-Upgrading system was dumbed downThis game isn't for everyone, it caters to those that know how bikes work and does very little to help the new guy get into bikes, that said, it wouldn't be as good if it was styled like an NFS game. It has done some of the homework to improve on previous titles, and the final piece is a fun game, if you are into it in the first place. It is the strongest Ride game available, and easier to sit down with than GP20 (and previous titles).For me, it is the best motorcycle experience available on a digital system (compared to titles like Ride 2/3, Isle of Man TT 2, MotoGP20).Update:A lot of the critique I see for this game revolves around the crude tutorial. Whilst I agree it is a very basic way of beating you with a sledgehammer until you understand the games physics and the way you play, I don't really see how it could be done better (except for the choice of bike, really should be something like an RC390 or R3, not an R6). If you look at "similar" titles like Forza Horizon, F1 2020, and other car racing games, they basically ask what difficulty settings you want (if even that) and then throw you into a race as introduction. FH4 (and other Horizon titles) straight up throw you into a Lamborghini of the faster kind and says "race to the festival, good luck!". The difference, and source of "annoyance" with Ride 4's intro, is that instead of crashing into a tree, backing up, and getting going again, Ride requires you to actually learn how to handle the game, before it throws you into the races, and the constant falling off invites a way of "the game is against me progressing" and frustration.Apart from changing the learner bike (and maybe track, Tsukuba is kinda technical, short version of Brands Hatch would be better), this is really the only way to learn the games handling model. It even lets you have tools to make it easier (3 or 4 settings of physics to begin with, ABS, Auto gears etc.). is it crude? Yes. But do you remember when you started learning to drive a car? You can't really slow down a racing game like you can a shooter to practise targeting, standing still and turning doesn't work here. The game isn't for everyone, but just like any other game, you walk before you run in this one as well, and I do not see people criticising Forza because "I haven't tried a racing game before, it's too difficult and I keep crashing". Neither do people jump into CoD and do 360 noscopes first try (is that still cool, I don't play those games anymore?).

_childDocuments_.review: This review was slightly negative after 5 hours, but I actually like it more and more, the more I play it. I decided to switch to slightly positive.In the beginning I though: oh no, another game that could have been a patch. Like in the previous games, the sounds are not great and the graphics are a bit outdated. Everything looks a bit too grayish and dull, which kills quite a bit of the immersion. But it turned out that if you change the weather, it gets a lot better.More importantly, the AI drivers are still extremely annoying and often crash into you, ruining your race. I'm not saying it's always their fault, but in other games more measures (maybe unrealistic) seem to be implemented to avoid this -- which in this case I would strongly prefer over the realism (I have no problems in Assetto Corsa Competizione or TT Isle of Man 2, and I know sim racing games and how to drive when others are around a bit). I really try hard to avoid them --  and I don't go full speed in the first 3 corners of course. But sometimes they just divebomb you in the middle of the race right before a tight corner and you crash.  In general, the racing is quite good though, but I prefer time trial to events with other participants. Everyone has their own opinions on the real racing physics, but I'd say: these are believable, and you can tune a lot.Pros:* it's a proper sim racer at heart* lots of things to customize and tune* mostly fun racing, official tracks* difficulty seems alright (see details below) and can be configured to your liking in great detail (both physics and AI difficulty, separately).* no annoying menu music, videos after races, etc.* plays great with a controller, default settings for the Xbox controller are almost spot on* it has NordschleifeCons:* the first time I needed to buy a bike in-game and clicked on buy, it opened a browser with the Steam DLC shop for the game: I needed to buy a DLC to be able to get the bike. FY.* mediocre but okay presentation* very similar to past entries in the series, with some of the same issuesA word on the difficulty:I read a lot of complaints about the game being too hard, but if you come from sim racing car games like Assetto Corsa Competizione or have played another motorbike sim racer or simcade game, it's definitely fine. I am by far not an experienced sim racer, but my 15 hours in the TT Isle of Man games and another few hours in other RIDE series entries made the difficulty seem very fair.Contrary to what I read in some reviews, where people said it was too hard to even complete the first few test events so that you are allowed to drive in a real race, I found it very easy to get the license for the first leagues. Maybe they made it easier since release? I did have to restart a few of the short events (1 lap each basically, very quick to do) once because I did not know the track variant, but that's it. E.g., the race at Nürburgring does not use the full GT track, and the resulting new corner caught me off guard.It is fair to say though that if you are new to motorbike games and to sim racing in general (e.g., you do not know the layout of some popular tracks and have only played arcade style games so far), then you will need to invest 10 to 15 hours to fully enjoy this. But this is true for any sim racing game. It's not a problem of RIDE 4.I give it a total 7.5/10. I have to say that the mentioned DLC popup really annoyed me to be honest. You buy a game, you want to buy your first bike, and it's locked behind a DLC. Just a very bad feeling. They should simply filter the displayed bikes by 'ones you can actually buy with your version of the game'. And no, even though there are many good filter options, that option does not exist.Verdict: 7.5/10. Get it on sale if you want to get into motorbike racing and do not own the other entries in the series.By the way, RIDE 5 is already there. I have not tried it, but most likely it will not be much different. The metascore is almost identical.

_childDocuments_.review: Ride 4, It's 4 Real!I highly recommend this game if you are looking for a racing game and are also a motorcycle enthusiast in real life!I played for 88 hours now but still there's a long way to run! I just unlocked the World league and surprised by a ton of events waiting for me to race on! What Ride 4 has to offer? Undeniably the best Physics!- The physics is superb! I find it so realistic in a way that you can feel the weight of the bikes, their acceleration, even their traction! Every bikes has their own characteristics! Spectacular details! - You can see every little details of the bike for you to mesmerize on. These beautiful masterpiece of machinery! Eye-catching graphics! - The graphics of this game is so surreal that there's already a video on YouTube that the viewers thought this recorded in-game footage is real life video recording via GoPro! How cool is that!A Ton of engagements in-game content! - At first, I thought that there are some missing piece in this game since it doesn't have an open world. But then again, you just need to unlock it in Career! Every bikes has their own "championship."- The in-game menu looks clean enough. It features you're bike with a footage showcasing how beautiful they are! - Huge variety of bikes to ride on! Character customization and Bike customization is a way to go! Tips for those who are seeking to play this game! - Start humbly, finish strong! Just like in real life, you must start with low cc motorbikes in this game in order to feel your progression!- Master the track! Learn every curve! - There's a riding aids and race setting! This is helpful especially for new players! - Lastly, learn to be patient! Just like in real life, champions don't win at a short period of time! They devote themselves with practice and master every track in order to win! A motorcycle enthusiast best gaming experience!

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best version of ride so far. 14 hours over 1 week and I'm having a blast trying to get gold on all the races. The Positive1) AI is excellent. Riding in a pack of motorcycles is amazing and feels like the real thing. The AI's riding varies from race to race, it doesn't feel like it's on a script anymore. There is give and take from you and the other riders. I've had riders block me out and I had to react by backing off. I've also had instances where I had the upper hand, taking the inside of a turn, and they had to back off. 2) Bikes look and sound awesome and don't seem to be recycled from previous years. I have owned two of the bikes in this game and I'm very impressed with how spot on they got things visually, audibly and how they feel being ridden. 3) The tracks look and feel great. No graphical hiccups and fps keeps up with my monitor's 144hz vrr. 21:9 is well supported which makes me happy.The negative1) The DLC out the gate is a bit much. I understand that the bikes were redone but maybe wait a month before you hit us up for more money. Also, where is the season pass on Steam? Things like this erode our trust in the product. 2) The rain on lens effect. Milestone, please add an enhancement to let us disable this. I'm really not a fan of gimmicky type of graphical enhancements like this. 3) Few bugs here and there. I had to disable the right stick on my controller because the dead zone appears to be way out of whack. Also, if you run off the road, sometimes the sound of gravel stays stuck on. Milestone is pretty good about fixing things though. However, if I wanted to put in bug tickets, I would go to work and make money doing it. We pay money to not have to do those things.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE:  Xbox player, moved to the PC - So I have around 50 hours in the game.This game throws you in at the deep end and expects you to learn the ropes as you progress through the stages.   It gets a lot of negative reviews for this reason, but if you stick with it and actually learn to ride the bikes its one of the most satisfying motorcycle sims out there.  If I could give one tip, turn off all the Riding Aids and set the Physics to realistic.   Just keep the trajectory "on for corners"This way every bike with have its own weight and unique feel.   For example, you will zip into corners on 300CC but will really have to pull the bike into the turn on 1000CC.   It's well worth the struggle to get a feel for all the bike classes in the game.  There are a ton of bikes.  I'm still discovering them!Honestly, give this game your time and it will reward you.   The Ulster GP and NW 200 tracks are incredible.  It's a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is realistic and while riding a motorcycle in the real world is fairly easy, racing at high speeds on a motorcycle is very challenging, difficult to master and very dangerous. Therefore playing this game is hard as nails but winnable for hardcore racing aficionados without racing aids and higher level of AI difficulty with to many hours of practice. It is also hard but winnable with much practice for casual players if you dumb down AI and turn some racing aids on. Think of it as a Dark Souls of racing games in terms of difficulty that is rewarding to overcome (much like Dirt Rally 2 in this respect). Although frustrating to play in the beginning Ride 4 is ultimately satisfying once you put in enough time to learn the intricacies of racing on a motorcycle. Many bikes and tracks are available to unlock and the game looks and sounds amazing. Very worthwhile to buy, play, master and enjoy if you are even remotely interested in motorcycles and can stick with it long enough to get good. If you can't it will be one of the worst gaming experiences you have ever had and a big waste of your money.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It looks shiny but it's so unpolished it's barely playable.I'm biased. I love bikes, I like riding on track and I like to play moto games during the down time in the winter. I really wanted to like this game but as it stands I just can't recommend it, especially if you are new to the series. Here are my main issues with the current iteration:- The AI is out for blood. It keeps crashing into the player. Playing with AI and without rewind to avoid them is damn near impossible.- The physics seem off. Bikes exhibit a lot of oversteer / a very loose rear end both under braking and under acceleration. I couldn't dial it out with a setup either. - To make the oversteer worse, the traction control doesn't function properly either. Even with TC and EBC on the highest levels the rear keeps loosing traction.- The game is very grindy. A race, especially in the beginning might earn you a few thousand credits, many of the more interesting bikes cost hundreds of thousands. The fact that there is a 'credits multiplier' DLC leads me to believe that Milestone did this on purpose. Combined with the day 1 DLC this leaves a really bad taste.- The whole fail, retry cycle involves way to much clicking and waiting for the autopilot to do it's thing.- It's very beginner unfriendly. There is no tutorial. There are no sane default setups. It just gives you medium/medium tires for every race unless you change them.BugsI encountered several bugs as well the most notable was a case where the 'autopilot' that runs at the beginning of a challenge just kept crashing the bike. Looks like the AI can't deal with the physics either.I really hope milestone will address these issues. This game could be great if it just got dialed in properly.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the fact that I like the "vibe" I get back from the Gran Turismo 5 days that is present in Ride 4. The goals to unlock, the fact that nothing is truely "given" to you on a silver plate, and the fact you have to learn. And learn a lot, IF you are not familiar with motorcycles games. I like bikes, I had a few back in the days, but road is too dangerous nowadays to ride any, so the game sort of compensate that itch.Basically the gameplay career idea is nice. But it's awfully done.I'll talk solely based on the career mode, as it's probably what a new player would want to play to get a "direction" and learn from the game. At least it's been what Gran Turismo, Forza Horizon, and many other game did.The devs wanted to try to give you a sort of "learning" tool by setting up "licenses" and that's good. What is absolutely awul is that it directly launches you in a "time trial" without even giving you any time to get the feel of how bikes drive in a more relax way. That could lead to an instant refund for any gamer that does not have the "need" to play a bike game.Then the game does absolutely NOT present you ANY of it's mechanic on what you can actually do with electronic assists that are set to the max to start with, and further more, I found it way harder to be able to "beat" those time trials, and even AI, with maxed diving help assists, as it simply "nerf" the bike too much, taking away the possibility to be a bit more aggressive. So my first few tries, I was totally unable to break hard enough, meaning I missed almost all my apex, was unable to accelerate when I wanted to, etc etc.The game became way more enjoyable with a lot of assists tuned down (or even off), and it's where I started to "feel" like driving a motorcycle. And then, indeed with a few tries, time trials became completable. A few more tries, and I could finally get gold.Yet, way too soon in my opinon, you are thrown into too powerful bikes for the need of your career, with not enough time to truely learn the circuits, and then more time attack events...For your license you are thrown into riding a specific bike for 2 events, then an other for 2 other events, and a third for the last 2 events. And that, with very different bikes category, both on style and power. Making it even harder to learn how to drive the circuits and / or the bikes.Now I understand that devs wanted to give you a way to ride various bikes early, and that is a good idea, but simply poorely executed. What will I learn when I jump from an underpowered 300cm3 sport bike to a way too powerful 800cm3 Road bike that is not really made for "racing" that I have to race and which is truely hard to control when riding at the limit to get those gold rewards ? and then you end up on a sport 600cm3.Basically the game does that. Throw you left and right without enough time to truely "learn" anything from it.All the time trials make it a pain to get the gold reward you may need (a specific bike) in order to avoid to buy it for your next step in the career. It's not like you are rewarded with a super prize for gold, and at least a basic bike for silver to get to the next step. No. It punishes you if you are not able to get gold.Don't get me wrong. I'm perseverent, so I got the gold rewards I needed. But in those days of instant gratification, I think the game had gone a step too far in the "elitist" direction.Then, all bikes have "electronic assists" available. Great... Conveniently enough the early game steps NEVER EVER teach you that. Once again, learning how to use them is also key on how the get more performance of your bike.Thanks game for NOT teaching me something as important as that. I don't expect a 1993 bike to have that btw... and yet there it is.Due to how Forza Horizon 4 throw you cars left and right, I had WAY more pleasure playing Forza Horizon 4 in the early hours of gameplay than what I had with Ride 4. Also, Forza horizon 4 let me choose what cars I wanted to drive for races, so I could learn the tracks at my pace, not forcing me to drive too powerful cars for my level at the early stages. Here it's so rigid, and so stupidely done, you are forced to drive way too powerful bikes way too early in your learning curve. Unless you decide yourself to play on specific races (ooutside of career then) at your pace, which is truely NOT how carrer should have you do it.Also, if memory serve, in Grand Turismo, you had that progression on tracks getting harder and harder. Here, it's way steeper, as you are quickly thrown into some quite technical tracks. Poorely executed once more.Basically this game gets a bad review from me, only due to it's progression, learning curve and TOTAL LACK of teaching you anything to HELP you passed that steep early learning curve. It's a game I would simply completely discourage any non bike riders/lovers to buy.When I buy a Forza Horizon game, I buy it because it has a large panel of cars and not only race cars. If I wanted an elitist car game, there are plenty others out there. I truely hoped that Ride 4 would do that, and I went for it, as I did not want a MotoGP or SBK "elitist" type of bike racing game. But I was wrong in my expectations, as it also tries to be in that "elitist" bike racing category.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I will give RIDE 4 a cautionary thumbs up. However, and make absolutely no mistake there, this game isn't finished, and if the DLC policy of RIDE 3 is anything to go by, you're financially most certainly better off just waiting for one or two years until a complete edition goes on sale for the same price as the base game currently is at release.Let's start with why I do kinda like the game and can recommend it IF you're willing to put (quite) some trust into the devs fixing a lot of things and don't mind putting some more money on the line for DLC bikes that were present in the previous game but are missing now for some reason, for instance the much revered GSX-R1000 K5 or the Ducati Hypermotard. That alone might be understandably a dealbreaker for a lot of you, so be advised that you're most likely gonna have to purchase them again as DLC in this game.Also, I'll freely admit that I am a bit biased and in the honeymoon phase right now, as RIDE 4 added not only my very own beloved GSX-R1000 K7 but also lets me customize my rider with gear very similar to the one I wear in real life. So there's that.Now, I did purchase RIDE 3 quite some time ago on sale with all the DLCs, but refunded it shortly after. Reasons being the physics feeling very off and the bikes not really providing a satisfying sound stage.And I am happy to say that in RIDE 4, the physics are much improved and the bikes now do sound meaty and aggressive, as they should. Some are off by a bit, like the new Suzuki Katana (1000cc K5 engine, which sounds like a 600cc at higher revs for some reason), but most bikes do indeed sound very close to their real life counterparts and, most importantly, they all handle in a believable fashion now.They feel alive and the rider's movements correlate with how you would imagine yourself adjusting positions.So there's no disconnect there, which is vitally important to me at least when playing a motorbike game. And after a short while of getting used to the controls, I was smashing the gold requirements and could nicely race with 100% (of 120%) AI setting.That being said, however, it is noticeable that these are basically the same physics as in MotoGP20, just with some MUCH needed throttle sensitivity adjustments, animation improvements, and of course applied and tuned to mostly street-legal bikes.RIDE 4 is actually very similar to MotoGP20, in many ways. Suspiciously so, you could say. And not all of them good, certainly.For instance, the AI. While they promised to be much improved, they seem to have the exact same, hyper-aggressive, dive-bombing behaviour from MotoGP20 to me. I have lost count of how many times I have been forced into a lowsider because the guy behind me decided to overshoot the apex in an effort to force the overtake mid-corner. Thing is, MotoGP bikes kinda have a lot more grip and handle much more responsively than a 2004 Street Triple. So while in that game, I could at least work around the suicidal AI maneuver, in Ride 4 this consistently forces me to abuse the replay function to not get yeeted into a wall.Oh, and also: The simulated tyre wear doesn't seem to count for the AI. This means that by the end of a 5-lap race in career mode, you're drifting around on completely destroyed rubber while the AI still maintain a clean line at consistent speed. This is infuriating, as it requires you to essentially block them during the last lap at least.By the way, speaking of MotoGP20 and previous RIDE titles, you now only have 3 riding styles to choose from. Balanced, Shoulders Out, and Oldschool. With Balanced and Shoulders Out basically looking identical except during maximum lean angles. You notice a trend here, yeah? There's quite a lot of content mysteriously absent despite the framework already having been developed. So like I said, I can only hope that we will get at least more riding styles, a couple more pieces of gear and some free bike packs over the course of RIDE 4's lifespan. Apart from this, I'll cut myself short:- The career mode is nice and brings me some Gran Turismo 4+5 vibes. Challenges, races, cups, for which you will be rewarded with bikes if you get all gold medals for each set. It's nothing to write home about though. Just nice, and will hopefully be added more content to in the future.- Performance is OK. It runs worse than MotoGP20 at maximum settings and suffers from some anti-aliasing glitches, but you can expect 60fps+ at 1440p on a GTX1080. I'd like 144fps though, at least the consistent 120fps I am used to from said other game.- I don't know why, but for some reason they still won't let you adjust controls properly. Namely setting deadzones, linearity or sensitivity for your controller. Like I said, the game handles fine, but it's unfathomable to see these settings absent still. - There are a lot of weird glitches. Touching the inside of a kerb might launch you off your bike for no good reason at all. And the ragdolls may break, causing your rider to spaz out floating in mid-air while your bike slides away. I don't know, this just screams "NOT PROPERLY TESTED" to me.- The UI is so simplistic to the point of being really boring. RIDE 3 was much better from my memories. At the same time, however, it is needlessly complicated. For instance, say you own both street tyres and race slicks for your bike. You have to mount them in your garage, and once you go to the track you cannot swap them out anymore. And only slicks allow you to pick between soft, medium and hard compounds. It's just annoying.Alright, thank you for reading all this if you got this far. You might be wondering by now why this is still a thumbs up. Well, like I said at the beginning, it's BARELY one, but one that I will defend with confidence as the foundation is there. And I am assuming based upon how much content RIDE 3 received (albeit the actual bikes obviously mostly paid content), RIDE 4 is still going to be worked on for quite some time.If, however, you are not a die-hard motorcycle fan or a fan of the series... Well, again, wait for a year or two and check on the game once more. The reviews right now are understandably mixed, so go from that.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant. One of the only games of its genre, fortunately a very good rendition. It plays somewhat like Forza, leaning more towards sim than arcade but noticeably less realistic than its brother MotoGP. The unrealistic aspects of Ride 4 improve frustrating areas of motorbike racing, particularly how unresponsive bikes feel and how easy it is to drop or crash the bike. Complaints many have about MotoGP.There are a huge number of bikes with a bias towards sport bikes, but the more sporty nakeds are also in the game. There are large and very noticeable differences between the different bikes, which fit very well with the reviews. My own bike, '08 ZX6R, handles absolutely identically to its real performance which inspires confidence. Upgrades can be added, setups can be changed, all make a difference. Similarly there is a very good number of varied tracks, many with multiple layouts. No complaints with the volume of content.My main complaint is with the tuning. On most bikes it seems like hard tires are required just to manage a 5 lap race, with mediums wearing out significantly by the end. Smaller bikes can happily drive forever with the softest compounds. This is a significant drawback. The campaign is functional (and long) but uninspired, consisting of a number of races on different tracks with different bikes to drive. A campaign with leagues or promotions, anything dynamic, would be a great improvement.Additionally transferring some aspects from MotoGP would be nice. The MotoGP mechanic makes tweaking suspension incredibly easy and largely automated. Upgrading bikes is nice, but having decisions to make would be better. Perhaps allowing a range of tweaks to improve low end torque vs pure horsepower. Or speed vs grip for tire pressures and sizes. Something to make it more than merely upgrading everything to maximum and leaving it there.Ultimately though I'm very glad to own Ride 4. I personally prefer MotoGP, but whilst waiting for the 2021 version I've been having a blast on Ride 4. I'd imagine most might lean towards Ride 4 as it fits between the feel of car racing and the feel of bike racing nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: RIDE 4 is my first bike racing game. I'm used to play car racing games and wanted to try something different. Already knew that it will be difficult to adjust to the characteristics of riding (brake much earlier, turn much earlier, accelerate much later), but after a few hours of trial and error I managed to get the hang of it. The European tracks are more difficult compared to Americans and Asians, so I suggest starting with one of the last 2 options. At launch, time trials were savage - a few centimeters off the track and the lap got invalidated - this has been patched. Bikes with high acceleration value are insanely difficult to control on certain tracks, and you can easily fall off your bike in certain places (like the back straight in Suzuka, in Virginia or certain parts of Nordschleife) if you hit a little bump on the track that is not properly represented in the track's visuals. Carreer progression is clear if you read everything in the menus. You don't have to do all races to make progress, only collect a certain amount of points in each category of events. Some of the qualifying rounds are too hard at first, but with a little patience all of them are doable - you can also adjust difficulty in racing events if you need to make progress faster. If I have a VR headset plugged in, the game boots in a fake VR mode, but there is no VR support - the whole image is scrambled and you can't even see menu items. Overall, the graphics are well made, sounds are amazing, and if you have the specs to run this game at high FPS it really gives you the feeling of a chill ride. The difficulty feels unfair at first, which is discouraging, but if you give this game another chance after failing in succession, it will thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been riding 600cc super sport bikes for many years. This game captures the speed, handling, feel, & braking (riding aids / most riding aids off) of a real bike. Your riding line is everything. Smooth riding, transitions, and throttle application is the name of the game. This all adds to the challenge.I use helmet cam view and a racing wheel Logitech G27 (with x360ce). I set the wheel to 60 deg rotation and centering spring to max. I can't get anywhere near the top 100 of the leader boards. Again I really enjoy the challenge of this game.The sound of the engines are perfect. I especially liked how they captured the sounds of wind in the helmet cam view (using headphones). Graphics are amazing. The race replay feature (rider helmet cam view) looks a like real life video. Especially in the rain / wet. Game has ran smooth for me with no bugs (GTX 1070 8 gig). I don't bother with the career mode. Got tired of the AI randomly dive bombing me in the corners. I just do time attack and learn a track. To get money fast. Get the credits x2 multiplier downloadable content add on (wait for a steam sale), do the weekly challenges (found in the in-game menu). Bronze lap time 400k, silver 700k, gold around 900k. I lucked out with a track that had a lap time of just over 1 minute (short track). Kept getting gold lap times. You can do this over & over and buy all the bikes you want.Great selection of bikes. They all have their own handling dynamics. As mentioned in other reviews, this game a sim style game not an arcade game. It takes lots of work and patience to get good lap times. Especially the Nordschleife.

_childDocuments_.review: As of May 2021, most of the major bugs have been ironed out. Headlights work as intended and the Wet weather tyres can be selected in the pits when it rains. Time Trials are far more forgiving now, better than ever. Physics have been dumbed down a little but it is still challenging. Optimization seems to have improved, as I can run it without much trouble on my GTX960M.Coming onto the game itself: 1.) Endurance aspect in this game is very well done, it is as real as it gets, for the time being atleast. The atmosphere around the track is really decent, and it is an experience watching the sunset/sunrise and witnessing the track lights come alive. As someone who has spent good chunks of time driving Assetto Corsa, Project Cars 2 and Automobilista 2, I am used to racing without using the REWIND feature which seems to be missing from Endurance Races. In my opinion, it is for the good because it makes you take calculated risks. 2.) The Career Mode is varied. There is lots to do, but outside of the Endurance Events, most Career events (Short Races and Time Trials and other sorts of events) lack Fuel Management. Not a big deal because you won't be in the need of managing the fuel while doing Time Trials. 3.) The Photo Mode is amazing. In terms of functionality, it is very similar to the one that you have in Project Cars 2 or AMS 2 but with far more intuitive UI and optimization. Lots of options to mess around with, and the photos are guaranteed to look amazing.4.) Time Trials, this time around the Time Trials are far more forgiving, from what I've noticed. In the previous games, for example RIDE 2, the track limits were way too strict but seems like they fixed upon that in RIDE 4. 5.) People seem to be complaining about the difficulty, particularly that of the acquiring the licenses. In my opinion, if you have some experience with motorsports, it wouldn't take long for you to figure out the racing line and how (at what angle) you'd be attacking the corner, which will translate to faster lap times without exceeding the track limits. As of those who are new to track racing, you'd probably have to understand some of these concepts before the game seems forgiving. Personally, I enjoy the challenge that we have in here.

Track selection, Suzuka and Mugello have been added. NW200 is missing but licensing issues are understandable.The bad:1. Bugs, sound bug in many low revving bikes between 6 and 7 K rpm. _childDocuments_.review: I bought ride 4 after playing ride 1, i never played ride 2 or ride 3 so i cant compare ride 4 to those games, but compared to ride 1 this game is exponentially better. not only the graphics and sound quality, but the gameplay too, i think people dont like the fact that ride 4 is more realistic than other ride games, for example; people say the ai is terrible, well iv watched videos of ride 2 and 3, and u could basically ram into other players and not fall down which is so unrealistic and boring, and in this game u have need to be carefull when you overtake someone because unlike the other ride games, ramming into someone will actually cause you to fall down instead of just scratch them and keep going. this is why it feels so rewarding to overtake someone in this game. Another topic people complain about is the time trial penalties. if u go outside the track, chances are that, that wont be your best time anyway, so it doesnt matter if it counts or not, on the other hand if you're just trying to speedrun the game and you dont care about getting the best possible time, then dont complain about the penalties, because the game is meant to be played in such a way where you should strive to achieve the best possible time, instead of just beating the level and moving on (because that makes the game boring). _childDocuments_.review: I like it, mostly.On realistic the bikes feel good to drive. The simulation/gameplay itself is good. The tracks are good.But IMO there are several game design issues that make career and other modes unnecessarily frustrating and unfun.The game feels like it has built-in "sleep(5000ms)" code between way too many things, and several races/challenges have you waiting for 10+ seconds between clicking restart and the restart actually happening. It ends up being a lot of waiting. Even with good racing it becomes boring when every retry is spaced out that far.If the devs can do a few things to fix this, go through the game and remove as many unnecessary wait-times as possible (for example the one after completing a race, where you have to wait 5 sec to proceed to results with the option to restart), and also shorten the wait for annoying Auto-Pilot starts by 60-70% and change the counting up of "Your Time" on Time Attack to have no animation, just be instant. Then I will change my recommendation.By the way, in this game you have to be quick and precise as ♥♥♥♥ to succeed at all, which I've started to get into after 3 days of playing. Bronze tier on challenges and racing against Easy tier AI is genuinely difficult. Not impossible after some experience, but definitely not easy. Not really holding that against the game though. Comparing these bikes to the cars in most racing games, it feels very high-risk high-difficulty high-reward. You also get the rewind function which is a really great tool, especially while learning.RIDE 4 proves to me that bike-racing can feel at least as good as car-racing. But it still feels a little incomplete. (also some weird UI choices in customization, and in the livery editor there is no mirroring option) I've done most of my hours in custom races, because career sucks. Personally I'd love these MC mechanics in an open world setting. Maybe even VR. Maybe even with guns, kinda like a modern (maybe Asian?) GTA IV Lost and Damned. But I'm guessing that's not likely since they're just racing focused.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it funny seeing all the people giving negative reviews because they claim the handling and steering are near impossible to learn. I don't think these people know how to ride a motorcycle or even know the basics. When you figure out that the "steering" in this game is actually just shifting your body weight to account for a higher lean angle, the game becomes much easier. Don't be the guy who leaves a negative review because you can't understand the physics of a motorcycle and expect this to be another car racing game because, at the end of the day, it's maybe the best moto game on the current market, even with "Ride 5" being released.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the absolute GOAT game when it comes to motorcycles. It shows I have <2hours played at the time of writing this because I switched over to PC from console but I had about 120 hours in this game on my PlayStation. This is the pinnacle of Milestone games. I own MotoGP 19 through the latest, MotoGP 22. I own Monster Energy Supercross 4. I own MXGP 2020. I also own a bunch of games by competitors such as Rims Racing and both of the Isle of Man Ride on the Edge games. I also happen to own Ride 3. Nothing, and I mean nothing, out of my motorcycle game library even comes close to Ride 4. The physics are a perfect blend of arcade and sim; it's not as unforgiving and unpredictable as the recent MotoGP games but its no Need for Speed of bike racing games either. The variety of bikes available is unprecedented. The graphics are gorgeous. All the bikes sound spectacular. The track selection is very diverse and is bound to please everybody. Overall, this is the most 'fun' bike game for me.Sure, there are drawbacks but none of them are substantial enough for me to warn against getting this game if you're into bikes and bike games. Maybe they could have chilled with the amount of DLC, but hey, Milestone gonna Milestone. I got the complete edition for super cheap on both my PlayStation, and now, on my PC. If you can do the same, it will be money very well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended, the most important point, you must use the joystick control, and set the right stick up push to throttle control, can greatly improve your game experience.ride4 is a very interesting motorcycle simulation game. The difficulty is between motogp21 and ride3. There are not as many bikes as ride3 for now, but the graphics and photo mode are so much better than ride3. I enjoyed taking pictures of different brands of bikes.This game can only be controlled well with a joystick. Here are the settings for the joystick, which are very important.The throttle and clutch of a real motorcycle are very important, especially since they provide linear control, that is, the ability to have a large number of linear values between off and full on, and inside the joystick, the only 2 things that can provide linear control is the left and right joystick, the left joystick controls steering by default, and the right joystick, I highly recommend setting it to throttle control, and suggest setting the upward push to throttle so you can have a soft push instead of only being able to switch between off and full on if you use the default trigger setting.It's a shame there isn't a third button or joystick on the handle that provides linear control, otherwise it would be nice for the clutch to gain linear control as well.Also recommended to use the manual gear for a better experience.Enjoy your motorcycle life.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros and cons:+New and better handling model.+Graphics improvements.+Much better sounding engines.+Endurance races for the first time in Ride series.+Realistic cockpit view for all bikes.+New Tyre wear and fuel consumption features.+You can now customise your racing outfits,helmets and make stickers for suits in addition to customising bikes.+Being able to choose from 3 different tyre brands (Pirelli,Bridgestone,Metzeller)+New brands for rider gears such as Held,Taichi and Schuberth and more.+New tracks that had never been in Ride series and old tracks from previous Ride games.+Dynamic weather and time changes.+You can now use clutch for wheelies and other stuff.-There are less bikes than Ride 3.-Some most played tracks from Ride 3 are not included in Ride 4.-You can't change your bike's mirrors,brake pads and paint brake cables anymore.-It is disappointing that Kawasaki Z nakeds and Yamaha MT-07-09 are not included in Ride 4.Overall,i liked Ride 4 and enjoy it.It feels a lot more realistic than Ride 3 in terms of graphics and physics.8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to say but I wouldn't recommend this game. The game looks great and I can't really complain about the sounds (nothing has struck me as being god awful) but there are some downsides. The tyre wear model is ridiculous. I love having a challenge and I can definitely see the change it's made with my riding on the game. I've become a much smoother rider on it but that doesn't stop my rear tyre having 75% tyre wear at the end of the FIRST lap of a race. It feels like the AI are about 200kg heavier than the player rider with the ease at which they can push you off your bike. The time trial career events are so anal that even a slight excursion sends you back to the event menu to restart the event to then wait 30 seconds to a minute whilst you watch the auto-drive get you into position. The timed gate events turning off your racing line if you happen to rely on it (good luck with those events).I feel the devs could change my opinion with a couple of fixes but it looks like they're too busy pumping out DLC*, such is the way of a modern game dev. Stick with RIDE 2 or 3 and you'll probably be sorted.*To buy all the DLC is now more than the actual game itself so it seems I was right on this.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start with some of the things that i find are disgustingly bad. The AI acts as if you aren't even there. They have no mind for you and if you are in the way of their line they do not care one bit and will plow straight through you to get to where they want to go, and that is their line. They also love the inside line, so cover that with all your might. You still will have that one AI that will take off a disappear from the pack to never be seen again just like how you had back in Ride 3, still there. The handling is genuinely trash. It is so bad that i doubt that any of the devs have ever ridden a motorcycle. It feels like you are riding a 3 ton cow with a front end that is controlled by a tortoise. It is literally impossible to get the bike to turn into any of the turns that you will try to get it to go into, unless you brake super early, which brings me into my next point. I have noticed that none of the braking points that i have from IRL work on this game with this games physics model. Im not saying that i am a good racer by any means, but I am damn sure that the braking points that i have should work, especially when im going into the turns with the same speed that I come into them IRL with. I have to brake SUBSTANTIALLY earlier in order to get the bike to turn in. There is a tuning option that gives you aggressive braking, and i have no clue what in the ♥♥♥♥ that does because i feel no change coming into a corner with that on vs off. The tracks look nothing like they do IRL. I have some decent time on Road Atlanta, and it looks nothing like how it looks in the game. The track has all sorts of pot marks and tarmac changes that just aren't represented in this game at all. Additionally, the track feels nothing like how it does. There are several bumps at Road Atlanta that are very apparent when you hit them and will upset the bike, and they aren't in the game. If you're coming here for realistic looking tracks, this ain't is chief. Bloom is ENTIRELY TOO MUCH and will blind the ♥♥♥♥ out of youSome good thingsSound design is pretty decent. Models are okOverall Textures are decentYea i can't recommend this game to anyone, not with how it is currently. If you want a good motorcycle racing game go play TT Isle of Man Ride on the Edge 2. Fantastic physics model, you can steer bikes, braking points work REALLY well, sound is amazing, and don't even get me started on how awesome the helmet perspective is. That is the most realistic perspective of any racing game, car of bike, that i have ever used.

_childDocuments_.review: First let me give you the "Bad News".This is long, so settle in.AI RACERS:The AI is absolutely terrible. They are all related to Stevie Wonder. Why you may ask? It's because they do not see you. They do not try and avoid you. They simply plow right throughyou or into you in a corner. They also purposefully go out of their way to block you or stimmy your progress up the trail of motorcycles. I have tested this numerous times. I am coming up very fastand for what ever reason the bike on the other side of the track will veer over to either causeme to him or hit me. This is especially apparent on the start of the race. I have tried going left, going right, staying in the middle, and it does not matter they will always try and block you. They will even slow down mid corner causing you to run into them. And I mean practical joke slow too.THE BIKE & LIVERY EDITOR:There is a game out there called Forza, you may have heard of it. They had this same editor for over13 years. Milestone copied their homework or contracted the same company who built Forza's, and then jacked it up.When you place a sticker or shape it will translate to the inner surface. If you place a decal on the front of the bike, it will project on every surface at the position you placed it. Meaning the airboxcover, the back of the tank cover and the seat pillon where you butt settles in at high speed. You putanything on the top it will telegraph on the underside of the subframe cover. When you place a decal onthe left/right side and try and push it forward it telegraphs onto the front rock guard. So, it is virtuallyimpossible to make most liveries.You will not be able to recreate the MV Agusta 'Fecce Tricolore' at all. Notwithout extreme sacrifice of detail and accuracy. They should just release skin templates or separate each panelon the bike by:*Front Rock/Mud Guard*Upper Faring*Lower Faring*Belly Faring*Airbox Cover*Tank Cover*Knee Guard*Tail Faring*Swing Arm*Rear Rock/Mud Guard*Grips (We used to have this)*Triple Clamps (we used to have this) - and we should be able to buy aftermarket TC's and GripsThen just let up edit in 3D instead of picking a side to work on. Also a 'Warp and a Bend feature would be welcome. Your also not getting an opacity modifier which would have been very welcome. They can also make all the monchrome decalscolor-able as well. And make them for ever single decal they have. It seems this whole feature was just thrown in haphazardly. And editing suits is pointless. _childDocuments_.review: While I'm willing to recommend this, it's a decent motorcycle sim and I own a lot of them, there is far too much emphasis here on fiberglass and fuel injection, i.e. sport bikes, and far too much emphasis on grand prix circuits.I don't mind some sport bikes and grand prix circuits, they can be fun, but they shouldn't be the entire picture in a motorcycle smorgasbord.Milestone, who along with politicians everywhere has never learned life's prime directive, to wit, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it!" has inexplicably removed most of the traditional bikes and open-road type tracks that were present in Ride 3 and prior editions.That is why I'm taking a, "wait and see" attitude toward purchasing their new title, "Ride 5". If they add some traditional bikes and open-road course, such as the Triumph Bonneville T120 and Garda Lake or The Snake, I'll buy it. If it's just going to be a copy and paste of Ride 4, no thanks.So yes, I'll recommend Ride 4, but be aware of the content. And as far as the Harley Davidsons go, THOSE are the models that you chose to include, out of the entire history of Harley Davidson? You're off your meds, aren't you?And if Harley Davidsons really sound that way these days, I'm extremely glad that my last Harley was a Shovelhead with open drag pipes.So yeah, this is a decent motorcycle sim, but they need to include things for the entire motorcycle community, not just the skateboard and surfing set. Get it, but you should probably wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of this game. I love the emphasis on street bikes rather than Moto GP. I started playing time trials, and ended up getting a #1 (Utah west course) lap time. If you're into racing games, this is the best I have played. An almost hellish learning curve may be discouraging, but it made learning how to play this game so worth it. The game will start you with all the riding aids on, and I recommend starting that way. As you gain more experience, it is a good idea to begin turning things down, but if you were to start playing this game with no aids, then you will most likely not be able to advance in the story mode. That being said, precision is rewarded greatly. If you want your lap times to be competitive, you will have to eventually remove just about all the aids the game starts you with. Realistic difficulty with no anti wheelie and no traction control is the only way to start setting competitive lap times. Again, that's only if you're into trying to be the fastest. This game is plenty enjoyable for over 100 hours just playing the story mode. I highly recommend this game. I understand racing games are not for everyone, but they are definitely for me. I greatly look forward to playing Ride 5, which is coming out is August. Really fun game. 10/10 stars

The other racers are difficult but not too difficult to the point of unwillingness to play. _childDocuments_.review: Ride 4 is an overall good game. Good graphics, nice physics and a huge amount of races in career mode. However, before buying this game, there are some things that have to be taken into consideration:First of all, this game is NOT beginner friendly. Ideally, you have some experience in bike games. It is a "hard to learn, hard to master" type game. Once you´ve learned it, its pretty fun though. The AI is often reckless asf and will just run you over sometimes, which is ESPECIALLY annoying when you are in your fifth round on the last turn. I also saw the AI take turns on medium-hard difficulty which where, in my experience, impossible to even do with the rider physics. The grind in career mode is hard. You WILL fail a lot of times for said reasons, you have to be dedicated.However. if career mode isnt for you, you can still do time trials or single races. The only problem is that for racing your favorite bike, you will have to earn credits which you can only get from very hard weekly challenges or career mode. Aside from these things, it is an overall good racing game once you have mastered it. I am 70 hours into the game and not even halfway through the availabe content. For these of you who dont like to read:Graphics: 8/10Content: 8/10Story: No StoryGrind: 10/10Difficulty: Dark SoulsConsidered Difficulty: Fun: 9/10 for experienced riders, 2/10 for absolute beginners

_childDocuments_.review: An early review: I've enjoyed the challenge of the game so far, however not having played any Ride games before, I found it extremely difficult to learn how to play, and the lack of beginner support was very disappointing. The license tests were way above my skill level, and though I can't speak for others, I would imagine that they were above most beginners skill levels as well. (I did do the European license tests, which I have heard are the hardest ones, however imo the first races of the game should serve to teach you how to play, not provide challenge from the get go.) The only way I could learn how to play the game was hopping into a time trial on an easy track (I opted for Imatra) and just doing invalid lap after invalid lap until I was capable of consistently putting down valid times. After that, the rest of the license tests that I hadn't done were fairly straightforward, and took under 30 minutes of attempts each. Following the completion of the license tests, the game has been very fun, however my first 3 hours of playtime were torture, and it was a big struggle to learn how to play with such little support, especially since a lot of the difficulty options actually make the game harder, for example, even with ABS on, joint brakes apply way too much back brake, and until I disabled that, I was high/lowsiding into every corner.Overall, Ride 4 is a good game, however for the price tag it seems quite poorly thought out, and from what I've been told on forums, isn't much of an improvement from Ride 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not recommend in its current state. The AI is horrible. Everything else about the game is pretty good aside from some bike customization, but as of now the AI is making this game so boring, frustrating, and repetitive. The AI is just god awful. "ANNA" seems to be a sales pitch or something because these AI are the dumbest of any racing game I have ever seen. If you are new to bike racing games the AI will be challenging. Not in a very good way though as they are very aggressive. Once you get a hang of the games physics which are very good on this game, or if you are a veteran of these bike games the AI is a utter joke even on max difficulty. They are no challenge at all and do not give you a good battle that you would want in a racing game. You will be beating them by seconds even up to minutes on some road tracks. The AI really struggle with chicanes it seems and the road courses are unbelievable for the AI. The Southern 100, Northwest 200, and Macau races are just horrible for the AI. They constantly keep crashing and going into the walls or curbs, sometimes they even follow the next AI in front of them and they all crash at the same spot. The AI also seem to not be tucking in down the straights. Playing with manual tuck in you are able to blast past them down the straights even on a less powerful bike. Save your time and money either for a sale or when the game is fully fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good riding simulator. A must have for bike enthusiasts and racers.Overall 4.5/5 Stars, and any constructive criticism below is a complaint on a very high level.Please keep up the good work. Pros:+Beautiful graphics with attention to detail+Amazing riding physics and realistic look & feel not just from the design but also the physics side of things+Best onbaord cam I've ever seen. The riders-POV is so realistic, I get anxiety when the bike slides/drifts+Gameplay is quite challenging but still funCons:-Ragdoll-like, unreal, animations can apprear when the rider crashes at high speed-Lack of tracks. While it has the staples from US/UK/ITA it's lacking many of the best European tracks and riders favourites. Germany, Netherlands, Czech Republic and Austria are all missing or at least underrepresented. Please give us Brno, Most, Assen, Sachensring, Oschersleben, Hockenhem, Spielberg etc. -The number of laps in a race are fixed (to 5) and there is no rewind button like in Forza. Hence, if you race an otherwise perfect race but crash in the last lap ... you have to start from scratch. And since the AI can literally attack you and the realism of the game makes a fast lap not ever "safe" to drive this happens a lot. - thereby dampening the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The good: Great atmosphere in the menu and excellent but repetitive music, greatly improved bike details and track details compared to the previous RIDE games. Tracks are still not that accurate especially if you come from car sims you will notice a lot of inaccuracies but still improved and playable. A large amount of career content to play with which can keep you busy for 40 hours+. OK bike and ride customization, but you have the ability to download other people's liveries or suit and helmet designs which is great. reportedly dedicated servers for MP as well. The bad: physics on the simple setting feels easy and predictable but unresponsive and leaves you wanting more... the realistic setting which I play with 100% of the time is very unpredictable and sluggish, it feels like every time you go into a corner with the same racing like and braking point you experience something different from the bike. braking is also atrocious! when you go into a hard-breaking zone while braking in a straight line a lot of times your tires just slide in place and the bike never slows you down and often you lose traction and fall through no fault of your own. rear braking is almost useless because as soon as you touch it - even in a straight line - your bikes can't maintain traction and you immediately fall. so it generally feels really really unnatural and frustrating and it makes you feel it is unrewarding to push.I play on the highest difficulty AI (120%) and the AI riders don't even acknowledge your existence, they often lung you into corners and they go wide and hit you, and if you go to their inside they turn into you on the apex. if you go wide they dont slow down and hit you off your bike. the amount of times I got taken out by AI in the 20 hrs I played the game is not even funny. it's sad... really sad. I wanted this to be the Gran Turismo of bikes I really did but Milestone didn't get even the fundamentals right. but there is hoping for future RIDE games to be better...Edit: on Dec 9th, the devs thought it's a good idea to fix the physics by implementing a patch that made your bike glued to the ground by making traction control systems ultra-aggressive... what a waste of money and time.Edit #2: they made another update on the 18th of December and dumped down the physics even more, made the bikes really unresponsive and understeery... to the point where even race bikes like the RM-R6 cant turn for ♥♥♥♥. you basically now can't fall off the bike unless you make something fundamentally wrong like suddenly full throttling while in a turn or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review: After several more hours of extremely frustrating grinding, and introducing the game to a friend who used to competitively race IRL, I've been compelled to keep playing as my friend was objectively better than me without ever playing it. We've been doing multiplayer races against each other with a couple different classes of bikes and it's a lot of fun. I've gone back and redone some of the starting career races and I've gotten much better. I've been able to disable a number of the aids and if the AI is too hard, I just lower it a bit until I get better at it. Like I said in my original review, the game takes a lot of patience, but it is actually quite a bit of fun, especially if you can convince a few buddies to race with you. To that effect, I will change my review to recommended, but heed my warning that the first 8 or so hours will most likely be extremely painful, but if you can get past the initial learning curve, you'll get your moneys worth.OG Review: This is where I think steam should have an in-between review. Bought on heavy sale. For $13 I thought it would be cool to have on the deck and take some rips on my IRL bike since the roads are currently ice rinks where I live. Game is pretty, seems to have a lot of bikes and is probably fun if you have the patience for it but honestly riding a real sport bike is easier and far less frustrating. I might change my review if I can ever get past the second gate on the career race im on and continue playing the game. luckily I was able to unlock enough credits to buy my IRL bike, but the game doesn't even have just a free-ride mode that I can see which seems like a missed opportunity. _childDocuments_.review: I originally did not recommend this game, but after playing some more I do recommend it but a very cautionary recommendation. The physics need revision as the front ends still feel heavy and wish the bikes felt a bit more flickable. The most annoying thing and originally resulted in not recommending the game was and still is the AI; they are awful. On some tracks they are fine (Road Atlanta, Donnington and Road America) are great examples where they act fine. But other tracks like Tsukuba, Sugo and Brands Hatch are some of the worst where they cause massive pileups, while crashes happen in real life, the AI act like kamikaze pilots in a lot of cases. If this was improved, there would be no doubt a highly recommended game.The other issue while small, is the slow start to the game. It is tedious, mostly filled with time trials and the godawful time trial with the cones. The hit boxes aren't perfect on the cone time trial and sometimes screws you up, this is frustrating as the first couple hours while you are learning the physics makes it a grind. The meat of the game is in the world league which is unlocked after a couple hours of the regional grind. There are a ton of fun races once it opens up especially with the endurance races. Where the game excels is how rewarding it is, while learning the physics I had the difficulty very low but have now been able to bump it up to difficult which doesn't guaranty a win but when you do win it feels awesome. The game has a great list of tracks, sucks that some of them just don't work well with AI. The bikes all look amazing, the graphics are so much better than Ride 3 as well. The sounds are good as well.TL:DR The AI is broken on some tracks making it annoying to play sometimes. Once you get past the regional area and learn the physics the game is a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: [UPDATED Nov 18]I was really waiting for Ride 4 to come out, and after a several hours of gameplay I wanted to write a honest review of the 4th installment of the franchise.If you dont want to read, i'll make a pros/cons summary at the end. Before going into the game itself, I faced no issues or crashes. Runs beautifully at 1440p, 60fps, without any problems at highest settings. My pc is runs old gen components, i5-4690k, 16gb DDR3 ram, GTX1080, the game is installed on an SSD.I have been playing Ride games since the 1st one, which was awful. Ride 2 was less awful, still graphics and content sucked.Ride 3 is a great game, one of my all time favs and a great place to start on the franchise.Now, imagine the 1st Gran Turismo for ps one. You could not do anything interesting until you get those very very hard licenses, Ride 4 works somehow like that initially.You need to choose one of 3 leages, american, european and asian, where there's a World League after you completed the other ones.However, Ride 4 asks you to complete a couple of license challenges before you can actually start the regular races and championships. They are mostly time attacks, that are quite hard,  and have very hard to achieve lap times. [Initially, if you went out of track, even by an inch, the test automatically failed, this was addressed in an update and is no longer the case]If you have played other ride games, or other moto gp games, you'll find these challenging, and will require several attempts as the bar is quite high. Nonetheless, they are far from impossible, and by no means make the game unplayable or the fiasco some reviews appear to present. If you have never touched other motorcycle games, start with Ride 3 and stay away from this game.Once you past these licenses, you will start participating on local cups and tournaments, very much like Gran Turismo used to be, climbing up from rookie cups (sunday cup) to Endurance events.IA is not as awful as some people find it. If it crashes into you, is because you are going too slow, which in a racing videogame is not a fun thing to do.It is not great, but somehow feels more realistic than in Ride 3. They do not always do a perfect line, they crash, slide, bump into each other, rain affects them as it does to you.The career feels like a step backwards from Ride 3, and very often you will find yourself being forced to ride bikes you dont like, or fighting to finish the new 5 lap races.Physics are great for my own liking. It is hard and you will need to be very delicate while delivering power going out of corners, and will need to pay extra attention to braking and weight shifts as now bikes tend to slide or drift more frequently. Suspension tuning is useful and will allow you to adjust a little bit to your riding style. A new kind of setting is introduced since Ride 3, which is an option that allows you to toggle braking and acceleration from Soft to Agressive. [After initial release, devs updated this as well and the handling has been improved, power delivery is less punishing and braking is somewhat less agressive, it is still hard to master though]This game is difficult to play, but through that difficulty, winning a race is quite rewarding.Not everything is great though. The variety of bikes is reduced at this point, with 3 dlcs out that add just a few bikes. Probably Milestone will expand this through more downloadable content, we will see if they charge for all of them or give some for free.[So far 2 paid 1 free, even though on their instagram account they suggest more free dlc will come]Bike customization has been completely destroyed. Instead of going into further customization details, they went backwards from Ride 3 and basically you upgrade the whole engine, the whole brake system and the whole suspension in 2  stages or lessNo more discs, calipers, cables, valves, cylinder heads, air filters, all gone, just stage 1 and stage 2 and that's it.Rims are basically the same as in ride 3 in brands and models, however they added tire brands and models as well.Exhausts are also pretty much the same as in ride 3, could not see anything to highlight there.SummaryIn my opinion, this is a great game, has a lot of potential and gives hope that developer has actually taken into account the reviews and made positive updates both in gameplay and also fixing some minor bugs.Pros:-Graphics are great-Bike and overall sounds have been really improved-New tracks, very detailed.-Gameplay is challenging but rewarding-I liked the new physics being a biker myself, but may or may not be your cup or tea.Cons:-Number of bikes is very low, with only a few to choose from for each category.-Customization system has been destroyed and watered down to a bare minimum. -Some may find it too hard.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Ride4... their best effort yet.... but still many annoying things need addressing.....PRO's:Best physics of a motorcycle racing game out there.Sound is wonderful and true to their counterparts.Variety of motorcycles and levels of modelled detail is astonishing.Bonus packs and updates still keep comingRacetracks beautifully captured with only a few niggling hitches on some tracksReplays and photo modeAdjustable Control layoutsSetups actually have good impacts and changes to be felt on trackRoad Racing and Short Circuit Racing. As long as it's a real track in the real world...I'm stoked. No Street Crap please....Cons:Some stupid go through hoops to pass rounds.... takes away simulation and makes it an arcade.Dusk races don't exist in real life, only in endurance racing will they see dusk, dark and a dawn. Bin it.... may graphically look nice.... but is stupid to ride in without lights or fully floodlit tracks.Nearly all challenges have very limited laps and racing, The Championships don't have any feel of a championship and winning anything feels hollow and rewardless.Upgrading a bike has no feel of earning that entitlement.Pay money for a download to give you more money and XP?Tyre modelling is good.... but a super soft in real life will last as long as an in game medium compound. (Tyre wear needs a lot of work).Fuel should be adjustable.Traction control and Anti-Wheelie should not be an option on bikes without such tech.Needs more simulation and championship qualities to keep it away from arcade. Almost like they wanted to build a sim with detailed handling and characteristics but then told the gameplay designers it was an arcade just bash around for 5 laps races.Overall: I love it, keep playing it, just has soooooo much more potential and they should really leave the "arcade qualities" far behind them. They have the best motorcycle game out there.... way better than the Motogp series, but it's very obvious they lack direction and focus. Proper racing challenges please....(Retired SuperSport rider from the 90's)
