A good pack of tracks and variants too, and includes bike and rider customization.But that's where it kinda ends. The game is really really hard, even for players that have to do with racing games in general.Many times if you start breaking as soon as the yellow line is displayed it is way too late already. Engaging Joint Break, breaks so little with the rear that is basically for nothing as you still need to manually apply the break.Different types of races, that automatically disable your rewind feature or the Lines on the road, and it becomes just frustrating, instead of having fun playing with the bikes you love, you need to start over and over again, just maybe you get a bronze medal so that you can go on.I understand this wants to be a sim, but if it is not set to realistic difficulty, it shouldn't act like it ... Most of the time you'll find yourself rewinding a lot, as the AI crashes into you right from the first corner.Also, rewind a lot as you take the corners (like an inexperienced person), while the AI, on any difficulty is a little Marc Marquez, but then on the straight line,  it is a lot slower, so this is another irritating fact, that if you are on a technical track, setting to the easiest possible difficulty might still lead to a Lose.Upgrading the bike, automatically upgrades the AI bikes, usually more than yours can ever get, so it is kinda useless.So in the end, if you just want to freeroam, it is nice, let's say.You'll find yourself grinding for credits (yeah you get 3000 to 30000 per event of tens of minutes) and a cool bike is hundred of thousands of credits, so you'll find yourself grinding a lot, or at least trying.Some bikes are indeed cheaper, at around 20-30k.I think if they could make the AI race consistently, and remove some stuff, from the career, like races you must do without lines, or in a specific time, it could be a lot better.C'mon I am here to play, race and have fun. Ok, make those type of events some sort of qualification round. But that's it.So, I wouldn't really recommend it to someone, especially who might not be into racing games, as it will infuriate you more tan creating any satisfaction.The only reason I actually bought it, was thanks to the bikes, as I like them, after getting my license, but that's kinda it.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Too sim to be fun. The creators of this game seemed to have forgotten that they were making a game. It simulates bikes nearly to the point of unplayability. It is unforgiving and takes itself far too seriously. The riding aid don't help much at all with and the rewind is more of a "crash worse" than an a "do-over". This game hits many marks, but fun is not one of them.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: This review is coming someone who spends every weekend (Late March through October) going round and round a racetrack on a motorcycle:I bought this because I LOVE motorcycles and spend a LOT of my time on the very tracks in the game.  Ride 4 is the ONLY game that you can buy with standard production motorcycles in it.  The graphics and track representation are absolutely BEAUTIFUL.  Riding around VIR in first person mode looked pretty much like the real thing.  I really wish the developers put the time to get the "humps, dips, bumps" right, as that gives each racetrack it's true personality.  The physics and game play is where this game falls flat on it's face.  I understand bike physics are harder than car physics, but you figure they could get this right by now.  The developers made such a effort to make this game a pure simulation, but it's honestly not even close.   It pretty much makes the game unplayable unless you want to devote an insane amount of time learning the totally inaccurate mechanics.  There is no controls sensitivity adjustment to brakes/throttle/lean/anything to at least attempt to put a band-aid on how bad this game handles.  The list of flaws is far too long to mention (It's BAD).  They would of been better off making this more arcade in the physics department. Maybe one day we will get a decent moto-game to help cope during the winter with withdrawls from the real thing... *SIGH*TLDR:  Real race bike = way easier than this game.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: I've been riding IRL for about 5 years now, have always been interested in racing games, have been interested in motorcycles for a long while as well.This game brings all that together. Sure it might have it's flaws but it's a beautiful game.The learning curve might be hard for some, and some of the aids in-game might be a bit more of a hindrance or might not be what they should be (e.g. some of the racing lines) but for a nice relaxing time, this game is amazing. The bikes look amazing, the customization is top, downloading other people's liveries make's finding a nice one for your own taste super easy. The bikes sound amazing and sound like their IRL couterpart.Tons of tracks, tons of motorcycles, the DLC's are awesome, both the free and paid ones. I can surely recommend this game, nice and relaxing, but can be very serious at times as well.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy playing the Ride series casually as I do then the first bit of this game is going to be F***ing miserable. You have to complete 6 different trials that are incredibly challenging. In those trials you have no rewinds and if you wreck or even touch the white lines it forces a failure right then and there. On some of them there is absolutely no chance of winning them if you have rider aids tuned on, you have to slide and out pace what the aids will allow you to do. It took me a little over two hours just to get past that. As far as the rest goes its pretty much another ride game, but with more aliasing / artifacting then ever. As far as bike customization goes its far less alterations to be done, For the motor there is stage 1 & 2 and that's it. No quick shifters or friction reduction. Also for some reason going from street tires to racing slicks decreases your accelaertion and does nothing to improve handling points. I'm conflicted on this one, I love the ride series but the developer making it hard for newcomers and removing already existing features is a damper. Last but not least Day one DLC makes me want to return this game and tell everyone I know to stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Do you feel like games are too easy? Is Dark Souls a piece of cake for you?Are you tired of always being the 'champ' in every racing game you've ever played?Does it feel like other players couldn't even qualify as beginner bots in Forza?Do you have absolutely no self control?Well boy oh boy do I have a treat for you...Turn this on, turn off all driver assistance and get ready to send your driver into Every Single Object next to the track.It took me 71 minutes to Finish a track 3 times. Well below the minimum required to pass.I have never had a game look at me and tell me to go ♥♥♥♥ myself and man did I need this.This is not a game, this is absolute pleasure for when life feels too easy and it is a fantastic masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Not easy and the performance of the virtual bikes does not match the real world counterparts.Practice Brands hatch indy with a bike in time trail and you will have half a dozen bikes in your garage to zoom around  just a couple of hours.Should help to give you hope to carry on playing.Not like riding a real motorbike the handling is too constraining.Like riding on a narrow road no matter how wide the road is.Not terrible handling wise.Not seen any recent updates or bug fixes lately.So like it like this or play something else.It looks good,really good .The sound is a mixed bag of real for some ,generic for other bikes.It plays alright.It will take time to be good at it.i'd still recommend Ride 2 or the first big ben tt game over this.Being a biker all my life;those two feel more like the real deal for me.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of races. decently paced but still lots of freedom to race w.e. you want minus the few championchips. so your not locked into a bike class for more than a race. good bike roster. would ideally be every generation of the bikes but it comes close to hitting all the breakthrough fun and iconic ones. greatly improved ai. greratly improved physics. bike details and looks are so much better. highly recommend over other iterations of the series. load times are 200% faster over ride 3 its so much easier to fall into an endless loop of races 4 hours deep without waiting 4 mins or longer to load in and race.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Game can be pretty fun and it looks good but the absolutely terrible AI detracts from the experience. They will ram into you in the corners and cause you to fall off but will almost never fall off themselves and are also capable of taking turns much faster than the player. Rain races are especially bad because you have to slow down to 40-50mph just to make the turn but wet conditions don’t affect the AI at all. They just fly through the corners at over 100 in the rain with no problems so beating them becomes impossible .
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Usually more into car games but i had to try this for the lovely graphics and sense of speed you get in first person view on a motorbike. It did not disappoint!! Little bit of a learning curve. I jump in head first to these games and always opt for realistic settings to get it as sim like as possible. The speed wobbles you get at high speed are heart stopping and depending on the bike you are on, there are ways to correct it and keep control of it but get it wrong and you will crash. Crashing is apart of this game but its always a big lol watching my guy die over and over again hitting fences and sign posts. Each time i choose a new bike, i get a liking for it after a few spins about. They all feel uique and im just taming the ducati now and its wild beast.Lots of fun and defo worth a go if you into going fast and falling off
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: AI difficulty = straight line speed; how stupid is that? So in the corners they still posses godly grip and speed but on straights you will easily overtake them. This of course becomes problematic when a track doesn't have any proper straights. And on tracks with proper straights, its just not fun to rush past your opponents. As my father used to say: "Everybody is able to go fast on a straight". Also the AI seems to completely ignore that you exist, i got rammed of so many effing times so far. Don't get me started on the physics, it feels too "raily". Physics-wise I really loved Ride 2, disliked Ride 3, and well, the downward spiral continues. Also WTF? DLC Credits Multiplier?EDIT1: Amount/Variety of bikes is laughable + F the DLC policyAlso, if your controller (XBOX ONE Wireless in my case) disconnects once, e.g. because of inactivity, it sometimes does not reconnect, so you have to restart the game.EDIT2:Multiple graphics look "pixely" e.g. the buttons to switch the races, or the rider positions on the minimap while driving. Got nothing to do with graphic settings, i am maxed out.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: The game was obviously rushed out before it was finished. There's a huge number of bugs, much fewer bikes than previous ride games, endurance races are pointless because there's some bug where your bike hits huge invisible bumps in the middle of the track knocking you off and there's no rewind in endurance mode. The cost of bikes is much higher than in previous games and the credit income is much lower so it takes a lot of grinding to get some of the more expensive bikes. The rear brake is currently pointless it just locks the rear no matter how soft you press it. It's a shame because i feel like it could have been a great game but it was released much too soon and obviously wasn't tested properly.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: I not a racing sim fan, but I'm a seasoned rider in real life, with some track experience.Something to know about this game before tacking any of its flaws... is that the .It's demanding, meaning that you'll start being real bad at it. But the learning curve is not so steep, and you'll soon see some great progress if you are persistent enough. At this point, you'll start removing ideal trajectory, remove other help, and slightly reducing electronics. Then you'll get an awesome feeling of accomplishment when doing a decent lap.No, the game is not perfect. - Some of the guys complains about DLC, but there are already a decent number of bike and track. Just don't buy the DLC.- The carreer is not immersive at all. You'll just grind some predefined set of races on predefined categories of bikes, and buy new bikes.- a lot complain about IA. I think it's ok. You're not a real rider and most of the time players are unpredictible. You've got the rewind feature if anything goes wrong with them. So it's not perfect, but it's not as bad other pretend it to be.- The game is not an accurate sim on a lot of aspects, especially bike tuning / improvements. You just buy generic upgrades that improve stats or unlock some settings for the bike. Far from the variety that reality offers to transform a stock bike into a track bike.- all bike customization and livery editors are ok, but again, quite limited in the range of features. You'll have to spend an incredible amount of time to get your idea on the bike.- Bike performances are sometimes inaccurate in terms of stats. I guess it's to keep some prestige on some older bikes.- You'll have always the same electronics settings available for all bike, including very old bikes. I'm pretty sure you can't manage the antiwheeling, traction control or Engine brake on a vintage stock katana from 1982.- Some animation are weird, especially crash or rider position when doing some wheelie.- while talking about sim being not accurate. The grip on rain seems too good to be true, even with rain tires. Tires don't manage temperature, or tire wear seems way too fast. 5 laps, tires are super-dead. etc.- Some stuff is annoying. Can't manage electronics before the greenlight, only on the heat of the race. Autopilot before doing a lap is too long, you'll have to wait 15 seconds before actually controlling the bike.But now, for the good part, Bike details are amazing. Too bad there are not more option to examine them or take static pictures. It just look too net sometimes, like your bike belong to a showroom, not a track.Time and meteo looks great too !Photo mode is a super nice feature.onboard camera is so net !Most of the time, bike sound is pretty accurate too.But the most important thing why I would recommend this game : The actual ride man... once you know the bike and the track, you'll have a blast pushing the bike and carrying the most speed possible in curves, fighting the power of the bike. It will slide, wheely, get the grip back, shake the rider when it does, and rev a lot. the bike is alive and controling it is pretty convincing.Just remove the trajectory help, learn the track and push your riding skill to the limit.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Game is like Forza but for motorcycles. Many say the game is too hard but its because it's focused more on realism. if you actually ride and apply a lot of the same techniques as you would in real-life such as trail braking in a corner, game becomes A LOT easier and more enjoyable. If you're a biker like me and have to stow your bike because of winter, this game will help soothe your riding addiction until riding season returns.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Its the best motorcycle game ever released. Period. Why do I think so? Read the review. After release Ride 4 got a lot of mixed reviews. Lots of people didnt like the difficulty level, smaller amount of available bikes and customisation. But from my point of view its a small flaw comparing to positives about the game.There is a lot I like about the game. First one is the attention to details. Marshals with flags, beautiful fully animated dashboards, photorealistic bike models, track lights, sounds that change depending on the distance from the source or even the photographers models next to the track. Night and day cycle. All of that give imersive experience you will not get in any other motorcycle game. Physics are fine but in last patch Milestone made it easier to meedlt expectations of less skilled players. Unfortunately ☹️ anyway when racing hard there is still easy to crash if you press the brakes too fast, or accelerate too rapidly. Dynamic temperature of tyres affect braking distance and bike handling. Newly introduced tyre wear affected by riding style also is a game changer. Unfortunately very high off track grip and too strong traction control, give that arcadish feeling which could be improved for realistic settings.Career is made very well. Divided into 3 leagues, let the rider progress and gather experience. Unfortunately after some time it gets boring, and finishing it needs a lot of patience. Fortunately you can earn money in single olayer or multiplayer races amd buy the bikes you want. They are not locked like in Ride 3, but doing career its easier to earn money.AI is decent but after series of updates it became less agresive and slightly easier. Its fun tobrace against it because its not hitting the player all the time like it was after game release.Multiplayer is for me, the biggest disappointment. Lack of qualifications and endurance mode make it feel its the aspect of the game with smallest progress. Dedicated servers allow lagless experience which it great for close racing, but general experience isnt much difference comparing to Ride 3.The flaws? Lack of endurance mode and qualifications in online mode, simplified physics with high tyres edge grip introduced in last patch, strong traction control, supersports that wheelie in 3rd gear. Thankfuly Milestone adressed most or the issues in the oatches so the game experience is very good. For me its the best motorcycle game ever released.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: This racing game is awesome, especially if you manage to get everything(DLC) at a discount for around 20€.There are some bugs, but the only real flaw; you have to play it on the ,,realistic,, difficulty, or else you wont be able to reach silver or higher.small update (50h. 33%)Yeah, so the game is still awesome. I really like the physics a lot; I've never had such good physics. However, difficulty doesn't matter in some races because some are too easy, even on the hardest difficulty, and some are so hard that there's no chance. I've learned to hate the Ducati... and basically all high-PS naked bikes. I played the same race for 4 hours and still lose because once your tires hit 40%, it's over. And I don't use the rewind function... because I can't find the X button! xD.btw this game is better then ride5... dont fall for it, at least yet see you soon on the next update51% (71h)I hate naked bikes67% (118h)So, I'm done with the World League, and Ride 5 has been fixed, aaaand at the moment, it only costs 15€. Since I haven't played it yet, I can't really recommend it, but all the reviews I've seen are very positive. So, I guess just get it instead – for such a low price, it can't be wrong.I must say, after so many hours, the roads are getting boring. Not because there’s a lack of roads, but because it's always the same tracks you play. I know there’s a Japanese track in the game that’s very narrow, but I think I’ve only played it once.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: This game is HARD but so rewarding. I've played all of the Ride series and a few of the MotoGP games and still struggle at times with this game. But when you get the feeling of the bikes, when you understand the handling, when you've memorised the track, it is one of the most rewarding racing games I've ever played.- The graphics are much better- The physics have been heavily revised since Ride 3- The sounds are much improvedThe game will frustrate you and no, it is not perfect. There are some design decisions which I question but when the act of riding is this good in a game I am happy to forgive them.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: RIDE 4 is my first game from the RIDE franchise and even though it isn't perfect I can recommend it for similar newcomer like me (experienced player of MotoGP, but new to RIDE).+++ : Physics and bike handling feels natural to me. There is plethora of manufacturers, bikes and circuits (Nordschleife, Cadwell, Suzuka, ...). AI is well trained I enjoy racing against opponents, even though they're aggresive I find it more fun. Only oversight is their ramming from behind when slipstreaming, but I believe it should be something not that hard to update.--- : So far only small details. Let me start endurance race without auto-pilot. In Time-Trial when I leave track invalidate the lap, but do not force me to restart.These pros won't satisfy players coming from RIDE 3, hence the number of negative reviews, but I am enjoying it so far.Decide for yourself, what you expect and what you want from the game. I would also suggest checking price of the game in your local store as Steam price tag is inflated.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Having played through the whole franchise of RIDE i kinda thought i knew what to expect, i was wrong. DO NOT buy this game thinking it will be similar to RIDE 3 because it isnt, its leagues  the wrong direction. it depends what the devs wanted to achieve. did they make an arcade game? no, deffo not. did they make a sim game? yes, but badly.with Ride 3 you knew what you were getting, it was good but it had its issues like the robotic AI that were bulletproof, they always followed the same line, never made mistakes and were generally may as well not have been there. in Ride 3 the bike sounds were hit and miss. some bikes sounds great....others horrendous (see my ride 3 review)things have changed in Ride 4, the AI are not as infallable as they once were, they do make mistakes, crash into each and run wide etc but the always seem to be able to take a tighter line and go faster than you this was the same in RIDE 3, nothing has chanaged in that dept. the bike sounds have also improved to some extent, the sport bikes do sound better, but the naked bikes and twin engine bikes still sound like a bee in a trombone for want of a better explanation.there is also a graphics improvement, the bike models are amazing as is the scenery and the rider movements are believable. there are however a few problems. things are just very inconsistent. there are issues with throttle sensitivity, all is well at low revs but there seems to be a dead zone where the revs are controllable up to a point and then after they go into maniac mode. this is turn has a detrimental effect when coming out of corners. you just end up spinning up the back wheel and high siding the bike. take it easy to avoid this and the AI just shoot pass you. even with TC on. its utter nonsense . (i am using a ps4 controller via DS4 windows. those with xbox one controllers may not experience this) what this game screams for is the option to change sensitivity and linear control changes. just then, it might be worth a blast.Cornering is a total lottery. at times youll find the bike will turn in rather well and you will nail the corner. other times youll find the bike stiff and unresponsive. its all very very weird! i ride bikes in real life, i can honestly say this game isnt true to real life...but then its just a game i guess.I dont like the license thing either. ive got as far as the interlagos track and i have to ride the bmw 1000rr. again its so inconsistent. you gotta ride through these gates, which means correct line and correct speed. problem is it isnt possible, you have to pass the first gate on the straight at a min speed. but even the min speed means you cant make the braking point and take the apex for the first corner and hit the 2nd gate. this isnt an issue missing the 2nd gate but you do get a 0.5 second penalty making it impossible to get a gold in this test. i honestly dont know what the devs were thinking of  making these tests mandatory. it is in all honesty crap and a poor idea.when i first play a racing game i always leave ideal trajectory turned on, just until i get used to the way things are. in RIDE 4 turn it off immediately, i dont even know why this is in the game, it isnt anywhere near good enough and using it will cause you to crash. braking zones are much longer than the game says it is and the racing line must of been coded by stevie wonder. even the AI dont take the projected line, so what does that say? learn yourself and turn it offspeaking of turning things off. also turn off the semi auto gear box. its hopeless!! it can never make up its mind what gear to select and there is a place reserved in hell for the person who coded that into this game and thought that they had done a good job! use manual and you might also solve the issue with spinning up the back tyre.is RIDE 4 a bad game? thats hard to answer, it has its good points but its mainly bad IF you compare it to RIDE 3. as it stands the handling mechanics dont work at all mainly due to the over sensitivity issues, if these can be solved then yes, it would be a good game.  but as it stands for me right now.....no i wouldnt buy it if i knew then what i know now
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a Motorbike fan, i highly recommend this game. it is fun as heck. Graphics are good not mind blowing but good better than ride 3. The game can be arcady if you so choose but if you want to have more of a simulation experience you can deactivate all help functions to make it more fun and i suggest that you to play it like that. I'm having a blast and raging when i took a corner too wide or too slow or if  i brake too late.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, this is probably my favorite game of 2020, and I play a LOT of games. Learning curve is quite hard, but if you put the time in, this game is extremely rewarding. A must have for any motorcycle fan, excellent graphics, tons of tracks and bikes, awesome soundtrack...  watching a replay is fantastic. Really a hidden gem, props to the developers on making an excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I was disappointed, much less content than the Ride 3. Super simplified mechanical modifications. There are no more modifications of air filters, pistons, connecting rodsecu, valve caps, they removed the modifications of the brake pads, the calipers, the brake cable, removed the modifications of the suspensions, which affected the visual and mechanical part., they took everything out. Not to mention customization like brake levers, Christ, throttle grips etc.I honestly expected a better change, and it was for the worse. The only thing that improved a bit was the graphics and sounds, and some things about the circuits.But when it comes to bike modification options, everything simplified.The calipers and brake cables cannot be painted any more.It is not possible to individually improve the mechanical parts of the engine, such as the air filter on one hand, the pistons on the other, the connecting rods, etc. In other words, it does not allow you to improve the bike individually engine parts.Now what they did is put, engine kit 1,2 and 3 nothing else.The same applies to the brakes. Suspensions only one kit.They simplified everything absolutely everything, and the best options that the Ride 3 had, they took them away.Not to mention the abusive DLC policy.Conclusions, they simplified everything and the best things that ride 3 had got it out.A disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: After paying full price for Ride 3..Bought Ride 4, again full price..  (shouldn't loyal customers get a discount on the next version?)Great game IF you don't mind having to pay AGAIN after purchasing to buy extra bikes in order to complete the game....And, even worse when you pay the full price for Ride 4, my favourite track and bike is missing (from Ride 3), which means I have to install BOTH games, needlessly..(Lake Garda and MT-09 in case you wondered..)No Doubt Ride 5 (announced already), will continue the tradition so I'd need to install ALL THREE to play my favourite tracks on my favourite bikes....
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Best motorbike sim game i've played. The physics are by far the best compared to its rivals which as a simulator is one if not the most important factor of this game in my opinion. Both bike and track models look stunning aswell as the selection of the two you are offered is amazing, the best I've seen in a motorbike or even any racing game for that matter. However there are still a lot of issues that need ironing out. A couple of which is the AI, from my experiences they are set on rails and will run you off the track if you get in there way leaving you re-spawning at the side as you watch all the other bikers fly past you. My solution to this was to enable and use the rewind feature whenever you are getting bullied.  Another problem is the licences you have to complete in order to progress in the career mode. They are way too hard. As a semi competent player myself, I found them do-able but extremely difficult to the point where I struggled to even get the bronze medal. But my friend however, (yes I only have one.) has pretty much given up with the game within a day of owning it, and that's with with easiest settings. Yes I know not all games hold your hand such as dark souls and should pose a challenge to those who seek it, but I believe the it should be made a little bit easier for the sake of the not so good players.Over all i recommend this game. But be ready for the frustration and tears that come with it.Happy Riding! :)
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Great looking game, authentic sound some although some of the 2 strokes sound more like crazy frog samples than the actual thing. good overall game play however the realism is a little off,  i have it set to realistic and it will happily let you go through a hair pin, full lock while still jamming the front brake on without as much as a wobble. The UI could be improved, the race reset process takes 4/5 inputs to start over (this could be streamlined). The AI is laughable, there's no collision detection and they will just ride through you or other bots for that matter if they share the same racing line. nothing like getting to the end of a race and getting wiped out and having to start over because you have the rewind setting off or certain race modes disable it. if they sort the bots then i would put this as recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Unless your willing to put a few hours into the game to understand the basics principles of racing in this game you should probably steer clear of this game. Ride 4 has a very very steep learning curve with easily one of the highest I've seen in a racing game but once you get past that barrier you get an amazing game. It feels like they went for a simcade model for this game but messed up which makes it pretty difficult to work around but it made the game much more enjoyable for me. Learning tracks and different bikes is incredibly rewarding once you get to the stage of everything being second nature.(If you're struggling to pickup the game disable assists and search up a tutorial or two and you will start going much much faster)
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: A Ride worth taking.Pros:Realistic motorcycle physics!Excellent Gran Turismo / Forza level graphics.Real-time day cycles with a varying weather system.Extensive and varied career mode.Over 170 bikes to choose.Cons:Callous A.I. riders that'll frequently knock you off your bike. NEEDS adjusting!Boring sterile menu presentation.Lackluster custom race variety.Shallow multiplayer experience.Often inaccurate driving trajectory line.Conclusion: If you can overlook the cons then Ride 4 is probably the most realistic motorcycle riding experience, currently available and offers plenty of riding fun to be had.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, it could have become a relay good game and had a lot of potential but after 200 hours of play I am just done with the game (Milestone). Graphically the game is just great, at least only for those who like to be blinded by it. It is(was) technically a huge step forward in terms of driving physics, if you compare it with Ride 3. But seriously instead of Milestone sitting down properly and improving the many problems and bugs and the messed up online mode via patches, Milestone takes the easy way as always. Don't do anything that is difficult to fix and downgrade the whole game to an arcade game where the motorbikes drive like on rails so that even the dumbest casual idiot can handle it. If anyone looking for a reasonable motorcycle racing sim is wrong here. It could have been but since the last patch it's just garbage. In MotoGP20, Milestone had a great online mode with qualifications, a sophisticated tire wear simulation and fuel consumption. Why don't they do that for Ride 4? It's better to program some nonsense that doesn't work and let the ♥♥♥♥ as it is. So if someone is looking for a decent motorcycle simulation, I think they should go for MotoGP2020 or wait for the BSE Bike Simulation Experience. Who wants to have a screwed up arcade game can be satisfied with the crap here.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: Ride 4 – The modern interpretation of the legendary Tourist Trophy?Is Ride 4 the modern interpretation of Tourist Trophy? – Maybe…Firstly, I`ll start off with mentioning the pro’s and con’s.Pro:-	Challenging AI (finally)-	A lot of events and riding to do-	Nice detailed bikes-	Dynamic weather-	Similarity to Tourist Trophy in career mode-	Wide range of different classes-	Good graphics-	Good performanceCon:-	Bike sounds are better than Ride 3, but still a little flat-	Career mode is somehow repetitive (time-trial, trackday in almost every category)-	Wet races are there to make it much more difficult (AI struggles less)-	AI sometimes really stupid and overly aggressive-	Some bikes are stupidly expensive -	What are those DLC-politics??? (*add word here*)The career mode feels similar to Tourist Trophy. Before you’re able to participate in an event/league, you have to receive your license. The small categories in every league is also similar to Tourist Trophy. If the career mode wouldn’t be so repetitive in terms of events like time trial and trackday, etc., it would be a great mode. It is still good, don’t get me wrong. Nevertheless, I think it is a shame, that some bikes are so expensive. You have to grind so much for some bikes, it’s a shame. However, I enjoy the variety this game offers you. Just cruising around with some naked-bikes or pushing the limits with superbikes. If you have time for a longer session, it is worth checking out the endurance category, although I am a little disappointed of the AI in terms of pit stops, because they are stopping too much and way too early, but it is still a fun experience.All in all, this game gave me nice childhood-flashbacks when I was grinding Tourist Trophy with my dad. I really enjoy this game to be honest. In my opinion it is worth checking out, but buy it on sale, because 50€ and those shady DLC-politics is a downer to be fair…Thank you for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Thrilling and Authentic Racing Experience - Ride 4Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)One of the standout features of Ride 4 is the incredible attention to detail put into the bikes and tracks.Each bike handles uniquely, giving players a sense of the real-world characteristics and nuances of these powerful vehicles.The career mode in Ride 4 offers a vast array of challenges and events, providing hours of gameplay for solo players. From single races and time trials to endurance events and championships, there is a variety of content to keep you engaged.Multiplayer is where Ride 4 truly shines. Compete against friends or other racers from around the world in exhilarating online races. The matchmaking system ensures fair competition, and the racing action is intense and satisfying.However, Ride 4 is not without its flaws. The game's physics, while generally solid, can occasionally feel a bit too forgiving, resulting in unrealistic crashes or collisions. Additionally, the learning curve for newcomers might be steep, as mastering the controls and handling the bikes effectively requires practice and patience.In conclusion, Ride 4 delivers an impressive racing experience that will captivate motorcycle enthusiasts and racing game fans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: While RIDE 4 is starting to show its age a bit in comparison to the more polished recent entries in the MotoGP series from Milestone, the sheer variety of bikes, tracks, and race modes make this a tremendously fun game for any motorcycle racing enthusiast. However, there are a lot of bugs including some major game breaking ones that Milestone has known about since 2020 and not bothered to fix.I really do enjoy the game, but I really can't keep recommending Milestone games when they'd rather crank out DLC than fix major bugs.Pros:- SO. MANY. BIKES. Even if you don't buy any paid DLC.- Great variety of tracks from all over the world. Standard race tracks, street courses, and absolutely punishing road race courses.- Career mode is pretty extensive in terms of taking advantage of the above variety and motivating you to unlock new stuff - Events aren't just pure races. Track days, time trials, and a timed event where you have to pass through gates on the track at a minimum speed (helps learn the tracks).- Bike handling is decently sim-ish on "realistic". e.g. Still braking hard and the weight is still shifted way forward? Bike won't turn in very well. Start letting off the brakes? Weight shifts further back and bike turns more.- Fast bikes are fast. The last superbike license race with the Panigale on a road racing course? My poor rider would be dead 1000x over.Cons:- Endurance racing has been broken since like early 2020 because if it rains you can't switch to rain tires but the AI can. There are numerous forum posts and I'm sure people have tried to submit bug reports to Milestone but ¯\_(ツ)_/¯- If you finish qualifying in 1st but you were in the pits looking at times and fast forwarding, you might wind up starting from the back.- Random bugs with sound on certain bikes like a weird knocking noise on the Racing Modified KTM 390 after a session restart.- To buy all the paid DLC was around $90 CAD. The extra content is good, but you'd think they'd fix long standing bugs as well.- Controller feedback is really poor compared to the current MotoGP games which gives much a better feel on the triggers.- Minor issues  - Choosing tires is basically guesswork. You don't get to see the track/ambient temp until you're on the track. Also even soft tires stay super cold in some races.  - The physics sometimes seem to go a bit awry with the bumpy road races and can be suuuuper frustrating when doing qualifying and a lap takes 4.5 mins.  - Braking for suggested racing line seems way too aggressive on more powerful bikes.  - Flaky AI. Even at the same difficulty setting they can be inhumanly fast on one track and ridiculously crash prone and slow on another.  - Bike setup tooltips are not that helpful for someone not mechanically inclined. I wish Milestone would put a bit more into helping players understand visually what changes to the setup do to the bike handling.  - "Upgrading" bikes doesn't have the same fun factor as upgrading a car in a game like Forza Horizon. Maybe we could find a happy medium between this and RiMS for Ride 5?  😀tl;dr - If you love motorcycles and racing, and can overlook a bunch of bugs including the fact that the entire endurance racing section (probably 50-60 races?) is effectively broken, you might still generally enjoy the game like I do, but for everyone else you'll probably quit pretty quickly. If it's really cheap on sale, pick it up, otherwise skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Ride 2, Ride 3 and now Ride 4 and the only one that will remain on my hard drive is Ride 2. Ride 2 has the best balance of good physics, good challenge, good progression system, good AI and most importantly good fun!Ride 4 comes with a few issues that ruin it for me, regardless of it's improved sounds and graphics.Here's my take on it:+ Improved graphics (but you're going 100+mph so take this with a grain of salt because the graphics in Ride 2 still hold up well enough with that in mind)+ Improved sounds (the fidelity of the engine sounds is noticeable and appreciated)- Less tracks/courses to race on (this is a downgrade) Ride 2 has about 30 tracks/courses and about 14 of those are county road & city street type courses whereas Ride 4 only offers I think 2 or 3 road types and the rest are race tracks...so if you love your road and city type racing then forget about Ride 4...so depending upon what your own personal likes are this one could actually be a positive for you....but I prefer road and city courses for bikes more than race tracks.- Braking is difficult due to benign lack of "feel",  and braking distances which seem to be greatly increased beyond reality- Leaning seems to be a bit less responsive or slower than usual- AI difficulty does not scale down well and they will run you over and down your bike at every slow point on every track...unless you get good enough to always stay far enough ahead of them so that they can't catch you. They are not bound by the same physics restrictions as the player and the difficulty slider does not do enough to offer a fun race experience for lower skilled or casual players that don't want to grind 500 laps to get good enough just to enjoy themselvesSo in a nutshell, the negative comments mentioned above make Ride 4 more of a frustrating experience rather than a fun experience, IF you're a more casual rider. However, that being said...if you're someone who likes having sweaty balls mile after mile then Ride 4 might just be the game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I am a follower of this game since the first ride. I'm a bike enthusiast and have a fair amount of riding experience. That being said I have never ridden on track so take some of the technical information with a grain of salt.PROS:-Graphics have improved a fair bit-Bike models are much more detailed and fun to look at-The replay feature is very good-Weather variation a welcome addition-Bike variety is pretty good (about the same as Ride 3)-Tracks look better than ever and there are quite a few of them-AI is general an improvement with a few caveats-Endurance mode is good, and pit stop animation is very good-Front doesn't wash out as unrealistically as in previous titlesCONS:-Having to pay for a day one bike pack is slimy-Tailored to a more hardcore enthusiast than ever. Less players will enjoy this one than previous titles.-Can be very frustrating at times. The game does not hold your hand at all.-Rear tire now slides out too easily IMO-Bike upgrades aren't as diverse as before-AI can be VERY aggressive at times, and don't seem to suffer the same fate when you hit them as when they hit you-Front end "feel" is harder to gauge in this title than before : /-Bikes take a long time to unlock, forcing you to buy the credits multiplier.Notes: Overall the newest installment in the ride series is a welcome one. The franchise has matured a lot since the first game, but in doing so has discouraged less hardcore bike enthusiasts from trying the series out. The physics are VERY good, but as with all bike games they can always be better. I've always said the ride games the Forza and Gran Turismo of the bike world, and for the most part that is still true. My favorite improvement from the last game is the bike models. Not only do they look more detailed than ever, they sound and feel more unique making each bike stand out from each other. It's clear that they weren't able to afford the same treatment to every bike however as some bikes look MUCH better than others, but this isn't different from other games as I imagine it must be very time consuming to treat every bike this way. Overall, I continue to recommend this series to serious bike enthusiasts and beginners interested in getting into bike racing as the standard bike racing game.

You go from 0 to 100% input instantly, and your bike is going to run wide or high side and throw your a** if the rider aids don't save you.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: An experience constantly teetering from fun to absolutely miserable. Get it on sale if you like sport motorcycles AND enjoy the frustration and eventual satisfaction that comes from learning driving sims, otherwise just steer clear and hope the next installment fixes the many issues.THE BAD-Not beginner-friendly at all. No introduction, no "riding school" or any effort put into teaching newcomers the basics of riding and steering at speed, leaning, throttle and brake management, nothing. Career starts by choosing a regional league and being given a kick in the pants with a "Here are some bikes, tracks and your objectives, good luck."-The AI is absolutely horrible, more A than I. Opponents don't avoid or adjust their racing lines for the player or even each other at all, even if that means running into you and causing a huge crash, completely ruining your race and theirs.-Most of the interesting events are locked behind the starting league, even those acquired through DLC, so if you can't clear whatever regional league you choose then you're SOL.-Playing with a PS5 controller is an unresponsive nightmare unless you spend the time and effort of tweaking the deadzone and response settings.THE GOOD-A decidedly decent selection of sport bikes throughout the decades with a few interesting and niche choices here and there along with some of the most iconic models for various manufacturers-A good selection of tracks from the three wide regions offered with some of the most well-known tracks around the world and the option of riding around the full Nurburgring.-Great sound design, the game sounds great through speakers and headphones. -You get rewarded for doing time trials and practicing just riding around the track completing laps thus allowing you to access more bikes without needing to win races or go through the career.Good looking graphics that allow the game to run in a wide variety of systems without detracting too much from the experience.-Decent physics but can take a bit of time to get used to and learn.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: I HATE THIS GAME! Yes,  It's beautiful, the bikes, graphics, and sound are 11/10, and the physics on the bikes are the best in a motorcycle game! but it's so ridiculously hard! Even if you make a perfect run, that sh*t doesn't matter, the AI will let you around 30sec behind even BEFORE completing the first lap!Those "time attack" events have the most ridiculous times to beat, for example:gold 00:57silver 00:58bronze 00:59lose the race 00:59:01 and aboveOne sec apart? wtf? And where is the buffer zone? Again, you can make your most perfect run ever, and still barely get bronze.Also, what is the deal with those tracks? Ride 2 had some of the coolest tracks! Around the mountains, airports, desert, city, some official race tracks too! but now it's 95% race tracks. No only that but they replaced the cool races/events from Ride 2 with fricking traffic cone races on an insanely hard timer? comeeeee ooon..  Which btw they are using it as a Gatekeeper to the other events, So you HAVE to beat those to continue. In ride 2 we can just ignore those boring races and still can to go on with the carrer mode with zero issues!I mean, If we wanted that, we would just get MotoGP, and not RIDE. This it's supposed to be the more arcade and fun between those two. Remember? And Milestone makes BOTH games! Why they are making Ride into a clone of MotoGP ? What's the point!?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is garbage!  As a track rider and avid gamer let me tell you none of the physics in this game are on point.  You can barely trail brake without the bike lowsiding, the stock brakes dont work for ♥♥♥♥ and overall the bike and rider feel like they are fighting each other constantly. I use stock tired and brakes at the track all the time and have never had an issue with them. _childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying Ride 4 for the most part, but there are a number of issues that are preventing me from recommending it.There are a number of bugs that I had hoped to miss due to picking it up nearly 8 months after release. But, exhaust flashes often emanate from the rear wheel (rather than the exhaust), going over a jump of any kind causes the front to drive, regardless of whether you're leaning back or not, and often results in an uncontrollable speed wobble on landing.My biggest issue comes with the suspension; unless you're riding a fast Ducati, chances are the rear tyre will be too cold, regardless of your tyre choices or suspension settings. I've seen claims that all bikes have exactly the same suspension, meaning for light bikes, you can't get it soft enough, and I'm tempted to agree. I've always enjoyed tuning suspension in the racing games I play, but near as I can tell, they don't have any direct impact on the bike - no combination of settings has had any effect on a bikes tendency to wheelie, for instance, or how hard you can actually accelerate when leant over. No combination seems to have any effect on the way bikes nose dive instantly coming off a small jump, let alone the speed wobble of death after.Meanwhile, Milestone are pumping out DLC... The cynic in me wants to wash my hands of the whole thing, it's just a shame it's some of the best bike racing available right now.

If you are faster or slower then they are, they just ram you, and you fall off.  You touch them ever so slightly, you fall off, but they almost never crash.  Knee-down in the dirt...they can do it.  You hit the curb, you fall.  This makes the game just about unplayable.  It is not fun, and just makes you frustrated.

It is a shame they do not have CROSS-PLAY because the online race lobbies are almost non existent... You came to the wrong place sir!This game is so frustratingly hard, you'll soon see, that you made a grave mistake buying it within two hours of playing it.There is no learning curve, it's just an unnecessary, un-fun, stupid game. Ride 4, is so torturous, they should use this game to torture terrorists for information. Just force a terrorist to play this game, and I swear they'll tell everything. _childDocuments_.review: Wasn't expecting such an upgrade after a rather disapointing Ride 3 but this one is definitely my favorite of the series.Physics are much better, more realistic than the previous title, still not a hardcore simulation though. It's not GPBikes, but each bike feels different now and piloting is challenging. Falling feels more natural than the previous title, if one wheel is in the dirt and other one on the asphalt you'll crash. No more recovery on the wall and while it's easier to make an opponent fall, it's also more random, making it an unreliable strategy.The graphical upgrade is thin but noticeable: cockpit view is better (moving brake liquid reservoir), weather effect is neat. It  overall feels less gamey than Ride 3.Engine sound is great, too bad it doesn't change when changing the exhaust but i guess i'm asking too much here. The ost is suprisingly ok.The game is not perfect, be aware:- The AI is slightly better but they still crash into you (online players too sometimes)- The difficulty is too high for timed events and lowering the diffculty doesn't affect the timer.- Rear Brake cannot be precisely controlled with an analogic stick, you got to tap the button (it only goes 100% brake power if you stay put).- There is no text chat in multiplayer room and i'd like to freely express my safety concerns after someone crashed into me at start for the 3rd time.The online community is still there, had no trouble finding an online race, but winning it on the other side...Recommended for those wanting a fun motorcycle game without too much sacrifice on simulation.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite frankly, this game is a huge disappointment. I have been playing racing games (including Ride 2 and 3) for the better part of 20 years, and never have I come across such an unrewarding title as Ride 4. As many other reviews have mentioned, in order to even reach the races in the campaign you must first go through a 'licensing' period, which consists of a couple time trials and other odd events. This would be a cool idea in theory, but in practice the devs have made the minimum time requirements so strict and difficult that they are nearly impossible to reach. Not all of us have 100+ hours to devote to a game to perfectly learn every single line of every single race course in order to achieve the 'perfect' time. Some would like to pay their $50 and enjoy a motorcycling simulator while the weather is cold and their own bike is stored up for the winter. Quite frankly, I want my money back.The game itself is beautiful, the bikes are cool, the graphics are great, and the physics are good enough. I just expected that for my money I would be able to actually PLAY the game I thought I was buying, not race an underpowered Harley boat anchor around one of the most difficult tracks in the world.If you are looking for an enjoyable motorcycle racing simulator, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 4

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to give this game a chance, but with it's ever-growing list of flaws, I can't recommend it to anyone. The Speed Trap time trials, which are mandatory for Career to move forward, are utterly broken as a mechanic. The game requires you to pass them at certain speed and in correct driving line, yet gives you no feedback what went wrong this time. They also have a weird bug of every now and then penalizing you for the next gate's speed, which can be really frustrating when you're taking a corner at max speed you can, and suddenly it requires your speed to be the same as the next straight's full send speed.The AI is horrible, they seem to be stolen from some bumper car game or demolition derby. No regards to the player or correct driving lines, you might be consistently taking the suggested line and suddenly be rammed into full speed from the inner corner.The bikes and tracks in this game are also very limited compared to older games in the same series. I'd love some more naked bikes from the old game, for example. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who has put many hours into Ride 2 and 3, I was expecting Ride 4 to be a "Ride 3+". Milestone went -sadly- into another direction. Let's start with the positives. First of all, yes, the physics have changed a lot, making the game way more immersive but also way harder. This isn't helped by the really poor "tutorial" or the tendency the game has to send you on fast bikes too soon after said tutorial. But, once you get the hang of it, the driving becomes more interesting and challenging than before. Second, the graphics have impoved. My PC can't run this game on high enough settings for it to be "night and day" but there are a few places where even I, with my old computer, manage to spot improvements.Now, the bad, and ohhh boy it's a doozy. The difficulty seem to spike in the weirdest of ways, some events will be a breeze while some other are frustrating to an incredible level. I could excuse those if they were "endgame" events but no, these are some of the first events you're going to encounter in the career. I would advise not to start your career mode in the European region as its probably the worst offender. The racing is "fine", single races can be really enjoyable and the AI, while far from perfect, doesn't seem to be such pushovers as before. Hell lies in the other modes. The track day mode is sometimes super easy, sometimes incredibly hard for no good reason. The "checkpoints" mode (or whaterver its called) is quite bad, forcing you into gates that sometimes are way out of a natural trajectory. But the worst offender is Time Attack. It's difficult for all the wrong reasons. If you dip a wheel offroad you'll fail (this has been -somewhat- improved by a day 2 patch, but is still very poor). You'll need to restart the entire event but not before a 3-4 seconds long video plays (imagine the Gran Turismo 4 Licence fail video) and then you'll need to manually restart the event (no quick restart here !). This will send you back to the "event start menu" and force you into a -short- loading time everytime and then you'll need to wait for the 5-10 seconds of autopilot before the actual event start. This is not helped by the fact that you can fail the event before crossing the line to start the timer, nor is it helped by the autopilot coming off at some of the worst moments imaginable on some tracks and the absolutely useless "dynamic racing line" is sure to make you miss braking zones and send you offroad. This alone made me want to refund the game after less than 2 hours played. But the biggest gripe I have with this game is the content. While the couple of tracks added are nice additions, the rest is VERY poor in my opinion. Rider customisation seems very "light" in terms of content, might even be worse than in Ride 2 (!) And then there's the bike selection ... Which seems like a bad joke. Both the quantity and variety of bikes present in the game at launch are incredibely poor. Some career events (even some of the earliest ones !) are giving you a great selection of 2 (!!) bikes to choose from. A lot of my favorites are gone. A lot of good beginner bikes that were present in previous games are gone (125cc two strokes for exemple). Trail bikes introduced in Ride 3 are gone. The incredibely small number of vintage bikes that were in Ride 3 has been reduced to ... 2. Some manufacturers are completely gone.This honestly feels like a ripoff after Ride 3 and this isn't helped by the fact that Milestone is going to crank out badly priced DLC's where we're sure to find all the missing content back behind a horrible paywall (and without a season pass to try and get that price down either). While I understand that a lot of these bikes needed to be re-done to suit the improved graphics, this is nonetheless a big letdown and a bad business practice. There are no excuses for this.In conclusion, I wanted the transition from Ride 3 to Ride 4 to be like the one from Gran Turismo 3 to 4. Instead it feels like the transition from Forza Motorsport 4 to 5. The few "improvements" were made at the cost of vast amounts of content. New players coming into this franchise might not feel that way, but people who stuck by are sure to feel burnt. If you want to get into Ride, get Ride 3 and all of its (many) DLC at a steep discount. Ride 4 is simply not worth it at the moment. This might get better with patches and -probably pricy- content drops but I can't recommend this game right now. I'll change my review if Milestone does actually change something about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this mostly on a different acct, which is why the time played is low. Believe me, I got a few hours into the game before writing a review. Hours I'll never get back. Not a great motorcycle game with physics that feel like a step backward from Ride 3, which I also didn't recommend. Bike selection is down from previous titles. Tracks are recycled. AI is braindead as always. The only 'action' comes from you the player. The AI will now crash on it's own once in awhile, sadly it's often into you, ruining your race. Look- in real life there is barely any difference between machines despite what every street Rossi wants to think. Remove the plastic and logos and people would have no idea what brand they are on. This game does at least capture that-- it feels like there are about half a dozen bike physics models and the devs just slapped a slightly different skin on to create the illusion of lots of bikes. Literally I think there is about 10 bikes programmed into the game and just reskinned to make it look like the game has a hundred bikes. The braking in the game has no relation to the actual universe we live in, Forget trail braking, in fact forget the rear brake since the front acts like linked brakes.  Nothing about braking in this game resembles braking on an real motorcycle. The fact that the rear brake is default mapped to a button (making the brakes an on/off switch) should tell you that this isn't a 'sim' level experience. Another useless 'career' mode that isn't anything like an actual racing career. Another completely useless rider gear customization that exists only to promote real world branding. Zero impact on the game, zero reason to change your suit other than vanity. It's not part of a sponsorship mechanic-- you know like in real life. Same for the bikes themselves. You don't race a series on a team, you randomly pick from eligible bikes and go, and can change bikes at will. Again- how this is considered a racing 'career' boggles the mind. Graphics are fine. Bikes look nice, animations are smooth. Sound is boring and reused for half the bikes. Exhaust sound is the same despite different manufacturers. Overall muting the game and playing music would be better. No Suzuki TLR 1000 (or TLS street version) which was in Ride 3. This bike competed against Honda's RC51 in Superbike, yet it's absent here. Few vintage bikes earlier than the 80's. You get 25 versions of GSXR, most indistinguishable from one another- but forget reliving the heyday of cafe racers. Career isn't just racing in a series according to year and class. It's a series of time trial events, passing events, and sometimes an actual race. The pass/fail nature of events means that if you get stuck on something--- you just have to keep repeating the event until you get whatever the devs decided was a win. Solve this by just letting players create custom series. Let players choose an era, bike class, types of events, number of events, tracks used, etc. Simply an expansion of the single race custom event already in the game. Instead you get whatever random crap the devs decided makes up a 'series'. In short- bikes are virtually the same making the large roster a bit BS. Physics aren't realistic, braking is atrocious. AI is barely passable, but a tiny improvement over Ride 3. Character customization exists only to promote real brands and has no effect in game. Career is anything but. Lastly- obviously nothing about sitting in a chair with a controller relates to riding a real motorcycle, especially at race speeds. So 'realism' is used VERY loosely here and I actually give the game a lot of leeway in that regard. Even so- it still disappoints. This is a tank slapper simulator more or less. I think overall Ride 3 was better. Don't recommend Ride 4 at all.

_childDocuments_.review: -- Update 11.10.2020OK Milestone, here is a challenge for you:Prove that "World Licence" test 5 (BMW S 1000 RR 2019, Interlagos GP, Rain) is passable on Gold with all assists off, no abs, max physics, etc. with the current release.If you find someone, then I will no longer complain that this game is too hard. -- Revision 10.10.2020RIDE 4 is great - and I have to revise my previous review of the game (which contains many bad words, like masochism, Italian-based companies won't hear you [just like EA], and more not-so-nice stuff) and will give it a recommendation now. I guess one could easily feel the frustration I had at the time of writing, since I was really looking forward to the next iteration of the RIDE series.I played some more hours because I didn't want to simply give up.First let me start with some words about what you get when you buy RIDE4:- an excellent looking bike riding game that indeed feels like a next-gen product (much better than RIDE 3)- performance improved on my system compared to RIDE 3- tracks seem to be more realistic in terms of bumpiness and grip- weather and night cycle is great- engine sounds differ heavily between the bikes and to me are awesome and realistic while reving- each bikes feels and behaves unique- the physics have been so much evolved to something much more harder and probably more realistic than RIDE 3 (feels like MotoGP'20)- many events seem to be hard and frustrating, either because AI is more aggressive and unforgiving even on lowest difficulty or when you have to pass strange Gran Turismo-like testsSo why did I change my negative mind about it?If you recently played RIDE 3 and you are used to it, you're gonna have a really hard beginning when playing this new title - that's what happened to me.Milestone didn't even try to make the game beginner-friendly. Your only chance to master the game is try and try and try again. The more you get used to it, to the current bike and track, the more it will feel comfortable. It will never be easy - even the smallest mistake can destroy your race, so it's simply a challenging experience and each win feels better because you know you deserved it.I don't know if this was the right decision for the series - we'll see.What I know is that Milestone - because of it's long time experience with motorcycle simulations - has delivered an excellent, but often really really hard racing title that some will hate, but hopefully many more just love. I tend to be one of the second ones because there are so many things that are great in RIDE 4.A final thought to consider: right now, Milestone is the one-and-only company on the market that is able to produce a high quality bike simulation. I really hope they'll sell enough units of RIDE 4 to be able to make future titles.

_childDocuments_.review: A followup to RIDE 3 which is hard to beat in high detail motorcycle riding/racing. After riding this title I can say that RIDE 4 has some improvements to show. Overall a decent title that the publishers will improve starting with and bugs that may of already been reported.  They already have done a minor update for some issues reported early. I tested racing the same bike and track in RIDE 4 then on RIDE 3. The improvement on the actual riding was almost exactly the same except for the higher level of detail in RIDE 4. If you don't have RIDE 3 and want a lot of bikes and locations right away then RIDE 3 would be your best bet (Especially if it's on sale). and see how RIDE 4 is developing. Milestone has fine tuned RIDE 3 for 2 years now and is a great title. This title rocks.

I am struggling a lot and have to do many attempts to even win a race on easy mode.+ The license-challenges and even the whole game has less to do with skill. _childDocuments_.review: OMG what a disappointment!So anticipated this game and Milestone have had the experience from the previous RIDE series to get this game perfect, however they've created a product unfit for purpose.Where do I start? Well the physics for one are just too unrealistic. I've been a biker for decades and even the worst of my bikes have never understeered like all the models in RIDE 4. Wobbles, engine pick up and characteristics (especially at the top end of rev range) are flawed. The graphics though are beyond belief but is this enough?On all the RISE/MotoGP series I ride on realistic settings with AI on hard. I've lowered everything to the lowest settings and still on some tracks the AI have better drive out the corners whereas my bike struggles for traction. THIS SHOULD NOT HAPPEN AT THE LOWEST SETTINGS! I'd say I'm quite an expert at car/bike sims so I truly feel sorry for any newbies to the game. They won't touch it again after a few hours!I remember similar complaints with RIDE 2 and Milestone fixed them with updates, however two series on to release a product so initially flawed is almost criminal.Milestone. Fix up look sharp - it's just not good enough!

_childDocuments_.review: The best modern motorcycle racing game. This is your equivalent to Forza on bikes IMO. _childDocuments_.review: Party Animals isnt just a game, its a saviour of my life. This beautiful physics-based game is a masterpiece of its kind, this was the inevitable grand upgrade from gang beasts. I didnt know how badly i needed such a game to come into my life. You see, I suffer from a lot of illnesses, you name it - i got it. Anyway, this game became a runaway escape to a vast new reality, away from all my illnesses. I didnt have the stress of doctors running in and out of my hospital room, giving me organ and blood transplants, no... this game was a whole new dimension for me. It wasnt just a game anymore, it was the reason I was saved. I played and played party animals and slowly the doctors noticed I got better. Not long after, I had mildly healed from most of my illnesses, and soon after, I didnt have them anymore. I slowly looked to my screen with the lobby screen of Party Animals, a tear shed from my eye. I impulsively hugged the screen as tears ran down my face, "Party Animals" I cried, "Thank you so much...". Party Animals had saved my life. I was free. _childDocuments_.review: There are some valid complaints regarding offline play, but this game was always intended for online play and the game doesn't deserve to be blasted with the amount of negative reviews that it has.It's an incredibly chaotic and fun casual game, with a lot of variety in maps and game modes. In one, two teams will be on two trains and you have to deliver coal to speed yourself up and make it to the goal before the other, while simultaneously committing sabotage on the other train by pulling the breaks. Another will have you and a buddy on a continuously breaking iceberg which you must try your best to stay on lest the ice cold waters take you.Another nice thing is in the last stand modes (where you try to outlast everyone else amidst a crumbling stage) is that you will always have a partner so even if you get eliminated soon into the round, you still have a chance of winning. Better still when you are dead, you can still effect the match by throwing fish, bananas and bombs which helps a lot in making falling off a stage feel less bad.The developers certainly could have done a better job with communication which they have apologised for in their recent announcement, but otherwise this is a very well made game that'll give you the experience of punching a cat in the face and watch them plummet off a bridge, which is pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Party Animals delivers uproarious multiplayer action with its physics-based gameplay and wacky characters. Whether you're brawling in a ring, racing through obstacle courses, or engaging in other silly challenges, the game promises endless laughs and chaotic fun with friends. 🤣🎮 With a diverse range of game modes, including Battle Royale, Soccer, and Sumo, Party Animals keeps the excitement fresh and engaging. Each mode offers unique objectives and challenges, ensuring there's something for everyone to enjoy and plenty of replay value. ⚽🥊  While Party Animals thrives in multiplayer settings, its lack of substantial single-player content may disappoint solo players. Without a compelling campaign or robust AI opponents, the game's longevity and appeal may be limited for those seeking solo experiences. 🕹️👤 Some players have reported encountering technical issues and bugs, including crashes, glitches, and performance issues. While these issues may vary in severity and frequency, they can disrupt gameplay and detract from the overall enjoyment of the experience. 🐛🔧  While the game's colorful and cartoonish art style contributes to its lighthearted atmosphere, some players may find the visuals overly simplistic or lacking in detail. Additional visual polish and variety could enhance the game's aesthetic appeal and immersion. 🖌️🎨 Party Animals features a limited soundtrack that may become repetitive during extended play sessions. More diverse and dynamic music tracks could help maintain the game's energetic atmosphere and prevent auditory monotony over time. 🎵🔂  Party Animals is a riotous multiplayer experience that shines brightest when played with friends. Its diverse game modes and zany gameplay ensure endless entertainment, though the lack of single-player content and occasional technical issues may dampen the fun for some. Overall, it's a wild party game that's best enjoyed in the company of others.

_childDocuments_.review: By definition this is a live service party game, without any offline capabilities which is a shame. In the past it was much worse as the game didn't even have a split screen nor any co-op based remote play, this is where I would have usually given a thumbs down review. Who crashed the party? The game have so much potential with its physics and player-to-world interactions, alternative game modes and arcades, but it seems like the most money is being poured into cosmetics to keep the game alive financially. I will not comment on this decision. This game is fun after all. Where the heck else you can punch your friend in the face for being a literal furry? The character design is cute, the physics are entertaining enough to play around and master movements over time. There is always an essence of chaos present in each game, not including player actions, vertical gameplay or item drops. There are requirements you have to meet in order to play it properly, but I will expand on these later on in this review.The anniversary and following updates have spiked an interest for this game once again, but it is worth noting that its player base seems to be declining over time nonetheless. To catch a wave and play with real players you are basically given one day per week, which in my view is enough for a game of this kind. Log in, have fun with your friends or interact with strangers, leave to comeback another week and repeat if it still brings you joy. All others days of the week are basically pointless to play at, since you will be likely matching with bots, which is a long-time issue for this game during activity dips. I will admit, it is definitely a tight time window to fit in, thus it usually occurs during the weekends.The paid content includes cosmetics and most of the times you are able to acquire it on your own terms. The community benefits heavily from all of free minor and major updates, special events and "free" battle-passes. I put quotation marks here only because most of the times you are required to earn currency needed to purchase the battle pass by playing the game continuously.It is easy to make friends, custom lobbies are the best and provide a lot of opportunities for newcomers and bots can't join these. The only downside of regular matchmaking are die-hard competitive sweats, because there is no real balance in terms of skill and team formation is random. Ending a last stand match in 3 minutes is simply ludicrous, an entire lobby basically plays a spectator for the whole duration while one guy single-handedly wins the game. It might be fun for them, but the lobby will struggle to find it amusing in the slightest. As a seasoned player I will always adjust to the play style and skill of my opponents, because I seek a chance for all participants to genuinely have a good time playing the game. Over the time you will most likely form a friend group or two and this way you can avoid all of the issues listed above, by hosting custom matches and tournaments.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this since release, I have now surpassed 500 hours in this creative masterpiece, and am desperately attempting to take a break from it, I feel like it's a good milestone to take some time and talk about it. I have no doubt I will spend thousands of hours here as the time goes. This game has been no contest the alltime best investment of my money on Steam, and that won't change simply because of how much fun I've had with it already. I laughed in the ways I didn't know I could laugh, and honestly - I really needed that. I never expected it to tick all my boxes, but it sure did.This game is goofy, silly, random and super stylish. Everything, EVERYTHING is superb- gameplay mechanics, visual presentation and the kickass funk fusion of a soundtrack. Even the tiny references here and there to various creative works around the world.Even if it doesn't seem to be your cup of tea, even if you are turned away by XYZ things about it - just play 10 or so games, and I guarantee you will have a good chuckle at some point. Even though the game is very random at times (and that's its design intention, even though I may not agree with some parts of it), there's plenty room for being competitive and showing "skill", which I personally consider important. It's this mix of pure random and skill based factors that make it more fun for me, there's a certain beauty in trying to tame the chaotic nature of the game.Oh, and it's a great place to make friends, actually really great.Now the devs themselves have admitted this is their first serious project and they are new to game development, it shows partially, but I haven't really seen anything critically bad. So far they have responded rather quickly to critical game issues, bugs, and at the same time add more and more content to the game. A lot of the criticism regarding the game I don't get, like the micro transaction stuff, there's nothing wrong with it. It's not a pay to win game or heavily micro transaction based. If you don't gamble all your "Nemo Bucks" away on eggs to get the skins that will always be available, especially now with the redesigned reward system, the developers give you around 10k of those for free as long as you reach Level 100 (a bit of a grind, but not tedious in the slightest). You can also get that currency from mystery boxes that drop daily.There are a bunch of bugs that haven't been adressed for a long time (like the bugged steam friendlist), but I can forgive that. The rest is just miscellaneous game random or ping related things, or servers lagging because more and more people flock to the game.All in all, I find it simply great and it has quickly become one of my all-time favorite games. I hope it thrives and flourishes for a long time, and more people get to experience this amazing unhinged chaos. 🙂Here's a little video I made back when I just started playing the game:
