_childDocuments_.review: First things first, this game is awesome, I've played about 6 hours in the closed beta, and its a fun game, but there are somethings the developers could have done and shouldn't have done that would have made this game better. My first gripe with it is that it has excessive micro transactions, It would make sense if it was a free game, but as it is now, there is no reliable way to get the premium currency after you get all the achievements, and levels (making you pay for more skins). First there is a fortnite like item shop with rotating skins in it to make you fear of not being able to get it again after the time is up or FOMO, then there is a gacha or loot box system where you get you egg coins and basically gamble for a skin, this is baffling. we already paid 20 - 30 dollars on this game and now were expected to pay more? I know they have to make money but this is way too excessive. Next is the game modes, why isn't there a queue??? Every time there is team mode, which I really don't like playing as there is no "Team" as everyone is just doing there own thing, I end up leaving the game and getting a match penalty. just add a queue for the game modes you want to play in, pretty simple. Next and this is a big one for some people, why is there no offline play? You wanna play offline split screen with some buddys? Too bad, because that isn't allowed, because how are you gonna spend money if you are offline? Speaking of split screen, it seems to me like split screen has been more of a after thought, which really disappoints me because split screen is what half of these party games are. if you didn't want to read me ranting, basically Party Animals is a phenomenal game help back by weird design choices like not being able to queue for certain game modes, not being able to play offline, a messy split screen, and excessive micro transactions. If they got these things fixed (which I highly doubt for the micro transactions) then this game would be a ten out of ten for me, but how it is now I can't rate it higher than a six out of ten.

_childDocuments_.review: incredibly rage-inducing even though it's supposed to be a casual family game. if you don't believe me, you probably haven't seen enough content creators play this game. everything about the game is executed well except for the combat system which is incredibly scuffed and inconsistent. for example, you can only reliably do a heavy punch with the right hook, it almost never does the left hook. i'm not sure if this is keyboard-exclusive, but either way, it makes the heavy punch about as worse as throwing haymakers. there's no settings to change this so it's the left hand instead that does heavy punches, i've searched the game settings several times, and there doesn't seem to be a way to control which hand throws the punch. another example is the grab feature, whether for climbing or for picking up objects. it never picks up reliably, and there's a 50/50 you have to try more than once to pick an object up. for climbing, it's absolutely insufferable; it's an okay feature for most of the maps, except for the ones where climbing is required to be the victor. on top of that, some weapons are nearly impossible to counter and only with a stroke of luck you can best them; there's very little skill involved in countering opponents with weapons because of how awkward the combat and movement is. another thing i don't really understand is the inability to have offline matches with ai or LAN. it's a basic feature most combat party games have, but this doesn't. you can make a custom match and the ai has three difficulties, but it has to be online. a waste of bandwidth if you want to play without encountering people targeting you because you are on a hot streak of three matches in a row where your randomly selected teammate is afk for the entirety of the game and only gets kicked in the dying seconds of the game because despite you reporting them as afk, the counter persists at counting down from 30 seconds. if your teammate is afk for any amount of time, you're pretty much crippled, which ruins the fun of the game where you work together to win. despite there being microtransactions, i don't see an issue with that being present. the currency you can buy is for buying cosmetics; no weapons or abilities are locked behind anything in this game. that being said, there's a lot of good things about this game, such as the music, the post-match photo, and the maps. the visuals are great too and run surprisingly well. they continue to add more characters and cosmetics, ever since the game was first released. a lot of people compare this to gang beasts for its graphics and combat, but i would say because of the additional mechanics in combat that differ it from that game, it has some extra downsides that make me enjoy gang beasts, but not this game. hopefully the combat and movement is adjusted eventually, because it makes the game incredibly unfun for a percentage of people. i encourage you to only purchase this game if you have a lot of friends to play with for custom matches, although the vast majority of achievements are locked behind quick-play(matchmaking) to prevent you from farming them since some unlock rewards. if you're achievement hunting, don't bother unless you want to spend most likely hundreds of hours for completion. if you're wanting to play for pvp, don't bother either, it's less pvp then most combat games because of the lack of control you have over most of your movements.

_childDocuments_.review: Tired of having to put up a front on a work day shift with annoying coworkers or dealing with rude customers? Did you have an argument with a relative or a friend? Invite them to a match on this game with the premise of having a good time, under the disguise of calling a truce and...Give them hell with your fluffy paws!First of all you will never know for sure if the people teaming up with you are going to play against you. And that's the first lesson you have to learn for surviving this cute animal game turned into "The Squid Game" show just for the mere laugh of the impersonators acting as your team mates.You can start by punching the title screen letters as a warming up for what's going to follow.And once in the proper menu don't fall in love with the cuteness displayed, the characters might be fluffy but they hit hard! I ended up being a sandwich more than once and not in a sexual way... The music made your shoulders dance as possessed by some unknown force that could even bring back the old compilations of summer songs mixes they used to sell in CD format. And yet here I am being a dinosaur talking about obsolete mediums to hear music and not being able to use a proper T-Rex as my little representative...The game mechanics are explained in a tutorial which will make you think asap about switching for a controller, as your real life weapon, to stand a chance against all the hungry creatures that want to throw you away from the map in the most awkward yet funny ways possible. Is really hard to concentrate on punching the right buttons to accomplish something while dying by a laugh attack that can make you sound like an octogenarian being smoking for almost their entire life. Add not peeing yourself in the process due to the aforementioned laughter and also the arduous quest of remembering to breathe correctly, yeah, air is necessary to some degree.If you get three stars on the tutorial an achievement would be yours but that doesn't mean you are prepared for the authentic showdown…You know nothing... Little Poochi Snow…As for the game itself… Or should it be better to say games? In this case due to the different possibilities lying ahead... You can vote the maps you prefer and even if the premise is smash like Hulk used to say, the primary objectives can be different.Daily quests can be completed to gain experience faster, and with that you will unlock new animals, cosmetics such as skins, avatars and even in-game currency.You can see how far you are progressing to keep earning rewards. And even if it seems like a season pass, it's not.I am so grateful to the heavens since for once in more than a decade these game developers are not trying to get on our wallets the nasty way! Now that all the online games, and even some of them not being multiplayer/online use this as a basic feature, that could be even mistaken by some kind of commandments list in the unknown Bible of developing games. So yeah, be happy because just by playing you can unlock or earn everything needed to harvest a wild collection. This is not a dream of the past glorious days anymore. HOORAY!Friendly reminder: Don't try to say cheese in the photos, clench your teeth because they will surely be blown away!I am not a “living picture" of that statement!If you didn't have trust issues beforehand, soon you will!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Chaos Galore: Imagine a brawl where fluffy animals fling each other off cliffs, into rivers, or just flail hilariously—it’s pure, unadulterated chaos.So. Much. Cuteness.: Ever wanted to karate chop a corgi? Or suplex a penguin? Here’s your chance, and they’re adorable.Easy to Pick Up, Hard to Put Down: Anyone can hop in and start whacking their friends in seconds, but the laughs will keep you hooked for hours.Party Perfect: Whether you’re screaming in a room with friends or cackling online, this game guarantees peak entertainment.Wacky Variety: From tug-of-war over a candy bar to frantic free-for-alls, every mode is a new flavor of madness.Cons:Repetitive Chaos: Let’s be real, you’re here for the mayhem—not deep strategy—but the gameplay loop might wear thin after a long session.Overall:Party Animals is like a sugar rush in video game form: cute, chaotic, and endlessly fun. Grab some friends, pick your favorite floof, and prepare for the most ridiculous brawls you’ll ever have.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, which IMO is it's main selling point. I've been waiting so long for a fun dumb knock around party game with friends. I was half tempted to buy Rumble Party or even Gang Beasts again (I have it on PS), but saw this game advertised a year ago and was waiting ever since. All the reviews complaining about a "predatory" store and battle pass, are way over exaggerating. The game never shoves it in your face, or has a paid for battle pass alongside the free one, there's just one "battle pass" everyone gets and you unlock currency/skins/characters by playing the game. You can also do the same by completing challenges like: "Win *insert game mode* 5 times" or "Get 5 knockouts in a game" etc. So unless you're really upset that you didn't get a vampire skin for the cat or something while it was a limited time, you'll honestly live. There's way more predatory games out there, and this barely counts. IMO $20 is a steal, and this game deserves support, here's hoping it isn't just the next Fall Guys or something because this game is guaranteed fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a blast.It's Gang Beasts but more polished, with streamlined and simplified controls, but has a similar level in skill ceiling still. And more fluffy. And it's not left broken with desync and bugs. You can run properly, which makes your punches hit harder and you really just have to press jump and then press kick to do a drop-kick, which will lend you flying away if your running. There's a slow-motion effect when you knock-out  adversaries or when you get knocked-out, which feels so freaking good.Broken Arrow is pretty much Blimp, Typhoon is similar to Trawler, Blackhole Lab is similar to Vents, etc. but there's a lot more maps with more unique mechanics. There's also Smash mode where the winning team gain points rounds after rounds, playing different maps, where you can select buffs inbetween. Then there's a Kart mode which is pretty much the same as Mario Kart.Good stuff!There's a Battle Pass system where you gain cosmetics as well as Cookies, Nemo Bucks and Egg Coins. The pass is free and infinite so you never really have to pay a dime to have fun and get some cosmetics you want. Nemo Bucks is the currency you can spend real money on. You can buy cosmetics in the Item Shop with Nemo Bucks or Cookies. You can buy more Cookies with Nemo bucks if you want and you can use Egg Coins or pay Nemo buckss directly to get Surprise Eggs.Nothing pay to win, really.I haven't seen any issues with the game and I'd say it's pretty much perfect for anyone who wants to have some fun time punching and drop-kicking cute fluffy animals.
_childDocuments_.name: Party Animals

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, do you crave fun? Do you get some joy out of some fuzzy cartoon animals beating the ever-loving sense out of each other? Then I might have a game that might deserve your attention. Just don’t tell the Peta organization, although if you look into their dealings, they might have actually harmed more animals then they have saved.Gameplay Grade: A+Party animals is family friendly casual type of game, where the player takes control of one of a selection of playable animals whose objective is to brawl it out over various game modes. Currently there are three modes available to play. Might not seem all that much but each one is enabled to be modified further with the game lobby settings.To help spice things up from time to time and keep things fresh, random items at random intervals will fall from the sky similar in such games like Super Smash Bros. Items such as a frying pan to send folks flying, plunger that sticks to people, freeze gun for well freezing other players, a taser to try out electroshock therapy, and plenty of others goofy little things. So, if you like, you can be a rabbit with a baseball bat, smacking down a dragon only to be drop kicked by a cat in swat tactical gear inside of a blackhole generator.At its heart this game is a party game which means it is meant to be played with friends, or with strangers if you do not have any via quick play option. However, I must admit, the game loses its luster after around 2 hours because everyone has their enjoyment for the day and watching animals smack each other with shovels stops being as funny as it used to. That is until next and folks are trash talking towards one another and just enjoying their time being spent among friends in discord. This is a game you do not play for long periods of time, but after a break this game reminds fun and enjoyable.I would give the gameplay an A+ for outstanding work. This game knew what it wanted to be, and it achieved it in this category. Presentation Grade: BThe presentation within the game is phenomenal. The usage of bright colors makes things appear more cute then it actually is, which given game’s style choice helps it tremendously. In an age where a lot of game developers are trying to push more pixels and higher fidelity, they fail to realize that given time that their style choice will fade where games that went with a softer more bright color style will last far longer. For example, you can look towards the Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker. The sound design is spot on especially with all the little items you can pick up and use. Yet the only real draw back within the presentation is that if you do creation content and have this game, you must disable the music within the game because it is copyrighted, thus if you publish videos or live stream it, you will get struck by the copyright system, and as of the time of posting there is no streamer mode. This is horrible because we live in the age of the internet, and does things that are counterproductive towards the age. No one would have much desire to share content of this game if they are going to get copyright struck.Presentation earns a Solid B for doing the minimum to stand out but not going above and beyond.Drawbacks Grade: FOnto the negatives, this game does not feature an offline play mode in any capacity. Yes, you can play split screen locally however you must connect to an online server initially to be able to play. This takes away from the customer because say these servers go offline, then your game is no longer available to be played. For recent example of this look towards Payday 3. You can have your online services but allow players to play the game they of bought.The next thing I’m going to bring up is not excusable. The original description of the game had blatantly said offline play was in the game. However, it was then later removed shortly after the game’s release due to backlash for not having said mode. The developers had given a news post on Wednesday September 20th stating that this was due a translation error. Granted things get lost in translation but you had 2 years to comb over everything since the last beta to launch. Even if was not meant to, you have falsely advertised your game. This game also has an in-game shop where you can exchange your money for paid currency in currency packs. Common practice in current affairs but they also do the thing where you cannot directly purchase the cute outfits you desire and will you will have left over currency. This is known tactic, which may be known as a “Dark Pattern” to direct the player to buy even more currency. Now I will state that a large number of outfits can be obtained through standard play given time, but that doesn’t excuse the fact that you can exchange your paid currency of a 2 to 15 rate to buy the earnable outfits much faster if you have the money. I also need point out that the shop store is a rotating one which is known to pressure people into buying things because they do not know when something will be available again if ever. Through leveling your account, you will earn up to $20ish dollars of paid currency for free. Some outfits could be more expensive than the game itself. You are also unable to purchase the outfits directly and must buy the currency packs.There is also loot boxes but referred to as surprised eggs, you can earn a token during play via leveling up or by purchasing a spin via paid currency. As the game currently stands, you can only get set number of spins for free from leveling up. It reminds to be seen if the player will be able to earn more after reaching max level. If I recall Loot boxes are banned in the Netherlands and legislation around the world is picking up about the issue.Either through lack of attention, incompetence, or outright direct design, this game has a Dark Pattern. If you like to have a thorough explanation or further information, The Youtube channels Techquickie and Extra history have done video content that explains this further then I can in this steam review due to character limitations. In short, this game will never ask for your confirmation when you purchase something. The F.T.C. here in the United States has been battling these types of issues in court cases. Please add a confirmation button to the game.Final Grade: C+Greatness can be easily ruined by horrible actions, hopefully this game can improve upon the groundwork that has been laid. Party Animals can easily get an A+ but the drawbacks are too great. I want this game to be a success because video games are my hobby and I want the best for everyone. Sadly I would have to leave a not recommended here because there is no neutral setting in the process.Consider joining the Steam curator group:

_childDocuments_.review: Forget the picket fences and cozy crafting of other survival games. Party Animals throws you headfirst into a chaotic world where the cutest creatures become the most deranged brawlers. This isn't your grandma's tea party – it's a hilarious physics-based battle royale where the only thing softer than the characters are their landings.Party Animals' charm lies in its utter pandemonium. The wobbly physics turns every punch, flail, and flying body into a side-splitting spectacle. Sending your best friend plummeting off a cliff or into a spinning fan never gets old – just make sure you're not next!Don't let the cuddly exteriors fool you. Party Animals offers a surprising amount of depth. Choose your favorite fighter from a quirky cast, each with its particular style and humor! Multiple game modes keep things fresh, from free-for-alls to objective-based battles where teamwork (or lack thereof) is key. Play soccer games, survive black holes, or be the last animal standing in a submerging submarine!While the core gameplay is a blast, there are a few things to consider. The physics-based controls take some getting used to, and mastering throws and dodges requires practice. Half the battle in Party Animals is fighting the controller! (and button smashing to get up~). The current map selection, while creative, could be expanded for long-term play. Local multiplayer feels less polished compared to the smooth online experience.Party Animals is a fantastic party game for anyone looking to unleash their inner animal (and unleash some hilarious chaos) with friends. The wacky physics, multiple modes, and adorable cast create an unforgettable experience. While the learning curve exists and the maps could be more plentiful, Party Animals is a must-have for your next game night. Just remember – friendships may be tested, but your sides will be split with laughter!If you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator!

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 Chaotic Fun with Friends Online! While I do understand the frustration of not having Offline Multiplayer (Especially when it was described as having had it) the game has been an absolute blast so far. I have only played a few rounds with randoms, and have to acknowledge that the most fun I've had with the game and the most time spent has been playing with lobbies of my friends online. Minus a few spelling errors here and there which will likely be patched out the game is pretty amazingly polished with my only gripe being that I didn't receive some rewards for having played the beta. Between the hilarious animations, game modes, weapons, and adorable characters there is an enormous amount of content for $30 dollars. The majority of the 18+ maps each have a unique core mechanic at play and while one of the game modes could use more maps, they are exceptionally fun to play as they are.From my play time so far, it would seem like the plethora of characters and cosmetics all seem to be unlock-able at some point down the road without having to pay for micro transactions, and there are A LOT of characters and cosmetics available right from the start. Even with my short amount of playtime and the time I played during the demo I unlocked 2 or 3 characters and some really awesome cosmetics for them as well. Game looks great, plays great, and if you have some friends to play with online it's absolutely worth the money. As one more note on the offline side of things:I bought a copy of the game also hoping to play it with my niece and nephew offline and I know they don't have plans to bring it offline, but I do wish they'd reconsider. In a very small concession if you weren't aware of it, you can at minimum have another person join you locally to go online with you.

_childDocuments_.review: PROs:Cute art style, adorable characters: Many players on Steam have praised the game's art style and character design in their reviews. The animal characters in the game are designed to look like plush toys, with cute and cuddly appearances. Whether they are walking, running, or attacking, their actions are cute and lovable, which makes them highly attractive to players. This allows players to enjoy visual pleasure during the gameplay, making it highly appealing to players who prefer cute styles.Excellent physics engine, innovative gameplay: The physics-based game mechanics provide players with a unique gaming experience. The actions of the animals are realistically reflected by the physics engine, such as their movements, attacks, and collisions, which are all very realistic and interesting. Players can take advantage of these physical characteristics to engage in intense competition with other players or interact with the environment. For example, they can knock their opponents out with a punch or use scene props and traps to eliminate them. This innovative gameplay keeps players hooked.Diverse game modes, varied maps: "Battle Royale" features multiple game modes, including survival mode, score mode, and arcade mode, each with its own unique gameplay and challenges. At the same time, the game has multiple maps, each with unique terrain and environmental settings, providing players with a diverse gaming experience. Players can try out various strategies and tactics in different modes and maps, increasing the game's replayability and longevity.Strong social interaction: This is a game that is well-suited for playing with friends, as the online multiplayer mode allows players to interact and compete with players from all over the world, enhancing the game's social aspect. Players can team up with friends to take on other players, enhancing their friendship and interaction through voice communication and cooperation during the game.Potential for continued updates: The developers have indicated that they will continue to maintain and update the game for a longer period of time, which has left players looking forward to the game's future development. Some players believe that if the developers can continuously introduce new content, such as more characters, maps, and game modes, the game's quality and replayability will be further enhanced.CONs:High price, low value-to-price ratio: This is a problem that has been joked about by players on Steam. The standard version of the game costs 98 yuan, and the deluxe version costs 147 yuan, which is relatively high for a party game. Especially compared to the content volume, many players feel that the price does not match the value. The number of maps in the game is relatively small, and some players feel that the gameplay may become monotonous after a period of time, so they are dissatisfied with the price.Unstable servers and serious queue problems: Server instability was a more prominent problem during the initial launch of the game. Players need to queue up to enter the game, and there may be lag, disconnections, etc. during gameplay, which seriously affects players' gaming experience. Although the official has made some optimization and improvement, the server problem is still one of the focuses of players. Controversy over the in-game purchase system: The in-game purchase system has also caused dissatisfaction among players. The game adopts a buy-to-play system combined with in-game skin purchases, and some players feel that the in-game purchase price is high, and some rare skins can only be obtained through the egg machine, which makes players feel that it is not fair. In addition, players also have some controversy over the fact that the game has an in-game purchase system based on the buy-to-play system.Insufficient optimization and high system requirements: Some players have reported that the game's optimization is not good enough, and the system requirements are high. During gameplay, there may be frame rate drops and lag, especially when playing locally in split-screen mode, which will cause a significant drop in PC frame rate and affect the smoothness of the game.

You have no choice but to sit there not playing the game...At least in games like World of tanks and such if you die, you can return to the garage and pick a different vehicle to play another round with. _childDocuments_.review: Party Animals is a fun game with creative levels and cute characters you can earn through leveling, including additional costumes that can be earned through achievements or the shop as well. So in that sense, there is a lot of variety in which a player can choose and earn through progression. However there is a lot of unexplained bs I find myself experiencing the longer this game exists and I play it. I'm discovering I mostly experience this on a handful of last stand maps which include Ichiban, Winter Is Coming, Wind Tunnel, and Gator Valley. Ichiban seems to suffer from irregular and varied windows in which the player will be instantly knocked out from a punch or item used by another player. Not to mention it feels I have significantly less time to jump back up out of the gas than others players do, even dying within a second after losing consciousness regardless if I did before I was thrown down there. Winter is Coming is one of the most bs levels I've played given it seems I freeze a lot quicker than others players do at the end game while they can get up instantly or roll back without ever freezing at the end way too often to not be noticed. I see this happen on variety of other levels as well mentioned above at times including a handful of team levels. I don't know if that's due to anything in particular but it's becoming more apparent the longer I own this game. Because of that alone, I find myself playing this game less and less due to the bs luck people get in general. As mentioned, they are able to wake from knockouts, get back onto ledges, or even roll back into play before timeouts on various levels way quicker than I can. I don't want to hear the "lack of skill" and that kinda crap. I've played this game during Beta over 20 hours including the version from a couple years ago. It wasn't this bad at the start but you notice it more obviously the longer you play, whether a session or playing the game for a number of weeks. I'm seeing a game become less fair in non team games the longer I play this game. Sadly that means it's becoming a crappier product unless it's 4v4 a lot of the time to balance out the unexplained bs.Would I recommend the games? Yes. However I can't say I tend to have much fun outside of 4v4s with a friend as randoms are insufferable to deal with as your team mates in a 2v2 setting or the fact they expect you to fully carry them.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a crazy ride! After all and all, I finally aced the achievements! I always wait for full achievements to make a review, this one has just been one of the tougher ones, if not the toughest! I really admire this game in most of the aspects. You don't often get a game that is this replay-able, this carefully designed and this well-executed. As a party game it has the right vibe --- the competitive aspect works just fine, not too much nor too light. On the other hand, the physics in the game hits different --- It may look just like some other games which I won't name, but you have to play it to know how different they are. Not to mention the cute visuals --- Probably is what attracts people in the first place! While the game is casual, the achievements are quite challenging. As much as I struggled with some of them, I have to say they are well designed. They provide a sufficient amount of challenges, and in the mean time fun to attempt and does not ruin the game for you teammates (for the most part, some of them does require you to be a little selfish).There has been many controversies around the game. The price does prevent a significant amount of my friends from joining me. The devs may not have taken the right response in many occasions. However, rarely do I see a hateful comment on the game itself: almost everyone agrees this game is great to begin with. Some may think overpriced, some may hate the micro-transactions, but that does not hinder its outstanding gameplay!Overall I would recommend this to my friends (which I already did), but also to any of you who stump upon this review. I wish this game could give you sufficient amount of joy, I meant it wholeheartedly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game could be good, but suffers from the typical problems of online-only multiplayer games.  Every unlockable cosmetic either costs too much of one of the forms of in-game currency, or requires ridiculous amounts of time spent playing to unlock.  The rewards of the leveling system are pathetic for the amount of grinding you have to do to level, and the experience needed to level up increases each time, resulting in diminishing returns.  And if you're not winning every single match, you're barely gaining any experience.  The game feels like a grind.  Not to mention, many of the rewards for leveling up are essentially worthless avatars, avatar frames, or emojis rather than characters or character costumes.  No one cares about unlocking emojis.The core gameplay is fun but clumsy, and too many characters and costumes are locked behind leveling and the in-game shop.  How is that a good model for a casual family game?  Start being more generous with character and costume unlocks, and come up with some more character designs (try some new species besides cats and dogs; 9 variations of cats/dogs are more than enough).  This game could be brilliant, but it falls short because of the problems above.

_childDocuments_.review: Party Animals is one of my most played games in my library and I continue to enjoy it on every revisit. But the more I play it, the more I see that it's difficult to recommend to newcomers. On the surface you can imagine that it's a casual party game with cute animals punching each other; however, this is deeply contrasted by the extremely competitive nature of the in-game community. Players who have previous experience with similar physics-based games, such as Gang Beasts or Human Fall Flat, should have a knack for Party Animals and it'd be an easy recommendation. But players with no prior experience should carefully consider if this game is right for them. The following sections of this review will elaborate on my complicated love and hate story with Party Animals.The fighting controls are more complex than Gang Beasts' and random weapons spawn on the arena to spice up each round. There are several modes to play such as Last Stand (2v2v2v2 or 4v4), Team Score (4v4), and Cabin (for casual off-brand Uno games). The combat is very rewarding once you get a proper handle on it. Exp earned unlocks unique rewards up to level 100, and the achievements also unlock costumes and currency. Players who invest enough time into Party Animals can get around the gacha and game currency limits by gaining experience past level 100 to earn daily mystery boxes containing cookies, Nemo bucks, or lottery coins. I never had a hard time buying the costumes I like in the game's shop because I've earned and saved plenty of currency.The majority of my hours was spent in solo play but I had more fun whenever I was in a party with friends. Team work is at the heart of each game mode and it's very fun to embrace it with like-minded players. My favorite map of all time is Fluffy Redemption. The respawns are unlimited and there's room for mistakes. I like to switch my roles whenever needed, I could be placing coals into the firebox for a few minutes, attack the opposite team's train to slow them down, and then go back to my train to defend it.I love the animal and environment physics! Animals can be tossed out of the arena with the right momentum and movement. Each Last Stand map has a hazard that gets deadlier as time passes. Castleween is notable for its random environment destruction. I also enjoy how it's possible to knock out animals with random stuff such as lamps, fishes, and hats. There's no shortage of crazy stuff that can happen in Party Animals. The replayability is practically infinite.The initial two hours played on Party Animals may not be enough time to determine if the game is right for some players. In my case, I had a blast during my first 100 hours even while I was solo queuing for matches. But I'm sure newcomers will be frustrated once they encounter the tryhards and toxics in the community.The matchmaking in Party Animals is split into 2 categories: Quick Match and Custom Games. Custom Games offers limited exp gained daily, and Quick Match allows you to level up indefinitely to level 100 + 3 daily mystery boxes. Custom Games are filled with AI bots and it's not obvious which ones have human players. Quick Match is a very simplified system with no variety of options. You can't select Last Stand or Team Score as the mode you'd prefer to join, and you can't opt to join a queue filled with other solo queue'd players. Instead, Quick Match will join together solo queue'd players with coordinated players in a party, and they'll have to vote on a Last Stand or Team Score map. This creates an environment that throws newcomers into a trial by fire. I've read other players' reviews on Party Animals and I can definitely see where they're coming from: the game turns into a waiting simulator after being eliminated quickly in Last Stand. I find that Team Score modes are more casual than Last Stand, and it'd be a great boon for newcomers if there was a "Quick Match - Team Score" option.Quick Match is also the only practical way to earn rewards + exp. Winning will award a lot of exp towards a level up, and losing will award very minimal exp regardless of how well you've played. And many of the achievements require amazing feats in Quick Match. Here's an example: "666 - In Buzz Ball, single-handedly accumulate all points for your team and win (Quick Match)." These tryhard achievements contrast the intended spirit of a casual party game. All in all, players are encouraged to play competitively to extremes if they want to earn currency or unique costumes. It's no surprise that there're so many tryhards and toxics, not to the mention the AFK players who farm exp.There's a lot to love about Party Animals, but there's also a lot to hate about it. I keep returning to Party Animals because I love physics-based games and platformers. I think the good outweighs the bad, despite having many complaints. Newcomers, on the other hand, should beware of the Quick Matchmaking and the community's git gud attitude. Party Animals' learning curve is pretty high but will reward those who are willing to overcome it. My final rating for the game: 9/10. My rating for the in-game community: 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: So after playing for a few hours, I heard about the review bombing. And a good half of them are about the micro transactions which...seem plain dumb. One half of THOSE is people saying "Why are some skins more than the cost of the game!?" whilst the others are "This game is expensive, How dare they!" and to both parties I ask....Have you been sleeping under a rock since the 90's? Any modern AAA game is 3x the cost of Party Animals and most will have micro transactions in them as well. Call of Duty costs far more than this game AND has skins that cost more than this game. War Thunder, a 'free to play' game has vehicles in it that cost as much as a AAA game, and people suck it up like fine wine. The other half are a split between servers [which I can't attest to], and Offline mode. There are people upset that this game has no solo mode. A game called...PARTY Animals...has no solo mode. Colour me surprised! Why would you ever pick up a game that has always presented itself as a multiplayer brawler and think it has a solo mode. It's like people have lost their critical thinking skills. Onto brighter things, the game plays well. It has a simple premise and it nails it, the brawls are intense and though sometimes I am frustrated by a random lucky punch from an opponent, in the very next round I'll be crying with laughter as I knock someone into next week with a lolipop. If you enjoy the sort of game that has low downtime between games, can make your sides hurt with laughing and provides a real rush when you get on a spree of knockouts then I strongly recommend this game. If you think having an item shop or playing online is a sin, free up the lobby space.

Some more interesting than others imo but still fun nonetheless.For a $20 indie game, I feel like a lot of these "problems" should get overlooked, since in the grand scheme of things they aren't that important. But if u think the game looks fun give it a try and form your own opinion. If the "offline" mode or skins end up being that big of a problem. This games not for u anyways. These do not prevent u from playing the actual game at all. I honestly thought what was in the 2020 demo was going to be whole game basically. I.e a couple of maps and beating up your friends. 3 years later they added so much more than I could've imagined.Bottom line, if u like the gameplay you'll enjoy it. _childDocuments_.review: One one hand it's a very nice and absolutely addicting multi player game.On the other hand, I MASSIVELY dislike is the in-game money-making scheme. There are a bazillion characters and any cool characters have to be purchased or drawn from an egg dispenser lottery (also for money). The despicable thing is, the algorithm also draws characters that you already have. And in that case exchanges it to another in-game currency that mostly buys common characters. On top of that some characters can only be bought with real currency. So if you ever want ALL the characters you have to sink HUNDREDS of dollars in this game, if not even thousands.Another critique are the loading times which are absolutely horrible. In Smash-Mode where you have a different level each round, you almost spend more time waiting at the loading screen than playing. There's also just a handful of levels, so I don't really understand why they can't already be loaded in the background while you're playing.In conclusion I can only recommend this game under the pretense that you just enjoy it for what it is: A little online fighting game, that will always try to bait you into spending more money.

_childDocuments_.review: A Long Wait in Vain: My Disappointing Journey with Party AnimalsAs a dedicated gamer, I've eagerly anticipated the release of "Party Animals" for what felt like an eternity. With teasers and promises swirling around for three long years, my excitement knew no bounds. The premise of adorable animals duking it out in chaotic party games seemed like a recipe for endless entertainment. Sadly, after finally getting my hands on the game, my hopes came crashing down in disappointment.The initial charm of Party Animals cannot be denied. Its cute, cuddly characters and whimsical arenas instantly put a smile on your face. From cats to dogs to bunnies, each furry contestant has its own unique appeal, and the game's colorful aesthetics are a visual treat. However, beyond the surface, the game begins to unravel.One of the most glaring issues is the lack of content. After three years of development, one would expect a plethora of mini-games, arenas, and customization options. Instead, Party Animals offers a disappointingly small selection of mini games that grow stale far too quickly. The handful of arenas feels like a missed opportunity for diverse and exciting settings for these animal brawls. There's a stark absence of a compelling single-player experience, leaving solo players with nothing but an empty party.Party Animals also disappoints in terms of longevity. With such a limited selection of games and lackluster mechanics, the game's replayability quickly dwindles. After a few hours of play, it's challenging to find motivation to return to the same handful of minigames.Even more disheartening is the missed opportunity for online play. Given Party Animals' potential for raucous multiplayer fun, the omission of robust online features is a letdown. The absence of competitive modes and leaderboards leaves players with little incentive to engage with the game beyond the occasional couch co-op session with friends.It's worth noting that Party Animals could have been a vastly different experience if the developers had taken the time to listen to player feedback during its three-year development cycle. However, it appears that the game was rushed to release without addressing these fundamental issues.In conclusion, "Party Animals" was a game I waited three long years for, hoping for a fantastic party game experience. Sadly, it failed to live up to the lofty expectations it had set. The lack of content, uninspired gameplay, and absence of online features make it a game that quickly loses its charm. It's a reminder that hype can sometimes lead to crushing disappointment, and in the case of Party Animals, the wait was ultimately in vain.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it feels like it has a little bit of everything anyone is ever looking for in a party game.  It is silly, goofy, sometimes enraging, and wholesome.  The toxic player base that flies and swarms overhead most multiplayer games is extremely small for this game, ofc you get the occasional toxic player, but out of all the multiplayer games I've played (yes I've played a lot, yes a good amount of them have also been party games) this is the most wholesome of the fan bases.  Another great thing about this game is it is completely playable without comms, a lot of multiplayer games your performance basically relies on who has the most mics available, but these little guys are so wobbly and wonky that comms basically don't do anything except allow you to rage at your friends if that is what you so desire.  Also the little emoticons, they have one for basically everything it is actually impressive out of all the games I've played they have the cutest, silliest, and the most variety for emoticons.  And if the main gameplay doesn't suit you, you can literally just go start up a  custom lobby which you can make open so randoms can join (if you don't have any friends) and surprisingly the lobbies are actually pretty popular and I often have full lobbies, where you can just play uno or find treasure, drink, start a bar fight, or just vibe!I love this game, obsessed even, I think about this game all hours of the day, when I am playing other games I think about this game and how much I'd rather be playing this.  All my friends are tired of me asking to play it, they are sick of me conning them into playing multiple times a day even.  I love this game so much that you, yes you can even play with me if you download this game, add me and invite me I will be summoned to join your party, I may not be good but I will be there TRUST.  I think everyone should play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so disappointed by Party Animals.  I had hoped to be able to play local couch co-op last night but the implementation of this feature is an absolute afterthought at best.  I had controllers all controlling player one, with no real understanding as to why - not had this problem in other couch games, so why this?  Probably because Recreate Games' goal was to focus on a single player per game, matchmaking online model.  I didn't buy this game expecting a live service model, and the always online aspect has put me off completely.  This game sorely needs an offline only couch co-op mode, skipping the necessity for logging in to a server.  Why?  Because once this game for whatever reason dies and the servers pulled, it's completely useless like any other live service game.  I sincerely hope the developers listen to their community and the criticism they've faced and make plans to rectify it.  Until then this is categorically not a party game.

_childDocuments_.review: Party Animals is a fun and chaotic multiplayer party game developed by Recreate Games. It is designed to offer an entertaining, competitive experience where players control cute, anthropomorphic animals in a series of wacky, physics-based mini-games. The game combines elements of combat, teamwork, and mayhem, with an emphasis on fun and laughter rather than skillful precision.Gameplay Overview:In Party Animals, players take control of various adorable animal characters—such as dogs, cats, and even dinosaurs—as they compete in a series of fast-paced, silly mini-games. The core gameplay revolves around brawling, using basic controls to punch, grab, throw, and slam opponents in over-the-top arenas. However, the game’s quirky physics system means that characters can move in unpredictable ways, creating hilarious and sometimes absurd outcomes during gameplay.The game features a range of mini-games that can include traditional battle royale-style combat, team-based objectives, and survival challenges. The goal is to outlast or defeat your opponents in fun, absurd ways, all while avoiding hazards and navigating obstacle-filled environments. With its simple mechanics, Party Animals is accessible for players of all skill levels.Features:Multiplayer Chaos: The game supports both local and online multiplayer, allowing up to 8 players to compete in various party modes. The more players involved, the more chaotic and entertaining the experience becomes.Cute and Customizable Characters: Players can choose from a variety of adorable, customizable animal characters, each with unique skins and accessories, adding personality and flair to the gameplay.Wacky Physics and Controls: The physics system creates unpredictable and funny moments as characters struggle to stay upright, fling themselves into hazards, or awkwardly try to grab onto things.Variety of Mini-Games: Party Animals offers a wide range of mini-games, from free-for-all brawls to team challenges, with each one offering a unique, dynamic experience.Colorful and Whimsical Aesthetics: The game’s visuals are bright, colorful, and filled with cartoonish charm, contributing to its lighthearted and entertaining vibe.Platforms:Party Animals is available on platforms like PC (Steam) and consoles, making it accessible for a broad audience. It supports cross-play between different platforms, allowing friends to join in regardless of their preferred gaming system.In Summary:Party Animals is a playful and chaotic party game that delivers fun for both casual and competitive players. With its adorable characters, unpredictable physics, and variety of wacky mini-games, it offers an engaging and entertaining experience that is perfect for multiplayer sessions with friends or online matches. Whether you’re throwing your opponents into a pit or teaming up to complete challenges, Party Animals ensures plenty of laughs and absurd moments.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like, but let's be real and address all the negatives first and foremost:1) The game is always played with 8 people. So if you've only got three friends who own the game, prepare to be matched with 8 random internet strangers, some of whom are probably 5 years old, all of whom are pretty awful. "Well, that's not so bad, as long as my friends and I are on a team," I hear you say. *ahem*2) Whether your game is a free for all, four teams of two, or two teams of four is entirely dependent on the arena selected and, I'll remind you, random internet strangers will be the ones controlling at least a considerable slice of this vote. 3) You could work around issues 1 and 2 if the game would take a leaf from Rocket League's playbook and allow you and your group of friends to select the sort of match you'd like to play before queuing up. Seriously, why can't me and 3 friends select "4v4 matchmaking" and then be presented ONLY with arenas that are compatible with that? AT THIS STAGE, I'M NOT ASKING FOR NEW ARENAS OR GAMEPLAY MECHANICS -- just a filter!4) Some new game modes would be helpful, but even they don't require all new arenas to be made. Ice Hockey, Soccer, etc could still be fun even in a 2v2 setting. But no, you *have* to be online in this PARTY game with "PARTY" literally written in the name. And the "why" you have to be online might be the biggest downside of this game by far:5) This is a game that you purchase (for $20 USD, no less) that then expects you to shell out money indefinitely for costumes and characters. I want you to pay attention to the quotation marks I'm about to use here, because they mean a lot tonally: You can "earn" opportunities to "win" a "chance" at a character or costume that you want, but those require you to win matches and earn experience points. Not only does the experience required to go from level to level increase drastically (meaning that you might need to win 10 matches to "earn" your first "chance" at a character or costume, but you'll have to win 30 to "earn" your next), but their tied to your "animal level" which has a limit.So even if you were MADE of free time and just really LOVED the game, you will eventually run out of opportunities to 'win' the character or costume you want and there are already far more characters and costumes than there will be ever be opportunities you can "earn" as opposed to "buy."Does any of this sound familiar to you? Well, it should if you're familiar with the rise and fall (heheh) of "Fall Guys" which started as a pay-to-play game, people were irritated at the level of money the game was expecting you to pump into it for cosmetics and so started requesting refunds. Steam put pressure on the publisher to change their pricing, and they said, "well if you want us to go free to play, we'll sign on with Epic since they'll pay us for exclusivity on PC" and even with their sizable check from Epic and all the whales spending real life money to buy cosmetics, the devs still abandoned any efforts to stop hackers/cheaters from ruining the game for everyone leading in a rapid decrease in the game's popularity.So with that all said, let's address the good: Do you like gang beasts? Well this is that but with cute animals. If that's enough for you to enjoy yourself, then by all means have fun. But you might be better waiting for this game to become free to play, which I can pretty well guarantee will happen sooner than later.

_childDocuments_.review: Party Animals follows the same footsteps as party fighter/combat games like Rubber Bandits, Gang Beasts and Super Smash Bros. There is also additional game modes to choose from appart from the regular fighting gameplay. The sound effects is also a nice touch from a freezing snow blizzard to wind blasting past your character while walking on the wingtips of a airplane makes it a even more nerve wracking experience than anticipated while fighting out for glory against your friends. To put it simple, this is a combat game similar to Gang Beasts, but with way better graphics and simpler gameplay. So no need to be button mashing 20-30 times to acheive your wanted commands for your character. _childDocuments_.review: The controls work only after you figure out exactly how they work, (no thanks to the tutorial), because of how it's designed. To throw a person, it's not just grab them and face a direction and press x (or whatever on a KB and Mouse), you have to anticipate the momentum the person and yourself have and then sort of slingshot them in the direction you want.Now with that in mind, you have people spending their entire days and nights figuring out how to micro-manage these tiny details so they can do a combination of button presses to fly across the level to knock you out within 5 seconds of the round starting and toss you 15 meters into the nearest pit because they're just learned how to be  in a game designed like this.Again, has an amazing potential, has been a lot of fun with friends, but it saddens me that every time we play it always ends with frustration because of one guy in the lobby who's spent an abnormal amount of hours in this game eliminates us all within seconds and abuses niche mechanics that aren't taught to players in the tutorial.One final thought that's been apparent to me is that the game offers very little to no feedback to the player during playtime. You'll only ever know if you knocked another person out or if they knocked you out and if you're dead. This causes so much frustration because half the time you don't know if you're doing anything my swinging at another player and you feel as though the game begins implementing an RNG element here you have a 50/50 chance to knock someone out on a hit. Idk, maybe a skill issue, but some more feedback regarding play actions would be sooo incredibly appreciated.

_childDocuments_.review: When someone told me to try Party Animals I almost puked. At first sight, to the uninitiated gamer it looks like a kiddy pool of skin farming and bad matchmaking. And while that is not totally wrong, it is also incredibly wrong.Beneath the surface, Party Animals is a carefully crafted fighting game made for both child and man. The short tutorial introduces the player to the game, but the true depth of the combat complexity is revealed in the multiplayer, which can be done through random matchmaking, private lobby, or a mix of both.Through the intricate control mechanics, move combinations, random bonuses and gadgets that spawn during matches, and harnessing the unique settings and surprises of each map, the player gets to explore the deep learning curve of Party Animals. Even after several dozen hours and having faced opponents of both high and low ELO, the game never becomes tedious, as no battle ever plays out the same way.If that did not pique your interest, keep in mind that Party Animals permits people to play the game without having to buy it (with some limited actions in-game) to play with their friends, which is nothing short of a genius marketing strategy by the publisher.With over  characters to play as, each with a large subset of skins, as well as a selection of emojis, Party Animals can cater to just about any cosmetic preference,  elements. Every skin has the same hitbox, and many skins can be earned in the course of playing the game.Buy it on sale and party like an animal

_childDocuments_.review: if you came here for an honest review you came to the wrong place. but if you came for the most delicious cake youve ever had you are right where you need to becook time: 25 MINUTEStotal time: 1 HOURyields: ONE 2 LAYER CAKECake For 2 Layers 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder 1 1/2 teaspoons baking soda 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder 1 teaspoon salt 2 eggs, at room temperature* 3/4 cup buttermilk 1/4 cup plain greek yogurt 1/2 cup canola oil 1 tablespoon vanilla extract 3/4 cup strong brewed coffee, hot 1/2 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips (optional)Whipped Chocolate Buttercream For 2 Layers 3 (1 1/2 cups) sticks salted butter, softened to room temperature 3 cups powdered sugar 3/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder 2 teaspoons vanilla extract 3-4 tablespoons heavy whipping cream InstructionsFor the cake: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease 2 8-inch round cake pans. Line with parchment paper, then butter/spray with cooking  a medium size bowl combine the flour, sugar, unsweetened cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder and salt. Set  the bowl of a stand mixer (or use a hand held mixer) beat together the eggs, buttermilk, greek yogurt, canola oil and vanilla until smooth.Slowly add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients with the mixer on low until there are no longer any clumps of flour. Add the hot coffee and mix until combined. Batter should be pourable, but not super thin. Stir in the chocolate chips, if using.Pour the batter among the 2 cake pans and bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the tops are just set and no longer wiggly in the center. Remove and let cool five minutes, then run a knife around the edges of the pan. Grab 2 large flat plates, line them with wax or parchment paper and invert the cakes onto the paper lined plates. Cover and let the cakes cool completely before frosting.For the Frosting: Add the butter and powdered sugar to the bowl of a stand mixer (or use a hand held mixer). Beat the butter and powdered sugar together until the butter is light and fluffy, about 4 minutes. Add the cocoa powder and vanilla and beat, scrapping down the sides as needed another 2 minutes or until there are no streaks of white. Add 3 tablespoons of the heavy cream and whip the frosting for 2-4 minutes or until light and fluffy. If desired add the remaining tablespoon of the heavy cream (I normally do) and whip until combined. Taste the frosting and add more powdered sugar if you like a sweeter or thicker frosting.Place 1 layer, flat side up, on a plate or cake stand. With a knife or offset spatula, spread the top with frosting. Place the second layer on top, rounded side up, and spread the frosting evenly on the top and sides of the cake. Decorate with sprinkles, chocolate curls or whatever your heart desires. *To quickly bring eggs to room temperature place them in a bowl and fill with warm water. Let them sit five minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: Tbh, I get the frustration from all the Southern continents and the Devs made a pretty big error by phrasing that the game could be played both online and offline, when there is actually no offline-mode (only a splitscreen-mode, which still needs an internet-connection). But except from that and really little to none communication to the community until a few months ago, I have to say this a very good game, if not my favourite one right now.I know it's a big privilege to play this game without any issues because there are a lot who have waited as long as I did (if not longer), so people who think about buying Party Animals should really reconsider to buy, if they are not from Nothern Continents. I hope the Devs will fix their server-structure asap, so this game can be enjoyed globally. I'm really sorry for you guys. :(Anyway, for people from the Nothern side of the world this is a must buy. Don't listen to people who are complaining about microtransactions because you can play the game totally without it and still get alot of cool characters and skins in no time (actually every character and every skin is unlockable for free, except for the Beta Tester 2020 character, which is fine). For sure, legendary skins are hard to get or really expensive, but I am totally fine with that. It would be totally weird to see to many people playing legendaries after 2 days post-release, so when I someday pull one of these I can actually happy  about it. Number of characters and skins is great, music is phenomanel and maps/gamemodes are plenty, if one reconsiders that this is Recreate's first real published game.Gameplay is outstanding and involves a wide range of emotions (in a good way).Only downside for me right now are AFK-Players, which can't be kicked and that quick matches can be played with a party of max 4 players, but a lot of maps are 2v2 team based, so ultimately you can't play with your whole party all the time, but have to fight them. Not a big deal, but if I play with a party, I want to play with them not only to enjoy the game togehter but earning xp, too. With the way it is now, only half of my party gets the winning xp on certain maps (if a pair of us wins ofc).

_childDocuments_.review: Given that the game is clearly aiming for a Gang Beasts-style PARTY game and even states several times in their pitch that its a great game to play together on the same screen as your friends (local coop), it's pretty inexcusable to charge $20 for an always-online game with poor local coop support.The good:- It's Gang Beasts with a much more polished look to the characters and levels.- More of a cuddly and cute selection of characters, which appeals to more people (especially the kiddos).- Simpler control scheme to climb/grab/throw than Gang Beasts- Other game modes to mix things up nicely- Unlocking new characters/skins is a good idea... but see below for where that goes wrong...- Giving each player their own quarter screen can be a nice experience for certain maps, but comes at a cost, see below...- Once players are out they can still interact to a degree as a spectators.The bad:- MTX. Unlocking new characters/skins is clearly a money grabbing microtransaction pit, and in order to force us to confront it constantly, we have to live with this terrible always-online business.- Always online. Need I explain why this runs counter to the very idea of a "split-screen party game"?- Yes there is split-screen, but it is not implemented well. You have to jump through several "custom game" hoops to access it and set it up. Why not make a local, private game a default main menu option???- You can only play with up to four local players, and only in a couple of game modes. The other ones, like the go karts, are not 4 player split screen.- By making every map split-screen (instead of shared screen like Gang Beasts), we are probably never going to see the ability to have more than 4 players local. Additionally, if you have a smaller-size monitor/TV, it can be annoying having to split the screen into 4. Surely quite a few of the last man standing maps could be shared screen like Gang Beasts?In sum:Party Animals rolled out some nice improvements and made a cuddlier, cleaner game, but the devs immediately crippled it by adding MTX, always-online, and poor local coop support. Maybe try it if theres a super sale for a few bucks, otherwise keep playing Gang Beasts until someone releases a game who actually understands what party gamers want.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The gameplay is a lot of fun and it's easy to pick up, but there are better, cheaper party games that come without the over-monetisation and live-service issues. Best to wait for a sale or choose a different game altogether.I played the original demo back in October 2020, along with my friends. We all loved it; it was simple and lighthearted, with easy-to-learn mechanics, cute fuzzy animals, vibrant colours, and creatively designed maps. When I got playtest access, I was excited to learn that all these highlights had survived the long development process and had even been improved upon in some respects – new maps, new animals, new ways to customise your animal. Unfortunately, these were the only improvements over the original demo, and the only good things I have to say about the game.At 20 USD, Party Animals is comparable in price to other party games. Unlike other party games though, the upfront cost doesn't grant access to everything. Many items need to be purchased using one of 2 currencies - Cookies or Nemo Bucks - or randomly obtained from Eggs (their cute version of lootbox / gacha mechanics). Initially, I was under the impression that all these currencies could be obtained through regular gameplay  real-money purchases, and so I treated it as a progression system (I have since learned that Nemo Bucks are only available for real-money purchases). Thinking that everything was tied to these 3 currencies, I was surprised on day 1 when I opened the shop to see a bundle for a new character that didn't appear in my locker - the "Cabbage Dog". It was only available through a bundle costing real money - 5.9 USD to be exact, or a little under 1/3 the price of the game. It was incredibly insulting after paying an upfront cost to  be presented with content that was inaccessible without paying more.I wasn't surprised that the time-limited playtest required an internet connection to play, but I wasn't expecting it from the full release. Unfortunately, there is  offline mode. Want to look through your locker at the animals and cosmetics you’ve collected? You need to be connected to the internet. Having some friends over and want to play with them on your couch? You need to be connected to the internet. Going to a party and want to bring this game along? Better hope they’ll give you their internet password. Going on a road trip? Plane ride? Camping trip? Anywhere else with a lack of stable internet? Tough. You can’t play this game, even locally, until you’re reconnected.Even if you're someone who is always connected to the internet, the online-only model makes me question the longevity of the game. Party games tend to be short-lived. They are the type of game you return to when you want mindless fun, not the type of game you play consistently. As such, party games tend to quickly lose their players. For a game that's online only, a consistently low playerbase is the indicator of an upcoming end-of-service. When that happens, say goodbye to your access, and any hope of playing your beloved game again.Party Animals is a solid party game. Its controls and mechanics are well polished, its visuals are gorgeous, and each match is full of mindless fun. You will enjoy your time with it, especially if you have friends to play with. But enjoyment is not the same as being worth the price. The lack of an offline mode means that even your local games will be affected by high ping, and further means that you will lose access altogether if/when the servers get shut down. If you  want to get it, wait for a sale... but there are plenty of party game alternatives available that can be played offline or online, and  don’t charge for cosmetics.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial review of this wonderful game was negative because my experience was very undesirable. However, upon gaining more playtime, looking at the developer's responses to feedback, and what other people say, I can confidently change this review to a positive one.I'm a guy who has waited a long time for a lot of games. Elden Ring, Tears of the Kingdom, Persona 3 Reload, Pikmin 4, Baldur's Gate III, The Thousand-Year Door remake and the like... but I digress. Games aside, I have waited like the rest of you for this release. Sure, this game does have it's issues. There are complaints that certain regions, such as Australia, simply don't have any servers. The community's understanding was that this game would feature both online AND offline multiplayer. However, the developer's have since retracted and edited their statement, saying they have no plans to create an offline mode. I would highly, highly suggest they reconsider. This is an amazing title with a large following who has waited for a very long time- we're here to see it grow, not just stagnate several years down the line when online play is no longer supported.Sure, some games have a gripping story, beautiful music, and some even the potential to romance intricate characters. Yadda yadda yadda, but can you knock the absolute cr*p out of them like this..? I didn't think so.[TL;DR] In conclusion, this game is worth your money and your time. _childDocuments_.review: Things to help improve your experience: Accept that you are not in control of your character, the magic 8-ball Party Animals uses as a physics engine is.  You may go flying across the arena at a moment's notice. Why? Don't ask, just accept it.  You are able to climb back into most arenas using the jump and hold buttons together, but that's only the case until the game decides you're not. Turn the the music volume  the way down. Congratulations, the Ice Breaker stage is now bearable. Inviting friends to your party is as easy as a digesting a chicken steak tartare. Recreate Games has decided to make Steam's social system redundant by creating their own. You'll have to set up your profile, collect your account ID and then pass them to your friends rather than just inviting them directly through Steam.  There is no offline mode despite the game advertising one. As it turns out, this is a huge deal for some people. Keep this in mind if you're looking to buy Party Animals. Microphone chat is ON by default.  The game is intended to be played using a controller. No one gets to use Moonmoon but me. It's mine. Pick something else. Recreate has decided to punish people who choose to leave the game by giving them a Quick Match ban (as if this game is a serious esport), but don't do anything about people who will stay AFK in a match for prolonged periods of time. It takes a really long time for you to get kicked for being idle and replaced with an AI. If you get unlucky enough to be matched with an AFK teammate,  will be the one punished if you leave, your teammate might be able to stay idle for long enough to collect the experience at the end of a match. Thanks Recreate, very cool.Ultimately, there is a lot to enjoy here if you have the patience to put up with all of the bugs in the game's physics. Your character will never quite do what you're telling it to do and this will get you eliminated more often than not, which can be frustrating if you're particularly competitive.The sound design is nice, the soundtrack absolutely is not.The graphics are cute and highly stylised, but can already seem quite dated if you notice the weird pixel edges around fur and some objects. Other than that the graphics look great.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to directly compare this game to Gang Beasts in my review because they are very similar games, although in my opinion, Gang Beasts is better. I'll explain by telling you the difference between the games.In Gang Beasts, you stay down longer each time you get knocked out, with your first time getting knocked out being only a second unconscious. And then going closer to knockout #10, you'll be down for around 6 seconds. So you have lives, in a way, because even if someone knows how to throw, then they won't have time to throw you off the edge unless you got knocked out right next to one.In Party Animals, how long you stay down is seemingly random. I'm unsure without testing it, but it could be tied to your stamina, but I've been insta-knocked out on Spawn and been out for at least 4 seconds before, so I don't believe it's fully tied to stamina if at all. But in Party Animals, it's luck based on if this knockout is gonna be the killer for you, and if you spawn right next to somebody, you've got a 50/50 chance. And with the added caveat that there's a designated throw button and the fact that knockouts send you meters away, you can easily be thrown off map the second you get knocked out, if the blast from the punch didn't do it for you already.In Gang Beasts, there is no stamina bar except for an invisible one when climbing or ganging from something in general. Just basic attacks and jump attacks, which are stronger. Bodies were heavy as they realistically are, so you had to be sure to pick someone up in the right way to throw them, and then get them right near the edge.In Party Animals, stamina is a key feature, and you do more damage based on how much stamina you have. On top of that, running punches and dropkicks are heavy attacks so KO's happen pretty quickly. If you are out of stamina and get knocked out, it's an instant death. As well as if you land in water without stamina, it's an instant death. So juggling your stamina bar while fighting your opponents is something you always have to keep watch on, which takes away a bit of the fun of just beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of your friends and strangers. In my opinion, simple works better with brawlers like this. And you'd think that'd it'd be less random with these kinds of systems, but somehow it's not.In Gang Beasts, every customization item is free and available to you, with options to save different presets.In Party Animals, monetization is a big part of the game. While you can earn the three different currencies from leveling up; once you hit that level cap, buying is your only way to get currency until they release a battle pass, which will also cost money.In Gang Beasts, controls are limb based and deliberate. Climbing is one hand a time, and grabbing onto one specific thing purposefully is entirely possible.In Party Animals, climbing controls are simpler, but more random. You throw  yourself upwards by launching yourself up, letting go, and grabbing on again. But if the surface isn't entirely flat, or somebody is in your way, prepare to fall all the way down because when you climb, you let go with both hands each raise in height, so if your arms don't connect, you fall. And might even get knocked out when you land as well.There are more comparisons to make such as map designs and modes, but this would be way too long of a review. All in all, this game is fun for a little, while Gang Beats is fun for a while. If Boneloaf would update Gang Beasts, it would be top of the charts again.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend picking up this title for a cute physics based brawler with great polish. I had access to the playtest and found that the added gamemodes on release was refreshing. My hope is that they will continue to add more gamemodes, which I'm suspecting they will! The gameplay is very similar to Gang Beasts but I believe the added cosmetics to each animal will give everybody a way to customize their favorite critter. There's nothing like seeing a Darth Vader Duck get knocked out by a boomerang he threw, meanwhile a Wizard Crocodile is desperately swimming towards safety, all while you have a Pink Shark with a t-shirt on it's head camping the edge. While the gameplay supports solo queue, it is far superior to play with a group online (up to 4 players per lobby), with there being support for far more players in a custom lobby. However, while I do recommend picking this game up for a fun time I'm a bit saddened to see some micro-transactions pop up in the store for some characters. It's not as egregious as other games, as most cosmetics are available through leveling up your account (and spending the two different currencies available). My hope is that most of that content will be unlocked for free in the future.Some of the weapons are incredibly overpowered compared to the rest. I'm looking at YOU (shovel), but the balancing of different weapons is something they can fix in the future. Regardless, the mixture of long ranged, to wide swinging, and just downright hilarious weapons make for a fun and (sometimes) aggravating experience. Oh, and voice chat makes it 10x funnier.
