_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The puzzle design is definitely one of the best in the genre, but could be better. My critique is that the puzzle design(by choice) is too direct about what is needed so solve the puzzle. I think it's great and all but we can go a bit further. Most puzzles only has one twist, and the entire puzzle design revolves around it. Figuring it out automatically solves the entire puzzle. However, those twists does require in-depth understanding of the mechanism. There's still so much potential in the core mechanism and I am glad custom levels exist.

_childDocuments_.review: Glorious Sokoan-style, pushing block puzzles that seem impossible, but eventually reveal themselves.  (Except "Open 5" which frustrated me until I looked up the obvious-in-retrospect solution.) _childDocuments_.review: (DISCLAIMER: I tested this game. My name's in the credits. Also I suggested a mechanic that ended up making it into the game. Also also, while Steam shows that I have 8.9 hours on record at review time, my actual game time is longer since I beat the game in pre-Steam builds, and have been keeping up with new/edited levels in build updates; at review time, my savefile actually reads 14 hours 34 minutes.)Patrick's Parabox is a game about what Patrick's Parabox is a game about.Patrick's Parabox is a recursive Sokoban game. Boxes are rooms and you can push them into and out of other rooms. Sounds complex, you say? Yes! And you don't even know the half of it.If you've ever played Recursed, your main question is going to be how similar this game is to Recursed. My answer is "a bit, but not really". Unlike in Recursed, rooms are not instanced; the boxes can therefore be thought of as  to existing rooms, rather than the "chests that spawn new copies of rooms" of Recursed. This of course leads to a different set of puzzles, which leans less on the Sokoban as Recursed does on platforming.Like with every other pure puzzle game separated into distinct worlds and levels, every world introduces a new mechanic. Here, there's a mix of classic "new mechanic discovery", where you are introduced to an explicitly new type of puzzle element (e.g. boxes that are mirrored, boxes that are clones of other boxes), and have to grapple with what it does; and of SSR-style "new mechanic discovery", where you discover a new interaction between existing elements that was only impossible earlier because the level layout didn't permit it. Obviously I won't say too much about what those are, since Puzzle Solutions Are Spoilers™. If you must know, however, there is at least one mechanic that is not represented in the trailer (and it's the best one in the game because I was the one to suggest it).Difficulty-wise, though, Patrick's Parabox is quite gentle; far moreso than the trial-by-chest lategame of Recursed. The music is quite chill and friendly, too, as is the general vibe of the game, so it's clear that this game was designed for a more general audience. However, that's not to say there's nothing for hardcore puzzle fans. Each world has plenty of optional levels if you really want to bash your head against something, and there are additional challenge levels once you beat the game, as well as bonus levels that outright change the rules of the game, too (how might the game have been different if you could push a box from within itself?).Despite this, Patrick's Parabox didn't really hold any crazy surprises for me, unlike many modern puzzle games. But maybe that's just because I also watched some developer streams so I had some idea of what to expect going in. I can't claim this to be universal, and certainly you yourself may end up being surprised.(As a technical note for those who care, Patrick's Parabox is provably in PSPACE.)In conclusion, this is definitely a must-play puzzle game of 2022 if you have any interest in puzzle games, no matter how casual or hardcore of a puzzler you are. I enjoyed my time with it and if you care enough to have read this review, you probably will too.

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a paradise of recursive blocks, infinite loops, and plenty of satisfying "ah-ha!" moments! Each world whisks you through a new mechanic as you travel down the recursive rabbit hole, breaking and rebuilding your brain as you come face-to-face with infinity. Often times, creating a paradox is part of the fun of finding the solution. Each level challenges you to think outside the box (sometimes, quite literally) and aids you in grasping the rules that govern the game. Parabox reminds me of Portal and Baba is You, with , multiverse elements. Its whimsical soundtrack adds a final flourish to this wonderful, brain-expanding game. I highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It's maybe slightly too long, but honestly? This puzzle game is bananas. _childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a very good entry in the minimalist indie puzzle game niche. Each mechanical twist gets its own set of introductory levels, explaining the core idea without divulging exact nuances. Then each of those intro puzzle packs are followed up by a smattering of optional and required challenges that ask you to discover those intricacies. That process of unfolding the mechanical origami packed into this game is satisfying, even after several hours. The polished presentation is also a nice treat, helping to highlight the reality-warping spaces that you are presented with. If you have any positive inclination towards sokoban gameplay, you should check this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best paced puzzle games I've ever played! The game is a masterclass on how to introduce mechanics to players and create levels that help them discover how they interact with previously established mechanics. Each world has some harder optional levels that I encourage everyone to try as the game does its best to prepare you for them. After you finish all of the main worlds there are some extra worlds with harder levels putting all the mechanics together (something like a proper final test) and a few short worlds with alternate mechanics that truly change the way you think about the game. I still can't believe that a game with such complex and potentially confusing mechanics, managed to have such a masterful design that it's guaranteed you'll never have a "Oh I didn't know I can do this" or "that's a bs solution" moment while not feeling like it's holding your hand and providing a very good challenge!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a very good puzzler. This is a game that for a most part hits that sweet spot, not too easy but not too hard. It is a game about box inside a box. Along the way it introduces new elements and it never feels boring,I played it every 2 or 3 days so I forgot how some mechanics work. That is why I had to repeat some intro levels. I finished the main levels but there is more after you beat the main game. There are challenge levels aka harder levels and 3 separate level packs so there is more than enough levels for the asking price. Quality puzzler that I can recommend to everyone. Really can't find nothing bad to say about this game. Worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: While certainly far from the hardest puzzler on Steam, this little block pusher is absolutely delightful, featuring a fair but solid difficulty curve where the level selection system nicely lets you choose the pace you want to take the game at. _childDocuments_.review: Very high quality puzzle design. Effectively introduced and developed ideas just through puzzle progression, no explanations. So there were a lot of profound aha moments. Playing this made me feel really nice and clever. I also feel like it has made me a little better at thinking reflectively/recursively in other domains. The clean visualization of recursive environments, that are also interactive, gives you the opportunity to really taste and touch recursion in a way not previously possible. I finished 100% of puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good! The levels are very short, so you can do lots very quickly, which feels great. There are generally multiple levels available, so if you get stuck, you can try a different level. After you've made your way through several worlds, you can go back to levels you had skipped previously and find that you understand them now!The way the concepts are presented, without tutorials or explanation but just by seeing what happens when you experiment, really works for me. The way you can be inside a box that's inside itself, and therefore effect both the box you're in and the box surrounding it at the same time, is super interesting and engaging. And occasionally things happen that are disorienting at first until you figure it out.I would compare this to something like Baba Is You, except that Baba Is You got too hard for me very quickly, whereas with Patrick's Parabox I've done over 100 levels and I don't feel completely stuck yet. Very cleverly designed and fun!Note: Be sure to look at the controls in settings so you know how to undo and reset etc.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must have for anyone who enjoys puzzle games.It has a lot of unique concepts that kept the puzzles fresh and interesting. Each concept also has introduction levels through which you can learn how the concept works. The puzzles are also split into mandatory-easy ones and slightly more challenging ones that don't need to be solved to progress onwards so you can revisit them whenever you want to.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this puzzle game because it excels at both puzzle design and art direction. Overall one of the best puzzle games I've played in a long time, and one that can be played in short spurts at that.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a friendly sort of charm that only grows more appealing as you progress. The difficulty ramps very gently, beginning with an extremely basic introduction of fundamental sokoban mechanics, escalating through a series of level groups which are each named for the concept they introduce. People who play a lot of puzzle games may find the early game a bit easier and less exciting than they'd like, but as the game starts iterating on combinations of mechanics the boards start becoming intensely clever. It is absolutely fantastic at presenting a situation that immediately looks impossible yet contains all the subtle tells needed to back out what  happen to reach the goal. There are many excellent "wow" moments where you can barely comprehend what you're seeing, yet the game is always admirably legible and easy to read.Just truly excellent craft on display in every area. I was a bit soft on the soundtrack from my impression of the demo, but after listening to all the tracks through the full game (they change for each named area) I am much more positive, with several standout tracks that I really enjoy. The inclusion of some otherwise unused mechanics as 'appendices' was really great to see--Patrick clearly has a lot of good ideas but is also willing to make thoughtful decisions about editing and scope discipline. Having them as a small post-game bonus is a great way to handle this; they don't get very much time but some of it is just excruciatingly clever. In any case, there seem to be a fair number of user levels exploring these concepts, so I think it works out beautifully.In short, perhaps the most amiable game I've ever played, with some of the sharpest and smartest puzzles this side of The Talos Principle.The reward for solving ALL the puzzles is a very small thing, but it made me smile :)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I've 100% completed Patrick's Parabox, along with many other puzzlers. TL;DR: This one is an overall 7/10 (Very good). If you are new to puzzlers, this is a perfect start.DIFFICULTY: 5/10. Compared to some other tile based puzzlers, this is one of the easiest out there. Once you wrap your head around the concept of things being multi-layered, most levels come with either trying the only thing possible, or learning a new mechanic.MAIN CONTENT: 9/10. Each level has a small section dedicated to simply teaching the mechanics of the game, and most sections add completely new mechanics into the mix. The mechanics are never overly complicated nor out-blown (except in cases where the solution is presented to you instantly, as more of a fun experiment rather than an actual level). Additionally, the tutorials don't overlay previous mechanics too much, allowing you to properly learn the concept before throwing it into the pot.SIDE/POST CONTENT: 7/10. Most of the side content is either: 1. Some new mechanic not presented in a previous level, or 2: a combo of old and current mechanics. This is true for the post-game content too, however most of it is mechanics unused, mainly in the challenge section. The hardest puzzles existed there, but not because the logic was hard, but because the mechanic existed no where else.OVERALL: 7/10. While an easy puzzler, its an enjoyable mind-bender. For someone who doesn't play many puzzlers, but wanting to try some out, this could be a perfect start.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked "Baba is you", you'll love this one. Fiendishly awesome puzzle game that teaches you the rules as you go. _childDocuments_.review: There's something that really fascinates me about Patrick's Parabox: it makes WAY too much sense.It's a puzzle game about boxes within boxes, where the levels are boxes and the boxes are levels. Put a level inside itself and voila! recursion. You can enter it over and over and over and over. After that, every world adds a brand new mechanic.Understanding what's going on gets progressively more difficult as you progress, but once you get past that mental barrier, the levels themselves aren't as difficult to solve. Most are a simple showcase of that world's mechanic or an interesting consequence of it. Optional challenge levels on the sides then build on those ideas, and that's where you'll spend most of your time.The music is fitting for the genre, being present but never getting in the way. Each world has a different song that plays through it, and the title theme is in fact incredibly catchy.As you "enter" deeper into the worlds you realize something interesting: most of their so-called "new mechanics" are just a core part of how the game has always worked - or perhaps a natural edge case -, that were cleverly withheld in the previous worlds, being brought into light only when they were needed to increase complexity. So much so, that after you see them, you can't help but think "of COURSE that's how that works! it's the only logical thing!"This way, by the end, everything you thought you knew about the game at the beginning is recontextualized. However... true to its own recursive nature, it's not recontextualized into something different, but into itself: it's still a relatively simple game about boxes within boxes, where the levels are boxes and the boxes are levels.The post-game has some small worlds that playfully tweak some of the interactions, radically changing how the game plays out; and a big world full of the toughest challenges the game has to offer. This was the point of the game where I finally found some puzzles where I simply cannot explain how they work. Thankfully, a fully complete understanding of the "why" isn't necessary to figure out the "how" of beating them, so I was still able to beat 100% of the game.This will not be the hardest puzzle game you ever play, but damn if it isn't one of the smartest. I recommend it to anyone who is even vaguely interested in the genre. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game pleasantly surprised me. I didn't expect it to go this far with its concepts, and I suspect it hasn't really gotten all the way, leaving some room for experimentation to those who want to make custom levels. Most of the main puzzles are relatively simple, only requiring the player to figure out one trick which unravels everything else. That is not to say there aren't some headscratchers in there. I'd say accessible is the right word for this game, as the threshold for making progress is usually rather low. The concepts the game uses do get quite complicated, but it eases you into it in such a way that you always intuitively know what to do at any given main level. The "challenge" levels do need more brain juice to get past, obviously. Most of the solutions to puzzles gave me a feeling of awe the moment everything clicked, and it kept me occupied for a fair bit, so I'd say this was money well-spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This was an absolute delight. Patrick's Parabox has the smoothest difficulty curve of any puzzle game I can think of, but that doesn't mean any of the levels are trivial. While most levels on the main path won't take more than a couple minutes to solve, they still teach and/or require you to figure out some new interesting consequence of the game's mechanics. And with over 360 levels, the game explores those consequences extremely thoroughly. Plus, there are optional side, challenge and post-game puzzles, which include some real stumpers.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I usually balk at block based puzzle games - even Baba is You tired me at some points where the soko-banniness intersected too much with the main concepts. This game has no "annoying tight block push" moments. The block-pushing is entirely a front for the logic puzzles, and the music is incredible, and I can't recommend it enough. Great experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: If this game doesn't force your subconscious brain to soft reboot after repeated mind expansion from the crazy puzzles in this game, then you are going to have to power yourself down for a full update at least once before you can attain the BIG BRAIN required to complete the puzzles in this game.On a more serious note, the thing that I judge every game on is the graphics. And I am not going to lie, the graphics are pretty good in this game, your guy is 1 big pixel and then you interact with other big pixels. The art direction here is clear and the music really makes you feel like your are grasping infinity.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Dear puzzle games enjoyers, definitely take a step here and have your fun.This game is perfect in every aspect of a puzzle game. The mechanics are introduced calmly, one by one, then with more complexity, and it never goes on too many puzzles of the same kind. You'll find them again later in combinations, and without realizing it, you do crazy things with a relative ease.I rarely had so many moments of epiphany in a puzzle game. I can say I loved every single puzzle in the game, and I did 100% it. The challenge puzzles are definitely the way to go for content, it gave more to chew after the main worlds. It took me around 20h of try-hard while being a Baba is You hardcore veteran and a very long time puzzle games player. Most players could probably expect a significantly longer time.It definitely is shorter than Baba is You, but it's up there on the quality, while maybe being more accessible and displaying a little more steady progression. Concepts used, of different spaces (box) containing other spaces or even themselves, are, once again, extremely clever while being very understandable and ramping up later.Graphics are cute and efficient, clear, legible, a handful of options are there just in case.Audio design is chill, relaxing, consistent and does the job perfectly.This being mainly the work of one person, and a small team, this is astonishing. Puzzle games so elaborate are rare to come by, but they're even harder to create. Hats off.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A fabulously smart puzzle game. Despite its complicated premise, it's built to be friendly to those (such as myself) who are not great at solving hard puzzles. It also provides its fair share of genuinely difficult levels for people who are more well versed in puzzle games. It may seem like a generic box-pusher puzzle at first glance, but the further in you get the more you see how much this game turns the genre on its head. There's plenty of content to enjoy, with hundreds of levels that introduce more mechanics the further in you go. It isn't too hard to "beat" the game by mainlining through all the required puzzles, but the real meat lies in the optional challenge puzzles that use the skills you learned already to really test your creative thinking and problem solving skills. Your perception of space and direction will be warped as you push boxes into other boxes, or sometimes a box into itself. There's even a special achievement for creating a paradox and breaking everything. That's fun.Highly recommended for any puzzle enjoyers, or even for people who may not be so strong with puzzle games. Every puzzle feels like a new puzzle, and you are always discovering new ways to interact with the funky world our little purple protagonist inhabits. For the developer's first commercial game release, this is a big achievement! Huge props. Love ya Pat.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: solving the first few sets of levels has already been a joy to play and think about!it's really subjective but one thing I adore about puzzles is if I'm capable of solving them entirely in my head before making a single move and this is one of those few puzzle games where that's easily possible because its rules are really intuitivenow me and my partner can't wait to play more and finish it together!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: If you like spatial puzzles, especially those that are physically impossible in our real world but have a very logical and consistent set of rules, boy have I got a game for you! A great overall concept with more and more added to each new stage of puzzles. I imagine that the level creator is precariously straddling the genius/insane line. I strongly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant, creative, clever, mind-bending, and cute. Parabox is somewhat similar to Baba is You (which is also an amazing game), but to me, it seems significantly more balanced in terms of difficulty level (i.e., less frustrating). The game gently introduces each new mechanic, and there is a smooth progression in terms of complexity, creating a nice gameplay flow.Some levels made me go “Whoa” or laugh out loud because of how ridiculous they looked at first, but not even once did I feel completely lost.Strongly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Ever year a puzzle game comes out that blows your mind. 2022's was Patrick's Parabox. You're a cube that does Inception level magic to move other cubes into a set location in a way that sounds way more epic that what you're reading. The game I would compare it to is the other masterpiece Baba is You. You get new rulesets centered around creating copies, paradoxes and other mind-bending tricks in a way that any fan of puzzle games will love. It's not an easy game, but you don't need complete every level, you only need to complete around 75% of each level to move on. So those who get anxiety from their brains hurting can rest easy and say the are smart by playing a game like this.Showcasing the mind-bending nature of the game
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the only puzzle games I've ever fully completed. Each puzzle is unique and super clever. There are plenty of mechanics but they're all introduced slowly, and you never feel overwhelmed. Actually one of the reasons why it feels so unique is because of each mechanic. An absolutely incredible experience that you would never forget.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I'm rarely impressed by <puzzle game that has unique mechanic> because a lot of those mechanics get really frustrating once the novelty wears off and the dev tries turning up the 'difficulty'. This one avoids those pitfalls, it really could be this year's Baba is You!! The mechanics are super solid and intuitive, and yet the puzzles themselves can come as a surprise
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a block-pushing puzzle game where the main mechanic is recursion, i.e. you can put a box inside itself. Similar to Baba Is You, it has a simple base set of rules, that gets added upon to make more and more complex puzzles. This game keeps blowing my mind. Each mechanic that gets introduced makes perfect sense and yet it still takes a while to wrap my mind around it. The solutions are always obvious once you figure them out but impossible until then. It's the sort of puzzle game where you have to both be methodical and take a leap of faith. If you like mind-benders, this is a must-have.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best puzzle games I've played. There is a lot of depth in this game. There are so many puzzles, and every one of them has some interesting aspect of the mechanics to highlight. Some of the puzzles are pretty mind-bending, but once my mind bends around it and I have that realization of what I need to do, it feels so good.Since you only have to complete a certain amount of puzzles in each area to advance to the next one, you never have to be stuck on a single puzzle that you're struggling with. And some that I was banging my head on and skipped for a while I was able to get pretty quickly when I came back to them later, so being able to set them aside for a time was very helpful.There's also a pretty good pacing to the game. Each area introduces a new concept, and the puzzles start off pretty simple to let you get a feel for how it works. Then the difficulty ramps up and the later puzzles in the area can be pretty challenging. But once you clear those and move on, you get a nice break to be introduced to another fun aspect of the game.The designer chose to focus on the mechanics and puzzles, so there's not a lot else going on in this game, and that's not necessarily a bad thing. The mechanics and puzzles are so unique and interesting that I wouldn't really want it muddied up and lost in a complex narrative or world. This game is an inch wide and a mile deep in that it keeps a pure focus on exploring all the facets of the mechanics. Really a joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't already own Baba is You I don't recommend you buy this game. I can't give this game a negative review because the concept is so clever and the mechanics are so thoroughly executed, but I felt pretty let down. It took me 9 hours to beat all the 300 main levels, at the time of this review I haven't finished all the challenge levels but I'm not super excited to play them except for the achievement.It only took me about 2 minutes per puzzle but the vast majority of them took far less than that, usually I would quickly finish 2-4 puzzles in a row then spend 15 on one puzzle, but the ones which I spent more time on didn't feel harder I just think I wasn't able to see the solution very quickly. Almost all the puzzles either introduce a new or clever trick, or they make you do that trick multiple times. Sometimes doing it multiple times requires more thinking but often it doesn't. It felt exhausting to finish all the levels, when I spent a long time on one puzzle only to find the clever trick I felt more stupid than accomplished or just lucky after trying nearly every possible way to push the blocks into each other. I think this would probably be a better game if you just took the best 100 levels. It felt like the 300 levels in the game were the first 300 levels ever made and in a hurry. Most of them can't really be adjusted to be better the only way to improve the quality of the levels would be to create another 500 levels then throw away all the ones that aren't excellent. Sure 9 hours is definitely worth the $20 but I would probably wouldn't be nearly as critical if it was $10.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it costs a lot for what it basically is.BUT, this game goes beyond any puzzle game that I encountered. Speaking as a programmer and physicist, this is exactly the kind of game that I was looking for, playing with infinite loops, paradoxes, mutliple dimensions, this game is just... genius. Thank you.All in all, try the demo, and if you like it, go on, get it, or wait for a discount.Things that could be corrected:- Adding some kind of reward system, maybe giving the player the possibility to custom that little guy- Making a puzzle maker would be a GAMECHANGER. Literally. Imaging all the possibilities with the created puzzles on a workshop from players all around the world.- A coop mode with even more challenging puzzles, locally (could be easily implemented) or online (not necessarily) I can only dream about that workshop, please make it happen!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of puzzle games and puzzles in games, especially the sokoban/block pushing types. I think this is the absolute best version of this style of game I've ever played. I still haven't played another game that uses the recursive mechanics, so that was super fascinating, especially when the game started to get more difficult. I like Baba is You so much, but I had to look up so many clues and it got to where I didn't enjoy the challenge. Patrick's Parabox can be quite challenging, but I was always able to solve the level before it got to feeling laborious. Solving these puzzles made me feel brilliant. Patrick Traynor has created an incredibly smart recursive sokoban puzzler that kept me engaged for about 15 hours.Definitely play the demo or buy this game if you like this type of puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: My new favorite puzzle game. Mind bending and creative but super approachable due to the excellent puzzle design. You're never given an overwhelming amount of tools to work with in a given level, and while for some that would make the game too easy, I personally found that it made each challenge snappy, concise, and easy to follow. There's a pretty substantial amount of content to work through, yet the game continually throws in fresh ideas that constantly pile on top of one another. Having finished everything except for the endgame areas, I haven't found a single solution to be unsatisfying; I'm not sure if I can say that for any other puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinated by the concept of recursion in this game, I bought myself a car key pendant, a perfectly accurate down-scaled model of my car. One evening, while I was driving home, I suddenly had a strange vision in which I saw a small copy of myself sitting in the car model. This inspired me to change my life! I spent all the remaining money to buy a neat model of a villa. I placed it on a car seat and put my car model in the middle of its lawn. Exiting my car, I indeed found myself in front of an expensive villa that was all mine. Now I just needed to find a suitable display site for my villa model so that I would live a life of luxury in a villa which contains a copy of itself. On closer inspection, though, it was revealed that it wasn't a villa but a sanity asylum.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A great mind-bending sokoban-like puzzle game in the post baba-is-you era. I've been looking forward to this game for two years or so, ever since the preview version came out. Finally got to play it, and I'm blown away. This game is way beyond my expectation. Before playing it, I thought Baba Is You kind of killed the sokoban-like genere by rendering all the other games obsolete, and there would be no more exciting sokoban-like. But this game has proven I was wrong, and I'm glad to be disproved. Great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully complex, clean, smooth, and extremely satisfying to figure out! It'll stretch your brain and prompt you to think of ideas in ways you've most likely never explored before, enticing you to "Think Outside of the Parabox!!!" I am absolutely in love with the concept and cognitive strategy required in order for one to solve certain intricate levels in this game. 100% worth the money. 10/10 would buy again! 🧡🧡🧡
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Ten out of ten for stylish graphics, ten out of ten for level design, ten out of ten for mind-blowing "eureka" moments. Same sokoban-inspired premise as , but infinitely less frustrating as alternate paths to the solution are  clear to you when your current solution doesn't work (Always "Maybe I'll try this instead", never "What the hell am I supposed to do? Nothing works"). This game kicks ass.Listen to psychedelic/complex electronic music while playing for best effect.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game that forces you to stop thinking inside the box and instead think within infinite parallel boxes.IMO it finds an almost perfect balance between complexity, difficulty, and level length. Writing this review after having 100%ed the game, I never felt the need to lookup answers nor did I ever feel I was spending a deeply unreasonable amount of time on a level, but I was always engaged by the puzzles and mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun puzzle game. Has quite a lot of interesting ideas. Self referencing mechanics is used quite well, and it's never too confusing to understand. It's not as hard as other puzzle games such as Stephen's Sausage Roll or Baba Is You so even if you think that you are bad at puzzle games I think you can enjoy this Patrick's Parabox.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I unfortunately don't think I can recommend this game this game at $20. Patrick's Parabox does present some interesting ideas, but doesn't flesh them out enough to create a true sense of increasing difficultly. It took me only 5 hours to beat the game and almost every world to completion, because despite having over 300 levels, many of them are either solved with near identical solutions or the solution is the only set of unique game actions you can take. Despite that, I did enjoy myself and there were a handful of levels I thought were clever, but comparing this game to something like Baba is you is night and day. Which makes the price point of Patrick's Parabox being $20 seem ludicrous to me. I would probably recommend the game if it was $5-$10, but as it stands it unfortunately under delivers. Also on a different note the soundtrack just really does not do it for me, forgettable and annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a block pushing puzzle game on the level of Baba is You.The basics are simple: push block here and stand here to finish level. What this game does uniquely is include recursion. Boxes can go into other boxes. Boxes can go into themselves infinitely. Those infinite patterns can layer onto itself.The learning curve was excellent at letting the player figure out properties themselves. Nothing felt like filler and all levels explored different concepts in different ways. Also appreciated are the dedicated undo/redo/restart buttons, and the ability to undo a restart. The game also lets you unlock or relock all puzzles at any time. Music, UI, and aesthetics are also great.I generally dislike puzzle focused games but have some exceptions: Portal 1/2, Antichamber, Baba is You. I can now add Patrick's Parabox to that list.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: very unique and creative puzzle game!  having loads of fun with it and would definitely recommend at least trying out the demo!  but there are LOADS more levels in the full release than there are in the demo, and the mechanics keep expanding deeper and deeper, so it seems well worth the cost!  im not a big puzzle game guy, but the mind bending mechanics have me so enthralled, and the base puzzles arent TOO hard.  you just have to think outside of the box  ;)  really hoping for a built-in level editor in the future, because the interactions get super nutty, and id love to mess around with themedit:  i have now reached the end and my feelings have not changed!  honestly wish it went on for longer, i was having so much fun LOL.  but it went on for a while, and it was definitely well worth the money.  PLUS i still have all the harder side challenges to check out!  ive seen other reviews saying this is the best puzzle game ever, and their statement definitely has merit to it!  i dont think any puzzle game has bent my mind like this one has, and it was an absolute blast figuring out the mechanics!  so yeah i absolutely recommend this game, so much fun
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I'd be willing to say this is one of my favorite puzzle games, maybe ever. It's simple to understand the basic concepts, and then it starts mixing everything it has to offer in a way that scratches my AuDHD brain in just the right way. I've probably replayed the whole thing at least 12 times by now.If you're into puzzles, and even more into specifically abstract puzzle concepts, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly a fantastic brain buster. Some of the challenge levels near the end play it a little to close to obscurity especially once the flip and infinity start appearing together where it isn't entirely obvious what is going on. Despite that very small grievance, there are so many fantastic puzzles and concepts in here for you to spend time thinking about. Its the kind of game whose concepts make you imagine in game scenarios when you leave it eager to try them out when given the opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I first played the demo of this game during a steam festival few years ago. It was instantly put on the top of my wishlist, waiting for the full game, and I instant bought it when it was released!This game is a mind-blowing puzzle game! Level layouts generally seem so simple and yet they are quite often very hard to solve, giving the player a real challenge. Compared to other puzzle games I have played, Patrick's Parabox renews its mechanics and surprises us all the way through the game, not making the mistake of getting too hard to solve, or getting the player bored of using the same mechanic over and over again. I think it can be compared with Baba is You in terms of puzzle mechanics creativity, and mind-bending game design.Long story short : if you like puzzle game, go buy this game! It deserves its success
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic bite-sized puzzle game with a mind-bending premise, yet ends up being surprisingly intuitive. Most levels are fairly short solves demonstrating a specific concept, once it clicks the level becomes trivial. There are definitely some mind-benders here and there as well though, especially towards the middle-late section. And the little amusing surprises caused by different recursive interactions makes me smile. Overall a great game to show friends and progress through when you're hopelessly stuck on a level of Baba or Sausage Roll.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: - Great Puzzles- No hand Holding- The game is ready for you to break logicThis game has simple controls, simple graphics and a simple premise. The quality of puzzles is great. Most puzzles games get compared to something, i would compare this to Inception or Dr. Strange with the way you have to think about things. This is a fantastic game, I've already put 3 hours into it and i'm about half(?) way through. This is easily worth the $20 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Love it.  Not nearly as hard as Baba Is You (still haven't completed the extra stages on that one), but very much in the same block-pushing-mind-melting genre.  I beat all the standard stages (and their challenge levels) in about 9ish hours, but there are still a bunch more challenge levels that are revealed after the game "ends".  I'm still working on those.  Highly recommended.UPDATE: Finished all the levels. only took me 15 hours "steam-time", but probably less actually sitting at the computer thinking.  There are some options to randomize the levels colors/orientations to mix it up on replay, but I won't replay it any time soon.  I need to forget the solutions to the puzzles before that.  Still highly recommended.NOTE: I played using a steam controller in Ubuntu 20.04 on a laptop with intel integrated graphics.  My laptop's fan was running pretty hard, but the game played great. Controller support was great.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The premise, once you boot up the game, seems so simple. And yet it gets so hard, while always being fair and easing you into every concept without a single word about the rules and interactions. You just try the thing the game wants you to learn about in a simple puzzle in each new area, until you get it. Then you clear the area, and maybe hop on the red-bordered levels to see if you actually understand what you're doing. And you move on to the next area. It's just so satisfying to figure out the solutions, and I'm only 50 puzzles deep. If this kind of brilliance is maintained throughout, it's gonna be an easy homerun and strong contender for puzzle game of the year. The undo/redo and restart level hotkeys also help out tremendously in making this a challenging but fun experience. All in all, totally worth the full price, try the demo if you're still somehow not convinced, but this is an A+ game in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a wonderful evolution of the classic block-pushing Sokoban game. It has the same simple controls and objectives as Sokoban, but the ability to move in and out of boxes allows for so much more freedom and creativity. It's just a lot of fun working out how all the different pieces fit together. Well worth buying!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle game. As soon as I saw the main premise, I knew I was in for a treat. Difficulty wise it is actually very balanced, the devs could have gone ham with so many elements and interactions they introduce, but I am grateful it didnt become absurdly complicated. On that note, I really liked the way each element is introduced, with a few easy puzzles to get used to it and then the more complex ones.I don't think there is much more to say. Good puzzle game, very satisfying. Grab it if it picks your interest.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent short puzzle game. I don't normally like sokoban-style games, but this one is an exception, in part because it can build hard puzzles using a small number of very simple objects: one of the final puzzles I'm stuck on has only 4 objects (counting both the player and the stage itself), all with simple geometries. I also like how every edge case in the rules (of which there are several, thanks to the infinities involved in recursion) is turned into an opportunity via a new set of puzzles to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: "OMG! O.M.G!" Get ready to say that at the beginning and end of every level.The satisfaction of solving a gruelling puzzle is unlike any other. Every level is consistent to the theme or the title of that level. The variety of puzzles is mind-boggling, it just continues to go over, under and inside (LOL).There are NO cons to this game. Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is clever and is a refreshing take on the Sokoban genre. The answers are deliberate and rewarding. The developer does not waste space or employ cheap tricks: the puzzles are created from someone who truly enjoys sokoban puzzles and is able to explore the concept thoroughly. Parabox is as much a game as it is an evolution and exploration of the genre.  The tutorial feels natural and it evolves into the game play quickly. The game moves at the players pace and is never weighed down by redundancy. Each puzzle feels like a clever branch of the last without holding you back or pushing the player too far forward, it builds on concepts and it's up to the player to execute them.  Whenever I got stuck on a puzzle I liked being able to play the other puzzles in the sequence again to find the missing link or move ahead and come back to the puzzle with fresh eyes. I've managed 53 of the 350+ puzzles so far at the time of the review. I can't wait to jump back into the game. Solving the puzzles feels natural and the more difficult moments have a good balance of challenge and eureka moments wrapped in. Additional notes! The game is disability friendly: great UI/accessability, full control remapping, the ability to add a grid, clear legible font, undo/redo buttons, good contrast in the colours and is colourblind friendly in its design.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A really elegant and challenging puzzler. Very simple rules that somehow can lead to incredibly complex puzzles. It doesn't quite have the galaxy brain potential and expansiveness of Baba is You (I can get 50+ hours out of Baba is you but can fully explore the limit of this game's mechanics in 10-15) but it a great short puzzler. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best puzzle box type game made yet. You heard about The Witness and Stephen's Sausage Roll, and those are all difficult games that make you think and unfortunately also do stuff. Often time you can figure out the solution far before you can actually solve it and then have to go through the actual tedium of solving the dang thing. Patrick's Parabox on the other hand goes the opposite direction where your exploration of how the rules function and your progress through a particular level tend to coincide, where you figure out how you got to the solution just moments before you actually get to the solution. Sometimes this strays too far and you get to the solution without really realizing why you got there, but those are often the introductory puzzles that show you how a mechanic works. My only complaint, I need more. The game as it stands introduces a number of concepts and rules that all layer on top of each other, but aside from my first "paradox" I have not hit the "it goes one meta layer deeper" that the others (Baba is You, Stephen's Sausage Roll, The Witness, etc) get to, though I will admit that I am not quite done with all the levels. I honestly think that this is the freshest take on sokoban style mind bending puzzles I have ever seen. Most go too far and are far past the point where I am smart or patient enough to complete them, but this hits the absolute sweet spot and really is the best for anyone, even if you do not normally like these sorts of puzzlers.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible puzzle game. It manages to show you the most impossible-looking starting screens you have ever seen--but then, 10 minutes later, you know exactly the process you need to take to solve the puzzle. All of the levels feel like they belong, with none that I can remember being filler. This game has the most satisfying 'aha!' moments I have ever experienced, which I think is its most defining feature.This game manages to explain the concept of infinity in the best and most tangible way. Patrick's Parabox teaches you about ordinal numbers better than all of the math youtubers I've watched combined. Very nerdy game, very fun to learn, very challenging in the challenge section.I said  prolly like 1000 timesin my top 3 puzzle games of all time
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately it's quantity over quality in terms of puzzle design. A lot of solutions are either too similar to each other or don't feel "elegant" but forced. I also had several levels I solved by chance without fully understanding the mechanic. That's like a deadly sin in puzzle design. And with the possibility for changing the layout by pressing "7" a lot of puzzle become a lot easier and, even worse, the box-in-a-box-in-a-box idea starts to feel more like a gimmick than a feature. All things considered my review probably would have been positive, but this game is way too inferior to "Baba is you" and "Stephen's Sausage Roll". And last but not least I think this game would be pretty much perfect for mobile devices.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, easily would recommend to anyone who enjoys puzzles, no matter the skill level. I personally enjoy puzzles that require out of the box solutions and this game has tons. Almost every section introduced a really exciting mechanic or concept that had me stunned, The entire game concept seems so unique, and it feels like the developer had barely scratched the surface. Just 2 things I didn't like about the game: 1) The introduction into semi-difficult puzzles took a while, even though no puzzles felt repetitive. I felt like a majority of puzzles within the first few sections took no more then a minute and didn't provide any sort of challenge.2) Probably about 1/2 of the main line puzzles, the solution was really easy to stumble into. Sometimes I didn't understand why something worked, but it did.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: After years of preparation and training, I have finally brought myself to the purest level of enlightenment. I have considered the possible consequences, and have meditated on the things I may see and experience, but I have come to decide that in order to reach full enlightenment, it must be done. No, I am not talking about the ability to connect to the forces surrounding us and all life, nor my inner self, nor my third eye. I, my friends, am talking about Patrick's Parabox. It has been constantly overlooked, its’ values not taken seriously, but as I have come to discover,  Patrick's Parabox is one of the most powerful versions of enlightenment possible. It brings you straight into a world of pure bliss. A world of Boxes and Recursion as far as the eye can see. The best part: Everything is recursive and infinite. This world is currently inhabited by very few, but these few have been truly enlightened. These few have reached where no other gamers have reached before: an alternate reality directly crafted to enlighten you. There is no possible form of enlightenment more powerful than one that brings the infinity to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the entirety of this game 100%ing it I can safely say this game needs a level editorI can also say this game was alot easier than baba is you, because people keep comparing them. With some levels in baba is you taking me literal days to figure out, with me passivly thinking of solutions when I was off of it. While no level here took me more than an hour. I loved baba is you as the puzzles made me feel like an actuall genius for solving them and getting to the true ending. Patrick's Parabox doesn't make you feel like a absolute genius for solving some of it's puzzles, you don't ever get stuck, so you don't feel dumb as often. And you can feel smart for flying through the levels. So I will say Patricks paradox is a much better puzzle game for those with less patience. Baba is you is better for those with alot of patience or are just better at puzzles in general. If you like puzzles and have the money, buy both.Minor spoilersI love when you have those Mind blowing revalations you have Over time you can figure out the game has two main parts, boxes and walls. the blocks you are familiar with are functionally boxes filled with wallsand the player you are familiar with is functionally a possesed box full of wallsrecursive boxes are just boxes inside a clone of itself,You can tell these things from levels where you build the recursive box yourself or from player showing that the player can be more than just its basic shape.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I thumbs up this because I want more original puzzle games like this.  The game is great.  However, the execution is very lacking.  There aren't enough visual indicators to tell you what type of block you're pushing around.  Maybe it's just me, but I often find myself wonder what the hell just happened after I push a light green something into a slightly darker green something else and have no idea what the dark and light color difference meant.  A few more minutes could have been spent on the graphics, too.  It feels like this was a game that was pounded out in a weekend then charged the same price for other AAA games.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A great, refreshing new concept for a puzzle game, marred by incredibly mediocre level design. I often start levels in puzzle games like these by randomly "experimenting"- just doing the first action I see without thinking, to get a feel for cause and effect, and most of the time I found that I solved the puzzle before I started thinking.There is barely any sokoban here, and the puzzles are effectively "do one of the two possible things you CAN do"- you exhaust your options within a minute and solve the puzzle. It feels like if Portal's levels only ever had two or three portalable spots in each level. Towards the end, I saw some good puzzles, but they were in the last two or so worlds, in the very last 5% of the game.The result of all of this is a game that is incredibly easy to finish through brute force or random actions. I finished probably 80% of the main story without actually using brain power (just via randomly doing the first thing I see), and couldn't bother finishing the challenges because they were largely the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is an amazing puzzle game but by all that is holy, it is hard as hell at places.You will go insane.You will feel like you have developed schizophrenia.You will break down laughing while steaming this.The insanity will consume you.You will never be the same.You are now broken by the Parabox.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting this to be another mind-blowing Sokoban game like Baba is You or Stephen's Sausage Roll, and while the basic premise is very cool and expanded upon greatly, this game just has far too much fluff for me to enjoy it entirely.A lot of the puzzles are very, very easy, to the point where your first solution is usually correct. There's also a ton of repetition, often the "harder" versions of puzzles require the same solution as the previous puzzle, but applied to a different shape of block, or just repeated multiple times. Even when new mechanics are introduced, it often feels like you can apply the same few tricks you used in previous levels to most puzzles.I'm about 130 puzzles in at time of review, but there's been less than 10 puzzles that have really felt difficult and satisfying in their solution. I think I would have enjoyed this game a lot more if it had like, 75% less puzzles. As it stands right now, by the time I've cleared an area, I'm already tired of its mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I didn’t enjoy this game and there are a couple of reasons for that. First of all the game always follows the same pattern. It introduces a new mechanic and then you have to do 8 tutorial levels for the new mechanic and then there are maybe 1 or 2 interesting levels in a section before the game introduces a new mechanic. The ratio of just going through the motions and actually solving a puzzle is terrible, maybe 10-20% of levels are actually good.The game is too similar to regular Sokoban. Sokoban has a bunch of problems and pretty much all of them are present in this game. Quite often you can see the solution right away but you have to shuffle the pieces around to get there. Shuffling the pieces around is tedious, there isn’t a lot of room in most levels and pushing things against a wall by accident and having to redo parts is annoying.Because the game is just Sokoban with tiny rule changes the game can’t make interesting puzzles without just making the puzzle bigger. Some of the challenge levels at the end are just old puzzles but they doubled the amount of moving pieces. Just with the base game there are maybe 10-20% good challenge levels at the end and the rest is garbage.I’m not sure what this game would need to be fun, maybe less but higher quality puzzles? Maybe stronger mechanics that would allow for more interesting solutions?
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good thing this game can be played with one hand using a controller.  That leaves your other hand free for much head scratching as you try to figure out the 364 puzzles.  If you're a fan of Sokoban, this is basically Sokoban, but non-euclidian.  Boxes within boxes, boxes that clone boxes, levels where you are the box, pushing boxes clear out of reality, it's quite the brain teaser.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty good game. Here are the pros and consCons:- I found it strangely enough, too easy. Maybe I'm just better than average at weird recursive sokoban (I did have an easier time with Baba is You than most of my friends and family who played it), or maybe something about the levels makes it too quick to reverse engineer the solution. I managed to solve the levels in under a minute on average, and only got stuck on two or three of the post-game extra levels.Pros:- Despite how easy it was, I still found it fun and interesting to explore what this kind of meta-sokoban would entail, and, for that reason, I don't regret buying it.- The level-design is (barring difficulty) excellent. There aren't annoying red-herrings and the puzzles had varied solutions. Some levels build on each other, but it never felt like I was playing the exact same thing.- This game has fantastic communication! The "tutorials" (if it's even right to call them that, they're really just introductory levels) made every new mechanic intuitive without feeling like the game was questioning your intelligence. For a game that introduces a fair number of new mechanics, it did not feel overwhelming. Also, everything is well-telegraphed and consistent.- The polish is amazing! Accessibility options are great, didn't encounter a single bug, everything about the way the levels look and the characters move was quite charming.So, I would recommend this game, but make sure to savor it because otherwise, it might feel underwhelming.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: To be fair, you have to have a very high IQ to understand Patrick's Parabox. The puzzles are extremely subtle, and without a solid grasp of theoretical physics most of the solutions will go over a typical player's head. There's also Patrick's nihilistic outlook, which is deftly woven into his characterisation - his personal philosophy draws heavily from Flatland literature, for instance. The fans understand this stuff; they have the intellectual capacity to truly appreciate the depths of these puzzles, to realize that they're not just funny- they say something deep about LIFE. As a consequence people who dislike Patrick's Parabox truly ARE idiots- of course they wouldn't appreciate, for instance, the humour in Patrick's existencial catchphrase "It's Paraboxin' Time" which itself is a cryptic reference to Sega's Japanese epic Morbius. I'm smirking right now just imagining one of those adapted simpletons scratching their heads in confusion as Patrick Traynor's genius unfolds itself on their computer screens. What fools... how I pity them. 😂 And yes by the way, I DO have a Patrick's Parabox tattoo. And no, you cannot see it. It's for the 4D beings' eyes only- And even they have to demonstrate that they're within 5 reality layers of my own (preferably lower) beforehand.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short game and I literally just 100%ed the game, but god dang it's good, go play the demo to find out whyGeneral Pros:+ Very thorough exploration of the mechanics it introduces - one mechanic in particular tends to be reserved more for indicating a failure state, I won't specify what though since it's a bit of a spoiler+ Steady difficulty curve - It's generally always on a slow upward climb but it will drop when you start up a new section; and then there's the bonus levels lul+ Music's nice and diverse, keeps you calm while you're bashing your brains out figuring out how the frick to do the thing+ The game also has an option to let you cycle through a set of "representations" of the level, which can be really useful if you have trouble keeping track of where you are+ There's custom levels! Just no easy way to make or import them at the moment, but that's fineGeneral Cons:Nothing that I can really think of right away!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: If all you want are the best mind raping puzzles on the planet then look no further. The simplistic graphics also make it easy to understand what is going on on the screen, which you will need from how often solutions require you to understand the big picture from all of the recursion that happens in the second half of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Best puzzle game I've had the pleasure of playing through. No filler, no repetition, every level brings a new idea for you to work your way through. Nothing too difficult either, only took about 13 hours for me to 100% this game with its 350+ puzzles, but every puzzle still feels rewarding because it made you figure out something new. I recommend this game to everyone ever.

_childDocuments_.review: It seemed to me that it was pretty expensive for a puzzle game, but there are so many levels and so many brilliant ideas that it's totally worth it. Doesn't hurt to wait for a sale, but anyway it's a great game. In the meanwhile you can try the demo.Update after completing the game: none of the levels were particularly challenging but they were immensely fun to play!Final update: Ok, a few levels form the "Challenges" box were actually quite challenging (nomen omen). Overall it took me 9h for the main part (~250 levels) and 5h for the extra part (~100 levels).

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed the game; Screenshot:Tl;Dr? (Really?!)  RECOMMENDED - HUGE STAMP OF APPROVAL - WONDERFUL MIND BENDING 2D PUZZLE EXPERIENCE!(Now read a few paragraphs - sheesh)At time of writing this, i have sunk a little under 16 hours on this to completion (take about an hour or two for idling for mental breaks). Patrick's Parabox is a wonderful 2-dimensional puzzle game. There are a variety of levels with specific themes in mind - not to overload the player with too many ideas even at late stages of the game - until you unlock Challenges which combine all prior knowledge learned over the course of the game. The music sets a nice ambiance that's not distracting while the sfx give a nice return on actions you make (a lot of puzzle games I've played are completely silent in this regard and I personally find that lacking).The visuals are nothing flashy, but that's so you can concentrate; the visuals don't detract from the experience as it feels they made them with specific focus in towards letting the player easily consume what is going on.The complexity I feel is the real seller. They build you up by easing you level by level into the concepts they throw at you until you feel like you've mastered the idea. THEN you take a wrench to the head as they combine earlier problems or expand even further on the problem at hand. You have 'Infinite' planes mastered? How about 'Double Infinite' planes? Perfect, now try moving 'Double Infinite' planes through 'Epsilon' ones.The price is justified. Loved the moments i spent scratching my head over this product. My only dissatisfaction is there isn't any DLC yet; I want to play more.10/10Wonderful concept executed perfectly!{Edited for Correctness}

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game that I really enjoyed, but there is absolutely no world in which this game should cost more than Baba Is You (which is admittedly underpriced at $15 USD), a comparable game with far, far more content. I'd say that it's still probably worth picking up if you're into puzzle games, but where many indie games on Steam feel like a great deal, this one just feels like an okay deal. It still lands in thumbs-up territory for me, but it'd get a much more emphatic thumbs-up were it not for how it is priced relative to similar games.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew about this game since the demo days but I always put off actually playing it. Going by the insane premise I assumed it would be one of those puzzle games I enjoy for an hour or two before the mechanics get too overwhelming as too many layers are added too quickly. But recently I was in a puzzle game mood so I gave it a shot finally, and it's surprisingly really accessible and designed. Each of the zones in the game are themed after a specific mechanic that it focuses on for the whole zone, at first gently easing you in with puzzles simple enough to teach the new element before opening up with optional puzzles to test and further your understanding of that mechanic.There's were only two puzzles in the whole main campaign that stumped me to the point I had to come back later, and those were mostly me being stupid and overlooking smth but I still got them later on.Overall it's incredibly worth it, the main campaign with all the optional levels took me around 8 hours to finish, and there's more stuff added in the post-game that I'm yet to finish as of writing this review, it's accessible enough so even if you aren't a puzzle game nut you should still be able to enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I've played in a long time. Admittedly I haven't played a lot in the puzzle genre recently. Friend put me on to this game, gifted it to me in fact, and it reminded me of how a good puzzle game should be. The rules range from simple logic to the esoteric, but there are always a handful of easier levels at the start of each new concept that not only show off said mechanic; it also shows you nearly the full extent of the mechanic as well. Moves, techniques, the works. The challenge comes of course from applying your knowledge in the optional side levels, which range from self explanatory to... well... you'll be shoving boxes around aimlessly for half an hour until it suddenly clicks.There were some moments of frustration in this game. However, a distinct majority of times where you get stuck, the solution turns out to be something that you just overlooked. Thinking outside the box, one could say, haha. There are a couple hitches, and the challenge levels at the end are certainly headscratchers (I still haven't done them all as of writing this,) but overall it very rarely felt unfair, or pulled something out of the aether to trick you. It gave you room for error and time to experiment, and you could remedy any mistakes or misinputs with a back button and a restart button (back button also undoes your reset if you accidentally hit it like I did a dozen or so times, haha.)Other than that, not much to say. The aesthetics are simple and cute, and the music is very pleasant, and fitting for the respective worlds they're in. Certainly a recommend from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty interesting concept for puzzles, but oddly approachable. There are some really challenging puzzles, but nothing felt unachievable nor that the leap for the Aha moment was too far or simply obtuse. I think it might actually be a bit disappointing with how the last couple of mechanics kind of stopped evolving on neat concepts and became focused on creating scenarios. Hard to describe without spoiling, but I had a good time.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics, music, game design, level design... it's simply a very well crafted game on every aspect!Absolutely mind-bending and in the end I decided not to complete all extras because it simply was too hard for me and not fun anymore. I didn't enjoy the end as much and the beginning, despite the clever level design.Fun fact: the author tried to "keep an approachable level of difficulty, relatively easy compared to other games in the hardcore puzzle genre".
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Sokoban but like a twist and some really mind-bending puzzles, this is for you.Each section (hub) presents a new addition to the way you can modify a Sokoban and I have to say all of them are amazing. The levels grow in terms of how hard they are, which is really nice and I believe quite difficult, so kudos on that. The "main line" is not terribly difficult I think (although still hard to complete), some of the side levels are really big brainteasers. I still have yet to finish many of them, and I absolutely intend to, it's just that addictive. The only issue is that after 5-6 puzzles, I know I need to stop because it's quite draining sometimes and I'm not in the perfect condition anymore lol. 10/10 second best Sokoban I've every played (after Fish Fillets II).
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been this awed by a puzzle game since I played Portal for the first time. The most amazing part to me is that every puzzle so far has felt completely manageable; I could easily see a world in which these mechanics feel too overwhelming or have too many steps to be able to really think about a solution but it has never gotten to that point yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Clever puzzles with a fun central mechanic of puzzle arenas being nested within other puzzle arenas, including themselves. It's a little easy at first, but after about 60 solved (of ~360) it's starting to feel reasonably hard. You will enjoy this if you like going "ah, of course!". There aren't a huge amount of red herring solutions, you just have to think things through with the information presented and usually the logical solution is the correct one. Whether you think that's good or not is personal taste.Would like to point out that there's some accessibility issues in the optional harder levels - there's some that continuously zoom out or in in a concentric level, which doesn't make the puzzle meaningfully harder but messes with your ability to process things. I would appreciate a checkbox that disables these UI screws. Not sure how frequent this is going to be, but there's been 2 of them as of 65 levels in.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Really fascinating how much the developer have been able to accomplish. I'm amazed over how the game continues to challenge me and constantly changing. Truly impressed over how the developer is making so much of a game with so "little" (few controls, and similarity in the "objects"). It's only downside is that you sometime have no idea of what to do and get stuck.., but on the other hand that also makes it more satisfactory when the solution gets clear.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game! It as a very minimalist design, but to me, the puzzle design was perfect and the difficulty was perfect such that the levels were very challenging, but I was still able to solve every one without a guide, even if I had to spend up to 30 mins doing so. The solutions never felt cheap, always satisfying, and the same goes for the mechanics. For most new mechanics in the game, I never thought, "where did that come from?", they make sense within the game world, and may have even been something you already thought about before it was introduced as a mechanic. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Very good introductory puzzle game! Not to say it doesn't get difficult, but it eases you into the concepts gently. Left me wanting more.To put my praise simply, I am not a puzzle guy, or a completionist. I 100%ed this game. I've 100%ed 3 games. It was easy enough that I never got frustrated, and hard enough I wasn't bored.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good box pushing puzzle game that does some fun, trippy stuff with its recursion mechanic. It constantly plays with new gimmicks and twists to provide a varied experience. While it gets reasonably challenging and has some good head-scratchers, the game overall is on the easier side - I got stumped twice in total out of the 364 puzzles, and felt like a dunce when I looked up the solution for one of them. The overall design trends toward a clean minimalism, with little in the way of obfuscation, red herrings, or complex solutions. Most of the levels are so barebones you can usually figure out what to do simply by poking around and trying every option available. Some of the later stages of the game feel like they're more about highlighting unique gimmicks but don't manage to work the gimmick into a satisfying puzzle. Still, the best puzzles here hit the mark of being a satisfying challenge but not something that will cause most people to give up in frustration. The challenge puzzles after you beat the "normal" game are for the most part very rewarding. Points for creativity as well. I'd recommend this one a lot to anyone who likes puzzles but isn't a super hardcore expert solver.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much another puzzle game masterpiece, if you like being challenged. Generous amount of levels with a broad enough offering such that you'll rarely get hard-locked out of a path to progress. Definitely has a "rhetorical" approach to introducing concepts within the vast possibilities of its ruleset which steadily builds upon itself: "Okay you just successfully applied this concept, but how do you apply that with other things you've learned, or with this constraint?"You have to think outside the box, you have to think inside the box, you have to BE the box. If you have Baba is You or other similar spatial-logic/sokoban games in your collection, this is a necessary addition.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Finished the challenge levels. My brain is mush. I can see the 6th dimension. game gud One of the single most accessible and well-designed puzzle games ever. Almost every single puzzle feels completely incomprehensible yet perfectly intuitive and I was always dumbfounded at how much sense it made while being complete gibberish to spell out. You can tell by the end that the base game puzzles become just "hey look what I can do" but I will update once the challenge puzzles are done with. I had a lovely time with the game.I played Recursed (one of the inspirations for this) before this and while I dropped that game after a while since one level in particular stumped me (and the crystals were too spicy not to attempt to find so I kinda dug my own grave) I finished this one (haven't done the challenge puzzles yet).
