_childDocuments_.review: Very fun mind-bendy puzzle game. The puzzles are generally pretty easy by the standards of a dedicated puzzle-game, but more than make up for it in uniqueness. Often half the battle is just figuring out what's going on. It also does a good job introducing new mechanics to center each chapter around, while always feeling like a natural extension of what you'd seen so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game in a puzzle games bundle and yesterday I completed it at 100% and LOVED every bit of it. IMO, Patrick's Parabox is puzzle design perfection: perfect progression, perfect learning curve, every puzzle (until the very last) felt like adding just a little bit of something new without ever feeling repetitive or filler and every new mechanic is added just at the right moment and then presented again in the last part when you've mastered it.If you love puzzle games, you'll love Patrick's Parabox.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a great puzzle game that throws new concepts at you while never really becoming overwhelming. Each world has a new mechanic that you are slowly introduced to and then slowly get grander and grander within each world. It's a puzzle game about recursion so it can be a bit mind bending but once you start figuring things out, it's really satisfying. This is a great puzzle game and if you're a fan of puzzle games, you should absolutely play this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10, and I don't say that lightly.If a video catches your interest, there is a demo.If you like the demo, know there is a LOT more content in the full game. Like... a LOT. Brilliantly designed! Every level is just a single step further into the deep end. It never felt overwhelming except for some of the end-game challenges, but that's why they are called that.Consistently fresh through it all.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A masterclass of puzzle design. Boxes inside boxes inside boxes... Infinite delight :)No bullshirt mechanics, no padding levels, no unreadable graphics, no easy-to-understand-but-hard-to-execute puzzles, just you, your fried brain, and a cute little elevator music10/10Pro-tip: if you're stuck, come back tomorrow it's going to be okay
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome. Author has to be a genius. So much creativity and mindbending mechanics. In later levels I giggled almost in each one when I figured it out.  Patrick's Parabox has a honour place on the top of my favourite puzzle games next to the games like The Fish Fillets, The Witness, Cocoon, Snakebird... Thank you., Patrick.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a cool Sokoban-style puzzle game that loves to throw in new ideas, like being able to enter inside boxes and recursion.It has a lot of puzzles and mechanics, but they are gradually introduced, and each section is centered around a theme.To progress, you only need to complete the main puzzles, which are easier than the optional puzzles you’ll find around each section as well.Just beating the game is hard but doable; however, some challenge puzzles are tricky. Good luck beating all 364 puzzles on your own!Thankfully, there are plenty of guides available, even to just give you a hint to help you progress.The game is also well-presented, with smooth graphics and animations, and a nice soundtrack.An easy recommendation on sale if you enjoy the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: So good. So so so good. Really intuitive but also mindtwisty puzzles. Love the whole aesthetic as well - made it easy to understand where/when I was. I could often deduce the general gist for each level on first view, but with just enough unknown/uncertainty that I got some of that great 'aha' juice when I finally figured it out. For the most part (except for the most complex levels)  I didn't feel the challenge was in implementing the solution, but rather in figuring out that last little twist that would make my solution work.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful piece of art. If you like puzzle games at all, you owe it to yourself to play this one. The puzzles are mind-bending, but so well designed and paced, that you will be surprised that the puzzle is possible up until you understand how to complete them. This game's difficulty curve for me was exactly in the right place. I got into a sort of flow state and just kept going solving more and more complex puzzles until the game ended. And the post-game content was great as well.A++ 10/10. One of the absolute best games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, the premise of this game is very creative, and the implementation of that premise is near perfection.  At no point in this game was I very frustrated, and I never felt that any puzzle was unapproachable.   The vast majority of mechanics in this game are fun and intuitive, with only a few exceptions.  I personally like the artstyle.  I thought it was cool how recursion looked, which I'm sure was complicated technically.Overall, Patrick's Parabox is an enjoyable game. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Superb. Block-pushing puzzles through the looking-glass, in a dimension of telescoping recursion and nested infinities. Gleefully counter-intuitive, dizzy, mind-boggling... and also eminently fair and friendly. The game wants to disorient you, but it also wants you to succeed and have fun. I don't take that for granted! Kudos to the designer for making mind-bending craziness feel welcoming and, ultimately, logical. A thrilling experience for anyone interested in puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of the greatest puzzle games i've ever played. every time you think you've got it all figured out, it throws another completely insane mechanic at you that makes you feel like an absolute neanderthal. and yet, when you come out the other side, you'll feel like the smartest person in existence. 100% recommend, even if you're not that into puzzle games.also, whoever designed the ascii levels is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sadist.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A real thinker with a great overall learning curve. New mechanics are introduced in each section of levels, with each area building on the mechanics before it to make for increasingly complex puzzles that you'll have no trouble keeping up with. I've found that the red challenge levels can sometimes have a punishing difficulty spike, but that makes solving them all the more rewarding. So many moments that made me "Wow!" at the creativity behind this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: "A fun, but quite short game. There's only so much you can do with boxes, rooms and walls before it gets repetitive." - Is what I expected, but boy was I wrong. I'm impressed how many different tricks this game has to offer without adding more and more elements. Every puzzle is unique and challenging, some more than others. Despite borrowing some ground rules from Sokoban, it never felt remotely like that because it's a different kind of challenge.Better pack some Aspirin if you like to think outside the box, because here that's still inside the box.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A very good puzzle game. The principle of recursivity between boxes leads to very clever puzzles. I did all 364, the dev disclaimer that there is no 'filler', no repetitive puzzle, is true : Each one is different, and forces you to think to another solution. By the way, nice music too.I loved this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I love puzzles but Sokoban-style games are always super intimidating to me. "Stephen's Sausage Roll", "Monsters Expedition", "Snakebird", the most frightful, "Baba Is You". These are amazing games but they have serious difficulty curves, and maybe I'm dumb but in all three it's not long before you hit levels that you need to chew on for hours, or even days.This game does not have this problem. The puzzles escalate seamlessly in difficulty, never feeling too easy but it never overwhelms. It's challenge but also a joy to play.And the genius exploration of an already genius puzzle concept easily sets the game right up next to the greats. Where other games would introduce lots of new mechanics with levers and gates, Patrick's Parabox only introduces one or two new "mechanics" in the whole game. Instead if focuses in on tons of fascinating interactions between them, giving the feeling of being a scientist in a world with alternate physics.10/10 puzzle game, would break the fabric of spacetime again.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an amazing premise with really clever puzzle designs that are challenging without being frustrating. Each new concept is introduced with some simple, straightforward examples, and new concepts are introduced often enough that the game never feels drawn out.Many standouts in this genre also have amazing premises and clever puzzle design, but they all have a frustration wall where the solutions quickly become so obtuse that a significant amount of playtime comes from trial and error and that starts to dampen the satisfaction of finding a solution. In Patrick's parabox, it felt like the vast majority (>95%) of the puzzles had an obvious solution, and the challenge was figuring out which steps you needed to take to achieve that solution. There was very little trial and error, and most of the trial and error was confined to very simplistic puzzles meant to introduce the player to a new mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game so much! It contains some of the most truly challenging but pleasantly reasonable puzzles. The progressive difficulty of the levels strikes a perfect balance between steadily introducing new features for players to get familiar with and providing more complicated challenges for those interested. The novelty and creativity of this game is on a whole new level among its category. So proud of myself for solving all the levels on my own! Definitely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: For a game revolving around pushing boxes with unique quirks, Patrick surely did his best to provide this weird and quirky game. And with his name no less! Even I wouldn't put my own name like this for a game this good!Regardless, I had my share with Parabox, especially when I was screaming my head when  (yeah I think they're like...non-binary). It takes a while to solve each puzzle, but afterwards, you get the hang of each mechanic and how they work. And heck, with 300+ levels no less, you'd be wanting to take time to solve each and every one of them.Overall, I had my solid time with Patrick's funny game. Do pick this up if you want to waste your time with blocks.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A great puzzle game. New mechanics are (for the most part) added on in a way that makes it feel like you are uncovering new aspects of the world's rules, rather than adding stuff to the game; each mechanic choice is choses carefully to allow for incorperating other mechanics and leaving no uncoved case.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 I gained 3 IQ points just for completing the gameThis is an amazingly well-designed puzzle game. In less than 15 minutes it introduces all the core mechanics, and the rest of the game is just exploring the consequences of these mechanics.  I was continually amazed by the emergent behavior that appears in certain configurations of boxes (e.g. ). The mathematician in me was very happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt one of the best puzzle games I have ever played. Every time I thought I had a good grasp on the mechanics a new wrinkle would be added that kept it interesting from start to finish. Also, you might think to yourself during the main game "What if X mechanic worked like Y instead?", like I did. Luckily the game has an appendix with a handful of levels based on what the game would have been like if the mechanics function in different ways that still make sense. An absolute blast and a half! If you like puzzle games, and especially the Sokoban subgenre, do yourself a favour and check it out! This is up there with 'Baba Is You' as far as quality, design, and brain melting goes! Can't wait to see what comes next from this dev!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing twist(s) on the classic sokoban formula. If you enjoy puzzle games you'll like this one. I finished all non-challenge puzzles plus about a quarter of the challenge puzzles in just under 9 hours. The challenge puzzles get pretty hard, and even the regular puzzles are amusingly mind-bending. :) As others have said, there's no story. It's just puzzles, but that's standard for sokoban.Comparing directly to the maze-solving game The Witness my impression was that in the witness no puzzles were solveable "by accident" (i.e. you were required to understand the mechanics in order to solve every puzzle and no puzzle could be solved without understanding the mechanics). In Parabox /some/ of the puzzles require understanding, but because of the more limited move space it's possible to solve a number of the puzzles without fully understanding what you did or why it worked.Overall a very solid puzzle game, especially played in short spans. Makes your brain hurt, but you can keep coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent puzzle game. The game made me dizzy at times, but I thoroughly enjoyed all the mechanics. As I was nearing the end of the main game, I was interested in seeing some more demanding puzzles. I was pleased to see there was still a nice chunk of puzzles left after the reading the "end." I liked how the challenge puzzles really tested my understanding on the mechanics.I played the entire thing on the SteamDeck, and it ran flawlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good at making me feel smarter then I probably actually am. It has puzzles which are mind bending and a bit crazy, and while I have a good grasp of the game. I still sometimes barely grasp some of the more complicated mechanics Despite this I worked my way through the game, half through logic and half through intuition. It really is a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: To play parabox is to be invitied into a world of of interesting phenomena that you can discover through experimentation, and the world is pulling you along and excitedly leading you through its sweetest discoveries.Which is to say, it's a game, that is good.The music, though a little strange, is uniquely joyful.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: this is genuinely one of the best puzzle games I've ever played and I haven't even 100%'d it or checked out any custom levels yet, got it from a humble bundle recently and I can't believe I slept on this game for so long, don't even wait for a sale or bundle like I did, even at full price I promise it's worth every penny
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game strongly reminds me of , but with a cleaner design. Gravity, water, locks and keys, etc. are all ditched to focus more on the Sokoban gameplay and recursive levels. You also don't need to remember which rooms go where because the whole level is generally visible to you at all times Every world features a themed nuance or new mechanic to keep you scratching your head.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game enough if you want a truly head scratching puzzle game. I played the demo a while back and let me tell you it's been a few years since a demo made me want a game bad enough to... practically immediately buy it.Speaking of buying it. Is it worth the price? Yes. If you can get it on sale it's a bonus. I don't think I paid full price? But I can say that if I had I wouldn't regret it.I'm 2.7 hours in (probably a bit more since I've played some on steam deck while not connected to wifi) and I don't know how many puzzles I've gone through but I know without a doubt that I'm NOWHERE near the 350 puzzles in this game. On top of that, even when I do beat it I know I will be able to replay this game. The puzzles are enough of an "out of the box" thinking *buh dum tis* kind of situation that I promise you won't beat this game and go back and remember the solution to everything. So you'll definitely be able to go back and play it more if you liked it the first time you played it.The puzzles in this game ARE difficult, and it takes the kind of thinking of games like Baba Is You. Difficult puzzles, but never difficult in a way that doesn't make sense or that seem unfair. You just have to try to look at things a bit differently. This game is hard but I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love it.When I want to wake up the skull organ this is the game I've been picking up.I've also not used a guide yet. I refuse. I get a kind of competitive with games like this one and Baba is You. Where I REFUSE to use guides because damn it that would mean the game wins. I can't let the game win! I'm the one playing a game! So I have to be the winner! And I won't let that win be tainted by guides!!!So sometimes I've been sitting there beating my head against the wall that is this game and then I figure it out and I'm so damn proud of myself!Enough of me raving about the puzzles though. Let's talk other more technical stuff.The art design and sound design are also simple, but still wonderful in their simplicity. It's nice to look at and the music is nice to listen to.The puzzle design if you don't know what the puzzles actually are is brilliant. You will have several places you need to move boxes and yourself into in order to beat a puzzle. This will generally require moving boxes in and out of each other in a paradoxical way. It's really... REALLY cool. Just pushing boxes into more boxes sometimes almost in a russian nesting doll kind of situation with a box inside a box inside a box as you try to get everything arranged the way you need to.I mentioned briefly that I've played this on steam deck. It does play REALLY well and I have zero complaints about playing it on the steam deck.Controls are really simple. Just use WASD to move around.All in all. Patrick's Parabox is one of the best puzzles games I've played since finding Baba Is You (I keep comparing it because the kind of difficulty they both are makes me compare them). And I've played a lot of puzzles games and many have felt like they fell short in either length or puzzle difficulty (looking at you A Little to the Left).Patrick's Parabox presents a lot of puzzles, feels like I will get a lot of time with it, and really really good difficulty for the price you pay and I can't recommend it enough. It's not aesthetic. It's not quick. It's not easy.But it does manage to be chill, simple, yet really difficult in a way that is still REALLY enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The "gimmick" on how to solve the puzzles is really inventive and honestly really awesome. I kept getting surprised by the new additions that kept getting thrown in as you progressed worlds. The problem is puzzles aren't as tight as other games. I have completed every puzzle up to almost the end of world 9, Transfer.There are a bunch of puzzles that don't feel inventive enough from the prior puzzles to warrant its existence. The entire first hour, up to world 4 or 5, was a complete slog filled with, well, filler. It got better but was still marred with filler. There were a lot of puzzles as well where I just happened to stumble upon the solution just trying to map things out and it didn't make me feel great. A thing that is starting to rear its head that stems from the mediocre puzzle design is apparent in Transfer. There are first blocks that you can enter with even number of spaces. This makes knowing where you will enter something you have to find out by experimenting rather than something intuitive. The boxes also don't signal to you bow many spaces they do have so this is something you again have to test yourself rather than being able to just "know". This isn't an issue with earlier levels but at world 9, they start throwing boxes with different spaces that you need to transfer between. One puzzle in particular I spent more time figuring out that the puzzle boxes were spaced 3x3, 3x3, and a 9x9 than I did figuring out the actual solution. Then the game starts throwing mismatched box sizes that aren't a clean multiple of the other, i.e. 5x5 transfer to a 6x6. This is going to have to lead to experimentation on how the logic works for transfer along with some transfers may only work 1 way due to this.The lack of tight puzzle design was already bad early on and gets worse as I progress. World 9 is my breaking point as I assume that it will just get more and more junbled the further I progress in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I can't explain it well but this game is beautiful in how it seems to embed its mechanics within the game itself. If you don't know what I mean, think Baba Is You. Patrick's shares a lot of the same DNA and accomplishes a lot of the same goals, but in a more approachable well paced package IMHO.Easy recommend for any avid puzzle/sokoban fan!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while, but I did it. I completed every official puzzle in Patrick's Parabox. My opinion after 100% completion: It's absolutely worth buying if you love puzzle games. There's no story to speak of, so you'll really only be playing it for the sense of completion. For me, it was good game to boot up here and there, complete a couple puzzle boxes, then go back to whatever I was doing.If you want the best experience, DON'T LOOK UP THE SOLUTIONS. There were points where I wanted to tear my hair out, especially with those end-game challenge levels, but if you just put it down and come back to it later you'll usually figure it out. And when you do, you feel like a genius.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and mind-bendy, but not hyper-difficult (at least for me). It's a similar feel to games like Stephen's Sausage Roll or Baba Is You or Monster's Expedition, but I didn't find it nearly as difficult as any of them. The meta trick of a box inside itself is used well in many puzzles, although I was just a tiny bit dissatisfied with how they handled some of the edge cases. (Some little side thoughts about this last point. In a game like this, once the creators set up the general rules of the universe, there's an obvious way that most things should behave. But there are always those strange little exceptions where the mechanics seem to conflict with themselves, and the creators have to have the game do *something*, even if it's going to seem completely arbitrary. Some games make it so that those exceptions are rare or that no puzzles depend on the arbitrary mechanics they implemented. Some relegate those mechanics to only bonus puzzles or only a few of the hardest end-game puzzles. Parabox just embraces them completely, relatively early in the game, building entire sequences of levels around those arbitrary edge case behaviors, thus creating even more edgy edge cases, and the end result is that those puzzles just don't feel as natural as the others. Don't get me wrong; they're still fun to solve. They're just not quite as satisfying to understand.)Anyway, I enjoyed Patrick's Parabox quite a bit. The puzzles were just difficult enough to force me to bend my brain around them, but not so hard that I couldn't relax while playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoys the concept of puzzle games, I wanted to check a mind-bending experience like this one out. I snagged it from a Humble Bundle deal where there was a variety of puzzle games for an inexpensive price. Patrick’s Paradox highlights the mechanics through the area names. However, some experimentation has to be done to see how these all unfold. Regardless, this provided me hours of brain power and fun to work with. It’s okay to walk away when thinking about solving these because you then approach it from a different perspective. I never thought I’d cause paradoxes as a square.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It's a total mind melter. "What happens if I move a portal inside of itself?": The Game. It has tons of recursive puzzles that make you think in completely new ways and form completely new connections. Play the demo. It starts off with the basic square block pushing puzzles and goes completely off the deep end.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A unique twist on the Sokuban formula with flawless execution. Challenging enough to feel rewarding without a single level that felt unfair. Every set is optimised to make the most of each individual mechanic and ensure you never feel lost even on the more complex levels. The simple controls, graphics and music greatly aid in ensuring the game never feels frustrating to play. Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys puzzles, especially if you've played Baba is You.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games of all time.  I remember playing a block-pushing puzzle game themed around a pirate on my Kindle, and I have a great affection for it, but this is the absolute pinnacle of the block-pushing form.  Everyone should play this game.  It's also much easier than Baba Is You, another fantastic block-pusher which is good for completely different reasons.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. Don't get fooled by the minimalistic visuals, this game is seriously impressive. I've been obsessed with it all day and had to force myself to quit so I don't get weird dreams (might be too late for that already). Right when you feel like you get the hang of the mechanics, the game introduces new twists and forces you to keep thinking in new directions. As stunning and mind bending as these puzzles are, I'm almost more impressed by the amount of effort it must have taken to keep the core gameloop, which really just boils down to pushing boxes around, so consistently fresh and rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best puzzle games i've ever played. the core mechanic of entering and exiting boxes is very interesting and well executed, and there's also a nice spread of mechanics added onto it that make for neat puzzles! the whole thing is wrapped up in very clean polish that pulls everything together, and the music's great and fits well. i wasn't totally stumped by any of the puzzles like i was with a handful of baba is you's tougher puzzles, but there's some nice and tricky ones here! highly recommend to anyone who enjoys pure puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is, as of writing this, THE best puzzle game I have ever played. Like, out of all 364 levels in the game there was only 1 I got kinda annoyed by, and I can't even say I dislike the level, it just had a tedious setup process to get to the actual puzzle I did like 2 dozen times before figuring it out. That's it, that's the 1 and only complaint i have with this game, a single puzzle.From the music, to the level design, to the art style, this game is just perfect for what its trying to be. If you're even slightly into puzzle games definitely give this game a shot. It's level structure and plentiful amount of beginner friendly puzzles means even if you're not very good at puzzle games you'll still probably be able to beat the game at the very least.Many of these easy puzzles don't even feel like filler either if you already understand the concepts they're teaching, as many of them are what i can describe as "Spectacle Puzzles", technically easy to solve but look really cool to solve. Not many puzzle games lend themselves to being able to do this as they're concept as a puzzle game just doesn't allow for easy but cool looking puzzles, just another big reason this is now my favorite puzzle game.So anyway, buy this game, it's absolutely worth the 20 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and cute logic puzzle game which introduces a new gimmick every few levels. It scratches the same itch "Baba is you" does by introducing an original concept and building on top of it to gradually make the game more complex.I'd say, if you enjoyed "Baba is you", you should definitely keep this one in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. It's everything I want in a puzzle game and there is a lot of content. I'm 3 hours in and I've not even completed half the levels, and I haven't completed every available level. Great game, super worth the price. If you liked the puzzles of portal, you'll probably like this too.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: You can be looking at a puzzle for 10 minutes, have no idea how to solve it and leave it. You come the next day and solve it in 20 seconds.The graphics are simple and the game-play is also simple. The puzzles gain complexity as you progress. This combination and a great level design, makes this game challenging and very enjoyable. Totally recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: By far the most fun I've ever had with a puzzle game. The introduction of the recursion mechanic made me feel genuine joy. Many of the puzzles are so mind bending they lead me to audibly say "what the ♥♥♥♥." The dopamine hit upon solving those ones is better than crackEven after just a few hours, with all of the mind bendingly awesome features this game has packed in, I've already had more fun than I would after dozens of hours playing most games. I had to stop the game to write this because I am just so genuinely blown away at how this game evolves as new mechanics are introducedI wish I could pay more than the asking price for this game
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games you could ever play. Its simple concept gets twisted in interesting ways that will keep your brain active. You will feel like a genius after solving some of the puzzles. If you like games like Baba Is You, you will definitely love Patrick's Parabox. Congrats Patrick on a masterpiece of puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: After going through the brain-melting experience that is Baba is You, I was desperate to find other puzzlers like it.  Stephen's Sausage Roll was WAY too hard for me, a Monster's Expedition was very good, but not super long, though.  Patrick's Parabox, however, does it all for me.  Tons of creative levels, user-created levels, and is absolutely brain-melting in the best ways.My only real gripe, which is quite minor at most, is the linear level progression.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I like logic games a lot so this game fit the bill pretty well. I paid full price for this game which is something I rarely do and I can say it was definitely worth it. It was fairly addicting, so I just played for hours till I finally 100% the game. As you can see by my hours spent playing, it is fairly long to finish to completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic puzzle game. The mechanics are so fluid, well thought-out and complementary to each other that, after a while, doing the base puzzles of each level almost felt like learning a new chapter of a language, and doing the challenges like using said language in the most natural, fluent way possible. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a super mind-bending but still accessible puzzle game. If you want to try something that is difficult and mind blowing at several points during the game, but still want to be able to 100% the game as a casual player (given enough time), I highly recommend this game. It's difficult, but I think it still manages to stay accessible to the average player, who I expect would be able to complete every one of the 350+ puzzles, assuming you're willing to put in the time.Very underrated puzzle game, just beat it 100% and it was amazing :)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic fractal puzzle game, you must move the world within the world and more to solve many sokoban-like puzzles.Self-similar, non-self-similar and even holons are present in this game. The music is alright too, the art can be quite stunning actually. A rare game belonging to the same class as that of Baba Is You that breathes fresh life into the puzzle genre, a superb entry.Extremely good, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox
