_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent logic game. Very minimal graphics, nice smooth colors, and low but ever present music. Move some (para)boxes into their spots, move on to the next level. However, space in this game is relative, and that's where this game shines. I 100% love the "blue side" (?) levels, where the levels go ultra minimal and present as ascii, like something out of a console output. Very very much recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game for those who love puzzles. Great level design & soundtrack too.I dibble dabble in puzzle games here and there but wouldn't call it my jam. Despite that, I really enjoyed the game although it did begin to outstay its welcome for me towards the end. There are a huge number of puzzles! Way more than I'd expected.An easy recommend from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is excellently paced and designed, teaching you each element and its varied applications one at a time before asking you to begin piecing them all together. Having 100% the main game, I can confidently say it has plenty of challenges to try your mind at with ever-increasing difficulty. Sometimes, it's even just fun to see what sort of paradoxes you can create!And...wow, that's a lot of post-game puzzles. I've a long way to go even still.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of sokoban type games, and Patrick's Parabox is one of the most interesting, fun, and surprisingly kind of easy. I hate to admit this, but I do occasionally use walkthroughs for games like Baba Is You, but I never felt the need to in this game. Lots of fun concepts that get explored pretty thoroughly throughout the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a real gem, a modern Sokoban game aimed at math/computer nerds, incorporating concepts like recursion and infinities of various orders.Although the creator is relatively unknown, he is an indie dev with over a decade of experience, and it's easy to believe it: the way the mechanics are explained and executed is nothing short of masterful.If you're playing this game, you're likely on the autistic spectrum (it's impressive that 10% of players have platined it, unprecedented numbers). As a result, you might find the main game a bit straightforward (the puzzles tend to solve themselves to some extent, hard to explain precisely), but fret not, the developer has hidden around fifty mind-bending levels behind the credits.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Requires creativity, imagination, planning and execution - a mind-bender of sorts. I recommend this game to anyone who likes to bang their head against a wall until it breaks or search a dark room for the light switch. Contains a vast variety of puzzles from incrementally solved ones to eureka moment puzzles. Challenges you to realise that your worst enemy is your own thought process and imagination and forces you to push past them.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I bought "viewfinder" the new hotness in puzzle games, it was too easy and basic, they didn't think about all the implications of their own mechanics, so I returned it, and used that money to buy a real puzzle game, that continues to reinvent itself, thinks about all its own implications, and provides a real challenge. thank you Patrick. This is money well spent.  Highly highly recommend. Leave games like "viewfinder" with its flashy but basic mechanics for the masses, and let us puzzle game sickos have the real stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and challenging Sokoban (box moving puzzle game) that uses reality-warping logic puzzles to create some fantastic challenges.While the core mechanics take a little bit to get your head around, like moving boxes into boxes and then moving them in and out of themselves, everything naturally flows and there were only a few times I found myself getting stuck in paradoxical loops.The ghost blocks were the only ones that really caused me confusion as you have to 'possess' other boxes and that can get very confusing when it interacts with the other mechanics, otherwise everything felt very cleanly implemented and resulted in some really challenging and exciting puzzles.Highly creative, lots of fun, a smooth progression of mechanics that keep you playing, and they really go to lengths as they explore so many fun possibilities based on all the different ideas at play. A must have for any puzzler.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the demo for this game in a mystery game tournament a couple years ago, and was mesmerised.  Great puzzle game, with plenty of fun mechanics to build off of. The difficulty was well balanced, with the main levels being pretty quick, the bonus levels being rather tough, and the challenge levels being waking nightmares. Most mechanics were explained very well, but *SPOILERS* the order in which the additional players that copy your movements could have been better shown. Maybe the happier faces move later? Regardless, I highly recommend this game. Well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Given the game mechanics' implications, it's a complete wonder how the game functions so well and smoothly. It genuinely boggles the mind that this game exists and just... works.Great puzzle design on top of that. Despite the unintuitive mechanics, the puzzles ease you into understanding them while staying fresh throughout the game, thanks to some unexpected but natural twists.There were only 2 puzzles (out of hundreds) where it felt unclear to me what was going on, and both were in the optional post-game challenge section.In short, this game just an absolute blessing upon this world and a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: is, simply put, one of the most creative and challenging puzzle games I have ever had the honor to play. You get to explore several fascinating paradoxes in this block-pushing game, like infinite recursion, shrinking infinitely small, or exiting into an infinite void. It may start out simple, but you will be delighted by how advanced and mind-bending many of the puzzles can be. Never once was I unsatisfied by a box's solve, and it is a testament to the game's fun and creativity that 10% of players have strived to complete all bonus levels. With ~15 hours of puzzling problems and 10 more of advanced challenges, this game is WELL worth your time and money. Buy it, and you won't regret it!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best  puzzle games I have ever played. Really does some cool things with the idea of boxes within boxes creating paradoxes and so on. I never really felt the game jumped in difficulty too far and only during the post-game challenges did I feel it got ridiculously hard sometimes, which is totally fair. Took almost 24 hours to complete without the help from any guide, so definitely worth the price. If you're uncertain because of the price, just download the demo to get an idea of the types of puzzles first, they're really cool and make your head spin sometimes
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: (played this game mostly offline, so playtime is not accurate)This is an fantastic puzzle game, each group of levels introducing a new mechanic. While every mechanic can be used in the earlier levels, they have been hand crafted in such a way that the straight forwards route is the fastest and most obvious one.Also works great on the steam deck
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: The gameplay in Patrick's Parabox is its best strength. The main game is incredibly well balanced, I never had to use a guide and the challenge felt fair. It introduced and evolved on concepts and didn't immediately present you with tough levels, which is a problem I've encountered with other puzzle games. Once you reach a new area, the process starts all over again, keeping it fresh and making you improve your skills over time.Neutral: The post-game is a substantial step-up in difficulty, but I could see it being enjoyable for someone who is better at Sokoban puzzle games than me.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a top tier sokoban puzzle game.Mechanics are very unique and plentiful. They are explored and intermixed to the deepest. There are no useless parts and puzzles are small. Difficulty is medium to challenging. Presentation is beautiful and clean.If you liked AAA puzzles like BiU, SSR and Draknek puzzles - don't hesitate, you'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I was scrolling through the multiple puzzle games that were on sale in Steam, and I happened to come across this game, Patrick's Parabox. I decided to buy it after reading the description, cause I do like infinite loops and all that. The game started off simple: you push a box into its corresponding hole and you win. As the levels progress, new mechanics are introduced such as pushing a box outside of itself, going inside of boxes, and even possessing them! This game really tests your problem-solving skills and each new level really tests your brain. And while it may take a while to solve a level (or even days), you'll eventually get that "aha" moment and know how to solve it instantly. It's a very rewarding game and gives you the sense that "you did that all by yourself with no hints whatsoever!" The soundtrack also fits the mood of the game as well, whether it be taking your time with puzzles to hardcore "thinking" music for moments like "How do I solve this," and "So if I move this block here..." and other moments like that. If you're looking for a very casual puzzle game with a relaxing soundtrack to get by the day, I would definitely try Patrick's Parabox! Each level will cure your boredom right from the start!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mindblowing puzzle game with well designed puzzles and mechanics that force you to think in unusual (but self-consistent and logical) ways while being beautiful to look at. Screenshots and videos don't really do it justice because part of the beauty of it only really emerges when you start playing with the mechanics and realising the consequences of different things.If you aren't sure, just try the free demo! I skipped buying this on sale a few weeks ago, as I had too many games, but a few days ago I tried the free demo and it made me immediately buy the game for full price that night. It's just so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are all well-balanced, being a perfect size, and all based on a single principle which can be reasoned out without resorting to brute force. The new themes with every set of puzzles, and occasional new mechanics, mean that it never gets repetitive or stale. A very satisfying puzzle experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is my new favorite puzzle game. The overall puzzles can be fairly complicated but by working backwards and figuring out where the pieces 'need' to be it's very possible to break the larger puzzles down conceptually into a connected sequence of shorter puzzles so I'm rarely too frustrated. Overall this game has probably made me think harder than anything else in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Not as mind-boggling as Baba is You, but for many this may be seen as a plus, as this game has a much smoother difficulty curve than Baba. Patrick's Parabox is a very clever puzzle game that always introduces new interactions every world to keep things fresh. While many levels can be solved in a minute or two, some require a little more thinking.The game does feel a little short, but I still think it's worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game will keep breaking your brain. It's a sensational puzzler and to find this much more fun and challenge out of the classic Sokoban gameplay is beyond impressive. The main puzzles move on a nice curve of encouraging play and experimentation with no real consequences. The challenges levels require a lot of thought but if you keep thinking the way the game trains you they will come to you after some work.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I met Patrick at IndieCade a few years ago when he was demoing this game. He was really nice to chat with, and I was really impressed with the game and added it to my wishlist with high hopes. I finally got around to playing it and just finished the main campaign, and I have to say the game really delivered on my expectations. It's a great puzzle game, and he really explored the potential nicely. Challenging, but not too difficult, and pleasant to play, the music is nice too. Looking forward to more puzzle games from this developer in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a fan of Sokoban puzzle games. I think too many in this subgenre rely on irritatingly specific solutions and end up being more about positioning yourself rather than working with a game's mechanics to understand a solution. Add in elements of spatial uncertainty and Patrick's Parabox sounds nightmarish by construction. But after checking out his previous game (Linelith, which I highly recommend), I needed to give this title a fair shake, and it is easily the best Sokoban game you can play right now.Right off the bat, Patrick's Parabox doesn't restrict you as a player. You frequently have free reign to solve puzzles in whatever order you want, and you only need to solve the bare minimum of puzzles in one area to move onto the next. Even when I was hopelessly stuck, I never felt trapped since I had many other conundrums to work out instead. There are also options if needed to unlock all puzzles and solve as you wish, but I personally felt content with the pace of the game's natural process.Patrick's Parabox maintains the Sokoban standards of pushing blocks into a desired position, but the main gimmick is that many boxes are collapsable on themselves or can create infinite loops, allowing you to bend space and push blocks and access corners you normally couldn't. I was consistently surprised at the depth some boxes could provide mechanically, and with over 300 puzzles, there are tons of extremely clever ideas that are gradually and intellectually expanded upon. An early idea teaches you that boxes will move into the center when pushed, and soon you will be exiting one looping paradox to use this center idea to shove a box into an impossible pathway. The simple presentation is always a misdirect from the complex, but never unfair thought process you must have to find a way to a correct solve. I was floored by how little a puzzle gave you to finish it and how much you could actually do with the tools you're handed, but I was equally stumped as often, finding myself toying with directions and boxes in any way I could. Patrick's Parabox is a marvelous title. There is no story; this is a pure puzzler. And while some of the late and post game puzzles are borderline neuroticly difficult, I really enjoyed reaching the credits on PP and hope to play more innovative games from Patrick Traynor in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I am a puzzle lover. The first game I bought for my first paycheck was Opus Magnum from Zachtronics, and I still come back to it from time to time. I did play Baba Is You, but that was a bit hard for me and I ultimately left it alone. Patrick's Parabox (which is a name I love to say aloud and any pun hater can fight me over it) feels like the middle ground - more challenging than Zach Barth's "Problem Solver" games, but not as hardcore as the "Thinking with  Baba" that Baba Is You's later levels requre, at least not right from the start.Would recommend to genre veterans and new dabbling puzzle solvers alike, and of coirse, pun lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Certainly the most innovative sokoban puzzler I've ever played. I started with the demo, and for the first few puzzles, was somewhat bored, as they were simple. That changed when I did a particular thing in one of the levels, that prompted the following thoughts:"Did I just leave reality?""...Oh crap, the later levels are going to require me to leave reality to win, aren't they?"Having just completed all the puzzles, I am moderately pleased with the game. The most interesting part, though, is how the game feels almost less like a puzzle game, and more like a tech demo for making puzzles. Each "world" has about 8-13 puzzles, but only about 2-4 of them felt challenging. The remainder served as an introduction to a new mechanic, and showing how it interacted with the other mechanics.I'd be interested to see what kind of man-made horrors could be made by the community via Steam Workshop, though as far as I can tell that's not in the works.Overall, nice mid-weight puzzle game. A little repetitive at times, but has some very interesting things going on. Not nearly as demented as Stephen's Sausage Roll, for better or for worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance this game has a lot in common with an old game boy game called boxxel.  You have to push blocks to fill in a square and then move the player to a specific tile.  Simple premise right?  This game goes inception deep however.  Just within my 1st hour of the game I could tell this is instantly one of the best puzzle games ever.  Every world brings a new concept and layer to the brilliance that is this game.  The recursive nature of the puzzles will blow your mind.  Parabox out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun puzzle game.The main campaign is not too challenging, with a few exceptions.Each menu-box (stage) introduces a new mechanic gently and the puzzles scale in complexity from there. A lot of effort was obviously put into the level design.The final challenge levels really stumped me for a while, though I was able to solve them all without help eventually. Though occasionally a bit frustrating, once it clicked, there is no better feeling of success.Compared to Snakebird, another great game, Patrick's Parabox has a lot more levels (~350), though you can mostly solve them in a couple of minutes. Snakebird is much more challenging throughout, (difficulty comparable to the final challenge levels here), but with fewer levels and mechanics overall.I thoroughly enjoyed both.The game took me 22,4 hours to get to 100% completion, but a bit short. Time flies when you're having fun I guess.If you have a bit of patience and don't mind some mind-bending thinking-it-through (pun intended), it's great fun.Overall: Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game!If you enjoy puzzle games, you should definitely try this one. There were some levels that I had to leave for a while and come back to after a few hours, and there were two levels that I couldn't solve until the next day. However, it was still manageable, unlike Baba Is You, where I found even getting into a level to be too difficult.But sometimes, I found the puzzles to be too straightforward. For example, when there was an opening in a wall, I initially tried to find a solution without using it, but then realized that my approach was probably wrong because I wasn't utilizing the opening. Once I started thinking about how to use the opening, the solution became quite obvious.Still a great game though.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is an outstanding, mind-bending logic/puzzle game, flawlessly executed, and I heartily recommend it without reservation to my fellow puzzlers. I'd compare it to Baba Is You in the sense that it twists your brain into knots trying to grok each puzzle's set-up so you can work its particular, potentially infinite, "rules" to your advantage, and yet it's also entirely unlike Baba.The game starts out easy enough, but it keeps adding more and more complexity as it goes, repeatedly expanding beyond what one might expect, much to the player's delight (or chagrin? lol). I managed to complete the entire thing solo without needing to look up anything at all, but some of the problems (especially toward the end) definitely took substantial effort and time to figure out.The main game is comprised of a total of 298 puzzles---after which the credits roll---but then there are an additional 66 puzzles following that (in Appendix, Gallery, and Challenge sections). Completing all 364 puzzles grants an achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Man this game is fun! Every time I solve a puzzle I feel like the smartest man alive and simultaneously dumbfounded at the sheer complexity of the game. Each puzzle builds off the previous and can be solved with mostly just trial and error. This simple yet complex game is something I would recommend even to puzzle haters. That is how good it is
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A very clever take on block pushing puzzles. Patrick's Parabox has you pushing blocks into other blocks at first, but very soon goes into non-Euclidian territory where the box you're pushing is the level itself, where boxes are cloned or replica'd or other weird stuff.This isn't the only puzzle game that does it, but where others (especially Baba is you) push you in the deep end, PP seems to be more open to exploration and trying out things. Yes, the puzzles might look impossible at first, but it doesn't have you jumping through all sorts of hoops to reach a solution. PP has plenty of ideas and wants you to find them, not show off how clever the creator is. As such, puzzles often have that "OF COURSE! :D" moment when you figure out how things work. Even though it's sometimes hard to explain...kind of like a Christopher Nolan movie. ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game sometimes makes me feel like I'm tying knots into my brain and that's exacktly why I love it! Simple concept, yet very engaging and it really challenges you to think in ways you might not be used to from other puzzle games. Also the general design of the game and the soundtrack is very aesthetic and calming.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unbelievably good. I discovered it while scrolling Youtube, and from a youtuber I don't even really care about, no less. But the game looked so fascinating I knew I had to try it out. I got the demo, played it, and loved it so much I immediately shelled out $16 to buy the full game. And boy, was it worth it.Never have I been so consistently excited while playing a game. Every level does something new, and yet somehow there are over 300 unique levels. Practically every level I completed left me giddy and hungry for more. Every level is a blast, and the mechanics are presented in such an intuitive manner that I was never left wondering how the game worked - only how to solve the puzzles.It gets quite difficult at times; but the difficulty isn't borne of bad puzzle design, mind-bogglingly large puzzles, or red herrings. When I got stuck, it was always because there was some new use of the mechanics I hadn't thought of yet. The mechanics have a ton of depth, and every puzzle takes advantage of this fact.Easily one of the best games I have ever played. If you love puzzle games, I'm sure you'll love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Simple concept, extremely deep mechanics. Easy to learn, hard to solve. It is a perfect puzzle game that doesn't increase difficulty by just adding more steps to the solution. It actually incorporates new ideas and new patterns to force you to learn and none of it overstays its welcome. 9/10, only thing missing is a banger soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: If you think the biggest problem with Baba Is You was that the "LEVEL" keyword wasn't used enough and would like an entire game about it... well, you're looking at it.The big feature of Patrick's Parabox is that the level is an element inside itself, and a lot of puzzles are based around moving things into and out of the level depending on where the level is situated in itself. And that's just one layer of recursion, it can go deeper than that.I just cleared a puzzle where I needed to swap a clone of the level with the real version so I could push the real level into itself so I could exit it into a section of the level I couldn't reach when I pushed the level onto a switch needed to activate the goal. And that was still the TUTORIAL section of that world!Depending on if you think this stuff sounds cool or dangerous to your brain, you probably already know if this is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Pusher puzzles. Easy, right? Just move the pieces into the right position and you're done. No trouble at all.Sure. Now nest your pusher pieces inside other pieces. Nest them inside themselves. Mirror them inside themselves. Add shadows of self. A simple pusher puzzle takes on a recursive, dimension-distorting reality all its own. Welcome to the rabbit hole.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is an excellent puzzle game. It takes great pleasure in unfolding itself across fifteen (or so) worlds, slowly bringing the player into its mechanical depth until they are flying in and out of the walls and to infinity and back. It's playful but focused, and the progression is quite smooth, though it doesn't really take the reins off its creativity until seconds before the end. The postgame starts to sketch out a little more of the world of clever puzzle tricks and funky computation devices that this concept enables, but still leaves room for the imagination. Nonetheless, I had a lovely time shunting these boxes around.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the best way to describe this game would be to say "I cannot believe that worked." This game is a recommendation on the coding alone, cause I have absolutely no idea how you would code in all of these rules without there being some insane exploits. Regardless, I feel like this game never really leaves you in the dust with its utterly baffling mechanics, with each level set having multiple introductory puzzles so that they can make sure you're ready for the more difficult puzzles later on. The design of this game also lends itself incredibly well to very difficult puzzles to, with simplistic but exacting art allowing for the difficulty of the puzzles to clearly be a matter of understanding mechanics and not the puzzles themselves being poorly communicated.Overall, I feel like this game rivals many of the greats of the puzzle genre while still having its own identity. Highly recommend if you want a satisfying but difficult puzzle game
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a serious master piece in game design.  I know that's a bold statement for a game that on the surface is about pushing blocks around.The thing is, this game shares a design style similar to one of my other favorite designed games -- The Witness.See, there's no tutorials.  No hand overt hand holding.  But it's not a brutal "screw you, figure it out" motif.  They game TEACHES you subtly.  Every new level is comprised of a dozen or more individual puzzles.  Each level builds on a theme and new mechanic, and the mechanics are CLEVER.Each puzzle within a level are roughly sequential, and they are well designed such that they gradually get harder, but teach you more about what you can do with the new mechnic.  But you can also usually skip a few if you get stuck.  There are also optional ones outside the main solution path where you can really go for the brain twisting.All in all, it's a very good pick up and play game, and is constantly delighting you in new ways of solving the puzzles.  Just when you think "what else could they do with boxes?" they come up with some other mind warping mechanic that makes you glad AND sorry you asked.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: In all honesty I found the game to have really good pacing of its puzzles start to finish. Very satisfying to make progress, nothing ever feels too extreme or out of place. A genuinely fresh gimmick which makes you think in a new way. As close to peak puzzling as it gets, to my mind. It holds up against the titans of the genre, like snakebird and good snowman
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Unique and basically flawless puzzle game, up there with Baba Is You and Stephen's Sausage Roll.Something that stands out is that the game never makes you suffer. The game is unusually good at letting you reason your way toward a solution rather than feeling like you have to guess what was in the designer's head. The puzzles are very focused and very carefully ordered.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Reasonably simple in concept (when you get over how cool it is!) but dastardly clever in its execution. These head-scratching, think-quite-literally-outside-of-the-box puzzles are elegantly designed, feeling impossible right up until you hit that moment of realisation.Instantly one of my favourite puzzle games, and paced in such a way that it almost encourages you to do 20 minute sessions of real brainstorming. Also, the box is cute, which is a bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing puzzle game, with a nice balance between length and difficulty. By keeping the scope of each puzzle relatively small, I think it allows the player to visualize the entire solution before acting as opposed to moving at random. Occasionally, the limited number of possible moves has the downside of making you solve the puzzle regardless of your understanding of the mechanics (and a couple of times I didn't even understand what I had done after I did it) but that's a minor concern. The difficulty curve is well thought out and the game gradually makes you dive deeper into each mechanic for a pleasant 100% experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This guy Patrick he knows the trick! He uses this cool idea called pushing blocks but blocks also can be pushed into blocks and sometimes the block is the level and uhhh... Its cool! :) Different parts of the game uses different concepts making the experience very fresh at all times. Feeling like a smart guy? Go ahead and buy!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Clever reality-twisting sokoban puzzler. If you are familiar with the concept of recursion you will get a kick out of this game. A plethora of puzzles, although a few of the sections did feel like they had a few too many puzzles for one concept. The challenge puzzles and appendix are very worthwhile and truly show what this developer is capable of.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: What a great puzzler this is... don't miss it.It scratches a similar itch as Baba is You, but I liked this one better. In Baba, I seemed to just stumble into the correct solutions randomly a lot. In this game, I was able to actually figure out pretty much all the levels. The difficulty was perfect.I noticed one intriguing thing while playing this. I felt there was an interesting interplay between my intuitive brain and calculating brain when playing this... In many cases, I had to actively think and reason out the solution, and in many other cases I felt like my brain went on autopilot and resolved problems faster than I would have been able to explain. In many levels, both processes were present in a pleasant way. I really liked this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games on Steam. Very accessible, fair and intuitive puzzles.Highly recommend you increase game speed in settings. There's undo and reset buttons so don't worry about input mistakes.Haven't beat the game yet so I can't defend the price but definitely have this on your wishlist for seasonal sales.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: just really satisfying in a way i just cant describe. The devs have created an experience with just the correct level of thought, and challenge, without it being impossible. However it still inspires that feeling of how do i describe it...... this desire to say "AW SCREW THIS, Im done with this game"  put the game down because your brain hurts, only to come to the game when you're fresh and  see what mistake you made and feel an accomplishment when you solved a puzzle that you then realize wasn't nearly as hard as you first thought.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite puzzle game ever (except maybe for Portal and Talos Principle, but thats different).Only 3 puzzles left to do now, if you like puzzle games you won't regret it.You don't have to complete every puzzle to make progress which is good if you get stuck.Some of the game ideas are a bit weird, but there's a new idea in each section so you can't get bored.There are challenge levels at the end too which are really bizarre.This game will help you understand the nature of fractals better too.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: What a great puzzle game! The premise is pretty ingenious: if boxes can contain boxes, what if a box contains itself? This self-referential aspect of the puzzles is interesting from the start, but it's even more amazing to see the consequences developed through the course of the game. Seeing new, unexpected behavior emerge from rules I thought I had grasped frequently made me smile.Several other reviews mention the pleasant difficulty curve - I wholeheartedly agree! It's great how the game manages never to ask too much, yet to stay engaging at the same time.One detail I quite enjoyed is the option to select between different graphical styles (in most levels). I'm particularly fond of the ASCII option. Although it's not the most beautiful, it makes it easy to appreciate what's going on behind the scenes.All in all, it's among the best puzzle games I've played, and I had a wonderful time with it. Now to figure out how to create custom levels...
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily my favorite puzzle games I've played in quite some time. It's a very hands on type of puzzle, with very good designs for doing so. With both reset puzzle and rewind a step, and the rewind being able to rewind a reset, it's very kind to people who just want to start trying stuff or push something a step too far. Beyond the good setup, the puzzles are also all very well done, and force you to think about things in different ways. I can not recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really interesting, but I do have a few problems: - There is no meta endgame like there is in a lot of modern Sokoban-like puzzlers. - The level editor is its own unity project. I feel like the dev should update the game, because this is extremely annoying for people who can't get Unity like me (lack of space) - A lot of the endgame puzzles are impossible to understand.Otherwise, the gimmick is really interesting, the levels within levels are mind-boggling in a good way, and the endgame gimmicks are fun to mess around with. I honestly can't describe this game in detail without parroting the word "interesting". Enough to make me give a positive review.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Remind's me so much on my childhood.Where I spend hours to figure out how the next Kwirk Level has to be solved.It is so rewarding when you try to figure out how to solve it - try a couple of things and 5 min. later you come up with an idea thats totaly crazy and it work - on to the next level.Great idea to the developer! I enjoyed every level so far.Tiny tipp ... if you can't figure it out - just give it a sleep over - next day promis you solve the puzzle!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out fairly simple, but the amount of complexity in the later puzzles is really amazing. The game does a fantastic job of introducing new rules, and then flipping those rules on their heads when you start to feel too comfortable.  is the sort of game you can't stop thinking about when you're not playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This perfectly-curated museum of puzzles stands out for its minimal frustration and maximal intuition-based solutions, flow, and delight. I laughed at some of the solutions once I completed them just because of how fun they were to watch. It felt like a conversation, like I was exploring rules of recursion along with Patrick, and seeing what magic possibilities happen.I just completed every puzzle in the main game (before the dark gray box), having only needed to look up hints for two of the puzzles (and the solutions were far easier than I thought they were.) I'm looking forward to seeing how challenging these extra ones are!EDIT: Where some puzzle games just toss the convoluted or leftover ideas in the challenge section, Parabox's bonus puzzles are just as carefully designed and chosen as the main puzzles, and it took me some pondering but I was able to figure out all of them without having to look up any hints. Excellent game from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely some top tier sh*t in the puzzle game genre, seriously. The games runs so smoothly and the puzzles are just so fun. It gets harder and harder and sometimes a bit too hard for my stupid brain but it never gets frustrating. Also the music is very well made too, it's soothing and calm and somehow sounds really fitting to the world in this game. To think that the game is made by one guy?!?!?!?!?!?!?! It's  the best possible way.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: When I discovered this game I noticed the 99% positive reviews and I thought to myself how weirdly high that number was for a game with such a simple appearance.Funnily enough, I now think that the percentage of positive reviews this game has... is actually too low.I'm giving this a solid 10/10 even though I'm not even past half of the game yet. From a puzzle game perspective, Patrick's Parabox is simply perfect.Highly recommended to every single puzzle-loving gamer out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: is an extremely well-designed puzzler with a great learning curve, and puzzles that intrigue and delight instead of stumping and frustrating. It has super audio design and cute aesthetics. But most importantly...Problem with puzzle games deriving from  is that way too often turn up the difficult at latter puzzles by just making the space intricate. For example,  eventually turns from a delightful game about manipulating rules (where the main difficulty is figuring out the sequence of rule changes) into a boring game of complicated box pushing (where the main difficulty is distinguishing zigzagzagzagzigzagzigzagzagzagzagzig from zigzigzagzagzigzagzigzigzagzagzagzig). . It always gives you enough room to focus on the high-level stuff, has an Undo and Redo buttons, and its levels have a grokkable size.If your spatial imagination is bad enough that  is intuitive to walk through but you keep getting lost in , this game is for you.(Also, I bought the game  finishing the demo. Demos work!)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Game #7 of me playing the games on Steam with the highest user reviewsI feel like every puzzle in this game blew my mind. Every set of levels introduces a new mechanic which is completely refreshing and satisfying to figure out. If you like puzzle games you'll love this. To be honest, at a certain point I lost patience for the challenge levels, but the core levels never had me stuck for too long and kept me interested until the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles tend to feel like they solve themselves by nature of having very few options; experimenting with the mechanics/geometry you know you're probably supposed to use will usually get you most of the way there. I would say this game is more focused on guiding you through all of its mechanics and showing off all the possibilities of the system rather than providing a maximally satisfying solving experience. It's somewhat easy overall, but definitely some of the optional puzzles are tricky enough and I haven't attempted that many of the puzzles in the "challenge" section yet. Overall a good game, a league below the best of sokoban that I've played but definitely good
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the main game. There's appendices and challenges at the end that I haven't gotten to yet, but I think I can say my piece.This game is MARVELOUS! Cute and charming while being mindboggling and difficult at times. Ironically, I personally found the later levels easier than the mid-tier levels. How that happened I don't know, but I had fun the whole time.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a pure puzzle game. The controls are simple, the graphics minimal, and the concepts bend your brain in a way it has never been done before. There is no story or platforming or mechanics to really speak of, only puzzles.The difficulty progression is near perfect. Nothing ever seems too easy or too difficult (until perhaps you reach the post-endgame challenges), but almost everything requires you to think through the puzzle and work through it logically. The additions of complicating ideas such as recursion and infinities all feel natural and logical conclusions of the world this game lives in. Nonetheless, this game has bent my brain in more ways than one and I was left speechless a number of times upon figuring out the solution to a given puzzle.Playing Patrick's Parabox, I am continually reminded of Baba Is You. Both games feel very similar, have similar logical puzzles with no story to speak of, with similar levels of polish and difficulty. If you've played and enjoyed Baba is You, you will certainly enjoy Patrick's Parabox, and vice versa. If you've not played either game, and enjoy puzzles, I would certainly recommend playing both.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! 10/10Felt hard at times, but not too hard in my opinion (definitely easier than Baba Is You).A lot of satisfying "Aha!" moments, and most levels require a very unique solution.In terms of progression, the game builds its difficulty almost perfectly, and manages to introduce new concepts gradually in a way that makes sense to the player.I was very much hoping for very specific end-game content -  meta levels! Similar to the end-game content in Baba Is You.. In a way the entire game is a block within a block within a block, but the idea of meta levels isn't explored in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a few stages in, but I am greatly entertained so far. I got really stumped a couple of times, and probably will get stuck many more times, but it is a well-polished gem that does the thing it intends to do very well.It slowly familiarizes you with game mechanics. It is suitable for even people who feel puzzle-dumb because of it. And I saw in the menu that it also supports custom levels while being very clear in how it conveys information, aiding those who have practical limitations they prevent them from playing many other games.It's a bit expensive, but I have no regrets: this is one where every second of your experience with it feels like care was taken to make it perfect. Where other games often have rough corners left and right because they had to meet deadlines or simply because they had a huge scope, this is like those physical Japanese puzzles in that you can tell it was crafted by people with passion and eye for detail.And that level of quality alone makes it worth the money IMHO.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game. Puzzles derive their difficulty from having an advanced understanding of the game mechanics rather than being convoluted. The puzzles are hand-crafted, not repetitive, and very challenging. There's enough content to keep you going for a long time. Even after beating the game the challenge puzzles are still mind-blowing.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Good puzzle game which is great for picking up and solving a few in short sessions. There's no story or comedy or anything additional like that, which I think this game could have used. The puzzles are challenging, and there's a decent variety of mechanics, but it doesn't have any grabs to help keep you invested.Played on Deck, had to restart the game every time to get it to recognize the controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great puzzle game based on a novel concept. There are also many unexpected variations on the concept of pushing things into yourself. I finished the main game, but keep coming back to solve the rest of the puzzles because I want to see what other weird things can be done. i think I won my copy in a raffle, but would have purchased it anyhow since it looked so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Pure artistic genius at work here ladies and gents. I've only dabbled in puzzle games *very occasionally*, and by that I mean free mobile games and the Portal series. However, I came across Patrick's Parabox through a GMTK video and was quickly intrigued by the recurvise nature of some of the puzzles.Well geez! Patrick's Parabox is easily one of the most creative games I've ever played, and I'd strongly recommend it to anyone who finds the trailer even remotely intriguing. The most impressive part so far is how the mechanics are gradually introduced so that in a very short amount of time you'll soon be having "wtf, this is insane" moments of clarity. Awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: its fantastic and made of superlimital like inspiration！At first that you may learn from the tutorial that this is just something like pushing box upgraded.But when you go into the blue cube, it is just the beginning of this game.Just try it. imagination pushes not only boxes themselves, but different perspective to watch and understand true paradox.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: What I love about these puzzles is that unlike other puzzle games, difficulty is not increased simply by adding a greater quantity of elements to each puzzle. There is always somewhere between two and six elements to play with and the trick is in learning how to apply the mechanisms in each puzzle. This in my mind is the hallmark of a truly excellent puzzle game.I never thought I'd be playing a variation of Sokoban where I have to move blocks through myself in order to solve a puzzle.Better than Baba Is You IMHO
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to purchase this game due to the price being higher than a lot of other 2D puzzle games but I'm glad I did. I'm a fan of the genre and the first 2D push-the-blocks puzzle game I played was over 30 years ago, yet this one brings something new with it. The puzzles are a nice difficulty, some of which are playable by my 5yo son, others leave me scratching my head for a while. There is an element of repetition to the puzzles but for me it's a good thing which aids learning the mechanics of the game play.  The graphics are okay, the animations are a nice touch which draws you into the game. My only minor criticism, is that the puzzles sometimes feel like they could do with being within a more expansive arena, when compared with other 2D puzzlers, they can be a little confined (in spite of the recursion enlarging the space in which you navigate your character around). Overall though, I'm really enjoying the game, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A  quick puzzle game if you know what you're doing - ~100 minutes is all it took me to finish it. Yet there's no way I'm going to refund this, it was thoroughly worth every penny!The basic premise: It's Sokoban, except you can enter the boxes you push. Boxes can also contain themselves. Shenanigans ensue.There's a few gimmicks, like turning the player into other blocks (fun), pushing blocks into the player (great), turning into walls (a gimmick that I hope to never see again in my life), and shunting around subworlds in weird and wacky ways. I played the demo of this a year or so ago, and was disappointed that something I stumbled upon early seemed to just be coded out for convenience... I was really glad that it got expanded upon literally tenfold!There's a few iffy worlds: Center is just fiddly, Clone feels like a gimmick that was just invented to make some worlds possible. Cycle is also mediocre and feels like a totally different game. But that's 3 "misses" out of 15 worlds, the rest of which are great.Overall, this is a fun concept that thoroughly explores the design space of "what if reality was Sokoban, crossed that one scene from Futurama where they end up with a box that contains their own universe". Definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: creating a good puzzle is really hard, but this game consistently makes great puzzle after great puzzle, it teaches you a small handful of deceptively simple mechanics then shows you all the weird ways they interact.i'd say it does a pretty good job of slowly introducing new mechanics in an easy to understand way.has alot of content so it's worth the price.also if you're worried about getting stuck, each "area" has branching paths of levels and to complete the area you only need to complete some of the puzzles, allowing you to come back to the harder ones later.i highly suggest this game to anybody who likes puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little puzzle game. You start out just the bare basics of pushing blocks around, and with every world a new mechanic is introduced and focused on, with a few simple levels to demonstrate the new gimmick and let you get a feel for how it works. If you're more of a casual puzzler then just stick to the middle path and go to the next world once you've beaten the required amount of levels. But if you feel like challenging yourself then there are red and blue levels which usually force more thought and difficulty. There is no story to miss, so you can take the game at your leisure. 100% each world before moving on, or only do the bare minimum to get to the next world and see what else the game has to offer. Once you beat the final world you unlock some bonus areas, which involve some puzzles with unique mechanics which solely work in those mini-worlds, as well as more difficult challenge puzzles. I 100% the game, and some puzzles can really throw you for a loop learning how to make the solution work. While sometimes I'd get stuck, come back to it later on, and see that the solution was much simpler than I thought and I just needed to work backwards from how I thought the final solution should be.This was a real fun experience that I'd heavily recommend for either a casual or an experienced puzzler.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Saw a review saying if you love puzzle games to not hesitate and buy it now. That comment is right. IF YOU LOVE PUZZLE GAMES DO NOT HESITATE AND BUY PATRICK'S PARABOX. I love puzzle games and this is one of the best, most well made puzzle game I've ever played. The learning curve and balance between challenging and fun is perfectly balanced, as all puzzle games should be. Only about 3 hours in, but excited to continue playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterclass in puzzle design with excellent pacing and progression. This game teaches its mechanics brilliantly in a way that feels natural and rewarding rather than contrived. While there are some devilishly difficult puzzles here, it's not because of any deliberate or artificial obfuscation, instead it's a testament to the superb craftsmanship of the puzzles themselves. It's arguably one of the most innovative and thoughtful Sokoban games ever made, second only to Baba Is You.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth the price.One of the best games I played that came out this year, and in general. There is something extremely satisfying about this game, and it has kept me hooked. As far as what I like about it: The ideas and design of the game is very clear and complex. There is enough easy puzzles to explain harder puzzles, there is a great variety of different puzzle types - and there is hardly a need to look at guides, which also probably would ruin the game. The visual style although it is very simple, reinforces the clarity of the game in a really interesting way too. The music is fire and really makes this game a nice way to pass by time when taking a break from work or daily tasks. My only gripe so far is the over-world map, while its interesting to have the maps recursively emerge within other maps, it would be nice to be able to see how all the worlds connect in sequence to some extent. Also there's a weird undo bug if you hit the windows key by accident while undoing your moves.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the 'Core' game in about 3 hours and reached the end. I plan to go back and try to beat all the levels though. The game is Reminiscent of Baba is You, though a bit more approachable throughout. each world is 'atomic' in the sense that it introduces a new mechanic, and the whole world is about that mechanic. Theres little to no overlap in mechanics across "Core Levels" in each world, though the extra levels may have older mechanics show up. Its incredibly approachable, and just feels great to play.There is also a bit of End Game content to unlock by reaching the end, which is always great to see (including some prototype art and 'behind the scenes' stuff I love seeing as a programmer)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it more at the beginning but now and then there are still levels with a surprising twist.I kind of dropped off the game eventually - the puzzles are solid but I have a feeling that for some I just stumble into a solution, even at the later stages. It still is one of the best Sokoban style puzzles out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is one of the better sokoban-like puzzlers there is. The visual clarity is great, although some puzzles require exploring them a bit to really get an idea of what is going on. Most of the puzzles aren't that hard, but near the end of the game there are some pretty difficult puzzles for which you really have to think. If you haven't played sokoban-like games before or want a relaxing time then this is a great buy, but if you are looking for a really difficult puzzle game there are better ones out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: What if you took Baba is You, and instead of rewriting the rules, you used a higher plane of existence? This game uses levels as the blocks, yourself as the block, yourself as an immovable wall, levels that you push outside of itself to clone itself, and so much more absolutely mind-bending interactions with 2d projected onto 2.5d space.Theres simply nothing like this game.
