_childDocuments_.review: Delightfully brain-bending expansion of block-pushing games into far too many dimensions (while remaining strictly 2D)."Only" ten hours or so to complete the main game (although I'm nowhere near finished with the "appendices"), but they were absolutely ten of the best hours I've ever spent at a computer.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is about boxes. Boxes within boxes within boxes within boxes. The goal is to place boxes on their designated positions (similar to the classic sokoban) to complete a level.The levels become more difficult as you progress and can appear impossible at times.  You can spend over an hour on a level without making any progress. Walk away and come back to it later, then you have that 'ah-ah' moment and complete it immediately. The levels can be figured out with logic instead of brute force which many puzzle games suffer from.Overall, Excellent puzzle game, Recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Boxes in boxes in boxes in boxes!It is good and fun, but a bit too simplistic for puzzle games in general until you reach level 80-100 or so (about 1/3 of the game in total). Not bad, but it was a bit boring until getting to the more involved puzzle/solutions.Overall, I think other games do this better, especially Recursed, but this is a great puzzle game if you like that style of recursion puzzle and/or sokoban. Maybe wait to get it on sale for $10 or so though if you're a big puzzle person since the first 1/3 of the game is pretty boring and mindless which hurts it a little bit.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I've only completed about 70 puzzles, but I just gotta give this a review.It's Baba Is You, but even more rewarding to my mind as the rules are incredibly simple and clear right from the start. It's only between you and your understanding of recursion, and infinity. I don't know how the designer did it, but every single puzzle feels a bit more rewarding than the last. I've played quite a lot of puzzle games, and the fine line between stuff that is too easy, or stupidly hard (as in, you would need information you didn't know existed, or it's kinda luck based, or so intricate you can't really make out the steps in your mind) is incredibly hard to walk. A puzzle that truly challenges you, but every time you complete it feels completely fair and fun, and that you deserved completing it through your own, sheer (lul) intelligence.Plus it truly takes a genius to code these puzzles and think in advance of everything that can happen with this mind-bending core principle. So, yeah, absolutely check this out if you're looking for clever design and a genuinely fun playing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the simple graphics fool you, or make you think that the game is not worth its price. I fell into this trap myself and didn't buy upon release; but thank goodness I bought it in the end.This game bends your brain in a way that only few puzzle games can do. Only game that I can think of that is as smart is Baba is You. And Baba is You is probably not as good as it tends to get very abstract. With Parabox, if you think hard enough, you'll get there in the end. Please buy and support the dev. £12 -£15 is not much to ask for 300+ handcrafted and geniously designed levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few puzzle games I've played lately that I really enjoyed.(legend: o; neutral, -; negative, +; positive)What it does do:+ relatively simple mechanics that are easy to pick up and hard to master+ allows for 100%ing without breaking an arm and a leg (as far as I've seen at least, I'm not quite there yet)+ epsilon and infinity are nice math jokes that are actually correctly applied, but I figure that's a plus just for me+ it has five or so hints that basically amount to "Don't Panic", which is nice despite not being written in large red friendly letters+ proper recursion, no time travel, y'know, it just behaves as I expect it to (as a programmer)+ hard puzzles+ funky retro levels that feel like a CLI version of the game which I find very attractive <3What it doesn't do:+ does not hold your hand every step of the wayo it actually doesn't hold your hand at all, it just kicks you into free fall and lets you figure out what to do (which works *most* of the time, but not always)- some mechanics remain entirely unexplained (mostly precedence for some actions) which is hard to get right- it's not very longo there is no story whatsoever+ it is not a Portal spin-off (yes, this deserves its own point in this genre)+ most puzzles that melt your brain are not the required main puzzles so you can skip themA few levels are really awkward to the point of feeling like IEEE 754 floating point rounding errors, but hey, it makes for a nice change of pace for a dozen levels.Overall I liked it and I think it's worth the ~20 bucks, albeit a bit expensive it is nice to see a game excel in this genre without going over board, being a portal spin-off, or being incomprehensible, YMMV.If in doubt wait for a 50% discount, 10 bucks would be absolutely worth the buy IMHO.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Such an innovative puzzle game, thoroughly enjoyed all levels. Some of the levels were looking head scratchingly difficult but most of the time solution was a witty little thing you missed. Also game consists of 19 hubs (IIRC), and each hub has between 6-10 puzzles and the puzzles are ordered in a way that first puzzle shows the new mechanic and it gets harder with each puzzle which was a nice touch. Absolutely recommended  for people who love puzzles and also its a good purchase for people that don't really play puzzle games
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game. The early sections are easy, as you'd expect, but it keeps introducing new concepts and new tricks which make each section a fresh challenge.I like to just dip into it for a couple of puzzles at a time, because it quickly wears my brain out! I think I'm near the end, and I have over 18 hours of solid puzzling behind me. I love how a puzzle can seem completely impossible, to the point that you'd swear blind it can't be done, but if you leave it and come back the next day, you might just "get" it.Strongly recommended, and excellent value for money, given that my 18 hours were solid puzzle-solving with no filler, and I only cheated once!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best puzzle games ever. It starts out very simple, but quickly breaks your brain. When you finally understand, then you go "aha", and it is satisfying. Every world has it's own unique challenge, gradually getting harder, but never getting too hard because you can always skip a few levels if you don't know the solution. All in all it's a great game. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most mind-bending things I've ever played—maybe  most ever. Though this game doesn't get extremely complex with its puzzle solutions, the puzzles themselves are so abstract and fun to learn and mess around with that it doesn't really need to. Plus, the collection of challenge levels at the end do provide some high difficulty. But what really makes this game shine so tremendously well is how it grounds theoretical physics into reality, represented clearly. I won't go into detail for spoilers, but the game gets much stranger and crazier, especially near the end, with mechanics that take some serious thinking to wrap your head around and which are mind-blowing to attempt to do so. Yet despite that, the game is able to ease players into these mechanics so smoothly with tutorial puzzles throughout the game that I think just about anyone can do it. Some of the areas' BGM is really nice as well.Overall, probably the second-best Sokoban puzzler I've ever played behind Baba Is You, and one of the best games I've played this year. Fantastic work.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox doesn't just think outside of the box when it comes to sokoban-style puzzles - it reinvents the box, and in many cases, it IS the box.  This puzzle game masters the balance of having puzzles that are euphorically mind-blowing without being overwhelming to the player.  In part, the beauty of this lies in the fact that the vast majority of the game's puzzles are pretty short - so while solving a level might be tough, you're always within arms reach of the solution.  This allows players to solve levels at a fast enough rate where they're frequently rewarded - and to compensate for this speed, the game is packed with hundreds of levels to keep you going.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game nearly full price, fearing that it would be too short.Well, it's not. Very good investment if you like puzzle games. Constant new ideas and concepts ; you'll say "woah!" more than one time. In my case, I like to play only a few levels each day, I don't think it's the kind of game you want to binge.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Sokoban++Patrick's Parabox is way, way, way more fun than it has any right to be. All of the different mechanics are introduced gently, but there's plenty of challenge to really get you thinking around every corner. The different levels introduce new functions/features or present puzzles built around a common quirk making the game feel anything but samey or boring.Puzzles inside of puzzles, recursive puzzles, puzzles on the surface of your face... yeah!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It is rarely that I encounter a puzzlegame, that just keeps blowing my mind. Too many puzzle games makes the later levels more difficult by simply adding more and more "objects" thereby being harder by sheer numbers. Patrick's Parabox does not do this - Yes you get some more objects in the later levels, but it's nearly always just a new way of using the same objects that you already know. Also not just learning you a new trick and then abandon it - no you will have to rely on what you have learned to keep pushing forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Mind bending, superb puzzle game. It's basically a sliding puzzle, but with recursion. Everyone's seen pictures of this concept (a picture with the same picture in it, and in that picture, the same picture again, etc.). Creating puzzles in such an impossible space is just a brilliant idea. With just a few elements this gives rise to really bizarre problems with surprising solutions. There is a really smooth learning curve in the puzzles. The puzzles are hard, but never too hard, building on the strategies learned from previous puzzles. Each puzzle solved feels very rewarding, and I had several moments where I made a discovery and just sat back from the screen, amazed at the possibilities of this logic. The minimal, colorful design is lovely and the user interface is very intuitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, with a simple beauty and elegant design. It falls short of perfection, however, because many of the more advanced puzzles are difficult to appreciate and hard to understand, EVEN AS YOU SOLVE THEM. There is a strange dissatisfaction that comes with that. Sometimes I would solve a puzzle by simply trying different permutations until it was solved -- it's the puzzle equivalent of button mashing. I think there are two root causes of this problem. First, the visual design for the various mechanics in the game are not quite memorable enough to keep straight as they are used in tandem. Secondly, infinite recursion is difficult to intuit, especially visually. Still, I don't want to harp on the negative, so let me reiterate that this is a great game, and I fully recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't quite beaten Baba is You as I've gotten stuck so many times. Patrick's Parabox was a nice palette cleanser because it walks you through the progression of mechanics much more gradually. It's probably as hard, but the game guides you in abstract though much better than Baba is You. I couldn't say which I prefer, but Patrick's Parabox definitely functions better as a 'fun game'.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful take on Sokoban-style puzzles, polished to within an inch of its life. Every level feels like it's there for a reason, and nothing feels wasted or overdone. Patrick's Parabox adds many new mechanics to Sokoban, but strangely they all seem to fit together extremely well. Each mechanic is introduced in a logical and straightforward manner, and its consequences are then explored. The result is a rich series of "aha" moments and clever insights. It's clear the author spent a great deal of time thinking carefully about how the player would engage with the game and its systems, rather than just slapping together a few dozen levels and calling it a day, as is so common with puzzle games these days.Less interesting tidbits:
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A stunningly elegant puzzle game, up there with the likes of Baba Is You. Its simple premise opens into a deep and vibrant puzzlescape. Each puzzle is well-designed - only a handful felt at all clunky or contrived - and the order in which they are presented to the player creates a cohesive experience of increasing difficulty, sometimes through complexity and sometimes through abstractness. All told, I got a very enjoyable 18 hours out of the game, and I am excited to see what Patrick Traynor might create next.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is an incredible puzzle game, with an incredible premise and concept. This game's 300+ levels are sorted into 18 worlds, with each of these worlds introducing a new mechanic. There are also optional challenge levels, which are harder, and optional side levels that change the basic game formula a bit.The difficuly curve is really good - hard enough to be interesting but not to the point of frustration. The game is easier than some other games of this genre (Baba Is You is considerbly more difficult), but I don't see that as a downside. The artstyle and music fit the game really well. The postgame content could be better, but it's pretty good anyway.I have 100%ed this game, and I just want more of it. There is custom level support, but it isn't all that accessible so I have never used it. I really hope for a sequel or an in-game level editor in a future update, because I just want more of this game.One warning though: this game is best enjoyed blind. It's best to discover the mechanics yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A well executed puzzle game with great complexity and expansion on concepts. It starts off simple and then gets to mind bending. For those of you who enjoy good spatial puzzles, I highly recommend it. You'll find yourself smirking at the clever solutions to the puzzles as you move through the infinite spaces.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes straight to the hall of fame of my favourite puzzle games!Twisted as hell, but never hardcore (as shown by the fact that I could solve all but three levels without any help).I liked how new mechanics gets introduced with every new level and I love how all the twists and corners of the main idea (boxes containing themselves) gets unraveled and deeply explored.My only (tiny) complaint is that some mechanics feel more "forced" than others... I personally didn't enjoy much the "multiple player" mechanics, it involved too many layers of new moves and too much forward thinking for my poor, non-chess-adapt brain! I cleared the three linked challenge levels by walkthrough and I still don't understand what I did... usually, when I give up and look for hints, I'm immediately like "Damn, that was obvious"... not this time, though, I feel instead I would have never got over those levels!Nonetheless, the overall game is a masterpiece and if you love puzzle games you MUST have it!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Many have compared it to Baba is You and rightfully so, but this game in my opinion is more approachable and simpler in concept than the former. It's fun, the music is tranquil, it's challenging but not overwhelming and it can easily be set down when you need a break or don't have lots of time to devote. Highly recommend picking it up, even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Another great entry in the genre of "box-pushing game with more to offer than you'd think." If you enjoy the kind of game that Baba Is You is, with all of its puzzling yet fun-to-overcome mechanics, this game feels like you're playing it all over again. Just when I thought I had seen every possible way the game could explore its main gimmick of recursion, there was yet another set of levels that twisted the rules even further. This is definitely the type of game where the less you know going into it, the more fun your experience will be.The music is fairly simplistic and there is no story, but this type of puzzle game does not need a narrative to be enjoyable. You're here for the head-scratchers, and that's what you get. It's an easy game to pick up, but finishing every last puzzle requires more than just thinking outside the box -- you must come to a complete understanding of the layers of "infinity."The concept is refreshingly original, and I would love to see this game expanded upon with more puzzles or a level editor (I know that one exists, but I mean one with something like workshop support for easier sharing.) Very fun if you like to feel smart, then helplessly stuck, then smart again.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite puzzle game of all time, and the only puzzle game I've ever played which I would recommend to those who are not normally fans of the genre. It's really refreshing to see a puzzle game with a more average difficulty that I could realistically see most people who pick it up completing it in a world where it feels like every other puzzle game tries to be as brutally hard as possible. The game also has a unique approach to puzzle design that I really like where most of the difficulty comes from understanding and experimenting with the game's concepts rather than the difficulty of the actual puzzles. I rarely say this, but I'd recommend this game to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice little game. Very genius. Must try for any puzzler. Seems to get pretty complex. I would say It's easier than Baba Is You, but who likes Baba will prolly find joy here aswell. Baba seems a bit tough for me personally, but i think I might pick it up again after I complete this masterpiece :) Big thanks to the developer. Good Work. Need more games like this :)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. Superb level design. The game feels very polished overall and gives me an amount of "ohhhh" moments I never had before in a puzzle game. Very surprising in the best possible ways, try to play the game with looking at as little content as possible beforehand.Didn't know that I could get so addicted to what seems like a simple puzzle game on the surface. Very much remommended
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a real gem of a puzzle game. I love the concept of recursion and it's usage here is very well done. The game length is very good at 17 hours (for me) to finish 100% of the game's content. I think the game has a slow enough difficulty curve that most people will be able to progress throughout the game as they learn all its mechanics. It maintains a good level of challenge though, especially with the optional challenge levels. I highly recommend checking out the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I believe Patrick's Parabox is the greatest Sokoban-based game of all time.  The game starts out with a very gradual learning curve that is accessible to people who haven't played similar puzzles.  Once the game introduces self-similar fractals, the developers continually bring in new twists to the puzzles without making the rules any more complicated.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well designed puzzles wrapped in a clean and relaxing atmosphere. Forgiving undos and a flexible world layout minimizes frustration. The concepts are simple yet deep, creative yet intuitive, reasonable yet satisfying.Compared to some of my other favorite puzzle games of all time: lighter and more accessible than Baba is You (with a ton of similarities to Baba otherwise), less fluff that The Witness, more non-gamer-friendly than Portal 2, faster paced than Antichamber; Patrick's Parabox deserves to be on the list of greatest puzzle games of this generation. Would recommend this game without a doubt.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game... where to begin?  I'm a longtime puzzle game fan, I love puzzle games, and I try to play all the best ones.  Patrick's Parabox is definitely at the top of the heap; it's one of the finest puzzle games ever made.  The only games I can think of that are in the same league are Stephen's Sausage Roll (which this game's name is an obvious homage to) and Baba Is You.  And though I love those games, I love this one more.  It's curious, because visually, this game isn't much to look at.  It's basically just colored squares over and over.  But the gameplay is so weird, so mind-bending, and so  from anything I've ever played before that I'm totally hooked.  Patrick gets a tremendous amount of mileage out of the recursive boxes-within-boxes theme, and he finds an endless number of variations on this theme. I find I can't play this for more than a few minutes at a time before my mind starts going numb (but in a good way, honestly!).  I like that the levels have a path that has to be completed to get to the next level, but there are also a few optional challenge puzzles on each level.  This avoids the syndrome where you get stuck on the one impossible puzzle which makes you rage quit the game.  Also, the puzzles themselves aren't difficult in a typical finding-the-needle-in-the-haystack way that many puzzle games are; instead, you just need to learn to think about the puzzle in the right way, and then it's (usually) easy.  Maybe this means that this game is easier than Stephen's Sausage Roll, but it's still plenty hard and, more importantly, plenty of fun.  This developer has real talent, and I'll be watching his future work closely.  If you like puzzle games even a little, you should buy this immediately!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of, if not The best difficulty curve I've ever experienced in a puzzle game. The concept is so satisfying, and the extensions and variations it is taken to are both intuitive and mind boggling. Most of the solutions were either somewhat "obvious", or very clever, a few were difficult as an "oh" kind of moment, but none had extra mess that made finding the solution to feel dissatisfying. You have scratched one of those corners of my brain so thoroughly, I may yet look into attempting to create custom levels and expanding the Paradox cases. I can only imagine the adventure that coding this game must have been.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is seriously amazing... Every Sheldon will love this genius game. I've had many genuine laughs getting locked inside cubes in the middle of the night. Mazes are full of simple but clever tricks that seem made especially to slap your ego in the face, but in a very gentle way. It is very cerebral and calming. The music is excellent too and suits extremely well the overall game design. It reminds me of old Autechre tracks during their ambiant period. This game is very well thought while being ultra minimalist. I could never program such a game, I would end up in a mental institution. Very well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun concept, really interesting, if a little lacking in execution. If you're looking for moderately difficult puzzles, this game is for you. I would have liked to have seen more harder puzzles, and perhaps the mechanics could have been explored in a little more detail, but there's lots of community-made levels to look at. I would say that if you play only the levels in the game itself, and ignore community levels, you are not really getting all this game has to offer - if there wasn't a good community, I would not be recommending this.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox has a brilliant set of mechanics that are completely brain-melting in the best possible way. The game does a fantastic job of gradually and gently introducing the mechanics to the player in a way that isn't overwhelming. It definitely contains some really challenging puzzles but by the time you get there the game has prepared you for the challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game, only very few puzzle are still resisting me (less than 5 after the end of the game). The difficulty is easy, but the advantage is that get to learn the various mechanics very progressively, and have the time to practice them, which will be needed for the challenges after the last level.These challenges are very nice, they're the real deal, even if they're still not the most difficult for the majority of them, and too few of them. Still I recommend the game, cause there is a way for the community to make its own puzzles, which is great and potentially adds an infinite new content
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly short Sokoban-like block pushing puzzle game that uses mechanics of blocks within blocks in a refreshing and enjoyable way. Each idea is introduced, explored and expanded upon in sections, and forces you to push blocks into positions where in a typical block pushing puzzle game it'd render the puzzle unsolvable.There are minimal explicit tutorials, as the game prefers to let the player encounter hurdles and mechanics of escalating difficulty in a controlled environment, forcing them to learn the mechanics to progress.Excellent puzzles and mechanics that are thought out and executed to their fullest extent.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: After looking up the solution for 92% of the challenge puzzles, I'm glad to call my run complete. Puzzles range from head scratchers to muscle busters to real humdingers to those that are just a real treat to behold. I was a bit sorry for myself when solutions didn't start coming anymore and I just looked things up instead of bruteforcing. Beyond that everything is rather amazing, it feels so cool to manipulate the infinities and the epsilons and their voids. Ant Man prolly has to do this kinda work every time he moves.Very well the ultimate block pushing game? Why don't you buy to find out!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: this is definitely my favourite puzzle game. it's extremely accessible in its puzzles and takes the time to emphasise every single game mechanic from the absolute simplest to the most complex, to the point that no other game I've seen has managed to do welllike, the initial premise is already weird (what if I could have levels inside levels, with nested recursion), but it somehow manages to get even weirder to the point that I was somehow even more surprised as the game progressed until the very end as new mechanics were introduced and exploredthat said, the puzzles are hard, and most of the optional puzzles really push the boundaries of what you can do. even when I hadn't finished them all, I never felt like I didn't have the tools to solve them, but I definitely took a while to figure out how.the game is definitely on par with the magnificence of games like Stephen's Sausage Roll and Baba Is You but way more accessible IMHO. if you liked but had trouble with those types of games, you may like Patrick's Parabox even better.extremely small nitpick is the puzzles which move the camera around, which does affect the accessibility. there is a way to change the camera (press 7 to cycle between display modes, including the text mode), but I feel like this could have been advertised a little better.overall: I absolutely love it. play this game and enjoy.----SPOILERY ADDENDUM BELOW:wish you could have used omega instead of the generic infinity sign since it'd complement the epsilon better; in the extended real numbers, epsilon is between 0 and all real numbers, and omega is after all of them, with 1/epsilon = omega. that said… I 100% understand why you didn't, since most people will understand seeing a big infinity symbol better, and you're basically expected to see infinite exit before infinite enter. this is basically me being a nitpicky mathematician and not actually complaining.but I also know most people aren't as mathematically inclined and it would have been weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The appendix concepts are interesting, could use a lot more puzzles with altered rules. A bit too easy, I could have used a bit more difficulty. Maybe more appendix stuff could have provided it. I remember rating "Filament" as "a nice mellow not too hard not too easy difficulty". So I would rate this as very slightly too easy. Still recommend. If one new to puzzlers makes a point to make a backlog of the "greats" to play, as many of us puzzle lovers have, I would recommend this be one of the first you play. Because this game is good, great even but I find that it is outshown by many many other puzzle games. Build up to titans later, play this early.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little puzzle game. Challenging enough to be immensely satisfying when you crack a hard level, but rarely overly frustrating. I like the way it has a core set of puzzle mechanics that are thoroughly explored throughout the game, instead of just piling on more and more disjoint mechanics as you progress.If you ever find yourself completely stuck on a level, I suggest skipping the level or putting the game down for a bit, and coming back to it later. There have been plenty of times when I've been banging my head on a level for ages, only to complete it nearly immediately when I pick it up the next day.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The greatest puzzler I've played in a while. Beautiful, intuitive, mind-boggling. Most levels feel like a fever dream -- I wake up on the other end having solved it, and I can replicate the solution, but I can't put it into words. Sometimes awe-inspiring, sometimes unsettling, always incredibly clever.Long live recursion!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Splendid sokoban variant!Our brains are pretty good at solving puzzles that involve figuring out where there's room to slide things, because of our inherent knowledge of how physical space works. What's awesome about a puzzle like this is that we get to find out that our brains are also pretty good at adapting our inherent knowledge of physical spaces to impossible and/or paradoxical spaces!This game loads ridiculously quickly.  I can click the button and be playing in five seconds, which for my weak computer is miraculous.Oh, and the music is lovely, perfectly fits the atmosphere of peaceful mindbending.Update: Just got to the end of the game (though I'm still working on some of the optional puzzles) and my opinion stands! One of the best puzzle games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: + Great puzzle concept+ Loads of levels (current number of levels solved: 286/364)+ Smooth controls+ Nice graphics and soundtrack+ Level editor included- Due to the simplistic level design, I found many puzzles easier to solve by trial and error rather than actual deduction based on the mechanics of the game
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, easier to grasp than you'd expect from the screenshots and videos. ...For the most part, anyway. Some of the bonus puzzles can get pretty tricky to wrap your head around. However, you only have to finish a handful of puzzles at a time in order to unlock the next set. So if you're not a 100% completionist and just want to reach the end, you could probably do it and still have a fulfilling, abstract puzzle experience. Easy recommendation for fans of something like Baba is You.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Overwhelmingly positive for a reason - this puzzle game hits all the right notes, has an excellent difficulty curve, gives you plenty of options to progress and come back later with an enhanced understanding of how all these puzzles slot together. The game doesnt tell you much, just throws you into the first puzzle and gets you to start pushing boxes around. Three hours in I've completed over 100 puzzles and have reached the "Open" chapter, and feels like the difficulty curve is just starting to ramp up.If you are a fan of puzzle games at all (Baba is You, The Witness, Wildfire Swap, Stephens Sausage Roll, etc) then you must try this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute treat, through and through. Easily the best puzzle game I've ever played, in my opinion. Every gimmick ties together incredibly well, and the game introduces them in such a way that you never feel overwhelmed or like you're given an unfair challenge. Admittedly the price tag is a bit to swallow, but honestly it is worth every. single. penny. Absolutely phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game if you are into mindmelting puzzle games. The main "story" is not too hard to get through, but completion is a little bit trickier. Still I didn't get stuck for too long on any puzzles, because they are generally small enough to figure out by trial and error if you are not getting the idea of what the puzzle wants you to do. On the other hand this can lead to some puzzles feeling less satisfying to me, because the game really does lead you in the right direction oftentimes and doesn't let you try out too many different thigs. It definitely feels more guided than some other recent puzzlegames, so keep that in mind when deciding to buy. I can still completely recommend this game, it was just good fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game implements recursion in a meaningful, consistent, comprehensible way. But recursion isn't the only draw here; it's implemented as part of a more general system of levels and sublevels. And in that system lies the beauty of Patrick's Parabox.The pacing in this game is really, really good so far. I always have time to get used to and internalize a concept before a new mechanic is dropped on me to melt my brain all over again. Each new world brings a concept that fundamentally changes how a sokoban style game works, and in an entirely different way than the concept before it.If you liked Baba Is You, you'll probably like Patrick's Parabox. The base interactions at play are simpler, yet the consequences are somehow even more insane. It doesn't take Turing completeness to produce beautiful insanity.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say I'm very confused but the game does such a great job teaching you its mechanics that you don't even notice that you've gotten used to creating multiple paradoxes and doing other crazy ♥♥♥♥. a 10/10 game that is very approachable while still having some mind bending challange levels that are very fun and satisfying to solve
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I've played since the Witness or Stephen's Sausage Roll. A unique mechanic with basically zero repetition and plenty "a-ha" moments. At no time did I feel pandered to, and when I felt stumped it usually meant I needed to come back the next day with fresh eyes. Just a great balanced game and well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game with a brilliant core mechanic that explores every twist, trick, and contradiction you can think of. Your mind grows to adapt to a concept that is impossible in our world, yet somehow has incredible self-consistency within the gameworld. I loved it so much, constantly laughing at the utter ridiculousness of the paraboxes and mindboggled from the simplest rooms with subtle, clever solutions. Absolutely sensational puzzle game, in leagues with Baba is You.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried not to spoil myself too much about this game until now. I finally got it and WOW it's much better than what i thought it would be. Totally one of the best puzzle games out there, it feels to me like an easier type of Baba is you game But then again I might not have gotten to the hard parts yet :eyes:
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect balance of simple mechanics compounded to make puzzles that are simple in nature, but difficult to solve.The difficulty curve is just perfect, with nothing left unexplained, even all the way up to the challenge levels.There's three of four levels that overextend their welcome by forcing you to repeat a series of moves several times, and any level featuring "friends" are an annoyance simply because its very hard to tell which order they'll move (either an icon showing their number or a "legend" would help a lot)Great game for going for 100% completion, it doesn't become extremely difficult nor has too many puzzles to do so.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent puzzle game, overall a bit on the easier side I would say. Kinda feels like getting a "few" math problems to solve as homework and then it's like 1. a) b) c) d) f) g) h) 2. a) b) c) d) f) g)... Solutions feel a bit samey sometimes you know. But that's also a part of the game teaching you concepts well, I just think it was a bit over-excessive at times. Also some levels feel more like neat ideas that the developer wanted to share, more than actual puzzles. Overall, I enjoyed it, but it's not as tight nor difficult as baba or sausage roll (imo).
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I'm updating my review to say this:This is the best puzzle game i have played. Period.Previous review:hurts my brain, 10/10If you like logic puzzles in any capacity, you'll probably love this game. It's really challenging, but easy to get into, and as it progresses you'll scream at the screen at how great the puzzles are - and how impossible they seem at first. It's the pinnacle of puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant. Best puzzle game I've ever played. Great for people who love games who challenge your reasoning and also for people who like Logic, Maths and solving problems/puzzles.The relationship, intentional or non-intentional, between this game and Set Theory, Logic and things like Russell's Paradox is just beautiful. Experiencing recursion first hand and creating paradoxes is priceless.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a wonderful puzzle game. While I haven't played almost any hardcore puzzle games (my experience only goes as far as the Professor Layton series and various Nancy Drew games with some experience in the Witness), this felt like a really great opening to that world. The concepts in it are slowly introduced, allowing the player to really get the feel before the harder puzzles come along. Overall, I never felt that a puzzle was unfair or required large leaps of logic. Even when I would get stumped on a puzzle, I would just leave and come back later to see a solution I had not previously considered. The music and minimalist graphics were charming and added to the experience. It combines a lot of fun gimmicks that, excluding the gimmicks from blue challenge levels, are useful throughout the main game and never truly go awayMy personal recommendation is to give this game a go. It's a fun experience and definitely makes you think outside the parabox. While it may feel easy for veteran puzzle gamers, I think it's an amazing introduction for people wanting to get into this genre. Even then, I think many veteran puzzle gamers will still enjoy the concepts and ideas found in this game, so I recommend giving it a try no matter your skill level.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of those "gets meta and weird" puzzles complete with the "now that I solved it I don't know if I feel like a genius or dumb" feeling that good ones always have; think Baba Is You or Recursed in that sense. It's also far and away the most accessible of the three. It does at times feel like things get overcomplicated in the sense of there being too many variations on the mechanics of the game instead of playing with the basic ones to something close to their logical conclusions, but maybe that won't feel like the case after I've done more (there's a bit more than a third of the puzzles to go). The game does a pretty good job in making basic puzzles that explain each new mechanic without actually telling you what the new things do and if you enjoy doing those experiments you will like that part; some will take a little time. If you like puzzles at all and you probably do if you're reading through the reviews there's a demo so there's absolutely no reason to not just download it and give it a shot yourself, so you should probably just do that.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: There were so many times I began spontaneously laughing at the pleasantly absurd situation I found myself in on screen due to the self-referential/feedback loops mechanics.The creators did a fantastic job of laying down simple foundations & easing users into new mechanics. The scope of puzzles in this game is vast. Before I knew it I was doing things I didn't understand but could work with. Sometimes this included solving a puzzle without knowing how – which is great for replayability. Great job!Def rec this game if you like puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Parallel universes, alternate universes, reversed universes, universes within universes within universes. Now you're thinking with universes.Great game. Also seems like it developed by one guy, Patrick Traynor, with music by Priscilla Snow. There are a LOT of levels too. Well worth the money. Thanks for a cool game, Patrick.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: 350 levels, Inventive and clever mechanics. With a very incrementally sloped difficulty curve. Each level is just new enough of a challenge without ever leaving you in the dark. Although if you're an experienced puzzler this will not be terribly difficult it will entertain you with its inventiveness. If you're new to Sokoban puzzles it might overwhelm you at times. However it seems that if you replay a few recent levels to cement the core concepts you will be able to advance again readily. This game was perfectly paced for my skill level but I just wanted to include experiences of other players that I've seen. If this game tickles your fancy in any way, I'd wholeheartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant puzzle game, and one I think should be called a classic. The puzzles are simple, slowly introducing mechanics that interface well with previous ones. I've loved working through every puzzle, and each new mechanic feel so natural and well thought-out for a puzzle game. Based off of my experience, this game is well worth the $30 price - I would still recommend buying even if it was more expensive.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best puzzle games I have played in a while, and I've played a lot.  It's challenging, and aside from the first one or two "teaching" puzzles in each new section, nothing feels too easy or too out of reach with some actual thought.  And the "disconnected" puzzles are quite unique.  Runs beautifully on my M1 Max MBP.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Started this game because it looked like it had a similar vibe to Baba Is You, and it does to an extent. Like Baba Is You, trying to verbalize the solutions in your own words to someone watching is a really funny challenge. It was definitely engaging enough for me to 100% the game. The 350+ levels are in a somewhat linear setup (you can skip a lot of levels if you want) but you won't find any meta/overworld puzzles. The final ~20% of the game takes the mechanics to some hilariously complicated places though.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful and well made puzzle game, pretty smooth progression, and the core conceit (worlds within worlds) plays very well with default block-pushing-puzzle/sokoban logic and expands the play area. Highly recommended for puzzle fans! The demo also gives a good taste if this is your kind of puzzle :)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brilliant!Maybe too brilliant at times. I feel as if it would have benefitted from being maybe four games, of simelar size. I think I will replay it, since sometimes it felt as if I didn't get the rules, and just stumbled around until I solved a room. And then it was time for the next area, with new rules. When I did get it, it was always fun and satisfying, though.I think for me it would have been better with maybe four areas before new rules and mechanics was introduced. Then I would have built up a deeper unerstanding of a lot of the quirks, and it would have been more satisfying. I marvel at the scope, and ambition. There is so much to enjoy in the game. I would definitly recommend it. I just didn't enjoy it as much as I thought, and as the puzzles deserve. Maybe a future replay will rectify this :-)

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a Sokoban block puzzle clone. Push the blocks into the right spaces and then get to the exit. The mandatory twist is that blocks can contain mini-levels inside of themselves. So you can push a block inside another one, then shrink down inside the mini-level to retrieve the block later. This opens up a whole lot of possibilities for getting blocks off walls and navigated around corners.That's the mandatory twist. The real twist is that blocks often contain recursive copies of the level. This gets nutty.You can push a block off the edge of the level, and then it reappears inside of the level next to the recursive copy. You can push the copy to a hard-to-reach location, then walk off the edge of the level later to teleport next to the block - or enter the block to get back the to the edge. Some levels have recursive copies inside of recursive copies, requiring you to turn them inside-out to have the right number of blocks in the right copy or move them around each other to keep blocks from getting stuck on walls.One thing you'll inevitably stumble upon by accident is that you'll push a level up next to its own edge and then step outside. This drops you into a void you can never return from, a mathematical dead-end marked by an infinity symbol. And then you think about it. Each time you step out of the level, you go up one stage of recursion. So if the level is up against its own edge, then when you exit the level, you're outside the edge of the next stage already. So you go up another stage, but you're still outside the edge, so that means... Oh dear.It's a very cute little joke, handled cheekily and easy to undo.It's also foreshadowing - and far from the most mind-bending idea the game requires you to wrap your head around...The puzzles hit this fantastic sweet spot where every single level gets you to wrap your head around another way of looking at the same mechanics, but there aren't so many mechanics that you get overwhelmed with options. And the puzzles are generally only a few steps long with a lot of generous space to navigate the mazes - there's no tedium about figuring out the exact right way to navigate a claustrophobic mess.And the final levels in the game are impressive for just how hard they run circles around dizzying existential ideas of infinity, treating the incomprehensible endless with the same casual indifference that Mario treats coins. Honestly, they're not hard puzzles. The last puzzle in the game in particular is also probably the easiest. But that's fine. The point isn't to challenge you. The point is that over a couple hundred puzzles, the game has taught you how to conquer the very boundaries of existence, and you deserve to have some fun with that knowledge before you're sent off.

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me stop and go 'Woah!' It's on the level of puzzle games that alter your ways of thinking like Portal or Baba is You do. The first few levels alone will make your brain expand 3 sizes... and that's just the start of how deep the rabbit hole goes!Can't recommend it enough if you like puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Creative inception puzzle that is frustratingly satisfying. The game does a great job introducing new concepts to you every step of the way and leaves you feeling triumphant after finally having that "ah ha" moment of victory! I enjoyed my time with this game and would recommend it to anyone that enjoys a good puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Sokaban levels are pretty boring, as its just moving blocks around. This game manages to make that fun by thinking 'in' the box. The boxes you push could be infinite boxes, the level itself, a clone of the level that mirrors whatever comes out of it. There is a ton of creativity put into such a simple puzzle design that I feel this deserves its price tag of $20.The puzzles themselves are very simple where you will find the exact same solution used throughout the stage, just with one or two more steps. What sets this apart are the optional challenge levels and post-game which guarantee will have you feeling dumb staring at the screen for 20 minutes. Not to mention a custom level creator i'm excited to see what can come out of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, clean, bug free, good design (though very simple). The mechanics are interesting, but in terms of difficulty, where I rate the true ending for "Baba Is You" a 9/10, this game sits on a solid 4/10. Even the tough puzzles require only a few iterations of experimentation before the puzzle solution presents itself. This persisted until pretty much the end-game - there were a few headscratchers in the challenge and Appendix missions, but otherwise the difficulty remained pretty consistent.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a masterpiece in puzzle design elegance. It is the ultimate result of:In fact, the simplicity of the rules is arguably a spoiler - if you think hard enough, you can figure out many of the concepts explored in the game!Just those mechanics would be enough to make a solid, small game... but Patrick's Parabox takes it to the next level with additional mechanics. It's very easy to make a game convoluted and overwhelming by introducing additional mechanics, either by having too many mechanics or each mechanic being too complicated. Patrick's Parabox does not fall for this trap - there are just enough new mechanics to keep things interesting but not overwhelming, and each mechanic is so natural that it only takes a single introduction level to fully understand it.The puzzles themselves are also excellent. The negative reviews I've seen contradict my own experiences - to quote the Steam description:The overall difficulty of the game  indeed easier than other games like Baba Is You. If you're a puzzle game master, Patrick's Parabox overall difficulty might be a bit on the easier side, and each "new idea" might be so simple for you that they don't seem like new ideas. On the other hand, this makes Patrick's Parabox's excellent ideas much more accessible to a wide variety of people without the need to enable the "Unlock all puzzles" option in the settings.I personally found the difficulty pacing to be excellent - the main puzzles are indeed on the easier side, but there are harder optional puzzles marked with a red border, extra-hard post-game puzzles and a level editor for user-made levels.If Baba Is You is like a fine dining restaurant, Patrick's Parabox is like a brunch cafe: sometimes, you're just not in the mood for something deep and complex, but aren't willing to go as low as junk food.
