_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing puzzle game that mixes the mind-bending qualities of The Witness and Manifold Garden with the level design of Baba Is You.I highly appreciate how the game "teaches mechanics by doing them" rather giving explanations or lengthy/text-wall tutorials, and does an excellent job not feeling like someone's holding your hand through them. Many of the mechanics are very unique and the game wonderfully builds on them as it progresses. This includes when it starts combining those mechanics in ways you wouldn't have originally thought of, or adds in twists on top of what you've already learned.There are a bunch of subtle touches that make things even more immersive and enjoyable like seeing your character sprite around the cube you're working in, and the "redo" feature is also super helpful in trying things out. There's also a healthy number of meta-type things to discover.Visually this game is stunning especially when the gimmicks are involved, and gives me that challenging struggle-relief type of joy just like Baba did. It equally makes me want to complete the game 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a lot of things right, that make a puzzle game good:But most importantly, the game nails what I'm looking for in a puzzle game.  Specifically:I want to feel clever for solving a puzzle, and I want to feel like the designer is clever for creating the puzzle.  I don't want to feel like I lucked into a solution, or brute-forced it - I want to feel like I understand the idea the level is centered on.  And that, the game does in spades.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is a polygonal puzzling masterpiece. Parsing the pieces of each puzzle is perplexing and yet rewarding. It starts off simple, allowing you to enter and exit boxes, but quickly escalates to mastering .Each puzzle contains a new concept, even if some are variations of previous puzzles-- note down what you learn from each of the main series puzzles (you'll know when you hit the bottom) so you'll have an easier time tackling the extra Appendix and Challenge puzzles at the end- wherein the Appendix Puzzles contain  and the Challenge puzzles simply being brutally difficult even if you've made it that far.It took me approximately 19 hours to conquer all 364 puzzles this game had to offer, and there were countless moments that I felt like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiot when I solved a puzzle-- having repeatedly come within a step or two of solving the puzzle but not quite getting it.I would STRONGLY recommend you pick this up even if you are a fan of puzzle games-- even if it's to the smallest extent. Parabox is very beginner friendly with how approachable and understandable the puzzles are-- every time a new mechanic is introduced, it eases you into it softly.This game is EASILY in my top 10 for 2022.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A great mind-bending thinky puzzle game with a surprisingly lenient difficulty curve.If you like the new wave of "sokoban games with a twist" (Stephen's Sausage Roll, Pipe Push Paradise, Baba Is You, puzzlescript games like VEXT EDIT, etc), you'll like this too. And viceversa: if you like this, make sure to check out those games, too (and the rest of the genre; there are way too many great puzzlers to make an exhaustive list here).
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox perfect puzzle game (so far).  I've only passed 50-60 puzzles and it's starting to get hard already so I'm bracing myself.  Sometimes my brain cannot comprehend the paraboxes, but it's oh-so-satisfying to complete a puzzle i was initially stuck on.  Also, Patrick is so cute. Excellent. Very box. Would recommend for people who like puzzles and adorable boxes.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and interesting little puzzler. Some good, crunchy mechanics and the variant puzzles are nicely distinctive - does not suffer from the "a billion tiny variations on the mechanics with no playtesters helping pare things down" issues I've seen in other indie games. Worlds are reasonably constrained (i.e. mechanics are isolated mostly to the worlds they're introduced in) with more blending of mechanics in the challenge levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I've gone back and forth on this game, from loving it to hating it. Mostly now I hate it.Most of the puzzle mechanics are interesting a fun to work with. So I guess I got my moneys worth from the levels which used these puzzle mechanics.Then the game introduces the "infinity" puzzle mechanic and it all goes downhill. At first it is easy enough to solve the puzzles with infinity but later levels make it the only mechanic in the puzzle. I have no idea what the puzzle designer was trying to achieve with this mechanic, but for me, it totally ruins the game. This game isn't big on clever puzzle design, the puzzles are either easy or nonsensical. For the nonsensical levels, for the few I did solve, when I solved them I had no understanding of why the solution worked. I guess I just don't "get" what the designer was trying to achieve. I've never encountered this before in the dozens of puzzle games I've played on Steam.I'll recommend the game in spite of the infinity mechanic as there are enough other levels to make the game somewhat worth a purchase, at least on sale. But for me the game is overrated.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are really great, the game is highly addictive and each "zone" will slowly uncover the rules of the game, there is a lot of content here. In time of writing, currently 145 puzzles solved.Creating infinite recursive constructs is really nice. I think this is what a function being passed through a Y-combinator has to feel like :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for these kind of puzzle games and this one is very well made. The learning curve is consistent and not too steep. With 7hrs in I'm at about 2/3 to the end, however as the puzzles are getting harder this might even extend a bit :)I applaud the existence of the Demo. If you are eyeing this, definitely take a chance with the Demo and you'll get an idea if this is for you or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a puzzle game, a Sokoban game, but honestly you don't have to be a Sokoban aficionado to enjoy it. There are plenty of tough Sokoban sorts of challenges, but if you're stuck on a puzzle there's almost always a way to progress deeper in the game without having to solve it. Honestly, as solid as the puzzle-solving is, it's not the core experience. Instead, the core experience of this game is in wrapping your mind around the really trippy mechanics at play. This game is full of "oh my god what" moments, consistently followed by "ohh, that's why it's doing that" moments. If that sounds fun, you will enjoy this game. I found myself playing many if not most levels multiple times just to let it all digest.(One complaint regarding the postgame content, though – )
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best puzzle game I've ever played. Please, if you like Baba is You, the Witness, or even just, like, recursive mathematics, please play this game. The puzzles are hard, but not TOO hard. The puzzle design is absolutely exquisite, the rules of its world are consistent and fascinating. After almost every single level I had to lean back in my chair and say out loud "wow...". The game is full of perfect "aha" moments. Buy it, play it, solve all of its puzzles.You like infinite ordinal numbers right? Play this game. This is one of those special gaming experiences, please play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS SO SPECTACULAR wowee what a wild dive into mindbending shenanigans from something that seemed so simple... I loved every bit of the out-of-the-box (?) thinking involved in these puzzles, and I'm still going back for all the extra ones.I first played this game as a demo and thought it would be fun to see what else they did in the full version, but WOW I did not expect to get to experience so many delightfully sane little insanities. Absolutely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Great game of infinite recursion. First time through took about 13 hours for 260 some odd puzzles. I never needed to look a solution up. In comparison I needed help on more than 50 different Baba is you levels. I still can't solve 16 or so levels. I also struggled with monster's expedition and needed to look for solutions on Youtube at times. This game however was the perfect difficulty level for me. Music was a plus. You can check out the music here. I thought it paired very well with the style of the game:
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing puzzle game that constantly surprises you with new concepts but also by applying old concepts in a different way where you just go "oh of course it would work like that." If you play all the side levels the game is also decently long, something these indie puzzle games usually have an issue with.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: "Patrick, so great to see you! Hopefully the drive over wasn't too tiresome. Would you like me to take your Parabox for safekeeping? I'll put it in the closet next to the Sausage Roll and You. Please, take a seat by Stephen and Baba, I'll join you in just a moment...""Oh, and welcome to the great puzzle game club! You'll fit right in!"Another delightful puzzle game that has the perfect balance between challenge, innovation, and wonderful 'Ah-ha!' moments that don't feel too cheap or too extreme. Great little game!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted another puzzle game to be added to the top tier collection such as the witness, baba is you, myst, etc.? Then I highly recommend this. As the name suggests, the level is a parabox of the level. Each stage is teaching you that theme and then expending on it so much that you feel pleased with the answer (while your brain is fried from thinking too much).It has simple movement keys, reset key, undo key, and mouse is used to inspect the levels if you want to think ahead.  Oh, you wanted to know the story? Box, puzzle, solve, feel proud. There are also levels with red borders to show those are optional harder levels and you don't need to beat any of them to finish the game. What happens after you finish? That's up for you to find out. $26 well spent!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The beauty of this game is that it visualizes logic, and demonstrates how complexity can arise from simple rules. It empowers the player to break down these complex problems into their many simple parts, allowing to more easily handle them. By understanding the power of the rules, the player can make that power their own and there is pure bliss in that process.The game also does a create job of balancing the difficulty of its levels, offering both easy applications and advanced ones to choose at any time, allowing the player to traverse the zones of different ideas it keeps throwing at the player at their own pace. Just the right mix of linear guidance and free choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very well-designed puzzle game. Like other great ones (Stephen's Sausage Roll, Baba is You), this game has thought of every possible consequence of its rule set, and designed puzzles incorporating all of them in mind bending ways. Everything you might possibly do in a world where boxes can be pushed into other boxes (including themselves) has been taken into account, leading to some fun situations where you'll discover something while solving a puzzle wrong, and possibly much later realize it was an intentional mechanic that can actually be used.It's a bit on the short side, but the puzzles are often challenging, and extremely satisfying; solutions feel elegant most of the time, because so much can be done with so few pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal puzzle game -- there's simply no other way to put it. So much care was put into the development of this game, and it really shows. This game introduces you to its mind-boggling mechanics in ways that make them feel intuitive, and the difficulty curve is a smooth and steady climb the whole way through. The game is structured in such a way that you don't have to solve all the puzzles in order to continue to the next "batch" of levels -- and on the other hand, if you found a section to be fairly easy, there's an abundance of much more challenging & completely optional puzzles that you can take a crack at along the way. And if you get through all of those (or even if you don't), once the game has introduced all of its mechanics, it opens up yet another huge area with dozens more of the game's hardest levels, which combine any and all of the crazy tricks you've learned along the way.I can't stress enough just how incredible the level design of this game is. I can be pretty nitpicky when it comes to game design -- and I'm definitely prone to getting stuck on puzzles every now and then -- and I truly have nothing bad to say about the level design in Patrick's Parabox. It was a joyride from start to finish, and it never got boring for me; not even once.If you like puzzle games, you'll love Patrick's Parabox -- whether you're new to the puzzle genre or an experienced puzzle master.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Recursion is not a hard concept to understand. It consists of an object, and that object contains itself. This game utilized the concept for its puzzles and makes an amazing game. What starts as simple box pushing will eventually become mind boggling. Patrick's Parabox has a semi-linear progression and each level introduces a new rule or mechanic that you need to figure out. If you are struggling to solve a specific puzzle you can try another one or two levels ahead and come back to it. Don't be afraid to experiment because some solutions may be something you would have never thought of. I waited at least a year for this game to come out and I am very satisfied with the results.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest puzzle games of the modern era.When you have a smile brimming from ear-to-ear on each and every level, you know you're playing a good game. There was no frustration or confusment, just pure bewilderment at every new increase in difficulty. I won't spoil anything but the game is very much different from the first few levels. And when you think it can't get any more complex... well, you'll have to play to find out.10/10 - recommending this to all my logic-loving friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: An amazingly well done puzzle game. The puzzles proved adequately difficult and constantly engaging. I finally hit the bottom after about 5 hours, but there's still plenty to do: extra challenges, post-game puzzles. Certainly worth picking up if you like solving puzzles and recursively pushing boxes. If you're unsure, there's a generous demo that gives a solid idea of the rest of the game's mechanics without spoiling any of the more fringe interactions.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cool! The main concept is so mind-bending and unique, I definitely recommend it. It took me about 8 hours to fully complete the game, 12 including the challenges after the main game.The core concept is so so cool. It's the kind of thing that hurts your brain in a good way. Fortunately it is all introduced very slowly, and you learn how it works by playing many simple levels, as the complexity slowly ramps up. It really feels like every last bit of potential was squeezed out of it.My criticism is that some levels felt like slight variations on other levels, just recycled a bit. As the game goes on, it introduces a few mechanics and concepts that don't feel as natural or as elegant. It seems like the main idea reached its limit too soon, and more stuff was added to fill space.There are also some times where you can brute force levels without understanding why your solution works, which does not feel good.BUT despite these negatives, this game is unique and fun to experience. I'm glad I played it, and I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzle game about recursive structures of levels. The difficulty curve is quite a bit more gentle than many other puzzle games and the game has many puzzles that build upon demonstrations of the strange mechanics with relatively small examples.It's quite interesting and I look forward to what the community can do with the level editor to break our brains even further.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. I've been following the development for a couple of years since I first played a demo, and the full release is everything I could have hoped for. While the idea of recursively visiting boxes is tricky to wrap your head around at first, the game does a great job of introducing new mechanics as you go through the puzzles. And, like all great puzzle games, it makes you feel like a genius when you solve a tough level. It's one of the best games I've played in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant, mind bending and a lot of fun.The difficulty so far for me is varied - some puzzles are rather easy, some are moderate and some can take a while or I left for later. Good thing hard ones are optional so you can still progress. Visuals are rather basic and minimalistic, but work; music is great.I would recommend it to puzzle and logic games fan obviously, but also others who enjoy brain melting crazy ideas. What I saw on trailers, it delivers.I will be showing this to my non gamer friends and family, as for me it's something special and really outside the box ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant puzzle game. Critical path is very forgiving and always with many options of puzzles to try, and then there are dozens and dozens of fiendishly difficult puzzles for those who want the challenge. Each room explores a new idea, and the ideas get very 'outside the box' (apologies). Highly recommend for lovers of thinky puzzles, and even those who bounced of Baba is You's tricky difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant block puzzler packed with a staggering amount of content for the asking price.  The difficulty is also digestable for normal people to reach the end, but offers a ton of extra and optional puzzles for those who want to be pushed to their limits.  Highly recommend for any puzzle fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant puzzle game that introduces mind-bending mechanics at every turn. The recursion element creates many "A-ha!" moments as you progress. The aesthetics are simple but pleasing, and the music fits the tone perfectly. Pat really created something special here and if you have any interest in puzzle games you must check this out!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like puzzles?  Do you like adorably cute square blob-things that push boxes around?  Do you like thinking outside the box, while simultaneously thinking inside the box, while also seeing that the outside and inside of the box are the same place?  Do you like breaking the universe?  Do you just like boxes?If you answered 'yes' to any of these questions, you should buy this game.  Or buy a box.  Or put the game in a box...Boxes boxes boxes boxes boxes...
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: At first it was like "ok this is kinda weird but I understand" And then it became "this is getting out of hand I have no idea what I'm even doing anymore but by some act of God the puzzles are getting solved" And then "I am the God solving the puzzles, I see in 4 dimensions and have complete control over the will of the boxes, the laws of this universe are exposed to me" And then finally right back to "wtf is even going on anymore I understand nothing"In all seriousness, this is the most consistently fun puzzle game I've ever played because the pacing is PERFECT! Each puzzle took between 1 and 5 minutes for me to solve, and even the hardest ones the game had to offer only took a max of 20 minutes. Because the puzzles are short, you are constantly being bombarded with new concepts, rules, and mechanics to the point where you always feel just slightly overwhelmed, but never completely lost. The levels being short is a good things since it keeps the dopamine from solving a puzzle constantly flowing. If the game gave you more time to think about how everything works, the puzzles would probably be too easy and you wouldn't have any fun, and if it went any faster, they would be impossible and you wouldn't have any fun. It hit the sweet spot perfectly. I finished every puzzle in the game and if you asked me to explain how some of the mechanics worked I literally wouldn't be able to because its just that far out.If you like puzzle games this is one of the best.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game since the demo came out, and HOO BOY does it deliver. Plenty of good normal puzzles, plenty of good hard puzzles, all sorts of ways to twist your mind around recursion and space manipulation...Easily my favorite puzzle game in years. I haven't even looked at the user-generated content yet - and by the way, have I mentioned there's custom level support? Incredible, you don't see nearly enough of that type of thing these days. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: An inventive and surprising puzzle game that could be deemed a "Sausagelite": instead of full mechanical purity, it occasionally adds on new mechanics that still feel like natural extensions of the system. The puzzles here are bite-sized and not quite as overwhelming as Baba Is You, for instance. If you like, you may breeze through the approachable main path, or complete every one of the challenging optional puzzles first. But perhaps the thing I love most about Patrick's Parabox is that it's not afraid to play with wild, wacky rules in small sets of puzzles put off to the side. (The thing I love second-most might be the cool camera work.)
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely lovely game! I've been anticipating its release for quite a while now and I was worried it wouldn't live up to its hype. But I'm not disappointed, quite the opposite actually, the game surprised me in multiple occasions. It's an incredibly clever and innovative sokoban that introduces complex topics and handles them consistently well while teaching their rules gradually. I've only finished the main game (Although definitely planning to 100% soon) but at no point was I frustrated or very confused. The puzzles are challenging but not confusing and each level feels unique, innovative and rewarding with gimmicks being introduced at every chapter/world.If you like puzzle games and/or sokobans, I cannot recommend this game enough. Especially if you've played Baba Is You and want a different yet similar feeling mind boggling puzzle game.Edited for the nomination badge, nominating this game for my GOTY.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Patrick's Parabox is the best puzzle game in years!Puzzles are deep but simple. Executing on a solution is never tedious.This is a puzzle game with such strong well defined rules that when you think you're breaking them it's actually all just part of the game. The developer is always two steps ahead of you.Mechanics are introduced at a brisk pace. The beginning will have you shoving boxes around and the ending has you probing the secrets of the universe.You should buy this game if you liked "Baba is You" ESPECIALLY if you found yourself putting it down as the solution space grew too complex to make sense of.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Sokoban with a twist so gameplay changing that it's genuinely one of the first box shoving puzzle games I've ever seen that outright can't be called a Sokoban clone anymore.The best part of this game is that it keeps changing the formula with new features. First you start with boxes that you and other boxes can go inside of. Then you get boxes that contain themselves. Then it follows up with boxes that have copies of itself. I've also come into contact with mirrors recently, and I can't wait for what other new twists the game will throw at me.--EDIT: Having finished all of the puzzles now, I must say I'm sticking with my review. Absolutely. Amazing Game. Enjoyed every mind numbing puzzle right up to the end with every twist it threw at me and kept surprising me.I was hoping for rotational puzzles as well, but even this is explained in-game to be too complex code-wise, which I can understand, but can't help but cross my fingers that it might still be added at some point.In the end I finished it almost within a day, but worth every brain melting penny.--The puzzle mechanics themselves are introduced in an extremely kind way, where you first get to learn the basics, and are even forced into pulling off fun tricks before it throws you into the deep end with (optional) much harder puzzles. I personally really enjoy the ASCII version where you have to visualize everything yourself with all the things you've learned so far.It's just superbly crafted and just really well thought out. Couldn't recommend any puzzle game more.Can't wait for the sequel to this game where you make the exact same game, but in 3D.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Demo after I saw Patrick won IGDA Best Design.  Patrick's Parabox is a great mind-bending living puzzle that keeps levelling up the difficulty and I look forward to playing the full game for many hours to come! It's simple to learn the mechanics, and yet a lot of fun to figure out each increasingly complex sets of moves you have to figure out to solve the next puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Of the small handful of puzzle games I've played, this one definitely feels like it properly sets forth a Beginner Level of sorts - Not boringly easy, mind you, and there are certainly a few brainbusters to test your knowledge of the game.I could draw similarities between this and Portal - The mechanics are all laid out cleanly in the earlier levels, each Level Set covering the various niche mechanics until, by the end, one should have a clear understanding of the ins and outs of the outer-ins and inner-outs of this game's rendition of Recursive Block Pushing.I'll not spoil any of the mechanics you'll find, but each and every one adds a unique twist that's explored in depth, and isn't fully abandoned once you progress deeper - Every ounce of knowledge gained eases one through the later levelsI beat the game in under 8 hours, and despite getting absolutely stumped at one stage, I was able to progress to the deeper stages thanks to the lenient level completion requirements to proceed to the next stage, before coming back once I'd gotten a better grasp of what that level set was going over thanks to working with it with more intricate (and somehow easier for me to understand) mechanicsGetting 100% was fun, and, save for having watched Aliensrock's first episode on this game (covering the first two or three level sets), I managed to do it without any guides or outside help. And once the credits roll, there's a lot more to do! Even a subset of levels that make yet more interesting twists on the mechanics!As long as you remember to step away from a level if it's stumped you, there's a good balance of brain busters, progression rate, and deep thinking moments provided by this game. Would absolutely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game since playing the demo a couple of years ago, and from what I've seen so far (after approx 150 puzzles solved), the full game has lived up to my expectations.It takes a single clever idea, and explores it fully. The puzzles are more bite-sized than similarly mind-bending games like Baba Is You or Recursed, and take a while to ramp up in difficulty, but so far they've all been bringing new ideas and variations to the game's core concept.The game is also well-polished, especially for one built by a solo developer. It has a simple, clean art style and a good variety of background music. The animations of boxes going in and out make it clear what's happening (which can be surprising in the more peculiar edge cases).I'm looking forward to seeing what different mechanics are introduced in the remainer of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautifully elegant and thoroughly enjoyable puzzle game. I found myself getting lost in enjoyment as the time graciously passed by. This is a must buy game for all experienced & beginner puzzlers alike. There are surprises around every corner, and there is tremendous satisfaction with every "Aha!". Cannot recommend enough. I see myself playing through this game in entirety several times. So excited that it is finally released!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles in this game aren't the hardest, but they should still give your brain a nice workout. There is a lot of content in this game which should keep you busy for hours. Some of the recursion levels that had the infinite zooming in camera did make me feel nauseous for some reason, but there aren't a lot of them compared to the other levels in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: I love this! When I first tried the games demo it wasn't nearly as smooth as it is now.It reminds me of The Witness because it's got that same sustained eureka-high which goes on and on. Just like The Witness it explains concepts to you through its puzzles in a way which builds on itself. It's like a guided path up a lofty mountain... the path is soundly constructed and not too steep, but thinking clearly will be a challenge as you ascend above the clouds.If you're a fan of conceptually interesting puzzle games like Baba Is You, Steven's Sausage Roll, A Good Snowman is Hard to Build, and  A Monster's Expedition, than this is an epic journey and a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. Really good. Starts off easy but the concept is interesting enough to keep you from getting bored. The difficulty increases steadily and you'll soon find that you can't just rush through it all anymore. Although I'm not done, I can tell that this game fully explores its limits, if you're thinking "what if you could..." after playing for a bit, there's guaranteed to be a level or part of a puzzle based around that idea.Just go play it, it's a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: Edit after 7 hours: still a great game! The game seems a bit easier than Baba is You but has the same amount of "WAIT WHAT just happened??"In the first few hours of playing this game, I completed several worlds. What I like most is that new gimmicks keep appearing, none of which I ever thought would be possible! None of the gimmicks are overused, but they are not underused either. Just the correct amount of challenge for me.Can't wait to play it more!
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

_childDocuments_.review: A mind-bending recursive puzzle game about boxes within boxes within boxes within boxes. Learn to use infinity to your advantage as you explore a deep and elegant system.
_childDocuments_.name: Patrick's Parabox

name: SIGNALIS
detailed_description: Searching for dreams inside of a nightmare Awaken from slumber and explore a surreal retrotech world as Elster, a technician Replika searching for her lost partner and her lost dreams. Discover terrifying secrets, challenging puzzles, and nightmarish creatures in a tense and melancholic experience of cosmic dread and classic psychological survival horror. SIGNALIS is set in a dystopian future where humanity has colonized the solar system, and the totalitarian regime of Eusan maintains an iron grip through aggressive surveillance and propaganda. Humanoid androids known as Replikas live among the populace, acting as workers, civil servants, and Protektors alongside the citizens they are designed to resemble. The story of SIGNALIS begins as a Replika named Elster awakens from cryostasis in a wrecked vessel. Now stranded on a cold planet, she sets out on a journey into depths unknown. Experience fear and apprehension as you encounter strange horrors, carefully manage scarce resources, and seek solutions to challenging riddles. Explore the dim corners of a derelict spaceship, delve into the mysterious fate of the inhabitants of a doomed facility, and seek what lies beneath. Discover an atmospheric science-fiction tale of identity, memory, and the terror of the unknown and unknowable, inspired by classic cosmic horror and the works of Stanley Kubrick, Hideaki Anno, and David Lynch. Wander a brutalist nightmare driven by fluid 3D character animations, dynamic lights and shadows, and complex transparency effects, complemented by cinematic sci-fi anime storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game for both gameplay and story reasons. Gameplay: I've heard the gameplay described as "old school resident evil style with a fixed camera angle and strict inventory management mechanics." I've never played a RE game, so idk if that's accurate. The camera angle is a sort of top down overview of one room at a time. You control a character by walking them around a room and picking up items. Sometimes you encounter a room with a puzzle in it but you mostly just pick up a hexagonal item or a ring and take that to another room and place it in the hexagon shape. I hope you like the sound of doors opening and closing because you'll be moving items from one room to another for the whole game. I didn't find the gameplay aspect of rearranging items between rooms to be interesting, exciting, or fulfilling. A couple puzzles were stimulating but I didn't experience anything very memorable puzzle wise. The inventory management was my biggest frustration. There are several weapons (guns) you can find and use. Each has its own unique ammo type. The guns don't really feel any different from one another with the exception of the very first gun you get. The only reason that one stands out is because it does such little damage that you need 3 or 4 bullets to take out each enemy whereas other weapons mostly require only one bullet per kill, sometimes two. It feels like the existence of multiple gun types only serves the purpose of frustrating inventory management. You only ever find 3-4 bullets at a time, meaning after you kill three enemies you need to find a safe room to switch out to a different weapon. You only have 6 inventory slots. Most of the game is spent running between any given room with an item you need to pick up to the safe room with a storage box, putting your current inventory items in the storage box, and running back to the item you wanted to pick up. Maybe you enjoy managing 6 inventory slots without being allowed to drop/discard items to the ground, and maybe you enjoy running through very similar rooms with lots of black screens between doorways. I didn't really enjoy that so I can't recommend. Story:The story is designed for each person to have their own interpretation of what's happening in the story. I didn't finish the game, I only got to the end of the second chapter. I realized after 6 hours that I didn't understand why I was doing anything I was doing in the game and the scattered notes on the ground hadn't clarified anything yet. I wasn't enjoying the gameplay, especially as the second chapter is almost a carbon copy of the first both gameplay and story-clarity wise.People seem to really enjoy both the gameplay and story. I hope you do. This was my first game in this genre and I don't think it's for me.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: A true survival horror masterpiece that reaches the heights of the top tier franchises including Silent Hill and Resident Evil. The blend of the cyberpunk genre and classic survival horror controls perfectly mesh into this surreal nightmare. I would highly recommend this to any horror fan out there as it is genuinely terrifying, but also has incredibly precise and engaging gameplay with some of the best puzzles I have experienced in years. Truly an unforgettable triumph mainly created by a mere two people. Support these devs please the game is well worth the price and then some.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most beautiful game I've ever played.I didn't know what I was getting into when I started it at first enticed by its Classic Resident Evil / Silent Hill gameplay vibe.Making my way through it the story just resonated with me so much that by the ending that I got (The Promise)I was left speechless in tears, I couldn't stop crying.I can't go into detail about anything going on in this game other than the fact that if you are a fan of classic survival horror and deep compelling stories that take you through a journey this is the game to do exactly that.Open your mind and your heart to it, be perceptive, receptive and open-minded through it all. Let its signal reach out to you, let it show you what it needs to show you.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: The game completely lost me after doing a fakeout ending which I didn't know was a fake-out ending until I looked up what achievements I'd missed.At this point I had already sort of switched gears into feeling like I had "finished" the game, and had uninstalled it. Weirdly, I would have been less disappointed if the game really did finish like that.So I had to reinstall the game, rewatch the vague "ending", sit through the unskippable credits again, and then read several pieces of lore as soon as the game resumes. The whole sequence felt like a chore, I was just so fed up with the game at this point.It took me a while to switch gears back into being able to enjoy any of it. But then the real ending to the game didn't turn out to be that much clearer than the fakeout ending. And I'm reminded of something someone once said about good storytelling, that true story depth has clear water all the way down, but murky water may seem deep even though it's only a puddle.Maybe it's only because I was annoyed with the game, but the story only felt pretentious. Not deep and not clever. And having given it a week for my annoyance to wear off, and to reflect on the story, I don't feel any different.Annoyance is the overriding emotion whenever I look back at my experience.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a horror game the ambiance and entire game in general is really calming to me, like a warm blanket, even during struggling combat. Even some of the more obscure beeping coming from different radio signals makes me feel comfortable. The story is beautiful, the characters are beautiful, its all beautiful. There's something magnificent about a robot woman powering through literal space and time, again and again, even losing limbs and parts of her body, purely to fulfill the promise she made to her girlfriend. She never stops, no matter the struggle, because she will fulfill her promise. It's magnificent.and plenty of people like to complain that the lesbian robots and lesbian main characters get too much attention and people look over world details but those people are idiots. The world only goes through these changes because of your girlfriend your trying to save, you only go through changes because of your girlfriend your trying to save. Each female robots have a counterpart female robot they bond with so they stay sane. Its truly written into this magnificent world and people who complain about it are garbage. As you learn more and more while progressing through the story you realize how much love for another person has truly altered the world your on, and existence in general. How fragile the robots minds are, how they stem from previous people, how their brain alters and changes when exposed to certain material, and how one girls love for a female robot was the catalyst to setting off all the events in the game. And how the love that female robot holds for her spans multiverses, space and time, infinite amounts of deaths, purely to fulfill a promise they made together.Its a masterpiece, I literally have no record player but despite that I'm considering buying the vinyl record. That's how much of a masterpiece it is.And as a bisexual trans woman let me tell you it makes forging through cosmic horrors for your girlfriend even more meaningful, even more powerful. But I believe anyone can enjoy the game, even if you aren't in love with women. For it is truly a masterpiece, whether your lesbian or not. The message, the story, the love, its still there regardless of alignment or gender. Buy and experience Signalis sweet individuals!!
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: Signalis is Rose Engine's first game and wow what a start. It brings back the old-school horror gameplay of Silent Hill combined with the resource management of Resident Evil, wrapped up in a gooey eldritch sci-fi story and damn did I love every bite of this short experience.You control Elster, a part organic robot called a Replikant, looking for someone in a facility that's gone to hell at the edge of the solar system. I can't talk much more about the plot without spoilers and while I was a little unsure at first, by the end I was vibing with the enigmatic setting that's both surreal and nightmarish in all the right ways. I wasn't sure about the anime look at first either but it's surprisingly restrained and it makes sense in how it reflects the themes resulting in some iconic visuals.The gameplay has you exploring the building, carefully juggling resources, and solving puzzles. I found the combat okay for the most part but sometimes had trouble locking on to enemies properly. The stealth mechanics and limited resources mean fights shouldn't be started carelessly, but unavoidable bottlenecks and bosses left me having to retry a couple of times as a result. The other issue is it feels like there are a few too many weapons crammed in to such a short game with the power leaning top heavy as the pistol is quickly overshadowed and all but useless by the end of the game.The puzzles themselves are mostly simple but fun and feed into the exploration side of the game using a mix of environmental and logic problems. I had a page of notes and sketches by the end which is often a good sign. I've heard people complain about the 6 slot inventory and while it can be a little restrictive it didn't bother me at all, though the developer is apparently taking steps to address this as it's been such a point of contention.Overall Signalis is beautifully put together. From the lovingly crafted low-poly PS1 aesthetic, animations that evoke memories of Evangelion, and writing that hints at a bleak and brutal existence on the edge of space during war-time. It manages to be deeply atmospheric, dark, and creepy with mysteries that kept me hooked from one surprise to the next without a single jump scare. I rate this one highly for managing to create something unique and compelling out of the best parts of its inspirations, and coming from a 2 person team it's all the more impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I am submitting a negative review, I still would like to acknowledge the positives of this game:the overall aesthetic is its strongest suit. The pixel art, the cyberpunk-noir / horror setting, the somewhat convoluted story open to interpretation are very intriguing elements.However, the gameplay is poorly executed. The limited inventory space is just an unnecessary complication, and the level design eventually just makes you running around backtracking a lot without any serious action, just looking for the right place to be, which decreases the immersion for me and just turns into a grind.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: This game got so many positive reviews but for me personally it's boring. This game has such a slow pace and such a slow burn. Managing inventory system in this game is such an old thing that's very out dated in this day of age. I understand it's a survival horror game but for me it could've been so much more and better. Plus why can't some monsters or zombies die even after you shot them like more than 30 times? After 1 hour and like 30 min of gameplay i'm already bored. I refunded the game. It's just not my thing. It could've been so much more and better.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: What is the value of a human life? How far are you willing to go for the one you love? What separates dream from reality? And does it even matter in the grand scheme of things?Signalis is a game of questions. While these questions are not new and have been asked since the dawn of time, themes revolving around the nature of mankind, reality and creation are as compelling as ever. The game's unique presentation is mesmerising, dripping with soul from the first minute. The story is a perfect blend of lovecraftian cosmic horror and bittersweet romance. Every detail has been meticulously crafted, from the sound design to the various puzzles.But what really sets this game apart is the room for interpretation. Its refusal to give easy answers. Signalis does not spoon feed or hold your hand, it encourages you to embrace the uncertainty and complexity within its shadowy depths.To reveal too much about Signalis would be to rob it of its power. The less you know about this game, the better. Please just play it.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: I think that if every game was made with the love and care and thought that was poured into this, and by only two people no less, then there'd be a lot less regrets in my steam library purchases.Visual and auditory perfection, with damn solid survival horror mechanics based on 90s classics like the original Silent Hill. Impeccable, wretched vibe. A heartbreaking love-story. A game chapter name called "Gestaltzerfall", meaning shape/body decay, which might be the best word for anything I've ever seen. Its just. So good.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: Finished Signalis and what a game! Truly one of the best games I played in a while, rivaling Fear and Hunger in levels of atmosphere and story telling!From the characters, the design, to the soundtrack, everything hit perfectly. I might try to figure out ALL the secrets later, but for now, I'm content to say that this run has a been a blast. Learning all the lore, how to avoid or best enemies, and how to figure out the mystery of what happened in the story. And since it's ambiguous, I can interpret it as anything I want.Also I can't stress enough how unnerving everything is. This is a horror game that does the genre right. It doesn't rely on cheap scares or have a cast that makes me root for the monster kill them. No. It's a game that truly understands the meaning of dread and invokes that feeling in all who play it. Even when you get weapons, when you feel safe, you still aren't sure and never know what else the game throws at you. Whether it be visually or psychological, all the creeping dread you feel with keep you on your toes as you try to figure out the terrifying reality you stepped into.All and all, I highly recommend Signalis.

_childDocuments_.review: What a brilliant game. There's so much thematic depth to Signalis. Everything from the broadest strokes to the tiniest details feels deliberate. It's such a beautifully constructed tragedy -- a gut-wrenching meditation on how fears of loneliness and guilt go hand in hand. Aaaand it's all in the context of an excellent survival-horror game. _childDocuments_.review: An immaculate survival horror experience. A treat for those who enjoy games like the original resident evils, where you need to conserve your resources carefully and solve various puzzles. The graphics mostly emulate something you'd have seen on the ps1 and the intentionally low polygon models and pixelated textures are really charming. Probably a big selling point for some is that there are no cheap jumpscares. The game's horror comes from the well-crafted atmosphere thanks to great sound and level design.I beat the game in around 9 to 10 hours while progressing at a comfortable place, I didn't really get stuck because of puzzles besides once towards the end of the game. That being said the game does have multiple endings based on your playstyle so there is some replay value there outside of just achievement hunting.The story is one of those types where you either spend a lot of time poring over every line of dialogue and clue and make your own opinion on what is going on, or watch a ton of youtube theory videos.If you are comfortable with the survival horror genre I recommend playing the game on the hardest difficulty from the get go.

_childDocuments_.review: *This was the primary thought going through my head as I was attempting to enjoy my time playing the game.In short, the game suffers from a combination of it's combat and inventory system seemingly designed to waste your time. Sure, as you've probably seen from the other reviews, many people like that kinda thing. But of course, for many others.. we don't.You'll spend a staggering amount of time running back and forth between a save room or puzzle rooms because the game wants to waste your time by limiting your entire inventory to 6 spaces. Yes, you read that right.. SIX!That includes not just puzzle pieces, keys, healing items and ammo, but also the weapon and tool you currently have equipped along with the mod (flashlight/radio/ect) you have attached.The final nail in the coffin, is that enemies respawn. So between your seemingly endless trips to the safe room to swap out items, you'll have to continuously dodge enemies, regardless if you've killed them or not (saving the "burn flares" for boss fights).Essentially, there's no reason to kill anything.. just empty everything you've got into the vault.. or well, you'll need that flash light! aaaaaand prolly those keys to open doors/rooms you haven't explored yet.. what? I'm already out of inventory space? really!?In truth, I stopped playing shortly after getting the flash light (3 hours) because it just wasn't engaging. It felt like playing FFXIV's story mode again, where I'm running between dozens of pointless NPC quest givers to barely advance in progress.tl;drThe game is decent and I might change this review if they ever implement an official patch that allows you to carry more items. Sure the game would be "shorter" but atleast then, I don't feel as though I'm wasting my time playing.+++++++ UPDATE ++++++I realized the game just isn't for me and refunded it.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Retro Survival Horror? Do you like stories which aren't direct, yet have excellent world building? If yes to both of the above, you'll probably like Signalis. If you haven't played a survival horror but do like the sounds of a game with intriguing world building, I'll briefly summarize. The game is good, but flawed. The intent behind the game, and the story, isn't one that is going to be naturally fulfilling. This means it won't be a game for everyone. The game has beautiful moments, but also significant mechanical frustration. The biggest spoiler is the exact number of boss fights, and why all except for one sucks. If you want to go in blind, skip to the next paragraph. The first boss fight does not telegraph that there is a boss fight, and if you don't have your pistol and specific items on you the fight becomes unwinnable. This fight occurs very soon after you acquire a shotgun, and due to inventory management, its not unreasonable that you might think a shotgun alone will work, it doesn't and deals no damage to the boss during its "vulnerable" state. The second boss is a meat cage which requires you to run around for 3 minutes straight. That's it. Its the worst boss I've seen in a game. There's no fighting, just running around in a small circle for 3 minutes. Even longer if you accidentally walk to the wrong side of the arena. The final boss however is good. Its nothing to write home about, but it lets you know its coming, makes use of prior mechanics, forces you to think on your feet, and is difficult, but fair. The overall story is something that, well, its flawed. So why recommend the game? Because it does something that most other games don't do, and is successful in doing so. The game is incoherent, but does so for the sake of immersion. The games world building and art direction are superb, its coherent and oppressive. Its a very immersive game, yet also one that does not make sense. Mostly. The game is purposefully vague about the story, and it does try to clear up certain aspects of the game by its ending, but you will not be satisfied when the credits roll. Instead, you kind of have to sit on it. Sitting on it doesn't solve some of the plot contrivances, nor does it let you fully understand the... well flow of the story. It doesn't make the game suddenly coherent, it just makes the incoherence more palatable.

_childDocuments_.review: If you took the best parts of dead space, resident evil, and threw them into a dystopian cyberpunk pixel art world this is what you would get: a masterpiece. A triumph of gameplay that makes the weapons feel like they pack a punch but also makes you scared to use them for the lack of ammunition. _childDocuments_.review: A beautifully horrific game that will drive you mad as you try to find answers where there are only more questions. _childDocuments_.review: This amazing indie survival horror game is a challenging and unique experience, with similar vibes to Silent Hill and with the inventory management similar to Resident Evil 1 remake. I’m very happy to have completed this beautiful game. It stands out as a 2.5D survival horror title featuring decent puzzles and a good inventory system. If you're not a fan of the 2.5D perspective, there’s a mod available that allows you to switch to either 1st or 3rd person view.With four different endings, the game offers some replay value. However, the absence of additional game modes or a randomizer modifier will not make me comeback anytime soon. One thing I really appreciate is the developers' decision post launch to give players the option to increase the maximum inventory slots and to not let the flashlight taking up one to let players play however they like. You can toggle these settings on or off based on your preferences. Be aware, though, that to get all the achievements, you need to complete a run with both options disabled while playing on hard mode.There’s also a "stealth" mechanic that adds some other ways to handle enemies. If you're skilled enough, you can avoid enemies in certain rooms and hallways completely. This reminded me of the lickers from Resident Evil 2 remake and I really like this feature.My only main complain is that enemies often appear directly in front of you as soon as you open a door, leading to unavoidable damage most of the time. This is very frustrating, especially on hard mode, and I hope it gets fixed.In conclusion, I absolutely recommend this game to both experienced and veteran survival horror players, as the difficulty starts rising a lot from Chapter 2, even on normal mode.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a missed opportunity. I know I'm in the minority on this opinion, but I just can't grok this game.I launch the game and in a few minutes I just have a sudden urge to exit. It's tedious just for the sake of being tedious. Artificially injected tedium, from everything to the enemies respawning, to the tedious level design and map objectives, and limited inventory and resources. Also, there are just such weird design choices like being damaged while within proximity of enemies even if they are not attacking, which is just absolutely janky and breaks immersion. Or when they constantly camp doors so you are just immediately screwed with unavoidable contact damage when you re-enter rooms. Which you will be doing **a lot**. I just don't want to play it. I've played SH2 and RE2, they weren't like this. I don't think it's trying to deviate from traditional horror gameplay elements, it just seems to go overboard with the tedious elements of those games.On a side note, the performance is surprisingly poor and framerate can vary wildly depending on the current area.

_childDocuments_.review: A hauntingly, heart-breakingly beautiful sci-fi horror adventure. And Yuri to boot!The way this game has left me feeling and thinking, it was an amazing experience. _childDocuments_.review: very clearly wears its influences on its sleeve, with the grotesque, rusted aesthetic and storytelling of , the philosophical questioning of , and a lot of general aesthetic cues from . Despite not shying away from showing off what inspired it, the game still manages to be wholly unique in its presentation and delivery of its themes.Gameplay-wise, it hearkens back to the feeling of the classic  games, modernized but still carrying that torch with it proudly. I can think of few better examples of a game that takes familiar ideas and puts a new spin on them. The story can be somewhat difficult to follow, but there's no denying the sheer emotion of it. It really is the kind of thing that will sit with you for a good while after finishing it.The game is overall a wonderful experience that clearly had a lot of love poured into it, and is absolutely worth playing if it even slightly piques your interest.

_childDocuments_.review: Signalis is a compelling tale of love and tragedy told in the form of classic survival horror. The art style is beautiful, the lore is deep, and the game is quite fun.If you are thinking about playing this game, GO IN BLIND!!!! There's a lot going on in and things won't really make sense at first! I think the game does a fantastic job of bringing all of the breadcrumb clues together so keep going! After you beat the game I would recommend looking up some discussion about it if you are still searching for answers in a place where there are only questions. There are a lot of story breakdowns and discussion that I felt added greater meaning and understanding to the game after I beat it.I found the survival horror elements a bit frustrating at first as I am not a longtime fan of the genre, however they grew on me as I became more knowledgeable about the game. Playing on the "normal" difficulty as opposed to "survival" for my first playthrough was also quite helpful. I'd still recommend the game purely for the story, even if the game might not be your usual cup of tea, as Elster's journey is truly memorable.Remember our promise. T_T

_childDocuments_.review: an early Resident Evil-styled survival horror game with an art style reminiscent of 90s-00s cyberpunk anime. Altogether, we're talking puzzles, hyperstylized androids, keycards, low polgon models, cryptic messages flashing on screen, storage boxes, the inability to move and shoot at the same time, and themes on the nature of memory and personhood. The cast is predominantly women, and sapphic themes and relationships feature prominantly.Art direction and presentation are by far it's strongest features. Plays often with word art, jumpcuts, allusions to literature (King in Yellow, coughcough), camera perspectives, and the game interface itself.Strong recommend to anybody who likes short campaigns, survival horror, cyberpunk, and polished indie titles (made by two women, Barbara Wittmann and Yuri Stern). You can beat it in 10-12 hours.A word of caution for a certain type of player: avoid the attitude that the best, most transformative part of a game must come at the very end. You will be disappointed. Instead, like Soulsborne games, you're going to get the most out of the story by close reading and cross-referencing documents. If you like trippy, interpretive experiences and are okay with ambiguity (Kingdom Hearts, Donnie Darko, Evangelion, David Lynch), this is for you.Most importantly: no jumpscares! I love all things spooky, dark, and disturbing, but I have a crippling fear of jumpscares. Thank you Rose Engine for abstaining.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice nod to older survival horror games. You need to manage your inventory and supplies decently well to be able to get through it. The game doesn't outright tell you the story in a simple way. A lot of it is up to interpretation and it is the type of story that wants you to speculate on what happened/happening. Only did one playthough of the game but adored it, and felt like it is one of my favorites. Only hope more people can pick it up and try it out. _childDocuments_.review: L  I  G  M  A  L  I  SMetal Gear Solid + Resident Evil + Cyberpunk 2069 (or anything where android/cyborg female entities have a booty every straight male would happily commit snu snu seppuku with. Ex Machina comes to mind as well.)Movement flows like Solid Snake getting the gold medal in figure skating, without the hyper-emphasis on stealth. We're still completely capable of sneaking by enemies and it's recommended we do so as to conserve ammo and utilities a la RE-style inventory management. Instead of an orchestrated alarm ringing our eardrums we're presented with anxiety in the form of heavily bitcrushed and distorted sound waves. We love the goosebumps we get every time the tracks fade in upon us.Combat slaps like Resident Evil. We curb stomp downed enemies in order to maim and knock their asses out, albeit temporarily. This successfully increases the tension and leads to a retreating peen whenever enemies awaken, like a panicked turtle shriveling back into it's shell as a defensive tactic. Those bastards reanimate with a thunderous bone(r)-chilling screech and catch us off guard every damn time. Tippy-toes from now on. This is no problem at all.Challenging puzzles, but fair. Some of us may be inclined to brute force these and can possibly get away with doing so, but patience is key here. The longplay-dominated YouTube gamer water landscape taunts us as we consider opening a new tab in your favorite hentai-dominated browser. But we stay strong and hold our ground. The urge to go the easy route is bested and we go back to the game after a quick meditative break to find ourselves making sweet coitus to the puzzle as the developers intended. We wipe off our chest and press forward to the next puzzle. Rinse + wash + repeat.GOTTA LOVE SURVIVAL HORROR WITH PUZZLE INTERLUDES TO BREAK UP THE SPOOKS.WE LOVE THAT SH!T.Nine hours in. We're enjoying ourselves. Solid entry for $20. One simply cannot look at this offering and be turned off in any way, especially if your past was filled with bodacious bubble gum polygonal PSX titles barely holding their shape together. I was a PlayStation poser with my Nintendo 64 by my side growing up, but was still able to muster some wonderful friends who shared their disc-based console experience alongside me. MGS and RE stand out. Yes RE2 was on the N64, but we don't talk about that version besides the technical achievement present of fitting that ♥♥♥♥ onto a single cartridge.This is the real deal and one many gamers have been asking for without knowing it. We tip our collective fedoras and pinch both nipples to rose-engine and friends. She's a beaut and worthy of all the incoming awards.Onward to the final stretch of gameplay...

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, not a great game.The throwback to resident evil 1 & 2 style gaming is good fun but at times this fails to tighten up the resource balancing and in the long run fails as survival horror.I died once and had mountains of ammo and health left at the end. The final boss was finished with the starting pistol. At no point did I feel under pressure. I'm not particularly good at these games so I would expect more of a challenge.The light module mechanic is really annoying. Some random rooms are completely dark and you need the light module to navigate them. You sacrifice one inventory slot to the light module. This is all fine in principle, you sacrifice space for convenience, however, those dark rooms are unforeseeable so you either have to carry the light module all the time or run back across to a storage box to pick it back up. Ok, frustrating but fine. But let's say you memorised the room and killed the monsters earlier, you could just forgo the light module and make your way to the exit? Nope. If you don't have the light module you can't take the exit you want even if you know it's right there, the game will say "it's too dark to see".The puzzles are ok, there's some logic and clue solving involved but nothing too strenuous. I'd say that this is probably as difficult as it needs to be, or would be if the resource management and combat offered more of a challenge.Some of the horror themes pulled in are interesting but the inclusion of the King in Yellow feels a little arbitrary and lacking, like there's more that could have been done with the themes.Was I spooked? Yes, the sound crafting and general atmosphere does a lot to contribute to a claustrophobic world ever more consumed by an unknown darkness.==end of review==Did I enjoy the game and was it worth it? Absolutely. It's worth a purchase and your time (It took me around 20 hours to complete). There's enough here to keep you engaged and pushing through. The team did a good job with the atmosphere and this carries you through to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished Signalis a year ago at this point and it's still stuck with me, more than anything else has, or maybe ever will. It ate at me for weeks after I finished it. Anytime I'm reminded of it, I can't seem to get it out of my head for days at a time. It's sometimes hard to even replay it at this point, which isn't to say it doesn't have replay value. It's just the way it has scarred me in a sense. I know how much it broke me the first time, and it's hard to go back knowing something had that affect on you. The way Signalis blends it's inspirations (literary, film, games, etc) into something exceptionally unique is remarkable. It feels like it's inspirations (Silent Hill, Resident Evil, David Lynch, etc), but it doesn't feel like a rip off or something trying to do exactly what has been done before. It's something new born of love for classic horror. The score and the audio design are some of THE best put in games. The guns, screams, footsteps, puzzles, sound so . The score has become a comfort album despite holding some of the scariest ♥♥♥♥ I've heard (it still unnerves me to my core), but its got such beauty in it. It's very reminiscent of Silent Hill, but has it's own sense of theme and style. You haven't truly lived until you've heard the track Hamstrung at 5am. ♥♥♥♥ hits different.Story, go in blind. Broke me.Gameplay is true classic survival horror. Some of the best, and I'm sure this will be the thing everyone talks about so I won't go in depth, but if you like very limited inventory, critical thinking, resource management, and great puzzles, than this is for you.The style of this game is jaw-dropping. So insanely beautiful. It's insane how good this game looks and runs. It's fully 3D despite looking 2D, the way the lighting works and casts shadows, sometimes several shadows if there's multiple sources of light is really cool. It's not a huge marvel, oh wow shadows, but I just didn't expect them to be there. The way the environments looks and work is so good, man. It's so visually distinct and I didn't have to completely rely on a map because each room is so unique and identifiable which a lot of games struggle with. I'm so glad I played this game when I did, and I will be coming back to it as the years go on. Forever thinking about it every once in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could talk about this game.I wish I could tell you why this game is good, and why you should play it, but that'd require that I understand what this game is. Maybe it's a charming, Silent-Hill-meets-Resident-Evil survival shooter, or maybe it's a cosmic horror movie brought to new life in game form, or maybe it's an ARG-level mystery-puzzle game so complex that it reaches Lovecraftian levels of incomprehensibility. Truthfully, saying that Signalis is any one of those things feels like lying, because there's so much more to it than that.if you don't understand what's going on, that's good, but keep trying anyway; Signalis relies on the player's confusion to power it's narrative. This game is one of the most complex indie games I've played in a long time, and the developers have made it abundantly clear that they spent at least as much time thinking about the game as they did making it. So I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who likes games of the sort, it's a wonderful experience that goes as deep as you're willing to look.Just maybe learn some German beforehand.

_childDocuments_.review: The short version is this is a solid survival horror game very evocative of the classics of the genre, for better or worse, and while it has a few gameplay/game design shortcomings it's still a very well executed game while the story and narrative certainly reaches into the 'artistic' level of things.As for the longer version...There's a clear inspiration from the old survival horror games, especially along the lines of Resident Evil and Silent Hill. I'll say there's some instances where this game falls short. Namely it keeps some old holdovers that it probably shouldn't, or could easily do better than it did. My #1 issue with this is the inventory system, where classic holds you to 6 items, much like OG Resident Evil. The thing is RE always had a nearby safe-box and exploration tended to branch out from these central rooms, where-as in Signalis you're often dropped into a whole new area where the inability to drop items (only destroy ammo/healing items) can very quickly cripple you as you desperately look around for the safe room and loot box. There's also a comparative large amount of weapon variety, which while you think would be great ultimately just means more weapon and ammo juggling. Do yourselves a favour and if nothing else play with the extended inventory setting, you lose nothing and remove a good chunk of the headache this causes. Besides that it's a pretty standard, solid survival horror topdown. Nothing gameplay wise especially impressed me or struck me as new or innovative, but what's there is solid. Puzzles and such are also quite good, I ended up with a whole page of scribbled notes and drawings of clues, codes, hints etc in front of me by the end, very nostalgic and satisfying while never feeling too convoluted or confusing. The story and narrative is where the game really comes in. This is easily one of those titles that goes well into the "Video games as art" category and honestly knowing German and Chinese probably would help you get even more out of it. With heavy inspiration, use and allusion to various literary, artistic and spiritual themes, beliefs, theories and philosophy the story and narrative can easily be a deep dive. It's the kind where there's 2-hour breakdowns of the game on youtube that you will genuinely want to watch after the fact. All of these things are coupled with what I'd say was an ultimately impactful character narrative that I was surprised fit together at the end for how potentially conceptually difficult a lot of it is. I won't pretend like I understood everything by the credits, but enough that it was still a good impact (and a kind of story I'm admittedly a sucker for). The youtube lore video on the end just helped bring it all together even more and really made me appreciate the depth and amount of effort and thought that was put into it by the developers. When a youtube starts talking about a bunch of rather obscure themes and you go "This sounds kind of ridiculously out there" only to see hard proof of symbolism included in the game I couldn't help but be impressed.Long story short, play it if you're nostalgic for old survival horrors, or enjoy an artistic and well presented psychological character funhouse. Meanwhile, turn off the limited inventory system and be aware it's by no means a perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am amazed at how this game has so many positive reviews. The only positive thing I can say about this game is that the aesthetic was great and managed to create the space horror theme very well. However everything else about the game is either extremely frustrating or lacklustre.The inventory system is probably the worst I have ever experienced in a video game. You are limited to 6 inventory slots to hold your healing items, weapons, ammo, utility items like a flashlight as well as key items such as keycards and so son. The only way to remove things from your inventory is by using an item or by depositing it into a storage box at each save point. Ammo can be destroyed but it is the only exception. You cannot use a healing item at full health, and items are rare so you are inclined to hoard them if you can. This means you will constantly find yourself in the position of being unable to pick up a key item due to having a full inventory and having to run all the way back to a save point to deposit something before returning to pick up the key item. It got to the point where I was actively avoiding picking up resources because I was worried I would find a key item and would have to spend 5 mins running back and forth between the save point. The combat is very simple but has some major flaws. It is inconsistent as to how many shots it takes to kill enemies, sometimes I was one shotting them but the next guy took 3 shots when i wasn't doing anything different.  The enemies can also occasionally respawn which means killing them is sometimes not even worth it and just running past them is the better tactic as it is just a waste of resources to keep killing them over and over. Also, when you are picking up items you have to select 'yes' to confirm the pick up whilst the game is still running in the background. This means trying to run past an enemy to pick something up will result in you getting hit and possibly not even pick up the item. This makes the combat feel unsatisfying and frustrating especially when dealing with the inventory issues above.Puzzles were okay most of the time, but nothing really stood out as being fantastic. One thing that blew my mind was the fact that the devs actually put the answer to one of the puzzles right beside it. Couldn't believe it, completely defeated the point of doing the puzzle.The story is a pretentious mess. I have very little idea who these people are or why I should care about them. The overall plot is hard to follow and you only get vague answers to questions you may have regarding what is happening and why. Some spoilers to follow:  Overall this is a highly overrated game and I would not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Signalis says it's a game, and it does have game-play... but it's lying. It's actually a very traumatic piece of interactive art with a deeply touching story that will make you cry. You'll feel feels you didn't know you could feel. Brilliant work, and a story like none I've witnessed before. The sound design is very immersive, and goes well with the pixel art graphics. Speaking of the visuals... wow. It has that sorta PS1 era horror game feel, but better. I don't know if it's the creature or level design I was more impressed by.Okay, I guess I can talk about the game-play. Combat feels pretty good. The puzzles are all very engaging. The game does have one "feature" that falls short of its goal: finite inventory space. This is a pacing killer, because key items take up inventory space and a lot of them are also required to combine with each other. Several times around the half-way point in the game I got stuck where I couldn't progress because my inventory was full of stuff and I couldn't find a save room. The idea is limited inventory space is meant to make you think about what you carry, but there's a reason similar survival horror games tend to not count key items against you. What this ends up doing is artificially extending how long it takes you to complete the game because you run errands ferrying stuff back to the storage box in the save room.However, this problem is fairly easy to solve, as there's already a mod that ups your inventory size from 6 to 8. I played through the entire game with the inventory size 6, and i promise you're not missing anything if you mod that restriction out. Yes, there is a mechanic where the "zombies" can get back up if you don't burn them, and items that burn corpses are as a result made more valuable because of how much repetition is involved in all the trips carrying loot or keys. But honestly you're already going to make a number of those trips even without the very limited inventory space, so those fire items didn't need to be made even more valuable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... unique, to say the least. I could classify it as a "survival combat puzzler" game. The story is in no way simple either. There are multiple MAJOR plot points which are left intentionally vague, putting it on the player to interpret the story in their own way. While yes the story is "linear" as you will be doing the same tasks throughout every subsequent play-through, if you choose to play multiple times for the multiple endings, every play-through will give you a different understanding of different situations as so many of the plot points are so vague, as said before.If you have any interest in games with complex stories, literary works by the likes of H.P Lovecraft or artworks like "Isle of the Dead" and "The Shore of Oblivion".
