_childDocuments_.review: One of the best horror games I've ever played, if not for being actually scary to me but for the atmosphere and story alone. The gameplay is tight, responsive, and tense. So many really close calls that stood out in my playthrough in regards to managing resources and playing tactically. The puzzles and exploration are fun as well, and often somewhat challenging to think through. The absolute best part of the game to me though is the impeccable world-building put forth for you to read about and engage with. Its so well done with so much lore and secrets to put together and form a cohesive understanding of this eldritch, messed up reality you inhabit while playing the game. Everything about this game just makes it stand out as one of the absolute greatest I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: Man, once in a blue moon something off the radar dips in and grabs your attention and is totally unexpected in its awesomeness. That's SIGNALIS. It's like the first RE games mixed with some System Shock with some Ma.K. thrown in for good measure. It's crazy. The art is top notch and the fact it's mixed in with some Appleseed anime type characters in some crazy Maschinen Krieger universe is throwing me for a loop. Then add in a bunch of German and you've got yourself a crazy good time. Unexpected and awesome.Gameplay is great. It's classic RE style "hunt the rooms" type scenarios for items you need, hunt or stealth around enemies, figure out some decent little puzzles and save your ammo for the boss. Sound design is stellar. Game world is just, wow. The art sells everything in this game. From the story to the scenes to the battles the snippets of information you gather looking at or observing things. Just wonderfully done. If there's one thing that I think knocks a "star" off of this for me is that the enemies seem to be ramped up severely high once you get past the first area. Obviously, you're learning the ropes for the first scenario but after that it's no joke. Use STEALTH as much as possible, use your items that control situations, etc, but whatever you do do NOT waste your ammo lighting up every single enemy you see. It just won't work for you. Still, I'm getting the hang of it and while I do believe the enemies have increased significantly I'm trying my best to work around my own hang-ups with getting the gameplay down with this increased difficulty I"m facing. Still, for a game out of nowhere it sure has grabbed a lot of people's attention, including mine. It's fantastic so far. Also, whatever you do, DO NOT use a guide unless you're absolutely terrible at these kind of games. Using a guide TOTALLY KILLS what the game is asking you to do. Which, tbh, is to use your head, write some things down if needed (your jounal does a fantastic job of keeping everything you see organized), and figure stuff out on your own. PLEASE use the brain you were born with and get through this like a champ.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: I love Sci-fi horror so much this game is amazing. If you enjoy classic survival horror you'll be right in your element with Signalis they nailed it. The art design is beautiful, the atmosphere is intense and unsettling, the music is melancholy/memorable. I honestly can't think of much negative to say just a few small things. The puzzles are tough like you'd expected from the genre and there are plenty of them, but they are well designed and feel satisfying. I'll admit the butterfly room stumped me and I ended up looking it up haha. I saved WAY to much ammo lmao I killed the final boss with like tons of unused bullets in my storage chest and could have killed way more enemies I ran past nearly everything. So don't be afraid of killing things atleast onnormal. The story is little confusing to me and some of the visuals are kinda headache inducing but that's just me. The combat feels like highly refined and much more fluid than other resent retro style horror games it's great. The enemy variety could be better and I would have liked more boss encounters, but what's there works well.  The length and content is spot on as well not too long not too short well worth the money. Overall I should've played this way sooner and highly recommend anyone play this, it's easily one of the best indie horror experiences in recent years. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The 1.2 patch makes two key items take no slots and, if that's not enough for you, adds an option to increase the inventory size. This doesn't address all my following points, but it will make inventory and storage management much, much more bearable. Just get this game.This is a game with some serious flaws and downright stupid rules, but still I can't give it a thumbs down because of how unique and refreshing it is.Be warned the game suffers from poor combat design, some of which seems to be deliberate. Enemies you encounter are all slow zombie bullet sponges that respawn after a while, AND ammo is a whole new level of scarce. On the other hand, healing items are relatively plentiful, so you have to understand very early that in order to beat the game you have to force your way through enemies, constantly getting hit, basically speedrunning through it. This does not make for a fun discovery of the game, as you'll run into dead ends with enemies on your tail, get hit too many times, use too much of your resources and make the rest of the game even more tiresome in the process.It seems the game is intended to be played through multiple times, if only to see different endings and better understand the plot, but doing so is tedious as there will be no difference between runs except knowledge of maps and puzzles. Story alone is not enough for more than one playthrough, .There are a few more questionable mechanics, but it's impossible to talk about them without spoiling anything, so this space intentionally left blank.But in the end, despite all that, I just have to recommend Signalis, singly owing to its amazing and refreshing worldbuilding, atmosphere and storytelling. Puzzles are very well put together and varied, I only wish the enemy encounters were as well. A flawed game for sure, but unforgettable. I hope these new developers acknowledge their mistakes, or better yet, fix them or provide more gameplay settings, and I'm looking forward to playing their next game.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed Signalis quickly  because at one point I stopped playing for the day but was eaten away at by a need to continue and finish it. The atmosphere, the story, the music...I feel compelled to write a review for this game a relatively rare feat for me and I dont even know why. To say its a good game feels like a disservice.I feel compelled to say something, to not let this utter gem of a game to go without a single ounce of the reverence and praise it deserves, but at the same time almost lost with what to write. In some ways maybe to give a game that's going to haunt me for rest of my life an opportunity at closure though I feel the gentle motif of Die Toteninsel is going to weigh down on my soul for a long time.So get it,and one small spoiler free hint... _childDocuments_.review: What I think on my first dive into Signalis:This game is really fun! The story is intriguing, and the puzzles aren't to hard, or too easy. The combat makes for a good break between solving puzzles, so it doesn't get boring.I like how you are forced to conserve your ammo, by having the option to sneak around enemies, or use a different weapon. I learned this when I had to restart 3 times at the beginning because I kept on being careless!What I don't like about the game:The save system is annoying when I only have like 1 or 2 in the entire map, and I have to walk all the way back to it if I am too far away.Enemy re spawning is cool, but the few times it happened it was really annoying because I was either low on health or ammo when I re encountered them.Compared to the rest of the game so far, those are only minor issues. I would highly recommend you play this game.What I think now that I've finished (one ending of) Signalis: (spoilers)WOAH! That was awesome! All I said at the top still holds true, so I am just going to add to what I've noticed here.Story is a little confusing. Not really a problem, probably just going to watch an explanation from someone else. Might also just be because I skimmed through most of the papers. The atmosphere was perfect, and also did well to tell the story.Gameplay was fun throughout, but also got a little lackluster at the end because by chapter 3 nothing feels new. Puzzles on the other hand were the perfect difficulty (for me)! My favorite was the blank card printer.The map layouts got more and more confusing. I had to use a guide once in a while to find what I had missed. Also I think there should've been more healing items and ammo in the later parts of the game because once I had only a small amount of each I could never get it back up.Bossfights were cool, but also kind of felt, easy? I think they were too simple, and could've used one more attack pattern. Also MYNAH reappearing as a regular enemy later in the game made the first fight feel less compelling.Finally inventory management. I actually didn't have much of a problem with it, my only real problem being in the meat hell section and in Rotfront when it got tedious going back and forth from storage box to puzzle.All in all, amazing game, rose-engine! Despite a few issues with finding and moving gear, you nailed the combat and overall aesthetic and feel of the game. Final score: 9 blobs of pulsating meat/10 blobs of pulsating meat.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an experience unique to itself. Music like no other that truly enforces the feelings meant to be conveyed, making you feel them whether you want to or not. Not a traditional "Horror" game of today, more like horror of reality, and horror of the mind. I'm not exaggerating when i say this game stuck with me for weeks after finishing it, making other games pale in comparison do to how impactful it was. 100% a story game at its core, has combat, loot and puzzles and monsters to kill, but if you are here for a run and gun horror shooter where to strive to survive, this game isn't for you, and that's fine, i'm not a story buff kinda person, but this game made me think i'm one, so even if you don't like story's, this is one you should play. _childDocuments_.review: This game left me thinking about it for up to a year after it's initial release. Maybe longer, we'll see. Regardless, it's a solid survival horror title, with a story shrouded in mystery. My personal favorite game of 2022.This game expects you to put an effort into it - in both the act of playing, and unraveling the story. Although the gameplay sometimes shows fault in the areas of a few high-intensity combat encounters and item management (the latter isn't even really an issue after the last update!), the story is an impactful and memorable narrative that kept me fixated even after the credits rolled.What I appreciate about this game is that it allows you independence - gives you enough knowledge of the base game mechanics, and then leaves you alone for the ride. This can sometimes lead to frustration in terms of puzzles on the first time around - it's a wavelength you've gotta find on your own. This extends to the story as well - they give you the most of the major pieces, but you've gotta put them together yourself and fill in the blanks (this is my bread and butter - but it's also not everyone else's, so do be warned).The art style is very evocative of BLAME! and classic cyberpunk-adjacent manga on a carefully considered and tasteful palette. It's hard to go into detail beyond the surface level, but it manages to be visually appealing without compromising the rot of the dystopia, as well as produce some striking imagery.Overall, it's a REALLY strong game. Gets a recommend if you like sci-fi and/or survival horror. And remember - every time you cheat a puzzle in this game, you rob yourself of a eureka moment so intense that you can actually FEEL your brain wrinkle up

_childDocuments_.review: Classic survival horror perfection. This game takes clear inspirations from the early Resident Evil games and especially the Silent Hill series, as well as many other pieces of media. But they are simply inspirations, as the game stands amazingly on it's own with an unparalleled aesthetic and presentation like no other that I haven't seen in a horror game like this in a long time. Combine all that with gameplay that really puts the emphasis on survival, where you will be barely scraping by for ammo and healing, at times even having no option but to run away, and I couldn't have it any other way (Do note that I played on the hardest difficulty and before the inventory update so that may have had some effect on that as well). The story and lore itself is also just as amazing, especially considering how much it's able to show and build up in a short time. It may take some time to piece it all together, but once you do you won't forget this incredible experience. A must play for any person who enjoys this genre.

You could play only the audio of nearly everything in this game and I guarantee you  a Signalis fan would know what it's from. _childDocuments_.review: Signalis is among the best takes on the classic Resident Evil style of survival horror games, striking very high marks across the board for the small indie weight class. The game presents a deep, dark adventure-mystery, tense survival horror action, and beautiful use of retro graphics with lots of memorable shots and original art. Easily a great buy for any gamer and an entry into my personal list of greatest of all time horror games.You play as Elster: a female android and ship's technician looking for her partner/pilot after waking up crashed on an unknown planet, or at least that is what you are told. Without spoiling anything, it becomes clear right away that things are not as they seem and something very big is going on. The game heavily uses mysterious imagery and symbolism to convey its themes of confusion, oppression, and longing. For the most part, I think these ideas all land and help to create the game's dark and moody horror atmosphere, but if you aren't a fan of indirect storytelling, then this game's story will likely come off as trite. Even if it may be overly flowery at times, the core gameplay and presentation is still strong enough to stand on its own.You are a lone adventurer on a dungeon crawl in an abandoned base that has been overrun by monsters. You go around solving inventory object puzzles and logic puzzles while shooting and/or evading monsters with your standard arsenal of various small arms; your best defense being your agility and ability to navigate efficiently. It's all vanilla, but it has a ton of polish. The arsenal is tightly designed and fun to use, the puzzles are actually fairly challenging, and the game nails its balance between horror and action-oriented perfectly. Much of the tension comes from the enemies being a constant threat and also way faster than they look, and much of the horror is of the moody, atmospheric variety with some Lovecraftian horror stirred in. This is all aided by the cold, retro-futuristic setting. Everything is done in analog radios, scan lines, and industrial platforms; even the music, which is also amazing.Tension, running from evil, scarcely armed and bleeding out against an overwhelming threat where everything is going wrong: Signalis is everything a survival horror sci-fi game should have. If you are a fan of the genre then this is likely already a must buy for you, but it's just a good action game overall. If you like retro futurism (or tall anime robot girls), it also hits that mark. In addition, it has a ton of interesting lore for those who like lore hunting. To the developers if they read this: excellent work and a round of applause. Would love to see another game in this world setting or by this developer team. Definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface, a retro-style survival horror with great atmosphere and slightly clunky controls. Very good, but nothing revolutionary. But make it more than half an hour into this game and you will uncover one of the most viscerally emotional stories in the genre. It is beautiful, tragic, horrifying, and will leave you thinking about it long after the credits roll and the tears finally cease. It is not perfect by any metric, but it is still a brutal kind of masterpiece.It would be a lie to say I "enjoyed" this game, as one does not engage with a story like this to enjoy it. But it is now securely in my top three Lovecraftian horror games, and I cannot wait to see what developer rose-engine does next.

_childDocuments_.review: ... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.So, I generally hate horror games. I've actually never played through one all the way through. Until Signalis! Which I binged in three play sessions. It was 100% worth it.This game is absolutely incredible, especially for those who enjoy horror-puzzle kinds of games a la Resident Evil. It does *not* rely on cheap jumpscares, which is something that puts me off of 95% of horror games. Instead, it relies heavily on an incredibly tense and oppressive atmosphere, and a terrifying story. At no point do you feel unable to defend yourself, mechanically, but there's no telling what the hell you're going to go up against next. And that's the best kind of fear for these games!What stands apart about this game, though, is the writing and presentation. It's... really good. Like, really, *really* good. Which is why I got into it despite not typically being a horror fan. This game is oozing with its own distinctive style, with a world that feels both alien and fully-realized. A lot of details are almost subliminal - a flash of some wild text in German or Chinese that, if you look into it, *always* means something relevant to what's going on. You don't have to be bilingual or pull out Google Translate to enjoy this game, don't worry, but it IS there if you want to dig in. That rules.It also just create a great sense that there's so much more going on than what you can perceive, in a way that's far better than the typical Lovecraftian crap of, "oh no, looking at this rock makes my head hurt, that's so scary :(". There is a ton of thought put into every single ounce of this game and its plot, and I'm incredibly impressed by how comprehensively it all comes together, as both a horror experience and a really good story. I'll probably be decompressing this one for a few weeks at least.As for the main plot, it's incredible. Ripped my guts out at least twice. Don't spoil yourself, just go for it. It's worth seeing through to the end, and then further past that.... Man, this game was good. Just play it! Worth it even if you're a person who doesn't typically enjoy horror. I honestly played through the game more because I needed to see it through to the end, despite these games not being my scene, and that's a great testament to what this game is pulling off.A++, highest marks. <3

_childDocuments_.review: (whatever the steam time says, I played Signalis for 4-5 hours)I don't understand the hype. I guess if that's what you're looking for, you'll get it with Signalis, but I was tired of that when I was 10 years old. _childDocuments_.review: Signalis is a game that has taken over as my favorite game, ever.The horror survival genre is one that was built upon games that people nowadays will call "classics". Kings of a genre like Silent Hill and Resident Evil are hard to come by, a game that will be known as PINNACLES of it for years and years to come. This isn't a game that will stand as a pinnacle of their genre, but one that has gone through and written itself a true letter of love and passion for what laid the groundwork of what makes it such an enjoyable type of game. Details upon minor details fill this game to the brim with little kisses on the cheek of style or mechanical references to these giants, and it does so with respect. Not only that, but those with keen eyes and are fans of anime like Evangelion or Ghost in the Shell will catch even notes of those and others similar; creating a theme that feels almost familiar and yet completely alien as you desperately clutch at straws to try and realize what is happening to you. They have built their own unique experience and story that will suck you in and chew you the ♥♥♥♥ up. A hero's story, ruthlessly drowned with eldritch machinations that will make you reconsider everything that has happened to you through the game, and it will ruin you. It's cute and soft at times, teasing you with something lovely to break away from the despair of your journey. But of course nothing good can last, you made a promise. And you will do ANYTHING to see it through... tldr, classic elements of survival horror and horror anime meshed into a modern idea made with love(p.s. play the game, support the devs, they put so much love into this game and it's well deserving.)

_childDocuments_.review: Signalis is a deeply engrossing survival horror. For those interested, I'd give a strong recommendation.What follows is a discussion into themes, motifs and design that I consider .Signalis is significant in its presentation, so if you're convinced, for a truly blind playthrough, stop here.If you are on the fence, or just want to see another person who played it and their thoughts, go on.Signalis taps into an unsettling Lovecraftian story that is for the most part masterfully paced out. It wears its inspirations on its sleeve. Wholly familiar when considering Silent Hill, but unsettlingly unique in world and story. A story always on the cusp of understanding, yet never close enough where the whole picture comes into view.By every metric, it is a game you set aside time to get absorbed into. Dripping with unspoken history, Signalis shows restraint and rarely gives away much, leaving you perplexed— morbidly invested; but never lost in the machinations of its plot.For the squeamish, it never crosses the threshold into cruel, horrific or even morbid  , however it is unnerving and distressing in ways precious few media can match.Gameplay wise, map design is truly excellent, with very sparse points of safety at key areas. You'll come to know map layouts like the back of your robotic hand. Sound design aids well in combat, as the chambering and ejecting of empty shotgun shells ring hollow onto the ground. The combat itself however can lean on frustrating, with some enemy types being essentially immune to traditional firearms.Yet that too served a purpose, pushing me to avoid enemies instead of a purely confrontational approach, and when they eventually went down, I was incentivized to ensure they would As for in depth story, such discussion has no place lost among random steam content, much less a review; it is a disservice to its masterful writing.Signalis earns a spot among the most engrossing, thought-provoking media I have consumed in quite some time, and I don't see it losing its stranglehold on me anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Signalis is a very special game that invokes an incredible feeling. If you've been playing games for a long time, but have certain blind spots in your history of gaming, then Signalis is a special game for someone who has only recently gotten into survival-horror games, and passed over the genre back during its PlayStation golden age with titles like Resident Evil or Silent Hill.Playing Signalis is like being transported back to the late 90s, with sharp angled polygons, dark rooms, enemies with eerie and unsettling silhouettes, and stark music and sound design cutting through the atmosphere. It pays every homage possible to those fabled 90s era PlayStation survival-horror games without getting too caught up in becoming them exactly. It is still its own game, as a dark sci-fi game, playing as a sort of android searching for her human partner in a long and twisted narrative that exposes you to a truly dystopian future among the stars. Making progress means questioning what is even real anymore as you trudge your way onwards with only one goal: find your friend.In terms of actually playing the game, it is as deliberate and spartan as the games it's based on. Gunplay against the monsters of Signalis is slow and calculated, and it tows the line between feeling in control of the situation with careful inventory management of your six item slots and that emotional fight or flight response as you encounter more threats that you can reasonably manage at present. You will be doing a lot of backtracking as you explore, juggling key items for puzzles and precious ammunition, so will you kill what you can to make life easier, or will you sneak and run in order to conserve ammo and health? You'll constantly be sitting on the edge of confidence and fear while exploring the halls of Signalis.I played through the entire game with settings and filters that further still transports me back to a time of fuzzy CRT television screens, blocky polygonal figures, and detailed level designs. I also turned off the simulated CRT filter several times and was still impressed at art design and lighting. Screens and technology pulse with jargon out of my favorite kinds of lo-fi cyberpunk settings, while sudden and abrasive Japanese kanji evokes memories of Neon Genesis Evangelion, intermixed with a unique German language choice that I don't often experience myself.This game is a top contender when I decide on a Game of the Year for the year of 2023 that I played it. If you feel the slightest bit of curiosity for what this game stands for, I implore you to act on that curiosity.

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting game. Love the art style, the switching of perspectives, the music, the tension. For much of the game I felt like it was really good at being neither hand-holding nor infuriating. A little past 6 hours in, there were a couple times I was feeling myself more on the frustrated side of things. But in the end when I found what I was missing I generally felt it was a fair detail that I had missed. A couple things really do have you reaching for a puzzle solution though.  If you're familiar with and like staples of the survival-horror genre; limited resources, inventory management, safe rooms, backtracking through familiar areas to reach new locations, etc. this game might be a good fit for you. Combat can be occasionally difficult and require planning but not to an extent that I've found very punishing - so far I've had one death. Resource management is constant and I've had a couple of tight spots but have never felt like any situation I was in was due to just not being given enough resources. They're there so any time I was short it felt like it was due to my own mistakes.The game is very good at filling you in on new details and gameplay mechanics with either examples or fairly strong hints provided in the environment and notes.

_childDocuments_.review: I struggled to enjoy Signalis. While the atmosphere and commitment to a retro horror aesthetic is seriously commendable, I can't get over how often you get a key to open a door with another key in it. This point-n-click style loop isn’t particularly immersive or horrifying to run around in. It doesn't help that the inventory space is so cramped that the protagonist can't carry their wallet, phone, and keys without leaving their shoes behind. You have to make stops at the item box more frequently than you need to pull out a gun or heal.Signalis’ approach to items greatly hinders the rest of the experience. Keep in mind that you may as well save every time you visit the box. So, whenever you take substantial damage, miss too many shots, or are basically doomed, removing the negative impact of those few minutes by quitting to the menu becomes a favorable option. The need to return to the box and also conveniently save essentially devolves into incentivized save-scumming which thoroughly ruins the experience’s continuity. When the ‘survival’ is made cumbersome and repetitive, the ‘horror’ suffers for it.And, as an aside, it's particularly irksome that the final area . If not for the rampant key collecting and needlessly restrictive inventory, I reckon that Signalis, with most of its strengths lying in its presentation, would've been an excellent extension of its inspirations.

_childDocuments_.review: Very depressing and VERY cryptic storyline, but still definitely recommend it for anyone whose a fan of survival horror. The combat and the puzzles and the inventory management and the level design are pretty much all top notch classic homages to the early resident evil games and others like them. That said, I just want to really emphasize how cryptic the storyline is. Like it really doesn't fully make sense even after you beat it. That being said, I think its very much open to interpretation in a lot of ways and though it doesn't fully make sense even at the game's conclusion, it at least makes a bit of sense more than it does for a large chunk of the preceding game. Just be a bit patient if you're totally lost like I was for much of the game's very mysterious and rather unorthodoxly conveyed plotline.Oh yeah, also the art direction is really interesting. I'm normally not the biggest fan of the classic anime art style, but this game managed to put an interesting twist of it that made it quite alluring to me and added a nice contrast between the aesthetically "clean-looking" characters and the utterly grim and often grotesque horror aspects of the monsters and environments they're all caught up in.

_childDocuments_.review: Are video games art? Are they more than just a method of mindless passive entertainment? Can video games provoke deep thought, can they be an expression of the soul? Can they do this without being confined by the constraints of the medium? Games such as Metal Gear Solid 2 Son of Liberty, Nier Automata, and now SIGNALIS are here to make the argument that yes, video games are a very valid and thought provoking form of art, up there with the best of the arts, be it paintings, composers, and literary masterpieces. Very tight survival horror gameplay that hits the spot between the old school clunk of vintage resident evil, but with just enough modern tweaks that one would expect in the modern day.  On normal the game felt difficult and at times Insurmountable, but never broken and unfair. Be warned if you cheat the answers online you might be able to soft lock yourself. Make multiple saves so you dont get stuck in a resource drained state. The art direction... its unbelievable. There are games more whacky, more colorful, but this game strikes a very dark and brooding tone, without falling into any of the trappings survival horror games fall into, its very hard to put into words but it easily the most visually striking games i've played in the 2020s, and I am one jaded manThe actual graphics are a mix of fear effect psx, with pixel art, with a cyberpunk soviet German tinge of color, with some anime styling in the design of the cut scenes. There are references to classic anime for sure, see if you can spot them. The sound design is perfect. The soundtrack goes between low sub bass rumbling droning notes, to piano crescendos and classical pieces, to complete still silence, every single piece is perfectly curated to elevate the mood. Survival horror games tend to have a pretty typical soundtrack, youve heard one, youve heard them all, but SIGNALIS goes way above and beyond here. Distant lo fi german shouting on repeat, disturbing radio sounds, warble infused,  chorus filled, bit crushed  sounds. The sound design adds so much to this game, youll slowly be trained like a dog, hearing certain ques will trigger responses from you... just for the game to subvert them. Do yourself a favor, get some nice audiophile tier headphones, or some nice in ear monitors (feel free to message me for advice) and lose yourself in what might be the best sound design ive heard in all of gaming. The lack of voice acting just adds to the perfect mood, it really lets you hone in on that sweet sweet sound track, and gives you just enough space to internally ponder. And the visual storytelling? Best in class. You could forgive bad writing here, Signalis goes above and beyond in all aspects that you can expect for it to get away with some campy horror writing... but no, the writing somehow manages to steal the show, its incredible. Without saying much... Hp lovecraft horror meets Nier Automata / Ghost in the Shell existentialism, meets Metal Gear Solid 2 meta narrative, meets classic horror writing. You will walk away thinking about this game for a long time.In 2024, the question is why is AAA gaming dying? Used to be even the most niche gamers could rally with mainstream gaming under at least one title, but current day it seems we get flop after flop, nothing of substance, games with 100's of millions of dollars being used to shovel mindless slop to a consumer base that happily lays their tray to receive the next heaping serving of nothing. Yet Signalis, developed by two people, leaves me profoundly moved, in an existential crisis, feeling empty inside, feeling the true power of what art can do, yet somehow still being a fun and engaging video game. Do yourself a favor, play this. Buy this asap and play it. This is a game that validates video gaming as an art form, and it makes me so frustrated that not many people will give games like this a chance. I say this with confidence, this is by and far the single greatest game ive played since Nier Automata. Its that good.In conclusion Signalis is a love letter to the very best of the survival horror genre, yet it takes all of that influence, and influence from film, anime, literature, music, to become its own thing, and finally ascend survival horror from a trope filled genre of cheap scares and poor game play, into a legitimate work of art.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: If there is a line between inspiration and stealing, then this game crosses it many times, blatantly copying many famous designs, gameplay mechanics and story elements from other games, such as Silent Hill 2, Nier Replicant, Oxenfree or Evangelion (and probably many others). And yet I feel like the game has enough of it's own vision, emotions and stories to share to be considered something of its own. The ending that I got (Promise) left a strong aftertaste, if there was an NG+ with additional content I'd play through game again just to see other endings. This is incredibly solid game for a studio debut, I wish Rose Engine's next game would be as stylish and emotional as this one, but wouldn't rely on/reference already existing stuff so much

_childDocuments_.review: The Gameplay:The game is extremely well designed. Everything is well made, and the puzzles are challenging but intuitive. It is similar to an isometric Resident Evil or Silent Hill game, and it becomes very engaging to solve the puzzles and areas it presents. A must have for fans of either series, or horror in general.The Story:Signalis is a game that wears its inspirations on its sleeve. Blending together Resident Evil's area-puzzle action, Silent Hill's atmosphere and story telling, the visuals of PS1 games, Myst in certain points, Blame!, NieR, and a lot more. However this does not make the game derivative or unoriginal. It manages to use these inspirations to remix imagery and ideas and create something extremely unique and impactful.Everything serves the narrative. The surreal imagery, isolating gameplay, the intense and vibrant world that sucks you in, and the obtuse and unordered storytelling. These elements come together to paint a tapestry of emotions that leave the interpretation of events up to the player. The player is meant to piece together their own reading, which allows the game to be more impactful. It is in my opinion a masterpiece because of the tight marriage of engaging and fun gameplay, with this intense and emotional story. How will you interpret it? How will the game impact you? Play it and find out...Also, I just really like robots :P

_childDocuments_.review: Signalis is a work of art created in an attempt to explore what it would happen if a person became so removed from themselves that they no longer were the same person. The truth is buried beneath Serpinski station, and you, the player, are helplessly drawn in to explore why you see the white haired girl within our protagonist's dreams. All in all, the story telling woven into the level structure, environment art, architecture, and overall methodologies employed by the two authors is incredibly streamlined and focused. All knowledge has been firmly hand picked and curated by the "perfect" language, set up by what can only be described as an authoritarian dictatorship. This government created the beautifully bleak environment you now  inhabit and explore. While I have given what I consider to be a spoiler free initial overview of the setting, this game's story is splendidly sinister and creepy, and I value the internal message exploring the ideas of identity in a more nuanced and cerebral vein of thinking. I highly recommend this experience, but only to those who are not easily startled or disturbed by gore and seeing others in pain. Buy this, play alone in the dark, and see what I mean. Also, click "Continue Without Saving" at least once. Very fun detail from the authors!

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend playing blindly through this game. Don't look up anything about it, just play it and discover the fragments of the story by yourself. I'm glad it was possible for me to play this game without getting spoiled.The story of Signalis has moved me in a way I never thought it would. While nothing about the characters is revealed directly, the player rather discovers information on most of them through notes and other text files. The story and its endings can be interpreted in many different ways. _childDocuments_.review: A gem of a retro survival horror game in the same vein as Resident Evil and Silent Hill. You play as Elster, an android girl trying to find her missing partner in a monster-infested facility after their spaceship crash lands nearby. Suffice to say, things go from bad to worse as she's forced to push further into the depths of the ruins and untangle the mystery what led to the installation's downfall.Pros:+ Tight resource management gameplay: I always had enough bullets to make it through to the next section, but never so much that I felt like I could afford to waste them. Elster automatically locks onto targets in front of her with a clear indicator for when the shot is going to land so the focus remains squarely on managing your ammo rather than testing your aim. Encounters are designed to allow you to sneak past or run away from danger, never making me feel like I didn't have options even when ammo was scarce.+ Great atmospheric horror: The horror of SIGNALIS comes from its well crafted atmosphere and world building. It does an incredible job of fleshing out the locales you visit to make it feel like you're plumbing through the ruins of what used to be a functioning facility.+ Beautiful graphics: Gorgeous pixel art is combined with tasteful lighting effects to wonderful effect. It's beautiful in a "rundown, blood soaked, den of monsters hellscape" sort of way.Cons:- Overly limited inventory space: You're limited to 6 inventory slots for the entire playthrough. No packs to increase your carrying capacity or options in the settings to make things easier. Even when I was running around with nothing but a pistol in my inventory, this led to a lot of tedium in needing to constantly backtrack to collect puzzle pieces out of my stash or ferry all of the resources I'd found back to the safe room. It got especially egregious later when puzzles start to require 6 different key items, forcing me to either make multiple trips or forgo even carrying a weapon. Next time, let the 6-slot inventory schema die on Arklay Mountain with the rest of the zombies.- Later puzzles can get fairly obtuse: Early puzzles are pretty good about leaving plenty of documentation scattered around to give hints on what you need to do. Later puzzles both get more complex and give fewer hints at the same time. There were a couple times I ended up having to look up a guide to figure out what I was supposed to be doing to begin with.Overall, I'd say it's a stand out survival game kept just shy of perfection by what are ultimately niggling annoyances. I'd give it a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: You awaken stranded on a cold alien world, alone and with no hope of survival. The only possible salvation you can find is a warm fleshy pit; a strange red chasm contrasting the ceaseless winter. Even stranger, inside this pit you find a computer, a bed, radio equipment, and most importantly: A book. REMEMBER OUR PROMISEIt has been four days since I've finished SIGNALIS and I have not stopped thinking about it. It's the rare kind of game that haunts you and refuses to leave your mind. Now, just to get it out of the way: SIGNALIS plays really well. It nails the survival horror loop: tight inventories and limited supplies, claustrophobic yet easy to remember environments, tense game play that slowly turns into you feeling like a pro, etc. Really, it's survival horror through and through, not bringing much new to the genre but rather doing a lot of things exceptionally well. Some things of note to me: Stealth is never forced onto you but is instead encouraged by the game's restraint on giving you resources, the 6 item inventory forces you to think about exactly what you should be taking with you and exactly what is worth picking up, and the game's enemies are designed in such a way that most rooms perpetually feel unsafe even after being "cleared" of all threats.So, TLDR, if you like Survival Horror, you're gonna like SIGNALIS.What makes SIGNALIS special lies in the world it's trying to immerse you in. After the prologue, you start the game in Sierpinski-23, a mining facility where something has gone horribly wrong. This place is absolutely incredible. Every room has a purpose and is full of tiny details. The few living characters you meet show how horrifying whatever happened to Sierpinski really was. Notes aren't all masterpieces of immersive story telling, but so many flesh out SIGNALIS' world, tell stories of characters you will never meet, and depict what life was like before the events of the game. For example, you can find two posters for the STAR unit, one being a military propaganda poster and the other one being the same poster but autographed. Upon entering the shooting range, you find that the top three spots of the leader board are all taken by the STAR unit that autographed the earlier poster. This rabbit hole then goes deeper, as you discover more about the functions and flaws of STAR units, and then more as you explore the rooms where the STAR units lived, and even further as it becomes more and more apparent what really happened in this place. This happens a lot. You get small seemingly inconsequential fragments that come together to form an impressively detailed view of the world SIGNALIS takes place in. This method of telling a story in fragmented bits of information is also how SIGNALIS handles its' main narrative. Things don't make sense. Things don't line up. You're thrust into the game with limited knowledge. Time after time, you come to a conclusion based on the limited information the game gives you, only for a new piece of information to rip the rug out from underneath you and force you to reconsider what you thought you knew. It isn't until you enter the last act of the game that you finally understand what the narrative of SIGNALIS is about, and the game is fully re-contextualized into something deeply personal. This narrative is the exact reason I can't stop thinking about SIGNALIS. It struck an emotional chord with me and has been haunting the back of my mind since. Yet, I don't know how to praise it without spoiling it. I can't talk about how it effortlessly side steps ludonarrative dissonance, or how each playthrough the game makes more and more sense which in turn makes the story hit harder and harder. So, the best I can do, is be upfront: the story of SIGNALIS is incredibly rich, it's emotionally impactful, and gives a lot of food for thought. it's a great story on its' own, but everything around it comes together to make something truly special. The visuals, the music, the world building, just the act of playing the game. It's a story that takes full advantage of what being a video game means. Dare I say, the kinda game that is unequivocally a work of art.Here's a bit more rambling praise cause why not: I want to give praise to the soundtrack done by 1000 Eyes and Cicada Sirens. It runs the full range between distressing industrial noise and peaceful melancholic isolation. Eulenlieder is a personal favorite of mine, a track that plays once in the entire game, combining with the environmental storytelling of the room it plays in to create a very effective emotional gut punch. I've alluded to it several times, but the environmental design for SIGNALIS is stellar. It's incredibly easy to forget that you're technically playing a retro throwback game because of how good everything looks. Even when there are areas where the lower poly graphics don't quite do their job, the game cleverly side steps this limitation with fantastic directing and camera work. No place is this done better than in the cutscenes, which combine 3D graphics, 2D animation, and abstract visuals for spectacular results. There are some cutscenes in this game I don't think I will ever forget. My one and only nitpick is that I kinda wish there was maybe one or two more enemies. It's hard to even call it a nitpick, cause I didn't think the enemy encounters ever got stale throughout my playthrough. What's there is fantastic, they're suitably creepy and only get creepier the more you learn about them; one later game enemy in particular is likely to be the source of many nightmares. I also now have the honor of saying "depressing robot game that is the peak of video games as an art form" is my favorite genre of game. Oh and, thank you so much Rose-Engine, I can not emphasize enough how much I loved playing your game.If you're looking for a TLDR: Play this game, you won't regret it

_childDocuments_.review: This game pays homage to classic survival horror games like the original Resident Evil trilogy and the Silent Hill games. The story is both beautiful and sad and really got to me towards the end of the game. The puzzle solving, combat, and resource management are done really well in this game. The combination of 3D polygonal PS1 style graphics with the pixel art-style is amazing and is similar to games like Zeekers (Lethal Company, It Follows, etc.). I would recommend it fully to anyone who is a fan of classic survival horror and wants something unique. I do have a few criticisms though and if you do not want that to spoil your experience stop reading. The game itself is very creepy, has horrific and upsetting imagery and story elements, and makes you feel nervous and on edge during gameplay. That in itself is not an issue, but I never felt scared or terrified by the world. It is still immersive and draws the player in, I just wish some more was done to really make you fear going around every corner. This is offset by the amazing sound design but again, that makes you more uneasy, not scared. Second, the  To avoid this, make sure you  Lastly, the  was annoying to deal with especially with all the other tools you had to sort through. This could be solved by mapping it to a button or key, and it should not take inventory space while on the Survival difficulty. The inventory is quite limited in Normal, and making the modules take up space is annoying while puzzle solving. This is not offset by less items either as I was able to save quite a few healing items and bullets until the end of the final act of the game, though that could be a personal issue that others may not experience.All in all, Signalis is an amazing experience with some replay-ability, great story, amazing puzzles, and survival horror mechanics that forces the player into making difficult yet fun decisions as you navigate the horrors within the hallways along your journey. This game is an easy 9/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit of Lovecraft, a bit of Kubrick, all wrapped up in a liberal sprinkling of anime waifus.The developers did an excellent job creating the game's atmosphere. The game's resource management does a great job at building tension by making the player question for every enemy whether or not it's worth the bullet to remove the threat, or whether it would be better to try and sneak around (and question whether they have the healing materials to survive if stealth fails). This is further reinforced by having enemies that don't always stay dead. They also did an excellent job of world building, teasing out the lore of the world in small doses, revealing bit by bit not only the horrors of the game's events but also the wider dystopia the the characters are part of. The puzzles are... OK. A little on the easy side, but it's not a big deal. You can't have everything.If there is one glaring issue with the game however, I'd say it was the decision to make all of the characters anime waifu girls. I'd definitely consider that a mistake. The somewhat comical nature of the world being filled to the brim with waifus really did more to undercut my feelings of dread more than any other aspect of the game. It also made it difficult for me to follow what was already a pretty convoluted storyline, already complicated by heavy elements of time looping and blurring of the identities between characters, because everyone looked the same to me. Even the ones that were not literally clones.Overall, worth the time if you're looking for a creepy game with strong vibes but are OK with a story that's easy to lose track of.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start ? Perhaps by saying that this game cracked my top 10 of favourites games ? I could but who am I in this world ?Signalis is a breathtaking videogame experience, complete with a simple yet deep and intertwined storyline. Incredible use of both original soundtrack and classical music, beautiful character design and prime example of retro graphics done beautifuly. The game is a top Down survival horror, incorporating the perfect elements of the genre, while never really reinventing them, because it simply doesn't need to.The plot is set in a distant future, a dystopian society where a totalitarian nation employs : Androids created from human neural imprints for labor force, military or space exploration.You play Elster, a Replika unit who's looking for her memories, having apparently lost those. And that is basically all I want to give away, because I really don't want to spoil you anything else.I stand with my inital title saying the game is a masterpiece, developped by two people only, kudos to them for this amazing work, the game is cleverly full of pop culture references and clever nods.From the exploring and uneasiness felt in Silent Hill, to the impactful textual Evangelion aesthetics, the inspirations are numerous, and their codes, perfectly executed.It's a 10/10, you should experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ṛ̷̓͊̒E̸̮͔̪̓͆͛Ḿ̸̢͐̕ͅE̷͖͕͓͑̀͘M̸͙̯͗B̷̨͎̎̃Ę̸̝̅̒R̸̲̘͝ ̷̡̜̈̾͊O̸̘̐͒U̶͈͕͑͜R̷͈̬͉͠ ̶̗̳̥̇̅P̸̧̤̰͂Ṙ̵̡͇̘͗̓O̴̞̓̒M̴̭͚̮̐́I̵͕̍͜S̷̲̾Ė̶̡̫͇Signalis is a phenomenal game. One of the best Survival Horror games I’ve ever played, and this means a lot coming from me, somebody who has played the greats ranging from Resident Evil and Silent Hill, all the way to things like Fear Effect, Alisa and others.If all you are looking for is the endorsement of a fellow Survival Horror fan, here it is. Go play it.Signalis is deeply interesting to me in presentation and story as a german speaker. Not only is the game set in a place that is VERY german in theme, specifically east-german as there are many things that are reminiscient of the German Democratic Republic such as a very GDR-like flag being displayed in the game, along with terminology of the GDR being used (Mainly the use of “Polytechnische Oberschule”, which is the name used for the school system of the GDR).There are also terms that are made up such as “Rationmarks” or “people’s navy”In general, the world you inhabit seems to be ruled by an authoritarian-socialist state very much like the German Democratic Republic that rose up against its former form of ruling, which is simply referred to as “The Empire”. The world is literred with german propaganda posters with striking visuals and messages that evoke that distinct feeling of authority and collectivist-ethos.In fact. A lot of the game will be spent looking at german text: Even if your game is set to a non-german language, you will still see german text in many of the game’s environments or cryptic cutsenes. And I feel that german speakers will get just that tiny bit of edge in their playthrough by being able to understand some things that non-germans won’t.What I also love is the mixture of sci-fi and old analogue technology in the world. Often times you will see quite utilitarian and futuristic environments and technology such as sliding doors, spacecrafts and other things, but with old analog tech sprinkled in such as casette players, or computers that look like they came out of the late-80s to early-90s (One computer you use in particular seems to be an old IBM PC that has an Operating System that looks quite similar to Windows 3.1x or 95.It is such nice presentation and I felt that there was no area in the game that lacked in visuals whatsoever. I enjoyed taking my time and exploring the world and it leaves me yearning to see more of the universe. Though I doubt that this game will receive a sequel.Let us get to the gameplayThe gameplay in Signalis will feel immediately familiar to anyone who has even glanced at a Survival Horror game before: You have 6 inventory slots and several interconnected areas to explore with puzzles to solve.I played through the game on the hardest combat difficulty and felt like I was absolutely just BARELY scraping by at many points in the game. I would have to traverse hallways with little ammo and try to avoid confrontations because a single enemy attack is enough to put you in danger, with 3 hits being enough to kill you most of the time (Note! Hardest difficulty, Standard may be different).Now get this: Enemies don’t stay dead unless you burn them using either a weapon you find later on, or using Thermite flares to burn the corpses of enemies and create safe pockets for you to traverse in. You will never feel as though you are entirely safe and you will NEVER have enough resources to burn an entire area, meaning that you either gotta sneak past enemies or HOPE that they don’t get up off the floor again after your 5th time traversing the area.It is phenomenal and I felt truly rewarded for beating the game this way. The only nitpick I have is that I would constantly have to travel back to the saferooms and deposit junk in the storage boxes as often times, I’d explore a new area, get filled with items that AREN’T key items, and then be forced to deposit them before progressing the game.You will notice that a lot of your time is spent rubber banding from your saferoom, to areas around the saferoom and then back as you grab things. This is a little bit tedious, but it comes with the genre and therefore didn’t annoy me much.Other than that? I had no issues with the game whatsoeverYuri Stern and Barbara Whittman. You’ve both created one of my favorite Survival Horror Games of 2022, if not of all time (Though beating Resident Evil and Silent Hill may be a bit too much of a task :3)You two and everybody involved in the project should feel proud for what they’ve created, Ein wirklich wunderbares Stück Kunst!Here’s to hoping that we see more german developers and their influence in the games industry!

_childDocuments_.review: Top-tier quality survival horror brought to you by Resident Evil fans.Ammo ratio well adjusted : you will have enough but not enough to kill every enemy that you cross. _childDocuments_.review: Intensely gripping with a really compelling story, a cast of characters that will stick in my mind for a while, and a tragic romance that tore my heart to shreds. Extremely close to perfect, but has a few glaring fundamental flaws in it's worldbuilding that make the tone feel deeply confused and the messages muddled. Signalis is a great case study of how having a skewed and deeply biased view of real world history can deeply affect one's ability to craft a convincing work of fiction. The depiction of the DDR and socialism in general in this game reads like that of an 8th grader who bases their politics on having read 1984 once or a mouth frothing conservative ranting about how those nasty commies are comin' for their kids. This completely shatters the tone, especially in a game that (rightfully) takes itself as seriously as Signalis does.8/10 Beautifully crafted and a worthwhile experience, but just keep in mind the fact that the politics of the game, particularly the rabid anticommunism. I will say the telescope DDR flag ♥♥♥♥♥ hard tho. Broken clocks and whatnot. Also Falke do u need a gf.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second time playing this game, first one being from when it was on the pc xbox pass i started this game blindly without any knowledge of what it is besides a silent hillesque survival horror game and didn't had any expectations but Signalis gave me an unique experience of story telling and left a lot of room about interpretation of the story and letting the player chose the way they think the story goes by braking the concept of existence literally giving the same feeling you get while dreaming it is the real world to you until you wake up and that becomes your reality and this ties very well with "a dream about dreaming" , since then i have fallen in love with this game. The art and the story telling are way above the most usual triple A games and the endings left me shattered. It will live rent free in my head for a long time. Truly a masterpiece and it should get more attention.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. 10/10If you like survival horror games like the early resident evil games you will love this.To me the survival horror part (Ammo/Resource/Inventory management) didn't feel too hard or frustrating, just the right amount. Meaning generally you have a good amount of resources if you are somewhat conservant. And even though you are happy to see some extra bullets or health you never feel too pressured that you might run out of resources.It has some clever puzzles that never felt to convoluted but just tricky enough to give you a feeling of accomplishment.The atmosphere feels spot on and keeps you on edge while fully supporting the story narrative throughout the game.  Same with music, lovely soundtrack that fits the mood of the game just right.The story begins kind of slow but then rapidly starts developing after about half the game. By this time you will probably have a lot of questions, which some of them will get answered while others are left up for speculation. Most of the Story is told through textlogs you find throughout the game (with the odd very short cutscene inbetween), and while some might seem unimportant at first, combined with other little tidbits of the story they suddenly create a whole new aspect of this universe. I love games with a story like this, where after the first playthrough it just answers enough questions to leave you hungry for more about this universe. Can highly recommend and i really hope to see more from these talented developers!
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: This game has blown my mind. The art direction is beautiful, and I really suggest taking your time taking the story in and explore: You play as an android with a mission: To find a certain someone. A fair warning though: If you’re a story skipper, or someone who doesn’t like interacting with the game’s environment and reading the notes and posters that are spread around in the game, then unfortunately the story will be kind of hard to piece together. The game pretty much requires you to put pieces of lore together from inspecting the environment, though you can still probably get a vague (but confusing) idea of what /may/ be happening. Lore about the characters and different androids can also be learned from inspecting the environment, and will really have you thinking. The enemy designs and mechanics set the survival horror mood just right. Truly nothing scares me more than walking into a room with a KLBR and having my entire screen barely legible.I’ve been told that this game’s most obvious inspiration is from Silent Hill, which I have not played, so I can only comment on the Resident Evil inspo (which I have played). A lot of the time in this game is spent running back to the safe room to drop off your items. This game has very strict inventory management, which you unfortunately are not able to upgrade (probably inspired from RE1): Six slots, meaning you can pretty much only ever be holding one gun at any given time, especially since gun + ammo + flashlight already means that 3/6 slots are always being used. You will be running back to safe rooms a lot with the enormous amount of key items you will find. This wasn’t necessarily a negative thing for me, but it can be annoying for some people, especially since enemies never permanently die. Great game for survival horror fans, and not too scary for me personally :)
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: This gets close to being very good. There's one major detractor for me and it's SIGNALIS' over-reliance on endless blatant references to other media that influenced it. There are a lot of these in the game, and they're not at all subtle, going as far as to straight up directly copy several shots from shows as an example. References are fine, and I (really) like most the media this game pulls from, but when it does it to this degree it kinda undermines the mood and also gives off a heavy lack of confidence in its own storytelling. I like most everything else about it, bar some nitpicks, but this one aspect does a lot of harm to the rest of the legitimately good things in the game imo, which is a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: It's taken me a while to finally decide to write a review on this simply because this game hits in a way I was not expecting, and I needed to figure out the right words to do it justice. I had not seen or heard anything about Signalis, and picked it up purely because it came across my discovery queue and I liked the aesthetic. I had no experience with the RE style gameplay, but figured it would be a neat change-up from my norm. I was not expecting to become as invested in it as I am now. Ironically, the RE style controls play wonderfully, and once you get used to the limitations, they almost work to enhance the atmosphere by adding an awkward clumsiness to something as simple a firing a gun. This in turn makes something as simple dispatching a normal enemy incredibly stressful, and only adds to the feeling that you are a small, fumbling thing struggling against something much larger than you can understand. I know people will say I'm giving it too much credit, but it just fit so well. Story is where this game hits hardest, The designers managed to convey so much with so little in the way of model detail and texture resolution, and a lot of care was put into ensuring the limited dialogue was only enhanced by the character animation. I don't think I have had a game in recent memory that ended with me needing to just stop and process for a while afterwards. It leaves you wanting more, but still feels complete. It's disturbing, grotesque, will make you incredibly uncomfortable, and I adored every second of it. I know games like this aren't for everyone, and some may be put off by the archaic feeling presentation regarding graphics, but this is a game that will stick with me, and I can not recommend it enough for that alone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been the greatest introduction I could have to the horror genre. Everything works with each other so seamlessly that they all connect like puzzle pieces leaving this absolutely well-crafted atmosphere that feels consistently eerie throughout. I find it's main outliers coming from the beautiful art direction, the sound design, and the story. It's incredible how much a game's visuals can be such a defining part in it's identity. The early PS style chosen for the art direction really helps delve you into its atmosphere helped by the amazing use of color throughout. The music and sound design compliment the art direction so well with providing such a perfect balance between beautiful and straight up terrifying at times. So much of the moments in the game, either it be tender or filled with tension, are elevated tenfold by the music and sound design . Lastly, the story is a masterpiece on its own. Its themes of death, grief, love, and hints of cosmic horror drives the originality factor up by so much and even characters with little or either no screen-time still get a chance to shine and be recognizable no matter. And it's personally amazing to see such a challenging feat be beaten with how much we delve into the main players on the story and explore them with still room for side characters to compliment the world around. And don't get me started on the writing of the Totalitarian nation and it's world-building. Everything about this game is perfect. 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: "None of us are here by choice" The writing and lore in this game is honestly one of the greatest things about Signalis. The gameplay is also amazing and really makes you think about your inventory a lot. Which item do i bring? do i need to bring healing items? is it worth carrying the flashlight with me? Things like this. The core game play loop is inspired by the OG Resident Evil games. With the amazing gameplay, it also comes with a story that you will never forget. Its a story that til this day is still being deciphered by the community. No one truly understands Signalis or its meaning. To me, this is beautiful. SIGNALIS is pure art. The story is beautiful yet terrifying. Its a game that will play with your mind and makes you question everything that Elster (Protagonist) is going through... is any of this real? what happened to the Sierpinskis? where is Alina? What makes us human? If you're looking for a horror game that will mess with you psychologically and emotionally, then I can't recommend SIGNALIS enough.I love this game so much that It caused me to create a video on this game. I've been working on it for two months now and I felt like this was the only way to express how I feel about this game.I will say it... I think SIGNALIS is one of the greatest Horror games ever made... if not, the best.

_childDocuments_.review: So i'll be damn honest. This probably is one of my favorite games of all time.Without delving into too many spoilers, since I want you to play this game fully blind, so you can dive head-first into this horrifying yet beautiful world, here's what I CAN say about it.First and foremost, the atmosphere of the game is absolutely breathtaking. Sure it may be dark and gloomy, but it's of an atmosphere that I rarely see in games. Think Silent Hill 2, but in space, music-wise, and atmosphere-wise.Speaking of the music, the soundtrack for this game is BEAUTIFUL, so much so I ordered the vinyl soundtrack (to which i'll hopefully get mine in a month or two maybe). Composed by 1000 Eyes and Cicada Sirens, the soundtrack sets an absolutely fitting tone for the entire game. Whether that would be dark unsettling moments, aggressive noise in combat, or emotionally charged scenes, every song hits the nail on the head.Now onto the actual gameplay itself. One major aspect you'll notice is how it is VERY clearly inspired by Resident Evil, specifically the early EARLY entries. And like most survival horror games, you cannot just reload infinitely, you HAVE to save on bullets, and use them as sparingly as possible. Here, if you run out of bullets, you're either going to have to look for more, or in the case of further exploration, run past enemies. This, though can be ESPECIALLY grating for those new to this type of genre. Hell, I finished this game on the Survivor difficulty because the game and its atmosphere works BEST in a way that feels authentic, and Survivor always keeps you at the edge of your seat. One more... Meme at this point but major factor nonetheless... You, yes, you, the player, are only able to hold 6 items at a time. An inventory limit is always necessary in games, but 6 feels... Extremely restrictive. Especially considering there may be areas in which you require let's say a number of keys or artifacts that fill all your inventory. Though of course thanks to an update, you are able to upgrade the inventory from the gameplay menu to 8, i.e. a more revised inventory limit (meaning certain items like the flashlight for example does NOT take up a slot). Though of course, that ultimately depends upon what you feel like playing with.Without delving too deep into the plot, I have to say, it is something that once you start diving into, your brain is taking into a space where.. You are basically unable to escape. The lore goes very deep, whether that would be intense, tragic, somber, or just downright disturbing. Surrealism plays a huge factor (hence the David Lynch inspiration on the Steam description page) in this game. And while explicit narrative progression can feel at almost a dead stop sometimes, you are still encouraged to keep going.One final thing I guess I should mention too are the aesthetics. The game may be dark, and it may be grotesque, or industrial, or... Atmospheric, but it also has this otherworldly feel to it, that is honestly difficult to describe in words. The interplay of languages too, like Japanese and German are STRONG here in Signalis. To the point that.. You may learn a word or two here or there. But other than that... This... game, feels like something i'd see in a dream, like something that would come up in my mind during sleep... And.. Honestly, this game feels like reliving exactly that. Of course, everyone's dreams are different, but this game just struck a chord with me.Other than that, I must admit, Signalis is a game that probably changed something in me, of course it may not be for everyone, and it certainly may not be some people's cup of tea. But if you yourself are a fan of survival horror, interesting puzzles, and deep lore, and an overall dark aesthetic, then this is the perfect game for you. You should genuinely try it <3oh, and i just gotta say, gotta love some of cute girls doing cute things in the game.play it, you'll understand :3~M

_childDocuments_.review: Game has his points and I understand why the positive reviews. However, I got bored and disappointed very quickly.  SINGALIS tries to be like old horror games from the 90s (RE1, 2, SH1) but it falls short, it doesn't compare to those great games, even to some Indies that are in the same idea.First, I didn't like the map design, it consists in corridors with many rooms that most of them look the same, feels repetitive. Second, the graphics design are very blurry for my taste, I felt like I was playing a 1.0 AAA adapted game in my Nintendo Switch. There is not eye for details, first enemies design were flat and uninspiring for me, same for the map design.Finally, gameplay could be better even for an Indie game,  aiming during gunplay and using melee weapons feels unreliable, shooting enemies doesn't feel organic, kicking enemies animation is awful, and only 6 slots space for inventory made me to travel back to save rooms  more that I would like it. Anyway, if I could, I would like to give it a neutral review. I prefer Indie games like Lone Survivor, Darkwood or Heaven Dust 2 for example.

_childDocuments_.review: Art is 100/10Puzzles:Puzzles are really really good. Each one feels very unique. Complex enough to warrant going over old notes, using the in game camera, and requiring some hard thinking but was not difficult enough for me to require looking at a guide. Felt very satisfying completing each one.Story:Story is really good and is very silent hill inspired. HOWEVER, there are a few issues I have with the actual presentation. The actual understanding of anything going on is backloaded into the game. Nothing really made sense in a satisfying way until the last like 30 minutes of the game. The endings and some parts of the story are extremely vague so be ready for that going into the game. The world building and the actual meat of the story that isn't vague is really good. The multiple ending system is dependent on how you play the game (hours, kills, non choice based interactions). I don't like this especially because the endings vary wildly in tone.Gameplay:If you like survival horror you will like this. If you don't you will not. A few frustrating points below:- The enemies attack ranges are wildly inaccurate- Slot based inventory rather than grid based (I prefer the new grid based style in new RE and MFN)- If you want to use tech attached to you, you can't use consumables- Maps have to be both collected and explored. For some reason if you get the map it still won't show rooms until you get to them but then there is an area that has no map that you will never fill out. Weird inconsistency that makes that particular area a pain to navigate.tldr if you like survival horror and the art draws you in this is worth trying out but I wouldn't recommend this to everybody as there are some pain points for anyone to really enjoy this

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.  All I can say so far is just: wow.  I have always been a fan of games like Resident Evil but I really am into the more sci-fi stuff than the "zombie apocalypse" or "virus out of control" stuff.  Signalis is a masterpiece.  I don't say that lightly.  I have played for only about 8 hours but I have been obsessed with the lore and watching videos about the game and it's story.  If you have considered giving this game a shot or are on the fence this is your sign to buy the game.  And for the price?  An absolute BARGAIN.  The aesthetic, atmosphere, story and art style are all just perfect.  I truly am blown away.  How this game isn't one of the most talked about games modern times I can't understand.  You NEED to play this game.  Unless you are someone who absolutely hates survival/horror/suspense/sci-fi/etc, I truly believe everyone who enjoys video games needs to play this game.  I hope this studio (another mind-blowing factoid - I think it's just two people!) create more amazing games going forward.  The art style is to die for.  The story is fantastic.  The puzzles are the perfect level of challenging.  I am not an expert at puzzles but all of the puzzles in this game are tough enough to make you think but not so challenging that you can't figure them out.  The inclusion of the radio as a puzzle element is wild.  Love it all.  10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A poetic horror affair. Signalis is a game that won’t let go after you finish it. Its atmosphere is dense and filled with lore and a story, that takes mental work to comprehend. After multiple playthroughs, I still have several questions left, but am also satisfied with having come to my own interpretation of the events, making it a very personal adventure. On a first glance the top-down visuals might appear like common retro visuals, but it is executed with care and attention to detail to create a style that is truely its own. Quality artwork and first-person scenes are only surpassed when encountering some of the cutscenes in this game. Their use of style, pacing, and audio is absolutely special and left me reloading saves just to watch them once again. Signalis takes traditional painting, literature, and music, and weaves it expertly into the moody mix of gritty lovecraftian low-poly horror, bold type design, and anime pixel-art, daring to be an actually unique audio-visual experience.The gameplay captures the survival-horror feeling, including tough inventory management, extensive backtracking, solving obscure puzzles, and dealing with enemy encounters. Different guns and tools have a distinct feel and are fun to use. Combat and interactions can rarely be a little clunky or sluggish, but that doesn’t hinder the gameplay overall. Puzzles stay interesting throughout the game with a mix of deciphering riddles and procuring key items within various unexpected locations that keep the game gripping to the end. The combat difficulty can be adjusted if needed and preparing a pen and paper to take notes is practically mandatory to complete the puzzles. If you can find the time, give it a second playthrough, as it helped me a lot to understand things in the beginning with the knowledge of seeing the ending once before.
_childDocuments_.name: SIGNALIS

_childDocuments_.review: Striking retro aesthetic with low polygon count models and exaggerated aliasing. Finishing the game once allows you to follow the succession of events but understanding what set them in motion and how they tie together requires you to read through many pieces of text scattered around the game. Remember that some people complained when it first came out that inventory management is cumbersome. Although I played it as it was originally intended, I noticed that there's now an option to enable a larger (i.e.: more than 6 slot) inventory. This criticism is purely subjective. I for one don't enjoy conserving ammunition due to not knowing when I might need it. I'm not advocating for including a "guns blazing" playthrough option, but since stealth is an integral element anyway, why not add silent takedowns with a melee weapon? Anyway, at least each boss fight offers you the consumables required to beat it. Although I don't mind any of the endings, the criteria of achieving any one (of three total) in particular are mind boggling: die X number of times, open doors Y times, don't talk to NPCs, etc. Moreover, the secret ending that requires you to engage in a second playthrough looks too underwhelming.
