_childDocuments_.review: *Achtung*That single word, in a language I do not speak or understand, is seared into my memory. It feels as if it was the first word you hear when the game begins, and perhaps heralds all that sets the events of the game into motion. Does this have anything to do with the review itself? Maybe, most likely not. But just know that there will be phrases and moments that will settle forever in your mind and randomly resurface, irrespective of context.Let me preface everything else by saying that while I am familiar with the inspirations Signalis draws from, I have no experience with most of them. I have never played the original Silent Hill or Resident Evil games and as such cannot speak to their influence on the game. But if Signalis is a fair representation of what those games were then boy oh boy am I tempted to give those a go and experience what they had going on.Signalis for me is a game that demands attention and focus. It isn't one you can truly experience or enjoy while listening to something else or half engaged in another activity. The music, the world, the lore, all are granted in small tidbits, leaving the onus on the player to put them together. If at the end of the game you come out like Charlie Day like that famous GIF from It's Always Sunny, then perhaps the game has succeeded in doing what it desired, which for me it did. The world and the story is esoteric, with no definitive answers given save for those that can be parsed by you and other members of the community. I confess, I missed a lot of things, and it was only hindsight along with the aid of videos and discussions that I realised them. So if you feel as if you are not someone who is particularly smart like me, rest assured that it will still be an extremely meaningful experience and there will be plenty of things you will still put together.The core gameplay loop is survival horror, a genre I was up until now entirely unfamiliar with. Resource and inventory management as you run around dark corridors with grotesque creatures is the name of the game, with plenty of puzzle solving. The puzzles were intriguing, and if you're someone with not a particularly strong memory I highly encourage you to take constant notes either through pictures or merely jotting them down.A din of voices has spoken their encouragement for Signalis, and I join my voice to theirs. It is a story of numerous themes, and to reveal them is to spoil the experience. You will notice that I have been rather vague in terms of most aspects of the gameplay, and that is purposely done so. Go in blind, knowing that for the next 6-9 hours you will be going on a journey that is esoteric, sometimes difficult to follow, and extremely engaging and moving. The game is one that I thought I had finished and now, despite the days that have passed since then, I have realised it isn't done with me. This is a game that demands reflection, reconsideration. And even if I never intend to go back and play it again, I do not think there will come a time soon where the experiences I am left with will dissipate from my mind.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not interested in reviews that are front loaded with pretension, so I will try to keep it straight to the point as much as I can.Looking at it strictly as a video game, its fine. Its a silent hill/resident evil clone. Survival horror with the usual inventory limitations that people either hate or love. To me, the inventory management wasn't frustrating. there is minimal backtracking to retrieve items if you take a second to plan ahead. Puzzles were well done. They weren't too challenging but didn't hold your hand either.Looking at it as a piece of art, Signalis is a success. It's a beautiful story about the horror of love. The game starts with one of the best cold opens I've ever seen in any medium. From then on it keeps you engaged as the weird nightmarish reality of this game unravels. Even though the narrative is intentionally obscure and confusing - which many people will understandably dislike - It emotionally resonated with me, which is rare for a video game. _childDocuments_.review: In terms of gameplay, writing, and atmosphere, there is little I can say here that others have not. The art is breathtaking, the soundtrack managed to constantly tug at my heartstrings and leave me in awe, it feels spectacular to play, and this is all wrapped around some of the best writing I have experienced in years. From start to finish, Signalis is a love letter to survival horror that I genuinely could not pull myself away from. I completed a full playthrough in one long day, just before 2AM, because I simply couldn't rest until the credits rolled.Generally, horror is not my typical genre. As much as I can enjoy it, I sometimes find it exhausting to play through. And yet, the emotional horror at the heart of Signalis' storytelling kept me enraptured for nearly 12 hours. Signalis masterfully wields horror, breathless shock, and heartbreak in a rare and beautiful way.Truly, few stories have made me feel the kind of sorrow that I felt upon reaching the finale. And yet I find myself eager to find time for another playthrough, so that I can see it all over again. I'll never get that first experience again, I may not sob over the credits again, but I want more of what I felt over those 12 hours. From the bottom of my heart, I cannot recommend Signalis highly enough. Whether you love survival horror or not, you should play this game. There are generous options for adjusting difficulty, and quality design ensures that even when things are dire, you're never entirely SoL. Give this game a chance, I don't think you'll regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: SIGNALIS starts by following an android named Elster searching industrial sites for a lost human companion. Along the way, reality proves unreliable as identity, physics and recollection fracture. The world depicted is a totalitarian interplanetary regime which ruthlessly exploits human and synthetic beings. Elster served alongside a human companion called Ariane onboard a doomed spacecraft called the Penrose which seemingly became lost to deep space. Much remains enigmatic regarding promises made between the two amidst shared trauma and the true nature of the psychic force called "bioresonance”. But tender bonds endure despite inexorable forces eroding the integrity of their bodies and memories.SIGNALIS is a also a love letter to classic survival horror titles Silent Hill and Resident Evil, on a surface level. But it goes beyond cheaply referencing them in crafting its own unique world and narrative, which has been the subject of much subsequent discussion in the form of video essays and discussions online. The true nature of the story is intentionally ambiguous on some levels, and so those looking for a cut-and-dry linear tale which puts all its cards on the table might be frustrated. But for those who derive satisfaction in delving into the symbolism, decoding strange puzzles, and considering questions about personal identity, what's real and unreal--you may well enjoy SIGNALIS's enigmatic, intricately crafted story. Though it's not necessary to do so in order to enjoy the haunting atmosphere, soundtrack, and familiar, retro style survival horror gameplay.I've been thinking about this game for a long time since finishing it, and since it's simple enough to finish it in well under ten hours, I even played through it again (which is rare for me!). So for these reasons, I can happily recommend SIGNALIS.

_childDocuments_.review: A distinctly modern survival horror story with gameplay grounded in the past in the best of ways.Playing Signalis feels in part like stepping into an old school PS1 Resi game, but with a more polished, nuanced look and vibe. While the polygonal models and pixel art backgrounds and cutscenes may remind players of the past, the distinct clunk and jank in that era is long gone. The low poly models create depth through the intentional animation, and pixel art is crisp where it needs to be, murky and drenched in grime and static elsewhere. The music is suitably atmospheric, and the use of classical piano arrangements paints a haunting backdrop and weight in the cutscenes.The moment to moment action is standard survival horror fare- figuring out proper resource and inventory management in order to navigate the various levels with efficiency and safety, dodging enemies along the way as you work to unlock doors and solve puzzles scattered throughout. It's an intense, gritty affair, choosing what enemies are worth spending the limited bullets you have on, and which you might be better off dodging around. The constant decision making is what makes these games so addicting.The story is murky, and tackles enough topics in its short runtime that I think any given person could interpret both the physical events and their meaning quite differently. This isn't a bad thing, however, as a core tenet of this game is in cosmic horror, a push to understand what cannot be picked apart and dissected, and to find meaning in something inherently more vast that comprehension. In that sense, the story of Signalis is presented as a human fable wrapped in a web of cosmology, which gives you just enough to press forward, much like the gameplay. Everything about this game's design feels very intentional, whether it be the visuals, gameplay, or story. It makes the choice to conceal information, to look fuzzy when it wants, and to give no clear answers on its meaning, because that's what horror is- the unknown. In that sense, I think Signalis may be the best cosmic horror game in recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game on its own, Signalis is a love letter to horror games. Taking much of its inspirationfrom classic (pre-4) Resident Evil and Silent Hill, tensions run high due to low resources and disturbingenvironments.The main character is one of several types of beings called "Replika" -- an artificial cyborg createdto perform vital tasks to maintain a militaristic fascist society. She is an LSTR unit, designedto survive long, lonely missions, which is the source of the strength that allows her to handle thehorrors that she dutifully marches into. As you start, all you know is that she wants to find a womanthat is important to her, and will do anything to find her. But you will soon discover that some mysteriousdisease is killing all of the humans, and turning all of the Replikas into violent monsters. What typeof monster they become depends on what type of Replika they were in life.As you progress further, things become crueler. Environments become more twisted and surreal, and youencounter characters that are breaking down either physically or mentally. Progression is locked behindkey items that often require you to solve puzzles. You may use a cybernetic enhancement tophotograph a keypad solution from another room, fix some broken-down machinery, or receive a passwordfrom a radio transmission. These puzzles are all unique and offer a fun challenge, as well as a welcomebreak from the fear.With the game relying more on anxiety than jump scares (though I did jump once or twice), your resources will run thinas you explore your environment. Once you make the horrifying discover that no enemy dies you have to decide if you want to defeat an enemy and waste your ammo, or just avoid them.And, if you defeat them, do you enter the room again and risk having them wake up, or do you take adetour? The only way to permanently defeat enemies is to use a flare, an uncommon item that will burncorpses. Intelligently choosing where to use these flares is vital to making rooms you frequentlyvisit permanently safe. In the early game I started by trying to defeat all enemies I encountered,but near the end I was too afraid of running out of items, and chose a combination of stealth andmaneuvering to make my way through the game instead. In the end I had more ammo than I needed, but the factthat I severely overestimated the danger ahead shows how well the game did creating a tense, horrificatmosphere.There are no "good" emotions in this game. You'll feel scared, anxious, depressed, sad, and disoriented. And Ilove this game for doing that. You, the player, have no emotional incentive to continue, but you do it anyway.Without giving away too much, I'll tell you that this idea is core to the story of Signalis.If, as you play the game, you find the story to be vague, just remember:

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful return to form for the survival horror genre. For what feels like the past decade the horror genre has been diluted into cheap thrills and jump scares while running away or otherwise avoiding invincible entities that will instant kill you if you fail whatever condition that needs to be met. The survival horror experience of the 90s being swept under the rug with the idea of it being a 'mechanically obtuse' and 'unforgiving' style of video game.Signalis single-handedly blows away any idea that the design philosophy built upon by titans of old (Silent Hill, Resident Evil, Siren, Alone in the dark ect.) has become outdated and unworkable in the current year. From the atmosphere that pulls you in from the main menu, to the area design that seems meticulously crafted, the top-notch puzzles that would make silent hill blush, the varied weapons and enemies to use those weapons on, the fantastic music and a wonderfully made setting that surrounds the entire experience with a beautiful backdrop that eludes to not only man-made dystopian horror but an ever present yet completely mysterious cosmic horror element as well. This game deserves to stand among all the previously mentioned titans of old as an absolute exemplar of what a horror game can be. I can only hope this game serves to be a new generations silent hill 2 or resident evil 2 or siren and helps to usher in a new era of survival horror. At the very least I hope this isn't the last game we see from these very talented developers and story tellers.Buy this game right now.

This is almost exclusively due to the super small inventory size and the outrageous decision to make key items take up inventory space. All this does is create a very annoying sense of padding to the game that, at my age, I just don't have time for anymore.Example:- I clear the East wing, find a key item. My inventory is full, can't pick it up.- I run all the way back to the save point, retreading the area I just cleared of enemies I couldn't avoid, and drop items off in the item box.- I run back to grab the key item, but now the enemies I had previously killed come back to life (you can't actually finish off enemies, at least in the early parts of the game, they revive after some time), and I have to waste more ammo or get hurt because the corridors are so small you literally can't avoid the enemies in many cases.-I get annoyed, because if key items didn't take up inventory space, or there were more inventory spaces bare minimum, I wouldn't be retreading the area I already cleared.I believe it's actually a pretty good game, but I'm getting older and I don't have time or patience for frustrating padding in games anymore. If that type of thing doesn't bother you, the rest of the game seemed really well done.Devs, I may be in the minority here, but nostalgia only goes so far...not every trope from the past was a good one. Silent Hill had infinite inventory, and just made weapons and ammo scarce overall to achieve the same effect. That's the objectively better way to do horror without padding out your game. Please consider that for future titles.People are free to disagree with me. I've beaten most RE games (besides REZero, for the same reason as this one), Silent Hill 1-4, and Tormented Souls, so I'm very familiar with the genre. Still, most of those games gave you more space or put quest items in a separate spot. Games aren't supposed to be annoying. 20 years ago, you only had a few games to choose from, so you would deal with the annoyance. It's 2022, I have thousands of games to choose from (most people have hundreds or thousands of games to choose from at any given time), and just don't play games that annoy me.TL:DR It's a pretty cool game; if you aren't bothered by tedious backtracking as a principle game-play element, I would actually encourage you to buy it. Steam doesn't give me a neutral option so it's a "no" from me, dawg.

_childDocuments_.review: SIGNALIS is a beautifully crafted psychological thriller and survival horror game, heavily inspired by the old PS2 era horror games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill 2. I cannot find adequate words to describe how much I love this game and its story without revealing what makes it so special. If you are reading this review, and youre considering to play the game, I strongly encourage you to stop reading reviews and try it for yourself. The less you know about this game, the better. Story aside, this game is mechanically smooth. Combat is simple and fluid, and you're almost always given enough resources to handle whatever challenge is at hand, so be creative and don't fret over every mistake. I recommend using your backup saves, exploring, and keeping a notepad and pen by your side. Some of the puzzles will require some problem solving and critical thought; but nothing should be difficult enough to require an external guide or walkthru. I believe the atmospherics, story, and artstyle that this game provides is beautiful, unique and well executed; and as a result, this game is on my list of all time favorites. Its very much worth its full price, and I strongly recommend playing it even if youre not a fan to the survival horror genre.

_childDocuments_.review: A good survival horror game with big inspiration from Silent Hill. It's incredibly easy to get immersed into the atmosphere created by the aesthetic, art direction and world building. Where the game goes south for me is the combat and enemies. I understand it might not be the main focal point of the game but it really soured my experience. So many times playing this game I just kept questioning why I wasn't given more ammo. I understand that I'm supposed to be selective with using it, but due to all the backtracking that you have to do in the game due to receiving pieces or information that can solve a puzzle for you elsewhere, you constantly run into all the enemies. This wouldn't be a problem except the enemies consistently respawn unless you burn their bodies with an item. The majority of the time I would find myself running by enemies or leading them one way and running past them just to get past the room (where I've already spent tons of ammo to kill them before). The movement and combat overall just felt incredibly clunky, especially those terrible mini-boss fights.The 6 item limit might not be a complaint for most people but to me it just felt way too low. With all the running around you have to do and switching out of weapons because ammo is so scarce you would constantly have to leave items behind or make multiple trips to the storage box which is just annoying, coupled with the flashlight which really made it feel like you only had 5 slots.Most of the puzzles were pretty cool and well thought out but honestly wish they were harder. I would've loved to really dig deep and get stumped on some of the puzzles because a lot of them had the potential for that.Overall still a really cool experience for about 10 hours of gameplay and would still recommend just for the art direction.

_childDocuments_.review: You may be in a state of shock by seeing a negative review for Signalis seeing as it is so well liked in not only the reviews on Steam but also in the general gaming media. The truth is that I do not hate this game and I did have some fun with it but there are a few things that annoyed me and these are as follows -1) The 6 item slots created a lot of needless wandering around in the game. By the time you equip a gun and an attachment, some ammo and maybe a healing item, you're left with 2 slots to pick up key items (or consumables). I started forgoing carrying a healing item which helped but I think it would have been nice to upgrade the inventory especially towards the end of the game.2) I enjoyed the way you interact with the puzzles, however I ran into an issue that some of the solutions for the ones that required memorisation of a pattern were pretty much unsolvable unless you took a photo with your phone of the screen. I ran into this around 3 times. I will admit that maybe I missed something obvious in retrieving these clues from the game so perhaps don't read too much into this point but I'll level with you in that I am an experienced games player (I hate the term gamer :-)) 3) I almost missed the last part of Signalis as the credits rolled and it chucked me back at the title screen. It was only when I looked at an FAQ to see if there was any hidden stuff that I found out I needed to go back into it. Some people may think this is cool but I thought it would have been better for the credits to roll and for it to continue and overall I thought it was rather pretentious.  4) When there are 3-4 enemies on screen all coming after you, it is very difficult to aim at alternative targets other the the one closest to you. I kept dying a lot because of this and it was the final nail in the coffin for me. I quit and uninstalled in the middle of chapter 3.Like I said at the beginning of this review, I don't hate this game and I did get some decent enjoyment out of it but in my opinion, it is nowhere as good as other people make out. I guess that's just hype culture gone wild. The bottom line for people looking to buy Signalis is that if you feel any of the above points would affect your enjoyment of the game then I would suggest spending your money elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I seriously need to stop taking what anyone says on the Steam platform seriously when it comes to their reviews on games.I'm going to refund this.This is not an enjoyable game. It's not stressful, suspenseful or scary or anything like that, it's just not fun. I don't even find it to be all that interesting. I'm not compelled to want to know more about who these robots are or what they're doing. The game doesn't provide that for you in any sense.Nothing is voiced. Everything is delivered to you by text. This isn't a dig, just a heads up.Story is practically non-existent, which seems odd as everyone seems to be gushing over it. The elements of story you do get are fragments and don't serve to explain anything. I'm nearly 2 hours in and I still have no idea who anyone is, why any of this matters, where I am, how I got there or what I'm supposed to be doing or accomplishing. I think the MC is looking for their robot partner (or lover?) who I have a picture of (this takes up an inventory slot btw).There's no mystery or tension, just a complete lack of information of any kind. You're told (never mind shown) nothing. There's no wondering if you've been led false, or missed something, there's nothing to miss because there's nothing to find. Just another door to open.I've been teleported around to completely new areas 3 times already and I'm not sure if these are events that happen before, after or concurrently to anything else that I've seen, experienced or completed before. I've never really encountered story telling like this, and I don't like the style at all.You have to back track constantly to pick up items you left behind because you only have 6 inventory slots and tons of keys to pick up. This only serves to pad the amount of time you spend playing the game. Doesn't make it fun or challenging, just annoying. Much worse than any Resident Evil game, and they're some of my favourites (not Village though, that was pretty bad). Generally inventory management doesn't bother me too much,  but it's fairly egregious here.Every key serves as a method of opening up the way to the next key, so the entire game is finding key A, opening the door, then finding key B, and opening a door, then finding key C and opening a door and on and on and on while running down a bunch of hallways. Sometimes you'll find a note explaining some part of the puzzle (to get the next key), a technical manual, or a small fragment of story that you'll have to keep mind of so that you can attempt to put it all together later (maybe?).RE is similar in a lot of ways, but does a much better job of masking the fact.With this game, you pick up on it immediately and there is no masking or filler. It's one key and then on to the next and then on to the next with nothing in between.If DayZ and Death Stranding are walking simulators, then this game is a door opening simulator and perhaps I'm just getting tired of door opening games of this variety. Alien Isolation was the same and I couldn't stick with that one either. I'll have to think about that. I certainly expected better (and more).There are essentially four item varieties: weapons, their ammo, keys and medical items. You have to juggle these constantly. Enemies do not stay dead. They will randomly revive and attack you again as you back track through any particular area for the third or fourth or tenth time. Ammunition is extremely limited. There is no skill in terms of killing enemies. No head shots, no limb shots. You either miss them via poor aim or you don't. There doesn't appear to be much enemy variation. They all look the same to me. The low resolution art style doesn't help with this.Every gun has a laser so it's hard to miss if you're patient which is good because it takes quite a bit of ammunition to bring down any enemy. Avoid them whenever possible.You can hold shift to run and sort of lead them around the area if it's large enough but you'll be doing this CONSTANTLY. Hope you enjoy it because there will be a lot of that. More of that than anything else I'll wager. I doubt the game loop changes much as you go through the rest.I spoiled something for myself by googling what the diagnostic screen meant in the documents/radio tab. Don't do that if you want to keep it a mystery. Just ignore the diagnostic screen entirely. The dot will move after you get injured but appears to recenter itself after some time. I have no idea if player actions have anything to do with that, it's a possibility.Thanks for the accolades, it really means a lot.It shows me that you took the time to read what I wrote if nothing else, and I appreciate that.If you're mad about my negative review, and you're providing them ironically, sorry I didn't like your lesbian robot game (I'm not).

_childDocuments_.review: SIGNALIS was a shocker for me, I went in with zero expectations and was pleasantly surprised by a well-crafted story about love in a dystopian world of horrors. Much has been said that bears no repeating, so I'll add some fair criticisms to keep in mind before you go in.The game suffers from large amounts of backtracking. Even with shortcuts opened, you'll be constantly running back and forth delivering puzzle pieces as you struggle with the intentionally restrictive inventory. The developers wisely kept this in mind and made it so enemies could revive after some time, keeping you on edge even as you run through familiar grounds. But be aware that at some point tedium will set in as you ferry items back and forth, just wanting to get it over with and move on to the next section.On gamepads, I found aiming mechanics less than ideal - too often the targeting reticle will stick to an undesired enemy, making it hard to choose and prioritize targets. The target reticle also has difficulties with enemies that are too close, something that happens more often than you'd imagine.There are ample photosensitive warnings, please take them seriously as there are quite a few flashing screens. Non German speakers will also lose on some of the writing in a few of the more chaotic scenes, as they are written in the developers' mother tongue and some of them add, in my opinion, important flavor to the game. The game has a very German brutalist influence, after all.The game also requires active participation of you in order to glue all the story bits together, it'll be on you to form your own narrative interpretation of the game and its different endings. While some of it can be presented somewhat obtusely, it shouldn't be hard to form a pretty good picture of what's happening.A moody game that requires patience and participation of the player, the reward is an engrossing game that left me wanting more, washed over by intense feelings of desperation, loneliness and confusion, but also determination and love. Equal parts Dead Space and Resident Evil, SIGNALIS is worth playing, but more than anything, it's worth .

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that like many other reviewers have mentioned throughout steam: I wish it had a middle choice.I had signalis on my radar for awhile, and intentionally stayed rather blind to what the game was about it. The game starts out pretty strong and enjoyable with inspiration from games like Nier, Resident Evil, and Silent Hill. The problem I have with this game, is that as the game continued to go on, it took TOO much inspiration from those games.While the story is enjoyable, initially, a machine finding her human female companion, it felt like a muddled mess at times that tried to be very unique and play the game from a backwards approach to what was going on the entire time. That, and the story doesn't feel all that special when you realize how much the game borrowed from other games. Tons of environments are about growing flesh, areas that are very dark, metal cages on enemies like silent hill, environments made of nothing but metal that are dark and seem satanic in origin, small inventory spaces, retro type styles and resident evil aiming, the multiple nier type endings that only tell you part of the story until you play it again and again, etc.Then you have other issues that just added to the mess for me: The 6 slot inventory that is incredibly annoying because of how many items they attempt to give you. This requires you to run back to your storage over and over again just to be able to keep up with the required items in the game. They also have you kill enemies with guns, but the enemies never truly die unless you use, you guessed it, ANOTHER item in the game that only has a finite amount causing you to be very selective where you use it.The game also heavily uses puzzles, but it just does that to prolong the extent of the game. You find yourself going into 3 ?different areas, to find 6 different items that you have to navigate through tons of keys, pots, items, all in your 6 slot inventory, to be able to unlock a new area to do it all over again in order to further the game.The game is just too much for me. While it does appeal to a niche group out there, it just isn't for me and I wasn't having fun with it. If you want something different or takes heavily from those type games, and only pay $20, you'll get some enjoyment out of it and your money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I was extremely hyped for this game ever since the announcement trailer back in 2020, simply because I saw The King in Yellow (which happens to be one of my all-time favorite books). I was slightly worried it wouldn't deliver, but it completely blew my expectations out of the water. Music aside this was essentially made by two people and they delivered in spades.  I can safely say this is one of the best survival horror games I've ever played. I don't want to say anything about the story because I feel like it's best experienced with as little prior knowledge as possible.  I'll only say this: If you like any of the following: cosmic horror, retro tech sci-fi like Alien, Silent Hill, Tsutomu Nihei and old-school  cyberpunk in general, body horror, plenty of lore and a story you'll have to piece together yourself which is also open to interpretation, then you should buy this sh*t ASAP because you're in for one hell of a ride. There are multiple endings based on how you play the game (similar to Silent Hill 2) + a secret ending, so there's plenty to enjoy. I adore how SIGNALIS looks. It generally goes for a PS1 look, but instead of just slapping together poorly looking models that tend look worse than what was on the actual hardware like most attempts I've seen, there's genuine effort put into its style and the result is gorgeous. My only real criticism is with the in-game CRT shader. I wanted to use it so bad because it looks great, but the forced curvature creates weird artifacts on the sides of the screen at 1080p (for whatever reason they don't show up on screenshots) so I ended up using ReShade instead. If you like Akira Yamaoka's work on Silent Hill you're in for a treat. The sound design is excellent and creates an amazing atmosphere that really gets you immersed in the setting. There's no voice acting, but I don't really think the game needs it. The soundtrack is by Cicada Sirens & 1000 Eyes and its pure perfection. I'm setting aside some shekels from my next paycheck to buy it, I need it in my collection! The game plays like a mix between the RE1 Remake (Chris scenario) and Silent Hill, but from an overhead perspective (with a few exceptions). There are even optional tank controls.  Your inventory is limited to 6 slots and everything you pick up takes up a slot, so it's up to you to decide what to carry with you. The save rooms are very much Resident Evil. No ink ribbons here though, you can save as much as you want. The enemies are not particularly difficult to fight, but there's a lot of them and you have nowhere near enough resources to deal with every single one. You can save a few bullets by kicking them once they are down (like you can in Silent Hill). Similar to REmake they won't stay down forever and will eventually get back up. The only way to get rid of them permanently is to burn them with flares or a flare gun you find later in the game. Keep in mind that said flares are rare, same with ammo for the flare gun, so you'll have to plan accordingly. Resource management is key, like in any proper survival horror. Grab a pen and paper for the puzzles, most of them aren't particularly difficult, but you'll need to take notes for a few. Use the radio. Overall it's exactly the kind of gameplay I want out of my survival horror games and I have no real complaints. The only minor gripe I have is that the difficulty setting was in the options menu and I completely missed it the first time around. Next run is on Suvival difficulty for sure. SIGNALIS is easily one of the best horror games I've ever played. It makes good use of its inspirations while creating its own identity. Loved the story, loved the visuals, loved the audio and the gameplay was exactly what I wanted it to be. For a mostly two people project it's an absolute masterpiece. Go buy it, it's completely worth the 20 bucks and the devs deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: Signalis is one of those games I have to take the time out of my day to write a review for, because it's that good. Despite this, my comment will not be as sophisticated as others who go out of their way to analyze everything that makes up the game in detail. Instead, I'll be giving you a more watered down version. The following is of course, my biased opinion. Because I ADORE this game.While it adds no credibility to my review, I want to note that I have beaten this game exactly four times. Three runs on the normal difficulty, one run on the hardest. I have done my own speedrun of it twice. I clocked in at around 3 hours and 15 minutes for my fastest run but I have no doubt that you can go lower. Now, if you're totally fresh to the game, your first run will likely take you around 12 to 13 hours if you take your time to try and explore all that you can find. If you go for EVERY BIT OF CONTENT the game has to offer, it will take you a total of around 35 to 40 hours. That said... I will attempt to gloss over some of the finer points to this game.The story. It's there, and it's perfect. You take the role of LSTR-512 "Elster" who is on a search for her girlfriend, and you'll DO ANYTHING to find her. There's only one catch. Will you remember your promise?That's as far as I will go into the main story. As for the world itself, it's mind-blowing. Why? Because the world has been built with such fine detail and you get to learn so much about it in such a short span of time. That in itself is stunning to me. There are documents, journals, letters, pictures, and posters, strewn throughout the various places you visit that help fill in the blanks. The game tosses you in with nothing, but by the end of it, you understand your place as Elster in this universe. I could go on about the world building, but it's not an experience I want to take away from anyone reading this review. Just know that if you take the time to get into everything that makes up the world of Signalis, you'll be in for a fun ride. There's enough material to make a book or a short anime, honestly.The soundtrack by  and  is phenomenal, and I highly recommend a nice pair of headphones to help immerse yourself within the world. The tension of attempting to slip past enemies undetected. Hearing a scream as you're spotted before you frantically fire off rounds at the threat. The music kicking in as a heart-thumping chase ensues. The discordant cries. The sound of something bashing against the door you're hiding behind gradually fading away, after you barely made it into the safety of another room. It's tense, sometimes even nerve-wracking. I don't think there's a better way to say this, but the dichotomy between music and sound effects is masterfully woven into this game, in such a way that the two end up complimenting each other. It makes for a terrifying atmosphere, and creates the 'Thank God' moments when you make it to a safe room.  and  really nailed it with the sound design.I have a habit of exploring every nook and cranny during my first playthrough, so by the time of my second playthrough, I was familiar with the layout of every map and knew precisely where to go. This speaks wonders to me. This might sound silly, but the level design isn't just 'level design' in Signalis. It's also a . Since it ties into the story, I won't explain any further than that and leave you to interpret what I mean on your own. I will give you a hint though. Some rooms previously locked do open, allowing you to see- and understand things- you were unable to before. You'll find that locations have been constructed with meticulous amounts of care- and love, too, with exceptionally well-done in-game models that match the theme of the world: Eurasian cold war retro-tech sci-fi.I absolutely LOVE pixel art, and by God is the art in this game EXCELLENT. I stopped mid-gameplay often as I was captivated by the dozen or so posters you can find within the game.I used a keyboard and mouse. Had absolutely no problems. I don't have much to say on this other than that the movement is clean and precise with actions being responsive. You hit a key. It does the thing. No 'jank' from my experience.If you want a classical survival horror game experience, look no further and pick this up right now. This game is a gem, and I hope some big Youtuber picks it up and draws more attention to it. HUGE thanks to Yuri Stern and Barbara Wittman for such an extraordinary experience. I'm not even one for horror games but the art drew me in, so I gave it a try, and I don't regret it. I only wish that there was more, but it's only normal to want more of something this good.Some areas of game design I failed to be as thorough on in my review, so I implore you to check out other reviews that do a better job. I felt the need to touch upon a little bit of everything for the love I have for this game.Orrery, The Red Gate, Memory, Troublesome Creek, and Warm Light are some of my favorite soundtracks from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When you have a story that is trying to do high concept things while dipping into surrealism, there is a very fine line to the writing in making it succeed. Many, in fact most, works don't do it. They either let the concept get away from them and it descends into meaningless nonsense, or they're not brave enough to push it as hard as they could have and it just becomes a bog standard story with some gimmicky imagery.SIGNALIS is one of the few games that pulls it off, the whole way through. Up there with the best of them, and not just compared to other survival horror games. Precise, clever, thoughtful writing, no more and no less than exactly what's needed, in a story that absolutely stabbed be personally in the heart. Truly the top of what this medium is capable of.Also it plays really nice too!

_childDocuments_.review: GOD I LOVE WOMEN WHY CAN'T WOMEN BE REALnah but really, a fantastic game. You go in with 1 or 2 questions, get halfway through with 30 and then end with 4 questions answered and 86 left unanswered. The game's atmosphere and characters really sell you the entire time of the feeling of hopelessness. Never once when i was playing was i thinking there was a light at the end of the tunnel for anybody. There could've been, but who knows? I highly highly HIGHLY recommend playing this without a guide, and completely spoiler free. The experience is enhanced tenfold from it. Use a guide if you're stumped for awhile on a puzzle, but try your best to stay away from them.  The gameplay as expected is much like Resident Evil, with Areas you go back through, inventory management and a helpful map with room and door statuses to help you navigate. _childDocuments_.review: What a game. Great as a homage to PS1-era survival horror classics, honorable to its many aesthetic inspirartions, and stands firmly on its own in just as many aspects. The atmosphere and tone this game creates is peculiar in terms of how it balances cosmic mysticism and hard sci-fi groundedness. Well-crafted ambient soundscape helps a lot - from the most melancholic save room theme since original Resident Evil 2 and 3, to a thoughtful utilization of in-game short-wave radio stations ("number stations" as they are known in IRL popular culture). This game fully delivers on a _promise_ of a modern take on classic survival horror. Hats off to rose-engine.

name: Blightbound
detailed_description: The world lies in peril. Decades ago, a band of legendary warriors slayed the dreaded Shadow Titan after a long and ferocious struggle, but their celebration was short-lived. The Shadow Titan’s true intentions revealed themselves when from his broken husk flowed the Blight; a corrupting fog that alters any living creature exposed to its evil. Blightbound is a multiplayer dungeon crawler that tasks three heroes to venture down from their mountain refuge to face the abominations of the Blight - a mysterious and corrupting fog that enshrouds the land. Explore handcrafted dungeons, fight a terrifying cadre of mystical and monstrous enemies, grab valuable loot and recover fallen heroes to expand your roster of available warriors. Each player will fulfill a specific role on the team - warrior, assassin, or mage - to overcome colossal bosses and solve clever puzzles. Can you collect and complete all the challenges, and conquer the Blight once and for all? FEATURES Blightbound is an ever expanding game with new dungeons to explore, new heroes to recover and use, and new loot to retrieve with planned free updates for the community. Collect unique heroes, each with their own skill set, passive abilities, and fully narrated story to complete. Hundreds of unique items to loot and craft to improve each hero and alter their repertoire of attacks and abilities. Build out your refuge atop the mountain by recruiting new artisans to craft more items, fulfill bounties, and training your heroes. Battle through three distinct lands, each with several dungeons to conquer, including the eerie Gravemark, the oppressive Underhold, and precarious Blood Ridge. Distinct class roles that reward team play and powerful ultimate abilites that charge from fulfilling your role. Block damage as a warrior, interrupt enemies as an assassin or heal your allies as a mage. Stunning mix of hand-painted characters and realtime 3D models and lighting effects.

_childDocuments_.review: 15/11/21 Update. Just a note to say my review below related back to the game in July 2020. The game has changed a lot since then, and although I haven't had a chance to play it in the current state, the devs (as have messaged below) have removed my main issue with the game - the notoriety system. I did have a lot of fun with the game when I first played, so please don't let my review below turn you off if it piques your interest. -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Original review - preserved for posterity.Sadly, this  game just isn't ready for EA and has some core design issues.My main gripe is the notoriety system. In a nut shell, you complete a mission with your group, your notoriety increases and with higher notoriety comes harder difficulty dungeons and better drops. Sounds good right? Well, there's one flaw...Notoriety is TIED to the group and resets when the group changes. So if you're not playing this game with friends and a dedicated premade, and instead using the match maker system you're never going to see the harder difficulties and will instead be forced to play the boring level easy mode content again and again and again. Solution? Notoriety needs to be tied to the individual and not the group. Everyone should havea personal notoriety rating that increases when you complete a dungeon.

_childDocuments_.review: Not very far in, but I'm genuinely confused as to what the hate is about.  Seeing lots of complaints about not having a single-player mode, which is false (though the "Play With Bots" button is maybe a *little* difficult to see, and the opening menu options of "Play Online" and nothing else should maybe be reconsidered from a user experience perspective).  I can charitably interpret that as wanting a mode where you don't have to collaborate with the bots' questionable AI, and if that is what you want, then I guess this probably isn't the game for you: The role-asymmetry is baked pretty deeply into the design, and it doesn't seem likely that such a mode was actually being built for.  At the end of the day, this is a game with multiplayer dynamics, so pick one: A) play with friends, B) play with randos (and deal with slow matchmaking), or C) play with bots (which act like friends but are kinda dumb).Beyond that, the inter-mission RPG mechanics seem fairly compelling, the art and visuals are well done, and though I see lots of hate about bugs here, I have literally encountered zero of them.  Maybe they've been hotfixed, maybe I'm just lucky, grains of salt, etc.I'll update if I am shocked by some negative revelation, but right now I'm liking this game quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Development for this has concluded.  It was a potentially great game, weighed down by what seemed to be sheer neglect.  I don't know if they never funded it much to begin with, or if the team was spread too thin, or whatever other variables kept them from properly making this game.  What it comes down to is that this game is worth half it's asking price at best, IF you get a full party to play it with.  Since it will never improve from this point onward, I recommend you never buy this game.  A non comprehensive list of reasons why:Buggy.  To this day, spells that freeze enemies in place will sometimes make them invulnerable.  Combat cannot be reset and you cannot leave areas without finishing combat.  Due to this mix of bug and game design, your run ends without rewards.  This is one example of the way bugs and poor development will interact to cause you nothing but frustration and boredom more often than I find acceptable.  Bad bot AI:  Not much to say here, the bot AI is pretty garbage.  It's not even just lack of combat effectiveness or inconsistent behavior, sometimes they just don't do puzzles.  They'll kind of try, and then break.  If you're lucky enough to be able to leave the area and come back you might get it working, otherwise you just run around and hope the AI eventually finds the one KB of memory it's sharing between itself and every other piece of code the game has poorly slapped together.  Unrewarding loot/progression:  Most playable characters are just barely different reskins of other characters with maybe 1-2 different abilities, but ultimately behave extremely similarly if not exactly the same.  Gear drops seems to be pure RNG(Can't attest to whether it actually is, but the important part is it FEELS that way), you can hop between shop and running missions and almost never get anything good, fun, or exciting.  Worst part is you must play a specific class to get upgrade mats for that class, so you can't boost alternate classes up to a point where you enjoy playing them without slogging through the crappy part of them, making you repeat easy and endlessly replayed content even more just to progress certain things.  Poor overall design:  Things that are hard to quantify without making me go back in and waste my time replaying this/things that may be more based on just my opinion go here.  Movement can feel off, the way projectiles often skim by opponents that seem to definitely have hit or at least nicked them, the randomly generated maps have almost no variation and thus are actually worse than having them set(if they were always the same they'd be just as boring but I could at least speed run them for more efficient progression), cooldowns are very long without having anything besides running around to do while you can't cast/attack(could add more AOE or environmental hazards/damage that you could have to avoid/use against enemies while stuff is on CD for example), story is boring and nearly nonexistent, forcing players into tank/phys dps/mage party structure is insulting and definitely done to make balancing the game easier on the devs who seem to have done nothing with most the time given to them, etc etc etc.There is a few hours of fun to be had here if you have nothing else to do and want to play a game with ONLY 2 other friends(3 people is max party size, less means dealing with the terrible AI) and if you find the game on a steep discount.  After my 10th ruined run due to crashes/disconnects/run ending bugs I decided 5.4 hours was enough for me.  It's not my job to make this game enjoyable to play by working around these obstacles, and the devs have decided it's not theirs either, so it looks like no one will be here to take responsibility for this mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Thats an honest review, if the truth hurts your feelings please avoid reading it.I was very passionate about this game and full of hopes, but my trust in this developer has completely disappeared in 6 days. From questionable decision to sell this product under EA tag after Open Beta revealed that the game is at best in Pre-Alpha stage to lack of communication and responsiveness from devs and a wipe of Steam's discussions. The only dev member that is really trying hard is one of their Art Designers, at least I was told that he is an Art Designer. Their CM does not care about anything but Marketing and Hyping the entire dev team and all their products. I can understand that its his job, but in those desperate times you should focus on providing clear communication between devs and customers to calm things down. We were told on discord to not ping Devs and redirect all our questions and concerns to CM, so I did. Guess what, CM was ignoring anything related to current problems and was actively participating in "normal daily chat" massages, but was ignoring any bug reports or questions regarding a so broken state of the game.Last but not least, this game's design choices are very questionable. The game turned out to be not what I was expecting after it's reveal. From lack of Procedurally Generated Maps(as far as I know it will not be implemented, but you can always try to ask devs themselves if you dont believe me and I urge you to ask questions) in a dungeon crawler to claims that they will have 20 Heroes. When in reality its only 3 heroes with like 5 variations. Each hero has 1 Passive, Left Click Skill, Right Click Skill, Ultimate Skill and 2 Titan Skills(Basically its a fancy name for skill). The only things that change from hero to hero of the same class(Only 3 classes) are the Passive, the Ult and IN SOME CASES(yes, only some Heroes will have it) 1 different Titan. I dont know what your standards are, but to me thats not even close to be a different hero.I honestly could go on and on listing downsides, but the most important downside is the dev. Sorry if the truth hurts your feelings, but current generation needs to see the truth more and face it, no matter how harsh it is.I am really fed up with those Early Access tags thrown in our faces every time we complain that we paid for a product that is not ready to be sold. This game is at best in Pre-Alpha state, in no world I will ever believe that devs did not see it, yet they still decided to start selling it. This product should not see the light of day for at least another year maybe even longer. Running out of money? Go and try to get help on Kickstarter or look for investors.P.S.: I could say that I will update this review when and IF things change, but honestly, the chances of me coming back to this game are extremely low. Lets face it, there are too many good video games out there to enjoy, that I just dont have the time for second chances and that is something developers that go Early Access need to finally understand in order to stop killing their product's player base.*Product received for free via a giveaway on Twitch by a streamer that purchased a 3-pack. I have also played it during Open Beta.

_childDocuments_.review: Dont let the negative reviews scare you away from this one! It might not seem like it at first but this game has pedigree. Its another diamond in the rough from Devolver. IMO its one of the more accessible indies they've picked up in the last several years of back to back bangers. Ronimo has a small list of titles, but Awesomenauts released in the glorious age of xbox live arcade and has continued to get updates to this day. In an age of $60 AAA Flops and heartless money grabs, Blightbound stands true to its roots. $20 is a bargain. The (now fewer) negative reviews i read had me holding off on purchasing Blightbound for a couple reasons. Complaints of the grind and difficulty curve, poor bot ai, connection issues, repetitive levels etc. You'll run into them here as well. Im here to denounce them all fools. The difficulty is a non issue, if you're paying attention to the difficulty ratings of the missions and matching them to your party level in an easy to understand UI. Eventually you will be able to handle mission difficulties several levels above your party level if you take the time to master the gameplay. That brings us to the curve and the grind. If you dont want to NO PROBLEM. Im 10 hours in with a single friend to co-op and we have switched characters so many times we are still running Blight level 6 or less (Normal or Easy). We TEND to find Easy mode a cakewalk, but still sometimes get pasted by a new boss, which is great! Its great because even if you die you retain all your material rewards, which filter into crafting for better gear. This is a roguelite. If your problem is dieing, you're playing the wrong game. 10 hours into the game Im still unlocking new characters who all have individual stories and questlines to follow. I havent finished a single one. You will find yourself repeating the same levels often, but with new characters and new storylines (albeit sparse ones) to continually unlock you will find yourself jonesing to return. There are still a handful of levels we havent explored or cleared entirely, and enemy and trap mechanics seems to change as difficulty increases, leaving the missions feeling fresh.Ill say initially progression can feel a LITTLE slow. But reliably whenever i began to feel that way, a new feature for my refuge, or another character would drop into my lap expanding and deepening the gameplay further. At this point i am so earnestly impressed that i feel compelled into writing an over the top review.The Bot AI is the one thing that actually needs some love. Occasionally they will entirely misbehave, failing to trigger puzzles, or triggering where they ought naught. I imagine this makes for obnoxious do overs in single player. However, in multiplayer the bots are always leashed to one of the players, and in practice if the Bot is getting uppity one of us just walks to the other side of the room while the other solves the puzzle.Let me tell you that my PC is inches from death, and a recent windows update left my disk drive hanging like a mother-♥♥♥♥♥♥, causing most games to crash. Blightbound seems to have a ton of built in saftey measures for when your pc or network hangs up. Coop partner reports that I am invincible at all times that my game is frozen. In the few instances i jumped the gun and restarted the game or my pc before Blightbound unstuck and continued to run, all my items and quest progress was saved as i was returned to the refuge. I was earnestly awestruck. Thats the good ♥♥♥♥ right there. No game/server connection issues whatsoever. Your mileage may vary.Best enjoyed with a Controller for Melee and a Mouse for Caster and Menu navigation.

_childDocuments_.review: I discovered this game late. Unfortunately, without a community playing online, it's too difficult to review what this game might have been. _childDocuments_.review: The game is good HOWEVER I recommend you do NOT buy this game for the time being. This is (mainly) because of the Desync Issue. Basically, the way the game works is you beat lower difficulty dungeons to unlock higher difficulty dungeons. However this can only be done in one sitting (without logging off) and with the same group of people (same party of 3, if one leaves you start over). Normally this is pretty manageable (system should be modified for players who are wasting time on easy modes, but not a huge problem for now) for the time being HOWEVER every so OFTEN YOU WILL BE FORCED TO FAIL A MISSION AND RESET YOUR DUNGEON LEVEL BACK TO ZERO (ESSENTIALLY WASTING HOWEVER MUCH TIME YOU SPENT GETTING THERE). Now, I will inform you that the developers are aware of and are currently working on solving the issue. HOWEVER, I think you should save your money for now, until this issue is fixed. I don't believe in selling a malfunctioning product. But buy the game if you want, just letting you know. This issue was in beta, so I actually recommended the game then because it was free, but as a product it is incomplete. I played for 22hours on beta during the 3 days it was avalible..
_childDocuments_.name: Blightbound

_childDocuments_.review: Good concept, but so far, poor execution. The game feels very bland very early, mostly because of cooldowned evasion/quicksteps which are relevant for a wizard teleporting away, but takes out LOTS of the tactical aspect in close combat. I would have expected a stamina bar for that.As a result, you can be a damage sponge as a warrior (who can actually use his shield as he wants to mitigate damage and get counterattack bonuses), but the rogue, while powerful, is also frustrating to play because of their frailty and inability to gracefully dodge WHEN YOU NEED IT. Thus, the game doesn’t really reward spacial placement skills : you have luck or have managed to step back (terribly slowly) at the right moment, or you take damage. No parry mechanic either.I failed to see the roguelike element as well. BTW, the multiplayer is not a problem if you have a couple friends to play with, but the dungeons are almost always the same, which is a fraud for a game advertising itself as having a roguelike element (read the tags). The different heroes are just skins with slight skills/spells variations, but you’ll find yourself going back to the basic characters because… they simply are better, and they are the ones you leveled up in the first place.The crafting is also very underwhelming. You just get more stats with a shiny new skin. No new moveset, very little mechanic variation…In the end, the game is just a mindless button masher which could totally have been made for smartphones, or in the 2010s. At least, that’s what the lazy, bland combat mechanics suggest.Positive point : the art is great. But that’s the only positive aspect of that game. Kudos to the game artists.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent coop game. Combat is fun and often challenging, requiring teamwork especially on some of the harder/more rewarding levels. _childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend to play this game for a simple reason - insane amount of bugs.Game has a tendency to punish you for everything you do or dont do - like if your random teammate disconnects or leaves as soon as match started - you will lose points and soon will be unable to play one character for certain amount of time. Sounds fair and smart? Hell no.Difficulty level resets when someone leaves the lobby - so you can not play with randoms. Sounds smart? Hell no.Even if you got decent teammates, after every run chance that someone will be stuck between levels and disconnect will rise - so after 3rd-4th run some one will disconnect - the difficulty level will reset, you will lose points. Sounds smart? Hell no.So the only way to get decent loot - is to find someone, trap them in your room and dont let them leave untill you are finished. (just kidding, pls, dont do that). In order to do that - you need to convince your friends to try to play the game that will randomly disconnect from every 3-5 games. Sounds smart? Hell no.Sometimes you can not finish level or even leave the location - due to the bug. It was the same in beta. What is the point of creating beta if you dont fix bugs? Sounds smart? Hell no.You may say - well, this is an early access.That is not an excuse at all. If i can pay for a game, download in and play - that is a product. It doesnt matter if it alpha, beta, prototype, draft or whatever you call it. If anyone can buy it - that is a product. And if product has a lot of bugs and unpolished - that is a bad product. It may be surprising for developers, but bad products have tendency to get bad reviews.I may say that game is somewhat playable. _childDocuments_.review: It's an interesting game in a rather good shape. But it's still Early Access.A nice dungeon crawler, with a Diablo mixed with Darkest Dungeon vibe.It's a coop game though, that requires you to play with 2 people (or friends) in order to go far. Bots will come, but they'll probably not be as good as humans =p3 classes : Warrior, Assassin and Mage, and you go with a team containing each one.Fortunately, there are several characters to play in "each" class, so you'll see some variation (they share the mandatory skills like heal for mage, but they do play differently). Characters have to be found and collected by fillings goals, sometime, well hidden.There's already a good chunk of characters to get, and lot of legendaries. So you can play some hours before griding all the content already.As it's an Early Access though, there are still some issues like bugs, a certain lack of levels, and a rather enhancable notoriety system (which makes missions harder) but devs do update the game kinda weekly with fixes, and every 2 weeks with new content, so they're working on it at a rather fast pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I don't agree with most of these negative reviews. Is this game buggy? Of course, it was released in EA yesterday (as of me writing this review). At first, i felt the character's were too strong (I'm looking at you scarlet) but with the notoriety system, the difficulty ramps up very quickly. I agree, it can be annoying that the notoriety system is tied to the group, but i also believe this opens the community up to find people to play with, if you yourself don't have a core group of 2 other people to play with. I do have a group to play with, but even then, i do join random lobbies and i have people that leave after one match, but i have also played 3+ runs with the same group of random people. Just because some of these reviewer's got a bad group of randoms, i don't believe warrants a bad review.The art style is great in my opinion, and the animations are very visible and apparent. The crafting system is much more in-depth then i had really initially realized, and every hero differs, without getting to far away from the base class, from their counterparts. The (currently) 3 different heroes for each class, all work pretty well together, but there are definitely some comps that work better together, and i like being able to build a team like that (again, im looking at you scarlet and tek'ka)The ramping difficulty is very nice, and really benefits you if you have a group to consistently play with.I believe the blight system is significantly better than i first thought, seeing as at first, i thought it was a non-factor, always keep them topped off, but the more i'm playing the more i realize it pays to keep some characters blight sick, and others not.Don't listen to anyone that has less than 4 hours in the game, because they haven't gotten to experience the real potential in this game.TL;DR- support the devs. This game is EA, but has so much room for growth. Please don't let this one die. Go out and make friends, and keep this game alive.I have an edit, because i have learned since this review, there is one dungeon in particular that is very unstable, and i have only been able to complete it once without it bugging out. All other dungeons work well for me.Edit #2: The game has now been out for about 2.5 weeks, and they have made significant progress to the desyncing and connection issues a lot of these reviews have experienced. So i repeat, please support these devs, they are really working hard to make this game better.

_childDocuments_.review: In the time spent on this game so far, I would rather I could have given the game a meh rating. There's a few drawbacks the game has that prevents me from wanting to give it a positive score, yet it does not deserve a negative score either.What I liked about the game:-I like the art style and the music chosen. -Combat is simple enough, and objectives are easy enough for anyone to pick up, imo. -There's quite a few characters to play with, and I like how I can unlock them simply by playing the game and progressing through maps and discovering them as "map secrets." As opposed to buying character packs and what not.-Losing a game still earns you whatever you picked up, and so there doesn't seem to be a downside to losing terribly in a difficult match-up.Some of the things that made the game meh imho:-Players are forced to matchmake to join up with other players to play the game, and that there seems to be a non-existent playerbase for that. I've spent a total of 3-4 hours matchmaking during my time ingame and only had 3 people join. 2 of whom immediately left the game with the 3rd being afk for half an hour until I left. For a game that is considered a multiplayer dungeon crawler, this is not a good experience.-I am unsure if the bots are a recent new addition to the game or not, but they seem to not do very well in combat. This is noticeable when the main player is downed with mobs of enemies and a boss attacking(namely the oracle). The bots will often get themselves killed as they simply stand around and take hits while bugging out trying to revive the player, canceling, and reattempting to revive. Else when we get to puzzles involving bells needing to be hit in a specific order, the bots simply hit every single bell and frustrate me.Things I didn't like about the game:-A complete lack of information on many of the things ingame. Namely how skill damage/titan damage/attack damage and how they work with certain characters would help, especially when playing some like the newly released Clegg. I'm still unsure if I did the right thing in making a minion build with titan damage, or if I should have gone all crits/health/pure damage instead or some other stat.-Many characters of the same class play the same way, and share the same 5 or so class specific skill pool. They have no skills unique to them individually, with a few exceptions.-Difficulties on maps are locked in until players complete a map, then all difficulties refresh. This prevents efficient map farming, if you will, and forces players to play other missions instead. I'm unsure if there's a way to change map difficulties either, but there doesn't seem like a way to do so.-Builds for characters are limited to damage/skill damage only. Health seems like a minor stat to pick, as well as many of the other stats.The game has quite a few drawbacks and things I'm probably nitpicking on. but it gets a meh rating from me for now. I feel it can definitely improve later on, and deserves the positive rating I am preemptively giving it.

_childDocuments_.review: Blightbound game progression is too slow and grindy. I've already get bored before unlocking any hero or special gears. _childDocuments_.review: Stay far clear of the game for now. The base combat can be enjoyable, but much beyond that is not enjoyable. The game has plenty of very nice ideas, but the execution was not done well. The refuge system actively nerfs your characters later if you keep your characters in tip top shape (easy to do if you don't go down and always pick random hero which nets extra blight cleanse). The notoriety is a super cool concept but one person dropping screws the whole party out your notoriety meaning I have to waste my time doing 3-4 missions of useless loot that I have heaps of already before I can find anything remotely relevant to me. Loot is randomly awarded from mission clear from a static and fairly small pool, there are no diablo-esque prefixes or affixes. The game is also riddled with bugs, some game breaking to where you just have to quit the game and restart it screwing over the party you were with in the process. I somewhat forgive this as its early access and bugs come with the territory but some things happen so frequently a single mission would have revealed it. Also warrior's shield blocking doesn't actually block any damage unless you're the host, this is also true for quite a number of hero passives. The game also weirdly touts 20 heroes, but the 9 heroes we have are very small changes in kit (sometimes a single skill and a passive change). I'd much rather a smaller number of heroes that have actual time put into them. All that being said the art is nice, so there's that I guess.Edit as I forgot to mention, the game is mandatory online 3 player co-op with bots added later at some point. The games dwindling player count has made it very difficult to even get into a match lately. Spent 8 minutes in queue looking for other players, finally found one who promptly left queue after another 4 minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: This could be a really fun game if it didn't crash every other run. Basically the difficulty gets harder and the drops get better as you progress, but whenever someone crashes or the game bugs, you can say goodbye to your progress. There is no grace mechanic where you can continue if something happens.I wouldn't suggest anyone to buy this game at this point.Edit: I see some people giving positive reviews and saying that "this is an early release, you are not being fair, there can be bugs"The game's itemisation progress is based on continuity. If there is no continuity because of disconnection issues, then it means that this is a major problem. Tooltip bugs, visual bugs, stat bugs, any type of interface bugs would be acceptable. But a network problem where it happens every 3-4 runs and destroys your whole notoriety progress? That is unacceptable even for an early release. I've been playing games on steam for over 15 years, I've seen early releases which looked like the final product, I've played early releases that had bugs, but I've never played an early release where the main mechanic of the game was problematic.I don't like people releasing half baked products and get your money and then make you wait for them to fix things for you later. I also don't like people who say "you're not being fair". This is actually me being fair. If I wasn't, I would've refunded it already.On top of bugs, the game is missing a lot of information like a lot of people said. Character stats and etc. Also the additional heroes that you unlock have only 1 different skill than the previous one, which I think was a very lazy thing to do. You just added extra characters but what you actually did was adding characters with different skins.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically leave reviews... but I wanted to bump up the positives for this game as it shouldn't be 'Mixed'!I want to first say - DO NOT believe the bad reviews that are saying there is no single player or couch co-op. It has both! They're just lazy naysayers lol. Yes, you have to select 'Play Online' to get to it, but before you hop in a Dungeon, you just add the other controller or "play with bots". Nothing you can't easily learn.If you like Gautlet-like games, this is great and you will enjoy it! The art reminds me a lot of This Darkest Dungeon - with it's dark, gothic kind of look. _childDocuments_.review: I really dig the aesthetics of the game and the overall mood. And I want to spend a lot of time in this grim world, fighting disfigured monstrosities alongside my friends, but!Negatives:1. Not enough locations/missions: there are 3 hubs, each with 3 missions. Which gives 9 missions in total, and that's it. You will play them over and over (because it's a grindy kind of game). 9 missions doesn't sound that bad, but they share big part of the biome, so efectively each mission is 60% the same as others in that biome. Locations are not generated, they are always the same. Sometimes some details change, or some local event appears. That's not enough to make it satisfyingly replayable, it feels like Early Access still. The game needs more locations and most importantly: randomizations. 2. Uncomprehensive world map: missions do not appear in any order, you can chose whichever you want, but there is no description other than name and difficulty level (and if you can progress any quest there). Difficulty level change randomly, so you have to click every missions each time you want to play to see which one is "reasonable" right now. There is no sense of acomplishment or progression there. And it feels like there is nothing more, like i discovered nothing and will dicover nothing else.3. Random difficulties of the same mission: imagine you going into the deepest dungeons and defeating the challenging boss (pretty epic), another time you go to the same place, and everything is the same, but super easy, and the challenging boss looks exactly the same, but it's way weaker. It breaks the immersion so badly, instead of "lets go and see if we can beat this thing" you have: "let's see who they gonna let us beat today".4. Static melee combat: characters stay in place while attacking. While it feels good when being a mage, it is horrible when you are a fighter or assassin. Guys, just push the character in the direction of the attack, you will see how much more fun it is.5. Minor gameplay issues: sometimes shown Areas of Effects differ from the real ones, sometimes you're not sure if you are hitting the enemy or not, shooting does not play too good on gamepad, gamepad has strange initial setup (you can change it though), unclear projectiles volume, unequalized sfx volumes...Positives:1. The mood and visuals: while environments are okay, the effects and characters stand out positively. And all this bloody (and sometimes messy) theatre on the screen is just a pleasure to watch.2. Satisfying gameplay: there always have to be 3 classes in the match but synnergy between them works well. While the regular "punching" feels just alright, the skills works great; allowing to set up combos with your teammates.3. Variety of characters: there are only 3 classes, but within those classes there are different characters (7 per class I think), and those characters looks different, speaks differently, and vary in skills (not entirely, but enough to make them worth checking out and picking your favourite).4. Equipement with skills: you can change the equipement of your characters to change the balance of their stats or add a passive buff (like lifesteal), but items also have more interactive skills (like setting up a bomb, or exploding). It's really adds one more layer to the character customization.5. Characters storylines: each character has their own storyline consisting of several small quests and a single "personal goal". The quests can often be completed only in certain location. It gives one more reason to play a certain character a bit more, or just few more times to acomplish something.6. Game can be played in couch co-op, up to 3 players. Tested - works fine.My overall recommendation is positive because i want this game to be further developed. It has a huge potential, but it's not fully realized in the current installment.
