_childDocuments_.review: Ok, let´s see. Blightbound is a 3 people cooperative dungeon crawler action oriented. You play with some people, kill mobs and bosses, complete missions and earn loot, which becomes better and better the more you play with the same team. You also develope the refuge where your characters level up and equip as you earn experience, and you can unlock many characters and their backstories as you preogress. First of all, remember that this is an early access game. There are bugs, and lacks content, but I must say that the developers are active and updates come regularly.I really like the backstory of the game, where you try to survive in a blighted land full of monsters. And love the fact that your characters develope their stories as you play with them. A lot of lore there, which I love. Sound and visuals are lovely, too, even when the backgrounds look pretty similar (yes , everything is ruines and devastation). I also like the voice acting, pretty good and varied. Maybe I miss some more voice-over in the enemies.As in gameplay, it is satisfying and fast-paced. Many of the downvotes come from people who think all characters are the same with only one or two skills changing. This is partially true, many characters in the same class share one or two skills, but looking at the different combinations makes different styles of play and different sinergies with other characters, which I guess was intended. I personally like it, as you can accomodate to one role yet change the playstile while still fullfiling this role. For me, the ideal would be to reach the moment where you could choose for your character among all the skills that his class had. Finally, there is the issue with the multiplayer and the infamous notoriety system. Multiplayer means that you need three players to play the game. Lobbys are not always full, and sometimes is hard to find people to play with. Playing with people also has the problem to sometimes play with people that plays different and teams dissolving after just one match. Notoriety system makes that the more you play with the same groups, the harder difficulties you can choose, and the better equipment you can get. The bad thing is that if anybody leaves the party, the notoriety falls down to zero again, making you to restart building it. Recently added bots solve part of the problem (at least you can play without a full party), but they do leave the party after each match, reseting the notoriety counter. My best guess is that the developer wants this to be a mulyiplayer, not a single player with bots game, which I totally not only understand, but support. The bad side is that I am a casual player, and many times I have no time to more than two or three games in a row, which doesn´t let me room for opting for the greater difficulties or rewards. This could be a problem if, as I said, I was not a casual player with not so much free time. For me, it´s ok. But I get that other people have problems with it, even when I want to remember that this is an early access. Ok, summarizing. Good game, addictive gameplay, a lot of replayability. Coop (you can even play in the same computer with friends!), and pretty interesting. But still in developement. For me, is a good product enough as it is, but it promises a lot more. I recommend it, and, if you like it, just give the creators some feedback for them to improve what you don´t like.Edit: Roland is my new favourite

_childDocuments_.review: My recommendation is more of a "meh..." than a straight-up "No". There is the potential for a good game here.....if the damn application can remain stable enough for the player to get some actual damn playtime out of it.  At first, I was only experiencing crashes during the tutorial, which seems to be experienced by many other players. In one of the threads I posted to about this, a dev response basically said "Skip tutorial, patch soon". Well, my first several hours in the normal campaign went well enough, as far as crashing went: there weren't any. But, that changed a few hours prior to my writing of this review. Now, I have experienced 2 crashes during normal gameplay; both have been while playing with other actual players. Keep in mind, this is even more frustrating when you consider that you have to wait on average 5-15 minutes for an actual player to join party. The playerbase seems to be non-existent at the moment.With all of that out of the way, the game is reminiscent of the classic D&D arcade games developed/published by CAPCOM from the 90's. Also similar to the Gauntlet series, Legends and Dark Legacy in particular, but a little less horde-y. It's a double-whammy of nostalgia.FINAL VERDICT: Not worth buying now, too unstable.  Maybe down the road, after a few patches.

_childDocuments_.review: Blightbound is an abandoned multiplayer/co-op focused ARPG, a bit like a lighter tone Diablo, with cartoony character art and the usual top down type perspective as you fight hordes of fantasy baddies using spells and swords and all that stuff.The core gameplay is okay but not great, and that's kind of the big problem, because outside of the core loop, there's not a huge amount of content.  It gets repetitive really quickly.  The devs were banking on a co-op experience to carry the game and make it "go viral".  If the only fun thing about a game is other people, that just means other people are fun to game with, and doesn't say anything for the game itself. The devs washed their hands on the game and moved on, leaving it in a playable but somewhat shallow and incomplete feeling state. So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Blightbound has the overly optimistic price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  It's way too overpriced for an abandoned game, this is worth $1 at best, and even then it would be a "maybe".  And even if it was a "maybe", Valve doesn't give us that option.  Which makes sense, because a million "maybe" reviews don't actually say anything useful about a game at all. For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Stray", "Yakuza 0" or "Detroit: Become Human".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off that I did have fun playing the game after getting it on sale for 7.99 and I got 10hrs of enjoyment, but its hard to recommend the game because of the following:There are 21 characters to unlock, 7 in each class (warrior, assassin, mage) all with minor abilities difference.  I had a fun time unlocking the characters, and they all have their own "personal quests" to unlock their full story BUT here is the problem. To unlock the full story of each character it requires alot of grinding,  and there are  only around 10 lvls in the game. 1. You spend tons of time repeating the same lvls over and over with not much variety in any puzzles or enemies.2.  Completing the full story of a character just rewards you with all 6 dialog scripts which are voice acted... but very very underwhelming. If each character had their own final boss encounter or even a special event at the end of their quest line, I would have thumbs it up, but they end with nothing.3 the inventory system has limited spaces, and the crafting is frustrating. you have to get class tokens to craft certain weapons. I played the warrior class but had to play the assassin class to get assassin tokens to craft swords since they required both warrior and assassin tokens. I do not like playing the assassin class so I did not want to grind any weapons. Also most characters you unlock came with a legendary item which you can swap to any character.I was hoping to unlock all the characters and grind through their personal stories for some sort of payout like a boss, special encounter, or even a cinematic. At the end I just got a conclusion voice script saying they completed their task and decide to return and hang out in the camp for more adventures.TL:DR:+/-Combat is okay, not much variety in the characters within their classes (warrior, assassin, mage)+Cool art style +I was able to beat the entire game solo with bots-Not much variety in lvls, and the game requires you to grind ALOT-Character personal stories have underwhelming conclusions and not worth unlocking.-Crafting was almost worthless, most characters you unlock came with a base "legendary" item which you can swap to any character.

_childDocuments_.review: Constant de-sync issues. Players going invisible.Game is in super poor condition. They shouldn't have released this at this stage, for consumers, at all.This feels like a beta. A beta product is something you pay a closed group of participants to test, so that you can clean up any issues they might find, and you as a developer have missed, before releasing the product to the public.It's basically a non-functioning product. The premise of the game is to get streaks of notoriety, by completing dungeons with the same party. The higher the streak, the better the dungeons and the rewards. Without this, you will always be getting poor quality items.Okay, but what happens when you de-sync just after gaining a single notoriety? You have to re-do the very same boring dungeon, rewarding you with the very same boring loot.Oh, and it gets better. Did you just reach 3x Notoriety? Tough luck you just got de-synced again, just as you got closer to getting some legendary loot, huh?And mind you, de-sync is just part of the large amount of issues this game faces. But I'm not going to make a wall of text, and just end it with this:Networking is a core concept in your product. How dare you, as a developer, release code, that yields de-synchronizations? How dare you, ask money for it? Anyone can write that kind of a code.

I have experienced no bugs, no crashes, no freezes, no glitches+Art style is extremely well done with 3D environments and some powers, as well as amazing looking 2D artwork for the characters that reminds me of Darkest Dungeon+Jiggle physics for BOTH genders haha+Great soundtrack+6 varied levels (with much more coming soon)+3 classes with 3 sub-classes each that feel different enough to warrant picking favorites+Interesting and challenging boss mechanics including some extremely difficult ones+Different difficulties for dungeons providing a deeper challenge and varied fight every timeI can't recommend this game enough, if you enjoy dungeon crawling, or the art style, that alone should convince you to get this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game seems to have two development teams working on this game. Team 1 That loves this game and wants to create a passionately influenced powerhouse of fun for small party gamers, and Team 2 that doesn't know what a video game is yet and are trying to figure out the basics of RPG synergies. Half the items in this game will have you scratching your head, and the other half will have you excited for what you can create. This also goes for abilities, however much more steeply as some abilities will have you laughing at how pathetic they are, while marveling at the strength of others. Because of the polarity of these abilities you are forced to select the best PRESET combination of abilities in champions. For me, Clegg was the overall warrior powerhouse with a taunt (now sadly as of release it's been replaced with the worst warrior ability, Lava Stomp). This strong difference in items and abilities make it nigh impossible to believe there is actually any options in heroes to choose from since the majority of them just simply suck horrendously. There's no incentive to push higher level maps (I stopped after beating a level 32 map)I'm not particularly big on the 2.5D map layouts, or the many loading screens between small areas (Why is this even a thing). The game was fun, but after the update, it's pretty much ruined/nerfed any end game min/max or synergy team comps with friends. TLDR: Low/High quality divided dev team on items/abilities, most heroes have bad ability setups, maps have poor layouts/many loading screens, grindy to get items and may take you 75hrs to unlock everything through a lot of grinding boring maps. End game build/combos are nerfed. I'd recommend pre-release over the post haha.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok this is gona be hard...I came across this game by chance and it sucked me in. Its like a mix between MOBA and Streets of Rage... Very addictive very interesting concept. However after playing it for long hours in beta and release I can say there is problems and I would avoid this as plague till they get addresses main issues.Essentially everything is broken in the game and I mean everything...- The quest line for characters is either unfinished or bugged.- Many skills and items do not actually work the way they should.- The calculation for variety skills is bugged and not working as intended- There is desync issues affecting the whole game which means you cannot play more then 4-5 games in row before you disconnect, whole game is designed in a way that if you want to obtain harder items you must reach higher notority level which increases difficulty of dungeons which you cannot reach because by time you do someone disconnects and you are back to easy mode dungeon...- The level scaling of classes is broken the higher the level of player the more difficult dungeon is.. In theory great concept but again broken because if you have very high level character you essentially are playing impossible difficulty on easy mode without the loot....- Items disapear constantly be prepared to lose your legendary items- Tooltips overlay each other so lot of ui problems present tooThere is very little variation in charactersThe levels and maps are pretty much recycled. There is only really 3 levelsThere is so many issues it is quite frankly insane this should not be early access this should be pre-alpha at best. What gets me is that latest patch they tweaked difficulty level and broke the whole thing instead of focusing more pressing bugs.. There is lot of potential but this is main saying for most early access games.I would give this 6 month and then come back and see what is the status. In current state stay away!

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game as it currently has a lot of issues.- Desyncing happen frequently (Has happened over 10 times to me so far) and makes it borderline impossible to get good drops as you need to do consecutive runs (In the same group) without anyone leaving to get better loot chances.- Many item and skill effects do not do what's written in the item tooltip. (One Example of this is one of the assassins skill is supposed to reset if the ability kills and enemy, which it does not)- The game can feel sluggish as the performance crawls to 30 fps often in combat (I'm running the game on: CPU: i7 7700k  GPU: GTX1080ti)- When you equip items they have a chance to disappear, which means the Legendary item that you've worked hard to craft/obtain might disappear if you want to move it to another character.Also the game has very little character and map variety at the moment.- There are 3 classes to play, which have 3 characters each as of me writing this.- All characters within a class have very little to make them feel different to the other options. (Most notably is usually that   the passives are different.)- There were 3 levels in the open beta, but the 3 new levels introduced in the Early Access feel very similar to the maps   already present in the game. The new levels use the same style and some also whole sections from the earlier levels. - The levels are also not particularly long, so the gameplay loop currently consists of doing the same 6 short levels over and over in hope of that the game doesn't desync before getting a decent item.

I have no desire whatsoever to play any game online with randos ever, so if we are forced to to play with some kid named Stonerboobs69 or whatever when playing only two player local, I will likely try to return the game.I'm becoming less optimistic. _childDocuments_.review: Blighbound is a situation of a great idea, but poor execution. A strictly co-op game with forced online support is already a fairly bad idea due to the limited nature of the game's ability to match you with players of similar strength, if it can match you with other players at all. I have personally found myself lucky enough to have two others to brave the dungeons of this game with.Pros:The game itself has a well-crafted, albeit generic. world. The story itself is told through personal quests of each of the heroes you acquire. The art style and sound design are unique and blend well enough together to provide a well-crafted audio and visual cue combat system for most encounters.The voice acting is passable and won't break your immersion as far as reverb or distortion not being edited out. Props to the VA's for delivering technical quality to an indie game.You'll end up seeing many enemies repeating over the course of your experience in the game. Bosses feel unique enough between areas, but some are admittedly uninspired or borrow the designs of other elite enemies you can already face throughout the dungeons.One dungeon in particular, The Descent, has an amazing elevator event that you use to progress throughout the dungeon itself. Fighting enemies, dodging lasers, and the feeling of stress due to actual difficulty and not inflated HP values and/or damage, is truly good game design.Middle-ground:The repetition of dungeons can prove to be incredibly monotonous for some, while I don't mind it myself, especially having played many roguelites. The gearing mechanics and attribute system can feel like it has less than the desired impact at times, but I also know many people like small increments of increasing power rather than large milestone boosts. This game only really excels in small increases of power, so if that's your jam, here you go.The color scheme is incredibly drab and bleak. This is intentional and a stylistic choice due to the state of the game world itself being one of apocalyptic struggle. If you need brighter colors in your games, steer clear of this one. It's all dark reds, grays, and greens. Cons:I hate that this part of the list will be the most extensive, but I have a lot of issues with the core tenants of and execution of the game as it stands at the moment. I've tried to keep in mind that the game isn't finished, but at the same time, some of the design choices are abysmal at the moment, and I need to hope the devs plan to rework them. Boss names appearing every time you encounter them, loot feeling largely ineffective until legendary due to them just being basic stat boosts, puzzles being repeated between every dungeon you run, so they never feel fresh or different, just tedious, and skills that are set in stone for each hero, not allowing for any kind of mix and match for unique builds, as well as a map that provides limited info and cannot be fully opened or zoomed out for more info on where to go during a dungeon for quests, as far as I know. These are just a few of the smaller things I'd like to mention before I break down my bigger issues below. The quests are mediocre and feel like filler rather than actual personal stories. The tedium of collecting 500 mana orbs on a warrior is absolutely insane. Your counter only goes up if you collect them yourself, while you compete with a mage who can literally teleport to his mana orbs as needed. This shows a weird dissonance between the message and intent of co-op, but having mechanics that starkly place each player at odds with each other. Loot is distributed round-robin as it's picked up, leading to a separation in loot. This isn't the worst offender, but it feels bad to pick up loot knowing you won't be claiming anything for yourself. Reducing the amount of trash loot and making loot count for all players at once would do wonders for creating a value in pushing higher dungeon levels, rather than having them feel like a slog. Enemy balance feels lacking at the moment, with quite a few of them feeling awful to play against. The large bruisers with shields have a repeating large AoE attack that denies you access to their weakspot. This would be fine if not also amplified by the pressure that each smaller enemy can provide. This creates situations where it feels positioning does not matter and is instead just frustrating, feeling unable to do anything meaningful. As the warrior, get used to just holding down block due to the incredibly high burst damage some enemies do. The large tracking skulls are invulnerable, with a decreasing health bar as they chase you. They do such massive amounts of damage that you most physically stop what you're doing and run. You cannot survive their proximity attack for more than 2 or so seconds, even as the warrior blocking. This is AWFUL and feels awful as well. The builds are non-existent outside of some of the legendary items granting special effects, which are admittedly done decently. Rather than having an amount of select skills to customize and create builds with, you're given characters that you're unable to customize in any way. It leaves MUCH to be desired when you're forced to play a character who's skills you don't enjoy playing, all the way up through their lower levels (as they all level separately, even amongst those in the same class, creating unnecessary grind and tedium.) This is all done JUST so you can do their personal quest, which again, your allies can't actually help you with as they cannot see your objectives on the map. Instead, they should delegate the characters to a cosmetic system, allowing you to craft builds with different skills, and run the quests based off of the current skin of the character you're wearing. It places power and control into the hands of the player, while also still providing the opportunity for a narrative quest system. Ultimately, even with a party of three, this co-op game lacks proper co-op elements, and generates more frustration and irritation rather than any sort of entertainment. It's really disappointing to write a negative review here, but much of the game design is lacking. A strictly co-op game is lacking much of what makes co-op games feel co-op. The online matchmaking is more or less dead, along with a relatively boring progression system that leaves a lot to be desired. I'll gladly update this review if they revisit much of this game to help it become the diamond it can be, but at the moment, so much of this game just works against itself. It's a frustrating experience you can share with friends. Can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Blightbound is a grim 2D brawler with RPG and party builder elements. You play any of the three classes (tank, assassin or healer) and venture with two other players in a dungeon featuring monsters and traps. Based on the power level of your selected hero, and the notoriety of your team (how many dungeons you have completed with the same party), you gain access to a range of dungeons with varying difficulty: the harder a dungeon is, the better loot you get upon completion. That loot allows you after to better equip your heroes, and you can also do some crafting with those (useful to get a legendary item that you seek).Each class has a left click ability (auto-attack), and a charge-based right click ability (shield, damage burst or healing), both having no cooldown. Each class also has an ultimate (powerful ability lasting for a short amount of time). There are several heroes per class, each hero has two titan skills - these are low cooldown (5-10 sec) abilities that have to be timed right to get the most benefit out of them. These titan skills are not specific to a hero: two heroes usually share one titan skill, so the major difference between one hero and another is one different titan skill out of two.Each hero also has 5 stats: strength (damage bonus), agility (movement bonus), willpower (cooldown reduction), vitality (health increase) and luck (crit damage + magic find). Each hero gains several stat points to spend when levelling up.You also have a Blight mechanism and a "village" that grows over time, but right now these mechanisms aren't too developed and are quite shallow.Each monster in the dungeon has specific attack patterns, which makes it possible to time blocking or dodging. How well you do in the dungeon depends a lot on your team coordination and your timing for bracing enemies attacks. It is possible to carry your team, especially since the game adapts the difficulty based on who is present on your team.You need three players to dive through a dungeon, however right now there is matchmaking ensuring you always get two other players - and for the future, the devs are planning to add the ability to play in single player.The gameplay loop is solid. Once you get to the right level of challenge, it's very entertaining, fun and rewarding.However, you have to get to this right level of challenge. The first two dungeons you will run into (in a party) are usually too easy: you button mash everything, and try to complete the level as fast as possible so that you can gain notoriety and access better loot on your next run. The notoriety depends on your party, so if you solo queue you will always do your first two runs at notoriety 0 or 1.The game is fun for the first few hours, however, the gameplay does become a bit repetitive after a while, especially since you don't have any way to customize your heroes' skills, and the only difference you'll get in terms of hero power is in your stats. There are some additional effects granted by legendary items but I found their effects to be a bit shallow so far (very powerful, but shallow in the sense that it won't change your gameplay decisions). I hope the devs will allow for either deeper builds or deeper itemization to rise in the future, for an ARPG title it's, in my opinion, a necessary thing to have.That said, right now I am evaluating this game as an Early Access title: and as an Early Access title, it's fun, promising, and with a lot of potentials. So here's my thumb up :) And I recommend this game: you will have a good 10 hours of good fun with it in its current state, perhaps more with time.

_childDocuments_.review: Blightbound, developed by Ronimo Games, is a co-op dungeon crawler that offers a unique and immersive multiplayer experience. With its dark and atmospheric setting, challenging gameplay, and strategic teamwork mechanics, Blightbound sets itself apart from other games in the genre. In this review, I'll delve into the game's key features and highlight what makes it an engaging and captivating experience.Captivating Dark Fantasy World:Blightbound takes place in a beautifully crafted dark fantasy world, brimming with atmospheric visuals and hauntingly detailed environments. From the eerie dungeons to the decaying villages, every location exudes a sense of foreboding and mystery. The art style and attention to detail in the world design contribute to the game's immersive experience, drawing players into its rich lore.Unique Character Classes and Abilities:One of the standout features of Blightbound is its diverse roster of character classes, each with their own distinct playstyle and abilities. From the mighty warrior to the agile assassin and versatile mage, there is a class to suit every player's preferred combat style. The strategic aspect of forming a well-balanced team is crucial, as each class brings unique strengths and weaknesses to the table, encouraging cooperative gameplay and thoughtful decision-making.Challenging Gameplay and Progression:Blightbound offers challenging gameplay that rewards skillful coordination and teamwork. As players venture into the depths of the blighted realms, they'll encounter formidable enemies and treacherous traps. The combat requires precise timing, quick reflexes, and effective communication to overcome the various obstacles and boss encounters. The sense of accomplishment that comes from successfully navigating through the dungeons and defeating powerful foes is highly satisfying.Engaging Co-op Mechanics:The game truly shines when played with friends or other players online. Blightbound emphasizes cooperative gameplay, with up to three players forming a party to tackle the dungeons together. The synergy between different character classes is vital, as players must coordinate their abilities and strategies to overcome the challenges. The ability to revive fallen teammates and share healing items reinforces the importance of teamwork and creates a strong sense of camaraderie.Loot and Progression System:Blightbound features a rewarding loot and progression system that keeps players invested in their characters. As you explore and conquer dungeons, you'll acquire powerful gear, unlock new abilities, and level up your heroes. The constant sense of progression and the desire to acquire better equipment adds a layer of long-term motivation, encouraging players to keep venturing into the blighted realms.Conclusion:Blightbound offers a captivating co-op dungeon crawling experience with its dark fantasy setting, strategic gameplay, and engaging cooperative mechanics. The immersive world design, diverse character classes, and challenging encounters create a compelling gameplay loop that keeps players hooked. While the game could benefit from additional content and further balancing, the potential for exciting updates and expansions is promising. If you're a fan of cooperative dungeon crawlers and enjoy the thrill of conquering challenging dungeons with friends, Blightbound is definitely worth exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another classic case of "kind of". The game's basic formula is really good, and its got great bones. However, they seem to have shot themselves in the foot in a few areas. I'm sure other reviews will get into the details, so I'll just give a basic summary of my problems. You can't really select a difficulty. It gradually ramps up when you win consecutively with the same party, but that means you have to go back to easy missions when you start back up, or more commonly, have to restart due to a bug.There are guaranteed legendaries starting at medium (hard) difficulty. This means you can just run pretty easy missions with a decent team, and get some hilariously overpowered gear. This kind of makes progression totally moot. Why craft when you can just roll into amazing legendaries? Why try when you can just get multiple different items that give you functionally infinite healing?The content isn't proc gen. This is worrying because I've just already played all the maps like a BUNCH of times, and I already have all of the gear I want. This formula lives and dies on micro progression of randomly generated loot, and replaying randomly generated dungeons, and they just don't have it.Hopefully they can fix the first two issues, but the third issue is gonna be *shrug*. Wait and see, It will certainly get better, but it remains to be seen if it will become good. I will update this reviews as I come back to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/10 for fun.  Could be 9/10 when complete, but from dev decision trends, it's more likely the game will be DOA before it exits early access..  "Online 3 player ONLY" with all the normal problems that entails.  No offline available, no solo.  There are bots now, but they died 10 times EACH on one "easy" map, and I was unable to test further.  See below on "difficulty."  Desperately needs single player 'offline' mode, as most randoms are terrible, and just cannot play their randomly selected class, or worse, matchmaking takes 10 minutes because everyone wants to play Mage.  I feel this will only get worse as early access goes on, and interest in the game fades.  Forcing the game into 3 player was likely the first mistake.Developer company & team appears responsive, and regularly responds to community feedback, but is pushing this to be a "difficult" game, with all the challenges that brings.  The game engine does not lend itself well to such an endeavour, as controls, camera wildly disagree with each other.  Since several patches ago, HP sponge enemies, and unkillable flying death skulls are the norm, rather than the exception.Per-character class differentiation is voice, pixels, and 1 to 2 skill differences.Systems for class building are present but seem to have near zero impact, even at the max character level and max gear.  RPG stats appear to be a token nod rather than impactful due to this.  Instead of allowing focus of stat purpose or role, the team decided to rebalance cooldown so it was useless, which bodes poorly that RPG stats will ever mean anything.  Like most games that focus on "difficulty," it's likely that only [Total DPS] will ever be a useful stat output, and that other play styles will be fully discouraged by inherent game systems.  This being the case, the token RPG stats are a curiosity, and the cooldown nerf suggests the dev team is fully willing to enter into an "arms race" with players.Lag issues appeared to be smoothed out several patches ago, so credit where credit is due. Overall, the game is a mess of poorly chosen systems and decisions that could have been great, but are unlikely to ever be so due to balance and gameplay decisions.  Buying and playing this game will not give you more joy than 4 caramel macchiatos.  The game is still early access, and there are, were, and will be game-breaking bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: There aren’t many co-op games being made nowadays. Sure, you can play with your buddies in a shooter, but sometimes you just want to play something different, but without having to resort to the singleplayer experience. Here we have Blightbound, a dungeon crawler that lets three friends hack and slash their way through the monsters of the Blight. The game is in early access, but it nevertheless feels fleshed out with a good amount of content for its launch, leaving me with a favorable impression of my experience.There is fragments of story here and there, but you don’t need to know much about the plot. Here’s the chant: Many years ago, an evil being known only as the Shadow Titan was defeated by heroes that were legendary for their time. It was not known to them, however, that defeat was the Shadow Titan’s true plan all along. The world was plunged into total darkness due to the fracturing of the Sun, and the corpse of the giant spewed out a nauseous and corrupting fog known as the Blight. The result is that humanity’s last stand resides in the refuge, a mountaintop hideout that holds the only hope for mankind to reclaim their lost lands.The refuge will serve as your base of operations. It is here that you will start your expeditions into the blighted lands below. Every party will have three members—either friends or randoms from matchmaking—with each person having an assigned class to play: warrior, assassin, and mage to act as tank, DPS, and healer, respectively. Each class has different heroes to pick from with different skills and abilities to use, but their roles will remain the same. Your destination are three environments: Gravemark, Underhold, and Blade’s Edge. Your goal: defeat the boss, rescue survivors, and collect loot. But most importantly, stay alive. Even on normal difficulty fights can go sour if one of your teammates don’t pull their weight. The warrior must block damage for his comrades, the assassin needs to deal damage as well as interrupt fatal blows from the enemy, and the mage has to heal the wounds the party will inevitably sustain. If one link is broken, the run will end in failure, and the expedition will fall to the Blight.Whether your dungeon run ended in success or failure, you will return to the refuge and be greeted by … well, nothing, most likely. At the start the refuge is almost completely barren of anything. It is your objective to rebuild it to its full potential by improving prosperity levels through methods such as recruiting heroes and rescuing survivors. Each level you reach will provide you with a reward like stat points. You will also be able to recruit artisans to gain access to new features at the refuge; the merchant unlocks a venue for purchasing goods and the occasional hero, while the blacksmith lets you use the forge to craft new items.It is in the refuge that you are able to sort through and equip the loot you salvaged from your runs. The two main things you will be looking at are weapons and trinkets. The weapons you find can come in the form of a sword, a shield, a dagger, or a staff. Each weapon will have a specific amount of damage dealt (or, in the case of shields, percentage of damage blocked) and will possibly have modifiers such as an increase to health or a cooldown reduction to your skills. Trinkets also have modifers but are not class-specific. You can equip them on any hero of any class and stack trinkets of the same effects together. If you’d rather not rely solely on the loot you find from the merchant or dungeons, then crafting is your best bet. In the beginning you will only be able to forge items that are common drops, but as you gain more crafting materials, you can eventually create legendary items that are far superior to any generic equipment you could find.There is one important detail that must be noted: this game does not support singleplayer. Each run must have three humans players and has no bots to fill in a slot. This decision is understandable when you consider the fact that the game’s dungeons have puzzles to solve and fights that would require a level of teamplay an AI would not be able to replicate. But for those without two other friends to play with, what can they do? Sure, there is a matchmaking feature, but many who would play this game would most likely already have friends to play with. And those who opt to play with randoms will be challenged with the lack of communication a friend with voice chat has. There is an in-game text chat, but no one will be chatting in the middle of a fierce boss fight. My worry is that this game will become even better than it already is, but, years later, will you still be able to matchmake with people? The only reliable way, now and in the future, to play this game is to do so with two friends that you trust. [...]

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: There WILL be kind of spoilers in my review, so be warned.I really gave this game a chance, but it's just not good at this moment, it needs a lot of extra polishing before I could confidently say that this game deserves a recommendation from me.First, the cons:            - Interesting 3-player concept synergy idea            - A larger amount of items to choose from to try and have a different playstyle for different situations/dungeons            - The artwork is very very nicely stylized, I've VERY much enjoyed to look at the all the artworkAnd now, a few things which make me not have fun while playing this game, which is why I'm referring to it as not yet polished:            -  - The gameplay gets a bit stale after a while, even with the different characters (available somewhat different ability kits) available for each of the 3 main character roles. It's fun to have different characters for different roles, but if they have only 1-2 skill different than others, it feels a bit like they are simply rehashed to seem like there is an abundance of choice. Why not have just a single characters with a choice to have different abilities? I'm guessing because the focus was to have different characters with different story and lore, but this just seems like it's bloating/inflating the amount of playable characters without much actual incentive to try others that much. Some skills seem to be extremely powerful, while others seems extremely situational and not really worth considering for that "what if" moment - just makes my choice of characters dwindle to a few.            -  - The prosperity system is just utterly awful. It's somewhat slow to level, which by itself is not a problem, but having a few levels without any rewards feels very... unrewarding. Making me not really look forward to try and increase the prosperity at all, and additionally -- a character having an item count toward the prosperity rating just makes it seems like you have to randomly equip higher quality items to different characters, which you may or may not even play, just to give the prosperity rating a little boost. It feels like too much min-maxing on something that makes it more complicated to manage items in case you want to re-equip some higher tier items on another character. Just feels very not thought through, or rather, unrewarding.            -  - The item system feels quite a bit unrewarding. At the start, the item drops were extremely rare, and crating something never really felt rewarding because you would sometimes need to grind quite a while before a random drop actually gives you the item you need. I can understand the concept of grinding for items, just so you can grind for some more items very well (something I love the most in games), but this specific low drop rate + shop randomness + super high prosperity level blacksmith unlocks, just make it feel unnecessarily tedious and not fun to grind for. And I'm not sure if changing the drop rate of items would feel rewarding enough, the system just inherently feels broken.            -  - The hitboxes were one of the more infuriating things that seems like it shouldn't have been an issue -- there were a larger number of times where I was outside the circle of the enemy skill attack, however, it still registered as me being hit. I have played other games in which precise movement is necessary and dodging attacks at just the right amount moment is crucial (Sekiro for example), while I can admit that I'm not the greatest at those skill based actions, Blighbound's way of indicating a range of an attack is just improper.            -  - The bounty system is very badly designed. You get 5 random bounties which you CANNOT switch with. If you get 2 Impossible and 1 hard bounty at the start of the game, you can effectively only do the other 2 bounties until much later once you get higher level characters and a lot better items - having the possibility of switching those Impossible ones once every few runs would help a lot in this manner, but it's still far from being great. The map choosing system feels a bit off in case you wish to hunt for a certain bounty, sometimes you have to re-run random other maps until the difficulty drops below a threshold you can do with the characters you wished for. Trying to force you outside of your comfort zone can be a good challenge for players, but this feels needlessly random, and again, doesn't make the game feel any more fun.            -  - The randomize character option does not yield coins of all 3 types of you play with bots. The amount of "gold" dropped is fluctuating greatly, for some easy missions (without drop enhancement items) we get around 9k on one run, while the next run, on a higher difficulty on the same map yields ~3.9k, which feels extremely unbalanced - by that logic, just rerunning lower level dungeons as fast as possible will give you the most gold? Which is suggestive for the players to actually re-run lower level maps, and not even try higher level maps. The level cap seems very low and feels like it stopped before we could even build the characters properly - if the character level stops at 8, and the highest stat can get to 10, it feels like there is little progress to be done for any one character. - If I have to play 20+ hours for a game to have some kind of progress which *might* lead to fun, it doesn't seem worth trying to grind out the levels. It just flat out feels unrewarding to go through dungeons, try different characters, or try and grind to get better items. While I really want to game to be fun for me, I REALLY gave it a chance, it still needs quite a bit of polishing as the game at this state just doesn't feel fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice art style and a great combat system that encourages you to actively avoid damage and pay attention to what your teammates are doing. There are 3 totally different classes (each comes with 3 slightly different subclasses), and I enjoyed playing them all. When you start out, the game forces you to play a random class so that you familiarize yourself with their mechanics, and after about 1 hour of play you get the ability to always play the class you want.The game has a difficulty scaling system which lets you up the challenge and the rewards if you stay in the same group after winning a game. (If one player leaves the group, the difficulty resets.) In practice, this means that if you want maximum challenge, you'll have to play with friends, which is both good and bad. It's good because it doesn't split the matchmaking for various difficulties and it limits the frustration in public groups, and bad because you can't play on harder difficulties if you don't have a static group of friends so it quickly becomes stale for solo players who seek challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Devs took my advice, I am preserving my negative review below, but am changing my review to positive until I play enough to make a new review.I hope my feedback is constructive, and though its pretty negative, know that its only because I see so much potential in this game, and did have slightly more fun than I had frustration. Every update adds a bad idea because of a commitment to keep old bad ideas.  The game has great potential, and is a fun concept, but developer judgement thus far is leading me to give up hope for the game ever improving for now.  The game requires notoriety (keeping the same party for several hours of play for good loot) This is a bad idea. They made it so more difficulties are available to get better loot, but even on impossible the game is easy and gives loot that is crap for my level. They got rid of knowing what tier of loot you would get after spending half an hour playing, bad idea. Then they added bots, so the dwindling player base could find a party, or make a party that didn't leave  and reset the stupid notoriety idea, but guess what, it includes a terrible idea, bots leave the party and reset notoriety after every level, making them useless.  Bad ideas compound upon each other out of some weird blinding hubris keeping them from throwing it out that I cannot understand. Think things through with your games, and throw out trash ideas if you cannot fix them.  Adding more characters with samey skills isn't drawing anyone back in. Fix the game's basic poorly thought out elements (especially notoriety, burn this horrible idea in a fire) and maybe I'll want to play it again someday.

If this fills, your character cannot do missions for a set period of time. _childDocuments_.review: The game is good, it really is. It just has a few issues which will likely be fixed in the next updates.There are some complaints in the reviews section which are wrong, and I'd like to address them.Some people mention that you're not able to pick which hero you'd like to play as, which isn't true; you just click on the hero, and with its sheet on screen you press the ready button.Desync isn't that common of a deal after the first updates, but there are times in which a desync problem will likely send your party to the gameover screen. There's a workaround for it, but it's tough to get a bunch of strangers to coordinate and do it nonetheless.After grinding for a while, you'll notice that notoriety is essential for gaining legendary items, which allow you to really customize your playstyle with each character, and makes them feel less generic than they do after you've been playing them for a little while.It's really important for you to be able to grind such items, but since your notoriety level gets lost after a single member from your party leaves, most of the time you'll end up getting back to a notoriety level of 0 thanks to the guy who just played 2 runs with you, leaving.The best way to fix this would be to make it so you lose your notoriety level after TWO party members leave, that way you could keep playing even with one friend, and not feel like you're getting ripped off.These issues aside, the notoriety one being the most important, the game is great fun.Not only is it a game which relies on cooperation for successfully completing each run, but makes it fun to cooperate, even with strangers.At the time of this review, the endgame is also really good, allowing you to, as mentioned before, customized your playstyle to your likings. It's just a shame that there isn't that much content since, well, it just came out.tl;dr:I really recommend it.It's fun and it is challenging, let's just hope the desync issues get completely fixed, as well as more content coming soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I can easily recommend this to anyone who wants some co op hack n slash with enough progression to chase after. This adventure is definitely better with friends but still enjoyable solo,The Heroes and items are different enough to encourage a lot of experimentation. The bots can be frustrating but will normally be enough to get the job done if you play smart. The bots are of course worse than most experienced players; but an easy choice over reckless or  foolhardy players.There are still a few bugs present that can kill a run. An occasional Humongoro will get stuck in battle stages, bots will sometimes get stuck outside of nav by charging, blinking, or jumping. I crash when opening the steam overlay for some reason (unless I alt-tab out first).It can be grindy but the loop is fun. There is definitely room for more maps, characters, and items. The current roadmap shows all of these coming in future updates. I can highly recommend if you have 1 or 2 buddies. It is decent solo but nothing compared to building a party and synergizing different toons in different ways. _childDocuments_.review: This is probably the most solid early access game I have played in a long time. I'm 60 hours in and I still feel like my characters and actual progression still need to get better to hit end game. The toughest mission I have been able to take down so far is a hard and it was no cake walk. There are still 2 tiers above that. Even though it's a small population and the AI is frustrating (mage AI gets stuck on one map and overheals, tank AI doesnt revive when both other characters are down), the game is still worth getting for the challenge.I like the take on the 3 player team rather than the traditional 4. I also like how there are no daily quests shoved down your throat like most games. Just pick it up and go. Legendary gear doesn't feel like a total grind to achieve (although I do wish it was a bit more challenging). There are also enough characters to learn so the experience doesn't get stale.There are most certainly a few changes I'd like to see (longer dungeons/raids, more puzzles, larger community, fixed AI, time trials, solo dungeons) but for what it is worth, I totally recommend it. It is still early access. If you like team based progression RPGs, pick this up today.

_childDocuments_.review: To start, most comments are correct that this game is not designed to be played solo. Thats the intent here, this is a CO-OP game at it's core.But if you have a group of 3 to play this game with (which I do thankfully), it is a BLAST. (Also, bots are being added in the future so you CAN play the game with just 1 or 2 people and not wait around for a 3rd random in queue.)Me and my 2 friends are always looking for great co-op games to play, from MMOs to party games. Blightbound sits comfortably in the co-op hack and slash genre. The connectivity features are super clear, invite friends is a cinch. Additionally, you can play with 2 players locally and invite a third, which is genuingly rare in co-op / online multiplayer games. This means me and my GF don't have to buy 2 copies of the game, can play on one computer, and our third friend can still join us via internet connection.Gameplay itself is very clean. It's a bit simple, but fulfilling your party role is truly the focus here. The 3 class archtypes are very distinct and clear in their roles. Mage heals and provides shields. Assassin deals big damage and inturrupts boss big attacks. Tank draws agro and blocks hits. All 3 classes pump out alot of damage in between fulfilling these roles, but they're all very important. If one player goes down, the entire fight starts going south. If one player is not fulfilling their role, the entire party can feel it.Theres alot of characters to unlock, tho admittedly they don't feel wildly different from each other within their class archtype, but it's definetly enough to keep things fresh. Characters level up and require you to assign stat point improvements, so it lets you experiment with different builds. That said, you can't reset your stats (at least I haven't figured out how) and that really makes the game harsh for no reason. Would love to be able to reset stats so I don't regret putting points in the wrong thing.Overall, this is a great co-op hack and slash. The look you get is just rewarding enough thanks to a pretty in depth crafting system. The voice acting is actually really flavorful. The story is pretty bleh and the maps all suffer from the same aesthetic causing them to look very similar, but if you've got a group of 3 this is going to be a fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Blightbound

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing game that truly shines only if you have 3 players in your party.I have spent 10 hours playing this game, and I would say at least 2 hours of that, if not more... has been spent in que... waiting for a player to join my party.This is very disappointing, and truly is a shame.This game is lacking some very necessary elements.For example, where is the harm in allowing players to play this with 1 or 2 players instead of 3.Why not allow players who have progressed in the game, to unlock higher starting notoriety.This game feels very stagnant in its current build with nothing to do, after you experience high notoriety runs. Going from a high notoriety, to easy tutorial level stuff… is very unrewarding, and a disruptive flow.The characters, while different in appearance, don’t feel all that interesting when it comes to kit. The fact that different characters don’t have completely different kits, is shocking. Though I can see this being a design choice, because of the limited scope of weapons and trinkets that actually matter.I would suggest these changes.-Add support to allow players to play with people missing from their party. Remove obstacles that all characters cannot complete, in levels or add a way for others to trigger them…. -Remove the abilities from legendaries and epics that effect certain abilities… or limit them to certain abilities that all characters will possess. I.E. Shield block, heal, execute.- Make scaling modifiers to the game that players can toggle based on their current party. I.E. Make a new building that allows player to add more challenge to the start of their runs, for increased rewards. I.E. Epic monsters a 25% more likely to spawn, and have 15% more chance to drop an item. Bosses have 20% less HP and 20% less damage, but normal mobs gain 75% HP, and named monsters deal 20% more damage.-Make the characters seem like different people who have lived very different lives and developed different skill sets. Right now the similarities between characters who are supposed to be distinctly different, is unimaginative and boring. Give different characters different dashes, attack patterns, make passives more noticeable, make the abilities they share(Shield block, heal, and execute) Visually different, and remove similarities in all of their other abilities.-DO NOT be afraid to add more items for niche circumstances, I want there to be more items in the Epic and Rare slot that feel useful for a certain thing. Just because an item is uniquely powerful for a certain situation, doesn’t mean you shouldn’t make it. Also, please shy away from the idea that an item needs to be legendary to be powerful. I understand the mechanic behind the rarity system and making it easier to show players which items are generally powerful… but I think there is a unique benefit to making Epic items powerful and unique as well.Again, this game is EARLY in its development, and should be praised for the creative idea. Also we should be thanking this devs for sharing this project with us this early. So here are the things I enjoy.-The art style, my goodness this is a refreshing view.-The character story progression, id even love to see this built upon more. Making characters more different or having the models change based on the story progression… but also make this longer, or more unique.-I love and hate the loot system here… while it feels rewarding… without prefixes or rolled stats you gain gear here… too fast, which could be a problem for sustained interest.TLDR; This game shows promise, and will entertain you and 2 friends for several hours before some replayability issues arise.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't lie to you fellas, I had some serious doubts about this game. We've had several forgettable beat-em-ups over the years and it looked like there was another that was going to be added to the pile.Bought the game because I love Awesomenauts so much. They've been pooling all their resources into Blightbound to the detriment of their MOBA, so I was hoping it'll be worth it.Despite the lone, awkward fighting in the tutorial, my first online mission had me love the game right away. It's a strange mix between Trine, Darkest Dungeon, Awesomenauts, Diablo and unlike Swords and Soldiers, it's a formula that harmonizes well.It's much more interesting than your typical loot crawler. The three characters have specific jobs to do, and if each player does it right, they'll get rewarded for it. Sometimes you'll be confronted with puzzles, which offer a great change of pace during a run.Graphics look amazing. The artists at Ronimo were working overtime. I'm glad they're keeping up with modern rendering. Shadows, lights and fog really complement some already great looking environments.It's a great game, really. I highly recommend it. Despite early access, it feels pretty complete as it is. There is enough content to keep you playing for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game with high hopes, as it seemed like a super fun game to play with two friends on a call or something. It was definitely an experience, but I wouldn't really call it fun.Firstly, the main menu is just two buttons, "Play" and "Quit". They don't let you customize your settings before going into the actual game, which can prevent people with lower end computers from playing altogether (I know this isn't a very resource heavy game but there are computers and computers). The game plays nicely, if not a bit sloggy.The tutorial's done and I want to play with my friends now. Getting in a party together is really difficult for no reason, the game sometimes just doesn't want you to play online so you join the party but in offline mode and you can't change it. After a lot of trial an error we managed to make it work, played a few levels. It was very mediocre. "Maybe we'll have fun after we play it for a while" we kept thinking, but after having to play the exact same level over and over to unlock more levels we gave up, and tried to refund the game. Of course, with all the technical problems, we spent more than two hours on the game, half of which was probably just trying to figure out how to make it work.So now one of my friends is stuck with this game that feels raw and coded on Scratch. This is a great idea for a game, but the execution is terrible. Shouldn't have been pulled out of Early Access so early.Recommendation? Maybe wait until the game is better. Also, buy on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoy this game. It has some puzzle elements, loot-gathering, intense fights and unique characters.The art style as well is just gorgeous.I would mostly however like to clarify something mentioned in quite a few of the negative reviews-There are a significant amount of reviews complaining that it's marked as "Singleplayer" in steam, when it's only online.They're making the assumption that online = multiplayer. It's just how information and saves are stored, it seems. You absolutely can play singleplayer. You don't need to play with anyone else, but you can with the exact same method of choosing a level.It's like considering Warframe a "Singleplayer" game along with its multiplayer and co-op tags.A bit of an odd description, but not false. You can absolutely play tons of the game by yourself with no interaction with anyone. Same goes for this one. Multiplayer works great, but it's not a requirement. Being online is.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game. I know it is still in open beta, but I'm not talking about bugs, a lot of the design decisions feel like they are in service of the game mechanics and not in the service of making the game fun to play. For instance, I've lost so many matches because I can't revive my teammates (or they can't revive me) because doing so means that we have to stand in a boss' AOE attack for a few seconds. The only counterplay to this is to run around avoiding the AOE's on the ground (ignoring your teammates), or attempting to revive them and risk dying.  Give this game a few months, it's not finished yet and needs a lot of work. Hopefully they will make the quality of life changes to make this game fun.  In the mean time, I'll be playing games that don't punish me for wanting to play them.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this with I played thousands of hours of Diablo 1-3. I absolutely love dungeon crawling, grinding, looting games.I know this game is Early Access and a lot of things aren't done or ready yet. But that said, I think the issue isn't bugs or crashing. It's not the party system, champion selection, etc.The fundamental problem is the game isn't engaging. The dynamics of it aren't fun alone or even in a group. The loot system seems eh, unclear what I even want or will work up to. The dungeons themselves are monotonous, and poorly designed.  Some people complain about loading screens, that doesn't bug me. It's a bad user experience, but if the gameplay was actually fun, they would be tolerable. I will put up with a lot for if the core game mechanics are fun. Blightbound doesn't have fun core gameplay. The combat isn't interesting. The classes are simplistic and shallow. There's no reason to continue playing or feeling like I need to get another dungeon run in.I think the developers need to seriously re-think the core of the game. I wouldn't recommend it in its current form. Hopefully it improves drastically as development continues. I would love to see a successor to Diablo, but right now, this isn't even close.

_childDocuments_.review: I come from a long line of dungeon-crawling maniacs. Sure, this isn't as robust (yet) as Diablo, nor as story driven, but let's be fair about some things...(aside from a rocky/still rocky launch)- cross-play is a HUGE deal.- play with friends (stop being a loser and make some)- I watched my significant other finagle the bots through many 'almost impossible' situations and level his home base numerous times on the launch day (for those who clearly have no patience, savvy, or determination)The game play is pretty even keeled. I honestly wish there were more well-thought boss encounters OUTSIDE of a level's final boss. There are a couple of great end bosses that are tricky almost every time. Maybe more puzzles, or timed trials, a little bit of zest.We still haven't really figured out how we're supposed to navigate the 'Impossible' levels. Even on 'Normal' there are mob attacks that will one shot people.I also bought this before the release and somehow missed the DLC releases and there's no going back for that special content even though I probably had access. My fiance bought this on the PS5 and his heroes are joining with Legendary items, and he has all the special Cosmetics available... So, I do feel like I was shafted on these concepts.I wish that ALL of the warriors and mages weren't male and all the assassins weren't female. It would be neat to have a mix, and more 'creature-like' heroes.Overall, we're hopeful that the devs will continue to support the game and release interesting/well-thought content.Side note:When has a game been 100% great out of the gates in the last 15 years? The moment the internet came into the picture was the moment game devs realized they could hot patch to their heart's desire. Huge developers are guilty of this... half-♥♥♥♥♥♥ game release/go-live, where the game works but it's obvious it is not complete.

_childDocuments_.review: [original "Early Access Review," posted August 14, 2020.]-- Should you buy this game right now?In most cases, probably not.-- Should you buy this game eventually?In my opinion, yes. _childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of games like Castle Crashers, Diablo, or Dungeon crawlers of any variety that you can play with a few of your friends, this game delivers in spades.PROS:It's got a great aesthetic, with killer personality. You expect nothing less from the creators of Awesomenauts.LOOT, and cool loot. Even now as I write this review in the initial early access, loot allows lots of very cool and different play styles for the various characters and classes. And you can work towards the loot you want, or just happen to stumble into something cool that you didn't know you wanted. Very engaging gameplay, that's challenging. Keep in mind, as you play more with the same party, you get increasingly harder quests. The most difficult quests will require you to communicate, and quickly react and play well. Or that'll be it and you'll miss out on some sweet loot, and take some blight sickness.Lots of different ways to play the game. So far there's 3 base classes, and 3 characters for each class that share some aspects of the class, but bring their own unique skills and passives that change things up. You combine this with the notoriety system, that makes increases difficulty as you play, and you have a great excuse to try new characters on low notoriety, and then go back to your best and favorite guys to tackle the real impossible stuff. The combat is close to perfect, visually it's extremely easy to read whats going on, and what you need to do. Hits feel meaty, and setting up big WOMBO COMBOS with your pals is always fun. Personally, I think they could do with introducing even MORE enemies on screen, and make things more hectic. The game is definitely at it's best when you're scrambling to control the situation. CONS:It's early access still, and while it has an incredibly solid foundation, there's still a lot of work to be done on the content side of things. At the time of this review, there's 4 areas with a couple different quests between them, but I'd like to see that variety continue to climb as time goes on.Some bosses at the moment just aren't on the same level as others. And some are a little broken, as to bexpected with early access. That said, when the bosses work, and you're SCRAMLBIN' and movin', and communicating, it's honestly a better experience that I've ever had in a game like Diablo or PAth of exile, and that's largely due to the clarity with which the combat communicates to you where BAD space is, and good space.This isn't a game for solo players, it's co-op only, and while there is match making, this game is absolutely at it's best when you're playing with pals. However, everyone I've queued with randomly I've welcomed with open arms and met some cool friends. So even if you can't convince your pals to play this thing, If you're not a fan of 2D brawlers like Streets of Rage, this game might just not appeal to you. That said, I think it's worth giving a shot if you really like dungeon crawlers, and wanna try it with a new spin.Match making can be a little slow sometimes, but jump into the discord server and you can ahve a group going real quick. Game lacks some polish, it's hard sometimes to know what skills an item will or won't effect (is left click a skill? My right click? My ultimate? My titan skills?), there's no stats pages, there's no history of runs, there's no end mission stats screens, but based on the developers past work on AWesomenauts, I expect nothing less th an for these features to be fleshed out.Overall, even in early access, it's a solid 9/10. And it's looking like a BIG 10er if they can keep up the momentum and add the couple of pieces that are missing.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is not as fun as I expected. They claim it's 9 characters to unlock, but the two I found is very similar, they have the same skillset as the previous archclass. The loot is very uninteresting and that's where the "builds" are. Which is mostly cooldown reduction or crit chance/damage. Game needs a lot of work. Many of the enemies seems the same to me as well, either they do damage around themselves or in a straight line. Most dungeons looks more or less the same to me. There are some OK puzzles in this, some teamwork required and some best done alone, as you need to think. And it's mostly getting the right candles lit or all of them lit (and some blow out others etc). Kinda boring to be honest.If you play as a rogue, you have a lot og AoE, and currently it's too risky to go in, as you'll end up dead most of the time. Don't know if that's the tank not tanking, or the mobs running to the nearest player to hit them or what the issue really is there.If you play as the mage, he has the healing responsibility alone, and can get up to three mana. Mana which drops of enemies, which most of the time is in melee range, AND other characters can pick them up, ruining it for you. Would be nice if the mana that the team picks up goes to you instead of vanishing.If you play as the tank, you usually have a lot more HP, but it's hard to see when an enemy is about to attack (as you want to block incoming damage), and if there's 3 or more, you're better off just standing there, taunting and blocking. But the tank is by far the coolest with the spell effects: his ultimate makes you pop wings as a paladin in wow, or avatar f you know warrior. It's the coolest looking ability by far.Right now, the characters feel the same (from the same archclass), they have the same abilities and 1 unique passive. They can all wear the same gear except weapons. But the same archclass can use the same weapons. The dungeons are very similar to me, same with puzzles. Enemies need variety. It's an ok skeleton of a game, but needs work, content and variety in all kind of things.You need to get to level 9 before you can choose a specific hero as well, it's all RNG before that. That took me about 1-1,5 hours. Currently, would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Moving around the map feels awful, all the characters feel like they run in slow motion and they're responsiveness is really sluggish.2. Melee enemy units hit me without making any connection to my model, leaving me wondering why I should even bother with dodging when I can just outdps the fodder. Why punish the player for attempting to maneuver when it's encouraged?3. Locking players out of character select until you reach a level threshold is for lack of a better word- awful. It's truly awful that a game that's trying to display it has a steep learning curve wants to force you to play different characters during the LEARNING period. Broadening your skills across all champions is fine, but not when they're trying to learn.4. Bosses are truly out of balance in comparison to the other encounters on map. When I dish out and take punishment in dicey encounters it felt fine, but bosses melting you with tethers and puddles that have next to no true indicators of the danger is horrible. On top of that any interrupt I use on boss channeled attacks doesn't do anything so why give me an interrupt if the mechanic doesn't really help? On top of that as mentioned above dodging and maneuvering is sluggish and feels awful with the exception of blink dashing.5. I have to struggle to close menus in the hub because i have to click off the boxes or tab in and out because you won't let me collapse menus with ESC.6. All the characters have some goofy and hammy way of speaking while delivering random and unwarranted exposition. Why are all the heroes tonedeaf to the setting? The enemies and setting are dark and cool, why is the dialogue dead set on removing you from the immersion at all times?7. Don't ever force a game to REQUIRE two other people, have AI if you must but waiting for players is awful and expecting multiple friends to opt into Early Access to get the proper assessment of the experience is inconsiderate and unfair.8. The art direction and music/sounds feel great, but it's all marred in the problems above and honestly the game doesn't feel as good to play as it is to watch in action with devstreams. If the game feels this unfun out of the gate I don't want to risk waiting for it to get better past my refund window. I will come back to this game in the future if it gets significant improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Hate to do it, but after a few more hours I've gotta change my tune on this one.The levels all feel very samey. That's all on that one- fighting the same bosses, often in the same levels.I actually wasn't having a hard time finding teammates past the first character level or so, but there are, in my view, fundamental gameplay issues. You're always playing the same three characters- one of each, in every round. Build diversity, if it exists, is a late game thing. Their are many different 'sub-classes,' but as far as I can tell, they all feel nearly exactly the same. The only difference seems to be their secondary skill. That makes some difference, but doesn't move the underlying tank/healermage/rogue feel-needle by much.I've got comments on in case I've misunderstood something (not that anyone should care what I think), but at this point I can't see any reason to keep playing this one. Hopefully it has more coming later in the EA, but it feels flat now at 7 hours played.--------This is a fun game. It has a little bit of 'if darkest dungeon was an ARPG' feel going.It's best played multiplayer, and at the moment, matchmaking is spotty. Sometimes you get a couple people, sometimes you sit there for five minutes. You can play with bots, but that's not quite as fun to me. If you enjoy single player only, the bots do their jobs serviceably. There is another game that was quite similar to this many years back, which has recently gotten a platinum collectors version etc... and I can't remember its name. Dragon something, I think. Helpful, I know. That said, if you're watching the trailers and you've played that one, you'll know what I mean. This has deeper systems (though I'm only a handful of hours into it), and more importantly, no egregious anime tits on the female characters. That's all I've got- it feels like a good game, but it needs a community to thrive. It's not that no one is playing, but it is a toss-up regarding whether you'll find anyone or not, and the fact that there can only be one of each class archetype in each game (warrior, assassin, mage) means that the possible matches are further diminished (unless I'm misunderstanding the system... but I don't think I am- you may be able to select 'I'll play whatever')I do hope it picks up a following because the games with other players are quite fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine an aRPG mixed with a brawler, and you've pretty much got this game. I recommend it with some serious caveats. There is a desyncing issue, and stability has been a problem--every time one bug gets squashed, another appears. Another frustration is the blight system, which locks you out of playing your characters if you die too many times. It's unforgiving, and means you can potential lock yourself out of all your characters. It would be nice if it passively went down between runs, or only accumulated after a team wipe. Right now, you gain blight if someone disconnects. That, combined with the desync issue, is brutal. Also, a lot of the heroes share abilities, which makes them redundant. I will come back and re-reviews this game in a couple months to see if any progress has been made, but the bugginess makes it drop from 8/10 to a 6 or 7.
