_childDocuments_.review: Honest Review for Early Access: Also note I bought the 3 pack for myself and 2 friends. While my review says: Do Not Recommend, I would LIKE to recommend this game! It has A LOT of potential. So maybe by release, I would recommend it! If the changes below are implemented. Pros: -Really Great combat!-Great Art Style!-Great Co-op mechanics between the 3 players-Classes are fun, and style of switching characters in and out is great!-Has A LOT of potential! Cons:-Game will randomly freeze, 1 every 5 games. Forcing you to quit and lose the level for all 3 players-Levels needs an entire re-design for the entire game. The levels have to much back tracking, load screens, pointless segements. And only having 10 or so levels to play. It gets repetitive really fast. -Game needs proper world progression. Better structured levels, leading through acts and new environments. Only then revisiting those levels on higher difficulties later. Needs more of a Diablo style act campaign. -There seems to be no way to respec your heroes. So once you make a mistake, your heroes are nerfed forever. -Missions seem to have a timer, which neither myself or most allies are aware of. Suddenly everyone just randomly dies without warning. This mechanics needs to be made more apparent.-Gear could use a better progression. All good items are acquired through crafting which is cool. But you never get a sense of fun loot along the way. -Inventory needs to be unlimited. With the point above, you are always collecting EVERYTHING to craft new items for all 3 class types. But the inventory is limited, and everything is required. You cannot afford to discard items, yet you are forced to do so.. Its a real pain. Best bet is to only craft and gear 1 class at a time. Which defeats the play style of this game.-Classes: The concept of multiple classes and class types is great. But unfortunately falls a bit short. Most of the new characters are exactly the same as the last, with maybe 1 skill changed out. Needs more range and variety between them. However, spending stats differently to make one tank more of a brawler and the other more of an actual tank. Is one way to play it. However, there is no respec... You'll learn this when its too late.With all that said. I'm really sad to not recommend this game. I'm also frustrated with the fact this could have almost been one of my new favourite games. The core mechanics, art style and gameplay is SPOT ON. But the itemisation, level design, campaign flow, & heroes all need a MAJOR face lift. I think with a proper flowing campaign, with levels that feel unique and memorable. Proper gear progression along the way, leading into new acts and environments. Which snowball into New Game+ difficulties. Tweeks to heroes with Respec options. This game has potential to be Legendary. Just to many things feeling incomplete at this moment. Still fun for 10+ hours! :)I really hope this game gets fine tuned for release. I will come back and review the final product. I don't regret my 3 pack purchase. But I also wouldn't recommend it, just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Blightbound hits a particular type of nostalgia for me. Fond memories of teaming up with friends to slash our way through Castle Crashers or iconic phrases like “Warrior needs food badly!” It definitely has that classic co-op hack ‘n’ slash feel going for it, but also has some RPG elements layered on top for an older, maybe more refined audience. For instance, each class (warrior, rogue, and mage) play very differently. Each level requires each player to be on top of their specific skills and execute them when needed. The mage is the only character that heal and if they aren’t on the spot then you won’t be getting too far. The added complexity makes the encounters more interested than a typical hack ‘n’ slash. It also means you can replay them for different experiences.You unlock many different characters over the campaign, each with their own personal story, and unique abilities. For instance, the second mage character you unlock comes with a “gravity well” ability that pulls all the enemies in. This opens the warrior up to unleash massive damage and the rogue to drop area of effect abilities. It may look a little confusing and chaotic at first, but once you figure out each character’s rhythm and role, the game really shines. It can also be quite challenging, requiring everyone to be on point for boss battles and other challenges.Each level rewards you with loot and money, and you get *something* even if you fail the level. You collect weapons, armor, and trinkets for your various characters that give them boosts and boons. As you level up your base you also get access to item crafters. It’s a decent addition to what could easily been a repetitive hack ‘n’ slash experience.That’s not to say you won’t be repeating levels and grinding for gold and materials. There are about a dozen levels at launch to play through, but luckily each one is a pretty unique. You may be rescuing prisoners to boost your numbers in one, and the next you could be thwarting an evil cult’s ritual. Each level is broken up into a hand full of rooms and many of them have secret, optional areas you check out if you want some extra challenge of loot. They also offer a large variety of color palettes and architecture, which looks great against the detailed, colorful characters.All in all, Blightbound is a solid co-op focused dungeon crawler. It has enough unique aspects to set it apart from others in the genre, and is fun for both casual and competitive players. If you’re worried about not being able to find someone to play with, you should know that it has crossplay matchmaking between PC, Xbox, and PlayStation, so no matter where you play you should be able to find others to delve with. You can also play with bots too, which are pretty good at their jobs.

I get the devs want to keep the game "alive" by making it where bots only fill when others aren't online. It doesn't work though as it just rubs people the wrong way. It's why most games have the ability to play private lobbies by yourself or with bots. Vermintide 2 is a good example. You can play solo with bots, in a private group with friends or online with randoms. They give incentives for people to play online with random people, not make the game inaccessible to the people who don't want to.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't complain much since I got this game as a gift. It looks nice and... and that's it. There are just way too many things that devs can improve. Starting from adding BOTS/AI, ending with fixing Notoriety and adding sort of an "end-game" part to the core mechanics of the game. It really felt very "YIKES" when I discovered that Notoriety is actually bound to the players that you play with. I mean, the way the game works, is that it wants me to queue for a game with 2 randoms and I have zero idea who they are and how long they will play for. One thing I'm sure of, is that they will leave the party eventually and I will have to start over with the boring low difficulty. I want to explore the game and how far I can go, but it's own matchmaking system does not allow me to do so. Basically, if you don't have 2 more friends playing this game, you need a miracle to get to the hardest difficulties.Despite that, I also felt bored from combat almost immidiately. I want to have more skills and more options to make some sick combos. Modifying my gear and maybe even skills, with some support gems/trinkets, I really wanted to create my own build but I'm almost sure that there are simply not enough options to do so. You go into a dungeon, gather some loot, equip it and level up. That's it. If only devs can sit and talk about the content they want to add, listen to the community and implement the ideas from various sources, they will definitely come up with a very solid and polished game. But so far, I cannot give this game a good review.Having said that, you have to keep in mind that this is an early access game, so HOPEFULLY things will change. I will definitely come back to this game and check on how everything is going.

_childDocuments_.review: let me start off by saying that I am pretty sure this game will be great by the time it leaves early access. however, I don't think it's ready now for public consumption, considering how I made it in 30 minutes before rushing to the uninstall button.+ fantastic, one of a kind art style.+ nice sound effects.+ the actual combat (stabbing, casting spells, etc.) feels super satisfying, when the animations are working properly.- the first dungeon after the tutorial has TERRIBLE AI for the bots you're running with; multiple times they would just run around instead of reviving me. one time they just froze there and I thought I would have to call it quits there.- the bosses in that dungeon do insane damage, and the mage doesn't get enough heals to make it so that your party is not constantly trading spots reviving each other instead of fighting the boss, because you're holding on by a sliver. combine this with the horrendous AI, and you have a first practice dungeon after the tutorial which is a long, painful slog where the game consistently is not letting you do the thing it is best at, stabbing monsters.- the fact that you are saving all of these nerds throughout this dungeon for 15 minutes all so they can die immediately as soon as they become support NPC's makes me not want to replay this dungeon since where's the reward? there almost certainly is one, but it isn't effectively communicated, so I have no incentive to return as is.- general jank; levers will seem like they're close enough to be pulled and will have the prompt to pull them pop up, but you actually need to be one inch closer to do that. characters will momentarily get caught on terrain. there isn't much indication to go where you need to because there will be part of the level obscured by the camera.I'll come back to this when it's a better, cleaner experience. til then, it's giving me no desire to push through the jank any more than I have, and I have plenty of other games begging to be tried. not gonna be refunding to support the development, and if you want to do so as well, that's the biggest reason why I would potentially suggest picking it up now. if you want a genuinely good game when you purchase it, wait. this thing has potential, but it just isn't there yet.edit responding to the dev: I did see that it has long left early access, however I have other obligations rn (reviewing new releases, my day job, personal projects, etc.). I appreciate your evident passion for the game Niel, and intend to get around to it soon enough.

I'm downvoting this game for sexism, but its not like it sounds, let me explain!This game has three classes, warrior, rogue, mage. Its a pretty simple setup.There's a fair few heroes, 13 at the time of writing. Among them is 4 women.That's fine, i'm not complaining about that, i don't expect equal genders or anything.The problem is, there are four female rogues. Every single female character is a rogue. There are no lady warriors, no witches or sorceresses. You have a choice between backstabbing or sausage.This is made a bit worse by the fact that the heroes within a class are pretty similar. about half of the stuff that each hero can do is generic and shared with the others in their class. So all these girls play the same.This is statistically improbable, it feels deliberate, and nonsensical. I want to play a girl and i want to not play a rogue, i don't think that's a lot to ask I feel like the designers are working out some personal issues about a backstabbing ex wife.It doesn't even make sense. Maybe you could make a case that women are too small for a tank role generally, though we could still have some amazonesque barbarian lady to be an exception.But sorceresses and witches are a popular thing.  It takes no muscles to say magical words and support the team from afar, that would be more fitting than rogue. The mage role is also the healer. Isn't healing the girliest playstyle of all ?

_childDocuments_.review: After Dungeons & Dragon Dark Alliance flopped hard on release I was itching for another co-op brawler in a fantasy setting. Blightbound is here to scratch that itch. Oddly the game kept crashing during the tutorial mode so I had to skip the tutorial halfway through. EDIT: The tutorial issue has been fixed in the latest patch and no longer crashes.From there you have your starting town, the refuge as the hub setting before you go on your adventures into dungeons and dangerous areas. There are three types of characters, Warriors, Assassins and Mages. The Mage is also a healer. You can unlock new characters during missions. Each character can be levelled up, equipped with new weapons and trinket accessories. As you progress you also upgrade your starting refuge town. The game is easy to play on a controller which is good for couch co-op or splitscreen co-op. The combat is fun and intense, especially on higher difficulties.There weren't many players in matchmaking but this is to be expected with any indie title that doesn't have a gigantic budget for a mass marketing campaign. If you play solo you have two bots on your side instead.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I would like to say that I love this game. The sense of progression is very addictive. The gameplay with friends feels great and the artstyle hits the right tones for me. But there are two major issues with it:1. Server-side hit detection.This game is very challenging if you choose a dungeon that is "hard" or "tough" or even a more difficult dungeon and I like that. Your lifebar can vanish in an instant if you are doind something wrong and that is good. What is not good is that if your not the host sometimes you die for apparently no reason. The reason turns out to be that you were standing in a laser but it was not on your screen because of lag or packets got lost  etc.. On the computer of the host though you died for whatever reason so you are dead now. It is very frustrating, especially since you have to finish a dungeon to get the good loot. That turns the game into a RNG game since the host can easily declare you for dead at almost any time. The internet is not very reliable and that is why games like Dark souls and nioh and others have client-side hit detection where unless you see with your own eyes on your end that you got hit then everything is fine. Blightbound is not fine.2. Unclear visuals.  The camera is too low. Some  objects are in the foreground and some are in the background. When the screen is cluttered with enemies and enemy attacks there is no way of figuring out what is actually happening in the background. There is this guy with a huge bell that summons a wall of crystals with his attacks that covers the entire screen. It is ridiculous. There are also invisible walls that pop up in some bossfights. Upon nearer inspection you can see that those are mist walls but they are just barely visible and easy to miss in a hectic bossfight even on multiple repeat sessions.I am aware that this is an Early access game and it has it's share of bugs. But things like the camera being on an angle that is too close to the floor so objects in the foreground cover up the objects ins the background cannot be fixedi in this phase of gamedevelopment. Just like the server-side hit detection cannot be just switched to client-side hit detection with a push of a button. I'm pretty sure but I'd like to be wrong here. Anyway, I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly really love the idea of this game! _childDocuments_.review: The game concept is great, and I enjoyed the game play as is. However, I do not suggest this game at current stage. So many bugs, from UI to AI. The item system also need some work as it is not attracting at all. Will revisit at some point but currently it is just a test beta, not for public.Update 14/10/2023:Dead game, Developer bankrupt. Game developing is hard. Updated review 19 Oct 2021:After forcing myself playing this game(more like no other game to play at the moment lol). I think I know where the problem is:1, New player & introductionThere are certain expectations for a new player after playing for the 1st hour, and that will help the new player have an idea if they should invest more time into it.This game did a really bad job/design by scaling the mechanical difficulty to a really high level, and didn't introduce any NPC or mechanic to help the new player to go through this stage. Imaging telling someone to play this for half an hour and end up dying on a lvl 1 dungeon, then fail again and again. 2, The dungeonThis part is fine, but with its length and difficulty, it will not only add frustration to new players, but also veteran player. A shorter dungeon with more variety would be better.3, The AI and current queuingThis goes hand on hand with the other design choice. The AI is obversely for when there is no enough player, and not to replace the players, but unfortunately because the lengthy dungeon and difficulty, the risk/reward when playing with a random player is just not worth trying.The game is fun and competitive, but the developer should really think about balance the early game so more people will have the time and interest continue playing the game. This game has a lot of potential and depth but unfortunately I can not recommend this game to new players, especially if you don't have a lot of time going through the early stage of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying the game so far! It's really challenging to play solo though. The bots are decent, but they do some really dumb things sometimes. For instance, the mage loves to double spam the heal for some reason and is always eating up an extra orb as a result. Also, puzzles can be a nightmare with bots since they tend to go ballistic if you don't position yourself in a certain way. Bots will also randomly dive into their deaths when the win could have been easy with normal players.This brings me to my last gripe with the game. Finding a matchup is near impossible. It would be nice if there were lobbies or some way to see what classes are needed in order to get matched up more often. Roughly 80% of the time I have to deal with just soloing with my bots which has made progress pretty slow.On the positive side, unlocking and gearing heroes is pretty rewarding. It's a little difficult to see the effects of my stat spread though. However, there's a lot of replay value in doing the camp side quests as well as figuring out what to do next in each hero's personal quests. At the same time, completing those personal quests open up the lore which keeps me interested in what's happening next. I think this game has great potential if the QOL issues are fixed for release since the strengths are worth the stress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had a lot of potential. I enjoyed the class aspect where every person in the party had to play a different class, no repeats. Dedicated tank role, mage role, etc. The combat was also very nice with a lot of unique playstyles. Sadly, the game was hampered by the developers' stubbornness to change certain features until it was too late.This included but was not limited to:- Forced online play (no singleplayer/offline whatsoever)- Blight build-up system to force you off of preferred roles- No way of resetting your attributes- Tons of disconnects that compounded the horrible map tier aspect that required chaining map runs in a single session (always have to be online btw)Although a lot of these systems were eventually changed, it was already too late to keep the game alive. It's very hard to find a reason to play this game even now. I think it would've been better to have had a campaign with a few acts, and a separate roguelite mode to keep players coming back. But, I cannot recommend this game as it is right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the game is great. It has some issues and more than a few bugs, but nothing that makes me want to hang it up. I won't list any bugs here, because the dev team is already working on them and making great progress. I would anticipate the game will be rock solid shortly.The only true issue I see is the notoriety system. Play through missions with a team, incrementally unlock a harder challenge and better loot. Makes sense. Unfortunately, the system will reset your notoriety whenever your group changes, whether you a leaving the group, or if someone else leaves. This can pull the rug out from under you as you are building up momentum in notoriety, only to have someone leave the group randomly, putting you back down to 0. I can see that at least a few of the personal goals tied to certain characters revolve around grouping with friends, and that seems to tie in well to maintaining a group for longer periods, but sometimes that just isn't an option. This can take what is already a grind, and make it feel virtually meaningless. I mean, how many common items does one person need. I'm not sure exactly what the fix is for it, but the dev team has my complete confidence that they will come up with something nuanced and satisfying, that preserves the spirit of the system. Other than that, it's a great experience. Hack, slash and blast enemies to bits. Find fun and powerful combos and synergies. and best of all, LOOT. Lots of unique and fun loot to find, and the crafting system makes for something to work towards. Leveling is fast and fun, and each character has a great, unique feel that fills a certain function on a team.10/10 would recommend to people to pick up, even in EA.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: this game is a blast in its own right and myself and my 2 friends spent 9 hours playing this over the course of one night. One of the big issues my friends and I have are for Hemog and his lesser General versions. Idk if it's bug of some sort or an unclear mechanic, but no matter the difficulty (normal-impossible), we spent up to TWENTY minutes playing whack-a-mole because no matter what strategy we come up with (kill all clones or attack only him), he dives under after a single hit. Because of this one enemy, we went from full steam ahead to calling it a night.Other than that, some bugs need to be ironed out. When playing a mage, my friend became silenced and couldn't do anything but run around the area trying not to die until we crossed to the next room. In that same run, my warrior somehow lost one of his shield icons with no explanation as to why and no blight sickness. Also, when playing a new warrior character with no blight built up, I was met with blight sickness with no explanation as to why.Aside from those things, we really enjoy the bulk of the game and intend on spending time leveling most, if not all the characters to max.

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this, with a few buts.The game is a cool and interesting concept that has potential. However, currently it's very early access. The classes/characters need some work to make the different characters of the classes feel more unique. Constant disconnects suck. The levels are a bit boring after a few times, and some of the enemies need a huge overhaul (that death ball head thing that will insta kill you), The minimap is complete garbage and you need to be able to expand the map to see the whole level or what you have explored.It just needs some polish, so hopefully the devs keep working on it and deliver something good. _childDocuments_.review: At the moment I'm on the fence about this game. It's fun when its working right and you're not disconnecting from your group and causing your notoriety to reset but as of the last update, it seems to be working fine if you're queing up with some friends but still buggy if you're on your own. Otherwise, I love the fact that it forces you to play other classes besides getting stuck to one. I know most don't appreciate it but I do. I do hope they fix the issue of those who decide and que up and just sit inside the instance for the sake of making the group suffer and cause them to lose their notoriety and leave group. They should implement some kind of penalty system that will not allow you to join a group (5 to 10 min) if you leave early but not disconnected due to game malfunction. WoW did a decent job implementing this when people were refusing to play their role and gave the group the option kick that one individual who refused to leave or was AFK the entire fight. Just something to think about. Honestly, I really do like the game and hope it progresses well when the full version is released without all the current flaws. I understand its an early release and it will come with its challenges but I hope the devs are listening and making the changes necessary to make this a fun and potentially great experience for those who bought into it early... _childDocuments_.review: This game is simply amazing. I'm an rpg fan and a hobbyist game developer and Blindbound ticks all my boxes. Surely there are a few bugs here and there which I intend to report since a few are game breaking but the game is so good that I just ignore them and move on. And I'm a QA for a living so I have really high standards. The game is still in early access and clearly a lot of love has been  put in it. It is actually hand-drawn and it reminds me of a Co-op version of Darkest Dungeon but more action packed. Pulling a combo with the rogue where you dodge spikes, enemy abilities, take mana orb for your support and re-engage without being hit once is super satisfying. I love the control of the block skill on right click on tanks or the versatility of the support. Please buy this game to support the hard work that has been put into it. In my view it deserves every penny. I really hope it will expand and more content and heroes will be added to it because the ingredients are there and the potential of it is absolutely massive. Great game guys, for me it is a pleasure to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Bad: The game is extremly glitchy and some of the worst glitches I have ever encountered in a video game. Glitches such as not being able to progress throught the story because the game either dosen't register you have picked something up or you are doing something to quick for it I guess such as picking up a skull in one of the most glitchest missions in the game called To Whom the Bell Tolls and unlike the Metalica song the bell in this mission never tolls I guess because it won't allow you to progress through it, It got so bad that my friend left and might I add the game punishes you in 2 ways if your friend leaves by taking away your notoriety ( a system that rewards you for winning) and by taking away your Blight ( A system that will not allow you to play a character you want to play if they become blight struck) { Might I add ur not even allowed to pick ur character until you are level 9 which is kind of BS} So make sure you have a party because if you ever and I mean ever dare to queue with randoms you will feel the wrath of god or Blight in this case and the lack of items with drive you mad without notoriety. Like do you want a class that can do bursts of damage cc ur enemy's and HEAL! WELL YOUR IN LUCK BECAUSE THE MAGE CAN DO IT ALL! _childDocuments_.review: Lets start by saying there is a bit of a learning curve to this game. You WILL get frustrated early on and the inability to select your character or really understand the UI is a pain. The UI is not very clear and gameplay itself takes a few rounds to understand. This game is not very noob friendly or easy to pick up.Now that is out of the way.. the game shows a lot of promise. Graphically it's stellar and we're at the very beginning. For $11 it's a no-brainer but in for $18 in it's current state? I'd be hard pressed to recommend it at that cost unless you REALLY like Darkest Dungeon crossed with Diablo 3. My only hope is that the development is consistent and adds compelling gameplay. The game right now is hollow but as we know this is EA and there is no where to go but up from here.I need to see more variety between the heroes and unique items would also be interesting. Also more classes would be fun to see, since we're basically forced into linear "knight, mage and rogue" gameplay. What about Necro style? What about ranger? A monk? _childDocuments_.review: According to their update roadmap, this is a game you should pick up now and not wait on patches. Definitely the sort of game you'd only want to play for a few hours at a time anyways, just due to how repetitive the quests can get if you play them constantly, and new tangible content that you can play, farm and experience is set to come out one to two times per month. Recommended to pick up and play until you're bored after 20 hours and then come back for another 10 after each patch. Rare and game breaking bugs were patched and early access "features" continue to get patched out by dedicated devs. Especially if you have a few friends and the 3 pack is on sale again, this game is definitely worth your time and money. If you have to rely on matchmaking keep in mind the game won't start with less than 3 players, at least for now, as devs are working on bots as well.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is self is fun as long as you have dedicated premates. The game is punishing you, if you play solo with randoms. The longer a party sticks together, the harder the dungeons get and you get more / higher rewards. The difficulity of the dungeons reset everytime back to easy/normal as soon as just 1 player leaves the party which makes it a pain in the ass if you play with randoms. Legendary items can only be craftes (a few) and some others can only be farmed in higher difficulitys like "impossible". The rating goes like easy, normal, hard, very hard, tough, very tough and impossible. Having randoms stick to your party until you reach impossible is very rare and I can even understand people quitting random lobbies if they need to go or their premates come online, because playing with premates rewards you with more legendaries in the long run. Everyone who just wants to play casual is getting punished for having no friends online at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access, it's pretty good, I recommend playing with at least 1 more friend to shorten the queue time.Goods:-Currently there are 9 playable characters and 3 classes, 3 for each class (I think, haven't unlock the last one yet). -The blight mechanic makes you switch character often after 1-3 games early on but that helps you level up all characters which is needed for later difficulties. -Fun gameplay, needs alot of teamwork for later difficulties.Bads:-Missing features (lobby browsers; host migrate for people disconnecting, you will fail if someone disconnects; when someone unready, you have to re-select character to queue as before queueing again, can be annoying since people leave/unready to change character all the time; etc.).-In combat, some moves are poorly telegraphed, enemies' skill effects can be hidden behind a cloud of smoke, which is bad because some of them are an instant player down/party wipe moves.-Minor bugs (unable to equip/unequip gears, can be fixed; joining other hosts can unselect the character you chose when queueing, forcing you into a random character/class; etc.).

_childDocuments_.review: The game has amazing potential. What others would describe as a negative I look at as a new interesting concept for an ARPG. For example when you begin a party in game for a session the party starts doing lower level dungeons and then can work their way up to doing extremely challenging content for the chance at amazing rewards. If you leave that party or a member leaves the party starts over and works its way up again. I love this, to me it feels like when you went to the arcade with your buddies back in the day and played a side scroller together....I like that every session is kind of starting a new run to try and get that epic loot instead of just a b-line to the best loot. There is progression through the leveling of your own camp and characters though and the items you gain in your adventures can be used to make characters stronger.Overall I think this is a great shot at merging rogue lite and ARPGs together to try and create something new. The game feels like a mix of Darkest Dungeon and Diablo, and plays like an arcade side scroller....It really is great fun and I can't wait to see the future updates. 8/10 how it is now could easily go 9 with some work. Great job....

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a great hack and slash with crafting/team mechanics and loot mechanics with multiple characters that basically do the same thing but have one ability that is different with their own personal story and lore.  However there is a desyncing issue that drops a player or two from the game and if you alt f-4 or leave then the entire party fails the mission and gets blight added to them.  It happened several times to me.  I'd honestly buy it if you want to have some fun and don't care about the desync right now, otherwise I'd wait until they fix that one glaring issue before buying.TLDR Game is jank right now, wait for them to fix the desync issue.  Otherwise a pretty good game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is GREAT. The connectivity to it is NOT.One of the game's core concepts is playing in a group of people. Specifically people, not AI. As you play with the same group, you increase your "notoriety" which allows you to do more challenging / more rewarding difficulties. However, as soon as even a single member leaves, that "notoriety" resets back to 0, and it does not restore if that same player rejoins your group.That wouldn't normally be a problem (it opens up the realm for things like "how far can we  push it tonight?"), but there are desync / connectivity problems in about 1 out of every 3 rounds. This means that not only can your group no longer complete the mission, but also that all of your "notoriety" gets reset every time there's a sync problem.This may also have to do with the fact that the game is server based instead of p2p, and there are only 3 servers (US West, Amsterdam, and Singapore if I'm not mistaken).The game has a lot of potential, and is worth keeping an eye on, but as of right now I can't justify its early access state. As soon as the connectivity is fixed, it'll be easy to recommend to anybody with 2 friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Blightbound

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game until they fix it. This is an example of why Early Access is usually a bad idea. Optimization is non-existent, boss fights sometimes don't progress to the next phase causing you to lose your progress of that run, crashes and desyncs are happening more often than they should.My biggest gripe about this game though is the REQUIREMENT to play all classes until your refuge is level 9. That's a horrible design decision. To be forced to queue as a random class at any point is forcing people to play a class they might not want to play. Just a bad idea. So yeah, expect your first 2 hours or so in this game being forced to queue as either a warrior, assassin, or mage. You don't get to pick.The game has potential, but between design decisions and the rough shape this was released in, I'd highly suggest waiting on this one for a few patches to come out.

_childDocuments_.review: Keeps crashing today, which is expected with Early Access - but it is punishing us by accruing 'Blight' every time another user disconnects. It happened so often in a row that I now have no warrior to play with, and I lose out on extra rewards for randomly queuing. It feels like I'm being punished for trying to fill teams properly and is killing the fun. However, fun is there; as long as people continue to queue up. I hope there are more maps and heroes to play with soon. Wish there was an offline component or a way to deal with the blight accumulating on our favorite (or worse, necessary) characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Fantasy Loot 'Em Up. Old school brawler with some RPG stats and gear looting in a Dark Fantasy setting. Throw in some difficulty scaling for longevity and it's tons of fun. We have a bunch more content coming ranging from heroes to levels and gear. There aren't many brawlers that get released these days and when they do, they usually suck. This one has potential, give it a look. Just keep in mind it is Early Access but Ronimo is doing it right, they are very involved with the community when it comes to feedback and bugfixes. They are also just generally super active over on the official discord at gg/ronimo. Can't recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: In the beginning there were many issues that I had to live through within the game. However, over a few week the issues were patched and corrected.  The game feels a lot better and the dungeon runs are intense as your notoriety level goes up.  If there is one thing I can tell the developers, it would be more of a suggestion.  If they can add a way to allow you to keep your notoriety within games. For example, if three friends play this game and make it to notoriety level 7, if one has to get off to handle a personal issue, the notoriety level resets to zero.  In this case, it should allow the three players to vote for a break or something allowing us to come back and start where we left off. I think this would be more fair.I don't play the game as much because it requires two other players to commit to playing 3 or 4 hours in order to get to notoriety level 7. In this case, every time we get to notoriety level 4 or 5 someone has to leave. Which really kills the competitive aspect of the game.  If there was a way for three players to vote on coming back that might encourage more players to play together.  I have two friends that I play with. Every time we play, after 3 hours someone has an issue to tend to and it kills the vibe. I have tried playing this game with randoms. It's even worse with randoms because you don't know when they're going to quit and when they do the game resets your notoriety level.  Overall, it's a fun game. _childDocuments_.review: This game, while in early access, has a few bugs but it quickly makes up for that in potential and gameplay.You get to choose 1 of 3 roles: The Tank, The DPS, the Caster.While self explainatory, the tank has the abilty to negate most damage and shield his teammates. This is static against all tank characters and each one has a unique ability set that changes up the way you can play!The DPS is a melee rogue that has multiple characters as well that have their own unique abilities to fit your play style. Its massive burst but also responsible for interrupts.The caster is your ranged DPS, Cleric and in some cases all causes for Crowd Control which can help combo with other characters. There are multiple mages to select and each one has a unique skill set.The gameplay requires that you cycle through characters which may sound lame at first as you really just want yo play your favorite, but you quickly learn that each character is quite fun with their own quirks that make you kinda glad you gave em a shot.I very much enjoy this game, and while you encounter the bug from time to time, they aren't very common and not exactly game breaking. 9/10 for early access!

name: The Company Man
detailed_description: Battle the corporate machine in The Company Man! A 2D action-adventure where you can hit your crazy co-workers with a keyboard and shoot your evil bosses with emails. Survive the struggles of working life and fulfill your lifelong quest to be CEO! THE WAR OF WORK Jim finally graduates from university, ready to launch his epic career in the Good Water Company. But things quickly spiral into insanity as he finds himself fighting to keep his job. Drink coffee to survive the tortures of working life. Learn the quirks of each department, from the air-conditioned ice lands of accounting to the mountains of paperwork in human resources, beating every floor on your journey to the top! GAME FEATURES Unique enemies including real-life inspired farting co-workers. Beautifully painted environments. Thoughtfully crafted hand-drawn animations. Classic side-scrolling action.

_childDocuments_.review: developed by a Malaysian team of mostly first-timers:  Was going to leave it on wishlist because though I’ve no beef with action-adventure platformers- the feeling isn’t mutual. Upon a closer read and as a student about to graduate, enter the workplace like the protagonist- I had to give it a whirl! Surprisingly though, I managed quite well (phew) and am now missing only 1 achievement.      What totally caught my eye at first was its semblance to  both in theme, dress, circumstances about a newbie in the workplace. It’s just the gameplay that fundamentally set them apart. You could even draw parallels to  as the responsibilities and requirements of the job quickly warp one’s perception of self and values. Are you a good fit for this company? Let’s have a look~You are Jim “off the record” Halpert, a recent graduate turned new clumsy employee at the Good Water Company! After being roped into vandalizing company property, he gets demoted into customer service. From there he must restore his reputation all while swinging keyboards, spamming emails, sipping coffee and evaluating his future with the company~Your most prized and powerful weapon is your pimped up keyboard, with a hilt like a sword for melee attacks. Remember to stretch and flail your body around by jumping, dashing. If your colleagues are not performing or in your way- whack them with that keyboard and “fire” them! On the off chance that fatigue set ins and you feel like dying- coffee stations acts as checkpoints for some reorganization of thoughts bugging you and restoration of health!With 7 levels to explore, each governed by an iron fist boss and mid-boss. Impress them by attempting to dethrone, steal their jobs and they’ll reward you with a free coffee voucher used to claim OP coffee bean upgrades at your company’s barista located at the lobby. Also, the cute-as-a-button receptionist is there. Job training will also be provided and you can unlock ranged email-based attacks (certs too of course).Tips: 1) Enemies can just be skipped past.2) Finding it hard to progress? Replay past stages to get more vouchers!!The workplace is like a whole other realm where time and space get disrupted. “Customer Service” is like a prison where even the sipping of coffee has them eyeing you from their stations. Human Resources is stacked with giant buzzsaws for shredders and paperwork piles. My absolute bias is the Marketing level, where there are clouds, rainbows, gimmicks like portals and blimps in the background.Enemy design is differentiated and plentiful with 3-4 catered to each floor and with their distinct move sets and hindrances. Notable mentions include the abacus-wielding bookkeeper, a seal-like diver swimming in paperwork and the list goes on. It’s just a pleasure to meet and fire them! I haven’t even touched on the wonderful horrible bosses. The music is carefree and vibrant, like you’re stealing company time. But it’s also unafraid to get booming and swanky, as in you just don’t give any cra*~ The story’s motivated by the likes of  where it’s just impossible to keep up with the day-to-day shenanigans. Even a cameo from “Dwight Schrute” and his title. However,  is perhaps more accurate because of the dreamer protagonist who likes videogames and there being a beverage too being manufactured! Luckily it manages to maintain the upbeat, nonsensical vibe of the two and bring in its own documentary appeal, we just can’t get enough of exposing the workplace~SCARY: 1st) There are many office worker stereotypes which also unveil the unfairness of it all. Putting up with gossips, competition and learning that colleagues don’t automatically translate to friends. 2nd) As someone who’s not very up-to-date on things but still has some knowledge about Malaysia’s politics, I know corruption is a ginormous issue there. And it’s touched on here as well!! Whereas Yuppie Psycho focused more on working conditions, CPM sheds light on the lack of ethics to the customers and transparency.  3rd) Try as you might to effect change to the shady organization chart- there will always be shareholders and higher ups beyond the figureheads. Which makes you feel insignificant and so you wonder when does it end? In some ways, CPM is remarkable in its execution and oozes so much charm, innuendo. However, it’s also rather vanilla in that the stages drag on after a bit and it’s just defeating / running past enemies. There’s nothing interesting to do aside from the specific environmental hazards in between point A to point B. I was all for the plot and it started off well, even threw a twist in the middle but did not pursue it after that. And it came off as telling- juggling three different stories; the familial, the occupational and the semi-professional. But really only one is ever advanced. And so, the other two are discarded in the wastebasket… unless there’s a sequel?BUGS:x Jarrett fight; “W” appears split-second on left side. Pressing it allows you to skip encounter.x Aerial enemies disappear into ceilings/despawn when you try to take the fight to them.x Evan fight; always starts off with him getting hit instantly on the right sidex ~ “Job training” email tutorials don’t work properly; doesn’t matter if you follow the steps. You’ll get previously attained certificatesx Unintended jump boosts when hit in mid-air.NITPICKS:~ Story portions have to be replayed no matter what. Why not make them skippable at the tap of a button?~ Dialogue / thought bubbles have way too many forms and lack consistency. Some automatically advance, require a prompt and others delayed.~ Currently only one default difficulty~ No way of navigating straight to boss battles- you have to go through the entire gun-and-run stages, mid-boss.CPM simulates the chaotic and morally plastic environment of working for big corps! Doesn’t lack in any department but creative output… INSANE! Superb company to be around, just don’t work in it~ With over 20+ unique enemies, 10+ well-choreographed boss fights- every inch of the design is quirky and professional. The hipster soundtrack, interior décor specifically matching the clever, punny themes. You can tell the team are so done dealing with office drama most likely having worked in one or through firsthand observation.   Gameplay gets a little stale and overstretched, mitigated only by the demanding bosses. It’s true the story doesn’t shine as much, and in facts suffers from covering too many things. But if you don’t mind and just want to take in the sights like a tour of the company’s feng shui and colorful employees. Perhaps jump at the opportunity to even hone your platforming skills and with a bonus of being entertained by the workplace humor, CPM has a spot for you~

_childDocuments_.review: Don't expect the story to keep you glued to your RGB gamer chair. The theme is corruption in "big-bad" corporations. Sadly the game adds nothing original to the conversation, nor is the delivery in some way unique. The exposition is delivered through single lines of monologue every time you stop for a coffee break, with an occasional boss one-liner before you duke it out. And they are just so  and , that I can't even remember a single line of dialogue.As I was writing about the story,  popped into my head. It reminded me of how unique characters and good writing can elevate your enjoyment of a game - like the weird shady magician that doesn't let you open his closet in . I spent 20 minutes listening to him (because I opened his closet), laughing at his corny puns and insanely stupid yet profound wisdom. Good writing matters, and  lacks in this area immensely. There is no charm, no wit, nothing. As a 2D platformer, you'll mostly be dodging environmental hazards, with an enemy here and there and an angry boss waiting for you at the end to give you a poor evaluation. One thing to remember is that if you, for whatever reason - pizza at the door, the dog needs a walk, or your wife is giving birth, quit mid-stage, back to the beginning you go. I don't understand this, as it doesn't apply to dying which respawns you at the last coffee station. However, this approach does teach you a valuable life lesson - . So the game gets a bonus point for that.Frankly, there are more negatives than positives, so I'll get those positives out of the way first.. A lot of care and love went into bringing this unique and twisted company to life. The cartoonish style complements the enemy design and their attack animations. They nailed it out of the park, with each enemy feeling unique and fresh. Their design uses a common stereotype associated with that particular position in a company as its base and creates some rather funny caricatures of their real-world counterparts. The same goes for levels, with their backdrops giving you an overall vibe of that department and what kind of people their employees are.And sadly, now it's time to turn in my not so satisfying "employee evaluation"., or rather, its execution. It's simply all over the place. The first five levels offer no challenge whatsoever, with the last two at least providing a decent challenge. I am by no means some chad platformer god, but I finished my first run in under 4 hours, as it was super easy to "skip" large parts of each level by just running past enemies and well, most of the levels have too much "dead space".That leads us into my next con -  or "how to prolong a level artificially without any need". There is no need to have a 2-minute "section" where the only activity is running in a straight line without any platforming or combat. It isn't fun. It's boring. Also, why is there so much useless space but no secrets to find?Following this, there's a distinct . In my opinion, this is the biggest misstep. If you want to make something challenging, there should be something to give your action urgency. One enemy and two slow falling icicles are not going to do that. Only the last two levels get this correct. They have a better enemy count, with excellent attack variety (air, ground, ranged, melee), which actually make the platforming segments somewhat challenging and not trivial like the levels before. Up next, we have the combat. It's basic, and that's the highest "praise" I can give it. There is nothing fun about it; The hitboxes can be weird at times, and smashing someone with a keyboard just isn't enjoyable. It lacked "flow", with the attack animations just feeling stiff. There are two ways of dealing with enemies: melee and "special" attacks. Melee has no variety whatsoever, just "press B to hit"; No new melee attacks, just a basic melee slash. The "special attacks" have variety, but even that loses its appeal once you see how  and  some of the "better" ones are. . They just lacked creativity. Yes, there are ok ones, but you can count them on (the fingers of) one hand. Here is the average platforming segment - a platform for you to jump on, a slight chance for an enemy or environmental hazards, but it's usually just . These segments lack a sense of urgency.  While there were two okiiiiish ones, showing some glimpse of good boss design, the majority have way too many safe spots and are just easy to cheese. It ruins the fun and challenge they could have presented, well at least it did for me. Let's take the spider-woman/accountant/Mr. Freeze as an example. She has two attacks (which is pretty poor in itself) - one is a ranged attack, the other is a butt slam. Her stage has two floating stationary platforms during the whole fight. Just hide under the platform when she uses her ranged attacks, then jump on the platform when she uses her butt, attack her in between, and . There should have been something that stops you from camping under those platforms. Have her remove the ground as a safe spot during her ranged attacks, forcing you to use those platforms, or you die. This way, her ranged attacks might actually have a slim chance to hit you.Oh, I almost forgot, there is also zero, and I do mean zero, replayability.If you were to ask me to recommend you a 2D platformer,  would not be one of them, and I only played like five 2D platformers in my short, but very slav life. It simply has too many shortcomings that keep it from being enjoyable. You can paint a Yugo to look fabulous, and it will, but if the thingies under the hood, that make it go  are not good, it'll probably just explode when you start the car. I do hope that, even after reading this review, if the game piqued your interest, you do check it out. The devs could use more feedback, helping them grow and improve for their next game, hopefully. But, if you asked me would I recommend you buy this? Sadly, no, I wouldn't.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, the Malaysian-made indie 2D platformer The Company Man starts off jovial and satirical. You play a corporate worker named Jim as he rises to the top, fighting co-workers in a big corporation in different sectors using his keyboard weapon like a sword and emails as projectiles.The first few stages of The Company Man is clear as day with its homage. You’ll get vibes of Mega Man X as your main man Jim can perform Zero-style slashes and air dashes, as well as “send emails” in the form of long-ranged bullets or in a wide short-ranged “shotgun” burst.The title is pretty fun when you’re just cruising along, hitting each checkpoint, and braving the next challenge. There’s even a simple upgrade system where defeating a boss nets you a free coffee beans coupon, giving you your choice of powerups ranging from health and energy extensions to skills like life-leeching and destroying projectiles with your keyboard swipes.But once you’ve proceeded past the initial stages and enter the realms of Accounting, Marketing, and beyond, you start to see the design cracks of a supposed solid platforming base. The game devolves into an exercise in frustration with fewer checkpoints leading up to the obviously tough bits to the odd hit detection and situations where it looks like you can make a jump or assume your main character’s dash gives you a low profile. It doesn’t.There are also one or two wasted segments begging for challenges and gauntlet-style segments; I was hoping for more action when Jim was on an airship platform in one of the game’s later stages. That segment was quite a bore as I just killed a slew of the same marketing enemies I fought, the platform slowly flying to the right side of the screen amidst the scrolling background.Some challenges seem like they were added with not much thought. There’s a stage using teleporters that feature a puzzle that requires you to quickly switch teleporters while mid-air after you made the blink. However, you fall straight down and aren’t given much time to react from the get-go. There’s also a frustrating part at the penultimate stages where spiked barricades send you back to the beginning of the course if you so much as touch them. While it’s better than starting over from the last checkpoint, I feel that there can be other ways to not make these segments this quirky.Plus, the later bosses in the game seem to die faster than usual, leaving final tense moments a little anti-climactic. Long story short, the difficulty spikes here are about as unstable as a startup founder after getting way too much for its seeding goal. The less said about the banal music the better; save for the end credits theme which was given more thought to make than the entire OST.The Company Man is not as polished as its inspiration. It barely hits the level of competency and averageness when it comes to indie-level 2D platforming. There are also some technical issues too; the game doesn’t seem to register me defeating the game’s last few bosses.It’s a shame because I see a lot of potential with the game’s engine and controls. While I’m glad that there are more folks making 2D action games in the veins of the Mega Man series, this Malaysian game really needs more fine-tuning and polish. It’s one thing to be a difficult game, but The Company Man just crosses over that delicate line of challenging and frustrating with no indication of such spiking curves from the get-go.I finished the entire title, but I felt that I got through by blind luck and using exploits in hit detection rather than through pure skill & practice. For comparison, the 2D indie title Cyber Shadow sets those expectations early on and doesn’t let up from start to finish.No amount of charm and cute art is enough to hide The Company Man’s skeletons in its closet. It’s not the most superficial and worst title I’ve played, but there are way better and more rewarding indie 2D platforming options out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Excellent environment and character art. - Great animation. - Interesting, well-executed "corporate grind" theme. - Solid controls.Cons: - Unacceptably buggy for a game at this price point. I fell through the ground and died twice. I had to replay a level because the game randomly didn't save at the end of a level once. - Poor level design. There are looooong stretches where you are just running to the next room in a completely open and empty space with no enemies. - The music is very forgettable.  - At 6 levels plus a final boss, the game is quite short. What this game does well, it does very well. Specifically, the art direction in this game is AAA level. The characters, enemies, and environments are all very detailed and well-animated. Visually, this game is a treat to look at.Unfortunately, that's where the compliments end. I feels like the dev team spent most of their time making the game look as pretty as it does. The bugs and poor level design kinda took the wind out of my sails for this game. This game could've been much better if it were a bit more polished. As it is now, I think it's too expensive for what you're getting.

_childDocuments_.review: It's always complicated and sad to rate negatively a little indie project, which I'm sure, the devs have put lot of heart, time and effort in it, but even if It started very well, with a funny little satire of how big companies work and companies greed, it didn't last long before I noticed all I didn't like with this game.THE GOOD:- The Art Style of the characters (not anime style but close) and the animations- The ennemies are fun- The satire (but)THE BAD:- A bland experience after the first stage- The music!!! OMG! It's a torture for the ears! I've never heard that in my entire life, I don't know who validated that and who thought it would be a good idea to use that awful music for every.single.stage! Only the reception music is good. I wanted to take a break multiple time in that very short game, because the music was so atrocious that I coudln't handle it.- Too gentle, the satire doesn't go very far. It lacks a bit of substance.- The hitbox feels weird- The stages are not really interesting. It's a background pattern that roughly repeat itself throughout the same stage and the first 4 stages look extremely similar, atleast that's the imrpession that gives coz they are so repetitive.- The stages are stretched and stretched and stretched with absolutely no other purpose than give you a false feeling that they are long, because most of the time they are totally empty (even from ennemies, except the 2 final stages)- They didn't even implemented a "duck" mechanic, something you find in 99% of platformers. That could have help creating more diverse situation with the annemies and obstacles.- As a platformer you can't do more generic and bland than that (millions of generic platformer like that)- The level design is quite bad (pattern background, cheap platform mechanics, a few obstacles repeated on every single stage ad nauseam etc.- The placement of ennemies is so weird sometimes and even if well design, it always feel liek they were placed on the stages totally razndomly without even thinking about where they should make the most sense and the amount and variety that woudl be appropriate- Relatively easy (which is fin for me as I prefer easy game, but most people would not like that that's why I put it in the negatives)- Not possible to chose a difficulty- No reasons to even fight the ennemies when the game doesn't force us to do it byt artifcially locking the stage with a door that opens only once we defeat an ennemy we've been fighting 14564 before i nthe same stage. Fighting them brings nothing besides health or a coin or 2. So I skipped most of them once I disocvered the new enemies design of each stages.- No secrets, nothing to discover, nothing to collect.- Less than 3 hours to finish it. And I've seen playthrough where the game can easily be beaten in 2 hours...- No resolution beyond 1080p / no graphical options- Heavy aliasing on the characters when playing 1080p on my 4K monitor (don't know if it's also here on 1080p monitors)If you can grab it for maximum $1/1€ maybe $2 at best on sales (I bought it for that price), maybe give it a try, but it's certainly not worth more than that, and certainly not the asking price of $15$ or $10 on sales... This is delusional. The game is only saved by the funny side of the satire (not funny haha, more funny blowing through the nose and "oh good idea". The most funny part is actually the "certfications" you receive once you fire employees, not even actual gameplay) and the character designs.

_childDocuments_.review: The Company Man had promise, and it's not without it's fun moments. However, the game felt half-baked in the end, making it difficult to recommend.Now I will praise certain aspects of the game. The animations, environments, and character designs are all top-notch. Everything feels fresh, and the sheer amount of attention to detail given to the visual style actually reminds me of Wario Land: Shake It! with the focus on good animation. I also liked the concept of fighting through an office. They found creative ways to incorporate corporate concepts and office items into hazards and weapons. It was Near the end of the game is a glitch-fest. In the marketing level, I fell straight through the stage, forcing me to reset. The final boss was completely buggy, not panning the camera properly in several areas which forced me to basically restart again, made even worse by the fact that the final boss is 2 phases long. This also ties into another issue I have with the game: the janky hitboxes. It's always hard to tell what will and won't hit you, because the sprites are so large. Also, the upgrades. Good luck affording anything, because you can't. It makes the coffee shop feel a little redundant.My final issue with this was the story. While it brought up an interesting idea of corporate greed being larger than one person or even a handful of people, it ultimately went nowhere. Even Jim's backstory feels utterly unfulfilled, as the ending is just a still image. It would be nice to have had some text to accompany this CG, or even just one final cutscene to show how Jim's character has progressed.All in all, if you want to play this I recommend waiting for a sale, as it's just not worth the hefty 20$ price tag, both in terms of the content it offers, and it's performance. While The Company Man undeniably has some great style, flair alone cannot carry this game, as it's bugs and lack of a true ending leave it feeling like a truly mid experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The Company Man:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~The corporate world is truly an exciting place to make your mark as an individual, there are two ways about it.  Either you work your way up the ladder in one company and then snag your next big opportunity in another.  Or you have to prove to your current employer that you are a team player, willing to learn and most importantly, that you are able to walk over anyone who challenges you on your way up the ladder to becoming the next big CEO!  And here is our next contender . . .  he goes by the name of Jim! Jim just started his new job, and he is dreaming big; really big!  That’s right, he reckons he can become the next big CEO in five to ten hours. Is it possible? No one has done it before, but with your help, Jim just may become the next big CEO in The Company Man.The Company Man is a 2D action platformer game developed and self-published by Forust on the 28th of May 2021 on the Steam platform.The game consists of seven levels which include 11 boss fights in total.  But first, you need to pass the corporate orientation.  In your case, this experience wasn’t the greatest. Not because of your capability, but just because you followed the orders of William, your supervisor, and therefore found yourself in immediate trouble. This is basically a small tutorial. From there on, you’ll be demoted on your first day, and you’ll start your journey at the Customer Service Department, which is at the bottom of the corporate ladder. Then you’ll have to fight your way through Accounting, R & D, Marketing, Sales and Legal, and finally fight the big CEO and the Corporate Machine Boss.Jim will be armed with a keyboard which he uses as a weapon; this is one of the ways in which to fire/fight a colleague (enemy).  The chairman of the company will teach him special keyboard attacks as he successfully completes each department.  Winning a boss’s fight will earn him a coffee coupon which he can use at the coffee shop located in the main foyer. There, he will be able to upgrade his energy bar, health, and a few other things. I enjoyed playing this game, and I must say that I really like how smooth the animations are. Jim, the main character, is so much fun to see moving, jumping, slashing and dashing his way through the levels. I like the different themes for each of the levels. For me, the icy cold accounting and the crazy marketing levels were my favourites. The enemies that you fight (or fire, in this case) are pretty fun but easy to overcome as you understand their patterns. That also includes the boss fights. It might take you a few goes to beat each of them but not more than that, with the exception of the final boss, the Corporate Machine, which is straight after the CEO fight; you will carry over any damage you sustained.As mentioned, I like the different themes in the levels, you’ll encounter a few new enemies to fired, and they are well-designed. Even if the current version doesn’t have a set of difficulties (easy, normal or hard), Jim will lose health if he gets hit by an enemy projectile or by simply being touched by a worker (enemy).  The thing you’ll look forward to is the coffee machine; when you reach it, not only will the game automatically save your progress, but you’ll get all your health back. I play a fair few platformer games, and they need to have the right amount of fighting and moving forward. I think this game misses the right note in that regard. Is it because we don’t have a higher level of difficulty to play, and therefore the game is not as challenging? Maybe, but for me, I needed more actions within each of the levels. The artwork and animations are fabulous, and the game runs really well. The story is fun with great humour all the way through. I thoroughly enjoyed the game, but it would be really great to have a couple of difficulty levels added to the game, giving extra replayability. You can play with your keyboard in terms of the controls, but I recommend playing it with a gamepad.  Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great artwork+	7 levels with 11 bosses to beat+	Interesting worker to fire +	Fun story with great humour+	Easy to play+	Full controller support & Steam cloud+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	No trading cards as yet -	Only one level of difficultyHow fast are you going to climb the corporate ladder? Let’s see, in The Company Man.7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good start for an indie developer, and is extremely well drawn and well animated. Thematically, it's also an excellent game with a lot of corporate puns, with interesting takes on the hierarchy and theme of the different corporate departments. I also really love the Malaysian Easter eggs scattered throughout the game.However, it's really held back by its gameplay design. I would have preferred if the gameplay loop was tighter. Stages were large but repetitive, which felt like an attempt to inflate the number of hours in the game. The save mechanic through the coffee machines was interesting, but it made the game a chore to play when the hardest parts of the stages are often right behind a coffee machine (i.e. save point), which means you have to run through a large segment of the game that you already cleared to get back to where you died. For a game this heavily inspired by action platformers like Mega Man, it took the bad stuff like few save points which really slowed down the pace of the game, and forgot to include the good stuff like different gameplay mechanics via weapons. Mechanics like slows, DoT, and stuns can be explained by in-world explanations like lag, computer viruses, and BSODs respectively, and would make the email gun more interesting.This still gets a thumb up from me primarily because the graphics and BGM are absolutely amazing, and of course, Malaysia boleh. I really do think that you've a game with a lot of potential on your hands if you provide enough content updates. Good luck!

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I was hooked when I saw the trailer. Thought this one would be a great game... but it's a Cardboard Hasslehoff. A pretty picture to look at maybe, but it's a flat façade that can't stand up to scrutiny.Maybe with the good points?:It looks gorgeous at a glance. And they included a silly little animation for if/when you try to leave through the lobby's revolving door.The BAD points then, as they do deserve the capital letters:-Hitboxes for yourself and the enemies are wonky. As in: you can't help but get hit while trying to hit enemies.-It's short. I beat the final bosses in under 3 hours. Not a good look that puts 15 hours as the slowest to finish time in the achievements section.-It's way too easy. If you manage to make it past level 1-1 in Super Mario Bros 3, you can ace this game.-Boss HP seems to vary wildly in terms of hits you need to deliver.-Level design is bland. While pretty at a glance, you see some nice design elements, they're repeated ad nauseum in uninspired fashion. The stage gimmicks and the enemy spam rooms only serve as padding rather than making the game more interesting.-Grinding is more padding. You want the shop achievement? Grind.And the meh points:-The music is exceptionally meh. It's not bad, but it's by default elevator music.-The game tries to be funny about corporate hell. But got the wit from the cornfield.There's a lot of games that make fun of corporate cliche's, some do it right like  SuperEpic. And then there's The Company Man that makes you wonder why you wasted €15 on a poop water equivalent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game had two different people at the helm, on one hand some of the animations, designs, and gimmicks were really fun and interesting.  I think the lawyer and marketing levels were particularly good. On the other hand a lot of the enemies felt sloppy, the sound design and music were particularly lackluster and I feel like the bosses in particular were either exceptionally easy or had one or two attacks that would hit out of nowhere (I'm looking at you Boba).  Overall, I felt like the game had a lot of potential but lacked a whole lot of polish.  It was also REALLY short, I wasn't particularly trying to go very fast through the game and I blew through it in under 5 hours.  For a game with a $16 pricetag I was expecting a little more.  I wouldn't call it a bad game, if you're looking for a pretty easy platformer with some interesting level design maybe give it a try.  I just can't recommend it unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall pretty disappointing. It comes off as a Mega Man styled action platformer with a big business twist where you going around defeating all of the different department managers and gain their abilities. Its far from it, unfortunately, and just ends up being a pretty one note action game with some very mild platforming thrown in. For starters it is a completely linear game, which isn't bad, however it does make the levels less of a challenge and make the later enemies more of the "bullet sponge" type instead of the skillfull timing and positioning enemies that Mega man is known for. The platforming is basic and really only ends up being jump at the end of the ledges instead of staying on top of what on nearby platforms and moving platforms with different obstacles like fire and stuff to force you to stay on your toes. The bosses are basic patterns that have no changes and just end up with you wailing on them during specific animations in which they hold still instead of you finding different times to get hits off on them during their attacks. The different abilities are all different shot types, shotgun, chain gun, snipe, etc. You will almost never use them unless you want to deal a little extra damage during a point in which you can approach the enemies. Finally, while the story appears to have a message on the surface, it can be summed up as , moving up in a corporation takes a lot of your personal freedom away and even if you rise to the top your still beholden to somebody. Yeah, that's work, corporations tend to pay a bit more and be more straightforward than running your own business or living off of the land. That's why so many people work for them, its a bit simpler and more financially rewarding. I thought for a second there it was gonna go into how the government and big corporations will work hand in hand to increase they're own profits and take away from others, essentially forming government sanctified monopolies but nope, that's it. TL;DRHonestly quite a disappointment, you tolerate bad game play for a non story if you get this, so don't.

name: Football Manager 2021
detailed_description: The manager is the beating heart of every football club. In Football Manager 2021 , dynamic, true-to-life management experiences and next-level detail renews that focus on you, the manager, equipping you with all the tools you need to achieve elite status. With more than 50 nations and 2,500 clubs at every level of the football pyramid to choose from, the possibilities are endless. It’s over to you, boss. Choose your colours and the challenge that best suits your ambitions and then work with your club’s hierarchy to ensure you meet theirs… or face the consequences. Join forces with your backroom staff to assess the strength and depth of your playing squad before dipping into the transfer market. There’s likely to be a starlet in your Academy knocking on the door of the first team… Craft tactical strategies, formations and styles of play for every occasion to maximise your club’s chances of winning football matches and getting those three points. Immerse yourself in the spectacle of match day and revel in the glory of management as your planning pays off on the pitch. Interaction Communicating with your players and the media has never been more purposeful or realistic. Gestures enable you to express every emotion, while Quick Chats improve those short, informal conversations which are part of day-to-day life as a manager. In FM21, others will feel the impact of your words and know the sort of manager you are. Matchday Every fixture now feels like a true spectacle with our best-looking match engine ever. You’ll receive better analysis and advice in the pre-match build-up and those data improvements combine with our remodelled match UI to bring you closer to the action than ever before. FM21 also boasts a raft of AI improvements across every area of the pitch. The rate of decision-making has increased and there’s more nuance to the decisions that players make, allowing them to be more reactive and make faster decisions. This improved decision-making process has enabled better defensive and goalkeeper intelligence, enhanced central play and more variety in the final third. Additionally, you’ll also get more reaction and data post-match, including our brand new SIxG system, which will let you know well or badly your team performed relative to the chances they created. Analysis and Stats Our extensive data improvements go beyond Matchdays, giving you all the tools to level up your pre-match preparations. Managers benefit from a vastly increased amount of data reporting and visualisation this year, including monthly reports from the new Performance Analyst that mirrors the data real managers receive. New graphs and data maps provide clearer insight into their team’s strengths and opposition weaknesses, while there’s a wealth of new stats that will give you full statistical overview of the entire pitch. Recruitment New staff roles, meetings and interactions freshen up one of the game’s most popular areas. Recruitment meetings now ensure that you and your scouting team are on the same page, both for your next moves and the club’s longer-term strategy in the transfer market. Moreover, you’ll now be able to approach agents directly about a player's interest in joining your club. End of Season Re-live your campaigns and revel in your success like never before. A new season review presentation picks out your best moments on and off the pitch, while showpiece victories feel much sweeter with improved title presentations and masses of media attention. This is a game that rewards planning and knowledge but there’s no pre-defined ending or script to follow, simply endless opportunities. Every club has a story to tell and it’s up to you to write it.
