With more than 50 nations and 2,500 clubs at every level of the football pyramid to choose from, the possibilities are endless. It’s over to you, boss. Choose your colours and the challenge that best suits your ambitions and then work with your club’s hierarchy to ensure you meet theirs… or face the consequences. Join forces with your backroom staff to assess the strength and depth of your playing squad before dipping into the transfer market. There’s likely to be a starlet in your Academy knocking on the door of the first team… Craft tactical strategies, formations and styles of play for every occasion to maximise your club’s chances of winning football matches and getting those three points. Immerse yourself in the spectacle of match day and revel in the glory of management as your planning pays off on the pitch. Interaction Communicating with your players and the media has never been more purposeful or realistic. Gestures enable you to express every emotion, while Quick Chats improve those short, informal conversations which are part of day-to-day life as a manager. In FM21, others will feel the impact of your words and know the sort of manager you are. Matchday Every fixture now feels like a true spectacle with our best-looking match engine ever. You’ll receive better analysis and advice in the pre-match build-up and those data improvements combine with our remodelled match UI to bring you closer to the action than ever before. FM21 also boasts a raft of AI improvements across every area of the pitch. The rate of decision-making has increased and there’s more nuance to the decisions that players make, allowing them to be more reactive and make faster decisions. This improved decision-making process has enabled better defensive and goalkeeper intelligence, enhanced central play and more variety in the final third. Additionally, you’ll also get more reaction and data post-match, including our brand new SIxG system, which will let you know well or badly your team performed relative to the chances they created. Analysis and Stats Our extensive data improvements go beyond Matchdays, giving you all the tools to level up your pre-match preparations. Managers benefit from a vastly increased amount of data reporting and visualisation this year, including monthly reports from the new Performance Analyst that mirrors the data real managers receive. New graphs and data maps provide clearer insight into their team’s strengths and opposition weaknesses, while there’s a wealth of new stats that will give you full statistical overview of the entire pitch. Recruitment New staff roles, meetings and interactions freshen up one of the game’s most popular areas. Recruitment meetings now ensure that you and your scouting team are on the same page, both for your next moves and the club’s longer-term strategy in the transfer market. Moreover, you’ll now be able to approach agents directly about a player's interest in joining your club. End of Season Re-live your campaigns and revel in your success like never before. A new season review presentation picks out your best moments on and off the pitch, while showpiece victories feel much sweeter with improved title presentations and masses of media attention. This is a game that rewards planning and knowledge but there’s no pre-defined ending or script to follow, simply endless opportunities. Every club has a story to tell and it’s up to you to write it.
short_description: New additions and game upgrades deliver added levels of depth, drama and football authenticity. FM21 empowers you like never before to develop your skills and command success at your club.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's better than last years and I enjoy playing it, why have I given it a negative review you ask?2 words..Exploit Tactics!Managed through a difficult season where I won lots of games to begin with then went on a losing streak narrowly beat the sack got a few more wins and then went on another losing streak.During the second losing streak it made no sense at all as I had strengthened the team, had 2 tactics now and had experimented in the games I lost to make a few tweaks. Even little things like the end of season roundup you get has been improved over what it was in previous years; just some emails that pop up in your inbox.  I could not recommend this game enough, especially for players who are familiar with previous editions but grew disillusioned with the lack of a more realistic match engine or the lack of little quality of life changes. Sure the animations look a bit better and we see some dinks now but there are really disappointing things that happen on the defensive side of the game which lead me to believe that the ME has regressed.Defenders are incapable of dealing with long balls WHEN AN OPPOSITION PLAYER IS NEAR THEM. They either miss the header, misjudge the flight of the ball and see it sail over their heads or just watch the forward control the ball and run past them for a 1v1 (deeper defensive line caused the last one to occur more). It happens far too often. Also, the way defenders attempt to deal with opposition players running directly at them with the ball is awful. More often than not they react appropriately when the opposition player is already past them (and by react appropriately i mean run fast to try to catch up with the player at which point they’ll bump into their heels because as far as I can see there still are no animations for physical battles between players). I thought defenders were going to be more aware of their surroundings this year but I am not seeing it. Sane gliding past the entire team and creating a 1v1 all by himself, regardless of where he received the ball and how many defenders are between him and the goal, happens far too often.I know SI tried to buff the defensive side of the game because they knew it would be left behind due to the changes made to the attacking side but more work on that is still needed in my opinion.The FM backheel where a player keeps the ball in play by backheeling it conveniently for an opposition player has been replaced by the FM bump the ball out of play this year. The FM backheel wasn’t even a problem in the last few versions of FM20 but the greatest FM ever has reintroduced it for reasons unknown. I have also seen a keeper save a shot from 6 yards when he was looking at the net instead of the ball so the ME doesn’t even factor the direction players are facing into the simulation.I am not a fan of the new UI during a match. The players at the bottom of the screen in between highlights limit the amount of information displayed on the tablet if you dont minimise it so why was this not incorporated into the tablet? The dugout section has some useless information like the prompt to the change pen taker not disappearing after the pen is over or your assistant manager advising you to change from short to direct passing now being accompanied by a graphic of a pitch showing you all passes in the match which quickly turns into useless noise and does not disappear after a few seconds like in previous FM’s. The match stats on the left should be customizable like the match stats in the tablet section. The game doesn’t tell you who assisted a goal like before. Revisiting a game and viewing highlights or goals in the match, like a lot of other things, now takes more steps to do. Clicking individuals when attempting to give a team talk to a one or a few players pre ticks every player for some reason, which makes no sense. UI text scaling in the game doesn’t work properly so if you want to have as much info on the screen at one time as you did in FM20, you have to set the zoom so low that everything becomes much too small.I listened to Miles when he said the gestures weren’t just the tone system in disguise. I’ve found them to be useful during player interactions but they add nothing more than what the tone system added to press conferences. Press conferences are still as useless as ever.The game is a meh for me. There is a lot of football managing still there and I don’t have a reason to doubt that SI will update the game regularly and make it better as time goes on (especially ME) much like what happened to FM20 but as things stand currently I dont think the game/ME deserves the hype it is getting now.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Football Manager 2021: A Masterclass in Football Management SimulationFootball Manager 2021, developed by Sports Interactive and published by SEGA, is the latest installment in the long-running football management simulation series. This year's edition has been praised for its numerous quality-of-life improvements, making it the most accomplished and accessible entry in years.Graphics and User Interface:While graphics have never been the main selling point of the Football Manager series, FM 2021 has made significant strides in improving the overall user interface. The new matchday overlay provides quick access to important information, reducing the need to navigate through multiple screens for substitutions and other vital actions (Trusted Reviews).Gameplay and Depth:FM 2021 continues to offer the deep, detailed football management experience that fans have come to expect. From managing the board of directors to nurturing your under-18 team, the game rewards players who invest time and effort into achieving success (OpenCritic). The match engine has also seen improvements, with more fluid and natural animations, as well as more realistic player behavior on the pitch (GamesRadar).New Features and Improvements:While FM 2021 may not introduce any groundbreaking new features, it does bring a host of small but impactful changes that enhance the overall experience. The addition of expected goals (xG) as a stat provides a more accurate representation of scoring opportunities, and the optimization of the game for lower-end machines ensures faster loading and saving times (GamesRadar). Other minor additions, such as pre-transfer window recruitment meetings and improved "regen" player faces, contribute to making this installment a delight to play (GamesRadar).Conclusion:Football Manager 2021 is a triumph for the series, offering a more complete and accessible package than ever before. The combination of numerous quality-of-life improvements, a refined match engine, and a deep, rewarding gameplay experience make FM 2021 a must-play for both long-time fans and newcomers to the franchise. With its focus on strategic thinking, data-driven decision making, and continuous learning, Football Manager 2021 is the definitive football management simulation game on the market today.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review, I've logged 254.5 hours of playtime. A large volume of that time has involved testing elements including the user interface and match engine, as opposed to playing the game normally. After purchasing every version of Football Manager, and its Championship Manager predecessor, FM 21 is the poorest iteration in the series. Somewhat controversially, the game is only a meagre update of FM 20 with some additional stats like xG sprinkled on top. While the game’s marketing materials suggest that the new innovations stretch to more complex interactions with the club’s board and squad, those are, at best, trivial and simply add more bloat to the standard user experience. With regards to the match engine, there have been the customary patches from the developer to correct a myriad of technical issues. All of which have been detrimental to the immersion of watching two teams play competitive football. However, this year’s offering stands out as recent patches to the game have caused further, more serious issues with the analysis of player performance. At present, there’s an issue where individual player ratings have been greatly reduced across the board. For experienced players of the series, it’s unusual to see players win end-of-season awards with average ratings between 7.1-7.25. Callum Wilson scored 35 goals in 35 games in my last season, an incredible haul, and barely scraped an average of 7.1. Full backs, wingers and central midfielders all suffer as the game doesn’t currently track key tackles, an important performance metric for players who aren’t scoring or creating. The animations reflected within the match engine have been increased in volume, but the player behaviour has become farcical. Defenders standing still when they can easily reach a ball first is a frequent occurrence and renders so much of the players tactical activity meaningless. The developer’s forum keeps a track of the list of issues which have been fixed and those that are still being worked upon. Another disappointing trend has been the number of clicks a user must make to access information which used to be easy to retrieve 5-6 years ago. The implementation of the ‘social’ tab where a large amount of the game’s news is hidden beneath has only grown in size with every new version. In the developer’s quest to be seen to bring innovation to the annual release, so much of that innovation is presented as affecting the most laborious aspects of the game. Press conferences. Player interactions. Board interactions. All of this leads to the user making more clicks in order to advance to the core managerial gameplay. Meanwhile, not enough innovation has been brought to the manner in which the match engine produces content. There’s also a disappointing lack of options for users to rearrange parts of the user interface to best suit their needs. The new match-day experience presents a vast amount of data through an extremely limited number of panels. Few of which are customisable. This creates a bottleneck of data visualisation which is so needless and easy to fix. This year, IGN came down hard of FIFA 21 for the Nintendo Switch for charging full price for what was essentially a threadbare update of FIFA 20 on that platform. Other review outlets did the same. Whilst there’s clearly been the challenge of developing during the pandemic, the game is a weak update of FM 20 with more than enough immersion-breaking bugs that the game simply cannot be recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: After a surprise promotion run that saw a team that was seeded bottom of the table win playoffs and get promoted to the next league, the Sky Bet League Two, Phoenix National found out what it really meant to be in another league. They were handed loss after loss, and could only barely eke out draws occasionally. It wasn't long before, mid season, they were bottom of the table. Meanwhile their promotion partners, Notts Co, who had also come up from the lower leagues with them, was showing their true talent as a top of the league team. By mid season they were placed #1, Phoenix National at the bottom #24Head coach Cope decided then to radically change his tactics. He abandoned the defensive, passive style of football he'd taught for the last season and a half and switched to an incredibly aggressive possession style of football that truly controlled the pace of the game. Phoenix national got their first win. And then another. An unbeaten string of games from mid-season all the way up into a surprise playoff contention spot just barely squeezing in at #7 after an incredible run that included a 4-0 rout of a team that had previously crushed themNotts Co had always been a difficult match for Phoenix National, but Phoenix beat them in a surprising 2-1 game, shocking the attendees. And then. Playoffs came. The very first match saw #3 seed Notts Co vs Phoenix National #7. In a tight first game, Phoenix just barely got the better of their rivals in a 2-1 game, and drew the second winning by aggregate. Then Phoenix went on to rout the playoff finalists Southhampton in a 3-0 crushing victory, securing themselves a second promotion in a row. Phoenix National had truly risen from the ashes.As a game, there are the occasional bugs and problems, I've seen a couple clipping errors. But as a story-making device, as a simulation, it's phenomenal. Creating your own club, taking a bottom-of-the-league team and turning them into a success story, watching your striker go from goal drought to rainforest, cheering when your players win after a hard-fought penalty kickoff. Where FM21 really shines is how it makes you attached to each one of your players, and riveted by their growth.

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager 2021 engulfs you in it's wonderfully complex world that, makes you  like you are a manager.The tactical mechanics are fun to use and work well, but it could be taken to a deeper level. One way of achieving this would be to allow players to adjust formations automatically based on the phase of play, just as teams do in real life. For example switching from a 4-3-3 to a 3-4-3 when in possession of the ball, where your CB's split and your DM drops between them, while both FB's move higher up the pitch into a Wing Back position.I believe console games offer something similar to what I am describing.FM continues to improve and I am glad to see improvements to the match engine, but I must admit that I do dream of a match engine built by one of the big boys...Transfers feel realistic, clubs negotiate astutely at times and it's not often I get frustrated when clubs are being unreasonable... but perhaps that's in fact, less realistic?Overall it's a solid effort with real improvements, some of the highlights being the UI and match engine upgrades. _childDocuments_.review: I finally upgraded to FM21 after skipping FM19 & 20 - mostly it was the xG feature that piqued my interest, but I also like to update every so often for little things like competition rule/qualification changes, refreshing rosters, etc. Coming from FM18, I've been pleasantly surprised at some of the new features added in FM21 - not only do I really enjoy the xG thing, I love the overall improvement in what I'd call "realism": The interaction with staff continues to get better and better, the way staff and management present you with reports and call meetings is awesome, and the scouting meetings before transfer windows are so damn cool. It all combines to make you feel like you're actually a manager and not just playing a game. I'm at around 230 hours of FM21 and I'm still constantly finding myself engaging with new things. Last, I'd just like to share my experience/thoughts on scum-saving. For the most part during my thousands of hours of FM over the years, I felt like I was pretty fair about reloading matches - I only tended to do it if I had a bad injury to a star I'd just signed, or conceded a BS glitch/bug goal, etc. Sometimes if I was having a bad day and fired up FM only to be down 4-0 to Man City in the 35th minute I'd just Ctl-Alt-Delete and replay the match a few days later. But with my new save in FM21, I've been experimenting with a strict no-save-scumming policy, and it's added a whole new compelling element to my gameplay. I had a real stinker of a game against Newcastle (5-0 I think) - the sort of game I'd have been tempted to reload in the past - and a day later my players refunded the supporters' tickets for the match. How cool is that!? I also got to within one bad result of getting sacked, and had to get something away at Sheffield Utd - what a nerve-racking match that was! My boys pulled out a 3-1 win to keep me alive, and we had a short run of good form to finish the season, allowing me to get the transfer reinforcements I desperately needed. So TL;DR: FM is hands down the best sports management sim on the market, I felt it was well worth the money to upgrade from FM18 to FM21, and if you've never experimented with a no-save-scum policy - give it a whirl. I think you'll find it rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: What more needs to be said? I came into this with a rudimentary understanding of football and now I'm a self-confessed addict. What is essentially a series of numbers interacting with each other (more so than any other game) produces such high-stakes drama that I've elicited concern from housemates at my explosive swearing or cheering. Your attachment to your team and players, and subsequent exploration of their real-life counterparts, results in a grand soap opera experience where losing can be just as thrilling as victory. I now have an encyclopaedic knowledge of Colombian football and it's byzantine league system for instance! While there is an inexhaustible supply of resources online to help in tactic formation and player selection, Football Manager still remains opaque enough that my main concerns are likely conspiracy theories. I feel like team training is way over-thought by most guides (it's just raising the bars using the appropriate training module right?). I'm also CONVINCED that there's a dice-roll whenever you start the game which determines whether you inexplicably drop in form! This is my first foray into the franchise, which has long been criticised for resting on it's laurels and iterating slowly. Should this be my only Football Manager though, the experiences and dramas will be more than enough to get my money's worth. Also: f*** you PSG!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a sports fan of any team game in our known universe.  As a matter of fact, I've always hated team sports.  These hates have spanned about 65 years.  I tried team sports in school while growing up, I hated them all.  The funniest fact of all is that soccer was my most hated team game next to basketball.  Soccer was THE most hated team sport, the top of my hate list.  Man has hands and soccer won't let him use them.  Stupid.However...My most favored genre of games are management, builder, and simulation.  In 2020 I saw Football Manager 2020 and instantly hated it.  The only good looking part of what I saw on Steam was the color purple.  I like purple.  Then I saw the word Demo.  I also like the word Demo, reminds me of the word Free.  Soooooo, I tried the Purple Demo.Then...I was amazed at the massive amount of management options, supported with tooltips and help.  The more options I tried, the deeper I fell into management bliss.  One option led to another option, and a spiderweb of fun began to form.  I was liking the sport of soccer, team sport and all!  Pretty soon I owned FM2020, then FM2021, a purple mass of team sport management greatness.  The many varied ways these games inter connect within themselves is beyond amazing.  I've been impressed with a few choice games of this genre, but never even close to the amazement of this FM series by Sports Interactive.

_childDocuments_.review: I get up at 7:30am every morning, I brush my teeth and shower my filthy body. I kiss my girlfriend on the cheek and leave to drive the 20 minutes to my office. I arrive, sling some of the dirty brown grind into the pot and squeeze out the life source for the morning. I glance through my spreadsheets, sales are up, revenue is down, number, fractions and formulas. My boss is screaming in my ear "I am not pleased with your performance today", I look down at my keyboard, my hands are trembling... Does he not know? I watch as he glances through Resume after Resume of potential candidates. Did somebody leave? Do we have an opening? I catch a glimpse of the same set of skills on my own resume. Is it true? Is he trying to replace me? I submit my work into the drop box at 16;45, plenty of time before the end of the day to show the boss I am ahead of schedule. I look across to the conference room, that guy he hired last week, presenting a spreadsheet by the same title. I spent days working on my one and I've been replaced. I clock out and drive the 20 minutes home, the note on the kitchen counter from my girlfriend "I'm sorry, I'm leaving you. My new boyfriend has recently recieved a billion dollar investment and he's building a new house". I should of known. I've carefully been balancing our budget so I could afford her that delightful argentinian terrier she wanted. Now for what? Nothing. I open my laptop and the sweet bliss as I click play on Football Manager. That's right, now it's my turn. I click into the first match, I watch as my boys demolish Stoke City 7-0. It's 42 minutes in. It's already over, but I'm not finished. I click the button that we all love so, "Demand More"tldr this is a fun game

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the interface this year is simply awfull. I wanted to give it a little time before writing the review because I thought I could get used to it, but from menus hidden in menus, to making the preferences a keyword search instead of a simple list you could scroll down to find what you were looking for, the interface is just getting more and more frustrating every year. You remember those super complicated computer screens in syfy games/movies which look like a browser with 100 pop-ups? Yeah that's how the match screen is right now. The match-screen is flodded with pointless menus and stats while you can only customize roughly half of your screen and the most unimportant parts of it. Forcing you to look at non stop pop-up suggestions you most of the time don't want to take, taking up 1/3 of your screen while something as essential as head to head tables/subs are "hidden" behind several clicks and only allowing you to look at either your or the oppositions team or at a table. It feels like they realized people would play to fast with new saving and loading times and made the game harder to manoeuvre instead of simply adding actual depth.Sadly it does not end there, poor sizing of boxes and bad use of space and what feels like 10 different box sizes and menus all around your screen instead of just putting it into one bar (have you ever used a computer with an operating system???) in addition (maybe the lockdown can be blamed for this) SI refused to give us a simple dark/light reskin of the base skin, forcing you to use their rebrand advertising color purple. Hell, my fav color is purple and I can't stand it because it is simply to much and it strains the eyes, because a color like this is not ment to be used as base color.Saving times and match engine have improved slightly, but the dynamics are once again a bit off with players learning new positions strictly being mad for playing in said new position. Many of the reocurring issues in FM such as board interactions regarding club improements are still as boring as in previous versions and the latest "big" update has caused my processing time to go up signifcantly. The new transfer and contract screens suffer from similar issues as the match day, but I will be fair, I havent spent much time in those yet. Despite the new saving method which to be fair only takes a few seconds I will probably go back to 2020 on which as in several other versions I have recorded over 1000 hours. This iteration is simply a waste of time until the skin-ing community has finally gotten out some proper skins, which feels off because I paid for a full release title that feels like a tech-demo.

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell, I think it's definitely the best FM that's been released so far. Maybe it's not a release that's had major tweaks and improvements made to it but the cosmetic changes and other small changes across the game have definitely made it better. You'll see a lot of people say / use the arguement "it's not FIFA" when it comes to graphic improvements but I definitely welcome any improvements that are made to the graphics, especially when it comes to newgens. It definitely helps add more immersion and realism to the game when the newgens actually look half decent. Yeah, there could be more variation to them but it's something that hopefully SI will work on and fix so it's not an issue.I think just adding small things such as 'administrators' to the game and having the administration process as it is in real life helps - it's one of many small but realistic changes that have been made that help the game move closer to how it should be.I won't be pretend that I'm not gutted that more bigger changes could have been made, and haven't, but I'm certainly happy with the changes that have been made this year. It's safe to say I wasn't expecting much from the feature releases and trailer but I've been impressed so far. For me, although I have excellent hardware already, the improved processing & save times are fantastic and have helped me fly through months faster than I have ever experienced before and I love it. If you're stuck on an old copy of FM because you've not fancied upgrading, I'd definitely recommend giving this one a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to give this game a negative review but I will until the following issues are fixed. Mainly because SI stated they were going to fix it but still have not, making the game incredibly difficult for me to play for extended periods. Some UI decisions have been questionable at best. They didn't even take into account those with poor vision or colourblindness, like myself. It's so hard for me to gauge my players fitness. They say "it was unrealistic to see a players fitness by a percentage". Well it's also unrealistic to know a players exact "reaction" after a shout. When I hear a manager shouting in real life on the side line - I don't see them take out a smiling emoji?!?!?! Nor do they smile, give a thumbs up or act delighted. 99% of footballers are so focused they totally ignore anything and the only reactions you do see are celebrations or anger fuelled by their adrenaline. So lets put this talk of "realism" on the back burner and put our eyesight and long term/extended play as a priority. If it aint broke, don't fix it.Also regarding fitness etc. At least you hear managers say in real life "he's about 70% fit at the moment". Knowing a players "feelings" by body language is way more unrealistic - same as morale.Some other UI decisions are weird - like the crooked "official team sheet" that represents data on an angle - totally triggering my OCD. Never present data on a weird angle - its ugly. Also when you do team talks - theres half the starting line up on the left and then the attackers along the top. Si stated and I quote "this is a bug we will be looking to fix for the full release". Still not fixed. Also highly triggers my OCD and it's just difficult to look at. This was perfectly fine on FM2020...just leave this stuff alone, seriously.The match engine is a huge improvement but I still see a lot of "ping pong" rebounds and very odd decisions where players keep trying to all shoot into a wall of players. I almost felt compelled to make a video of it with pinball sounds as a joke. I also noticed that there is some match speed changes this year. Match speed at 50% feels like its in slow motion at times and 1 notch to the right seems too fast.Match sounds (which have not been updated in over 15 years) have managed to regress again. It suddenly and abruptly cuts off during highlights - giving the game an unpolished feel. I know 99% of FM players play with the sound off but sound is a huge part of football - it's a huge part of the atmosphere. Covid has already taken this away from us in 2020, so please fix the sounds or work on a HUGE expansion to the sound in FM22!!! The only reason 99% of players play with the sound off is because its bad. They don't play with the sound off because they want to. If FM21 had similar sounds to say (FIFA or PES) they wouldn't play with the sounds off. This is the classic chicken or the egg question...you tell me this. How many people play FIFA or PES with the sound off. How many people play ANY game with the sound off?? That's right - not many - if any. Improve your sounds and you will see most people will play with the sound on. Selling players is incredibly difficult this year because they tried to add "covid" effects for realism. Look - either add Covid in FULLY into the game with empty stands, the actual virus and all of its effects in the game or leave this cruddy disease out of the game and allow us to forget about 2020 and enjoy a fantasy 2021. I think it should have been totally left out - with 0 effects from covid and allow us to enjoy the game normally, with normal finances and the ability to sell players at least for their value. It does make buying players easier, but then again - most clubs I have managed have a 0 budget to begin with...cause of covid! Thanks!! Can't even enjoy a fantasy.Also match day camera angles. They now added a zoom to the TV view. This actually gives me a little bit of motion sickness and dizziness at times. I don't experience this with a real life game, but in a video game at 60fps it does make me feel a bit queasy. Please give us an option to turn this off or add more camera angles (like a manager first person view). This is the first FM where none of the camera angles are suitable for my enjoyment. Director Cam is actually fine, but I hate all the other weird and distant angles during corners and throw-ins. Again a director camera with a toggable "other views" would be good.The other stuff is pretty good - its a big improvement compared to older FM's but some of these design and UI ideas and implementation doesn't take into account those with colourblindness and/or poor vision - causing eye strain during extended play.As stated, the match engine has improved but its still a bit silly at times.SI do the same thing year after year - they put in 110% effort and deliver a product to 90%. That extra 10% is always missing and eithe requires multiple patches until March to get things to maybe 95% or they let things slide for another year - then eventually letting things slide for over a decade (like sounds). They need a decent competitor to shoot a rocket up their butts to actually deliver 110% effort and a 110% product. For a full AAA price year after year - and one of the best sellers on STEAM - the old excuse of "we are just a small company" no longer suffices. This is a company that makes hundreds of millions of dollars and hiring some sound developers and giving the game a much larger improvement to atmosphere and graphics shouldn't be as slow as a progression as it has been. Ultimately this game still has graphics of a game from 2006 and sound from a game in the mid 90's. Again, this is a game that I love and pump a bunch of hours into - but at the same time - I expect more and I expect a polished product that takes into account people with vision issues, colourblindness, ocd and such.I will update this to a positive review when they at least fix the UI as they promised. I won't hold my breath for the match sounds to be fixed but I hope that it will be a feature of FM22 "New and improved match day experience and atmosphere!".My guess is that by FM2030, they still won't have updated sounds.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re reading this Football Manager 2021 review, the FM series shouldn’t need any introduction, but I still prefer to do a quick recap for newcomers to the game. Football Manager has been an undisputed leading football manager game in its field for over 20 years. While the heart of the game is playing the role of a coach intent on climbing to the top of the world, much more is hidden under the hood of this game.Besides coaching, the player will also have to devote himself to collateral activities such as relations with the press, transfer market, and much more. Football Manager is therefore a deep and complex title, at times even too much, but thanks to the improvements made over the years it has allowed more and more possibilities to manage and personalize the experience at the helm of the club.Having entered the franchise perspective, let’s get ready to discover this new chapter of the series together. You start the game by creating your coach, then you choose whether to start with a club or go in as “unemployed” and wait for a proposal from some team. Once you have chosen your preferred mode and signed the contract, you are ready to get to the heart of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Having taken a World of Warcraft sized break from FM, I grabbed FM20 cheap at the end of the game cycle and recaptured the addiction, leading me to FM2021.This iteration is not without flaws, but for the most part they are minor and related to my own personal idea of sim vs reality. The engine is the best its been in the versions I've played since 3d became a thing. It has some quirks, but most of them are down to the engine showing a player acting a certain way but the visual representation isn't realistic enough to look at and say, "I get why he did that". For example, a player may not react to a ball over the top as swiftly as you would hope and it seems like an oddity of the engine, when in fact its down to the player not having high enough concentration or anticipation, so by the time the ball is in the air he's reacted too slowly and moved toward the ball when its already heading over him.The game is yet to become remotely uninteresting for me after 500 hours working to return Hamburg SV to greatness whilst never signing anyone over 19, so I'm still shocked when I finally hit the quit button and the time isn't 11PM but 3 AM. If that isn't an endorsement, I can only imagine you're completely unfamiliar with the franchise. To any FM veterans (or CM old guys like myself) that have not yet dived in, my advice to you is this: Order a weeks shopping, kiss the family goodbye, make sure the pets have their care accounted for and click BUY.

_childDocuments_.review: My recommendation of FM 21 is based on the fact that it´s still a good game based on the foundation of previous iterations, however there is very little new under the table. Most of the changes that are required for an optimal game play have simply been ignored by the devs.1. Fixture congestion is a real problem, you will often have f.ex. 11 days with no fixtures or internationals only to have to play 3 games in 6 days, in a WC season I had 6 games in 12 days. It has been problem for a long time.2. First team players who aren´t constantly starting will be restricted to light training schedules if you have a very busy season with games every 2nd or third day. It means they aren´t really evolving, sending them to the U23 squad to get normal training makes them unhappy and the "elevator" micro management of each player isn´t desirable either. A simple solution for U23 players would be to have the "Available for first team" option but so far I havn´t been lucky in getting any responses.3. Regardless of tactics you will still encounter "super keepers" who just are your only opponent, their entire team getting 6.2 avg rating while the keeper is getting 8.5, I still win, sometimes by a large margin but their keeper is often MoM still. I have lost 4 finals in a row, conceded 4 goals in 4 shots while their keeper made MoM in all games.4. Penalties are weird, in one of the 4 above mentioned finals I missed 5 penalties, Wolves missed 4 and scored on the last thus winning. At least the AI is having difficulties with penalties as well, in the league I have about a 50% penalty conversion rate and so does the AI, this has gradually worsened as seasons have passed so it could be a regen issue.5. Speed/Pace still has too much of an influence.6. While you can be successful without constant high pressing it´s difficult, it´s doable but tactics rely too much on total pressing. This especially proves true if you have high acc/speed players.7. The AI harassing you about wanting your players is okay, in FM however this gets taken to entirely new level and you can hear about it every single week throughout an entire season how much X club wants half of your team. When it comes to the bidding however .... they try to buy your players for peanuts. Aston Villa would probably receiving 3-5 bids every week of about 20 million euros in FM in 2037 on a relative comparison, he is worth about 50 million I believe.8. You get asked the same questions from the press every single week, one would think they would have had the time to develop interviews to be diverse, it´s like a loop that never ends.9. The training schedules from the ass. manager are horrendous, they may work if you can´t be bothered to change them but results on the pitch definitely improve vastly with a lot of tweaking. This becomes especially true when you are involved in all competitions and the schedule has heavy duty training the day before a match.

_childDocuments_.review: With thousands of hours in FM starting in 2008 I can safely say this is the update I've been waiting for. The last few releases have felt like re-skins but they've made some really nice changes this year.Firstly the match engine has definitely been improved. I see some comments saying it hasn't but if you've played/watched enough FM games you'll know the outcome of almost every highlight during a game but now some things will happen that you didn't expect. For example teams can counter attack 2 or 3 times before someone actually has a chance. Passing and movement seem much slicker too. The interface now shows useful information in-between highlights such as match stats, player ratings, opposition formation and a live league table instead of just staring at an empty pitch.Outside of the match engine I've noticed players don't moan as much and are easier to appease. Usually every season half of my squad want to move to a bigger club but in 3 seasons so far I've only had 2 players ask, I convinced both to stay.At the end of the season there's what I can only describe as a presentation of your season highlights. From a veterans point of view it's a really nice touch. It shows all the things I would usually look for at the end of a season in a really nice format, without me having to check each one manually or through an email. _childDocuments_.review: Here it is, another QoL update for Football Manager 2005. And there is nothing wrong with that (except the full game price we need to pay every year). Sports Interactive continuously evolving the game, making it more detailed. Though their vision about what is needed to be done may differ from yours (so, no multi-monitor support, no female leagues, no from-scratch/sandbox environments), it's hard to deny the effort.This year they focused on interactions, adding the gestures instead of the old speaking tone. While "kick the chair" may look funny, I doubt I'll ever kick it. But for some people who want to roleplay Jurgen Klopp, it may be of some use.I'm happier about match interface changes, especially about the detailed "Match Stats" widget. It's finally possible to see woodwork stats again after all those years! (And yes, it's pretty much high).I can't say much about how useful the recruiting meetings are, as in the first season I usually play with what I have, but they look nice. The same goes for the season review as I still haven't finished one (but can't wait for it).One of the most important things: they finally fixed visual tearing plagued FM20 on some systems (ignoring VSync settings).As for the match engine, nothing changed. I loaded my tactics from a previous FM, and it worked without any difference - more or less same stats, same performance, same (expected) results. That's rather good than not. But there is still no different attack and defense formation settings. Even PES has it for years. You can't recreate asymmetrical formation change in FM at the moment, and it makes Andrea Pirlo sad. Maybe next year? Time to give us more tactical flexibility.Let's cut it short. If you want a quality football simulator, not sports anime/manga-style (PES) and not arcade-style (FIFA), with a huge up-to-date database without errors even in the top team rosters (cough, cough, KONAMI), look no further.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to FM19, this game is a good improvement in my opinion. I haven't played FM20, so I can't compare this game to the last one. The match engine feels smoother and better. Players seem to really play football now and it's harder to tell when you will score or concede a goal. There's a also good amount of VAR moments, but it's not an annoying amount as it was in earlier games. The interface looks cleaner and feels a lot smoother. Loading times are also better and I really love the new UI. The only issue I have is the new logos that are used for fitness, etc. I hate the hearts and would love if they brought back the option to turn it into numeric percentages. The youth development and scouting tabs of the game have been changed and definitely improved. While it seems more advanced, it's also more user friendly to understand what the game is telling you about different players. A downside of this game seems to be the punishment you get from playing high intensity strategies, because it seems to really hurt your players and get you a lot of injuries. It somewhat forces you to play a less intense strategy, which doesn't really fit into everyone's playstyle..The last issue I currently have is the amount of spelling and grammatical mistakes that are in the Dutch translation of this game. I can't tell if this issue applies to other languages as well, but it's annoying. It could and should've been avoided. That said, I do think this game is worth it and is a great experience and upgrade from the earlier games. 8.5/10

One where I went up 0-3 and they made 3 goals in  7 minutes between the 80th and 90th minute, another where I went up 2-0 and they equalized in the 92nd minute.And the ultimate test to show that the system is basically setting you up to fail no matter whatSemi-final Belgian cup OHL (Opponent) vs Genk (me). I replayed this game 5 times* OHL won all off them (two after extra-time)* Genk had the higher xG in all of the matches* Genk didn't score a single goal, in 5 games, during regular time* During regular time Genk had an xG of over 1 three times out of five* The most atrocious one was a 3.92 (Genk) vs 0.39 (OHL)* Which OHL won during regular time with 2-0Others things that are still, and have been for a long time, in the game* Ridiculous number of blocked shots/crosses. Often by one of your own players* Ridiculous number of wide/over shots and headers* GK moving into position before a shot is even made* Opposition turning into tiki-taka Barcelona* Opposition getting perfect tackling. Tackle after tackle and not a single foul* VAR is just annoying. Every tackle near the box gets a VAR check even if it's clear it's meters outside of the area* Goals after the 88th minute. It's just a given. You play a top team and they will have at least one goal in that timeframe. Doesn't matter if you're defending a narrow lead or if they're already 3-0 up at that point. In conclusion: the match engine, the part that has needed some major attention for years, is still a cheating mess. Also: maybe people like the menu overhaul but to me this is way too cluttered.Edit: So I played a few more hoursThey seemed to have "solved" some match engine problems by dumbing down the AI. So once again we have GK not picking up a ball right in front of them, players running away from the ball, throw-ins going to an opposition player that doesn't even have one of your own players near him, in one memorable instance my five (5!) defenders let a single attacker run straight at goal with my two central defenders actually turning away from him.Also: too many bugs with regards to player happiness. I had three players complaining and being unhappy because they weren't included in the Competition Selection (except that they were), one being unhappy because I did not give him a loan, while I just accepted a loan, and one player being angry he was left out of the starting line-up while injured.One of my top players had 4 promises. I kept three but somehow he was still unhappy. A few months later he announces that he is now happy but it's still impossible to get him to sign a new contract because "he is currently unhappy". It's infuriating how many of the player dynamics mechanics do not work properly.Another one: the locker room leaders demand I give my star defender a transfer. When he is sold to Bayern one of the same group comes back complaining that he can't believe I let him go ...And another one: Player is unhappy demands to be transfer listed. I did. He then didn't show up for training but showed a willingness to improve his behavior. Two weeks later he withdraws his transfer request because he's happy now. The day after he wants to be transfer listed because he's unhappy ...And a last one: player was unhappy because I left him out of my Serie A squad. Said player was out on loan when I had to submit the squad and would not be available for the next three months.And the last one: Transfers are still broken. It is still common for clubs to constantly send you a low-ball offer for your starters, actually: it is beyond rare that they come anywhere near the market value. And when you refuse you get a new, still way lower than market value, non-negotiable offer which will make your player become unsettled if refused. Or they keep sending you the same offer over and over again. I have rejected an offer, the exact same offer, from Bayern 10 times now.Loans: same nonsense. I'm trying to loan out players for which I decline transfer offers all the time. Yet when I offer them for loan for no fee, no contribution to wages, etc nobody wants them. Have that make sense ...

_childDocuments_.review: I've only started playing FM since 2019, I know I haven't played a lot of the games but I can say with total confidence that FM21 is one of the best FM games. The good:The game shows improvement in the area of UI, mainly when playing matches where you can comfortably see the status of every player, everything else is pretty much unchanged but that's not a bad thing. The match engine has definitely changed. I don't know how to explain it but it feels very smooth and looks (most of the time) like an actual football game. The interview mechanic has been overhauled, it now has an actual purpose, it's not like previous games where I didn't care about it at all and skipped them, now you can have relationships with the press and change the mood of players but it can get old pretty fast since the interviewers almost always ask the same questions and at that point, you know what to answer to improve or worsen your relationships.The bad:The game is STUPIDLY EASY. I don't know if it's the formation I use or my tactics but it's VERY EASY. I can't emphasize that enough. I've only lost 4 games across an entire season and now I'm almost halfway through my second season and I haven't lost yet. Mind you, I picked an Argentinian football team so it's not like I've chosen incredibly popular teams. Sometimes the players do whatever the hell they want. Like I said at the beginning, I don't have a lot of experience when it comes to FM games but players just ignore orders, do whatever the hell they want and make stupid decisions. I'd like to believe that this is some kind of "realism" where players tend to do things wrong and not because of the game itself.It's also very annoying that at one point, your players will want a raise that reflects their improvement as a footballer but your club will not have enough money to pay them, leading to selling said players. I believe there should be some kind of option or a solution of some sort to tell them: "bro, why you asking so much, we don't have that much money". I've lost 3 good players because of this and even though I managed to mitigate this quite a bit, I'm about to lose a couple more. Overall, I think this is a great entry to the FM series, despite the issues, I think the good things outweigh the bad things. If you're thinking of giving the games a try, check this one out. As long as you get past those incredibly frustrating moments, it's a pretty chill game where you can dump time into.

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who played Football Manager right from 2005 through to 2015, and then flat out refused to buy or play a single other iteration of the game until now, it's fair to say I have mixed feelings about the franchise.I decided to take the plunge again after reading a whole host of good reviews from the beta, with many casting positive judgement on the new match engine and improved AI.For a game that has a 3d match engine for over a DECADE now, you'd think there would be scope for major, major improvements...now I'm not expecting to watch a simulated game of FIFA, but I still cringe at the physics, modelling and player interaction offer, and I've already switched over to my beloved 2D as I cannot stand to watch yet another:-Winger fly past/through a fullback at a million mph whilst STILL looking like he's got his finest hover board to hand-Wingers running down the flank to the final third, seemingly beating their man for pace and then STOPPING and passing back to the full back or CM.-And last, but OF COURSE not least, a winger getting to the byline and SHOOTING INTO THE SIDE OF THE NET - this has been happening since THE FIRST 3D MATCH ENGINE THEY BROUGHT OUT - When I saw it happen the first time on this version I nearly had PTSD symptoms.Press conferences are still the same repetitive, boring drivel which I of course subject my poor virtual assistant manager to every single game - SORT THIS OUT, MAKE IT FUN FOR THE LOVE OF GOD.That all being said, the new analysis tools are really helpful (xG in particular is a real game changer), which is nice. I have decided to give the game a recommendation because in these very early stages I feel that it's generally serving up the goods and it's a franchise so dear to my heart, but I cannot believe I'm experiencing many of the same woes that plagued this brilliant franchise over 5 years ago.Please SI, please please please sort out this match engine it's well beyond a joke, it's holding this game back from being the only game I'll play all year.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game, except for one major flaw; the match engine's hard coded bad streak / good streak mechanic. No matter what you do after a good run there will be one match a season, veterans will know the match I am talking about, where all of your players become limp fish on the pitch and lose form at exactly the same time. And before the hardcore fans come out and say "oh it's complacency" no, it's not there is not a single player with a complacent body language and everything has been done to reduce potential complacency. Messi's dribbling turns into Peter Crouch, Kompany's defending becomes like Ozil, and world class players just watch the ball go past them, hit the woodwork all of the time, miss every 1o1, cross the ball into defenders more often, pass the ball long straight back to the other team even though you have defensive short passing on, injuries to the best players etc etc. It's pretty much the same as the FIFA scripted mechanic. Then after this one match, the next 10 or so will become extremely difficult, and no change in tactic, roles, swapping in players, match talks, press talks... nothing will change this mechanic. The form is hard coded in the game and there's nothing you can do about it. Some people will say this is like real life; teams go through bad forms, and that is true, but the question is do we want to play a game which forces a bad form onto you which is completely out of your control, or would you prefer to have some influence over the bad form? This bad form will hit once a season on average, no matter what you do, consistent rotation or no rotation, changing tactics to adapt to the AI, or keeping them consistent it doesn't matter. Alot of people also respond to this criticism by saying, "the AI adapts to your tactics after a while if you are winning", and the AI does change their tactics, but them changing their tactics has nothing to do with why your team suddenly can't pass forwards without an interception, or they stand and watch the ball go past, or dribble straight into the opposition players, or hit the woodwork or get injured at 300% rate than normal, or suddenly can't make a first touch anymore, or their crosses hit the opposition and create a corner and you know all 1o1's will end badly during this form. Most of this has nothing to do with the opposition tactics, just because they went counter attack, shouldn't mean my players all lose 10 to their dribbling, passing, first touch, positioning stat for 10 games. The next response to this I see often is "what incentive would SI have to put such a mechanic in the game?"Because commercial incentives developers have in keeping their customers coming back every year. SI can't make the same game every year with an updated roster and a couple differences in the UI and match engine without generating an addiction in their customers. This bad/good form streak creates an actual dopamine psychological addiction, similar to loot boxes in other games or player cards in FIFA. The reward in this game is good form, and a feeling that you have overcome something which was prior out of your control. When you regain the good form streak, where now all your players dribble like Messi, and shoot like Lewandoswki, you feel like you are responsible. The human condition of contrast effect (is the enhancement or diminishment, relative to normal, of perception, cognition or related performance as a result of successive (immediately previous) or simultaneous exposure to a stimulus of lesser or greater value in the same dimension) creates a much larger sense of achievement when we get into a good form relative to the out of control bad form. Doubly it has an additional contrast effect as we feel like the game is out of our control during the bad form (external locus of control), and in control (internal locus of control) during the good form creating a massively exaggerated sense of being in control during the good form and we experience a dopamine feedback loop for the good form as we, without cognitive awareness, compare it to the experience and external locus of control of the bad form. SI used to have an addiction rating in the game based on the number of hours you played, they are well aware of how dopamine responds to this contrast effect of psychological states of external and internal locus of control. I worked in insurance gamification, so even more morally bankrupt than EA with FIFA, and they are very aware of mechanics for creating addictions in the customers. It's a business, it would be poor business management and product development if they didn't find a way to get customers coming back every year. SI would without a doubt have KPI's and OKR's and targets for customer retention every year, so the department responsible for hitting these targets would be probably the ones responsible for keeping these frustrating game mechanics in the game. Add to this that this bad form also creates an artificial difficulty spike which keeps the game engaging for veterans, who would stop buying the game if they found it too easy every iteration. This mechanic is actually not as bad as in FM2020, but it is still there and I doubt they will be removing it any time soon. I probably wouldn't have played this one for so long without the sense of achievement I had in being better at this one than FM20 which had even more bad form/good form mechanics. But my skeptical mind tells me they make each iteration in a rotation of difficulty to keep that addiction fed. FM22 will probably be more difficult again, and FM23 will be easier, so they generate a long term meta contrast effect, and we feel more in control in this version relative to the last so we enjoy it again, then it's too easy so they make the next game more difficult and frustrating again. Cycle repeats. It's actually good game design if you don't notice it, but once you notice it, you can't really go back in good faith realizing you are just actually psychologically addicted to the cleverly crafted dopamine cycles. And if you think it's not possible to be psychologically addicted to a game, gamblers on the slot machines have been shown to have actual similar dopamine responses to winning as people have to hard drugs. Think about that before you buy a game that intentionally gets you addicted. SI are no better than gambling companies, they just use a different psychological effect to get you addicted, just instead of money as the reward they give you a sense of inflated control relative to the bad streak.. which come to think of it is the same as a slot machine. To your brain there is no difference between winning money and winning a sense of control, they represent the same thing. The problem is if they made this mechanic transparent, it wouldn't have the same addictive effect, the same way knowing that a slot machine will ALWAYS hard coded give you a return of 96% on your $1, most people who realized this don't gamble. This game does the same with their hard coding of streaks, and once it's become transparent it doesn't have appeal anymore. So they need to keep it intransparent to keep the game engaging, and we will forever be frustrated at that bad streak until we liberate ourselves with the knowledge that this bad streak is intentionally there to keep you interested, and spending more money.

_childDocuments_.review: Look. I've owned every Football Manager since 2004. If there was a way for me to give the the "Mixed" button - somewhere between Yes and No, I would add it to the review. But if you're a Football Manager fan, it's worth getting it. But, there are still some concerns I want to address.First, I want to address all the positive reviews about the match engine. I have a weird feeling it's fake reviews, because the match engine is the same as last year's, and the same as the past five editions of FM now. Honestly, I know exactly when a goal will be scored, when I'll concede, and when certain events will happen. Even in this new FM. The animations are still the same, after about 5 years of SI promising us a "new and revolutionary match engine." I can tell you this ain't it.There are some nice additions to this new game, though. The addition of gestures makes it feel like you're there when you're doing the team talk. The press conferences have a bit more variety than before. When signing a new player, you have the option to welcome him with open arms, or pat him on the back, for example. These are all nice.I don't like the new in-game screen, though. It's far too cluttered, and when I'm making changes, I can't open a player's profile to see his best position. Also, I don't like what they've done with the stamina bars - I feel like they've dumbed it down from before, and now you don't exactly know just how tired a player is just judging on the colors of the "health" bar.But the elements that make us love Football Manager are still there. You can play as almost any team in the world and sign all the players you want with very realistic negotiations and all that. Still a long, long way to go when it comes to the match engine.UPDATE: After playing FM21 for a bit longer, I have the following to say:- If you own FM20, it's not worth buying this game. It definitely does not justify the price as there are not that many changes - if there are, they are minimal. I feel practically the same playing this game as I felt playing FM20. Save your money and download a mod with the latest transfers instead.. If you're new to FM or if you haven't owned it in a few years, then I'd say yes, it's worth it, but wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The match engine is an absolute beauty to watch, an amazing step up from 2020. I haven't screamed at the game for shot into the side netting for some time. The marking system overhaul is beautiful to see players intelligently cover space that others move from.  A lot of the goals are a lot more intelligently set up in the build up, it's very pleasing watching the football unfold.One feature about the transfers- you can ask agents what would make their players available, and they'll tell you estimated salary and requests before you even make a deal with their team along with whether they'd want to join now or if they'd consider it after promotion. The scouting meetings actually feel like meetings and can help newer players recognize what they're lacking much easier, helping the game become more accessible.The market has also been adjusted for covid, making players cheaper than ever and salaries affordable. I have only played until about February 2021 so far, but in a lower league save all these cheap deals, easy loans, and free agent players definitely allows you to get an easier step up.  According to SI this normalizes in a few years, so it'll be interesting to see how it unfolds.My only complaint- some of the UI is some seriously clunky nonsense.  I'd rather have a more compact menu with coherent information rather than a flood of random tidbits taking up all of the space on the screen but I'm sure there will be mods to address this problem shortly after the game goes live.  Considering a number of areas of the game took considerable steps up along with some much needed QOL changes (auto ready unfit guys for u23 games? hells to the yes), I suppose not all the changes can be winners.That being said, Having only started playing with FM19, this is the best looking and feeling iteration I've played. The whole match engine experience feels a lot more polished, and the games are more entertaining than ever to watch. If you've read this far, I'd like to say thank you for taking my review into consideration, and if you bought the game leave a comment and let me know how you're doing in your save. I'm curious to see others thoughts on the match engine as well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love to grind, this game is for you.If you're married and your wife hates the sound of the Xbox/PS turning on, this game on your laptop is for you.Observations: the depth of this game is vast compared to FIFA. With a couple hundred hours into it, I only made it to the end of my fourth season. Granted, it was my first time ever playing an FM game so it took me awhile to learn. I watched numerous YouTube videos, Twitch channels, you name it. I was all in. Now, I'm exhausted. I was told that the game was more realistic than FIFA, maybe so. But the actual games... infuriatingly unrealistic. The amount of times the opposition scored in the final moments of stoppage time, times the opposition scored multiple goals a man down, times my players played the ball directly to the other team leading to one-on-ones with the GK. (Memphis Depay notoriously did this two times in a single game and at least 5 times in a season before I rage sold him for pennies on the dollar to the Chinese Super League.) I get it, unpredictable things happen in soccer/futbol. Great. But not like this. Not to where these are the usual. Not to where you become so numb that you no longer have anxiety as the extended highlight shows the inevitable.In their determination to make it unpredictable, they made the game unplayable.My breaking point was a little experiment that I did with Liverpool and Chelsea. More specifically, Liverpool U23 and Chelsea. In the FA Cup Quarter Final. The game had made me so jaded towards Liverpool that I just wanted to destroy them. I pulled out the In-Game Editor for the first time and stuck it to Liverpool. I loaned out all their Senior squad members, making them play with only their U23 players. But that wasn't all. I wanted them to feel my anger, my hate, so I made all of them "Abysmal" morale through the editor as well. That would do the trick.I was wrong.After 7 games, Chelsea's senior squad starting eleven finally beat Liverpool U23 in the FA Cup Quarter Final.The U23 squad won 3 games, tied another 3 and finally lost the final game.Different formations were tried, 5-3-2, 5-2-1-2, 4-2-3-1, 4-3-3Different starting styles: Defensive, Cautious, Balanced, Positive, Attacking. But all led to Very Attacking in the final 10 minutes trying to muster another goal in the waning minutes of stoppage time. Yet Klopp prevailed with his Youngsters time after time.The final (only) win: 4-2-3-1, Gengenpress, Attacking. But even then, Klopp had his group of U23 tied 2-2 in the 80th minute before conceding two late goals to lose 4-2.That was when the realism was lost. Regardless of tactics, formations, or style, Chelsea starting eleven should beat Liverpool U23 barring the use of extremely unrealistic formations.I had started to question the realism in my first save when I was Manchester United and won the treble (Premier, FA, Champions)  in my first year (completely unrealistic) without ever save-scumming. The FM gods granted me this, trying to suck me in. And it worked.Maybe I'll play again. I can't say that I won't. I might have a weak moment. But I'm FM will quickly show it's colors.T&P's to all you brave souls who continue the ruthless grind, for you are better men/women than I.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played FM properly for about 10 years... sure I bought the odd game here and there but, now in middle age, rarely had enough spare time to let it get under my skin in the way that CM03/04 or early FM games once did. Don't get me wrong, some of those problems still exist - but somehow FM21 manages to make the whole experience far more approachable and accessible. The various in-game tutorials are succinct and helpfully explain the interface, whilst the ability to let your backroom staff take over tasks you don't want to manage (or don't yet understand) lets you crack on with the parts you enjoy. Even elements like press conferences and player interactions now feel far more neatly packaged and (a little) less like an immersion-breaking overlay on an access database... Sure most of this isn't new, but FM21 seems to have found a sweet spot that neatly wraps up the frightening depth of the game in a really approachable and understandable way.One thing still remains true... once this game sinks its teeth into you, you'd better have time in your diary and an understanding partner because there is nothing quite as addictive.

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager 2021 is the first FM game I have purchased since FM05 and before then CM01/02. The bones of the game haven't changed massively since then even as a lot of bells and whistles have been added. It is still an extremely in-depth football management simulation that still requires a massive time commitment in order to get anywhere. My impression is that in comparison to those early 00s versions, the game is trying to provide you with more assistance in figuring out what you actually need to do to have success. That is actually a big plus. In the old games there was a bit of an arcane element which could lead people down the rabbit hole for sure. There's still some of that but there is a more apparent effect of cause and reaction to what you do and how it affects the outcomes. There are also mechanisms that clearly were designed to take some off the workload from you. This also seems like a welcome attempt to make the game more accessible, and honestly it's very much needed. All the bells and whistles added since those early 00s games have hugely increased the amount of things on your plate as a manager in FM. If you've ever held a job in which monitoring an email inbox was a big part of your duties, well, much of the game will feel remarkably like that job to you.I have found that it was relatively easy and still satisfying to go through all that as long as you still feel that drive to lead your beloved club to that promotion, that league title, and eventually that European trophy. Once you've done that though and have gotten your 100 hours in just to accomplish that, well, the tediousness of it all may very well catch up with you. It can easily take a full day of playing this game just to get through an off-season. Even during a pandemic with nothing else going on, and your 'office' being the living room couch, that started to wear on me eventually. My feedback is thus still the same it was give or take 15 years ago. This is game that is aimed at hobbyists. And I don't mean people for whom football is the primary hobby, I mean people for whom playing football computer games is the primary hobby. This is a 1000+ hour plus game. The old adage "Less is more" is certainly something SI could take to heart to make a wider audience happier i.e. football lovers who still nevertheless enjoy the company of people, want to pursue other activities etc.In spite of that, I will give it a recommended vote because if you love football and want to play a football computer game, this is certainly the best option out there right now given the relative decline of the FIFA/PES series. And at least for now, I think most of us have just enough time to at least get some joy out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game since the early days of Championship Manager (and more sporadically in more recent years). All I can observe with any clarity is the fact that the fun element disappears year after year in place of supposedly 'realistic' aspects of management. They aren't realistic at all, they are superficial, piecemeal, callow notions of realism. All that made CM fun in the first place was doing your tactics, buying your players and watching the match. The trainspotter/statto/micromanagement mire of modern incarnations is testament to the ridiculous fanboy deference so many people have to the monopolisation of this genre by Sports Interactive. How about they actually release something that's fun? How about they stop acting like Adobe with yearly incarnations of Photoshop and stop introducing pointless measures of tedium just to justify taking £40 off you each your for the same game? Boring, tedious, not a simulation, not a fun game either.

_childDocuments_.review: 50 Hour ReviewFootball Manager 21 is a massive improvement over Football Manager 20. There are a few new features but really, this game overhauls some of the major features of the other Football Manager games.Sports Interactive have made it so your tactic files etc are compatible with this years game which is a really good move. Currently, you're not able to transfer training schedules but i believe this is due to a bug and will be fixed in the future.The new recruitment feature is decent and seems to be a really good feature at first  and honestly, it would help some newer players to the game but if you're a FM veteran, you'll find yourself using it less and less as time goes by.The graphics have had an overhaul and are much better than previous years, there isn't really too much i can say other than... they look great!The media and interaction features are really fun, the new gestures can really have a chat with a player, the media or the whole team much more effective. 50 Hours in, i'm still not telling my assistant to do it xD but, it does start to get a little repetitive after a while, once you have got past the "oh, this is amazing" feeling. It is still beneficial to both yourself and the team to have a good media relationship though as this can change the way the media talk about you, support or not support you during tough times and potentially buy you more time than you would have if you were struggling with your team. The new heart conditioning thing is really useful and does stand out more than using percentages but it would be nice to have the option to use either the heart display or percentage display. it does stand out more though.The way everything is displayed when in the match is a lot better and less cluttered than previous games, it feels good and i'm still not bored of watching my team actually play xD The last FM, i ended up downloading a skin that would let myself instant result but i can't see myself doing that this year as i'm really enjoying it a lot more.The new xG thing in FM is great and is a useful tool to understand how your team... strikers mainly are performing, please comment on this review if you have any questions about xG and i'll be more than happy to answer them. I really love the focus on more statistical information this year too.FM21 does seem to run a lot faster than previous years, i have players loaded from every continent etc with a lot of leagues and it's still really fast where as other FM games would have really slowed down the processing time, this one doesn't really affect much.There are more features in this years FM which i haven't mentioned but they don't seem significant enough to need to write about them. They are all really really good though and really does make this years FM feel much better.You're currently unable to search players by position etc when looking for new signings but Sports Interactive have come out and said that this is a bug and will be there in the future.Highly recommend FM21, any questions, please comment on this review and i'll get back to you as soon as i can <3
