_childDocuments_.review: A hybrid of Slay the Spire, and Into the Breach. Like many deckbuilder roguelikes lately, it's pretty good other than where its gameplay and progression mechanics deviate from Slay the Spire. The starting deck is way too strong, which makes the whole deckbuilder formula break down from the get-go. Because the starting deck is so strong, adding an unupgraded card to your deck EVER is pretty much a noob trap since it will reduce how often you draw your upgraded cards, which are immensely more powerful. You get stronger by spending money to upgrade cards at gyms, and money pretty much only comes from side-objectives in fights ("win within X turns" being the most frequent from what I saw). Some of these turn limits are borderline impossible, despite being a core progress mechanic. There's no risk/reward, only do well or do poorly.Event floors. From what I've seen, they're RNG based and neutral propositions at best, making them essentially wasted floors. In a game like this you should expect, on average, to get slightly stronger (or gain/restore vital resources like money and HP) each floor.Momentum is a resource that behaves like energy in Slay the Spire. After I beat the boss and got a thing that gives me +1 momentum per turn, my reaction was "what am I supposed to do with this?" Every single card I've seen is 0-1 cost (you even start with multiple 0-cost cards, and many that upgrade to 0-cost, and some cards that cost combo instead).There's considerable potential here. The stylized graphics are cool to look at and appealing in their own way, and the Into the Breach style tactical stuff works very well and is a welcome addition to the genre. Fights are well designed and tightly balanced. However, Fights in Tight Spaces makes far too many blatant missteps in its gameplay and progression design for me to recommend at its hefty pricetag.
_childDocuments_.name: Fights in Tight Spaces

_childDocuments_.review: Fights in tight spaces is 100% an entertaining deck builder. The John Wick vibe is strong, and the animations and aesthetic are on point. I also love manipulating enemies to damage or kill one another, as I feel like that really highlights the hand to hand combat vibe. The game also ramps the difficulty enough to be satisfying, and it took me a while to survive the final stages and secure my first win. At this point I have gotten a win on each of the 4 starter decks, which do put a twist on your combat style for each run. The recent addition of optional enhancements after clearing a stage also makes strategically building your deck far more viable. With that being said, while I feel like I got my money's worth, at this point the game doesn't draw me back in to try out new builds. I feel like there are just some cards you automatically pick, other you automatically avoid, and the deck composition variety is somewhat lacking. Deck themes eventually boil down to stuns, counters, throws, or big damage. There are some things that I feel like could be incorporated from other games (just rip off slay the spire, I mean come on, haha) that would add significantly more replay value.  My suggestions would be...1. Incorporate some kind of equipment system to provide more build variety and excitement from game progression. Some examples I think would be interesting include special neckties for choking, cuff links for conditional card draw, hidden wrist blades that add a bleed effect... the possibilities seem pretty broad if you are pulling from the secret agent genre, and it would serve to make individual runs varied enough to warrant further creativity from the player base. Perhaps this would go against the brawler feel the devs are going for, but I stand by the assertion that more variety like this is necessary to make this a bigger crowd pleaser. More card variety would go a long way as well. 2. Enemy variety could use some variability as well. Right now the factors that vary the enemies are primarily range, HP, attack strength, "heavy" status, counter status, movement reactivity, and block regeneration. I think enemies that grapple to restrict movement would be a wise addition, enemies that limit playable card options could be interesting, and I think enemies that reduce momentum via their attacks could be another viable option. Again, lots of possibilities, and I don't think they fall too far outside the secret agent or brawler genres to be adapted into the game. 3. I feel like as of now the medic station is kinda pointless. If you have any idea on how to build an effective deck, you can easily avoid the need to visit the medic, and are almost exclusively going to the gym to upgrade your deck. The expense of the medic functionality and the limited payoff for that expense is just too high to warrant when considering the significant opportunity cost of missing out on a gym visit. Many times, if you are going to take damage (which can primarily be avoided through effective positioning), the enemies eat through your hp so fast that no amount of maximum health would justify worrying about expensive max hp upgrades either. Another option might be to surround medic stations with fights that allow for max momentum upgrades to make me at least consider skipping a gym visit. Or simply make it to where the gym and the medic aren't mutually exclusive, so I don't feel such an enormous opportunity cost for making a medic visit.4. The combo system is very satisfying, but I would like to see more rewards associated with getting a high combo beyond additional damage or making a card playable while not requiring momentum. Healing, stun duration, player movement enhancement, and aoe chip damage could all be nice ways to reward combo accumulation, and could add to the options for my equipment suggestion in point 1. 5. The feeling associated with beating the game is dampened by the tacked on completion scene. It doesn't feel as epic as I would like, and I don't know how this could be achieved outside of some kind of cutscene that adds some hint of plot progression or celebration for your accomplishment. While there is a good amount of satisfaction derived from overcoming the games difficulty, I don't feel rewarded by the bland and brief finale "scene".All in all I would certainly recommend getting into this this game, but I would love to see it become the next big deck builder by incorporating more run variety to enhance replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Fights in Tight Spaces

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. It was my first Roguelike Deck Building game so I was coming to this without much knowledge of the "greats". The visuals and style are top-notch and the ragdoll effects of each kill can range from satisfying to hilarious. It took me a couple of runs to really get into it, but the first time I wiped a room with slick uses and combinations of movement, counter, combo, and attack cards in practically one turn really woke me up to the potential. I definitely see a lot of room for improvement in terms of more cards, events, levels, enemies, and whatnot but as it's in early access and just released I don't think it's fair to criticize that part of the game just yet. Especially because what's here is pretty substantial.To put it in perspective, this game made me want to play Slay the Spire as I'd heard a lot about it beforehand so I bought it. And I just completed my first run of Slay the Spire in 10 hours. In contrast, I have 24 hours of playtime on Fights in Tight Spaces and I haven't reached the fifth and final area yet. Maybe I'm bad, I don't know. But I do know I've already gotten my money's worth at this stage of development. Keep it up guys! Can't wait to see how this turns out.

The only thing I dislike is how they reward you money (to spend on upgrades, new cards, healing) you can only get money through events or completing stage missions, for example keeping someone alive or beating the stage in a certain amount of turns. _childDocuments_.review: Great game! Simple in learning, but very interesting and addictive. Great pool of random possibilities creates almost endless variations of outcome. You can pass through available campaings one time after another, and each time it will feel like unique character and expirience. Feels a lot like a John Wick movie. Would fit a lot better, than official John Wick game. Subjects for further improvement:- more story campaigns. Passing over the same pool of bosses and levels after ~100hrs feels a little bit dull;- moderate character customization would be nice, Nothing too harsh, keeping the feel an visual style of the game, but offering people to fool around with their character's look, maybe add some elements inspired by the look of classic action movie heroes;- replay mechanincs need some fine-tuning. A lot of moments, where camera goes behind objects, failing to show the fight. Some renewed cinematic replay version would be nice too: with smoother (not so step-by-step, as in game itself) movement, better camera angles and maybe even some cinematic effects: motion blur, color and light effects & etc. Feels like it could boost the game among content makers community - it would be much more interesting to stream, you would get much more intersting video conten from this game to share.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked "Attack the Spire" & Are  fan of hyper action martial Arts films with a sense of Humor toward them, You will love this Game.Fans of "Magic the Gathering Card games" will find a labor of love here. The card style system combines an idea of deck building with an eye to themes. From Brawlers  to knife fights in the Prison shower, cards drawn are used to change the circumstances of fights.Tactics are needed to defeat challenges in the rounds. Do well in the combat puzzle tactics card game and you will have the best cards for your theme.Think you can build better?Build your own and test it out.This game is unique in its title and fresh game style. A combination of several games without being too serious. Perfect for working at home or handling another boring meeting and need the ability to pay attention but demand a little distraction to get through it.

_childDocuments_.review: An stylish, fun little adventure that you won't get tired of beating over and over. Think the John Wick movies turned into a roguelike card game. It's very unique on its application of rules, adding a third dimension - literally - to the formula. Instead of just blocking damage, you could just... get out of the way by moving to where the enemy is not going to hit.It's like making your own action movie, frame by frame. Pick the action of your characters and earn extra reward by being cool and completing additional objectives that can give you a few rewards. The replay value comes from starting with one of the set, pre-established formulas with a coherent strategy, and slightly modifying your strategy depending on what randomness dictates to adapt to the challenges ahead. It's not overly challenging, but it's also not that easy, and there are plenty of difficulty levels were to pick from. Instead of increasing the enemies' damage or health, it simply takes off your training wheels, so you can actually stand against the world all by yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Review edited for 02/06/21 v.0.18: Don't bother, the deck building that has been introduced doesn't actually let you choose from all the cards but rather a selection of random cards that it brings up, you can spend 10 minutes re rolling by going back to the menu each time you don't get a build you are happy with, when you finally do you still have the issues of enemies getting block added every turn which makes no sense, enemy health that far outstrips damage, lack of ability to use their firearms or weapons, lack of damage from firearms, lack of damage from punches, seriously this could have been a great game but I've a total lack of faith in the developers seeing the direction this is going. It's less James Bond and more Benny Hill, the slapstick fights can go on forever if you get stuck in a loop of bad draws. The only positive is the dark theme is less irritating on the eyes. It's a 6/10.A fun fighting puzzle game, I put quite a few hours into the Demo on a different account and bought this within an hour of it going on sale. The presentation style is very nice, there are many varied enemies and the AI is very good at using them.Reasonably well balanced though I'm not much into deck building games so I'm not the best to say, you effectively have 4 characters that all look the same (Balanced, Attack, Defence and Gadgets) I've played with the first 3. Attack struggles to draw movement cards  but is also not strong enough to knock out 2 people per turn meaning you often get grouped up and whittled down, over the course of 20 or so encounters you've usually taken too much damage so prioritising purchasing healing becomes the only option, a lot of the big attack cards are also situational requiring you to be next to a wall or to have a certain combo meaning you're able to attack less often, or less times per turn, than Balanced.Defence has the opposite problem, you get slightly more movement but because you have next to no attack cards you rely on counter, which deals damage when you get attacked, however most block cards are 6 or 10, and counter is 8, meaning even a turn where you use only block and counter and don't move you can do at best 28 (often 14-24 depending on RNG card draws) but most enemy attacks are 8-12 meaning if you are taking on more than 2 and sometimes even more than 1 enemy you find yourself putting out low damage over time and taking damage just to be able to deal it.I've not yet played with gadget deck so I can't say, but Balanced seems to be the only viable deck as you can add more attack and movement cards as you go along and it always has enough movement cards cropping up to move to avoid taking any damage which is better than sitting still and taking it just to be able to hit back, and seems to always have attack to if not take an enemy out in one turn, circle around taking no damage and beating them up over 2 or 3 turns.It's a fun cerebral puzzle with the veneer of brutal human aggression, a blood stained Rubik's cube, and while I tend to keep going to see what is in the later levels I suspect it lacks the true replay-ability of FTL or (although I haven't played them) something like Darkest Dungeon or Slay the Spire.Most of the attacks are well balanced, a couple of kicks like jumping kicks don't have knockback, you can block pistols which also feels a tad strange (counter if you were one tile away would make sense like Bond or Bourne grabbing the gun to deflect but me putting my hands up from across the room probably shouldn't stop bullet) and some sorely lacking combat options would be things like if you can move around an enemy then punching them in the back of the head should stagger for one turn, doing a certain amount of damage (say 75% of their total health) in one turn should also stagger because it feels a little cheap when I superman punch someone, slam their face into a wall and then roundhouse kick them to head for them to just shoot/punch/stab/whack me like it's no big deal.You can also fall foul of the dreaded RNG, I was having a particularly good run until I spawned trapped in on all sides by enemies that auto attacked me, and RNG decided I also wasn't allowed my slip cards that would let me escape, meaning all I could do was throw a punch and then got wailed on by shotguns and nightsticks, an ignominious end to Mason Borne super spy extraordinaire.The level progression also makes less sense than FTL, where you are travelling through a galaxy and random events pop up, giving you story and starting fights or random chance choices, in this you know what you are going to always, but random events are ALWAYS separate from fights, with no story in between. Meaning you have to actively choose to avoid playing the game to get random events, which out of the 10 or so times I've got them seem to always be bad anyway, far from being a tactical way to avoid damage and just make it to that health stop or shop they can end a run on their own if you are low on health and if you aren't can often give you more damage than you'll normally take. Especially as they are independent of the titular fights in tight spaces it seems like odd game design to make the player actively choose to not play the game in order to do them even if they were to always work out well, personally I think they'd be better just randomly cropping up every so often between fights, like FTL.Perhaps a bigger issue is the lack of story, there is a story about interconnected gangs and etc as you might expect, but between the fights there is no story, it's a string of random fights, fight the boss, get told that they are connected to another gang. The story really amounts to a backstory of exposition given at the start, a history on the gang. But there's no explanation why I'm going from one bar to the next beating up bikers or why people are trying to shoot me in the prison showers. I get that as it is Randomly choosing rooms it would be very hard to connect these fights but even something small to connect them would be good, just like FTL's random one line dialogue boxes that can pop up. "You search the body of one of the bikers, his phone says meeting in X Alley at Y time" and then your next fight is an alley.Unless gadgets deck allows you to do this you are also totally unable to carry guns, knives, bats, or use pans, books, pencils etc in the environment, something the Jason Bourne, Sam Fisher (circa Conviction or Blacklist) or John Wick fans might be annoyed by. I get why I can't bring a gun into prison (although the inmates seem to have raided the armoury and there are no guards trying to stop them, which would be nice touch, not exactly allies as they attack whoever is nearest but something to distract and make it feel less like an all vs you game) but perhaps at the start of the biker mission I could have one, until it gets taken off you by an event or knocks out of your hands when you take damage? You can't disarm them out of bad guys hands either, SOMETHING that would make the Defence deck a really good pick.I'd give it a tentative 7/10 hoping that it will improve as it is very early access at the moment, but at the moment probably 6/10 which yes is over average but I still wouldn't recommend buying...yet.

_childDocuments_.review: First off let me say, I've been sim racing for 3 decades (which yes, makes me old!).  I started with Indianapolis 500: The Simulation and have played each and every Papyrus game since.  I have also run iRacing and I have been a HUGE fan of each and every one of those games.  This year, during the pandemic, NASCAR Heat 4 was on sale and I thought, what the heck, I have time on my hands, lets give this thing a try.  I set out wanting to not like it to be very honest.  My expectations were low, quite low in fact.  After running my first few races I felt I was liking it just enough to try running a career.   A few days in I realized something.  I was having fun.  More fun than I expected.  I kept playing, and my fun level continued to rise.  I continued to play NR2003 for my weekly races but kept coming back to NH4.  It was a damn fun game.  Was it perfect, absolutely not.  But, the racing was very good, the setups fun to build and I was moving on up in my career.So here we are, Boxing Day here in Canada.  Again I took advantage of a sale on Steam and bought NH5.  I'm sorry to say this but, those that are bashing this game are not being fair and open minded.  I think it is very, VERY good.  There was enough of a tweak in the physics, paint updates and the ability to remove that damn steering wheel in cockpit view to make it worth the $22 CAD I paid for the Gold edition.  Is it perfect?  No.  Is it NR2003 or iRacing?  No.  But, maybe it doesn't need to be.  I mean it's now 2021.  Should a game that came out a few months ago be the same as one that came out 18 years ago this Feburary?  I don't think it should.  These guys did what I feel is a great job on this game.  I look forward to their next effort with a new game engine.  And if I could be so bold, I'd like to offer my following top 10 suggestions (or wishlist if you will):1.  Setup notes:  I have been making setup notes on my iPad after each race so I know what I've adjusted, how it has run and where I finished.  This would be a great addition to the garage if it could be done in game.2. The ability to modify the setup immediately after the race.  Allow us to return to the garage after the race and "debrief" with our crew and make some changes to the setup right then and there.  I guess you could exit the event, reload and make your changes that way but this feature would be much more user friendly.3. Track bar adjustments on pitstops:  Ok, this is kind of a must.  Not sure why they aren't there but the next game really needs to have this.4. Practice leaderboard:  It's also kind of a must to get an idea where you stack up against your competition during practice.  It could be live, or, it could be something that is generated after you end the practice session.  Either way that is important info every NASCAR team has.5. Race info positioning:  As someone who uses a triple screen setup, it is horrifying to look all the way to the left or right to find out this valuable in race information.  Maybe a choice of "narrow" which brings them in much closer to the FOV of a triple screen driver?  6.  Paintbooth:  Pretty well done for an in game booth, however, it would be nice to be able to import our own numbers, logos, or even fonts.  I don't see 704 opening up the game to import 2nd party paintjobs ala NR2003 since they make their money off the monthly pay content but a bit more....flexibility would be nice.  A nice meet in the middle you'd say.7.  Driver name editing:  Ok, so 704 want's you to purchase their monthly content.  That's cool, it's a business and it's their business model.  Cool, I can live with that.  But please allow us an easy way to edit the drivers names.  Another way to meet us in the middle.8.  Smoke colour:  Sweet baby Jesus....tire smoke from burnouts is NOT GREY!  Nor is it for spin outs.  It's white and it needs to be white in the game.  It would be cool if the game could recognize when it's tire smoke (white) or engine/oil/terminal issues (more grey than tire smoke).9. Donuts ON the car after side by side contact:  When I raced IRL I would love my kart/car showing the wounds of hard racing battle after close races with another car.  Those 1/2 or 3/4 or even 1/4 little circles of rubber on the sides looked so cool, sometimes I'd even leave them there for a few weeks.10. Sun positioning (ok, this is getting nit-picky I know):  So, for example.  At Michigan, if you are sitting at the start finish line, the sun rises directly in front of you over the backstretch.  As a result, the sun sets directly behind you and the grandstand.  It would be a nice little touch to check these facts out and implement them accordingly to each track.So there you have it.  A completely honest review of NH5 from a self admitted Papyrus fanboy.  I really sugest you give this game a shot and play it with an open mind.  I think you'll be surprised like I was at the result.RJMikP.S.  I really hope 704 reads my suggestions.  I think they are valid and not tremendously difficult to implement.P.S.S.  Thanks for updating the trophies in NH5 with the patch.  It did kind of bother me seeing NASCAR HEAT 4 on them in NH5.  Buuuuuut......someone really needs to issue that girl on the right in victory lane a new laminate.  Hers is still from NH3.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to give the game time to grow on me. You would think 5 years into this project it would have made incremental progress toward games that game out in the early 2000's at least. Positive reviews for this game are from people clearly content with the lackluster. The studio has barely even made graphic improvements despite the release of TWO generations of graphics cards since the first installment. Since I have nothing positive to say about the game, I will just list the CONS. Also, before the nerds come out and attack me about something I DIDN'T say, let me add that I am not reacting to this as a racing simulator. I fully understand the game as an arcade racer.CONS1. Still no paint booth. How hard is it to give us a paint/wrap studio similar to Need for Speed? You have like 10 preset paint patterns, and about 10 preset number styles. All you're allowed to do is change the colors. By the way, all the number  preset are TERRIBLY UGLY! 2. Victory burnout physics is TRASH! You can't do donuts because the car stops spinning after a 180. You cant smoke your tires or anything. 3. Victory lane celebration is boring. No champagne. No trophy holding or posing for pictures. There is also no special scene for winning the CHAMPIONSHIP! Just the same BS as winning a race. 4. DLC paint schemes are literally the same as the originals, but with an added decal on the rear fenders. 5. 18+ filter is ridiculous. Do they really think taking the beer logos off is making a difference? A difference in what? I don't  get why I have to see "BRAD" on the hood of my favorite drivers car instead of the Miller Lite logo. 6. Career Mode goes nowhere. You don't earn sponsorships and cant have multiple sponsors to create different cars with  different paint schemes. There are no multi-year contracts. Teams are not competing to earn your services as a driver. All the payouts are predetermined. 7. You earn money but don't have anything to spend it on. 8. There is no LIVE roster in the game. None of the drivers retire opening up new potential landing spots for you or other drivers. Jimmie Johnson will just drive forever. No driver firing for poor performance. No studio created drivers to come in and fill those positions. And teams aren't hiring you to drive a certain car. As long as you meet the requirements to join a team, you can join and just kick any driver from their ride and take it as your own. Example: If my dream is to drive the 24 car for Hendrick, I can just kick William Byron out of the car. But then where does he go? He just disappears into thin air. He doesn't change teams or drives another car, Its not like Jimmie Johnson retires, so Hendrick moves Byron to the 48, and then I take over the 24. Nothing. And by the way, despite me driving the 24, everywhere in career mode it still shows Byron's picture AND his name above the door of the car. 9. Create a driver is....you guessed it! LACKING CONTENT!!! About 10 preset fire suits and none of them look like the nice ones they wear in NASCAR. They all look like cheap, amateur fire suits that local short track drivers wear. 10. Your name is NEVER said in game. You're referred to as "DRIVER" by your spotter who in real life probably has a more intimate relationship with you. 11. There is ZERO pre-race ceremonies, driver intros, National anthem, flyovers, NOTHING!12. The skill gap between difficulties is INSANE. Now Im not a great race driver. But the on easy, Im literally blowing by everyone. But on normal and I can barely finish P10-P15 without even a chance to win. List goes on but I'm tired of typing already. Racing fans deserve better. There are too little games out there for us. They need to do better. There is no competition so give us the game we deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, sim-cade at most, more arcade really, but nowhere near as bad as many people make it out to be. At least not now for the 12 euros 50 (or current humble bundle) they are asking for it. Career mode has nice progression and you can choose whether to start in Dirt Late Models, or jump further and start from Trucks (like i did), Xfinity or Cup and either make your own team, or drive for other teams and try getting as best possible results as you can to get better offers, or in the case of being an owner driver, finish as high as possible to earn more cash and please your sponsors to then upgrade your cars.AI is also excellent, first of all having TONS of settings for skill range, starting spread, mechanical failure frequency, recovery skill, etc, they don't drive in a train, take a variety of lanes, block, push, and if they are from a better team with better equipment they absolutely drive the same lines and times as you can, they don't cheat.Devs also finally added the gameplay settings allowing for realistic terminal damage in case of very bad collisions for both the player and the AI. So if you really smash yourself into a wall you get a big fat DNF.Is the game perfect then ? Hell no ! Ultrawide screen support is nice, but no VR, no FoV sliders and no seat position changing really screw up the cockpit view, where even if you can turn the in-game wheel off, the seat is just way too far back and it looks absolutely off, so you have to drive with either of the two hood cameras, or just either of the two chase cameras.Do i recommend the game to fans of Nascar even if the roster is outdated and there are no next-gen cars ? If you want a good career mode and race against excellent AI in a Nascar game on all official tracks, using the top 3 official series for basically dirt cheap, then yes, i recommend the game, because driving 4-wide at Texas is absolutely thrilling !

_childDocuments_.review: From what I have seen, most of the negative reviews for this game are either people that aren't good at racing games, hate nascar, or expected this to be HEAT 4 again or something. This game is great, if you already enjoy racing games and have some skill with them. I couldn't imagine playing this as a newcomer to racing games. Otherwise, I highly recommend this game. No knowledge of nascar is required to enjoy this game, either. I grew up watching it as a kid, but that was several years ago, and I only recognize a few names on the grids now, but it didn't make it any less fun. It gave me a newfound appreciation for the unexpectedly very tricky art of turning left at 150MPH. I know that's everyone's go to joke, but I'm serious. I absolutely love how much you can get out of driving in a circle for 100 laps. No race ever really feels the same. There are some tracks I absolutely dread going to, but that's more of a me problem than a game problem, and I imagine it's the same case for everyone else. It's very satisfying to pull off a really clean pass, or even better, a spin-out on your rival where you come away with just a spot of paint missing. I've had no major problems with the game. There are really only two "issues" I have with the game, but neither of them are any kind of dealbreakers.  I kinda wish they had done something more with the rival/friend system. The fundamentals of it are all there and they work fine, it's just that it feels kind of bare-bones, in a way. The other problem is the qualifying for superspeedways. It just... doesn't work. The goal times in practice and qualifying are unrealistic. I'm assuming the times they use are from when the AI uses the drafting mechanic, which is absolutely necessary at those tracks in order to get a good time, so you're almost always guaranteed to start at the back on those tracks, but if you're like me and play with a high number of laps, if anything it makes it more fun, as you weave your way to the front.In conclusion, this game is great for those who are into the sport and those who aren't, but enjoy racing games nonetheless. at $15, I can safely say I've already gotten my money's worth, and I'm far from finished playing the game. P.S. having my childhood hero, Jeff Gordon, as my spotter, was another level of wish fulfillment that definitely doesn't create any bias towards this game

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play Heat 4 so I'm not going to complain about the lack of new content in 5, instead I'll judge the game in its own right.The driving mechanics are fine, not the most realistic sim by any stretch, but the races are fun and that's what counts. It sits in the middle ground between sim and arcade racer,  à la Forza, Gran Turismo and F1. The set up menus are quite simplistic and don't make a whole difference to the behaviour of the car, but that was presumably to make the game accessible to the more casual sim fans. Again, that's not necessarily a problem, but just be aware that this isn't the most in depth racer.The career mode spans Xtreme, Trucks, Xfinity and Cup Series, and as a nice touch you can start your career in any of those categories instead of being forced to start at the bottom. You can join existing teams or create your own, recruit mechanics, makes friends or rivals with your fellow drivers and amass fans. While it is admittedly more involved than the barebone career modes offered in many other race sims, it still sorely lacks features seen in other sports games. This is definitely a priority for improvement in future instalments. Multiplayer is functional and gets the job done, although you'll often notice player and AI cars rubber-banding which can make overtaking difficult and risky. Not a deal breaker and it's still fun, but can be immersion breaking.On the presentation side of things, the graphics are sub par, looking like a late 360/PS3 game. That doesn't bother me one iota but I know some people would inevitably moan about it so I thought it was worth mentioning.  There's the usual licensed rock soundtrack, though I swear there only seems to be about 4 or 5 songs! For the technical side, I have yet to experience a game crash and I had no problems setting up my G29.Overall, it may feel a little lacking in content and features, but this is a very enjoyable racing game and its flaws can and should be overlooked when you factor in the reasonable price.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good sim racing game. Not iRacing level of sim, but more than most racing titles these days that are much more 'arcade' style. I am not even a NASCAR fan and couldn't name a driver beyond about the 1990's. I got this almost exclusively for the dirt track content. Short track, dirt track and 'grass roots' racing is under represented in games that focus on the highest level of the sport. I am an old school guy that goes to my local 1/4 mile paved oval every saturday to watch people turn left. My father used to race on a dirt oval in the 1950's. So I would love to replicate that kind of racing more than the Daytona 500. I also like the progression system here that actually feels like a 'career'. If you start in the lower series (dirt or trucks) you can earn offers to single rides in the other series, so you will get a chance to drive more than just the vehicle for your current series. There is a rival system that doesn't really seem to matter. AI does get more aggressive if you drive rough but it doesn't seem to carry over from the post race text exchanges. Dirt racing is a lot of fun and despite being the 'beginner' series, is actually the hardest cars to drive by far. Getting the flick into a corner and steering sideways takes practice and is super hard to be consistent lap after lap. The cars look and sound great. This is a real challenge to race cleanly, but some paint trading is to be expected. Moving into the truck series seems like you just hit easy mode. Glorious grip on asphalt. The trucks handle well and are pretty forgiving of minor mistakes and collisions. A good introduction to paved oval. AI seems a bit too aggressive at times like it's using the dirt track AI. But overall the AI doesn't crash or spin out very often. Once you get to the cup cars, difficulty goes back up as they are very easy to spin, lose the back end, and don't react well at all to even the smallest brush against the wall. Sound is good and the cars look great bumper to bumper. AI is solid, mostly clean racing and few rookie mistakes. Played with a wheel it feels good and holding a line is natural and neutral. I did have to tinker with the brake calibration some but other wise set up took no time at all. Online is a mixed bag. Hard to find a full lobby on an older game, and of course it's often a train wreck of idiots. If you find a good lobby though- the racing is spot on and a lot of fun. You can choose to drive for teams or create your own, which brings a new element of team management and car development. It's not complicated and adds an element of role playing to the game. Car set up is detailed enough to satisfy the weekend shade tree mechanic but not overwhelming to the average person. The default set ups do well enough that you can get by with those if you are a good driver. I've had no stability issues or problems with online play. As a sim level racing game- it's pretty good and if you want realism it's better than most newer titles offer. You don't have to be a NASCAR fan to get good racing out of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Much more of a racing simulator than the NFS franchise games or Forza, but not as hardcore of a simulation as iRacing, etc.  Overall it's a really fun game if you're into NASCAR and want that experience and is still leagues better overall than the dumpster fire that is NASCAR 21 Ignition.Career mode is solid and progressing through the different series as your custom driver is fun and satisfactory.   Outside of competing on the track you can customize the look of both your driver and car, but nothing else in terms of character depth or immersion.  A little more of that would have gone a long way in taking career mode from good to great.Driving mechanics-wise the game is solid.  No glaring holes to speak of, but do expect a learning curve to be able to get around the track if you're coming from playing arcade racers.  There is a plethora of driving aids to help you if you need it or turn them all off for a nice realistic challenge.The AI is very good in my opinion, but not perfect.  They provide a nice challenge to race against from track to track once you tweak all the settings to fit your liking and skill level.  My only real complaint about them is that they all feel the same to race against.  Would be nice if they had perceivable driver traits on the track instead of just being clones of each other with different skill levels per track based on the quality of their ride.  Overall though they provide a more than adequate and quality opponent for you to race against.I wouldn't recommend springing for all the DLC, as most of it's outdated now and there are mods that have updated drivers, cars, and schedules available to download for free that do a better job of all that.If you're a NASCAR fan it's still the best game for that experience available and will definitely give you a quality fix.  If you're just looking for a racing game you'll find the game fun, but most likely wish there was more to do or experience outside of just racing and progressing through your career from track to track and series to series.I think a 7/10 is a fair rating.  It's a pretty good, but not great game.  Racing experience is solid and fun, but don't expect much else in terms of gameplay depth beyond that.  If you're a fan of NASCAR it's still definitely worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. The car's physics. The physics in this game are perfect for a simcade oval racing experience. 2. Variety. This game has 39 tracks across 4 different series. This allows you to race in a ton of different ways.3. Fun. The gameplay is just plain fun.1. The car's physics (again?). Earlier I put the car's physics in the good category; however, that only applies to the racing on ovals. The road course racing in this game is not very fun. The car just doesn't feel as fun to drive on road courses as it did in past NASCAR games.2. No 35% race length. In my opinion, 35% is the best race distance because there is time for strategy, there's time for intense battles, and there's time for some chaos; however, 35% is not so long that you get bored. 1. Pit road is a nightmare. Imagine you have had a good race so far. You are running in 5th place and you are close to the leaders. You see one of the leaders get loose and spin out which causes a big wreck. You don't know where to go so you make the split-second decision to go low to avoid the wreck. This seems like a good idea, but the entrance to the pits is there and the game decides that you are now pitting and there is no way for you to change that. This same exact scenario has happened to me several times and it's pretty annoying.2. Cars that were in a caution-causing wreck get to keep their positions. This is the one that annoys me the most. Some guy will be on his roof and the game will be like "well he was in 5th place when the caution happened so he gets to restart in 5th place" even though he was literally upside down.This game is fun, but with all of its flaws, I just can't recommend it. If you want a good NASCAR game, then there are plenty of better game on the market, such as, NR2003, NASCAR Thunder 2004, iRacing, and many more. If you want a fun NASCAR game, then just play one of those.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: "You see, the track's an oval so we'll be going straight then turning to the left" - Eric CartmanAs a European F1 fan I thought I'd give the game a go when it was on sale and I've been having a blast. Car handling is accessible and the difficulty options allow for some fine tuning while you learn. If it isnt realistic enough for you, it is still a good stepping stone to figuring out ovals. The AI is quite good, it will fight the player but wont pull too many dumb moves, when it does they feel like "realistic dumb" moves you might see from an actual driver. Career mode could be more than it is but is pretty fun; you can work your way up from the dirt series, start in the top tier (NASCAR Cup series) or anywhere in between. Though beware if you start in cup you'll be with a back marker team for the first season. Alternatively there's championship mode, where you can drive whatever you want. Another fun part of career mode is starting your own team as an owner-driver, you hire team members and pay for their training (a better trained team results in a better car) while also managing multiple cars' wear and upgrades (there are different cars for each type of track). This keeps career fresh once you have won everything as a driver. Overall I'd say this is a great game for the money, I payed a tenth of what I did for F1 2021 and have more hours on record, big thumbs up from me!

_childDocuments_.review: This is only the third NASCAR game I've owned apart from NASCAR Thunder on PS2 and NASCAR: The Game 2013 from here on Steam. The game requires a controller or wheel in order to properly play it, and while I have both a controller and a Logitech racing wheel, i don't like being forced to have to use them if I don't want too, because there was once a time where I also only had a keyboard/mouse. That aside, the game is fun but there are a few quirks to me that I feel I should add to this review. PROS:- The graphics look good and the game runs good on my PC (1070ti, i5)- The sounds are good quality.- The cars look nice (I can't speak for the people having DLC issues, I don't have any)- The tracks seem to be faithfully recreated.- A variety of different series to keep you entertained such as dirt track, truck series, xfinity, etc.CONS:- The handling and force feedback can be a little finicky and tedious, I've figured it out and can deal with it but I can see how this could be a pain. The steering can be a bit strange and if you don't know the technical stuff when it comes to car set up (such as myself) , it can be difficult to set your car up to where it handles decent. And there seems to be a pretty sharp learning curve when it comes to dirt racing and truck racing, as it is easier to lose control of your vehicle.- There doesn't seem to be much of an inbetween when it comes to the career and single races (talking mostly about cup series). If you just pick a car of a regular driver, you're automatically the fastest car out there and can dominate by a large margin given you know the track, but contrariwise if you're starting out in career mode you seem to always be last and don't have  a car that can compete. Take this with a grain of salt though and experience it for yourself, it could just be me. _childDocuments_.review: Steam ReviewSome quick initial positives and negativesPositives: - The AI is improved a good amount from Heat 4, I ran a Kansas race in both games back to back and it was easy to see the difference. It may not be a huge step up from Heat 4, but it is still better, whether that's enough to justify a purchase is up to the consumer to decide.

_childDocuments_.review: This won't be a surprise to those of you paying attention, but Nascar Heat 5 is a resounding success for developer 704 Games. The racing minds at 704 Games have developed another racing game that walks the fine line between uncompromising accuracy and a fervent rush to the checkered flag. If you lean more towards a gradual simulation, you'll find pretty much what you're looking for here. On the other hand, if you favor more arcade-style gameplay similar to Need for speed, this one will definitely hold your interest.Those who have played the previous games in the series, like Nascar Heat 4 for example, will be familiar with what this title has to offer. Aside from a few enhancements to the 3D engine, there really isn't much new here. The Options remain very similar to what has been offered in previous games. You can take part in single-player races, choose to race in Championship mode or go at it in a full Nascar season. Of course, if the AI isn't to your liking, you can take your skills online and race against the best drivers around. A total of 24+ tracks are included, including Atlanta Motor Speedway, Watkins Glenn, and the famed speedway of Daytona. Add to that all the top Nascar drivers and you got a complete Nascar game right in front of you.While all the options and features have a lot of depth, the customizable game design was created to be friendly to newbies and veterans alike. Turn the driving aids down a few notches and the game switches to a full arcade fun. Turn it up, and you'll be in awe of how complex a stock car can be. This flexibility is perhaps one of the best things that Nascar Heat offers. While other racing simulators try to overwhelm the player with their depth right from the get-go, this one acclimates players in slowly. This is thanks to both the simple design and easy adaptability of the game.From a graphical standpoint, Nascar Heat 5 is just slightly above average in terms of visuals and presentation. Graphics are crisp, yet oddly undistinguishable. Part of this probably has to do with the subject matter because aside from the colorful and detailed cars, how much more vibrant can a big grey race track become? The pit crew on the other hand are very well done and animate very life-like. It's too bad we can't see more of this type of animation around the track. Sound is serviceable and spotters do a good job of helping you navigate through a crowded field. Personally, I never listen to my spotters and just tune them out when racing.Despite these shortcomings, Nascar Heat 5 is a worthy purchase for any serious or casual racing fan. I couldn't ask for anything more than this invigorating mix of a thinking man's sim and an arcade fan's thrill ride. It has enough new features to justify the purchase, but just don't expect a brand new overhaul of a game especially if you still play Nascar Heat 4. Of course, this probably says more good things about the former title than bad things about the current one. Regardless, you definitely should have both installed on your PC. They are that good.Nascar Heat 5 is perhaps the best Heat game of the franchise. If you're a casual or serious racing fan, you definitely need to try this one out!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT Sept. 8th 2020 :Now that most of the bugs have been fixed and all the features work as advertised (including DNFs and Custom Season Mode), I would still not recommend buying it for full retail price, since NH4 comes very close to it feature-wise for a fraction of the cost.However, once this goes on a sale (30 bucks or less) later this year, it is definitely worth a shot!It's a solid 7.5/10 (September 2020) and quite playable in its current form!This is also going to be my final update on NH5, but I highly doubt that they'll spend any more time on NH5 anyhow, now that we're approaching the Next-Gen Console launch with the upcoming NASCAR Heat game already on the horizon.Oh and hey 704.... just release a finished and well tested product next time, to avoid all the hassle and stress with your Community, how does that sound?Original Review prior to all the fixes (no longer relevant or true) :Sorry 704, but this is unacceptable.First off let me begin by saying, that I'm well aware of the fact, that the old "Monster Games" studio doesn't exist anymore and a new studio "Motorsport Games" is now in charge of the NASCAR Heat series.Also yes, they have indeed mentioned, that NH5 is going to be pretty much a rehash of NH4, with a couple of added extra features as a bonus.But as it sits right now, the game is pretty much broken, lacks certain promised features and in general quite a bit of polish.DNFs are a great example and one of the only reasons I wanted to get Heat 5 for in the first place - they announced this "big new feature" of "Player DNFs" being in the game, although just weeks before the official release, they did away with that Bulletpoint on there website, so it was nowhere to be found.On their public Discord Servers the Devs were still publicly mentioning DNFs, however all of the sudden it is now supposed to be a Career Mode only feature, which disappointed me quite a bit and could be considered false advertising.The first time I played it though... this entire deal got even worse.I can 100% positively say, that there are literally no DNFs in this game.They seem to be scripted in very badly and work only under specific circumstances - namely when you overrev your engine like an idiot in first gear for 20+ seconds... else I could not get myself to crash out, no matter how hard I tried to hit the wall at 180+ mph.Also there are BUGS... lots and lots of BUGS...Simply put, for a quick rehash, this performance is borderline criminal.They didn't add much besides a Test Session Mode, Custom Championship Schedules, new 2020 Paint Schemes and supposedly a DNF system that just won't work, so how on earth could they have screwed this game up even worse than its predecessor?!It still runs rough, there are the typical audio issues known from Heat 4 that were never patched, also old bugs and even typos remain in the game completely unchanged + new bugs made it into here as well.Sorry guys, but this is a big NO NO!Especially asking full retail price!This could have easily been a patch or DLC for NH4, which I'm willing to bet most people would have preferred anyhow, even if it was priced at around 15-20 bucks.For now I can only tell everyone out there, no matter how big of a NASCAR fan you are, stay far away!If you really want something new-ish, go take a look at NH4.It was on sale recently and you can get it on key-reseller  sites for less than 6 bucks.Else there's still NR2003 Season with dozens of free mods - unbeaten to this day.This game gets a 4/10 from me as it stands. (July 2020)In case they patch all the problems out, I will edit this review accordingly, but I wouldn't hold my breath for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I feel it is a lot of fun in terms of recreating the feel of Nascar racing. I enjoy the racing strategy and the career progression. I like the way you can build up rivalries by bumping drivers or insulting them etc that's great, although it is too easy to make it all ok by apologising afterwards lol!I started playing at 98% in the one off races, with no assists at all, at expert driving difficulty and I had a decent challenge. I tried 105% (max AI level) but that was too high.The AI is fairly sensible it has to be said, they try to win but they don't ram you, they try to avoid crashes but they still race aggressively. They do make some mistakes and skid off which is nice to see. Pit stops seem to fix everything and any sort of damage, no matter how bad, in a matter of seconds. Damage types could do with being improved, at the moment there only seems to be aero damage, engine blow ups and burst tyres, all fixable in seconds it seems lol.Regarding wheel control I did get my GT Driving Force wheel mapped ok and wheel use is better than the last game as this game allows a full 900 degrees of rotation. You will need to set the same rotation in your wheel settings in Windows. The wheel control on road courses feels rather lacklustre and the brakes are very sensitive. Some road courses are fun, like Watkins Glen, but some are a nightmare, like Sonoma. Don't know if this is realistic but Sonoma is a nightmare to drive on in Project Cars 2 as well.Little sense of force feedback, no track undulations or bumps, little feeling of travelling at speed. You can feel the grass, some track margins, and the gravity on the corners. I would have liked more feeling of driving on varying track grades. The car moves loads in cockpit mode but those movements aren't translated into FF for the wheel unfortunately, PCars 2 has a much better driving feel.Sound is ok you can hear the wind 'draft' when you are behind a car, that's quite useful. Skidding is very quiet so you can't judge when you are nearing the limit of your grip very well.Not much has changed from Heat 4 I would not recommend buying this if you already own that game, unless you are a Nascar fanatic and must have the latest game. There are improvements in this game over that one but they are quite minor - AI driving ability, stats, private testing, slight graphics improvements (not noticeable). The best one is being able to choose you own tracks for a Custom Championship so you can just do all Speedways if you want to. I like that the racing is done in stages so if you drive badly in one you can still recover in another especially if you time your pit-stop well.Its frustrating there is no ability to save in between sessions. So you have to practice, qualify (2 stages), and race all three stages in one sitting. That is possible on 25% race length but it would be nice to practice and qualify one day and then do a long 50% or full length race the next day. No way to do that presently.Regarding bugs I haven't experienced any.I started off enjoying the speedways but actually I really enjoy the short circuits now the best, they are challenging trying to get past the AI cars without being too aggressive and getting a bad name for yourself. But the speedways are also great fun. Some of the road courses are ok, I hate Sonoma though that is just uncontrollably bad. But the rest of the tracks are challenging and fun in different ways. The short ovals are very intense scraps whereas the long speedways are all about pack position and retaining speed, and some of the speedways result in split up cars other have one large pack you have to stay with to retain speed. Interesting representation of Nascar and makes you appreciate the skill required.So overall, this a good fun recreation of Nascar racing I think. I am having a lot of enjoyment with this game. There are little issues and things that could do with improving to make it a better game, but generally I think its very good.

_childDocuments_.review: NASCAR Heat 5 is a console ported track racing game, licensed from, yes, you guessed it, American NASCAR. The console port is deplorably bad here, and it seems the developers set out deliberately to offend PC gamers (it's inconceivable that anyone could be incompetent enough for ineptitude to be the explanation for this mess).  They deliberately locked out keyboard support, demanding the game must be played with a console peasant children's toy gamepad (but you may be able to use a racing wheel... under some circumstances).  See, the developers did such a hamfisted effort on the control schemes that the keyboard is disabled even in the menus.  If your game controller doesn't precisely fit their expectations, you can't even browse into the settings menu. Assuming you are able to play the game with the controllers they require you to use, instead of having freedom to choose your own control scheme, you'll find a game that was made in 2020 but looks like it was made in 2010, and plays worse. Once more, consoles, and console devs, have made gaming worse for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: "NASCAR Heat 5" delivers a heart-pounding racing experience that's sure to thrill fans of the sport. As an avid gamer and racing enthusiast, diving into this latest installment was a treat. The game offers a robust selection of modes, including Career, Championship, and Quick Race, providing ample opportunities to test your skills on the track.One of the standout features is the Career mode, where you create your driver and work your way up from the grassroots of the sport to become a NASCAR legend. The progression feels satisfying, with each race offering a chance to earn experience points, upgrade your vehicle, and attract sponsorships. It's a compelling journey that keeps you coming back for more.The gameplay itself is where "NASCAR Heat 5" truly shines. The controls are responsive, allowing for precise maneuvering around tight corners and daring passes on straightaways. The sensation of speed is exhilarating, especially when drafting behind opponents or making a daring last-lap move for the win. The AI drivers provide a decent challenge, with varying levels of aggression and skill, ensuring that every race feels competitive.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a NASCAR game, you go fast and turn left a lot. Like all you do is go fast and turn left. Then pay some employees who mostly tell you what to do and then you go fast and turn left more. Did I mention that you are supposed to both go fast and turn left? There are a few road courses in the game but I don't know how to turn right so I'm bad at them.All jokes aside if you enjoy the genre of American oval and stock car racing this does scratch that itch. The racing physics blend arcade with enough real world basis that its enjoyable without being incredibly challenging. The career mode is lackluster at best with the sponsor missions becoming repetitive and very easy to achieve once you get into a decent team or have your own well developed team. Speaking on teams and building one my largest gripe is that after you own a team in a series you must run that series every single year and it simply doesn't work that way in real life. Some days I don't want to run 10 events for my race week between practice and actual races. You should be able to opt out of some series events as the game progresses to avoid it becoming overwhelming. The repetitive nature aside the game does provide a somewhat authentic oval racing experience with an acceptable AI allowing for a good level of challenge combined with a decent track selection. These days though I think NASCAR games are hard pressed to stand on their own when they can easily be integrated into other things like i Racing, and Forza Motorsport.  That being said if you want a stand alone game with several divisions of NASCAR racing available on most of the popular real world tracks, this ill do it for you just don't expect anything groundbreaking or innovative as its simply go fast turn left and pay the suspension guy.

_childDocuments_.review: **Pros:**1. **Authentic NASCAR Experience:** The game faithfully captures the essence of NASCAR racing, with realistic car physics and track details.2. **Deep Career Mode:** Immerse yourself in a comprehensive career mode with team management aspects, adding layers of strategy and progression.3. **Diverse Racing Options:** Multiple series, tracks, and race types provide variety, catering to both casual and hardcore racing fans.**Cons:**1. **Graphical Limitations:** While satisfactory, the graphics might not match the visual standards set by some other contemporary racing titles.2. **AI Behavior:** The artificial intelligence of opponents could be more refined, occasionally leading to questionable race incidents.3. **Limited Innovation:** NASCAR Heat 5 doesn't introduce groundbreaking features, relying on a formula that might feel familiar to players of previous iterations.In the end, NASCAR Heat 5 delivers an authentic NASCAR experience, especially appealing to fans of the sport. However, it falls short in terms of graphical innovation and AI refinement, making it more of an incremental upgrade for series enthusiasts than a groundbreaking installment.

At the lowest settings, it will probably run on a lower-class computer without any major problems. Great optimization, low hardware requirements and little space taken up on the hard drive.The sound design is phenomenal, as is the music in the game. Perfect music sounds for fast driving.Gameplay-wise... oh my god. The control system, physics, support settings, AI settings, AI driver work... everything is fantastic, giving you the full immersion of being a NASCAR driver.The career mode is also fantastic and you'd be hard pressed to find one like it in other, more complex racing games. Unfortunately.Really great job at Nascar.There are only 3 elements of the game that irritate me, although they are only cosmetic and completely subjective...The first is the lack of customization of the logo and name of your own team. _childDocuments_.review: I was very reluctant to have this game at all, because I've read some pretty negative reviews about it online, as well as seeing some pretty negative videos made about the game on various social media Platforms. HOWEVER, the game was gifted to me and I decided to give it a shot. So, here is my assessment:Pro's----------------- The game is an arcade racer. Meaning people that have never played a racing game before can pick this game up and have an absolute great time.- The Dirt series in the game is some of the funnest racing I've ever done in an arcade racing game.- The Online Multiplayer is filled with talented drivers that can give you the challenge you are looking for if you are looking for something harder than the AI races.- The Car Customization screen is very robust and easy to understand. Plus with it's simplicity and the way it works, other people in multiplayer races can see your custom paints.- The Career mode is very in depth, and has enough going on that you won't get bored with it easily. I'm currently 25 hours into the game and I just got into the hot seat position in the Xfinity series. Cons------------ The AI are way too easy. Once you get involved with a good team in Career mode, create a team with good engine technicians the AI opponents are VERY easy to beat on the highest difficulty. - There are driving assists (I won't go into detail about which ones) that veteran racing game players can take advantage of to give them a SEVERE advantage on short tracks. The reason this is listed as a con is that it can be abused in multiplayer lobbies, and it is. - The multiplayer lobbies are on a timer system, meaning you can't just start the race whenever you want. You have to wait for that timer to go to 0 and then it launches the race automatically. Just remove this feature entirely and add a damn button that says "Start Race." It really is that easy. - No ability to create custom paintjobs externally and upload and/or add them to the game files (even if I am the only person that can see it) without modding the game.Overall my experience with this game so far has been positive in majority. The game is easy to grasp, is a good way to waste some time if you just want a game you can chill and play when you're taking a break from other games, and it's an absolute blast to play with friends.overall 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Used to be good, however I haven't had a problem with DLC like others, I only have one DLC though. There are a lot of AI glitches, however not as bad as ignition 21. The game didn't always have AI problems like it does now. It only is a problem though in an online lobby where the AI is operating on a distant machine only. The game doesn't handle communicating the AI's position well across internet. There are times during multiplayer where the field can be going 200 mph and suddenly drop to 100 or 50 mph as a result of miscommunication between computers. There is also an issue where you can get stuck on yellow permanently for the entire race with other players being on green. Again, all these problems are related to online play. If you ask me to many entities are being transmitted across the internet which is causing problems. I would imagine this is an easy fix but something the developers are unwilling to do; which is decrease the loaded graphics and resolution for all players. the physics may also need simplified or just calculated in a way the requires fewer steps. That's just my thought though, but given the state of this developer, I would rather see a new game by a different developer.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, whilst playing the game, it handles exceptionally well in terms of performance for my low-end gaming laptop, you can have some variety in your races with A.I like changing how many number of cars you want on the track or something. _childDocuments_.review: I'd say this ones a great example for the neutral or a maybe rating. You can make your own character, car designs, theres the challenge series.Now my issues with the game, coming from someone who still plays Nascar Thunder 2003 and Nascar 2005 Chase for the Cup, this ones the closest you'll get to them. BUT its missing a few features that keep it in the "Maybe" section for me. The Hero/Villain system is gone [saddly, I loved that feat], Yellow Flag replays are gone, you can still make rivals but they feel souless. Where they'd actually race you harder and make effort to mess you up at times in 03 and 05, they more or less just s***talk you on twitter here [Fitting, right?]. IMO, the game just misses its soul, its personality. It feels bland, theres very few sponsors for the cars, the racers just feel like straight bots, not AI. But then again, compared to other Modern Nascar games, this is best your gonna find. I recommend picking it up on a heavy sale, over 50% off. Otherwise, save your money, get your fam something nice or buy yourself a nice meal.

_childDocuments_.review: Who the ♥♥♥♥ followed a Unity 5.6.1 tutorial to make a simulation game?I'm not kidding- Heat 5's an itch.io project with this magnificent binary code toggling everything between Stick or Slick. Braking fails completely at the slightest of a turn...just sometimes(???), and if you roll some bad RNG, you'll magically spin out, in complete ignorance of your tire wear....But yet, the AI is railed to the track like they're  Slot Cars. They never slip, brake perfectly fine, and feel like a brick. Its almost impossible to push your way to the inside, or spin out the a-hole in front of you. Oh but, anything's a walk in the park for them. Everybody on the track has plot armor except you. AI also really, really sucks at actually racing, even on the Ovals. Incredibly easy to pass when you're on the inside.704Games also deleted Downforce from their C# spaghetti.Yeah, I understand barreling it down a track with slicks makes your car very feeble to flipping out if your terrain changes. But unless a Stock Car is somehow featherweight, if you throttle from 30mph at the top of a 10 degree hill and attempt a hard left, there's somehow enough power in the rear to 90-spin this 2 ton car. Hoonigans have more grip....Yet the AI turns like this without any amount of slippage. Try the Michigan Track....Good luck.Also relying on Difficulty Assists is NEEDED to remedy this game's physics. Screw that, just play Assetto or something. There's genuinely no reason to buy this....This makes me hate NASCAR. If this game is truly a "simulator" then Stock Cars are trash.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much the best "casual" NASCAR game you can get from recent years. It's fun and has a few different modes, including the career mode, which although is similar to that in previous Heat games, it does offer the dirt series which is a lot of fun. I've played the game with both a controller and force feedback wheel and both are supported quite well. The handling of the cars is not completely accurate and realistic, but this is also more of an arcade-style game so that is to be expected. The AI simulation is quite good. They put up a good challenge (unlike the ignition AI which I have heard are incredibly flawed) and have good spatial awareness (unlike the NASCAR '15 AI which I have experienced myself, who will mindlessly run you off of the track.) All that being said, I am really disappointed that we will not be getting the Next-Gen car for this game. It would have been great to run the current seasons in Heat, but looks like we're stuck with Motorsport games for now.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game very much, but it's drawbacks make it difficult to hold my interest. The cars are great and have a fair amount of tuning range, as well as customization when creating your own vehicle.They feel very natural to drive and do what you expect.The damage models aren't incredible, but this is one of those games where damage isn't really a focal point.The graphics are very good. I wouldn't say you lose touch with reality, but you do feel like you are there, and that's a huge plus.The HUD in the vehicle is very clear and simple.The menu UIs are also pretty decent, and are straightforward, easy to use.The multiplayer is limited to a certain number of cars, causing multiplayer races (especially long ones) feel very empty. The multiplayer also feels slightly laggy. Most games, this isn't a huge deal, but if two players are trying to bump-draft, it can become a chaotic mess very quickly.In single player the AI difficulty is very unbalanced. I play on hard, and on some tracks I cannot keep up, it feels like my car is genuinely slower, and on other tracks I can go from dead last to first in a very unrealistic amount of time. The drafting also feels very off. The AI can barely handle a slight tap and almost lose control constantly. The biggest problem is that when the game decides the car in front of you is a "draft partner", they attempt to stay directly in your trajectory. This is great on the straights, but on the turns they tend to position themselves as if you were going straight, making it extremely difficult to center your bumper on theirs.The last thing that really got me was the lack of ability to save mid-race. I enjoy the satisfaction of completing a race at full length, but life happens, and sometimes you just need to save and come back later, but that is not an option here. That alone is the difference between me giving a positive rating.This game clearly states that it is incompatible with keyboard/mouse, but that is not the case. You can do it, but you'll have to figure out the controls yourself, the ones on the UI do not change.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to recommend this game.I picked the game up for $5 and it is worth that, so I will review it as a $5 game.I only play career mode in these games, so this review will not mention multiplayer, so I have no idea how the multiplayer performs.That being said, the career mode is fun for awhile, but it's a Nascar game so it does get repetitive.The pros:Game runs smooth4 different race series (Dirt, Truck, Xfinity, and Cup)Decent graphicsThe cons:Lacks personality of its own, victory lane is dull, and the other drivers will send you tweets on how you did or events, but they are repetitive after you see 5 of them.Same with victory lane, when you win a championship it's the same celebration as if you won a normal race. In games like Madden for example, there's a big celebration at the end. This game doesn't even have that.There is always a clear winner every race, with the exception of Super Speedways or Short Tracks. Which the most common tracks are Speedways. Speedways there is always one dominant car, the rest can't keep up. which makes the races dull. I personally don't play long hulled races, my races are short and sweet. But the lack of toe to toe racing and every race makes the racing part boring. The only fun tracks I've experienced was Dega and Daytona (super speedways) where every race is a nail biter. I'd say if they decide to make another game, they really need to step up there game with giving the career mode more personality. There is effort there with the tweets, but it's just not enough. Where's the end of race interviews? Where's a real victory lane? Why can't I do a burn out and drive into victory lane myself? Why can't I pick a reply to a tweet instead of 2 choices, be nice or be a douche, and you can't even see what the comment is.I do recommend the game, but only if you can pick it up for under $10. Fairly dull after the first 15hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Well..... it's been about a year almost since I've taken up sim racing.   I graduated from xbox PC Game Pad to a Fanatec GT-DD Pro with V3 Pedals and the V2.5 RIM with an added Podium paddle system I put on myself.    The way I see it if I'm gonna hot lap and feel a need for speed why not invest in something of realistic quality to make the sim enjoyable.   I mainly mess with EA F121 and 22.  I really enjoy KAOS's IR18 Mod.    I also signed up for iracing to test drive the IR18 but right after I did this it then became restricted, plus I don't like the concept of renting a game, and not having a leg to stand on in any situation according to their EULA.   Now.... NASCAR Heat 5?!   Months ago I dabbled with it using a game pad.  So I decided to see if I could load this up again from my library and see how it handles.  Right off the bat my TrackIRv5 doesn't work with it. I guess it doesn't support VR. I like using my head tracker in F1 and Indy, or GT in ACC, but I guess not in Heat 5.    Without setting up the car at all or doing anything I just wanted to take it for a test drive..... I prefer cockpit view.  So I'm testing this car out, I can't even remember who's car it was, I just wanted to take the game for a feel.   Nice feedback.  No Head tracking......  Driving full speed was super easy on the Daytona track, I achieved pole position with no effort in Expert mode, no assists.   That felt arcade fake.    Seemed like a false sense of accomplishment.   So then I qualify and place 1st pole position, bear in mind I've done nothing to the car's set up.   So then I race and during an early part of the race one car tried to get by me on my left side. He fell behind.   Full speed ahead by the third lap the whole pack behind me was nowhere in sight.      I won.   Just seems strange.  Fake.   Did my burn out and then uninstalled it back into the library.     Honestly.... I'm thinking the sim wants  my pedals to be connected to my GT-DD unit.     So I uninstalled it.This is supposed to be a Heat 5 review , I know, but it's all relative and from the same company related at that.   Back to my  Indy and F1 I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played many more hours of Heat 4 on PS4. Heat 5 is virtually the same with a few small additions.It's not great, but you can do far worse when it comes to a NASCAR game. I think this is still good enough that even someone who isn't necessarily a NASCAR fan will find enjoyment in this. The racing itself is good and the AI is competent enough. The AI can even bring out the caution on their own via spin out or a blown tire. I do appreciate the NASCAR Thunder 2004-esque friends and rivals mechanic where making enemies with drivers will force you to deal with some retaliation from said enemies. The career mode is very in depth, offering similar progression as the old Dirt to Daytona game, allowing you to start out on dirt and work your way up through the leagues.There's lots of customization here to tailor the game to your preferences whether you want a more arcade experience or a more realistic one. There's even a setting to adjust how much contact effects your car and the AI cars. That said, the physics are pretty good, for the most part. On a more realistic setup, a small little love tap in the corners can get a car loose and potentially spin out and next thing you know, you just caused the big one at Daytona. However, the game doesn't seem to always handle heavy contact and rollovers very well. Blowovers looks cool until the car lands, going into a very odd and cartoonish flip most times.All in all, the game is currently worth its $15 price tag and the only other NASCAR games worth your time are going to be from more than a decade ago.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am rather enjoying this game. Racing itself reminds me a good bit of Forza Horizon's racing systems albeit maybe a bit more tight handling compared to the former. Got a sudden itch to play Nascar games because I remember playing Nascar Thunder 2003 as a kid, and this really satisfies that itch I'd say. Career mode so far hasn't been super in-depth and it's very easy. I personally would've preferred if the game didn't let you keep restarting during qualifying so you could always get a good time, and restart during races to position better, but that's how the game works, and most games nowadays have very lenient difficulty so it's not that big of a deal. Not to mention the difficulty options themselves can make for some challenging gameplay if you wanted, so I imagine the qualifying stuff wouldn't be much use in that circumstance.The micromanaging aspect of it is kinda limited in terms of enhancing your car. Seems like coming up with a rhythm to constantly getting your cars in top shape before races is not hard at all, but the tuning is pretty in-depth, and is a bit too overwhelming for me at the moment, so that's nice to see. Overall it's a pretty nice game. A bit more simulation-esque compared to some of the other racing games I am used to. I quite enjoy it.Expect a much better review when I play this more.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I have really enjoyed this game. It is definitely rough around the edges (there are literally spelling mistakes in the menus) but overall I think it is worth the money. It has a decent career mode and good customization. Some criticisms I have are,1. You can't play as a girl. You will race against girls who are real drivers in the series you are racing in, but there is no option to be one. I mean, come on, it's 2020.2. The reputation system (how other drivers like or dislike you) is very lazy and easy to manipulate. It really requires a professional level suspension of disbelief to feel like you are racing against real opponents.3. I run a 2080ti, 3950x, 64gb of ram, and I still have to set the settings to low to not have a frame rate nightmare. Doesn't make the game less fun to do so, but it does make it less pretty. If I were to suggest anything to be changed/added it would be adding an actual paint booth for the customization of the Custom Car with options to add any sponsor, not just the ones in the current menu, and design a car with plenty of shapes and other stickers to make a unique car, also I would add the ability to field a second (third, and fourth) car in career mode.
