_childDocuments_.review: The Pale BeyondAn outstanding, semi-linear narrative-focused game that suffers from a few annoying, consistent bugs.I wholesale recommend this to anyone who doesn't mind doing a lot of reading. This isn't an action game in the slightest, it's all menu management. Frostpunk-esque in a lot of ways. There isn't any voice acting beyond the few times shanties are sung. Yet, despite that, it's possibly one of the best game narratives with a strong ensemble of incredibly well-written and developed characters.The visuals are done in a hand-drawn style, and it always looks great, no matter what the situation is. I legitimately have no complaints about it- it's phenomenal.Aside from the lack of voice-acting, the sound design itself is amazing. Ambient music, occasional shanties, the sound of the cold and wind, it's all there, and it's all masterfully-used.You play as First Mate Shaw, hired onto the exploration ship Temperance by Captain Hunt, searching for the remains of the first ship that was sent, the Viscount. You'll deal with everything from stowaways, to rationing, to brawls and agitation, threats of mutiny, and managing your ever-dwindling set of supplies and rations as you strive to survive your ship getting wrecked in a frozen wasteland with rescue almost a year away, and maybe even achieve your original goal of finding the Viscount- if you're lucky.The gameplay is simple. You will have a map, and from which you will choose to divert crew to certain tasks. Hauling coal to the boiler, going on hunts across the ice, resting in the medical bay, repairing damage, working the boiler, along with resolving any potential personal requests your crew come to you with, and so on. Simple, but the game does a good job of forcing you to carefully stretch and manage your limited supply, and it makes it all that much more intense and more nail-biting as the game progresses.While technically you have a large crew of 29, about 9~ of which are largely going to be the focus. The rest are more-or-less background NPCs that occasionally chime in, though they're all still largely standouts, and many of them go through their own arcs that you can peer into from time to time. However, the main nine are far, far more fleshed out, well-developed, and you're able to interact with far more often. And they're all very, very strong characters in their own way. Saying any more would practically spoil the game.The game does suffer from a small handful of bugs, though. Sometime, when you go to distribute your resource cards to the heater-boiler or soup pot, you'll find that stacks will just... Sometimes disappear? Closing and reopening the menu resolves this, thankfully. I haven't had resources inexplicably completely vanish without a trace on me. But it's annoying to deal with, especially once you get into the 'rhythm' of how the game is played, and you don't really need to sit and think on how many resources to spend and where. Some of the dialogue menu options also are weirdly-placed, particularly ones toward the end, one in particular where the bottom line was half-clipped into the edge of the screen, even though there was plenty of room above that option for it to go. That being said, you could still read it and understand it.A solid recommend for anyone looking for an amazing narrative in a fresh setting, with excellent visuals, and excellent sound design.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is a challenging survival game with great character development. There are a few annoying bugs, but I didn't encounter any that were game breaking. The story takes a genuinely weird turn that I didn't expect, but it was done well, so I have no complaints about that.I don't feel like it has the replayability it is going for just because there is so much dialogue to sit through and no easy way to skip it. I may come back and try to finish the remaining achievements later, but I don't have the patience right now. I still feel like it's worth the price, because one playthrough takes about 12 hours.One piece of advice, though. If you are a dog lover, proceed with caution. Yes, you can pet the dogs. However, This was almost a deal breaker for me recommending the game, to be honest, but its strengths made that devastating emotional blow worth it. And actually, if that's not the highest praise I could give this game, I'm not sure what is.

_childDocuments_.review: Not just for people who got obsessed with AMC's "The Terror" or the Dan Simmons book it was adapted from, but it helps. It's more of a mish-mash of things that happened to lots of real polar expeditions, but the influence of the Franklin Expedition is pretty strong. Some UI bugs and occasional editing slip-ups do not detract from what is probably one of the best survival management games I've ever played. TPB has a great atmosphere, particularly from the music and sound effects, and the artwork is beautifully done. The writers know when to vary the mood (there are some genuinely funny bits among all the grim foreboding tension) without there ever being a jarring change in tone, and this game has the two most important things: A setting you can believe in, and characters you can care about. It also has cute dogs you can pet, so something for everyone there. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best resource management games out there backed by an entourage of strong characters, beautiful and bleak art, good music and great general sound design. It gave me a similar frozen-survival feeling to Frostpunk whilst being set in a setting I hadn't quite seen before in a game.My only disappointment is that The Pale Beyond is surprisingly forgiving for a game focused on survival and once you've established a good balance between afflictions and resource gathering, you don't really need to worry about food or fuel through the whole game. The choices themselves weren't too difficult to make and almost all sacrifices could be avoided if you played your cards right, which is rewarding if you've got yourself into a good resource management loop, but took away from the tension on the narrative side. The best part was how well paced it was, with very few weeks feeling empty and always something happening with enough to leave me itching for more.The game overall felt quite polished but a few glitches/bugs/QoL issues that stood out were:- Sometimes I could click on an option before it had appeared on the screen while advancing text, some of which used up valuable resources.- If there were announcements, it would block me from selecting the next dialogue option- If there were announcement and try to assign crew to a task, the display for crew members won't show up- Text could often advance quite slowly or there were built-in delays between one dialogue line and the next, slowing things down- Zooming was the scroll wheel was agonisingly slow, even on the fastest settingOverall I'd give it an 8/10 and if there's a sequel, I'd buy it in an instant!

_childDocuments_.review: "Every decision matters and the ice doesn’t care."TL;DR: I fully recommend this game to anyone who likes narrative-focused games, and anyone who is interested in the general premise. Survival gameplay isn't amazing but the story and presentation carry everything and make even the more mundane choices super compelling. Choices matter and attention is rewarded. Buggy in its current state but totally playable and still receiving active updates. Some of the best €20 I've ever spent on Steam.----------Full review/ramble (I just really wanted to talk about this game lmao):Great little game. While the core survival gameplay isn't super interesting, as you're basically just dividing resources while choosing between bad and worse options, it is super compelling and the presentation (storytelling, music, art) is amazing. I felt every single decision and wasn't bored for a single minute of my almost 10-hour playthrough.Some reviewers have complained about sometimes stuff just happening out of nowhere that you couldn't prepare for and I really want to comment on this. While, yes, sometimes ♥♥♥♥ really just does happen, that is entirely within the spirit of the story. You're the (acting) captain of a doomed mission to the least hospitable area on earth. "Every decision matters and the ice doesn’t care." is literally in the store description. However, you are always able to anticipate and/or adept. I only failed once in my playthrough and that was because I just completely missed an obvious choice. There's always something you can improve on, which is pretty fitting with the theme of being thrust into a leadership position you didn't want or expected. It's on-theme and makes for extremely compelling gameplay that never actually feels stupid or unfair from a mechanical sense.Lastly, I want to mention the bugs. I had a couple of small bugs during my playthrough, as well as one actually gamebreaking one involving an important choice late in the game. It's nothing a simple restart didn't fix, but still worth talking about. Especially since I didn't even register the gamebreaking one as a bug. I just chalked it up to me misreading something, only finding out that I was supposed to have a choice in the outcome when reading discussions. It didn't affect my ability to finish the game but really is something that should be fixed. While the game is 100% in a playable state, potential buyers should be aware that the game (as of march 4th 2023) is somewhat buggy and that they will have to reload from a save every once in a while. Thankfully the devs are actively supporting and updating this game so I only expect it to improve in the coming months.

_childDocuments_.review: Very short story heavy game that is still great value for money!Filled with amazing characters and actually sensible consequences and reactions to your decisions. However, if the ending had been better I could have easily given a 9/10 for this game in its genre, but with that in mind, I still feel 8/10 is lowest I could give this gameIf you like visual novel style survival games with a strong focus on character development and having your decisions really matter, this game is an easy recommend

_childDocuments_.review: The game presents you with meaningful choices. For example, at one point in the game I knew that I was going to lose a man to Frostbite (med tent was at capacity). So I had decided to sacrifice a younger member of the crew due to the fact that he would oppose me in a potential popular vote. As it happens, the very same character ended up asking to be assigned as an assistant to someone of my choosing. I (correctly) assumed that assigning him to the medical team would increase the capacity and allow for all to be saved. I love how the game was able to create such a tense situation without it being explicitly scripted by the developers. The potential of having such organic developments in the story is remarkable. By this, I mean that the game rewards players that interact with all of its systems and read all information that is provided. For example, you can collect multiple firearms. These weapons can aid in obtaining food during hunts. Each weapon has some flavor text when inspected in your inventory. Remembering the description of those weapons (that you are never encouraged to read) helped me choose a suitable weapon against a foe at a crucial moment in the story (where the life of a crew mate was at risk). Not knowing what weapon would be suitable in that situation could have proven disastrous The music is very good, especially some of the more humorous acordeon pieces. Although not completely sold on the character art style, I do appreciate the different camp backgrounds and layout change. Also, I believe the map design is ingenious. Every in-game week, I found myself going over the terrain changes since the start of the expedition, noting our progress and how far we've come. A lot of them present at launch. Although none was game breaking, they can become annoying after some time. These are the ones I encountered repeatedly. Hope they get patched at some point. Although the intention was to give each crew member a name and a face, there is a clear divide between the main characters and those that were initially supposed to be the "faceless crew". Honestly, there were simply not enough chances to engage with these characters and learn about their motivations. Was expecting it to have more uses, especially after having to manage it constantly. Maybe some checks interspersed at certain story points? Crew refusing to follow orders if your standing with their faction is insufficient? The role of Research is never properly explained. The flavor text states that Research is how the success of your expedition is evaluated, but it's never brought up. Another thing is how food impacts status effects. For example, if serving a certain type of food removes the more serious version of Depression (forget its name now), why can't it also heal the less serious, initial one? Finally, some roles are clearly more important then others. Why would I choose to have an extra engineer when I could have an extra medic? The engineer can only heal the Frozen status effect, but not Frostbite. Meanwhile, the medic can heal both. Yes, curing Frozen with a medic still benches the character in question for a week, but it's still a more versatile ability and it's very likely that players won't always be able to optimally assign roles. As far as I am concerned, I would always end up with 1-2 remaining workers during the winter phase (the time when the comparison between engineers and medics is most apt, I feel). Would be nice to have a fast forward option (like Ctrl keybind in VNs) for situations when we go a few days back into the decision tree. Same applies for a conversation transcript, in case we accidentally skip a text panel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant game, grounded and emotional with an incredibly likeable crew joining you into The Pale Beyond. This game includes some elements that are not for everyone, namely  and it handles it severely as well, if at all you think this could dissuade you from the game I recommend looking into it further before deciding if you wish to join the expedition.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: When scrolling through reviews I found one where this game was depicted as 'Frostpunk with visual novel elements'. After playing it through (once), I must say: that is pretty damn accurate.As a resource management + survival -game this one is well balanced. At least on the first go I had the constant feeling that there was never enough ... well, anything. Story itself is good and characters are interesting (though at least one of the endings is weird. Not  - just ).One thing I wasn't so happy with was the navigation. I found it a bit clunky. Meaning: I preferred the tent (where everything was visible at one glance) over the ship (where you had to - quite pointlessly -  to get from top to bottom... and back again). I also had some trouble adjusting food/fuel sliders.I would recommend this game if you like survival (against environment), managing resources and crew (with some room for errors on normal difficulty), and if you ... erhm, well ... if you want a good story with a surprise.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, visually stunning, but it wants to hardcore on the survival which is fine but it has a massive scaling and ramping problem that could have been avoided with proper testing by people other than fanboys of the publishers youtube fame. The game has MASSIVE thresholds for survival. 50% of your food per day to avoid malnourishment? That is ridiculous. And what makes it worse is your food can get spoiled if you try to preserve it as the game repeatedly TELLS YOU TO DO at a certain point. Fuel also is spent VERY rapidly to the point that eventually you are required to split already ridiculously rare resources between two sources. The numbers need to be scaled back from the beginning. There is zero reason for yo to have to limit rations from week 1 when you arent even in danger yet. Im sorry but this game needs some serious tuning and never should have been released in this state. There are plenty of bugs that could have and should have been solved by having the devs play the game. Its almost ironic that this game came from a studio who's fame comes from youtube videos critiquing studios for doing the very same. Im quite disappointed in the execution of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond was an emotionally gripping tale that didnt quite stick the landing in a few key ways. It's a survival/management game with a narrative focus, and its strengths are in presenting the player with situations that appear stressful but are navigable with good planning. I say "appear" stressful there because personally, I found the game to be too easy on normal difficulty, which undermined the narrative. It really seemed like the game expected me to get to the end with half my crew dead and the other half disloyal, but by the end of it I had only one death and all but one of my officers remained by my side. If you're experienced with management type games, I'd probably recommend playing on hard mode for the best narrative experience.The narrative itself is solid but it's held back by a few key aspects. You play as Robin Shaw, first mate in a doomed expedition to the South Pole. It's a compelling tale, and the characters' speech gives strong vibes of 18th century adventure novels - "Treasure Island" especially springs to mind. In terms of minutia, the game's writing is quite solid. All of the major characters have solid dialogue and there are plenty of small pockets of excellent writing woven throughout the various characters' small conversations with Shaw. The overarching narrative, by contrast, feels a little sporadic. My impression is that the goal was to take a streamlined approach, cut out the fluff from the story and focus on the big dramatic moments. This works well enough early on, when there are enough periods of management and milling about with the crew that it's not really noticeable. This facade wears thin in the latter half of the game, though, as the connective tissue of management fades into the background and the story becomes a series of set pieces strung together by little to no other elements. The ending was compelling, if a little frustrating. Without spoiling anything, it ends with a partial fourth wall break that feels awkward, but at the same time I cannot call it ineffective because it did spark some imagination in me.Beyond the aspects already listed, the game is very well put together. The visuals are often stunning, and the music and sound design work incredibly well. I found the way that portraits changed in difference scenes to adapt to the new environments to be quite endearing. Overall it's a solid game and one that I do recommend, though it's nowhere near perfect. It's definitely enough that I'll keep my eye on the future works of this team and its developers, though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic narrative game! The story grabbed my interest very quickly and did not let go. In addition to narrative twists and turns, there is a lot of flavor, making the environment and the crew feel real. The mechanics are poorly explained but the checkpoint system isn't too bad (though I do wish there was a faster means of skipping dialogue) so some trial and error experimentation isn't too painful. I highly recommend The Pale Beyond if you're into this sort of thing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't much interested in this until they did their video after launch discussing it a bit more and I found it mildly intriguing. Well it's actually quite good so far. I'll definitely see it through. The music is fantastic and the art is really well polished. The writing feels pretty much average, perhaps a bit above average. It does have humorous moments that are quite well done. I find the atmosphere really immersive with all the sounds and such. It's crazy they wrote 25 characters for this game. I'll update it when I'm done playing. A few critiques that I think could be ironed out quickly should the devs see this:1. when selecting a reply in a conversation (something you do hundreds of times during a play through obviously), it then puts your reply into the little chat box thing on the other side of the screen where the other party is replying. I'm sure the point of this exactly, maybe it's standard in this type of game, idk. But my problem is it has a perhaps half second lag as it  shows up before you can click the button again to progress to the next dialog choice. This slows down conversation a bit but also is annoying because it means I need to press a button twice, but not doubletap it, because of the little lag time. I would suggest making a toggle for this. Either allow the player to skip that entirely, or at least make it one button press.2. the dialog response boxes will sometimes extend off the screen if I change my text size depending on how many responses there are. Mayhaps allowing for those boxes to be scrolled through? I don't imagine it would be too hard to allow for the player to use a button to move it up and down a little bit. You'd simply be changing the y axis a little while putting restrictions on how far up and down it can go. I've programmed this type of system myself, it's not complicated.3. couldn't find an option to switch between C and F for temps. Would be nice for us idiot Americans lolOther than those minor gripes, though the first one gets a bit annoying because it's a constant issue, the game is quite polished. I only noticed one typo so far. In one of my journal entries, the second time I was made to open it by the game, there was a place where a space was missing between two sentences.I've liked it more than I thought, but I guess I should have expected that because I read and write every day so something like this should be up my ally. I've only played a game like this in Tales From The Borderland. This, for being a 2D, lower budget games, scratches an itch that that game didn't. Probably the survival aspect and the higher consequences.Highly recommend, even if you don't usually play these types of games.Edit: still enjoying it. Though I have just got my first game over at only act two, so I haven't fully experienced it. The game is quite difficult, so who knows if I'll ever win lol
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly fantastic. Not much else I can say other than that. I really felt the struggle and hopelessness associated with being stranded on the ice with no ship.SPOILERS:I literally cried like a baby when I had to leave the dogs behind and then they showed up on shore as we were taking off. That was pulling at my heart strings hard. I only lost one true crew member and everyone else survived on normal. Most of the human lives were meh to me if I am being honest except for a select few, but the dogs..... That ♥♥♥♥ was evil to put in a game. I wanted to see a quick rescue expedition to rescue the dogs if possible. The crew literally owe their lives to them. Ok enough ranting about the dogs. This game is 100% worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful looking, well crafted if slightly shallow resource management game.The story is for the most part, what carried it. a combination of excellent artwork and solid writing did wonders at immersing yourself in the pressures of a leadership role during a crisis. Crew needs and morale is a bit of a learning curve. its very easy to lose crew members early on when you dont know what youre doing, but over time you pick up the major points and after that its reasonably easy to keep all your crew members alive and reasonably content.For all the talk of crew votes on your captaincy i only experienced 2 votes, both of them mandatory and easy to accomplish. most of the crew follow one key supervisor, therefore as long as hes in your pocket youre grand, even if you cant convince loyalist members of the crew to join you, youll still have a majority so long as you dont go out of your way to annoy others.Resource gathering/scouting is relatively basic and its not difficult to aquire the ammount of goods needed to keep everyone happy and healthy.The endgame/ending left me feeling a little sold short. the plot kind of falls away at the end with hitherto unknown maguffins and stakes neither myself nor the crew really seemed to care about all that much. like theres such a lurch in the final act and without spoiling anything youll know immeadiately what im talking about if you play it for youself, but basically you go from just trying to survive to suddenly deciding the future of humanity, and i really feel like the game didnt need that. a more grounded, harroving ending probably would have served a lot better.But in summary its a choices matter story game with resource management that managed to hold my attention and at times even draw me in, mostly because i love anything with a nautical theme. I enjoyed the game and will be on the lookout for other titles from the developer!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I have followed the folks behind this studio for years. I was so excited to play this and I must say. I love this game. The art, the aesthetic, the music.I happened to win my first playthrough (lower difficulty) relatively easily, but not perfectly. And the story was fascinating and gutpunching enough that I could not help but try again for the better ending. And several more times for different, also good, endings. And to try it over and over just FITS with the story. You will come to hate a man, to empathize with him, to pity him, to understand him.The gameplay is serviceable. The characters delightful.  The pups cute as hell. I just can't bring myself to play it badly on purpose for the bad endings. :(Help yourself to a good game. Help this indie studio. They're one of the good ones."For I'll lead these souls, so help the gods, out of the pale beyond."
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I fully recommend this experience to anyone brave enough to venture to the ice.  However, at this point, I do advise waiting a few weeks before you start your expedition through the Pale Beyond, due to some issues I've encountered. Most of which I know the dev team is aware of and are working on a fix for. - Like the stack bug. When you want to add multiple of the same resource to anything it quite often makes the entire stack disappear. Pressing escape fixes this issue temporarely so it doesn't make the game unplayable.- Or the entire UI itself not showing up when switching between menu's too fast after receiving new information. Exiting the menu helps so nothing game breaking, just immersion breaking.- Personally I had some issues with understanding the status effects in the game. I don't know if I missed an explanation early on but I only found out that scurvy untreated means the crew member dies the following week through a pop up during a request midway through the game. So I've been unsure if frostbite worked the same way but I was to scared to try it out. Also it says that putting someone in the medbay clears them of all status effects. Except demoralizaion apparently, which makes sense but the wording did make me think it was possible.Again I do fully recommend this game. The narrative is amazing and I truly cared about the lives of the entire crew. None of the issues were fully game breaking, so if you think you won't be bothered by these issues, go ahead! Set sail.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:Good resource management game. Story can go really dark if you let it.CONS:A lot of reading that doesn't really serve the storyline, a lot of pointless melodramatic dialogue. Writer needs to take a page out of Nonary Games, Forgotten City, Detroit Become Human and other top-tier narrative games in how to write NPC dialogue - it needs to be relevant to the story to be interesting.Takes FOREVER to redo storylines - they really should let you power skip dialogue so you can see alternative endings.Overall I'd give it a 6.5/10 - I recommend it if it's on sale and you like narrative games. But the amount of time it takes slogging through pointless dialogue to get to the different branching storylines is such a pain that probably most people will just play through it once.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The only bad thing I can say about this game is that there isn't a sequel. For now at least! I love all of these complex characters so much and the amazing gameplay, the artwork, the music, ugh! Such a good game, that's all I can say. Will for sure be looking at these devs for future games if its anything like this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not something like I've played before. It is interesting and looks great. I find myself immersed come about the third "week" of playthrough. It is a slowish starter, but I feel like if you were just thrown in the deep end, you'd either be lost or turned off. You need the slow story building in the beginning. I'm 4 hours in and I don't see a reason I would not give this a full go through the entire story. I recommend to anyone to just give it a shot and see if this type of game is in your wheelhouse.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This was like a video game version of the book The Terror by Dan Simmons. I really enjoyed the choose your own adventure gameplay. I got 5 or 6 different endings, and my only complaint is that I wish some of them were fleshed out more. But that might just be due to thew fact that I really enjoyed the story and wanted more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the frustration. While it has a great art style, music and interesting characters expect frustration instead of fun.Such a promising concept, however the developer seems unable to properly execute on it.I've uninstalled after my save was ruined by a bug causing it to become impossible to cure scurvy.The save system is a horrific mess that will leave you redoing the same dialogue over and over again.The UI is clunky and not good at showing you important information, which if you miss means reloading and playing over a massive chunk of dialogue again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: So, I like this game but I want potential players to be aware of some criticism that might be useful going into it. First, I think the atmosphere is great, the style is unique and the visual novel type game play was fun. But I also hate the save system and I'm not a huge fan of how drastically it shifts from a character builder into asset management. The game gets very punishing rather quickly and you won't even make it to the second act of five acts without optimizing your resources. If you don't know how, and I'm not joking on this, literally everyone will die and the best you can do is delete your save points and try again.  Overall, I think this game is worth trying with a guide. Without one, you're basically as stranded as the characters. I probably won't finish it and at near full price, I somewhat regret my purchase. 6\10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I Wishlisted this game first time I heard of it on the Bell news channel and bought it on day one. Absolutely no regrets!It's a really nice and fresh game. But it also reminds me of some of my favorite games like the Obra Dinn and Frostpunk. And the marine biologist in me loves the Antarctic survey setting.The survival, writing, look and music aspect are on point. It is incredibly immersive and I really want to know where the story goes. I have made it to week 17 so far... There are some gameplay mechanics, save tree and UI elements that needs polish or fixing but I am sure the team is already working on them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I was anxiously waiting for its release since playing the demo months ago and I was not disappointed. There are some minor bugs but they aren't game breaking and the devs have been very responsive and patching things up since release. The game is amazing. Period. Great story. Original gameplay. Great replay value. Choices really matter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This was a good story focused game. I completed my first run with just over 6 hours of time. A couple things to note before you get into it is the game is focused around choices. Everything from talking with the crew, to resource management, and the story itself. As some have mentioned this game is akin to a choose your own adventure. Events will happen and while there is some agency in your choice and the path following these events, the story will occur one way or the other all often times all you can do is react. The game is entirely text based with no voice overs but I think that just helped to add to the charm of what the game already had going for it. The interface was for the most part easy to use, with some tweaks in the settings to speed up zooming in and out and panning. The hand drawn style of the game I think fits very well, and the small attention to detail as the game progresses to the more cinematic cuts were great to see. The music tying all of those parts together. The story itself had its ups and downs but was an overall fantastic journey. The characters each had some sort of motive driving them, and that added some depth. Events made you actually care about the crew. With the final bit tying everything up nicely for the conclusion.If you want a story focused, resource management, with some choose your own adventure style game I think this is a solid choice and worth the price. Depending on how things go with your choices there is some replayability to change certain events you think could of gone better or just to see a what if scenario. While I don't know if the developer is planning to add anything else to this game, I hope they continue in this style or at least continue the world building they already have with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn between wanting to play it again and being genuinely concerned I won't handle another stab right in the feels like this again.Pros: * Wonderful graphics and soundtrack* Characters you actually want to care about* Resource management mechanics simple enough not to get in the way of the storyCons:* Some interface glitches (resource cards disappearing when placed on the wheel, text being rendered partially off-screen)* Certain resources feel like they do not benefit you in any immediate way and are not explained well enough.* Story writers working through some trauma at the expense of the unsuspecting players. Why did you do that? Who hurt you?! You monsters! You KNOW what I'm talking about!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A soothing, beautiful, narrative game. The atmosphere, music, and art style blend together with the storytelling to create impactful events with characters.If you're looking to feel something in the games you play, where your decisions feel like they impact other characters who have emotions and histories, The Pale Beyond will be a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Theres really no colletion, or amount of words to describe this game, this must be what reading a good book fells like, its over and I really dont know waht to do, i could play it again, but it wouldnt be right, the crew more than deserve theirs rests.PS: this is honestly as good as disco elysium, and i ♥♥♥♥♥♥ love that game
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for December 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before January 2nd, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Sailing into the frozen south to find a mysterious wreck. The Pale Beyond starts with an interview for the main character to join the interviewer’s crew as a first mate.  The game is played in a slow story-based style where players have to make choices but also those questions will make the player think a bit about their character.  The game says that decisions will change the crew, their opinions of the player, and their morale.  There are also several resources that players will have to balance between food, fire, and the aforementioned morale.   The game moves at a brisk pace but there’s probably a lot more to discover after the first hour.  At the same time, this does seem to be very story-heavy.  I’m not sure how much each decision will matter, and the game pretty much forces most of the important choices in the first hour.  It’s likely just holding the player's hand but as usual, this is a game claiming “choices will matter”, and the question as always is “how much”.  It seems the gameplay is more about staying alive than necessarily changing the ending, but that’s also where the challenge will lie. Pick this up if you like a story-based game.  Parts of me were thinking about Return of the Ober Din due to the language and an experience on a ship, but that was more of a puzzle game and this is more of a narrative.  Still, something is intriguing about this story so far so it’s possible I’ll play much more. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A simple game with a well told story and simple narrative. Enjoyed the story and characters, as well as the setting of the world and the revelations at the end. The game could use a little bit more polish as there are some annoying bugs but those did not keep me from enjoying this from start to finish. I recommend this game for people who enjoy narrative games and resource management/survival mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Its a first game of a new studio from a popular gaming YouTuber Bellular and it is a good, fun game.The graphics are nothing to write home about, but are decent at immersing oneself in a heavy story driven game.There is no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that plagues gaming today and i was happy to pay the price they asked. I will be looking forward to future games this studio makes
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond
