The guys at Bellular actually made a guite a great experience.It mixes in a great bit of narrative, with dialogues and resource management gameplay. Very worthwhile.Also, the graphical style of this game is trully something to enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable narrative driven game. Despite so many characters, they all have necessary roles in game and having to see to their needs and explore their story makes all of your choices feel really interesting. First play through I would often hit decision points and have to stop and actually think about how I wanted to proceed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly bought this game originally just to support Bellular. I have never played a game anything like this since the days of Oregon Trail. I ended up not being able to walk away from it and 4 hours later I failed the mission. It was so much more fun than I expected! I want to play again and try to do better, however, I am worried that I'll end up exactly where I did last time since I of course made all the perfect decisions the first time through, lol. I would recommend to anyone who is looking for a great time that doesn't require fast past combat. The art was great, the characters were interesting and the stakes were very very real.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork is beautiful, the gameplay is engaging, the story has high stakes and a compelling mystery to engage with. The music is great too. So why the negative review? It's hard to explain exactly why, even to myself, but the only real explanation I have is that by the end of the game, I was just ready to be done with it. It almost feels like the game accomplishes its goal a little too well. The journey is harrowing and long and difficult and by the end of it, I'm just finished.I don't have any desire to interact with any of these people anymore. Not because they're not fleshed out, but because I have been trapped on the ice for months with them in a desperate survival situation and half of them were being irrational, suicidal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.I have no desire to learn about our big secret mission or go through any of the effort that would be required to do so. The game has kicked me and taken all of my stuff so many times at this point that I'm sick of rebuilding and I don't want to engage in an "optional" one. Additionally, throughout the entire game they don't give you any information as to why you should care even slightly about the mission at all and so when it came time to make a decision, it wasn't one.I just want to go home and be rid of everyone. Absolutely thematic as hell, but not optimal in a game you're supposed to be playing for fun. I just don't have any desire to go back and learn any of the other endings. The game is too much work for too little payout and by the time it turns to me and asks "DO YOU STILL CARE?! ISN'T THIS EXCITING?!" my only answer is no, this sucks actually and I want to be done.I got everyone home in one piece and I just don't care at all about the Viscount or its mystery in the slightest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I cried a solid 20 minutes of heartbreaking tears, doubting my own choice, during one of the story progression events. Haven't had a choose your own adventure type of game doing that to me in a long long time. Highly recommended for anyone fascinated by stories of high arctic survival/expeditions, and wanting to enjoy a game with a good storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is a well-crafted and challenging game that will test your survival skills in a harsh and unforgiving environment. The game's replayability adds to its overall value, and the sound and visual presentation contribute to the immersive atmosphere. I highly recommend this game to fans of resource management and survival simulation games. As of writing this, I just got through my first play-through but look forward to going back and trying some things I had second thoughts about, as well as just trying some wacky things that I wouldn't normally do just for the entertainment value.While this doesn't directly apply to my gameplay, I also just have to give Kudos to the development team as they have been keeping right on top of any negative feedback and trying to address any issues that have been reported. It is encouraging to see the developers responding to negative comments and actually taking action to try and correct them. Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A few days in so far and I am already hooked! I played the demo first, which was enough to get me to purchase the full game. To avoid spoilers I will not mention much of what happens, but know that the voyage will not go to as was planned. I really enjoy figuring out how to play to the strengths of each of my crew members, slowly gaining more and more of their trust. Having to step on the toes of some to win the trust of others is needed though. Overall the narrative is very engaging, I find myself interested in the stories of all my crew members, as well as ensuring their survival and loyalty as the days and supplies are stretched further and further.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely artistic desigm, enchanting otherworldly music. So far have enjoyed the story and survival management.  I haven't delved into the save tree's much yet but I feel like its a cool idea that could be better implemented. I like the idea of branching out but also miss being able to save at any point.  Overall though if you like atmosphere, story, stellar art design and fantastic music then this is well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful yet harrowing experience with beautiful backdrops to distract you from sounds of your crew freezing/starving/bleeding to death nearby as you desperately search in vain for any way out.  The narrative and characters that carry it throughout are well written, I found myself growing attached to a few of them through their dialog, loyal to some and even a bit jaded to others, all in ways that fit the story playing out from my choices, it makes for a beautiful anxiety as you search for able bodies to send on supply runs only to find your favorite the last one idle, possibly freezing or malnourished at risk of turning worse but the only one fit to scavenge the resources we desperately need to save the others.Choices are hard, but fair.  The narrative will bring you to moments where you must sit and consider the ramification of a good idea only because it will make something else harder down the line, but it is the captains duty to make such choices.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: You take decisions that have consequences and the game branches depending on what you choose, and it does a pretty good job at that (not like other games that only give you the illusion of choice). The story is nice and has a twist. You also have to manage your relations with the various characters, which are all pretty cool. Feels like a typical point and click adventure, with a resource management minigame.Definitely recommended on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: "The Pale Beyond" presents players with a chilling and immersive polar exploration experience, devoid of supernatural elements, while still evoking a sense of unease and mystery. Embarking on a perilous voyage through a frozen wasteland, the game captures the essence of survival and uncertainty reminiscent of the eerie atmosphere that is present in the first season of "The Terror".  Set in an unforgiving Arctic landscape, players find themselves in the shoes of an unexpected leader faced with daunting challenges. The game's stunning visuals depict the harsh and ever-changing environment that can shift at any moment, heightening the feeling of isolation and danger. As you navigate through the icy expanse, the eerie ambiance creates a constant sense of foreboding.Every decision carries weight and consequence. Resource management becomes paramount as players must carefully balance safety, morale, and the crew's well-being. The game puts emphasis on making tough choices and managing meager resources to ensure the survival of the expedition.The expedition's progression and the approaching Polar Winter serve as a backdrop for the unfolding narrative. As you lead the crew through the treacherous ice, the choices you make will shape the story and determine the outcome of your journey. The importance of maintaining crew unity and preventing a mutiny adds tension and interpersonal dynamics to the gameplay, creating a captivating experience that echoes the challenges probably present for polar expeditions.  "The Pale Beyond" excels in delivering an eerie and atmospheric gaming experience, focusing on the unforgiving nature of the Arctic environment and the harsh realities of survival. While it may not incorporate supernatural elements (or does it?), the game embraces a sense of mystery and unease, keeping players engaged as they navigate through the unknown. If you appreciate atmospheric storytelling, challenging decision-making, and a palpable feeling of eeriness, "The Pale Beyond" offers an intriguing expedition into the unknown. With the multiple endings the price is on point giving you plenty of hours for a pretty low price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The story of this game really pulled me in. I've been wanting a game on polar exploration ever since I watched the Terror several years back. This game genuinely had me worrying how the crew was going to make it. I had some minor gripes about some of the mechanics but the story kept me going. Definitely worth it in my mind.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first venture into the narrative survival genre and this game delivers the goods.  The music, the story and the imagery all serve to make me feel like one of the members of the crew.  I love this game... now I only need to convince my toddlers to let me play it more often.UPDATE:  I finished the game and I could not feel more fulfilled.  The story is compelling and the ending(s) are satisfying.  I actually feel like I learned a lot about managing individuals from this game; especially in difficult scenarios.  Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Love the characters, art style, story and general vibes. The writing is 10/10! It takes a bit of trial and error to get used to managing everything which is fine, but I wish you weren't penalised so harshly (literally with death) for failing early on. Everyone died on my first playthrough because (MILD SPOILER) I didn't realise you had to move them off the ship within a certain amount of time. It's frustrating to start getting immersed in the story and characters, only to be abruptly met with the (unskippable) credits sequence. It doesn't hold as much weight to see everyone die when you barely know them, so I just wish death could be easier to avoid towards the start of the game. Nevertheless, I am really having fun with this game so far. If you'd similarly like to focus more on story than on survival, play on the easiest difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game at first, but my experience was tainted by a story beat that I felt like was not foreshadowed/warned about/given any solution or opt out. History does not always forget the animals. It doesn't have to. That story beat felt like it was primarily for shock value, and it really tainted the entire experience. I was planning on replaying it and will not be now.The art is beautiful, the love for the arctic and the combination of foolishness, bravery and mettle it takes to do something like that is evident in the game. The characters are wonderful, I wish you could get to know them more deeply/have more one on one moments. But again, that moment really took me out of it.I know the arctic is brutal, I've been studying it for years, but this is a fictional game. The writers chose to put that in and I fundamentally disagree with them about it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely one of those games I wish I could wipe from my memory to experience again for the first time. Not only due to it being so damn good, but also to the fact that as much as I do want to replay it, I simply don't think I could willingly put myself through the stress of being a ships first mate in a survival situation again.  "Gonna be a 10/10 from me dawg." - Randy jackson
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Only 4 hours in and will play more and change the review as updates come out, but there are a lot of tiny little bugs that really annoyed me after a while, things like selecting resources just to have the stack disappear and only reappear once you left and reloaded the menu. Every once in a while is fine but when its happening consistently on every interaction in the game it becomes very annoying very quickly.  The save system is also a minor gripe, I understand the decision to lock saves behind weeks but it does feel bad if you can't finish out a week and have to redo it if you needed to put the game down. The core loop is pretty fun and the characters seem to be pretty well though out, the art direction itself is very nice but I feel like the resource management portion of the game is a little tedious with such limited reserves that just feeding people take up half your total storage making stock piling difficult/unintuitive.If you like a very hard survival game then I can recommend this but I'd really wait until all the bugs are fixed because right now that's what is making it more frustrating than fun to play.**Edit just encountered another fun bug upon going back in my save tree that prevents me from using the medical tent to heal people, so yeah just give this a month or two for the bugs to get fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Its an absolutely fantastic game. Theres a demo to figure out if its something you'll enjoy or not, but I found the writing to be fantastic. I'm not sure how I feel about the answer to the mytery of the viscount. Its neat, but its pretty much out of relation to everything else in the story, and adds a mystical element that isn't really needed. Loved everything else though. All of the main characters were great, and even most of the individual crew stood out enough to be memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A truly great game, despite a few bugs. It's two games in one; the survival element, which is mostly worker placement and resource management, and the story element. The survival element is OK but nothing we haven't seen before in games like Frostpunk. The story is the real strength, it has multiple branches and choices with big consequences, most of all in the finale which is epic, adding some fantasy elements. Every one of the game's 26 characters has a  distinct personality and must be handled differently to get the best from them. The game is heavily based on the Shackleton Expedition and the McClure search for the Franklin Expedition. It seems very appropriate that a game based on so many Irish heroes should be made by an Irish game studio! Look out for historical Easter eggs like the stowaway, mutinous carpenter, heart attack, lead poisoning etc. Sadly though, no Mrs Chippy! If you like this game watch a Shackleton documentary on YouTube or read 'South'.  -40 degrees out of 10; would die of scurvy again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this one's hard to not recommend.  I've listened to Bellular's channel during my World of Warcraft days, so I know there are people behind this who want to have a good quality product.  In the sense of the game, its great!  Dialogue is good, decisions are tough, resource management is fun.  Artstyle and music are perfect.  So why am I not recommending you buy this?The bugs.  Oh god, the bugs.  I bought the game a week after its release and I have encountered at least two bugs that have caused me to reset the entire week of decisions, and one game breaking bug that makes it almost impossible to beat.  I've reported these.  What shocks me is how easy these bugs are to find.  It feels like they either did not hire a good QA, did not budget time and money for testing, or have a programmer or two who needs to code more carefully.  Its incredibly disappointing, and someone who made the decision that this was ready for launch made a massive mistake.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It was a great experience from begigning to end.The art and music are fantastic and i like the character desing a lot.The story and gameplay  go hand to hand very well, creating a felling of tension that never leaves until the very end.the resource management is thought but fair. Your crew consumes plenty of resources so if you dont go with the mindset of cutting cost from early on you might find yourself in a spiral of disasters. At the same time the game gives you plenty of tools to survive, so if you look carefully at what is at your disposal you are gonna be able to pull yourself up even after making some mistakes.The crew is pretty charming and is really enjoyable to spend time seing everyone  devolpement in this hellish situation. I've never been so invested in making a grumpy stuborn accordion loving  bastard like me. Ended liking all the specialist members of the crew.A minor gripe regarding the crew is that i wanted more, i wanted to talk more with some of the regular sailors and explorer that i never saw even in petitions. While i understand that you cant give every character the depth  of the specialists, i wish that there were a couple more of petitions of events to at least a moment with every member of the Temperance.Despite all that there was a moment that i was afraid of losing my favorite scout   and it almost gave me a hearth attackAnother minor gripe is that while  understand not wanting give Shawn a defined appeareance, i would like to have at least a body to place among the rest of the crew. I think it would make some moments hit even harder.This game will make you suffer and when you think its done it will keep you grabbed by the B***S for another hour or two until it finally lets go. I think that this will stay in my mind for a while and i look foward to the future of this studio
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I have been enjoying icy survival games of late and this game delivered! Not in exactly the same way as other survival games though. The game advertises itself as a character/narrative focused story and it delivers. I really appreciated that each crew member had a portrait, a name, a personality and wasn't just a number on your resources list. It made my first, disastrous, playthrough all the more heartbreaking. I genuinely grew to love the crew, and played through again to try and do better for them. (long section, but I just had trouble explaining minor bugs) There are some bugs I encountered fairly regularly in the game, but nothing gamebreaking. The most frequent were to do with adding resources to the furnace/pot, it would black out the resource selection after selecting just one out of a stack of items (like 1 seal out of 5) and I would have to exit out of the menu and back in to finish adding all the items I needed. I also had issues with the number of dogs that the menu estimated I would use for trips, sometimes it would say 14 for one go, which confused me a lot in the beginning. Fortunately, once you get used to it, the correct number of dogs still gets sent, so this can be ignored. The bugs will be fixed soon enough I am sure, and did not greatly impact my experience.But really, this is a great game. I enjoyed the music, the backgrounds were beautiful (despite being mostly ice) and the characters were wonderfully written. And the portraits! So expressive and so many different emotions portrayed! I was really impressed. For sure give this game a go if it has caught your eye!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Visually beautiful game, cool characters,The story is good too.I have finished the game in one day of gaming. It is short, and in some way it reminds me of games like Portal or Firewatch: they are quite brief, but very intense.There's always some dialog options, but once you get to know the characters, there's almost always one that stands out as the most appropriate. The weakness of this game would be its replay value. I also think there could be better in-game explanation of the inherent mechanics.I had to do a second playthrough about a third from the game because I had not understood some mechanics well.The game was much easier when I knew about the way the optimisation works in it. It was a dull, because it felt like having to watch the first hour of a movie again to know the end, because your dvd (or vhs tape lol) broke at some point.There were some bugs that appeared in my playthrough, one regarding the interface not assigning ressources/people properly, and one that completely blocked my progression by week 38. It seeems there were quick fixes for those issues, though, and it's understandable for a game that just came out.I hope there is some sort of DLC with a new storyline, because the content was good, but it feels like there should be more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. POTENTIAL SPOILERS AHEAD Let me start with saying I rarely write reviews, but this game deserves so much more praise and to be mainstream. The game mechanics were interesting and fun to learn, I was so enthralled that I wish there was even more character and world building. One of the issues I did have was it was buggy at times. Had issues putting stuff in the furnace and pot sometimes, also I had a few cutscenes with the kid the first time I played through, even though he wasn't there. However, I easily looked passed that due to the quality of the game. The art style is cute, with it cutting between minis and visual novel standards. Grimleys song has been stuck in my head for days, and the ending brought tears to my eyes. When I lost people, I felt responsibility and sadness, even for the characters that aren't considered to be part of the "main cast". Being able to make Grimley my first mate put such emotion through me, I wish the game was 100 times longer. I wish I was able to be in every minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game truly takes you on a journey. The gameplay is easy enough and not too difficult, however, it is the choices that you'll make that will be nerve-wrecking in some cases. This game had me sobbing in the middle of the night and on the verge of quitting, but at the same I couldn't stop. The writing is superb and I am in love with the diverse characters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming gameHowever game takes place in like a past victorian era and you have members of the crew who identify as "THEY THEIR" like im playing the game to escape reality i dont want WOKE nonesense in every game i play. There is also obviously a trans crewmember which isnt so bad, but hearing everyone including yourself as the main character and the crew around you feed into that delusion of "THEY THEIR" and being more than two genders is cringe and immersion breaking.Storytelling doesnt have a real pushy political agenda in it and im thankful, most games made by tender foots do, so if you can hold your breath through a few moments of cringe immersion breaking dialoug and a few bugs, you have a pretty good story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A valiant first effort for this developer, the Pale Beyond is a point-and-click worker placement game with numerous dialog choices that will prompt you to make difficult decisions to keep the loyalty of your crew. It's a good game to play blind if you mainly care about the story. That seems to be the focus here, as the game frequently keeps you in the dark about what your actions will mean mechanically. If you're a more gameplay-focused person who cares about optimization, this game may frustrate you with its sometimes obscure mechanics and interface. On the bright side, there seems to be almost no randomness involved, and you can start over from any previous "week" of the game if you made a mistake and are willing to spend extra time. If not, there is more room for error than you might expect.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I have a mixed review of this game for a few reasons. First the good:-Great graphics-Excellent storytelling-First half of the game with the choices and dialog is greatNow the bad:-After the first half of the game and you are stranded, the game becomes boring-Basically too hard, I had to restart three times due to choices-Once you play the game, you really wont want to play it againMy suggestions are:-Add additional choices, instead of everything being rigid-Introduce fishing and hunting earlier-Some weeks felt shorter than others, add additional content
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of "Point&Click-Adventures"...."The Pale Beyond" combined my love to decisionmaking-games and the survival mechanics of Frostpunk.I've reached the end of the Story after 25h of active playtime! I would have never imagined to be hooked this hard. I love the story. The everyday taskmanagement was quiet challenging tbh. Yes, from time to time the inventory Ui bugs where a little anoying but not gamebreaking. I totally recommend this game and i cant wait what lies beyond in future( 10/10 )
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art and music, captivating story. it does have a lot of reading and no voice acting, but I had no problem bringing my own narrative to it. I recommend if you enjoy city sim / mystery stories. My first play through was on hard but its not hard to manage. I only made a mistake once of losing decorum as I wasnt paying attention to how low it was at the end of a week and tried to get away with staving them a little much.solidly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A game that starts with a very ominous introduction which it keep engage for beginning to end. You're mainly playing the game for the story, but the resource management and crew interactions are deep enough to keep on your toes meanwhile you're figuring out how to keep your crew alive in the frozen wasteland.There's some jank when it comes to handling the panning camera, which is my only complaint to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A roughly 10-hour journey that is nail-bitingly gripping. With strong characterisation, a solid, mysterious plot and a melancholic, if not a little stressful resource management gameplay loop. You really feel like you've got to make some tough decisions, and you will, and once you do the true beauty of this game shines. Would easily recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Game is riddled with bugs. Most of them are just UI related and make the game feel low quality and unfinished but won't kill the experience for you if you are really committed to powering through it, but I am now officially soft locked about 3/4 of the way through the game (when you reclass a normal crewmember into something in the "specialist" class, which is unselectable for crew actions, the game still thinks of them as a selectable crew member even though you can't do it... it caused janky gameplay situations for a long time and then I finally hit a hard stop when the game forced me to select all available crew members for an action before continuing)*Update: The soft lock has been "fixed" by hardcoding it to advance the event when you run into it. The UI and game systems still don't recognize the character correctly.  Hacking out a solution on a day one patch is much better than nothing, but the phrase that continued to linger in my mind as I played was "low quality."  I've now finished one play-through with no desire to go find other endings/achievements (which I think was supposed to be a big part of the game's value).  The gameplay was interesting for the first couple hours but doesn't do enough to keep you on your toes once you've identified the mathematically efficient resource patterns so playing more just seems like tedious busywork. It's one of those games that probably gets out of hand fast once you let things start going wrong but it was very easy to never get to that point for me.  I think this game would have been forgettably average at $5, but at $20 I'm definitely regretting the purchase.  I knew the risks buying the game on day 1, that's just how it goes sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The resource management in the game is a bit unforgiving, but I think that's intentional, and I don't feel like it's overly difficult, you just kind of have to accept ♥♥♥♥ is not going to go well and power on. Personally I really enjoyed this and it was a deeply emotional and nailbiting 10 hour experience. I found myself crying at two parts, one over something bad happening to something that wasn't even living
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews for games, but I feel I have to for this one. In all honesty, I liked it. There were some annoying bug/UI issues that I had to live with, but it didn't completely sour the game for me. I would have probably given the game a good review if I hadn't been forced to make a decision that I didn't want to make. It really ruined the experience for me. Perhaps I'm overly sensitive. I've played and enjoyed other games that have required difficult decisions, but this one just felt cruel. I was offended that there was enough content to get me invested before being faced with that unavoidable dilemma. If I had known what was coming, I would have never purchased the game to begin with. If you're reading this and not sure what I'm referencing: you will understand if you play it. And don't get me wrong - there is a lot to enjoy about the game. I'm just disappointed the creators felt it necessary to force their players to do something so heartbreaking.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent story, was hooked from the Demo.Devs made sure you can't save scum your way through the "right" choices >.<Even with my cons list being longer, they aren't game breaking cons. Will edit review once bugs are fixed.10/10 would buy again.Pros:Great storyStylized art styleRelaxing (most of the time)Cons:UI is pretty buggy. Items will disappear when trying to add them to Hoosh pot. have to back out and try againCamera will jump to bottom corner of screen when using pan function sometimesUI elements get stuck displaying sometimesText scroll is sometimes painfully slowScroll and pan speed settings seem to do absolutely nothing. Same speed regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the Terror, so I really wanted to love this game. It's by no means a bad game, but to me it does not really feel like it lives up to it's potential. For a game pitched at surviving the cold antarctic, it never feels like the player is asked to make a hard decision. The majority of the time, there's a 'right' decision to be made - very rarely does the game force you to choose between two undesirable outcomes. While theres a loyalty system in play, I pretty much maxed out all but one crew member's loyalty on my first play through, just by picking the obvious dialogue choice with each crewmember. There's a brief segment where two factions of the crew develop some friction, but the option to have both sides reconcile is so obvious I'd think you'd have to be deliberately trying to stoke tensions for RP purposes.The resource management system also felt very dry and boils down to how you manage your sickbay. There's no repurcusions to letting your crew get scurvy/frostbite since all it takes to cure them is a week's rest (or administer magic medicine that instantly cures everything). Once I figured that out, keeping everyone alive was fairly trivial.Edit: I also wanted to add that that despite the subject matter, the game maintains an fairly upbeat atmosphere (minus a few specific scenes). I'm not sure if this a deliberate design choice, and  to be fair I don't think the game pretends to be anything else. Just don't expect anything like This War of Mine, Frostpunk or Pathologic 2 in terms of atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying this game so far, but also have some minor grievances. Things you're told in dialogue don't always reflect the gameplay; for example, I made the decision to leave the ship ASAP based largely on Hammond stating that it would be easier to heat a camp than the ship. I figured this meant a decrease in how much fuel is needed, but nope. Same daily fuel needs.Another character, Grimley, you can speak to nearly every day and earn loyalty if you chose the right dialogue. I almost always did. After having friendly conversations in which he acts like he respects me nearly daily for the entire voyage thus far, you'd think he likes me. Yet, he despises the protagonist and actively riles the crew up against me in every main story beat. It feels weird and disjointed to have parallel, different versions of the guy who treat the protag completely differently running at the same time between the casual conversations and the story-essential ones. Other characters keep urging me to make peace with him, and when I do nothing happens. It makes me wonder if the "Loyalty" thing is at all consequential?Now for a nitpick that doesn't much matter; it is very silly that when we ditch the ship, the furnace is just out in the open. These poor sailors are getting frostbite hunting for seal oil to fuel the thing, but almost all that heat is just wasted entirely as it rises and dissipates into the cold and vast antarctic sky. Seems like Hammond is running it day and night just to burn things for the sake of burning things. So odd that it wouldn't be in some kind of a mess tent where people can gather and efficiently get warm.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: First, I'll admit that I've been a fan of Bellular for a long time.Second, this game was a delightful way to spend my weekend. The game mechanics steer me towards caring about the characters of my crew. When mechanics encourage emotional investment in a narrative game, it's great. I had to make really tough decisions, and there were times when I truly felt the crew's frustration.I know I've only seen one possible ending (though all my crew survived), but I'm excited to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game. An interesting and immersive story. Simple but fun mechanics. An atmosphere of constant struggle to survive. Trying to strike a balance between the loyalty of your crew members and the difficult decisions necessary to survive. The perfect game for fans of victorian era and  exploratory expeditions. Steam engines and canned peaches, what more could you want?
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much heart for a story about desperate times and measures. Fans of Citizen Sleeper will find lots to like here, despite clear distinctions in their gameplay dynamics. Where Citizen Sleeper prevents you from getting 'trapped' in unwinnable situations, The Pale Beyond has no problem letting you spend hours on a doomed mission. It will often warn you about a Wrong Decision, but it rarely warns you twice, and these unwinnable runs can take a long time to resolve making it easy to feel like you wasted time with them. There are compelling narrative reasons for this, but you need to stick with the game for long enough to find them. So don't be afraid to reload from the start of the current week! I'd consider skipping this if that kind of play style doesn't gel with you, or if you have big triggers around animal death.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A diamond in the rough. At the time of this review, the game is plagued with bugs, UI issues, and unresponsive buttons. It's a testament to the strength of the narrative and the characters that I was willing to fight through the issues and play through to the end multiple times. The game soars in spite of its flaws, many of which I expect will be ameliorated in due time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, this scratched my banner saga itch in some ways, as I have been waiting on a new game from Stoic.  Pale Beyond blends an interesting combination of strategy and narrative intrigue.  While there are a few minor bugs to work out, it is nothing that effects game play in a meaningful way.  For the price tag this game offers quite a bit of replay-ability, and I am interested to see what a new ending will look like.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Point and click adventures learnt 30 years ago that having death conditions in narrative adventures was fundamentally moronic.No-one wants to play through hours of already seen footage in order to push past a poorly signposted event, or obtuse gameplay mechanic. Life is too short for that sort of tediousness.It's a lesson that "visual novels" (and how I hate that term, the only novels that are not visual are Braille) really do need to learn.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This has been a great game!  It is reminiscent to me of an Oregon Trail style game, but more detailed and more punishing.  I have yet to beat the game, but the challenge of surviving this arctic landscape shouldn't be simple.  Well made, smooth performing, and a lot of fun!!!  Also, the music and sound design are very good!  Well done, Bellular Gaming!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Having beaten this game on Hard I can say that was a very enjoyable experience.The gameplay while lacking in variety of what I should be keeping track of makes up for it for it's narrative - these characters were well written and the story had me hooked. Sure it can be a little text heavy and I realise some conversations can be ignored as they are "flavour text" but honestly I really liked how the crew sort of had their own discussions that were not connected to the plot, it gave me the sense that even the background characters had voices.I really liked the song in the game as well, the characters were all opinionated and not everyone seemed to agree with me which really gave me the sense of managing a crew like this. While I don't suggest you play like me and play nonstop until the end, I really do like how this game is different... the story is rich without being too excessive, I do wish there were voice acting as I think that's what this game lacked and the writing in this game made me surprised they didn't hire one!This is one of those games that came out of nowhere and gave me a day of enjoyment, I do think the gameplay could have been improved in areas and at the end the gameplay suddenly stopped to make room for the narrative but I think this is easily one of my favourite games narratively, the art is really good as well, as a casual game it's good. Though it can get slow in areas only because of how much talking there is... it's both a strength and weakness and although I would probably need to play the game again to fully understand the plot I do think this is a game that's worth playing to the end.It's rare I see a game this enjoyable by the characters alone that shanty is going to be stuck in my head a while. I honestly thought at the end my crew were dead but I somehow managed to survive with not enough firewood at the end - I'm not sure if they thought it was too hard at that point or what but I'll take the win it was challenging enough anyway!I might reinstall one day just to see the rest of the content, I just liked this game a lot, sort of a mix of frostpunk with narrative I could only dream of being in that game. It took a simple concept and ran with it, strangely enjoyable.Oh and yes: all my crew survived, I have a feeling I'm going to have to put myself through some depressing scenes to understand the rest of the plot though! I'll probably have to lower the difficulty to enjoy the rest properly though I think even with the difficulty lowered it'll be hard to get through in a different sense.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A very average Visual Novel about an expedition surviving a polar mission. I don’t feel like recommending an average game to othersDespite being average, the game is still fun, the art is pretty, the story is somewhat interesting and strategy part of the game is a little engaging.Why the game is average? The Survival mechanics are very simple, meaning you don’t need to put much thought in it. Also, there aren’t many choices that you take through the mechanics: for example, you gain more loyalty complimenting your crews member's shoes than by keeping the decorum high.As Visual Novel, the game doesn’t have interesting mechanics. Choices don’t matter, because there isn’t branching (except a small choice at the end).  If the developers wanted to create a master piece VN, this game needed branching plot where your choices change the overhaul narrative. Unfortunately, choices mostly only alter flavor text, which I find poor.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished it. and I am honestly really impressed.  The story is tight, the choices matter. When you start the journey, the crew are total strangers.  By then end, you know everyone's name by heart.It's not what you expect. It's not going to do what you expect. But it's really, really good.I have anxiety, is there anything I should worry about?
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a "meh" button.. because Im really 100% on the fence about this game.  Its VERY boring.  Seriously.  Unbelievably boring.  Run the same 4 actions every day... rinse, repeat.  Its only the 'events' that are ever actually any different.... and they are FAR too few and far between to keep the game interesting.  I just cant play it anymore.. its just not for me.  But the game 100% works, runs great, is simple to grasp in concept and design.. solid production.So because of that.. I'll give it a positive review.Mainly because compared to Blood Bowl 3... this game is legendary.#()$*& YOU CYANIDE GAMES!  You ruined Blood Bowl!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is a depressing visual novel disguised as a survival game.Most survival games include some sort of glimmer of success. The Pale Beyond is just a never-ending parade of awful, contrived situations. The food and fuel management is a bit nonsensical. Attempting to keep all of your crew happy means all of them are going to be unhappy.I played 5 hours of it, got through 80-90% of the game and won't be finishing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I know a lot of people got interested in this game because of Frostpunk, and I am here to tell you that it is... absolutely nothing like it. That being said, if you enjoyed the narrative/setting side of Frostpunk as much or more than the actual gameplay, you are going to love this game. Very well put together, narrative focused, almost a visual novel but with rescource/morale management. I can't speak for the quality of the story as a whole, as I have not yet finished it, but so far, the game's writing has been impressive. The visuals are also praiseworthy, as well as the whole presentation. I am very much looking forward to see the rest of the story unfold, but from what I have already seen, it seems extremely promising.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is a survival game which tells the story of a research expedition to the south pole. When the ship becomes trapped in the ice and the captain goes missing, the player must take command and keep the crew alive until rescue arrives.•	Manage scarce resources of food and fuel. Cutting rations will lower morale, but could be necessary to survive long term.•	Assign crew to tasks based on their specialisations. Engineers can maintain the furnace which is your only source of heat, scouts can search for areas of interest, sailors can gather supplies from the ship or hunt animals, and scientists can collect research or produce medical supplies. But there might not be enough crew to do everything, especially if someone is unavailable due to sickness, so you’ll often have to prioritise.•	The crew will come to you with special requests which you can approve or decline, and when they have disagreements with each other you can choose who to support. But your dialogue choices and decisions will have consequences for the safety and loyalty of the crew.•	There is permadeath, and various ways to lose crew members including frostbite, scurvy, and story events. The game autosaves at the start of each week, so if something goes horribly wrong you could go back and try again.•	I played on normal difficulty and I was close to keeping everybody alive, but one person died because three got frostbite at the same time and I could only treat two.•	Story is good and features many interesting characters. Sadly there is no voice acting, but I suppose this is understandable for a small indie game.•	It took me just over 10 hours to complete the story, which is good value for money at the normal purchase price.•	I didn’t notice any bugs or crashes.•	When you assign crew to a task, the effect is immediate and irreversible. I wish there had been a planning stage so that I could change things before confirming. There were a couple of times where I realised I needed a specialist to do a task that only they could perform, but I’d already assigned them to other general tasks that anybody can do. I had a spare crew member and it would have been simple to just swap them around, but instead I had to either accept the inefficiency, or reload the last save and start the week again.The Pale Beyond is an excellent game and I strongly recommend it to anybody who enjoys a good story where your choices have actual consequences.There are similarities to Frostpunk, This War of Mine, and Banner Saga, so I definitely think fans of those games would enjoy this.

The notable mentions are:- Navigation can bug out, I frequently had to reload the week to be able to navigate from place to place, it happens most often on the controller. - I managed to get myself stuck in a conversation unable to click the return option. - Once the interaction return option got stuck on the screen and persisted even in the main menu. - Replenishing the pot can also bug out making you enter it multiple times, as you'll be unable to assign multiple rations at a time. - Dog counter can also sometimes bug out indicating that dogs will be used for a given action and then proceed to not be used.- Once I managed to select both options at once, specifically during the holiday feast option. _childDocuments_.review: I'd give this a middling review if I could, but since most of the other reviews have been positive I'm going with the negative to highlight what I think are some shortcomings with the game.To be clear where I'm coming from, I love hardcore survival games, and I'm mostly into the mechanics of games like this rather than the story. I'm big on games like Dead in Bermuda, Dead in Vinland, Frostpunk, etc, and I bought this game because it looked like it was in a similar vein. My biggest criticism of the game is that it largely sacrifices a focus on the survival mechanics for its narrative. So, if you're okay with that, then disregard the negative rating, because the game is nicely polished, has a good story, and interesting characters.It's just that it never really lets you get into the survival aspect of things. It wasn't much of a challenge on normal. There were no really difficult decisions I had to make and I finished the game with everyone but two people surviving. These died during narrative choices. Resource management didn't represent much of a challenge and you never really get a chance to establish yourself, because the game keeps moving you onwards to new camps, which don't really represent any new challenges but just give you more of the same. It's really one of those games that gives you a veneer of survival mechanics, but you can tell that there hasn't been heaps of thought into giving them the depth that other games in that vein do. These games are all about their balance and the tough emergent trade-offs that you get presented with, requiring difficult decisions, and I felt that this was largely lacking from the game.Having said that, the story is nice, and it was a pretty fun little playthrough. So, I would say if you're looking for a legit survival experience, this is probably not worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Having watched Bellular for years, I'm keen to see how his passion for story and player driven games translates into this. Music is astoundingly beautiful and appropriate. _childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Story - Immersive and well told. You care about the mission, the characters, their fatesVisuals - Beautiful visuals despite the bleak environment the game takes place inGame play - Point and click survival/resource management. I love worker placement board games (like Agricola) and this is basically a single player story driven version of it. Has a decent amount of difficulty but can be optimized pretty quickly. Most of the difficulty comes from if you care to keep everyone/specific people alive and well. Cons:Some annoying (but not game breaking) bugs - Mostly with food and fuel adding. It's annoying to keep opening and closing the menu when it glitches.Save/Load system - It's interesting and for a story with branching decisions like this I see what they wanted from it. Ultimately it has potential but I think it needed some more refinement. Last 10% of the game -  Almost entirely story with not much game play. You have some decisions and last chances to influence the crew but the tension kinda falls away once the survival game play is gone. For some people one of the main endings will land and for others it won't. It worked well enough for me but it's definitely out of left field and I get why it won't land for everyone.All in all enjoyable. After about 14 hours of playing I have 5 of the story branches done. I may toss it around for a couple more hours to get new endings but I imagine it'd take another 6 hours or so to 100% for all the different branches. I recommend it for anyone that enjoys the more relaxed pace of a point and click style. Also to prepare you ahead of time, expeditions like the one in this game always have loss involved. Even a "perfect" play through will make you sad at certain things so go into it prepared for that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for a while through development and was very excited for release!I like to play these kinds of games with a controller and on release there were a few bugs and clunky controls that made me put it down. Kudos to the developers for being so responsive to the community with updates and fixes :D Picked it up again a few weeks after release and everything played great!Having played through once now, if you're on the fence just go for it, this game is well worth the play through. Characters are great and well written. I LOVE how disposition with the different characters isn't as simple as "be nice." Each character responds to your manner differently, some of them want you to be a smartass to them haha, which really makes them feel real and builds an emotional connection. Speaking of emotions... . Between the art style, strong characters, great narrative, and responsive devs, I recommend this game to any fans of the genre or those just looking for some good old indie game fun :)I am very much looking forward to what these devs do next on this game and any future games they make!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of feelings and a lot of words for this game, however short it may be. It has its mechanical flaws what with the food and coal system being quite un-reasonable if you want to succeed, but that's as far as the issues go.The art, the music, the characters, oh the characters. You don't want to make them sad because they feel so real, the consequences are not just that you lose loyalty with them, it's that you *disappoint them*. Very few game have truly captured the feeling of a "found family" story as well as this has, and I truly applaud the developers. If you want a touching, rough story about a crew that made it through the frozen hell, I implore you to play this game to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I had played the demo for 2 hours, and thought that it would be worth to buy the full game since I had enjoyed what I experienced, despite some minor annoyances. _childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A little too slow for me, the game meanders a lot and the dialogue choices feel extremely unnecessary a lot of the time, mostly just existing for flavor but then sometimes they'll have mechanical impacts which can be jarring. _childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It is worth its value especially if it's in steam discounts. I would seriously suggest anyone likes the challenge of survival in dire conditions. Had finished in 1 situp around 8,5 hrs. ***The game starts in the epilogue as you are being drafted as the 1st mate of the ship for a dangerous expedition to the South Pole. Your vessel is a ship with sails and a locomotive engine applied steam ship mix. There are three major resources, morale, food, and resources for the steam engine.  Also, a substantial importance is the crew loyalty, you are going to need them loyal to you so being a patient captain pays off.I played with normal difficulty and only loaded twice  near the end-game had a perfect run so wanted to keep it that way I suggest all finish the game first then try the Adam & Eve scenario. Well, to keep it unspoiled this is all I can say.It's a solid one, feels a bit like an expedition in side quests of Frost Punk or a piece of Jules Verne's novel. Keeping count on resources is important  but the catch is you can't realize the specific significance of those in your first run.For first-time runners: Get as much as from the ship, so you can keep your options fine at the end-game.I also really liked the end-game theatrics, I kept my entire crew alive so could see their decisions after the expedition and it was a nice touch.Beware, your dialogues with them affect their after-expedition plans ^^I only need to run back from the point where I  and need to fix something that will spice up the end.Make sure you won't miss this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A game id recommend to anyone. Beautiful artwork and music. With characters that are very unique in their own right. Every choice you make will effect your outcome and who lives or dies. and the overall story. The journey is difficult, but if you can make it to the end in tact with your crew and their loyalty, Its so rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Man I love indie games. And this game is RIGHT up my lane. The wonderful thing about waist deep in indie games for over ten years is you start to see how they influence each other. This game is like a combination of Banner Saga, Frostpunk, and Citizen Sleeper. It takes the best elements of those games and rolls them up into a scrumptious penguin and peaches burrito. (better than it sounds when you're starving...)The game devs had the genius idea of making every single member of your crew an actual person. Each with backstory and personality, some of these characters are great. I was very invested in getting them home, I pretty much couldn't put it down and only didn't beat it in a single day because I was incredibly tired. I cared about all the characters and felt some genuine swells of emotions or heavy-hearted moments in the game. There's one part in particular that actually had me cry.It balances its punishment and reward pretty well. I did have to reload SEVERAL times to get ending I wanted, and I never felt the game was being to unfair, just challenging. I also really liked the music and the art. It's amazing that a indie game like this can manage to have more character portraits to captivate emotions and feeling of the characters than some big budget games that have like one character artwork for each character for the whole game that slightly changes the facial expression. Anyway, a great game. Really recommend it if you like resource management and visual novels.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really atmospheric, enjoyable game - feels like a blend of Frostpunk and Sunless Seas/Skies. While it feels very challenging to manage all your resources, I found at the end (on normal difficulty) I ended up supplies to spare and no one dead, so I think it does a good job of feeling more demanding than it actually is - it feels very tense & high stakes, but it's not so punishing that you as a player feel hopeless.Ultimately I finished the campaign in just under 9 hours, and other than some variation at the end I don't think there's a huge amount of replayability, so would probably recommend buying on sale. But definitely recommending!Stanberry for Captain <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something speciel. It creates a world and then envelops you in it, forcing you to care for its character without you even noticing, making you invested in each one of them and their perception of you. That is something i have rarely felt in a game. That said, when i played though it, it has some annoying bugs, mostly in a couple of choices not being reflected in the graphics while being reflected in the gameplay or the other way around. The gameplay is nice, its not revolutionary or anything like that, but you don't get tired of it. Which i do a bit too often in some story-focused games. It creates some great/horrible choices that you have to make. Lastly, just when you think the game cant throw anymore at you it of course find a away to do so. And the best thing is, that these events never feel forced. They feel realistic, they feel real.All in all its an amazing game that i can only recommend, but i suggest waiting 2 weeks getting it, such that some of the bugs are fixed (a lot have already been fixed). I will certainly explore more routes of this game after waiting a week, just so that the amazing game that this is, is not damaged but the existing bugs.(edit):they have fixed the bugs and added and epilogue which is quite nice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game, is not really for me. But, for people this game is for, it's perfect!If you're a fan of story, tough decisions and good art over good graphics. Then this game is for you. Don't get me wrong, the graphics are great for what they're going for. But, well, you know what I mean. The art is great. Everything feels and looks exactly how it's supposed to look. Above deck is cold, harsh, unforgiving, below deck is warm, cosy, but cramped. Off the ship you're facing cold, scary, dark. The developers are super cool and even have an industry news channel on youtube (Bellular News) definitely check them out! They're a lot more than just Bellular, they have a lovely team of friendly people who deserve praise for this game. They've been working on patches to fix bugs that they weren't aware of before release.My play time is fairly low. I played the demo a lot more.I just wanted to support the developers. I've been a fan of Bellular news / gaming for years. Huge love to you guys, you deserve all the love this game is getting!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I’m going to be a bit vague because playing this game without knowing anything about it is quite the experience. The Pale Beyond has an extraordinary narrative that will capture your imagination and curiosity. The overall story is fascinating. It can feel very harrowing and tense but also wondrous. You really appreciate the calmer times. It has a whole cast of interesting characters. Getting to know the crew is a very satisfying experience and an absolute highlight for me was making connections with each one of them. I wish I could just ramble about each one of them and why I like them but that would spoil surprises. It is a challenging resource management with tough choices. The art is stunning; the environment is enchanting, the characters are charming, menu design is thematic. The music is gorgeous and immersive. This game tells a great story that would be a shame to miss out on. More accordion, specifically more Grimley songs please and thankyou.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: An eloquently interwoven narrative, with such effective resource management that it succeeds in more ways than as a visual novel.  I'm surprised at how much variation there is in individual events ("taking requests" in-game) and how well they translate into consequences.  I'm also surprised at how clearly I see my past decisions get integrated into text much later.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Normally i don't really like survival type games, in general they are leaning to much in one of the directions meaning ether you have to focus on survival and story is flying by or the survival aspect is almost non existent. this game managed to surprise me with surprisingly engaging story that keeps you engaged for the whole journey with a surprising turns when you think your arse is safe and sound. additionally the save system is ingenious locking your decisions and making you stuck with them for better or worse with a nice touch of showing you the different tree branch when you really botched the story to show you where you went wrong for the entire play-thou. but does not punish you in the way to restart the whole game, just an act.10/10 story telling: brilliant story, engaging characters, spectacular turns.8/10 survival: haven't seen much purpose in some mechanics such as "research"
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: When I sat down to write this review I really didn't know if I was going to recommend the game or not. While I had fun playing it, I only logged 6 hours into my play through and for $20 that isn't a good deal at all. Still, I felt this game could be worth a recommend, until I started writing the cons. You'll see what I mean below.PROS-The artwork is fantastic-Music and original songs are great-Story is interesting-Writing is terrificCONS-There's not much to the survival aspect of the game other than keeping your crew warm, fed, and sane. It's a pretty shallow system that doesn't involve much thought. However, if you start to get behind on food and fuel, you'll find yourself suffering more and more each week that passes. I found that by Act 3-4 my decorum (resource that represents the crew's overall mental state) was always in the danger zone. You can run out of food or fuel and you won't fail the game, but if your decorum reaches zero you lose. If you find yourself failing due to decorum loss you have to reload pretty far back to be able to overcome the lack of decorum, as it's a resource that can quickly drain and is hard to increase, especially later in the game. Having to reload a save from 4-5 weeks ago and replay everything that already happened is not very fun and is more a pain than anything.-I'd have preferred a system where if decorum reached zero there would be a mutiny attempt or a character would go crazy and do something rash. Instead, you just get a game over screen. I can't help but feel that the decorum resource is a terrible replacement for actual consequences to your decisions.-Most issues you must deal with as captain don't really feel that important or have that much meaning in the grand scheme of things. For example, there's a part where SPOILERS: -A single play through took me 6 hours and that is with loading a previous save to try the alternative ending-Some parts of the story make little sense such as SPOILERS: -Convincing the crew to remain loyal to you wasn't difficult at all and the loyalty system only really matters during the VERY end of the game after everything is finished. The correct dialogue choices were pretty obvious for each main character to increase their loyalty and the only person I couldn't convince by the end was Grimley, but he's designed to be a constant adversary. If there was a forced vote for a new captain midway through the game the loyalty system would be more important, but it's a complete waste of time to care what each person thinks. You could go the whole game and piss off everyone and it doesn’t matter.I had just recently finished reading The Worst Journey in the World, which is the memoir of Apsley Cherry-Garrard who was one of the three surviving members of the ill fated Terra Nova Expedition to the South Pole from 1910 - 1913. I was hoping this game would provide me with an experience similar to the one I read about. Unfortunately this game didn’t come close to that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Never before has a game left me this speechless before. I have genuine love and care for each of these characters, the music sets the mood wonderfully. The art style alone is reason enough to enjoy this game. The integration of story and game play elements is phenomenal. The ONLY complaint I have is there is some finicky business in the save menu but that will most likely get patched soon.I love getting scurvy, 10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend it enough. If what you see on the store page appeals to you, just do yourself a favor and buy the game. Nothing since has scratched that particular itch for adventure for me - until The Pale Beyond, that is. This feeling is just not something that could ever be priced. Thank you for all those involved in the making of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining game. Writing is good, characters are good, music is good, art is good. The game makes you care about the characters and their well-being.The resource management is a bit simple yet remains interesting. I have a couple minor issues with the tutorials being kind of weird, but it's mostly nitpicking.It does fail to stick the landing and the endings feel rushed, but beyond that I would recommend it. _childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoy tough Frostpunk-esque management? Like visual novels with choices and consequences? This game is a fantastic blend of both. Pure pressure with great relief afterwards, a wonderful story with a handful of temptations. I also fell in love with the art style, it has a fairytale charm despite the rather dark plot.Don't hesitate to rewind the saves if you get stuck, but don't try to make the run perfect, this game is meant to push you to the edge every single time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A great first entry for Bellular Studios, they've presented a very intimate and intriguing story within a survival resource management game. It plays well but is rather tough, I felt like some of the negative decorum stats mid-way through just pile on and were too harsh after a few plot points. I know you can turn off decorum endings in the settings but that removes a level of the strategy that makes the game more interesting to manage. It would have been nice to have a few settings to toggle between for those who still want a challenge or allow for minus decorum for a week or two so the player can work on raising it rather than an instant ending. I only really struggle with this at main crisis points in the story.Overall I really enjoyed my first playthrough, the characters were memorable (which i didn't expect from a management game like this), the world lore was engaging, the gameplay mechanics and the interactive cycle were enjoyable. I can't wait to see what Bellular Studios do next and I would like to see some of these characters again in the future. Hopefully more adventures await! Until then I'll be checking the other endings and playing some of the other paths.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I came to The Pale Beyond with mixed feelings, as a fan of Frostpunk, I felt it is a rip off from that franchise. But I gave it a try.And I have been taken on a wonderful journey that changed my heart.Of course in it's core it is frozen land, survival, population management game.However in contrast to FP it has a very rich story and characters that you actually start caring about after few cold weeks.Game mechanics are simpler than those in FP, just two resources to gather - food and fuel, there is no building aspect except for few quest driven events. On top of that health and loyalty of crew are additional variables.Locations and environment is gorgeous, the effect of time passing on equipment, clothes is nicely displayed.Background music helps with immersion and I can only applaud it's choice.I have spent ~30 hours in two playthroughs and I can say that despite of numerous bugs that I have encountered, it was money well spent and I have no regrets.Pros:- Lightweight ice survival game- Great story- Deep character development- Decent level of choices to be made- Game feels fresh in the genreCons:- BUGS   - version 1.2.2 still has a critical bug that sometimes prevents crew member to he put into medical treatment   - other UI bugs with adding resources to stove and fireplace - not game breaking just annoying   - frequent UI issue with location/person action icons not active due to zoom or panning   - UI issues incorrectly displaying resource addition or usage (UI only not affecting true amount of resources)- Ability to branch out before completing at least a single playthrough makes it too easy in the challenge- Only one difficulty level which is too easy for this genre veteransOverall it is a very good game and especially taking into the account that it was developed by a fresh indie studio.Once defects are squashed, UI improvements done this would be a solid 85/100 game in my books.I'd like to see multiple difficulty levels added and some DLCs that add different quests into the main story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been able to fill a void I was looking to fill for a long time. Frankly I always struggled with management type games, as they failed to keep me engaged because purely the managing aspect was not enough.I always preferred heavily choice based RPGs.The Pale Beyond managed to hook with its atmosphere and story from the first few minutes. Then it also let me discover how the management part works, without the annoying tutorials I encountered in other games. Then it kept me on my toes and guessing with all the events that started unfolding. The characters feel very real and excellently written, the art style is beautiful, the music is not too intrusive and goes well with the game.I have been unable to step playing it in the past few hours. So far it is a 10/10 and it also seems to be really replayable which I love.Thank you for this great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good but confusing game. I was gifted this by family as a gift from my wish list (it looked like if I got it from a company I dont need to check the box, but its unclear). I struggled with some of the mechanics of the game, for example, repairing the tent happens after food and requests, leading to frustrating "gatcha" moments with frostbite and death. But this is my only negative report. The story is compelling, the tone shifts like the ice and sea itself. Though you can memorize outcomes and get the ending you want. For a few hours, the Pale Beyond is a game that grips you like frostbite and holds on like solid adventure novel would. The motivation of the people you work with are filled with variety. I would love to see this game and game style with its art and direction and creators, become like a Poirot style mystery novel, or a Victorian political intrigue simulation, where the kingdom needs balance to face a greater threat, kind of like Dragon Commander was. (If you need a good idea fairy I am excellent at that.)

_childDocuments_.review: I want to mention that I haven't finished the story yet, but there have been some really silly design issues which already make me want to ward others away. I'll start on the positive: If you want to play this game, it will almost certainly be for the story. The crew are interesting, and the general tale of survival and kinship is great. I don't doubt that the ending will be some mix of heartbreaking and heroic, and will make subsequent runs all the more interesting. That said, I'm still not 100% sure if what I'm seeing here is 'a game of interesting decisions where you try to balance discipline against kindness, or comfort against survival, etc...', or if it's a game where there's one true path to success and the only way you get there is by knocking your head against a wall until you find the one solution that gets everyone home alive and happy with you. That said, the reason this game is a no for recommendations is: - Sometimes the chapter just moves ahead. Without spoiling anything, I think the ideal set up is where you gather the resources you need, you attend to the needs of the day, and then with everything squared; you proceed onto the next day/ week. Sometimes I found that I advanced the plot (I'm looking at you boiler room incident #1) when I meant to go do X first. I'm fine with the story forcing you forward uncomfortably, but there's a difference between 'You have 60 seconds, what are you going to grab first?' vs. 'Hey, you better not touch that thing before you've grabbed everything or I'm kicking you out of the room'.- At the end of every period, you are asked to determine how much fuel or food you wish to dole out. If you try to provide more fuel or food than you have, you can't advance to the next chapter (which makes perfect sense); however the game doesn't really indicate why that is. The button just greys itself out and while you figure this out for yourself fairly quickly; it feels a little odd to sit at a screen wondering why you can't advance anything with no way to go backwards. - I dislike the map function of going back and forth between weeks. When you decide to look at the map, you can (if you'd like), flip the dates back and forth. This gives you an idea of where you were before, and you can flip forward to get back to where you are presently. However, the only way to exit the map is to go back to the present day and select the ship icon which just feels like a design oversight? Why can't I just put down the map? Why this weird navigation? Again; you'll figure this out fairly quickly for yourself but it's just another cumbersome thing to dodge around when you're trying it out for the first time. - I'll confess that I may be 100% wrong with this, but I was under the impression that the ship's journalist wanted to interview everyone. Very cool little minigame where you can build up your ship's morale meter, at the expense of dedicating someone to a non-task. However, there is no way to tell who she's interviewed before vs. who is left to interview. Maybe it doesn't actually matter if she's interviewed everyone, but if that is a thing; it'd be nice to be able to tell who's yet to be interviewed vs. not.- I think something might not be working right when it comes to assigning crew. For the first several weeks, I couldn't assign my wounded crew members to be healed (but it started working mysteriously later on for no apparent reason). At one point, one of my crew members became a specialist which meant I couldn't assign them to anything (including the medbay to get healed which became a problem when they got ill). - I shouldn't be able to use the ship's medicine stores if there's nobody in the medical bay to heal. With the game only running saves at the start of the week, I was a little annoyed that I'd accidentally used up my medicine on an empty bay (a misclick on my part), which again feels like one of those simple things that could've been countered with just a little more forethought. So yeah... There's probably a great story here, and I'll likely just go look up a walkthrough or a wiki to see how the game properly plays out, but I'm kinda fed up with the 'gotchas' (whether they're timing/ pacing related, or interface related).
