_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed playing the Pale Beyond, it's a very different game to anything I've played before. From it's wonderful art and sound design to it's compelling story and survival mechanics I really felt like I was Captain during an arctic expedition, and despite it being 2D and the camera being somewhat far away from the action I really felt immersed, which is an incredible achievement. From what I can tell decisions early on in the game can really impact your journey through it, I spoke to friends and found it really interesting that characters that really liked them really hated me! I was astounded at the end when I saw just how small the team was, and very pleased to see that the updates keep on rolling out, I bought the game as soon as it was released and didn't personally come across any bugs but it's clear that the quality of the game is really important to the team as they continue to make improvements and seem to really respond to the feedback given even having a discord set up to have a direct line to them, really shows how much the care about creating something special and engaging with the community.As previously mentioned the Pale Beyond is quite unlike anything I've personally played before, the closest would probably be Papers Please, but I am a huge fan of the Long Dark and I think there's something poetic about being trapped in the ice/snow, sometimes in life it can feel like we ourselves are trapped and have to forge ahead to survive and there are so many lessons in The Pale Beyond about choices. The most obvious choice isn't always the right one, the safer sounding path may actually lead to danger and the risky path may lead to salvation, sometimes being direct is better than being cautious.If you're a fan of games that make you think and maybe teach you something about yourself along the way (not to mention the many interesting facts about arctic expeditions) then this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: First - game have cute graphics and interesting story but it itsn't a quest, it's a proper resource management game.Reasons why I don't recommend this game now (26 Feb):It doesn't allow you to save at any moment of game - and yet it not like a hardcore one-savefile-for-all. While you can have multiple saves they'd done automatically at beginning of next week - and you don't allowed to load any save but latest one (until you will delete it). Yes, you need to do extra actions to delete those saves if want replay previous week or a few weeks at once. I could understand hardcore rogue-like system but this one is a source of pure annoyance as meaningless mix between hardcore and casual save systems.I really want to give a ticket on Temperance to designer of it >_<At Week2 we are introduced to resource system and begin to waste our resources even during a safe&happy sailing. Yes, your best move is to cut rations at game start. No, there is no roleplaying reasons to do it.There is a no logic here but providing a starting penalty for a new player and advantage for experienced one. Crazy design #2 >_<Aside from UI&resource ones game is still having bugged saves after a Day0 patch. Currently (1.2.2) wounded crew is corrupted in savefile and after loading - unable to get into Med Bay for healing. That's efficiently broken my new game at Week4.Sorry devs, but after my very @#$% experience with another game - I have zero tolerance for bugs with save/load system that block you from completing the game. Anything but this.P.S. Also music isn't consistent with sudden bursts of loudness but it's a very minor flaw.

_childDocuments_.review: A shame I have to give this a thumbs down, there are good gameplay ideas and some very decent writing; the characters are distinct and the art is surprisingly solid for a low budget title.The problem is that the story arc is very clumsily put together in an attempt to force you down the intended path. You're often presented with the illusion of multiple options or choices when there is only one that doesn't end in total disaster, sort of like those old Choose Your Own Adventure books where you just turn to a page and it says "The End". Only in this game, the surprise "The End" comes after an hour of clicking through story text and micromanaging eight ship resources to make sure you live through the night. Oh well, guess you better reload that last save and do it all again but say "yes" instead of "no" to Templeton this time!Just too much NPE and frustration to be worth your time, which is a shame because it had a lot going for it.Edit: After some more play I discovered that the game forces you to murder dogs. Please, google it, you literally can not avoid this game path and are actually shown an image of your character pointing a rifle in a dog's face then forced to acknowledge that you choose to pull the trigger.Naturally, not having been warned in any fashion that I would be forced to murder dogs in the game, I posted my dissatisfaction with that fact in the forum. I was told by the developer that the "real expedition" this game is based on had to shoot their dogs. I asked if the real expedition also had a magic tree with time-travel fruit, as this game does. Obviously, this was an attempt to point out that the comment seemed like a cop-out. The developer has not kept particularly close to the real history, and they have clearly CHOSEN to include the scene of animal abuse. I was then permanently banned by the developer. I was a little shocked but with just a small amount of research I found that apparently this is a common response by the developer any time someone is vocal about not liking some aspect of their game.AVOID THIS GAME. The way it railroads you down its narrative is lazy, it forces you to abuse animals (!!), and the developers are actively trying to stifle community response. I strongly recommend you do not give this developer your money.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot of fun, great narrative and atmosphere. However there are some criticisms i have in regards to the general design and play experience. I'll give a bullet list and then go in depth on some problems i had.Pros:- Great storytelling- Very nice atmosphere- Fun survival managementCons:- A lot of clicking through repeated dialog, could use a skip or fast-forward for parts you've already done (EDIT: patch 1.2.2.0.0 Fixes this as you can hold ctrl key to fast forward dialog)- A branching decision tree type load system that doesn't work with the survival mechanics and isn't focused around clear 'decision points'- Research points.. they don't do anything.- A few UI bugs outstandingSo to talk over the cons listed. I found that my experience was that i played my first run, got game-overed a couple of hours in, and then had to start from the beginning because my issue wasn't any one particular decision made, but rather just not having known how to optimise resources from the beginning. This meant that i had to click through a huge amount of text that i'd already seen just to reassign some rations differently next time. From what I've seen this is a common issue, and leads into the other major criticism i have. The game uses a branching system for loading your save, the implication being that these points are where you can make different decisions to effect your run. BUT, that's not really how this game works at all. Being a survival game the major thing you're fighting is gradual erosion of your supplies or loss of crew, and that isn't an easy load back to fix. This usually means that in case of a game over you have to load a long way back and not just to the last "decision point". This combined with the fact that there aren't really branching narratives so much as a couple of different but very similar outcomes towards the end mean that your decision tree is just one or two game overs and then a straight line to finish once you learn how to optimise resources. Not only that but because the game doesn't really have much in the way of a branching narrative there really isn't any motivation to come back and try something different at certain points either as you'd be clicking through so much repeated dialog until either hitting a game over or reaching the ending.Finally the research points are inconsequential, I've asked around and it seems they give you a +1 to a specific dialog ONLY if you don't have enough loyalty, making them almost entirely meaningless in the game. This is rather silly given that they require allocating workers and sacrificing resources to obtain, and are never really clearly explained.Ultimately i really like the game, but i think the branching load system was a bad design choice, and exists purely for the sake of metaphor (somewhat ironically). The core survival system and narrative are very fun, but include some weird additions like research points, and game overs unfortunately make it so you end up having to repeat huge segments of text until you're no longer having fun. All love to the devs and definitely not trying to be a negative nancy, but thought i'd express my honest thoughts.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is the kind of game that will make you forget about everything else in your life. Seriously, I started playing it and before I knew it, four hours had passed. It's the kind of game that sucks you in with its amazing story and characters, and before you know it, you're living and breathing in its world. I went into the game wondering who I was and who I wanted to be, and by the end, I was a fully-immersed badass leader making decisions that felt like they had real weight.One thing I loved about The Pale Beyond was that each decision I made felt like it had a real impact on the story. I was constantly on edge, wondering if my choices would lead to success or failure. But that's what made the game so great - it was never predictable. Just when I thought I had it all figured out, something would happen that would throw me off and make me question everything.The characters in The Pale Beyond were excellently written and felt very real. I found myself getting emotionally invested in their stories and wanting to keep them all alive. And speaking of alive, I must be a natural born leader because I managed to keep everyone alive (although there were a few close calls). But even if you're not a great leader, you'll still love this game. It's not overly difficult, but it's not a walk in the park either. It strikes the perfect balance between challenging and fun.There were a few minor bugs when I played the game, but they didn't detract from the overall experience. And honestly, the bugs were a small price to pay for the joy I felt playing this game. I'm already planning on playing it again to see what happens if I take some riskier choices. It's worth every penny, unless you're someone who doesn't like amazing stories, engaging characters, and fun gameplay.

Not to draw comparisons, it's just the only other game of this type that I have played.Survive by managing resources and morale, but this is more personal, you have to manage people, people who you talk to and get to know. Making decisions, hard and easy and handle the many surprises you will face.I love the atmosphere, the music. Snow, Ice, Blizzards, the unkown, I am all about that. Also the warmth of certain places, people, things and sounds, nailed. Incredibly drawn characters too, even just looking at them is nice.It got really emotional towards the end (all depending on choices of course). Especially . It got me very invested in them and I chose to go for That was all for the review part, now I'd like to provide some feedback, some scattered thoughts and things I'd like to see that would also improve the experience in my opinion.First about the . There have been some bugs with it, like hovering over a crew member (I think it always happened with the 1st one up left) not displaying them, but the last one shown. I feel they are too closely intertwined, sometimes I'd just like to ask someone something, but often there is the fear that it will rub them wrong and you will lose loyalty. This had me a bit confused at the midpoint of the game. But I reached a week in the winter where there was no way to not lose and had to disable decorum game overs because I would have to rewind back a lot to change this.I'd like to see a sort of  ingame, explaining each mechanic clearly. _childDocuments_.review: This is a solid adventure romp. Not everybody will be happy.But you are the leader.

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating journey. Truth be told, there isn't much "game" to be had in this title, but the writing is excellent. A largely visual novel, that does a great job of getting you invested into the story and the characters. You'll be forced to make some tough choices and the story can take quite diverse paths as a result.Somewhat unfortunately, the game did not prove particularly challenging. Starting with the "hard" difficulty, I only failed once in my first run as I was still learning the survival mechanics. My second run ended up being perfect. Full crew survival, full loyalty. With plenty of every resource and reputation to spare. After which, the only things left to do, would be to try out some alternative ending choices.Still, despite the somewhat short length of the game, the price is perfectly in line with it. 10-20 hours is a solid amount of fun to be had and I do not regret it. I grew quite attached to my crew.I would recommend the game to everyone who enjoys visual novels and an interesting survival story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game left me shocked. I DON'T PLAY games like this, but for some reason... this one hit right. I think it's mostly due to the atmosphere, sound, visuals, and characters bringing a level of immersion I haven't experienced in a game before. Three hours in I found myself drinking coffee and tea because I FELT COLD. When I lost my first crew member.., failed my first crew member, I instinctively had a moment of silence. I honestly can't remember the last time I was so attached and invested in the characters. Yes, there are bugs (the only one I ran into was one that kept me from clicking multiple items. Exiting and entering the menu fixed it) but where this game shines is in world building and narrative. If you want a solid story that will stick with you days after... maybe give this a go.Like I said... don't play games like this so here is a quick break down I wish I knew before hand.Gameplay loop is this.1. Crew wakes up and you sit down at your desk to handle issues they have or entertain suggestions on the direction of the expedition. Choices can mean more or less resources, gaining or loosing faction loyalty/crew sanity or causing the entire crew to die. Decisions have a lot of weight...2. Mid morning: You assign tasks for the day. Put crew members on scouting/hunting, research, sick bay, the furnace to cure freezing, etc.3. Night time: Tell the crew to have dinner. Go around the camp and check in with story characters. Learn their stories, gain or lose their loyalty and make decisions that will impact their lives on an individual level... mostly.4. End the week by allocating how much fuel goes to the furnace to keep members warm while not running out for future weeks. Same with food and hunger. Rationing can cause freezing, malnutrition and lower moral.That's the whole game. The gameplay loop feels like a day but is represented in game as a week.Overall I freaking loved it. Ended up not sleeping till 5am the first night I had it.... Not proud of that, but damn this was a ride. I recommend, but it wont be for everyone.I did beat the game and wow... the ending was something else. Perfectly fits in with the concept of the game itself. If this is what I can expect as this company's first game... can't wait for them to take my money on the next one.

_childDocuments_.review: A great feel-bad simulator! This game is depressing as all heck, frustrating, and just outright hostile. That said, it's a good dive into desperation and resource management. Barely made it halfway through on my first run, but learned plenty for next time. The characters are interesting and they don't all just *love* the protagonist like in so many games. All that being said, there are still some visual bugs that I've noticed. A few subtle spelling errors, your resource counters (specifically dogs) behaving erratically, and some text boxes that look out of place by touching or overlapping each other. Nothing mechanical or gamebreaking so far, but hopefully the visual bugs get a touch up soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially didn't have much faith in this game, and bought it because Bellullar made it and wanted to support him, and was curious about the game he chose to make. After 2 failures on the ice I have to say, buy this game. There are a couple of bugs that make things annoying, but not broken, but even those do not take away from the game play which is brilliant.Lets start off with the cons, as there aren't as many:1) there is seemingly a bug that keeps me from adding more than one of an item to the boiler, or food pot. So when there is a stack of item, such as seals, or even bags of coal the game makes me add them one at a time, instead of multiples. And I don't mean in one add slot, it makes me add one, then the choice to add more disappears and I have to submit those to be burned or cooked, then go back in and add more. Not game breaking, just annoying.2) This may be on me, but I have no idea how the crew feels about me at any given time. There are times where I can talk so someone and lose 5 favor, and now they dislike me, and then the next week get 20 positive with them and maybe they will like me again. It seems very arbitrary at times, I wish I could have a menu to see where I stand with the crew.3) There is one point where a holiday shows up, and if you don't have just enough food left in the pot from the previous week you can't celebrate it. That's all fine, but in the dialogue that follows it says that I refused to let the party happen, when I totally wanted it to but didn't have enough food so it wouldn't let me choose that option. So I get negative feedback for something I have no control of. Which is ok for this survival game, but the wording of the character makes it seem like it was a hard no, even when i checked the soft no with a reason that there wasn't any food for it.That's about it for negatives. Now for positives:1) The player character is brilliant. Where most games have a create character front loaded into the game, not so with The Pale Beyond, the protagonist evolves with the story, and their backstory is created whenever you choose to interact. Are you married with children, you can be if you want, or you can be single and alone. A soldier that's killed before or a sailor that hasn't, the choices that you make to build up your own lore are great, and not just some random menu at game start.2) The characters are great. As you adventure with the crew all of the backstory and connections that happen organically make sense. The characters in Pale Beyond have lives and hopes and dreams, to go with their skeletons and nightmares. Even with 2 play troughs I don't know everything about the crew, and that makes me want to learn more.3) Replay is amazing. As you go through the game and make choices you soon see the consequences and file that information away so next time maybe that won't happen. I haven't made it through a positive game yet, with failure always my nemesis, but the two were very different play troughs. 4) The Pale Beyond is hard. I love that about it. It isn't some choose your own adventure that has a good or bad ending when you get to the end. This game makes you work to get as far as you can, and the struggle is so real as you try to last for rescue. I really feel like a struggling captain in a bad situation that nobody was prepared for, and ultimately when I fail It does not make me want to rage quit, it makes me want to analyze my path, see what I could do better, see who I can support more. And then the next time is a little easier but not cakewalk, its always hard. You feel the crews anxiety so well because of the difficulty.8/10 would recommend this game to anyone that was curious. I can't wait to see the next game this studio puts out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Would recommend for all the choose your own story folk. Some UI bugs exists and some gameplay glitches. I had a glitch where the game forced me to give an eulogy for all the fallen crew members but I didn’t have any casualties. But generally, none of the bug were gamebreaking nor kept me from wanting to keep playing. WOULD BE AMAZING IF IT HAD VOICE ACTING!! The game is quite well balanced although I would like a sandbox mode with harder difficulty. Also wish there was an epilogue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is a great game. The gameplay is similar to Help Will Come Tomorrow / Dead In Bermuda, but more varied and more suitable to role playing purposes (less focus on a perfect outcome). There's a heavy focus on narrative, and the personality of each crew member was clearly a consideration during development. Some of the interactions are optional, but add a lot to the story. The ending is rather abrupt and suffers from too much exposition, which made some of the choices weak (but not all of them!). The epiloque however more than compensates for this and makes this game just so damn good. Perspectives matter and can change, depending on your choices.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Summed up in one word....'Oof'. This game is a beautiful and harsh game. No matter what you do at least one person will die...probably more during your first and maybe even second/third play-through. The story is amazing and well paced; you want to keep these people alive despite the environment fighting back with everything it has.Good luck out there in The Pale Beyond!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: While I have experienced a few minor bugs, one of them requiring me to load to a previous state, the game experience more than makes up for it's small blemishes. Every time I boot up Pale Beyond I sink into my chair and cozy up for a few hours of intense decision making. While this game has been promoted like an rpg with the vibes of Frostpunk, I think a better game play comparison would be to that of Pentiment. Both are narrative driven, choices-matter, role playing story book games with delightful 2d art and emphasize tone and careful planning of a limited set of time based on a clock. One is set in 16th Century Bavaria, while the other is an isolated crew in the ice-caps. Just as in Pentiment, The characters, art, and authenticity are the real stars of this game. I end up finding the game's reference tools for the crew very helpful at remembering personalities and names. Couldn't be more satisfied with the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyable. If you like stories of polar exploration and games with hard choices, you'll like this. The art and music are stunning and I highly commend the developers for their dedication to making the game as gender balanced and - neutral as is humanly possible in the setting.Caution for dog lovers though!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is a question with three choices then, a question with three choices then, a question with three choices then, a question with three choices then, a question with three choices then, a question with three choices then, a question with three choices then, a question with three choices then, a question with three choices then.I wanted to like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't leave reviews, but this game is truly excellent. It's unforgiving, and difficult to complete, but when you do it feels genuinely rewarding. There are some visual bugs and typos at the moment that the developer will hopefully squash, but the game overall runs very well. In a world of copy-paste open world collectathon game releases, it's a breath of fresh air to experience something different from the norm.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a glorified visual novel with little to no gameplay. Some NPCs are unnecessarily hostile with little room for improvement. But it is my fault for supporting indie devs, I should've stuck to what is popular and tested during the refund window.The art is nice though and is the only saving grace.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed every minute of playing this! Absolutely get it and give it a whirl if you can! It's reasonably short (I completed it in about 10-ish hours, though depending on how quickly you read and how much thought you put into decisions your mileage will vary), the gameplay is as tense as you'd expect from a game about surviving at the South Pole but never strayed into overly stressful for me, the story and characters you interact with are utterly fantastic, the music is super well-used and atmospheric and your decisions really feel like they carry weight with the story.Overall, a great bite-size game with plenty of replayability that I'll definitely come back to plenty! Now to endeavour to play a run where Grimley might actually like me by the end of it :P
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: 0 Voice acting. This is the first thing that comes to my mind regarding this game. Now, I do play lower budget games fairly frequently where I also believe there is minimal or no voice acting, but I have not noticed this "lack" with other games. Here it just really shows that there is no voice acting at all through hours and hours of the game. Additionally, I played "Classic" difficulty, but if the wrong 1-2 people on your crew get killed then it's gonna be very challanging to win in the end. You can easily draw out not losing, but you will not make it to the end. Given all the games availalbe nowadays, a hard pass.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Games like these give me hope that the indusry is not lost and everything can be fun again.You are looking at an excellent emotinal journey with well written characters with the elements of base management. You will have to look after your crew, listen what do they say and call for tough choices. You will get emotinal, you will care for those bastards, even when they will try to act crazy and do dumb stress related stuff. As the sidenote, give a game a week to cook, there are some annoing bugs that are small in scale and easy to fix but they will get you out the flow.Anyway, great game, give it a go at least for 2 steam refundable hours to decide-> forget about the refund and complete it one player session
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo and it got me pretty excited about the game. It has yet to disappoint, but it's a bit harder and less forgiving on your resources in the full game.Otherwise the art, story and character development are well done. I have yet to explore the "Tree Save" system but its nice to know that i don't have to replay the whole game to see different endings
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I first watched John Carpenter's The Thing (1982) as a kid I've been obsessed with the concept of trapped crews in extreme weathers. No outside contact, limited resources, limited time, limited options, and the gradual but guaranteed mental collapse.The game scratches my itch, but it may not be for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave a review on games but for this I think it is deserved.The game is an amazing well rounded package. You will get a feeling for each of the members and if you like a narrative driven game with bits of survival and management then this will probably hit the mark.I will say that there where some minor bugs present in my playthrough. Nothing gamebreaking, more some minor stuff on the UI that bugged out.I can see and feel that the guys and girls developing this game had their hearts invested for this and it shines through. I know they made it with replayability in mind but if I have to be honest then I don't want to play this again (for the foreseeable future) as I feel it would cheapen the story I created. I want it, for better and especially for worse, to be the story of my Capt' Shaw. But when some time has passed I will definately take another turn to traverse the snow, hunger and shearing cold, making it into the pale and beyond!This has been all the money worth and I highly recommend it for those looking for a good 7-10 hour game with amazing characters and story, and look forward to see what this studio will bring to light in future projects.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really invested in the characters more than i thought. There's a lot of them, but they each stand out on their own ( with maybe a couple exceptions) as interesting and I wanted to know how their journey ended with me.Definitely going to be playing through again soon.Well done Bellular this is awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's my kind of game. You get to be a min-maxer with lives of fictional characters. Acts as the game calls its different chapters, are somewhat plays differently. You don't get a clear heads up sometimes. This makes acts disjointed between themselves, moreso because of this is a resource management game. Save system was nice. Art is very fitting and looks nice even in dramatic scenes. There were not a lot of thing to deter me from enjoying its moments. Low budget indies should be made on point like this. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice game, following  a dramatic but believable plot that offers genuine dangers and demands many choices, often hard and occasionally hard to fathom . Characters have interesting personalities. The graphics are simple but effective, and the music is a bonus. There is enough intrigue to keep you going despite the anxiety the game may cause. Some similarities to the also excellent Frostpunk - battling the cold, calculating resources, and managing people at the same time!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so hooked into this narrative-driven game! If you're a fan of the genre, you're also going to love this one!I love the writing and the sound desing. The art grew a lot on me too, it's very beautfil I just grew up with a different influence in terms of art but this here is still exceiptional... I can't stop playing this game and I want go outside!EDIT AFTER FINISHING THE GAME:Despite a few UI bugs (like the screen going black when switching locaitons a bit fast, if a wounded person is cured of their freezing, they are unable to be added to the med bay and some unclibable elements) which were very rare and most, if not all, encountreable towards the second half of the game, I loved this game very much. It reminds of The Banner Saga and I still stand be the recommendation I wrote here earlier.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not well made. It is a text based visual novel with unreadable text. The game aspect centers entirely around making incredibly minute micro managements that are ultimately incapable of affecting the plot of the story. The game takes place in menus that do not work. I found myself swearing out loud as I had to exit out of menus (sometimes more than a dozen times in a row) before it would let me select my "cards" so I could use them. The ending manages to be both weird and boring, allowing for only a very binary choice that doesn't make a lot of sense and left me feeling like I had wasted my time on the game. I have played other games by Fellow Travelers and they are all plagued by these weird design problems. Citizen Sleepers had such an unusable UI that I had to return the game even though I'd been looking forward to playing it and Beacon Pines had a boring short linear story that did not lend itself to an interactive medium at all. I'll be going through my wishlish and removing any games this developer is associated with. My recommendation is people spend their time elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I found the characters and dialogue to be very authentic and engaging. The conflicts that I had to solve didn't feel forced and the decisions that you have to make are never the simple good vs. evil type, that are found in some other games.Unfortunately, I couldn't see it to the end, since I messed up big time when it comes to resource management, and my crew ended up succumbing to the ice a little over halfway through. The game is quite punishing, and you really have to think ahead when it comes to how much food and fuel you stockpile. I will definitely give it another shot sometime later. Some people, however, have complained about how the continue system works, so please read a few other reviews if you care much about replayability.Overall, if you like narrative driven games that are very well written, with authentic characters as well as difficult decisions and conflicts to solve, I recommend this game. Just be prepared that your first run might not have a happy ending. This isn't the type of game that will drip-feed you dopamine.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The game has certain quirks, especially in its narrative, that may seem inconsistent or taking away from player agency. Some mechanics are poorly explained, while some of them are not designed in the best way. However, the vivid characters, the reponsibility and the decisions you have to make will make you enjoy this game nevertheless. I hope the next project from these creators will be a more polished version of what they have managed to do here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat the game and here is my take.The game isn't really my style, but I did enjoy it.  I found myself skipping a lot of the dialogue near the end because its hard for me personally to keep focus'd.  I think this game would be wayyyy better if it had voice acted dialogue, to which, i would of probably listened to it all.The dialogue was a bit cliche and predictable, so when i found myself skipping it and catching a glance here or there, it was what I would of expected.  Though, not all the dialogue was as such, just most.I did have to restart the game about half way through because some dialogue options end the week immediately and i did not have a chance to cure my crew of illnesses or gain resources despite having the ability to do so, which in a survival like game, is incredibly important.  I had to take a couple days break from the game because it was upsetting.   I learned later how the "pruning" your saves works, so I probably didnt need to restart, (I am the kind of gamer that prefers a clean start to finish play through rather than rewind back a little) but it is still immersion breaking and upsetting.I still have no idea what research is for, why should i get it , etc.  On my 2nd play through, i skipped all research expeditions and just had my science crew do nothing but collect food and make medial cures and I was still able to clear the game, and have no idea what i might of missed out on.With that being said, I did make it to the end without any of my crew dieing and all loyal to me.  I think it is a good game and what I would expect from an indie companies first game.  I would reccomend it to people who do like a good story.I think the re-playability might be capped at about 2 or 3 times for most people.  Probably only once or twice for me.Personally, I would rate this game a 6/10 or 7/10 over all but a 7/10 or 8/10 given that its a indie studio and its first release.I want to say "Well done" to the creator and devs, keep up the good work, and I will keep an eye out for future developments.  Please don't let this review dissuade anyone, the game is not bad at all.I acknowledge I am biased in my review because I do not normally play these kind of games, but I wanted to give it a good try for Belluar and give a good honest opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I love love love this game! ♡ It's like an arctic expedition combined with the Disney Atlantis animation film and with Moby D|ck or something. I really started to care about these people.The art is soulful and the gameplay and story are so well designed in this game (except maybe assigning tasks, sometimes).If you love resource management games like 'Help Will Come Tomorrow' or 'Dead In Vinland', you'll like this for sure 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: For the game's scope and scale (and let's face it, fair price as a result) this game is a success. The beautiful artwork, strong character writing and absolutely stellar soundtrack come together to create a setting that despite being bleak, has a certain magic to it. Atmosphere is essential for a game that is basically played by reading text and interacting with UI elements, and this game has it in bucket loads.My only complaint is that I was invested in the story, but my playthrough ended quite abruptly. I understand that this is where the replayability comes from, in making better choices on another attempt, but it did feel like a bit of a rug pull knowing that I'd have to either start again, or choose a random point in the past where I thought I was still doing well enough and try and remember exactly where in the story that point was.Some people will love this, trying again and again for the perfect playthrough in order to get the 'best' ending, but to me it feels like that isn't making the choices I would make, it's making the choices the game mechanics want me to make, despite going against my story and character decisions I would make.That being said, I'm not sure how else you would approach designing a game like this. It's supposed to feel bleak, decisions are supposed to be hard and have consequences. I'm not sure I'd even want an 'easier' difficulty, because I do think I'll come back to this game and try again. All in all, the developers should be proud of what they've made for a first release. This game has a lot of promise and I'd like to see what the team can do with a larger budget (imagine this with full voice acting!) and all the experience from putting this together.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of these "ok" games. Sadly it did not tip into the positive ok for me. The art work is great, the premise is great and the story has potential but the mechanics, burning penguins for fuel and research is meaningless. The pacing is also way of imo, also the ending although good it needs some more build up for me to get invested in the story from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and on my play through i never really experienced any major issues sometimes after assigning jobs i would have to wait a second for it to finish animations of healing before reusing the furnace but besides that it was great. I was hooked early and have gotten my money worth out of it.  Well done
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good game in terms of story and writing. However, there are a few moments where the writing feels very forced and emotionally manipulative. Other than that, the gameplay is serviceable albeit a bit one dimensional. I wish the characters had more individual strengths that would affect the tasks they perform. It would help me get to know them more and actually remember their names so I care more when they die. Instead, everyone just performs their tasks equally well and gets homogenized. Those are just minor gripes I have with the game. The biggest problem I have with the game is the immersion breaking food and fuel management. It is actually more efficient to alternate the weeks between 0 food/fuel and max food/fuel. So one week I would give the crew nothing to eat and no fuel for week and increase it to max the next week. This actually gives a net positive morale and saves you a staggering 25% of resources. It is especially immersion breaking because every cycle the crew would be eating dinner regardless of the fact that I assigned 0 food that week. However, with all that said, I would still recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is a narrative game with an engaging story and interesting characters. You'll also manage scarce resources and make tough decisions that matter a lot.You sign on as first mate on an expedition that sails into the permanent ice of the South Pole. Your objective is to rescue an earlier science mission that was lost, and ideally finish the work that they couldn't complete. The details remain mysterious, though - you're not being told what the original mission was sent out to accomplish, nor are you told who's actually financing the expedition. While your ship tries to find a way through the ice, disaster strikes and the captain goes missing. You become acting captain and try to keep your crew alive, warm, fed, and in good spirits.The setting itself didn't do much to raise my interest - there's nothing wrong with it, it's just a bit limited with regard to the stories that can plausibly be told within it. However, I found the stories in this game captivating and engaging. Each of the (up to 29) crew members has their own personality, many of them have their own small story arcs, and they definitely grew on me while I was playing. You will frequently talk to them and can also listen in on conversations between them. The writer showed good attention to detail, as well as an ability to write plausible dialog for characters with very different personalities.At the end of the game, the main characters will recapitulate their experiences with you, and there are also epilogue scenes depicting how they went on with their lives, depending on the decisions that were made while playing. I found that a nice way of bringing closure to all these story arcs.Your tasks are to procure enough food for your crew, enough fuel to keep the generator running, and to attend to the requests of your crew (which often, depending on how you deal with them, affect morale and loyalty). Crew requests and other conversations are handled in a standard "pick your response" style that usually gives you 3 choices.In addition to that, you can also assign crew members to certain tasks such as scouting, hunting, doing research, fetching rations or coal out of the ship's hold, running extra shifts on the boiler, or resting in the doctor's tent. You'll also have to decide how many resources to spend on meals and warmth - being frugal might be necessary but will affect the crew's morale, and also bears the risk of people getting frostbite or developing scurvy - either condition can quickly lead to death if not treated quickly. People can also get wounded from certain tasks. While those management mechanics aren't particularly complex, I found them engaging and interesting, though the challenge level was actually considerably lower than I had expected. While there were a few tense moments, keeping everyone well didn't actually seem difficult.For the first two-thirds of the game, events such as the fate of the ship or the change of seasons are fixed, they will always happen at the same time. This limits player agency and replayability, but usually the game at least foreshadows important events and gives you options to prepare for them. In the final act, the resource management mechanic is dropped completely, but you get more important decisions to make, and the story branches into two different paths which lead to multiple different endings.The game uses hand-drawn graphics in a comic-book art style that is more detailed than I usually see in narrative games, but I still found the drawings a bit crude. The artist didn't do a great job depicting different emotions, there's one prominent attempt at anger that looks more like a caricature. But considering the amount of different characters and backgrounds in the game, as well as the probably rather limited budget, I think the developers found a decent compromise between quality and quantity.Ambient sounds like blowing wind or creaking wood enhance the atmosphere. The occasionally playing music was also pretty decent and quite varied (including a sea shanty that was apparently written specifically for the game). The dialog is not voice-acted, but I don't think it needed to be - with the fairly large amounts of text in this game, it's always difficult for small indie teams to find good voice actors that fit in the budget. I prefer having lots of well-written text over situations where the texts had to be kept short to make voice-acting viable.The game offers settings for screen mode, resolution, texture quality, vsync, and anti-aliasing, as well as three separate volume sliders. You can also change the text size, zooming speed, and panning speed (which makes sense as graphics are often bigger than the screen). If you want to make the game even easier, you can also switch off game-overs caused by the morale mechanic.The game can be played completely with the mouse, though keyboard shortcuts (using either arrow keys or WASD to move between UI elements) are also available. The latter cannot be rebound though, which may cause issues for players who might want to use keyboard control on a non-ASCII keyboard (though the arrow keys could be used instead).After every "day" of gameplay (which accounts for 1-5 weeks on the calendar), the game autosaves, and all saves of the current playthrough are kept in a timeline. This means you can go back to a previous day of your playthrough very easily, which encourages experimentation and lets players negate catastrophic events (though I would suggest using that feature sparingly for this purpose, as the game seems easy enough as-is).I did not run into any bugs.I enjoyed my time with "The Pale Beyond", and recommend it for fans of narrative games with management or simulation elements. Especially so if the setting appeals to them, though as my own experience shows, this is not a requirement for enjoying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A very engaging little visual novel. The aesthetics and writing are both very high quality, and weave together a grim tale of desperation that I've seldom seen elsewhere. However, the gameplay feels kind of half baked. If you fail, I suggest just turning the decorum mechanic off and picked right back up - the game doesn't feel terribly balanced. Not that a game about surviving the polar ice caps should be fair, but it often felt like there just weren't adequate opportunities to survive, rather than inadequacy on my part. Either way, stalling out 75% of the way through the game because your people were too sick to hunt and having to start all over again isn't fun or engaging. That being said, I also wouldn't recommend save scumming - the consequences of your narrative choices are much more interesting and are the real star of this game. Give it a try, I found it an enjoyable read.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's an enjoyable niche game, with some major mechanic/QOL issues. There's just so much trial-and-error, and you are bound to replay a fair amount. Which means having to re-read a bunch of samey-dialogue, and go through a bunch of the same motions again. But if you do certain things in the wrong order, you lose out, and sometimes what seems almost negligible will be a matter of life or death weeks down the line.  Certain things in the game are really good - The setting, the story, the characters, the atmosphere, the music, etc. I even liked the interface, which is akin to the encampment areas in Banner Saga. But having to realize much too late certain rather unintuitive things, like raising heat to cure frozen costs engineers and not fuel. There's just a lot of things like that which kind of make the game a slog. And it's really not an easy game, despite it being a survival visual-novel, more or less. I get polar survival is brutal, but the game forces you into corners, rather unexpectedly at times. You have to start hoarding as soon as possible, and if you forget, you will pay for it. But redoing some of the early levels is truly a chore. It may sound like I don't like the game,  but I really do. In fact wish more games were made like this. It's just also frustrating and monotonous.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good game, solid and polished, a sweet combination of a dramatic novel and resource management well done! For resource management - solid but simple mechanics, easy to understand and with plain non-conflicting rules. Doesn't get boring, since game flow takes quite surprising turns, but never truly punishing (at least on normal difficulty).10/10 for a game of this size/grade
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with beautiful art and meaningful decisions. So much so, I feel that aside from a few times when I was still learning the mechanics of the survival game play, most rewards and mistakes were mine and earned. I managed to make it to the end on my first play through, and perhaps because of that the alternative options aren't so appealing.  While I'm probably missing out on some great content, the game sells the decisions you have to make well enough that the idea of tweaking a decision or response here or there to try and get the perfect ending doesn't appeal. I'm happy with my imperfect run, and that's not common. Well done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: After trying my hardest, for many hours, many back and forths, and just cant recommend this game. The lack of clarity about which decision entails, what the result of my choices will be it's just bad design. I get the "there is no perfect solution" approach to telling the story, but random events and choices seem unfairly distributed. The pacing is wrong, the narrative seems disjointed, and the crew doesnt seem to be trying to survive at all. As the captain you are dealing more with egos and arguments than actual survival challengs. I really tried playing this game, but it's just too frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea, very poor execution. Art's good, music's good. Story is meh past the first few hours, and completely nonsensical at crucial points. The choices you make don't matter much mechanically, and the resulting story changes are equally bland. My favorite nonsense is a.. mild spoiler: the waterfall at the end, which would prevents movement - and is pretty emblematic of the production team's thought-processes.Good work for the artist and musicians, the rest should stick to work where they make no decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. The controls aren’t perfect (played on steam deck); at times I also accidentally chose unintended dialogue options because of the pace of text loading.However, I loved the gameplay loop, writing, and mystery surrounding the story. The game also has an interesting save tree so that if you make a mistake or want to try alternative paths with your decision making, you can easily reload to a previous week (loop). Despite choosing the easiest difficulty setting, I still found it challenging (though not too punishing) to balance resources and decision making. Some suggestions to iterate or improve:-allow a toggle for instant text loading during character dialogue-better explanation, tutorial or resolution with research points. Even though I played to multiple endings I don’t know what the benefit was for this, though it’s also very possible I missed these indications or did not pursue a path where these are leveraged.-As other reviewers pointed out, navigation can be optimized (zooming, panning, or moving from one objective to another)-More information about the characters or ability to log what you learn about them along the way (to better influence your decision in dialogue to raise their loyalty)Overall, loved the concept, atmosphere and writing. It was great on the steam deck, despite the mechanical challenges described above. 8/10 for me as a lover of strategy and story + atmosphere-rich games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game, although it's short, I found myself surprisingly gripped by what is essentially a visual novel with some hardcore management thrown in.Stories great, if you're interested in anything like Shackleton's expedition or you've watched The Terror, you'll find a lot to love here. It's not a topic I've seen explored in video games that much that I got a kick out of.I didn't feel too compelled to replay it, but the only entire playthrough I got out of it felt like my moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I am so glad I picked up this game! I'd recommend you play it if you like resource management, interactive fiction, and expertly written dialogue and stylized art. If you're not taken by point-and-click mechanics, this game will not be for you (I love those kinds of games!).For context: I have played one full run of the game and have gotten one game over screen. This took me around 10 hours. I think the price tag is already justified by this play time, and you could play the game again for different endings and choices if you wish.What I liked:1. The characters, their personalities, and how they play into ludonarrative. This game would not be good if the writing lagged, and luckily for us the writing is stellar. Not only is the dialogue well-written, but it feels personalized to each character. The conversations you have with them are mechanically important to your success, and you'll likely have strong feelings on most characters (even if you don't like all of them). Characters will react differently to your protagonist depending on your chosen background --- which I also thought was a nice touch.2. The art! Beautiful in both environment design and character portraits. A great touch, and especially heart-wrenching in moments of failure or necessarily sacrifice. 10/10!3. The game presents conflict in a way that isn't impossible but also isn't clear cut. You are playing with incomplete information. If you're me, that means you die the first time around. That's okay! You can play again and things will go better for you. Even when you don't die, you live with the consequences of your resource allocation, politicking, and morale preservation. I feel like the narrative is best played all the way through, without the urge to get a perfect ending --- at least the first time through. When I took full ownership over my story and the big plot decisions I made (and the small, devastating or charming interpersonal ones), I was fully swept up in this game's machinations. 4. When you lose, you can restart the game at the beginning of any major chapter. I think this is generous, but it might mean repeating some decisions you've already made. Often this is necessary --- death on the ice is often presaged by several weeks of mismanagement. I know some people disliked the fact that saves weren't more frequent, but I am happy with the cadence the developers provided.BONUS: There is some singing in this game and it was phenomenal. Not a constant feature of the game, but a gem of a moment that I'll remember for a long time.What I didn't like:1. Though the sound design that was present was great, sometimes the ambient noise loops became apparent (especially the longer I played the game). I would have appreciated a bit more differentiation on the soundtrack.2. When you do replay, it's difficult to skip through dialogue. This can mean you're mashing space --- which is annoying.I'm looking forward to other releases by this studio, and heartily recommend this game to folks interested in a good story. Grab a blanket, get some tea, and buckle in for a suspenseful adventure. And also, I have a newfound hatred and fear of leopard seals! Just y'know, for your knowledge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you like narrative games, resource management, and weighty decision making, give The Pale Beyond a spin. At the end of Act 1, The Pale Beyond is an impressive first outing from Bellular Studios. The Pale Beyond's art direction, writing, and sound design come together in a way that gives the game a very unique feel that plays intricately with it's setting. Each of the major characters on the Temperance are likable in their own ways, and for some are incredibly intriguing. Even the less-major members of your crew, those with faces but less development, are still treated with care to their characterization in minor dialogue. The foundations are laid early for you not just to care about your crew not just for their strategic advantage, but to genuinely see them through the Pale Beyond.In the gameplay department, fans of the weighty decision-making of games like Frostpunk will feel right at home in the Pale. The game follows a deceptively simple loop: Major decisions usually made at the beginning of a given week, and management of three stockpiles of resources, in essence, morale, food, and fuel. Perhaps it's the presentation, but beyond the immediate resource effects on major choices, you feel the weight of even the most minor choices on the effect of the expedition. To give an example, and to oversimplify an early choice: Your crew has found a stowaway. Do you take them on as an extra pair of hands for the expedition, or do you not run the potential risk of having one more mouth to feed than needed? There are a few bugs that I noticed through the first act, and while minor overall, they were fairly annoying. Multiple times throughout the act when attempting to use resource cards (Fueling the furnace, Feeding the crew, etc) stacked resource cards, when attempting to drag them onto the interface, would disappear and bug out the interface. An easy work around was to simply click on the resource cards and add them that way. A far more minor, but far more annoying bug, was that in just about every crew assignment or use of a resource card, the amount of dogs available in the kennels for the week would show that it would go down, as if there were a cost associated with using the card, but upon using it would actually have no change. This made planning out a couple of weeks very frustrating. I haven't played around with the Save Tree system yet, from my understanding a way to re-load and explore different outcomes by re-loading specifically at large branch-points, I suspect to prevent active save scumming. In a game like this, I'm intrigued on how the system handles the "problem" of save scumming. I've already got many ideas of what I could have done better throughout act 1, and I'm certainly interested to explore them. Overall, as of right now, I'd recommend The Pale Beyond. Certainly worth the price, and despite some roughness around the edges on day 1, it's got an engaging game play loop, intriguing narrative, and a stellar presentation. Excited to see the rest of the story play out, and for future projects from Bellular Studios.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is an incredible resource management survival game that will have you on the edge of your seat from beginning to end. The game puts you in the role of a leader in an expedition that has gone wrong, and your main objective is to keep your team alive while making tough decisions that will affect everyone's morale and safety. From the captivating story line to the stunning graphics, everything about The Pale Beyond is top-notch.One of the standout features of the game is the resource management aspect. You have to balance your limited resources, including food, fuel, and medical supplies, to keep your team alive. This creates an immersive experience where every decision you make has real consequences. It's a challenging game, but the difficulty level is just right to keep you engaged and invested in the outcome.The Pale Beyond also has an incredible atmosphere, with haunting music and stunning visuals that really set the tone for the game. The sense of isolation and danger is palpable, and it really draws you into the world of the game. The story line is also compelling, and it keeps you on the edge of your seat with unexpected twists and turns.In summary, The Pale Beyond is an outstanding game that deserves all the praise it gets. It's a must-play for anyone who loves survival games or resource management games, and it will keep you hooked from start to finish. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere. Crisp, detailed art. Fine writing that's mostly good but with some missteps and unearned asides. For a while I was afraid it was all gonna fall apart somewhere along the middle, with the game mechanics being a little disappointing and the story missing a couple beats.Story-wise there's especially one (long) scene towards the end that's definitely hits you like a punch in the gut, but more due to the subject matter than the story actually deserving it. In my view the story hadn't earned a scene as gruesome as that. It made sense to the story, in its own way, but it was at the same time a sudden and rather abrupt aside. This happened a few more times, where the focus of the game and the story shifts dramatically and to something seemingly quite far from the main part of the game and the story (in particular the votes). Again, it makes sense they're part of the story; the emphasis put on them jars, however, and it left me thinking they were plopped in, because there needed to be a raising of the stakes and make you feel something rather than because it made the most sense story- and gameplay-wise.Another example are the long, unskippable pan-outs of the camera happening every now and again. The art and the atmosphere is cool, but suddenly and without warning putting so much emphasis on the surroundings kind of drains them of that grandeur. I'd rather be better able to marvel at the surroundings myself and, better yet, experience it alongside all the great and highly detailed (both in terms of art and character depth/evolution) characters.Ultimately, for me, the game props itself up on a high pedestal, and while for me it doesn't really achieve all that it sets out to do, it does hold up, on a story-front and a gameplay front. It doesn't excel in either area - the gameplay never really grows into much more than guesswork, and the story part sometimes focuses perhaps too much on the loyalty aspect and too little on the intriguing mystery part (there really isn't much mystery at all - other than unanswered questions) until the very last act where suddenly all the mystery is... displayed more than revealed, I suppose.If you're on the fence, Boring Dad Gaming has a great series on YouTube. Maybe check it out there first and see if it's to your liking.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing story, hard choices and all in all a great game. There were some moments where I felt so many different emotions, and it really felt like a struggle, my resources growing ever scarcer. I recommend it to fans of story-based survival games. It has a few bugs, but never gamebreaking, at least for me. Also the UI could be more clear.Overall I'd say a great 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: game is good. really good. the characters and artwork are really charming, the setting and plotline is extremely cool  and its clear that its a game that was made with a lot of compassion and earnestness. absolutely one of the most interesting genre combinations i've ever seen in a game — it leans visual novel-y whilst having a very verbose writing style, the resource management elements are not particularly realistic and a bit incongruous with the story but honestly it does the job being nerve-wracking to manage in a narratively satisfying way and once you internalise the game-iness of that side of pale beyond, you kind of just get used to it. this game's major efforts went into its storytelling and that's completely fine by methere are some minor things to address within the writing, mostly just the way some events and relationships are presented. to begin with, don't listen to people whining about the 'insensitivity' of the dog deaths. the game does force you to execute all but one dog in your party but it does not read as needless edginess at all and serves the story, and moreover, is treated with the weight and respect it deserves. for reference, many polar expeditions ended with various sled dogs and other pets being killed for practicality — the scene in this game very much a homage to such tales, and the game does not treat it flippantly or jokingly. this moment serves as a central part of a character's entire arc and it's very effective. it's good writing that you feel bad about having to kill a bunch of dogs. not every game can be a wholesome "can you pet the dog?" simulator, and i feel like that expectation is unreasonable when this game is very much about.... trying to survive in the cold in the middle of nowhere.otherwise, delving into spoilers: oh, also, this game is VERY funny. made me bust a gut a couple of times. nobody will warn you about this
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 10/10 Great story, amazing characters and resource management that will put you on ice.I fell in love with The Pale Beyond quickly. The characters, the mechanics and the motivation to keep everyone alive was felt every step of my journey. I got so griped in completing it after my first story tree I had to challenge myself ever more into the frigid south pole. I decided this masterpiece was worth much of my time and dedicated my afternoon and evening narrating and recording it. Thank you for creating an amazing game that despite some passages being hard to stomach was the most memorable story I have read outside of a books binding. Aerogwin on Twitch and Youtube if you care to watch it before playing. This is worth your time if you want a griping story that immerses you in its telling. I received this game from humble bundle, another great community to be a part of.

The game is so intriguing with an amazing story that hooks you it, and it makes it all the more painful to have the carefully handcrafted experience ♥♥♥♥ on by an endless stream of bugs.So far I've experienced:Dialog that belongs to an entirely different playing random.Your position in the game will sudden change, teleporting you to different areas with different prompts/situations.Crafting menus will just not accept inputs, making it impossible to do things like send dogs out, or assign crew to certain roles.The enormous zoo of bugs this game contains RUINS the carefully crafted experience, utterly.What an absolute tragedy this game is; it's bordering on a SCAM.Even at the reduced price, this game is ABSOLUTELY NOT ready to be played yet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok. It's not great but it's not *that* bad. Ultimately, I'd rather have my 10 hours back, so I'm giving it a thumbs down. The game makes some implicit promises to the player based on genre and tone, but doesn't deliver. It bills itself as a moderately gritty resource management game. Unfortunate, there are few challenging decisions and the resources nearly manage themselves. There should have been more resources to manage, more ways to obtain resources, more ways to spend resources, and more hard decisions to make. You hunt for animals, and the choice is to eat them or burn them for fuel. I just wasn't very logistically challenging. It was almost more like a puzzle, with particular options simply being better -- but not like a fun puzzle. Like a tedious one. I completed the game on my first try with the best ending, not losing any crew. Well, I did have to wind back to an earlier save once. (Aside: I did like the story tie-in to the save mechanic.) I misunderstood the freezing mechanic and accidentally killed 4 or 5 crew men early on. I played for a couple more weeks before realizing that my run would be dead in the water without them.The writing is not great, but not the worst; it's passable. You always know what the "right" dialogue choice is, or action to take. That wouldn't be that bad if it weren't for the loyalty subsystem (more on that below). The writing was non-essential. If they added a skip button, you could use it without being terribly disadvantaged. The loyalty subsystem rrequires you to arduously talk to every crew member each week just to pick whatever dialogue option makes them +5 more loyal to you. Honestly, you could click through the dialogue until you got to a choice and then select whichever option was vaguely optimistic or kind (or at least not callous), and then you'd get +5 loyalty. I don't know how you could complete the game without a majority of the crew being loyal to you.The decision outcomes are well telegraphed. They make sure you know the stakes and what will likely happen if you choose XYZ over ABC. There aren't any major gotchas or cruel surprises, which is good, but there also aren't any terribly difficult decisions. It's almost always clear which is the "best". Even the moral decisions were pretty black and white. Not a lot of gray here. All in all, I'd give it a 6/10. It's just meh. I kept me engaged long enough to finish it, but I wouldn't recommend it. It's not outright bad, and it seems to have executed on its vision well, I just don't think it was for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Positives:    Exceptional art    Engaging storyline    Challenging and gratifying gameplay loop    Overall, had an enjoyable experience playing.Negatives:    Occasionally, controls and music (loop) felt a bit awkward.    Loading after a critical mistake (one seemingly minor decision turned out to be significant) may require revisiting dialogue, resulting in some time wastage.    The ending fell slightly short of expectations.Overall, I relished my playthrough and would gladly recommend it to friends.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! Definitely one of my all time faves. Can pet the dogs.The art style is beautiful. The music is nice and atmospheric. The resource management is brutal and some of the choices you have to make feel heavy and consequential. I really liked the social aspect of balancing loyalty and decorum with survival. The characters are pretty fleshed out--definitely fleshed out enough to make you care about their survival. The dialogue options can be a little black/white at times but mostly they're pretty nuanced and human. 10/10 I was very stressedMy only criticism would be that there's no way to remap the controls, which I guess makes sense since it is 90% point and click. Would have liked to change the zoom in/out controls though.Also I never did figure out why there are so many possible crew members when I only met and played with about half of them. Are there more to be added? Or were they limited due to my choices? No idea, still super fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game is as difficult as you make it. Everything else like the soundtrack, story, art direction and characters have soul put into it. The heartfelt moments hit when they land. I find it at the same time a relaxing game where I can lose time in it, and when logging off, I feel satisfied. The game also becomes intuitive enough to not lose track of your objectives and of what you did before.I think the appeal to emotion and the atmosphere around it works in this game, and that's what it does best. Be aware choices matter for some things, but also not for others. I think the way consequences are managed in this game are balanced enough for what it is trying to deliver. I think you'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Love the setting, characters and art style. Shackleton's story must be one of the most inspiring and greatest adventure stories of all time. I really want to like the game. But unfortunately the gameplay and controls sour it for me.It's a simple worker placement mechanic. Almost like a board game. That by itself would be fine, but you don't get sufficient feedback for how you're doing (you might already have lost the game, but only realize after hours more play). And the Interface is tedious and cumbersome.The save tree mechanic would be a cool idea - it's a branching timeline where you can only ever replay fixed increments - but it doesn't work with a narrative game. I don't want to read all the story repeatedly just to try a minor gameplay variation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Basic mechanics but still a lot of fun. You really feel the stress later on. The characters of course are absolutely brilliant and I seriously love all of them, but the endings I have done so far felt rather weak and basic. For instance, Otherwise this is one of the best games I ever played and had a good pace.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I never touched the game since the day I downloaded it, an update came out (I was away but left the game running).BUT, even though I haven't played it, just look how much love this game gets!! It's like Beta Minecraft, legit getting 4-5 updates a MONTH!! Not many games in this day and age get so much polish after already being really well made.
