_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I can no longer count the times I died and had to reload only because I forgot to throw the food&fuel into the pot / boiler to actually use what I had in my storerooms.Also you have no clear overview over the amount of food you have, because many things can be used as either food or fuel, so you have an inventory instead of a clear number of food left.The first 5 hours are strictly linear and only conversations, maybe to keep you from being able to refund the game? I dare not make that accusation, but it passed my mind. Also it took 3 ingame weeks to get to know everyone of the 29 crewmembers, which seemed strange.There are several contradictions in the story and conversations, which I won't go into detail about. Half of the game seems to be conversations to increase crew loyalty to you, the other half is mikromanaging how many crewmembers you can afford to get cold each week and still be able to heal them next week, which is surprisingly complicated (e.g. burning all your fuel will warm up 3 people at most... didn't know space around a hearth is so limited).Many gameplay options are not explained (migration paths, medical comfort only curing but not allowing to put other people in medbay the same day, etc) so you have to try them out and them reloading and replaying the entire long day, maybe even 2 days with all it's lengthy conversations. I found that tedious and there is next to no information on the internet about gameplay questions.So the game has it's charm, but is too finnicky for a really good survival game and the prologue is far too long and boring while setting up the mood(?). Good thing is you would not have to replay the prologue in a second game, because you can jump back to any week and start from there (savegame-tree it is called) but thats actually not so different from just saving every week like in any other game.It is actually challenging, because you have to spend enormous amounts of food/fuel to keep the crew happy or they will kill you / mutiny / ? (the game just ends when they get unhappy)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: An unexpected, lovely, and sincerely affecting experience. Play it your way, don't be afraid to reload if you get caught out by something that feels janky. Wasn't a common experience for me, only twice in what was for me a ten hour game, vastly outweighed by my experience with it. Think Citizen Sleeper, if you've played that, but with what was to me a tighter but still open-ended conclusion.Months of darkness. Low wages. Slim chance of safe return. What will you do, when steel hearts break and courage does abscond?
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Only an hour in, and I'm really enjoying the game so far. The choices I make have impacts and I wonder about the choices I'm not making. Looking forward to the game really hitting its stride now we're in the ice.(edit) I'm impressed by the developer's focus on bug fixes post release. For a small indie, a few bugs will always make it to release but this company seems very focused on getting those fixes out there as quickly as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Only a little over an hour in, I can tell I'm in for a treat with this game. I've been following this game since Michael Bell first announced it on his YouTube channel and it's amazing to see it completed. There's a few issues with screen fit if you play on the steam deck, but you can tell the game was well optimized for both controller and mouse gaming. The story feels realistic and the cast of characters each feel like a real person you're getting to know. The music in the game... What a treat. I'll update more after I finish my first playthrough, but so far in I have no regrets about the money spent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: INCREDIBLY GOOD. i will say that it's first and foremost interactive fiction and that as a result the gameplay and interface are a little creaky, but imo it doesn't take anything away from the experience -- just don't go into it expecting a gameplay-focused survival game. the characters have incredibly intricate, interconnected arcs, and the story is compelling and heartbreaking. I really cannot overstate how beautiful the art and music is. highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is truly a marvel of indie story telling. Watching their documentary on what it took to get this game made, it reflects the journey through the ice that Shaw and the crew embarked upon for what seemed to be a mad venture. The game play is easy to learn, but the stress of each week kept me playing for hours. I still feel as if many more things could have gone wrong.The cast of characters is diverse and engaging, although at times, there felt like more opportunity to test the loyalty of the crew (perhaps many more playthroughs are in order?)I highly recommend supporting this small studio. You can tell they care. And nowadays, supporting good folk who try to bring art into this hell of a world should be lifted up. It was a hell of a ride.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: What a phenomenal game/story! This games story will be forever cemented into my brain after the events from one absolutely heartbreaking week and follow up conversations towards the end of the game. Had me, a grown ass man, literally BALLING! my eyes out for solid moments. The way the characters are written was incredible, you can really feel their presences if its not from the disdain from Grimley or the jovialness from Kurt. The music making everything seem so isolated is the perfect cherry on top to complete the whole experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good, it's a survival game, but in a more storybook point and click style. It's got the emotional choices and consequences of a game like "this war of mine" and "frostpunk", but it's not exactly a colony simulator in a conventional sense. Loyalty does end up mattering pretty seriously at the ending of the game, and there seems to be at least 5 different endings, potentially more. Good replay value, an interesting save system, good art, and good music. If you like this game for the choices and consequences aspect, try frostpunk, this war of mine, and ixion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone that enjoys the story of the Franklin Expedition, this game is for you. If you don't know what that is, check into it and I'm sure you'll have the urge to experience something like it thru this game.The game is relentless in its realism. I see negative reviews because of people having to play hours of the same part again after poor decisions earlier on that didn't become apparent until later. I had to do this myself, but it is a intentional part of the game. I made the best decisions I could, and they backfired. That's real life. Sometimes you can play it perfectly & still have something go wrong that ruins it all. At least in this game you get to learn from your mistakes and try again. The real emotions I felt while playing this game would have not been so intense had it been easier. Had I not seen how bad things could be & celebrate what I had accomplished in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A WONDERFULLY thought out indie title!  Exploration, survival, hard choices to be made, and consequences to follow.  Character interaction is great as well, winning people to your side or putting them in their place.  The mechanics are age old but a fresh take on how their implemented make this game amazing.  The new mechanics implemented are just as unique as well.  Take the save tree for example.  The story literally branches out depending on your choices and consequences, allowing you to go back from a major day and make different choices to see where its consequences branch to.  The artwork is stunningly beautiful and well done, but also imprints upon you the dire circumstances you find yourself in.  Highly recommend well worth the price, and time you will want to put in to it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This was enjoyable for what it was. Great story and the resource management wasn't grating and easy enough to not make it take away from the story for the save scummer power fantasy type player like me. I did think there was gonna be more eldritch stuff in this from the concept and atmosphere, but I still enjoyed the story for what it was. a survival tale where you have to make hard decisions but bright enough to not break the spirit, though even when you do everything right it does come close for my weak sauce self particularly on Week 37, you guys who've played probably know what I mean. But for the price and the time, I'd say it's solid. Need more relatively easy going but narratively engaging games like this for my busy self nowadays rather than the grindfest a lot of other games seem to be nowadays. Unrelated to this game, but I feel like if you're not building an actual physical or mental skill grinding is pointless. Also great music. Some criticisms:I feel having hover overs for the different traits of your crew and what they mean, especially the conditions, would come in handy. Also would be nice if your journal properly recorded the convos and choices you've made. this game is kinda visual novel-esque and lot of vn's have that feature. Not a deal breaker just forces me to take notes instead. Zooming speed with a scroll wheel is really too slow and it is to the point of actually being annoying, i'm guessing they didn't have different scale for the scroll speed be it the right analog stick or the scroll wheel and they prioritized the controller feel. There's also a bunch of pretty regular UI bugs such as crew members sometimes disappearing from the menus, not being able to click on the save tree sometimes, and it would be nice if it was more direct when you didn't have enough sled dogs to do something rather than just spinning the send beyond button graphic super fast, but I don't think they're enough to take away from the overall experience. But yeah enjoyed it, wish for games like it, but kinda wish there was more eldritch and supernatural stuff in the story, but I think that's just me having misplaced expectations thinking this was a sunless sea type game when I first saw it, but it has a demo so that sorts that out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: An overall excellent game that mainly wins over the player by getting super immersive. This is not something you want to play passively, but engage with, put yourself in situation in your head and act in character, not as a player. I haven't been thinking about what to do next in the game while not playing to this extend for a while.The outcomes of decisions are not always predictable and the game doesn't always give you all the information to make the best calls, but this is part of the challenge. There is no expectation to get to a good ending on first attempt, which is bold but works in the games favor.It takes a while to get there, the opening is pretty slow and it tests the players patience before you get to the actual gameplay loop. The other small criticism is the unintuitive timeline feature that only started making sense once the crew reaches a specific ending. This ending by the way might be pretty devisive in what it does to the game. Recommend to everyone looking for an cross between immersive survival sim and character driven choose your own adventure narrative. Some of the early pacing issues and timeline related issues aside, fantastic. Really looking forward to what the studio does next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful and haunting experience. I found it to be perfectly paced and filled with memorable characters and really powerful moments. The mood and tone of the game is very tightly honed and I think this is definitely worth playing if you have any interest in this sort of game. Well done devs!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game a lot, possibly my favorite game of the year. I had so much fun playing it I literally played through a whole run in a day LOL. I was so invested in my crew and their stories, I really didn't want them to die. I got teary eyed at some parts. I loved the game mechanics and the resource management of food, fuel, morale, crew, and loyalty. I'm a super big fan of Frostpunk, and this game reminded me a lot of it except it had a story and personable characters. The music was beautiful, the writing was surprising, and the art was gorgeous!! Choices definitely matter. Would highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

The resource management isn't extremely deep, but there is room for taking important decisions, and the game knows when to stop and avoid things becoming too repetitive.Overall, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The story and atmosphere are the clear hooks here. I also love the experimentation that the Save Tree system allows for. After my first failure I was bummed but now I feel free to experiment and try things knowing I can always go back if things go poorly. There are some really cool moments that left me shocked, and the weight of my decisions truly hit me at times. Really recommend for anyone looking to dive into a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and gorgeous game, excited to see what it looks like totally polished. To begin, the art, worldbuilding, and story suck you in completely from the jump. The art is gorgeous, and I was immediately invested in all of these characters. The characters are interesting (especially Stanberry, haha!) and easily identifiable, and even change with the course of your journey. Really incredible and emotional to take that journey across the ice with them. Trying to figure out the systems took me a bit since I don't play a ton of survival management sims. However, even being a rookie at the genre I found it very simple to catch onto within the prologue once I understood a few general principles. And the game clearly hints at important tasks to take care of in case you're struggling to prioritize. It felt like it really hit a sweet spot, where I was physically tense trying to make sure our crew made it through parts of the winter and making grim but necessary choices to make sure we'd pull through while not feeling like I was running up against an impossible wall with too many systems to wrap my head around. Even though I'm not really experienced with management sims I was able to succeed pretty well with a bit of practice in the early acts, where you have more wiggle room.The only issue I would have is with some of the polish of the game - some typos, sometimes dialogue and multiple clicks trying to buzz through it means the choice you want passes you by, research points seem a little unnecessary. And while some people disliked the branching save tree, I did like it a lot. It was a cool way to mix the narrative with the actual gameplay, and while the save points didn't completely correlate 100% of the time I do feel they were helpful enough to succeeding and I did enjoy what it added to the narrative. With some further little polishes I think it'll be an even more incredible game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This caught my eye because it seems they  based it on one of my favorite books and True Stories “Endurance”.  If this game looks interesting to you at all I would recommend playing it.  It does however… require some patience since you will need to go back and replay parts of the game which does get repetitive.  It’s not bad though,  and gives you the chance to catch things in dialogue you didn’t notice before. They also make it very easy to speed click through conversations. The Resource Management gameplay is pretty basic but I found it very engaging.  But… the main part of the game of interacting with the story and characters is masterfully crafted! Also packs great Art and MusicWOW!All in all I think the devs should be proud of this nice little adventure.  I got a solid 20 hours out of it and never got boredThank you guys!

If you liked something like Frostpunk in essence but with it's game play and narrative ratio flipped, this is for you. The Pale Beyond ultimately boils down to a visual novel with some resource management that can get you if you are not careful. I don't recommend this game for people who are sensitive to animal/pet death.That being said, if you're okay with that narrative point, this is a good survival game. It's sort of an interesting mix between something like Dead in Vinland and Frostpunk. The story is engaging and the characters are well-written and fit the setting very well. _childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like reading a really good book. Once you start, you quickly become entranced by the narrative and want to keep going to see how it develops. Both art and music are perfectly suited to the purpose of the narrative.The game mechanics are relatively simple, but the margin for error is minimal and this generates a good sense of progression. If you are an experienced player who understands minmax resources, they are enough for you to be entertained and have to think carefully each week (turns).Game takes about 10 hours to complete, more if you have to go back due to deaths and there is some replayability in the form of decisions, different endings, and optimization of relations/resources.I initially bought the game just to support the developer I've been following for years and was curious about the product as it talks so much about game design and wasn't even intending to play it at the time. But I ended up opening the game and after half an hour I ended up spending my whole day to finish it because I needed to finish it.The only problem was some visual bugs, but nothing that impeded the progress and it seems that they are already being fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember the faces of the people that died because of you? He asked me. Every single one, I answered. He was right; it's not the choice that is difficult. It's living with the consequences.I wasn't sure what to make of The Pale Beyond, at first. The closest game I'd compare it to is This War of Mine, but make no mistake - this is a very text-heavy affair. And the way your choices weave into the gameplay, the character dialogue, and the general direction of the story? Oh, let me tell you about that.If you've played Disco Elysium, you probably remember how impossibly impeccable its script is when it comes to adapting to what you've said and done; how some small remarks can almost turn into arcs that develop and resolve in a satisfying manner. Well, here it's perhaps not as expansive, but it's still the same amazing feeling.Listen, Robin: they will remember what you said. Whether you stay true. Who you chose to help, why, and how exactly. It never feels like you're just exploring a dialogue tree, and it's never obvious which dialogue option will do what. You need to intuit it. Feel what really makes your crew tick. Can you do that, Shaw? But then there's the...  A really big one. It's almost enough to make me reconsider my recommendation. Almost.See, the game's resource system pretty much expects you to sacrifice something, and then to regain it later. Which is fine - but it never mentions that. Your very first playthrough is pretty much bound to end up in a disaster because of mistakes you commited a long time ago. To avoid spoiling anything and being too specific: it's okay to sometimes not give enough. The crew is hardy, Shaw. As long as you care for them, they'll be fine; they might complain at the moment, but you'll find ways to appease them again. Calculated risks are an absolute must - especially earlier on, when things are... less deadly.Now. I'm sure there's a question going through your head. Is... is  possible? Can you...?And the answer is yes. You can. But some sacrifices must be made. Painful ones. Ones you might not be able to live with; but you'll have to. That, my friend, is the true meaning of leadership.There's one more thing, Shaw. One of the endings provides you with a, shall we say, revelation. It's one of those that don't hit very hard at first. Only after a while, after you thought about it for a bit. It fully solidifies this game's central theme as "sacrifice". For what, you ask?Well, what will  sacrifice for, Robin?Listen. It's late. I need to retire for the night. I'm certain you've heard enough, and your mind is already made up anyway.Bring them home, Robin Shaw.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: What a surprise! I've never heard anyone talk about this game but it perfectly captured that feeling of reading a Jules Verne book. Good story pacing, the gameplay provides suspense, and the game isn't scared to straight up hid things from you if you're not willing to commit to taking major risks. My only complaint would be that the game seems a bit too easy after I played it on the "classic" difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a treat. I loved every second of it, beginning to end it had me hooked. After playing through Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood I was looking for something else to satisfy that itch, and this was exactly it. Poignant storytelling, good and fleshed out characters, and meaningful and impactful decisions. If you're familiar with the Banner Saga, it plays a little similar to the way that the decision making as the leader went in those games, but more streamlined to be the main event.I loved getting to know my crew, and watching them warm up to their new captain as the game went on. It made for a beautiful experience. And I enjoyed the ending and the updates ending scenes as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Great concept, not really anything else like it on Steam, as far as I'm aware. If you liked "The Terror", check this game out.No wokeness. No gay romances. No real world politics being smashed into your face. You get to make choices that can impact on whether people live or die, or remain loyal to you. Decent but not fantastic writing and characters.Save tree system is interesting. You can go back in time and start from previous weeks if you want to. You just overwrite every save from the weeks ahead of where you restart from. Good if you want to go back and try a different option in  a certain week without having to play through the whole game again up until that point.Cons:Resource management, particularly in the beginning isn't great and leads you to metagame things that a real captain or first mate would never actually do.  Also you're told by the captain that the ship has enough food and fuel for 6 months at the start, which is a complete lie, as you'll be constantly having to scrounge and/or ration your supplies from early on. (even before the plot gives you a good reason why you would have to do this) You can only save at the start of a new week. (turn)Not much replay value. I did two runs. I lost my first about halfway through, and then won my second. I really don't feel like playing it for a 3rd run.  I don't think enough would be different to justify it.The ship's crew seem to have very little respect for rank. I know it isn't a military ship, but the majority of the crew treat each other either like buddies, enemies, or random people. Seems weird that the ship's company would refer to the captain by his first or last name only, to his face. That's a very nit-picky con though.Conclusion:It's good, and I wish there were more games with a similar concept. I liked playing as the captain of a crew, making decisions, dealing with the crew, trying to win and maintain loyalty etc.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Eh, kind of a sideways thumb on this one.  Cons: It features a common mistake in dialogue driven loyalty games, where the only way to succeed is as a simpering sycophant, complimenting everyone until they love you enough to get a decent ending.  Except in a few occasions, where people respond randomly.  In either case, 9 times out of 10 it seemed like any dialogue choice was just pretend.  The ending is a mess.  Dead characters somehow show up in the epilogue, it has two whole denouements, the science mechanic I sacrificed lives to score up through the whole game end up having no meaning or use at all.  And this complaint may vary amongst players, but I found it problematically anachronistic.  If you want to make a sailing period piece where half the crew is female, you really need to establish it early on as being in an alternate history setting.  Otherwise it seems like you jammed a bunch of political correctness in at the expense of good writing.And indeed, that wasn't the only time plot suffered.  In what possible world is a first mate on a tiny boat for two weeks where almost everyone sleeps in the same room, and he still hasn't met everyone?  Pros: Nice artwork, especially on the environments.  A good "never have quite enough of what you need to get by, yet somehow you get by" mechanic.  Something I like in a game but rarely is done in that fun turn based way.  Cool surprise reveal.Fun characters.  Addictive to always see what the new day will bring, lots of surprises and challenges to be had.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing Pale Beyond, so I do recommend it, but with some serious concerns about its narrative. Pale Beyond has an excellent and unforgiving management system that you really need to be good at the entire way through. There is some margin for error, but there are some decisions that can make or break a run pretty easily which feel arbitrary (hunting, for instance,).  Still, it should be punishing and difficult. Since my first run had the crew fall apart basically a turn before the end-game I would say it succeeded in that harshness. Getting to know each character and win them over was probably my favorite aspect of the game. Each one of them has their own narrative arc which makes sense, is rewarding to see through, and fun to engage with. I think it is a missed opportunity to not be able to SPEND loyalty like a currency. Imagine having a very good friend and you ask them to help you move. They volunteer and spend the day working hard to help you. Then the next day you ask to borrow $500... and maybe they give it to you... then the next week you ask them to throw you a birthday party... You CAN spend loyalty IRL and asking a lot of people can strain relationships. As it is loyalty is useful for only some characters throughout the game (I can think of two, ). Then of course loyalty is important at the end of the game... there is a point in the beginning where it LOOKS important, but isn't really. I would have loved for you to be able to spend loyalty for extremely useful bonuses at a high cost... maybe the 'best' endings are barred behind surviving without leaning too hard on your crew...I also really enjoy the premise of the game, but not its central conceit . The rest of this is going to be spoiler heavy, suffice it to say that the crux of the story seems unnecessary and contrived, especially given how little it seems to really matter. So that was disappointing for me... but I can't say I didn't love the 30 or so hours I spent playing it. My only final complaint is that I discovered TLDR; the mechanics are fun, the characters are great, getting to know them and surviving is dramatic and entertaining... but the central plot is not great and sometimes you can fineagle the mechanics in ways that break immersion. I don't regret my 2 and 1/8 th play throughs.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I would give a thumbs up to support this game. But I don't think the very positive status is correct. Am not sorry I bought it, because I wanted to support Michael, as I like the guy and his content, and believe that he can actually create an even better game than this but, it's understandable that his first game can't be a masterpiece.So what do I like about the game?-atmosphere-survival elements-adventureWhat I don't like?-Although the story as a whole is good, the dialogue is boring and drawn out, and not voice acted-Shallow yet cumbersome gameplay mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: For the twenty USD asking price, I give this game a temped recommendation. If you like narrative games, this is easily one of the best to come from a western studio in over a decade. That reflects as much on the game itself as the state of narrative game developers in the west. If you already know you don't like narrative games, you will not like this game. Many of the worst tropes in the genre are all present and accounted for.For it's strengths, the game's writing is generally solid. There are a few instances of that trope where when you choose a dialogue option it produces results completely different from what you were expecting. If you were hoping to express that you were happily unmarried, well, don't. That withstanding, the writing team was able to convey personalities with virtually no time and little script to work with, which is impressive. If you try to approach every crew member with the same demeanor, you will have half your crew hating you. Excluding a few very specific instances, the art direction is excellent. The game wont wow you with visual fidelity but the simple fact that I really only have one specific nitpick speaks to the game's credit. Completing the game as intended does give you a sense of satisfaction, which is usually the hallmark of a good narrative game.What undermines the game, in no particular order....1: The art goes from great to jank the minute it wants to subject you to any of it's animated sequences. I will assume that there simply wasn't budget for, say, animating the sails in the panoramic cut scenes but it sticks out like a sore thumb. The game wants you to look at the pretty picture and then you have a sail boat in the middle of it who's sails 2: The game clearly resents the idea of save scumming- since you can't really do it and it's save system bookends each day instead of each decision- but then makes it exceedingly easy to stumble and get someone killed. The ability to simply rewind text is so taken for granted that the most popular visual novel engine- Ren.py- has it by default. Which would make it a lot easier when, say, misaligned menu options have you miss the, "react appropriately in time of crisis" option and instead click, "Well I guess I'm a sociopath, that fool must die now" option. And because of course it's the kind of decision that happens dead last, you are then stuck replaying a bunch of decisions you already made because of course you rewound your save.3: The game does a horrible job conveying itself. What little game play exists revolves around managing three resources- food, fuel, and mood. The problem? It hammers it into you that you need to prepare for a span of weeks where you wont be able to gather any. This is complete nonsense. You are always able to gather more food and fuel. There is actually no skill involved and no complicated decisions. The game actually progresses through the second chunk of weeks faster than the first chunk, while maintaining the same consumption rates for fuel and food. As long as you understand that anything other than seals are a waste of time, you will do just fine. Or if you just look up a map guide. And then just to top it all off, it doesn't matter how well you prepared because....4: Forced player states in a narrative game are awful. And, without spoiling anything, it doesn't actually matter how well you are doing. After a certain point it stops mattering if, say, your entire crew is freezing, or starving. You lose all your carefully provisioned supplies, but you also only have to spend them one single, additional time.5: When the game tells you that you should conduct your day in a certain order, the game isn't joking. For whatever reason the game will let you allocate labor before taking your daily requests, which isn't a big deal early on, but if you do it that way later on it can functionally soft lock you into a game over. Why they don't just force you to do things sequentially, I have no idea. 6: It gets really obvious after chapter 3 that the team ran out of time or budget and probably both. I don't know if the writing team was aware but it sticks out like a sore thumb when your game almost completely abandons the core game play system it's been hammering on about for most of the game only to service a plot that suddenly gets extremely meta and borderline breaks the fourth wall. And while it is somewhat fitting, given the plot, that the ending kind of just sneaks up on you and resolves everything, it's still annoying. 7: Mass Effect Syndrome. Writing choices are frequently unbelievably shallow and gravitate between being a good leader and a proper boy scout and then oscillate to, "How much of an irredeemable jerk do I want to be?" Which then makes some of the achievements rather exhausting in nature. Especially when what should be the most difficult achievement- making sure everyone survives- is going to either be the easiest, or second easiest achievement to get. I just completed the play through where no one dies and I was able to command the loyalty of the entire crew. I already had little interest in the, "Be a ♥♥♥♥" play through but I have even less considering that. The idea that the hardest play through to get is the one where you reach the end without getting subjected to a mutiny, and with zero crew loyalty makes it seem more exhausting than fun.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have pointed out, basically a visual novel with one correct path, and one correct way to play, and correct options to take in each dialogue tree (which are usually super obvious).... your choices do not really matter, except that you make the CORRECT choices. That isn't how "choices matter" in games. That's just having one way to play the game, period. I haven't played it much yet, because I hate the UI, I hate the repetitive nature of clicking through the ship, clicking through the one line of dialogue at a time (which cannot be sped up, and seems to respond very sluggishly to you trying to speed it up manually by clicking). Seems very shallow and very hard to get into. Your relationship with people really doesn't match the way they talk to you, they talk to you the way they talk to you, and have a separate relationship quality apart from that, whether they are "loyal" or not. There's a lot of illusion of choice, illusion of strategy, illusion of resource management but there's no depth or complexity here, and it's a chore to play. I will eventually play through it, I imagine, and I may change my mind. Hopefully.Also, this has gotta win the award for "game that would've most benefited from something lovecraftian happening"

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond presents a daunting expedition with memorable and well-written characters, tons of choices that affect the narrative, and surprises up until the very end. The gameplay did not hit as hard as the writing, but it was still fun managing my resources for most of the game. I just wished the game played a little less fair and rewarded more attention to detail. Sending a one-armed man on a hunting party proved no different than sending the strongest in your crew. A husband and wife could be assigned different duties for the entire expedition with no protest to their constant separation. I hoped for a more particular experience. Regardless, several moments are going to stick with me for a very long time, more than making up for any shortcomings in how it played.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: So let me start from this: this is basically Dan Simmon's Terror (with dogs, and a little bit sweeter, less horryfing). Or should I say the lost expedition of John Franklin (since it was an inspiration for Terror book)But don't get me wrong, this comparison is not a bad thing (duuh)!  It's the exact opposite of bad. It's superb. I loved Terror, and the Franklin expedition itself was a bizarre, and curious story. It's a hard game and I would normally rage quit somewhere in the middle because I always follow my heart when making hard choices, which almost always ends up badly and with the game over, but I didn't want to give up. I wanted to make sure that Francis, I mean our protagonist, makes it to the end. Summarizing: I've loved it, and highly recommend everyone. Not only to Dan Simmon's Terror fans. <spoiler>But the dooooogs.... why couldn't we save them all ;(

_childDocuments_.review: What a game! Breathtaking views! Gorgeous art design! Fantastic writing and great characters, good replay value, touch choices, this game is wonderful!If you are interested in this time period or anything to do with the topic of this game I highly suggest you give this game a try!The atmosphere is great, the writing is top notch, there are tough choices you have to make, the art design is gorgeous and the audio and music is well done to.Not run into any big bugs either so far, runs good on the Steam Deck to.
