_childDocuments_.review: from the moment that the introductory cutscene starts, the pale beyond had me in its grip. a long time ago i went through the demo (and have now caught up to where i left off!) and was and still am blown away by the tone and atmosphere, the intelligent and sensible dialogue, and the way every choice felt significant. each character has their own needs and personality - responding with 'the nice thing to say' or 'the advice that will fix their problem' isn't always the best choice in a given situation, as some characters respond poorly to empathetic responses. i found this immediately fascinating - you really have to pay attention to the needs/priorities and personality of each character, and it's not a simple decision of "be nice and then everyone will like you" (though this will work for some characters!)the initial journey before reaching the pale beyond itself serves as a great tutorial, a way to meet the crew and glimpse into the mechanics that will soon mean life or death for you and your crew once you reach the arctic. it clearly outlines how the mechanics work, but in a way that feels immersive and diegetic to the story, and builds the stakes steadily. the prologue serves as a very tight experience where nothing feels superfluous. the music is lovely, as is the art style. every moment of the game feels like you're in a struggle for survival against a bitter cold that doesn't care if you live or die. at the same time, it doesn't feel like the cold is overly anthropomorphized or "malicious" - the focus is kept squarely on the crew thus far. i'll also pay compliments to the journey itself - watching the background change as we approached the antarctic and after we arrived was particularly effective in building up an exciting sense of dread  personally i'm very fond of games that make you survive in extreme or seemingly hopeless conditions, and the pale beyond thus far fills that need perfectly in what appears to be an intelligently written, heavy-narrative game where it genuinely does feel like your decisions matteri may return to update this review further once i've finished the game lastly, touching on the creator and to be fully honest: i haven't watched bellular in several years, and only have vague memories of the fact he had a studio that was making a game. when i came across the demo on the store page a long time ago, i was immediately intrigued and installed it without even looking at the developer. it wasn't until afterward - when i was trying to see if there were other titles by this dev team - that i saw who created it. so to anyone who is hesitant if it's worth buying on its own merits: i say just try it out and see for yourself. for me, it's been more than worth it thus far and i'm excited to see where the story leads
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: 40 weeks (turns in-game) of doing mostly the same things. Nothing major changed, you only have to juggle wants and needs of people.I really liked the premise, but it just too slow and boring for my tastes. I expected some development for the first 10 weeks, but nothing interesting happened, hence why I got bored and stopped playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely astounding.I have nothing to compare to in its league.  Closest to it is Frostpunk.  Frostpunk had one issue though some choices felt menial and that it was a game. Here, it matters. It all matters the choices feel real. I love the game so much already.(No mean to insult Frostpunk I am very exited for the second game and cant wait for it, hoping it reaches this level of weight to the choices)- Minor spoilersAs mentioned choices matter. A lot. The most magnificent moment was when getting elected captain. The realisation that last nights events were only the start and that the entire crew now depended on you to save them and lead them hit it was like nothing else. I am absolutely blown away with how much urgency and pressure the game can create.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful weekend game with excellent music, beautiful artwork and surprisingly soulful characters.I didn't have much experience with survival management games so I didn't play on a hard difficulty, still the save tree system serves well so you can undo any huge mistakes. The game does well to instil mystery with the disappearance of some of the crew and the elusive benefactor for the near suicidal expedition. The game offers multiple endings (that I haven't yet explored) around completing the original mission and what to do with what you find. The key members of the crew (the specialists) have some decent character growth and a good level of deepness that is revealed as the story unfolds.The game does well to keep throwing problems towards the player, through crew disagreements, crew that are disloyal to you and environmental pressures.Sometimes it felt like what should be the correct answer for dealing with a character was somehow the incorrect one, however, generally the crew responded well to praise - maybe too well, making you feel like a HR manager rather than a stern captain. However, perhaps this is due to the choice I made when the captain near the start of the game asked me what quality I thought most important for a leader.Either way, the game was most enjoyable. I got it on sale for around £8, I'd say it was decent value, given that there's some level of replayablity with some different key choices to make. For full price, I wouldn't advise it unless you know you usually find a lot of replayablity in these survival management clicker sort of games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have played in a very long time. The writing for the game, the graphics, and all of the other wonderful aspects of The Pale Beyond deserve much praise. Thankful for the people who developed this game, and I truly do look forward to my next play through of it. If you do not have this game yet and are at all interested in it, I highly recommend purchasing the game and playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Normally story games aren't my thing unless they have enough action or the story's writing is good enough.on this i can say i was surprised by both.The twists and turns and hard choices forcing a brutal unforgiving realism with twists of fantasy was something i wasn't prepared to see. The story was perfect and the danger and options truly made it diverse and unique to you. each story line branches and leaves you completely up to making your own path. Honest 10/10 i could have ever imagined, worth the money in gold.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: So I'll start by saying, I usually don't write reviews for games, sure i'll talk about them to friends and give my opinion but i felt like I really needed to write a review for this gameso here goes.First of all, this type of game is NOT at all usually the type of game I will play, at first I purchased this game simply to support Bellular and his game studio, but by god by the end of the game I was extremely happy with my purchase. Fantastic art, amazing cast of characters I actually cared about and tried my damnedest to keep alive loland the music sets the atmosphere and tone very well. The story had me hooked around week 4 or 5 and I just had to know what happened next, which in my opinion a story driven game needs to hook players in early and this did the job!There is a lot I would love to say about the story but I will refrain as to not spoil for others. There were a ton of moments where I could feel the tension rising in the game, "how am I going to survive next week?""Oh god 4 of my crew have Frostbite, what the hell am I going to do" etc etc.This game grips you!Now, I did encounter some bugs during my playthrough such as the resource cards not displaying correctly, or when you use 1 stacked food resource out of say 7, it would consume all 7 instead of just 1, they were annoying but backing out of the menu all the way and going back in usually fixed it for me. There were some other UI and text based bugs and some grammar errors but it overall did not hinder my experience. (I believe most of these bugs have been addressed by now)The games survival mechanics did trip me up a few times, but it was a learning curve I enjoyed. Honestly, i did have a very enjoyable experience with this game and I do intend to go back and do another few runs to see different outcomes or endings I may have missed.Purchase this game if you enjoy narrative focused games!Can't wait to see what this studio puts out next!8.5/10Now I did want to briefly mention something about the ending I received so spoilers ahead!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: !!!mild spoilers!!!You play as Second in Command on an expedition to the north pole.when the captain himself vanishes, you are put in charge. As this is your first mission aboard the vessel, you have to win over the crew, whilst also making sure you'll survive the harsh environment. The game is a rollercoaster of emotions.I never felt so immersed in a story like this one. I feel like really was the Captain. Whatever the crew felt, I felt. I was constantly worrying I took the wrong steps, made bad decisions and was so worried to get crewmembers upset. I felt their exhaustion, anxiety and was frustrated with them at other times. And I was crying my eyes out in the storyline with the kennel master. Always while trying to make the best decisions to ensure survival.I felt an immense weight lifted from my shoulders when I got everyone home safely.I can not recommend the game enought. A masterpeice and my Game of the Year.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Surprised at how 'sucked into' the game i became. Simply looked to try it out and support Bel and his team. Currently at week 13, made a few mistakes, 1 dead guy so far. The game has me griped, i'm intrigued, exciting to see how my choices play out. The game is 10 times better than i expected. reminds me of frostpunk a bit so far but playing out the story of survivors wondering the ice & snow. Highly recommend it and can honestly say the most fun iv had playing a game in years. And iv been an avid gamer for a good 25 years. Nothing has interested me so much since WoW Legion. Would love to see additional choices/story options to be included in future updates/dlc's just to add more replayability. Or new journeys altogether.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: So far the characters and stories are engaging and compelling. The art style is moody and atmospheric in a way that really leads to an immersive experience.  However, certain parts of this game are confusing and unintuitive.  I’ve lost the game twice in a shockingly low span of time, like the day I became captain because I somehow didn’t understand how the food resources worked and I inadvertently starved my crew…twice.  I still don’t understand what I did wrong so it might be my third downfall as well.  I also did not understand the decision tree impact on file saves and when I came back to play and hit continue, it did not load up the last game I saved, so I ended up playing several game weeks on the wrong file.  It took me quite a while to figure out that I was on the wrong save file.  The dates and time played did not make any sense.  All and all I do like this game, and I would recommend it, but there is a steepness to the learning curve that took me very much by surprise.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just past Act 1 and I'm really really enjoying this game so far. It's unlike anything I've played before. My single criticism is the map panning/zooming - all around movement. It's *really* buggy. If you can get past that then this game is definitely a hidden gem. It's a mixture of visual novel + strategy/management with beautiful art. The writing is great while the choices feel actually difficult with consequences/benefits coming from either decision. The characters all have unique personalities that pull you in. I even find myself worrying about my crew while trying to keep them safe.-- While I did receive this as a gift, I'd have definitely bought it myself had I stumbled across it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Great story. Worth the time. It's hard for games to make you really connect with characters, yet both them dyeing at your hands or living and saying farewell both have an effect. If you like story, resource management, and mystery it will scratch the itch, and leave you with that slight ache when you finish a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game, well written and interesting subject matter. Choice and consequence heavy, a nice oppressive atmosphere pervading interspersed with moments of levity and heartwarming. A few issues with minor bugs and the branching narrative at the end, but definitely not enough to detract from the game itself,
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I meant to sit down and check out the first 4 weeks, I ended up playing 12 weeks XDGraphics, sound, gameplay all on point. I enjoy the tension with the resources and the survival aspect of the game. The few bugs I did encounter (v1.2) were minor, like some glitchy ui stuff when allocating resources or people to tasks, but usually leaving that window and re-entered it fixed it right away. All in all, this game's a win for me. Great job.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so well done in so many ways that I genuinely want to leave a good review, but there was one issue with the writing towards the end of the game that just completely took me out of it. To be clear, the mechanics of the game were great, the atmosphere was great, and most of the writing was incredible. The art especially was really good. If that is what you're looking for, then absolutely buy the game and have a good time. it is GOOD game and everyone involved in making it deserves props. Stop reading here because of spoilers. So, SPOILER ALERT FOR CHAPTER 4.The dogs. The justification for the thing with the dogs felt so ham-fisted and forced that it came across a little more than trauma-porn, especially given how close to the end of the game it is. It seems like the writers were trying to advance the theme of suffering, difficult choices, and the fact that sometimes you "can't win for trying", and that's good storytelling for sure. But to have the set up for such a heavy thing be "well dogs can't sail", felt really poorly done, like it was an afterthought plot point spliced in after the story had already been written in order to pump up the sad. The exact same scene could have been written in, achieving the desired effect with devastating results, by moving it a little earlier in the game and making it a choice between feeding them to the crew or possibly letting people die of scurvy. It's just as hard-hitting without feeling as unjustified as "dogs can't sail". As it stands, it's a real "Jack can't fit on the door" moment in my eyes. Because of that I lost my buy-in to the story and ended up feeling really apathetic about finishing the story. I played on a little more and then decided to leave it there. There's a lot to love about the game, but in the end I can't recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic narrative driven game with a charming cast of characters and full of tough choices which always felt impactful. Loved the polar expedition and world building but the crew made it worth the journey. Gorgeous art, the characters jumped of the screen and the environs were hauntingly beautiful. The sound design and music were a treat for the ears too!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game for about 4 hours now and I'm absolutely in love with it. Imo it's very hard to accurately capture celtic voices without it feeling cringe, but this game nails it. The characters are engaging and the setting/narrative is as enthralling as it is brutal. I really love the art style and the sound design is top notch. It's a strange feeling when you're looking forward to playing but not looking forward to what happens next? A bittersweet balance. Great job team!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game, the demo drew me in and I'd been following the production since. I prefer the slower story driven games, this one in particular has a very appealing art style and the characters are unique and entertaining where I feel many games fall short on really fleshing out their characters. Some of my favorite interactions were the ones my character wasn't even in on; there's moments to listen in on the crew talking amongst themselves and it really makes them feel alive and as though my decisions carry weight. The price is well worth it and I hope to see more like it from the devs even if it's without these characters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable in a somber way. I happily recommend this game. I plan on spending many more hours trying to keep my crew alive, even if it feels like they don't want me to help them.There are some UI errors, for example: Dog count showing it will go down when adding to the Hooch, but then it doesn't. However, I didn't find it stopped me from doing anything, or impacted my gameplay too much, and they will probably be fixed as they are brought to the attention of the devs. Speaking of the devs, thank you for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: That ending sequence, g'damn. I've played a handful of these living-novel-choose-your-adventure-book-style-games. This one is the first that I've finished. What it lacks in fancy mechanics is a story that you feel a great deal of influence. Solid writing. Heavy moments. Memorable characters. A run through to the end took 7 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The main focus of this game feels like the retelling of The Endurance with all the desperation and hope that follows. Decisions have impact on your focus towards the crew. I have lost by week 15 simply because I was wishy washy on trying to appeal to all sides. You are required to make hard decisions to focus on your survival. Would you focus on hunting season or trying to build shelter against the upcoming winter freeze? I attempted both and lost, it does not pay to try and be an all around "good" guy in this game. Several other decisions involved are what build the story, including your response to this horrific ice hellscape and the way certain crew members act under stress. Remember - every crew member will think you are going to side with them and often this results in conflict throughout the crew. This game is wonderful at building horror, suspense, tension, and humor, through the natural phenomena around you in this environment. There will be moments where you can empathize with their plight in the harshness of this desolate area and you will fall in love with the puppies to help stay warm through the cold night. 8/10 for me until they fix some of the other issues, namely:Menu for feeding hoosh / furnace is wonky right now.This game seriously punts your GPU/CPU in the butt, temp wise, on my specs. i7-4790k, 1080, 16 GB DDR-3 RAM.Some sort of option (not the daily journal) to see my history of conversations between characters so I can remember if I was being nice or bad towards them (including a loyalty meter or something on the dialogue screen). Dogs should be on the ship from week 1 for optimal petting experience.Zooming and scrolling system could use some tweaks (max zoom setting still makes you use the scroll wheel 10 times to get closer).Somewhat spoiler - at least one character should mention something about stripping the ship bare for its resources before you go to the ice camp stage (or if they did, I do not remember it), I know it is my mistake for not thinking about it - but still annoying to realize I missed out on it.tl;dr: If the book Endurance excited you, games like Frostpunk excite you, and you enjoy using niche nautical terms, give this game a shot, well worth the price so far. Looking forward to starting my second campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: made me cry, made me laugh, made me go back several times to avoid offending NPCs. 10/10. also the visuals are stunning and the music is very atmospheric.edit: i did some research on the historical inspirations and i am honestly amazed and amused at the many nods to shackleton's expeditions. especially the achievement "an ernest attempt" got a chuckle out of me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: An alright narrative driven resource-management game that focuses on the many different characters part of your expedition crew, and the choices you have to make that affect the crew and the mission directly. The game is mostly text-based besides keeping track of your inventory and decision costs (time, number of crew to do an action). I dig the art style and it adds to give each character their own personality. In the beginning the writing and concept was intriguing, but by the fourth act the character writing took a nosedive; everyone's issues and flaws could be conveniently resolved if you are literally just be nice to everyone...contrasted with some of the difficult choices the game presents you, the writing overall can feel like a mixed bag. The few different endings were interesting and worth going back for. The fact that each character was unique and were categorized into their own role made the fact that any of them could actually die throughout the journey add to the tension. I also like how it is a bit more difficult to save scum some choices with the save system, at least on your first play through, to encourage seeing how your poor choices culminate by the end of the game.Overall The Pale Beyond is an enjoyable mix of resource-management survival and visual narrative, but certain issues prevent it from excelling in either genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This can be quite the punishing game I gotta say. Some huge things can happen if you just don't know what's scripted to happen. Like game-losing stuff.However, the overall story is pretty nice and (as I later discovered) is based off of a real ship.There are a few things that I feel aren't super explained, but I do like the whole rep system.A few resources out there will say not to use the existing save system to roll back time basically and 'prune' your save, but I think that's personal preference. It's literally part of the game.All in all, I enjoyed the game and found quite a bit of the dialogue to be hilarious.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the story, the characters, the art, and the twists and turns. I was totally sucked in and couldn't put it down until I'd made it to the end with my crew. If I had to make a criticism it would be that the research mechanic doesn't seem to be all that well developed- I noticed that you could research to see migration routes of different game and you could go research different spots on the map but without knowing any migration routes I was fine and visiting places also didn't seem to do or change anything. All in all I recommend it to anyone who likes story rich, atmospheric, resource management  in a beautifully rendered environment with great characters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The game is wonderfully written, with amazing characters. I will say this game is definitely NOT for everyone, it is a tough as nails resource management puzzle to ensure everyone's survival, and there are a few points where the game will sucker-punch you with little to no warning. If you've enjoyed games like Darkest Dungeon, Frostpunk, The Atlantis film, and you don't mind buying what essentially amounts to a good novel then this is the game for you. having reached an ending with everyone alive on my first playthrough (yes i'm bragging) I can say that I sobbed with the crew both tears of sorrow and elation.It should be noted this game is not without its downsides. I played it three days after launch and there are more than enough annoying bugs to make me rage quit after a few minutes of playing, These bugs are hopefully on the mend, and nothing game-breaking occoured to me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Love the characters, very well written.Interesting Gameplay loop.I wish there would be more procedurally generated events, it feels like every event is programmed before and the same in every playthrough.And I understand that that is kinda needed for the story and to finish the gameplay with everyone alive (or atleast make the ending not dependent on RNG).All in all good game, good story, good fun. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A grim and intriguing strategy game set in a steampunk-like alternate history where the player takes the role of First Mate on an expedition to the game world's "south pole". Inspired by the true story of the John Franklin expedition where all 129 members of the HMS Erebus and HMS Terror perished while succumbed to the ice struggling to survive.      This game captures this feeling of grimness and despair quite well, especially when you weigh decisions on who lives and who dies throughout the story. The developers have created a unique visual style here with their Victorian-era steampunk like designs, and all the character designs have their charms. Character dialogue is never bland, and I was drawn into clicking what each character had to say when prompted. There are also multiple endings to the story and the developers even released a free post-game update that expands on the different epilogues. If you have an interest in lost expeditions, games set in the frigid polar regions, or just management strategy games in general this game is a worthy purchase even if only to play through once to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this title, expecting it to be a narrative RPG with some resource management. Instead what I got was a mess where the delineation and explanation of mechanisms and decisions were poorly thought out, if at all. What made it even worse was the confusing save system which forced me to restart the game from the beginning and lose more time, only then to realize the repetition and lack of actual player agency had as I went through the beginning choices all over again. All of this was not helped when the game finally got to the resource/social management portion of the game and did not explain ANYTHING in terms of sourcing for your needs. By this time I was fed up with the game and the narrative which I found charming at the beginning just wore me down as it was obvious that my choices were not choices at all other than 'keep that meter high as possible'. I reached this point at a bit over 4 hours of play and have no interest in returning to it -- it's a real shame, beyond my ability to get a refund, as I wanted to support the people who made this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lovely game with an incredible atmosphere and a wonderful story! I love the art style and the fact that it's based on numerous Arctic / Antarctic voyages (Shackleton, Franklin etc). The music and one particular song is very charming, as are all of the characters which manage not to be one dimensional! The gameplay is not in depth and there isn't much to it, but that's not what the game's about. One of the most standout games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful atmosphere, interesting gameplay and visuals. This team does an amazing job at making you feel the weight of being a captain trying to pull everyone through and survive. The music is fantastic, calming at some points, and evocative exactly when it needs to be. One minor UI bug that persisted through my playthrough but it didn't affect gameplay. If you are a fan of character driven narratives this is a must play! Well done to the design team!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is for sure a different take on survival games. Its more of a point and click one but don't let that deter you from trying the game, it has amazing artwork with some interesting mechanics and beautiful music. This game has a really interesting story that will you have guessing your next action very much knowing this could cause the end of game or the end of someone you care about. If you want a survival game that is unique and beautiful art you need to check this one out, well done devs truly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game, I thoroughly enjoyed myself playing this all day today. I managed to get through the story without a single death, and only Grimsley unloyal (he was like 5-10 away, alas). Did the abandon the mission and find the ship endings, and I was really satisfied with both. Highly recommend people try out at least one variation of the find the ship ending.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Game was fine enough up until week 15, then the pain happened. Decided i didnt like the cascade of poor choices i made and went to see if i could reload. To my surprise i was reverted all the way back to week 8 with no way to go back. Pretty awesome. NOT. I can't be bothered to go through all of that again sorry. 2/10 game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying myself until I had too many UI issues and some of my resource cards poofed into thin air. It's way too much of a bother to restart and the save system makes it too difficult to restart. The lack of a quick save/load is truly a shame. I felt this game would of overall been a better experience with a central hub for "Events" Listening, or talking to NPCs. Going into the Kennel to talk to Cordell for the 20+ time just becomes tedious. Leaning into more of a Visual Novel experience similar to taking requests menu would of been a drastically more pleasant experience in my opinion. Also no auto scroll for text as well as a backlog in such a text heavy game is a crime!Overall I wish I could recommend this product but too many little issues broke the camels back.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Very good story, but also very hard, the classic mode is what I was able to beat it on, but that says more about my skill with worker placement games and managing resources than it does the true difficulty of the Game.I honestly can't wait to see the next game these guys and gals put out, just hope it's not a rough ride for them one the way there!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A really great achievement. Especially for a studios first release. Excellent writing, story, characters, setting, art and production. Mechanics come together so well to make an atmospheric and tense whole. You can feel the weight and tension of every decision the game throws at you as you watch your resources tick away and your forced to make decisions both big and small that end up having long term consequence . Some moments of the game feel perfectly sudden and brutal  and there is a great variety of outcomes and consequences littered throughout the game.the game has a few annoying bugs that hamper what is otherwise a very good experience. some saves didn't load properly when i tried to go back to certain choices. One bug i found annoying was when entering resources for food and heat the resource would randomly disappear or would go from say 5 resources to 2 after inputting one item. Happened twice near the end of the game and if the rest of the experience wasn't so stellar i would be a bit more negative about that. But hopefully this can be fixed with a few post launch patches.Overall strong recommend and i will be encouraging my friends to buy it too. Great work overall. You should be proud of what you made here because I genuinely sincerely loved it and am excited for any potential future games Bellular makes
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, good writing, characters and story.Game is incredibly buggy, UI breaks all the time, often forcing the player into decisions before being able to fully understand them. It's impossible to plan anything because events just happen randomly, especially in the "winter" its insanely easy to get stuck with game ending setup where just 1 min ago everything would have been fine. It's hard to understand how to balance things in such a way that another week can be successful. Later into the game difficulty is nothing but arbitrary and frustrating, I wish there was an option to turn off this nonsense so I could get the rest of the story and be done with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed it, but hard to recommend. The game is designed for you to game over your first time playing it, but replaying the same sections over again just takes too long, requires clicking through too much dialogue, and overall just isn't as enjoyable or interesting as the first go around. The story and dialogue don't change enough to make replaying after a game over not feel like a chore.Overall, probably a solid 6.5/10, the art and writing are both excellent, the survival mechanics have a good foundation, the structure of the game just needs some tweaking.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is great. In practice, it is a visual novel with resource management elements woven in: which are two genres that I'd usually be on the fence about. What sets it up as a great game however, are the ambience (which I would argue is pushing the same quality as titles such as Darkest Dungeon) and the characterisation. Characters feel deep enough that even when you understand their personalities, there is more depth than just saying the thing they want to hear. Choices are often genuinely difficult to make: not just the classic: a) Donate to Charity or b) Strangle a Baby.The game can feel pretty brutal on occasion: both in terms of difficulty and story. EA should be taking notes however: as THIS is how you give players a sense of accomplishment. Trying to remain spoiler-free, reaching the final stretch of the game, I actually got the same kind of feeling seeing my actions pay off as I did when playing through Mass Effect 2's suicide mission. That's actually kind of amazing - for me at least.Now, it's not perfect by any stretch: there are a few bugs and gripes I have with the title: mostly UI or tutorial related. When assigning characters to tasks, there's a VERY common bug where a a character both will and wont be assigned to the roll: but this is only a visual bug and can be solved by quitting out and restarting the selection process. Nothing major. The game has a lot of replay value but occasionally decides that no - you're not allowed to skip through this text or that cutscene. Great on a first run - less great when you've seen it more than a handful of times.I've seen murmurs that additional content for more branching paths may be added in the future - don't know how much of this is true and how much is wishful thinking but given a certain branching point in the story, I feel like this would elevate the game to real 'top tier' stuff. There is so much potential to explore other routes that I would love to see realised.That said, I give it a solid recommendation. Oh, and the artwork is beautiful too: like, actually stunning levels of beautiful on more than a few occasions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story, writing, setting and set of characters, who all feel and behave like believable people, yet very different.the art style is gorgeous, the music is also great and the consequences from your choices can be devastating or offer redemption. the resource management part of the game is very basic, and could have used more layers, or at least nuance. the main issue of this game is that playthroughs can end based on specific player decisions, and if the player wants to finish the game, he has to restart potentially whole weeks before disaster, which means reading through the same text again. this can be very tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I heard of it because of the devs, and it caught my interest the more I saw.I can say, now getting my hands on it, that it is quite engrossing and beyond my expectations; good characterization and feel to the characters and the environment. However... 2 things you should know, I'm a dirty save scum-er (and still having my butt kicked) and letting me pet something cute is always a plus!Edit: I beat it and I gotta say that was really friggin good, very satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: First look from the demo : Will update when i finish the game. Really dig the atmosphere and art. Inrteresting setting.Edit: Finished my first playthrough (with a failure). As i said before art and atmosphere is on point. Nice events. Not terribly well balanced though. Hopefully they work on that. Still easy to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Love this type of narrative-driven strategy game. I'm a big fan of The Terror, so it scratches the itch just right as well as adds a subtle yet rich world-building. I know I'm going to play it alot! Also the demo is a nice big chunk of story for free, 3 hours of game is very generous and gives you a feel for if you'll like to play it!This place wants us dead and I love it
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game so far. Got it on sale for $15, and knowing what it's like I'd say it's worth the full $20 price tag. There are a few hiccups along the way. The accessibility setting for larger text cuts off text boxes sometimes, and some actions have unintended consequences that come out of left field. (I put a hat on a dog and suddenly loose loyalty with a character who is not even in the room? Come on now.) But all in all these are minor annoyances in an otherwise stellar game.8/10. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Just a few hours in, but this game is really something! I get strong Frost Punk vibes when it comes to the survival mechanics but much more woven into the really gripping story and the characters. 9,5/10 so far for me. My only concern is that it may be a bit too easy or less harsh than I expected. But I will see...
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The setting is really interesting, most of the characters are well developed, the art and music is great. There's definitely a really cool world here that I'd love to learn more about in a future game or update. The save system was a little wonky when I first started but it seems they applied some fixes in an update.Vague spoiler in the following paragraph here:I don't know if I'll replay this soon, but I probably will one day, especially if more content is added. Overall though I really enjoyed my time with The Pale Beyond
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell, the game is like a modernized Oregon Trail on steroids.+15 Loyalty from Stanberry if you buy it now!When playing, you will be faced with the following:- Meaningful choices that directly impact every outcome - Moral dilemmas that leave you second guessing yourself- The opportunity to explore what kind of leader you are when things get (very) tough - Critical moments where life and death balance on a thread - The infinite puzzle of balancing dwindling resources against time and crew morale - The temptation to value your popularity above survival And that's just the gameplay! The Pale Beyond also features an enchanting soundtrack, charming characters, and a beautiful art style. Every aspect of what the studio put into this game works to immerse you in their story. You feel the weight of every decision and every outcome. The joys and anxieties, the mercies and tragedies - every aspect is translated by art and prose into a believable human experience with you at the helm.Seriously, get the game. If you don't, that's a +15 Loyalty from Templeton - AND NOBODY NEEDS THAT!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this one enough. The characters are great and well written, the dialogue is excellent, the audio is immersive and the artwork is great. Story moments which, I hate to admit, did jerk a tear out of me. And the gameplay is amazing. If you ever played Frostpunk, it's that but without city-building and more immersion. Had one play-through, and already see the appeal of multiple replays. The only gripe is that while dialogue is amazing, if you've heard it once and want loyalty, you will have to listen again. Though I understand: from their perspective it's the first time, and you can skip it. You just won't gain loyalty.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - A good mix between visual novel and resources management survival. - Interesting story and characters. Great writing, music and atmosphere. - Reasonable price based on length and quality.Cons: - The user interface is extremely buggy at the moment. - No difficulty setting. The game is hard and when you fail you have to reload back in time and go through the same dialogues and events until you get it right, which can gets tedious. - No voice-over.The game is good but too buggy atm. I will play it again soon and update my review when the bugs are ironed out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a partial recreation of Ernest Shackleton's expedition, worth doing research if you enjoy the game. The game follows almost all of the details quite faithfully, with most differences coming from order / duration of events, and then taking a turn near the very end.Despite the rather numerous bugs - at least on day 1 - the game is very enjoyable. Best described as a combat-less Banner Saga, you take care of the crew, making sure they don't die or you don't run out of resources. The game is very light on any strategy, constructing or even difficult choices, gameplay revolves around simple gathering and stockpiling resources, while juggling some negative statuses and keep NPC's happy. It is a story-driven and focused game, and the story, characters and MUSIC are all very solid.That said, the ending did feel somewhat rushed, leading to forced issues. The pacing changed and it became apparent that writing tried creating drama, despite the outcome being obvious from the very start. With all the bars filled, the narrative still punched me in the face with "BUT ARE THEY LOYAL?!" a bit too frequently.As for the replay value, here i am with the best ending, missing 20 achievements for doing 'worse'.Definitely a recommend, just know what to expect
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I got this because of the Frostpunk vibes and what I expected to be a depressing management game. I stuck around all the way through because of the engaging story, the well-written and charming characters, the agonizing decisions, the gorgeous artwork & art direction, and the smart ways in which the story and gameplay intertwined.If you like games with an interesting story and managing difficult decisions, I can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It often locks my mouse to only respond to the game on startup, especially when I alt tab to do something more interesting than looking at a loading screen. Ad now it has even started to drain all memory while starting up. Combine this with the fact that the current version of Windows doesn't run task manager in a seperate stable OS, and that means my entire computer can become hard to use. Luckily I could use TAB, arrow keys, and space to end the task otherwise I would have had to reset my computer entirely.On to my review of the gameplay, (for as far as I have managed to play it on those few times it didn't crash one way or another.) It look like a fun story, and the gameplay is well done enough. There's just one annoyance that only applies to fast readers: The letters appear one at a time in what I assume must be someone's normal reading speed. This is really annoying since I click to get the entire sentence, read it in the time it takes me to click again, so I am constantly clicking just to get to read more than five words at a time. Oh, and sometimes the sentence is only a short single word so what I think is my first click actually becomes my second click, which means I skip both this tiny little text block and the next before I can read them. (because the third click becomes the fourth).Please go take a look at how old games did this: At least an entire paragraph at once and don't drip feed it, just give me the entire thing at once. Personally I prefer the Space Quest 1 style: entire walls of text so you don't have to click multiple times to get to the end of whatever you're trying to say.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is an incredible adventure.  It's a uniquely atmospheric story told with deliciously bleak charm.  It's a short game, my own playthrough clocked in at about 9 hours, but those hours were extremely engaging.  The characters were wonderfully well written, the decisions were nerve-wracking and impactful, and the ending that I got in my playthrough was deeply satisfying.If you're on the fence about getting this, I would strongly encourage you to take the plunge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: idk if I'm the right sort of player for games like these but I'm literally on the first week and I'm not in the mood to progress but I have to since I need to hit the next story hook.Which means, playing when I don't want to or replaying content I've just played through - a bit demoralising. Thing is, it's probably not even that much further but I can't tell either so that's not really an incentive to continue playing.It doesn't help that I've mainly played MMOs, RPGs (where there's a quicksave), TD and Idle games either. I kinda get the reason why you want players to play in chunks but peoples' "Chunks" can be fairly diverse. I saw your vid addressing the save issue and I must have misunderstood as I thought you could just go to an area to save - but maybe that's still being worked on?I'll probably just let this sit and revisit it in a few months or something. Also, I still recommend this game, the graphics are solid and I'm enjoying the soundtrack. I'm still early in it but I can kinda see how character focused it is - although it appears that the dialogue options aren't branched (again probably too early to tell) as I'm going for a certain mood in my responses e.g. the photographer where you have the option of being angry at her or not but at the end of the conversation you can still be angry at her - kinda doesn't gel with being nice earlier (but that might just be me)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great narrative focused indie game. For me, the main highlights are the art, the music, the narrative, and the characters.The art can be incredible, especially when the game takes a chance to show the scale and beauty of a particular scene. There are a couple near the end that are especially fantastic. The music has great moments too, there are some really great original songs. I especially loved the sea shanty Grimley writes for the captain. My main wish was that they did more of them! Love a good sea shanty.The story and characters are fantastic. While it feels a little slow in the middle, on the whole the narrative is engaging with a good hook and satisfying payoffs. Each of the major supporting characters feels like a geninue, fleshed out person, that you can connect with and be frustrated with in their own unique way. I wish we had gotten to know more of the minor characters, and that who they were played more of a role in their interactions and your choices throughout the game. I imagine it would have been really compelling (and brutal) to have to make a choice about who to give resources to if, for example, Ward is less effective as a worker because he has one arm, but he's a father whereas more capable characters might not have any family. Even without that though, some of the scenarios in the game are incredibly compelling. That moment with Cordell near the end was especially brutal, but felt like a genuine consequence of what was happening and I appreciate that the game didn't pull any punches. That one's going to stick with me.For me, the place where the game didn't stand out as much was in the moment-to-moment gameplay. While not bad, I feel like they set up a lot of potential for tough, complicated choices, that they didn't have a seem to follow all the way through on. Even on hard it's pretty easy to get to the end with everyone safe and sound. The day-to-day management and choices was also a bit shallow. It wasn't bad by any means, but I think pushing deeper would have elevated an already great experience.Last note, I do love the save tree system, and I love the way they worked it into the story! Overall, a cool experience and I'll be following the studio to see what they come out with next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: So you make choices, from limited options who doesn't seem that much better or worst than one another and hope you choose the "correct" one to keep progressing...Pros:Nice artworkGood dialogueStory is somewhat interestingCons:Gameplay is rather boring, you answer requests from your crew, take decisions that will either help you or f you, no way for you to know, then you go through the different deck levels, healing the sick, feeding the crew, gather some coal to heat the furnace, click on the character, listen to what they have to say. Rince and repeat.Gameplay keeps in the way of the story.You think you're taking the right decision but this game isn't open too much on what are the correct choices.Which mean you'll just reload if you f up and try a new line of choices.The game doesn't help you too much on how it works for gathering food, research, supplies, etc, and on how to use those ressources, its trial and error and there aint too much space for error in this game.I choose everything I could in the benefactum of the crew and yet not too long into the game the boat was crushed under the ice and everyone died. So I guess the only correct choice was to abandon ship...Needless to say after everyone died I was pretty much done with the game as I didn't feel like to reload a previous save and go through all the choices again. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played this style of game before, so I cannot say if this review will be of use to many. But i found the game to be wonderful. I was a little nervous at the idea of making wrong choices, but the game seems entertaining and challenging no matter the choice. A couple of small bugs but nothing fancy, far better than any modern triple A game :DWonderful, a lovely art style and great characters!I have since finished a route of the game and can confirm its still as wonderful as 2 hours in :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: My review is of the initial part of the game (roughly the first 30 minutes). it's more of a "does it succeed in pulling my into the world...etc"I can safely answer YES. The team does a great job at crafting a narrative that strikes alot of emotions.It also really makes some AAA devs look very lazy in their own games. and the gaming space needs that more so now than ever.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this to any fan of tense story telling games. The music is phenomenal and sets the mood impeccably. The characters are well rounded with a good variety in personality, the conversations are fluid and show emotion. The jargon used is easy understandable from context. Most of all the art, words can barely do it justice. This game has a lot of difficult decisions that make the replay ability phenomenal, after finishing the first playthough  the save game system makes more sense.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's easy to get lost in this world for hours. Compelling story and gameplay that is thankfully free of many of the timewasting tropes a lot of modern similar games use to pad our content. I think about what's coming up next when I'm not playing it which is amazing. This is not a triple A title or the next GTA, but for a narrative driven survival game it's definitely worth the asking price and has learned it's lesson's from similar games very well and improves upon them in a lot of ways. It's hard to review a game like this without spoiling the plot so I'll leave this here. Grab it, bargain!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. A bit slow at start, but once it starts rolling the storytelling is great. It keeps you on the edge. Only a one or two frustrating moments, no big deal. I'm not big on narrative-based games (i.e. without action), but was pleasantly surprised with this one.PS: to find link to their discord, check their front-page video on their youtube page. _childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent but flawed game. I had fun with it, and can definitely recommend it to others who like the survival genre.Among the strong points is the writing. The characters have believable characterizations, the dialogue charming and humane and I never really felt like my time was being wasted, even though there is a whole lot of writing in the game. Because it made me curious. What is this character feeling and thinking in this moment? So yeah, kudos on that front.I will say though, these people are perhaps some of the toughest people around. They really do not show the stresses from their circumstances as much as I'd expect. Though I suppose I do prefer overly tough characters than characters who turn murderous at the first sign of trouble (The Walking Dead, for example).One of the big weak points is actually the gameplay. There's a few menu bugs here and there at the time of writing this, though the biggest issue is that... Well, the resource management.(Gameplay spoiler)On the other hand, and a lot more glaring issue wise, is that there is two things that's absolutely broken in terms of how good it is, spoilers for an amazing strategy ahead: Finally, the actual resource management is way too tough if you don't play dirty with the games mechanics. Each entire bloody penguin gives you 6 food, and you need 50 to avoid malnourishment. That's 8 penguins a day. EIGHT PENGUINS. Who the hell eats that much?! And you also need to feed the furnace at the same time, which is less efficient generally speaking; so now we're eating eight penguins and burning 8 big penguins. And the game really doesn't give you any way to actually produce that amount of resources in a day, so the  become a necessity.The real kicker as to why the above kind of sucks is that it really adds a layer of ludonarrative dissonance. (Strategy spoiler) The only resource that really acts like I'd expect it to is Decorum (morale).---All in all, to me, this game is perfect if you want a survival *narrative* game, and less perfect if you desire good survival mechanics. Though, to be fair, the survival mechanics are serviceable, so they don't detract from the narrative; and the narrative is interesting! So if 'story rich survival game' sounds like your type of deal, it can definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best video game experiences in my life. This game is pure art.I was never a visual novel kind of guy, but this game has me completely in clutches. It's a survival game, and not an easy one. I am completely emerged as the character and totally invested in the fates of my crewman. When I lost a couple of them I've backed up several levels to not lose a single soul. I am only on the 15th "week" in the game and already had a bunch of OMG moments. This is one special gem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: In The Pale Beyond you are the first mate on a ship that sails to the south pole to discover what happened to another ship and its crew. But when catastrophe hits, you suddenly have to prove yourself as a leader of your small team, keep your sailors alive and motivated and lead them through cold ocean and ice.The game feels like a more personal Frostpunk, so you get to know and care about the people that you could lead to their demise; the story seems heavily inspired by the story of "the Terror", that has also been made into a series. The games difficulty is pretty high, it's highly unlikely that you make it through the game on your first try without having to step back on a save a few times, but after getting to the end(s), I have to say, the story and characters are well worth the effort to reload a few times to fix a few mistakes you might have made along the way.All in all this game is a hidden gem that should get more attention and acclaim.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This one will definitely end up on my favourite games of the year list. The art style is gorgeous and every character so unique. Not only in their looks but also in personality. The team really paid attention to every little quip and every phrase, so not a single sentence feels out of character after they are introduced. In a game without voice acting, I find that very impressive. The environments are stunning, even though there aren't a lot of animations in the game, they still managed to give a sense of movement with partical effects. And it just looks so good!The sound design and music are beautiful as well. Especially the crunchy sounds of the ice whenever something goes wrong really impressed me. The soundtrack is a joy to listen to, really chill on one hand but when the emotion hits, the music really knows how to pull you in.For me the game finds the perfect balance between the vusial novel and the resource management. Overall, I think the game falls on the easier side, once you figured out all the gameplay mechanics. It's not a This War of Mine, it's much more chill.The story is decent, but the game definitely shines the most narratively when interacting with the characters. I love all of them!This one gets a definite recommendation from me!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It was a great journey, that I didn't expect.Great story with clever management system - the game is both cozy and stressful, because week to week I worry for the fuel and food. The first time, we all died, the second - we all survived against the harsh elements, and we even all liked each other. The game puts you on the spot that you weren't prepared for, ask you to make decisions you don't know outputs of and ask you to raise to the challenge. I was very much entertained.There are minor issues: adjusting slider at the end of the week sometimes just doesn't respond, and a few times when I load a previous week, I haven't seen the dialogs. But it was all fixable, so don't worry and sail ahead!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got around to playing this game. First off, it is the perfect Steam Deck game. A nice narrative choose your own adventure style game that has a nice immersive feel, great story with a bit of mystery to it and game play mechanics that are easy enough to learn. I enjoyed the story and how the game flowed and I recommend this game to play through for the story alone. With that being said, there were plenty of problems with the game that I feel could be polished on in a sequel. The way you get scurvy and frostbite was kind of confusing and could have been explained better or used different colors/icons to indicate what was going on. The way you get materials and find things out through the story was very limited, I felt that half the time the crew was just sort of pointless. You never had the opportunity to add more crew members throughout the missions and the daily tasks could have contributed to the story more. I felt there was a missed opportunity to make the hunts and scavenging missions more interactive, maybe make a little mini game where you press some buttons, move an analog stick around, match some colors, literally anything to make it more interactive than just press button, go about your day. I personally will not replay the game as I got pretty much all I wanted out of it by the end of it and after you kind of reached land I felt that the game kind of had a weak middle point as far as story and direction went but like I said, overall, very pleased with the game all minor critiques considered.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game purports to be steam deck verified, but early on you're asked to take the wheel, at which point you're supposed to use a mouse right click to pan around, and you're scuppered. I found the game very promising up to that point, but have been unable to find a workaround, therefore I have to give a negative review for now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not good at resource management games, and really this is my first one. Consequently, I've killed everyone twice, but I've learned a LOT from those early mistakes and I'm moving forward. The game is engaging, fun, tragic, and rewarding. There are a few minor bugs the Developer has been very open about and seem to be getting fixed fast, so I'm not even concerned by them. If you like story and character-driven games where your decisions actually matter (not like "Duck will remember that..." and then it never comes up again, but like... people die when you mess up here), this is a good game for you. Pros:* Excellent Art* Decisions Matter* Bad choices are punishing but feel more fair once you've learned the game a little more (see below)* Great music* Excellent atmosphereCons:* A few bugs (again, being worked on)* Not the clearest UX in the world, but you do figure it out but a tutorial moment would help (if it's there I missed it)* Limited voice acting and LOTS of dialogue.     Note - I don't really mind this one because it usually takes people longer to voice act a line than it takes to                 read it, but I know it would bother some people. A toggle would be excellent, but also voice actors                 for every line in this game would be cost prohibitive for an indie dev. * Bad choices are still punishing, even if they feel fair eventually. Out of the box, for me this is an 8/10, and I think it'll be a 9/10 soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit like Frostpunk if you cared about your citizens. And it's one of the very few games of the genre (management, survival) I've played that actually makes you (forces you if you want good endings) care for almost every single character. Survival and tough decisions are made harder and more impactful if you will be genuinely sad if someone dies/leaves/gets crazy.The way the game manages to have you care is that you need to learn how each person wants to be treated, but while this might make you seem like a people-pleaser as a character, it forces you as a player to actually listen to the characters and remember things about them.To go into some light spoiler territory, of course you will need to please people. They don't know you, and yet they have to trust you, and of course they won't obey your authority if you try to enforce it our of nowere. You will need to respect them, their character, their needs, and even their quirks if you expect to get respect back. And there are absolutely times when you need to step up and show authority (like ).One point that might be negative is that by the end of the game, I knew so much about the people and was so invested in the decisions I made that I didn't want to try and play a different branch. This was my story, the story of me and my crew. It wasnt' perfect by a long shot but I was happy with the results. You can absolutely try to replay things (some fourth wall breaking shenanigans encourage you even to do it), but I think I'll come back after some time has passed to enjoy the story once more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The good:Beautiful art and atmosphereWell written charactersChoices matterThe bad:As of version 1.2.2.2; bugs, bugs and more bugs, most noncritical, UI and controller (played with steam deck) orientedVery unlikely to reach the end of the game on the first trySome of the endings reveal some hidden secrets that I do not think match with the rest of the themes and the game itself, and I think that paradoxically more generic secrets would fit better with the story itself. Because of that it feels like the game thinks it's smarter than it is, or is trying to use a trope that I do not think is needed. Cannot say more without spoilers.The game is trying to seem like it has a lot of replay-ability, but if you get your decisions somewhat right in the first 90% of the game then all you need to do is repeat the last 10% to discover everything. Unless you want to experiment with "bad" decisions.It might sound like I dislike the game, but that isn't true. As a software developer myself  I know (at least some) of the challenges indie developers face and I value the effort put into this game and I see a lot of love and passion from Bellular Studio in it. There is a lot to love and enjoy and I feel the price matches the experience. I however do think that the game is trying to appear a bit better, or *smarter* than it is, especially with some of its themes in some of the endings, and would actually be better overall if it stayed true to its original atmosphere and presentation.I'm quite impressed with this being the first game from the studio and I am looking forward to seeing more games in the future, no matter if in the same genre or something completely new.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I have not been this emotionally invested in a game for years, this has honestly instantly become one of my favourite games ever.!! Please note this is much more of an interactive story than a traditional video game, so if you are here for combat and more traditional gameplay mechanics, you will not find it here. THOUGH THIS IS NOT A BAD THING !!I usually ONLY play games for the gameplay, I couldn't give a damn about the storyline in most games that I play, I do not read books, I do not care about lore, I just want to fight stuff, so the fact that I adore this so much is a real testament to how well made and gripping it is. I will be playing this again and again for all the different endings.The story is so rich, the characters are deep, the writing is powerful, and I cried on multiple occasions throughout, especially during the later chapters.if you are in the mood for a truly moving experience, and you're not afraid of tough decisions, powerful emotions and a very dark and challenging story line, do yourself a favour and play through The Pale Beyond.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really love the concept and micro-management of the game but it has 2 flaws I hope to see it resolved if the game sells well. 1.) It DESPERATELY needs voice acting. I don't like clicking a thousand times to advance dialog options. 2.) It needs a difficulty slider. Even though some feel it's fairly balanced, it needs further balancing for those of us who just want a pedestrian experience with minimal challenge. I get that it's a survival management game, but when I play 2 hours and have to restart cause I'm trying to just be a decent person, that's a little too challenging. Love the Bellular crew and their first forray into gaming, but I need that difficulty slider for super-beginners.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough, and I'm going to try again later - with a different approach in hopes of a different ending. The visual style is perhaps a bit too cutesy for this kind of a story. Especially the dogs are like from some other game entirely. Also I'm a bit disappointed that I can't order the specialists around. Nevertheless, this was quite captivating!I would recommend the Pale Beyond to those who enjoyed games like Frostpunk or the Banner Saga.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: i never really considered myself to like resource management games alot but playing this game has really changed my opinion on the genre. Having to both manage the resources and how loyal your fellow crew are to you made this an especially challenging game, but when you did make the right decision and it ended up paying off in the future made it feel so rewarding. Saving everyone or basically telling everyone to ♥♥♥♥ off is what really made me love this game. Going from the game play itself to just the simple talking with the crew made it an overall fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version: A story-driven management sim with an engrossing premise, a compelling gameplay loop, and an endearing cast of characters to root for, all accompanied by an expressive art style and gorgeous music. However, there are some gameplay aspects to be polished if there is to be a sequel, spiritual or otherwise, in the same genre. 8/10.My criticisms of the game are relatively minor gripes that didn't spoil the experience as a whole but I must still must be faithful to my own experience:(-) The UI for the dialogue choices specifically leaves something to be desired. I'm a fast reader so I usually press the Enter/Space key to keep that pace; however, every time a prompt appeared, the Enter/Space key would automatically be read as an input on the choice and I would say something I didn't mean to without reading it. Since "The Pale Beyond" auto-saves on a in-game week by week basis that could mean reseting the whole week if the mistake was big enough, so beware of that. And the more you replay, the faster you want to go through repeated dialogue you can't otherwise skip... I recommend using your mouse to click through text. I put this as a lack on the designer's part because other games, "Disco Elysium" to give another text-heavy example, deal with the problem by linking player choices with keyboard's numbers. Despite having many, many more dialogue choices than "The Pale Beyond" I never once pressed an option by mistake on "Disco Elysium".(-) On the subject of choices... Despite the replayability aspect being baked into the plot itself, there isn't as much wiggle room in the narrative as one would expect. Once that sweet, first initial run is over, you might be surprised that most of the main characters are protected until almost the very end of the story, and the choice of who lives and dies is practically telegraphed: you pretty much have to ACTIVELY choose to kill someone for them to die. Which is not ideal in a setting where survival is the main source of tension in the story.(+/-) Related to that last point, as far as management sims go, this one is pretty beginner-friendly imo. Once I got the hang of the mechanics after the first in-game weeks, everything was a smooth ride from there. Surprise is the only thing "The Pale Beyond" has against you, and after the first few runs, it will become apparent. In that regard, it might be TOO forgiving with some mechanics --and I made my playthrough unnecessarily harder by expecting a more grueling experience--, which I don't think hard mode necessarily remedies. Here are two examples:*You might think that the 100/100 food/fuel meter is how much you have in your camp as a whole, but no. It's something you have to fill week by week, which means that, *minor spoilers ahead* during the first few weeks on the ship, you have UNLIMITED food/fuel in your storage, only limited by how many units you want to assign to the task itself. So you can stockpile during the prologue, and that can carry you FAR.*Warming up the ship to thaw Freezing units costs no additional fuel. Zero. Zilch. Nada. It's free. This is immense when Winter reaches the South Pole. One week during mid-game, I had six crew members freezing and made the choice to warm them up no matter the fuel cost or otherwise have them progress into Frostbitten and make my medical bay collapse. What was a hard choice that might kill me down the line completely lost its value because I realized that I could amp the temperature forever. From then on, managing heat became almost trivial.*With the exception of Grimley (kinda? ), it's really easy to tell which options will net you points with each main crew member --which isn't the WORST, mind you--. But what is baffling to me is that there's no mechanic for breaking their trust, which removes an incentive to role-play. E.g. Templeton will usually confide with you privately about what he thinks you should do; you can agree with him verbally and do the exact opposite of that, and it won't incur ANY additional penalties. In fact, it's optimal to do this because the extra approval you net for lying will soften the hit you will take for not taking his advice.(+/-) My last criticism is perhaps more nitpicky but I thought that the Voting section was such a cool idea that only came up twice: once at the beginning (which you can't lose) and in the ending routes. This makes grinding for Trust with your crew way less urgent once you realize you have the whole game to do so, I played a lot of the game under the impression that there would be narrative curveballs that would force more Voting sections and losing them could significantly impact the choices I could make. Still, since you're Substitute Captain, it would be weird if you didn't have some vetoing power, so I admit that maybe THIS game in particular would have problems implementing this idea further. But it has a lot of potential.In conclusion, great, fun game with some caveats that I really hope the Devs keep improving on. If you aren't convinced, buy it on sale.
