_childDocuments_.review: A really drawn out annoying and frustrating experience.After the first failed play through a couple of hours in I really didn't feel like sitting through that again to get where i was with a few changes to get past where i was.At least when frostpunk kicks you in the nuts you can see where you went wrong and you don't have to sit through the same 2hour movie you just watched to continue.Its like trying to watch the lord of the rings extended trilogy where you have to restart occasionally.Looks nice though.Edit:To add some clarification the visuals were nice and the dialog/writing was goodThe problem is the game play, choices feel arbitrary and random.Even if there is a week by week tree to go back on which i didn't notice at first that doesn't help with the game play problems, sure I could keep reloading and making random choices until something works but where is the fun in that if there is no logic to it?It is like compiling a maths equation where i don't know what the end result is or the parts...A + B + X + Y = ZI don't know what Z is so i randomly assign values to A/B/X/Y until Z = winReloading random weeks in this branching save system to blindly make changes to the choices with no logic to it is tedious.May be if it wasn't such a long process to see what these arbitrary changes to choices did and how it effects the story were quick then maybe but as it stands it only nailing the frustration of being trapped powerless on the ice in the middle of nowhereIt feels like a more frustrating version of a visual novel with branching paths where the illusion of game play keeps breaking the immersion.At least in frost punk (as an unforgiving ice based resource management game) I could see ok everything went to hell at this point because i didn't plan for enough fuel/heating which i could see the lead up to the failure so now I could load a save 20min ago and address the plan for that.In my play through of this ♥♥♥♥ went sideways so fast out of nowhere i still have no idea what happened or how it could have been avoided or why things were happening without just replaying the entire thing from the start and RNGing more choices.I mean the game was a good effort but i feel the game play was designed by someone who was designing puzzles with the answers in mind and not thinking about people who didnt have those answers so they didn't think about the logic of the answers from the point of view of people who did not have them.Kind of like a magic trick, im sure its logical to the magician who has performed it a million times but hell if i know how ♥♥♥♥ is randomly appearing out of nowhere because he designed the trick to be surprising not to be easy to figure out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gem of a game!I just finished playing it a second time, only 11 survived the first time and it gutted me.I'm a huge RPG and story driven games nerd and THE PALE BEYOND really drew me in fast. An experience unlike anything I played before. Beautiful art style and mesmerizing music.It's as much a resource management sim as it is a relationship sim. I would argue the characters are what makes this game special. It's a really well written narrative with believeable grounded characters that grow on you and make you care. Some great humor too.  I cried a few times towards the end. I got all kinds of emotional seeing these people struggle and then overcome these struggles with my help, see them butt heads only to respect one another at the end. Earning their loyality feels great.The endings are well done and I enjoyed learning what happened to the crew. I just wish the sailors got an epilogue too. They do have personality but they ultimately don't matter for the narrative and are forgotten at the end. That is my only gripe with the game.I believe the big reveal at the end could be divisive. I can understand why some people wouldn't like it. It definitely wasn't what I expected. But I rolled with it.If the devs are reading this: GREAT JOB!Please make more such games. It was a wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Only three weeks into the game, will be playing it slowly and might update when I'm done with it. This game is like if the ship management component of Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire was expanded upon into a Pentiment-like game. As a big fan of these Obsidian titles I am liking this game a lot. It is gorgeously drawn, well written and has a wonderful soundtrack. I do have one issue with the game though. It isn't immediately obvious when the game is safe to quit; I had to redo one week because you apparently have to climb to the top deck before it saves. I am also not too fond of the fact that I have to complete the week before the game saves. I wish games would bring back save states or something. As such I quit out of the game every time I finish a week so that I can pick the game back up when I am sure I will have enough time to fully complete a fresh week.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of Bellular, I had to try the game made by his studio once it released.For a first title, it is quite extraordinary, and it's really quite captivating to start with. Many developers just simply fail to deliver a compelling narrative, even in story driven games like this one, but Bellular Studio has me really invested right away. On top of that, the game is all about resource management and replayability, which is not something that's easy to pull off.I'd say this game, besides a few bugs here and there, is a solid game worth its money. I'm looking forward to seeing more games from Bellular Studios, and I'm actually quite excited to replay this game for the perfect ending. I'm not a completionist, but I am a hopeful feller.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Well written, very tense, and really succeeds at making you feel hopeless. The game is intentionally very slow-paced, so make sure you're up for that before you play. There were some quirks with the UI, like dialogue boxes not showing up or the inventory closing when crew notifications appear. I'd like to see more intuitive keyboard controls, like returning from the scouting screen to camp when I hit Escape.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: A charming survival sim, you are put as the captain of an expedition that gone wrong. You must manage your people and resources carefully while also not getting on the bad side of people. There's a reputation system pick the wrong dialogue and they dislike you, pick the correct one and you're +5 social score. The best way i'd describe the game it's "stressfully cozy" The music, artstyle and setting is cozy but the options presented will make you second guess everything and everyone. There is a small mystery as far as the story goes as to why you are there and what happened to parts of the crew. To learn that you will need to either pick carefully your dialogue, sacrifice your social credit score or  have multiple playthroughs. Depends if you're a slow reader or not this game will last an average 7-10 hours so if you are curious enough for a second different playthrough it's worth it. As far as the price goes i think it's okay, 17 euros on release and 20 at full price. It's a good price for the playtime but if you're on the fence get it on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of survival games, I was impressed by The Pale Beyond's consideration and attention to detail. The game features excellent music and art, and its narrative is well-written and thoughtfully crafted. The branching conversations add depth to the game's moody atmosphere and make it easy to get lost in.I found The Pale Beyond to be enjoyable and easily got into it. Its gameplay balance is challenging and well thought-out, and the tension is real when trying to overcome hard situations. The game's flaws are minor and tolerable, and the ending isnt amazing but satisfying. Overall, I highly recommend The Pale Beyond to anyone looking for a well-designed, atmospheric, and engaging survival game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Nice Graphic Novel / Survival game. Game did a pretty good job at capturing what it feels like to be the captain of a dangerous expedition to the Antarctic. Tough decisions for a tough missionMy only issue with it is something that is hard to explain without spoiling the game.The way they integrated a certain system into the game for when you finished a playthrough really breaks the whole immersion to me. Let's just say that with that mechanic and "how it affects the story's ending" just makes my first playthrough and subsequent ones fairly insignificant in the grand scheme of things. It demotivates you from playing in my opinion. (It's kinda how it felt after Season 3 of Lost lol)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: this game is beautiful, really well-written, and really interesting. a very unique resource management and visual novel esque typa deal going on here. i didn't find it hard at all on normal difficulty, which i'm not sure if that's a good or bad thing. never had anyone die or anything of that sort, though it's clear such things are possible if you aren't careful.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best narrative driven games I have ever played, it is definitely up there with Disco Elysium in terms of choices and art, music and story direction. The game is an amazing mix of resource management and choice driven game. I felt thought the entire game that I always had control of the direction I wanted to take. I have only completed my first playthrough and i can see that is has a good amount of replayability. I cannot recommend it enough if you like a game where your choice have an effect in game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I had the chance to play test an early build of this game and enjoyed myself enough that I picked up a copy as soon as I could, and am looking forward to really diving in once my exams are finished.From my play so far I'm enjoying the characters, setting, and player choice within the story.It's not a sandbox style game but there is a lot of exploration and unlocks (both story events and tech).Game offers multiple end game states as you navigate the story attempting to keep your crew alive (and loyal).This is the sort of game that has a short single play through time along with replay value so you could to a full play in a couple session over a weekend with total play composed of several weekend runs as you explore the various paths.For folks who enjoy story and choice driven games this is an easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful story, graphics and game overall. Not actually difficult to survive and save everyone, just save on fuel or food (fuel is easier to save).Love the Terror undertones - the game is heavily inspired by the TV series, which in turn is made from Dan Simmons' Terror novel, a fantasy take on 1848 Franklin's expedition.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim when I saw it was on sale. I like resource management and stories so why not. Little did I know I would laugh, sob, and commit unspeakable acts to bring a 2d crew I loved home. 10/10 would recommend if you like questioning every decision you make and the real burden of leadership. I feel like I went through this all again and again and again to get the ending. But it’s done this time! Ay ay captain!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game is reading a novel. Which is fantastic if that's your thing. But the studio would have done well to hire an optional voiced narrative for the game so people could have that experience if wanted. It wouldn't have costed that much, as you can hire some interesting audio book voices for around 500-1000 even cheaper if you go independent. Or better yet Michael could have done it himself and saved the money. I think it would have appealed to a wider audience. Like it or not people do not like reading long slogs anymore overall. Blame who you want or what you want but it is true.Overall the game is 20,000 Leagues under the sea, meets Monkey Island with elements of Alive (the true story of the crashed soccer team). There are many good things here but the way they chose to make it digestible to the audience isn't for everyone.Divide that by the bugs and UI issue and honestly I would have rather they  just write a novel.This game feels like it should have been a rogue like Darkest Dungeon with a narrative thrown on top after the a series of battles.I hope they consider a more refined narrative experience with a rogue like for their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: First of these types of story-driven games are not my usual cup of tea,but after follow the developers YouTube channel for more yearsthen I can remember I thought I would at least support them andgive it a shot, and I'm glad I did.Really enjoyed the experience.Good stuff.The music is phenomenal.Rest of the sound design is also great.Art is also amazing.Love the setting of the game.The characters are rich with personality.Choices that do matter.Enjoyable food/fuel/moral loop.Love the save system, being able to go back and see different paths whenI've finished the game without replaying the whole thing.Did I say the music if phenomenal.The minor issues.Mostly graphical glitchesCharacter portraits getting stuck on the screen (which was fixed by just swiping them with the mouse)Screen going all black with only the markers showing (which was fixed by just entering the "world map" and back again.I just picked up the book on audio that inspired the game and will give that a listen asap.Congratulations on a great game Micheal, Thomas and the rest of Bellular Studios.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Considering that I have over 30 hours in this game and have gotten every achievement and ending the game has to offer, it is quite clear that I enjoy this game and consider it very worth my while. ——Summary -The Pale Beyond is a game I recommend for its stunning art, music, characters and interesting story. It is a point and click style resource management game with choices that can get difficult to make and a story you can easily become invested in. The game is very dialogue-heavy, making it slower-paced than the common Frostpunk comparison. I can imagine that it isn’t for everyone, but it works well for players who are more invested in the story and characters. Its main issue is that it experiences performance issues the more you play, majorly issues with crashing and softlocking. I found the issue is easily solved by clearing out your save files, but it could still get frustrating. Some people may find the gameplay mechanics to become repetitive, but personally, I quite enjoyed it as a whole. The game, at the time of writing, is about a year old, so these issues may or may not be fixed. I’m hoping that they will, as this game really deserves more of an audience. ——To elaborate;Pros-The art in this game is phenomenal. Both backgrounds, assets, interface, and characters are stunningly illustrated with a lot of personality and emotions. While being mostly a point-and-click game, the sheer range of art, expressions, and variants of every sprite genuinely amazed me through all playthroughs, as I would find a new one almost each time. The music perfectly matches the ambience of the game and creates an atmospheric experience. The characterization is also very impressive; all characters have very specific personalities, goals, values and ways they like to be spoken to, woven in with a loyalty system that is a lot more in-depth than I had expected. The game sets itself and its play styles up very well in the prologue, matched with challenging points that take time to learn and plan how to best allocate the scarce resources you have.There is a plethora of routes, endings and dialogues that you can get depending on the choices you make, matched with an interesting premise and characters that are easy to grow fond of. Cons-The game is quite buggy and prone to crashing. The two problems I’ve experienced the most is rouge assets and the game becoming slow and crashing completely.I’ve found that the more I played, the more it took for the game to load, save, and boot up. Each time it would save at the beginning of every in-game week, it would softlock itself for a couple of minutes as well. Once again, the issue can be solved by cleaning the saved files.In rare instances it would crash my computer completely. I will admit that I am not sure how much of it is the game's fault and how much of it is my computer, but I have not had an issue with a game like this before. This also extends to achievements, some taking a couple of attempts to become logged and counted.———All in all, it is a very nice game; I enjoyed it thoroughly, and I hope it is played by more people as it deserves more appreciation :-)!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic narrative, wonderful characters! I found the resource management to be pretty easy to manage after the first go around when I had no idea how things worked. Knowing that hunting nodes are consumed whether you send one or four people to it is an important thing to know. The save tree is certainly a very interesting addition.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: First of all you can pet the dogs so what else do you want? :DI got sucked into the game right away for few hours. Overall very good game with solid gameplay, nice music and great atmosphere. Gameplay looks similar to Dead in Vinland but with better written dialogues. I am not sure if you can eat the crew in the game but it certainly has the "Terror" vibes.Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: I am obsessed with this game. Accidentally stayed up until 5am one night because I had to see the mission through. The art is gorgeous, the characters interesting and the story kept me enraptured. The ending I got the first time hooked me, as it was nothing I was expecting. Now I am so enthralled with the story line that I keep replaying it. Without giving away too much, hopefully, I will offer a Trigger warning related to the sled dogs. This is a survival, Arctic adventure, there are very unhappy outcomes so keep that in mind when trying to decided if you can handle some of the scenarios (again especially related to dogs). I felt so many emotions and I expect to be hyper fixated on this game for a while to come.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game, liked it more for the story then the gameplay which I found difficult.Story seems to take inspiration from Ernest Shackleton's Endurance expedition, but if not it did a good job at getting me to look into it.If you're looking for a game with a good story but are off put by difficulty there is a helpful guide that shows you how to make the game easier on yourself in the steam guides
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic artwork, great music, and (as a whole) a wonderfully crafted narrative. The gameplay will potentially not be for traditional fans of the survival genre, but those who enjoy games that are equal parts movie (or in this case, book) will be quite happy. All in all, I would happily recommend this to people who want a relatively quick — in my case, less than ten hours — game to play through and get some beautiful moments in the process. This game will live in my memory for quite some time, though I do wish there was a bit more diversity in the general game loop.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Finally finished the game and man what a fun concept. Give the game your time and the characters your attention and you'll find yourself warming up to them as they warm up to you. I think once you start out there's a little bit of a learning curve as you don't really know what the next few weeks in the expedition can hold. But once you get your understanding of mechanics, you'll find that you make for a good ship AND ice fairing captain.If you like narrative stories with likeable characters and a freezing twist definitely check this out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It´s a lovely game telling a fantastic and intriguing story,which pulls you in so easily.It even more inspired me to write my own stories and combine them with my second passion which is videogames. You can really feel these characters have their own souls and even tho there can be the grumpiest person you ever met,you still find yourself coming to love them as everyone else.Each person has there own ways to look at life and you can see that nobody is really wrong in their own eyes ,nobody means wrong to others,yet  you can see and feel those conflict bubble.If there is anyone who loves fantasy books and videogames,if you loose yourself daydreaming about adventures. I can only recommend this game to you and I hope you will enjoy it the same way I did.Thanks for your attention. Love to the studio that made this and every person who contributed <3 I´ll be happy to support you in the future
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very good.A true labor of love game.Visual novel + resource management, some branching narrative elements, beautifully executed, and had my heart racing in my chest multiple time for so many different reasons.I will not write a narrative critique , as I want you to experience this for yourself, cheers.Word of warning, it is... very dark in places, and will absolutely rip your heart out
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: If you like a combination of the following: story based games with light "chose your own adventure" game style elements, light "ressource-juggling", slow paced gameplay, survival stories, arctic / naval settings, end of 19th century / turn of the 20th century setting, and hand drawn art,  you will probably like the game. I certainly did. Knowing that you are in a dire situation and can not succeed in every way yet knowing that some decisions might sentence crew members to death was a big part for me. Not setting but gameplay wise it reminded me of The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante which I also enjoyed a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game! If you're a fan of The Oregon Trail, 60 Parsecs, or other similar games you will love this one. It really is pretty difficult, I personally don't like the fact you can load any previous week instead of just starting over from beginning, but neither here nor there. The food and fuel is REALLY hard to comeby once you're stuck on the ice, and only gets worse from there. I made it to 26 weeks and the last 10 were just me pushing to survive as long as I could for an inevitable death. Compared to other games of the same type, this one plays a lot more fun than the others and has a loyalty system invovled that is ever changing and will creep up on when it effects you or not. Some people you think you won't be able to please..get them dead early just saying lol. Games that normally have this top down view are difficult for me to see, but the zoom in/out feature is reallly helpful in that regard. ALSO THANK YOU devs for doing white-ish text on a dark background, for someone who is colorblind is the most easily visible there for me to see. Overall this game gets a 9.5/10, easily the best game I've played since 2019.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. It catches you attention and it has a good script. The characters are very well crafted and you can become attached to some of those. Even tough, it can become massive at some points, due to the lack of mechanics variation. It's all essentially point and click and the alternatives are very clear one from the other. Sometimes, dialogues are boring... But the art is sooooo beautiful!Oh, the load select screen is not good in MacOS, at least. And I can't have different saves (more than one tree).If you find it in a promotion, it's a good game to keep you entertained for 20 hours or less.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This is an initial impression and I will change he review if it gets better. At this point I've done one try and played for about 3 hours.I usually don't put out reviews this early for a game but I just had to. After my first shot at the game, I found myself very bored and disappointed.I think most people will go into this thinking they are getting something similar to Frostpunk or something along those lines. Answer is, no. Not even remotely close.What this game REALLY is mostly is a visual novel. Tons and tons of text and reading.I was getting really sick of constant clicking and clicking and clicking and clicking and clicking through dialog/textSeriously. This is 85% visual novel and 15% survival management.The other thing that was baffling was the total lack of mouse-overs or explanations of game elements. Some examples of what I mean and other ramblings:- In the top corner there is circle that is used to represent time. Above the circle is a ship. Below the circle is an arrow. So which one is showing the time? The ship or the arrow? If it's the arrow, what is the ship? If it's the ship, what is the arrow?- Why use a circle for time? This game has phases of time. Circles like this are generally used in games that have constantly progressing time. Why not just have something that says "Morning, noon, night"? This is a common method in visual novels and is also the way time moves in this.- You have traits you can choose for yourself at the start of the game, yet none of these traits are explained. The same goes for your crew. Many of them have unique traits, but you have no idea what they mean. Without explanation, they might as well say "Generic trait 1, Generic trait 2, Generic trait 3".- I would also mention that the whole gathering coal and gathering food on ship things is poorly explained and doesn't really make sense to me. You have limited supplies but you don't have limited supplies? Which is it?- There is a catastrophic event that happens/can happen early in game. The crew warns you about this, but at the same time says you have weeks before this will happen (Time progression in this happens in weeks not days). Then the event happens like 1 or 2 weeks after they tell you. If you tell me I have weeks, I am going to assume I have at least 3 or 4 if not more. Also I would expect that the crew would notice when things are getting critical and say something.After my first shot, I was left with a really sour taste in my mouth. Not from losing, but from the thought of having to trudge through ALL THAT TEXT again. Endless clicking and clicking and clicking through dialog. Yes I know that I can start again at a save waypoint. But if I'm going to start over, I'd rather start knowing what mistake I can correct from the first try.I will give this another go. Maybe later the game gets better. If so I will modify this review.But for now I'm very disappointed.---------------------Edit:So after playing again, and going all the way to day 15, I was just bored and fed up with the game. I did not want a visual novel but that's what this is. I finally quit due to being very bored and sick of all the text and clicking though it. My initial impression still remains.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10A storyline resource management game that really hits the sweet spot when it comes to merging narrative and gameplay. If you liked The Banner Saga this game is a winner (no combat tho), what might seem to be an inconsequential choice might have a big impact later in the game and merges this with a truly immersive and outstanding story (akin to Frostpunk and the Sunless Sea).If you are new to this genre of games, this game might feel very punishing and unforgiving. However this is where this game really steps it up! The "save tree" comes into play, you can go back several "rounds" and make different choices, this will not overwrite the "timeline" you left but instead creates a "branch", creating an "alternative timeline". This is great as one realises that the choice one made several weeks ago "might not" have been the wisest one while at the same time lets you "explore ahead".Not many negatives, if pressed it would be that to these kind of "rougelike resource games" some mechanics are a chore, like always "manually" looting resources every day to "get that little advantage". Overall a truly  great game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: While not my preferred style of game play the execution here is phenomenal. I found the art style, sound design, and narrative direction fit the setting perfectly resulting in a deeply enjoyable play through. I was surprised to find myself being genuinely invested in the characters, and a little disheartened by my own attempts to meta-game the situation by the end of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: ❤️❤️🤍🤍🤍This is essentially a visual novel with unforgiving survival elements based around resource management.The gameplay is basically centered around you talking to the other sailors, and making decisions along the way, while managing the crew’s happiness, temperature, and food situation. I did like how the dialogue system helped define my character and how choices affected future interactions. However, the characters themselves felt fairly shallow because of the point system rewarding you for picking the “correct” option. I would have personally liked a way to hide that information because as soon as I understood what a character valued, it was very easy to game the system and manipulate the crew into liking me. The survival elements were tougher to manage. You need to be extra mindful of how to treat negative status effects suffered, as your crew is highly specialized, and very few people can help out with another person’s job. This also means that, as soon as you lose a key individual, things start to spiral out of control. I played this game fully resigned to the fact that it was not something to beat, but a journey to experience. Having enjoyed games like  in the past, failure was something I expected, and ready to enjoy. The game is choice driven, and it’s not always clear what the consequences of your choices will be. Much of the tension comes from not knowing if you did the right thing or not. Sometimes you must make hard decisions and hope that people understand. Other times you must trust that people know what they’re talking about, and that you should heed their advice. My biggest problem with the game was that I didn’t enjoy the resource management at all. I felt like I was punished way too hard for saving resources. Reading around, it seems the best way to treat the system is to game it (alternating between using zero resources for a week and max resources the next) instead of rationing, which I felt to be the most reasonable thing to do in many situations. I also didn’t like how, in the beginning of the game, you are expected to select how much food and coal you should use prior to reaching the last port before heading out on your journey. I saw this as a tutorial, so I maxed out the resources thinking we would restock on supplies at the last stop. I assumed restocking would be the smart thing to do before heading out on a dangerous journey. But no, the game decided to punish that decision for no reason. Still, I managed to keep things under control for most of the journey after that. At least until my crew ended up losing all morale several weeks later after people started dying. When you have such a punishing game, it would be nice to at least get an interesting game over. However, the ending I got was just uneventful and rather uninspired. I would have wanted a more spectacular game over. But perhaps there is something poetic about the struggle ending in the least eventful way possible. Or maybe the design is intentionally unsatisfying in order to convince you to reload an earlier save. Afterwards, I did notice that game overs due to low morale could be disabled in the game settings, which was interesting. I do wonder if the fate of my crew could have been avoided, but at the same time I can’t say I feel very compelled to reload an earlier save to try and change things, even knowing that the option is there. The problem is that it’s hard enough to pinpoint exactly where things started to go wrong for it to matter. I personally feel content with just leaving things as they are and never play the game again - and that’s okay too.While most of the various story beats where enjoyable to me, one event stood out as rather poor. Fairly late into the playthrough, I had penguins visit and talk to me. That felt like a complete disconnect from what the game was trying to say about the harsh reality of the journey. It felt like an attempt at comedy that fell rather flat. At first I wondered if my character was starting to go crazy, but nope, that’s an actual event that happened in the game. Had the game been less serious from the start, or had it been much more silly prior to that event, I would have been more accepting of it. As it was, however, I kind of lost interest at that point. If the game doesn’t take itself serious, why should I? Another thing that speaks against the game is that it doesn’t seem to have random events, but is instead more of a scripted journey. This makes it even less likely that I would want to replay it from the beginning and give it another try.If there were random events, the developer could have put more thought into the resource system and perhaps even manipulated some numbers behind the scenes to help the player along the journey to reach a more interesting ending. All in all, this game attempts to scratch a very particular type of itch, but I personally don’t think it succeeded as well as it could have.

_childDocuments_.review: Well written narrative game with light mechanics focused on management using four main resources that trade off on each other in addition to an excellent interpersonal relationship system. The writing is good and actually had me looking up the definitions of several new terms I'd not heard before during the play. The music score interwoven with the writing scenes mesh well making this feel far more vibrant than it would otherwise.For the cons : There are some issues with the game even post bug fixes. As an example, if there is a way to add food to the 'hoosh' pot or 'fuel' to the furnace when an event closes a camp or at the very end of a day from the 'assign rations' screen I have not found it. This causes a reload if you were not expecting a particular option selected in the morning to end the entire day instantly or happen to have forgotten to add in some materials into the respective areas. This leads to you having enough materials to survive for a night but not actually being able to access them. It's a minor annoyance but it does exist.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very decent game. I wasn't expecting to enjoy it; it was just something that was amongst other games in a bundle. I only played it for the sake of having played it (I try play as many games in my library as I can). I assumed I would find it a bit boring - the store page does not entice me. I am pleasantly surprised. At first I thought I wasn't particularly interested in dialogue or anything. I just wanted to get through it. It took a while for me to actually take interest in it, the whole choices matter thing was just meh. But after a while I started to like a few characters and almost like others. After a while the game suddenly decided to grab my attention by making me feel emotions. It started getting really depressing, then it would be wholesome and back to depressing with the music too. I wasn't expecting some of the things that happen in this game and one scene in particular is pretty damn surprising and horrible.The game does a great job at being tense and being horrible. I felt like I was actually cold and hungry. Part of that would be because I actually was hungry IRL and had eaten nothing for several hours before playing this for several hours nonstop. But still, the game's depressing atmosphere is great. The ending and near the ending of the game is where the game made me feel emotions the most and some of the dialogue is really wholesome, cute and heartwarming. Othertimes people are very annoying.You lead a group of misfits who hate you, but be nice to them and be a good leader and they'll learn to respect you eventually.Spoiler: So yeah, I recommend this game, but maybe don't starve yourself like I did. I don't know why I did that but I guess the stuff I do is incomprehensible even to myself.

_childDocuments_.review: While The Pale Beyond has a good story, artwork, decision trees/dialogue options.I ran into a game breaking bug at about 90% completion that required me to rollback my save several hours and try it again, and again and again. After replaying the final scenes 3-4 times i simply just wanted it to be over. There is a map bug in the 2nd to final act that will corrupt your save if you try and rollback after a certain point. It really threw the experience for me sadly as i had dialogue options running with no graphics and scenes playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Concept is great, but the implementation is awful. I didn't think the majority of gameplay would be micromanging cliche survival resources (morale/food/cold), and would focus more on the story- that's unfortunately not the case. I watched a playthrough to see if it gets better and it's the same gameplay loop for 7 hours.UI and the save system are terrible. The slider that you use every 5 minutes is touchy and not responsive. Positive reviews are bc it's a content creator and a good concept- game is trash.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy recommend especially considering the price.The soundtrack is fits perfectly with the feeling in the game (the moment you set sail, simply spectacular) the art direction is spot on and the characters you spend time with on the expedition are very believable and well written. You genuinely feel the tension at certain critical moments and if you are not prepared for them oh baby you are in for a hard time. I won't spoil the plot but quite simply the place you are going to is not hospitable to humans at all, and you feel it!Also kudos to them for not offering a discount as a pre-order bonus (and not taking pre-orders at all for that matter) but instead offering a discount on the 1st week after launch. Very good and pro consumer move. Happy customer right here.

_childDocuments_.review: An extraordinary game, and a lovely story alongside it.The mechanism of survival will take a little while to work out, but it's very much worth sticking to it. The characters are interesting and their development is... lovely.The meta-story is also interesting, and there's a bit of replayability around that.I've played 12hrs, and I'll probably do another few... but the game has been worth every penny I paid for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is a good story. Challenging without being impossible on Normal. Very clever ways of building game mechanics of branching save games into the game's story; I didn't actually use it as of the time of writing.The team did this very well in Ink Engine. _childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is a narrative-driven survival game that is akin to other resource-management games like Frostpunk or the Oregon Trail. The frosty ice floes of the Antarctic are brutal to survive and it's up to you to manage resources, resolve disputes between the crew, investigate the true reason for your voyage, and most of all, survive.Pale Beyond's gameplay loop is consists carefully managing resources and balancing which of the crew you allocate to given tasks. Besides this, there are many important decisions you must make on behalf of the crew, with your various crew leaders giving conflicting advice on what might be best to do next. Listening carefully to your crew is  in ensuring your survival. This game does have a lot of reading, which I personally don't mind, but keep that in mind before diving in.I will say, this game does aim to feel brutal, unforgiving, and harsh in its tone - there are several instances where catastrophic events will punch you and the crew directly in the gut, forcing you to scramble to adapt - but despite this, I found the game slightly too easy. One large part of Pale Beyond is its Save Tree, where you can reload an earlier save and make different decisions that the game will save as a separate "branch", maintaining both copies of your progress. Part of the intent is that you'll eventually need to reload when your crew meets their demise.Unfortunately, I actually completed the game successfully on my first try. Additionally, many of the decisions in the game are choices that can be described as "successful" or "unsuccessful", minus a single large choice at the end. As a result, I felt less interested in going back to change my prior decisions as only wanted to change one or two small choices I made, and I didn't want to replay through the game and purposefully perform worse or lose to get achievements.That being said, there are a large number of endings depending on how you fare, and what decisions you make towards the end.Thankfully, the writing in The Pale Beyond is absolutely wonderful. The major characters of the game are popping with personality and completely captured my attention. They'll provide advice on how to proceed, they'll share details of their lives at home and out at sea, they'll argue with others, and they'll even share tender moments with one another. I generally looked forward to every opportunity to interact with the game's characters through the end. Even the minor characters are interesting - you'll overhead them chatting with one another, and all of them have uniquely written personalities as well.One thing the game's story is great at doing is striking its dark, oppressive tone. Over and over again, disaster will come across your crew, and you're forced to make the right call to ensure everyone's safety. Various members of the crew have their allegiances to different leaders, and maintaining their loyalty is something you must do carefully. I never felt truly safe on the ice floes, as you never know when the ice may crack, or the local wildlife may attack.The mystery of  also was well-executed. Many of the crew members that have been left in the dark grow tense as the journey encounters yet more obstacles in the name of a purpose that they don't even know.One last factor that stories with dark tones have is the dichotomy of light and dark. Having disasters happen that make you feel hopeless or doomed are balanced with the light at the end of the tunnel, where you have some hope that you will all survive your journey, and maybe even find what you were looking for. Some of the characters various arcs that complete towards the end of the voyage are legitimately heartwarming, especially after everything the crew has been through. One of the decisions late in the game had me in tears, since you know what you have to do, but it's simply so hard to actually go through with it.All in all, this game is completely worth the price for this great writing. I think the only flaws I can give the game are:1. Shaw (your character) is a blank slate. You can pick some backgrounds for him but these don't have any story purpose, just some flavor dialogue choices.2. The choices you make in the game are pretty much objectively good or bad choices. There's no instances where you need to pick between choices where some are arguably justifiable depending on your perspective.That being said, I enjoyed the writing nevertheless.Pale Beyond has some very nice artwork to it. The character portraits convey a lot of emotion and give plenty of insight as to how the crew carry themselves. Hammond, the engineer, stands with his arms crossed and a straight expression on his face, whereas Nutlee, the nervous doctor, often has a sheepish expression or averts his gaze with you. The maps are also quite pretty as well.The music and sound do a similarly good job as well - the ice cracks, the waves against your boats, everything carries the weight of hearing sounds in the otherwise eerily quiet white snowscape.The UI generally works well, but there are a number of bugs you may run into. Usually closing and re-opening the menu fixed these for me. Though The Pale Beyond isn't perfect, I can say I enjoyed my time with it and would generally recommend it. I think it may be some time before I start another run, especially now that I've seen most of the story and do not see other challenges I'd want to try. That being said, I'd still recommend trying and playing the game - perhaps more casual players will take more interest in the game's Save Tree system to experiment with the game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience literally saved by them adding snipping to the save tree system, the amount of misclicks that caused me to replay 5 weeks was shocking to me, this game's one difficulty is simply UNFORGIVING (and flipping you off). I had resigned to not finishing the game. the next day they added it I snipped "one week" and now i have completed the game and feel very satisfied, One thing I would liked to have heard more of was the music. need to actually add that phonograph(record player) in game ;)More than anything this game reminded me of being a child again, even the weird bugs in the game made it feel like that, this game was made with more than fantastic writing, an immersive world and an engaging interactive story. This game has soul.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: The Pale Beyond is definitely what I would call an underrated gem. While it took me an hour or two to fall in love with the game, once I did, I never wanted to put it down. I wanted to stay in this world with these characters as much as possible. This is a game where you can really feel the heart and soul that was put into it.You play as Officer Shaw, first mate of the Temperance, second in command to Captain Hunt, tasked with finding the mysteries of a stranded ship that went missing years ago and never came back. Your entire trip is shrouded in mystery, and little by little, you start discovering that things aren't at all what they initially seemed. After a somewhat slow start with the prologue, you find yourself meeting a cast of very unique and lovable characters. Over time, you start getting attached to them and rooting for them, doing your best to make them happy. After all, being stranded on the ice for months is definitely one way to make friends. Each and every character is very well written, and it takes you a while to get to *truly* know them and understand what makes each one happy. After which, you get to discover more about who they really are as they warm up to you and open up,Without spoiling anything, the story has some seriously heartbreaking moments, difficult decisions, pleasant surprises, and surprising twists that retroactively make the entire game a lot more meaningful and special. The ending(s) was also extremely well written and tied everything up beautifully!At surface level, this is a survival resource management game, yes. But don't get it twisted, The Pale Beyond is a story heavy game, first and foremost, with a lot of dialogue and choices that affect your relationships with your crew. The resource management part was very reminiscent to Frostpunk for me (cold setting, scarce food, difficult decisions), and as one of the biggest fans of that game myself, I really liked the gameplay of this one too. Essentially, you need to manage food, coal, people's decorum (i.e. their morale), and sick crewmates each week without messing up any of them, but the game is much more forgiving than the aforementioned Frostpunk even on the hard difficulty. There's a few options for what you want to assign your crew to do each week, though I have to admit, for around half of the game there's not much for your crew to do and you end up with a few idle hands.I can't review The Pale Beyond without bringing up its most astonishing aspect: the art. The amount of detail that is put into these hand-drawn characters and environments is INSANELY stunning! It has some of, if not the prettiest portraits I have ever seen in a video game. I was completely blown away by the amount of different artworks were made for this game too! You got almost 30 different characters with different facial expressions and physical states, and you got COUNTLESS environments that were all highly immersive, vibrant, creative, and simply beautiful! Some of them were only on screen for a few seconds as well, so I always had my finger ready on the screenshot button. I simply cannot praise the art in this game enough...Another thing that has to be highly commended is the OST and the sound design. The OST has everything, chill tracks for a relaxing scene, tenser stuff for serious situations, and wholesome tunes for all the heartwarming parts, and it all fits so perfectly! The sound design was also very detailed, which added a lot to the immersion.- Now, if I had to criticize a couple things, I would say that some of the choices definitely didn't hold as much weight as the game makes you think. In particular, there's a decision that is somewhat close to the end that the game makes up to be very important, but then you quickly realize that it didn't matter whatsoever. Another thing that might turn some people off is that, it's kinda hard to lose in this game. - While it is a resource management game, even if you do a bad job you can still make it to the end with only a few losses overall. I personally didn't mind that much at all since all I really cared about was the story and characters, but I definitely enjoyed the resource management part a lot nonetheless.- As a completionist though, one thing that bugged me a bit was the achievements. A few of them are missable/bugged and while you can easily rewind through the game's save system, a lot of them require different playthroughs, and a single playthrough for me was at least around 10 hours. I get it though, since the game has a lot of different endings and variations for those endings, so maybe the achievements are an incentive to discover them all, but I don't find it fun at all sitting through around 10 hours of unskippable dialogue that I've read before intentionally making the worst decisions just to get the achievements for the bad endings. I'll definitely be passing up the 100% badge on this one.Overall, The Pale Beyond was a very special experience that I'll be thinking about for a while, and maybe coming back to it sometime later to see my favorite characters again. If you like well-written stories and characters, or if you want a chill (pun intended) experience that isn't too tense while still being very wholesome and rewarding, I would HIGHLY recommend The Pale Beyond!Thank you Bellular Studios for this wonderful experience ❤️

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully told story that combines managing resources and making tough decisions with and for the crew. Usually I stick with action games, fighters/shooters etc but I made an exception for this game and have no regrets.There are currently some minor UI bugs but don't let that stop you from checking the game out, the atmosphere, art, music and storytelling/dialogue more then make up for it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Having never heard of this studio, I was intrigued by the art style and some of the reviews about the makers of The Pale Beyond. Having just completed the first act, I can say that this game will be going into my "must plays". It feels to me like a mix of Disco Elysium and Frostpunk, in the best of ways. The writing is engaging and each character has their own distinct voice and personality, which really sells them as individuals. The player is also given quite a few options when steering dialogue, which brings a great RPG feel to the game. The resource management is engaging and the division of labor can be intense. Also, you can pet the dogs. Overall the game is phenomenal so far and I'm excited to see how it continues.Make sure you grab the bolt action, you're going to need it.10/10 watched a man be eaten by a leopard seal.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's quiet good. For story-heavy games like this that rely on a lot of player decision, I was afraid of running into moments where bizarre logic is needed to explain the 'best outcome', but that never happened. For those going into this - go in blind, and commit to it, even through your worst outcomes.If anything, I wish there was a way to skip through text a bit faster, but beyond that, this game stands out.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is probably my favorite game of the year- and I don't normally like visual-novel style games. However this was intriguing and the glut of choices you have to react with are wonderful. I'be gone back and explored other choices, failed and failed and failed again in ways that motivated me to try again. It's delightfully difficult, and I feel like the characters- all of them you can interact with regularly- have real depth and motive and I was absolutely compelled to try and do right by the NPCs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Fun and enjoyable mechanics/gameplay. I thought the storytelling was fantastic. Every single character had a distinct personality, everybody was . Nobody was boring, flat, unbelievable, or just taking up space to fill out the game. They really did a great job in designing everyone. Every interaction was legitimate. Every dialogue choice was satisfying, I never felt like there was something I wanted to say but couldn't because the option to say that wasn't put into the game.With all of that said, there's more than enough gameplay/choice/risk that it's not just like a visual novel or choose your own adventure. I think the developers did a good job walking the line between survival simulation & storytelling. The music and artwork were also awesome. The developers are actively still updating and improving the game too. Definitely worth $20.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an unexpected surprise. I bought it to have something casual to play when I got bored with the usual suspects... I didn't expect to be forcing myself to go to sleep at 5:30am because I was so engrossed in the story that I lost track of time. Take the time to read the dialogue boxes- the characters are interesting and well-written. Awesome game for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Great story (except the ending, about which I'll talk in cons section).- Great characters with distinct personalities and motivations. You will really need to put some effort into getting to know them, and getting some of them to respect you.- Resource management, including the crew's morale as a resource, balanced in a way that makes you really feel like you're continually one step from dooming the expedition.- Good dialogues (when they aren't full of typos), where the "nicest" option often does not mean "best".- Truly difficult decisions, one of them in particular so heartbreaking I won't forget it anytime soon. - And, last but not least, I feel that the game really manages to convey some of the incredible hardship of polar expeditions.Cons:- The game's narrative is great right until the ending, which feels like it was cut and pasted from a completely different game. The moment you progress into the ending, your gritty story of hardship and survival becomes a fairy tale riddled with plot holes, and dialogue cohesion falling apart and erratic behavior of some characters makes it even worse.- The game sometimes fails to recognize some of the early decisions you make, and characters that have not been part of your crew since the beginning magically pop up in your camp 20 weeks later to have a chat.- The save system (which only lets you load the game at specific points) can be tedious when you're forced to replay 30 minutes of the game because you got caught up in dialogue and forgot to do one chore.- You need to be extremely cautious about assigning people to work, because if something more important pops up, you are for some reason not allowed to reassign tasks -- even if people doing them are right there.- The closer to the end of the game, the more typos there are, which kind of spoils the immersion.Overall I still recommend playing the game, for its story (minus the ending) and the characters. Keeping my crew alive and gaining their hard-won loyalty was the true ending as far as I'm concerned, and the real ending I'm going to do my best to forget.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review: Before anything else, I just want to say that while I am recommending this game due to the quality of the game itself, I should probably warn you of the truly game-breaking bugs. Specifically, the bug that makes the game unable to launch, preventing you from playing the game completely. When you are able to play this game, it's incredible, a real gem of a resource management survival simulator...but only when you're able to play the game. Which is not a guarantee when you try to launch the game, at all. Still, it is a really incredible game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pale Beyond

_childDocuments_.review:
Five years ago, The Viscount and its crew set sail through The Pale Passage in search of absolute magnetic South. The ship and its crew were tragically lost to the ice, never to be seen again. Her sister ship, The Temperance shall follow in her path, hoping to find answers where The Viscount failed.

You didn't ask to lead this expedition, but here you are. Stuck in the ice, Captain missing, miles from civilisation. Someone has to take charge.

Manage your meagre resources, balance safety and morale, make the hard calls, and head in the only direction you can - through The Pale Beyond.

name: Death end re;Quest 2
detailed_description: Story Mai Toyama seeks an escape from her traumatic past. She enrolls at Wordsworth, an all-girl’s dormitory situated in the small, mountainous town known as Le Choara where it was rumored that her sister, Sanae, was last seen. Hopeful, Mai seeks to find her kin, but she soon finds terrifying inhabitants which lurk throughout the town after dark. At night, Le Choara’s streets are filled with Shadow Matter—a horrific group of menacing creatures. Around every cobblestone corner, Mai discovers that her hope of finding her sister lies beneath the long-buried secrets which haunt Le Choara. Key Features Overkill Brings Huge Rewards – The Overkill system is an added feature where characters can stack damage beyond the health of an enemy for bonus experience! Try to inflict as much damage to all the monsters for bigger rewards.​ Beware of the Berserker – During dungeon exploration and battle, a faceless, black figure will appear out of nowhere. The figure will also display an area of attack once it appears. Mai and her squad must step away from the Berserker’s area of attack, as it will instantly kill anyone with one single blow. Run away from the Berserker in the dungeon or defeat all the existing monsters in the battlefield to escape!​ Day n’ Night – Mai will need to explore the town of Le Choara during the day and speak with the townspeople to find out clues as to where her sister is. By night, Mai will fight her way through dark creatures stylized in a turn-based RPG. Experience the story through the lens of a visual novel during the day and battle it out against horrific creatures by night!​ Don’t Call it a Knockback – The Knockback system is back in Death end re;Quest 2, but this time, Mai and her squad can smack Shadow Matter even harder! Combo your attacks by flinging monsters to other party members!​

short_description: In collaboration with Corpse Party scenario writer Makoto Kedouin, this horror RPG follows Mai Toyama’s search for her sister in a quiet lakeside town. She’ll unravel clues to the town’s past by day, and battle Shadow Matter by night. Can you uncover the truth before reality is consumed by darkness?

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this game is okay. It doesn't shatter any new ground over the first and I think it suffers because of that, because it does everything worse than the first.The port is very bad, having to stop and start every 30-60mins because of a soft lock bug that I got. It also suffers with graphical issues.The story feels weaker than the first and kind of drags on by the half way mark. It didn't quite capture the mysteriousness that it's forebear did, it felt kinda dull. It didn't help that the gore was toned down as part of it's censorship, which knee capped it even more.The characters are mostly forgettable and seem as more plot devices than real characters. They're kind of just there. Rottie had potential, but her obsession with Mai and mentioning her every 5 seconds just got real old real quick, it didn't feel real at all, very forced. Liliana is kind of just there, and the decisions to ignore her and move on being better decisions just drives that nail in. The side characters are mostly just bad, and considering that most have no involvement in the plot or are not in the gameplay section, they become a chore to get through. Couldn't care less about their relationships to one another. Mai is at least interesting, and being the MC, that matters.Music wasn't really worth mentioning as it's mostly the same as the first.The graphics need tuning or third party input.If you love the first game like me, you'll be disappointed. If you haven't played it, I'd advise getting the first game as the world building really requires it. But I hate to say it, I just can't really recommend it in it's current state with all of the bugs. If the PS4 version runs better, I would probably have recommended it. It had potential going on from the first, but I just felt nothing from it, it doesn't really stand on it's own.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, you've played a lot of Compile Heart RPGs, and you've enjoyed most of them. However, nothing prepared me for the original Death end re;Quest. It had good strategic combat without being too complex. The story was engaging with lots of twists and turns to keep me invested in the mystery. Even the flavor of the signature transformation sequences added something new and different. I honestly didn't know Compile Heart had it in them to make such a good game. And oh, that ending! Man, seeing how much got changed by that True End, I couldn't wait to see how they'd build on it.Answer? They didn't. This is not the most disappointing sequel I've ever played, but it is disappointing for the same reason. They lost sight of what made the original good, and their new additions don't even come close to making up for that loss.Combat? That's been dumbed down, and it makes the game world feel much less dangerous this time around.Original party members? They're back, and even playable! But their inclusion has so little impact on the game story, you'd think they were an afterthought DLC option.Constant twists, turns and Death Ends? That kind of pacing is hard, so you'll just be left with the knowledge that the creepy town is creepy until a massive info dump just before the final dungeon. Also, those Death Ends that were all over the original game? Those things that are literally in the title? There are maybe seven or eight total.Game length and variety? Well, you're mostly limited to the creepy town and the surrounding woods. And you won't be spending as much time there, because this game is much shorter.Main cast variety? There's a lot less of that here. I like the main character Mai. Her backstory is interesting, her personality makes her tough without being uncaring, and I like her look (you can't go wrong with a red jacket). There are two other meaningful party members, along with the original game's six non-DLC characters. One spends all her time gushing over Mai. The other is referred to as frail, in need of protection, and lacking in stamina, and it got to the point where the game convinced me I didn't want to keep her in my active party. They aren't one-note characters, but none of them get as much development as the first game's party members did. None of them are anywhere near as creatively designed as the first game's party members. If you were hoping for something more interesting than a glitch-corrupted girl chained to a floating chair, abandon that hope now.Intriguing supporting cast? I literally didn't come across any supporting character as interesting as the first game's shopkeeper who is glitched out and literally exists at every store simultaneously. Like I said, these girls constantly talk about how cute other girls are and little else. I'm not making any judgments about that as a general concept, but if you removed every instance of girls calling each other cute, this "dark fantasy horror" RPG would probably be 20-30% shorter, and four or five supporting characters would disappear entirely. I don't think I'm exaggerating here. It's seriously that prevalent. If that sounds interesting to you anyway, I regret to inform you that there's not even variety here. Girl A says Girl B is cute. Girl B says Girl A is cute. Girl C says Girl A and B are cute. No descriptor other than "cute" is allowed. No details are allowed. Everyone is cute in a nonspecific way.At this point, you may be asking yourself, with all these things reduced or missing entirely, why would I want to play this? Well, I have wonderful news. Have you been looking for girls talking about wetting themselves? Repeatedly? If so, look no further! Do you think every girl should be required by law to say every other girl they see is cute? This game will show you the utopia you've always dreamed of. Do you like catchy opening themes with interesting videos? The game gives you that, so full credit there.If this were a standalone game, I'd think it was fairly dull, but it showed there could be promise in future installments. As a sequel though? Massive downgrade. It feels so different, it's like it's ashamed to be connected to the first game and hides most of its flimsy connections to the original game in scenes you'll only see on a second playthrough.I played through this one pretty thoroughly, hoping it would eventually bring back that original game feel and make me glad I sprung for the Limited Edition preorder. I got every achievement, beat every mission, saw every scene... The magic just isn't here.Final verdict? If you played the original, but it's been a while, go play that again. You'll have significantly more fun than this game can offer. There's literally nothing the sequel does better, and a lot it does worse. I tried not to get my hopes too high, but I didn't try hard enough. This game's final achievement has a sequel hook, but not even that caught my interest. You failed, DERQ 2, and failure has consequences. I won't even consider that sequel. It seems my relationship with this series has hit a Death End, and it's quite a tragic event.Pros:Catchy opening song, and good music in general, much of it from the first gameDecent character designMai is an interesting main characterSome of the late-game twists were interestingVoice acting is solid across the boardCons:Weaker mystery, weaker suspense, weaker storyDull supporting castCompletely retconned Buggies to make them story irrelevantWastes the original game characters to the point I wish they hadn't been includedShadow matter appearances pad out the game by making you backtrack for 15-second stretches to kill timeDoesn't live up to the original on any levelOverall, it's certainly playable, and it often isn't boring, but it's got so much wasted potential that it's hard for me to understand why they even bothered making a sequel. I'm not mad. I'm just disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: (Expect Spoilers)For one i'm going to focus on the Censorship aspect as that is the most important to me.I originally discovered this game because the original DE;RQ1 was promoted by a YouTuber by the name of  "RomanainTvee" or just "Vee" who made a video talking about how the developers at Idea Factory for the first game actually releaased a poll asking us the fans/consumers what we wanted in their release of the game to PC.Uncensored as it was intended or the Censorship model that was released for the PS4.When it came to the PC release it was overwhelmingly in-favor of the uncensored version, open shut case.They for some reason even after knowing that the PC Community prefers uncensored/original works, asked again for DE;RQ 2's pre release. This was the first red flag.Pretty much all a characters even down to their designs are inherently censored. They're either heavily covered up under the guise of being the original designs or returning combat characters from the previous game having their original designs altered for the sake of censorship.Idea Factory cannot be trusted to not censor their games no matter the platform even though they have sufficient data to suggest that players atleast for the PC Version prefer their games to be uncensored or originally interpretation of a(n) developers work.on these grounds alone do not purchase this game or really any release from Idea Factory gonig forward.With that said. letws move on to the following...This game isn't a sequel in the sense that your favorite characters return to truly reshape or expand on the already existing world/setting. You start off with three new characters Mai, Rottie & Lilliana, in an entirely different town than Tokyo, which you can immediately become confused about if you know the setting of the first game and its conclusion.Mai Background - Abused by her father who after attempting to kill her, defends herself & is sent off to Wordsworth, this process of actually having killed someone at Age 14 does have a toll on Mai & actually has you questioning her sanity & thought process going forward.Rottie Background - Daughter of the Head Mistress of Wordsworth, exists to be Mai's Morale Pet & is often trying to get Mai to show her affection in-kind which Mai eventually starts to embrace to some degree, after being incredibly cold to her from the beginning of the story.Liliana Background - Introduced mid-story, she attaches herself as the final member of the trio. Looking towards Mai as a mother figure of sorts & all while still wanting her actual parents who weren't the best, likely abusive also, to one day return to bring her home from Wordsworth. She aslo has devoted her life to defeating demons as she has come to the conclusion that her parents were bad people because of demonic possession.With that said.. Pretty much the only characters who come back are Arata/Shina who will never actually spend time together in this game & they're not dating in this one either, despite it being implied that they were going to have that talk after all the effort Mizunashi and by extension the God of  Death did to revive Shina & achieve the true end.Ultimately for the story I'm not going to give a complete breakdown because I'm still trying to figure out the retcons and potential plot holes introduced by the time aspect like how Mai moved all the girls who died in the past forward in-time without the events of both games being effected directly.. Actually I'm not even sure what year it is in this game.But essentially it's 80% of Slice of life Yuri VN(Where nobody really hooks up or nothing intimate/sexual goes down). They have over 20 odd female students who study/live at Le Chora, all under 18 and the biggest fault is that almost none of them are really developed & yet you interact with them for the majority of the story to make the world feel more alive. Which in a way is good on paper, but none of your interactions with them really matter, takes up alot of time & ultimately they feel forgettable since they don't really add anything to the story or the mystery setting.IRIS who was given a physical avatar in the real world is now a program again, who when place in the presence of Shina the persona she loved so much, that the Ludens literally reality warped the game and merged it with reality in an effort to appease Iris. Once she was near Shina in Laptop form she ignored Shina's questions only taking answers from Mai the laptop's master, but also answers Rottie's questions.Reality Warping + Time Traveling elements make you question what's happening in the story, it's honestly all over the place if you take this story standalone with no context to the OG, and even with that context you'll be lost. I addressed one earlier in this review.Overall I'm not going to focus on Combat because this isn't Lost Ark, the Story comes first and the story alone is a reason to not grab this game. The Censorship makes this game dead in the water for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Alright, I've finished the game now and if I am to believe steam achievments I got the "true ending". It took me 12 hours to finish the game, I spend time grinding once before understanding that it was useless. It's short but honestly it's not completely a bad thing as it makes the story well paced. In those 12 hours of playtime I had to alt+f4 the game more times than I could count, everything broke, the combat system, the shop, the UI, I even had a bug where the game told me I saved but when I quit and restarted the game it didn't save the last 20 mn... In conclusion: play it for the story, however there's a ton of gamebreaking bugs and it's really short so be mindful of that before you buy.--------------------------------------------------------Original review:As of today, the game is definitively worth a play but it's really hard to recommend in it's current state, so wait for a patch.The game in it's structure is really different from the first one, there's less gameplay in the VN sections and less VN in the gameplay sections. So when you're in the middle of a dungeon you won't have 30 min of VN completely messing up the rythm of the game. The combat system is roughly the same, so it's a lot of fun until you meet a boss. And that's because the game feels really unbalanced. here's an exemple: I'm exploring a dungeon when the 3rd char finally joins the party, for some reason she's level 20 while my other characters are level 37 (seriously) just after that there's a bossfight, I go in thinking I'm overpowered since I'm 17 levels higher that what the game wants me to be, however the boss kills me in one hit....So every single turn I have to sacrifice one of my actions to help other party members and it's just a chore.You still have those horrible choices where you have 50% chance of dying ( there's only ever 2 options one good one bad) .However in this game you have an option to go back to the last choice when you die instead of losing hours of progress on luck like in the first game. Save points are more numerous than before, however it's still really easy to die. When you explore a dungeon there's a chance that a shade will appear, if you touch it it's game over, most of the time it appear when you try to go make a detour to save your game ahah.  It's easy to avoid however I imagine that if you are in a dead end this can result in a game over (It seems scripted though so I don't think this will be an issue).  Story so far is very different than the first one, it's interesting though, and the different main characters are cool. The game is very buggy right now (some bugs are the same as those in the first game sadly). So you'll have to deal with a mouse cursor in the middle of the screen at all times and be ready to alt+f4 when you press and command button and everything stops working. Also the audio mixing is terrible, even with music at 100% and voices at 10% it feels like they are screaming in your hears and you still can't hear the music...Hopefully those will be adressed soon. Until then buy at your own risk. I 'll still leave a positive review though, as I enjoy playing the game even with all those bugs.
