_childDocuments_.review: The only bugs I encountered in this game are the ones meant to be there! While the game is broken into chapters, it isn’t entirely clearly cut when a chapter change is going to occur. The story flows seamlessly between the chapters and is broken into two types of delivery. Visual Novel style with a mixture of spoken and text on screen and through little pop up messages while in the field. I can tell you that the hybrid of spoken and text is a little strange at first but it actually works decently well. Some scenes are delivered purely with text on screen for you to read while others have spoken dialogue injected between the pure text screens. If there is spoken dialogue typically it is used when the character is actually speaking and anything the character is thinking is usually just text on screen. It isn’t consistently done though with quite a bit of spoken word being just delivered in a pure text format. While you are inside the orphanage there are usually a number of scenes to witness before you sneak out at night to enjoy the actual gameplay.The gameplay has a few questionable choices made but they do make sense as to why they were made. Every night you start out as you leave the dormitory. You then have to walk through the creepy streets to get to where you are going that night. This means effectively walking through the same area repeatedly as you progress through the game and that does get very repetitive and dull. It would be nice to have it automatically teleport you to the next starting area, but it does help give it the feel that you are leaving the dorms each night to go on an adventure so of course you will be passing through the same areas each time. Usually once you get to wherever you are going the game quickly wraps up after a boss battle and you are back to the orphanage again. If the town at night was more interesting to look at, it would make a difference but every area you pass through looks very similar to the last. Kind of featureless with a lot of glowing corruption intertwined. Since the town itself isn’t really a prime focus of the game and is more of just a setting for it, it can be forgiven that a lot of time wasn’t spent making all the buildings stand out at night, but it does make for a bit of a dull trek each night. This format changes a bit after while once you progress outside of town. Here everything is much more vibrant and even the corruption has a different colour to it! I won’t spoil anything though so I won’t say too much more on that. The other kind of questionable choice is the whole monster in the dark theme of it. Every now and then you encounter a special monster that chases you but it doesn’t really move all that fast, you get plenty of warning it is coming and you mostly just have to run a little way away from it before it de-spawns again. The game does make it clear that letting it catch you would be a mistake, but unless I was away from the computer when it showed up, I didn’t really feel like it was much of a threat, especially not early on. If it was a major threat it likely would have been very annoying, but as it is, it is a bit of nuisance but not that big of a deal. I do like the idea of it though and I think it does add something to the otherwise potentially repetitive stroll you are on.Let’s stop with the negative though because this game has far more positives in its gameplay than negatives to talk about. The combat is very similar to how it was in the first game. You can chain attacks together and depending on various factors you might unlock new abilities that way. Discovering new abilities helps keep the fights interesting as it forces you to try new things each time rather than just relying on the same tried and true abilities every time. You are mostly free to wander about the field to try to find the optimal position to start unleashing your attacks from; however, the bugs in the field are back again too. Touching the bugs (little glowing circles) will cause you to gain corruption and possibly some other effects too. Gaining enough corruption will unlock your powerful corrupted form. Gaining even more of them will kill you so all things in moderation I suppose! As you blast your enemies with your various moves, knockbacks and super knockbacks can occur as well as collisions too. Enemies’ colliding with other enemies hurts them both and potentially will send the other enemy flying too. An enemy colliding with an ally will cause that ally to swing their weapon at the enemy and ricochet it away doing heavy damage in the process. Overkilling an enemy is rewarded so it’s best to try to figure out the best way to inflict maximum damage each time you obliterate your enemies. The somewhat complex battle system for a Visual Novel style game is something that made me want to play Death end re;Quest 2 after having previously enjoyed the original. Another thing that brought me back to the Death end re;Quest series is the fact that your choices do matter more here than they do in some other games I have played. A wrong choice can get you killed! It actually feels like it takes longer for Death end re;Quest 2 to start giving you these choices in comparison to the original but they are still there. If you are a sucker for punishment, it can be fun to try to figure out which option is the wrong one and going for that instead of trying to choose the best option. I mean sure you will likely end the game with a gruesome game over, but that is what your saved games are for.One thing that is needed in a Visual Novel style game is a healthy smattering of character tropes and this game has pretty much all of them covered. All of the characters are quite well detailed although primary characters definitely look even fancier than their NPC counterparts. It was quite easy to tell who my third party member was going to be once I met her and sure enough she eventually joined me. With so much focus given to dialogue while inside the orphanage it’s good that there is a variety there to work with. Each one has enough character building to make them feel like they matter and each one of them tends to have a bit of an interesting and checkered past that lead them to be at this mysterious orphanage. The school itself, following a religion unique to the town, possibly being haunted and frequently having strange disappearances that are classed as adoptions is also a bit fascinating to learn about. Since it is hard to talk about a story heavy game, I will refrain from talking more about it and talk more about the technical side of things.The audio works very well and despite the spoken dialogue being peppered in rather than consistent, it is enough to be enjoyable. The fact they were talking in English for a change was very welcome, it’s been quite a while since I played one of these style of games with an English Language option. I don’t mind non-English audio but usually I prefer it just because I find reading subtitles often makes you miss some of the action. The sound effects are a bit generic but they work well within the game. The atmospheric music and sounds did help set the tone and mood of the game very well. The only thing that got a little tiresome, and honestly, I would never suggest to remove it or omit it from future titles is the repetition of the same dialogue lines before and after combat. Sure, there are a number of different lines said and that really helps, but eventually it plays through them all and it just starts getting tiresome. It does let you skip it though so it isn’t that big of deal.The controls for the game, at least when using a gamepad, work very well. I found some of the keyboard key layouts a little awkward but it isn’t anything that would be too difficult to figure out plus it can all be rebound anyway. I have more to say, but I'm at the character limit!

_childDocuments_.review: Worse than the first game in almost every way, largely carried by  and some .I'm not even sure why this is a Death end re;Quest game, as the connections to the first game are minimal and many mechanics no longer make sense as we're not inside a virtual world anymore. The narrative is still written by Makoto Kedouin but seems to be an adaptation of his prior work, the Dolls Fall manga. The protagonist, Mai Toyama, kills her drunkard father after years of abuse, and ends up in a girls' orphanage in a small mountain town in an unnamed European country. There she meets the other 2 main characters, Rotten Dollhart and Liliana Pinnata. And then spooky stuff starts happening and the girls explore the town together at night when it transforms into something creepy, not unlike Silent Hill. The game uses a Persona like calendar system where you do social events at the orphanage by day, and go out exploring the town by night.There's no dual protagonist system like in the first game, which improved the pacing massively, as you no longer need to jump between two worlds and read long exposition dumps. But to be frank, 80% of the story is slice-of-life scenes with the orphanage girls, many of them being yuri. I believe there are at least 3-4 lesbian couples, and Mai and Rottie are heavily shipped together. I don't have a problem with yuri, but 20 hours of nothing but girls calling each other cute and blushing can numb your brain a bit. Aside from the slice-of-life, the game follows a "victim of the week" structure with each chapter having different girls going missing, which you can sometimes save depending on your choices. The actual plot is info dumped right before the final dungeon in a long visual novel scene. While the horror is not the focus, it's still there and those scenes seem to be more violent than the first game, with a lot more gore and sadistic descriptions of the girls being slowly tortured and killed.Characters from the first game have only minimal appearances outside of Shina. Shina eventually joins your party and gives you "data clones" of the whole DERQ1 party. How or why is never explained. There are also some annoying retcons, to make the mechanics work in a different setting. For example, buggies are now "guardian spirits". Bug tiles and corruption are never explained though.If you loved the combat in the first game, DERQ2 will disappoint you. Too many rough edges have been filed down, and it's really casual now.- Most skills cost 4-10 SP, so it's largely impossible to run out of SP- Bug tiles no longer hurt you, so you can go glitch mode on practically every turn- Reaching 100% corruption doesn't kill you- Counter attacks were largely removed aside from a couple boss fights- All of Arata's gimmicks were removed, such as codejack, genre change etc- If you don't feel like actually playing the game, there's an auto mode where an AI will control your partyAlthough there's a few more positive changes too:- You can now see exact enemy stats when examining them, including physical and magical defense scores- There's a warning if an enemy can counter attack and what exactly will they counter- Pressing A/Confirm during the knockback/knockblow animation triggers super knockback/knockblow which does a lot more damage and launches the enemy much fartherThe game overall feels incredibly rushed. It's only 20 hours long for a full playthrough, compared to 40 in DERQ1, and a large chunk of the playtime is slice-of-life scenes. There are no real dungeons, most of the action takes place on the streets and outskirts of the town, and they're all very samey looking. There are only 3 real party members, outside of the DERQ1 clones. Even the developers felt the game was too short on content, so they added a new game plus mode to pad it out a bit, in this mode you play the exact same game, but with about 2 hours worth of cutscenes added, yet there's no new game content whatsoever, no new bosses or items or anything.

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much. I kept looking for new updates each week for several months until finally it came out. And what a surprise this is. I regret buying this more than any other games and wish I could have been refunded before it's too late. I will list a few things that made me feel this way. Keep in mind that I haven't finished the story yet and to be honest I'm not sure I want to.- After many months upon release they still didn't fixed the most annoying bug I've encountered in a game: the mouse cursor will keep popping up in the middle of the screen each time you open the menu, start a fight, open the shop, etc... you will keep having to move the cursor away. And you will have to engage in a alternative solution requiring some prep time and post-game time, every single time you want to play.- The storyline is nowhere near as good as the first Death End. It's not engaging at all, you won't look forward to next chapters in this one.- The Berserker (the black figure that sometimes popup) is a joke. You're walking at triple his speed and to get caught you have to be real close to it. It's not a 'danger' by any means.- You can view the episode chart, which only serves two purpose: Make you regret that you can't go back a chapter to see a Game Over you missed, and collect cheap Eni (for some reason?) each time you click on a event you saw. Not that you'd want to click on every single one of them one by one to get as much Eni as you would killing low level monsters.- The update to fix the glitch outfits made me unlock all characters prematurely halfway down the game. When I'm supposed to be alone, I'm certainly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ not.- The graphics customization is so little you'll wonder what the ♥♥♥♥ were they thinking. You'll be forced to deal with excessive blur and many other options that you can't turn off or change.- Shiva made a 180 degrees change in personality that's completely out of character compared to the first game.- The main character can 'hack' computers to access cameras that will show you how a wall is in fact not real and you can get through. Sound good right? Except the team at IF forgot that your map already displays a path behind the 'hidden' walls...- If you don't manage to kill a boss character when he's down at about 15-20% HP, well tough luck man he will do a full heal. And when we deal with millions of HP here and it took a lot of time reviving, healing and dealing damage you will get frustrated and rightly so. Add to that the good old 'Boss characters are immune to all status effects' and you're in for a bad time.Do yourself a favor and don't buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Death end re;Quest. It was not what I expected to come from Compile Heart but in the end: I got an amazing story, very nice character and a pretty great battle concept. The typical Compile Heart mixture of Visual Novel and JRPG worked amazingly.Hearing there would be a second part, I've been quite sceptical. How would a second part to a game with a pretty completed story work? Would they do an mk2 on it? As in: pretend everything from the first game didn't happen and start again. Well: In a way... maybe? In another way: maybe not. But well: can't talk about this here because you know - story spoilers. And I wouldn't want to destroy any story relevant parts for you.Should you play Death end re;Quest before this game? Yes, you should, although it isn't absolutely necessary - while the story is linked, see above, it's independent enough to not require it.The gameplay concept over the original didn't change overly much - you have visual novel scenes throughout the day in the isolated Eastern European town called Le Caoara - you attend a school called Wordsworth there. And Le Choara turns into a dark evil place at night - which you will be able to explore at night in JRPG style. Enjoy it.The gameplay challenge is nicely balanced: Easy mode will literally let you enjoy the story as you can just progress from battle to battle - make the necessary battle and you'll advance quickly enough. Medium and Hard modes require you to grind more and experiment with the battle system a bit more. The battle system has a lot of variety so if you seek a challenge: Go ahead - you have Super Knockbacks, you have a decently interesting way to learn attacks, and the characters in the game add to each other rather well.While we're on it: I really enjoyed the chemistry between the 3 main characters which would be Mai  (spoiler reveals the names of later characters in the game). Or four - if you count a character from the first game. The interactions between other Wordsworth students and Le Choara residents were interesting enough to keep me entertained.Like the original: the game is quite bloody, sometimes the language can contain swear words - but overall it just fits the general style of the game. There are the typical fan service scenes which Compile Heart cannot refuse to add to any of their games although this game honestly wouldn't need them. But well, they're there. What else would you expect?On a minor note on that: in Death End re;Quest 1 the characters in the Glitch mode which returns in this game had very revealing outfits. The console version had those adjusted (aka censored) - for the PC version these adjustments were reverted for original characters who returned. Kudos for that, Idea Factory!All in all: Good game! You liked the first: Play it! You didn't like the first? Don't play it then, it's very similar. You didn't play the first? Well, maybe check out the first one for now but you can just jump into the second.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, Death end re;Quest 1 is one of my favorites games. I bought the 2nd without hesitating.The story begins very well and is very engaging. We learn about Mai Toyama who was the hacker of Enigma server in the first game. But at 1/3 of the game, it feels like there are missing pieces in the story to connect the events. For example, key elements like the introduction of "Bugu" are very anecdotal, so much so that the game doesn't refer to it anymore afterwards. Glitch mode is not even explained by the scenario. Dialogues with other NPCs are practically disconnected from the scenario to such an extent that it makes you want to skip them. I didn’t finish the game in one go, I didn’t play for 6 months because the story degraded after chapter 3. I was thinking of never coming back to the game but I really wanted to know how bad the story could end.The end of the game tries to make up for mistakes in the story. BUT the obligation to redo the game a second time just to learn 2% more of the story is not welcome at all. A Visual Novel section would have been enough, especially since all the events presented take place before the main story except for the last one. The characters from the first game are poorly used. In any case I liked the plot around Mai Toyama, especially the bad endings.Let us speak about a Death end re;Quest 1 feature: the camp...  it’s useless! In the first game, there were events with the different characters to learn more about each character and their relationship. You can always talk with the team members, but it's just a random and unimportant dialogue. Where are the dungeons? The areas of the city are without much identity. The level design is really bad, what's the point of putting fake doors if the key is hidden 10m away and visible on the mini-map? Just like the fake walls which are visible on the mini-map, there is no need to use hacking terminals to find them. The level design gives the impression of being sloppy or unfinished. This is the only reason that I see which could explain the useless feature "Break house or car windows to make noise" and the light walls placed everywhere with the item to pass them right next to them.The combos for unlocking the skills are still there, but the probability to unlock is hidden, good luck to find them all.The fights, the majority it’s one shot each enemy except bosses, big PV bags. _childDocuments_.review: Death end re;Quest 2. It's an Anime RPG game made by Compile Heart and published by Idea Factory International. It is one of Compile Heart's Galapagos RPG Projects for anime gamers. The 2nd episode, which came back, continues the story of the previous episode in a completely different place. Death end re;Quest 1 was set in the game world and Japan, However Death end re;Quest 2 is set in a rural village that is likely to exist somewhere. The main protagonist has also changed to Mai Toyama. As you may know, Corpse Party scenario writer Makoto Kedouin took part in this project. What story and gameplay are waiting for us this time? Let's take a look at it with Nyanco-chan! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)Due to her traumatic past, Mai Toyama is entrusted to Wordsworth where it is an all-girl’s dormitory situated in the small town known as Le Choara. She was told that her sister Sanae was there, but when she arrived at the dormitory, she couldn't find her sister. What's more, this dormitory has strict rules, and at night the town looks completely different. Then one day, a dormitory colleague is attacked by an unknown monster. She gets to realize that the village and the dormitory are not normal. She decides to escape with her colleagues. There are some parts that can be understood by experiencing  the Death end re;Quest 1, so it is recommended to play it first. Moreover, characters from the previous work appear here, including the main character of the first episode, Shina Ninomiya.The previous game was divided into the in-game world and the real world, but this time the play style changes depending on the day and night. During the day, you can enjoy various events with people in the dormitory or near the dormitory places. Daytime events can be enjoyed casually as if enjoying visual novels. Interesting events that would take place in the female dorm are unfolding. In addition, all the lines of the characters have their own voices, which enhances the sense of immersion. The character CG illustration has 2D Live animations. After 12 o'clock, the night event begins. At night, you can wander around and explore the town. Battles can be played at night. Various gimmicks were added to the top color of the map so that you can find someting fun. In particular, the battle system that received good reviews from the previous work was brought, and the bug pollution was improved. The knockback and overkill system are the key points in the battles.Death end re;Quest 2. It is an interesting anime JRPG. This game is full of charming anime girls. The gameplay well keeps the core fun of the JRPG. It takes a second play-through to get true endings and a variety of collectable elements. The gameplay time is about 20-30 hours or more. The main point of this game is to experience various bad endings. It is recommended to save frequently to get them. The game scenario is also interesting, and the charm of the characters makes the player more immersed in the game. If you like JRPGs featuring anime girls, Death end re;Quest 2 is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, In this review i will try to explain my theory about the game story, and my speculation regarding the general reason as to why this game is not well received by the player base (Overall review is "Mixed" as of the time im writing this review with some of the reasons being confusing story, general lack of engaging plotline, bad optimization, and the seemingly lack of connection to the first game)This will be a pretty long essay so, i hope you're okay with reading long blocks of text. But don't worry! i'll put a TL:DR and i hope you'll forgive any grammatical error and such since i will inevitably make some.[TL:DR At the bottom]-First impression review- (Written 3 hours into the game)Since everyone is talking about the performance already, im going to talk about the story instead.Like the first installation of the series, the story is great. The atmosphere, the tension, the thriller, the setting, the mystery, are all woven together beautifully.It managed to keep me glued to my screen throughout the whole intro, with the creepy atmosphere and the seemingly haunted town.Im still in the very beginning of the game but i can tell that im probably going to enjoy this game very much.If i have to point out the negative though, is that the English dub isnt complete. Some scenes are dubbed while some are dont, even though it is fully voiced in Japanese. But luckily you can change the voice language at any point of the game so, i'll just use the Jp voice for any scenes that the En dub didnt cover.Oh and, Most of the reviews seem to complain about the games performance, but as far as my experience goes, it runs very well. It stayed at a stable 60fps throughout the exploration part of the game. Not to mention im using a very outdated system (Xeon X3450 with RX 570) and im playing at 1080p. So if my rig can run it smoothly, i dont really get why people would say they had a rough time running the game. Probably an old review of the game when it was still problematic. But as for me, i'll say its very well optimized.----Post game review- (After achieving "Bad" and "True" end. 1 hours into the NG+)Here, i shall try to explain my reasoning as to why people doesn't like this sequel as much as its predecessor! SPOILERS AHEAD !Okay, so after finishing the game once, i can see why people seems to be not too interested with the story of this game.You see, there's a lot of unanswered question in the ending(s) of the first game, and a lot of people expecting the sequel to answer those questions like who is Lydia actually?, what happened after the world fused together? Why is Shina a Luden now? And general "WTF Is going on!?" with the ending.And with people expecting the sequel to answer those myriads of questions (Because honestly the ending for DERQ1 gives off more question than answers) but after playing DERQ 2 people find out that this game has so little to nothing to do with the first DERQ.And the big change for the games theme might also be a factor.DERQ1's conflicts revolves around Cyber Terrorism, Conscious AI, and general future tech stuff.Whilst DERQ2's conflict is about Religious cult kidnapping childrens. And the place that the story takes place on has no technology at all (Takes place roughly on 1980s rural Europe)In fact, i think DERQ2 has more in common with Resident Evil 4 than DERQ1.Religious cult, Kidnapping, Strange 'lil village in the middle of nowhere in Europe, and an Agent from abroad coming to investigate about the strange happenings (Arata's reason for coming to Le Choara)El Strain? More like El Illuminados >,>Like what are they trying to do here? Make a brand new story with the only common thing of the series being violent deaths? (Well i think that would be a pretty cool idea.)Its as if its a standalone story. Not having anything to do with the first game at all! Although they do explain some of the things that going on in DERQ1 in the NG+, but i really doubt people would want to play the game twice just to make a connection with the first one. Keep in mind, finishing this game takes roughly 20 hours, and just to see the connection to the first game would require you to replay through the game again. Which i understand why some people might not like the idea. Granted that after you've beat the game once, you will be rewarded with an alternate opening featuring Lydia and the rest of the gang from DERQ 1.Its as if the NG+ is DERQ 2 v.2.0But this too feels like a scrapped project that they just recycle, because they probably initially planned DERQ 2 to be about Lydia, but maybe some creative clash happen in the discussion room or something, so they just go with a brand new story, But at the same time they don't think that the new cast could carry on the series so they make some lame excuse so the OG cast can have an appearance in this installment.And in the process makes the appearance of the DERQ1 characters seems unreasonable to the point it might be better just not include them in the first place. Shina's and Arata's role could easily be played by an entirely new character. Since most of the dorm mates are just... ExistingAnyway, in the NG+ you'll get some tid bits of info that people actually want for the sequel. They actually explain stuff about Lydia's back story (And probably more. I haven't finished NG+ yet, but  i expect more info about what happened in DERQ 1 to be explained in NG+)But honestly, i wonder why they put these new scenes on the NG+ instead on NG. Because these extra stories don't really change anything about the base story. It feels as if they're putting these extra scenes as an excuse so theres something new in NG+ instead of expanding upon the ending.Had they just add these scenes in NG, i believe players that are seeking answers for DERQ 1 would be far more willing to play the game.-Now that i've explained my theory regarding peoples "Less than warm" reception towards the game, Now i shall point out the difference and the improvements they make...There's a lot less Death Ends here (Only 6) but those Ends feels more terrifying than DERQ1.Instead of just reading about the characters death which some honestly feels rather forced in DERQ1Here those 6 Ends feels much more natural. And whilst theres only 6 Ends for the playable character, Your choices still dictates the fate of your friends. Some choices you make will result in your Dorm mates death thus locking you out of their interaction in the subsequent days.Now then, lets talk about the new gameplay.They removed Arata's Hacking skills like changing the games genre and summoning bosses.Though this change makes sense since there's no tech wizard to modify the game.Although they have Iris. She can make those modifications with some excuse since Mai can unexplainably summon the characters from DERQ1 anyway. I don't see why Iris couldn't "Hack" the battle arena at all, since she seems to be aware of whats happening even when Mai isn't actively fiddling with the laptop.I think Iris is quite a wasted character here. Only there as a convenience rather as a plot device.[TL:DR]If you like the story of the first game, This isn't for youIf you want answers for the first game, Play the NG+If you like the battle system for the first game, This one is simplifiedI think they're trying to tie every mystery this series had in the finale, where players would be like "Ooh so thats what happened". That's why there's seems to be quite an abundance of "Unanswered mysteries" in the series, such as how did Mai summon the DERQ1 characters? Why is there's a field bugs? Doesn't this take place on reality? Why is there's even corruption and glitch mode?I can honestly understand people's frustration with the game. By the time im writing this review, They already confirmed a spin off and the next numbered entry. I guess all that's left to do is to wait and see what happens next... Anyway thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: This sequel is just unbelievably bad. I don't know if they fired the entire writing team between games, but the story of this game is so awful, I couldn't even finish it. From the plot to the characters, I feel like I'm playing through a fanfiction written by someone who played the first game.First off, the overall story is just badly written and horribly paced. 4 hours in and I still don't have any clue as to where the game is going, and frankly, I'm so bored I don't care. The setting makes no sense, Japan is mentioned by name, and they clearly have cars and electricity so it's a modern setting, yet somehow certain characters have never heard of a computer before?Second, the characters are laughably written at best and downright creepy at worst. It feels as though someone wrote a fetish fanfiction where "all-girls dorm" equals "all girls are lesbians" and made that into a game. It's disturbing and not something that can be blamed on anime tropes or fanservice, but literal fetish wish fulfillment. On the second in-game day, a girl you've just met the day before talks about sniffing your clothes and how she wants to sleep with you. This extends beyond just the main cast and even side characters talk about how they're attracted to the main character or other side characters as well.The above problem is made worst by the fact that nobody even seems human. Where the first game did well by introducing characters slowly over the course of the game, within the first hour of this one, you've got about 20 named characters getting introductions dumped on you one after another and in some of the most awkward ways possible. Nobody here acts at all reasonably how a person in these situations would act, and it's made worse by the game even calling attention to characters filling tropes as if making a joke about it somehow gives them a pass.Combat is somehow the same and yet even worse than the first game. Difficulty has severely dropped. Normal in this would have been easy in the first game. Glitch mode is available right from the start (and to add to the long list of story issues, characters have no reaction to each other somehow being able to transform into powered up versions of themselves.) To make matters worse, on normal there's no penalty for triggering corruption bugs so every fight including bosses for the first several chapters can all be won by simply running around and triggering glitch mode to wipe everything out. I think out of the maybe 30 or so fights with mobs and bosses, I maybe took damage a total of 3 times.I knew the game had technical issues, which didn't bother me, but I was hoping for more of what made the first game good. But all I got was a poorly written story with fetish wish fulfillment undertones that leaves what I thought was a decent series with a bad taste.

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing so many bad reviews I had to post a positive one to try and balance the scales a bit, because I genuinely enjoyed my time with this game. Also, first time writing a review of any kind, so please bear with me.On a technical level, the game is a slight improvement to the first one. The game ran smoothly in general unlike the first, which constantly stuttered during exploration and had weird laggy pauses in between the visual novel bits. They tried to rectify my biggest issue with the first game by actually giving us granular volume settings, but in the process messed up volume as a whole. The character voices will always feel ten times louder than everything else, no matter how low you put the volume, while sound effects and music are strangely low (except for the intro song, which is always blasting at 100% no matter the settings).Storywise, I actually enjoyed it a lot more than the original. The first game was an incredibly fun ride with unexpected plot twists, references to weird occult events and conspiracy theories, and some seriously sickening death scenes (which sometimes dragged on a bit too long). I think it was a bit of a misplay to have so many characters in the game, because outside of Arata and Shina the story didn't really get to explore any of them in a meaningful way.DerQ2 has a smaller cast of main characters, focusing more on Mai, Rottie and Liliana and doing a great job of actually developing them. The supporting cast of characters are very one-dimensional but they actually get enough screen time that you kind of start to care for them. I've seen people say that Mai is an unlikable protagonist and I feel like these people are missing the point. She is coarse and rude to everyone she meets because she cannot trust people. Everything in her past has taught her to be a loner. Despite this, throughout the story there are some moments of genuine warmth and care for the well-being of others, which make Mai a lot more human.The characterization even extends to the "buggies" the girls have. Mai's buggy is a snail because she is literally retreating into a hard exterior shell and needs others to tease out her soft interior. Rottie's buggy is a mosquito because she is loud and irritating, but she manages to pierce that hard exterior front that Mai put up. Liliana is a whip-spider... I have no clue what this is supposed to mean.The story itself is focused on a small, remote town where mysterious things happen. The scope is much smaller than the first game, as there are no world-shattering events or illuminati-esque shadow organizations wanting to rule the world. And personally, I prefer the smaller scope because it made the story feel that much more personal for everyone involved. If you wanted a continuation of the first game's story, you will be sorely disappointed. The few threads that tie the game together make sense, but honestly DerQ2 could have been completely standalone, just set in the same universe. As a result of the smaller scope, you will be mostly exploring the town and its surroundings, which again I find a welcome change from the original. The map design is much more coherent this time around and the areas you explore make sense within the context of the setting. But I do agree that it gets a bit same-y mostly running around through town streets at night. The forest, lake and rural area are a welcome break from the streets, but maybe they could have thrown in a cave or something, just for added variety.

_childDocuments_.review: For this review I will not be speaking about the UI issues (Soft locks) since they should be fixed here soon. Nor will I compare it to . I only say this because the game was produce in collaboration with Corpse Party's Scenario Writer Makoto Kedouin. I feel this has produced a creative difference in what the story was planned to be. With that I feel like I won't compare them, even though this is considered a continuation.Total I'll give the game an . The reasoning will be broken into 5 Multiple Parts; Story, Characters, Gameplay, Graphics/Design, and Music.You are first introduced to Mai Toyama and learn about her arrangement with her family. Through this small interaction you can understand the atmosphere for the rest of the narrative. These Dark tones persist with sprinkles of lighthearted interaction between the rest of the cast. These characters are expanded upon, learning small tidbits about each of them, their devotion, determination, generosity, and persistence. Yet they still each have their flaws hinted at, each being different, some more noticeable than others. The atmosphere then shifts during the night from the cheerfulness back to the dreary, creating a nice duality between the days. Continuing through these days, you start to piece together small things and by the end contradictions come into play. Albeit quiet rushed, information begins fill the gaps of the larger pieces of this puzzle.Considering how much I enjoyed questioning each part of the Narrative when something new didn't seem to add up. Then finally realizing that my theory's were completely wrong/spot on, at some points really creates a fun story for me. Some of these being hard to put into words. The 3 main cast members, , are very unique in their own ways, but each have a common ground in regards to their families. This helps allow them to connect to each other a little easier. You learn about each of their pasts and what they want to accomplish. You even learn as to why some are more disconnected from their current reality. The more interesting of the cast would be the other students at Wordsworth. Each of them are unique in terms of personality and their troubled backgrounds leading them to this orphanage. Each have their own little dynamic which makes them entertaining. Some feeding off the attention of others, another is strong and collected, one even wanting to rebuild her past legacy. I personally enjoy how every bit of the characters are very distinct, both in their intentions and underlining flaws. The gameplay in terms of combat itself is pretty straight forward, Normal Combat Triangle, Magical/Physical Damage types, Buffs, and nifty character unique passives. Nothing too crazy or new, besides glitch modes and Knockbacks. Glitch mode allows you to temporarily increase your stats to deal more damage or sustain some hits. While knockbacks is where your DPS can really increase. The pinball mechanic of knocking the enemies around is an extra hit on each of the enemies allowing for some quicker fights, or more strategic. In conjunction with floor mines and random buff tiles in the arena, strategies sometimes are forced to change.When it comes to learning new abilities, that's the hardest part about the combat. It's tough trying to find out what may or may not give you something new. But that's where it's fun, you cant be handed everything. Figuring things out yourself feels more rewarding.Despite the crazy mechanics it's still another one of those check damage types and hit accordingly and you'll breeze through the game. It's not very challenging even on the Hardest difficulty, and if you hit a wall, Level grinding can easily fix that.Out of Combat they give you these small puzzles, Easily bypassable by using the map, or by running around and grabbing the Items throughout the areas. They are pretty straight forward and not too challenging either. There's really not much to say about graphics here. In terms of Compile heart and Idea factory, nothing much has changed. Only thing that's a little bothersome is how I feel like I always need my glasses on when walking around on the maps cause its so blurry. Other than that, the only thing that really saves it is the, Artwork, characters are each very unique, and the new areas are interesting. otherwise it would of been a tad lower. I'm just gonna leave this one pretty short, the music is top, it's not annoyingly repetitive like some other games. It also  keeps the game engaging and fun. Final boss music is great, Intro music is fun to listen to on it's own. And if you ever get the chance, when your being 'Chased' by the Shadow Matter just enter your character menu and listen to the music. Good Vibes all around.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I wasn't sure if I wanted to play this series because of its mixed reception. But I still have warm feelings toward the first Corpse Party game that was created by the same person, so I decided to give Death end re;Quest a chance. And so far it's my favorite "bad" JRPG.But let me be clear, I don't like calling things I enjoy "bad." The story of both Death end re;Quest games was entertaining, the mystery was intriguing, the characters were likeable, and the gameplay was fun (it's easy, but I don't mind). And most of all, it was great to find such a dark JRPG. Of course, there are a lot of games that go in this direction, but so far nothing vibed with me as much.The second game goes even further at borrowing horror tropes. The setting is darker, there is more violence and twisted stuff in general. Also, you can clearly see that the creator has experience with RPG Maker horrors because there is a new mechanic that occasionally forces you to run away from a monster (don't worry, it's really simple) while New Game+ literally has a minigame featuring Ao Oni.Speaking of which, NG+ isn't simple bonus content, but an actual second route of the story. It connects both games, expands the setting, explains the true nature of the main villain, adds new scenes, and presents a new epilogue with an important reveal.So, what makes this game worse if it sounds good on paper? My biggest complaint is that the game is a technical mess. BGM volume is broken, there is no way to adjust brightness (don't you like bumping into an enemy because you simply didn't see it), and constant stuttering on Steam Deck doesn't help either despite the Verified mark.But I still enjoyed the ride and it's worth giving a chance if you're a fan of dark/mystery stories. Let's hope the third game will come out because there is definitely room for more.From my . Take a look at it if you're interested in VN news, opinions, and more. I'll be happy to see you.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you enjoy the pain and suffering of Death end re;Quest 1 and want your PTSD to continue? Well Death end re;Quest 2 has your back!The plot of the game is quite simple. Nah I am just kidding, the beginning smacked depression right in my face. The further I got in the story, the more I wanted to play. It contains a lot more JRPG elements than the 1st game as the choices you make, lead to different scenes in which certain characters are either missing or present. It also contains the bad endings and are more fleshed out which is a step up from the 1st game. Boy did they turn the horror bar up.(Although there are less death endings). The character interactions and relationships is the most intriguing and enjoyable part of the game.The gameplay is similar to Death end re;Quest 1. Glitch mode is more fun and easier to activate, the knockback system is back and vamped up, The new aspect is the overkill feature which allows you to gain more experience as you kill enemies. The soundtrack is a real slapper. Sound effects traumatized me,meaning it is very well done and horrifyingly realistic (seriously though, I was honestly terrified by the sound effects. BY THE GODS THE BLOOD GUSHING SOUNDS!).I personally found Death end re:Quest 2 unpreditcable. No, really I did. I did not suspect certain things at all. It is also sequel friendly as you are not required to play the 1st game, but has nice references which veterans will appreciate. The game had quite a few bugs and graphic issues, but most of them are now fixed as of October. All in all, Death end re;Quest 2 is a great game that JRPG lovers will enjoy. The Death end re;Quest series needs more recognition Go play it. Just do it.

_childDocuments_.review: I will say this now before I start my review I get where most people who hate this game is coming from I also do not enjoy alot of aspects of this game however after replaying it on PC my opinions on it has died down and I can respect what they went for with this title. In my eyes Death end Re;Quest 2 is the video game equivalent of a monkeys paw and I hope my review can explain that.The gameplay is more faster faced, it has a auto battle which can help fix some of the grind of the first game and allowing the more casual player to cruse through the trash mobs while still posing difficulty. Although bringing back the Flash Drive system it's missing one of the most integral parts of the game which split DERQ from other JRPGS. Since you're no longer in a game Mai doesn't use code to manipulate the world around her to the extent that Arata did. Although she can change the field bugs that is all she can do she cannot do the things Arata could like giving field boosts and resets, implementing genres and summoning previous bosses to help so sadly the game loses some of its identity in sacrifice for more fluid battle systems.The game also introduces a faceless humanoid being called a shadow matter that will appear and stalk the player if they interact you die instantly and its game over. They're quite interesting since they tie to the story but in gameplay its comical they're considered a threat they walk slower then someones grandma and the only they they'll catch you is if they spawn infront of you or you just wanna see what happens.Something I praise the game for as well is adding one of the easiest things in human history an option to re select your choices after a death end making it less punishing for not saving before a death event. They then proceed this by having 1/4th of the amount of death ends making the implementation almost unimportant.I personally enjoyed this games story more then others but will agree that the first world building and overall cast was more impact and felt more alive even if being in a game. In my eyes the biggest problem with the plot is the fact its a sequel to DERQ it loses alot of what made the first game unique and tells a interesting story about a cursed town filled with shadow matters demons personified by the anguish and extreme emotions of the towns citizens but has many points where the plot will come back and will explain worlds odyssey, the events of DERQ1 and programmers. The parts where this game shines is with the day to day lives of the orphans, the friends Mai makes and the lingering dread of the hellhole of a town being in a city filled with no technology makes the scene with it immensely jarring because how is her phone still alive how is the laptop Arata left still alive and most importantly if they made it a big part in the third act to leave why didn't they do it during the day? the game is hindered by these simple but massive plot holes which brings the overall story down. But I will admit the twists, the final act and NG+ content with returning cast is actually really sweet and makes me have some hope for a possible third title.The characters except the fellow Orphans are quite small only having 3 main characters with Shina returning as a support character. As much as I do enjoy the new characters their potential was very much left to not be fully used. Mai post trauma and bouts of rage wasn't used to its full extent she never truly had a moment to reflect on everything and fully grow as a character although she does grow but not to the best the writers could've done. Liliana is an interesting character and grows after many chapters and her epilogue was sweet. Rottie however doesn't get the same treatment although getting some points where you sympathise with her the character ends up being a tool to just say moe stuff and love Mai at worst at best she is one of the many anchors that keeps Mai from falling into despair which if they went more into that would've made for an interesting dynamic.The final character to talk about is of course Shina but i'll also add the other playable characters from the first game they're immensely underused and almost felt like last minute additions to remind the player is a squeal then an actual part of the world which is one of the additional reasons I feel like it'd been better if this game was standalone.I wanted to add this part because honestly most of this games music are bangers. The battle theme, the final boss theme, the opening and everything in-between was all great additions to the game. Personally was never the biggest fan of DERQ1 soundtrack it was very forgettable.DERQ2 was in alot of aspects a step down from the first game in mine and alot of peoples eyes but that was because the first game was a pretty solid overall game and while this one is also good in its own ways it tries way too hard to be a sequel to game that didn't need one and is hurt because of it. I still like this game the atmosphere and overall dread I felt in this was game was real and if they would love to see another attempt at this style of game just as its own separate entity the trying to follow its big brother.7/10 buy it on a sale

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:It is......really bad to be honest. I hate to type this but strategy isn't really a thing until the very final chapter. I played on Hard Difficulity for chapter 1-10 and Normal on the final boss. Most battle requires the biggest damage that can hit every enemy to get rid of them asap so they don't just dogpile on you. It seems that the battle are designed with the player going first in mind which means that whenever there is a boss battle there is a chance the boss decide to just hit everyone and 2 hit the entire party. In a Midgame boss I made my tank did triple guard, defense increase, migrate half damage and the boss still does 1000/1600 damage in a single hit and 592 in the next. I think they realise this is a problem which is why EVERY SINGLE CHARACTER HAS REVIVE. There is no real strategy until chapter 10, where there are enemys with high physical defense and low magical defense and you can no longer spam that hit the entire map spell. Due to the obscene damage bosses does, It is very hard to recover from a fallen teammate. Since the boss turn comes before the revived teammate turns, it will most certainly walk up to that teammate and knock her down again. In fact due to how boss fights are treated as ambushed, usually the boss go ahead of the player. In the final boss the Boss and it's 4 minions killed my entire party before anyone can even move. I am not sure why the system to get new skills has been reworked for the worst, you now learn new skills from leveling up, but you have no indication on how to learn new skills using your current skills. In the previous game it shows you if there is a skill to be earned, this is no longer the case here and I did not even get one of the tier 2 spell for the Main character until the Chapter 8 Boss. For the sake of your sanity just play on normal or even easy, its the story that is worth it not gameplay.Gameplay is also riddled with bugs, minor bugs can be look past, but said bug include the UI vanishing basically locking you into a frame. I alt f4 about 6 times during my 20 hours of gameplay, which is really bad. Seriously sometimes the game prevent you from even going to the menu, maybe it will be fixed in the future In which I will comment on it if it happens.Story: The story description on the steam page is accurate enough, the character growth is gradual enough it is believable. There is enough ups and downs and there is no longer so many death ends that I just stop caring. While the game can be played alone some times will not make sense(Arata, why are monsters normal) unless the first game is played. There are a few plot holes (2nd character gets a gun? How?) but they can be ignored as the game wanting to give us a ranged character. There is a payoff to the story which ends with a bittersweet enough ending.If i must give it a score I will give it a 4/10, while the story is worth it either wait for a sales or for them to fix the damn game before getting it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more polished than the first game, it's more complete than the first game, and it has better pacing than the first game. _childDocuments_.review: Deaths end re;Quest was a slightly boring open-ish world rpg that was saved by it's characters and a mysterious plot, until the very end you are confused as to whats going on. To top it off the mystery in the first game is gone, because you as the player can guess what's going on at the beginning of the game if you've played the first one. The absolute WORST part of the game was allowing you to use characters from the last game, making some of their abilities necessary on the hardest difficulty, restricting your usage of them for story-related reasons, and not letting you interact with them at all. It felt like a middle finger to get to use my favorite characters from the last game, and be punished for it.The port wasn't great either as the game is very dark and relies on effects to keep it bright enough to see, but those effects make it extremely blurry at 1080p or higher, if you turn them off you can't see, if you turn them on you can't see, it's a lose/lose situation. I ended up using reshade to make it look half-decent, but with how much of it is a VN, I needed to swap the effects on and off constantly. Also all the hidden paths are on the minimap and that was clearly not intended.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Compile Heart games, where do I even start with you? So let me get this out of the way. This game is NOT the typical funny hahaha kind of Compile Heart game. This game is dark from a storyline perspective, with some very adult themes. So let's get into this review. This game was played entirely on the Steam Deck as a verified title, I will say that the game would be fantastic if it were better optimized. The performance on the Deck ranged around a solid 35-40fps with high settings.Pros- Dark story - (This is the draw of the game, the exact opposite of what Compile Heart games typically are.)- Battle System - (Glitch Mode, Knockback attacks, and customization of attack combos, so there is a bit of strategy.)- Graphics -  (The VN parts ,character portraits, are superbly done. The Boss monster design is unique, and a horror atmosphere are also well done.)- Sound - (The voice acting is all solid, the soundtrack is great, and the opening song is one of the best I have heard in a Compile Heart game.)- Short - ( About 15-20 hours a quick game by most JRPG standards.)- Fan Service ( Enough said there.)Cons- Performance - (This is a general issue with Compile Heart games across the board. A beefer machines can brute force better performance, but given what the game is pushing from a graphically POV, the game needs better optimizations.)- Fan Service - ( Not that so much that there is fan service, but most some of it does not fit thematically with the dark story)- Characters - ( There are four main characters that the story focuses on, but there are other playable characters, that don't have much beyond just being party members. 1 or 2 of those main characters will either love them or hate them kind of characters as well.)- Difficulty ( Easy is just blow through the game kind of easy not a challenge, so good if you like the story, but bad if you want to get into the gameplay.)Overall, I enjoyed the time that I put into Death End Re; Quest 2. It was nice to have kind of a shorter JRPG to play. I also enjoyed the very dark and much more adult-oriented themes this game presented, it is a nice break from the usual Compile Heart formula of games. So I would recommend this game if you are looking for a shorter JRPG with a dark story.

The cutscenes are fine but the 3D dungeons have a lot of stuttering. Add this to your launch options to fix:WINE_CPU_TOPOLOGY=1 PROTON_USE_WINED3D=1 %command%I used Proton Experimental.  You can also install "unclutter-xfixes" and run "unclutter" in a terminal before you start the game to get rid of the mouse cursor in the middle of the screen in battles. This is an issue on Windows too.  And to fix the lack of vsync, you can turn on TearFree with "xrandr --output $OUTPUT --set TearFree on" where $OUTPUT is your video card's output. You can find it by running "xrandr" and looking for its name. Mine for example is "HDMI-A-0"

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure why, but I absolutely loved this game - even before I purchased and knew little about it, I knew that I wanted to play it. It was also then that I knew I wanted to play the first as well. It's a solid horror experience imo, but if you're not a fan of JRPGs it might be a turn off, since battles are frequent and you have to explore the dungeons to progress the story, having a boss at the end of a chapter.Unlike the first game, this isn't VN-heavy and establishes the story fairly quickly. The story will expand and become more interesting over time, as you discover the mysteries behind this technological-indept town, Le Choara... including, the disappearances of many people.The combat had refined from the first game, but excluded the third-person shooter and another combat type - which were redundant and rarely came into necessity, aside from the one part you needed to use it to progress. It looks smoother and feels more fleshed out, as well as more flexible to the player - but don't think you can cheese battles just because of this. A refined combat systems means more refined foes as well.Shina Ninomiya, from the first game, makes an appearance here as well - I wont mention why as I don't wish to spoil too much, but let's just say she's searching for something in Le Choara too. You unlock her after completing chapter 4, so if you were hoping to play as her, you can rest happy knowing she'll be an optional party member once unlocked, as well as the other avatars from the first game, with the exclusion of Mizunashi.Death End 2 has references to Death End 1 - if you haven't played the first, you wont be completely lost, but you may have to do research into past characters/information mentioned.I highly recommend checking this game out - but not if it's not for you. It's not rated mature for no reason. From grotesque scenes, to dialogue describing very disturbing and gut-wrenching events, it may not be your type of game. But if you're looking for a horror JRPG with a dark story, you've come to the right place.A note if you do plan on buying this game - if you're worried about optimization, it's better than the first game's port, but you'll still experience frame drops here and there, regardless of the settings you tweak. Again, not as bad, as I don't mind 25-30 FPS, but if that bothers you than you might want to look into the console versions instead.TL;DR I recommend this game if you love horror and JRPGs, but it's not for everyone. Optimization's better, but still has issues. Story takes a more mystery-driven approach than the first game.If you have any questions, I've comments enabled. Thanx for reading. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I don't normally write reviews, so I apologize if I'm terrible at it. I saw things for Death end re;Quest 2 starting about 2 months ago. Seeing the character designs and backdrops got me extremely interested. I watched about an hour of a lets play and really liked the story that it was building. I decided to look into the first game and started watching a lets play on it. Honestly I wasn't as impressed. Now this could be because I wasn't actually playing the game but I just didn't find the stuff happening with the parts you actually play all that interesting. The stuff happening outside of the game were way more interesting to me.Now that I got that out of the way, Death end re;Quest 2 is fantastic. Is it the best game ever made.... well no, but opinions vary on what makes a game the best game ever or not. For me it being focused on just the main characters you play as and not splitting the story into 2 separate things going on really helped me enjoy the story more and connect with the characters. I am not going to say that the first game didn't do this with the separate scenarios happening, but as I said I found the stuff happening outside the game world way more interesting.I am a fan of visual novels and JRPGs, and I really felt like they did a great mix of the two. I honestly didn't feel like I was reading for too long before I was playing and I didn't really feel like the gameplay was dragging....minus the parts where I got lost and didn't understand where I was supposed to go and ended up running around for about an hour till I found out that I was going the complete wrong way. But that was also because I was an idiot and didn't check my objective and use my map.I felt like the pacing and creepiness of the story was really familiar feeling. Then I found out that the developers worked with Makoto Kedouin, just the scenario writer for Corpse Party! I really enjoyed the story and would love to go back and get more story scenarios and endings! I just really enjoyed the characters and all their interactions. Mai and Rottie were just such a fantastic pair, they play off each other so well.It took a little bit to get use to the battle system. I'm more use to basic turn-based JRPGs, you know you get an attack then you ally then your enemy etc., but honestly I got used to the free movement and 3 command turns pretty quickly. I do like that learning new skills is based on you using different skills together instead of just unlocking them as you level up. Very interesting way of getting new skills. Granted there are still that unlock when you level but this brings a more experimental way of playing. Glitch mode took a bit for me to understand. While you do have a special attack in this mode, your other attacks are more powerful and can be used without losing your glitch mode right after. Very helpful for the tougher enemies. All in all, after playing for 25 hours, I'm still in love with the game. I want to play NG+ and get more story scenarios, look into the mini game, and possibly 100% it! Yes, I enjoyed it that much.So in closing. If you like games like Corpse Party and don't mind visual novels and like JRPGs, then honestly you are probably going to enjoy this game. If you hate reading and just want to play, you're probably are not going to enjoy it all that much. The story and the gameplay are pretty equal in terms of how much you read versus how much you play. Theres probably more reading but I tend to read a bit faster than a non-reader so I really didn't feel like the reading parts took too long. Also I should point out that I only played it with Japanese VAs so I can't neither confirm nor deny that the English audio doesn't have areas that are not voice. I did notice this during the lets play of the first game. Large sections just didn't have audio. For me almost everything had voice acting. Pretty much every character had a voice and besides the parts where it was only narrations, I never really didn't hear a voice behind the character. Also the Japanese voice acting is amazingly done. Just to help. Mai is voiced by Chiwa Saito, any Monogatari fan would know that its the voice of Hitagi Senjougahara! Took me a while to pin down where I heard her voice before. Mai's mannerisms are pretty similar to Senjougahara's at first. Still if you don't mind the Japanese VAs, I can honestly say, its great!I think I rambled on long enough. Great game in my opinion. would love to see more after game stuff if possible, even if its a totally different tone than the game. I just really enjoyed these characters and would love to see more.Also the opening is freaking amazing!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I find it absurd that people leave negative reviews because this isn't a continuation of the first game. It's not. It lays the groundwork for a potential DERQ 3.The combat system has been cut down from the first game, removing the useless gimmicks. _childDocuments_.review: Now I'm not too in depth when it comes to in game analysis, and whatnot, so please forgive me if my opinion isn't as in depth as you'd like or if I don't clarify on things, I am but a simple man. DISCLAIMER: I did not play the first game yet.Combat: The combat system is a turn based combat system using a rock paper scissors type of damage, somewhat like fire emblems green blue and red enemies, with attacks having magic or physical damage properties to them, with each attack covering a different area of affect. The combat takes place in a ring in which you essentially play pinball with the enemies, using your moves with knock-back, knocking them off walls or your fellow teammates for bonus damage. While I had a blast with this early on, I reached a point in the game where just about the only way to kill the atrociously high HP enemies was to place my characters around the enemies in a triangle and ensure that when I knocked an enemy back they would continue to bounce off my teammates and not off somewhere else within the circle. The combat wasn't incredibly difficult on hard mode, up until a difficulty spike around chapter 6-7 where the enemies suddenly had insane amounts of HP and defense. The final boss of the game was the only place in the game where I turned the difficulty down, since one of my units kept getting one shot and I wasn't really feeling it.Story: The game's story is given to the player in a Visual Novel format, with interactions between the main characters and the girls in Wordsworth being played for you, allowing you to get a see their personalities and sometimes the reason they were sent to Wordsworth in the first place. During these phases of the game, you can just kick back and relax, as the gameplay of this game in terms of making choices and combat is only located within the night phase of the game, so grab some popcorn and enjoy the scenes play out. Having not played the first game and unlocking what seems to be the true ending of the first game, there were some minor plot issues as far as how the combat is explained in the game, but I found no issue with it, aside from a brief "wait where did the loli find the gun" (which is never explained and I feel it's for the better). With the story of the game being written by a main member of the Corpse Party team (whether they wrote the story or were an advisor, I'm not 100% sure, so don't quote me on that) the story seemed to play out about how you would think, with the exception of some twists and turns that I didn't think the game would take so suddenly, but were alluded to earlier on in the game. The game has enough horror themes to keep me happy in the Visual Novel sequences of the game, but it's something about when horror games allow you to take on these lovecraftian horrors in 3D and you know you'll just beat the everloving snot out of them in two seconds once the cutscene is over that just takes the suspense out of it for me personally. Missions/Achievements: This game has a wide array of easily unlockable achievements that players will almost certainly unlock after a couple playthroughs, with most ranging from "unlock all abilities by leveling characters" to "view all story sequences", pretty standard video game stuff right? The only thing that I have an issue with is the mission system, with little bounties being placed by the shopkeeper at the camp, having you kill certain enemies for items, or finding items out in the world. This alone isn't really a problem, but I would certainly appreciate a location hint as far as where to find some of the items, as the game has a very large map. Bounties on creatures to slay will require that you view enemies for their names/weaknesses in combat, as the game lacks a Bestiary/Enemy Encyclopedia, and that is somewhat of a disappointment, as looking through the Bestiary to see what enemies/secret bosses you may be missing is one of the best parts of RPG's for me. Bugs/Glitches: This game is early enough on in it's life, so it's to be expected that there will be some bugs in the game, but some of these can be downright horrendous for the experience of the game for some. Personally the first glitch I experienced were the UI glitch where you're unable to click anything in the menu and you have to force restart your game (happened about 8 times in my 22 hour playthrough) which can be avoided for the most part by saving frequently at every single save spot you find. The other glitch that I personally found was a glitch in combat where you cannot select certain spells from your combat menu, however this has a quick fix of going to a combat tab where you can find usable abilities, press back, then go back to fighting as usual, this glitch however only appeared for me during the final boss battle and hasn't happened since on my NG+ playthrough, so it may be fairly uncommon. However, some players on the discussion boards have experienced some game breaking glitches like "when I look up in free roam mode I can't see anything/the game crashes, and have thankfully been getting some dev responses saying they'll look into it, and to submit an issue ticket on the forum site so others can be updated in case they suffer from the same issues as well. Final Verdict: With my first playthrough resulting in the "True Ending" I would say that this game was fun and engaging about 95% of the time as the pinball system is interesting enough to make even trivial fights engaging just for the reason that "haha enemy go zoom". While I can say with the utmost certainty that I'm a weeb, this game had somewhat of a lack of fan service which I'm pleasantly surprised about, as most games ruin tension with it when it comes to horror games. The separation of the day and night (VN/Open world exploration/combat) allows for all of the fan service and character archetypes to be in the day, with the night being saved for story related dialogue for the most part, allowing for the player to become immersed in the intense atmosphere of the game without side characters attempting to break the tension every 3 seconds with their whacky antics. Overall as far as RPG's/JRPG's go, I would rate this among the top of the lists, much to the cringe of every hardcore RPG fan that may be reading this review. The non traditional combat makes for every fight to be a different experience, and made the rare moments where I had to farm for levels enjoyable. The story of this game was extremely interesting to me, with a smart explanation to how all of the events in the game are possible, that doesn't need prior knowledge from the first game to understand, although knowing what I know about the first game's story now, it would have for sure provided some nice context. I played through the entire game in two sittings of 10 and 12 hours (covid unemployment hitting hard lmao) and I can say that that might have made for a better experience story wise. The archetypes of all of the side characters blend together, with some scenes even being self aware, talking about how many girls at the academy are tsunderes. This results in a somewhat forgettable cast, where I found myself thinking "okay from the way shes's acting in this scene it could be one of 4 characters, what did we do in our first conversation?" and while it confused me during my first playthrough, in the second I was able to fully keep track of the stories and it made for a better gameplay experience. I would rate this game a solid 9.5/10, with my only real issues with the game being the bugs (but the game devs are working on it, and they've only been talked about for a couple days.) and the lack of mission clarity and a bestiary. But that's just a personal preference. Thanks for the time in reading the review if you made it this far! I'd suggest watching some combat footage if you're interested in the game, as no explanation that I provide would depict an accurate image of the amount of fun I had pinballing enemies.

Field bugs doesn't damage characters (unless specified) and provide a lot more bonuses, which is good since some monsters have too much hp. On the other hand, glitch mode is so accessible that you can basically cheese most field fights, while it doesn't work all that well against bosses.Another thing that I'd like to include is that the characters from the first game are back, somehow. They are not really part of the story, but they are available to use in your party. The bad thing is that they suck compared to the 3 new characters, so you are basically stuck with the same party unless you want to have an underperforming team.All in all, I can't really recommend this game, neither for IF fans nor for those that liked the first game or are looking for a serious JRPG

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: Before buying the game have a look at the forum and check a thread about an early game-breaking bug. Many people still cannot play the game after starting the first dungeon. At the moment this review is published, the bug is still present, but the team practically solved the problem. My original review was negative due to the bug, but an additional branch of the game provided by the Idea Factory tech support allowed me to continue to play through the game without problems. This is an experimental branch but I think it is just a matter of days till the problem will be solved for everybody with an actual patch. According to other players, the game has other potential bugs, but on the branch I played everything worked quite fine. However, maybe if you have the possibility, a console version of the game is a safer bet right now. Anyway the following is the review of the actual game, without considering the bug.Death end re;Quest 2 is classified as a horror JRPG for a reason, and it does everything to support the definition. The general atmosphere is oppressive and tragic, a world where every person could experience a brutal death or an unfair fate. Every story and background is not for the faint of heart, usually involving abuses and tragedies. This is the story of a girl with a traumatic past, searching for her sister in an orphanage for girls only. This story is not a common drama but something deeper and more twisted, set in a mysterious town with a secret. People at school and also at the town are involved in the mysterious religion of “El Strain,” so it will be very clear since the beginning that the small town is hiding a secret, and the curfew at midnight is only a part of it. Obscure religions and alternate realities will meet cyberpunk themes connected with the first Death end Request, creating a complex atmosphere for one of the few and rare Japanese horror RPGs. However, knowledge of the first game is not essential to enjoy the sequel.Gore and blood are also quite present, especially in the cutscenes, both in anime and 3D events. Special examples are the Bad Endings, graphic and violent Game Over scenes that are associated with bad decisions during the events, even if it is often text-only violence. This in not unfair as could sound, and discovering all these violent endings will soon become more interesting than avoiding them. The darkness of the writing it is not a surprise knowing that Makoto Kedouin, writer for the survival-horror series Corpse Party, was involved in Death end Request 2. Worth to notice that several secondary characters are disturbed or plainly psychotic, behind their friendly facade, with cases of bullying and toxic friendships.The game shows two souls, perfectly divided both for aesthetic and gameplay. During the day, Death end Request 2 is mainly a Visual Novel (VN). The player can explore the school and the town to interact with several secondary characters and discover new events. During the night, the gameplay will switch toward horror JRPG. The player will explore the town, a creepy and eerie place of twisted architectures, where disturbing monsters roam in the streets.You can find my complete review here:
