_childDocuments_.review: As a big Destroy all Humans fan, I cannot recommend this remake! And here's why:I loved the original game to the bone, to the point which I completed it from 0 to 100% multiple times.You're probably wondering "if this guy loved the original, why does he not recommend this remake? it's a near-identical clone after all, right?"Wrong! If you quickly glance at it, yes, it's the same game with updated graphics. Now, when playing the game to completion, it's a whole another story.Missions were removed, such as the odd job "Take it Like a Man" (I'm not going to talk about that mission for obvious reasons, google it). Most afro hippies voice lines were removed.A lot of free roam events also didn't make it to the remake.Blisk mutants and blisk spores suffered a pretty questionable redesign, I just hate them. The spores now look like some kind of cartoon-faced coronavirus. The mutants lost their human remanescent traits and are now all covered in blisters. They also have a stupid long tongue, something straight outta Marvel's Venom.The game is now looking good as ever, even more than the previous remake! But, the game is riddled with bugs and glitches, also a terrible optimization.It goes from petty bugs like something that you can fix by quitting to the menu and returning, to game-breaking bugs and weird graphical glitches! After some time playing you will start to notice flickering textures, odd texture artifacts and some crazy colored texture overlays, probably result of the bad programming on the Free Love mechanic.I lost count of how many times I had to return to checkpoint because of some bug on the mission or targets not spawning, it's absurd! I also did not receive the blue furotech cells from the last mission I completed before writing this review, even though the game said I received on the results screen.Now regarding the optimzation, it's pretty trash, you've probably read a lot of complaints by now. I rock a RTX 3070 OC, with a R7 5800X and 32GB RAM, I know it's not a spaceship of a computer, but it's pretty decent, so the game wasn't supposed to dip from 60-90fps on maximum settings to 5-10fps on certain situations, like when multiple blisk warriors start blasting their energy beam at you.Conclusion: If you value your money, do not buy this remake! I just can't get over how good Black Forest Games did with the first remake, and now they deliver us this ugly mess, I'm offended by it! It's Resident Evil 3 remake all over again. If you're really into playing  Destroy all Humans 2, go play the original one. This remake deserved way more love and time in the oven.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Never mind, they fixed it.ORIGINAL REVIEW:I really want to recommend this game, but at launch, bugs and performance issues have made it difficult to even play the thing.On first boot, the game launched at 4K native res. with everything set to Ultra. No internal resolution scaling is available. A bit much for my rig to handle. Lowering the resolution to 1440p in fullscreen mode causes the game to repeatedly cycle between fullscreen 1440p and 4K in a box in the corner of the screen (not a window.) _childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans 2 is a fantastic step up from the original game. It is larger and definitely more enjoyable. However there were a few problems which i'll address later. This is also coming from a person who played it on day one so I am not surprised about these things as they were kind of expected.Let's start with the story. In the previous game you play as Crypto who is accompanied by Pox. They were sent to earth to attempt to take over. In that game we were only restricted to exploring the USA. You would go around completing various missions and eventually take over the capitol and take power as the president. This then ties in with the new game. As the previous one was set in the 50s this now takes place in the 60s. We can see that the environment has changed. The Hippie movement has arrived. But so have the soviets. Crypto is first confronted by them and soon has to work out how to get rid of them. Unfortunately while this is happening Pox ends up getting blown up and for the rest of the game takes form as virtual pox. After slowly discovering the soviets plan we are then told to go to another location. This time out of the US which I love. We can finally explore more of the globe. We then visit places like Japan and Russia. The overall story I think is pretty good. But longer and more interactive than the first game. One thing which I really prefer is that there are no more challenges. Instead there are multiple side quests where you can help various people across the area (most of the time they're your enemy). You even get to start your own cult too!Compared to the first game it is pretty much the same. So there's not much to talk about. The control are exactly the same and so are a few of the weapons. There are a few new ones which are quite enjoyable to use. Throughout my playthrough I experienced a few problems. Firstly was on one of the first big missions. Where it crashed completely. Luckily it didn't corrupt anything but it came out of nowhere. It happened I think another few times. I also experienced a lot of lag even on low settings on bigger areas which was really weird. But other than that the game would sit at a solid 60fps.It's going to be around an 8/10. I would definitely recommend it for old and new fans of the series as I thoroughly enjoyed it. Just those annoying bugs every now and then. Was super fun trying to get all the achievements too. There was so much to do! Definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for February 2024, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before March 5th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Updating a PS2 game for modern audiences, kind of. Destroy All Humans 2! Reprobed is the follow-up to the Destroy All Humans Remake from Humble Choice April 2022, and it feels almost similar in quality.  Take a PlayStation 2 game, update the visuals and graphics, and attempt to retain what made the original stand out such as voice acting.  The experience here is good and delivers on the sequel.  While it’s not a completely different experience it still delivered a game for players that wanted a second helping of this franchise. Still, when I say modernized the game, there are limitations, the game still has the old fade out at the end of missions, some of the gameplay elements are a little static, and there’s an older feeling to the game.  Now I love Playstation 2, it’s what I’m spending a lot of time playing currently, but if players don’t have a love for that era in gaming, this is going to feel quite rough.  Also Destroy All Humans 2 was not as great as the original, so in that way, it’s a bit of a step down.Pick this up if you like the original Destroy All Humans, especially the remake, and want more.  I think they did a better job with the remake here, but the original sequel was a touch weaker, so it evens out.  The humor also feels a little dated, not cringy necessarily, but I don’t know the last time I heard or thought about hippies from the 60s.   It’s just not a reference that's common in 2024.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is a mixed bag for me; its great graphically but some changes to core game-play are really baffling; The jet pack starts with max levels, and there is a ground skating ability which makes traversing the map far too easy (though its a welcome addition, the issue is you get it right away). In general, there is a lot of changes made to progression. I don't really understand why there were censored (removed) missions either, as the game is not meant for kids and it has a content warning for that exact purpose. AI has been dumbed down, removing little things that made the first game challenging, you just ♥♥♥♥ on every enemy, I think you can probably beat this game in like a fraction of the time that it took to beat the original (because of how trivialized traversal and combat have become). I think that the art has been greatly improved, style-wise and graphics-wise, which is a plus. Despite my excellent specs I still get stutters (3090TI, Ryzen 5950x, 128gig ram) which is actually insane, I have no idea how the average PC runs this game if mine has issues. My biggest gripe is the difficulty though, I know I don't have to use the new features such as skating but I just don't understand why they made the game this easy, even on the max difficulty I feel immortal. The original game wasn't that hard, but the combination of weapons and movement upgrades that you receive right away really makes it less fun. Like it took you a while to get your jetpack to a good level in the original game, whereas now you start maxed out and can literally dodge any and all enemies no matter how many are thrown your way. It feels like some executive played the original DAH2 and decided to remove all of the "tedium" to improve the game, but instead took out any sense of progression. All they had to do is make the skates an upgrade and leave the jetpack as it was. Also, lots of dialogue was removed that made it interesting to scan brains, no idea why (once again it feels like some executive just tried to make this game as noncontroversial as possible, despite the fact that the slight edge the original had added to its charm)I would give this game like a 5/10 (currently because of balance and performance issues), though this game would be worth it if they make it run better on regular specs (most people aren't terminally online and don't have 3090TI). Also I would love if they would add some progression limits, like in the original, not having to upgrade the jetpack is a really significant change, despite that not seeming like a big deal, you used to have to earn upgrades whereas now it feels like you start on new game plus. I'm glad that they kept the co-op but frankly removing that would really take this down from a 5/10 to like a 2/10. Co-op is really important for DAH2, it was one of the coolest features because everything is better with friends.Ultimately I think we have finally entered the era when my generation (gen z) are just being exploited for nostalgia money, yeah I love that this franchise got a remake, but the poor performance and gameplay changes feel like the developers just don't care about the game as much as I do. We're gonna get a Banjo-Kazooie remake soon too, don't believe me? just wait, we're gonna get remakes of any and all old properties that were remotely popular because the gaming industry has really begun to stagnate, new games are poorly thought out and have a shorter lifespan than most perishable foods that you buy at the supermarket, so nostalgia bating seems to be the way to make a quick buck. While there will be a good remake once in a while I think that this is just a sign of dark days to come. I understand that games are a business and need to make money, but I feel like we are settling for worse and worse products every year, even if these new games technically look great.will bump up to a "worth a buy" when they fix the performance and add the progression back, otherwise, you are literally paying for something that is worse than the original in everything but looks. Buy on sale, not worth 39.99, and definitely don't buy the skin packs.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the game after playing through it on the GOG version, because frankly I don’t think this is the lazy or “bad” remake that I’ve read a lot of people saying it is, and this is coming from someone who finished the original game a couple of years ago when it came out through the ps2 emu on the ps4, I even platinumed the freaking thing back then.Now, it is true that the developers for some absurd reason removed and took a side mission that had a man dealing with being transgender or something of sorts, apparently that’s out of the realm of satire nowadays; I say this because the game lampoons -just like the first-, a number of different crowds from the time period it takes place (the 1960’s) hippies, the military, the Russians, spy films, science fiction films, James Bond movies, everything about the counterculture, the British invasion, the Indian spiritual influence in the west during the time, etc. But for some reason, that one mission had to go away. If they were smart, they would release it as DLC, either free or paid, just get something out of the controversy.As for the actual game? I feel as if people are more keen in mentioning what got taken out rather than what was kept in and improved, it is a remake after all, and there’s a lot here that’s as fantastic as it’s ever been if not a lot more, there are frankly a lot of side content I didn’t remember the original having, there’s also the ability to replay through the side and main mission content with different modifiers in a similar fashion to something like say a traditional NG+ mode where you get to keep all of your upgrades, whilst at the same time experimenting with the game’s mechanics and difficulty settings. That’s another addition as well, the difficulty settings in the game range from easier difficulty settings to fairly difficult ones at that, although the game for the most part is well balanced independently of whether you’re playing on easy, normal, or hard and very hard. Except for one mission near the end that serves as a escort quest through some sort of alien base which made me want to tear my hair out because of how badly it had been updated (if updated at all).There’s also the revamped combat & movement most people seem to just gloss over for some strange reason, maybe they don’t remember how the original game played or something? The original game was really slow and clunky, it was a completely different kind of gameplay experience, more methodical in a way, lot less chaotic and fun in my opinion. In this one you’re essentially a one-man army, and there are upgrades here for both your movement as well as your arsenal, so you’re left with completely new weapons that weren’t available in the original versions of the game. There’s an upgrade to your ion detonator which pulls objects and enemies towards it making them ragdoll in the process, and on top of that, it has a strong chance to convert any objects it destroys in more ammo for your weapons; and that’s not even talking about the upgrades to something like the Anal Probe, which allow you to not only shoot multiple ones creating utter chaos as enemies and npc’s alike run around grabbing their buttocks, but also convinces some of your  enemies to fight on your side, whilst in other cases the effect multiplies to others whether you fire at them or not. It’s pretty darn fun, and there’s a number of different, newer weapons on top of that, that frankly, I didn’t use because I was just so pleased with how they handled the original arsenal.There’s the story which has remained for the most part unchanged, some of the jokes are going to land, others are not, the problem is that it relies on a lot of stereotypical humour to make fun of the decade, but in the midst of it you can actually get some pretty sensible and clever jokes here and there, overall I would say I liked the story and the character’s in it, but I completely understand why people might get put off by it, I personally really dislike how they kept the extremely cartoony aesthetic for people, some of them look great such as Natasha, but others just look too goofy for me, and they do change the overall atmosphere of the game as a result.Having said that, I do appreciate what THQ has done with these games and I can only hope they either remaster the rest of them, or alternatively come up with newer versions of the titles. There are issues here and there that still need some sorting out, even in this title, like the fact that there are some balancing issues in that escort mission, or alternatively how some of the tutorials are mislabelled for kb & m players, plus there’s also the fact that the game got that side mission taken out and to top it off, they didn’t really build on top of the collectible locator, which if you’re like me and want to get 100% completion, it can get really, really annoying. They just kinda added a pulse indicator that gets progressively closer as you get closer to the collectibles; why not add an upgrade system for that, maybe one that lets me actually mark the collectibles in my map? That would’ve been awesome.I’ve also heard some have had some pretty big performance problems, but I personally haven’t run into any of them, unless I’m doing something else while I’m playing or I’m absolutely destroying cities, as in running around and obviously doing stuff that the devs didn’t intended for me to do, like completely try and combine different saucer upgrades and weapon attacks to obliterate an entire town. There are five towns here and they’re all fairly detailed, a lot of the locales have their own small activities that you see people partaking in, so in America you’ll have some hippies protesting, while in Britain you have some of them meditating and there will be side content build around it a lot of the times, which is pretty cool as well. Some of the later stages are fairly detailed as well, and I didn’t run into more than a single crash at one point where I enabled a lot of game modifiers when replaying a pretty hectic mission, not trying to excuse it, but just saying, it’s not really a game you want to “stress” that much. As for my settings? I literally left everything by default, the game defaulted to borderless fullscreen with vsync on and put most settings on Ultra, and I was happy.I didn’t even talked about the tons of costumes you can get and change as you play, this was one of the coolest additions in the first game’s remake and remains a beautiful addition here, now you can even customize your saucer with some pretty cool skins which, if you’re like me, you’ll really come to appreciate. The skins by default are fairly detailed and I’m planning to get the dlc ones because they’re frankly quite good and seem like work went into them.So overall, I do recommend the game, although I do think that is more of cautious recommendation because even back then it was quite a “niche” game, most people probably won’t get a lot of the references, nor humour that the game is using, simply because you have to be familiarized with a lot of aspects of the decade and the historicity of it in order to get a lot of the jokes. But yeah, I think THQ does deserve a commendation for this title, despite its issues, hopefully they won’t abandon it and keep sorting out the problems people seem to have and, although I’m not holding my breath for it, they really should do something about the mission they took out and the balancing problems at later levels in the game, plus maybe… add some upgrade to the collectibles, like a toggle that lets me see all of them in the map after finishing the main story? Maybe? Maybe a way to upgrade the locator? Just a thought people, don’t take this ♥♥♥♥ too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful Re-make of the original game that - as far as i can tell - deviated from the source game as little as possible. There were some new additions that make some aspects worlds better, but some crucial changes that personally frustrated me. Overall, the pros outweigh the cons and this is still the gold standard for how you remake a classic title (looking at you, ratchet and clank!)Compared to the original there are many pros, but not without a few cons:Pros:-The maps, textures, guns, environments, NPC's, and every other asset imaginable got a huge facelift. Secondary characters like Shama LLama, Dr. Go!, Sergei, ETC, have more unique character models, and Citizens/cops/soldiers/etc have more variation.-Cutscenes, cinematics, main missions, side missions are completely redone. Original dialogue and music is updated and word for word just as witty and well voiced as i remember.-Upgrade levels (as far as i remember) add more variety and utility to Crypto's arsenal, meaning that every weapon has some viability-Crypto's arsenal gets a few new toys, namely the SKATE (basically, hoverboard shoes) and the Saucer gets a repulsor blast that repels and eventually redirects missiles. Both Additions dont massively change the gameplay, but feel like that last little piece that was missing from the original DAH2. The SKATE lets you zip around the map at great speeds, and despite sliding around alot when turning, once you get used to how it handles its alot of fun to use. Crypto and the Saucer now have swappable skins, which i personally didnt care for, but make it fun when playing multiplayer with a friend.-Crypto can now use PK and shoot at the same time! despite my lengthy gripe with the new PK system, this adds a fun level of freshness to the combat.-Overall extremely faithful to the original. The story, missions, characters, dialogue and locales are simply better looking versions of their former selves, despite the cons listed below. Side missions also now have more cutscenes and an extra level of polish, which makes them feel a little more important than just goofy one offs for the sole purpose of getting more upgrades. Some areas, like coyote bongwater's boss arena, now have their own unique map, which is a nice touch.-I also feel as if they added a few voice lines to NPC's? I dont at all remember them making snarky comments to when you ran out of ammo. Additionally, anal probing a blisk only for them to say "Huh, i didnt even know we had anuses!" is one of the funniest lines ive ever heard, and i know id have remembered it if it was in the original. If this is the case and they did add more dialogue, great!Cons:-The weapons, despite adding new variety with the upgrade system, feel like theyve been poorly re-balanced. Ion Detonator has alot of great new perks (transmog chance on every detonation), but it feels like its been powered down significantly. Meteor Launcher sees a completely redesigned firing animation (a wormhole showers dozens of meteors down instead of a barrage of 3) but once again, even they feel like theyve been severely nerfed. You're telling me dozens of thousand pound rocks hurtling at breakneck speeds wont demolish a building? In addition, some weapons are now much more powerful, and overshadow the rest. The anal probe and disintegrator, when fully upgraded, can carry you through the whole game, if you somehow decide to use the guns instead of PK throwing EVERYTHING away for an instant kill. Gastro's AI never seems to work consistently for me, and the Burrow beast will often just completely disappear even with fresh "bait" still applied to enemies. -The PK system is my biggest personal gripe. In the original title, all PK powers (Extract, Free Love, Psychokinesis throw and lift, and forget/follow) all worked off of a lock on system followed by a button press. That made sense to me, as it allowed you to select your target precisely and then do what you desire. Now, Free love is a gadget in the weapon wheel, PK levitation and throwing is an odd pairing of Holding/Tapping the RMB. Free love, is now alot less OP - Basically a "Stop shooting at me and forget the whole thing" button - but despite its new functionality of requiring more people to start the dance its still pretty easy to cheese. Extract brains, after a certain upgrade, is now hilariously OP in congested areas. Basically, after one head pops, itll spread to another person, but if you manually pop a few heads itll spread to EVERYONE and suddenly youre swimming in brains. Despite this, its still very entertaining to use. -PK throw, specifically, functions in a way that i really dislike. Originally, picking objects, people, and vehicles up felt both natural and otherworldly at the same time. A crate could be lifted into the air and moved around freely and swiftly, while a tank was sluggish to lift and when thrown hit with alot of force. Now, All objects can be whisked around gleefully (heavy objects sort of "Wiggle" for a few seconds until being whisked into the air), and you either have the option to toss things around gently (releasing PK), or THROWING THEM INTO ♥♥♥♥♥ ORBIT (PK Throw). In addition to this, People when picked up used to flail around helplessly and goofily while tossing out their dialogue. Though the funny dialogue remains, now they just kinda float there like a plank of wood. Also, you used to be able to move them around, pushing, pulling, raising and lowering the object. Now, it just hovers over your shoulder. While its still fun to toss people around and throw things at will, it doesnt move things around with the same sort of weighty and chaotic nature, which leaves it feeling bland after the first map. PK's utility and overall feel was one of my favorite things to fool around with in the open world (Nothing made me laugh harder than lifting a hippie van into the air, Them diving out, and immediately yelling "catch me ground!" only to faceplant with an abrupt "Oof". Now they wont even jump out of the car!!)-The jetpack is no longer upgradeable. This is a bit of a pro and a con, as i distinctly remember the vanilla jetpack being pretty lackluster, but what i still enjoyed about the first game is that it gradually gets more powerful if you choose to upgrade it. Minor, but i did kinda wish we had the option to upgrade for more height (or maybe an upgraded hover ability?) The SKATE upgrade tree adds an immediate jetpack boost vs the typical slow controlled lift, but it only serves to help with getting in the air during a fight.-I dont care for the updated mutant designs. They feel way too much like Venom! Additionally, the spore clouds have now become spore creatures, with faces and erratic flight patterns. I kinda preferred the sort of gas cloud they were in the original. I got over it though.-In terms of quality and polish, i periodically experience a bit of pop in and textures that wont fully render. The biggest bugs ive seen is where AI regularly tends to pause and NPC's move without walking animations, disappearing, or alltogether glitching out when manipulating with PK. Occasionally during dialogue sections, some characters' dialogue will play without their mouths or faces moving. Most of these bugs are minor and dont present themselves too often. Overall, despite the cons and my cranky ranting, its still a great remake. The Devs didnt take any creative liberties, made a few efforts to add some new features and do away with older problems, and completely enhanced the overall visual appeal of the game. If youre a fan of the original, i recommend picking this up!

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! 2 has always been my all-time favorite game! I played it for the first time back in 2009 on my PS2 and I was just enraptured by it: the plot, the characters, the wit, the references, it was all simply amazing. I had always hoped that the franchise would pick up, but alas, it'd seemed as though it was no longer going to continue beyond PoTF (released in December of 2008).Fast forward some 10 years, and I saw that THQ was working on releasing a remake of DAH! (which I'd never played) and DAH!2. The amount of joy and thrill I was overcome with was indescribable. And in the end, having to play and re-live my childhood experience with Crypto and Pox all over again was truly heartwarming—and a blast!The graphics rework is out of this world! The depth and level of detail in the maps and objects were just insane. I thoroughly enjoyed the aesthetic element of the game alongside the actual game play.I loved how they made the NPCs look distinct and unique with features that distinguished one from another. I only felt that they seemed a bit too toony compared to the more realistic original version. They also removed some scenes that I was hoping to see, or altered them, which was kind of nice, but I would have loved it if they kept them true to the original.Also, I'm not sure if it was just me, but the maps also felt a little more "compact" in the sense that I was able to get from one end of the map to the other in less than a minute. Everything seemed to be "closer" to each other, and distances shorter, making the world feel smaller. The camera angle and closer panning might have been a reason. Or maybe, is it that I'm comparing this experience on a 16" laptop screen to having played it on a large screen TV back in 2009? It could also just be that things appear larger to you the first time you engage with them. Nostalgia can distort perception!The one thing that really disappointed in the remake was that they removed the travel cut scene, something that was really iconic in DAH!2. Honestly, they should bring that back!Overall, I'm really grateful to the devs who brought this gem of a game back under the limelight. It deserved that! I'm now hoping they intend to release a remake or remaster of the other two games: Big Willy Unleashed and Path of the Furon!

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! 1 & 2 are examples of my ideal way of "remaking" older games.  I never played the original DAH!2, but I can tell this remake is in keeping with older styles of game design.  It's not a bloated, Poopisoft-inspired mess of repetitive open zone gaming, like Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is.I want "remakes" of action/adventure games to feel like the old days of gaming, before they all converged on the same optimized "best practice" designs that have made the current AAA scene feel homogenized and formulaic.There's not much I can say about DAH!2-R (2022), other than it delivered just as well as DAH! (2020).  It has classic arcadey gameplay, pre-MCU genuinely humorous dialogue, a bombshell of a woman with ideal feminine body proportions, and can be fully completed in a reasonable time frame - all things that modern AAA action/adventure games refuse to give us anymore.If we MUST get inundated with remakes, hopefully at least some will be like the DAH! remakes.

_childDocuments_.review: So it seems like many folks are experiencing bug issues (less and less with each subsequent update it would seem). I suppose  I got lucky in the sense that I did not have any bugs impede my progress (a few textures would pop out here and there but that was about it). I never played the Destroy All Humans series on the original PS2, but remember the existence of the games and my desire to play them at the time. When the remaster of the original came out in 2020 I picked it up since I was in an early pandemic-induced "whatever, I'll give this a shot" kind of mood. I enjoyed the experience quite a bit, and so was willing to go down the rabbit hole once again for the sequel. I type all this as a way of saying that my connection to this series is not one rooted in nostalgia. I have enjoyed them for what they are without my perception being colored by personal experience. I remember thinking of the first game in this remastered duology as very much a warmed over PS2 game, with all the shallowness and antiquated design that that might imply. I am happy to say that this one feels like something a little more timelessly modern (in terms of its gameplay loop anyways). There are still some missions that are massive difficulty spikes (there's one Russian saucer mission that will haunt my dreams), but for the most part you run around and zap people and it's all enjoyable and colorful enough.That being said, anything beyond the basic gameplay loop feels half-baked at best. The dialogue is annoying and I found myself skipping most of it. I understand that it's all preserved from the original and I'm not here to harp on the actual content of the dialogue, it's just unfunny. You are given options to be able to choose different dialogue, but it doesn't change anything beyond hearing other VO lines and I really couldn't care less. I would love to see this team make their own Destroy All Humans game not based on an existing title. I would love to see this series truly updated for the modern age. Here's hoping.

_childDocuments_.review: **NEEDS DEV ATTENTION IN ITS CURRENT STATE! Game is poorly optimized and visual, audio and gameplay bugs exist throughout the game! People playing should report bugs as they appear to the devs so they can be smoothed out and the game allowed to be as good as it can be.Overall it's a mostly faithful, fun and beautiful remake of what was already a great game. Strongly recommend getting, and providing constructive feedback so it can be improved.PROS* NPCs, visual effects, environments, lighting, are all gorgeous to look at* Updates to weapons and gameplay features never deviate too far from source material while helping them feel fresh and ironing out kinks in their original iterations* Environments are carefully crafted and fun to explore* Game is capable of loading many more NPCs onto the screen at once than the first DAH remaster* Introduction of gameplay difficulty was HUGE for me, I enjoyed playing on harder difficulties much more* Many new enemy types and NPC models* Adjustments to story, character descriptions and some mission details make some politically backward moments more palatable (but are sometimes very transparent)CONS* Optimization at launch is terrible. My PC is capable of running about anything with high graphics settings, but for me the game was initially unplayable. After adjusting graphics settings, updating drivers, restarting the game etc. it runs much better, but still constantly lags in times of action or in populated areas, and even changing graphics to their lowest settings still results in framerate issues* Visual effects, lighting and some weather effects are flickering, jagged and distracting. The lighting effect around extracted brains is the most glaring example to me, some lamps in Albion and Tesla coils also look like this* Many small texture errors or bugs. Most Crypto skins have no helmet bubble on Solaris, all stationary AA guns have US Army markings, some parts of buildings will remain suspended in space after their destruction, backwards CCCP markings on dome structure supports in Solaris, flickering text decals on Soviet and Takoshimese tanks, bizarre keysmashing on the Bay City KGB poster collectible... Nothing gamebreaking, but noticeable issues that should be patched out* Issues and undesirable quirks with physics, especially PK. NPCs and objects shake violently when being held with PK or the saucer's abduction beam (this looks ugly and makes objects difficult to maneuver, which was a problem when placing vans on rooftops as part of a mission) and lag behind Crypto when he skates, and vehicles sometimes roll over or fly into the air inexplicably* Game often has trouble spawning NPCs when moving quickly through areas* Some audio problems. Phone booth operator voice on some maps like Tunguska and Takoshima switches between male and female on prank calls, voices in dialogue branches are sometimes much too quiet, some male hippies have the wrong cortex scan voice and some NPC types get stuck repeating mission-specific dialogue* At one point, after unlocking and visiting Tunguska and then going back to Takoshima, Tunguska disappeared for me from the world navigator. I was able to fix this by replaying the first Tunguska mission

_childDocuments_.review: "Destroy All Humans! 2 - Reprobed" is everything I was hoping for in a remake of one of the best games of the PS2 era. The game oozes with wit and charm thanks to the new enhanced and beautiful graphics while keeping with the series' original iconic, on-the-nose humor, and fun gameplay. The game once again follows the alien invader Crypto and his boss Pox as they explore 1960s Earth and uncover a shocking (and hilarious James Bond/spy movie parody) Russian conspiracy. The game retains all of the fun mechanics and features of the first "Destroy All Humans!" game and expands on them with new weapons and abilities, as well as additional content and side quests. It's an all-around great time if you are a fan of the series and enjoy some good old-fashioned destruction and mayhem.

_childDocuments_.review: . Where should I begin? Well, I guess I should start with the remake that came out 2 years ago. In fact, most of my feelings that apply to this game also applied to the remake. So much so that I'll simply  instead of rewriting it all here. Crypto's movement and gunplay still feels amazing, there are still some minor control issues, the mission structure still reeks of 2000's game design, and almost everything else I said applies.What's different? Well, there's a few new weapons to start us off. One you get very early is the Dislocator, a weapon that fires purple disks that sends targets flying. It's not quite the same as the one from 2006 that would slowly lift cars into the sky; instead, it will now violently pinball your target around the world, creating concussive blasts wherever it hits. It's definitely more useful in this edition (I practically never used it in the 2006 version because it was such an inefficient weapon), although your trusty Zap-O-Matic and Anal Probe is more useful most of the time. The other 'new' weapons from 2006 are also represented here. They all follow a similar pattern as the Dislocator (which was also a problem in 2006); the original weapons and abilities are so devastating that half the time you forget to pull out the new gimmicky weapons with their more niche uses.  At least they fixed the Ion Detonator issue I had; you can now refund upgrades for experimentation.Visually, this is a pretty game. It's clear that tons of attention to detail went into this game. Every map is dripping with personality. Bay City rooftop smoking lounges, Takoshimese markets and side streets, and Russian tundras are all gorgeously depicted. There's a few problems, such as lights having shimmering problems (at least with AMD FSR 2.0 enabled), certain effects being too brutal (especially in the final map, bring some sunglasses), and some smaller issues that I noticed (the Sun and Moon do not set in the North), but on the whole they went the extra mile with making these environments feel expressive and lived-in. It's definitely more impressive than other current open-world sandbox games.The story and writing is almost entirely unchanged. It's puerile and crass, it breaks the fourth wall more times than the number of humans you destroy, and it's definitely a product of its time... but I still found myself laughing at the jokes here in spite of myself. It's also not only phallus jokes (not that there's anything wrong with those, mind), there's a good number of deeper cuts in here. Hope you're read up on your 60's pop culture references here, kids. Otherwise, the story is strictly okay. Nothing too fancy here. It's still a better love story than Twilight, though!The missions here are revamped a touch, with optional objectives again peppered in to keep things fresh. Some are totally different and more complex, the boss battle at the end of the first map being a prime example. No longer is it a boring room, it's an entirely new set piece with new rules of engagement. Instead of challenges from the first game, now you get side jobs to earn your upgrade currencies. These can be very hit-or-miss; I hope you like running around in disguise and doing escort missions, because that's what you'll be spending a lot of your time doing for these. Sure, they may have some entertaining qualities such as giving cheap yucks with the abundant number of minds to read, but they don't hold up so well on repeated playthroughs (which the game now encourages, you can replay any mission with a number of modifiers that range from cheat codes to hardcore difficulty increases. I have not played around with these too much, but it's a welcome addition.)Let's chat about difficulty. I played this game on the hardest available difficulty (I played the first remake on medium.) I thought it could have been a touch harder. I failed a mission here and there (mostly due to dialogue trees or restarting due to missing optional objectives), but I never actually died (despite coming close on occasion.) The late-game enemies start off promising, and do shake things up a bit, but once you adjust to them and learn their quirks you dispatch them as easily as every other threat in the game thanks to your frankly ridiculous roster of weapons and abilities. Some of the optional objectives were more frustrating than difficult due to chaos inherent in the game systems, especially towards the end of the game; Allies killing targets that you're supposed to, enemies technically dying from sources other than the one they're meant to, things like that. As missions get longer and more complex this gets annoying, especially if you accidentally hit a checkpoint. It also doesn't help that sometimes objectives broke in unexpected ways, with mandatory targets glitching out-of-bounds or allies getting stuck, causing soft-locks. Which brings me to... We have:...and more. The worst bug I found was a huge disappointment at the very end: You get a special resource to use on the final upgrades for your weapons by beating main story quests, and you're supposed to get several of these for completing the last mission. The end screen said I got them, but they did not increase my counter in the shop. This means that I can't actually 100% the game on this save file, I lack the resources for the final upgrades.I don't know if it's a bug, but the saucer felt way too weak. It takes half your Sonic Boom ammo to destroy one tiny shack. Forget about using your Death Ray on that shack, it takes even longer. Even with all upgrades on both. I really think it's unintentional.Closing thoughts: I recommend this game with an asterisk: You might not enjoy the sense of humor. You might not enjoy the dated mission structure. And while some are benign and funny (to an extent), you're certainly not going to enjoy the bugs. But if you're okay with all that, you're gonna get more  I know I focused on the negative in this review, but . My gushing in that linked review applies here too and is just as relevant.So pleasepleasePLEASE Black Forest Games: fix the bugs, and then make an original third game. You have such a solid foundation in just how GOOD playing this game feels. Very few games succeed in making you feel as badass as this one. Don't squander this potential, I'm begging.P.S. the first is still my favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I hate giving this remake a negative review, considering all the love and care that was put into it by developers, the state of the game is still really BAD. Yes, everything written about the optimization in all of the discussions about DAH!2 is true. I thought that people are exaggerating a bit or that everything was fixed already, - but nope. It's not as horrible as it was during the release and a few first months, but even after several big patches and updates it still stutters, freezes, crashes and breaks apart. Sometimes the framerate gets so low that your game turns into a silly slideshow. Overall it's safe to say it's kind of a mess. Just not as a big mess as it was a year ago...  Despite all of the statements above I can see that it's a great remake and even more than that, - a great game. I've played the original a while ago and in my honest to God opinion the Reprobed version is overall a better experience and not as sluggish and clunky in terms of animations and gameplay as the 2006 counterpart. Style is a bit off and I much prefer the more realistic old one, but it all comes down to preference. Everything is still looking gorgeous, cartoony, and colorful. You would love it, if it's your thing. I just find the original better.I would advise you to wait for patches (if we ever get them) and only then buy the game. There are not much single-player PS2 type of games with no strings attached left nowadays, so I still have some belief in developers and I still hope they will fix all the bugs. If not, - well, we all would think twice before buying a new Destroy All Humans! game.

_childDocuments_.review: Groovy! Destroy All Humans! 2 - Reprobed is both a very good remake of the cult classic from 2006, and an excellent improvement on the 2020 Destroy All Humans! Remake. There are a some things that have been removed or changed in this game, so it's not a 1:1 recreation of the original, but it IS an amazingly fun and hilarious time, and most things that have changed are for the better, or simply to give a new experience. But over the new coat of paint, it's still the same wacky and fun time we all had with this game back in '06.For a modern audience that might never have played the original, it will likely be a breath of fresh air in the modern gaming landscape, and a wonderfully fun time. (And I highly encourage playing the '06 original, be it through emulation or original hardware.)While I personally recommend this game and find it a total blast, there are quite a large number of bugs and minor technical issues with this game, sometimes things will go off the rails. I have had nothing game-breaking happen to me currently, but you'll notice the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: A tireless lover, the main hater of radiation in the entire universe, a master at insulting anyone - Crypto is back. He just wanted to hang out and have fun with the girls, but the Majestic, the KGB, the yakuza, the hippies, the mafia, the nasty crayfish won't let him do it in peace. Krypto's second campaign against (for?!) the human race begins. This is the case when nostalgia makes it even more painful, because even just a good game from those times is perceived as an order of magnitude funnier, more inventive than attempts to “joke” many modern games. Humor constantly walks on the edge, not being afraid to be on it, therefore now it is perceived even funnier. Albion turned out to be the only faded location, the missions turned out to be too unpretentious there, but I swear by my atomic blaster, I laughed like crazy from everything that happened in Japan. The same, albeit to a slightly lesser extent, applies to America and Tunguska, where both the main and secondary quests make you want to laugh wildly. Everything is so hypertrophied and crazy, as it should be in such a game, it's stupid to be shy about something.How cool it is to hear the screaming voice of Richard Horvitz, the embodiment of my favorite Invader Zim from childhood, through his character Pox constantly bickering with Crypto. Their quarrels are an art in their own right, it's like a game within a game, I didn't miss a single opportunity to exchange barbs with each other. The plot is perfectly silly, there is no place for common sense and some kind of stopcocks. And in the gameplay, everything is so in place that there is nothing even to scold. The weapons are fun and different, flying on a flying saucer, hunting for the fleeing military is a pleasure, the enemies are constantly evolving, and the main bosses are forced to strain all their resources. A huge number of collectibles will make you carefully explore the map; some of them are hidden unusually cleverly. The only obvious drawback so far is the technical situation, if I didn’t meet any critical bugs, then the game crashes were quite common, and the optimization was lame in places, but it is likely that this will be fixed with patches in the future ..Crypto is so lazy to fight threats again that his victories feel even more inexplicable and hilarious. The game is so archetypal that it becomes the sail that carries it forward.  And it's true, all the games of those times need is a modern look, and they are capable of delivering pleasure even after 16 years. Great return, our little vicious alien!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR If you are a fan of the original and played it extensively, you will be disappointed. This hurts me to say but this is a bad remake. Especially compared to the first. It is better now but still pales in comparison to the first.I came into this with very high expectations after the work done on the remake of the first game. To say I am disappointed would be an understatement. The game is not a very faithful reproduction like the first. There are several gameplay elements that have been altered, and most of them are bad. The Dislocator, which was one of the most enjoyable weapons in the game, is now a complete mess. It basically just dribbles NPCs or vehicles on the ground a bit then disappears. It doesn't behave at all like the orginal. Since the dislocator was my favorite thing from the original, this is honestly my biggest gripe. NPCs ragdoll physics are also completely broken so any time enough force is applied, you get the spaghetti effect. This applies to PK attacks, Dislocator attacks, and Gene Splicer beam on the saucer (more on this later). Overall weapon damage is extremely unbalanced. A dislocator shot on a vehicle usually destroys the vehicle before it has had a chance to cause any mayhem. A new attack added called PK Slam allows you to grab an NPC and slam it into objects. The damage dealt from this is insanely unbalanced. Saucer's death ray is also very weak compared to the original. Now for the saucer in general. The controls are atrocious on keyboard and mouse with no easily found way to change them. Your altitude is controlled by moving the mouse up and down. Obviously so is your camera. Every time you turn the camera your saucer is wildly flailing up and down. Why it isn't just bound to Q and E is a mystery to me. The Gene Splicer, which is a major tool for upgrading abilities and progressing through the game, is also broken. The force applied to the NPCs caught in the beam is so high that they either disappear completely, spaghetti out and clip through the ground, or get successfully abducted. The later is about 1 in every 10-15 in my experience. The angle of the beam is also the same as the death ray. It should be straight down. Apparently this can be changed on the fly but this may be a glitch on my end. Speaking of abducted, the Abduct-O-Beam is useless now. The camera doesn't pitch down automatically like it should so you cant see what is caught in the beam. As far as I could tell anything that I should have been picking up in the beam wasn't doing anything anyway. I have had no success in using the beam to abduct NPCs for gene splicing either. This was how the original game worked and should have been kept that way. I am having a lot of glitches surrounding the saucer controls so hopefully this will be fixed. The camera cannot be pitched at all manually on the saucer either, which is like the original. However, the angle it is locked at now makes it very difficult to use the gene splicer effectively and seems to be pitched higher than the original game. ***EDIT***The camera is pitched up and down by holding control. This took a bit to get to work. IDK why but considering the other glitches I have had I am not too surprised.There are a lot of artistic changes that have been made to story missions just in the first hour of gameplay too. *** SPOILER ALERT *** Such as the acid trip sequence that happens during the "boss fight" with Coyote Bongwater. This boss fight is also one of the most obvious examples of enemies popping in as well. It is very easy to find the spawner, kill the enemy, and watch another spawn directly in front of you. This happens a lot through the first section of the game. This should all happen off screen, and to a lesser extent as spawning of enemies is so high it detracts from the boss fight and other gameplay. How these issues made it through QA is an absolute mystery. Among other artistic changes are the additions of more foliage and objects. It is cluttered. There are a lot of obstacles in your path now. Another artistic change is the UI. The new UI is extremely un-intuitive and should have been built off of the original. Enough said. The only welcome change is the addition of S.K.A.T.E. which is an upgrade you could get from your Dash power in the Pox-Mart. You now start the game with it. It works well, so long as you aren't doing downhill. I am only an hour in, so this is already a lot. I will have more to say I'm sure. My biggest question to the Devs is why? Just why? _childDocuments_.review: Upon firing up Destroy All Humans 2, you'll be met with a disclaimer. It reads “While the experience has been upgraded, the content and historical record of the original invasion of the Furons remains a near-identical clone. The story, words and images contained within may be shocking to the modern human brain!”Let that serve as warning, though it isn't entirely accurate. I wouldn't describe the writing of DAH2 as 'shocking'; puerility, jokes about sleeping with teenagers, and good ol' fashioned stereotyping don't shock so much as bore. I'd call it schoolyard humour, utterly lacking in tact or charm. When I was ten years old, this stuff was the height of hilarity, but the only people who enjoy this kind of writing in 2023 are those sad sacks who bang on about how modern comedy is ruined and we should all return to fart jokes and punching down.Sure, there's some stuff in the narrative that still works. Much like the first game, there are some excellent satirical critiques of American culture in here, and some genuinely witty fourth-wall breaks. Pox and Crypto are wonderfully voiced and their banter is sizzling. Sadly, these high points are drowned out by lame jokes about ninjas and hippies, or tired Cold War caricatures. I don't like using this word, but honestly? The story is cringe.Gameplay sensibilities are similarly dated. There are three types of missions - blowing stuff up in the ship, blowing stuff up on foot, and stealth. None of these are particularly fun and there's no real difficulty spike beyond 'throw more enemies at you'. This sort of 3D action platformer was all the rage in 2005, but we've largely moved beyond them - they feel simple and shallow to modern tastes.Having said all that negative stuff, if you played DAH2 back in the day and you know already that you enjoy terrible humour and dated mission design, you'll love this remaster. Whatever else it is, it is a good-faith attempt to recapture exactly what the original version was. The soundtrack and voice acting have been given a great refurbishment, but the upscaled assets are where this game really shines. Great care was taken to make everything look modern and gorgeous while preserving the very specific aesthetics of the original titles.My verdict? Leave this one for the nostalgia chasers.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW AFTER 100%A fun, fairly faithful recreation of the 2006 classic. It maintains all the charm of the original with updated visuals and more fluid feeling gameplay. Everything that was good about the original is also good here, such as the very funny and witty writing, music and the multitude of fun weapons that provide a lot of variety in how exactly you decide to destroy all of the humans. The only weapon that I found lacking was the Disclocator, which unfortunately received a change from the original version to now have a charge up and cause the enemy to bounce instead of flinging them in the air. The final mission is also just as much of a frustrating slog as it was in the original version. Some of the optional objectives can be a real pain in the ass (the Black Ninja trials for me were especially infuriating) but those are as the name says entirely optional if you aren't going for 100%. The fact that Co-Op is split-screen only is maybe this game being faithful to a fault as the lack of Online is definitely an issue for a 2022 game, but Steam Remote-Play can remedy that a bit. Destroy All Humans 2 on the PS2 when it first came on was one of my favorite games of all time, and this Reprobed version is a wonderful recapture of that game with a shiny new coat of paint. If you're familiar with the 2006 version than you know what to expect and this should be a hell of a nostalgia trip. And if you aren't, then this is a fun Alien sci-fi game with hilarious dialogue and an entertaining sandbox to play around with.

_childDocuments_.review: Crypto goes global. Story:Set 10 years after the events of the first game you're now playing as Cryptosporidium-138, a clone of the first games Crypto. Now rocking the role of President of the USA and regaining his "package", life is sweet, however all of that is soon to change. KGB deeming Crypto a threat, destroy his mothership and kill Pox (yet he's still around as a hologram) as they set their sights on him, but all of that is soon to change when you realize the KGB have grander plans than just killing you.The story of the game is basically identical to the original game with a few minor changes that don't really change anything significant and I'm glad to report that it's just as good as it was all those years ago. Just like it's prequel the comedy does not miss a beat and has some genuinely laugh out loud moments and many moments aged like fine wine, which make the story an absolute delight. Graphics: Black Forest stuck to their guns and decided to keep a similar art style to the first game, however this time around models are a lot more refined. One gripe I had with the remake of the first game is the character models for the human side. While I did like them for the most part, I found a lot of them to be pretty weird looking and I can definitely say that this time around the characters translated much better, especially Natalya, yeah I ain't afraid to admit it. The environments too have gotten a major face lift as well. Each country you visit feels visually distinct and has it's own unique architecture and look, something which was a slight issue in the first game. I especially appreciated how well Takoshima translated in this remake, which was my favorite location in the original and was my favorite location in the remake as well. Audio:Now I'll give the developers props for crisping up the original audio to make it sound like it was recorded just for this game. This was of note in the original where sometimes characters had that PS2 audio quality, which is not an issue here, everything sounds crisp and nice. This also goes for the soundtrack which sounds great in action as well and I especially loved how it had licensed tracks just like the original in key moments of the game.The new sound effects for guns and your spaceship are also back and sound pretty much spot on to how they did in the previous one. Not that it's an issue, because I genuinely loved the audio design of the weapons and how meaty they felt. However there is one massive glaring issue with the audio and that is the dialogue volume. In the original game even when you're in the heat of combat you could always fully understand when characters talked. While there were lines that slipped by you at least you always could make out what was being said. Here that's not really the case. Sometimes the characters speak so quietly that you will just hear faint noises in the background. This is mostly noticeable in the Solaris portion of the game. Gameplay:Destroy All Humans 2 Remake is basically a gigantic DLC for their first remake. It's the same basic principle with new additions that the original DAH 2 brought to the table. New weapons, a new mission structure, new upgrade system, etc. So let's go over what worked well, what didn't and the new issues that this remake introduced. Overall the game feels absolutely fun to play and I had an absolute blast. Even coming straight off the original game, I had a blast, like I was experiencing something new. Combat feels fun and tight and the large arsenal of weapons allows for really fun experimenting. New guns like Meteor Strike and Gastro gun being my favorites, causing mayhem with them is a blast. I also love how the more tedious missions are remade to be much less annoying, while still required a bit of skill to get through. I really liked the new mission objectives to add more variety to missions which was an issue in the original where you would be doing the same type of mission over and over, which would add to the tedium. While there are a few new objectives that aren't as fun, it's more positive than negative.Now onto one change that I didn't like. In the original once you've grabbed enough collectibles the mini map would display what you're missing which allowed for a quick mop-up to get that 100%. This was changed with a radar which would beep the closer you got to it. Considering there's more collectibles this time around and the fact that they changed their locations, hunting them down was much bigger pain. I wish there could have been an option to choose for those that wanted the old system or the new one.The biggest issue is the technical issues. There were a few instances of bugs and hiccups with framerate in the first game, but this time it feels like it got amplified. In some of the more heavy action moments frame rate would drop into 40-50 FPS range, which got slightly annoying. But there are issues with bugs like enemies getting stuck in the ground which forces you to restart to last checkpoint, AI pathing not working as intended and there was huge issues with crashing which required a patch rollback, but it worked as I managed to get my 100% completion.Verdict:If you liked the first remake, then 2 is the bigger better version of that. 2 was the better game and it translates well in the remake formula. There are issues, but they are easily overlooked when the game is an absolute blast to play. I think it's prime time Black Forest took us on an original adventure next.Final Rating:9/10Pros:+ Visuals are even better now + Gameplay is as good as it ever was with more toys to mess around with+ Writing aged like fine wine + Audio design is great Cons:- The new collectible hunting system sucks- Dialogue is sometimes way too quiet in the more action packed moments of the game- Tons of technical issues If you liked this review please consider joining  and

_childDocuments_.review: Short version --Edit as of 12/29/2022 This is kinda wack, first time I have really had a lot of fun playing a game in ages. At the same time it was the most broken and buggy play through of a game I have ever had by leaps and bounds. I do not plan to repeat that for any other game ever. Some of the review that follows is older news while accurate I did manage to figure out a way past the bongwater fight (the guys name is bongwater) in the early parts of the story which is a big problem for a lot of people. Many cannot progress through that part. I am adding the tricks to add stability here so hopefully you can progress through the bongwater fight if anyone reads this and still buys the game. Keep in mind these settings will help no matter how powerful the rig is specifically for this fight. After you can change your settings back. -Settings - everything lowest , dx 11 , fullscreen, v sync 60hz cap. From there stay out of the clouds of gas and fumes. Seems that the crashing is due to a particle issue. For me staying on the island you spawned on for first 2 rounds worked then fly up high and stay to the middle of the map using the floating objects to get to the treehouse in the 3rd round and then the top of the tower in the 4th. Stay up high and use those flying objects to stay up high away from the particle effects. Listen to the reviews about performance issues and mission breaking/game breaking bugs and crashes. I did a little looking but I saw enough positive reviews to make me thing the game was generally stable enough I could get somewhat through it. Nope.... I have crashed like 12 times in 94 min of gameplay 1-2 were before the bongwater fight (early mission) do not want to spoil anything though. (story wise so I will just say that much.)Longer Version: I never got to play the original destroy all humans games but I got into them with the remake of the first game and I have been pretty stoked on the series. From what little i have gotten to play of 2 I like some of the changes and the maps are quite large and the graphics are quite good mostly maxed out. I like some of the mechanics changes like the ship acts like part of the upgrade menu instead of back on the spacestation in orbit stuff like that. There was some other changes to abilities and gameplay I also liked but maybe everyone will not like the changes. One change was how the body swap mechanic works for disguising yourself as a human. it is more of a swap now instead of a cloak for the lack of a better way to describe it. I really have been enjoying this remake when it is not crashing.  The bad: while mostly easy to run or easy enough (running it at 3440x1440 nearly completely maxed out. The game still crashes mostly engine process halts for some reason. Been trying to troubleshoot but the 2 hour steam refund window is getting a bit close for me. Some people doing a integrity check of the files helps and for others driver updates have helped and for others changes to game settings also helped but quite a number of us cannot get past the early mission Bongwater fight. That is where out of about a dozen crashes I have had all but 1-2 there. It always crashes a few seconds into the fight and nothing I seem to do can stop it from occurring. Each time i restart and try again after trying a potential fix or workaround it costs me 1-2 min of playtime towards the refund period so I really only have gotten about 70 ish min. of gameplay and that was quite good with 1-2 crashes and nothing so bad I would want to refund it. (weird for me cause I normally will not touch games that are buggy at launch) Like for example I refuse to purchase no mans sky or cyberpunk because of the clusters those have been. I will never pick them up on premise. Reading the reviews I was thinking the issues so far with this remake were far and few in between and only some people were having them. No these are a lot more widespread at the moment. I did a lot of checking around after running into some of them on Reddit and other places and yea... Just rough. They are patching some of these but I do not know when the game will actually be playable. a few people have no issues some have only a few and most of the rest of us either have gameplay breaking bugs that make us go back and redo missions or in my case like many others I can not progress at all cause of this crash on the bongwater fight. The good: Graphics are quite good considering the style and everything else not that hard to run either I like some of the changes to the gameplay and the menu system where the ship handles upgrades and the normal menu allows modifications to your character. The story so far was good too and I liked some of the new characters and enemy types. The ship also has some neat changes but I do not really want to spoil to much so I am kinda worried to say much there. What I will say though is I spent a bit of time looking at the guns (and how many there are) even though many are locked and I do not know what they are yet. From what I did see though the upgrades have a bit more variety between the guns , ship, and upgrading your characters abilities so this might lend to a bit more tweakable for more runs of the story. It is not a huge series of changes but it does seem a bit more interesting and varied. Another pro is I really like some of the new abilities (or rather I personally really like them but you may or may not) I wish they launched the game after like another 6 months of bug/stability testing or they pushed out some form of a beta/more testing. This is the oddest mix up of good polished textures ... fairly well running game while at the same time being stupid buggy and unstable. I have beta tested quite a number of games before and never run across anything nearly this unstable. Usually internal testing/QC gets it past this point.  I would have to say at this point do not pick this game up in the current state... they seem to be putting out somewhat consistent patches if they manage to fix the game then I would say buy on sale. I have however pretty annoyed at the parent company and the publisher for pushing this out in this kind of state. From what I understand the playstation and Xbox ports are not in not much if any better state. one other thing to note though I understand they did not include some original content (only a bit) due to the current climate around lets call it political correctness. I personally kinda wish they made a couple new missions or something to make up for the content taken out but I can not really fault them for trying to make sure they do not get canceled in the current climate.

_childDocuments_.review: First time I ever played this game was back as a kid on ps2. I had this huge nostalgic memory of it being so much fun, and crazy silliness. I honestly wish I kept it that way, because playing it again as a 30 year old in 2024 made me realize just how awful this game has aged and how dull and generic it actually was.The graphics have improved obviously and the game looks good, however it doesn't look as good as the original because for some reason the developers never updated majority of the AI or character animations and they look very off. I don't usually care about graphics but it's weird seeing the disconnect between the graphics and animation quality outside of cutscenes. The actual game play itself is fun for a short burst of gaming. I had forgotten just about everything in the game so playing the story again is kind of cool...but at the same time it's just bad. The story missions are short and have aged horribly. There are a few missions that do work really well and those are the ones I remembered...but like 75% of these missions are just you waiting to finish them.They added in customization now which is a nice addition but it doesn't really make up for the weaknesses of everything else. Small map sizes, tedious and repetitive combat, awful AI that even on the hardest settings just cannot beat you, and a story that is at times funny, and at other times cringe. It's starting to sound like I hate this game but truthfully I don't. It's a nice little casual game to just throw on for 10 minutes and go destroy a city or 2. Maybe it's me and my standard for games has risen. I think that they could have done more to modernize the game by making the maps bigger and redoing the missions so they don't feel like a ps2 Era game or spent more time evolving the world. I wish steam had a "Meh" button because that's the best way I can describe it.Do i recommend it? Not really no. I don't think it will offer anything you dear reader haven't already experienced before, and I don't think that it's going to really feel good spending money on this when there are so many other, better free roam games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans 2.  Rating this properly will require a division between the core content and the remaster.  Destroy All Humans 2 wasn't a title I had the opportunity to play in my youth, so I was excited to have the opportunity with the remaster.  Core experience:The Core experience is definitely a step back from the original title.  Whereas Destroy All Humans 1 focused heavily on the Alien Conspiracy/Big Brother archetypes and world building with a heavy handed emphasis on cultural references and stereotypes to poke fun at.  (This worked quite well, especially for a more mature audience and kept the experience flowing smoothly for much of the run through.)  Destroy All Humans 2 gutted much of the Sci-Fi world building  and focuses heavily (if not exclusively) on the cultural references and stereotypes.  Unfortunately, there's just too much of it.  Filler content is loaded with pointless dialogue that is often painful to get through.  It might be intended for shock value, but I found it tedious and often pointless.  If you're going to be offensive, at least try to be funny?  The story is choppy and the plot, mind-numbing.  I'm read to finish the title and uninstall it never to be played again.  (I'll go back to the first game, I loved it.)To the remaster:  The game's beautiful (CRASH) it is easy to see a lot of effort was (CRASH).... put into (CRASH) rebuilding the multiple places (CRASH) (CRASH) (CRASH).......The game looks great, and I'm sure I'd be having fun if it would stop CRASHING!!!!  Seriously... I'm "not" on a low end rig, I've tweaked the settings, it still crashes and at the weirdest times.  It's such a pain.  Especially with all the pointless dialogue the original experience overloaded the game with that you have to get through to move the plot along.  Can I recommend it?  No.  I wouldn't recommend the original core experience at anything short of a major discount; with the crashes that the remaster brings to the table, I can't recommend it at all.  The first game is where the fun is at.  If you haven't picked it up, definitely go give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun, but a bit too horny, and sometimes dated.This game is good. But it has issues I’ll go into. As a sequel, it works well, the story makes sense minus the one character who honestly feels like an insert at the last second, to become talk. And no doubt existed so kids will buy the game… let’s not pretend they want that.The dialogue can be hilarious, but it is seriously way too horny.The graphics are good. For what is a remake or whatever you call this type of update to a game, it seems pretty good, I never played the original. As is, the graphics and art style are great. I will say some areas can feel underwhelming until you visit Takoshima. Albian is nice too, Bay City is okay, but that’s about it, I found the other areas a bit underwhelming. Gameplay, really good. This feels like an improvement over Destroy All Humans 1 which was just repeated side activities that for some reason locked its progress behind upgrades. In this, upgrades are mission locked which is bad, but the upgrades are good if you know what to invest in. Also get the Alien artifacts to get the super weapon, it’s worth it. It felt accessible enough minus some missions which lack checkpoints and even quality of life. I did like this style of gameplay though as it felt more involved and integrated with the idea of humans and aliens coexisting. With some great twists and turns. The weapons are amazing. Easily some of the best I’ve seen in a game, just really fun to use. Though transmogrifying doesn’t always work which sucks, and it is RNG based. Travel is also really good versus the last game. Much more accessible and faster. This is a 16 hour experience if you go through it normal difficulty and do all missions. But this leads onto the bad side. Whilst the map is appreciated, it seems to be lacking a way to track collectables… it shows how many you have, but that’s not helpful. How am I supposed to locate them? I found it difficult to locate collectables in this game and even required a guide at one point to get the alien artifacts. It just felt lazy to me. Some of the gameplay is a bit dated too. Some objectives aren’t explained very well at times. There seems to be a lack of a way to regenerate health during combat which is, what? It’s such an obvious issue. Another part of it is how there’s no safety locks involved in some of the gameplay. For example, in one mission I had to move eggs carefully without enraging this, monster thing, which auto fails if the bar is filled. It doesn’t have checkpoints, and it’s a long mission. Well, 6 minutes at least. But still tedious, and one mistake, it’s over. Do it all again, including the bonus objective. There are other missions where you need to use psychokinesis, and because of how finnicky it can be to use, you can accidentally kill targets that you need to live. It’s frustrating. There is no psychokensis cancel button, and there needs to be. Yes, I was tapping it. And my targets still died. Skipped dialogue. For some reason you can’t always skip dialogue in this game, but when you can, it skips twice. I press space, and suddenly two pieces of dialogue go past. This is an obvious bug.  Low dialogue audio. In some missions, they are really low compared to the rest of the game. But as well as that, it’s unsubtitled. Yep, missing subtitles. That’s a first.  Performance. This game was weird, because I had zero crashes, but I can see why others were having crashes. This game is not very well optimized for older PC’s. I’m on an RTX 3070 and Ryzen 5800x, and just barely made it through. I had high FPS on max settings, but the FPS sometimes dipped at random for seemingly no reason. A lot of onscreen effects also cause the dips. But even stranger and this is why I suspect other players may have issues with running this, the loading screens cause the game to freeze briefly. A sign that it wasn’t optimized during loading. Like it throws everything at once at the computer hardware, leading to the crashes. This needs an urgent fix. If my PC was struggling with it, I don’t doubt others will. That aside, I can strongly recommend this game. If you liked Destroy All Humans 1, or hated it even, you might like this. If you can look past the horniness and insert character. There’s some good gameplay and dialogue here, and an interesting story.
