_childDocuments_.review: Game was poorly optimized at launch but was playable, but after the first patch, the game is completely broken from me and crashes during the loading screen to continue the game. I decided to go to the forums and see if any fix was available only to find that even if I had been able to load into the game, many more seemingly game breaking bugs were introduced in the patch. While reading through the post I kept seeing the same response from someone representing the game in an official capacity telling people to verify the game files, restart the computer, and check if you meet  the minimum requirements. Not a helpful answer since most responses said that did nothing, but at least it was something. Then I saw this response by "Home" and it made me feel the need to give the game a negative review.Their reply was this"Ok I understand your all annoyed at the performance / crashes, please double check your PC meets the requirements.If it does meet the requirements then please ensure that the game has been verified via steam / your drivers are up to date / have you restarted the PC?If after all of these options the game still refuses to co-operate then please make a bug report via the thread below"The first part seems to try and shift the blame to the consumer while also acknowledge the game has both poor performance as well as crashes. My computer could run the game as smoothly as anyone can get this game to run before the patch, but crashes on loading after the patch. Did the requirements double after this patch? Is a 2070 super no longer a strong enough card, because if so I would change the requirements in the store page. Destroy all Humans 2 is a great game, but this isn't the way to play it. If you have a ps4 I would suggest getting the classic 2006 version and pass on this.Edit: It looks like I can start a new game, but the game runs to poorly for me to replay 10 hours of it. Updates that break save games with no warning or the ability to postpone the update is kind of unacceptable for any game outside of early access. If I had not gotten this game off humble bundle I would be requesting a refund.Edit 2: It seems even though verifying the files claimed all was good, a clean install made my old save playable. I was able to finish the game and enjoyed the ending, other than the final boss. Where I am struggling is if I should change the rating. This is when I wish I could give a sideways thumb. If you can get the game on sale, or possibly when the game is in better condition, I would suggest this remake. Although as someone who bought the game day one, played the buggy day one version only to have the first update break my save. I am going to have to keep this with a not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Original fan here, let me just say its cool this franchise is still "alive" kinda after years of it pretty much being dead. However, there's just one slight problem with this game, and that's the fact the game is basically the original, but neutered of charm, difficulty, story, world, and pretty much everything else EA could get their hands on. It's just a watered down version of the original. I just can't recommend this game if you are a fan of the original, sure the game play is fun, but so what? Everything else about it has pretty much been dissected and modified for pretty much no reason. All I wanted was the original game, but updated. What we got instead was the rotting corpse of the old game puppeteered like it's Weekend at Bernie's. The entire time I played, I just kept saying to myself "this just doesn't feel right" or "the original had done this better imo" and over and over again I just kept telling myself that the original was just better. The worst thing about this game however is not Freelove being a weapon, nor is it the unusual cartoonish style this game replaced with the originals realistic yet comedic vibe. No, the worst thing about this game for me personally, is the world design. All the worlds are basically the original, but smaller and simplified in various aspects. For example remember how big the park entrance ways were in the original? They were so big that the only real way to get up on top of them to get that data core that you really wanted was to upgrade your jetpack. Now however? Yeah they're tiny, and so is everything else, everything feels smaller and dumbed down. Remember how some of the missions in the original were actually pretty difficult? Yeah, most feel like nothing. Remember how hard it was to chase after that guy with the documents? Yeah you can kill him INSTANTLY now. Why? Why, why, why, why? That's all I can ask. Why didn't EA just completely copy the original? Why did they feel they needed to tinker the game to the point where it just doesn't feel remotely the same? In the original, everything felt relatively grounded despite the absurd premise of aliens and the sci-fi. Now? It feels like I've entered a circus, nothing feels even remotely real nor grounded, I just can't get immersed in the game AT ALL. I've been disappointed by remasters before sure, but this is just... why? Why can't we just have the original but updated to newer consoles or pc? Why do I have to go and download a ROM and Emulator just to play a better version of this game? Why, oh god why does this exist? They could've just copied the original completely and frankly it would have been better. Idk I just can't say this game if for me, If you never played the original, you'll probably enjoy it. Otherwise I just can't in good faith recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I loved the series when it first came out. In fact it was kept out of my hands on release until I was 16 years old because strict parenting. Back then games were coming into themselves, going through big changes and expressing new ideas. Nowadays studios are a dime a dozen and as soon as you put out one type of game that sells good, a thousand more will take it places soon after.DHA2 remains true to the original and suffers no drawbacks visually that I can see. It's one big old nostalgic trip to the forbidden fruit of my younger years, that warms my heart to have enjoyed to the capacity that I did. However...DAH2 fails to live up to the standards of modern gamer have set and thus falls away in places. The game feels closed off and restricted, broken down into moments rather than maps. Yes you can explore the game still to the same extent you always could, but between the missions and the cut scenes, it feels like there's a loading screen every 3 minutes. Which instantly takes you out of the moment. It's an easy game, even at it's peak difficulty, so the action is quick to rise and falls off instantly. This for me is the biggest issue. I want to walk around once I finish a mission, not slow mode down and get shown an end screen telling me how I did. I know how I did, and the information you're giving me does not require you to stop the game in it's tracks to show me. The game looks nice but lacks juice, missing the feel that made the series so interesting. The humour remains one of the heights of this game obviously, but it only goes so far to improve the game. And considering the self-offending cancel culture of today, will likely not appeal to new age gamers. It's too slow for them. The second by second action would not appeal to the same extent it did before, which is no fault of the developer and is more of a side tangent on my part.DHA2 is a good game. It has issues and frankly you should only play it if you enjoyed the previous game and want your second hit of Cryptosporidium-138. The constant loading screens whip lashed me out the fun and could have very much been avoided by the devs, but was not. I wouldn't suggest you play it because you're not missing much. However, I would suggest playing it if you played the original series when you were younger.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake of Destroy All Humans 2, even better than Black Forest Games' remake of the first game. Cutscene animations are smoother and more lifelike, the cartoonish art style has been toned down in comparison to the first remake so characters no longer look like hideous exaggerated caricatures, and all locations like Bay City are meticulously detailed.However, there are many technical issues like textures sometimes not loading on NPCs, mission objectives breaking which forces you to reload your last checkpoint or restart the mission entirely, and poor frame rate/stuttering amongst countless other issues. Also a few lines of dialogue and one side mission were unnecessarily cut and the ending of the game was altered slightly, though it remains largely the same as the original game. Furthermore, the UFO's arsenal and some weapons like the Meteor Strike are severely underpowered, taking way too much ammo and time to destroy a single building which made me completely avoid destruction in free roam unlike the first remake.Overall a very fun open world sandbox game just like the original 2006 Destroy All Humans 2 but the countless plethora of bugs desperately need to be fixed, performance needs to be improved, and some weapons need to be buffed.

_childDocuments_.review: A Warts and All Remake of the classic Mascot shooter.As with a Warts and All remake, gameplay problems from the original game are still present. Weapons in this game steer into gimmicky and tragically kind of stay there. The classic Combination of Zap-O-Matic and Disintegrator can deal with basically every enemy in the game and you can Max out their upgrades after about 2 hours of play time.The game also has a fair amount of bugs, a good few missions had to be restarted because an objective had bugged out, a death wasn't counted, or a enemy you needed to kill didn't spawn. it didn't happen constantly, but when they popped up it'd always be obnoxious.Side Quests are very uninspired, usually boiling down to Destroy X in a certain way or Get X and Bring to Y. Thankfully these quests are quite short and give you an excuse to use some of the silly weapons so that's all right I guess. I'd say the main gripe of the side quests is that they're desperately lacking in context. They don't tell a story or lead to anything significant, I wouldn't fault anyone for muting the game and putting on some music instead. You won't miss much.Collectables are kind bare, with the most significant being upgrade material. Something I thought was very bizarre: despite having collectable songs, you can't play them over gameplay. If you want to listen to them you have to stop what you're doing and listen to them from the menu. With the sidequests being what they are, and how long it can take to find the collectables. Having some music fitting of the Psychedelic 60s would have been a blast.Something I found quite odd as well, is the maps get more bare over time. The first map is a large city that's quite densely packed, with the second map follows it up with a very nice Metropolitan area. But from there it gets smaller and smaller and much more Barren.For everything I've said, there's a lot to like to. The humor in the game is pleasantly low brow, The racial sterotypes straight out of it sci-fi B movies are a delightful throwback. The Combat, while easy, is still entertaining even with the Imbalances.The Saucer Combat is quite Solid once you get some upgrades, and the Co-op. Though I'll be the first to admit, I have immense Nostalgia for this game.If you want a Blast from the past that's not too difficult, I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s getting to the point where I think I should just abandon the oldest portion of my backlog and wait for the inevitable remakes. One bonus outside of the positives of improved graphics and usually better interfaces is that I won’t have the seemingly exhaustive burden of comparing it to the original. I can just enjoy the game as it is. That’s what I did with Destroy All Humans, and I was happy to continue with the similar-but-better sequel, Destroy All Humans 2 – Reprobed.Abbreviated Review: I was a bit thrown off when the intro to the game retroactively killed off the original protagonist (Crypto-137) and replaced him with a clone featuring the singular distinct feature of an always-hidden set of male reproductive organs. I suppose that sort of highlights how indifferent Furons are to their cloned nature – which probably reinforces the fact that every aspect of the previous character shifted to the new one. You still get the same Jack Nicholson caricature voice and the same juvenile comedy that regularly shifts between cringy and hilarious while always being extremely dated. Not just for the fact that this game is 16 years old because some references date back to television shows from the late 60s – which I guess is appropriate for the setting, though I don’t know how it relates to the player base 40 years later.Much of the general gameplay experience makes its way over from Destroy All Humans as well. The core set of weapons are the same and you still have the telekinetic power to launch people and objects (and later much large objects like vehicles) into or over anything in your vicinity. However, they are some new weapons that, while useful, really only seem to augment what you have and provide more entertainment value than they enhance your destroying of all humans. Though you do you have one major new psychic ability that allows you to blast out a cone of funky music that convinces people caught in its path to start dancing. I used this primarily to keep my disguised form up since you’re no longer able to (or required to) constantly read minds to maintain your camouflage like the previous game.The biggest change from Destroy All Humans is that you’re no longer relegated to exploring the world only within the context of a mission. Missions are still there, but when you’re not on one, you’re free to explore the entirety of the map without any limitations. Of course, being derivative of a game from 2006, there’s not much map to explore, and what is there is pretty static and non-interactive. You can, of course, blow up buildings, and cars, and whip people into orbit at your leisure, but it really doesn’t change anything and only fires up a minimal-effort version of GTA’s star rating. While this change is certainly a welcome one and provides the avenue necessary to explore the five maps for collectibles, it’s hardly the rich open-world experience we’ve come to expect in modern games.The missions use the set pieces of each map pretty well though, so it doesn’t feel like they were jerry-rigged onto the existing map. It’s all very seamless and you won’t notice you’ve wandered into a place where a cutscene takes place until you’re in it. Part of this is because the amount of detail is extremely high for parts of the map that otherwise have no purpose. It seems a bit odd at times though to have areas with so many physics objects you can throw around and meticulously crafted environments when the only thing you can do outside of missions is pick up pieces of the soundtrack and artwork. There’s a clear visual improvement over the previous remake, which is nice to see, even though the characters still look like their faces were all carved with a butterknife and a socket wrench.Destroy All Humans was a decent game. It didn’t blow me away, but I was compelled to finish it (except for that annoying final boss fight). My expectations weren’t high for this sequel, but I was pleasantly surprised by what was presented. The mission structure feels more cohesive even with the typically disjointed nature of open-world games. It has a story with quite a few surprises and new character introductions, so you’re not just stuck being annoyed by Orthopox or randomly monologuing. While it does unravel a bit toward the end, I was still more invested than I ever was with whatever was happening in the first game.The gameplay held its own for the notably longer game as well. Despite easily being twice as long even without completing the majority of the side quests, I blasted my way through the first four maps having a pretty good time. Yet, toward the end of the campaign, the design of the encounters started to feel clunky and claustrophobic – and that kept going. Enemies become more numerous and quite a bit larger and combat often gets crammed into locations that can’t accommodate them comfortably. This appears to be the method they chose to increase difficulty, which it achieves, but it also increases my annoyance as the screen is filled with flashes, enemy characters, and a camera that doesn’t want to navigate it.Overall, though, Destroy All Humans 2 – Reprobed is a clear improvement over the previous remake, but probably won't change the minds of those who didn’t enjoy that predecessor. You’re still going to get the crude humor, the janky saucer controls, and the straightforward gameplay. The stealth portions are less annoying and better integrated, and the saucer portions are far less important (I only upgraded one saucer weapon), which were two common issues. However, this version had a few notable bugs for me, and I also grew very frustrated with a dialogue skip option that seemed to arbitrarily move forward sometimes erasing whole lines before I could read them. The final verdict is easy to float into ‘recommended’ with this binary system, but it still feels like a game that could be better and could be funny without every joke being a ♥♥♥♥ joke.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely this game is a blast, basically similar to the first DAH except the scale is much higher in terms of map size, weapon sandbox, and RPG elements. Certain parts of the RPG system are dummed down to an extent because leveling your arsenal doesn't require much in comparison to the first but is prioritizes the players focus around side missions. The story was actually an original way to take the character of Crypto, he hates humans but struggles with his emotions after he meets a woman who he falls for after his leader and mothership had been blown up by the KGB. Why are the KGB so hellbent on destroying Furons and who is this woman spy that Crypto falls for? You gotta play to find out and it does a good job with its parody-like fourth wall writing while introducing characters that you meet in-game. The only problem is that I feel there is a distinct lack of cutscenes which are replaced with "dialogue box" sections, I also feel like the ending was half-assed in a way because once you reach the final section of the game the story threads fly by at a mile a minute and the last mission of the game hits you about as fast as it did in Cyberpunk 2077. Because of this, the ending of the game feels a bit like a Halo 2 ending with a cliffhanger to a sequel for what probably should've been more gameplay. The story isn't at the fault of the developers, however, because this is a remake and it is a SPOTLESS one. Because this remake is so great and it adds features that compliment the gameplay so well I would say this is the only way anybody should be playing Destroy All Humans, similar to my opinion about the last game. I can feel that Black Forest Studio listened to criticisms about the previous game revolving around it's "cartoonish" artstyle and changed the way civilians looked in this game. While citizens in the world still look a bit goofy every now and then it is a big change from the first remake. Besides the artstyle still being a bit different from the original the game also preforms terribly in lots of sections, I have a GTX 3090 and with DLSS set to "Balanced" and all settings on "medium" I would drop to 30 frames sometimes! The majority of the game ran at around 80 frames but it is still too low, regardless, it was a small price to pay in order to see the stunning and beautiful re-imagined cities that were created nearly 2 decades ago. I am currently 25 y/o and I played this game when I was 6 y/o, I definitely got nostalgia glasses on but this game REALLY took me back, so much that I can't believe I played this at such a young age just because my parents saw a teen rating, it is incredibly lewed but awesome. Can't wait to show my own children and ruin their childhood someday 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: is a remake of the original Destroy All Humans! 2 from 2006. It mixes in a number of new and old features that keep it fresh enough. Both the classic and the remake are whacky games that are a bit of fun and I personally enjoyed them.+ Whacky gameplay that is as over the top as you would expect. Flying saucers, horny aliens, crazy guns and explosions. If you like mindless fun, these games are great for that.+ Wide range of alien arsenal - from a zap gun to meteor strikes, you have everything you need to cause massive destruction.+ Six maps available where you can cause mayhem. Individual maps are not too big and not too small, perfect sizes for this type of game. There is a lot of variety in them as well, from USA to UK and all the way to the moon (yes, THE moon).+ Dialogue is well written, especially for a game that was originally released in 2006. I believe most of the lines are directly taken from the original so the remake shouldn't differ in this aspect. (Keep in mind that a lot of the jokes and whatnot were relevant in 2006, not so much in 2022 when the remake was released.)- Boss design is really crappy and annoying! It is a constant spam fest with all of your arsenal until the enemy goes down. You can't really dodge in the game so you have to move around while you are being shot by a dozen enemies.- Mission design is also far from great. Most of the time you either escort someone, move objects to a specific location or deal with a target. Apart from missions that involve bosses (a few in total), you will quickly start repeating the same objectives.- The game ran "OK-ish" for me but there were some bugs along the way. I did experience crashes here and there and also texture issues in a few places.It is a pretty fun game and I would recommend it when it goes on sale. The regular price of 40€, however, is a lot and I would not suggest you pick it up for that much. Since it was bundled recently, you can get it for less than 10€ which I would say is a fair price.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! 2 - Reprobed : By Triple F"Destroy All Humans! 2 - Reprobed" is more than just a remake; it's a meticulously crafted homage to the absurd, over-the-top antics of the original, infused with the visual and technical prowess of modern gaming. This reimagining successfully captures the spirit of the 2006 classic while introducing a host of improvements that elevate the experience for both newcomers and longtime fans.The core gameplay loop of Reprobed remains largely intact from its predecessor: open-world mayhem, punctuated by structured missions. Players once again assume the role of Cryptosporidium-137, a foul-mouthed alien invader with a penchant for world domination. The joy of the game lies in its ability to effortlessly transition between stealthy infiltration, frenetic combat, and chaotic destruction.The revamped control scheme and improved aiming significantly enhance the overall experience, making Crypto feel more responsive and agile. The array of alien weaponry, from the classic Zap-O-Matic to the Ion Detonator, remains satisfyingly destructive. However, the game's difficulty curve is somewhat inconsistent, with some encounters feeling overly challenging while others are disappointingly easy.A notable addition is the expanded alien abduction mechanic. While still primarily used for replenishing health and DNA, players can now abduct specific targets for mission objectives or experimentation. This adds a layer of strategy to the gameplay, encouraging careful planning and execution.Reprobed's narrative is a classic blend of campy humor, sci-fi tropes, and pop culture references. The story follows Crypto as he navigates the turbulent 1960s, clashing with the enigmatic KGB agent, Milenkov. While the plot is undeniably silly, it serves as a solid backbone for the game's chaotic gameplay. The voice acting is consistently strong, with the return of original voice actor Grant Albrecht as Crypto being a particular highlight.Reprobed is a visual marvel, with vibrant colors, detailed environments, and impressive character models. The game's art style successfully captures the aesthetic of 1960s pop culture while adding a modern flair. The open worlds are filled with interesting landmarks and hidden secrets, inviting exploration.The audio design is equally impressive. The game's soundtrack is a nostalgic blend of psychedelic rock and spy-themed tunes. Sound effects are crisp and impactful, adding to the overall immersion. The voice acting, as mentioned earlier, is top-notch, with the characters delivering their lines with appropriate energy and enthusiasm.Overall, "Destroy All Humans! 2 - Reprobed" is a successful reimagining of a cult classic. While it doesn't reinvent the wheel, it delivers a polished and entertaining experience that will satisfy both old and new fans of the series. The game's strengths lie in its engaging gameplay, charming humor, and impressive visuals. While some minor issues with difficulty balancing and repetitive mission structure prevent it from reaching true greatness, Reprobed is undoubtedly a must-play for fans of action-adventure games and those seeking a nostalgic escape to the swinging sixties.

_childDocuments_.review: To start with, I have played the original Destroy All Humans 2 as well as the DAH 1 remake that THQ Nordic has made previously. I have not completed the entire story in the remake yet, however after getting about 3/5 the way through I have a good idea of how the game plays.TLDR: I recommend the game, there are bugs but I expect them to be fixed, and if you liked the original you will enjoy the remake as well. Long winded explanations:I fully recommend this game, with all its quirky humor and crass dialog. It has a story with a decent open world and side missions that can challenge without being overly complicated. It is a remake so don't expect too much in terms of mind bending extra features. But the core fun is still there, whether you are in the mood to complete a story, or just go out on a night on the town (blowing it up). I am not even necessarily a fan of the more comic booky feel/look of the game but that's a minor gripe at best. It looks beautiful, it plays well (usually) and they haven't changed much imo that made anything worse. I have seen complaints regarding weapon balance, or more accurately, saucer balance, and there is some truth to these. the weapons however are not underpowered like some may think. As far as I can see, the PK abilities are just so strong the weapons lag behind in comparison, which is an issue I hope they fix.also, and this is a big one, this game can be a buggy mess. They really need to polish some of the mechanics of this game, it almost feels like they should have delayed it about a month for some finishing touches. for example:1: occasionally you will have the sensor for collectibles just stop working. this usually just needs reset by going between maps. 2:occasionally the health bar and/or alert symbol will stay on the screen after you aim at an enemy for too long. this fixes itself after a while but it does need fixed. 3: flashes... omg the flashing. some objectives (side objectives, I haven't seen main ones do this yet) will flash on the map on and off repeatedly. it makes it very difficult at times to track them, properly.4: this is the biggest one I know about thus far and can be game breaking. the navicom may not be working and may result in an immediate unreal engine crash whenever you try to access it. Now I experienced this and was very concerned. Fortunately, my issue was that I had an extremely out of date software for my drivers, and after a rather quick update to said software, I was able to continue. However, I have seen others have this issue and I do not know that they could use the same fix I could.5: missons sometimes will not function properly. this isn't to say youcan't complete them, but occasionally you may have to restart one if you use the voice lines in a "wrong" order or sometimes you may just have to skip any extra dialog so the mission doesn't mess itself up. I have also had missions with several steps just immediately jump to the last step and had no idea why or how. these are some of the bugs I know need fixed, and I'm positive there are more I am either forgetting or just haven't run into yet, I can say there are frame drops in high fidelity areas as well, although that can be my system as I am not on the top end hardware of today lol.these are all things that need fixed, absolutely, but barring the navi-com crashes (which in my experience I have seen so far is an issue with windows 7 users as well as the drivers fix which may be the problem as well) none of these will break your game and most glitches are mild inconveniences rather than large scale issues. It's definitely a game that could have used an extra month of QA, but it is not like they released "the most polished madden ever" Bottom line, is it worth your money? that's a question only you can answer. But is it worth your time? in my humble opinion I believe it is. The company that made it still updates the remake of the first Destroy All Humans so I have no doubt these bugs will be looked at and corrected with time. So far the remakes that THQ Nordic has made have all been handled well and a quality product. I fully recommend this one as well, as even the issues I have seen have not impacted the enjoyment I have had and I believe you will have if you buy this game. Do be warned though, you may want to find some videos of the old one or even someone playing the first few missons of this one to make sure the humor and style is to your liking, as only seeing and hearingi it will give you a true idea of how it is if you haven't played the original.

_childDocuments_.review: As I'm nearing the final few missions of the game I think I've played it enough to leave a review.Black Forest have once again knocked out a graphically beautiful rendition of the Destroy all Humans franchise.To be blunt when I was a child playing these games I barely remember playing the first but I vividly remember the second installment. Which is where my praise will have hiccups at times when regarding the Black Forest version of the second game.The original version of Destroy All Humans 2 had a very specific "feel" to combat. Weapons did high damage and dying wasn't uncommon, more importantly it was supplemented by the variety of factions and enemies in the game.Mind spoiler alert beyond this point ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Of the main factions the original often had in-fighting between A.I. , Kojira fighting the Japanese Defense Forces. I remember kicking back on a building and watching Kojira tear through the streets while laser tanks and infantry fought her for minutes at a time before coming in when she was more wounded to finish her off. Likewise a similar situation in Tunguska with The Blisk happened often, the noxious green gas that's just an ambiguous "poisonous chemical" now used to be the way to convert humans into the mutant creatures but ever since Black Forest changed the way the spores physically appeared as well as changing certain game play features like projectile size, speed and damage, you now can't do what I used to do as a child, lure The Blisk from their base towards the KGB base and let them hash it out with each other, making my time getting through one base or the other all the easier. This is <particularly> problematic on Solaris.There are vital battles which take place between the Solaris troops and The Blisk due to the revamping of the A.I. and the combat in general, the A.I. is aggro'd by you more than each other which is incredibly stupid and makes the game far less appealing for me personally. Why is it that The Blisk, having heard of an insurrection on Solaris, would break through the air lock, see a bunch of Solaris troops roused to fight them, stop fighting them mid gun fight, and both sides focus <you> down?Halo The Master Chief collection did this the correct way, they ported the A.I. entirely as it should have leading to missions like "Keys" being just like when I was a kid, you could lure the Flood down a hallway and let them and the Covenant defenders fight it out and wait until the herd was thinned to move on. This helps with the higher difficulty modes and makes it so tedious and unenjoyable now in Destroy all Humans 2 by Black Forest. Removing that feature is a death blow for my interest in the game.Visually it's stunning, I also am not terribly opposed to different game play like the "boss fight" with Bongwater or Kojira having a glowing weak spot or fighting Oranchov for longer than 3 seconds. All of those changes are great the issue is that the standard A.I. isn't how it <should> be.The new animations, graphics, sound, music, extras they're all lovely but the base story is the same, naturally, but the game play has been ruined with the revamping of the A.I. Oh and as one more small gripe, what happened to the fun little animation of Crypto taking his saucer into orbit over the Earth and flying in the direction of where he wants to go when going from one country to another (or Solaris), that animation was handy for helping with loading back then I'm sure but losing it makes the game feel more flavorless.Overall it's a very solid 5, maybe 6/10 it's average maybe slightly above average. It could've been an easy 7/10 for me had they ported the A.I. properly but as it stands it's just not as I remember and when you're porting a game from one platform to another, many years after the originals were released, you're going for Nostalgia and if it isn't precisely as it was before, then you're going to lose some fan's interest, like myself. I'll finish this game but I won't play it ever again after, like I did the dozens of times with the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Two years later and another remake is out. I had a good time playing through the first one in spite of its flaws, so I was lookng forward to giving the second a look.The first thing I noticed this time around is how much better this game looks compared to its predecessor. I’m not talking the art style - that still maintains the same goofy, retro look - but more so the map density, the level of detail, the models - all of that. The studio has done a great job not only in faithfully recreating the look of the original 2006 game, but improving upon what they did just two years ago in the first remake. The environments were already pretty good in the first game, but in 2 they feel much less barren and WAY more varied.Right at the start you already have access to a bunch of abilities, but that only grows as you progress and while not all of them land, the ones that do are very fun to use and the pacing is managed well enough that there’s always something new to look forward to.The gameplay in general maintains that distinct mid-2000s vibe where the focus is on just having fun and not really worrying about little things like what equipment is the best to upgrade or “is this the best way to tackle this mission”? It’s very freeform and I honestly miss this kind of game design - it’s one of the reasons why I got into gaming in the first place.Just like the first remake, the mission quality varies wildly here. You get the occasional really good mission that introduces a new ability and weaves it into the gameplay in a fun way followed by another three or so boring missions that alternate between simply “go here, destroy this, repeat” missions and the dreaded escort missions. There are so many escort missions that it kinda ends up feeling like the default, even if some alternate between walking and riding the saucer.It really brings down the experience at times, makes it feel monotonous in spite of all the fun equipment and such you have access to. For an experience that is roughly seven or so hours long, it is very disappointing that they had to resort to such repetition to fill that time.In the first game, I found the story to be enjoyable enough. Here though? It’s kinda average. The same cheeky humor is here, but some of the jokes kept getting repeated over and over and it just wasn’t funny anymore. I don’t know, it just felt the first had a better handle on things and was more witty, less reliant on crude humor, making this one feel like an overall downgrade.As a side effect of the visual upgrade, the game is definitely more taxing than the first. That’s fine, I far exceed those requirements anyways. However, that did not stop these absolutely wild fps fluctuations from the steady 90-100 or so down to 40. It was still playable and I definitely could have remedied the issue by lowering settings even further, but an fps fluctuation of 60 is quite a lot and more optimization would be very welcome here.I also ran into a few bugs, including NPCs not moving at all, textures flickering during cutscenes, and micro freezes when opening certain game menus. I didn’t have anything else outside of those issues, but they felt worth mentioning regardless.Destroy All Humans! 2 - Reprobed is a decent remaster of a decent game. Although not quite as refined as the first remake, it does have better environments, more weapons to play around with, and a larger scope. However, it also suffers from the same monotonous mission design as that first game along with having a subpar story and some technical issues too. Really, if you liked the first remake, then you’ll probably like this one and won’t need a review to tell you otherwise.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: A comedic hack-and-slash-like game about being an alien with an assortment of wacky weapons used to cause chaos throughout the world.Destroy All Humans! 2 strongly resembles its predecessor, featuring the same basic gameplay premise, but expanding it at almost every corner. After having conquered the United States, Crypto returns in the 1960s, being tasked with dismantling KGB operations around the globe.Just like in the first game, you’re given an assortment of widely different guns to achieve this, with new additions to your arsenal including a sentry drone and an aimable meteor strike amongst others. Similarly, Crypto’s space ship returns with a couple new tricks, such as the ability to create negative gravity fields in order to lift and later drop objects. All of these additions are very welcome and do a lot to shake up the game by providing new options. Crypto also retains his jetpack and hover skates, along with the abilities to read and control minds, use telekinesis and extract humans’ brains.You’re once again send on a string of missions, following a light narrative and taking you through quite a few distinct regions of the world. These missions are once again rather varied given the available gameplay options, with optional bonus objectives once more giving you a way to increase their difficulty in interesting ways. As for a new addition, there are now also various side missions available throughout your playthrough, which feature more basic but still mostly fun premisses.Throughout these different missions, you’ll earn currency used to improve and diversify your weapons and your ship’s abilities. Crypto’s abilities on the other hand are upgraded by using your ship’s suction beam to collect certain types of humans, making for a nice bit of variety.Destroy All Humans! 2’s levels can once again be accessed outside of missions, containing different types of collectibles used for unlocking music, artwork and upgrade currency, making them overall feel a bit more rewarding than those of the first game. Beyond this, they now serve as hub worlds, with missions being placed throughout them and menus for upgrading your gear, moving between levels etc. only being available at your space ship. Most landing spaces for said space ship also start off inaccessible, needing to be unlocked by completing small tasks nearby.While all of this means that reaching missions and navigating the game in general are more inconvenient, it also serves to make the sandbox levels much more interesting and fun to explore. Aiding this is the fact that the different levels come off as bigger overall, with more detailed environments which feel closer to actual places that might exist.The narrative of Destroy All Humans! 2 is also broader in scope, featuring various recuring characters alongside the classic duo of Crypto and Pox. This however doesn’t mean that the game features some groundbreakingly interesting story – it’s once again mostly fluff serving to give a reason for missions and your journey as a whole. Humour is once again the primary concern of the narrative and works well enough to cause chuckles every now and then. The amount of dialogue is noticeably expanded, with you being able to choose different options for how to continue conversations. This mostly serves as a chance to get some more banter but is at times also used as a part of missions, where you’re required to select beneficial options to continue.Like its predecessor, Destroy All Humans! 2 looks rather nice, with some neat visual upgrades like damaged buildings catching fire and collapsing more cinematically. On the other hand, some effects are a bit overdone, with smoke and fog often blocking your vision way too much and becoming a genuine hinderance to the gameplay. Some cutscene animations in particular are also once again rather rough. Beyond these minor gripes, there’s a pretty glaring issue found with the game’s performance. While the game runs buttery smooth for the vast majority of the time, there are sometimes extreme performance drops at seemingly random points, resulting in massive stuttering even on a beastly PC that usually runs the game at Ultra settings with multiple hundred frames per second. This feels simply awful, and is especially bad when it happens during time-critical tasks, as you’ll essentially be unable to control the game for multiple seconds and end up teleporting around massively with each stutter.Performance induced problems aside, Destroy All Humans! 2 isn’t a very difficult game. Certain mission objectives, especially bonus ones, are definitely challenging, but never feel too overbearing, with the game providing relaxed fun throughout. For some further challenge, you can get the “Challenge Accepted” DLC, which adds various timed bonus missions based on those found in the first game to the hub worlds. These reach from quite easy to rather demanding and can make for a nice change of pace from the rest of the game, although completing them sadly doesn’t provide any useful reward. You can also once more complete various minor tasks in order to unlock cosmetic skins for Crypto as well as his space ship.In conclusion, I found Destroy All Humans! 2 to be just as entertaining as the first game, with basically all of the game’s aspects being sensibly expanded. While the performance issues in particular took away quite a bit from my experience, I’d still recommend getting the game given how much fun I had in lieu of these problems

_childDocuments_.review: DAH2 offers more of the silly, over-the-top alien power fantasy provided by the first game. If you enjoyed the first game, you'll likely enjoy this one. If you didn't, this sequel won't change your mind. It has more  side-missions, weapons, enemies, locales and cosmetic options but the core gameplay and structure remain very much the same. There are some notable differences, though. It seems like missions have a greater emphasis on stealth than in the previous game, which can either be a good or bad thing depending on your preferences. In addition, the writing is decidedly more risque this time around, making it a bit less family friendly but if your kids just want to fly around and blow stuff up, it should be fine, It also offers local co-op, which I haven't yet tried. DAH2 won't win GotY or anything and it's a bit buggier than I'd like but otherwise, it's a solid AA action/stealth game with humorous writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! 2 – Reprobed:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Well, where do I start, humans? First, Cryptosporidium 137 died, but before doing so, he cloned himself to Crypto 138, which now has a purer Furon DNA and has taken over the white house as the . . .  I can’t remember which number was next, but he took over the body of the American President. Amazingly, the KGB discovered it and launched a missile strike on the Furon mothership which was happily on standby in earth’s orbit. The strike was successful and blew the spaceship into pieces. Thankfully, Crypto 138’s boss, Orthopox 13 or Pox for short, managed to save essential Datacores before impact. Well, here you are Crypto 138, and your adventure starts in the lovely American Bay City in Destroy All Humans! 2 – Reprobed.Destroy All Humans! 2 – Reprobed is a third-person adventure /action game developed by Black Forest Games and published by THQ Nordic on the 31st of August 2022 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. This is the remastered version of the original game, which was released on the 17th of October 2006.In this second adventure, Crypto will be visiting Bay City in America (which has been overwhelmed by hippies), London (which is also full of hippies but with a strange accent), and Takoshima Island (home of Ninjas and other gangs), along with a quick dash to the old Soviet Union and a trip to a secret base on the moon. Our favourite Alien that sounds just like Jack Nicholson will take his mission from NPCs in each location. Most of them will be from Pox and the hot Russian Spy Natalya, who Crypto is very fond of. Several other NPCs offer side missions in all locations. The story is very good with plenty of humour. My favourite part is the gameplay; I had so much fun inflicting pain on the pitiful human race. Crypto will start with one weapon in hand, the Zap-O-Matic, and it is just like being struck by lightning. The Ion Detonator is fun, too.  But I couldn’t pass the Anal Probe, it just kept me entertained all way through the game! Seeing hippies, cops, soldiers, and KGB agents running like chickens with their hands firmly stuck on their derrière and saying one-liners such as “all the way to Russia” was hilarious. However, you can only start probing people when you reach England, and being French, that suited me perfectly. In total, Crypto will have nine different weapons. However, I had only unlocked eight by the time I’d finished the game. He also has powers that you’ll be using all the time. Crypto has the power to ask people to follow him, and he can also body snatch, which is taking over a human for a certain time. For the body snatch to be successful, it has to be done without being seen by other humans. If he is spotted, people will start running toward a phone box to call the police or call for reinforcements. If you are quick enough, you can use the forget power on those people and voila! You need to be careful to make sure you do not raise the alarm meter to the colour red. Otherwise, you’ll have the cops, agents and military personnel, including tanks, on your tail until the meters cool down. The only way for Crypto to do that is to fly away using his jetpack and hide for a while. In some missions, you’ll have to use the cortex power on people to find the location of a specific individual that you must eliminate. These types of missions will usually get you across the city, which is good because there are plenty of collectables to find in this game. I must mention that I hadn’t died too many times playing this game, as you can just fly away and get your health back up by waiting on roofs for a while. Yes, Crypto can hoverskate to get away too, but the best way is to use the airways to avoid dying. Bosses fights are where I died a few times, but it was later into the game when I started fighting the other Alien race, the Blisks. It took me a while to pass them, but apart from that, it was smooth sailing. Some of the missions will involve using your flying saucer, but there are not too many of them, which disappointed me. The other thing you need to know is that you will not be able to use the Gene Blender immediately as you need to reach England (Albion) before you can use it, and it is the only way to upgrade your Psi powers. In terms of upgrading both Crypto and his flying saucer’s weapons, it is all based on Furon cells. Each time you finish a mission, you’ll be awarded Furon cells. Most of the time, you’ll receive green cells, but in some missions, you’ll also receive blue ones. Each weapon has two categories: Strength and Quantity. With the green cells, you can upgrade each category twice per weapon. Remember that the cost of green cells will increase each time you upgrade a weapon. But to fully upgrade each category per weapon, you must pay with one blue cell. If you successfully complete the main and all the side tasks per mission, you will also unlock skins for Crypto and for his flying saucer. You can refer to the fabulous gamepedia at any time during the game to see what skins you now have, or what you’re missing, to unlock the other ones. As I mentioned above, there are plenty of collectables to find in each of the locations. One of them is Furon green cell canisters which are helpful for upgrading your weapons. The others are posters, vinyl discs and artworks. You can also unlock all the saucer landing zones by finding the all-mighty Arkvoodle relics.Fabulous graphics and soundtrack. The voice-overs are good, and I believe from the original cast. It’s full of humour, you’ll have a lot of giggles and smiles. I had a few unfortunate crashes to the desktop, which annoyed me and affected my final score. However, it is a great remake and a must-have.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics and soundtrack+	A fun story with plenty of humour+	Good arsenal, some with hilarious consequences+	20+ hours of gameplay+	Plenty of collectables to find and skins to unlock+	Achievements  Negatives:~~~~~~~~ -	I experienced a few crashes to the desktop.-	No trading cards as yetWhat a great remake! It’s a pleasure to play as Crypto again; a must-have! 7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: i waited a long time to get this game because i read so many reviews about the performance. i thought that surely, 2 years later it would be fixed. sadly, no. most of my hour playtime was me trying to figure out how to get the game to stop stuttering every 4 seconds (no exaggeration, you could count to 4 and it would stutter every time, even when i didn't move).i tried changing settings on and off, lowering graphics, shadows, downloading a mod, setting the affinity of my cores, etc. nothing worked. the only thing i found to fix it was to run the game in windowed and manually drag the window to be as close to fullscreen as i can get. with this, the game runs like butter and actually looks fantastic, but it is a shame that i cannot run it fullscreen at my native resolution (1440p). seeing as how the game has basically been abandoned and hasn't received an update in over a year and a half, i feel doubtful these performance issues will ever be improved.here's the thing though: will this fix work for you? maybe, or maybe not. a lot of other peoples fixes didn't work for me. you may have to do a lot of troubleshooting yourself. it is sad, because despite the performance, the game seems to be a great remake so far, but i cannot recommend it unless you are willing to spend some time troubleshooting to figure out how to get the game into an actually playable state.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! 2 is a competent 3rd person shooter building on the strengths of DAH!1, fixing some of its flaws and adding a fair bit of content and variety in its environments (by invading other countries).Like its predecessor, it's all about outlandish setups and jokes rather than rewarding or challenging gameplay, with its mechanics clearly showing their age in the post-Gears of War era of shooters. A clear result of that are a couple of difficulty spikes in some boss fights that can be smoothed out by cheesing the game rather than "being good" : something DAH!1 wasn't suffering from.The writing too can be dated for the 2020s, with all the "I don't understand Humans" jokes replaced by sexist dad jokes, racist accents and dated references. In that, DAH!2 is closer to Saints Row than DAH!1.I still recommend it because it's a decent and enjoyable game ... But I was on the edge for this one. I missed the clear mars Attacks! vibes from the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying Destroy All Humans 2 was my favourite game as a kid, I've finished it multiple times and even once a few years ago in 2020.Reprobed is a faithful recreation of the story and that is all. The sounds are the same but that's because they literally reused a lot of the same sounds and music. The graphics, gameplay and UI all feel totally different. That is possibly a good thing for a lot of people but I went into this hoping for a remaster of the original game with maybe some added goodies, not Destroy All Humans 3 with the story of Destroy All Humans 2.The more I play the more I realise this just isn't the game I was hoping for.The level of polish just isn't there as it was in the first game. Even simple things like the dialogue NPCs give you when scanning their brain are just not there, they all have 1 thing to say whereas before you could scan them multiple times and get different dialogue each time.This game is absurdly easy too, even on the hardest difficulties. You can just pick everyone up and yeet them into the distance, you could do that before but it was far more deliberate and you could only throw people about 20-30 meters, now you throw them literally 1000 meters off into the distance in about a third of the time.The UI is 'nice' looking but very confusing to understand, so many glowing and flashing bars all over your screen. Took me ages to realise which one of them was my health bar.One thing I do like is the PK skateboard you use to get around, the issue is the maps are so small that it really makes you feel like the city is tiny whereas in the original you had to walk everywhere or use your ship which really made you feel like the world/s were huge.The guns have all changed and for me at least don't feel satisfying to use, you just press a button and crazy sparkles come out and stuff dies whereas before every bullet felt deliberate and impactful. Even the way the NPCs die feels a lot less realistic. Before they would ragdoll and lay limp on the floor, now they feel like weightless balloons.The cutscenes are really well done aside from the music that often players loudly over the characters talking to each other making it hard to hear or get immersed in the scene. I tried turning the music down in settings but apparently it doesn't affect music in cutscenes.I could sit here all day and try to quantify why this game doesn't feel right but I don't know if I'd ever find the words. The magic just is not here. The people saying this is nothing but a copy of the original are off their rockers, this is nothing like the original aside from the story.Oh and if you do get this game, make sure you turn off 'Nvidia Reflex Low Latency' or you will have very awful and inconsistent fps, and for some reason it is on by default.

_childDocuments_.review: DAH! 2 - Reprobed is visually amazing, and a remake of an amazing game that I definitely recommend. I played the whole thing in local co-op with a friend... I wish they had added online co-op as a quality of life addition, but it ran alright for us in Parsec.We started playing right after launch, and over the following months there were a number of bugs and random game crashes, some of which have been fixed, and some of which I don't think have as of writing this. One big in-game bug that I think hasn't been fixed is that the in-game collectible radar doesn't work after you start a quest, until you either go to another in-game area (e.g. from Bay City to Albion) or go back to the main menu and re-launch your save. Another bug has caused me to not be able to unlock the "Golden Boy" skin after completing all the challenges, I read that the bug had been fixed but saves that had it still cannot unlock the skin (so I'd have to launch a new game and do everything all over again). The bugs and decent amount of crashes didn't take away from our fun that much, except after the second update where every time I launched the game it would crash shortly after, but that was luckily fixed after a bit. I've played 53 hours and I 100%'d the game. The original DAH2 was one of my favorite games when I was younger, I've missed it a lot and was glad I got to play it again in this form. It's been a long time since I played the original so I'm not positive, but I feel like some of the controls and stuff old players remember may have been changed... like I don't remember PK being as powerful as it is now... and I remember being able to comically pick up or dislocate cars and have the occupants dive out, which was seemingly lacking.

These bugs manifested themselves in missions that had to be restarted due enemies not respawning or getting trapped in the floor of levels. When moving from Bay City to the next area my game crashed. The game also has a major issue of locking up and crashing when you restart a mission whether you failed it or just happen to hit replay. Also experienced many times where the game would lock up or bug out when replaying or just exiting a challenge.There are also other non crashing bugs including vehicles driving through buildings like they are not there, characters walking through solid objects like bins and trees. _childDocuments_.review: Consider this review "mixed" - had more fun than not so leaving it as positive, but would only recommend this on sale, not at full price.The game is fairly fun, and gameplay wise it's a massive improvement over Destroy all Humans (2020) (playing on the hardest difficulty, it is actaully possible to die in this game, unlike the aforementioned game), but when it comes to story, humor and general "feel" of the game (not gameplay), I feel this falls a bit short of the previous game, especially in the later levels.The main story also feels a bit "short". Yes, at the moment of this review update I have 22 hours in the game, but that is 100% completion (with exception of the "challenges" DLC), which I was very inefficient with in the first couple of levels, + some AFK time. I don't know how long it takes to play through this if you're just doing story mission, but as stated, the main story felt a bit "short".This game is also horribly unoptimized and struggles with frequent stutters and poor FPS, even on powerful hardware. The game also suffers from some strange design choices, like the "dialogue system", which seems for the most part to do nothing. There are certain missions where you have to choose the right options or fail the mission, but for the most part, it just makes every conversation drag on and require uneccesary inputs. Also if you want to upgrade all your weapons or go for 100% completion, it's a "collectathon" where you have to run around every map collecting x amount of stuff, which becomes (in my opinion) tedious, boring and repetative very fast.Overall, decent action game that struggles with terrible optimization.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun as ♥♥♥♥, you get to run around as an alien and blow stuff up, which is basically the core gameplay loop. The voice acting is fun and fitting to the tone of the game, the characters are for the most part likable and fun, and the core mechanics of the game are fun enough to play around with outside of the main story as well as within. Some of the humor isn't the best or is a little to reference-y and didn't quite click, but the majority of it is solid and even managed to get a chuckle out of me. It's obviously reminiscent of the PS2, so if older forms of game design are a deal breaker for you then probably don't buy it, but I loved it. There are some bugs at the time of my writing this, but those will probably be patched out eventually. It doesn't make the game unplayable like some people are saying, its more just a few odd things here and there where you go "oh that probably isn't meant to happen" or maybe a target goes under the map and you have to load the last checkpoint but its a minor inconvenience at worst.My only major issue is, without spoilers (though the game is a remaster of one that's been out for almost 2 decades), is that the ending is very anticlimactic and the final boss is laughably easy. Mind you, I was playing on what I think is normal difficulty (veteran), so I wasn't expecting anything insane, but it was still a cakewalk. This surprised me because there had been previous bosses that both took longer, and were far more challenging. In addition the sound design began to fall off around that time too. At certain moments in cutscenes it was just dead silent when it feels like something should have been there. I don't know if that's a bug or not but I have a hard time believing it was intentional.Everything up to that point though was fantastic. I would definitely play a 3rd installment of this series, provided they are able to capture the same tone. I wish Armquist was still around though.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Gotta be honest - this game kinda blows. Seems like a cash grab. The game play is weak (but there is a lot of it) and is surprisingly easy for the most part. The bosses are OP and what kills you is usually a bug in the game mechanics. It's a grind. Here's the recipe: find the yellow marker on the map, have dialogue, accept mission, kill people/blow things up, find next yellow dot, have dialogue, and so on until you "complete" the mission, after which you find the yellow dot, have dialogue, accept mission... Speaking of the map, the map sizes are sorta tiny in each city. Felt like there could have been more. The graphics are potato. I don't even have a graphics card and I played this at 1080 high settings. Don't know where their recommendations were coming from. I didn't have an FPS counter going, but it felt like 50's most of the time. Honestly it looks a lot like the first game from 2005. The cut scenes are a joke in that their timing, and sometimes framing, are way off. They take wayyyyyyy too long to get through, and the only options you have for dialogue are snarky, childish lines that really did not hit. The dialogue is a little... incel-inspired I guess is how I'd describe it. It tries way too hard to be cool, there's a lot of forced sexual tension, and there was only one joke in the game that made me laugh. The misogyny was thick with this one. Oh and, good lord, the voice acting paired with the writing was actually cringey. Y'all... I know it's tough to get real Russian input on common phrases and pronunciation at the moment, but even a little research would have helped. Also relying on stereotypes wasn't a comedic tool, it was just hard to get through after a while.The story is presented in the beginning in a way that made me feel I was woken up in the middle of the night and asked to recall details about something long ago. It was headache inducing, confusing, and made me want to go back to bed. After that, it relies mostly on cliches from spy films. I actually feel really bad about writing this, because I loved the first game when I was a kid and was hoping this would be not just a nostalgia engine (after all, they had enough time to make it good...). This feels like a pet project one or two dedicated, but overworked, people put together over the course of a year or two. Had that been the case, I'd have said "well done" and left it at that. I don't get the feeling that was the case here. Look, at $60 I would have asked for a refund, but seeing as its release price was $40, I'm just going to think it was a poor decision. At $20, I'd say it's probably worth a try if the downsides I've listed aren't too off-putting.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! 2 - Reprobed by Black Forest Games is a literal Destroy All Humans simulator where you...Destroy All  Look I don't know I'm not funny, but I'll tell you what this game is actually funny. The original game to me is one of my favorite games of all time and when I saw the release trailer for the original Destroy All Humans remake I was excited for it...mostly because I was hoping they would make a remake of this game. And of course they did so I had to get it, which shoutout to my buddy Casey for getting it for me, you f u c k ing chud! Gonna go to the positives before I state my main problem with this remake.The gameplay is fantastic, to me I love it but it's also reminiscent of a PS2 game because the remake almost faithfully recaptures basically every little piece of the originals. Basically if you played the remake of the first one you'll get more of the same except new stuff like added guns, a couple of new abilities, etc. It is basically an alien murder game and you go around completing main mission/side missions, destroying buildings, reading peoples minds for funny quips, leaving prank calls for the local police department, etc. You can go on foot and glide everywhere with either the jet pack or the hover board (which I'll discuss in a bit) as well as go into your UFO and destroy whole buildings from there. There's a lot to really unpack and I don't think I can do this game justice, but what I can say for the most part is that the game play aspect like everything else does what the original does but feels more smooth and controls a lot better in my honest opinion. And a lot of that is what struck me about this game compared to the original; it just feels more accessible compared to the original on PS2/Xbox. There were no hover boards in the original but now you can move faster, Psychokinesis now throws people all the way into the stratosphere, like the game feels great. I can't give enough props to this game for being what I believe a remake SHOULD be.The plot basically sticks verbatim to the original PS2 version as well. You play as Crypto once again as the KGB blow up your mother ship for an unknown reason, and you have to figure out why they did it and whose controlling the strings so you can kill them. In between you run into alien fertility god cults, ninjas, parodies of James Bond, a seductive Russian spy, and all sorts of parodies and pastiches from old sixties culture. The beginning of the game says that this game is a product of it's time, and the truth is while it is with a lot of humor that might be considered tasteless now, I still think that this game is a hilarious satire that dunks on the stupidity of everyone while throwing out references left and right, fourth wall breaks, etc.; it might be just rose tinted glasses but truth be told I thought the original as well as this game was hilarious with everything it had going for it though I'd understand if other people really didn't dig it. To me it's still a great story, not mind blowing but it's a lot of fun to be had and you'll be traveling around the world  compared to strictly just the United States in the first games. Some of my favorite side missions include setting up a satellite to "phone home", dealing with a parody of Mothra and getting rid of the eggs, hunting down a "Yeti", and the Arkvoodle Cult stuff.The graphics/sound design/art design; it's made in the Unreal Engine 5 so it looks good graphically; I guess my only gripe is that in a way I kind of miss the old style that didn't make everyone look totally like a caricature but with the way this game handles it's satire honestly it fits so I can't really complain and they did the same with the first one. Also as far as I know the sound design is basically the same with the original PS2 game (though maybe with some stuff changed that I barely noticed) so if you like how the original sounded it'll mostly be the same.The only bad thing I can personally say about this game: dear god this remake has glitches. For the most part they're just hilarious: one glitch I was replaying a level and I used the little Gojira pet you can choose before my game crashed. I came back on to the actual free roam and the little monster was still following me around shooting people; then eventually I don't remember if they died or not but when they did they clipped through a building and expanded in size to what the normal model in Takoshima looked like. Another example is you can body snatch a human and go to a nearby payphone to prank call or get rid of/bring police to your location; somehow I found one in Tunguska (The cold Soviet Union area) that had the voice lines of those from the first area in Bay City, and that was only one. Cars will randomly flip around for no reason, and sometimes missions will glitch out like the Mothra parody mission where you'll try to drop eggs in the volcano and the base will be open before suddenly closing or they'll say I pissed off Moghra when the meter was barely full. Frame rates will randomly drop sometimes and textures can take a while to load as well. It was a strange combination that honestly definitely needs to be patched to some degree. Otherwise that's the only bad thing I can truly think of.If I were to say anything it would be this, I'm thankful that Black Forest Games has been remaking these games. I love the original two but truth be told if you go back and play them now while they're good some might find them a bit too old for their tastes, and these games (and the future of the franchise) honestly deserves more. And in a weird age of remakes where I personally feel certain games deserve it (this series, Demon's Souls, etc.) and certain games don't (The Last of Us mainly, though Dead Space while apparently great follows up) this game to me is what I felt a great remake should be. My hope is that while I wish the original games would be ported to PC (I will die on the port every game hill), that now that Black Forest has remade the first two they'll go through and remake the so-so Big Willy Unleashed and the franchise killer: Path of the Furon, and make them better. That being said, please patch the performance issues and glitches. I personally feel it's worth the money and sunk a lot of time into it but what you value the game at is really up to you. Again thank you very much to my dude Casey for getting this game for me for Christmas, but f u c k off you can't get my sister's number lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Just don't buy right now, this is a messy PC port. It's a damn shame because I honestly loved the first remake, hell I even loved the original games - 2 was my favorite! But they botched a number of things here that make me regret paying full price. First thing is I'm pretty sad to say that I actually don't like the second game as much as the first now in retrospect. DSH!1 just has a better atmosphere, story and character dynamic for Crypto and Pox. DSH!2's plot is just all over the place, has weak side characters, and didn't really grab my interest until way late into the story. Making Crypto simp over a love interest the whole game really irked me, it kinda derails his character and just seems unnecessary. More importantly though, this game has a litany of technical problems. Game crashing every hour or so. Very annoying but at least it saves mission checkpoints. Texture streaming issues on character models and backgrounds every time the camera moves. Frame stutters and dropped FPS whenever loading into the level. And an ugly fog that permeates almost the entire game and makes appreciating the newly designed areas hard when things are so blurry. Bay City and Albion especially are kinda ruined by this fog.This port also badly needs an option to switch off motion blur because I honestly couldn't play with it on. I ended up going into the engine.ini to turn it off, although doing this creates a barely noticeable trail effect on character outlines. It also needs an option to adjust Bloom because **** me it's horrible, worse than the first remake's. More settings options should be available for a PC title in general, they did the bare minimum here. I really recommend just playing the first remake, this second game just seems so lackluster in comparison. Sad to say but I don't believe I'll be interested anymore in DSH! after this, as the quality of the series dropped after the first two anyway. I wonder if they'll even continue seeing as this port is a disaster...

_childDocuments_.review: So let me start off that the original DaH 2 was one of my all time favorites. And I honestly had a blast playing through this. Really hit those nostalgia buttons and I even liked some of the things added to this version (seriously SKATE is a god send). So why the negative review? Well the first thing will be the bugs. This game is buggy to high hell. Not as bad as Path of the Furon but it would be hard to top that. But there are times when keys seem to randomly unbind themselves or will do one thing when you want to do something else. This one seemed to happen a lot in Avalon for me while I was trying to land the saucer. Landing and extracting brains are bound to the same key so I would try to land, only to pop some guys head off a block away. Takoshima seems be the most unstable map with random frame drops and NPCs just breaking. The final boss and the odd job after it dont give out their stated reward. There is a mission in the last area that is supposed to pit two factions against each other but nothing happens (and yes, it did happen in the original.) And I was lucky, there are others that have found game breaking bugs that forced them to lose their saves. Then there is the content cut from the game. Admittedly its minor for the most part: cut cortex lines from some targets, an odd job, the reactor exploding in Tunguska but it kinda undermines the whole idea behind these remasters. And finally there are the nerfs. The lack of PK ragdolls, the Dislocator, the underwhelming nature of anything from the saucer. The maps feel smaller despite them adding at least one extra military base to each one. Hell, the NPCs dont even react to bodies anymore. Coop isnt great. There is no online coop so you either have to use Remote play together or something like Parsec. But even then, the way coop works is both better and worse. The lease that kept both players together is gone but they removed the turret from the saucer. Now both players control half the saucer, one flys and shoots while the other has the cloak and drain and is just clunky. The split screen they went with just awful with a third of the top half dedicated to the current objective (or just a black box if there isnt one) while a third of the bottom half is for the map.If you liked the original, set a timer to see if you will like this one too. Otherwise, wait for some serious updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! 2: Reprobed is the follow-up to the remastered Destroy All Humans! I know that's probably a weird sentence since this is a remaster of a sequel to a game released in 2005, but in this context, I think it works. Just like my review for the remaster of the first game, Black Forest Games has again done a real bang up job and translating the original '06 release of Destroy All Humans! 2 to a more modern engine as well as a modern audience, pretty much all the dialogue from the original has been carried over with updated visuals, slightly updated combat that is basic but enjoyable, updated character models that are just as cartoony as the previous game, and most importantly the overhauled destruction makes a triumphant return. I will say I did run into some small bugs this time around with minor soft-locking, but it's nothing too substantial that can't be easily patched out, I also did crash from time to time so take that into consideration. All in all it's a damn good remaster and I highly recommend it.
