_childDocuments_.review: Millennia is a game with loads of potential!Yes the game is not perfect, there are a few issues i have come along so far, such as balancing, graphics etc... However i am still really enjoying this game! This is a game that should not be played like or even compared to CIV. I love CIV, it is my all time favourite game series to play, i have over 1000 hours of CIV 6 on PS5. But Millennia is a huge breath of fresh air. I tried human kind on PS5 and felt let down with in 2 hours. I am really impressed with the features such as the production lines, vassal states, different ages and the way the domains have been integrated into the game. I am extremely excited to see where the devs take this game. All of the people who bought this game and gave negative reviews mention either no multiplayer or lacklustre graphics. I will admit, the graphics are the biggest let down of this game. How ever they aren't horrible. the only extremely poor graphics are on the combat scenes. But lets be honest we are all going to skip it anyway. Just like how everyone was using accelerated combat and movement on CIV 6Is this game a CIV killer? my answer is NO, it is a completely different game and also plays completely different. If you're looking at the mixed reviews as i was and wondering if you should buy this game, i will say only buy it if you go in with the mindset that it is a 4x strategy game not to be associated with any other in the genre.Well done to the devs of Millennia, I'm excited to see where you take the game in the future with the DLCs

Also please improve the performance in HUGE maps seems its really laggy.PLEASE ADD RESTART like on Civilization 6 instead of repicking again on main menu, Please improve the selection as its time consuming on selecting everytime the initial plots are not ideal.For positive impact, This game has a great age system and will make you excited going forward as you have many options. _childDocuments_.review: A very interesting take on the Civ 4X genre. I'm having fun with it. It plays very differently than Civ and even other more "regular" 4X games. _childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying the game so far! It definitely has some rough edges, but takes a direction I've wanted from 4X-Games for a long time, and actually makes me feel like I play a new civilization that is formed by my decisions and the events in the world instead of being pre-determined.They still could go that direction more consequently (why are there still names of modern nations in the stone age, or BC/AD for counting the years?), and the mechanic of how the next age is chosen could be more elaborated than just "first player who rushes research decides", but I can deal with those details when the game gives me lots of interesting decisions to form my nation.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good faith recommend this game. The bones are there, and there are a lot of things I like! The variant ages, the push pull between advancing ages and getting techs you need. The base of an amazing game is there! It's just.. Well I'll be honest, it's the AI. If you are playing Chess, the AI is playing Checkers. Want a variant age? Better rush the requirement, because you have -3 turns to get to it. Ahead on technology? No you're not, the AI will get to the next age in half the time, your 101 knowledge per turn meaning nothing. I watched the third age in another try get sniped by a nation with less population and vassals, while I popped Eureka's and got my knowledge upto 9 per turn.Want to build some defence but not go to war? Too bad, atleast 1 AI will go full aggro vs you and throw an ungodly amount of units at you. Using production that you need for other things being used up for defence... while this attack heavy AI beats you in knowledge output,even after they've thrown 400 strength of units at you (which are probably about 20 turns worth of production) somehow. I get the AI needs some help so it doesn't get outpaced. But outpacing a human player by a significant margin even when you're doing your best to min-max isn't fun. It's infuriating.

_childDocuments_.review: Nations are too generic, giving a singular boost. Since you can just swap it out though nations in fact do nothing but change the look of your cities. Barbarians are very harsh, and will be constantly a pain if you do not go for a military focused start. AI will hate you, and there's not much you can do about it without specifically going for being diplomatic, that also means you cannot trade with them either as they'll just take your traders. I tried going war focused start, seemed good, but because you need government xp to actually make them into cities they barely did anything. Also lowers your culture by holding too much so could no longer expand those cities very far considering I was unable to create any towns for them. There's some interesting things going on like chains of production where you make one good into another, but otherwise the game is quite empty. It just feels rather bland. Music is eh, visuals are... Well, not great, but it's a strategy game and it works out except quite a few things being rather small. For this price? Don't bother, wait for them to release at least some DLCs, as of course they always will. Quite the expensive game considering, but as usual I go and buy Paradox games pre launch so I can get the version with the first DLCs. Even that seems rather bad since we only get two with it. Oh, also, multiplayer does not have consecutive turns and you need to host it yourself and open ports. Rather unplayable as it would be unbearable slow, and it severly restricts the amount of people who even bother to try it.If you want to try another Civilisation type game, I guess it's something, but I'd rather play Civ 4, 5 or 6 than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously spoilers below. Review current as March 27, 2024Here are the things/bugs/etc that I have found to be wrong/right with the game.Cons-Unfinished game. -Terrible multiplayer at the moment assuming you can connect at all-Unable to map keys-Unable to build previous versions of improvements which is annoying because the lower level improvements require less resources to operate and maintain the chain of production. -Poor starting areas - i.e. Playing as continents with 3 people total and all three people spawn on same continent. -Claim territory function claims territory for the wrong region 100% of the time (some pop-up could fix it). -No way to invade from sea to land if all the tiles are taken by enemy.-No auto explore for any units (Sad for Scouts and Explorers)-Help (F1) only shows the stuff that you have unlocked. That seems fine, except that I have no idea what I need to do to unlock the next special age because the 3 word description on it is not enough. -AI is unnecessarily hostile despite having weaker military (barely stronger (790 vs 760)  on paper but poor tactics and single unit movements instead of the army results in quick loss of towns and armies) . Will attack you regardless, which then forces  you into battle against unrest (and if you're unlucky to not have any coin barbarian warlords invasion)-Which brings me to the cost of early game crisis is too much (you have to basically forego the innovation to get the money in order to be able to prepare for crisis. - No chain of production for tuna or any fish food really-limit on the amount of regions you can create which is really bad considering that the regions captured from enemies cannot be destroyed so really limits the expansion on large maps.-Steel requirement is Age before you are actually able to make steel. Mixed-Combat play has cartoon-y(mediocre) animations that's not expected from a game in 2024. -There is no way to destroy or change regional capital so you end up with AI spamming mini cities that you cant destroy and end with logistical nightmare in terms of resource management since the cities cant expand territory. ( though you could just leave them as vassals and never worry about it.-Town specialization list can be refreshed by clicking on the town drop down list. (not intuitive)-While domestic supply chain can be expanded to multiple slots, unfortunately you can still only pick one destination. Pro-Really cool town and improvement feature -Great supply chains. Can have a region focus on logging, export it to another region where -Multiple utilizations for outpost (military vs economic)

_childDocuments_.review: You can't choose your starting location, and you can't win if you can't maintain armies big enough to scare off the AI. (Diplomatic relations and AI personality do nothing; a pacifist at relation +100 will jump you as readily as the Zulus or the Aztecs if your army's weak compared to theirs.) So if you don't have at least two cash-generating resources within two hexes of your starting location, you can't win and need to restart.The idea of a production chain in a Civ game is interesting, and there are lots of other interesting ideas here too (including independently-developing resources that can even be used to train soldiers, freeing up your city production for other things), but it's an extreme roll of the dice whether or not you'll get them. I won the game once, because I had cash-producing resources nearby, and lost I don't know how many times, because I didn't and I didn't realize that this was the source of my distress.I'll probably check on this game again in a few years, but I don't recommend buying it now.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game better than Civilisation? No...Does it make sense to compare the two?No.Here's why: Millenia and Civ share the similarity that they are both a 4X game with a historical approach, but they feel nowhere near the same. Millenia is focused a lot more on history and shaping your nation as well as production chains. In Civ it's all about getting the best yields more numbers = more science, culture, productoin etc. In Millenia you get a bunch of different points that you use to shape your nation. These unique decisions shapes your nation throughout the game.The combat is built around army compositions (graphics are horrible but you get used to seeing the little guys fight.)Instead of adjacency bonuses like in Civ you want to build up your production chain as you progress through the ages1 Pop working a farm tile produces  wheat  -> 1 pop working a mill tile produces flour using that wheat -> 1 pop working a bakery tile produces bread using that flour. You get the idea.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I have seen the reviews thus far.  However I think that this is a very good game that will provide lots of replay entertainment.  Sure, it is not Civilization, but in many ways, it goes deeper and it has enough changes to ensure that Millennia is its own unique game.  That said, I hope the developers make some tweaks like including a search bar in the infopedia, allows a better road/transportation management network, and allows time to pass slower.  There are other little things I would've done differently, however this game is solid as is and I recommend it to people who enjoy the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Millennia is a game with wasted potential, with a  design and interesting ideas overshadowed by various elements of the game.It's unfortunate that the developers couldn't push such an important thing as multiplayer to the release, which shows what a red flag this game is.After playing through one campaign  and experiencing most of the basic and some more advanced mechanics, I conclude that I played a product in its early production phase.This product demonstrated how mechanics that could be described simply and understandably become incomprehensible and disproportionate to the time invested., called the  gives me the impression that the developers they wanted to ♥♥♥♥ on me.The game may be worth the money in a few years, but currently, apart from the ideas and the only well-executed mechanic, it feels unfinished.I do not recommend it at the moment.Reviewer's Note:"Millennia's gameplay is compelling enough to keep me coming back." - "An exciting, complex Civ-like game that blends familiarity with innovation.""The replay value is really high; it will definitely stay on my drive." - I'm afraid we players received a completely different game.You should be ashamed."

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this game, truly I did. For people who played Civilization, this game may be unlikable and the reason is fairly basic, its too similar but too different. That in of itself isn't a bad thing, but Civilisation had the fun element dialled in at this point, so the effort to be different is what hampers this game.Perhaps those new to the genera will enjoy it? I don't know for sure. What I do know is that I feel bored trying to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed one full game, I am really enjoying this title. It does improvements more elegantly than Civ 6 or Humankind, making the choices you make in how to specialise a city and take advantage of natural resources actually interesting and fun, the different ages random events can help shape your nation in unpredictable ways, meaning you might pivot to a different strategy from intended (unlike Civ 5+ where your civilisation dictates how you'll play to a large degree).That said, the graphics aren't spectacular, the UI is a little janky, late game performance isn't great and some of the systems are really convoluted, but I really like the bones of this game and hope many of these issues can be fixed. _childDocuments_.review: If ur a true 4X player, you will appreciate Millennia. Sure it has some things to change but the base game is wonderful. If you keep comparing all the time to Civ then you're just blind. Want to keep a city with just one archer? its not realistic its quite awful gameplay if you compare it with millennia3. Want to keep re-architecting based on your age and need then millennia is better compared to Civ instead of simple 3-4 options4. Ability to kill off enemy cities on the map is needed, ability to absorb if possible2. Go above the 8 limit for cities is needed3. unforseen AI snipping ages4. caps on using domain powers is needed5. performance improvements for the graphics is neededOnce the improvements kick in, it will be an even more awesome game to play.

_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Millennia is a game that has man flaws. A lackluster of hotkeys that are'nt even conifgurable. Missing overlays to have a more precise overview about the map, as well as statistics (finding those remote camp was a pain in the ass) . A crude diplomacy system that feels hapharzadly with AI inviting you to an alliance only to be instantely at war with other nations, even those you are already allied, and that without any warning (autosave every turn is recommended because of this alone). Non functioning religion system, in my game out of 6 nations no one founded a religion, making it very easy and bland to win a religious victory in the Age of Harmony.  Finally, overall missing QoL features.However, behind that crust of half-bakedness lies a game that a fantasticly refreshing new outtake to the 4X genre. Every run is unique not only because of the different ages through your path can take, but also the different categories of XP, like warfare, expansion, diplomacy, etc. There is plethora of resources you have to manage, as well as different domains and government systems that have huge impact at how you play and adapt to win the game. The replaybility factor is enormous and the addiction is on crack level. A complex yet simple to play gameplay system.Overall I would say, Millennia is a diamond, but a diamond in the rough. It had been better that Paradox released the game at least a few month later to give it the necessary polish. However, I'm confident that they will do it justice and besides that, mod support should be coming soon enough.I give a Millennia a 8/10, but with some spit, good rubbing, grind and time, it has the potential to become a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you what I love about this game.Instead of being the identity of the nation you select, you're taking part in alternate history and choosing the strengths for that nation to succeed by selecting national spirits that shape it into what you want it to be.Humankind does this, but what makes Millennia stand out is that your decisions stick with you for the entire game. You don't just magically lose the national spirit you've picked in the next age.Where I would like to see improvements/expansions on gameplay: Let your religion evolve over the course of the game with you and further shape and influence your nation.Have unique government and national spirit options for the alternate ages. Overall, a great game. I'm looking forward to the DLCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those odd games where a lot of other review compare it to CIV. I personal think is different enough that it can stand on its own. There are few problems with the game for me but AI is a big part of this, similar challenge to other 4x have same issues but either they are dumb or super aggressive and.  UI could do with improvement like all 4x games.The biggest disappointment i had with this game which is also its defining feature is the supply chain aspect of product, its really cool early to mid game but once you get to late ages i didn't find huge amount of benefit creating the complex chains that produce less benefit then just a new building that checks all the boxes. To sum up like other 4x games is not feature complete on launch day and this game won't be, it has potential and the excitement of the different ages and crisis events. A strong recommend when its discounted and look forward to the 2025 roadmap
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Millennia is a difficult game to enjoy and for me is an incredibly disappointing game.For starters the UI looks like it's ripped straight from a mobile game. The buttons and UI elements are missing detail and almost appear fuzzy or out of focus. Especially the minimap just feels poorly done. I don't understand how the developers of this game looked at the UI and said "yeah that looks good". This takes a significant amount of enjoyment out of the game, as it makes me feel like i am playing a low budget mobile game. It could do with some serious sharpening and detail, or maybe just a total overhaul.I have found it difficult to continue playing after just a couple of hours. It seems clear to me that some major parts of the game are poorly done. You can only queue up one thing to build at a time, meaning you can only have a city build 2 things by itself before you need to intervene. The max army size is 3 units (from what i can tell) so you can't queue up a whole army to build. That becomes especially annoying when you are dealing with hundreds of barbarians rushing you at all times of the day.As many people have said the multiplayer function is not working. But the game also lacks bigger things like world generation settings. There are only a handful of civs to choose from and when choosing your civs colour, red is not an option.The unit movement animation is atrocious. For instance when moving forward 5 tiles, your unit teleports forward to the last two tiles. your units only actually walk the last two tiles, making it look very jittery and poorly animated.The combat screen is just ridiculous. When you attack, your units stand in a poorly rendered battlefield and mindlessly charge at each other until your combat turns run out. There is no way to change how a unit attacks, or what unit attacks first, as far as I understand it is all automatic. There is no way to tell how successful your units will be in combat any ease. The only way to find out is by checking the stats of an opposing army then comparing it to your own and making a wild guess. As opposed to civ, where you get an indication of how much damage you will do and how much you will take. As well as a list of modifiers effecting combat.The game devs are already participating in scummy tactics only a handful of hours post release. The game itself does not include any nuclear weapons, on it's own this is a big issue. Who hasn't played a civ game that ends in nuclear Armageddon? In my mind nuclear weapons are a core part of any 4x game such as this. Not having them implemented on release is very disappointing. But here comes the scummy part, nuclear weapons and nuclear research is part of the first DLC "Nuclear Ambitions", set to release next year! I can't understand how the devs, knowing that the game is not in a complete state, decided to announce core 4x game play components will be DLC only.The devs of this game clearly have not been watching the release of Humankind and have fallen into many similar traps the Humankind team have. As an example, releasing in an incomplete state and planning DLC immediately. I won't be refunding the game just yet, as I hope the devs will fix this mess but I definitely cannot recommend it in this state.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Don't buy this, get it when it inevitably goes on massive discount.There is a decent amount of innovation in this Civilization clone, and some genuinely fun additions to the standard formula. Unfortunately, it really wasn't ready for release.Bugs and missing features galore; I've experienced multiple game-breaking bugs, including several that prevent you from ending your turn. AI is definitely more A than I, particularly in its questionable choices in troop movement and city improvements. No save feature for custom scenario settings. No spawn quality or any other settings in custom scenario. Sometimes you start a match with literally no improvements around your starting city. You can also get locked into a crisis Age by an AI opponent doing its aforementioned questionable choices; I recently got an Age of Plague courtesy of the AI, that was a tedious one to slog through. You also don't get to try out an Age you think looks cool as a result; I wanted to try out the Age of Aether, but the AI started some crummy religion Age instead.If you want to try this game, wait for it to go on massive discount. But you're probably better off waiting, Paradox are notorious for releasing games too early and gradually patching them into a functional product.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay, not great.  It seems unfinished.  When you hit a big event and you;re expecting an exciting cut scene.  Well, nope.  You get something that looks like a high school power point presentation.  You can only have a max 8 maybe 10 cities(killing off rivals helps get more geography).  Seems cities are suppose to be tied to a region, but what a region is, geographical or city influence, never explained or shown. Oh, don't use settlers to make other "cities" they become vassals and they help your region city in some obscure and unclear ways.  Use explorer to create towns which expand your city foot print.  It's all not very clear.  It's almost a good game, but feels only ALMOST done.  Then again, they just admitted Cities 2 should not have been released as early and ALMOST finished as it was.  But they did. I think this game suffers from it.  It's ALMOST a competitor to Civ.  its a lot of ALMOST something good, but never actually good.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Ive played for 4 hours now and i can say I like it. So much to do and choose from in the game. I mean once you start planting or taking cities everywhere you can get real busy building them! I also dont mind combat as certain units are better vs others, which can help turn the tide. Barbs are a very dangerous threat early on and you have to be ready for them to come for you. I havnt played deep into the eras but im enjoying trying to figure out how everything works.That being said, there are a few things I hope they do something about. Rebinding the keys would be nice as I like to use my space bar to end my turn. Also, being able to move the different UI stuff would be nice as the Improvement points are hidden on the very bottom of the left side. Makes it a bit hard for me to see at times and I would like it more up somewhere above. Dont know why, but wish I could move them.All in all, not a bad game and Ill be playing it for awhile. If you are familiar with Civ or anything of the many games of 4x, you will prolly like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: This game is...paradoxical, lol. On one hand, I love so many of the mechanics. It is often the best of both worlds where Civ and Humankind are concerned. I did not care about the early performance issues as many of the games I buy have such issues the first couple of months. What bugs me is the baffling absence of certain things. For example, why do I have a B-17esque bomber in 2047? Why do jets just not exist? Why can I not build airfields to service my horribly ranged aircraft? Where the heck is the aircraft carrier???? This is a paradox game so it obviously has been set up to receive a million updates and FLC and DLC, but the places they chose to leave empty for these updates just baffles me. The diplomacy is particularly atrocious, and even Humankinds pitiful diplomatic system is better. The list of baffling choices really is endless. I would certainly recommend this for diehard fans of the genre like myself, but certainly not to anyone else in it's current state. Wait for it to at least have nuclear power, yet another baffling absence that was left for a 5 month DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: I would give it a mixed or on sale rating if I could.  The early game feels like an early access game.  The infopedia lacks useful information, game setup is bare bones, and nations don't feel at all unique. Part of the infopedia issue likely stems from emergent bonuses making it hard to give specifics on bonuses.  But not listing basic stuff like rivers giving +1 food to farms at the start of the game feels negligent.However after the bronze age things pick up, adding new mechanics every age or two and when you can get material and supply chains going it gets much more interesting.There are a lot of questionable balance choices, like rushing ages since the first person to pick picks an age for all nations, and barbarians spawning on the border of EVERY region in the game even if an NPC nation gets the event.All in all it's not as accessible or pretty as the last CIV but it's deep and fun despite being rough.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: This game should not have been released. I don't know who signed of on millenia shipping like this, because the genius behind the actually great mechanics of the game is clearly visible, but the performance, the graphics and the general user interface is just unacceptable for a 40€ game in 2024. The graphics of the game look like something produced in the early 2000s.This is something I could maybe accept if the game exchanged his horrible looks for a great user interface and good performance. But that is definitely not the case, the game performes horrible. Even moving units in the midgame or switching the camera from town to town lags the game horribly. The UI is weird to use, looks horrible and the important information, is something you have to actually hunt for. The Tiles of your city are confusing and do not display information very well, the way combat is reported is just weird and ugly. The saddest thing about this whole debacle of a release is that the base mechanics of the game are freaking genius, the different ages, the different paths to individualise your civ, the resource mechanics are incredible cool and bring something fresh and new to the genre and are very well designed.Do not buy this for 40€ if you are not super resistant to bad UI and graphic experiences. Inform yourself with videos about the game before you buy this. Yes there is a group of players who might take great enjoyment out of millenia, but the wasted potential paired with the 40€ price, doesn't allow me to recommend this, however great some of the mechanics might be, this kind of release is just not acceptable especially if you have a publisher like paradox behind you. (Yes paradox isn't exactly known for graphic fidelity, but it is ridiculous how bad this game looks and how bad it performes with such lackluster graphics)
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: it's okayish, it just doesn't suck you in like these usually do. my first big problem was it seems like you can't really tech rush, its like it just pulls everyone up with you unless everyone in my game is tech rushing at the same time, but i even tried cheats to test and they are right there with me. tech is also very limited and kind of disappointing. has a lot of potential, but i'm going to stop playing until it has some updates and see what they change. i really want to like it, but i'm just indifferent. with most civilization style games you have that "just one more turn" feeling that keeps you going late into the night, this one was pretty easy to set down and walk away from. its neat you can choose a different path each game, but meh. great potential, but they will have to realize some of that to make me want to play so i wouldn't recommend it now
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: My first impression, like many others, was disappointment with Millenia.  Millenia replacements most Civ mechanics with a variant all it's own.  This is great and fresh, but the lack of detail in the Infopedia makes this very frustrating.  For example, you might want to know how to invade an island occupied on all hexes by barbarians.  You right click from your sailing ground based unit, that's how.  How do you get a fighter to rebase?  Right click the target.  It took me 50 hours of gameplay to figure these things out. That is both a blessing and a curse.  The game feels new with fresh mechanics, but the learning curve is steep and there is little help on the internet.  The in-game infopedia could really shine here, but it is embarrassingly sparse.One of the biggest criticism I have had personally of 4x games in general is that technology is the most important thing.  It trumps all other strategies.  Many games have tried to mitigate that, at least making other strategies more powerful... but tech is still king.  Millennia does well to introduce new strategies and mechanics.  BUT - technology is once again King.There are 10 tech eras, with 5 offering variant ages.  These basically have a major unique mechanic and then some flavorful variation such as building details, small rule changes, unit appearance, etc.  For example, the age of plague -- a giant plague destroys your population and cities production.  One thing that stood out to me is that the "Big Plantation" upgrade is replaced by "Cash Crop Plantation" which is terribly nerfed.  This means I could make much less bread than I had originally planned as technology progressed.  Small details like this are nice - if albeit annoying.  And the annoying part is where the hate for variant ages comes in.  There are 4 crisis ages, which each have a terrible debuff mechanic.  I have experienced Plague and Dystopia, in both, the debuff mechanic randomly renders your hexes around your city useless until you cleanse them.  It can topple your empire literally.  It's a war of attrition to survive.  The clencher is that he who wins the tech race and gets to the next era first, sets the next age.  Simply put, it's not fun to have a 40+ long disaster dropped in your lap.  It's simply tedious.  What's more horrible is that there are victory ages, where you can win early by meeting conditions.  But guess what?  Not if buckwheat gets to the Age of Plague first.  I once lost my victory age to a crisis age because of the random turn order resolution -- it was a tie but I lost.  In my case, I was in a war with Japan so I had a lot of chaos from capturing cities, which meant I could only advance to the Age of Dystopia.  I have to admit that this completely wrecked all the computer players and they never recovered.   Many cities dropped to population of 1 because the computer player lost the war of attrittion.  The map is still stained with dystopian riots to this day.   The game was on easy mode from that point.  It seems odd that just by racing tech you can send the world into an irrecoverable state of hell.Diplomacy is as simple as Civ 2.  It's underdeveloped; wars are too easily declared and too often have no battles and are completely pointless.  You can't ally with anyone, because they will declare wars every 5 turns and ruining your diplomatic standing with everyone else.This game has a lot of promise, and I look forward to patches and DLC rounding out some rougher edges.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Although I kind of hate the UI (it took me an hour and a half to realize where the Improvements button is) the bones of the game are very solid.  I don't care about the old graphics because my laptop is powered by a hamster.  There is a LOT of potential interesting games here.  I hope that we can detach Ages from other players at some point in the near future, just to let things get nice and wacky and more customized.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: To play this game feels like observing the genetic improved child of the best Civ-Games and Humankind growing up. (Well, it also looks clunky like a superchad)There are so many new and fresh approachs to established gamemechanics.Way to many to list here.The demo was good but the game is amazing.Only setbacks so far are the problematic multiplayer, less world-customization and the clunky graphics.I guess, the balancing is not perfect. Have to test this. But with this many new mechanics its a miracle that it is as good as it is!No crashes or other technical problems so far. Good work for release nowadays.You have to got an eye for detail. this game is not for casual gaming.Most likely the reason for the first bad reviews. just unjustified.let's see the endgame...
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I played the NextFest demo I've been eagerly awaiting this game, and at least for me it hasn't disappointed.It takes a new spin on the classic Civilization formula; though the press release focused on the alternate ages mechanic what I enjoy the most is the production chains and economic system. The domains are also a lot of fun to play with. The alternate ages probably add replay value but so far I've been mostly focusing on learning the vanilla mechanics.I admit the graphics don't bother me, but honestly I don't think they're as bad as people say either. It's prettier than most indie games, but I guess it's caught in the middle; because the graphics are good for an indie game but not great for a major game, a lot of people judge it by major game standards in which case it's lacking.One cautionary word I will throw in, while this game has multiplayer it's apparently pretty backwards, reliant on IP connections and fiddly at that. The devs have already stated they'll look into changing that to something fit for this decade, and simultaneous multiplayer is also listed as coming soon, but if you're buying this game for multiplayer you might want to wait on those updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: It doesnt walk you through a game, or have specific scenarios to gradually introduce you to mechanics. Its a bit strange at first. It does play similar to civilization and i do enjoy the game so far. It just requires a bit more time to figure out what you are doing. I like that it is a sandbox style game, and I dislike how there are no scenarios to play.Edit:  The game has had updates and has made big improvements. Worth playing, and buying full price
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Three of the things the negative reviews will say regarding this gameA: Graphics are not that great, especially the battle screen. It's terrible and I won't try to hide that, so I'll definitely consider that valid.B: The game is a clone of CivilizationC: The game isn't adding "X" feature of Civilization and needs to do so.B and C..literally cancel each other out.  Either way, the game is going to get dogged. There's no way to please both groups opinion holders.Millennia is trying something new and different while retaining things that turnbased 4X have had for quite some time. It has some things that Civ has. It has some things Civ doesn't have. It's a different game. Not trying to be a clone, while not going so far out of the borders of the genre to be completely unrecognizable.Looking forward to exploring the ages and the deep economy system. And hopefully in the future will see some visual improvements.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended for any TBS buff with a history civ-type game itch to scratch. I saw others complain in forums and reviews that the game's various "nations" are unformed and have little or no character. Perhaps that's because this is really the first game I've found that actually has you, the player, devise your won nation, culture and society from almost scratch. I'm going to guess that a lot more thought went into the interwoven systems in the game, than did any effort to make it "pretty" or 3-D realistic. Yes, it has some quality of life improvements I'd like to see them take care of, but nothing that ruins the overall game experience. Millennia has been a most pleasant surprise and I'm  enjoying the heck out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first run of the game, and I greatly enjoyed it. I particularily love the systems, and the way your cities' needs evolve over time. Every age presents new challenges. Although the game does not feature settings to determine game length, I did find the game speed to hit the "sweet spot"; every turn felt like I had interesting decision to make, and it never felt like I had to spam "end turn" a bunch of times waiting for something (as I often get in Civ 5 and 6, esp. the later ages).You do have to manage your expectations going in somewhat. Although very similar, it clearly has a very different design vision on some aspects of the game compared to Civ. For example, selecting your starting nation is really just about choosing a flag; you customise your nation through the "national spirits" as the game goes on, which is where you get the unique powers, units, and buildings you might be expecting.Warfare, at present, is very simplistic. You declare war when you feel like it and you beat each other up until you grow tired of doing so. TIP: Click the "next" button on the combat screen every 2 seconds to make it go a lot faster without skipping the action entirely.The variant ages are very interesting, but do not go in with hopes of getting to pick and choose your desired age. Actually, I set down the difficulty on my first run and did in fact get to pick and choose, but it made me realize having less control would have actually been more challenging and exciting. I haven't actually seen a crisis age yet.Anyways, I highly recommend it. I found it very engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: While I started this game with some reservation.  I haven't been able to get into a Civ like game really for many years.  I never got into Civ5, civ6 was great, but I wasn't a fan of some of the systems in it.  Humankind started off with some good concepts, but the execution wasn't great.  I saw this and wasn't sure, it was quite a bit different from all of those.  Now to the main topic, the combat graphics in particular were a turn off.  It took me about 100 turns until all of the systems together kind of clicked in my head, I went back to my turn 1 of my save file played the game entirely differently and had a blast.  Those first 100 or so turns, weren't that bad, but there were so many mistakes I realized I made, I wanted to see what I could do with the same circumstances from scratch.  It led to me turning up the difficulty, I had started on the default difficulty and went up to master after that first game.  Don't get me wrong it isn't the ease of the game that I like, it wasn't easy to start, it was the way it all flowed together.  The way you can mix and match things to make a custom Civ based on your circumstances, that kept me coming back.  Would it be cool to have a more defined starting civ, sure, but the customization as you play through the game, the innovation and chaos system, and the events that occur from them and even how they tie into the national spirit system is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: There's not a lot more to be said about this, then other reviewers have mentioned.  The fact that nations has no identity, and one doesn't really form as you progress through the ages.  I figured you'd see cool transformations as you went from one age to the next, but they are almost independent of each other.  The "Bad" ages are just reasons to span enemies right at your regions.  Choosing your path during each of the ages, doesn't really redefine your nation which is even more disappointing. Special units aren't even upgrade-able into the next age, wasting resources on those.  In my 4x mind-world, I'm an immortal leader leading my people to the future, Civ does this well, Dominions does this well, Old World does it okay, but I have no affinity for the 'culture' I'm playing in Millennia.The end game lag is annoying, the screen skipping around.  At the beginning it's useful for your units to pause when an enemy is seen, but when you get alliances, and you have to click "Keep Moving" three times to complete a move around even allied space is frustrating as heck.Resource management is interesting, has good width, but not much depth.  Generating too much of one could lead you to a bad age, or is required for a good age.  Chaos and Innovations is an interesting concept, but has the lacks the luster of actually changing the game. Also disappointingly knowledge is the most important resource to move through the ages. you can't enter an industrial age by generating the most production, you still need to have significant knowledge.The combat pop-up is just a waste of two clicks.  It's boring and repetitive.  If they'd done something like Dominions, and had scripting to give tactics, that would've added a great dimension to it, but as it is, blah.And the most disappointing thing is end game is just a pop-up.  No Game Stats, no comparison of nations, nothing.  That really pisses me off.  It's a 4x, I want to know how well/badly I did in all the things.It's like all the other entrants in this genre, injects some interesting ideas, but fails to integrate them into the formula in a satisfying way.  RIP Humankind, Old World, and now Milennia.You'll get a couple of good hours out of it, but you won't be playing for a decade like any of the CIv's.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Update 5 and the Ancient worlds DLC have made this game feel completely different for me in the best way possible. The rebalances have gotten me to pay a lot more attention to where I make my cities, and the landscape and resource generation has gotten me to specialize them in a way that feels rewarding and natural, and gotten me to use the domestic export mechanic as well as resources and improvements I previously almost completely ignored. The Ancient Worlds DLC also allowed me to site my capital in an optimal place (which is incredibly important to do) without being left behind, and added a lot more variety and engagement to the early game, which I really like. I don't think this game goes into quite enough detail in some places. Like farming towns not getting a boost from hunting camps, and figuring that stuff out the hard way is annoying. Also, knowing precisely where to found cities is very important, especially due to the town mechanic, and I feel the tutorial doesn't warn new players about this or go into it enough early on so you can avoid irreversible mistakes, which has lead me to be frustrated sometimes, and I think will frustrate any new player.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: The good:-Experience system allows for instant boons or later additive bonuses and this really stands out among 4x games-Production chains make the resources in a region have so much more weight to them, and makes unique/rare resources stand out that much more-Vassal system allows you to build "thick" in addition to tall and wide and makes taking over enemy nations much less painful-While there is minimal starting bonuses, you gain them via specializing every 2 ages (you get new government options when you aren't choosing them) this allows for much better replay value and doesn't make you feel pigeon holed into something from the get-go-Good sense of pace when revealing new mechanics/resources age by age, gives them time to mature but keeps things fresh-Being able to choose/get forced into alternate ages is pretty cool, not infinatly replayable, but funThe bad:-the graphics are absolute dogass, from the distance you usually see things from its not that bad, but up close (like in the battle system) it's literally, truly, with no hyperbole, PS2 graphics-many really basic options like gamespeed or really any customization for the worldgen are totally absent - The diplomacy screen is terrible, no rulers, no real sense of what causes what mood, I don't even think the AI react differently to what you do like some in civ liking peace or others respecting wealth etc.The ugly:-Paradox game, while this is actually the best paradox launch in the past decade, that isn't saying much, besides missing features, some people are having problems with multiplayer-Because its a paradox game, there are already 2 dlcs preplanned because of course there are-In half a decade the game will be swamped with dlc adding new "content" that are just features they left out of the original release (by incompetence, overambition, or just greed is your guess)Still, I really enjoy this quite a bit, just beware if you are weary of Paradox's BS
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game but in it's current state, it's got serious gameplay problems.  The AI puts us into an Age of Plague every time I play.  The Chaos system makes it almost impossible in the late game because taking an enemy city causes major chaos, and there are a lot of enemy cities... and then after you take it there's no way to raze it so you end up with a horrible mid-to-late game that isn't fun.  I hope they continue to work on this game because I like a lot of the ideas.  They just need to work better (and run better).
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the reviews stop you from playing this game. It is NOT a civ killer. It brings a lot of new innovations to the civ genre and is FAR deeper than it appears. People just want this to be a civ clone, but it's really not. The graphics aren't the best, but who cares? We don't play 4X games for the graphics.Pick this up if you're tired of Civ and want something a bit different, something that adds freshness and uniqueness to the genre. I plan on putting hundreds of hours into this game. So should you.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: To my background: I have played 1 campane with 7 AI (Master) players and have started a new one on Adapt to compare. I had some experince with the first 3 Ages from the Demo.I was playing a Diplomatic game so I didn't go murder everything in sight, as most players do. I picked Olympians instead of Raiders.At first the AI's outperformed me on Knowledge, well they did all game long unless set my 6 regions, that I managed to hold, to produce Knowledge and than I think I was mostly even with the AI's and my Olympic Games Culture saved the game. The only Age that I managed to enter First was the Age of Departure, where I technically didn't even got first as an AI should have finished it on the same Turn as me.So now the the pros and cons of the game:I will start with the Cons as this is what most people will be interested in.- AI's get a ♥♥♥♥ ton of bonuses even on Adept dificulty, so I would really prefere to have them be a bit smarter and get less free stuff. - It seems a bit random, as i expect my units to attack what they are strong against as long as they can, especially when I have a leader in the Army. The graphics of the combat window seem a bit placeholder to me, especially the Navy graphics. - AI settels a bit to agrassive imo and you do not have an option to raze a city other than minor nations. (just five me +50 or +75 Chaos and let me raze a city)- Diplomatics need some balancing as it is way to hard to get AI's to like you if they have a boarder with you and in the late game even my long term allies just started to hate me for no reason. Also one of the AI's had a -10 modifier for me being friendly with an AI that was eliminated from the game.'-' Performance tanks a bit in the late game, but this could just be my old CPU on my end.Now to the pros:+ Ages add a lot of replayability for the game+ Building your Civ up thorugh the Ages is really interesting and adds a lot of flavor if you like to roleplay a bit more instead of just going for the boring META play.+ Regons and Vasals solve a big problem of other 4X games+ Overall Graphics and Sound is great.'+' Has an undo Freature for misklicks, but is a bit buggy sometimes (will be fixed in future)Overall I had a lot of fun in my fist game, that I manged to edge out a win in the end, even tho the AI took me down an all Standard Ages Route. I had my wars where i managed to hold out against the agression and even take a City from another AI in the early game. If you are looking for a game that brings some fresh new mechanics to the 4X games this is a greate one. It still has some problems but with Paradox as Publisher this game will become a greate one in the future. Don't mistake this as a CIV clone and expect to run at least 1 full game before you understand most of its mechanics. It brings a lot of new and different stuff that I have not seen in other 4X games so there is a lot to learn.

_childDocuments_.review: Millennia is a niche game aimed at the hardcore 4X crowd. I believe that many of the negative reviews come from people outside of that niche. And that's fair - Millennia has really bad presentation, the UI looks like a browser game and the combat screen's even worse - but personally, I've had more fun with this game's gameplay than with any other 4X that's released after Civilization 4.What I particularily like about Millennia is the focus on long-term strategic planning and interlocking tradeoffs. Going by Sid Meier, a game is supposed to be a series of interesting choices - and most choices you make in this game veer on the side of "interesting" instead of "pointless micromanaging busywork" (with the balance unfortunately shifting in favor of the latter late-game, though).  Where do I place my cities, so that they remain viable in the long term but work out in the short term? What about the towns? The outposts and colonies? Which improvements do they need and in which order? Which national spirits do I pick, and what Domain XP do I prioritize in city/building planning based on that? Which culture powers do I prioritize; how often can I get away with pressing the Local Reforms button vs. necessary long-term culture? How do I plan to spend my Domain XP in the first place? Does my planning shift based on my national spirit choices? Which eras do I plan to get and what does that mean for my city planning? Do I need to re-evaluate my plans based on the Eras that happen, or the settlement / war plans of the AI? And this really blossoms over time in subsequent playthroughs, as you understand how these choices you made play out in the long term, and what these other choices you're making now do for you instead.The game still has some problems, and can turn into a chore in the late-game between the classic Civilization ennui of having to finish a won game, the tanking performance and some of the tight design unraveling as scarce resources become abundant. The AI's frankly really bad at warfare sometimes, too. However, if the above paragraph sounds like the definition of a good time to you, then I can fully recommend Millennia.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 1/11/2024:Another DLC released and still not even an acknowledgement at how boring the current AI behaviour makes every single game. I guess decide if you think the price is worth it if you will only get 2 or 3 interesting games out of it, since once youve seen the AI spam useless cities around your border once and realise its the only thing they do, things get boring fast.EDIT 13/08/2024:As predicted, they have released the DLC, and despite multiple people in almost every forum noting the issues with the AI and the diplomacy, they have refused to acknowledge this as an issue even once. They happily respond to people praising the game, and respond to some cherry-picked issues, but silence on the AI issue and the diplomacy issue.I can only imagine that means they dont know how to fix said issues, so hope people buy the game and dont notice it until they have played it a few times.The fact that they are focusing on pumping out DLC but not fixing these core issues which any play-tester could have told them during beta (which this game should still be in), tells you exactly where the priority of these devs lay.Extremely dissappointed in the treatment of the most innovative addition to the 4x genre in many years.Original Review.A game with fantastic core mechanics let down by some HUGE gaps in features.I can honestly say this is the first "civ" style game whos mechanics i thought were clear improvements across the board. I love the game, and wish so badly it wasnt let down elsewhere.The AI is terrible. The spam ♥♥♥♥♥♥ city after ♥♥♥♥♥♥ city around your borders then get mad at you for being too close to their boarders. This inevitably leads to the AI basically just warring you over and over.So you can take those ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cities in war, but then you either need to keep these terribly placed trash heaps, or you raze them which causes a mechanic i actually like, "Chaos". Too much chaos spawns a negative "event". And ifi didnt have to raze 5 or 6 stupid cities every war, id say the chaos mechanic was quite well balanced.I know the AI in any of these games "cheats" at higher levels getting bonus resources, but you can destroy every single improvement (and in this game, every building is an on map improvement, nothing hidden in the city), and it doesnt affect their war fighting capability at all. They still spam military units and settlers.Their war fighting skill is a joke. I know all these game struggle with it a bit, but i will set there and wipe out unit after unit after unit, and no change in accepting a truce. Like, ive razed most of your cities including some that arent ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, everything outside every city is on fire, the only reason i havent taken your capital is because its location is poor, ive killed 50 times (not an exaggeration) the number of units that youve killed of mine, and you have 0 interest in a truce. Sigh.It makes every game the same, and that becomes boring. I dont mind if one of my neighbours is a warmonger and wants to crush me. But that seems to be the only think the AI can do.I think the problem is, they never added any other systems for the AI to really compete with you in. religion you can a little bit, but its not like your MASSIVELY cultural city affects the borders around ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ city 4. And they cant cultre bomb you either. They cant do any kind of economic warfare, they diplomacy is like 3 possible actions (peace, war or allies) and is the most bare boned diplomacy feature ive seen in these games.I couldnt even give my ally their second biggest city back. They lost it one turn before i got there. I reconquered it immediately for them. Except nothing in diplomacy lets you hand it back (you cant offer or demand things as part of a trade, but you can buy luxuries i think). So instead i get a message next turn about how my borders are too close to theirs (since i now own a huge city in the middle of the rest) and they break the alliance. Sigh.The core concepts are there is what is so frustrating. But its been 3 months and this game still needs to be in early access so they can finish adding the full feature set. The way you can go into different "ages" based on what happens in the current age. The alternate history ages where mana and laylines appear, or heroes of legend have to chase down heroic quests. Or you enter an age where alchemists can make gold from lead.And the buildings in them are interesting as they are different depending on which age you enter.The "era bonus" choices are also super cool, often totally changing your gameplay because you choose a specific race that has a unique resource, or a unique unit, or a totally different way of doing something.But until the fix up even the basic ♥♥♥♥, like stop the city spamming, maybe allow the giant centres of culture to remove ♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemy cities, make the AI evaluate war better, stop the AI entering a doom spiral of war and hating you because one of your scouts tried to squeeze between ♥♥♥♥♥♥ city 7 and 8, and they decided thats a buildup of forces.If they release the DLC before fixing this ♥♥♥♥, ill be very very annoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: Millennia

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game far more accessible and fun than other 4x games.  I like Civ and Old World but they get overwhelming and grind to a halt.  I don't mind the graphics at all.  I like the combat viewer.  I never play multiplayer anything so I don't care about that.The variability of the ages and the national spirits is super fun.  Many other design decision just click, such as supply chains, outposts, various currencies to spend, etc.Looking forward to massive replayability.Edit: I've never posted a Steam review before.  Felt it was my duty since I think this game is very underrated.
