detailed_description: Starship Troopers: Extermination is a pulse-pounding co-op first-person shooter. Join the Deep Space Vanguard, an elite Special Forces branch of the Mobile Infantry, in the fight against the Bug menace and claim victory for humanity! Your trusty Morita Assault Rifle, support tools, and fellow Vanguard Troopers are all that will keep you alive while exploring the hostile surface of these ugly planets, these… Bug planets. Would You Like to Know More? THE WAR EFFORT NEEDS YOUR EFFORT! Retake and rebuild bases, construct refineries, and complete a variety of other side objectives to wrest control of the planet away from the Bug menace. Massive, detailed maps with several unique zones add to the incredible replayability, and swarm-based combat with hundreds of enemy Bugs on screen delivers the sense of taking part in an overwhelming planetary struggle! WELCOME TO THE NEW VANGUARD Choose from six different classes to best suit your playstyle and support the rest of your squad. From the assault-ready Ranger and Sniper to the devastating Demolisher and life-saving Medic, the Deep Space Vanguard has a place for all types of players. As you progress in each class, you’ll unlock new weapons, equipment, and perks as well as cosmetic options to help you look the part of an elite warfighter! THE ONLY GOOD BUG... Increasing Bug threat levels bring bigger and more dangerous enemies to the fight, and you’re going to need to hunker down to stand a chance. Construct walls, towers, ammo stations, and more to beat back the Bugs until Fleet can come and get you. You’ll encounter Drone, Warrior, Gunner, Plasma Grenadier, and so many more Arachnid bastards! Keep your eye out for that Tiger Elite… DO YOU HAVE WHAT IT TAKES? Starship Troopers: Extermination is being built alongside the community. With a lower entry price at Early Access launch, we want to encourage Troopers to sign up with the Vanguard. We are boots on the ground with our community, ready to listen, as we take the game from Early Access to a full launch.

_childDocuments_.review: For $25 this game has been an absolute blast.  It's definitely rough around the edges and needs some polish here and there along with QOL things but overall it's great.With 16 players having Team/Local voice chat there is pretty much always a fun and overall positive atmosphere going while slaughtering hunters of bugs and the base building isn't too bad either.  There are 3-4 primaries per class as of right now basically and Operator(Medic) overall feels significantly good as he gets a grenade launcher, has a huge arsenal of support items to bring in and has a drone that can revive you or a random downed teamate nearby up to 4x per useage.The hunter(Assault) as of right now feels slightly weaker as he's having to use the generic 3 guns that all classes get with no exclusive, but has a jump jet that allows him to get up on extremely high ledges and buildings making his survivability and overall traversing really nice.  Plus later in levels it looks like he has some extremely lethal tactics to kill huge clusters of bugs (along with any unfortunate teamates nearby as well)And the Bastion(Tank) has a deployable 360 shield that gives him a ton of armor that allows him to tank pretty heavily against almost everything while wielding an LMG that has some absolute bonkers recoil unless you ADS or use your tactical.  While also getting a good amount of tacticals as well centered around team support he's definitely my second favorite behind the medic.Either way the game runs great and has minimal bugs considering how new it is and if you're looking for just a fun time with 15 other random people on voice chat killing bugs like deep rock galactic, i really recommend giving the game and trying it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Do you want to know more? Starship Troopers, the new video game adaptation from "Off World industries" based on the iconic movie, has arrived, and it's a blast! Strap on your power armor, load up your weapons, and prepare to dive headfirst into an adrenaline-pumping battle against hordes of deadly bugs. This game is a true tribute to the beloved sci-fi film, delivering outstanding gameplay that keeps you engaged from start to finish.One of the most commendable aspects of Starship Troopers is its remarkable attention to detail in capturing the essence of the movie. The developers have managed to replicate the intense and chaotic atmosphere that made the film so memorable. From the vast and hostile alien landscapes to the distinct sound design, every element feels like a faithful extension of the Starship Troopers universe.But let's talk about the gameplay, because that's where this game truly shines. It's a seamless blend of intense first-person shooter action, strategic squad-based combat, and heart-pounding co-op missions. As you and your fellow troopers face off against waves of gigantic arachnids, you'll experience the thrill of battling for humanity's survival firsthand. The controls are smooth and responsive, allowing you to swiftly navigate the treacherous terrain and unleash a barrage of firepower on your insectoid foes.The level design is nothing short of exceptional. Whether you're fighting through large-scale outdoor skirmishes, each mission feels meticulously crafted and offers a diverse range of challenges. The variety of weapons at your disposal is impressive as well, from the classic Morita assault rifle to 3 round rocket launcher enough to any bug go splat. It's the perfect arsenal to bring justice to the bugs and send them running.As you progress through each skirmish, you'll have the feeling of being in the movie, leaving you with a nostalgic rush.i found myself yelling into my mic, "Come on, you apes! You want to live forever?" i bet you too will find yourself uttering those very words as you and your comrades face insurmountable odds, displaying bravery and heroism in the face of annihilation.the cooperative multiplayer mode is an absolute blast. Team up with friends or strangers, strategize your approach, and engage in epic battles together. It's an exhilarating experience to coordinate attacks, cover each other's backs, and come out victorious as a unified squad.the need to aust severs are a must and with some luck they will be here soonIn summary, Starship Troopers is an outstanding video game that successfully captures the essence of the beloved movie. The gameplay is addictive, the graphics are immersive, and the true-to-the-source material is a treat for fans. So, suit up, grab your buddies, and join the fight against the bugs. Starship Troopers will have you screaming, "Kill 'em all!"and remember "Service Guarantees Citizenship."RATING: ★★★★☆

_childDocuments_.review: I still vividly remember the day I went with my dad to watch the movie in 1997, so this movie has a special place in my heart... and this game, makes me recoil in disgust at how badly they've butchered this franchise. TriStar Pictures should be ashamed for allowing this game to be spunked into existence... but alas, I fear they have no shame, because let's face it: they also allowed the painfully terrible Starship Troopers 2 movie to be made... so for them, this is just another step down the ladder of awfulness.Pros:  ? Haven't found any yetCons:  The game has no singleplayer and has no bots. You MUST play with humans. This means that in a few weeks when this game's playerbase nose-dives to less than 300 players, you're going to really really struggle to find 15 other players to play with in your particular region. The tutorial is terrible and doesn't cover many important game mechanics The enemies have no attack animation... when they attack, they literally freeze in place. Arbitrary limits have been set on how many of a specific building you can build. How does it make sense, to arbitrarily limit the building mechanic, in a game where building a stronghold is a huge part of the game? The game has a massive problem with dust/smoke... the amount of times I had my entire FOV obscured by a smoke screen/dust is insane. This game has more smoke in the air than a bad 1980s porno. The game features the kernel-level anti-cheat software known as 'easy anti cheat'. When I pointed this fact out on the steam forums, the devs deleted my post. Why would they include this crap in their game, if they're embarrassed about it? If you're going to infect your customers' PCs with kernel-level software, then at least have the balls to stand by your decision... don't try to sweep it under the rug like thieves in the night. And I don't even need to point this out but: 'easy anti cheat' doesn't prevent cheaters, so why even include it in your game? The game features none of the original actors, voices, scenes or music from the movie. If you're gonna base a game on a movie... THEN BASE IT ON THE DAMN MOVIE. When you shoot, the sound of shooting continues even after you've stopped shooting. The game randomly disconnects you while playing When you are disconnected for whatever reason, you receive zero experience or rewards for kills/progress made during the match. The game has no weapon customizations (no reticles/grips/stocks/barrels/etc.) The lvl1 starting gun, is more effective at killing stuff, than the SAW which you unlock later in the game. Repairing is glitched and sometimes doesn't function Abilities are glitched and sometimes don't function The animations are dog poo. I've seen better animations in games from the 2000's. The game is for sale in Russia The game's regional pricing is hella terrible. The game is at least 500% too expensive in multiple different regions.In summation: There are too many shooter games out there that have you facing off against hordes of PvE enemies for this game to be even remotely worth anyone's time... just look at Destiny 2, Division 2, World War Z, CoD Zombies, Fallout 4, Fortnite StW, etc. all of which are vastly superior to this game in every way.Here's my first impressions of the game: For more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game in early access for $30. It was a great, if simple game early on. As the updates progressed and the launch of 1.0 drew near, things began to deteriorate rapidly. Updates began being a lot more buggy and having performance issues. The engine transition to UE5 made things a lot more unstable and messy overall. After 1.1 the game is in a pretty sorry state. Optimization and stability is horrible, the game crashes almost every every time I launch it, the bug animations are stiff and clunky, and I swear bugs have been double or triple hitting players per animation as you no longer have the ability to get surrounded and extricate yourself or have amazing final stands like before way back in early access. You get surrounded, you're dead instantly regardless of class and difficulty.The single player campaign is not even a campaign. It's a glorified tutorial that is needlessly and painfully drawn out over 25 missions. Even then it fails to go into comprehensive base building mechanics outside of what key to use to bring out your build tool and to deconstruct or repair. It is boring, tedious, repetitive and uninteresting. It's just flat and hollow with nothing of real value outside of the most basic information that could be useful to a new player if they have the fortitude to go through every single mission in the few hours it would take. It is nice the campaign gives you weapon XP and is probably the only redeeming thing about it so you can turn off your brain and grind a low XP weapon or two.Overall the game had promise and was quite fun in early access. Now it's a buggy, unoptimzed and disjointed mess. I would struggle to justify purchasing it for $30 in its current state, let alone the full asking price the game ascended to after the 1.0 launch. This game is in desperate need of being rebuilt or heavily passed with optimizations, fixes, and tweaks. Unless this game one day makes a big turn around and focuses on fixing itself give it a pass unless you get a hefty discount or sale. Your money is better spent elsewhere at the moment. Space Marine 2 and Helldivers 2 are much better alternative games if you need to scratch your horde shooter fix.

But the peculiar thing is that no one was offended, no one was upset, everyone was laughing having a good time, and that's something I don't see much with online games anymore. 10/10 would get spawn-camped by Inferno Bugs again.

_childDocuments_.review: - Performance Problems, Fps drops when alot is on the screen, sometimes feels like a slideshow-Performance on the company mission on the icy planet is especially bad. I get huge frame spikes and it is literally unplayable, this definitely needs fixing.-Right now, almost no bugs spawn while the arc is active and counts to 100%. Simply boring, because literally nothing happens. This needs immediate fixing aswell. Might have to do with the last update.-Game crashes when a mission is finished-When joining a mission, you might get an error and get kicked from the server immediately-The servers are overall very unstable and cause lag and might randomly shut down during a mission, thus losing all the experience and invested time. This actually happened quite a few times-Respawning is bugged, you just see the blue arc building and are stuck in the revival screen. This time it even happened in one of the normal game modes outside of the horde mode. This is a game breaking bug, since you are not able to continue playing. If you press the button "E", nothing happens.-When standing inside the rescue ship, your character might get pushed outside, because the physics inside are totally wonky, which really shows when the drop pod starts, everyone's character bounces alot. You also might die, when getting pushed outside into the bugs.-Right now you fall through the drop ship when it lifts off and i don't think we get experience points for the successfull rescue- Too many bugs and screen effects (fog, explosions, fire) often block your vision and you don't know where you are and cannot target your enemies-Enemies come from every direction, and there are very few defending points-Sometimes the big grenadier bugs (the blue ones) or the bigger fire artillery bugs shoot from behind a wall onto the fortress and simply destroy it. They should always be forced to have a line of vision, to be able to shoot them- Symbols shown in the User Interface are confusing, can get difficult finding your way to a goal or your teammates- Weapons don't feel realistic enough in my opinion, they should have more of a punch- Recoil on many weapons is too high- While running, sometimes you aren't being able to shoot with your weapon, instead it shoots off to the side or sometimes you aren't able to zoom. Should feel more flawless, to go from running into shooting- Building menu should be more accessible.- A huge problem while bulding is, when there seems to be another structure in the way, even though you should be able to place a wall or anything, it sometimes won't let you build it.- Building in itself is highly problematic, given the little time.A Suggestion would be to build the item you want, right where you look at. At the moment you have to look at the ground to build something within the building zone. It is highly unpractical to look on the ground to build something up on a wall on a strategic point. Does not make any sense.- Strange leveling system with multiple leveling ranks for different things. Keep it more simple.-Leveling takes way too long, its a huge grind. Tune it down.- not enough maps and terrain variety- should have more customisation options for different playstyles.- a few more weapons won't hurt anybody (except the bugs)- Sometimes a bomb bug falls on top of you and one shots you out of nowhere. The sound of these bomb bugs comes way too late and does not give you a proper reaction window. I would suggest you remove these bugs all together, because they add nothing of value to the game- You cannot join a specific guild, if it doesn't appear in the guild browser- As a grenadier you often need 6 or more tries to place your bomb on the ground, which makes placing it often virtually impossible-The extraction to the drop ship is highly unfun, because you either run in first and make it or you cannot find your way and don't. There is no in between. You cannot fight your way to the drop ship. Might be due to the nature of the game, but its just not fun to not be able to fight your way to the drop ship when you run a little late. (Yes i know it involves alot of teamwork, but most people don't use the voice chat)-In Horde mode the games sometimes does not let you respawn at the HQ, your only choice is to leave the game-The fire from the flamethrower shouldn't be able to easily kill the technician when the fiery bugs touch him. He should standarized wear fire protective gear-The flamethrower overall feels too weak in the open field, because it has not stagger effect and very low ammo against single enemies. Against hordes and base defense it is a great weapon, but overall it needs some adjustment to make it fun and more usable or you cannot even fend off more than 1 enemy outside of the base. Especially since the engineer gets two shot from a normal warrior bug, which is in an instant-The range shield from the guardian, which you can place 3 of, feel pointless, they should rather serve a defensive position and be able to block or funnel the bugs instead of only blocking range damage, which no one cares about and the shield is too small anyway-Sometimes you fall out of bounce and it takes a while until you are allowed to respawn-Overall the balance of the game feels off, sometimes there are a thousand bugs on normal difficulty and sometimes its way too easy. The game should have a mechanism which detects when a group cannot progress and lower the hazard level, or else you might be stuck forever killing bugs and not being able to progress your main objective. Sometimes you feel like you need a break to restock and take care of the objectives. Would be great if you killed lets say 300 Bugs (or whatever feels balanced), so the game detects it and gives you that much needed break. And vice versa if it is too easy.-Sometimes, when you die and get revived, your character gets stuck, somehow floating over the ground and unable to climb anymore. And also your weapon might get stuck, so you can't shoot anymore. It just vanishes. The only way to solve this, is to kill your character and respawn again.-The medic stim does not work properly, most of the time you need to do the healing animation twice and click heal twice, before you can heal once. Very annoying when you're in between the bugs and desperately need to heal or die.-The arachnid threat level encounters on the map may get stuck at 3/40 kills and you cannot kill anymore arachnids to advance that counter, so it is impossible to reduce the threat level-As an engineer you cannot use your special abiltiy in the base, because the standard building menu overwrites your extra building menu, thus rendering this ability (except for the faster building speed) almost completely useless. You should be able to use your extra buildings inside the base.-The newly built turret from the engineer should always destroy the old turret, so you can move forward with your troops to a new position. Right now, you have to destroy your turret first, which is highly inconvenient, up to the point, that if you miss to destroy it, you won't be able to build a new one throughout the whole game-Also the building outside of the base is quite difficult, you should be able to place your turret and other buildings where you want, but often times you don't find a good spot and simply cannot build it at all, because the blueprint stays red-The bugs overall feel too strong, they absorb way too many bullets-the first aid arrow gun does not work properly. Often times people's bodys lie somewhere else than they seem to be. It is a server side issue. So you are not able to actually hit the dead bodies on the ground and are not able to revive your teammates, rendering the first aid arrow gun useless. It needs to work reliably, or else why pick a medic in the first place?

_childDocuments_.review: May 18th, 2023Do I enjoy the game?  Yeah!  Are there fun people sometimes meme'ing the hell out of it?  Oh yeah!  Will I continue to play a bit more?  Yeah!  Then why don't I recommend this title at this point in time for the price point?Lack of content.  There is 1 map.  The objectives appear at random locations, but within 2-3 hours you've seen every spot at least once if not several times.  There are 5 primary guns in total I believe to unlock. There are 2 different pistols. You get some grenades to toss around, and that's it for weapons.  There are perks you can unlock, but they are also re-used and just in a different order for each class. So overall, there's a few hours of content.  The rest is doing that same content over and over to level up or because you enjoy the experience.  But that is going to quickly wear off in another few hours.  You'll have every gun available for every class, every grenade, and most perks.  Then you're left to just rinse and repeat the same map and objectives over and over and over again.  I get it, it's EA.  And by the time it full releases it could have mountains of content worthy of tens of hours of time, but that's not the state it is in right now.  So I cannot recommend spending $25 for a few hours of content.  That's before mentioning the optimization issues which cause the frames to drop to 30 on the last stage of the mission every time.  Too many bugs and explosions and your frame rate will drop substantially, doesn't matter what you're running.  Again, that's a common EA issue is optimization.  That's usually pretty low on priorities compared to content.  But this is a review as it stands today.  I am super duper excited for what this can become.  And I stay away from EA titles usually these days, but this looked like a hoot, and it is.  But it's not exactly filled to the brim with things to do.  Sort of like an appetizer.  My general rule of thumb for games is one hour of playtime per $1 spent.  Which means at $25 I'm hoping to get 25 hours of enjoyment out of the title.  There are exceptions for things I'm in love with like star wars or something.  But that gets balanced out by games like Rocket League where I have 2,000+ hours at a $20 price tag.  I feel it's a decent rule of thumb to think about, anyways.  Especially in a game like this where replayability is the selling point. Anyways, check it out if you have some money to burn.  If it's between this and something else that you're torn, get the full game and leave this in the oven for a bit longer to get more bang for your buck.  That's my take on it.  I hope it was helpful for you at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing since the initial Early Access release and I've watched as the player numbers have dwindled. Judging by the roadmap, it may not be worth revisiting this game until 2025. Performance/Graphics- Framerate on some of the maps is borderline unplayable, Performance should not be this awful for the graphics quality that this game provides. - Visually, this game looks 10 years old. Typically I wouldn't judge a game for its graphics if the gameplay holds up, but this is not the case with this game. - General performance has been getting worse as each patch is releasedEnemy AI - Animations for the bugs are janky at best (Particularly in movement, changing directions, death)- When viewing enemies from a distance, animations appear to skip frames- AI pathfinding is pretty awful (constantly get stuck in map geometry, only run in straight lines)- Enemy models are not particularly reactive to being shot beyond their awful death animations and blood effects- There are no interesting shooting mechanics like weak points or dismemberment, just hold down mouse1 until you see a red hit marker.

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers: Extermination is an ambitious early access game that immerses players in the intense and chaotic world of interstellar warfare against swarms of deadly bugs. While it's important to keep in mind that the game is still a work in progress and not without its flaws, there's a lot of potential for it to become an exciting experience.One of the noticeable drawbacks of Starship Troopers: Extermination is the early access status. As expected, the game may not be polished to perfection, and players might encounter a fair share of 'bugs' and performance issues. Screen clutter can sometimes be overwhelming, obstructing your view and making it challenging to focus on the action. Moreover, it's frustrating to experience bugs that result in the player getting sliced through walls or encountering other immersion-breaking glitches. However, it's essential to bear in mind that these issues are likely to be addressed as the game continues to be developed and improved.Despite its shortcomings, Starship Troopers: Extermination does manage to deliver some genuinely enjoyable gameplay moments. The battles against waves of relentless bugs can be incredibly intense and action-packed, offering adrenaline-pumping encounters. The variety of weapons and gear at your disposal adds a layer of depth and strategy to the combat, allowing players to experiment and find their preferred playstyle. Additionally, the cooperative mode provides an opportunity to team up with friends, enhancing the game's overall experience and increasing its replay value. (Hopefully the amount of weapons and gear increases with time)In summary, Starship Troopers: Extermination is not the best game ever, but it's important to remember that it's in early access. Despite the screen clutter and occasional bugs that can be frustrating, the game manages to offer an enjoyable experience, especially when played with friends. If you're a fan of the Starship Troopers universe or simply enjoy action-packed shooters, this game might be worth picking up now and then. However, it's worth keeping an eye on future updates to see how the developers refine and enhance the game. With the right improvements, Starship Troopers: Extermination has the potential to evolve into an outstanding and thrilling gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I've wanted a game like this for a while, and after playing it for a few hours and letting the content digest for a few months - I've come to the opinion that it is...a decent game. Don't get me wrong, you feel like a part of Rico's Roughnecks, and with so many players in a single lobby - it seems like a full-flung military ground-operation. What's the meat and bones to this game, you may ask? Well, this video-game is themed around the franchise of Starship Troopers, obviously - heavily inspired by the book by Robert A. Heinlein, a sci-fi novelist. You drop from high-orbit from landers on the infested planet of Valaka as part of the elite Deep Space Vanguard, protecting key resources and objectives (which can often take thirty minutes, upwards to an hour, depending on the skill of your team), fighting hundreds of Arachnids along the way, of which there are multiple variants, and then awaiting evac in the form of the same lander that brought you to the planet. Seems simple, right? It can be repetitive. With a lack of maps and variety of objectives, you find yourself in the same environments and doing the same types of missions over and over again, it's boring. There are few weapons as well, and they are rather dull, though it is nice to see them in action from the films. If this was some generic nameless franchise without an intellectual property, no one would have bought it, but this is Starship Troopers, so people care, because these games are rare. But I don't hate the game. I want to see it grow. I see potential. With promises features on the way in December 2023 and 2024 on the way, I look forward to seeing the future of this game. I recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers: Extermination is a game developed by Offworld Industries, based on a popular mod for their "Squad" game. Would you like to know more?It's a 16 player co-op horde shooter where you take control of a valiant member of the Mobile Infantry, choosing from one of three classes. Content is decent for a game entering Early Access, and the game's priced better than Offworld games usually are. The two modes are fun, but the game really shines in the ARC mode, which sees your battalion holding down a single area, building a base, and stocking it with resources before a final showdown with the Arachnid horde. Bug variety at the moment is a little lacking, but the additions that can be made are obvious and will most likely arrive in the coming months. Pick up a Morita and do your part today!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm fairly torn on this game. It's a fun time waster, the graphics are great and the gameplay is pretty smooth. There's not a lot of bugs (outside of the ones your getting swarmed by) which is refreshing considering all the games that have come out lately that have. But put simply in it's current state I can't recommend it. There's very little to do. There's two separate game modes both of which are tedious and repetitive. Cooperation can be rough as there are griefers that join and don't contribute or actively attempt to sabotage success. There's no way to mute individual players so people with out push to talk mouth breathe and play music or you hear the game through their mic...(seriously who uses speakers to game?). Instead you have to decide whether you want to mute voice chat all together or deal with the mouth breathers. The class play is pretty good though there's no reason to play anything other than the operator especially once you get the grenade launcher. I believe that the bastion is unique enough to warrant playing, but the hunter is pretty uninteresting. There is a certain feeling you get when your getting swarmed by arachnids that immerses you in the game and really brings to life the movie. When you see your budy get hit by a plasma lob from the plasma bug and gets destroyed or they start tearing through the defences. It's pretty great. But the same map over and over with dumb ai mechanics and very little interms of map mechanics get stale fairly quickly. Maybe once horde mode or other game modes come out it'll be better. Personally I'd like a starship troopers/planetside 2 kind of game where one side plays arachnids with increased player capacity and the other plays Mobile Infantry and you fight over territory would have been a better option. BUT it does scratch an itch and it's fairly cheap compared to other games nowadays so who's to say.

_childDocuments_.review: Good day Citizens, we are here with our Early Access first impressions of Starship Troopers Extermination out now. The main takeaway from this game is that it's fun, great sound design for weapons and bugs. Hilarious community of people that do not know what they are doing, but still get work done. It is the experience that makes the game worth dealing with the bugs and some graphical issues.Besides that, some weaponry needs fixing with bad recoil and at times when you pull the trigger it does not fire. This is an all-around fun game and being that it is in early access, I am quite satisfied so far. The main thing or rather take away is the community so far not being toxic and mostly all being Starship Trooper fans shouting out all the quotes from the films. So far making it a great experience. Love that even though you are on a specific team you can still communicate with the other squads or talk privately with your own team. Reminds me of the old days of Halo when you had a private coms button for your squad. Combat wise the bugs are relentless as they should be and fun to battle against. The developers took care in giving us that experience from the films where at times you can have bugs pop up out of nowhere and swarm you. Grenadier Beetles, Tiger Tarantulas, and sniper bugs are a menace that you need to keep an out for. However, hoping down the line they add the other bugs like the brain bug as a possible capture and contain mission, the flying ones, and the firebugs. Leveling up is straightforward forward if you fight and do what needs to be done with you make the points you need. It is straight forward and some missions will have a job individually for each trooper. Speaking of you will have three choices of a trooper and right now I am using the Bastion which is the Heavy Artillery trooper, there is a support class and an assault class. A Well diverse crew so far. All and all spending four hours in one night just laughing, killing bugs and just having a blast. Also if you get your own crew of 16 players you all can play with buddies together. Because that is the max for your personal squad. However, there are 5 teams with 4 players on each team This would be a great time to set up a big community night. Hoping for down the line we get exo-suits for all classes and more melee weaponry and of course better gun controls. My initial thought is worth the buy, but again keep in mind it is in Early Access. Either way have a great time and hopefully we can get a game together. - Beast Out -

Not being able to play this game, and specifically ONLY this game on High, let alone Ultra is just poor. When a game from the early 2000's (also aptly named Starship Troopers) managed to fit hundreds of bugs on screen, this title handles a handful before lagging. Poor choice of engine when others do it better.The next issue is that the game installs software without permission. I specifically uninstalled ALL EPIC store content from my machine for my own personal reasons, primarily their predatory behaviour - and instead, this game decided to - without permission from myself - install EAC and Epic Store. I am 100% certain that in Germany this is not permitted. Until the above issues are fixed, this game is nothing more than an Alpha. Beta implies functional and playable, but this is just trash right now. I know some will disagree, but buy it and find out for yourself if in you dare.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely amazing and I would fight that it is still a fun game. I played this game when it first came out for early access in May 2023 and that is where I got most of my hours in. The game ran well and crushing bugs was as smooth as could be. Now a lot has happened in-between now and then with some highs of content updates like hoard mode and new classes but it has also had some pretty hard lows of incredibly poor performance and game breaking glitches as well as poor servers. This 1.0 update while I wasnt expecting it to fix everything I was expecting for it to add new and fun content with a fresh coat of paint. I was doing my best to manage my expectations while also holding onto expectations for what I would consider my dream game. However this update has really crushed alot of my enthusiasm. What did we get in 1.0? We got a galactic war, we got the tanker bug, a new planet, a company system, and a solo tutorial. I think that covers the big stuff. So what is the problem? Well nothing seems to work as intended. Lets start with the galactic war which is what I was most excited for. This feels absolutely nothing like a war. The galactic war is nothing more than a menu and 4 lines of statistics, with those being how many troopers died, how many bugs died, how many operations have been completed and I think something about intel. There is no sort of "Turf war" going on here like in helldivers or For honor. You are filling up a percentage meter. It really lacks the feeling of two sides trying to kill each other and conquer ground from the enemy. Alright well what about the tanker bug? Well that comes with problems too. The tanker only seems to spawn as a mutator on the new ice planet so already it feels like its contained to a rare encounter. More than that Iv yet to actually see this bug breach the walls, it spawns and kind of just flounders around being a bullet sponge. I havnt seen anyone die to this thing unless they were trying to get on its back. The final nail in the tankers is that the bug has just randomly despawned for no reason, making it even less threatening. Alright how about the new ice planet? Well that has been put behind the new company system and requires intel for you to be able to access it. Now I suppose this would be fine if the company system actually worked. (Im getting to that) And this issue can be worked around by leaving a company and forming a new company giving you free intel to play on the new planet but its just annoying that i have to find a way to "work around" it. Alright last but not least, the company system. There is no way for you to invite your friends to the company you make and there is no way for you to search for your friends company. In other words the company system straight up dosnt work at all. Id argue in its current state it works more in the idea of "proof of concept" because in function it feels like it dosnt add anything. Worse than that they are looking to fix the problem of this core mechanic in Q1 2025. Chew on that for a minute. All that being said I still enjoy playing this game. The core gameplay for me is pretty neat. However Starship Troopers deserved a better release than this and it honestly cripples the strong hopes that I had for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel the Devs went kind of old school with the overall feel of this game, but in a great way. The game is a 16 player Co-Op, with very simple mechanics and game modes. The match lengths feel PERFECT in length, being the right amount of time to enjoy them greatly, but they almost never feel like they drag on. The Co-Op nature feels like it encourages everyone to have fun, rather than be overly competitive, and the simple nature of the game mechanics means that even someone who can only casually play games on occasion would be not only be able to hop in to a server and have great fun themselves, they wouldn't be dragging anyone else down (on the contrary, even a very bad player is still a great help), and in general this helps promote a positive gaming experience with minimal toxicity. Really love what the Devs are doing with this game. If you're someone a bit older that doesn't have the time to learn complex game mechanics, but wants a simple, fun game to hop in to and start blasting with friends, this is the game for you. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Only 6 hours in and this could change but I am finding the game rather good fun. It's certainly janky with a lot of weird glitches and soft locking the game from time to time. Hitting redeploy had me stuck with no countdown or way to rejoin in the game. Hitting the map key just before the round ends, your left with the map overlay on screen and no way to continue the game. Keybinds not working sometimes which was happening to my friends but I never experienced it myself. Grenadier bugs spawning inside of buildings with only their legs sticking out. That sort of buggyness :PPerformance at the defence and extraction needs a lot of work as I'll dip all the way down to 25-35 fps then. When I am a comfortable 80-90 all the other times on high settings at 1440p.Now the good things that I can see in the game. _childDocuments_.review: In its current state, I cannot recommend this game. My biggest gripe is that it runs poorly. For reference, I have a GeForce 1660 Ti, a Ryzen 7 2700X CPU, and 16 GB of DDR4 3200 memory. You would think that a machine made to run ARK: Survival Evolved on high settings (with little-to-no stutter) would mean the game is playable without lagging directly into a horde of bugs. But such are the perils of Early Access games where the recommended system requirements are a bald-faced lie.I have other complaints, but they're all my fault, and I wouldn't give this game a fair shake if I added them to this review. Actually, I should at least touch on the tutorial. All it does is teach you how the building mechanic works, and you're done in five minutes. It doesn't cover the finer points of how you should apply that knowledge (which would help new players understand what's happening half the time during a multiplayer session). If the developers even wanted to, they could make a short campaign game into the tutorial, where you can play with bot players and understand how each game mode is supposed to play out. But I've heard that programming trooper AI isn't in the cards, along with other things that would guarantee the game's longevity (community servers being the most notable example).All in all, this game's launch into Early Access is like the battle of Klendathu: high hopes for success, an utter disappointment, and a mess that needs to be cleaned up sooner than later.

_childDocuments_.review: Its good mindless fun.It gives that feeling of Left4Dead where you and 3 others are running and gunning, trying to accomplish something...but instead of boring zombies they're giant bugs...and its 15 other people. These matches are also all "quick match", so no waiting in long Queues to get into populated servers or anything. Playing in a party with friends you can also Quick Match into a game as a unit.Make no mistake though, this is early access. Animations and movement can feel a little jank, but the shooting generally feels great. The core is definitely Squad-based, but sped up. Ammo reloads from a reserve rather than managing per-mag ammo, and there's no stamina for sprinting.The Levels are all pretty basic desert, but with some good terrain variances. The random time of day also helps them feel a bit richer. Primarily complaint after 4 rounds is 2 of them were a map layer where one of the territories only had a single Mineral extractor...and the extractor kept having to go on cooldown for like 3-5 minutes. During that time, enemies don't infinitely spawn or anything, so we all just sorta stood around until we could squeeze 8 canisters out of the one extractor.The "final hold" construction is also a cool feature. I'd love to see something like this in a higher-speed squad, as its really nice that EVERYONE can build, and EVERYONE can place. It's also much quicker to build up and repair. Repairs cost nothing, they just have to be done while it isn't being attacked...very easy to do mid-swarm with a bit of teamwork. The unlock system is fairly deep, albeit some items are recycled between classes currently it would appear. However, they unlock at differ class ranks, so you still see a variety in gameplay. All 3 classes feel valid despite some other reviewers saying otherwise. I've exclusively used the default Assault class as many others use the other two classes, and I've had no issues making short work of enemies. I have yet to die across 4 sorties as the jetpack makes a great escape tool, and it opens up a lot of firing perches that only ranged enemies can get to you.As a fan of Offworld Industries' work, I'd easily recommend this game to others wanting to support their intended final product. It is a fun core gameplay, that now needs some polish and growth. For the cost of what it takes to Door Dash McDonald's you too can blast bugs along with 15 others.

They could have followed the trend of 4-player horde shooters like L4D, Vermintide, etc. but they instead decided to go for a twenty-five player versus ~2,000 bugs (I'm guessing here) battle.Sure, you can take on a bug, you can take on a group of them if you manage to not miss any bullets in your magazine. But the truth is you -need- your squadmates or you're not going to have a very good time being torn to bits the moment your gun clicks with an empty chamber. Encouraging teamwork via a threat of evisceration is a big plus to me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun. Most of the community has been great and its obvious that people have a passion for the source material. The gameplay loop is weird because although there's only one map and 3 classes right now, I haven't yet gotten tired of playing it.Some people rushed to get all 3 classes maxed and I'm not sure why anyone does that. The game itself is fun on its own.I feel genuine fear when I'm trying to catch up to my squad and get intercepted by a bug. They nailed the emotional impact of going 1 on 1 with a warrior bug only to need a reload right when his friends show up and murder you. Seeing waves of bugs piling up outside of your base walls is both fun and sweaty, as you'll quickly find that if you let up even for a second, those bastards will have your wall down, eating your friends.That said, the game needs some work. I think its telling that the game just came out and people are chomping at the bit for more. Classes need a little work. More weapons. Bug diversity. Another game mode would also be nice. A little more nuance in a lot of places, really. This is the kind of game that makes me hate Early Access because I want more, right now, but I have no idea when or how that will happen.There is a small level of toxicity brewing in the community. Hackers have already arrived, cheating in a PvE game? For reasons? Getting matched up with people who don't understand how to build bases is also not so fun. But when the game is good, its really really good. Fun. Intense. Difficult to be sure, but definitely fun.This is an opportunity for Offworld to do something truly great, and more importantly unique. I firmly recommend this game as its a blast to play with your friends or even strangers. I'm also firmly crossing my fingers for this game to become everything I hope it can be.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:  Now fails to launch because it can't find CreateFile2 in KERNEL32.dll.  Enabling VxKex fixes this, but then the game stops at: "Unrecognized game client. Cannot contlinue."  In short, no longer playable.OLD REVIEW BELOW:Pro:* It's really fun!  I haven't been this hooked on a shooter since Counter-Strike or MechWarrior Online.* Good difficulty selections.  On easy everyone will be running around quoting the movie and having a blast, but the bugs still take quite a few hits to put down.  On harder modes it feels more tactical; you need to stick with your teammates, coordinate who is working on which objectives, and place your shots carefully.* All of the missions (so far) include building up a base, withstanding a bug horde, taking a short breather, then making a mad dash to the pickup ship with respawn disabled.  All of this works quite well and the escape is exciting!  (Note: the Reload button also switches the Build tool between Repair and Place modes.  This was not clear to me in the tutorial.)* Playable on Windows 7!  Just put "-dx11" (no quotes) into the launch options.Con:* Waiting for resource canisters to fill and then slowly carrying them to a dropoff gets tedious, though the vulnerability while carrying it does allow for some good teamwork.* Performance during the final escape sequence is always choppy, though still playable.  I found no improvement reducing video settings or between DX11/DX12 modes (when my Windows 11 decides to actually boot) so I hope this is just a lack of optimization in the alpha stage.  This is the only game I've seen my RTX 3070 struggle with, and it's not THAT pretty.* On Windows 7, it crashes if you attempt to view loadouts, and after each mission ends.  You still progress towards unlocks when completing a mission, but you'll have to boot another OS just to modify your loadout; your selections there will apply to Windows 7 as well.  Fortunately the default equipment does work well and feels movie-accurate, so this isn't critical.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of this IP for as long as I can remember, this game is moderate at best.If you're looking for some dumb fun with a group of friends, this team-base horde shooter could be it to fill some time before your 'next game'. However, the current state of this game is incredibly unpolished. Yes, it's an early access game but it shouldn't be an excuse for certain core aspect of the game  (gunplay, animation etc.) but so far I haven't experience any game breaking bugs (without the capital B) so that's a plus.- Class:Class system is pretty much a joke at this point, since Support is currently the most valuable one meanwhile Hunter is straight up trash. All the passive, weapon and utility at this point is basically all the same with all the classes, to determine which class is the most useful is all up to their unique class ability. Support in this game can practically do EVERYTHING. They can revive people in an instance, carry two canisters at once (which is the main winning objective of the game), and since they get the have the sniper rifle at level 2, they can deal good damage too. At the same time, the most valuable thing a tank class can have is their LMG because their knock back and damage is strong and they can take a good amount of hits with the right perks. The class ability is pretty strong as well as it can tank a lots of Bugs.So what does the Hunter, the suppose damage class, can offer? They can fly and it's not even that useful. You might say they can go to the high ground and do good damage but at the end of the day, you need people to help fix the walls when the Bugs overwhelm you and your Hunters, all they can do is watch and be the first one to get on the extraction ship cause they run a bit faster than others. They don't even get the grenade launcher because support has it.- Content:There are only two game modes at the moment, AAS and ARC. The difficulty I recommend is Hard and it is the only difficulty I recommend you playing if you want to get the desperation vibe from the films. AAS is your to go quick match mode if you just want to shoot some Bugs. However, ARC, if you don't not have a well communicated team, you are basically doomed. The progression system, like I said, the game doesn't have much to offer as all perks and weapons are all the same throughout the class with only a few exceptions. The same unlockable just spreads out at different level with different class.The base building system is very straight forward, build some walls and fences for the main objective. The only thing you need really need to put your brain in is where the towers and turrets should be placed but it really doesn't matter that much. Overall, this game at the current state is good for some dumb fun for a short period of time but it's not a great option if you're looking for a well designed system to have fun with.Would you like to know more?

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers: Extermination is an intense 16-player co-op first-person shooter that plunges you into a gripping battle against the dreaded Bugs. As an elite Deep Space Vanguard Trooper, you and your squad are entrusted with the critical mission of reclaiming planets overrun by the relentless Arachnid threat. While the game showcases potential and delivers an enjoyable experience, it currently suffers from a lack of content that prevents it from reaching its full potential.One of the game's strengths lies in its immersive and action-packed gameplay. The intense battles against swarms of Bugs are thrilling, and the cooperative nature of the game fosters a sense of camaraderie as you work together with your fellow players to overcome the odds. The mechanics are solid, with responsive controls and satisfying weapon handling that make you feel like a true trooper on the front lines.The graphics and sound design further contribute to the game's immersive atmosphere. The detailed environments and creature models bring the hostile alien world to life, enhancing the tension and adding to the overall immersion. The sound effects and dynamic soundtrack effectively create a sense of urgency and danger, further immersing players in the heart-pounding battles.However, despite its enjoyable gameplay and immersive presentation, Starship Troopers: Extermination falls short in terms of content. At this time, the game feels limited in its offerings. While the cooperative gameplay is engaging, the lack of variety in missions, environments, and enemy types becomes noticeable after extended play. The absence of a meaningful progression system or unlockable rewards also dampens the long-term motivation to continue playing.To truly shine, Starship Troopers: Extermination would greatly benefit from the addition of more diverse missions, locations, and enemy encounters. Expanding the game with new planets to explore, varied objectives, and a wider array of Bug types would inject much-needed variety into the gameplay experience. Additionally, implementing a progression system that rewards players with new weapons, gear, or abilities would provide a sense of accomplishment and encourage continued play.Despite its current lack of content, Starship Troopers: Extermination demonstrates promise and offers an enjoyable cooperative FPS experience. With updates and expansions that address the scarcity of content, this game has the potential to become a must-play for fans of intense sci-fi action. If you're a die-hard fan of the Starship Troopers universe or simply enjoy cooperative shooters, it's worth keeping an eye on this game as it evolves and grows in the future.Live Stream:

The game pays homage to the source material, capturing the essence of the Starship Troopers franchise with impressive attention to detail. The bugs themselves are brilliantly designed, bringing a sense of realism and immersion to the game. The developers have done an outstanding job of recreating the thrilling atmosphere and intense battles depicted in the books and shows.Exterminations offers a wide array of missions that keep the gameplay fresh and engaging. Whether you're clearing out bug-infested tunnels, defending crucial positions, or engaging in full-scale bug assaults, each mission presents its own unique challenges and objectives. The variety of environments, weapons, and trooper abilities ensure that no two missions feel the same. The game's mechanics are solid, providing responsive controls and satisfying gunplay that truly make you feel like a battle-hardened Marine.One of the most exciting aspects of Exterminations is the promise of future updates and content. As an enthusiast of the Starship Troopers universe, you can't help but be excited about the potential for even more bug-slaying adventures. The developers' dedication to delivering a complete and immersive experience is evident, and the anticipation for upcoming features and expansions only adds to the excitement.While the game provides an excellent platform for bug-killing mayhem, it would benefit from further storytelling elements. As someone who appreciates the rich lore of the franchise, a more robust narrative would enhance the immersive experience. Deepening the character development and adding more engaging storylines could help players forge a stronger emotional connection to the game world.In conclusion, Starship Troopers: Exterminations is a dream come true for fans of the books, shows, and the Marine Corps. It allows you to fulfill your bug-fighting fantasies with its intense gameplay, immersive environments, and faithful representation of the Starship Troopers universe. While there is room for improvement in terms of storytelling, the game promises an exciting future with its upcoming content updates. Wait and see if they can be bothered to address any of the issues (and server side performance appears to have gotten worse somehow?), rather than rolling out micro-transactions for skins.--They asked for reviews, so I guess they want the current game state noted? Performance is quite poor; lots of server side hitching, the bugs teleport, the pacing is inconsistent (you work up to the final horde, and it spawns waves 10% of the size you were getting mid mission). Randomly fall through the map, guns stop working, sometimes you can't respawn, most classes have one viable set of perks. Engineers can consistently build base structures out of bounds. Occasionally, the map doesn't end, and you get an infinite countdown timer. If you complete the rescue missions, the trooper bots lag the server for every player.They've not posted to say any of these issues will be resolved with 1.0. I have to assume they won't, and strongly recommend you don't purchase prior to release, and confirmation these  issues have been fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright you apes! You wanna live forever?! I used to think I wanted to but now I can't wait for the sweet release of... nevermind. Starship Troopers: Extermination wasn't really on my radar until I saw some live gameplay on Twitch. I liked what I saw and, frankly, I was tired of Helldivers 2 and its plethora of issues. I decided to gamble and pick it up on sale and see if it was for me. Would you like to know more?Starship Troopers: Extermination is a first person shooter where you join up with 15 other players in a cooperative experience where you are killing all of the bugs. The maps/missions vary but always have some horde like and base building mechanic. The maps are bespoke and not procedurally generated. Each map has its own gimmick but there is always a twist on which way presents it so it doesn't get boring. There are maps that are also just dedicated horde mode with the base building. Speaking of base building, I'm doing my part!The base building is based on a currency system and sometimes you have to start small and fight some waves while collecting resources, sometimes you fight toward the Arc where you build a giant base around it to protect it as the final objective of the map. Every class can build or repair structures. I was worried, "What if I put something wrong or am not optimal?" It doesn't matter, just put stuff down, its all useful. Just do not, and I mean it, put proximity mines inside the base because it does damage your structures very fast. We have the technology! The overall level system, the classes and their levels, and the gun progression system is fantastic and I think every single class based shooter should use Starship Troopers: Extermination system. For example, every class starts with the basic rifle, the Morita. The progression you make using the rifle on your Guardian will carry over to when you use the same rifle on your Medic or Demolisher, for instance. They do a very good job of making sure you feel like you are always earning something and moving forward, because you are. As far as the technology side of the game, it looks great and runs...okay. For the most part it runs flawlessly despite there being literal hundreds of hundreds of giant bugs on screen. In some places, especially during high level horde modes, it does get a little slide-showy. I'm running the game on a AMD Ryzen 9 3900XT and a 3090TI. It is in early access and I have a feeling they will clean it up before the full release. The shooting feels excellent, the one great thing about Helldivers 2 was how good the weapons feel. Starship Troopers: Extermination feels amazing to play and shoot. Each gun feels different and even the very basic rifle is a joy to shoot and is effective. The balance in this game is absolutely fantastic. As far as the things that need improvement? Well as I said earlier, they need to optimize it better but I'm confident they'll get there. There are some weird issues with crashes and things. An odd example, that might be a weird edge case that only affects me, is that it seems to crash after I play Final Fantasy XI. I get about halfway through a match and its crash to desktop. That very could be because of all the weird mods I have to run to make FFXI modern feeling, but I don't have that issue with any other games. If I play FFXI, then restart, then play ST:E, then there aren't any issues whatsoever. The controller support is abysmal. I wanted to try and play it on my ROG Ally but the aim speed is ridiculously slow and, from what I saw, cannot be adjusted at all. Since it is going to be released on consoles this fall, I am confident they will address this. You need to do your part because the only good bug is a dead bug! Its an incredibly fast paced, great feeling, well balanced, and most importantly, fun first person shooter. Layer on top of that an excellent class system with some wicked fun abilities along with base building? This is game is a recipe for success.

_childDocuments_.review: Sep 2024: Will change review in near future if/when worthy improvements for our money is made.The fun part is shooting bugs. Tons of them. Graveyards worth of bugs. You're invading a planet of bugs that presumably did nothing to you and you are encouraged to commit genocide on these bugs  that's about it... for now. As you may suspect, it's a game where they replace humans as bugs and incite you to commit genocide (I recommend you dig deeper to finding out what actual country on Earth guarantees citizenship for your military service whilst committing alleged genocide on a people whom are called animals/bugs/dehumanised, the answer lies in the lobby on the top left the logo above the word "Vanguard").You satisfy your craving of emptying hundreds of rounds into these 1's and 0's and you'll look at your Steam library what other investments you had made to fulfil other cravings.A lot of players hang around base and neglect objectives.  but these objectives don't carry any real meaning of what contributes to a victory or its opposite. When the match ends with a "victory" or "defeat" we feel completely  about it.You're not met with an interesting boss to fight with different mechanics/strategies to explore. This is simply a sandbox physics of guns that can shoot at bugs with simple list of objectives whether you complete them or not.Early access is supposed to give us a taste of what to expect down the road and encourage others to invest. What am I investing in? A game like any other? There are other games that allow me to shoot bugs, this offers less and asks for more money.The highest hours played among my Steam friends is roughly 4 hours.Considering it's from the makers of Squad I was a little concerned that my budget PC would perform poorly but to my surprise it seems better optimized than most early access games I've come across. With an RX6600 and Ryzen 5 5500 I'm rocking anywhere between 60FPS (intense combat) to 120FPS (idle) on Low graphics with Ultra Performance for FSR (great job adding FSR devs).Despite low graphical settings the game looks great enough to be immersed.Yes, it's 40$ just to satisfy a minor craving that hasn't come back...

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I think you should know that this is indeed a fun game, but technical issues have to be fixed for it to be worth imo.This is essentially Helldivers but in First Person (even though technically Helldivers is inspired by the Starship Trooper movies, kinda funny since Sony also has part of production and distribution rights of the Starship Troopers :P)The game as of now is pretty fun but it is plagued by a lot of graphical issues (most likely since its UE 5). Any sort of Upscaling methods other than Unreal's engine based one tends to cause an issue where the screen occupies the top left quadrant while the other 3 sections have extended lines in them. This fixes itself sometimes and the other times its gives you a flashing screen like situation since it keeps going back and forth from normal to this.Other than that, the base performance of the game is also kinda bad, with frame rates dropping to as low as 26 on Low 1080p settings when you get into the action (playing on the RTX 3060 6GB version). With the minimum specs required being a GTX 970 you'd expect better optimisation (I understand that the game just came out of early access so I'm just stating these as issues that will most likely be fixed)Currently, the price is kinda close to that of Helldivers 2 (in my region atleast) so when you compare it that way, HD2 seems like the better choice, but you can't get a FPS experience in HD2. Recommended, if you currently have a decently powerful system.Else I'd suggest you to wait for a while. This game has potential, as long as the devs keep supporting it and people who play MP Co-op FPS games stick with it.I would like to give a neutral recommendation lol but since that is not possible we'll go with a No.. for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Alrighty, after 14.9 hours of gameplay, i'll be as helpful as I can to those potential Citizens, I mean players, still sitting on the fence.Pros. -16 player games are wonderful. Having such big groups is awesome and makes the game play feel more unique and interesting, not to mention finally being able to play a PvE FPS game with more then 3 friends.-Bugs(the insect kind) are both powerful and weak. When you're on your own, a small group of bugs can easily take you down. However, add a Roughneck or Two to that squad, and the tables reverse immediately. Bug swarms that are insignificant from the top of the walls are game over when there isn't a foot of reinforced steel blocking their chompers.-Building. Slightly clunky. There is definitely more for the devs to add to the game like manable turrets and half walls, but it works. Building adds a level to the game that I hadn't realized I've been missing, and all in all adds flavor.-Memes. So. Many. Memes. I love saying "I'm doing my part!" in chat, just to hear the chorus of voices calling out the same. People shouting out movie quotes and jokes adds another level of immersion that takes a boring round and turns it into a heated battle between bugs and humans. There's no feeling quite like hearing someone yell, "They've breached the north wall!"and turning to see a sea of bugs charging across the compound toward you.-Voice chat. The voice chat works. You don't get annoyed at hearing information you don't need, or at people who decided to be a jerk today, you just talk your task with those around you, or speak with your squad about their tasks. Having just a local and squad chat works, and is one of my favorite VC's to date.-Room to grow. The amount of content that can be added brings me true joy. I can't wait to charge through infested bug tunnels, or fight my way through the underbrush of some sordid swamp. The amount of game modes that can be added and fit is awesome, and leaves you desperately waiting for the next update.Cons.-I don't know what the problem is, but the FPS drops HARD toward the end of each round. So far it hasn't put too much of a damper on my fun, but having your FPS crash at the best part of the round hurts.-There isn't much content. The couple of modes they have so far are fun, but I find myself relying on things like talking with other players and napalm(Oh napalm, sweet, sincere napalm!) to keep me in the zone and having fun.All in all, there's real potential. I hope the devs push through on this game, because I could see myself coming back to it for years to come. I'd say to those wondering if it's the game for you, if you like games like Deep Rock Galactic or Second Extinction, BUY IT!!! If the devs add much at all, it will be worth it. Do you want to know more?

_childDocuments_.review: Current Review:It's been very apparent that OWI didn't simply give up on this game and were really hard at work at delivering an experience that the entire community could get behind. I know a lot of people were upset when we heard about the current changes and class xp wipes, but I'm glad to say that I actually prefer what they've implemented over the old system. The game still feels alive and even if the player counts aren't the same, it's fun to see people that I've remembered from previous games. ST:E was definitely worth my money when I bought it, and I can say now that I do not regret my purchase. I would like to apologize to OWI for not having faith in them. This is a great game and a must own for anyone who enjoys team-based PvE shooters.Original Review:I wrote a whole bunch of stuff and then checked "allow comments" and steam deleted all of it. Basically, I don't regret my purchase, but I don't recommend you spend your money on it right now. $30 USD is too much for the too little content there is and that has been added. Your mileage may vary, but the four main issues are bad performance (reported, didn't experience it personally), bad servers, lack of consistent content updates, and low player numbers. At launch there were over 16,000 people and now on average there are less than 1,000 per month.If you're interested in this game I recommend you wishlist it and just pop in regularly to see how the development is going. This game is a paid early access that should have been a free open-beta. I want this game to succeed because for a time I did enjoy playing, but now I just can't justify playing. It just feels like a waste of my time. But I'll be keeping my eye on it and hoping that everything goes the way the developers have said they wanted it to.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest review. On paper, this game sounded fun and come on, Starship Troopers? Haven't we all wanted an overwhelming swarm of bugs to kill, type of game?First off.. Performance. The game looks DECENT. Nothing new, nothing that exciting, but it has its fluctuations of FPS. You can tune a lot of settings but in the end, my buddy and I (Both with good PC's) just ended up cranking most of it down due to FPS drops, mainly in large scale fights. The end game battles will tank FPS to <60 and my buddy said he hit 10 at one point.Next up.. Gameplay. I hate it say it, but there just wasn't much to do. You run around the map with no coordination and janky objectives. There doesn't seem to feel like any cooperative elements other than everyone go gun-ho on bugs. Which sounds fun either way, but it really isn't. The "special abilities" of the classes don't work half the time (Jetpack will just hover you in the air 1m off the ground and you don't go anywhere). The support was really the only useful mechanic for the heal.The building aspect felt awkward. There wasn't much to build and everything felt like pre-built and you just had to left-click to put the structure. Everything breaks in seconds, and you find that the only real structure elements you end up using are the ones already in the base that don't get destroyed. Felt like an added gimmick rather than a fun tactical element for a base defense.Lastly.. End game battles are a lag-fest to even enjoy. It just wasn't.. fun.Overall.. It IS EA at time of this review, I get there isn't much in the game now, but it didn't feel worth it enough for my buddy and I to enjoy. We did refund the game.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment I can only recommend to Starship troopers fans. The early access is boring, missions are quick. You come to objective, build some walls and then defend it after some timer is done you get to dropship and leave. Game is co-op shooter with building elements.Gameplay: You shoot your way through bugs to get to game objectives. After finishing objectives you get into dropship to finish the game. If you die you will respawn. The shooting has some nice sound effects. Dying individually does not have any impact on your team or game. There is respawn timer that gets you back fast into game if teammate does not revive you.Building system lets everyone build base from several available wall options on a grid based zones. The walls spawn from thin air and disapear into thin air after being destroyed by bug enemies. While the final defense goes on players can also repair the walls out of thin air to instantly spawn walls back. There are almost no restrictions on how many walls can player spawn. (The restriction is mostly the space). The base as result looks most of the time chaotically designed and it just seems like the Federation likes to waste resources for which human lives were sacrificed for. The dropships are indestructible and and withstand the horde until the timer for leaving ends. Whoever does not make it gets left behind but not really with any consequence. The bug enemies are halfway there. The most unfun enemy is the sniper bug that can shoot you down from distance without you having any chance. I played the game on veteran as the other difficulties were too easy and it seemed like you don't have to play to win. The classes give some teamplay element to the game - you can scout and evade enemies with jetpacked hunter. Provide extra DPS with machine-gunner (that is also a tank wth C ability) and heal teammates with engineer. Too bad you get easily respawned, because then the healing would have some weigth. It seems like everyone in team does whatever and runs around map without any lead.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mobile Infantry offers many job opportunities for all sorts of youth. Not only does service guarantee citizenship, but serving your part against the ever approaching bug-menace is a part of your 'moral obligation' as a human being. When you ship off, you will come back to your neighborhood a hero or in a hero's casket. But one thing is for sure, all your other friends will be either doing the same or doing the same exact thing they did out of primary education, twiddling their thumbs, wishing they had basic access to all the benefits of citizenship. But you? You had the audacity, the integrity, commit, honour and strength to risk body, limb and soul. Mobile Infantryman kill and are killed. That is what we made for. But ask yourself, do you really want to live forever? Anyways, we're dropping in t-minus sixty seconds!I played this on a whim with some friends, knowing fairly well that this was a game for people exactly like me and them. The result was entirely predictable, it was an incredible experience. After a few casual games, I was told "all the real fun is on the hardest difficulty where everyone actually tries." This was true. The game was actually so perfect, an absolute success in every level of communication and competence, as well as people having a light, fun time... but not only that, the tension was at an all time high. A friend and I more or less held a wall by ourselves against an endless onslaught of bugs and it really felt like we were at the end of our rope, which had already become as thin as the wire.Yet, we made it to the end and miraculously, every single person made it aboard the evacuation ship. A feat that would have been great to witness (I hope, sincerely, someone recorded it and its up somewhere on youtube without our knowledge for the benefit and entertainment of others), but to experience it? It has been some many years since I last had an experience in multiplayer that was as *perfect* as this.Especially as we waited for the last two people to board, one of them being a friend of mine, as he had escorted someone back from the grave to the evac point. The bugs were literally at our heels the entire game and somehow, by pure confidence, conscious application of game logic, competent teamwork and communication (neither too loud, too much or too little) - everyone did their jobs and came home.We had a job to do and we all did our part.So much so, much like any actual Mobile Infantryman, I hold onto the glory of this experience but dread ever soiling it with another attempted run. I have not played the game since, for some reason, but this experience alone was worth being a gamer in general and that match was worth this game's price times ten. Should you play this game? Even if its just for a day or a few hours?Yes.Its existence is bound to be brief in the ever changing, drastically competitive market of gaming, but this is an example of a rough gem that's polish is best experienced in the hand. Rather, this game is a gem yet to be mined and perhaps, it will never be mined and processed fully. But Starship Troopers, an IP that people are fiercely loyal too, beyond just memes (as well as being a book that is a mandatory read in most western militaries, having been the original source of Somalians being called "skinnies" during the Black Hawk Down incident, a reference not to the famine but the "skinny" alien race in the book) but also an icon in media to the point it has developed its own inherited cultural memes in media (the movie itself, being one of the most misunderstood adaptions of hollow-masculine military mannerbund and casual fascism alongside American Psycho) that its existence as interactive media is just utterly necessary. This is far from the Starship Troopers games we always wanted, but its certainly a game we deserve (don't get me wrong, this punches way above its weight class regardless in terms of actually being a game with game mechanics that are genuinely fun) and the loyal fans of this IP have loyally given the devs what they in turn, deserve. Games like this prove that soul is more important than AAA development cycles without it.I'm doing my part. Also, Team Ifrit every time, btw. ♥♥♥♥ everyone else."I'm from Buenos Aires and I say, kill 'em all!"

The base building is so unique and you can tell that there's something really special there if they develop it. The absolute CHAOS of boarding the exfiltration ships is something I've never seen in any other game (Titanfall included). The game is fun, but it's short lived. The bones are there and this really could be the Starship Troopers game we have all always wanted. It's just not quite there yet. But a little TLC and this game is a contender for game of the year and I mean that.  That being said, for an early access game that's 3 days old, this game is fun! There's not a ton there yet but it has so much potential. It is a beautiful game that Offworld can either nurture or strangle depending on how they handle the next few months. I put my money down because I wanted to let them know that this is the kind of game I want to see. This could be something really impressive, but it needs work. Offworld has a lot to do, but if they do it, this is cult classic worthy of the Starship Troopers name.
