_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:Many changes have been made since my original review.  Sadly, almost none of them are positive changes, and the dev's naked disrespect for their customer base has been made clear.The devs migrated the game from UE4 to UE5 and did a terrible job.  Performance, while a bit janky before, is now unplayably bad unless you have a high-end machine (e.g. 13th or 14th gen Intel i7 or i9, Zen 3 or Zen 4 X3D AMD, and a 7900XT/XTX or 4080/4090).They also added 2 new modes (Horde and Cave Hunt).  Cave Hunt is clearly balanced only for those who have unlocked everything available and are in the leet class of players - everyone else should expect to spend most missions stuck in a corner fighting endless waves of enemies that never subside long enough to even allow 3 meters of progress on any setting other than easy.It doesn't stop there, though.  Now they are also force-installing Epic game services with no opt-out ability.  Whether this is to help increase their lobby sizes by forcing cross-play between the services, or it's to help Epic by allowing them to mine your Steam info doesn't matter.  It seems that most players (or at least the majority of the vocal players) don't want this.  For me, I have no desire or intention of sharing my Steam data with Epic and no need or desire to play with those who are exclusively using Epic.  I have plenty of friends on Steam who have the game - if I wanted to play with the 4 friends I have on Epic (who are also already on Steam) I would have bought the game on Epic.  I'm a little surprised that Steam would allow this to be forced on their users without some kind of opt-out ability considering this is not an Epic exclusive and does not require Epic to be played.As of now I can NOT recommend this game at all.  If you *must* have it, and/or have some need to support devs that clearly don't care about their customers, buy it some place where you can get a key for no more than $10 or so - and that's only if you're OK with all the caveats listed above (and below).  Otherwise, spend your hard-earned money pretty much anywhere else.To my friends who have bought this game based on my recommendation I offer my sincere apologies.ORIGINAL REVIEW (this is also still valid as of the above update):I'm doing my part.This is a tentative recommendation.  Would you like to know more?The game, as of right now, is pretty messy and needs a LOT of love and attention.  Welcome to EA.  It does, however, do a decent job of capturing the chaos and confusion expected from a bug fight in the Starship Troopers universe.  Beyond the obvious things like the need for polish and more content, crash fixes, etc., the biggest thing that will probably frustrate new players the most in early play is the fact that you will probably die (often) for seemingly no reason - even if you don't want to live forever.  Usually what got you was a bug, but the bug will have seemingly come out of nowhere, without warning.  Just so you know - that bug came out of the ground right behind you (immediately after you turned away) and insta-killed you.   There is no sound made when the bug is erupting from the ground, and the squeal they make at seemingly random times is never made during this surfacing or when they immediately attack after they surface.  Stick with someone else and cover each others' backs - try not to be alone...ever.  If it's not that, then you might be at the top of a tower and be killed by the bugs attacking the base of the tower.  Or you might just die for no discernible reason - haven't quite figured the supposed causes of these kind of deaths yet (although I'm pretty sure at least some of these are due to the bombers).  The next problem for new players (well, actually the first, but this comes and goes pretty quickly) is that the training scenario does not at all prepare you for what the actual game play is like.  You'll learn how to use your build/repair tool and how to do basic resource harvesting - that's it.  The insanity you'll face in the 'real' game will probably be a bit of a surprise the first time you drop in - even if you're familiar with the source material.  Next up is voice comms.  Since the typical game play loop has everyone breaking off into squads and building/repairing/defending different areas of a base, not knowing if something being said applies to you and your group (or not) requires having enough time in-game to have a handle on the base layout and build/defense strategies that have been ironed out by those with more playtime.  It is nice that there are both local and team-wide voice comms - that seems to help keep the team-wide comms channel from filling with chatter by players that are near each other - but not always.  One final note:  as of now, the movement and gun play feel pretty uninspired and make the game feel, for lack of a better descriptor...generic.  Hopefully, sprucing that up is on the to-do list - after fixing the silent/stealth bug problem.If you want in, and you're OK with the above, then it may be worth considering diving in now - the game most likely isn't gonna get cheaper until it's first post-release sale.

_childDocuments_.review: There seems to be a lot of bitterness and contempt for this game all of a sudden, prompting this review as a response. This game is in Early Access, has a smaller budget, and is considerably smaller in scope than some recent releases, but I still like it and feel it deserves a chance if you have the time for it. Based on the Starship Troopers movie, but with less fascism, this is a budget FPS co-op game. It's got heart, 16 player missions, and I haven't been dropped from the servers or hard crashed during extraction. No micro-transactions either!And yes, people still play this. US servers still has a game available on Normal and Hard available within like 30 seconds on the weekends, I don't know where y'all are playing from, though.Unfortunately, unlike HD2, it doesn't measure ammunition by magazines, the only thing I really hate.A co-op FPS in Early Access currently undergoing serious revision to its classes, but with good core gameplay and design. It incorporates a lot of popular elements like being able to party up with players as a group, contextual pinging, and RTS style base building with randomly occurring side objectives.There are 3 16 player game modes and a more classic co-op FPS 4 player mode. The 3 modes are Advance and Secure, Horde, and ARC mode. The 4 player mode, Hive Hunt, is more of Left 4 Dead/Deep Rock sort of thing where you go on an expedition, fight past hordes in corridors, and set some bombs before making a heroic escape as everything explodes. I'll be focusing more on the 16 player modes since that's frankly the main reason it stands out from its competition.All 3 of the 16 player modes mix combat with base building, with players being split up into 4 squads and having the choice of 3 classes (as of time of writing) for the match. The 3 classes currently are:You have an overall XP level, everything productive in a mission generates XP. The classes also have their own levels and unlocks. Unlocks are sequential - overall ranks unlock cosmetics, colors, helmets, as well as higher difficulty levels. Class levels unlock equipment for that class, in a predetermined sequential order. No battlepasses or 'war bonds' or whatever.Gating the harder modes behind levels may seem silly, but you want AT LEAST the first weapon unlocks for each class before you start trying to fight the hard mode hordes.The 16 player modes involve a complicated dance of building up an initial base, gathering resources, using those resources to get resupply and build defenses, and shooting an amount of Arachnids that would make the Earth Defense Force proud."But wait, that sounds like RTS gameplay!" Indeed! That's what makes this whole thing interesting. You all have to juggle between the responsibilities of resource gathering, combat, rushing to randomly spawning objectives, and not dying. It gives me good memories of C&C Renegade, Natural Selection, or more recently what I saw of Silica.Gameplay is straight co-op FPS, however. You pick a class and squad for the match, get dropped off on a weird alien planet, and soon a voice over the radio yells at you to go somewhere and build something. A variety of bugs soon comes along to keep you entertained. With murder.There is no overall commander, or even a squad lead, though you all have local and team wide voice chat. Your performance as a squad mainly determines who gets the 'most efficient squad' listing at the end. Your squad mates are highlighted but you won't be punished or anything for running around with others. Succeeding, especially on harder difficulties, requires you to read the situation, keep a diverse role composition, and at least some coordination in difficult moments to survive. Side objectives can spawn mid-mission, usually either an additional "mine ore" objective, killing an amount of arachnids at a location, repairing generators, or boosting a signal. The rewards vary - extra resources for your base or for mission progress, lowering the threat level and giving you a breather, or rocket launchers. God, I love rocket launchers... Failures don't have any penalty except for the "High-Priority Threat" missions, which always results in a threat level increase if you don't do it.There are also mutators for Advance and Secure and ARC modes on Normal and Hard difficulties, a random assortment of minor to moderate gameplay changes that switches up every hour. This range from slight changes like "More grenades for everyone" or it can be a nightmare of "ELITE ARACHNIDS AT MAX ALERTNESS, ALL HORDES ALL THE TIME". Horde Mode and Hive Hunt are unaffected.Attack and Secure revolves around you attacking territory, building a base to defend it, and moving on. You get dropped off, are told to find/build a mobile HQ, hold it for some objectives, and move on to another area to do it again. After enough shooting and hooting, the shuttle comes along and you run to it as bugs chase you. Sidemissions and mutators add complications, but this is a pretty fun mode to play with your brain at low activity on easier difficulties.Horde is very static and time limited - you can only build and repair fortifications and turrets between waves, and you only have the one location to fight and defend at. If you lose health, you can be revived indefinitely, but no one can respawn. You auto revive if the wave ends. Bugs do more damage, get faster, and have more health over time. You have to last 10 waves before the shuttle comes to get you. You still get side missions, along with the threat level penalties and rocket launcher rewards! Incredibly stressful on hard mode.ARC Mode revolves around you defending the... well, ARC. You still explore the map as in Attack and Secure, but everything revolves around the outpost. You still get a Mobile HQ and Blue Space Rocks to build your defenses, but mission progress is contingent on you getting the Yellow Space Gas. You have to juggle mining blue rocks for resupply and defence, and getting the yellow mission critical gas to finish the mission. The Side missions also pop up to complicate things. Maybe I'm unlucky, but I swear the Gas Refinery is always in the single most awkward place on the map, every time... Once you get enough Space Gas, the bugs get all mad and you have to hold off a horde for a set time before fleeing into space on the shuttle.There is room in this world for Helldivers 2 and this game, they do different things. While this game is still pretty early in the EA lifespan, it has good core gameplay and an interesting mix of offense and defense based gameplay. Guns are fun to use and meaty sounding, class abilities make a difference. You don't need to be super sweaty or  on mic if you don't want to, and with 16 players you can blend in and be part of the crowd or try to be a hero to your squad, as you like. Easier difficulties are chill, higher difficulties require effort. You can join mid mission or leave mid mission, there aren't huge penalties. Chill. Shoot bugs.

Every encounter with the bug aliens becomes a delightful puzzle to solve, and the satisfaction you feel when you hit that Bugussy dead on is indescribable!The developers have done a remarkable job in designing the Bugussy mechanic. This level of detail showcases the thought and effort put into the game's design. The Bugussy is the ultimate reward for players who are willing to push their limits and master the art of bug-slaying.But the Bugussy is not just a tool for victory; it's a source of pure joy! The adrenaline rush that courses through your veins when you successfully take down a massive bug alien by targeting its Bugussy is unparalleled. It's an incredibly satisfying experience that keeps you coming back for more, striving to improve your skills and tackle even greater challenges. Starship Troopers: Bug Assault is a masterpiece of aggressive gameplay and bug alien warfare. The inclusion of the Bugussy as a central element in combat adds depth and excitement, making every battle an exhilarating test of skill. _childDocuments_.review: the game still isnt bad but doesnt perform very well. some issues with gameplay.weapon ranges are a joke because you either use standard bullet weapons and have damage dropoff but can still damage enemies beyond max range or you have to be at nearly point blank range to actually use epulse weapons because their max range is hard. they literally cant hit anything beyond this range. so if you forget their max range you will waste alot of ammo as the game does not remind you in any way that your hitting max range but not the target.weapon damage also feels like a joke. with the new armor system being a simple 1-5 system a blue mark shows up when your not penetrating it but when your using a pen 5 weapon why am i getting the blue mark against the standard warrior. then theres the fact a 200 damage weapon needs to hit a warrior 5 times with crits in order to kill it. the standard morita does ~50, and i know it kills warriors in less than 20 hits. the numbers do not line up. there is a new clan system added with a max size of 30 people. why is it so small? _childDocuments_.review: Memes and fanboy-ism aside, this game is pretty well done but it would probably be a good idea to get an anti-griefer system in place if there is not some hidden one already.2 simple suggestions, -  Deconstructing should have a cool down timer. Maybe 3 buildings and then you have to wait 3 minutes until you can deconstruct the next one.- Team killers should damage themselves along with the team damage they do. If they manage to get 2 team kills, they get insta-killed with no rez timer so they have to wait out an extended respawn timer at least.That said, i only saw one person doing either of these things in about 6 matches total across both the instant action and the more tactical ARC mode and they either stopped doing it quickly or maybe they were just REALLY bad at the game.For the most part, people are being very fun to play with and there was actually someone running a soundboard over voice chat at key moments in the defense that added to the epic-ness of the firefight in a not actually annoying way.The asking price for the amount of game play you get here is more than fair.Other than the enemies, i didn't encounter any actual bugs myself.This is a great game to play with a group of friends, especially after you all hit level 5 to unlock the more tactical mode where fireteams can take on different objectives.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thrilled to see this awesome game getting so much love right out of the gate on Steam. I fully expected it to launch to Mixed (at best) reviews, given that it's one of the buggiest (heh) Early Access experiences I've ever played. That in mind, I'm cautiously recommending this game to folks that don't mind a raw experience, but I suggest that others wait for a few content/polish patches before "doing their part." I'll plan on changing this to a thumbs up after that.All this in mind, here's my Day One review.Bugs abound both literally and figuratively in Starship Troopers: Extermination, a 16-person objective-based horde shooter that pits you, the outgunned, outmanned, outnumbered, out planned United Citizen Federation against the unending Arachnid Empire. Releasing into Early Access on May 17th, ST Extermination successfully captures the 1997 cult classic film’s sense of overwhelming. Really, there were moments during each of the dozens of roughly 20-minute missions I played where I felt gleeful despair at how innumerable my long-legged foes were and how impossible our odds seemed. But are these frequent moments of frantic joy worth the occasional moments of agonizing exasperation when ST Extermination’s bugs get a little too creative in the ways they’re trying to kill you (e.g., error reports, black screens, etc.). First and foremost, the story. Just kidding! We’re here to kill bugs, and you don’t need a plot for that. What you do need are guns... lots of guns, and three classes, each with a special ability. Hunters have jetpacks that come in handy when you'd rather fly than die. Bastions have a comically short deployable circle shield that bugs, God bless ‘em, are too stupid to step over. And Operators have a little med bot that’ll heal all your bleeding buddies. And trust me, between the stabby bugs, the bullet bugs, and the big bertha bugs, you’ll bleed a lot. Together, your team of 16 will actually split up immediately into smaller squads of four, and from there you’ll stumble your way through a variety of objectives, beginning with capturing a point only to be promptly crushed to death as thanks, to mining ore that you’ll use fund your big ol’ bug base. That’s right, each mission culminates in an all-out assault on a base of your making, so be sure to coordinate tower defense efforts with your team (personally, I found myself partial to the electric fence.) After that, respawning stops and it's a mad dash to the extraction point. Fun!So, all that to say the intense combat in STE left me impressed, as did the varied objectives. And, while the base building mechanics feel a tad clunky, I'm really happy they’re here, as the game would feel a bit bland without them. As for world, I encountered what felt like one big map over and over again and sometimes at night, though Offworld Industries have said they’ll add more map variety, not to mention new enemies and boss fights during Early Access. But before they spend a second on adding bugs, I beg of thee, please! Hire a handful of QA exterminators to cull the bugs we don’t want from this otherwise enjoyable title. I got black screens, I got stuck, I had server crashes at the very end of missions that resulted in zero XP. My goodness does this game need some polishing. That said, I was happy at how little lag I encountered on Epic, considering all the visual chaos. Speaking of visuals, STE is a pretty game if you find the time to wipe aside all the bug guts from your screen and pause to enjoy the arid environments and starry sky boxes. It also sounds great and sports a fun soundtrack that’s reminiscent of the beloved franchise. In the end, Starship Troopers: Extermination is the exoskeleton of a fun game that’s currently more chrysalis than it is crystal. And, because it’s a tad content poor and frequently flirts with the bad kind of bug, I don’t currently recommend it at its starting price of $25. However, with a little polish and a few patches, I can definitely see STE blossoming into a beautiful, blood-soaked butterfly (which is perfect seeing as how flying enemies are in fact on the roadmap).I’m giving ST Extermination a subject-to-change aggregate MEGA score of 3.2/5 (full scoring breakdown available in video form) and am happy to answer any questions you have about the game or my review.

Your get everything else that's coming to the game for free so its worth while investment just for that.Check out the gameplay video on Youtube for real good idea what gameplay is like .If your not one to by Early Access games I would at least recommend keeping this game on your radar till full release.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is nearing the end of early access, the devs' work is very serious and the game is progressing quickly.I started the early access from day one, there were ups and downs, I had doubts about the skills of the devs, some of their choices were very questionable but they knew how to listen to the community and each time proposed something better.Today, the game is very good, and if it were to be released in an official version, it would certainly receive very positive reviews.The gunfighting is very good, the trooper classes are very varied, and there's something for every taste. Burn them, snipe them, explode them, shoot them, atomize them, do as you please, but shoot'em all.Strategy is important, some players act as shields, others as logisticians, others as cover, everyone has a job to do, and if everyone does it well, then the game is won.The atmosphere of the movie is respected by the devs and also by the players.I like to see the solidarity between players in the game, which is something that had disappeared in co-op games, where everyone plays for his own gain.In Starship Troopers, players play together, and when it's time to leave the base for extraction, players often move together, respawn each other and sometimes even go back to save one of our brothers.That alone makes this game unique.The game is very beautiful, the maps are more varied, at the beginning of early we complained a lot about the maps that were too few.The only negative point is the smoke that can come out of the ground or from explosions creates a huge flash every time you shoot, and this really hurts the eyes. I hope this will be improved, as it can bother a lot of players.I can't get enough of it, the progression was much too fast at the beginning of the early, but the devs managed to fix that too, and today the player's evolution is perfect.The progression to unlock weapons is a little too fast for the player's rank.The evolution of rank has too little influence on the player's equipment and therefore limits the time needed to reach the best equipment level, which also needs to be improved.Even at maximum price, this game deserves to be bought and played, and the devs' work is well worth the asking price.The final version of the game offers us, in addition to everything that was already great in the game, a little story to play solo.The final version of the game is great, don't hesitate to buy it, there will certainly be other updates and DLC.

The sound design is excellent making bugs go from clanky to silent depending on where you're walking - and this will get you killed and save your life.Missions are great, base building is simplistic but excellent - you will laugh at poorly built bases which will be plentiful. It's simple to build a good base but nobody knows the rules, so you end up defending crazy areas that are subpar.Community so far is great, moreso than most shooters. _childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge Fan of Starship Troopers since I first saw it on TV around 2007.  I loved watching these squads of soldiers with limited ammo, equipment, and numbers fighting against an endless swarm of giant, ruthless, chitin armored arthropods.  It even inspired me to make a couple stop motion Lego videos based on it when i was in high school.  The more i watched it, the more I really wanted to experience this in a video game format.shortly after becoming a fan I saw there was a game released for it in 2005.  I downloaded the Demo and played it for hours (i actually didn't get the full game until i was out of college).  Not only were there tons of bugs on screen, but I loved seeing the large number of NPC troopers fighting alongside me as well.  I would spend hours fighting up Plasma Mountain just to see how many NPCs i could save by the end of the run.  True, it was not the best developed game on the market, but i still enjoyed the experience (except when i couldn't zoom in with the sniper rifles because my ATI Radeon graphics card kept giving me a black screen). When this game was first announced I was excited to see that there were people who were willing to give the IP another shot.  I was hesitant when i saw it was going to be an early release product, thinking there would be a good handful of bugs and optimization issues.  despite these fears I purchased it anyway and was not disappointed. I was actually surprised at how well it ran on my computer, No lag, no rubber-banding, there were a couple crashes but those were few and far between.  The game does well to put dozens of bugs on screen without taxing your processor.  The map they give you is big and you will spend 20-40 minutes per game running around it.  The weapons are limited but all are fun to use and sound powerful.  There are only 5 bug types at the moment and i hope to see hoppers, tankers, and plasma bugs in the future.  I think the feature I love the most is the fact that you are fighting alongside 15 other players making you feel like an army, compared to other horde shooters that limit you to a four man squad.  In this game, you are not a one-man-army, you are a soldier in the Mobile Infantry and cooperation is the name of the game.  All players must work together to transport complete objectives, set up fortifications, and lay down suppressing fire against the endless onslaught.  You may be able to hold your own for a bit, but eventually a single warrior bug will reach you and cut you down,  a single gunner, or multiple, will pin you down behind a structure, or a Grenadier will blow you straight to hell from halfway across the map.  When that happens you will be glad to have a fellow trooper nearby to pick you up...................................................... or you will be pissed because you bleed-out the second they get there and they end up accidentally saluting your body.I really look forward to watching this game develop and what other features the developers will bring to the table.

_childDocuments_.review: I had big hopes for this game. On launch it was enjoyable and the highest difficulty made for some moments requiring good teamwork to overcome the swarm. All that being said the last few updates have been painfully slow and have done more harm than good. The first mutator update broke the difficulty scaling and added stupid unavoidable mutators server wide that more often then not had me and my friends preferring to shut the game down and wait for the mutators to change to something else. The HMGs are pointless because you sacrifice two shooters for a mediocre turret that was likely built in a poor location. The caves are absurdly difficult due to how little ammo and firepower you can bring to bear with 4 people. By far the greatest middle finger is the lack of weapons, and unwillingness to make that a priority. They had a handful of guns on launch and then decided to remove half of them by making them class restricted. When a weapon shined they nerfed it like the grenade launcher and hawkeye on operator. The shotguns are useless too short range and take half a tube to kill a warrior you're better off in melee at that range and carrying the Morita. TLDR: Poor and slow development cycle that has done more harm than good.

name: Beacon Pines
detailed_description: Beacon Pines is a cute and creepy adventure set within a mysterious book. You play as both the reader of the book and its main character, Luka. Something strange is happening at the old warehouse, and Luka and his friends seem to be the only ones taking notice. Sneak out late, make new friends, uncover hidden truths, and collect words that will change the course of fate! While helping Luka investigate the strange goings-on in Beacon Pines, you’ll collect special golden charms, each with a word engraved on it. These charms can be used at certain turning points in the story to fill in a blank word and drastically change everything that follows. As the book's reader, you’ll navigate the story’s turning points using The Chronicle: an interactive story tree that branches and grows along with your choices. Exploring one set of events can unlock new charms to use on another branch, leading you to jump back and forth between entirely different versions of the story in order to unravel the mysteries at the heart of Beacon Pines.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game, it's has an incredibly charming book aesthetic where you reach points in the story that you can flip back to at any time to change key events and it will actually flip through a physical book with page numbers and all. The narration is wonderfully done as the narrator will flex her vocal range to suit the mood of the scene and it really feels like the narrator is just as invested in the story as you are as the twists and turns unfold.Alongside an incredible musical score that both helps accentuate the deeper mysteries of the small town and it's citizens. But also a really brings to life a wonderful sense of childlike exploration as the main characters play around and live their lives.I was so invested that I actually could not put the game down and finished it in two sittings over the course of one day just because of how compelling it was.It's not the longest game in the world, but every branching path somehow managed to tell an equally engrossing story that together paint the whole picture.All in all I don't actually want to go into any details about the actual story as it is better experienced than explained.Bravo Hiding Spot you've created a truly special game and I hope you'll continue your magic again!

_childDocuments_.review: Great narrative experience that lasts around 5-6 hours. It starts off a little slow, but the hook of the first "ending" grabs your attention and is a great way to enforce the narrative's overarching themes. I greatly enjoyed all of the branching paths, and the path that gets you the actual ending is enhanced by all of the what-ifs explored in the paths that end badly. Highly recommend if you like mystery stories and don't mind the backtracking. Also appreciate that the voice-over can be disabled.

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines has been an ASTOUNDING game to play! From the beautiful visuals, to the funny script, even the wonderful voice of the narrator, everything about it is wonderful. _childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a branching long form choose your own adventure game. In order to unlock the game’s true ending, it is necessary to play and fail several times. Each failed branch unlocks new branches of the story. Although you are seeing different angles of the story, the characters only really know what’s happening in the current branch. Near end game this starts to make the story feel a little muddy and unclear. But beyond that, the character art is fantastic and I think there are still some cool and impactful moments in this story.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so engaging in both story and gameplay! The charm mechanic is a really clever way to tie paths together and turn many branching paths into a cohesive narrative. Plus, the art style is adorable, and the music suits the mood at every moment. Highly recommend if you're looking for a mystery with a cute style, dark themes, and a gripping story.

Cause that entire gig of it having mutating properties (growth), everyone getting Snowgraved in nearly every "ending", on top of the apparent thing of the original town location being frozen over only has me thinking it was the games way of saying Nuclear Winter happened after some freak accident that occurred, thus leading to the town "pushing it somewhere else"Otherwise this review is more of a neural-leaning no.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game but it has some major flaws you should know before playing it:1. The decisions you make ultimately don't matter. Almost all of them will lead to "endings" which are really just dead ends. This can be frustrating because you will now have knowledge that the main character won't have, and they will then make seemingly terrible decisions which feel preventable because you know so much more about the bigger picture.2. Multiple major plot points, as well as a variety of minor plot points, go completely unresolved even after 100%ing Beacon Pines. This is notable to the point of major plot points not being discussed at the end of the game because by the time you reach the true ending, the game expects you to have brute forced each of the dead ends. Hell, there is even a major physical change to a main character which is unresolved and borderline ignored by the end of the game, which kind of comes out of nowhere. Feels like there should have been at least one more chapter to wrap things up.3. Turn off the narrator immediately, the game will feel a thousand times better once you get rid of it. Also be patient with the beginning of the game, the narrator will stop intruding every three seconds. It just takes a bit.4. The writing can be all over the place. Some moments of the game work really well and will make you tear up, but others are predictable, poorly written, or are just extended dialogue for exposition.  You don't need to tell me a character bowed while smirking when he is the only thing moving on the screen, the camera is zoomed in on their face, and he smirks obviously then bows. I'm not a three year old, I can see what's going on. A lot of the plot feels a bit forced and kind of comes out of nowhere or your character will say things way out of character or that simply don't make sense just to get the plot moving. It feels like this game was originally more of a choose your own adventure but the devs cut a ton of places where there was originally choice but they decided to make the plot more linear afterwards, which causes a bunch of scenes to feel like something is missing.5. Expect some heavy overlap with Night in the Woods, some so obvious that I'm almost certain Beacon Pines copied elements from NITW. If you haven't played Night in the Woods, play that first then come to this. It is a much better game overall and if you are going to experience Beacon Pines, it is better if you experience the source material first. Spoilers ahead about arguably stolen content: But while these cons are extremely annoying at times, and there are many more minor ones, the pros are absolutely great! Gorgeous artstyle, fantastic soundtrack, lovable and hateable characters (when they're not written poorly...), and great presentation. Additionally, this game is not for kids but captures the realism of being a kid. The main cast is a group of 12~ year olds and they occasionally curse and act a bit rude which is great! It makes the characters feel more real, something which is desperately needed due to the mixed writing quality. Definitely worth checking out AFTER playing Night in the Woods!

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines follows in the footsteps of games like Night in the Woods with its mysterious plot, idyllic small town setting, and plucky cast of characters. And while the mechanics are extremely straight forward and rely heavily on its narrative, almost visual-novel aspects, the beautifully drawn locations and catchy score seem to harken back to the whimsical point-and-click experiences of the late 90s like Kings Quest 7 and The Curse of Monkey Island. As an old fan of early adventure games, this was extremely comforting to me as it put me in a specific, nostalgic headspace that few contemporary games do these days. As others have stated, the game is a short play and feels like a short play, which I count as a positive criticism considering I was left feeling as though I could have happily enjoyed many more hours in this world with these characters. And despite its novel Charm mechanic and branching narratives, the game ultimately feels very linear and somehow less alive because of it. In the end however, the story is left opened-ended enough to invite the possibility of another game set in Beacon Pines or possibly beyond, and if we do get a sequel with Luka and his friends, I will absolutely jump at the chance to come back to this universe again.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A super cute game with enough sadness and mystery sprinkled in it to keep it interesting. A story about change and malice. The visual novel part is done very well with the branching story, while it took me only about 4 hours to reach the end; all in all it was worth it. The music is great, the twists are interesting and sort of foreshadowed at times so they work. Definitely recommend to try for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: On a sliding scale between a movie and a game, this occupies a position very close to a movie. This game could be classified as a visual novel of sorts where the core gameplay loop consists of running around in the world and talking to characters. Occasionally, you also participate some additional interactions with the objects in the room. While there are some puzzles, they are very easy, and one shouldn't buy this game with the intention of solving interesting puzzles.The game appears to be a [Choose Your Own Adventure] game where you choose branching paths in the story using cards that you collect during the game play. However, the game is actually a lot more linear than it seems. Indeed, a single branch of the story is considered the canonical ending, while the other branches are considered failures. You cannot accidentally or intentionally stumble upon the canonical branch without exploring the whole tree, since you need to collect certain cards in the other branches that will unlock the canonical branch. Thus, this game is not really a true CYOA game, but a visual novel with a non-linear narration.The cute characters might give the impression that a children's game, or a cozy game. However, this is rather a Young Adult small town mystery game. The core plot of the story is about two corporations which run the economy of a small town, getting engaged in the invention some nefarious technology. The story is gripping and is brilliantly told. I finished playing this on two sittings on a Saturday afternoon, and took me around 6 hours.The ending of the story gets slightly confusing, however. It would be nice if we had a feature recounting the events that had happened in each timeline.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful gem of a game.  The writing, art, music and narration are all spot on.  It took me around 5 hours to complete the game and get all the achievements, and every minute of it was a treat.  There are a couple of moments in the game that require a little accuracy in hitting targets with thrown objects and some mild puzzle solving, but mostly this is just a game in which you explore the "what-ifs" and visit most or all of the possibilities of a branching narrative to get an ever-clearer view of the spoopy but charming story - and ultimately help the characters save the world and get their happy ending.  Similar to the classic "choose your own adventure" novels but with a clever mechanism that requires you to visit all the bad endings to learn from them.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and got all the achievements in a single run, and i have to say it, it truly was an awesome experience. _childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game. I haven't played anything quite like it before.It's a visual novel, but with a twist - you get to make choices and manipulate the storybook. You can always go back and change outcomes, which adds a unique dimension to the gameplay. The narrator's voice is incredibly soothing and adds to the overall charm of the experience. The game is filled with exploration, puzzle-solving, and quirky characters, and the captivating art style is the cherry on top. I've never seen such a cute art style in a game before. The story is incredibly creative and innovative. I haven't read/seen it anywhere before. It is truly unique. It even moved me to tears a couple of times.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a cozy mystery game with an innovative choose-your-own-adventure storybook twist. If you love Stranger Things, this game is for you. The soundtrack is perfect and combined with the watercolour backgrounds, the game creates an atmospheric experience that will stay with you long after the book closes.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun figuring out the mystery as the story progressed, but it's more like a book than a game. Everything unfolds itself before you eventually. The true end felt rushed, and due to not really having to figure out a solution it didn't really feel like a hard-earned true ending, but I still recommend it if you like that kinda book/game genre. It's a good read with charming characters, beautiful art and an intruiging mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: this was amazing. like, I'm telling everyone how good it was. if you like story based games (think oxenfree, for example), you'll love this. perfect for a peaceful gaming experience (no quick time events or platforming or combat), but also still heart pounding due to the plot!! which, by the way, is fantastic. like wow, great job, yall. gravity falls vibes-- very cute, spooky, sci-fi/fantasy energy. the construction of the game itself is wonderful, from the gameplay to the art to the voice acting. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I thought the game was really boring. The voice acting was cringe, the characters were underdevelopped, and most importantly: there's not a modicum of player choice in it. It's very cute, and it has interesting mechanics, but the mechanics are underutilized and fall flat. The game really wants you to think you're having an impact on the story (as said by the narrator in an over-acted teary eyed voice), but this is more like a novel with pretty graphics than it is a game at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet game with a really cute art style! I went into it without looking anything up and was surprised how similar it is to Stories: The Path of Destinies (perhaps an inspiration?), which I'd highly recommend as well if you enjoyed Beacon Pines. Overall, the ending was a bit underwhelming I thought but other than that I was quite engaged and beat the game in one sitting.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying that this 'game' is more of a linear story presented in game format. There's nothing wrong with that, but despite the ability to run around there's story beats that you hit in order. It follows then that the interesting part of this was the story, and it did a very good job of presenting it. The main gimmick is that it works similar to a choose your own adventure book, where you get set options that you can pick as things go on. You unlock these options by exploring and finding (or having them be given) in other paths. By its design, you'll find yourself going down most paths just to unlock the final ending, but in doing so you get to reach an ending each time, each time giving you parts of the whole story.This means that you will learn of the big twists throughout the game, but the characters won't always know them. I counted 3 to 4 big twists in the story, some of which I figured out but some I didn't until it was spelled out for me. Overall I'd say this was a great 4 hour experience and well worth the (very reasonable) price.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: 10 / 10, and that's really just it.I picked up this game at complete random, and immediately fell in love with this short but sweet, cute and creepy little story game more than I've any other. I cannot recommend this game enough - It's no open-world, 200 hour thriller, but it's the most engaged I've been in a story thus far.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This was a good game. It was interesting playing through the paths to get fragments of the truth and piece together the story. A good mystery game with a bit of drama, it was at times both dark and childish with some humor.I finished it in 5 hrs with a break halfway through. It worked fine with a controller. No bugged achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Such an engaging mystery game made cozy. It is a "Choices matter" type of game, but you are allowed to explore multiple story progressions at any time and even if you encounter a bad ending. So that eliminates all the pressure that comes with these types of games. Through exploration of multiple plot lines, you also gain a lot more background about the whole story.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Dark, charming, and beautiful little game that you can tell the developers put their heart and soul into. _childDocuments_.review: This game reminded me of the old point-and-click adventure games that I grew up playing, but with more storytelling in between. _childDocuments_.review: SPOILER-FREE REVIEW!--------This game delivers an extremely cute and cozy atmosphere that alone almost carries it to a "would recommend" category for me. It looked like an interesting take on the "choices matter/choose your own adventure" genre, so I was excited to try it out at some point when I got it in a Humble Bundle last year. The story itself, as well as the characters, are fine - some might even say great! Unfortunately, the constant swapping between timelines to progress the story in a game that is already so short left me with very little time to just sit in one and get immersed with it. By the end of the game, I had an idea of what was going on, but very little emotional investment to associate with it. Maybe this is also why I felt so underwhelmed by the ending, but it seems like many of the other negative reviews also agree with this sentiment (for other spoiler-y reasons that resonated with me).I'm sure some of the things I have mentioned were completely intentional by the developer, and from the looks of the reviews I am in the minority of people that feel this way. I'm glad that they were able to find success and an audience that enjoyed their content.This all being said, here is my verdict: If you are looking for a "move-and-interact" adventure with a "what if Gravity Falls made a less good spin-off and turned it into a game" story, this might be worth getting on a sale! Otherwise, I'd personally recommend a lot of other titles instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. The art is cute, and the story is fantastic. It's a way darker story than I expected, which I loved. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, sort of a twist on a visual novel. You'll get pretty much every one of the endings baked in just by the way Beacon Pines works. It's a bit short, I finished in about 6 hours, though I haven't gotten all of the achievements yet. I enjoyed my time in Beacon Pines.The narrator has an amazing voice, and she knocks it out of the park. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little game and a great way to go about a visual novel. It is like a visual novel+ or 2.0 or something. Great characters, a great storyline, and Narrator--you are amazing and were the perfect choice for the role. The music is also beautiful and the art style is also fully my kind of thing. I also love how the game is set up/organised. Like, there is no having to hit autoskip and all to get 'all the endings' like in most visual novels-- it is very cleverly done.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game. Definitely one of the most impactful games of this year. Very few games can make me tear up and cry. This was one of them. The story is wonderfully crafted, beautifully told with great writing, and the characters really pop out. The art style is gorgeous as well as the presentation. 9/10 for me. Excellent game, you will not regret buying it. There is a plothole or two in the game in regards to a certain character and a certain type of event, but maybe that’s my own perception. Maybe we’ll get a second game that goes into depth with that more. I can’t really hold that against this game. Specifically: SPOILERS AHEAD, WARNING!—The mouse in the old beacon pines. He’s really mysterious and we don’t know much about him or why he exists. —The dream sequences are either foreshadowing events to come or metaphorically telling the player of events and emotions Luka is feeling. I’m not sure what to think of them, but it made me think Luka somehow time traveled back to greet his younger self with the help of the mouse (and possibly the source) to warn him of things and also show luka how he could change for the worse. Feel free to let me know what you guys think tho, cuz otherwise this is a perfect game~ ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is charming, well-written, and well narrated. It's engaging right from the start, and I thought the core mechanic of tracing out the different possible branches of the story was clever and well implemented. Luka and the gang are so gosh darned likeable and I enjoyed getting to know them for the past several hours. The love that was put into this game really shows, as there's a lot of polish and attention to detail here. Thanks for melting away a quarter of my 30-hour train trip!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It´s a pretty nice little game, it is more interactive than other novel type games but on the other hand also very short and has imho little replay value.You´ll probably discover most what it has to offer in about 6-8 hours of playtime (on the 3rd hand there might be something said for games you can actually finish fast...) It has overall a bit of a stranger things feeling to it but much much less horror - you explore the story in treebranches and by discovering differnt actions in differnt branches you forward the story overall. I think they do that branching quite nice and I never had to replay a part in a way that would have made the thing boring but it might be difficult if you pause the game for a longer time.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable and engaging - looked forward to this since I saw PlayFrame play the demo and backed the Kickstarter. Often had me figuring out a mystery *right* before the reveal of the answer, which felt immensely satisfying. Because of the nonlinear design a lot of character development happens in "bad ends", meaning a lot of the best scenes happen outside of the path to the "true ending" and are never experienced by the characters on that path, which weakens the ending a little bit - but it's still a heartwarming cap to a fantastic experience. 100% recommend.I will note - for those who want more of a "choose your own adventure" experience, despite the design of the game involving branching paths, you often get the charm you need to continue in a bad end, meaning you'll often get to forks where there's only one option leading to a bad end, which gives you the charm you need to get a better outcome. This means that despite appearances, there's actually quite a specific order you will go through the game - there's only one or two places where you can choose which of multiple endings to experience first, and you have to go through nearly every path to complete the game regardless. It works very well for the story it tells, but if you're hoping for a true "choose your own adventure" experience where you have the chance to get the "true ending" from the start - that's not what you'll get here.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Well this game took a turn I didn't expect, lol. So yeah, it's a mystery sort of game in a small town with branching paths but it's less meta about it as opposed to something like Zero Escape. Key word being less, not none at all. The characters are really cute and characterization is strong for the most part. However, it wraps up the mystery fairly abruptly all things considered and to make it happen, they make some characters act a bit too cartoonish for my tastes.So yeah, overall I highly recommend it. It has a lot of heart and it's a lot of fun to see in action. Seeing whatever wacky curveballs they throw at you is part of the fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines' whole mechanic is that it's a choose your own adventure type story. Most of the options you pick end badly, but there is a "true ending". If you play this, the only thing I'd say is it gets frustrating when you've got to go back and find a "charm" which will basically give you one of your choices, which caused me to quit after about an hour and a half because I got so frustrated. But hey, maybe you have more tolerance for that kind of thing. Luckily the game is built so you don't have to redo much when you pick the "wrong" choice.I did google the "true" ending, and my best way to describe it without spoilers is "anticlimactic". But overall it's a good game. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: It might be a bit early, since there's still some of November and all of December left of the year but Beacon Pines is looking to be my GOTY. _childDocuments_.review: Lovely artstyle, hearthfelt story and a bittersweet true ending (it really is a story about change).Played it in one sitting, while getting over a nasty cold.Only negative I can say, is that the major gimmick, Turning Points was underutilized. Most of them only have two options and usually you are only given a new path forward towards the end of another. So there's very little jumping back and forth.You just go forward until you run out of ground and are given a 'password' that lets you resume another thread.I think the branches could have been more convoluted and intricate, maybe even looping back or crossing over into another storyline.Also, a single charm should have had multiple uses and open more than one path. As it stands, besides a couple exceptions, most charms only have a single purpose.

_childDocuments_.review: On the macro level, Beacon Pines has a good story and characters, wonderful art style and soundtrack, and on-point comedy beats that provide an engaging experience for most of it. The player has enough agency through some miniquests and dialogue options to immerse them in the story, though I would caution that At the micro level as an avid reader and "story rich" game enjoyer, completing this game was like reading a nice 20-chapter book that has had chapters 18 and 19 removed. It sets up so many interesting concepts that could be explored in great depth (specifically, ), but answers practically none of them, prioritizing following the ending climax abruptly by an (otherwise very satisfying) epilogue that is so definitive in tone, I experienced whiplash at the sheer amount of previously setup concepts ignored. There is an artistic, poignant way to leave open-ended questions for the reader (player) to answer in a story even upon finishing it, but this game does not accomplish that, or even give enough clues for the readers to speculate on the author's (developer's) intent.Review is positive, as I enjoyed the other aspects of the game, and the above most likely isn't a breaking point for the majority of the audience here.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It's definitely something else. A sit-back-and-relax kind of game for sure, it's a weird (but immensely interesting) mix between a visual novel, an RPG, and a light puzzler. Heavily story-focused, it has a choose-your-own-adventure style, but with a radical twist. When I was a kid, I used to read the choose-your-own-adventure books, and I kind of felt like the book wasn't truly finished until I had read every possible ending. Because of that, I often employed many bookmarks and placed one at each disambiguation, so that I could go back to it once I'd reached an ending branch. Now, in this game, you actually have to do something similar in order to grasp the full story and reach "the true ending". It's done in a really smart way, and in spite of what one might think if one were told all of this beforehand (I went in blind), it's not repetitive at all. They've actually managed to find an incredibly efficient way to pull this off, and it's engaging all the way through.Story-wise, the game is pretty interesting and fun. You want to know what will happen, how things will unfold, and how to fill in the blanks that can't be found in the branch of the story you're on. You slowly unravel the mystery, with some very cool plot-twists along the way. There are a couple of flaws, but they are mere nitpicks (the main example is that there's a very easy way to reverse some negative consequences that happened on the true ending, and yet they don't; it's a bit more "realistic" that way, but it doesn't really make sense inside of the story; you'll get what I mean once you see it through). In any case, that's really small, and the story is great overall.Game-play wise, I've already mentioned the most relevant aspects before, but I'll add that it all works smoothly. Puzzles are very simple, they move the story forward, and keep you engaged. Walking speed is somehow perfect; you never once feel like you're going too slow here. I didn't feel the need for a map to move from location to location at all during the game. Areas aren't big, and like I said, you move fast enough.Soundtrack and especially, voice acting, are amazing. I can't praise the narrator enough. She is outstanding. Every phrase, every word, they all convey the exact impression and emotion required for each particular moment of the story. I presume that she is a trained story-teller, or perhaps simply a great voice actress. The story is also very well written, so everything fits. Top-notch quality throughout.Performance wise, there are no bugs, no crashes, no frame-rate drops, literally nothing to complain about. Everything is saved automatically, and there's no way to loose progress. You can go back to any part of the story you've already watched, at any moment. And the art... oh, the art is amazing. It's just great, overall. You'll likely spend quite some time during your playthrough simply contemplating the nice backgrounds, or the character models. It's all lovely.This is a solid game, with top-notch quality throughout. Everything fits. They even keep updating it: a new mini-game was added this very day (I actually found out about it a few days ago, when I finished my first playthrough, and waited to review it until after the minigame came out, so that I could also say that it was fun). I definitely can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Its not often I finish a game in under two days, but this was so gripping, the characters so charming, the art and music so masterfully done, and most importantly of perfect length that it managed. To anyone who enjoyed choose your own adventure books or just a plain ol' good mystery, I wholly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines was an incredibly enjoyable experience from start to end. I played it with a couple of my friends watching, and we had such a fun time acting out the dialogue and uncovering the mysteries of the plot. There were even scenes that tugged at our hearts and caused me to tear up a bit (though maybe that's just me!) The characters themselves are easy to get attached to, and there's plenty of witty banter and heartfelt moments to go around.I would go more into detail, but it's one of those games that you don't wanna spoil yourself on before you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It's an incredible story rich game with a uniquely beautiful and creepy atmosphere that rocked me emotionally. I loved every moment of it. It kept me on the edge of my seat while still letting me frolick and get to know the characters enough to really care about them. It's cute, cozy, scary, funny, and sad all at once in a way that I wish more games could pull off._________________❥ AccessibilityIt was a very accessible game with everything both written and spoken, no intense flashing or anything to worry about, just overall an experience I think anyone would be able to enjoy.❥ Audience/Difficulty☑ Easier Than Easy/Story Mode/New Gamer FriendlyIt's a story rich game where you play both the narrator of the book as well as the characters running around in it, while there are parts that are exploration and parts that are visual novel - there aren't really any parts that a new gamer player couldn't handle. It's very new-gamer friendly.❥ Bugs☑ No bugs encountered❥ Graphics (Accounting for different art styles)☑ An actual masterpieceFrankly, I find this game to be an actual masterpiece. It's beautiful.❥ Gameplay☑ Fun☑ Well paced☑ Meant to be explored thoroughlySome of the game play elements are so brilliant that I hope Hiding Spot makes more games that have those or very similar elements so I can experience them again and again.❥ Game time / Length☑ Short (4 - 8 hours)I played it more than once and really explored everything, and I have about 11 hours in the game. The first playthrough was about 8 hours probably and my second playthrough about 3.8 hours as I went through it mostly just to play with specific elements again, or check certain things out closer than before.❥ Music☑ Beautiful☑ OMG Buy the soundtrack. Perfection. *Chef kiss*I love listening to the Beacon Pines soundtrack❥ Price / Quality $☑ Worth full priceI would personally find this game to absolutely be worth full price. Hiding Spot deserves the support in what they do. But if you feel like maybe it's too short for the price, I have definitely see it go on sale before.❥ Story☑ Story-Rich☑ Masterpiece☑ All story, no actionThere is technically a little bit of other game place, but it's like 90+% story and I still find that totally worth every moment of it.Over all, I think if you like a story and you want to be creeped out, melancholy, overjoyed, nostalgic for childhood hijinx and better times, thrilled, savor bittersweet moments, distressed, amused, and deeply entertained - this is a game worth trying. You're not in for an especially long time, but I personally feel like you're in for an especially good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very lovely narrative-focused game. It's hard to say too much without spoiling anything, as the game is quite short, but I loved all of the characters and was fully invested in their emotional growth from the beginning of the game. I'm not sure I would agree with the visual novel tag, but cozy fits perfectly. Beacon Pines is a beautiful, cozy experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an incredible experience! Did you ever read and enjoy those "choose your own adventure" books? Maybe even with a slightly creepy/mysterious story? Oh you'll love this narrative game then!Great narration and a truly gripping story with many twists I did not expect in the least.Also cute characters!There are some games where I thought "Why'd it have to be so long?" at the end. The kinds of games where completing them starts feeling like a chore at the halfway point. This is the polar opposite!I'd gladly play more like this and was kinda bummed when it was over and completed, but it was so worth it.I take quality over quantity anytime!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable little adventure game with a unique approach to storytelling. Colourful characters, interesting plot with a few very compelling twists, good music and easy gameplay make this game a very good scratch for the itch that Night In The Woods fans might have due to a lack of similar games. Get it and you won't even notice when your 8h will disappear :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of my favorite games of all time. Everything about it is perfect to me. It has a fun structure with the storybook frame and the various words/charms to impact the story. These characters are fleshed out and nuanced – my opinions on several people changed completely as I played. The art style is literally my favorite I've ever seen. Definitely cried. I know I'm gushing, but this is honestly such a great game and worth a play!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a game that I was gifted for Christmas. I felt like trying it out for a few minutes only to find myself immersed and in a state of "one more page" syndrome. This game is very cute. It's about this hick town called Beacon Pines that was established as a farming town. The main source of income is generated from the crops which are yielded with help from the fertilizer company established by the town founder, Sharper Valentine. Things went south, an accident happened, and now a new company has moved in to help this down about town back to its feet by cleaning the fallout. Our main character is a mischievous 12 year old boy that goes on adventures with his friends, but one act of mischief changes his life forever.This game reminds me of a choose your own adventure type of book. You can control the protagonist and have him interact with the environment and objects, but it's mostly a visual novel type of deal where you can select special "charms" that are words you can use to fill in a mad libs entry in the story which changes the story branch. There is also a storyteller that comments on the endings and events as they happen, some of which are pretty grim despite the colorful and cuddly presentation. By far some of the craziest outcomes often involve death of not only side characters but also the protagonist.I highly recommend this game if you like mystery stories. The whimsical antics of the preteen characters invoke a sort of nostalgia for bygone days where all you had to look forward to during summer break was what you were going to do next rather than go to school or work or fulfill some obligation.Game took me a little over 6 hours to 100% even with taking short breaks to grab a snack. It also works great on the Steam Deck, which is what I played it on. The experience and story is well worth it, and I'm hoping that more games like this are developed in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think that I could recommend this enough. The gameplay may be simple, but the narrative kept me wanting more. It has it all. Made me laugh, made me cry, and made me feel empowered. Final straw was when I realized that I wasn't listening to my music playlist and I was absolutely enraptured by the musical score. I would probably pay money for the OST, which is not something that I even consider very often, the last time that was the case was P4.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is very cute and the story has a dark twist that keeps you wanting to know more. You collect emotions/charms that you find as you explore the different options and the world, they can be used to change the story or bad endings to help you find the true ending. I like that you can go back after you find other charms later and change past actions or endings without having to restart the whole game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super worth playing for those who love casual games, cute characters and a good story.I found the story quite unexpected and with a darker turn which was very pleasant!The artwork is adorable both characters and environments.The narrator has a reallllyyyyyy soothing voice which I personally liked a lot!The only critic I have for the game is the sounds that the characters do when the talk. I found those didn't quite match the game's visual and music. But again this might just be a personal opinion. With that said the game let's you reduce the sound if preferred.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: If you are going through rough times, just play this game.Heart warming and can make you shed a few tears along the way.Loved all the characters of this story and the cuteness of it all is just the cherry on top !I can't recommend this game enough, you do feel like you have some agency when it comes to choices as well.I cannot wait for the next game they're going to release !
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a beautiful and cute little game. A bit simple for those who want a little more of a challenge. But getting to see all the different options come about. And getting to experience each little quirk of the characters was such a joy. I wish there was more to it! I didn't want the game to end. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a cute mysterious story told in a very unique way. I loved all the characters and the way they handled the branching. It was so fun piecing together the story over time and through... some fatal errors. The art is so well done and the person they found for narration did such a good job.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Very good story with lots of twists and turns. The art style is great for the most part with the exception of one particularly ugly character >.<. The gameplay is pretty minimal, but it was honestly more than I expected from a visual novel.It's quite short, and the game is very on rails even though there are branching paths to the story.
