_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended if found on sale or in a bundle (got it from Humble Bundle February 2024 myself). It's cute, mystery visual novel. Because of the non-linear story style, it is easy to get confused and want to yell at Luka for his choices.I found they chose the right level of vulgar language for preteens to be using, and I would recommend the game for 10+.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: a fairly linear ending oriented game which allows one to do plenty of  branching missteps in order to build the world. surprisingly effective at what it does and does not overstay its welcome. do pick it up if you are on the lookout for a narrative oriented game with excellent visuals, gorgeous soundtrack and an interesting plot telling device with a well done story.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I do really like the story and the art is great! The story just kind of ends a bit too early and unsatisfyingly. It leaves me craving for more which can be taken as a compliment. The "gameplay" part in this game, The choices and the charms might fool you in to thinking that they actually affect the story but in reality the story is VERY linear and you make choices how the game wants you to make them. This mechanic though is a good excuse to provide more behind the scenes intel on the story and lore on characters. This is a sit down and listen to the story type of game, no funny business in here.I feel kind of empty now but cannot lie and say that the story didn't captivate me.edit: (changed the review to thumbs down instead of up)The longer I sit on it the more I think about the ending and "what could have been" honestly the game leaves you with a couple of plot holes and speed runs the curtain call. Can't tell if they run out of money mid production but this story is a horrible pile of potential. It could have been something extraordinary but settled for better than average. This is not a "I hate the game" thumbs down it's more like me being frustrated with it. Like a season 1 of a tv show was amazing but in season 2 they trample it which leaves you with mixed feelings.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! I loved the story, musics, visuals and -most importantly- the execution of choose-your-own-story mechanics. Beacon Pines's approach to choose-your-own-story genre solves a fundamental problem about this genre: Player being forced to play contents they already did in order to see the whole content and endings of the story. The mechanic of using "charms" and being able to play directly from turning points solve this problem.The story is ingenious. Its mystery successfully keeps the player wonder what will happen next, while complying to a branching story format difficult to execute.Musics are lovely, I especially loved the dynamicity of them. Visuals and voice acting are excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely story. It's not a literary masterpiece, but it doesn't have to be. The characters are charming and the plot twists are foreshadowed enough to make you think "a-ha!" without being overly contrived. The art style is warm and painterly and the music was surprisingly my favorite part. A great game to spend a cozy night playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.I should address that though this game is choice based some maybe disappointed with the amount of choices, I wasn't bothered by this as this game to me is more of a non-linear story, and really good story at that.If you want a game with the focus more directed to the branching paths "The Letter" maybe better for you, but if you want a game where the branching paths are used to help explore a tightly woven together story, this game is for you. It's clear the developers thought about how each paths story ties with the larger story as a whole.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! I put it off for a while because I thought it was going to be a 2 dimensional kid's game. Turns out it actually has a pretty creepy/dark undercurrent to it, juxtaposed by all sorts of adorable animals.There's not too much actual puzzling or detective work; it's very reminiscent of a Choose Your Own Adventure story with minimal choices to be made, with more emphasis on actually exploring and talking to the townsfolk. There are branching storylines, although not many - but this doesn't take away from the charm or wonderful storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A very intriguing storytelling, mystery, adventure game. Loved how the narrating felt so genuine and how they went into details within every character, showing all the connections to each character. Loved all the possible endings and the will to never give up until the end vibes. The more I played the more I was hooked into the story wanting to finish it. Extremely grateful that every question you have within the game gets answered eventually. I highly recommend this game if you love mystery storytelling games with a hint of cutesy animals as characters. The only thing I would say that i disliked about this game is that there isn't more to play, I'd love to see more adventures with the same characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable little narrative with some interesting twists, and a core mechanic done well. Felt rewarding exploring it all, though the gameplay is very simple so don't expect much in that department it's mostly about the characters and the narrative. It's also very pretty and well drawn. The characters are all super cute. Definitely give it a try
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is an excellent little game. The heart of the game is its story and characters, and both of these are excellent. While it is quite short, it uses that time well to tell a story with a good mix of lighthearted fun, quiet reflection, dark twists, and high tension. The art, music, character designs and voice acted narration are also fantastic, adding up to a great package. I think it is definitely worth a play, and I only have a few small things I wouFirstly, the game is not about making choices with significant consequences. While there are branching storylines, you progress through these in a mostly linear fashion. You continue down one until you reach the end, then go back in the timeline to try a new path. You can unlock every dialogue option and every ending with minimal exploration, so think of it mostly as a visual novel, rather than traditional "good/bad/true ending" interactive story. This branching story is excellent however, and the game uses each path to unravel parts of the mystery piece by piece, and to add tension when you jump back with your new knowledge. This allows for a story that is tightly written, rather than one that branches out wildly. Some more interactivity within each branch would have been a bonus, but understandably a lot of extra work.For the most part, the game holds a great command over tone. It knows when to ramp up the tension, and when to pull it back. However, I feel like the ending was a little too rushed, and shifted away from the tone i was expecting for an ending. I have some issues with the ending being a little rushed, but really this is only a small portion of an otherwise excellent story.Overall, a fantastic game. The very small issues I have with the game only stand out because the rest of the game is so excellent. Incredible work, give it a play if you like a good, touching, engaging story.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, from start to finish, I found this to be a really charming little game, it had me laughing at points, horrified at others and even had me crying at a few parts too.The whole thing presents itself as a story book, almost like those choose your own adventure books (with a small twist to add some gameplay and replayability) and it absolutely nailes these aesthetics, balancing out the parts that make this an actual game and the parts that make this an interactive book (or visual novel that you'd find on Steam).I would say it is a LITTLE pricey though I'd say around $15 AUD or so ($20 at most) would be more appropriate then $30 AUD, but that's just what I think, it doesn't really detract from my experience at all.All 'n all, I'd absolutely recommend this game to anyone who has any interest in playing it, 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Played it in one sitting. This game has a really good mystery and lovely characters, but makes the mistake of no keeping the continuity between timelines. Character development that happens in one time line, seems to cross over into other time lines where the characters should have no memory of those previous events happening.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable game about how small changes can have huge impacts. This game is sorta reminiscent of a choose your own adventure book, except in this case even the bad endings are part of the full story. You see the story of Luca, a young deer kid, trying to figure out the secrets and mysteries surrounding their small town. The main structure of the game is sorta visual novel like in that you are reading lots of dialogue and at specific parts of the game make choices with specific words you pick up along the way. Some of the words you get from interacting with the world as you run around town, others from the many bad endings you will find on a path to get to the true ending. I feel like the main story always had me guessing at what would happen next and there were a lot of reveals I didn't quite see coming in a very nice way. All of the characters were just joys to talk to as you delve deeper into everyone in town. I couldn't stop myself from just running around and talking to every single person in town every time I ran through. I adore the cast of characters you meet and so many of the characters really shined throughout the story. The art is gorgeous 2d sprites with lovingly crafted backgrounds and amazingly done character art while people are talking. There were plenty of beautiful locations to run around in, characters to meet, and even new expressions that really help show you all the sides of these wonderful characters. The choose your own adventure book link is strong because you really don't actually make choices that often, so you are going through a linear story for large bits of time, with segments of running around town that break it up nicely until the next choice. It is a short experience as I 100% beat the game and got all the achievements in less than six hours and I was taking my time. This doesn't detract at all from the experience and actually made it a bit nicer to go through or even re-experience again. Overall this is a lovely game with a great story, wonderful characters, and a real heart that keeps you wanting to see what happens next at every point.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing story driven game with mechanics that reminisce RPG books from the 80's and 90's - but in this case you can go back at any time to re-do some part of the stories using tokens that you can collect by exploring the game which then unlocks new branches of the narrative. The game is however pretty straightforward and linear since you'll be required to go back to branch the story as the developers intended - and by no mean this is a bad thing since the story and dialog are very well written.I simply cannot deal with how cute the characters are.If you're looking for a more relaxed and story driven narrative with some amazing visual art and cute characters, I totally recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a cute game where you explore a vibrant world and talk to unique animal characters, but it's not all sunshine and rainbows either, there's a mystery and you and your friends must figure it out through multiple branched choices and put the pieces together to find a way to get the best ending. You work alongside the narrator to place words into the story, vastly changing the outcome. This is a game where your choices matter, and making mistakes is crucial in solving the mystery. The characters are freakin' adorable, lovable, and relatable and it makes me root for them hardcore. There's a little humor, but mostly just some intense moments and a sinister plot. It's not too long of a game, about 5-7 hours maybe, but I've had a blast with it already and do recommend it greatly.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute game and engaging story for someone looking to spend a day enraptured by twists and turns. The game is by all intents a visual novel that will actually keep you thinking on the story until you finally finish it. Which won't take long as the game is about an afternoon of content and doesn't have much in the way of replay value. Make no mistake though I very much enjoyed the game and would recommend it to anyone looking for a good 6 hours spent!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute! The art was beautiful and very soothing. Choices in the story can be manipulated but I wouldn't say they matter. The narrator redirects you many times to follow different choices to get to the true ending of the game. It's really an interactive novel. The story had many fun surprises and it was enjoyable to play. It definitely didn't take 15 hours! Maybe 6?
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a game about change. It follows a straightforward-yet not straightfoward path. Most of your adventures will end in failure. But you can go back and tinker with things. Improve. Change. Despite the game forcibly ending the story and urging you to start another playthrough every time this happens, It's wonderful how narrator's few lines of lukewarm commentary lessen the impact of the abruptness of this. Narrator helps bring the life to the story throughout the storyline but I felt this is where she truly shined. Salute to your performance, Kirsten! And the art. It really didn't have to be this good. I personally feel a little repulsed by the idea of anthropomorphic animals because of my regrettable brief trip to the forbidden place that is named Deviantart(I've seen one too many wolves in Hugo Boss uniforms, diapers, and both), but the characters in this game are SO. DAMN. ADORABLE.Beacon Pines' refined execution of its core story mechanics alone makes this game stand out from other similar games I've played before. I feel they were really honest about the product they made. They could've made this as just another linear one path, no branch story that is just okay to experience. But they chose to put extra effort into making this game what it is. And that effort should be rightfully recognized. So, I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: play like a cross between an adventure game and interactive fiction. There are a host of exciting quests to do, intriguing areas to traverse and eclectic characters to meet. Exploration is pleasantly interrupted from time to time with little bits of narration from the book that is being written by the player as they make different choices and complete the game.Overall, Beacon Pines is a pleasure to play. It will take around 7-10 hours and never once feels like it is dragging thanks to the immersive narrative design and gameplay. The original combination of mechanics, engaging story with multiple paths and endings and the cute and creepy aesthetic that perfectly matches the game’s narrative all come together in harmony to create a comprehensive and satisfying experience that I wholeheartedly recommend.My full review of this game where I go into detail about gameplay, narrative and styling is available on .
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 game. I will say that the people who made this really had a certain passion and care and attention and I went in blind and was pleasantly surprised. I think my best review would be if you like fun stories and rich characters and want to just get lost in something, this probably for you. It kind of resonated with me a lot due to personal circumstance but that would vary depending on the player.On the technical side I'd say the art is pretty amazing, the sound fits well and is very pleasant and sets the mood. The voice acting is very well done. I won't review the game itself or the story as I feel that'd be spoilers. I will say that it isn't long and it is a bit linear but it is in my mind of a very high quality. If you aren't looking for 1000 generic quests to run around and do, this is a great gem of a game. I hope the people behind it make something else. I feel kind of sad it's over and that generally means it was great as I wouldn't miss a bad experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so so SO much.  First of all, the art is just stunning.  The game play mechanics are simple and user-friendly -- anyone can play this game.  The story is incredibly charming and I had so much fun exploring the various endings and getting to know all of the residents of Beacon Pines.  10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed unraveling the mystery of Beacon Pines, it was a really fun engagement.It took me a while to enjoy the narrator's voice, but it did grew on me and in the end I liked her style a lot.The game is quite short though, so I am glad I bought it while on sale, full price seems a bit too much for my taste.The style of characters is not to my liking and didn't make any sense plot-wise. The character art is very beautiful, but it's obviously a story about humans. I was half expecting that Luka would at the end wake up as a human-boy, and he just dreamed/imagined everything with animal-forms.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game oozes charm, the art style and direction are top notch, the music is great, the characters are absolutely wonderful. The story is interesting too, and though I'm not sure it's done perfectly, I still think it's one of this game's plusses. The storybook works for the gameplay, but I consistently found the writing for the narrator to be cringey and immersion-breaking. Luckily, these comments don't happen too often, but unfortunately they often happen right after important moments.All in all, 9/10, my one big gripe isn't nearly enough to make me say that I didn't absolutely love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a . The plot takes place in the city of Beacon Pines and the protagonist is Luca Van Horn, a boy who lost his father in an accident and his mother recently disappeared. The game is a web of mysteries waiting to be discovered. The main theme of the game is to advance the story until a bad ending and then try again by choosing another path. These choices are limited by  , specific words that you need to find by exploring the city's various scenarios and talking to the city's residents. Armed with Charms , the narrator will always suggest coming back at some dead end and using the new words to help Luca get out of trouble.Like a good mystery plot, the best thing is to discover it by playing, I loved the game and recommend it to anyone who likes adventures, narrated stories and mysteries. The game has a very simple difficulty and its platinum is relatively easy to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Cutesy and creepy at the same time, Beacon Pines is the story of a young group of friends trying to uncover the sinister mystery lurking underneath their cozy little town. While I don't feel like it doesn't wrap all its plot threads up very neatly, Beacon Pines kept me engaged with its charming characters and aesthetic, timeline-switching mechanic, and decent plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sweet little mystery game with some, I guess, spooky-esque vibes (I played it because so many people compared it to games like Night in the Woods and Fran Bow but admittedly I liked those a lot more). I think maybe the fact that I found out about it from people who suggested it was creepier than they expected led me to believe it would be creepier than it was. The other thing is it does a weird mix of explaining too much and not really explaining enough? Like you do find out most of the things by playing through the different options on the branches, but some of them felt like.... they were explaining a branch only "I" (the player) would have known and yet the other characters knew? I dunno. Also, I still have no idea why (the thing that happens in several play throughs) happened in the first place, like before the other thing.... also, the person writing the story seems like she's supposed to be really important but.... I'm not sure if she was? I'm gonna look this up!Okay vague. Anyway, definitely a cute and fun time with mystery vibes!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game crafted with love and passion, wrapped in an artistically fantastic aesthetic! It comes with a very unique story telling experience, although with the caveat that a pivotal story telling mechanic can end up a bit annoying Overall, this is a cozy, well thought out little game that I can definitely recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I guess I'll add my voice to the chorus of "overwhelmingly positive" reviews, if only because there's nothing wrong with it (other than maybe some excess silliness). But other reviews that led me to buy this were misleading, so I'll just say that if you were hoping for the emotional payoff or sense of place that you'd find in a game like A Night in the Woods, you're not going to find it here. At no point were my heartstrings pulled, not once did my face get misty, and the fanciful bits of the story were more of a negative than a positive. Additionally, choices don't matter, and you're not choosing your own path; you're following different branches to a preordained conclusion. Yes, it's an interesting narrative approach, but when the game says your decisions matter, it's lying.It's a solid, workmanlike bit of interactive storytelling, but nothing groundbreaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little thrown by the cheery narrator for the first 15 minutes, wondering if this was the game for me. Then the first twist happened and I was like "Ohhhh, yeah let's do this." Well-written, well-paced, with good moments of highs and lows, I really enjoyed playing this game. I will say, it is more of an interactive novel than a "game-game", but I think that's pretty obvious from the first shot of the game where is shows a book opening up lol. I want to give a separate shoutout to the ART of the game. The characters were beautifully rendered, I loved the stylization.If you want a game with almost NiTW or Stranger Things type vibes (kids exploring a tiny town and finding creepy ♥♥♥♥) that you can complete in a night, this game is for you! I'll definitely add this to my recommendations list!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: What's this? A game that's cute, has great art AND is engaging? Is that even legal? I don't know, but this game's the real deal. Once you start playing it's hard to stop, so it's a good thing it only took me 6 hours to get to the true ending.It might not be obvious, but this game is in fact a visual novel above all else. Yes, you can walk around, explore, talk to non-essential NPCs but the general structure is like in a branching VN. So you walk around and read dialogue until you find a "branching point" - there you're given a choice based on which charms you've found... and you keep going until you hit a dead end. Yes, you die in almost every bad ending. Then you go back to a different branching point and use a different charm this time.If you've played some of the newer VNs of Kotaro Uchikoshi, such as AI: The Somnium Files, you'll find that structure familiar. There are many paths and you need to visit all branches to get to the true ending. Here it's enforced in a fun way: you only have choices A and B, but choice B's charm is locked behind choice A. In other words, you have to play the branches in a specific order. This might sound bad to you, but thanks to this the narrator acknowledges what you've already seen and comments on that - and besides, the flow of the story is better.The story itself is well-written. The plot twists are properly foreshadowed and their delivery is very good - often you realise what's really happening some 30 seconds before the actual reveal; that is amazing. Combined with great visuals and pleasant, emotional music... some scenes really make your heart racing. I also feel like the young teens - the protagonist and his friends - are very believable. Not an easy feat.I have three complaints, though. One - the game uses Kickstarter characters. What this means is that there are some  conversations which would point to a character being more involved in the story than they currently are - but it goes nowhere. I don't like that. Either actually write them deep into the story or don't have them at all.Second: As you progress, you're being given interesting glimpses of something even more meta than an actual narrator of the story talking to you. Those moments are tense, a little scary, somewhat prophetic... and they also go nowhere. It felt like this is a foreshadowing of something pointing to the truest of endings, but it ends up being nothing. Disappointing.Finally - the true ending. No spoilers, but this is the kind of story in which several loose ends need to be taken care of for everything to be resolved correctly. And watching the characters carefully solve all issues that destroyed them in different routes is the catharsis that we all crave. And yet somehow here it didn't feel impactful at all - to be honest, I didn't even realise that this is what's happening until it was almost completely over.But you know what? These complaints mean nothing in the long run. The story's great. The characters are lovable. The music's powerful. Maybe some things aren't as good, but so what? It still remains an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought it was a lovely little game, and really well crafted, but the story is so short - completed in four hours, and I didn't really like some of the elements of the ending. Moreover there were a few continuity errors (Luka finding out about things in the background that we weren't given info about in that partciular timeline)- the time is really too short for £15 game (£12 on sale). Moreover the ending felt a bit rushed and the narrator (who did a great job with the voice acting) ended up telling you what to feel about the game instead of letting you just feel them. So I liked the game a lot but I don't think it was worth the money. On the plus side as I say a lot of good work was put into the game, it was really cute, I liked the art and the characters a lot- the mystery was compelling, and despite the choose your own adventure nature it never really felt like I was rehashing the same thing over and over and going long distances to places I've been before a million times to hunt for little easter eggs or branches and experiencing the same dialogue every time (one of the biggest issues I had with night in the woods). It's really a matter of taste - if you think 4-6 hours depending on your attention span is not too short to spend the money on then it's a great game! I just wish it had a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute and fun little adventure game. It was intriguing to gradually uncover the story and the secrets of Beacon Pines and its residents through different branching timelines, and I thought the plot, while simple, was pretty unique and cool. Even though there are different timelines that are determined by your choices, there is, I believe, only one true end and a bunch of bad ends that you must go through before you can get there. You are able to go back to certain plot points and make different choices by gradually unlocking "charms" as you progress through the story, until you ultimately are able to make the right choices to make it to the good end. The story is concise and easy to understand with -most- of the loose ends being wrapped up satisfactorily and no glaring plot holes. It's not too dark, nor is it syrupy-sweet. The good guys are all spunky but well-meaning while the villains, while evil, are ultimately just selfish CEOs and lackeys so it never felt too scary. I feel like it could have been longer and more fleshed-out, but it's pretty small-scale. A good way to spend a weekend or unwind after work over a few days.

_childDocuments_.review: Luka VanHorn has had a difficult childhood. He lost his father when he was six years old, and his mother mysteriously disappeared without trace not long afterwards. His Grandmother looks after him now, but those events, even six years on, still play on his mind daily.Living in Beacon Pines, a small sleepy town in the countryside, is nice, but times have been hard ever since the “foul harvest” hit and the founder of the town died. His best friend Rolo does his best to distract Luka from his thoughts with as much mischief and imagination as they can both muster. Their secret lair, affectionately dubbed “Mission Control” is there go to place to hatch up plans, games, and just to behave like inquisitive children.It isn’t long before their meddlesome ways land them in a spot of bother, and suddenly events are revealed that have a profound effect on all of their lives.Beacon Pines is a choices matter, narrative adventure, that plays out a lot like a visual novel, but has the freedom of player movement with different endings. Playing as Luka VanHorn, you control the character on screen as he travels around the town, talking to inhabitants, and completing short quests he has been assigned.The focus switches between town life and their conversations and happenings, to the storybook, where the narrator introduces events, characters, and provides lore and background to the story.When controlling Luka, you can walk around the town and talk to any inhabitant, if a speech bubble is present, and a graphic of each character appears with their conversation. Text can be skipped or the pace controlled by your keyboard or controller, making text flow at a pace that suites you. Actual conversations are not voiced, but have different sounds mimicking speech and differentiating between characters. The town itself is not that big and you’ll often be asked to meet a particular character in a certain place. It doesn’t take that long to memorize the town and know where a character will be hanging out. They usually frequent in the same places, like market place stalls, shops, or amenities like libraries. You can enter certain buildings for a change of scenery.There is no map, quest finder or hints, but they’re not really needed considering the size of the town.If a special event occurs, we are thrown back to the book where the narrator analyses the situation and may ask us to use a charm to affect events.You collect charms as you progress, and these may be picked up through encounters with characters, or by interacting with certain objects. If you investigate everything, and why wouldn’t you, they will pop up quite frequently. They are just simple everyday words that can be used to change a sentence on the storybook and send you down a different narrative.If one of these choices results in death, and sometimes this can happen hours later, you are asked to return to any of these turning points and pick a different word to see how that turns out. In my experience you mostly only have between one and three charms to use, but there were rare occasions when I had more. Beacon Pines is a very enjoyable adventure if you are a fan of reading, visual novels, or just a decent story, told in an unusual and entertaining way. It is a gentle experience, with lots of heartwarming encounters, camaraderie between friends and tons of mischief, but there is also a darker side with reflections on loss, greed, and ambition.I am not one for copious amounts of text, and although Beacon Pines does have a lot of text, it is always kept short, punchy, and entertaining, and I found myself happily following events as they unfolded on the page, like a writer penning his story for the first time.The actual writing is wonderfully written, with exciting and flamboyant use of language, which flowed expertly as to provide a riveting read. Often somber, often exhilarating, the tones were masterfully set to provide the right mood at the right time. A great deal of this, was to do with the narrator, who voices the words as they appear on the page. Spoken with feeling, and gusto, she transforms the words on the page and paints pictures in your imagination.The artwork is sublime too, with a storybook feel and a whimsical use of direction, the pages felt alive, and effortlessly flitted from the book, back to the characters and their roles within the town environment.With an outstanding use of music, which was noticeably impressive in many scenes, it just rounded off a superior storytelling experience.The only minor gripe I had with the whole package, was the use of the choices matter part of the affair. I haven’t conclusively decided if it added anything to the overall package, and I think at least another play is required to ascertain whether it is a gimmick or cleverly designed. Initially, it left you at a dead end. I don’t think there is any way you can complete the story without dying and returning to an earlier part of the story to try again. I might be wrong, but I didn’t get that impression; Mainly because you don’t have enough charms to affect events at that stage, and it takes a while to collect enough to even attempt traversing a different route.I probably died four or more times in my playthrough and was often flung back a few chapters to try a different word that may or may not affect events. Sometimes, if you owned enough charms, there were a few different words you could use, and some may take you to another dead end. I didn’t mind it too much however, as each time you start again, the story cleverly molds around events you have already experienced, and it actually provided more background lore, character interaction and a deeper involvement in the narrative. It gave the story and characters a weird three-dimensional feel where lots of slightly different happenings were occurring at the same time, but culminating in roughly the same ending no matter what path you took.Thanks to the Indie Game Collective for providing the key.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I really dislike giving this game a negative review, because I mostly enjoyed it. The visuals are great, the voice acting is fantastic, the story is good and original, BUT...The game evolves around finding charms that you can use to alter the game's story by selecting certain charms at key moments to branch the story. But this is mostly a linear affair: Picking the single charm you have available, unlocking a new charm along the way, reaching a dead and, and revisiting a previous branch later with your new charm option. All of this happens in a completely linear way. There are no different endings, no different ways to progress the story, and not really any creativity that you, as the player, can bring to the table.It barely qualifies as an "interactive" game. Sure, you can navigate little Luka around the beautifully made little maps, but there are not really any meaningful choices you can make. If you enjoy a good story, by all means, play the game. But if you expect choice and freedom in your gameplay, this is not for you. This game is 100% on rails.

_childDocuments_.review: I played for around 6h and was through the game.Which is not necessarily a bad thing, because I remembered almost every minute. The story is not unecessary stretched and I do have a big sweetspot for storytelling, where you want to find the best ending.All characters are memorable (which is rare for me, since I sometimes struggle to remember the names of characters, when there is nothing unique about them in their respective story).The art is amazing. The gameplay is basic, but I prefer that over a dozen mini-games, which have not actual meaning for the plot, except stretching gameplay.And the plot is what you should be getting the game for.To summarize:Beacon Pines is like reading a good book, on a snowy day, on your couch, with a blanket and a hot chocolate.Something I will look forward every year.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: +Cute characters+Cute animal characters+ So what if I'm a furry, totally unbiased.10/10 GOTY. Jokes aside, I really enjoyed the story telling and the way they went about the "choices matter" genre. They still matter, but you don't feel punished in the same sense and can go back any time to try something else out instead. Fun times and well worth the price in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The game is charming in all aspect except the illusion of multiple choices. If you want a cute, simple but warming story, pick this up. But unfortunately the charm system doesn't offer much of a replay value, at least not at this state since there is only 1 "true" ending at the moment (other ending will simply force you to go back to a specific point to try another charm).It is essentially a linear visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly dark and spooky! Reminded me a lot of Night in the Woods in terms of ambiance, but it's more of a Visual Novel than a platformer/puzzle game. The concept of a choose-your-own-adventure game was really intriguing to me! The voice acting was a bit much at first, but it really grew on me throughout the game. It took me about 4.5 hours to get all the achievements and endings. I do feel like the game could've been a bit longer for the price tag, but I'm not unsatisfied. There was so much heart and soul in the dialogue and art that this game really felt worth it, even for the short playtime.If there's one thing I wish could be improved, it would be adding a quick skip button for people replaying specific paths to get new Charms or achievements. Instead, I had to button mash through scenes I've already seen for about half an hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This was a heartfelt and sometimes dark but nevertheless beautiful story about love, forgiveness, friendship, and CHANGE. It is entirely narrative, with different events occurring based on the decisions you make; however, you can always go back and change the storyline whenever you want. Overall, I loved this game. It was super chill and cozy. The best parts of this game are the characters and the art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really worth playing. It hooked me so fast i finished this game in one day.One of the best things about this game are the characters, all are very likeable and easy to sympathize with. Another good points about this game are the story telling, art work and are unique game play, Just the timelines have some little problem but i guess this comes with timelines,
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a narrative experience than a game. I think that will calm any expectations and make it a lot more enjoyable. There's some mini-game experiences, but otherwise it's like a choose your own adventure book that requires a computer so that you unlock choices in a certain way. Unlike narrative games where your choices impact the story, this game for better or worse has you play through all the content in a surprisingly linear fashion. The story is charming and well written. I say this as a published author with an MFA. They really know how to do the important parts of telling a story. But think of it like hybrid audiobook with an ebook with a comic that all requires navigation. It's a great experience. Enjoyable use of time. You'll laugh and cry. Both. You will do both.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews for games on steam. But this game is so highly underrated. The artstyle and character design is what made me curious, some of the reviews saying it gives "night in the woods vibes" sold me.Once I started playing I just couldn't stop. Discovering all the mysteries of Beacon Pines, gaining new information with each path you take was hooking me in so much! I looked at every possible little item, listening to what the narrator had to say about it, discovered all possible endings and outcomes. It's just a perfect game, even made me shed a tear once!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic visual novel type of game, with multiple endings (good and bad). I just finished the game at about 10 hours of playtime. The story is all at once mysterious, absurd, and heart-warming. The reveals you get with each bad ending are just enough information to keep you wanting more. I had a great time playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a unique and captivating point-and-click adventure game set within the mysterious world of a narrative. You play as Luka, a curious teenager who stumbles upon strange occurrences in his hometown. With the help of his friends and the words (charms) you collect throughout the story, you’ll unravel the town’s secrets and make choice which alter the course of the narrative.Firstly, Beacon Pines has an extremely strong story. A mix of mystery, coming-of-age and the supernatural, keeping you constantly guessing what the ending is the true ending. The aesthetic of the game was charming and pulled you into the story. Your decisions throughout the game have an impact on the story, specific charms have different ending events. Every character had its own unique personality and quirks, and you start to build relationships with each as you explore the town and further progress through the story. The music is extremely relaxing and in my opinion is the perfect game to unwind and relax.The game’s achievements were fairly easy to obtain, the majority of which is just following the story and discovering the different, multiple endings to each. There are two “mini-games” with achievements for each. Both were a fun addition as you use the charms you find throughout the game to complete them. The game is not too long, sitting around 3-4 hours if you are to explore all options and aim to gain all achievements, easily completed within a single sitting. Beacon Pines is primarily a narrative-driven game, so apart from the achievements, there is minimal things to do other than relax and follow the story.Overall, Beacon Pines is a relaxing narrative game, with its mysteries, quirky characters and unique storytelling. While the gameplay may be a bit light, the narrative, charming visuals and impactful choices while playing make it a worthwhile experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacons pines is a wonderful experience. The way they handle branching routes is reminiscent of nonary games, and works well to lead players towards seeing the big picture. VA work is good, people complaining about that seem to miss the point that it's supposed to sound like an adult reading to a child. Game gets heavy at certain points, betraying is cute style, something I found super impactful.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It's a story about change and growth and about how all of our little actions can influence the world around us. Is it better to stand our ground when the odds aren't in our favor? Can a bully be forgiven? If the right thing to do was change a plan years in the making, would you do it? Beacon Pines is all of these questions and more, with a twisting fun story, gorgeous art, enjoyable charm mechanic, and characters that can tug at the heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good. I would say it doesn't deserve it's horror tag. I was more scared by the possibilities due to the tag than anything the game actually threw at me. It feels like a choose your own adventure book and a mystery. It's technically pretty linear and is an easy game, it feels very much like an interactive visual novel, but it's fun to figure out things right before the game gives you the answer. 10/10 would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly creative. The best way to describe Beacon Pines is to say that it's a contemporary choose-your-own-adventure novel. By experiencing bad endings and roadblocks, you unlock more options for Luka to use to progress other parts of the story. It's endearing, beautifully crafted, and entirely unique in it's approach.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: I liked this game. It's really good. But I can't recommend it. If I could give it a neutral review, I would.On a positive note, the game looks and feels very well. No bugs to be seen, nice visuals, etc. The characters as well as the story are interesting, and the gameplay is fun.And while the story is interesting, it has its weakness. The "plot twists" were foreshadowed so much, the only twist would have been if there was a red herring.That itself would have been okay, but there is  else to the game. It feels like the bare minimum. A branching story was written, and well executed, but they forgot the world building except the bar minimum which was necessary to untwist the plot twists (see above). We didn't get time to explore most characters, and I really wanted to explore , which I never got to. The whole game I was looking forward to finally get in there ...I backtracked every area I could access in every chapter, spoke with everyone and examined everything, left the game running one hour because I had someplace to be and there is no safe/load (or any real options) and it got me to 6 hours of play time. Buy on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A well-written story with charming artwork. The game plays like a mix of point-and-click and choose your adventure novel. The main story is linear, but there is a very interesting mechanic where you can discover various story branches and reveal more secrets as you play. This lets the story unfold slowly, exploring possibilities of bad endings and different character interactions. I loved the environments and character designs - they look like something out of a fairytale book. The way the narrator read the story with emotion was great, as well. It's not a long game in terms of playtime hours, but those few hours are engaging and worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: If you love branching narratives with different choices and endings then this is a game for you! The token system is such a creative way to backtrack and change the story without constant saving/reloading or restarting the whole game! The art style is incredible and each character has their own distinct style and voice.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: There are many games about friendship and this is one of them, of three friends in a town recovering from disaster only to have the trio find themselves neck deep in mystery and adventure.Good+ Lovely art style that is adorable and whimsical+ Lovely furry characters with a host of interesting personalities and hidden depth to their life.+ Nice accompanying slow and soft music.+ Interesting mechanism of branching narrative of which you can choose the outcomes.+ Lovely written story with twist and turns, nothing world changing but sweet, heartwarming and saccharine at times.Cons+ Short game, but still sweet+ Game is generally linear, a choose your own adventure game play with not too many choices in the end.+ No re-play value once you complete the game.+ No major difficulties and generally easy to beat.+ No voice acting for the characters except for the narrator.It's a short, sweet and easy to digest game, worth it for a play through for the story and characters involved.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Get it on sale for sure. but for all my misgivings the first 95% is cute and has some good moments and the art/va/music smash it. It's a "cute" VN like game with mostly minimal gameplay. the ending doesn't answer most of the important stuff. or most of the important things even. it's a bit tragic. I'd recommend it but it's not a master piece. SPOILERS ahead. Has a cool thematic and pretty location / story but it really, really drops the ball in the last 5%None of the plot threads link back to each other, charms feel a little arbitraryThere's entire subplots that "don't" happen but in the "true" ending it seems like everything has ended well (i.e the bully character is now friends with the MC but it happens off screen. aswell as the entirety of one of the major plot threads is mostly forgotten / offscreen in this route)One of the coolest routes made us root for a character, who ends revealing a VERY likeable and selfless side, then it's just all gone forever when we choose a different option. it also features a char that never turns up againThere's a dream sequence section every so often which has huge implications but it ends up unresolved. absolutely amazing work from the VA for them also though
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A marvelous little choose-your-own-adventure esque visual novel, with a fun twist on how to unlock routes. As you try different things and talk to different people, you gain important words/actions. You might hit a brick wall, but you'll gain new options to use on old paths and continue! 6 hours long and I loved every moment of this big mystery in a small town.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines a super captivating point and click adventure game that caught me completely off guard—in the best way possible. The story sprouts branches that twist and turn so you will legit be talking to your partner about it as your falling asleep long after you have put the game down. It's impossible not to become emotionally invested in Lukas story :sob:. Besides the utterly charming aesthetic, the endearing characters and the unique way it tells its story Beacon Pines presents some social challenges which will really get you thinking about the impact.The Devs have done an exceptional job creating a world/story rich in detail that makes your time spent in it feel personal and impactful but in some ways the game is also so simple at heart. The emotional depth of the story is :chefkiss:, there have been many moments I'm laughing and then crying. If Beacon Pines isn't on your gaming radar, it absolutely should be. For me its a 10/10 because the story and art were amazing and I cant pass up an old throw back to the Goosebump pick your path books. I really truly hope you give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Runtime: 4 hoursI beat this game in four hours, and I really quite liked it. The whole plot twist at the end of the game however didn't make much sense to me, it felt like it was a last moment "gotcha!" twist. The whole "your best friend got experimented on and grew taller and now is mistaken for an adult" was also kind of . . .odd. I loved the flashbacks of the dad, I loved the artwork and the storytelling. Each character was memorable and I felt like I should actually talk to each and every NPC. It surprised me when in one of the early endings, the MC actually DIES! Rarely do I see that in games like point-and-click adventure ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect it to be SO GOOD. The story gets unexpectedly dark sometimes, but it has a happy ending! There are a lot of story branches to clear before reaching the end, but don't worry - each is unique, so there's no repeating the same segments for a different result. All of them provide some chunks of story and it all comes together with many unexpected plot twists (but they make perfect sense) and a really amazing narrative. Please play it if you like story based games.Also, visuals and audio are lovely.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I actually really love the format of a game with multiple options/paths that actually organically walks you through every one of them and none of them are really optionalYou get a complete sense of the game and story without feeling like you have to go full completionist route which can take you out of the story since you get so focused on just finding every possible combination
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I've missed playing games like this without even realising it. I lost myself in the story, and would be thinking about other endings, other choices when falling asleep. If you enjoy interactive stories that creep into your brain, paired with great art and an awesome soundtrack... you'll love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 visual novel. Twin Peaks if it were a video game. Excellent art, writing and music. Story unravels in a very satisfying way that really leverages the medium; I don't think this would have quite worked as, for example, a TV miniseries. Took around 5 hours to finish, 6 to circle back for achievements, and I did it practically all in one sitting. If it were a book you'd call it a page-turner, TV you'd call it binge-worthy I guess. I don't know what you call it when it's a video game, but you should play it and find out.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of these experiences you wish you could go through again blind, it's got a little bit of meta stuff going on with the narrator talking to you, the player, and you being able to go back and rewrite the story, which I always love in a game.The rest of the game is just a wonderful time all throughout and I don't want to talk too much about it because that's what playing the game yourself is for! I was left touched and brought to tears several times. I also adore the artstyle and character designs <3
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent story uniquely told.Having just completed the game there are two things that stand out to me the most:- The charactersAll of the characters are excellently written; but I specifically loved watching Luka and Rolo interact, they are the perfect example of goofy friends, and they brought a smile to my face whenever they were together.- The branching story-book formatThe story would've been good if it was told in a traditional way, however because it changed the classic multiple-ending-game formula, it became great.In other games where you have branching paths, you could potentially get to the end on your first try. But, if you wanted to see any of the other endings, you'd have to start over from the beginning. Which, in my experience, can cause a loss of momentum in the story as you are forced to re-cover a lot of old ground. Especially if you just wanted to change one small decision near the end of the game.Beacon Pines on the other hand brings up a (literal) decision tree that you can jump to any section of at any time. This, combined with the fact that you slowly unlock options and endings as you go, means the story never looses momentum by forcing you to re-tread old ground. In fact, every bad ending only adds to the stakes and makes the true ending all the more satisfying.This isn't even mentioning the incredible art, music, and narrator voice acting.Beacon Pines is an excellent game all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Spellbinding.  It's rare that I find a story that conjures genuine emotion, or characters with whom I immediately fall in love.  I was initially drawn to this game by the artwork (which is absolutely stunning at every turn) and immediately knew upon the first few minutes of playing that I'd happened across something special.  The design, environments, and character art is all gorgeous.  The subtlety of facial expressions brings these characters to life in a delightful and powerful way.  A lot of virtual novels fall prey to the trap of having static sprites that quickly lose their veneer of life, but this game avoided that pitfall beautifully with a wide array of art for every major character.The soundtrack, as well, is beautiful, and I was blown away when I noticed that it actually swelled and adapted dynamically, introducing new tracks and instrumentation to match the scenes as they progressed.Interacting with the book with its narration and commentary was delightful, and the narrator delivered her performance with incredible warmth and loving personality.  The writing had me enthralled throughout and eagerly wanting to explore the next ending.  There were moments where I laughed out loud, moments where I teared up, and moments when my jaw dropped in a genuine shock. This is a world that I leave wanting more of in the best possible way.  This is a rare and special thing; something made with love, passion, and a wholesome and earnest story to tell.  I have a feeling this game may fall off of a lot of people's radar because of the very stylized anthropomorphic characters, but I urge anyone who loves a good, spooky, heartwarming story to check this out.  You'll be glad you came.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It's a CYOA where you need to find so called charms for the branches. Those are hidden in environment or appear in dialogues. Also they are retrieved in dead ends, allowing you to switch to another branch. Which leads to dead end hopping to advance the game. Never seen that kind of mechanic before.The story is also interesting. The MC is fully orphaned and lives with his grandma. The town suffured from a decline since the harvest failed 6 years ago. A new company arrived and helps the town. But if that was all, then this would be simply idyllic. Instead there are secrets to uncover, which requires you to go through the different branches. You are then at different places and see what other people are doing.Apropos characters: They and their respective dialogues are written very well. Everyone has a different personality and you understand how things progressed to form them into what they have become. The town feels alive, and if there is a point of critique, too small for a town considering that there are about 2 dozen buildings depicted. There are areas and people that have not been shown, but I get it that just adding areas where nothing is inside of them detracts from the game instead. Insofar the used space was well designed.I just feared I missed out looking in some places, because while the MC can jump - where there is no reason to need to jump - you can't run. I have really missed that. But in the end, this didn't detract from enjoying to peel back every layer and see what secrets have been buried.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The visual design is amazing. I love the story book design and the backgrounds. I think the details are amazing and I love the shading and brushed look of the trees. Each character has great design and I especially love how they are drawn for their reactions as well. The best detail is that the characters are still moving in the background during dialogue scenes. The music is amazing!! It makes it so exciting to listen as you progress through the game. I love that each character has different sounds for their speech bubbles and it is distinct enough for you to get a real grasp of how the characters would sound like if they had voice actors. Each chapter and branch of the tree wasn't boring at all to play in. This game could have easily played a same repetitive feel like in usual visual novels. I loved that each different path you took in the game was different but was still important to the whole story of Beacon Pines. The only negative I feel from this game are as follows: saving function. This game doesn't really allow you to save even though I understand it is a short game compared to others. Two times I have exited the game due to just wanting to save it for another day and it either saved at the beginning of a chapter or it saved during the chapter which is inconsistent. I feel as though there should be a save function that allows you to save at any point of the game but that is very minor inconvenience. If anything I feel that the beginning of the game there should be a warning or something that shows that it is saving for you just to not ruffle anyone else's feathers. The game for me was phenomenal! I loved this game and I am so happy that I waited for it to come out since playing the demo. Thank you so much for creating this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. It's a short game, but with so many twists and turns that it is one of the best mystery/visual novel games I have ever played. The art design, character design, story and overarching themes are some of the best out there. That being said, the game is still only five hours long, but don't let that discourage you from picking this up and playing it for yourself. You will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

Absolutely loved everything about it and wasn't disappointed at all. Buy it if you like mystery and the art style!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.I'm not very good at writing, so that's it. Probably not for you if you don't like primarily story and character driven media. There's not much outside of that in way of puzzles or the like, but the story and the characters herein truly do a wonderful job of capturing your heart and mind. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A neatly presented and compact crossover between adventure game and fairy tale book. The writing is good and the story - about a bunch of anthropomorphic animal kids bonding as they uncover a conspiracy and fight corporate greed - can be heartwarming at times, though it is also quite naive and unoriginal.The presentation has been given a lot of attention with pretty bite size stages popping out of book pages, well drawn characters that are easy to attach to, and above all an absolute killer of a soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Great little mystery story! Short, but that's not a bad thing. Lasts just long enough to enjoy it without overstaying its welcome. I would recommend to anyone who enjoys cozy games with a good story and characters, but who don't mind games that take their time and aren't action heavy. Very happy I picked it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story game. There is no skill required, nor guesswork, nor anything really, except to hang along on the wild ride. But it is a great ride. The story is told in a very imaginative way. I played the entire game together with my kids, and we had a blast trying to guess where the story was going next. Each new word was truly exciting, and the ending(s) were interesting and often unexpected. It was fun. My only regret is that the tree of options was shorter than I'd expected. With this kind of format, I thought they would let us access the plot more often, but the real number of branch points was rather limited - not nearly as many as a choose your own adventure novel. Maybe they could keep that in mind for the next game - which I'm hoping they will make.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with the bad: the "charm" mechanic, whilst great, is not some butterfly effect puzzle mechanic. You basically are required to go down every branch to get the correct charms to complete the story. But as long as you're happy with it being a visual novel, it's excellent. it's a very cosy game. Reminds me a lot of Night in the Woods except rather than mostly being a coming of age story with a little rural supernatural it's a lot of rural supernatural with a little coming of age. The "charm" mechanic of how you can go back and forth down different narrative branches is a great way to explore all the paths of what is basically a visual novel. Overall, dripping in charm and highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This felt more like watching a movie unfold than playing a game. The game rides high on being something of a 'pick your adventure' format, but really it controls all players progress pretty unilaterally-- meaning that every player ends up playing the exact same game. It was fun from an escapist point of view, a lot like reading a YA novel, but I would never recommend it. I only got 6 hours of game time and completed all possible adventures, and I'm 20$ poorer. 1 out of 5 stars. Only because the characters were cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. Beacon Pines is done and dusted. Curiously, this is the second visual novel I’ve played in a row that incorporates breaking the fourth wall into its story, which has been a successful aspect of both games (the other being Paranormasight).Beacon Pines is a visual novel. However, the author doesn’t really know how the story is going to unfold, so she asks you, the player, for advice in how this will happen, and together, you work through many permutations seeking an acceptable ending to the story.Which is a mystery novel wherein three kids end up working together to solve a missing persons case, a murder, and a conspiracy that could kill or enslave everybody in the sleepy town of Beacon Pines.Instead of humans, all the characters are anthropomorphic animals, but for all intents and purposes, they’re people. And everything about the game is crafted with eye towards cuteness and whimsy. Except the story itself, which does carry those aspects, but, as mentioned before, also features a more sinister plot.In fact, this is one of the most pleasant looking games you’ll ever play. Its truly charming artstyle is disarming. The author (narrator) is voiced. All the characters also have unique voices, but instead of words, they speak in gibberish. With real word subtitles. It was really a perfect way to approach things.As far as gameplay goes, you’ll explore Beacon Pines and some areas just outside the town. Most of the game is dialogue driven. However, you’ll find encounter cues throughout the game that can be used to alter the direction of the story, and key events are illustrated on a story tree with branching paths based on the encounter cues you select. Typically, each key event has two or three cue options, with consequences and story progression based on the specific cue chosen, which includes several death scenes (not graphic deaths though). You can access the story tree at any point to try out new cues as you find them.Oh…and the main character can either walk or hop around as you travel about and explore. Hopping was somehow incredibly satisfying, lol.Beacon Pines is fully Steam Deck compatible and you’ll get between 2 and 2 1/2 hours of gameplay on a full battery.Anyway, it took me right at five hours to 100% this game. Almost everything can be uncovered by simply doing everything available to you in each story branch. I played into the 100% organically with no issues. I thought this was a truly captivating and charming experience with a splash of sinister that was well worth the cost of entry. I can easily recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: If I had any complaint to give, its just that I wish I had more. I fell in love with the characters, even the minor ones, and just wanted more time with them. This is probably the most engrossing choose your own adventure style game I have ever played (and I have played a decent number of them) and what makes it special is your ability to jump between the choice timelines so you never quite know which path will actually lead you to you final end.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I was a backer on Kickstarter, and it was well worth the investment! What an incredible story with beautiful and quirky characters, art, music, and voice acting that all worked so well together to make this game. It's like an interactive story that you just want to keep playing to find out what the heck is going on the whole time! Also a very unique gameplay in how the story unfolds. I can't wait to see if this team does anything from here. If you're looking for cozy mystery with heartwarming plotlines, twists and turns, and a rag-tag group of characters, this is your game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Some games are a fun challenge and some are a pleasant story to escape from reality, but Beacon Pines is a masterpiece. Simple, yet thoughtful and relatable characters got me invested in the story from the beginning and I found myself time after time feeling like I was a kid again as I played through each chapter. The story kept me engaged and determined to find the answers to each little and big mystery, and I was genuinely surprised by each twist that came along. This is truly a work of passion and you can see and feel it in the artwork, the voice work, and the music. My word, the music is truly top tier, reinforcing the tension at some moments and amplifying the gut punch of emotions at others.I laughed. I cried. I fist-pumped. I sat in shock. This game had me riding a roller coaster and while I was sad when it was over I know I will go on it again. It may not be the same the next time(s) around, but this is one of those experiences that you feel glad to have experienced even just once and will have you searching to feel it again. 10/10 Would slap the melon again
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't really into it at first, but I'm glad I pushed through! It's a little like those choose-your-own-adventure books, the beginning felt a little out of my age group, but turning the narrator off helped a lot (...sorry! I can see how it's helpful for kids/non-native speakers though) and the story is actually quite rewarding if you're paying attention. Mystery/conspiracy vibes. Finished in a few evenings, had fun, artwork's gorgeous :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wonderful little supernatural mystery with a big heart. Beacon Pines can be a bit amateurish at times when it comes to technicalities (like noticeably poor sound engineering of narrator's voicelines), but the story can be truly gripping. It blends many influences, like OXENFREE and Night in the Woods, yet the game manages to firmly be its own thing. Childish, hopeful, sometimes depressing, sometimes heartwarming, but always sincere. It is really easy to forgive the lack of any meaningful gameplay thanks to the charming (although not terribly deep) cast of characters, good music and unique, Gravity Falls-esque vibe of... Well, everything.Surprisingly, it has a lot in common with Kotaro Uchikoshi's works; namely, the Zero Escape series. Before finally reaching the true ending, you will have to suffer through many, many bad ones, and that is probably the one thing that the developers didn't think about carefully enough. The Zero Escape visual novels made jumping between story branches an integral part of the story, but in Beacon Pines it feels more like a framing device that doesn't actually contribute much to the experience. You are, after all, reading a children's book.Some part of me hoped that the keyword mechanic, which (supposedly) allows you to influence key story decisions, would be somewhat more enaging, but alas. That said, Beacon Pines is still very much worth your time if you're looking for an entertaining supernatural thriller that manages to both be genuinely funny and suspensful at the same time.  Just do not go into it expecting a truly branching narrative where each action has consequences. It is a children's book written for adults, and i am grateful i got to experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic art direction, music, and voice acting. The story is great and felt complete despite the game only taking 4-5 hours to finish. Overall the whole game felt very polished and I didn't encounter any bugs while playing. There isn't much to the gameplay beyond walking, talking to people, and making choices, but if you enjoy playing games for the story and characters I'd highly recommend checking this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think you could ever find a storybook as magical as this, the one that tells the tale of Beacon Pines. A story of mystery, friendships and deep emotions. One page will make you burst out laughing at Rolo's brainless antics while the next page drops a revelation so shocking you nearly fall off your chair. Most of the time, though, you'll be crying your eyes out. Tragedy (and tragic ends) are rampant within, fit to leave you with wet cheeks and a broken heart. But there are also scenes where fate is kinder to little Luka, leaving you crying tears of joy. This story will bring out a wealth of emotion from you with its exceptional writing and immaculate artwork, I guarantee. It's a story I'll never forget; One I hope you all read and hold in your hearts forevermore, too!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

I didn't finish it because the game just restarted when I opened it one time. Was close to the end, though, but not playing through everything again to see the end.

_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so at first, I was a little unsure. I thought the narrator sounded a bit cheesy and it read like an audiobook type of narration for children's books, so I felt not super into it. But wow, I quickly changed my tune and could literally not put this book -- I mean, game -- down. I literally held in my piss to finish this game because my brain said there was no pause in this storyline! While it's a game that only takes 3-4 hours to play, it's some of the best 3-4 hours ever.
