I can't say much without spoiling it, but give it a chance. It's so worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a cutesy adventure and visual novel game. Featuring themes of horror, mystery and wholesomeness. Its story is masterfully told, with an exceptionally voiced narrator and a brilliant script that made the words come together ever so elegantly. I have nothing but praise for this title and I wholeheartedly recommend this to all narrative fans.All characters are utterly adorable anthropomorphic animals, with the protagonist being Luka, a young boy from a small agricultural town called Beacon Pines. Luka spends his days with his best friend Rolo, a mischievous fox who likes to cause havoc, whereas Luka is a bit more reserved. The two decide to start their holidays by delving into a town mystery and exploring a spooky abandoned factory after hearing local gossip. Of course, there is much more background story to this factory that is discovered later on, but this sets the scene for the tale.Despite Luka's unfortunate family situation, with his mother missing and his father deceased, he still manages to rally those around him. Quickly becoming friends with new-girl Beck, whilst the other townsfolk all enjoy his presence as well. Although, behind the town of Beacon Pine, lies a deep, undercover secret. A secret that will impact everyone's lives once it becomes known. Luka, alongside his friends, quickly become dragged into this labyrinth, uncovering the true history of the town, and are responsible for its fate.The story is made up of branching paths. The narrative takes a different turn depending on which charm (word) is used in a particular turning point situation (see gameplay section for more details on charms). The story is cleverly constructed, and it is not the typical mindmap mechanic. The game is designed to have reached multiple endings, but to push forward until the "true" ending is discovered. Therefore, it is not necessarily made with replayability in mind, and the branching paths are not large divulging paths, but intertwined. If it is the "wrong" choice, that route will typically end fairly quickly, with the narrator saying something alike "No, that can't be it, we're so close now, we can't give up!" Pushing the player forward. The credits themselves will only roll once this true ending is reached, further highlighting the game design to be played to reach this ending, where all loose ends are tied up, and everything is appropriately explained.Beacon Pines is predominantly a visual novel, and thus there is a large amount of text to read. Only the narration is voiced (and wonderfully, might I add). The game truly feels like an interactive story book, and quite literally so, in charm scenes, or chapter beginnings, the words are read from a book. Majority of the game is spent conversing with characters, exploring the vibrant world and collecting charms.Charms are the defining gameplay feature and are what diverges the paths. Charms are words, these words can be found through exploration, or are compulsory finds, directly related to story progression. These charm cards are able to be used in "turning points" of the game. For instance, when someone is being argumentative towards you, choose to tickle them, or fight them. Each charm used will vastly change the set course of the narrative, and  repeatedly, players will need to go back to The Chronicle to alter the path, by using a previously unattained charm. This results in switching timelines somewhat frequently to collect more charms which can be used at differing turning points, to ultimately set Luka on the final path to the "true" ending. A handy addition to The Chronicle, is that it will display a tick beside each charm, advising that the charm has been used to its maximum potential. If there is no tick, it may be a good idea to go back and change fate. Although this makes for quite simple gameplay, it allows its story to flourish, and be  told to its fullest potential, which I think is a big positive.Beacon Pines is undeniably gorgeous. Its vibrant child-like art and anthropomorphic characters  all add to its cutesy style. I also enjoyed the story-book background and use of written words being so impactful. However, it is important to note that there are still light themes of horror, with dead bodies and many endings leading to deaths (non-graphic).Audio is another significant positive in Beacon Pines. As aforementioned, the only voiced character, the narrator,  is simply fantastic. Her voice is filled with emotion exactly when needed, she is masterfully articulate and completely drew me into the story. She completely reminded me of how I had always imagined children's picture storybooks to be told. Not only this, but the soundtrack is astonishing. Profoundly dramatic when it needs to be, but also quite melancholic in times of despair. Approximately 6 hours. In this time, I completed all branching paths and uncovered the true (or final) ending.   Yes (but player choice). Somewhat. If optional endings are missed, then yes, it is good to go back. Beacon Pines completely blew me away with its polished and seamless gameplay. Furthermore, its proficiency in its story-telling ability is immense. The narrator is voiced expertly, the script is eloquent and well-constructed, the art is gorgeous and the story itself is simultaneously cute and creepy. I simply did not find anything here that I could think of in a negative light. Beacon Pines is a gem of a game, and one I hope to see gain the popularity it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely exceptional game. Art, music, and writing flow together to make a genuinely touching and engaging experience. This is not meant to be a mechanics game: it's about finding the story. It caters to the part of you that wants to go back and select different dialogue options in a scene. One of the best parts is expanding on individual characters' stories by choosing a different charm to engage with them. I admit that I've stalled a little bit as I've gotten close to what feels like end-game, because I don't want the story to be over.Only critique: I get a little embarassed when playing on the train and hitting a moment that puts tears in my eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Very good! Alot more interesting than it seems at first (atleast for me it was). Narrator had a calming voice, and you get invested in the characters. You have to play some bad endings to get the full story but thats par for the course. Overall if you're looking for a chill*hah*, compelling story to enjoy at your own pace with awesome visuals and sound as well as a cute atmosphere, this is for you!

It doesn't take long to get all the endings (and achievements), but in the epilogue, I cried a lil. So lovely. <3 What I would give to be able to play this again for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: somehow just a bit beyond articulation...everything so instantly inviting to Me Specifically, and i just happened to play it when im in the mood for something like that. childhood terror, adorable furries, lavish on a sensory level, and Just Meta Enough to make me reflect on my long-neglected enjoyment of writing stories, of the necessary curiosity required to explore things before they happen, a tension and anticipation not unlike actually experiencing the story. the things u learn from weird dead ends, how they all contribute to the texture as new wrinkles are added in real time, things that U Do Yrself surprise u as they click into place. rly solid refutation of the idea that Only Literal "Canon" Events Matter, and a deeply comforting Exploratory Experience
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Think Neopets + Life is StrangeI know that a lot of people love this game, but I have to be the devil's advocate here and say that it's just "OK." Beacon Pines is a very sweet and charming visual novel with likable characters and a very interesting "rewrite the story" mechanic. But it really doesn't do anything special. It takes a lot of fun twists and turns and provides an overall satisfying experience. The "creepy, more mature" story couldn't be anything but. I felt like Beacon Pines's writing followed its art style, it's cutesy, basic, childish, and tries to send a message that falls flat by the end. The narrative is almost like if you took a children's book like The Magic Treehouse and then added in cuss words just because you could. There is, virtually no gameplay, and we have yet another visual novel "game" that has stripped video gaming down to it's most basic components. There is no choice, no "this or that" multiple endings. You have to play out all of the different story arcs to get to the end of the game. I was very disappointed that collecting charms was really just a mechanic for maybe the first hour of gameplay. You don't have to do any looking around or interacting with the environment to find something you may have missed that has a significant impact on the story. Thus the illusion of choice is frosted over almost complete linearity, thereby destroying all replay value. Beacon Pines kills a few hours, and doesn't leave a sour taste in your mouth. If this is your style of game, it certainly is only worth picking up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A very compelling game, I played this with a friend and we had a lot of fun trying to piece together what was going on! We usually take forever to finish games but we did this one in three sessions (about six hours total) because we were so eager to find out what happened next, and because it was so easy to keep on playing. It involves fewer choices than I expected so it feels less like a branching narrative and more like a linear narrative that happens to be told in a non-linear way, but that's still a really interesting way to experience the story. Some very poignant moments too, though there was one BIG loose thread that's gonna bug me... pun intended?Also the art and music are really beautiful. There's just something about an indie game about a dying industry town with a dark secret that just hits the spot.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful mystery game that had me hooked from the moment I started it. The story book like appearance and narration really immersed you into the small town of Beacon Pines and I loved every single branch the story tree had to offer (good or bad ). You can tell the creators of this game poured their heart and soul into this game and I highly recommend buying it and checking it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

It's like those books where you chose a path that gave you a specific page to turn to in order to continue the story line that you chose. But the GORGEOUS painting-style artwork adds a new depth. I hope more games follow this style, because I am HOOKED.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing! The storytelling, the characters and the fine attention to detail are great.I am usually not one to explore all round and dialogues when I game a game, but this game had me find everything one the first run and encouraged me to do so as I played. The voice actress could also be really proud of herself for this one, she truly carries you trough the feelings of it all. This game is so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a videogame reviewer, but I do play a lot of games. I want to keep this concise and accurate so you have a better idea of what you're getting.Whether you're partial to furries or not, this is simply an adorable game with a town full of forest critters, big and small. It has an almost "choose your own adventure" vibe, with mystery, friendship, comedy, and wholesomeness strung about the entire way. The game happens to take place in the self-titled town of Beacon Pines. The narrative is told in a storybook fashion, with a narrator who is ever inclined to put in her two cents. I honestly only have one semi-negative thing to say about the game, and its that the narrator is almost trying TOO hard to appear on the player's side.  She does a good job of providing descriptors for settings, for emotions the characters are feeling, and she even helps give unseen info on how certain characters show up to different locations. But often-times I'd find myself mashing a bit through her dialogue as to progress to the next part of the actual story. Despite that, she did her job well and helped pull me into the experience. It left me wanting more, but after eight or so hours in Beacon Pines I'm happy to say this felt like a story worth experiencing. I came for the artwork and mystery, and stayed for the gripping dialogue.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is an extremely well illustrated, very story heavy adventure game with some light puzzle and choose your own adventure elements. The game quickly teaches you about it's Charms and Turning Points. In Turning Points you may use Charms you've found in the game world to influence how the story goes, by finding all the Charms and going through all the possible routes you'll be able to figure out the dark secrets of Beacon Pines and how to reach the true ending of the game.Overall a very enjoyable experience and highly recommend to anyone looking for a mild-mystery themed story heavy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly enjoyed this game so much and absolutely loved it. The art, effects, sound, story hshshs just everything, really made me happy! this game is story-rich but not as 'deep' or 'emotional'. Mostly the lighthearted moments really put a smile on my face. The squabbles between friends hit close to home for me which is great so it is not too far from reality. This game is calm and casual, a literal storybook just to relax your mind and play around with options and such. So glad there was no mini game puzzles incorporated because, for me, that might distract and ruin the story-like ambiance! I don't have any dissatisfied comments, I went into the game hoping for something to cheer me up and have my mind 'off'. It's a great game. I got this when it was discounted and on a whim, no regrets. For the original price, I would say it's worth it, especially when you really take in the production of the game, the price could never compare. Do download this and give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: bought the game since it looked cute, didn't expect much. i wasn't sure if i would like the cutesy story-book style of it at first. figured it would be a game i played for a bit and then never picked back up. i was VERY wrong. the music, art, story, and mechanics come together in a very beautiful and emotionally appealing way. i have spent the last 6 hours absolutely hooked on this game. the story was very fun to puzzle together, and the mechanic of unlocking new ways to handle key points in the story was handled very well. i was concerned it would get repetative, but it never did!my only complaint is that some parts of the story-telling parts of the game had a black screen with no art, which sorta broke my immersion/interest. i think even a still image of some sort could be benefital to these areas, but not having one didn't hinder my enjoyment of the game too muchfantastic game, worth your money!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It's more or less a visual novel with the added feature of being able to run around and explore a bit, and talk to folks.The gimmick is that you can go back and change key words of the story to completely change the timeline and take the story in a new direction.It's not very long but it is engaging and fun. Very cute, a little dark. I expected it to get darker than it did, if I'm being honest. I wish you got to know the characters a little better though. I feel as though you really only get to know the main character and Beck enough to really feel invested in them. The themes are relatable enough and the writing and narration are both lovely.It's mostly just a nice, relaxing experience with some twists and turns. I hope to see more games from this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is up there among the top visual novels I have ever read. I laughed--a lot, I cried, I smiled, and I never lost interest until I had fully completed the game with all of the branching storylines and all of the achievements.The story is brilliant. The characters were strong. The protagonist was easy to empathize with from the first scene to the final scene at the end of the epilogue.A narrator takes you through the game, and you use "charms" that you have collected along the way to fill in words at "turning points" in the story to lead to the various branches and endings to the story. There are a lot of turns in the story and each of the various branches to the story--even those that lead to bad endings--help flesh out the entirety of the narrative.The artwork fits seamlessly with the story. You traverse through the pages of what feels like a beautifully illustrated children's book. This includes the various chapters that are altered with different choices at the "turning points" along with the flashbacks.The diner flashback with the cooking minigame and the pond flashback with the fishing minigame are two of my favorite points in the game.The sound track, which consists primarily of piano pieces and an acoustic guitar piece with a coffee shop feel at the end of the epilogue, is a perfect fit to enhance the ambiance.Although you have to go back to different points in the story and try different and new charms, it never feels like a grind. This is game is an definite thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game about cute animal people and change. Uh, I kinda stumbled into the ending, so the impact was a little less. So... this is one of those games where you pick the weird options first just to see everything, but also, sometimes the weird choices are correct. So, I'unno, good luck. Maybe there is a spoil-free walkthrough out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Great roughly 6 hour story game that was intriguing the whole way through. If you had previously played the demo it might seem more linear than it first advertised but I feel that was the correct choice and ensures you have all the pieces to let you puzzle out the twists yourself before they blatantly spell it out for you. Also if you were thinking it, no its not that kind of furry game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been following this game since stumbling upon the demo, I am thrilled to have beaten the game and enjoyed every moment of it. Between the emotive art by Ilse Harting and the delightful narration from Kirsten Mize giving life to Matt Meyer's story, this game will stick with me for a while and I couldn't be happier. I wholeheartedly would recommend this to anyone, especially those searching for something that is cozy, spooky and deeply introspective.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to help fund this game on Kickstarter a bit over a year ago, and I'm glad I did. It's a wonderful, branching narrative where said branches are unlocked through Charms gained through either a bit of exploration or travelling down its paths. Its twists sprinkle clues throughout the charming story, building groundwork so even if you do piece them together ahead of time it feels like an accomplishment. A great mystery with a sci-fi touch, fun characters, fantastic art, and wonderful music/atmosphere, I greatly enjoyed this Novel experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with a lovely soundtrack, but unfortunately short.The branching story aspect was honestly disappointing, most 'charms' (words that cause a branch to occur) are only used a couple of times. The branches themselves feel meaningless. There is one early decision that splits the game into two halves, but almost every decision after that either continues the story, or gives brief exposition followed by a game over screen. It doesn't feel like there's much choice when only one option is the 'correct' choice.I'd give it a 'maybe' recommendation if that was an option.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game on Kickstarter and I couldn't be more happy that I did. It was a gorgeous, engaging and thoughtful game. I had so much fun playing it, and as someone who recently lost my dad as well really felt for the main character. I loved this little game and would 100% recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Truly the best way to start the equinox was opening this game. You're whisked away to a peaceful narration of a story about a young Luka looking for his missing mother, where you - dear player - are in charge of important turning points.I'm usually hesitant of "choices matter" games due to the nature of picking the "wrong path" and suffering the consequences of my actions, but this game rewards the bad choices as much as the good ones. Exploring is the name of the game, and the more you learn and the more you explore, the better the chances you have of getting Luka to the correct end of his journey.I'm still very early on in my journey but between the art style, the lovely narrator, and the colorful cast of characters I'm deeply charmed. There are some more emotional and creepy elements waiting that remind me of Over the Garden Wall, and I would highly recommend checking out this game and all its branches for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A well-told story with an interesting gimmick.  Characters were interesting and expressive.  The plot twists were surprising every time.  I'm somewhat considering playing through the game a second time to see what I missed the first time.  A seemingly innocuous conversation with somebody early on becomes something very different once you know what their secret is.  It's short, but definitely a great way to spend a day.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like Scooby Doo, Mystery Incorporated (the TV show) in the best way possible! The mystery is intriguing, the mechanic of revisiting alternate endings without having to play through it again is brilliant, and the music/art fits perfectly with the aesthetic! This is one of those games that I wish I could wipe from my memory so that I can play it again!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with beautiful and emotional music, charming artwork, and a light-horror story that will keep you playing till the end (in my case in a single sitting). This game is primarily a Visual Novel. The part that allows you to alter the course of the story is less of a game mechanic and more *a part* of the story itself. You can't actually beat the game without experiencing most of the endings, and this is intentional. Every time you "fail" you uncover more of the plot and get closer to the "true ending" (completing the game). I love this game's story, as it is a story that cannot be told in any other medium. Only in a game, with this "time-altering" interaction, is such a story possible, which is why I love video games as an art medium. As it is a novel, there is a lot of reading. The downside to this is that if you are trying to 100% the game, it is a little tedious to go back through all that text to get to the "hidden" charms or conversations you missed. There is overall very little interaction with the game, outside of choosing the order you uncover the plot, and who you talk to, and I honestly believe it is to its benefit. There is just enough player agency to make it feel like your choices matter, but the game is trying to tell a story, not create a gameplay loop.Many reviews say the game is very short (at about 4-5 hours depending on how fast you read). While it is true that the game is short, It does not really feel that way. They story that is told is wrapped up nicely in that time. I would say the reason people complain about the length is that the game does leave you wanting more, similar to the feeling after finishing a good book series. You don't necessarily want another book in the series, but there is now an empty feeling (something that the game actually addresses if you talk to one of the characters in the library during the epilogue.Love the game, love the art, love the music. My only regret is that I cannot experience it again with fresh eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap, i have some high praise to say here This game had me hooked from start to finish, all in one sittingThe story was amazing and really tugged at my heart in some partsLoved the storybook style and design of the town/charactersI highly recommend this if you want a combat free, choice heavy experience, i promise you wont regret it <3
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Game was fine but The amazing VO that did the narrator couldnt pick up the slack of the honking and wheezing other characthers in the game. If you dont mind that this game might suit you just fine, not for me tho. But I do wish theyd add a mute other characters than the narrator option and Id defenetly reconsider this again.EDIT can turn the honking off now
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game mostly in one sitting, and I think it’s rather important that you do play this in one sitting. The main mechanic is that you’re able to change the story at certain points by using charms you collect along the way to diverge the story—a cool mechanic, and it’s executed well; but a consequence of this is that it will be easy to lose track of which timeline you’re in. The game does help you a little with this, but if you don’t play it mostly in one go, I’d imagine it’s hard to keep track.Overall, the plot deserves a lot of praise. There are twists and leads that hint to these twists very well, and the plot does well enough to keep you informed just enough that you want to keep going. There may have been some minor things that aren’t exactly explained, but I remember not having too much of a problem with it.As for the ending, I can say I’m not *entirely* satisfied. I still have questions about things that happened in the game, and while it’s definitely well executed (and, trust me, this isn’t reason enough to dislike the game); I still have a few loose questions.There’s not much to say elsewhere. The art is well done, the characters have their own voices & personalities, and that’s really all I can think of. Overall, I was a little bit disappointed that I didn’t have all my questions answered, but other than that, still a definite recommendation to anyone who enjoys these types of games. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game? Sure. But if you're playing on PC, be aware that there seems to be some sort of bug that doesn't allow you to get the cling charm so you can get the agile angler achievement and that may be the most frustrating thing out of all. Plus, the "true ending" might be the most disappointing out of all of them lol. Why is this tagged as horror?
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It had a good idea, however it didn't go hard enough with it to provoke a change in me.From the start of the game till the end I disliked it, plus not being able to fully use the engine to show the most important scenes as they would just describe it in text it didn't really fit with me.The only characters that are decent and just scratching the decent character development are the 3 main ones. The others are just completely underdeveloped.I'd say if you want to play something that's worth your time... Play Night In The Woods, where your decisions matter and it feels like every character is important and they grow with you.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute game that gradually unravels a mystery with satisfying pacing. The story is engaging, and while it's mostly told as a serious kids-in-small-town-uncover-conspiracy sort of way, there's a good mix of humor thrown in to keep anything from getting too heavy. I thought the charm system to change the story at certain branching points was clever (although there wasn't really as much puzzle as I expected in collecting most charms). The art is great! Soundtrack is good. The length was just about right (although it's a game that's easy to pick up for a chapter or two then put down, just like a good book).
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is cozy, well-written, and exceptionally well-narrated in a way that will draw fans of walking-simulator-style games right in.  It's a pretty much perfect length for what it is, and the branching paths explorable through the Chronicle make the whole thing feel that much more special, even if the story gets a bit implausible at times.  I had a great time and was engaged throughout, despite the lack of "gameplay".  Easy recommendation to anybody willing to spend an afternoon or two just reclining in a chair and enjoying a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes with story rich games, I find myself only taking half the words in order to get through it faster. Not this game, I read every last word. It's a choose your own adventure game in it's truest form. Maybe it's my age and because I grew reading adventure books but this game scratches an itch very few do. You can very clearly see this game was made with the most love.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Narrative-driven games are arguably my favorite and this is GOTY material for me, easily. It simply has too much going on to explain exactly why I love it, at least without giving away its precious secrets. I belly laughed, I ugly cried, I could have spent hours in wonder at the soundtrack and artistic direction, I ~have~ spent hours geeking out about how cleverly they constructed the story and its shifting paths... I don't know if I can speak for everyone, but I know this is a game I'll keep talking about for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a 6 hours adventure / visual novel with a presentation that oozes charm. It hides the linearity inherent to most games of its type with a clever "charms" system ; branching paths unlocked progressively by "words" you discover during your adventure.  The story is well-written and touching. The "universe inside a book" theme is well exploited and adds a certain flair and originality to the narration.I wished the game was longer but what is here is top-notch.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute delight to play. The story is compelling and I loved the characters. I recommend this game to anyone who likes both a branching narrative,but also wants to retain some control over proceedings. It is a uniquely told story,its a game you are going to wish you could experience for the first time twice
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute graphics, it really felt like you were in a story book. The story is a good one of loss and accepting it, along with fighting for what you believe in and not giving up.Some of the endings felt a little rushed. I know some people complained that it was too short but I thought it was perfectly timed. The mini games are fun as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo during one of Steams promotional events and was immediately hooked! I couldn't wait for it to release! and when it finally did I bought it right away! It was worth every penny! The art is beautiful, the soundtrack is awesome, and I love the branching story lines! If you're the type of person the plays games purely for the story this game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. Worth the money even at full price but I got it from humble choice. Gotta say I love Most of the game. Like truly a 9.5/10 I'd have to say the ONLY issue i had is that the true ending final chapter feels a little rushed. It's a bit upsetting but it makes up for it by having 2 other braches that are really good. One that's beautiful and another that kinda doesnt make sense. It even has a random annoying character that's only available in the singular chapter & branch for like. No reason. There is a plot hole or two in the true ending but i love it regardless for the AWESOME epilogue.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: There's something special about this game. While I love reading in general, usually a visual novel's story telling can only hold my attention for maybe 15 minutes (something about the video game medium makes it feel more tedious than enjoyable). Beacon Pines was an exception. Nothing about this game looked like it would be up my alley, but I took a chance and you should, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and creepy is a fairly accurate description, although it definitely leans more on the cute side.It's a fairly linear story told in a non-linear way, which slightly annoyed me at times but overall was an enjoyable experience.This is clearly a game made with a lot of love, and definitely worth picking up if you can afford it or it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: okay so.. dont get me wrong.. the story is great, love the alterative routes you can take and see how it all plays out and theres very strong story writing in some of them.. The ending tho.. was a little lack luster and wasn't as fullfilling as you hope it'd be. there's a few plot holes still there and the ending needed alittle bit more omph to it. But it's still is a good game to experience with a ton of great characters in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Great narrated adventure with very lovable characters.It's basically a 'choose your own adventure' game, but you will see (nearly) every possible path in one playthrough.If you have played the '9 doors' series, then you are already familiar with how this works.My only gripe is the ending, which seemed a bit rushed and not quite as satisfactory as I had hoped.But nevertheless it's gorgeous, not too short, funny and pretty wholesome, so definitely recommending this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game was super cute! I loved the art style and was super invested in the story. The whole "changing timelines with single words" mechanic was super cool, and I liked learning things in other timelines that weren't revealed in others; made the story feel very well rounded. Definitely recommend for those who enjoy simple, unique mechanics and story-driven gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The story is enthralling and it's wonderful the way the decision tree mechanism helps to unfold parts of the story even for dead ends. The mini-games were fun. Some of the cut scenes were incredibly long and I wouldn't have minded an option for skipping dialogue for branches that have already been explored so that I could easily clean up my unfinished achievements without having to replay so much, but overall I really enjoyed the story and the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully presented fractured story that you experience, branch after branch, through the eyes of our young hero.Walk around, talk to people and solve small puzzless as the story unfolds and draws you in.+ Well-performened narration (the only voice acting), that helps to draw you in.+ Beautiful painted art locations.+ Cute and well-developed characters.+ Plenty of twists and turns!+ Kind of dark, in a good way.- The experience is largely linear, even if you go back and forth. As most of the branches in the story are available after you've completed another.- Walking is a little slow and there is no run.- I didn't like the sounds they used for the the talking, but it's a minor nitpick.It's a great little, heartwarming experience with a good ending. Or endings?
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I have really been enjoying Beacon Pines. I'm really particular about what games I play and this is a hit. The animation is beautiful, and I have a soft spot for the adorable character, Rolo. The storyline is way more in depth and dystopian than I imagined, and its incredibly interesting. The gameplay is engaging but simple enough for "less skilled" gamers like me lol. It's cozy, spooky, and has been my favorite way to end the night, along with a warm cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: when i bought beacon pines, i was in need of something autumnal that would satisfy my night in the woods loving selfsomething autumnal i did getbeacon pines is a shorter but adorable game with spooky vibes and an autumnal setting, even though it is set in the beginning of summer the main character and his friends are adorable, even though they sometimes feel older than twelve, but maybe that's just me getting olderthe visuals are stunning and so is the audio, you can tell a lot of love was put into this. the narrator was brilliant, chef's kissnow, for the negatives - i played this game on pc and i don't know if it's just me, but i did have troubles controlling luka at times, he went in the general direction of where i wanted but also not, every time i wanted to go up to the cafe i had to go several times because he ended up running out, but over all this is the most i can come up with in terms of negativesone thing people might not like is that this is a choices based game that doesn't really give you a choice. yeah, multiple endings, but the game won't let you get a bad one unless you turn it off and never look back so if you want to get the most out of the game, you need to get to the true ending aka the one with the credits. so even though the charms are adorable, they don't really give you a choice, more like clues. which brings me to the story. i loved it and i loved how even though you can tell most of the plot twists if you pay just enough attention, they don't feel watered down or poorly done and even then the story can surprise you. the thing is, i don't know how well it stands on its own. the way the story is now is like a big tangled up string so you come to a conclusion, find a dead end, forget the conclusion and then remember it after two other dead ends. great for suspense, not sure how well it would work as well if it were a linear story that didn't throw you all around the place. overall, an evening well spent, especially now with the spooky vibes and all.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly cute and lovely game. Really liked the artstyle and the small unnesessary interactions you can have with the town folks. Plus, you don't need to go through the same dialogues/story every time you want to make another choice, each choice actually does lead to a new path and allows you to progress.However, that's where some ussues lie. You need to go through pretty much every single branch in order to get to the actual ending. On one hand the gameplay is way less repetative than it could have been (which, for me, is a good thing), on the other - the "impacful decisions" part is completely missing. You don't really choose the way the story goes - only the order in which you go through it.The story is fine, I guess. It's not bad, but it's not something amazing either. A lot of characters are underdeveloped, and the main mystery is, once again, not completely dissapointing, but not that amazing either.Regardless of all that, I really enjoyed playing this game and do recommend to try it by yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is absolutely wonderful, with amazing art and incredibly cozy athmosphere. Everything in this game is perfect: the art, the character designs, the character themselves, the story, the music, the narration. The story choice mechanism is brilliant. It's one of the best indie games I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game mostly blind and thought it would just be a cute game about lil animals solving small town mysteries but OH MY GOD??? AM I IN *GRAVITY FALLS????* It took so many turns I didn't expect and i thoroughly enjoyed the characters and plot, I never knew where it was taking me next and I LOVED IT AHHHThere is a choice element, but it does ultimately funnel you towards the good ending which I didn't mind and actually appreciated, but be aware that's how the choice element runs in this!EITHER WAY FULLY RECOMMEND!!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great story. I was invested the entire time and never had a dull moment. Without getting into spoilers, the options and doing certain things to unlock options later was pretty cool. If you're into more story driven games or just want to invest your imagination, totally get the game. I would say it's 110% worth the money. Oh, and the art is absolutely amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The game "Beacon Pines" is a cute short game. It impresses with love to the detail graphics. The gameplay feels smooth, there are no long loading times and the music is harmonious. The biggest feature of the game is that you can choose from a selection of several decisions, which then leads to a different ending. Unfortunately, this feature is not well implemented. Often there is only one possible option, which then leads me to end X, where I unlock the other option in order to move on to another storyline. This means that the game is still very linear and it doesn't really matter which decision I made. Another problem is the game's tempo. While the beginning progresses quickly, the dialog increases as the game nears its end. Too much dialog for me personally. This took the tension out of the game for me in many places. Another problem is that I get thrown out of the game at very exciting points because the right decision is missing. Then you're back in a quiet storyline and have to work your way up to the tension again. That was tedious and almost annoying.All in all, I can recommend the game to anyone who likes cozy and relaxed games. The game is quick to play, maybe it might be better to buy it in the sale because honestly I think the feature is really not implemented.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: While it looks like a point-and-click adventure game, with a few exceptions it structurally is more like a visual novel. Don't expect any kind of challenge-based gameplay.OTOH, it's very cute and the story is reasonably good. If you want a cute (but somewhat strange and occasionally dark) story with cute animal people, this will do nicely.(100% completion in <6 hours. I don't mind, but if you're not okay with pretty short games be warned.)
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is incredible! The art is beautiful, the characters are charming, and the plot GOES PLACES. The beginning "tutorial" seems slow with some hand holding, but don't worry, the narrator lets you go off on your own and you quickly get swept up into the world of Beacon Pines. The game follows Luka and his friends on their mysterious adventures as they try to unravel the secrets of their tiny town. I wasn't sure what to expect when I played, but I was taken away by the plot twists, the reveals, and the cozy/mysterious/suspenseful atmosphere. Definitely recommend this for anyone who loves narrative games, wants to explore branching plots, and is ready for a cozy game with emotional scenes and incredible music! I still think about this game even months after finishing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite an incredible game! I'll admit, it's not my typical genre, but I saw a friend playing and HAD to try it! The story was very compelling and even had me tearing up at the very end. All of the different options make it exciting and interesting as you try to find everything you need to get all of the endings! Besides all of that, the music was PHENOMENAL! An absolutely wonderful game all around if you ask me!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing in so many different ways! The artistic direction is top notch, the story is intriguing, the music is quite nice... What I personally loved tho is the treatment of the choice mechanic: unlike games like telltales where you have to replay the entire game to see alternate paths, this game makes you go over the shorter alternatives while you play, so you're always advancing on the story, just through different turning points that shape your understanding of the story and the characters. Finally, without spoiling, the structure of the narrative is a great echo of the main theme of the game in the structuration of time...
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It was my first visual novel type of game and I must admit this one was really enjoyable. The story was cute and had its moment of tension and creepiness. The cast of character was enjoyable and the artwork simply adorable. The game runs very smoothly. My only complaint would be that the choices are mostly illusions. As you pass through the game you unlock different part and versions of the story but there is only one "real" ending and your choices are only used to unlock those different part/versions of the story in an order that seems pretty much preordained. The story is nice enough and the mystery of the town of Beacon Pines compelling enough that it wasn't a big issue to me. All in a all, it was a good game and a good story. It's a bit expensive for a 5 to 7 hour long story though.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Great narrative adventure. Very short but filled with good writing. It can be a little predictable at some points, but still has some interesting plot twists. The narrator is ok.... can be a bit annoying sometimes. The art is excelent, probably this game's strongest point.Recommended to anyone who wants a short story driven game filled with very likeable characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I... Oh my gosh...It is like playing a choose your own adventure but you feel it so deep. The characters are deep and have had lives and loss, and they have future hopes and dreams. I loved this game. It was really touching and I enjoyed every second - from the art, to the music, to the story, to the narration. I wish I could experience this again for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. This is a  with cute art You play as Luka, a kid who's mother recently went missing. The more you start investigating, the deeper you'll delve down into the rabbit hole. Nothing is as it seems. The unique personalities of these cutesy characters really stand out. They start to grow on you. Especially due to the game's . It's story is sweet, spooky, mysterious and emotional. Iggy, don't look at me, I'm not crying it's my immune system reacting to a foreign substance  ಥ_ಥ, but doesn't feel as linear because you can scuttle around, kicking watermelons along the way. The story let's you revisit certain story paths in a very clever way that doesn't feel repetitive. You'll be collecting  during your play-through by engaging in certain dialogues. Each charm represents a word which, once collected, you can use to change the story at certain points in the game. New story arcs will be revealed, with completely new scenes, new characters to meet and many unexpected outcomes. Slowly you'll start to unravel the mystery, bit by bit, even if you get brutally butchered. Highly enjoyable. Especially enjoyed the dream sequences which slowly turned nightmarish. Music slowly intensifying. Made me sit at the edge of the couch, press X at the very second the narrator finished a sentence, for her to continue reading. Very engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is an amazing story-driven game with dreamy art and one of the most beautiful soundtracks there is. Even though it looks like a multiple-choice game, it is in reality a linear story with an ending that doesn't live up to all its potential. Nonetheless, it's the best work so far from Hiding Spot Games, and - if you like a good mystery - one game that you should surely give a try.Beacon Pines is a cozy and, yet, thrilling game. It has a well-written and engaging story about the life of a kid and their friends living in a small town that sort of exhales some Stranger Things vibes to it. It's a short game that I highly recommend to be played entirely on a rainy Saturday day, it only takes 6 to 10 hours to complete 100% of the game.But beware, even though the game sells the idea of a "multiple ending" game where your choice matters the most, this is not exactly true. Yes, the story of the game branches, but the game keeps pushing you to discover its true ending, so it's basically a linear game with one single ending. This single ending has three "alternate" versions of itself, but are overall the same. If you go with that in mind, you won't be disappointed.The only thing truly disappointing about this game is that some of the "false endings" have a better ending than the TRUE ending of this game. I write this because, compared to 90% of the game, the ending felt rushed, unpolished, and forced. Which is a shame, because I couldn't stop playing this game as I was totally immersed in its story - I mean it: After all the plot twists, all the mysteries, I simply COULDN'T go to sleep until I finished it! And the ending felt... Underwhelming, to say the least.But anyway, this didn't destroy the whole journey. I loved each Beacon Pines characters, its cozy atmosphere, its amazing soundtrack (one of the best I heard to this day!) - Everything was perfect! But I would prefer to wait for a sequel to get the true ending of the game than what was delivered.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I finally finished this beautiful game. I loved every minute. The scenes are gorgeous and well done. Some scenes are like beautifully painted dioramas. The music is excellent. The narrator does such an amazing job. The writing and the story is just excellent. The characters are well written and I was completely invested. The fact that you can move the characters around in the environment the story is taking place I think helps to make the player feel like they really are a part of the story. There aren't any challenging puzzles that need to be solved, combat, or action in the typical sense of a video game. But it's mostly about the experiencing the story, the characters, and the world the story is taking place in. Now I have that feeling that comes when you finish a really good book. You're a little sad that it ended but so happy for the experience of such a good story. I will definitely revisit this one when some time passes. Beacon Pines is excellent.Gameplay Video below
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I'm obsessed with this game! It was an amazing experience and I fell in love with all the characters and their personalities. The fact that you can change the story with charms that you'll find along the way makes this game so fun to play. And the plottwists are amazing. Lovely game to play this fall. I laughed out loud and cried during this game. 5 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinating story with a range of endings from the outlandish to the most soul moving I ever had the pleasure of reading, definitely worth the 5h played.I will buy the art book and sound track when my next paycheck comes in.My reviews tend to be a bit longer than this, however, there's not much I can say, and my heart is still recovering from how enjoyable the story was. I couldn't even think of any headers, or any further improvements. What I can say is that the story grows as you explore each ending, or at each opportunity, and often gives nods to endings you've already encountered, or to endings you've yet to approach. The story-telling was delicate, intricate and powerful, and is definitely enjoyable.I'll probablies revisit the review in the future, when I'm less tired, but damn Beacon Pines is something that has left a massive impression on me.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a unique take on visual novels. As you progress through the branches the story takes you will unlock more options in earlier choices. It's a mechanic that you have to go back to different story lines. This makes it interesting as you find out more about the town and the calamity that will befall it, you start to wonder how the kids you play as are going to find out. It's an amazing story that makes you want to keep playing and messing around with the differing paths. It takes around 4-5 hours to full go through every little thing around Beacon Pines, and I'd happily recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super adorable and yet dark game at times. It's fun to see how different paths affect the story (and they do so quite drastically)Towards the end it gets extremely linear though and the charm mechanism looses more and more of its purpose (imo), but it doesn't sppoil the experience.The story is exciting, the characters are lovable and each of them has their own personality. It's a lot of fun to run around town and speak to everyone and slowly solve the whole mystery.And, ofc, the artstyle is adorable as hell. There is so much love in this game, it's a blast to play. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines isn't your typical cute game. Sure, you play as Luka and explore a charming town, but beneath the adorable surface lurks a hint of something creepy. This unique blend was what hooked me!  The game truly shines with its time-manipulation mechanic. By finding special words, you can rewrite events and experience entirely different storylines. Every decision you make feels impactful, shaping the narrative in surprising ways.The central mystery of Beacon Pines keeps you engaged. Alongside your friends, you'll delve into the town's secrets, uncovering hidden truths. With its beautiful visuals and engaging narration, Beacon Pines offers a truly captivating adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy and charming game, it may seem a bit short but with lovely characters, impeccable art style, exciting story, and gameplay a bit simple but it doesn't make it boring. The charms/choice system is very clever and well made in my opinion, well-made ost and even the narrator is nice to hear, transmitting emotions. This game is like a cozy book to read on a rainy Sunday.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game! Basically an interactive story (not a complaint at all).  The writing is excellent, the art is beautiful, and while it is a short game (5 hours to complete all route choices for me) it didn't feel too short or too long. Plus the true ending is very satisfying. Looking forward to more games from this studio!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS (slightly) AHEADThe visuals are fantastic, every character is bursting with life and, well, character! The music is cute and charming, the charm mechanic is interesting, and the narrator did a wonderful job being the only voice in the game. The game really does feel like a storybook you'd read a child at night before bed, with a storybook ending. The true ending(s) are kinda anticlimactic, but the town is better off and it's a properly happy ending, so that's well worth it.One thing: I kinda wish this was more sinister. Like the very first ending is great because it sets up a sinister tone, but the other ones don't really develop it. It's kinda the same "whisked away by people in yellow suits" or "everyone is frozen", and while it hits hard the first time, it gets repetitive with how many endings are variants of those. All that being said, it's a great game well worth the price, and worth playing through and 100%-ing.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This was soooo good. Super cute character design, but beneth the cutesy desing there's a wonderfully told story. Pretty clever game design and writing where you get snippets from the story throughout the various bransches you explore , even if most end in tragedy and then go back to another to try and find the true ending. You might cry.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Such delight! Although I had already finished the game, I still visit Beacon Pines from time to time. After I got all the achievement and decided it's time to delete the game file, since my laptop doesn't have a lot of storage, but I just couldn't  bring up the strength to do so. Beacon Pines has such brilliant and heartwarming story, lovely characters, it's so hard to say goodbye to them all, especially Rolo, my smartest detective lol. _childDocuments_.review: The story is cute at times, often quite sentimental. The art is beautiful, between the backgrounds and the art style of the characters. It's definitely worth picking it up and playing through, or at the very least watching someone else play it. The way the story is told is really clever imo, and has a lot of potential, more than was used in this game. I really do recommend it and think it's worth your time.That said I can't help but feel some design decisions, pacing and plot problems hold it back from being perfect.Some spoilers for the central mechanic of the game, but you'll be playing through multiple branching paths of the story to gather charms, which grant you additional options at those branch points - all on a quest to find the proper ending to the story. You will often hit branches you are unable to progress down until you progress on other branches to find new charms. Your character remains (supposedly - i'll get to that) unaware of the events of other branches. Vague(ish) spoilers ahead.One of the problems with this, is that this often leads to some real pacing problems, where you can go from urgent mystery and uncovering the plot to, well, not that. The true ending branch is eclipsed by two of the bad ending branches you likely achieved right before it, where most of the plot mysteries are revealed. This really mutes the impact of the ending, making it feel like a formality. It's sort of staggering how rapidly the true ending is over - and because a previous ending spoiled the twist, it hits really weakly.This combines with another issue with the writing - while the character is supposed to be unaware of the events of other branches, it really doesn't come across like this with some of the logical leaps and contrivances they have to make to progress on some of these paths. If you were to cut out the other branches and simply play the 'true ending' path the whole thing would be pretty confusing - it feels like the game wants to have it's cake of separate story branches but eat it too by making those branches overly contingent on the players meta-knowledge. It feels like this could have been avoided by simply having the character remain aware of other events - the core mcguffin of the story even provides an easy avenue to explain why this occurs, and some of the dream sequences, imo, point to this as potentially being an idea during the development that I'm guessing was scrapped.It feels like there was a lot of content here that was cut or never really finished or fleshed out - one of the bad ends involves a fairly mysterious character you only meet in that route, and just leaves a bunch of questions. It's clearly supposed to be a sort of parody/nod at long book series that refuse to end, but in the context of the story is really out of place and makes me wonder if that character (natt) was originally supposed to play a bigger role in the story. This is something shared by a lot of the bad ends in the story - many of them really don't fit, and often feel abrupt like they were supposed to be more involved but got cut down. They *feel* like they're bad writing, which does somewhat fit the theme of the game (being told as a book, with you searching for a good ending) but completely trashes the verisimilitude of the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is one of the most well-written and cleverly-designed games I have ever played.In a whimsical tale with a number of different endings, the book's unnamed "author"/narrator tasks you with finding a finale you can both be satisfied with. The problem is: Beacon Pines is in a bad way; most of the stories's possible paths end in tragedy. These different paths hinge on "Turning Points" - essentially choices in which you can change an action or description in the story by using a Charm, little keepsakes engraves with a word you've picked up somewhere else. In terms of writing, Hiding Spot excels. Beacon Pines is full of charismatic and fun characters, a series of solid mysteries that unfold organically, an interesting premise, inside jokes, and a healthy heaping of irony (with some of the best examples of dramatic irony I've ever seen in literature, to the extent a game is "literature"). There are phrases and themes in the game that pervade the experience and that you'll find yourself remembering for a long time afterwards; in-jokes you'll be smiling at by the end; and character quirks present throughout. It's a hole thing!If there is any area Beacon Pines comes somewhat short in, it would probably be the buildup later in the game. It's possible the team rushed to push this game out. It's far from unfinished, but a few things were wrapped up somewhat quickly. There's certainly nothing that ruins the game, just a some things that could use improvement. It's interesting to note that not all of the scenes in the (current) trailer seem to appear in the final game (you'll have to play to find out which ones, though).Overall though, this game is one of my favorite of all time, and certainly the best one I've played in 2022. I wholeheartedly recommend it for any story-lovers looking for a fun, interesting tale. If you like games with good stories, charismatic and "cute" artwork covering "creepy" undertones, and fun and interesting characters, you might enjoy Beacon Pines. Its twists and turns never disappoint, but across all the branches of the Chronicle, there's only one thing I can say for certain.This is a story about change.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Looks beautiful- Great voice acting (narration only)- Pleasant soundtrack- Fantastic story telling - Engaging game-play. Its basically a visual novel (in quite a literal sense since you are playing out a story read from a book) but you are free to walk around between various dioramas of beacon pines town and interact with characters in a semi open world. The other unique aspect of the game-play is that at various points you are given the option to drastically effect the story by deciding on a particular word in the book such as a particular emotion or action.  You can go back to these turning points at any stage and also play out several branches simultaneously if you wish by switching back and forth. Its a really interesting mechanic and the implementation here is fantastic. There are also a couple of mini-games which also involve the different words you have gathered. Overall its a great package.Cons- Only the narration is voice acted. There is  a lot of dialog between characters that is just text. I understand voice acting is expensive.- The dioramas of beacon pines are nice and I do understand they are meant to be illustrations of the book but i would have preferred more traditional fully fledged scenes. - No Mouse supportApart from the no mouse support, I really had to struggle and nit pick to find any cons at all. _childDocuments_.review: Prologue:I dived into, Beacon Pines, completely blind folded and I'm glad I did. I don't even remember how I stumbled onto this game. What I do know is, it's a story book that will spell bind you until The End.Chapter:P.S. Personal Taste.BEACON PINES, ENCHANTED ME. I love personal writing; when the Writers know how to tear their Hearts open and show you the Love and Pain that afflicts us all. And, I’m sure we can remember countless amounts of Writers that disappointed us with their writing completely void of any personality.Not, Beacon Pines.It’s more than love letters to Adventure Book’s, the narrative is more than plot driven nor personal bias. I see a well written book, and this theme translated very well into the game. I’ve become attached too, Luka, Rolo, Beck, ‘cause the Writer’s made them real to me; not many books nor games make me laugh and cry, or let me care about the mirthful and tragedy’s that befall characters. Beacon Pines, is a perfect character driven story; the branching narrative threads slowly unravel the truths in a way that’s grounded to the choices characters make.I can only assume and hope for the Dev’s to understand, they’ve helped create a very special game. I cannot yet fathom how much Beacon Pines means to me, and I can’t forget my experience. If I somehow forget, I hope to laugh and cry the same again.The End?

_childDocuments_.review: I was tempted to call this "Stranger Things for furries" but nah this game deserves more than quips, it's a short but lovely, warm experience.General premise is that you play as a deer kid, Luka, who stumbled onto some shady going-ons in his tiny hometown. With a growing bunch of friends and acquaintances he then tries to get to the bottom of it. There's everything, really, multiple overlapping secret conspiracies, weird science, mass scale coverups. Also character growth and revelations, so it's a full, proper, satisfying plot.The gameplay is pretty simple too if you even call it that. While there are some interactive scenes and minigames, you mostly roam around the town, interact with character, and explore the branching story - see, there's this branching timeline thing, while playing you unlock words that go into a sentence at some major story turning point, and that's how you progress trough narrative. Must say though, it's less properly non-linear in that things are paced in the optimal way, in the middle of game there will be several branches to explore at a time, later on there will be like one viable option at a time. On other hand the way how branching stories take you to very different spots all while feeling like same story is really thoughtful.The art style is really nice, and so is soundtrack, though I think stylistically what fascinates me most is how they managed to combined almost childish storybook and cartoon characters with more teen or young adult oriented narrative full of mystery conspiracies, death and people swearing. It just works, it may sound clashing when described but they made it work in practice!It's short, like 6-7 hours but if you're sold on the premise and the feel just go ahead, the game is plain satisfying, trough and trough!

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon pines hits all the right notes.  The art, characters, animations, and story all delivered and kept me engaged the entire time. _childDocuments_.review: I was one of the backers for this game and I must say that it was absolutely worth it to see the game completed! This is a fantastic little story that I believe is fully worth your time and money.PLOT: Luka VanHorn is just about to be starting his summer in Beacon Pines when his best friend, Rolo, tells him he has seen strange things at the Valentine Warehouse. With boyish curiosity spurring him forward, Luka suddenly finds himself embroiled in a plot that could spell his doom! But, with your help and the power of "Charms", you can help Luka to create a proper happy ending for this story!PROS: While it is simple, I quite like how the "Charm" system works in this game, as it creates a fascinating system that allows you to explore the story and learn more and more as time goes on. It also goes a fairly good job at creating the various branches that you will use these "Charms" on.The characters are very well done for the story, with special props going to our main characters Luka, Rolo, and Beck. All of them feel like real kids in both ways good and bad. They aren't always perfect and can even be little brats at times, but they are good children and never seem malicious in the way they act. The other characters are well done too, each one fitting a good balance of funny and intriguing.One of the best things about the game, however, is the overall presentation. The art is incredible, looking like a storybook brought to life right upon the pages. The animation is also pretty good, never feeling stiff or janky. Perhaps one of the best parts, however, is the music. The soundtrack for this game, by Matt Meyer, is incredible, creating emotions of wonder, serenity, melancholy, and tension, even managing to easily shift between these emotions when necessary.CONS: While the game is absolutely worth a playthrough, one unfortunate thing to note is that not ALL of the charms you collect throughout the game are used too often, if at all. It's a shame we didn't get to use some of these, but at the same time a few of these charms would've been so specific that they'd probably only be used for singular moments in the game. But if they eventually make a sequel, I would love to see them find a use for any and all "Charms" that are collected.Overall: A game that was worth all the money that was put into it! If you love these sorts of stories, I couldn't recommend it enough! Give it a try and enjoy! I'm sure you'll be just as CHARMED as I was~ XDEDIT: This game is going to be getting further updates in the future, including a cooking minigame that will hopefully mean more of the charms will be used in funny, cute ways! Looking forward to it! :D

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a game that took me a while to get into, not because I didn't think it was intriguing, but because I had forgotten about it in the midst of all the other games that came out during its first release period. With its quirky characters and amazing drawn out emotive situations to the soundtrack, it is every bit as brilliant as a game like Steins Gate or even Ai Somnium Files. I was so engrossed in it that I couldn't put it down for 8 hours. That is an impressive achievement given that I can usually only tolerate two hours of gameplay, even with games I enjoy. _childDocuments_.review: 11 hours later and I'm officially done with this game -- I think there's one more route I can take, but I got what I can only assume is the best ending, so I'm not in a hurry to experience anything else. This isn't really the type of game that I feel the need to go into any great detail about in a review, but I guess I will anyway. It's a sweet, sad, and beautiful story with some really good, and often amusing writing that tells the story of a small town, and its trials and tribulations. As with any fictional town 'out of time' like Beacon Pines -- which is to say, it's sorta like a time capsule; almost feeling like a town that would've existed back in the 70s or something -- there's dark secrets hiding in the town's past and present.It's up to your little rag-tag gang of cute, but very intelligent kids to solve the mysteries and save the day. I think the biggest thing I keep coming back to when I think of this game is just how competent the characters feel. A lot of games that feature children behave as if they're stupid, and incapable of understanding what's going on around them. Beacon Pines treats its cast, even the youngest among them, as real 'people' (or animal people, I suppose), and gives their writing all the respect it deserves. To be clear, I don't think this game is absolutely incredible. It is not the most compelling tale I've experienced in recent memory, nor does it have amazing gameplay or the best characters ever or anything like that -- It's just a good, honest, linear, heartfelt adventure game. Please go into it expecting that. This is not a 80-hour game where your choices have major weight. This is a linear adventure game that's structured in a way that uses your choices to guide you along the same path as everyone else, but in an interesting way that helps your experience feel a little more personal. I don't really have anything else to say. Beacon Pines is money well spent, and so long as Steam has a binary recommendation system, this will be an easy 'Yes' from me.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, I enjoyed it. The art is good, was really impressed with the details of the characters during conversations. The game does feel a little short for its price however; I got 100% in about 4 hours. As is generally the case for narrative heavy games, there's no replayability to it. Once you have seen and done, there is no reason to come back. Also, there isn't a whole lot of game to it. It's a walk around and talk to people / interact with things and occasionally make a decision kind of experience. The decisions are also strangely not at all impactful as not only can you revert to any decision point, but you must in order to reach the true ending. _childDocuments_.review: This game was such a joy to play, and I really enjoyed every moment of this game.  I had found it at a Steam Next Fest last year in September and fell in love with the demo from there.  The story, the music, the art style of the game itself...  It was all so wonderful and captured my attention so well that I had immediately added it to my wishlist.  Being able to play this game a year later instilled that same love for the game as it had before and is one of the very few games that I made sure I purchased on its release day.The movement animations remind me of Scribblenauts and has an enjoyably cartoonish feel to how you moved around.  The actual character drawings and expressions were wonderful and adorable.  It was clear who was a child and who was an adult, though I loved how fluffy and soft everyone looked.  It's a unique style that works perfect for this and the characters being depicted.  Every character is memorable in their personalities, from shady Mr. Nuncreed, to the excitable Rolo, to even the adorable and knowledgeable Kado.  The soundtrack was beautiful and fitting for every moment of the game as well.  My favorite song out of them all was the lullaby that Luka and his mother Eleanor sang together.  I would honestly buy the soundtrack just for that song alone, though the rest of the tracks were just as wonderful.  It could change from playful to remorseful to stressful at any given time, which is what any good soundtrack would do.  I would absolutely spend a lot of time outside of the game listening to the music from this game again.Now, the storyline for this was original and enrapturing from start to finish.  It starts off as a small, sleepy town just trying to make ends meet after a terrible catastrophe, but this eventually ramp up with what the town has to do, resulting in several plot twists that kept the reader surprised without adding in any unnecessary questions.  Even with the multiple time-lines and endings, there were always answers to the questions that were posed throughout the story so the true ending felt well-deserved for the characters and completely rounded.  It does however leave room for a potential sequel if the devs ever decide to do so, but otherwise the game finishes on a wonderfully beautiful moment.  I personally do not think there are any cons to the game itself, other than it can be time consuming to gather the charms you need to further the story, but even then the game itself makes it easy to backtrack and figure out what your missing and even gives hints here and there to help find the charms you want and need for the story.  I loved every moment of playing this game, and it had permanently found a spot in my favorite games list.  Perfect amount of content and game play for the price, and it absolutely is not a purchase you would ever regret making.  I thank the devs for making such a wonderful game, and I absolutely recommend anyone with a love for great stories to pick this one up!!
