_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines takes you on an adventure in a small, modest town harboring a big and eerie secret. An accurate way to describe this adventure would be as 'a cute and cozy version of a Stephen King piece'. In this choose-your-own-adventure-style game, the mystery unravels as you navigate different branches of the story. You acquire new words by experiencing one of the many storylines, and these words can unlock different story branches. The relaxed gameplay is accompanied by an exquisite atmosphere, meticulous storytelling and a hint of humor, creating an immersive experience. I highly recommend it if these kind of games spark an interest in you.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I have extremely conflicting thoughts about this game because I am excruciatingly close to being in love with it, the characters are likeable, the dialogue is snappy, the mystery is compelling and the game is immaculately illustrated. So why then, do I go with Not Recommended?It's a problem I lay mostly at the feet of its structure. Beacon Pines's core gameplay concept is about collecting "Charms" which are essentially keywords that you can slot into sentences that change the trajectory of the narrative. That's the sell anyway, evocative of branching narratives and adventure game style puzzle solving with your word arsenal, but in practice Beacon Pines is a mostly linear affair where you bounce back and forth between whichever point in the timeline you most recently acquired a single charm for that will allow you to advance that timeline.So already this is probably going to be fatal to a lot of people expecting a non-linear experience, you're not getting one. This in general smack of a game that had bigger aspirations but had to get its scope cut back for time or budget but despite this I was still willing to meet the game halfway and attempt to enjoy it as a linear visual novel, a genre I have no qualms with.But even that proved challenging because of its cut down aspirations to non-linearity. You're constantly chopping back and forth between occasionally very brief bits of the timeline and needing to constantly recalibrate yourself to what characters know at that point in that timeline and it can result in the story feeling a bit stop and start in the middle even when the twists start rolling in hot and frequent. This culminates in the story's unfortunately pretty weak actual ending branch where the story has largely let all of the air out of its proverbial balloon by burning through all of its twists on the other routes, leaving what's supposed to be the Grand Finale to quite literally fizzle out instead and go to Epilogue. This causes other problems because the "true" timeline has the characters uncover surprisingly few of the truths to the mystery, so you're left to assume everyone just got backfilled on what they missed between the ending and the epilogue which is very Awkward Storytelling. Particularly two of the game's best scenes ("Hum" and "Accept") simply don't happen on the true branch, which kind of retroactively blunts one's impression of them.And yet despite all of this, I do not *dislike* Beacon Pines, I am in fact, really close to extremely liking it. But the question is "would I recommend this to people?" and my answer to that is "No.", which is upsetting! I ultimately want the game to succeed and do well because there's something truly Great here that I hope the team gets a second crack at attempting. But ultimately, Beacon Pines is a game that I don't think does either its central gameplay concept or its wonderful characters and setting the justice they truly deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEWING EVERY GAME I'VE PERFECTED:One of the very few games I can confidently and happily rate 10/10The art style is beautiful, from the simple in-game art style, the highly detailed renders during conversation, and the amazing sketches in the turning point journal, every piece of art in this game captured my attention fully, I found myself investigating everything just to see more of the art it had to offer, it was truly beautifulThe character design, appearance and personality wise, while simple, was very effective and memorable, I found myself getting attached to almost every single character. They're all designed beautifully with their own unique personalitiesThe story was incredible. If linear, the story would've been short, but the mechanic of the turning points in this game allowed for a long-winded, engaging story, allowing you to piece  things together through the other paths you have taken. But the actual story itself is incredibly constructed and well written, I found myself on the verge of tears multiple times, it truly captures your attention and your feelings. _childDocuments_.review: Didn't expect to get so emotional over a cute animal storybook, but there we are! It's partly because of how adorable everything is that the story hits so hard. And everything is so absolutely adorable! The character art is gorgeous, and I couldn't wait to meet more people around town just to see how they look up close; the backgrounds are so lovely I wish I could live in Beacon Pines; the music is wonderful, and the Animal-Crossing-esque "dubbing" is very suited to each character (even if it sometimes gets a little bit grating on the ear). And lastly, the narration is so full of personality and emotion that it's impossible not to be moved by and with it.The gameplay itself is very clever, inviting the player to explore different outcomes by changing choices in key plot moments, a bit like old "choose your own path" books. Initially I was worried it might get repetitive to go through the same story beats again and again, but the game works very well in creating new paths while keeping in mind what the player has already learned from others. It makes for a really cool storytelling experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: When i bought this game i didn't know anything about it. But i liked the art style and the fact that some reviews compared it to Night in the Woods, a game i really love.And i didn't get disappointed. Beacon Pines is a really nice story, well told on many levels: Fun, drama, nostalagia, adventure, likable characters, well written dialogue, a great story teller voice, good music and visual art. Not a challenging game at all (there's no combat, no puzzles, just a few minigames), but just the right game to grab the controller, lean back and enjoy a good story. It's kinda like a visual novel, but with more walking around and exploring stuff.A true little indie gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend!I can't say much without spoiling the story, but in short:- the voice acting is top notch- the story is emotional at times- good character development along the branching paths- Crucially, the game doesn't make you replay the whole thing from scratch to get to the different choice you need to make for each path.I honestly don't have a negative thing to say about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the mystery and thriller this game presented. The game is about 5 hours, which is typically shorter compared to most visual novels, but it was still a great experience nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It's an amazing game, I finished the game 100% withing 6 hours in one sitting and it was well worth it!It's a unique way of story telling that I really enjoyed and got infested in the story and the people.The way they  give you smaller and bigger endings that vary dramatically makes you want to work towards the one ending you see fit.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I was given this game as a birthday gift and played through the whole thing before bedtime.It's not a challenging game - in fact, I'd say it's more like reading a really nonlinear book with animated illustrations. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one that is so into story games but this game just got me interested so fast that i played the demo before the game came out and knew i had to get it.I so recommend this game because of all the cute characters and good story and i even like the way you can decide the stories its such an unique way.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little story. Basically, a visual novel with a few branching paths to go through and a few locations to walk through. Nothing great, nothing bad.Story: straight-forward story that you discover piece by piece through the different paths. A few reveals, but nothing exactly surprising.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Not the best anthropomorphic-animals-in-a-small-town game (Night in the Woods), and not terribly original in its small-town-with-a-dark-secret plot, but still a thoroughly entertaining story. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game.. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: i've never written a review before, but i think this game warrants it. i went into it expecting something lighthearted and cozy, maybe a little spooky. i got that and more. the writing was phenomenal and made even greater by the voice-acting. the art was gorgeous, and the music really set the scene. made me feel like i was a child again, gripped by the words of a whimsical novel.all in all, a poignant yet beautiful tale about loss, fate, and most importantly of all: change.

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is an Adventure game narrated with Visual Novel and Choose Your Own Adventure elements. You play Luka VanHorn, a twelve year old who was befallen with a second tragedy after his father died when he was six, this time his mother disappeared under mysterious circumstances. Not wanting to lose another parent, Luka embarks on an investigative journey with his good friend Rolo, and the first stop is the abandoned old warehouse of Beacon Pines.At one with Luka in terms of suffering tragedies, the town of Beacon Pines and its residents being mostly a farming town are picking up the pieces of what they call “the Foul Harvest”. Which triggered after the unexpected death of the owner of a fertilizer company, Valentine’s, the company that was helping to build the town. As things and the town start to wane, a new company steps in out of nowhere, hoping to revive the town's fortune, but at what cost?As you slowly start to explore Beacon Pines, you’re introduced to “Charms”, a story mechanic that lets you respond to the story and alter its course at vital junctures. For this is where Beacon Pines develops its unique way of storytelling, as responding to a situation with a different charm will write the story in a certain way, but often it leads the player down a path that ends the story. However, the player can “rewind” and choose another alternative Charm to steer the story away from an unfortunate end.Beacon Pines is filled with colourful and interesting characters that when given the chance to interact with, always gives the player a bit more of an idea of their personality and such. Interactions and Points of Interest in Beacon Pines don’t repeat, meaning once the player has interacted with it, it won’t be available again in most cases.The story of Beacon Pines shines in the way it is delivered. The beginning and ending of chapters and story bits are delivered by a narrator who does an exceptional job at delivering the story and always makes you feel like you’re experiencing the story together with the narrator side by side as she reacts as you are, to events that occurred.With some expert delivering, that standard of storytelling continues on to the gameplay aspect of it when you play. The path it goes, the unexpected (some expected) twists, the multiple sides to the characters that develop them further and not be one dimensional may not be new but it keeps the player at the edge of their seat.There is plenty to gush about in Beacon Pines. But there are bits that should be known coming in, though it starts off as a story with branching paths, it is linear in the end as the player will go through multiple charms before getting a “proper” ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes you find a game with cute cartonish graphics, with that open feel good vibe and think it'll be just a little heartwarming story. But then, you slowly notice little hints of weirdness that eventually run in an intricate maze of awe and wonder. This game is exactly that. Under the "Stardew Valley" coat we have a tale heavily reminding of the weirdness of Twin Peaks (the title of the game is a vague reminder).The story is build with different paths that can be chosen using chasms the player might find, and taking the plot in very different directions. Every "path" shows us some part of the story, being both complementary and alternative to each other. All of it flows in such a neat and rewarding way you basically can't stop playing it,  what's lurking behind your next choice. I'm surprised this game is not more well-known than it actually is, it's a little gem everyone should play. There is no difficulty, it's just us discovering the story and getting to know the complex events surrounding this only apparently calm town. I'm sure even the Log Lady would appreciate it.Just go and get it <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game was wonderful!I've had it on my wish list since forever and finally got to experience it!At first I was a little disappointed that the overworld sprites weren't exactly like the talking ones but that quickly passed as I played more and more, can't picture this game without both now!I have to say I have never played a story game like this one, having the freedom to do whatever I wanted and being encouraged to explore every possibility was great and really felt like you were trying to craft the perfect story WHILE actually figuring out the whole plot!My mind was blown multiple times as every plot twist in every other reality made me look at every NPC differently!Obviously I'm a furry so being the target audience for this maybe makes me regard the game higher than normal, but I really think that all the characters being animals helped so much with making them memorable and especially helping with me making their voices match their looks. Which I must say having the freedom to read aloud and match the voices of the characters to the little sounds each one of them makes was so nice, I highly recommend to play the game like this even if you're playing by yourself!(bonus points if you gave all of the towns folk more country-men accents :D)And speaking of voices, huge shout out to the narrator!She was so lovely to listen to and really felt like she was right there with you through the whole journey!I love that in some scenes you can just FEEL how wide she was smiling while reading her lines!!!As a whole I think this is an unforgettable experience and I must congratulate everyone involved in this wonderful game you guys made!So much of it was relatable to some of my life that I feel like I can revisit this game time after time and get a new experience!Thank you!

The writing feels very natural, and the story is the right mix of charming, wholesome, and unsettling to really hit the right beats both for the Twin Peaks-y supernatural happenings in a small town and for the coming-of-age tale of a boy caught up in it. A few word choices seemed a bit off given that this game would naturally appeal to a younger audience. Use of words that some would consider swearing such as ♥♥♥♥ and ass appear in the game (not incredibly heavy but noticeably there against an otherwise very child friendly title). _childDocuments_.review: The truest form of 'choose your own adventure'. This game somehow manages to be quirky, campy, and endearing which is quite the feat. Your aim is to complete a full story start to finish all while choosing actions that your hero takes. Some plot lines are terrifying, others are heartwarming, and others will have you emotionally invested. It's a quick game - I completed all story arc avenues and achievements within 5 hours of play time. It's a quirky little game but it had me compelled and enthralled the entire time. Well worth my time and money and that's what I hope every game to be. Overall 9/10 - There's no true replayability which is a shame, but I was emotionally invested throughout the entire 5 hours I put into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure whether one could call this "playing a game" or rather "reading a storybook". It reminds me of those kind of very old book series for children where you could actually do this with a real book, although the paths and stories were way shorter back then (written press limitations). This game is taking me right back to my childhood and enhancing that awesome sensation of taking command of the story, with great storytelling, heartfelt images and a wonderful world full of mystery. It's a wonderful game and I really recommend it to anyone who loves reading - or listening- to a great story, with the plus that you are the one in control. Everett's Many-Worlds Interpretation in all of its glory!
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as gift from a wonderful friend :) This game is so well written. It is a mystery set in a small town of cute characters. However do not be fooled, the art style may be cute but the story is dark in parts. And not every path will end up being a happy ending, but the story allows you to roll back to certain time line events and chose an alternate path. Each time you go back you reveal more pieces of the overall puzzle. It is very well done! A lot of "ah ha" moments as you get closer to the end of the story. It took me just over 5 hours to complete the game. I experienced no crashes, no bugs and it supports wide screen (not ultra wide but you will get black bars on each side). The game uses the keyboard only, no mouse. However it has a option for controllers too if you like. A really polished game that is rich with vibrant characters, beautiful artwork, and a intelligently written story that leads up to a great ending. 📚
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and creepy is definitely the best way to describe this game. Surprisingly dark at times too, considering the kid protagonists. Some heavy themes here about loss, acceptance, moving on, growing up, ect. Visuals are great, very colorful and easy to see what's going on at all times. Plays a bit like a visual novel, a bit like a point and click, a bit like a mystery game, and yet none of those. Remember the old Winnie the Pooh cartoons with a narrator following Pooh through a book that was also a world the cast lived in? Yep, like that. You'll be trying to find the best ending while getting some bad ends, some not quite right ones, ect. The game encourages finding all the endings, with branching paths opening up as you find new "badges" (life lessons? experiences? whatever) to apply to older situations that you didn't have before, and the ability to immediately go back to those points in the story as desired. Kind of a short game (I should finish it/get all the achievements at around the 5 hour mark, with no guides helping me) but I feel like I got my money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines is a non-linear adventure game with one 'true' ending and epilogue. The game is told in a meta-narrative context where the player is offered ten choice points (plus a tutorial one that only matters for that specific conversation, and a flashback to fishing with Luka's dad). The choice points, other than the pond sequence, are represented on a literal branching tree map. There are around a dozen outdoor locations in the main town, and another five remixed versions accessible on certain paths. Certain snatches of dialogue and interactable items provide Charms that allow the player to perform different actions at choice points. Many of these are necessary to achieve the true ending - although a handful only matter for the pond sequence where fishing for all possible items grants an achievement. Individual sections of gameplay mainly show linearity by not allowing Luka to travel in certain directions if he has something 'important' he'd rather do in a different part of town at that point in time.Because of the quest to find Charms, most of the dead-end non-standard game overs are necessary to achieve the final ending - although there are several that are included mainly for enriching the storyline or setting up jokes. The perspective is consistently told through the eyes of the player character, although there are divergences to observe other characters interacting. The narrator will also take breaks from the interactive portion of the gameplay to narrate Luka's dreams and flashbacks to his mom uncovering the conspiracy enveloping Beacon Pines.The non-story game mechanics are satisfying with the ability to run around a very nicely painted world with neat characters. There's a jump button that's only included for enhancing player experience as it isn't used to solve any puzzles. There's a throw mechanic accessible in some areas for throwing berries and snowballs - it's hard to aim, but the stakes are low as there's unlimited ammo. There's some cool 'toys' such as a smackable watermelon that plays a nice beat and grants a 'Smack' Charm, as well as a field of fluffy dandelions that will blow away as the player runs Luka through them - which will 'Tickle' his nose the first time through, granting a Charm and causing Luka to sneeze. There's probably only about five minutes worth of non-story game mechanics spread across the five hours of story-based gameplay, which were fortunately well-represented in the short demo released alongside the game's Kickstarter. The full release is aimed at players who want to experience the story and the fairly unique way that it's presented. A hundred percent completion run generally takes three to four hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It would be a disservice to say that this game is anything less than perfect. It is an expertly distilled, bite-sized gaming experience with an abundance of passion, love, and joy poured into it.It is short. And while it is the perfect length and doesn't run too short by any means, I still wish it was longer, in the same way I wish a gorgeous book is longer when I finish it, and I sit there clutching the tome to my chest and sighing wistfully as I leave the world within, never able to experience it for the first time ever again.But I can share it with others. I can take joy in knowing others will experience it for the first time, and feel their own feelings the games brings out of them. And if I share it with people I know, they can give me little snippets of insight into what they find within, and I can feel the embrace of this wonderful world for a fleeting moment once more.Please, play this. And please share it with the people you love once you are done. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: beacon pines would be better described as a visual novel, an incredibly well crafted visual novel that goes beyond mere nostalgia with its plot and feel inspired by stranger things and the goonies. the characters and lovable, the writing is tight and the entire audiovisual department kicks it out of the park. the only thing i'd complain about is the level of control the player has of the story, which is not that much at all, but the story itself and how it presents to the player is good enough to compensate. had a great time, would love to revisit again in the future, replayability be damned
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: lovely!! i enjoyed my playthrough and i really love how the story is being told through different paths while *still* being very linear (you explore different endings until finding the good one). i thought the storytelling was really well done and i got really attached to the characters!! if you like visual novels, i think you'd like it. i don't think it fits the "Choose Your Own Adventure" tag that well though.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and intriguing game that definitely has you interested in continuing to play as the story unfolds. It is an extremely simple game however with little replay value based on the way it flows. Regardless, I'm definitely going to play the game from start to finish again another time down the line. My only personal qualm with the game is the fact that the very beginning isn't part of the post-game navigation. I would really like to see (spoilers)  I understand why this isn't the case, but still rather disappointing. If you love talented storytelling, beautiful artwork and interesting narration, this game will definitely be one you'll enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRThe Good: An interesting take on the Choose-Your-Adventure genere.The Bad: A sprint button wouldn't hurted.The ???: I guess I'm a furry now.Full disclosure, I backed this game on the kickstarter.Beacon Pines is a charming valley town with a dark secret. That you know, as a reader is your job to find an end to the story. That encapsules the gameplay loop of this simple game: you poke around and find out what are the consequences of your choices. The game is beatiful, and beatifully narrated to, inviting you to investigate everything that can be investigates to see what is exactly what the Narrator will tell you, with the charm system as a reward. The charms are a nice and clever way to make you naviaget the story, as when you obtain one you quickly begin to wonder where it can be used to obtain a different result on a previous dead end.The story itself follows the threads of that kid of exotic adventures a Choose-Your-Adventure might have, they start with a mystery that hooks you and then branch out, with plot twists and reveals at every turn. The more holistic aproach this game takes, as well a the chance to easily retrace to certain key moments for retrials, allow you to explore the world and fish for all the details, helping you piece together the big picture throug diferent iterations of the same fundamental event.The overall shortness of the game might be its biggest draw back, as well as the fact that the choices offered at key moments are not that innovative, nor is the plot at certain points. Navigating the world, specially once you have become familiarized with it, can also become a bit of a chore, specially with the walking speed of the protagonist.That being said my overall review of Beacon Pines is very positive and I greatly recomend it to anyone who might be reading this.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: When i sponsored this on kickstarter i was had no idea whether this game was going to be good or bad. i can say with great joy in my heart that this game is awesome. The story and gameplay are amazing. All the characters are well developed and you come to love them all. I know they were joking about a sequel but i really hope they do make one.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game AND a great story! I had a few crashes and not knowing where I would be when I went back in was a little frustrating, but I'm really glad I stuck it out and got to the end(s) of the story. I appreciate the way this game handles the branching logic paths and never felt like I was just redoing something for the sake of redoing it. Everything with a purpose. Plus, the graphics are super cute and really coherent in application.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon pines is a cute and an engaging game with its twisted storylines. I am slightly disappointed in the game as I expected it to be more rpg and explore more; the charms of the game really drove it.. (which is the whole point) Characters are cute, engaging and well written.Art: very pleasing. It’s one of the reasons why I wanted this game. _childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game. You play as Luka, the main character in the story book, but you also exist outside of the book. You have an unknown name or appearance, and your only instructions are from a feminine voice, asking for your help finding the good ending to the story. You start Luka's journey after his father has passed and his mother has gone missing. Your grandma came from out of town to take care of you, but she's not who she seems. As you adventure through the story's world and people, you realise things are not how they seem and the town has some deep hidden secrets. With your friends by your side, you're tasked with saving the town and exposing the truth. Follow each path to go deeper and deeper into the story.The game works like a mad lib. You fill in a word in the sentence of the story and the whole path changes. You need to get the correct sequence of choices to reveal the true ending, but will more likely hit the bad endings of the story first. I normally wouldn't like a game like this, but the game let's you pick off where the choice was and lets you make a new one. As you go along the story, you discover other words that you can use to fill in the choices.The story is amazing and had me wanting to discover more. It did get a bit confusing here and there, trying to remember what part of the story I was on, but it wasn't too bad. I finished it in about 3.5 hours I believe and got all the endings I could find. The art style is beautiful and the story draws you in. I couldn't stop playing! I discovered no bugs or glitches and the UI and controls were almost perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! It was cute, creepy, and had me laughing out loud at the same time. It was not what I expected, but it was an interesting twist on a story-driven game. Instead, each branch uncovered more truths to the main story, even when taken on paths where you were meant to fail. It was cleverly done, and I'm so happy I decided to pick up this gem of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly charming atmosphere, lovable characters and a decent story with some surprisingly dark twists. The unique hook of  is the ability to alter the story and experience different timelines, like in an adventure book where at the different endings, instead of having to restart, you get to choose a different outcome in key scenes. However, in order to choose all possible outcomes you have to traverse and explore the world a little bit, finding hidden items and emotions scattered throughout that can then be used to explore different timelines.To be honest, I was a bit worried at first, because I don't really enjoy replaying story sequences, but  does an excellent job making sure that you don't do that. In fact, despite the different timelines and outcomes, the overall story is actually quite linear for the player and the game's narrator (the only character with a real voice, but no face). This becomes a little bit of a problem towards the end, when the player and the narrator both know more about what's going on than the characters (which are stuck in a particular timeline), as the game still tries to not repeat itself and thus big emotional or dramatic developments from other timelines are often revealed to the characters in throwaway lines. If you were to experience only the main path (you can't, since you have to find the keys to unlock the main path in the side paths), the emotional impact of the story and several motivations would be totally different (in a bad way), which poked at the back of my mind while playing the epilogue. Speaking of which, the ending has a positive and uplifting vibe for all characters, but realistically, it's still quite ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and full of problems. I don't know if there is a secret ending (I don't think so?!?), but the fate of some characters is a bit too grim for the happy-go-lucky storybook ending that the game portrays. Or maybe that's just me...Anyways, I had a good time for about five hours, so I do want to recommend the game for its story, unique approach to telling its story and mostly for its exceptionally cute and lovable character design.

Nothing was amiss. 10/10 in my book and I'm picky.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the whole game on XBGP and loved it so much I bought it through steam! The game is an amazing story-centric experience presenting itself as a unique choose-your-own-adventure book in a digital format. It works multiple timelines into one fluid experience that builds on the alternating timelines upon itself. It doesn't make you feel like you know too much while it's story progresses as the 4th wall, and so every story arc feels unique and provides new content!Along your travels across Beacon Pines you will find chunks of story that you will be able to predict, however the story-telling systems in place provide more than ample opportunity to still surprise you! You may play a good continuous chunk of one story-line and learn things that aren't apparent in another series of events, but that series will then expand on the questions you had about the previous timeline. It works so well for story telling in a linear story that I am more than excited to experience the game over-and-over to experience the majority of alternate timelines in a different order and to see where the game checkpoints carry you between those events!If you're looking for a long game, this isn't it, it can be completed in less than 5 hours. However, the story is definitely worth experiencing at least once for the price, imo. If you are a hunter for replayability, there's only one story here, only how much of each series of events can you experience in continuity changes... If you just enjoy story-telling and unique characters, this is right up your alley! If you're a big fan of unique art and anthro characters... This is right up YOUR alley... If none of this appeals to you, I urge you to continue searching for your next experience.I also neglected to mention the killer soundtrack, so if you like collecting OSTs this game has a fantastic track list.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and surprisingly emotionally heavy game. _childDocuments_.review: Twelve-year-old Luka has already dealt with his fair share of tragedy. Six years earlier, he lost his father, and more recently, his beloved mother has vanished without a trace, leaving him in the care of his loving (but mysterious) grandmother. Now, on the first day of summer, Luka has decided he wants answers, and sets out on his own investigation with Rolo, his best friend, and Beck, a new girl looking for some excitement. But as these stories are wont to do, it soon becomes apparent that things aren't what they seem..."Beacon Pines" isn't necessarily a game that does anything new or groundbreaking. Instead, it's a pretty standard adventure game that does what it does really, really well. The game's main draw is the story, which has a noteworthy gimmick: charms. These charms you find throughout the game represent different words, and at critical points of the story, different words can be used to determine which direction the story goes.And I will give this game credit, they did a great job mapping the story out. Depending on what words you use, the story can veer off in a completely different direction that makes sense to the overall narrative, and seeing all these different directions is what will ultimately help you find the best ending.Just be warned: despite the cutesy-looking character and background designs, this story can get dark. As you start to learn more about exactly what's going on in Beacon Pines, the stakes get much higher. And the fact that Luka and his friends are kids does not mean they are exempt from being threatened.In short, "Beacon Pines" isn't a terribly long game (I finished it in a little over three hours), but if you like games with a cute-looking art style and a deep story, I'd say give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely cute narrated 'choose your own adventure' story-game.* Lovely character and environmental art* Good characters you want to learn more about as the story progresses* Very chill musical scoreThe interesting twist is that the story branches through choices you can make at a variety of key moments, sometimes leading to wildly different endings which aren't shy of being a bit gruesome and dark. You can also return to key moments at any time, and pick different choices. Plot points are revealed little by little as you explore branches of the narrative tree.The story here has a little bit of a stranger things vibe, the player character and companions mostly being kids up against a big weird maybe-paranormal conspiracy. As said, it can get dark - which is not to say it gets genuinely frightening - this is a pretty kid friendly version of dark, good October spooky fodder.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the few negative reviews of this game verses the positive ones, there seems to be one determining factor as to whether you like this Beacon Pines, so I'll just lay it out up front:This is a visual novel that has one true ending.  It is a "choose your own adventure" type story, but it is one that intentionally winds you through a bunch of bad endings on the way to the good one. Your choices do not actually impact the ultimate conclusion of the game, but they will lead you through a variety of alternative universes where the fate of the characters was very different based on what decisions are made at key moments, but then it will rewind back to that moment, and have you choose again.For me, the design of this was a massive positive and not a downside. Normally with "choose your own adventure" type stories, I feel compelled to playthru the game a bunch of times to see all possible endings.  I loved the novel way  that this game intentionally allows you to discover these organically along the way, so in a normal playthru you will see many or most of the possible endings.  Additionally, makes it easy to change course when desired, whether because your choice was bad or just curiosity. If you do make a definite "wrong" choice, you find out almost immediately without wasting a lot of hours moving ahead in the story only to find out that a choice you made ages ago set the tale down the wrong path, and it puts you right back to that critical moment to choose again. I loved that by the time I finished the real story, I had only missed one single alternative outcome, and that in a few clicks and a few seconds, I was seeing what happened with that selection. Literally the only downside of this arrangement is that the game doesn't have any replayability unless you're going back for any missed achievements, but that's not personally a thing I care about for this type of game, as long as I get to see all the storylines/endings one way or another.The characters are very endearing, the music is good, the art is beautiful, and I was surprised that what was supposed to be a casual mystery game had a lot of feels.  The characters are not voice acted, but the narrator of the story is, and I thought it was very well done.  Several parts of dialogue were laugh out loud funny, and I took a number of screenshots of things that amused or resonated with me. People have called the game juvenile, and it's true the characters are all kids and some of the jokes are a little silly, but I'm an old lady and I thought the story was cozy and sweet.The only negative thing I can possibly say about this game is that there was a couple loose ends at final ending of the game that I expected to be wrapped up and addressed because the world had allowed the potential to do that. However, instead it choose not to, and to leave those things unresolved even though the story had implied a resolution was possible. I thought it was a little weird, but it did not change my overall feelings on the game at all. I enjoyed my time in Beacon Pines with Luka, Rolo, Beck, and the delightful cast of townies.  (Shoutout to Dawn, the adorable bat who stole my heart, despite being a minor character).This game is definitely worth the hours you'll spend in it -- I believe it took me just under nine -- so don't hesitate, especially if you can catch it on sale. If you like story games, visual novels, or walking simulators, definitely this is one to check out. It's the kind of game I played a little of each night before bed when most people would be watching tv shows or doomscrolling on their phones, and I feel it was infinitely better time spent for me.

After you get the first bad ending, you can't escape them, so it gets boring after a while. it isn't a 'choices matter' story as almost all of your choices lead to the exact same ending, and when you know whats gonna happen almost every time you DO make a 'game altering' choice, you just give up.That doesn't mean the game is terrible, though. The mystery behind what's going on is interesting. I haven't finished the game yet, i got bored after 7 deaths or so. but i probably will complete it later to get the real ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story about change.a story about how 1 change in word can affect the outcome of the story.As you play, you discover more special words or "charms" as the game call them.you use these charms at special keypoints in the history to change the outcome.One of the short commings of this game however is that these charms... some of them are never used.and the only places where you can use charms, the game only lets specific charms be used for that instance.I can understand the need to limit the brances the story can take. to many branches in a story gets harder and harder to keep track off and program.But I would personally have liked if the game had a little more wiggleroom in the choises.for instance, when you walk around and talk to the other characters in the game. Why not let me chose some dialog words from time to time. Just some small dialog to npc's that otherwice would have no effect on the overall story.seriously. among one of the first "charms" you get, is the word "♥♥♥♥".So why not let me be a potty mouth after that point if I want to ?I can even see the achievement for me."Potty mouth - offend everyone with 1 word"
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from Humble Monthly and did not know much of what I was in for.If you expect a game with lots of challenging gameplay, you'll be sorely disappointed.HOWEVER! If you want a good story with well rounded characters set in a story which pans out in different directions based on where in the decision tree you are, this might be right up your alley. I left the game feeling it was a bit in the style of Night in the woods, and To the Moon.Like in Stories : Path of Destinies, there are points in the story where you have 2-3 options on how the game should progress, sending which part of the town, or what led up to where you are into quite different directions.Do not read this as a game which you can replay over and over and get different outcomes. Instead it is crafted to move you along fairly linearly. Go down one branch of the decision tree and get a keyword which will allow you to go down another branch from a previous decision. This also allows the game to have you know what is going on elsewhere without having to cut, just expecting you to remember what you've already played.So in short: If you want a good story and pleasant art and intrigueing plot. This is quite good.If you want a game-game with more to do than walk around and interact to move the story ahread, look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I was hooked from the demo, and snatched up the game as soon as I was notified that it came out; it did not disappoint.Pros:-Perfect blend of RPG elements and visual novel-esque storytelling-Excellent story for the short time-Dynamic and interesting characters-Chilling plot twists-Cute looking characters mixed with a dash of cognitive dissonance in the horrific events-You don't need to replay the game from the beginning every time you hit a bad ending-The fishing flashback is cute-The narration is witty and fun-The music sets the mood very well-Due to the short playtime, it doesn't take ages for the player to get answersCons:-The game is very short; taking about 5-6 hours if you're methodical and click on everything-The scene after the Epilogue does not align with what information given about the location-Due to needing to go through different branches periodically, it can sometimes take a moment to re-orient yourself with what decisions/charms led up to that path-Like with the above, the swapping of the branching paths sometimes leads to information being repeated or laid out in a non-linear way-A certain mysterious mouse is never really explainedOverall, it was as good as I expected after trying out the demo and I'm glad I picked it up.  While it is short, I see it more of a visual novel sort of game (highly narrative and story driven) so I knew to expect a short game.  I would highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasing story-book style with a semi-linear structure. It touches on a variety of themes with varying degrees of success. Oddly, I feel the story would have had more weight if the characters hadn't been cute anthropomorphic animals. Some games can pull off a Watership Down; others can't.If you prefer visual novels without voice acting (as they are an iffy proposition in indie games at the best of times); would I recommend dropping the voice volume to zero.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely brilliant and charming game. The characters are super cute and are easy to get invested in. You really grow attached to all the characters and the little town of Beacon Pines. The utilization of the story gameplay mechanics makes it so interesting to see where one path leads. Would highly recommend if you're looking for a plot based game that you can throw yourself in.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little adventure game.  Not for everybody, but definitely enjoyable for those who like exploring branching paths.  Finding specific words along different paths that you can go back and use to find the real ending is what this game is all about, and it has a good story that had me a little teary eyed a few times to boot.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game. The art style is beautifully cutesy and I like the character dynamics a lot. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, the mistery is well thought out, the characters are super likable and the art and music really carry the whole game to the finish line. There are a few of loose ends that i hope will be addressed in a more than probable sequel but apart from that i really recommend this game to people searching for a light (and sometimes dark) fun multiple-path adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little game for a cozy day/evening. Nice for completionists who like to open/touch/try everything to reach all different kind of endings. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, anyone remember those old choose your path books? _childDocuments_.review: storytelling at its absolute best, scratches that inquisitive itch of wanting to know every outcome, bad or good, in the most perfect way.fell in love with the characters, the art-style and the everything, the fact it can be finished in a relatively short amount of time isn't even a negative because I don't see how the story could be prolonged any further, the canonical ending was sweet and tied up everything in a way that didn't leave me expecting.my only qualm is that i don't have the opportunity to play it for the first time again.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely one of those cases where I REALLY wish Steam had a "Maybe" option instead of a binary "Recommend" or "Don't Recommend".Here's my TL;DR in case you don't want to read a somewhat longer review: This is an alright game. It's not incredible, and be prepared to spot a myriad of flaws in it as you play it if you do buy it, but I still think it's worth a play.Beacon pines is a kind of... choose-your-own-adventure, visual novel, mystery solving game. Much like an ogre, the game has layers. But not all of those layers service the story, which is the main driving point of the game. There's very little to be had in gameplay here past walking from point A to point B to see a cutscene, and that's alright. However, a lot of the story beats in this game (including, unfortunately, the final, climactic scene) feel... rushed.There are entire characters and story branches that serve almost no purpose in the over-arching story. One particular character comes to mind-- a character added as a kickstarter backer reward, who shows up during one branch to say the story at you, and then is never seen again without any explanation as to who they are or how they know the things they know. There are several instances like this, where the story happens AT you instead of feeling like the characters are organically learning the information. For every bit of information actually sussed out by the characters, another piece of important information is clumsily revealed in a flashback, or by a particular scene's dedicated infodump character.The artstyle is wonderful, and the dialogue is charming (pun not intended). A lot of love very clearly went into this game, but my theory is ultimately this: The devs didn't know what they wanted from this game when they launched the kickstarter. It was a vague idea that sounded cool in their heads, but when it came to making a cohesive story they suddenly realized they had no idea how to. As a result, during development, several things had to be shifted, altered, and otherwise changed in the main story while other things stayed static-- and as a result, the final product just feels a little disjointed. The release trailer (and indeed, the kickstarter page itself) showcases a number of scenes that simply aren't in the game, which give me the impression that the game was, sometime late in development, flipped on its head to service an entirely different story or perhaps change the order of events. I can't be certain. What I can say is that the end product is a bit of a mess, but still ultimately worth a play.My final score for Beacon Pines is a 6 out of 10. Beacon Pines is a game clearly inspired by character-driven and mystery greats like Night in the Woods, Twin Peaks, and Gravity Falls, but falls short where the stories it draws from excelled-- but is still redeemed by its fun characters, wonderfully watercolor artstyle, and despite the end result being a bit disappointing, a compulsion to turn the next page to find out what happens next.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasant little game with hand drawn backgrounds and fluffy critters.The most interesting part of the game is the story branching system.You can take decisions in the game that will lead to a different story. One plot on danger, one on friendship, one on ...And the nodes are shown explicitely in the story tree.Though it's not an open story despite what the branches suggest. You litteraly have to go through all branches in parallel to unlock new options on other branches. All the branches will likely lead to an unsatisfying ending that makes you want to carry on and improve the outcome, solve the riddle, know more etc...The story itself is seen from a children's perspective, so it may look a bit dumb but the story is for mature audience with sometimes mildly horrific scenes and it's rich enough for you to want to know more about this town.All in all a pleasant gameplay. Maybe sometimes the spamming of the button to carry on the conversation is a bit annoying but the narrator is nice.The max difficulty has been finding the right object among 8 others to solve a riddle... so, don't expect any brainplosion.For all those lovers of story driven games.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting narrative game with branching paths, the "choose your own adventure" aspect is kind of a half-truth since there is a linear path to the good ending, but I prefer what this game does anyways. Jumping between different routes to unlock new scenarios is compelling and you never retread old ground. The linearity also smartly gives the player new information about the full plot throughout the different routes in some really cool ways. It's good and Rolo is my friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Beacon Pines. Playing through this game, meeting its inhabitants, experiencing its branching, complicated story. It's like feeling nostalgia for a place you've never actually been. That's a rare emotion for a game to give you, and a special one at that. Every time I thought I knew where the story was heading, a plot twist would come along and sweep me off my feet.Every step along the way, I was only along for the ride. And what a ride it was! This was a special gem, a hidden one, unfortunately. If you're reading this, know that buying this, supporting the devs, and giving the game a chance is something you'll surely not regret. This one is special. Take your time, don't rush, pour some hot cocoa, or whatever else, and enjoy the ride.Beacon Pines is worth your time. It was certainly worth mine. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this after finishing the true ending to the game. When I first started playing I simply thought that the idea of one word can change an entire story was a cool concept / very cute story book method. I never expected a story that had endless plot twist and emotions. This is the first game I have ever played were I truly wanted all the characters to have a happy ending that especially include the town bully. I genuinely cried going through the town that though out playing you grow to love one last time. This games true ending ties all the reasons why it was hard to play all the bad endings, feeling bad for specific characters or not wanting more. _childDocuments_.name: Beacon Pines

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that has such good reviews, I really expected a lot more from it. It feels like it's trying way too hard to be sincere and some kind of Night in the Woods competitor.
