_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a review about the servers being down, that'll be fixed soon enough and isn't really a reason to stay away, it's just a little frustrating. What is a reason to stay away for now: The leveling process and the fact that it's always online, without the ability to play and level up offline. The Infamy leveling, meaning your character's level not your weapons, is tied to what is effectively just a big list of achievements. This sucks for anyone looking to play a specific build for any real amount of time. I want to play shotgun + ammo funnel but after getting the early achievements out of the way for that gun I am consistently making no infamy progress at all with each heist I complete. This sucks and forces me to use guns I hate like the Uzi if I want more skill points to put toward the build I actually want to play at all. The lack of solo play is an issue for multiple reasons. Obviously the sever issues right now are a problem that could have been avoided but the real annoyance is waiting on matchmaking even when it's working when I'm trying to solo stealth. I hate that even if I'm only trying to play alone I have to sit around while their matchmaking server thinks really hard about putting me in a lobby alone for some reason. I also hate that if I lose internet connection I just can't play the game at all, while I could happily play Payday 2 without a connection at all. Considering how ♥♥♥♥ Charter/Spectrum is, I'm really not looking forward to getting kicked out of a long stealth mission at 2AM when they decided to push some garbage change to production and knock me offline. Hopefully both of these issues will be addressed in future, but honestly for now I'd wait and maybe just play a bit of Payday 2 again. The actually moving and shooting feels great but everything surrounding it is a downgrade. I expect once they hopefully cave to requests for an offline mode and leveling is reworked the game will be great, and hopefully I can come back and change my review. For now I can't really recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It definitely does a couple of things better than the second game, but it's not really enough to outweight the negatives. You can certainly have fun with it, but it's probably going to get old pretty fast. Never played Payday 1, so I will not compare it.The good:-The feeling of handling the guns feels far superior, although the results of using them do not. More on that later-Mobility had a massive upgrade and feels great now. The vaulting and slides add a lot to it.-There's a lot of perks to choose from out of the box which opens up lotsa possibilities for experimenting with builds, although there's a catch I will mention later.-Hostages now feel more impactful. Not a lot more impactful, but more. In addition to just dragging them around for easier negotiations, you can trade them for extra supplies, or even use them as human shields.-You can now shoot out the glass in shields to fight a shield solo without building for it with a perk.-You now have the option to carry 2 bags if you build for it!-Concealment isn't a stat anymore, opening up more doors for kit in the event you do screw up your stealth run and aren't a quitter when something doesn't go in your favour. Concealed interactions have also been improved so that you aren't stuck incapable of doing absolutely anything when unmasked.-The new tools section is quite neat. Personally enjoy the Micro cam myself as it allows me to check up on my turret without running all the way back. Lets me know if I need to reboot it or not, aswell as allowing for eyes around the map during a stealth mission.-The new enemy options are kinda interesting. I quite like the idea of having to watch out for grenades now-Overkill weapons is a fun idea, and a better option for implementing the minigun that doesn't make you feel like a clown for not bringing something more viable.-New maps are very pretty. Just a shame you only get to see most of them onceThe bad:-T̶h̶e̶ m̶u̶s̶i̶c̶ o̶n̶ t̶h̶e̶ G̶o̶l̶d̶ &̶ S̶h̶a̶r̶k̶e̶ m̶a̶p̶ w̶i̶l̶l̶ m̶a̶k̶e̶ y̶o̶u̶ i̶n̶t̶i̶m̶a̶t̶e̶l̶y̶ a̶w̶a̶r̶e̶ o̶f̶ w̶h̶a̶t̶ i̶t̶ f̶e̶e̶l̶s̶ l̶i̶k̶e̶ t̶o̶ h̶a̶v̶e̶ b̶l̶a̶s̶t̶i̶n̶g̶ t̶i̶n̶i̶t̶u̶s̶ f̶o̶r̶ t̶h̶e̶ w̶h̶o̶l̶e̶ r̶u̶n̶. This was likely a bug or something. Please disregard that. I will keep it in the review for context to the comment though.-The armour system makes my tits scream. I partially like it because I'm normally into games like Tarkov where your gear degrades as it does its job, but it doesn't really fit aswell with the horde shooter style Payday has going on. When you lose all your armour and it doesn't come back, you might aswell just accept your defeat and let them take you into custody so you can respawn with armour, unless someone brought enough armour plates to keep ya going.-There is actually 15 maps, but  doesn't seem to actually work right now, so you don't get to pick which you join into unless you go solo, and people only seem to play 3 maps, so if you join via quickplay, chances are you're going to get Cook-Off 75% of the time, Road Rage 7% of the time, and Dirty Ice 13% of the time. Hold out hope for that 5% mystery map!-Enemies are too tanky already from lower levels. The most common enemy type should NOT be surviving 2 7.62x39mm rounds to the face from an AKM without dying immediately on only Hard (2/4 skulls) I want whatever milk that guy's been drinking.-The selection of pistols is too small, and SMGs are in primary slot now, so you've got 12 pistols to choose from, 3 of which are copies of each other, 2 others basically being the same pistol aswell, and 3 others being revolvers. I guess this is where the "This would be a great weapon if it wasn't an SMG" argument brought us.-There are no numbers on weapon stats and the bars feel inconsistent with what they show and what they produce, partially because burst weapons get huge damage spikes since it doesn't seem to represent your damage per bullet on those. What's the difference between Stability and Recoil? Couldn't tell ya. -Weapon mods are unlocked by levelling your weapon, which means you have to use it for extended amounts of time, so you will not know if you like the end result until you finish levelling it to the point where you have the mods you intended to put on it.-There's only 4 deployables. Health pack, Ammo pack, Armour pack, and Sentry if you happen to have a point in the engineer tree. Mine habibster in bruh, really?-Looking at the nerd mask gives me diarrhea.Can't think of more to list, but I probably missed something. Don't exactly have the largest amount of hours yet, but this is what I've experienced so far. Not gonna say the game isn't fun in small doses, but I would feel weird recommending it, or saying that it's an improvement over the second game overall. I DON'T think it's horrible, but it's not GOOD either.

_childDocuments_.review: My current list of grievances with PAYDAY 3:-Heist layout and objective randomization is almost non-existent.-Many of the objectives feel kinda boring, with the vast majority of them ultimately just being ones where you stand around and wait for something to happen/finish. Also, why is Bile used on so many of the heists as the method of escape? It's feels kind of unimaginative. Throw in Twitch and those two make up almost all of the escape objectives in the game excluding Road Rage, 99 Boxes, and Boys in Blue.-Team AI is often stupid and frustrating to play with, making Solo just unfun to play.-The grit-edge-rush skill system feels tedious to play with as I find myself having to do small arbitrary actions very often just to keep my skills active. I would rather just have passive skills that encourage particular playstyles without forcing me to do specific actions that add nothing to the gameplay.-Although there is server browser now, there are still a couple of significant problems I have with it. Firstly, the filters lock to the ones I initially had set before starting a heist, forcing me to restart the game in order to change the filters again. Secondly, if I want to only search for one specific contract, I have to disable each and every contract/contractor in the filters by slowly flipping through each and every one of their tabs and disabling them, which gets annoying fast.-The preplanning system is kinda lame, especially in comparison to PAYDAY 2 with heists like the Big Bank and Golden Grin Casino as it adds little variety to how the heists actually play out. Even when they do, all of the heist-specific ones require me to get them from RNG drops from playing other heists, which also feels pretty lame; And the fact that I have to buy certain assets from the main menu instead of the preplanning menu itself where it would be convenient is completely baffling to me.-UI design (still) feels lacking in charm and the UX is not good. Most of the UI elements (still) looks like it consists of nothing but squares. The UI itself also feels quite clunky to use in general. I wish weapons in the shop could be sorted by weapon category, like Pump-Action Shotguns under one category and Marksman Rifles under another and so on and so forth. (edit: The latest "UI revamp" update made the menu design look a little better, but the UX has had pretty much no significant improvements as far as I can tell.)Until Starbreeze can meaningfully address these issues, I cannot see myself recommending the game, even at its now apparently reduced price.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After the thoughtAfter playing for 100 hours and with everything that happened, it is hard to say the game is worth its price. Any payday fan will be disappointed. Anyone who has played Payday 2 will be disappointed. Someone who says "What is a gosh darn payday" will most likely enjoy this game as it is heavily targeted to casual/new-age gamers. Everything old has been thrown out the window and they are trying to re-write the receiptAll in all, do not expect it to be the game of the year, it is a good game to play with friends and it has potential but needs a lot of time to grow, it did not release in a finished state and can be considered "in development" for the time being.Pay day fans do not get your hopes upCasual PC gamers, think of picking it up.Release comment:All I see is people complaining about the servers not working, some have decent feedback.Some choices made in designing this game are questionable, like the removal of the offline mode and I'm not the biggest fan of the lobby system. Some of the best moments I had in PD2 were chilling with friends in the lobby showing off our silly masks and talking in VCs without even playing.Other than that I have not seen anything egregiously broken with this game only some models glitching out. I have played the beta a bit and now the real game for a few hours with friends and I can say it is still payday. It offers new mechanics and some fresh air in the franchise after the 2 last games being mechanically very similar.I do believe it is a good game and will only become better with time.The devs have a decent track record with listening to the community and I hope this will be prevalent throughout the further development of pay day 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics is good, and the mechanics are far more polished compared to the earlier games.The game is also a lot more realistic compared to the previous. The stealth aspects are more challenging as well. Example in the art gallery where going through trip wires and motion sensors to get to the "precious" paintings is a rewarding approach.Although the matchmaking issue has been alleviated, I do a feel the lack of content and limited range of heists available. Most players can complete the whole game within the first 20 hrs and what's left is grinding for levels through completing challenges.The loud approach isn't as fun as the previous games. It not like the dumb coop shooter where players can spend an eternity cooking meth. The theme seems to be completing heists as quickly as possible, since armor chunks dwindles upon taking damage, and armor bags will deplete either by you or teammates. Without armor, staying in a heist is a bust. Thus, players will inevitable be led to a certain build, and there are little diversity to circumvent this approach.I do hope the developers will improve the skill system, perhaps a little of the past glory, like ahem.. "shouting at teammates to revive them instantly" or "converting cops to become meatshields". I'm sure those broken skills were excluded for a reason, but well.. this is PAYDAY!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally do pre-orders. They almost always end in rage-inducing disappointment. Payday2 was a favourite of mine for awhile. I figured Starbreeze deserved going against my "no pre-orders" disposition. Turns out I shouldn't have compromised on my ideals.Payday3 is everything I hate in modern gaming.-Login *REQUIRED* to play. NO.-Denuvo (which they thankfully walked back) Denuvo is hot garbage.-Connection required, even in solo games (did an EA exec take control of Starbreeze??)We have a perfect ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of Starbreeze's own making. Requiring an account and a live connection at all times, but then not having the server horsepower available (For a VERY anticipated, popular game) so that effectively nobody can play the game. On top of it all, I am seeing tons of stability issues from other people, once one CAN get into the game. I haven't experienced this - I never got past the obnoxious login screen.I have a game I paid full price for, and I cannot use it. I refuse to make an account for a game that's not an MMO. It makes no sense to have an account requirement for a game like this. "Oh it's for cross play" no it isn't. This whole thing feels like greed. Greed turns me completely off. Therefore, I'm returning this game. If Starbreeze pulls their collective heads out of their asses, I *might* re-buy, but my trust has vanished. This was a rude slap in the face from a company I once trusted. I won't be making that mistake again.Huge disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: *Update 7* - 31/05/2024As of the most recent update the developers at Starbreeze should reflect upon a job well done with this particular update. The progression system and the animation improvements namely and new skill line. While for a lot of frustrated players it will not be anywhere near enough, it will however at least provide them with a reason to pick up the game again, not much of a reason.. but one nonetheless. With such an abysmal launch with so much promised and to live up to it was understandable for most players to want shelf this game and watch Starbreeze burn for what felt like a real life heist of gamer's cash. I personally do not want to see this game or starbreeze burn and I was only recently reminded of how poor Payday 2's initial launch was. A poor excuse to repeat the same mistake twice however, if the game continues to be worked on and gameplay improved, I am sure most will look past this instance of time as it was with PD2.The game is missing a substantial amount of content, im not just talking about guns.. or heists. Fundamental systems are needing to be reworked.Utility and concept had a chance to be massive for payday 3.What happened to the drill and its subsequent utility skill tree. What happened to the handheld saw?What is with this obsession with standing still in circles for heist progression?The positive in all of this is that there are so many systems to improve, change and content to add that so long as Starbreeze keep at this game it can evolve into something great. The game is on a knife edge. Let's see which way it falls The foundation is here, great graphics, gunplay feels fun and chunky. The small animations are great for realism. It just needs to built upon with carefully considered balance, and depth! (not complicated) but depth - i.e drill equipment and saw equipment - with mechanic skill lines

_childDocuments_.review: I love Payday 2 and I like Payday 3. The predecessor to this game is simply just better. Which is becasue of one simple factor, time. This has allowed growth between a time span of literally 10 years for Payday 2. It might have been good at release but the room of improvement that it filled was fantastic. Some people say that Payday 3 is an unfinished product. Which I disagree to. I think unfinished is a level too far. But I would like to see more than I have already. However, almost everything with Payday 3 I have experienced is positive. I like the loud combat more than in Payday 2. Mostly because it feels more challenging. Stealth is absolutely amazing in my opinion. So much versatility you can do with skills and make a great build for a specific heist. Now I know many players in general just dislikes the game. In a way I mean if anyone played Payday 2 the diesel engine can not be compared to Payday 3's unreal engine experience with mechanics and graphics. But then progressing in Payday 3 is definitely where it all goes wrong. You who are reading this and do not know or own the game, the progression is slow and will get more frustrating the further/higher level you get. The challenge system for leveling up is insane and should be a supplement for completing heists etc. Not the only way. From personal experience playing the game I have suffered a lot from game crashing, disconnected at the end from a heist and even lag spikes. It is really annoying when it happens many times. Although these are probably the two things that I disagree to with the game. For anyone who played Payday 2 I will recommend this game. For anyone who haven't heard about Payday 2 or played it I will say if you like shooting games and co-op go for it. Or wait until a sale comes, the game is a bit on the expensive side. In conclusion I am not fully satisfied with the game. But Payday 3 is very fun nonetheless. I have trust in the developers that they will improve the game a lot for the forseeable future. Like I said before time is a key factor for success. I think Payday 3 can only get better. I reccomend this game

_childDocuments_.review: Bad start of launch servers aside, The game play feels like a refreshed payday 2. What i'd expect from a sequel handles and feels like 2 "Aside the grenade button being "G", I've lost many a civilian to that change. Though did make for some fun, Oh ♥♥♥♥, moments haha (Just a quick key-bind change)" but the new features of hacking cams in new ways, point holding moving and stationary targets, & snagging key cards from the belts of guards is so refreshing + more I'm forgetting! Along with the new tree features of speed, offence, defense (Forget perk names) and how each perk further down the tree plays off of these perks being activated in real time makes the tree feel more alive and apart of your character. Rather than blue flashes every now and then to show the 25+ish perks making the dodge build work in 2. This feels more moment to moment active with perks flashing on screen as they activate instead of passive. I believe it's a good sequel, sad that a few server issues cause all the cool new game-play stuff to be overlooked. Side rant: People with .5hrs in the game giving negative reviews complaining about the servers and servers alone are causing such a nice refresh to such a great game to be lost and maybe never expanded upon if funding gets pulled. Play the game, then give a proper review of the game, positive or negative so be it. I know the comment would prob be "I would if I could" which fine if you don't want to be patient get out of line, refund if you must, Come back later. I get it it's frustrating, I just lost 1hr to a solo 100% stealth night club 40ft from the drop with only two bags to go and then a 20ft run to exit, it sucks, but I enjoyed the loop and would do it all again (Just like the normal gameplay-loop of the game). Just get rid of your server complaint negative review so this game and all its cool new features can thrive. _childDocuments_.review: Have any of you ever played an online game on launch? By your reviews it doesnt seem like it. Every major brand like Blizzard with their WoW and CoD releases have had the same issues. Only sometimes there werent "Server down issues", but there were queue times which were sometimes 8 or more hours.I get that people took a day or two off work just to play the game at launch, but that culture seems weird as the game is always the worst at launch and usually gets better with more and more updates. Especially PD series. Now, I am not trying to shame those people, but do you really expect servers not to suck at launch? When there are 80,000+ players looking for a game at the same time? Yes, I am not happy with the full online model as well... but we knew it was coming. I dont know why you guys are so mad that there aren't as many weapons/masks/upgrades as there are in PD2 but for god's sake, PD2 on release also didn't have everything It has now. Just play with what is in the game currently. I have played hundreds of hours on PD2 and let me tell you... At launch, it sucked. 4 years later? Amazing!But the content changed not the mechanics or the soul of the game. Just wait for the content to come.- Great new stealth overhaul (almost)- Great gun sounds- Great visual experience- Good-Old scary bulldozers- Great new picking mechanics- Great new skills and skill mechanics/synergies- Fantastic loud experience with balanced waves (sometimes maybe easier) and negotiation- Unlimited cable ties- Servers are fragile because of the volume- Offline mode would be nice now however in the longrun it doesnt really matter- Low weapon arsenal- Some map optimizations (stutters, overall low framerates)- Weapons not put into groups (Primary, Secondary, Rifles, SMGs) but mixed up into one menu- Menu feels way too gamepad friendly and bad to use with keyboard sometimes (especially friend invites)- Hopefully the stutter and so on will be fixedYes, the servers are a pain currently. Yes, the content is low. BUT! Those are just current problems which will be soon eradicated. I would still recommend this game because the most important thing in my view is the soul and feel of the game. It still does feel like payday. It is still the same good old franchise. That is what I personally wanted. Good old PAYDAY. The overwhelmingly negative response it got is definitely not deserved. See you in a couple years when this will be one of the best games.

_childDocuments_.review: Payday 3 really harks back to the roots of Payday 1, which will upset those that are use to the hot and fast gameplay of Payday 2. That said, the game feels much more balanced in terms of choices you make between attempting to go stealth and potentially getting much more loot than normal, or going loud, and risking a easy and quick payday, but for less cash. AI police are much better than the first and second game, they are ruthless to say the least. Unlike the other two games, the police in Payday 3, if you are being aggressive and opening fire at the first sign of a police officer, they will start to relentlessly attack you in waves just like the fist two games. However in Payday 3, they will eventually become one endless wave which will wear you and your team down to nothing. Stealth on the other hand is like one big puzzle for each and every map requiring you and your team to unravel the puzzle to get the big loot. While not incredibly hard to stand the mechanics, the cameras, guards, and even civilians will make it difficult to pull off quickly, requiring a more methodical approach. In regards to gunplay, this game is king compared to the other two versions of payday. Firefights feel very fast paced and intense and can get overwhelming fast if you dont have the right perks. Speaking of perks, there are a lot to choose from to tailor yourself to the ideal criminial in the team. Either attempt to be a jack of all trades, or specialize deeply in one of the many available trees. All of them have purpose, and in many cases you might be swapping them out for others because some are just better in certain situations while others are better in others. I really like the balance of Payday 3 and feel its a strong standing game on its own. Its only fault at this time is the match making issue (which they are fixing) but also the lack of content to say, payday 2, but then again, payday 2 had so many DLCs that it made your head spin. I hope to see this kinda of support for Payday 3 in the future as I feel the foundation for Payday 3 is very strong compared to the other two games.

_childDocuments_.review: First i would like to say that at the time of writing this review, game is experiencing a problem with servers which caused many people to write negative review about state of the servers and pleading for offline mode (something that was present in Payday 2).I must say that even with bugs like:- Bots being stuck in the walls for the entire heist. (Happens rarely)- Not being able to revive teammate (Happens rarely)- On Under the Surphaze map, in the vent on the bottom floor from "hidden" staircase to wall next to room E1. Without putting an extra input or running into the vent, your character just slides through it into the other side of the vent. (Sometimes/Often)- Some challenges don't give you xp right away but later (Often)I would still recommend the game if you play with your friends. What makes it hard for solo player currently is the matchmaking. System that many players complain about it. Compared to the   from Payday 2, matchmaking is very dissappointing downgrade. Matchmaking currently works like this: You choose a map from 8 available that you want to play, you decide on which difficulty you want to find lobby, choose public mode  and you start matchmaking. After you've done that you are placed into a public queue and you're waiting for system to let you join other people's lobby or it'll make you a new public lobby which makes you it's leader and allowing other players to join you via matchmaking. However when you're in matchmaking queue it will only look for the heist on difficulty that you've chosen. Not only that but the game doesn't show you how many public lobbies there are on this map/difficulty so you may sit alone in the matchmaking or later your own lobby for some time waiting for people. Compared to the  from Payday 2 where you could see on a "map" which lobbies were playing which map, on what difficulty, how many people are in party, if they are playing stealth or not and also filter them by showing you only specific maps or specific difficulty or both. So as you can see  was superior "queue" system. Also since i forgot to add it before, even when playing solo in "invite only" lobby, you'd still need to wait 1-2mins for your lobby to be created.Next thing is a bit controversial: Leveling system aka. Challenges.In Payday 3 you level up by doing challenges. There are 639 Heist, 89 Career and 408 Combat challenges. Heist challenges focus on doing something with maps like:- Finish X map, on X difficulty before/or after assault (Stealth or Loud)- Finish X map X times on X difficulty- Escape without being downed during loud mission on X map- Get every bag on the X mapCareer challenges focus on your level. You get them by reaching certain level and instead of XP these reward you with in-game special currency (which you can buy via in-game money only).And also Combat challenges, which require you to:- Kill X enemies using X weapon- Slide X meters- Kill X enemies with X weapon via headshot- Kill X enemies while using Human Shield- Save a crewmate from Tazer X times- Deploy X times ammo/doctor/armor bag or sentry turretetc.Around level 40, time required to level up is longer due to easier challenges were been finished already. Outside of character level, every weapon could also be leveled up. By using them in your heists you gain weapon xp which in turn unlocks new attachments for that weapon. Due to weapon leveling system, many combat challenges are unlocked just by playing the game.You can change appearance of your character by choosing which character you want to play and 3 backups if they are already taken in lobby. You can also choose different suit, gloves and ofc customizable mask.Your loadout consist of few things:- Primary and Secondary weapon (I believe that for now the only secondary weapons availible are the pistols)- Deployable: Ammo/Armor/Doctor Bag or Sentry Turret- Throwable: Frag Grenades/Flashbang Grenades/Smoke Grenades and Throwing Knifes- Overkill weapon: Grenade Launcher or Special Sniper Rifle- Armor (Armor only affect how much "armor" chunks you have and how fast you're moving. More armor chunks = Lower speed, Less armor chunks = Faster speed)- Tool: MicroCam/Infrasonic Mine/ECM Jammer/Motion SensorAnd ofc skills. There are 17 different archetypes. Some focus on Hacking Cameras, others on Movement, another one is for Trading Hostages more efficiently or improving one's Armor. Possibly one of my favorite changes from Payday 2. Where you're limited (on higher difficulties) to 2 maybe 3 working builds.One of the many changes we'll recieved in Payday 3 compared to Payday 3 is difficulty spike. Not only loud missions feel harder than on Payday 2 but doing stealth on overkill (highest difficulty currently) is also difficult due to changes on the map. Key items might be placed in different places, you have only 2 pagers (instead of 4 in Payday 2), codes seem to be different. Certain areas of the map could be harder to navigate on higher difficulty. And not to mention new stealth system. Now you can do a lot more in stealth while you're in casing mode (mask off). Taking items, carrying bags, interact with objectives etc. However i feel like casing mode is a bit too op at least with moving bags. While you're carrying a loot bag in casing mode guards don't notice anything wrong with it. Because of that you can finish stealth mission with "mask on" or maskless, giving you advantages from being in the casing mode like: guards when alerted by your presence only make you follow them to nearest public area. Speaking of which, now we have 3 different areas in the map:- Public Area - While in casing mode you won't be detected by anything outside of doing illegal things like lockpicking- Private Area - While in casing mode only guards and cameras can spot you. If guard spots you he will make you follow him into the nearest Public Area. If camera spots you it will alarm nearest guard to check position where camera saw you. Guard then will come to that place and if he finds you he'll lead you to the nearest Public Area. If guard doesn't find you there he will trigger "Search" - guards will leave their patrol routes to try to find you.- Secure Area - Area where even being in the casing mode doesn't help you, if you're found out there, guards can shoot you or trigger an alarm.Pros: - New stealth mechanics and interactions- New systems like: Human shield, Overkill weapons, Tools and many more- New skill system with different archetypes to choose- No concealment (it was Payday 2 stealth system)- Changes on map depending on difficulty in stealth- More tactical gameplay than in Payday 2- Difficulty spike (compared to Payday 2)- Ability to cross-play PC with ConsoleCons:- (At the time of writing) Server issues- You can't create offline lobby- Matchmaking system is bad- (For some people) Level up by making challenges instead of doing heists- (For some people, At the time of writing) Only 17 weapons available- (At the time of writing) Worse mask customization than in Payday 2My raiting 8/10.I was really hyped for Payday 3 and I'm not dissappointed. Server issues should be fixed soon, and bugs I've encountered aren't gamebreaking. Changes to combat and stealth are really cool and make game more tactical for me. There is also high incentive for taking hostages due to changes in this system which makes it a lot different than in Payday 2, where people rarely cared about them. I see a lot of potential moving forward, I'm looking forward to changes in Matchmaking and adding Offline mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this in good faith to anyone who isn't a hardcore Payday 3 until the servers get fixed, but I am concerned for a number of reasons, even though I bought it day 1 and have thoroughly enjoyed the few times I've been able to play.Payday 3 has massively improved some of the weakest parts of Payday 2, namely stealth being completely reworked into being extremely dynamic and rewarding while removing all of the tedium, The removal of detection, addition of public/private/secure areas, and an overall increase in the depth of the mechanics.I'm also a big fan of most of the changes to loud, though the meta needs to develop before any real conclusions are drawn. the new skill system is interesting, the special enemies feel very dynamic and threatening, and while the heists are limited and somewhat derivative of previous heists, their complexity is tenfold anything seen in Payday before.Now I am worried about a few things in Payday 3. The Infamy system seems quite grindy and annoying, and once you cap out it be pointless to continue playing outside of (my very real) love of the game. The lack of offline mode is annoying, and even assuming competent servers the matchmaking system currently blows and is nowhere near as easy and convenient as Crime Net.I'm confident that Payday 3 will get to a spot where it's worth its price, albeit for someone cynical reasons. Overkill is not in the  spot to squander any money, and the good will that the fans have for this game is in some respects worth actual value that they can't afford to lose. I'm pretty confident that many of the decisions that caused this game to be in an a weird or bad spot (online only, limited content, poor ui/ux, limited polish) are due to a combination of the engine being ported, the failure of Overkill software's other products, Overkill's near bankruptcy, the Covid-19 pandemic, Payday 2 being revived for development post White House, and Overkill's new publisher Deep Silver. There's plenty of excuses and legitimate failings of Overkill but I'm confident there's no lack of love for the unique experience they've managed to make with this series.Don't buy Payday 3 right now, wait until things get ironed out and stable, and I'll update or remove this review when I feel that's happened. I look forward to recommending this game, but I can't as of yet.

_childDocuments_.review: "Payday 3" had a troubled launch, but the game has seen significant improvements thanks to regular updates. The stealth mechanics, especially the new casing mode, bring much-needed variety, allowing players to perform key tasks while blending in with civilians. The gunplay also feels more refined, with tighter control and a return to the tactical feel of earlier titles.Environmental interactions have been revamped, making activities like lockpicking and safecracking more engaging with mini-games. Even smaller features, such as the ability to close doors during a heist, add a layer of strategy that fans will appreciate.That said, the game still faces issues, particularly with its matchmaking system, which is slow and frustrating. The absence of a solo mode, Crime Net improvements for better matchmaking control, and pre-planning tools make the experience feel incomplete. The lack of in-game features like marking missions as Stealth or Loud also limits player options.Despite these shortcomings, "Payday 3" is heading in the right direction. There’s still a long way to go, but with continued updates, it could become the polished heist game fans have been waiting for. If you’re a "Payday" fan, it’s worth picking up on sale or keeping an eye on future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignoring all of the technical issues/bugs, I honestly believe this is the worst game I have ever played. It seems like they took the best mechanics and perks from payday 2 and threw them out the window when making this game. The standing in circles to "hack" mechanic is not fun at all and I can't believe this game was play tested and that mechanic wasn't removed/changed. In my opinion, there are only two decent changes. The first is that you can do more stuff without your mask on. The second is the addition of the different areas like public, private, and secure. Even with these two great mechanics added to the game, it is still just not fun.The next big problem is the XP change. You barely get XP from completing heists. Insteaad you get XP fro completing challenges. This wouldn't be an issue if the challenges were fun, but most of the challenges are to complete thee heist on a certain difficulty up to 60 times i believe. These challenges would be somewhat acceptable even in Payday 2, but that's because most of the heists were fun to play in Payday 2, unlike this game.Overall, I do not think this game is worth it now, and do not think the game will be worth it in the future unless there are major mechanics changes. They should have just kept updating Payday 2 instead of releasing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: PAYDAY 3 is a mixed experience. The gameplay has so much improved over PAYDAY 2 with a ton of new stealth mechanics and smooth as well as intense loud play. But everything around that is a downgrade in my view. The menu, HUD, the progression system, matchmaking (no, you can't open or join a lobby via a good old server browser, it's all quickmatch - and also: online only, which means when the servers are down, you cannot play).There have been been improvements and also new content has been added since release, so I now rate this game just so slightly positive. Still, I would only recommend this if you are really into the gameplay part PAYDAY offers, else wait for more updates.

_childDocuments_.review: It seems very clear that the developers of this game understood two things about Payday: Steal things, and Shoot cops.Unfortunately beyond that, it's as though they never played Payday, or Payday 2. In fact I would go so far as to say, I am not sure the people that developed Payday 3 have every played a video game at all.The UI is a gigantic mess - simple things to fix (like the text in some of the messages that appear) are just downright misleading. You'll hover over something on the left and the instructions for what to do with it will appear on the bottom right. Then you'll hover over something on the left and the instructions will appear on the bottom right. Then you'll hover over something in the center and the instructions appear on the bottom left? Who thought this through? The answer is: no one. There was no planning or thought put into this at all.We'll start with a simple sign up process - I clicked create account (This shouldn't be necessary, but the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ publishers want to collect your personal information so they can sell it, more on this later) and it spawns a browser window. So I setup my account but the form has no place to put my password. Whatever I create it, validate the security code, and immediately can't login. One password reset later I'm logged in and the game immediately wants my Zipcode Country and State. Why? Why do you need that information? OH that's right, so you can sell my personal information later to make more money. This is not the more on this later, that's still coming. So now I attempt to associate my profile with STEAM. Now I have a Steam overlay browser window open and I have to go to the Steam webpage, and sign into my steam account. Fine, whatever. Now my account is setup and linked. I close the overlay and go back to the game. It says login, but that's okay, I know my username and password. So I put it in. And BAM. Error message. This account has already been linked, cannot login. WTF does that even mean? If you know my account is already linked why am I still sitting at this screen? We have to re-launch the game to continue. Fine at least this time the game comes up - aaaannnnddd immediately asks me to sign away my Privacy rights, and then wants the telemetry data from my computer. The second I can ALMOST understand, but the FIRST, way to be transparent about how much data mining you're attempting to leverage out of people. This is criminally overkill for a video game developer, and you should be ASHAMED of yourselves for even asking for it. This is 2023 and privacy rights have been all over the news. Oh right, that would require educated developers, giving the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ login experience and third party account that's required, we shouldn't be surprised they don't understand privacy rights.(I will say one thing positive about this - by DEFAULT the have the box 'unchecked' to receive 'promotional emails'. I am sure that some VP is going to read my review and instead of fixing all the broken things I'm pointing out, he's going to make someone fix that, but you actually have to Opt In to receiving emails, which is a nice thing for them to do. Which is why inevitably it will go away.)Okay fine whatever, I'm in game finally, time to join my friends. Oh a tutorial prompt, how useful. Do the tutorial mission. End the tutorial mission. Aside from the ABSOLUTELY GARBAGE KEY BINDING there are no problems here. I don't know what asinine developer didn't play Payday 2 and decided that it was time to change the THROW BAG keybind to the THROW GRENADE keybind, but they should be fired, and blacklisted, for not knowing the product they were working on. We get to end of what is (I come to find out later) one of FOUR tutorial missions, and...there is absolutely no prompt saying to do anymore tutorials. No indication that there are three more. That's okay, because I've played Payday 2, right? So this will be fine.My friends send me a friend request. Hidden in the corner of the screen and with no toaster popup announcement I finally find my way to the social panel. One of my friends is listed as a Steam Friend and the other...is not. He has sent me a friend request. I click on it. Nothing happens. I click on it again. Nothing happens. I click it on the indicator on the upper right side of the screen for a third time and finally see that the directions to accept the friend request are actually down in the bottom left corner.(Side note: This is likely due to them programming the game for Console users first. I don't use a console to play games, so maybe this is a normal thing? I don't know, but either way, indications are in that this is actually a console port to PC and that doesn't thrill me.)Friends finally added, we've joined a party. I start clicking around the interface. The pricing of things horrifies me - unlike Payday or Payday 2 it's clearly going to be a LONG TIME before I can afford to up my gear. This is more apparent after my first heist where it takes me five head shots to kill any enemies but only three if I shoot them center mass in the back (because that makes sense, right? remember when I said these people have clearly never played video games before?), but I digress.I click into the PLAY section, expecting to see ....well anything like the Payday 2 interface, or some kind of lobby like in Payday one, or anything at all indicating to me that I'm part of a group that is queued for a match. Instead there is a weird timeline like thing at the bottom, so I click on the first heist. Immediately it says at the top "Looking for Lobby" and I panic, I didn't mean to do that! I click cancel matchmaking and...it drops me from the party. That was the party queue, which the game tells you no where. There is no indication that it's your party looking for a game or how many people are in your party or what game you are queued for...Fast forward twenty minutes of me leaving and joining a party (because no one is explaining to me what is going on) and we finally get into a match. We're all stealthy, everything is fine, I sprint across a camera (Payday 2 mechanics) and it alerts on me. Fine. I shoot it, a guard is coming...so I run away. Because that's what you DO in Payday 2, and remember, the game has done nothing to indicate to me that I haven't completed the tutorials. The whole heist goes loud, no problem I warned my friends that would happen.What a mess already. I start searching through files because they are interactive. I don't know what I'm searching for. But that's okay. A door to lockpick so I hold F and...what is this interface? No idea. I start randomly clicking and...nothing happens. You have to hit a key, a specific key. Fine, easy enough to solve. New skill unlocked and now I know how lockpicking works. Then we find a safe, and remember, we still haven't been through the tutorial (because the game never told us there was anything other than the first one...whose brilliant idea was that?). After a few minutes of playing with this interface I figure out that's...broken. Because you can actually advance past the correct number and if the dial is still green, move backwards to find the right number, which isn't possible on a real safe, and actually disregards what the tutorial says about safe cracking. So what are the rules for safecracking? Some Developer who has clearly never played a video game programmed them randomly, I think. Your guess is as good as mine.This game is a mess. I was warned, but after having so many server issues with Payday 2 and friends that have antiquated hardware that make it hard to play, I decided to bite the bullet so they could crossplay with us (one feature that, for me, seems to be working?).This game is a huge step backwards for Payday, and a GIANT step backwards for video games in general. The development team here is not skilled enough to pull off what they were trying to accomplish.I ran out of space, so no comment on the few positives.

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many issues with this game still after launch and with the servers working, but the biggest problem this game has is the HARD LOCK GATEKEEPING. So XP is tied exclusively to challenges. And some of those challenges are locked behind other challenges. So even if you wanted to focus on one, which you shouldn't HAVE to, you couldn't anyways because it's locked behind another you have to complete first. And there is so much INSANE tedium to them and it's built purely to FORCE players to grind and grind and grind and spend more time in the game than just ENJOYING it. As an example, if you want to reach level 150, you'll eventually need to run the heists an X amount of times. On Normal? 150. Hard? 100. Very Hard? 80. And Overkill is 40. BUT WAIT! That's only for running it LOUD. You also have to do it the same amount of times for STEALTH. AND you have to run it loud BEFORE you can unlock the stealth ones! SO. You will have to run all 8 heists AT LEAST 300 times EACH, 150 in Loud, then 150 in stealth - by the way, that's IF you run them in the other difficulties FIRST since running once in Overkill also counts for 1 of all the others - for a total of 2400 heists. In Payday 2, this wouldn't be MANDATORY. It'd be a godd**n achievement and a cool mask. And this right here breaks the game for me the most. Forcing players by hard locking them. At the time I'm posting this, I DO NOT recommend this game AT ALL. I spent $40 dollars, and I still feel ripped off. Maybe if they fix this, change it and make XP not...THAT. Maybe I'll play it again. But right now? Hell no.

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play the game, the more I notice how much has been cut, a lot of little things that are essential.Either the release was rushed or it was just supposed to be a very simple game for casual/console players.There is currently no chat in the lobby, the matchmaking system is just annoying and confusing.Once you have pressed ready, you are no longer allowed to make it unready, which means you are no longer allowed to change the build profile if you accidentally do so chose incorrectly.You can no longer rename profiles either.The outfits are not saved separately in the profile. If you change your outfit, this applies to all profiles.No precise information when choosing missions, you don't know how many times you have played it.There are no multi-day missions.The mission menu is not well thought out, it is not divided into categories, you have to scroll for a long time. If more missions are added in the future, you will have to scroll for a very long time.Then you have to turn off the “mission videos” beforehand so that you have a better overview. Every time.And also watch the intro every time, even if you just restart the mission, you can't skip it.RNG is hardly available, so you can skip a lot of objectives next time.You can no longer give orders to bots, they are useless.Sometimes they even get in the way of stealth when they suddenly put on the mask and start shooting around. During loud missions they sometimes stop somewhere and then go down unnecessarily.But I like the new stealth system, it's different than Payday 2 and the only positive thing about the game.But everything around it seems cut and very, very simple.The mission leader's voice is monotonous and annoying.Her information is also not helpful. She says the bags are all at the destination while we are still carrying bags. There is no information about how many bags are left, so it will be a bit difficult with achievements.You often just want a perfect run with all the loot and be rewarded for it. But you won't be rewarded, it doesn't seem to be important.Because now you level with random challenges, so you don't concentrate on the missions, but have to make sure you do your personal challenges.So you slide around pointlessly (because it's a challenge) or use weapons that you don't even want to play.On the one hand, such challenges can be quite good; as they progress, it shows how much knowledge a player has of the game, weapons and mechanics. Gone are the days when players even with high infamy/level had no idea about the game because they just played the same missions for XP over and over again.On the other hand, the missions in PD3 just seem like an excuse and but it feels forced and isn't fun.There should also be a lot of XP for side tasks, optional things that you can include during the missions.But if you don't complete any challenges, you hardly get any xp.And there is no sense of success, which is not a good thing in the long term.The skill system is also unnecessarily complicated; you unlock everything one after the other. So at the beginning you play with certain skills so that you can unlock them first.Only then can you create your desired build. It artificially extends the playing time.There are no more meele attacks in the game, you can only use them to stun cops or force civilians to the ground.You can no longer dominate enemies (unless the guards give up beforehand), there is hardly any interaction with them.The enemies generally seem kind of boring. The Cloaker that you see running around, sometimes looking confused, but then very determined to blow you away. You often don't have a chance.The bulldozer looks like a stupid gorilla that charges and then runs into a wall. That seems ridiculous.I like the shields though, I also like the effect when you get too close to them. You can no longer turn them off as easily by dancing around.What I like are the little mini games at the locks, finally no stupid pressing of F until it is open.But so many details are missing. Paintings have e.g. the same bags as other loot. And no longer curled up.Throwing bags also feels strange.No dual weapons, no lasers.. Payday never had a crosshair (it came as an update for PD2, but very, very late). I always thought that was good and unique.Everything seems as wannabe-modern as all the other shooters.The music is also no longer as exciting as in the previous games.In one mission it sounds like in cyberpunk. It lacks the feeling of thrill when the assault is about to begin and the excitement when there is a break. You don't headbang anymore because the songs just play along and you don't pay attention. Too bad.One wonders whether there was even a gamedesigner who had an overview of everything and had small but important things added.I can only shake my head as to what they were thinking releasing it in this state.As if they haven't learned anything in the last 10 years.I tried to like the game, but I'm not really having fun yet and I can see so many mistakes.It's not a bad game, the graphics are pretty, there are a lot of first missions, but everything seems like a generic shooter without anything of its own, everything that Payday is all about with all the attention to detail and charm.(Because there is no neutral thumb on Steam, I'll give it a thumbs down.Let's see what happens in the future)

_childDocuments_.review: Just another rushed halve baked game. The only positive about this game is the moment to moment gameplay, stealth is more developed and the gunplay is better, than in PD2.Account progression is based on achievements/challenges, NO XP gained from just completing a heist.Those challenges/achievements have zero QoL to them: -NO ping current challenges in order to track progress.-NO key words search bar for more convenient searching.Overall they are more chores than challenges:  kill "x" amount of "n" type of enemy with a specific weapon or place "x" item "n" amount of times.Need Nebula account and is always online, no  matchmaking.You cant create lobbys like in PD2. NO pre planning, NO no drop in joining, cant change type(friends only /invite only/ public) of game during heist. Cant choose between loud or stealth approach. If you want to play private, you still have to wait to find a game, cant just start by your self.New skill system is inferior to the PD2 one. Just 8 one day heists, unlike PD2 with 2 or 3 day heist with escape the cops bonus day. The heist are with basic objectives, no cooking or find the right thing.Do not waste your money on this BETA, wait until is improved over time.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay is evolved from Payday 2, and very fun, but Payday 2 was around for so long, that still makes this game feel on-par with shooters five years ago. The UX, however, is a step back. The pause screen no longer shows how many bags you've secured.  The type of loot and value of loot no longer appears on-screen when you secure it. You have to matchmake individual heists, rather than simply launching heist from a lobby or searching for any active heists. Join-in-progress no longer exists. You do not stay in a lobby after the heist. Did you have a great crew of randoms? They're gone forever. The ONLY real positives are how much better progression and weapon attachment unlocking works.TLDR; This game is a few small steps forward and a couple leaps back. Go ahead and wait for a sale- the game is great fun- but bring some friends and don't uninstall PAYDAY 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was very skeptical about how different it felt from payday 2 but I gave the game a chance. I admit it was growing on me, but I didn't like a few things. Gun attachments are specific to each gun. You cant get a sight from a payday or coins and put it on any relevant gun. You have to level up each gun for a few heists before you can put anything on it. This sucks when you just buy a new gun and have to suffer through it having zero attachments for several heists before it becomes less crappy.The cop AI is just as stupid as it was in payday 2, which is fine. That game evolved into an excellent and addictingly fun horde shooter of sorts. But now the cops are fewer and farther between and have much more health. Also, non-headshots do practically zero damage. We're talking 5-6 body shots from a marksman rifle compared to one headshot. This wouldn't be a problem except for the next part. The lighting and visibility is completely awful and in some areas, cops are almost impossible to see until they shoot at you. All the weird visual effects that felt like motion blur were always on for everything and just made my eyes melt into mush. I'd look down the sight of a rifle and I could not see a thing. It felt horrendous. It is just so hard to see things in less brightly lit areas and at a distance. Cosmetics and customization also feel fumbled. The mask-building screen is all gone from the first game and you have to go back and forth between all these different awkward menus and it is not clear what you're allowed to buy and what you aren't. I'd have things lit up and I tried to click on it and was informed I needed to be level 95. Some of it doesn't make sense. Why do need to be level 95 to get this pink paint job compared to this lighter pink paint job you only need to be level 20 for? Why does this charm cost 20 of the C-Marks or whatever to get instead of cash? Its weird and I don't know why it is like this.I wouldn't care as much about any of this if the servers worked but they don't at all. They're terrible. Six matches in a row I've been booted out mid game. Pathetic. I want my money back.

_childDocuments_.review: While not as expansive as Payday 2, this is expanding and growing significantly every time there is an update. There are some definite differences that take getting used to if you're an experienced payday 2 heister, but it is undeniably a good game that is getting better. I give it 4.3 out of 5 lockpicks. That said, I preferred the way they handled specialization in payday 2. The perk decks along side the skill points was masterfully done and I loved the interplay of being able to use such varied and unique builds for getting through tough heists quietly or even on loud runs where you just needed that extra oomph. The way they sort of merged the two into a gestalt for payday 3 felt very clunky and awkward, and the changes have smoothed it out considerably, but it still feels inferior to the previous game system. I'm excited for changes that are being made and to see what gets added to the roadmap next. There were a lot of issues initially on this game, and its launch was troubled, but I honestly feel like they're doing an excellent job of recovering from that and listening to the community in making changes that are wanted and needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Great bones, horrible decisions.Payday 3 at its core, is a very fun game, flat out, I have a great time playing it solo or with friends, stealth feels great, loud feels good, new movement is refreshing, skill tree is diverse.And thats the end of good things to say, progression in this game makes absolutely zero sense, a list of challenges that just get progressively longer is the  way to earn character XP, I assume they did this to prevent people from just grinding the same heists over and over to power level, guess what?  The most efficient way to level up in this game is to sit and watch a choke point, and kill the endless wave of law enforcement that enter, you don't have to steal money, you don't need to monitor hostages, there is no point. Just focus on kills to level, it actively punishes you for wanting to play casually. All you have to do to fix this, is just acknowledge that the new system doesn't work, and reward people for the amount of loot stolen per heist, and if you still want to push people to do challenges, or give them an incentive to progress in their challenges, give them bonus XP for amount of law enforcement killed. Boom, people who just want to stealth get rewarded for getting as much loot as they do, and boom, people who don't care for loot and like playing loud get rewarded for killing as many as they can. Attempting to deter people from grinding the same heists has harmed both play styles, don't punish people for not wanting to dedicate all of their free time to your 8 heists. And lets be honest, Payday is at its best when you feel like you're in a crime gang from the movies and everyone can specialize in what they like to do. Also a sincere middle finger for not having Offline mode, y'all can do better.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR AT BOTTOMAs the game is currently offered to us as a consumer I cannot recommend this to anyone. If you are not playing this through Xbox Game Pass I would not suggest paying money for this game. The game has some extremely high areas where is succeeds but the area's in which it lacking is very staggering to properly enjoying this game. I would break it down to 3 major factors that ruin the gameCons-Social Aspect/Matchmaking:For whatever reason we have a worse lobby system than PD2 where match completion boots you back to the main menu so staying with the team you just played with is practically impossible. ALSO NO PRE GAME LOBBY OR MATCH CLEAR TEXT CHAT?!?!?!?!??!?!!??!?! WTF. Also not being able to talk in Voice Chat hampers the ability to work together with your team. Discord is really saving this game in its current state. Server Issues:This game is online only so if you wanna play solo its a hassle and if the servers are down then guess what, NO ONE IS PLAYING. There are times I've tried to do solo Very Hard or Overkill for stealth and while inputting friends only or invite only and it keeps giving me issues trying to create the lobby. Also match is based solely on hosts internet but thats whatever and its expected I guess.Content:Only 8 heists and they feel like they ramp up in terms of complexity to ease everyone in and be a more beginner friendly game but that means out of the 8 only like 6 are extremely full of depth and replayability. That doesnt sound bad if they're hitting on all cylinders at like a 75% rate but it actually is when you take into account the fact that there are no multi day heists, no returning heists on top of these 8 original or the fact that the missions we have don't generate to a different tileset on in game restart.This game does have Pro's though so don't think this is all negative:The gunplay is so satisfying. Guns feel and sound AND look good. They got shooting right in this game and the movement feels extremely smooth in comparison to PD2. I can play hours on end just off the main mechanics in the game. The weapons all feel extremely different as well in terms of function, range and potential. The perk system is also a cool new take and it's not my cup of tea but it's something different so I'll take it. The maps all look good and have a nice layout for the most part.THE REAL UPGRADE is absolutely the SPECIALS. The Dozer is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ real tank and the cloakers are scary as ♥♥♥♥. The naders and tasers also can be real threats if not treated immediately and you feel the tension whenever you know one of them is in your immediate area. They really help to spice up the gameplay and the fact we can expect more soon and for free is so exciting as a PD fan.If you are a diehard payday fan then get this by all means but if you are just a casual fan I dont think it would be justified paying $40 for this game in its current state. I would wait for a sale or until possibly the UE5 upgrade. Maybe the engine upgrade will be a vast improvement to how the game handles and allow them to pump the game with more content faster.TLDR- The game is good if you love Payday but if you're not already a huge Payday fan this probably won't make you one. Play on gamepass only if you just wanna try it out or casually play Payday.

The fact that they're continuing to push out paid DLC in a base game that is so severely lacking is appalling. Progression is still dominated by boring, repetitive challenges, offline mode has not been added or even so much as announced, and builds are dominated by a few armor-centric perks because of the changes to armor from payday 2. The devs need to focus on making the base game tolerable and at least comparable to payday 2 as far as features and systems go before they think about trying to make an extra buck off of DLC packs that give you very little content for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Payday 3 is an interesting tale.We all know/heard about how the launch went. With server issues out the wazoo and many flawed gameplay mechanics bogging down the experience, the game's launch was a complete disaster. There is no denying that. Since then, the flow of actual content in the game (in terms of new weapons, heists and things of that ilk) has been dreadfully slow. For the past nearly 7 months or so, the game has been in an interesting limbo in terms of content.HOWEVERDuring those months during "Operation Medic Bag," the game has made many fixes, overhauls and updates to either improve, completely change or overhaul certain mechanics and systems in the game. Now with many of these major fixes and changes out of the way, Payday 3 is finally receiving new content again! Following the release of Boys In Blue, the second heist added as part of the year one roadmap, I fully believe that this will mark the turning point for Payday 3. The game at it's core is exceedingly fun. The gunplay is satisfying, the movement is smooth and the overall feel of the game is great. With the systems surrounding the core game being changed and fixed as time goes on, the game is primed to be saved.If you're on the fence about trying this game, I would dive in and try for yourself. Now is the perfect time to give it a try while it's on sale! PAYDAY 3 is on the road to recovery, and it seems that the speed is about to pick up!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an avid PAYDAY player, nothing major but enough to know enough about the game. I've played a lot of PAYDAY2 and base a lot of these points on that game. If you want reasons to and reasons not to play, check this out - bare in mind, this is simply my experience.Reasons I like PAYDAY 3:- Gunfights & general shooting is so much better than PD2- Shooting fire extinguishers, gas cans and other items are great for spontaneous gameplay events- Hostage system is a lot better than PD2, having the ability to hold them and use them for situations is great- Lockpicking having it's own mechanic now makes it so much more immersive than simply holding a button- Stealing keycards from guards is fun - QR code stealing, wifi connection, hacking phones are all great new mechanics- Drills seem more fair in PD3 than they were in PD2, don't break down as much and seem more maintainable- UV lights on keycard readers makes it easier for players to determine the right code - Hostage negotiation for time & resources gives the player a good option of sacrifice and decision making- The lowered amount of characters in the PAYDAY gang makes it less confusing removes unnecessary characters (i know i'm in the minority)- Getting caught by guards in private areas only gets you kicked out of said area, doesn't cause mass panic- Graphics. Great step-up.- Short videos before and after heists are great for story and bring a lot for new playersThings I am not so keen on in PAYDAY 3:- XP system relies solely on challenges now, unlike PD2 where XP can be gained from random things like killing guards. On occasion you can complete an entire stealth mission and not gain any XP because you completed no challenges.- No offline mode for singleplayers (unlike PD2)- No pausing (unlike PD2)- No customisation for bot players (unlike PD2)- No preplanning or heist maps (unlike PD2)- Character customisation, suits, guns, gloves, masks are very limited and lacklustre. I doubt the community would mind if PD2 customisables were implemented but adapted to the updated graphics.- Bots can be released from custody without the main player needing to do anything- Bots on occasion can get stuck and become completely useless- Bots make it difficult to pass them bags with their random and unpredictable movement- No ability to stop the dialog from the characters on the heist menu, you will hear this every. single. time.- Guards are not alerted when you close doors on/near them, or other events for example the window shutters in No Rest For The Wicked- Melee weapons. There are no melee weapons.- Menu's seem less creative than PD2, too modern and not necessarily the PAYDAY style- Missing features which made PD2 that bit better - no safehouse, no crime spree. no , no offshore account- Overkill weapons seem - meh. There doesn't seem a lot of incentive to go and get them and use them for me- Player is unable to stop all dye packs in No Rest For The Wicked when solo- Little amount of heists make the game repetitive and boring- Not many guns to buy and choose from- Some objectives are extremely hard for new players and even old players when not given a lot of promptingWith all this said, I still enjoy this game, and a lot of things I've listed are probably due to be added. But if you're looking to buy this game and play it now, hoping for all of the above, maybe hold out until more information is given out.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this by saying that I am a huge Payday fan. I had played the original right before 2 came out and then I've been playing 2 since release and through all of the changes/updates/system refreshes. When this game came out I had blocked all media to be excited and surprised when I finally booted it up. I do not believe this was the right call and in the game's current state, I do not recommend.The proverbial straw that broke the camel's back was being stuck in a lobby, "searching" for a private match. While it is perfectly reasonable to have a system down-age every now and again it appears that the issue has been going on most of the release day. This is only a small issue though when it comes to the overall narrative that the game will always be online. In previous titles, if the servers went down you were allowed to play single player-offline mode. This was also perfect for when you wanted to perfect your skills or maybe had a busy moment and needed to pause. The offline mode is no longer available. You can play single player, but this will be online and tied to a "lobby". This means that there is no pausing a mission, and when you need to restart, a vote will technically need to be done in order to reset the match. The main issue with this is that when servers go down like they did during launch, everyone is not allowed to enjoy their game, and when the servers are running, you cannot immediately jump into a heist. Extra time is needed to "search" for  a server and then load in. Payday 2 heists on release were random at best, but offline mode and the ability to start a heist immediately offset that.When I could play the game it was good if not lacking. I do agree with most here that the overall stealth system is very much improved. Abilities like being able to walk around and interact with items/objectives in casing mode is a godsend and the seeing the major differences when doing a heist on overkill versus very hard or normal is a huge plus. Heists are not randomized with every restart (though they are randomized every time the mission launches from the main menu) so you have the ability to perfect your run and if a mistake is made at the end, same/similar steps can be followed. The ability to take hostages and move them to the exact spot you want them or use them for objectives is great. There are no real downsides to stealth at this version of the game.If the heist starts out loud or inevitably goes loud due to your *fantastic* crew, the minute to minute game play is solid. Weapons feel punchy and good to operate. Police presence feels more encompassing and feel more aggressive than the previous title. With a completely decked out build I can see serious fun in any loud heist. Performances during the cut-scenes are very well performed and was definitely something I looked forward to whenever I finished a heist, but the still images with hidden faces were a bit of a disappointment. A comic style would've been preferred if they were going the route of animation. Music for this game, like it's predecessor is top notch and almost reason enough to make your heist loud.  There are a few other minor personal issues I really had with the game though. The OVERKILL weapons (or at least the grenade launcher) are not really worth the effort. The weapons cannot be switched out and when you need to maybe utilize a pistol to kill a single cop the weapon needs to be dropped, or lack the power to do serious damage. The Grenade Launcher can kill 6 cops in a room, but it's only marginally better than a grenade and with many of the maps being close quarters, end up hurting yourself more. With only two weapons it's *EXTREMELY* situational and in my playing is rarely more effective than a standard weapon.The tutorial also covers zero additions for stealth and is extremely linear. Several new features are included in Stealth Heists but there is nothing to explain what they do.My last issue worth noting is the UI and menus/store are both a pain to navigate and unattractive. Having weapons level up in a Call of Duty style system is okay, and I will take that over randomly hoping for the wanted mod/cosmetic. Playing this on a controller though there are some issues when it comes to navigation, with my main gripe being if you are in your inventory, you choose to buy a weapon, you are brought to the weapon store. No problem with that, but you cannot push "B" (Or circle for PS users) to go back to your inventory after being in this screen. What you have to do instead is navigate back to the inventory screen. This is the same whether you are buying a mask, gloves, or an outfit too. Also, when choosing to purchase a sidearm you're brought to the generic store screen, this lead me to believe I could use a single shot rifle and assault rifle at the same time which is not the case.  If more weapons are to be added, the secondary weapons need to have their own purchase screen so that the player can know what weapon builds they can work with. To summarize I do want this game to succeed and for Starbreeze to continue making improvements just like they did with Payday 2, however with Payday 2, I feel like I was getting a complete game and while the $40 price tag helps Payday 3, I can't shake the feeling that I'm playing an Beta. I will return to play Payday 3, but I cannot recommend it in it's current status and I will not recommend a game that forces online only when a large chunk of it's fanbase is also single player.Edit:Reviewing this there are additional tutorials for other features. These did not launch automatically so there was no way for me to know unless I chose to reopen the tutorial tab. I retract about the tutorials not being present but this does add that the UI needs deep improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm heavily considering a refund.Overall payday 3 in it's current state is not very enjoyable. The game runs like crap, there are stutters and frame drops, sometimes you get a random stutter when an objective finishes sometimes you do a quick 180 and you get a mini freeze, just enough to throw your aim off. It's very irritating. To add to it the game doesn't even look that impressive graphically.The servers are bad, the past two days you were lucky to get into a game, now it's a bit better, unacceptable that you have to connect to a server to play solo, peer to peer has been dropped.The progression system is flawed and broken, completing a heist can yield no exp if you don't complete any of the finite challenges, not very motivating, apart from that some challenges are broken and some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy(complete the same heist 150 times). The system needs a major rework. Progression is also slow and linear which means everyone unlocks the same weapons, the same masks and the same customisation options, it's hard to stand out.The menus are atrocious, they look like they are from a mobile game, hard to navigate quickly and inefficient in their design.The skills are another thing that I would expect to get redesigned. They might have aimed for a more grounded feel, but with we lost the fun and variaty that the builds in payday2 offered. Controversial opinion but I would much rather they rework the skills into something more influential on your gameplay.The UI is very generic and I much preferred the one in the second game, had more spirit to it, this is a minor concern as i'm sure there are going to be plenty of mods that alter the HUDAnother minor issue of course is the lack of content, yet this is something that with time will improve and it's unfair to compare the game to payday 2 with it's 10 years of support.With the deepsilver deal monetization is another concern for the game, microtransactions and other predatory mechanics are to be expected in the future. C stacks already look awfully like a scrapped microtransation systemOn the positive note, the gameplay seems to be good. I didn't get to play too much and the performance of the game distracts you from the gameplay but it seems to be good, also I didn't get to experience the higher difficulties because of the challenges being broken.Under the pile of stink there is an ok payday 2 successor, DO NOT BUY YET unless you really cannot wait to play, thank you
