Oh, and the best part? The stats aren't even visible in game so unless you go onto the website you wouldn't have a damn clue. AND you have to specifically enable telemetry for it to count. Absolute disaster. Boys in Blue was fun, but not mind blowing by any means. The variety is at least welcomed. The armor system still sucks eggs and everyone just uses the Adaptive armor that is meant to be like the PD2 armor system. Apparently they're coming back from summer vacation to drop a free heist and the next DLC (shotgunning them as I mentioned 2 months ago). Hopefully those end up being a nice refresher. I just want this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game to be good. I loved PD2 and was so amped for this game and they keep trying to sprint this game to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grave. It genuinely feels so incompetent that I'd more likely believe the higher ups are actually trying to flatline this game. I just wanted to play some GD Payday man. I'm not gonna "show up now" for a game that not only doesn't reward my time but actively spits in my face Almir. Get real dude. Pull your damn heads out of the sand and put your listening ears on.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------5/28/24Still crickets. They've added a skill line or 2 I think? I saw something about an LMG as if Loud gameplay was that good. Uhhh a grenade? And it sounds like they are starting to tease the second dlc. Considering they've got 4 months to release 3 dlc, it's not looking good. My guess is they are going to shotgun the content in the next 3 months or so and it's going to play like ♥♥♥♥. All the medic bag fixes they've done have basically just gone back to what worked in PD2... like it probably should have been. We can blame a publisher all we want on this, but the wild amounts of ineptitude surrounding this game just leads me to believe Starbreeze didn't have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clue what they were doing. Knowing they've already starting tanking in market value again they've got very little room to turn this around, but there aren't many games that can hit the level of 200 players a day and like 7 viewers on Twitch and truly bounce back from that. So I think I've just got to accept that I threw my money in the blender to play an Early Access game and move on with my life. Maybe I'll poke my head in next year and find something worth playing. More likely I'll see they've abandoned development to focus on their D&D game that'll inevitably suck.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------2/29/24Well the below aged like milk. The below was written at a time of nostalgia. It was also written as someone who got early access and got to play it without immediately being bodied by server outages for 2 weeks before even getting into a lobby. The below review also believed they might actually do something with this game. Sure I've got my time out of this game, but after the first 30 it just became a slog and a grind. I plowed through it out of the excitement of updates and expansions, but after about 6 months, with only 4 updates, none of which have been that notable, I no longer have any faith in Starbreeze nor this game. The fact that they have literally driven this game into the ground out of inaction just makes me think they took my money and ran. It is a heisting game after all. We just didn't know we were the ones being robbed. As someone who loved PD2, while the actual movement and combat feels better, this game spits on that memory. It's honestly heartbreaking. I've not played much since the launch and only briefly when the first DLC dropped but with this 4th update, I'll finally be uninstalling this game. Maybe someday I'll be back, but it's going to take a hell of a lot to get me there. 6 months for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unready button. Meanwhile you've got Arrowhead doubling capacity to a game that was already wildly more successful than they ever planned for in a matter of 2 weeks and the content tap is already starting to flow. The rate PD3 is going tells me that even if the game was somehow a bigger success and didn't have the issues it did, they still would have lost their player base with their poor decisions and their complete abandonment. To call this game actively developed is honestly a bit of a joke. Just save your money and go buy lunch or Helldivers 2 or something.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------If you liked the first 2 games, you'll like this one. It truly is just a better Payday 2. I've got small complaints here and there, like the menu being pretty basic, no quick join feature, etc. But they are all things that can be fixed and if there is anything to say about Starbreeze, they do a good job listening to the community. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so badly, I really did. I have over 1200 hours in PAYDAY 2, and have been a longtime fan of the franchise since PAYDAY: The Heist. Despite all of the graphical and gameplay improvements made with PAYDAY 3, I honestly cannot recommend this game until the developers fix the matchmaking/solo play issues. I downloaded this game onto MY hard drive, to run on MY computer, playing with ZERO other players. There is absolutely no reason I should be forced to connect to an always online service to play this game. Until this is remedied, this review will remain negative.8/4/24 UpdateNearly one entire year from release and this game is still just as much of a trash fire as it was on day one. Solo mode BETA took months to finally implement, skill system overhaul was much needed but done far too late. Adaptive armor is a welcome return to form but currently has very few skill synergies in a game based around a COD Warzone based armor system. Developers are focused on paid DLC content and have been dripping a slow feed of "fixes" in a vain attempt to placate the angry fans. Just to put it in perspective, PAYDAY 2 received 7 DLC heists within the first year after release. Only 2 of which were paid content priced at $4 each. PAYDAY 3 has received 4 new maps, 2 paid and 2 free. Developers have clearly shown where their priorities are with PAYDAY 3. It's not to make a good game, but to claw every single dollar they possibly can from your wallet. Avoid PAYDAY 3.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like Payday 3.I'm a massive fan of Payday in general (I've got hundreds of hours on console Payday 2 which really goes to show the love I've got for this series) but I cannot possibly recommend this in its current state. It's nice to see the servers running much better than they did at launch, but the game feels rushed and unfinished. If Payday 3 had come out in EA instead of a full $40 release, maybe this could've gone a lot better. The XP progression system is so awful I can't believe it managed to actually release like this. In some parts of the game, it feels smooth and polished - and in others, like it was thrown together at the last minute like they were trying to rush this out the door. The UI is bland and uninteresting, the Crew AI is unbelievably broken, and altogether nothing was learned from Payday 2. So many QOL features (How do we not have voice chat?!) are missing that are in Payday 2. I know Payday 2 has 10 years of content under its belt, but those 10 years of experience (+ Payday: The Heist) should've been used to make Payday 3 better instead of this mess. The only reason I'm playing this game now is because of the modding community making the game feel cared for and fresh.I really hope I can edit this review one day to positive.

_childDocuments_.review: Avoided this piece of shovelware for a while before I caved with the last sale because heist games are my favorite genre. A year after what was easily one of the worst launch days in the modern gaming era with all filler and no substance (looking at you Starbreeze/New York Bank Vault giveaway promotional day), it is safe to say that Payday 3 is depressingly okay- it refuses to take the risks it needs to in order to be a proper sequel to PAYDAY 2 and every facet of this iteration takes a firm step back in most areas for me. PAYDAY 2 simply felt more open and fun with how you could play. This is much more restrictive in both movements and character builds.Its definitely lost a lot of the magic and luster of PAYDAY 2 with many of the previous game's core features and highlights being trimmed down for the worse. Masks are very limited and many of the guns feel so similar that you may as well just focus on one or two you like and leveling them with the now seemingly standardized Call of Duty Warzone upgrade system. Perks have been gutted too, with many of them feeling situational at best on loud heists. The DLC guns unfortunately outclass every base game gun, so those who are looking to invest should absolutely grab the Gold edition (shamefully promoted at around a cool 35 USD when I purchased this). This sort of reveals the direction Starbreeze took PAYDAY and largely why I would not recommend this game. DLC has always been a part of Starbreeze's equation in their games and many of PAYDAY 2's DLCs missed the mark (H3H3 pack, Goat Simulator Heist, OVERKILL pack, Biker/Rust Heist, The Alesso Heist just to name a few), but players cannot even access the heists without the DLC purchase- a feature in PAYDAY 2 allows the host to be sole owner of the DLC allowing non-DLC owners to play- and the base game heists are absolutely stale. Each DLC heist would rank above all the base heists for me if I had to list them in order. Finally, the highest difficulty (OVERKILL) is a joke and Starbreeze desperately needs to add some sort of patch to include Death Wish difficulty from PAYDAY 2 as I finished all available heists in both loud and stealth if available with randoms using the Desert Eagle and one of the five shotguns and it was not challenging- I think I experienced two mission fail screens over the course of my 27 hour playtime.One of the real highlights is the music, which has been updated but keeps much of the high-pace energy during shootouts and low skulking tones during stealth operations. As well, the human shield factor/civilian rework is nice. I feel many games are too scared to try this nowadays just off the optics alone, and while PAYDAY 3's system is a little inconsistent, it feels like a big reason to try the game out for me since they have a whole perk tree for those game mechanics. That's about it. I don't see too much reason to get this right now unless GTA/Red Dead Online are not cutting it for you and you don't want to take the gamble on Rockay City being a dumper. The heist genre needs a lot of love and I think while the game has its fun moments, PAYDAY 3 is not worth your time unless you have a dedicated friend group willing to commit to the grind and play it out. Avoid it at all costs at full price, it is objectively not worth 50/60 dollars and the base level game is simply not worth purchase at all.Hopefully Starbreeze can continue their momentum on this game and change my review, but I would need a serious rework to some mechanics/leveling systems and a higher difficulty setting for all available heists.

_childDocuments_.review: As promised, if the matchmaking error was fixed I'd change my review and it seems to have been fixed! So here we go, clowns.Payday 3 had quite the rollercoaster launch experience, which initially led me to share a negative review due to recurring matchmaking issues. However, it's worth noting that the game's stability has significantly improved since then. In fact, over the past couple of days, I've encountered matchmaking issues only once, even while playing with people from different parts of the world.Let me dive into some of the fantastic aspects of Payday 3 that make it a substantial upgrade from its predecessor, Payday 2. The introduction of new physics adds a delightful layer of realism to the gameplay. Weapons have a satisfying and substantial feel to them, making every firefight an enjoyable experience. The inclusion of intriguing puzzles, such as pressure plates and a new lockpicking system, injects a rush of adrenaline into heists, especially when you're trying to avoid a patrolling guard just around the corner.The game boasts a diverse range of maps, ranging from straightforward and accessible ones to complex stealth missions lasting over 30 minutes. It's refreshing to see that the enemies are not impervious tanks but react realistically to shots, prompting players to aim skillfully to conserve precious ammunition. Additionally, the return to a more serious tone enhances the overall immersion in the game world.However, there are a few areas where Payday 3 could use some improvement. For instance, it's somewhat inconvenient that players need to restart the game to track their progress with firearms. Furthermore, levels are tied to specific challenges rather than allowing players to enjoy the game in their preferred style. While the initial arsenal of available weapons is somewhat limited, given Starbreeze's track record, it's reasonable to expect a steady stream of new firearms through future updates.The parkour system could benefit from some refinement, as players often find themselves repeatedly falling off the same objects or encountering unexpected leaps through vents instead of smooth entry. Additionally, there appears to be an occasional issue with guards inexplicably converging on the room where hostages are held, although I anticipate these issues will be addressed in due course. (Please make the shotgun more meaty up close though..)In summary, I would rate Payday 3 at 8/10 clown masks, signifying a highly enjoyable experience.

Customization is quite boring and limited, not a lot of patterns for masks or guns and those you can get there are extremely basic. I expect the good stuff to be locked behind the DLC, which I guess is the future of gaming. Who wants a 40+ Euro game with lots of content anyways. AI teammates are quite dumb. There are no numbers for weapons when you switch parts, only some visual bars, some plus and minus makes no sense as they do the opposite of being a plus or minus compared to everything else. Having to get a civilian to see you and react to you before you can shout them down to the ground, with the marking stuff button, is kinda jank. Finding lobbies is awful, never get a full lobby on normal or hard, either get 1 or 2 and people instantly leave, probably because of AI kicking you if you "unready".The good parts is that the movement feels great, the lockpicking is great, enemies feel better and smarter. Some special enemies are not as annoying and the shooting feels good. Being able to stealth with mask only is a great addition and feels fun. The maps looks good, performance is okay. The skill unlocking system is kind of dumbed down from Payday 2 and it's ok still, it was ok in payday 2 as well, nothing spectacular.First game I've pre-ordered in a long time, but I know now that I shouldn't make exceptions even for series that I earlier loved. Still a good game with lots of bad stuff, so I can't wholeheartedly recommend this to anyone. Feels like a 2015 game with a 2023 skin. Which has taken a lot of bad parts from "modern games".EDIT: The more I play, the more I hate this game. When you can do a heist and get literally 0 exp, is devastating. Ah yes, give me all this money that I can't use on anything, because I can't level up to get anything to buy! The level system is the worst I've ever encountered in a game ever...EDIT 2: I literally can't level. Seems bugged now. No challenges completed no matter what.EDIT 3: I keep playing it and it is a fun game, with not a lot of bugs at least. The challenges seem to register now, without having to restart the game, guess that's a point of not being able to communicate exp progression to the server, lol. I still can't play whenever I want, as in "peak hours" which are a lot of hours at this point the servers still go down, so you can't play anything at all at those times. The infamy leveling system is still dumb and leveling weapons is still really slow as I feared. There is a lot of good stuff that makes the game feel great, but bogged down by a lot of dumb and unpolished stuff. You need WAY to many c-stacks(secondary currency) to buy a lot of the stuff in-game, which locks out attachments for your guns even. It's a system made for you to come back and play every week overtime... Like a mobile game.I would recommend this game  probably never, it's not in state where I can say you won't be frustrated by some stuff and mechanics, but it is also enjoyable at it's core if you're not into grinding.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would give the current state of the game an 8/10. At the time of this review I have 36 hours and am rank 51.Overall, most of the negative reviews can be split into two general categories: 1) Networking Issues and 2) How Infamy is gained. Let me address these concerns:1) I cannot think of a multiplayer game that on release didn't have networking issues. While it's certainly disappointing, it was not unexpected. Matchmaking stability is mostly stable now. There are still a few issues, but it has improved significantly. I do agree with other people's sentiments that an offline single player mode should have been available from the start for a variety of reasons and was a major oversight on Starbreeze's part.2) In PD3, You career level (aka Infamy) in this game, is gained through completing a variety of challenges. Max infamy is currently level 150, and I would argue most players can achieve infamy 100 with 100-150 hours of intentional play. This will unlock most of the weapons and all of the skill points available to you. You will not be max level in a week, and that is a good thing. The previous Payday games have all had long runs with a active player-base, and this system is built for the long hall. The vast majority of these challenges are pretty easy to get such as kill X number of people with X gun OR complete a mission on X difficulty. There are few that will be challenging; My friends and I still haven't been able to get the centerpiece in the art gallery. And yes, there are a handful that want you to do every mission 150-300 times, but those are long term achievements gained from playing a long time so not sure why the community is upset about them..I like the challenge system over a flat xp system because it ties into the lore and the nature of the game. With the challenge system, a heister who has high infamy is known for accomplishing several different types or heists. Versus a flat xp system where a heister has robbed a gas station 10,000 times? That doesn't make sense.That being said, my only complaint at this time is that I don't think every challenge is achievable solo which is objectively unfair to players who prefer a solo experience.Some Improvements I would like to see that other may not have mentioned:- Easier way to navigate challenges. i.e. filter by weapon type, mission type, and a search feature.- Make weapon attachments impact weapon performance more. My choices do not feel meaningful.- Clearer information on what a weapon attachment does. i.e. "+Hipfire Recoil" decreases the recoil bar on a weapons stats which is confusing. Its it "Yes, more recoil" or "Yes, less recoil"? Or inversely, "No, more recoil" or "No, less recoil"? Very confusing.- Would like to see new missions the focuses more on outside environments, moving objectives (like a train), navigating civilian spaces. Most mission are these self contained little areas that require long periods of patience. I would like to see more "chaotic" missions that require players to dynamic move around the level snaking they're way to objective. More reaction based vs calculated movements.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very worthy sequel - as PAYDAY 2 got on in years, it shifted away from being so much of a tense heist sim to more of a horde shooter. More heists were loud-only, Pro Jobs were removed, more and more difficulty levels were added, etc. If you wanted to stealth a heist in that game by the end, you needed to do it in a very exact way with no mistakes, crouch jumping around the map and shotgunning guards into corners to avoid using body bags. I, personally, still enjoyed this style in its way - but it was extremely "video gamey," where if something went wrong the first resort was the restart heist button.After all of Starbreeze's various dramas with publishers and the problems with the long-in-the-tooth Diesel Engine, I think what this franchise needed most of all was a moment to take a breath and a clean slate.That's essentially what PAYDAY 3 provides. Without spoiling too much of the fun of discovering the new systems for yourself, I'll give you a brief rundown of things I found wonderful.First - stealth has been so overhauled, with the new "social stealth" system. There are now three levels of privacy for areas in a map: public, private, and secure. If you get caught in a private area, security will escort you out, and even if you get caught in a secure area you can let yourself be cuffed without masking up. Not telling how, but there are heists you can complete *without even putting your mask on.* It feels like Ocean's Eleven when you pull off a score like that, it's great.Second - the skills have been significantly simplified, but not too much. Perk decks have been entirely removed, and replaced with skill lines you can research in whichever order you like, and you gain the option of using more skills in a line by having it equipped. There are now three statuses that you can have at any given time: EDGE, GRIT, and RUSH, and different skills give you those statuses in different ways, or different bonuses for having those statuses. To be quite honest, the massive jumble of percentages and meters away and different cooldown timers made crafting your own builds kind of ridiculous for anyone without a degree in PAYDAY 2 - this system is a good fix for that problem.Third - console heisters, your ship has come in! This PAYDAY has crossplay!Okay, so maybe that's not of the utmost importance to the Steam community, but it still made me happy. If you've read this far, here's my hidden tip - put points in Grifter. After getting shafted for years (again, probably in no small part due to the various dramas and the idiosyncracies of the Diesel Engine) players on consoles can finally enjoy popping helmets and bagging cash with the rest of us.Fourth and finally - the current climate around how the game is played. This one's a bit more nebulous, but (at least in early access) people are willing to let a heist you've been stealthing go loud and shoot your way out, even if their build isn't optimized for it. This I probably love most of all, cause it really captures the feeling of the heist movies that inspired this whole franchise. "Ah crud, the S has HTF. Mask up, cops are inbound. Send out some hostages, it'll buy us a little extra time on the drill! Not too many charges in the ammo bag, either... screw it. Alright, time to start blasting!" That tension and thrill, the Mr. Pink running from the cops or Chris Shiherlis fleeing the bank sort of feeling, was really missing for a while there. It's cool to have it back.In short, highly recommend picking this one up

_childDocuments_.review: Payday 3? More like Payday 0.3, because that's about how much content you're getting for your hard-earned cash. I had high hopes for this game, but it's a total disappointment from start to finish.First off, let's talk about the weapons. There are only a few to choose from, and they all feel like they were pulled from a bargain bin at a dollar store. Where are the cool, customizable firearms we were promised? It's as if the developers decided to phone it in and give us the bare minimum in this department. If you're a fan of variety and excitement, look elsewhere, because Payday 3 certainly won't scratch that itch.Then there's the heists. Or should I say, heist, singular. It feels like you're stuck doing the same job over and over again. There's so little variety that it becomes mind-numbingly repetitive. Where are the creative and intricate missions that made the previous Payday games so engaging? It's like the developers just copy-pasted one heist and called it a day.But the absolute worst part of Payday 3 has to be the server issues. Good luck trying to connect to a game with your friends. You'll spend more time staring at a loading screen than actually playing the game. It's infuriating, and it makes you wonder if the developers even bothered to test their servers before releasing this mess.Overall, Payday 3 is a colossal disappointment. With a lackluster selection of weapons, a dearth of heists, and server problems that make it nearly unplayable, it's a game that's not worth your time or money. Save yourself the frustration and look elsewhere for a worthwhile gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Being a newcomer to the Payday series with no prior experience, my initial five minutes of playing Payday 3 left me pleasantly surprised. The game not only met but exceeded my expectations on multiple fronts. Its gameplay felt incredibly intuitive, delivering a wholesome first-person shooter experience. The firearms provided a satisfying, almost arcade-like sensation reminiscent of Call of Duty. Moreover, the game boasted fluid movement mechanics that added to its overall enjoyment.Despite the controversy surrounding the game's launch, I had pre-purchased it the day before its release and encountered no server-related problems. _childDocuments_.review: This game is Great; and I feel its hard to go back to payday 2 after how much ive enjoyed of it so far.WARNING! :If you think this game will be Payday 2 'The Sequel'. then you'll have to understand its more 'payday: The Heist 2.0' than just a updated version of payday 2.Also, the state of the servers are now in a better state and / or Fixed since it the release two weeks ago.so if you hear people talking about issues with servers, they are most likely dealt with.Thank you.So to start off;This game is what i felt was missing from payday 2 in most ways. A game about the thrill of heisting, and challenge of those heists. so here we are, and it was a rough launch; servers were a mess, which i seen plenty of 'That' kind of issues in games before like Apex legends or Warframe when the influx of people is TOO great. For warframe in perticular during tenno-con with the amount of players joining ingame for the event. Then of course theres the whole issues of "Not enough weapons, cosmetics, heists, ect." from a majority of reviews. which its funny, that people expect a new game that released in a way, the same way as payday 2 launch; including but not limited too, both games having few starting heist at launch with 11 heists in PD2 vs 8 in PD3. not alot of stuff early on, and heck even not alot of perks and such from the start.so lets keep our cool here, and not go rage inducing at starbreeze for not having everything right here.and too be honest, i feel this might be also a case of a publisher gunpoint at them. i mean, Deep Silver helped publish this game; and were the same publishers that force the direction of the reboot Saints Row game, yes the that bad one. and the same ones who put alot games that weren't ment to be Epic Games Exclusives too. so dont try and be all pointing guns at starbreeze, when even they themselves might be have a publisher point a gun at them.so do keep in mind here, Payday 3 right now is the start, not the finish line.so other than that, lets get started with pros.THE PROS:- Gameplay is smooth and rich as ever.the gun-play is a step above payday 2 in everyway! and its movement too!with vaulting being moving and pressing jump when near a ledge or small wall or window; or heck even a vent! its well rounded and very nice! the whole game feels a step ahead with the new engine, and its new features as well.- it's combat is Hard, challenging and thrilling.( Can be taken as either positive or negative depending on view. )its more tactical and harder than payday 2, making PD3 normal feel like PD2 very Hard. cops are tough but still vulnerable, specials have been tweaked and changed to be both vulnerable and more dangerous too (especialy cloakers and dozers being realy scary now!). Dificulty scaling is now based on Damage and Aim, and not Health. after all, cops are now more like what they should be, tough on bodyshots weak on headshots. but not overbearingly tough like PD2's cops on high dificulties.The Cops are now designed with reason behind, with some specials having weaknesses besides headshots; shields are not a wide cover, and their front peice can be shartered to headshot him. Zappers have their battery box to shoot to stun him and other cops around him. Grenadiers have the grenades on their front peice and can be shot to explode. Claokers are more agile, quicker, but dont mean an insta-down if taken care of. and Bull-dozers put the fear of god back in you, with their charge, and Auto-shotgun these guys dont play around at all .So if people complain that "Cops are too bullet Spongy" then thats a skill issue.- Stealth is 100% improvement from before!its better, it has more improvements and options. and if stealth fails, it transistions to loud with no issues, and its very seamless too.The Stealth in this game is so good, that payday 2 stealth i cant go back too after playing it. its thrilling, redesigned to be more grounded and more balanced. the stealth shows how much they wanted to inprove on what pd2 was lacking for a long long time. one issue with it, a minor one but can be serious at times, i wish there more rewards for going all stealth on heists.but lets get to the nitty gritty with stealth on how much is improved.Stealth, at a base level is now universal, no more detection risk, and do just as much in casing mode as masked on.Casing mode is now more redefined and way better! heck you can just have one with a mask and another without and complete a stealth with no issues. you can do alot more in casing mode too; lockpick stuff, sneaking around, hacking cameras and interacting with stuff. a way better improvement!if your caught in casing mode, its not a immediate game over and mask on; gaurds are now gaurds, and will escort you out of private areas. only on secure areas were they will cuff you, and even then its not a full blown out of luck if you have the perk to uncuff yourself, or have a teammate to uncuff you.Pagers are now alot better and if lose your last pager, its not an immediate alarm, it will go into search mode, wich then if you answer a pager while on search, it will lead into alarm.Plus! you can build yourself for both loud and stealth and can switch or cross over when needed. or just go all stealth and have no issues.even if theres a few points for pros, dosent mean everything else is bad. far from it.but now we got to talk about the cons.THE CONS:- Online Only;not the worst thing, and besides in many of dev streams after release they did mention about adding it in. the reason i believe had to do with either their response about cheaters, or just the publisher deep silver being a pain and forcing them.still this was mainly complained because of server issues at launch, which for the most part are now fixed.- Exp and Leveling.its not the worst, but it can be a pain. plus this whole challenges progression was also in Payday the heist. but even then, i would love to have a dual system of just gameplay progress with the challenges to help earn specifics or just have better rewards attached to them.THE REVEIWS : yes im making a section about the reveiws, you'll understand.alot of people mainly position themselves with the reviews on alot of launch issues (which yes is important, but also not pernament and lasted about a week with the server issue), as well as people complaining about the perks being weaker and less interesting than pd2.- with perks i sorta understand, but at the same time; i played game like borderlands 2 and warframe with better customization and abilities than PD2 with warframe being a bit more complicated.i mean, think about it, you have a perk deck that determines a way to play (with none even primarly built for stealth by the way), and skills to be built around it.in PD3, its more condense and more design for gameplay choices, than a whole build just to do even  stealth normaly. plus, this is the start of PD3 with more perks coming in the future, so there will be more to choose.- Not enough 'this' or 'that'.alot of complaints about that for a game that took a good while to make, redefined and all; and they expect to have alot of content at the start, even though this is a slow cook, not a one and done meal. To be honest, i dont mind what we got right now. and i know there will be more to come soon.CLOSING STATEMENT :so for all of you who read my review, or just skiped all of what ive said to this part, then let me say this."Payday 3, is a Diamond in the Rough"its not bad, its very fun, and theres a couple of issues.nothing more or less. and i think it will go far, as long as others gives it a fair chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, yet I can't contest that all the negative reviews are very well deserved. The gameplay is very solid and genuinely fun, but, sadly, the game is plagued by weird decisions like:THE CRITICAL ONES- always online, so if you don't have a connection, can't play- waiting for matchmaking even when playing solo and closed lobbies, which means that if servers are down, can't play- lobbies are not hosted by a player, meaning you can lag even when creating a lobby or playing solo. You can even disconnect from a lobby and lose progress of a solo match you were inTHE NOT SO CRITICAL ONES- infamy (exp) feels very weird since it is directly tied to niche "achievements" and so if you don't do any of them in a heist, you only get money and no exp, meaning no new unlocks like weapons, masks, etc- some weapon mods need outrageous grinding to unlock, while other weapons can unlock all mods rather quickly and don't feel grindy at all- loud and stealth were meant to be non-binary, still are. The ideia was so that you could start a heist in stealth and if something went wrong, the team could just finish it in loud without any problems; yet there are perks that are clearly exclusive to stealth and others to loud, which means the ideal method STILL IS to have a dedicated stealth loadout, which is bad at loud, consequently not being able to finish the heist if it goes loud and just having to restart like in PD2This game deserves so much more, and I don't mean the reviews, people are right about the game's issues; I mean that the franchise, the gameplay, are SO MUCH FUN but decisions outside of the game's concept really bring it down.Oh yeah, I forgot to mention: my PC is garbage and the game still runs very well. :)

_childDocuments_.review: (I'm writing this review because I've been sitting in matchmaking for the last 40 minutes with no end in sight.)The launch of this game is absolutely horrible.Here's a short list of grievances on the matchmaking and servers alone:Non-matchmaking/server related thoughts:Guns have to be leveled up if you want to equip them with mods. Fair enough if you enjoy progression. Making any random build with any gun you fancy like PD2 is no longer an option, however. You're stuck using weapons that don't feel very good until you're skilled and modded.Progression is annoying. It's locked to challenges, presumably because their design philosophy is that players should be forced to try everything. I can get behind that, but I already tried all of the weapons in PD2 because I WANTED to try them all and come up with builds for them, not because I was forced to if I wanted EXP. You don't get EXP for heists - only challenges, ie. kill X number of enemies while ADS.Graphics are decent. Better than Payday 2, but I would hope they're better than a 10 year old game. Faces are kind of bad, but I can excuse them as this isn't a face-to-face conversation-based game. Visually they went for a PDTH-look with its lighting and aesthetics.UI is horrid. Mobile game simplicity to a fault. I have no idea what anything does because it's all vague stat bars and descriptions. It's essentially year 1 Payday 2 where you have to wait for dedicated spreadsheet makers to come to the rescue. Modding and cosmetics all require lots and lots of submenu-ing and tabs. Menus shouldn't have a learning curve.Performance is OK. I've turned my game down to Medium because exploding cartoon barrels lock up the game for a second otherwise.That said, conceptually the skill system is decent. I'm already enjoying theory-crafting wacky skill builds.Gameplay is fun enough, but I lament the loss of PD2's one-man-army style. PD3 is more PDTH in sticking together + splitting up roles when necessary. Loud feels a tad clunky in controls (at least until I get QoL skills). Sliding when you crouch while running is incredibly annoying and will get you killed on roofs.Stealth is where the big changes are. This is a massive improvement to PD2. You are "rewarded" for learning stealth and having a crew splitting up. However, thanks to the progression system being tied to challenges, you are not actually rewarded anything besides equipped weapon exp.Truthfully, I enjoy the game just enough that I'll stick around and hope this improves, but this reeks of corporate nonsense. If you're on the fence, wait a few months for sales and improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs down with some caveats. The gameplay itself is nice! The new stuff like vaulting, the new stealth system, lockpicking, all that stuff is great. I like the maps. The graphics and music are nicely updated.But the stuff outside the actual moment to moment gameplay of heisting is where my eyebrow raises a bit. The menus/UI outside of the matches is pretty bad, it feels like a placeholder in a beta. Weapons not being separated by primary/secondary, no ability to sell weapons, etc. These features seem obvious and they are a clear step down from what Payday 2 already has done for years and years.The leveling system is an issue. You don't get XP for doing heists anymore but instead have to do challenges. You get some of them done without trying early on but once you hit level 15 or so, it starts to really slow down. You have to go out of your way to do these challenges instead of just focusing on the core of the game - the heist. These challenges should be bonuses, not THE ONLY WAY TO LEVEL.Obviously the online-only stuff is a real problem right now because of the server overload but I'm not counting that itself as a knock against it or part of the thumbs-down. Obviously this will be fixed in time, but right now people are trying to get into a game that I'm not sure feels like it was ready to come out.These are all fixable issues. Payday 3 could be a fantastic game and a great sequel to 2, but right now it has some kinks to work out. The UI and progression desperately need an overhaul and I hope it happens fast.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who has been playing PAYDAY for over 9 years and has 1500+ hours of playtime across all games in the series, the third installment in the franchise certainly feels like an interesting experience.To begin with, it definitely feels more like a sequel to PAYDAY: The Heist both in terms of its groundedness and grittiness, it is certainly not over the top with absurdity like its predecessor, PAYDAY 2. I say it with a good heart though, PAYDAY 2 is hands down one of the funniest games in existence.However, it is expanded beyond belief with all kinds of enjoyable additions, so let's dive into them.To begin with, the graphics are gorgeous; the Unreal Engine is refreshingly smooth. I was genuinely awestruck just strolling through the lobby of the Gold & Sharke bank, or looking at the golden sun rays permeating the penthouse on the Touch The Sky heist. Or the noir-ish overcast & foggy Ashton Fine jewelry store... sheesh! The game is aesthetically delightful! Each heist feels like a Hollywood movie scene complete with tiny details such as cars driving around with music blasting out of them, civilians engaging in small talk, and guards buying soda midway through their patrol route. When you look at, say, the jewelry store or the nightclub from PAYDAY 2, it's just laughable compared to this game, looks more like fan-made heists. The level design of this game and the prequel are literally as contrasting as night and day. Additionally, a lot of the heists do not even conceal the fact that they are recycled from the prequels. The aforementioned Gold & Sharke is clearly a rendition of the Big Bank, the Under the Surphaze and Touch the Sky heists are visible homages to the first and third days of the Framing Frame job, respectively, etc. And what do I think about it? It's brilliant! They took the classics that stood the time test and put an AAA+-type quality spin on them. Just playing these new heists once will make you want to stay in them. They are not copies; they are mature and fully fresh spiritual successors to their predecessors, and I'm all here for it.Speaking of the gameplay itself, the stealth has certainly had the most notable glowup. The best stealth heist in PAYDAY 2 was arguably Framing Frame Day 3, the penthouse infiltration where teamwork, finesse, and coordination meant everything to your success. Even the bag moving part was made so tastefully that you enjoyed it. Now take that heist, add advanced non-linear objectives and device hacking, reworked casing mode which sometimes allows you to complete the entire heist without even masking up, and the Search Mode which forgives some of your mistakes in stealth instead of immediately calling an army on you, and extrapolate it on every other heist with even more cool additions for you to explore! There are, however, two HUGE issues with stealth. First, a fixed RNG seed which does NOT reset after you restart the heist. It means that upon restart you can bypass many if not most objectives of the mission, which trivializes the game beyond reason and is honestly straight-up cheating. Example: on the first bank heist (NRFTW) you can find the code to the vault on attempt A, and upon restart on attempt B go to it and open it without ever bringing the manager to the biometrics scanner, which is required by the game by default and is the most difficult objective of the mission. Second, online only. Once I was stealthing the Gold & Sharke bank for nearly 3 hours, and just as I was about to toss the last bag into the van and escape, I disconnected from the server. Enough said. Now with the gunplay come a few issues. The gunplay is gorgeous and truly feels like a Hollywood Shootout. In the midst of combat it sometimes feels like I'm playing Battlefield or Call Of Duty, especially with the stunning visual effects blasting on the screen. But at the same time, it really feels like most maps available at launch clearly favor silent gameplay rather than loud gunplay, both in terms of the maps' not-so-big scale, and objectives, which not always, but sometimes turn from dynamic and engaging to the more classic ones such as «wait for the drill/helicopter» and/or «move the bags».It seems that the game at its current state simply cannot showcase all its newfound gun-blazing glory due to, quite simply, lack of heists.Repeating myself, many maps feel claustrophobic and geared towards stealth. When you infiltrate, say, the Neon Cradle nightclub, the objectives are very dynamic and are NOT all about loot moving or vault drilling. But, as soon as the alarm goes, you suddenly find yourself tossing many bags around while engaging in primarily close-quarter combat. Don't get me wrong, I have certainly enjoyed it, but when 6/8 heists are focused mostly or solely on it, it gets old quickly. Had you given me my full-auto Saiga from PAYDAY 2, however... The game DESPERATELY needs heists a-la the community-certified bangers Hoxton Breakout, Rats, and Hotline Miami, where dynamic shootouts across all ranges take up most of your playtime and the objectives are both challenging and dynamic, not boring and timer-oriented. Developers did a good job with it on heists like Road Rage, which has been reminiscent of both the Hoxton Breakout and Green Bridge heists, but it needs SCALE, FUN, and EXPLOSIONS. A bomber helicopter appearing out of nowhere, a cussing Russian commissar, or blowing up a whole petrol station, that's the sexy stuff we want, you feel me? I'll say a few words about the unfortunate launch, too. Not talk down on the company, everyone is fed up with that already anyway, but speak from the perspective of a long-standing PAYDAY fan. I knew exactly what PAYDAY was, so by all means was I not surprised by this launch. The people in charge of the company are known for making unreasonable, greed-driven decisions in the past (isn't it ironic that a greedy company made a game about giving in to your greed?), but they are also known as one of the most attentive creators in the industry who always consider the needs of the community and successfully implement them into the games. Don't hate on the developers though, they have clearly poured their heart into the game.At its core, it's a masterpiece game with tremendous potential, but most importantly, it's the PAYDAY we all know and love with a new exciting spin put on it. I'm certain that all of the bad marketing decisions were made by the corporate bosses who are eager to line up their own pockets and perhaps save the company from bankruptcy which was impending not that long ago. But they have to understand that in 10 years the money will be spent and there will come a time to make PAYDAY 4. However, people will only want to play it if the company works on the longevity of the title and the reputation of caring for its core player base. Is the game half-baked? Not at all. Here and there there are mistakes, sure, but without a lengthy beta test, it's impossible to reveal them all. PAYDAY 2 at launch didn't have more than 85% of the content it has today. Literally. I counted. That's kind of the premise of the title: the game expands drastically with time to keep it fresh and relevant for new and experienced players alike. Realistically, you can expect the game to be fully playable in mid or late 2024 when more updates come unless they make even more detrimental decisions (micro-transactions, I'm looking at you). Would the game have come out better 6-12 months later? Perhaps, with fewer bugs and a bit more content, but I'm sure that the core decisions such as online-only would have been made, regardless. Now they have a clear-cut community reaction and conclusions to draw from it. A vivid case study. So let's hope they'll make the right decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a great game under all the trash systems surrounding it, which is a shame - this is the third COOP horde shooter in a while (Back 4 Blood, Darktide, and now Payday 3) where this is true. Companies need to really start respecting the time of people who play their game - especially in these COOP games - there's no incentive to play on a harder difficulty, rather - you must only farm kills on loud heists with all the guns (1000 with each!) to fill arbitrary challenges. The stealth which is genuinely really fun is pointless, and I groan every time my team feels like doing stealth. Loud feels alright, but it's still just payday gameplay, and with the really slow levelling system for guns (I have no idea why the gun experience is so slow, I've barely maxed out two primaries - the DMR and the AK, and each primary has a different max level.) - the overall levels don't function either, another attempt by Overkill to try to dissuade people from spamming the most efficient heist.. yet we're at that with the forced loud heist being the most played one.C-Stacks are also just awful - the final attachments in categories cost 50 of these things, and to get a decent amount, you need to essentially pay up in what is an exponential scheme - where it resets per week, limiting what you can buy. This then extends to weapon/mask/suit/glove slots, where you'll eventually need C-Stacks to buy more of them for whatever purpose. This currency should genuinely ♥♥♥♥ off and be useful only for cosmetics.Preset weapons are completely worthless, namely due to their price - they were toted as a way to gain experience on a gun that you might not even have yet, but they cost far too much to use, and since you can't modify them - you're likely going to have to get used to a weapon's ironsights. Speaking of ironsights - attachments all have a downside, including scopes, so you cannot just use what you like the look of, it might just reduce your weapon spread, sprint to fire speed, or targeting speed. Attachments are very vague, and stats are displayed in bars once again - a mistake echoed from Payday 2's launch, and from Darktide recently.Ultimately, a good game - but held under layers of filth from bad decisions.PS, bring back the server browser/remove online only requirements.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get too caught up in the mixed to negative reviews this game has. Almost all of the people who are writing negative reviews are about how the online component is somewhat questionable. In my personal experience from playing the Early Access I haven't had that much difficulty nor have I had any particular problems from a connection stand-point, but I can easily understand why people would be down on it, since not everyone has perfectly stable net. If nothing else at least the game is pretty lax with reconnecting to people and drop-in, drop-out lobbies tend to function well enough to where the game retains all of what you were doing prior to the crash so there's no real issues with that. Outside of the online component which is definitely the biggest sore spot for a few reasons (Although PD2's online component wasn't any better, since that game's netcode was the equivalent to a pack of popsicle sticks taped together to resemble a proper server), the other major complaint have is with the Challenges. I'm going to go out on a limb and say that most people who are complaining about them, didn't actually do too much reading into what these challenges entail to begin with. It's true there's a lot of challenges that are repeat X, but for the most part challenges just reward you for interacting with all of the game's systems in meaningful ways. Blow up Nader belts, Blow up Zapper Bats, Trade hostages, Kill Dozers, Use Bodyshields, as well as a bunch of generic kill with X weapon challenges and heist difficulty completion challenges. Overall, nothing particularly brutal, and is definitely not as grindy as people are suggesting, especially when you take into consideration that you'll have a good chunk of the important stuff by around level 30-40 which you can get to in about 10-15 hours, which is roughly just playing all of the heists at least twice.There are also a lot of complaints about UI, which I think are mostly legitimate. The Menu UI and especially the Lobby UI/UX is just horrible. You can't buy guns from the loadout screen, you can't chat in lobbies, you can't keep playing with the same people in the same lobby post-heist completion, you can't buy assets from the lobby, but instead have to buy them individually (Without a slider!) from the shop. It's just a bunch of small weird ass problems that definitely need to be patched up in the future. But outside of what might seem like a gargantuan amount of issues, the truth is PD3 is actually a fantastic step up from the previous entries in basically every way that matters. A lot of people say the skill trees are bad. Those people are wrong and are probably pissy that they got rid of comedic crutch skills like Inspire and Swan Song from PD2. PD3's skill system is vastly more robust than PD2's and the actual skills on a one - to - one basis are way more significant than any individual skill was in PD2. Y'see, PD2's skills actually had this quirky little issue where most of them were actually just borderline filler you'll never feel in an actual game, and some of them were proper skills that actually gave tangible effects. You never make a build without skills that give tangible effects. So in PD3, they just got rid of the pointless skills that did next to nothing, and it's all just stuff that does tangible things. Skills from all sorts, Retrive thrown daggers and daggers can ricochet, killing enemies in close proximity grants buffs, Marking targets for a significant amount of time and dealing/taking more/less damage, Grenades strip armor, Throwing SWAT units from a bodyshield lights a smoke grenade in their place and many, many more countless examples (And only in Loud!) exist for the skills. No Fat, all Substance.Everything about this game is All substance, No fat. The heists are the most packed with variety they've ever been. Objectives are varied and interesting, and though they use the wi-fi hotspot gimmick a few too many times for my tastes, it's still infinitely more interesting than waiting for a drill for 3 minutes (That's on Harvest and trustees' by the way, the first heist in PD2!). The Objectives are interesting, and the story development and concept for a storyline in Payday is absolutely what people have wanted for years. Ultimately PD3 is a good game on release, that's only going to get better with time. Just how PD2 aged like fine wine from it's pathetic start, I have no doubt in my mind PD3 is going to blossom into another 10 year stretch of non-stop content and seasonal events, purely on how good the existing basis already is compared to it's predecessors.

There's a solid foundation for things to come. It really is a "less chaotic" Payday 2 that seems to return to a more "grounded" Payday:The Heist style of gameplay.What have they done to the characters ? I never thought I'd miss the live action from the second game this much (I laughed when I saw ). And I hope we'll get to reunite the whole gang. The "cutscenes" aren't very convincing. Something feels off with the tone of the Payday 3 world. But as far as I'm concerned story-wise, to each their own. Basic ennemies in loud are maybe a bit bullet-spongey... Or it's just that weapons feel weak.Why is this coop shooter seems to go out of its way to prevent me from having a good experience in coop ? Why can't I group up with random and stay with them and bond over mutliple heists like in 2013 ? Why are C-stack this dumb ? (if it's not to prepare the audience for actual mtx)Always Online my ass !  MatchMaking is working, I still have to wait at least 60-120 seconds to get my PRIVATE game started...  Why no lobby ? Why no real solo play like the tutorial missions ??  The controls are fine but a bit weird - maybe it's the ten years of Payday 2 that refuse to let go. Why do hostages become invincible when rescued by the cops ? If I shoot near a civ, they should get their face on the ground. Why so much elements (features, QoL, mechanics) are missing ?  We're not talking number of heists or weapons, etc. but missing lobbies, good matchmaking, grouping up with folks, , a safehouse,  skippable heists intros, pregame lobby chat, a better UI (currently the worst of the year personnally), working online services, body bags, a real XP system (not this Halo Infinite challenge type of garbage..), getting  the van, no melee weapons, no akimbo... Why after multiple years of work, and constant betterment of Payday 2, do I feel like this is a new IP from a new studio ? I get that it is a new game alright, but it never felt like the third installment of a series that's been there for this long. It doesn't seem to build up from Payday 2.To add to his list, why the ♥♥♥♥ did you replace xp with challenges ? That killed it more for me than the atrocious "will never be down" servers. And why do the weapons feel worse than PayDay2...The launch should serve as a warning to Starbreeze. You should not make an online only game if this is the quality of your service. It was the same with Payday 2 and constant disconnects. We can only hope that the "We're listening to the feedback of the community" shtick is at least partially true, because people only want a better Payday 2 and this ain't it for now.UPDATE : It's still a complete mess. The only non downside is the heist Boys in Blue which isn't a total failure. Weapons are still some of the dullest feeling while shooting, maybe because it takes two/three headshots to reliably kill stuff...There still ain't no corpse bag, and you still can't throw a body you just let go of it. The dialogues are... abysmal, like the cutscenes. From live-action cutscene (at least for the key parts) in 2 to a slideshow. It's appalling. I'm beginning to wonder what they didn't do with AI, the more you look at it, the more something feels really off.Each character design is so far behind its PD2 counterpart it's not even funny. Still getting random micro stutters, some freezes, and even got an "out of memory" error while the game is running fine otherwise..For some reason I still can't unready in lobby. Guards will or won't see a corpse through walls, they will or won't do their job and patrol, civs will or won't tie up, doors will or won't get lockpicked... _childDocuments_.review: **Update 11/5/24**Game: 7/10The Good:- Offline mode...........finally-exp system feels pretty great where it is right now, I have been able to get the stuff I wanted without over grinding the game. - 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Dlcs for year 1 are actually pretty fun on both stealth and loud options (4th DLC I believe is only loud)- Some of the DLC weapons are really fun to use in normal gameplay.The Bad:-Skills still need some love after all this time (most are useless and there isn't much in terms of making unique builds)- The new armor system seems overly complicated but we shall see in December- The game could still use some more content, and honestly more free content at that. Hard to say if I will get the next season pass. But payday 2 was the same way for a while. -There is little to no choice for the gear you bring. The med bags and grenade are fine as is, but there isn't really any good options for tools in loud besides the mines but they have little to no effect at higher levels. There needs to be a lot more of these then it will work a lot better.Overall:The game is still coming back with an upward trend but the developers on several occasions have taken user feedback, disregarded it, and implemented more sloppy updates in attempts to make more money. The 1st DLC is a scam, and the devs have even acknowledged this fact. However the rest of the dlc have actually been pretty nice, but the missions are a bit small. Also the devs are working to made the dlcs worth more per dollar as well. The exp system is a lot better than it was and it is slowly starting to feel more like a stable game. It is still a long way from being a FULL game but its getting there. Realistically if all of the dlc current and planned where base game it would be a lot better. Biggest issue right now is that there isnt a lot of content and there isn't a lot of build diversity so every "build" has most of the same perks and weapons because that's just what is available right now. I give it a 7/10 but it still has a long way to go. If the year 1 edition is on sale for about 50% off its probably a decent purchase. Once the skills, guns, and equipment are a bit more diverse the game will be in a good state.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never seen a game fall so flat following in the footsteps of an already established set of ideas and mechanics. After a collective 2,000+ hours playing Payday 2, I was expecting so much more from this game.TL;DR: Payday 3 is a massive downgrade from its predecessor. Many obvious options and features are missing and the missions offer very little in the way of replay value. With the foundation that Payday 2 created, this game should have been an easy home run.- Graphics generally look pretty good.- New stealth mechanics are very welcome.- Performance seems to scale much better than Payday 2 did.- Mechanics like taking human shields and new hostage trading are nice and having armor that doesn't regen is a good idea and provides a welcome challenge.- No option for solo play. You can create a private lobby but you can't play offline or pause the game and there are no QoL options for solo players.- For a multiplayer game, there is a severe lack of features such as lobby chat, the ability to return to lobby after completing a mission and any form of mission preplanning just to name a few.- The included "story" feels like a bad fanfic, with low effort cutscenes included.- Missions offer very little in variations. After you've played a mission once, there seems to be little reason to play again.- Mission objectives make no sense. You'll find yourself running from one end of the map to the other multiple times in a heist because your new handler, Shade (replacing Bain), is apparently so incompetent at planning heists that she can't plan for things like bag drops or pick ups before the very second you need them.- Neat details like live action background footage for heist info screens have been replaced by a cheap menu featuring a static image of your contract broker. You also can no longer see the physical armor the characters are wearing. We should be playing in an era that allows you to not only see armor on a player, but also their deployables, holstered weapons, objective items, etc.- Enemies are bullet sponges on every difficulty. I was really hoping this would finally be the game that steers Payday in a more tactical direction. The guns feel very weightless and pack little punch. Even a shotgun will take 2 to 3 shots to dispatch a standard enemy on normal difficulty. I think that less enemies, higher damage for both sides and smarter ai would have benefited the game tremendously; especially with some of the added features like human shields and better hostage trading.- The new perk system is terrible. Everything revolves around these three mechanics, "Rush, Edge and Grit" and seem to make very little difference on actual gameplay. The game also doesn't really explain how you obtain new skill points or how to unlock later skills in the tree after researching the initial starting skill.- The progression is terrible. I know they're planning on changing this soon but as it stands, having to complete challenges to gain levels is an awful idea. It forces you to play the game in a way you may not want to just to gain an extra level.- The UI is hideous. Every menu is plagued with massive boxes taking up way too much room and is just really ugly to look at. Also the ability to rename loadouts and weapons is entirely absent, making it difficult to remember which loadout is which.Ultimately this game is a massive disappointment. It feels extremely soulless compared to Payday 2 and offers very little reasons to play. Hopefully in time it will find its true identity and provide a fun and rewarding experience. As it stands, it's just a downgrade from Payday 2 in almost every way.
_childDocuments_.name: PAYDAY 3

_childDocuments_.review: Now that server issues are starting clear up, people are finally able to play the game and judge it for what it is. As of now, the view on the game is poor, and I seriously don't think it's fair.In many ways, the game is a huge step up from Payday 2. During the server's downtime, I went back to Payday 2, it felt absolutely horrible. I never realized how poor the movement and some of the mechanics are, but Payday 3 seriously feels amazing to play. The gunplay is a huge step up along with the movement changes, but I don't think people argue against this as it seems to be a common conception.Where this game gets really divisive is when it comes to progression and skills. Most people I see talk about the skills system talk about it in a negative way, stating that it's a step down from Payday 2 and are uninteresting. But I really couldn't be more against that. Sure, they got rid of dodge, but in Payday 2, dodge felt like it was the only way to play the game loud other than Kingpin or Anarchist. There were only 3 viable builds on DSOD, the hardest difficulty, and there were really no variation in builds. I, for one, couldn't wait until they removed dodge with Payday 3 because of how much it felt like the only option and how RNG reliant it was. With Payday 3, while we are still early in the game and metas aren't yet built, it does feel like there is more room to make a build you are comfortable with. Whether that be infinite ammo DB shotgun, a smoke spamming support, hostage taker, human shield connoisseur, hell even turrets are good, these builds all work on Overkill difficulty. Right now, the only true meta I feel exists is the armor meta, as there is no way to get armor other than using bags which means it is sort of the only deployable worth bringing.The progression is even more hated however, with many a person finding it to be the worst part of the game, going as far to leave a negative review and refund. Is it a step down from Payday 2's progression? No, IMHO. Does it need to be adjusted, yes but only slightly. The only way to get XP as of now is from completing challenges, which can range from getting kills with a specific weapon or completing a heist X amount of times. As of writing this review, challenges are bugged and about 20% of them are locked, not able to be completed, as far as I know. In Payday 2, leveling up was essentially spamming Hoxton Breakout, Crime Spree, or Holdout. I know for me, I reached max level before I even touched some of the maps that I assumed were more difficult like Big Oil. What they are doing now in Payday 3 is to have your level reflect how much of the game you've actually experienced, meaning in order to reach max level you must play every map, in both stealth and loud. You must experience multiple ways to play the game, like using human shields or different deployables. All of this, I see as a good change, forcing me to actually play and understand stealth, instead of just ignoring a whole different way of playing the game. Once challenges can be filtered better and the locked ones are fixed, I think it'll become way easier to understand the direction they were going for and maybe you'll start enjoying it.The biggest flaw of the game in my opinion is the lack of QoL features that were in Payday 2. Biggest of all being  and being able to know what tactic your lobby is planning on using. When I'm not playing with friends, I'm playing with randoms rather than these awful bots; and too many times have I joined in hopes of playing loud but we end up stealthing the map and I am forced to walk on eggshells with my loud gear and unsuppressed weapon. Unreadying in the lobby is still not a thing but will hopefully come in the next update, which really isn't something that should ever be said for something as simple as an unready button. Quick play also should've been a thing on launch and there's no excuse for why it isn't. Lasers, jukebox, lobby chat, preplanning, persistent lobbies, and muting heist briefs are all something so small that really should've been a thing on launch. Offline mode is something that they are looking into but even if it doesn't come, I do hope the recent server instability will cause them to put more effort in keeping servers stable.With how much fun I've been having, I'd say the game is worth the $40 and I know it'll only get better from here on out.

_childDocuments_.review: At time of writing, I have a hard time recommending this game. The game uses online servers only, so you can't just make a lobby with friends and play. You have to make a party with friends, queue for a heist, wait for matchmaking to find a room (Even if you have a full party, or if you're solo), then you can play.This is truly a terrible setup for Payday 3, after Payday 2 had everything set up just fine. No private p2p hosting, just the online servers. In 2023, there's absolutely no reason a game can't have those as an option.As far as gameplay goes, it's more payday 3. Pretty much all the good fun you expect from a payday game. The content does feel rather thin, but there's enough things there to keep you busy for a while.TL;DR: The gameplay is solid and still fun - more Payday. Can't use p2p servers to run your own games with friends, or even AI. Can't play offline solo must always connect to an online room. Come on guys, it's 2023. This is inexcusable.

_childDocuments_.review: Here are the big things:-MATCHMAKING IS TERRIBLE -Graphics are good-Gun play is good-Atmosphere is good-Missions are good-Feels like someone at starbreeze was a big fan of COD-UI is crisp and modern but absolutely terrible to navigate and I personally hate it with every fiber of my being  -Weapons level up in order to get attachments-There are no lobbies, just matchmaking -No pregame chat to discus a plan before playing-Matchmaking is for specific maps, no random matchmaking (maybe thats not in PD2 either, i cant remember)-Weapon attachments feel mostly useless-Xp is gained through challenge grinding-There is no Xp gained from the map or difficulty you play on at all. (makes grinding levels get old fast, especially since you only have 8 maps to choose from atm) -Always online/Need an account-There is a secondary currency, but it is purchased through in game money and not micro transactions (subsequent purchases of secondary currency increase in price)-No more random loot-Cant purchase weapon mods with the secondary currency-Skills system is a weird merge of Perk Decks and the Skill system from PD2 (its growing on me) -Skills system and game play are insistent on this system of 3 temporary buffs. Most perks are either getting these buffs on a specific action or being able to do something while you have a buff active. _childDocuments_.review: Game is hella fun for like 12 heists, then the lack of content and diversity makes the game feel like a chore.I pretty much did every heist twice, once on stealth and once on loud (there were less than 10 heists, eight in total) which isnt exactly a huge letdown, as we werent exactly promised a huge array of heists to choose from, but about half of the heists are unplayable on stealth mode in solo mode, because you cant take your mask off (this is just a me thing, but i was hoping for an unmasking feature) This isnt a complete deal breaker of course, and this game is worth the 40 dollars i would say, but i also think payday 2 is a more fun experience. You can probably get payday 2 with every dlc for the price of 40 dollars or less, if its on sale. Which is COMPLETELY WORTH IT! Payday 2 was one of the best and most fun games i have ever played, and like all the other reviews are probably saying, this game is currently a straight downgrade. To be completely honest, there isnt a single feature this game has that is actually better than payday 2. You can use hostages as "human shields" which, as far as i can tell, does absolutely nothing. Instead, they just shoot the part of you that isnt covered up by the hostage. Also, you can trade hostages for extra time, and health. The thing is, trading them for time is possibly the stupidest thing ever, because you only get 10 SECONDS of extra time before an assault, which you could instead put towards actually doing the objective and getting way more value out of your time. Being able to trade them for health is fine, i guess. I dont really use it that often because the health packs are tiny and sitting still for the 3 seconds it takes to consume them is probably not worth the damage you are going to take. In conclusion, i cannot reccomend this game to anyone who isnt the very specific type of person who has completely finished every payday 2 heist and finished everything to do in payday 2,  is looking for an extra 8 heists to play, and is willing to pay 40 dollars for a glorified DLC with minimal mechanics added. The mechanics in which, are janky and difficult to figure out.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Saints Row '22 from Deep SilverWith over 2k hours in PD2 and as a diehard fan I was incredibly hyped at launch day but refunded before ever making it into a game after 10 minutes of waiting for the game to be playable. Played again just today on gamepass (so ignore hours)I had been holding out hopes that the game would be worth playing if flawed after offline mode and server browser was added but during 3 hours or so of gameplay I was constantly finding new things about this game that just suck. What hit me first were the technical issues, immediately after loading in I had to downgrade to medium visuals to get an FPS that wouldn't induce eye bleeding on a pretty top notch gaming PC, I walked into a bank and shot a camera only for the game to lag out, repeated 3 times with the same results and was able to have the same issues with a grenade tossed in a hallway. Missions were boring and anti-climactic, gunplay was unsatisfying with enemies feeling like bulletsponges even on easy mode to the point a pump action shotgun at point blank range wasn't one shotting standard enemies. The menus are hellishly "modern" and pointlessly difficult to navigate. Armor is no longer visible on characters because presumably clothing packs are now a core DLC strategy. The perk trees of 2 are gone replaced with generic perk decks that do little to mix up gameplay or provide for fun variation in play style. By far what was most gutwrenching was the gunsmithing, Payday 2 was legendary for the amount of variation and customization you could put into a gun and that's been replaced now with an ultra simplified barebones experience, for example on my shotgun, my revolver, and my AR I have the option of short barrel, long barrel, or "tac" barrel,.. I could go on for hours.It really does feel like Payday 3 was handed off to a completely novice dev team who made a cheap rip off of their own game. Most of the talent at Starbreeze has apparently departed the studio. The top review at time of writing is "let this cook a year" and I have to disagree, and it wouldn't surprise me if around then is when Starbreeze goes the way of Volition and shuts down, which would be just about enough time for them to finish up putting out all the gold edition DLC. I used to think like Darktide this game was a flawed gem that could be shined up, if only they added a few things (and made the game Peer 2 Peer) but now at this point I writing of Payday 3 as another Rockay City. They would have to completely remake this game from the bones up with a pitiful playerbase and furious season pass holders howling over how bad the DLC they're getting is.

_childDocuments_.review: After years of anticipation... Started from PD: The Heist back in the day, played PD2 through its good and bad times... This, as it stands, ain't it my gamer.F*ck man, I used to watch the live action trailers like there was no tomorrow, listen to Criminal Ambitions single when I was in the gym because you felt so bad a*s back before PAYDAY 2 went apesh*t - and we started doing weird, otherworldly stuff for Bain and Yakuza exc exc. Now we got a random chick that replaced Bain - the quality between the two is NOT even up for debate. She sounds robot. Would've expected a better writing and voice acting, as she's probably gonna be the person you hear most during your gameplay.I won't go into technical issues too much for now - as many people already did with their reviews, but I gotta get these off of my chest. Currently matchmaking is F tier with what I assume is the launch day players filling up the servers (got the gold version so was playing it 3 days before, wasn't perfect but wasn't this bad then) which will probably be fixed soon. Still scuffed as f*ck and a massive downgrade from . Or the horrible UI system that is a huge disappointment from everything that PD2 accomplished so far and seems to be designed to actively piss the player off and with more buttons to press to do even the simplest of tasks in the menu. The weapon customisation seems to be (mostly) irrelevant too.The gunfights and skill system took a different direction, it's much less a horde shooter compared to PD2, and more of a calculated tactical shooter that PD: The Heist was. Whether it's good or bad, time will tell, but I'm currently enjoying it, the more I level up, the more stuff makes sense. Although it doesn't have the goofiness and the creativeness of some of the skills and builds that PD2 had, it kinda matches the path they're taking with this PD: The Heistish, more realistic setting. Stealth was drastically improved and I actually want to actively play it. Obviously the game looks better, albeit some performance problems, which again, I'm sure, will be fixed eventually.My real anger and sadness comes from the fact that after years of experience, this game has MANY downgrades in MANY areas compared to PD2. Overkill or Deep Silver - whatever they are now. They have done some f*cked up sh*t in the past that pissed off the community, but this whole launch is again a slap to the face to the veterans. I don't want to speak for everyone here, but I think vets would appreciate what I'm saying right now. I wasn't expecting the huge amount of heists / weapons / content that PD2 had of course, but with the amount of experience they got from fixing and updating the second game for years, I would expect a better polished product. But the overall image they're drawing right now is this was an Early Access / Beta release. The lack of content makes me think the game will be upgraded over the years with paid DLC (OVK being OVK, makes sense).I'm sure someday, this game will be much better, improved, polished and my review will be positive. But for now, as a veteran and a long time supporter of the series and the devs, I can't shake the feeling that I was betrayed by them.
