_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid and was on my way to school in my mom's car, sometimes I would look out of the window and imagine myself running at the car's same speed, jumping, wall-running, and sliding between cars, signs, and buildings. Well, this game fulfilled that fantasy. I love the concept, the graphics, the speed. That feeling of accomplishment when you die repeatedly and finally figure out the correct approach to a map. The game has potential. However, it is lacking in multiple aspects.First, as you would expect, the pvp player base is small. Sometimes, you would jump into a game with only one more player. It is understandable, however. The game is new and needs some polishing, which I will get into later. Personally, I don't care. I like PvP games, but what I really like is the PvE mode. The challenges are fun. Time limits, jumping through rings, collecting speed boosts. There is a decent variety, but the number is limited. As of now, there are only 33 challenges. Each one should take 5 to 10 tries, depending on your skill. Next is the loading time. It is alright for PvP but for PvE, where you will be restarting over and over again, it gets annoying. Imagine you start running, and after three seconds, you make the wrong jump and die. You could keep going, but you know you lost precious seconds and won't finish the challenge on time, so you restart. That's 8 seconds of loading, plus another 6 seconds of unskippable cinematic, and that's not even counting the countdown to start the race. Then you die again 4 seconds after restarting. You get the point.Finally is the game personality. Maps look similar to me, except for different neon colors. Each one should have more distinctive elements so you can easily identify them. It's the same for the runners—limited customization in the form of recolors. I want to make my runner look different from everyone else. I wanna play, see my runner and think, “Yeah, that's how I would dress if I were competing”. The feeling I get right now when I look at my runner is that it looks like an NPC. If the developers address my previous points, i think the game would be slightly better. HOWEVER, if there is something I think would make the game 10 times better is A MAP DESIGN TOOL. I just can't stop thinking how cool it would be to create my tracks and test them, try other players' creations, try to beat their scores, come up with silly track ideas, cool tracks, tracks that are challenging, tracks that require you to be slow to be precise, tracks that play themselves just by accelerating (kinda like Happy Wheels where you just start a map and enjoy the show the creator made for you). If this is implemented, the game would get so much replayability. Devs, even if your focus is the PvP, I think you would get a bigger player base by doing this. I want to see this game succeed, i really do. It has potential, so I hope the developers listen to the feedback.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tricky game to recommend. I like it a lot, and I think it's really something special. It feels like an Xbox 360 game you'd take a chance on at Blockbuster and be pleasantly surprised with. The core gameplay is very rewarding and fun, and gives you an intense sense of speed. The game's theme is cool, even if I don't really think it works well in this genre. The graphics are also very impressive, even if I can't personally appreciate them since I'm on Deck and need to run everything at low quality. That said, there's a lot of small issues that bog the overall experience down for me. Looks like the devs introduced an offline mode, which is excellent!The content for this game is really lacking. I'm not holding it against the game too much as it just released, but there's only a handful of tracks and the PvE mode leaves me wanting more. The various modes are fun and difficult (as you'd expect if you've played a Sonic racing game), but there's only 9 missions. There are 4 mission types, and each have 3-5 tracks, all laid out in a basic menu. The race start and finish times are far, FAR too long. There's been a few times that the races themselves are quicker than the load times before and after it. I also find it frustrating that when I play PvE, I can't quickly restart when I'm in a race. For a game that scratches the gotta go fast itch, it enjoys making you wait.I mentioned this in the beginning of my review, but I personally don't think this theme really works in the arcade racing genre. It looks cool visually, but tracks all have the same feel and a similar style, and it's very hard to tell them apart. The characters are also a little bland. I like playing racing games that have characters with personalities and different stats, but with Deathsprint 66 I find the characters uninteresting and boring. A majority of the character unlocks are recolors, or maybe a helmet here and there. There's no real customization aside from cosmetics.Lastly, there's some general jank to the game. There's a lot of annoying checkpoints that will spawn you directly in front of an obstacle (or even off the map) and not being able to see your boost meter for a few seconds after respawning is a minor gripe I have. Some rails don't let you lean if you don't jump onto them, causing you to get hit by a grinder. I also find obstacles, powerups and the time rings sometimes blend into the stage and are difficult to spot. I think a lot of this stuff will get fixed eventually, but for now it's worth mentioning.

_childDocuments_.review: You were probably drawn to this game if you love games like Extreme G, F-Zero, SSX, Sunset Blvd, Speed Runners, etc.Even though this game has its moments of fun, awesome electronic music, and some cool ideas, I wouldn’t recommend buying it unless there’s a great future update or if you can get it for $9.99 USD or less. I’m surprised there aren’t more negative reviews, as the game seems shallow.To me, this game has major problems.Matches end quickly, and you spend more time waiting for another match to load than playing. By the time I get into the match and start enjoying the race, it’s over. Most races last around 2:20 seconds, and then you wait 4-5 minutes for a new match. I couldn’t find any options to change the race settings meaningfully.The weapons don’t feel satisfying. I’ve never felt excitement over a single kill because the weapons feel bland. I wish they had more interactive elements, like a drone locking in front of another racer and dropping obstacles for enemies to dodge.There’s no time for great comebacks or to be neck and neck with an opponent. The only comeback mechanic is a Mario Kart Bullet Bill type weapon, which when it ends the race is already over.You don’t have time to get to know other players or build rivalries.The characters all look the same, and the tracks are too short and lack distinction. I felt like I’d seen them all after a few plays. Just very boring.The game is beautiful and has potential, but the devs need more imagination. If they don’t fix the lobby wait times and make races longer and more enjoyable, the community will die quickly, leaving this server to be a ghost town.

_childDocuments_.review: There's plenty of potential here but it does feel a bit unfinished.I'm enjoying it for the most part, but there's quite a few things that are stopping me recommending it:It's Mario Kart, in a lot of ways, pity items for being at the back of the pack, start line boost for going at the green light, drift mechanic with a boost for holding it for a while, basically all the items you would expect from it, including the fun killing lightning bolt (EMP) that forces you to be slow, knocks you off traversal elements like walls to your death, and effects everyone.  But if this wants to feel like a game that rewards you for less deaths and good movement through the track, the style just doesn't fit here. It doesn't feel like this was meant to be a party game.Beginnings of races off the line are a mess. Everyone is just bumping into one another and knocking each other around, and the camera doesn't really know what to do with any of it. Even if you're ahead of the pack, the collisions from all other racers will quickly drop you to the back of the pack, and most of the time, I can't even see what is hitting me. A solid animation for a shove that's obvious would at least help with clarity. Perhaps having an automatic mag shield for all players at the very beginning might resolve that, just until the pack starts to break up.Mines are expected to be jumpable. It feels like a gamble doing so, as it looks like you cleared it, but you explode. Jumping a lot earlier than you think is required seems to get around that, but watching bots jumping them, they jump right before and are fine. I just chalk this up to a bit of lag.Drifting doesn't feel good, feels like you lost all speed, and the boost you get seems to be a bit random, based on speed and angle and you don't get it as often as you'd expect. Seems boosting into a drift and getting a harder angle is better, but it just feels kind of bad overall.Fame feels random, I can go through a track without a death, and come in first, but I get more fame in runs where I get absolutely murdered.restarting PVE takes way too long with an unskippable cutscene, and the same 2 or 3 voice lines from the announcer, which is just grating on a difficult track you might be grinding out. I'm not certain there are rewards for PVE either, but I could be wrong on that.It looks like hitting faster speeds gets the game running into performance issues, a lot of stuttering and lost frames, and considering the speed being a big part, that really has to be resolved.Matchmaking also seems to take a long time, and an option to ready up to go to the next race if all players are ready, would be nice to avoid the 40 second wait to get to the next one. It doesn't sound long, but when you're waiting for something, you feel it a lot more. This does not include the additional 30-40 second it takes for the level to load and connect the players up. The bots you get paired with are braindead. They will repeatedly run into the exact same gauntlet of traps in a straight line, and only just make it on pure luck. I just got done playing and I genuinely watched one stop, turn to the side, run into the side of the barrier and just jump to its death. I guess the timer counting down to its head exploding was too much to deal with.Stage hazards are good for the most part, they feel avoidable and fair, and you benefit from knowing the track. But some are a genuine gamble. You took the wrong rail at the wrong time, or there was a trap that was right around a corner that you can't really be expected to see. Traps are fine, but placement really could do with some work. Making them stand out would be huge, as there's a lot of sections of red, with red traps in them like lazers, saws, swinging logs of spikes, and mines that players can drop (Or just appear on the track) that are also red. some colour change really would improve visibility.Finally, customisation unlocks are just a bit lacklustre. Most of the colours I get are similar in pretty ugly schemes, banners are fine, the emotes feel like an afterthought that I can't see anyone really caring much about at any point. I'm at level 10-15 for each of the experience bars for reference, and each level tends to give something. I've got 2 skins I like out of about 10.I'm not recommending you pick his up right now, not for £20, but I am recommending you keep an eye on it for improvements. I'll be happy to change this to positive if these things can be looked into.

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't say enough good things about this game. _childDocuments_.review: Ima leave this review earlier than I usually do.SURGE SURGE SURGE, learning when to surge(boost) to get optimal speed is fun, You basically have to be surging constantly if you are playing correctly. My favourite mode is where the rings, where your head explode if the time runs out. The game is very pretty. And you can get pretty good with it.This game has a very good price. The controls are so responsive, its crazy. Every few minutes I figure out what I'm supposed to be doing to go even faster.I started off running then trying to make the turns like a car, then you press surge at weird times. The I realized the max speed is not something you can easily hit outside of the surge gamemode, if there even is a max speed. So basically keep using your surge , and keep one in the tank for if you die so you can get up to speed quick.Then you start drifting around the corners like a madman. And pressing surge while drifting to build up a boost and surge at the same time. You get really quick. And its very fun. My concerns/gripes currently are:The bloodbath maps al took me like 1 maybe 2 tries each cause the AI ends up dying alot and they don't dodge buzz saws. The difficulty is a little weird cause the ring maps are fun and  hard and you basically have to learn an optimal route to even be able to beat it compared to bloodbath where you just dodge a few saws.The announcer says speed is the name of the game here folks in the surge gamemode but don't listen to him that is a lie. The objective is to go as slow as possible still beating the buzzer but picking up as much of the surge as possible(the little lightning). Wish there was just a time trial gamemode cause not one of the gamemodes allows you to go as fast as possible.Bloodbath has bots that basically makes the starts feel random and you often die right on start, the rings have you going out of your way to pick up rings and the surge gamemode has you picking up surge. There is no gamemode that lets me get a faster and faster time. And the medals are only a completion medal and there doesn't seem to be a grading system. Going for those diamond medals in distance, or the trackmasters in trackmania has me playing those for hours. Well have to keep track of things on an external site like  or something.It is very multiplayer focused, But If custom lobbies exist they are hard to find. Wish there was a gamemode where you host your own instance locally and you face the ghosts of other players like a time trial tournament or something. The leaderboards are a cool ldea. I like that you unlock items by playing.My requests to the devs are the following: custom maps editor (this basically equates to endless content), and times saved on each map like an arcade leaderboard. So you know if you did better than last time and not only if you completed it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get the elephant in the room out of the way - Deathsprint 66's launch didn't go great.  Its launch price is (in my opinion) too expensive.  Not because the game isn't worth it - it honestly is.  But because it's too high a price to convince a community who's mostly never heard of it to give it a try.Seriously, nobody has heard of this thing.  The marketing was poor.  Every friend I've talked to, even ones who are VERY interested after seeing me play it, haven't heard the name once.  I hope there's a way to gain a solid community soon, or at least when console versions inevitably launch.But to talk about the game itself - honestly, there's just nothing like it out there.  Deathsprint 66 feels like if Mario Kart was a bloodsport - the insane speed on offer feels absolutely phenomenal and the intimate nature of the matches (8 players max) makes it competitive without being too chaotic.The PvE modes are a nice touch, though frankly I do wish there was more in the way of a formal campaign - another thing that would've helped mass adoption for this title quite a bit.  But overall, this is a really unique multiplayer title in a sea of extremely uninspired PvP games, and i think it deserves credit for taking something different and executing it spectacularly.  Now we just need players :(

_childDocuments_.review: Full Gameplay Walkthrough - When I first got my hands on Deathsprint 66, I immediately noticed the similarities to classic racing games like F-Zero, Wipeout, and Super Mario Kart, with some wall walking curiously of Titanfall. It brought a smile to my face, as I spent countless hours with those games. At its core, Deathsprint 66 is a circuit racer, and the DNA of those iconic titles is unmistakable. But Deathsprint 66 is far from your average circuit racing game. Beyond speeding along its deadly tracks, depending on the mode, you’ll either race against the clock or compete with other Clones—who’d love nothing more than to introduce your face to a saw blade or some other brutal fate.PVE in Deathsprint 66 is a mixture of what’s called Episodes, which are various events from time trials where players need to jump through rings to prolong their life, death-defying races against AIs, and is an alternative to those who don’t like to play along against other players (PVP). Despite not including the human element, it’s still a lot of fun and more than originally thought it would be.Then there’s the PVP, which is a mode where you and 7 other Clones will compete over any number of tracks. It’s mostly online but if there are no online players, you’ll get bots. The goal is simple, try to come in first and survive. This sounds simple, but depending on the track and skill of the other players could be anything but. Everything that you can do in the PVE mode can also be done in the PVP mode, just with human players. It’s here where I can see most players enjoying the most, as it’s only human nature that we attempt to show off how superior we are against other players.Overall its gorey , wacky and all the right mixture of things GO FOR IT8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: "Welcome, Welcome, Welcome!" The announcer's voice booms through loudspeakers all across the the dilapidated cityscape. The broken and crumbling brutalist infrastructure comes to life with the hum and glow of seething lasers and garish screens showing advertisements for the greedy conglomerate; the latest excuse for a chemical imbued beverage. "Have we got a show for you tonight!" The only thing that could be argued as louder, was the thumping in my chest. I exchange a nervous look with my fellow clone jockeys, of whom sport the ludicrous colours of their next sponsorship. They must be good. Although their eyes are covered by the ultra-drag resistant visors, there was a very brief sense of comradatory between us. That feeling would be fleeting. We all knew what we had to do. It's what we were made for.I take position at the asphalt starting line as the pre-recorded cheers of the AI powered spectatortrons die down. Exhale. A bead of sweat forms down my temple behind the helm of my nano-suit as the grav-enhancers engage on my boots.BZZZt! The deafening silence is interrupted. One red light. Did I ever have thoughts of just running away? Perhaps. But the C6 charges embedded within the nano suit would detonate if we went off-track. A legal requirement since the jockey uprising of 2058. At least on the track, there was a chance of survival, if only an insane one, to be had.BZZt! Two red lights. This is it. No going back. It was now or never. The mental images of the other clones bisected by my Bachman supplied razor saw will be a distant memory once I have my fame and freedom.BZZt! Three red lights. Inhale.Bing!Welcome to Death Sprint 66Death sprint is a grim, competitive racing game with with parkour elements and power-ups to destroy your opponents. Imagine if your competitive kart racing game was blended with both a parkour platformer and gory action game. This is it. Races are short, adrenaline fuelled and gripping the entire duration. A death in this game is only a minor setback with quick respawns to get you right back into the action again, meaning being in last place is absolutely not a surefire loss. One conveniently placed track hazard can dramatically rearrange the race leaderboards.The visuals are a spectacle with futuristic and deadly lasers and saws set against a run down urban backdrop. The graphics and frame rate are excellent, comparable to a AAA studio. It does a really good job of building the world this gritty race is set in through its environmental story telling. The buildings don't have windows, the people are replaced by automatons and the city seems abandoned to make way for cheesy company adverts and this twisted death race to profit on.The controls are seemless, abiding to the "easy to learn, but hard to master" philosophy. A specific tutorial mission shows you the ropes with the basic controls and showcasing the core features such as rails to grind on and the traps to avoid. I would personally suggest having a go at a time trial or two before jumping head first into online PVP mode, just to make sure you can also perform under pressure. The sound designs provides a constant dopamine loop from go, through to finish. I would like to personally tip my hat to the person who sound designed the runner taking steps. It must have been a headache to get the thump just right to sound powerful, but not heavy. The humming sears of lasers as you get near them and the screams of the other racers as they perish keep you on edge while the pulsing boost sounds and whirring zip lines spur to to go even faster! Usually to my own demise mind.The soundtrack is excellent. A lot of dark synthwave to go with the neon city and is a very fitting choice. I would love to have this on apple music and spotify. I've actually discovered two other games I frequently enjoy, just because their soundtrack appeared on my recommended list.Would I recommend this game? Yes. For, (currently outside of any offer,) 19.99 pounds is a very reasonable price. It would be dramatically improved with the addition of extra game modes like tournaments to set up, team games and limited lives elimination mode, but it's still such a wild experience. There are very minor fixes that have been addressed on the discord server for Sumo/Secret Mode and i'm looking forward to seeing those.Thank you for reading and if I've persuaded you to buy, then I look forward to seeing you on the track.Stay awesome. Pickle out.

_childDocuments_.review: Good concept, but bad execution on the single-player side of things. I don't understand how developers make games like this and don't include a quick restart. More often than not, a single failure in some of the single-player maps results in inevitable failure of the map, which results in you having to watch your player walk his slow ass up to the starting line again. It's a BASIC speed-running mechanic to grant a quick restart when failures result in frequent restarts. This game is LITERALLY a game about speed-running and doesn't grasp the basic concept that making the player repeatedly watch the opening intro is a bad thing.Multiplayer is good enough and the visual style and general control of the game is great, which makes it even more painful that the devs botched the single player mode. by not including a basic and easily implemented function that should be present in EVERY time-trial speed-running game where player death is a frequent occurance. Full stop. I can't even attribute it to laziness, because implementing a quick restart is so simple of a task that it's practically effortless. On the upside, along with multiplayer and the control feel, the main character's ass is also fairly impressive, though it loses some appeal after you've been forced to watch it during the level intro repeatedly. I'm giving the game's general control feel and multiplayer a seal of approval, but single player flunks hard for the dumbest possible reason. And because by no rights should I ever tire of having to look at that ass, and yet, I do.

Each track is laced with deadly traps, reminiscent of the light cycles in Tron, where one wrong move spells disaster.If you're looking for a game that blends the visual aesthetic of Tron with the fast-paced action of Wipeout and the strategic combat of Twisted Metal, Deathsprint 66 is an absolute must-play.My only con about this is that, I rarely get to play with other real players.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.  One of the best speed racers I have ever played.  All the concerns I had reading some reviews were dismissed after playing the game.  The concept is great (essentially Motorball from Gunm/Battle Angel Alita), the execution flawless, the speed and difficulty just right - easy to learn, hard to master.  There is a good diversity of levels.  The game goes so fast and you are so focused on not dying all the time that the power ups take a back seat.  It seems to lack players but thankfully the bots do a great job.  The main think is that, like Wipeout, F-zero or Extreme-G, the gameplay loop is incredibly fun.  The price is right.  See you on the grid, runners.
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Mario abilities combined with Tron aesthetics. Its like the fastest and most vivid fever dream you could think of for a game. I've loved every second of it. Getting used to the controls took me a sec, but i learned, even through the rage of getting blown up 5 times in a row, to love playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun racing game, lots of unique mechanics and ways to travel across the courses which makes it not only exciting but challenging to race, alone or against others. There is a bit of chaos involved, what with the weapons and the obstacles that you need to avoid as you race, which makes it closer to Mario Kart than anything else (if Mario Kart was a gory death race that is). The aesthetic is unique and entertaining, though I do agree that the color palettes make some things hard to see (but I feel it's more of a filter issue than a colors issue). I like the variety of the maps and the racing modes, though I feel like some maps in the PVE modes like the cyberspace courses could also be used in the multiplayer modes to add even more variety (unless that's already the case?) I highly recommend it to everyone, we need more people to play and enjoy this hidden gem!
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a game which is fast paced, and thank God I found this one. Its gameplay is easy to learn, the graphics are beautiful with those neon signs and tracks. There are PVP and PVE, challenge modes with different requirements. I think it can be priced a bit more and still worth it. What it needs  is even more modes, like a marathon, in which we'll run in about 50 laps instead of 5.
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the ads for this game I was really excited because I thought it was a cool concept to racing games. and let me tell you it is. I love the game I've already gotten a total of 4 hours on this game and i just downloaded it. I truly love this game and I really hope it gets received well and the servers don't shut down. If they do I will be very upset. I would also like to state that I really don't like racing games but I sure do love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. There is some room for improvement with optimization and minor bugs here and ther, but the concept is gold. It has everything, insane speed, gore, fierce competition, etc. There IS a learning curve, but once you get it you have so much fun, remember death is a part of the game, and all the ways you can be killed are comical. I havent had so much exhilerating fun in so long. Please, if you love racing and pvp do yourself a favor and get this game. its really great for the price point.
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit on the fence at first when I started playing this game, but the more I got comfy with the controls and with the feel of the races, I gotta say, this game is FUN. Some stuttering/frame rate issues here and there but it's day one, I'm not too worried about it. It runs pretty well for the most part. Graphics are great. _childDocuments_.review: As a previous speedrunners enjoyer this game fills that niche of having a fast pace running game that you can easily jump in an have a blast with your friends. Get power-ups to send into your opponents to gain the advantage. Find the most optimal path for your race and you send yourself into super speed, crushing your competition. _childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the right idea. A little bit more refinement.. lower price then i could see it being way better. I do believe the price should be better.. around the 5-10 dollar range maybe.. you could almost replicate this game on fortnite without the gore.. that's why i say that.. i would give it a good 6.9 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything iv been missing. I usually play shooters and high stakes games to get a dopamine hit. This game brings to the stage a state of mind that forces you to be focused and make very quick choices; while also making it easy to pick up and play. Also gives you the since that mastering it is hard. I started playing through the "Episodes" AKA Time trials and challenges. You learn quickly how to play the game and what it takes to succeed. Highly recommend. I find myself obsessing over the perfect run because of the feeling you get when you dont mess up.
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun! It looks great and moves at sonic levels of speed once you get going. I love that we can use power ups on each other and push other players into hazards or just right off the course! Also there is NO STORE !!! You get cosmetic unlocks at a steady pace and there are a lot of them from what I have seen so far. If you are looking for a fun and fast racing game without having a motor under you, check this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: DeathSprint 66 is a high octane adrenaline rush with an incredibly creative and dedicated team of developers behind it. With fluid controls, precision movement and beautifully gory death physics, it's fun for your whole friend group! The game features an eight player party system, giving you plenty of space to play with people, even being able to fill an entire PVP lobby with just people you know. The time trials and PVE modes are engaging and still pique the adrenaline, but the PVP is where the sweet spot of player on player carnage lies. The game is also filled with little lore tidbits to engage you, even outside of the races. With massive advertising billboards, and a carousel of rolling headlines it really helps to cement the world of DeathSprint 66 outside of the spotlight and the races. I would heartily recommend this game for anyone who enjoys a little bit of high octane gore!
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: [DISCLAIMER]: THIS REVIEW WAS ONCE POSITIVE AND MORE IN-DEPTH ABOUT THE GAMES STATE, HOWEVER DUE TO LOW PLAYER COUNT AND AFTER PLAYING FOR OVER 50 HOURS NOW, I HAVE DECIDED TO COMPLETELY REDO THIS REVIEW FOR ANYONE JUST NOW FINDING THIS GAME.Game has a great foundation but it suffers heavily from an identity crisis. The game has a settings and elements that would make you think it should be a competitive arcade racer where you compete against others through an obstacle course and the person who can do it the fastest wins. At the same time the game also has items for you to pick up similar to mario kart that allows you change the outcome of the race by using your items effectively. The problem is that this makes each race very RNG heavy, and this level of RNG is not good for a game that wants to be competitive. The game plays more like a party game right now for you and some friends to hop on for an hour and have a good time and then leave it for another day.The player count is so low that I can not recommend this game for anyone who wants to play competitively and not just want to have fun in a party game.
_childDocuments_.name: DeathSprint 66

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE reduce waiting time in between races. some races don't even take a minute and then it takes 90 seconds to two minutes until the next one starts. so you want to play but end up sitting there 70% of the time with your controller in hand waiting and watching those unnecessary flat 40 seconds tick down.I'd suggest to cut 20 seconds from the 40 seconds menu waiting time and let players skip the rest of the race when there's only bots left racing.

name: Button City
detailed_description: Fennel is a shy little fox who just moved into town. After discovering the local arcade, he makes new friends and gets swept up in a whirlwind adventure to save it from being shut down at the paws of greedy fat cat Peppermint Pepperbottom! Button City is a narrative adventure game about friendship and community. Enter a pastel diorama world inspired by 90’s nostalgia and filled with cute characters to befriend. Complete quirky quests around town, play arcade games, collect fun costumes, solve puzzles and more as you follow a story from beginning to end about growing up and saving the things that are important to you. Explore a beautiful and lovingly crafted world in a low poly art style. Befriend a cast of charming animal characters. Complete fun and silly side quests at your own pace. Master arcade games to unlock new game modes and prize items! Dress up in fun costumes and decorate your room. ★ Gobabots is the latest craze sweeping the arcade. Two teams of four cute fruit robots battle it out in an intergalactic competition to make the biggest smoothie! Each Gobabot has its own unique weapons and attacks -- collect them all at the arcade prize counter, form your perfect team, and become arcade champions! ★ Zoom down Watermelon Mountain in tuned-up electric cars in rEVolution Racer , a pastel take on classic arcade racing games. Race as Evie in her custom EV Sprinter against her fierce rival Spin. Drift to charge your batteries then unleash extreme boosts to speed past the competition! ★ Prisma Beats is a rainbow rhythm game with funky visuals and awesome tunes! Hit notes on the beat and show off your best dance moves -- and try out the challenge modes, if you’re feeling competitive.

short_description: Button City is a cozy narrative adventure game about a fox and his friends banding together to save their local arcade! Explore a diorama world, play exciting arcade games, complete quirky quests and meet cute animal friends.

_childDocuments_.review: ☑️Wholesome Game.☑️Adorable Atmosphere.☑️Funny Jokes.☑️Quirky Purrsonalities.☑️Animal Crossing vibes.☑️Really fun mini-games.Button City is a colorful low poly adventure game about cute little beans and an their local arcade. It is one of the most adorable and rather short (roughly 5-6 hours) games about a few friends having fun at their local arcade, but then a big corporate slime paw tries taking over their local arcade to tear it down for *Shiver* their own selfish greed. HOW COULD HE!?You play as Fennel, a nervous little fox that just recently moved into a new city. He's a little shy and awkward but manages to get outside and explore the diorama world which is Button City. The city is all stacked on top of each other which is a nice twist to see in a game. You'll fine yourself playing exciting arcade games, and meeting cute and quirky animals/friends while trying to become one of the best Gobabot teams in the local arcade! "FLUFF SQUAD ASSEMBLE!"You'll get a lot of joy out of this small packed game, if not the mini-games at the very least the conversations and quirky characters with all of their ups and downs. It's not all about fun and games, there is some solid story telling in this game. If you're looking for fast paced game-play and things of this nature, then this game is not for you. It's essentially Animal Crossing meets Night in the woods meets arcade games. I would highly recommend this game to everyone and anyone looking to have a really chill and fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: 100% achievement Yes (~3 achievements). Yes (15 achievements). No. is a low-poly adventure game that tells about the daily life of , a little fox, and his gangmates. Three minigames become the focus of the game in addition to the exploration that the gang has to go through to deal with their problems.- 3 minigames with adjustable difficulty- Optional side quests- Accessories for cosmetic purposes- Accessories are reset after you close the game- Playing the minigames too many times can be boring- Some performance issues and soft locks can happen if you are not carefulIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650If I would describe it in one word, it would be cute. The low-poly style works well to make everyone look cute while the vibrant color palette helps to give life to its surroundings. I like the small design of each area, focusing on one object of interest at a time to make it easier to explore. Moreover, the interactable objects also become easy to distinguish due to the white outline.Since the game focuses on children's life, it's obvious that you'll have a lot of silly problems to deal with. Gang wars, competitions, chill time with your gangmates - everything revolves around what the children do in the city, and the interaction between them can give a smile on your face. However, it can be hard to remember everyone's names - there are a lot of people in the town and I didn't even know one of my gangmates' names until near the ending.The game plays out like other adventure games where you can explore the city and move around, except that traveling between locations can be done as simple as teleporting: you just need to press a button, choose your destination, and you'll arrive there in no time. It might not sound as impressive as it looks, but trust me, it works. It's easier to look through the places that are available at that time and the small size of each region helps to scroll through the areas easily.As I said before, the game focuses on three minigames. There is a simplified MOBA minigame where you can go into 4 vs 4 matches to put as many fruits in the middle as possible, a racing minigame that focuses on drifting, and a rhythm minigame where you need to press four arrow keys at the right time, just like how  works. The first one will be mandatory to finish the game, although you are free to skip the latter two if you want. The thing is, everyone in the town loves playing these, so you can always challenge them to play one minigame that they like.Side quests are abundant. There are a lot of side quests that can come at an unexpected time. It helps to break the repetitiveness of the game, especially if you are fed up with the minigames. The quests usually revolve around fetch quests where you need to go to a certain location to either find or talk to people. It can be hard to find where you are supposed to go due to the number of people that you need to remember and find, but you can always scour through all areas and talk to everyone in case you are not good at remembering things like me.I finished the game in 11.5h, but that's also because I took my time and challenged all residents in the game for their favorite minigame, which is not necessary to finish the game nor getting 100% achievements. The only challenge that you'll get in this game comes from the minigames, but you'll be able to select the difficulty and add some modifiers to make it easier or harder. I still found them to be on the easy side, although some people who don't like rhythm games might have trouble in the harder difficulty.The game slowed down a bit when I played the rhythm minigame in the hard mode, although it's still within the acceptable range. There are also some  that I found when I played the game. Lastly, the main character's walking speed is very slow - it can be annoying to navigate through one long area because of it.I'm impressed with . It looks colorful and lively for a children's game, except that it's also can be enjoyed by adults due to its cheerful nature. The camera does a good job of zooming in on the cutscenes, making it as if you are seeing a movie. The transitions between screens, as well as the music, are also done beautifully, adding more to the experience. Sadly, the game can be taxing if you play the minigames too much like me, and some annoyances and soft locks can happen if you are not careful. It doesn't retract my enjoyment from the whole game, but you might want to be careful because of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is packed full of charm, style, and wholesome fun. The art is vibrant and adorable. The writing is clever and gives each character their own personality and quirks. The music (done by Slime Girls whose music you may have heard in Ooblets) complements the gameplay perfectly by matching the mood of each scene. It's refreshing to find a nonviolent game that focuses on the relatable anxiety of making friends and trying to fit in. The 3 playable arcade minigames are just as polished and cute as the main game. There are points in the story that require you to play some of the games, but winning isn't mandatory in order to advance the story and the minigames never feel forced. This game feels like a warm cup of tea in a world full of energy drinks. Disclaimer: I bug tested this game on PC, so I received the game for free.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: My childhood was not surrounded by tons of friends, and the few I had didn't share the same passions as I did: my passion for all kinds of video games was kept mostly to myself while growing up, and while playing this game, I found myself surprisingly feeling like the young, lonely girl I was when I was growing up-- but it also made me feel like the fun-loving, yet somewhat mischievous kid I was before adulthood. I saw this game's demo in a recent Steam sale based on animals, (one that was actually not on the front page of Steam, and was hidden!) and none of the games really appealed to me, aside from this little one hidden in the cracks. I decided to grab the demo while it was active, and I was kind of in love with it, keeping skepticism in mind. While the game shows need of polish, with a bit of a sluggish pace and the need of a few of some control improvements, what this game offered beyond that was genuinely another experience I wasn't expecting at all.Right out the gate, you might cross a connection with another game using a similar style, specifically one about animals; the animations and character designs are certainly inspired by this, but the similarities end there, as Button City poses itself as a very unassuming, quaint and cute world, with funny writing, cute character motives (and solutions!) and a surprisingly emotional storyline, hidden deep underneath its' facade of adorable fluffiness. Simply playing arcades and making friends seems enjoyable enough, but the level of intricacy in what lay beyond was really special.In a standard game of crossing animals, the interactions you experience are interactions you, the silent protagonist, chooses to make with them: in this game, however, each character feels connected to another character in some way, whether they're friends, rivals, or people just doing their job. Your fox-protagonist, Fennel, is charmingly sharp, mischievous and curious, and his interactions with the characters makes for a very heartwarming experience that'll make you smile, want to giggle to yourself, and in a few particular instances, clever usage of breaking the fourth wall. It's executed in an adorably innocent way..-- However: this game also introduces its' share of surprisingly real themes, and they came as a complete surprise-- and it really leaves an impression that is not at all what I expected when I first tried this game's demo. Due to my own experiences in life, relating to many things in this game, the deeper connections truly resonated with me, resulting in a somewhat rare instance where a video game made me cry: That said, I love Button City, wholeheartedly-- and after completing the game, my heart tells me that the developers of Button City love its' players too. While not the longest experience available on Steam, sometimes it's nice to just slow down a bit, take time and enjoy yourself. Button City gave me the right excuse to do just that.Lastly, to the developers,Thank you for putting all of your love into this game and working so hard to release this game, making it feel as connected as possible-- and thank you for providing a narrative that I won't forget for quite a long while. I hope you'll continue to make more games like this, and I hope the future is bright for Subliminal, Button City, and anything that might come after.

_childDocuments_.review: Stayed up way too late playing this game. It's really frickin adorable. The animals are cute, the story is cute, the style is cute. And the main arcade game? It's actually really fun. Bonus points for girl power and a disabled character who is still a person (well, animal). As a disabled person, very much appreciate. If you are looking for a frustratingly difficult game, this is not it. But if you are looking to chill on the couch and kill three hours in an enjoyable fashion -- 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Even if it's not the most apt comparison, this game somewhat reminds me of Night in the Woods, except the cast have the POV of kids instead of young adults.Button City has the look of one of the many wholesome games that have become popular in recent times. It has bright pastel colours, a style of animal character and expression reminiscent of animal crossing, a cute story about saving an arcade and a quite goofy sense of humour. The game doesn't just feel like it's trying to fit into the completely wholesome game category however, while the tone is light it does reference the characters real issues, adding a slight touch of reality to the story that makes it all the more engaging to me.The main gameplay, appropriately for a game about arcades, is split between three arcade games, a rhythm game, a racing game and a...robot battle fruit blending game. I enjoyed all of these, especially the racing game which takes obvious inspiration from Initial D and as a result is *very* fun to drift around and get new high scores in. I do feel that the robot minigame may have been a tad overused as by the end it had begun to feel somewhat repetitive, but overall I had a great deal of fun with it.Beyond these, gameplay involves talking to people and either running an errand for them or passing an arcade game challenge. All of these were enjoyable to me due to the very charming presentation and writing, though once again a few toward the end that required many repeat trips between locations did feel somewhat repetitive.In spite of those slight issues however I would very much recommend Button City. It would be criminal not to, after the amount of times its managed to make me smile.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: I... I just can't.It truly breaks me that a game this polished and well-made and beautifully designed has to be ruined by the weird and sluggish progress you make by each minute you spend in game.Don't get me wrong. I love a good casual game that can help me forget about my bad day, or bad week. A warm Saturday evening with some tea and a cozy game - well maybe not this one.I first found this game and thought that the mini-games are gonna be fun, maybe the story can be intriguing, maybe the cute character design can make this game even better. But well was I horribly wrong about all of them.I don't mind giving backstories, maybe showing how the characters are, but really the way this game tried to show story and give quests is just unbearable. It's so slow and sluggish that I couldn't handle it anymore. In the span of an hour of me staring at the monitor and reading all the unnecessary dialogues, I only got to play the 'actual' game maybe two or three times which only lasted 2 minutes each. I thought the actual game meant to be relaxing and maybe somewhat challenging, but the idiotic AI made it frustrating and infuriating - exactly the opposite feeling I was aiming for. Even the mini-games were either too easy or just straight up dumb. I personally thought the racing mini-game is supposed to be more engaging and just fun, but it was boring just like the rest.I'm not going to be all critical and cynical about it. The charm and the artstyle is quite pleasant and worthy of praise. There were some moments that were quite funny and somewhat dark, but yet again they were all ruined by the sheer amount of lack of care in how the story was executed.I can't express how much I was disappointed at this game. I can't recommend it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who really was excited for this title before it came out and then played it for a while and forgot about it I was just generally disappointed at how slow and sluggish the game felt. I really gave it a solid chance and played it for as long as I could but I would really not recommend the actual game. The art is really fun and it is a pretty cute game, but the mini-games don't control particularly polished and a lot of the progress in the game is bogged down by extremely long sequences of nothing but walking based fetch quests. It just feels like the game has been padded for extra length with this and it just got too drawn out and I basically stopped playing and forgot about it until now when I am publishing this review. I hope the creator of this passion project goes on to do lots of other cool things, I just hope that they pay more respect to player's time. I enjoy a good slow paced game like the original Animal Crossing, or Point and Click adventures like the Humongous Entertainment games I played during my childhood, but I think if a game is gonna make you do something slow you should at least have something to show for it and not be sent on another walk across 10 screens at the very slowest walk cycle possible.
