_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and chill game. Characters are funny and cute. I'm not usually fan of story based games, but this game is one of my fav games ^w^Minigames were fine, but somehow buttons for dancing minigame with controller were way too messed up so I had to use keyboard for that. I think dancing minigames were a little too hard too, but that might be just me.Very much recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: I received a key to play this on my stream, and I'm so glad I did. It's a cute little story, with enough mini-games and side quests to keep you busy for a good few hours (I'm sitting at 9 hours play time right now). I'm a huge fan of the rhythm game you can play at the DDR machine.I especially liked the casual representation/inclusivity in the game - it was so nice to see someone being referred to solely by they/them pronouns (without their identity being made into a big side plot).You should pick it up if you want something calm and fun, and play through a wholesome little story about a neighbourhood arcade. Also doesn't hurt that all of the characters are cute animals.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City is a relaxing game about a small local arcade, and the kids who essentially consider it their second home.I'll start by saying this game definitely isn't for everyone - it's not fast paced and the only action you see is in the mini games. However, that doesn't make it a bad game. As someone who loves wholesome, relaxing games, I really enjoyed it! I found the gabobots minigame a bit annoying at times, especially when AI decides to be extra stupid, but overall, a great experience!Most of this game is either fetch quests, or challenging the townsfolks to one of three minigames - racing, dancing, or the staple of the game, gatobots. The racing is probably the simplest of the games - just hold down x the entire time to constantly utilize your boost, and turn as often as possible to build said boost. Dancing was a huge pain when I tried using the arrow keys, but mostly due to me mixing up what key was what symbol - once I switched to 1, 2, 3, and 4, it became much easier. Gabobots is pretty straight forward, just collect the berries to bring to the center and beat up your enemies so that they can't. You can collect a small hoard of gabobots, but in the story missions that include matches, you're stuck to your starter (who in all fairness is definitly not the worst of the lot). Personally, I find that having a crew of mostly long-distance characters works best, maybe with the tank of a melon added in. The only match that I truly found hard was the post-game one - and you'll know it when you see it. There are still some minor bugs in the game, but the dev team has been great at being responsive in a timely manor and patching the issues as they come up. Overall great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: I was following the development of Button City for a decent while before release, so was very much looking forward to playing it (as soon as I could afford to). As someone who enjoys a pretty wide variety of games of different genres, structures and tones, I was sold on Button City's vibe as soon as I saw its visual style. If joy could have a colour palette, you'd see it in the screenshots above.As someone struggling with depression, I've found it pretty important to inject some bliss into my backlog (since that's about as close as I can get to my bloodstream these days), and Button City definitely delivered: while it does touch upon some pretty serious subject matter from time to time, the game managed to keep me genuinely smiling for much of its runtime. If a miserable cynic like myself can be so impacted by this game's charm, I wonder as to how much happiness it could give others.It's worth noting that I did encounter bugs fairly frequently while playing, but most (if not all) were addressed and/or fixed in a patch shortly after I finished. With a small team, especially when creating numerous minigames of different genres on top of a core narrative (which would require a lot of attention to logic and triggers during development), bugs and a smaller scope are inevitable. Regardless of the minor shortcomings, games like this are important, and I really wish that this one could receive the traction and success it deserves.This is why I'm recommending this game: while the developers may have lacked the budget of their "AAA" peers in the industry, I'd say that the love they poured into Button City is more than tangible in the result - it's infectious.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: this is the best game ive played in a long timei havent had so much fun with a game in months. its so cute and adorable and has so much variety. and you get a lot of content for this price (or even on sale)theres so many side quests and achievements to unlock and lots of fun mini games! i love button city <3
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: I have a LOT of love for Button City, and that came as a surprise in all honesty.I thought it would be a simplistic game, maybe even a little unfinished, with a focus on the arcade mini games (as the trailers seem to highlight).But this game has so much more life and heart in it.The story is brilliant and you get to see bits of the characters' lives as the main story unfolds. The writing got me invested, as well as everyone's personalities and the cute details. It makes me feel nostalgic for those childhood days.The developers did really well making the dialogue a mixture of humour, sweetness, silly moments and sincerity. It actually made me tear up at some point.Another thing I really liked was the direction and camera angles in the cutscenes. The shot would zoom in perfectly on a character's face, or reveal a funny expression. I can see exactly how the developers wanted the scene to play out visually.Along with the main story are a number of side quests to do, and you can have a go in the arcade practically whenever - or challenge somebody to a game of their choosing.You can collect wearable items, decorations for your room, and food items that give you status effects in the arcade games. Interestingly, you can also add cosmetics to the arcade games as well! I didn't notice this at first, and was wondering what some of the things in the backpack were used for. But when you load up an arcade game, you will see a section called "fluff buffs" where these items will come into play. That was a really cool addition.If I had to pick a criticism, it would be that sometimes the movement feels a bit off. When you interact with a character, there might be a little walk-around and a zoom-in of the camera before the dialogue starts. Or you might have to move around slightly to correctly interact with a door. It feels a bit wonky. (And maybe the backpack could be a little more organised.) It didn't really bother me, though!I'm actually kind of sad that I've finished Button City. I had a great time playing it and relaxing in that colourful world. A really pleasant surprise and an easy recommendation for fans of heartfelt, cosy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about being the new kid making friends in town and visiting the Arcade known as Button City ever day!No school, no work, no bills just kids being kids having fun and playing Gobabots! (This worlds, Pokemon, Digimon, Yugio, ect) Does a great job depicting a young disabled child as just another kid trying to live life to their fullest and making friends while having fun on the way. Different families and life styles are shown. Childhood issues, growing up, ect.It has plenty of mini games, puzzles and side quests to enjoy especially at the Arcade!If you loved Arcades as a kid growing up this game is amazing! If you like Animal Crossing I'd bet you like this game too. I highly suggest gamer parents to play this game with their kids, it should be a blast. Great story and very cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: A very simple, cute, and silly story about a skittish fox making new friends in a new town with a heavy focus on the local arcade as the place to be for kids. Its a very slow burn with a simple but cute art style and cute characters of varying personalities. The only real problem I had with the game at some point is how slow the movement is. Towards the end of the story, or if you're doing 100% with all the quests, there's a lot of tasks that just require you to go back and forth a lot. The maps are all pretty small though, with about two exceptions, so in a way its paced out nicely with how quick it is to go from the arcade to the cafe to the park. Choices don't matter so you don't have to worry about losing out on a secret route or something that you might come to expect from visual novels. Other than the VN aspect being the driving factor there's also three minigames that are fun in their own rights. A simple little racing game, a rhythm based dancing game, and a simple 4v4 moba that is the centerpiece of the story. This may or may not be a deal breaker for some people depending on the price just because most of the appeal is from the story itself rather than the extras but its there as well, and with the moba game taking the spotlight the other two are given little side stories to give you a reason to be interested in them.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very cute and relaxing experience with cute chibi animals. The minigames are actually surprisingly fun and addicting, and the story had more depth than it might seem at first with core messages about growing up that might hit home with some people. My only issue would be with the ending. By the end of the game, naturally you are invested in what's happened in the story thus far, but I would almost recommend *against* getting too invested here. Don't read too much into the inner workings of the main character's family or their seemingly dark past that they hint at, or the backgrounds of his friends, because it will not be expanded upon.To me, at least, it felt like the game dropped off very suddenly at the end, which seems to be very common with indie games, so I would say this is an amazing game to play if you want exactly what it looks like: a simple, cute chibi animal game with pretty engaging minigames that are fun to grind out for achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely AMAZING!!! I love every part of it and it's very underrated!! All the aspects of this game are wholesome and cute, and if you tend to take lots of time on games exploring every nook and crany or collecting achievements, you will have a lot more then 6 hours on this game (I have 15+). I love the new take on exploring, where each place is a platform. All your fluff squad members have stories and family that you get to meet and get to know. Everyone is sweet and the story is great, it's bittersweet at almost the end and it might be more emotional to others. The soundtrack is SO GOOD, and each character you meet does something. All the achievements aren't hard to get and are super fun. All the arcade games never get boring and it's all just perfect. You can decorate your room, collect items, clothes, and boosts and complete lots of fun side quests. The ending was happy and I'm so sad it ended. The developers are so kind, and respond to all questions. I can't explain how perfect, unique, and underrated it is. It definitely deserves a lot more purchases as an indie game. 10/10 so so happy I got this. :))
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: I like the story elements coming together and the side quest content galore. It could have used more time in the oven for more plot elements I think... More hangouts with the main cast would have been cool. The last part of this game made me want to know more about the main character, but it kind of ends after getting a light look into their life. Maybe a few more minigame events? Or more play revolving around the arcade itself beyond primarily Gobabots.One issue I had was the character rotating/squirming slowly to interact with things while trying to pathfind into the correct spot to properly interact, even for entities that should have been interactive from any angle. I also feel like the dance minigames are a fair bit too difficult to clear without numerous mistakes, but at least they're forgiving. I don't know if there's a plan to add more to the game after release, but just know I'll be here for it as I complete the rest of this game's side quests and listen to the last remaining story beats. I recommend it based on how it handles sensitive topics. If you have family members suffering from certain problems, it's easy to relate to certain characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely cute game with endearing characters and dialogue. It's very simple and sweet. Move speed is pretty slow, but it didn't bother me at all because just being in this cute world and sporting costumes was the fun part. There were some bugs here and there (sometimes music stops after you finish an arcade game, or sometimes the screen just goes black, but this happened very rarely), but it wasn't anything that kept me from enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great time! The characters, story, and music are all extremely charming, and the minigames in the arcade are all very fun. rEVolution racer in particular is very addicting, and the main Gobabots game has a surprising amount of strategy and depth! Lots of laughs from the dialogue, if you're looking for a chill way to spend your time, you can't go wrong with Button City!
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute and charming game with a lot of personality and character. And characters. A surprisingly easy-to-remember cast with how well defined many of them are and while the plot itself is nothing outstanding or unique it's still engaging for what it is. The minigames are all decently fun too, special shout-out to prisma beats making me really miss DDR, and the game's just got a chill energy throughout that I really enjoy. If you're looking for a hardcore gamer's game then you won't find it here but for a fun, cozy time full of a lot of charm, it's definitely worth looking into.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is too stinking cute. If you enjoy wholesome games and may or may not have nostalgia for arcades, then this is absolutely for you. An adorable little game with varied gameplay, great characters, and even some neat representation! Most of the game is walking around and talking to characters, completing quests, etc. But there's plenty of minigames to play and rewards to earn from the arcade gift shop. Hopefully you're better at Prisma Beats than I was!Gameplay can be found here:
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City is masterfully written, charming and funny. It's always taking unexpected twists and leaning on the fourth wall. There's not any real difficulty to the gameplay, so the writing is what made me stick around, which is unusual for me. The ending gave me all the feels.The soundtrack is incredible, by the way. And there are so many fun sidequests they probably take longer to finish than the main storyline, thanks in part to all the minigames in Button City arcade. In spite of being easy (except that rhythm game, I'm terrible at it), they are all super fun minigames.I like how you can teleport out of downtown and watch all the extra buildings fold back into the fourth dimension.This is the kind of game you could buy for your kid, but also enjoy for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Great enjoyable game.Notes for those going for 100% completion:1.For the Fancy Fluff achievement you need to buy all wearables from the prize shop on the second floor of button city, even if you have duplicates of that wearable already.2.For Poppy's Clean Week quest you might have to do other quests to unlock areas that have trash for you to pick up. For example, I had 48 out of 50 of the trash and had to complete Sage's quest (coffee shop person) to access a new area that had the remaining 2 pieces of trash.3.Interior Designer and Fancy Fluff achievements require some quests to be completed in order to get those achievements. So if you're not getting them go and finish quests.I will update this review later with more info and an actual in-depth review.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City has colourful and charming low poly aesthetics that hides some surprisingly deep moments behind it's cartoonish nature. While the game is largely goofy and focuses on the nostalgia or growing up in the boom of arcades and the community surrounding it, each character is given brief windows into their life and the difficult emotions of growing up. It's not the deepest storytelling out there but considering I didn't expect it at all it balanced the humour and the brief tone shifts decently, perhaps a bit on the rushed side but the story itself is rather short. Gameplay wise your time is split between traversing the town, through a neat little warp between bite sized dioramas, and various mini-games. The mini-games consist of a lite MOBA style game (that drives the story forward), a racing game and a rhythm game. Aside from the rhythm game there's not much difficulty to be found, in fact I found the rhythm game so difficult I had to switch from gamepad to keyboard in order to get the corresponding achievement. The layout of the gamepad inputs just didn't feel intuitive at all. Despite the lack of difficulty in the other mini-games I found them enjoyable enough, and honestly I cheesed the racing game enough that it became lightly meditative to play lmao. Exploring the dioramas and interacting with the townsfolk was a joy, I loved the design of all the animals and their animations were very reminiscent to Animal Crossing and their dialogue and personalities were fun and quirky. There was a good amount of side quests involving most of the townsfolk so I felt like I got to really experience the small community.Overall a fun little game that's characters alone make it worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City was admittedly more than I ever expected, from an Animal Crossing vibe with the facial expressions and animations to a few surprisingly deep characters in an otherwise upbeat game. Do not let the aesthetics fool you into thinking this game is simple; it is an obvious labor of love.I did encounter a few bugs and there were a few quests that were annoying backtracking, but I would play it all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is great, the characters and writing are fun, but it is just sluggish and floaty and does not feel good to actually play. This is going to sound like a comparison that's out of left field, but you know how in Red Dead Redemption 2 you frequently had to approach interactable items at the exact right angle before you could actually interact with them? Button City does that a lot too, and it is incredibly frustrating. The way the camera slowly pans down and in when you try to talk to someone else is pretty annoying, too. A damn shame, really.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City is a cute little adventure game, a nice little story and cast of characters. Nothing overly complex, but makes good use of all its parts. I particularly appreciate actually having mini-games for the arcade games, even if they can get a bit monotonous if you choose to challenge everyone in town.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: The simplistic art style grabbed me as it reminded me of an Annapurna game. I finally picked it up during a sale and wow, I wish I bought this sooner. I love the story from what I've played so far. Super cute game concept, I love the traveling system between places. It's like a fresh new idea implemented with a familiar looking indie style of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City has its shortcomings, but ultimately I did 100% it and don't regret any of it, so I would recommend it.Pros: - Good character writing- Good art and design- The arcade games are mostly fun- Getting rewarded with accessories added a layer of customization that was enjoyable- Decently replayable. I could see myself playing through this game again in a couple years.- Wholesome. Comfortable. Friendly.Flaws:- It could've used a couple more arcade games- Lacks polish in certain aspects- Lots of backtracking/mindless fetchquests- Somewhat awkward pacing- Could've used a bit more depth- No run button.OVERALL:7/10, will play again, would recommend it for 20$ or less.STRAIGHT UP SPOILERS:I found that the arcade currency was mostly worthless. The game *makes you* accrue arcade currency to finish side quests which themselves aren't necessarily rewarding, but besides that, you get some decently worthless decorations for your room (which you are barely ever in) or some accessories that aren't really worth going out of your way to wear and have no function.Besides Prisma Beats, the other two arcade games are engaging but lose all sense of challenge once you get familiar with them, and the game expects you to do them several, several times if you want to do everything the game has to offer. This could have been remedied with some better AI, further balancing of the game mechanics, & unique maps you could unlock.My critique of this game is mostly that it could have been better or deeper, but I can't blame the developers for that. For 20$, I'm definitely happy with what I got, but I would personally spend an extra 10 to fix the problems I have with it.More arcade games, more ways to make money, better balanced currency & purchase options.I want to add, the game has a couple "dark" implications. One in a sidequest, one in the main story. I liked the sidequest because it was fun and interesting, but it ended up being completely unrewarding. Felt more like an easter egg.In the main story, however, the game teases a complex relationship between the main character and his mother, but doesn't expand on it at all. It doesn't *need* to, but it suddenly dropped some really dark ♥♥♥♥ at the end of the game where the kid feels like his mother blames him for his father leaving?? And then they don't really talk about that or handle it at all. I would've *loved* it if the game had more depth focusing on the relationships of children with other children, or children and their parents, as a way to reflect on the psychology of these things. Instead, the game just kind of... hinted at it, teased it, and then ended.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: A shy young fox moves to a new neighourhood, befriends a gang of quirky personalities and goes on wacky hijinks to save the local arcade. Full of charm, genuinely funny writing and the occasional emotionally heartwarming story beat as the cherry on top that ties it all together. It's a short little jaunt, a casual "adventure" mainly composed of errand quests and minigames, but by the end I had become invested in all these pixel pals I had come to known during my adventure and it lead to a genuinely lovely finish. A hidden gem, which I'd fully recommend to anyone who loves these slice-of-life story/character-focused games.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game. I did find the achievements to be annoying because I have no idea how to get some of them. It would be a cool addition for people with quests to have a quest marker over their head or something similar. I have things in my inventory that say they are able to be used on arcade games but I have no idea how to do that. Overall a fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just a good time all around. It is an endlessly charming point and click story adventure game. Achievements are pretty easy for anyone who is going for 100% completion.I do recommend playing the Demo before buying the game, because it contains an unique scenario and dialogue that is NOT in the main game. I can't seem to download it again for some reason.What drew me into the game are the art-style and graphics. Anything low-poly looking yet modern gets a good score from me pretty quickly. I call this game an Animal Crossing-like because the character models (and especially animations) look like Nintendo's series. This isn't a fault, because it is a style that is shared with other indie games like "A Short Hike." I consider this my favorite Animal Crossing game because I don't have to keep up with chores or play it daily like actual Animal Crossing.The story itself works really well, and there doesn't seem to be any branching paths, only different dialogue choices. There is only one direction where the story can go in and there are no alternate endings. There are side quests that can be done when they come up, and nearly every NPC has one at some point.Performance-wise, I played on a desktop that uses Intel HD Graphics 630 with 16GB of RAM on an SSD. It loaded faster and ran better than the Nintendo Switch version did, especially when playing Plasma Beats.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City is pretty fun honestly. I personally know the developers via a local game making group, but I did purchase the game for myself and enjoyed my time with it. I currently have about 10 hours in the game, with the main game and the majority of the game finished. Really the stuff I haven't finished either felt too grindy (Achieving 10k buttons and Drinking 10 sodas) or were dealing with a minigame I personally did not enjoy (Beat all Prisma Beats songs in hard mode). That and of course the final achievement which requires me to finish the others. Button City kinda feels like if Night in the Woods art was more pastel based, both in visual style and in the story. You play as Fennel, a fox new to the town who must try and prevent Button City from being bought out by a rich businessman in a pretty typical "We got to save the Community Center plot". Hi-jinks ensue and Fennel gets some friends and gets to explore the town he moved to. The game uses a interesting stacked world mechanic where you can teleport between layers, which does a good job making the exploration not lag too much. Personally I just wish the ability was usable inside buildings as well, as it would be great to teleport out when I no longer need to be there, rather than having to walk my way out.Overall a very charming game that was pretty fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute little game. Sure I could nitpick some small stuff and point out a couple themes that are briefly touched upon that might be sensitive to some. Overall though despite the relative simplicity it was a fun experience that I couldn't stop playing until I'd seen almost everything the game had to offer. (7~8 hours from new game to completed main game and most of the quests)
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City is a wholesome 90s-inspired narrative adventure about a group of friends who are trying to save their local arcade. The game features a very colorful low-poly art style along with a joyful soundtrack.The story is all about friendship and community. Our protagonist is Fennel, a cute little shy fox who recently moved to town. They will join a friend group called the Fluff Squad that will compete against their opponents, the Tuff Fluffs, in the newest arcade’s game: Gobabots. However, things quickly change after both groups find out Mr. Button will close his arcade. Both Fluff Squad and Tuff Fluffs will try their best to stop Mr. Button from selling the place.Gameplay-wise, Button City is super chill. Inside the arcade you can either play Daytona-like reVolution Racer, Dance Dance Revolution-inspired Prisma Beats and Gobabots. Outside the arcade you walk around town and meet the cute low-poly animals, most of them named after condiments and spices. The game has a main quest but the player canalso complete various fun and quirky side quests.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Button City is a game that makes you feel nostalgic about something you've never experienced before. It gets you to feel good and bad; sad and happy. It reminds you that things can be complicated, but you can still be optimistic about how they'll turn out. The game feels like a classic children's film that never existed. While the execution and gameplay might not be perfect for some, it's the deliberately slow pace that draws you into the title's warm atmosphere and story. This isn't a game that's going to throttle you around with twists and turns, instead it acts more like a comforting drive down a gentle country road that you know like the back of your hand.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Get a shower, Fennel. And stop sniffing trash. The issues compound each other.Absolutely adorable and heartfelt little game about kicking butt and saving your beloved arcade. The kid logic and kid problems are charming and believable. Would love to see more arcade games (like a fighting one or a puzzle game) down the line, as well as more maps for the racing game, but overall, a wonderful good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute and fun game. The characters are very well written and the story is very nice. It is a very simple game, yet very entertaining. There are some issues here and there ... if you dislike walking around a lot you might not like this, I dont think you can run and there's some level of backtracking (maps are really small though! not a big deal, but not good for the impatient ones). The minigames are good, Gobabots(MOBAlike minigame) is probably the best one. Theres a lot of collecting stuff as well (clothes, decorations, gobabots, trash).There's even a built - in visual novel mini game. It is not a long game, but every second is filled with cuteness =) and love for videogames.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: The characters are charming, the art-style is cute and colourful, and the story is very sweet, getting surprisingly emotional at times!It's simple, but enjoyable. Easy to get behind and burn an hour or two.Beyond the main story, there's plenty of side-quests and mini-games to explore.There are a couple of bugs here and there, but nothing too serious (at least, that I've run into, and that hasn't already been fixed); and the devs seem to regularly look into anything reported.If you want something to play that isn't super hard and will lift your mood, I suggest this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: A charming game that makes you feel like a kid again. The main story is great, the minigames are engaging and fun, and the world is a place you want to go back to again and again to finish sidequests and earn achievements.The soundtrack is excellent, and both the visuals and writing are charming; all together they always put a smile on your face.Couldn't recommend it enough for anyone who likes chill, story-driven indie games and cute animals.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much that, even though I original bought it on the Switch, I bought it again on Steam just so I could positively review it.I've been looking for a game like this for so long. A Narrative Adventure, with surprisingly real, lovable characters, a fun world to explore, a great nostalgic soundtrack, creative mini games, and so much more. I feel GOOD inside when I play these games. Great for depression.Maybe it's a sign that I am getting old, but I am just tired of mindlessly violent games. This game is a shout out to my youth. Hanging out at arcades, and genuinely getting to know people. It reminds me a lot of Night in the Woods or Eastshade. And it's perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: It's an utterly charming adventure game with a big and colorful cast of NPCs and locations. You control a fox kid adventuring around a town with his gang of friends, trying to prevent their favorite games arcade from being closed (the arcade even has playable games!). Graphics are very Animal Crossing.I wish there were more kid friendly adventure games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little indie game about cute animals playing arcade games and assaulting a CEO. It made me laugh, cry and smile at every turn, and I can't recommend it enough to anyone who enjoys games like Pikuniku or Donut County. While the story itself only took me around five and a half hours, I KNOW I'm gonna keep coming back to do all the little side quests and finally get good at Prisma Beats. If anything about this game remotely interests you, I implore you to buy it and give it a shot, and to fall in love with all these cute and interesting characters just like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: Here's what I want to say about this title. (As of the time that I wrote this.) The gameplay, albeit very simple, is easy to grasp and virtually almost anyone can play it. The aesthetics while low-poly, are designed and color schemed in a way to be soft and welcoming. Most of the soundtrack is full of variety and genres, and fit most environments and story scenes very nicely. Plenty of memorable and quirky characters to meet and interact with, while engaging in plenty of cheeky dialogue and moments. The story isn't forcing you to get it done as fast as possible (outside of a few scripted moments) and can be played whenever you feel like it. At certain parts of the main story, there are actually a few moments that handled certain subject matter in a mature/down to earth way. Plus the main story takes up to 5-6 hours so it doesn't overstay it's welcome. The main character is written in a way I can Imagine some people relating to, for their personality and sense of humor. Side objectives with their own unique goals and rewards in return.You can only wear ONE COSMETIC AT A TIME, why? I suggest a total of three cosmetic slots total, so people can mix and match at their leisure. Unskippable dialogue: You have to wait to until any sentence is completely done in order to skip. Vendors, side characters, and the main character have the same problem. Being able to skip dialogue/cutscenes where you don't have to make choices helps stop unneeded redundancy. Adding different maps to Gobabots (a mini-game you can play almost anytime) to add some variety in this unfortunately repetitive mode. You get plenty of Gobabot combinations and perks included, but one map gets old really quick. For some reason Revolution (A racing mini-game) can barely perform a simply turn half the time, and other times when I do, I make a complete 180 or crash. Even the trailer shows the car bumping into stuff unintentionally. I suggest make the turning and drifting more responsive, while making the speed more consistent. Possibly include a few extra side character related quests outside of the original one side quest for one character method When will we ever get to interact with Fennel's (the main character) mama once the main story is complete? After you beat the main story, you never see her again. Anytime you click on her door, Fennel says something like: "I better not go into mom's room, she's going to be home late from work." There is a glitch where if you hit restart a mini-game and return to the main game, all music stops entirely. (I'm even talking about when you restart the game after the glitch occurs as well.) Last Suggestion, have more than 4 minigames to play! I understand that this is a fairly new indie company (with only so much of a budget backing them up.)  but still, only 4? There are like 6 or 8 other games in the arcade and you never get to play them. Why have them in there, in an ARCADE mind you, when you can't even play them? There are even side characters that play them, and you can't even challenge them or play them by yourself. I feel like this is the one thing that needs the most improvement.My final verdict, do I recommend this game? Yeah, but I hope that some of these problems are addressed. I honesty want to see certain aspects improve, so anyone can a have better experience. I hope this team knows they did a great job at creating a game with genuine love, passion, and soul behind it. Thank you for taking the time to read this. Have a lovely day/night whenever you're reading this.
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little game where you play as a shy little fox that winds up making a bunch of friends--and rivals!--and may or may not involve a lot of helping people around the town, particularly if you want to be a completionist and do things like pick up trash to keep the neighborhood clean!It's bright, colorful, and vibrant, and the characters are all very interesting (at least imo) although the naming convention threw me for a loop at first and did make remembering who was who a little bit tougher for me (wait, which one of you was Oregano again?) but it's still a really funny and fitting quirk, given the main arcade game's fruit-based gimmick.If I had to pick -anything- to gripe about, it would have to be that Prisma Beats only tells you the controls one time, and I failed to memorize them at that moment and promptly failed every single time I tried to dance lmao(I will git gud eventually, tho!)If you ask me, it is absolutely worth a buy, at the very least you owe it to yourself to check out the demo if it looks even remotely interesting!
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: My review: I'm close to the 2 hour mark on this game but the long and short of it is that I really like it! This is basically a story about how your character Fennel is a new kid in town who is shy and looking for friends (something I'm sure a lot of us can relate to). You find an arcade full of cool games and are quickly thrown into a new squad of friends who recruit you to be their 4th person in a video game tournament for "Gobabots." The story unfolds from there where you try to get to know your new found friends and try to get good at a new game you've never heard of.It's got a really colorful and vibrant art style, the writing is fun and makes the little animal characters pretty interesting and I'm curious to see where the story is heading next because it definitely heads into some directions you don't expect (like some real life issue kind of stuff)! Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Button City

_childDocuments_.review: I actually LOVED this game so much that I'm writing a review for it, that's a lot to ask for most steam purchasers. BUT, genuinely, this game is fantastic, the characters are great, the story is sweet and emotional, the length of the game is fair for the price, the gameplay is fun with a BUNCH of minigames to play with and just some fetch quests going on are fun to play through as well. I streamed this game and it seemed like everyone who watched really enjoyed the experience of the game so thank you devs for a great game, good job and i hope you can continue making games. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Button City is a colorful low poly narrative adventure game about a fox and his friends banding together to save their local arcade! Explore a diorama world, play exciting arcade games, complete quirky quests and meet cute animal friends.

name: The Last Faith
detailed_description: The wicked and the blessed will be judged the same - let nothing stand in your way. Often brutal, always empowering, The Last Faith is an unholy alliance of metroidvania and soulslike. The Last Faith thrives on merciless and precise combat, with a huge range of custom executions to perform. Discover a formidable arsenal of melee weapons, arcane spells, and long-range firearms, allowing you to carve a path your own way. Nonlinear exploration is at the core of The Last Faith. Gorgeous pixel art depicts an imposing gothic landscape. Journey along snow-dusted mountains and castles bathed in moonlight. Discover and upgrade a formidable range of tools for destruction. Step into The Last Faith’s ravaged world as Eryk, who awakens with no recollection of his immediate past. Soon he will discover he is in a race against time as his mind and conscience begins to deteriorate. His desire for salvation from this affliction sets him on a cursed mission that crosses paths with ancient religions and divinities.

_childDocuments_.review: Caution: 100% personal opinions incoming.Overall great game with some minor flaws which can be improved upon on possible future projects.Personally a big fan of pixelart well made. Gorgeous Eldritch/Gothic aesthetic. The soundtrack fits pretty well in all of it. Also a really thought out story with many, many bits of lore you can dig into so you can puzzle out everything there is to know about the world, the characters and generelly what's going on in all of it. Bosses had cool designs, easy to learn patterns without making them too difficult. A great implement for people that like to challenge themself as well as those who want to play more casually and still experience everything that is to find.And like every metroidvania worth their salt this game brims with secrets, hidden walls and pathways you can backtrack to the moment you unlock new moves.The amount of weapons and spells that are to be found fits well with the overall length of the game. Still would be cool to have more build specific options. Being dependant on ammo when you try to play a full gunslinger is a sure way to a grindfest, which also could be improved upon. Though you may find the feeling that you're stuck with specific weapons due to your build it is possible at a certain point in the game to reset all your stat to try out new builds. It is not that expensive but can end up people having to grind a bit. Though personally I did not have many issues with the amount of currency I got during my playthrough. Some improvements could be made with balancing out personal power and enemy power. In my experience the amount of healing you can provide yourself in conjunction with received and dealt damage can deliver a way to make the game easier than it probably intents to be. In theory you can just waltz through many stages if you play your cards correctly.Im summary yes, there are flaws but all in all I loved every second of playing. Videogames are an artform and the artists here did a fantastic job.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania Game with graphics that nostalgically remind me of older Castlevania games like Dawn of Sorrow.It does need some practice to get through the bosses and in a Hollow Knight style you need to recollect your currency upon dying where you died, but you don't need to enter the boss rooms to collect the currency in question.It is a nice, time consuming game that is a lot of fun if you like this style of game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The art direction is great, the map is big and full of secrets, the controls are tight and the combat is mostly fun... But the game lacks some VERY basic functions (resolution? borderless mode? vibration??) and was a nightmare to switch to other monitor; no QoL items (no "return to bonfire" + no auto-save on exit), weird status effects (a periodic stun effect for 40 seconds or the bleed with NO dedicated item to remove it), the lore makes no sense and the general feel of the game is just eh. Also removing all NPC before the last boss is just ???Clearly, next game from these devs will be worth checking out, but this one just... exists.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: 9 hours in and this game has pissed me off but not for the reasons most people would expect. I'm sure I'll see some "git gud" replies but my problem is not with the combat, aside from the flying enemies.-- There's too many flying enemies and no way to attack upwards. I found myself having to wait quite often for the ice banshees to fly down low enough for me to be able to jump attack them.-- Jump attack sometimes eats your momentum and you end up doing a short jump. Ended up falling down a pit a couple of times while trying to attack an enemy while jumping across a pit to not get hit by one of their attacks.-- There's one particular boss that I do not want to spoil, but I can only assume it's due to the way the boss arena works that it makes it to where if you die, you cannot recover your souls (or whatever they are called in this game) as when you return to the boss room, they are nowhere to be found. At this point of the game I had close to 20k souls and I ran into this boss room on my way to an altar to go spend them so I was forced into the boss fight and lost all of them after dying the 2nd time trying to retrieve them.-- I ended up in an area below the long bridge of ice banshees where you apparently require the air dash to get out of which I do not have. I ended up beating the challenge down here and I'm currently sitting here with 25k souls and no way to get out. There's no items to teleport you to your last checkpoint so I'm pretty much SOL and will have to kill myself and lose out on all those souls.-- I've been running around with 0 - 4 health vials as the game just won't drop any for me and the only time it gives you any is when you're about to enter a boss fight and it'll spawn up to 4 at the nearby altar.I get that this game is trying to be like Bloodbourne but that just doesn't translate well to a Metroidvania style game. I have seen the bad design mega thread and agree with mostly everything else there. Getting frustrated over getting killed over and over while learning a fight is something I can deal with.But losing out on 20k souls due to something that is completely out of your control and then being rewarded for exploring by losing out on another 25k is just extremely bad design. I doubt I'll be finishing this game as it is. Perhaps I'll return to it after some major patching is done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's phenomenal, get it unless you hate games and wandered into Steam's storefront by accident.Some time ago, The Last Faith appeared in my discovery queue and I wishlisted it as I'm big on Metroidvania's. At the time I wasn't exactly sold on Soulslikes though, nor combinations of the two like Blasphemous. While I've since become a major fan of Soulslikes (good ones that is), I still waited a little before picking up the now released TLF and diving in. Lies of P and all that jazz had my noggin abuzz. But when I finally got to TLF I was very pleasantly surprised at just how well this game combines Bloodborne-esque Soulslike qualities with Symphony of the Night-like Metroidvania qualities. It's not perfect, there's gripes to be had, sure... but this is the best combination of these two very different game types I've played.TLF has beautiful pixel artwork, a great soundtrack, mostly responsive controls, a lot of different weapons and magic spells/items to use and interesting npc's. The environments are dark, brooding and brim with little extra animations such as paper flying about if you run through papers on the floor. Bosses are imposing and distinct. Exploration is a crucial aspect of the game ofc, and lore bits can be found all over the place. Getting to the true ending is worth the effort btw.Much as TLF is a gorgeous game, it still has some flaws. Controlwise, sometimes your character will cancel out of an attack because you touched the button a split second too long and the game thinks you want to charge an attack. Or having difficulty registering that you want to use a weapon's special attack. It's also possible to get stunlocked by multihit attacks that impart status effects like burning. Sometimes this will mean a boss can effortlessly eradicate you. Hnnn... Much as I like exploring, the game has a bit too much "WTF do I go now" moments. And a bugged achievement/item. Worst may be that there's no lore closure.Despite my gripes, The Last Faith is phenomenal. Just be prepared to take your time with it's Soulslike difficulty level.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I refunded this game.It does not feel challenging; it feels cheap.I started with the Stargazer class, expecting I'd be using magic spells and that maybe I'd be a bit of a glass cannon. The two starting spells are inferior to the starting hand weapon. The stronger of the two spells was mostly useless on the first boss, and the weaker spell did less damage than a well placed hand weapon attack.Enemy attacks feel awkwardly telegraphed, and it felt like my inputs were being eaten. Spamming the attack button will cause you to combo and eventually do a combo finishing move which will give the enemies an opportunity to catch you off guard. The damage done from the combo finisher seems negligible and it seems to serve the purpose of punishing the player for spamming the attack button. Winning combat felt more like hoping I wouldn't be caught with my pants down than it did a test a of skill.Mana and life restoring items can easily be found by smashing pots and defeating enemies, but they do not replenish at save points. Acquiring them felt like an unnecessary grind. The one drop item I got that was not a mana or life heal was useless to the class I chose. When you die you lose some nycrux thing, which seems to be like the guilt in Blasphemous, but when I fought the first boss I would start at the save point with the nycrux thing right next to the save point, so I don't know what that game mechanic was all about.Within 10 or so minutes of starting the game, I was railroaded into the first boss, and I was very disappointed that after choosing a class that seemed like it would be spell focused I instead found myself relying on the basic attack. I gave the first boss a good couple of tries and even got close to beating it, and I decided it just didn't feel fun or rewarding enough for me to continue. I wasn't looking forward to stutter-stepping my way through the game and grinding for free heal items that seem necessary for victory.The art style looks nice, though I don't like how monotone everything seems. This also felt like an issue with the telegraphing of enemy attacks. The music and sound design seemed competent, though nothing special. At the character selection there were 4 distinct portraits that looked cool, which was part of the reason I went for the Stargazer, though the in game character model looked very generic, like I had chosen a combat class.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I started out enjoying the game enough, but the more you play it, the more problems become apparent. It's clearly trying to be to Bloodborne what Blasphemous is to Dark Souls, but it lacks the polish that Blasphemous had. I think where this is most apparent is in the combat. Simply put, it is sluggish. Your character moves around like they have a brick in their pants and the controls just feel unresponsive. Arial combat/attacking anything in the air is just absurd as there don't appear to be air combos of any kind. For a bird enemy, you just have to jump, get a single slash in, and then repeat until they are dead.Furthermore, there are a variety of annoyances. Misses coming from and enemies attacking you from off screen, enemies stacked so tightly upon one another that it looks like you are only facing one when in reality you could be facing three, arbitrary enemy behaviors. Sometimes you will attack three times and it will stun an enemy long enough for you to kill them, while other times it shrugs off your attacks like nothing and slash at you, even though it's the exact same enemy.Speaking of enemies, it feels like many times the game has gone for a quantity over quality approach as far as they are concerned. The enemies don't seem to get harder as the game goes on, there are just more of them, with some mobs being reused in high level areas with the only change to them being a slight color swap and an increased health bar.The visuals are alright and if you REALLY like the gothic art style then you will enjoy them, but again, when compared to other Metroidvania style games, the visuals/art style just seems rather plain.Simply put, this is a VERY poor man's Blasphemous. If you absolutely adore Metroidvania style games and need your fix, buy this one when it's on sale, but if you go into this game expecting the quality that Hollow Knight or Blasphemous had, then you are going to be disapointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure where all the undo hate for this game comes from. It's a reasonable Metroidvania game for those people wanting something with a Bloodborne vibe. Yes, it covers most of the same bases and hits the same notes in terms of story, but it captures a fantastic tone of gloom and mystery. The game play is solid and easily accessible. It's is reasonably challenging but able to be overcome with some practice, so if you are looking for a difficult challenge perhaps look elsewhere. The sprite work and pixel art is lovely and makes me curious what else this world can offer. 7.5-8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if it's just me but this game reminds me a lot of Blasphemous, from the level design to lore similarity. Of course The Last Faith is a way better metroidvania than Blasphemous, and yet the way the dev handles level designs feels like an outdated formula. Not to mention the infamous "blood vial" system from Bloodborne, already two major flaws affect the gameplay experience. Fortunately, the boss fights are very fun to fight, and the stylish weapons are not just for show. Due to the reasons above, I have never been this torn about whether I recommend it or not. If you have no issues towards the problems I mentioned above, then The Last Faith is a good Bloodborne-inspired pixelated metroidvania to pick up.Fighting mutated beasts seems to be the main focus when it comes to boss design, and the dev does a great job at it. There is always a sense of spectacle involved in each bosses. From the giant skeletal beast that can summon dark meteors, to the dual bosses that each possess one element and their movesets complent each other, every fight is a wonderful dance between each phase. Their attacks are well-telegraphed, and the visuals as well as the  style are nothing to scoff at. The dev also keeps player's progression in mind and scales all these bosses' health accordingly. As a result, players won't easily steamroll the bosses when overleveled. The thrill of conquering the strong foe will always stay.This is certainly the case of quality over quantity. Even though there are only a handful of weapons and spells in the game, their usefulness and charm outweigh the problem. They not only have  gorgeous and haunting icons, the abilities attached are also the real deal. Some skills allow the weapon to transform temporarily, like the starting weapon Nightfall Blade: it extends and becomes a spear when activated; Others contain a well-done animation, cover more grounds, and deal a lot of damage in the process, like Ethereal Great Blade: a lunge, an explosion, and finishing things off with a rock blast. Spells also feel good to use. Each of them has different property that allows the player to combo with the right weapon for the best result. Something worth noting is that it is really satisfying to hurl spells at some of the giant bosses. They may not deal lots of damage, but sound effect and the visuals really make you feel like you've done something wonderful.→Excellent pixel artstyle.→Decent voice-acting.→Item description actually incorporates lores, just like Souls-like.→Thanks God there's no contact damage.→: Breaking several locks to open the sealed door is a common level design as old as time. It's fine to have it, but overdoing it often makes gameplay dull. The Last Faith, sadly, has multiple levels that are just "doing x amount of stuff to open the lock". Breaking the chains to lift the sealed gate is good for letting the player do some exploration. This is fine for introduction. It is not fine to do the exact same thing on many separate occasions. The only difference is what you need to do open the locked door: snuff off five burning brazier, collect four mirror pieces, kill four VIPs, etc.→: This is the most annoying part of the game. The dev really enjoys putting ranged enemies at the edge of the platform to mildly annoy the player. What's worse is that most of the time there will be traps or other environmental hazards besides these platforms.→: This is a hot take. I feel like this design in particular is outdated. Getting key abilities after defeating certain bosses makes the level leading to said bosses boring. The Last Faith suffers this problem. The level often feels like narrow corridors connecting with each other. Even if you eventually acquire the ability, the level itself doesn't feel like it is designed to encourage the player to use the new ability.→I will never understand how could anyone see the "blood vial" system in Bloodborne and thought it was a good idea. →The band-aid change to address the issue above only works for bosses.→Stigmas and charms are lacking in quantity and novelty.→I wish you could still use the weapon skill even when you run out of mana.→Bombs and powders feel underwhelming.→Lacking more items to collect, the reward for exploration feels unsatisfying.→Ye old Thesaurus dialogue writing.→Hiding crucial ability behind shop defeats the purpose of metroidvania.中文小簡評→這款有諸多問題，真的很猶豫該不該推。→優劣權衡後，我覺得還是值得一玩，如果玩完其他類銀河系惡魔城還覺得意猶未盡的話，再用特價買吧。→哥德式點陣畫風非常耐看。→王戰打起來特別好玩，每個Boss設計很有特色，特別是大型怪。→武器與法術雖然不多，但每項不僅好看，實用性也頗高。→沒有接觸傷害真的是謝天謝地。→配音不錯聽。→難得看到其他類魂遊戲認真在道具敘述上寫典故。→遊戲系統選單沒有調畫質與解析度的選項。→關卡設計缺乏新意，同樣開鎖的設定換皮重複用了好幾次。→製作團隊很喜歡放遠程敵人在跳台上搞玩家，跳台前又喜歡放即死陷阱或環境危害。→這個比較偏個人看法：我覺得把關鍵技能放在王後容易讓王前關卡的探索變得相對乏味。→怎麼會有人覺得血緣詛咒的血瓶系統會是個好主意……→製作團隊亡羊補牢的一技僅限王前中繼點。→徽章與護符數量少且沒啥特色。→希望武器戰技沒魔的時候能繼續用，降低傷害和效果。→炸彈跟各式buff武器的道具沒啥威力。→用字遣詞隱晦生澀不會讓你聽起來很有哲理。→把重要技能放在商店裡是類銀河系惡魔城一大禁忌啊！

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't too bad, but I wouldn't recommend it because of so many annoying little things, like1. You can't shoot or cast spell when jumping even though there are flying enemies in this game2. You can't attack while ducking, some small enemies are amazingly hard to hit because of this3. Enemies' health is so much inflated, to kill an enemy you need to hit attack button 5 times, rolling away to dodge enemies' attacks, then close in and hit the attack button 5 times again4. To block enemies' attack you need to hit 2 buttons (in other games you usually have to hit only 1 button). This makes blocking super annoying, so it's better to roll with 1 button5. You die instantly when falling into chasm. Wanna check if there's a secret area down there? Nope, there's no secret area, now die! Slightly miss timing your jump? Go back to the last check point!Not sure if it gets better in the later part of the game, but it's too boring to continue

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited for this for a long time and it does not disappoint. It is a little bit easier than Blasphemous (which is not a bad thing really) and I like the setting more too. Just met the third boss and I cannot wait to see what game has for me in the next levels. It works on a steam deck as a charm.EDIT: After 13 hours of gameplay I must say that it is getting better and better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a solid 9.5/10. Only thing lacking is more content (though there is quite a lot already).The gameplay is pretty crisp and mostly responsive (dodging sometimes feels weird, but it's probably a timing issue on my end). The only negative I could point to is that the game uses either the D-Pad or Analogue stick for movement - Which really sucks since I would rather use the D-Pad to move. This means that I have to switch items with the analogue stick which just doesn't work. I think this could easily be solved with a different set of controls since the Souls games are clearly able to handle that.The Metroidvania element is definitely there. It's pretty much the same as Blasphemous in some ways (Even the graphics are similar). Pretty good backtracking overall. I rarely felt lost and even got the True Ending by myself. The weapon upgrades are also pretty straightforward and convenient. Only 2 different "ore" types and you really only need 1 type. 3 "Blueprints" must be found to be able to fully upgrade a weapon, which is just so clean in my opinion. No need to find various different +Tiers of upgrading material all over the world (as seen in souls games).Some quests/dialogue are a bit confusing though. It's obviously deliberate, but I honestly wouldn't mind the important text being highlighted - If it is important. To illustrate: Two separate quests said something about going to a certain location. One of them didn't seem to tell me anything important, and was pretty much fully complete. The other one had, in my opinion, easily the best spell in the game. I didn't think that the quest wasn't over yet since you are given a spell and the NPC is gone (And you also receive an achievement on Steam). Perhaps it would be too on-the-nose for some, but I'd prefer that slight bit of clarity.If you've enjoyed Blasphemous, you'll most likely enjoy this game. I could compare it to games like Bloodborne since it obviously borrows from it, but it's just too different. It's closer to Blasphemous in so many ways. Helps that it's also a 2D Metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, to be honest.  A great mashup of bloodborne themes and metroidvania elements.  Combat is well done, feels good.  There is that element of backtracking and retracing forcing you to get to know the maps.  I wish they gave players color dots instead of 4 chosen symbols only to mark your map though.  Also I was lost once due to a major story path being locked behind stumbling on an NPC in a previous area that had nothing before.. that was annoying but could have been my fault? Anywho I wasnt sure at first and wanted to hate and ended up loving it.  Long time souls guy with a bagillion hours and have played all these type of games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I managed to hate-finish the game hoping it was going to be rewarding, but the story still feels like I'm missing a chapter or two in the middle. I went from killing speechless monsters to being called "the problem" by intelligent abominations all of a sudden. The game looks great but the actual gameplay is janky. The hitboxes on yourself and enemies are just way off sometimes, you get hit by things that clearly missed you completely. Some enemies have practical cheat or spam abilities that if you get caught by them just absolutely ruin you. I felt most of the time I was just brute forcing my way through the game instead of using finesse or skill. Just take a buttload of damage and heal it off if I can.The elemental debuffs are probably the most unfair thing of all: they're easily applied and REALLY hamper you. Burning not only takes off health, it gives you a slight hit that interrupts you, so its difficult to even cure it. Nightmare absolutely does a lot of damage and reverses your controls when fully applied. Electrocution paralyzes you every couple seconds. These effects are ON TOP of the damage tick they do.Until they tune some of this stuff, I can't see it being any fun of a game for someone other than a player looking for a stubborn Metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMENDEDA well-designed metroidvania with souls-like aspects with a Bloodborne-inspired theme.  Beautiful art design, fluid motion controls, and a lot of different play styles. This is not a perfect game as I do feel that the balance needs a little tweaking. Animation delays when trying to use an item after attacking can also prove to be challenging. _childDocuments_.review: This is a review after completing the game with 100% achievements.Q. What is the genre? A. A hybrid metroidvania and souls lite. If Lies of P was a mixture of Bloodborne and Sekiro, The Last Faith is a blend of Blasphemous and Bloodborne. If you haven't touched any metroidvania, or FromSoftware games this game might be more difficult as it has some git gud elements.Q. What are the nitpicks for this game?A. It takes time getting used to the movement as the protagonist likes to glide. This is a game that requires methodical approach and preparation especially in combat areas and boss rooms. The map, intended or not, is very sluggish. That one boss,  The filter on the voice is almost tangible I feel like ripping it out like Eryk does when he does executions.Q. Do you recommend this game?A. As much as Lies of P is its own thing, The Last Faith is faithful to itself and is its own unique take on the genre. I highly recommend it for those who are more into stylized animation, combat focused, and pixel enjoyers. I get the same vibe as Prince of Persia (1989) movement wise.Blasphemous and The Last Faith could be in the same world in two different continents.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very surprised at how high quality this game is compared to the reception behind it. I've been seeing reviews with the oddest complaints.Similar to Blasphemous? Not really. In Blasphemous you have one character that has a pretty linear leveling path.Last Faith has a wide variety of builds and tons of different weapons with a variety of different scaling options to suit your play style. I immediately booted the game up again upon beating it to try a whole new play style. My first run was a Dex/Mind spell blade who meshes awesome spells in with melee. Now I'm playing a Str/Instinct hybrid and trying other weapons and strategies.Then there's the gfx looking similar. Yes, when you have a game that is going for a certain style it will look like another. No one says anything when it comes to 3D assets in games always looking similar but for some reason people get more fussy when it's pixels. It's a style, and it doesn't belong to Blasphemous.People complaining about clunky combat... What? Are we playing the same game? I was doing all sorts of attack cancels, rolls, weaving spells into my combos and all manners of wild and cool stuff between spells, guns, and weapons. Are people just maxing strength, swinging the big sword and then saying combat is boring? Obviously it's going to be boring when you approach it that way.The game is also nonlinear. I managed tool explore a whole part of the game while missing out on an entirely different spot only to find it later. The game does reward exploration and there's plenty of it.The music is very good, the save room theme haunts me in my sleep... In a good way. The set pieces that accompany the locales in this game also set the mood perfectly alongside the variety of areas to explore. Some idiot on IGN said everything is a house or a city? That guy is an idiot and probably only played for 2 hours.Theres a swamp, icy caverns, moody churches, a mansion of mirrors, a sprawling Gothic city and more. This game is very pleasant to the eye and a joy to explore.Wanna know what my complaints are? Enemy variety. Not even a huge deal, should've had a few more pallete swap enemies though (here's a enemy design philosophy you could've stole from Blasphemous lol). It was annoying to always see those homeless dudes with the knife charging at me in like every area past the ice cavern. Maybe have like elemental versions of this enemy, have different elements and colors form more enemies. Def can be implemented just use the hue slider in photo shop to change their colors and add some elements to their attacks.But the enemies and bosses especially are all well designed and fun to fight, just wish there was a bit more variety sometimes with some specific fodder types.Other complaint, please put a mark on the map for lost exp. It wasn't hard for me to mark the spot myself, but this is a standard QoL feature that should be here too.Other than that, this game kicks ass.It's not Blasphemous, it's The Last Faith... Amen. PS: I love Blasphemous too, but stop acting like this isn't a gem too just because they both exist in the same space.

_childDocuments_.review: "Oh this game is totally 2D Bloodborne! Look at the gun and the setting!"FOOLS! This game is not Bloodborne-like! I struggle to even call it a soulslike! It's even better! After 18 years, we finally have a spiritual sequel to the Castlevania: Sorrow series!Here we see Soma Cruz, all grown up, graduated, living abroad, and has fully embraced his high school goth phase, as he is now wearing all dark clothing, as opposed to his trademark white trench coat. He also stopped bleaching his head, which is a nice touch. Also, apparently wherever he lives has a bad problem with people farting, because his shirt collar is perpetually glued to the bridge of his nose. (That or he's still ashamed with how he looked in the DS game. I wouldn't blame him). Just to put it all together, he legally had his name changed to Eryk LastFaith (catchy ring for a single man, ya know?)Following the events of Dawn of Sorrow, it is apparent that his high school sweetheart, Mina, straight up dumped his ass, and left him in a state of depression. (Again, probably because of how he looked on DS) So what does he do? What every JRPG protagonist does when they so much as stub their toe: Set out on a quest, take anything that isn't nailed down, and kill everything that has a face; up to, and ESPECIALLY, God.Following that, just for good measure, and because he's done this in the previous Sorrow games already, He decides God wasn't good enough, and goes after God's twin mothers, and then kills THEIR God just for good measure! Damn, Soma! You SCARY!Rating: Now stop calling it 2D Bloodborne/10

As a lone warrior on a quest for redemption, you traverse hauntingly beautiful landscapes filled with perilous foes and ancient secrets. The combat is intense and satisfying, requiring both skillful timing and strategic thinking to overcome the horrors that lurk in the shadows. The game's dark and atmospheric visuals, accompanied by a haunting soundtrack, immerse you fully in its grim and foreboding world. The narrative is rich and deeply engaging, weaving together themes of faith, sacrifice, and the eternal struggle between light and darkness. Every encounter and discovery feels meaningful, driving you forward in your quest for truth and salvation. Despite a few technical hiccups, The Last Faith delivers an unforgettable experience that will leave a lasting impression. Highly recommended for fans of atmospheric action-adventure games with a dark twist.

_childDocuments_.review: While I wish I could talk about this game without talking about Blasphemous, certain design and enemy choices while require me too. Let me stat off by saying this is a great game. I played it through to the end and back tracked for most of the extras on a sizable first play through (15 hours).Pros:This game has really cool world design. It's nothing ground breaking or genre defying, but it's nice to see a darker color palette and architecture direction. This game was clearly inspired by Bloodborne and Blasphemous which are both the titans of their respective genres. The different elements are spells were fun and having access to multiple different weapons for replay-ability is refreshing when you're usually tied to 1 or 2 weapons. The game is also fully voice acted which is surprising for a pixel metroidvania.Cons:While this game is definitely inspired by Blasphemous, it dips into the category of copying it a few too many times. There are some bosses & enemies that are a straight rip from Blasphemous when you notice their attacks. There's also several bosses in this game that are reused 2, and sometimes 3 times. Not sure why they decided to keep instant death pits and falls in this game, as its more frustrating than anything. There were a few times where it wasn't very clear where the next objective was and whenever I died there was no marker on the map to find my souls which caused a loss of souls more often than not.Other than that, hats off to the small team of developers for making a full, complete game with pretty pixel art, fun combat choices, and secrets to discover. If you liked Blasphemous, Bloodborne, or any of the Steams tags you'll like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of Metroidvanias and Bloodborne, I was so hyped for this game. After beating it twice I can say that this is one of my favorite games of the genre. Despite this however, there are a few problems with the game; both some minor and major ones, but nothing too game breaking. PROS: - Great combat- Amazing Music (better that I thought it would turn out.)- Great, but challenging boss design- Art style is translated well into the 2D sprite work, looking every detailed- Save points are place around fairly. No save point feels too far away or too close- Build options and weapons allow for trying out new weapons and encourages multiple playthroughs.CONS:- While combat is fluid and great, dodge rolling/back stepping has a slight delay in-between actions. Essentially, when you dodge, you can't do so again immediately. You can get used to it, but it does fell awkward and kind of an odd choice. Other Metroidvanias have quick and responsive dodging mechanics that it feels like a oversight or poor decision to make dodging somewhat restrictive.- For people that love to complete every inch of every room, it's not currently possible as some rooms have ceilings too to reach; even with all movements abilities unlocked, so your map will look incomplete. I'm not sure how the % counter save completion progress. Hopefully they address this issue in a future patch. As a tip, use the right analog stick to look up and down for things like jumping when trying to fill out rooms on the map as looking either way counts are you exploring these areas too high.- Back to the map, there are visual errors that make you think you haven't completely finished exploring a room. These occur with rooms that take place outside (bridges, cities, etc,) will not have a white border around the top like the rest of the map, making it look like you missed reaching the top. Ignore this. It you see a clean cut off on the top of the room in the map, you've finished that room. Also certain rooms will look like there is another room underneath them. This too is a visual error. These are mostly happens with rooms that have bridges to cross. - For achievement hunters, be aware there are bugs that will prevent you from earning certain achievements. From experience, the boss ||Old Wymond|| drops an item that is needed to not only unlock all spells, but to also complete a quest for ||Lady Dorothea||. It doesn't happen all the time, but sometimes the item won't drop when he is killed, making this achievement impossible to earn unless you start a new playthrough. There are other bosses that drop the same item, but this bug doesn't seem to affect them. I believe the devs said something about adding a NG+ mode in the future.- There are builds you can have, but its so unbalanced to the point where it feels like there is only one build you can have (Strength) and the other don't even exist. Don't take it as there are no builds to make; they definitely do exist.Despite this, I trust they will address these issues in a future update. I fully recommend this game to people trying to scratch that gothic horror/Bloodborne itch.
