_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game but there's a lot of odd design choices that would make this excessively bizarre for metroidvania fans and souls fans alike. Small quality of life issues which feel like they should be changed or addressed as it severely hurts the gameplay.The primary problem is that boss HP is exceptionally spongy. I'm talkin your weapon is a butterknife and you need to cut through a concrete wall sort of spongy. Even with a weapon upgraded as far as you can get it, enemy defenses and HP pools tend to increase at an exponential rate. Because you upgrade your weapons in the souls-like fashion (getting an applicable + level and stats) it can make some progression feel unnecessarily grindy. Expect to spend at least a good 5~10 minutes hacking away unless you've powerleveled yourself to some obscure peak with some sort of glitch becauseFarming in this game is bullocks. You need tens of thousands of ingame currency to upgrade a single weapon and that takes a long, long time to even get. Need to respec because your gameplay philosophy isn't the same? Well expect to spend half an hour making that weapon endgame. At least respec is just paid for after acquiring a certain item.You can't aim up, you can't crouch attack.  Yet there are a plethora of enemies in the air, and enemies who's attacks you can duck under. There also isn't a slide...I'm sorry Castlevania fans...You have at least a second of downtime for some reason before you can dodge again. I don't know why it's so long but it feels like it's on a timer that's far, far longer than it has to be.Mobility of your character is extremely subpar for how large the map is. Wanna explore? Hope you have your evening cleared out. Unless you're using a guide it's gonna take you that long to backtrack as you watch your guy saunter-march at the speed of smell.If you play Instinct, enjoy spending excess time leveling up firearms and buying bullets to always run out of ammo mid-fight with no way of getting more then proceed to flounder about spamming the attack button doing 1/3rd the average damage of a Dex or Str build. Even Mind build does better. Can't really main that stat because the game disagrees with it.The game is awesome if you can ignore these or mitigate them somehow. However, I feel like the devs need to have a real sit down and decide what they actually want to do.

_childDocuments_.review: The animation style really captures the SOTN vibe for me. Music is good, if a little repetitive, and the voice acting is quite good as well. The story is typical obtuse dark souls fare. Gameplay is addictive once you get accustomed to the controls. The key here is the exploration. At first, it starts out somewhat linear, but then at some point, you realize there's multiple threads at once. Lots of little collectibles that unlock secret items, that type of thing. Where I wish there was more substance, was the descriptions of the stats. For the most part, it's straightforward, but it would be nice to know upfront instead of guessing. The audio quality can at times also be a bit jarring. For example, walking from one room to another, footsteps suddenly get loud and a bit tinny sounding, like the reverb effect is too strong. It's not overly distracting, but it is noticeable. The map is a bit bland. It would be nice to have more detail on what type of lock is on the door. Is it a regular key? Maybe a lever lock? Or do I need a specific ability? These details would prevent so much unnecessary backtracking. It's also a bit unclear what is an elevator and what isn't. Having some additional visual design, like say dotted lines or something, would help players navigate. All in all, this is a solid 7.5/10. It feels like a proper tribute to SOTN in all the right ways. If you liked that game,  chances are good that you'll enjoy this as well.

_childDocuments_.review: For now it's a no for me. There is nothing egregiously wrong here, it's all small things that contribute as a whole dissatisfaction in the experience, maybe the game don't start with it's best cards?. I'm a big fan of all of the inspiration that this game references (castlevania, Bloodborne, Blasphemous) and of the metroidvania genre, yet here all seems shallow. Beautiful backgrounds with nothing to do in it. I found myself simply passing through scenarios with simplistic (if any) platform layout, one or two enemies and that's it?. The combat didn't also cut it for me, i mean i can bypass all the map problems if the combat it's good, but even here terrible first impression. The attacks are very basic with very little flare to it. i choose the "gunslinger" archetype and shooting it's locked in a straight line? i mean it's -ok- it's a design choice not a bad thing in on itself, but then you immediately present me with dogs i cannot shoot and flying enemies i cannot shoot?. it feels like the enemies are calibrated for another combat system kinda? again nothing "wrong" per se, it's serviceable, but being serviceable isn't enough with the other problems. The writing it's also -fine-, it's ok, it's dark, moody soulslike dialogue that here, i don't know, they talk too much for saying so little. I've played basically any metroidvania you can think of, and i get that the genre takes time to get really going (even hollow knight has ONE attack and a basic jump at the beginning) but every other game has "something" that makes them stand out. Here i found sadly a collage of other ideas that on paper are basically made for me and my taste but severely lack something. And that's a shame because the art is gorgeous.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were to mesh Castlevania with Bloodborne, this is the 2D version you would get. I took my time and highly recommend if you enjoy those kinds of games. It has guns. Most feel similar to ones used in Bloodborne. The weapon selection is pretty good, although it could use more weapons. I enjoyed trying each weapons special abilities. Yes, there is magic. I used a little and enjoyed what I was able to use. I could see a full magic build obliterating the game. There are throwable bombs too. I thought the level layout was done well. There are secret areas, bosses, hidden walls, and shortcuts you can open up. I enjoyed the fact fast travel was there from the beginning. Where the game could use some polish for example is when buying items, there is no option to hold down the button to select the qty. which would speed up the selection. This needs to be changed. Bosses at times felt a bit easy. I think if there were option added, it would help those that need more of a challenge or those that want less. I would like to see a NG +. It needs more map option markers. I ran out. The music in the game was stellar. I really set the mood for each area. At times it reminds me of Bloodbornes music. Overall, one of the better Metroidvania games. 8.5/10 if we are giving a score rating. 39 hours to complete for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so this is going to be a very critical positive review.  And I want to be clear ahead of time that this is a okay game, but it's also disappointing because I feel like it could have been so much better.  It's for this reason that I have so many issues.One thing that I think needs some serious looking at is being able to access the Frozen Caverns right after beating Hermann.  I was having such a hard time understanding the huge difficulty spike and nearly impossible platforming until I got well past the second bonfire and ran across a jump I simply couldn't make without some kind of double jump.  I wasted so much time, so much effort, and lost a ton of souls ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around in this area I wasn't even supposed to be in.  It was frustrating to the point where I was considering refunding the game.  And I play a ton of Souls-likes.The inability to pause is also questionable.  The reason the Souls series didn't do that was because there was an always online component to them.  In Last Faith, there isn't.  So why have this?  And what's even better is that one thing they didn't keep in was quitting out.  Resting is a hard save, and if you quit out in the middle of exploration, you lose all progress since the last time you rested.  And what's the deal with not being able to use items from the menu?  Like, you can't use anything without first putting it on the hotbar.There are blind jumps all over the game that will get you either hurt or killed.  There are platforms that if you jump to them, you have no other option than to just kill yourself because you can't get back.  And again, quitting out isn't an option.  And the devs seem to have this thing with loving ranged enemies.  It feels like half the time, you're dealing with a mini bullet hell, and it doesn't feel good.As far as the metroidvania side of things go, I really felt like the trickle of skills was really slow, and there are far too many areas, doors, and ledges to realistically keep track of, and the things I did happen to remember or mark on the map were incredibly hit and miss on if it was even worth the time to backtrack for.  Also, not getting double jump until basically the end of the game was... a choice.Despite ALL this, the game still manages to be a decent experience.  Combat was mostly fun, and definitely challenging.  I do like that, despite there being so few weapons (compared to other souls-likes), they were all very different from one another.  The game looks great and the soundtrack, while not very memorable, was atmospheric and was a more ambient compliment to the game.  And even if the devs never changed anything, it would probably still be worth playing through.  But I would love to see this go from an okay game to a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is, personally, a 8/10. It's quite easy to get into, has a beautiful victorian setting and visuals in gorgeous pixel art, is a nice take on a "soulsborne-metroidvania" concept, has it's challenging moments, brutal finishers, a good variety of weapons and spells for a 2D pixel game (with their own sprites and animations), a good variety of enemies and bosses, and good tracks in the OST. It's a well-rounded game in the genre.It has it's flaws, but they don't soil the overall experience.Issues in enemy/boss combat, rare annoying bugs, guns and spells feel underwhelming, pitfalls don't make sense, some bosses feel "too easy", some areas are "too short", no alert for the "point of no return" and the lore feels shallow and disconnected. It's like there's still stuff that should've been there but will come in DLC.Still, don't give up on it because of comments like "it's trash because it's not like Blasphemous or Bloodborne" (wonderful games, do also play them) or "it's too easy". It's a diamond with rough spots, but with lots of potential.* Tips for the game:- HIT THE WALLS;- Kill the smaller enemies first;- Use the arrows (camera) in open areas to check for items and hazards (seriously, it helps);- Don't upgrade every weapon. Focus on one that fit's your playstyle or build;- Min-max is the way to go for better DPS and survivability;- Want an "easy-normal game? Go Warrior (Strength + Vitality), because "unga-bunga" tanks better, kills better and scales better;- Want an "normal-hard" game? Go Rogue (Dexterity + Whatever your heart desires), because it's a hard early to a "balanced" late game;- Want that "Hardest/"Oh, sh*t!" game? Go Mage or Gunslinger (Mind/Instinct), because you'll only get proper stuff and damage post 50-70% of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to revise this review after finishing a lot of the content. I initially was disappointed with the lack of weapons and combat in the game but some of it can get a bit better as the game progresses forward. I would describe it as a 2D bloodborne type game.Pros:- Good pixel art- Some interesting designed enemies and bosses- Various spell type skills- The special skills for primary weapons can be useful and fun to use and it can also chain combo.- Able to execute enemies for focus- A lot of content and secrets. - Map is designed well, immersive, and areas interconnect well- Boss rooms are fairly close to checkpoints- Few more weapons, better upgrades, and skills later in the game.Cons:- Combat: This is the most frustrating out of everything. You get locked into an animation when attacking except when you use dodge to roll. There are no rolling attacks. You cannot aim your sidearm at all, shoot in the air, or even crouch to shoot lower enemies. There are no other combo attacks when jumping in the air. The parry is super janky, it has a meter for limited uses, and you need to activate two buttons to execute it. There is a special skill for the primary weapon that uses a focus meter and you can do a charged attack but the focus meter is limited depending on how many points invested in it. There are some fun spell skills but unless you invest in the skill points to the focus bar, it's very limited use. Overall, the combat feels pretty clunky. It's much more bearable using certain strength weapons though like the greatsword. I cannot speak for the other dexterity ones or mind/instinct.-Grinding: I felt like I needed to grind a lot to get a lot of needed weapon upgrades and to upgrade enough levels. Put a lot of points into vitality or get one-two shot.-Skill Level Tree: There is no way currently to reset the skill tree to try different builds- Weapons: Only found 1 strength weapon for my class and only had the starting firearm in the first 4 to 5 hours then finally got the greatsword. The other weapons are found a lot later in the game and they are limited. I only had the greatsword and the final strength weapon towards the end of the game and a couple other useful sidearms. So three total primary strength weapons-Settings: You cannot re-bind your controller nor adjust any graphic settings.-World Environment: The game starts off reasonable but certain parts of the maps are super frustrating. There are parts were you can get electrocuted, bleed, and frozen easily and the status effects are at least 30 seconds which is frustrating. The icicles that fall regenerate themselves in the frozen area and it doesn't help with all the enemies thrown in.-No NG+ With everything said, I still would only recommend buying if on sale, if they patch and add more weapon content, or if you really need another metroid souls-type game to play.  I was not really into the story (seemed average) but this game could be much better if some of the combat is modified and more weapons added earlier on. Hopefully some of these issues will be patched in the future and more content will be added.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game today with a STR character build.In general, a very well made game, i encounter almost no bugs throughout the game, the gameplay was fun, lore was interesting, music was average, and sometimes control can be a little clunky, but overall i give it a solid 8-8.3 for the game overall.However, there are some things that are not quite balanced about the game, and i'm sure they will fix it in the upcoming patches, but i'll list them here if you wanted to try the game.- STR build is the most OP build currently, there's a sword that's mental, and you can found it fairly early in the game. And upgrading in this game doesn't require a lot of resources (the stones required can be found quite easily throughout the area, plus, you can buy it from the upgrade merchant.), you can get overpowered fairly early with couple of upgrades on the weapon.- There's balancing issues about the other non related STR weapons throughout the game, i believe other builds are fairly under-powered.- one thing that annoys me the most >> there are a lot of running in this game. There's no "return to the last bonfire rested" option in the game yet. Maybe they will add it in the future, maybe they will not, i kind of get where they're coming from because there's plenty of checkpoints (bonfires) spread throughout the area, however, still, when you require to backtrack to some area because you got new unlocked abilities that can make you reach certain items or area that are unreachable before, you have to run to the area, and then run all the way back to the checkpoint, with all enemies re-spawned (just by touching the checkpoint in this game, will make all enemies re-spawn, there's no "rest" button.)- no new game plus option yet, they said they will be adding it in the future, i would like to try some other builds, but i think it's not re-playable currently.But again, a very solid game, that maybe better to be played when patches came to fix the couple of balancing issues.recommended tho!

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts with a pop up telling you that A is jump and then tells you that X is attack. But, never once does it say how to equip and use healing items. I'm fine if the game wants me to just learn as I go, but then why in the world would you give me such an obvious pop up about A being jump. A is always jump. But, knowing how to heal would have made that first boss significantly easier. The pixel art is good, the voice acting is alright. But, it just comes across as too try hard. It just seems like the gothic aesthetic is just for the sake of being edgy, not because it's actually a creative decision like with Blasphemous. Also, the fact that so many boss attacks have a huge area of effect around where they actually hit is not cool. The point of learning boss attacks is watching their attack, but how am I supposed to predict where there will be huge damage spikes in addition to where their weapon hits except by being hit by it a bunch of times. Also, instant death spike pits all over the place for almost every jump? In a souls-like? No thanks.The fact that you have to travel to a quest giver to level up instead of just at every save point is just extra busy work.Just nothing comes together with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed the game on Kickstarter and I'm glad I did. If you like Metroidvanias like Blasphemous and/or 2D Souls-likes, this is a great pick for you. It's easily on par with Blasphemous in terms of combat, bosses, visuals and level design, maybe even better at times (seriously, this game is absolutely gorgeous). The story is whatever, but I'll be honest and say that I never cared about that in any game similar to that, so it didn't bother me at all. If anything, it's at least a bit easier to understand and less weird and nebulous than, say, Blasphemous. Side-quests and secrets are also less obnoxiously obtuse, while still requiring investigation and careful exploration.I played before the big patch, and even then I had absolutely zero bug the whole time (almost unheard of nowadays...) and I found the combat and difficulty to be fairly well balanced. I'd say some mid-game bosses are possibly harder than later ones, but the couple of bosses near the end were by no mean trivial.A lot of people complain about the "blood vial" system borrowed from Bloodborne, and... well, I get it. In Bloodborne it didn't bother me and I never really ran out because they dropped frequently from enemies and I always spent the leftover blood echoes on topping up my vials. In The Last Faith, I feel the drop rate isn't quite as generous, which sucks. That said, if you do the "spend your leftover currency on a bunch of vials" regularly, you should be fine. I completely ran out exactly once, against a fairly difficult mid-game boss, but it only took a few minutes to farm a bit of Nycrux to buy a big stack of healing injections, and then I trounced the boss first try (go figure). So, overall not as bad as I feared, and you shouldn't let that stop you from trying this game.I will say that guns could be a bit better, early on they aren't bad as ranged support, but they quickly become middling and there's not much point in upgrading them. Perhaps the balance patch helps, though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: If you love 2D souls-likes or are a fan of metroidvanias, then this game is a must have! Really enjoyed the journey and was extremely satisfied with my time spent in The Last Faith. There are a ton of really sick weapons depending on how you want to play, but after I found my big greatsword I stuck with that! The firearms are cool and the custom executions were awesome as well. The world feels huge and with there not being a linear path, you can end up in areas that you are not supposed to be in yet. Being able to mark on your map where items/doors/locations are that you need to backtrack to is a great quality of life feature. There is a nice variety of magic spells to play with as well. If you enjoy creepy NPCs with their own questlines, plenty of hidden areas to uncover, and an awesome art style; then you’ll love exploring this game. I’m a big fan of the dark atmosphere this game has, kind of reminds me of Bloodborne/Castlevania. Once you get your character to the right level and keep your weapon leveled, the bosses aren’t as big of a challenge. With that said, I loved the design of every boss, especially the hidden ones. There are achievements that you can get locked out of if you progress the story too far without meeting questline requirements but a lot of the cheevos come naturally. In the future, an NG+ feature would be a great addition to wrap up any missed achievements that you miss. Overall, this game is really solid and is an insanely fun time!Achievement Count: 53Time to 100%: ~25hrsDifficulty: ★★★✩✩Genre of Game: Metroidvania, Souls-like, Pixel GraphicsFun Rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: on the surface this seems like a solid metroidvania with a splash of soulsborne, and if that was the goal the developer succeeded. issuesBalance - 1. Monsters are literal HP sponges - it takes 10+ hits to down a target as a caster. you will find yourself skipping 60-70% of enemies in this game due to how frustruatingly much effort it takes to kill things until basically endgame as a caster. 2. Caster builds blow until end game. the only viable caster weapons with decen scaling are located behind a hidden boss  at the 75% point of the game3. MP Costs are absurd, and you cant afford to spam them, ironically untill the end of the game. 4. HP/MP/Focus are all increased substantially when defeating a handful of specific bosses. this makes any effort to level HP a waste of stats - with 20 Hp stat, you'll tank any boss hit just fine for the entire game. 5. theres no reliable way to recover MP other than costly consumables, of which only the weakest  ones are available for limitless purchase. 6. STR cant even compete with dexterity by end game - nothing can not even casting. 7. far too much backtracking. the developer thought it would be a great idea to make every zone have items that can only be gotten with double jump. Double jump is convieniently only unlocked after defeating the **THIRD TO LAST BOSS IN THE SECOND TO LAST AREA**.8. No "return to last rest point" item, making backtracking an exceptionally tedious and frustrating endeavor. if you plan to do any backtracking you might as well just spend all of your souls, and then take a face first dive into a spike pit or chasam. 9. combat is janky and unresponsive. theres an invisible 1 second cooldown on dodge rolls that just make it frustrating to play, and the air dash shares a cooldown with the dodge roll. Plot - its just not a very good plot at all. it tries to explain things, but falls short, and fails to explain too little in the way a souls game would. its like reading a half finished book which ends with  AND THEN THEY ALL F#$%&* out of nowhere. length -Pathetically short. Game isnt even 10 hours long unless you specifically go for every single objective possible. i was able to do 99% of the trophies in a 19 hour play. the only trophy that is missing is one that was blocked due to a bug causing a monster to not spawn. Features - No NG+ is a big downer - now i have to do an entire fresh game from start to get that one single achievement preventing me from 100%.   TL/DR: This is only worth it for the most diehard metroidvania fans on the planet. 5/10 game - its pretty,. but has a lot of issues. Most of these could probably be fixed with some TLC in the future, but as it is now  i wouldnt buy this as a normie.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't know where all the hate for this game is coming from. Maybe it was buggy on release and got fixed before I bought it? About 34 hours of gameplay, decent enemy diversity, plenty of biomes, pretty good boss fights with one exception, decent diversity of weapons and while some are objectively better than others, the gap isn't that big.My only real criticism is that there's no New Game+ and so no real incentive to keep playing once you've seen all three endings.

_childDocuments_.review: Review update 3: A large patch was dropped today; I haven't checked it out yet, but the below criticisms of bugs may no longer apply. Review update 2:Somehow, the bugs have all gotten worse. So, here's some brief tips for getting past game-breaking bugs:1)If no NPCs spawn in or around the manor when you first get there, there's no saving your gamefile. You need to start over. The NPCs there are important. It is possible to get quite a ways into the game, and through some warps to get some beginning areas from entirely the wrong side, but you cannot progress the intended way, and you will not be able to level up. It will also be impossible to get the true ending, but you can achieve a bad ending. 2) If a certain flame-using boss seems to only repeat one move over and over and over again, your game is also dead in the water. This is caused by the game variable that causes the almost-last boss to glitch, where he will leave the scene for an attack and just . . .  never come back again. 3) If you get a grappling hook and can't figure out how to use it . . . reload the game and try again. Sometimes it just doesn't load up properly. 4)It's best to focus on either the left or the right side hydra heads. If you focus on both, then with bad timing, you can cause them both to leave the screen at the same time, which will cause no head to replace them. 5)vsync doesn't work and eventually breaks the graphics, don't enable it6)Controller inputs are often eaten as the game regularly checks to see if a controller is still connected, and during that time, it acts as through the controller has been disconnected and reconnected. This will also reset the "use dpad for movement" option to default, so just . .. leave it at default. 7)When fighting Edwyn keep to the centre of the screen. If you're too far to either side, you won't fall down with him, and you will be unable to continue the battle8)If you're having lag and input trouble on the snowy area, save at a savepoint, quit and reload. There's a memory leak, and leaving it too long will corrupt your savefile.There's plenty of other glitches, but those are the ones that will kill your game. Review update 1:I may recommend this game in the future; but for now, there are some major bugs that make it not worthwhile. Wait till they're fixed!In particular, I just booted up my game for the day and discovered . . . my save file is completely missing. No sign of it anywhere on my machine when I go to poke around the folders. Just gone. I imagine this is due to the crash last night that gave the message "access violation", which led me to stop playing for the day, but the message seems to indicate the file was already deleted at that time. I have had to deal with constant crashes, and an ever-annoying bug where the game kept resetting my choice of "move with analog or d-pad" *during play*. So I would freeze in place and suddenly start cycling through items while trying to move. This is very frustrating in combat, ESPECIALLY frustrating when jumping over death pits, and continues to happen with a keyboard emulating a virtual controller; in particular, when this happens, I can see the inputs fed to the game by the virtual controller do not translate into actions on-screen for a brief moment, (most visible by writing a script to keep the right analog stick constantly rotating and watching it briefly dip back towards the centre when inputs are interrupted), so I believe the game engine is creating a situation where it believes the controller has been disconnected, (impossible for a virtual controller to be disconnected), and the reconnection process defaults to movement on the analog stick regardless of what your options are set to. This also leads to stutter-y movement at the same instances when you do not change the default option. More minor glitches include that I couldn't equip charms or items, or in general fill blank spots in my inventory with items; it only worked if I replaced a weapon with another weapon. Another was a more fun glitch where you can gain jump height by playing with the camera; I think infinitely. In general, I have seen so many things I believe were unintended that I'm not fully certain how many minor glitches I've seen and how many were intentional design. Original review:I am unable to properly review this game as a metroidvania as of yet, because while I've played 19 hours, not all of them have been horribly productive and I haven't come across any movement tech except for the double jump so far. Many of the game's progression items that I have found are of the type "collect four of these to get a door somewhere else to open", which is the most boring form of metroidvania progression by far. I also do not have the movement items needed to collect all such items for any one place yet, (except for a starlit lake with a very fun boss, but the presumed reward room is locked behind a glowing door I can't access yet), so I might be missing the excitement of a fantastic reward behind them. There are a lot of large areas which appear to have nothing of importance in them whatsoever, but I may be incorrect because I haven't unlocked everything. As a soulslike game, it mostly has satisfying combat, if a bit simple, but is weak in many areas introduced by the metroidvania format and some poor level design. For example: do you like jumping down random pits to find out what's in them? That's necessary in this game! A lot! That also causes you to die. A Lot! And like early castlevanias, the game is littered with enemies designed to knock you back into pits. So you will lose your accumulated experience points very often.There's a lot of enemies and bosses which kill you in one hit, which while they were satisfying to overcome, I can't help but feel that I was meant to find out how to level up somewhere along the way, and nowhere in the various menus can I find any option to do so. Not that I would have had a terrible amount of XP to do so with, because getting back to where I died past a gauntlet of one-hit KO enemies was usually a roughly 50/50 chance once I got good at the area. There are a lot of challenge rooms which you aren't meant to be able to beat when you can first access them. This is great in a metroidvania, as it allows early access to advanced areas or equipment for skilled players. This is horrible for a soulslike, because now all of your stockpiled experiences points are locked behind entering that challenge room to reclaim them, and then beating that challenge room where the enemies one-hit kill you and have many times the health they normally do.The game is obsessed with shortcuts, which I view as a positive, and you will often finish a challenge room just to find the road back home again. I think challenge run and speedrun routes will be quite interesting!Some minor design elements stick out as not fun; grabbing a free-floating ledge is incredibly precise, and there are many places I did not realize were platforms because I did not grab any ledge when trying to climb them. Many jumps REALLY stretch your horizontal jump limit and I don't see the point of that; a notable amount require jumping after rolling off a ledge and achieving what I believe is sub-pixel precision, which I'm not down for in causal games. There are a number of places prior to the double-jump acquisition which actually seem downright impossible to get out of with the movement tech availible to you at that point, so say goodbye to your accumulated XP if you end up down those pits :/Overall, discounting the bugs, I would anti-recommend this game *so far* for metroidvania fans, and recommend it to soulslike players as a 2d soulslike with metroidvania elements.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game I ever backed and that was three years ago. I was expecting something amazing, but so far this has not even been close to worth the wait. The game is incredibly easy. I don't have to do anything aside from attack, dodge and jump. Most enemies I can just chain stun over and over and I haven't even needed to upgrade my weapon yet. I haven't really needed to use a side arm or the parry ability. Most enemies die before I even get a chance to press the execute button. The input lag is horrendous at times and after 6 hours I have found all of three weapons, three offhand weapons which aren't even pistols.  One charm and one Stigma. I hope this game is incredibly long because if this is all I've found and I'm even a quarter way through, I'm going to be even more disappointed. Not to mention I apparently don't get the backer Katana weapon that I was looking forward to because they just "didn't have time" to put it in the game. _childDocuments_.review: This game boasts a large map, and is for all intents and purposes a PC gaming, 2d, bloodborne that has been an itch many people have wanted to scratch without buying a whole PS4+. What it has over Blasphemous 2 is the Souls-style levelling system, weapon scaling, and resource management, as well as the open world aspect- it has much less linearity.On the other hand, the beginning of the game has a lot of the same air as Blasphemous 1- don't know where to go, some places are not so clear where you should go, and you have to save up to buy wall jump for 10k nycrux- but these are a product of having an early demo for a kickstarter- you don't necessarily want to pave over those parts of the game just to make the rest of the game better.The bosses are dynamic, easy to learn, and if you're the right level for that boss it never feels like it's unfairly difficult. Perhaps one complaint is that resistances scale only with your stats and only barely through charms, so that invalidates certain builds (strength governs frost resist, which half the game takes place in, making it a very strong choice as opposed to, say, Mind for a pure spell run) leading to having to place some stats into those areasThere are some visual bugs, glitches, and slipups in voice text, but this game is less than a month old from release. I'm sure these will be fixed, and all the good parts outweigh the bad. Easily the top 1 metroidvania of 2023, a must have for any 2d soulslike enjoyer.Only true complaint is it detects the keyboard even when in the background, so I ended up deleting my save one time, which would happen even now on a near-100% save if I simply pressed backspace and then spacebar while typing this.

_childDocuments_.review: There's some jank. There's a lot of "wow this is stupid". There's nightmare rooms and a few questionable hitboxes and deep, deep inspiration from [insert metroidvania title here], but? I haven't had this much fun playing a game like this is such a long time. If you like the art style but, like me, enjoy just curb stomping things? Strength. Only strength. You get a big sword early-ish on and that's the one, frens. All the other stats? Hardmode. Hard hard hard because the game feels balanced around strength. AND YET. It's really so much fun. If you love being frustrated, squinting at a questionable map looking for anywhere there might be yet another breakable wall, and pumping souls into a stat for big, chronchy slaps? This is the game for you. If you're thinking "I'd rather play Blaphemous" do that, though. Thank you, devs, for making this. And for giving me that phalanges spell because I would have lost my /Mind/ otherwise. hohohoho

_childDocuments_.review: is yet another religiously themed Metroidvania game comparable to  franchise. However, while artistically much darker and religiously much deeper as it deals with the theme of false god,  isn't as great in terms of gameplay as  was.The game offers thirteen different choices of primary weapons, six different secondary weapons, and sixteen different spells, but you don't really need all these options to beat the game; the differences among these weapons are purely stylistic and every weapon is pretty much replaceable with one another. Considering this is the central feature of the gameplay, I believe they could have used all those resources for something else.Also, artistically speaking, the dark and gothic theme is truly one of a kind, but it comes with a cost. The dark theme is somewhat too dark and makes different stages of adventure less distinguishable from each other. Do not get me wrong, they have distinguishable features, however, they are all dark and gloomy places and don't feel like different places. This didn't happen with , so in , it feels less like an adventure, and more like a pilgrimage.Overall,  artistically feels a lot heavier, and more serious than . It's still a tough call whether one is better than the other, but I believe if you particularly like gothic aesthetics and the theme of dark pilgrimage, then  is certainly worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, fantastic art direction, great music, good sound design.Fun to play, feels like it wears its inspirations quite proudly - the bosses are varied, they feel cool to fight, and Eryk has a great arsenal of weapons and abilities.The single biggest downside to this game is that it did not launch with a New Game Plus - I would have played through it three times by now to catch stuff I know I missed on my first go-round but I'm surely not starting over from scratch.  These days, most games of this nature have NG+ and many at launch, so hopefully it shows up here soon, all I know right now is that a November 2023 discussion response from KSG says it is "planned."

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT - I'm glad to see they've already made an update addressing the imbalance issues that I so lengthily complained about in this review.  Unfortunately I already spent over 6o hours on this game, pre-update, and really have little to no desire to go back to it for a second round to see how they did with it.  I will say that after about 50 hours in when I had got myself to such an absurdly high level, the game became a little more bearable.  But then I read in the in the patch notes that they fixed the Hungry and Starving essence exploit which is the only way I got myself to that high of a level to make the game bearable.  After you become overpowered the game does become much more fun, at least imo.  I dont know what the designers of this game were thinking?!?! Every aspect of the combat will just frustrate you and piss you off.  The controls are horrible, janky, and again, poorly designed, leaving you dying over and over and over again because they have some idiotic cool-down implemented on things that have no business having a cool down.  For example, if you do a roll into a jump you cant do an air dash while in mid air.  It wont take effect until your literally one pixel from landing back on the ground. Your dodging & rolling, the stuff you MUST do to avoid enemy attacks, can not be done during your attack animations, so using a slower more powerful weapon is also made nearly pointless because even though you're dealing more damage to the enemies you cant dodge their attacks, but they most certainly can and will attack you while you're striking them!! All the items and tools needed to make the game a fun and balanced experienced are impossible to use.  Either the items are made useless because the animation for using them takes LITERALLY 2-3 seconds to finish, most notably the health injections, during which you're totally vulnerable to all attacks, which during a boss fight and multi-enemy encounters is absolutely vital.  Your honestly more likely to die or to get hit AGAIN just trying to use them, wasting the injection completely.  The other items in the game are impossible to make good use of because, again, the horrible design of this game has you having to scroll through these items via the D-pad to access and use them which is 1) hard to see 2) takes too long 3) cant be scrolled through while having to use the joystick during combat which is when you NEED to use the items!  You can not pause the game...yes you heard that right, when you "pause" to pull up the menu or map, the game is still going on in the back ground and you will die if you have not totally cleared the room before accessing the menu/map.  The absolutely ridiculous amount of grinding you have to do in this game is also unreal, even when playing in the intended linear fashion.  The absurdly drastic jump in enemy hit points and damage dealt to the player is also a shining example of just how unbalanced this game really is...I shouldn't have to grind for 6 hours so I can go from level 10 to 35 just so I can survive longer than 5 seconds in the very next zone you're supposed to be progressing through.  The Nycrux gained from defeating enemies through normal exploration and defeating major and minor bosses should be enough to level up sufficiently to survive in the next area.  I don't think it would shock anyone to say that this game is a blatant rip-off of Blasphemous...however, everything that Blasphemous did right, this game sadly got all wrong.  I waited for over 6 months for this game to come out and I really, really want to like it, but it's just so poorly designed in all the aspects that REALLY matter, that I just can't like or recommend this game at all.  Do NOT waste your money on this game until the devs give us an update that makes this game what it should have been from the beginning!  I will say, though, that the game looks fantastic.  The world, the monsters, the characters, the backgrounds and music, are all utterly fabulous...but without the gameplay to go with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 7/10 game that I would recommend to anyone who wants to play a Metroidvania game and has already played some of this genre's better offerings(Hollow Knight & Blasphemous) or is more interested in the "Bloodborne" aesthetic. The Last Faith provides a complete Metroidvania experience that includes the "Key" finding and sense of exploration that are hallmarks of the genre. This game pulls a lot from the From Software playbook, most notably the weapon upgrade system from the Dark Souls trilogy. The boss fights are all strong and general combat never feels solid with most weapons(some weapons and strategies being easier than others). That said not much about this game is particularly remarkable, excluding a few of the more memorable bosses and the execution mechanic. ***MAIN ISSUE*** This game does(& may still) have some bugs at the time of its release but none that resulted in a dead save or true soft lock(across my several runs through the game). At the time of this review it appears that there is an issue with some of the achievements for the game, the "Get all Achievements" achievement in particular.

_childDocuments_.review: A little bit more above average metroidvania that gave me mixed feelings leaning towards more positive than negative ones. It has those Lovecraftian vibes that are kinda of a mix between Bloodbourne and Blasphemous which is good, but on the other hand there was something in how it was written that did not really get me engaged with the story. The gameplay was also solid, but it had some flaws, like giving you freedom to build your characters stats how you want, but this being just a trap luring you in as any other than STR scaling weapons were kinda bad, this further was cemented with you getting a choice to pick 1 of 4 classes, from which 2 kinda suck. The game also took the idea from Bloodbourne to let you go with a melee weapon in one hand and a gun in the other, problem is that while ammo was limited, the gun was not used to parry, nor stagger enemies, not to mention you were kinda locked in animation when shooting, and this usually was taking much longer than swinging your sword once.To summarize, the story was so-so and the gameplay solid with some balancing issues and some pointless mechanics that were there to pad the gameplay with some stuff, that in the end was so bad that you even forgot it existed. So if any of those problems already make you think this game is not for you, than its probably that case. I myself can only recommend this to real die hard fans of metroidvania games and even than its a sink or swim recommmandation.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult game to fully recommend. It does a lot of things right, but it also does a lot of things wrong. It's a game that lacks polish with a few questionable gameplay decisions. I was going to put a Good, Bad, and Ugly type thing, but it's really more of Okay, Less Okay, and Frustrating. The Okay:--It's a serviceable Metroidvania and, as others have said, is definitely is reminiscent of Blasphemous. I don't see the Bloodborne connection, other than the gothic art style, but it really has more of a Castlevania vibe for me. --The upgrade and progression systems, weapons, spells, etc. function well enough. The boss designs can be interesting anc compelling.Ultimately, all of these things are just fine though, nothing that stands out.The Less Okay:Here's where the game falls apart a bit. --The story is needlessly convoluted, and not because it's a complex story, but because it's written in such a obtuse way. It's like when someone writes and you know they've just used a thesaurus because the words are all fancy, but aren't quite appropriate. That's how this is written.--The controls can be sloppy and janky down to completely frustrating. For some reason when you try to change direction, your character backsteps three steps before turning. It makes the movement feel unresponsive. --There are a lot of interaction points (talking to characters, performing an execution, grappling) that require you to be standing in a very specific spot, more specific than typical for this sort of thing.--There are a number of random side/fetch quests, but many of them have pointless or even no rewards. Like you find and bring this item back and they say thanks, you get an achievement, but nothing else. In fact, the rewards seem misplaced throughout the game. Walking down a regular hallway? Here's a nice weapon or rare collectable. Beat a secret boss in a secret area? Here's a regular upgrade stone that you could have bought from the merchant. It's weird. The Frustrating:--Numerous upgrades are near pointless. You can get a ton of different spells, but few of them do little more damage than a basic attack; and the ones that do hit hard have to be so perfectly placed to actually connect with the enemies, that you end up wasting them more often than not. --You also gain special abilities, like increasing your attack speed, or your movement or damage output, but they all have active timers that are so short they're next to useless. More on this in a moment.--The bosses can be enjoyable, but many have very similar attack patterns. Often times they teleport around the screen as part of their attack, and while it's typically well telegraphed, they always seem to end up on the opposite side of the screen from you, forcing you to spend most of every fight just running back and forth trying to catch up to them to get in a few meager hits before they teleport away. This is made all the more tedious because every boss is a damage sponge that takes just shy of 500 hits! And so you may think, well, I'll just use one of those fancy special abilities I have to maximize my damage windows. The problem is, their movement and attack patterns can be so erratic, that trying to time when to activate your ability is near impossible. Not to mention, if you do find yourself on the right side of the screen as the enemy, the animation to activate your ability takes up so much time you've lost your attack window. Literally, you have to predict when and where the boss will be, so that you can time your activation, because you only get 5-10 seconds once it's activated, all the while dodging their near constant attacks. And to boot, it's only marginally better than your regular attack. And so, as mentioned, it effectively makes all of your special abilities useless. Ultimately, this game is okay, it's worth playing if you like these sorts of games, I don't regret my time playing, but it's not going to blow you away. It's serviceable, but it's on the cusp of being far better, and I think that's the most frustrating part. A bit of polish and balancing for the main mechanics and it could be a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Encountered a game breaking bug.After fighting and defeating Dr. Hermann, his health bar remains on the screen, I get locked in the room with nothing but the sound of his corpse turning into a kool aid puddle, and Im unable to progress. I think to myself "whatever Ill just do the fight over again it was easy". Well the same thing happens again. I try 3 more times and to my surprise the same thing happened every....single....time. I could restart at this point as its probably an hour into the game when youre getting your footing, but honestly the game itself feels overly simplistic and I cant be bothered. Like it doesnt feel bad, it just feels beyond basic. Parrying and most abilities are clunky or down right unnecessary. Like why would i use a parry mechanic when spamming jump attacks works on literally everything. At this point, the idea of starting over doesn't exactly excite me, which says a lot, because metroidvanias are some of my favorites. Regrettably giving this one a down finger, which is a shame, because ive been looking forward to this one for a while.Edit: Did a reinstall and restarted my play through, didnt run into the same bug this time, and completed the game. Everything else mentioned above still stands, everything is unnecessary when spamming jump attack and pretending to be Ike in smash brothers is the most effective/easiest way to play the game. Could you use spells, guns, sigils, and the knock off Devil Trigger mode? Sure, but they're not as good as Jump attack spam.  In total I died 4 times to bosses, and a handful more to attempting jumps i shouldnt have / falling off cliffs. Disappointingly easy. Its not an up for a down finger, its a sideways finger, its no hollowknight or blasphemous.

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhere between Blasphemous and Bloodborne, I'll be frank: The Last Faith is not an original game. That being said, it's a fun one. The pixel art is solid and clean, the bosses are pretty fun, and the maps are fun to explore. My only real complain with the game (lack of originality is not a complaint if its executed well!) is the controls. Movement is kind of stiff, and I couldn't figure out a button layout that didn't cause me to flounder under pressure occasionally. That being said, I'm having a good time with it. As a disclaimer, I'm someone who doesn't mind using a guide (I'm too used to Dark Souls games and their absolutely baffling quest progression) so the fact that this game gives you next to no guidance isn't that much of a problem for me. I enjoy that feeling of getting lost in a world and consulting a guide every so often is fine by me. Overall, if Bloodborne is an A+ and Blasphemous (IMO) is an A-, the Last Faith is a solid B. Definitely worth the price for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this one for three reasons: the game feels awkward to play, it apes the Fromsoft formula too closely without thinking about why or how doing so would make this game better, and it ultimately brings nothing new to the table.The most important part of any Metroidvania is movement. It needs to feel smooth and fluid. The Last Faith, unfortunately, fails this first test. The walk speed feels just a little too slow, not just slowing down the game play, but it feels like the distance covered per step doesn't match the character's walk animation. The animations in the preview videos looks sped up just slightly. Dodging has an awkward dead stop at the end of the animation and the camera follows the character only at the zenith of the jump, making it feel shorter and more abrupt than it really is.This game tries to be a 2D Bloodborne. That's a great starting point, but doesn't reach to make it's own mark, aping the look, style, and weird things like hitting start to enter the menu not pausing the game, which makes sense in a game with invasions, but is nonsensical in a single player game. Sometimes a gamer needs to pee, you know?Finally, the game does one thing that isn't done better in other, similar games, like Vigil: the Longest Night and the venerable Salt and Sanctuary, and that's being able to wing chairs at enemies. Using environmental items like that could have set this game apart from the pack if it was made a focus, but doing so lacks any advantage, doing less DPS than a weapon attack with no invincibility frames for the 0.75 seconds it takes to chuck something. This is a legitimately good idea that other games haven't really done, and it feels wasted.Any one of these issues would have been fine and led to a solid recommendation, but all of them together makes this a soft pass. It's okay if you're desperate, but only if you've exhausted everything else with a Metroidvania tag. An early access period could have made this game great. As of now, it's a sub-par game with solid graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is frustrating, although it has improved since release. It is very satisfying at times, but its mostly a janky mess. Grabbing ledges, turning around, jumping, are all badly designed and they mainly just seem to halt the flow. It's poorly indicated where the player should go next; I often found myself deciding whether i should face down mobs that seemed too strong to my level OR a ledge that seemed to be juuust impossible to grab for some odd reason (grabbed it around my 40th try, then a mob pushed me off).The weapons are fun, even if a bit simple. Aesthetics, environment, enemy visual design, etc are great. Music is okay, it sets the mood. The VAs seem... bored(?) for lack of a better word. Idk, just uninspired.Certain enemy attacks cause an absurd amount of damage. I kill mostly every enemy, didnt loose many souls, but I often feel like I should farm more, although i put around half my points into health. The janky controls also mean that most situations where you face more than 1 enemy, you just get staggered to death after one attack catches you.All in all, the game is promising, very much so. But I feel like it's hard to love this game at it's current state, it needs more work.

_childDocuments_.review: Sound design is great and really creeped me out on a couple of occasions. But imagine making a metroidvania without making exploration feel rewarding. Found 3 weapons, 2 of which I couldn't use. Found a buttload of spells, which, believe it or not, I also couldn't use without heavily investing in a stat I have no interest in (no respecs btw). Found a total of 5 bosses, with two of them being the same enemy but using a different element. Oh, and they also turned a former boss into a random field enemy. It hasn't even been six hours man.In short: One of the most boring and uninspired metroidvanias I've played over the years. Banking on Bloodborne vibes isn't enough guys.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a 2D soulslike metroidvania and a wonderful mixture of Blasphemous and Bloodborne that feels like Castlevania's R rated cousin. The world is oozing with dark gothic horror with beautiful visuals, chillingly creepy music and awesome voice acting. Other than perfecting dark gothic visuals, TLF especially succeeds in having some of the most satisfying boss battles in the metroidvania genre (special notice should be given to The Burnt Apostate, Nyxaroth and Lord Laddak). I thoroughly enjoyed my time in TLF which took me roughly 20 hours to get all the achievements, though one could potentially get through the game in 10-12 hours depending on skill level. In contrast to other soulslike metroidvanias, TLF feels much more forgiving  and I appreciate that about it.As much as I enjoyed it, TLF is not perfect and has some aspects of it that make me scratch my head. While most of the boss fights in the game are incredible, it was puzzling that there are several that are reskins (but not rematches) of prior fights with minimal changes as well as one that I was not aware was a boss until after it was defeated (Voracious Terror). TLF also creates a few systems such as a parry mechanic that helps you regain health and a superpowered transformation, but does not make you engage with them. You could theoretically go the entire game without ever parrying and never notice that you missed out on a cool mechanic of the game. I do wish TLF forced or highly encouraged players to interact with these aspects of the game as I feel like the devs put in a lot of effort designing these systems and it should be appreciated. Speaking of things the dev put a lot of effort into, it is baffling that there is not a bestiary. For a game that has so many unique and beautifully designed enemies, it is very surprising there is not a catalog for them. Maybe in a future update?A few questions aside, TLF is a wonderful gem of a game and should be picked up instantly by anyone who enjoys metroidvanias, soulslikes or both.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: One-line review: Bloodborne and Blasphemous had a baby and it's a killer metroidvania.Graphics: Cribbed heavily from 32-bit era pixel graphics games like Castlevania SOTN but with modern technology allowing fluidity of animation and detailed cutscenes that era could only dream of. It's not going to wreck your GPU but it is a feast for the eyes.Sound: Incredibly moody soundtrack and excellent sound effects really keep you in the world of the game. Nothing spectacular, you're probably not going to be listening to this one outside the game unless you're trying to get to sleep tbh, but it fits the game nicely.Control: This one definitely leans more into combat feel than platforming, the movement is deliberate like a FromSoft game, you need to be sure of your intent before pressing a button or you're going to get smacked. I have issue with the gripping mechanic but since they're obviously going for keeping things grounded in a physical reality it fits into the overall game aesthetic. It feels a little muddy if you're coming from games like Hollow Knight or Ori, but it isn't bad, just different.Story: Someone definitely likes their Souls games here, cryptic pieces of lore strewn about the world, NPCs spouting dialog that you don't understand at first but which paints an overall picture of a good story. Very derivative though of Bloodborne for sure, but it doesn't hurt the experience, just doesn't add anything new to the genre.Overall: What can I say, I'm a sucker for everything this game is offering. As a lifelong metroidvania enjoyer and a fan of all of FromSoft's soulsborne catalog this game absolutely knew who it was targeting and it touches all the right places in my brain. You could do a lot worse than this one and at the price it's going for it's a steal of an experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: After finally playing this game, i can say that its a decently good time. Its not as good as games similar to it, but it scratches that Metroidvania itch.Lets start with the positives. The sprite art is amazing. Its very similar to the first Blasphemous, and a lot of the designs are great. On the same topic, some of the visuals are good. There were times I admired the scenery and background of some of the areas. Secondly the combat is really good. You have a variety of weapons that youll get in your journey with varying movesets. While I didnt play with all of them, I used the axe weapon and the greatsword, there could be a weapon that you will like using. Plus, theres the option of using magic and ranged weapons, but I didnt use them throughout my playthrough. Thirdly, the execution moves you do against the enemies. Like the first Blasphemous, there are a variety of executions you can do against enemies and theyre really good, my favorite being the one where you knock an enemy with it's musket and shoot it dead.While there were things i liked, i have some issues with the game. Starting with the areas. There are few areas that are decently sized, but there are times where areas are so big it feels like they drag on and on to the point it makes you wonder  wheres the next checkpoint or boss. Spoilers, but theres an area thats this massive palace place and it felt like forever to traverse. Speaking of which, the locations arent that memorable, and by that i mean that they dont have something that makes them stand out among others. While there are few that have something, like the area with the screaming fire statues, the Esk Mansion with the mirrors, the snow village with the damaging blizzard, the Junas Ministry with it's visuals, a lot dont have something that makes them stand out. To me, an area in a Metroidvania should have something that makes it stand out and be distinct, like it having a certain mechanic, unique hazards or design in general, and The Last Faith offers a few of that, maybe its just me. At least the areas have some unique enemies.Secondly is that, while I liked the combat, there was no reason to use magic or ranged weapons. This could be personal opinion, but I didnt feel the need to use any firearms or magic abilities. Some day Ill try using them if i ever revisit this game.Thirdly, the bosses werent that memorable to me. While I found the bosses to be decently challenging, the bosses werent that memorable in terms of design and appearance. The first few bosses were nice, but as the game progressed, the bosses declined in terms of fights. Sure there were some stand outs, at least to me, for instance the duo boss fight was really good, I liked the one with the burning sword, and i felt like the final bosses were pretty good aswell. However the rest felt rather bland or just uninteresting. One I have to mention is the giant water hydra boss that appeared in the trailers. What a let down, what i thought was gonna be one of the best bosses in the game, turned out to be just a massive pushover. Maybe it was my expectations, but since bosses like Sierpes from Blasphemous exist, I expected something on a similar level. Another boss was a late game boss that for some reason felt like an early game boss due to how basic it's attacks were. In short, the bosses are pretty hit or miss.Fourth is the music. There are a few good tracks, mostly boss tracks but the rest of the soundtrack felt lackluster and not memorable. Most of the Metroidvanias ive played have had great soundtracks that I sit down listen from time to time. The Blasphemous soundtracks being one, Vigil the Longest Night, Dead Cells and even Moonscars, which has some of the best atmospheric soundtrack ive ever listened. Then you got The Last Faith and its just... lacking.Finally, the movement. It felt clunky and it felt slightly better to control with power up such as the double jump. And I wonder who thought adding a side stepping animation when turning around was a good a idea?Anyways, with all that said, I think The Last Faith is just decent, I liked it, but I dont love it. Its not on the level as games like Blasphemous or similar games, but that doesnt mean its a bad game by any means, but just a decent Metroidvania you buy in a sale and play it once.

_childDocuments_.review: NOT A METROIDVANIA, Don't call it one (Update)Now finished with the game, my first review still stands,It's still really not a metroidvania until the very end. It's a souls-like with Metroidvania elements added to it. It's more tedious than it is rewarding, and the Metroidvania aspects come down to a sprawling map, that circles back on itself in some situations, and the occasional need for a double jump or dash or something to reach a ledge.This is 2D Bloodborne plain and simple. If you a want a more traditional SOTN experience with a horror Gothic aesthetic, play Blasphemous 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and can be frustrating at times. Mainly the frozen areas as in most video games that have a frozen area. Most my frustration is probably self-imposed probably due to the fact I wanted to do a Mind build and never upgrading my weapon until I got a weapon called Spinal Chain Blade and proceeded to use all mats that I had to get it to +5 and I started melting everything in my path. Main concern is the lack of Mind weapons. There was only one but it mainly scaled with Dex with a small scale in Mind. It isn't feasible to spam your magic because there isn't enough recovery to do so.Anyways. The map is huge I never found it tedious to explore. Although, the secrets that are spread throughout the map need to have better rewards though. Maybe if they add more weapons they can use some of those spots for that. The enemies are placed in a way that you need to kill them as you see them and to not rush past them or you can get swarmed if you aren't good enough to fight so many. Overall the game is enjoyable and I hope to see more from them.

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania's are my favorite genre for games.. and I've played a lot of them.  The Last Faith is a good one.  When I first purchased the game, I encountered several bugs and glitches, and  immediately refunded it.   After reading later reports of bug fixes, I re-purchased the game and gave it another chance.  I'm glad I did.  The Last Faith is a beautiful game.  The art is amazing, the animation is top notch, the music is vibey, and the gameplay is very responsive and rewarding.  The Last Faith is also brutal.  The game can be very difficult, along the lines of the Blasphemous and Dark Souls series.  If you want to get the "FULL" experience of this game, prepare to spend hours "farming"to level up your weapons.   Some people will like this, but for me this is one of my gripes of the game as I feel like farming should almost be an organic process along the way of exploring new areas.  Although, I can appreciate the variety of weapons and attacks, I also feel like maybe there are a bit too many options.. Some times less is more in this department.     Storyline is there, but not super compelling or anything like that.. however, who really cares about story these days?  I just wanna kick some demon's asses anyways. I was leaning at giving this game a 7 outta 10, but towards the end, the game got really good and crazy awesome with the additional detailed boss fights. My verdict:  I give it an 8.5 outta 10.  I recommend you go for the good ending if you really want the true full experience.  I'm hoping for more games out of this developer.  Congrats on a successful game!

_childDocuments_.review: The short version: Fairly serviceable game, solid overall. 7-8/10, depending on how I'm feeling. If numbers are all you care about, there you go.The long version:The pros:-Visual design is on point. Everything feels gothic and grungy.-Location variance. Going off the previous pro, every locale feels distinctly its own, and has its own pacing for traversal.-Dialogue maintains integrity with the visuals. It is hard to deny that they way everyone speaks feels antiquated.-Sound balance. Nothing feels inappropriately loud or like it's drowning out other pertinent sounds.-Weapon design. Each weapon feels suitably unique, and the varying speeds and strengths lend to a healthy variety of options.The alright:-Music is good where it's present, but the inconsistency of its presence is a little weird. You have your checkpoint rooms with their theme, and good, simple music for other levels, but it's a bit weird when there's then locations that just have ambiance and enemy noise.-Boss design. Only had a three bosses that held me back beyond a handful of tries. To refrain from spoiling, the ones that stood out as annoying because they each demanded so substantially more time were in a cold mansion, buried in the deepest depths, and on a cold lake shore. The last one may have just been because I think I might've stumbled into it early.-Enemy design. There's a healthy variety of enemies in the game, but it is impossible not to notice that some designs just get reused between areas with a modification of extra area and effects to their attacks.The cons:-Healing system. I get that it's inspired by Bloodborne, but I feel like it hurts pacing and the ability to keep cracking at a boss in an effort to make progress if you die, and then find out that you're out of healing entirely, forcing the player to go grind for healing items, rather than letting them keep trying at the boss (or rather, forcing the expectation that if they want to, it will have to be done without healing at all.) A potential alternative for future consideration could be creating a minimum that will always refill whether there is spare stock, but increasing the maximum that can be held, so that if you need more, you can draw upon more.-Weapon upgrade system. While upgrading the weapons feels good for making them keep pace with the increasing health pools of enemies and bosses, it fundamentally feels like it hurts the experience when there's some weapons that you're not going to get until the last third of the game, which if that was the one you want to use, then you've likely had to upgrade other weapons first to keep pace, but then have to go through that full series of upgrades on the new weapon, of which the cost in Nycrux is rather steep, requiring a hefty grind for even one weapon.-Clarity. While I understand that the Fromsoft inspiration is there, it would be lovely to not require a half-hour video after I've finished the game to actually understand what is going on. Unfortunately, as nice of a touch as the antiquated language is, it also obfuscates a lot of the story, which can hurt the general theme that may be trying to be conveyed.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game; Really enjoyed it. With extra exp. grinding, getting all the weapons and finishing what I believe to be all the side-quests it was a solid 26hrs.+ for me. Only maybe 2 or 3 bosses gave me any serious Ef-this-crap-grief; thankfully grinding levels actually makes a pretty big difference so was able to level my way out of those few bullet-sponge a-hole bosses. So word to the wise; if you don't want 15min.+  boss battles (which both frustrate the heck out of me, and bore me simultaneously), just do a bit of level grinding and apart from the death/retry loop to figure out a boss' quirks and patterns, most bosses are beat in 5min or less. Also, the parry mechanic is pretty friggin' jenky; other than the easiest-to-read-telegraph animations for the slower melee enemies I'll be darned if I could figure out how to counter 95% of attacks, so the in-game description of "works against most enemies" is a pretty ambitious claim. And since it's a big way of replenishing magic you better keep a bunch of mana-stones handy if you're going to use spells! melee attacks replenish your counter meter, but a-la Hollow Knight if they replenished your magic meter it would go A LOOONGGG way to make a magic-focused build more viable!Also, the map is pretty jenky too; plenty of parts of it and areas that LOOK like they'd lead somewhere, or you should be able to get to, and they don't and it's just design jenk, or in some b.s. occaisions friggin' insta-death. Definitely looks like maybe unfinished bits of areas that the devs figured it was easier to just leave there? Dunno, but as you near completion you'll totally understand what I mean.Otherwise, a great game, but definitely room for improvement.Will definitely do another run as soon as a MUCH NEEDED new-game-plus mode gets added as per the reached kick-starter-goal. Whatever the level-cap is, it ain't 99, as my current character's at 101 and OP'ing my way through a second run would be a ton of fun for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith seamlessly blends the atmospheric allure of Bloodborne with the exploration-driven charm of a Metroidvania. The game's dark and mysterious world is a visual treat, echoing the haunting art direction of Bloodborne. From the intricate gothic architecture to the nightmarish creatures that lurk in the shadows, The Last Faith nails the aesthetic that fans of both genres crave.The gameplay is a satisfying mix of challenging combat and exploration, with tight controls that make every move count. As you traverse the interconnected world, unlocking new areas and abilities, the game keeps you engaged with secrets and shortcuts that reward your curiosity. The challenging boss encounters add an extra layer of excitement, requiring strategy and skill to overcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid metroidvania with challenging combat and a lot of secrets to find along the way.  Combat controls are not as responsive as I'd like. Especially striking in the air - very easy to not get a swing at all because you need to hold the button down seemingly forever to get a swing registered. There's a lot of potential variety in the way of available builds.  I enjoyed playing around with the varying primary/secondary weapons/spells and stat allocations to optimize them.  The starting class just determines starting stats and primary weapon, so you're not stuck into a particular archetype.  With enough time/money/patience, you can try everything out and see what you like.Art style, overly cryptic/nonsensical story and theme feels very much like Blasphemous.  However, I'd say that I enjoyed The Last Faith more overall as the gameplay was just more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Walked in not expecting much, I just like metroidvanias, and was this game just kept getting more and more impressive.  Enemies have varied attacks and a lot of variety with designs.  The weapons are plenty all have a unique feel along with the special attacks they can do.  Magic is in the game too, but I went for a melee run so not the one to ask on that.  Even the core mechs are nice.  You get a parry that gives heath and mana back, executions also give mana back and happen frequent enough.  Ammo for guns, consumables for health, mana, and booms.   You can easily pick a new weapon up too as you will get the ability to purchase the items need to upgrade, so you are not locked into whatever you upgraded first.Best of all, the game is an actual challenge.  I had to hit some of these bosses a few times to get that win, and it was damn close for some.Pro tip, the parry is about YOU hitting the enemy's hitbox during their windup, not their weapon. The only gripes I can think would be there is no new game plus and the upgrades feel out of order compared to just about every other game in this genre so use your map markers whenever you see something you cant get yet cause you will get lost as hell otherwise.  I don't see myself going back through this game ( I found my favorite weapon and stuck to it ) , but I did 100% it and had a good time going it.  10/10 would like to see more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Solid metroidvania. Good combat and exploration and some really solid boss fights. Needs some quality of life changes such as better fast travel interface. Parrying is cool but I hardly use it cause it's not that useful. It definitely needs a huge nerf imo- just increase the health gain and damage output. Yes and no mouse support? I beat the game with keyboard only but mouse would have been so much better....I sincerely hope they bring mouse support.And while its cool that each weapon has a special power moveset, I do think some more moves would've been better such as ground slam attacks and a better ariel moveset.Soundtrack is okay, nothing too memorable.It's overall a pretty cool game and I was hooked from the get go. I have 100%ed the game in a single playthrough and it took me around 28 hrs to do so.I hope the devs keep updating this with new features such as ng+ and the QOL changes.Congratulations to the devs for what they've achieved and I wish them all the best.Also massive thanks to IS BLOODBORNE ON PC for the steam key.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game that has major SoTN vibes with a much heavier dose of lovecraftian horror. Super big bosses, quite a few pretty similar looking due to story reasons, most are fun.  You get a LOT of various weapons that are very unique from each other and a lot of fun to play and combo up with various firearms. It does have the standard "getting lost around the middle" portions of the game where progression isn't well defined, and you will most likely need a guide to really find everything necessary to get the best ending, which has a pair of final bosses that are fantastic.
