_childDocuments_.review: Really great metroidvania. Full of secrets, lore, exploration, power progression. There's obvious inspiration taken from Elden Ring and the grim-dark souls-like games, but not a carbon copy, and a great integration of metroidvania platforming and combat. Encounters are unforgiving but fair and there is a good progression of difficulty as your character gets stronger. Beautiful, detailed pixel art, characters, foregrounds, and backgrounds really bring the game to life.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Blasphemous, I really enjoyed this game and it kept me well entertained from start to finish. The detailed pixel art, scenarios and some of the boss fights are great. The cathedral at the end is one of the best-looking metroidvania areas I have seen and they did an excellent job to convey the cathedral is gigantic! The areas are also huge and complex, which is a big plus for me.However, it does have MANY flaws:- The religious themes and story are not so present and well-developed. From the title of the game I was expecting this- You have to periodically GRIND NYCRUX (the currency of the game) TO BUY "FLASKS", which is just a terrible decision. All the times I had to stop trying to beat a boss because I ran out of heals almost made me uninstall- There are some absurd difficulty spikes, which are planted right at the middle of early game areas. I understand the player has to figure out that is not the place to go. but there are just so many locked areas with several waves of enemies of optional, endgame content, which can be annoying when they make you lose al your Nycrux- This game desperately needs a "homeward" spell or item to return to the manor or the latest checkpoint. That's because you lose progress if you quit the game without saving in a checkpoint. This makes exploration pretty boring on the way back to the checkpoint...- I don't think it was a good idea to have the major (and by far the most difficulty) part of the game in an ice area. The frozen status can be VERY annoying, especially if you are not building STR...- Speaking of which, I played a DEX/MIND build and experienced some huge difficulty spikes and most of the bosses (and even some enemies) were big sponges which took a lot of time to defeat. I made sure to be fairly leveled and had my weapons upgraded as much as possible, but the damage for this build was not there the entire game... So for me, the game was very hard, but not in the best way: sometimes it was frustrating.To summarize, great metroidvania, but when compared to Blasphemous it no more than a shade

_childDocuments_.review: One does not even need to play The Last Faith to see that it was heavily inspired by Bloodborne. There are also some pretty strong wafts of Blasphemous in there, as well. Nevertheless, the issue with many Souls-inspired games is that they end up being clones with no unique identity, rather than being tributes or homages to them. This is especially true of The Last Faith, at least during the time that I played it. It wasn’t just trying to feel like Bloodborne or give off reminiscent vibes because The Last faith Bloodborne. Not just in terms of gameplay, but also in terms of the mood, atmosphere, and visual aesthetic; a gothic-style world engulfed in evil and bereft of humanity. If Blasphemous and Bloodborne had a kid together, their little lovechild would be The Last Faith. Once again, this is not a compliment. Nothing I encountered while playing indicated that this game had an identity of its own. Personally, I find this type of development a bit pathetic and shameful because  at the end of the day, it’s just copying someone else’s creation and pretending like it was their own. Like... stop riding coattails and come up with your own ♥♥♥♥ ffs. In terms of mechanics, it all appeared to be more of the same. Yet another Metroid-vania, complete with the enemies, weapons and backdrops you’ve seen so many times before. The combat wasn’t bad, necessarily. It was inoffensive for the most part, but also nothing to write home about. It was just kind of a nothing-burger. The bigger issue, though, was with the tempo. Combat and movement felt sluggish which had an impact on the overall pace of the game. It was very reminiscent of early-stage Blaspemous before any of the Mea Culpa upgrades that gave the game more fluidity and momentum. To be fair, though, what I played of The Last Faith was also early-game and could very easily change with progression, so take that as you will. Can't recommend this one. Not even to big Souls/Bloodborne/Blaspemous fans. I, myself, am a big fan of those titles, but there comes a time when you just have to tell yourself "enough is enough". There is an enormous amount of souls clones out there and they are becoming less and less unique and intriguing. In a nutshell, that is The Last Faith. Your $30 could be better spent on so many other things.

_childDocuments_.review: Key Ingredients You NeedCake Flour: Lighter than all-purpose flour, cake flour produces a soft crumb.Baking Powder & Baking Soda: The two add plenty of lift under the heavy topping.Salt: Balances the sweetness.Butter: Instead of melted butter, use 6 Tablespoons of softened butter. (Not the whole stick, though you do need more for the topping.) Creaming butter and sugar guarantees a buttery soft crumb. It’s how I prepare my vanilla cupcakes, too.Sugar: White granulated sugar sweetens and tenderizes the cake. There’s brown sugar in the topping to provide essential flavor!Egg Whites: Don’t let yolks weigh down a cake that’s already weighed down by the fruit topping. After all my recipe testing, I now swear by just egg whites here. So there’s no waste, here are my recipes using egg yolks.Vanilla Extract: Flavor.Sour Cream: Along with cake flour and egg whites, sour cream promises a tender cake crumb. Plain yogurt works in a pinch.Pineapple Juice & Milk: Liquid is key in most cakes because it thins out the batter. You typically make pineapple upside down cake with canned pineapple, so use some of the liquid in the can for the cake batter.My #1 Tip for the Topping: Blot the wet pineapples and maraschino cherries before using. The more liquid in the fruit, the more liquid that won’t “set.” Excess liquid creates an unpleasantly wet cake.Prepare the topping: Melt the butter, pour into an un-greased cake pan or pie dish, sprinkle with brown sugar, then arrange the blotted pineapple rings and maraschino cherries as you see in my photos and video tutorial. I always refrigerate the topping as I prepare the cake batter—this helps solidify the designed arrangement underneath the wet cake batter.Prepare the cake batter: Whisk the dry ingredients together. In a separate bowl, cream the butter and sugar together. Beat in the egg whites and vanilla, then the sour cream. Pour the dry into the wet ingredients, pour in the pineapple juice & milk, and then beat to combine. You’ll have about 2 cups of cake batter and it’s very straightforward to prepare.Spread over topping: Pour and spread the cake batter over the chilled topping.Bake: Because of the wet bottom layer (which is the topping), the cake takes much longer than a typical 1 layer cake. Its juices will bubble up the sides, creating these incredible caramelized edges. (They’re so good!) With upside down cakes, it’s always good practice to place a baking pan or sheet on a lower rack to catch any juices should they splatter over the edges.Cool: Cool the cake for 20 minutes before inverting onto a serving plate. Inverting any sooner will create a seeping mess—we want the topping to “set” as much as it can. You can serve this cake warm, though it slices much better if you let it cool completely at room temperature first.Expect a Dense CakeI’ve been making pineapple upside down cake since I could hold a spatula. I’ve made hundreds of versions, or so it seems, and I say with 100% certainty that this cake will always be on the denser side. (Unless you are using store-bought cake mix.) You see, the cake is served upside down. The weight of the topping, which is the bottom of the cake as it bakes, weighs down the crumb beneath it. Pineapple upside down cake will never be as light and airy as white cake. If you were to make this exact cake batter and serve it right-side-up, the cake would taste much airier.Does that make sense?I know you’ll love its unique texture, especially paired with the brown sugar caramelized fruit topping. Let me know how you like it!IngredientsTopping1/4 cup (60g) unsalted butter, melted1/2 cup (100g) packed light or dark brown sugar8–10 pineapple slices (see note)*15–20 maraschino cherries (see note)*Cake1 and 1/2 cups (177g) cake flour (spooned & leveled)1 teaspoon baking powder1/4 teaspoon baking soda1/2 teaspoon salt6 Tablespoons (85g) unsalted butter, softened to room temperature3/4 cup (150g) granulated sugar2 large egg whites, at room temperature1/3 cup (80g) sour cream, at room temperature1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract1/4 cup (60ml) pineapple juice, at room temperature (use leftover from can)2 Tablespoons (30ml) milk, at room temperatureCook Mode Prevent your screen from going darkInstructionsPreheat oven to 350°F (177°C).Prepare topping first: Pour 1/4 cup melted butter into an ungreased 9×2 inch pie dish or round cake pan. (Make sure the pan is 2 inches deep. I recommend this pie dish, which is 1.8 inches deep but I never have an overflow issue.) Sprinkle brown sugar evenly over butter. Blot any excess liquid off the fruit with a clean towel or paper towel. (The wetter the fruit, the more likely the cake could overflow or the topping could seep over the sides when inverted.) Arrange about 6-7 blotted pineapple slices and all the cherries on top of the brown sugar. I like to halve 3 pineapple rings and arrange them around the sides of the pan, too. See my photo and video above for a visual of the arranged topping. Place pan in the refrigerator for a few minutes as you prepare the cake batter. This helps solidify or “set” the topping’s arrangement.Make the cake batter: Whisk the cake flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together. Set aside.Using a handheld or stand mixer fitted with a paddle or whisk attachment, beat the butter on high speed until smooth and creamy, about 1 minute. Add the sugar and beat on high speed until creamed together, about 1 minute. Scrape down the sides and up the bottom of the bowl with a rubber spatula as needed. On high speed, beat in the egg whites until combined, then beat in the sour cream and vanilla extract. Scrape down the sides and up the bottom of the bowl as needed. Pour the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients. Turn the mixer onto low speed and as the mixer runs, slowly pour in the pineapple juice and milk. Beat on low speed just until all of the ingredients are combined. Do not over-mix. You may need to whisk it all by hand to make sure there are no lumps at the bottom of the bowl. The batter will be slightly thick.Remove topping from the refrigerator. Pour and spread cake batter evenly over topping.Bake for 43-48 minutes, tenting foil on top of the cake halfway through bake time to prevent the top from over-browning before the center has a chance to fully cook. The cake is done when a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out mostly clean—a couple moist crumbs are OK. Don’t be alarmed if your cake takes longer or if the cake rises up and sticks to the foil. (We serve the cake upside down anyway!)Remove cake from the oven and cool on a wire rack for just 20 minutes. Invert the slightly cooled cake onto a cake stand or serving plate. Some of the juices from the topping will seep over the sides—that’s ok. You can slice and serve the cake warm, but the slices will be messy. I find it’s best to cool the cake completely at room temperature before slicing and serving. Do not refrigerate the cake to speed up the cooling process because it could end up tasting overly dense.Cover leftover slices and store for up to 3 days in the refrigerator or 3 months in the freezer. Thaw at room temperature. I don’t recommend freezing the cake as a whole because the topping arrangement doesn’t thaw very nicely

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly one of the best Metroidvanias I've played. I see this game having a lot of replay value for me, especially when they bring out the extra content later (NG+, boss rush, dungeons, etc.) Things I liked:Combat - The combat in this game feels great, but a little weird at first. You may notice a very slight delay when attacking because the attack button is bound to both attack and charge attack, but you get used to it very quick. I hardly noticed it within about 10-15 minutes of playing. I also like the fact that there's animation cancelling. Soundtrack - The soundtrack in this game is very good. The songs for each area really helped with setting the tone of the game. The only thing I somewhat dislike is that some bosses have the same song, but it's only for a few. Even then the boss themes are still good. Setting - The setting of this game is good. Typical gothic architecture which I enjoy. Not much to say here.Difficulty - The difficulty of this game feels good. Most bosses took me three or more attempts, some only took two or less. The attack patterns for the most part are pretty simple and easy to dodge. Enemies feel a little spammed at times, but it's only a few. This is one of the few Metroidvanias, much more, Souls-likes where the areas actually felt hard to me. PSA: I've seen a few reviews complain about areas where enemies are too tanky and they're being one-three shot. Here's a couple tips. 1. LEVEL VIGOR. A little crazy I know, but leveling vigor increases survivability. 2. EXPLORE. This is not a linear game. You are meant to explore the world. If you are getting one-three shot that typically means you aren't ready for the area and should go somewhere else. I speak from experience. I've had plenty of times where I've gone to an area and died immediately. Things I feel could be updated/changed (or mixed opinions):Rebind controls - If you play this game on mouse and keyboard you don't have an issue with this but for people like me who like to play Metroidvanias on controller I wish we could rebind the controls. It kind of sucks that we're stuck with the controls we're given. NG+ - I wish NG+ was already implemented as some weapons you don't get until mid-endgame but it'll be here later. Health Adjustment - A couple of bosses could use a health adjustment. By late game I expect bosses to be really tanky, but I feel a couple of them in the early game should be scaled a bit down. Most notably, third boss. The third boss has a LOT of health, maybe a little too much for how much damage we deal early on. Things I disliked:I can't really think of anything I heavily disliked. Outside of what I've mentioned above, this game is great. I'd give this game an 8.5 out of 10, probably a 9-9.5 once the extra content releases. From here I'll just put a bug report in-case the devs look at reviews.- I've noticed a bug where having the  weapon equipped while using the bombs in the  area doesn't remove the blockades. When stepping out of the room, equipping another weapon, then walking back in this fixes the bug and the blockades can be removed. - During the  final boss I was hit by an attack and it clipped me under the map.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic soulsvania that wears its Bloodborne inspiration on its sleeve. For the most part this works out to be a good thing, aside from the frustration of deciding weather its worth using your non-refilling healing items on a Boss fight as you learn the ins and outs of a bosses moveset in the same vein as bloodbornes blood vials which you will have to farm up or purchase every so often to keep pushing a difficult encounter. There is a fair variety of weapons and spells to choose from and and many worthy playstyles for however you would like to invest your level ups; the only downside being that some elemental weapons/spells and the associated status affliction are only so helpful, as basic enemies are rarely worth afflicting, and most bosses are immune to most affects, making an elemental heavy playstyle fall flat in that regard. Difficulty is just about right, few true roadblock bossfights that required heavy grinding to bolster stats to tackle them unless you detoured into a higher level zone to fight a few optional foes ahead of schedule; MOST main progression path bosses felt appropriately difficult with only a few health spongy exceptions.All in all it was a good experience if your looking for a solid Soulsvania hybrid to sink about 20-30 hours into depending on how much you wish to grind and go after every unlockable item on the path to earning the hidden ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played alot of metroidvanias in my life. I have never EVER played one that busted my balls more than this one. On the surface its a fine looking game. Great graphics, simple combat, just another castlevania with some soulslike thrown in. But that facade fades quickly, and whats left is HORRENDOUS design and difficulty that would make "I wanna be the boshy" blush.First issue is that lack of simple soulslike features. No homeward bones, no popable souls for quick cash, this means back tracking is essential for keeping your level ups, and a pain in the ass when your too far forward on a path. Dark Souls would give you a shortcut or bonfire when your about to reach your limit. Last Faith does have both, but either they are hidden behind invisable walls or im just blind, because even when i back track through an area i cleared, i only find side routes to whole new areas with massive spikes in difficulty. Back tracking in any souls game is a smart plan to regroup and refresh with restored items and new levels, but Last Faith almost demands you stop progress and retreat as to not lose that incredibly valuable cash.That leads me into the next issue, the enemies and status effects. Most enemies have status effects tied to their attacks, nothing new but the status effects themselves are incredibly damaging to the player and last forever. Shock lasts about 30 seconds and freezes the player in place every 5 or so seconds, frost freezes the player in place and requires a button mash to get out, curse deals a DOT regardless of status bar, bleed causes damage everytime you roll, all these effects would be fine if not for the fact they proc instantly and last far too long, forcing the player to retreat and wait until the duration is over. On the other hand, YOUR status effects dont last nearly as long, even something as mundane as a souls increasing elixir from kills only lasts like 20 seconds. The game is trying so hard to be difficult but in the worst ways.Hitboxes are inconsistent and not easily readable, general platforming is inconsistent and changes what you can and cant climb on randomly. Your death doesnt show on the map and can be easily lost, enemies are spongy, bosses amplify every con i posted above. The biggest issue i had with bloodborne was the need to farm for blood vials, Last Faith amps that by making them a scarce enemy drop and forcing you to buy them. Leveling up is not just recommended but mandatory to get any form of damage output or vitality. Parrying is inconsistent and unlike Dark Souls or Bloodborne, changes the parameters of a successful parry per enemy, meaning, in Dark Souls you parry as the attack animations starts, Faith cant decide if its before you're hit or as the attack animation starts. I want to like this game. I'm going to restart my playthrough with the full knowledge of how unbearable the game can be in a desperate attempt finish the game. I don't HATE this game, but its easily the most frustrating game i've played in a long time.Update:♥♥♥♥ this game, flushing this ♥♥♥♥ down the toilet. I'd refund it if i could.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely dope little brother of Blasphemous with absolute peak moments and an amazing and gory artstyle.Just gonna start right into it with the big strenght of TLF which are the bosses. Oh boi i played TONS of soulslikes and the bosses in this title are amazing! Super well balanced, feeling very unique and being designed very immersive. Its that type of gameplay that feels like dancing and doesnt even really tilt you when youre losing time and time again just to better understand some patterns and finally overcome the challenge. The soundtrack overall, but especially in the boss fights, is really well done and creates some good tension in the battles! Props for that. I mean there wasnt really a single boss besides the "tutorial" one that felt annoying and lackluster. Theres also a good mix of bosses teaming up, double phasing or going rage on half life, you got everything on the table. Even tho i explored like crazy to not miss anything it seems that i still didnt see multiple bosses which is crazy.The general gameplay as well is very well done and absolutely enjoyable. You gather multiple movements and keys throughout the game to progress, they all add mostly great into battles. The weapons are kinda few, but still enough to be interesting to consider which one to pick and most of the stuff just feels very good in your hands. The various weapons got unique, and hefty hit feedback. You really feel like dishing out some serious damage, it just feels good. Most melee weapons also got special attacks that are very different and super lit. Combat overall is precise and fast paced. Nothing wrong there.When it comes to overall progression and exploration it feels good to get upgrades, strenghtening your char and gathering new equip. I backtracked nearly everything when i got new movements to find some secrets and i had fun doing so.For the overall map design im not that happy. Like there are LOTS of different bioms offering different tones and theyre solid, some are really good, others mediocre. But my issue is that the levels itself are really big, mostly there are like 3-5 switches or something similar hidden to open the "boss door" or some neat shortcuts. Hidden walls are everywhere and i had fun to check for those but overall you find crappy stuff for 90% of places. Heal, ammo, useless bombs or some weapon enchantments that felt useless as well. Meaning even while i kinda liked to explore all it didnt feel very satisfying at all. The loot variety is simply too small. --I quickly wanna highlight that theres no basic amount of heal flasks that you got, so you can basically run out of them, but its very easy to gather them via normal gameplay and cheap merchants in the base. At the end i had around 170 or so while constantly consuming them. Its not an issue at all.--Another con i got is the lore and general immersion. Apart from the boss fights which are absolute peak highlights my vibes toned down quite a lot. The lore seems dull, vague and random to me. It didnt seem very fleshed out and im not sure if you can really get into it and understand whats going on. I tried to and i didnt manage to succeed, maybe its on me idk but i didnt enjoy it. A few biom layouts felt definitely immersive, especially through nice soundtracks or just environmental sounds in general, cool backgrounds and so on but the majority felt empty and soulless for some reason. The artstyle is very very similar to Blasphemous, which i absolutely enjoy and appreciate, especially after they have changed their animations to some sort of cartoon bs. TLF is just oldschool raw and simplistic BP style, its amazing. Some cool artwork, some cool cutscenes and level backgrounds. Good work here <3Overall TLF is HEAVILY inspired by Dark Souls, BB, and BP. Some scenes, enemies, soundtracks and gameplay ideas are kinda directly stolen, which didnt issue me personally tho. I love those games and getting a bit more of that is nice. -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------All in all i had a blast playing through, with some letdowns inbetween but even stronger peaks with pretty much every boss fight, especially the late game bosses. I definitely think that BP itself is a better choice, simply for a bigger loot pool and more interesting level exploration. Therefore im not THAT happy with the current price. But thats nitpicking at a very high level. I had lots of fun playing through and i definitely recommend anyone to check this game out that likes good and responsive soul likes with quality bosses and just good gameplay overall!

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get something out of the way real quick - I am huge fan of the original Blasphemous.  I have sunk probably something like 150 hours into both the PC and Switch versions of the game, alongside its Randomizer element (shoutouts to BrandenEK).  I know the game like the back of my hand - the abilities, the glitches in the original release, the sequence breaks, etc.  I'm consciously aware of the game's strengths and weaknesses.I write this as a preface because, inevitably, The Last Faith will draw comparisons to the aforementioned game.  And at face value the comparisons make sense - European-influenced pixel-art style?  Metroidvania trappings?  Large cosmic and faux-gothic horror bosses and enemies?  But as The Last Faith progresses, you'll find a game capable of standing on its own merits, lifting elements from games that came before it and channeling them into a strong addition to the Metroidvania genre, if not necessarily breaking any new ground.  It is NOT a Blasphemous rip-off, nor does it even play or feel very similarly at all.  I'd argue they're actually in different genres - Blasphemous being a quintessential Soulslike, The Last Faith being a Metroidvania.And yes - this game *is* a Metroidvania through and through.  The movement mechanics you develop through the course of the game are inherent to progression through its 15-ish hours of gameplay.  Double jumps and dashes are par the course for the genre, but The Last Faith sprinkles a few interesting decisions into the movepool - not all of them for the better.  I fully get why a grappling hook is an unlockable movement skill - but *two* different kinds of blocked doors that require new skills is a little too much 'padding' for my liking.  There's also one potential frustration in obtaining one specific skill - this is locked behind a badly-indicated, pretty-expensive resource barrier, *and* it's held by an NPC that moves!  One mild spoiler warning - be conscious of what you're spending early on, because grinding to get enough resource to buy the aforementioned skill is slow and dull.Speaking of padding - there's a *lot* of beautiful artwork in this game.  The backgrounds, with their multiple layers of parallax scrolling providing a delightful sense of depth and gravity, are legitimately stunning.  Enemy designs are creepy, distinctive, and unique enough that you're never in any doubt about what challenge is laying before you.  Even such small things as menu icons are brimming with strong artistic decisions that really emphasise the gothic/cosmic horror setting.  I mention "padding", however, as there are a number of re-used assets through the bosses and, bafflingly, some startlingly pretty game areas in which literally *nothing* happens.  No enemies, no collectables, no story, no cutscenes - not a lick.  I assume some these will end up being utilised as part of potential upcoming DLC, or a content patch - but as of this writing, there are far too many of these empty rooms that add literally nothing mechanical to the game.The biggest difference between The Last Faith and the original Blasphemous is in its deep combat system.  Tons of weapons litter your arsenal - melee weapons like hefty greatswords and sizeable battle-axes, firearms from chain guns to dual pistols, dozens of magic attacks, alongside a couple of additional mechanics I shall not spoil here.  There's such a variety that it seems almost criminal that lots of these weapons are found rather far into the game, and with no New Game + option at this writing it seems like players will sink time (and resources) into earlier and more familiar weapons, blocking themselves off from some very fun alternatives.  All the weapons feel great in the hands - swings have weight and impact sounds give immediate feedback, exactly as you'd want from a combat heavy game.  Enemies increase in spongi-ness as you progress, accounting for your improved skills and bolstered statistics - it can be tempting to tread lightly into areas maybe a little too dangerous for your own good, but the drastic change in enemy health-pool is a pretty good indicator of "come back later, you're not ready" that really cements this game also within the realms of Soulsborne games.If it wasn't already obvious, the game takes great inspiration from Bloodborne - and not just in setting and visuals.  The statistic/level-up system is clearly 'inspired', healing and bullets being a semi-finite supply (yes, you can purchase more from vendors but the costs increase as the game progresses and you already have a *lot* of things you need to use your resources for), the combat system is built around aggression and moving forward.  This last point bleeds (pun not intended) into the games bosses - due to the way the game presents its optional parry and defense mechanics, movement and attacking are the most viable options.  Sometimes it's worth taking the risk to go for the final killing stroke, or to tank a little bit of damage because you know you can deal a little more with the chance to heal afterwards.  All the menagerie of monsters on display have well telegraphed and easy-to-read attacks, leaving almost every bit of error to be entirely down to the player (exactly how these things should be, I'd say).  A word of advice - if it seems like you're being hit unexpectedly, watch the attacks more closely.  There's a few strange design decisions here - no crouching attack?  Really? - but overall the game's combat system is a sturdy piece of game design.Sadly, though the game's audio is strong, with good voice acting and chunky sound effects, the music leaves a lot to be desired.  It's nice, atmospheric, and fits the vibe the game is going for - but it's just not that memorable, even through some intense boss battles and some beautiful cut-scenes.  Being a musician I'd normally be all over this but it is possibly the most disappointing part of the game, primarily because it's just *there* rather that elevating the action on screen.I've seen a couple of bugs and small soft-locks through my time with the game - there is a weapon that bugs out certain game mechanics (clearly an oversight and I'm sure it's been noted by the devs), you can accidentally throw yourself through both walls and the floor with another undisclosed mechanic (repeatable but rare, thankfully), and if you get clever but greedy you can end up in a place a little earlier than the game wants you to be, with no way of escaping but death, losing you precious resources.  Asides from that, it's surprisingly sturdy - no hardlocks or crashes, no current way to sequence break, no way to out-of-bounds in a useful way.  This is still less than a week after release, so I don't doubt glitch-hunters and speedrunners will be on the lookout for further shenanigans.The Last Faith is a great-but-mildly-flawed.  A few unusual design choices thankfully are overshadowed by the game's energetic and flexible combat, tough but fair bosses, and stellar art design and atmosphere.  15 hours I haven't regretted, although there are definitely better games on the market.  An easy recommendation if you're a Bloodborne fan or if you are interested in the art style.- No, it's not as good as Blasphemous, but then again few games are!DISCLAIMER - game key was provided directly by the game publisher, but I was intending on buying and playing the game regardless

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend this game, but I wanted to write a note to the devs about what a pile of trash Manfredd is as a boss. He's got a cool move set, but he's the worst kind of bullet sponge. Go watch the videos on Youtube of people fighting him- you use a two handed sword or scythe, or else you suffer through an agonizing fight. His first half of the bar is a cakewalk. So much so that you won't have to heal. But it takes FOREVER to get through. Then the second half of the bar is just a bunch of "Got ya" moments whenever you try to heal. That would be fine if the devs didn't just waste 10 minutes of your time getting through the first half of the bar. The challenge of this boss isn't learning his moves. The challenge is trying to not go insane from the sound of you spam clicking X. And again, if you use a high damage two handed weapon it looks easy. But god help you if you decided to run a dex build with a one handed weapon. For the record I'm level 81 and the rest of this game has been fairly reasonable so far with damage scaling.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs fixes really bad. I love a good hard Soulsvania that requires some discipline and "getting gud."In its current state The Last Faith is cheap. It is a very frustrating game that has the design/writing/art to be a great game.My issues:- The map does not properly convey the geography of the region. What may look like an unexplored ridge is an instadeath jump.- Too many jumps in this game are insta-death overall.- No pausing when accessing menus. If you are lost and not aware an offscreen enemy is about to throw something at you, you can die while looking at the map- All items need to be equipped to an item bar to be used, and have to be cycled through with the dpad in order to use. If you are frozen by an enemy and want to clear the status, you are not really given enough time to cycle through your equipped items to find which pixelated squiggles helps relieve frost before the status kills you.- Items take too long to be used in relation to how fast the combat is. If all fighting was measured and souls-like, then finding an opening to use a life saving item would be part of the fight strategy. As it stands it is the only slow and considered part of otherwise twitchy combat.- While there are a few items automatically entered onto the map like the game's equivalent of shrines, and locked doors, bosses are not marked, nor is the last place you died, instadeath areas, or areas blocked by anything besides a locked door. The game allows you to add custom markers, but due to the game not pausing when you access the map (as mentioned above) you may not know exactly where you encountered that boss or lost your life to mark it. - Lack of video and accessibility options. When playing on Steam Deck, you cannot enlarge the text size, even though the area reserved for text when talking to NPCs is about a third of the entire screen, with tiny text in the middle. You could fit comically large text in that allotted space without changing any of the core design. Let me do this.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a classic metroidvania that did the genre justice. 10/10The dark underlying tones of the atmosphere and the story provide similar environs as Bloodborne and Blasphemous in regard to its harkening to a corrupted church experimenting with a disease that spread beyond their control.The gameplay offers a wide range of combat options and tactics with its choice of many primary and secondary weapons, along with a slew of spells at your disposal. Combat mechanics aren't tough to learn and pick up, and integrate well into the movement patterns of the character and enemies. As movement goes (as you can expect with most metroidvanias) the game sticks to the linear pathing and does it well; while some things require a certain amount of precision (wall jump-dodging), there was never a point where it felt overbearing.Backtracking in any metroidvania should provide some sense of accomplishment and desire to explore the map fully rather than exhaust a player and make exploration become a chore. The Last Faith delivers on this and hides many secret areas that can be found earlier on in game progression and others that you can see from a distance but know you'll have to wait until you acquire that double-jump to come back for.The art style shares its inspiration with so many other metroidvanias with the typical 8-bit style animation, but it isn't lackluster and stands up in a modern game. The soundtrack for the game isn't anything particularly stunning but melds into the game seamlessly, giving a complete aura to the areas a player explores and the bosses they fight along the way.All in all, The Last Faith is a great metroidvania title that I can recommend strongly to those who have never played a game in the genre before, as it is a great example to draw from and offers a friendly learning and integration of controls and skills as the game progresses; it's certainly a game I would recommend to any fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: When writing this review: 8 hours in and 37% completed. I like it a lot so far, as someone else already commented it really scratches that Blasphemous itch for me but it also is it's own game. Atmosphere and Level-Design fit well together and exploration is awarded appropriately, I also love that fast travel is unlocked from the start as you need to backtrack after gaining new mobility tools quite early (put marks on your map!). Combat feels fluid and there are a lot of options for how you fight, boss moves are well telegraphed imo. Bosses (6 or so until now i think) so far never felt unfair and after dying a few times and learning the movesets they can be beaten quite easily (not saying they are easy just beatable with effort yk).At the start it's a bit too linear (I got lost and wandered around for 30min bc I didn't see the one single door to progress) but it then opens up and you have the choice in which area you want to progress. Although for some areas it's obvious you are supposed to do them later since the enemies are stupidly overleveled and you do no damage. That's the one thing I wish they did better by adjusting enemy strength to your own level.Except the 10% discount when I already bought it I'm quite happy with the game as a whole experience and can recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: "A BLAST!"Not sure why the initial negative reception here. This one is a very competent and satisfying soulslike, including metroidvania exploration, thrilling combat system, gorgeous pixel art and animations, huge map full of secrets with environmental puzzles which are actually clever and epic boss fights. If this is your thing, you WILL have a blast.20 hours in and you are nowhere near the end. it comes eventually, and the only gripe I have is that I would have liked even more content with combat-style-specific bosses, so that the 3 builds you can max out could truly shine independently.  It does not reach the highs of Hollow Knight fame... but the overall combat and all the bosses are over the top. A better map grid in the menu would have really helped (it is the worst part of the game, which is sad for a metroidvania) as well as higher difficulty toward the end of the game, with maybe a higher monster density. These are the only things keeping this game slightly back compared to Blasphemous 2 and Hollow Knight. Although the grim mood and the beautiful pixel art with gripping combat, make it worth your while, everyday, twice on sundays. No doubt.EDIT: This review was edited after finishing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing! A Perfect mix of Bloodborne and Castlevania.This game was a blast, the somewhat klunky and heavy feel of combat and general scenery took some getting used to but once I did, I couldn't stop playing. Early into it's release there were quite a few bugs but non that ever really impacted my experience but with some patches they've mostly been fixed. _childDocuments_.review: Released on November 15, 2023, The Last Faith: Unveiling a World of Conflicts and Inspired by the Elegance of Bloodborne.Strengths:The Last Faith, developed by Kumi Souls Games, stands out for its non-linear approach and progression tied to the gradual discovery of character enhancements. The choice to offer a wide range of weapons and abilities, reminiscent of the metroidvania tradition, allows players to face challenges in a varied manner. The combat system is robust, providing strategic options for both close-quarters combat and dealing with adversaries at a distance. The narrative, although based on elements found in text files and letters, maintains a balance between clarity and the need for exploration, delivering an engaging experience.Weaknesses:The Last Faith, heavily inspired by Bloodborne, may be accused of lacking originality in its aesthetics and setting. The resemblance to characteristic elements of Yharnam, such as gothic architectures and the presence of disease in the story, may lead to direct comparisons. While the game has its own soul, some moments in the initial phases may border on imitation. Additionally, although exploration is encouraged, the lack of subjectivity in the narrative may leave some players seeking a more immersive experience.Innovations and Consistency:Despite evident influences, The Last Faith offers notable innovations, especially in the successful combination of metroidvania and soulslike elements. Backtracking, a genre characteristic, is well-managed with strategically placed teleportation points, providing smooth gameplay. The dark-gothic atmosphere, although reminiscent of Bloodborne, has a distinctive soul, contributing to the uniqueness of the game. The artistic quality, game solidity, and engaging story, despite being familiar, elevate The Last Faith above mere imitation.Conclusion:The Last Faith emerges as a successful metroidvania, balancing tradition and innovation in a captivating manner. While some may point out its striking similarities with Bloodborne, the game transcends these influences to offer a unique experience. Its straightforward narrative, combined with solid and varied gameplay, positions it as a notable addition to the genre. Despite facing competition in a saturated genre, The Last Faith stands out as a work that honors its roots while adding layers of complexity, providing players with an engaging and challenging journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend this game, with some caveats. Solid 7/10, middle-shelf Souls-Castlevania-clone. Wait for a sale. There's no real BIG downside, but a bunch of piling little ones that make for some irritating sections. Listing a couple examples below:  --Enemy attacks can be finished (as in, they return or are in the process of returning to their neutral state), but the damage frames of their attack are still active resulting in damage being taken. --Due to this game not having contact damage (Definition: When the player model contacts with the enemy model, regardless of whether either party is attacking, and takes damage just from contact), the dodge roll does not have invincibility frames. Except sometimes it does, but not with all attacks? And it's never clear, because you can dodge roll the same attack twice and the first time you'll take damage, but the second time you won't. --There's a parry mechanic. Introduced very early into the game, and you're given plenty of enemies to test out your parry move against. This parry is pretty good, because it also acts as a form of health restoration. Unfortunately, the further you get into the game, the same problems like with the dodge roll begin to appear. You can parry one attack from an enemy in Junas Ministry, and then the exact same attack won't be parryable (even if the attack is the exact same). For the most part, if the attack is preceded with a white glint and a 'ting' sound effect, it can be generally parried. But even that isn't consistent. --No NG+. --A need to farm for restoratives (Both Health and MP). Unless you're The God-Gamer who can play it blind-folded, backwards, drunk, and one-handed, damage is inevitable in one form or another (and usage of abilities is also inevitable unless you stick with the game's fairly bland attack strings). Having to farm blood vials and crystals between boss attempts isn't fun, only tedious. And even if you can buy them from the game's merchants, that's still a need to farm the game's currency to be able to restock. --The above point would be less of a hassle if it weren't for the fact that the game adds to the tedium when trying to farm, purely through enemies being strung out and spread out across multiple screens. I understand this is meant for balancing combat encounters, ensuring the player doesn't face too many at the same time. But when trying to farm for levels and resources, again. Tedium.

_childDocuments_.review: A Metroidvania with the bones of Blasphemous and the blood of...uh, Bloodborne. The Last Faith wears it's influences on it's sleeve and as such will be compared to them based on look and feel alone. But does it live up to those heights?Honestly, I'm not really interested in questions like that. Everything is derived of something else, no one creates in a vacuum. Moreso I am interested in how much something is able to take from it's influences while providing something different or new. And even more than that, even if it's something completely derivative, is it fun? Did I like it or enjoy it? Is it a good game? The answer to that question is yes. The Last Faith is a good game. It's a fun game. It's a very enjoyable game.Well that was an easy review.Fine, I'll delve a bit deeper. From one look the aesthetic is executed extremely well and I can say that it's influences delivered a style and not a mirror image. While keeping a similar feeling to those worlds, Last Faith makes it's own locations, people and creatures come alive with it's own unique ideas and wonderful pixel art and animation. There is a large variety of locales with not everything having the same coloration, tone or feeling and yet it keeps the world feeling contiguous and same; i.e. not just haphazard unrelated areas thrown next to each other but mountains, swamps, cities with their own individual flavor and everything grounded in the whole overarching world. Visuals for this game are wonderful.Gameplay is great. You have five stats to level that will govern your health and what types of weapons and damage you can use or do, and while there isn't an enormous variety there is certainly enough to make you change up your loadout when you find a new one for your build. The item variety around the damage types is generous so they expect you to regularly use the bombs and curatives they give you. Sure healing items and bullets for your gun are finite and you need to scrounge or buy them but I never found myself running out and having to grind for them like in Bloodborne. As a Metroidvania you will gradually acquire new abilities and maybe it's just my tastes but I found myself a bit overwhelmed at the choices to the extent that sometimes I'd forget I had an ability because they gave me so much to play with. Then again, people love third person character action games with weapon switching and three different modes and parries and stringing crazy stuff together so perhaps they'll adjust easier than I did. Without using a couple of them maybe I made things harder for myself but it also didn't impact my enjoyment. Combat remains fun throughout and I'd actually argue that as the game goes on the bosses become more and more enjoyable to fight. There are one or two optional ones and a couple near the end that I found really well balanced and super fun.The music is quite good, themes humming in and out from different areas or to indicate a save room or just to have a cool accompaniment to a boss. Voice acting is similarly nice. Art and pixel work as said above is phenomenal.My complaints are small. A couple optional fights that were re-used noticeably down to the mid fight damage switch. Bad signposting in one area of the game that made me confused where I was supposed to go. Maybe enemy health was a little too high as I always felt normal enemy fights were slightly longer than they should be? Biggest critique being that the story is not complicated or convoluted but it sure feels that way due to the way it's told. Sure sure, we're all used to the Soulslike formula of item descriptions and vague dialogue and there's something inherently charming and thrilling in figuring things out that are hinted at or laid softly at your feet. But you really need to be careful with your wording when doing things this way as there are many times in this game where an NPC or item was communicating an important story part to me and I had question marks for eyes because the way they said it was so obtuse or meandering that it completely lost me. At the end, I did understand what had transpired and the flow of events but that was in spite of the writing and not because the writing was so good at leading me. Again though, this is a small critique and the biggest one I can muster.All in all, it's more than the sum of it's parts. It is not a reskin, it is not a copy, it is very much it's own thing and a passionate project that should be judged on it's own merits. Played over the course of a couple days because Last Faith was engaging throughout and I wanted to see where it went.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Metroidvania genre continues to add repertoire to its arsenal, with constant releases that don't seem to stop. This time, The Last Faith joins the ranks with a dark gothic setting that places us in a world inspired by titles like Castlevania, Blasphemous and Bloodborne. In addition to the mix of genres that is already Metroidvania, we'll also see Soulslike elements such as level progression, weapons with specific stat scaling and challenging but fair bosses. While it doesn't bring anything new to the table, The Last Faith provides an interesting experience and proves that even if a game draws from others, if done right it results in something just plain fun.In the Last Faith we assume the role of Eryk, a traveler who has no memory of his immediate past, and who’ll have to act in search of a cure for the strange affliction he suffers from, before it's too late. We'll travel through a devastated and dark world, and we'll face a variety of mutated creatures, religious with their own motivations and so on, and we'll also meet the few poor people who still maintain a shred of sanity, while we seek that Eryk does not lose his. The story is cryptic in style, reminding me of Dark Souls, where you have to tie up loose ends, read descriptions of objects and pay attention to conversations and abandoned notes, to hopefully form an idea of what's going on. It's not that complex to follow, although it can confuse us from time to time. It's interesting but not what attracted me the most to the game.What caught my attention the most when I saw the game for the first time was its visual section, what a surprise, right? I know I talk a lot about pixel art, but I can't help but get hung up on the incredible design in The Last Faith. No matter the location, the backgrounds and environments always look immaculate. From the dreary swamp with colors that scream "this reeks of death", to interiors that pay the utmost attention to detail with objects stacked nearby and the like. I'll also mention that the animations are fluid and feel very cool, both for attacks and executions, moves where an enemy gets dizzy and we can finish them off, preferably in a very bloody way. The enemy design is quite varied, leaving aside the amount of bat-like creatures, and the bosses have sprites that raise the level of detail to the maximum. You can instantly appreciate the level of effort put into this section, truly excellent.As for the gameplay, we'll have a progression system very similar to Dark Souls, where we'll have to use our resources, in this case Nycrux, to increase our parameters and thus our level. At the start we'll have four predetermined builds, and each one focuses on a particular stat, such as strength or dexterity. However, like other games of this kind, we can put the points where we want, and make our own personalized build.In addition to the stats, we'll have a variety of weapons for our arsenal, although we'll have to find them as we explore. Some scale better with dexterity, others with strength, and so on, so you have to choose which one to use depending on the type of character you're building. The only thing I found a bit disappointing was that most of the weapons are pretty scattered after about half of the game (or so I felt), and at first it was hard to find something that I really felt comfortable with. To make matters worse, I spent so many resources on the initial sword that I then had to farm a bit to be able to upgrade the cool scythe I found later.Because of course, you can't not have a weapon upgrade system in this kind of game. We'll be able to increase the effectiveness of our weapons after meeting a certain NPC, using Nycrux and minerals. It should be noted that the Nycrux is the only currency in the game, so it’s used for everything as you can see, and it’s kind of necessary to manage it for leveling up, purchases, etc. There are several other NPCs, and while not all of them sell something, they will always have something to say at first, or some mission to give, but as there are no objective markers on the map you have to pay attention to dialogues and explore.I mentioned before  the fluidity in the animations, and it also feels that way in terms of controls, both in rolling and jumping, and fighting. Combat is dynamic and fun, and the variety of enemies means it doesn't get too repetitive. Adding to the repertoire of melee weapons, we'll also have pistols and shotguns, amulets that increase different parameters, stigmata that give us skills such as shield or more attack speed, and of course, spells and gadgets. From fireballs to electric force fields. As far as exploration is concerned, we'll be able to go through an interconnected map very in tune with the genre, full of secrets and passages. The platforming aspect feels pretty good, although it has some details with the ledges; sometimes Eryk had a hard time holding onto them, but it was something very sporadic. Like other Metroidvania, we'll also have skills for exploration, such as grabbing onto certain walls or the mythical double jump! By the way, it looks super cool here, it reminded me a lot of Hollow Knight’s Monarch Wings.Although it has some details that frustrated me a bit, like the ice zone that I suffered a bit early in my adventure; and the amount of enemies firing homing projectiles is a bit questionable. I also felt it slowed my progress a bit when I ran out of syringes, and had to go back to farm them, or get Nycrux to buy them. Fortunately, for the bosses at least they leave you four nearby, and past a certain point I no longer had any problems with this. I recommend not saving your Nycrux as much as I did and leveling up or upgrading weapons frequently, even though this can lead to lowering the difficulty level of some fights.The inspirations are more than obvious, but they don't subtract from the experience or make it any less unique. The Last Faith stands on its own feet and offers a nice proposal to the genre, a fun experience, which is what I particularly look for, beyond other aspects. The visuals are gorgeous, and the music is very atmospheric, especially the piano melodies; and the voice acting adds a very special touch. The combat is the icing on the cake, and the bosses present a solid challenge. In conclusion, a game that meets expectations, and that personally leaves me intrigued to see what else the studio will develop in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really enjoying this game for the first couple of hours, right up until I got to the ice area. Ice areas are always trash in virtually any game, for the usual reasons. All of those go without saying. But the game's flaws started to really become oppressive.Let's start with this game's single most absurd thing: Why are you going to give me a gun, give me a Gunslinger style build, and then make the gun completely useless? Every enemy in the game that should reasonably be vulnerable to a gun -- namely, the jumping spider guy who leaps out of the way as soon as you swing at him, who keeps you at a distance, who spits a ranged weapon back at you, exactly the kind of enemy that is begging for some kind of long-ranged weapon to chase him down with -- every single enemy who you should be using the gun against CANNOT BE HIT BY THE GUN. They are too short. And your character, for whatever reason, cannot jump and shoot, nor can he crouch and shoot, at the same time. You cannot aim the gun. It fires one projectile, directly forward, that does no more damage than your basic attack, even though it consumes an expendable resource. It has no more stopping power than your normal attacks. I really want an answer from the developers on this. Why can I not crouch and shoot?This game also does an absolutely horrendous job (that is, none at all) of telegraphing when a pit is bottomless or not. The game teaches you that there is no fall damage, so naturally you will try to jump into pits because there is often progression there, and the game's horrendous map also shows bottomless pits on the map with an open border which, in any other MV style game, would indicate clearly that there is map progression beyond that pit. MULTIPLE times I have fallen down a pit thinking there's ground below and I just die. The dev's solution to this is to put a temporary checkpoint just before the pit so when you inevitably try to do the thing the game has taught you to do, you will be able to respawn close by. So my indication that a pit is lethal now is that the developer has put a safety net in the screen just before it. Idiotic. And the game doesn't even have the decency to fill in the map where the pit was!The game's progression felt near perfect up until the ice area where every room will have 4-5 enemies swarming you all at the same time AND environmental hazards AND status ailments all affecting you at once. I don't understand this sudden change of pace.I've put the game down and I'm probably not coming back to it for a long time, if ever, unless it gets some serious gameplay tweaks to make it not waste my time. Given that it looks like a lot of this stuff was brought up in the beta and not fixed, I'm not holding out hope.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try to be 100% honest, if you're a souls-game fanatic like me, play this game. Otherwise, play Blasphemous.NOW, THE PROS- The gameplay is very enjoyable. You have a wide variety of melee and ranged weapons (and a huge collection of items) to sweeten your combat experience. As a souls-like it's not too punishing. Most of the bosses are easy. When you die to a boss, you never loose your currency. It spawns just beside your latest save point.  Also, regular mobs have repetitive attack pattern, so they aren't much of a challenge either.- The weapon design is the best aspect of this game, they are a fine blend of steampunk and gothic art design. Similar to Bloodborne, all of them have a special attack where they may change the shape or grant the player some special combo or magic.- There is no stamina cap. You can keep spamming the attack button, jump and dodge as many times as you want.NOW, THE CONS- Sadly, this game has lots of negative sides. It's unfinished and unpolished. There is no graphics adjustment settings. You can't change the resolution, can't turn off the v-sync, can't change from fullscreen to borderless. If you have dual monitors or want to play in ultra-wide, you''ll have a hard time adjusting.- Parrying is very weird in this game. You can't parry normally until you've killed your first boss. Then you'll be granted an item called 'Stigma' which lets you parry. What's worse, parrying is dependent on a meter which is called Power Meter and you have to fill it by attacking enemies but it runs out quickly, making you stop parrying after every 2-3 times which I didn't find enjoyable. Also, Power Meter is needed for a certain ability later in the game. So if you use that ability, your meter goes empty and voila, no more parrying. This is infuriating.-  When you're doing combo attacks the controls feel unresponsive. After a dodge or heavy attack you can't immediately start regular attacks. The player's movement is heavy and clunky. It was released in June 13, 2023, received a bunch of updates and all the devs did are adjusting a few damage numbers and a skill reset but no actual improvements. SHAME!- The fast travel locations are all jumbled. They are neither arranged alphabetically nor in the order they're unlocked, so who tf even decided to arrange them like that?- The game is a mixture of Blasphemous, Bloodborne and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. Took the core mechanics of all three games and made a meaningless blend.The art style and weapon design copied Bloodborne, the combat copied Blasphemous and platforming copied Castlevania. I agree that most of the modern platformers copy Symphony of the Night. Modern games upgrade old mechanics and make them better, that's why people love them. But this game feels like a downgrade, it does nothing new, nothing memorable.- The story makes no sense, it's inspired from Bloodborne (or should I say outright copying). Just like the FromSoft's fan favorite title, this game also features Eldritch beings, a powerful man who wields their power, a cult who worships them and him, a mysterious affliction named Shadow Scourge (similar to Ashen Blood) which turns people into monsters and after the hero manages to acquire some secret items he have the option to kill these Eldritch beings and end this nightmare. But here are lots of unanswered questions -- The Shadow Scourge is very confusing cuz it turned some into vampires, some into ghastly looking things and others remain normal but went mad instead. I get the 'driven mad by eldritch knowledge' part but there should be some insight to make us understand who becomes who.- Our hero, Mr. Eryk is also infected with this Shadow Scourge but his infection transforms him into a Frankenstein-like superhuman. There are 2 more test subjects that are like him but how a disease which came from some cosmic being causes entirely different mutations in different persons? The devs probably thought that, it'll be cool to add Vampires, meaningless grotesque monsters, zombies and Yetis all in a same game. No sir, they messed up the story.- Bloodborne shed some light about how the Eldritch blood was the reason of the affliction. But The Last Faith doesn't provide any suitable explanation about what is what and why is why.- There are multiple factions with no actual goal or contribution to the story, What is Sepolcri? Who are the Starborne and why they're at war with Ethereal Order? Who was Eryk, why he was locked inside the Temple of the Deposed Gods? No explanation, like the devs added so many elements but later forgot what to do with them.There are lots of minus sides I haven't touched yet, but this review is getting bigger and more boring, so that's it folks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the closest to the C:SOTN we ever got. If you enjoy Metroidvanias, this is a no-brainer.- Level design is great, better than Blasphemous 1 and 2- Lots and lots of enemies to fight against- Tons of hidden areas and optional locations- Responsive movement- Great art-style- Large amount of spells and weapons- Couple challenging bossfights- Satisfying combat- You receive tons of items you will never use because game forces you to swap single item slot... Controller scheme should be made differently with shortcuts for more than just one item. It should just use d-pad to use up to 4 items immediately.- Rewards for exploration are a mixed bag. Sometimes you can see an item that you can't reach for the 70% of the game and once you get an ability to reach it - it's a healing item that you already had or something similar.- While art-style is great and backgrounds are awesome, some tiles are repeated or mirrored which looks awkward especially on small platforms. It's something that Blasphemous dealt with perfectly but here it's jarring at first. Not a deal-breaker though.- Anti-climactic lack of animations in some areas. In many places you activate something and either screen fades to black and  it feels like there should be some kind of animation happening but nothing is going on, it fades in again and now you're in a different location or suddenly an item becomes active. It was confusing and a bit awkward but it might be just budget cuts. It's not a huge problem.- Recycled bosses, it felt like many bosses were very similar in their looks, their move-set was different though which was great.- Too many "exploding" enemies - that's a very subjective one but it kinda bothered me how many enemies were burning me after death for no good reason, like there was a tree-type enemy who did not have fire attacks at all and yet after killing him, he started burning which caused me to burn too if I was too close. That's fine with couple enemies but I felt like there were too many of them.The game is overall great. The overall fun factor in it is on par with Blasphemous 2 in my opinion, although it's not a game without its own issues. Still, it's one of the better Metroidvanias I played and it feels very close to C:SOTN.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulslike are some of my favourite games. I loved Hollow Knight and "cryptic" hard metroidvanias...as long as the mood and story holds them.In soulslike games story is told through legends and item descriptions, letting you creating your own narrative through obscure - but pretty clear in words - references. Hollow Knight starts mysterious but it becomes clearer the more you go onward with the game, both in lore and story.The Last Faith...tries to recapture the mystery of soulslike and modern metroidvania like blasphemous and hollow knight, except it does it in a weird way.People will tell you the story...but in such a convoluted and verbose way, that you cannot really understand it.After finishing the true ending, I have still NO IDEA why this game happened at all. I think I have a pretty good grasp of english language, and yet I do not know who the NPCs are or what they want, I do not know who the bosses were, and I did not understand a single thing that happened in the ending.All because characters just speak weird and and cryptic, and the notes give you snippets that don't make any sense unless you open your menu and start reading them one after the other. I don't think this works, like, at all. It made me bounce off the immersion from the game, and made everything lose an edge even if the mood and pixel art is great.I also found the fact that you have to grind "souls" to get some spells/upgrades for weapons since they cost so much INCREDIBLY painful. This game makes grinding boring, I do not care for going back into places that I have already visited, but I did not mind it in Hollow Knight, for example. I don't know why, or how, but this game does it wrong.I found the gameplay pretty standard for a metroidvania. I again wish there was a "neutral" or "meh" option for reviews...I'm going to choose not recommended because 27 euros is WAY too much for a game with a gameplay this basic and not understandable story.It's good at around 15 euros though, so if you ever find it for that price, I'd say it's a good buy.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the art. Just look at it. Visually in most ways superior to Blasphemous and just the best looking pixelart metroidvania full stop.The arsenal is great. Multiple weapons with different move sets and special, scaling, status damages etc. All look awesome and fun to experiment with. I found pistols and spells (except some late-game ones) very underpowered but that's also not where I invested my stats.That's ok, melee is strong enough, feels punchy and every enemy has a gory finisher. Wouldn't hurt if the game had some way to communicate status effect weaknesses and go deeper into the significance of some RPG elements that here are rather surface-level.Another strong point is bosses IMO, are really good and pose a reasonable challenge. Fun to learn. 5-10 tries each is a good sweet spot, big plus.Pary window is super lenient but still way too risky, I barely used it. Shame almost all magic is offensive. There is no way to block till very late into game so the only way to survive against enemy attacks is dodging and positioning in general.This exacerbates what many people seem to hate about the game - some mid-game mob enemy setups are incredibly annoying, and that's where the game is often at its weakest.Most enemies fire homing projectiles that are way too fast and in way too many cases fly through the scenery, often leading to stunlock and very cheap feeling deaths. This can be truly infuriating when entering areas underleveled - the game often allows you to explore areas in an order you choose but is balanced around the "correct" one. Just don't get into the frozen cave the first occasion you get.In addition, the game pushes item scarcity way too far towards "hoard and never use" territory. Health injections are limited and do not replenish on death which is a pain in the ass in early game, until you find a vendor that sells them at your base.Platforming is mostly fine except for instances where you need to make leap of faith type jumps that result in death unless you've done it before, mostly in optional areas but that is still poor design in my book.On that note, the map is absolutely horrible. Makes is way harder to asses how far you're into exploring an area - why don't ladders or elevators show up as outlined connecting paths between different screens but look as if there is an unexplored gap in the area? I haven't seen a single bug (except one progression breaker with a weird workaround, thanks forum), and the 100% achievement on Steam is broken for everyone atm.Overall, a great debut for the studio. Far from perfect, but despite minor annoyances about mid-way through, I loved the journey.If you liked Blasphemous make sure to check it out.8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game BUT I highly recommend against it because of some quite strange design decisions. The good things:- art, style and atmosphere (yes, yes... All the Bloodborne on PC jokes are partially correct)- enemies, combat and variability of it - some good design decisions E.g: finishing enemy off with the "special" killing blow not only shows unique animation, but also replenishes mana and grants extra currency. Or dying to a boss respawns your lost "souls" next to a save spot, rather than on boss arena (which is nice, since it's more metroidvania, than actual soulslike), etc. Some "OK" things:- map design could be better, honestly. You have a room with a bottomless pit falling to which kills you instantly. Ok. Quickly enough you learn that those are marked with red on a game map and that is NOT a transition to a new area. Yet you have a room above this room directly which has a bottomless pit as well. You would expect that you fall through to a level below, but no. That's instant death as well, lol. Confusing stuff. - some areas are there as a hommage to souls/borne? Like the swamp location. Why is it there? What purpose? No special boss, no plot, no lore. Just three screens of a biome that annoys you for what? But diversity is fun, ok.- Mana/power system is confusing at best. You have "magic" that uses "blue" mana bar, and then you have "special ability" that uses "light blue" mana/power bar. Oooookaaaaay, totally not confusing. Wasn't using those much, so, ok.- I finished the game with 2/3 endings, killing most of the bosses, yet I still can't say if there's a parry system in this game and how it works. At times when fighting certain bosses they were getting staggered (no special moves from my side) and pressing "Y" executed a special animation that heavily damaged them. (Just like in BB) Why? Did I meet some requirements to do that? Did I meet some timings while counter attacking? I have no clue. Anyways, if you don't ask questions - you won't get confused. :)And finally the bad parts that won't allow me recommend the game in the current state:- controls. I don't know if that's a problem with optimizing XBOX controller specifically for this game, or is this happening with all the gamepads, yet the movement is quite clunky. Especially when it comes to jump attacks. I completed the game with a two handed sword and multiple times I had a strange problem with "faulty swings" where the character would shake the sword as if he was about to swing the sword, yet it never happened. Only releasing the attack button for a second and pushing it again resulted   in a proper swing. (NOT if you tried to jump at the same time, lol). So yeah, either gamepad support is not perfect or the controls are not pinpoint accurate. - Second and the most frustrating thing is game progression. Do you remember all those great game, like Castlevania: SotN, Hollow Knight, Dark Souls 2 and Bloodborne? All of them have true endings, right? And you can beat "final" boss, then read the guides (or explore yourself) and find the missing parts that will lead you to a true ending? Well, imagine achieving first ending in BB (the "yeah, sure, I accept your offer, dude) and boom! - next thing you see is waking up in clinic again (very beginning of the game) and you have to complete the game all over again to try to find the missing parts of the puzzle to a true ending. This game does exactly this: once you do a certain thing (and nothing indicates that you should not do that) - you're locked out of completing the game, unless you re-do it all over from the start. I've put 15 hours to complete it and I have no intention to do it again just because the devs had no better solution. No, seriously... Why, in the first place, somebody thought it was a good idea? And you know what adds to a frustration even more? Certain areas have locked doors and it's not a "hit the wall and find a secret passage there", no. While exploring the map you can navigate to the opposite part of the map and find a mirror that will teleport you exactly to the room behind that locked door. This gives you a false feeling that you are free to explore in your own pace and manner and that you are supposed to look everywhere and kill everything to unlock certaing backtrack paths. It's not. It will lead you to a situation described above. So what we have as a summary: This is a good looking metroidvania with soulslike elements that can boast itself with some great atmosphere and variety of weapons/monsters/biomes and other content, yet it has some critical flaws that come from controls execution and design decision. Once the devs decide to fix it - I would definitely recommend this, but as for now my word is: Either wait for improvements, or just toss down you urge for thrilling exploration and play with the walk through opened on you second screen. Cheers!

Mini map lacks necessary mark.Ex, some parts are death of fallen, and the map shows missing, which is annoying.I have to go back again and again to check if I miss sth.2. Story is too fuzzy.
