_childDocuments_.review: the good:combat feels great. you dont get iframes but you dont need them if you memorize attack patterns, which is the whole purpose of this kind of game and what makes it fulfilling to play through (except maybe for the 2 bosses but even then its manageable). the game is designed to be challenging, which i enjoyed, but even if you're having massive trouble you can respec and try a different/better approach - this is great. the weapons and their variety feel great - you get not just the basic weapon moves but specials as well, and there are tons to choose from (personally the macewhip was my fav, 4th hit on its special attack is the most satisfying thing ever). setting is fantastic - i understand some may not be fans of the grimdark, but i think this game nails that; also if you're a fan of lovecraft, you'll appreciate this game. sound and level design are well made. (neutral):castlevania with bloodborne vibes. personally this clicked with me. it should be noted that this game takes perhaps too much inspiration from Fromsoft games, as in you will not be told where to go almost ever. more importantly, there is no way to track quests, so keep your notepads and guides ready. again, im a huge fan of fromsoft and played through all their games so i didnt mind, but this could be a dealbreaker for some. thankfully you get different map markers to track what you missed without certain upgrades, so exploration is rewarding if you pay attention and use everything that game gives you. story is also a bit hard to follow, but there were enough interesting tid bits which had my attention.the bad:some mechanics feel out of place. there is not nearly enough emphasis on parry - it should have been a core mechanic that could work on all enemies (depending maybe on attack), not just an upgrade you would swap out in the middle of the game. same goes for spells - you can't make a dedicated caster build, you HAVE TO rely on attacks due to very limited mana pool and spell costs. even if cost was manageable, for any spec you choose in terms of stats you will find a weapon that deals more damage than spells, and that's just with basic attacks (discounting weapon specials).finally, perhaps the most important con - having to grind is excusable in games like elden ring (it might either be intended or simply unavoidable). this game simply has no place for it, and you will probably have to do it as the final boss is unbeatable without at least 120 (unless you are a PrO gAmEr which I, and many others, are not).the ugly:development is over from what i've heard. devs promised a few additional features which i would ABSOLUTELY love to see, but it doesn't look like we are getting those, neither any bug fixes. a real shame - with a bit more love this game could be one of the top metroidvanias.conslusion:despite it's flaws, this game deserves a thumbs up. if you're not familiar with the genre, it might take you 30 hours to 100% and get all achievements. it's challenging, even gruelling at times, but extremely satisfying in the end. definitely grab it if it's on sale
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: ProsBeautiful pixel animations and world, very detailed. Enemies, bosses, main character, weapon attacks etc all animated really well.Cool variety of weapons and spells Cool fun bossesNice atmosphere A lot of hidden little destructible walls and secret items hidden out of sight.Enjoyable meaty weighty combatCons:Controls are a bit clunky especially when platforming and trying to grab ledges. (blasphemous 1 had same issue)Annoying Leaps of faith where you cannot see whats below you and need to fall to find out if there are spikes, a death pit, or a safe landing or secret item. Really amateur trial and error design.Status ailments like burning, freezing, nightmare etc need an item to heal them but each tick of damage from the ailment will interrupt your attempt to remedy it leading you to need to almost spam the item to make it work. Its annoying, very clunky and disrupts the flow of combat in a very bad way. Just feels horrible.Lack of memorable music, there is some ok themes in here but more would have been welcome. Poor map use. The map itself is not the problem but how you interact with it when fast travelling. When fast travelling you are forced to choose from a list of fast travel points rather than simply having a zoomed out look at the map and being able to move the cursor to your desired spot. This gets very annoying as you first need to open your map, look at where you want to go and then close map, open fast travel and cycle through the options and try remember which one it was you wanted to travel too. Again it just feels unnecessarily clunky. Some underwhelming upgrades. Having areas blocked off by little blue blocks only to get an upgrade that allows you to push little blue blocks just seems lazy and out of place.I come off quite negative here but I did actually enjoy the game overall but it needs more polish and if a few patches come out that address my issues above I will come back to update my final score. Overall I think this game is worth it if you want a decent metroidvania and like the gothic setting. Final Score. 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Very immersive game. The set pieces and sound design are fantastic. Lots of secrets to uncover from exploring. Grateful there is a stat respec you unlock fairly early on to change builds, but resource prices for upgrading gear are expensive so a lot of grinding is required. Build variety is plentiful, but a lot of the fun weapons are locked behind middle and late game. The game is moderately difficult, but usually consistent, outside of a couple bosses where the difficulty spikes a tad much for a casual player. Absolutely get this game if it goes on sale. Maybe pass on it if you're not a fan of difficulty. Still it has been a solid experience and I'm happy to have completed this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a casual metroidvania and souls-like player. Having competed both Blasphemous games, was looking for something along those lines. Last Faith delivered in spite of some flaws. I actually liked it a little more than B1, much more than B2. I do wish the dev team was more forthcoming on upcoming features or updates.Pros:* Eerie setting* Atmospheric music* Nice pixel graphics* Not overly difficult, still a challenge IMO. I won't post how many times I had to fight a few of the bosses.* Simple character stats* Entertaining fatalities* Able to skip intro cut scenes before boss fights (this is a huge failure in Blasphemous 2 BTW)* Unlike Blasphemous 1 & 2 I could see replaying with a different build* Support for PS5 controllerCons:* Controls felt awkward and unresponsive at times, which took some getting used to* Awkward NPC dialogue from NPCs and in-game documents made it difficult to follow the story. In all   fairness I didn't take notes, which may have helped.* No monster encyclopedia (they show the names when you first kill them, then nothing)* The setting and overall story seemed strangely similar to Blasphemous with regard to the religion theme. _childDocuments_.review: Great art, below average gameplay.Blasphemous (1) is the most obvious point of comparison - clunkier Symphony of the Night-style combat and platforming in a grimdark setting with some light soulslike influences like committing to attack animations and losing your held cash/xp on dying twice in a row. The combat and platforming both feel slightly subpar for the genre - there is significant input delay or turn delay that often prevents quickly turning around and attacking from targeting the right direction, animations do not transition into each other (e.g. charged attacks do not combo into standard attacks), and ledge grabs are finnicky. The movement/exploration upgrades I've found so far have been the most boring of bog-standard metroidvania standbys- things like the ability to push boxes, walljump from specific and rare wall textures, or grapple to specific and rare hooks. In the best metroidvanias, the movement upgrades that gate area progression are all applicable to multiple scenarios: enabling previously impossible progression, improving speed/ease of general platforming while backtracking, and shaking up combat either by providing more ways to positionally respond to enemy actions or by having damaging/debuffing effects. So far, these upgrades have no possible use in  general platforming or combat. Like Blasphemous, there are creative and satisfying execution animations, which seem to be unique for every enemy. Also like Blasphemous, unfortunately, whether these can be triggered seems to be strictly down to an RNG call when an enemy is at low HP rather than as a reward for good play, and having too much damage can render them impossible to trigger for an enemy type, which is a huge shame. Weapon special attacks and spells are both cool, but the mana costs are often too prohibitive to fully incorporate them into combat because there's no mechanic for mana recovery apart from from resting at a checkpoint or using consumable items.The game isn't a soulslike metroidvania (e.g. Salt & Sanctuary, Grime, Unworthy, Death's Gambit), but it does take a bit more influence than Blasphemous. For example, you can level to dump points into various stats - HP, mana, str/dex, etc. Unfortunately, not all the influences it takes are good things, even for fans of both genres. The game starts with a class selection that determines your initial stats, but oddly classes  come with a set of class-essential equipment, like a weapon scaling with your primary stat, a spell for mage classes, or a gun for the marksman class. Cribbing the Dark Souls model for weapon upgrades makes weapon variety illusory, as you'll be locked into whichever weapon you first start upgrading both in the short-term by the fact that newly-discovered weapons would require a significant cash/xp investment to perform well enough to be worth genuinely trying and long-term by the fact that the materials required for weapon upgrades are highly limited. As in soulslikes, rolling gives i-frames -  Most projectiles and certain melee attacks ignore i-frames, and this isn't tied to another system (e.g. the way that some attacks are unblockable or unrollable in Sekiro or Lies of P) or even visually communicated to the player. You'll just be occasionally shocked that your roll did nothing for you and have to memorize that particular enemy attack animation ignores the system. Worst of all, it doesn't take the Dark Souls approach to healing (making a fixed, usually upgradable amount of healing available after every checkpoint use)  influence from the smart approaches of some modern metroidvanias, like the way Hollow Knight and its followers tie the availability of healing to combat performance or others make healing freely available when out of combat. Even old-school metroidvanias like SotN handled healing better by ensuring that (respawning!) healing power-ups were adequately available throughout the levels themselves. Instead, healing in The Last Faith comes in the form of consumable items, a la Demon's Souls/Bloodborne, which can be found as one-time drops in levels, on rare occasions as random drops from enemies, or purchased from some vendors. This means that if you run low, viable exploration range will suddenly and massively drop and bosses will become unbalanced, and rote grinding is the only way to fix it. The bosses I've seen haven't been particularly hard, but that's a concerning problem to see in a genre where learning difficult boss patterns across multiple attempts is a core philosophy. The same is true of bullets, if your build/playstyle incorporates a ranged weapon.Like Blasphemous, this game is carried by its strong visuals and strong art direction, and it's not bad so far, but it's mechanically weak enough that I can't give it a general recommendation in this state. If the art  appeals to you, you'll be able to get past the frustrations and price-point and have a good enough time, but it doesn't seem stand out as either a unique or a well-executed example of the genre from what I've seen.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an interesting mixed bag that is worth checking out; it had it’s strengths & weaknesses.STRENGTHS:-The graphics/music were solid. I liked the horror/vintage style of both as it added to the spooky atmosphere. If ‘Castlevania 2: Simon’s Quest’ was made today, this would have been the perfect brand to tell that story.-It is hard to mix modern weaponry (like guns & explosives) with pre-modern weaponry (like swords & crossbows) into a movie/tv/videogame series without it feeling anachronistic but this game did it very well.-The boss fights were challenging and had some good cinematics (like when you fight the flying skeleton boss and you fall through several floor levels throughout the fight).WEAKNESSES:-When you die, you lose all of your experience (which also doubles as your money/currency throughout the game). Not only that, you have to retrieve it by fighting back to where you lost it which can not only side-track you but make you lose it completely if you can’t get to it (especially since you can use up all your health potions trying to get it back). In addition to the map not showing you where your experience was lost, it made the game less desirable to play. I prefer it when you save a game and die, you simply go back to your save point with all your experience/gear that you had at the time of save so you aren’t spending most of your time trying to regain something you can lose so easily. -Not having health potions to buy from the get-go can be very frustrating, especially given my last point about losing your experience on death.-The plot seemed very cryptic & confusing for no apparent reason. I feel that if you are going to add a plot, it is better to keep it simple if you don’t have a well-fleshed out one at the ready.-While the weapons/equipment/skills were interesting, they felt like that had weird names & backstories that instead of feeling intriguing were simply flashy & pointless.CONCLUSION:-Regardless, the game is worth checking out for it’s strong points, even if you play the game briefly. I think the game makers are very talented and have a lot of potential. If they smooth out the bumps along the way and play to their strengths, they can make great games in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pros:1) Deep, detailed world with plenty to find and very substantial, rewarding side content.2) Great blending of Bloodborne, Castlevania, and Blasphemous for a unique artistic vision.3) Solid mechanics and smooth gameplay.The Cons:1) In the last two areas of the game, excessive enemy/boss health & damage artificially inflate difficulty instead of requiring more skill from the player.2) Clunky pause between rolls/dodges results in unnecessary punishment to the player when trying to learn attacks and combos.3) Consumable healing.Overall, this is a very good video game not lacking in quality, effort, or content for the price. Unfortunately, a handful of small failures in execution impact the game more and more as the game approaches the end and taint the experience slightly when a little bit more polish and rebalancing would have ironed them out. Still definitely worth the playtime and the purchase. A very solid game for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the most clunky and unresponsive games in this genre that I have ever played.It even manages to be comparatively clunkier than dark souls 1, and that game is the clunkiest 3D souls game.- It has queued actions in all the wrong places (for example, if you jump attack and hold the attack button for just a LITTLE BIT longer than the game wants, you'll start another attack when you touch the ground), and missing them in the right places (jumps and dodges don't queue after attacks)- It has a very annoying but reproducible bug where if you attack and then press jump right at the end of the attack, it'll do the lowest possible jump, regardless of how long you hold the jump button- You can't dodge out of crouch, and you can't immediately jump out of crouch either, it's like a 0.5-1 second animation that gets you killed near the endgame if you press it in the wrong situation- Your dodge has like a 1 (or more) second cooldown, and the dumbest part is that this cd is shared with the jump-dash...- It has THE WORST parry I have EVER seen in a game... it's unintuitive and basically just ♥♥♥♥. You're not parrying attacks, you're parrying intentions, you can get good at parrying some low level mooks (like knife guys) and you do it when they raised their hand, not when they actually strike at you...Generally, the combat is rather bad.However, the game makes up for it with amazing bossfights. This game has some of the best bossfights in the genre, some of the best are "Igor and Lena", "Fred the Man", "Patrick 'I AM THE LAST FAITH' Laddack", "Cosmic Voice", "Discount Cthulhu", "Hermann".The game also has absolutely beautiful art, very expansive, and even the background scenery is well thought out and you can tell they put a lot of heart into it (and IMO like 90% of the budget went here xD). Though the only bad thing I can say about the artstyle is that I honestly can't tell the weapons apart from the menu icons, they (and most menu icons in general except for usable items) all look way too similar IMO.The soundtrack is amazing, really can't say anything bad about it.And the most important thing that this game does. The cherry on top. The piece du resistons (or whatever ye French say):THERE IS NO CONTACT DAMAGE!And even if the game was completely garbage, I would still recommend it simply because there is no contact damage.Contact damage is the dumbest mechanic in this genre and should have been discarded and buried when we got machines powerful enough to actually animate attacks (since that's the only reason contact damage existed in the first place).All in all I'd give this game a solid 7/10:- Art: 10/10- Sound: 9/10- Bosses: 9/10- Combat: 8/10-- Sub total: 9/10- Minus 2 whole ass points for clunkiness--- Total: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. And if I could, I would give it neutral review. It could be great game, but... it's very, very unpolished.The Last Faith at first looks like a child of Blasphemous and Bloodborne. But it isn't. It's accursed child od Dark Souls 2, Castlevania and Blasphemous in Bloodborne Halloween costume. It's pretty, has great enemy variety and design, level design is fine, music is ok. Boss battles are on the simpler side, but are mostly fair (except true final boss) and very high quality. Spells and weapons are creative and fun to use.BUT...Controls are one of the clunkiest I've ever experienced. Also, remapping them works awful. And I few times experienced a bug when my controls suddenly are remapped. And only restarting the game fixes it. There are also very small sections of the map, where your controls doesn't work how they normally do. Like, your double jump suddenly doesn't work at all. Sometimes you press dodge ore heal and instead Eryk attacks. Nothing gamebreaking, it wasn't that often.But even when they work as intended, they're not good at all. There are some hidden cooldowns to dodge (with almost zero iframes if it has them at all). And there is latency with almost everything you do. But you know, it is fine, I've got used to it and still had fun.I hate minimap tho. It isn't helpful and how backtracking works here and when some items are hidden... Yeah. Also, changing layers of the map did nothin for me. It's just impractical. I've seen worse. But I hate, when I don't know if it's uncleared room or room, where I can not reach sealing, because it's impossible. Or how bottomles pits or doom are marked. You know that they're pits of doom, because they're red on the minimap. But you must get very, very close to them at the actual level, so they'll get marked.Dialogues and item descriptions here are so boring and convoluted that I couldn't care less. It's edgy story with vampires and pseudo Old Gods, so I'm kinda sad, because it could be good. It could be atmospheric and interesting. Quests are... Yes, they are. And nothing else. No cool rewards, just "Find my old socks", "ok, cool, here is thou achievement".Weapons are fun and great, BUT... WHY MAJORITY OF THEM ARE STRENGTH WEAPONS?! There are four character classes (str, dex, mind and instinct), and almost all weapons are str. Especially in the early and mid game.I'm angry and sad, because The Last Faith has potential to be one of the best soulsvania games. And it was released over year ago. There is no NG+, there is no boss rush. There are not new very needed patches. And this is why my review is negative. Because it's good, fun game, but it's so much unpolished.

_childDocuments_.review: is a masterfully crafted experience that made me wish we had Bloodborne on PC. The game allows you to acquire every achievement in a single play through, which is a plus. I have beaten the game once at the time of writing this review and was locked out of getting 4 achievements on my first play through because I beat the cathedral boss before submitting quest items. While I do find it upsetting I was locked out of achievements for defeating a boss, I had a good time overall. The bosses were easy so long as you had the proper weapon upgrades for the area, which can make switching weapons a bit of a hassle, having to spend the nycrux you would normally use on levels getting your new weapon into a usable state.The combat flows very nicely, allowing you to cancel slower attacks into a dodge during startup. The dodge roll kills all momentum once it ends so it can be more useful to jump out of your rolls. While the game does have a back-step option, I found myself almost never using this as it would often leave me in the boss' attacks.The weapons are definitely my favorite part of the game overall. The melee weapons, for the most part, all have fully unique move sets. Each weapon has a unique special attack using focus, almost always being a more powerful attack at the cost of MP. It took me 4 hours to realize i could repeatedly press the special attack button to initiate  a combo. some weapon combos, especially on the heavier weapons feel very strong, often doing full basic attack damage at 2-3 times the speed, sometimes including a multi-hit attack in the middle causing the weapon to hit often 4 extra times on larger enemies and bosses.I found myself only using the games secondary weapons when I needed extra range to hit an enemy over spikes. Even then often preferred jumping out over the spikes/pit and just drifting back to safety. I only found myself using magic at the start of the game when I needed the extra damage output and statuses. Towards the end of the game I killed most enemies in a few hits so I never felt the need to use magic after the third boss. The guns in the game are very unique and have their own use cases, though some are almost direct improvements to others. I found myself trying to use guns in combat and bosses but found them to be too slow and committal to be worth the effort for the damage they gave.The bosses in this game are quite fun and unique. There are only 3 reused bosses in the game, even then its done like Hornet from Hollow knight where they are similar, but with new moves. I only found myself struggling on bosses towards the end of the game where they out-scaled my damage and healing. The bosses are made considerably easier by the health potions scaling off your max health, to the point only 2 health pots were needed to fully heal from nearly dead. The last few bosses can feel a little overwhelming, especially t=some of the side bosses. The damage the bosses do feel adequate for when you fight them, I often find myself panic healing from getting combo-ed to low health. Each bosses, save the last few, have obvious safe windows for attacks and you can often stun earlier bosses for ripostes, especially using the parry.  I never found myself taking more than 5 attempts for a boss, though some people may fin this to be a negative.I do have some minor issues with the game. The potential for platforming this game has is immense, but they do nothing with it. Specifically the grapple hook and the way it carries momentum through it lends itself really well to platforming, so long as they let you chain them together mid-air. The ledge grab mechanic can be finicky at times, though works well 90% of the time. It can struggle to grab some ledges if you don't position yourself just right. The lack of a run option can make backtracking through rooms tedious. I spent probably around 30 minutes total just walking through cleared rooms. I found that rolling and jumping towards the end felt a little faster, though its hard to tell. Some enemy and boss attacks seem like they can be parried when they can't. The parry stigma is what you have for half the game, yet its usefulness tapers off once you leave Mythringal. The only boss I could reliably parry was the Demo boss. I often tried parrying moves I thought I could only to get the timing right, then losing half my health anyway since the move can't be parried. Charge attacks can't be dodged through, unless its a dog. Some enemies have unique charge attacks where they run across the room. It is impossible to roll through these attacks like how most games would let you; Instead you have to jump over the attack while avoiding whatever other enemies are in the room. I can understand this for attacks that cause objects to erupt from the floor, like with the first boss, but it feels un-intuitive to have to jump some attacks and projectiles when you can roll through other similar attacks. As mentioned earlier, I was locked out of 4 achievements on my first play-through. These achievements are very late game, about 17 hours in for my case, and while the weapons are high quality and unique, I feel there isn't enough different about them to warrant an immediate second play-through while there is no new game+.TLDR: I had some minor problems with the movement and momentum of the dodge. The bosses are a bit easy for those more experienced with souls games. Recommended for those that love more hectic boss fights and combat supplemented by Bloodborne-esque transforming weapons.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Too many issues to name, but this falls under the "Souls like" umbrella where awful game design is excused by advocates by the mindless repetition of "Git gud". Healing items are initially granted by alters (bonfires), then once the first boss is encountered, it drops to 4, then after that, it drops to 0. The game never explains this and moments of difficulty from that point on are turned into farming loops, where you have to grind souls and items until you have enough items to try again. Horrendous design that removes fun. There are several levels, where enemies are placed at the end of collapsing platform sections, so you have the option of avoiding their attack and falling, or getting hit. This triggers another grind loop, of doing "dink" damage until the enemy is dead and progress can continue, which is horrendous design.There other baffling design choices, for example an item that gives "frost resistance" is hidden in an area that inaccessible until you gain the additional movement ability, granted by beating the frost area. From a distance it makes sense that this item exists, but there's not logic in where items are placed, or at time you uncover areas of the map. Most of the interesting abilities and weapons are hidden until towards the end of the game, where they are now rendered completely pointless because player progression. IE - You find a new sword you like better, great, you've now got an hour+ of grinding souls to level it up to your current weapon level, or even worse, you're not far enough in that you can buy the crafting resource, so you're stuck with an under-level weapon. It's just not satisfying and the design of it keeps you from investing in the game or character, which is criminal in a game which encourages you put points into stats for customisation.Note - The devs are obsessed with breakable walls, and sometimes, breakable walls BEHIND breakable walls! However there's no visual cue as what is and is not breakable, so it's just either just trial and error grind, or spoilers / guides, which isn't fun.The combat is slow and clunky, it doesn't have punch and because so many abilities are hidden behind consumable usage, you're never free to play as you wish. Instead the game has you in a constant in a grind mindset, which isn't fun. A lot of the boss fights hinge on never getting hit, as even if you are over levelled, most bosses will still take 1/2 to 1/3 of you health with a single hit, and if you try and heal, you just open yourself to being hit again, so epic fights become an annoying grind down of getting swatted around,while trying to use items.Finally, I got this from a key site, and I'm glad I did, so the Devs won't see a penny of my money because they really don't deserve any. It's a dull, slow metroid-vania souls like. Heavy on needless grind, bad map design, pointless side quests and padding. There are better games in the genre, Avoid.Thumbs down - I would have refunded the game if I was able to.Edit - I played this game thru for 100% completion and to get all achievements - Which required 2 playthrus because there are miss-able quests and items - Additionally, there is a a "point of no return", but the gave NEVER tells you this ("GIT GUD" design strikes again). On my 2nd playthu I did look at the game again with fresh eyes to see if my initial negative opinion still stood. I did have a better time, but mainly because I knew what weapons & spells were good and how to immediately seek those out, but for most players they'll simply have the poor first experience or a spoiler heavy experience using secret guides. Overall, I still don't have an overall positive view of the game or could recommend it in good faith.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is an enjoyable metroidvania heavily inspired by Bloodborne, the aesthetic is simply gorgeous, I love the variety of weapons and spells you get, I find the gameplay core fun and engaging (not without issues) enough to get me hooked.As a con I could say that the parry is unreliable at best, at least for me, the fact that you need two buttons to make a parry is stupid, especially difficult of pulling it off playing on a steam deck.Another con is the insta death spikes, such a cheap way to die, combine it with a below average (or average at best) platforming and you get a recipe for disaster on those sections.Overall I think the game is good, I’m having a blast (but I’m biased because of the bloodborne inspiration), I’m not an expert on metroidvania games so I’m just saying this as a casual of the genre. For me is a 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good Metroidvania, although very derivative of Blasphemous and souls-games. Somehow I think I liked this one more than Blasphemeous 2, though I am not sure it really deserves that, and I can't quite understand why. I guess being able to level up always adds a bit of an addictive quality to a game, and the different weapons have had some work put into them.The environments and graphics are really nice, and the map is huge.There are some downsides, it seems to sometimes drop inputs if they're too tightly timed, often the forward-dash move after a jump. I would also have liked to be able to sprint when jogging back from some dead end after clearing it of enemies. The map view is somewhat impractical to navigate and could be a bit clearer. I think the writing was pretty bad, it felt like it aped the souls-style without catching the magic of it. The voice acting is also OK at best. In the end though the gameplay is more important, and I find this was fun enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but not without its quirks. Some weapons could use some fine tuning, hit boxes could be improved, and some things cost a bit much.I really felt myself digging into the game past the initial difficulty curve, same feeling I had when playing Bloodborne, Blasphemous, Lies of P, etc.The weapon and spell selection is great, however, most characters felt bland and only served as plot points. I do wish they were a bit more involved in there on a deeper level. Good boss battles all around so far with plenty of enemy variety.Pros: Executions feel great.Most boss battles are challenging and fun.Enemy variety is plentiful. Fun weapons/sub weapons.Character upgrades hold up well.Environments feel varied enough.Cutscenes have character and help paint the story nicely. Cons:Could make a cleaner interface when traveling from place to place, could make it to press a button to redirect to the manor like in Lies of P’s Hotel Krat.Better balance amount of item costs, weapon upgrades.Lack of costumes or even different color palettes for Eryk.Auto dying to pits and spikes. Could be fixed like in Blasphemous 2 when the consequence isn’t as dire. Map could be improved or cleaned up.I really hope they continue patching this game because I’m looking forward to DLC and a sequel. The potential is there. I’m still not finished but I’m enjoying it the more I go through the game. If I were to score it I’d give it a 8.5/10. 9 if stuff is fixed and content is added post game.

Well there are none, apart from the comedic lack of any narrative, to the point where reading items or talking to NPCs that seem to mostly all think of you as a piece of ♥♥♥♥ with little to no context helps practically nothing with shining a light with why you are doing anything in this game. _childDocuments_.review: Cool metroidvania, it's like Bloodborne and Blasphemous in one. Variety of spells and weapons.  You can play with melee, spells or mix of both. _childDocuments_.review: Went into this expecting a soulslike metroidvania. Instead, I got a half-baked version of Kingdom Shell. The map is barely functional being full of bugs and performance issues. There is no upward attack even though this game REALLY needs that. Kingdom shell doesn't have an upward attack either but at least the enemies are designed around that. The healing system is slightly better than kingdom shell but overall both have a bad system. I don't remember if kingdom shell has a corpse run but this definitely does.Ultimately, you should go buy kingdom Shell instead. While that game was also initially released in a half baked state, the dev has made a lot of improvements to it since then, unlike the devs of this game who seem to be content with keeping the game half baked.Update:I ultimately decided to continue playing the game and reached the endgame and what appears to be the penultimate biome. The game's problems get a little more manageable as the game progresses, that is until the boss at the end of the penultimate biome is reached and all of the game's problems all come together to create a boss battle that is impossible to overcome due to all of the problems with the game. I advice people interested in this game to go play Blasphemous, Blasphemous 2, and kingdom shell instead. All Three are much better designed and significantly more polished than this. The only advantage this game has over them is the pricing, which is really low in comparison to the amount of content in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I do not play a lot of 2D games and honestly the ones I do, I do not finish. This game though? Might change that. Amazing music, amazing acting (which surprised me), amazing art and very fun combat. Give it a shot!AddendumBecause the below list has grown as long as it has, I have to go wait for sale. Or please read issues before buying. I agree with others, this game could be a BANGER but it depends on if the Devs fix the issues. I think one patch could address a lot of the grievances by myself and others. I truly hope they fix it because this game has a great foundation! Now they just need to build off it. UPDATEAs I play more, there are some issues to call out and be warned of. 1. Enemy projectiles. Is what it is, issue I have, you cannot air dodge for some time. So as that enemy clocks you time and time again in the air, with pin point accuracy, you have ZERO maneuvers. Basically, its a health chipper and the Devs designed it that way. 2. I-frames. Some attacks should absolutely be re-worked. There will be times the move didn't touch you but the game sure thinks, scratch that, KNOWS it does. 3. Controls. I am not sure if this is a controller thing or keyboard also has an issue, but there will be times you press a button and the game will ignore it. 4. Pause between dodge. There is no stamina in this game. Some may love it, I don't. Honestly, just because there will be plenty of times you'll go against multiple enemies. Some throw projectiles while others melee. Issue is, if one swings, one shoots, then one swoops down on you, you are GUARANTEED a hit. Because there is a second delay before you can dodge again. So you may move out the way of one attack, dodge through another, but that third is going to hit because running isn't fast enough and dodge is on cool down.5. Enemies can see / throw through the floor / off screen. At the same time, YOU obviously cannot. This means an enemy out of frame may jump into the fight or level you're on out of nowhere. Causing a pile up depending on where you are and if you're already in a fight with some enemies. This isn't even including projectiles, which can happen too. Out of nowhere projectiles will come into frame, and you now have to use your dodge (which has a cool down), if you can. If you cannot dodge, or you're already in the air, well too bad for you boss hoss. (FIXED) 6. As always, upon death you loose your carried experience. Issue being, after death the game does not give you a clue where you were. For beginners to metrovania like me, an annoyance for sure. 7. The snap is strong with this ONE. I capped 'one' because only one enemy does this so far. She will teleport from her location to yours. Which is fine, UNTIL, the game SNAPS you into her arms. You'll see her teleport pop up behind you and be warned, I truly mean she will come out flying towards you. BUT! Even if you're ready and roll out of the way and she misses, you want to feel gratifica..... the game snaps you into her grab anyway. There goes 3/4 of your health in one grab! 8. INCORRECT layout. The game has a UI like most. Bottom left in the screen shots you'll see three icons. From left to right it goes, spell/firearm, heal and melee weapon. Just so you know, on controller at least, this is VERY MESSED UP. Left trigger SHOULD correspond with the left image, right? RIGHT!? NOPE! Spell/firearm, being the left image, is actually mapped to the right trigger. While healing is mapped to the left trigger, however that is represented by the middle image and finally your melee weapon, right image, can be used by the X button... lol! I don't mean to laugh but man! This warped my brain for far too long as I was learning the controls.  You cannot alter this neither. A patch could easily fix this but this blew me away as I realized they released it like this.. Nobody? NOBODY caught this.. Not one. This explains a lot about the world we're living in right now. If I could, I would alter it to, spell/firearm to the right image corresponding to the right trigger. Heal to the left image, matching the left trigger and your melee weapon in the center, used by X as is. Right/left d-pad allows you to swap weapons and spells/firearms. While up and down d-pad alters your selected items. To USE the selected item, tap LB (which isn't used on controller).(FIXED) 9. YOU CANNOT PAUSE!!! At this point this has to be an inside joke for Pubs and Devs of the SoulsBourne genre. It truly makes NO sense but they just wont stop doing this. I don't even like it when FromSoft does this if you're not playing online. Issue here, from what I can tell, Last Faith doesn't even have online play to begin with! So why is it here!? I don't even think the Devs know. So, to ALL the future Pubs/Devs of SoulsBourne games, you DO NOT have to copy this design. IT MAKES NO SENSE. P.S.You may ask, "Why so frustrated over this?" For me, it comes off as an obvious copy and paste which I cannot stand. Truly, there is no reason for this outside of an always online game. The only reason outside of online only, is the Devs asking, "aRe wE cOnSideReD a sOuLsLiKe yEt!?"..... 10. You CANNOT use items from the inventory screen. When you're afflicted with a status (like bleed, burn or frozen) there are tablets to remedy these issues. However, I HATE the inventory slection on SoulsLike and just ignore it. But if you do catch a status element, you're REQUIRED to pause, go to the inventory screen, go to items tab, select item, put it in an item slot, un-pause, adjust items to select THE item needed, THEN you can use it. As I said, I find this system lacking, annoying and cumbersome. For the most part I ignore it in all games and just leave my healing item as the only option (simple). But here, you HAVE to use the item select. So if you're like me, too bad boyo! This is a copy of a copy of a copy that NOBODY seems to want to address....Unless FromSoft does, THEN we might see positive change in the genre. ConclusionA this time, I still recommend the game. Despite the flaws, honestly I do find myself enjoying it. But WHY Devs!? My goodness it is infuriating to say the least at times with the bugs and design issues. If the Devs come in and patch some of this (which we have no word of), trust me, it is golden. Till then though, Last Faith comes with bad design (projectiles) choices and clearly broken (snapping into enemy grabs) enemies. I hope to see a fix soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game, I enjoyed the setting and gameplay. It's a mix of blasphemous and bloodborne. I have a couple of pet peeves though:1) Not having a means to return to the latest checkpoint/hub (i.e., homeward bone in DS) makes exploration a bit annoying since you have to walk back manually. I feel this is a basic quality-of-life feature all metroidvanias and soulslikes have, but this one doesn't for some reason.2) Weapon upgrades are too expensive, costing almost 120k to 150k per weapon. The lack of a teleportation mechanic means you have zero incentive to farm nycrux to try different weapons.That aside, if you enjoy blasphemous and souls like games, you will enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to love the game, the theme and gothic aspect of it is fantastic, critical execution are really good and love doing them, but the game lacks the Metrovania aspect... let me explain.Yes, is set up as a metrovania game on the design, but the lack of items drops from enemies makes it not just difficult, but rather annoying. Imagine this, you get items only 4% of the time that you kill an enemy, like literally you could go hours playing and maybe 2 items drops from like 100 enemies you killed, no matter if they are weak or strong, farming for item is close to non existent, and marchants that sells some of the good items, have limited supply (weapons power up) coughs*The currency and level up are the same thing, so you chose to buy items you need (because they don't drop at all,) or level up your character, or go in to a room where it locks the door and you are ganged by the same easy enemies you've been killing in that level, but they are on steroids, with a energy drink and with a bad yuyu on them... at level 47 with HP at 173, this monster are from like level4 of the game, and in this room, they need to hit you twice and you are done. Maybe 3 times and you are done. If one sends you flying, while in the air, the other one can hit you.(in the middle of the animation of you falling back, you still can get hit) to then drop all your currency collected, to go back to the same room, get the doors locked and get your behind handed all over again. And you need to kill the first 3 monsters, then 2 running ladies on each corner, and then 4 more... and remember! They are OP! The level up system is frustraiting, as you have to spend the currency you get from killing monster in to attributes... and can only be spend on one attribute and not the entire character development, so if the next level takes 10,000... you will spend that level in only one out of 5! I'm level 47 and some of my attributes are at 8 and 7 lol because my character is strong 💪,37, vitality 32, dexterity 12, mind 7, instinct 8....Lastly, it would of been amazing to have this game a bit more HD, or more detailed on the characters and visual effects. The team has something good going on, but if they make the leveling like castlevania or and RPG, where experience gets all your attributes a little higher, and money for buying items, it would be a classic and definitely something to look forward to as a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game and one of the best 2D dark fantasy metroidvania / soulsvania games I've played. Game is slightly rough around the edges. Some people seem to say game borrows a lot from Bloodborne (which I haven't played), it is obvious that game's combat system is very soulslike, so blind rushing and button bashing will get you killed quickly. I don't see game borrowing that much specifically from Castlevania SotN like some seem to say (it IMO borrows more from Blasphemous), a game that I played only recently. Progression in game is pretty enjoyable in regards to story and traversal abilities, first hour and starting area felt a little bit sparse, but after that game gets a lot more enjoyable. Story is quite OK, but pretty vague on purpose, but that doesn't make much of a difference. There are several refreshingly different areas to explore, side characters, hidden objects, mini-quests, and hidden things to find. All the dialogue has quality voice acting which was a nice surprise. There are several weapons and spells to find and buy. Player and enemies have a few moves, so it almost feels like one was playing a 3D game instead of pixel art 2D game. Boss battles are pretty enjoyable and even memorable, although almost too hard for me, but at least you can grind and level up generously. I think some of the default inputs could still be changed and some of the in-game menu navigation controls too could be changed to make menu navigation more fluent. Gameplay itself feels slightly stiff, but  not so much that it would ruin the game IMO, sometimes it also feels like character locks too long time in an animation without an option to cancel the move, and there is quite a lot of input buffering for attacks too, and sometimes it feels like ledge grabs are slightly unpredictable.Visuals are overall great looking which is usually a must for me to enjoy a game, some of the environment pixel art is really top notch, and especially animations and character designs are good and fit the world. Music and audio effects too are good, nice movement, weapon and enemy sound effects, and quality fantasy movie style soundtracks for each area and boss battles.Game still has several smaller glitches and bugs here and there, but nothing game breaking, but there seems to be some cases where you can be locked out of some achievements which can cause frustration. At least devs seem to be quite responsive, they have fixed several things people have complained about and even added things people have asked, like being able to respec character stats later in the game and controls remapping. I wish the devs would add an easy mode to games like this, catering to small minority of hardcore gamers ain't that nice of a strategy. Despite of this, I still managed to 100% the game.NOTE - currently, the game can be ONLY played in full screen mode, this was a slightly nasty surprise as I play on a big screen, and I didn't see this mentioned in any reviews I watched/read.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a textbook example of an artist directing a game:  The presentation here is outstanding, and it's wasted on poor game design, informed by other adjacent games in the genre but with blatant disregard for the context in which they exist (or whether or not they are good to begin with).The strengths of this game are clearly in it's visuals.  The backgrounds are wonderfully detailed and despite zones being large, the individual screens feel distinct.  The animations as well are lovingly crafted and numerous, with a great sense of motion and momentum present where it should be.  Bosses are beautifully crafted with wonderful animations in tow as well.  Brightly colored elements are reserved for some spell and weapon effects, making them distinct against the otherwise dim backgrounds.The music evokes a lot of the From Software-isms:  Relatively minimalist with denser choral arrangements for bosses.  It's not necessarily moving the needle from this standard, but it's executed well.  The audio and visuals together successfully craft a convincing atmosphere - it is undoubtedly a major strength of this game.Before I start to tear into the rest of this, I want to really emphasize that the Art Direction is fantastic - they should be proud of what they did here.   Among small metroidvania teams, I think The Last Faith is easily among the best looking games and has completely and thoroughly executed on it's artistic goals with strong results.  Well done!But now, for the pain...This game is heavily influenced by DS.  The number of ideas ripped straight from the series is staggering and this is actually totally fine, but only if they made any sense.Menuing does not pause the game.  This is a DS-ism because the game can be multiplayer, but The Last Faith isn't.  This is the beginning of a theme with this game:  "Steal from DS without understanding why these rules exist."  There is no reason for the game to not pause in menu here since there is no multiplayer element, but DS did it so LF made a bad choice.The resistance and debuff system of DS is not particularly good, and it's REALLY not good in LF.  A major problem with DS is that the function of stats, especially non-primary stats, is completely obfuscated.  This is not a Good Thing, but LF again copied it verbatim.  Tell me, what exactly does 1 more resistance against the 'burning' debuff do?  When I'm allocating stats, do you expect me to be able to make good choices based on the information being provided?  What also is the expected game plan when you get Electrocuted?  I usually just went AFK for a minute and got a glass of water.  This is bad design, and it's part of this theme of pulling ideas off of DS without understanding whether or not they were even good to begin with.Something that wasn't pulled from DS but should have been is the Estus Flask system.  In LF, you have limited healing items of which you can have 7 total, but when you respawn you are given 4...  You can go farm some more if you want, but that's not fun - that's tedious.  Someone making decisions didn't understand the Estus Flask.The inventory management system of From Software games is atrocious.  Not being able to use items from my inventory is dumb.  Do not copy UX design from From Software - they are terrible at it.The list goes on here but suffice to say, the System Design in LF is badly misinformed and the genre conventions are misunderstood by the designers.Motion in this game is done better then it's other systems, but still has a lot of warts.  On the good side of things, you are given a lot of control over your jump arc and the roll / backdash feel great to press.  Mid-air attacks follow The Correct Genre Conventions™ and you get a lot of expression in how you move moment to moment.  What is incorrect here though is how your attack animation intersects with motion.  You can't jump out of an attack, but you CAN roll out of it and you can then jump out of a roll.  Spot the problem here and win a prize!There is also just a general lack of small implementation details that should be present in modern games.  A buffer of any kind on movement abilities seems to be non-existent and I don't think Coyote Time is implemented at all here (which is fine if it was deliberate - SotN doesn't implement Coyote Time either and it's fine, but it's also not as necessary in a game where your movement abilities are so generous).  I'm not willing to extend the benefit of the doubt on these kinds of things given how sloppy the rest of the game is.Why can't I level up at a teleport alter?  Why do I have to: Open Travel Menu > Select Mansion > Confirm > Exit Mansion > Talk to Lady > Select Level Up > Enter Mansion > Open Travel Menu > Select my previous Location... How does this not strike a designer as completely asinine in playtest?Also, Parry is 2 buttons.  A reactive, combat command is 2 buttons!  That certainly is a decision!The world here is big.  Too big.  There is a ton of filler content between the bosses, which are easily the highlight of the game.  The filler content also isn't that good, with a lot of the usual trappings that trip up poor designers of the genre.  It's more common then not that vertical as a means of avoidance is restricted... in a metroidvania.  If you want to make 'jump' a thing, then you have to let it breathe in combat.  Sharking enemies (hitting them through floors and walls) is effective as ever due to haphazard level design.  "Reverse Sharking", where you bounce between different vertical layers is equally effective in this game.  A lot of enemies can be very safely dispatched with these kinds of cheesy tactics, and in a game where stakes are high, that behavior ends up being encouraged and it makes traversing a world with too much cruft in it even more tedious.In a game with highly structured combat, it's very important that your boss previs animations are consistent and reliable.  Literally every boss except the first one has problems with this, where previs animations are being shared by different moves with different timings, or they aren't consistent.  Throw it on the pile of sloppy design I guess.The bosses otherwise were definitely a highlight and I had the most fun progging on these fights.---The problem with this game and so many others like it is not one specific thing, but it's a death delt by many cuts.  You just *cannot* screw up the basics of movement, combat, menuing, etc. etc. in this genre in 2023.  There are too many good games that nail it such that ignorance of the conventions - ignorance of what works and what doesn't - is not an excuse any more.The light at the end of the tunnel for this game is that none of these problems are actually unfix-able (except level/scenario stuff).  These are problems that can be fixed with a patch.  I'll keep an eye on this game in the future - lurking underneath all this cruft is a good game waiting to come out, but it's going to take a lot from the developers to come to terms with that cruft before it can improve.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I'm NOT recommending this game because after 20+ hours of gameplay the game locks you out of progressing side quests with NO warning. Also there are multiple bugged achievements that won't pop, which have not been properly address. This isn't a complete game yet.ProsThe gameplay is fairly customizable: You have multiple builds to choose fromThe gamplay is also challenging: Expect to die a lot and learn by those deaths.The story is engaging: All dialog is voice acted, which is great and the story actually has plenty of interesting characters.ConsProgression locks: The game locks you out of progressing multiple times with little idea how to move forwardPrepare to get lost often: There is no objective marker to be found, there are invisible walls everywhere that you need to find but are never tutorialized, and  many characters speak in riddles.1 build to rule them all: STR and VIT build puts the game on easy mode. Guns are very limited and underpowered, magic never outpaces STR in damage and the strongest attacks in the game are STR based or cannot be used easily. The story is really hard to follow: There is a lot of voice acting, which is great. But some character's do not speak properly and others use old english. No idea what they wanted for me, so I had to google what to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game featuring amazingly intricate pixel art animations and very creative, enjoyable bossfights. It would be nice if the game had some more ways of guiding you just a tiny bit more through listed quests or more indicators on the map. The lore seems fairly interesting, however, the way it is told, you don't really understand much of what's happening. Would probably not play again but had very fun 20 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: this game rules. play this game. gameplay (both combat & traversal) is incredibly fun and responsive in well designed levels & some of the most fun boss fights i've personally ever played. character designs, art, environments, animations... all of it is so lovingly put together, so expertly polished. if you like metroidvanias at all, i highly recommend this game, and if you don't, i tentatively recommend it. i personally havent played a lot in the genre, and i found this both approachable as a beginner and challenging as i started to get the hang of enemy patterns. in my opinion, the story was weak and dialogue relied too heavily on being cryptic to cultivate a particular tone without much substance behind it, BUT i also found that even as someone who typically prefers story-heavy games, it didn't bother me much at all. every single other thing about the game made it a complete blast and i really didn't mind.any other issues i had with the game were extremely small and easily set aside when i remembered this was a really small team's first game. i can not stress enough how functional, playable, beautiful and FUN the game was. my expectations were met and well, well exceeded. it's clear they put a ton of love and hard work into this game and i'm really looking forward to their next project.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I would describe The Last Faith as a 2d Bloodborne with metroidvania elements. It's a souls-like first, and this important to keep in mind. A lot of people have compared this title to Symphony of the Night, but the only thing these two have in common are aesthetic and thematic choices. The gameplay couldn't be more different. So if you're looking for the fast-paced metroidvania experience that can be found in both titles that kickstarted this genre, as well as any other subsequent Castlevania titles what you're looking for is actually Bloodstained Ritual of The Night. If you are into souls-likes and don't mind the slow gameplay then go for it, you'll love it. I had lots of fun with it and even though I don't see myself coming back to play more of this game I'm glad I bought it and got platinum on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I love Metroidvanias but this is a frustratingly disappointing one. The gorgeous pixel-art and fantastic sound design aren't enough to carry a game littered with weird design choices and unfinished/ poorly balanced gameplay. It's a shame too because this is so close to being good but just can't quite deliver.The Last Faith really seems like it should be solid and gives the illusion of choice with builds but if you don't go str you aren't finishing this game-- some bosses are bordering on impossible with anything but the stupid great sword and/or being severely overlevel and to make things worse there's never saves near most bosses, only checkpoints. Think you'll practice a boss using that? Well, healing items are consumable and need to be farmed so if you want to learn a boss you burn down all your items and have to grind for them... absolutely stupid. You also cannot respec at all so you're committed to playing with whatever path you started down and just hope you find a decent weapon your build supports or combat is going to be bland for huge sections of the game. How well you resist certain attacks / elements also heavily depends on how you built your character so without a massive time investment in grinding you can easily soft-wall yourself for no good reason. After a while I figured all these things would just be fixed in post-game / NG+ but there isn't one!Challenging is fine but I can't endure tedious, multi-phase boss fights while the game offered me no good weapons for the build I chose until I was 50% through so I end up tickling half of them to death for 10 mins and then just switch to the g*d*mn great sword with no str just to beat them... first or second try. Repeatedly. It was also baffling that once I had an even okay weapon all challenge evaporated for a few bosses and I even did two completely hitless after really struggling with others.You also can't customize any video settings (can't even change resolution, refresh, nothing) and also can't remap any buttons on controllers. The vibration is excruciatingly annoying and can't be turned off in any way within the game so I ended up emulating an Xbox controller while using a PS4 controller just to get rid of it because the game refuses to recognise any overrides on your system, in Steam etc.Dodging and movement mostly feel good but the maps are huge and empty and your character is painfully slow and there's no real dash unless you want to back dodge or forward roll the entire game. If you moved say 30% faster as base speed the game would play and feel infinitely better but you don't get anything beyond an air dodge that moves you a very short distance so have fun crossing long, horizontal maps over and over. After a certain point I just completely gave up even fighting mobs and just dodged through them to progress because it's faster than killing them and then walking around empty screens.Attacking frequently drops inputs and/or "commits" you to awkward movements which is jank, the parry is 2-button and to say it is unreliable is incredibly generous... Good luck using ducking strategically; it often works better than jumping or dodging on high boss attacks but you can't use it because your character has to completely stop any action like attacking / moving for it to register so you'll never want to interrupt yourself and end up dodging instead. The story is adequate I suppose but is weirdly muddled by bizarre writing. Pretty sure the devs thought they were being atmospheric but you have to scroll through paragraphs of word salad and infer what characters mean because all of them talk in over-embellished circles instead of getting to the point. I just started skipping it after the Nth non-descript NPC prompted my character to say something along the lines of "But what do these words you utter mean?" I'd like to know that too but after sinking 20+ hours playtime I have a feeling it was something akin to "enjoy our quirky 2-D Castle-Bloodborne! You get to use a giant great sword and play a str build!"There are 2.5 ice levels and they are by far the biggest areas in the game and they are an absolute slogfest if (surprise!) you didn't do a str build. I quit at the end of the last one after finally killing the stage boss only for him to kill me with a projectile after he started his death animation... realizing i'm progression locked without completing but too sick of level grinding/training the same enemies and too far in to restart so I just gave up. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ Maybe if they patch in some basic QoL features like you know, non-sticky controls, an actual settings menu, attribute respec, bestiary (name cards pop up upon first-time killing mobs but an actual entry / stats page is completely forgotten), controller remap (literally unused buttons and yet parry is 2 buttons, wtf), NG+ and balance the bosses to not be boring, bloated HP bags this will be worth playing. Throw it back in the oven for a couple more patches, she's a little too raw for me just yet. Or just wait until it's 75% off and deal with the frustration.TL;DR: Did I mention you should do a str build and use the Ethereal Great Sword?

_childDocuments_.review: When I initially saw this, it seemed interesting and it looked like it would be to Bloodborne what Salt and Sanctuary was to Dark Souls. The art looks nearly identical to Blasphemous but that could be forgiven since that game has great art. Having played it, I can say it is like Bloodborne, if Bloodborne had terrible level design, unresponsive controls, practically no color other than grimdark, a 1/3 of the enemy variety, generic locations (though the house of mirrors was pretty cool), and unmemorable bosses. Its so obvious this game wants to be 2D Bloodborne it's embarrassing. There's homage, and then there's blatantly ripping off the Plain Doll and her functions. They keep Bloodborne's Blood Vial mechanic, but don't replace the rally mechanic with anything, so you'll have many awkward moments where you run out of "Blood vials" and have to either beg them from enemies or find the one seller who is never in the same place. They also keep the pain in the butt way of leveling up from Bloodborne where every time you want to do that, you have to warp to the Plain Doll / "Not" Plain Doll, level up, then remember where you were and warp back. It's so damn tedious. But this is what happens when you blindly worship your influences rather than trying to see what worked and what didn't. Also, Castle Cainhurst was a highlight in Bloodborne, the ice area (called the "Damned Fortress of..." and what a fitting name) here is the worst part of the game, the absolute nadir being a room where you have to deal with slippery ice, numerous enemies with projectile attacks, and the game fooling you into thinking you make certain jumps. The game doesn't do a very good job explaining the controls. It feels the need to tell me how to jump and attack (the two most basic moves in gaming) but not how to use items or secondary weapons. The map is very big, but there is little interconnectivity between the levels so you have to rely on a warp system that is more confusing than it is helpful. While the clunkier controls didn't bother me at first, it became very annoying when I needed to dodge quickly to avoid boss attacks and it just wouldn't register. This would be fine if the game has a stamina mechanic but it doesn't. You can't attack upward, which is a huge issue. There is an ax that can help you strike enemies above you, but it rarely helps. There is a subweapon that you can throw upwards, but some genius made it where you can only use it while standing on the ground (meaning they're usually out of your reach). C'mon guys, even the clunky original Castlevania on the NES let you use sub weapons while you were jumping. I'm at the point of giving up looking for something to scratch that "Metroidvania" itch since now the genre just wants to ape Dark Souls without understanding what makes either work. Hollow Knight and Blasphemous were two exceptions, even though both had their problems. I'm going to be a contrarian about the games art style. While it is good and you can tell that there is a lot of effort put into it, I can't help but feel that it is all so drab and dull. If you look at the Rosetta Stone of the genre (Symphony of the Night), it is a very beautiful and colorful game, yet very few Metroidvanias seem to go for that, instead always going for the washed out color palette of Dark Souls (which worked in that game but not in every other). Also, one of the reasons I love playing dark fantasy games is seeing what sort of crazy and twisted designs enemies and bosses are given. Symphony of the Night had plenty, Dark Souls had plenty, Bloodborne had plenty, Blasphemous had plenty. But this game? Barely any. The enemies are all the same zombie like creatures and those that aren't are ripoffs from Bloodborne. This game only has two boss types: humanoid and skeletal dragon (at least from what I've seen). I didn't get to the Hydra, which I know is in there because that was in all of the promotions I saw of the game, but now in hindsight, it seems wildly out of place of this game. Only get this game if its seriously discounted or if you want a textbook example of what copying your influences with no critical eye will do. You want Bloodborne for PC? Keeping begging FromSoft, because this isn't it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a metroidvania that attempts to entice players with its art direction while fundamentally failing to deliver a combat system that works in its chosen medium.  The game looks great from screenshots but feels stilted when animated, like an anime that skipped one too many frames on the cutting room floor to ship out the door under budget.  Your character's movement feels less locked in place than a game like Blasphemous but still too stilted to comfortably operate within the frame timings presented by enemy attacks.So much of the leveling gimmicks in this game boil down to grinding out EXP to make numbers go up which mostly serve to prolong playtime while offering the bare minimum in return for that investment.  Failing to do so will leave you with a much more tedious combat experience as enemies become far too spongy when you don't have weapons tuned to beat them efficiently.  I understand the need to promote persistent player engagement naturally produces this decision by most devs these days but the trade off is a notable lack of toolkit expansion over time as you pump currency into +1 for the dozenth time.The narrative is delivered in an emo sort of tone that I am not sure whether to interpret as tongue-in-cheek or genuine.  It certainly does not seem interested in adding much context to the visual framework but if you value a cinematic feel in your games it is certainly present for what that is worth.  Every word of text dumped into item descriptions seems hellbent on lambasting you with the totally ominous nature of the eerie, futile landscape you found the item in without delivering anything of substance to a narrative or plot or lore.  The sound of your character jumping seems to be a callback to 3D Legend of Zelda games and as often as you will resort to using it in a 2D platformer the sound grows quite tedious very early on.  The soundtrack is certainly worth listening to although most tracks seem to lack a rhythm or tone that set them apart and serves more as a form of mood music or ambiance.The game's RPG mechanics revolve around "leveling up at the lady" with stats that increase HP and your chosen damage type(s) with some damage resistances thrown in gratis a la Souls-like.  Serviceable enough for anyone familiar with this formula.  Attacks are spammable with no stamina meter to rely upon.  You have STR, DEX, INT and ranged classes to start with more weapons/abilities to incorporate along the way.  As with many other aspects of the game there is a cookie-cutter, carbon copy feel that runs throughout, which may be perfectly fine for anyone interested in a half-baked, more-of-the-same offering but I see little that stands out, innovates, or perfects on that of previous works.  You can swing a whip or a scythe and find little to differentiate them beyond a bit more hitbox in exchange for a bit less damage.  For those who are interested, the dodge roll appears to have no I-frames so your ability to avoid damage will depend entirely on getting out of the way or using the clunky parry system that uses up a meter to prevent spamming and requires two buttons to activate despite there being enough buttons on a standard controller to not require such a system.The first boss enemy you encounter is a textbook example of opaque telegraphing.  All of the boss' attacks involve him raising his arms before slamming back down again.  The time you would spend reacting to these attacks is largely consumed with the same animation each time.  The quickest of these actions requires the player to jump as soon as they see the attack coming to avoid a shockwave that travels across the floor.  The problems begin when you learn that his 2nd attack involves the same wind-up with a slight pause and flash signaling a local shockwave with debris that arcs up and will likely hit you if you prepared to jump the original type of attack.  This combination is easier to prepare for if you get some distance between you and the boss but is undone by the bosses third attack which sees him leaping at you with little to no wind up save for the several frame animation of him raising his arms like he would with either of the first two attacks.  You can freely roll through the boss with impunity to create space should this leap push you into the corner.  By the time you get his HP down below half he will introduce a charged form of the leap that leaves a shockwave across the entire screen to jump and rains fast moving debris from above for several seconds while the boss proceeds to attack you will any of his other attacks.  Jumping during this interval will likely see you slammed by falling rocks since you barely have time to avoid them from the ground.Is this first boss fight hard?  Not necessarily.  You have the option to break pots and debris on the way to the boss fight from the checkpoint to farm healing items that can undo any attack you fail to read but this solution does not invite an entertaining boss encounter. Especially for a starting area first encounter.  Immediately after you will encounter spike pits that instantly kill you if you haven't worked out your jump arch so the game seems genuinely interested in catering to the hardcore aesthetics that have been employed by the games they sought to emulate.This design philosophy of punishing the player with near identical attack telegraphing combined with the disappointing choice to have the player farm healing items ad nauseam speaks to a dev team that does not respect the player's time.  They seem content to resort to spamming animations across what amounts to a significant amount of in-game real estate rather than spend more time and development on fleshing out the locations present within the game.  While the game's atmosphere is remarkable at first glance, over time I believe many players will find their experience dulled by the repetition of textures and animations.  I don't mind going for a walk in the woods but eventually even the staunchest wilderness enthusiast may find themselves a bit tired of staring at the forest.This game cut corners in order to exist and I believe these shortcuts will impair the experience for many players.  Not being able to rebind controller inputs will certainly be an issue for some.  Video settings consist of "On" while in-game.  These issues have been addressed as works in progress by the devs but by the time they arrive you may find yourself spending less and getting the game on sale if you enjoy the genre and atmosphere this game provides.My suggestion for now would be to wait for this cake to bake, its price to deflate, or another dev team to offer up a less frustrating and tediously designed experience.  In the meantime, go play a Metroidvania with a thumb's up assuming you haven't gone through all of them already.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game.  Blasphemous 2 was better, but this was still worth while.Pros:- Awesome boss fights.  Some were pretty tough, but it seemed like after mid game the bosses only took 1-3 tries while early bosses up to 20.  End boss(good ending boss) took about 13 tries.  Blasphemous 2 suffered from the same problem, but overall every boss encounter was enjoyable.- Nice variety of magic spells.  - Nice dark, victorian atmosphere...like Bloodborne or Lies of P.  Lovercraftian even.  I prefer dark medival, but this would be my second favorite.- A couple npcs that were nice and creepy- I enjoyed Eryk as the main character, despite always prefering to be able to create my own character, but you can't win em all.- Decent art...could be a little more extreme...but that is a taste thing.- Nice big world to explore with interesting biomes- Solid understanding of what is a metroidvania.  Some devs really drop the ball on that one.- Some cool weapons but...Cons:-  You are basically locked in to 2...maybe 3 weapons depending on how you decide to level.  I ended up using the starting weapon for every boss and the vast majority of my playthrough.  I decided I wanted to be dex/magic as I read about a dark katana you could find later in the game.  Starting weapon is the only weapon that gets an S scaling in dex whilst the katana was more magic focused.  It was not doing close to the dps as of the night blade as I put like 60 in dex and 35 in mind.  So I was stuck with the intro weapon for the majority of the game.  Now...you can unlock infinite upgrade materials and farm to have 99 in everything but the 5 hour grind to switch weapon for another 5 or so hours of gameplay was not appealing.  They could have solved all of this with a respec option.- No NG+.  Would have felt right with this game so you could try high level quality builds. - Many quests had no real reward other than an achievement.  I got 44 out 53 achievements without really trying to hard other than getting the good ending...but many of those achievements were my only reward.  For making a long treck over and over again bringing this weird ghost girl toys, you just get a ore you could buy for 4 minutes of farming.  Not a big deal.- My biggest complaint.  The writing.  It's not great.  I would argue it isn't even good...more mid than anything.  It tries to emulate HP Lovecraft but falls flat.  It's wordy just to be wordy.  It is cryptic just to be cryptic.  All without really adding anything to the story or the vibe.  After the god tier writing in Blasphemous 2, this was a major fail for me.  I love reading the lore and experiencing the story part of games, but this was disapointing.Verdict:  Fun game despite a couple of flaws.  I'm glad I played it to the end and would recommend for fans of metroidvanias and Lovecraftian things.  7.15 outa 10

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding addition to the Metroidvania genre. The atmosphere is perfect, the enemy variety is perfect, the dark Gothic tone is throughout the game and the bosses are fair but difficult until you get the patterns down. This is a game that respects your time, offers rewards for exploration, and allows you to show your mastery of the game by flawlessly beating the bosses after your learn their behavior.
