_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic Metroidvania game. Rather than traditional level ups, the game goes the souls route. It also takes a couple of gameplay elements from bloodborne such as expendable potions and bullets. I'm very glad the developers did not listen to the folks complaining about these mechanics. In actuality this system is far more forgiving than the flask system. I have 9 instant heal potions, and 10 HoT potions  per rest point already. They provide you will plenty of potions between bosses, and they also sell for a measly 50-130 souls from a vendor you unlock early in the game. Combine this with the overall fairly easy difficulty of the game... there really should be nothing to complain about here. You can kill 2 mobs and buy 2 stacks of potions. I also saw someone complaining about the dodge, i-frame, and hit-boxes. No clue how he came to these conclusions, but all of this feels very good. There is also a parry mechanic that works decently, but I usually just dodge. Also the game gives you a ♥♥♥♥ load of i-frames when you use your mana based melee power attack. Again, its MUCH more forgiving than a souls game for instance. Level design isn't near as good as something like Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, at least so far, but its certainly good enough. You will need tools and special items to backtrack on previously explored areas. One complaint I have is that the platforms can be hard to grab onto at times. It's not always clear that you CAN grab onto a platform because you have to land the jump, and hold up as you hit the platform. Sometimes its hard to tell if you just need to hit the jump perfectly, or if you need double jump or some other tool. As a result some of the jumps end up being very frustrating. Overall a solid game for $25 USD. I would definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It really is unfortunate that this game is unpolished as it is, because there's the bones of a really fantastic game here. However, I do have several issues which when combined, prevent me from being able to recommend this game in it's current state. I don't know how I really want to structure this review, so I'm just going to list the issues I've had with the game so far.Poor hit detection on grabbing ledges, and also unclear where exactly a ledge is grabbable. Once you get past the first couple of areas the enemies suddenly gain a ♥♥♥♥-ton of HP making even garbage caster or cannon-fodder enemies take way too long to kill. Little flying enemies should not be able to face-tank 10 hits with a dexterity scaling weapon. The cooldown for the dodge roll is really long, although I'm unsure as of yet if there's an equipable item that can remedy this like in Blasphemous. Additionally, it's unclear if the dodge roll actually gives invincibility or not, because I've been grabbed out of it by enemies multiple times. This isn't a huge issue for me, I don't mind the dodge being relegated to more of a repositioning tool but some clarity on its function would be nice. For some reason if you choose to bind your movement to the dpad of a controller like any sane person would choose to do so in a 2D platformer, you can only swap weapons or consumables by moving the left joystick, which has really terrible detection as to what your input is. In a boss fight or a tight combat scenario this is a death sentence. Despite your character being built like a brick ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and having the movement speed of a snail, he's incredibly squishy and dies to most enemies in three or four hits. For all the inspiration this game takes from Bloodborne visually, it has none of the combat pacing.This all isn't to say there's no redeeming qualities in this game, all of the visual and atmospheric elements are there and really strong. Unfortunately the mechanics just aren't up to snuff. I feel like a lot of my personal gripes with this game are things that are fixable in a future patch, but in it's current state I cannot recommend this game in good conscience.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a little torn with this game...I think it is very good in it's presentation that it borrows from its obvious influence in Blasphemous. A lot of this game feels like Blasphemous in everything but setting and combat. The one thing that I don't think it does right is feeling like the game is TONS of weapons to choose from. Primary weapons, Secondary weapons, and even Spells at your disposal. The thing is it feels pointless as there are obvious weapons that are just extremely superior than others that it makes no sense to worry about the rest of the ones you have acquired. So take it to consideration to not max out a weapon too early.Many times the game makes you feel like you "just have to beat the next boss" to feel any sense of progression. While every video game has bosses and it really is the goal, this does not string it well. It never really feels grandiose like Blasphemous did. It definitely overstays it's welcome with too many biomes and bosses, I feel. Yet again, since it is a "Bloodborne" influenced game, it also feels like it must have this amount of bosses. I think it ultimately comes down to grinding for stats that it kinda becomes a stat check for some area's of the game. Blasphemous never really had that feel. It just tested your patience with some of the bosses.Speaking of bosses, you will fight some of the best bosses in a Metroidvania out there. All unique in their approach and strategy with some interesting phases that you REALLY have to get the timing down. 3 bosses that I think are so stupid to put in semi-late in the game that it feels like an unnecessary difficulty spike.A solid Metroidvania/Soulslike that brings the Style of Blasphemous with the world of Bloodborne in a decent fun package. Worth playing if you are looking to scratch that Blasphemous itch that you will have when beating 1 or 2. Can skip if you are not a fan of Soulslike as I feel it is more Soulslike than it is a Metroidvania.

_childDocuments_.review: Before launch I was very much looking forward to 'The Last Faith'. It looked like souls met Blasphemous, with smooth combat, great artwork and a vast world. These things mostly hold true, but the developers have decided to change up a lot of the game mechanics, which souls games have iterated upon over the past decade and which we have now come to expect as the gold standard.However, to change a formula, you have to understand it first, but I don't think these guys do - Had they just stuck to what's proven, this game would be an 8 or 9 out of 10 easily.Instead, there are a handful of odd design choices that make gameplay more of a chore than a fun time, namely: - There is no resetting stats and stats are rather limited. So most players will go the cookie-cutter route of main-stat/vitality and never experiment with some of the very cool weapons (& spells)- Parry is so bad, it basically doesn't exist. To demonstrate, I checked the achievements 4 weeks after release: 90% of players had not even parried 50 times.... to expand on why the parry is so awful: It requires a resource, which is shared with another ability. There are very few things you can parry and fewer still the more the game goes on. The parry is also fairly underwhelming, yet hard to reliably hit. And maybe worst of all: It's a 2-button combination, yet an unbound shoulder button exists.- ... and on that topic: There is no control rebinding. Seriously.- Potion farming instead of Estus/bonfire. It's just never a good idea- Status effects absolutely ruin gameplay. They're so bad that if you catch one, you can basically go AFK for a minute and not play. For example, if you get the shocked effect, you'll get stunned for 1 second every 2 seconds for a minute straight. And these effects are not rare.- Coupling resistances with stats. For example, to get cold resistance, you have to put points into strength. Since entire zones are designed around elements and their (awful) status effects this is an absolute nightmare...Other, smaller issues:- Weapons choices are a huge issue for a lot of builds, other than strength. I played rogue, but out of 13 weapons there is only 1 pure dexterity weapon: The one you start with. - You can only attack left/right. No up/down/diagonal slash and no attacking while crouching.- You can only level at the starting hub, lots of unnecessary teleporting- You cannot use items from your inventory, have to bind them to the 'quick-menu' first.- Bullets are too limited a resource and just don't really do damage. They should be limited yes, but refill at checkpoints or so. Having finished the game I found a total of <200 bullets. How is "Marksman" supposed to play the game I wonder? Ah, that's right, by using a sword.- All weapon-buffs/bombs scale based on the instinct attribute and basically do nothing without it, so most builds can ignore half the consumables entirely.- All classes look exactly the same. They could've atleast recolored the sprite a little. The classes also don't really add anynthing to the game. I do not think classes should exist.- Potions for bonus souls: You're very starved for souls, but these potions exist and so you're forced to drink a potion before you open a crate or kill a boss. Not fun.- The playtime is artificially inflated: Lots of empty, pointless loops, with too many monsters and an obscene amount of backtracking.- Monsters & bosses are often HP-sponges I'm sad because there is so much greatness in this, but I just didn't enjoy the game at all. Everything gets overshadowed by odd design- choices, and so I cannot recommend this game.However, if the above list is not a turnoff for you, you should absolutely play, because everything not mentioned there is great: Pixel art, music, atmosphere, lore, monster variety, bosses, weapons, and spells are all on point.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Again, I really wish there was a "Neutral" option.   It's not a BAD game, it just needs a LOT of work.Kinda wished I hadn't backed the Kickstarter, because I get the feeling it's going to take another year or more of patching and tweaking to make it actually playable.  Visually, the game is gorgeous and very Castlevania: SOTN-like. Zero complaints there. Control-wise, it's nearly as janky and frustrating as the original NES Castlevania games, and that absolutely breaks it for me.  If you're expecting me to perform precise Souls-like dodge maneuvers at a split second's notice just fighting regular grunt enemies (who can very easily kill you in a couple of hits if you aren't extremely careful), you're going to have to give me controls that are fluid and responsive. Your're expected to spam back-dash at the first hint of danger, but it only works if you're standing flat on the ground and not already performing an action. You can crouch, but there's no crouch attack or slide (at least not in the early game) and likewise, none of your special weapon attacks work while jumping or crouching and have such a long animation cycle and do so little damage that they're essentially worthless.  In the time it takes you to fire your gun, the enemy has already shrugged off the minimal damage, closed the gap, and hit you with an attack that takes away 1/4 of your health. And using one of the random drop healing syringes has the same clunky animation that locks you in place for a couple of seconds while the enemy uses the opportunity to take a free shot and hit you for nearly the same amount of damage as you healed.At least as of the latest update they've finally fixed the pause feature (which previously paused you, but not the enemies) but you still can't remap controls, or cycle between subweapons without manually switching them through the pause menu. Item use is annoying and it's very easy to accidentally activate the wrong one.  Level design is... meh. They promised us a Metroidvania, but I think they massively overdid it on the locked doors, ladders and elevators that can only be used after you activate a particular switch. There's a huge amount of backtracking and wandering around largely empty levels, since the enemies don't automatically respawn after you kill them. I feel like if the controls were more responsive and the grunt enemies were a little less murderous and easier to kill in only a few hits (but respawned as soon as you left and reentered the room) the constant backtracking would be more entertaining than it currently is.  There are several other nitpicky problems that I hope will be fixed soon. I could see this eventually becoming nearly as good a game as SOTN or BROTN, but it feels like basic player movement and control mapping is the sort of thing they should have worked out before it ever left Alpha.    I can't honestly recommend playing the game in it's current state.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith does not innovate too much, and is just another brick in the wall in the metroidvania genre... It has some nice points: a good selection of weapons, special attacks, and spells, well buit environment and soundtrack (althought this last one lacks mythical tracks, it fits the general atmosphere of the game), and proper pixel art in agreement with the game thematic and genre... all that is cool.The game is not too difficult if you are used to this kind of games and have good reflexes, and the secrets are, in most cases, not too difficult to find (although some of them are more well hidden than others, of course).Unfortunately, in our times there are many games that accomplish this. And this one has also flaws that... play against it. The art initially seems great and is quite interesting, but as you advance, it becomes boring, as many bosses are very similar (the lead artist must have a fascination with huge bat wings and white hair), and they become repetitive. Some enemies are quite well designed, while othres... well, it was clear that either they were made in a rush, or there was lack of ideas at that moment. The images that represent the different characters that appear in the game are lackluster and don't really stand up, they lack personality and didn't me help to get into the story.And speaking about the story... it could have been interesting with all its "lovecraftian" winks, but it is so convoluted, the words used are of obscure and confusing, and the EU Spanish translation is so weird and buggy (I played with that language)... that, unfortunately, all my interest dissapeared in a few hours, as I couldn't understand what was going on. One thing is to keep the "mistery", and another one, is to write a script that makes little sense.Regarding gameplay, the ranged weapons are... just for show, as they are not very useful (with a few exceptions), the parry system is a disaster, and even if there were some interesting skills added later in the game, they take so much time to activate and last so little, that they are, again... quite useless.All in all, it is not a bad game, and if you like metroidvanias with a dark touch, you should indeed give it a try... but there are too many things to polish here... I would advice to  get it when there is a good offer, if you are interested, because full price... seems a bit too much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game with beautiful artwork. Creative enemies and boss battles that are so enjoyable to fight. Some issues/things that could make it better:- Lot's of backtracking and not knowing where to go, especially after defeating Dr Hermann (had to watch walkthroughs on YouTube to figure out how to go Site Cave)- Edwyn the dragon has too much health, in the first phase it spends too much time in the air, unable to deal damage. Getting killed in the second phase by the insanely high damage purple fireballs and having to go through the first phase again is pretty annoying.- Some rooms that lock doors and spawn enemies are really tough, no near enough temporary save point available for those rooms which require lot's of time walking back to the same room when dying (forced to clear the room if I want my nycrux back).- One hit kill spikes and falls are pretty annoying. Especially when falling is required to know if there is a secret place beneath.- Could have some instruction on how to equip the health injection at the start of game.- Parry requiring 2 key presses makes it harder than it already is.- Some execution animation took a little too long.- Hard to remember where NPCs are, and also reasons why certain place can't be accessed at the moment, resulting in more backtracking.These are just my opinions and what I wrote could have just been a me problem.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect combination of Bloodborne and Symphony of the Night.  I played Blasphemous prior to this and while that was also a great game, I much prefer this one due to the Soulsborne leveling system.  Being able to level up and upgrade weapons made this game much more enjoyable for me and incentivized getting better and proceeding with the story.  I wasn't a big fan of many of the areas having puzzles where you were bouncing back and forth throughout the whole map trying to find all of the switches or items to continue on to the end goal of each zone, but it kept me on my toes.  I recommend this to anyone who is into metroidvania's especially if they enjoy the Soulsborne/souls like games as well.

_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a interesting game that has some good things going for it and some extremely awful things going for it. Let's start with the good:1. The animations and art are very nice.2. Decent metroidvania with only a little bit of backtracking.3. Basic systems work but...Now the bad:1. Copy/paste -You have copy pastes of other games but none of it done better or even well. You have Bloodborne healing charges... except you get a million of them, so not sure what the point of that is. You have a Dark Souls bridge section being bombed nonstop (Instead of dragon attacked) and other sections straight ripped from other games - You have Bloodborne aesthetics and a Blasphemous story line with executes. You have the classic souls vague story line and item descriptions which eerily feels like it was ripped straight from a Blasphemous DLC.Basically, the game is a huge copy and paste. It's kind of ironic to see all these systems, events and set pieces kind of mushed together but not being as good as the original.2. Speaking of systems - The Last Faith really doesn't feel original at all and the systems it did copy seems to feel very patched in the most awkward way possible. You get the RPG mechanics of SOTN and other Castlevanias, but none of the depth. You get the Bloodborne consumables and attempt at a parry system - A parry system you will never use. You get Blasphemous executions except they are utterly pointless to perform.3. No video options - Momma mia! Come on, devs!Over all the game is good and a fun time, but it all just feels... off. Off in a way that makes you want to play the original games  that Kumi Souls stole from. It's a fun time, but The Last Faith really needs something, anything, original to it. My advice, worth picking up on a heavy sale only. I am enjoying my time with it and would recommend it, but I can't stress enough it's almost mind boggling how much is just a copy of paste of every souls game we have played in the past.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a Souls-like game. There are several moments that are downright frustrating, but like the best Devil May Cry games, satisfying when you "get it." A fun Metroidvania, but can be a little tedious sometimes. Dying twice without getting your XP back is one of the most frustrating aspects of the game. But stick with it, and combat, exploration, even the story, can be an enjoyable experience. While it borrows a lot from Blasphemous, it has just enough to stand on its own. Recommended, especially if you don't mind dying a lot.Now that I've beaten the game, I would have to say that the weakest part is its multiple endings. Of the three, only one of them is remotely satisfying, and even then, it's only "meh." I sure hope the developers go back and improve them. Classic case of the journey being more important than the destination, I suppose. Still recommended, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally played on Switch but performance was poor and I felt the game deserved to be played at potential. Really dig The Last Faith. I've been on a Metroidvania kick recently and this one is pretty special. Everyone points out its Castlevania/Bloodborne roots which is very true but The Last Faith is great on its own merits. The story is interesting, weapon selection is varied, spells are fun and the combat is satisfying. Specific standouts are the boss music and environment design which feel like they exist an especially grand scale for a 2D metroidvania. I think it's going to age well and I can't wait to finish it!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I have mixed feelings of this game. If there is a neutral review, this is most likely it unless they patch some stuff up. Also, I'll finish the game but there are some stuffs that needs fixing. To start off, I understand that this game is a hybrid &  to be a Bloodborne + Blasphemous 2D metroidvania. Fair enough but then you didnt take the best part of those games.One of the great things about Bloodborne is that if you get hit, you can quickly hit back to get health back. This is a good feature. What isnt a good feature is farming for heals. Its grindy and annoying. Yes, you can go to the girl to buy heals and yes, you can "counter" to get health back but you still have to grind money to buy the heals in the long run. Thats why DS1-3 have flask, its to remove the time wasting to buy / grind for heals. Even Blasphemous have flasks. []Anyway, the good parts about this game, the enemies can actually status effect you. Getting nightmare = reverse controls, getting burned = health lost per/s and etc. A lot of variety weapons with different skillsets. Oh, another good point is having voice actors. Not really necessary per say but still better than nothing. Lastly, I'm not sure if its the game or my controls ( using bluetooth controller or w/e ), the game doesnt read inputs properly and somehow screw up my inputs. Here are some videos to show how it: . _childDocuments_.review: Not great, not terrible.Most good soulslike games are able to strike that balance of hard/fair. Sadly as of now, this game hasn't hit that balance. Between unmarked instakill pits, instakill spikes/traps, unchangeable controls, unreadable enemy attacks, getting attacked from outside the screen and other small issues, its hard to give a solid recommendation at this time unless you're a fan of the aesthetic / genre. The level design is okay from what I've seen so far (roughly 10-12 hours in) but nothing to write home about. As I mentioned before, the map will show "unexplored" areas that are actually just death pits or places you can't actually reach which will throw people who have played games with a similar map structure before.There will (very likely) be times where you need to grind exp/souls to make it past some areas/bosses, its tedious and boring in the unremarkable environments. I'm not saying the game is too hard per se, just that it needs a little tweaking to feel like its not just trying to waste our time to artificially extend its length.I will say the animations and enemy design is fantastic, some of the best I've seen in a game like this.The game really just needs a little balancing / tweaking and I'm sure it'll be one of the better souloidvania's out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to fall in love with this game. I'd been watching for the last couple years when it was in development and kickstarted. At first, the small flaws are just kinda 'whatever', and you over come them because you want to see more of the world, but at a certain point, the punishment of an I-frame not working, or being locked into an animation, or a hit box not working on, feels too much to bare. The art really carries the gameplay, and I really would have loved to see more of it, but I got to a certain point that the promise of more world building and beautiful things to look at, didn't stave off my frustration of being 2 shot in an area that you need to make progress in. Also, if you're locking a QUEST ITEM that you need to PROGRESS behind a 10k currency drop, that the devs expect you to grind out to get, and then you immediately go into a room that is made to frustrate you after this, and there isn't another path to a new area, this is the only one, I'd say you've made a bad call in design. Farming something out for 45 minutes, only to be met with one way path that's designed to kill you in unfair ways, was my breaking point. The scaling seems to not make too much sense, there is janky hit boxes/movement every so often, so a death doesn't feel like it's your fault. And it doesn't feel like you can 'git gud', but just brute force your way through with farming stats.  This is less funIf things were made a bit more fair and the movement/control was tightened up, then I'd love to play through it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a really good metroidvania Souls like game despite some flaws; now then what is the story. Deep in a temple a man named Eric wakes up after being branded with a curse and no memory of his past, but soon Eric ventures out into the land, only to discover that it is infested with all kinds of vampiric monsters. Now Eric must fight his way through and find a way to break the curse before it consumes him, armed only with his skill and faith that he can be saved and maybe even save the whole city.Alright then let's talk about the likes, the gameplay is really good it takes a lot of inspiration/the best parts from bloodborne, metroidvania and blasphemous it has the exploration and power-ups of a metroidvania, the horrifying monsters and trick weapons of bloodborne and the combat and execution attacks from blasphemous. It also has a good balance for the most part of hard but fair like  learning enemy attack patterns, dodging, countering and attacking as well as gaining power-ups defeating certain bosses or exploring  the levels as well as upgrading your character or weapons and finding which weapon or magic or gun is best to use.The weapons and magic are good you have your standard weapons like swords and axes, but you also have trick weapons just like in bloodborne like an ice ax and blood Katana that when you attack an enemy with it enough times it can cause a status effect; they also had good variety with plenty of interesting designs as well as special moves.The magic attacks were quite good; these different magic attacks come in four categories electric, fire, ice and darkness. While some were more useful than others, they all had very good looks and were fun to use. There are also items that you can use to add a status effect to your regular weapons as well as different bombs to use, all of it was very good and all of it had great animation.The enemies and bosses are all really good they all have these nice gruesome designs that are quite unique, you can definitely see the bloodborne inspiration from all of them. I like how they're all vampires it's a nice contrast to the wolf monsters and such from bloodborne and like bloodborne they have different designs and unique attacks that keep them from getting stale.The graphic art style is very good sometimes beautiful with so many nice little touches  that makes you just want to stop and stare at all, some of it could even make good PC wallpaper. The levels are all very good, quite diverse with most levels not looking the same and each part is quite distinct, it just makes you want to explore everything and find all its secrets.The story was good like any souls like game a lot of the story is told through item description, notes and character dialogue, the story we piece together is quite good and tells you the hubris and greed of humans.The characters were good with interesting looks and nice dialogue, I think my favorite happens to be the kids they were quite adorable and spooky, I will there is a problem with them but I'll get to that in dislikes. The music is quite good with plenty of great epic tracks that fit the game very well, the voice acting was also good although I will say some voice acting felt a little bit stiff but I didn't really mind it. The animation for the whole game was quite good very fluid with nice little touches like this one enemy that stabs itself to create an ice spear, also when adding a power up to your weapon. The atmosphere is good as you're wandering around this levels infested with monsters, it's pretty spooky for a metroidvania side scroller.Alright then let's talk about the dislikes, well there are some bugs, nothing really game breaking, although there was this one time where I transformed into beast mode and did some flash steps and somehow got lodged in a floor and I couldn't get out of it which made me quit and reload the game. Also for some reason my new controller would randomly make my character activate a magic spell or shoot a bullet without me pressing anything, I don't know why this is a new controller it’s a 8Bitdo Ultimate C Wired Controller. But my older controller didn't have that problem when I used it. Also lastly when I was fighting the true final boss of the game for some reason my screen closed and the game did not pause.Now speaking of bosses there are two bosses that are absolutely bunk, one boss being Manfred the accursed, he's extremely difficult especially in his second phase with dark energy attacks and a phantom that fights you. Then the other is the true final boss, that fight was bull because this boss has a shield that she activates which got really annoying, especially when she goes into her second phase.Now for the little girls I did like them, but I do wish there was more they could do in the game like after completing their quest they sell you something or give you something if you need it, also would have liked a few more side quests to do in the game. Finally I have to say the parrying system isn't really good, I mean in blasphemous parrying is advised, but here I don't know I rarely used it, it just felt completely under utilize.Alright then with all that done with The Last Faith is a really good metroidvania Souls like game despite some flaws; with really good gameplay, really good enemies and bosses and a good graphic art style. So this is a really good metroidvania souls like game that's definitely going to sit next to the greats, like Blasphemous and Ender lilies I also hope there's going to be DLC whether it be an art book or new levels.

_childDocuments_.review: I call back to the old school 2d games.The game is a mix of bloodborne and castlevania SOTN and the elements blend together pretty well, It has some flaws that should be looked at again but overall the game is really fun and challenging Le good:enemies scale as any souls game, with enemies being much harder in areas you aren't ready for yet. weapons can be upgraded as well like souls games and have basic combos with a special ability that costs mana to use, mana can be regenerated using finishers on enemies or using shards, which makes your skills and magic almost synergistic with melee combat. there are also guns but most of the time I don't use them, they're good to get enemies into a finish state as they do low damage but other than that i don't see them being a good dedicated weapon choice.Bosses are super fun to face and present a fun challenge, they really feel like skill checks to test your ability to dodge, read attacks, and utilize openings.There Is a bullet hell sense to the game with players needing to dodge a sequence of attacks or take horrible damage, I personally love these aspects as it feels great weaving through attacks and continuing your assault.Le bad:some things in the game make no sense to me, such as falling. most areas you can and will fall down seemingly miles and take no damage, but if the fall below has a transition to another area it kills you, this honestly should be changed as It doesn't make any sense In a technical sense. or add fall damage, either or.the first item you get lets you parry enemies and regain health, which is nice as the meter needed to use this ability refills after each successful hit (fast hitting weapons are perfect for building this meter) however there are no indications on what attacks can be dodged or parried other than trial and error.Its very, VERY easy to get lost or overlook something, with a lot of areas needing later game skills to access and by that time you've completely forgotten about them, This isn't a bad thing technically since older games like this did this quite often but older areas always tied into later ones, this game doesn't seem to do that and if it doesn't not very well.Overall this game is a must buy for players who are familiar with old school side scrolling games, the feel and controls along with the style of the game really touch base with my nostalgia of much older games on the PS1 and older while adding the challenge and difficulty of a souls type game,  I hope games like this become more common place and that this game especially gets some more content or another game down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! It's like a mixture between Bloodborne and Blasphemous, but it has its own thing going on.You have stats just like in a Souls game, so you can choose how you want to build your character, adding replay value and encouraging experimentation. Controls are tight and responsive, I haven't encountered any bugs or crashes in my 10+ hours with the game. You unlock new abilities as you progress and the game isn't linear (much like Blasphemous). You have the freedom to explore though some areas will have enemies that are much higher leveled than you. The difficulty isn't too high, but it's not a cakewalk either. Since this game has elemental attacks, some bosses will be harder depending on your build/resistances, which I really liked. The 2D pixel art is gorgeous and the animations are smooth, really good enemy variety as well as superb boss design. It's the closest anyone could get to a 2D Bloodborne, in my opinion. Now regarding the story, this is probably my only nitpick with the game. The story itself is vague, convoluted, told mostly through item descriptions (as you would expect in a Souls game) but what bothers me is that they made every single character speak in a cryptic, philosophical, grandiose manner. It's fine for some characters, but imagine if every Dark Souls character spoke like the Locust Preacher. You also need simpler lines like the ones you'd hear from Andre, Patches or even Sparkly the Crow, to break up the monotony. In the Last Faith it felt like they were using big words just for the sake of sounding more profound, also the voice acting is a bit off sometimes (but that I can forgive). The main character isn't a silent protagonist, but his short and simple lines clash with the aforementioned style and feel out of place (like he's being super friendly/understanding to every creature that can speak, regardless if it's a lady or an eldritch abomination).Overall, love my time with this game, highly recommended for anyone into Metroidvanias and Soulslikes. Hoping they add more content over time and maybe some new game modes as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, The last Faith,  a 2D bloodborn experience.The good:The art style is very well made with beautiful pixel art, the aesthetic of the world fits pretty well for the type of story they are going for,  the music its pretty nice, setting the atmosphere very well, in boss fights it gets intense as the fights goes on, the exploration is quite nice, as is expected in metroidvanias, secret walls, heal upgrades, ammo upgrades, weapons and such.The bad:Okay, my biggest critique on this game is the janky movement, ledge grabbing is off, movement feels jank, combat feels very jank, which is a problem when that's what you will be doing 70% of the time,  animations feel like they are lacking frames, I swear the running animation of Eryk is like three frames, and I know the developers can do better because later on I found a flying bat moving a 60 fps, so i'm just baffled.The story of this game is very, very scarce, you will never understand why Eryk is, or what he is, why he was imprisoned or what the hell happen to the world, even after finish the game and getting the true ending there was still so many unanswered questions.Conclusion:Is this a fun game? yes it is, is this game worth 30 dollars? no, hell no, I 100% this game in 24 hours, so I didn't even got 1 hour of entertaining for each dollar I spend on it, im not much to throw shade at the developers but for how unpolished this game feels, is not worth 30 dollars, is a beautiful game but have too many little issues plaguing it.I will recomend to get it on a sale.A broken Promise/10

_childDocuments_.review: A yet further game to add to the ever growing pile of games from developers who went "oh, Dark Souls is good because hard, right???" without ever actually thinking about what made them good in the first place: mystery and intrigue. Throwing a bunch of random made up words (with no explanation for what they are) into badly recorded dialogue isn't intrigue and mystery, by the way, its just bad writing. The VAs also sound like they're more than half asleep, because they all talk SO SLOWLY. As for the gameplay itself, it's clunky at best, like you're moving slow as molasses while the enemies are moving way faster than you, so Git Gud(tm) idiot, because HARD MEANS GOOD, RIGHT?? The bosses themselves are annoying simply because there's no  about them. It feels like "we have filled an arbitrary amount of space with identical rooms, so here's a big one with a bigger dude in it now, I guess. ♥♥♥♥ you." The shrine placement (or whatever they're called) is also god awful, because it feels like in the first few areas there's one every other room and then suddenly you have to go through two whole dungeons without finding a single one. The entire time I was playing, I kept thinking of an audio from TikTok: "Day 3 on the way to Shmenmangor. It's been ages since we left Perinelifnel. As always, my companions Perbinsholfdup and Carl are with me."I saw one review that said this was the best thing since SOTN, and I need to know what they were smoking, because this game feels derivative at best, and just garbage at worst. If you want to play this game and haven't played Blasphemous, just get that instead. They just released the sequel, so there's two whole games that you would do better to spend your time on. If you have played Blasphemous, just play it again, because it'll be a lot better than this.

The backtracking is not terrible, but it is somewhat inconvenient to run across the map to get 1 item, and then run back through an empty map to get back to the save/warp point.The game just released, so I'm hoping the devs go back and make a few adjustments.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game all in all! Combat feels good, has a good bit of weight to it. The enemies are well-balanced to be strong, but not annoying (for example, there's no enemy that flies away from you when you get close). There's a bunch of weapons and spells, though I mostly stuck to Biggest Sword and smallest gun. Maybe I'll try magic if I do another playthrough. Bosses in particular are a highlight, which is what you want I think. Some really well-realized gimmicks. The art and animation is gorgeous, and I never felt like I got hit by something because of poor telegraphing.There are some problems. The writing is so bad that the only way I know it wasn't made by AI is by all the made up words and names. The world is kinda bloated. There's a lot of rooms that feel like they serve no purpose other than to extend the experience. Normally that's not a big deal, but it combines with the map's issues to be kind of annoying. The map doesn't have a special way of showing if something is a bottomless pit or more map, so re-exploring areas in the late game is really annoying. If the map was smaller so it was easier to remember what various rooms were it would be less of a deal. The map also breaks in places, not filling in or showing rooms that aren't there. It would also be nice to have a larger variety of map icons.Despite the issues I had fun with it and would recommend it to anyone who liked Blasphemous.

The biggest problem this game has is that you've seen everything it has to offer before and other similar games are a bit better.  But that's not to say that this is a bad game or not worth playing because it's a very good game and absolutely worth playing.

This is Blasphemous x Bloodborne.This game has it's issues but the good things outweigh the bad for me.Bad:I liked blasphemous 1 and this game is very comparable. I think overall this game as a gameplay experience is a worse version of Blasphemous, but the theme is so good and well put together that I finished and really enjoyed this game and I don't regret 1 second of gameplay. Pixel art in both games is top notch and full of vibe.Exploration:The zones and enemies look amazing.The map layout in Blasphemous is ridiculously clever. The Last Faith's map tries to be a maze like but it's not clever, it has a few patterns and that's it, the zones are well defined and not intertwined like in Blasphemous. But the simplicity is refreshing and I enjoyed a more relaxed exploration so I don't complain but it's worth noting.Combat:Parry is very bad. Executions have a weird timing.In Blasphemous you have 1 weapon, but the combat is varied. Each enemy forces you to a combat style and because of that they feel very different. In The Last Faith you can chose from multiple weapons but There isn't much difference between enemies, standard dodge the charge attack. Its not bad but it requires less thinking and even with the weapons choices combat isn't that diverse as in Blasphemous.Spells and pistols don't feel good. They feel as a waste of resources and time. Basic attack feels the best choice (not charge attack).Sure you have diversity but you don't have an incentive to try different things.Music:The soundtrack is not that huge, but is awesome.Story telling:Is good. Blasphemous is great, but they have a big base with the religious theme; they explored the big and small themes and they twisted them in great ways (e.g. washing of feet). But for what The Last Faith had to work with it did great.Loot:I am not a big fan of farming for heal potions and bullets. This makes the game more punishing. The strong point of souls-like games is figuring out combat patterns and mastering them. Farming and enemy that you already know just so you have more tries for a boss is less fun. I more fun to die at the boss 100 times and getting better each time than to die at the boss 20 times and farming for resources so you have more tries. Failure is not necessarily a bad experience, farming (and reseting the enemies for farm) is boring.But it stays true to Bloodborne for who likes that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: No idea why this game is rated yellow on Steam Deck.  Whatever this mysterious "hard to read text," is, I never encountered in 30 hours and a nearly-completionist playthrough. Dead Cells was literally used to show the Steam Deck off and this game runs exactly as well.Probably the souls-iest of the Soulslike Metroidvanias. Unlike games like Blasphemous and Dead Cells, this one has a full stats system and weapons based on stat scaling. This game definitely patterns itself off of Bloodborne moreso than Dark Souls; healing is done via frequently dropped consumable vials (that have a limit on how many you can carry at once) instead of reusable flasks, there's no block button (by default; it's an unlockable slot shared with other defensive abilities), and the setting is a Lovecraftian take on Victorian London rather than a decaying medieval kingdom.Combat feels good, and you mostly feel like it's your own damn fault when you die. My only real criticism was the terrible default control scheme (it splits difference between Dark Souls and Metroid, changing enough from both that your muscle memory will inevitably betray you), but the January 2024 patch made controls remappable.If you liked other combat heavy 2D Metroidvanias, there's a lot here to like. If you wish you could play/replay Bloodborne but don't have a PlayStation, this is spiritually the closest game I've ever played.The only real issue is that the late game kind of requires using a wiki.  It involves a ton of backtracking to get stuff you couldn't reach without the airdash and double jump.  You can mark this stuff on your map, but there's a ton of them and I wound up hitting the marker limit.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Cool art, very satisfying combat and well done plattforming. That's enough for an easy recommend.Neutral:I wouldn't call it a Metroidvania - exploration is held back by the linear weapon progression. While there are some shortcuts, not a lot of areas are connected in a way that would invite for sequence breaks or are just hard locked. Now that is not a death sentence for the game, it's still pretty good. It's just more like a 2D Bloodborne than an actual metroidvania.Negatives (until NG+ update or economy rebalance)Also a lot of weapons with cool skills come really late into the game, so either you look those up gimp your stats early until you get them or you are too deep into attribute distribution to actually use them properly. Paired with the insane expensive Weapon upgrades makes grind a necessity for upgrading those late game items when you've already heavily invested in early ones. Now keep in mind, as soon as NG+ drops this will be better since you can use those late game items and charms for more than 2-3 bosses at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a well-crafted, densely packed, extremely fun entry in the Soulsvania genre.While comparisons to Bloodborne and Blasphemous are apt and accurate enough, it's plain to see the sheer passion and talent that the devs so clearly poured into The Last Faith, serving to elevate the title beyond and distinguish it from being a simple sum of it's constituent parts; in my opinion to the degree of leaving a well-defined mark of it's own on the genre.The world of TLF is filled top-to-bottom with exquisitely crafted pixel art. weaving spectacular life into the bleakly-beautiful elegance of Mythringal and it's surrounding areas. This aforementioned pixel art is paired with snappy-smooth and eye-pleasing animations; animations which likely elicit a welcome and comfortable nostalgia in anyone with a history with Castlevania Symphony of the Night and it's ilk.The story of the game is delivered exactly as you'd expect of a souls game, with very little in the way of direct exposition. Instead trust is put in the player to interpret and fit the pieces together for themselves, with the majority of information being gleaned bit-by-bit through item-descriptions, notes and documents scattered throughout the world, and through the anecdotally interpretive insights offered up through dialogue with the games devishly-stylish, voice-acted caste of characters, creatures, and other entities.There's plenty of other reviews here to describe the combat and itemization in the game. Suffice it to say that I think the item system, including weapons, is well-focused on quality over quantity in a pleasing way, while still having enough options and ways to tinker with those options to find something interesting to work with for most playstyles.This game is absolutely worth the price of admission. The Last Faith stands shoulder-to-shoulder with those games which serve as examples of the genre at it's finest, and so if you consider yourself even a casual fan of said genre, I highly suggest you don't skip or wait on this one.You will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: This is a soft "Not recommend". There is enjoyment to be had, but at the end of the day there are other better options.The good? Controls feel tight, the lore is interesting. Individual zones are designed in interesting ways.The bad? Difficulty spikes wildly seemingly out of nowhere. Despite being a metroidvania, there is always a strongly correct way to progress. This progression is not always indicated by access/movement abilities (like most metroidvanias) but frequently by the difficulty of mobs.Most side quests I've completed feel unfinished, you do one thing / return one item, you get the little story line finished achievement, but there is no conclusion / progression to the character involved.Enemies are more damage sponge than hard, and the encounter design is occasionally atrocious. Notably, a named boss will show up as a normal mob (with no adjustment to its stats, I think?) prior to that boss if you take a minor detour.Balance also feels bad. At similar levels a character focused on strength can do significantly more damage swinging their sword than someone can with a cast of a spell, despite the spell requiring a longer wind up, and being heavily limited by mana. Why bother with the more interesting combat abilities if the basic ones are just better?

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, The Last Faith is janky.  Between annoyingly ruthless enemies, a terribly limited system of resources, unoptimized controls, and a quite frankly bland art design, the game does little to stand out in comparison to its peers like Salt & Sanctuary, Symphony of the Night, and especially its biggest source of inspiration, Blasphemous (both 1 and 2).  It just seems like someone tried to copy Bloodborne using the same programs as Blasphemous, but without any of the ideas, designs, or gimmicks that made those games special.  I do hope, however, that the game will eventually the refinement it may deserve.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing dark/gothic metroidvania that's well worth getting if you're a fan of metroidvanias, souls-likes, or both. The aesthetic is well established, an beautiful, which is quite the achievement for the 16-bit style. The music is even more impressive - somehow managing to make a single melody both melodic and peaceful, but tense and morose at the same time. Combat is tough but rewarding and fair.For as much as I've enjoyed the game, there are a few minor tweaks that would go a long way; combat can feel a bit stiff with the heavier weapons, and the stats definitely seems to favor them - a minor increase to weapon speeds overall would add to fluidity imo, and anything not strength based could definitely use a buff to damage output.Similarly could be said of the story - even with over 90% completion much of the narrative remains a mystery and for the life of me, I can't piece much together. Side quests don't fare any better - characters introduced tend to disappear as soon you complete what they want you to do with no indication what they intend to do in the future.However, most egregiously, is how convoluted the map is. You expect a certain degree of back tracking with metroidvanias, and that's fine, but with the sheer amount in this game coupled with a bare bones map can leave you lost and floundering for extended periods. They really need to flesh out the map with markers indicating paths that are locked behind various skills.Nevertheless, the game is great fun in spite of the nitpicks; and most of said nitpicks could probably be addresses in a patch or two (fingers crossed), but even if nothing changes this is still a rock-solid8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: As someone once said: It's fine.The games decent; combat is fine, weapons are fine, magic is fine...storys fine. Guess that's just it though. "It's fine.' it dosent really break any molds, innovate on anything, its just...average.It dosent have any real workings that make it stand out from others of this game type.  It's not bad, the gameplays fun in itself but just nothing to really stand out from say 'salt and sanctuary' or 'blasphemous' but you can do worse, ill only say the price point is kind of high, maybe like 10 dollars to much.(Side note: ADD SCREEN RESOLUTION OPTIONS AND WINDOWED MODE.)

_childDocuments_.review: I tried this back when it first dropped, and it didn't quite click. I love Metroidvanias, and I love a good Souls-influencee, which you could certainly call this- but I didn't give it much of a chance, and moved on after the first boss.During the February '24 debacle which was the technically disastrous release of Helldivers 2, I was forced to look back into my catalog, and I gave it another swing- and this time, it clicked quickly. It's a great, combat-centric Metroidvania.The Metroidvania aspects are executed well- abilities grow over time, increasing your ability to explore a non-linear map. Treasure and found items are typically impactful, and you can build your character in meaningfully different ways. Enemies are reasonably diverse, and dangerous- but not too dangerous.This is a hard game- but it's not THAT hard. It's a good challenge, but unless you tilt/get frustrated, careful play will see you through without too many deaths (I say this only 20% in, so who knows what terrors I may yet find...)Regarding tilt- health items do not replenish automatically. They drop with relative frequency, but if you're wasteful / burn them all fighting a single boss, you will find yourself in a frustrating situation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent so far! Absolutely breathtaking pixel art, the controls are easy to navigate and pick up if you are familiar with souls-likes, and wonderfully atmospheric tone and characters. The combat is pretty straightforward, sound and feel of the combos and strikes feel satisfying and meaty. Some critiques: the dodge roll could use some tweaking, feels like the timing is a bit short compared to other souls-likes and ends a little early in the animation, and there seems to be a recovery time after a dodge, so you can't chain or panic roll, which I get in terms of design, but would be nice to have some sort of meter or indicator when you can roll again or better indication of when iframes are active/over. As a result, I find that I rely on my jump more for dodging and spacing, as it has faster reaction and covers a  degree of movement so you can get out of attacks, even if it doesn't have iframes. I managed to kill the first boss on my first try using this method. This is just a minor detail though, the game looks and feels fantastic and is a great addition to my collection of soul-likes, can't wait for more!

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith (TLF) is a mildly challenging 2D metroidvania that seems primarily influenced by Bloodborne in terms of atmosphere and lore. Some will draw parallels to Blasphemous, and for sure there are many similarities, but that game is also derivative of the genre and TLF is visually distinct enough that calling it a clone is very silly.One thing that TLF does share with Blasphemous is the unpolished state in which it launched. Blasphemous is now so beloved that many have forgotten the lukewarm reception it initially received. A few patches in and things are much better for TLF. I'm hoping that a few more iterations will improve things further.So what does it do right?Well, your mileage may vary here but I found the combat quite enjoyable. There's a lot more diversity in builds than many other similar games with plenty of different melee & ranged weapons to find as well as spells and some other special abilities I won't spoil. The combat is quite deliberate and can feel a little clunky at first, in fact the movement itself can take a while to adjust to. Iframes on rolling are present and generous and combat in general never felt too unforgiving. If I hit a difficulty roadblock there was always somewhere else to go. Levelling up works very similarly to a Souls game with some weapons scaling better with certain stats.The exploration is also pretty decent. The map is of a good size and there are plentiful secrets and quests to discover. As with any metroidvania worth its salt, there's backtracking aplenty to explore ability gated areas, though the somewhat slow movement speed can make it a little tedious sometimes. There is fast travel from "Altars" (read: bonfires) but some kind of item to warp to an altar would be appreciated; think Homeward Bone from Dark souls.Visually the game looks amazing, with fantastic pixel art and lovely animation; especially the executions. The music is also good with one track in particular being very reminiscent of Bloodborne. Overall the game nails the dark Gothic atheistic and atmosphere.------------------------------------------------Things it doesn't quite nail? Some lost inputs, especially on the air dash. This is a very repeatable issue though it didn't impact my play-through too much as there is zero precision platforming here.The writing and lore just isn't well delivered. There's a skill to writing cryptic dialogue that imparts enough information to the player to start making some assumptions/connections while still retaining enough mystery to keep them intrigued. You can see that TLF is trying to emulate that Dark Souls style but the result is strings of words that are utterly incoherent and a chore to read/hear. Who knows or cares what's happening here?In summary, the game is good. With some more polish it could be very good but the lore is likely beyond salvation at this point meaning we'll probably need to wait for a sequel to see an A tier metroidvania from the devs.I have faith that they can do it and don't regret backing this game one bit.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Bloodborne meets Castlevania.It is a superb game that any fan of the above will enjoy.The pixel art is worthy of attention because it is damn gorgeous.The controls do feel a bit clunky at first but one thing you must take into account and that the game never tells you is that you can interrupt any attack animation in any moment to do the roll/backstep. Keep that in mind and you experience will be smoother.The challenge aspect of the game is perhaps my main critic. The map is MASSIVE, to the point you will even feel a bit tired because the areas seem to going on and on and on. However, the level progression is worthy of attention, the ice one especially is neat to travel because you go through snowy ruins, a frozen cave, a town under a blizzard until you reach the massive castle. The first hours of the game are pretty hard and can get frustrating at times because you can get to mostly any area right off the bat, but with just the vague hints you get from NPCs and items you will feel a bit lost, enemies will seems overpowered due to how easily they can kill you and how the exploration aspect is hampered until you get the double jump.Right after that things get easy, perhaps a bit too much, as you can easily abuse the movement mechanics to make any fight a breeze.Weapons are obviously inspired by the Bloodborne aesthetic too. There's even a pair of katanas for the edegelords out there. However, most weapons are very well hidden and you may not obtain them until the very end of the game, so you may not be able to enjoy the build variety as much as you want.There are also a few ranged weapons but they seemed kinda lame and weak compared to the melee options and the spells.The weapon upgrade system also seems unbalanced. You can just stick to the greatsword, get it to +10 and with 50 strenght you will get an attack rating of 1,000 (!) so you will kill almost anything in 1 or 2 hits sans for large enemies and bosses. If you truly want a challenge maybe you will refrain from getting overleveled or maxing your weapons.Bosses are one of the main aspects of the game and are fairly challenging, but once you get their patterns right and/or upgrade your equipment they should not be a problem.The thing that will kill you the most is the overtime damage due to status effects. Do not overlook them, there's a reason why the game gives you so much items to counter those ailments!Overall, it is a very solid game and I sincerely hope the devs keep at it, either with future DLC, game modes or even a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I wanted to like this game, but right off the rip it does some stuff I can't vibe with.-Game commits the modern cardinal sin of not letting you change your controls. -Can't change any sort of graphical setting, even something as simple as fullscreen windowed, or even just windowed.-Hit boxes are not clean. Ex: Had dog enemies (that can not jump) hit me at the apex of my jump.-Choosing the 'Mage' archetype does not give you any kind of starting spell before the first boss, leaving you at a weird stat disadvantage initially (something not noted when choosing your type.)-You can cancel attacks with dodges but not jumps? This should honestly be a neither or a both situation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, I honestly like it better than blasphemous, it feels more "souls" than metroidvania.Starting off some pain points a lot of people mentioned: farming heals. I don't get this, after you beat the second boss, you will have an NPC that sells them at 50 souls per vial. Only 50, later on they increase by a small amount, but still, every run through the map you get at least like couple K, 1000 souls will already give you 20 heals, not to mention the breakable boxes on the map drop vials too. I am overflown with heals in my play through I don't get how this can be a problem. It's not like BB they sell it at like 180 souls per vial. I-frames: this is another thing I don't get. There is rarely any collision damage on the enemies, only some, but most of them don't, same with most of the bosses. That means, you can just walk through or jump through them without any problems. And there is I-frame, just very short and I believe it's at the very beginning of the rolling animation (maybe I am wrong), but without collision damage in a 2D game this already made the game quite easy, I can't imagine the game would be fun and challenging with more I-frames on the rolling. Boss design, I actually think this game has better boss design than blasphemous personally. I've always had problems with the amount of projectiles in blasphemous series bosses. I remember really hated endless orison in blasphemous 2, because it's not hard, it's just annoying given how long and repetitive that battle was. The real boss fight was just dodging the projectiles rather than the boss itself. Which isn't the case in this game. Yes, I would say the bosses in this game are pretty easy, but at least it's fun. There are projectiles here and there but never the main element of any boss fights. You are fighting the bosses, learning their movements etc. Just like BB bosses, easy, but fun (not talking about DLC). There is indeed a big problem with class balance. If you want to play as a "mage" class, i.e. using spells mainly, it's going to be very difficult. You have a very small pool of mana, and the spell damage is a joke. It takes longer to activate a spell than a great-sword swing, and it does less damage than a great-sword hit, while consuming a big chunk of your mana. Plus you can't use spell in air. Same with guns, you can't shoot dogs with a gun, nor any flying enemies. So the only reliable attack is your melee weapon. Currently from what I can tell, nothing beats a great sword. They are fast, it's funny because great swords are too much slower than dex weapon, but has more damage. So depending on your weapon, the experience can range from extremely easy to extremely difficult. At some point with same stats, with a great-sword I was doing ~200 damage per hit, or ~70 per hit with a whip. Both had mind scaling. Parry is pretty useless too, I am not sure why it requires two buttons to parry, and the parry damage is less than melee hit. The map design is good, with a lot of varieties and things are connected through shortcuts pretty well. I would say the art isn't as atmospherical and great as blasphemous 2, but still pretty decent. I don't like how the UI is designed, it's quite counter intuitive that the right item slot is trigger by LT, and left item is RT, it's really confusing and I still get them wrong even I played this long. Plot is...? NPCs talk like freshly out of a Shakespeare play, so I lost my interest in what they say real soon. But overall, I think the combat and exploration is pretty fun, movements are smooth, good variety of weapons and move sets, fun boss designs, good map designs and enemy varieties. There aren't any platform challenges like typical metroidvania, so If you like souls type more, this will do for a 2D version.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a metroidvania with soulslike statistical elements that can be classified as medium-easy difficulty. Initially, we can choose between 4 “classes” (which will not be binding for the gameplay, we can change later or, after completing the quest of the girl who levels you up, we can reset everything): strength, dexterity, mind (magic), and instinct (firearms).The Last Faith strongly resembles Bloodborne and Blasphemous, and therefore often lacks that extra bit of personality.All in all, apart from some platforming flaws due to imperfect animations and some combat bugs (rare, but they can happen), it is a game that, in my opinion, deserves a 7/10 and is absolutely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait until I finished the game before making any comments on it, and while I will gladly recommend it, that recommendation comes with a caveat.This game certainly deserves all the hype that it was given, but it still is hype, and that tends to misdirect from any flaws there are and The Last faith is far from flawless. Amongst those are the many (many, many) crashes that I encountered,  and while possibly being easily attributed to it being made in Unity, is most likely due to poor optimisation on the developers end - as this has been a common enough issue being remarked in the discussion boards as well as warranting responses and hit or miss solutions from a cursory Google search. There is also the atrocious controller lag that I noted, as well as awkward input queuing that when come into contact leads to, well, awkward situations especially noted in combat.The lack of any form of extended or greater tutorial or manual explaining even in the most shallow way some key mechanics while expecting the player to assume said mechanics was also a bit frustrating - to me personally at least. As an example, at what point in any "Soulslike" weapon upgrading system has it been that upgrade components are not fully consumable? I spent 75% of the time with no more than +2 weapons because I was waiting to get a second blueprint as not to waste it. Turns out while it is needed to upgrade past that point, it is not consumable in and of itself. Nowhere is this mentioned as a thing, making things more difficult than necessary. There is also an extreme imbalance when it comes to weapons, with Strength build being either "normal" difficulty or, as it more likely due to starting with a Dex weapon, "easy mode" as it features as a stat in a majority of the non-spell and ranged weapons. This is also as well as being the only stat that has not just one, but two only stat weapons (out of a total of 13 "melee" or "primary") - and they are the highest damage output weapons on equal stat and upgrade, but also don't have a necessarily slower attack speed to balance out. Example, The Severance Reaper Scythe that is dual Dex and Str at 50 Dex and 44 Str topped out at 750-ish damage. The Ethereal Great Blade, which is found much earlier and is Str ONLY, tops out at nearly 900 at 50 Str alone. Other than the starting melee weapon and starting ranged you receive primarily Str based weapons or Str leaning dual stat weapons early on - leading to heaving build towards Str. Now, this in of itself is not an issue - IF this is how the dev's intended for it to be played as the baseline. But then note that on the "Class" selection screen. I may have just missed it but I don't believe that I did, just add a note to the remaining "classes" that indicates that they are "for advanced players" or "for those looking for a challenge". If Str builds are what everyone will mostly get funneled into or are what makes the game cheesable then why bother to have the other stats? Granted I played by putting a single point into each stat evenly across the levels, but there are few "Soulslikes" where that causes brickwalling in progress and the few that do make it known from the outset or are recognized as being unbalanced in gameplay.Nitpicks and gripes aside, this is a FANTASTIC game. Not only one of the best Metroidvanias I have played, but also a wonderful integration of "Soulslike mechanics" into the Genre - right up there with the Blasphemous series and Hollow Knight. Considering as well that it released on the heels of Blasphemous 2 and, as blasphemous as it might sound, completely eclipses it in sheer gameplay. It really is that good. But in all of that the flaws ultimately drag it down to just great, bordering at times on fantastic - where with proper polish and balancing it would be AMAZING. That's what I walked away feeling. Satisfied but disappointed.Now the dev team looked quite small to mid-sized from the credits and I don't know what kind of support the publisher provides or provided to them, but the publisher has a small but respectable library under their belt and this is a great addition, but I feel like it could have used a bit longer in the oven to reach the heights that are clearly there under the issues. The lack of NG+ might seem as passable, but while the primary loop is more Metroidvania than Souls - it is all Souls where this element is concerned - and as such really should have launched with it. Again, this is just me.TLDR;Amazing game brought down to just great by rough mechanics, lack of player information and optimisation issues that will all hopefully get fixed in future updates. But for what seems to be the first offering from a smaller dev team is a potential treasure and classic that comes with an absolute recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Not perfect but a great playthrough. Still has some rough edges, and apparently I lucked out by skipping the early versions, but I still enjoyed my time. _childDocuments_.review: Well......I waited a long time for this game, loving Metroidvania's. Unfortunately, every game is a Souls clone, I'm surprised they have added Soul's concepts to Madden or Call of Duty yet. In my honest opinion, this game is cool.....but it feels like something is missing. I found myself bored by the time I got to the big wing skeleton boss you fight on the bridge. There was no save point halfway through that area leading up to that boss fight which was annoying. I know, I know - get GUD. I am ready for a Metroidvania that is not, you are going to die a lot or run past all the enemies to get back to where you are. I love Dark Souls but hate it at the same time because everything is Soul's now, and I mean everything. One thing I miss about Metroid, and Castlevania is it is a fluid adventure with progression within reason, whereas all these games are not, Grime being the biggest offender. I beat that game but F that game. I like this game for the most part but I am not sure what is missing. I still recommend it though if you are into these. A final note, I am at the winged skeleton boss on the bridge but I have to go upgrade my weapons, but I am out of funds to do so. So now I have to leave the area go grind, go to the manor, and then go back and fight the boss - total chore, not fun. Happy Thanksgiving everyone. P.S. Nintendo ruined Metroid Dread as well, complete letdown.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Metroidvania games and Soulsborne games, i can easily recommend this game.  It has alot of features from the afamed Bloodborne such as healing vials and the weapon leveling system but has the exploration of a old 2D castlevania.  Only con i can see so far is that you die immediately when falling in holes or touching spikes and part of the metroidvania is exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Like Souls-like, metroidvania games? Maybe just gothic, or dark aesthitcs? This games for you. Its a great game, despite the occasional negative review. Addressing what I have seen:- The scaling: Not an issue, their is an obvious path of progression - stray from that and youll be  in for a challenge. The path is obvious if you play these styles of games and nothing stops you from turning around and finding the right way if your new to metroidvanias. - "I cant reach that": There are parts in the story where you need to retrace where you've clearly been before and access those rooms you remembered not being able to reach with the new abilities you've earned. When these breaks occur feels very well placed in the progression. They are ment for you to power up before progressing further into the story, exploring is VERY rewarding once youve earned a new mobility enhancement.-Build diversity: The weapon pool is not as saturated as say Elden Ring, but build diversity exists in a plethora of options with what you do have. Id recommend picking a build to start with around 1 or two stats. Eventually (and quite early for most souls-likes) youll find the ability to respec. From their you can get crafty with 3+ damage attributes.  The story caught me unexpectedly after I wasn't sure I was interested in that aspect but, I really enjoyed everything about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Not the best metroidvania I have ever played and certainly not the worst, at least until the bugs started flying in. The game has what I'd probably describe as challenge rooms where you find yourself locked in until you defeat a number of enemy waves. Well, I was carrying a lot of leveling currency going into a room, no big deal, but an enemy vanished as it spawned. Doors remained locked and I've got no way out. Lost progress, lost my currency, lost interest.

_childDocuments_.review: castlevania in the most direct sense (not Symphony of the Night, but more the classical ones) meets Bloodborneand it worksnow don't expect somehing akin to a From metroidvania, it's much "smaller", but that doesn't make it a bad game especialy looking at the price.you kill enemies/bosses they drop currency which you can either spend on a whole slew of vendors or on increasing your stats (Bloodborne-lightish). strength, dexterity and intellect serve as your classical damage stats, whereas mind serves as both: a damage stat and an increase to your "mana"-pool (focus here); vit is a base increase for your health-pool.there's a fixed amount of weapons, which means normal enemies don't drop "gear or loot", they drop either bullets for your guns (and a sword) or health-injectors aside from their currency.i think it's around 10 weapons, with each having a distinct move-set and feel. there's your basic 1 button combo, there's a charged attack, there's a dodge attack and a jump attack, aswell a special move for each weapon. it's more than enough in the grand scheme of things and it feels realy good to actualy play.you also get a wide variety of spells, like a sith-force-lighting, flame tornados or icespikes, etc. and a lot of guns.each spell and weapon also scales with different stats which in turn offers you damage upgrades (also stuff as classical requirements, but you can use everything despite not meeting said requirements, instead you get a slight damage malus)there's also classical soulsborne like weapon-upgrading.there's also rare 1 slot special stigmas, which offer a lot of utility specials like beeing able to counter or increase your attackspeed, aswell as 4 charm slots for passive boni.then there's a wide variety of usable items which remind me also a lot of From's games: weapon buffs, statuseffect healing items, HoT items, bombs, etc. .it's certainly not quite the vast amount a SotN offered or Bloodstained, but it's still rock solid.the metroidvania elements are also very well done. you get little puzzles, jumping puzzles, new abilities to unlock new paths, often also new ways to find the more special utility items or weapons, charms'n spells. i found the general level gameplay just as responsive and engaging as the combat. the game also as extensive world building (soulslike item describtions) and a lot of fully voiced dialogue. there's a lot of story here and a lot of characters. the soundeffects and the OST are also very competent, and some athmospheric soundscapes where downright brilliant.about the only complaint i got is a very minor one: due to the setting and the more gothic like appearence locations tend to look rather similiar. it's kinda hard to explain. each location has been very well done, it's quite stunning 2D pixelart, full of detail, but a bit more diversity in appearance (difficult to do, i get it: it's a gothic game) would've done wonders. but again: it's not a real issue.quite a standout game in the genre, with engageing exploration, boss fights and probably one of the best combat itterations in the genre. not quite on the scale SotN or Bloodstained offered, but a 100% recommendation still.
