_childDocuments_.review: It's a combination of genres, but doesn't do any of them particularly well. There's clearly Bloodborne influence, but a lot of mechanics that makes Bloodborne's game play great didn't transfer over. The colors and art direction are monotonous; every stage tends to look the same and bores over time. Eventually, I just found myself running through levels and bypassing enemies altogether. Maybe I'll pick it up again in the future, but there are more fun games to play right now, especially at this price point.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously awesome. I absolutely love the art style and animations. Like seriously, the animations here are incredible. The world and atmosphere is great, and the music is really good. Combat feels really good and has just the right amount of weight to it. Platforming works well and exploration is satisfying. It always has the right amount of challenge without feeling unfair. Some people are saying the game is like Blasphemous and Bloodborne had a baby, which I would definitely say is accurate though the game certainly stands on its own as well. Its very clear that a lot of love went into this game.I also see some people criticizing the game for balancing issues and idk... it seems pretty well-balanced to me. Some are complaining about severe difficulty spikes, but I think it may be because they went to later-game areas early on. For example, after you get the gravity ring, you shouldn't try the snow area next unless you're looking for a challenge - even though you can easily get to it. That's a later game area. Though of course, you can do things in the order you wish. The Last Faith will not hold your hand AT ALL - you have to figure it out for yourself, which I always love in games like this.Probably the weakest part of the game is the story. Its fairly standard souls-like fair where the game withholds information on purpose and you have to connect the dots, but it never really feels worth it to put in that effort. Dialogue feels awkward and some of the voice acting is questionable. If you're here for the story & lore you may be disappointed. The world & atmosphere are really good, but the story and characters within that world don't hit that same bar. Everything else in the game really shines though.The game does have some small quality of life issues that I hope they fix. You cannot rebind controls on a controller, which I know will be a deal breaker for some. For me the default controls have been fine. Fast travelling could be a bit better. It just gives you a list of fast travel points, which can be a little long and confusing once you find a bunch of warp points. It would be better if they were broken up by area. Menus don't wrap from top to bottom, which is a little weird. You can't select large amounts of items at once, you have to click individually for each one, which can be a little annoying if you're buying large quantities of bullets, for example. But I see these as very small issues which they can certainly patch in the future. I absolutely recommend the game if you like Bloodborne, Blasphemous, Castlevania, and metroidvanias and souls-likes in general. I'm having a blast with it and I hope you do too.tldr; Awesome game, definitely recommend. Fantastic art and animations, fun and satisfying combat and exploration, awesome world, atmosphere, and music. Story is pretty mid but everything else is great.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: TLF is fantastic as an intro to the 2D Soulslike genre. It isn't too difficult, but you do have to respect enemy moves and can't just facetank bosses. Level design is A+, especially the indoor areas. Length is good - I'm very near the end of my first playthrough at 22 hours, and I spent a lot of time backtracking and looking for obscure collectibles. Combat is a lot of fun although certain styles are definitely more challenging than others. Definitely worth full price if you like this genre of game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great 2D souls-like game. Perhaps not as difficult as a true souls game, particularly the levels, but a lot of the bosses were up there in difficulty. This game is semi-open world in the sense that you may stumble upon a high level area meant for late-game but there are certain abilities you need to discover before you are able to move on. I'd say it is more linear than open world but still lots of fun. Enemy variety is aplenty and I liked the fact that you can respec your stats by paying "souls" as opposed to having to find a limited amount of an item to do so. This allows you to test many different builds. I do wish there were more weapons and this probably is a hot take but stamina consumption should also be part of any souls-like game. In any case, I highly recommend this great little game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a perfect combination of Souls-like (Bloodborne, especially) and Metroidvania, namely Castlevania SotN and Blasphemous. The gameplay is tight and feels responsive. The art is some of the most beautiful art I've come across in many years, especially considering it's all pixel art. The soundtrack is also quite fitting and many songs feel like they could have been taken right off the Bloodborne OST. The overall feeling of the game is very much akin to Blasphemous but with even more Souls-like qualities like stats that you level up for more health/damage/mana as well as weapon requirements based on these. The difficulty seems just right, similar to Blasphemous 1, some enemies being tricky the first time you come across them but quickly mow through them the 2nd or 3rd encounter. Bosses are fun to learn and generally feel good to defeat, with some optional and secret bosses as highlights. I can't recommend this game enough. If you are a fan of Bloodborne, Blasphemous, Castlevania, Souls-likes or Metroidvanias in-general you will enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous x Bloodborne. Very impressive for such a small dev team. Great enemy diversity, interesting boss battles, lots of weapon/class diversity, beautiful pixel art.There were a couple of times I was stuck in a wall and had to exit the game so it can be a bit buggy at times. I would prefer a special icon for NPCs or interesting points on the map. Also, the balance of difficulty between some bosses was weird. There were 2 or 3 bosses that were way more difficult than others. I also experienced an instance on 2 bosses where I wouldn't get the free 4 healing injections upon respawn so I would have to travel to the manor every 2 tries to fill up my heals. Not too big of a deal, but a little annoying.Overall, if you enjoy metroidvanias and dark souls mechanics you will enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. After reading a lot of the negative reviews, I feel like those people played a different game than I did. I have played a ton of metroidvania style games and this one is easily in my top 5. The exploring is top-notch, the combat is really fun, and the art style and theme are very reminiscent of Castlevania games. It feels polished and it's just really fun to play overall. The only minor complaint I do have is with the map. I didn't like how the top/bottom of certain rooms would not close off with a solid line after I had completed exploring it. It made me feel like there were areas I had not explored when in reality it was either just an open sky area I could not reach or a pit with a kill plane. The positives drastically outweigh the negatives though and I highly recommend giving this game a chance if you enjoy Metroidvanias of any type.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The fighting is slow and clunky. Enemies are spaced quite far apart which leaves action slowed. When in combat, quickly moving directions and rolling aren't as smooth as they should be. Charged attacks build quickly though which is nice. Action cancelling has been an issue as well. I've found myself repeatedly attacking when I'm asking it to jump instead. Progression is a slog. Oftentimes you trigger the next progression with no clear idea where to progress to next. The health replenishing is not implemented correctly at all. In the beginning you get an overabundance of health but as you progress that completely stops. You can't replenish at a save spot. So if you die to a boss and used all of your potions the only option you have is to grind mobs for money, go to the mansion to purchase more, then return to the boss fight. That completely breaks the fluidity of the game and who wants to do that anyway? There's a reason the quality of life feature of restoring health vials after death is a thing I'm all other games. Also the distance between saves is farther than any other metroidvania I've played. Which wouldn't be bad but again with the health system is broken...

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The atmosphere paired with the music,make the game one of the best I played in this genre. The pixelated art is beautifully crafted,the weapons feel impactful,and smooth,and the lore is like a sip of fine aged red wine in a gloomy night. The only con I can give is that,ain't no way you can do 100% without a guide,you can miss so much,because the game doesn't have indicator for some boss encounters,even if you are a hardcore explorer.All in all, solid 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A good and fun souls-like 2D action platformer with some exploration. Very similar to Blasphemous. Some of the reviewers say it's like Symphony of the Night (SotN) but it really isn't a great comparison; rather, it plays like a souls game. The themes are dark/eldritch horror-esque which can be reminiscent of something from Castlevania but it's not.First, the items are predetermined (no random drops for upgrades/weapons/etc) except the consumables for ammo and health. Second, there's very little in the ways of faster movement; i.e. SotN has different forms and a backdash that make movement faster. There's a "backdash" but it's also tied into your dodge-rolls which are mostly just for combat.Note, none of the above is a "bad" thing, it requires more thoughtful gameplay when fighting enemies. But it's really not a good SotN comparison.The good: Each weapon has its own fighting style and are all viable. The boss fights are engaging and (mostly) not too difficult (though dying a few times is expected). The dialogue is voice-acted well. It's a fun and enjoyable game.The bad: Some of the puzzles are pretty samey (go to 4 locations, hit the things, unlock the door). The story is a bit confusing but not bad, there's a bit of jargon that makes it difficult to follow. Some abilities come a bit late. Consumable healing items means if you heal a lot you end up having to farm a bit by hitting boxes a lot (until later when you have more currency to buy items). Most of the early weapons are strength-based and my build was DEX so I didn't really get to try out most of the weapons. The guns are only OK but are easily outclassed by spells.There's a particular boss in a cold region that was way tankier than he should have been, but that was partly my fault as I missed an entire section I could have gone to earlier to upgrade my weapons further.There were a couple glitches but nothing gamebreaking. I wish that upon death that the Nycrux dropped would be set a bit further from where you died. There is a point of no-return in terms of completing quest-lines that the game hints at but should probably come with a pop-up warning. Lastly, there's some items you get that are required to get the "good" ending but you have no way of knowing they're important. It was a bit frustrating to get near the end just to learn I had to find all these items but had trouble identifying where I had already gotten some. Had I known they were important, I would have left markers down on the map.None of these are deal-breakers, the game is still great. I ended up looking up some item locations near the end just for completion-sake. I know I said a lot more negatives but they're more nit-picky than anything.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a game I wish I could like more than I have. It has some of the strengths of the properties it is influenced by (namely Bloodborne and Castlevania) but it also falls into their possible weaknesses. Like Bloodborne, it tries to provide background history and story fragmentally and obscurely. However, I just didn't feel like it all came together coherently. I got the gist of things, but the prose for the majority of the game's writing felt obtuse to the point of parody to me. I appreciated the gothic setting but I wish it wasn't the entirety of the game. And keeping the same color palette for most of the maps made a majority of the game feel monotonous.  The 2-3 maps where they do change it up was very refreshing. From the Castlevania side, my biggest gripe was a lack of a speed-boosting ability. The entire map of the game is impressively large but it's such a slog to have to backtrack through at your regular pace. That being said, there are a fair amount of things I did like. The sprite work is pretty damn great. The music is good. I appreciate that it had voice work for all the characters. The setting and lore has a good foundation, even if I didn't feel that it wrapped up effectively.  Bosses are a bit of a toss up. I liked them mechanically (besides the story's final secret one), but I wish there weren't so many "large bat-like thing" bosses. There are at least one or two that definitely did impress me. Overall, it's a 5-6/10 for me - average to just above average. Not bad. It is a fairly good game that gets brought down by several issues. That being said, I am interested to see what Kumi Souls Games produces next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Beware of the negative reviews before Dec 7 2023, there was a massive update that fixes a lot of the issues that most negative reviews have left. I just recently started the game. You can rebind controls on keyboard but not on controller yet. Healing items don't restock unfortunately. All weapons got balanced so it's not just only greatsword. I'll edit this review once I complete the game but just be aware of the negative reviews.Update: really wanted to give this game a try but pretty much got stuck in an area of the game where it is almost impossible to go further without taking damage. I ran out of healing items and refuse to farm souls (I do this with all souls games). I can't run past the enemies because of these giant ice stalagmites that will damage you upon contact and there's hundreds of them. So since I can't run past it that leaves me to fight my way through which is fine if it wasn't for the sheer amount of enemies in the path and being surrounded by said ice stalagmites which leaves me with little to no room to fight these enemies in; the floor is ice so if I dodge I'll be sent to the nearest icicle. So that means I parry right? No, cuz these enemies will sometimes whiff the 1st swing on purpose so you use up your parry meter and get punished. So it's pretty much rng if you get hit or not, and this is where I don't even have a chance because I have no healing items (because it's a consumable and I used them all up trying to get further!!).Honestly this would all be fine if you could get back your healing items when you go to the equivalent of a bonfire. Making healing items a consumable in a souls game where you WILL be taking damage to learn about bosses and the map is stupid. So if I want to learn a boss I have to start burning through my inventory just to survive long enough to see phase 2. And if I run out of pots I'm being punished for trying to see more of the fight? So all that leaves you with is farming enemies for souls to buy more pots. It's such a stupid decision on the Dev to do this.Really wanted to complete the game because it's interesting but that single part was so incredibly infuriating I actually stopped playing it, and I love souls games. It's like trying to get through blighttown in DS1 blind and trying to get to Quelaag at the bottom without taking 3 hits or being poisoned with no way to heal.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no mixed review option here so I'll just give my quick cautionary review:I enjoyed this game quite a bit on the PS5 (and beat it). In many ways it scratched the Blasphemous itch that Blasphemous 2 didn't quite manage to do for me as that sequel leaned more into Metroidvania tropes and away from the Soulslike vibes of the original. The Last Faith weirdly delivers on that front.That said, I excitedly bought it for Steam Deck, hoping to take it on the go (and seeing that it was "Verified") and it repeatedly crashed early on in the game. That was enough to scare me into asking for a refund.In short, the game is good, but if you're a Steam Deck owner, buyer beware.

_childDocuments_.review: No video options... So, if you play this on a 4k tv you'll have a blurry mess not at all like the videos you see online or here...The devs have said that they will add video options months ago, but still nothing. I'll change my review when they actually do it.I was so looking forward to this, but I refuse to play it in this state. Fix it please![Edit] I ended up playing it using reshade, with Lumasharpen and Vibrance. I set the first two sliders of Lumasharpen to the max but, of course, it's a matter of preference. Vibrance adds a bit of color to the world, which can be very bland. With these two options, the game was beautiful.The game itself is fun, despite some clear issues. It lacks responsiveness. For example, there is a delay when you dodge before you can dodge again, for no reason. There is also a delay between pressing the button to use an item and the animation. Sometimes it doesn't work at all. You can adapt, but it sucks during boss fights.I tried different builds, but in the end the strenght build is by far the best. You just can't do as much damage with the others. It sucks because many weapons are really cool.In short, it's an okay game which could have been great if the devs had really thought everything through.

_childDocuments_.review: Decently fun metroidvania with some souls-like mechanics. Standard ones being drop your currency on death, committal attacks, ressing enemies with bonfires and similar itemisation to a souls-like (so scaling with stats E > S, level up specific stats etc). Though it plays more like castlevania SoTN just less powerful, you don't ever get as quick as Alucard.There are a few minor knocks to the game but nothing to stop you playing, some bugs here and there that might be annoying. Also until you get used to it, the slow turn of your character might occasionally send your attacks the wrong way.One rather annoying thing for me is the iframes from getting hit are basically non-existent, so certain attacks from enemies can end up one-shotting you from near max hp (even with good vitality). Feels kind of bad that you dodge all a boss's attacks and mistime one dodge for a particular attack in a bad way and then die. Also banshees being able to stun you and instant-gib you for the same reason. They are easy to avoid but making a minor mistake causing a very quick death feels bad. There is a point of no return for quests and it is when someone tells you the enemy you have been chasing (last boss) is in the next room. It doesn't signpost it very well but turn around if you still have quests you want to do as you won't be able to do them later.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a beta test. Looks great and sounds great, but is poorly balanced, tedious, and full of little annoyances that just wear your down over time.Maybe if the devs keep working on the game it'll be genuinely worth playing. It is definitely fixable though and I believe it could be a top-tier game if various issues are addressed. If they aren't... then it's skippable or wait for a sale, in my opinion.Main pain points:-Dropped inputs, possibly because of no input buffer? That said I'm pretty sure there is an input buffer so I don't know what is causing it.-Exploration is absolutely tedious with the slow movement speed / no movement upgrades. While I do like the limited checkpoints for running through levels (gives lots of tension and weight to exploration) I don't like how hard it is to revisit areas. A homeword bone type item would alleviate many of these complaints.-Huge difficulty spikes. Edwyn, the Burned Apostate and the final boss feel overtuned in bad ways. The final boss' invincibility shield that it keeps casting is really irritating to deal with.-Enemies suffer sporadic hitstun: seems like first hit, and 3rd hit or 4th hit. As if they get hit and need to reset their animation to get hitstun again or there's some invisible poise. Either way, given how spongey enemies it feels bad.-Jump attacks feel awful. Attacking while jumping stops your vertical momentum immediately and is just really at odds with certain enemy design.-Upgrade prices are arguably too high.-Slow startup on weapons.-Some lingering hitboxes and some questionable hitboxes.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'd like to preface this by telling you I am one of the voice actors in the game, and I was the official audio mixer for NPC dialogue, so I may be a little biased. :')Although I've only got about 2 hours of gameplay in myself, I've played the demo and combed through silent playthroughs on YouTube, and I've seen enough to know, that this game is amazing!Sure, there are a couple of clunky and annoying mechanics, but in the grand scheme of things, it doesn't matter. Overall, I've absolutely loved this game! The spells are awesome, the boss and NPC designs are fantastic! Also, CUTSCENES, I love cutscenes! _childDocuments_.review: I genuinely enjoyed it until I began noticing some "Quirks".-> Let's start with some positives; I bought this game for a reason and I fell in love with the teaser trailer,- adding it to my Wishlist immediately. This game's music, atmosphere, and overall first impressions do it justice from a presentation perspective and can draw you in while we all cope with waiting for the Silksong release or Bloodborne on PC.The artists and composers of this game should pat themselves on the back. I love the weapons, the enemy designs, and the environmental aesthetic of the areas I find myself in but...we need to address the elephant in the room.-> I am so mixed on this game. I cannot recommend this game coming from a guy who loves Metroidvanias, because the fundamental design philosophy (YEAH I'M GOING THERE) is that those games ENCOURAGE exploration. If I got lost in Hollow Knight or Blasphemous, the enemies wouldn't be 3 times harder to kill for the sake of being harder. If you get lost in the last faith, you'll find yourself with enemies that deal triple damage, have triple the health, and are the same enemies you encountered in earlier areas but now significantly harder to kill.This game's philosophy is so dependent on telling the player "This area is too strong come back later" that even if you grind for an HOUR and come back it'll still feel like you do no damage. There's no sense of growth, there's no feeling of progression at times. I had to constantly worry about potentially entering fog walls that lock me in with wave after wave of enemies that are 3x beefier than the same enemies I just fought 2 feet away. I died from curiosity in an early game area and I couldn't get my Nycrux back! Why Punish the player for exploring IN A METROIDVANIA????You never know which area you're supposed to be in or if you're ready for because It feels like no matter how much you grind, there's no distinction of what area is supposed to be explored yet or not. Typically, if you find the McGuffin needed to unlock a new area, it's common to think you should revisit that roadblock. "Oh okay I found the ring that lets me move these heavy cubes! I remember seeing one outside the manor, so I should head their next!" Except no, you don't deal any damage to the enemies you encounter and they kill you easily in a couple hits. People underestimate the purpose of the pistol in Bloodborne. The pistol was never intended to deal heavy damage, it's purpose was to parry and create opportunities to heal or close gaps for otherwise aggressive enemies. The pistol in this game is intended to shoot straight away and deal next to nothing compared to your other tools. I bring this up because It was when I had collected so many demioxide bullets that I thought to myself, "Why should I keep using my gun? It leaves me vulnerable. it doesn't parry. it deals little damage. It can't hit enemies under 2 ft. why bother?" This is evident because I chose the MARKSMAN class in the beginningAnd that's what I genuinely believe this game is telling me: "Why bother playing a particular style? Why bother exploring and being encouraged to discover secrets if you'll be punished for it? Why bother grinding for hours to fight bullet sponge enemies that aren't worth your time? Why bother playing a game that wants to be several different things and can't commit to any one of them?"

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Faith is a straightforward metroidvania drawing heavy inspiration from other titles like Bloodborne and Blasphemous. It's a very fun and satisfying game to play at times, but without doing anything particularly innovative. This isn't a bad thing at all though; if you're looking for a solid 8-8.5/10 soulslike-metroidvania to sink your teeth into for a few dozen hours, then definitely check TLF out - it's likely to hit the spot for you!To get more into detail, I'll address four points. I want to first disclose that I followed some guides throughout my playthrough in order to 100% the game in one go, so my playtime would've likely been a lot longer if I had played fully blind. It's also been a couple of months since I played TLF, so I am sorry if some of my points are redundant now, thanks to updates. I've played a lot of soulslikes, and recently a lot of metroidvanias, both on here and on Switch/PS5, so I think I have a decent grasp of the important factors to consider when judging this game, so, let's get into it.First - is TLF a soulslike? I would say it definitely is. It has health and consumables a-la Bloodborne, rather than an estus equivalent item that resets on death/checkpoints, and it doesn't feature a stamina bar, but in almost every other way this game is a soulslike. Combat that requires you to learn enemy patterns and timing, you drop currency on death which can be recovered, 'bonfire' equivalents that reset the world/enemy spawns when you die/rest, an overly obtuse story and lore descriptions, and stats/levelling like a From Soft title. I actually quite like the term 'soulsvania' to describe games such as this or Death's Gambit, for example, although I am aware it adds even more (probably unnecessary) complication to genre definitions.Second - the difficulty: TLF is decently hard, but not overly difficult. I actually died more to falling off the map than anything else probably, aside from one boss that I struggled with. On that note - a lot of the bosses were too easy, with a couple of them vastly more overtuned than the rest. The general combat while exploring the world was a lot of fun and the difficulty felt right, though. Something important in TLF is a key item called Sepolcro, which you gain from some bosses, that buffs your HP/MP/power permanently. After acquiring a few of these, the difficulty felt like it dropped off a lot. Overall, I found the game a bit easier than the From Software titles, and similar in difficulty to some other metroidvanias like Death's Gambit, Symphony of the Night, and Bloodstained: Rotn. One more thing to note here was the traversal - dash, double jumps and grapples were satisfying and fun to use, but there were occasional jumps that were really annoying to make, even with the ability upgrades.Third - the map: I think the map could use a little bit of improvement, as it's one of the most important aspects of a metroidvania to me. It doesn't fill out cleanly and clearly as you explore, which really bugged me, as filling out the map always feel like one aspect of progression in metroidvanias. It's often not clear when you're missing a room or section of the map and whether you can actually explore it, or if you will just fall out of bounds to your death (this was the number one cause of death for me)!Fourth - the exploration to reward ratio: I think this could use the most improvement, though I am not sure how the dev could do this without adding something like an armour system, or more weapons/spells. The vast majority of the time, items you loot while exploring are bullets/heals/consumable weapon buffs, which aren't super useful nor exciting to loot in the quantity that you find them. You will occasionally find a new weapon or spell, or find a switch/item that goes toward opening another area or boss room. Just accept that the majority of the loot you discover is going to be filler. I think the dev could also benefit the game by just reducing the amount of loot pickups there are in order to make them feel a little bit more impactful. I used buff/cure consumables regularly throughout the game but still had plenty spare at the finale.To sum it up, I really enjoyed The Last Faith, and I think it ticks all the boxes pretty well when it comes to both metroidvania and soulslike design elements. In saying that, it has a few minor issues, and it's very conventional, without any innovation, so do be aware that it is not a groundbreaking game in anyway. Again, I want to say that isn't an inherently bad thing, as it does deliver a very solid and fun experience, and it did not detract from my enjoyment of the game. I also absolutely love the aesthetic and think it's one of the games' best aspects!

_childDocuments_.review: This Bloodborne port is weird but I'm not complaining.Honestly, it's nice to see a game whose devs you can tell legitimately understand what makes Bloodborne such a good game and have such an amazing atmosphere. I love how the villagers in this mumble to themselves in the same way Yharnamites do and actually sound like they ripped the sound files straight from FromSoftware.But yeah, many devs who are "inspired" by Bloodborne totally miss the mark in this regard despite many shamelessly ripping off 90% of the mechanics too *cough cough* Lies of P garbo *cough cough*Only gripes so far is some of the dialogue writing and voice acting. I do not like our level up lady and feel she could've been cast better or maybe it's the game's effort to sound VERY Victorian yet still missing the mark. It sounds kind of like a neckbeard complete with 'mladys'. It honestly has me laughing more than anything which isn't good.Bloodborne didn't really do that and most spoke much more naturally. I also dislike the voiced protagonist. We have some dialogue choices so that should've been enough. It takes me completely out of the game when I hear my dude say something I never would.Some of the voice acting is decent but again the script and direction is a bit off and tries too hard. They should've leaned more into a natural script while directing the Npcs to sound more "dreamy or uncanny".Combat feels good so far and I do agree the different classes should've started with class appropriate weapons especially when you find the basic starting weapons very soon anyway.The little lore bits on item descriptions are perfect! As is the art direction. I love the animations for the back step and roll, very Bloodborne. I also love that there's a back step attack unique animation.I'm very new to these types of games but I made it to the 3rd boss in blasphemous and didn't die HALF as much as I did to the TUTORIAL boss in this game. Idk if it's just me but to go from zombie hollows to that dude who literally has a phase 2 is a bit much for a literal tutorial. Seriously took me like 20 tries because you have to jump all his attacks and can't roll. Idk felt kinda bad to start off that way but maybe I just suck.All in all so far so good. I'm sure the devs will address things like input rebinding. That is a bit ridiculous that it wasn't included in release.

Bosses are challenging but not cheap. A hard to put down game. "Just one more screen" because you learn that something awesome could be around every corner. _childDocuments_.review: * 30 Hours - PC w/ 8BitDo Pro 2 Controller* 10 Hours - Steam Deck (Fall 2022 Model)* Game Completion: 100%* Achievements: 100%Quick and Dirty Verdict: The Last Faith is an excellent game in the same vein as Salt and Sanctuary and Blasphemous, however, it is held back from being a truly great title due to some baffling design choices. I do believe this title is worth the asking price and I would absolutely love for Kumi Souls game to improve the game, create some outstanding DLC and even work on a sequel.Bugs: I incurred no game breaking bugs. All of my bugs were minor, such as the game freezing twice (Windows 11), falling through the map during tile transitions due to beast mode dodge and having to restart a couple of boss fights due to the same reason (beast mode dodge). I managed to get every achievement on the first attempt, but the final achievement did not activate. The devs are aware of these bugs.Pros- It's a 2D Bloodborne metroidvania- The dark gothic visual design is incredible- Some great boss battles (especially the secret ones)- Excellent map design with plenty of secrets- Great soundtrack and sound design (except Lady Helenya, she sounds like she was hired from the budget section of Fiverr)- Performs incredibly well, even with the Steam Deck tuned to an absurdly low TDP and GPU clock speedCons- Default control scheme is absolute garbage. You'll get used to it, but not having input customization in 2023 is a travesty.- While the soundtrack is great, I'm heavily biased towards Castlevania games as their background music can make even uninteresting environments fun to explore. SoTN had some absolute bangers, for reference: - The beast mode transformation feels half baked and boss fights really weren't designed for it. On top of that, the phase dodge you get can cause you to glitch out of boss arenas and fall through the map if you dodge into the tile border.- I'm spoiled with directional attacks from Blasphemous. There were a number of times where I said to myself  "I wish I could aim my attacks."

_childDocuments_.review: Bloodborne style frenetic, aggressive combat.  Metroidvania style exploration and secret hunting. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: A downright disappointment.Let's set aside the fact that this game is a Blasphemous (and not even of the first one) and Death's Gambit rip-off, this game is just a let down.Gameplay - The mechanics feel clunky and sticky. If you want to turn around, you won't be able to instantly do it, but instead go through a tiresome slow animation of walking backwards (not turned around yet) and then you'll finally turn around. This proved frustrating ESPECIALLY when trying to talk to NPCs, which requires you facing their faces. It also proved annoying during boss fights.Which leads me to boss fights - some of them are just pure chaos, with bosses not leaving you room to dodge because of atrocious telegraphs. One boss used abilities that are near impossible to dodge, making it more luck dependent than skill dependant which is the worst thing a game like this could have.The game also likes to repeat the so called puzzle that requires you running around until you find buttons to push in order to open gates. Seriously, I've stumbled upon it so many times.Graphics - The art design is somewhat ok, but insanely repetitive. You'd see that some rooms use elements from other room over and over again without end.Map - The map is big, but it is just FULL with empy rooms. Feels like the developers wanted to create the illusion of size without actually committing to it.VA - Might be me, but some of the recordings sound like they used a gaming mic from a 20$ headset.The acting itself is mundane.Overall, wait for a discount and even then it might still not be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Love the environment, art, music and animations. However I feel like there are some insane spikes in difficulty in some areas. I was able to fight the starlight beast WAY early for what health and weapons I had. I found a different path which was a swamp where mobs and their annoying ass spells killed me over and over and over. Not sure if there is another path but I am sick of backtracking looking for other paths since there is no guidance at all whatsoever. Loved it but I am done with the wasting time and frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Many things have been promised from the devs regarding this game but they abandoned it and went radio silence for almost a year (at the time of this review). The game is complete and is good, not going to deny that. The gothic theme of the game is well framed by the graphic and sound, some of the background musics do a very good job evoking a sense of nostalgia and "apathy" (everything is lost and nothing really matters) without actually sounding depressing. Gameplay is more than decent although a bit clunky at times. Clean inventory and a good number of weapons/spells and items. The problem is that many of the pieces you need to complete a build are found almost at end of the game when you cannot use them for long anyway and this game has NO NEW GAME + (one of the things promised by devs but never delivered)The game is fun and good. Why the negative review then? Because devs promised many things when the game was on kickstarterNew Game +Boss rushSurvival modeAnd more (extra npcs, bosses and few more things). Not a single one of those things has been delivered. NOT. A. SINGLE. ONE. Their twitter is dead and nobody has heard from them in over 9 months. Here's the ice on the cake, a tweet from 19 June 2020Almost 5 times the original goal and that's it. Buyers beware, this game is abandoned and you get it as is, do not expect updates or anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to all of the downvotes and hate towards this game. Yes, obviously there are some things I didn't enjoy and would like to see the developer update, however for the souls-like metroidvania this game was advertised as, it sure hit the mark. If you enjoyed other similar games in this category such as Blasphemous, GRIME, etc. then this game will surely scratch that same itch. Overall it's a solid 8/10, though a bit on the pricey side for what it offers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Fairth is beyond janky, I fell down an elevator shaft and was stuck at the bottom of the screen causing time loss from quitting out (no autosaving, only saves at shrines). It's clunky too, ledge grabs works when it wants to, pressing jump while attacking will occasionally input more attacks, parry is a coin toss etc. There's also enemy and boss copy pasting with health and damage values tuned to the area. To top it off, the story really isn't anything special, the voice acting under delivers, and the subs have misspellings or even completely different words. Sounds like a terrible game right? You wouldn't be more wrong. Despite all these flaws, there's some serious fun to be had, with a ton of content as well. However the pixel art is the star of the show, everything looks incredible, you can feel how much effort went into designing and creating this environment. Even the difficulty curve is acceptable, if the game becomes too hard, it's probably because you're in the wrong area. Even then, at level 42 with a +2 Skullcleaver, and enough patience, I was able to take down a few higher leveled bosses early for some cool weapons and spells.Anyway, if you liked Blasphemous and thought 2D Dark Souls was a blast, you'll find a lot to like with 2D Bloodborne, even if there is no rally on health loss.

_childDocuments_.review: Besides losing track of where to go sometimes, this is basically a Soulslike (Bloodborne heavily inspired) Metroidvania. No stamina bar is a plus, but there are some weird animation/input eating moments. I enjoyed every boss fight as it was mostly pattern memorization and I didn't ever feel like I was hit by a cheap shot if I was smart about it. The game is *generous* with recovery frames on evade too. The weapons you find are very Bloodborne "has a special action". I wish you could find some of the weapons a bit sooner or there was a NG+ mode like souls games to use the weapons in. I missed a boss completely, no idea where they are (the promotional hydra) so I got *an* ending but it wasnt the true one.There's lots of things to find, NPCs to find much like Bloodborne and they go back to the HUB to offer a service or quest. There's also more breakable walls in this game than Bloodborne if you're into breakable walls IE: Castlevania.I'd call this more of a Metroidvania that's harder than most of the "soulsbornevania" games I've played but I've not played a lot of good ones. I personally enjoyed this game. The environment art is fantastic and the music and SFX are straight up Bloodborne feeling. If you want that Bloodborne feel, this is that game. I can only hope that this inspires them to do another and do some refinements. It's a great first try. A little pricey but ultimately I got a decent chunk of time out of it and I've seen games be more expensive for less (Hello Kirby and most 1st party Nintendo games that never go on sale).

The game is tedious in its current state.Edit: Initially, the NPC that sells unlimited heal items bugged out and didn't go to the manor so I was always short of heals in boss fights. However, now that I was able to get her to appear at the manor the game seems a lot more enjoyable. I will update this review upon completion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the demo it feels like a pixelized, 2D bloodborne. Now it feels more like a fused bloodborne and blashphemous. The map is not big or complicated, and well designed such that one won't suffer from running through the same area repeatedly for one boss. The story is a little weak, but the game-play is quite interesting thanks to the diverse weapons. There are some bugs and things to tweak, bug I'd say it's definitely worth trying if you're a fan of soul-like games or the metroidvania genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Nice Metroidvania, nothing groundbreaking, but well executed. Visuals, Combat, exploration are all good. Its fun, not too hard and never really frustrating. You get the standard power ups like air dash, hook, double jump (this one very late in the game tough). You get a variety of weapons and spells, though I pretty much stuck with the same sword, once I realised how much more powerful I can make it when I upgrade it at the vendor. I like the dark fantasy setting, enemy variety, the different bioms. The music is a bit of a let down, as its just not very memorable and doesnt really add to the atmosphere. I feel like like this was a missed opportunity, as the game might have stood out more otherwise, with more atmosphere. It doesnt distract from the nice gameplay tough. All in all a very enjoyable experience, very recommended for Metroidvania lovers
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been amazing to play. Truly captures the nostalgic feel of a classic 80s and 90s metroidvania mixed with the modernism of a souls like difficulty. This game will both excite and mentally break you at the same time leaving you never short of both enjoyment and a sense of dread.There is so much for you to explore within this game from secret areas that will have you hitting every wall in sight, to re-tracing your footsteps through previous areas to unlock all of its hidden gems to aid you in your difficult and hard adventure ahead.The voice acting Is truly well chosen. Often I can play a game and the voice doesn't quite match the design of the character. However this is not the case in this game. The characters are plentiful for you to come across and complete side quests for. Each with their own unique personality that will further aid you in your immersive plot lines and sub quests.I highly recommend this game for fans of the souls and metroidvania genres. Especially if you were a fan of Castlevania Symphony of the Night which seems to have a lot of influence within The Last Faith.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: The game sure is pretty and sounds good. BUT....- No video settings whatsoever.- Can't rebind keys.- No windowed mode! You can force it into windowed mode with Alt + Enter but the window will stick to your monitors native resolution with no way to change it. You can't drag the window border and there are no resolution settings, so its pointless.Apparently there are several gameplay issues as well but I'm not gonna get into those since I only played the game for a couple of minutes.The technical issues however... it's 2023 (!!) A lot of people use ultra wide monitors or simply wish to stream the games they play. I have no patience for devs that release their games without bare basic QOL features like a proper windowed mode, resolution settings, and key rebinds. Their response to those complaints has been: "The team will add this post launch!" . The game has been out for about 2 weeks now and there has been zero communication from the devs. No patches. No nothing. A perfect example how to not release a game in 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Soooo...Last Faith is a VERY dark, gritty game in the (surprise, surprise!!!) Metroidvania  genre that is more or less Blasphemous's darker cousin.  For some reason, the jumping feels heavier than Blasphemous, but just as satisfying.  I'll cut straight to the chase - I like this game VERY much, but it doesn't seem as polished as Blasphemous.  If you like THAT game, this one will prolly be right up your alley.  Get it.  You're welcome!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good thing I waited to write this review, as originally it would have been a lot more negative. The patches, however, have ironed out pretty much all of the things I would complain about, and the end result is an absolutely excellent game. The combat is deep and rewarding, and I'm really impressed with how enemy staggers are handled. The weapons have great variety and (as of recent patches) are fairly well balanced.The only real negative is that guns are absolutely awful, to a genuinely surprising degree. You can't move and shoot, or jump and shoot, in spite of the fact that enemy npcs can. Like in bloodborne, you're limited to only 25 bullets, but unlike in bloodborne, you can't trade hp for more bullets. Finally, there are only five guns in the game, meaning your options are really limited. Magic, on the other hand, is fantastic, with a wide variety of spells available. You can get additional mp by upgrading your mind, and you can carry up to 30 mp restoring items, meaning if you want to, you can cast expensive spells nearly 100 times before running out. It begs the question, why did they even put guns in the game, when magic is better in every way?
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Controls have a bit of a lag, animations lock you into attacks (leaving you vulnerable to enemy attacks), there's no real set pathway, so you're kind of just fumbling around, and enemies are a little too OP in certain areas. It's no Blasphemous, but I'll take it. Interesting story, wonderful art. Overall I'm happy with my purchase, and the price point as well ($27.00).

_childDocuments_.review: I love it soooo much!! The detailed pixel art,gameplay variety, and the soundtracks are great; especially Esk's Palace Ost,Dr. Ridley Hermann ,Lord Laddak,Nyxaroth the Eldritch Wight, and Drowned crypt.There are five Attributes. In order, they are: Vitality, Strength, Dexterity, Mind, and Instinct.Each one has a crucial impact on your character's performance based on the build you're using.Can't describe how wonderful weaopns and spells are. The Bosses were designed with great care, and I was hoping we would see everything we saw in the first Kickstarter trailer.Hope The devs add it later in a dlc/update.It's one of the best Metroidvania I've ever played.I notice one bug in Yegor & Leena Boss but that didn't affect or ruin my whole experience.However,I though I had an issue in Woman in Ink quest for finding collictibles called (Unborn of the Midnight Aristocracy),but I was wrong and done it.The True Ending and stunned my heart that I have never forgotten these moments.I recommend you to play this impressive game. _childDocuments_.review: This would be a positive review, the early parts were pretty mediocre and the game really shined in the middle, but near the end of the game there's a point of no return with no indication or explanation. It blocks you from many items, achievements, and upgrades that brought my pretty enjoyable playthrough to a screeching halt. Finished the 2 normal endings real quick and grabbed the items to do the true ending but couldn't be bothered to do the first final boss fight again due to frustration that my file was pretty much trashed due to poor game design and lack of communication to the player.In summary, if you go into this game knowing ahead of time you'll probably have a good time. Can't bring myself to give a good review after ending on that kind of note though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has no right to be this good. It’s easily on par with Blasphemous and it’s basically Bloodborne but 2D Metroidvania. One thing I love about this game and what it does better than most is exploration. You can 100% this game without looking at a guide, as the paths are way less obscure than in any other games of the genre. The map just makes sense. Masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: (Edited review after beating game fully)The game is a nice mix of SoTN with a bit of Blasphemus.The early bosses are easy to handle after only a few tries each, all I've met having easily readable tells for when to jump, dodge or roll.  The later ones let you mix it up, using your new skills and movement abilities to avoid the damage.  The only downside I notice, is every boss has a "Resting Phase"  Does certain attacks for you to avoid, then pauses to let you get damage in.  A more dynamic design I feel would have made it less noticable.Unlike Blasphemous the games experience/souls have to be collected on death since lose all you have earned.  The parry mechanic is a bit awkward as you need to press 2 keys to activate it(RB+Y for me), and it's a really short window so have to know enemies quite well, but once you get it down, great source of healing so rarely have to use healing items.I'd say combat wise, it's a good game even with those small flaws.  I enjoy the weapon leveling system, but dislike the stat system since just a copy/paste of Dark Souls with spells and weapons requiring a minimum stat or they do poorly.  I also feel they should have not limited upgrade items so could explore different builds more easily, and allowed a respec of some kind.Over all, was worth backing on Kickstarter.  An enjoyable and engrossing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: If you are lore driven and want to immerse yourself in a Metroidvania Gothic style world, keep looking.This games atmosphere design has the potential of being a solid story-telling world that can be built upon but the developers need to focus on the lore aspect to make it great. There are several positives in this game that I want to mention:Maps/Game Design is goodMonster designs/mechanics are good with some annoying monsters(good in my opinion)Character design and movement is fluent (Wish there was a speed skill/item to make you walk faster!)Music is solid for the atmosphere.Weapons/Spells are okay.The game really sucks you into this world and I was prepared to be immersed after learning the dodge, parry and attack mechanics. However, as you continue through the storyline, it just makes you scratch your head, then it slowly begins to piss you off! I played the game twice (Completionist and other reasons) which left me even more pissed off! Here are some of the cons about this game:Executions – Most of the executions you can perform are mostly on the monsters in the early stages of the game. After that, you go through the entire mid/late game without seeing others. I wasn’t expecting GOW, but the trailers made it seem like you would be able to perform executions on most or all monsters. I wondered if they ran out of time or if this is it.Bosses – Most are mid-size or large size bosses that cover up half your screen with nothing unique about them. They only feel challenging cause they can take a huge chunk of your health or are health sponges if your character is low level.False Screenshot/Videos – Right off the bat, the VERY first screenshot you see is the main character about to battle a Hydra. That battle does not exist in that environment, but you will face them elsewhere. There were also screenshots of certain areas that are nowhere in the game (screenshot 1, 14, 20-24). Granted, I believe 20-24 atmosphere changed to look brighter and gloomier…I am trying to be nice here. Also, there were trailers of your character at one point transforming into a bear, then a wolf. Neither of those transformations happen and it makes sense why not.NPC’s – 99% are not flushed out and give vague dialogue. Most speak in riddles of places that you ‘might’ have been or may not with zero clues of what the hell they are talking about. A person commented to a post of mines that nails it perfectly, “There's some place somewhere that is very dark and secret/sacred. Not going to say what its name is or even what direction its in, just going to sort of tease its existence while indicating it is possibly important, maybe, for reasons. You probably won't even be able to tell if you've been there based on what I am saying now. Isn't my dialogue just BRIMMING with murky atmosphere?"Lore - ….The lore has some potential, but the vague NPC dialogue, along with crappy notes you find litter throughout the game doesn’t explain much at all. You can’t paint a better picture of how things are unfolding because you are not given enough information to connect the effin dots!Ending – ooooooh…my effin gawd! I am doing my best not to spoil things, but all three endings are not satisfying. Hell, I pick the bad ending just to end it all. Someone explain who the ♥♥♥♥ were Annabella and Caterina this entire time! Also, the backers list (not the one with the quotes) should have been in a separate credits at the start menu or something. I can’t imagine being a backer and searching for my username in that ungodly amount of text. Key Items – Ahh, so we are going with the CSOTN spectral goggles but instead its somebodies’ eyes…so how do I equip them to see through the ‘truth’? There are a bunch of slots left for your Stigma and charms but there are not that many. Why create so many slots if there were only 3-6 charms out of 16 blocks showing to make it insinuate that I am missing items and need to search around more. When I saw I was at 97% completed with the map, I realized that I wasn’t going to find more. Once again, maybe there were plans to have more but ran out of time.I do believe that the developers have made something good and will watch what they do in the future. If this doesn’t become abandonware, I would hope the developers could flush out the NPC’s and story because it will leave you all disappointed. Whether it’s an update or DLC, taking the criticism and improving that aspect would help the game and possibly change my rating. Adding more depth to the characters and story would make this an all-around solid game.  Hell, get with Kagura Games developers who made The Heart of Darkness and ask them for assistance in Storytelling and lore!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Faith

_childDocuments_.review: Pros :- its a hard game- excellent sound- excellent music- excellent character voices done by actors- excellent pixel graphics- excellent atmosphere- excellent enemy variety - very good explorationCons:- the rooms with multiple waves of enemies ( that you cannot leave until they are defeated ) are poorly balanced, with terrible choice/number of enemies making them annoying at some point ( after more than 30-40 tries, considering i killed some of the bosses 1st try ) - some parts of some zones ( like the ice one for example ) are poorly balanced, with terrible choice / number of enemies and traps / icicles on the ceiling, forcing you to replay the same sections multiple times, without the option to just ignore the enemies - map / directions are sometimes misleading and unclear with a lot of backtracking, because you dont remember where you should you use the new progression item you have found- item usage is really slow and locks you in place, which makes some of the throwables like bombs most of the time not worthy the risk of using them- i happened to pick an item that reduces shock damage and makes me immune to being electrified ( shock status effect ) long after i was in an area with a lot of shock damage / shock traps- it has the same problem as Blasphemous - at times the platforming is too much, too demanding and sometimes annoying as hell. Also - sometimes a great precision is required in order to grab a ledge, which can become annoying in certain situations- using the elevator should not be the same button as movement ( analog stick ) because often, while pressing a diagonal, instead of going forward the elevator is being used, which can happen multiple times one after another- some enemies are WAY to easy to cheese and WAY too weak, considering they are in the late game areas - some of the puzzles / secrets are too vague and hard to remember were both / all of the parts are, in order to complete them - some weapons have too similar / exactly the same movesets!!!!!- At some point i felt like i have missed something, i have not done something right, that it was my fault. I had to check a video on Youtube in order to find, that there was an item / ability that enhances traversing some of the platforming sections, despite that once i happened to traverse over a gap that it seems i was not supposed to, which made me believe it was my fault that i cannot jump over other similar gaps. The game misled me to places / did not indicate ( despite i searched many of the areas multiple times ) that i have to take an item/ability in order to enhance platforming sections traversal. Due to that i lost a lot of time checking the same areas over and over again. I do enjoy fighting the same enemies, because i learn how to fight better, but at some point it becomes annoying to constantly check the same old places you were before and doubt your own competence / abilities to play the game. !!!!!The game DID NOT save my progress in the Liturgical pass. Yesterday i was showing and commenting with my girlfriend the platforming sections in this zone, i have fought the boss multiple times without killing her, when i logged in today, the whole zone was not even explored. Really disappointing. - There was a bug with a bomb item used to destroy some walls - if certain weapons were equipped the wall could not be destroyed- I cannot deliver the last dry liver in order to pick all spells, since the NPC is gone, despite her lamp ( the way to communicate with the npc if its gone ) being thereAfter finishing the game :I really want to give the game 8.5-9 score but i cannot do it due to the mentioned bugs and annoyances. Still - i could not put the game down until i finished it. I loved every secret boss. I loved the difference is zones / biomes with all the different enemies. There were some great secrets. There are great bosses - visually ( as an art ) and mechanically. I wish i could learn more about some of the characters. I hope they really add new game + feature. Some of the weapons and the story ( at some points ) are too similar to Bloodborne, that s not something bad, but the way they changed some of those similar things does not deliver / work as it should / the best way possible / does not make the items ( for example ) viable or interesting enough to be used. When taking so much from an existing game/ book / story etc i believe that more effort should be put in other aspects of the game, since some of the basics are already there. I hope a DLC comes out soon or another similar game to this one. Some of the bosses could be a little harder. Overall i totally recommend this game to any Dark souls / Bloodborne / metroidvania fan. Just ignore some of the less polished aspects and You will have an incredible time with the atmosphere, music, sounds, graphics and enemies.Total score ( for now ) :7.5/10if some little bugs, annoyances and balancing is made / fixed - it could be an easy 9/10P.S. if the bugs are fixed and some other annoyances i will change the score to 8.5/9 out of 10

The wicked and the blessed will be judged the same - let nothing stand in your way.

Often brutal, always empowering, The Last Faith is an unholy alliance of metroidvania and soulslike.

Step into The Last Faith's ravaged world as Eric, who awakens with no recollection of his immediate past. Soon he will discover he is in a race against time as his mind and conscience begins to deteriorate. His desire for salvation from this affliction sets him on a cursed mission that crosses paths with ancient religions and divinities.

name: Sanity of Morris
detailed_description: 'Dad’s urgent message, these documents… They don’t match up. Start thinking John. Build a case, write it down' Unnatural events are taking place in small-town Greenlake. A bloodcurdling Psychological Horror Detective. Move around unseen, outmaneuvering your enemies. Search for hidden clues to find your father. Discover YOUR version of the truth. Could there be aliens in Greenlake? Gameplay Using your flashlight reveals the vital clues you need, but risks you being seen. The game combines elements of stealth games with detective-adventure and psychological horror for a gripping story. Story After years of next to no contact, Johnathan Morris arrives in the isolated town of Greenlake to check up on the mental state of his father. Nothing is as he expected it to be. There are deadly forces at work that don’t want John snooping around. Equipped with nothing more than a flashlight and a notebook, it is up to you to step into the shoes of Johnathan and tell fact from fiction.

_childDocuments_.review: , creator of such works as the discontinued  and  back in 2019 has been sighted once more with , a mystery-thriller with psychological horror elements! I first knew about it through Keymailer and was granted a key to the demo- which is basically level 1 or a third of the full game. Which I was thoroughly impressed by, because of its novelty and just something irregular in the horror genre besides the usual ghost busters or hide-and-go-seek game. I was further gob smacked by how much I ruminated on the “alien” plot and that it seems to revive a once crazy preoccupation about those extraterrestrial beings being the subject of many a tv show, films and conspiracy theories, to name a few. It wasn’t flawless by any means but there’s something intriguing about it- that made me believe in it~Johnathan Morris receives an incoherent rambling from his father, Hank telling, him to go to Greenlake. The former obliges because he sounds even more frantic than usual. Once there- a shadowy pursuer sideswipes his vehicle resulting in a crash. Then the chase ensues on foot as some third party wants him dead and the truth almost as elusive as the strange plants sprouting around there~The whole game has you finding and getting to Hank, who’s mysteriously untraceable after his message. To do so, you have to get in the mind of a paranoid individual a.k.a. codes and trails left by him! Really visualize your surroundings and embrace the dangers in order to progress! But even your own senses can’t be trusted… not always, especially when you’ve been spending too much time in the dark. Best part for me was going through the neatly organized journal inspecting collected notes, ravings and reports. Then making my own judgement and also giving eyerolls at every sentence uttered by the deluded Hank, he just makes it too easy!! Furthermore, creatures and agents will patrol the area with their color-changing lights to indicate their shifting wariness so don't get your signals mixed up! With three levels in total and about an hour+ each, SOM can take about 3-4 hours to finish. There’s not so much replayability as it is about double-checking for answers in case you missed out on crucial information!1) Best to get all collectibles in one go! They reset with each playthrough!2) No deadly consequences for depleting the sanity meter. Just messes with your vision~The visuals are in one word, majestic! As is a staple to the signifiers of aliens, there are countless lingering bright lights of various colors. Usually, they give me hope, something to head toward to… But here, I was always hesitant as some are emitted by the invaders, and others are just an everyday light- much like yours! Sound design is akin to how I assume obsessed alien fanatics would score it! Most of it are noises to make you lose your cool and others incur that deep, profound vibe of being “lost and floating around the galaxy” or “swimming amongst the stars”. I must also praise the voice cast for boasting enduringly entertaining performances with everyday joe tones to their performances~ The plot is a more serious version of  or any other sci-fi films that pose the big question of “are Aliens real”? But instead of focusing wholly on validating that claim, it takes a more self-aware approach. As a result, it can feel like they’re placed in the backseat but still it managed to rock my world by being so uniquely captivating in that regard!SCARY: 1st) The obsession with “Aliens” is an allegory for being so consumed with something that it becomes a hindrance to the things that truly matter in life; family, career and personal growth.2nd) The title already hints at a vital foreshadowing! Whose deteriorating mind will we be subjected to? Is the “sanity” meant to be ironic!? 3rd) From start to finish, everything will be open to interpretation. Sure, it gets a bit stale once you realize there will be no resolution- but I’m beginning to think that’s overrated. Instead, it presents to you a seemingly banal question but one that probably remains to be definitively proven anyway~All the mystery and alienating elements are short-lived by some wildly sporadic mechanics. For instance, with light where in frequent exposure to darkness or dimly lit areas will cause Johnathan to panic, hallucinate and his sight gets cloudy. But then in level 2- this doesn’t happen at all despite fulfilling these conditions. It then resumes in level 3… so I was just lost. Similarly, objects require the torch to be switched on in order to “see” and interact with them. Makes sense, but not so much when it’s in well-lit areas. Sometimes, they’re able to be fondled with in the dark and commented on perfectly! Even sound-wise, the “jumpscare” and creepy, lasting effects are noticeably absent in level 2. Then overdone in levels 1 and 3.The stealth- which I thought was absolutely responsive in lvl 1 turned out to be deceptive. But that’s because it becomes a long mission revolving around sneaking past enemies in lvl 2 that I noticed how clunky it could get… Reminds me of the  inconsistent radius of detection! When they should’ve spotted me, they didn’t! In lvl 3, it was almost broken where they can’t even see me right before their eyes; flashing them and teabagging behind the cubicle wall or past the glass walls.x Skipped a puzzle entirely in 1st level?x Checkpoints in 2nd level; spawning right next to the "things"... Also, their patrol routes glitched out. x Agents spotted me when they shouldn't and even knocked me right out through walls.x Chase / danger music playing when everything is fine.~ Missed opportunity to include the ability to jump! Plenty of highly uneven terrain means it's a fumble for balance... And ridiculously tiny obstacles can't be crossed over.~ Johnathan dies falling from really short distances.~ A lot of objects are pretty much recycled. Some are given the honor of being examined for a "jumpscare" but nonetheless serve no purpose. ~ Same goes for enemy variety…~ Started out as a throbbing mystery but ruined by uncertainty of ending. Nothing new~~ Typos; “Octobre” and etc!~ No level select feature!? SOM is conceptually sound & atmospherically inviting. Implanting doubt in players even after the credits. Trouble stems from its implementation, which is as shaky as the protagonists’ conviction~If you love to figure out the answers for yourself and follow a trail of breadcrumbs to the supposed truth. And question your declining condition, all while being mesmerized by soothingly distressing lights of many shades. Then SOM is for you~

_childDocuments_.review: Dark adventure game with lots of stealth and puzzle elements. It begins really strong, but gameplay gets steadily weaker about half-way. Watching a playthrough video of the mid-game will give you a better understanding. The lovecraftian storyline of "secrets man was not meant to know" and alien-camp is enough for me to give a thumbs-up, but your tastes may differ. In fact, according to the Steam Achievements, only 26% of owners finished the <6 hour game.This game has exploration-heavy gameplay with no combat, no inventory management, and no jumping puzzles. The voiceacting and storyline is very good, and I liked how collected hidden objects created a conspiracy-type timeline, with pictures and notations. I reservedly recommend this game at full price.I searched the tunnels of Greenlake with an Ubuntu Linux desktop computer and an xbox-type gamepad controller. I had trouble getting acceptable framerates, and I turned down graphic settings, such as the lighting effects. The game uses the Unity Game Engine, and it takes up 2,200 MBs of diskspace.

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts as a psychological horror with very simple item collection puzzles. Then it becomes focused around creating new paths by manipulating the environment, but still very simple. Finally it becomes a very weak stealth game. QTEs are thrown in occasionally, but they're so simple as to be almost unnecessary. The individual mechanics never really come together except in the most basic ways. The only connection is how little each of the mechanics are explored. There are multiple endings but it's just a choice from a menu to pick one at the end, it doesn't matter how you played. It's as if the developers got bored of making the game halfway through. Maybe they had to make sure a checklist of features had every box ticked off to make the publisher happy.The environments aren't particularly inspired, but they're fine for what it is. Human models and animations are particularly bad, but there's not too many of them.The protagonist's voiced internal monologues get annoying very quickly. It's not a matter of being realistic, of course somebody might tell themselves to "keep it together" and "they have to find a way out" when they're scared and lost. In a game it just breaks immersion. Either the experience is scary to the player or it isn't. I don't need the protagonist telling me how scared he is. If his ramblings were completely removed, it would actually make for the better experience.If the stealth sections in the last area of the game was replaced with environmental puzzles, the game wouldn't be perfect, but at least it would be something I could recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played the demo I was given a couple years ago, it seemed okay at the time and I was very interested in where the story was going. Fast forward to now where I saw it in my to review list and was like sure I finally play this one. I definitely wasn't disappointed by the story but I was by everything else, it had been two years and the game didn't even feel updated from the demo I played.Pros:+ Great voice acting+ Really interesting story that keeps you thinking by the end+ Kinda interesting puzzle mechanics + The paintings at the start of the game were creepy and really freaked me out for a bitCons:- Enemies were boring and very glitchy, some killed me through walls some spawned in walls- Every time I died I got spawned in front or behind an enemy, one time it happened 3 times and I died instantly until it decided it couldn't see me- The horror was good if it worked but it only worked once or twice, I got freaked out by a child on a staircase but most of the time I missed the jumpscare and only saw the poof of smoke afterward- The item jumpscares were really really bad, hald the time the jumpscare wasn't even facing me and it should be on every pickupable item in the game because it got boring quickly and I decide to stop picking things up- It takes a good 5 seconds of waiting before you actually pick up items- The cutscenes and quick time events were really wonky and were just weird in general- The flashlight had a tunnel vision to it which made the first area incredibly difficult to search through- you can only interact with things when your flashlight is on- The game doesn't pause properly so you need to make sure you are in a safe location and have your flashlight on while reading the journal Full Playthrough & Review: Steam Curator Page:
