_childDocuments_.review: Sanity of Morris is a story-driven stealth/flight like Sir you are being hunted game but with a story. John, your character arrives at his father's house Hank who had been researching alien presence. Forced into early retirement by his company Hank investigated alien presence and kept logs of his work for John to discover.  John learns that alien life had been spying on humans through plants since the 1970s. The game can be completed in around 4 hours. The game is all about flight, hiding and simple stealth. You can avoid dying by crouching and avoiding the creatures light source. You can also easily die by not following certain path or jumping from one level to another. The voice acting and story is very well done.Overall for the price the game deserves a 75% grade,If you are lost check out my full walkthrough on my youtube channel.or spoilers below
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: Sanity of Morris is an unchallenging, gentle horror with interesting environments to explore and a solid plot. It has a well-focussed story with a simple objective, straight-forward mechanics, and a good atmosphere. Will take approximately 4 unstressed hours to complete your first time around. Gameplay boils down to using your torch to clear obstacles, finding items to open doors/change your environment, and using stealth to avoid enemies as you search for your missing father in strange, alien locations while seeking the truth about the role of a mysterious government agency.
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I really, really wanted to post a positive review of this one because the preview footage that I saw before playing made Sanity of Morris like it could be a cool romp in the vein of a video game X-Files.  Aliens and UFOs are a topic that most exploration/stealth horror games won't touch with a ten foot pole and I'll certainly give SOM credit in the initial plot set-up for giving it a shot.  While the game isn't all bad, there's enough technical problems and 2nd half stumbles that prevent me from recommending it.  Like a similar lukewarm (for me) horror title that I badly wanted to enjoy earlier in the year by the name of Intruders; Hide and Seek, I just can't really push picking this one up for horror purists.Things get off to a well enough start.  Your dad sends you a nutty ass letter and on your way to visit him you get run off the road by G-men and hunted down like the dog you are in a race to find pop's house.  This initial chapter and set-up is pretty solid.  Things starts off after some stealthing and quick-timing your way through the woods and you're set to do some sleuthing to figure out the secrets hidden in your family home.  Mechanics here aren't perfect and there were a couple of FPS drops but I enjoyed figuring out the minor puzzles and uncovering plot points in the house.  You'll learn that focusing your flashlight discovers secrets and triggers events in a faux-Alan Wake manner as things go from bad to worse as you detect your way to the entrance of an alien hide-out.  Man do things go downhill from here.  (WARNING; THERE IS SOME MINOR DEGREE OF SPOILERS INCOMING, UNWITTING EYES SHOULD LOCK THEMSELVES INTO THEIR OWN PRIVATE AREA 51 OR HOWARD HUGHES TOWER).Lord almighty is that second area in the hideout a technical disaster zone full of stuttering FPS, hard to navigate tunnels and lots of stealth.  The stealth unravels big time in this place.  You'll also have to contend with avoiding falling to your death as well, while scouring for eyesore spots to use your flashlight for progression purposes (both in terms of ho-hum puzzles and figuring out WTF you're goin', champ).  It just felt miserable to accomplish these tasks with technical glitching up the wazoo on a graphically high-end computer.  I'd have refunded it but think I crossed the 2 hour mark and it almost became a personal vendetta to soldier on and see if things, hopefully, got better.  They didn't all the way till the game's end, if you'd like the climax of the exciting story I've told you thus far.  I fell through the map on solid ground at least twice and got more and more irritated that the stealth was completely random and I was getting seen through objects.  It just never gelled in the gameplay department.  I will say that had the hideout part been technically better executed, it would have been straight out of The Arrival when Charlie Sheen discovered the Mexican radio station he picked up on his comms dish was a literal alien stronghold.  SOM reminds me of that fun B-flick several times throughout but it just never has the design or gameplay to hold up its notions.  That's not to say, I had an odd attraction to a few parts.  I'm not a Unity expert and maybe they were assets but I liked the alien design and the general atmosphere of the environments.  It's not a great looking game yet its grimy, lo-fi thrills suit the story.  The sound and voice-acting is done competently enough as well, although I'll agree with what others said; that main character needs to stick a sock in it from time to time.  There are so many flashes of what SOM could be throughout that makes you yearn for what it isn't and aggravated by what it is.  For achievement hunters and completion nuts, it's pretty easy to 100 percent this if you're a self-loather like me that sometimes has to tear up on an irritating game from head to toe just to laugh about doing it later.  I know, I know, I recommended (lightly) Follia; Dear Father and Today is my Birthday but something about their 80s gore-movie cliches and fairly fast pacing made them entertaining to me (they also had some degree of minor combat and the feel of more authentic survival horror).  They also both miraculously ran better than old crotchety Morris and co. too.  As rough as this review remains, I do believe this developer has the beginning tools to do some cool work in the horror genre.  I'm into the idea, the overall plot, the set-up and the whole deal of getting almost accidentally lost in an alien compound.  It was even kinda neat that a light mechanic came into play on the puzzles.  But the technical snafus for a game that shouldn't challenge any PC past 2005 puts a huge damper on what coulda woulda shoulda been an interesting, atypical horror outing.  I paid full price of this 'cause....aliens, though I'm going to caution you to watch your wallet.  But I do think the developer's had a great idea here, so I'll hope they'll use my $15 to finance a much better game that I actually think is within their capabilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Sanity of Morris is an action game combined with puzzling parts and a horror vibe. Already in the start of the game questions come up where you want to find the answers for. While you are looking for answers you feel hunted and been watched all the time. A real thriller. The graphics are good. The guides throughout the game is very meaningful, helpfully and entertaining. With an easy to listen voice. The music and sound-effects makes the experience even more scaryI'm very excited to play the rest of the game to find out, what the hell is going on.
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: Sanity of Morris is a game involving conspiracy and deceit. It falls to the player to discover clues and leads as to what really happened in Greenlake and make their own case of the story. Gameplay switches between more point-and-click style puzzle solving and more sneaky adventurous gameplay. Here and there horror-like elements appear as well, keeping you on your toes as suspense and mystery builds up in the background.Figuring out what happened through in-world clues and collectibles is one of the most fun parts for me, learning about what went down and trying to puzzle it all together. Combined with some good twists the game will keep you surprised and thinking!A first playthrough might take you about 6 or so hours, but for the completionists under us it will take a bit longer as collectibles and snippets of information can be hidden quite well!
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect for a Halloween night!This is a neat little Indie-Horror title with elements of exploration and stealth. Divided in three parts Sanity of Morris can easily be finished within 3-4 hours, including collectibles. The game does a great job at level design and progression, it's not the greatest or most innovative game ever, but it has a good pacing, switches up the gameplay just the right amount so it doesn't get boring, but it's also not a very challenging game.Given the fact that it is about aliens, taking the story seriously is a little difficult sometimes, but I feel this is on purpose. The team clearly tried to make an homage to other titles that were the OGs of the genre. Similarities to F.E.A.R., Half life and Prey can be found everywhere and it just works as a nostalgic trip.If you're not expecting the best game ever, yet are in for a devent one-sitting horror-experience this is the game for you. And for 1.50$ on sale it's basically a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Sanity of Morris for a couple of hours now and this is what I think so far:- very good graphics  and ambiance- the story telling voice is very nice to listen to and guides you gently through the story- there is some freaky stuff happening, but I personally really like that- the animations of the enemies and the cut-scenes feel a little bit clumsy, but that kinda adds to the unique look and feel of this gameI'm excited to play the rest and I'm really curious how the story will end!
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so awesome! It has pretty much everything you can think of in a horror adventure game. It has puzzles, awesome chases, stealth, and pretty darn good graphics! The story was amazing, I was questioning everything since the beginning! Items that can be collected were pretty easy to find until the last area, where there were too many enemies bundled up together, but it's not that big of a deal! All in all for what you're paying, I do recommend this game for the price! I think I beat it all within around 4 hours of collecting it, reading the documents, and listening to the story! Now, something that is pretty noticeable is the A.I. Their vision is not the best, and when they chase you, you better hope you have a place to hide nearby because they are really fast and will catch you!!If you guys want, I made uploaded a part 1 of my full Sanity of Morris Playthrough! You can check it out here if interested :) : Thank you!!

_childDocuments_.review: Sanity of Morris is a short story driven psychological horror and puzzle game.Without spoiling too much: You a John Morris, after being called by your father, whom you have not heard of in years, you decide to visit him in his countryside home. Here you find something went horribly wrong with him and the nearby area GreenLake. You go off to explore what happened.The best part of the game is the psychological horror. You are constantly in the head of John, whom is thoroughly voice acted. You feel what he feels in everything you do, as well as feel his state of sanity.May not be too long, but for the price definitely worth a play for lovers of the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: Sanity of Morris tells a powerful, well thought-out narrative with psychological horror flavor. You play as John Morris, who finds his father missing after the latter made a shocking discovery. Expect tense moments of stealth gameplay, intuitive puzzles and an intriguing mystery to wrap your head around. The music and setting keep you on edge and clues about the story push you forward as you piece together the mystery behind the Sanity of Morris.
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: Sanity of Morris is the opposite of Alterego Games' previous game. However, they created a small game by the name of Bloodstreet 13. They know how to create the suspense required in a horror game. The game Sanity of Morris has its up and downs, Alterego Games however did not lose sight of their greatest strength namely, their story telling. So, do you believe everything to be true, or is it all just an illusion? Or perhaps a figment of your mind? Go and find out, perhaps you can uncover the mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: Good story. However, the enemies killed you so often because you frequently spawned when they were on top of you. Also, the lack of lighting was supposed to add to the suspense, but all it did was make it difficult to play the game as you could not see hardly anything. And if you turned on your flashlight to see better, you were killed by an enemy within seconds. The frequent autosaves did help, but by the end, I just wanted the game to end. Would recommend when on sale and only for dedicated players.

_childDocuments_.review: A recommendation with caveats.  Only on a deep discount I think is this worth it. I wouldn't be surprised if you told me this started life as a phone game.  For starters it looks absolutely horrid.  Models, lighting, environments, everything.  It's very janky.  And pasted across this is this awful fog effects that swarms your vision whenever you're in the dark. And there's plenty of other jank as well.  For starters you can't pick up or activate some things unless you have your torch up.  And it's only some things.  If it was everything it would be manageable.  But I found myself abandoning many collectibles which help add meat to the story as I just thought they were set dressing when in actuality, I needed to have the camera on them.  And having to have your torch up all the time does not gel well with all the stealth sections.And there's other jank too.  If you get spotted by someone and you're trying to run away, sometimes some interactibles bug out e.g. certain doors, meaning instant death.  Which makes the awkward stealth sections all the more annoying.Now to be fair to it, the story is actually pretty decent, the voice acting is fine, and it kept me just engaged enough that I wanted to see it through.  And 3 hours to pretty much 100% it (as far as I can tell), even if it isn't a completely smooth ride, means it doesn't overstay it's welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Sanity of Morris

_childDocuments_.review: Part of me thinks this would have made a better slow burn mystery game than what it wound up actually being. I enjoyed exploring the house, looking for "clues" that were left behind. The "afraid of the dark" element was rather dumb, as were the hallucinations when you'd pick up objects, but I still liked the first area. Then the game decided to be a stealth/horror game instead and wound up just kinda blah. It immediately throws out the mystery elements for hiding from enemies and basically everything after the first zone felt like a chore. To be fair to others, I tend to be overly critical of horror games, so you may still enjoy it. I just wound up feeling disappointed.

detailed_description: Special Edition The Special Edition includes: DRAGON BALL: THE BREAKERS (full game) Special Edition content Features a set of cosmetic items that will make your Survivor stand out on the battlefield! Show off your style with a complete outfit, celebrate your wins with a victory pose, and escape with character using a fun vehicle skin! Customizable Costume items: Souvenir Jacket (Midnight Black), Skinny Jeans (Black), Slip-On Shoes (Gray), Casual Watch (Black) Victory Pose 'Two Handed-Good' Vehicle Skin 'Dragon (Yellow)' About the Game Season 6 is live! - New Raider Baby from DRAGON BALL GT appears! Baby can infect civilians and survivors! When a survivor is infected, one active skill can be sealed at random! Under certain circumstances, Survivors can be used as servants! Carry out the Plan to Turn the Entire Universe into Tuffles while hunting down the Survivors! - New Survivor Skins Bulla (GT) from DRAGON BALL GT appears along with Launch (Blue Hair) and Launch (Blonde) from DRAGON BALL! Use each character's unique skills to escape from the Raider! - New Gimmick When fighting Baby, the special item Ultra Divine Water appears! Using the Ultra Divine Water from supplies, you can use sealed active skills by Baby's infection once again! *Raiders and Survivor Skins added each season need to be unlocked in-game. ____________________ Strategy Defines Survival 1 powerful enemy vs. 7 ordinary citizens! Experience the overwhelming difference in strength that only Dragon Ball can offer! DRAGON BALL: THE BREAKERS is an online asymmetrical action game where a team of 7 ordinary citizens try to survive the Raider (a classic DRAGON BALL rival such as Cell, Frieza, and Buu), who will hunt and evolve into an unstoppable force! • SURVIVOR - Escape from the trapped temporal seam Cooperate with others and use various means to fight off the Raider and escape from the field! - Survive using a variety of power-ups and items! Make full use of the familiar Dragon Ball items and skills, such as Dragon Raider, Solar Flare, and Instant Transmission! Sometimes you can even borrow the power of a Super Warrior to temporarily transform and fight the Raider. Collect 7 Dragon Balls and call up Shenron to power up! You may be able to defeat the Raider...? Find your own combination from a wide variety of items and skills! • RAIDER - Don't let the Survivors get away! Prevent 7 Survivors from escaping the field by using overwhelming powers unique to Dragon Ball! Aim for total victory by annihilating all Survivors! - Evolution makes them even more vicious! Raiders keep evolving and becoming more and more powerful! Aggressively attack Civilians and Survivors to absorb energy. As they evolve, their Super Attacks and skills also become more powerful! The final form can unleash super-powerful Super Attacks! • CUSTOMIZATION - Each Survivor and Raider has their own customization elements such as skills and skins! Enjoy your own customization! *Internet connection required. *This product is a multiplayer game that is played mainly through online matches between players. The only modes that allow single play are Episodes, which will be the tutorial, and the Practice Mode, which allows players to practice the game. *Online matches allow you to play against players from all over the world. You will match with people whose network conditions are optimal for the region you play in.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I love it when people are so quick to shout "Pay to win!" even if a game isn't.Having played the alpha, and all the betas, I can fairly say that the things you CAN buy are at worst pay to progress- However, even this progression is pretty much all side-grades.I'm not going to put a penny into gacha pulls and I'm confident I'll be just fine for it.If you're a Dragon Ball fan and/or a fan of asymmetric PvP games (Think Dead by Daylight, but it plays very different) I'd recommend picking this up.I don't even like DbD that much but I enjoy this a lot.---------------I'll get the only two issues I do have out of the way- It's very difficult for a Raider against a well coordinated team of Civilians. With a bit of luck and mostly strategy, they can kill the Raider fairly easily if it isn't a skilled Raider.Whether you get a flawless victory or a partial victory on either side, your XP compensation won't suffer much. Match length and playing objectives are the biggest factors there.And then there's the queuing system. You can choose to queue for either Civilian or Raider.However, it works on a 'priority' system. Each time you queue for a role and don't get the desired role, your priority goes up by 1. I assume this is stacked against every other player's priority in queue at the time.Obviously, in a 7v1 game, there's going to be many more people ending up as Civilians that queue as Raiders. Thus, your chances of actually getting Raider if you queue for it are pretty slim unless you already have a few priority points.I played for about 3 hours and got 3 games as Raider... Queuing for Raider the entire time.I think I'd rather have longer queue times than be forced to play Civilian even if I don't want to.As a neutral point, however I still feel it belongs in this section-It can be a bit difficult to get a grasp of how exactly to play.There's a tutorial, and there's a guide NPC in the base area that has entries for pretty much all the facets of the game- but nothing really fills you in on the small details that affect how it actually plays moment by moment.Examples being how to best fight, (on either side,) how to fight back against a gank as a Raider, or how to successfully escape the Raider as a Civilian.---------------I mentioned a Gacha system in the TL;DR... Yes, this game has a gacha. Yes, you can whale premium currency and buy many pulls if you want.However, at worst the things you get are the same things you could earn for free with a bit of effort.And no, the grind isn't anywhere near as bad as some other games you may be familiar with.After all, this is a paid game... Thus, it doesn't have the same sort of predatory pay to win practices free to play games tend to.---------------Yes, there is a battle pass. Yes, you can buy levels on it if you want.But, there's no premium track. Whales or Free players are all on the same reward track.Progress on this battle pass is also a fairly steady pace too.Each day you can earn up to 10 points (At my current level, that's 1.66 BP levels) simply by playing the game. There's also the typical daily/weekly challenges- Most of which you can achieve just by playing the game however you were anyways.This pass is going to last 3 months, and we can assume the same for future ones. The max level is 50.Assuming you just played the game for a good sitting even every other day, you should have no issue maxing it out in that time. You could clear it in considerably less time if you were to make sure you completed each challenge as well.

_childDocuments_.review: While the gacha system walls out ways of playing the game that everyone should have access to, I will say I couldn't care less.I'm a gambling addict, getting to gacha every other day feels good for my monkey brain.I want to talk about the core gameplay, which is very good!As a survivor, your job is to power up the main time machine and run around to get away from the killer. Raider. Villain. Whatever you want to call them.You are given many ways of doing this, such as running away using abilities or using various items that you find around the map to help you and your allies.As a raider, your job is killing as many people as possible and destroying the planet.Every raider grows in stages. Depending on your stage effectively says whether or not the survivors can fight back against you. If your number is the same or lower than theirs, they can fight you. If you're higher, they literally cannot use basic attacks against you.My main issue with this game is that playing survivor doesn't feel good a lot of the time.Every action you do is slow, other than the vehicles which lock you out of every action in the game except running and jumping.Using an ability has a charge up and they barely help escaping the raider. The raider has projectiles that lock onto you no matter what and can knock you down in a matter of seconds, not to mention each one has various abilities to help find or knock you down anyway.When fighting back, you don't have a lot of time to do it and you're also not given the tools to properly fight either.It makes it incredibly hard to live longer than two minutes if you're the first person to go down.It also does not help that getting finished off once at any point of the game means your next down is an instant death.You are at the mercy of your teammates to end the very quick animation of you dying, suggesting that they even have the ability to help you.I want to suggest this game so badly because what we have is great and it'll take a bit more work to make it incredible, so I will, but currently the game feels unfair no matter the situation.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I like this game and will probably play it past the 3 month long season 1... I gotta say no for someone who is looking for a longer term experience.TLDR: Genuinely fun if you can appreciate that asymmetrical games, to this degree (1 v 7), will never be traditionally balanced nor competitive. Also you are probably paying early-access for a game that is designed to be a gacha F2P and somewhat P2W game. I assume it will be F2P in a year.---I genuinely enjoy this game as a fun arcade experience with randos. Even if I lose on the survivor team, it's fun to play as my OC and see if we can evade/objective-own/beat-up Freezer. Even if I lose as Cell, it feels real good to be drastically more powerful and put at least a few survivors out of the game.This game will never be "balanced" because it assumes survivors only communicate through emote stamps. It also will never be competitive unless some glorious third-party programmer creates a lobby browser with some voice chat integration using discord/mumble/ventrillo/microsoft teams.However, I assume it will be F2P in a year, because of it's biggest flaw.You play gacha for characters, moves, and costumes. You can purchase currency to do more gacha. When you get duplicate gacha sets, you get points to power up skills and moves. If you are a gacha addict, you'll have plenty of points to upgrade your skills. I don't know yet if there's a cap on these things (allowing comments for corrections).Might as well make it F2P because smaller paid games like these tend to not have a great population after year and that would discourage making purchases from the currency store.Still, it's a short time sink per individual game and it's a fun small arcade experience. I'll pay $20 for that for a game I assume will last for half a year assuming a second round of updates over 6 months.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start off by saying, I don't recommend anyone to buy this game, even on sale, this game just isn't worth any money no matter how low it drops in value.Here are some other reason why the game isn't worth playing.1. This game is heavily plagued by its gacha system to the point that you can't even compete against people who've dumped even like $10-50 on the gacha system, the complete lack of abilities leaves you defenseless in most any match you'll play, and your only real hope is the Raider isn't good, or is just going to let you escape.2. The current balance of the game is incredibly toxic, and downright impossible to play if you want to actually win as a survivor. The Raiders are so insanely overpowered right now you can get ki blast spammed from 100 meters away until you go down, and it doesn't take skill to do as there's no drawbacks whatsoever to spamming ki blast over and over and over until the survivor is down. Even in the event that say you use a grapple hook, or do get away on Bulma's bike the Raider can just easily catch up with you if they really want to kill you, and there's only one way out at this point which is your transphere, leading into my next reason.3. Transpheres in this game are such an incredibly cool and fun mechanic, where you and your friends who are weak and defenseless are actually given a real chance as a team to defeat the Raider, and win. If nothing else Tran spheres are meant to give you a real chance to fight off the killer and escape, but that's not even the case in this game.  When you get a Transphere your initial thought when you're new is "Wow! I can actually fight back and have a real chance to escape or defeat the Raider", but after a couple hours of playing the game you'll quickly realize Tran-spheres are terrible even if 3+ people rush the Raider and attack, it doesn't matter because you're going to turn back into a normal person in probably under 5 seconds if the raider so much as sneezes on you if you're under lvl 3.  Even in the event you have a level 4 on your team because thankfully one of you summoned Shenron and oh thank the gods you now have a chance, you're wrong. Having a lvl 4 survivor in this game is basically meaningless because your entire team has to backup this one player, and god help you if the raider is already lvl 4, unless he's trash he's going to roll your entire team like it's a joke.  Ultimately, the biggest problem with Raiders being overpowered is, survivors can que with their raiders and while yes it's guaranteed that their friend will be a Raider the fact you can do it at all is a problem.4. Teaming between Survivors and Raiders in this game is atrocious. It flat out shouldn't be a system, and I get the idea behind why it was probably implemented initially, and that being for friends to face off against each other...the problem is that should be kept to custom games or 8 stack groups only, not "hey let me que with my buddy and he'll give me the Dragon balls and tell me positions of his teammates while I go and kill them". 5. Another major problem with this game is, Raiders as unstoppable as they are, and as awful as everything else I've already listed is are heavily incentive to camp downed survivors, and the super time machine. Well you might say "Oh well the super time machine charges up over time so it doesn't matter" the problem with that is the Raider can trash the stm til it's one hit away from breaking, and leave it til it's about to finish and then they can completely destroy it to draw out the game as long as physically possible.  Besides camping the stm Raiders see nothing but benefit from camping downed survivors because they know other survivors will either run to revive them netting them another down/kill, or will let them die, and again letting them get an additional kill, this is a problem especially if the downed survivor is at an objective location like a key placement, or the STM.6. Survivor items for the most part are completely useless, and serve no benefit nor purpose.  The game has an assortment of tools that would be great and could really change things up for gameplay but the items such as Vegeta's gloves, Scouter, and rocket launchers flat out are useless. They don't do anything of actual value, at least not right now the way they're balanced.7. Options for Survivors to escape Raiders are pretty bad overall. In most cases most abilities that offer an opportunity to escape or get away are completely useless, for a variety of reasons. Kaioken Rush for example, a skill commonly used for traversal and potential escape from Raiders is exclusively useful for traversal because of 2 major reasons. 1. If you use it facing the Raider you'll just slap them for a pixel of dmg warranting a guaranteed down/kill. 2. The only really effective escape I've seen used is the Grapple hook, and even then most of the time Raiders will just follow to where u went and then down/kill you, or will hit you out of the air when using it.TL;DR: The game has really great potential and I really do enjoy it when I'm not getting slapped around by overpowered Raiders, and feeling like my transformations have little to no impact, nor reward for even getting it, it's a joy to play with friends but I think the game will be dead before 2024 if major issues aren't fixed. To my knowledge the game already experienced wave of massive player dropoff due to the devs overbuffing Raiders to the point of being downright not fun to fight against, the only one I even know about that can be easily dealt with is Spopovich (Buu's first form) because he's just weak apparently. If the game tones down its heavy reliance on the p2w model/gacha system, nerfs Raiders or at least buffs survivors to the point of not being fly's to a lvl 2 Raider then it'll be a great game for the most part.

_childDocuments_.review: EXTERIOR, A NAMEKUSEI VILLAGE - NIGHTInjured and cold, our ragtag team of volunteer Time Breakers is stunned and disoriented from the time jump, we could be anywhere... The comms come alive and the garbled voice briefs us: rescue time-jumped civilians from a past monster called Frieza -who destroys this very planet on this very day.  Try to get out alive.We run for cover, the beast could be anywhere, voice says Frieza has a scouter too.  We scramble to search for the artifacts that will set this time straight, and for the terrified civilians who suddenly found themselves here.  That's when I notice a fresh face among the bitter volunteers - the scouter clocks his power level at only 1.  You can tell this his first mission ever, and he is trembling with fear.  Survival rates are low, especially for rookies, and this one is as green as they come. His name is Oolong, ripped out from a time back when humanoid animals lived among humans on Earth.  Just a trembling, pale pig, peering at the dark alien sky from behind the rubble of what was once a building, tugging at his suspenders with anxiety.  That's when I decide that I'm making sure this pig gets home, and I can tell it's going to cost me everything if I can even manage to do it.  Foolish perhaps, but my transphere contains Krillin's ki and I can feel it won't---Boom!-An explosion from the East!  Maybe nobody... sure enough, one of us went down, and of course it's the pig.  He can barely move, and is waiting for death way in the open, at the opposite side of the map, looking around hopelessly, in no man's land.  It now rains fire on us and we dive for cover in a panic.  Frieza is looking for movement, so nobody can move, but Oolong is bleeding out.  There are three volunteers much closer to him than I am, but several seconds later it becomes clear nobody is willing to risk it.  He got dealt a bad hand, rookies almost never survive anyway... he has mere seconds left... what a fool I am, this is going to kill me and for what?  He's just a stranger lost in time... Krillin's transphere... KAIOUUUUKEN! I fly through hellfire directly underneath Frieza, even if for some miracle the monster doesn't see me, I still might not make it in time even in a straight line - Frieza sees me.  Goodbye world, I tried, Oolong... A volunteer jumps from a rooftop!  Inspired by what I was doing, he channels a warrior from the past in mid air and kicks Frieza off me.  That will probably spell out his end, but I flash across the war zone at Oolong and just barely reach him as he twitches his last and force feed him my only senzu seed.  His instincts kick in and he stands up, his body repaired.  I immediately dive into the water behind him to evade the ki blasts that are certainly coming.  Oolong just stands there, dumbfounded that someone came to save him.  He unfreezes and runs around in a panic until he starts sprinting toward some ruins.I find some supplies in an underwater cave, a Capsule Corporation body shield. They do the job most of the time, should come in handy.  Their technology is the only thing giving us the slightest chance to survive these encounters.  The rest of the team is managing to get a weak signal to the rickety time device.  If we can get it manually started after that, we could set all of this right.  Just then the comms tell us that we've evacuated all of the remaining civilians back to their own time, although it cost us two brave souls.  We knew what we signed up for.  Frieza looks bigger and stronger than before, and furiously destroys an entire mountain.  We had three men in that area, and they cease to exist.  Except for one of them, who is merely dying... Oolong, who is still hanging on to life one last time.  I can just barely make him out slowly dragging himself along the lip of a hot new crater.  None of the remaining boys have any illusions, Frieza is now too strong and he's destroying the time device slowly to bait us out.  All that work.  All those deaths... at least most of the civilians were evacuated before Frieza found them.  What remains of the squad figures the pig is doomed but maybe a couple of us can escape with our lives.Not on my watch, I risk everything, zig-zagging behind every obstacle, crawling here and swimming there, using every skill I have trained, and make it to Oolong just in time again.  I shove him into the crater to get a bit of cover.  I help him up, and give him my body shield though I doubt he'll pick it up before running away.  He actually does!  I transform into a rock in front of him to blend into the environment and to show him how to do it.  I scuttle this way and he scuttles that way, there being no directions anymore, only chaos and death.  The ground starts burning up, Frieza must have seen us. I burn the rest of my stamina in a mad dash to nowhere, then look around to see where I ended up.  The voice in the comms says to abort the mission and to try to make it to one of the two escape pods they sent just now. I struggle to spot the beacons through the dust and smoke,  One landed far from me, the other one landed very far from me.   Far it is.  I missile-fly in that general direction, not knowing where Frieza is but it's all I can do.  I fly low to the ground, weaving through debris and collapsed buildings at high speeds, I will explode if I so much as graze a wall, but I have only seconds until this planet explodes.  It's death either way.  I make it to the escape pod!  It takes some doing to get it started, and I still have no idea where Frieza might be. He could be standing right behind me and I wouldn't know.  But I have only seconds, so I can't turn around.  I activate the pod expecting him to blast me away from behind, and start sequence begins!  I look behind me in the second it takes to take off, and Frieza is somehow NOT standing there.  I can't believe I'm going to make it out. I pause my panic for a second to look at the comms, I forgot all about Oolong... but the comms show that everybody is dead.  Everybody except for two of us: Me. And. Oolong!  Dreaming that he could even get to the other escape pod, would he know how to operate it in a panic?  My hand hesitates for a full second, but I power down the escape pod.  Now I can feel death breathing down my neck, but I can't leave without so much as turning around to see if Oolong is even still... he is running toward me with his stubby legs across a battle-scarred plain with no cover, no supplies, no abilities, no plan.  Only terror.  Our eyes meet.  I have to get this brave little pig home, but there's no way we make it.  At least we'll die together.  I punch the escape pod to maneuver it at its maximum speed, but it was not designed for either... I drive the clumsy pod through the exploding planet, across the open and toward Oolong,  Every fraction of a second, I think I'm about to die but all I can see with my tunnel vision is Oolong.  All I can hear is my own heartbeat and my hand is frozen pushing forward on the pod stick.  Oolong leaps toward me and bear-hugs the fuselage of the pod for dear life as I enter the last code needed and we disappear in a flash of lightning.  The mission failed, but several civilians were rescued, and Oolong and I live to fight another day.I got the pig home, and it took everything I had.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot in good consciousness recommend this game. Feels like it should've been free with the gacha system, especially how awful it is. I've gotten 2 10 pulls in my almost 20 hours (at the time of writing this) hours. Genshin impact not only gave me more pulls, they gave me better ones. For instance, you can turn into one of the characters using transpheres. They give you skills and allow you to temporarily transform into them during the match, while also have a "special skill" aka a signature move. But, depending on which character you pull, you may not get any special skill, which is a huge part of the character's kit. For instance, I got a 5 star vegeta, the highest rarity, at the start of the game. I didn't get a special skill for him until 10-ish hours in the game, so he was essentially useless besides taking a hit when i turn into him. Not to mention, it's incredibly hard to win as raider. There's no tutorial on any of em, so good luck on your first match. But as you keep playing, you'll get it down more. Except, you're going to be around raider  level 6, while the survivors are almost fully kitted and around level 60, if you're lucky. There's so many little things the devs don't tell you about playing raider that could be easily solved with just a quick tutorial on all of em. Or hell, even just one. To sum it up: This game is extremely lacking in content. It is incredibly difficult to learn how to play raider as not only is it dependant on the survivors' luck, but also what stupid skills they have (usually the bulma scooter, which is op), and finally, charging 20 dollars and then putting a gacha system in is extremely scummy, especially with what little content this game actually has. And they are going to be very, VERY slowly putting out more raiders, survivors and the likes. They are on par with other game's seasons, like Apex, with the 1 new character and new map each season. Except those games actually launched with content, such as Apex and Dead By Daylight (7 killers, maps and 10 survivors). This game, as it is right now, is not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: NOV 18th updatechanging my review to no since the game seems very volatile with its balance changes. It's only been a little over a month since the game's release and we've already received even more drastic changes to game balance. I can't confidently recommend a game if I can't guarantee the experience I have will be the same one you'll be getting if you buy this game a few weeks out from the time of writing this. I also personally don't like the recent changes, they're very raider favored. A link below to raider gameplay as of November 18th is below.Initial review is below.Game is fun. With regards to balance, the only serious problems at the moment are Super Buu and the map Waterfront Warzone. Any complaints you see about anything else on steam reviews are simply skill issues.The rest of the review will be listing off facts so you can decide if the game is for you or not.The game is divided into two formats: Survivor and Raider. To play Raider, you must choose to have it as your preferred role. Any time you do not get raider, your priority will go up by one until you play it, then your priority will reset.Acquiring skills is done through a gacha system. It costs 15,000 zenny per pull. You will earn, on average, about 2500-3000 zenny per game. In a best case scenario you will earn enough for a pull every 4 games, but it usually averages out to 5-6.You may also purchase TP for pulls. It is about $1.50 per pull.Occasionally, you will get free pulls from mail from game devs, promo codes, friend codes, etc.Leveling up will earn you free pulls/TP, but there is a level cap of 100. Afterwards you will not get anymore.There is luck protection for super moves, but not for active/passive skills. It is entirely possible for you to pull 100+ times and not get something you may want.There is a season pass. It does not cost anything to unlock, but you may purchase tiers within it It is $1.50 per tier. Progression is entirely time gated through daily/weekly challenges and a daily rng drop while playing.Daily challenges usually take about 30 minutes to do each day.Weekly challenges usually take about 6 hours in total.The RNG drops vary. You can complete it in as little as 40 seconds or it may take you 5 hours in a single day to finish it. The current season pass runs for about 98 days. If you complete challenges every day, it will take you 26 days at minimum to complete the season pass.You can bank daily and weekly challenges, but not the rng drops.link to survivor gameplay, dated Nov 7th 2022: link to raider gameplay, dated Nov 7th 2022:

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of the game is really nice and the execution of quick, fast paced matches works really well for this game. the idea that you can fight an uphill battle against a powerful foe from the Dragon Ball universe is really cool too. However once you get past a few matches and start finding yourself pitted against any raider that isn't cell you immediately realize just how bad the balance and protection in this game is. Frieza and Majin Buu both have hit scan beam attacks that reach across the map which in normal hands is like hitting a needle in a haystack but since the game doesn't have dedicated servers and instead relies on Peer hosting, the cheats are already out since day one with anyone playing Frieza or Buu being extremely likely to be using aim and wall hacks to target people. Even without those hacks the hitscan nature of any of Frieza's beams makes a match against them not very fun since they can be spammed. Worse is the balance on Buu which is spopavich having the same exact beam as Frieza from the start, then massive double AOE in 2nd form, to the same hitscan beam and instant lockdowns on survivors with a short cooldown to finally having a arena wide insta-kill mechanic against any survivor that stands still for longer than a second.The game has poor balance, poor peer to peer hosting, easy anti-cheat not working, no unlocks beside a gatcha system for in game skills, or real money for cosmetics, and no way to set your region for play. And on that region play, if you are from north america, and have a friend from Europe that is in the party, then the matchmaking will ONLY MATCH YOU WITH OTHER PEOPLE from NA AND Europe, IE other groups that have someone from NA and someone from Europe.The game is fun though, if only when you're fighting against a Cell player because then it's balanced and a challenge. If they could get dedicated servers, allow you to change your region you wish to play on, fix the massive hacking issues, and not give every raider a hit scan beam along with massive nerfs to balance them (except Cell) then this would be a thumbs up. But for now it feels like they got a bunch of people working on systems for the game and had no real direction for the game besides get the game working, get gatcha in there to make money because that's the only way to make money on games now, and slowly add in more and more powerful raiders without balance testing.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like someone took one of those 'Warcraft 3:' Dragonball RPG Custom Maps where 8 players run around and try to train themselves to take on the person who opened the lobby and is trying to bully them except in Dragonball Xenoverse's engine instead of Warcraft 3. This is both good and bad as I feel we get this game does a unique job of feeling like a self contained DragonBall Z mini-arc where You and the 7 other survivors feel like Krillin, Tien, Yamacha, or Picollo attempting to train till your strong enough to survive being the the same area as a Villian like Frieza, Cell, or Majin Buu. Ultimately playing survivor feels kinda like the searching part of a Battle Royale except you know there is one player you cannot handle until near end of a game. There are ways to fight toe to toe at power level 2 or 3 if you fight alongside allies. If you manage to get all 7 dragon balls you can reach new heights and become strong enough to beat the raider in any 2v1 scenario as level 4 power has a ton of health to work with and throw out Super Attacks with.It's worth mentioning that the tutorial in DB: Breakers doesn't really tell you much about how the game is actually played just some of the most basic mechanics so alot of people will get a bad initial impression. It gives you the impression that you alone can do alot to stop the raider or at least waste their time but attempting that takes teamwork and resources that you need to gather while stealthing around the map.  Alot of people will try to play like the game is Dead by Daylight and hate DB: the Breakers because they will often get killed the moment they try to lead the raider on a chase. Stealth is more important in Breakers and knowing how to use your Transformation and movement abilities to round a corner and lose the raider before they catch up to you. You can also potentially fight the Raider but you will not be successful unless it's a team effort as the Raider can dodge survivors attacks while approaching them and stun them during the attacks startup. This does lead to the downside if you die early you probably cannot be saved as your team isn't strong enough yet to distract the Raider long to allow a rescue. You can go for a solo stun with Solar Flare (taiyoken) or Rocket Launcher items; however, the raider is very likely to hit you before you can hit them so pulling this off is very risky unless you know when they want to round a corner or have a ally to distract.Also unlike Dead by Daylight Survivors and Raiders have far more active abilities and more vertical movement. I think this may hurt balance long term as there are some abilities that just seem to have way more of an impact on the match then others. Stun and Movement abilities rein supreme as far as active abilities go and even the best passive ability is one that gives you a float which is faster then your run making hopping and floating the fastest way to move without putting the better movement on a cooldown. The float (hover drone)  helps you readjust after other movement abilities that leave you airborne and will even stop upward air momentum letting you fall back to the ground and hide faster in alot of scenarios. Hover Drone should just be a base kit ability for survivors with how much better it is than the other passive skills.Raider also brings up another issue in that it's fun to play but if you queue as Raider you have to play 3-6 matches as Survior first to build queue priority then you can play Survivor. It's a solution to Dead By Daylight and Video Horror Society's long wait times for the more popular role and it does work to get you in and out of games fast. Since I can't get anywhere near as many games as Raider as I can Survivor, I can't say as much about the balance between Raiders. I mostly play as Frieza who seems to do fine against the Survivors. I lose as many games as I win as Raider so that is a sign the balance is alright.The other downside to this game is that the progression to unlock currency for the gatcha system is awful. There isn't alot of content in the game yet and you don't get enough currency for 10 pulls so you spend alot of time doing individual pulls winding up with the same characters and abilities you already have. You get another currency for the duplicate pulls which helps level up your abilities but considerable investment gets you about 5-15% more cooldown or range or whatever alongside being able to use a Survivor's specific abilities on another Survivor. It's useful but it doesn't feel like progress you you are shaving off .5% cooldown every level that cost you the amount of currency you just got in your last Gatcha pull. Hopefully this problem fixes itself with continued development.Speaking of continued development this game is also a live service game so who knows how long the game servers will stay up. One could buy this game and have it just not exist in a few years let alone worrying about player numbers and queue times. If you want to try this game now could be your only chance.I know I covered more downsides then I did upsides in my review but this game can be very fun if you approach it with the right attitude. Personally I'm loving the game so far and if you can put up with a few frustrations here and there it can lead to some really entertaining moments and interactions. There being 7 survivors instead of Dead by Daylight's 4 also means you run into less games where someone is being 'dead weight' either on purpose or because they don't know how to play. You'll still get left to die from time to time but nowhere near as often as in Dead by Daylight. Even if most of the team can't pull it together in the end the emergency escape pod serves a similar function to Dead by Daylight's Escape Hatch except more 3 players can use it so you still have a way to kinda 'win'.TLDR; Fun game progression is too slow for how little content exists, the game does a bad job teaching you how to play it but once you learn the various systems you get a unique experience that leads to alot of fun moments.--------------------------EDIT-----------------------------------Alright the game is 7 seasons in at the time of writing this. It's got a small but playable audience 3 times as much content but it's locked behind paywalls.That said queue times are only short at peak hours. Expect 5-10 minute waits otherwise with some crashing. I really cannot recommend this game to anyone except Dragonball fans or people desperate for another Asymmetric Multiplayer game at this point, but the game isn't bad enough for a Negative Review. That said I now understand the Dead by Daylight formula mostly works as a game you can get your friends to play without much onboarding and OH BOY THAT IS NOT THIS GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: Have to change this to a 'No'. Season 2 provided some good additions to the game but the Gacha really is too punishing, especially for a game you have to buy. The chances of what you want are way too low and there's no pity system in place to ensure you ever get what you want, even when everything else is obtained. And even though I rarely played with other people, forcing you and anyone in your lobby to only play Survivor is... it's moronic, plain and simple. The fix to people teaming up with raiders was to let players block them post-match so they never get matched with them again. "But then they'll never find players again" exactly, don't be a cheating ♥♥♥♥♥, play the game as intended or just suspend them when people post actual videos of them doing this exact thing for a week or something, followed by a ban if they don't. The fix is not to take away being able to play in custom parties only as Survivor or forcing a FULL LOBBY to go in to practice mode, where they get absolutely no rewards or experience for the game they play. Dimps, you guys desperately need to make a QoL pass or the game won't survive until Season 3. Crossplay and making it free to play are the big two, but removing the ridiculous pre-made group restrictions is also a major change.-Original review below for posterity-I really, really, really like this game but it is not without its downsides; the current balancing is a bit off, favoring Survivors far more than Raiders (The villains) and there are some extremely cheap abilities at the Survivors' disposal but it's still a lot of fun, especially when you manage to take down Survivors that played well. EDIT: The game now favors Raiders after a balance pass, a bit too much, but the balance is closer than what it was; it just needs fine-tuning and some minor nerfs/buffs here and there.The game is 1v7; 1 killer and 7 survivors.Yes, there is a Gacha system in the game but, frankly, most of the best abilities are ones you buy from the shop with Zeni, which you just find playing matches; Zeni is NOT a premium currency, you only get that from playing the game. You can get tickets to use the gacha for free when you get levels, upgrade in the battle pass (Which is free and not too difficult to level in) and from various promotions and bonuses by the developers though you can also use Zeni or TP Tokens (The premium currency) to open them as well. If I had one complaint about this current Gacha system, it's that there should be a sympathy system in place to ensure you get something new every X amount of summons but this really is the least predatory Gacha system I have seen in a game. There's so many ways to get them that it really isn't that bad. Now, my biggest complaint are certain Weekly missions for the battle pass that directly oppose the current meta of the game, but hopefully those will be tweaked in the future to be more forgiving. All in all, the game is a lot of fun IF you enjoy asymmetrical multiplayer games, nut if you like the Dragon Ball series that is just a bonus.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I really like this game!I have played for a few days and it dosent get any boring for me, at least not now. There is so much to do, so many ways to play that it can be overwhelming at first but eventually you'll find your own style. While the graphics arent really amazing and the camera can be janky (at least on controlers, I play on mouse and keyboard so I dont have such problem), its still an enjoyable experience.For me I find playing survivor far more enjoyable than playing as a raider.Often people talk about the game cons, so I'll go over them really quickly.Gacha, while it can be annoying it really isnt that big of a deal, on the start you get one of the best if not the best ability in the game. Few characters to play as too and possibly some gifts to summon in the mailbox. While the abilities of certain characters like Krillin, Goku or Vegeta are very good you can easly do well in any kind of scenario with more common abilities and passives like Bulmas bike and Krillins vehicycle speed boost, raider literally cant catch up to you. While in dragon change no matter what character you use the damage stays the same for melee, the only thing that changes are super attacks which you can unlock with 20k upgrade currency, you get 900 if you pull something that you already have in the siphon and like 100 per game, its grindy. The only paid currency is TP medals, if you do not want to spend any money on that just use the TP you get trough Dragon Pass or trough leveling up on cosmetics, 150 is not worth it. If you want to pull something you might as well farm 15k zeni each time and as soon as you get it pull single, 10x pulls dont have any benefits. You can get a max of 4k zeni per game.Senzu Beans not giving invicibility frames. Well lets start off with the note that you SHOULDNT USE SENZU BEANS ON YOURSELF. Its a tool to revive someone instantly or if you really need it use it on yourselff if raider transforms or you hid yourself, otherwise you will get yourself killed.Raiders being way too op. In combat? Yes, absolutly but what we have to remember is that it isnt game like Xenoverse 2 or Budokai Tenkaichi, in this game we either run or stall for time, otherwise just dont fight, well maybe if you want to jump the raider, then go ahead just be careful, dont jump Freeza he transforms while fighting. Pay To Win. This game isnt pay to win, Dragon Pass is free and only game beneficial thing it gives is Farmer with a shotgun which isnt even that good, his digging mechanic isnt a guarantee spawn for an item, other than that you can buy cosmetics or pull warriors in the siphon. Considering that siphon only gives survivor abilities then if your friends have better survival likeability its good for you. You arent fighting the other survivors, you are trying to work together with them. Not only that but you can pair up so many "common" abilities with each other that will do just as good of a job as using very good abilities like Kaioken Rush or Space Pod.I believe I have gone over few cons and why they arent really cons but people not understanding the game. Honestly if you want to just buy it, Its cheap and fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hit or miss because admittedly it is a Dragon Ball Xenoverse asset flip with aspects that I dislike from that series like the combat having little variety (and even less in The Breakers) and the visuals which have been ugly and dated even when it released in 2015. I do greatly enjoy it because it feels like a thrilling hide and seek experience with a Dragon Ball flavor and player interactions that make me laugh every session. 2 main wishes for this game are voice chat and Bulma's bike skill nerf. Those are two things that deter from the experience:1.)There's already limited communication features between players. No text chat, 4 preset messages, no pinging when downed, there's no way to communicate enough between teammates unless using discord or some separate program. 2.)It's part of the meta to just sit on the maximum speed turbo scooter and be able to avoid all contact with the raider that even the targeting system and tracking moves can do nothing about. Players just sit on the bike in a hiding spot and wait for a telegraphed super move or for the raider to get close enough so they can drive to the opposite side of the map. It's a boring solo playstyle, they activate a low cooldown skill to stop participating in the game temporarily.The game does have lasting appeal with its playerbase, it may drop off if future updates gate off new content behind too much premium currency and the Spirit Siphon system is unfair for players not grinding missions daily and getting a lot of gacha tickets, but as of the timing of this review I feel that the game has a decent roadmap with new content being added every 3-4 weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ball the Breakers has reached its breaking point for me. I've been playing this since the Open Beta, the world's most foolishly Yamcha cultist with 1500 hours (700 in queues). MetaYamshi himself. And I'm done. Dimps, you have ultimately failed me.This game always had problems. It's an asymmetrical multiplayer game, it's going to have balance issues; the game favors survivors while single survivors are so weak and helpless on their own. So premades are considered overpowered while playing with randoms is far too unreliable for a game with a battle pass to unlock the few things not up to the gacha slot Gods of disappointment (my friend still never 100% Videl). And I put up with all of it. Raiders bouncing back and forth between tissue paper and canonically OP, learning the hard way which skills are actually useful enough to justify having on my builds, Cave_Of_ , Key Camping, Buu being more of a joke than Yamcha, ALL of this game's problems were worth it to play with friends and the early community.Because back in the day, you got a variety of players. The Raider might be a try-hard, it might be a newcomer, it might be a mid-level player, it might have been a joker who wanted to mess around, it might have been someone wanting a 1-on-1 duel with a level 4. They might just be a bug on a wall. But that was then. Now, it's solely the competitive side of the community going all in as either survivor or raider. It was worth the lengthy queue times because the die roll of the experience helped keep things dynamic. Once the game devolved into either new players or Vegeta Sweats, it just became a grind for battle pass stuff that I may or may not use.So when playing with my friends was the last thing keeping me going, with the 7 Yamcha Squad trying out an un-optimal build to show teamwork trumps the meta... they rolled in region lock. The use of VPNs and Crossplay helped mitigate that for a time, but it still made it a pain to play with friends. And that's the problem. This is a multiplayer game that doesn't want friends to get together and play. You can't have a party of 8 play and get battle pass progress, because apparently, the battle pass progress is more sacred than the player base they're desperate to hold on to.THAT much became apparent with coastal lock, or as my friend accurately calls it, time zone lock. Now, I can't even easily play with friends in the US because they live too far away. And this is on top of the many problems the leftover community has: feeders, lag switchers, hackers, body campers, stun spammers, the awful grind for the battle pass with increasingly weak rewards. If people didn't write this game off so quickly, YongYea would be making a monthly video on the state of this game.Between everything that's happened with this game and the fact that live services are a dime-a-dozen, I'm left with literally no reason to play this game anymore. I'm uninstalling the game, and unless season 6 is a come-to-Jesus moment, I'm done.And to think, they added the Yamcha Baseball outfit just in time for me to retire it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what can i say except the game is either really good or really bad, it all comes down to luck, theres never ever an average "satisfatory" in-game match, heres why:But before i breakdown my analysis even though i havent played much time, since the game is relatively simple you can get the gyst of it really fast so a few things first:There is only a brief tutorial on how to play as a survivor, no tutorial for raider, if you want tips, go read them yourself at the "help assistance" robot in game. The controls are very cluncky, you can choose controller presets but not customize your own so some skills/items/things you'd like to be able to do in a single key/button will require multiple ones, camera controls benefit a lot more the survivors than the raiders...There is a cash shop but so far i've seen no indication that the game is P2W, mostly all items are for cosmetic purposes and some skills, but i dont reckon they're game breaking so its green light in this regard,There is however a "gacha" system implemented where you summon for Z-fighters that give you abilities/skills required for when you transform in every match, you can either play for hours on end to scrap 150k in game regular currency for a 10 multi summon, get tickets as you level your "season-pass"bar, or (of course) spend money for the premium currencyThe items you get in each match (if you play as a survivor) are okay in general, they're all usable in a variety of situations but for some reason they decided you can only use senzu beans when you're down and the raider hasnt finished you off yet ( which is unlikely it will ever save you) i myself used it many times but to no avail since the raider was always on me...Game is set to 15 min but very rarely if even will last that long, this is a very fast paced game where (again) either get a good survivor team or a bad/new raider,You do not choose which role you want to play as, you select a "preference" which means that if you set your role preference as "raider" you will not be guaranteed to play as one, the average is between 5-8 games as a survivor and 1 game as a raider in my experience,If you have friends well great, you will have a great experience because this is another game where communication greatly changes your gameplay experience, this is why you will find it strange to find high level raiders already existing even though you can barely scrap 2 games to play as one (if you play more than 2 hours),Now if you're playing as a survivor:You, yes you, you will be the first or second player to die,70% of the games you play, so get used to it,why? because the raiders(cell and buu stage 3) can sense ki(as a skill with cooldown of course) and even though you have the ability to "hide" this changes nothing you will be found and they will still come after you, so pray...you can either focus on searching for the keys that activate the time-machine to fix the timeline orfocus on collecting the dragon balls so you can get a big power-up to defeat the raider,what decides this you might ask, well depending once again on luck if you find the correct items, meaning if you find at least a level 2 dragon ball radar you can choose to search for the dragon balls otherwise tough luck, you're stuck to key finding dutyif you play agaisnt survivors:They will all have dragon radars level 3, they will find power ups very easily reaching level 2-3 in a snap and they will also hide very well, because remember there is no lock-on camera system for raiders so even if you find them they will very easily slip by your fingers denying you the experience you need to grow stronger, they will find the dragon balls so fast you cant even get 1-2 players killed, one match i had i kid you not a player found all 7dbs before the 4 min mark i was barely level 2, he summoned shenron got his level 4 boost and wiped me clean, easy game for them, terrible experience for me,if you play as a raider:Always choose Frieza or Majin buu because even though all raiders start at level 1 only cell is incapable of killing players from the _childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ball: The Breakers is one of the coolest anime games that has ever come out and works wonderfully with the Dragon Ball IP. However, the game is held back by baffling design decisions that ultimately make me unable to recommend one of the most unique games from one of my favorite IPs, and it breaks my heart to say such a thing.It's held back by:- Region-locked matchmaking; an American will only ever be able to matchmake with other Americans, for example. This limits the potential player pool and matchmaking potential.- No crossplay; it's coming down the pipeline, but I'm really not sure how many people will care assuming it ever does get done. This limits the player pool and matchmaking potential even further.- Due to the two issues above, there's no Raider queue. In a game like DBD, you can queue for Killer or Survivor, but not here, and having a Raider queue simply isn't sustainable because of how many, quite frankly, idiotic decisions are on the matchmaking side of this game.- Leveling and progression systems that is ultimately just locked behind time and matches played. This can be especially grindy for Raiders, who you have a harder time getting around to playing as. - An always online, paid access, multiplayer only asymmetrical game. This game should  be paid access.Each of these issues also comes with their own flaws heavily related to them.- Leveling and progression being locked behind time played and actually playing matches means progression is super slow, and newer players will have a harder and harder time getting in as the more committed playerbase pushes to higher levels. There isn't even a bot mode to learn the game or get some extra levels to catch up to the rest of the playerbase. - The balance of the game is already incredibly volatile, and the Raider can absolutely stomp or be stomp. This isn't an issue in itself; volatile matchmaking can make for extremely fun matches and memorable moments. The issue is that a big contributing factor now is that it's a bunch of Level 100 experienced Survivors vs the Level 2 Cell, or vice versa. One is simply just massively unequipped to deal with the other in an interesting and fun way.If the game just went free-to-play, added crossplay, didn't regionlock and didn't go mega-predatory with the other forms of monetization they'd probably need to sustain the game, then it would probably be pretty good. The game is totally fun, but it feels like the people making a lot of the decisions for this game wanted it to fail.

_childDocuments_.review: Straight up, before we go in depth: Despite the issues it has, it's very fun and addictive, and I personally got well more than 20$ worth out of it. I'd buy it again for friends easily. That being said, let's tackle this.By which I mean, if you play for five days and finish your missions each day, you'll only get one set per day, but if you play for the sixth day after five days of not playing, all former five day missions are available to you on top of the sixth day, and they'll replace the finished missions as you go. Play once a month? You get the entire month's missions to do on that day.This is, I think, the first game with daily/weekly missions that doesn't punish you for not playing every day! In fact, taking a break is a good thing, because when you come back, you can binge the game and finish mission after mission if you want to. That's how I prefer to play, personally; wait a few days, come back and play a lot, repeat.I can say, if you believe nothing else is good, you have to acknowledge that the game does this point perfectly, fantastically, and awesomely.That's just how the  works. It's not unique to BREAKERS. Asymmetrical multiplayer inherently has to get rid of the large side for the small side to win. Furthermore, even if you die that early, you still get credit for anything your group has done. You can even hold off on leaving to get the benefit of winning if your team manages it without you. Or you can leave and immediately get back into queue.Matches are 15 minutes. It sucks to die too early. But that's just how asymmetrical works.Gacha systems in general are pretty bad and have no place in paid games (and even in free games, they're done horribly, imo). I want to stress, right now, that while I'm used to them and can deal with them, I do think it should not have been added into this game. I don't agree with it.That being said, BREAKERS actually has one of the least predatory gachas I've ever had to deal with. It's true that you don't guarantee a 5* from summoning, BUT you can buy Super Attacks for any character you've already pulled once with an only-in-game currency. Plus, the game tends to honestly be pretty generous with currency and tickets.Again, I am NOT defending the system. It shouldn't be here. I'm just pointing out that, if you can handle gacha systems, this is one of the lighter ones, and besides a couple of skills (like Android 17's Barrier), most any skills work just fine and you don't need to hunt them down.This is a problem I'm noticing, and I think it's because people are being turned off by the negative reviews. That said, the flex queue has always worked well enough for me, with only the rare occasional queue going over 10 minutes. As for Raider queues, I've always been a Raider within 5-6 flex/weight for it, so it's never  long before I can play Raider. Obviously, my account isn't universal, but this is just how it's been for me.I DO think they need to bring the Raider only queue back, but it was removed because of people complaining about how long it took (even though that's obvious, because you're looking for 7 other people who AREN'T Raiders).If you're looking for a game that guarantees major content regularly... this isn't it. It's not as big as Dead by Daylight or anything like that, so for the most part, the content comes much slower. It  constantly updated during the Season, however.Or rather, whatever they use for matchmaking does. I've heard it's peer-to-peer, I'm not sure, but if someone's connection is slow, the game can run... pretty slowly. And if someone is heavily lagging, that can lag you out, too. Personally, I found these to be mostly uncommon (and everybody lagging extremely rare), but it does happen.I personally expected it, since this isn't exactly something the DBZ games do often, but more balancing, more often, is definitely needed.This was an answer to a lot of people trying to game the system by going into a match with friends and letting them win, but it was a very poor choice to make. I don't think it should have ever been removed, regardless of the bad apples.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm incredibly mixed on this game.On the one hand, I really like the asymmetric gameplay between the raiders and the survivors. It is really thrilling when you are playing survivor and you are getting chased down by a raider and you are using all your active skills and map knowledge to avoid getting killed. The raider gameplay is also fantasically implemented when it isn't being cheesed and there are no cheaters.On the other hand, this game has a lot of flaws. It is really easy for the raider to camp a specific objective and drive the game to a screeching halt as survivors trickle into the objective to get absolutely blasted. I solo queue so maybe that's the issue, but in my experience the raider can pretty reliably win if they just sit on a key capture point and kill people as they try to place the key. There is also people quitting out of survivor role before the game starts to increase their raider priority. The devs have addressed the last problem this week, but honestly it doesn't look like it has even slowed down at the time of writing. And who can blame them? You have to play at least 5+ games as survivor to play raider and in my experience it is closer to 7 or 8 before your priority is high enough. Games take about 10 minutes meaning you are likely playing for over an hour straight before you even get the chance to play raider.There is also a big variety problem. 3 maps and 3 raiders at the time of writing. It doesn't take very long before it all starts to blend together for me and I know I'm not the only one. There are lots (about a dozen I think) of choices for survivor transformations, but these transformations usually make up less than a minute of gametime at most or several seconds of flying away from the raider if you are very unlucky. I suspect that the reason there is so much survivor variety is because of the gatcha mechanics that reward these transformations.In conclusion, I'm probably going to keep playing this game as long as I still find it fun. I've not paid a cent other than the fee for entry and I've got all the transformations and most of the skills and super attacks, so if you are willing to be patient you can get the transformation you are looking for. But the lack of map/raider variety, cheaters, quitters, and barrier to play as a raider semi regularly makes this game really hard to recommend to others at the time of writing. This might change if Bandai puts more maps and raiders in the game. They have a roadmap for future content, and judging from that it is going to be a few years before there is enough content to hold attention for more than 5 hours for most people.
