_childDocuments_.review: A great game that sadly seems to be getting review bombed. So let me explain the points most negative review are saying.1. No Crossplay/Cross-Region2. Pay-to-Win Gacha in a Premium Game3. Battle Pass4. Premium Cosmetics5. Unbalanced against SurvivorSo point 1 is valid. The game should have Crossplay as it is hurting the consoles quite a bit and Cross-Region because NA and EU is the only ones not having long queue times. Maybe it will be added, maybe it won't.Point 2 isn't looking closely enough. The Gacha is not Pay-to-Win because the game starts you with 3/4 of the best active skills in the game and gives you a ticket for the 4th, rolls are VERY quickly accumulated, and you earn points every match and every duplicate roll that allow you to outright buy any combat skills you are missing. So the only thing you don't get easy/instant-access to are passives that aren't necessary in the slightest to win. Yeh it's a Gacha, but honestly if every Gacha were like this one, people wouldn't find them so predatory.Point 3 is somewhat valid but honestly, it's mostly just that the game wants you to play every day just like every other game. The Battle Pass is 100% free and nothing at all in it is pay-to-win. However, you can only progress it so far each day/week due to limits being placed on how much can be earned in a day. However, dailies can be done 2-3 matches usually so it works well for people that don't have all day every day to play.Point 4 is something that should've been fought to the death when Horse Armor came out. It's here to stay in games now and it's never going away. Point 5 the game is NOT unbalanced. It's not quite perfectly balanced but it is very close. Most people with this complaint either had a bad team, had a really good enemy, or aren't playing Survivor correctly. Usually the not playing Survivor correctly comes down to the fact that THIS IS NOT A FIGHTING GAME. Survivors get levels to help them Survive against the Raider for a short period. If you use cooldowns properly, you can almost always run but if for some reason you can't, the best option is to just distract him for the team to win in the end because this is a team game. The only bit of unbalance I've seen in the game is a few attacks here and there are a bit too strong and Spopovich (level 1 Buu) is ridiculously strong for being level 1. Even then, every single Raider is beatable at every level. It's not a balancing issue, it's a skill issue whether stem from the team or the individual, it is a skill issue. If you're on the fence, I encourage you to try it for the 2 hours that steam gives you and if you don't like it, you can always refund. This is a fantastic game that does a great job doing what players have wanted to do in Dead By Daylight forever(kill the killer) and putting a Dragonball skin on it for Dragonball fans. This is a very different game from anything Dragonball has done before and I hope that it sticks around for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: As it stands currently, the game is fun for what it is, if not clunky in some ways... And the game is  predatory with micro-transactions due to the Seasonal Progression (Battle Pass), and the Gacha Machine. Too Long, I don't want to read: Otherwise, Lemme explain.Firstly, ,  there is a seasonal progression system that allows you to buy levels at $1.50 per level, or better said: 150 TP Tokens (Premium Currency), with 50 levels in total. It's filled with TP Tokens, Seasonal Tickets, Cosmetics/Voice lines, and currently: A new Survivor Skin at the very end (BIG PROBLEM FOR LATER EXPLAINING). TP 'Payout' of the whole season progression is 500 TP as FYI.Secondly, The Gacha system used in game is used for Transpheres, Which allow you to equip different passive/active skills, and special attacks when powered up during matches as survivor. Transpheres have a Base form they fall under, and differenting skills/attacks underneath. So 1 Goku transphere may have certain attacks or skills, while another one earned has different ones. Thankfully, they all meld into one when it comes to gameplay aspects, and you can mix/match as you please in there.You earn these in 4 Major ways, PER ROLL/GAMBLE:1. Gold Tickets, which are earned by leveling up Survivor Rank/Level, rarely.2. Season Tickets, Which are earned via Seasonal Progression.3. 15,000 Zeni, the Free Currency earned in-game and after matches.4. 150 TP Tokens ($1.50 usd)Getting a full repeat of unlocked skills/costumes/attacks refunds into Spirit Training Points (EXP Currency basically). I believe it's 900 of it, but I dont remember. Basically enough to power a skill up to +3 from baseline.(100->200->300->400 needed ect ect)So people who put down more money on this game will get access to the skills/attacks/skill upgrades quicker than someone who wont. The Survivor skin at the end of the Seasonal Progression also has it's own skills and abilities that can only be unlocked by that. (I'm gonna assume it can be unlocked after the season, hopefully, right?) But those skills/attacks/upgrades are only usable in the survivor sense, when you are playing with teammates. keep that in mind. So if you have a good person playing and they put money in this, they are your god friend.If you are the Raider/Evil-Dude, best of luck against those people. Raiders are pure skill as it currently stands, since there isn't ways to power them up other than playing as them. (Otherwise you are still pretty powerful)It takes about 5-10 matches to earn enough zeni for a roll, but games are decently quick.Finally, to bring a biit more info to Seasonal Progression, DP, or Dragon Points. Basically you can earn DP/Season Progression Points by:1. Randomly finding them in chests in-match. RARELY.2. Completing Daily challenges3. Completing Weekly challengesThat's it to my knowledge. You can probably complete daily/weekly challenges within a 5-6 hour playtime. 30 DP per total weekly challenges in total, and 3 DP per total daily challenges (I thiiink).Each Rank in the Season Leveling requires 8 DP to get to the next. You earn a total of 51 DP per week if you play everyday. And it would take 7 weeks worth of challenges completed to finish the Season Pass. You have 13 weeks as it stands writing this.I'm rambling at this point- Playing the game is fun, but if you want to 'complete' it your screwed.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, so it will be clumsily organised, but I hope to make my point across.So let's start with the bad, the graphics are... Modest at best, and the render distance of survivors is too high, it's easy for a raider to fly high in the sky and see survivors running around. The movement and controls take some getting used to, and they are clunky, sometimes I can escape the raider easily while other time I get stunlocked and I'm unable to react in any way.Finally (but that's really a genre issue) being an asymmetrical game, all matches are heavily matchmaking dependent, you can be the best Raider but you get out in a lobby full of already experienced survivors... You're gonna have a hard time. But this also works in reverse, you can get a lobby full of newbies and steamroll them.Same thing for survivors, you can find kil...raiders that have clearly no clue what to do and get stomped by even just 2 survivors. Or you can find a literal God who stomps everyone and leaves no room for salvation...Worst thing of all... Getting found by the raider right at the start and left to rot for 90 seconds because no one comes to rescue you...Now to the good things!The game is funny, full of personality, the customisation of the character is very good, you can choose your skills rather freely (the Gatcha is a non-issue) and both sides are balanced enough for a fresh game with an actually unique concept (let's not talk about Friday 17th game) I played one beta and kinda got hooked for now, even though I play alone and I'm 200% convinced this game is amazing with friends.Raiders get to taunt survivors and survivors get to make raiders waste time by stall-fighting, using traps and trying to escape.Overall I'd give a 8/10, but this is still early review, I'd wait until an actual meta is formed to before I'd say it's fun (at the moment it is really fun)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent take on the asym multiplayer genre, and an awesome new feel for Dragon Ball. As a long time fan of the anime, I think it nails the villains as the Raiders in a spectacular fashion. The game feels quite well balanced on launch, and I've honestly seen plenty of games go one way or the other. Both sides are fun to play as well, which is a hard thing to nail with games like this.To those worried about the gacha system, I'm not a huge fan of gacha systems in general and tend to avoid them like the plague (Dokkan Battle, looking at you) but in all honesty, the gacha and cash shop in this game aren't *terrible.*For one, the gacha system is *entirely usable without spending any of your hard earned dollars.* You earn plenty of money just by playing matches, and you also earn in-game currency every now and then. Those complaining about pull rates and IGC and microtransactions, you're really overthinking it. The current monetization scheme for the game isn't too greedy, but as tends to be the case, it would be nice to see the prices lowered a bit.For two, the prices in the cash shop. Most items by themselves are 300 TP Medals (Roughly $2-$3 cash depending on where you live) which is very attainable using the currency you get in-game. There are of course bundles, which reach into the 1000-2000 coin amounts, but that's to be expected when you want *all* of the items to look like a specific character right away.All in all, I was hyped when this game was announced, I've been hyped since I started playing and I don't want to put it down! If you enjoy Dragon Ball or asym multi games, give it a try! It's a fair price for the amount of content available on launch.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun. I was first excited about it since its a different spin on a dragonball game. There is quite a bit of a learning curve especially if you've never played a similar game like DBD. The tutorial gives you the absolute basics of only a few key elements but in actual games there are so many other tools to learn. As a survivor once you learn the maps, the uses of all the items, and what the Raiders can and can't do in their early stages it can create some really fun matches. If you're struggling with either role, really it just takes learning the game more. I've had amazing survivor groups that all work together and I've also had really well played Raiders that can end matches fairly quickly. Now for what I don't like: I played during the Last Chance Beta where Buu was not one of the raiders. Right now Buu feels really over-tuned and can make a winning match as a survivor turn into a losing one just by reaching third form. He could use some adjusting in his third stage. However, the above can be helped with some changes to survivor too. I'd love to see some invincibility frames for survivors for things like: eating a senzu bean right after being down, right after your shield breaks, and right after being revived by a teammate, some of those instances where it gives you a slightly better chance to get away from the raider if you're being hyper-focused especially early on in a match. I'll start this by saying I don't really -care- about there being premium currency or gacha in a paid game. I knew it was coming just by playing the beta. I just think the implement of it was pretty meh. To give us 300 currency when most people purchased the game for $20? imho I don't think it would have hurt them that much to give us $15-$20 of premium currency. There are plenty of outfits or special customization you can buy over the gacha. Will some people use it for the gacha? Yeah but is that also that bad? Chances of you getting specials for all the characters with $15 is already low. This could have been handled better. Finally to finish this rant the Dragon Tier "Battle Pass". You should get DP points per match. You can find 1 in a match maybe but it forces you to do the challenges when daily challenges will eventually lock until the next day (with a timer) While I am happy there is no "premium pass" (bless) it still feels meh to me but still better than it could have been. Overall tldr; This game is super fun whether you play survivor or raider. It can be really frustrating early on due to learning the maps, all the different items, and adjusting to what raiders/survivors can and can't do early on in a match. There's definitely a lot of room for improvement for BOTH roles and the gacha/premium currency is pretty meh but not the worst imho. I am super excited to continue to play this game and what other Raiders get added! Broly please!! (and Nappa/Raditz/Turles somehow idk gibemepls)

_childDocuments_.review: It's better than people give it credit for. It's easy to compare it to Dead By Daylight as the premise is the same - a larger group vs a solo player, with chaos happening where there's a lack of communication (outside of voice chat if premade)It plays differently though, and it will take time for people to get used to it. In DBD having anyone new is a recipe for a loss, and it's the same here. Most people don't understand survivor yet, and most don't understand raider, so wins/losses don't make sense yet.I like it being colourful, the art style is simple yet effective, I've had no slowdown despite using a 12 year old pc. There are a lot of fun memorable moments as survivor, which is nice.There's a lack of variety in active skills, passive skills, maps and raiders at this stage, but they all have the possibility of being increased. The 'battle pass' is free, and easily completed with daily/weekly rewards without any additional cost. A season seems to be 100 days, and 13 points are offered daily. 392 points are needed to max it, so that's 30 out of 100 needed, far easier than a lot of games I can think of. And that's not counting weekly quests either (which I dislike, because they require raider matches and I don't play that role).The gacha/rng needs a more expensive guaranteed option for buying an exact skill, but it isn't bad. To use Dead By Daylight again, that game locks certain skills behind paywalls entirely, with the only option to getting them being to wait for the weekly store to update, where they probably won't be offered. Dragonball has no paywall skills, and the worst drop rate is 1% (not 0.01% or something), which is still annoying if you specifically want one skill in particular... but plenty of them are not unique, and can easily be switched with a more common/non-drop skill. EDIT: now the lowest is 0.625% after they added more.It has a clear negative where you can't solely queue for raider, and you have to play survivor for some matches before being given raider. That does suck. But in a 1v7 game, the queue times would be crazy long otherwise. It probably should change in some form though, because people do intentionally kill themselves to get through matches to be given their raider game... which they probably won't get to play for long, as there's a chance people will suicide the match there too.As for the game itself, it's glorified hide & seek. I like it, but others wouldn't. *Especially* if punishing yourself with solo queue survivor games on Dead By Daylight isn't a preference of theirs.

_childDocuments_.review: At it's core there's a fun game here but sadly it's let down by several points.While fair on a basic level, there is a major balance issue on both sides, with survivor teams being able to sweep entire games without the Breaker so much as lay an eye on them the entire match, and some of the breakers being hideously broken. This issue encourages the toxic play style of both sides as you are battle necked into the behaviour just to even have a chance of a worth while game. Patchs only make the issue worse for one side or the other.Then we have the Breaker hounds. People desperate to be the Breaker, even with the new system, who join matchs just to dip out as they start in order to play as the Breaker faster. As a result half your team can be gone before the match has even started. Then there's the micro-transactions and gacha system. If you've got money to burn its fine, but if you don't then you likely never going to get any of the better Dragon Souls anytime soon and fat chance of ever getting the more pricey cosmetics without hours of wasted time. In fact after a certain point the game doesn't, or at least rarely, give you the type you currency you need for such items.And that is in itself another issue. The game has four types of currency spread between the shop, gocha (which has multiple types of tickets also) and skill level up. Combined that with the games ever shrinking player base and their is little incentive to get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game went from an amazing concept to a horrible execution in the span of 1 1/2 years. Season 1 gave us the ability to play full games w/ friends as the killer so you would have a great time. But later on, the game ended up focusing on micro-transactions for Raider voice lines and cosmetics that used to be purchasable with Zeni (the free game currency). They removed playing killer w/ friends to combat people farming zeni and raider experience while giving players a report system that barely works along with a Block button which defeated the whole purpose of getting rid of Raider w/ friends since you could have just ended up blocking and reporting people if they were teaming with and feeding the killer.Later on we got cross-play, but whoever decided to add in Region and Coastal lock deserves to have his head examined for scientific study since it defeated the whole purpose of having it in the first place. It literally made grouping with friends impossible if they lived in different regions of the world, and even MORE impossible if they lived on the other side of the United freaking States. I shouldn't have to perform TSA screenings to see if one of my friends can play with me and we can find games.Skills being locked behind a horrible gacha system with NO PITY is also a huge negative from me since other games with a gacha system actually gives you something to spend your summoning currency on along with an ACTUAL pity system. By the time you use your currency maxing out all of your actives/passives, you'll still be left with a crap-ton with nothing to spend it on. At least let us use a certain amount to purchase Transpheres and skills we haven't been able to get through this horrible gacha system.Lastly, the survivor dodging nerfs, along with having NO SUPPLIES DROPS if the killer is at level 2, was a terrible decision because it encouraged certain killers (Goku Black) to purposely stay at that level just to gain a huge advantage of winning if you weren't in a premade group that actually worked.I loved this game to death, but it brings nothing but stress and frustration now with the recent changes. Not to mention the ranked matches system is completely stupid. You will find players literally feeding themselves to play killer and later on purposely camp you and keep games hostage all for a mid shirt and little to no summoning currency. A casual game like this does NOT need to be competitive. Oh well, guess I'll just play Sparking Zero in the future and watch from afar whenever this game decides to die.Update on Season 7: This game still sucks and the 2nd Anniversary brought us not only a worst raider than the last, but also LESS content than last season! No new Raider voicelines in the Dragon Pass and all new Raider voicelines are all TP only. I don't think I'll be returning to this game any time soon unless Bandai/Dimps decides to treat the players like they give a damn and rewards them as such.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't. Just don't. Save your money. I played this game for a solid 40+ hours and got this product for free from a friend. When I tell you this game is so horrendous I'm planning on refunding HIM the 20 bucks he spent to get me this game, that says something. I already removed this game from my account on top of that. TLDR, this game is so broken, unfinished and janky that even playing with friends sucks. This game is not worth even 5 dollars. Literally save your money and get Dead By Daylight if you really like asymmetrical games.Raider Experience:So, I guess they made some changes as of 2023. Cell has now gone from hardest to 2nd easiest killer, overshadowed by Broly who requires zero brainpower to use. What I mean is Cell barely needs any civilian kills or survivor drains to reach level 4. At level 3 cell only needs 3 civvies, or 2 survivors. Cause someone at the dev team said "lets let Cell get to level 4 in 4 minutes flat." yes, this has happened numerous times. As for Broly, just dump all your points into Gigantic Rush. That's it. If a Broly knows spawn-points, he just gigantic rushes to one of the survivor spawn-points and just goes to town. Combine that with immediate level 2 putting survivors at a heavy disadvantage and you're almost always losing to broly players. Oh and can't forget he can actually zoom around the entire map in about 4-5 minutes flat. Mhm, balanced. Combat:Combat is still so janky and busted, it feels like I'm more playing Dragon Ball Legends than I am an actual combat system. Most of the time Survivors/Killers are launching attacks that don't even HIT THEIR TARGET, and yet the person on the receiving end of the attack will still take damage, despite a Special Beam Cannon whiffing past their target. On top of that some moves are so poorly unbalanced that some moves just have insane damage numbers at LVL 3 for survivor, making other options obsolete. As of 2023 though? The PTW system has completely taken hold and if you don't have the meta skills and you're up against a decent Broly or Cell? Your loss is guaranteed. New players are completely, utterly ******.Survivors:Nowadays, I guess Survivors did get some hard nerfs, considering how easy it is nowadays for raiders to get full sweeps. If a survivor doesn't know what they're doing, even though it's not their fault, the matchmaking will throw them into S rank lobbies cause the playerbase is so low they need to fill in the gaps somehow, right?Matchmaking:This game is so dead you will go against the same players for HOURS. ******* HOURS?! Nevermind that, the system loves to lie about Raider Ranks. Example, you're up against a Cell player, it says level 56, A5 rank. You play the match, get curb-stomped, and see on the results that Cell was level 56, Z2....seriously?All in all, from 2022 to 2023, this game has not improved. Instead it somehow found a way to get worse? Didn't think it possible, but considering we have Z5 rank broly's that are just one trick ponies, a now fully filled out gacha PTW system that fully dooms new players, and matchmaking that just straight up lies to you about the raider's rank and also puts gold and diamond survivors against Z Rank raiders at lvl 100....yeah, this game in 1 year has continued to hold it's title of worst game of 2023 by a landslide.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Dragonball, this was a perfect way for me to introduce myself to Dead by Daylight -style multiplayer.My Finnish review of the game from December 2022 (game had been out for a month or so): It is easy to jump in for a hour or two of quick matches, then get back to whatever you were supposed to do on your day. Which is pretty nuts considering the game having limited player pool due to the lack of crossplay. Yet somehow we keep meeting people who have a lot of levels on a Raider that might've come out last week, even though you'd have to have at least half an hour of games as survivor to have even single game as Raider... and maybe get one level since you were outplayed by veteran Survivors.The game has Battle Pass, cosmetics and other unlockables you CAN pay real money for, but most of the time you unlock stuff just by playing, especially when showered with regular EXP and Zen boost campaings.You can't skip tiers on the Pass so to unlock anything from it, you have to simply play. Only P2W aspect of the game would be the gacha transformations, but even those can be opened with ingame currency.Pros:- The setting makes sense, taking place in Xenoverse continuation of DB series.- Lots of references to DB series.- Soundtrack delivers what it needs.- When you get the good runs as Survivor/Raider. Mainly because of the matchmaking.- Matchmaking? What is that? (as the time of writing)- Game mechanics are simple to understand, yet satisfying to master.- Just by playing you might never have to spend another cent on the game after initial purchase.- Somewhat consistent updates to balance and gameplay.- Some form of dedication to keep content coming in has been displayed.Cons:- NO CROSSPLAY (as the time of writing)- Visuals are somewhat last gen-ish. I'm talking about PS3/Xbox 360-ish, not PS4/Xbone.- Wonky connection from time to time. Not sure if the game is P2P or server-based.- Matchmaking? What is that? (as the time of writing)- When you get the bad runs as Survivor/Raider. Mainly because of the matchmaking.- Game might feel grindy at times.- No consistent content updates, only ETAs (as the time of writing).- When playing in group smaller than 8 players, no one in group can't play as the Raider (as the time of writing). The lack of crossplay hinders the chances for custom games.Final Verdict:Game mainly has been targeted to the fans of Dragonball, especially ones with soft spot for Dead by Daylight -style of asymmetrical multiplayer games. If no further dedication is planned after initial purchase, I'd recommend waiting for a sale. Probably better pick for full prize with a larger group of friends, at least after cross-play may be introduced (as the time of writing)

Now, If the raider is above level 1, then the survivor loses. Virtually nothing more to say about it.Above all else, it committed  the most grievous sin in gaming , It is not fun. _childDocuments_.review: A perfect example of a great idea poorly executed.  That is the best way I can summarize this game after playing it for nearly 90+ hours.  The premise for the game is simple, it's an asymmetrical multiplayer game where you play as either the survivor or the raider.  The goal of the Survivor is to escape while the goal of the Raider is to eliminate everyone.  Seems simple enough but there are multiple ways of winning while playing as the survivor and this is where things kind of fall apart.  There are times that even while playing as the Raider, it's possible to get bullied by a well-coordinated team of Survivors.  Which I feel kind of goes against the whole point of the game.  However, this is the least of the game's problems.  One major issue I have with this game are its microtransactions.  The aggressive pricing of the items in the shop are appalling and on top of that there is a gacha mechanic which houses the best abilities in the game.  There is no other way of acquiring these specific moves unless you pull them using tickets, using the free coins from playing matches or the games premium currency (which requires real money or is drip fed to players through the battle pass).  Some summon banners only let you use tickets or the premium currency which is kind of scummy.  Despite my issues with the microtransactions there is another issue that hurts this game.Before the implementation of cross play, matchmaking times were abysmal and there are times where I had to wait over 30 minutes for a match to start.  Cross play appears to have fixed this, but I haven't played the game in a couple of months and not sure how things are now.  However, this was one issue that I had with the game and since this game is multiplayer online, a healthy online population is a must for consistent games to happen.  Due to the popularity of Dragon Ball, I'm sure that will keep people engaged but for how much longer?  I know that I've been mostly negative so far but let's talk about the things I did like.I like that you are able to create your own character or use already established Dragon Ball characters such as Bulma, Oolong and chi-chi.  Each character has their own unique abilities they can use in matches which is kind of a nice touch.  So, in other words, it's more than just a skin and I like the attention to detail on the moves they use.  Created characters can use pretty much any move you have unlocked however the create options are kind of weak.  If you are used to create-a-character having a ton of options, then you are going to be disappointed.  I also like the way the Raiders (Villains) moves are implemented in this game and makes sense for each of the Raiders currently in the game.   However, I should point out that it does seem some Raiders are better than others.  One final thing I do want to point out are the various stages that are currently available in the game.  Personally, I feel that there should be a lot more variety in the number of stages in the game.  There just simply isn't enough and you will be seeing the same stages over and over again in a single gaming session.  However, what is currently available is good and gives the players a mix of the various locations in the Dragon Ball universe.  Alright, let's go ahead and wrap this up.Dragon Ball The Breakers has an excellent concept and could have turned out to be a truly amazing game.  The business model currently implemented in the game has hurt it a bit and the lack of balance between the Raiders and Survivors is a huge issue for me.  I did buy this game day one and even managed to 100% all achievements in the game but was ultimately left unsatisfied.  Only buy this game if you're a fan of Dragon Ball, multiplayer games like Dead by Daylight or it's on a steep discount.  As someone that really wanted to like this game, it pains me to write this.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game as a lifelong fan of Dragon Ball Z and related medias as well as asymmetrical games like Dead By Daylight (1.4k hours on DBD at the time of this review). The concept of this game is amazing but isn't quite there yet in terms of gameplay, a multitude of issues prevent the game from being a worthy rival to DBD. Balance issues, character variety and the role queues come to mind on issues with this game. As of the time I'm writing this review their are only 3 raiders and 14 transpheres to pick from for survivors and killer respectively. With time this issue will be solved but currently the game can feel somewhat repetitive with the limited character pool. To queue into a match you select which role you prefer and it finds a match however unlike DBD the game forces you to play survivor games before you can play as killer. While in concept this isn't horrible to keep the queue times shorter the main issue is that you have to play anywhere between 2-9 survivor games in order to play as killer typically falling in the 5-7 area. This results in some survivors throwing because they want to get out of games asap to play as killer and a bad taste in your mouth for killer mains. Lastly the balance has been the biggest dealbreaker for most people playing this game as the devs have been swinging back and forth on who gets buffs and nerfs heavily catering one side in a patch rendering the other much weaker than the buffed side. It can be frustrating playing survivor as some killers just decide to camp as their isn't a penalty to it and when teammates refuse to play together and while on the contrary playing killer can be very frustrating due to survivors getting the dragon balls really quick due to knowing where they spawn and being beat up by a group of survivors. Overall I have a lot of fun with the game and do recommend it especially for the $20 price tag and 100% if its on sale. Just be aware of these issues before buying.TLDR: Game is fun casually and good for the price however it has its issues mainly being game balance

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now? I'd say give it a try and refund it if you don't like it. Ideas: - Raditz & Nappa as Levels 1-2 & 3-4 respectively? Or make them their own raiders (which would probably work better and gives you more content than just releasing one new raider) - Ginyu Force. The player could have the option to customize a member for each level with Ginyu always being Level 4? (One member would constantly sit out though) Or have it go Guldo>Recoome>Burter>Jeice>Ginyu from Levels 0-4. Guldo could throw stuff around to level up? I don't know. Pros: - Feels good to be Raider (when you get him). It makes you really FEEL like you're a genocidal maniac.  - Teamwork as Survivor feels great as well. Especially with teammates that do the same. - Customization is a tad lacking, but honestly, is fine for what it is. (I've seen others compare it to Xenoverse's customization) - Gameplay is overall fun. - Devs LOVE fanservice. Open Beta survey talked about the idea of Pilaf & Gang, Commander Red, General Blue, Turtle, Satan, and others joining for Survivor skins. I think that's a really great idea to keep engagement going. They seem to care more than your typical developer. - It's only about $25 which isn't too bad, all things considered. Cons: - The game feels unbalanced with the Raiders winning 99% of matches. Maybe I'm just unlucky and every single match I'm pitted with below average teammates or a tryhard raider. - I dislike that there's microtransactions in a paid game, but you can get that currency for free AND the battle pass is completely free, so it's hard for me to stay too upset at that. I do think the currency you do get isn't much. I played for 9 hours today and got a total of 5 matches as raider out of an approximate 30-40 and could only pull on the gacha about 10-15 times with the currency I had (excluding the tickets). - That goes into my next point about queue times. I don't know how they'd fix it, since they added "priority" since the Open Beta, but that doesn't stop said queue to often going above 4. - They removed the ability to spam voice lines, so now I can't hear Frieza say "I'm going to blow you". - Crashes. _childDocuments_.review: I went into this game expecting a unique Dragon Ball experience that would be fun to pick up and play on occasion. I watched a bit of the beta gameplay online and it seemed like a big change from the commonplace fighting games in the franchise.Honestly... I've been having way more fun than I expected. I read a number of reviews first, and the common gripes people have are the gacha element, the nerfing of the Survivors' Z-warrior power-ups, and the massive difficulty curve for newcomers.I'm gonna say this right now... A big con is that the raider can and will camp your downed allies, even from a slight distance. But a big pro is that (at least so far) you will find that allies frequently take the time to heal you when you're downed, simply because we're all in this together and need all the help we can get. It makes a lot more sense to save an ally (usually not right away though) than to leave them to die. Beware though... if you're downed a second time, it's instant death and that's game over for you. At which point, you can safely just leave the match and start up a new one without any consequence!I just want to say... the gacha system seems fine. Whether you win or lose (and even if you withdraw from a match after you're killed and can't be revived), you still earn currency that can be used to buy anything you want from the shop. All the game wants is for you to keep playing. At the time I'm writing this, nothing is locked behind premium currency (yet).Nerfing the Z-warriors so they can only land a few hits on the raider before reverting back makes a lot of sense and was very necessary imo. There's a lot of strength in numbers and when survivors hit you with a barrage of different tricks to hold you in place and then continue to launch the next attack in a blaze of teamwork, the raider is at a massive disadvantage if these survivors have a huge defense level. Once a survivor is about to run out, they should prepare an escape... and if they're lucky, the raider won't chase them down or land a perfect long-range shot to knock them out. Cooldown drinks and late game supplies to level the playing field really help make up for this. The raider feels like this dominant force throughout most of the game... but the devs made sure there's a realistic possibility for a comeback near the end. In fact, if the raider does extraordinarily well at the beginning and wipes out too many allies, the game's objective will change and give you an option to find a time machine to flee the timeline instead of performing the team-based goal you all originally set out to do. It's all very well thought out and the execution is pretty great.Lastly, the difficulty curve... The matchmaking in this game prioritizes ping and seemingly does NOTHING to prioritize player level range, so you'll find all kinds of mixes with levels 1-10 lumped together with levels as high as 50-70. There's no balance anywhere, it throws any player in with any other, as long as they're close by. But if you take time to learn the game and study the players' movements... maybe even stick around and spectate instead of instantly withdrawing... you'll get a real feel for the game and can learn all the ins and outs in no time (it's a little harder to figure out how to play as the raider though, since they have a radically different approach and require a very different strategy... and you can only play as them 1/6 of the time). The guarantee that you can play as raider after every 5 or 6 games by maintaining a priority level that goes up by 1 with each completed game (and the ability to just gracefully leave the match whenever you're dead, which still counts toward boosting priority level) is pretty fair though imo. When there are 8 players and only 1 raider, it's really all we can reasonably ask for.My favorite thing about this game is that it doesn't feel like mindless fighting... with all the gadgets and humans doing all they can to survive, it feels like the original Dragon Ball. I don't feel the same thing I felt from playing every other DBZ game... This is a more grounded, special feeling where you either have a sense of camaraderie with your allies and feel a unique kind of tension whenever the raider draws near.... OR you feel mightier and more menacing than ever before as a DBZ villain than in any DBZ game ever made so far. It sounds hard to believe since these are Xenoverse graphics, but you actually feel like you're blowing apart the planet with vast reserves of power for once.I've been enjoying this new feeling a lot, and learning to get better at the game can be so rewarding. If you botch your turn as a raider, it's a massively frustrating experience... but winning the game with your team (and especially winning as the raider) is a fantastic feeling that keeps us all coming back for more!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the biggest cases of missed opportunity I have ever played.The core gameplay for both sides is a steep learning curve, however once you get it down it is incredibly fun as Survivor and Raider.I played this game since its first beta and every season since launch, and it is my favourite live service game to ever release. However the development team has continued to make awful decision season after season to such an extreme that it seems almost as if to self sabotage the game's success.My friend's and I had a great time playing with and against each other during the betas to the point I bought the game for myself and about 8 other friends. In season 1 the game had balance issues and a handful of toxic players who would sabotage the game or have offensive player names, and no method to block or report players except through Steam itself.Season 2 removed the ability to play against your friends unless you did not want to earn any resources from in game events or any currency to acquire new skills, super attacks,characters or cosmetics in their gacha system (which has no pity system) or their shop. Instead they added a role select for each role and only survivor would let you play with other players you know, but then that immediately did not work and instead of reverting the system until it was fixed just made it so you would have to play flex or survivor (But hey it added a report system, which did not do anything and still does not).Season 3 added a new map that half of it was nearly identical to a map added in season 2, did not fix the broken queue system they changed to at the launch of season 2 and had a long extension due to a delay on season 4 which was really grating on the community since the raider added in season 3 (Ginyu Force) at the time was easily the strongest in the game and could be very easily overwhelming to less experienced players.Season 4's announcement was hugely exciting since it was the anniversary of the game and promised that the game would be adding crossplay in the future being able to unite the small communities that have been made across all platforms. HOWEVER it also added a region lock to the game meaning that the community that had formed in the first year of the game could no longer play with a large percentage of the player base if they were from other regions as the friends they made on the game and increasing the queues on the game to an average of 5-15 minutes (you cannot do anything in the game while queued for a match). It also added a forced ranked mode which made the general community far more toxic on average since the game was now more "competitive" and they cared about the funny number letter combination next to their name. This lead not only to toxic gameplay increasing immensely having almost every match involve the raider hard body camping a player when they would get a down (sending the survivor back to a likely 15 minute queue if they got unlucky early on) or players who only wanted to play raider intentionally dying in the matches as survivor to up their priority as raider faster and making it harder for the other survivor players in the lobby. Also the general community becoming far angrier and toxic in discussion on the game to the point that a large amount of players would get mad at other players if they played with anybody they knew in their queue (because it was OP to play with friends I guess). It also did not add any additional story to the single player mode of the game, which is not a particularly exciting mode anyways but did add changes to the lobby every previous season upon its completion adding new dialogue and advancing an ongoing story line.Season 5 finally added the awaited Crossplay to the game which was a great opportunity to bring the communities together, but it did not revert the region lock changes keeping certain areas isolated still. As a matter of fact not only did they not let the community return together but mid way through the season they added additional restrictions to "coast lock" the game meaning that you could only match up with players if they were not just close enough to your location but also in the same region. The removal of cross region play was likely in an effort to make connections smoother between players however there really wasn't a major issue with this before the change and connections only became awful consistently when players who unsurprisingly wanted to play with the friend's they made in the community had to start using vpns to do so which usually worsened their connection. What was far worse for connections though was certain abilities and actions in game being tied to the frame rate your game was running at giving players on certain consoles (or settings on pc) an advantage to give them additional i-frames or just awful connection between other consoles at times. It also continued the forced ranked play which again is awful and majority of the players do not enjoy.But wait there's more it also added easily the most overpowered raider to date who could easily "snipe" from across map to ensure players stayed dead while not being anywhere nearby them, and was able to ignore half of their mechanics to evolve and get stronger since they were much stronger than any other character at evolution level 2 (which is guaranteed on them) stopping the mechanic they had to give the survivors a boost to fight back at later points in the game. They also raised the cost of the killer this season making the price of entry to new content higher than it was before. Yet again no new story episode.Season 6 did not add a new map to the game like every previous season, added 3 new transformations for survivors through the whole season as opposed to the 2 or 3 every few weeks each other season. The new raider Baby is also a complete newbie trap character as he is very easily beaten by experienced players but has enough mechanics to completely devastate players who are inexperienced likely killing interest of any new players who face him. He also has mechanics in his kit that can lead to uncounterable camping in the early game if he catches any survivor and the Baby player chooses to do so. They also extended the season so that we are stuck playing with no new content despite the fact that data miners found files for everything added aside from Baby back in the first season of the game. No new episode to the story either.This used to be one of my favourite games to play and I invested a lot of hours into it have met a lot of great people and made a lot of great memories with the community. It's gameplay scratches a unique itch that I don't think any other game has come remotely close to capturing and has been the only asymm I have enjoyed playing. I used to say it was absolutely worth its low price of entry but with how many awful decisions and development issues it has in addition to no communication between the devs and its playerbase I absolutely cannot recommend the game to any new players, or even justify putting in any time to it in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: As many people have stated, this game is horrible. Why?The game is p2p with gacha elements. You spend 20$+ to be forced to spend more or getting bent over until you get what you need.Speaking of the gacha, it is hugely unbalanced. Every spin costs either 15000 Zeni, a (season specific) summon pass, or 100 TP tokens. Some skills are utterly worthless while others break the game. The best example for this is Afterimage vs Energy Barrier. Afterimage lasts 2 seconds, you are vulnerable to hits, and makes you stay actionless for the entire duration.Energy barrier lasts ~5 seconds, you are invulnerable, and you are actionable for ~4 seconds.Then lets look at raider characters and see how they fareThe most recent "DLC", as written of Season 3, is Ginyu Force.He regenerates his entire health bar every time he levels up, at the cost of a bit of less maximum health. But his leveling is automatic over time, sped up by killing civilians/survivors.When you die, you rotate to the next level, missing out on some buffs you get.The buffs are from Guldo, Recoome, and Jeice+Burtur. Guldo swarms around and freezes enemies in place, Recoome acts as a free get-off-me tool, and Jeice+Burtur enhance your ranged skills at max level. They also increase your health, damage and move speed respectively on switch-out.Let's compare this to another raider, namely Cell.He only automatically generates his level at his larva state (level 1)Any damage he sustains is permanent unless if you ask Shenron for a heal, although his max HP is quite high. But this doesn't mean you can't chip out his health bar.While he does have a scouting tool in energy reading, he is still all alone to fight. His skills are also less powerful than Ginyu's solely cuz he's new.And for reference, Ginyu is 550 TP tokens while Cell is free from the start. It took me to about level 40 in game to finally even be able to unlock someone with the free TP tokens you get and that's with the starting out bonus.This is straight up powercreep and the game isn't even one year old.If you're going to make a game that you want to last, stop adding more and more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to the mix that straight up invalidates older content. If older content becomes obselete, yet the only thing new players are going to get is that old content, especially in pvp, you've made a very bad game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played close to 70 hours between all betas and let me tell you, I LOVE this game.I'll address the elephant in the room first since this is the controversial topic about this game: I think the monetization is fine - if you played Overwatch before it became Overwatch 2, the gacha feels a lot like OW lootboxes not that the rewards from the gacha are purely cosmetic but there's this feeling of "I'll just get everything if I play the game long enough" and money is just used to expedite the process if you're in a rush. Dupes in the Gacha are massively beneficial to new players too because you can use the heat currency to untie skills from skins and transpheres making your loadouts a lot more flexible. The battlepass is free and for its duration I feel it's probably easy to accomplish filling it out without spending but that is definitely too early to tell, I'm totally okay with the current model however.As for the actual review:The game is AWESOME! But it's got a bit of a learning curve, there's a lot of information management for both raiders and survivors and while the tutorial is OKAY it leaves some things to be desired.It wouldn't shock me if this is the kind of game that will have the internet flooded with "7 SURVIVORS TIPS TO IMPROVE YOUR GAMEPLAY" kinda vids because there's such a dissonance between unskilled survivors just dying every match without knowing what they should be doing or what they could've done differently to unskilled raiders not finding anyone and losing to the time machine that they weren't even remotely able to stop.So what I like about the game:- It's an unique take on DB, I love DB and I love the character fantasy of both the raider and the survivor. The devs have said only DB can really accomplish that feeling of "overwhelming difference in powers" and I think they got that down to a T. When I was telling me friend that we SHOULDN'T try to jump the raider despite both of us being Dragon Change level 3 and the Raider being level 2 it really resonated with me "This guy is really strong we're no match for him" which is a very DB Feeling.- It has a lot of skill expression and player expression, you can make many varied survivor kits that are competent and no one clear load-out triumphs over everything else even if you were to know the Raider in advance. And the cosmetics are really great, some of the stuff you can get from TP Tokens is nuts.- Raiders and Maps feel very distinct from one another, Raiders have different strengths and weaknesses and certain maps cater to that more or less. You really don't wanna run into Frieza on Highland River and Cell might be right at home on Green Coast.- Good control scheme on both Gamepad and Keyboard and Mouse (aside from the key to open the map being Enter), this seriously doesn't get talked about enough but the game feels good on both even without a lot of adjustment from switching between the two!- It's fun with randos and even funner with friends, playing on a 8-man lobby with everyone on VC is actually an experience I'd recommend to anyone.- The game itself has a lot of charm and personality, you can probably tell by the fact that Bulma, Oolong and Farmer with a Shotgun are playable but this game gives off crazy "passion project" energy where they do small details that didn't have to be added but were.This is where I'd list any negatives that irked me but truthfully there's nothing for me to complain about that won't feel nitpicky to me. Like I guess Nimbus could be faster and they overnerfed Saiyan Pod?? The game is a blast and I'm eager to recommend it and support it in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, but there are a few major issues that need to be fixed.1. Random stuttering: This seems to be caused by poor optimization, so it should be an easy fix for the dev team. I had to look up a steam guide to fix it (it's a problem held by a decent amount of the player base) but the game can cause audio tearing and frame stutters from CPU maxing.2. No team chat: For a game that require strong teamwork, there is no voice chat or text chat. Rather, you have a small selection of pre-written commands you can use. These often fall flat, as they usually take a backseat to the gameplay, as no priority is set by the game for your teammates to see these. There are graphic commands that will take priority, but are often used for memeing.3. Raider Lag: The lobby you play in is a non-dedicated server (or at least operates like one) set  by whoever is the raider. The game will lag if the Raider is lagging, and one way to tell this is if the 15 minute game timer itself is lagging. If it's lagging, the Raider is lagging, and now all your inputs will lag until either the lag stops, the Raider dies, or they DC.I will update this review with any further issues or fixes that may come.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say I love this game...but i can't and its sad because the concept it decent but the execution is where this game falls flat.So i'm gonna segment this into 3 parts: Gameplay, graphics, and final thoughtsGraphics:It looks and plays like a game straight out of DragonBall Zenoverse 1 and 2 and I'm willing to bet the dev team merely copied and pasted assets which isn't a bad thing especially since the game's theme is quite literally the same, that is to say dragonball themed.Gameplay:Okay so this is gonna be a loaded segment in a way... so for starters its no shock people are comparing this to dead by daylight however unlike dead by daylight, survivors have far more powerful tools at their disposal to defend themselves in the form of spirit transformations that grant them the powers of iconic dbz characters, albeit temporarily. Killers on the other hand take on the form of one of three classic major villains from the dbz series, Cell, Freeza, and Majun Buu.The gameplay loop in this game is to power 6 generators, wait, no, got that wrong, use 6 keys to activate different relay points for a super time machine, all joking aside the concept is incidental to dead by daylight's with a few key differences being there is more than one win condition.  Surviors can win in one of 2 ways, activating all relays to power up the time machine or defeat the killer and unlike Friday the 13th, this isn't nearly as risky or hard to pull off for even the most noobish of teams assuming things go well for them which leads into the next part...The biggest problem with this game and why I can't say I love it is that it suffers from the same design flaw that most asymmetrical games of this type do, they can't balance the game so it adheres to all skill levels instead of either just top skilled players or new players.This leads to EVERY SINGLE MATCH playing out in one of 3 ways:1. Killer wipes the floor with the survivors with an easy win in under 10mins.2. Survivors get all relays powered up and power up the super time machine in under 5mins.3. Survivors find all 7 dragonballs, power themselves up to power level 3, summon shenron, get a power level 4 character blast the killer through 5 mountains 6 or seven times until he's dead in under 5mins. Okay, that last part is an exaggeration, you can't blast the killer through 5  oh no, they totally can murder the killer in under 5mins EASILY! that part wasn't an exaggeration. :PThe outcome is NEVER ANY DIFFERENT than these three and outcomes two and three occur ten times more often than outcome one. Now you can see the major problem with this game. Where as Dead By Daylight has found a middleground as of late(giving killers much needed buffs to no longer be a joke). This game is still in its infancy with survivors being over powered in a skilled players hands while even the most skilled of killers will struggle to edge out a win against most teams as it only takes 2 or 3 skilled players on a single survivor team to defeat the killer or get all keys powered up due to knowing the layout of most maps and what items to get first.And if all 6 players are skilled? Killer may as well put their controller down and/or walk away from the keyboard because they are not winning, PERIOD.This game needs a balancing overhaul in the worst way or some new mechanic that can give killers an edge when the odds are against them, I'm not in charge of developing this game so i don't know what the devs have planned but they need to act and SOON or this game is going to die.Hell for all we know it may have been sent out to die to begin with as a cash grab since there's one last thing I have neglected to mention:This game contains a gacha system. For the uneducated, a Gacha system is an interface you spend in game currency or paid currency(currency bought with real world money) for a set number of chances to obtain rare and valuable items known as "souls" which are used in game for survivor transformations. The items promoted on the front page of these gacha interfaces are NOT GUARANTEED TO DROP.  This means you could spend potentially hundreds of real world dollars just to get the soul you want but that's not the worst part, no, the worst part is, even if you get the soul you want, YOU DON'T NECESSARILY GET THE COMPLETE PACKAGE in a single 11 pull as these soul items contain the soul of the character and either one passive trait or Special attack on the given soul you collect.This means you have to spend EVEN MORE REAL WORLD MONEY to perform potentially MANY, MANY, MORE 11 drop pulls on this gacha system to get a COMPLETE SOUL. This system is beyond predatory which leads me to believe this game is a cash grab and nothing more.A shame too, yet another game with great potential destroyed by corporate greed...Or it could not be a cash grab and the devs may well fix the game, who knows?

_childDocuments_.review: The game is hilariously unbalanced, and a bit greedy with not too much content on launch.Playing survivor is fun for a bit but it gets boring due to the raider being so under powered and cheesable. Playing with friends as a party game is perfectly fine and fun.The game has a cosmetic shop, battlepass and its a gatcha to top it off, seems like most of the effort went into moneymakery than actual gameplay and balance. it should honestly be free, not 20$ or 30$.Honestly, unless your a masochist, i wouldn't bother with raider, its a very very survivor sided game. The matchmaking has a few issues, you can only choose priority for a role instead of a designated que, so you basically need to get lucky if you want to play the raider. On average id say i got about 5 survivor to 1 raider games. This causes a weird imbalance with leveling, with survivors generally being significantly more leveled than the raider. you upgrade skills when you level, so the L100 survivor is likely going to have a lot more and better tools than a L5 Raider. KI blast spam is pretty toxic in the current version, The raider being able to deny a wish by destroying the zone and sending the dragonballs to the middle is annoying. Bulmas Escape bike is very broken. Since the game currently doesn't have a lot of characters, i can only assume they are going to be added in future banners/summons. If you've ever played a gatcha then you'll understand the worry of power creep and P2W becoming the norm as they add to the game. Feels like a mobile game made for PC with DBZ slapped on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I enjoy this game but I can't recommend you buy it. I'll continue playing Breakers until it gets shut down (which probably isn't too far off) but you have to know that it is very limited on available players to be matched with. There is a region matchmaking system, I can only play with players on the east coast of the US and there aren't too many left. You will see similar people over and over, there are a few premade groups running meta skills and sometimes they purposely down rank themselves to pick on newer raiders. The gacha skills are, of course, luck of the draw and there are some that are very powerful. If you missed past seasons (like me) you missed out on some of the best meta skills/passives that you don't have an opportunity to get unless they do a special limited board. The resources required to do skill draws are too expensive given how long it takes to match up for a game so that is supposed to push people to buy microtransactions. Just don't buy this game unless you've seen people play it and you REALLY liked the gameplay loop. I got it for about $7.50 USD and I'd say I've got my fun out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game in concept is fun and could be a blast to play. Bandai has put in way too many downsides for this to be a good purchase.Progression:I'll start off with the main progression system, which isn't to bad for raiders but absolutely horrid for survivors. For survivors to progress in skillsets and abilities they have to go through a gacha system. Which can absolutely ♥♥♥♥ you over. Even being in 2/3 beta test I didnt unlock all of the content they provided. It doesn't help that even if you do amazing in a match and get diamonds across the board the cap for zeni gained per match is 4k meaning youll have to do 4 perfect matches in a row to get 1 gacha pull. The average match as a survivor if you are decent you should get around 2.6k-3.4k so it would be even longer to get a pull. Not to mention you can only outright buy super skills from the vault. So you have to rng and hope you are lucky enough to get the active skills and passive skills you want from the gacha system. I also have a bad feeling the gacha system will have a heavy monetary system imbedded into it self making it have a clear p2w system which is normally just in f2p games. If this game was f2p i would have no problem with it. It doesnt help either that i feel this is how they are gonna go since during the first closed beta the gacha pull price was a lot lower. So yes the gacha system is very important for survivors but needs to be removed since its their only way of true progression. It needs to be replaced with just having the ability to outright buy certain things or even allowing us to use ingame currency to get tickets which would be a guaranteed pull. Other than that raiders seem fine in their current state of progression.Balancing:As of right now the game is heavily raider favored especially since bandai thought it would be a good idea to buff the raiders by giving them a big damage boost along with major damage reduction. As of now the only real way for survivors to put damage on the raider is by coming as a team and stunlocking them. Some raiders complained about this yet they don't know they have 2 abilities that can get them out of the stunlock with ease. Its a clear showing of how a skilled raider can differ so much from a newbie raider. While for survivors even fighting a newbie raider can still be hard fighting a skilled raider grants a near impossible chance of winning unless they get super lucky with the rng and get the super time machine out really quick. I'll recommend some fixes and quality of life improvements for both sides at the end.Cosmetics:Cosmetics are honestly in a great state and I loved the style they went with for both survivor and raider. Funny enough it still raider sided as well. For base clothes for your cac can be earned at semi reasonable prices, but for transpheres you have to hope you get lucky with that damn rng system sadly. For raiders your cosmetics come from leveling and the shop as well it gives some amazing color alts that change each transformation which i love, they seem to unlock every 15 levels as well so i expect to see some amazing variations for you guys. Now the funpart for raiders voicelines which can all be obtained in the shop all have fair prices and if you are like me you like to mess with people every now and then and spam a line or 2. All be it finally the last thing to talk about with cosmetics are emotes and victory poses along with intro poses + stamps. I love em all since they add a lil bit of flavor to each survivor. Only thing id ask is to be able to use the emotes while in matches as well for when you get a nice lil stun off to taunt the raider lel.Suggestions + Quality of life Improvements:I'll start with this either make the game f2p and keep the gacha system or keep your price tag and remove the gacha system. I'd much rather have the gacha system removed entirely for a system based on leveling and or just being able to outright buy the things you want with in game currency.Onto balance changes as of right now i feel like the survivor stunlock is needed and raiders even have an escape for this so i believe it is fine. I am also fine with the damage reduction they have received but the damage boost they got needs to be reverted. A Level 2 raider can 3-4 shot a level 3 survivor.Survivor Improvement, the first thing id say needs ot be changed for them is the revive system not really changed but more so an addition. To which i must recommend the ability to carry downed survivors to a safe spot maybe even bringing them into a saiyan pod with you for a quick escape to revive them somewhere safe, This would help the system a ton and fair since it already takes forever revive an ally especially if you are the only one doing it. Sliding should be something survivors can do at any point in time and not be an ability that takes up a passive slot. Finally change power while transformed should be a lil bit slower, and using supers should not drain energy instead they should only be able to be used with how high your change level is if you are change level 1 you can use it once level 2 twice and level 3 three times, Level 4 shoudl stay the same and be able to be used as many times as you want since it has a special requirement. The last 2 things i will recommend for them are barriers take 2 hits and allow the ability to upgrade things such as power charge and grapple. Giving them unique additions when mastered. For power charge it can level you from 0-2 slowly when mastered. For grapple its range is increased along with speed and its cd decreased.Raider improvements raiders dont really need much right now i feel they are in a great state currently only thing they have ot worry about are stunlocks which can be escaped with abilities. But they will be get some nice benefits from the item changes i'll recommend.For items like the senzubean survivors should be able to use it after they have been fully downed by the raider. In return the raiders should be able to use senzu beans to recover a small portion of health like half a single bars worth for each one they find. I also believe raiders should be able to use the standard cooldown drinks to regain an ability on cooldown back quickly.Overall the game is a great concept but needs some major changes to reach its full potentialalso making a post about the full review since i could add everything.

_childDocuments_.review: game gud (scroll down to the bottom for a minimized review)I personally haven't run into cheaters, so idk why I saw a few reviews about cheaters, I wont deny the possibility that they exist, game needs a report system 100% though, ques are fast.I agree the rng banner system is kinda stupid, I don't mind it though seeing as minimum you get for doing something "good" (finding a power key, rescuing a civilian, setting a key, fighting the raider, rescuing another survivor etc) in a match is 1000 zeni, and the most I've gotten is around 6k, so the 15k per summon isn't really that bad if you know how to play.So to explain this next part I'll have to include the a few facts:I have a 4k monitor with 240 refresh rate, and a modern pc with the modern specs of the 3090 series (a damn good pc, god I love this thing)  lastly I have over 12,000 hours in xenoverse 2 on the Nintendo switch, PC, and psn combined, know every combo, have played and mastered every character that's in the game, and have 100% progress in each(can someone please shut bulma tf up? I'm in pain) Now moving on to the reason that that I added this part for. I've seen a lot of complaints of the models looking way too much like xenoverse 2's models, while it is true they look very similar they are by no means the same, the models in breakers are higher quality, and are shaded properly, and have great pixel density, I've made several models for the game vrchat in blender(around 300 or so) I know a different model when I see it, however I won't deny that some assets were likely imported from their other dragon ball games, what dev doesn't do that? it saves time for newer gamesSo to reiterate the game is by no means bad, it has a few flaws, that can easily be fixedit 100% needs a report system if it wants to last, easy anti-cheat wont stop all things from getting though, the devs need to realize that, game rewards you for playing like a game should etc, game good, 3.9/5 stars

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game anymore to anyone. Not that I was particularly fond of it to start with, but it felt at least playable, and moderately enjoyable in season 1. But as time goes on the gatcha becomes more intrusive, the pressure to use your TP to purchase everything, and the Daily/Weekly quest structure all become very tiresome. I'm no longer excited when new things come out, because it's impossible to get most of them just by playing the game. The way they want to peel back your patients and break into your wallet really gets old after a while. The Gameplay loop is simple, and was fun at one point, but now all the survivors who do play, just use the same builds, so playing as a raider isn't very fun. Meanwhile as a survivor the deluge of players using the meta have made raiders much more aggressive. They are less willing to leave a downed player, and chase people across the map. The game really needs some re balancing, some less intrusive currency systems and in general some more content to really be worth investing your time and money into.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.But I also hate it's balance.I love its concept and design.I hate its pace and implementation.I love the idea.I hate the result.This game is in a state of chaos. I do not see it lasting for long in its current state.I really love the game, don't get me wrong. Many many hours in the betas and now in the main game, as the numbers slowly dwindle through frustration, I find myself increasingly frustrated with what remains:No anti cheat that actually works. Easy Anti Cheat is a piss poor service at best and does not actually catch anyone clearly using any form of cheating scripts. It is extremely common place now that if you find a high level raider, over 50% of the time they'l be using wall 'hacks' to see where you are at any time. No way to hide. Defensive skills are easily interrupted by the raider.Balance is a huge issue. Between raiders with hitscan spam, level 1 Spopovitch's taking on entire teams of 2-3 level survivors and being fine, and massive balance differences between Cell, Frieza and Buu.Theres no report system. No punishment for cheating.The matchmaking only works from one region at a time. If you and a friend are from two regions, the matchmaking will not work properly and will then start looking for other groups that have friends from the same TWO regions. Meaning you'l rarely if any time get a game played. So you need to use a VPN to pretend to be from another region.Then Easy Anti Cheat will randomly kick you for authentication timeouts if you use a VPN. So you're kinda ♥♥♥♥ out of luck if your best friend is in a different country.Ranged spam: Raiders right now can counter pretty much most aggressive survivors by flying backwards and spamming projectiles. They can fly as fast or faster than the survivors, often have multiple escapes and endless ki to flick projectiles. Most high level raiders now understand this and will never engage in close combat. You'l often see raiders spamming projectiles and flying backwards, nullifying any chance of retaliation from survivors. Even multiples of them as they will not catch up to you.Gatcha system. This will work, but only if there are actual good results beyond getting what you need. Right now there are approximately 7 characters you can unlock in the system. Once you have them, this entire system becomes just fuel for the fire currency that is used to level up skills as a survivor. Thats all it's for.Buu right now is just outright busted. From being able to insta-grab you at a distance to hold you still for a combo to two different scream-styled big aoe attacks that will go off instantly (one not so much instant but if you're going in for a melee attack you're done for as it wont stop) that do damage in a wide area.Watched Buu knock down 3 survivors trying to do the time machine by doing that instant scream after flying up to it. It downed all three of them instantly as they already had been previously damaged. Aoe defensive screams should not do damage. Frieza's doesnt, why does Buu's?Lets not forget the third form absorb everyone mode. He can camp buu. You're at relatively close quarters which can be a benefit but at that stage he is level 3 as well. It's rare all survivors will be alive at that point and nearly all of the survivors would have used their charge at this point. Even if you get out, then theres kid buu, with his genocide attack that attacks all people on the entire map requiring constant movement to avoid to his large aoe's, by the time you are at this point good luck getting further.Now yes, there is an element of teamwork involved here. A well coordinated team of survivors on voice coms can make quick work of a raider. Given the games nature however, the limitations of matchmaking and the current state of anti-cheat not even working, it's becoming increasingly rare to win without an emergency exit.Having to rely on a VPN to play with friends is frustrating.Easy Anti Cheat is booting players that are trying to play legitimately while letting script kiddies rule the roost.Balance needs to be tweaked. Cell needs to be considered the staple for balance. Raiders need to be at least somewhat skilled to beat survivors. It should not be an easy win through spamming left click as form 2 Frieza for example.There is no report system. No punishment for cheating.Somewhat-predatory battle pass system limits your progress per day. You lose out if you dont log in and play for a number of hours each day. Random 'DP' coins drop but they are super are and only 2 per day to help progression. Daily and weekly rewards are only 3 of each and each only reward a pittance. Wanna pass faster? Pay up!Clothing options are super limited and are mostly re-colors of the same. There's approximately 4 shirts, 4 pants and each are coloured. That's about everything you can get. Character customisation itself is pretty decent and allow some creative outlets. BE PREPARED TO SEE MANY ADULT GOHANS.Given what this game is using, the engine it's using and the fact all of it is pulling from the Xenoverse engine, it is baffling to see such a limited array of balance, work and content on release. It still feels like a closed beta. It plays like a closed beta.To summarise:-Sound design is great. -Being a survivor and a raider have delightfully different feels to the game but sometimes it feels kinda nasty and mean playing raider. Far too easy to win.-Graphics are solid enough, but as it's the same engine as Xenoverse things like anti-aliasing seems to be problematic and still looks a tad scratchy even when rendering at 2-4x the natural resolution and smoothing.-Balance needs a heck of a lot of work.-Matchmaking needs an overhaul. Let us choose a region. If I have a friend from a different region we should not need to use a VPN just to play together.-Disappointing lack of content. Right now, 3 raiders, 4 survivor types (one of which is at the end of the battle pass, which you gotta pay to get or play for months each day) several transformations have the exact same moves as eachother.It hurts putting this as a negative review but given we've only played it for a week and most of my friends are over it, it kinda speaks for itself.Playerbase has already dropped by half, this is fairly common for new titles but after just a week?I'm more than happy to revise this review at a later date. Right now it is the 19th of October. I will wait for more updates to see how the game shifts but I do not see myself wanting to spend much more time in it if nothing changes soon.
