_childDocuments_.review: Being someone who followed this game from its announcement up to its release, my review will end up being a little biased. Instead, I am going to list the pros and cons and things they say are going to be fixed/added, and you can make the judgement if the game is worth purchasing.Pros: The game looks very visually appealing (I personally prefer it over XV), the base mechanics feel fair and balanced, playing as Raider makes you feel very powerful, well coordinated Survivors can make anything happen, lots of options to create unique builds, cosmetic customization for those who are into that, it doesn't feel like it gets old fast, and the game is relatively cheap (due to it being essentially an asset flip with a gacha system developed over a short period of time)Cons: Connection issues, game randomly crashing, not punishing leavers enough, no cross-platform play, no option to report players, occasional cheaters (in my 100 hours I've only seen one), lack of content, most games are stomps from either side, poor in-game communication systems (only "stickers" and basic pings), gacha system that awards in-game benefits, game starts to feel unbalanced once upgrades and unlocks are thrown into the mix, tutorial is very basic and doesn't fully explain the mechanicsOne of the worst draws of the game in my opinion is the terrible in-game "communication" system. Only these "stickers" which are few and communicate only a vague emotion, and a measly four phrases you can make show up in the top right of the screen. Survivors on "comms" will nearly always have the advantage over the Raider. But in random queues, where there is no way to directly chat or communicate with your teammates, the Raider just dominates and kills any attempt at cooperation. I find myself often yelling at the screen trying to tell my teammates to drop their item that I really need or to leave a risky situation. To the developer's credit, I have seen the number of bugs go down significantly from when the game was released. They've already added new Transpheres that come with new skills and passives. They have a release schedule that goes for three seasons with what seems like a lot of content. And also, the game is pretty fun, at least for me. Getting to play as your favorite villains is a rush, especially with how many tools you're given to stomp out the Survivors. Playing as Survivor it feels just as great to finally turn on the Raider who has been terrorizing you the entire game. I recommend this game not just because I'm biased, but because I genuinely feel like this is a fun game underneath the unpolished flashy glamour. If the developers continue to improve the game as time goes on, then I expect the reviews to start to go up.

_childDocuments_.review: I keep coming back because it's cool to get a unique take on Dragon Ball. This game should be free, it is not worth five cents, nor is it worth your patience. This game should be way better. The devs are either extremely underfunded or incompetent as this game continues to reuse assets from a game that came out in 2015, and everything that isn't a reused asset is ugly. The game is incredibly unbalanced on both sides. The Raider has it WAY too easy early game, and good Survivors have it way too easy late game. The game is a buggy mess, the matchmaking is so bad that you will go against players that aren't even close to your skill or experience level, and the devs REFUSE to add cross-platform when this game NEEDS it. Pair all of these issues with the fact that progression is locked behind a pay to win gotcha system while there is very clearly a meta you either conform to or you will lose most of your matches. From the very beginning this game feels like a cash grab, and the sad part is it clearly has potential. It's an incredibly fun and unique idea for a Dragon Ball game, ruined by a absolutely horrible execution of the concept. If you want to have fun, play something else.

_childDocuments_.review: IT'S A FUN GAME! IT ISN'T PAY-TO-WIN, IT IS F2P FRIENDLY!Disregard the bot-like reviews saying "don't get this game"; "avoid this game!"; "stay away from this game!" because they have to be distributed from NPCs. The game's core mechanics is survival, yes you're capable of fighting the raider with multiple people (assuming you're all equal to or greater than the raider's currently level) but that's an alternative and not the main objective. Your main objective is to collect the keys correspondent to the area you are in. Once you've collected that area's key you set it down. Done. Rinse and repeat for 5 areas to get the Super Time Machine, which the raider can destroy. You can speed up the process by going to Area X (the spawn area for the Super Time Machine) and interacting with it. You can also prevent the Raider from destroying it by fighting him or using stun-lock moves like Charming Pose, Krillin's Shoe, Solar Flare or the Trap Device. People who complain about the gacha system of this game are delusional to believe EVERY game isn't going to have micro transactions in 2022. A handful of games do not have the whole micro transactions, kudos to them. Unfortunately this isn't one of those games. You DO NOT have to spend money in order to progress. Yes you can spend money to SPEED up the progression of your survivor's abilities but realistically there's no reason to. You'd have to invest countless dollars to even make a noticeable difference in their active and passive abilities. So the way you level up your active skills and passive skills is by going to the Hyperbolic Time Chamber and spending Super Warrior Spirits. The way to earn these super warrior spirits is by:1. performing summons and earning duplicate units that'll grant 900 Super Warrior Spirit per duplicated transphere2. playing a game (the amount you earn depends on your performance in the match. The better you do, the better your rewards)that's it. Those are the only two ways. It won't be as quick if you're a F2P player and don't want to spend money performing summons for dupes, but you can earn tickets from the FREE battlepass and you can perform summons with Zeni and TP medals (WHICH YOU GET FROM PLAYING THE GAME ALBEIT SLOWLY). You also get free rewards with the friend code system. You go to the robot, you have people input your code and voila. It's a code valid for 6 people and you can earn tickets, super warrior spirits, and tp medals. Right now I'm at 50 games played (with the friend group) and I've performed at least 3-4 free multi-summons. On that note it should be noted that your survivor's progress is different from raider's progress. Raider doesn't need any of that. He only requires matches played and leveling up, but the chances of you getting raider are pretty average. Having acknowledged the morons who can't comprehend a 20 dollar game having a gacha system (which is somewhat free to play friendly) is implemented to generate revenue for a fairly cheap game, I will say there are some issues. Having 20+ hours in the main game, and 40+ hours on the beta test, I will say the most common issue I've run into is... It is wonky at times though and can often lead to someone getting downed.- Do NOT Senzu Bean in front of the Raider. You perform an animation when you revive and that gives the raider the chance to permanently eliminate you from the game. Instead you should just drop your Senzu Beans before you die so whoever comes to revive you uses it. I don't understand why they perform an animation when revived or why they're incapable of performing any movement, but that's how it is. Also the Raider can hear you reviving a fallen survivor or hear you using a Senzu Bean.- Tracking is another issue. I've had many encounters where I am hidden well enough, or so I thought. The Raider has struck me with Ki Blast multiple times unintentionally whether it be a random Ki Blast or a stray one. - Communication system is another issue. They could've implemented a way for Survivor's to communicate with one another via scouter (the scouter is COMPLETELY useless right now. The most worthless item in the game). The signal system hardly ever works, and when it does, people are unsure of how to properly drop their item/dragon ball. It can be frustrating.- Report system... oh wait, there is none. - Raider at any level does chunks of damage to Survivor's that are a level or two ahead of them. Avoid fighting alone, it is best to fight in a group. You are fine with just a duo, but do not fight alone unless the raider is a novice or if they happen to stumble into a cave. (it's difficult for raider's to fight in a cave without an AoE move like Majin Buu's 2nd stage explosive wave). That's about it. The game runs relatively well. The combat mechanic is well-implemented, the gacha system is fine, and it appeals to the fans as well as newcomers who want something of a different pace from DBD. I recommend the game. It's fun, it's even more fun with friends. Playing alone is okay, but playing with friends is where it really provides enjoyment. The gist of this game is to survive and avoid the raider while searching for keys and/or the dragon balls. You can utilize Shenron to give everyone a one level jump from their current Charge level or you can use it to instantaneously jump to level 4. This is mostly useful if you have one other person to assist you in combat, preferably two. As Raider your job is to prevent that from happening. Simple enough. Outside of in-game objectives, you are able to purchase cosmetics, perform summons, or level up with the training facility. Queue times are short, and the game has yet to crash for me. Unsure how people are experiencing that issue with this game but hey, who am I to say?It's a fun game and for 20 bucks you can't really go wrong with it. It might be a little frustrating but what game isn't nowadays, yeah? Invest some time into it, see if you like it, if it isn't your cup of tea then it won't hurt you too much if at all. Ignore the negative reviews as most of them hardly have ANY amount of hours put into the game. Oh and make sure to read the patch notes from their twitter as it has very crucial information on the shift of the game and which direction it is going in. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ball: The Breakers is an asymmetrical PVP Hide'n'Seek game with neat action in fast paced matches.Game is truly a bliss to play, as both sides feel as weak or strong as they should like & require the same amount of strategy & quick thinking to be played successfully. There are also almost zero game stalling objectives (standing idle while holding down a button for long periods of time) which is a very common thing in similar games. Let's get into more details! The events takes place in a parallel Xenoverse universe, where Time Patroller Trunks fights Villains that come out from Temporal Seams (different timelines) in order to keep the world's balance. After creating your character, you end up being pulled by one such Seam & meet up with Trucks in a welcoming short introduction tutorial. Then the real game begins! First of all, rounds follow a 7 versus 1 (citizens vs Raider) archetype and they last up to 15 minutes. Maps are pretty massive & split into 6 smaller territories (A-B-C-D-E & X which is the central one), each having a different theme, such as cities like west town & capsule city, underground caves, diveable lakes & rivers, the "let's fight somewhere empty" field, Frieza's enormous spaceship and more. As a Citizen (survivor) your task is to explore those areas & rescue NPC citizens beforethe Villain finds them, collecting equipment such as various tracking radars, senzu beans, rocket launchers, gold chucks to buy stuff from vending machines, bikes to explore faster &most importantly, finding power keys to call & power up the time machine which will sent the Raider back to their timeline. When all power keys are, the time machine arrives at the center of the stage and you have to manually power it up or keep the Raider busy so your teammates can do it for you.You always start at 0 level, in which you're completely powerless if spotted by the Raider, & you gain levels by power cubes which you find by either from rescuing NPCs, breaking crates & boxes, inside chests or buying'em from vending machines. When you reach level 1, you can unleash your chosen warrior's spirit for short amount of time, to fight back or escape.Higher level (that goes up to level 3 by normal means) gives you more power & time in which you can stay in the "Dragon Change" form. While tempting, it's always a bad bet going 1v1 versus the raider (unless under very specific conditions) so you'll be using it in it's majority for escaping or interrupting.You also have up to 4 active & 4 passive skills of your choosing, which are extremely important as you'll be using them a lot when facing danger or rescuing teammates.Last but not least, you can collect dragon balls to call Shenron, which is a big turntable & can change the tides instantly, since it lets the summoner either go up to level 4 and play as the real deal, that being either Son Goku himself or Vegeta, Picolo etc, or boost remaining citizens power level. Beware though, since both sides can pick up the dragon balls & they can be dropped while fighting! Two things I completely love on citizens side is that you can use "skins" (that are available for free so far)that changes your CaC into archetypal DB characters like Bulma & Oolong!The other is the special movements & animations while near a Raider! From survivors' facial expressions to the edge of their limbs, they radiate the terror they're in! Curling up as a ball on the ground or hugging a wall with your eyes wide open with trembling small pupils is a small but very immersive aspect, that delivers incredibly well!Raiders on the other hand, are truly a menacing & horrifying force that's shouldn't be taken lightly.Currently, at game's launch, there are 3 Raiders, Frieza, Cell & Majin Buuall playing completely different and having various unique traits & playstyles. For example, all Raiders start at level 1 and are able to fly freely at all given times,except Cell which starts as his "cockroach" form and can only fast walk around till he reaches level 2, or Majin Buu who starts at LVL 1 as Spopovich, that has to steal energy from NPCs & player citizens so he can reach level 2 and resurrectMajin Buu's first thicc form. All the Canon references are really well implemented and give that original vibe the game should have.So, as Raider, you gotta find & devour anything that moves & breathes to grow in strength. Each one has different skills & special attacks, that changes in every level gain. You can destroy all type of buildings & shelters to hunt down faster & every time you level up, you're given the option to annihilate entire areas, slowing down citizen's progress with the power keys and narrowing down the stage to your liking.Fighting is quite easy for both sides, with spammable long range beams or close range melee attacks, a dodge vanish and skills that each has it's own cooldown. Super special attacks have also short starting cinematic animations and deal hefty damage. Now regarding skill unlocks & the "Gacha" system that quite a few badmouth without a valid reason.All Raiders have all their skills & kit unlocked right off the bat so there should be no worry about them.Citizens start with a few skills already unlocked & have the strongest one imo (the Grappling hook which is the fastest escape mechanism with the biggest range ) right from the start at their disposal. They can also equip up to 3 dragon ball heroes, to borrow their strengths & skills when using dragon change. While you start with quite good options, you canunlock extra skills & DB heroes or better versions of what you already have, with the Trasphere system which is the game's lootbox mechanic. You can obtain Transhperes though with all types of in-game currency that you get by completing matches & since the game offers you more than enough, you don't have to spend a single dime. In my almost 30 hours of playtime, I've opened more than 20, have unlocked more than half of what's available & I have enough currency to buy 30-40 more which i don't do cause I already have what i want. Even if you don't get that specific "Drop" you want, you can unlock that skill with again in-game currency that you get from leveling up your account & dublicate drops. That may be quite a grind but nothing too far stretched. To top it off, game gives you as a welcome gift a ticket to unlock 1 out of 3 legendary skills.With all that being said, game has also its share of cons.Graphics looks like a downgrade from Xenoverse 2, which is from partially same developer (DIMPS) & uses same engine. Lack in certain graphical & resolution settings.Some terrains & surfaces look blurry & unpolished resembling the PS3 era & the survivor's movement while turning or strafing feels kinda flat unlike the great one in danger mode. The lobby is very small, with zero activities other than browsing mailbox, customization & shop booths. There is no tutorial for Raider & even the one that exists for the Citizens, while it does explain all game mechanics, it doesn't explain properly the game's pacing or even the in-game HUD. And the worst of it all. If you queue as a Raider you get into a priority queue & if there are many Raiders queued you'll most definitely end up playing as citizen 3~4 games before gaining enough priority. That's mine & many others biggest gripe with the game & I hope that it'll get addressed soon. All in all, Breakers is a great game with a few rough edges that I can totally recommend if you're into the DB universe or  asymmetricals. DB fans gets the chance the play with iconic character with their original voice actors,while asynchronous genre gamers will get to experience something refreshing & different from what they're used to

_childDocuments_.review: The Breakers suffers from a starry-eyed gameplay vision that, in execution, likely just wasn't as good as it sounded on paper. I think we all fell for that, really-- Including the developers. Should you buy this game? Depends on your patience with devs and your penchant for learning punishing games. This said, here's an essay about the love-hate relationship I have with this game:Mix the fast-paced and cartoony action of DBZ with the murderous gameplay of Dead By Daylight, and you get a game where we can all relive the various DBZ situations we've always wanted to be in-- Such as being Krillin getting popped by Frieza. A beautiful idea really, but now, let's talk about why this is not a very "playable" experience.From the very start, the lone "Raider" is a danger and a threat to "Survivors". Survivors protect themselves by using their limited telepathy in the form of a heartbeat that quickens as they near the Raider. "Z-Change" (transforming into a Z-Fighter) exists, but it is only really a small protection against the Raider... A vain struggle, at best. The only real screen between a Raider and a Survivor is stealth and cunning. Escape is hardly ever an option. This kind of counterplay requires genius-level skill and planning-- The kind of things you'd expect champion-level Poker players to be good at. Well, the Raider is a person too. If the Raider is clever and Survivors are not, the experience quickly becomes one-sided. The same goes in the other direction: Survivors can DESTROY Raiders if the Raider is unskilled, unobservant, or just plain slow to act.... THIS is where the core of the gameplay begins to falter...If a Raider catches many players, they upscale beyond the control of Survivors and can act with impunity. This leads to Survivors, inevitably, resorting to throwing each other under the bus so that they, themselves, can escape. Sounds fun in words, but sucks when *you're* the one getting run over. If a Raider catches no one, however, Survivors begin to develop enough space and enough objective zoning to prevent the Raider from ever catching up-- Leading to a severe and unending cyclone of disruption, harassment, and abuse from Survivors that usually ends up going completely unanswered. In other words: The Raider, very quickly, becomes "The Survivor"-- Except running away is just plain NOT an option for them.Because of the above, "good" matches are rare, as the border between a win and a loss for both sides is quite simply *razor thin*. It leads to everyone fighting like their lives depend upon it. The Survivors, never taking any risks and often hiding out until 4 other Survivors die. The Raider never stopping to toy around or appreciate their handiwork, since every moment that they are not spending murdering, the time machine is being completed (and limiting their play time), or worse: Dragon Balls are being collected, which leads to an obnoxiously-powerful, unabating Survivor appearing that is, quite literally, stronger than the Raider in almost every way (their HP totals, particularly). This makes the game stressful for all sides involved, and the game, in general, unfun as a repeat experience, as you are usually just relieved and grateful to get out of your current match alive.After you've had your kicks winning a few games in clutch ways, you begin to realize... You have already reached the game's peak. That's it. The game doesn't get any better than that. This is because, often, strategy does not exist-- And I don't mean because everything is randomized. It is rather because-- Once again, the line between winning and losing is so thin, any small variable can ruin it-- And trust me: There is A LOT of random and uncontrollable variables in this game. Focusing on keys? Well, all the setting points are on top of a mountain and the Raider won't leave. Trying to overpower the Raider? Sorry, you're struggling to find Change Power and the game has decided to plant the Raider in an area with 8 Civilians screaming for their help. Focusing on escaping? Too bad. Your team has already started the time machine, but no one wants to protect it, so the Raider is just casually hunting you down. Want the Emergency Time Machine? Sorry, but the escape points tend to spawn in objective zones, so the Raider is just there, waiting for you.What if you're the Raider? Okay, let's hunt down Survivors... Well, in your fooling around, they set all the keys in record time and you're going to lose soon. Protect an area? Maybe, but the devs insist on nerfing this behavior as much as possible, despite this being a built-in mechanic (literally destroying any area you want). How about finding the dragon balls? That would be great if your best wish wasn't just "level up once"... You might as well just go out and eat Survivors instead.Overall, there's this strange intent for Survivors to "harass" the Raider constantly and waste their time-- But there's also this intent to avoid the Raider at all costs. You are offered bazookas, laser gloves, and plenty of "barrier" items (hitpoint recovery)... But then, after heroically distracting the Raider for a full minute and dying, you are met with a results screen that shows 5 bronze medals. Confusing, isn't it? It is clear the developers didn't consider their players or the gameplay as far as this. It is likely they hoped players would figure it out for them, or that they could just tune the game as it goes and play it by ear... Well, from the multitude of mixed reviews this game currently has, you can tell... This isn't working very well.What would *I* personally recommend to improve the game and remove its flaws...? It's simple really: Make death for Survivors, in general, less punishing and REVERSIBLE (why can't Shenron bring Survivors back to life?! And why is Senzu Beaning yourself just plain suicide?!). This would encourage more daring, risky, and "goofy" play, rather than AFKing inside of a cave until the "Doki Doki" stops. Then, give Raiders more non-Survivor objectives (much like Lv1 Buu) so that there's less of a fixation on hunting down players... Perhaps, make collecting the Dragon Balls as a Raider more rewarding or strategic? Finally, "slow down" the game's overall pace! A good start would be reducing the amount of energy Raiders get from eating a Survivor for the first time (1/3rd is WAAAY too much). Maybe prevent keys from being set for a short time after the last one. Maybe put a short delay on opening boxes so that Survivors don't just clear out 3 zones within the 1st minute of the match. Maybe introduce a "stamina" system for Survivors so that vehicles are ACTUALLY useful and so that they have to use mobility skills and/or Z-Change to get around easier (rather than ONLY using either when they get caught by the Raider).This is just what I would do, and my opinion. Overall though, the flavor of the game is quite good, and I don't entirely hate the Gacha-for-skills mechanic. Keeps the gameplay spicy, rather than EVERY player automatically having Afterimages, Krillin's Shoe, Saiyan Pod, and a Grapple Device. The cosmetic items are a bit bland and stale though-- Not much dress variety (maybe add a color-pigmenting system at least...?!). As long as players are focused on the FLAVOR of this game's experience (being a DBZ character and reliving moments), I believe it would find more popularity and success. Afterall, it is both we, the players, and the developers who fell for the same dream: Living out iconic Dragon Ball Z moments in a non-canon, live-action game that takes place in a parallel universe!

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly wanted to write a review when I had more hours under my belt, however from the short experience I've had thus far, I can't say it's possible I'll return to the game but won't rule out an update in the future completely. Lets begin. I'll preface by saying I play Xenoverse, Legends and Dead by Daylight frequently, which will be my references for some expectations towards Breakers and how my view of this game doesn't meet the expectations I had for it. But with that being said, I went into the game treating it as it's own separate experience. Breakers was a game that I was hopeful for in a new and refreshing take on pvp for the Dragonball universe. Combining elements of Dead by Daylight with some Xenoverse got me really excited, their presentation sealed the deal on my decision to purchase it however now that I've gotten my chance to play, it falls extremely flat on what it was attempting to achieve and what could have been for many players including myself. First thing I'm going to touch base on is the fact that the game feels LARGE and EMPTY. The initial landing into the lobby already felt like a rather big smack in the face as I stare at the outskirts of Conton city, while expecting to some some familiar faces in some degree instead I'm greeted with stale interaction from Trunks, Bulma, Oolong, two characters that are basically OC CaCs (create a character for those that don't know) and the Farmer? There's no entrance or exit, nothing to interact with beyond the crude gatcha system (I'll touch on later) and cash shop that is really disappointing (another thing to touch on later). Loading into the maps, they feel rather large which I get for the concept but it's almost a little too large for what they're aiming to do. Making players bridge the gap with skills or transpiration that takes time to come off CD and use. I felt like I was forced to pick between a useful skill and being able to get around the map decently.What's so frustrating about this game is that a lot of features that could have been added to Xenoverse is instead wasted in this game. A free name change feature, the ability to simply adjust your character without the use of resources (Dragon Balls) and no new custom anything. Seriously, they're just re-using Xenoverse 2 models and assets without much of anything that's considerably new. The worst part about this is that you're essentially PAYING FOR THINGS YOU LIKELY ALREADY OWN IF YOU PLAY XV2, again...this was pointless. I can understand allowing the option for people to customize a character, but why not allow established XV2 players to just import their character over? Saving some a rather boring process of limited customization as is. No new hairs, faces, and limited voice options, we don't even get a variety of races which would have made more sense and added diversity into the cast of creation among players and really engage them. Bringing me about to my next point and that's the CASH SHOP, hooo boy that's really bad. Charging your players for items/costumes you can get in another game for FREE on their character is pretty scummy and greedy in my eyes. A lot of these outfits are lacking and most of what we COULD HAVE even as a PAID SKIN isn't even present. If they're rehashing already established items, why not just put them in the game for free and make them unlockable with zeni or play time like in the other game? While yes I'm aware there's some items already able to be purchased with zeni, there's plenty of items that require actual cash. For what reason are they charging for a Camo Bikini set when you get this free in raids.My next gripe is with the implement of a gatcha system which limits players ability to properly play the game and utilize the best builds for playing. I am more than understanding charging for Raiders/Survivors as this is something that is done in Dead by Daylight, as well as other games that tend to involve a pvp system with skins and such, but my issue is that players are charged for all that PLUS trying to earn abilities with limited/drip fed coins that can't properly supplement better banners and rolls without actual cash. The fact that Breakers also lacks a pity system means it's sapping players of money for measly rolls that could be free basic items to players for just playing.  Even games like Fate Grand Order and Genshin Impact (with the WORST rates for rolling) have a better system than this game which is shocking. I don't expect five stars on every roll, not even fours, but Dragonball Legends does better in the Gatcha department than this game. It amazes me that they still have a dedicated amount of players to any degree with how they bleed them for more and more. On to the gripes of PVP, my initial experience as a new player was downright AWFUL. The fact that you're encouraged to play both sides and get matched up with players WAY OUT OF YOUR LEAGUE is terrible. Compared to Dead by Daylight (even with this games heavy flaws), Killers still have a better chance of victory at level one with zero perks than Raiders in their early stages. I feel like Breakers was attempting to bottleneck their players into purchasing Raiders with the level 20 boost while punishing the ones that simply want to play and earn their rank. Even still, you're matched up with players hitting triple digits to your measly double or single to which you're full on destroyed by them. Resources gone, they're powered up and the Raider is simply bombarded and the match ends in painful loss after loss while trying to navigate and get custom to how the game plays. While on the survivor end you're easy pickings for a Raider clearly more familiar with the game. No matter what side you're on, it's a painful endeavor to deal with and makes the fun of the game absolutely lacking.  To wrap my painfully long review up, Breakers could have easily been a new game mode in Xenoverse 2 and people would have LOVED IT. They're already using what we have established in Xeno, they could have asily expanded and gave players more than what they'd expect without having to pay for an entirely new and rather overpriced bundle of scraps that players are suppose to eat up without anything to truly feed the hunger for fun. I expected more, I expected better, this game is not something I'd suggest anyone pay for let alone play. TL;DR... Add this as a new mode in Xenoverse and refund everyone who purchased it with a copy of Xenoverse 2. It would save so much time, effort and heartache to what could have been something amazing and great. I am so sorry to my fellow Dragonball lovers, we deserve better, not greed.

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon ball: The Breakers, although most people compare it to other asymmetrical games like Dead By Daylight, it's nothing of the sort. This is a pretty unique game that has a lot of identity behind it.Even though it's an online game, there is a bit of a story in the prologue. The time-space continuum had one too many vitamin gummies and started opening "Temporal Seams" all over the place that have been dragging innocent civilians into these chaotic realms (the maps you play on) where the past, present and future are all mixed together.It just so happens that you are one of the people who fell victim to this, it also happens that there's a super-powerful "Raider" willing to slaughter you simply for their amusement. "Time Patrol" member Trunks finds you unconscious and makes sure your okay, and he tells you about the situation, about how to escape it and about the things you'll be doing a lot in this game.You meet some other people like Bulma and Oolong during the prologue and you learn about the tools you'll be using like your gun. Most importantly, you also make use of the Transpheres, small orbs that hold the spirit of powerful warriors like Goku and even Trunks himself, drawing on this power allows you to take on the warrior's form temporarily and fight back against the Raider.Although the prologue is more of a tutorial, there is a respectable amount of world-building and dialogue there to help you get a grasp on the lore. It does a good job of setting up the game and explaining the current state of affairs, every match starts with you being sucked into another seam too so it's got good continuity with the main game.The game is pretty easy to grasp, the main objective of survivors is finding 5 power keys spread across the map, each one being in one of the 5 zones. Once all the keys are set, the "Super Time Machine" Startup Sequence is deployed in the middle of the map, survivors need to prevent the raider from destroying it by using items or transpheres to fight them off until it activates. Activation means victory, raider gets thanos snapped out of the timeline and everything is right with the world again, until the next seam that is.But if things don't exactly go to plan, there is a backup. If the startup sequence is destroyed (or if only 3 survivors remain before all keys are set) then the option to escape becomes available. Head to a beacon, call the escape machine and either wait for the others or peace out right there. Bear in mind, there's only the one machine and it's rather fragile. If the machine breaks, the survivors still in the game are screwed.If you'd rather go with the nuclear option, defeating the raider themselves is also an option. Takes a fair bit of teamwork and effort, but you can pull a "No U" and KA-ME-HA-ME-HA them into next week.Raiders just have one job. Complete. Global. Genocide. Technically, the Raider only needs to survive, regardless of how many survivors escape it counts as a victory as long as your still alive at the end. It's just that killing everyone is the much more fun option so...You go around hunting down the survivors and executing them to grow your power, doing everything you can to kill them off before they set all the keys and start the time machine. Destroying it is an option, but the survivors will put up all the resistance they can to stop you so you better be ready for a fight.There's plenty to do apart from the keys to give both survivors and raiders an edge, civilians around the map can be saved by survivors and killed by raiders to increase their power. The 7 dragon balls can be gathered to summon Shenron and grant a wish to whoever summoned him. Various items like rocket launchers and radars can be found in supply crates around the map.Each raider has their own gimmicks:Cell auto-evolves at level one, giving him a quick early-game.Majin Buu heals on executions and pulls survivors into a small arena when he hits his final level.Frieza can execute at a distance and if he gets the dragon balls he can wish for invincibility.Each raider certainly feels unique, they all have things that set them apart from each other really well, it's certainly noticeable just how different they each feel to play.Survivors have 4 abilities to make use of, these abilities can only be used with the appropriate transpheres equipped, you can't use Kaioken Rush without Goku for example, there are some abilities that are universal like the ones bought from the store and exclusive skills can be "Mastered" (used without restriction) after you level them up enough.It's a similar story with the 4 passives too, luckily most spheres have 2 skills tied to them so your loadout won't be dominated with spheres you'd rather not use.As the title mentions, this game does have its share of problems. So lets talk about them.-There's 2 skills that are just too good, the grappling device and the single-wheel bike. They're both available at the start of the game and everyone has them. The grapple by itself is manageable but the bike is just Initial-D levels of speed, and since most people pair the two together along with Expert Driver... It's basically a guaranteed escape from even the worst situations since raiders gain an automatic lock-on that prevents aiming manually whenever they get close to anyone.-The transpheres are obtained through a gacha system, you are told the drop rates and the game does give you a fair few freebies like tickets and the option to buy with earned currency but the fact that its in a game you have to pay for... Bruh. If it wasn't for the bike and grapple, you could get stuck with nothing of value to put on your loadout because RNG said so.-RNG itself, Raider games are heavily determined by how the early game goes, although it's less of an issue for Cell, there is always the chance for the raider to spawn in an area devoid of people to "put in the forever box" which leads to being under-powered and that just leads to suffering. Some of my raider games have turned into 1-sided curb-stomp battles because of bad spawns.It's not all that bad though, there are some positives to address.-The main gameplay loop is fun, gathering keys and items while slowly building up power during the lead-up to the final confrontation feels very fun & dramatic.-The music, it's spectacular, the dramatic tension as the violins signify the next raider level and the heroic music as you change to take them on. The absolute banger that plays when you get Shenron to grant you level 4 is just so damn amazing to behold! The chill vibes as you wonder around the pre-game lobby and the undeniable satisfaction of hearing that victory theme!-Although I've personally never seen even a single episode of it, there is a lot of Dragon Ball stuff in here that would really please fans of the show, voice lines for the raiders and the ability to cosplay as certain characters are no doubt going to draw in the more dedicated among the fanbase.-The store-bought skills might not be as good as some you obtain from the gacha, but the fact that it's an option means even the most unlucky players can still have a fair bit to work with, and that is something that I appreciate.7/10This game is pretty flawed but none of those flaws ruin the experience for me, and even though there are a few points against it, I can't bring myself to slander a game which keeps me entertained for most of the time I'm playing it. Nothing says you need to buy in to the gacha, and as I mentioned earlier, it's not as expensive as the big name games so your not losing much by giving it a go. -Loading screen tip #20.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Dead by Daylight except you can beat the hell out of the killer.It's not perfect by any means but anyone saying that this game has major balancing issues never figured out any good strategies for playing Survivor/Raider.  In my time with this and the playtest, I would say I've seen roughly a 50/50 split in which side wins.Myself and a couple friends have been having a blast playing this together. I get a much better sense of playing as a team on Survivor than in Dead by Daylight, and Raider is fun whether I'm stomping a bad Survivor group or being forced to strategize against a coordinated one. There's been tons of tense moments with some Survivors trying to work an objective while others fight and hold back the Raider. It's just genuinely fun.Having said that, this game is not without its flaws. The tutorial introduces you to the basic objectives but is not at all representative of what actual gameplay is like. The combat itself isn't anything super complex and can be janky at times, e.g. beam attacks connecting when they clearly didn't hit. Bad groups can make a game nigh unwinnable for Survivors (comes with the territory for asymmetrical games), and extremely limited communication options plus not having skill/level-based matchmaking doesn't help. I've also seen a few cases of deliberate teaming between a Survivor(s) and the Raider, and there's no way to report this. I'd recommend playing with a friend or two if you can.The game does have a gacha system, and some skills/characters considered to be must-haves can only be obtained through it. Earning currency is a somewhat slow process, so it can feel frustrating if luck isn't on your side. Finally, and what I consider to be the biggest flaw, is that there is no cross-play/cross-progression and is region-locked. I've seen tons of people complaining about long queue times, particularly on console in areas outside the US. For comparison, my friends and I in the Southeastern US have rarely had to wait more than 30 seconds to find a full lobby. I truly want this game to survive a long time (and from the announcement of a season 2, it seems Bandai Namco does as well), but I think it'll die sooner rather than later without crossplay.In short, if you like Dead by Daylight and you like Dragon Ball, then chances are you'll like this game. Despite it's obvious issues, it's still some of the best fun I've had with a game in a while. My hope is that the devs will be responsive in alleviating these problems and make it an overall better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, where do I even begin with Dragon Ball: The Breakers? This game is a catastrophic mess that somehow manages to take the beloved Dragon Ball universe and turn it into a dumpster fire of disappointment. From the moment I fired it up, I felt like I was plummeting into the abyss of regret.Let's start with the graphics – a jumbled, pixelated nightmare that makes even the most dedicated Dragon Ball fan question their life choices. The character models are so poorly rendered that I half-expected my screen to shatter from the sheer ugliness of it all. Dead by Daylight, in comparison, is a visual masterpiece that bathes its players in an atmosphere of terror and tension.Now, let's talk about the gameplay. Dragon Ball: The Breakers seems to have taken all the excitement of the anime and thrown it out the window, leaving players with a sluggish, clunky mess. The controls are about as responsive as a rock, and the combat system feels like a sad attempt to mimic other, more successful titles. Dead by Daylight, on the other hand, has refined its gameplay to perfection, creating an immersive experience that keeps players on the edge of their seats.And don't even get me started on the lackluster maps in Dragon Ball: The Breakers. They're uninspired, poorly designed, and feel like they were thrown together in a rush. Dead by Daylight, with its meticulously crafted environments, offers players a variety of hauntingly beautiful landscapes that add to the overall horror experience.Let's not forget the abysmal matchmaking system of Dragon Ball: The Breakers, which seems to think that throwing random players together is a recipe for success. Dead by Daylight, with its well-balanced matchmaking and dedicated player base, ensures that every match is a thrilling and challenging experience.Overall, The Breakers is a train wreck of a game that should have never seen the light of day. If you're in the mood for a truly exhilarating and polished horror experience, stick with Dead by Daylight. It's like comparing a rotten, overcooked Senzu Bean to the finest delicacies – there's just no contest. Dragon Ball: The Breakers, you've done the Dragon Ball legacy a disservice, and I regret every second I spent playing your abomination of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Well I'm 8 hours in and I'm loving it. This game is incredibly jank, but you are given more than enough resources at the start of the game to play and to possibly have a varied playstyle.  The gacha aspect is on the survivors side, allowing you to get Transpheres(Equipment which lets you borrow a characters abilities) as well as upgrading them with passive and active skills and sometimes costume changes.  Since one of the tickets you get guarantee's you your own choice of starter skill what you start with is up to you.  You have a very healthy chance of getting some good stuff with the rest of you free dollars and the grind doesn't seem that bad so far.   Getting 100% of the content would be insane, and I wouldn't even fathom how much money it would take to get it all, but theres no pressure to go for microtransactions.  You can earn all the ingame currencies tho the paid dollars one does take forever, so you can slowly grow your stable of Transpheres and find new ways to play.  On the Raider side of things is a bit more interesting.  Between them you have Cell who is a great starter as he gain's evolution for free, having a weaker second form to compensate, Frieza who while not being the strongest later on in the game has an incredible early game with tools to help you track, trap, and murder suvivors, Buu who also starts of strong and has such an incredibly strong late game that you typically don't really kill him you just kind of pressure him off the time machine.  The Raiders level up, allowing you to power up their passive and active skills by minute increments which eventually build up to drastically changing your effectiveness.   Main thing is I don't know how the long form of this game is going to shape out, having a lot of fun with it now but not sure if I'll care about it in a month.

_childDocuments_.review: After over adding another 50 Hours in to give this game another chance, finally recognized a lot of the issues this game has. I cannot recommend it at all, even if it was F2P.The core aspect of the game was fine. Dead by Daylight style game with DBZ characters and mechanics.This game however has had a core issue in regards to premades (basically +3 dudes in a group chat) and really good skills. The devs are allergic to nerfing skills and rather add another raider specifically for fighting premades (technically not entirely true as Unconscious Control got nerfed indirectly, I'll explain later). Season 5 brought some of the worst in-balance thanks to skills like the Galactic Patrol Ship. A skill when paired up with Expert Driver leaves most raiders in the dust (such as the legacy 3, the Saiyans and Ginyu Force). It was a Season 5 Free Season Pass reward, so a lot of players have it. There was also the viability of just spamming dodge which allowed both survivors and raiders to stall (though it was more egregious when fighting Goku Black). Basically, it was so bad, you had to play Zamasu in order to win a match as raider (he costs $8 USD btw)Season 6 was expected to more or less fix this inbalance in. A large wave of nerfs were made. Dodge Stalling was erased by adding endlag after a vanish, indirectly nerfing Unconscious ControlInvincible frames were removed or reduced on non-transformed survivors. This was to prevent survivors from going full Soulsborne and either escaping or delaying their death. Supply drops do not drop till level the raider is at Level/Stage 3 which is to discourage Key-Rushing and overpowering a Stage 2 RaiderSurvivors can no longer drink a cooldown drink while powered up (Dragon Change) which prevents them from having another one immediately ready. Raiders were also given buffs, majority of the raiders were given AoE blasts on their supers similar to Goku Black. Throwing Ki-Blasts while flying doesn't slow them down, can instantly descend to the ground by double tapping the jump button. Then there's Baby, a raider entirely designed around fighting the previous meta. His level 1 is invincible and can insta-down anyone he gets near and can practically scare anyone from exploring an area, his level 2 and level 3 have 2 evasives and AoE attacks. One of his evasives can also be utilize to disrupt a Barrier + Instant Transmission escape which is a combo that is effective against most raiders. He also has a mechanic that anyone he finishes off temporarily loses one of their active skillsSo, is the problem fixed? Short answer, noLong answer: Cell supposedly is said to be the raider who might of benefited the most, but I rarely come across good Cell players to verify that. Most of the supposed buffed raiders still have fundamental weaknesses that will screw them over against any competent team. Aside the obnoxious stun skill spam, the legacy trio can still be softlocked to their weaker Lv 2 or 3 forms. The Saiyans and The Ginyu Force mechanics can be taken advantaged of along with their pitiful health and only having a +20 second evasive. The attempt to make finding dragon balls more "difficult" didn't really do much, in fact. I find it that it's gotten easier for experienced players but harder for new or less skilled players. Ok, what about Baby? Surely he even the odds against premades. LMAO NO! In fact, Baby is the epitome of everything wrong with this game's balancing. His controversial Level 1 where he is a possessed civvie is the strongest and weakest Level 1 in the game. He is extremely strong against a team of randoms, doesn't matter how skilled they are. All Baby has to do is down at least 1 person and you are stuck with a handicapped teammate. His Level 1 does not auto-ping nor makes a heartbeat sound when he's near. What the Baby could do is just camp the body and unsuspecting/less experience teammates will rush in and add another body to the pile. So it's strong against, random/solo-queue players, what about premades. Almost a joke. With a bit a luck and a player with an ability like Flying Nimbus who's dedicated to pinging Baby's location, his Level 1 goes from being his strongest aspect to an Achilles' heel as he can't destroy vending machines. The other 6 players are given a good 2 and half minutes to get supplies. Baby also does not have any tools to find hiding survivors. So long as you actively avoid him and prevent him from getting any civvies, he's stuck at Level 2. It's possible for the Baby to clutch it, but if the survivors got the Dragon Balls and summon the Lv 4, he's most likely done for. So yeah, ultimately, the gap between the Solo Queue and Premade is larger. It's no surprise most people started quitting the game for that aside the lack of content. Matches never feel even or anything. It's always one sided. Sometimes, when I play the Raider, I'm in such a dominant position, it's almost boring, in other cases (usually against a team full over lv +200 players), it's frustrating and a one-sided beatdown in the end. On the Survivor side of things, it's also just as volatile, either a dominant victory or a humiliating loss with no chance at a comeback. Other issues with this game includes the long wait times (8-30 minutes to get into a match). If you want a Raider match, you are going to have to play at least 4 matches on average. So yeah, we're looking at playing at least an hour to finally get to play Raider. Then we have the competitive aspect the devs have been trying to force on the community. Leaderboard and Rank periods are just not fun. Ranked especially as it's forced onto everyone and goes on for the remainder of the season. Probably the only game that forces everyone to participate in Rank rather than have it as a separate mode. Content is drip fed. No new map this season, no new super attacks. SSJ4 Goku doesn't even have his badass x10 KamehamehaOverall, I just can't recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun for a while. However you are gated on the challenges by which role you are playing, either Survivor or Raider. Escape on the emergency time machine or destroy the Super Time Machine X times as an example. Outside of having a pre-made group you will need to play 5 to 8 matches as a Survivor to get 1 match as a Raider. This wouldn't be a problem if you just want to play Survivor or if the challenges in the game could be completed as both a Survivor and Raider in the form of an either/or of rescue this many npcs or destroy this many npcs. The pass system this game utilizes awards points that can be found up to a daily limit, 3 dailies, and multiple weekly challenges.  Weeklies do not reset if you do not complete all of them. There is no mechanic to ditch a weekly you do not want to do, and this is clearly by design to give incentive to pay them to complete their season pass or fuel their gacha mechanic system for transformations/abilities.Now enter the scenario of you need to something like destroy 2 Super Time Machines as a Raider in order to complete a set to get your new set of weeklies. A match takes anywhere from 7 to 15 minutes. You will need to play 5 to 8 matches to get a game as the Raider. Now you need the survivors to summon the Super Time Machine in order for you to destroy it. Do that twice. If you are just joining the game against the established players you are pretty much not going to get this done without hitting your head against a wall as you play survivor games to get thrown against Seal Team 6 composed of mostly 80+ level players. There is no real rating system in place to filter the player base and there is no crossplay so you will continue to be paired up against familiar names if you queue at certain times of day.Content is rather bare bones as well. Much of your resources are going to be thrown into the games gacha system to acquire abilities for your Dragon Change forms or spending points to level up your survivor skills, which is where facing high level players becomes a nightmare once they've bumped particular skills up to +20. Outside of that there are some limited cosmetic options and plenty of reminders about their premium currency,As of right now the game has a multitude of disconnection issues and crash problems. Interactions between certain abilities and events during matches can cause players to freeze and the lock on system can't be disabled to allow you to lead shots without hanging back from the target.In a few months some of these issues will likely be resolved but for now I'd advise sticking to other games in the genre like Dead By Daylight. If you have the cash to blow it is worth it for a few laughs the first 10-15 hours were rather great but after that it just became a grind. All stick, no carrot.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun asymmetrical game.Playing as the Raider is a power trip. You really feel like a hunter as you take down civilians and players.At the moment the game seems to favor survivors, as long as they gang up on the raider, but with good plays it is perfectly possible for the raider to win with some comfort. It's mostly practice.As the survivors, even when you lose you always feel like you've accomplished something. Getting at least to level 1 is easy, and as long as you move around constantly and carefully you'll be finding useful items and reviving comrades left and right. Don't miss out on the chance to team up on the Raider though, that can be a game changer.It's also good to see that the game rewards you for playing. You can get in-game currency, and even the premium stuff from just playing and going for the daily and weekly objectives.. The gacha element mostly provides cosmetics, and you get enough free tickets right off the bat to get yourself some new skills.At this point in time, while it helps to have 4 start characters, it doesn't seem to be a game breaker, as the combat focuses a lot on how well you time your moves and dodge the opponent. On top of that, the combat (as a survivor) is meant to be done as a group, so that makes it not as important to pull for the best characters.Overall, it feels like a rewarding, fun game, especially if you have ppl to play with. The micro-transactions are just for cosmetics, and the items and skills you can buy can be comfortably gotten through in-game currency.While some polishing needs to be done with the camera and movement, the game is a fun experience, especially for the price it is offered.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a bizarre freak of nature. If you told me years ago, during the emergence of the asymmetrical genre, that we were going to receive a 1v7 asymmetrical Dragon Ball game where the villains are treated about as horrifying as they would be to the average person, I would have thought you were insane. Now, I feel equally insane coming to you and telling you that for some reason, this actually works really well. The game revolves around the survivors searching the map for five keys and placing them in designated spots while the raider hunts both them and stationary civilians to "evolve"-- think of any transformation in Dragon Ball and you get the idea. The survivors scavenge for both keys and resources to fight back against the raider, which keeps the main objective search as something the survivors want to actively do in order to more effectively interact with the raider-- if you've played Dead by Daylight, you might know the pain of holding M1 on a generator when all you really want to do is get into a chase with the killer. The way this game side-steps this issue by making it an objective search does add some RNG into the mix, but I vastly prefer it as it keeps the game from ever really getting tedious.Breakers is a game I'd call "scrappy". Its piece-mealed together from assets from Xenoverse 2 mixed in with their own, with a fluctuating but dedicated fan-base. I mostly played it on and off during the first three seasons, but really got back into it with Season 4, and was thoroughly impressed with how much better the game feels to play now. It really feels like the team behind it is one of a rare few that do actually listen to feedback while trying to maintain their own comprehensive vision of the game, which I think mostly has worked out great in its favor. Despite all the jokes about this game, the devs have kept their heads down and worked passionately on it, which shines in the creativity of their skill design/survivor choices/raider design. Where the game really shines is in player skill and expression. In a similar manner to games like Dead by Daylight, survivors have a set of skills they can equip-- however, unlike DbD, this takes the form of four active skills, and four passives. Actives are skills you actually activate manually, like using trampolines, grappling hooks, various manners of stuns, and far too many bizarre and unique cases that it'd be hard to go over all of them. Passives are just things that either affect you passively, or when certain conditions are fulfilled. While there are "meta picks", they're not really at all required to do well. I've had many matches where I'm the walking embodiment of slipping on banana peels and setting up whoopee cushions under the raider that ended in nail-biting finishes that came down to the wire. The ability to express yourself with 8 of these makes your build really feel like YOUR build, which plays to exactly how you like to play the game, as opposed to having to make a build just to play the game effectively at all. The way you get these skills is through the gacha system; which at face value, I can't say I'm the biggest fan. It has pros and cons. The pros is that there's absolutely no real DLC for this game. Due to the in-game "Battle Pass" (there's no actual paid version of it, you just get rewards for playing each season) you can earn the premium currency, which can be used to buy paid things like Raiders, Premium Survivor Skins, etc. The gacha portion of the game can be paid with with that same currency, in game zeni you get from every match, and tickets which are pretty routinely given out. There are no "limited" banners, (barring one that only gave you transformations for Gohan and Piccolo, which are more just cosmetic than anything), as after each banner passes, it's added to a permanent one in the next season. Therefore, if you played the game now and rolled on that banner, you're basically getting insane value on every pull even though you came in late. It's... fine. I don't really like having it in a paid game, but I've also gone it's entire lifespan without ever feeling like I had to roll on it to begin with, which is more than can be said of actual gachas. A lot of the best abilities are stuff you quite literally start the game with, there's never really been any sort of power creep barring one or two abilities being common (if not necessary) staples in survivor builds.With the advent of cross-play, the laughably small player base on PC isn't an issue anymore; with the addition of ranked (when the ranked period is active), you do tend to get paired with people who are actually around your skill level. The game is balanced way better than it has been in any period (unless you're new to the game, in which case everything will appear overpowered if you're not the one doing it), and I can wholeheartedly recommend giving this game a solid shot. If you're looking to actually get into the game, creators like Ironcane have very solid guides you can peruse to get more of an idea of how to competently play the game. The people who play this game are dedicated, so if you're just looking to stop in and casually stomp people with friends without ever taking the time to improve at the game, this one might not be for you-- and that's fine! But if you're looking for fun asymmetrical game, that's both equal parts competitive and nonsense, as well as being Dragon Ball themed, then this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The good about this game has already been covered a lot, so I will just dispute the bad."Gacha system is pay 2 win" False. Base kit and store have everything you need to get around and play the way you need to as survivor. Level up skills from Oolong and Bulma (which lets you use them on base character) and you have all the active skills you need, and store has most of the passives. Nearly everything in the gacha system is cosmetic differences on base skill. Even the super attacks are mostly for show, since most of your damage will be dealt melee. Yes, there are some things actually unique to the gacha system, but not having them is not a handicap when the best mobility skills are basically free."The progression is limited in the season pass!" It is legit the exact same as one in Fortnite. Do weekly released missions and dailies, get progress. done. The 'Limit' everyone is bawling over is the limit of DP you can find IN A MATCH per day, not a limit on what you can get from quests as people seem to think. It's something you won't notice early on since finding DP in a match is extremely lucky."Survivors/Raider is too OP" The game isn't even a week old yet, and had limited pre release runs. This isn't the state of balance for the rest of time. Also, a LOT of people don't even know how to play optimally, on either side, so matches are very swingy. Give it time. I've had nice matches on both sides, and a handful of bad ones, but it's not like either side is legit impossible to win. Plus, most people making this complaint just want their preferred side to have a 100% easy win rate, just like the community in Dead by Daylight.I give this game a solid 8/10 because it is hitting a niche genre usually dominated by a single game, DBD, and has a solid start, better than, say, F13. I fully expect the game will get better and better as people give it time and balance improves. I can't put a number tho on satisfying it is to taze Majin Buu with a trap device, or solar flare Freiza while cosplaying Krillin.
_childDocuments_.name: DRAGON BALL: THE BREAKERS

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I have a long well made review in my back pocket for games nowadays, but this? This? Nope. Not at all.Allow me to tell you what your average match will be.Best way to summarize a match: Join. Get Gank'd by high level(s). Re-queue. Repeat.Won't even touch on the gatcha mechanics that should've stayed in Legends and Dokkan, the Pay 2 Win essences/souls/whatever, the odd control scheme, premium currency, or everything else. Go read other reviews or other videos (JP2427 on YouTube's video is a good one. It's named 'The Frustrating State of Dragon Ball: The Breakers') if you want a telling on the status of the game's fun factor and how it's been butchered over the year.Besides, it's all asset flips! Idle animations, emotes, models, flight animations, many voice lines, abilities, moves, animations in general, almost everything is ripped from Xenoverse 2! The art's from Dragon Ball: Legends. The sounds are from Xenoverse 1 and 2. Only unique things are some models like 3rd from Frieza (who looks like he has something wrong with him), Yamu and Spopovitch, Evil Buu (who appears for 2 seconds in a transfomation), and 2nd form Cell. For Dragon Ball standards that is sad. And they're putting things that were super easy to get like outfits from Xenoverse 2 into limited time premium currency deals, sparking FoMo. Gohan's highschool outfit is 3K Zeni (dirt cheap) in Xenoverse 2 and it's always available, why is it limited time here? And that's just one example.Nearly anything I could get out of this, I have gotten and will continue to get out of Xenoverse 2, and then some.At least you can remake your character whenever you like, unlike in Xenoverse 2 where you have to  get all the blasted Dragon Balls and even then not everything's changeable. There's a positive, I guess.I wanted to love this game. I really did. I've been a massive fan of Dragon since I was, like, 12. I love this series. I've played Xenoverse 2 for hundreds of hours, even platinum'ing it on PS4, I play FighterZ every day. I've watched all the shows, read a lot of the manga, and more. But this? This is sad. It is an amazing idea hidden behind pointless money grubbing. If this was free? Still bad, but excusable to an extent. But no, I paid an indie game's worth or some pretty big wardrobe of Team Fortress 2 hats for this. _childDocuments_.review: A very fun game regardless if your a DB fan or not. While its not perfect the overall balancing is honestly quite good as both sides have the means to utterly dominate the other and make a quick u-turn in the right moments. Personally I think its fun as a Survivor and thrilling as the Raider, allowing you to go on mini power trips and feel like a badass if your able to fight the Raider and win though obviously that's difficult and don't read that thinking you'll be able to 1v1 the Raider. No. 9 outta 10 times your not doing it.However there are pros and cons to consider if you want to get this game and its certainly not a game that everyone will enjoy in the long term.Pros:- Flexible system to customise your survivor's skills and appearance. Don't like something? Change it! Is there an ability you wanna use? Pick it! However there is also a downside to this.....- Everything (At least by the time of writing this) is earnable/unlockable by simply playing the game without needing to spend money. Complimented by the fact they are still adding more things into the game!- Ability to play as classic DBZ villians via the Raider, complete with their personalities and abilities that change how they operate from each other somewhat in games. You feel like a force to be reckoned with either way whomever you play as. (Lowkey accompanied on Survivor side that your able to play as the DBZ heroes as well via dragonballs)- Multiple objectives/roles to fulfill on Survivor side. While your all aiming for the single goal of either escaping or defeating the Raider and that's done by linear objectives. Each game is RNG dependent on what you'll find, which usually controls how you'll contribute. Maybe you'll find a radar to search for the dragon balls? Maybe you'll find a lot of power up items so you can fight/distract the Raider? Maybe you'll find support tools to assist your teammates? Its rare for a game to feel the same as the last you played and it'll certainly keep you busy unless you choose to specifically aim for something which you have the complete freedom to do so which is great! (Even if sometimes what you wanna do isn't what is needed to win at the time)- The tone of the game as a whole, graphics, music and etc fit it perfectly fine in my opinion. Nothing amazing by any means but it does the job well of selling the setting and moment to moment in the games.Cons:- .....The downside is that its RNG based to unlock certain skills/abilities that you want to use, there's nothing in the game to guarantee you what you want. Aside from supers being unlock-able for a steep price in spirit points, not the skills which is usually what your after!- To unfortunately compliment the fact there's RNG in place in what you'll get. Make no mistake this game is grindy in practically all aspects! This game demands you to play it frequently if you want to unlock most things. There is a 'Free' dragon pass for example which can get you all sorts of goodies just by playing. But to get them you'll need to earn dragon points which are earned via daily/weekly challenges on top of a chance to randomly find medals of DP which get you 5 immediately. But you'll be limited by how many you can find each day in games and if you've done all daily/weekly challenges, your not going to be able to earn more. Meaning you need to play every day/week if you want to keep pace on earning things or just cough up some real money to get it all in the dragon pass immediately. (At the very least the game does carry over these objectives so if you do fall behind you can do several weeks worth in one go)- Earlier I mentioned that its easy for one side to become the dominant force in games. This is also RNG dependent to a point as Survivors in theory are able to win the game within the first minute if things go exceedingly well in what they find! Sometimes making it impossible for the Raider to deal with them. Alternatively, there's little to stop a Raider just bullying the game if they get a great start instead.- Game is easy to grasp, but there's a deep curve to learn to understand on both Survivor and Raider ends. If you don't have the patience to learn and figure things out. Your likely going to become quickly confused and frustrated and this isn't helped by a poor tutorial which only tells you the basic points of the game, not the details that are important in how a match might go.- A variety of both small and big inconveniences with the game itself. Examples include, Lack of crossplay hurts its multiplayer as a major while some minors is having a frustrating menu/lobby system. (Who thought it was a good idea to need to go to the settings menu just so you can exit the game!?) or that the survivor side announcer 'Trunks' cannot be turned off. (I know we need the power keys! I've played enough games to know it!)I personally can recommend it purely because I find the gameplay loop fun (though I do get frustrated with the RNG Gacha system) But If your not a patient person or don't see yourself playing a game for multiple hours at a time, then don't get it! If your after a small game with a lot of people to play with, maybe yeah go for it for fun. I genuinely hope this game is supported further as it certainly has a potential to become great but at its current state, its future is uncertain and may very well die which I hope doesn't happen, but its player base that decides that.Sorry for length, but that's my thoughts.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fun, and not a single bit of it is pay to win unless you want to pay to progress. Although it can be argued that with the poor balancing of DLC raiders such as Ginyu and Vegeta, you can still earn the in-game currency to obtain them without spending any actual money in real life.There are three issues at hand, though. One issue with the game is how the ki blasts for characters, although unique, can be ludicrously weak, sometimes even outright forcing you to just level up the skill without using the transphere whatsoever. The other is that the learning curve for raider is ludicrously steep with non-skill matchmaking being centralized, practically discouraging players from picking up Raider because you'll most often find a lobby of people with 100+ levels in survivor ready to tear you apart and leave you with next to no spirits.The final and biggest issue is how there's not much of a tutorial for anything. You do get a mandatory Episode to understand the most fundamental basics of the gameplay, but you're not taught that you can use CTRL to cancel your transformation, how to signal, when and how to launch an attack on a raider(that knows what it is doing), and especially how certain items worked. If you're going to have a more proper tutorial, pretty much bug test the game out first in practice mode, and invite a couple friends so you can properly understand who has what mechanics and how to counter/use certain items effectively. An extra pro-tip that I learned recently online: Consuming cooldown drinks while in dragon change readies the next one pre-maturely.Besides that, you have every typical issue of every multiplayer game, bots, hackers, and even trolls.EDIT: They can't do something as basic as stopping a timer if there isn't all 7 players available. If you have a game balanced for 7 players vs 1 uber powerful one, then make it a game where you need 7 players dammit. _childDocuments_.review: Credit where credit's due: great concept and a very refreshing, original idea for a Dragon Ball game - asymmetrical multiplayer grabbing ideas from the likes of Dead by Daylight, Evolve, Friday the 13th: The Game, mixing them all together into what forms Dragon Ball: The Breakers. In execution however . A shoddy and otherwise terrible camera, underbaked fighting/PvP mechanics, tons of technical issues and limitations, terrible balancing, crossplay being only added years later, tiny playerbase, an exhausting queue system for the 'Raider' role, and worst of all locking skills/abilities behind a FOMO P2W Gacha system. I could excuse all of it's faults if it wasn't for that last bit alone - some of the most powerful skills for survivors are locked behind a Gacha system, stacked on top of a seasonal FOMO system. Would only recommend this game on a heavy discount and to diehard fans of the Dragon Ball series; otherwise stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: Of course this game gets a lot of comparison to Dead by Daylight cause of the asymmetrical style and I have a LOT of hours in Dead by Daylight. The fact that its a group vs 1 is really where the similarities between the two ends. In concept this is actually a smart idea. Its how the anime works. Its a group taking on one big bad and working together, powering up, sacrificing ones self to buy time for the others etc. All just condensed to a 5-10 minute match. At first because of the pacing it feels like chaos but once you get to grips with it its actually pretty fluid and I've been having a great time with it and some really memorable matches. There are a few issues I have but the game has a few things about it to help that though they may be controversial.Firstly playing Raider is just a fun romp in my eyes really. But there's a queueing system for it so essentially you always want to prioritise playing raider and have to wait your turn and play survivor matches until your number is the highest out of the lobby you are in. This sounds bad but its probably the best way they can do this to make it fair and not make lobbies take too long for those who just want to play. For me I don't mind because it makes me value the time as raider more whether I win or lose I just wanted to have fun and make it more challenging rather than just camp a survivor on the floor till they're out. Atm stats seem to indicate that its fairly even win/loss rate between survivors and raiders however no indication of this towards sets of comptent survivors and raider matches. And the loss for a raider may generally be down to inexperience as it takes a lot longer to get matches as them and each raider works differently and has different mechanics.Thirdly skills, unfortunately there are some cool skills that are from the animes themselves however in games are just not practical or very rarely work as intended while others pretty much guarantee you'll get away from even the most efficient raider. So balancing in that regard is an issue but the devs are tweaking based on play data already. These things take time. The last thing I want to really comment on is the gacha summons for new skills and transforms. Its controversial in a paid game and I can see why but its nowhere near as bad as some reviewers have made it out to be I haven't paid anymore than price of admission and have nearly everything currently available besides cosmetics. Theres a grind and random chance for this stuff but none of it is game breaking at all it just might be a bit annoying if your favourite character is not dropping and it might become a bigger issue when more seasons come out is all.Overall I'm really looking forward to more content coming for this game as I'm having a lot of fun with it and its something different for DBZ gamers who are used to the pure fighting. Just remember if you're a survivor you're working as a team. Letting others die on first down or not giving your dragonballs to someone who has more and needs them is a pretty easy way to get yourself killed and lose the game also
