_childDocuments_.review: The game started off fun and fairly balanced with a few notable issues. As time went on they added more abilities and a few more raiders. This lead to a huge power scale issue. Most games are either its 1 sided Raider or 1 sided survivors very VERY rarely is it in between. If your playing survivor and everyone works together you can damn near stun lock the raider making it pretty unfun for the raider players OR you play raider and everyone falls like dominoes and there are not enough resources on the field to do anything to the raider past small annoyances. This is my problems with the game. Items I feel should provide some invul after use (like seizue bean revives) just don't leading to situations where most revive items are useless outside of situations where the game is already heavily skewed towards the survivors winning already. Also moves that you may share with the raider (like solar flare) just straight up beats any version of the move you have as a survivor which sucks especially if you took the time to max the move out.Gameplay grips: As raider or survivor there is no camera lock on which makes fights very frustrating to engage as you have no way to keep track of the raider and survivor while in view of them. It also makes moves really hard to hit intentionally if they are not right in front of you. The controls while flying feel a bit clunky and cumbersome which makes movement as raider annoying or movement as survivor in your powered state unnecessarily tough. DI when being attacked can cause situations where you just straight up not allowed to move because of lack of invul as stated earlier. This leads you to just get stun locked until you either, as raider lose all your health OR as survivor lose your super form.Monetization: This games micro-transactions ARE TRASH. If you can do not buy them you don't really get anything worth it in terms of costumes or abilities. You can tell this game is mostly a cash grab by the devs and/or publishers.Lastly connection issues. This game is just straight up unfair if the raider has connection issues. Things that miss on your screen hits you on theirs, and attacks that connect from the survivor may just miss for no reason on the raider. This makes the game unbearable to play, as raider just DRAINS super form HP really fast.While the game was fun in the beginning its lost its novelty and has become really annoying and unfun to play even with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I side very strongly with many of the similar negative reviews. Dragon Ball: The Breakers was an insanely fun game to play with my friends when it first came out. It led to a ton of laughs and genuinely one of the best times I've had in a while since my Friday the 13th days. give or take a few nicks here and there I felt the game was perfect, unfortunately that feeling was quickly demolished by the competitive angle that the game wanted to head into, removing the ability to queue with a chance to be raider against your friends in favor of a new "raider queue" system that.. didn't even work for 2 seasons. Something that ended up pissing off both sides of the equation for listening to the few people who complained about the lack of an option without considering why so many people enjoyed it to begin with. I felt personally the priority system worked. It made queuing quick and simple as well as keeping both sides well stocked. It almost feels like the devs felt challenged to make it worse, going as far to even remove the ability to play with friends as a whole. Completely removing any of my remaining will to come back. Not even Mr Satan, a character I was excited to see come to the game, even nudged me.In short I feel the game's downfall shows a great example of "the sunk cost fallacy". They bent heavily into a competitive aspect and angle that no one saw the game for, and despite the constant push-back to revert, they dumped more resources into something very few people wanted. They tried to be more like Dead By Daylight, a game I've come to resent, Instead of Friday the 13th, a game I wish would come back.Final thoughts:to me this game went from "a fun game to play with my friends!" to "A game I can play with my friends!" to "a game!"

_childDocuments_.review: As you can tell, I've put a lot of time into this game. Do I recommend it? Based on the gameplay absolutly, but for those of you who are new, be aware the game has issues, primarily related to the servers, bugs, Dimps, other players, and the "gacha" system.First, the good.Playing as the raider, sneaking up and downing survivors, as well as getting into ki blast dodge battles are some of the funnest times I've ever had in any online game, and being on a timer to get all of this done in a timely manner makes for a very intense and focused matches.Playing survivor is more mixed, but if you learn how to play properly (and don't care whatsoever about daily challenges) you'll figure out to delay and escape the raider often, and gain STM wins. If you have a decent team, you can challenge the raider and gain some wins that way. If you have bad teammates and learn how to survive, you can also learn how to get escape wins fairly often. But is survivor as fun as raider? Not personally, but if you know how to rack up wins quickly, you'll get to the part of the game you want to play more often. Now for the bad.The servers.1. You may randomly be kicked at any time for no reason in the menu, the server just decides "lol, go away"2. Easy anticheat can randomly kick you for no reason (a hacker in a room? doubtful)3. Your teammates will fairly often vanish from being kicked, and the raider may also randomly disconnect4. The moment a new season starts, don't expect to get inside a game today5. You may be in queue, and the timer bypasses how long your "expected" to wait. If you do that and your a newbie, you may think "i'll just wait it out". Wrong, you should always leave, your stuck with somebody that won't get you a match, and this will just result in prolonged wait times for potentially hours depending on how long the other people are going to hang out6. The queues themselves are broken, and have been broken, and have had false promises by Dimps to fix them since the games launch. Raider queue was promised, added for 2 days, removed because it destroyed the servers due to Dimps incompetency, readded with the launch of season 4 (9 months later mind you) and than broke again, before being again removed and is once again "promised" to be fixed but just launches you in Flex queue. The game has been out for over a year, and raider queue has worked for less than a week total. That shows you how much Dimps cares.7. The game servers may boot you when you buy something from the shop or use the gacha8. The flex queue itself is also the reason raider queue results in the servers breaking. When they add raider queue, raider queue takes total priority, as well as results in survivors being sent to many different rooms instead of the rooms with a raider "available". This results in match queue times being 30-60 minutes, due to Dimps not giving Flex priority over Raider. And if you do use flex isntead of raider when raider queue is available, you will never get a raider match.Bugs/Dimps/Teammates1. I did not get to experience the Broly map once, as they broke it, and made it to where it is impossible for survivors to find the STM key if the raider destroys that part of the map. 2. Easy anti-cheat is idiotic and does not work. While I don't encounter "cheaters" very often, as the player count is too low for that to happen, you can and will encounter bots. I've encountered "Wetframe" and his other 2 alts on numerous ocassions, and despite reporting them for maybe a year, they still appear with disturbing frequency. 3. There is 0 drawback for a player who just wants to play raider to feed and just go die and let your queue increase. Sometimes players will just sit still, or they spawn with a senzu bean, run out, and get insta killed so they can get raider faster. This is a failure by Dimps to ever resolve this issue. As raider, I just down these people and let them sit with a 90 second timer.MixedThe gacha/loot/battlepass/TeammatesI never like these systems, and I never pay attention to these systems when I play a game. I just play until I'm satisfied and if I get something, great. You can absolutly learn to how escape with perfect frequency using most skill combinations. While some are far more OP than others, it does not provide one player with a such a severe advantage that it's impossible for the raider or other players to "Catch up". However, it does still provide other players an advantage, and this is a "Paid game", not F2P. I should be able to just purchase skills if I want.Finally, with each update, this results in players returning to the game, not understanding the games current meta, and than when they encounter something new (broly), having 0 idea how to actually survive. It's been weeks and I still see people get downed by broly instantly at the start of matches, and it's become pretty tiresome to have a match decided in the first 5 seconds. And than these same people have played against broly so often, that they forgot how to counter the other raiders. Currently with how the game stands, I still enjoy the game, but I have no wish to continue until raider queue is back and I can finally get raider matches that last longer than 1 minute, or survivors finally understand how to counter broly/focus on the STM and we can start gettings wins again. So probly not until 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this on a whim on a deep sale for about 50% off, and it's surprisingly a lot more enjoyable than the polarizing reviews (both overall and recent) would suggest. However all of this comes down to your expectations. If you're trying to find the next competitive and "balanced" asymmetric multiplayer game ala all the Dbd clones try to do then you'll be extremely disappointed. But if you want some mindless (I don't necessarily mean that negatively), and chaotic fun then you'll find it here. Especially if you like the DBZ franchise. This game feels like the love child of Dbd and Evolve with mechanics taken from both although DB: The Breakers leans closer to Dbd than Evolve gameplay wise. For what its worth it takes an interestingly fresh spin on ideas from both those games even if the execution at times is a little flawed.I think the biggest concerns/disappointments are a lack of crossplay which would help consolidate the entire playerbase across all platforms, the in-game gacha to gain more skills/abilities/"hero spirits", and lastly the 60fps framecap which honestly is just a nitpick.  I believe you get one guaranteed gacha ticket for free upon starting and I'd recommend using it to get "Kaioken" as it's a useful mobility skill for survivor, especially starting out. Luckily as of the time I'm writing this queue times are actually not that long and at certain times of the day super quick. And lastly this game could probably run on a toaster so you don't need a powerful PC to run it regardless of the resolution you play at.Edit 2/16/23 - Majority of my playtime was during S1, S2 just started at the time I'm updating this. So there has been some questionable balancing changes with the game alongside new content. I'm a little pessimistic about the future direction of this game, but it's too early to tell what things will be like plus Dimps may patch further in so we'll see.Edit 4/16/23 - Survivor since the beginning of S2 (arguably a bit before then if you include power key setting times and super time machine speed which are justified since those were too short at the time) have been getting nerfs and with the recent balance changes as of 4/14/23 they've been nerf'd heavily again mobility wise. If you're a raider main aside from matchmaking issues you should be easily feasting right now in games unless you're new/bad. Just a forewarning to prospective players. Dimps' decisions in terms of buffs and nerfs has been headscratching to say the least. New/Free-to-Play Players (Aka interacting with the gacha minimally with only in-game currency) have a much steeper hill to climb now when trying to escape competent raiders. Depending on the pool of active skills you have and if they're level'd enough aka +10 to throw them on any build.Dimps overtuned the game and continues to do so, and patched things hard in the wrong direction. As I alluded to earlier in a negative way where no one really wins (And is happy) regardless if you play survivor or raider. Basically in a similar situation to Dbd and the state of that game. It would take a lot to get this back to where it used to be. Copium, but I've had my fun with this at the end so I guess it doesn't matter. At least I got my moneys worth in terms of playtime while it was enjoyable to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite my many hours in the game I can't recommend this game to anyone regardless of how much fun I had. The game has some severe issues in spots that you wouldn't really expect from an assymetrical game. So to save you the time of reading a paragraph I'll just jot the bad parts below for you. Cons:-Game costs $20, but has a monetization pay model scheme that you commonly see in F2P mobile games-Should be free to play (F2P), but isn't-This game is definitely pay to win with some characters and abilities giving unfair advantages-The battlepass for some ungodly reason locks your progression until new challenges come out-The overall janky hitboxes of some moves and abilities will work against you most of the time as a survivor-Will most likely die within a couple weeks due to them ignoring the severe need for crossplay-Is very RNG based in some matches where either side can lose very quickly if they get good spawns-Has a horrible tutorial that doesn't explain the game properly-Not only has a battlepass, but also a very bad gacha system as well-The grind for said gacha and obtaining all of the currencies within the game, particularly the ones used for upgrading most skills is just downright criminal-Doesn't have a good way for survivors to communicate or coordinate together which leads to people not reviving allies most of the time-Gives the raider way too many opportunities to camp in the worst ways which lets them take games hostage-The senzu bean is the worst item in the game and is only useful for a last resort revival and has robbed people of their chance at a second life too  many times-Game doesn't close properly Pros:-Is a pretty good concept for an assymetrical game-Has the potential to be very fun at times when anything listed in the cons doesn't get in the way-When all things go right, the raider experience can be very thrilling as well as the survivor roleHonestly wish I could say better things about this game, but a group of greedy people behind the monetization plans of this game are ultimately ruining what could have been a great assymetrical game that you'd want to return to by yourself or with friends to mess around in. As it stands, the only way to give this game a chance at a longer lifespan is to commit to the F2P model and compensate the players who paid or fix the currency income overall so we don't feel like we're getting robbed of our time and money. I unfortunately bought the deluxe edition for $30 and can confidently say the bonuses let alone the game aren't worth the price tag, especially since they want you to throw practically double the amount at them for the gacha and battlepass individually. Also crossplay is a must at this point along with cross progression or we're going to see a server shutdown announcement within at least under a year depending on how much the playerbase carries this game on its back.The fact that Dragon Ball stans are throwing jester awards at me means that I'm %100 correct about this game and you shouldn't waste your money on it. Go buy anything else instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like the earliest version of Dead by Daylight in terms of its balance and content but equally manages to make the idea worse by default. You pay twenty-dollars to end up with a game that still insists you gamble at the lobby machine like a gacha game in order to get various qualities of iconic characters like Goku/Vegeta/and so on, you need to as they have abilities that you will need for passives if you want to be better while playing survivor.You don't play as the Raider when you choose, you can set a priority to play as the Raider and then you will be compared to others that had to play a handful of survivor games first and then they will play the Raider. You get bumped up in priority for every match you play through as a survivor. I have a mild appreciation for this mechanic as it prevents people from getting too good at the Raider to the point they can't be stopped, but equally it causes problems for those that don't agree with the concept and those that don't like not being able to appropriately learn one side.Content and customization is currently fairly shallow. You don't actually play as Krillen/Tien/Yamcha, you just don their clothes when you use the appropriate transformation to fight the Raider, you otherwise play as a character you customize. The game could use more clothes, character customization, and so on, as right now the initial creation doesn't have a whole heaping ton of options and additionally the clothing store doesn't have much variety for a purchase and even when I was buying the more expensive items did I become fully content with my outfit in just a small handful of hours.Combat is generally clunky? There's a tutorial that hardly teaches you very many of the mechanics, and none about being a Raider, so it's solely up to you to figure it out through trial and error and probably a lot of searching google/guides for answers that are not currently available to people currently as the game is still relatively new and people are trying to figure it out. You will see new things fairly often, and that's not really good. When you are playing a Raider, you will most likely be a lower level player and when you do end up going against others you will easily come to find that they potentially have gear and equipment that you did not as a survivor and thus do not know how to counter or what they even do. The reasoning for this is still falling back to the issue that a lot of the content is behind the lobby gambling machine that you pay for using a mix of paid for currency ( You can earn it at an.. Alright pace,) normal earned currency, and tickets you get for leveling/linking with your friends. Despite having four methods to pay for these though, fairly often have I been just out of luck in terms of getting several skills I've seen and have no access to as a result. This game does have potential, it can be better, but equally there's been too many asymmetrical games that seem to want to go the route of wanting money before they push a stable product that's going to last them that long. For twenty dollars? It's alright in the short term, but that's it, even then the negatives will far far far outweigh the positives.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I'd like to mention that all the people complaining about the Gacha system seem to forget to mention that all that stuff can be paid for with in game currency. In this specific regard the game is fairly generous and gives a lot of tickets that can be used for free as well so if the Gacha system is the only thing that's stopping you or keeping you on the fence, just don't let it stop you.This is not to say that I like having it in the game but I don't hear people complaining about DBD's Bloodweb which is completely RNG as well and unfortunately we are in a time period where games need some form of continuous income to keep supporting it and bring out updates.Now on to the actual review.The graphics:The graphics are very Xenoverse-y, not a bad thing and not a good thing either just very mediocre which doesn't really wow me. Maybe I've been spoiled by the artstyle in FighterZ.The gameplay:The game CAN be fun, playing with friends is a blast and I've also played quite a few matches on my own. It can get quite repetitive as there are limited things to do (Just like in DBD) but it's good in short bursts of a few matches every now and then.There are definitely some balancing issues though, it could be that I'm just bad at the game but I see it happen to almost every raider I've played against as well. Survivors can just team up and rush a Raider and there is basically nothing they can do about it. Especially if the survivors get all the dragon balls it's basically a loss for the Raider.Speaking of Raiders, you don't get to choose what you play as. You can pick a preference for survivor or raider but that won't guarantee you get that spot. You'll get a priority point for each match you play as your non-preferred role and usually have to get around 6 points to finally get your preferred role if that happens to be raider.There seems to be a clearly weak Raider and a clearly strong (wouldn't say OP) raider, Cell and Buu respectively.Overall I think the game has potential but needs a lot of support.Sound:Sound design is fine, nothing particular which is a bit of a shame because I always loved the dragonball soundtracksTL;DR : Can recommend the game but it's not perfect and not like most dragonball games. Get it if you're a fan or are looking for a DB themed party game

_childDocuments_.review: After putting about 50 hours into this game this is what I determined.For starters, I had to play about 6-8 matches before I really figured out what I was doing and what the point was, because TBH the tutorial does a pretty bad job explaining anything except moving and climbing.At this point in time, the game IMO is pretty strongly survivor sided. At first, when the raider catches you alone you get scared because you know he can just take you out easily, but once you understand your skills and play with players who have some decent time in game, you will quickly learn that survivors are easily given many tools to outplay the raider in nearly every situation. If the raider is persistent and skilled in their own right then they will eventually secure some kills, but it can be easy to get frustrated by survivors who team up. And if it comes down to the end game, it realistically only takes 2-3 survivors to team up against you in unison to make life hard.The fighting can take some time to get used to, it's mostly about learning about the space between you and your target and figuring out that spamming left click isn't a good idea. As a survivor, it can at first feel like your attempts to actually fight the raider is pointless and he just keeps shooting you or stun locking you in punches until you go down, but once you earn skills and figure out the mechanics a survivor can definitely fight the raider 1v1 at least for a small amount of time.Ultimately, I think that this game will probably see some changes to make survivors less powerful, but despite that, the game is still a lot of fun. There's many matches that end with the raider getting pretty brutally ganged up on, but not necessarily every game goes that way, and there's plenty of close matches. If you're the type of person who prefers to play the "killer" then it's important to know that this game uses the F13 method of choosing the raider, so it just collects the first 8 players that it can find and then chooses 1 of them to be raider after the fact depending on your priority number, which grows every game that you put raider as your preference and don't get it.I think this game is fun, and I understand that it's not for everyone, but I do wish people would consider the cheap price tag, and for a survival style game akin to things like DBD and F13 I think it is a breath of fresh air to people who enjoy that style of game play without necessarily desiring a horror type experience and likes the Dragon Ball series.

_childDocuments_.review: I played DBD, just could not get into it. Dunno what it was, loved hearing the strats, loved the lore. Just couldn't get into it.Then, I tried Breakers.This game is balanced in the oddest way possible. I dunno how else to describe it. Most of the wins or losses can be chalked up to misplays on either the raider or survivor side of things, if both sides are on equal footing. It really comes down to this interesting arms race, where the raider wants to get powered up before the survivors get the change power needed to combat them. And that's what I feel Breakers brings to the table in asymmetric survival: The ability to fight back and win as the majority.It makes the raiders worry more about survivors than in DBD. In DBD, the worst a survivor can do when left alone is continue to escape or help others. In Breakers, they could all get change power before you get enough evolution power to threaten them, or they could get all the dragon balls and summon Shenron to create something that even final form raiders struggle to defeat, or they could just set all the power keys, leading to you being forced to take out the startup or kill them all quickly system to secure a win.But although the survivors have a lot of options, the raiders have a lot of options too. From most raiders getting ki tracking or minions to ferret out survivors from where they're hiding, to dangerous attacks and get-off-me buttons to turn the tables on changed survivors, to LITERALLY ERASING PART OF THE MAP FROM EXISTENCE. Yeah, this game has no problem giving both sides tools to work with.And survivors have all the escape tools to not make that oppressive. While they can only fly while changed, they have a litany of gadgets and passives to help them. From a short burst of flight, to trampolines and grappling hooks, to a spaceship that can put you anywhere on the map, to the ability to warp out of a zone before its destruction or change automatically when they get their barrier broken. And raiders have their own skills and abilities too, some for holding people still, some attacks, some scouting measures, all balanced in the most powerful way possible.But with Dragon Ball, what else could you expect?I'd say the best thing to know to rack up wins as both as survivor and raider is to know your end goals. Survivors can escape with either of the time machines or by defeating the raider. The raider can win by sabotaging the boot sequence or having every survivor down at the same time. And here's the kicker: Both sides can win. If every survivor escaped using the backup time machine, there would be no losers in that game. Then, with that in mind, it becomes working toward your long-term goals with smaller goals, while adapting your plans on the fly as the other players interact with the world.This game seems to be shaping up to be a good competitor for DBD, or, dare I say, a DBD killer?Either way, you can bet your bottom dollar I'm gonna be here for it.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a really good game once you understand how to play it and how the upgrade/ability system in the game works. The UI is pretty bad at explaining these things, and the tutorial could've been better. I've even watched this game on youtube, through gameplay/tutorials, and none of them just explained "when/why" you do something, just "do this". So really, maybe it isn't the developers fault, as even community members struggle to really teach you the basics of how to gain new abilities/passives.I will say, I highly recommend just queueing as raider, to try and get it. It's been the most fun I've had on this game, a total of 6 matches. I usually play with a friend, in which you cannot actually queue as raider at the same time, otherwise I would have more raider games.  Raiders have access to most of their potential from a new player perspective, and are easy to get into.Survivors, I've had probably 6 good games. 5 were a win, 1 was a loss, but it was close. The other games are either people not understanding the game (mostly due to their low ranks, so I don't blame them), but we are up against raiders who are VERY high ranking (Z ranking, the highest) who just stomp us and don't even play respectful against noobs (body camp/key camp). Like bro, you will win without doing that against us. The queue being so bad might be because I keep playing on off-peak hours (9 pm all the way to 6 am my time, my schedule is bad right now). I have played a few games on "semi peak hours" (3-5 pm) and the queue was fine. So maybe it's just my fault for having such an off schedule for where I am located.Survivors can be EXTREMELY fun if people just go in at the same time, help each other, actually find the objective (keys). But a lot of the time, these people are noobs and just play for safe rank, and hide the whole game, trying to escape so they can rank up despite doing nothing. It's a pretty awful way to play the game and defeats the purpose of it being a game. The 6 survivors games I enjoyed, people actually went in, tried, 2 closes matches, 1 in which it was a loss, but it felt good because we tried. Overall, really fun game. Just don't play on degenerate hours like I have been and you should be fine to find a game. I also highly recommend not to spend money on this game, as I plan on being "f2p". The rates to get SPECIFIC upgrades in this game is really bad, and no pity system for really important things you might want. You can get all these skills f2p, but you need to grind, and tbh the grind isn't that bad. You even get the main game currency in which you can buy the "pay only" raiders with. So really, if you want the game to change for the better, don't buy the gacha, just enjoy the game, use your playstyles and use the plenty of good f2p skills you can get early on and if you get decent drops from the spirit summoner in the game (where you get abilities/upgrades).

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I've chosen to request a refund for the game because I have had several server issues and had no help after contacting support. I've also included my previous review for the game under this one.I wanted this game to succeed. I loved playing the game in the first Closed Network Test (CNT). That CNT made me want to buy the game. And I pre-ordered it. But, when the Open Beta (OB) rolled around, issues arose.During the OB, I would occasionally experience disconnecting/matchmaking issues. While annoying, I pushed through till the second day. There was a bug that would cause a server error after the match, which would softlock the game till you let the 180 second timeout timer go, or just Alt+F4ing out of the game. At that point, I stopped playing the OB on my PC, and switched to my PS4. I experienced 0 issues on PS4. So, I spent the rest of the OB period playing the PS4 version.After the game's full release, I experienced these issues still, as well as some new ones that made the experience frustrating. The new issue involved me losing rewards after playing a game, meaning I gained no Survivor EXP, Raider EXP, as well as potential level up rewards.Contacting support didn't help either. I was offered 5 potential solutions to test and see if they would work. They were: Use an Ethernet cable (I already do), Avoid streaming/downloading during gameplay (had issues even if I wasn't downloading/streaming), Power-cycle router (why did it work on my PS4 during OB then), Switch networks (Unplugged my ethernet cable, didn't work), Limit devices connected to your router (I live with family, that's funny).And while I'm at it, may as well mention the Gacha system. Why have this game be paid and have the Gacha system? I saw the Gacha system in both the CNT and the OB, and hoped the game would be F2P, which is the only way it would actually compete with DbD. Instead, they chose to double monetize the game and get people to fall for the Gacha, when skills don't matter if the Raider is competent.Original review below:TLDR: I've had disconnecting issues with the game that cause me to lose any level progress I made in a match when the disconnect happens after death/matchSo, while a lot of reviews are pointing out the Gacha system, I shall choose not to focus on it as you'll see a ton of reviews about it. What I'm going to base my review off of is my experience.I was in the first Closed Network Test, minimal issues. When the Open Beta started, however, was when I experienced glaring issues. I would regularly encounter network errors when connecting to a game, or after a game. The frustrating part of the latter is that it would soft lock the game till you waited the 3 minutes of how you did, or you have to close the game. I constantly got frustrated cause it happened almost every game I tried to play. But, you would at least get your rewards for the match. I started playing the Open Beta on my PS4, no issues whatsoever.And now we come to release. The disconnect issues persist after dying as survivor. And you lose ANY progress you make for Raider/Survivor levels and their rewards. Any hype I had for the game has been dampened by these issues. I was rooting for this game, but it delivered disappointment.Save yourself the hassle and just get Dead By Daylight instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying, I WANT this game to be good. When the games and the players are actually having a good time, then this game is super fun. It has potential. But in its current state, it is simply BAD. The main problem? The Raider.Imagine being a level 3, or a level 4 survivor (due to the Dragon Balls) and losing to a passive Raider at Level 2 because they wanted to float away and shoot Ki Blasts? Imagine giving a Raider a HITSCAN attack in a game where no matter what level you are as a survivor, you lose 40% to 50% of your health. Frieza is the greatest beneficiary of this. His attack can literally MISS, and still hit you. The amount of lvl 60+ Frieza players around is hysterical. Spopovich, 2nd Form Cell and Super Buu are also contenders for this. The gameplay of Raider boils down to "Mash X to Win." It's boring to play as, and HORRIBLE to play against. We are allowing Raiders to level up their skills to the point where a kill can charge their entire meter, or nearly all of it at times. Meanwhile, half the Survivor abilities either have insane start-up in tight situations (Solar Flare, Kaioken, Trap Device) or are just complete fodder that you'd never use. I made sure to play the heck out of this game before writing this review.  And I can tell you, this game is ULTRA Raider-Friendly. And if this keeps up, it will kill the game easily. Survivors who are a higher level than the Raider should not lose almost all their health from an attack. I literally watched a level 2 Buu defeat a Level 4 survivor simply by running away and mashing blasts. It's boring. Frieza is beyond unbalanced, with death beams doing half of your meter no matter what level you are, and auto-tracks your body. The most balanced raider is Cell, and even then, 2nd Form Cell has auto-tracking specials that are nearly impossible to dodge ever.  Super Buu has ki-blasts that have insane range, auto-tracking and damage. Raiders are simply overpowered. Also, no cross-play and region locking? That's an easy way to kill games on consoles, especially things like Nintendo Switch and PS5. There is nothing this game has to offer. Playing as survivor as a solo que player is a flip of a coin. Either you get teammates who are willing to cooperate and work together, or you get your "TTV's" and your players that just want to collect the Dragon Balls and get decimated first with five to six of them on their person. Or just the nature of this game being an RNG fest. Did the raider check your area first? Well, you lose. GG, go next. It's BORING. Did you get the abilities you needed from the Gacha system? No? Then you have a way harder time winning. It's just slot machine after slot machine, and a lot of the control is out of your hands. Don't buy this game. I have no faith they are going to fix the issues plaguing it, looking at you, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2. Just play a different game from a different company. It's clear that Bandai Namco does not know what goes into a style of game like this.Addendum (4/1/23): Buu is currently unrunnable, and every survivor has Energy Field + IT. Nice. Now the pendulum tilts in favor of the survivors. Imagine allowing survivors who are LVL 1 with one LVL 2 to completely steamroll a raider. This company doesn't know anything about game balancing. Punishing a player for playing well, but their character has NO tools to protect themselves. Nice balancing. Energy Field has 0 counterplay, and easily combos with Instant Transmission, allowing any survivor to just leave the fight instantly. No punishing, no risk, nothing. Done with this game.

If you don't live in the mainland U.S. or in Japan, don't bother getting this game until they remove the region lock that they implemented for no reason. And from what I've been hearing even some of those areas have problems. With an already extremely small playerbase why would they region lock it? And adding crossplay on top of it, makes no sense if you can't play with players on other platforms to begin with. It's like they want to make it harder for you to find a match.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Dragon Ball: The Breakers - A Riveting Adventure ContinuesRating: ★★★★☆Dragon Ball: The Breakers takes fans of the iconic Dragon Ball franchise on an exhilarating journey filled with action, humor, and the ever-present spirit of friendship. As a devoted follower of the series, I was eagerly anticipating this latest installment, and I must say that it did not disappoint.One of the standout aspects of Dragon Ball: The Breakers is its captivating storyline. The narrative takes place after the events of Dragon Ball Super, with Goku and his friends facing a formidable new threat. The Breakers, a group of powerful villains from different universes, wreak havoc across the multiverse. This fresh storyline injects new life into the Dragon Ball universe and keeps viewers hooked from start to finish.The animation quality in The Breakers is simply stunning. The vibrant colors, fluid fight sequences, and meticulous attention to detail bring the battles to life in a way that is both visually breathtaking and faithful to the original manga. The iconic character designs are faithfully preserved, and the animation team has managed to infuse the show with a modern flair while retaining the essence of Akira Toriyama's art style.The action sequences in Dragon Ball: The Breakers are nothing short of spectacular. From intense one-on-one duels to large-scale battles that shake the very fabric of the multiverse, the fight choreography is masterfully executed. Each character's unique abilities and signature moves are brilliantly showcased, reminding fans of the power and skill that make Dragon Ball so captivating. The fight scenes are complemented by an adrenaline-pumping soundtrack that enhances the overall impact and immerses viewers in the epic battles.While the action takes center stage, the humor and camaraderie that have become trademarks of the Dragon Ball series are not forgotten in The Breakers. The witty banter and comedic moments provide much-needed levity, creating a perfect balance between intense action and lightheartedness. The interactions between the characters, especially Goku's infectious enthusiasm and Vegeta's unwavering determination, continue to be a joy to watch.However, as much as I enjoyed Dragon Ball: The Breakers, it is not without its minor flaws. Some of the supporting characters receive less screen time than desired, and their development feels rushed at times. Additionally, while the overarching plot is intriguing, certain aspects of the narrative could have been explored in greater depth to provide a more nuanced understanding of the new villains and their motivations.Overall, Dragon Ball: The Breakers is a thrilling addition to the Dragon Ball franchise that will undoubtedly satisfy fans' cravings for more Goku and his companions. With its captivating storyline, stunning animation, exhilarating action, and the perfect blend of humor and heart, this series reaffirms why Dragon Ball has remained a beloved and enduring cultural phenomenon. If you're a fan of the series, this is a must-watch that will leave you eagerly anticipating the next chapter in the Dragon Ball saga.

_childDocuments_.review:
Caught out by an unexpected temporal phenomenon, seven ordinary citizens find themselves stranded in a Temporal Seam; they share their imprisonment with a Raider, a menacing enemy from another timeline with overwhelming power.

Their only hope for survival is to break out of the Temporal Seam with the Super Time Machine but the Raider is on their backs and getting stronger minute-by-minute.

DRAGON BALL: THE BREAKERS is a 1-on-7 online asymmetrical action game in which a band of seven everyday humans tries to survive the Raider (a classic DRAGON BALL rival such as Cell and Frieza) who will hunt and evolve into an unstoppable force.
